verses.sanskrit:
तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम्
नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
tapaḥsvādhyāyanirataṁ tapasvī vāgvidāṁ varam
nāradaṁ paripapraccha vālmīkirmunipuṁgavam

translations.english: The ascetic Vālmīki asked Nārada, the best of sages and foremost of those conversant with words, ever engaged in austerities and Vedic studies.

verses.sanskrit:
को न्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान्
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः
verses.transliteration:
ko nvasminsāmprataṁ loke guṇavānkaśca vīryavān
dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ

translations.english: Who at present in this world is like crowned with qualities, and with prowess, knowing duty, and grateful, and truthful, and firm in vow.

verses.sanskrit:
चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः
विद्वान्कः कः समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ
vidvānkaḥ kaḥ samarthaśca kaścaikapriyadarśanaḥ

translations.english: Who is qualified by virtue of his character, and who is engaged in the welfare of all creatures? Who is learned and capable. Who alone is ever lovely to behold?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मवान्को जितक्रोधो द्युतिमान्कोऽनसूयकः
कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
ātmavānko jitakrodho dyutimānko'nasūyakaḥ
kasya bibhyati devāśca jātaroṣasya saṁyuge

translations.english: Who has subdued his heart, and controlled his anger, is endowed with splendour, and devoid of malice; and whom enraged in battle, do even the gods, fear?

verses.sanskrit:
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे
महर्षे त्वं समर्थोऽसि ज्ञातुमेवंविधं नरम्
verses.transliteration:
etadicchāmyahaṁ śrotuṁ paraṁ kautūhalaṁ hi me
maharṣe tvaṁ samartho'si jñātumevaṁvidhaṁ naram

translations.english: I have great curiosity to hear of such a person. You can, O Maharşi,* know about a man of this description. *A great saint. The word, however, signifies one belonging to a particular order of saints.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा चैतत्त्रिलोकज्ञो वाल्मीकेर्नारदो वचः
श्रूयतामिति चामन्त्र्य प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā caitattrilokajño vālmīkernārado vacaḥ
śrūyatāmiti cāmantrya prahṛṣṭo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Vālmīki's words, Nărada, cognizant of the three worlds, said with alacrity, “listen to me”!

verses.sanskrit:
बहवो दुर्लभाश्चैव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणाः
मुने वक्ष्याम्यहं बुद्ध्वा तैर्युक्तः श्रूयतां नरः
verses.transliteration:
bahavo durlabhāścaiva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ
mune vakṣyāmyahaṁ buddhvā tairyuktaḥ śrūyatāṁ naraḥ

translations.english: Rare as are the qualities mentioned by you, I will, O sage, having duly considered, describe to you a person endued with them.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
नियतात्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान्धृतिमान्वशी
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākuvaṁśaprabhavo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
niyatātmā mahāvīryo dyutimāndhṛtimānvaśī

translations.english: There is one sprung from the line of Ikşvāku, known by the name of Rāma. He is of subdued soul; and is exceedingly powerful; effulgent; endowed with patience; having senses under control.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिमान्नीतिमान्वाग्मी श्रीमाञ्शत्रुनिबर्हणः
विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवो महाहनुः
verses.transliteration:
buddhimānnītimānvāgmī śrīmāñśatrunibarhaṇaḥ
vipulāṁso mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvo mahāhanuḥ

translations.english: He is intelligent; learned in morality; eloquent; crowned with grace; the slayer of foes: broad-shouldered; possessed of mighty arms, a conch-shaped neck, fleshy jaws.

verses.sanskrit:
महोरस्को महेष्वासो गूढजत्रुररिंदमः
आजानुबाहुः सुशिराः सुललाटः सुविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
mahorasko maheṣvāso gūḍhajatrurariṁdamaḥ
ājānubāhuḥ suśirāḥ sulalāṭaḥ suvikramaḥ

translations.english: And a broad chest; a powerful bowman; the repressor of foes; having plump shoulder-blades; of arms reaching down to his knees; with a beautiful head, and a graceful forehead; and endowed with excellent might.

verses.sanskrit:
समः समविभक्ताङ्गः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्
पीनवक्षा विशालाक्षो लक्ष्मीवाञ्शुभलक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
samaḥ samavibhaktāṅgaḥ snigdhavarṇaḥ pratāpavān
pīnavakṣā viśālākṣo lakṣmīvāñśubhalakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: And having symmetrical limbs, and of a cool hue; and possessed of prowess; and having a well-developed chest; with expansive eyes; crowned with auspiciousness and favourable marks.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मज्ञः सत्यसंधश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः
यशस्वी ज्ञानसंपन्नः शुचिर्वश्यः समाधिमान्
verses.transliteration:
dharmajñaḥ satyasaṁdhaśca prajānāṁ ca hite rataḥ
yaśasvī jñānasaṁpannaḥ śucirvaśyaḥ samādhimān

translations.english: Knowing duty; firm in promise; always engaged in the good of his subjects; of accomplished renown; furnished with knowledge; pure in body and spirit; obedient towards superiors; versed in self-knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य परिरक्षिता
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
rakṣitā jīvalokasya dharmasya parirakṣitā
vedavedāṅgatattvajño dhanurvede ca niṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: Practising all the duties of his class; and preserving those cleaving to him; versed in the profundities of the Vedas and the Vedāngas; accomplished in archery.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञ स्मृतिमान्प्रतिभानवान्
सर्वलोकप्रियः साधुरदीनात्मा विचक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
sarvaśāstrārthatattvajña smṛtimānpratibhānavān
sarvalokapriyaḥ sādhuradīnātmā vicakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Well versed in the dicta of all the sciences; brilliant; gifted with a good memory; the darling of all; unreproved; of unvanquished spirit; proficient in every branch of learning.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वदाभिगतः सद्भिः समुद्र इव सिन्धुभिः
आर्यः सर्वसमश्चैव सदैकप्रियदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
sarvadābhigataḥ sadbhiḥ samudra iva sindhubhiḥ
āryaḥ sarvasamaścaiva sadaikapriyadarśanaḥ

translations.english: Ever resorted to by the good persons even as the ocean is by the rivers; worthy of being honoured; having an equal regard for all; and capable of filling the heart with ever new sensations.

verses.sanskrit:
स च सर्वगुणोपेतः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः
समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवानिव
verses.transliteration:
sa ca sarvaguṇopetaḥ kausalyānandavardhanaḥ
samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavāniva

translations.english: Crowned with all sort of qualities, he enhances the joys of Kausalyā; being like that of the sea in gravity, and that of the Himavat in patience.

verses.sanskrit:
विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये सोमवत्प्रियदर्शनः
कालाग्निसदृशः क्रोधे क्षमया पृथिवीसमः
verses.transliteration:
viṣṇunā sadṛśo vīrye somavatpriyadarśanaḥ
kālāgnisadṛśaḥ krodhe kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ

translations.english: In prowess, he is like as Vişnu, and boasts of the personal attractions of the Moon. In anger he resembles the fire raging at the time of dissolution; and in forgiveness, he is like that of the Earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तं प्रियं दशरथः सुतम्
यौवराज्येन संयोक्तुमैच्छत्प्रीत्या महीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhaṁ śreṣṭhaguṇairyuktaṁ priyaṁ daśarathaḥ sutam
yauvarājyena saṁyoktumaicchatprītyā mahīpatiḥ

translations.english: In giving away, he is like the Bestower of riches Kubera, and in truth, he is like another Dharma. Desirous of doing that which would be acceptable to his subjects, king Dasaratha, from fuilness of affection, wished to install as his associate in the kingdom his beloved and meritorious eldest son. Rāina who of infallible prowess, and endued with sterling virtues, and ever intent on the welfare of the people. The king Dasaratha with great pleasure wished to install as the hairapparent of the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याभिषेकसंभारान्दृष्ट्वा भार्याथ कैकयी
पूर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत
विवासनं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyābhiṣekasaṁbhārāndṛṣṭvā bhāryātha kaikayī
pūrvaṁ dattavarā devī varamenamayācata
vivāsanaṁ ca rāmasya bharatasyābhiṣecanam

translations.english: Beholding the provisions of the installation, that lady the king's consort, Kaikeyī, who had previously been promised two boons, even asked him for those viz., the exile of Ráma, and the installation of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
स सत्यवचनाद्राजा धर्मपाशेन संयतः
विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथः प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
sa satyavacanādrājā dharmapāśena saṁyataḥ
vivāsayāmāsa sutaṁ rāmaṁ daśarathaḥ priyam

translations.english: Bound by the ties of duty in consequence of his promise, king Dasaratha banished his favourite son Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स जगाम वनं वीरः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन्
पितुर्वचननिर्देशात्कैकेय्याः प्रियकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
sa jagāma vanaṁ vīraḥ pratijñāmanupālayan
piturvacananirdeśātkaikeyyāḥ priyakāraṇāt

translations.english: In pursuance of his father's promise, and with the view of compassing the pleasure of Kaikeyī, that heroic one, commanded by his sire, repaired to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तं व्रजन्तं प्रियो भ्राता लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह
स्नेहाद्विनयसंपन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vrajantaṁ priyo bhrātā lakṣmaṇo'nujagāma ha
snehādvinayasaṁpannaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ

translations.english: On the eve of his departure for the forest, that enhancer of Sumitrā's joy and favourite of his brother (Rāma), his dear brother Lakşmaņa, endowed with humility, displaying brotherliness, followed him out of affection.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्ना नारीणामुत्तमा वधूः
सीताप्यनुगता रामं शशिनं रोहिणी यथा
verses.transliteration:
sarvalakṣaṇasaṁpannā nārīṇāmuttamā vadhūḥ
sītāpyanugatā rāmaṁ śaśinaṁ rohiṇī yathā

translations.english: As Rohini followed with the moon, Rāma's beloved spouse, sprung in Janaka's line-like as an embodiment of Divine power-sear (Rāma) as life itself, and engaged in acts of good, and furnished with every auspicious mark, and the best of wives, followed Rāma. Having been followed far by his father Dasaratha along with the citizens.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वनेन वनं गत्वा नदीस्तीर्त्वा बहूदकाः
चित्रकूटमनुप्राप्य भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्
verses.transliteration:
te vanena vanaṁ gatvā nadīstīrtvā bahūdakāḥ
citrakūṭamanuprāpya bharadvājasya śāsanāt

translations.english: Then wending from one forest to another, and having crossed many broad rivers, they, in accordance with Bharadvăja's directions, arrived at the Citrakūta; and constructing a romantic abode, the three began to live there.

verses.sanskrit:
चित्रकूटं गते रामे पुत्रशोकातुरस्तदा
राजा दशरथः स्वर्गं जगाम विलपन्सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
citrakūṭaṁ gate rāme putraśokāturastadā
rājā daśarathaḥ svargaṁ jagāma vilapansutam

translations.english: They spent their days in delight, in the company of gods and Gandharvas. And when Rāma had reached the Citrakuța, king Dasaratha, distressed on account of his son, went to heaven, bewailing the latter.

verses.sanskrit:
मृते तु तस्मिन्भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजैः
नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद्राज्यं महाबलः
स जगाम वनं वीरो रामपादप्रसादकः
verses.transliteration:
mṛte tu tasminbharato vasiṣṭhapramukhairdvijaiḥ
niyujyamāno rājyāya naicchadrājyaṁ mahābalaḥ
sa jagāma vanaṁ vīro rāmapādaprasādakaḥ

translations.english: When king Dasaratha had passed away heaven, the mighty Bharata, although pressed by the Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, to rule the kingdom, did not wish for dominion. And that hero went the forest, with the view of propitiating Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
पादुके चास्य राज्याय न्यासं दत्त्वा पुनः पुनः
निवर्तयामास ततो भरतं भरताग्रजः
verses.transliteration:
pāduke cāsya rājyāya nyāsaṁ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ
nivartayāmāsa tato bharataṁ bharatāgrajaḥ

translations.english: Bharata said, You are only the king conversant with Dharma. And the exceedingly generous, illustrious and mighty Rāma of a cheerful countenance did not wish for the kingdom, in consonance with his father's injunction. And having made over to Bharata, as his substitute on the throne, his own sandals, Bharata's elder brother repeatedly forbade him.

verses.sanskrit:
स काममनवाप्यैव रामपादावुपस्पृशन्
नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद्राज्यं रामागमनकाङ्क्षया
verses.transliteration:
sa kāmamanavāpyaiva rāmapādāvupaspṛśan
nandigrāme'karodrājyaṁ rāmāgamanakāṅkṣayā

translations.english: And then Bharata, finding his desire not fulfilled, touched Rama's feet, and began to rule at Nandigrāma, expecting the return of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्तु पुनरालक्ष्य नागरस्य जनस्य च
तत्रागमनमेकाग्रे दण्डकान्प्रविवेश ह
verses.transliteration:
rāmastu punarālakṣya nāgarasya janasya ca
tatrāgamanamekāgre daṇḍakānpraviveśa ha

translations.english: And when the auspicious Bharata, firm in his promise and of subdued sense, had gone away, Rāma again perceiving there the influx of citizens and others, eagerly entered Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
विराधं राक्षसं हत्वा शरभङ्गं ददर्श ह
सुतीक्ष्णं चाप्यगस्त्यं च अगस्त्य भ्रातरं तथा
verses.transliteration:
virādhaṁ rākṣasaṁ hatvā śarabhaṅgaṁ dadarśa ha
sutīkṣṇaṁ cāpyagastyaṁ ca agastya bhrātaraṁ tathā

translations.english: Having entered that mighty vast, the lotuseyed Rāma slew the Räkşasa Virädha, and saw Sarabhanga, Sutiksna, Agastya and Agastya's brother.

verses.sanskrit:
अगस्त्यवचनाच्चैव जग्राहैन्द्रं शरासनम्
खड्गं च परमप्रीतस्तूणी चाक्षयसायकौ
verses.transliteration:
agastyavacanāccaiva jagrāhaindraṁ śarāsanam
khaḍgaṁ ca paramaprītastūṇī cākṣayasāyakau

translations.english: He then, advised by Agastya, gladly possessed himself of Indra's bow, the inexhaustible arrows, the scimitar, and the quiver.

verses.sanskrit:
वसतस्तस्य रामस्य वने वनचरैः सह
ऋषयोऽभ्यागमन्सर्वे वधायासुररक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
vasatastasya rāmasya vane vanacaraiḥ saha
ṛṣayo'bhyāgamansarve vadhāyāsurarakṣasām

translations.english: While Rāma was dwelling there with the rangers of forests, the sages came to him in a body, for the destruction of the Asuras and Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन तत्रैव वसता जनस्थाननिवासिनी
विरूपिता शूर्पणखा राक्षसी कामरूपिणी
verses.transliteration:
tena tatraiva vasatā janasthānanivāsinī
virūpitā śūrpaṇakhā rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī

translations.english: It was while he was living there that, that dweller of Janasthāna, the Rākṣasī Śūrpanakhā, capable of assuming any form at will, was disfigured.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखावाक्यादुद्युक्तान्सर्वराक्षसान्
खरं त्रिशिरसं चैव दूषणं चैव राक्षसम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāvākyādudyuktānsarvarākṣasān
kharaṁ triśirasaṁ caiva dūṣaṇaṁ caiva rākṣasam

translations.english: It was while living there in the society of the inhabitants of Janasthāna, that Rāma slew in battle the Rākşasas Khara and Trisiras and Dusana, together with their followers, who all had been stirred up by the words of Śūrpanakhā. And fourteen thousand Räksasas were slain in that battle.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो ज्ञातिवधं श्रुत्वा रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः
सहायं वरयामास मारीचं नाम राक्षसम्
verses.transliteration:
tato jñātivadhaṁ śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
sahāyaṁ varayāmāsa mārīcaṁ nāma rākṣasam

translations.english: Having learnt of the destruction of his relatives, Rāvaņa wrought into frenzy by anger, sought the help of a Rākşasa named Mārīca.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादृत्य तु तद्वाक्यं रावणः कालचोदितः
जगाम सहमारीचस्तस्याश्रमपदं तदा
verses.transliteration:
anādṛtya tu tadvākyaṁ rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ
jagāma sahamārīcastasyāśramapadaṁ tadā

translations.english: And although strongly dissuaded by Mārīca, saying. You ought not to enter into hostilities with that powerful one. Do you, therefore, O Ravana, excuse me! yet, disregarding those words of his, Ravana, urged on by Fate, went into that asylum in company with Mārīca.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन मायाविना दूरमपवाह्य नृपात्मजौ
जहार भार्यां रामस्य गृध्रं हत्वा जटायुषम्
verses.transliteration:
tena māyāvinā dūramapavāhya nṛpātmajau
jahāra bhāryāṁ rāmasya gṛdhraṁ hatvā jaṭāyuṣam

translations.english: That one (Mārīca) commanding illusions, having drawn far the king's sons (Rāma and Lakşmaņa), he (Rāvana) carried away Rāma's wife, slaying the vulture Jatayu.

verses.sanskrit:
गृध्रं च निहतं दृष्ट्वा हृतां श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम्
राघवः शोकसंतप्तो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
gṛdhraṁ ca nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā hṛtāṁ śrutvā ca maithilīm
rāghavaḥ śokasaṁtapto vilalāpākulendriyaḥ

translations.english: And beholding the vulture slain and learning of the kidnapping of Mithila's daughter, the descendant of Raghu, deprived of sense, bewailed in grief.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेनैव शोकेन गृध्रं दग्ध्वा जटायुषम्
मार्गमाणो वने सीतां राक्षसं संददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
tatastenaiva śokena gṛdhraṁ dagdhvā jaṭāyuṣam
mārgamāṇo vane sītāṁ rākṣasaṁ saṁdadarśa ha

translations.english: Having with unassuaged sorrow burnt the vulture Jațāyu, as he was searching for Sità in that forest, he fell in with a Rākṣasa, Kabandha by name, of a dreadful and deformed shape. Having slain him, the mighty-armed one burnt his body,-and thereupon he went to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
स चास्य कथयामास शबरीं धर्मचारिणीम्
श्रमणीं धर्मनिपुणामभिगच्छेति राघव
सोऽभ्यगच्छन्महातेजाः शबरीं शत्रुसूदनः
verses.transliteration:
sa cāsya kathayāmāsa śabarīṁ dharmacāriṇīm
śramaṇīṁ dharmanipuṇāmabhigaccheti rāghava
so'bhyagacchanmahātejāḥ śabarīṁ śatrusūdanaḥ

translations.english: And the Rākşasa addressed Rama saying, O descendant of Raghu, Do you repair to the ascetic, Śabarī, conversant with all systems of morality.

verses.sanskrit:
शबर्या पूजितः सम्यग्रामो दशरथात्मजः
पम्पातीरे हनुमता संगतो वानरेण ह
verses.transliteration:
śabaryā pūjitaḥ samyagrāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
pampātīre hanumatā saṁgato vānareṇa ha

translations.english: Repairing to Sabarī, that destroyer of foes, gifted with exceeding energy, Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, highly honoured by Sabari.

verses.sanskrit:
हनुमद्वचनाच्चैव सुग्रीवेण समागतः
सुग्रीवाय च तत्सर्वं शंसद्रामो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
hanumadvacanāccaiva sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
sugrīvāya ca tatsarvaṁ śaṁsadrāmo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Than he met with Hanuman on the banks of the Pampā. Then, agreeably to Hanumān's advice, the exceedingly powerful Rāma saw Sugrīva. And detailed to him all specially touching Sitā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वानरराजेन वैरानुकथनं प्रति
रामायावेदितं सर्वं प्रणयाद्दुःखितेन च
वालिनश्च बलं तत्र कथयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
tato vānararājena vairānukathanaṁ prati
rāmāyāveditaṁ sarvaṁ praṇayādduḥkhitena ca
vālinaśca balaṁ tatra kathayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: Then the king of monkeys, out of friendship, mournfully related to him all about his hostilities with Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिज्ञातं च रामेण तदा वालिवधं प्रति
सुग्रीवः शङ्कितश्चासीन्नित्यं वीर्येण राघवे
verses.transliteration:
pratijñātaṁ ca rāmeṇa tadā vālivadhaṁ prati
sugrīvaḥ śaṅkitaścāsīnnityaṁ vīryeṇa rāghave

translations.english: Then Ráma vowed that he would slay Vālī. Thereupon the monkey described to Raghava the prowess of Vālī, and he feared lest Räma should not prove a match for Válī.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवः प्रत्ययार्थं तु दुन्दुभेः कायमुत्तमम्
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन चिक्षेप संपूर्णं दशयोजनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaḥ pratyayārthaṁ tu dundubheḥ kāyamuttamam
pādāṅguṣṭhena cikṣepa saṁpūrṇaṁ daśayojanam

translations.english: And with the view of convincing Raghava (as to Vali's might), Sugriva showed to him the huge corpse of Dundubhi, resembling a hill.

verses.sanskrit:
बिभेद च पुनः सालान्सप्तैकेन महेषुणा
गिरिं रसातलं चैव जनयन्प्रत्ययं तदा
verses.transliteration:
bibheda ca punaḥ sālānsaptaikena maheṣuṇā
giriṁ rasātalaṁ caiva janayanpratyayaṁ tadā

translations.english: With a single mighty shaft he pierced seven palmyra palms, a hill, and the sixth nether worlds, carrying conviction to Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतमनास्तेन विश्वस्तः स महाकपिः
किष्किन्धां रामसहितो जगाम च गुहां तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prītamanāstena viśvastaḥ sa mahākapiḥ
kiṣkindhāṁ rāmasahito jagāma ca guhāṁ tadā

translations.english: Thus convinced, the mighty monkey well pleased went with Rāma towards the cave called Kiskindha.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽगर्जद्धरिवरः सुग्रीवो हेमपिङ्गलः
तेन नादेन महता निर्जगाम हरीश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tato'garjaddharivaraḥ sugrīvo hemapiṅgalaḥ
tena nādena mahatā nirjagāma harīśvaraḥ

translations.english: And having arrived there, that best of monkeys, Sugrīva of a tawny and golden hue, set up loud roars. And at those mighty sounds, out came the lord of monkeys; and having obtained Tārā's consent came before Sugrīva for battle. Then Rāghava killed Vālī on the spot with a single shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुग्रीववचनाद्धत्वा वालिनमाहवे
सुग्रीवमेव तद्राज्ये राघवः प्रत्यपादयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sugrīvavacanāddhatvā vālinamāhave
sugrīvameva tadrājye rāghavaḥ pratyapādayat

translations.english: And, in compliance with Sugrīva's request, having slain Vālī in battle, Raghava conferred the kingdom on Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
स च सर्वान्समानीय वानरान्वानरर्षभः
दिशः प्रस्थापयामास दिदृक्षुर्जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa ca sarvānsamānīya vānarānvānararṣabhaḥ
diśaḥ prasthāpayāmāsa didṛkṣurjanakātmajām

translations.english: Then that best of monkeys having summoned all the various monkeys, sent them in various directions in search of Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गृध्रस्य वचनात्संपातेर्हनुमान्बली
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं पुप्लुवे लवणार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
tato gṛdhrasya vacanātsaṁpāterhanumānbalī
śatayojanavistīrṇaṁ pupluve lavaṇārṇavam

translations.english: Then at the suggestion of the vulture Sampāti, the mighty Hanuman crossed the salt sea extending for a hundred Yojanas (900 miles).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र लङ्कां समासाद्य पुरीं रावणपालिताम्
ददर्श सीतां ध्यायन्तीमशोकवनिकां गताम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra laṅkāṁ samāsādya purīṁ rāvaṇapālitām
dadarśa sītāṁ dhyāyantīmaśokavanikāṁ gatām

translations.english: Thereby arriving at the city of Lankā, ruled by Rāvana, he found Sītā in the midst of an Asoka garden, absorbed in thought.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेदयित्वाभिज्ञानं प्रवृत्तिं च निवेद्य च
समाश्वास्य च वैदेहीं मर्दयामास तोरणम्
verses.transliteration:
nivedayitvābhijñānaṁ pravṛttiṁ ca nivedya ca
samāśvāsya ca vaidehīṁ mardayāmāsa toraṇam

translations.english: Then having shown her the sign, he rtlated to her all about the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva, and having convinced Videha's daughter, he smashed the gate of the place.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्च सेनाग्रगान्हत्वा सप्त मन्त्रिसुतानपि
शूरमक्षं च निष्पिष्य ग्रहणं समुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
pañca senāgragānhatvā sapta mantrisutānapi
śūramakṣaṁ ca niṣpiṣya grahaṇaṁ samupāgamat

translations.english: Then having slain five generals, and seven counsellors' sons, and crushed the heroic Aksa, he was bound fast (by the arms of Indrajit.)

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रेणोन्मुहमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा पैतामहाद्वरात्
मर्षयन्राक्षसान्वीरो यन्त्रिणस्तान्यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
astreṇonmuhamātmānaṁ jñātvā paitāmahādvarāt
marṣayanrākṣasānvīro yantriṇastānyadṛcchayā

translations.english: Then knowing that in virtue of the grandsire's boon, he was free, he forgave those Raksasas that were leading him (to Ravana.)

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दग्ध्वा पुरीं लङ्कामृते सीतां च मैथिलीम्
रामाय प्रियमाख्यातुं पुनरायान्महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
tato dagdhvā purīṁ laṅkāmṛte sītāṁ ca maithilīm
rāmāya priyamākhyātuṁ punarāyānmahākapiḥ

translations.english: Then having burnt down the city of Lankā, with the exception of the place occupied by Mithila's daughter, the mighty one returned, with the intention of delivering the glad tidings to Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं कृत्वा रामं प्रदक्षिणम्
न्यवेदयदमेयात्मा दृष्टा सीतेति तत्त्वतः
verses.transliteration:
so'bhigamya mahātmānaṁ kṛtvā rāmaṁ pradakṣiṇam
nyavedayadameyātmā dṛṣṭā sīteti tattvataḥ

translations.english: That one of immeasurable soul having come before the high-souled Rāma, and circled him addressed him, saying,— I have truly seen Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुग्रीवसहितो गत्वा तीरं महोदधेः
समुद्रं क्षोभयामास शरैरादित्यसंनिभैः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sugrīvasahito gatvā tīraṁ mahodadheḥ
samudraṁ kṣobhayāmāsa śarairādityasaṁnibhaiḥ

translations.english: Thereafter accompanied by Sugrīva, Rāma repaired to the shore of the mighty ocean, and with shafts resembling the sun, vexed the deep.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शयामास चात्मानं समुद्रः सरितां पतिः
समुद्रवचनाच्चैव नलं सेतुमकारयत्
verses.transliteration:
darśayāmāsa cātmānaṁ samudraḥ saritāṁ patiḥ
samudravacanāccaiva nalaṁ setumakārayat

translations.english: Then that lord of rivers, the Ocean, showed himself. And agreeably to the advice of the Ocean, Nala constructed a bridge (over the water.)

verses.sanskrit:
तेन गत्वा पुरीं लङ्कां हत्वा रावणमाहवे
अभ्यषिञ्चत्स लङ्कायां राक्षसेन्द्रं विभीषणम्
verses.transliteration:
tena gatvā purīṁ laṅkāṁ hatvā rāvaṇamāhave
abhyaṣiñcatsa laṅkāyāṁ rākṣasendraṁ vibhīṣaṇam

translations.english: By that bridge Rama went to the city of Lankā, and slew Rāvana in battle. And, having recovered Sītā, Rāma experienced high shame (in consequence of Sītā's having lived so long in Ravana's place.)

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मणा तेन महता त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्
सदेवर्षिगणं तुष्टं राघवस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇā tena mahatā trailokyaṁ sacarācaram
sadevarṣigaṇaṁ tuṣṭaṁ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon assured by Agni as to the sinlessness of Sītā, Rāma became exceedingly pleased, and was honoured by all the deities. And at that great act of Rāma's the three worlds with all that was mobile and immobile in them, along with the sages and gods, were well pleased with the mighty-souled Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा परमसंतुष्टैः पूजितः सर्वदैवतैः
कृतकृत्यस्तदा रामो विज्वरः प्रमुमोद ह
verses.transliteration:
tathā paramasaṁtuṣṭaiḥ pūjitaḥ sarvadaivataiḥ
kṛtakṛtyastadā rāmo vijvaraḥ pramumoda ha

translations.english: Then installing that foremost of Rākşasas, Vibhișana, on the throne of Lankā, Rāma was perfectly easy, and rejoiced exceedingly.

verses.sanskrit:
देवताभ्यो वरान्प्राप्य समुत्थाप्य च वानरान्
पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य नन्दिग्रामं ययौ तदा
verses.transliteration:
devatābhyo varānprāpya samutthāpya ca vānarān
puṣpakaṁ tatsamāruhya nandigrāmaṁ yayau tadā

translations.english: Then Rāma, obtaining a boon from the celestials, revived the monkeys fallen in battle, and surrounded by friends, set out for Ayodhyā on the Puspaka.

verses.sanskrit:
नन्दिग्रामे जटां हित्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघः
रामः सीतामनुप्राप्य राज्यं पुनरवाप्तवान्
verses.transliteration:
nandigrāme jaṭāṁ hitvā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito'naghaḥ
rāmaḥ sītāmanuprāpya rājyaṁ punaravāptavān

translations.english: Having arrived at Nandigrāma, the sinless Rāma sheared himself of his matted locks along with his brothers, and having regained Sītā, got back his kingdom

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टमुदितो लोकस्तुष्टः पुष्टः सुधार्मिकः
निरायमो अरोगश्च दुर्भिक्षभयवर्जितः
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭamudito lokastuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ sudhārmikaḥ
nirāyamo arogaśca durbhikṣabhayavarjitaḥ

translations.english: (During his reign) his subjects will enjoy happiness, and contentment, and become hale, and grow in righteousness, and be devoid of mental disquietude and disease, and free from the fear of famine.

verses.sanskrit:
न पुत्रमरणं केचिद्द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुरुषाः क्वचित्
नार्यश्चाविधवा नित्यं भविष्यन्ति पतिव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
na putramaraṇaṁ keciddrakṣyanti puruṣāḥ kvacit
nāryaścāvidhavā nityaṁ bhaviṣyanti pativratāḥ

translations.english: Where a no person is to witness his son's death, and women will be ever chaste, and never bear widow-hood.

verses.sanskrit:
न वातजं भयं किंचिन्नाप्सु मज्जन्ति जन्तवः
न चाग्रिजं भयं किंचिद्यथा कृतयुगे तथा
verses.transliteration:
na vātajaṁ bhayaṁ kiṁcinnāpsu majjanti jantavaḥ
na cāgrijaṁ bhayaṁ kiṁcidyathā kṛtayuge tathā

translations.english: And no fear of conflagration (will exercise people), nor creatures be drowned in water. And no danger will come from hunger, or from thieves. And all will live happily as at the Krta age.

verses.sanskrit:
राजवंशाञ्शतगुणान्स्थापयिष्यति राघवः
चातुर्वर्ण्यं च लोकेऽस्मिन्स्वे स्वे धर्मे नियोक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rājavaṁśāñśataguṇānsthāpayiṣyati rāghavaḥ
cāturvarṇyaṁ ca loke'sminsve sve dharme niyokṣyati

translations.english: Having performed with countless gold an hundred horse-sacrifices, and bestowed with due rites ayutas and kotis* of kine on learned persons, and countless wealth famous Brāhmaṇas, Rāghava will establish an bundred royal families, and will employ each of the four castes in its own duties. Ayuta is ten thousand; and koti is ten millions.

verses.sanskrit:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च
रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca
rāmo rājyamupāsitvā brahmalokaṁ gamiṣyati

translations.english: And having reigned for ten thousand and as many hundred years. Rāma will depart for the regions of Brahmā.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं पवित्रं पापघ्नं पुण्यं वेदैश्च संमितम्
यः पठेद्रामचरितं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ pavitraṁ pāpaghnaṁ puṇyaṁ vedaiśca saṁmitam
yaḥ paṭhedrāmacaritaṁ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate

translations.english: He that reads this sacred, sin-destroying, merit-bestowing history of Rāma like that of the Veda itself, becomes cleansed from all sin.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदाख्यानमायुष्यं पठन्रामायणं नरः
सपुत्रपौत्रः सगणः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे महीयते
verses.transliteration:
etadākhyānamāyuṣyaṁ paṭhanrāmāyaṇaṁ naraḥ
saputrapautraḥ sagaṇaḥ pretya svarge mahīyate

translations.english: And the man that reads this Rāmāyaṇa conferring length of days, after death, is on honoured in heaven, along with his sons, and grandsons, and relations.

verses.sanskrit:
पठन्द्विजो वागृषभत्वमीया;त्स्यात्क्षत्रियो भूमिपतित्वमीयात्
वणिग्जनः पण्यफलत्वमीया;ज्जनश्च शूद्रोऽपि महत्त्वमीयात्
verses.transliteration:
paṭhandvijo vāgṛṣabhatvamīyā;tsyātkṣatriyo bhūmipatitvamīyāt
vaṇigjanaḥ paṇyaphalatvamīyā;jjanaśca śūdro'pi mahattvamīyāt

translations.english: If a Brāhmaṇa reads it, he attains excellence in speech; if a Kșatriya, he will acquire lordship over landed possessions, if a Vaisya, abundance of wealth in trade; and if a Sudra, greatness.

verses.sanskrit:
नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वाक्यविशारदः
पूजयामास धर्मात्मा सहशिष्यो महामुनिः
verses.transliteration:
nāradasya tu tadvākyaṁ śrutvā vākyaviśāradaḥ
pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā sahaśiṣyo mahāmuniḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of Nārada, that one of virtuous soul, skilled in speech, together with his disciples, worshipped that great sage.

verses.sanskrit:
यथावत्पूजितस्तेन देवर्षिर्नारदस्तदा
आपृष्ट्वैवाभ्यनुज्ञातः स जगाम विहायसम्
verses.transliteration:
yathāvatpūjitastena devarṣirnāradastadā
āpṛṣṭvaivābhyanujñātaḥ sa jagāma vihāyasam

translations.english: Having received due honours, that Devarși Nārada taking leave of him went to his ethereal regions.

verses.sanskrit:
स मुहूर्तं गते तस्मिन्देवलोकं मुनिस्तदा
जगाम तमसातीरं जाह्नव्यास्त्वविदूरतः
verses.transliteration:
sa muhūrtaṁ gate tasmindevalokaṁ munistadā
jagāma tamasātīraṁ jāhnavyāstvavidūrataḥ

translations.english: And when Nārada had left for the celestial regions, that holy person went to the banks of the Tamasā not very far from Jāhnavī.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तीरं समासाद्य तमसाया महामुनिः
शिष्यमाह स्थितं पार्श्वे दृष्ट्वा तीर्थमकर्दमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tīraṁ samāsādya tamasāyā mahāmuniḥ
śiṣyamāha sthitaṁ pārśve dṛṣṭvā tīrthamakardamam

translations.english: And having arrived at the banks of that river, the pious one, observing a holy spot devoid of mud, spoke to his disciple standing by.

verses.sanskrit:
अकर्दममिदं तीर्थं भरद्वाज निशामय
रमणीयं प्रसन्नाम्बु सन्मनुष्यमनो यथा
verses.transliteration:
akardamamidaṁ tīrthaṁ bharadvāja niśāmaya
ramaṇīyaṁ prasannāmbu sanmanuṣyamano yathā

translations.english: Saying-O Bharadvāja, behold this holy spot devoid of mud. And it is beautiful, and contains pleasant waters, even like the minds of good men.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यस्यतां कलशस्तात दीयतां वल्कलं मम
इदमेवावगाहिष्ये तमसातीर्थमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
nyasyatāṁ kalaśastāta dīyatāṁ valkalaṁ mama
idamevāvagāhiṣye tamasātīrthamuttamam

translations.english: O child, do you, put down your pitcher, and give me my bark. I will bathe even in this Tamasā, the best of holy spots.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो भरद्वाजो वाल्मीकेन महात्मना
प्रायच्छत मुनेस्तस्य वल्कलं नियतो गुरोः
verses.transliteration:
evamukto bharadvājo vālmīkena mahātmanā
prāyacchata munestasya valkalaṁ niyato guroḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by the high-souled Vālmīki, Bharadvāja ever intent upon serving his spiritual guide, presented the sage his bark.

verses.sanskrit:
स शिष्यहस्तादादाय वल्कलं नियतेन्द्रियः
विचचार ह पश्यंस्तत्सर्वतो विपुलं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa śiṣyahastādādāya valkalaṁ niyatendriyaḥ
vicacāra ha paśyaṁstatsarvato vipulaṁ vanam

translations.english: That one of subdued senses, having received his bark from his disciple, began to range around, surveying that extensive forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याभ्याशे तु मिथुनं चरन्तमनपायिनम्
ददर्श भगवांस्तत्र क्रौञ्चयोश्चारुनिस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyābhyāśe tu mithunaṁ carantamanapāyinam
dadarśa bhagavāṁstatra krauñcayoścārunisvanam

translations.english: In the vicinity of the forest, that worshipful one espied a pair of Krauñcas, emitting melodious notes, and ranging around never parting from one another.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्तु मिथुनादेकं पुमांसं पापनिश्चयः
जघान वैरनिलयो निषादस्तस्य पश्यतः
verses.transliteration:
tasmāttu mithunādekaṁ pumāṁsaṁ pāpaniścayaḥ
jaghāna vairanilayo niṣādastasya paśyataḥ

translations.english: At this juncture, a wicked-minded fowler, singling out the male, without any cause of hostility, slew him in the very presence of the holy man.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शोणितपरीताङ्गं वेष्टमानं महीतले
भार्या तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा रुराव करुणां गिरम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śoṇitaparītāṅgaṁ veṣṭamānaṁ mahītale
bhāryā tu nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā rurāva karuṇāṁ giram

translations.english: Observing him struggling on the earth, bathed in blood, his female companion began to bewail in piteous accents.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु तं द्विजं दृष्ट्वा निषादेन निपातितम्
ऋषेर्धर्मात्मनस्तस्य कारुण्यं समपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu taṁ dvijaṁ dṛṣṭvā niṣādena nipātitam
ṛṣerdharmātmanastasya kāruṇyaṁ samapadyata

translations.english: Finding the bird in that condition thus brought down by the fowler, the pity of that pious and righteous-souled Rși was excited exceedingly.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः करुणवेदित्वादधर्मोऽयमिति द्विजः
निशाम्य रुदतीं क्रौञ्चीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ karuṇaveditvādadharmo'yamiti dvijaḥ
niśāmya rudatīṁ krauñcīmidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Then considering it to be an unrighteous deed, with a heart moved with pity, that twice-born one, beholding the weeping Krauñci, spoke these words.

verses.sanskrit:
मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः
यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṁ tvamagamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
yatkrauñcamithunādekamavadhīḥ kāmamohitam

translations.english: O fowler, since you have slain one of a pair of Krauñcas, you shall never attain prosperity (respect)!

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतश्चिन्ता बभूव हृदि वीक्षतः
शोकार्तेनास्य शकुनेः किमिदं व्याहृतं मया
verses.transliteration:
tasyaivaṁ bruvataścintā babhūva hṛdi vīkṣataḥ
śokārtenāsya śakuneḥ kimidaṁ vyāhṛtaṁ mayā

translations.english: Having uttered this, he got worried within himself, What is this that I have said, afflicted with grief for the bird?

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयन्स महाप्राज्ञश्चकार मतिमान्मतिम्
शिष्यं चैवाब्रवीद्वाक्यमिदं स मुनिपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
cintayansa mahāprājñaścakāra matimānmatim
śiṣyaṁ caivābravīdvākyamidaṁ sa munipuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: Resolving thus in his mind, that highly-wise one and best of sages addressed his disciple, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
पादबद्धोऽक्षरसमस्तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितः
शोकार्तस्य प्रवृत्तो मे श्लोको भवतु नान्यथा
verses.transliteration:
pādabaddho'kṣarasamastantrīlayasamanvitaḥ
śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu nānyathā

translations.english: This speech that I have uttered is of equal bound with metre and accents; it has rhythm and is capable of being chanted according to measure to stringed accompaniment. Let it therefore go forth as a sloka!

verses.sanskrit:
शिष्यस्तु तस्य ब्रुवतो मुनेर्वाक्यमनुत्तमम्
प्रतिजग्राह संहृष्टस्तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्गुरुः
verses.transliteration:
śiṣyastu tasya bruvato munervākyamanuttamam
pratijagrāha saṁhṛṣṭastasya tuṣṭo'bhavadguruḥ

translations.english: When the sage had spoken thus, his disciple, well pleased, assented to his excellent speech; and thereat that pious person was gratified.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिषेकं ततः कृत्वा तीर्थे तस्मिन्यथाविधि
तमेव चिन्तयन्नर्थमुपावर्तत वै मुनिः
verses.transliteration:
so'bhiṣekaṁ tataḥ kṛtvā tīrthe tasminyathāvidhi
tameva cintayannarthamupāvartata vai muniḥ

translations.english: Then having duly performed his ablutions at that holy spot, the reverend sage retraced his steps, pondering over the incidents touching the sloka.

verses.sanskrit:
भरद्वाजस्ततः शिष्यो विनीतः श्रुतवान्गुरोः
कलशं पूर्णमादाय पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
bharadvājastataḥ śiṣyo vinītaḥ śrutavānguroḥ
kalaśaṁ pūrṇamādāya pṛṣṭhato'nujagāma ha

translations.english: His disciple also, accomplished in learning, and of meek demeanour, followed Vālmīki, carrying on his back a pitcher filled with water.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रविश्याश्रमपदं शिष्येण सह धर्मवित्
उपविष्टः कथाश्चान्याश्चकार ध्यानमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
sa praviśyāśramapadaṁ śiṣyeṇa saha dharmavit
upaviṣṭaḥ kathāścānyāścakāra dhyānamāsthitaḥ

translations.english: Having entered the hermitage along with his disciple, conversant with righteousness engaged in diverse kinds of talk, revolved in his mind the circumstances connected with the verses.

verses.sanskrit:
आजगाम ततो ब्रह्मा लोककर्ता स्वयं प्रभुः
चतुर्मुखो महातेजा द्रष्टुं तं मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
ājagāma tato brahmā lokakartā svayaṁ prabhuḥ
caturmukho mahātejā draṣṭuṁ taṁ munipuṁgavam

translations.english: It came to pass that desirous of seeing the best of sages, there arrived, that lord and creator of all, the effulgent Brahmā, furnished with four countenances.

verses.sanskrit:
वाल्मीकिरथ तं दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थाय वाग्यतः
प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतो भूत्वा तस्थौ परमविस्मितः
verses.transliteration:
vālmīkiratha taṁ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya vāgyataḥ
prāñjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā tasthau paramavismitaḥ

translations.english: Beholding him Vālmīki rose up suddenly and, wondering greatly, humbly and silently stood before him with clasped hands.

verses.sanskrit:
पूजयामास तं देवं पाद्यार्घ्यासनवन्दनैः
प्रणम्य विधिवच्चैनं पृष्ट्वानामयमव्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
pūjayāmāsa taṁ devaṁ pādyārghyāsanavandanaiḥ
praṇamya vidhivaccainaṁ pṛṣṭvānāmayamavyayam

translations.english: And duly bending low in reverence, Vālmīki offered that deity water to wash his feet, and other things for reception.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोपविश्य भगवानासने परमार्चिते
वाल्मीकये महर्षये संदिदेशासनं ततः
verses.transliteration:
athopaviśya bhagavānāsane paramārcite
vālmīkaye maharṣaye saṁdideśāsanaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: Having sat-down on a highly-honoured seat, that worshipful one enquired after the welfare of that sage Vālmīki knowing no deterioration, and then asked him to be seated.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा प्रहसन्मुनिपुंगवम्
श्लोक एव त्वया बद्धो नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca tato brahmā prahasanmunipuṁgavam
śloka eva tvayā baddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā

translations.english: Then smiling, Brahmā spoke to the excellent sage,-Those verses of your which you have composed a sloka shall attain celebrity: no doubt need be entertained on this head, It is because I had intended so, that those verses had come out of your lips.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मात्मनो गुणवतो लोके रामस्य धीमतः
वृत्तं कथय धीरस्य यथा ते नारदाच्छ्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
dharmātmano guṇavato loke rāmasya dhīmataḥ
vṛttaṁ kathaya dhīrasya yathā te nāradācchrutam

translations.english: Do you now, O best of saints, compose the entire history of Rāma. Do you relate to the world the history of the righteous-souled and intelligent Rāma crowned with qualities. And do you, as you have heard it from Närada.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेह्याश्चैव यद्वृत्तं प्रकाशं यदि वा रहः
तच्चाप्यविदितं सर्वं विदितं ते भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vaidehyāścaiva yadvṛttaṁ prakāśaṁ yadi vā rahaḥ
taccāpyaviditaṁ sarvaṁ viditaṁ te bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Relate all what is known, and all what is unknown to the world, O wise one, concerning Rāma, and Laksmana, and Videha's daughter, and all the Rākşasas. And even what is not known to Nārada, shall be unfolded to you.

verses.sanskrit:
न ते वागनृता काव्ये काचिदत्र भविष्यति
कुरु रामकथां पुण्यां श्लोकबद्धां मनोरमाम्
verses.transliteration:
na te vāganṛtā kāvye kācidatra bhaviṣyati
kuru rāmakathāṁ puṇyāṁ ślokabaddhāṁ manoramām

translations.english: No words of yours in this poem shall contain an untruth sacred. Therefore, now compose into verses. This delightful story of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्स्थास्यन्ति गिरयः सरितश्च महीतले
तावद्रामायणकथा लोकेषु प्रचरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvatsthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaśca mahītale
tāvadrāmāyaṇakathā lokeṣu pracariṣyati

translations.english: As long as the mountains and the seas exist on earth, the history of Rāmāyaṇa will remain prevalent among men.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्रामस्य च कथा त्वत्कृता प्रचरिष्यति
तावदूर्ध्वमधश्च त्वं मल्लोकेषु निवत्स्यसि
verses.transliteration:
yāvadrāmasya ca kathā tvatkṛtā pracariṣyati
tāvadūrdhvamadhaśca tvaṁ mallokeṣu nivatsyasi

translations.english: As long as this story of Rāmāyaṇa shall retain its currency, you shall reside both in this world and in mine.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्ब्रह्मा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत
ततः सशिष्यो वाल्मीकिर्मुनिर्विस्मयमाययौ
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā tatraivāntaradhīyata
tataḥ saśiṣyo vālmīkirmunirvismayamāyayau

translations.english: Having said this, the Lord Brahmä disappeared there. And thereat the sage and his disciples marvelled greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य शिष्यास्ततः सर्वे जगुः श्लोकमिमं पुनः
मुहुर्मुहुः प्रीयमाणाः प्राहुश्च भृशविस्मिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya śiṣyāstataḥ sarve jaguḥ ślokamimaṁ punaḥ
muhurmuhuḥ prīyamāṇāḥ prāhuśca bhṛśavismitāḥ

translations.english: His disciples sang those verses again and again; and, momentarily experiencing pleasure, recited it with exceeding wonder.

verses.sanskrit:
समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा
सोऽनुव्याहरणाद्भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः
verses.transliteration:
samākṣaraiścaturbhiryaḥ pādairgīto maharṣiṇā
so'nuvyāharaṇādbhūyaḥ śokaḥ ślokatvamāgataḥ

translations.english: Those verses, composed of equal accents, and furnished with four parts, have been sung by the great saint, have, in virtue of frequent repetition, been associated with a world of pathos and have attained the eminence of a sloka.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बुद्धिरियं जाता वाल्मीकेर्भावितात्मनः
कृत्स्नं रामायणं काव्यमीदृशैः करवाण्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya buddhiriyaṁ jātā vālmīkerbhāvitātmanaḥ
kṛtsnaṁ rāmāyaṇaṁ kāvyamīdṛśaiḥ karavāṇyaham

translations.english: Now it is the intention of that illustrious and self-centred sage to compose the entire Rāmāyaṇa in this metre.

verses.sanskrit:
उदारवृत्तार्थपदैर्मनोरमै;स्तदास्य रामस्य चकार कीर्तिमान्
समाक्षरैः श्लोकशतैर्यशस्विनो; यशस्करं काव्यमुदारधीर्मुनिः
verses.transliteration:
udāravṛttārthapadairmanoramai;stadāsya rāmasya cakāra kīrtimān
samākṣaraiḥ ślokaśatairyaśasvino; yaśaskaraṁ kāvyamudāradhīrmuniḥ

translations.english: The great ascetic Vālmīki of gracious appearance and unparalleled renown composed a poetry consisting of hundreds of verses in melodious measure, couching the significance of the history of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा वस्तु समग्रं तद्धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम्
व्यक्तमन्वेषते भूयो यद्वृत्तं तस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā vastu samagraṁ taddharmātmā dharmasaṁhitam
vyaktamanveṣate bhūyo yadvṛttaṁ tasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Having heard the entire prevalent history of the intelligent Rāma, capable of conferring religious merit and the two other cognate objects, as well as emancipation, Vālmīki again sought to get insight into it.

verses.sanskrit:
उपस्पृश्योदकं संयन्मुनिः स्थित्वा कृताञ्जलिः
प्राचीनाग्रेषु दर्भेषु धर्मेणान्वेषते गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
upaspṛśyodakaṁ saṁyanmuniḥ sthitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
prācīnāgreṣu darbheṣu dharmeṇānveṣate gatim

translations.english: And, sitting himself facing the east on a cushion of kuća grass, and sipping water according to the ordinance, he addressed himself to the contemplation of the subject through Yoga.

verses.sanskrit:
जन्म रामस्य सुमहद्वीर्यं सर्वानुकूलताम्
लोकस्य प्रियतां क्षान्तिं सौम्यतां सत्यशीलताम्
verses.transliteration:
janma rāmasya sumahadvīryaṁ sarvānukūlatām
lokasya priyatāṁ kṣāntiṁ saumyatāṁ satyaśīlatām

translations.english: Rama's birth, his mighty prowess, and kindness to all, and popularity, and forbearance, and goodness, and truthfulness.

verses.sanskrit:
गङ्गायाश्चापि संतारं भरद्वाजस्य दर्शनम्
भरद्वाजाभ्यनुज्ञानाच्चित्रकूटस्य दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
gaṅgāyāścāpi saṁtāraṁ bharadvājasya darśanam
bharadvājābhyanujñānāccitrakūṭasya darśanam

translations.english: And the swimming of the Gangā and Rāma sinter view with Bharadvāja; and his arrival at Citrakūta in consonance with Bharadvāja's injunction.

verses.sanskrit:
वास्तुकर्मनिवेशं च भरतागमनं तथा
प्रसादनं च रामस्य पितुश्च सलिलक्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
vāstukarmaniveśaṁ ca bharatāgamanaṁ tathā
prasādanaṁ ca rāmasya pituśca salilakriyām

translations.english: And Rāma's building a mansion there and sojourn; and Bharata's arrival, and his propitiation of Rāma; and Rāma's offering oblations to the manes of his father.

verses.sanskrit:
पादुकाग्र्याभिषेकं च नन्दिग्राम निवासनम्
दण्डकारण्यगमनं सुतीक्ष्णेन समागमम्
verses.transliteration:
pādukāgryābhiṣekaṁ ca nandigrāma nivāsanam
daṇḍakāraṇyagamanaṁ sutīkṣṇena samāgamam

translations.english: And the installation of the sandals; and Bharata's dwelling at Nandigrāma: and Rāma's removal to Dandaka and killing of Virādha.

verses.sanskrit:
अनसूयासमस्यां च अङ्गरागस्य चार्पणम्
शूर्पणख्याश्च संवादं विरूपकरणं तथा
verses.transliteration:
anasūyāsamasyāṁ ca aṅgarāgasya cārpaṇam
śūrpaṇakhyāśca saṁvādaṁ virūpakaraṇaṁ tathā

translations.english: And Rāma's interview with Agastya, and his obtaining the bow from him; and the dialogue of Śūrpanakha and her disfigurement.

verses.sanskrit:
वधं खरत्रिशिरसोरुत्थानं रावणस्य च
मारीचस्य वधं चैव वैदेह्या हरणं तथा
verses.transliteration:
vadhaṁ kharatriśirasorutthānaṁ rāvaṇasya ca
mārīcasya vadhaṁ caiva vaidehyā haraṇaṁ tathā

translations.english: And the slaughter of Khara and Trisiras; and the exertions of Rāvana; the killing of Mārīca, and the carrying away of Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य विलापं च गृध्रराजनिबर्हणम्
कबन्धदर्शनं चैव पम्पायाश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vilāpaṁ ca gṛdhrarājanibarhaṇam
kabandhadarśanaṁ caiva pampāyāścāpi darśanam

translations.english: Rāghava's lamentations, and the death of the king of vultures; Rāma's encounter with Kabandha, and his view of Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
शर्बर्या दर्शनं चैव हनूमद्दर्शनं तथा
विलापं चैव पम्पायां राघवस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
śarbaryā darśanaṁ caiva hanūmaddarśanaṁ tathā
vilāpaṁ caiva pampāyāṁ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Rāma's interview with Śabarī, and his subsistence there on fruits and roots; Rāma's lamentations at Pampā, and meeting with Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋष्यमूकस्य गमनं सुग्रीवेण समागमम्
प्रत्ययोत्पादनं सख्यं वालिसुग्रीवविग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣyamūkasya gamanaṁ sugrīveṇa samāgamam
pratyayotpādanaṁ sakhyaṁ vālisugrīvavigraham

translations.english: The former's sojourn to the Rşyamūka, and meeting with Sugrīva; Rāma's raising the confidence of Sugrīva and his friendship with the latter; and the encounter between Vāli and Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
कोपं राघवसिंहस्य बलानामुपसंग्रहम्
दिशः प्रस्थापनं चैव पृथिव्याश्च निवेदनम्
verses.transliteration:
kopaṁ rāghavasiṁhasya balānāmupasaṁgraham
diśaḥ prasthāpanaṁ caiva pṛthivyāśca nivedanam

translations.english: The destruction of Vâli, and the installation of Sugrīva and Tara's lamentations%3B the understanding between Rāma and Sugrīva as to the time for commencing the march. Rāma's stay at the wet night, and the ire of Rama the lion of Raghu's race; the levying of forces; and the despatch of envoys in deferent directions; and the assignment by Sugrīva of different quarters to the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गुलीयकदानं च ऋक्षस्य बिलदर्शनम्
प्रायोपवेशनं चैव संपातेश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgulīyakadānaṁ ca ṛkṣasya biladarśanam
prāyopaveśanaṁ caiva saṁpāteścāpi darśanam

translations.english: The making over of his ring by Rāma to Hanuman; Rksa's discovery of the cave. The abstemious abode of the monkeys on the shore of the ocean; Hanuman's interview with Sampāti.

verses.sanskrit:
आपानभूमिगमनमवरोधस्य दर्शनम्
अशोकवनिकायानं सीतायाश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
āpānabhūmigamanamavarodhasya darśanam
aśokavanikāyānaṁ sītāyāścāpi darśanam

translations.english: His entrance by night into Lankā; his ascertaining of conduct in times of helplessness; his journey to the Āpāna ground; and his sight of his car Puşpaka; his walk to the Asoka forest, and sight there of Şītā.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिज्ञानप्रदानं च सीतायाश्चापि भाषणम्
राक्षसीतर्जनं चैव त्रिजटास्वप्नदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
abhijñānapradānaṁ ca sītāyāścāpi bhāṣaṇam
rākṣasītarjanaṁ caiva trijaṭāsvapnadarśanam

translations.english: His presentation of the ring to Sītā and converse with her; and the roaring of the Rākṣasis; and the dreaming of the dream by Trijatā.

verses.sanskrit:
मणिप्रदानं सीताया वृक्षभङ्गं तथैव च
राक्षसीविद्रवं चैव किंकराणां निबर्हणम्
verses.transliteration:
maṇipradānaṁ sītāyā vṛkṣabhaṅgaṁ tathaiva ca
rākṣasīvidravaṁ caiva kiṁkarāṇāṁ nibarhaṇam

translations.english: Sīta's handing a gem to Hanumān; and the breaking down of trees; and the fight of the Rakasasis, and the slaughter of the salves.

verses.sanskrit:
ग्रहणं वायुसूनोश्च लङ्कादाहाभिगर्जनम्
प्रतिप्लवनमेवाथ मधूनां हरणं तथा
verses.transliteration:
grahaṇaṁ vāyusūnośca laṅkādāhābhigarjanam
pratiplavanamevātha madhūnāṁ haraṇaṁ tathā

translations.english: The wind-god's son being taken captive; and his terrible roars while burning down Lankā; and his bounding back over the ocean; and the forcible possession of honey.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवाश्वासनं चैव मणिनिर्यातनं तथा
संगमं च समुद्रस्य नलसेतोश्च बन्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavāśvāsanaṁ caiva maṇiniryātanaṁ tathā
saṁgamaṁ ca samudrasya nalasetośca bandhanam

translations.english: Hanumān's consoling Rāghava, and handing him the gem; Rāma's interview with ocean; and Nala's constructing the bridge.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतारं च समुद्रस्य रात्रौ लङ्कावरोधनम्
विभीषणेन संसर्गं वधोपायनिवेदनम्
verses.transliteration:
pratāraṁ ca samudrasya rātrau laṅkāvarodhanam
vibhīṣaṇena saṁsargaṁ vadhopāyanivedanam

translations.english: The army's crossing of the ocean; and the nightly siege of Lankā; and Rāma, interview with Bibhishana; the communication as to the means of destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णस्य निधनं मेघनादनिबर्हणम्
रावणस्य विनाशं च सीतावाप्तिमरेः पुरे
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇasya nidhanaṁ meghanādanibarhaṇam
rāvaṇasya vināśaṁ ca sītāvāptimareḥ pure

translations.english: And the killing of Kumbhakarna and Meghanāda; and the destruction of Răvaņa, and the recovery of Sītā in the enemy's city.

verses.sanskrit:
बिभीषणाभिषेकं च पुष्पकस्य च दर्शनम्
अयोध्यायाश्च गमनं भरतेन समागमम्
verses.transliteration:
bibhīṣaṇābhiṣekaṁ ca puṣpakasya ca darśanam
ayodhyāyāśca gamanaṁ bharatena samāgamam

translations.english: And the coronation of Vibhīşaņa, and the sight of Puspaka; Rama's return towards Ayodhyā, and meeting with Bharadvāja.

verses.sanskrit:
रामाभिषेकाभ्युदयं सर्वसैन्यविसर्जनम्
स्वराष्ट्ररञ्जनं चैव वैदेह्याश्च विसर्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmābhiṣekābhyudayaṁ sarvasainyavisarjanam
svarāṣṭrarañjanaṁ caiva vaidehyāśca visarjanam

translations.english: Despatch of Hanumān; and Rāma's meeting with Bharata; and the installation of Rāma; and the dismissal of all the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
अनागतं च यत्किंचिद्रामस्य वसुधातले
तच्चकारोत्तरे काव्ये वाल्मीकिर्भगवानृषिः
verses.transliteration:
anāgataṁ ca yatkiṁcidrāmasya vasudhātale
taccakārottare kāvye vālmīkirbhagavānṛṣiḥ

translations.english: Rāma's pleasing his subjects and renunciation of Sītā,-alleles besides concerning Rāma on earth, that has not yet taken place-have been dealt with by the worshipful sage in the following poem. earth, that has not yet taken place-have been dealt with by the worshipful sage in the following poem.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य वाल्मीकिर्भगवानृषिः
चकार चरितं कृत्स्नं विचित्रपदमात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
prāptarājyasya rāmasya vālmīkirbhagavānṛṣiḥ
cakāra caritaṁ kṛtsnaṁ vicitrapadamātmavān

translations.english: When Rāma had obtained his kingdom that worshipful sage, Vālmīki, composed the entire history (of that hero in) excellent metre and fraught with high meaning.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा तु तन्महाप्राज्ञः सभविष्यं सहोत्तरम्
चिन्तयामास को न्वेतत्प्रयुञ्जीयादिति प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā tu tanmahāprājñaḥ sabhaviṣyaṁ sahottaram
cintayāmāsa ko nvetatprayuñjīyāditi prabhuḥ

translations.english: And having composed it, including as well future incidents to happen afterwards, that lord relected as to who should publish the same before assemblies.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः
अगृह्णीतां ततः पादौ मुनिवेषौ कुशीलवौ
verses.transliteration:
tasya cintayamānasya maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ
agṛhṇītāṁ tataḥ pādau muniveṣau kuśīlavau

translations.english: And as that great sage of purified soul was thus pounding, in came Kuśi and Lava, in the guise of the sons of ascetics, and touched his feet.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु मेधाविनौ दृष्ट्वा वेदेषु परिनिष्ठितौ
वेदोपबृह्मणार्थाय तावग्राहयत प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu medhāvinau dṛṣṭvā vedeṣu pariniṣṭhitau
vedopabṛhmaṇārthāya tāvagrāhayata prabhuḥ

translations.english: And he found those illustrious princes the brothers Kusi and lava, knowing morality, and living in a hermitage, and endowed with rythmic voice, well versed in the Vedas. And finding them of a retentive endowment, and initiated into Vedic studies, that lord thought them how to interpret the Vedas, and that vow-observing one taught them the great Rāmāyaṇa in full, treating of Sītā's great life, and the destruction of Paulastya (Rāvana).

verses.sanskrit:
तौ राजपुत्रौ कार्त्स्न्येन धर्म्यमाख्यानमुत्तमम्
वाचो विधेयं तत्सर्वं कृत्वा काव्यमनिन्दितौ
verses.transliteration:
tau rājaputrau kārtsnyena dharmyamākhyānamuttamam
vāco vidheyaṁ tatsarvaṁ kṛtvā kāvyamaninditau

translations.english: Even as the reflection of the solar or the lunar disc resembles that disc; got by heart that excellent and moral story in its entirety; and those princes versed in the Fine arts, with a concentrated mind chanted it as they had learnt it, in the assemblies of ascetics and Brāhmaṇas and good men.

verses.sanskrit:
ते प्रीतमनसः सर्वे मुनयो धर्मवत्सलाः
प्रशशंसुः प्रशस्तव्यौ गायमानौ कुशीलवौ
verses.transliteration:
te prītamanasaḥ sarve munayo dharmavatsalāḥ
praśaśaṁsuḥ praśastavyau gāyamānau kuśīlavau

translations.english: Praised the praiseworthy Kuśi and Lava as they sang, saying,-Ah! what charming music! What sweetness of the verses!

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविश्य तावुभौ सुष्ठु तदा भावमगायताम्
सहितौ मधुरं रक्तं संपन्नं स्वरसंपदा
verses.transliteration:
praviśya tāvubhau suṣṭhu tadā bhāvamagāyatām
sahitau madhuraṁ raktaṁ saṁpannaṁ svarasaṁpadā

translations.english: All this happened long ago, yet it seems as if we saw it before us. And unified with the theme, both of them singing together sweetly, and at a high pitch, by means of şadja and the other notes, they entranced the audience.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रशस्यमानौ तौ तपःश्लाघ्यैर्महर्षिभिः
संरक्ततरमत्यर्थं मधुरं तावगायताम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ praśasyamānau tau tapaḥślāghyairmaharṣibhiḥ
saṁraktataramatyarthaṁ madhuraṁ tāvagāyatām

translations.english: They two thus went on sweetly singing at a high pitch, praised by those mighty sages priding in their asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रीतः कश्चिन्मुनिस्ताभ्यां संस्थितः कलशं ददौ
प्रसन्नो वल्कलं कश्चिद्ददौ ताभ्यां महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
prītaḥ kaścinmunistābhyāṁ saṁsthitaḥ kalaśaṁ dadau
prasanno valkalaṁ kaściddadau tābhyāṁ mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Some one in the assembly pleased with them presented them with a water-pitcher; and some one of high fame, being delighted, made them a present of a bark garment; and some one gave them a dark deer skin and some holy thread.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्चर्यमिदमाख्यानं मुनिना संप्रकीर्तितम्
परं कवीनामाधारं समाप्तं च यथाक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
āścaryamidamākhyānaṁ muninā saṁprakīrtitam
paraṁ kavīnāmādhāraṁ samāptaṁ ca yathākramam

translations.english: The sages said Wonderful is the story! And, O you accomplished in all kinds of music! beautifully have you chanted and finished this poem, charming ear and heart, and conferring long life and prosperity, which will afford themes to poets.

verses.sanskrit:
इमौ मुनी पार्थिवलक्ष्मणान्वितौ; कुशीलवौ चैव महातपस्विनौ
ममापि तद्भूतिकरं प्रचक्षते; महानुभावं चरितं निबोधत
verses.transliteration:
imau munī pārthivalakṣmaṇānvitau; kuśīlavau caiva mahātapasvinau
mamāpi tadbhūtikaraṁ pracakṣate; mahānubhāvaṁ caritaṁ nibodhata

translations.english: Rāma said, Although these Kuśa and Lava, of rigid penances, look like ascetics, yet they bear on their persons the signs of royalty. And, besides, the story conduces to my fame. Do you, therefore, listen to that history fraught with great worth!

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तौ रामवचः प्रचोदिता;वगायतां मार्गविधानसंपदा
स चापि रामः परिषद्गतः शनै;र्बुभूषयासक्तमना बभूव ह
verses.transliteration:
tatastu tau rāmavacaḥ pracoditā;vagāyatāṁ mārgavidhānasaṁpadā
sa cāpi rāmaḥ pariṣadgataḥ śanai;rbubhūṣayāsaktamanā babhūva ha

translations.english: And then commanded by Rāma, they began to chant according to the Märga mode, and Rāma seated in the midst of his court, was drawn to the music, anxious for the perpetuation of his history.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वापूर्वमियं येषामासीत्कृत्स्ना वसुंधरा
प्रजापतिमुपादाय नृपाणां जयशालिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvāpūrvamiyaṁ yeṣāmāsītkṛtsnā vasuṁdharā
prajāpatimupādāya nṛpāṇāṁ jayaśālinām

translations.english: This great story of Rämāyana treats of those victorious kings commencing with Prajāpati, and having Ikşvāku for their founder, who ruled the entire earth as no other kings had done so before them, and in whose line Sagara was born Sagara who dug the ocean, and whom, while out in progress, his sixty-thousand sons followed.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं वर्तयिष्यामि सर्वं निखिलमादितः
धर्मकामार्थसहितं श्रोतव्यमनसूयया
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ vartayiṣyāmi sarvaṁ nikhilamāditaḥ
dharmakāmārthasahitaṁ śrotavyamanasūyayā

translations.english: We shall now chant the entire history of that dynasty from the beginning. Do you, with minds free from ill will, listen to that story conferring merit, profit and pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
कोसलो नाम मुदितः स्फीतो जनपदो महान्
निविष्टः सरयूतीरे प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
kosalo nāma muditaḥ sphīto janapado mahān
niviṣṭaḥ sarayūtīre prabhūtadhanadhānyavān

translations.english: There is on the banks of the Sarayū a great and flourishing country called Kośala abounding in corn and wealth, in which the inhabitants passed their days pleasantly.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता
मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
ayodhyā nāma nagarī tatrāsīllokaviśrutā
manunā mānavendreṇa yā purī nirmitā svayam

translations.english: The capital of that country was Ayodhyā famed among men, which was founded by Manu himself that foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit:
आयता दश च द्वे च योजनानि महापुरी
श्रीमती त्रीणि विस्तीर्णा सुविभक्तमहापथा
verses.transliteration:
āyatā daśa ca dve ca yojanāni mahāpurī
śrīmatī trīṇi vistīrṇā suvibhaktamahāpathā

translations.english: That beautiful and mighty city was twelve Yojanas in length and Three in breadth; and was intersected outside with spacious roads laid out orderly.

verses.sanskrit:
राजमार्गेण महता सुविभक्तेन शोभिता
मुक्तपुष्पावकीर्णेन जलसिक्तेन नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
rājamārgeṇa mahatā suvibhaktena śobhitā
muktapuṣpāvakīrṇena jalasiktena nityaśaḥ

translations.english: And scattered with blown blossoms, and regularly sprinkled with water; the well-arranged broad high-ways looked beautiful.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु राजा दशरथो महाराष्ट्रविवर्धनः
पुरीमावासयामास दिवि देवपतिर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu rājā daśaratho mahārāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
purīmāvāsayāmāsa divi devapatiryathā

translations.english: That one bringing prosperity into great kingdoms, King Dasaratha, lived in that city, like that of the lord of the deities inhabiting the celestial regions.

verses.sanskrit:
कपाटतोरणवतीं सुविभक्तान्तरापणाम्
सर्वयन्त्रायुधवतीमुपेतां सर्वशिल्पिभिः
verses.transliteration:
kapāṭatoraṇavatīṁ suvibhaktāntarāpaṇām
sarvayantrāyudhavatīmupetāṁ sarvaśilpibhiḥ

translations.english: And the city was furnished with doors and gates, and well-arranged rows of shops. And it contained all kinds of instruments and arms, and was inhabited by all classes of artizans.

verses.sanskrit:
सूतमागधसंबाधां श्रीमतीमतुलप्रभाम्
उच्चाट्टालध्वजवतीं शतघ्नीशतसंकुलाम्
verses.transliteration:
sūtamāgadhasaṁbādhāṁ śrīmatīmatulaprabhām
uccāṭṭāladhvajavatīṁ śataghnīśatasaṁkulām

translations.english: And that graceful and matchlessly brilliant city abounded in eulogists and genealogists. And it was crowned with stately edifices with flags, and guarded by hundreds of Satāghnis. (A weapon commonly described as a stone set round with iron spiles).

verses.sanskrit:
वधूनाटकसङ्घैश्च संयुक्तां सर्वतः पुरीम्
उद्यानाम्रवणोपेतां महतीं सालमेखलाम्
verses.transliteration:
vadhūnāṭakasaṅghaiśca saṁyuktāṁ sarvataḥ purīm
udyānāmravaṇopetāṁ mahatīṁ sālamekhalām

translations.english: And the mighty city contained theatres for females, and gardens, and mango-groves; and was enclosed by a wall of såla trees.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्गगम्भीरपरिखां दुर्गामन्यैर्दुरासदाम्
वाजिवारणसंपूर्णां गोभिरुष्ट्रैः खरैस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
durgagambhīraparikhāṁ durgāmanyairdurāsadām
vājivāraṇasaṁpūrṇāṁ gobhiruṣṭraiḥ kharaistathā

translations.english: And encircled by a deep moat, the city was not accessible for enemies. And it abounded with elephants and horses, and kine and camels and asses.

verses.sanskrit:
सामन्तराजसङ्घैश्च बलिकर्मभिरावृताम्
नानादेशनिवासैश्च वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम्
verses.transliteration:
sāmantarājasaṅghaiśca balikarmabhirāvṛtām
nānādeśanivāsaiśca vaṇigbhirupaśobhitām

translations.english: It was thronged with neighbouring kings come to pay tribute, and inhabited by merchants from various countries.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादै रत्नविकृतैः पर्वतैरुपशोभिताम्
कूटागारैश्च संपूर्णामिन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम्
verses.transliteration:
prasādai ratnavikṛtaiḥ parvatairupaśobhitām
kūṭāgāraiśca saṁpūrṇāmindrasyevāmarāvatīm

translations.english: And adorned with mountain like palaces glittering with gems, and filled with sportingplaces for females, and like to Indra's Amarāvati.

verses.sanskrit:
चित्रामष्टापदाकारां वरनारीगणैर्युताम्
सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णां विमानगृहशोभिताम्
verses.transliteration:
citrāmaṣṭāpadākārāṁ varanārīgaṇairyutām
sarvaratnasamākīrṇāṁ vimānagṛhaśobhitām

translations.english: The city was wonderful to behold, gleaming with gold-burnished ornaments, and inhabited by troops of courtezans, and abounding in all kinds of gems, and graced with royal palaces.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहगाढामविच्छिद्रां समभूमौ निवेशिताम्
शालितण्डुलसंपूर्णामिक्षुकाण्डरसोदकाम्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhagāḍhāmavicchidrāṁ samabhūmau niveśitām
śālitaṇḍulasaṁpūrṇāmikṣukāṇḍarasodakām

translations.english: And it abounded in paddy and rice, and its water was sweet as the juice of the sugar-cane.

verses.sanskrit:
दुन्दुभीभिर्मृदङ्गैश्च वीणाभिः पणवैस्तथा
नादितां भृशमत्यर्थं पृथिव्यां तामनुत्तमाम्
verses.transliteration:
dundubhībhirmṛdaṅgaiśca vīṇābhiḥ paṇavaistathā
nāditāṁ bhṛśamatyarthaṁ pṛthivyāṁ tāmanuttamām

translations.english: And it resounded with the sounds of Dundubhis and Mrdargas and Viņās and Panavas.

verses.sanskrit:
विमानमिव सिद्धानां तपसाधिगतं दिवि
सुनिवेशितवेश्मान्तां नरोत्तमसमावृताम्
verses.transliteration:
vimānamiva siddhānāṁ tapasādhigataṁ divi
suniveśitaveśmāntāṁ narottamasamāvṛtām

translations.english: And that foremost spot of all the earth was like an aerial car obtained in heaven by the Siddhas, through force of ascetic austerities, and thronged with the best specimens of humanity.

verses.sanskrit:
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां मत्तानां नदतां वने
हन्तारो निशितैः शस्त्रैर्बलाद्बाहुबलैरपि
verses.transliteration:
siṁhavyāghravarāhāṇāṁ mattānāṁ nadatāṁ vane
hantāro niśitaiḥ śastrairbalādbāhubalairapi

translations.english: That city was filled by king Dasaratha with thousands of such Mahārathas light-handed and accomplished in fight, as could by force of arms or sharpened shafts slaughter infuriated lions and tigers and boars roaming in the forest; yet as would not pierce with arrows persons lorn or abandoned or hiding or fugitive. * A warrior coping with ten thousand persons, and protecting both his charioteer and steeds. A warrior fighting ten thousand Maharathas.

verses.sanskrit:
तामग्निमद्भिर्गुणवद्भिरावृतां; द्विजोत्तमैर्वेदषडङ्गपारगैः
सहस्रदैः सत्यरतैर्महात्मभि;र्महर्षिकल्पैरृषिभिश्च केवलैः
verses.transliteration:
tāmagnimadbhirguṇavadbhirāvṛtāṁ; dvijottamairvedaṣaḍaṅgapāragaiḥ
sahasradaiḥ satyaratairmahātmabhi;rmaharṣikalpairṛṣibhiśca kevalaiḥ

translations.english: It abounded mostly in excellent Brāhmaṇas, lighting the sacrificial fire, and crowned with qualities, and versed in the Vedas and the Vedāngas, and giving away thousands, and ever abiding by truth, and high-souled, and resembling might ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
पुर्यां तस्यामयोध्यायां वेदवित्सर्वसंग्रहः
दीर्घदर्शी महातेजाः पौरजानपदप्रियः
verses.transliteration:
puryāṁ tasyāmayodhyāyāṁ vedavitsarvasaṁgrahaḥ
dīrghadarśī mahātejāḥ paurajānapadapriyaḥ

translations.english: In that city of Ayodhyā resided king Dasaratha, versed in the Vedas, commanding all resources, far-sighted, of mighty prowess, dear to the inhabitants both rural and urban.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणामतिरथो यज्वा धर्मरतो वशी
महर्षिकल्पो राजर्षिस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāmatiratho yajvā dharmarato vaśī
maharṣikalpo rājarṣistriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ

translations.english: He was an Athiratha in the Ikşvāku line, performing sacrifices, engaged in the performance of duties, self-controlled like a Maharși, a royal saint famed in the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
बलवान्निहतामित्रो मित्रवान्विजितेन्द्रियः
धनैश्च संचयैश्चान्यैः शक्रवैश्रवणोपमः
verses.transliteration:
balavānnihatāmitro mitravānvijitendriyaḥ
dhanaiśca saṁcayaiścānyaiḥ śakravaiśravaṇopamaḥ

translations.english: He possessed of strength, the destroyer of foes, having friends, of subdued senses, comparable to ſakra and Vaiśravaņa by virtue of accumulated riches and other possessions.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा मनुर्महातेजा लोकस्य परिरक्षिता
तथा दशरथो राजा वसञ्जगदपालयत्
verses.transliteration:
yathā manurmahātejā lokasya parirakṣitā
tathā daśaratho rājā vasañjagadapālayat

translations.english: As the highly-powerful Manu protected the people, Dasaratha did the same.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन सत्याभिसंधेन त्रिवर्गमनुतिष्ठता
पालिता सा पुरी श्रेष्ठेन्द्रेण इवामरावती
verses.transliteration:
tena satyābhisaṁdhena trivargamanutiṣṭhatā
pālitā sā purī śreṣṭhendreṇa ivāmarāvatī

translations.english: As Indra rules Amarāvatī, that one firm in promise, and following duty, profit, and pleasure, ruled that best of cities.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्पुरवरे हृष्टा धर्मात्मना बहुश्रुताः
नरास्तुष्टाधनैः स्वैः स्वैरलुब्धाः सत्यवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
tasminpuravare hṛṣṭā dharmātmanā bahuśrutāḥ
narāstuṣṭādhanaiḥ svaiḥ svairalubdhāḥ satyavādinaḥ

translations.english: In that excellent city, the men were happy and righteous-souled, and widely-read, and each contented with his possessions, and devoid of covetousness, and speaking the truth.

verses.sanskrit:
नाल्पसंनिचयः कश्चिदासीत्तस्मिन्पुरोत्तमे
कुटुम्बी यो ह्यसिद्धार्थोऽगवाश्वधनधान्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
nālpasaṁnicayaḥ kaścidāsīttasminpurottame
kuṭumbī yo hyasiddhārtho'gavāśvadhanadhānyavān

translations.english: In that prime of cities, there was none who had not at his command a plenteous supply of the good things, and there was no householder who was not well off in horses and kine, and corn and wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
कामी वा न कदर्यो वा नृशंसः पुरुषः क्वचित्
द्रष्टुं शक्यमयोध्यायां नाविद्वान्न च नास्तिकः
verses.transliteration:
kāmī vā na kadaryo vā nṛśaṁsaḥ puruṣaḥ kvacit
draṣṭuṁ śakyamayodhyāyāṁ nāvidvānna ca nāstikaḥ

translations.english: And one could see nowhere in Ayodhyā persons given up to lust, or unsightly, or crooked-minded, or unlettered, or atheistical.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे नराश्च नार्यश्च धर्मशीलाः सुसंयताः
मुदिताः शीलवृत्ताभ्यां महर्षय इवामलाः
verses.transliteration:
sarve narāśca nāryaśca dharmaśīlāḥ susaṁyatāḥ
muditāḥ śīlavṛttābhyāṁ maharṣaya ivāmalāḥ

translations.english: And all the men and all the women were of excellent character, and subdued senses, and a happy frame of mind, and both on respect of occupation and conduct spotless like to the Maharsis.

verses.sanskrit:
नाकुण्डली नामुकुटी नास्रग्वी नाल्पभोगवान्
नामृष्टो नानुलिप्ताङ्गो नासुगन्धश्च विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
nākuṇḍalī nāmukuṭī nāsragvī nālpabhogavān
nāmṛṣṭo nānuliptāṅgo nāsugandhaśca vidyate

translations.english: And all wore ear-rings and tiaras and garlands, and abundantly enjoyed the good things of life. And all were clean, daubing their limbs, and perfuming their persons.

verses.sanskrit:
नामृष्टभोजी नादाता नाप्यनङ्गदनिष्कधृक्
नाहस्ताभरणो वापि दृश्यते नाप्यनात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
nāmṛṣṭabhojī nādātā nāpyanaṅgadaniṣkadhṛk
nāhastābharaṇo vāpi dṛśyate nāpyanātmavān

translations.english: And feeding on pure food, and giving away, and wearing Angadas (A bracelet worn upon the upper arm) and Niskas (An ornament for the breast or neck.) and hand-ornaments, and repressing passions.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाहिताग्निर्नायज्वा विप्रो नाप्यसहस्रदः
कश्चिदासीदयोध्यायां न च निर्वृत्तसंकरः
verses.transliteration:
nānāhitāgnirnāyajvā vipro nāpyasahasradaḥ
kaścidāsīdayodhyāyāṁ na ca nirvṛttasaṁkaraḥ

translations.english: There were not on Ayodhyā persons not lighting the sacrificial fire, or not performing sacrifices, or mean-minded, or thieving, or engaged in improper occupations, or of impure descent.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वकर्मनिरता नित्यं ब्राह्मणा विजितेन्द्रियाः
दानाध्ययनशीलाश्च संयताश्च प्रतिग्रहे
verses.transliteration:
svakarmaniratā nityaṁ brāhmaṇā vijitendriyāḥ
dānādhyayanaśīlāśca saṁyatāśca pratigrahe

translations.english: The Brāhmaṇas of subdued senses were always engaged in the performance of their own duties, giving away in charity, and studying, and receiving gifts with discrimination.

verses.sanskrit:
न नास्तिको नानृतको न कश्चिदबहुश्रुतः
नासूयको न चाशक्तो नाविद्वान्विद्यते तदा
verses.transliteration:
na nāstiko nānṛtako na kaścidabahuśrutaḥ
nāsūyako na cāśakto nāvidvānvidyate tadā

translations.english: None of them was atheistical or untruthful or be reft of hearing scriptures or detracting or incompetent or illiterate.

verses.sanskrit:
न दीनः क्षिप्तचित्तो वा व्यथितो वापि कश्चन
कश्चिन्नरो वा नारी वा नाश्रीमान्नाप्यरूपवान्
द्रष्टुं शक्यमयोध्यायां नापि राजन्यभक्तिमान्
verses.transliteration:
na dīnaḥ kṣiptacitto vā vyathito vāpi kaścana
kaścinnaro vā nārī vā nāśrīmānnāpyarūpavān
draṣṭuṁ śakyamayodhyāyāṁ nāpi rājanyabhaktimān

translations.english: And no man and no woman was seen devoid of grace or beauty, or lacking in reverence for their monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
वर्णेष्वग्र्यचतुर्थेषु देवतातिथिपूजकाः
दीर्घायुषो नराः सर्वे धर्मं सत्यं च संश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
varṇeṣvagryacaturtheṣu devatātithipūjakāḥ
dīrghāyuṣo narāḥ sarve dharmaṁ satyaṁ ca saṁśritāḥ

translations.english: The four orders with Brāhmanas at their head contained persons serving gods and guests, and endowed with gratitude, and munificent, and heroic, and possessing prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रं ब्रह्ममुखं चासीद्वैश्याः क्षत्रमनुव्रताः
शूद्राः स्वधर्मनिरतास्त्रीन्वर्णानुपचारिणः
verses.transliteration:
kṣatraṁ brahmamukhaṁ cāsīdvaiśyāḥ kṣatramanuvratāḥ
śūdrāḥ svadharmaniratāstrīnvarṇānupacāriṇaḥ

translations.english: The Kşatriyas were obedient the Brahmanas, and the Vaisyas followed the Kșatriyas, and the sadras, occupied with their proper vocations, ministered to the three other orders.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तेनेक्ष्वाकुनाथेन पुरी सुपरिरक्षिता
यथा पुरस्तान्मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण धीमता
verses.transliteration:
sā tenekṣvākunāthena purī suparirakṣitā
yathā purastānmanunā mānavendreṇa dhīmatā

translations.english: That city was ably govered by Dasaratha that lord of Ikşvāku's line, even as that foremost of men, the intelligent Manu, had governed it before him.

verses.sanskrit:
योधानामग्निकल्पानां पेशलानाममर्षिणाम्
संपूर्णाकृतविद्यानां गुहाकेसरिणामिव
verses.transliteration:
yodhānāmagnikalpānāṁ peśalānāmamarṣiṇām
saṁpūrṇākṛtavidyānāṁ guhākesariṇāmiva

translations.english: And as a mountain-cavern abounds with lions, it was filled with warriors resembling flaming fire, of straight ways, unforbearing, and of accomplished learning. to

verses.sanskrit:
काम्बोजविषये जातैर्बाह्लीकैश्च हयोत्तमैः
वनायुजैर्नदीजैश्च पूर्णाहरिहयोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
kāmbojaviṣaye jātairbāhlīkaiśca hayottamaiḥ
vanāyujairnadījaiśca pūrṇāharihayopamaiḥ

translations.english: And the city abounded with excellent horses sprung in Kamboja, and Vahlika, and Vanayu, and the banks of the Sindhu, and like to that best of horses, Hari's charger.

verses.sanskrit:
विन्ध्यपर्वतजैर्मत्तैः पूर्णा हैमवतैरपि
मदान्वितैरतिबलैर्मातङ्गैः पर्वतोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
vindhyaparvatajairmattaiḥ pūrṇā haimavatairapi
madānvitairatibalairmātaṅgaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ

translations.english: With fierce elephants sprung on the Vindhya mountain, and the Himavat, filled with juice, and of exceeding strength, and resembling hills.

verses.sanskrit:
अञ्जनादपि निष्क्रान्तैर्वामनादपि च द्विपैः
भद्रमन्द्रैर्भद्रमृगैर्मृगमन्द्रैश्च सा पुरी
verses.transliteration:
añjanādapi niṣkrāntairvāmanādapi ca dvipaiḥ
bhadramandrairbhadramṛgairmṛgamandraiśca sā purī

translations.english: And with Bhadra, Mandra, and Mrga* elephants; and those sprung from the mixture of the three, and from the mixture of Bhadra and Mandra, and froin Bhadra and Mrga, and from Mrga and Mandra, superior like to Airāvata, and coming from Mahapaama, Anjana, and Vamana breeds, fierce, and looking like hills. And that city was over two Yojanas; and truly it was called Ayodhya. (incapable of being conquered.) *(Those elephants whose limbs are contracted are bhadras; those whose bodies are fat, slack, and contracted are Mandras: and those whose bodies are lean and large are Mrgas.)

verses.sanskrit:
तां सत्यनामां दृढतोरणार्गला;म्गृहैर्विचित्रैरुपशोभितां शिवाम्
पुरीमयोध्यां नृसहस्रसंकुलां; शशास वै शक्रसमो महीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ satyanāmāṁ dṛḍhatoraṇārgalā;mgṛhairvicitrairupaśobhitāṁ śivām
purīmayodhyāṁ nṛsahasrasaṁkulāṁ; śaśāsa vai śakrasamo mahīpatiḥ

translations.english: Repressing enemies, that city was governed by the great and the exceedingly. And that lord of earth resembling Sakra govemed that city of Ayodhya bearing a true name furnished with strong gates and bolts, and auspicious, and graced with excellent edifices, and teeming with thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
अष्टौ बभूवुर्वीरस्य तस्यामात्या यशस्विनः
शुचयश्चानुरक्ताश्च राजकृत्येषु नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
aṣṭau babhūvurvīrasya tasyāmātyā yaśasvinaḥ
śucayaścānuraktāśca rājakṛtyeṣu nityaśaḥ

translations.english: That high-souled one of Ikşvāku's line had competent counsellors, capable of administering business, of diving into the motives of others, and ever intent upon the good of the monarch. And that heroic king had eight famous Counsellors, pure and devoted to the royal service.

verses.sanskrit:
धृष्टिर्जयन्तो विजयः सिद्धार्थो अर्थसाधकः
अशोको मन्त्रपालश्च सुमन्त्रश्चाष्टमोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
dhṛṣṭirjayanto vijayaḥ siddhārtho arthasādhakaḥ
aśoko mantrapālaśca sumantraścāṣṭamo'bhavat

translations.english: They were, Dhrsti, Jayanta, and Vijaya, and Surăştra, and Răstravardhana, and Akopa and Dharmapala, and Sumantra the cight, conversant with profit.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋत्विजौ द्वावभिमतौ तस्यास्तामृषिसत्तमौ
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च मन्त्रिणश्च तथापरे
verses.transliteration:
ṛtvijau dvāvabhimatau tasyāstāmṛṣisattamau
vasiṣṭho vāmadevaśca mantriṇaśca tathāpare

translations.english: And he had two family priests beloved to him; viz., those foremost of saints. Vasistha and Vamadeva.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामविदितं किंचित्स्वेषु नास्ति परेषु वा
क्रियमाणं कृतं वापि चारेणापि चिकीर्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmaviditaṁ kiṁcitsveṣu nāsti pareṣu vā
kriyamāṇaṁ kṛtaṁ vāpi cāreṇāpi cikīrṣitam

translations.english: And they were not unknown to what was done or sought to be done in the midst of their own or a hostile party. And they were adept in intercourse with people, and well-tried in friendship by the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
कोशसंग्रहणे युक्ता बलस्य च परिग्रहे
अहितं चापि पुरुषं न विहिंस्युरदूषकम्
verses.transliteration:
kośasaṁgrahaṇe yuktā balasya ca parigrahe
ahitaṁ cāpi puruṣaṁ na vihiṁsyuradūṣakam

translations.english: And they were ever busy in replenishing the exchequer and in levying troops. And they did not cherish ill will even towards enemies, when innocent.

verses.sanskrit:
वीराश्च नियतोत्साहा राजशास्त्रमनुष्ठिताः
शुचीनां रक्षितारश्च नित्यं विषयवासिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
vīrāśca niyatotsāhā rājaśāstramanuṣṭhitāḥ
śucīnāṁ rakṣitāraśca nityaṁ viṣayavāsinām

translations.english: And they were heroic, and ever high-spirited, following policy, and protecting those citizens that were pure.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रमहिंसन्तस्ते कोशं समपूरयन्
सुतीक्ष्णदण्डाः संप्रेक्ष्य पुरुषस्य बलाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
brahmakṣatramahiṁsantaste kośaṁ samapūrayan
sutīkṣṇadaṇḍāḥ saṁprekṣya puruṣasya balābalam

translations.english: And not bearing ill will towards Brahmaņas and Khatriyas, and filling the treasury, by inflicting punishments according lo the offences of the persons guilty.

verses.sanskrit:
शुचीनामेकबुद्धीनां सर्वेषां संप्रजानताम्
नासीत्पुरे वा राष्ट्रे वा मृषावादी नरः क्वचित्
verses.transliteration:
śucīnāmekabuddhīnāṁ sarveṣāṁ saṁprajānatām
nāsītpure vā rāṣṭre vā mṛṣāvādī naraḥ kvacit

translations.english: And during the time when those pure ones of one mind presided over the justice of the kingdom, there was neither in the city nor the provinces any that was a liar, or 'wicked, or going after others' wives. And peace reigned all around the city and the provinces.

verses.sanskrit:
सुवाससः सुवेशाश्च ते च सर्वे सुशीलिनः
हितार्थं च नरेन्द्रस्य जाग्रतो नयचक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
suvāsasaḥ suveśāśca te ca sarve suśīlinaḥ
hitārthaṁ ca narendrasya jāgrato nayacakṣuṣā

translations.english: And the ministers wore excellent raiment, and ornaments, and were engaged in observing pure Vows, and ever kept their eye of policy open in the interest of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
गुरौ गुणगृहीताश्च प्रख्याताश्च पराक्रमैः
विदेशेष्वपि विज्ञाताः सर्वतो बुद्धिनिश्चयात्
verses.transliteration:
gurau guṇagṛhītāśca prakhyātāśca parākramaiḥ
videśeṣvapi vijñātāḥ sarvato buddhiniścayāt

translations.english: And the king considered them as crowned with virtues, and they were famed on account of their prowess, concluding unerringly in consequence of their intelligence of other countries. And in all climes and times they could manifest their noble qualities.

verses.sanskrit:
ईदृशैस्तैरमात्यैस्तु राजा दशरथोऽनघः
उपपन्नो गुणोपेतैरन्वशासद्वसुंधराम्
verses.transliteration:
īdṛśaistairamātyaistu rājā daśaratho'naghaḥ
upapanno guṇopetairanvaśāsadvasuṁdharām

translations.english: Surrounded by such counseliors endowed with various qualities, the faultless king Dasaratha ruled the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अवेक्षमाणश्चारेण प्रजा धर्मेण रञ्जयन्
नाध्यगच्छद्विशिष्टं वा तुल्यं वा शत्रुमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
