avekṣamāṇaścāreṇa prajā dharmeṇa rañjayan
nādhyagacchadviśiṣṭaṁ vā tulyaṁ vā śatrumātmanaḥ

translations.english: Nor did he ever meet with a foe that was either his equal or superior. And possessed of friends, and having obedient commanders, and extricating his thorns by his might, that king ruled the earth, even as the lord of celestials rules heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रहितैर्निविष्टै;र्वृतोऽनुरक्तैः कुशलैः समर्थैः
स पार्थिवो दीप्तिमवाप युक्त;स्तेजोमयैर्गोभिरिवोदितोऽर्कः
verses.transliteration:
tairmantribhirmantrahitairniviṣṭai;rvṛto'nuraktaiḥ kuśalaiḥ samarthaiḥ
sa pārthivo dīptimavāpa yukta;stejomayairgobhirivodito'rkaḥ

translations.english: And surrounded by those counsellors studious of his welfare, and bearing affection towards him, and clever, and competent, that king, by virtue of his prowess in subduing others, resembled the sun surrounded by his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य त्वेवं प्रभावस्य धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मनः
सुतार्थं तप्यमानस्य नासीद्वंशकरः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tvevaṁ prabhāvasya dharmajñasya mahātmanaḥ
sutārthaṁ tapyamānasya nāsīdvaṁśakaraḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: And although engaged in austerities with the view of having sons born to him, the powerful and high-souled king, had no son capable of perpetuating his race.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयानस्य तस्यैवं बुद्धिरासीन्महात्मनः
सुतार्थं वाजिमेधेन किमर्थं न यजाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
cintayānasya tasyaivaṁ buddhirāsīnmahātmanaḥ
sutārthaṁ vājimedhena kimarthaṁ na yajāmyaham

translations.english: Mentally turning the matter over, the highsouled one thought, Why do I not celebrate a horse-sacrifice with the intention of obtaining a son?

verses.sanskrit:
स निश्चितां मतिं कृत्वा यष्टव्यमिति बुद्धिमान्
मन्त्रिभिः सह धर्मात्मा सर्वैरेव कृतात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
sa niścitāṁ matiṁ kṛtvā yaṣṭavyamiti buddhimān
mantribhiḥ saha dharmātmā sarvaireva kṛtātmabhiḥ

translations.english: That highly-energetic, pious and intelligent monarch, in consultation with all his counsellors of sedate minds, having made up his mind to celebrate the sacrifice, said to that best of counsellors, Sumantra, Do you speedily summon my spiritual guides, along with the family priests.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा रहः सूतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
ऋत्विग्भिरुपदिष्टोऽयं पुरावृत्तो मया श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā rahaḥ sūto rājānamidamabravīt
ṛtvigbhirupadiṣṭo'yaṁ purāvṛtto mayā śrutaḥ

translations.english: Hearing all about it, the king's charioteer addressed the monarch in private, saying, Do you listen to what is related in the Purānas, and to what I have heard myself!

verses.sanskrit:
सनत्कुमारो भगवान्पूर्वं कथितवान्कथाम्
ऋषीणां संनिधौ राजंस्तव पुत्रागमं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
sanatkumāro bhagavānpūrvaṁ kathitavānkathām
ṛṣīṇāṁ saṁnidhau rājaṁstava putrāgamaṁ prati

translations.english: This horse-sacrifice is enjoined by the family priests; and I have myself heard the following story celebrated in ancient chronicle. And what the worshipful Sanatkumāra had said formerly in the presence of the saints, applies, O king, to the case of your having a son.

verses.sanskrit:
काश्यपस्य तु पुत्रोऽस्ति विभाण्डक इति श्रुतः
ऋश्यशृङ्ग इति ख्यातस्तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
kāśyapasya tu putro'sti vibhāṇḍaka iti śrutaḥ
ṛśyaśṛṅga iti khyātastasya putro bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Kaśyapa has a son known by the name of Vibhāņdaka. He will get a son called Rșyasſiga. And he will grow up and pass his days in the forests.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वैविध्यं ब्रह्मचर्यस्य भविष्यति महात्मनः
लोकेषु प्रथितं राजन्विप्रैश्च कथितं सदा
verses.transliteration:
dvaividhyaṁ brahmacaryasya bhaviṣyati mahātmanaḥ
lokeṣu prathitaṁ rājanvipraiśca kathitaṁ sadā

translations.english: And that foremost of Brāhmaṇas will not know anything else save following his father. And, O king, it is rumoured abroad, and also always said by the Vipras, that the high-souled one will practise (Those that assume the staff and the kamaņdalu are reckoned the first order; while those that continue to live with their wives are considered as next in worth.) the two modes of Brahmacarya life.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य व्यतिक्रमाद्राज्ञो भविष्यति सुदारुणा
अनावृष्टिः सुघोरा वै सर्वभूतभयावहा
verses.transliteration:
tasya vyatikramādrājño bhaviṣyati sudāruṇā
anāvṛṣṭiḥ sughorā vai sarvabhūtabhayāvahā

translations.english: And he spent some time in serving the sacrificial fire and his famous sire. At this time, the powerful Romapāda of exceeding strength will be famed as king of the Angas. And in consequence of some default on his part, there will occur in his kingdom a terrible and dreadful drought, capable of striking terror in the all.

verses.sanskrit:
अनावृष्ट्यां तु वृत्तायां राजा दुःखसमन्वितः
ब्राह्मणाञ्श्रुतवृद्धांश्च समानीय प्रवक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
anāvṛṣṭyāṁ tu vṛttāyāṁ rājā duḥkhasamanvitaḥ
brāhmaṇāñśrutavṛddhāṁśca samānīya pravakṣyati

translations.english: And filled with grief on account of this drought, the king will call about him Vedaaccomplished Brāhmaṇas, and speak to them, saying, You are conversant with the Vedic ritual and the social duties. Do therefore, tell me how to expiate for this evil.

verses.sanskrit:
वक्ष्यन्ति ते महीपालं ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः
विभाण्डकसुतं राजन्सर्वोपायैरिहानय
verses.transliteration:
vakṣyanti te mahīpālaṁ brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
vibhāṇḍakasutaṁ rājansarvopāyairihānaya

translations.english: Thus accosted by the king, those excellent Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas, will say to the ruler of earth.

verses.sanskrit:
आनाय्य च महीपाल ऋश्यशृङ्गं सुसत्कृतम्
प्रयच्छ कन्यां शान्तां वै विधिना सुसमाहितः
verses.transliteration:
ānāyya ca mahīpāla ṛśyaśṛṅgaṁ susatkṛtam
prayaccha kanyāṁ śāntāṁ vai vidhinā susamāhitaḥ

translations.english: Do you, O monarch, by all means, bring Vibhandaka's son. And having, Oking, brought that Brāhmaṇa versed in the Vedas, Vibhandaka's son Rsyaśộnga, and duly honoured him, do you, O monarch, with a concentrated mind, perform the betrothal of your daughter śāntā, with him according to the ordinance.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा चिन्तां प्रपत्स्यते
केनोपायेन वै शक्यमिहानेतुं स वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tu vacanaṁ śrutvā rājā cintāṁ prapatsyate
kenopāyena vai śakyamihānetuṁ sa vīryavān

translations.english: And hearing those words of theirs, the king will began to think as to how he can bring over that one endowed with energy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राजा विनिश्चित्य सह मन्त्रिभिरात्मवान्
पुरोहितममात्यांश्च प्रेषयिष्यति सत्कृतान्
verses.transliteration:
tato rājā viniścitya saha mantribhirātmavān
purohitamamātyāṁśca preṣayiṣyati satkṛtān

translations.english: Then in consultation with his counsellors, the prudent king having come to a conclusion will, honouring them duly, desire his priest and his courtiers to set out in quest of Rsyaśộnga.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु राज्ञो वचः श्रुत्वा व्यथिता वनताननाः
न गच्छेम ऋषेर्भीता अनुनेष्यन्ति तं नृपम्
verses.transliteration:
te tu rājño vacaḥ śrutvā vyathitā vanatānanāḥ
na gacchema ṛṣerbhītā anuneṣyanti taṁ nṛpam

translations.english: Thereupon hearing the king's words, with aggrieved hearts, and with heads hanging down, they will beseech the monarch, saying, Afraid of the saint, Vibhāndaka, we shall not be able to repair thither.

verses.sanskrit:
वक्ष्यन्ति चिन्तयित्वा ते तस्योपायांश्च तान्क्षमान्
आनेष्यामो वयं विप्रं न च दोषो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vakṣyanti cintayitvā te tasyopāyāṁśca tānkṣamān
āneṣyāmo vayaṁ vipraṁ na ca doṣo bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Anon hitting upon the appropriate means, they say, 'We will search for the Vipra, and no blame shall accrue to us.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमङ्गाधिपेनैव गणिकाभिरृषेः सुतः
आनीतोऽवर्षयद्देवः शान्ता चास्मै प्रदीयते
verses.transliteration:
evamaṅgādhipenaiva gaṇikābhirṛṣeḥ sutaḥ
ānīto'varṣayaddevaḥ śāntā cāsmai pradīyate

translations.english: Thus by help of courtesans, the saint's son was brought by the lord of the Angas. And then the god (Indra) poured down showers; and the king conferred on him śānta.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्गस्तु जामाता पुत्रांस्तव विधास्यति
सनत्कुमारकथितमेतावद्व्याहृतं मया
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyaśṛṅgastu jāmātā putrāṁstava vidhāsyati
sanatkumārakathitametāvadvyāhṛtaṁ mayā

translations.english: And now your son-in-law Rşyaśộnga will help you in obtaining a son. Now I have related to you what Sanatkumāra had communicated.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ हृष्टो दशरथः सुमन्त्रं प्रत्यभाषत
यथर्ष्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीतो विस्तरेण त्वयोच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
atha hṛṣṭo daśarathaḥ sumantraṁ pratyabhāṣata
yatharṣyaśṛṅgastvānīto vistareṇa tvayocyatām

translations.english: Thereupon king Dasaratha, well pleased, asked Sumantra, Do you now tell me by what means Rşyaśộnga was brought over (by the lord of the Angas).

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रश्चोदितो राज्ञा प्रोवाचेदं वचस्तदा
यथर्ष्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीतः शृणु मे मन्त्रिभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
sumantraścodito rājñā provācedaṁ vacastadā
yatharṣyaśṛṅgastvānītaḥ śṛṇu me mantribhiḥ saha

translations.english: Thus asked by the king, Sumantra said these words-I will relate to you how the counsellors brought Rşyaśộnga. Do you listen with your counsellors!

verses.sanskrit:
लोमपादमुवाचेदं सहामात्यः पुरोहितः
उपायो निरपायोऽयमस्माभिरभिचिन्तितः
verses.transliteration:
lomapādamuvācedaṁ sahāmātyaḥ purohitaḥ
upāyo nirapāyo'yamasmābhirabhicintitaḥ

translations.english: The priest together with the counsellors spoke to Romapada, saying, 'The means that we have hit upon can never fail of effect.'

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्गो वनचरस्तपःस्वाध्यायने रतः
अनभिज्ञः स नारीणां विषयाणां सुखस्य च
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyaśṛṅgo vanacarastapaḥsvādhyāyane rataḥ
anabhijñaḥ sa nārīṇāṁ viṣayāṇāṁ sukhasya ca

translations.english: Rşyaśộnga has been brought up in woods; and is engaged in austerities and the study of the Vedas. He is ignorant of the pleasure that ensues from contact with women,

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियार्थैरभिमतैर्नरचित्तप्रमाथिभिः
पुरमानाययिष्यामः क्षिप्रं चाध्यवसीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
indriyārthairabhimatairnaracittapramāthibhiḥ
puramānāyayiṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṁ cādhyavasīyatām

translations.english: By help of things agreeably ministering to the sense, and ravishing the soul, we shall bring him to the city. Do you, therefore, arrange for them!

verses.sanskrit:
गणिकास्तत्र गच्छन्तु रूपवत्यः स्वलंकृताः
प्रलोभ्य विविधोपायैरानेष्यन्तीह सत्कृताः
verses.transliteration:
gaṇikāstatra gacchantu rūpavatyaḥ svalaṁkṛtāḥ
pralobhya vividhopāyairāneṣyantīha satkṛtāḥ

translations.english: Let courtezans of comely presence, clad in ornaments, repair thither. And if well treated, they will by various means bring him here.'

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तथेति राजा च प्रत्युवाच पुरोहितम्
पुरोहितो मन्त्रिणश्च तथा चक्रुश्च ते तदा
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tatheti rājā ca pratyuvāca purohitam
purohito mantriṇaśca tathā cakruśca te tadā

translations.english: Hearing this, the king said to the priest, 'So be it!' Then the priest and courtiers acted accordingly.

verses.sanskrit:
वारमुख्यास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा वनं प्रविविशुर्महत्
आश्रमस्याविदूरेऽस्मिन्यत्नं कुर्वन्ति दर्शने
ऋषिपुत्रस्य घोरस्य नित्यमाश्रमवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
vāramukhyāstu tacchrutvā vanaṁ praviviśurmahat
āśramasyāvidūre'sminyatnaṁ kurvanti darśane
ṛṣiputrasya ghorasya nityamāśramavāsinaḥ

translations.english: In accordance with the instructions, the courtezans entered that great forest; and remaining at some distance from the hermitage, endeavoured to meet with the sober son of the saint ever dwelling in the woods. And satisfied with serving his sire, he never strayed from the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
न तेन जन्मप्रभृति दृष्टपूर्वं तपस्विना
स्त्री वा पुमान्वा यच्चान्यत्सत्त्वं नगरराष्ट्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
na tena janmaprabhṛti dṛṣṭapūrvaṁ tapasvinā
strī vā pumānvā yaccānyatsattvaṁ nagararāṣṭrajam

translations.english: Since his birth he had never before seen men and women, or any other creatures living in cities and towns.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कदाचित्तं देशमाजगाम यदृच्छया
विभाण्डकसुतस्तत्र ताश्चापश्यद्वराङ्गनाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kadācittaṁ deśamājagāma yadṛcchayā
vibhāṇḍakasutastatra tāścāpaśyadvarāṅganāḥ

translations.english: It came to pass that on one occasion, walking about at will, Vibhandaka's son came to that spot and beheld the courtezans.

verses.sanskrit:
ताश्चित्रवेषाः प्रमदा गायन्त्यो मधुरस्वरैः
ऋषिपुत्रमुपागम्य सर्वा वचनमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tāścitraveṣāḥ pramadā gāyantyo madhurasvaraiḥ
ṛṣiputramupāgamya sarvā vacanamabruvan

translations.english: Colourfully attired, and singing sweet songs, the women came to the saint's son and said.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्त्वं किं वर्तसे ब्रह्मञ्ज्ञातुमिच्छामहे वयम्
एकस्त्वं विजने घोरे वने चरसि शंस नः
verses.transliteration:
kastvaṁ kiṁ vartase brahmañjñātumicchāmahe vayam
ekastvaṁ vijane ghore vane carasi śaṁsa naḥ

translations.english: Who are you? And where are you going, O Brahman? We wish to learn all this. And why is it that you range alone this far-off forest?

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टरूपास्तास्तेन काम्यरूपा वने स्त्रियः
हार्दात्तस्य मतिर्जाता आख्यातुं पितरं स्वकम्
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭarūpāstāstena kāmyarūpā vane striyaḥ
hārdāttasya matirjātā ākhyātuṁ pitaraṁ svakam

translations.english: Beholding these beautiful damsels never seen before, he from delight, hastened to inform them of his lineage.

verses.sanskrit:
पिता विभाण्डकोऽस्माकं तस्याहं सुत औरसः
ऋश्यशृङ्ग इति ख्यातं नाम कर्म च मे भुवि
verses.transliteration:
pitā vibhāṇḍako'smākaṁ tasyāhaṁ suta aurasaḥ
ṛśyaśṛṅga iti khyātaṁ nāma karma ca me bhuvi

translations.english: My father is Vibhăndaka; and I am his son. My name is Rşyasſiga and my occupation is known the world over.

verses.sanskrit:
इहाश्रमपदोऽस्माकं समीपे शुभदर्शनाः
करिष्ये वोऽत्र पूजां वै सर्वेषां विधिपूर्वकम्
verses.transliteration:
ihāśramapado'smākaṁ samīpe śubhadarśanāḥ
kariṣye vo'tra pūjāṁ vai sarveṣāṁ vidhipūrvakam

translations.english: This auspicious hermitage hard by belongs to us; and there I shall receive you all in due form O' lovely ones!.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिपुत्रवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वासां मतिरास वै
तदाश्रमपदं द्रष्टुं जग्मुः सर्वाश्च तेन ह
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣiputravacaḥ śrutvā sarvāsāṁ matirāsa vai
tadāśramapadaṁ draṣṭuṁ jagmuḥ sarvāśca tena ha

translations.english: Hearing the words of the saint's son, they all consented, and the women went to behold that asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
गतानां तु ततः पूजामृषिपुत्रश्चकार ह
इदमर्घ्यमिदं पाद्यमिदं मूलं फलं च नः
verses.transliteration:
gatānāṁ tu tataḥ pūjāmṛṣiputraścakāra ha
idamarghyamidaṁ pādyamidaṁ mūlaṁ phalaṁ ca naḥ

translations.english: When they had come there, the saint's son received them hospitably, saying, 'Here is Arghya,' 'Here is water for washing the feet,' 'Here are fruits and roots.'

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजां सर्वा एव समुत्सुकाः
ऋषेर्भीताश्च शीघ्रं तु गमनाय मतिं दधुः
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya tu tāṁ pūjāṁ sarvā eva samutsukāḥ
ṛṣerbhītāśca śīghraṁ tu gamanāya matiṁ dadhuḥ

translations.english: And thereupon they readily received his hospitality. And actuated by the fear of the saint, Vibhāndaka, they bent their minds upon departing soon.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माकमपि मुख्यानि फलानीमानि वै द्विज
गृहाण प्रति भद्रं ते भक्षयस्व च मा चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
asmākamapi mukhyāni phalānīmāni vai dvija
gṛhāṇa prati bhadraṁ te bhakṣayasva ca mā ciram

translations.english: They said, Do you also, O twice-born one, receive from us these excellent fruits! O Vipra! good betide you, eat them without delay.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तास्तं समालिङ्ग्य सर्वा हर्षसमन्विताः
मोदकान्प्रददुस्तस्मै भक्ष्यांश्च विविधाञ्शुभान्
verses.transliteration:
tatastāstaṁ samāliṅgya sarvā harṣasamanvitāḥ
modakānpradadustasmai bhakṣyāṁśca vividhāñśubhān

translations.english: Thereupon, embracing him joyfully, they gave him sweetmeats and various kinds of savoury viands.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि चास्वाद्य तेजस्वी फलानीति स्म मन्यते
अनास्वादितपूर्वाणि वने नित्यनिवासिना
verses.transliteration:
tāni cāsvādya tejasvī phalānīti sma manyate
anāsvāditapūrvāṇi vane nityanivāsinā

translations.english: And tasting those things, the glorious one took them for fruits, never tasted before by the dwellers of the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
आपृच्छ्य च तदा विप्रं व्रतचर्यां निवेद्य च
गच्छन्ति स्मापदेशात्ता भीतास्तस्य पितुः स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
āpṛcchya ca tadā vipraṁ vratacaryāṁ nivedya ca
gacchanti smāpadeśāttā bhītāstasya pituḥ striyaḥ

translations.english: Then, having accosted him the women, feigning the observance of some vow, went away, inspired with the fear of his father.

verses.sanskrit:
गतासु तासु सर्वासु काश्यपस्यात्मजो द्विजः
अस्वस्थहृदयश्चासीद्दुःखं स्म परिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
gatāsu tāsu sarvāsu kāśyapasyātmajo dvijaḥ
asvasthahṛdayaścāsīdduḥkhaṁ sma parivartate

translations.english: And when they had gone, that twice-born one, Kasyapa's son, became sad, and suffered from grief of heart and became restless due to sadness.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽपरेद्युस्तं देशमाजगाम स वीर्यवान्
मनोज्ञा यत्र ता दृष्टा वारमुख्याः स्वलंकृताः
verses.transliteration:
tato'paredyustaṁ deśamājagāma sa vīryavān
manojñā yatra tā dṛṣṭā vāramukhyāḥ svalaṁkṛtāḥ

translations.english: And the next day his mind momentarily running upon it, the graceful son of Vibhāņdaka, endowed with prowess, came to that spot where he had encountered the comely courtesans, adorned with ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वैव च तदा विप्रमायान्तं हृष्टमानसाः
उपसृत्य ततः सर्वास्तास्तमूचुरिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvaiva ca tadā vipramāyāntaṁ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
upasṛtya tataḥ sarvāstāstamūcuridaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: As soon as they observed him coming, they came forward, and said, Do you, O Brāhmaṇa, come into our hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तासां सर्वासां हृदयंगमम्
गमनाय मतिं चक्रे तं च निन्युस्तदा स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu vacanaṁ tāsāṁ sarvāsāṁ hṛdayaṁgamam
gamanāya matiṁ cakre taṁ ca ninyustadā striyaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon hearing those words of theirs capable of influencing the heart, he became bent upon going, and the women brought him away.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र चानीयमाने तु विप्रे तस्मिन्महात्मनि
ववर्ष सहसा देवो जगत्प्रह्लादयंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tatra cānīyamāne tu vipre tasminmahātmani
vavarṣa sahasā devo jagatprahlādayaṁstadā

translations.english: When that great-souled Vipra had been brought over, the god, Indra, suddenly poured forth plenteous showers, enlivening the spirits of men.

verses.sanskrit:
वर्षेणैवागतं विप्रं विषयं स्वं नराधिपः
प्रत्युद्गम्य मुनिं प्रह्वः शिरसा च महीं गतः
verses.transliteration:
varṣeṇaivāgataṁ vipraṁ viṣayaṁ svaṁ narādhipaḥ
pratyudgamya muniṁ prahvaḥ śirasā ca mahīṁ gataḥ

translations.english: When the ascetic had arrived, with showers, the king approached him in bumble guise, bending his head to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्घ्यं च प्रददौ तस्मै न्यायतः सुसमाहितः
वव्रे प्रसादं विप्रेन्द्रान्मा विप्रं मन्युराविशेत्
verses.transliteration:
arghyaṁ ca pradadau tasmai nyāyataḥ susamāhitaḥ
vavre prasādaṁ viprendrānmā vipraṁ manyurāviśet

translations.english: He offered him Arghya in due form, and with a collected mind; and asked for his favour, so that wrath could not influence the Vipra.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःपुरं प्रविश्यास्मै कन्यां दत्त्वा यथाविधि
शान्तां शान्तेन मनसा राजा हर्षमवाप सः
verses.transliteration:
antaḥpuraṁ praviśyāsmai kanyāṁ dattvā yathāvidhi
śāntāṁ śāntena manasā rājā harṣamavāpa saḥ

translations.english: And taking him into the inner apartments, and in due form conferring upon him in sober mood his daughter śāntā, the king became happy.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स न्यवसत्तत्र सर्वकामैः सुपूजितः
ऋश्यशृङ्गो महातेजाः शान्तया सह भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa nyavasattatra sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitaḥ
ṛśyaśṛṅgo mahātejāḥ śāntayā saha bhāryayā

translations.english: Thus the highly powerful Rşyaśřnga together with his wife śāntä, began to live there, respectfully ministered to in regard to every desire.

verses.sanskrit:
भूय एव च राजेन्द्र शृणु मे वचनं हितम्
यथा स देवप्रवरः कथायामेवमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
bhūya eva ca rājendra śṛṇu me vacanaṁ hitam
yathā sa devapravaraḥ kathāyāmevamabravīt

translations.english: And he said again, O foremost of monarchs, do you listen to me as I relate how that intelligent Sanatkumāra, best of deities, spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो भविष्यति सुधार्मिकः
राजा दशरथो नाम्ना श्रीमान्सत्यप्रतिश्रवः
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ kule jāto bhaviṣyati sudhārmikaḥ
rājā daśaratho nāmnā śrīmānsatyapratiśravaḥ

translations.english: In the line of Ikşvāku will be born a righteous king, named Dasaratha, fair of form, and firm in promise.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा राज्ञोऽथ तद्वाक्यं मनसा स विचिन्त्य च
प्रदास्यते पुत्रवन्तं शान्ता भर्तारमात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā rājño'tha tadvākyaṁ manasā sa vicintya ca
pradāsyate putravantaṁ śāntā bhartāramātmavān

translations.english: Hearing these words of the king, and having pondered well, he will make over to him Rsyasînga of subdued senses, together with Santa and his children.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य च तं विप्रं स राजा विगतज्वरः
आहरिष्यति तं यज्ञं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya ca taṁ vipraṁ sa rājā vigatajvaraḥ
āhariṣyati taṁ yajñaṁ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā

translations.english: And taking that Vipra, that king, his mind free from anxiety, with a glad heart, will prepare for that sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थं प्रसवार्थं च स्वर्गार्थं च नरेश्वरः
लभते च स तं कामं द्विजमुख्याद्विशां पतिः
verses.transliteration:
yajñārthaṁ prasavārthaṁ ca svargārthaṁ ca nareśvaraḥ
labhate ca sa taṁ kāmaṁ dvijamukhyādviśāṁ patiḥ

translations.english: And king Dasaratha, knowing duty and desirous of fame, with the intention of obtaining offspring and heaven, with folded hands, will appoint that best of Brahmanas, Rsyasriga, to conduct the ceremony. And that bringer of good will attain his object at the hands of that foremost of Brāhmaṇas.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्राश्चास्य भविष्यन्ति चत्वारोऽमितविक्रमाः
वंशप्रतिष्ठानकराः सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुताः
verses.transliteration:
putrāścāsya bhaviṣyanti catvāro'mitavikramāḥ
vaṁśapratiṣṭhānakarāḥ sarvalokeṣu viśrutāḥ

translations.english: And four sons will be born to him of immeasurable prowess, bringing fame to the family, and known by all.' Thus spoke formerly in the divine age, that worshipful and foremost of deities, Sanatkumāra.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमानय सुसत्कृतम्
स्वयमेव महाराज गत्वा सबलवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ puruṣaśārdūla tamānaya susatkṛtam
svayameva mahārāja gatvā sabalavāhanaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, do you, O tiger among men, repairing there, accompanied with your forces and equipage, yourself, O mighty king, bring Rşyasſrga over with due honours.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुमान्य वसिष्ठं च सूतवाक्यं निशम्य च
सान्तःपुरः सहामात्यः प्रययौ यत्र स द्विजः
verses.transliteration:
anumānya vasiṣṭhaṁ ca sūtavākyaṁ niśamya ca
sāntaḥpuraḥ sahāmātyaḥ prayayau yatra sa dvijaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Sumantra's words, Dasaratha was exceedingly delighted. And hearing these words, and permitted by Vasistha, he, accompanied with the ladies, and his courtiers, set out for the place where that twice-born one was.

verses.sanskrit:
वनानि सरितश्चैव व्यतिक्रम्य शनैः शनैः
अभिचक्राम तं देशं यत्र वै मुनिपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
vanāni saritaścaiva vyatikramya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
abhicakrāma taṁ deśaṁ yatra vai munipuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: And gradually passing by woods and fells, he arrived at the place where that foremost of ascetics was.

verses.sanskrit:
आसाद्य तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं लोमपादसमीपगम्
ऋषिपुत्रं ददर्शादौ दीप्यमानमिवानलम्
verses.transliteration:
āsādya taṁ dvijaśreṣṭhaṁ lomapādasamīpagam
ṛṣiputraṁ dadarśādau dīpyamānamivānalam

translations.english: And coming before that best of regenerate ones, he saw that sage's son near Romapāda, like that of a flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राजा यथान्यायं पूजां चक्रे विशेषतः
सखित्वात्तस्य वै राज्ञः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
tato rājā yathānyāyaṁ pūjāṁ cakre viśeṣataḥ
sakhitvāttasya vai rājñaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā

translations.english: Then the king received him respectfully, and with a delighted mind, on account of the friendship he bore him. He communicated to the intelligent son of the saint, the fact of their intimacy, and then the latter paid homage to Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं सुसत्कृतस्तेन सहोषित्वा नरर्षभः
सप्ताष्टदिवसान्राजा राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ susatkṛtastena sahoṣitvā nararṣabhaḥ
saptāṣṭadivasānrājā rājānamidamabravīt

translations.english: Having passed seven or eight days with Romapäda, receiving high honours, that foremost of men, Dasaratha spoke to Romapada,. saying, Let your daughter, O king, together with her husband, O lord of men, repair to my city. I am going to be engaged in a mighty enterprise.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति राजा संश्रुत्य गमनं तस्य धीमतः
उवाच वचनं विप्रं गच्छ त्वं सह भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
tatheti rājā saṁśrutya gamanaṁ tasya dhīmataḥ
uvāca vacanaṁ vipraṁ gaccha tvaṁ saha bhāryayā

translations.english: Hearing this as to the journey of that intelligent one, the king said to that Vipra, Do you repair with your wife! Thereupon the saint's son, promising to go, said to the king, So be it!

verses.sanskrit:
तावन्योन्याञ्जलिं कृत्वा स्नेहात्संश्लिष्य चोरसा
ननन्दतुर्दशरथो लोमपादश्च वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
tāvanyonyāñjaliṁ kṛtvā snehātsaṁśliṣya corasā
nanandaturdaśaratho lomapādaśca vīryavān

translations.english: Then with the king's permission, he set out with his wife. Dasaratha and the puissant Romapāda clasping each other by the palm, and embracing each other in affection, attained excess. of joy. Then Raghu's son, bidding farewell to his friend, set out.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुहृदमापृच्छ्य प्रस्थितो रघुनन्दनः
पौरेभ्यः प्रेषयामास दूतान्वै शीघ्रगामिनः
क्रियतां नगरं सर्वं क्षिप्रमेव स्वलंकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suhṛdamāpṛcchya prasthito raghunandanaḥ
paurebhyaḥ preṣayāmāsa dūtānvai śīghragāminaḥ
kriyatāṁ nagaraṁ sarvaṁ kṣiprameva svalaṁkṛtam

translations.english: He despatched swift messengers to the citizens, saying, Let the entire city be embellished; let it be perfumed with dhupa, and watered and decked with pennons.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टाः पौरास्ते श्रुत्वा राजानमागतम्
तथा प्रचक्रुस्तत्सर्वं राज्ञा यत्प्रेषितं तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paurāste śrutvā rājānamāgatam
tathā pracakrustatsarvaṁ rājñā yatpreṣitaṁ tadā

translations.english: Hearing of the king's approach, the citizens joyfully did every thing as per message they had been communicated.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स्वलंकृतं राजा नगरं प्रविवेश ह
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः पुरस्कृत्य द्विजर्षभम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ svalaṁkṛtaṁ rājā nagaraṁ praviveśa ha
śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaiḥ puraskṛtya dvijarṣabham

translations.english: Then the monarch, preceded by the foremost of Brāhmanas before him, entered the decorated city, to the blares of conches and drums.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तं नागरा द्विजम्
प्रवेश्यमानं सत्कृत्य नरेन्द्रेणेन्द्रकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pramuditāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā taṁ nāgarā dvijam
praveśyamānaṁ satkṛtya narendreṇendrakarmaṇā

translations.english: And beholding that Brāhmaṇa entering the city, duly honoured by the prime of men; subservient to Indra, like to Kaśyapa's son entering the celestial regions honoured of the thousand eyed lord of the celestials, all the citizens rejoiced exceedingly.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःपुरं प्रवेश्यैनं पूजां कृत्वा तु शास्त्रतः
कृतकृत्यं तदात्मानं मेने तस्योपवाहनात्
verses.transliteration:
antaḥpuraṁ praveśyainaṁ pūjāṁ kṛtvā tu śāstrataḥ
kṛtakṛtyaṁ tadātmānaṁ mene tasyopavāhanāt

translations.english: Then taking him into the inner apartment, and paying him homage according to the ordinance, the king considered himself as having gained his object, in consequence of the presence of that Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःपुराणि सर्वाणि शान्तां दृष्ट्वा तथागताम्
सह भर्त्रा विशालाक्षीं प्रीत्यानन्दमुपागमन्
verses.transliteration:
antaḥpurāṇi sarvāṇi śāntāṁ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatām
saha bhartrā viśālākṣīṁ prītyānandamupāgaman

translations.english: And all the inmates of the inner apartment, seeing the large-eyed Săntă thus arrived with her husband, experienced excess of joy.

verses.sanskrit:
पूज्यमाना च ताभिः सा राज्ञा चैव विशेषतः
उवास तत्र सुखिता कंचित्कालं सह द्विजा
verses.transliteration:
pūjyamānā ca tābhiḥ sā rājñā caiva viśeṣataḥ
uvāsa tatra sukhitā kaṁcitkālaṁ saha dvijā

translations.english: Then honoured by them and the king in especial, she happily spent there some time along with that twice-born one.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः काले बहुतिथे कस्मिंश्चित्सुमनोहरे
वसन्ते समनुप्राप्ते राज्ञो यष्टुं मनोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kāle bahutithe kasmiṁścitsumanohare
vasante samanuprāpte rājño yaṣṭuṁ mano'bhavat

translations.english: Then after a long while, when the charming spring had appeared on the earth, the king conceived the desire of celebrating the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रसाद्य शिरसा तं विप्रं देववर्णिनम्
यज्ञाय वरयामास संतानार्थं कुलस्य वै
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prasādya śirasā taṁ vipraṁ devavarṇinam
yajñāya varayāmāsa saṁtānārthaṁ kulasya vai

translations.english: Then bowing down the head before the Vipra effulgent like a celestial, he appointed him to undertake the ceremony, for the purpose of obtaining offspring to perpetuate his line.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति च स राजानमुवाच च सुसत्कृतः
संभाराः संभ्रियन्तां ते तुरगश्च विमुच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
tatheti ca sa rājānamuvāca ca susatkṛtaḥ
saṁbhārāḥ saṁbhriyantāṁ te turagaśca vimucyatām

translations.english: Then that Brāhmana said to the lord of the earth, the king, So be it! Get order the necessary provisions procured, free the horse set, and prepare a sacrificial ground on the north bank of the Sarayd.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितं गत्वा त्वरितविक्रमः
समानयत्स तान्विप्रान्समस्तान्वेदपारगान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sumantrastvaritaṁ gatvā tvaritavikramaḥ
samānayatsa tānviprānsamastānvedapāragān

translations.english: Thereupon, going out speeding, Sumantra of swift movements called together all the spiritual guides, as well as others versed in the Vedic ritual.

verses.sanskrit:
सुयज्ञं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम्
पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
suyajñaṁ vāmadevaṁ ca jābālimatha kāśyapam
purohitaṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ ca ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ

translations.english: Then the king spoke to Sumantra, saying, O Sumantra, do you summon speedily Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas and priests professing the Vedānta philosophy, Suyajña, and Vāmadeva, and Jabali, and Kasyapa, and the priest Vasistha, together with other excellent twice-born ones.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्पूजयित्वा धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्तदा
इदं धर्मार्थसहितं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tānpūjayitvā dharmātmā rājā daśarathastadā
idaṁ dharmārthasahitaṁ ślakṣṇaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Then, honouring them duly, the virtuous king Dasaratha spoke to them these amiable words, consistent with duty and interest.

verses.sanskrit:
मम लालप्यमानस्य पुत्रार्थं नास्ति वै सुखम्
तदर्थं हयमेधेन यक्ष्यामीति मतिर्मम
verses.transliteration:
mama lālapyamānasya putrārthaṁ nāsti vai sukham
tadarthaṁ hayamedhena yakṣyāmīti matirmama

translations.english: Consistent with duty and interest,-Ever pining on account of a son, I know no happiness,-therefore it is my intention that I should celebrate a horse sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तदहं यष्टुमिच्छामि शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा
ऋषिपुत्रप्रभावेन कामान्प्राप्स्यामि चाप्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tadahaṁ yaṣṭumicchāmi śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
ṛṣiputraprabhāvena kāmānprāpsyāmi cāpyaham

translations.english: So, I would like to perform a horse-sacrifice. And by the grace of the saint's son, I shall obtain my desire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः साध्विति तद्वाक्यं ब्राह्मणाः प्रत्यपूजयन्
वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्वे पार्थिवस्य मुखाच्च्युतम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sādhviti tadvākyaṁ brāhmaṇāḥ pratyapūjayan
vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarve pārthivasya mukhāccyutam

translations.english: Thereupon, the Brāhmaṇas with Vasiştha at their head honoured the words that fell from the king's lips, saying, Well!

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्गपुरोगाश्च प्रत्यूचुर्नृपतिं तदा
संभाराः संभ्रियन्तां ते तुरगश्च विमुच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyaśṛṅgapurogāśca pratyūcurnṛpatiṁ tadā
saṁbhārāḥ saṁbhriyantāṁ te turagaśca vimucyatām

translations.english: The Brāhmaṇas headed by Rsyaśộnga addressed the king, saying, Do you arrange for the provisions, loose the horse, and prepare the sacrificial ground on the north bank of the Sarayū river!

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा प्राप्यसे पुत्रांश्चतुरोऽमितविक्रमान्
यस्य ते धार्मिकी बुद्धिरियं पुत्रार्थमागता
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā prāpyase putrāṁścaturo'mitavikramān
yasya te dhārmikī buddhiriyaṁ putrārthamāgatā

translations.english: Since you purpose so virtuously for obtaining offspring, you shall obtain four sons of immeasurable prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतोऽभवद्राजा श्रुत्वा तद्द्विजभाषितम्
अमात्यांश्चाब्रवीद्राजा हर्षेणेदं शुभाक्षरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prīto'bhavadrājā śrutvā taddvijabhāṣitam
amātyāṁścābravīdrājā harṣeṇedaṁ śubhākṣaram

translations.english: Hearing those words of the regenerate ones, the king was exceedingly delighted. And cheerfully he spoke these auspicious words to his courtiers.

verses.sanskrit:
गुरूणां वचनाच्छीघ्रं संभाराः संभ्रियन्तु मे
समर्थाधिष्ठितश्चाश्वः सोपाध्यायो विमुच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
gurūṇāṁ vacanācchīghraṁ saṁbhārāḥ saṁbhriyantu me
samarthādhiṣṭhitaścāśvaḥ sopādhyāyo vimucyatām

translations.english: In accordance with the directions of my spiritual guides, do you speedily procure these provisions, loose the horse well protected, and followed by a priest.

verses.sanskrit:
सरय्वाश्चोत्तरे तीरे यज्ञभूमिर्विधीयताम्
शान्तयश्चाभिवर्धन्तां यथाकल्पं यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
sarayvāścottare tīre yajñabhūmirvidhīyatām
śāntayaścābhivardhantāṁ yathākalpaṁ yathāvidhi

translations.english: And prepare the sacrificial ground on the north bank of the Sarayu. And perform the ceremonies capable of securing the rites from disturbance.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्यः कर्तुमयं यज्ञः सर्वेणापि महीक्षिता
नापराधो भवेत्कष्टो यद्यस्मिन्क्रतुसत्तमे
verses.transliteration:
śakyaḥ kartumayaṁ yajñaḥ sarveṇāpi mahīkṣitā
nāparādho bhavetkaṣṭo yadyasminkratusattame

translations.english: Surely every king is competent to perform this sacrifice yet care must be taken that no default occurs in it.

verses.sanskrit:
छिद्रं हि मृगयन्तेऽत्र विद्वांसो ब्रह्मराक्षसाः
विधिहीनस्य यज्ञस्य सद्यः कर्ता विनश्यति
verses.transliteration:
chidraṁ hi mṛgayante'tra vidvāṁso brahmarākṣasāḥ
vidhihīnasya yajñasya sadyaḥ kartā vinaśyati

translations.english: For flaws in this foremost of sacrifices are watched by learned Brahma-Rākşasas. And should it come to be celebrated in violation of the ordinance, ihe performer thereof shall meet with instant destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्यथा विधिपूर्वं मे क्रतुरेष समाप्यते
तथाविधानं क्रियतां समर्थाः करणेष्विह
verses.transliteration:
tadyathā vidhipūrvaṁ me kratureṣa samāpyate
tathāvidhānaṁ kriyatāṁ samarthāḥ karaṇeṣviha

translations.english: And do you so order that this sacrifice of mine may be completed according to the prescribed ritual.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति च ततः सर्वे मन्त्रिणः प्रत्यपूजयन्
पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तद्वाक्यं यथाज्ञप्तमकुर्वत
verses.transliteration:
tatheti ca tataḥ sarve mantriṇaḥ pratyapūjayan
pārthivendrasya tadvākyaṁ yathājñaptamakurvata

translations.english: Thereupon honouring those words of the king, the ministers did as ordered.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो द्विजास्ते धर्मज्ञमस्तुवन्पार्थिवर्षभम्
अनुज्ञातास्ततः सर्वे पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
tato dvijāste dharmajñamastuvanpārthivarṣabham
anujñātāstataḥ sarve punarjagmuryathāgatam

translations.english: And having eulogised the king knowing duty, the twice-born ones, with the Monarch's leave, departed for their respective quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
गतानां तु द्विजातीनां मन्त्रिणस्तान्नराधिपः
विसर्जयित्वा स्वं वेश्म प्रविवेश महाद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
gatānāṁ tu dvijātīnāṁ mantriṇastānnarādhipaḥ
visarjayitvā svaṁ veśma praviveśa mahādyutiḥ

translations.english: When the Vipras had gone, the mightyminded lord of men dismissing his counsellors, entered his place. When the Vipras had gone, the mightyminded lord of men dismissing his counsellors, entered his place.

verses.sanskrit:
पुनः प्राप्ते वसन्ते तु पूर्णः संवत्सरोऽभवत्
अभिवाद्य वसिष्ठं च न्यायतः प्रतिपूज्य च
verses.transliteration:
punaḥ prāpte vasante tu pūrṇaḥ saṁvatsaro'bhavat
abhivādya vasiṣṭhaṁ ca nyāyataḥ pratipūjya ca

translations.english: When after a full one year, spring had again appeared on the face of the earth, the puissant king, intent upon getting offspring through the horse-sacrifice, sough Vasistha's side.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं प्रसवार्थं द्विजोत्तमम्
यज्ञो मे क्रियतां विप्र यथोक्तं मुनिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
abravītpraśritaṁ vākyaṁ prasavārthaṁ dvijottamam
yajño me kriyatāṁ vipra yathoktaṁ munipuṁgava

translations.english: Having saluted Vasiştha and duly paid him homage, he humbly spoke to that best of twiceborn ones, with the intention of having offspring.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा न विघ्नः क्रियते यज्ञाङ्गेषु विधीयताम्
भवान्स्निग्धः सुहृन्मह्यं गुरुश्च परमो महान्
verses.transliteration:
yathā na vighnaḥ kriyate yajñāṅgeṣu vidhīyatām
bhavānsnigdhaḥ suhṛnmahyaṁ guruśca paramo mahān

translations.english: You are my kind friend, and prime and mighty spiritual guide. Engaged in it, you will have to bear the entire burden of the ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
करिष्ये सर्वमेवैतद्भवता यत्समर्थितम्
ततोऽब्रवीद्द्विजान्वृद्धान्यज्ञकर्मसु निष्ठितान्
verses.transliteration:
kariṣye sarvamevaitadbhavatā yatsamarthitam
tato'bravīddvijānvṛddhānyajñakarmasu niṣṭhitān

translations.english: Thereupon that best of Brāhmaṇas said to the king, 'So be it! I will do all that you asked.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थापत्ये निष्ठितांश्चैव वृद्धान्परमधार्मिकान्
कर्मान्तिकाञ्शिल्पकारान्वर्धकीन्खनकानपि
verses.transliteration:
sthāpatye niṣṭhitāṁścaiva vṛddhānparamadhārmikān
karmāntikāñśilpakārānvardhakīnkhanakānapi

translations.english: He then said to the old Brāhmaṇas well-up in sacrificial affairs, and experienced car-makers, and highly pious aged people, and servants, carrying on the ceremonial operations till the end, and artists, and carpenters, and diggers, and astrologers, and artizans, and dancers, and conductors of theatres, and pure and learned persons variously versed in knowledge, Do you, in obedience to the royal mandate, engage in the sacrificial work!

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञकर्म समीहन्तां भवन्तो राजशासनात्
इष्टका बहुसाहस्री शीघ्रमानीयतामिति
verses.transliteration:
yajñakarma samīhantāṁ bhavanto rājaśāsanāt
iṣṭakā bahusāhasrī śīghramānīyatāmiti

translations.english: And fetch bricks by thousands. And do raise structures for the kings, commanding every convenience.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्ष्यान्नपानैर्बहुभिः समुपेताः सुनिष्ठिताः
तथा पौरजनस्यापि कर्तव्या बहुविस्तराः
verses.transliteration:
bhakṣyānnapānairbahubhiḥ samupetāḥ suniṣṭhitāḥ
tathā paurajanasyāpi kartavyā bahuvistarāḥ

translations.english: Do you rear goodly and comfortable buildings by hundreds for the Brāhmaṇas, replenished with various meats and drinks.

verses.sanskrit:
दातव्यमन्नं विधिवत्सत्कृत्य न तु लीलया
सर्वे वर्णा यथा पूजां प्राप्नुवन्ति सुसत्कृताः
verses.transliteration:
dātavyamannaṁ vidhivatsatkṛtya na tu līlayā
sarve varṇā yathā pūjāṁ prāpnuvanti susatkṛtāḥ

translations.english: And dwellings filled with diverse kinds of viands, and commanding everything desirable, and mansions for the lower orders of the citizens, exceedingly beautiful to behold. And meats should be duly dispensed with all hospitality, and not in the indifference of festive occasions, so that all may regard themselves as honourably entertained. And none should be disregarded out of lust or passion.

verses.sanskrit:
न चावज्ञा प्रयोक्तव्या कामक्रोधवशादपि
यज्ञकर्मसु येऽव्यग्राः पुरुषाः शिल्पिनस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
na cāvajñā prayoktavyā kāmakrodhavaśādapi
yajñakarmasu ye'vyagrāḥ puruṣāḥ śilpinastathā

translations.english: Those persons, and artizans, that will labour eagerly in the sacrifice, should by turns, be especially entertained.

verses.sanskrit:
निमन्त्रयस्य नृपतीन्पृथिव्यां ये च धार्मिकाः
ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियान्वैश्याञ्शूद्रांश्चैव सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
nimantrayasya nṛpatīnpṛthivyāṁ ye ca dhārmikāḥ
brāhmaṇānkṣatriyānvaiśyāñśūdrāṁścaiva sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Then they approached Vasistha, saying, Everything has been performed properly, without anything being left out. And what you say shall be performed, and nothing words, Do you invite all those kings that are pious, and Brāhmaṇas, and Kșatriyas and Sūdras, by thousands. And do you with due honours bring people from all countries.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्ठितं सर्वशास्त्रेषु तथा वेदेषु निष्ठितम्
तमानय महाभागं स्वयमेव सुसत्कृतम्
पूर्वसंबन्धिनं ज्ञात्वा ततः पूर्वं ब्रवीमि ते
verses.transliteration:
niṣṭhitaṁ sarvaśāstreṣu tathā vedeṣu niṣṭhitam
tamānaya mahābhāgaṁ svayameva susatkṛtam
pūrvasaṁbandhinaṁ jñātvā tataḥ pūrvaṁ bravīmi te

translations.english: With proper honour yourself bring the righteous, truthful, and heroic Janaka, lord of Mithilā. And it is because he is our old friend that I first mention him.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा काशिपतिं स्निग्धं सततं प्रियवादिनम्
सद्वृत्तं देवसंकाशं स्वयमेवानयस्व ह
verses.transliteration:
tathā kāśipatiṁ snigdhaṁ satataṁ priyavādinam
sadvṛttaṁ devasaṁkāśaṁ svayamevānayasva ha

translations.english: Then do yourself bring the amiable and ever fair-spoken lord of Kāśī, of excellent character, resembling a celestial.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा केकयराजानं वृद्धं परमधार्मिकम्
श्वशुरं राजसिंहस्य सपुत्रं तमिहानय
verses.transliteration:
tathā kekayarājānaṁ vṛddhaṁ paramadhārmikam
śvaśuraṁ rājasiṁhasya saputraṁ tamihānaya

translations.english: Then do you bring here along with his son, the highly-pious, old king of Kekaya, who is the father-in-law of this tiger of a monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गेश्वरं महाभागं लोमपादं सुसत्कृतम्
वयस्यं राजसिंहस्य तमानय यशस्विनम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgeśvaraṁ mahābhāgaṁ lomapādaṁ susatkṛtam
vayasyaṁ rājasiṁhasya tamānaya yaśasvinam

translations.english: Then also bring with due honours the king of Anga, and that mighty archer, the illustrious Romapada, the friend of that lion among the kings, along with his son.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठवाक्यं तच्छ्रुत्वा सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितस्तदा
व्यादिशत्पुरुषांस्तत्र राज्ञामानयने शुभान्
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhavākyaṁ tacchrutvā sumantrastvaritastadā
vyādiśatpuruṣāṁstatra rājñāmānayane śubhān

translations.english: Having heard those words of Vasistha, Sumantra speedily ordered the emissaries to bring the kings.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयमेव हि धर्मात्मा प्रययौ मुनिशासनात्
सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितो भूत्वा समानेतुं महीक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
svayameva hi dharmātmā prayayau muniśāsanāt
sumantrastvarito bhūtvā samānetuṁ mahīkṣitaḥ

translations.english: The virtuous Sumantra, in accordance with the injunction of the ascetic, himself speedily set out for the purpose of bringing the monarchs.

verses.sanskrit:
ते च कर्मान्तिकाः सर्वे वसिष्ठाय च धीमते
सर्वं निवेदयन्ति स्म यज्ञे यदुपकल्पितम्
verses.transliteration:
te ca karmāntikāḥ sarve vasiṣṭhāya ca dhīmate
sarvaṁ nivedayanti sma yajñe yadupakalpitam

translations.english: Then the servants came and informed the intelligent Vasiştha as to the articles that had been got ready for the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतो द्विजश्रेष्ठस्तान्सर्वान्पुनरब्रवीत्
अवज्ञया न दातव्यं कस्यचिल्लीलयापि वा
अवज्ञया कृतं हन्याद्दातारं नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prīto dvijaśreṣṭhastānsarvānpunarabravīt
avajñayā na dātavyaṁ kasyacillīlayāpi vā
avajñayā kṛtaṁ hanyāddātāraṁ nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Then well pleased that best of twice-born ones, the ascetic Vasistha, said to them, Do not give away disrespectfully or lightly. A gift bestowed with disrespect, indubitably destroy the giver.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कैश्चिदहोरात्रैरुपयाता महीक्षितः
बहूनि रत्नान्यादाय राज्ञो दशरथस्य ह
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kaiścidahorātrairupayātā mahīkṣitaḥ
bahūni ratnānyādāya rājño daśarathasya ha

translations.english: Then for several days, kings began to pour into Dasaratha's city daily and nightly, bringing with them various kinds of gems.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वसिष्ठः सुप्रीतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
उपयाता नरव्याघ्र राजानस्तव शासनात्
verses.transliteration:
tato vasiṣṭhaḥ suprīto rājānamidamabravīt
upayātā naravyāghra rājānastava śāsanāt

translations.english: Thereupon Vasiştha well-pleased said to the king, O tiger among men, obeying your mandate the kings have come here; and I too according to merit, have received those excellent kings with respect.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्यातु च भवान्यष्टुं यज्ञायतनमन्तिकात्
सर्वकामैरुपहृतैरुपेतं वै समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
niryātu ca bhavānyaṣṭuṁ yajñāyatanamantikāt
sarvakāmairupahṛtairupetaṁ vai samantataḥ

translations.english: Everything has been carefully made ready for the sacrifice by the persons concerned. Do you, therefore, repair to the sacrificial ground, for performing the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा वसिष्ठवचनादृश्यशृङ्गस्य चोभयोः
शुभे दिवस नक्षत्रे निर्यातो जगतीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
tathā vasiṣṭhavacanādṛśyaśṛṅgasya cobhayoḥ
śubhe divasa nakṣatre niryāto jagatīpatiḥ

translations.english: Then in accordance with the injunctions of both Vasiştha and Rşyasſga, the king came to the sacrificial spot on a day presided over by an auspicious star.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्व एव द्विजोत्तमाः
ऋश्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञकर्मारभंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tato vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarva eva dvijottamāḥ
ṛśyaśṛṅgaṁ puraskṛtya yajñakarmārabhaṁstadā

translations.english: Then, with, Rsyasrriga at their head, Vasistha and the other principal Brāhmaṇas wending to the sacrificial ground, began the ceremony, according to the ordinance; and in due form. And the auspicious king, in company with his wives, was initiated into the ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे तस्मिन्प्राप्ते तुरङ्गमे
सरय्वाश्चोत्तरे तीरे राज्ञो यज्ञोऽभ्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
atha saṁvatsare pūrṇe tasminprāpte turaṅgame
sarayvāścottare tīre rājño yajño'bhyavartata

translations.english: After the expiry of full one year, when the sacrificial horse had returned, the sacrifice, of the king commenced on the north bank of the Sarayu.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य कर्म चक्रुर्द्विजर्षभाः
अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे राज्ञोऽस्य सुमहात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyaśṛṅgaṁ puraskṛtya karma cakrurdvijarṣabhāḥ
aśvamedhe mahāyajñe rājño'sya sumahātmanaḥ

translations.english: And with Rşyasſága at their head, the principal twice-born ones began the proceedings in that mighty horse-sacrifice of that high-souled monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्म कुर्वन्ति विधिवद्याजका वेदपारगाः
यथाविधि यथान्यायं परिक्रामन्ति शास्त्रतः
verses.transliteration:
karma kurvanti vidhivadyājakā vedapāragāḥ
yathāvidhi yathānyāyaṁ parikrāmanti śāstrataḥ

translations.english: And the priests, each duly and according to the ordinance performing his proper part, engaged in the ceremony in consonance with the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिपूज्य ततो हृष्टाः सर्वे चक्रुर्यथाविधि
प्रातःसवनपूर्वाणि कर्माणि मुनिपुंगवाः
verses.transliteration:
abhipūjya tato hṛṣṭāḥ sarve cakruryathāvidhi
prātaḥsavanapūrvāṇi karmāṇi munipuṁgavāḥ

translations.english: And the regenerate ones, having performed the pravargya as well as the upasada according to the ordinance, duly completed the additional ceremonies. Then, worshipping the deities with glad hearts, those foremost of ascetics duly performed the morning ablutions and the other prescribed rites.

verses.sanskrit:
न चाहुतमभूत्तत्र स्खलितं वापि किंचन
दृश्यते ब्रह्मवत्सर्वं क्षेमयुक्तं हि चक्रिरे
verses.transliteration:
na cāhutamabhūttatra skhalitaṁ vāpi kiṁcana
dṛśyate brahmavatsarvaṁ kṣemayuktaṁ hi cakrire

translations.english: And no part of the ceremony was performed improperly, or left out, and every thing was satisfactorily celebrated with mantras.

verses.sanskrit:
न तेष्वहःसु श्रान्तो वा क्षुधितो वापि दृश्यते
नाविद्वान्ब्राह्मणस्तत्र नाशतानुचरस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
na teṣvahaḥsu śrānto vā kṣudhito vāpi dṛśyate
nāvidvānbrāhmaṇastatra nāśatānucarastathā

translations.english: And on that day no Brāhmaṇa ever felt tired, or hungry and there was none that was not learned, or that was not followed by an hundred persons.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धाश्च व्याधिताश्चैव स्त्रियो बालास्तथैव च
अनिशं भुञ्जमानानां न तृप्तिरुपलभ्यते
verses.transliteration:
vṛddhāśca vyādhitāścaiva striyo bālāstathaiva ca
aniśaṁ bhuñjamānānāṁ na tṛptirupalabhyate

translations.english: Brāhmaṇas, and Śūdras having among them ascetics, and Sramanas, and the aged, and the infirm, and women, and children, were continually fed. And although they ate their fill, yet they know no repletion.

verses.sanskrit:
दीयतां दीयतामन्नं वासांसि विविधानि च
इति संचोदितास्तत्र तथा चक्रुरनेकशः
verses.transliteration:
dīyatāṁ dīyatāmannaṁ vāsāṁsi vividhāni ca
iti saṁcoditāstatra tathā cakruranekaśaḥ

translations.english: And Give food, and clothes of various kinds (was heard all around) And those employed in the task gave away profusely.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्नकूटाश्च बहवो दृश्यन्ते पर्वतोपमाः
दिवसे दिवसे तत्र सिद्धस्य विधिवत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
annakūṭāśca bahavo dṛśyante parvatopamāḥ
divase divase tatra siddhasya vidhivattadā

translations.english: And every day food dressed properly in due form was to be seen in countless heaps resembling hills.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्नं हि विधिवत्स्वादु प्रशंसन्ति द्विजर्षभाः
अहो तृप्ताः स्म भद्रं ते इति शुश्राव राघवः
verses.transliteration:
annaṁ hi vidhivatsvādu praśaṁsanti dvijarṣabhāḥ
aho tṛptāḥ sma bhadraṁ te iti śuśrāva rāghavaḥ

translations.english: The foremost regenerate ones said, The viands have been prepared in the prescribed form, and they taste excellent. We have been gratified. God bless you! All this was heard by the descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वलंकृताश्च पुरुषा ब्राह्मणान्पर्यवेषयन्
उपासते च तानन्ये सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः
verses.transliteration:
svalaṁkṛtāśca puruṣā brāhmaṇānparyaveṣayan
upāsate ca tānanye sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ

translations.english: Persons adorned with ornaments distributed the victuals among the Brāhmaṇas, and they were assisted by others wearing jewelled pendants.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मान्तरे तदा विप्रा हेतुवादान्बहूनपि
प्राहुः सुवाग्मिनो धीराः परस्परजिगीषया
verses.transliteration:
karmāntare tadā viprā hetuvādānbahūnapi
prāhuḥ suvāgmino dhīrāḥ parasparajigīṣayā

translations.english: In the interval between the completion of one bath and the beginning of the next, mild and eloquent Vipras, desirous of victory, engaged in various disputations.

verses.sanskrit:
दिवसे दिवसे तत्र संस्तरे कुशला द्विजाः
सर्वकर्माणि चक्रुस्ते यथाशास्त्रं प्रचोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
divase divase tatra saṁstare kuśalā dvijāḥ
sarvakarmāṇi cakruste yathāśāstraṁ pracoditāḥ

translations.english: Every day in that sacrifice, skilful Brāhmaṇas, engaged in the ceremony, did everything, according to the ritual.

verses.sanskrit:
नाषडङ्गविदत्रासीन्नाव्रतो नाबहुश्रुतः
सदस्यस्तस्य वै राज्ञो नावादकुशलो द्विजः
verses.transliteration:
nāṣaḍaṅgavidatrāsīnnāvrato nābahuśrutaḥ
sadasyastasya vai rājño nāvādakuśalo dvijaḥ

translations.english: There was no twice-born one that was not versed in the Vedas and the Vedāngas, or that did not observe vows, or that was not profoundly learned, nor did any assist at the sacrifice that could not argue ably.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्ते यूपोच्छ्रये तस्मिन्षड्बैल्वाः खादिरास्तथा
तावन्तो बिल्वसहिताः पर्णिनश्च तथापरे
verses.transliteration:
prāpte yūpocchraye tasminṣaḍbailvāḥ khādirāstathā
tāvanto bilvasahitāḥ parṇinaśca tathāpare

translations.english: And when the time came for planting the Yüpas of bilva, as many of catechu, and as many of Palasa, and one of Sleşmätaka, and two of Devadāru well-made and measuring two outstretched arms.

verses.sanskrit:
विन्यस्ता विधिवत्सर्वे शिल्पिभिः सुकृता दृढाः
अष्टाश्रयः सर्व एव श्लक्ष्णरूपसमन्विताः
verses.transliteration:
vinyastā vidhivatsarve śilpibhiḥ sukṛtā dṛḍhāḥ
aṣṭāśrayaḥ sarva eva ślakṣṇarūpasamanvitāḥ

translations.english: Persons versed in the arts and science of sacrifice constructed these Yüpas. And at the time of throwing up the Yüpas for embellishing the sacrifice, these one and twenty Yüpas, each measuring one and twenty Aratnis, having eight angles, and smooth-faced, were decked out in one and twenty pieces of cloth, and were firmly planted with due ceremonies by artisans.

verses.sanskrit:
आच्छादितास्ते वासोभिः पुष्पैर्गन्धैश्च भूषिताः
सप्तर्षयो दीप्तिमन्तो विराजन्ते यथा दिवि
verses.transliteration:
ācchāditāste vāsobhiḥ puṣpairgandhaiśca bhūṣitāḥ
saptarṣayo dīptimanto virājante yathā divi

translations.english: And being wrapped up in cloths, and worshipped with flowers, they looked like the seven Rșis appearing in the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
इष्टकाश्च यथान्यायं कारिताश्च प्रमाणतः
चितोऽग्निर्ब्राह्मणैस्तत्र कुशलैः शुल्बकर्मणि
verses.transliteration:
iṣṭakāśca yathānyāyaṁ kāritāśca pramāṇataḥ
cito'gnirbrāhmaṇaistatra kuśalaiḥ śulbakarmaṇi

translations.english: And an adequate number of bricks was also duly made (for the ceremony.) And Brāhmaṇas accomplished in the arts constructed the sacrificial fire-place with those bricks.

verses.sanskrit:
नियुक्तास्तत्र पशवस्तत्तदुद्दिश्य दैवतम्
उरगाः पक्षिणश्चैव यथाशास्त्रं प्रचोदिताः
शामित्रे तु हयस्तत्र तथा जल चराश्च ये
verses.transliteration:
niyuktāstatra paśavastattaduddiśya daivatam
uragāḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva yathāśāstraṁ pracoditāḥ
śāmitre tu hayastatra tathā jala carāśca ye

translations.english: That fire-place of that lion among kings, set by skilful Brāhmaṇas, consisting on three sides of eighteen bricks, looked like the goldenwinged Garuda. And for the purpose of sacrificing them to the respective deities were collect beasts and reptiles, and birds, and horses, and aquatic animals. And the priests sacrificed all these in proper form.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋत्विग्भिः सर्वमेवैतन्नियुक्तं शास्त्रतस्तदा
पशूनां त्रिशतं तत्र यूपेषु नियतं तदा
अश्वरत्नोत्तमं तस्य राज्ञो दशरथस्य ह
verses.transliteration:
ṛtvigbhiḥ sarvamevaitanniyuktaṁ śāstratastadā
paśūnāṁ triśataṁ tatra yūpeṣu niyataṁ tadā
aśvaratnottamaṁ tasya rājño daśarathasya ha

translations.english: And to these Yūpas were bound, three hundred beasts, as well as the foremost of the best horses belonging to king Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या तं हयं तत्र परिचर्य समन्ततः
कृपाणैर्विशशासैनं त्रिभिः परमया मुदा
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā taṁ hayaṁ tatra paricarya samantataḥ
kṛpāṇairviśaśāsainaṁ tribhiḥ paramayā mudā

translations.english: Then Kausalyā, having performed the preliminary rites, with three strokes slew that horse, experiencing great glee.

verses.sanskrit:
पतत्रिणा तदा सार्धं सुस्थितेन च चेतसा
अवसद्रजनीमेकां कौसल्या धर्मकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
patatriṇā tadā sārdhaṁ susthitena ca cetasā
avasadrajanīmekāṁ kausalyā dharmakāmyayā

translations.english: And with the view of reaping merit, Kausalyā, with an undisturbed heart passed one night with that horse furnished with wings.

verses.sanskrit:
होताध्वर्युस्तथोद्गाता हयेन समयोजयन्
महिष्या परिवृक्त्याथ वावातामपरां तथा
verses.transliteration:
hotādhvaryustathodgātā hayena samayojayan
mahiṣyā parivṛktyātha vāvātāmaparāṁ tathā

translations.english: Hotás and Adhvaryus, and the Udgatás joined the king's Vāvātā along with his Mahișī and Parivrtti.* And priests of subdued senses, wellup in sacrificial rites, began to offer oblations with the fat of the winged-horse, according to the ordinance. *The Kșatriya kings could marry wives from among Kșatriyas, Vaişyas and Śūdras. The Kșatriya wife is called Mahiși, the Vaişya wife Vávātā and the Śūdra wife Parivrtti.

verses.sanskrit:
धूमगन्धं वपायास्तु जिघ्रति स्म नराधिपः
यथाकालं यथान्यायं निर्णुदन्पापमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmagandhaṁ vapāyāstu jighrati sma narādhipaḥ
yathākālaṁ yathānyāyaṁ nirṇudanpāpamātmanaḥ

translations.english: The lord of men, desirous of removing his sins, at the proper time smelt the odour of the smoke arising from the fat, agreeably to the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit:
हयस्य यानि चाङ्गानि तानि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणाः
अग्नौ प्रास्यन्ति विधिवत्समस्ताः षोडशर्त्विजः
verses.transliteration:
hayasya yāni cāṅgāni tāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇāḥ
agnau prāsyanti vidhivatsamastāḥ ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ

translations.english: Then sixteen sacrificial priests in the prescribed form offered the various parts of the horse to the fire.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्थ्यं द्वितीयं संख्यातमतिरात्रं तथोत्तरम्
कारितास्तत्र बहवो विहिताः शास्त्रदर्शनात्
verses.transliteration:
ukthyaṁ dvitīyaṁ saṁkhyātamatirātraṁ tathottaram
kāritāstatra bahavo vihitāḥ śāstradarśanāt

translations.english: It is customary in other sacrifices to offer the oblations by means of a Plaksa bough; but in the horse-sacrifice a cane is used instead. The horsesacrifice, according to the Kalpa-Sūtras and the Brahmanas, extend over three days. Thereafter, on the first day was the Catuștoma celebrated; and on the second, the Uktha, and on the third the Atirâtra.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्योतिष्टोमायुषी चैव अतिरात्रौ च निर्मितौ
अभिजिद्विश्वजिच्चैव अप्तोर्यामो महाक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
jyotiṣṭomāyuṣī caiva atirātrau ca nirmitau
abhijidviśvajiccaiva aptoryāmo mahākratuḥ

translations.english: And then the jyotisloma, and then Āyuştoma, and the Atirātra, and the Abhijit, and the Visvajit, and the Āptoryāma, all these various great sacrifices were celebrated with due rites.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्गात्रे तु तथोदीचीं दक्षिणैषा विनिर्मिता
अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे स्वयम्भुविहिते पुरा
verses.transliteration:
udgātre tu tathodīcīṁ dakṣiṇaiṣā vinirmitā
aśvamedhe mahāyajñe svayambhuvihite purā

translations.english: And in this mighty horse-sacrifice founded of yore by Svayambhū, that perpetuator of his line, the king, bestowed the Eastern quarter on his chief sacrificial priest, the Western on his Adhvaryu, the Southern on Brahmă, and the Northern on the Udgātā, as Daksinās.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रतुं समाप्य तु तदा न्यायतः पुरुषर्षभः
ऋत्विग्भ्यो हि ददौ राजा धरां तां क्रतुवर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
kratuṁ samāpya tu tadā nyāyataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
ṛtvigbhyo hi dadau rājā dharāṁ tāṁ kratuvardhanaḥ

translations.english: Having completed that sacrifice, that perpetuator of his race, and foremost of men, the king, conferied on the priests the earth; and having conferred it, that auspicious descendant of Ikşvāku experienced high delight. And then the priests spoke to that monarch, who had all his sins purged off saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न भूम्या कार्यमस्माकं न हि शक्ताः स्म पालने
रताः स्वाध्यायकरणे वयं नित्यं हि भूमिप
निष्क्रयं किंचिदेवेह प्रयच्छतु भवानिति
verses.transliteration:
na bhūmyā kāryamasmākaṁ na hi śaktāḥ sma pālane
ratāḥ svādhyāyakaraṇe vayaṁ nityaṁ hi bhūmipa
niṣkrayaṁ kiṁcideveha prayacchatu bhavāniti

translations.english: You alone are worthy to protect the entire world. We do not want the earth; nor can we rule it, being, O lord of Earth, constantly engaged in Vedic studies. Do you, therefore, confer upon us something instead, as the price thereof.

verses.sanskrit:
गवां शतसहस्राणि दश तेभ्यो ददौ नृपः
दशकोटिं सुवर्णस्य रजतस्य चतुर्गुणम्
verses.transliteration:
gavāṁ śatasahasrāṇi daśa tebhyo dadau nṛpaḥ
daśakoṭiṁ suvarṇasya rajatasya caturguṇam

translations.english: Thus addressed by the Brāhmaṇas versed in the Veda, that best of kings bestowed upon them ten lace of kine, and ten Koțis of gold, and forty of silver.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते न्यायतः कृत्वा प्रविभागं द्विजोत्तमाः
सुप्रीतमनसः सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्मुदिता भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
tataste nyāyataḥ kṛtvā pravibhāgaṁ dvijottamāḥ
suprītamanasaḥ sarve pratyūcurmuditā bhṛśam

translations.english: Then those priests in a body, accepting the wealth, brought it to the ascetic Rșyaśộnga and the intelligent Vasiştha. Then having received each his share, those foremost of regenerate ones were exceedingly pleased, and said, We have been highly gratified.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतमना राजा प्राप्य यज्ञमनुत्तमम्
पापापहं स्वर्नयनं दुस्तरं पार्थिवर्षभैः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prītamanā rājā prāpya yajñamanuttamam
pāpāpahaṁ svarnayanaṁ dustaraṁ pārthivarṣabhaiḥ

translations.english: Then having celebrated that excellent and sindestroying sacrifice, bringing heaven, and incapable of being celebrated by foremost monarchs, king Dasaratha, well pleased, spoke to Rsyasriga, saying, Oyou of excellent vows, it behove you to do that whereby my line may increase.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति च स राजानमुवाच द्विजसत्तमः
भविष्यन्ति सुता राजंश्चत्वारस्ते कुलोद्वहाः
verses.transliteration:
tatheti ca sa rājānamuvāca dvijasattamaḥ
bhaviṣyanti sutā rājaṁścatvāraste kulodvahāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon the best of Brāhmaṇas told the king that he would have four sons, born to him, as perpetuators of his race.

verses.sanskrit:
मेधावी तु ततो ध्यात्वा स किंचिदिदमुत्तमम्
लब्धसंज्ञस्ततस्तं तु वेदज्ञो नृपमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
medhāvī tu tato dhyātvā sa kiṁcididamuttamam
labdhasaṁjñastatastaṁ tu vedajño nṛpamabravīt

translations.english: Then that one of capacious intelligence, versed in the Vedas, having pondered for a time, and regained his senses, returned to the king this excellent answer.

verses.sanskrit:
इष्टिं तेऽहं करिष्यामि पुत्रीयां पुत्रकारणात्
अथर्वशिरसि प्रोक्तैर्मन्त्रैः सिद्धां विधानतः
verses.transliteration:
iṣṭiṁ te'haṁ kariṣyāmi putrīyāṁ putrakāraṇāt
atharvaśirasi proktairmantraiḥ siddhāṁ vidhānataḥ

translations.english: On your behalf, and with the view of obtaining sons for you, I will by help of mantras laid down in the Atharva Veda, duly celebrate the famous ceremony, capable of crowning you with offspring.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्राक्रमदिष्टिं तां पुत्रीयां पुत्र कारणात्
जुहाव चाग्नौ तेजस्वी मन्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prākramadiṣṭiṁ tāṁ putrīyāṁ putra kāraṇāt
juhāva cāgnau tejasvī mantradṛṣṭena karmaṇā

translations.english: Then with the view of obtaining sons (for the king,) that effulgent one set about the sonconferring ceremony; and in accordance with the ordinance, and with mantras, offered oblations to the sacrificial fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
भागप्रतिग्रहार्थं वै समवेता यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
bhāgapratigrahārthaṁ vai samavetā yathāvidhi

translations.english: And the deities, with the Gandharvas, and the Siddhas, and the principal saints, assembled there duly with the object of each obtaining his share of the offerings.

verses.sanskrit:
ताः समेत्य यथान्यायं तस्मिन्सदसि देवताः
अब्रुवँल्लोककर्तारं ब्रह्माणं वचनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
tāḥ sametya yathānyāyaṁ tasminsadasi devatāḥ
abruva̐llokakartāraṁ brahmāṇaṁ vacanaṁ mahat

translations.english: And having duly assembled there, the deities addressed these words to Brahmă the lord of creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन रावणो नाम राक्षसः
सर्वान्नो बाधते वीर्याच्छासितुं तं न शक्नुमः
verses.transliteration:
bhagavaṁstvatprasādena rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
sarvānno bādhate vīryācchāsituṁ taṁ na śaknumaḥ

translations.english: O you possessed of the six attributes, through your grace, a Rākşasa named Rāvaņa oppresses us all by his prowess, nor can we baffle him.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया तस्मै वरो दत्तः प्रीतेन भगवन्पुरा
मानयन्तश्च तं नित्यं सर्वं तस्य क्षमामहे
verses.transliteration:
tvayā tasmai varo dattaḥ prītena bhagavanpurā
mānayantaśca taṁ nityaṁ sarvaṁ tasya kṣamāmahe

translations.english: O lord, as you have well-pleased conferred on him a boon, we always suffer him in deference to it.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्वेजयति लोकांस्त्रीनुच्छ्रितान्द्वेष्टि दुर्मतिः
शक्रं त्रिदशराजानं प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
udvejayati lokāṁstrīnucchritāndveṣṭi durmatiḥ
śakraṁ tridaśarājānaṁ pradharṣayitumicchati

translations.english: The wicked-minded one harasses the three worlds furnished with prosperity, and bears illwill against them and seek o defeat Indra, the king of Tridaśa.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषीन्यक्षान्सगन्धर्वानसुरान्ब्राह्मणांस्तथा
अतिक्रामति दुर्धर्षो वरदानेन मोहितः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣīnyakṣānsagandharvānasurānbrāhmaṇāṁstathā
atikrāmati durdharṣo varadānena mohitaḥ

translations.english: And blinded by the boon he has received, that irrepressible one intends to bring down the lord himself of the celestials, and the Yakşas, and the Gandharvas, and the Brahmanas, and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
नैनं सूर्यः प्रतपति पार्श्वे वाति न मारुतः
चलोर्मिमाली तं दृष्ट्वा समुद्रोऽपि न कम्पते
verses.transliteration:
nainaṁ sūryaḥ pratapati pārśve vāti na mārutaḥ
calormimālī taṁ dṛṣṭvā samudro'pi na kampate

translations.english: And the Sun does not burn him, or the Wind blow about him; and at sight of him, that one engarlanded with billows, the Ocean, dares not stir.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्महन्नो भयं तस्माद्राक्षसाद्घोरदर्शनात्
वधार्थं तस्य भगवन्नुपायं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tanmahanno bhayaṁ tasmādrākṣasādghoradarśanāt
vadhārthaṁ tasya bhagavannupāyaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: Therefore, great is the fear that afflict us, coming from that Rākşasa of dreadful appearance. And, O lord, it behoves you to devise some means for destroying him.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः सुरैः सर्वैश्चिन्तयित्वा ततोऽब्रवीत्
हन्तायं विहितस्तस्य वधोपायो दुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiścintayitvā tato'bravīt
hantāyaṁ vihitastasya vadhopāyo durātmanaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the deities in a body, he said, Alas! I have, however, decided on the means of destroying that wicked-souled one. He had asked, 'May I be incapable of being slain by Gandharvas, and Yaksas, and gods, and Raksasas!,-whereat I said, 'Be it so!'

verses.sanskrit:
नाकीर्तयदवज्ञानात्तद्रक्षो मानुषांस्तदा
तस्मात्स मानुषाद्वध्यो मृत्युर्नान्योऽस्य विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
nākīrtayadavajñānāttadrakṣo mānuṣāṁstadā
tasmātsa mānuṣādvadhyo mṛtyurnānyo'sya vidyate

translations.english: Through disdain, the Rākşasa did not at that time mention men. Therefore, by men alone he is capable of being slain; nor can his end be compassed by any other means.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा प्रियं वाक्यं ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृतम्
देवा महर्षयः सर्वे प्रहृष्टास्तेऽभवंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā priyaṁ vākyaṁ brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam
devā maharṣayaḥ sarve prahṛṣṭāste'bhavaṁstadā

translations.english: Hearing this welcome speech uttered by Brahmā, the deities and the Maharșis became exceedingly delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विष्णुरुपयातो महाद्युतिः
ब्रह्मणा च समागम्य तत्र तस्थौ समाहितः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare viṣṇurupayāto mahādyutiḥ
brahmaṇā ca samāgamya tatra tasthau samāhitaḥ

translations.english: At this juncture, that lord of the universe, the highly-eifulgent Visnu, clad in yellow apparel, and bearing in his hands the conch, the discus, and the mace, and adorned with burnished Keyūras, (A bracelet worn on the upper arm.) arrived there, riding Vinatā's son; like to the Sun riding the clouds. And worshipped by the foremost of the celestials, he drew near Brahmā, and sat down with a collected mind.

verses.sanskrit:
तमब्रुवन्सुराः सर्वे समभिष्टूय संनताः
त्वां नियोक्ष्यामहे विष्णो लोकानां हितकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
tamabruvansurāḥ sarve samabhiṣṭūya saṁnatāḥ
tvāṁ niyokṣyāmahe viṣṇo lokānāṁ hitakāmyayā

translations.english: And bending low before him, the deities spoke to him saying, O Vişnu, for the benefit of the worlds, we shall appoint you to some work.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञो दशरथस्य त्वमयोध्याधिपतेर्विभो
धर्मज्ञस्य वदान्यस्य महर्षिसमतेजसः
तस्य भार्यासु तिसृषु ह्रीश्रीकीर्त्युपमासु च
विष्णो पुत्रत्वमागच्छ कृत्वात्मानं चतुर्विधम्
verses.transliteration:
rājño daśarathasya tvamayodhyādhipatervibho
dharmajñasya vadānyasya maharṣisamatejasaḥ
tasya bhāryāsu tisṛṣu hrīśrīkīrtyupamāsu ca
viṣṇo putratvamāgaccha kṛtvātmānaṁ caturvidham

translations.english: Do you, O lord, dividing yourself into four, O Vişņu, become born a sons in the three wives, resembling Modesty, Auspiciousness, and Fame, of Ayodhyā's lord, king Dasaratha, cognizant of Duty, and munificent, and possessing energy, and like to a Maharsi. Do you, O Visnu, becoming man, slay in battle this thorn of the worlds, the pampered Răvaņa, incapable of being slain by the gods; for the foolish Rākşasa by virtue of sublimated prowess, baffles the deities, and the Gandharvas, and the Siddhas, and the foremost of saints.

verses.sanskrit:
तदुद्धतं रावणमृद्धतेजसं; प्रवृद्धदर्पं त्रिदशेश्वरद्विषम्
विरावणं साधु तपस्विकण्टकं; तपस्विनामुद्धर तं भयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
taduddhataṁ rāvaṇamṛddhatejasaṁ; pravṛddhadarpaṁ tridaśeśvaradviṣam
virāvaṇaṁ sādhu tapasvikaṇṭakaṁ; tapasvināmuddhara taṁ bhayāvaham

translations.english: Do you utterly uproot the haughty Råvaņa of fierce prowess and enhanced insolence-that foe of the lord of celestials, who is the occasion of the tears of the three * Lit. the thorns of pious ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नारायणो विष्णुर्नियुक्तः सुरसत्तमैः
जानन्नपि सुरानेवं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato nārāyaṇo viṣṇurniyuktaḥ surasattamaiḥ
jānannapi surānevaṁ ślakṣṇaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thus besought by the foremost of the celestials, that searcher of hearts, Visnu, although cognizant of the means whereby Rāvana was to be destroyed, asked the gods these amiable words,-What, you gods, is the means of compassing which I could slay that thorn of the ascetics? Nara means a multitude, and Ayana, dwellingplace. He whose dwelling-place is a multitude, is Nārāyana. Metaphorically, the word means evidently the Scorcher of hearts, worlds, and dreadful to ascetics!

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ताः सुराः सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्विष्णुमव्ययम्
मानुषीं तनुमास्थाय रावणं जहि संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcurviṣṇumavyayam
mānuṣīṁ tanumāsthāya rāvaṇaṁ jahi saṁyuge

translations.english: Thus addressed, the deities answered Visnu, incapable of deterioration, saying,-Assuming the form of a human being, do you in battle slay Rāvana!

verses.sanskrit:
स हि तेपे तपस्तीव्रं दीर्घकालमरिंदम
येन तुष्टोऽभवद्ब्रह्मा लोककृल्लोकपूजितः
verses.transliteration:
sa hi tepe tapastīvraṁ dīrghakālamariṁdama
yena tuṣṭo'bhavadbrahmā lokakṛllokapūjitaḥ

translations.english: He, O repressor of foes, had for a long course of time performed rigid austerities; and thereat, that creator of all, the first-create Brahmā, was well pleased.

verses.sanskrit:
संतुष्टः प्रददौ तस्मै राक्षसाय वरं प्रभुः
नानाविधेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो भयं नान्यत्र मानुषात्
verses.transliteration:
saṁtuṣṭaḥ pradadau tasmai rākṣasāya varaṁ prabhuḥ
nānāvidhebhyo bhūtebhyo bhayaṁ nānyatra mānuṣāt

translations.english: And propitiated by his penances, the Master conferred a boon on the Raksasa to the effect, that, save man, no fear should come to him from the various beings.

verses.sanskrit:
अवज्ञाताः पुरा तेन वरदानेन मानवाः
तस्मात्तस्य वधो दृष्टो मानुषेभ्यः परंतप
verses.transliteration:
avajñātāḥ purā tena varadānena mānavāḥ
tasmāttasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhyaḥ paraṁtapa

translations.english: And in the matter of that boon-bestowing, man had formerly been disregarded (by Ravana). And puffed up with pride in consequence of the boon he received from the Grand-sire.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुराणां विष्णुरात्मवान्
पितरं रोचयामास तदा दशरथं नृपम्
verses.transliteration:
ityetadvacanaṁ śrutvā surāṇāṁ viṣṇurātmavān
pitaraṁ rocayāmāsa tadā daśarathaṁ nṛpam

translations.english: Hearing this speech of the celestials, Vişnu of subdued soul chose even king Dasaratha for his father.

verses.sanskrit:
स चाप्यपुत्रो नृपतिस्तस्मिन्काले महाद्युतिः
अयजत्पुत्रियामिष्टिं पुत्रेप्सुररिसूदनः
verses.transliteration:
sa cāpyaputro nṛpatistasminkāle mahādyutiḥ
ayajatputriyāmiṣṭiṁ putrepsurarisūdanaḥ

translations.english: At that time, eagerly wishing to have sons, that destroyer of enemies, the effulgent king Dasaratha, who was sonless, was celebrating the sacrifice that confer male offspring.

verses.sanskrit:
समवेक्ष्याब्रवीद्वाक्यमिदं दशरथं नृपम्
प्राजापत्यं नरं विद्धि मामिहाभ्यागतं नृप
verses.transliteration:
samavekṣyābravīdvākyamidaṁ daśarathaṁ nṛpam
prājāpatyaṁ naraṁ viddhi māmihābhyāgataṁ nṛpa

translations.english: He addressed the king, saying, O monarch, take me as a person commissioned by Prajāpati.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परं तदा राजा प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः
भगवन्स्वागतं तेऽस्तु किमहं करवाणि ते
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paraṁ tadā rājā pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
bhagavansvāgataṁ te'stu kimahaṁ karavāṇi te

translations.english: Hearing him speak thus, Dasaratha, with folded hands, said, Lord, you are welcomed? What can I do for you?

verses.sanskrit:
अथो पुनरिदं वाक्यं प्राजापत्यो नरोऽब्रवीत्
राजन्नर्चयता देवानद्य प्राप्तमिदं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
atho punaridaṁ vākyaṁ prājāpatyo naro'bravīt
rājannarcayatā devānadya prāptamidaṁ tvayā

translations.english: Thereupon, that person despatched by Prajapati again spoke thus, O king, having adored the deities, you have to-day obtained this.

verses.sanskrit:
भार्याणामनुरूपाणामश्नीतेति प्रयच्छ वै
तासु त्वं लप्स्यसे पुत्रान्यदर्थं यजसे नृप
verses.transliteration:
bhāryāṇāmanurūpāṇāmaśnīteti prayaccha vai
tāsu tvaṁ lapsyase putrānyadarthaṁ yajase nṛpa

translations.english: O tiger of a king, accept this excellent and divinely-prepared Pāyasa, conferring sons, health, and affluence, which you are to give to your worthy consorts, saying, Partake it. Through them you will, O monarch, obtain sons, for obtaining whom you have performed this sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति नृपतिः प्रीतः शिरसा प्रतिगृह्य ताम्
पात्रीं देवान्नसंपूर्णां देवदत्तां हिरण्मयीम्
verses.transliteration:
tatheti nṛpatiḥ prītaḥ śirasā pratigṛhya tām
pātrīṁ devānnasaṁpūrṇāṁ devadattāṁ hiraṇmayīm

translations.english: Thereupon, saying, So be it, the lord of men delightedly placed that divinely-bestowed golden vessel filled with the divine Payasa upon his head. And having saluted that wonderful being of gracious presence, he in excess of joy began to go round him again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दशरथः प्राप्य पायसं देवनिर्मितम्
बभूव परमप्रीतः प्राप्य वित्तमिवाधनः
verses.transliteration:
tato daśarathaḥ prāpya pāyasaṁ devanirmitam
babhūva paramaprītaḥ prāpya vittamivādhanaḥ

translations.english: Then Daśaratha, having received that divinely prepared Pāyasa, waxed exceeding glad; like that of a pauper attaining plenty. Then that highly effulgent being of a wonderful form, having performed that mission of his, vanished even there.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्षरश्मिभिरुद्योतं तस्यान्तःपुरमाबभौ
शारदस्याभिरामस्य चन्द्रस्येव नभोंऽशुभिः
verses.transliteration:
harṣaraśmibhirudyotaṁ tasyāntaḥpuramābabhau
śāradasyābhirāmasya candrasyeva nabhoṁ'śubhiḥ

translations.english: And Dasaratha's inner apartment, being graced with the rays of joy, looked like the welkin flooded with the lovely beams of the autumnal moon.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽन्तःपुरं प्रविश्यैव कौसल्यामिदमब्रवीत्
पायसं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्रीयं त्विदमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
so'ntaḥpuraṁ praviśyaiva kausalyāmidamabravīt
pāyasaṁ pratigṛhṇīṣva putrīyaṁ tvidamātmanaḥ

translations.english: Then entering the inner apartment, he spoke to Kausalyā, saying, Take you this, Pāyasa; for this will make you bear a son.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यायै नरपतिः पायसार्धं ददौ तदा
अर्धादर्धं ददौ चापि सुमित्रायै नराधिपः
कैकेय्यै चावशिष्टार्धं ददौ पुत्रार्थकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāyai narapatiḥ pāyasārdhaṁ dadau tadā
ardhādardhaṁ dadau cāpi sumitrāyai narādhipaḥ
kaikeyyai cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṁ dadau putrārthakāraṇāt

translations.english: Having said this, the king offered to her a half portion of this Pāyasa.'Then he conferred upon Sumitrā a fourth of it.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रददौ चावशिष्टार्धं पायसस्यामृतोपमम्
अनुचिन्त्य सुमित्रायै पुनरेव महीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
pradadau cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṁ pāyasasyāmṛtopamam
anucintya sumitrāyai punareva mahīpatiḥ

translations.english: Then in order that she might have a son, king Dasaratha made over to Kaikeyi an equal portion of what remained. And then having reflected, the mighty-minded one gave to Sumitrā the remaining portion of the Pāyasa resembling ambrosia.

verses.sanskrit:
तास्त्वेतत्पायसं प्राप्य नरेन्द्रस्योत्तमाः स्त्रियः
संमानं मेनिरे सर्वाः प्रहर्षोदितचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
tāstvetatpāyasaṁ prāpya narendrasyottamāḥ striyaḥ
saṁmānaṁ menire sarvāḥ praharṣoditacetasaḥ

translations.english: Thus the king dispensed the Pāyasa to each and all of his wives. And those foremost wives of the king, having received that Pāyasa, became exceedingly delighted, and considered themselves as highly honoured.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः
उवाच देवताः सर्वाः स्वयम्भूर्भगवानिदम्
verses.transliteration:
putratvaṁ tu gate viṣṇau rājñastasya mahātmanaḥ
uvāca devatāḥ sarvāḥ svayambhūrbhagavānidam

translations.english: When Vişņu had accepted the sonship of that high-souled king, the self-create Lord addressed the celestials, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
मायाविदश्च शूरांश्च वायुवेगसमाञ्जवे
नयज्ञान्बुद्धिसंपन्नान्विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमान्
verses.transliteration:
māyāvidaśca śūrāṁśca vāyuvegasamāñjave
nayajñānbuddhisaṁpannānviṣṇutulyaparākramān

translations.english: For assisting the heroic Vişnu firm in promise, always seeking the welfare of us all, do you create powerful beings, assuming shapes at will, cognizant of illusions, heroic, furnished with the celerity of the wind, versed in morality, possessing intelligence, like to Vişņu in prowess, unslayable, knowing the ways and means (of war and peace), gifted with excellent bodies, capable of resisting all weapons, and resembling immortals.

verses.sanskrit:
किंनरीणां च गात्रेषु वानरीणां तनूषु च
सृजध्वं हरिरूपेण पुत्रांस्तुल्यपराक्रमान्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁnarīṇāṁ ca gātreṣu vānarīṇāṁ tanūṣu ca
sṛjadhvaṁ harirūpeṇa putrāṁstulyaparākramān

translations.english: And from forth the bodies of the foremost Apsaras, Gandharvis, Yaksis, and Pannagis, Rks is (She-bears) and Vidhyādharis, Kinnaris and Vānaris (She-monkeys) do you produce sons wearing the shapes of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तथोक्ता भगवता तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य शासनम्
जनयामासुरेवं ते पुत्रान्वानररूपिणः
verses.transliteration:
te tathoktā bhagavatā tatpratiśrutya śāsanam
janayāmāsurevaṁ te putrānvānararūpiṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing this mandate of Him possessed of the six attributes, they began to produce sons endowed with monkey's forms.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषयश्च महात्मानः सिद्धविद्याधरोरगाः
चारणाश्च सुतान्वीरान्ससृजुर्वनचारिणः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣayaśca mahātmānaḥ siddhavidyādharoragāḥ
cāraṇāśca sutānvīrānsasṛjurvanacāriṇaḥ

translations.english: And high-souled ascetics, and Siddhas, and Vidyādharas, and Uragas, and Caranas, generated heroic sons, rangers of woods.

verses.sanskrit:
ते सृष्टा बहुसाहस्रा दशग्रीववधोद्यताः
अप्रमेयबला वीरा विक्रान्ताः कामरूपिणः
verses.transliteration:
te sṛṣṭā bahusāhasrā daśagrīvavadhodyatāḥ
aprameyabalā vīrā vikrāntāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ

translations.english: And the most intelligent as well as the most powerful amongst all the principal monkeys. Thus produced, there suddenly came into being by thousands, mighty bears, and monkeys, and Gopucchas, (Cow-tailed monkeys.) and of immeasurable strength, and heroic, and powerful, assuming shapes at will, endowed with bodies resembling elephants or hills, even those who would engage in compassing the destruction of the Ten-headed Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य देवस्य यद्रूपं वेषो यश्च पराक्रमः
अजायत समस्तेन तस्य तस्य सुतः पृथक्
verses.transliteration:
yasya devasya yadrūpaṁ veṣo yaśca parākramaḥ
ajāyata samastena tasya tasya sutaḥ pṛthak

translations.english: The sons of the deities retained distinctly the respective hues, forins, and prowess, that characterized their several sires. And those that sprang from the Golāngulas, possessed even more than the might of the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
विचालयेयुः शैलेन्द्रान्भेदयेयुः स्थिरान्द्रुमान्
क्षोभयेयुश्च वेगेन समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
