vicālayeyuḥ śailendrānbhedayeyuḥ sthirāndrumān
kṣobhayeyuśca vegena samudraṁ saritāṁ patim

translations.english: And they fought with nails and teeth, and were accomplished in all weapons. And they could move the largest hills, and crush the fixed trees,

verses.sanskrit:
दारयेयुः क्षितिं पद्भ्यामाप्लवेयुर्महार्णवम्
नभस्तलं विशेयुश्च गृह्णीयुरपि तोयदान्
verses.transliteration:
dārayeyuḥ kṣitiṁ padbhyāmāplaveyurmahārṇavam
nabhastalaṁ viśeyuśca gṛhṇīyurapi toyadān

translations.english: With their impetus, vex that lord of rivers, the Ocean. And they could with their kicks rend the Earth, and swim over the mighty main.

verses.sanskrit:
गृह्णीयुरपि मातङ्गान्मत्तान्प्रव्रजतो वने
नर्दमानांश्च नादेन पातयेयुर्विहंगमान्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhṇīyurapi mātaṅgānmattānpravrajato vane
nardamānāṁśca nādena pātayeyurvihaṁgamān

translations.english: They could penetrate into the welkin, and capture the clouds. And they could subdue mad elephants ranging the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
ईदृशानां प्रसूतानि हरीणां कामरूपिणाम्
शतं शतसहस्राणि यूथपानां महात्मनाम्
बभूवुर्यूथपश्रेष्ठा वीरांश्चाजनयन्हरीन्
verses.transliteration:
īdṛśānāṁ prasūtāni harīṇāṁ kāmarūpiṇām
śataṁ śatasahasrāṇi yūthapānāṁ mahātmanām
babhūvuryūthapaśreṣṭhā vīrāṁścājanayanharīn

translations.english: And with their roars, they could bring down birds singing. Thus came into being Koțis of high-souled leaders of monkey-herds, assuming forms at will.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ये ऋक्षवतः प्रस्थानुपतस्थुः सहस्रशः
अन्ये नानाविधाञ्शैलान्काननानि च भेजिरे
verses.transliteration:
anye ṛkṣavataḥ prasthānupatasthuḥ sahasraśaḥ
anye nānāvidhāñśailānkānanāni ca bhejire

translations.english: Some of these monkeys began to dwell on the top of the Rkşavān mountain; while others inhabited various other mountains and forests.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्मेघवृन्दाचलकूटकल्पै;र्महाबलैर्वानरयूथपालैः
बभूव भूर्भीमशरीररूपैः; समावृता रामसहायहेतोः
verses.transliteration:
tairmeghavṛndācalakūṭakalpai;rmahābalairvānarayūthapālaiḥ
babhūva bhūrbhīmaśarīrarūpaiḥ; samāvṛtā rāmasahāyahetoḥ

translations.english: This earth, furnished with mountains, and forests, and oceans, began to teem with those heroic lords of leaders of monkey-herds, inhabiting different places, bearing characteristic marks, resembling masses of clouds, mountain-peaks, possessed of mighty strength, and of terrible bodies and visages, in order that they might assist Rāma. or

verses.sanskrit:
निर्वृत्ते तु क्रतौ तस्मिन्हयमेधे महात्मनः
प्रतिगृह्य सुरा भागान्प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
nirvṛtte tu kratau tasminhayamedhe mahātmanaḥ
pratigṛhya surā bhāgānpratijagmuryathāgatam

translations.english: When the horse-sacrifice of the high-souled Dasaratha had been completed, the immortals, accepting each his share, returned whence they had come.

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्तदीक्षानियमः पत्नीगणसमन्वितः
प्रविवेश पुरीं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
samāptadīkṣāniyamaḥ patnīgaṇasamanvitaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ

translations.english: And the monarch, having observed all the rules of initiation, entered the palace with his equipage and retinue.

verses.sanskrit:
यथार्हं पूजितास्तेन राज्ञा वै पृथिवीश्वराः
मुदिताः प्रययुर्देशान्प्रणम्य मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
yathārhaṁ pūjitāstena rājñā vai pṛthivīśvarāḥ
muditāḥ prayayurdeśānpraṇamya munipuṁgavam

translations.english: And the lords of the earth, having been received suitably by the king, with glad hearts set out for their own countries, saluting that foremost of ascetics (Rsyaśặnga).

verses.sanskrit:
गतेषु पृथिवीशेषु राजा दशरथः पुनः
प्रविवेश पुरीं श्रीमान्पुरस्कृत्य द्विजोत्तमान्
verses.transliteration:
gateṣu pṛthivīśeṣu rājā daśarathaḥ punaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ śrīmānpuraskṛtya dvijottamān

translations.english: When the lords of the earth had gone away, the graceful king Dasaratha re-entered his palace, with the foremost of regenerate ones at his head.

verses.sanskrit:
शान्तया प्रययौ सार्धमृश्यशृङ्गः सुपूजितः
अन्वीयमानो राज्ञाथ सानुयात्रेण धीमता
verses.transliteration:
śāntayā prayayau sārdhamṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ supūjitaḥ
anvīyamāno rājñātha sānuyātreṇa dhīmatā

translations.english: Followed by the intelligent monarch with his retinue, Rsyasrnga, having been duly honoured, set out with śāntā. Having thus dismissed them all, the king, his object attained, began to dwell there happily, expecting sons.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतो नाम कैकेय्यां जज्ञे सत्यपराक्रमः
साक्षाद्विष्णोश्चतुर्भागः सर्वैः समुदितो गुणैः
verses.transliteration:
bharato nāma kaikeyyāṁ jajñe satyaparākramaḥ
sākṣādviṣṇoścaturbhāgaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ

translations.english: Then was born of Kaikeyī, named Bharata, having truth for prowess, endowed with all the virtues, and representing the very fourth part of Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ सुमित्राजनयत्सुतौ
वीरौ सर्वास्त्रकुशलौ विष्णोरर्धसमन्वितौ
verses.transliteration:
atha lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau sumitrājanayatsutau
vīrau sarvāstrakuśalau viṣṇorardhasamanvitau

translations.english: Then Sumitrā gave birth to Lakşmaņa and Satrughna, heroic, and skilled in all weapons, and endowed with the half of Vişnu.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञः पुत्रा महात्मानश्चत्वारो जज्ञिरे पृथक्
गुणवन्तोऽनुरूपाश्च रुच्या प्रोष्ठपदोपमाः
verses.transliteration:
rājñaḥ putrā mahātmānaścatvāro jajñire pṛthak
guṇavanto'nurūpāśca rucyā proṣṭhapadopamāḥ

translations.english: Thus were separately born four high-souled sons to the king, crowned with qualities, and graceful, and in loveliness resembling the constellations Prosthapada.* Thereat the Gandharvas began to chaunt sweetly, and the Apsaras to dance. And the celestial kettledrums sounded; and there showered down blossoms from the sky. *Otherwise called Uttarabhadrapada and Purvabhādrapada.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीत्यैकादशाहं तु नाम कर्म तथाकरोत्
ज्येष्ठं रामं महात्मानं भरतं कैकयीसुतम्
verses.transliteration:
atītyaikādaśāhaṁ tu nāma karma tathākarot
jyeṣṭhaṁ rāmaṁ mahātmānaṁ bharataṁ kaikayīsutam

translations.english: When the eleventh day had gone by, the king performed the Naming ceremony of his sons. And experiencing great delight, Vasistha conferred the names. And the high-souled eldest one was called Rāma; and Kaikeyi's son was called Bharata; and Sumitrā's son was called Laksmana, and the last was named Satrughna.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां केतुरिव ज्येष्ठो रामो रतिकरः पितुः
बभूव भूयो भूतानां स्वयम्भूरिव संमतः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ keturiva jyeṣṭho rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ
babhūva bhūyo bhūtānāṁ svayambhūriva saṁmataḥ

translations.english: Thus did he celebrate the natal rites of the princes. And among all those princes, the eldest, Rāma, like that of Ketu, (The ninth of the planets.) and the special delight of his father, became the object of general regard, even as the self-create Himself. And all of them were versed in the Vedas, and heroic, and intent upon the welfare of others.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मिसंपन्नो बहिःप्राण इवापरः
न च तेन विना निद्रां लभते पुरुषोत्तमः
मृष्टमन्नमुपानीतमश्नाति न हि तं विना
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇo lakṣmisaṁpanno bahiḥprāṇa ivāparaḥ
na ca tena vinā nidrāṁ labhate puruṣottamaḥ
mṛṣṭamannamupānītamaśnāti na hi taṁ vinā

translations.english: And even from early youth, that enhancer of auspiciousness Laksmana was ever attached to his eldest brother Rāma, that delight of all. And like to another life of Rāma, Lakşmaņa furnished with auspiciousness was in everything attentive to Rāma's wishes, even at the neglect of his own person. And that foremost of persons did not even attain sleep without Rāma's company, nor did he partake any sweetmeat that was offered, unless Rāma partook it with him.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्यापि शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणावरजो हि सः
प्राणैः प्रियतरो नित्यं तस्य चासीत्तथा प्रियः
verses.transliteration:
bharatasyāpi śatrughno lakṣmaṇāvarajo hi saḥ
prāṇaiḥ priyataro nityaṁ tasya cāsīttathā priyaḥ

translations.english: When mounted on horse-back, Rāghava went a-hunting, Lakṣmaṇa went at his back bow in hand, protecting him. And that younger brother of Laksmana, Satrughna, likewise became ever dearer to Bharata than life itself.

verses.sanskrit:
स चतुर्भिर्महाभागैः पुत्रैर्दशरथः प्रियैः
बभूव परमप्रीतो देवैरिव पितामहः
verses.transliteration:
sa caturbhirmahābhāgaiḥ putrairdaśarathaḥ priyaiḥ
babhūva paramaprīto devairiva pitāmahaḥ

translations.english: On account of those exalted and well-beloved sons of his, Dasaratha experienced the excess of joy, like to the Grand-sire on account of the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
ते यदा ज्ञानसंपन्नाः सर्वे समुदिता गुणैः
ह्रीमन्तः कीर्तिमन्तश्च सर्वज्ञा दीर्घदर्शिनः
verses.transliteration:
te yadā jñānasaṁpannāḥ sarve samuditā guṇaiḥ
hrīmantaḥ kīrtimantaśca sarvajñā dīrghadarśinaḥ

translations.english: And when they came to be furnished with knowledge, and crowned with virtues, and endowed with bashfulness and fame, and to attain wisdom in everything, and to be farsighted, Dasaratha, the father of such powerful and flamingly effulgent sons, became delighted even like that lord of worlds-Brahmā.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ राजा दशरथस्तेषां दारक्रियां प्रति
चिन्तयामास धर्मात्मा सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
atha rājā daśarathasteṣāṁ dārakriyāṁ prati
cintayāmāsa dharmātmā sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ

translations.english: Once upon a time, when the virtuous king Dasaratha, surrounded by his priests and friends, was reflecting about the nuptials of his sons, to that high-souled one engaged in thought in the midst of his counsellors came the mighty ascetic Visvamitra.

verses.sanskrit:
स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी द्वाराध्यक्षानुवाच ह
शीघ्रमाख्यात मां प्राप्तं कौशिकं गाधिनः सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī dvārādhyakṣānuvāca ha
śīghramākhyāta māṁ prāptaṁ kauśikaṁ gādhinaḥ sutam

translations.english: Desirous of seeing the king, he said to the warders,-Do you speedily announce that I, Gadhi's son, sprung in the Kusika line, have come!

verses.sanskrit:
ते गत्वा राजभवनं विश्वामित्रमृषिं तदा
प्राप्तमावेदयामासुर्नृपायेक्ष्वाकवे तदा
verses.transliteration:
te gatvā rājabhavanaṁ viśvāmitramṛṣiṁ tadā
prāptamāvedayāmāsurnṛpāyekṣvākave tadā

translations.english: Hearing those words of his, they, urged on by them, all hurriedly began to run towards the royal chambers. And coming to the royal apartments, they communicated to Ikşváku's descendant the arrival of the ascetic Viśvāmitra.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सपुरोधाः समाहितः
प्रत्युज्जगाम संहृष्टो ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā sapurodhāḥ samāhitaḥ
pratyujjagāma saṁhṛṣṭo brahmāṇamiva vāsavaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of theirs, Dasaratha surrounded by his priests, went out delightedly to meet him, like Indra going out to meet Brhaspati. According to Śruti BỊhaspati is the Brahmă of the gods-Brhaspatir devānām Brahmā.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा ज्वलितं दीप्त्या तापसं संशितव्रतम्
प्रहृष्टवदनो राजा ततोऽर्घ्यमुपहारयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā jvalitaṁ dīptyā tāpasaṁ saṁśitavratam
prahṛṣṭavadano rājā tato'rghyamupahārayat

translations.english: And having come to that ascetic observing vows and of flaming energy, the monarch with a cheerful countenance offered him the Arghya.

verses.sanskrit:
स राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्यार्घ्यं शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा
कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव पर्यपृच्छन्नराधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājñaḥ pratigṛhyārghyaṁ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
kuśalaṁ cāvyayaṁ caiva paryapṛcchannarādhipam

translations.english: There upon, having accepted the king's Arghya in accordance with the ordinance he enquired of the lord of men as to his continued prosperity and peace.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठं च समागम्य कुशलं मुनिपुंगवः
ऋषींश्च तान्यथा न्यायं महाभागानुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhaṁ ca samāgamya kuśalaṁ munipuṁgavaḥ
ṛṣīṁśca tānyathā nyāyaṁ mahābhāgānuvāca ha

translations.english: And approaching Vasiştha and the other anchorites, that foremost of ascetics of exalted piety duly asked them regarding their welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसस्तस्य राज्ञो निवेशनम्
विविशुः पूजितास्तत्र निषेदुश्च यथार्थतः
verses.transliteration:
te sarve hṛṣṭamanasastasya rājño niveśanam
viviśuḥ pūjitāstatra niṣeduśca yathārthataḥ

translations.english: And having been properly received by the monarch, they with glad hearts entered the royal residence, and sat them down according to precedence.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ हृष्टमना राजा विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम्
उवाच परमोदारो हृष्टस्तमभिपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
atha hṛṣṭamanā rājā viśvāmitraṁ mahāmunim
uvāca paramodāro hṛṣṭastamabhipūjayan

translations.english: Then gladly worshipping the mighty ascetic, Visvāmitra, the exceedingly generous king, wellpleased, addressed him saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यथामृतस्य संप्राप्तिर्यथा वर्षमनूदके
यथा सदृशदारेषु पुत्रजन्माप्रजस्य च
प्रनष्टस्य यथा लाभो यथा हर्षो महोदये
तथैवागमनं मन्ये स्वागतं ते महामुने
verses.transliteration:
yathāmṛtasya saṁprāptiryathā varṣamanūdake
yathā sadṛśadāreṣu putrajanmāprajasya ca
pranaṣṭasya yathā lābho yathā harṣo mahodaye
tathaivāgamanaṁ manye svāgataṁ te mahāmune

translations.english: Like that of the obtaining of ambrosia, like to a shower in a land suffering from drought, like to the birth of sons of worthy wives to him without issue, like that of the recovery of a lost thing, yea, like to the dawning of a mighty joy, I consider this your arrival. O illustrious ascetic, are you well come? What is even that which is nearest to your heart?

verses.sanskrit:
कं च ते परमं कामं करोमि किमु हर्षितः
पात्रभूतोऽसि मे विप्र दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि धार्मिक
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवितं च सुजीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
kaṁ ca te paramaṁ kāmaṁ karomi kimu harṣitaḥ
pātrabhūto'si me vipra diṣṭyā prāpto'si dhārmika
adya me saphalaṁ janma jīvitaṁ ca sujīvitam

translations.english: You, O Brahmana, are worthy of my best services. By luck it is that, O bestower of honour, I have gained you. To-day my birth has been crowned with fruit to-day has my life attained its object.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं राजर्षिशब्देन तपसा द्योतितप्रभः
ब्रह्मर्षित्वमनुप्राप्तः पूज्योऽसि बहुधा मया
verses.transliteration:
pūrvaṁ rājarṣiśabdena tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ
brahmarṣitvamanuprāptaḥ pūjyo'si bahudhā mayā

translations.english: And truly yesterday night has been succeeded by an auspicious morning, since I have beheld you. Having first attained exceeding effulgence by virtue of austerities performed for obtaining the title of Rājarşi, you have afterwards obtained the status of a Brahmarși. You are worthy of manifold homage from me. This your exceedingly holy arrival appear wonderful.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूहि यत्प्रार्थितं तुभ्यं कार्यमागमनं प्रति
इच्छाम्यनुगृहीतोऽहं त्वदर्थपरिवृद्धये
verses.transliteration:
brūhi yatprārthitaṁ tubhyaṁ kāryamāgamanaṁ prati
icchāmyanugṛhīto'haṁ tvadarthaparivṛddhaye

translations.english: O lord, by beholding you, surely my body has been rendered pure. Tell me, what is it that you would have, and what is the purpose of your coming?

verses.sanskrit:
इति हृदयसुखं निशम्य वाक्यं; श्रुतिसुखमात्मवता विनीतमुक्तम्
प्रथितगुणयशा गुणैर्विशिष्टः; परम ऋषिः परमं जगाम हर्षम्
verses.transliteration:
iti hṛdayasukhaṁ niśamya vākyaṁ; śrutisukhamātmavatā vinītamuktam
prathitaguṇayaśā guṇairviśiṣṭaḥ; parama ṛṣiḥ paramaṁ jagāma harṣam

translations.english: Hearing this soul-soothing, ear-charming, and free-humble speech that was uttered, the illustrious prime of ascetics crowned with virtues, and furnished with all perfections, experienced exceeding delight.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम्
हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā rājasiṁhasya vākyamadbhutavistaram
hṛṣṭaromā mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Hearing those astonishing words of that lionlike king, the highly-energetic Viśvāmitra with his down standing on end, said.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं राजशार्दूल तवैतद्भुवि नान्यतः
महावंशप्रसूतस्य वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिनः
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ rājaśārdūla tavaitadbhuvi nānyataḥ
mahāvaṁśaprasūtasya vasiṣṭhavyapadeśinaḥ

translations.english: O tiger of a king, sprung from an illustrious line, and having Vasistha, for your guide, these words become you alone on earth and no one else.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तु मे हृद्गतं वाक्यं तस्य कार्यस्य निश्चयम्
कुरुष्व राजशार्दूल भव सत्यप्रतिश्रवः
verses.transliteration:
yattu me hṛdgataṁ vākyaṁ tasya kāryasya niścayam
kuruṣva rājaśārdūla bhava satyapratiśravaḥ

translations.english: Do you, O tiger of a king, ascertain your course in respect of the matter I bear in my heart; and do you prove firm in promise!

verses.sanskrit:
अहं नियममातिष्ठे सिद्ध्यर्थं पुरुषर्षभ
तस्य विघ्नकरौ द्वौ तु राक्षसौ कामरूपिणौ
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ niyamamātiṣṭhe siddhyarthaṁ puruṣarṣabha
tasya vighnakarau dvau tu rākṣasau kāmarūpiṇau

translations.english: For celebrating a sacrifice, I, O foremost of men, abide by some prescribed course. And it comes to pass that two Rākşasas assuming shapes at will, have become bent upon disturbing the ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
व्रते मे बहुशश्चीर्णे समाप्त्यां राक्षसाविमौ
मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च वीर्यवन्तौ सुशिक्षितौ
तौ मांसरुधिरौघेण वेदिं तामभ्यवर्षताम्
verses.transliteration:
vrate me bahuśaścīrṇe samāptyāṁ rākṣasāvimau
mārīcaśca subāhuśca vīryavantau suśikṣitau
tau māṁsarudhiraugheṇa vediṁ tāmabhyavarṣatām

translations.english: And in that sacrifice which I have determined to bring to a completion, and which is on the eve of being completed, both these Rākşasas, Mārica and Subāhu, accomplished in arms and possessed of prowess, shower flesh and gore upon the altar. And on that ceremony being thus disturbed and by purpose thus frustrated, I considered my labours as all lost, and, therefore, have left my country in dejection. And, O monarch, I cannot bring myself to vent my wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वपुत्रं राजशार्दूल रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्
काकपक्षधरं शूरं ज्येष्ठं मे दातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
svaputraṁ rājaśārdūla rāmaṁ satyaparākramam
kākapakṣadharaṁ śūraṁ jyeṣṭhaṁ me dātumarhasi

translations.english: For such is the nature of that business, that it is not proper for one engaged in it to utter a curse. Therefore, O tiger of a monarch, it behoves you to grant me your eldest son, the heroic Rāma of genuine prowess, with the sidelocks.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं वेद्मि महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्
वसिष्ठोऽपि महातेजा ये चेमे तपसि स्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ vedmi mahātmānaṁ rāmaṁ satyaparākramam
vasiṣṭho'pi mahātejā ye ceme tapasi sthitāḥ

translations.english: Nor, o king, ought you to indulge in paternal affection. For ten nights only Rāma is to remain there, with the object of slaying those foes to my sacrifice, those Raksasas disturbing the rites. I tell you, do you consider the Raksasas as already slain. I know full well Rāma of sterling prowess, as also the highly-energetic Vasistha and the other ascetics present here. And if you, O king, set your heart upon acquiring religious merit and high fame on earth, do you then grant me Rāma!

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यभ्यनुज्ञां काकुत्स्थ ददते तव मन्त्रिणः
वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्वे ततो रामं विसर्जय
verses.transliteration:
yadyabhyanujñāṁ kākutstha dadate tava mantriṇaḥ
vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarve tato rāmaṁ visarjaya

translations.english: And, O Kākutstha, * if your counsellors together with the Brāhmaṇas having Vasistha at their head, consent, do you then dismiss Rāma! *From Kakud, an emblem of royalty, and Stha, residing, meaning a prince, the grandson of Iksvāku.

verses.sanskrit:
नात्येति कालो यज्ञस्य यथायं मम राघव
तथा कुरुष्व भद्रं ते मा च शोके मनः कृथाः
verses.transliteration:
nātyeti kālo yajñasya yathāyaṁ mama rāghava
tathā kuruṣva bhadraṁ te mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ

translations.english: Even this is my wish, and he also has come of age. Do you, therefore, part with your son, the lotus-eyed Rāma, for the ten days of the sacrifice! Do you act so, O descendant of Raghu, that the time appointed for the ceremony may not be overpassed. Good betide you! Let not your mind indulge in grief!

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा धर्मात्मा धर्मार्थसहितं वचः
विरराम महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā dharmātmā dharmārthasahitaṁ vacaḥ
virarāma mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ

translations.english: Having said these words consistent with virtue and interest, the mighty-minded and highlypowerful Viśvāmitra paused.

verses.sanskrit:
इति हृदयमनोविदारणं; मुनिवचनं तदतीव शुश्रुवान्
नरपतिरगमद्भयं मह;द्व्यथितमनाः प्रचचाल चासनात्
verses.transliteration:
iti hṛdayamanovidāraṇaṁ; munivacanaṁ tadatīva śuśruvān
narapatiragamadbhayaṁ maha;dvyathitamanāḥ pracacāla cāsanāt

translations.english: Then, having regained his senses, he rose up, and became cast down through apprehension. Having heard the words of the ascetic, capable of rending the mind and heart, the high-souled king of men became stricken with grief and shook on his seat.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राजशार्दूल विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम्
मुहूर्तमिव निःसंज्ञः संज्ञावानिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā rājaśārdūla viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam
muhūrtamiva niḥsaṁjñaḥ saṁjñāvānidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of Viśvāmitra, that tiger of a monarch remained insensible for a time, and then regaining his senses, spoke thus.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊनषोडशवर्षो मे रामो राजीवलोचनः
न युद्धयोग्यतामस्य पश्यामि सह राक्षसैः
verses.transliteration:
ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣo me rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
na yuddhayogyatāmasya paśyāmi saha rākṣasaiḥ

translations.english: My lotus-eyed Ráma is not yet turned of sixteen; and I do not perceive his fitness to cope with Raksasas in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
इयमक्षौहिणी पूर्णा यस्याहं पतिरीश्वरः
अनया संवृतो गत्वा योधाहं तैर्निशाचरैः
verses.transliteration:
iyamakṣauhiṇī pūrṇā yasyāhaṁ patirīśvaraḥ
anayā saṁvṛto gatvā yodhāhaṁ tairniśācaraiḥ

translations.english: I am the lord of this Akşauhiņi (A complete army consisting of 1,09,350 foot, 65,610 horse, 21,870 chariots, and 21,870 elephants.) of forces. Marching with this, will I engage with the night-rangers.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे शूराश्च विक्रान्ता भृत्या मेऽस्त्रविशारदाः
योग्या रक्षोगणैर्योद्धुं न रामं नेतुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ime śūrāśca vikrāntā bhṛtyā me'straviśāradāḥ
yogyā rakṣogaṇairyoddhuṁ na rāmaṁ netumarhasi

translations.english: And these servants of mine are Valiant, and warlike, and accomplished in weapons, and capable of fighting the Rākşasas,-therefore, it behove you not to take Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमेव धनुष्पाणिर्गोप्ता समरमूर्धनि
यावत्प्राणान्धरिष्यामि तावद्योत्स्ये निशाचरैः
verses.transliteration:
ahameva dhanuṣpāṇirgoptā samaramūrdhani
yāvatprāṇāndhariṣyāmi tāvadyotsye niśācaraiḥ

translations.english: And myself bow in hand, stationed at the van of the array, will battle with the rangers of the night as long as life is spared to me.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्विघ्ना व्रतचर्या सा भविष्यति सुरक्षिता
अहं तत्र गमिष्यामि न राम नेतुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
nirvighnā vratacaryā sā bhaviṣyati surakṣitā
ahaṁ tatra gamiṣyāmi na rāma netumarhasi

translations.english: Then well protected, your sacrifice will hold an unimpeded course. Therefore, I will repair thither, and it behoves you not to take Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
बालो ह्यकृतविद्यश्च न च वेत्ति बलाबलम्
न चास्त्रबलसंयुक्तो न च युद्धविशारदः
न चासौ रक्षसां योग्यः कूटयुद्धा हि ते ध्रुवम्
verses.transliteration:
bālo hyakṛtavidyaśca na ca vetti balābalam
na cāstrabalasaṁyukto na ca yuddhaviśāradaḥ
na cāsau rakṣasāṁ yogyaḥ kūṭayuddhā hi te dhruvam

translations.english: Youthful, and unaccomplished, and not knowing what constitutes strength and what not, and not equipped with the science of missiles, and unskilful in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रयुक्तो हि रामेण मुहूर्तमपि नोत्सहे
जीवितुं मुनिशार्दूल न रामं नेतुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtamapi notsahe
jīvituṁ muniśārdūla na rāmaṁ netumarhasi

translations.english: He is not a match for Räkşasas,-they being deceitful warriors. Bereft of Rāma, O tiger among ascetics, I cannot live for a moment. Therefore, it behove you not to take him. If, O Brahman, it is your intention to take Rāma, then O you of excellent vows, do you also take me along with the Caturanga forces! (An army consisting of foot, horse, elephants, and cars.)

verses.sanskrit:
षष्टिर्वर्षसहस्राणि जातस्य मम कौशिक
दुःखेनोत्पादितश्चायं न रामं नेतुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi jātasya mama kauśika
duḥkhenotpāditaścāyaṁ na rāmaṁ netumarhasi

translations.english: O Kusika's son, I am sixty thousand years old; and (at this age) I have obtained Rāma after undergoing extreme troubles, it therefore, become you not to take Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्णामात्मजानां हि प्रीतिः परमिका मम
ज्येष्ठं धर्मप्रधानं च न रामं नेतुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
caturṇāmātmajānāṁ hi prītiḥ paramikā mama
jyeṣṭhaṁ dharmapradhānaṁ ca na rāmaṁ netumarhasi

translations.english: And among the four sons of mine, I find my highest delight in Rāma, my first-born, and the most virtuous of them all, therefore, it behoves you not to take Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
किं वीर्या राक्षसास्ते च कस्य पुत्राश्च के च ते
कथं प्रमाणाः के चैतान्रक्षन्ति मुनिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ vīryā rākṣasāste ca kasya putrāśca ke ca te
kathaṁ pramāṇāḥ ke caitānrakṣanti munipuṁgava

translations.english: What is the prowess of the Rākşasas? And whose sons are they? And who, pray are they? And what are the proportions of their bodies? And who protects them O foremost of ascetics? And by what means shall either Rāma, or my forces, or, O Brahman, I myself be able to slay in fight those deceitful warriors—the Rākṣasas? Do you tell me, O adorable ore, inflated as they are by virtue of their prowess, how can I stand them in fight?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयते हि महावीर्यो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
साक्षाद्वैश्रवणभ्राता पुत्रो विश्रवसो मुनेः
verses.transliteration:
śrūyate hi mahāvīryo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
sākṣādvaiśravaṇabhrātā putro viśravaso muneḥ

translations.english: Hearing that speech of his, Viśvāmitra said, There is a Rākşasa named Rāvana, sprung from the line of Pulastya. Having obtained a boon from Brahmā, he boldly opposes himself to three worlds, being possessed of great strength and prowess, and backed by innumerable Räksasas. And, O mighty monarch, I also hear that that lord of the Rākṣasas is the very brother of Vaisravana and the son of the ascetic Viśravaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा स्वयं न यज्ञस्य विघ्नकर्ता महाबलः
तेन संचोदितौ तौ तु राक्षसौ सुमहाबलौ
मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च यज्ञविघ्नं करिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
yadā svayaṁ na yajñasya vighnakartā mahābalaḥ
tena saṁcoditau tau tu rākṣasau sumahābalau
mārīcaśca subāhuśca yajñavighnaṁ kariṣyataḥ

translations.english: When that one possessed of mighty strength does not stoop to disturb the sacrifice himself, those powerful Raksasas, Marica and Subāhu, being incited by him, disturb the rites.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तो मुनिना तेन राजोवाच मुनिं तदा
न हि शक्तोऽस्मि संग्रामे स्थातुं तस्य दुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ityukto muninā tena rājovāca muniṁ tadā
na hi śakto'smi saṁgrāme sthātuṁ tasya durātmanaḥ

translations.english: The ascetic having spoken thus, the king then answered him, I am incapable of standing that wicked-souled one in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं प्रसादं धर्मज्ञ कुरुष्व मम पुत्रके
देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षाः पतगपन्नगाः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ prasādaṁ dharmajña kuruṣva mama putrake
devadānavagandharvā yakṣāḥ patagapannagāḥ

translations.english: Therefore, do you, O you versed in morality, extend your favour to my son! Of slender fortune as I am, you are my guide and my god.

verses.sanskrit:
न शक्ता रावणं सोढुं किं पुनर्मानवा युधि
स हि वीर्यवतां वीर्यमादत्ते युधि राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
na śaktā rāvaṇaṁ soḍhuṁ kiṁ punarmānavā yudhi
sa hi vīryavatāṁ vīryamādatte yudhi rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Even the celestials and the Dānavas and the Gandharvas and the Birds and the Snakes are incapable of bearing Rāvana in battle, what then is man?

verses.sanskrit:
तेन चाहं न शक्तोऽस्मि संयोद्धुं तस्य वा बलैः
सबलो वा मुनिश्रेष्ठ सहितो वा ममात्मजैः
verses.transliteration:
tena cāhaṁ na śakto'smi saṁyoddhuṁ tasya vā balaiḥ
sabalo vā muniśreṣṭha sahito vā mamātmajaiḥ

translations.english: O foremost of ascetics, whether you are accompanied with my son or my forces, you will not be able to stand him. And how can I, O Brāhmaṇa, make over to you my son, of tender years, resembling an immortal, who is ignorant of warfare? I will not part with my son.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ कालोपमौ युद्धे सुतौ सुन्दोपसुन्दयोः
यज्ञविघ्नकरौ तौ ते नैव दास्यामि पुत्रकम्
verses.transliteration:
atha kālopamau yuddhe sutau sundopasundayoḥ
yajñavighnakarau tau te naiva dāsyāmi putrakam

translations.english: The sons of Sunda and Upasunda resemble Kāla himself in battle, and it is they who are disturbing your sacrifice. Therefore I will not part with my son. And Mārīca and Subāhu are possessed of prowess, and accomplished in weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य स्नेहपर्याकुलाक्षरम्
समन्युः कौशिको वाक्यं प्रत्युवच महीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vacanaṁ tasya snehaparyākulākṣaram
samanyuḥ kauśiko vākyaṁ pratyuvaca mahīpatim

translations.english: Hearing those words of Dasaratha's composed of letters faltering with affection, Kusika's son, stirred up with anger, answered the monarch, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्ह्वमर्थं प्रतिश्रुत्य प्रतिज्ञां हातुमिच्छसि
रागवाणामयुक्तोऽयं कुलस्यास्य विपर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
pūrhvamarthaṁ pratiśrutya pratijñāṁ hātumicchasi
rāgavāṇāmayukto'yaṁ kulasyāsya viparyayaḥ

translations.english: Having promised me first, you endeavour to renounce that proinise of yours. This surely is unworthy of a descendant of Raghu, and this can bring destruction upon the dynasty.

verses.sanskrit:
यदिदं ते क्षमं राजन्गमिष्यामि यथागतम्
मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञः काकुत्स्थ सुखी भव सबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
yadidaṁ te kṣamaṁ rājangamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
mithyāpratijñaḥ kākutstha sukhī bhava sabāndhavaḥ

translations.english: If, O king, in acting thus, you have acted properly, I will then repair to the place whence I had come. O Kākutstha's descendant false in promise, do you attain happiness, being surrounded by your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रोषपरीतस्य विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः
चचाल वसुधा कृत्स्ना विवेश च भयं सुरान्
verses.transliteration:
tasya roṣaparītasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
cacāla vasudhā kṛtsnā viveśa ca bhayaṁ surān

translations.english: And when the intelligent Viśvāmitra was exercised with wrath, the entire earth began to tremble, and the gods even were inspired with awe.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रस्तरूपं तु विज्ञाय जगत्सर्वं महानृषिः
नृपतिं सुव्रतो धीरो वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
trastarūpaṁ tu vijñāya jagatsarvaṁ mahānṛṣiḥ
nṛpatiṁ suvrato dhīro vasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And knowing that the entire universe was in trepidation, that mighty saint, the sedate Vasiştha of excellent vows, said these words to the king.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातः साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः
धृतिमान्सुव्रतः श्रीमान्न धर्मं हातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ kule jātaḥ sākṣāddharma ivāparaḥ
dhṛtimānsuvrataḥ śrīmānna dharmaṁ hātumarhasi

translations.english: Born in the line of Ikşvāku, you are the very second self of virtue. And endowed with patience, and auspicious, and observing excellent vows, you ought not to renounce virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातो धर्मात्मा इति राघवः
स्वधर्मं प्रतिपद्यस्व नाधर्मं वोढुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto dharmātmā iti rāghavaḥ
svadharmaṁ pratipadyasva nādharmaṁ voḍhumarhasi

translations.english: The descendant of Raghu is famed over the three worlds as righteous-souled. Do you maintain your habit of adhering to promise; for it does not behove you to act unrighteously.

verses.sanskrit:
संश्रुत्यैवं करिष्यामीत्यकुर्वाणस्य राघव
इष्टापूर्तवधो भूयात्तस्माद्रामं विसर्जय
verses.transliteration:
saṁśrutyaivaṁ kariṣyāmītyakurvāṇasya rāghava
iṣṭāpūrtavadho bhūyāttasmādrāmaṁ visarjaya

translations.english: If having promised, I will do so, you do not act up to your word, the merit you have achieved by digging tanks, shall come to naught, therefore do you renounce Rāma!

verses.sanskrit:
कृतास्त्रमकृतास्त्रं वा नैनं शक्ष्यन्ति राक्षसाः
गुप्तं कुशिकपुत्रेण ज्वलनेनामृतं यथा
verses.transliteration:
kṛtāstramakṛtāstraṁ vā nainaṁ śakṣyanti rākṣasāḥ
guptaṁ kuśikaputreṇa jvalanenāmṛtaṁ yathā

translations.english: Accomplished or not accomplished in weapons, the Rākṣasas cannot bear him protected by Kusika's son, like ambrosia, by flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
एष विग्रहवान्धर्म एष वीर्यवतां वरः
एष बुद्ध्याधिको लोके तपसश्च परायणम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa vigrahavāndharma eṣa vīryavatāṁ varaḥ
eṣa buddhyādhiko loke tapasaśca parāyaṇam

translations.english: This one is Virtue incarnate: this one is the foremost of those possessing prowess. This one surpass all others in learning, and is the refuge of asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
एषोऽस्त्रान्विविधान्वेत्ति त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे
नैनमन्यः पुमान्वेत्ति न च वेत्स्यन्ति केचन
verses.transliteration:
eṣo'strānvividhānvetti trailokye sacarācare
nainamanyaḥ pumānvetti na ca vetsyanti kecana

translations.english: This one is congnizant of all that exist in the three worlds furnished with mobile and immobile things;. but others do not know him,-nor yet shall know him hereafter.

verses.sanskrit:
न देवा नर्षयः केचिन्नासुरा न च राक्षसाः
गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवराः सकिंनरमहोरगाः
verses.transliteration:
na devā narṣayaḥ kecinnāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ
gandharvayakṣapravarāḥ sakiṁnaramahoragāḥ

translations.english: And neither the gods, nor the saints, nor the immortals, nor the Rakşasas, nor the foremost of Gandharvas and Yaksas, nor the Kinnaras, nor the mighty Serpents can know him.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वास्त्राणि कृशाश्वस्य पुत्राः परमधार्मिकाः
कौशिकाय पुरा दत्ता यदा राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.transliteration:
sarvāstrāṇi kṛśāśvasya putrāḥ paramadhārmikāḥ
kauśikāya purā dattā yadā rājyaṁ praśāsati

translations.english: And formerly while the descendant of Kusika was ruling his kingdom, Siva conferred upon him the highly famous sons of Kțśāśva in the shape of all w apons.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽपि पुत्राः कृशाश्वस्य प्रजापतिसुतासुताः
नैकरूपा महावीर्या दीप्तिमन्तो जयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
te'pi putrāḥ kṛśāśvasya prajāpatisutāsutāḥ
naikarūpā mahāvīryā dīptimanto jayāvahāḥ

translations.english: Those sons of Krśāśva were the offspring of Prajāpati's daughters. And they were endowed with various forms, and were effulgent and dreadful.

verses.sanskrit:
जया च सुप्रभा चैव दक्षकन्ये सुमध्यमे
ते सुवातेऽस्त्रशस्त्राणि शतं परमभास्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
jayā ca suprabhā caiva dakṣakanye sumadhyame
te suvāte'straśastrāṇi śataṁ paramabhāsvaram

translations.english: And Dakşa's daughters of elegant waists, Jayā and Suprabhā, brought forth an hundred exceedingly effulgent weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चाशतं सुताँल्लेभे जया नाम वरान्पुरा
वधायासुरसैन्यानाममेयान्कामरूपिणः
verses.transliteration:
pañcāśataṁ sutā̐llebhe jayā nāma varānpurā
vadhāyāsurasainyānāmameyānkāmarūpiṇaḥ

translations.english: And by virtue of her boon, Jayā obtained fifty sons of immeasurable strength and endued with the power of becoming invisible for the purpose of slaughtering the hosts of the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
सुप्रभाजनयच्चापि पुत्रान्पञ्चाशतं पुनः
संहारान्नाम दुर्धर्षान्दुराक्रामान्बलीयसः
verses.transliteration:
suprabhājanayaccāpi putrānpañcāśataṁ punaḥ
saṁhārānnāma durdharṣāndurākrāmānbalīyasaḥ

translations.english: Suprabhā also brought forth fifty sons named Sanhäras, incapable of being borne, and infallible and powerful.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि चास्त्राणि वेत्त्येष यथावत्कुशिकात्मजः
अपूर्वाणां च जनने शक्तो भूयश्च धर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
tāni cāstrāṇi vettyeṣa yathāvatkuśikātmajaḥ
apūrvāṇāṁ ca janane śakto bhūyaśca dharmavit

translations.english: Kuśika's son is adequately conversant with all those weapons. And that one knowing duty is also capable of creating wonderful weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं वीर्यो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महातपाः
न रामगमने राजन्संशयं गन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vīryo mahātejā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ
na rāmagamane rājansaṁśayaṁ gantumarhasi

translations.english: Such is the prowess of that highly famous Viśvāmitra possessed of mighty energy. Therefore, O king, it behove you not to hesitate in the matter of Rāma's going.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा वसिष्ठे ब्रुवति राजा दशरथः सुतम्
प्रहृष्टवदनो राममाजुहाव सलक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathaḥ sutam
prahṛṣṭavadano rāmamājuhāva salakṣmaṇam

translations.english: Upon Vasistha's representing this, king Dasaratha himself, with complacent countenance, summoned to him Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतस्वस्त्ययनं मात्रा पित्रा दशरथेन च
पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन मङ्गलैरभिमन्त्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtasvastyayanaṁ mātrā pitrā daśarathena ca
purodhasā vasiṣṭhena maṅgalairabhimantritam

translations.english: And when the auspicious rites had been performed by both Rāma's father and mother, and when the priest Vasiştha had uttered mantras, king Dasaratha, smelling his son's crown, with a glad heart, made him over to the descendant of Kusika.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीद्देवदुन्दुभिनिस्वनः
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः प्रयाते तु महात्मनि
verses.transliteration:
puṣpavṛṣṭirmahatyāsīddevadundubhinisvanaḥ
śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaḥ prayāte tu mahātmani

translations.english: Then there blow a Breeze free from dust and of delicious feel, on witnessing the lotus-eyed Rāma at the hands of Viśvāmitra. And as the high-souled one was about to set out, blossoms began to shower down copiously, accompanied with the sounds of celestial kettle-drums and the loud blares of conch.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रो ययावग्रे ततो रामो महायशाः
काकपक्षधरो धन्वी तं च सौमित्रिरन्वगात्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro yayāvagre tato rāmo mahāyaśāḥ
kākapakṣadharo dhanvī taṁ ca saumitriranvagāt

translations.english: Viśvāmitra went first, and next the highly famous Rāma with the side-locks, holding the bow. And him followed Sumitrā's Sun

verses.sanskrit:
कलापिनौ धनुष्पाणी शोभयानौ दिशो दश
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं त्रिशीर्षाविव पन्नगौ
अनुजग्मतुरक्षुद्रौ पितामहमिवाश्विनौ
verses.transliteration:
kalāpinau dhanuṣpāṇī śobhayānau diśo daśa
viśvāmitraṁ mahātmānaṁ triśīrṣāviva pannagau
anujagmaturakṣudrau pitāmahamivāśvinau

translations.english: And equipped with quivers, and with bows in hand, gracing the ten cardinal points and resembling three-hooded serpents, they followed the high-souled Viśvāmitra, like the two stalwart Asvins following the Grand-sire.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ खड्गवन्तौ महाद्युती
स्थाणुं देवमिवाचिन्त्यं कुमाराविव पावकी
verses.transliteration:
baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī
sthāṇuṁ devamivācintyaṁ kumārāviva pāvakī

translations.english: Those effulgent ones of faultless limbs went in the wake of the ascetic, illumining him with their grace. And like to those sons of him Skandha and Višākha following the incomprehensible deity, Sthāņu, those youthful brothers of comely persons and faultless limbs Rāma and Lakşmana, highly effulgent, carrying bows in hand, adorned with ornaments, and equipped with scimitars, with their fingers encased in Guana skin, flamingly followed Kusika's son, beautifying him with their splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्यर्धयोजनं गत्वा सरय्वा दक्षिणे तटे
रामेति मधुरा वाणीं विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
adhyardhayojanaṁ gatvā sarayvā dakṣiṇe taṭe
rāmeti madhurā vāṇīṁ viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: And having proceeded over half a Yojana, and arriving at the right bank of the Sarayū, Viśvāmitra addressed these sweet words to Rāma, O Rāma! do you, O child, take of this water: let no delay occur.

verses.sanskrit:
न श्रमो न ज्वरो वा ते न रूपस्य विपर्ययः
न च सुप्तं प्रमत्तं वा धर्षयिष्यन्ति नैरृताः
verses.transliteration:
na śramo na jvaro vā te na rūpasya viparyayaḥ
na ca suptaṁ pramattaṁ vā dharṣayiṣyanti nairṛtāḥ

translations.english: Do you receive the mantras Bala and Atibala, and you will not feel fatigue or fever or undergo any change of look, and whether asleep or heedless, the Rākşasas will not be able to surprise you. And, O Rāma, the might of your arms will be unequalled in this world,-nay, in all the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुत्पिपासे न ते राम भविष्येते नरोत्तम
बलामतिबलां चैव पठतः पथि राघव
विद्याद्वयमधीयाने यशश्चाप्यतुलं भुवि
verses.transliteration:
kṣutpipāse na te rāma bhaviṣyete narottama
balāmatibalāṁ caiva paṭhataḥ pathi rāghava
vidyādvayamadhīyāne yaśaścāpyatulaṁ bhuvi

translations.english: And, O Rāma, O foremost of men, if you recite Bala and Atibala on the way, neither hunger nor thirst will exercise you, O descendant of Raghu! And if you recite these, you will attain fame on earth. Those sciences fraught with energy are the daughters of the Grandsire.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं बहुगुणाः सर्वे त्वय्येते नात्र संशयः
तपसा संभृते चैते बहुरूपे भविष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ bahuguṇāḥ sarve tvayyete nātra saṁśayaḥ
tapasā saṁbhṛte caite bahurūpe bhaviṣyataḥ

translations.english: I intend to confer them upon you, O Kākutstha; and, O lord of earth, they are worthy to be conferred upon you; and they are possessed of various virtues. You need not entertain any doubt about it. And if you bear them in consonance with the precepts, they will prove of manifold good to you.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामो जलं स्पृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्टवदनः शुचिः
प्रतिजग्राह ते विद्ये महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः
विद्यासमुदितो रामः शुशुभे भूरिविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmo jalaṁ spṛṣṭvā prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śuciḥ
pratijagrāha te vidye maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ
vidyāsamudito rāmaḥ śuśubhe bhūrivikramaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Rāma with a cheerful countenance sipning water with a purified body received those sciences from the Maharși of subdued soul.

verses.sanskrit:
गुरुकार्याणि सर्वाणि नियुज्य कुशिकात्मजे
ऊषुस्तां रजनीं तत्र सरय्वां सुसुखं त्रयः
verses.transliteration:
gurukāryāṇi sarvāṇi niyujya kuśikātmaje
ūṣustāṁ rajanīṁ tatra sarayvāṁ susukhaṁ trayaḥ

translations.english: Then Rāma having rendered to Kuśika's son all the duties pertaining to a spiritual guide, the three happily spent that night on the banks of the Sarayu.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम पूर्वा संध्या प्रवर्तते
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā saṁdhyā pravartate
uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṁ daivamāhnikam

translations.english: And when the night had passed away, the mighty ascetic spoke to Kākutstha, lying down on a bed of leaves, O Rāma, surely has Kausalyā given birth to an excellent son! The first Sandhyā* should now be performed. Do you, O tiger among men, arise! You should perform the purificatory rites and contemplate the gods. *Brāhmaṇas have to perform their daily devotions thrice,-in the morning, at noon, and in the evening.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यर्षेः परमोदारं वचः श्रुत्वा नृपात्मजौ
स्नात्वा कृतोदकौ वीरौ जेपतुः परमं जपम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyarṣeḥ paramodāraṁ vacaḥ śrutvā nṛpātmajau
snātvā kṛtodakau vīrau jepatuḥ paramaṁ japam

translations.english: Hearing those proper words of the ascetic, those foremost of men, endowed with heroism, bathed, and, sipping water, began to recite the Gayatri. (The solar hymn of the Veda).

verses.sanskrit:
कृताह्निकौ महावीर्यौ विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्
अभिवाद्याभिसंहृष्टौ गमनायोपतस्थतुः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtāhnikau mahāvīryau viśvāmitraṁ tapodhanam
abhivādyābhisaṁhṛṣṭau gamanāyopatasthatuḥ

translations.english: And having performed these daily duties, those exceedingly powerful ones, greeting Viśvāmitra having asceticism for wealth, stood before him, with the object of starting on their journey.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ प्रयाते महावीर्यौ दिव्यं त्रिपथगां नदीम्
ददृशाते ततस्तत्र सरय्वाः संगमे शुभे
verses.transliteration:
tau prayāte mahāvīryau divyaṁ tripathagāṁ nadīm
dadṛśāte tatastatra sarayvāḥ saṁgame śubhe

translations.english: And as those ones endowed with exceeding prowess were proceeding, at the shining confluence of the Sarayū and the Gangā they bcheld a noble river flowing in three branches.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्राश्रमपदं पुण्यमृषीणामुग्रतेजसाम्
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तप्यतां परमं तपः
verses.transliteration:
tatrāśramapadaṁ puṇyamṛṣīṇāmugratejasām
bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi tapyatāṁ paramaṁ tapaḥ

translations.english: There lay a holy hermitage, belonging to ascetics of subdued souls, where they had been carrying on their high austerities for thousands of years.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतौ राघवौ पुण्यमाश्रमम्
ऊचतुस्तं महात्मानं विश्वामित्रमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītau rāghavau puṇyamāśramam
ūcatustaṁ mahātmānaṁ viśvāmitramidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Beholding that sacred asylum those descendants of Raghu, exceedingly delighted, spoke to the high-souled Viśvāmitra, these words.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्यायमाश्रमः पुण्यः को न्वस्मिन्वसते पुमान्
भगवञ्श्रोतुमिच्छावः परं कौतूहलं हि नौ
verses.transliteration:
kasyāyamāśramaḥ puṇyaḥ ko nvasminvasate pumān
bhagavañśrotumicchāvaḥ paraṁ kautūhalaṁ hi nau

translations.english: Whose is this sacred hemmilage? And what man lives here? O worshipfui one, we are desirous of hcasing this. Surciy, great is our curiosity.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुंगवः
अब्रवीच्छ्रूयतां राम यस्यायं पूर्व आश्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tayostadvacanaṁ śrutvā prahasya munipuṁgavaḥ
abravīcchrūyatāṁ rāma yasyāyaṁ pūrva āśramaḥ

translations.english: At those words of theirs, that foremost of ascetics, smiling, said, Hear, O Rama, as to whom the asylum has belonged in time past.

verses.sanskrit:
तपस्यन्तमिह स्थाणुं नियमेन समाहितम्
कृतोद्वाहं तु देवेशं गच्छन्तं समरुद्गणम्
धर्षयामास दुर्मेधा हुंकृतश्च महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
tapasyantamiha sthāṇuṁ niyamena samāhitam
kṛtodvāhaṁ tu deveśaṁ gacchantaṁ samarudgaṇam
dharṣayāmāsa durmedhā huṁkṛtaśca mahātmanā

translations.english: Kandarpa, called Käma by the wise, was once incarnate (on earth.) And it came to pass that as that lord of the deities, Sthāņu, having performed here his austerities in accordance with the prescribed restrictions, was wending his way in company with the Maruts, that fool-hardy wight dared disturb the equanimity of his mind.

verses.sanskrit:
दग्धस्य तस्य रौद्रेण चक्षुषा रघुनन्दन
व्यशीर्यन्त शरीरात्स्वात्सर्वगात्राणि दुर्मतेः
verses.transliteration:
dagdhasya tasya raudreṇa cakṣuṣā raghunandana
vyaśīryanta śarīrātsvātsarvagātrāṇi durmateḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, O descendant of Raghu, uttering a roar, the high-souled Rudra eyed him steadfastly. And thereat all the limbs of that perverse-hearted one became blasted.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य गात्रं हतं तत्र निर्दग्धस्य महात्मना
अशरीरः कृतः कामः क्रोधाद्देवेश्वरेण ह
verses.transliteration:
tasya gātraṁ hataṁ tatra nirdagdhasya mahātmanā
aśarīraḥ kṛtaḥ kāmaḥ krodhāddeveśvareṇa ha

translations.english: And on his body being consumed by that high-souled one, Kāma was deprived of his person in consequence of the ire of that foremost among the deities.

verses.sanskrit:
अनङ्ग इति विख्यातस्तदा प्रभृति राघव
स चाङ्गविषयः श्रीमान्यत्राङ्गं स मुमोच ह
verses.transliteration:
anaṅga iti vikhyātastadā prabhṛti rāghava
sa cāṅgaviṣayaḥ śrīmānyatrāṅgaṁ sa mumoca ha

translations.english: O Rāghava, from that time forth, he has become known as Ananga. And the place where he was deprived of his body is the lovely land of Anga.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यायमाश्रमः पुण्यस्तस्येमे मुनयः पुरा
शिष्या धर्मपरा वीर तेषां पापं न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
tasyāyamāśramaḥ puṇyastasyeme munayaḥ purā
śiṣyā dharmaparā vīra teṣāṁ pāpaṁ na vidyate

translations.english: This sacred hermitage belongs to Śiva; and these ascetics engaged in pious acts, O hero, have been from father to son his disciples. And no sin touch them.

verses.sanskrit:
इहाद्य रजनीं राम वसेम शुभदर्शन
पुण्ययोः सरितोर्मध्ये श्वस्तरिष्यामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
ihādya rajanīṁ rāma vasema śubhadarśana
puṇyayoḥ saritormadhye śvastariṣyāmahe vayam

translations.english: Here, O Rāma, in the midst of the sacred streams, will we spend the night, O you of gracious presence, crossing over on the morrow.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां संवदतां तत्र तपो दीर्घेण चक्षुषा
विज्ञाय परमप्रीता मुनयो हर्षमागमन्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ saṁvadatāṁ tatra tapo dīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā
vijñāya paramaprītā munayo harṣamāgaman

translations.english: As they were conversing thus, the ascetics were highly delighted on discovering them by means of their far-reaching spiritual vision, and they rejoiced greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्घ्यं पाद्यं तथातिथ्यं निवेद्यकुशिकात्मजे
रामलक्ष्मणयोः पश्चादकुर्वन्नतिथिक्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
arghyaṁ pādyaṁ tathātithyaṁ nivedyakuśikātmaje
rāmalakṣmaṇayoḥ paścādakurvannatithikriyām

translations.english: Then giving Kusika's son water to wash his feet and Arghya, and extending to him also the rites of hospitality, they next entertained Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्कारं समनुप्राप्य कथाभिरभिरञ्जयन्
न्यवसन्सुसुखं तत्र कामाश्रमपदे तदा
verses.transliteration:
satkāraṁ samanuprāpya kathābhirabhirañjayan
nyavasansusukhaṁ tatra kāmāśramapade tadā

translations.english: Having experienced their hospitality, they (the guests) delighted them with their talk. And then the saints with collected minds recited their evening prayers.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रभाते विमले कृताह्निकमरिंदमौ
विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य नद्यास्तीरमुपागतौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtāhnikamariṁdamau
viśvāmitraṁ puraskṛtya nadyāstīramupāgatau

translations.english: Then next morning which happened to be fine, those repressors of their foes, with Viśvāmitra at their head, came to the banks of the river.* Ganga. The legend is that when the saint Agastya had sucked up the ocean, the Ganges replenished it.

verses.sanskrit:
ते च सर्वे महात्मानो मुनयः संशितव्रताः
उपस्थाप्य शुभां नावं विश्वामित्रमथाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
te ca sarve mahātmāno munayaḥ saṁśitavratāḥ
upasthāpya śubhāṁ nāvaṁ viśvāmitramathābruvan

translations.english: And those high-souled ascetics observing vows, having brought an elegant bark, addressed Viśvāmitra, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
आरोहतु भवान्नावं राजपुत्रपुरस्कृतः
अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं मा भूत्कालस्य पर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
ārohatu bhavānnāvaṁ rājaputrapuraskṛtaḥ
ariṣṭaṁ gaccha panthānaṁ mā bhūtkālasya paryayaḥ

translations.english: Do you ascend the bark, with the princes at your head! May your journey be auspicious: let no delay occur

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रस्तथेत्युक्त्वा तानृषीनभिपूज्य च
ततार सहितस्ताभ्यां सरितं सागरं गमाम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitrastathetyuktvā tānṛṣīnabhipūjya ca
tatāra sahitastābhyāṁ saritaṁ sāgaraṁ gamām

translations.english: Thereupon saying, So be it! and having paid homage to those ascetics, Viśvāmitra set about crossing that river, which had replenished the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रामः सरिन्मध्ये पप्रच्छ मुनिपुङ्गवम्
वारिणो भिद्यमानस्य किमयं तुमुलो ध्वनिः
verses.transliteration:
atha rāmaḥ sarinmadhye papraccha munipuṅgavam
vāriṇo bhidyamānasya kimayaṁ tumulo dhvaniḥ

translations.english: And reaching the middle of the river, Rāma asked that best of ascetics, What is this loud uproar that seem to come riving the waters?

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कौतूहल समन्वितम्
कथयामास धर्मात्मा तस्य शब्दस्य निश्चयम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā kautūhala samanvitam
kathayāmāsa dharmātmā tasya śabdasya niścayam

translations.english: Hearing Rāghava's words dictated by curiosity, that righteous-souled one spoke, unfolding the true cause of that noise.

verses.sanskrit:
कैलासपर्वते राम मनसा निर्मितं सरः
ब्रह्मणा नरशार्दूल तेनेदं मानसं सरः
verses.transliteration:
kailāsaparvate rāma manasā nirmitaṁ saraḥ
brahmaṇā naraśārdūla tenedaṁ mānasaṁ saraḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, there is in the Kailāsa mountain an exceedingly beautiful pool, created mentally by Brahma, O foremost of men, and hence this watery expanse go by the name of Mānasa Pool.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्सुस्राव सरसः सायोध्यामुपगूहते
सरःप्रवृत्ता सरयूः पुण्या ब्रह्मसरश्च्युता
verses.transliteration:
tasmātsusrāva sarasaḥ sāyodhyāmupagūhate
saraḥpravṛttā sarayūḥ puṇyā brahmasaraścyutā

translations.english: And the stream that issues from that liquid lapse, flows through Ayodhyā: the sacred Sarayü issues from that pool of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यायमतुलः शब्दो जाह्नवीमभिवर्तते
वारिसंक्षोभजो राम प्रणामं नियतः कुरु
verses.transliteration:
tasyāyamatulaḥ śabdo jāhnavīmabhivartate
vārisaṁkṣobhajo rāma praṇāmaṁ niyataḥ kuru

translations.english: And as the Sarayū meets the Jāhnavī, this tremendous uproar is heard, being produced by the clashing of the waters. Do you, O Rāma, bow down to them with a concentrated mind.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यां तु तावुभौ कृत्वा प्रणाममतिधार्मिकौ
तीरं दक्षिणमासाद्य जग्मतुर्लघुविक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
tābhyāṁ tu tāvubhau kṛtvā praṇāmamatidhārmikau
tīraṁ dakṣiṇamāsādya jagmaturlaghuvikramau

translations.english: Thereupon, both of those exceedingly righteous ones, bowed down to those streams; and betaking themselves to the right bank, began to proceed with fleet vigour.

verses.sanskrit:
स वनं घोरसंकाशं दृष्ट्वा नृपवरात्मजः
अविप्रहतमैक्ष्वाकः पप्रच्छ मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
sa vanaṁ ghorasaṁkāśaṁ dṛṣṭvā nṛpavarātmajaḥ
aviprahatamaikṣvākaḥ papraccha munipuṁgavam

translations.english: And beholding a dreadful and trackless. forest, that son of the foremost of men, Ikşvāku's descendant, asked that best of ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाप्रकारैः शकुनैर्वाश्यद्भिर्भैरवस्वनैः
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहैश्च वारणैश्चापि शोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
nānāprakāraiḥ śakunairvāśyadbhirbhairavasvanaiḥ
siṁhavyāghravarāhaiśca vāraṇaiścāpi śobhitam

translations.english: Ah! deep is this forest abounding in crickets; and filled with terrible ferocious beasts, and various birds possessed of shocking voices and creaming frightfully; and graced by lion, and tigers, and boars, and elephants; and crowded with Dhavas* (Grislea Tomentosa). and Asvas and Karnas (Cassia fistula) and Kakubhas and Vilvas (Aegle marmalos) and Tindukas; (Diospyros glutinosa) and Patalas (Bignonia suave-olens) and Badaris (Fujube). Whence is this dreadful forest?

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
श्रूयतां वत्स काकुत्स्थ यस्यैतद्दारुणं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
śrūyatāṁ vatsa kākutstha yasyaitaddāruṇaṁ vanam

translations.english: Him answered thus the mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra endowed with high energy, Do you listen, O Kākutstha, as to whom belong this dreadful forest!

verses.sanskrit:
एतौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ पूर्वमास्तां नरोत्तम
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च देवनिर्माणनिर्मितौ
verses.transliteration:
etau janapadau sphītau pūrvamāstāṁ narottama
maladāśca karūṣāśca devanirmāṇanirmitau

translations.english: Here were formerly, O foremost of men, two flourishing provinces, named Malada, and Karāsa, built by celestial architects.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा वृत्रवधे राम मलेन समभिप्लुतम्
क्षुधा चैव सहस्राक्षं ब्रह्महत्या यदाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
purā vṛtravadhe rāma malena samabhiplutam
kṣudhā caiva sahasrākṣaṁ brahmahatyā yadāviśat

translations.english: In days of yore, O Räma, on the occasion of the destruction of Vſtra, the thousand-eyed one came to have hunger, to be besmeared with excreta, and to slay a Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तमिन्द्रं स्नापयन्देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः
कलशैः स्नापयामासुर्मलं चास्य प्रमोचयन्
verses.transliteration:
tamindraṁ snāpayandevā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ
kalaśaiḥ snāpayāmāsurmalaṁ cāsya pramocayan

translations.english: When Indra had been thus besmeared, the deities, and the saints having asceticism for wealth, washed him here, and cleansed his person from the dirt.

verses.sanskrit:
इह भूम्यां मलं दत्त्वा दत्त्वा कारूषमेव च
शरीरजं महेन्द्रस्य ततो हर्षं प्रपेदिरे
verses.transliteration:
iha bhūmyāṁ malaṁ dattvā dattvā kārūṣameva ca
śarīrajaṁ mahendrasya tato harṣaṁ prapedire

translations.english: And the deities, having renounced here the filth that had clung to the person of the mighty Indra, as well as his hunger, attained exceeding delight.

verses.sanskrit:
इमौ जनपदौ स्थीतौ ख्यातिं लोके गमिष्यतः
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च ममाङ्गमलधारिणौ
verses.transliteration:
imau janapadau sthītau khyātiṁ loke gamiṣyataḥ
maladāśca karūṣāśca mamāṅgamaladhāriṇau

translations.english: And thereat Indra becoming purified, attained his former brightness, and looked like to gold. And mightily pleased with this region, he conferred on it an excellent boon, saying, Since these two places have held excreta from my body, the going by the names of Maladā and Kārūsa, shall attain exceeding prosperity and fame among men.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु साध्विति तं देवाः पाकशासनमब्रुवन्
देशस्य पूजां तां दृष्ट्वा कृतां शक्रेण धीमता
verses.transliteration:
sādhu sādhviti taṁ devāḥ pākaśāsanamabruvan
deśasya pūjāṁ tāṁ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāṁ śakreṇa dhīmatā

translations.english: And beholding the land thus honoured by the intelligent Sacra, the deities said to the subduer of Paka,-Well Well!

verses.sanskrit:
एतौ जनपदौ स्थीतौ दीर्घकालमरिंदम
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च मुदितौ धनधान्यतः
verses.transliteration:
etau janapadau sthītau dīrghakālamariṁdama
maladāśca karūṣāśca muditau dhanadhānyataḥ

translations.english: O repressor of foes, these two places, Maladā and Karuṣā, enjoyed prosperity for a long time and were blessed with corn and wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी वै कामरूपिणी
बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्ती तदा ह्यभूत्
verses.transliteration:
kasyacittvatha kālasya yakṣī vai kāmarūpiṇī
balaṁ nāgasahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hyabhūt

translations.english: Then after a space of time, was born a Yakşīņi capable of assuming forms at will, and endowed with the strength of a thousand elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
ताटका नाम भद्रं ते भार्या सुन्दस्य धीमतः
मारीचो राक्षसः पुत्रो यस्याः शक्रपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tāṭakā nāma bhadraṁ te bhāryā sundasya dhīmataḥ
mārīco rākṣasaḥ putro yasyāḥ śakraparākramaḥ

translations.english: Her name, good betide you! was Tātakā, and she was the spouse of the intelligent Sundashe whose son is the Rākşasa, Mārīca, possessed of the prowess of Sacra; having round arms, with a huge head, a capacious mouth and a cyclopean body.

verses.sanskrit:
इमौ जनपदौ नित्यं विनाशयति राघव
मलदांश्च करूषांश्च ताटका दुष्टचारिणी
verses.transliteration:
imau janapadau nityaṁ vināśayati rāghava
maladāṁśca karūṣāṁśca tāṭakā duṣṭacāriṇī

translations.english: And that Rākṣasa of dreadful form daily frightens people. And, O descendant of Raghu, Tātakā of wicked deeds, daily commits havoc upon these countries, Maladã and Karuşă.

verses.sanskrit:
सेयं पन्थानमावार्य वसत्यत्यर्धयोजने
अत एव च गन्तव्यं ताटकाया वनं यतः
verses.transliteration:
seyaṁ panthānamāvārya vasatyatyardhayojane
ata eva ca gantavyaṁ tāṭakāyā vanaṁ yataḥ

translations.english: And now at the distance of over half a Yojana, she stays, obstructing the way. And since this forest belong to Tāțakā, you should repair there; and, resorting to the might of your own arms, slay this one of wicked deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि कश्चिदिमं देशं शक्रोत्यागन्तुमीदृशम्
यक्षिण्या घोरया राम उत्सादितमसह्यया
verses.transliteration:
na hi kaścidimaṁ deśaṁ śakrotyāgantumīdṛśam
yakṣiṇyā ghorayā rāma utsāditamasahyayā

translations.english: And, by my direction, do you again rid this region of its thorn; for no one dare to approach such a place, infested,

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथैतद्दरुणं वनम्
यक्ष्या चोत्सादितं सर्वमद्यापि न निवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ yathaitaddaruṇaṁ vanam
yakṣyā cotsāditaṁ sarvamadyāpi na nivartate

translations.english: O Rāma, by the dreadful and unbearable Yakşiņi. And now I have related to you all about this fearful forest. And to this day none is capable of letting that Yakşiņi from committing ravages right an left.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य मुनेर्वचनमुत्तमम्
श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलः प्रत्युवाच शुभां गिरम्
verses.transliteration:
atha tasyāprameyasya munervacanamuttamam
śrutvā puruṣaśārdūlaḥ pratyuvāca śubhāṁ giram

translations.english: Hearing this excellent speech of that ascetic of immeasurable energy, that foremost of men answered him in these happy words,

verses.sanskrit:
अल्पवीर्या यदा यक्षाः श्रूयन्ते मुनिपुंगव
कथं नागसहस्रस्य धारयत्यबला बलम्
verses.transliteration:
alpavīryā yadā yakṣāḥ śrūyante munipuṁgava
kathaṁ nāgasahasrasya dhārayatyabalā balam

translations.english: O best of ascetics, I have heard that the Yakşa race is endowed with but small prowess. How can then that one of the weaker sex possess the strength of a thousand elephants?

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं शृणु येन बलोत्तरा
वरदानकृतं वीर्यं धारयत्यबला बलम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro'bravīdvākyaṁ śṛṇu yena balottarā
varadānakṛtaṁ vīryaṁ dhārayatyabalā balam

translations.english: Hearing this speech that was uttered by Rāghava of immeasurable energy, Viśvāmitra, delighting with his amiable words that subduer of foes, Rāma, and Laksmana, said, Do you listen as to the means whereby attaining terrible strength, that one belonging to the weaker sex has come to possess strength and prowess by virtue of a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वमासीन्महायक्षः सुकेतुर्नाम वीर्यवान्
अनपत्यः शुभाचारः स च तेपे महत्तपः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvamāsīnmahāyakṣaḥ suketurnāma vīryavān
anapatyaḥ śubhācāraḥ sa ca tepe mahattapaḥ

translations.english: In former times there was a mighty and exceedingly powerful Yaksa, named Suketu. And he had no issue. And he was of pure practices, and used to perform rigid austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतस्तस्य यक्षपतेस्तदा
कन्यारत्नं ददौ राम ताटकां नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
pitāmahastu suprītastasya yakṣapatestadā
kanyāratnaṁ dadau rāma tāṭakāṁ nāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: And, O Rāma, the Grand-sire endowed her with that lord of Yakşas, conferred upon him a gem of a daughter, by name Tāțakā.

verses.sanskrit:
ददौ नागसहस्रस्य बलं चास्याः पितामहः
न त्वेव पुत्रं यक्षाय ददौ ब्रह्मा महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
dadau nāgasahasrasya balaṁ cāsyāḥ pitāmahaḥ
na tveva putraṁ yakṣāya dadau brahmā mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: And the Grand-sire endowed her with the strength of a thousand elephants; yet that illustrious one did not bestow a son on that Yaksa.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु जातां विवर्धन्तीं रूपयौवनशालिनीम्
जम्भपुत्राय सुन्दाय ददौ भार्यां यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu jātāṁ vivardhantīṁ rūpayauvanaśālinīm
jambhaputrāya sundāya dadau bhāryāṁ yaśasvinīm

translations.english: When she had grown, and attained youth and beauty, he gave that famous damsel to Jambha's son, Sunda, for wife.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालल्स्य यक्षी पुत्रं व्यजायत
मारीचं नाम दुर्धर्षं यः शापाद्राक्षसोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
kasyacittvatha kālalsya yakṣī putraṁ vyajāyata
mārīcaṁ nāma durdharṣaṁ yaḥ śāpādrākṣaso'bhavat

translations.english: After a length of time, that Yakṣī gave birth to a son, named Mārīca, possessed of irrepressible energy, him who became a Rākṣasa in consequence of a curse.

verses.sanskrit:
सुन्दे तु निहते राम अगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्
ताटका सह पुत्रेण प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
sunde tu nihate rāma agastyamṛṣisattamam
tāṭakā saha putreṇa pradharṣayitumicchati

translations.english: O Rāma, when Sunda had been destroyed, Tat akā along with her son, set her heart upon afflicting that excellent saint Agastya.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरुषादी महायक्षी विरूपा विकृतानना
इदं रूपमपहाय दारुणं रूपमस्तु ते
verses.transliteration:
puruṣādī mahāyakṣī virūpā vikṛtānanā
idaṁ rūpamapahāya dāruṇaṁ rūpamastu te

translations.english: And, in exceeding wrath, he also cursed Tataka. And, O mighty Yaksi, since in frightful guise with a frightful face you have desired to eat up a human being, do you immediately leave this (your original) shape, and become of a terrible form!

verses.sanskrit:
सैषा शापकृतामर्षा ताटका क्रोधमूर्छिता
देशमुत्सादयत्येनमगस्त्यचरितं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
saiṣā śāpakṛtāmarṣā tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā
deśamutsādayatyenamagastyacaritaṁ śubham

translations.english: Thus cursed by Agastya, Tățakā, overwhelmed with rage, lays waste this fair region, where Agastya carry on his austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
एनां राघव दुर्वृत्तां यक्षीं परमदारुणाम्
गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय जहि दुष्टपराक्रमाम्
verses.transliteration:
enāṁ rāghava durvṛttāṁ yakṣīṁ paramadāruṇām
gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya jahi duṣṭaparākramām

translations.english: Do you, O descendant of Raghu, for the welfare of Brāhmaṇas and kine, slay this exceedingly terrible Yakṣī of wicked ways and vile prowess!

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्येनां शापसंसृष्टां कश्चिदुत्सहते पुमान्
निहन्तुं त्रिषु लोकेषु त्वामृते रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
na hyenāṁ śāpasaṁsṛṣṭāṁ kaścidutsahate pumān
nihantuṁ triṣu lokeṣu tvāmṛte raghunandana

translations.english: Nor, O son of Raghu, does any one in the three worlds, save, you, dare to slay this Yaksi joined with a curse.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि ते स्त्रीवधकृते घृणा कार्या नरोत्तम
चातुर्वर्ण्यहितार्थाय कर्तव्यं राजसूनुना
verses.transliteration:
na hi te strīvadhakṛte ghṛṇā kāryā narottama
cāturvarṇyahitārthāya kartavyaṁ rājasūnunā

translations.english: Nor should you, O best of men, shrink from slaying a woman; for even this should be accomplished by a prince in the interests of the four orders.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यभारनियुक्तानामेष धर्मः सनातनः
अधर्म्यां जहि काकुत्स्थ धर्मो ह्यस्या न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
rājyabhāraniyuktānāmeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
adharmyāṁ jahi kākutstha dharmo hyasyā na vidyate

translations.english: Of those engaged in the onerous task of government, even this is the eternal rule of conduct. Do you, O Kākutstha, slay this impious one; for she know no righteousness!

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयते हि पुरा शक्रो विरोचनसुतां नृप
पृथिवीं हन्तुमिच्छन्तीं मन्थरामभ्यसूदयत्
verses.transliteration:
śrūyate hi purā śakro virocanasutāṁ nṛpa
pṛthivīṁ hantumicchantīṁ mantharāmabhyasūdayat

translations.english: We hear, O king, that in days of yore, ſakra slew Virocana's daughter, Mantharā, who had intended to destroy the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
विष्णुना च पुरा राम भृगुपत्नी दृढव्रता
अनिन्द्रं लोकमिच्छन्ती काव्यमाता निषूदिता
verses.transliteration:
viṣṇunā ca purā rāma bhṛgupatnī dṛḍhavratā
anindraṁ lokamicchantī kāvyamātā niṣūditā

translations.english: And formerly, O Rama, Visnu destroyed Kāvya's mother, the devoted wife of Bhrgu, who had set her heart upon annihilating the world, deprived of sleep (through fear of her.)

verses.sanskrit:
एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभी राजपुत्रमहात्मभिः
अधर्मनिरता नार्यो हताः पुरुषसत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
etaiścānyaiśca bahubhī rājaputramahātmabhiḥ
adharmaniratā nāryo hatāḥ puruṣasattamaiḥ

translations.english: By these as well as innumerable princesforemost of men have wicked women been slain. Therefore, O king, renouncing antipathy, do you, by my command, slay this one!

verses.sanskrit:
मुनेर्वचनमक्लीबं श्रुत्वा नरवरात्मजः
राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच दृढव्रतः
verses.transliteration:
munervacanamaklībaṁ śrutvā naravarātmajaḥ
rāghavaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā pratyuvāca dṛḍhavrataḥ

translations.english: Hearing those bold words of the ascetic, the son of that foremost of men, Rāghava firm in his vows, with clasped hands answered.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्वचननिर्देशात्पितुर्वचनगौरवात्
वचनं कौशिकस्येति कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया
verses.transliteration:
piturvacananirdeśātpiturvacanagauravāt
vacanaṁ kauśikasyeti kartavyamaviśaṅkayā

translations.english: In accordance with the desire of my sire, and in order to glorify it, I ought fearlessly to do even as Kusika's son says. And having been desired to that end while at Ayodhyā by that high-souled one, my father Dasaratha, in the midst of the spiritual guides, I ought not to pass by your words.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं पितुर्वचः श्रुत्वा शासनाद्ब्रह्म वादिनः
करिष्यामि न संदेहस्ताटकावधमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ piturvacaḥ śrutvā śāsanādbrahma vādinaḥ
kariṣyāmi na saṁdehastāṭakāvadhamuttamam

translations.english: Therefore, commanded by that upholder of the Veda, I, agreeably to my father's mandate, will, without doubt, bring about that welcome event-the death of Tataka.

verses.sanskrit:
गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय देशस्यास्य सुखाय च
तव चैवाप्रमेयस्य वचनं कर्तुमुद्यतः
verses.transliteration:
gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya deśasyāsya sukhāya ca
tava caivāprameyasya vacanaṁ kartumudyataḥ

translations.english: And in the interests of Brāhmaṇas, kine, and celestials, I am ready to act as desired by you of immeasurable energy.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तास्ताटका वनवासिनः
ताटका च सुसंक्रुद्धा तेन शब्देन मोहिता
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena vitrastāstāṭakā vanavāsinaḥ
tāṭakā ca susaṁkruddhā tena śabdena mohitā

translations.english: Having said this, that repressor of foes, with clenched fist, twanged his bow-string, filling the ten cardinal points with the sounds. And at those sounds, the dwellers in Tāțakā's forest were filled with perturbation, and Tātakā also amazed at those sounds, became exceedingly wroth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शब्दमभिनिध्याय राक्षसी क्रोधमूर्छिता
श्रुत्वा चाभ्यद्रवद्वेगाद्यतः शब्दो विनिःसृतः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śabdamabhinidhyāya rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā
śrutvā cābhyadravadvegādyataḥ śabdo viniḥsṛtaḥ

translations.english: And rendered almost insensible by anger, that Räksasī furiously rushed in a main towards the spot whence had come the report.

verses.sanskrit:
तां दृष्ट्वा राघवः क्रुद्धां विकृतां विकृताननाम्
प्रमाणेनातिवृद्धां च लक्ष्मणं सोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ kruddhāṁ vikṛtāṁ vikṛtānanām
pramāṇenātivṛddhāṁ ca lakṣmaṇaṁ so'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: And beholding that frightful one of hideous visage and colossal proportions, transported with rage, Raghu's descendant spoke to Laksmana,9

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण यक्षिण्या भैरवं दारुणं वपुः
भिद्येरन्दर्शनादस्या भीरूणां हृदयानि च
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa yakṣiṇyā bhairavaṁ dāruṇaṁ vapuḥ
bhidyerandarśanādasyā bhīrūṇāṁ hṛdayāni ca

translations.english: Behold, O Laksmana, the terrible and hideous body of yonder Yakṣiṇī! The sight of her strike terror into the hearts of even the brave.

verses.sanskrit:
एनां पश्य दुराधर्षां माया बलसमन्विताम्
विनिवृत्तां करोम्यद्य हृतकर्णाग्रनासिकाम्
verses.transliteration:
enāṁ paśya durādharṣāṁ māyā balasamanvitām
vinivṛttāṁ karomyadya hṛtakarṇāgranāsikām

translations.english: Mark! This irrepressible one, possessing all the resources of illusion, will I oppose, and deprive her of ears and nose.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्येनामुत्सहे हन्तुं स्त्रीस्वभावेन रक्षिताम्
वीर्यं चास्या गतिं चापि हनिष्यामीति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
na hyenāmutsahe hantuṁ strīsvabhāvena rakṣitām
vīryaṁ cāsyā gatiṁ cāpi haniṣyāmīti me matiḥ

translations.english: But I dare not slay her, she being protected by virtue of her feminineness. I intend only to oppose her course, and deprive her of her prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणे रामे तु ताटका क्रोधमूर्छिता
उद्यम्य बाहू गर्जन्ती राममेवाभ्यधावत
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇe rāme tu tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā
udyamya bāhū garjantī rāmamevābhyadhāvata

translations.english: As Rāma was speaking thus, Tāțakā, deprived of sense through ire, uttering roars, with uplifted arms rushed against him.

verses.sanskrit:
तामापतन्तीं वेगेन विक्रान्तामशनीमिव
शरेणोरसि विव्याध सा पपात ममार च
verses.transliteration:
tāmāpatantīṁ vegena vikrāntāmaśanīmiva
śareṇorasi vivyādha sā papāta mamāra ca

translations.english: Being thus hemmed in with a network of shafts, she possessed of the powers of illusion, rushed against Kākutstha and Lakşmaņa, uttering terrible roars. And as that Yaksi, in prowess like to a thunder-bolt, was rushing on, Rāma pierced her chest with arrows, and thereat she dropped down and died.

verses.sanskrit:
तां हतां भीमसंकाशां दृष्ट्वा सुरपतिस्तदा
साधु साध्विति काकुत्स्थं सुराश्च समपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ hatāṁ bhīmasaṁkāśāṁ dṛṣṭvā surapatistadā
sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṁ surāśca samapūjayan

translations.english: Upon seeing that grim-visaged one slain, the lord of the celestials together with the celestials themselves honouring Kākutstha, exclaimed Well, Well!.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच परमप्रीतः सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः
सुराश्च सर्वे संहृष्टा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
uvāca paramaprītaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ puraṁdaraḥ
surāśca sarve saṁhṛṣṭā viśvāmitramathābruvan

translations.english: And exceedingly pleased, the thousand-eyed Purandara, together with the delighted deities, said to Viśvāmitra.

verses.sanskrit:
मुने कौशिके भद्रं ते सेन्द्राः सर्वे मरुद्गणाः
तोषिताः कर्मणानेन स्नेहं दर्शय राघवे
verses.transliteration:
mune kauśike bhadraṁ te sendrāḥ sarve marudgaṇāḥ
toṣitāḥ karmaṇānena snehaṁ darśaya rāghave

translations.english: O ascetic, O Kusika's son, good betide you! all the Maruts with Indra at their head, have been gratified with this act (of Rāma's). Do you, O Brāhmaṇa, confer upon Raghu's descendant the sons of Prajāpati Kțśāśva, of true prowess, and charged with ascetic energy.

verses.sanskrit:
पात्रभूतश्च ते ब्रह्मंस्तवानुगमने धृतः
कर्तव्यं च महत्कर्म सुराणां राजसूनुना
verses.transliteration:
pātrabhūtaśca te brahmaṁstavānugamane dhṛtaḥ
kartavyaṁ ca mahatkarma surāṇāṁ rājasūnunā

translations.english: And ever following you, he, O Brāhmaṇa, is fit to receive them of you. And this son of the king is to accomplish a mighty task in the interests of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा सुराः सर्वे हृष्टा जग्मुर्यथागतम्
विश्वामित्रं पूजयित्वा ततः संध्या प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā surāḥ sarve hṛṣṭā jagmuryathāgatam
viśvāmitraṁ pūjayitvā tataḥ saṁdhyā pravartate

translations.english: Saying this, the deities, having paid homage to Viśvāmitra, joyfully entered the celestial regions.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मुनिवरः प्रीतिस्ताटका वधतोषितः
मूर्ध्नि राममुपाघ्राय इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato munivaraḥ prītistāṭakā vadhatoṣitaḥ
mūrdhni rāmamupāghrāya idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And now came evening on, when that best of ascetics, gratified at the destruction of Tāțakā, smelt Rāma's crown and said these words,

verses.sanskrit:
इहाद्य रजनीं राम वसेम शुभदर्शन
श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामस्तदाश्रमपदं मम
verses.transliteration:
ihādya rajanīṁ rāma vasema śubhadarśana
śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmastadāśramapadaṁ mama

translations.english: Here, O Rāma of gracious presence, shall we pass the night; and morrow morning, went to that hermitage of mine.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तां रजनीमुष्य विश्वामिरो महायशाः
प्रहस्य राघवं वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम्
verses.transliteration:
atha tāṁ rajanīmuṣya viśvāmiro mahāyaśāḥ
prahasya rāghavaṁ vākyamuvāca madhurākṣaram

translations.english: Having passed that night, the illustrious Viśvāmitra, smiling complacently, sweetly spoke to Rāghava, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
पतितुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः
प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
patituṣṭo'smi bhadraṁ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmyastrāṇi sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Pleased am I with you. Good betide you, O highly famous prince! With supreme pleasure, do I confer upon you all the weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
देवासुरगणान्वापि सगन्धर्वोरगानपि
यैरमित्रान्प्रसह्याजौ वशीकृत्य जयिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
devāsuragaṇānvāpi sagandharvoragānapi
yairamitrānprasahyājau vaśīkṛtya jayiṣyasi

translations.english: By means of which subduing such antagonists as celestials and Asuras backed on carth by Gandharvas and Uragas, you will in battle be crowned with victory.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि दिव्यानि भद्रं ते ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः
दण्डचक्रं महद्दिव्यं तव दास्यामि राघव
verses.transliteration:
tāni divyāni bhadraṁ te dadāmyastrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
daṇḍacakraṁ mahaddivyaṁ tava dāsyāmi rāghava

translations.english: All those celestial weapons, good betide you, I will confer upon you. And I will confer upon you, O Rāghava, the celestial and mighty Dandacakra,* and Dharmacakra, and also Kalacakra. And, ) foremost of men, I will confer upon you the fierce Vişnucakra, and Indracakra. *Cakra means discus. These enumerations specify different kinds of the discus.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रमस्त्रं नरश्रेष्ठ शैवं शूलवरं तथा
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव ऐषीकमपि राघव
ददामि ते महाबाहो ब्राह्ममस्त्रमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
vajramastraṁ naraśreṣṭha śaivaṁ śūlavaraṁ tathā
astraṁ brahmaśiraścaiva aiṣīkamapi rāghava
dadāmi te mahābāho brāhmamastramanuttamam

translations.english: The Vajra, and Siva's Sūlavara, and the weapon Brahmasiras, and Aisika, O mightyarmed descendant of Raghu! And, O tiger among men, I will, O king's,son, bestow upon you the matchless Brahma weapon, and, O Kākutstha, the two excellent maces, the flaming Modaki and Sikhari. And, O Rāma, I will confer upon you Dharmapasa,* and Kalapāsa, and the excellent Varuņapāśa. * Pasa means noose

verses.sanskrit:
ददामि चास्त्रं पैनाकमस्त्रं नारायणं तथा
आग्नेयमस्त्र दयितं शिखरं नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
dadāmi cāstraṁ painākamastraṁ nārāyaṇaṁ tathā
āgneyamastra dayitaṁ śikharaṁ nāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, I will bestow upon you the two Asanis, Suska and Ardra, and the Pināka weapon, and the Nārāyaṇa, and the Āgneya weapon called Sikhara, and the Vāyavya, called Prathama.

verses.sanskrit:
वायव्यं प्रथमं नाम ददामि तव राघव
अस्त्रं हयशिरो नाम क्रौञ्चमस्त्रं तथैव च
verses.transliteration:
vāyavyaṁ prathamaṁ nāma dadāmi tava rāghava
astraṁ hayaśiro nāma krauñcamastraṁ tathaiva ca

translations.english: O sinless one! And, O Rāghava, I will confer are upon you the weapon called Hayasiras, and the Krauñca weapon, and, O Kākutstha, a couple of darts.

verses.sanskrit:
असिरत्नं महाबाहो ददामि नृवरात्मज
गान्धर्वमस्त्रं दयितं मानवं नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
asiratnaṁ mahābāho dadāmi nṛvarātmaja
gāndharvamastraṁ dayitaṁ mānavaṁ nāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: And, O mighty-armed one, O son of the best of men, I will confer upon you the mighty weapon Vidyadhara, and that excellent scimitar named Nandana, and the favourite Gandharva weapon, Mohana, and Prasvapana, Pasamana, and Saumya,

verses.sanskrit:
मदनं चैव दुर्धर्षं कन्दर्पदयितं तथा
पैशाचमस्त्रं दयितं मोहनं नाम नामतः
प्रतीच्छ नरशार्दूल राजपुत्र महायशः
verses.transliteration:
madanaṁ caiva durdharṣaṁ kandarpadayitaṁ tathā
paiśācamastraṁ dayitaṁ mohanaṁ nāma nāmataḥ
pratīccha naraśārdūla rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava! And, O tiger among men, do you accept Varsana, and Sosana, and Santapana, and Vilāpana, and Mādana hard to repress, beloved of Kandarpa, and that favourite Gandharva weapon, Mānava, and the favourite Piśāca weapon, O highly famous prince.

verses.sanskrit:
सोमास्त्रं शिशिरं नाम त्वाष्ट्रमस्त्रं सुदामनम्
दारुणं च भगस्यापि शीतेषुमथ मानवम्
verses.transliteration:
somāstraṁ śiśiraṁ nāma tvāṣṭramastraṁ sudāmanam
dāruṇaṁ ca bhagasyāpi śīteṣumatha mānavam

translations.english: You, O mighty-armed Rāma, speedily accept the Tamasa, O tiger among men, and the exceedingly powerful Saumana, and the irrepressible Saſvarta and Mausala, O son of the king, and the Satya weapon, and the supreme Māyāmaya, and the Saura. Tejaprabha, capable of depriving foes of energy, and the Soma, and the ſisira, and the Tvāştra, and the terrible Daruna belonging to Bhaga, and Silesu, and Manava.

verses.sanskrit:
एतान्नाम महाबाहो कामरूपान्महाबलान्
गृहाण परमोदारान्क्षिप्रमेव नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
etānnāma mahābāho kāmarūpānmahābalān
gṛhāṇa paramodārānkṣiprameva nṛpātmaja

translations.english: O long-armed king's son, Rama! receive instantly all powerful, highly exalted forms that can be modified at will.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थितस्तु प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वा शुचिर्निवरतस्तदा
ददौ रामाय सुप्रीतो मन्त्रग्राममनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
sthitastu prāṅmukho bhūtvā śucirnivaratastadā
dadau rāmāya suprīto mantragrāmamanuttamam

translations.english: Then with his face turned towards the east, that foremost of ascetics having purified himself, gladly conferred the mantras upon Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
जपतस्तु मुनेस्तस्य विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः
उपतस्थुर्महार्हाणि सर्वाण्यस्त्राणि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
japatastu munestasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
upatasthurmahārhāṇi sarvāṇyastrāṇi rāghavam

translations.english: As that intelligent ascetic, Viśvāmitra, recited mantras, all those invaluable weapons appeared before that descendant of Raghu.
