translations.english: Density overtake all: Destiny is the prime way. Therefore it behove you to grant your favour to me extremely distressed, who crave your favour, and, good betide you, whole endeavours have been baffled by Density.

verses.sanskrit:
नान्यां गतिं गमिष्यामि नान्यः शरणमस्ति मे
दैवं पुरुषकारेण निवर्तयितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
nānyāṁ gatiṁ gamiṣyāmi nānyaḥ śaraṇamasti me
daivaṁ puruṣakāreṇa nivartayitumarhasi

translations.english: Other way will I wend none; nor is there any other refuge for me. It behove you to meet Density with exertion.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तवाक्यं तु राजानं कृपया कुशिकात्मजः
अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं साक्षाच्चण्डालरूपिणम्
verses.transliteration:
uktavākyaṁ tu rājānaṁ kṛpayā kuśikātmajaḥ
abravīnmadhuraṁ vākyaṁ sākṣāccaṇḍālarūpiṇam

translations.english: When the king had spoken thus, Kausika's son, moved with pity, said these sweet words to the king who had undergone Candāla-hood.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाको स्वागतं वत्स जानामि त्वां सुधार्मिकम्
शरणं ते भविष्यामि मा भैषीर्नृपपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvāko svāgataṁ vatsa jānāmi tvāṁ sudhārmikam
śaraṇaṁ te bhaviṣyāmi mā bhaiṣīrnṛpapuṁgava

translations.english: O descendant of Ikşvāku, have you had a pleasant journey? I know you well, O highly virtuous one. Refuge will I grant you, so fear not, O best of monarchs.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमामन्त्रये सर्वान्महर्षीन्पुण्यकर्मणः
यज्ञसाह्यकरान्राजंस्ततो यक्ष्यसि निर्वृतः
verses.transliteration:
ahamāmantraye sarvānmaharṣīnpuṇyakarmaṇaḥ
yajñasāhyakarānrājaṁstato yakṣyasi nirvṛtaḥ

translations.english: I shall summon all the pious Maharsis, who shall assist at the sacrifice. O king, and then you will be able to accomplish your purpose easily. And should the guise you have come by in virtue of your preceptor's curse, cling to you yet, you will bodily repair to heaven in this form. And since appearing before Kuśika's son, you have taken his refuge, I consider heaven, O lord of men, as if within they grasp.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः पुत्रान्परमधार्मिकान्
व्यादिदेश महाप्राज्ञान्यज्ञसंभारकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahātejāḥ putrānparamadhārmikān
vyādideśa mahāprājñānyajñasaṁbhārakāraṇāt

translations.english: Having said this, that exceedingly energetic one ordered his highly virtuous and profoundly wise sons to provide the sacrificial necessaries.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वानृषिवरान्वत्सा आनयध्वं ममाज्ञया
सशिष्यान्सुहृदश्चैव सर्त्विजः सुबहुश्रुतान्
verses.transliteration:
sarvānṛṣivarānvatsā ānayadhvaṁ mamājñayā
saśiṣyānsuhṛdaścaiva sartvijaḥ subahuśrutān

translations.english: Summoning his disciples, he said, 'Do you by my command bring hither all the saints together with Vasistha's sons; and our friends and their disciples an the family priests variously versed in lore.'

verses.sanskrit:
यदन्यो वचनं ब्रूयान्मद्वाक्यबलचोदितः
तत्सर्वमखिलेनोक्तं ममाख्येयमनादृतम्
verses.transliteration:
yadanyo vacanaṁ brūyānmadvākyabalacoditaḥ
tatsarvamakhilenoktaṁ mamākhyeyamanādṛtam

translations.english: Should any summoned by my mandate, say aught, 'do you fully represent to me the expression of slight.'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दिशो जग्मुस्तदाज्ञया
आजग्मुरथ देशेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो ब्रह्मवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā diśo jagmustadājñayā
ājagmuratha deśebhyaḥ sarvebhyo brahmavādinaḥ

translations.english: Hearing his speech, they set out in different directions; and Brahmavādis* began to pour in from various countries. And the disciples (of Viśvāmitra) returning, fully communicated to that ascetic of flaming energy the words of the Brahmavadis, saying. can * A Brahmavādi is one who maintains that all things are Spirit.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा ते वचनं सर्वे समायान्ति द्विजातयः
सर्वदेशेषु चागच्छन्वर्जयित्वा महोदयम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā te vacanaṁ sarve samāyānti dvijātayaḥ
sarvadeśeṣu cāgacchanvarjayitvā mahodayam

translations.english: Hearing your message, the regenerate ones resident in every part will come here, and some have already arrived, all save Mahodaya and the hundred sons of Vasiştha.

verses.sanskrit:
वासिष्ठं तच्छतं सर्वं क्रोधपर्याकुलाक्षरम्
यदाह वचनं सर्वं शृणु त्वं मुनिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
vāsiṣṭhaṁ tacchataṁ sarvaṁ krodhaparyākulākṣaram
yadāha vacanaṁ sarvaṁ śṛṇu tvaṁ munipuṁgava

translations.english: Do you, O foremost of ascetics, listen to the words that they said with accents tremulous with emotion.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणा वा महात्मानो भुक्त्वा चण्डालभोजनम्
कथं स्वर्गं गमिष्यन्ति विश्वामित्रेण पालिताः
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇā vā mahātmāno bhuktvā caṇḍālabhojanam
kathaṁ svargaṁ gamiṣyanti viśvāmitreṇa pālitāḥ

translations.english: How can celestials and saints partake of offerings in the court of him that in addition to being a Chandala, has for this priest a Kşatriya? And how high-souled Brahmanas, patronised by Visvāmitra, attain to heaven, having partaken of a Candāla's fare?

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्वचनं नैष्ठुर्यमूचुः संरक्तलोचनाः
वासिष्ठा मुनिशार्दूल सर्वे ते समहोदयाः
verses.transliteration:
etadvacanaṁ naiṣṭhuryamūcuḥ saṁraktalocanāḥ
vāsiṣṭhā muniśārdūla sarve te samahodayāḥ

translations.english: These cruel words, O powerful ascetic, did Vasiştha's sons together with Mahodaya, utter with reddened eyes.'

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां मुनिपुंगवः
क्रोधसंरक्तनयनः सरोषमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā sarveṣāṁ munipuṁgavaḥ
krodhasaṁraktanayanaḥ saroṣamidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing those words of theirs, that foremost of ascetics, with eyes reddened in anger, wrathfully cried.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्दूषयन्त्यदुष्टं मां तप उग्रं समास्थितम्
भस्मीभूता दुरात्मानो भविष्यन्ति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
yaddūṣayantyaduṣṭaṁ māṁ tapa ugraṁ samāsthitam
bhasmībhūtā durātmāno bhaviṣyanti na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Since blameless, as I am, those wicked-minded ones censure me practising fierce austerities, they shall, without doubt, be reduced to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वमांसनियताहारा मुष्टिका नाम निर्घृणाः
विकृताश्च विरूपाश्च लोकाननुचरन्त्विमान्
verses.transliteration:
śvamāṁsaniyatāhārā muṣṭikā nāma nirghṛṇāḥ
vikṛtāśca virūpāśca lokānanucarantvimān

translations.english: And this very day bound by the noose of Kala, meeting with destruction at the hands of Vivaśvata's son, (Yama) they shall for seven hundred firths range these worlds, wearing dead men's clothes, always feeding on dogs' flesh, going by the name of Mahodaya also has blamed me, although undeserving of blame; therefore, reproved of all, he shall undergo Nişadahood. And becoming cruel, and engaged in taking life, he shall through my ire fare wretchedly for a long lapse of time.'

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणातिपातनिरतो निरनुक्रोशतां गतः
दीर्घकालं मम क्रोधाद्दुर्गतिं वर्तयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
prāṇātipātanirato niranukrośatāṁ gataḥ
dīrghakālaṁ mama krodhāddurgatiṁ vartayiṣyati

translations.english: Having uttered this in the assembly of saints, that mighty ascetic, the highly powerful Viśvāmitra of fierce asceticism, paused.

verses.sanskrit:
तपोबलहतान्कृत्वा वासिष्ठान्समहोदयान्
ऋषिमध्ये महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tapobalahatānkṛtvā vāsiṣṭhānsamahodayān
ṛṣimadhye mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: And knowing (by virtue of his Yoga power) Vasiştha's sons together with Mahodaya as destroyed in consequence of his ascetic energy, the highly powerful Viśvāmitra said in the midst of the saints.

verses.sanskrit:
अयमिक्ष्वाकुदायादस्त्रिशङ्कुरिति विश्रुतः
धर्मिष्ठश्च वदान्यश्च मां चैव शरणं गतः
स्वेनानेन शरीरेण देवलोकजिगीषया
verses.transliteration:
ayamikṣvākudāyādastriśaṅkuriti viśrutaḥ
dharmiṣṭhaśca vadānyaśca māṁ caiva śaraṇaṁ gataḥ
svenānena śarīreṇa devalokajigīṣayā

translations.english: This descendant of Ikşvāku, the famous Trišanku, is virtuous and munificent, and has taken refuge in me, with the view of attaining the celestial regions in his own person. Therefore do you engage with me in the sacrifice, so that he may bodily repair to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं कुशिकदायादो मुनिः परमकोपनः
यदाह वचनं सम्यगेतत्कार्यं न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ kuśikadāyādo muniḥ paramakopanaḥ
yadāha vacanaṁ samyagetatkāryaṁ na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Viśvāmitra's words, the pious Maharsis readily spoke in harmony with duty, saying, “This descendant of Kuśika is a highly irascible ascetic, therefore what he said should, without doubt, he performed.'

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निकल्पो हि भगवाञ्शापं दास्यति रोषितः
तस्मात्प्रवर्त्यतां यज्ञः सशरीरो यथा दिवम्
गच्छेदिक्ष्वाकुदायादो विश्वामित्रस्य तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
agnikalpo hi bhagavāñśāpaṁ dāsyati roṣitaḥ
tasmātpravartyatāṁ yajñaḥ saśarīro yathā divam
gacchedikṣvākudāyādo viśvāmitrasya tejasā

translations.english: The worshipful one is like to fire, and, if angered, may curse us. Therefore, let us engage in this sacrifice, so that Ikşvāku's descendant through the potency of Viśvāmitra way repair to heaven in person.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रवर्त्यतां यज्ञः सर्वे समधितिष्ठते
verses.transliteration: tataḥ pravartyatāṁ yajñaḥ sarve samadhitiṣṭhate

translations.english: Then let us engage in this sacrifice. Saying this, sages entered the upon the ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋत्विजश्चानुपूर्व्येण मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रकोविदाः
चक्रुः सर्वाणि कर्माणि यथाकल्पं यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
ṛtvijaścānupūrvyeṇa mantravanmantrakovidāḥ
cakruḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi yathākalpaṁ yathāvidhi

translations.english: And in that sacrifice the highly energetic Viśvāmitra acted as the priest. And Ritwijas versed in mantras performed every thing in order with mantras, in accordance with scripture and prescription.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कालेन महता विश्वामित्रो महातपाः
चकारावाहनं तत्र भागार्थं सर्वदेवताः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kālena mahatā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ
cakārāvāhanaṁ tatra bhāgārthaṁ sarvadevatāḥ

translations.english: Then after a long time, Viśvāmitra of mighty austerities invoked thither all the celestials for receiving their respective shares; but the deities did not come to receive them.

verses.sanskrit:
स्रुवमुद्यम्य सक्रोधस्त्रिशङ्कुमिदमब्रवीत्
पश्य मे तपसो वीर्यं स्वार्जितस्य नरेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
sruvamudyamya sakrodhastriśaṅkumidamabravīt
paśya me tapaso vīryaṁ svārjitasya nareśvara

translations.english: Thereupon, getting into a wrath, the mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra, lifting up a garland, wrathfully exclaimed.

verses.sanskrit:
एष त्वां स्वशरीरेण नयामि स्वर्गमोजसा
दुष्प्रापं स्वशरीरेण दिवं गच्छ नराधिप
verses.transliteration:
eṣa tvāṁ svaśarīreṇa nayāmi svargamojasā
duṣprāpaṁ svaśarīreṇa divaṁ gaccha narādhipa

translations.english: O lord of men, do you witness the prowess of my self-earned asceticism. And, O king, do you in person repair to heaven hard to attain.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वार्जितं किंचिदप्यस्ति मया हि तपसः फलम्
राजंस्त्वं तेजसा तस्य सशरीरो दिवं व्रज
verses.transliteration:
svārjitaṁ kiṁcidapyasti mayā hi tapasaḥ phalam
rājaṁstvaṁ tejasā tasya saśarīro divaṁ vraja

translations.english: Something yet remains in me of the selfearned fruit of my asceticism; and, O king, through the energy of that asceticism, do you repair to heaven in person.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्सशरीरो नरेश्वरः
दिवं जगाम काकुत्स्थ मुनीनां पश्यतां तदा
verses.transliteration:
uktavākye munau tasminsaśarīro nareśvaraḥ
divaṁ jagāma kākutstha munīnāṁ paśyatāṁ tadā

translations.english: And on the ascetic saying this, O Kākutstha, that lord of men, bodily ascended heaven in the very sight of the anchorets.

verses.sanskrit:
देवलोकगतं दृष्ट्वा त्रिशङ्कुं पाकशासनः
सह सर्वैः सुरगणैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
devalokagataṁ dṛṣṭvā triśaṅkuṁ pākaśāsanaḥ
saha sarvaiḥ suragaṇairidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And beholding Trisanku risen to heaven, the subduer of Indra, together with all the celestial said.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिशङ्को गच्छ भूयस्त्वं नासि स्वर्गकृतालयः
गुरुशापहतो मूढ पत भूमिमवाक्शिराः
verses.transliteration:
triśaṅko gaccha bhūyastvaṁ nāsi svargakṛtālayaḥ
guruśāpahato mūḍha pata bhūmimavākśirāḥ

translations.english: O Trisanku, turn you back. You have not earned abode in heaven. O fool, you have been blighted by the curse of your spiritual guide. Do you therefore drop down headlong.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो महेन्द्रेण त्रिशङ्कुरपतत्पुनः
विक्रोशमानस्त्राहीति विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्
verses.transliteration:
evamukto mahendreṇa triśaṅkurapatatpunaḥ
vikrośamānastrāhīti viśvāmitraṁ tapodhanam

translations.english: The great Indra having spoken thus, Trisanku fell down, crying to the ascetic Viśvāmitra, 'Save me, save me.'

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य क्रोशमानस्य कौशिकः
रोषमाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vacanaṁ tasya krośamānasya kauśikaḥ
roṣamāhārayattīvraṁ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt

translations.english: Thereupon, hearing his distressful cries, Kausika waxed mightily wroth, and exclaimed, 'Stay, stay.'

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिमध्ये स तेजस्वी प्रजापतिरिवापरः
सृजन्दक्षिणमार्गस्थान्सप्तर्षीनपरान्पुनः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣimadhye sa tejasvī prajāpatirivāparaḥ
sṛjandakṣiṇamārgasthānsaptarṣīnaparānpunaḥ

translations.english: In the midst of the ascetics, like to another Prajapati, he created other seven Rsis* on the Southern way: and also, overwhelined with wrath created another set of stars. *Ursa major.

verses.sanskrit:
सृष्ट्वा नक्षत्रवंशं च क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः
अन्यमिन्द्रं करिष्यामि लोको वा स्यादनिन्द्रकः
दैवतान्यपि स क्रोधात्स्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
sṛṣṭvā nakṣatravaṁśaṁ ca krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ
anyamindraṁ kariṣyāmi loko vā syādanindrakaḥ
daivatānyapi sa krodhātsraṣṭuṁ samupacakrame

translations.english: And collied* with passion, that illustrious one in the midst of the ascetics created another system of stars in the southern direction. And, saying, 'I will create another Indra, or the world (that I create) shall be without an Indra.' And in anger, he went the length of creating celestials. *And passion having my best judgement collied.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परमसंभ्रान्ताः सर्षिसंघाः सुरर्षभाः
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानमूचुः सानुनयं वचः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paramasaṁbhrāntāḥ sarṣisaṁghāḥ surarṣabhāḥ
viśvāmitraṁ mahātmānamūcuḥ sānunayaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, in trepidation, the saints and the celestials and the Asuras humbly addressed the high souled Viśvāmitra thus.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं राजा महाभाग गुरुशापपरिक्षतः
सशरीरो दिवं यातुं नार्हत्येव तपोधन
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ rājā mahābhāga guruśāpaparikṣataḥ
saśarīro divaṁ yātuṁ nārhatyeva tapodhana

translations.english: 'This king, O highly exalted one, has been visited with the curse of his preceptor, therefore, O ascetic; he deserves not to ascend heaven in person.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां मुनिपुंगवः
अब्रवीत्सुमहद्वाक्यं कौशिकः सर्वदेवताः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā devānāṁ munipuṁgavaḥ
abravītsumahadvākyaṁ kauśikaḥ sarvadevatāḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of theirs, that best of anchorets, Kausika, in company with the celestials, said these pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit:
सशरीरस्य भद्रं वस्त्रिशङ्कोरस्य भूपतेः
आरोहणं प्रतिज्ञाय नानृतं कर्तुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
saśarīrasya bhadraṁ vastriśaṅkorasya bhūpateḥ
ārohaṇaṁ pratijñāya nānṛtaṁ kartumutsahe

translations.english: Good betide you, I have vowed to this king, Trišanku's bodily ascension unto heaven, therefore, I dare not falsify my vow.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्गोऽस्तु सशरीरस्य त्रिशङ्कोरस्य शाश्वतः
नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि मामकानि ध्रुवाण्यथ
verses.transliteration:
sargo'stu saśarīrasya triśaṅkorasya śāśvataḥ
nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi māmakāni dhruvāṇyatha

translations.english: Let Trisanku evermore dwell in heaven in person, and let these stars created by me verily endure as long as the worlds. This it behove you, you gods, to ordain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देवा महात्मानो मुनयश्च तपोधनाः
जग्मुर्यथागतं सर्वे यज्ञस्यान्ते नरोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
tato devā mahātmāno munayaśca tapodhanāḥ
jagmuryathāgataṁ sarve yajñasyānte narottama

translations.english: Then, after the sacrifice had concluded, the high-souled celestials and the saints of ascetic wealth went to their respective regions, o foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रो महात्माथ प्रस्थितान्प्रेक्ष्य तानृषीन्
अब्रवीन्नरशार्दूल सर्वांस्तान्वनवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro mahātmātha prasthitānprekṣya tānṛṣīn
abravīnnaraśārdūla sarvāṁstānvanavāsinaḥ

translations.english: And, O puissant one, seeing those saints gone, the highly energetic Viśvāmitra addressed those inhabitants of the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
महाविघ्नः प्रवृत्तोऽयं दक्षिणामास्थितो दिशम्
दिशमन्यां प्रपत्स्यामस्तत्र तप्स्यामहे तपः
verses.transliteration:
mahāvighnaḥ pravṛtto'yaṁ dakṣiṇāmāsthito diśam
diśamanyāṁ prapatsyāmastatra tapsyāmahe tapaḥ

translations.english: A mighty disturbance has happened in regard to the southern quarter: let us therefore repairing to another region, carry on austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्चिमायां विशालायां पुष्करेषु महात्मनः
सुखं तपश्चरिष्यामः परं तद्धि तपोवनम्
verses.transliteration:
paścimāyāṁ viśālāyāṁ puṣkareṣu mahātmanaḥ
sukhaṁ tapaścariṣyāmaḥ paraṁ taddhi tapovanam

translations.english: You high-souled ones, in the west there are extensive tracts; and there in Puşkara will we peaceably carry on our austerities. That asylum is really pleasant.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः पुष्करेषु महामुनिः
तप उग्रं दुराधर्षं तेपे मूलफलाशनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahātejāḥ puṣkareṣu mahāmuniḥ
tapa ugraṁ durādharṣaṁ tepe mūlaphalāśanaḥ

translations.english: Having said this, that exceedingly energetic and mighty Muni (Ascetic) began to perform terrible austerities, subsisting on fruits and roots.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु अयोध्याधिपतिर्नृपः
अम्बरीष इति ख्यातो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
etasminneva kāle tu ayodhyādhipatirnṛpaḥ
ambarīṣa iti khyāto yaṣṭuṁ samupacakrame

translations.english: And it came to pass that at this time that mighty lord of Ayodhyā, Ambarışa, prepared for celebrating a sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य वै यजमानस्य पशुमिन्द्रो जहार ह
प्रनष्टे तु पशौ विप्रो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya vai yajamānasya paśumindro jahāra ha
pranaṣṭe tu paśau vipro rājānamidamabravīt

translations.english: And as he was sacrificing, Indra stole away his sacrificial beast. And on the beast being stolen, the priest said unto the king.

verses.sanskrit:
पशुरद्य हृतो राजन्प्रनष्टस्तव दुर्नयात्
अरक्षितारं राजानं घ्नन्ति दोषा नरेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
paśuradya hṛto rājanpranaṣṭastava durnayāt
arakṣitāraṁ rājānaṁ ghnanti doṣā nareśvara

translations.english: O king, the beast has been stolen (away); and it has been lost through your dereliction. And, O lord of men, his own fault destroy the king that fail to protect (the beast).7

verses.sanskrit:
प्रायश्चित्तं महद्ध्येतन्नरं वा पुरुषर्षभ
आनयस्व पशुं शीघ्रं यावत्कर्म प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
prāyaścittaṁ mahaddhyetannaraṁ vā puruṣarṣabha
ānayasva paśuṁ śīghraṁ yāvatkarma pravartate

translations.english: O best of men, even this is the expiation: do you, while the ceremony lasts, speedily bring back the beast, or bring a man in its stead.

verses.sanskrit:
उपाध्याय वचः श्रुत्वा स राजा पुरुषर्षभ
अन्वियेष महाबुद्धिः पशुं गोभिः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
upādhyāya vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā puruṣarṣabha
anviyeṣa mahābuddhiḥ paśuṁ gobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the priest's words, that highly intelligent king began to range various countries and provinces, cities, forests, and holy asylums, searching for the beast, with a thousand king (as the price thereof.)

verses.sanskrit:
देशाञ्जनपदांस्तांस्तान्नगराणि वनानि च
आश्रमाणि च पुण्यानि मार्गमाणो महीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
deśāñjanapadāṁstāṁstānnagarāṇi vanāni ca
āśramāṇi ca puṇyāni mārgamāṇo mahīpatiḥ

translations.english: And, O child, it came to pass that arriving at Bhrgutunga, (A mountain peak) he beheld Řcīka seated there in company with his wife and sons.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच महातेजाः प्रणम्याभिप्रसाद्य च
ब्रह्मर्षिं तपसा दीप्तं राजर्षिरमितप्रभः
पृष्ट्वा सर्वत्र कुशलमृचीकं तमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca mahātejāḥ praṇamyābhiprasādya ca
brahmarṣiṁ tapasā dīptaṁ rājarṣiramitaprabhaḥ
pṛṣṭvā sarvatra kuśalamṛcīkaṁ tamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu. And bowing to that Brahmarşi flaming in asceticism, and propitiating him, the exceedingly energetic royal saint of unparalleled effulgence having enquired as to his complete welfare, addressed Rcika, saying, 'O highly pious one, O Bhrgu's son, if in order that I may have a substitute for my sacrificial beast, you sell your son, my desire I shall atain.'

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे परिसृता देशा यज्ञियं न लभे पशुम्
दातुमर्हसि मूल्येन सुतमेकमितो मम
verses.transliteration:
sarve parisṛtā deśā yajñiyaṁ na labhe paśum
dātumarhasi mūlyena sutamekamito mama

translations.english: I have ranged every country; but the beast I do not find. Therefore, it behove you to part with one of your sons for price.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो महातेजा ऋचीकस्त्वब्रवीद्वचः
नाहं ज्येष्ठं नरश्रेष्ठं विक्रीणीयां कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
evamukto mahātejā ṛcīkastvabravīdvacaḥ
nāhaṁ jyeṣṭhaṁ naraśreṣṭhaṁ vikrīṇīyāṁ kathaṁcana

translations.english: Thus addressed the exceedingly energetic Rcīka replied, “O best of men, my first-born I will in no wise dispose of.'

verses.sanskrit:
ऋचीकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तेषां माता महात्मनाम्
उवाच नरशार्दूलमम्बरीषं तपस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
ṛcīkasya vacaḥ śrutvā teṣāṁ mātā mahātmanām
uvāca naraśārdūlamambarīṣaṁ tapasvinī

translations.english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Rcīka, their mother spoke to that foremost of men, Amvarisha, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
प्रायेण हि नरश्रेष्ठ ज्येष्ठाः पितृषु वल्लभाः
मातॄणां च कनीयांसस्तस्माद्रक्षे कनीयसम्
verses.transliteration:
prāyeṇa hi naraśreṣṭha jyeṣṭhāḥ pitṛṣu vallabhāḥ
mātṝṇāṁ ca kanīyāṁsastasmādrakṣe kanīyasam

translations.english: O foremost of men, the eldest sons are generally the best beloved of their fathers; and the youngest, of their mother, therefore the youngest I would retain.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्मुनिपत्न्यां तथैव च
शुनःशेपः स्वयं राम मध्यमो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
uktavākye munau tasminmunipatnyāṁ tathaiva ca
śunaḥśepaḥ svayaṁ rāma madhyamo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And when the ascetic as well as his wife had spoken thus, the second son, Sunahsepa, O Rāma, himself said.

verses.sanskrit:
पिता ज्येष्ठमविक्रेयं माता चाह कनीयसम्
विक्रीतं मध्यमं मन्ये राजन्पुत्रं नयस्व माम्
verses.transliteration:
pitā jyeṣṭhamavikreyaṁ mātā cāha kanīyasam
vikrītaṁ madhyamaṁ manye rājanputraṁ nayasva mām

translations.english: My father would not sell the eldest; nor my mother the youngest,—therefore, I consider even the second as disposable. Do you then, O prince, take me.

verses.sanskrit:
गवां शतसहस्रेण शुनःशेपं नरेश्वरः
गृहीत्वा परमप्रीतो जगाम रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
gavāṁ śatasahasreṇa śunaḥśepaṁ nareśvaraḥ
gṛhītvā paramaprīto jagāma raghunandana

translations.english: When that one versed in the Veda had ended, that lord of men, O mighty-armed descendant of Raghu, taking possession of Sunaḥsepa, by paying koțis of kine, and heaps of jewels, and gold and silver by hundreds and thousands, went away exceedingly delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
अम्बरीषस्तु राजर्षी रथमारोप्य सत्वरः
शुनःशेपं महातेजा जगामाशु महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
ambarīṣastu rājarṣī rathamāropya satvaraḥ
śunaḥśepaṁ mahātejā jagāmāśu mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: That royal saint, the exceedingly energetic and highly famous Ambarīşa, placing Sunaḥsepa on his car, speedily set out.

verses.sanskrit:
शुनःशेपं नरश्रेष्ठ गृहीत्वा तु महायशाः
व्यश्राम्यत्पुष्करे राजा मध्याह्ने रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
śunaḥśepaṁ naraśreṣṭha gṛhītvā tu mahāyaśāḥ
vyaśrāmyatpuṣkare rājā madhyāhne raghunandana

translations.english: O foremost of men, taking Sunaḥsepa, that illustrious king at noon rested in Puşkara, O descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य विश्रममाणस्य शुनःशेपो महायशाः
पुष्करं श्रेष्ठमागम्य विश्वामित्रं ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
tasya viśramamāṇasya śunaḥśepo mahāyaśāḥ
puṣkaraṁ śreṣṭhamāgamya viśvāmitraṁ dadarśa ha

translations.english: And having arrived at the excellent Puskara, as the king was resting, the famous Sunaḥsepa with an aggrieved heart saw his maternal uncle Viśvāmitra in company with some saints engaged in asceticism. Thereupon, with a woebegone countenance, and sore afflicted with fatigue and thirst, he, O Rāma, flung himself into (Viśvāmitra's) lap, and said.

verses.sanskrit:
न मेऽस्ति माता न पिता ज्ञातयो बान्धवाः कुतः
त्रातुमर्हसि मां सौम्य धर्मेण मुनिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
na me'sti mātā na pitā jñātayo bāndhavāḥ kutaḥ
trātumarhasi māṁ saumya dharmeṇa munipuṁgava

translations.english: I have neither father, nor mother, nor relatives, nor friends anywhere. It therefore behoves you, O gentle one, to save me in the interests of virtue, O foremost of ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
त्राता त्वं हि मुनिश्रेष्ठ सर्वेषां त्वं हि भावनः
राजा च कृतकार्यः स्यादहं दीर्घायुरव्ययः
verses.transliteration:
trātā tvaṁ hi muniśreṣṭha sarveṣāṁ tvaṁ hi bhāvanaḥ
rājā ca kṛtakāryaḥ syādahaṁ dīrghāyuravyayaḥ

translations.english: And, O best of men, you are the protector of all, and their refuge. May the king have his desire and may I at the same time, attaining long life, and undeteriorating, gain heaven, having performed meritorious austerities!

verses.sanskrit:
स्वर्गलोकमुपाश्नीयां तपस्तप्त्वा ह्यनुत्तमम्
स मे नाथो ह्यनाथस्य भव भव्येन चेतसा
पितेव पुत्रं धर्मात्मंस्त्रातुमर्हसि किल्बिषात्
verses.transliteration:
svargalokamupāśnīyāṁ tapastaptvā hyanuttamam
sa me nātho hyanāthasya bhava bhavyena cetasā
piteva putraṁ dharmātmaṁstrātumarhasi kilbiṣāt

translations.english: Do you with a delighted heart become a lord to me that am without one. And, O righteous one, even as a father rescue a son, do you deliver me from this peril.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महातपाः
सान्त्वयित्वा बहुविधं पुत्रानिदमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ
sāntvayitvā bahuvidhaṁ putrānidamuvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing his words, Viśvāmitra of mighty austerities, pacifying him by every means, spoke to this sons, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
यत्कृते पितरः पुत्राञ्जनयन्ति शुभार्थिनः
परलोकहितार्थाय तस्य कालोऽयमागतः
verses.transliteration:
yatkṛte pitaraḥ putrāñjanayanti śubhārthinaḥ
paralokahitārthāya tasya kālo'yamāgataḥ

translations.english: That in view of which fathers beget wellwishing sons, the compassing of other's welfare is at hand.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं मुनिसुतो बालो मत्तः शरणमिच्छति
अस्य जीवितमात्रेण प्रियं कुरुत पुत्रकाः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ munisuto bālo mattaḥ śaraṇamicchati
asya jīvitamātreṇa priyaṁ kuruta putrakāḥ

translations.english: This youthful son. of the ascetic crave my protection. O you sons, do accomplish my desire by saving his life.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे सुकृतकर्माणः सर्वे धर्मपरायणाः
पशुभूता नरेन्द्रस्य तृप्तिमग्नेः प्रयच्छत
verses.transliteration:
sarve sukṛtakarmāṇaḥ sarve dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
paśubhūtā narendrasya tṛptimagneḥ prayacchata

translations.english: You are all of virtuous deeds, you are all engaged in the observance of righteousness, do you confer satisfaction upon Agni by one of you becoming the (sacrificial) beast of the lord of men.

verses.sanskrit:
नाथवांश्च शुनःशेपो यज्ञश्चाविघ्नतो भवेत्
देवतास्तर्पिताश्च स्युर्मम चापि कृतं वचः
verses.transliteration:
nāthavāṁśca śunaḥśepo yajñaścāvighnato bhavet
devatāstarpitāśca syurmama cāpi kṛtaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Thus Sunaḥsepa will obtain protection, the sacrifice will be freed from hindrance the deities will be propitiated, and finally my word will be made good.

verses.sanskrit:
मुनेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा मधुष्यन्दादयः सुताः
साभिमानं नरश्रेष्ठ सलीलमिदमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
munestu vacanaṁ śrutvā madhuṣyandādayaḥ sutāḥ
sābhimānaṁ naraśreṣṭha salīlamidamabruvan

translations.english: Hearing the ascetic's words, his sons, Madhucchanda and others, O foremost of me, haughtily and tauntingly answered.

verses.sanskrit:
कथमात्मसुतान्हित्वा त्रायसेऽन्यसुतं विभो
अकार्यमिव पश्यामः श्वमांसमिव भोजने
verses.transliteration:
kathamātmasutānhitvā trāyase'nyasutaṁ vibho
akāryamiva paśyāmaḥ śvamāṁsamiva bhojane

translations.english: O lord, how, neglecting your own sons, you desire to deliver that of another? This we consider as heinous, even like to eating one's own flesh.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां मुनिपुंगवः
क्रोधसंरक्तनयनो व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā putrāṇāṁ munipuṁgavaḥ
krodhasaṁraktanayano vyāhartumupacakrame

translations.english: Hearing this speech of his sons, that best of anchorets, with eyes reddened with anger, said.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वमांसभोजिनः सर्वे वासिष्ठा इव जातिषु
पूर्णं वर्षसहस्रं तु पृथिव्यामनुवत्स्यथ
verses.transliteration:
śvamāṁsabhojinaḥ sarve vāsiṣṭhā iva jātiṣu
pūrṇaṁ varṣasahasraṁ tu pṛthivyāmanuvatsyatha

translations.english: Disregarding my words, you have uttered this audacious and shocking speech, disclaimed by morality, and capable of causing one's hair to stand on end. Therefore, becoming Mustikas, and living on dogs' flesh, do you all, even like Vasiştha's sons, inhabit the earth for a thousand years.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा शापसमायुक्तान्पुत्रान्मुनिवरस्तदा
शुनःशेपमुवाचार्तं कृत्वा रक्षां निरामयाम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā śāpasamāyuktānputrānmunivarastadā
śunaḥśepamuvācārtaṁ kṛtvā rakṣāṁ nirāmayām

translations.english: Having cursed his sons, that best of ascetics then, by all means cheering up the distressed Śunaḥsepa as to his protection, addressed him.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे तु गाथे द्वे दिव्ये गायेथा मुनिपुत्रक
अम्बरीषस्य यज्ञेऽस्मिंस्ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि
verses.transliteration:
ime tu gāthe dve divye gāyethā muniputraka
ambarīṣasya yajñe'smiṁstataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi

translations.english: Do you donning on a sacred zone, and wearing a garland of red flowers, and bedaubing your person with red sand paste, hymn Agni with mantras, approaching the Vaisnava sacrificial stake; and, O ascetic's son, (at the same time) chant these two verses in that sacrifice of Amvarisha. Then you will attain success.

verses.sanskrit:
शुनःशेपो गृहीत्वा ते द्वे गाथे सुसमाहितः
त्वरया राजसिंहं तमम्बरीषमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
śunaḥśepo gṛhītvā te dve gāthe susamāhitaḥ
tvarayā rājasiṁhaṁ tamambarīṣamuvāca ha

translations.english: Thereupon, with a concentrated mind securing those two verses, Sunaḥsepa speedily presented himself before that leonine monarch saying,

verses.sanskrit:
राजसिंह महासत्त्व शीघ्रं गच्छावहे सदः
निवर्तयस्व राजेन्द्र दीक्षां च समुपाहर
verses.transliteration:
rājasiṁha mahāsattva śīghraṁ gacchāvahe sadaḥ
nivartayasva rājendra dīkṣāṁ ca samupāhara

translations.english: O lion of a king, O you endued with high intelligence, let us without delay repair hence. And, O foremost of monarchs, do you engage in the sacrifice and commence upon the initiation.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वाक्यमृषिपुत्रस्य श्रुत्वा हर्षं समुत्सुकः
जगाम नृपतिः शीघ्रं यज्ञवाटमतन्द्रितः
verses.transliteration:
tadvākyamṛṣiputrasya śrutvā harṣaṁ samutsukaḥ
jagāma nṛpatiḥ śīghraṁ yajñavāṭamatandritaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of the ascetic's son, the king, filled with delight, readily at once repaired to the sacrificial ground.

verses.sanskrit:
सदस्यानुमते राजा पवित्रकृतलक्षणम्
पशुं रक्ताम्बरं कृत्वा यूपे तं समबन्धयत्
verses.transliteration:
sadasyānumate rājā pavitrakṛtalakṣaṇam
paśuṁ raktāmbaraṁ kṛtvā yūpe taṁ samabandhayat

translations.english: With the consent of his court, the king fastened Sunaħsepa with a Kuśa cord, and investing him with a crimson apparel tethered him to the stake as the (sacrificial) beast.

verses.sanskrit:
स बद्धो वाग्भिरग्र्याभिरभितुष्टाव वै सुरौ
इन्द्रमिन्द्रानुजं चैव यथावन्मुनिपुत्रकः
verses.transliteration:
sa baddho vāgbhiragryābhirabhituṣṭāva vai surau
indramindrānujaṁ caiva yathāvanmuniputrakaḥ

translations.english: Being bound (to the stake), the ascetic's son first of all duly hymned Agni, and next those deities, Indra and his younger brother.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतः सहस्राक्षो रहस्यस्तुतितर्पितः
दीर्घमायुस्तदा प्रादाच्छुनःशेपाय राघव
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prītaḥ sahasrākṣo rahasyastutitarpitaḥ
dīrghamāyustadā prādācchunaḥśepāya rāghava

translations.english: Thereupon, gratified with the excellent eulogy, the thousand eyed Väsava conferred upon Sunaḥsepa long life.

verses.sanskrit:
स च राजा नरश्रेष्ठ यज्ञस्य च समाप्तवान्
फलं बहुगुणं राम सहस्राक्षप्रसादजम्
verses.transliteration:
sa ca rājā naraśreṣṭha yajñasya ca samāptavān
phalaṁ bahuguṇaṁ rāma sahasrākṣaprasādajam

translations.english: And, O foremost of men, that king also, having completed the sacrifice, obtained the manifold fruit thereof through the grace of the thousand-eyed deity,

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रोऽपि धर्मात्मा भूयस्तेपे महातपाः
पुष्करेषु नरश्रेष्ठ दशवर्षशतानि च
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro'pi dharmātmā bhūyastepe mahātapāḥ
puṣkareṣu naraśreṣṭha daśavarṣaśatāni ca

translations.english: O Rāma, And, O best of men, the righteous Viśvāmitra of mighty asceticism again carried on austerities at Puskara for ten hundred years.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु व्रतस्नातं महामुनिम्
अभ्यागच्छन्सुराः सर्वे तपःफलचिकीर्षवः
verses.transliteration:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu vratasnātaṁ mahāmunim
abhyāgacchansurāḥ sarve tapaḥphalacikīrṣavaḥ

translations.english: When the thousand years had been completed and the mighty ascetic had accomplished his vow, the celestials in a body desirous of conferring upon him the fruit thereof, appeared before him.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीत्सुमहातेजा ब्रह्मा सुरुचिरं वचः
ऋषिस्त्वमसि भद्रं ते स्वार्जितैः कर्मभिः शुभैः
verses.transliteration:
abravītsumahātejā brahmā suruciraṁ vacaḥ
ṛṣistvamasi bhadraṁ te svārjitaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ

translations.english: The exceedingly effulgent Brahmă addressed him in soothing words, saying, “You are henceforth a saint, good to you, and (this. eminence) you have attained through your own laudable exertions.'

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमुक्त्वा देवेशस्त्रिदिवं पुनरभ्यगात्
विश्वामित्रो महातेजा भूयस्तेपे महत्तपः
verses.transliteration:
tamevamuktvā deveśastridivaṁ punarabhyagāt
viśvāmitro mahātejā bhūyastepe mahattapaḥ

translations.english: Having spoken thus to him, the lord of celestials returned to heaven. And Viśvāmitra of mighty energy became again engaged in rigid austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
तां ददर्श महातेजा मेनकां कुशिकात्मजः
रूपेणाप्रतिमां तत्र विद्युतं जलदे यथा
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dadarśa mahātejā menakāṁ kuśikātmajaḥ
rūpeṇāpratimāṁ tatra vidyutaṁ jalade yathā

translations.english: And, O foremost of men, it came to pass that after a long lapse of time that prime of Apsaras, Menaka, was at that time perforining her ablutions in Puskara, and she was observed by Kusika's son like to lighting among clouds. And coming under the control of Kandarpa, (Cupid) the anchorite spoke to her, saying, 'O Apsari, has your journey been a pleasant one? Do you abide in my asylum.'

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्ता सा वरारोहा तत्रावासमथाकरोत्
तपसो हि महाविघ्नो विश्वामित्रमुपागतः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktā sā varārohā tatrāvāsamathākarot
tapaso hi mahāvighno viśvāmitramupāgataḥ

translations.english: Do you favour me; for, good betide you, I have been rendered senseless by Madana. Thus addressed, that one of shapely hips began to dwell there.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां वसन्त्यां वर्षाणि पञ्च पञ्च च राघव
विश्वामित्राश्रमे सौम्य सुखेन व्यतिचक्रमुः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ vasantyāṁ varṣāṇi pañca pañca ca rāghava
viśvāmitrāśrame saumya sukhena vyaticakramuḥ

translations.english: And mighty was the hindrance that befell Viśvāmitra as regarded his asceticism, as she, O Rāghava, staying in that asylum of his, pleasantly spent five and five years, O gentle one.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ काले गते तस्मिन्विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
सव्रीड इव संवृत्तश्चिन्ताशोकपरायणः
verses.transliteration:
atha kāle gate tasminviśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
savrīḍa iva saṁvṛttaścintāśokaparāyaṇaḥ

translations.english: And after this period had gone by, overwhelmed with shame and afflicted with anxiety and grief, the mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra impatiently thought,

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्मुनेः समुत्पन्ना सामर्षा रघुनन्दन
सर्वं सुराणां कर्मैतत्तपोऽपहरणं महत्
verses.transliteration:
buddhirmuneḥ samutpannā sāmarṣā raghunandana
sarvaṁ surāṇāṁ karmaitattapo'paharaṇaṁ mahat

translations.english: O son of Raghu, that all this mighty loss of austerities was the work of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अहोरात्रापदेशेन गताः संवत्सरा दश
काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं प्रत्युपस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
ahorātrāpadeśena gatāḥ saṁvatsarā daśa
kāmamohābhibhūtasya vighno'yaṁ pratyupasthitaḥ

translations.english: And deprived of his senses by lust, the decade had passed away imperceptibly as if it were one day and night; and this impediment stood in the way of his austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
भीतामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा वेपन्तीं प्राञ्जलिं स्थिताम्
मेनकां मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्विसृज्य कुशिकात्मजः
उत्तरं पर्वतं राम विश्वामित्रो जगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
bhītāmapsarasaṁ dṛṣṭvā vepantīṁ prāñjaliṁ sthitām
menakāṁ madhurairvākyairvisṛjya kuśikātmajaḥ
uttaraṁ parvataṁ rāma viśvāmitro jagāma ha

translations.english: Having a sigh, that best of ascetics burned in repentance. And with sweet words renouncing the terrified and trembling Menaka standing with clasped hands, Kusika's son, Visvamitra, O Rāma, went to the northern mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
स कृत्वा नैष्ठिकीं बुद्धिं जेतुकामो महायशाः
कौशिकीतीरमासाद्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
sa kṛtvā naiṣṭhikīṁ buddhiṁ jetukāmo mahāyaśāḥ
kauśikītīramāsādya tapastepe sudāruṇam

translations.english: And practising the Brahmacarya mode of life with the intention of subduing lust, that highly famous one engaged in arduous austerities on the banks of the Kausiki.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य वर्षसहस्रं तु घोरं तप उपासतः
उत्तरे पर्वते राम देवतानामभूद्भयम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya varṣasahasraṁ tu ghoraṁ tapa upāsataḥ
uttare parvate rāma devatānāmabhūdbhayam

translations.english: And as he was thus engaged in profound austerities on the northern mountain, a thousand years, O Rāma passed away.

verses.sanskrit:
अमन्त्रयन्समागम्य सर्वे सर्षिगणाः सुराः
महर्षिशब्दं लभतां साध्वयं कुशिकात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
amantrayansamāgamya sarve sarṣigaṇāḥ surāḥ
maharṣiśabdaṁ labhatāṁ sādhvayaṁ kuśikātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then taking counsel together, the celestials and the saints appeared before (Brahma), saying, 'Let Kusika's son obtain the title of Maharsi.'

verses.sanskrit:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः
अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्
verses.transliteration:
devatānāṁ vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
abravīnmadhuraṁ vākyaṁ viśvāmitraṁ tapodhanam

translations.english: Hearing the words of the celestials, the Grand sire of all addressed the ascetic Viśvāmitra, in these sweet words, 'O mighty saint, hast you had a pleasant journey? Satisfied with your fierce austerities, O Kausika, I confer upon you the eminence of the foremost saintship.'

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणः स वचः श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रस्तपोधनः
प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतो भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच पितामहम्
verses.transliteration:
brahmaṇaḥ sa vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitrastapodhanaḥ
prāñjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā pratyuvāca pitāmaham

translations.english: Hearing Brahma's speech, the anchorite Viśvāmitra bowing down thus answered the Grandsire with clasped hands, The incomparable title of Brahmarși is to be won by one by performing sterling works. And since you have not addressed me (by that title), it appears that I have not yet succeeded in subduing my senses. *The text is very faulty. The literal meaning would be, since you have not.....I have subdued my senses, which would be absurd. I have therefore rendered the passage freely.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा न तावत्त्वं जितेन्द्रियः
यतस्व मुनिशार्दूल इत्युक्त्वा त्रिदिवं गतः
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca tato brahmā na tāvattvaṁ jitendriyaḥ
yatasva muniśārdūla ityuktvā tridivaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Brahmā said to him, 'Do you exert thyself until you conquer your senses?' Saying this, Brahmā went to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रस्थितेषु देवेषु विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
ऊर्ध्वबाहुर्निरालम्बो वायुभक्षस्तपश्चरन्
verses.transliteration:
viprasthiteṣu deveṣu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
ūrdhvabāhurnirālambo vāyubhakṣastapaścaran

translations.english: And when the celestials had gone, the mighty ascetic, Viśvāmitra, with upraised arms, and without any support, and subsisting on air, began to perform penances.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मे पञ्चतपा भूत्वा वर्षास्वाकाशसंश्रयः
शिशिरे सलिलस्थायी रात्र्यहानि तपोधनः
verses.transliteration:
dharme pañcatapā bhūtvā varṣāsvākāśasaṁśrayaḥ
śiśire salilasthāyī rātryahāni tapodhanaḥ

translations.english: And in summer, the ascetic surrounded himself with five fires, and in rains remained in an uncovered place, and in winter day and night stood submerged in water. Thus passed by a thousand years of terrible penances.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्संतप्यमाने तु विश्वामित्रे महामुनौ
संभ्रमः सुमहानासीत्सुराणां वासवस्य च
verses.transliteration:
tasminsaṁtapyamāne tu viśvāmitre mahāmunau
saṁbhramaḥ sumahānāsītsurāṇāṁ vāsavasya ca

translations.english: And on the mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra being engaged in austerities, great was the agitation that exercised the celestials and Indra, in particular.

verses.sanskrit:
रम्भामप्सरसं शक्रः सह सर्वैर्मरुद्गणैः
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यमहितं कौशिकस्य च
verses.transliteration:
rambhāmapsarasaṁ śakraḥ saha sarvairmarudgaṇaiḥ
uvācātmahitaṁ vākyamahitaṁ kauśikasya ca

translations.english: Śakra together with the Maruts spoke to Rambha these words, fraught with weal to himself, and woe to Kausika.'

verses.sanskrit:
सुरकार्यमिदं रम्भे कर्तव्यं सुमहत्त्वया
लोभनं कौशिकस्येह काममोहसमन्वितम्
verses.transliteration:
surakāryamidaṁ rambhe kartavyaṁ sumahattvayā
lobhanaṁ kauśikasyeha kāmamohasamanvitam

translations.english: O Rambha, this mighty service you will have to perform in the interest of the celestials, even to take Kausika with the witchery of love.'

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्ता साप्सरा राम सहस्राक्षेण धीमता
व्रीडिता प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच सुरेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
tathoktā sāpsarā rāma sahasrākṣeṇa dhīmatā
vrīḍitā prāñjalirbhūtvā pratyuvāca sureśvaram

translations.english: Thus addressed by the intelligent thousandeyed deity, the Apsarā, O Rāma, with clasped palms, thus bashfully answered the chief of the celestials,

verses.sanskrit:
अयं सुरपते घोरो विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
क्रोधमुत्स्रक्ष्यते घोरं मयि देव न संशयः
ततो हि मे भयं देव प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ surapate ghoro viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
krodhamutsrakṣyate ghoraṁ mayi deva na saṁśayaḥ
tato hi me bhayaṁ deva prasādaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: O lord of the celestials, this mighty ascetic, Viśvāmitra, is a terrible person; and, without doubt, he will, O divine one, waxing wroth, curse me.

verses.sanskrit:
तामुवाच सहस्राक्षो वेपमानां कृताञ्जलिम्
मा भैषि रम्भे भद्रं ते कुरुष्व मम शासनम्
verses.transliteration:
tāmuvāca sahasrākṣo vepamānāṁ kṛtāñjalim
mā bhaiṣi rambhe bhadraṁ te kuruṣva mama śāsanam

translations.english: And O god, even this is my fear, and therefore it behove you to favour me. Thus apprehensively addressed by her in fear, the thousand-eyed one answered that damsel trembling and staying with clasped hands, 'Never fear, O Rambhā, good to you! Do you perform my bidding.'

verses.sanskrit:
कोकिलो हृदयग्राही माधवे रुचिरद्रुमे
अहं कन्दर्पसहितः स्थास्यामि तव पार्श्वतः
verses.transliteration:
kokilo hṛdayagrāhī mādhave ruciradrume
ahaṁ kandarpasahitaḥ sthāsyāmi tava pārśvataḥ

translations.english: Assuming the form of a Cole, captivating the heart, I will in this spring crowned with graceful trees, stay by your side in company with Kandarpa.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि रूपं बहुगुणं कृत्वा परमभास्वरम्
तमृषिं कौशिकं रम्भे भेदयस्व तपस्विनम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi rūpaṁ bahuguṇaṁ kṛtvā paramabhāsvaram
tamṛṣiṁ kauśikaṁ rambhe bhedayasva tapasvinam

translations.english: Do you adding to your beauty, diverse blandishments bewitch this ascetic, Kusika's son, O gentle one?'

verses.sanskrit:
सा श्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कृत्वा रूपमनुत्तमम्
लोभयामास ललिता विश्वामित्रं शुचिस्मिता
verses.transliteration:
sā śrutvā vacanaṁ tasya kṛtvā rūpamanuttamam
lobhayāmāsa lalitā viśvāmitraṁ śucismitā

translations.english: Hearing Indra's words, that comely damsel of luminous smiles, heightening her charms exceedingly inspired Viśvāmitra with desire.

verses.sanskrit:
कोकिलस्य तु शुश्राव वल्गु व्याहरतः स्वनम्
संप्रहृष्टेन मनसा तत एनामुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
kokilasya tu śuśrāva valgu vyāharataḥ svanam
saṁprahṛṣṭena manasā tata enāmudaikṣata

translations.english: He listened to the mellifluous strains of the Cole; and with a delighted heart, he beheld the fair one.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तस्य च शब्देन गीतेनाप्रतिमेन च
दर्शनेन च रम्भाया मुनिः संदेहमागतः
verses.transliteration:
atha tasya ca śabdena gītenāpratimena ca
darśanena ca rambhāyā muniḥ saṁdehamāgataḥ

translations.english: Anon, listening to the warbling of the Cole and her own incomparable singing, as well as beholding Rambha, the ascetic began to entertain doubts.

verses.sanskrit:
सहस्राक्षस्य तत्कर्म विज्ञाय मुनिपुंगवः
रम्भां क्रोधसमाविष्टः शशाप कुशिकात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sahasrākṣasya tatkarma vijñāya munipuṁgavaḥ
rambhāṁ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ śaśāpa kuśikātmajaḥ

translations.english: And knowing for certain that it was the thousand-eyed deity who had devised all that, that foremost of anchorets, Kusika's son, overwhelmed with anger, cursed Rambha, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
यन्मां लोभयसे रम्भे कामक्रोधजयैषिणम्
दशवर्षसहस्राणि शैली स्थास्यसि दुर्भगे
verses.transliteration:
yanmāṁ lobhayase rambhe kāmakrodhajayaiṣiṇam
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi śailī sthāsyasi durbhage

translations.english: Since, O Rambhā, you endeavour to seduce me who is bent upon subduing his anger and lust, you shall, O luckless one, remain as a stone for ten thousand years.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणः सुमहातेजास्तपोबलसमन्वितः
उद्धरिष्यति रम्भे त्वां मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृताम्
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇaḥ sumahātejāstapobalasamanvitaḥ
uddhariṣyati rambhe tvāṁ matkrodhakaluṣīkṛtām

translations.english: And a highly energetic Brāhmaṇa equipped with ascetic energy, will, O Rambha, deliver you, stained because of my ire.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
अशक्नुवन्धारयितुं कोपं संतापमागतः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
aśaknuvandhārayituṁ kopaṁ saṁtāpamāgataḥ

translations.english: Thus said that exceedingly energetic and mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra, unable to contain his anger and indignation of heart.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य शापेन महता रम्भा शैली तदाभवत्
वचः श्रुत्वा च कन्दर्पो महर्षेः स च निर्गतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya śāpena mahatā rambhā śailī tadābhavat
vacaḥ śrutvā ca kandarpo maharṣeḥ sa ca nirgataḥ

translations.english: And in consequence of his mighty curse, Rambha was turned into a stone. Hearing the curse of the mighty saint, both Kandarpa and Indra left the place.

verses.sanskrit:
कोपेन स महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते
इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
kopena sa mahātejāstapo'paharaṇe kṛte
indriyairajitai rāma na lebhe śāntimātmanaḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, on account of his anger, and his sense remaining still unsubdued he found no rest from deterioration of ascetic merit. And coming by decrease of ascetic merit, he thought within himself, ‘No more shall I suffer anger to exercise me, nor will I ever say anything to any.'

verses.sanskrit:
अथ हैमवतीं राम दिशं त्यक्त्वा महामुनिः
पूर्वां दिशमनुप्राप्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
atha haimavatīṁ rāma diśaṁ tyaktvā mahāmuniḥ
pūrvāṁ diśamanuprāpya tapastepe sudāruṇam

translations.english: Forsaking the northern direction the mighty Muni, O Rāma, betaking himself to the Eastern quarter, became engaged in dreadful austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
मौनं वर्षसहस्रस्य कृत्वा व्रतमनुत्तमम्
चकाराप्रतिमं राम तपः परमदुष्करम्
verses.transliteration:
maunaṁ varṣasahasrasya kṛtvā vratamanuttamam
cakārāpratimaṁ rāma tapaḥ paramaduṣkaram

translations.english: Adopting the high vow of taciturnity for a thousand years, he, O Rāma began to perform the most signal and arduous austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु काष्ठभूतं महामुनिम्
विघ्नैर्बहुभिराधूतं क्रोधो नान्तरमाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu kāṣṭhabhūtaṁ mahāmunim
vighnairbahubhirādhūtaṁ krodho nāntaramāviśat

translations.english: When the thousand years had been complete, many an impediment tried the mighty Muni staying like the trunk of a tree, yet could not anger enter his heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः पन्नगासुरराक्षसाः
मोहितास्तेजसा तस्य तपसा मन्दरश्मयः
कश्मलोपहताः सर्वे पितामहमथाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ pannagāsurarākṣasāḥ
mohitāstejasā tasya tapasā mandaraśmayaḥ
kaśmalopahatāḥ sarve pitāmahamathābruvan

translations.english: And at this, the three worlds became afflicted with fear. And bewildered on account of the energy of his asceticisin, and shorn of their brightness, and afflicted with anguish, the Devarsis and the Gandharvas and the Pannagas and the Uragas and the Rakşasas in a body addressed the Pitāmaha, (Brahmā).

verses.sanskrit:
बहुभिः कारणैर्देव विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
लोभितः क्रोधितश्चैव तपसा चाभिवर्धते
verses.transliteration:
bahubhiḥ kāraṇairdeva viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
lobhitaḥ krodhitaścaiva tapasā cābhivardhate

translations.english: O divine one, various were the means by which we endeavoured to affect the mighty Muni Viśvāmitra with covetousness and lust; but for all that he increase in asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यस्य वृजिनं किंचिद्दृश्यते सूक्ष्ममप्यथ
न दीयते यदि त्वस्य मनसा यदभीप्सितम्
विनाशयति त्रैलोक्यं तपसा सचराचरम्
व्याकुलाश्च दिशः सर्वा न च किंचित्प्रकाशते
verses.transliteration:
na hyasya vṛjinaṁ kiṁciddṛśyate sūkṣmamapyatha
na dīyate yadi tvasya manasā yadabhīpsitam
vināśayati trailokyaṁ tapasā sacarācaram
vyākulāśca diśaḥ sarvā na ca kiṁcitprakāśate

translations.english: Nor do we perceive in him ever so little of anger or lust. And if you do not confer upon him what his mind desire to have, he will annihilate the three worlds with all that is mobile and immobile in them. And the ten cardinal points are disconsolate: and nothing can be discovered therein.

verses.sanskrit:
सागराः क्षुभिताः सर्वे विशीर्यन्ते च पर्वताः
प्रकम्पते च पृथिवी वायुर्वाति भृशाकुलः
verses.transliteration:
sāgarāḥ kṣubhitāḥ sarve viśīryante ca parvatāḥ
prakampate ca pṛthivī vāyurvāti bhṛśākulaḥ

translations.english: And the seas are vexed, and the mountains, riven. And the earth shake, and the winds keep steadily blowing.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिं न कुरुते यावन्नाशे देव महामुनिः
तावत्प्रसाद्यो भगवानग्निरूपो महाद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
buddhiṁ na kurute yāvannāśe deva mahāmuniḥ
tāvatprasādyo bhagavānagnirūpo mahādyutiḥ

translations.english: By virtue of that mighty saint's energy, the sun itself has been deprived of his splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
कालाग्निना यथा पूर्वं त्रैलोक्यं दह्यतेऽखिलम्
देवराज्ये चिकीर्षेत दीयतामस्य यन्मतम्
verses.transliteration:
kālāgninā yathā pūrvaṁ trailokyaṁ dahyate'khilam
devarājye cikīrṣeta dīyatāmasya yanmatam

translations.english: Therefore, O god, against the mighty Muni bending his mind upon destruction, and consuming the three entire worlds like to the fire raging at the universal dissolution, that exalted one of exceeding effulgence resembling a flame, should be pacified.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमाः
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं वाक्यं मधुरमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve pitāmahapurogamāḥ
viśvāmitraṁ mahātmānaṁ vākyaṁ madhuramabruvan

translations.english: Even should he desires the dominion of the celestial regions, do you grant him his wish.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मर्षे स्वागतं तेऽस्तु तपसा स्म सुतोषिताः
ब्राह्मण्यं तपसोग्रेण प्राप्तवानसि कौशिक
verses.transliteration:
brahmarṣe svāgataṁ te'stu tapasā sma sutoṣitāḥ
brāhmaṇyaṁ tapasogreṇa prāptavānasi kauśika

translations.english: Then the celestials with Pitamaha at their head, addressed the high-souled Viśvāmitra in sweet-words, saying, "Welcome, O Brahmarşi! Well pleased have we been with your penances. And, O son of Kusika, in consideration of your fiery asceticism, you have obtained Brāhmaṇahood.'

verses.sanskrit:
दीर्घमायुश्च ते ब्रह्मन्ददामि समरुद्गणः
स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
dīrghamāyuśca te brahmandadāmi samarudgaṇaḥ
svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṁ te gaccha saumya yathāsukham

translations.english: O Brāhmaṇa, I will in company with the Maruts confer on you long life. hail to you! Do you accept this, good betide you. Go you, O gentle ascetic, bowing down to the celestials, said in delight,

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रवेदविदां श्रेष्ठो ब्रह्मवेदविदामपि
ब्रह्मपुत्रो वसिष्ठो मामेवं वदतु देवताः
यद्ययं परमः कामः कृतो यान्तु सुरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
kṣatravedavidāṁ śreṣṭho brahmavedavidāmapi
brahmaputro vasiṣṭho māmevaṁ vadatu devatāḥ
yadyayaṁ paramaḥ kāmaḥ kṛto yāntu surarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: If Brāhmaṇa-hood has really been obtained by e together with length of days, let Omkâra and Vaşaļkāra and the Vedas crown me; and let, you gods, that foremost of those versed in Kștra Veda ad well as of those cognizant of the Brahmaveda, even Brahma's son, Vasistha, recognise me. Having granted this prime desire of mine, do you go away, you gods.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रसादितो देवैर्वसिष्ठो जपतां वरः
सख्यं चकार ब्रह्मर्षिरेवमस्त्विति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prasādito devairvasiṣṭho japatāṁ varaḥ
sakhyaṁ cakāra brahmarṣirevamastviti cābravīt

translations.english: Then pacified by the celestials, that best of reciters, the Brahmarsi Vasistha, made friends (with Viśvāmitra), saying,

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मर्षित्वं न संदेहः सर्वं संपत्स्यते तव
इत्युक्त्वा देवताश्चापि सर्वा जग्मुर्यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
brahmarṣitvaṁ na saṁdehaḥ sarvaṁ saṁpatsyate tava
ityuktvā devatāścāpi sarvā jagmuryathāgatam

translations.english: 'So be it.' You are a Brahmarsi. There is no doubt about this. And everything has been compassed in your behalf, having said this, the deities went to their respective regions.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रोऽपि धर्मात्मा लब्ध्वा ब्राह्मण्यमुत्तमम्
पूजयामास ब्रह्मर्षिं वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro'pi dharmātmā labdhvā brāhmaṇyamuttamam
pūjayāmāsa brahmarṣiṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ japatāṁ varam

translations.english: And that Brahmarși, the righteous Viśvāmitra also, having attained excellent Brāhmaṇa-hood, paid his homage to that best of reciters, Vasistha.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतकामो महीं सर्वां चचार तपसि स्थितः
एवं त्वनेन ब्राह्मण्यं प्राप्तं राम महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
kṛtakāmo mahīṁ sarvāṁ cacāra tapasi sthitaḥ
evaṁ tvanena brāhmaṇyaṁ prāptaṁ rāma mahātmanā

translations.english: And, having secured his end, began to range the entire world, staying in asceticism. In this wise, O Rāma, was Brāhmanya actually obtained by the high-souled one.

verses.sanskrit:
एष राम मुनिश्रेष्ठ एष विग्रहवांस्तपः
एष धर्मः परो नित्यं वीर्यस्यैष परायणम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa rāma muniśreṣṭha eṣa vigrahavāṁstapaḥ
eṣa dharmaḥ paro nityaṁ vīryasyaiṣa parāyaṇam

translations.english: This, O Rāma, is the foremost of ascetics, this one is Asceticism incarnate. This one ever abide by duty; and he is the stay of ascetic energy.

verses.sanskrit:
शतानन्दवचः श्रुत्वा रामलक्ष्मणसंनिधौ
जनकः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच कुशिकात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
śatānandavacaḥ śrutvā rāmalakṣmaṇasaṁnidhau
janakaḥ prāñjalirvākyamuvāca kuśikātmajam

translations.english: Having said this, that best of regenerate persons paused. Hearing Satānanda's narration delivered in the presence of Rāma and Laks maņa, Janaka with clasped hands addressed the son of Kusika.

verses.sanskrit:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुंगव
यज्ञं काकुत्स्थ सहितः प्राप्तवानसि धार्मिक
verses.transliteration:
dhanyo'smyanugṛhīto'smi yasya me munipuṁgava
yajñaṁ kākutstha sahitaḥ prāptavānasi dhārmika

translations.english: Blessed and beholden am I, that you, O Kausika, accompanied with Kākutstha, hast arrived at my sacrifice, O puissant anchorite. Purified am I, O Brāhmaṇa, by your very sight.

verses.sanskrit:
विस्तरेण च ते ब्रह्मन्कीर्त्यमानं महत्तपः
श्रुतं मया महातेजो रामेण च महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
vistareṇa ca te brahmankīrtyamānaṁ mahattapaḥ
śrutaṁ mayā mahātejo rāmeṇa ca mahātmanā

translations.english: O mighty Muni. And from your sight have I received various qualities. O Brāhmaṇa, your mighty austerities have been related in detail; and myself as well as he high-souled Rāma have listened to the narration relative to your formidable ascetic energy; and the assembled courtiers have heard of your various perfections.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमेयं तपस्तुभ्यमप्रमेयं च ते बलम्
अप्रमेया गुणाश्चैव नित्यं ते कुशिकात्मज
verses.transliteration:
aprameyaṁ tapastubhyamaprameyaṁ ca te balam
aprameyā guṇāścaiva nityaṁ te kuśikātmaja

translations.english: Immeasurable is your asceticism; and ever immeasurable your power; and immeasurable your qualities,

verses.sanskrit:
तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे विभो
कर्मकालो मुनिश्रेष्ठ लम्बते रविमण्डलम्
verses.transliteration:
tṛptirāścaryabhūtānāṁ kathānāṁ nāsti me vibho
karmakālo muniśreṣṭha lambate ravimaṇḍalam

translations.english: O Kusika's son. I never, O lord, am tired of listening to that wonderful narration. Now, O foremost of ascetics, the hour for performing the daily devotions has arrived, and the solar disc hangs aslope.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वः प्रभाते महातेजो द्रष्टुमर्हसि मां पुनः
स्वागतं तपसां श्रेष्ठ मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
śvaḥ prabhāte mahātejo draṣṭumarhasi māṁ punaḥ
svāgataṁ tapasāṁ śreṣṭha māmanujñātumarhasi

translations.english: To-morrow morning, O highly energetic one, you will see me again. Welcome, best of reciters. It behove you to favour me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठं वैदेहो मिथिलाधिपः
प्रदक्षिणं चकाराशु सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā muniśreṣṭhaṁ vaideho mithilādhipaḥ
pradakṣiṇaṁ cakārāśu sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted, Mithila's lord, Vaideha, in company with his priests and friends, went round that foremost of ascetics,

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रोऽपि धर्मात्मा सहरामः सलक्ष्मणः
स्वं वाटमभिचक्राम पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro'pi dharmātmā saharāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
svaṁ vāṭamabhicakrāma pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ

translations.english: And the righteous Viśvāmitra also together with Rāma and Lakşmaņa, having been honoured by the high-souled ones, took up their quarters there.

verses.sanskrit:
तमर्चयित्वा धर्मात्मा शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा
राघवौ च महात्मानौ तदा वाक्यमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tamarcayitvā dharmātmā śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
rāghavau ca mahātmānau tadā vākyamuvāca ha

translations.english: The next morning, which happened to be bright, the lord of men, having performed his daily devotions, welcomed Viśvāmitra and Rāghava. And having, in accordance with the scriptures, paid homage to the former as well as the two high-souled Rāghavas, that virtuous one said,

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्स्वागतं तेऽस्तु किं करोमि तवानघ
भवानाज्ञापयतु मामाज्ञाप्यो भवता ह्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavansvāgataṁ te'stu kiṁ karomi tavānagha
bhavānājñāpayatu māmājñāpyo bhavatā hyaham

translations.english: Hail, O worshipful sir! What shall I do to you, O sinless one? Do you command. Surely, I deserve to be commanded by you.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा जनकेन महात्मना
प्रत्युवाच मुनिर्वीरं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ sa dharmātmā janakena mahātmanā
pratyuvāca munirvīraṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the high-souled Janaka, that first of ascetics endowed with a righteous soul, well versed in speech, answered,

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रौ दशरथस्येमौ क्षत्रियौ लोकविश्रुतौ
द्रष्टुकामौ धनुः श्रेष्ठं यदेतत्त्वयि तिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
putrau daśarathasyemau kṣatriyau lokaviśrutau
draṣṭukāmau dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṁ yadetattvayi tiṣṭhati

translations.english: These sons of Dasaratha-Ksatriyas, famed among men, are eager to behold than best of bows.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्दर्शय भद्रं ते कृतकामौ नृपात्मजौ
दर्शनादस्य धनुषो यथेष्टं प्रतियास्यतः
verses.transliteration:
etaddarśaya bhadraṁ te kṛtakāmau nṛpātmajau
darśanādasya dhanuṣo yatheṣṭaṁ pratiyāsyataḥ

translations.english: If it be with you, do you show it to them, may it be well with you! having obtained a sight of that bow, the king's sons, their desires crowned with success, will success, will return as they list.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु जनकः प्रत्युवाच महामुनिम्
श्रूयतामस्य धनुषो यदर्थमिह तिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu janakaḥ pratyuvāca mahāmunim
śrūyatāmasya dhanuṣo yadarthamiha tiṣṭhati

translations.english: Thus accosted, Janaka replied to the mighty Muni, saying, Lisen to why the bow lie here.

verses.sanskrit:
देवरात इति ख्यातो निमेः षष्ठो महीपतिः
न्यासोऽयं तस्य भगवन्हस्ते दत्तो महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
devarāta iti khyāto nimeḥ ṣaṣṭho mahīpatiḥ
nyāso'yaṁ tasya bhagavanhaste datto mahātmanā

translations.english: There was a king known by the name of Devarata. He was the elder brother of Nimi. And, Oworshipful one, this bow was consigned to the hands of that high-souled one, this bow was consigned to the hands of that high-souled one as a trust.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्माद्भागार्थिनो भागान्नाकल्पयत मे सुराः
वराङ्गानि महार्हाणि धनुषा शातयामि वः
verses.transliteration:
yasmādbhāgārthino bhāgānnākalpayata me surāḥ
varāṅgāni mahārhāṇi dhanuṣā śātayāmi vaḥ

translations.english: Formerly with the view of destroying Dakşa's sacrifice, the puissant (Śiva), drawing this bow, sportively spoke to the celestials in ire, saying, 'Since, you gods, you deny me the shares (of this sacrifice), which I lay claim to, I will with my bow even sever those heads of yours.'

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विमनसः सर्वे देवा वै मुनिपुंगव
प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं तेषां प्रीतोऽभवद्भवः
verses.transliteration:
tato vimanasaḥ sarve devā vai munipuṁgava
prasādayanti deveśaṁ teṣāṁ prīto'bhavadbhavaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, O powerful ascetic, with agitated hearts, the deities fell to propitiating that lord of the celestials, and Bhava was pleased with them.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेतद्देवदेवस्य धनूरत्नं महात्मनः
न्यासभूतं तदा न्यस्तमस्माकं पूर्वके विभो
verses.transliteration:
tadetaddevadevasya dhanūratnaṁ mahātmanaḥ
nyāsabhūtaṁ tadā nyastamasmākaṁ pūrvake vibho

translations.english: And well-pleased with them, he conferred this upon those high-souled ones. And even this is that jewel of a bow belonging to the high-souled god of gods, and which was ultimately, O lord, consigned as a trust to our ancestor.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ मे कृषतः क्षेत्रं लाङ्गलादुत्थिता मम
क्षेत्रं शोधयता लब्ध्वा नाम्ना सीतेति विश्रुता
verses.transliteration:
atha me kṛṣataḥ kṣetraṁ lāṅgalādutthitā mama
kṣetraṁ śodhayatā labdhvā nāmnā sīteti viśrutā

translations.english: And as I was ploughing the mead, arose a damsel, and as I obtained her while hallowing the field (for sacrifice), she has come to be known by the name of Sītā. And arising from the earth, she grew as my daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां जिज्ञासमानानां वीर्यं धनुरुपाहृतम्
न शेकुर्ग्रहणे तस्य धनुषस्तोलनेऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ jijñāsamānānāṁ vīryaṁ dhanurupāhṛtam
na śekurgrahaṇe tasya dhanuṣastolane'pi vā

translations.english: And on their being curious (as to the bow), I showed it to them; but they could neither hold nor wield it.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां वीर्यवतां वीर्यमल्पं ज्ञात्वा महामुने
प्रत्याख्याता नृपतयस्तन्निबोध तपोधन
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vīryavatāṁ vīryamalpaṁ jñātvā mahāmune
pratyākhyātā nṛpatayastannibodha tapodhana

translations.english: And, O mighty Muni, finding those powerful kings to be but endowed with small prowess, I passed them by. Hear what then befell, O you of ascetic wealth. Then, O powerful anchorite, in high ire, the kings, doubtful as to their strength in stringing the bow, laid siege to Mithila. And those potent princes, conceiving themselves as frustrated by me, began to harass the city of Mithila, waxing wondrous wroth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे क्षयं यातानि सर्वशः
साधनानि मुनिरेष्ठ ततोऽहं भृशदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁvatsare pūrṇe kṣayaṁ yātāni sarvaśaḥ
sādhanāni munireṣṭha tato'haṁ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: And when a year had been completed, my defensive resources were entirely exhausted, and at this, I was exceedingly aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देवगणान्सर्वांस्तपसाहं प्रसादयम्
ददुश्च परमप्रीताश्चतुरङ्गबलं सुराः
verses.transliteration:
tato devagaṇānsarvāṁstapasāhaṁ prasādayam
daduśca paramaprītāścaturaṅgabalaṁ surāḥ

translations.english: Then I sought to propitiate the deities; and well-pleased, the celestials granted me a Caturanga army.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भग्ना नृपतयो हन्यमाना दिशो ययुः
अवीर्या वीर्यसंदिग्धा सामात्याः पापकारिणः
verses.transliteration:
tato bhagnā nṛpatayo hanyamānā diśo yayuḥ
avīryā vīryasaṁdigdhā sāmātyāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ

translations.english: At length those wicked kings, meeting with slaughter, broke and fled in all directions, together with their adherents, bereft of vigour, and confidence in their strength.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेतन्मुनिशार्दूल धनुः परमभास्वरम्
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि दर्शयिष्यामि सुव्रत
verses.transliteration:
tadetanmuniśārdūla dhanuḥ paramabhāsvaram
rāmalakṣmaṇayoścāpi darśayiṣyāmi suvrata

translations.english: And, O puissant ascetic, this highly effulgent bow will I show to Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यस्य धनुषो रामः कुर्यादारोपणं मुने
सुतामयोनिजां सीतां दद्यां दाशरथेरहम्
verses.transliteration:
yadyasya dhanuṣo rāmaḥ kuryādāropaṇaṁ mune
sutāmayonijāṁ sītāṁ dadyāṁ dāśaratheraham

translations.english: O you of excellent vows. And, if, Ascetic, Rāma succeeds in fixing string to it, I will confer upon Daſaratha's son my daughter unsprung from the usual source. Sītā,

verses.sanskrit:
जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
धनुर्दर्शय रामाय इति होवाच पार्थिवम्
verses.transliteration:
janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
dhanurdarśaya rāmāya iti hovāca pārthivam

translations.english: Hearing Janaka's words, the mighty Muni Viśvāmitra said to the king, Do you show the bow to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स राजा जनकः सचिवान्व्यादिदेश ह
धनुरानीयतां दिव्यं गन्धमाल्यविभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa rājā janakaḥ sacivānvyādideśa ha
dhanurānīyatāṁ divyaṁ gandhamālyavibhūṣitam

translations.english: Thereupon the king Janaka commanded his ministers, saying, Do you bring the wonderful bow furnished with unguents and garlands.

verses.sanskrit:
जनकेन समादिष्ठाः सचिवाः प्राविशन्पुरीम्
तद्धनुः पुरतः कृत्वा निर्जग्मुः पार्थिवाज्ञया
verses.transliteration:
janakena samādiṣṭhāḥ sacivāḥ prāviśanpurīm
taddhanuḥ purataḥ kṛtvā nirjagmuḥ pārthivājñayā

translations.english: Commanded by Janaka, the ministers entered the city; and placing the bow in their front, those, endowed with immeasurable energy, came out.

verses.sanskrit:
नृपां शतानि पञ्चाशद्व्यायतानां महात्मनाम्
मञ्जूषामष्टचक्रां तां समूहुस्ते कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
nṛpāṁ śatāni pañcāśadvyāyatānāṁ mahātmanām
mañjūṣāmaṣṭacakrāṁ tāṁ samūhuste kathaṁcana

translations.english: And deposited in a case on a cart borne upon eight wheels, it was with difficulty drawn along by five thousand stalwart persons of welldeveloped frames.

verses.sanskrit:
तामादाय तु मञ्जूषामायतीं यत्र तद्धनुः
सुरोपमं ते जनकमूचुर्नृपतिमन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
tāmādāya tu mañjūṣāmāyatīṁ yatra taddhanuḥ
suropamaṁ te janakamūcurnṛpatimantriṇaḥ

translations.english: And having brought that bow plaited with iron, placed in its case, the royal counsellors spoke to Janaka resembling an immortal, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
इदं धनुर्वरं राजन्पूजितं सर्वराजभिः
मिथिलाधिप राजेन्द्र दर्शनीयं यदीच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ dhanurvaraṁ rājanpūjitaṁ sarvarājabhiḥ
mithilādhipa rājendra darśanīyaṁ yadīcchasi

translations.english: Here is the best of bow, O king, worshipped of all sovereigns. O foremost of kings, O lord of Mithilā, if it please you, behold the same.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां नृपो वचः श्रुत्वा कृताञ्जलिरभाषत
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं तौ चोभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ nṛpo vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata
viśvāmitraṁ mahātmānaṁ tau cobhau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Hearing their speech, the king with ciasped palms said to the high-souled Viśvāmitra as well as Rāma and Laksmana,

verses.sanskrit:
इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मञ्जनकैरभिपूजितम्
राजभिश्च महावीर्यैरशक्यं पूरितुं तदा
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ dhanurvaraṁ brahmañjanakairabhipūjitam
rājabhiśca mahāvīryairaśakyaṁ pūrituṁ tadā

translations.english: This best of bows, O Brāhmaṇa, has always been worshipped by the Janakas: as also by mighty kings incapable of wielding and stringing it.)

verses.sanskrit:
क्व गतिर्मानुषाणां च धनुषोऽस्य प्रपूरणे
आरोपणे समायोगे वेपने तोलनेऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
kva gatirmānuṣāṇāṁ ca dhanuṣo'sya prapūraṇe
āropaṇe samāyoge vepane tolane'pi vā

translations.english: And neither the celestials, nor the Asuras, nor the Rākşasas, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Yakş as, nor the Kinnaras, nor the mighty Uragas, how shall men fare have succeeded in stringing or stretching it, or fixing the arrow to it, or pulling its string, or wielding it.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेतद्धनुषां श्रेष्ठमानीतं मुनिपुंगव
दर्शयैतन्महाभाग अनयो राजपुत्रयोः
verses.transliteration:
tadetaddhanuṣāṁ śreṣṭhamānītaṁ munipuṁgava
darśayaitanmahābhāga anayo rājaputrayoḥ

translations.english: This foremost of bows has been brought here, O chief of ascetics. Do you, O exalted one, show it to these sons of the king.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा श्रुत्वा जनकभाषितम्
वत्स राम धनुः पश्य इति राघवमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitrastu dharmātmā śrutvā janakabhāṣitam
vatsa rāma dhanuḥ paśya iti rāghavamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Janaka's words, the righteous Viśvāmitra said to Rāghava, O Rāma, do you, my child, behold the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
महर्षेर्वचनाद्रामो यत्र तिष्ठति तद्धनुः
मञ्जूषां तामपावृत्य दृष्ट्वा धनुरथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
maharṣervacanādrāmo yatra tiṣṭhati taddhanuḥ
mañjūṣāṁ tāmapāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā dhanurathābravīt

translations.english: At the words of the Maharsi, Rama, opening the case, took a sight of the bow, and said,

verses.sanskrit:
इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मन्संस्पृशामीह पाणिना
यत्नवांश्च भविष्यामि तोलने पूरणेऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ dhanurvaraṁ brahmansaṁspṛśāmīha pāṇinā
yatnavāṁśca bhaviṣyāmi tolane pūraṇe'pi vā

translations.english: This divine bow will I touch with my hand, and shall I also strive to wield and draw it?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्याश्वस्ते जने तस्मिन्राजा विगतसाध्वसः
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
pratyāśvaste jane tasminrājā vigatasādhvasaḥ
uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṁ vākyajño munipuṁgavam

translations.english: On the people being reassured, the king conversant with speech, his apprehension removed, with folded hands addressed that puissant ascetic, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्दृष्टवीर्यो मे रामो दशरथात्मजः
अत्यद्भुतमचिन्त्यं च अतर्कितमिदं मया
verses.transliteration:
bhagavandṛṣṭavīryo me rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
atyadbhutamacintyaṁ ca atarkitamidaṁ mayā

translations.english: O worshipful one, I have beheld the prowess of Dasaratha's son. This is verily wonderful and inconceivable; and I did not think this was possible.

verses.sanskrit:
जनकानां कुले कीर्तिमाहरिष्यति मे सुता
सीता भर्तारमासाद्य रामं दशरथात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
janakānāṁ kule kīrtimāhariṣyati me sutā
sītā bhartāramāsādya rāmaṁ daśarathātmajam

translations.english: My daughter, Sītā, being united with her lord, Dasaratha's son, Rama, will shed lustre on Janaka's line.

verses.sanskrit:
मम सत्या प्रतिज्ञा च वीर्यशुल्केति कौशिक
सीता प्राणैर्बहुमता देया रामाय मे सुता
verses.transliteration:
mama satyā pratijñā ca vīryaśulketi kauśika
sītā prāṇairbahumatā deyā rāmāya me sutā

translations.english: My promise viz., that I will confer Sītā upon him that will bend the bow, has been fulfilled, O son of Kusika. And this Sītā, this my daughter, dearer to me than life will I confer upon Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
राजानं प्रश्रितैर्वाक्यैरानयन्तु पुरं मम
प्रदानं वीर्यशुल्कायाः कथयन्तु च सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
rājānaṁ praśritairvākyairānayantu puraṁ mama
pradānaṁ vīryaśulkāyāḥ kathayantu ca sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: O Brāhmaṇa, by your permission let my counsellors speedily post hence, O Kausika, to Ayodhyā, in cars; and with humble speech bring the king to my capital. And let them communicate to him all about the bestowal of Sītå upon Răma, in consequence of his having bent the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
मुनिगुप्तौ च काकुत्स्थौ कथयन्तु नृपाय वै
प्रीयमाणं तु राजानमानयन्तु सुशीघ्रगाः
verses.transliteration:
muniguptau ca kākutsthau kathayantu nṛpāya vai
prīyamāṇaṁ tu rājānamānayantu suśīghragāḥ

translations.english: Let them acquaint the monarch with the welfare of the Kākutsthas protected by the ascetic; and let them, speedily posting hence, bring the delighted king.

verses.sanskrit:
कौशिकश्च तथेत्याह राजा चाभाष्य मन्त्रिणः
अयोध्यां प्रेषयामास धर्मात्मा कृतशासनात्
verses.transliteration:
kauśikaśca tathetyāha rājā cābhāṣya mantriṇaḥ
ayodhyāṁ preṣayāmāsa dharmātmā kṛtaśāsanāt

translations.english: And thereupon Kusika's son said,-So be it. And the righteous king, summoning his counsellors, despatched them to Ayodhyā with his letter, to communicate all duly to the king, and bring him thither.

verses.sanskrit:
जनकेन समादिष्टा दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः
त्रिरात्रमुषित्वा मार्गे तेऽयोध्यां प्राविशन्पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
janakena samādiṣṭā dūtāste klāntavāhanāḥ
trirātramuṣitvā mārge te'yodhyāṁ prāviśanpurīm

translations.english: Thus commissioned by Janaka, the envoys, having spent three nights on the way, entered the city of Ayodhyā, with their conveyances afflicted with fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
ते राजवचनाद्दूता राजवेश्मप्रवेशिताः
ददृशुर्देवसंकाशं वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्
verses.transliteration:
te rājavacanāddūtā rājaveśmapraveśitāḥ
dadṛśurdevasaṁkāśaṁ vṛddhaṁ daśarathaṁ nṛpam

translations.english: In accordance with the royal commission, entering the king's residence, they saw the aged king Dasaratha, resembling a celestial.

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्ट्वा कुशलमव्यग्रं वैदेहो मिथिलाधिपः
कौशिकानुमते वाक्यं भवन्तमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭvā kuśalamavyagraṁ vaideho mithilādhipaḥ
kauśikānumate vākyaṁ bhavantamidamabravīt

translations.english: After having enquired after your complete welfare, Mithila's lord, Vaideha, by permission of Kausika, addresses you thus,

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञा विदिता वीर्यशुल्का ममात्मजा
राजानश्च कृतामर्षा निर्वीर्या विमुखीकृताः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvaṁ pratijñā viditā vīryaśulkā mamātmajā
rājānaśca kṛtāmarṣā nirvīryā vimukhīkṛtāḥ

translations.english: You know the vow I had made formerlyviz., to confer my daughter upon him that would bend the bow,-and the kings, in consequence of their having been deprived of prowess, and being baffled, have come to entertain spite against me.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्च राजन्धनुर्दिव्यं मध्ये भग्नं महात्मना
रामेण हि महाराज महत्यां जनसंसदि
verses.transliteration:
tacca rājandhanurdivyaṁ madhye bhagnaṁ mahātmanā
rāmeṇa hi mahārāja mahatyāṁ janasaṁsadi

translations.english: And that daughter of mine, O king, has been won by your son, arrived one, that divine, jewelled bow has been snapped in the middle by the high-souled Rāma in the midst of a large assembly.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मै देया मया सीता वीर्यशुल्का महात्मने
प्रतिज्ञां तर्तुमिच्छामि तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
asmai deyā mayā sītā vīryaśulkā mahātmane
pratijñāṁ tartumicchāmi tadanujñātumarhasi

translations.english: Upon that high-souled one should I confer Sītā, having prowess assigned for her dower. And in this wise will I free myself from my vow; and this you should permit. 10

verses.sanskrit:
सोपाध्यायो महाराज पुरोहितपुरस्कृतः
शीघ्रमागच्छ भद्रं ते द्रष्टुमर्हसि राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
sopādhyāyo mahārāja purohitapuraskṛtaḥ
śīghramāgaccha bhadraṁ te draṣṭumarhasi rāghavau

translations.english: O mighty king, do you, good betide you, come speedily headed by your priests. It behove you to see the Rāghavas;

verses.sanskrit:
प्रीतिं च मम राजेन्द्र निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि
पुत्रयोरुभयोरेव प्रीतिं त्वमपि लप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
prītiṁ ca mama rājendra nirvartayitumarhasi
putrayorubhayoreva prītiṁ tvamapi lapsyase

translations.english: And, O foremost of kings, to see me delivered from this vow. And do you attain the joy incident to the nuptials of both your sons,

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विदेहाधिपतिर्मधुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञातः शतानन्दमते स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ videhādhipatirmadhuraṁ vākyamabravīt
viśvāmitrābhyanujñātaḥ śatānandamate sthitaḥ

translations.english: Thus spoke sweetly the lord of Videha, permitted by Viśvāmitra and staying by the opinions of Satānanda.'

verses.sanskrit:
दूतवाक्यं तु तच्छ्रुत्वा राजा परमहर्षितः
वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च मन्त्रिणोऽन्यांश्च सोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
dūtavākyaṁ tu tacchrutvā rājā paramaharṣitaḥ
vasiṣṭhaṁ vāmadevaṁ ca mantriṇo'nyāṁśca so'bravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of the envoys, the king, exceedingly rejoiced, addressed Vasiştha and Vamadeva, as well as his counsellors, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
गुप्तः कुशिकपुत्रेण कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा विदेहेषु वसत्यसौ
verses.transliteration:
guptaḥ kuśikaputreṇa kausalyānandavardhanaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā videheṣu vasatyasau

translations.english: Protected by Kusika's son, that exhancer of Kausalyā's joy stay in Videha in company with his brother, Laksmana.15

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टवीर्यस्तु काकुत्स्थो जनकेन महात्मना
संप्रदानं सुतायास्तु राघवे कर्तुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭavīryastu kākutstho janakena mahātmanā
saṁpradānaṁ sutāyāstu rāghave kartumicchati

translations.english: And the high-souled Janaka has witnessed the prowess of Kākutstha; and he wish to bestow his daughter upon Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि वो रोचते वृत्तं जनकस्य महात्मनः
पुरीं गच्छामहे शीघ्रं मा भूत्कालस्य पर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
yadi vo rocate vṛttaṁ janakasya mahātmanaḥ
purīṁ gacchāmahe śīghraṁ mā bhūtkālasya paryayaḥ

translations.english: If this alliance with the high-souled Janaka is relished by you, we shall speedily repair to his capital. Let there be no waste of time.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिणो बाढमित्याहुः सह सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः
सुप्रीतश्चाब्रवीद्राजा श्वो यात्रेति स मन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
mantriṇo bāḍhamityāhuḥ saha sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ
suprītaścābravīdrājā śvo yātreti sa mantriṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, the counsellors along with the Maharsis said, Excellent! And the king highly delighted, said to the counsellors, Our journey commence on the morrow.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिणस्तु नरेन्द्रस्य रात्रिं परमसत्कृताः
ऊषुः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे गुणैः सर्वैः समन्विताः
verses.transliteration:
mantriṇastu narendrasya rātriṁ paramasatkṛtāḥ
ūṣuḥ pramuditāḥ sarve guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitāḥ

translations.english: And excellently ministered to, the counsellors of that foremost of monarchs (Janaka), endowed with every excellent quality, spent that night in joy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः
राजा दशरथो हृष्टः सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato rātryāṁ vyatītāyāṁ sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
rājā daśaratho hṛṣṭaḥ sumantramidamabravīt

translations.english: Then when the night had been spent, king Dasaratha accompanied with his priests and adherents, well pleased spoke to Sumantra, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य सर्वे धनाध्यक्षा धनमादाय पुष्कलम्
व्रजन्त्वग्रे सुविहिता नानारत्नसमन्विताः
verses.transliteration:
adya sarve dhanādhyakṣā dhanamādāya puṣkalam
vrajantvagre suvihitā nānāratnasamanvitāḥ
