translations.english: To-day let the officers in charge of the treasury, taking plenty of excellent wealth, and furnished with various gems, go in advance under proper escort.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुरङ्गबलं चापि शीघ्रं निर्यातु सर्वशः
ममाज्ञासमकालं च यानयुग्यमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
caturaṅgabalaṁ cāpi śīghraṁ niryātu sarvaśaḥ
mamājñāsamakālaṁ ca yānayugyamanuttamam

translations.english: And let the fore-fold forces sally out with speed. And at my command let horses and conveyances and elegant vehicles march out

verses.sanskrit:
एते द्विजाः प्रयान्त्वग्रे स्यन्दनं योजयस्व मे
यथा कालात्ययो न स्याद्दूता हि त्वरयन्ति माम्
verses.transliteration:
ete dvijāḥ prayāntvagre syandanaṁ yojayasva me
yathā kālātyayo na syāddūtā hi tvarayanti mām

translations.english: And let Vasiştha and Vamadeva and Jābāli and Kasyapa and Mārkandeya endowed with long life and the saint Katyāyana-let these regenerate ones go forward. And do you also yoke my car. Let not the proper time pass away; for the envoys urge speed upon me.

verses.sanskrit:
वचनाच्च नरेन्द्रस्य सा सेना चतुरङ्गिणी
राजानमृषिभिः सार्धं व्रजन्तं पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात्
verses.transliteration:
vacanācca narendrasya sā senā caturaṅgiṇī
rājānamṛṣibhiḥ sārdhaṁ vrajantaṁ pṛṣṭhato'nvagāt

translations.english: At these words of the king, the four-fold forces together with the saints went in the wake of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
गत्वा चतुरहं मार्गं विदेहानभ्युपेयिवान्
राजा तु जनकः श्रीमाञ्श्रुत्वा पूजामकल्पयत्
verses.transliteration:
gatvā caturahaṁ mārgaṁ videhānabhyupeyivān
rājā tu janakaḥ śrīmāñśrutvā pūjāmakalpayat

translations.english: After having passed four days on the way, they arrived at Videha. And bearing of Dasaratha's arrival, the auspicious king Janaka experienced great delight, and having obtained the aged king Dasaratha, he honoured him duly.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो महातेजा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः
सह सर्वैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठैर्देवैरिव शतक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā prāpto mahātejā vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ
saha sarvairdvijaśreṣṭhairdevairiva śatakratuḥ

translations.english: Do you experience the joy earned by the prowess of your sons. And by luck it is that I have obtained the highly energetic and worshipful saint Vasistha accompanied by the foremost regenerate ones, like him of an hundred sacrifices, by the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या मे निर्जिता विघ्ना दिष्ट्या मे पूजितं कुलम्
राघवैः सह संबन्धाद्वीर्यश्रेष्ठैर्महात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā me nirjitā vighnā diṣṭyā me pūjitaṁ kulam
rāghavaiḥ saha saṁbandhādvīryaśreṣṭhairmahātmabhiḥ

translations.english: By luck it is that I have overcome the obstacle; by luck it is that my race has attained renown, in consequence of alliance with those endowed with prowess, the exceedingly potent Rāghavas.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वः प्रभाते नरेन्द्रेन्द्र निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि
यज्ञस्यान्ते नरश्रेष्ठ विवाहमृषिसंमतम्
verses.transliteration:
śvaḥ prabhāte narendrendra nirvartayitumarhasi
yajñasyānte naraśreṣṭha vivāhamṛṣisaṁmatam

translations.english: O lord of men, to-morrow morning after the completion of the sacrifice, do you perform the nuptials, in company with the foremost of the saints.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋषिमध्ये नराधिपः
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā ṛṣimadhye narādhipaḥ
vākyaṁ vākyavidāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca mahīpatim

translations.english: Hearing his speech in the midst of the saints, that best of those conversant with words, the lord of men, replied to the monarch, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिग्रहो दातृवशः श्रुतमेतन्मया पुरा
यथा वक्ष्यसि धर्मज्ञ तत्करिष्यामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
pratigraho dātṛvaśaḥ śrutametanmayā purā
yathā vakṣyasi dharmajña tatkariṣyāmahe vayam

translations.english: A gift should be accepted, this I heard formerly. And what you say, O you cognizant of duty, will we accomplish.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्धर्मिष्ठं यशस्यं च वचनं सत्यवादिनः
श्रुत्वा विदेहाधिपतिः परं विस्मयमागतः
verses.transliteration:
taddharmiṣṭhaṁ yaśasyaṁ ca vacanaṁ satyavādinaḥ
śrutvā videhādhipatiḥ paraṁ vismayamāgataḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words of the truthful (king), chiming in with morality and conducive to fame, the lord of Videha was filled with admiration.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सर्वे मुनिगणाः परस्परसमागमे
हर्षेण महता युक्तास्तां निशामवसन्सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sarve munigaṇāḥ parasparasamāgame
harṣeṇa mahatā yuktāstāṁ niśāmavasansukham

translations.english: Then the ascetics experiencing great delight, passed the night in each other's company.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा च राघवौ पुत्रौ निशाम्य परिहर्षितः
उवास परमप्रीतो जनकेन सुपूजितः
verses.transliteration:
rājā ca rāghavau putrau niśāmya pariharṣitaḥ
uvāsa paramaprīto janakena supūjitaḥ

translations.english: And the king, overjoyed on beholding his sons, the Rāghavas passed (the night) in exceeding delight, splendidly entertained of Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
जनकोऽपि महातेजाः क्रिया धर्मेण तत्त्ववित्
यज्ञस्य च सुताभ्यां च कृत्वा रात्रिमुवास ह
verses.transliteration:
janako'pi mahātejāḥ kriyā dharmeṇa tattvavit
yajñasya ca sutābhyāṁ ca kṛtvā rātrimuvāsa ha

translations.english: And the exceedingly energetic Janaka also, versed in men and things, having in accordance with the ordinance completed the sacrifice and performed all the preliminary rites relative to the nuptials of his daughters, reposed for the night.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रभाते जनकः कृतकर्मा महर्षिभिः
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः शतानन्दं पुरोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prabhāte janakaḥ kṛtakarmā maharṣibhiḥ
uvāca vākyaṁ vākyajñaḥ śatānandaṁ purohitam

translations.english: Then next morning Janaka skilled in speech, having in company with the Maharsis performed his daily duties, addressed the priest Satānanda, saying

verses.sanskrit:
वार्याफलकपर्यन्तां पिबन्निक्षुमतीं नदीम्
सांकाश्यां पुण्यसंकाशां विमानमिव पुष्पकम्
verses.transliteration:
vāryāphalakaparyantāṁ pibannikṣumatīṁ nadīm
sāṁkāśyāṁ puṇyasaṁkāśāṁ vimānamiva puṣpakam

translations.english: My highly energetic, puissant and eminently righteous brother known by the name of Kusadhvaja dwell in the auspicious city, Sāņkāśyā, whose ramparts are ranged round with pointed weapons, and which is laved by the river Ikşumatī, and which resembles the celestial regions or the aerial car, Pușpaka.

verses.sanskrit:
तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि यज्ञगोप्ता स मे मतः
प्रीतिं सोऽपि महातेजा इमां भोक्ता मया सह
verses.transliteration:
tamahaṁ draṣṭumicchāmi yajñagoptā sa me mataḥ
prītiṁ so'pi mahātejā imāṁ bhoktā mayā saha

translations.english: I wish to see him, and he is in charge of my sacrifice. And that highly energetic one will partake with me the joy of this occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
शासनात्तु नरेन्द्रस्य प्रययुः शीघ्रवाजिभिः
समानेतुं नरव्याघ्रं विष्णुमिन्द्राज्ञया यथा
verses.transliteration:
śāsanāttu narendrasya prayayuḥ śīghravājibhiḥ
samānetuṁ naravyāghraṁ viṣṇumindrājñayā yathā

translations.english: And commanded by the monarch, off they want, mounting on fleet coursers, with the view of bringing over that tiger among men, like Viş nu at the mandate of Indra.

verses.sanskrit: आज्ञया तु नरेन्द्रस्य आजगाम कुशध्वजः
verses.transliteration: ājñayā tu narendrasya ājagāma kuśadhvajaḥ

translations.english: And hearing the tidings conveyed by those foremost of envoys endowed with great fleetness, Kusadhvaja set out at the mandate of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श महात्मानं जनकं धर्मवत्सलम्
सोऽभिवाद्य शतानन्दं राजानं चापि धार्मिकम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa mahātmānaṁ janakaṁ dharmavatsalam
so'bhivādya śatānandaṁ rājānaṁ cāpi dhārmikam

translations.english: And on coming to Videha, he appeared before the high-souled Janaka addicted to righteousness. And saluting Satānanda as well as the eminently virtuous Janaka, he sat down on an excellent and superb seat worthy of a King.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेषयामासतुर्वीरौ मन्त्रिश्रेष्ठं सुदामनम्
गच्छ मन्त्रिपते शीघ्रमैक्ष्वाकममितप्रभम्
आत्मजैः सह दुर्धर्षमानयस्व समन्त्रिणम्
verses.transliteration:
preṣayāmāsaturvīrau mantriśreṣṭhaṁ sudāmanam
gaccha mantripate śīghramaikṣvākamamitaprabham
ātmajaiḥ saha durdharṣamānayasva samantriṇam

translations.english: Having been seated, both the heroic brothers of immeasurable splendour addressed that foremost of counsellors, Sudáman, saying, 'Go, foremost of counsellors, and speedily bring over the irrepressible Ikşvāku of immeasurable splendour along with his sons and ministers.

verses.sanskrit:
औपकार्यां स गत्वा तु रघूणां कुलवर्धनम्
ददर्श शिरसा चैनमभिवाद्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
aupakāryāṁ sa gatvā tu raghūṇāṁ kulavardhanam
dadarśa śirasā cainamabhivādyedamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon, repairing to the camp of that enhancer of the race of the Raghus, he saw Dasaratha, and saluting him with beaded head, addressed him.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्याधिपते वीर वैदेहो मिथिलाधिपः
स त्वां द्रष्टुं व्यवसितः सोपाध्यायपुरोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
ayodhyādhipate vīra vaideho mithilādhipaḥ
sa tvāṁ draṣṭuṁ vyavasitaḥ sopādhyāyapurohitam

translations.english: O heroic lord of Ayodhyā, Vaideha, the master of Mithila, has wished to see you along with your priests.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिश्रेष्ठवचः श्रुत्वा राजा सर्षिगणस्तदा
सबन्धुरगमत्तत्र जनको यत्र वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
mantriśreṣṭhavacaḥ śrutvā rājā sarṣigaṇastadā
sabandhuragamattatra janako yatra vartate

translations.english: Hearing the words of that best of counsellors, the king accompanied by the saints and his adherents, came to Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा मन्त्रिसहितः सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठो वैदेहमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā mantrisahitaḥ sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
vākyaṁ vākyavidāṁ śreṣṭho vaidehamidamabravīt

translations.english: And in company with his counsellors with his counsellors and priests and adherents, the king, foremost of those skilled in speech, spoke to Vaideha.

verses.sanskrit:
विदितं ते महाराज इक्ष्वाकुकुलदैवतम्
वक्ता सर्वेषु कृत्येषु वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः
verses.transliteration:
viditaṁ te mahārāja ikṣvākukuladaivatam
vaktā sarveṣu kṛtyeṣu vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ

translations.english: O mighty king, you know that the worshipful saint Vasiştha is the spiritual guide of our race; and in every ceremony that we undertake, he it is who serves the function of a spokesman.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञातः सह सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः
एष वक्ष्यति धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठो मे यथाक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitrābhyanujñātaḥ saha sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ
eṣa vakṣyati dharmātmā vasiṣṭho me yathākramam

translations.english: And permitted by Viśvāmitra along with all the Maharsis, even this one of a righteous soul will relate my genealogy.

verses.sanskrit:
तूष्णींभूते दशरथे वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वैदेहं सपुरोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
tūṣṇīṁbhūte daśarathe vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ
uvāca vākyaṁ vākyajño vaidehaṁ sapurohitam

translations.english: And on Dasaratha resuming silence, the worshipful saint Vasistha, versed in speech, spoke to Vaideha in company with his priests, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्ययः
तस्मान्मरीचिः संजज्ञे मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
avyaktaprabhavo brahmā śāśvato nitya avyayaḥ
tasmānmarīciḥ saṁjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: The perpetual, everlasting, and undeteriorating Brahmā sprang from the Unmanifest (Brahmā). From him sprang Marīci; and Kasyapa is son to Marīci. And from Kaśyapa sprung Vivasvat; and Manu is son to Vivasvat.

verses.sanskrit:
तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम्
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुतः श्रीमान्विकुक्षिरुदपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
tamikṣvākumayodhyāyāṁ rājānaṁ viddhi pūrvakam
ikṣvākostu sutaḥ śrīmānvikukṣirudapadyata

translations.english: This Manu is otherwise called Prajäpati; and Ikşvāku is Manu's son. And this Ikşvāku you must understand, was the first king of Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजा बाणः पुत्रः प्रतापवान्
बाणस्य तु महातेजा अनरण्यः प्रतापवान्
verses.transliteration:
vikukṣestu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān
bāṇasya tu mahātejā anaraṇyaḥ pratāpavān

translations.english: And Vikuksi's son was the exceedingly energetic and powerful Bāņa. And Bāna's son was the highly energetic and powerful Anaranya.

verses.sanskrit:
अनरण्यात्पृथुर्जज्ञे त्रिशङ्कुस्तु पृथोः सुतः
त्रिशङ्कोरभवत्पुत्रो धुन्धुमारो महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
anaraṇyātpṛthurjajñe triśaṅkustu pṛthoḥ sutaḥ
triśaṅkorabhavatputro dhundhumāro mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: From Anaranya sprang Prithu; and from Prithu, Trisanku. And Trisanku's son was the highly famous Dhundhumāra.

verses.sanskrit:
धुन्धुमारान्महातेजा युवनाश्वो महारथः
युवनाश्वसुतः श्रीमान्मान्धाता पृथिवीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
dhundhumārānmahātejā yuvanāśvo mahārathaḥ
yuvanāśvasutaḥ śrīmānmāndhātā pṛthivīpatiḥ

translations.english: And from Dhundhumāra sprung the Mahāratha, Yuvanāśva. And from Yuvanāśva sprung Māndhātā, lord of earth.

verses.sanskrit:
मान्धातुस्तु सुतः श्रीमान्सुसंधिरुदपद्यत
सुसंधेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसंधिः प्रसेनजित्
verses.transliteration:
māndhātustu sutaḥ śrīmānsusaṁdhirudapadyata
susaṁdherapi putrau dvau dhruvasaṁdhiḥ prasenajit

translations.english: And Māndhātā's son was the graceful Susandhi. And Susandhi's two sons were Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit.

verses.sanskrit:
यशस्वी ध्रुवसंधेस्तु भरतो नाम नामतः
भरतात्तु महातेजा असितो नाम जायत
verses.transliteration:
yaśasvī dhruvasaṁdhestu bharato nāma nāmataḥ
bharatāttu mahātejā asito nāma jāyata

translations.english: And from Dhruvasandhi sprung the famous Bharata. And from Bharata sprung Asita; to fight whom were born as hostile kings, those heroes, the Haihayas, the Talajanghas, and the Sasabindus.

verses.sanskrit:
सह तेन गरेणैव जातः स सगरोऽभवत्
सगरस्यासमञ्जस्तु असमञ्जादथांशुमान्
verses.transliteration:
saha tena gareṇaiva jātaḥ sa sagaro'bhavat
sagarasyāsamañjastu asamañjādathāṁśumān

translations.english: And since intending to destroy her foetus she that was co-wife with her had administered poison to her, Sagara* was born together with the poison. *Gara-poison. Sagara means, with poison, i.e. here, one born with poison.

verses.sanskrit:
दिलीपोंऽशुमतः पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथः
भगीरथात्ककुत्स्थश्च ककुत्स्थस्य रघुस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
dilīpoṁ'śumataḥ putro dilīpasya bhagīrathaḥ
bhagīrathātkakutsthaśca kakutsthasya raghustathā

translations.english: And Sagara's son was Asamanja, and Ansumat. And Dilīpa was son to Ansumat, and Bhagiratha to Dilīpa.

verses.sanskrit:
रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्धः पुरुषादकः
कल्माषपादो ह्यभवत्तस्माज्जातस्तु शङ्खणः
verses.transliteration:
raghostu putrastejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
kalmāṣapādo hyabhavattasmājjātastu śaṅkhaṇaḥ

translations.english: And from Bhagiratha sprang Kākutstha, and from Kākutstha, Raghu. And Raghu's son was the puissant Pravşdha, feeding on human flesh.

verses.sanskrit:
सुदर्शनः शङ्खणस्य अग्निवर्णः सुदर्शनात्
शीघ्रगस्त्वग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगस्य मरुः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
sudarśanaḥ śaṅkhaṇasya agnivarṇaḥ sudarśanāt
śīghragastvagnivarṇasya śīghragasya maruḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: And he came finally to be known by the name of Kalmāşapāda.* And from him sprung Śarkhana. And Sudarśana was Sankhana's and Agnivarna was Sudaśana's son. He incurred Vasiştha's curse, and was turned into a Rākşasa. He took up water, intending to clear scores with Vasistha; but at the request of his wife, desisted, pouring down the water at his own feet. Hence the name of Kalmāşapāda.

verses.sanskrit:
मरोः प्रशुश्रुकस्त्वासीदम्बरीषः प्रशुश्रुकात्
अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोऽभून्नहुषः पृथिवीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
maroḥ praśuśrukastvāsīdambarīṣaḥ praśuśrukāt
ambarīṣasya putro'bhūnnahuṣaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ

translations.english: Śīghraga was Agnivarņa’s, and Maru was Śīghraga's son. And Maru's son was Prasuśruka, and from Praśuśruka sprung Ambarīşa.

verses.sanskrit:
नहुषस्य ययातिस्तु नाभागस्तु ययातिजः
नाभागस्य बभूवाज अजाद्दशरथोऽभवत्
तस्माद्दशरथाज्जातौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
nahuṣasya yayātistu nābhāgastu yayātijaḥ
nābhāgasya babhūvāja ajāddaśaratho'bhavat
tasmāddaśarathājjātau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Ambarisa's son was Nahusa, lord of earth. And Nahusa's son was Yayāti, was Nābhāga. And Nābhāga's son was Aja, and from Aja sprung Dasaratha. And from this Dasaratha have come the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
आदिवंशविशुद्धानां राज्ञां परमधर्मिणाम्
इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातानां वीराणां सत्यवादिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
ādivaṁśaviśuddhānāṁ rājñāṁ paramadharmiṇām
ikṣvākukulajātānāṁ vīrāṇāṁ satyavādinām

translations.english: It is in the interests of Rāma and Lakşmaņa belonging to the heroic and truthful and pious sovereigns sprung in the Ikşvāku line, and possessing purity of race even from the time of their founder, that, Oking, we solicit the hands of your daughters. And, O foremost of men, it be-hove you to confer like brides upon like bridegrooms.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं जनकः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः
श्रोतुमर्हसि भद्रं ते कुलं नः कीर्तितं परम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ janakaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
śrotumarhasi bhadraṁ te kulaṁ naḥ kīrtitaṁ param

translations.english: When Vasiştha had spoken thus, Janaka with clasped hands answered to him, saying,-It behove you to listen to our genealogy as related by myself. In the matter of disposal of daughters, O foremost of anchorets, one's own line should be described by one boasting of a noble ancestry. Do you then, O mighty-minded one, listen to the same.

verses.sanskrit:
राजाभूत्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः स्वेन कर्मणा
निमिः परमधर्मात्मा सर्वसत्त्ववतां वरः
verses.transliteration:
rājābhūttriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ svena karmaṇā
nimiḥ paramadharmātmā sarvasattvavatāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: There was a king famed over the three worlds by his own acts, Nimi-eminently picus and the foremost of those endowed with strength.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पुत्रो मिथिर्नाम जनको मिथिपुत्रकः
प्रथमो जनको नाम जनकादप्युदावसुः
verses.transliteration:
tasya putro mithirnāma janako mithiputrakaḥ
prathamo janako nāma janakādapyudāvasuḥ

translations.english: His son was named Mithi, and Mithi's son was Janaka. And from this king Janaka have we son was derived that word as applied to every one of us. And from Janaka sprang Udāvasu;

verses.sanskrit:
उदावसोस्तु धर्मात्मा जातो वै नन्दिवर्धनः
नन्दिवर्धनपुत्रस्तु सुकेतुर्नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
udāvasostu dharmātmā jāto vai nandivardhanaḥ
nandivardhanaputrastu suketurnāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: Udāvasu's the pious-souled Nandivardhana. And Nandivardha's son was the heroic Suketu.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेतोरपि धर्मात्मा देवरातो महाबलः
देवरातस्य राजर्षेर्बृहद्रथ इति श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
suketorapi dharmātmā devarāto mahābalaḥ
devarātasya rājarṣerbṛhadratha iti śrutaḥ

translations.english: Suketu's son was the mighty and righteous Devarata. And the Rājarși Devarāta's son was Brhadratha.

verses.sanskrit:
बृहद्रथस्य शूरोऽभून्महावीरः प्रतापवान्
महावीरस्य धृतिमान्सुधृतिः सत्यविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
bṛhadrathasya śūro'bhūnmahāvīraḥ pratāpavān
mahāvīrasya dhṛtimānsudhṛtiḥ satyavikramaḥ

translations.english: Bịhadratha's son was the heroic and puissant Mahāvīra. And Mahāvīra's son was Sudhști, endowed with fortitude and having truth for prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
सुधृतेरपि धर्मात्मा धृष्टकेतुः सुधार्मिकः
धृष्टकेतोस्तु राजर्षेर्हर्यश्व इति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
sudhṛterapi dharmātmā dhṛṣṭaketuḥ sudhārmikaḥ
dhṛṣṭaketostu rājarṣerharyaśva iti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: Sudhrtia's son was the pious-spirited and eminently righteous Dhīșțaketu. And the Rājarși Dhistaketu's son was Haryasva.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्यश्वस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रतीन्धकः
प्रतीन्धकस्य धर्मात्मा राजा कीर्तिरथः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
haryaśvasya maruḥ putro maroḥ putraḥ pratīndhakaḥ
pratīndhakasya dharmātmā rājā kīrtirathaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Haryaśva's son was Maru; and Maru's son was Pratīndhaka. And Pratīndhaka's son was the righteous king Kirtiratha.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रः कीर्तिरथस्यापि देवमीढ इति स्मृतः
देवमीढस्य विबुधो विबुधस्य महीध्रकः
verses.transliteration:
putraḥ kīrtirathasyāpi devamīḍha iti smṛtaḥ
devamīḍhasya vibudho vibudhasya mahīdhrakaḥ

translations.english: Kirtiratha's Devamidha, and Devamidha's Vibudha, and Vibudha's Mahidhraka.

verses.sanskrit:
महीध्रकसुतो राजा कीर्तिरातो महाबलः
कीर्तिरातस्य राजर्षेर्महारोमा व्यजायत
verses.transliteration:
mahīdhrakasuto rājā kīrtirāto mahābalaḥ
kīrtirātasya rājarṣermahāromā vyajāyata

translations.english: Mahīdhraka's son was king Kirtirāta endowed with great strength. And the Rājarşi Kirtirāta had Mahāroman born to him.

verses.sanskrit:
महारोंणस्तु धर्मात्मा स्वर्णरोमा व्यजायत
स्वर्णरोंणस्तु राजर्षेर्ह्रस्वरोमा व्यजायत
verses.transliteration:
mahāroṁṇastu dharmātmā svarṇaromā vyajāyata
svarṇaroṁṇastu rājarṣerhrasvaromā vyajāyata

translations.english: Mahāroman, the virtuous Svarnaroman. And the Rājarşi Svarnaroman had Hrasvaroman born to him. son was

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पुत्रद्वयं जज्ञे धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मनः
ज्येष्ठोऽहमनुजो भ्राता मम वीरः कुशध्वजः
verses.transliteration:
tasya putradvayaṁ jajñe dharmajñasya mahātmanaḥ
jyeṣṭho'hamanujo bhrātā mama vīraḥ kuśadhvajaḥ

translations.english: This high-souled king conversant with morality had two sons: the elder, myself the younger, even my brother, who was the elder son, and consigning to my care Kusadhvaja, our father sought the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धे पितरि स्वर्याते धर्मेण धुरमावहम्
भ्रातरं देवसंकाशं स्नेहात्पश्यन्कुशध्वजम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛddhe pitari svaryāte dharmeṇa dhuramāvaham
bhrātaraṁ devasaṁkāśaṁ snehātpaśyankuśadhvajam

translations.english: And on my aged sire ascending heaven, I righteously ruled the kingdom and cherished my brother Kusadvaja resembling a celestial, with the eye of affection.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य सांकाश्यादगमत्पुरात्
सुधन्वा वीर्यवान्राजा मिथिलामवरोधकः
verses.transliteration:
kasyacittvatha kālasya sāṁkāśyādagamatpurāt
sudhanvā vīryavānrājā mithilāmavarodhakaḥ

translations.english: It came to pass that on one occasion a certain powerful king named Sudhanvan came before Mithilā intending to lay siege to it.

verses.sanskrit:
स च मे प्रेषयामास शैवं धनुरनुत्तमम्
सीता कन्या च पद्माक्षी मह्यं वै दीयतामिति
verses.transliteration:
sa ca me preṣayāmāsa śaivaṁ dhanuranuttamam
sītā kanyā ca padmākṣī mahyaṁ vai dīyatāmiti

translations.english: He sent word to me, saying, 'Do you give me the all-excellent bow of Śiva, as well as your daughter, the lotus-even Sītā.'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याप्रदानाद्ब्रह्मर्षे युद्धमासीन्मया सह
स हतोऽभिमुखो राजा सुधन्वा तु मया रणे
verses.transliteration:
tasyāpradānādbrahmarṣe yuddhamāsīnmayā saha
sa hato'bhimukho rājā sudhanvā tu mayā raṇe

translations.english: And is consequence of my not granting him either, king Sudhanvan, O Brahmarsi, entered into hostilities with me; but he was both defeated and slain by me in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य तं मुनिश्रेष्ठ सुधन्वानं नराधिपम्
सांकाश्ये भ्रातरं शूरमभ्यषिञ्चं कुशध्वजम्
verses.transliteration:
nihatya taṁ muniśreṣṭha sudhanvānaṁ narādhipam
sāṁkāśye bhrātaraṁ śūramabhyaṣiñcaṁ kuśadhvajam

translations.english: O foremost of ascetics, slaying king Sudhanvan. I installed in Sānkāśyā my heroic brother Kuśadhvaja.

verses.sanskrit:
कनीयानेष मे भ्राता अहं ज्येष्ठो महामुने
ददामि परमप्रीतो वध्वौ ते मुनिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
kanīyāneṣa me bhrātā ahaṁ jyeṣṭho mahāmune
dadāmi paramaprīto vadhvau te munipuṁgava

translations.english: Thus one, O mighty anchorite, is my younger brother, and I am his elder. O powerful ascetic, well pleased will I confer on you these as your daughter-in-law,

verses.sanskrit:
सीतां रामाय भद्रं ते ऊर्मिलां लक्ष्मणाय च
वीर्यशुल्कां मम सुतां सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम्
verses.transliteration:
sītāṁ rāmāya bhadraṁ te ūrmilāṁ lakṣmaṇāya ca
vīryaśulkāṁ mama sutāṁ sītāṁ surasutopamām

translations.english: Sītā on Rāma, good betide you, and Urmilā on Laksmana. And, I take oath thrice that, without doubt, I will with a glad heart confer upon you, O potent ascetic, as your daughters-in-law my second daughter Urmilā and also Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial, having prowess assigned for her dower.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणयो राजन्गोदानं कारयस्व ह
पितृकार्यं च भद्रं ते ततो वैवाहिकं कुरु
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇayo rājangodānaṁ kārayasva ha
pitṛkāryaṁ ca bhadraṁ te tato vaivāhikaṁ kuru

translations.english: do you now, O king, give away kine on behalf of the nuptials of Rāma and Lakşmaņa; and also perform their ancestral rites, good to you; and then complete the marriage ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
मघा ह्यद्य महाबाहो तृतीये दिवसे प्रभो
फल्गुन्यामुत्तरे राजंस्तस्मिन्वैवाहिकं कुरु
रामलक्ष्मणयोरर्थे दानं कार्यं सुखोदयम्
verses.transliteration:
maghā hyadya mahābāho tṛtīye divase prabho
phalgunyāmuttare rājaṁstasminvaivāhikaṁ kuru
rāmalakṣmaṇayorarthe dānaṁ kāryaṁ sukhodayam

translations.english: To-day the star Magha is on the ascendant. On the third day, my master, when the Phalguna will be on the north, do you, O monarch, perform the marriage ceremony. Do you now, however, dispense gifts for invoking blessings upon Rāma and Laksmana.24

verses.sanskrit:
तमुक्तवन्तं वैदेहं विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
उवाच वचनं वीरं वसिष्ठसहितो नृपम्
verses.transliteration:
tamuktavantaṁ vaidehaṁ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
uvāca vacanaṁ vīraṁ vasiṣṭhasahito nṛpam

translations.english: When Vaideha had spoken thus, the mighty ascetic Viśvāmitra is company with Vasiștha addressed that heroic king, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्त्यान्यप्रमेयानि कुलानि नरपुंगव
इक्ष्वाकूणां विदेहानां नैषां तुल्योऽस्ति कश्चन
verses.transliteration:
acintyānyaprameyāni kulāni narapuṁgava
ikṣvākūṇāṁ videhānāṁ naiṣāṁ tulyo'sti kaścana

translations.english: O puissant one, the lines of the Ikşvākus and the Vaidehas are exceedingly noble and incomparable. No other race can by any means compare with them.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशो धर्मसंबन्धः सदृशो रूपसंपदा
रामलक्ष्मणयो राजन्सीता चोर्मिलया सह
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśo dharmasaṁbandhaḥ sadṛśo rūpasaṁpadā
rāmalakṣmaṇayo rājansītā cormilayā saha

translations.english: O monarch, this youthful union of Rāma and Lakşmaņa with Sītā and Urmilā is fit by all means; and it is worthy of their wealth of grace.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्राता यवीयान्धर्मज्ञ एष राजा कुशध्वजः
अस्य धर्मात्मनो राजन्रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि
सुताद्वयं नरश्रेष्ठ पत्न्यर्थं वरयामहे
verses.transliteration:
bhrātā yavīyāndharmajña eṣa rājā kuśadhvajaḥ
asya dharmātmano rājanrūpeṇāpratimaṁ bhuvi
sutādvayaṁ naraśreṣṭha patnyarthaṁ varayāmahe

translations.english: Now do you, O foremost of men, listen to my words. This youthful brother of yours, king Kusadhvaja, O you versed in morality, this pious-souled one, O king, has, O prime of men, a couple of daughters, unparalleled on earth in beauty, whom we would ask for, to become wives to the prince Bharata and the intelligent Satrughna; as we, O king, ask for your own daughters in the interests of those high-souled ones (Rama and Laksmana).4-6

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रा दशरथस्येमे रूपयौवनशालिनः
लोकपालोपमाः सर्वे देवतुल्यपराक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
putrā daśarathasyeme rūpayauvanaśālinaḥ
lokapālopamāḥ sarve devatulyaparākramāḥ

translations.english: And these sons of Daśaratha are endued with youth and beauty, resembling the Lokapalas, and possessed of the prowess of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
उभयोरपि राजेन्द्र संबन्धेनानुबध्यताम्
इक्ष्वाकुकुलमव्यग्रं भवतः पुण्यकर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
ubhayorapi rājendra saṁbandhenānubadhyatām
ikṣvākukulamavyagraṁ bhavataḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Therefore do you, O foremost of sovereigns, by this alliance with both the brothers, bind the Ikşvāku race. And in this may your mind never waver!

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठस्य मते तदा
जनकः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच मुनिपुंगवौ
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭhasya mate tadā
janakaḥ prāñjalirvākyamuvāca munipuṁgavau

translations.english: Hearing Viśvāmitra's words embodying the sentiments of Vasiştha, Janaka with clasped hands addressed both the potent ascetics, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं कुलसंबन्धं यदाज्ञापयथः स्वयम्
एवं भवतु भद्रं वः कुशध्वजसुते इमे
पत्न्यौ भजेतां सहितौ शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ kulasaṁbandhaṁ yadājñāpayathaḥ svayam
evaṁ bhavatu bhadraṁ vaḥ kuśadhvajasute ime
patnyau bhajetāṁ sahitau śatrughnabharatāvubhau

translations.english: Whatever you wish, even that shall be done, good betide you. Let these daughters of Kusadhvaja together become the wives of Śatrughna and Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
एकाह्ना राजपुत्रीणां चतसृणां महामुने
पाणीन्गृह्णन्तु चत्वारो राजपुत्रा महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
ekāhnā rājaputrīṇāṁ catasṛṇāṁ mahāmune
pāṇīngṛhṇantu catvāro rājaputrā mahābalāḥ

translations.english: On the same day, O mighty Muni, let the four highly powerful princes espouse the hands of the four princesses.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरे दिवसे ब्रह्मन्फल्गुनीभ्यां मनीषिणः
वैवाहिकं प्रशंसन्ति भगो यत्र प्रजापतिः
verses.transliteration:
uttare divase brahmanphalgunībhyāṁ manīṣiṇaḥ
vaivāhikaṁ praśaṁsanti bhago yatra prajāpatiḥ

translations.english: The learned consider bridal celebrated on the day succeeding those on which the Phalgunis are on the ascendant, and having for its presiding deity Bhagas-the most auspicious.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा वचः सौम्यं प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः
उभौ मुनिवरौ राजा जनको वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā vacaḥ saumyaṁ pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
ubhau munivarau rājā janako vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Having said these amiable words, king' Janaka arose, and with clasped hands addressed both the foremost of ascetics, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
परो धर्मः कृतो मह्यं शिष्योऽस्मि भवतोः सदा
इमान्यासनमुख्यानि आसेतां मुनिपुंगवौ
verses.transliteration:
paro dharmaḥ kṛto mahyaṁ śiṣyo'smi bhavatoḥ sadā
imānyāsanamukhyāni āsetāṁ munipuṁgavau

translations.english: I have reaped high religious merit (by these nuptials), and I also am your disciple. And do you, you anchorets, occupy these best of thrones, (belonging to us).15

verses.sanskrit:
यथा दशरथस्येयं तथायोध्या पुरी मम
प्रभुत्वे नासित्संदेहो यथार्हं कर्तुमर्हथः
verses.transliteration:
yathā daśarathasyeyaṁ tathāyodhyā purī mama
prabhutve nāsitsaṁdeho yathārhaṁ kartumarhathaḥ

translations.english: And even as this kingdom is to Dasaratha is Ayodhyā to myself. Do you not therefore entertain any doubts as to your lordship. Do you therefore do as it behove you.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ब्रुवति वैदेहे जनके रघुनन्दनः
राजा दशरथो हृष्टः प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā bruvati vaidehe janake raghunandanaḥ
rājā daśaratho hṛṣṭaḥ pratyuvāca mahīpatim

translations.english: And as Vaideha Janaka was speaking thus, Raghu's son, king Dasaratha, well pleased answered that monarch, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
युवामसंख्येय गुणौ भ्रातरौ मिथिलेश्वरौ
ऋषयो राजसंघाश्च भवद्भ्यामभिपूजिताः
verses.transliteration:
yuvāmasaṁkhyeya guṇau bhrātarau mithileśvarau
ṛṣayo rājasaṁghāśca bhavadbhyāmabhipūjitāḥ

translations.english: Countless are the excellences that pertain to you brothers, lords of Mithilā; and saints and sovereigns are honoured by you,* auspiciousness be yours. *The commentator here seems to be in fault. He ever explains-By you have your royal ancestors been honoured. Evidently an error. I differ from him. The particle ca (and) makes the point clear.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते गमिष्यामि स्वमालयम्
श्राद्धकर्माणि सर्वाणि विधास्य इति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṁ te gamiṣyāmi svamālayam
śrāddhakarmāṇi sarvāṇi vidhāsya iti cābravīt

translations.english: Good betide you, I will repair to my own quarters, there to duly perform the Śrāddha ceremonies.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापृष्ट्वा नरपतिं राजा दशरथस्तदा
मुनीन्द्रौ तौ पुरस्कृत्य जगामाशु महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
tamāpṛṣṭvā narapatiṁ rājā daśarathastadā
munīndrau tau puraskṛtya jagāmāśu mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Then having greeted that king of men, the illustrious Dasaratha, placing those foremost of ascetics in his front, went away.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा निलयं राजा श्राद्धं कृत्वा विधानतः
प्रभाते काल्यमुत्थाय चक्रे गोदानमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā nilayaṁ rājā śrāddhaṁ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ
prabhāte kālyamutthāya cakre godānamuttamam

translations.english: And reaching his quarters, the king performed the Srāddha according to the ordinance, arose the next morning, and made excellent gifts of kine.

verses.sanskrit:
गवां शतसहस्राणि ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नराधिपः
एकैकशो ददौ राजा पुत्रानुद्धिश्य धर्मतः
verses.transliteration:
gavāṁ śatasahasrāṇi brāhmaṇebhyo narādhipaḥ
ekaikaśo dadau rājā putrānuddhiśya dharmataḥ

translations.english: And to Brāhmaṇas the monarch severally gavę away kine by hundreds and by thousands, for the welfare of his sons.

verses.sanskrit:
वित्तमन्यच्च सुबहु द्विजेभ्यो रघुनन्दनः
ददौ गोदानमुद्दिश्य पुत्राणां पुत्रवत्सलः
verses.transliteration:
vittamanyacca subahu dvijebhyo raghunandanaḥ
dadau godānamuddiśya putrāṇāṁ putravatsalaḥ

translations.english: And that puissant one gave away to the regenerate ones four hundred thousands of kine furnished with horns plaited with gold, and each having her calf, together with bell-Mattel vessels for milking them.

verses.sanskrit:
स सुतैः कृतगोदानैर्वृतश्च नृपतिस्तदा
लोकपालैरिवाभाति वृतः सौम्यः प्रजापतिः
verses.transliteration:
sa sutaiḥ kṛtagodānairvṛtaśca nṛpatistadā
lokapālairivābhāti vṛtaḥ saumyaḥ prajāpatiḥ

translations.english: And that descendant of Raghu addicted to his sons made presents of various other valuables and the Brāhmaṇas, on behalf of his sons. And having given away kine, the surrounded by his sons looked like to the amiable Prajāpati surrounded by the Lokapālas.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रः केकयराजस्य साक्षाद्भरतमातुलः
दृष्ट्वा पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
putraḥ kekayarājasya sākṣādbharatamātulaḥ
dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṁ rājānamidamabravīt

translations.english: And it came to pass that the day on which the king made excellent presents of kine, the heroic Yudhājit, son to the lord of the Kekayas and maternal uncle to Bharata, presented himself before Dasaratha. And having seen the king and enquired after his welfare, he said to him.

verses.sanskrit:
केकयाधिपती राजा स्नेहात्कुशलमब्रवीत्
येषां कुशलकामोऽसि तेषां संप्रत्यनामयम्
verses.transliteration:
kekayādhipatī rājā snehātkuśalamabravīt
yeṣāṁ kuśalakāmo'si teṣāṁ saṁpratyanāmayam

translations.english: The lord of the Kekayas has from affection enquired after your welfare, sayiing,-'They of whose peace you are anxious, are at present well.' And, O foremost of kings, desirous of seeing (Bharata) together with his wife, that lord of earth repaired to Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा त्वहमयोध्यायां विवाहार्थं तवात्मजान्
मिथिलामुपयातास्तु त्वया सह महीपते
त्वरयाभ्युपयातोऽहं द्रष्टुकामः स्वसुः सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tvahamayodhyāyāṁ vivāhārthaṁ tavātmajān
mithilāmupayātāstu tvayā saha mahīpate
tvarayābhyupayāto'haṁ draṣṭukāmaḥ svasuḥ sutam

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu. And learning at Ayodhyā that your sons for the purpose of marriage had, O monarch, come to Mithilā with yourself, I have speedily hide hither, with the intention of seeing my sister's son.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ राजा दशरथः प्रियातिथिमुपस्थिम
दृष्ट्वा परमसत्कारैः पूजार्हं समपूजयत्
verses.transliteration:
atha rājā daśarathaḥ priyātithimupasthima
dṛṣṭvā paramasatkāraiḥ pūjārhaṁ samapūjayat

translations.english: Then king Dasaratha, on having that dear guest with him, rendered to him all the respect that he deserved.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तामुषितो रात्रिं सह पुत्रैर्महात्मभिः
ऋषींस्तदा पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastāmuṣito rātriṁ saha putrairmahātmabhiḥ
ṛṣīṁstadā puraskṛtya yajñavāṭamupāgamat

translations.english: Then having passed the night in company with his high-souled sons, that one versed in men and things arose in the morning, and having disposed of his daily duties, approached the entrance of the sacrificial ground, headed by the saints.

verses.sanskrit:
युक्ते मुहूर्ते विजये सर्वाभरणभूषितैः
भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः कृतकौतुकमङ्गलः
वसिष्ठं पुरतः कृत्वा महर्षीनपरानपि
verses.transliteration:
yukte muhūrte vijaye sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaiḥ
bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ kṛtakautukamaṅgalaḥ
vasiṣṭhaṁ purataḥ kṛtvā maharṣīnaparānapi

translations.english: Then at an auspicious moment called Vijaya; Rāma with Vasiştha as well as other Maharşis at his head, and accompanied by his brothers adorned with various ornaments, who had all performed the rites relative to their nuptials, (approached the entrance of the sacrificial ground). Then the worshipful Vasistha, coming to Vaideha, spoke as follows.

verses.sanskrit:
दातृप्रतिग्रहीतृभ्यां सर्वार्थाः प्रभवन्ति हि
स्वधर्मं प्रतिपद्यस्व कृत्वा वैवाह्यमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
dātṛpratigrahītṛbhyāṁ sarvārthāḥ prabhavanti hi
svadharmaṁ pratipadyasva kṛtvā vaivāhyamuttamam

translations.english: King Dasaratha, O foremost of sovereigns, that chief among the best of men-accompanied with his son, who have performed all the rites relative to their nuptials, stay the orders of the bestower (of the bride); for the meeting of the giver and the receiver is indispensable to every transaction (of this nature). Do you therefore maintain your merit by accomplishing this excellent nuptial ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः परमोदारो वसिष्ठेन महात्मना
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा वाक्यं परमधर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ paramodāro vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
pratyuvāca mahātejā vākyaṁ paramadharmavit

translations.english: Thus addressed by the high-souled Vasistha, that exceedingly generous and energetic one versed in morality answered, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
कः स्थितः प्रतिहारो मे कस्याज्ञा संप्रतीक्ष्यते
स्वगृहे को विचारोऽस्ति यथा राज्यमिदं तव
verses.transliteration:
kaḥ sthitaḥ pratihāro me kasyājñā saṁpratīkṣyate
svagṛhe ko vicāro'sti yathā rājyamidaṁ tava

translations.english: Who act as my warder there? And whose commands does he stay? And what need of exercising judgement in such a matter? As this kingdom is mine, so it is verily your. O foremost of anchorets, my daughters resembling flames of fire, having performed all the rites relative to the incoming nuptials, are at the foot of the dais; and, sitting beside the dais.

verses.sanskrit:
सज्जोऽहं त्वत्प्रतीक्षोऽस्मि वेद्यामस्यां प्रतिष्ठितः
अविघ्नं कुरुतां राजा किमर्थं हि विलम्ब्यते
verses.transliteration:
sajjo'haṁ tvatpratīkṣo'smi vedyāmasyāṁ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
avighnaṁ kurutāṁ rājā kimarthaṁ hi vilambyate

translations.english: I myself had been expecting you every moment. Do you perform everything without let. What need of delaying further?

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वाक्यं जनकेनोक्तं श्रुत्वा दशरथस्तदा
प्रवेशयामास सुतान्सर्वानृषिगणानपि
verses.transliteration:
tadvākyaṁ janakenoktaṁ śrutvā daśarathastadā
praveśayāmāsa sutānsarvānṛṣigaṇānapi

translations.english: Hearing those words uttered by Janaka, Dasaratha entered in together with his sons and the body of saints.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम्
इयं सीता मम सुता सहधर्मचरी तव
प्रतीच्छ चैनां भद्रं ते पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना
verses.transliteration:
abravījjanako rājā kausalyānandavardhanam
iyaṁ sītā mama sutā sahadharmacarī tava
pratīccha caināṁ bhadraṁ te pāṇiṁ gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā

translations.english: Then bringing Sītā adorned with various ornaments near the fire, and placing her before Rāghava, king Janaka addressed the enchancer of Kausalyā's joy, saying, This Sītā, my daughter, to you accept, good betide you, as your partner in the observance of every duty: do you take her hand by yours. May she be of excited piety, and devoted to her husband; ever following you like your shadow!

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणागच्छ भद्रं ते ऊर्मिलामुद्यतां मया
प्रतीच्छ पाणिं गृह्णीष्व मा भूत्कालस्य पर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇāgaccha bhadraṁ te ūrmilāmudyatāṁ mayā
pratīccha pāṇiṁ gṛhṇīṣva mā bhūtkālasya paryayaḥ

translations.english: And the celestial kettle-drums sounded, and blossoms began to shower down copiously. Having thus given away his daughter Sītä, with water and mantras, king Janaka, overflowing with delight, said, Come forward, O Laksmana, good to you. Receive you Urmilā ready to be bestowed by me upon you. Do you accept her hand: let there be no delay about it.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमुक्त्वा जनको भरतं चाभ्यभाषत
गृहाण पाणिं माण्डव्याः पाणिना रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
tamevamuktvā janako bharataṁ cābhyabhāṣata
gṛhāṇa pāṇiṁ māṇḍavyāḥ pāṇinā raghunandana

translations.english: Having addressed Lakşmaņa thus, Janaka spoke to Bharata, saying, Do you, O descendant of Raghu, take Mandavya's hand by yours own.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नं चापि धर्मात्मा अब्रवीज्जनकेश्वरः
श्रुतकीर्त्या महाबाहो पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnaṁ cāpi dharmātmā abravījjanakeśvaraḥ
śrutakīrtyā mahābāho pāṇiṁ gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā

translations.english: The righteous lord of Mithila spoke also to Satrughna, saying, Do you, O you of mighty arms, take Śrutakīrti's hand by your own. May you all be good, and vowed to excellent life! And be, you Kākutsthas, you united with your wives. Let there be no delay about it.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा वेदिं राजानमेव च
ऋषींश्चैव महात्मानः सह भार्या रघूत्तमाः
यथोक्तेन तथा चक्रुर्विवाहं विधिपूर्वकम्
verses.transliteration:
agniṁ pradakṣiṇaṁ kṛtvā vediṁ rājānameva ca
ṛṣīṁścaiva mahātmānaḥ saha bhāryā raghūttamāḥ
yathoktena tathā cakrurvivāhaṁ vidhipūrvakam

translations.english: Hearing Janaka's speech, those four perpetuators of Raghus's line, staying by Vasiştha's opinions, taking the hands of the four brides with their own, went round the sacrificial fire, and the dais, and the king, and the highsouled saints; and in company with their wives, agreeably to direction entered into matrimony in accordance with the ordinance.

verses.sanskrit:
ननृतुश्चाप्सरःसंघा गन्धर्वाश्च जगुः कलम्
विवाहे रघुमुख्यानां तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
nanṛtuścāpsaraḥsaṁghā gandharvāśca jaguḥ kalam
vivāhe raghumukhyānāṁ tadadbhutamivābhavat

translations.english: There was a mighty shower of shining blossoms from the firmament accompanied with the sounds of celestial kettle-drums, and choiring and instrumental music. And the Apsaras, danced and the Gandharvas sang melodiously, at the bridal of the foremost of the Raghus. And this seemed wonderful to witness.

verses.sanskrit:
ईदृशे वर्तमाने तु तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिते
त्रिरग्निं ते परिक्रम्य ऊहुर्भार्या महौजसः
verses.transliteration:
īdṛśe vartamāne tu tūryodghuṣṭaninādite
triragniṁ te parikramya ūhurbhāryā mahaujasaḥ

translations.english: To the blowing of trumpets, those exceedingly puissant ones, thrice going round the fire, in company with their wives went the encampment.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोपकार्यां जग्मुस्ते सदारा रघुनन्दनः
राजाप्यनुययौ पश्यन्सर्षिसंघः सबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
athopakāryāṁ jagmuste sadārā raghunandanaḥ
rājāpyanuyayau paśyansarṣisaṁghaḥ sabāndhavaḥ

translations.english: to The king, having seen that all the auspicious ceremonies were performed, went in their wake accompanied by the sages and his adherents.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
आपृच्छ्य तौ च राजानौ जगामोत्तरपर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
atha rātryāṁ vyatītāyāṁ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
āpṛcchya tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam

translations.english: Then when the right had passed away, the mighty Muni Viśvāmitra, having greeted the monarchs, yet out for the Northern mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रो गते राजा वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम्
आपृच्छ्याथ जगामाशु राजा दशरथः पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro gate rājā vaidehaṁ mithilādhipam
āpṛcchyātha jagāmāśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm

translations.english: When Viśvāmitra had gone away, king Dasaratha, greeting Mithila's lord, Vaideha, actively prepared for setting out for his own capital.

verses.sanskrit:
कम्बलानां च मुख्यानां क्षौमकोट्यम्बराणि च
हस्त्यश्वरथपादातं दिव्यरूपं स्वलंकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
kambalānāṁ ca mukhyānāṁ kṣaumakoṭyambarāṇi ca
hastyaśvarathapādātaṁ divyarūpaṁ svalaṁkṛtam

translations.english: Then the king of the Videhas gave a dower consisting of various things. And Mithilā's lord gave many hundred thousands of kine, and excellent woollen stuffs, and Koțis of common cloths; and elephants, and horses, and cars, and footmen, as well as an hundred damsels adorned, endowed with elegance to form goodly waitingmaids. And well-pleased the king gave as a noble dower gold and silver and pearls and coral.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविवेश स्वनिलयं मिथिलां मिथिलेश्वरः
राजाप्ययोध्याधिपतिः सह पुत्रैर्महात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
praviveśa svanilayaṁ mithilāṁ mithileśvaraḥ
rājāpyayodhyādhipatiḥ saha putrairmahātmabhiḥ

translations.english: Having given divers kinds of articles, that king, the lord of Mithila, bidding adieu to the monarch (Dasaratha), re-entered his own capital. And the master of Ayodhyā accompanied with his high-souled sons, and headed by the saints in a body, started on the journey, followed by his own army.

verses.sanskrit:
घोराः स्म पक्षिणो वाचो व्याहरन्ति ततस्ततः
भौमाश्चैव मृगाः सर्वे गच्छन्ति स्म प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
ghorāḥ sma pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti tatastataḥ
bhaumāścaiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: As that tiger-like one was on his way, in company with Rāghava and the saints, the fowls began to utter frightful cries all around, and the beasts on earth to stream in a Southern direction.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्दृष्ट्वा राजशार्दूलो वसिष्ठं पर्यपृच्छत
असौम्याः पक्षिणो घोरा मृगाश्चापि प्रदक्षिणाः
किमिदं हृदयोत्कम्पि मनो मम विषीदति
verses.transliteration:
tāndṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṁ paryapṛcchata
asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāścāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ
kimidaṁ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati

translations.english: Beholding them, that tiger-like monarch asked Vasistha, saying, Those birds of fierce aspects emit frightful cries and beasts stream in a Southerly direction. What is this? My heart tremble and my mind is not at ease.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञो दशरथस्यैतच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यं महानृषिः
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं श्रूयतामस्य यत्फलम्
verses.transliteration:
rājño daśarathasyaitacchrutvā vākyaṁ mahānṛṣiḥ
uvāca madhurāṁ vāṇīṁ śrūyatāmasya yatphalam

translations.english: Hearing the speech of king Dasaratha, that mighty saint spoke sweetly, saying, 'These fowls of the air by their cries presage some dreadful impending evil; but these beasts betoken peace restored. Therefore do you renounce anxiety'

verses.sanskrit:
तमसा संवृतः सूर्यः सर्वा न प्रबभुर्दिशः
भस्मना चावृतं सर्वं संमूढमिव तद्बलम्
verses.transliteration:
tamasā saṁvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarvā na prababhurdiśaḥ
bhasmanā cāvṛtaṁ sarvaṁ saṁmūḍhamiva tadbalam

translations.english: As they were thus conversing, there blew a strong wind; and all the earth began to speak; and the trees to topple down. And a deep gloom enveloped the sun; and no quarter could be discovered. And enveloped in ashes, that host became stupefied.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठ ऋषयश्चान्ये राजा च ससुतस्तदा
ससंज्ञा इव तत्रासन्सर्वमन्यद्विचेतनम्
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaścānye rājā ca sasutastadā
sasaṁjñā iva tatrāsansarvamanyadvicetanam

translations.english: At that dreadful hour, Vasiştha and the other saints and the king alone retained their senses, all else were deprived of their senses, and the army was enveloped with ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
कैलासमिव दुर्धर्षं कालाग्निमिव दुःसहम्
ज्वलन्तमिव तेजोभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यं पृथग्जनैः
verses.transliteration:
kailāsamiva durdharṣaṁ kālāgnimiva duḥsaham
jvalantamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṁ pṛthagjanaiḥ

translations.english: The king saw that repressor of kings, the descendant of Bhrgu, Jamadagni's son, dreadful to behold, wearing a head of matted locks, like to the Kailāsa, had to baffle, resembling the fire at the universal dissolution, difficult to bear, flaming in energy, incapable of being looked at by the unrighteous, with his axe on his shoulder, equipped with a bow like to the lighting, and fierce arrows, looking like Śiva the slayer of Tripura.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसंकाशं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्
वसिष्ठप्रमुखा विप्रा जपहोमपरायणाः
संगता मुनयः सर्वे संजजल्पुरथो मिथः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṁkāśaṁ jvalantamiva pāvakam
vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ
saṁgatā munayaḥ sarve saṁjajalpuratho mithaḥ

translations.english: Beholding him of dreadful appearance like to flaming fire, the Vipras headed by Viśvāmitra, engaged in reciting mantras and and offering oblations to the fire, those saints assembled together, began to converse with each other.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्पितृवधामर्षी क्षत्रं नोत्सादयिष्यति
पूर्वं क्षत्रवधं कृत्वा गतमन्युर्गतज्वरः
क्षत्रस्योत्सादनं भूयो न खल्वस्य चिकीर्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
kaccitpitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṁ notsādayiṣyati
pūrvaṁ kṣatravadhaṁ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvaraḥ
kṣatrasyotsādanaṁ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam

translations.english: Is this one, enraged because of the slaughter of this sire, intent upon exterminating the Kș atriyas? Formerly, having slaughtered the Kșatriyas, he pacified his ire and mental ferment, 'therefore, the annihilate the Ksatriya once again can never be his endeavour.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वार्घ्यमादाय भार्गवं भीमदर्शनम्
ऋषयो राम रामेति मधुरां वाचमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvārghyamādāya bhārgavaṁ bhīmadarśanam
ṛṣayo rāma rāmeti madhurāṁ vācamabruvan

translations.english: Having said this, the saints offered Arghya to Bhrgu's son of dreadful appearance; and addressed him in soothing words, saying, 'Q Rāma! O Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजामृषिदत्तां प्रतापवान्
रामं दाशरथिं रामो जामदग्न्योऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya tu tāṁ pūjāmṛṣidattāṁ pratāpavān
rāmaṁ dāśarathiṁ rāmo jāmadagnyo'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Accepting that homage rendered to him by the saints, that puissant one, Jamadagni's son, Rāma, addressed Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
राम दाशरथे वीर वीर्यं ते श्रूयतेऽधुतम्
धनुषो भेदनं चैव निखिलेन मया श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
rāma dāśarathe vīra vīryaṁ te śrūyate'dhutam
dhanuṣo bhedanaṁ caiva nikhilena mayā śrutam

translations.english: Rama, son of Dasaratha, I have, O hero, heard of your wonderful prowess; and I have also heard all about your breaking of the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्भुतमचिन्त्यं च भेदनं धनुषस्त्वया
तच्छ्रुत्वाहमनुप्राप्तो धनुर्गृह्यापरं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
tadadbhutamacintyaṁ ca bhedanaṁ dhanuṣastvayā
tacchrutvāhamanuprāpto dhanurgṛhyāparaṁ śubham

translations.english: Having heard of that wonderful and inconceivable breaking of the bow, I have bent my steps hither. Do you take another auspicious bow,. Do you stretch it, fix the arrow upon this mighty and dreadful bow, belonging to Jamadagni; and thus display your prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
तदहं ते बलं दृष्ट्वा धनुषोऽस्य प्रपूरणे
द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदास्यामि वीर्यश्लाघ्यमिदं तव
verses.transliteration:
tadahaṁ te balaṁ dṛṣṭvā dhanuṣo'sya prapūraṇe
dvandvayuddhaṁ pradāsyāmi vīryaślāghyamidaṁ tava

translations.english: Then, having witnessed your might in stretching the bow, I shall offer you combat, laying under contribution our utmost strength.

verses.sanskrit:
भार्गवाणां कुले जातः स्वाध्यायव्रतशालिनाम्
सहस्राक्षे प्रतिज्ञाय शस्त्रं निक्षिप्तवानसि
verses.transliteration:
bhārgavāṇāṁ kule jātaḥ svādhyāyavrataśālinām
sahasrākṣe pratijñāya śastraṁ nikṣiptavānasi

translations.english: Hearing his words, king Dasaratha with a blank countenance, and clasped hands, said, You have quenched your ire against the Ksatriyuas; and, moreover, you are a Brāhmaṇa boasting of high austerities. It therefore behove you to dispel the fears of my sons who are boys. You bring your life from the race of the Bhargavas engaged in observing vows, and studying you Veda; and you have renounced arms vowing in the presence of the thousandeyed one.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं धर्मपरो भूत्वा काश्यपाय वसुंधराम्
दत्त्वा वनमुपागम्य महेन्द्रकृतकेतनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ dharmaparo bhūtvā kāśyapāya vasuṁdharām
dattvā vanamupāgamya mahendrakṛtaketanaḥ

translations.english: Embracing a life of righteousness, you did were confer the earth upon Kaśyapa and repaired to the forest, making the Mahendra hill your home.

verses.sanskrit:
मम सर्वविनाशाय संप्राप्तस्त्वं महामुने
न चैकस्मिन्हते रामे सर्वे जीवामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
mama sarvavināśāya saṁprāptastvaṁ mahāmune
na caikasminhate rāme sarve jīvāmahe vayam

translations.english: O mighty Muni, you have come here to compass the destruction of my all; but if Rāma be slain, we shall never live.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रुवत्येवं दशरथे जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्
अनादृत्यैव तद्वाक्यं राममेवाभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
bruvatyevaṁ daśarathe jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān
anādṛtyaiva tadvākyaṁ rāmamevābhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Thus addressed by Dasaratha, the powerful son of Jamadagni, disregarding his words, thus addressed Rāma,

verses.sanskrit:
इमे द्वे धनुषी श्रेष्ठे दिव्ये लोकाभिविश्रुते
दृढे बलवती मुख्ये सुकृते विश्वकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
ime dve dhanuṣī śreṣṭhe divye lokābhiviśrute
dṛḍhe balavatī mukhye sukṛte viśvakarmaṇā

translations.english: These two foremost of bows, extraordinary, and worshipped of all the worlds, and stout, and powerful, surpassingly excellent, constructed with care by Viśvakarman.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिसृष्टं सुरैरेकं त्र्यम्बकाय युयुत्सवे
त्रिपुरघ्नं नरश्रेष्ठ भग्नं काकुत्स्थ यत्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
atisṛṣṭaṁ surairekaṁ tryambakāya yuyutsave
tripuraghnaṁ naraśreṣṭha bhagnaṁ kākutstha yattvayā

translations.english: One of these, O foremost of men, for the destruction of Tripura, the celestials gave to Tryambaka, desirous of encounter, even that which, O Kākutstha, which you have snapped.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं द्वितीयं दुर्धर्षं विष्णोर्दत्तं सुरोत्तमैः
समानसारं काकुत्स्थ रौद्रेण धनुषा त्विदम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ dvitīyaṁ durdharṣaṁ viṣṇordattaṁ surottamaiḥ
samānasāraṁ kākutstha raudreṇa dhanuṣā tvidam

translations.english: This second, which is irrepressible, was given to Vişnu, by the chiefs of the celestials. And, O Rāma, this bow belonging to Vişnu, is capable of conquering hostile cities.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा तु देवताः सर्वाः पृच्छन्ति स्म पितामहम्
शितिकण्ठस्य विष्णोश्च बलाबलनिरीक्षया
verses.transliteration:
tadā tu devatāḥ sarvāḥ pṛcchanti sma pitāmaham
śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇośca balābalanirīkṣayā

translations.english: O Kākutstha, equal in energy to the bow belonging to Rudra. Once on a time the deities, with the object of ascertaining the respective prowess of Visnu and the blue-throated one, asked the great-father, foremost of those abiding by truth, reading the intention of the deities, fomented a quarrel between them.

verses.sanskrit:
विरोधे च महद्युद्धमभवद्रोमहर्षणम्
शितिकण्ठस्य विष्णोश्च परस्परजयैषिणोः
verses.transliteration:
virodhe ca mahadyuddhamabhavadromaharṣaṇam
śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇośca parasparajayaiṣiṇoḥ

translations.english: Upon that quarrel breaking out among the deities, there took place a mighty contest capable of making one's hair stand on end, between Vişnu and the blue-throated one, each burning to beat the other down.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा तज्जृम्भितं शैवं धनुर्भीमपराक्रमम्
हुंकारेण महादेवः स्तम्भितोऽथ त्रिलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
tadā tajjṛmbhitaṁ śaivaṁ dhanurbhīmaparākramam
huṁkāreṇa mahādevaḥ stambhito'tha trilocanaḥ

translations.english: Then on Vişņu uttering a roar, Siva's bow of dreadful prowess became flaccid. And thereupon the three-eyed Mahadeva became moveless.

verses.sanskrit:
देवैस्तदा समागम्य सर्षिसंघैः सचारणैः
याचितौ प्रशमं तत्र जग्मतुस्तौ सुरोत्तमौ
verses.transliteration:
devaistadā samāgamya sarṣisaṁghaiḥ sacāraṇaiḥ
yācitau praśamaṁ tatra jagmatustau surottamau

translations.english: Upon the assembled gods with the saints and the Cāraṇas beseeching those two foremost of celestials, they became pacified.

verses.sanskrit:
जृम्भितं तद्धनुर्दृष्ट्वा शैवं विष्णुपराक्रमैः
अधिकं मेनिरे विष्णुं देवाः सर्षिगणास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
jṛmbhitaṁ taddhanurdṛṣṭvā śaivaṁ viṣṇuparākramaiḥ
adhikaṁ menire viṣṇuṁ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāstadā

translations.english: Upon beholding that bow of Śiva rendered flaccid by Vişnu's prowess, the deities with the saints acknowledged Vişņu as the more powerful.

verses.sanskrit:
धनू रुद्रस्तु संक्रुद्धो विदेहेषु महायशाः
देवरातस्य राजर्षेर्ददौ हस्ते ससायकम्
verses.transliteration:
dhanū rudrastu saṁkruddho videheṣu mahāyaśāḥ
devarātasya rājarṣerdadau haste sasāyakam

translations.english: The enraged Rudra of high fame made over the bow along with its shafts to the hands of the Rajarsi, Devarata of Videha.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं च विष्णवं राम धनुः परपुरंजयम्
ऋचीके भार्गवे प्रादाद्विष्णुः स न्यासमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ ca viṣṇavaṁ rāma dhanuḥ parapuraṁjayam
ṛcīke bhārgave prādādviṣṇuḥ sa nyāsamuttamam

translations.english: O Rāma, this bow belonging to Vişnu, capable of conquering hostile cities, Vişnu consigned to Bhrgus' son, Reika, as a worthy trust.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋचीकस्तु महातेजाः पुत्रस्याप्रतिकर्मणः
पितुर्मम ददौ दिव्यं जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ṛcīkastu mahātejāḥ putrasyāpratikarmaṇaḥ
piturmama dadau divyaṁ jamadagnermahātmanaḥ

translations.english: The exceedingly energetic Rcīka made over the divine bow to his son of immeasurable prowess, my sire the high-souled son of Jamadagni.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यस्तशस्त्रे पितरि मे तपोबलसमन्विते
अर्जुनो विदधे मृत्युं प्राकृतां बुद्धिमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
nyastaśastre pitari me tapobalasamanvite
arjuno vidadhe mṛtyuṁ prākṛtāṁ buddhimāsthitaḥ

translations.english: Once on a time, on my sire surcharged with ascetic energy, renouncing the bow, Arjuna, under the influence of unrighteous sentiment, compassed the death of my father.

verses.sanskrit:
वधमप्रतिरूपं तु पितुः श्रुत्वा सुदारुणम्
क्षत्रमुत्सादयं रोषाज्जातं जातमनेकशः
verses.transliteration:
vadhamapratirūpaṁ tu pituḥ śrutvā sudāruṇam
kṣatramutsādayaṁ roṣājjātaṁ jātamanekaśaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, learning of the lamentable and untoward slaughter of my sire, I from ire, annihilated the Kșatryas, springing up afresh by numbers, then bringing under sway the whole earth, I, O Rāma, on the sacrifice being over, conferred it upon the righteous Kasyapa as Daksina.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्त्वा महेन्द्रनिलयस्तपोबलसमन्वितः
श्रुतवान्धनुषो भेदं ततोऽहं द्रुतमागतः
verses.transliteration:
dattvā mahendranilayastapobalasamanvitaḥ
śrutavāndhanuṣo bhedaṁ tato'haṁ drutamāgataḥ

translations.english: Having made this gift, I was dwelling in the Mahendra hill equipped with ascetic energy, when, hearing of your snapping of the bow, I have speedily come hither.

verses.sanskrit:
योजयस्व धनुः श्रेष्ठे शरं परपुरंजयम्
यदि शक्नोषि काकुत्स्थ द्वन्द्वं दास्यामि ते ततः
verses.transliteration:
yojayasva dhanuḥ śreṣṭhe śaraṁ parapuraṁjayam
yadi śaknoṣi kākutstha dvandvaṁ dāsyāmi te tataḥ

translations.english: Do you now, O Rāma, agreeably to the cannon of the Kșatrya morality, take this excellent and mighty bow of Vişņu, that had belonged to my father and grand father. And do you set upon this best of bows an arrow capable of conquering hostile cities. And, O Kākutstha, if you succeed, I shall then offer you combat.-28

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तज्जामदग्न्यस्य वाक्यं दाशरथिस्तदा
गौरवाद्यन्त्रितकथः पितू राममथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tajjāmadagnyasya vākyaṁ dāśarathistadā
gauravādyantritakathaḥ pitū rāmamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing Jamadagni's, words, the son of Dasaratha, in consideration of the presence of his father, said these words in subdued tone,

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतवानस्मि यत्कर्म कृतवानसि भार्गव
अनुरुन्ध्यामहे ब्रह्मन्पितुरानृण्यमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
śrutavānasmi yatkarma kṛtavānasi bhārgava
anurundhyāmahe brahmanpiturānṛṇyamāsthitaḥ

translations.english: O Bhrgu's son, I have heard of the deeds you have performed, resolved on avenging your sire. O Brāhmaṇa, I acknowledge that.

verses.sanskrit:
वीर्यहीनमिवाशक्तं क्षत्रधर्मेण भार्गव
अवजानामि मे तेजः पश्य मेऽद्य पराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
vīryahīnamivāśaktaṁ kṣatradharmeṇa bhārgava
avajānāmi me tejaḥ paśya me'dya parākramam

translations.english: But, O Bhargava, you insulted me abiding by the Kșatriya duties, as pusillaniinous or devoid of prowess. Do you to-day witness my energy and vigour.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा राघवः क्रुद्धो भार्गवस्य वरायुधम्
शरं च प्रतिसंगृह्य हस्ताल्लघुपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā rāghavaḥ kruddho bhārgavasya varāyudham
śaraṁ ca pratisaṁgṛhya hastāllaghuparākramaḥ

translations.english: Saying this, the enraged Rāghava, endowed with fleet vigour, took up Bhrgu's noble bow, together with the shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
आरोप्य स धनू रामः शरं सज्यं चकार ह
जामदग्न्यं ततो रामं रामः क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
āropya sa dhanū rāmaḥ śaraṁ sajyaṁ cakāra ha
jāmadagnyaṁ tato rāmaṁ rāmaḥ kruddho'bravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: And fixing the string upon it he set the arrow. And then Rāma enraged addressed Jamadagni's son, Rāma, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणोऽसीति पूज्यो मे विश्वामित्रकृतेन च
तस्माच्छक्तो न ते राम मोक्तुं प्राणहरं शरम्
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇo'sīti pūjyo me viśvāmitrakṛtena ca
tasmācchakto na te rāma moktuṁ prāṇaharaṁ śaram

translations.english: You are a Brāhmana and through Viśvāmitra, art worthy of my homage. Therefore it is, o Rāma, that I can not let go this life-destroying shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्ययं वैष्णवो दिव्यः शरः परपुरंजयः
मोघः पतति वीर्येण बलदर्पविनाशनः
verses.transliteration:
na hyayaṁ vaiṣṇavo divyaḥ śaraḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ
moghaḥ patati vīryeṇa baladarpavināśanaḥ

translations.english: Which of these shall I reduce to aught, O Rama, Your aerial course, or the merit you have attained through your asceticism of ascending to certain incomparable regions. This wonderful arrow of ours sprung from Vişnu, capable of conquering hostile towns, never hit fruitless, with energy destroying the pride of prowess of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
वरायुधधरं राम द्रष्टुं सर्षिगणाः सुराः
पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तत्र संघशः
verses.transliteration:
varāyudhadharaṁ rāma draṣṭuṁ sarṣigaṇāḥ surāḥ
pitāmahaṁ puraskṛtya sametāstatra saṁghaśaḥ

translations.english: And with the object of beholding Rāma holding that foremost of weapons, there assembled in a body the celestials and the saints, with the great-father at their head.

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव सिद्धचारणकिंनराः
यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च तद्द्रष्टुं महदद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration:
gandharvāpsarasaścaiva siddhacāraṇakiṁnarāḥ
yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca taddraṣṭuṁ mahadadbhutam

translations.english: The Gandharvas and the Apsara and the Siddhas and the Cāraņas and the Kinnaras and the Yakşas and the Rākşasas and the Nagas assembled to behold that mighty wonder.

verses.sanskrit:
जडीकृते तदा लोके रामे वरधनुर्धरे
निर्वीर्यो जामदग्न्योऽसौ रमो राममुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
jaḍīkṛte tadā loke rāme varadhanurdhare
nirvīryo jāmadagnyo'sau ramo rāmamudaikṣata

translations.english: And on Bhārgava's energy having been observed by Rāma bearing that best of bows, Jamadagni's son became bereft of prowess, and Rāma (Parasurāma) kept steadily eyeing Răma.

verses.sanskrit:
तेजोभिर्हतवीर्यत्वाज्जामदग्न्यो जडीकृतः
रामं कमल पत्राक्षं मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tejobhirhatavīryatvājjāmadagnyo jaḍīkṛtaḥ
rāmaṁ kamala patrākṣaṁ mandaṁ mandamuvāca ha

translations.english: And rendered inert in consequence of his energy having been dispelled by Rāma's own, Jamadagna mildly addressed Rāma of eyes like lotus' petals, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
काश्यपाय मया दत्ता यदा पूर्वं वसुंधरा
विषये मे न वस्तव्यमिति मां काश्यपोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kāśyapāya mayā dattā yadā pūrvaṁ vasuṁdharā
viṣaye me na vastavyamiti māṁ kāśyapo'bravīt

translations.english: When formerly I gave away the earth to Kasyapas, he said to me, You must no longer stay in my dominions.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं गुरुवचः कुर्वन्पृथिव्यां न वसे निशाम्
इति प्रतिज्ञा काकुत्स्थ कृता वै काश्यपस्य ह
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ guruvacaḥ kurvanpṛthivyāṁ na vase niśām
iti pratijñā kākutstha kṛtā vai kāśyapasya ha

translations.english: In consonance with the words of my spiritual guide, ever since that time I have never spent three nights together on earth. Even this had been promised by me, O Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिमां त्वं गतिं वीर हन्तुं नार्हसि राघव
मनोजवं गमिष्यामि महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tadimāṁ tvaṁ gatiṁ vīra hantuṁ nārhasi rāghava
manojavaṁ gamiṣyāmi mahendraṁ parvatottamam

translations.english: Therefore, O hero, it behove you not to destroy my course, O descendant of Raghu. With the speed of the mind shall I now wend my way to the Mahendra, best of hills.

verses.sanskrit:
लोकास्त्वप्रतिमा राम निर्जितास्तपसा मया
जहि ताञ्शरमुख्येन मा भूत्कालस्य पर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
lokāstvapratimā rāma nirjitāstapasā mayā
jahi tāñśaramukhyena mā bhūtkālasya paryayaḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, the regions I have conquered by my asceticism do you destroy with that foremost of arrows: let there be no delay about it.

verses.sanskrit:
अक्षय्यं मधुहन्तारं जानामि त्वां सुरेश्वरम्
धनुषोऽस्य परामर्शात्स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु परंतप
verses.transliteration:
akṣayyaṁ madhuhantāraṁ jānāmi tvāṁ sureśvaram
dhanuṣo'sya parāmarśātsvasti te'stu paraṁtapa

translations.english: Even from your handing of this bow I know you to be the chief of the celestials even that eternal one, the slayer of Madhu. Hail to you,

verses.sanskrit:
एते सुरगणाः सर्वे निरीक्षन्ते समागताः
त्वामप्रतिमकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
ete suragaṇāḥ sarve nirīkṣante samāgatāḥ
tvāmapratimakarmāṇamapratidvandvamāhave

translations.english: O vanquisher of foes! And all these celestials assembled are beholding you of unparalleled deeds, and without an antagonist in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
न चेयं मम काकुत्स्थ व्रीडा भवितुमर्हति
त्वया त्रैलोक्यनाथेन यदहं विमुखीकृतः
verses.transliteration:
na ceyaṁ mama kākutstha vrīḍā bhavitumarhati
tvayā trailokyanāthena yadahaṁ vimukhīkṛtaḥ

translations.english: And, O Kākutstha, neither ought I to be ashamed (because of this discomfiture); I have been baffled by the lord himself of the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
शरमप्रतिमं राम मोक्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत
शरमोक्षे गमिष्यामि महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
śaramapratimaṁ rāma moktumarhasi suvrata
śaramokṣe gamiṣyāmi mahendraṁ parvatottamam

translations.english: And it behove, O Rāma to disengage this peerless shaft (from the bow), O you of noble vows; and on your shooting the shaft. I shall repair to that fore most of mountains, the Mahendra.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ब्रुवति रामे तु जामदग्न्ये प्रतापवान्
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमांश्चिक्षेप शरमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā bruvati rāme tu jāmadagnye pratāpavān
rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmāṁścikṣepa śaramuttamam

translations.english: When Jamadagni's son, Rāma, had said this, the puissant and graceful son of Daśaratha, had said this, the puissant and graceful son of Dasaratha shot that excellent arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वितिमिराः सर्वा दिशा चोपदिशस्तथा
सुराः सर्षिगणा रामं प्रशशंसुरुदायुधम्
verses.transliteration:
tato vitimirāḥ sarvā diśā copadiśastathā
surāḥ sarṣigaṇā rāmaṁ praśaśaṁsurudāyudham

translations.english: Then all the quarters became cleared of gloom; and the celestials and saints fell to extol Rāma when he had shot the arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
रामं दाशरथिं रामो जामदग्न्यः प्रशस्य च
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य जगामात्मगतिं प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
rāmaṁ dāśarathiṁ rāmo jāmadagnyaḥ praśasya ca
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya jagāmātmagatiṁ prabhuḥ

translations.english: And that lord, Jamadagni's son Rama, having gone round Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, and honoured (by all), set out (for his own quarters).

verses.sanskrit:
गते रामे प्रशान्तात्मा रामो दाशरथिर्धनुः
वरुणायाप्रमेयाय ददौ हस्ते ससायकम्
verses.transliteration:
gate rāme praśāntātmā rāmo dāśarathirdhanuḥ
varuṇāyāprameyāya dadau haste sasāyakam

translations.english: When Rāma had departed, Dasaratha's son the illustrious Rāma, of serene soul, made over the bow to the hands of Varuna of immeasurable strength.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्य ततो रामो वसिष्ठ प्रमुखानृषीन्
पितरं विह्वलं दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
abhivādya tato rāmo vasiṣṭha pramukhānṛṣīn
pitaraṁ vihvalaṁ dṛṣṭvā provāca raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: Then saluting the saints headed by Vasiștha, Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, seeing his son stupefied, addressed him, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
जामदग्न्यो गतो रामः प्रयातु चतुरङ्गिणी
अयोध्याभिमुखी सेना त्वया नाथेन पालिता
verses.transliteration:
jāmadagnyo gato rāmaḥ prayātu caturaṅgiṇī
ayodhyābhimukhī senā tvayā nāthena pālitā

translations.english: Now that Jamadagni's son has gone away, let the fourfold forces maintained by you as their lord, march in the direction of Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दशरथः सुतम्
बाहुभ्यां संपरिष्वज्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā rājā daśarathaḥ sutam
bāhubhyāṁ saṁpariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya rāghavam

translations.english: Hearing Rama's words, king Dasaratha embraced his son with his arms, and smelt Rāghava's crown; and hearing that Rāma had gone, the monarch became exceedingly delighted, and considered himself and his son as having attained a second birth.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च सुमध्यमा
वधूप्रतिग्रहे युक्ता याश्चान्या राजयोषितः
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā
vadhūpratigrahe yuktā yāścānyā rājayoṣitaḥ

translations.english: And entertained by his own relatives with all objects of enjoyment, the monarch rejoiced exceedingly. And Kausalya and Sumitră and the slender waisted Kaikeyi, together with other wives of the king, were busy, receiving the brides, with the necessary ceremonies.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांश्च सर्वा राजसुतास्तदा
रेमिरे मुदिताः सर्वा भर्तृभिः सहिता रहः
verses.transliteration:
abhivādyābhivādyāṁśca sarvā rājasutāstadā
remire muditāḥ sarvā bhartṛbhiḥ sahitā rahaḥ

translations.english: And the royal spouses received the exalted Sītā and the famous Urmilā and both the daughters of Kusadhvaya, graced with silken apparel, with homas performed and blessings invoked, on their behalf. And having paid reverence at the abodes of the gods, and rendered homage to those that deserved the same, the daughters of the kings, well pleased, in private, took joy with all the brothers.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतदाराः कृतास्त्राश्च सधनाः ससुहृज्जनाः
शुश्रूषमाणाः पितरं वर्तयन्ति नरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtadārāḥ kṛtāstrāśca sadhanāḥ sasuhṛjjanāḥ
śuśrūṣamāṇāḥ pitaraṁ vartayanti nararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And having attained brides, and arms, with wealth and friends, those foremost of men, engaged in ministering to their father.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामतियशा लोके रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तरः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmatiyaśā loke rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
svayambhūriva bhūtānāṁ babhūva guṇavattaraḥ

translations.english: Rāma having truth for prowess, by virtue of his excellence appeared to everyone the most meritorious of (Dasaratha's son) like to the self create Himself to all being.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्तु सीतया सार्धं विजहार बहूनृतून्
मनस्वी तद्गतस्तस्या नित्यं हृदि समर्पितः
verses.transliteration:
rāmastu sītayā sārdhaṁ vijahāra bahūnṛtūn
manasvī tadgatastasyā nityaṁ hṛdi samarpitaḥ

translations.english: In the company of Sītā, the wise Rāma, bending his mind to Sītā, with his heart dedicated to her, passed many a season in delight.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रिया तु सीता रामस्य दाराः पितृकृता इति
गुणाद्रूपगुणाच्चापि प्रीतिर्भूयो व्यवर्धत
verses.transliteration:
priyā tu sītā rāmasya dārāḥ pitṛkṛtā iti
guṇādrūpaguṇāccāpi prītirbhūyo vyavardhata

translations.english: Rāma's beloved Sītā, as having been bestowed upon him by his sire, by her loveliness, and her perfections as much as by her loveliness, went on enhancing his joy. And her lord came to exercise a double influence on her heart.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य भूयो विशेषेण मैथिली जनकात्मजा
देवताभिः समा रूपे सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी
verses.transliteration:
tasya bhūyo viśeṣeṇa maithilī janakātmajā
devatābhiḥ samā rūpe sītā śrīriva rūpiṇī

translations.english: And by her own heart, the daughter of Janaka, Mithila's lord, resembling a goddess in grace, and like to Śrī (goddess of wealth) herself in loveliness, completely read his inmost sentiments.

verses.sanskrit:
तया स राजर्षिसुतोऽभिरामया; समेयिवानुत्तमराजकन्यया
अतीव रामः शुशुभेऽतिकामया; विभुः श्रिया विष्णुरिवामरेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tayā sa rājarṣisuto'bhirāmayā; sameyivānuttamarājakanyayā
atīva rāmaḥ śuśubhe'tikāmayā; vibhuḥ śriyā viṣṇurivāmareśvaraḥ

translations.english: And experiencing delight, Rama, receiving the Rājarși's daughter, exercising her own will the excellent princess-looked graceful, even like the lord Vişņu the chief of celestials on being joined with Śrī. BĀLAKĀŅDA

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्र न्यवसद्भ्रात्रा सह सत्कारसत्कृतः
मातुलेनाश्वपतिना पुत्रस्नेहेन लालितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatra nyavasadbhrātrā saha satkārasatkṛtaḥ
mātulenāśvapatinā putrasnehena lālitaḥ

translations.english: And there he abode with his brother, being ministered to in very respect and tended by his maternal uncle, Aśvapati, with all the fondness of a father (with the fondness shown to a son).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रापि निवसन्तौ तौ तर्प्यमाणौ च कामतः
भ्रातरौ स्मरतां वीरौ वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्
verses.transliteration:
tatrāpi nivasantau tau tarpyamāṇau ca kāmataḥ
bhrātarau smaratāṁ vīrau vṛddhaṁ daśarathaṁ nṛpam

translations.english: Albeit thus staying, with every ministration extended towards them as much as they could wish, yet those heroic brothers failed not to remember the aged king Daſaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
राजापि तौ महातेजाः सस्मार प्रोषितौ सुतौ
उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ महेन्द्रवरुणोपमौ
verses.transliteration:
rājāpi tau mahātejāḥ sasmāra proṣitau sutau
ubhau bharataśatrughnau mahendravaruṇopamau

translations.english: And the puissant king also on his pare remembered his sons away from home, Bharata and Śatrughna, resembling the mighty Indra and Varuna.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्व एव तु तस्येष्टाश्चत्वारः पुरुषर्षभाः
स्वशरीराद्विनिर्वृत्ताश्चत्वार इव बाहवः
verses.transliteration:
sarva eva tu tasyeṣṭāścatvāraḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
svaśarīrādvinirvṛttāścatvāra iva bāhavaḥ

translations.english: All those four chiefs of men were dear to him even as four hands issuing from his own body.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामपि महातेजा रामो रतिकरः पितुः
स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तरः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmapi mahātejā rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ
svayambhūriva bhūtānāṁ babhūva guṇavattaraḥ

translations.english: Yet among them all, that highly energetic. Rāma was the favourite of his sire. He was the foremost of in every virtue, like to Svayambhu's (Brahmā) self in the esteem of creation.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं च भाषते
उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
sa hi nityaṁ praśāntātmā mṛdupūrvaṁ ca bhāṣate
ucyamāno'pi paruṣaṁ nottaraṁ pratipadyate

translations.english: He was aye of quiescent soul; and always precluded his speech with an amiable phrase; and although he might be addressed in a harsh manner, yet he returned no corresponding reply.

verses.sanskrit:
कथंचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति
न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁcidupakāreṇa kṛtenaikena tuṣyati
na smaratyapakārāṇāṁ śatamapyātmavattayā

translations.english: He was gratified even with a solitary instance of benefit; and from freedom of soul did not remember an hundred injuries.

verses.sanskrit:
शीलवृद्धैर्ज्ञानवृद्धैर्वयोवृद्धैश्च सज्जनैः
कथयन्नास्त वै नित्यमस्त्रयोग्यान्तरेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
śīlavṛddhairjñānavṛddhairvayovṛddhaiśca sajjanaiḥ
kathayannāsta vai nityamastrayogyāntareṣvapi

translations.english: In the intervals of martial exercises, he always discoursed with persons of character, or wise men, or the aged, or the virtuous.

verses.sanskrit:
कल्याणाभिजनः साधुरदीनः सत्यवागृजुः
वृद्धैरभिविनीतश्च द्विजैर्धर्मार्थदर्शिभिः
verses.transliteration:
kalyāṇābhijanaḥ sādhuradīnaḥ satyavāgṛjuḥ
vṛddhairabhivinītaśca dvijairdharmārthadarśibhiḥ

translations.english: And he was the spring of all good; and was saintly; and of undisturbed soul; and truthtelling; and candid; and humble towards the aged twice-born ones cognisant of virtue and interest.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मार्थकामतत्त्वज्ञः स्मृतिमान्प्रतिभावनान्
लौकिके समयाचरे कृतकल्पो विशारदः
verses.transliteration:
dharmārthakāmatattvajñaḥ smṛtimānpratibhāvanān
laukike samayācare kṛtakalpo viśāradaḥ

translations.english: He was cognizant of virtue, profit, and interest; had an excellent memory; and was possessed of genius. He was an adept and was well versed in social usages and customs.

verses.sanskrit:
शास्त्रज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च पुरुषान्तरकोविदः
यः प्रग्रहानुग्रहयोर्यथान्यायं विचक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
śāstrajñaśca kṛtajñaśca puruṣāntarakovidaḥ
yaḥ pragrahānugrahayoryathānyāyaṁ vicakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: He was conversant with the scriptures; and was grateful; and could read the hearts of others. He had sagacity to perceive the seasons for duly showing favour or disfavour. are

verses.sanskrit:
आयकर्मण्युपायज्ञः संदृष्टव्ययकर्मवित्
श्रैष्ठ्यं शास्त्रसमूहेषु प्राप्तो व्यामिश्रकेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
āyakarmaṇyupāyajñaḥ saṁdṛṣṭavyayakarmavit
śraiṣṭhyaṁ śāstrasamūheṣu prāpto vyāmiśrakeṣvapi

translations.english: He had attained proficiency in all the scriptures and literary works composed in both Sanskrit and Prakrit. He sought pleasure without sacrificing either interest or morality; and he was never dilatory in duty.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थधर्मौ च संगृह्य सुखतन्त्रो न चालसः
वैहारिकाणां शिल्पानां विज्ञातार्थविभागवित्
verses.transliteration:
arthadharmau ca saṁgṛhya sukhatantro na cālasaḥ
vaihārikāṇāṁ śilpānāṁ vijñātārthavibhāgavit

translations.english: He understood the of those who entertained others. He knew the various heads on which wealth was to be expended. He was skilful in riding and training up horses and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
आरोहे विनये चैव युक्तो वारणवाजिनाम्
धनुर्वेदविदां श्रेष्ठो लोकेऽतिरथसंमतः
verses.transliteration:
ārohe vinaye caiva yukto vāraṇavājinām
dhanurvedavidāṁ śreṣṭho loke'tirathasaṁmataḥ

translations.english: He was the foremost of those accomplished in archery; and was acknowledged among men as an Atiratha. * He led his forces in the direction of the foe; and he slew his enemies; and was accomplished in marshalling the troops. *He who alone vanquishes an innumerable host of warriors is called an Atiratha.

verses.sanskrit:
अभियाता प्रहर्ता च सेनानयविशारदः
अप्रधृष्यश्च संग्रामे क्रुद्धैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
abhiyātā prahartā ca senānayaviśāradaḥ
apradhṛṣyaśca saṁgrāme kruddhairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: He was incapable of being repressed in fight even by the enraged gods and Asuras. He was not given to carping, and had subdued his anger, and he was never elated, or malicious.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं श्रेष्ठैर्गुणैर्युक्तः प्रजानां पार्थिवात्मजः
संमतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वसुधायाः क्षमागुणैः
बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यो वीर्येणापि शचीपतेः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ śreṣṭhairguṇairyuktaḥ prajānāṁ pārthivātmajaḥ
saṁmatastriṣu lokeṣu vasudhāyāḥ kṣamāguṇaiḥ
buddhyā bṛhaspatestulyo vīryeṇāpi śacīpateḥ

translations.english: He did not disregard any creature; he was no slave to the times. That son of the monarch was furnished with such qualities. And he was liked by the subjects as well as by the three worlds. In forgiveness he was like to the Earth; and in intelligence like to BỊhaspati; and in prowess like to the Sacī's lord.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा सर्वप्रजाकान्तैः प्रीतिसंजननैः पितुः
गुणैर्विरुरुचे रामो दीप्तः सूर्य इवांशुभिः
verses.transliteration:
tathā sarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisaṁjananaiḥ pituḥ
guṇairviruruce rāmo dīptaḥ sūrya ivāṁśubhiḥ

translations.english: Furnished with such qualities acceptable to the people as well as gratifying to his father, Rāma looked beautiful like the effulgent Sun surrounded by his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवंवृत्तसंपन्नमप्रधृष्य पराक्रमम्
लोकपालोपमं नाथमकामयत मेदिनी
verses.transliteration:
tamevaṁvṛttasaṁpannamapradhṛṣya parākramam
lokapālopamaṁ nāthamakāmayata medinī
