हन्तेदानीं प्रवक्ष्यामि कैकेयि श्रूयतां च मे
यथा ते भरतो राज्यं पुत्रः प्राप्स्यति केवलम्
verses.transliteration:
hantedānīṁ pravakṣyāmi kaikeyi śrūyatāṁ ca me
yathā te bharato rājyaṁ putraḥ prāpsyati kevalam

translations.english: Ah! O Kaikeyi, consider: Listen to my words, telling you how your son alone will obtain the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वैवं वचनं तस्या मन्थरायास्तु कैकयी
किंचिदुत्थाय शयनात्स्वास्तीर्णादिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvaivaṁ vacanaṁ tasyā mantharāyāstu kaikayī
kiṁcidutthāya śayanātsvāstīrṇādidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Manthara's words, Kaikeyi raised herself a little from her tastefully spread bed, and said.

verses.sanskrit:
कथय त्वं ममोपायं केनोपायेन मन्थरे
भरतः प्राप्नुयाद्राज्यं न तु रामः कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
kathaya tvaṁ mamopāyaṁ kenopāyena manthare
bharataḥ prāpnuyādrājyaṁ na tu rāmaḥ kathaṁcana

translations.english: Do you tell me the means. By what means, O Mantharā, Bharata will gain the kingdom, and in no wise Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तया देव्या मन्थरा पापदर्शिनी
रामार्थमुपहिंसन्ती कुब्जा वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tayā devyā mantharā pāpadarśinī
rāmārthamupahiṁsantī kubjā vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thus addressed by the noble one, the wickedminded Mantharā, envious of Rama's interest, thus spoke to Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
तव देवासुरे युद्धे सह राजर्षिभिः पतिः
अगच्छत्त्वामुपादाय देवराजस्य साह्यकृत्
verses.transliteration:
tava devāsure yuddhe saha rājarṣibhiḥ patiḥ
agacchattvāmupādāya devarājasya sāhyakṛt

translations.english: Formerly during the wars of the gods and Asuras, your husband taking you along, went with the royal saints for the purpose of assisting the king of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
दिशमास्थाय कैकेयि दक्षिणां दण्डकान्प्रति
वैजयन्तमिति ख्यातं पुरं यत्र तिमिध्वजः
verses.transliteration:
diśamāsthāya kaikeyi dakṣiṇāṁ daṇḍakānprati
vaijayantamiti khyātaṁ puraṁ yatra timidhvajaḥ

translations.english: O Kaikeyī, ir Dandaka, situated towards the south, there is the city known by the name of Vaijayanta, where dwelt Timidhvaja, otherwise called Samvara, possessed of an hundred conjurations, and a mighty Asura. That unreproved gave battle Sakra one to accompanied by the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्महति संग्रामे राजा दशरथस्तदा
अपवाह्य त्वया देवि संग्रामान्नष्टचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
tasminmahati saṁgrāme rājā daśarathastadā
apavāhya tvayā devi saṁgrāmānnaṣṭacetanaḥ

translations.english: Then king Dasaratha warred with the Asuras most heroically. And that mighty armed one, O worshipful lady, losing his senses in consequence of wounds received from weapons, was removed from the field by you. In that imminent danger, your husband, sadly cut by weapons, was preserved by you.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वयोक्तः पतिर्देवि यदेच्छेयं तदा वरौ
गृह्णीयामिति तत्तेन तथेत्युक्तं महात्मना
अनभिज्ञा ह्यहं देवि त्वयैव कथितं पुरा
verses.transliteration:
sa tvayoktaḥ patirdevi yadeccheyaṁ tadā varau
gṛhṇīyāmiti tattena tathetyuktaṁ mahātmanā
anabhijñā hyahaṁ devi tvayaiva kathitaṁ purā

translations.english: Thereupon gratified, he, O, you of gracious presence, granted you two boons. Whereupon you did say, 'I shall receive from my lord the boon whenever I shall wish. Thereupon that high-souled one said., 'So be it? I did not know anything about this, O respected one; and it was you who did formerly communicate this (to me.) And it is because I bear affection to you that I have not forgotten it. Now do you forcibly make the monarch desist from installing Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ वरौ याच भर्तारं भरतस्याभिषेचनम्
प्रव्राजनं च रामस्य त्वं वर्षाणि चतुर्दश
verses.transliteration:
tau varau yāca bhartāraṁ bharatasyābhiṣecanam
pravrājanaṁ ca rāmasya tvaṁ varṣāṇi caturdaśa

translations.english: And ask your husband for these two boons, the installation of Bharata, and the exile of Rāma into the woods for fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधागारं प्रविश्याद्य क्रुद्धेवाश्वपतेः सुते
शेष्वानन्तर्हितायां त्वं भूमौ मलिनवासिनी
मा स्मैनं प्रत्युदीक्षेथा मा चैनमभिभाषथाः
verses.transliteration:
krodhāgāraṁ praviśyādya kruddhevāśvapateḥ sute
śeṣvānantarhitāyāṁ tvaṁ bhūmau malinavāsinī
mā smainaṁ pratyudīkṣethā mā cainamabhibhāṣathāḥ

translations.english: Entering the anger-chamber to-day, do you, O daughter of Aśvapati, clad in soiled garment, lie down on the uncovered floor.

verses.sanskrit:
दयिता त्वं सदा भर्तुरत्र मे नास्ति संशयः
त्वत्कृते च महाराजो विशेदपि हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
dayitā tvaṁ sadā bharturatra me nāsti saṁśayaḥ
tvatkṛte ca mahārājo viśedapi hutāśanam

translations.english: You have always been the favourite wife of your husband. Of this I have not the least doubt, For your sake the monarch can enter into a flame.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वां क्रोधयितुं शक्तो न क्रुद्धां प्रत्युदीक्षितुम्
तव प्रियार्थं राजा हि प्राणानपि परित्यजेत्
verses.transliteration:
na tvāṁ krodhayituṁ śakto na kruddhāṁ pratyudīkṣitum
tava priyārthaṁ rājā hi prāṇānapi parityajet

translations.english: He can never anger you, nor can he eye you when angered. For compassing your pleasure the king can renounce life itself.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यतिक्रमितुं शक्तस्तव वाक्यं महीपतिः
मन्दस्वभावे बुध्यस्व सौभाग्यबलमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
na hyatikramituṁ śaktastava vākyaṁ mahīpatiḥ
mandasvabhāve budhyasva saubhāgyabalamātmanaḥ

translations.english: Therefore the monarch can never set aside your word. O senseless lady, do you now reflect upon the strength of your good fortune.

verses.sanskrit:
मणिमुक्तासुवर्णानि रत्नानि विविधानि च
दद्याद्दशरथो राजा मा स्म तेषु मनः कृथाः
verses.transliteration:
maṇimuktāsuvarṇāni ratnāni vividhāni ca
dadyāddaśaratho rājā mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ

translations.english: King Dasaratha will offer you rubies and pearls and gold and gems of various kinds; but do not you bend your heart to them.

verses.sanskrit:
यौ तौ देवासुरे युद्धे वरौ दशरथोऽददात्
तौ स्मारय महाभागे सोऽर्थो मा त्वामतिक्रमेत्
verses.transliteration:
yau tau devāsure yuddhe varau daśaratho'dadāt
tau smāraya mahābhāge so'rtho mā tvāmatikramet

translations.english: Do you, O exalted dame, bring into Daśaratha's recollection the two boons which he had granted you at the time of the war between the gods and Asuras, and you shall not fail to achieve your objects.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा तु ते वरं दद्यात्स्वयमुत्थाप्य राघवः
व्यवस्थाप्य महाराजं त्वमिमं वृणुया वरम्
verses.transliteration:
yadā tu te varaṁ dadyātsvayamutthāpya rāghavaḥ
vyavasthāpya mahārājaṁ tvamimaṁ vṛṇuyā varam

translations.english: And when that descendant of Raghu, raising you will go to bestow the boons, do you then binding him fast by oath, unfold to the monarch the boons, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
रामं प्रव्राजयारण्ये नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च
भरतः क्रियतां राजा पृथिव्यां पार्थिवर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
rāmaṁ pravrājayāraṇye nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
bharataḥ kriyatāṁ rājā pṛthivyāṁ pārthivarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Send Rāma to the forest for nine and five years, and let Bharata, becoming on earth the foremost of monarchs, carry on the Government.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रव्राजितश्चैव रामोऽरामो भविष्यति
भरतश्च हतामित्रस्तव राजा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ pravrājitaścaiva rāmo'rāmo bhaviṣyati
bharataśca hatāmitrastava rājā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Thus banished Rāma will no longer maintain possession of the hearts of the people; and your Bharata with his foes put out, will be the king.

verses.sanskrit:
येन कालेन रामश्च वनात्प्रत्यागमिष्यति
तेन कालेन पुत्रस्ते कृतमूलो भविष्यति
संगृहीतमनुष्यश्च सुहृद्भिः सार्धमात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
yena kālena rāmaśca vanātpratyāgamiṣyati
tena kālena putraste kṛtamūlo bhaviṣyati
saṁgṛhītamanuṣyaśca suhṛdbhiḥ sārdhamātmavān

translations.english: By the time that Rāma returns from the forest, your son, your prudent son along with his friends, securing the hearts of the people externally and internally, will have been firmly established on the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तकालं तु ते मन्ये राजानं वीतसाध्वसा
रामाभिषेकसंकल्पान्निगृह्य विनिवर्तय
verses.transliteration:
prāptakālaṁ tu te manye rājānaṁ vītasādhvasā
rāmābhiṣekasaṁkalpānnigṛhya vinivartaya

translations.english: Now is the time, I apprehend. Renouncing fear, do you forcibly make the monarch remove from his mind his intention of installing Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अनर्थमर्थरूपेण ग्राहिता सा ततस्तया
हृष्टा प्रतीता कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
anarthamartharūpeṇa grāhitā sā tatastayā
hṛṣṭā pratītā kaikeyī mantharāmidamabravīt

translations.english: Having been thus made to accept that for good which was really evil, Kaikeyi, desirous of obtaining the boons, was filled with delight. And at the words of the hump-backed woman, that exceedingly beautiful Kaikeyi experienced the height of surprise, and betook herself to this wrong course, like a mare attached to her young, (springing up after it). And she said to Manthara.

verses.sanskrit:
कुब्जे त्वां नाभिजानामि श्रेष्ठां श्रेष्ठाभिधायिनीम्
पृथिव्यामसि कुब्जानामुत्तमा बुद्धिनिश्चये
verses.transliteration:
kubje tvāṁ nābhijānāmi śreṣṭhāṁ śreṣṭhābhidhāyinīm
pṛthivyāmasi kubjānāmuttamā buddhiniścaye

translations.english: O excellent wench, O speaker of things fair, your wisdom I do not dishonour. In ascertaining the propriety or otherwise of actions, you are the very first of hump-backed women on earth. And ever intent on my interest, you seek my welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमेव तु ममार्थेषु नित्ययुक्ता हितैषिणी
नाहं समवबुध्येयं कुब्जे राज्ञश्चिकीर्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
tvameva tu mamārtheṣu nityayuktā hitaiṣiṇī
nāhaṁ samavabudhyeyaṁ kubje rājñaścikīrṣitam

translations.english: I had not, O hump-backed one, (ere this) apprehended the endeavours of the king. O humpbacked one, there are many deformed, crooked and unsightly women (on earth).

verses.sanskrit:
उरस्तेऽभिनिविष्टं वै यावत्स्कन्धात्समुन्नतम्
अधस्ताच्चोदरं शान्तं सुनाभमिव लज्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
uraste'bhiniviṣṭaṁ vai yāvatskandhātsamunnatam
adhastāccodaraṁ śāntaṁ sunābhamiva lajjitam

translations.english: But you alone down, look beautiful like a lotus bent by the breeze. Your breast weighed down by your hump, is high near the shoulders.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमायताभ्यां सक्थिभ्यां मन्थरे क्षौमवासिनि
अग्रतो मम गच्छन्ती राजहंसीव राजसे
verses.transliteration:
tvamāyatābhyāṁ sakthibhyāṁ manthare kṣaumavāsini
agrato mama gacchantī rājahaṁsīva rājase

translations.english: Your countenance is like the bright moon, Ah! O Manthara, how lovely do you look! Your hips are smooth, and is decked with chains; and your thighs and legs are of large proportions. O Mantharā, O you clad in linen garment, O graceful damsel, with your pair of spacious humps, you go before me like a she-crane.

verses.sanskrit:
तवेदं स्थगु यद्दीर्घं रथघोणमिवायतम्
मतयः क्षत्रविद्याश्च मायाश्चात्र वसन्ति ते
verses.transliteration:
tavedaṁ sthagu yaddīrghaṁ rathaghoṇamivāyatam
matayaḥ kṣatravidyāśca māyāścātra vasanti te

translations.english: In your heart reside all those thousandconjuration's belonging to that lord of the Asuras, Samvara; and besides thousands there are many more. Intelligence and policy and conjuration's reside in your elevated hump resembling the nave of a chariot-wheel.

verses.sanskrit:
जात्येन च सुवर्णेन सुनिष्टप्तेन सुन्दरि
लब्धार्था च प्रतीता च लेपयिष्यामि ते स्थगु
verses.transliteration:
jātyena ca suvarṇena suniṣṭaptena sundari
labdhārthā ca pratītā ca lepayiṣyāmi te sthagu

translations.english: When Bharata has been installed and Rāma gone to the woods, I will, O hump-backed one, furnish your hump with a garland made, O beautiful one, of well melted gold. And when I shall have attained my object and be happy, I will smear your hump with sandal paste.

verses.sanskrit:
परिधाय शुभे वस्त्रे देवतेव चरिष्यसि
चन्द्रमाह्वयमानेन मुखेनाप्रतिमानना
गमिष्यसि गतिं मुख्यां गर्वयन्ती द्विषज्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
paridhāya śubhe vastre devateva cariṣyasi
candramāhvayamānena mukhenāpratimānanā
gamiṣyasi gatiṁ mukhyāṁ garvayantī dviṣajjanam

translations.english: O hump-backed one, I will prepare for your face an excellent tilaka of gold; as well as other ornaments. Wearing elegant apparel, you will go about like a very goddess. With an incomparable countenance challenging the moon himself, you will attain pre-eminence, defying your foes.

verses.sanskrit:
तवापि कुब्जाः कुब्जायाः सर्वाभरणभूषिताः
पादौ परिचरिष्यन्ति यथैव त्वं सदा मम
verses.transliteration:
tavāpi kubjāḥ kubjāyāḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
pādau paricariṣyanti yathaiva tvaṁ sadā mama

translations.english: Even as you serve me, other hump-backed women adorned with every ornament will serve your feet.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रशस्यमाना सा कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्
शयानां शयने शुभ्रे वेद्यामग्निशिखामिव
verses.transliteration:
iti praśasyamānā sā kaikeyīmidamabravīt
śayānāṁ śayane śubhre vedyāmagniśikhāmiva

translations.english: Thus praised by Kaikeyi, as she was lying down on a white bed, like to fire up on the sacrificial dais, Manthară addressed her, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
गतोदके सेतुबन्धो न कल्याणि विधीयते
उत्तिष्ठ कुरु कल्याणं राजानमनुदर्शय
verses.transliteration:
gatodake setubandho na kalyāṇi vidhīyate
uttiṣṭha kuru kalyāṇaṁ rājānamanudarśaya

translations.english: O blessed one, when water has flown out, it is not proper to set up a dyke. Arise. Do your welfare. Show yourself to the king.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा प्रोत्साहिता देवी गत्वा मन्थरया सह
क्रोधागारं विशालाक्षी सौभाग्यमदगर्विता
verses.transliteration:
tathā protsāhitā devī gatvā mantharayā saha
krodhāgāraṁ viśālākṣī saubhāgyamadagarvitā

translations.english: Puffed up with the pride of good fortune, that noble lady of expansive eyes thus encouraged (by Manthara), went with her to the angerchamber. (Having entered the chamber), that exalted lady put off her pearl neck-lace priced at many hundreds and thousands of gold, together with other elegant, beautiful and rich ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हेमोपमा तत्र कुब्जा वाक्यं वशं गता
संविश्य भूमौ कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato hemopamā tatra kubjā vākyaṁ vaśaṁ gatā
saṁviśya bhūmau kaikeyī mantharāmidamabravīt

translations.english: Then sitting down upon the ground, Kaikeyi, comparable to gold, under the influence of Manthara's words, spoke to her, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इह वा मां मृतां कुब्जे नृपायावेदयिष्यसि
वनं तु राघवे प्राप्ते भरतः प्राप्स्यति क्षितिम्
verses.transliteration:
iha vā māṁ mṛtāṁ kubje nṛpāyāvedayiṣyasi
vanaṁ tu rāghave prāpte bharataḥ prāpsyati kṣitim

translations.english: Do you, O hump-backed one, tell the monarch, that I am dead at this place. On Räghava having gone to the forest, Bharata will obtain the earth. I do not require gold, or gems, or repasts; this will be the end of my existence if Rāma be installed.

verses.sanskrit:
अथैतदुक्त्वा वचनं सुदारुणं; निधाय सर्वाभरणानि भामिनी
असंवृतामास्तरणेन मेदिनीं; तदाधिशिश्ये पतितेव किन्नरी
verses.transliteration:
athaitaduktvā vacanaṁ sudāruṇaṁ; nidhāya sarvābharaṇāni bhāminī
asaṁvṛtāmāstaraṇena medinīṁ; tadādhiśiśye patiteva kinnarī

translations.english: Having said these cruel words, and thrown off every ornament, the wrathful dame lay down on the ground having no covering, like a fallen Kinnarī.

verses.sanskrit:
उदीर्णसंरम्भतमोवृतानना; तथावमुक्तोत्तममाल्यभूषणा
नरेन्द्रपत्नी विमना बभूव सा; तमोवृता द्यौरिव मग्नतारका
verses.transliteration:
udīrṇasaṁrambhatamovṛtānanā; tathāvamuktottamamālyabhūṣaṇā
narendrapatnī vimanā babhūva sā; tamovṛtā dyauriva magnatārakā

translations.english: Casting away her excellent garlands and ornaments with her countenance clouded with the gloom of wrath, the King's wife became sunk in thought looking like a sky enveloped in darkness, with the stars hid.

verses.sanskrit:
आज्ञाप्य तु महाराजो राघवस्याभिषेचनम्
प्रियार्हां प्रियमाख्यातुं विवेशान्तःपुरं वशी
verses.transliteration:
ājñāpya tu mahārājo rāghavasyābhiṣecanam
priyārhāṁ priyamākhyātuṁ viveśāntaḥpuraṁ vaśī

translations.english: "To-day it has been fixed to install Rāma, but Kaikeyi has not yet heard of it”, thus thought the monarch. Therefore with the view of communicating the welcome news to that lady deserving of good, (Kaikeyi), that renowned one of subdued senses entered the inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
यदिदं मम दुःखाय शेषे कल्याणि पांसुषु
भूमौ शेषे किमर्थं त्वं मयि कल्याण चेतसि
भूतोपहतचित्तेव मम चित्तप्रमाथिनी
verses.transliteration:
yadidaṁ mama duḥkhāya śeṣe kalyāṇi pāṁsuṣu
bhūmau śeṣe kimarthaṁ tvaṁ mayi kalyāṇa cetasi
bhūtopahatacitteva mama cittapramāthinī

translations.english: I do not know why you have been angry with me. O noble lady, who has reprimanded you, or who has offended you, that, О auspicious one, in this guise you are lying down in dust enhancing my sorrow? And wherefore are you down on the ground, I, who seek your welfare, being yet alive? O you that afflicts my heart, are like one under the influence of a malignant spirit.

verses.sanskrit:
सन्ति मे कुशला वैद्या अभितुष्टाश्च सर्वशः
सुखितां त्वां करिष्यन्ति व्याधिमाचक्ष्व भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
santi me kuśalā vaidyā abhituṣṭāśca sarvaśaḥ
sukhitāṁ tvāṁ kariṣyanti vyādhimācakṣva bhāmini

translations.english: I have skilful physicians whom I have completely satisfied with gifts, they will render you whole. Do you, O angry wench, mention your malady.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य वा ते प्रियं कार्यं केन वा विप्रियं कृतम्
कः प्रियं लभतामद्य को वा सुमहदप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
kasya vā te priyaṁ kāryaṁ kena vā vipriyaṁ kṛtam
kaḥ priyaṁ labhatāmadya ko vā sumahadapriyam

translations.english: Whom do you wish to please; and whom to displease? Who shall to-day receive an welcome office, and who a highly unwelcome one?

verses.sanskrit:
अवध्यो वध्यतां को वा वध्यः को वा विमुच्यताम्
दरिद्रः को भवत्वाढ्यो द्रव्यवान्वाप्यकिंचनः
verses.transliteration:
avadhyo vadhyatāṁ ko vā vadhyaḥ ko vā vimucyatām
daridraḥ ko bhavatvāḍhyo dravyavānvāpyakiṁcanaḥ

translations.english: Do not conceal your thoughts, nor, O noble one, afflict your person. Who, that should not be slain, shall be put to death; and who that should, is to be set at liberty? Who that is poor is to be made rich; and who that is affluent is to be turned into a pauper?

verses.sanskrit:
अहं चैव मदीयाश्च सर्वे तव वशानुगाः
न ते कंचिदभिप्रायं व्याहन्तुमहमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ caiva madīyāśca sarve tava vaśānugāḥ
na te kaṁcidabhiprāyaṁ vyāhantumahamutsahe

translations.english: I and mine are at your command. I dare not cross any wish of yours. Tell me your mind, and I will satisfy you by laying down, life itself.

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्ता सा समाश्वस्ता वक्तुकामा तदप्रियम्
परिपीडयितुं भूयो भर्तारमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tathoktā sā samāśvastā vaktukāmā tadapriyam
paripīḍayituṁ bhūyo bhartāramupacakrame

translations.english: Thus addressed and encouraged, she desirous of saying that disagreeable things with the view of afflicting her lord still more, spoke to him thus.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्मि विप्रकृता देव केनचिन्न विमानिता
अभिप्रायस्तु मे कश्चित्तमिच्छामि त्वया कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
nāsmi viprakṛtā deva kenacinna vimānitā
abhiprāyastu me kaścittamicchāmi tvayā kṛtam

translations.english: O worshipful one, none has wronged or reprimanded me. I have a certain intention, which I wish that you will carry out.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिज्ञां प्रतिजानीष्व यदि त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि
अथ तद्व्याहरिष्यामि यदभिप्रार्थितं मया
verses.transliteration:
pratijñāṁ pratijānīṣva yadi tvaṁ kartumicchasi
atha tadvyāhariṣyāmi yadabhiprārthitaṁ mayā

translations.english: If you will execute that do you then promise to that effect. Then only will I express my desire.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तया राजा प्रियया स्त्रीवशं गतः
तामुवाच महातेजाः कैकेयीमीषदुत्स्मितः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastayā rājā priyayā strīvaśaṁ gataḥ
tāmuvāca mahātejāḥ kaikeyīmīṣadutsmitaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, by his hands placing Kaikeyi's head upon his lap, the mighty monarch, under the influence of passion, smiling fairly, addressed her lying on the ground,

verses.sanskrit:
अवलिप्ते न जानासि त्वत्तः प्रियतरो मम
मनुजो मनुजव्याघ्राद्रामादन्यो न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
avalipte na jānāsi tvattaḥ priyataro mama
manujo manujavyāghrādrāmādanyo na vidyate

translations.english: O you that are swollen with the pride of good fortune, you know that foremost of men, Răma excepted, there live not any that is dearer to me than yourself.

verses.sanskrit:
भद्रे हृदयमप्येतदनुमृश्योद्धरस्व मे
एतत्समीक्ष्य कैकेयि ब्रूहि यत्साधु मन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
bhadre hṛdayamapyetadanumṛśyoddharasva me
etatsamīkṣya kaikeyi brūhi yatsādhu manyase

translations.english: O gentle one, my heart is in what I say. Do you, considering this, deliver me from this distress. Taking all this into consideration, do you, O Kaikeyi, speak out what is in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
बलमात्मनि पश्यन्ती न मां शङ्कितुमर्हसि
करिष्यामि तव प्रीतिं सुकृतेनापि ते शपे
verses.transliteration:
balamātmani paśyantī na māṁ śaṅkitumarhasi
kariṣyāmi tava prītiṁ sukṛtenāpi te śape

translations.english: You see the power you wield in me, therefore it behove you not to fear. I will do your pleasure, by my good deeds do I swear this.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन वाक्येन संहृष्टा तमभिप्रायमात्मनः
व्याजहार महाघोरमभ्यागतमिवान्तकम्
verses.transliteration:
tena vākyena saṁhṛṣṭā tamabhiprāyamātmanaḥ
vyājahāra mahāghoramabhyāgatamivāntakam

translations.english: And delighted at the king's speech, she unfolded that dreadful intention of hers like to the approaching death.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाक्रमेण शपसि वरं मम ददासि च
तच्छृण्वन्तु त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवाः सेन्द्रपुरोगमाः
verses.transliteration:
yathākrameṇa śapasi varaṁ mama dadāsi ca
tacchṛṇvantu trayastriṁśaddevāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ

translations.english: You swear repeatedly, and confer on me a boon. Let the three and thirty deities headed by Indra, hear this.

verses.sanskrit:
निशाचराणि भूतानि गृहेषु गृहदेवताः
यानि चान्यानि भूतानि जानीयुर्भाषितं तव
verses.transliteration:
niśācarāṇi bhūtāni gṛheṣu gṛhadevatāḥ
yāni cānyāni bhūtāni jānīyurbhāṣitaṁ tava

translations.english: Let the Sun, and the Moon, and the Sky, and the Planets, and Night, and Day, and the Cardinal Points, and the Universe, and the Earth, with the Gandharvas and Rākşasas, and the Rangers of the night, and all Beings, and the house-hold gods residing in dwellings, together with all other creatures, know your utterances.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यसंधो महातेजा धर्मज्ञः सुसमाहितः
वरं मम ददात्येष तन्मे शृण्वन्तु देवताः
verses.transliteration:
satyasaṁdho mahātejā dharmajñaḥ susamāhitaḥ
varaṁ mama dadātyeṣa tanme śṛṇvantu devatāḥ

translations.english: Let all the deities hear that a highly energetic one speaking the truth, and pure, and cognizant of morality, and abiding by his promise, has conferred on me a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
इति देवी महेष्वासं परिगृह्याभिशस्य च
ततः परमुवाचेदं वरदं काममोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
iti devī maheṣvāsaṁ parigṛhyābhiśasya ca
tataḥ paramuvācedaṁ varadaṁ kāmamohitam

translations.english: Having entreated the monarch thus with a view to prevent him from swerving, and keeping him firm in his promise, she again addressed that mighty bowman, overcome by desire, who was ready to confer on her a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
वरौ यौ मे त्वया देव तदा दत्तौ महीपते
तौ तावदहमद्यैव वक्ष्यामि शृणु मे वचः
verses.transliteration:
varau yau me tvayā deva tadā dattau mahīpate
tau tāvadahamadyaiva vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vacaḥ

translations.english: Thereafter she thus spoke to the king about to confer a boon, who was under the influence of passion, saying, Of the boons that you had then promised me, I shall speak to-day: do you listen to my words. Preparations are being made for installing Rāghava. Do you with the provisions made ready install Bharata in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
नव पञ्च च वर्षाणि दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः
चीराजिनजटाधारी रामो भवतु तापसः
verses.transliteration:
nava pañca ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyamāśritaḥ
cīrājinajaṭādhārī rāmo bhavatu tāpasaḥ

translations.english: Let the gentle Rāma, clad in deer-skin, lead the life of a mendicant in the Dandaka forest for the space of nine and five years. And let Bharata gain the heir-apparentship rid of thorns.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतो भजतामद्य यौवराज्यमकण्टकम्
अद्य चैव हि पश्येयं प्रयान्तं राघवं वने
verses.transliteration:
bharato bhajatāmadya yauvarājyamakaṇṭakam
adya caiva hi paśyeyaṁ prayāntaṁ rāghavaṁ vane

translations.english: Even this in my prime wish; and I beseech you but to grant the boon you have already promised. Even this very day will I see Rāma despatched to the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः श्रुत्वा महाराजः कैकेय्या दारुणं वचः
व्यथितो विक्लवश्चैव व्याघ्रीं दृष्ट्वा यथा मृगः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śrutvā mahārājaḥ kaikeyyā dāruṇaṁ vacaḥ
vyathito viklavaścaiva vyāghrīṁ dṛṣṭvā yathā mṛgaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Kaikeyi's fell speech, the monarch bewailed for a time, and then thought.

verses.sanskrit:
असंवृतायामासीनो जगत्यां दीर्घमुच्छ्वसन्
अहो धिगिति सामर्षो वाचमुक्त्वा नराधिपः
मोहमापेदिवान्भूयः शोकोपहतचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
asaṁvṛtāyāmāsīno jagatyāṁ dīrghamucchvasan
aho dhigiti sāmarṣo vācamuktvā narādhipaḥ
mohamāpedivānbhūyaḥ śokopahatacetanaḥ

translations.english: And pained and woebegone, like to a deer at the sight of a tigress, he fetched a deep sigh, and sat down on the uncovered ground. Like a venomous snake confined by power of incantation within a circle, the lord of men, in indignation exclaimed. “O fie!" And deprived of his senses by grief, he again swooned away.

verses.sanskrit:
चिरेण तु नृपः संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य सुदुःखितः
कैकेयीमब्रवीत्क्रुद्धः प्रदहन्निव चक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
cireṇa tu nṛpaḥ saṁjñāṁ pratilabhya suduḥkhitaḥ
kaikeyīmabravītkruddhaḥ pradahanniva cakṣuṣā

translations.english: After a long while, regaining his senses, he extremely aggrieved, wrathfully, and as if burning in energy, addressed Kaikeyi, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
नृशंसे दुष्टचारित्रे कुलस्यास्य विनाशिनि
किं कृतं तव रामेण पापे पापं मयापि वा
verses.transliteration:
nṛśaṁse duṣṭacāritre kulasyāsya vināśini
kiṁ kṛtaṁ tava rāmeṇa pāpe pāpaṁ mayāpi vā

translations.english: You cruel one! You of vile ways! You destroyer of this race! O wicked woman, what has been done by Räma to you; or what wrong have I done you?

verses.sanskrit:
सदा ते जननी तुल्यां वृत्तिं वहति राघवः
तस्यैव त्वमनर्थाय किंनिमित्तमिहोद्यता
verses.transliteration:
sadā te jananī tulyāṁ vṛttiṁ vahati rāghavaḥ
tasyaiva tvamanarthāya kiṁnimittamihodyatā

translations.english: Rāghava ever serve you as a mother. Why you are then bent upon wronging him?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं मयात्मविनाशाय भवनं स्वं प्रवेशिता
अविज्ञानान्नृपसुता व्याली तीक्ष्णविषा यथा
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ mayātmavināśāya bhavanaṁ svaṁ praveśitā
avijñānānnṛpasutā vyālī tīkṣṇaviṣā yathā

translations.english: It is to bring down destruction upon myself that through ignorance I brought to this house you like to a serpent of virulent poison.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवलोको यदा सर्वो रामस्येह गुणस्तवम्
अपराधं कमुद्दिश्य त्यक्ष्यामीष्टमहं सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
jīvaloko yadā sarvo rāmasyeha guṇastavam
aparādhaṁ kamuddiśya tyakṣyāmīṣṭamahaṁ sutam

translations.english: When all men show their regard for Rāma's virtues, for what transgression shall I forsake my dear son?

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यां वा सुमित्रां वा त्यजेयमपि वा श्रियम्
जीवितं वात्मनो रामं न त्वेव पितृवत्सलम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāṁ vā sumitrāṁ vā tyajeyamapi vā śriyam
jīvitaṁ vātmano rāmaṁ na tveva pitṛvatsalam

translations.english: I may renounce Kausalyā or Sumitrā or the kingdom, or life itself; but Rāma, filled with affection for his father, will I not renounce.

verses.sanskrit:
परा भवति मे प्रीतिर्दृष्ट्वा तनयमग्रजम्
अपश्यतस्तु मे रामं नष्टा भवति चेतना
verses.transliteration:
parā bhavati me prītirdṛṣṭvā tanayamagrajam
apaśyatastu me rāmaṁ naṣṭā bhavati cetanā

translations.english: I experience supreme delight on beholding my first-born and when I see him not, I lose my senses.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठेल्लोको विना सूर्यं सस्यं वा सलिलं विना
न तु रामं विना देहे तिष्ठेत्तु मम जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭhelloko vinā sūryaṁ sasyaṁ vā salilaṁ vinā
na tu rāmaṁ vinā dehe tiṣṭhettu mama jīvitam

translations.english: The world may exist without the Sun; and corn without water; but this life does not exist in this body without Räma.

verses.sanskrit:
तदलं त्यज्यतामेष निश्चयः पापनिश्चये
अपि ते चरणौ मूर्ध्ना स्पृशाम्येष प्रसीद मे
verses.transliteration:
tadalaṁ tyajyatāmeṣa niścayaḥ pāpaniścaye
api te caraṇau mūrdhnā spṛśāmyeṣa prasīda me

translations.english: Do you then that entertains unrighteous aims, abandon this intention of yours. I lay my head at your feet. Be propitious to me. Why does you, O sinful one, cherish in your mind such a frightful idea?

verses.sanskrit:
स भूमिपालो विलपन्ननाथव;त्स्त्रिया गृहीतो हृदयेऽतिमात्रता
पपात देव्याश्चरणौ प्रसारिता;वुभावसंस्पृश्य यथातुरस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūmipālo vilapannanāthava;tstriyā gṛhīto hṛdaye'timātratā
papāta devyāścaraṇau prasāritā;vubhāvasaṁspṛśya yathāturastathā

translations.english: As bewailing thus like one forlorn the ruler of earth whose heart was captivated by Kaikeyi on account of her supreme beauty proceeded to take hold of her feet, who having banished all self respect, sat with her legs stretched, he, without being able to come at them, fell down in a swoon, like one enfeebled with disease.

verses.sanskrit:
अतदर्हं महाराजं शयानमतथोचितम्
ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकात्परिच्युतम्
verses.transliteration:
atadarhaṁ mahārājaṁ śayānamatathocitam
yayātimiva puṇyānte devalokātparicyutam

translations.english: Then as the mighty king was lying down in this unbeseeming and improper guise, like Yayāti dropped from the celestial, that lady, personating the ruin of the race, not fearing public odium, who had discerned danger from Rāma to Bharata, not having attained her wish, again addressed the monarch, concerning the boon he had promised to her.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं कत्थसे महाराज सत्यवादी दृढव्रतः
मम चेमं वरं कस्माद्विधारयितुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ katthase mahārāja satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ
mama cemaṁ varaṁ kasmādvidhārayitumicchasi

translations.english: You describe yourself, O mighty monarch, as speaking the truth and firm in vow. Why then do you hesitate to confer this boon on me?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु कैकेय्या राजा दशरथस्तदा
प्रत्युवाच ततः क्रुद्धो मुहूर्तं विह्वलन्निव
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu kaikeyyā rājā daśarathastadā
pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtaṁ vihvalanniva

translations.english: Thus addressed by Kaikeyi king Dasaratha, remaining stupefied for a while thus answered her in wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
मृते मयि गते रामे वनं मनुजपुंगवे
हन्तानार्ये ममामित्रे रामः प्रव्राजितो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
mṛte mayi gate rāme vanaṁ manujapuṁgave
hantānārye mamāmitre rāmaḥ pravrājito vanam

translations.english: O ignoble one! O enemy of mine! On my being dead and that chief of men, Rāma, repairing to the woods, do you, yours wish attained, become happy.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि सत्यं ब्रवीम्येतत्तदसत्यं भविष्यति
अकीर्तिरतुला लोके ध्रुवं परिभवश्च मे
verses.transliteration:
yadi satyaṁ bravīmyetattadasatyaṁ bhaviṣyati
akīrtiratulā loke dhruvaṁ paribhavaśca me

translations.english: If I shall truthfully say I have sent Rāma to the woods for compassing Kaikeyi's pleasure, that will count for a falsehood.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा विलपतस्तस्य परिभ्रमितचेतसः
अस्तमभ्यगमत्सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
tathā vilapatastasya paribhramitacetasaḥ
astamabhyagamatsūryo rajanī cābhyavartata

translations.english: As king Dasaratha was bewailing thus with a heart wrought up with grief, the sun set and night came on.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्रियामा तथार्तस्य चन्द्रमण्डलमण्डिता
राज्ञो विलपमानस्य न व्यभासत शर्वरी
verses.transliteration:
sa triyāmā tathārtasya candramaṇḍalamaṇḍitā
rājño vilapamānasya na vyabhāsata śarvarī

translations.english: But although crested with the lunar disc, the night failed to bring comfort to the king, distressed, and indulging in grief.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैवोष्णं विनिःश्वस्य वृद्धो दशरथो नृपः
विललापार्तवद्दुःखं गगनासक्तलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
tathaivoṣṇaṁ viniḥśvasya vṛddho daśaratho nṛpaḥ
vilalāpārtavadduḥkhaṁ gaganāsaktalocanaḥ

translations.english: Then the old king Dasaratha, with his eyes fixed at the sky, sighing hot, lamented in this strain.

verses.sanskrit:
न प्रभातं त्वयेच्छामि मयायं रचितोऽञ्जलिः
अथ वा गम्यतां शीघ्रं नाहमिच्छामि निर्घृणाम्
नृशंसां कैकेयीं द्रष्टुं यत्कृते व्यसनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
na prabhātaṁ tvayecchāmi mayāyaṁ racito'ñjaliḥ
atha vā gamyatāṁ śīghraṁ nāhamicchāmi nirghṛṇām
nṛśaṁsāṁ kaikeyīṁ draṣṭuṁ yatkṛte vyasanaṁ mahat

translations.english: Or do you speedily repair for I do not wish to see the hated and relentless Kaikeyi, who has brought this calamity upon me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा कैकेयीं संयताञ्जलिः
प्रसादयामास पुनः कैकेयीं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rājā kaikeyīṁ saṁyatāñjaliḥ
prasādayāmāsa punaḥ kaikeyīṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Having spoken thus, the kind conversant with the duties of Sovereigns again endeavoured to propitiate Kaikeyī, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
साधुवृत्तस्य दीनस्य त्वद्गतस्य गतायुषः
प्रसादः क्रियतां देवि भद्रे राज्ञो विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
sādhuvṛttasya dīnasya tvadgatasya gatāyuṣaḥ
prasādaḥ kriyatāṁ devi bhadre rājño viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: O noble dame, do you show favour to me, who am of honest ways, who am distressed, who have made myself yours, who have finished his life, and who, in especial, am your king.

verses.sanskrit:
शून्येन खलु सुश्रोणि मयेदं समुदाहृतम्
कुरु साधु प्रसादं मे बाले सहृदया ह्यसि
verses.transliteration:
śūnyena khalu suśroṇi mayedaṁ samudāhṛtam
kuru sādhu prasādaṁ me bāle sahṛdayā hyasi

translations.english: That I have spoken you thus was because, O you of shapely hips, I had been deprived of my senses (through grief). O girl, do you show your favour to me, be generous, be propitious.

verses.sanskrit:
विशुद्धभावस्य हि दुष्टभावा; ताम्रेक्षणस्याश्रुकलस्य राज्ञः
श्रुत्वा विचित्रं करुणं विलापं; भर्तुर्नृशंसा न चकार वाक्यम्
verses.transliteration:
viśuddhabhāvasya hi duṣṭabhāvā; tāmrekṣaṇasyāśrukalasya rājñaḥ
śrutvā vicitraṁ karuṇaṁ vilāpaṁ; bharturnṛśaṁsā na cakāra vākyam

translations.english: Having heard the exceedingly piteous words of her husband, the king of pure sentiment, who was distressed, with his eye rendered coppery and flowing with tears, that wicked minded and merciless woman spoke not.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स राजा पुनरेव मूर्छितः; प्रियामतुष्टां प्रतिकूलभाषिणीम्
समीक्ष्य पुत्रस्य विवासनं प्रति; क्षितौ विसंज्ञो निपपात दुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa rājā punareva mūrchitaḥ; priyāmatuṣṭāṁ pratikūlabhāṣiṇīm
samīkṣya putrasya vivāsanaṁ prati; kṣitau visaṁjño nipapāta duḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat seeing that his favourite dissatisfied wife persisted in urging the banishment of his son, the king struck with grief, again fell down to the earth, senseless.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रशोकार्दितं पापा विसंज्ञं पतितं भुवि
विवेष्टमानमुदीक्ष्य सैक्ष्वाकमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
putraśokārditaṁ pāpā visaṁjñaṁ patitaṁ bhuvi
viveṣṭamānamudīkṣya saikṣvākamidamabravīt

translations.english: Then that sinful woman, seeing the descendant of Ikşvāku distressed on account of his son, and deprived of consciousness, and lying inert on the ground, spoke to him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
पापं कृत्वेव किमिदं मम संश्रुत्य संश्रवम्
शेषे क्षितितले सन्नः स्थित्यां स्थातुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
pāpaṁ kṛtveva kimidaṁ mama saṁśrutya saṁśravam
śeṣe kṣititale sannaḥ sthityāṁ sthātuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: Having promised to grant me the boon, how distressed do you lie on the ground, as if you did commit some sin? It behove you to keep untainted your dignity by performing what you have promised.

verses.sanskrit:
आहुः सत्यं हि परमं धर्मं धर्मविदो जनाः
सत्यमाश्रित्य हि मया त्वं च धर्मं प्रचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
āhuḥ satyaṁ hi paramaṁ dharmaṁ dharmavido janāḥ
satyamāśritya hi mayā tvaṁ ca dharmaṁ pracoditaḥ

translations.english: Truth, say persons cognizant of it, is the prime virtue. And it is in the interests of virtue, that I have been exhorting you.

verses.sanskrit:
संश्रुत्य शैब्यः श्येनाय स्वां तनुं जगतीपतिः
प्रदाय पक्षिणो राजञ्जगाम गतिमुत्तमाम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁśrutya śaibyaḥ śyenāya svāṁ tanuṁ jagatīpatiḥ
pradāya pakṣiṇo rājañjagāma gatimuttamām

translations.english: Having promised his own person to the hawk, that lord of earth, Saivya, having granted the same to the bird, went the excellent way.

verses.sanskrit:
तथ ह्यलर्कस्तेजस्वी ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे
याचमाने स्वके नेत्रे उद्धृत्याविमना ददौ
verses.transliteration:
tatha hyalarkastejasvī brāhmaṇe vedapārage
yācamāne svake netre uddhṛtyāvimanā dadau

translations.english: In the same manner, Alarka, being asked, plucked out his eyes readily and bestowed them on a certain Brāhmana versed in the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit:
सरितां तु पतिः स्वल्पां मर्यादां सत्यमन्वितः
सत्यानुरोधात्समये वेलां खां नातिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
saritāṁ tu patiḥ svalpāṁ maryādāṁ satyamanvitaḥ
satyānurodhātsamaye velāṁ khāṁ nātivartate

translations.english: And the lord of rivers, having promised, even on occasions of Parvas, does not pass over his bounds for the sake of truth.

verses.sanskrit:
समयं च ममार्येमं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि
अग्रतस्ते परित्यक्ता परित्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
samayaṁ ca mamāryemaṁ yadi tvaṁ na kariṣyasi
agrataste parityaktā parityakṣyāmi jīvitam

translations.english: If you did not fulfil this noble vow, O worshipful Lord, you have made to me, forsaken by you will I even in your very presence renounce my life.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रचोदितो राजा कैकेय्या निर्विशङ्कया
नाशकत्पाशमुन्मोक्तुं बलिरिन्द्रकृतं यथा
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ pracodito rājā kaikeyyā nirviśaṅkayā
nāśakatpāśamunmoktuṁ balirindrakṛtaṁ yathā

translations.english: Thus fearlessly urged by Kaikeyſ the king could not take off from himself the noose (of promise), even as Bali could not take off the noose that had been fixed upon him (by Upendra) at the instance of Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्भ्रान्तहृदयश्चापि विवर्णवनदोऽभवत्
स धुर्यो वै परिस्पन्दन्युगचक्रान्तरं यथा
verses.transliteration:
udbhrāntahṛdayaścāpi vivarṇavanado'bhavat
sa dhuryo vai parispandanyugacakrāntaraṁ yathā

translations.english: Thereupon, the king looked blank, and his heart became agitated, like to a beast of burden moving tortuously when placed within the yoke and wheels.

verses.sanskrit:
विह्वलाभ्यां च नेत्राभ्यामपश्यन्निव भूमिपः
कृच्छ्राद्धैर्येण संस्तभ्य कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vihvalābhyāṁ ca netrābhyāmapaśyanniva bhūmipaḥ
kṛcchrāddhairyeṇa saṁstabhya kaikeyīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Then calming himself with a great effort, the king, as if not seeing Kaikeyi, with his haggard eyes, addressed her, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्ते मन्त्रकृतः पाणिरग्नौ पापे मया धृतः
तं त्यजामि स्वजं चैव तव पुत्रं सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
yaste mantrakṛtaḥ pāṇiragnau pāpe mayā dhṛtaḥ
taṁ tyajāmi svajaṁ caiva tava putraṁ saha tvayā

translations.english: "I do here, O wicked wretch, renounce that hand of yours which I had held with mantras before the sacrificial fire, and I do also renounce along with you own-begotten* your son Bharata. * This is a new coinage rendered necessary for the exigencies of translation. If 'first-born' is justifiable, 'own-begotten,' is also such.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पापसमाचारा कैकेयी पार्थिवं पुनः
उवाच परुषं वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञा रोषमूर्छिता
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pāpasamācārā kaikeyī pārthivaṁ punaḥ
uvāca paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ vākyajñā roṣamūrchitā

translations.english: Then Kaikeyi of vile ways versed in speech, rendered senseless by wrath, again addressed the monarch in harsh language, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थाप्य राज्ये मम सुतं कृत्वा रामं वनेचरम्
निःसपत्नां च मां कृत्वा कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sthāpya rājye mama sutaṁ kṛtvā rāmaṁ vanecaram
niḥsapatnāṁ ca māṁ kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: What words, O king, do you say, comparable to poison or painful indisposition's. It behove you to summon hither your son, the energetic Rāma. Having established my son in the kingdom, and rendered Rāma a ranger of the woods and made myself rid of rivals, I shall attain my end.

verses.sanskrit:
स नुन्न इव तीक्षेण प्रतोदेन हयोत्तमः
राजा प्रदोचितोऽभीक्ष्णं कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa nunna iva tīkṣeṇa pratodena hayottamaḥ
rājā pradocito'bhīkṣṇaṁ kaikeyīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Thus urged by Kaikeyī, the king like to an excellent steed stung by a sharp goad, again spoke to her.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मबन्धेन बद्धोऽस्मि नष्टा च मम चेतना
ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं प्रियं रामं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि धार्मिकम्
verses.transliteration:
dharmabandhena baddho'smi naṣṭā ca mama cetanā
jyeṣṭhaṁ putraṁ priyaṁ rāmaṁ draṣṭumicchāmi dhārmikam

translations.english: I have been bound fast by the ties of virtue, therefore have I lost my senses. I now only wish to behold my beloved eldest son, the righteous Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स राजा तं सूतं सन्नहर्षः सुतं प्रति
शोकारक्तेक्षणः श्रीमानुद्वीक्ष्योवाच धार्मिकः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa rājā taṁ sūtaṁ sannaharṣaḥ sutaṁ prati
śokāraktekṣaṇaḥ śrīmānudvīkṣyovāca dhārmikaḥ

translations.english: Then the graceful and virtuous king, waxing disconsolate, on account of his son, and with his eyes reddened with the effect of grief, seeing the charioteer, said, “This eulogy of your pains me the more."

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रः करुणं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा दीनं च पार्थिवम्
प्रगृहीताञ्जलिः किंचित्तस्माद्देशादपाक्रमन्
verses.transliteration:
sumantraḥ karuṇaṁ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā dīnaṁ ca pārthivam
pragṛhītāñjaliḥ kiṁcittasmāddeśādapākraman

translations.english: Hearing those sorrowful words and finding the lord of earth aggrieved thus, Sumantra with clasped hands went off a little.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा वक्तुं स्वयं दैन्यान्न शशाक महीपतिः
तदा सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रज्ञा कैकेयी प्रत्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
yadā vaktuṁ svayaṁ dainyānna śaśāka mahīpatiḥ
tadā sumantraṁ mantrajñā kaikeyī pratyuvāca ha

translations.english: Seeing the king utterly incapable of speaking any thing personally owing to his heavy sorrow, Kaikeyī, the best counsellor in matters like these, addressed Sumantra with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्र रामं द्रक्ष्यामि शीघ्रमानय सुन्दरम्
स मन्यमानः कल्याणं हृदयेन ननन्द च
verses.transliteration:
sumantra rāmaṁ drakṣyāmi śīghramānaya sundaram
sa manyamānaḥ kalyāṇaṁ hṛdayena nananda ca

translations.english: Sumantra, Bring the beautiful Răma here, I want to see him. Thinking that some good would accrue to Rāma, he was pleased at heart and away he went speedily delighted at the royal mandate. Being asked again by Kaikeyi to hurry on at the time of departure Sumantra thought within himself.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सूतो मतिं कृत्वा हर्षेण महता पुनः
निर्जगाम महातेजा राघवस्य दिदृक्षया
verses.transliteration:
iti sūto matiṁ kṛtvā harṣeṇa mahatā punaḥ
nirjagāma mahātejā rāghavasya didṛkṣayā

translations.english: "Evident it is that the Queen has become impatient to see Rāma's installation and hence is the hurry, and the king will now take rest.' Thinking this the energetic charioteer with great delight, intent on seeing Rāma, issued out of the city like a lake near the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुरस्तात्सहसा विनिर्गतो; महीपतीन्द्वारगतान्विलोकयन्
ददर्श पौरान्विविधान्महाधना;नुपस्थितान्द्वारमुपेत्य विष्ठितान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ purastātsahasā vinirgato; mahīpatīndvāragatānvilokayan
dadarśa paurānvividhānmahādhanā;nupasthitāndvāramupetya viṣṭhitān

translations.english: Having come out of the presence of the king suddenly, he saw the warders, various citizens and great personages sitting at the gate.

verses.sanskrit:
अमात्या बलमुख्याश्च मुख्या ये निगमस्य च
राघवस्याभिषेकार्थे प्रीयमाणास्तु संगताः
verses.transliteration:
amātyā balamukhyāśca mukhyā ye nigamasya ca
rāghavasyābhiṣekārthe prīyamāṇāstu saṁgatāḥ

translations.english: The Brahmana, versed in in Veda, the counsellors, the commanders of military forces and the leading merchants, together with the royal priest, all brimming with joy on account of Rāma's installation, were waiting at the royal gate all night long

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां यथा राज्ये संभ्रियेताभिषेचनम्
तथा जातीयामादाय राजपुत्राभिषेचनम्
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ yathā rājye saṁbhriyetābhiṣecanam
tathā jātīyāmādāya rājaputrābhiṣecanam

translations.english: And all musical instruments, bringing these and all other things necessary for the installation of the descendants of Ikşvāku, in accordance with the king's permission, the panegyrists and other persons were assembled there.

verses.sanskrit:
न पश्यामश्च राजानमुदितश्च दिवाकरः
यौवराज्याभिषेकश्च सज्जो रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
na paśyāmaśca rājānamuditaśca divākaraḥ
yauvarājyābhiṣekaśca sajjo rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Not finding the king present there, they began to speak amongst themselves;, “Who will intimate the king of our arrival? The Sun is up and we do not see the king amongst us as yet. All articles necessary for the installation of the intelligent Rāma are ready."

verses.sanskrit:
इति तेषु ब्रुवाणेषु सार्वभौमान्महीपतीन्
अब्रवीत्तानिदं सर्वान्सुमन्त्रो राजसत्कृतः
verses.transliteration:
iti teṣu bruvāṇeṣu sārvabhaumānmahīpatīn
abravīttānidaṁ sarvānsumantro rājasatkṛtaḥ

translations.english: While they were thus conversing, the charioteer Sumantra, well respected by the king, reached there and spoke to all those persons and the kings the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
गता भगवती रात्रिरहः शिवमुपस्थितम्
बुध्यस्व नृपशार्दूल कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
gatā bhagavatī rātrirahaḥ śivamupasthitam
budhyasva nṛpaśārdūla kuru kāryamanantaram

translations.english: The worshipful night is gone and blessed morn has arrived; arise, Oh! you great king, and perform morning ablutions.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणा बलमुख्याश्च नैगमाश्चागता नृप
दर्शनं प्रतिकाङ्क्षन्ते प्रतिबुध्यस्व राघव
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇā balamukhyāśca naigamāścāgatā nṛpa
darśanaṁ pratikāṅkṣante pratibudhyasva rāghava

translations.english: Brāhmaṇas, commanders and merchants are assembled at the palace gate, desirous of seeing you, do you therefore arise, Oh descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
स्तुवन्तं तं तदा सूतं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रकोविदम्
प्रतिबुध्य ततो राजा इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
stuvantaṁ taṁ tadā sūtaṁ sumantraṁ mantrakovidam
pratibudhya tato rājā idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Perceiving from the voice that it was charioteer Sumantra versed in good counsels, who was thus eulogising, the king rose up from his bed and thus addressed him:

verses.sanskrit:
महाकपाटपिहितं वितर्दिशतशोभितम्
काञ्चनप्रतिमैकाग्रं मणिविद्रुमतोरणम्
verses.transliteration:
mahākapāṭapihitaṁ vitardiśataśobhitam
kāñcanapratimaikāgraṁ maṇividrumatoraṇam

translations.english: Then proceeding a little, Sumantra saw the beautiful palace of Rāma towering like the Kailāsa hill and resembling the abode of Sakra. It was closed with two big panels at the gate way (of which the trap-door was flung open), and adorned with hundreds of terraces, on its top were many idols made of gold, and arches crested with pearls and diamonds; its colour was white as the autumnal cloud and bright as the golden cave of Sumeru.

verses.sanskrit:
स वाजियुक्तेन रथेन सारथि;र्नराकुलं राजकुलं विलोकयन्
ततः समासाद्य महाधनं मह;त्प्रहृष्टरोमा स बभूव सारथिः
verses.transliteration:
sa vājiyuktena rathena sārathi;rnarākulaṁ rājakulaṁ vilokayan
tataḥ samāsādya mahādhanaṁ maha;tprahṛṣṭaromā sa babhūva sārathiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon arriving at this abode filled with wealth, and having its beauty greatly intensified with deer's and peacocks, moving to and fro, resembling the exquisitely splendid palace of the lord of the celestials, that charioteer was extremely enraptured, having the hairs of the body erect.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्रिकूटाचलमेघसंनिभं; महाविमानोत्तमवेश्मसंघवत्
अवार्यमाणः प्रविवेश सारथिः; प्रभूतरत्नं मकरो यथार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
tadadrikūṭācalameghasaṁnibhaṁ; mahāvimānottamaveśmasaṁghavat
avāryamāṇaḥ praviveśa sārathiḥ; prabhūtaratnaṁ makaro yathārṇavam

translations.english: He saw well adorned ministers dear to the king with horses, chariots and elephants; and leaving them all on either side, entered unprevented, like to the marine monster Makara entering the ocean containing many pearls and diamonds, the splendid apartment of the ladies, resembling the clouds that hover over the summit of the Hill Himadri, and having a number of beautiful houses comparing with great celestial cars. as

verses.sanskrit:
स तदन्तःपुरद्वारं समतीत्य जनाकुलम्
प्रविविक्तां ततः कक्ष्यामाससाद पुराणवित्
verses.transliteration:
sa tadantaḥpuradvāraṁ samatītya janākulam
praviviktāṁ tataḥ kakṣyāmāsasāda purāṇavit

translations.english: Sumantra, well versed in legends, after passing by the gateways crowded with people, reached the solitary apartment (of Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र काषायिणो वृद्धान्वेत्रपाणीन्स्वलंकृतान्
ददर्श विष्ठितान्द्वारि स्त्र्यध्यक्षान्सुसमाहितान्
verses.transliteration:
tatra kāṣāyiṇo vṛddhānvetrapāṇīnsvalaṁkṛtān
dadarśa viṣṭhitāndvāri stryadhyakṣānsusamāhitān

translations.english: Having youthful warders, carrying dares and bows, wearing ear-rings, cautious, attentive and devoted and saw (seated at the gate) several old men commanding female warders, mindful of duty, wearing red cloths and excellent ornaments, and having rattans in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
ते समीक्ष्य समायान्तं रामप्रियचिकीर्षवः
सहभार्याय रामाय क्षिप्रमेवाचचक्षिरे
verses.transliteration:
te samīkṣya samāyāntaṁ rāmapriyacikīrṣavaḥ
sahabhāryāya rāmāya kṣipramevācacakṣire

translations.english: They all seeing Sumantra, ever wishing good to Rāma, approach, rose suddenly up from their seats with due respect.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिवेदितमाज्ञाय सूतमभ्यन्तरं पितुः
तत्रैवानाययामास राघवः प्रियकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
prativeditamājñāya sūtamabhyantaraṁ pituḥ
tatraivānāyayāmāsa rāghavaḥ priyakāmyayā

translations.english: Rāma hearing of the arrival of his father's charioteer, ordered him to enter into the apartment, having his father's pleasure in view.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वैश्रवणसंकाशमुपविष्टं स्वलंकृतम्
दादर्श सूतः पर्यङ्के सौवणो सोत्तरच्छदे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vaiśravaṇasaṁkāśamupaviṣṭaṁ svalaṁkṛtam
dādarśa sūtaḥ paryaṅke sauvaṇo sottaracchade

translations.english: He (on entering) saw Rāma resembling Vaiśravaņa, will adorned and seated on a rolled sofa, with a beautiful coverlet on.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थितया पार्श्वतश्चापि वालव्यजनहस्तया
उपेतं सीतया भूयश्चित्रया शशिनं यथा
verses.transliteration:
sthitayā pārśvataścāpi vālavyajanahastayā
upetaṁ sītayā bhūyaścitrayā śaśinaṁ yathā

translations.english: Having his body sprinkled with holy and fragrant sandal of the best kind, red as the blood of a hog; and having by him Sītā with a chowry in her hand, like moon himself in the company of citra.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तपन्तमिवादित्यमुपपन्नं स्वतेजसा
ववन्दे वरदं बन्दी नियमज्ञो विनीतवत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tapantamivādityamupapannaṁ svatejasā
vavande varadaṁ bandī niyamajño vinītavat

translations.english: Whereupon Sumantra, acquainted with decorum, humbly saluted him (Rāma), the conferrer of great boons, and resplendent like the mid-day sun.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राञ्जलिस्तु सुखं पृष्ट्वा विहारशयनासने
राजपुत्रमुवाचेदं सुमन्त्रो राजसत्कृतः
verses.transliteration:
prāñjalistu sukhaṁ pṛṣṭvā vihāraśayanāsane
rājaputramuvācedaṁ sumantro rājasatkṛtaḥ

translations.english: And he well honoured by the king, seeing the king's son seated on the sleeping sofa with a delighted countenance, spoke these words to him with clasped hands.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या सुप्रभा देव पिता त्वं द्रष्टुमिच्छति
महिष्या सह कैकेय्या गम्यतां तत्र माचिरम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā suprabhā deva pitā tvaṁ draṣṭumicchati
mahiṣyā saha kaikeyyā gamyatāṁ tatra māciram

translations.english: Oh, Rāma, great son of Kausalyā, your father and the queen Kaikeyi want to see you; so it behove you to go there without delay.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु संहृष्टो नरसिंहो महाद्युतिः
ततः संमानयामास सीतामिदमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu saṁhṛṣṭo narasiṁho mahādyutiḥ
tataḥ saṁmānayāmāsa sītāmidamuvāca ha

translations.english: Being pleased with these words the mighty hero of great effulgence, honoured his father's behest and spoke to Sītā thus.

verses.sanskrit:
देवि देवश्च देवी च समागम्य मदन्तरे
मन्त्रेयेते ध्रुवं किंचिदभिषेचनसंहितम्
verses.transliteration:
devi devaśca devī ca samāgamya madantare
mantreyete dhruvaṁ kiṁcidabhiṣecanasaṁhitam

translations.english: Oh, darling, doubt there is none that my father, going to Kaikeyi. is parleying with her regarding my installation.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्षयित्वा ह्यभिप्रायं प्रियकामा सुदक्षिणा
संचोदयति राजानं मदर्थं मदिरेक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
lakṣayitvā hyabhiprāyaṁ priyakāmā sudakṣiṇā
saṁcodayati rājānaṁ madarthaṁ madirekṣaṇā

translations.english: Conceiving the king's intention that clever lady, of dark eyes and desirous of doing good to the king, that mother, the daughter of the king of Kekaya, pleased and intent upon king's welfare as will as upon that of mine, is hastening the monarch for my installation.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशी परिषत्तत्र तादृशो दूत आगतः
ध्रुवमद्यैव मां राजा यौवराज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśī pariṣattatra tādṛśo dūta āgataḥ
dhruvamadyaiva māṁ rājā yauvarājye'bhiṣekṣyati

translations.english: Worthy of the meeting at the inner apartment, the messenger has come, and I doubt not that the monarch shall install me to-day as the heirapparent of his throne.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्त शीघ्रमितो गत्वा द्रक्ष्यामि च महीपतिः
सह त्वं परिवारेण सुखमास्स्व रमस्य च
verses.transliteration:
hanta śīghramito gatvā drakṣyāmi ca mahīpatiḥ
saha tvaṁ parivāreṇa sukhamāssva ramasya ca

translations.english: Therefore I shall speedily go hence and see my father. Do you remain and enjoy here the company of your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
पतिसंमानिता सीता भर्तारमसितेक्षणा
आद्वारमनुवव्राज मङ्गलान्यभिदध्युषी
verses.transliteration:
patisaṁmānitā sītā bhartāramasitekṣaṇā
ādvāramanuvavrāja maṅgalānyabhidadhyuṣī

translations.english: Regarded by her husband, Sītā of dark eyes and intent upon her husband's welfare, followed him to the entrance and said.

verses.sanskrit:
स सर्वानर्थिनो दृष्ट्वा समेत्य प्रतिनन्द्य च
ततः पावकसंकाशमारुरोह रथोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa sarvānarthino dṛṣṭvā sametya pratinandya ca
tataḥ pāvakasaṁkāśamāruroha rathottamam

translations.english: And met all his friends assembled at the middle apartment. Then that great son of the king, casting a glance upon them all who were present there to see him and pleasing them with sweet words ascended, like to the thousand-eyed Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
मुष्णन्तमिव चक्षूंषि प्रभया हेमवर्चसम्
करेणुशिशुकल्पैश्च युक्तं परमवाजिभिः
verses.transliteration:
muṣṇantamiva cakṣūṁṣi prabhayā hemavarcasam
kareṇuśiśukalpaiśca yuktaṁ paramavājibhiḥ

translations.english: It had two excellent horses tied to it like to two young elephants, and was of quick motion, resembling that of Indra's chariot carried by his horses.

verses.sanskrit:
हरियुक्तं सहस्राक्षो रथमिन्द्र इवाशुगम्
प्रययौ तूर्णमास्थाय राघवो ज्वलितः श्रिया
verses.transliteration:
hariyuktaṁ sahasrākṣo rathamindra ivāśugam
prayayau tūrṇamāsthāya rāghavo jvalitaḥ śriyā

translations.english: Ascending the car, Raghava, of great effulgence, went speedily on, making (the space) resounded like to the muttering cloud on the sky. He issued out of his abode like the beautiful moon passing through a huge cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
छत्रचामरपाणिस्तु लक्ष्मणो राघवानुजः
जुगोप भ्रातरं भ्राता रथमास्थाय पृष्ठतः
verses.transliteration:
chatracāmarapāṇistu lakṣmaṇo rāghavānujaḥ
jugopa bhrātaraṁ bhrātā rathamāsthāya pṛṣṭhataḥ

translations.english: Lakşmaņa, the younger brother of Rāghava, standing behind him on the car with a splendid Chowry in his hand, began to guard his body.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हलहलाशब्दस्तुमुलः समजायत
तस्य निष्क्रममाणस्य जनौघस्य समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tato halahalāśabdastumulaḥ samajāyata
tasya niṣkramamāṇasya janaughasya samantataḥ

translations.english: And there was caused a great tumult by the crowd gathering around on the issuing out of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स राघवस्तत्र कथाप्रलापं; शुश्राव लोकस्य समागतस्य
आत्माधिकारा विविधाश्च वाचः; प्रहृष्टरूपस्य पुरे जनस्य
verses.transliteration:
sa rāghavastatra kathāpralāpaṁ; śuśrāva lokasya samāgatasya
ātmādhikārā vividhāśca vācaḥ; prahṛṣṭarūpasya pure janasya

translations.english: Rāghava then heard the people coming from different quarters and the well-pleased citizens, talking amongst themselves regarding him in the following strain.

verses.sanskrit:
एष श्रियं गच्छति राघवोऽद्य; राजप्रसादाद्विपुलां गमिष्यन्
एते वयं सर्वसमृद्धकामा; येषामयं नो भविता प्रशास्ता
लाभो जनस्यास्य यदेष सर्वं; प्रपत्स्यते राष्ट्रमिदं चिराय
verses.transliteration:
eṣa śriyaṁ gacchati rāghavo'dya; rājaprasādādvipulāṁ gamiṣyan
ete vayaṁ sarvasamṛddhakāmā; yeṣāmayaṁ no bhavitā praśāstā
lābho janasyāsya yadeṣa sarvaṁ; prapatsyate rāṣṭramidaṁ cirāya

translations.english: This Rāghava going shall obtain through the grace of the king great wealth, and all our desires will be gratified when he will become our governor.

verses.sanskrit:
स घोषवद्भिश्च हयैः सनागैः; पुरःसरैः स्वस्तिकसूतमागधैः
महीयमानः प्रवरैश्च वादकै;रभिष्टुतो वैश्रवणो यथा ययौ
verses.transliteration:
sa ghoṣavadbhiśca hayaiḥ sanāgaiḥ; puraḥsaraiḥ svastikasūtamāgadhaiḥ
mahīyamānaḥ pravaraiśca vādakai;rabhiṣṭuto vaiśravaṇo yathā yayau

translations.english: Like to Vaisravana he began to proceed, being dignified by the horses and elephants going before sending forth great sound, and eulogised in various metres by persons singing his glory, by the panegyrists and by men tracing his noble ancestry.

verses.sanskrit:
करेणुमातङ्गरथाश्वसंकुलं; महाजनौघैः परिपूर्णचत्वरम्
प्रभूतरत्नं बहुपण्यसंचयं; ददर्श रामो रुचिरं महापथम्
verses.transliteration:
kareṇumātaṅgarathāśvasaṁkulaṁ; mahājanaughaiḥ paripūrṇacatvaram
prabhūtaratnaṁ bahupaṇyasaṁcayaṁ; dadarśa rāmo ruciraṁ mahāpatham

translations.english: He saw the courtyard thronged with young and old elephants, horses, chariots, and the high ways crowded all over with people, many pearls and various merchandises.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामो रथमास्थाय संप्रहृष्टसुहृज्जनः
अपश्यन्नगरं श्रीमान्नानाजनसमाकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmo rathamāsthāya saṁprahṛṣṭasuhṛjjanaḥ
apaśyannagaraṁ śrīmānnānājanasamākulam

translations.english: Rāma, having his friends delighted, ascending the car, and viewing the city adorned with pennons and flags and incensed with Dhūpa and Agaru, entered the high way, crowded with people and containing houses coloured as the pale white clouds, and the place between the two rows whereof scented with Dhūpa and Agaru.

verses.sanskrit:
आशीर्वादान्बहूञ्शृण्वन्सुहृद्भिः समुदीरितान्
यथार्हं चापि संपूज्य सर्वानेव नरान्ययौ
verses.transliteration:
āśīrvādānbahūñśṛṇvansuhṛdbhiḥ samudīritān
yathārhaṁ cāpi saṁpūjya sarvāneva narānyayau

translations.english: Having heard benedictions uttered by many in the following strain and paying proper respects to all, he wended his way.

verses.sanskrit:
पितामहैराचरितं तथैव प्रपितामहैः
अद्योपादाय तं मार्गमभिषिक्तोऽनुपालय
verses.transliteration:
pitāmahairācaritaṁ tathaiva prapitāmahaiḥ
adyopādāya taṁ mārgamabhiṣikto'nupālaya

translations.english: Being installed this day do you following in the footsteps of your fathers and grand-fathers cherish and protect us.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा स्म लालिताः पित्रा यथा पूर्वैः पितामहैः
ततः सुखतरं सर्वे रामे वत्स्याम राजनि
verses.transliteration:
yathā sma lālitāḥ pitrā yathā pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ
tataḥ sukhataraṁ sarve rāme vatsyāma rājani

translations.english: You taking the reins of government we shall live more happily than what we were under your ancestors.

verses.sanskrit:
अतो हि न प्रियतरं नान्यत्किंचिद्भविष्यति
यथाभिषेको रामस्य राज्येनामिततेजसः
verses.transliteration:
ato hi na priyataraṁ nānyatkiṁcidbhaviṣyati
yathābhiṣeko rāmasya rājyenāmitatejasaḥ

translations.english: Seek not we earthly comforts or the highest things (in the life to come), if we can only see. Rāma installed in the kingdom issuing out from his father's abode. There is nothing more pleasant to us than the installation of the highly energetic Rāma on the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
एताश्चान्याश्च सुहृदामुदासीनः कथाः शुभाः
आत्मसंपूजनीः शृण्वन्ययौ रामो महापथम्
verses.transliteration:
etāścānyāśca suhṛdāmudāsīnaḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ
ātmasaṁpūjanīḥ śṛṇvanyayau rāmo mahāpatham

translations.english: Rāma, hearing these and other auspicious words from his friends eulogising his own self, went on his way without being moved.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तस्मान्मनः कश्चिच्चक्षुषी वा नरोत्तमात्
नरः शक्नोत्यपाक्रष्टुमतिक्रान्तेऽपि राघवे
verses.transliteration:
na hi tasmānmanaḥ kaściccakṣuṣī vā narottamāt
naraḥ śaknotyapākraṣṭumatikrānte'pi rāghave

translations.english: Rāghava passed away, but not a single person could withdraw his eyes and mind from that best of men.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषां स हि धर्मात्मा वर्णानां कुरुते दयाम्
चतुर्णां हि वयःस्थानां तेन ते तमनुव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣāṁ sa hi dharmātmā varṇānāṁ kurute dayām
caturṇāṁ hi vayaḥsthānāṁ tena te tamanuvratāḥ

translations.english: That righteous one showed mercy to all, old and young, of the four castes, and hence, they were all obedient to him.

verses.sanskrit:
स सर्वाः समतिक्रम्य कक्ष्या दशरथात्मजः
संनिवर्त्य जनं सर्वं शुद्धान्तःपुरमभ्यगात्
verses.transliteration:
sa sarvāḥ samatikramya kakṣyā daśarathātmajaḥ
saṁnivartya janaṁ sarvaṁ śuddhāntaḥpuramabhyagāt

translations.english: And in this way passing by all, and ordering his followers to go back, entered the inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रविष्टे पितुरन्तिकं तदा; जनः स सर्वो मुदितो नृपात्मजे
प्रतीक्षते तस्य पुनः स्म निर्गमं; यथोदयं चन्द्रमसः सरित्पतिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ praviṣṭe piturantikaṁ tadā; janaḥ sa sarvo mudito nṛpātmaje
pratīkṣate tasya punaḥ sma nirgamaṁ; yathodayaṁ candramasaḥ saritpatiḥ

translations.english: That son of the king entering into the presence of his father, all were extremely gladdened and were eagerly expecting his return like to the lord of water expecting the appearance of the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्शासने रामो निषण्णं पितरं शुभे
कैकेयीसहितं दीनं मुखेन परिशुष्यता
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśāsane rāmo niṣaṇṇaṁ pitaraṁ śubhe
kaikeyīsahitaṁ dīnaṁ mukhena pariśuṣyatā

translations.english: Rāma saw his father, seated on a beautiful sofa with Kaikeyi, looking sorry and poorly and with his countenance dried up.

verses.sanskrit:
स पितुश्चरणौ पूर्वमभिवाद्य विनीतवत्
ततो ववन्दे चरणौ कैकेय्याः सुसमाहितः
verses.transliteration:
sa pituścaraṇau pūrvamabhivādya vinītavat
tato vavande caraṇau kaikeyyāḥ susamāhitaḥ

translations.english: And humbly bowing down at the feet of his father first, he saluted Kaikeyi with due solemnity.

verses.sanskrit:
रामेत्युक्त्वा च वचनं वाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणः
शशाक नृपतिर्दीनो नेक्षितुं नाभिभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmetyuktvā ca vacanaṁ vāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
śaśāka nṛpatirdīno nekṣituṁ nābhibhāṣitum

translations.english: Uttering the word "Rāma" only, the poor king with his eyes full of tears could not see him nor could he speak to him.

verses.sanskrit:
तदपूर्वं नरपतेर्दृष्ट्वा रूपं भयावहम्
रामोऽपि भयमापन्नः पदा स्पृष्ट्वेव पन्नगम्
verses.transliteration:
tadapūrvaṁ narapaterdṛṣṭvā rūpaṁ bhayāvaham
rāmo'pi bhayamāpannaḥ padā spṛṣṭveva pannagam

translations.english: Seeing this unforeseen and terrible appearance of the king, like to a serpent trampled under foot, Rāma was exceedingly terrified.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊर्मि मालिनमक्षोभ्यं क्षुभ्यन्तमिव सागरम्
उपप्लुतमिवादित्यमुक्तानृतमृषिं यथा
verses.transliteration:
ūrmi mālinamakṣobhyaṁ kṣubhyantamiva sāgaram
upaplutamivādityamuktānṛtamṛṣiṁ yathā

translations.english: He was dejected and pulled down much with sorrow and penitence. He was sighing hot and hard and his heart was greatly pained. His heart was troubled like the wavy ocean agitating though incapable of agitation, and clouded like the Sun possessed by Rahu, and (that of) an ascetic speaking falsehood.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्त्यकल्पं हि पितुस्तं शोकमुपधारयन्
बभूव संरब्धतरः समुद्र इव पर्वणि
verses.transliteration:
acintyakalpaṁ hi pitustaṁ śokamupadhārayan
babhūva saṁrabdhataraḥ samudra iva parvaṇi

translations.english: Thinking of this unthought of sorrow of the king he became agitated like to the ocean during the course of the full-moon.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयामास च तदा रामः पितृहिते रतः
किंस्विदद्यैव नृपतिर्न मां प्रत्यभिनन्दति
verses.transliteration:
cintayāmāsa ca tadā rāmaḥ pitṛhite rataḥ
kiṁsvidadyaiva nṛpatirna māṁ pratyabhinandati

translations.english: And clever Rāma, intent on his father's welfare, thought within himself:, Why does not the king display joy on my arrival to-day.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्यदा मां पिता दृष्ट्वा कुपितोऽपि प्रसीदति
तस्य मामद्य संप्रेक्ष्य किमायासः प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
anyadā māṁ pitā dṛṣṭvā kupito'pi prasīdati
tasya māmadya saṁprekṣya kimāyāsaḥ pravartate

translations.english: Angry though, he used to express joy whenever he saw me; then why does his sorrow prevail even seeing me to-day?

verses.sanskrit:
स दीन इव शोकार्तो विषण्णवदनद्युतिः
कैकेयीमभिवाद्यैव रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa dīna iva śokārto viṣaṇṇavadanadyutiḥ
kaikeyīmabhivādyaiva rāmo vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Being pressed with sorrow, Rāma of pale countenance, like one miserable, saluting KaikeyI, spoke to her the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्मया नापराद्धमज्ञानाद्येन मे पिता
कुपितस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व त्वं चैवैनं प्रसादय
verses.transliteration:
kaccinmayā nāparāddhamajñānādyena me pitā
kupitastanmamācakṣva tvaṁ caivainaṁ prasādaya

translations.english: Is it not that I committed some offence through ignorance that I see my father angry? Do you propitiate him therefore.

verses.sanskrit:
विवर्णवदनो दीनो न हि मामभिभाषते
शारीरो मानसो वापि कच्चिदेनं न बाधते
संतापो वाभितापो वा दुर्लभं हि सदा सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
vivarṇavadano dīno na hi māmabhibhāṣate
śārīro mānaso vāpi kaccidenaṁ na bādhate
saṁtāpo vābhitāpo vā durlabhaṁ hi sadā sukham

translations.english: Is he subject to any physical or mental disturbance? Oh! happiness uninterrupted is very dear.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्न किंचिद्भरते कुमारे प्रियदर्शने
शत्रुघ्ने वा महासत्त्वे मातॄणां वा ममाशुभम्
verses.transliteration:
kaccinna kiṁcidbharate kumāre priyadarśane
śatrughne vā mahāsattve mātṝṇāṁ vā mamāśubham

translations.english: Has any evil befallen the good-looking Bharata or high-souled Śatrughna? Is it not all well with my mothers.

verses.sanskrit:
अतोषयन्महाराजमकुर्वन्वा पितुर्वचः
मुहूर्तमपि नेच्छेयं जीवितुं कुपिते नृपे
verses.transliteration:
atoṣayanmahārājamakurvanvā piturvacaḥ
muhūrtamapi neccheyaṁ jīvituṁ kupite nṛpe

translations.english: Dissatisfying the king, disregarding his words and offending him, I do not want to breathe for a single moment.

verses.sanskrit:
यतोमूलं नरः पश्येत्प्रादुर्भावमिहात्मनः
कथं तस्मिन्न वर्तेत प्रत्यक्षे सति दैवते
verses.transliteration:
yatomūlaṁ naraḥ paśyetprādurbhāvamihātmanaḥ
kathaṁ tasminna varteta pratyakṣe sati daivate

translations.english: How can a man disregard him who is god himself seen and felt, and who is looked upon as a cause from whom he has sprung.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्ते परुषं किंचिदभिमानात्पिता मम
उक्तो भवत्या कोपेन यत्रास्य लुलितं मनः
verses.transliteration:
kaccitte paruṣaṁ kiṁcidabhimānātpitā mama
ukto bhavatyā kopena yatrāsya lulitaṁ manaḥ

translations.english: Oh mother, have you spoken any harsh word to my father either through anger or through haughtiness for which his mind is thus pulled down?

verses.sanskrit:
एतदाचक्ष्व मे देवि तत्त्वेन परिपृच्छतः
किंनिमित्तमपूर्वोऽयं विकारो मनुजाधिपे
verses.transliteration:
etadācakṣva me devi tattvena paripṛcchataḥ
kiṁnimittamapūrvo'yaṁ vikāro manujādhipe

translations.english: Oh worshipful one, tell me all this, who am exceedingly anxious to get at the real truth. Why has this unforeseen sorrow overtaken the heart of the lord of men?

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि वचनाद्राज्ञः पतेयमपि पावके
भक्षयेयं विषं तीक्ष्णं मज्जेयमपि चार्णवे
नियुक्तो गुरुणा पित्रा नृपेण च हितेन च
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi vacanādrājñaḥ pateyamapi pāvake
bhakṣayeyaṁ viṣaṁ tīkṣṇaṁ majjeyamapi cārṇave
niyukto guruṇā pitrā nṛpeṇa ca hitena ca

translations.english: Oh! shame to me. May it not please you, Oh worshipful lady, to speak such words to me. I can at the king's words jump into the fire. Being ordered by him, who is my father and who is my king especially, I can drink virulent poison and drown into the ocean. Speak you, Oh worshipful lady, what is the desire of the king, and know that I shall carry it out, Rāma does not contradict what he has once spoken.

verses.sanskrit:
तमार्जवसमायुक्तमनार्या सत्यवादिनम्
उवाच रामं कैकेयी वचनं भृशदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
tamārjavasamāyuktamanāryā satyavādinam
uvāca rāmaṁ kaikeyī vacanaṁ bhṛśadāruṇam

translations.english: Then that wicked Kaikeyi spoke these highly cruel words to Rāma, simple and truthful.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे पित्रा ते मम राघव
रक्षितेन वरौ दत्तौ सशल्येन महारणे
verses.transliteration:
purā devāsure yuddhe pitrā te mama rāghava
rakṣitena varau dattau saśalyena mahāraṇe

translations.english: Foremerly in a great war between the gods and Asuras, your father, being wounded with shafts was tended by me for which he conferred upon me two boons.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र मे याचितो राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्
गमनं दण्डकारण्ये तव चाद्यैव राघव
verses.transliteration:
tatra me yācito rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam
gamanaṁ daṇḍakāraṇye tava cādyaiva rāghava

translations.english: Of these two boons I have asked of the king the installation of Bharata, and the departure of Rāghava into the Dandaka forest even this very day.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि सत्यप्रतिज्ञं त्वं पितरं कर्तुमिच्छसि
आत्मानं च नररेष्ठ मम वाक्यमिदं शृणु
verses.transliteration:
yadi satyapratijñaṁ tvaṁ pitaraṁ kartumicchasi
ātmānaṁ ca narareṣṭha mama vākyamidaṁ śṛṇu

translations.english: Oh you best among men, if do you wish to keep your father's vows as well as yours, hear what I say.

verses.sanskrit:
स निदेशे पितुस्तिष्ठ यथा तेन प्रतिश्रुतम्
त्वयारण्यं प्रवेष्टव्यं नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च
verses.transliteration:
sa nideśe pitustiṣṭha yathā tena pratiśrutam
tvayāraṇyaṁ praveṣṭavyaṁ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca

translations.english: Your father is bound to me by promise, obeying therefore your father's mandate, do you repair to the forest for nine years and five.

verses.sanskrit:
सप्त सप्त च वर्षाणि दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः
अभिषेकमिमं त्यक्त्वा जटाचीरधरो वस
verses.transliteration:
sapta sapta ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyamāśritaḥ
abhiṣekamimaṁ tyaktvā jaṭācīradharo vasa

translations.english: Forsaking this installation, do you repair to Dandaka forest for seven and seven years and wear bark and matted hair.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतः कोसलपुरे प्रशास्तु वसुधामिमाम्
नानारत्नसमाकीर्णां सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम्
verses.transliteration:
bharataḥ kosalapure praśāstu vasudhāmimām
nānāratnasamākīrṇāṁ savājirathakuñjarām

translations.english: And here in this Kosala let Bharata govern the world, adorned with many pearls and diamonds, with elephants, horses and chariots.

verses.sanskrit:
तदप्रियममित्रघ्नो वचनं मरणोपमम्
श्रुत्वा न विव्यथे रामः कैकेयीं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tadapriyamamitraghno vacanaṁ maraṇopamam
śrutvā na vivyathe rāmaḥ kaikeyīṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing these unpleasant words like to death, Rama, the destroyer of foes, was not pained, and spoke thus to Kaikeyī.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमस्तु गमिष्यामि वनं वस्तुमहं त्वतः
जटाचीरधरो राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन्
verses.transliteration:
evamastu gamiṣyāmi vanaṁ vastumahaṁ tvataḥ
jaṭācīradharo rājñaḥ pratijñāmanupālayan

translations.english: Be it what you say; carrying out the promise of the king, I shall repair to the forest from this place wearing bark and matted hair.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं तु ज्ञातुमिच्छामि किमर्थं मां महीपतिः
नाभिनन्दति दुर्धर्षो यथापुरमरिंदमः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ tu jñātumicchāmi kimarthaṁ māṁ mahīpatiḥ
nābhinandati durdharṣo yathāpuramariṁdamaḥ

translations.english: Now I want to know only why that lord of the earth, invincible and the conqueror of foes, does not receive me in the same way as he used to do on previous occasions.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्युर्न च त्वया कार्यो देवि ब्रूहि तवाग्रतः
यास्यामि भव सुप्रीता वनं चीरजटाधरः
verses.transliteration:
manyurna ca tvayā kāryo devi brūhi tavāgrataḥ
yāsyāmi bhava suprītā vanaṁ cīrajaṭādharaḥ

translations.english: be not angry, Oh worshipful one, I speak before you, be you propitiated well, and I shall go to the forest wearing bark and matted hair.

verses.sanskrit:
हितेन गुरुणा पित्रा कृतज्ञेन नृपेण च
नियुज्यमानो विश्रब्धं किं न कुर्यादहं प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
hitena guruṇā pitrā kṛtajñena nṛpeṇa ca
niyujyamāno viśrabdhaṁ kiṁ na kuryādahaṁ priyam

translations.english: What is there that I cannot perform, considering it good without suspicion, if I am ordered so by my well-wisher, spiritual leader, father and king, who acknowledges your service (rendered in time of danger).* *The epithet Krtajñena may as well as be rendered into general terms; such as 'who acknowledges services rendered to him.' Here in translation I have followed the commentator who has restricted it to the special sense suitable to the occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहतीव मे
स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्
verses.transliteration:
alīkaṁ mānasaṁ tvekaṁ hṛdayaṁ dahatīva me
svayaṁ yannāha māṁ rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam

translations.english: But this one sorrow burns my heart, why king did not tell me personally of the installation of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि सीतां राज्यं च प्राणानिष्टान्धनानि च
हृष्टो भ्रात्रे स्वयं दद्यां भरतायाप्रचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi sītāṁ rājyaṁ ca prāṇāniṣṭāndhanāni ca
hṛṣṭo bhrātre svayaṁ dadyāṁ bharatāyāpracoditaḥ

translations.english: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at your mandate joyfully make over to Bharata, my kingdom, Sītā, wealth and even my life, thereby satisfying you, and fulfilling my promise.

verses.sanskrit:
तदाश्वासय हीमं त्वं किं न्विदं यन्महीपतिः
वसुधासक्तनयनो मन्दमश्रूणि मुञ्चति
verses.transliteration:
tadāśvāsaya hīmaṁ tvaṁ kiṁ nvidaṁ yanmahīpatiḥ
vasudhāsaktanayano mandamaśrūṇi muñcati

translations.english: Do you now console the bashful king; why has he, with his eyes steadily fixed on the ground, been shedding tears slowly?

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छन्तु चैवानयितुं दूताः शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः
भरतं मातुलकुलादद्यैव नृपशासनात्
verses.transliteration:
gacchantu caivānayituṁ dūtāḥ śīghrajavairhayaiḥ
bharataṁ mātulakulādadyaiva nṛpaśāsanāt

translations.english: Let messengers, with fast going steeds go today at the command of the king to fetch Bharata from his maternal uncle's house.

verses.sanskrit:
दण्डकारण्यमेषोऽहमितो गच्छामि सत्वरः
अविचार्य पितुर्वाक्यं समावस्तुं चतुर्दश
verses.transliteration:
daṇḍakāraṇyameṣo'hamito gacchāmi satvaraḥ
avicārya piturvākyaṁ samāvastuṁ caturdaśa

translations.english: I shall, not even judging the propriety of my father's words, speedily repair to the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हृष्टा तस्य तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा रामस्य कैकयी
प्रस्थानं श्रद्दधाना हि त्वरयामास राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
sā hṛṣṭā tasya tadvākyaṁ śrutvā rāmasya kaikayī
prasthānaṁ śraddadhānā hi tvarayāmāsa rāghavam

translations.english: Hearing those words of Rāma, Kaikeyi was pleased, and being certain about his departure, hurried on Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं भवतु यास्यन्ति दूताः शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः
भरतं मातुलकुलादुपावर्तयितुं नराः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bhavatu yāsyanti dūtāḥ śīghrajavairhayaiḥ
bharataṁ mātulakulādupāvartayituṁ narāḥ

translations.english: Let it be that messengers with fast going steeds shall go to bring Bharata from his maternal uncle's residence.

verses.sanskrit:
तव त्वहं क्षमं मन्ये नोत्सुकस्य विलम्बनम्
राम तस्मादितः शीघ्रं वनं त्वं गन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tava tvahaṁ kṣamaṁ manye notsukasya vilambanam
rāma tasmāditaḥ śīghraṁ vanaṁ tvaṁ gantumarhasi

translations.english: I do not think it proper for you, O Rāma, to delay, when you are so anxious; it behoves you therefore to depart from this place speedily to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
व्रीडान्वितः स्वयं यच्च नृपस्त्वां नाभिभाषते
नैतत्किंचिन्नरश्रेष्ठ मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
vrīḍānvitaḥ svayaṁ yacca nṛpastvāṁ nābhibhāṣate
naitatkiṁcinnaraśreṣṭha manyureṣo'panīyatām

translations.english: The king being abashed, does not himself address you, there is nothing else than this. Do you, Oh best of men, dispel this wretchedness of his.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्त्वं न वनं यातः पुरादस्मादभित्वरन्
पिता तावन्न ते राम स्नास्यते भोक्ष्यतेऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
yāvattvaṁ na vanaṁ yātaḥ purādasmādabhitvaran
pitā tāvanna te rāma snāsyate bhokṣyate'pi vā

translations.english: As long as you shall not hurriedly depart from his presence, Oh Rāma, your father shall not bathe, or eat anything.

verses.sanskrit:
धिक्कष्टमिति निःश्वस्य राजा शोकपरिप्लुतः
मूर्छितो न्यपतत्तस्मिन्पर्यङ्के हेमभूषिते
verses.transliteration:
dhikkaṣṭamiti niḥśvasya rājā śokapariplutaḥ
mūrchito nyapatattasminparyaṅke hemabhūṣite

translations.english: 'Oh fie!' 'what affliction' sobbing hard with these words, the monarch, filled with sorrow, swooned away and fell down upon the sofa, embellished with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
रामोऽप्युत्थाप्य राजानं कैकेय्याभिप्रचोदितः
कशयेवाहतो वाजी वनं गन्तुं कृतत्वरः
verses.transliteration:
rāmo'pyutthāpya rājānaṁ kaikeyyābhipracoditaḥ
kaśayevāhato vājī vanaṁ gantuṁ kṛtatvaraḥ

translations.english: Raising the king up, Rāma, being directed by Kaikeyī, began to hurry on his departure to the forest, like to a steed struck sharp with a whip.

verses.sanskrit:
तदप्रियमनार्याया वचनं दारुणोदरम्
श्रुत्वा गतव्यथो रामः कैकेयीं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tadapriyamanāryāyā vacanaṁ dāruṇodaram
śrutvā gatavyatho rāmaḥ kaikeyīṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing those cruel and unpleasant words of the wicked Kaikeyi, Rama, not being distressed, began to address her with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहमर्थपरो देवि लोकमावस्तुमुत्सहे
विद्धि मामृषिभिस्तुल्यं केवलं धर्ममास्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
nāhamarthaparo devi lokamāvastumutsahe
viddhi māmṛṣibhistulyaṁ kevalaṁ dharmamāsthitam

translations.english: Oh worshipful one, being addicted to wealth do I not long for living in this world; like to Rșis, know me, to be well established in pure religion.

verses.sanskrit:
यदत्रभवतः किंचिच्छक्यं कर्तुं प्रियं मया
प्राणानपि परित्यज्य सर्वथा कृतमेव तत्
verses.transliteration:
yadatrabhavataḥ kiṁcicchakyaṁ kartuṁ priyaṁ mayā
prāṇānapi parityajya sarvathā kṛtameva tat

translations.english: If I can, even at the sacrifice of my own life, satisfy my worshipful father, rest assured it is to be done first in all manner.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यतो धर्मचरणं किंचिदस्ति महत्तरम्
यथा पितरि शुश्रूषा तस्य वा वचनक्रिया
verses.transliteration:
na hyato dharmacaraṇaṁ kiṁcidasti mahattaram
yathā pitari śuśrūṣā tasya vā vacanakriyā

translations.english: There is no virtue greater than the serving of the father and carrying out his words.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुक्तोऽप्यत्रभवता भवत्या वचनादहम्
वने वत्स्यामि विजने वर्षाणीह चतुर्दश
verses.transliteration:
anukto'pyatrabhavatā bhavatyā vacanādaham
vane vatsyāmi vijane varṣāṇīha caturdaśa

translations.english: Even though not commanded by him, I shall, for your words, live in a solitary forest for fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं मयि कैकेयि किंचिदाशंससे गुणम्
यद्राजानमवोचस्त्वं ममेश्वरतरा सती
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ mayi kaikeyi kiṁcidāśaṁsase guṇam
yadrājānamavocastvaṁ mameśvaratarā satī

translations.english: Oh Kaikeyī, certain it is that you are not acquainted with my foremost virtues, inasmuch as possessing full authority to rule me, you have requested the monarch for this.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्मातरमापृच्छे सीतां चानुनयाम्यहम्
ततोऽद्यैव गमिष्यामि दण्डकानां महद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
