tvayā lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau prāṇaiḥ priyatarau mama

translations.english: Should you specially regard Bharata and Śatrughna like to your sons or brothers, who are dearer to me than my life itself.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रियं न च कर्तव्यं भरतस्य कदाचन
स हि राजा प्रभुश्चैव देशस्य च कुलस्य च
verses.transliteration:
vipriyaṁ na ca kartavyaṁ bharatasya kadācana
sa hi rājā prabhuścaiva deśasya ca kulasya ca

translations.english: You should not do, Oh Vaidehī, any such thing as might be unpleasant to Bharata, for he is the king of the land as well as of the family.

verses.sanskrit:
आराधिता हि शीलेन प्रयत्नैश्चोपसेविताः
राजानः संप्रसीदन्ति प्रकुप्यन्ति विपर्यये
verses.transliteration:
ārādhitā hi śīlena prayatnaiścopasevitāḥ
rājānaḥ saṁprasīdanti prakupyanti viparyaye

translations.english: The monarchs are always propitiated by being served with assiduity and good temper; they are offended when any thing contrary to it happens.

verses.sanskrit:
औरसानपि पुत्रान्हि त्यजन्त्यहितकारिणः
समर्थान्संप्रगृह्णन्ति जनानपि नराधिपाः
verses.transliteration:
aurasānapi putrānhi tyajantyahitakāriṇaḥ
samarthānsaṁpragṛhṇanti janānapi narādhipāḥ

translations.english: They renounce even their own son, born of their lions, when they find him bringing about their mischief, and admit into their favour persons devoted to their welfare bearing no relationship whatever.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं गमिष्यामि महावनं प्रिये; त्वया हि वस्तव्यमिहैव भामिनि
यथा व्यलीकं कुरुषे न कस्यचि;त्तथा त्वया कार्यमिदं वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ gamiṣyāmi mahāvanaṁ priye; tvayā hi vastavyamihaiva bhāmini
yathā vyalīkaṁ kuruṣe na kasyaci;ttathā tvayā kāryamidaṁ vaco mama

translations.english: I am going to the forest, Oh my darling, and you shall live here. Oh excellent lady, abide by my word as did you never formerly falsify it.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही प्रियार्हा प्रियवादिनी
प्रणयादेव संक्रुद्धा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu vaidehī priyārhā priyavādinī
praṇayādeva saṁkruddhā bhartāramidamabravīt

translations.english: Being addressed thus, Vaidehi, beloved and sweet speeched, spoke to her husband the following words, offended as it were on account of her great affection.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्यपुत्र पिता माता भ्राता पुत्रस्तथा स्नुषा
स्वानि पुण्यानि भुञ्जानाः स्वं स्वं भाग्यमुपासते
verses.transliteration:
āryaputra pitā mātā bhrātā putrastathā snuṣā
svāni puṇyāni bhuñjānāḥ svaṁ svaṁ bhāgyamupāsate

translations.english: Oh dear husband, father, mother, son, brother, daughter-in-law, all of them abide by the consequences of their own actions, it is the wife alone, Oh best of men, that shares the fate of her husband; it is therefore that ever along with you I have been ordered to live in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
न पिता नात्मजो नात्मा न माता न सखीजनः
इह प्रेत्य च नारीणां पतिरेको गतिः सदा
verses.transliteration:
na pitā nātmajo nātmā na mātā na sakhījanaḥ
iha pretya ca nārīṇāṁ patireko gatiḥ sadā

translations.english: Neither father, mother, son, friends, nor her ownself is the stay of a woman in this or in after life, it is the husband along that is her only support.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि त्वं प्रस्थितो दुर्गं वनमद्यैव राघव
अग्रतस्ते गमिष्यामि मृद्नन्ती कुशकण्टकान्
verses.transliteration:
yadi tvaṁ prasthito durgaṁ vanamadyaiva rāghava
agrataste gamiṣyāmi mṛdnantī kuśakaṇṭakān

translations.english: If do you repair today to the forest impregnable, I shall go before you, oh Rāghava, treading upon the thorns and prickly grass.

verses.sanskrit:
ईर्ष्यारोषौ बहिष्कृत्य भुक्तशेषमिवोदकम्
नय मां वीर विश्रब्धः पापं मयि न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
īrṣyāroṣau bahiṣkṛtya bhuktaśeṣamivodakam
naya māṁ vīra viśrabdhaḥ pāpaṁ mayi na vidyate

translations.english: Confident do you take me with you, Oh great hero, renouncing jealousy and indignation, like to water left after drinking; there exists no sin in me that could justify forsaking.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रासादाग्रैर्विमानैर्वा वैहायसगतेन वा
सर्वावस्थागता भर्तुः पादच्छाया विशिष्यते
verses.transliteration:
prāsādāgrairvimānairvā vaihāyasagatena vā
sarvāvasthāgatā bhartuḥ pādacchāyā viśiṣyate

translations.english: To woman is preferable under all circumstances the shade of her husband's feet to the tops of a palace, the celestial car or excursion in the airy path.* *It was generally believed that by certain processes of Yoga one acquired power to fly in the air.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुशिष्टास्मि मात्रा च पित्रा च विविधाश्रयम्
नास्मि संप्रति वक्तव्या वर्तितव्यं यथा मया
verses.transliteration:
anuśiṣṭāsmi mātrā ca pitrā ca vividhāśrayam
nāsmi saṁprati vaktavyā vartitavyaṁ yathā mayā

translations.english: I have been taught by my father and mother to follow my husband in all conditions of life; and I shall carry out now what I have been taught; I shall not abide by any other counsel.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखं वने निवत्स्यामि यथैव भवने पितुः
अचिन्तयन्ती त्रीँल्लोकांश्चिन्तयन्ती पतिव्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
sukhaṁ vane nivatsyāmi yathaiva bhavane pituḥ
acintayantī trī̐llokāṁścintayantī pativratam

translations.english: Happily shall I live there as if in my paternal house, giving no thought upon the prosperity of the three worlds, thinking only of the services that are to be rendered to my husband.

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्रूषमाणा ते नित्यं नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी
सह रंस्ये त्वया वीर वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु
verses.transliteration:
śuśrūṣamāṇā te nityaṁ niyatā brahmacāriṇī
saha raṁsye tvayā vīra vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu

translations.english: I shall sport with you, O great hero, in that forest impregnated with the fragrance of flowers, tending you constantly, having my senses subdued, and being engaged in austere performances.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि कर्तुं वने शक्तो राम संपरिपालनम्
अन्यस्यापि जनस्येह किं पुनर्मम मानद
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi kartuṁ vane śakto rāma saṁparipālanam
anyasyāpi janasyeha kiṁ punarmama mānada

translations.english: Oh great hero, capable are you to maintain many thousand others in the forest, what of me.

verses.sanskrit:
फलमूलाशना नित्यं भविष्यामि न संशयः
न ते दुःखं करिष्यामि निवसन्ती सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
phalamūlāśanā nityaṁ bhaviṣyāmi na saṁśayaḥ
na te duḥkhaṁ kariṣyāmi nivasantī saha tvayā

translations.english: Undoubtedly I shall always live upon roots and fruits, living with you always I shall not bring about your affliction.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं गमिष्यामि वनं सुदुर्गमं; मृगायुतं वानरवारणैर्युतम्
वने निवत्स्यामि यथा पितुर्गृहे; तवैव पादावुपगृह्य संमता
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ gamiṣyāmi vanaṁ sudurgamaṁ; mṛgāyutaṁ vānaravāraṇairyutam
vane nivatsyāmi yathā piturgṛhe; tavaiva pādāvupagṛhya saṁmatā

translations.english: I shall go there in that dense forest full of deers, monkeys and elephants and live there as if under my paternal roof cleaving to your feet and abiding in your pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
अनन्यभावामनुरक्तचेतसं; त्वया वियुक्तां मरणाय निश्चिताम्
नयस्व मां साधु कुरुष्व याचनां; न ते मयातो गुरुता भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ananyabhāvāmanuraktacetasaṁ; tvayā viyuktāṁ maraṇāya niścitām
nayasva māṁ sādhu kuruṣva yācanāṁ; na te mayāto gurutā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Do you accept my entreaty whose heart is entirely yours, knows none else, and is ever attached to you, and who am resolved to die if forsaken by you; thus repairing I shall be in no way a burden to you.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ब्रुवाणामपि धर्मवत्सलो; न च स्म सीतां नृवरो निनीषति
उवाच चैनां बहु संनिवर्तने; वने निवासस्य च दुःखितां प्रति
verses.transliteration:
tathā bruvāṇāmapi dharmavatsalo; na ca sma sītāṁ nṛvaro ninīṣati
uvāca caināṁ bahu saṁnivartane; vane nivāsasya ca duḥkhitāṁ prati

translations.english: That best of men, reluctant to take Sītā with him, who had spoken thus and who was greatly attached to virtue, related to her about the many miseries consequent upon dwelling in the forest, with a view to prevent her from following him.

verses.sanskrit:
स एवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां धर्मज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः
निवर्तनार्थे धर्मात्मा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sa evaṁ bruvatīṁ sītāṁ dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ
nivartanārthe dharmātmā vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: And consoling her whose eyes were stained with tears, that virtuous-souled one spoke to her the following words with a view to prevent her from going.

verses.sanskrit:
सीते महाकुलीनासि धर्मे च निरता सदा
इहाचर स्वधर्मं त्वं मा यथा मनसः सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
sīte mahākulīnāsi dharme ca niratā sadā
ihācara svadharmaṁ tvaṁ mā yathā manasaḥ sukham

translations.english: Oh Sītā, you are born of an illustrious family and ever intent on the performance of religious deeds; do you practise virtue here as it may conduce to the happiness of my mind.

verses.sanskrit:
सीते यथा त्वां वक्ष्यामि तथा कार्यं त्वयाबले
वने दोषा हि बहवो वदतस्तान्निबोध मे
verses.transliteration:
sīte yathā tvāṁ vakṣyāmi tathā kāryaṁ tvayābale
vane doṣā hi bahavo vadatastānnibodha me

translations.english: Oh Sītā, Oh you of the weaker sex, Do you act up to my counsels; there are evils enough in the forest, do you learn them from me who am about to dwell in it.

verses.sanskrit:
सीते विमुच्यतामेषा वनवासकृता मतिः
बहुदोषं हि कान्तारं वनमित्यभिधीयते
verses.transliteration:
sīte vimucyatāmeṣā vanavāsakṛtā matiḥ
bahudoṣaṁ hi kāntāraṁ vanamityabhidhīyate

translations.english: Renounce therefore, Oh Sītă, your intention of flying as an exile to the forest, which for its impenetrableness is said to abound in evils.

verses.sanskrit:
हितबुद्ध्या खलु वचो मयैतदभिधीयते
सदा सुखं न जानामि दुःखमेव सदा वनम्
verses.transliteration:
hitabuddhyā khalu vaco mayaitadabhidhīyate
sadā sukhaṁ na jānāmi duḥkhameva sadā vanam

translations.english: It is for your welfare that I give utterance to these words; happiness there is none, it is always covered with miseries.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिनिर्झरसंभूता गिरिकन्दरवासिनाम्
सिंहानां निनदा दुःखाः श्रोतुं दुःखमतो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
girinirjharasaṁbhūtā girikandaravāsinām
siṁhānāṁ ninadā duḥkhāḥ śrotuṁ duḥkhamato vanam

translations.english: The roarings of the lions living in the caves of mountains, swelling with the sounds of the water-falls, produce a very painful impression upon the ears; so the wood is full of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
सुप्यते पर्णशय्यासु स्वयं भग्नासु भूतले
रात्रिषु श्रमखिन्नेन तस्माद्दुःखतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
supyate parṇaśayyāsu svayaṁ bhagnāsu bhūtale
rātriṣu śramakhinnena tasmādduḥkhataraṁ vanam

translations.english: Being exhausted with the toil of the day, the dwellers of the wood have to sleep in night on the bed made of leaves fallen from the trees on the surface of the ground; so the wood is full of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीव वातस्तिमिरं बुभुक्षा चात्र नित्यशः
भयानि च महान्त्यत्र ततो दुःखतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
atīva vātastimiraṁ bubhukṣā cātra nityaśaḥ
bhayāni ca mahāntyatra tato duḥkhataraṁ vanam

translations.english: There are always violent winds, darkness hunger, and great fear; so the wood is full of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
सरीसृपाश्च बहवो बहुरूपाश्च भामिनि
चरन्ति पृथिवीं दर्पादतो दुखतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
sarīsṛpāśca bahavo bahurūpāśca bhāmini
caranti pṛthivīṁ darpādato dukhataraṁ vanam

translations.english: Reptiles, many and of various kinds, creep there on the path, O excellent lady, with haughtiness; so the wood is full of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
नदीनिलयनाः सर्पा नदीकुटिलगामिनः
तिष्ठन्त्यावृत्य पन्थानमतो दुःखतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
nadīnilayanāḥ sarpā nadīkuṭilagāminaḥ
tiṣṭhantyāvṛtya panthānamato duḥkhataraṁ vanam

translations.english: And snakes living in the rivers and of crooked course like them, always await the wayfarers, hindering the passers-by: so the wood is full of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
पतंगा वृश्चिकाः कीटा दंशाश्च मशकैः सह
बाधन्ते नित्यमबले सर्वं दुःखमतो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
pataṁgā vṛścikāḥ kīṭā daṁśāśca maśakaiḥ saha
bādhante nityamabale sarvaṁ duḥkhamato vanam

translations.english: Birds, scorpions, insects mosquito's and wild gnats, always disturb the dwellers, O fair one' of the weaker sex; so the wood is full misery.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रुमाः कण्टकिनश्चैव कुशकाशाश्च भामिनि
वने व्याकुलशाखाग्रास्तेन दुःखतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
drumāḥ kaṇṭakinaścaiva kuśakāśāśca bhāmini
vane vyākulaśākhāgrāstena duḥkhataraṁ vanam

translations.english: There are trees full of thorns, having their branches moving to and fro, and the kusa and kāsa grasses with thorny blades constantly undulating; so the wood is full misery.

verses.sanskrit:
तदलं ते वनं गत्वा क्षमं न हि वनं तव
विमृशन्निह पश्यामि बहुदोषतरं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tadalaṁ te vanaṁ gatvā kṣamaṁ na hi vanaṁ tava
vimṛśanniha paśyāmi bahudoṣataraṁ vanam

translations.english: You should not therefore go to the forest, it forebodes no good to you. Weighing well, have I concluded that the forest abounds in innumerable evils.

verses.sanskrit:
वनं तु नेतुं न कृता मतिस्तदा; बभूव रामेण यदा महात्मना
न तस्य सीता वचनं चकार त;त्ततोऽब्रवीद्राममिदं सुदुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
vanaṁ tu netuṁ na kṛtā matistadā; babhūva rāmeṇa yadā mahātmanā
na tasya sītā vacanaṁ cakāra ta;ttato'bravīdrāmamidaṁ suduḥkhitā

translations.english: While the high-souled Rāma, resolved thus not to take Sītā with him to the forest, she, greatly sorry, did not accept his words and spoke to him in the following way.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रामस्य दुःखिता
प्रसक्ताश्रुमुखी मन्दमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
etattu vacanaṁ śrutvā sītā rāmasya duḥkhitā
prasaktāśrumukhī mandamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing these words of Rāma, Sītā greatly sorry, with tears in her eyes, spoke gently to him the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वया कीर्तिता दोषा वने वस्तव्यतां प्रति
गुणानित्येव तान्विद्धि तव स्नेहपुरस्कृतान्
verses.transliteration:
ye tvayā kīrtitā doṣā vane vastavyatāṁ prati
guṇānityeva tānviddhi tava snehapuraskṛtān

translations.english: The evils, thus enumerated by you of living in the forest, do you know, appear as so many good qualities to me, who have been made forward by your affection.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया च सह गन्तव्यं मया गुरुजनाज्ञया
त्वद्वियोगेन मे राम त्यक्तव्यमिह जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
tvayā ca saha gantavyaṁ mayā gurujanājñayā
tvadviyogena me rāma tyaktavyamiha jīvitam

translations.english: I shall follow you, taking the permission of the respected ones, without you, O, Rāma, I will renounce my life.

verses.sanskrit:
न च मां त्वत्समीपस्थमपि शक्नोति राघव
सुराणामीश्वरः शक्रः प्रधर्षयितुमोजसा
verses.transliteration:
na ca māṁ tvatsamīpasthamapi śaknoti rāghava
surāṇāmīśvaraḥ śakraḥ pradharṣayitumojasā

translations.english: If I live by you, O Rāghava, Sakra, the lord of celestials, shall not be able with his mighty power to defeat me.

verses.sanskrit:
पतिहीना तु या नारी न सा शक्ष्यति जीवितुम्
काममेवंविधं राम त्वया मम विदर्शितम्
verses.transliteration:
patihīnā tu yā nārī na sā śakṣyati jīvitum
kāmamevaṁvidhaṁ rāma tvayā mama vidarśitam

translations.english: 'A woman, without her husband, cannot live' this truth has been pointed out by you. O Rāma, to me.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ चापि महाप्राज्ञ ब्राह्मणानां मया श्रुतम्
पुरा पितृगृहे सत्यं वस्तव्यं किल मे वने
verses.transliteration:
atha cāpi mahāprājña brāhmaṇānāṁ mayā śrutam
purā pitṛgṛhe satyaṁ vastavyaṁ kila me vane

translations.english: Besides, I heard before, O you of great intelligence, in my paternal house from the Brāhmaṇas that I should live in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्षणिभ्यो द्विजातिभ्यः श्रुत्वाहं वचनं गृहे
वनवासकृतोत्साहा नित्यमेव महाबल
verses.transliteration:
lakṣaṇibhyo dvijātibhyaḥ śrutvāhaṁ vacanaṁ gṛhe
vanavāsakṛtotsāhā nityameva mahābala

translations.english: I have heard this from the Brāhmaṇas versed in palmistry, and I have all along been anxious.

verses.sanskrit:
आदेशो वनवासस्य प्राप्तव्यः स मया किल
सा त्वया सह तत्राहं यास्यामि प्रिय नान्यथा
verses.transliteration:
ādeśo vanavāsasya prāptavyaḥ sa mayā kila
sā tvayā saha tatrāhaṁ yāsyāmi priya nānyathā

translations.english: O mighty hero, to go to the forest; I shall therefore obtain permission and go, O dearly beloved to the forest with you; nothing can make it otherwise.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतादेशा भविष्यामि गमिष्यामि सह त्वया
कालश्चायं समुत्पन्नः सत्यवाग्भवतु द्विजः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtādeśā bhaviṣyāmi gamiṣyāmi saha tvayā
kālaścāyaṁ samutpannaḥ satyavāgbhavatu dvijaḥ

translations.english: I shall secure permission and follow you; the time has arrived; may the Brāhmaṇas be of truthful words.

verses.sanskrit:
वनवासे हि जानामि दुःखानि बहुधा किल
प्राप्यन्ते नियतं वीर पुरुषैरकृतात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
vanavāse hi jānāmi duḥkhāni bahudhā kila
prāpyante niyataṁ vīra puruṣairakṛtātmabhiḥ

translations.english: I know, O great hero, that there are many evils incident to living in the forest; but they generally befall those men who have not their senses subdued.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्यया च पितुर्गेहे वनवासः श्रुतो मया
भिक्षिण्याः साधुवृत्ताया मम मातुरिहाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
kanyayā ca piturgehe vanavāsaḥ śruto mayā
bhikṣiṇyāḥ sādhuvṛttāyā mama māturihāgrataḥ

translations.english: I heard, when I was a girl, that an ascetic woman of well-disciplined character, came to my mother and apprised her of my future abode in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादितश्च वै पूर्वं त्वं वै बहुविधं प्रभो
गमनं वनवासस्य काङ्क्षितं हि सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
prasāditaśca vai pūrvaṁ tvaṁ vai bahuvidhaṁ prabho
gamanaṁ vanavāsasya kāṅkṣitaṁ hi saha tvayā

translations.english: I had requested you, O my lord, many times before in this house to take me to the forest with you for enjoyment, and you ware pleased to agree.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतक्षणाहं भद्रं ते गमनं प्रति राघव
वनवासस्य शूरस्य चर्या हि मम रोचते
verses.transliteration:
kṛtakṣaṇāhaṁ bhadraṁ te gamanaṁ prati rāghava
vanavāsasya śūrasya caryā hi mama rocate

translations.english: For your welfare, O Raghava, having received your permission to follow you, I like to serve you, O great hero, while living in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
शुद्धात्मन्प्रेमभावाद्धि भविष्यामि विकल्मषा
भर्तारमनुगच्छन्ती भर्ता हि मम दैवतम्
verses.transliteration:
śuddhātmanpremabhāvāddhi bhaviṣyāmi vikalmaṣā
bhartāramanugacchantī bhartā hi mama daivatam

translations.english: O you, pure-hearted one, surely shall I become sinless if I follow my husband, out of affection; for my husband is my Divinity.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेत्यभावेऽपि कल्याणः संगमो मे सह त्वया
श्रुतिर्हि श्रूयते पुण्या ब्राह्मणानां यशस्विनाम्
verses.transliteration:
pretyabhāve'pi kalyāṇaḥ saṁgamo me saha tvayā
śrutirhi śrūyate puṇyā brāhmaṇānāṁ yaśasvinām

translations.english: I have heard this pious report from the Brāhmaṇas of great fame that even in after life your company is greatly beneficial to me.

verses.sanskrit:
इह लोके च पितृभिर्या स्त्री यस्य महामते
अद्भिर्दत्ता स्वधर्मेण प्रेत्यभावेऽपि तस्य सा
verses.transliteration:
iha loke ca pitṛbhiryā strī yasya mahāmate
adbhirdattā svadharmeṇa pretyabhāve'pi tasya sā

translations.english: She, who has been given away as wife by her father to one, with due rites of gift peculiar to each class, touching holy water, shall be his, even in her after life.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमस्मात्स्वकां नारीं सुवृत्तां हि पतिव्रताम्
नाभिरोचयसे नेतुं त्वं मां केनेह हेतुना
verses.transliteration:
evamasmātsvakāṁ nārīṁ suvṛttāṁ hi pativratām
nābhirocayase netuṁ tvaṁ māṁ keneha hetunā

translations.english: For what reason then did you not wish to take your wife with you who is of good character and devoted to her husband? Do you take me.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्तां पतिव्रतां दीनां मां समां सुखदुःखयोः
नेतुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ समानसुखदुःखिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
bhaktāṁ pativratāṁ dīnāṁ māṁ samāṁ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
netumarhasi kākutstha samānasukhaduḥkhinīm

translations.english: O Kākutstha, who am poor in spirit, devoted to my husband, ever given to your service, and participating equally in your joy and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मां दुःखितामेवं वनं नेतुं न चेच्छसि
विषमग्निं जलं वाहमास्थास्ये मृत्युकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
yadi māṁ duḥkhitāmevaṁ vanaṁ netuṁ na cecchasi
viṣamagniṁ jalaṁ vāhamāsthāsye mṛtyukāraṇāt

translations.english: If you do not purpose to take me with you, surely will I do away with my life by drinking poison, entering into fire, or drowning myself in water.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधं तं सा याचते गमनं प्रति
नानुमेने महाबाहुस्तां नेतुं विजनं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bahuvidhaṁ taṁ sā yācate gamanaṁ prati
nānumene mahābāhustāṁ netuṁ vijanaṁ vanam

translations.english: She begged Rāma in these and various other means to take her with him, but that mighty hero did not consent to lead her into the lonely forest.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा चिन्तां मैथिली समुपागता
स्नापयन्तीव गामुष्णैरश्रुभिर्नयनच्युतैः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā cintāṁ maithilī samupāgatā
snāpayantīva gāmuṣṇairaśrubhirnayanacyutaiḥ

translations.english: Being accosted thus, Maithili was wrapt up in thought and bathed her breast with tears trickling down from her eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयन्तीं तथा तां तु निवर्तयितुमात्मवान्
क्रोधाविष्टां तु वैदेहीं काकुत्स्थो बह्वसान्त्वयत्
verses.transliteration:
cintayantīṁ tathā tāṁ tu nivartayitumātmavān
krodhāviṣṭāṁ tu vaidehīṁ kākutstho bahvasāntvayat

translations.english: And Kākutstha having control over his ownself, with a view to dissuade her who was angry and engrossed in anxious thoughts, began to console her in divers way.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्त्व्यमाना तु रामेण मैथिली जनकात्मजा
वनवासनिमित्ताय भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sāntvyamānā tu rāmeṇa maithilī janakātmajā
vanavāsanimittāya bhartāramidamabravīt

translations.english: Being consoled thus by Rāma, Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, fearing separation, lovingly and haughtily laughed at Rāghava of spacious breast, and spoke to him, her husband, the following words with a view to follow him to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
किं त्वामन्यत वैदेहः पिता मे मिथिलाधिपः
राम जामातरं प्राप्य स्त्रियं पुरुषविग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tvāmanyata vaidehaḥ pitā me mithilādhipaḥ
rāma jāmātaraṁ prāpya striyaṁ puruṣavigraham

translations.english: What thought of you, O Rāma, my father, the king of Mithilā, accepting you as his son-in-law, who was a man if form but (in deeds)a woman?

verses.sanskrit:
अनृतं बललोकोऽयमज्ञानाद्यद्धि वक्ष्यति
तेजो नास्ति परं रामे तपतीव दिवाकरे
verses.transliteration:
anṛtaṁ balaloko'yamajñānādyaddhi vakṣyati
tejo nāsti paraṁ rāme tapatīva divākare

translations.english: Henceforth, if people through ignorance say that the sun has not that burning flood of light which in Rāma does shine forth, woe is them, it is falsehood.

verses.sanskrit:
किं हि कृत्वा विषण्णस्त्वं कुतो वा भयमस्ति ते
यत्परित्यक्तुकामस्त्वं मामनन्यपरायणाम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ hi kṛtvā viṣaṇṇastvaṁ kuto vā bhayamasti te
yatparityaktukāmastvaṁ māmananyaparāyaṇām

translations.english: Why are you so dejected and whence is your fear that you are willing to leave behind your wife who has none else but you?

verses.sanskrit:
द्युमत्सेनसुतं वीर सत्यवन्तमनुव्रताम्
सावित्रीमिव मां विद्धि त्वमात्मवशवर्तिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
dyumatsenasutaṁ vīra satyavantamanuvratām
sāvitrīmiva māṁ viddhi tvamātmavaśavartinīm

translations.english: Know me to be perfectly under your influence like to Sāvitri, following her husband Satyavān, the son of Dyumatsen.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वहं मनसाप्यन्यं द्रष्टास्मि त्वदृतेऽनघ
त्वया राघव गच्छेयं यथान्या कुलपांसनी
verses.transliteration:
na tvahaṁ manasāpyanyaṁ draṣṭāsmi tvadṛte'nagha
tvayā rāghava gaccheyaṁ yathānyā kulapāṁsanī

translations.english: I have not, like one bringing stigma on her line, ever in my life thought of a second person, but of you whom I must follow into the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयं तु भार्यां कौमारीं चिरमध्युषितां सतीम्
शैलूष इव मां राम परेभ्यो दातुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
svayaṁ tu bhāryāṁ kaumārīṁ ciramadhyuṣitāṁ satīm
śailūṣa iva māṁ rāma parebhyo dātumicchasi

translations.english: Do you, like to an ordinary actor, wish to hand me over to others, who am chaste, pure as a virgin, and long held in conjugal affection?

verses.sanskrit:
स मामनादाय वनं न त्वं प्रस्थातुमर्हसि
तपो वा यदि वारण्यं स्वर्गो वा स्यात्सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
sa māmanādāya vanaṁ na tvaṁ prasthātumarhasi
tapo vā yadi vāraṇyaṁ svargo vā syātsaha tvayā

translations.english: It does not behove you to repair to the forest without taking me along with you. Be it the austerity of an ascetic, the forest or heaven, with you will I be everywhere.

verses.sanskrit:
न च मे भविता तत्र कश्चित्पथि परिश्रमः
पृष्ठतस्तव गच्छन्त्या विहारशयनेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
na ca me bhavitā tatra kaścitpathi pariśramaḥ
pṛṣṭhatastava gacchantyā vihāraśayaneṣvapi

translations.english: No toil shall I suffer on the way, as if lying on a bed of luxury, while following you in they footstep.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशकाशशरेषीका ये च कण्टकिनो द्रुमाः
तूलाजिनसमस्पर्शा मार्गे मम सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
kuśakāśaśareṣīkā ye ca kaṇṭakino drumāḥ
tūlājinasamasparśā mārge mama saha tvayā

translations.english: When with you, the various thorny grasses, the Kuśa, the Käsa, the Sara, and the Işika, and the thistles and brambles on the way, shall be to me in touch like to linen and deer-skin.

verses.sanskrit:
महावातसमुद्धूतं यन्मामवकरिष्यति
रजो रमण तन्मन्ये परार्ध्यमिव चन्दनम्
verses.transliteration:
mahāvātasamuddhūtaṁ yanmāmavakariṣyati
rajo ramaṇa tanmanye parārdhyamiva candanam

translations.english: The dust that will cover me, thrown up by the gush of wind shall be, O ravisher of my heart regarded by me as the finest sandal dust.

verses.sanskrit:
शाद्वलेषु यदासिष्ये वनान्ते वनगोचरा
कुथास्तरणतल्पेषु किं स्यात्सुखतरं ततः
verses.transliteration:
śādvaleṣu yadāsiṣye vanānte vanagocarā
kuthāstaraṇatalpeṣu kiṁ syātsukhataraṁ tataḥ

translations.english: When I shall lie down on the bed of green grass in the forest, it shall appear to me more pleasant than one covered with a coloured blanket.

verses.sanskrit:
पत्रं मूलं फलं यत्त्वमल्पं वा यदि वा बहु
दास्यसि स्वयमाहृत्य तन्मेऽमृतरसोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
patraṁ mūlaṁ phalaṁ yattvamalpaṁ vā yadi vā bahu
dāsyasi svayamāhṛtya tanme'mṛtarasopamam

translations.english: Fruits, roots and leaves which you will bring yourself and give me, be they great or small in quantity, shall be to me like to the ambrosiajuice.

verses.sanskrit:
न मातुर्न पितुस्तत्र स्मरिष्यामि न वेश्मनः
आर्तवान्युपभुञ्जाना पुष्पाणि च फलानि च
verses.transliteration:
na māturna pitustatra smariṣyāmi na veśmanaḥ
ārtavānyupabhuñjānā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca

translations.english: I shall never think of my father, mother, or my abode; I shall enjoy fruits and flowers growing in various seasons.

verses.sanskrit:
न च तत्र गतः किंचिद्द्रष्टुमर्हसि विप्रियम्
मत्कृते न च ते शोको न भविष्यामि दुर्भरा
verses.transliteration:
na ca tatra gataḥ kiṁciddraṣṭumarhasi vipriyam
matkṛte na ca te śoko na bhaviṣyāmi durbharā

translations.english: You shall not witness any thing disagreeable there; for me you shall not experience any sorrow, no shall I be a burden to you; do you take me with you.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्वया सह स स्वर्गो निरयो यस्त्वया विना
इति जानन्परां प्रीतिं गच्छ राम मया सह
verses.transliteration:
yastvayā saha sa svargo nirayo yastvayā vinā
iti jānanparāṁ prītiṁ gaccha rāma mayā saha

translations.english: O, Rāma, conceiving with pleasure that your company is a heaven to me and your absence a hell. If you do not take me to the forest which I count freed from all evils, surely I shall drink poison and never come under the influence of my enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्चादपि हि दुःखेन मम नैवास्ति जीवितम्
उज्झितायास्त्वया नाथ तदैव मरणं वरम्
verses.transliteration:
paścādapi hi duḥkhena mama naivāsti jīvitam
ujjhitāyāstvayā nātha tadaiva maraṇaṁ varam

translations.english: When through affliction I shall not live after separation, better it is, O Lord, that I die immediately at the time of my being forsaken by you; I cannot bear this grief even for a moment. How shall I be able to live without you for fourteen years?

verses.sanskrit:
इति सा शोकसंतप्ता विलप्य करुणं बहु
चुक्रोश पतिमायस्ता भृशमालिङ्ग्य सस्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
iti sā śokasaṁtaptā vilapya karuṇaṁ bahu
cukrośa patimāyastā bhṛśamāliṅgya sasvaram

translations.english: Thus lamenting, Sītā, racked with sorrow, embraced her husband and began to cry aloud.

verses.sanskrit:
सा विद्धा बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्दिग्धैरिव गजाङ्गना
चिर संनियतं बाष्पं मुमोचाग्निमिवारणिः
verses.transliteration:
sā viddhā bahubhirvākyairdigdhairiva gajāṅganā
cira saṁniyataṁ bāṣpaṁ mumocāgnimivāraṇiḥ

translations.english: Like to a she-elephant, she being pierced by the poisonous shafts of Rāma's words, began to shed tears, long kept off, as an Araņi wood emits fire continually.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः स्फटिकसंकाशं वारि संतापसंभवम्
नेत्राभ्यां परिसुस्राव पङ्कजाभ्यामिवोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ sphaṭikasaṁkāśaṁ vāri saṁtāpasaṁbhavam
netrābhyāṁ parisusrāva paṅkajābhyāmivodakam

translations.english: Tears caused by her sorrow and white as the crystal began to trickle down from her eyes, like to water falling in drops from lotus petals.

verses.sanskrit:
तां परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां विसंज्ञामिव दुःखिताम्
उवाच वचनं रामः परिविश्वासयंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṁ visaṁjñāmiva duḥkhitām
uvāca vacanaṁ rāmaḥ pariviśvāsayaṁstadā

translations.english: Finding her almost insensible with sorrow, Rāma flung his arms round her and reviving her (with consolation) spoke the following words to her.

verses.sanskrit:
न देवि तव दुःखेन स्वर्गमप्यभिरोचये
न हि मेऽस्ति भयं किंचित्स्वयम्भोरिव सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
na devi tava duḥkhena svargamapyabhirocaye
na hi me'sti bhayaṁ kiṁcitsvayambhoriva sarvataḥ

translations.english: I do not long for, Oh worshipful one, even the abode of celestials gained through your affliction; fear there is none for me like to the self-create Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
तव सर्वमभिप्रायमविज्ञाय शुभानने
वासं न रोचयेऽरण्ये शक्तिमानपि रक्षणे
verses.transliteration:
tava sarvamabhiprāyamavijñāya śubhānane
vāsaṁ na rocaye'raṇye śaktimānapi rakṣaṇe

translations.english: Not apprised of your full intention, O you of beautiful countenance, I could not, though capable of escorting you, desire your abode in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्सृष्टासि मया सार्धं वनवासाय मैथिलि
न विहातुं मया शक्या कीर्तिरात्मवता यथा
verses.transliteration:
yatsṛṣṭāsi mayā sārdhaṁ vanavāsāya maithili
na vihātuṁ mayā śakyā kīrtirātmavatā yathā

translations.english: When you are determined O Maithili, repair to the forest with me, I cannot leave you behind, as one possessing self-knowledge cannot renounce munificence.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मस्तु गजनासोरु सद्भिराचरितः पुरा
तं चाहमनुवर्तेऽद्य यथा सूर्यं सुवर्चला
verses.transliteration:
dharmastu gajanāsoru sadbhirācaritaḥ purā
taṁ cāhamanuvarte'dya yathā sūryaṁ suvarcalā

translations.english: O you, having thighs resembling the trunks of an elephant, I shall resort to that virtue which was exercised by great and good men going before, do you follow me therefore like Suvarcalā following the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
एष धर्मस्तु सुश्रोणि पितुर्मातुश्च वश्यता
अतश्चाज्ञां व्यतिक्रम्य नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa dharmastu suśroṇi piturmātuśca vaśyatā
ataścājñāṁ vyatikramya nāhaṁ jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: Obedience to his parents is the virtue of a son. Disobeying the command of my father I am not eager to live. we

verses.sanskrit:
स मां पिता यथा शास्ति सत्यधर्मपथे स्थितः
तथा वर्तितुमिच्छामि स हि धर्मः सनातनः
अनुगच्छस्व मां भीरु सहधर्मचरी भव
verses.transliteration:
sa māṁ pitā yathā śāsti satyadharmapathe sthitaḥ
tathā vartitumicchāmi sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
anugacchasva māṁ bhīru sahadharmacarī bhava

translations.english: Therefore do I desire to follow what my father commands me, treading in the path of truth, and this is the virtue eternal.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च रत्नानि भिक्षुकेभ्यश्च भोजनम्
देहि चाशंसमानेभ्यः संत्वरस्व च माचिरम्
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇebhyaśca ratnāni bhikṣukebhyaśca bhojanam
dehi cāśaṁsamānebhyaḥ saṁtvarasva ca māciram

translations.english: Do you give away jewels to the Brāhmaṇas and edibles to the beggars longing for them, and make haste without delay.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टा परिपूर्णमानसा; यशस्विनी भर्तुरवेक्ष्य भाषितम्
धनानि रत्नानि च दातुमङ्गना; प्रचक्रमे धर्मभृतां मनस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭā paripūrṇamānasā; yaśasvinī bharturavekṣya bhāṣitam
dhanāni ratnāni ca dātumaṅganā; pracakrame dharmabhṛtāṁ manasvinī

translations.english: Convinced that her going to the forest was desired by her husband, Sītā began to distribute them speedily with a delighted heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामो लक्ष्मणमग्रतः
स्थितं प्राग्गामिनं वीरं याचमानं कृताञ्जलिम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīnmahātejā rāmo lakṣmaṇamagrataḥ
sthitaṁ prāggāminaṁ vīraṁ yācamānaṁ kṛtāñjalim

translations.english: Then the highly effulgent Rāma spoke thus to that sedate Lakşmaņa, who stood praying before him with clasped hands.

verses.sanskrit:
मयाद्य सह सौमित्रे त्वयि गच्छति तद्वनम्
को भरिष्यति कौसल्यां सुमित्रां वा यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
mayādya saha saumitre tvayi gacchati tadvanam
ko bhariṣyati kausalyāṁ sumitrāṁ vā yaśasvinīm

translations.english: If you do accompany me to you forest, O son of Sumitrā, who shall serve Kausalyā and the highly renowned Sumitrā.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवर्षति कामैर्यः पर्जन्यः पृथिवीमिव
स कामपाशपर्यस्तो महातेजा महीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
abhivarṣati kāmairyaḥ parjanyaḥ pṛthivīmiva
sa kāmapāśaparyasto mahātejā mahīpatiḥ

translations.english: That highly effulgent lord of earth who will satisfy the world with the fulfilment of its desires like to rain spreading in showers over the earth, is himself now shackled with desires to Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हि राज्यमिदं प्राप्य नृपस्याश्वपतेः सुता
दुःखितानां सपत्नीनां न करिष्यति शोभनम्
verses.transliteration:
sā hi rājyamidaṁ prāpya nṛpasyāśvapateḥ sutā
duḥkhitānāṁ sapatnīnāṁ na kariṣyati śobhanam

translations.english: That daughter of Aśvapati obtaining this kingdom from the monarch, there will be no end of the miseries of these co-wives.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः श्लक्ष्णया गिरा
प्रत्युवाच तदा रामं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ ślakṣṇayā girā
pratyuvāca tadā rāmaṁ vākyajño vākyakovidam

translations.english: Accosted thus by Rama, Laksmana, well versed in speech, spoke to him the following humble words.

verses.sanskrit:
तवैव तेजसा वीर भरतः पूजयिष्यति
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च प्रयतो नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
tavaiva tejasā vīra bharataḥ pūjayiṣyati
kausalyāṁ ca sumitrāṁ ca prayato nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Being afraid of your power, O hero, Bharata shall adore. Kausalyā and Sumitrā, there is no doubt about this.

verses.sanskrit:
धनुरादाय सशरं खनित्रपिटकाधरः
अग्रतस्ते गमिष्यामि पन्थानमनुदर्शयन्
verses.transliteration:
dhanurādāya saśaraṁ khanitrapiṭakādharaḥ
agrataste gamiṣyāmi panthānamanudarśayan

translations.english: I shall go before you pointing out your course, with stringed bows, a hoe, and a basket in my hands.

verses.sanskrit:
आहरिष्यामि ते नित्यं मूलानि च फलानि च
वन्यानि यानि चान्यानि स्वाहाराणि तपस्विनाम्
verses.transliteration:
āhariṣyāmi te nityaṁ mūlāni ca phalāni ca
vanyāni yāni cānyāni svāhārāṇi tapasvinām

translations.english: I shall bring for you every day various roots and fruits and other that grow in the forest and which the ascetics use in their sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
भवांस्तु सह वैदेह्या गिरिसानुषु रंस्यते
अहं सर्वं करिष्यामि जाग्रतः स्वपतश्च ते
verses.transliteration:
bhavāṁstu saha vaidehyā girisānuṣu raṁsyate
ahaṁ sarvaṁ kariṣyāmi jāgrataḥ svapataśca te

translations.english: You shall amuse yourself with Vaidehī on the sides of the hill, and I shall perform everything for you whether you are asleep or awake.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्त्वनेन वाक्येन सुप्रीतः प्रत्युवाच तम्
व्रजापृच्छस्व सौमित्रे सर्वमेव सुहृज्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmastvanena vākyena suprītaḥ pratyuvāca tam
vrajāpṛcchasva saumitre sarvameva suhṛjjanam

translations.english: Being extremely gratified with these words, Rāma spoke to him, saying, Do you follow me, O son of Sumitrā, obtaining permission from all your relatives.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्दिव्यं राजशार्दूलः सत्कृतं माल्यभूषितम्
रामाय दर्शयामास सौमित्रिः सर्वमायुधम्
verses.transliteration:
taddivyaṁ rājaśārdūlaḥ satkṛtaṁ mālyabhūṣitam
rāmāya darśayāmāsa saumitriḥ sarvamāyudham

translations.english: And that best of princes, the son of Sumitrā, showed Rāma those heavenly arms worshipped and well adorned with garlands...........

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाचात्मवान्रामः प्रीत्या लक्ष्मणमागतम्
काले त्वमागतः सौम्य काङ्क्षिते मम लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
tamuvācātmavānrāmaḥ prītyā lakṣmaṇamāgatam
kāle tvamāgataḥ saumya kāṅkṣite mama lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: Seeing Laksmana arrive there, Rama, having control over his ownself, greatly pleased, spoke to him the following words. "You have arrived, O Laksmana, just when I wanted you."

verses.sanskrit:
अहं प्रदातुमिच्छामि यदिदं मामकं धनम्
ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तपस्विभ्यस्त्वया सह परंतप
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ pradātumicchāmi yadidaṁ māmakaṁ dhanam
brāhmaṇebhyastapasvibhyastvayā saha paraṁtapa

translations.english: I want to distribute with you these my riches amongst the Brāhmaṇas and the ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
वसन्तीह दृढं भक्त्या गुरुषु द्विजसत्तमाः
तेषामपि च मे भूयः सर्वेषां चोपजीविनाम्
verses.transliteration:
vasantīha dṛḍhaṁ bhaktyā guruṣu dvijasattamāḥ
teṣāmapi ca me bhūyaḥ sarveṣāṁ copajīvinām

translations.english: There are many excellent Brāhmaṇas having firm reverence in their preceptor. I want to distribute my wealth amongst them and many other personages who depend upon me for their maintenance.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठपुत्रं तु सुयज्ञमार्यं; त्वमानयाशु प्रवरं द्विजानाम्
अभिप्रयास्यामि वनं समस्ता;नभ्यर्च्य शिष्टानपरान्द्विजातीन्
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhaputraṁ tu suyajñamāryaṁ; tvamānayāśu pravaraṁ dvijānām
abhiprayāsyāmi vanaṁ samastā;nabhyarcya śiṣṭānaparāndvijātīn

translations.english: Bring here speedily the worshipful Suyajña, the son of Vasiştha; want to repair to the forest after duly adoring him and other excellent Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit:
तं विप्रमग्न्यगारस्थं वन्दित्वा लक्ष्मणोऽब्रवीत्
सखेऽभ्यागच्छ पश्य त्वं वेश्म दुष्करकारिणः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vipramagnyagārasthaṁ vanditvā lakṣmaṇo'bravīt
sakhe'bhyāgaccha paśya tvaṁ veśma duṣkarakāriṇaḥ

translations.english: Receiving this pleasant and beneficial mandate of his brother, Lakşmaņa speedily went to the abode of Sujajña, and finding thai vipra in the chamber where the sacrificial fire was maintained, worshipped him and addressed him, saying; "friend, come and behold the abode of that one of arduous deeds(Răma) renouncing his incoming installation.”

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संध्यामुपास्याशु गत्वा सौमित्रिणा सह
जुष्टं तत्प्राविशल्लक्ष्म्या रम्यं रामनिवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁdhyāmupāsyāśu gatvā saumitriṇā saha
juṣṭaṁ tatprāviśallakṣmyā ramyaṁ rāmaniveśanam

translations.english: Finishing his prayers, Sujajña accompanied Lakşmaņa and arrived at the splendid mansion of Rama, filled with riches.

verses.sanskrit:
पर्यङ्कमग्र्यास्तरणं नानारत्नविभूषितम्
तमपीच्छति वैदेही प्रतिष्ठापयितुं त्वयि
verses.transliteration:
paryaṅkamagryāstaraṇaṁ nānāratnavibhūṣitam
tamapīcchati vaidehī pratiṣṭhāpayituṁ tvayi

translations.english: Vaidehi wishes to present you with this fine bed-stead with its coverlet studded with various precious jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
नागः शत्रुं जयो नाम मातुलो यं ददौ मम
तं ते गजसहस्रेण ददामि द्विजपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
nāgaḥ śatruṁ jayo nāma mātulo yaṁ dadau mama
taṁ te gajasahasreṇa dadāmi dvijapuṁgava

translations.english: I offer you, o great ascetic, with a thousand gold coins, this excellent elephant, called the destroyer of foes, which had been bestowed upon me by my maternal uncle.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः स हि रामेण सुयज्ञः प्रतिगृह्य तत्
रामलक्ष्मणसीतानां प्रयुयोजाशिषः शिवाः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ sa hi rāmeṇa suyajñaḥ pratigṛhya tat
rāmalakṣmaṇasītānāṁ prayuyojāśiṣaḥ śivāḥ

translations.english: Being addressed thus by Rāma, Sujajña accepted all those offers, and showered benedictions upon Rāma, Sītā, and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ भ्रातरमव्यग्रं प्रियं रामः प्रियंवदः
सौमित्रिं तमुवाचेदं ब्रह्मेव त्रिदशेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
atha bhrātaramavyagraṁ priyaṁ rāmaḥ priyaṁvadaḥ
saumitriṁ tamuvācedaṁ brahmeva tridaśeśvaram

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma spoke to his beloved considerate and fair-speaking brother, the son of Sumitrā, the following pleasant words, like to Brahma addressing the Lord of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अगस्त्यं कौशिकं चैव तावुभौ ब्राह्मणोत्तमौ
अर्चयाहूय सौमित्रे रत्नैः सस्यमिवाम्बुभिः
verses.transliteration:
agastyaṁ kauśikaṁ caiva tāvubhau brāhmaṇottamau
arcayāhūya saumitre ratnaiḥ sasyamivāmbubhiḥ

translations.english: O son of Sumiträ, do you invite the excellent Brāhmaṇas, Agastya and Viśvāmitra, and adore them, O Raghava, by conferring upon them gems, as people cherish corn with water.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यां च य आशीर्भिर्भक्तः पर्युपतिष्ठति
आचार्यस्तैत्तिरीयाणामभिरूपश्च वेदवित्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāṁ ca ya āśīrbhirbhaktaḥ paryupatiṣṭhati
ācāryastaittirīyāṇāmabhirūpaśca vedavit

translations.english: Do you confer upon that good Brāhmaṇa, the preceptor of the Tittirīya portion of the Vedas, who crowns Kausalyā with blessings every day, silk cloth, conveyances, maid-servants, and such other things, till the twice-born one is satisfied.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तद्धनं लक्ष्मणः स्वयम्
यथोक्तं ब्राह्मणेन्द्राणामददाद्धनदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghrastaddhanaṁ lakṣmaṇaḥ svayam
yathoktaṁ brāhmaṇendrāṇāmadadāddhanado yathā

translations.english: Thereupon Laksmana, that best of men, distributed amongst all these Brāhmaṇas all the entire riches as ordered by Rāma like to the Lord of wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्बाष्पकलांस्तिष्ठतश्चोपजीविनः
संप्रदाय बहु द्रव्यमेकैकस्योपजीविनः
verses.transliteration:
athābravīdbāṣpakalāṁstiṣṭhataścopajīvinaḥ
saṁpradāya bahu dravyamekaikasyopajīvinaḥ

translations.english: Seeing his dependants in a wretched plight, shedding tears continually, Rāma proffered to them various articles for their maintenance, and said, Do you occupy in turn until our return my rooms as well as Laksmana's.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा दुःखितं सर्वं जनं तमुपजीविनम्
उवाचेदं धनध्यक्षं धनमानीयतामिति
ततोऽस्य धनमाजह्रुः सर्वमेवोपजीविनः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā duḥkhitaṁ sarvaṁ janaṁ tamupajīvinam
uvācedaṁ dhanadhyakṣaṁ dhanamānīyatāmiti
tato'sya dhanamājahruḥ sarvamevopajīvinaḥ

translations.english: Having spoken thus to all those dependants who were racked with great sorrow, Rāma ordered the Treasury officer to bring his riches there.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तद्धनं सहलक्ष्मणः
द्विजेभ्यो बालवृद्धेभ्यः कृपणेभ्योऽभ्यदापयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghrastaddhanaṁ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
dvijebhyo bālavṛddhebhyaḥ kṛpaṇebhyo'bhyadāpayat

translations.english: Rāma, the best of men, together with Laksmana, distributed them amongst the Brahmanas, boys, the old, and the poor.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रासीत्पिङ्गलो गार्ग्यस्त्रिजटो नाम वै द्विजः
आ पञ्चमायाः कक्ष्याया नैनं कश्चिदवारयत्
verses.transliteration:
tatrāsītpiṅgalo gārgyastrijaṭo nāma vai dvijaḥ
ā pañcamāyāḥ kakṣyāyā nainaṁ kaścidavārayat

translations.english: There lived in that quarter a Brāhmaṇa of a tawny colour, by name Trijata, descended from the line of Garga, earning his live-hood by digging the earth with spades and ploughs.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजपुत्रमासाद्य त्रिजटो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
निर्धनो बहुपुत्रोऽस्मि राजपुत्र महायशः
उञ्छवृत्तिर्वने नित्यं प्रत्यवेक्षस्व मामिति
verses.transliteration:
sa rājaputramāsādya trijaṭo vākyamabravīt
nirdhano bahuputro'smi rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
uñchavṛttirvane nityaṁ pratyavekṣasva māmiti

translations.english: O mighty son of the King! a poor man am I, having a number of children. I maintain my family by digging the earth; do you therefore look upon me mercifully.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच ततो रामः परिहाससमन्वितम्
गवां सहस्रमप्येकं न तु विश्राणितं मया
परिक्षिपसि दण्डेन यावत्तावदवाप्स्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca tato rāmaḥ parihāsasamanvitam
gavāṁ sahasramapyekaṁ na tu viśrāṇitaṁ mayā
parikṣipasi daṇḍena yāvattāvadavāpsyasi

translations.english: Whereupon Rāma replied laughing: "I have not distributed as yet even one thousand of my cows. Do you hurl this rod, and you are the master of all those cows occupying the space at the extremely of which this rod shall fall."

verses.sanskrit:
स शाटीं त्वरितः कट्यां संभ्रान्तः परिवेष्ट्य ताम्
आविध्य दण्डं चिक्षेप सर्वप्राणेन वेगितः
verses.transliteration:
sa śāṭīṁ tvaritaḥ kaṭyāṁ saṁbhrāntaḥ pariveṣṭya tām
āvidhya daṇḍaṁ cikṣepa sarvaprāṇena vegitaḥ

translations.english: Upon this, swiftly tightening the cloth around his waist, Trijața firmly grasping the rod hurled it with a mighty force.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच च ततो रामस्तं गार्ग्यमभिसान्त्वयन्
मन्युर्न खलु कर्तव्यः परिहासो ह्ययं मम
verses.transliteration:
uvāca ca tato rāmastaṁ gārgyamabhisāntvayan
manyurna khalu kartavyaḥ parihāso hyayaṁ mama

translations.english: Seeing this, the virtuous-souled Rāma despatched to the hermitage of Trijata all the cows that lay extending up to the banks of the river Sarayū, and consoling him afterwards accosted him with the following words. “Be not offended."

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सभार्यस्त्रिजटो महामुनि;र्गवामनीकं प्रतिगृह्य मोदितः
यशोबलप्रीतिसुखोपबृंहिणी;स्तदाशिषः प्रत्यवदन्महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sabhāryastrijaṭo mahāmuni;rgavāmanīkaṁ pratigṛhya moditaḥ
yaśobalaprītisukhopabṛṁhiṇī;stadāśiṣaḥ pratyavadanmahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Then Trijata, being pleased with the accession of cows, went away along with his wife, showering happiness and joy.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्त्वा तु सह वैदेह्या ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं बहु
जग्मतुः पितरं द्रष्टुं सीतया सह राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
dattvā tu saha vaidehyā brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṁ bahu
jagmatuḥ pitaraṁ draṣṭuṁ sītayā saha rāghavau

translations.english: Having distributed much wealth to the Brāhmaṇas, the Rāghavas set out with $ītā for the purpose of seeing their father.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गृहीते दुष्प्रेक्ष्ये अशोभेतां तदायुधे
मालादामभिरासक्ते सीतया समलंकृते
verses.transliteration:
tato gṛhīte duṣprekṣye aśobhetāṁ tadāyudhe
mālādāmabhirāsakte sītayā samalaṁkṛte

translations.english: The two looked beautiful with a couple of handmaids (following them), taking the weapons that had been decked by Sītā with flowery wreaths.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रासादहर्म्याणि विमानशिखराणि च
अधिरुह्य जनः श्रीमानुदासीनो व्यलोकयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prāsādaharmyāṇi vimānaśikharāṇi ca
adhiruhya janaḥ śrīmānudāsīno vyalokayat

translations.english: Then crowds of elegantly-attired citizens, mounting on the terraces of three-storied and seven-storied houses, looked on the scene with hearts filled with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि रथ्याः स्म शक्यन्ते गन्तुं बहुजनाकुलाः
आरुह्य तस्मात्प्रासादान्दीनाः पश्यन्ति राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi rathyāḥ sma śakyante gantuṁ bahujanākulāḥ
āruhya tasmātprāsādāndīnāḥ paśyanti rāghavam

translations.english: Unable to thread the streets because of a vast concourse, they ascending the terraces of the buildings, eyed Rāghava with woebegone eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
पदातिं वर्जितच्छत्रं रामं दृष्ट्वा तदा जनाः
ऊचुर्बहुविधा वाचः शोकोपहतचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
padātiṁ varjitacchatraṁ rāmaṁ dṛṣṭvā tadā janāḥ
ūcurbahuvidhā vācaḥ śokopahatacetasaḥ

translations.english: And deprived of their senses by grief, the multitudes,* beholding Rāma proceeding on foot in company with Sītā and his younger brother, said. *Another reading i.e., Beholding Rāma without his umbrella and walking a foot.

verses.sanskrit:
यं यान्तमनुयाति स्म चतुरङ्गबलं महत्
तमेकं सीतया सार्धमनुयाति स्म लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
yaṁ yāntamanuyāti sma caturaṅgabalaṁ mahat
tamekaṁ sītayā sārdhamanuyāti sma lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: He that used to be followed by the vast body of the four-fold forces, proceeds now along with Sita, followed by Laksmana alone.

verses.sanskrit:
ऐश्वर्यस्य रसज्ञः सन्कामिनां चैव कामदः
नेच्छत्येवानृतं कर्तुं पितरं धर्मगौरवात्
verses.transliteration:
aiśvaryasya rasajñaḥ sankāmināṁ caiva kāmadaḥ
necchatyevānṛtaṁ kartuṁ pitaraṁ dharmagauravāt

translations.english: Knowing every kind of enjoyment, that magnanimous one who has tasted of every luxury, for maintaining the dignity of morality, does not wish to falsify (his father's) word.

verses.sanskrit:
या न शक्या पुरा द्रष्टुं भूतैराकाशगैरपि
तामद्य सीतां पश्यन्ति राजमार्गगता जनाः
verses.transliteration:
yā na śakyā purā draṣṭuṁ bhūtairākāśagairapi
tāmadya sītāṁ paśyanti rājamārgagatā janāḥ

translations.english: And that Sītā whom formerly the very rangers of the sky could not see, is to-day beheld by the passers-by.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गरागोचितां सीतां रक्तचन्दन सेविनीम्
वर्षमुष्णं च शीतं च नेष्यत्याशु विवर्णताम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgarāgocitāṁ sītāṁ raktacandana sevinīm
varṣamuṣṇaṁ ca śītaṁ ca neṣyatyāśu vivarṇatām

translations.english: Now summer's heat and winter's cold and the rains of the wet season wil speedily stain Sītā, whose person is worthy of being dyed, and who used to daub her limbs with red sandal paste.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य नूनं दशरथः सत्त्वमाविश्य भाषते
न हि राजा प्रियं पुत्रं विवासयितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
adya nūnaṁ daśarathaḥ sattvamāviśya bhāṣate
na hi rājā priyaṁ putraṁ vivāsayitumarhati

translations.english: Surely to-day Dasaratha speaks thus, possessed by some evil spirit; for the king ought by no means to banish his beloved son.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्गुणस्यापि पुत्रस्या काथं स्याद्विप्रवासनम्
किं पुनर्यस्य लोकोऽयं जितो वृत्तेन केवलम्
verses.transliteration:
nirguṇasyāpi putrasyā kāthaṁ syādvipravāsanam
kiṁ punaryasya loko'yaṁ jito vṛttena kevalam

translations.english: Who ever exiles his son, albeit he be worthless? And what is to be said concerning a son that has fast secured all men's hearts by his behaviour?

verses.sanskrit:
आनृशंस्यमनुक्रोशः श्रुतं शीलं दमः शमः
राघवं शोभयन्त्येते षड्गुणाः पुरुषोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
ānṛśaṁsyamanukrośaḥ śrutaṁ śīlaṁ damaḥ śamaḥ
rāghavaṁ śobhayantyete ṣaḍguṇāḥ puruṣottamam

translations.english: Universal benevolence, kindness, learning, goodness, the restraint of the senses, and the control of the faculties, these six qualities adorn that best of men, Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्तस्योपघातेन प्रजाः परमपीडिताः
औदकानीव सत्त्वानि ग्रीष्मे सलिलसंक्षयात्
verses.transliteration:
tasmāttasyopaghātena prajāḥ paramapīḍitāḥ
audakānīva sattvāni grīṣme salilasaṁkṣayāt

translations.english: Therefore the subjects will be afflicted in consequence of his separation, even as aquatic animals are, when summer dries up the waters of a tank.

verses.sanskrit:
पीडया पीडितं सर्वं जगदस्य जगत्पतेः
मूलस्येवोपघातेन वृक्षः पुष्पफलोपगः
verses.transliteration:
pīḍayā pīḍitaṁ sarvaṁ jagadasya jagatpateḥ
mūlasyevopaghātena vṛkṣaḥ puṣpaphalopagaḥ

translations.english: The entire earth is distressed on account of the distress of this lord of the earth, even like a tree bearing blossoms and fruits, when its roots have been severed.

verses.sanskrit:
ते लक्ष्मण इव क्षिप्रं सपत्न्यः सहबान्धवाः
गच्छन्तमनुगच्छामो येन गच्छति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
te lakṣmaṇa iva kṣipraṁ sapatnyaḥ sahabāndhavāḥ
gacchantamanugacchāmo yena gacchati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, accompanied by our wives and friends will we like Lakşmaņa follow the departing Rāghava by the same way that he takes.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यानानि परित्यज्य क्षेत्राणि च गृहाणि च
एकदुःखसुखा राममनुगच्छाम धार्मिकम्
verses.transliteration:
udyānāni parityajya kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca
ekaduḥkhasukhā rāmamanugacchāma dhārmikam

translations.english: And leaving aside our gardens and fields and abodes, will we, making the righteous Rāma's happiness and misery our own, follow him.

verses.sanskrit:
वनं नगरमेवास्तु येन गच्छति राघवः
अस्माभिश्च परित्यक्तं पुरं संपद्यतां वनम्
verses.transliteration:
vanaṁ nagaramevāstu yena gacchati rāghavaḥ
asmābhiśca parityaktaṁ puraṁ saṁpadyatāṁ vanam

translations.english: Let the forest to which Rāghava repairs resemble a city, and let this city renounced by as be converted into a wilderness.

verses.sanskrit:
बिलानि दंष्ट्रिणः सर्वे सानूनि मृगपक्षिणः
अस्मत्त्यक्तं प्रपद्यन्तां सेव्यमानं त्यजन्तु च
verses.transliteration:
bilāni daṁṣṭriṇaḥ sarve sānūni mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
asmattyaktaṁ prapadyantāṁ sevyamānaṁ tyajantu ca

translations.english: Inspired by the fear of us, serpents will leave their holes, and beats and birds the caves of mountains, and elephants and lions the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं विविधा वाचो नानाजनसमीरिताः
शुश्राव रामः श्रुत्वा च न विचक्रेऽस्य मानसम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ vividhā vāco nānājanasamīritāḥ
śuśrāva rāmaḥ śrutvā ca na vicakre'sya mānasam

translations.english: Rāghava heard various words uttered thus by the populace; and having heard them he did not suffer his mind to be agitated. And that righteous one of the prowess of a mad elephant, form a distance began to make for the residence of his father resembiing in brightness a summit of the Kailasa mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतीक्षमाणोऽभिजनं तदार्त;मनार्तरूपः प्रहसन्निवाथ
जगाम रामः पितरं दिदृक्षुः; पितुर्निदेशं विधिवच्चिकीर्षुः
verses.transliteration:
pratīkṣamāṇo'bhijanaṁ tadārta;manārtarūpaḥ prahasannivātha
jagāma rāmaḥ pitaraṁ didṛkṣuḥ; piturnideśaṁ vidhivaccikīrṣuḥ

translations.english: Seeing that well-wisher of his thus depressed, Rāma endeavouring by all means to do his father's bidding, cheerfully went on, desirous of beholding his sire.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्पूर्वमैक्ष्वाकसुतो महात्मा; रामो गमिष्यन्वनमार्तरूपम्
व्यतिष्ठत प्रेक्ष्य तदा सुमन्त्रं; पितुर्महात्मा प्रतिहारणार्थम्
verses.transliteration:
tatpūrvamaikṣvākasuto mahātmā; rāmo gamiṣyanvanamārtarūpam
vyatiṣṭhata prekṣya tadā sumantraṁ; piturmahātmā pratihāraṇārtham

translations.english: And with the view of meeting the aggrieved king before repairing to the forest, the magnanimous son of the Ikşvāku race, seeing Sumantra, stayed there, so that that nobleminded one might inform his father of his visit.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्निदेशेन तु धर्मवत्सलो; वनप्रवेशे कृतबुद्धिनिश्चयः
स राघवः प्रेक्ष्य सुमन्त्रमब्रवी;न्निवेदयस्वागमनं नृपाय मे
verses.transliteration:
piturnideśena tu dharmavatsalo; vanapraveśe kṛtabuddhiniścayaḥ
sa rāghavaḥ prekṣya sumantramabravī;nnivedayasvāgamanaṁ nṛpāya me

translations.english: And making up his mind to go to the woods in accordance with the command of his father, Rāghava seeing Sumantra, said to him; “Do you inform the king of my arrival. to

verses.sanskrit:
स रामप्रेषितः क्षिप्रं संतापकलुषेन्द्रियः
प्रविश्य नृपतिं सूतो निःश्वसन्तं ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmapreṣitaḥ kṣipraṁ saṁtāpakaluṣendriyaḥ
praviśya nṛpatiṁ sūto niḥśvasantaṁ dadarśa ha

translations.english: Then the mighty and incomparable Rāma of eyes resembling lotus-petals said the charioteer, "Do you announce me to my father.” Thus commissioned by Rāma, the charioteer entering the apartment, found the king heaving sighs, his senses overwhelmed with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
आलोक्य तु महाप्राज्ञः परमाकुल चेतसम्
राममेवानुशोचन्तं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरासदत्
verses.transliteration:
ālokya tu mahāprājñaḥ paramākula cetasam
rāmamevānuśocantaṁ sūtaḥ prāñjalirāsadat

translations.english: And he saw the monarch like the sun afflicted by Rāhu, or like fire enveloped in ashes, or like a i tank deprived of its waters. Thereupon concluding that the king agitated by sorrow was bewailing Rāma, the charioteer said with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं स पुरुषव्याघ्र द्वारि तिष्ठति ते सुतः
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा सर्वं चैवोपजीविनाम्
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ sa puruṣavyāghra dvāri tiṣṭhati te sutaḥ
brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṁ dattvā sarvaṁ caivopajīvinām

translations.english: O foremost of men, your son waits at the entrance, after having distributed wealth to Brāhmaṇas and his retinue. Let that one having truth for prowess, good betide you, see you. Having greeted all his friends, he now wishes to see you. Know that he is about to set out for the mighty forest. Do you, O Lord of earth, see him furnished with every perfection, like the Sun himself surrounded by his rays.:

verses.sanskrit:
स सत्यवादी धर्मात्मा गाम्भीर्यात्सागरोपमः
आकाश इव निष्पङ्को नरेन्द्रः प्रत्युवाच तम्
verses.transliteration:
sa satyavādī dharmātmā gāmbhīryātsāgaropamaḥ
ākāśa iva niṣpaṅko narendraḥ pratyuvāca tam

translations.english: Thereupon, that virtuous and truthful (king) resembling the ocean by virtue of his gravity, and motionless like the welkin, answered Sumantra, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रानय मे दारान्ये केचिदिह मामकाः
दारैः परिवृतः सर्वैर्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
sumantrānaya me dārānye kecidiha māmakāḥ
dāraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvairdraṣṭumicchāmi rāghavam

translations.english: O Sumantra, you bring hither my wives. who are here. I wish to see Rāma accompained with my wives.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽन्तःपुरमतीत्यैव स्त्रियस्ता वाक्यमब्रवीत्
आर्यो ह्वयति वो राजा गम्यतां तत्र माचिरम्
verses.transliteration:
so'ntaḥpuramatītyaiva striyastā vākyamabravīt
āryo hvayati vo rājā gamyatāṁ tatra māciram

translations.english: Reaching the inner apartment, the charioteer said to the ladies, “The worshipful king calls you. Do you come speedily."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः सुमन्त्रेण नृपाज्ञया
प्रचक्रमुस्तद्भवनं भर्तुराज्ञाय शासनम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ sumantreṇa nṛpājñayā
pracakramustadbhavanaṁ bharturājñāya śāsanam

translations.english: Thus addressed by Sumantra at the mandate of the monarch, the ladies in a body, informed of their husband's command, went to the king's apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्धसप्तशतास्तास्तु प्रमदास्ताम्रलोचनाः
कौसल्यां परिवार्याथ शनैर्जग्मुर्धृतव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
ardhasaptaśatāstāstu pramadāstāmralocanāḥ
kausalyāṁ parivāryātha śanairjagmurdhṛtavratāḥ

translations.english: And three hundred and fifty females furnished with coppery eyes and observing vows, surrounding Kausalyā, proceeded slowly.

verses.sanskrit:
आगतेषु च दारेषु समवेक्ष्य महीपतिः
उवाच राजा तं सूतं सुमन्त्रानय मे सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
āgateṣu ca dāreṣu samavekṣya mahīpatiḥ
uvāca rājā taṁ sūtaṁ sumantrānaya me sutam

translations.english: On the females coming there, the monarch seeing this, said to the charioteer, “O Sumantra, do you bring hither my son."

verses.sanskrit:
स सूतो राममादाय लक्ष्मणं मैथिलीं तदा
जगामाभिमुखस्तूर्णं सकाशं जगतीपतेः
verses.transliteration:
sa sūto rāmamādāya lakṣmaṇaṁ maithilīṁ tadā
jagāmābhimukhastūrṇaṁ sakāśaṁ jagatīpateḥ

translations.english: Thereat the charioteer taking Răma, Lakşmaņa an Mithila's daughter, speedily came before the lord of earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा पुत्रमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा दूरात्कृताञ्जलिम्
उत्पपातासनात्तूर्णमार्तः स्त्रीजनसंवृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā putramāyāntaṁ dṛṣṭvā dūrātkṛtāñjalim
utpapātāsanāttūrṇamārtaḥ strījanasaṁvṛtaḥ

translations.english: The king seeing his son drawing nigh with joined hands, nastily rose up from his seat in company with his wives.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिदुद्राव वेगेन रामं दृष्ट्वा विशां पतिः
तमसंप्राप्य दुःखार्तः पपात भुवि मूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
so'bhidudrāva vegena rāmaṁ dṛṣṭvā viśāṁ patiḥ
tamasaṁprāpya duḥkhārtaḥ papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And casting his eyes on Rāma, the king rushed towards him, but before reaching his son, the aggrieved monarch fell down to the earth in a Swoon.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रामोऽभ्यपातत्क्षिप्रं लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः
विसंज्ञमिव दुःखेन सशोकं नृपतिं तदा
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rāmo'bhyapātatkṣipraṁ lakṣmaṇaśca mahārathaḥ
visaṁjñamiva duḥkhena saśokaṁ nṛpatiṁ tadā

translations.english: Rāma and that mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa swiftly neared the king stricken with grief and rendered senseless by sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रीसहस्रनिनादश्च संजज्ञे राजवेश्मनि
हाहा रामेति सहसा भूषणध्वनिमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
strīsahasraninādaśca saṁjajñe rājaveśmani
hāhā rāmeti sahasā bhūṣaṇadhvanimūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And there arose in the palace cries of women by thousands of "Ah Rāma,” mingled with the tinkling of ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
तं परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
पर्यङ्के सीतया सार्धं रुदन्तः समवेशयन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṁ tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
paryaṅke sītayā sārdhaṁ rudantaḥ samaveśayan

translations.english: Then both Rāma and Lakşmaņa along with Sītā took the king up with their arms, and with tears in their eyes laid him upon the couch.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रामो मुहूर्तेन लब्धसंज्ञं महीपतिम्
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा शोकार्णवपरिप्लुतम्
verses.transliteration:
atha rāmo muhūrtena labdhasaṁjñaṁ mahīpatim
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā śokārṇavapariplutam

translations.english: When the lord of the earth oppressed with the vapour begot of grief and overwhelmed with emotion, had regained his senses, Rāma with joined palms said.

verses.sanskrit:
आपृच्छे त्वां महाराज सर्वेषामीश्वरोऽसि नः
प्रस्थितं दण्डकारण्यं पश्य त्वं कुशलेन माम्
verses.transliteration:
āpṛcche tvāṁ mahārāja sarveṣāmīśvaro'si naḥ
prasthitaṁ daṇḍakāraṇyaṁ paśya tvaṁ kuśalena mām

translations.english: I ask you, O mighty monarch, as you are the lord of us all. Do you see me safely despatched to the forest of Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणं चानुजानीहि सीता चान्वेति मां वनम्
कारणैर्बहुभिस्तथ्यैर्वार्यमाणौ न चेच्छतः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaṁ cānujānīhi sītā cānveti māṁ vanam
kāraṇairbahubhistathyairvāryamāṇau na cecchataḥ

translations.english: Do you permit Lakşmaņa, and let Sītā also follow me to the woods; for although prohibited by me with various reasons, they do not wish to be left behind. Do you O bestower of honour, permit us all, renouncing sorrow, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā and me, like Prajāpati permitting his sons.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतीक्षमाणमव्यग्रमनुज्ञां जगतीपतेः
उवाच रर्जा संप्रेक्ष्य वनवासाय राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
pratīkṣamāṇamavyagramanujñāṁ jagatīpateḥ
uvāca rarjā saṁprekṣya vanavāsāya rāghavam

translations.english: Seeing Rāghava about to set out for the forest, the lord of earth said to the calm Rāma waiting for his orders.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं राघव कैकेय्या वरदानेन मोहितः
अयोध्यायास्त्वमेवाद्य भव राजा निगृह्य माम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ rāghava kaikeyyā varadānena mohitaḥ
ayodhyāyāstvamevādya bhava rājā nigṛhya mām

translations.english: O Rāghava, I have been deprived of my senses in consequence of my having conferred boons on Kaikeyi. Do you therefore confining me to-day become king in Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो नृपतिना रामो धर्मभृतां वरः
प्रत्युवाचाञ्जलिं कृत्वा पितरं वाक्यकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
evamukto nṛpatinā rāmo dharmabhṛtāṁ varaḥ
pratyuvācāñjaliṁ kṛtvā pitaraṁ vākyakovidaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the monarch, Rāma, the best of the righteous, well versed in speech, with joined hands addressed his father thus.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्वर्षसहस्राय पृथिव्या नृपते पतिः
अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि न मे कार्यं त्वयानृतम्
verses.transliteration:
bhavānvarṣasahasrāya pṛthivyā nṛpate patiḥ
ahaṁ tvaraṇye vatsyāmi na me kāryaṁ tvayānṛtam

translations.english: O king, do you rule this earth for a thousand years, I will reside in the forest. I do not wish for the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयसे वृद्धये तात पुनरागमनाय च
गच्छस्वारिष्टमव्यग्रः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्
verses.transliteration:
śreyase vṛddhaye tāta punarāgamanāya ca
gacchasvāriṣṭamavyagraḥ panthānamakutobhayam

translations.english: Do you, my darling, with the view of attaining welfare here and hereafter and auspicious fortune, go calmly your fearless way, so that you may return hither (in time.)

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य त्विदानीं रजनीं पुत्र मा गच्छ सर्वथा
मातरं मां च संपश्यन्वसेमामद्य शर्वरीम्
तर्पितः सर्वकामैस्त्वं श्वःकाले साधयिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
adya tvidānīṁ rajanīṁ putra mā gaccha sarvathā
mātaraṁ māṁ ca saṁpaśyanvasemāmadya śarvarīm
tarpitaḥ sarvakāmaistvaṁ śvaḥkāle sādhayiṣyasi

translations.english: Do you, seeing me as well as your mother, stay here to-night, Then ministered to every way, you will set out to-morrow.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रामस्तथा श्रुत्वा पितुरार्तस्य भाषितम्
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा दीनो वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha rāmastathā śrutvā piturārtasya bhāṣitam
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā dīno vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing these words of his distressed father, the humble Rāma, along with his brother Laksmana, said.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्स्यामि यानद्य गुणान्को मे श्वस्तान्प्रदास्यति
अपक्रमणमेवातः सर्वकामैरहं वृणे
verses.transliteration:
prāpsyāmi yānadya guṇānko me śvastānpradāsyati
apakramaṇamevātaḥ sarvakāmairahaṁ vṛṇe

translations.english: Who will confer on me the merit to-morrow that I shall reap by going to-day? Therefore, I prefer even the journey to the woods to enjoying comforts here.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं सराष्ट्रा सजना धनधान्यसमाकुला
मया विसृष्टा वसुधा भरताय प्रदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ sarāṣṭrā sajanā dhanadhānyasamākulā
mayā visṛṣṭā vasudhā bharatāya pradīyatām

translations.english: Do you bestow upon Bharata this earth renounced by me, this kingdom abounding in corn and kine and filled with people; my mind determined upon dwelling in the forest, does not waver. Do you, O bestower of boons, grant Kaikeyi everything that you had promised to her at the time of the war* Another reading is, The boon that you had well-pleased conferred., Another reading, Nor Mithila's daughter., Another reading is, Nor any of these worlds., (you had waged against the Dänavas), and thereby do you follow truth.

verses.sanskrit:
अपगच्छतु ते दुःखं मा भूर्बाष्पपरिप्लुतः
न हि क्षुभ्यति दुर्धर्षः समुद्रः सरितां पतिः
verses.transliteration:
apagacchatu te duḥkhaṁ mā bhūrbāṣpapariplutaḥ
na hi kṣubhyati durdharṣaḥ samudraḥ saritāṁ patiḥ

translations.english: Banish your grief, and suppress your tears. That lord of streams, the irresistible ocean, never forsakes his own magnanimity.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरं च राष्ट्रं च मही च केवला; मया निसृष्टा भरताय दीयताम्
अहं निदेशं भवतोऽनुपालय;न्वनं गमिष्यामि चिराय सेवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
puraṁ ca rāṣṭraṁ ca mahī ca kevalā; mayā nisṛṣṭā bharatāya dīyatām
ahaṁ nideśaṁ bhavato'nupālaya;nvanaṁ gamiṣyāmi cirāya sevitum

translations.english: Do upon Bharata this city and this kingdom and the earth renounced by me. Doing your behest, I will repair to the forest, sojourning there for a long time.

verses.sanskrit:
मया निसृष्टां भरतो महीमिमां; सशैलखण्डां सपुरां सकाननाम्
शिवां सुसीमामनुशास्तु केवलं; त्वया यदुक्तं नृपते यथास्तु तत्
verses.transliteration:
mayā nisṛṣṭāṁ bharato mahīmimāṁ; saśailakhaṇḍāṁ sapurāṁ sakānanām
śivāṁ susīmāmanuśāstu kevalaṁ; tvayā yaduktaṁ nṛpate yathāstu tat

translations.english: Staying at the auspicious frontiers, let Bharata barely rule this earth furnished with watery expanses, cities and forests, when it has been renounced by me. O king, let what you have said be as you wish it.

verses.sanskrit:
न मे तथा पार्थिव धीयते मनो; महत्सु कामेषु न चात्मनः प्रिये
यथा निदेशे तव शिष्टसंमते; व्यपैतु दुःखं तव मत्कृतेऽनघ
verses.transliteration:
na me tathā pārthiva dhīyate mano; mahatsu kāmeṣu na cātmanaḥ priye
yathā nideśe tava śiṣṭasaṁmate; vyapaitu duḥkhaṁ tava matkṛte'nagha

translations.english: You confer I do not, O king, set my heart upon any great object of desire, nor do I seek my own behoof, as I am bent upon, O you beloved of the good, working out your will. O sinless one, you will not therefore reap any evil on my account.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्य नैवानघ राज्यमव्ययं; न सर्वकामान्न सुखं न मैथिलीम्
न जीवितं त्वामनृतेन योजय;न्वृणीय सत्यं व्रतमस्तु ते तथा
verses.transliteration:
tadadya naivānagha rājyamavyayaṁ; na sarvakāmānna sukhaṁ na maithilīm
na jīvitaṁ tvāmanṛtena yojaya;nvṛṇīya satyaṁ vratamastu te tathā

translations.english: Associating you with untruth, I would not, O sinless one, wish even for your company who are agitated with anxiety,* or this entire kingdom, or every object of desire, or the earth, or Mithilā's daughter. Even this is my truthful vow, let also your vow prove true. *Some texts, Living.

verses.sanskrit:
फलानि मूलानि च भक्षयन्वने; गिरींश्च पश्यन्सरितः सरांसि च
वनं प्रविश्यैव विचित्रपादपं; सुखी भविष्यामि तवास्तु निर्वृतिः
verses.transliteration:
phalāni mūlāni ca bhakṣayanvane; girīṁśca paśyansaritaḥ sarāṁsi ca
vanaṁ praviśyaiva vicitrapādapaṁ; sukhī bhaviṣyāmi tavāstu nirvṛtiḥ

translations.english: Living upon fruits and roots in the forest, and surveying mountains and tanks and streams and graceful trees, I shall be happy on entering the forest. Do you cease to lament.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुमन्त्रमैक्ष्वाकः पीडितोऽत्र प्रतिज्ञया
सबाष्पमतिनिःश्वस्य जगादेदं पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sumantramaikṣvākaḥ pīḍito'tra pratijñayā
sabāṣpamatiniḥśvasya jagādedaṁ punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Then that descendant of Ikṣvāku afflicted because of his promise, sighing and his heart filled with the vapour begot of sorrow, again addressed Sumantra, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सूत रत्नसुसंपूर्णा चतुर्विधबला चमूः
रागवस्यानुयात्रार्थं क्षिप्रं प्रतिविधीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
sūta ratnasusaṁpūrṇā caturvidhabalā camūḥ
rāgavasyānuyātrārthaṁ kṣipraṁ pratividhīyatām

translations.english: O charioteer, do you speedily Marshall the army consisting of the four kinds of forces for following Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
रूपाजीवा च शालिन्यो वणिजश्च महाधनाः
शोभयन्तु कुमारस्य वाहिनीं सुप्रसारिताः
verses.transliteration:
rūpājīvā ca śālinyo vaṇijaśca mahādhanāḥ
śobhayantu kumārasya vāhinīṁ suprasāritāḥ

translations.english: Let sweet-speeched courtesans and opulent traders grace the extensive army of the prince.

verses.sanskrit:
ये चैनमुपजीवन्ति रमते यैश्च वीर्यतः
तेषां बहुविधं दत्त्वा तानप्यत्र नियोजय
verses.transliteration:
ye cainamupajīvanti ramate yaiśca vīryataḥ
teṣāṁ bahuvidhaṁ dattvā tānapyatra niyojaya

translations.english: Giving them immense wealth, do you also send with him those that depend on Rāma, as well as those with whom he delights to wrestle.

verses.sanskrit:
निघ्नन्मृगान्कुञ्जरांश्च पिबंश्चारण्यकं मधु
नदीश्च विविधाः पश्यन्न राज्यं संस्मरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nighnanmṛgānkuñjarāṁśca pibaṁścāraṇyakaṁ madhu
nadīśca vividhāḥ paśyanna rājyaṁ saṁsmariṣyati

translations.english: Killing deer and elephants, and drinking wild honey, and beholding various rivers, they will ultimately forget this kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
धान्यकोशश्च यः कश्चिद्धनकोशश्च मामकः
तौ राममनुगच्छेतां वसन्तं निर्जने वने
verses.transliteration:
dhānyakośaśca yaḥ kaściddhanakośaśca māmakaḥ
tau rāmamanugacchetāṁ vasantaṁ nirjane vane

translations.english: And let our granary and treasury follow Rāma who is to reside in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
यजन्पुण्येषु देशेषु विसृजंश्चाप्तदक्षिणाः
ऋषिभिश्च समागम्य प्रवत्स्यति सुखं वने
verses.transliteration:
yajanpuṇyeṣu deśeṣu visṛjaṁścāptadakṣiṇāḥ
ṛṣibhiśca samāgamya pravatsyati sukhaṁ vane

translations.english: Performing sacrifices at holy spots, and dispensing the prescribed Dakşiņās, let Rāma happily reside in the forest in the company of saints.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतश्च महाबाहुरयोध्यां पालयिष्यति
सर्वकामैः पुनः श्रीमान्रामः संसाध्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
bharataśca mahābāhurayodhyāṁ pālayiṣyati
sarvakāmaiḥ punaḥ śrīmānrāmaḥ saṁsādhyatāmiti

translations.english: The mighty-armed Bharata will govern Ayodhyā. Therefore, do you furnish the auspicious Rāma with every object of enjoyment.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कैकेय्या भयमागतम्
मुखं चाप्यगमाच्छोषं स्वरश्चापि न्यरुध्यत
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvati kākutsthe kaikeyyā bhayamāgatam
mukhaṁ cāpyagamācchoṣaṁ svaraścāpi nyarudhyata

translations.english: When that descendant of Kākutstha said this, Kaikeyi was inspired with apprehension: her countenance became blank, and her utterance was choked.

verses.sanskrit:
सा विषण्णा च संत्रस्ता कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
राज्यं गतजनं साधो पीतमण्डां सुरामिव
निरास्वाद्यतमं शून्यं भरतो नाभिपत्स्यते
verses.transliteration:
sā viṣaṇṇā ca saṁtrastā kaikeyī vākyamabravīt
rājyaṁ gatajanaṁ sādho pītamaṇḍāṁ surāmiva
nirāsvādyatamaṁ śūnyaṁ bharato nābhipatsyate

translations.english: O righteous one, like to a liquor whose lees alone have been left, Bharata will not receive the kingdom tasteless and denuded of all substance.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्यां मुक्तलज्जायां वदन्त्यामतिदारुणम्
राजा दशरथो वाक्यमुवाचायतलोचनाम्
वहन्तं किं तुदसि मां नियुज्य धुरि माहिते
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyāṁ muktalajjāyāṁ vadantyāmatidāruṇam
rājā daśaratho vākyamuvācāyatalocanām
vahantaṁ kiṁ tudasi māṁ niyujya dhuri māhite

translations.english: While the shameless Kaikeyi was speaking thus sternly, king Dasaratha said to that one of expansive eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेयी द्विगुणं क्रुद्धा राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
तवैव वंशे सगरो ज्येष्ठं पुत्रमुपारुधत्
असमञ्ज इति ख्यातं तथायं गन्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyī dviguṇaṁ kruddhā rājānamidamabravīt
tavaiva vaṁśe sagaro jyeṣṭhaṁ putramupārudhat
asamañja iti khyātaṁ tathāyaṁ gantumarhati

translations.english: Even in this line of yours, Sagara deprived his eldest son Asamañja by name of the enjoyment of the kingdom. In this way this one deserves to go to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो धिगित्येव राजा दशरथोऽब्रवीत्
व्रीडितश्च जनः सर्वः सा च तन्नावबुध्यत
verses.transliteration:
evamukto dhigityeva rājā daśaratho'bravīt
vrīḍitaśca janaḥ sarvaḥ sā ca tannāvabudhyata

translations.english: Thus addressed, king Dasaratha said, "O fire!" and all present were afflicted with shame: but Kaikeyi feigned not to understand all this.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र वृद्धो महामात्रः सिद्धार्थो नाम नामतः
शुचिर्बहुमतो राज्ञः कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatra vṛddho mahāmātraḥ siddhārtho nāma nāmataḥ
śucirbahumato rājñaḥ kaikeyīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Then a notable, aged, pure-spirited personage held in high esteem by the monarch, named Siddhartha, addressed Kaikeyi, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
असमञ्जो गृहीत्वा तु क्रीडितः पथि दारकान्
सरय्वाः प्रक्षिपन्नप्सु रमते तेन दुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
asamañjo gṛhītvā tu krīḍitaḥ pathi dārakān
sarayvāḥ prakṣipannapsu ramate tena durmatiḥ

translations.english: Asamañja by way of sport catching people on the way, used to throw them into the waters of the Sarayū, and that wicked-minded wretch made merry over the same.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा नागरः सर्वे क्रुद्धा राजानमब्रुवन्
असमञ्जं वृषीण्वैकमस्मान्वा राष्ट्रवर्धन
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā nāgaraḥ sarve kruddhā rājānamabruvan
asamañjaṁ vṛṣīṇvaikamasmānvā rāṣṭravardhana

translations.english: Seeing him do so, the citizens in a body, waxing wroth spoke to the monarch, 'O enhancer of the kingdom's prosperity, do you either banish Asamañja or us.'

verses.sanskrit:
तानुवाच ततो राजा किंनिमित्तमिदं भयम्
ताश्चापि राज्ञा संपृष्टा वाक्यं प्रकृतयोऽब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tānuvāca tato rājā kiṁnimittamidaṁ bhayam
tāścāpi rājñā saṁpṛṣṭā vākyaṁ prakṛtayo'bruvan

translations.english: To them he replied, 'Whence is this fear of yours?' Thus asked by the monarch, the subjects said.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रीडितस्त्वेष नः पुत्रान्बालानुद्भ्रान्तचेतनः
सरय्वां प्रक्षिपन्मौर्ख्यादतुलां प्रीतिमश्नुते
verses.transliteration:
krīḍitastveṣa naḥ putrānbālānudbhrāntacetanaḥ
sarayvāṁ prakṣipanmaurkhyādatulāṁ prītimaśnute

translations.english: “Through his impudence this one of perverted sense by way of diversion throwing our sons into the Sarayū, finds extreme delight.'

verses.sanskrit:
स तासां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रकृतीनां नराधिप
तं तत्याजाहितं पुत्रं तासां प्रियचिकीर्षया
verses.transliteration:
sa tāsāṁ vacanaṁ śrutvā prakṛtīnāṁ narādhipa
taṁ tatyājāhitaṁ putraṁ tāsāṁ priyacikīrṣayā

translations.english: Hearing these words of his subjects, that lord of men, with the intention of doing good to them, forsook that mischievous son of his.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमत्यजद्राजा सगरो वै सुधार्मिकः
रामः किमकरोत्पापं येनैवमुपरुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
ityevamatyajadrājā sagaro vai sudhārmikaḥ
rāmaḥ kimakarotpāpaṁ yenaivamuparudhyate

translations.english: Thereupon that worker of iniquity went to the forest and went about seeing mountain fastnesses. Thus did the virtuous king Sagara renounce his son. But what offence has Rāma committed that he is to be banished?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु सिद्धार्थवचो राजा श्रान्ततरस्वनः
शोकोपहतया वाचा कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu siddhārthavaco rājā śrāntatarasvanaḥ
śokopahatayā vācā kaikeyīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Siddhārtha's words, the king, his voice waxing exceedingly feeble, addressed Kaikeyī in words surcharged with emotion.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुव्रजिष्याम्यहमद्य रामं; राज्यं परित्यज्य सुखं धनं च
सहैव राज्ञा भरतेन च त्वं; यथा सुखं भुङ्क्ष्व चिराय राज्यम्
verses.transliteration:
anuvrajiṣyāmyahamadya rāmaṁ; rājyaṁ parityajya sukhaṁ dhanaṁ ca
sahaiva rājñā bharatena ca tvaṁ; yathā sukhaṁ bhuṅkṣva cirāya rājyam

translations.english: Forsaking my kingdom, forsaking happiness and treasures, I will to-day follow Rāma. Do you with Bharata for the king, forever enjoy dominion according to your heart's desire.

verses.sanskrit:
महामात्रवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथं तदा
अन्वभाषत वाक्यं तु विनयज्ञो विनीतवत्
verses.transliteration:
mahāmātravacaḥ śrutvā rāmo daśarathaṁ tadā
anvabhāṣata vākyaṁ tu vinayajño vinītavat

translations.english: Hearing the words of that worthy, Rāma conversant with modesty, humbly addressed Dasaratha, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्तभोगस्य मे राजन्वने वन्येन जीवतः
किं कार्यमनुयात्रेण त्यक्तसङ्गस्य सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
tyaktabhogasya me rājanvane vanyena jīvataḥ
kiṁ kāryamanuyātreṇa tyaktasaṅgasya sarvataḥ

translations.english: What O king, have I, that am renouncing everything and am going to dwell in the forest subsisting on what the forest yields, to do with a following?

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि दत्त्वा द्विपश्रेष्ठं कक्ष्यायां कुरुते मनः
रज्जुस्नेहेन किं तस्य त्यजतः कुञ्जरोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
yo hi dattvā dvipaśreṣṭhaṁ kakṣyāyāṁ kurute manaḥ
rajjusnehena kiṁ tasya tyajataḥ kuñjarottamam

translations.english: Of what avail is a person's attachment for the tether of a goodly elephant, when the elephant itself is renounced by him?

verses.sanskrit:
तथा मम सतां श्रेष्ठ किं ध्वजिन्या जगत्पते
सर्वाण्येवानुजानामि चीराण्येवानयन्तु मे
verses.transliteration:
tathā mama satāṁ śreṣṭha kiṁ dhvajinyā jagatpate
sarvāṇyevānujānāmi cīrāṇyevānayantu me

translations.english: Thus it is with me, O foremost of righteous ones. What shal! I do with the army, O lord of men? I will confer everything on Bharata. Let them bring me a venture of bark.

verses.sanskrit:
खनित्रपिटके चोभे ममानयत गच्छतः
चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वसतो मम
verses.transliteration:
khanitrapiṭake cobhe mamānayata gacchataḥ
caturdaśa vane vāsaṁ varṣāṇi vasato mama

translations.english: And for me who will go to the forest and reside there for fourteen years, bring a hoe and a basket.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ चीराणि कैकेयी स्वयमाहृत्य राघवम्
उवाच परिधत्स्वेति जनौघे निरपत्रपा
verses.transliteration:
atha cīrāṇi kaikeyī svayamāhṛtya rāghavam
uvāca paridhatsveti janaughe nirapatrapā

translations.english: Thereupon Kaikeyi herself brought a bark dress and that shameless one said to Rāghava in the presence of all, “Do you wear this.”

verses.sanskrit:
स चीरे पुरुषव्याघ्रः कैकेय्याः प्रतिगृह्य ते
सूक्ष्मवस्त्रमवक्षिप्य मुनिवस्त्राण्यवस्त ह
verses.transliteration:
sa cīre puruṣavyāghraḥ kaikeyyāḥ pratigṛhya te
sūkṣmavastramavakṣipya munivastrāṇyavasta ha

translations.english: On this, that foremost of men taking those two pieces of bark from Kaikeyi, left his fine attire and put on the ascetic garb.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि तत्रैव विहाय वसने शुभे
तापसाच्छादने चैव जग्राह पितुरग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaścāpi tatraiva vihāya vasane śubhe
tāpasācchādane caiva jagrāha pituragrataḥ

translations.english: And Lakşmaņa also, renouncing his choice raiment, put on the dress of an anchorite before his father.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा कण्ठे च सा चीरमेकमादाय पाणिना
तस्थौ ह्यकुषला तत्र व्रीडिता जनकात्मज
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca sā cīramekamādāya pāṇinā
