tasthau hyakuṣalā tatra vrīḍitā janakātmaja

translations.english: Putting on one piece on her neck and holding the other in her hand, the daughter of Janaka, feeling uneasy, stood overpowered with shame.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तत्क्षिप्रमागम्य रामो धर्मभृतां वरः
चीरं बबन्ध सीतायाः कौशेयस्योपरि स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstatkṣipramāgamya rāmo dharmabhṛtāṁ varaḥ
cīraṁ babandha sītāyāḥ kauśeyasyopari svayam

translations.english: Thereupon that best of righteous persons, Rāma, speedily coming up to her, fastened the monastic garb over Sītā's silk attire.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां चीरं वसानायां नाथवत्यामनाथवत्
प्रचुक्रोश जनः सर्वो धिक्त्वां दशरथं त्विति
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ cīraṁ vasānāyāṁ nāthavatyāmanāthavat
pracukrośa janaḥ sarvo dhiktvāṁ daśarathaṁ tviti

translations.english: When Şītā, having a husband although seeming as if she had none, was putting on the ascetic guise, the people got into a wrath and exclaimed, “O Dasaratha, fie on you!"

verses.sanskrit:
स निःश्वस्योष्णमैक्ष्वाकस्तां भार्यामिदमब्रवीत्
कैकेयि कुशचीरेण न सीता गन्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
sa niḥśvasyoṣṇamaikṣvākastāṁ bhāryāmidamabravīt
kaikeyi kuśacīreṇa na sītā gantumarhati

translations.english: Aggrieved at the uproar that arose there in consequence, the lord of earth banished from his heart all regard for life, virtue, and fame. And sighing hot, that descendant of Ikşvāku spoke to that wife of his, saying, O Kaikeyi, Sītā deserves not to go in a Kuća dress.

verses.sanskrit:
ननु पर्याप्तमेतत्ते पापे रामविवासनम्
किमेभिः कृपणैर्भूयः पातकैरपि ते कृतैः
verses.transliteration:
nanu paryāptametatte pāpe rāmavivāsanam
kimebhiḥ kṛpaṇairbhūyaḥ pātakairapi te kṛtaiḥ

translations.english: Surely, O nefarious one, the banishment of Ráma is enough for you. Why then do you bend your mind to perpetrate these atrocious sins?

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवन्तं पितरं रामः संप्रस्थितो वनम्
अवाक्शिरसमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvantaṁ pitaraṁ rāmaḥ saṁprasthito vanam
avākśirasamāsīnamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thus commissioned to the forest, Räma who was seated sealing his lips, said.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं धार्मिक कौसल्या मम माता यशस्विनी
वृद्धा चाक्षुद्रशीला च न च त्वां देवगर्हिते
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ dhārmika kausalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī
vṛddhā cākṣudraśīlā ca na ca tvāṁ devagarhite

translations.english: O righteous one, this my mother is aged and famous and of lofty spirit. May she not meet with improper treatment at your hands! It behoves you, O bestower of boons, to show greater honour to her when she shall be deprived of me and be plunged into a sea of grief and afflicted with unprecedented woe.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां महेन्द्रोपमजातगर्भिणीं; तथा विधातुं जनमीं ममार्हसि
यथा वनस्थे मयि शोककर्शिता; न जीवितं न्यस्य यमक्षयं व्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ mahendropamajātagarbhiṇīṁ; tathā vidhātuṁ janamīṁ mamārhasi
yathā vanasthe mayi śokakarśitā; na jīvitaṁ nyasya yamakṣayaṁ vrajet

translations.english: O you comparable to the mighty Indra, you should so behove with my mother smitten with my separation, that exercised by grief in consequence of my residence in the forest, she may not, renouncing life, repair to the mansions of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा मुनिवेषधरं च तम्
समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगतचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā muniveṣadharaṁ ca tam
samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigatacetanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words, and seeing him dressed like an ascetic, the king in the midst of his wives was deprived of his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
नैनं दुःखेन संतप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत राघवम्
न चैनमभिसंप्रेक्ष्य प्रत्यभाषत दुर्मनाः
verses.transliteration:
nainaṁ duḥkhena saṁtaptaḥ pratyavaikṣata rāghavam
na cainamabhisaṁprekṣya pratyabhāṣata durmanāḥ

translations.english: And burning in grief, the king could not eye Rāghava, nor seeing him could that one of arilicted mind answer anything.

verses.sanskrit:
स मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञो दुःखितश्च महीपतिः
विललाप महाबाहू राममेवानुचिन्तयन्
verses.transliteration:
sa muhūrtamivāsaṁjño duḥkhitaśca mahīpatiḥ
vilalāpa mahābāhū rāmamevānucintayan

translations.english: Then remaining unconscious for a while, the mighty-armed lord of earth oppressed by grief began to bewail, thinking of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये खलु मया पूर्वं विवत्सा बहवः कृताः
प्राणिनो हिंसिता वापि तस्मादिदमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
manye khalu mayā pūrvaṁ vivatsā bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ
prāṇino hiṁsitā vāpi tasmādidamupasthitam

translations.english: I conclude that formerly I deprived many a cow of her calf, and took the life of many creature, and it is for this that the present calamity has befallen me.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वेवानागते काले देहाच्च्यवति जीवितम्
कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानस्य मृत्युर्मम न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
na tvevānāgate kāle dehāccyavati jīvitam
kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyurmama na vidyate

translations.english: (I infer) that life never departs from the body unless the time comes, for although sore tried by Kaikeyſ, my life does not go out of me, and for I can see before me this one resembling fire, clad in the dress of an ascetic, having left his fine venture.

verses.sanskrit:
एकस्याः खलु कैकेय्याः कृतेऽयं क्लिश्यते जनः
स्वार्थे प्रयतमानायाः संश्रित्य निकृतिं त्विमाम्
verses.transliteration:
ekasyāḥ khalu kaikeyyāḥ kṛte'yaṁ kliśyate janaḥ
svārthe prayatamānāyāḥ saṁśritya nikṛtiṁ tvimām

translations.english: These people are in trouble in consequence of Kaikeyi alone striving by help of this craftiness to secure her interest.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं बाष्पेण पिहितेक्ष्णह
रामेति सकृदेवोक्त्वा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu vacanaṁ bāṣpeṇa pihitekṣṇaha
rāmeti sakṛdevoktvā vyāhartuṁ na śaśāka ha

translations.english: Having said these words, Dasaratha, his senses overpowered by the vapour of sorrow, exclaimed "Rāma!” and could not proceed further.

verses.sanskrit:
संज्ञां तु प्रतिलभ्यैव मुहूर्तात्स महीपतिः
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁjñāṁ tu pratilabhyaiva muhūrtātsa mahīpatiḥ
netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāṁ sumantramidamabravīt

translations.english: Then soon regaining consciousness, the lord of earth with tearful eyes, addressed Sumantra, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
औपवाह्यं रथं युक्त्वा त्वमायाहि हयोत्तमैः
प्रापयैनं महाभागमितो जनपदात्परम्
verses.transliteration:
aupavāhyaṁ rathaṁ yuktvā tvamāyāhi hayottamaiḥ
prāpayainaṁ mahābhāgamito janapadātparam

translations.english: Yoking a riding car with excellent horses, do you come hither; and take the exalted one to the south of the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं मन्ये गुणवतां गुणानां फलमुच्यते
पित्रा मात्रा च यत्साधुर्वीरो निर्वास्यते वनम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ manye guṇavatāṁ guṇānāṁ phalamucyate
pitrā mātrā ca yatsādhurvīro nirvāsyate vanam

translations.english: The virtuous and heroic Rāma is being banished by his father and, mother Even this methinks will be asserted as the fruit of the virtues possessed by the pious.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञो वचनमाज्ञाय सुमन्त्रः शीघ्रविक्रमः
योजयित्वाययौ तत्र रथमश्वैरलंकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
rājño vacanamājñāya sumantraḥ śīghravikramaḥ
yojayitvāyayau tatra rathamaśvairalaṁkṛtam

translations.english: Receiving the mandate of the sovereign, Sumantra endued with fleet vigour, yoking a car adorned with horses, came there.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रथं राजपुत्राय सूतः कनकभूषितम्
आचचक्षेऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rathaṁ rājaputrāya sūtaḥ kanakabhūṣitam
ācacakṣe'ñjaliṁ kṛtvā yuktaṁ paramavājibhiḥ

translations.english: Then the charioteer with joined hands announced to the prince that the car adorned with gold was ready, yoked with excellent horses.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा सत्वरमाहूय व्यापृतं वित्तसंचये
उवाच देशकालज्ञो निश्चितं सर्वतः शुचि
verses.transliteration:
rājā satvaramāhūya vyāpṛtaṁ vittasaṁcaye
uvāca deśakālajño niścitaṁ sarvataḥ śuci

translations.english: The king, versed in time and place, and pure, speedily summoning his treasurer, said to him these words firmly.

verses.sanskrit:
वासांसि च महार्हाणि भूषणानि वराणि च
वर्षाण्येतानि संख्याय वैदेह्याः क्षिप्रमानय
verses.transliteration:
vāsāṁsi ca mahārhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca
varṣāṇyetāni saṁkhyāya vaidehyāḥ kṣipramānaya

translations.english: Do you without delay bring to Vaidehī excellent and costly attires and noble ornaments, counting these (ten and four) years.

verses.sanskrit:
नरेन्द्रेणैवमुक्तस्तु गत्वा कोशगृहं ततः
प्रायच्छत्सर्वमाहृत्य सीतायै क्षिप्रमेव तत्
verses.transliteration:
narendreṇaivamuktastu gatvā kośagṛhaṁ tataḥ
prāyacchatsarvamāhṛtya sītāyai kṣiprameva tat

translations.english: Thus desired by the foremost of men, that officer repairing to the treasury, procuring all those, speedily presented them to Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
सा सुजाता सुजातानि वैदेही प्रस्थिता वनम्
भूषयामास गात्राणि तैर्विचित्रैर्विभूषणैः
verses.transliteration:
sā sujātā sujātāni vaidehī prasthitā vanam
bhūṣayāmāsa gātrāṇi tairvicitrairvibhūṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon that pure-sprung one, Vaidehi, ordered to the forest, adorned her goodly limbs with those rare ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यराजयत वैदेही वेश्म तत्सुविभूषिता
उद्यतोंऽशुमतः काले खं प्रभेव विवस्वतः
verses.transliteration:
vyarājayata vaidehī veśma tatsuvibhūṣitā
udyatoṁ'śumataḥ kāle khaṁ prabheva vivasvataḥ

translations.english: Thus decked out, Vaidehī graced that chamber like the effulgence of the Sun irradiating the welkin with his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
तां भुजाभ्यां परिष्वज्य श्वश्रूर्वचनमब्रवीत्
अनाचरन्तीं कृपणं मूध्न्युपाघ्राय मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ bhujābhyāṁ pariṣvajya śvaśrūrvacanamabravīt
anācarantīṁ kṛpaṇaṁ mūdhnyupāghrāya maithilīm

translations.english: Then embracing with her arms Mithila's daughter of noble behaviour, and smelling the crown of her head, Sītā's mother-in-law said.

verses.sanskrit:
असत्यः सर्वलोकेऽस्मिन्सततं सत्कृताः प्रियैः
भर्तारं नानुमन्यन्ते विनिपातगतं स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
asatyaḥ sarvaloke'sminsatataṁ satkṛtāḥ priyaiḥ
bhartāraṁ nānumanyante vinipātagataṁ striyaḥ

translations.english: Those women that although having always been carefully tended by their husbands, do not regard them during the incident of adversity, are in this world reckoned as unchaste.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वया नावमन्तव्यः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो मम
तव दैवतमस्त्वेष निर्धनः सधनोऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
sa tvayā nāvamantavyaḥ putraḥ pravrājito mama
tava daivatamastveṣa nirdhanaḥ sadhano'pi vā

translations.english: Therefore although my son is going to be banished to the woods, you should by no means disregard him. Whether he be wealthy or poor, he is to you like a god.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञाय वचनं सीता तस्या धर्मार्थसंहितम्
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदं श्वश्रूमभिमुखे स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
vijñāya vacanaṁ sītā tasyā dharmārthasaṁhitam
kṛtāñjaliruvācedaṁ śvaśrūmabhimukhe sthitā

translations.english: Hearing her mother-in-law's words fraught with virtue and interest, Sītā facing that lady, said with joined palms.

verses.sanskrit:
करिष्ये सर्वमेवाहमार्या यदनुशास्ति माम्
अभिज्ञास्मि यथा भर्तुर्वर्तितव्यं श्रुतं च मे
verses.transliteration:
kariṣye sarvamevāhamāryā yadanuśāsti mām
abhijñāsmi yathā bharturvartitavyaṁ śrutaṁ ca me

translations.english: I will do all that the noble one says. I know how I should act by my husband. I have heard all about that (from my parents.)

verses.sanskrit:
न मामसज्जनेनार्या समानयितुमर्हति
धर्माद्विचलितुं नाहमलं चन्द्रादिव प्रभा
verses.transliteration:
na māmasajjanenāryā samānayitumarhati
dharmādvicalituṁ nāhamalaṁ candrādiva prabhā

translations.english: The worshipful one ought not to place me on the same footing with unrighteous persons. As brightness does not depart from the moon, so I cannot swerve from virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
नातन्त्री वाद्यते वीणा नाचक्रो वर्तते रथः
नापतिः सुखमेधते या स्यादपि शतात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
nātantrī vādyate vīṇā nācakro vartate rathaḥ
nāpatiḥ sukhamedhate yā syādapi śatātmajā

translations.english: The Viņā without strings does not sound; and the car without wheels does not move, so although having an hundred sons, a woman without her husband cannot attain happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
मितं ददाति हि पिता मितं माता मितं सुतः
अमितस्य हि दातारं भर्तारं का न पूजयेत्
verses.transliteration:
mitaṁ dadāti hi pitā mitaṁ mātā mitaṁ sutaḥ
amitasya hi dātāraṁ bhartāraṁ kā na pūjayet

translations.english: The father gives in measure, the father and the son give in measure, but who does not worship that bestower of riches fineless', the husband?

verses.sanskrit:
साहमेवंगता श्रेष्ठा श्रुतधर्मपरावरा
आर्ये किमवमन्येयं स्त्रीणां भर्ता हि दैवतम्
verses.transliteration:
sāhamevaṁgatā śreṣṭhā śrutadharmaparāvarā
ārye kimavamanyeyaṁ strīṇāṁ bhartā hi daivatam

translations.english: O exalted one, having learnt from my superiors the principal as well the minor duties, shall I disregard (my lord)? A husband is a deity to the wife.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा कौसल्या हृदयंगमम्
शुद्धसत्त्वा मुमोचाश्रु सहसा दुःखहर्षजम्
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā kausalyā hṛdayaṁgamam
śuddhasattvā mumocāśru sahasā duḥkhaharṣajam

translations.english: Hearing Sītā's words which went directly to the heart, Kausalyā endued with purity of spirit, out of fullness of bliss and bale suddenly shed tears.

verses.sanskrit:
तां प्राञ्जलिरभिक्रम्य मातृमध्येऽतिसत्कृताम्
रामः परमधर्मज्ञो मातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ prāñjalirabhikramya mātṛmadhye'tisatkṛtām
rāmaḥ paramadharmajño mātaraṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Then with joined hands that foremost of virtuous ones addressed his mother, who, duly honoured by all, was seated in the midst of his other mothers, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अम्ब मा दुःखिता भूस्त्वं पश्य त्वं पितरं मम
क्षयो हि वनवासस्य क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
amba mā duḥkhitā bhūstvaṁ paśya tvaṁ pitaraṁ mama
kṣayo hi vanavāsasya kṣiprameva bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O mother, without indulging in grief, you should minister to my father, and the term of my abode in the woods will shortly expire.

verses.sanskrit:
सुप्तायास्ते गमिष्यन्ति नववर्षाणि पञ्च च
सा समग्रमिह प्राप्तं मां द्रक्ष्यसि सुहृद्वृतम्
verses.transliteration:
suptāyāste gamiṣyanti navavarṣāṇi pañca ca
sā samagramiha prāptaṁ māṁ drakṣyasi suhṛdvṛtam

translations.english: You will find these five and nine years pass away as if in a sleep. Then again, getting me, you will see me surrounded by my friends and relatives.

verses.sanskrit:
ताश्चापि स तथैवार्ता मातॄर्दशरथात्मजः
धर्मयुक्तमिदं वाक्यं निजगाद कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
tāścāpi sa tathaivārtā mātṝrdaśarathātmajaḥ
dharmayuktamidaṁ vākyaṁ nijagāda kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Having spoken out his mind to his mother, Rāma attentively eyed his three hundred and fifty mothers. And with joined hands Daśaratha's son spoke words fraught with virtue to his mothers afflicted like Kausalyā herself.

verses.sanskrit:
संवासात्परुषं किंचिदज्ञानाद्वापि यत्कृतम्
तन्मे समनुजानीत सर्वाश्चामन्त्रयामि वः
verses.transliteration:
saṁvāsātparuṣaṁ kiṁcidajñānādvāpi yatkṛtam
tanme samanujānīta sarvāścāmantrayāmi vaḥ

translations.english: If have said anything harsh to you in consequence of familiarity, or done any wrong through ignorance, do you forgive the same. I salute you all.

verses.sanskrit:
जज्ञेऽथ तासां संनादः क्रौञ्चीनामिव निःस्वनः
मानवेन्द्रस्य भार्याणामेवं वदति राघवे
verses.transliteration:
jajñe'tha tāsāṁ saṁnādaḥ krauñcīnāmiva niḥsvanaḥ
mānavendrasya bhāryāṇāmevaṁ vadati rāghave

translations.english: As Rāghava was speaking thus, there arose a loud wail proceeding from those wives of that chief of men, like to the cries of Krauncis.

verses.sanskrit:
मुरजपणवमेघघोषव;द्दशरथवेश्म बभूव यत्पुरा
विलपित परिदेवनाकुलं; व्यसनगतं तदभूत्सुदुःखितम्
verses.transliteration:
murajapaṇavameghaghoṣava;ddaśarathaveśma babhūva yatpurā
vilapita paridevanākulaṁ; vyasanagataṁ tadabhūtsuduḥkhitam

translations.english: And the abode of Dasaratha which formerly resounded with Murajas, Panavas, meghas,* was now filled with cries of distress and lamentations. *Musical instruments.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रामश्च सीता च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः
उपसंगृह्य राजानं चक्रुर्दीनाः प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
atha rāmaśca sītā ca lakṣmaṇaśca kṛtāñjaliḥ
upasaṁgṛhya rājānaṁ cakrurdīnāḥ pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: Then exceedingly distressed, Rāma, Sītā and Lakşmaņa, bowing down to the king, circumambulated him.

verses.sanskrit:
तं चापि समनुज्ञाप्य धर्मज्ञः सीतया सह
राघवः शोकसंमूढो जननीमभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ cāpi samanujñāpya dharmajñaḥ sītayā saha
rāghavaḥ śokasaṁmūḍho jananīmabhyavādayat

translations.english: Then with the king's permission, the righteous Rāghava, stupefied with sorrow, in company with Sītā, paid respects to his mother.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्वक्षं लक्ष्मणो भ्रातुः कौसल्यामभ्यवादयत्
अथ मातुः सुमित्राया जग्राह चरणौ पुनः
verses.transliteration:
anvakṣaṁ lakṣmaṇo bhrātuḥ kausalyāmabhyavādayat
atha mātuḥ sumitrāyā jagrāha caraṇau punaḥ

translations.english: Following his brother, Lakşmaņa saluted Kausalyā; then he again took hold of his mother Sumitrā's feet.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वन्दमानं रुदती माता सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्
हितकामा महाबाहुं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय लक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vandamānaṁ rudatī mātā saumitrimabravīt
hitakāmā mahābāhuṁ mūrdhnyupāghrāya lakṣmaṇam

translations.english: As the son of Sumitrā was thus engaged in honouring his mother, his mother smelling the crown of his head, thus spoke to the mightyarmed Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
सृष्टस्त्वं वनवासाय स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज्जने
रामे प्रमादं मा कार्षीः पुत्र भ्रातरि गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
sṛṣṭastvaṁ vanavāsāya svanuraktaḥ suhṛjjane
rāme pramādaṁ mā kārṣīḥ putra bhrātari gacchati

translations.english: Although attached to your friends here, you have my permission to go to the forest. When Rama shall have gone (to the woods), do not, O son, show any negligence to him.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यसनी वा समृद्धो वा गतिरेष तवानघ
एष लोके सतां धर्मो यज्ज्येष्ठवशगो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
vyasanī vā samṛddho vā gatireṣa tavānagha
eṣa loke satāṁ dharmo yajjyeṣṭhavaśago bhavet

translations.english: O sinless one, whether in prosperity or in adversity, even this one is your way. That a younger brother should follow his elder is in this world the duty of the righteous.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं हि वृत्तमुचितं कुलस्यास्य सनातनम्
दानं दीक्षा च यज्ञेषु तनुत्यागो मृधेषु च
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ hi vṛttamucitaṁ kulasyāsya sanātanam
dānaṁ dīkṣā ca yajñeṣu tanutyāgo mṛdheṣu ca

translations.english: These are the legitimate duties ever observed by this race, charity, initiation into sacrifice, and renunciation of the body in the field of battle,

verses.sanskrit:
रामं दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्
अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmaṁ daśarathaṁ viddhi māṁ viddhi janakātmajām
ayodhyāmaṭavīṁ viddhi gaccha tāta yathāsukham

translations.english: Do you consider Rāma as Daśaratha, and Janaka's own-begotten as myself; do you regard Ayodhyā as a wilderness, go my son, at your sweet pleasure. Having thus spoken to that dear descendant of Raghu, who had made up his mind (to journey to the forest), Sumitra again and again said to him, “Go! Go!"

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुमन्त्रः काकुत्स्थं प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
विनीतो विनयज्ञश्च मातलिर्वासवं यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sumantraḥ kākutsthaṁ prāñjalirvākyamabravīt
vinīto vinayajñaśca mātalirvāsavaṁ yathā

translations.english: Then like to Mātali addressing Väsava, that one understanding humility, Sumantra, with joined hands humbly said to Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
रथमारोह भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः
क्षिप्रं त्वां प्रापयिष्यामि यत्र मां राम वक्ष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
rathamāroha bhadraṁ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
kṣipraṁ tvāṁ prāpayiṣyāmi yatra māṁ rāma vakṣyasi

translations.english: O illustrious prince, good betide you: do you ascend the car. O Rāma, I will speedily take you to wherever you will tell me.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानि वने त्वया
तान्युपक्रमितव्यानि यानि देव्यासि चोदितः
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyāni vane tvayā
tānyupakramitavyāni yāni devyāsi coditaḥ

translations.english: You will have to spend fourteen years in the forest, and your stay must commence from this very day. So the noble lady has ordered.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रथं सूर्यसंकाशं सीता हृष्टेन चेतसा
आरुरोह वरारोहा कृत्वालंकारमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rathaṁ sūryasaṁkāśaṁ sītā hṛṣṭena cetasā
āruroha varārohā kṛtvālaṁkāramātmanaḥ

translations.english: Then having adorned her person, that best of her sex, Sītā, with a glad heart ascended the car resembling the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैवायुधजातानि भ्रातृभ्यां कवचानि च
रथोपस्थे प्रतिन्यस्य सचर्मकठिनं च तत्
verses.transliteration:
tathaivāyudhajātāni bhrātṛbhyāṁ kavacāni ca
rathopasthe pratinyasya sacarmakaṭhinaṁ ca tat

translations.english: And then he placed in front of the car various weapons, coats of mail, a basket bound in hide and a hoe, At length the brothers Rama and Laks maņa swiftly ascended the flaming car garnished with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतातृतीयानारूढान्दृष्ट्वा धृष्टमचोदयत्
सुमन्त्रः संमतानश्वान्वायुवेगसमाञ्जवे
verses.transliteration:
sītātṛtīyānārūḍhāndṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭamacodayat
sumantraḥ saṁmatānaśvānvāyuvegasamāñjave

translations.english: And seeing them with Sītā for the third, mounted, Sumantra drove the car yoked with goodly horses resembling the wind in celerity.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयाते तु महारण्यं चिररात्राय राघवे
बभूव नगरे मूर्च्छा बलमूर्च्छा जनस्य च
verses.transliteration:
prayāte tu mahāraṇyaṁ cirarātrāya rāghave
babhūva nagare mūrcchā balamūrcchā janasya ca

translations.english: On Rāghava having left for the forest to stay there for a long period, the men and beasts within the city were deprived of their senses (by grief).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्समाकुलसंभ्रान्तं मत्तसंकुपित द्विपम्
हयशिञ्जितनिर्घोषं पुरमासीन्महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tatsamākulasaṁbhrāntaṁ mattasaṁkupita dvipam
hayaśiñjitanirghoṣaṁ puramāsīnmahāsvanam

translations.english: And in the city there arose a mighty tumult in consequence of the hurrying of people, the elephants waxing mad and furious, and the neighings of horses.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सबालवृद्धा सा पुरी परमपीडिता
राममेवाभिदुद्राव घर्मार्तः सलिलं यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sabālavṛddhā sā purī paramapīḍitā
rāmamevābhidudrāva gharmārtaḥ salilaṁ yathā

translations.english: And the entire city containing, young and old, extremely afflicted, rushed after Rāma, like persons oppressed with the heat of the sun rushing towards water.

verses.sanskrit:
पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चापि लम्बमानास्तदुन्मुखाः
बाष्पपूर्णमुखाः सर्वे तमूचुर्भृशदुःखिताः
verses.transliteration:
pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhataścāpi lambamānāstadunmukhāḥ
bāṣpapūrṇamukhāḥ sarve tamūcurbhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ

translations.english: As his side and back, the people bending forward with their faces covered with the vapour of grief, and sighing hard, said to he charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
संयच्छ वाजिनां रश्मीन्सूत याहि शनैः शनैः
मुखं द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य दुर्दर्शं नो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
saṁyaccha vājināṁ raśmīnsūta yāhi śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
mukhaṁ drakṣyāmi rāmasya durdarśaṁ no bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O charioteer, rein in the horses, do you proceed softly. We will see the countenance of Rāma, which we shall never see again.

verses.sanskrit:
आयसं हृदयं नूनं राममातुरसंशयम्
यद्देवगर्भप्रतिमे वनं याति न भिद्यते
verses.transliteration:
āyasaṁ hṛdayaṁ nūnaṁ rāmamāturasaṁśayam
yaddevagarbhapratime vanaṁ yāti na bhidyate

translations.english: Surely the heart of Rāma's mother is made of iron, for it does not burst on witnessing her son resembling Skanda repairing to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतकृत्या हि वैदेही छायेवानुगता पतिम्
न जहाति रता धर्मे मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा
verses.transliteration:
kṛtakṛtyā hi vaidehī chāyevānugatā patim
na jahāti ratā dharme merumarkaprabhā yathā

translations.english: Vaidehī, attaining her desire, follows her husband, like a shadow, attached to virtue, she does not forsake him, even as the Sun forsakes not Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो लक्ष्मण सिद्धार्थः सततां प्रियवादिनम्
भ्रातरं देवसंकाशं यस्त्वं परिचरिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
aho lakṣmaṇa siddhārthaḥ satatāṁ priyavādinam
bhrātaraṁ devasaṁkāśaṁ yastvaṁ paricariṣyasi

translations.english: O Laksmana, you are blessed, since you will serve your god-like brother ever speaking fair.

verses.sanskrit:
महत्येषा हि ते सिद्धिरेष चाभ्युदयो महान्
एष स्वर्गस्य मार्गश्च यदेनमनुगच्छसि
एवं वदन्तस्ते सोढुं न शेकुर्बाष्पमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
mahatyeṣā hi te siddhireṣa cābhyudayo mahān
eṣa svargasya mārgaśca yadenamanugacchasi
evaṁ vadantaste soḍhuṁ na śekurbāṣpamāgatam

translations.english: This design of yours is great; this is your mighty good fortune; this is the way to heaven that you are following him.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ राजा वृतः स्त्रीभिर्दीनाभिर्दीनचेतनः
निर्जगाम प्रियं पुत्रं द्रक्ष्यामीति ब्रुवन्गृहात्
verses.transliteration:
atha rājā vṛtaḥ strībhirdīnābhirdīnacetanaḥ
nirjagāma priyaṁ putraṁ drakṣyāmīti bruvangṛhāt

translations.english: Then the king, his sense overcome by grief, surrounded by his distressed wives, went out of his house, saying, “I will behold my dear son.”

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्रुवे चाग्रतः स्त्रीणां रुदन्तीनां महास्वनः
यथा नादः करेणूनां बद्धे महति कुञ्जरे
verses.transliteration:
śuśruve cāgrataḥ strīṇāṁ rudantīnāṁ mahāsvanaḥ
yathā nādaḥ kareṇūnāṁ baddhe mahati kuñjare

translations.english: He heard before him a mighty noise proceeding from weeping women, like to the roars of she-elephants, when a great elephant has been taken captive.

verses.sanskrit:
पिता च राजा काकुत्स्थः श्रीमान्सन्नस्तदा बभौ
परिपूर्णः शशी काले ग्रहेणोपप्लुतो यथा
verses.transliteration:
pitā ca rājā kākutsthaḥ śrīmānsannastadā babhau
paripūrṇaḥ śaśī kāle graheṇopapluto yathā

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma's father, the graceful Kākutstha, became shorn of his splendour, like to the full-moon enveloped at the appointed time during the eclipse.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हलहलाशब्दो जज्ञे रामस्य पृष्ठतः
नराणां प्रेक्ष्य राजानं सीदन्तं भृशदुःखितम्
verses.transliteration:
tato halahalāśabdo jajñe rāmasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
narāṇāṁ prekṣya rājānaṁ sīdantaṁ bhṛśaduḥkhitam

translations.english: Then seeing the sovereign senseless and stricken with exceeding sorrow, the multitudes at the rear of Rāma broke out into a loud tumult.

verses.sanskrit:
हा रामेति जनाः केचिद्राममातेति चापरे
अन्तःपुरं समृद्धं च क्रोशन्तं पर्यदेवयन्
verses.transliteration:
hā rāmeti janāḥ kecidrāmamāteti cāpare
antaḥpuraṁ samṛddhaṁ ca krośantaṁ paryadevayan

translations.english: And seeing the king weeping aloud with the inmates of the inner apartment, some exclaiming "Oh Rama," and others, “O Rāma's mother," began to be-wail.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्वीक्षमाणो रामस्तु विषण्णं भ्रान्तचेतसम्
राजानं मातरं चैव ददर्शानुगतौ पथि
धर्मपाशेन संक्षिप्तः प्रकाशं नाभ्युदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
anvīkṣamāṇo rāmastu viṣaṇṇaṁ bhrāntacetasam
rājānaṁ mātaraṁ caiva dadarśānugatau pathi
dharmapāśena saṁkṣiptaḥ prakāśaṁ nābhyudaikṣata

translations.english: Then turning back, Rāna saw that his sorrowstricken and bewildered father along with his mother, was following his track.

verses.sanskrit:
पदातिनौ च यानार्हावदुःखार्हौ सुखोचितौ
दृष्ट्वा संचोदयामास शीघ्रं याहीति सारथिम्
verses.transliteration:
padātinau ca yānārhāvaduḥkhārhau sukhocitau
dṛṣṭvā saṁcodayāmāsa śīghraṁ yāhīti sārathim

translations.english: And seeing his parents deserving of comfort and worthy of going in a carriage, going on foot, Rāma said to the charioteer, "Go you swiftly.”

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तत्पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुःखदं दर्शनं पितुः
मातुश्च सहितुं शक्तस्तोत्रार्दित इव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
na hi tatpuruṣavyāghro duḥkhadaṁ darśanaṁ pituḥ
mātuśca sahituṁ śaktastotrārdita iva dvipaḥ

translations.english: And that foremost of men was incapable of bearing the looks of his father and mother, like to an elephant afflicted with the hook, (not being able to look at what is placed on its back.)

verses.sanskrit:
तथा रुदन्तीं कौसल्यां रथं तमनुधावतीम्
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च
असकृत्प्रैक्षत तदा नृत्यन्तीमिव मातरम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā rudantīṁ kausalyāṁ rathaṁ tamanudhāvatīm
krośantīṁ rāma rāmeti hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
asakṛtpraikṣata tadā nṛtyantīmiva mātaram

translations.english: Rāma beheld his mother Kausalyā running after the car, bewailing aloud, “Rāma, Rāma, Ah Sītā, Lakşmaņa,” shedding tears for Rāma, Laks maņa and Sītā, and appearing as if she had been dancing incessantly.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठेति राजा चुक्रोष याहि याहीति राघवः
सुमन्त्रस्य बभूवात्मा चक्रयोरिव चान्तरा
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭheti rājā cukroṣa yāhi yāhīti rāghavaḥ
sumantrasya babhūvātmā cakrayoriva cāntarā

translations.english: The king exclaimed, "Stay,” Rāghava said, "On, On." Sumantra's mind vacillated like that of one placed between two hosts burning to encounter each other.

verses.sanskrit:
नाश्रौषमिति राजानमुपालब्धोऽपि वक्ष्यसि
चिरं दुःखस्य पापिष्ठमिति रामस्तमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
nāśrauṣamiti rājānamupālabdho'pi vakṣyasi
ciraṁ duḥkhasya pāpiṣṭhamiti rāmastamabravīt

translations.english: Rāma said to him, “When taxed by the monarch (on your return), you will say, 'I did not hear you.' But delay will impart me terrible pain."

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य स वचः कुर्वन्ननुज्ञाप्य च तं जनम्
व्रजतोऽपि हयाञ्शीघ्रं चोदयामास सारथिः
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya sa vacaḥ kurvannanujñāpya ca taṁ janam
vrajato'pi hayāñśīghraṁ codayāmāsa sārathiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, doing Rāma's bidding, the charioteer, telling the people to desist, made the horses already coursing, run faster.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यवर्तत जनो राज्ञो रामं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्
मनसाप्यश्रुवेगैश्च न न्यवर्तत मानुषम्
verses.transliteration:
nyavartata jano rājño rāmaṁ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam
manasāpyaśruvegaiśca na nyavartata mānuṣam

translations.english: The retainers of the king stopped after circumambulating Rāma, but their minds did not turn back. But the others did not return either bodily or mentally.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां वचः सर्वगुणोपपन्नं; प्रस्विन्नगात्रः प्रविषण्णरूपः
निशम्य राजा कृपणः सभार्यो; व्यवस्थितस्तं सुतमीक्षमाणः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vacaḥ sarvaguṇopapannaṁ; prasvinnagātraḥ praviṣaṇṇarūpaḥ
niśamya rājā kṛpaṇaḥ sabhāryo; vyavasthitastaṁ sutamīkṣamāṇaḥ

translations.english: Then the courtiers said to that mighty monarch, Dasaratha, “He that is expected back should not be followed far". Hearing their words, the king endued with every virtue, with his body covered with perspiration and his countenance woebegone, and exceedingly distressed, stopped short and stood with his wife looking at his son

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिंस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रे निष्क्रामति कृताञ्जलौ
आर्तशब्दो हि संजज्ञे स्त्रीणामन्तःपुरे महान्
verses.transliteration:
tasmiṁstu puruṣavyāghre niṣkrāmati kṛtāñjalau
ārtaśabdo hi saṁjajñe strīṇāmantaḥpure mahān

translations.english: When that foremost of men had gone out of the city with joined hands, there arose a chorus of cries proceeding from the females residing in the inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाथस्य जनस्यास्य दुर्बलस्य तपस्विनः
यो गतिं शरणं चासीत्स नाथः क्व नु गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
anāthasya janasyāsya durbalasya tapasvinaḥ
yo gatiṁ śaraṇaṁ cāsītsa nāthaḥ kva nu gacchati

translations.english: Where goes he that was the stay and refuge of the friendless, the feeble, and the helpless.

verses.sanskrit:
न क्रुध्यत्यभिशस्तोऽपि क्रोधनीयानि वर्जयन्
क्रुद्धान्प्रसादयन्सर्वान्समदुःखः क्व गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
na krudhyatyabhiśasto'pi krodhanīyāni varjayan
kruddhānprasādayansarvānsamaduḥkhaḥ kva gacchati

translations.english: He that although falsely accused, used not to be moved by anger, who pacified every enraged person by renouncing things calculated to fan anger and who felt equally for all, where goes he?

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यायां महातेजा यथा मातरि वर्तते
तथा यो वर्ततेऽस्मासु महात्मा क्व नु गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāyāṁ mahātejā yathā mātari vartate
tathā yo vartate'smāsu mahātmā kva nu gacchati

translations.english: Where goes that highly energetic and magnanimous one who conducted himself with us as he did with his mother Kausalyā

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानेन राज्ञा संचोदितो वनम्
परित्राता जनस्यास्य जगतः क्व नु गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyā kliśyamānena rājñā saṁcodito vanam
paritrātā janasyāsya jagataḥ kva nu gacchati

translations.english: Afflicted by Kaikeyſ and commissioned by the monarch to the woods, where goes the deliverer of these people, of the entire world

verses.sanskrit:
अहो निश्चेतनो राजा जीवलोकस्य संप्रियम्
धर्म्यं सत्यव्रतं रामं वनवासो प्रवत्स्यति
verses.transliteration:
aho niścetano rājā jīvalokasya saṁpriyam
dharmyaṁ satyavrataṁ rāmaṁ vanavāso pravatsyati

translations.english: Ah! the senseless monarch is sending to the woods the stay of all creatures, the righteous and truthful Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सर्वा महिष्यस्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः
रुरुदुश्चैव दुःखार्ताः सस्वरं च विचुक्रुशुः
verses.transliteration:
iti sarvā mahiṣyastā vivatsā iva dhenavaḥ
ruruduścaiva duḥkhārtāḥ sasvaraṁ ca vicukruśuḥ

translations.english: Thus all the queens, oppressed with grief, burst out into lamentations like kine bereft of calves, and loud was the sound of their wailing.

verses.sanskrit:
स तमन्तःपुरे घोरमार्तशब्दं महीपतिः
पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः श्रुत्वा चासीत्सुदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tamantaḥpure ghoramārtaśabdaṁ mahīpatiḥ
putraśokābhisaṁtaptaḥ śrutvā cāsītsuduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the loud tumult of lamentation in the inner apartment, the lord of earth burning in grief for his son was stricken with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
नाग्निहोत्राण्यहूयन्त सूर्यश्चान्तरधीयत
व्यसृजन्कवलान्नागा गावो वत्सान्न पाययन्
verses.transliteration:
nāgnihotrāṇyahūyanta sūryaścāntaradhīyata
vyasṛjankavalānnāgā gāvo vatsānna pāyayan

translations.english: And oblations to the fire had not been offered; and the Sun set; and elephants forsook their forage; and the kine did not suckle their calves.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिशङ्कुर्लोहिताङ्गश्च बृहस्पतिबुधावपि
दारुणाः सोममभ्येत्य ग्रहाः सर्वे व्यवस्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
triśaṅkurlohitāṅgaśca bṛhaspatibudhāvapi
dāruṇāḥ somamabhyetya grahāḥ sarve vyavasthitāḥ

translations.english: Trisanku, Lohitanga, Brhaspati, Budha and the other Grahas getting at the Moon, remained with fierce aspects.

verses.sanskrit:
नक्षत्राणि गतार्चींषि ग्रहाश्च गततेजसः
विशाखाश्च सधूमाश्च नभसि प्रचकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
nakṣatrāṇi gatārcīṁṣi grahāśca gatatejasaḥ
viśākhāśca sadhūmāśca nabhasi pracakāśire

translations.english: The stars are shorn of their brightness; the Grahas deprived of sheen; and Viśākhā appeared enveloped in haze.

verses.sanskrit:
अकस्मान्नागरः सर्वो जनो दैन्यमुपागमत्
आहारे वा विहारे वा न कश्चिदकरोन्मनः
verses.transliteration:
akasmānnāgaraḥ sarvo jano dainyamupāgamat
āhāre vā vihāre vā na kaścidakaronmanaḥ

translations.english: And all of a sudden the citizens have been stricken with poverty: and no one turns his thoughts to eating or drinking.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखो राजमार्गगतो जनः
न हृष्टो लक्ष्यते कश्चित्सर्वः शोकपरायणः
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpaparyākulamukho rājamārgagato janaḥ
na hṛṣṭo lakṣyate kaścitsarvaḥ śokaparāyaṇaḥ

translations.english: And with their faces washed in tears, the wayfarers betoken no delight, but all are being exercised with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
न वाति पवनः शीतो न शशी सौम्यदर्शनः
न सूर्यस्तपते लोकं सर्वं पर्याकुलं जगत्
verses.transliteration:
na vāti pavanaḥ śīto na śaśī saumyadarśanaḥ
na sūryastapate lokaṁ sarvaṁ paryākulaṁ jagat

translations.english: The cool air does not blow, and no moon of mild appearance is seen, and no sun heats the world, all the entire Earth is overwhelmed with woe.

verses.sanskrit:
अनर्थिनः सुताः स्त्रीणां भर्तारो भ्रातरस्तथा
सर्वे सर्वं परित्यज्य राममेवान्वचिन्तयन्
verses.transliteration:
anarthinaḥ sutāḥ strīṇāṁ bhartāro bhrātarastathā
sarve sarvaṁ parityajya rāmamevānvacintayan

translations.english: Sons depend not upon their parents, husbands on their wives, and brothers on brothers, and all forsaking each other, think of Rāma only.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तु रामस्य सुहृदः सर्वे ते मूढचेतसः
शोकभारेण चाक्रान्ताः शयनं न जुहुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
ye tu rāmasya suhṛdaḥ sarve te mūḍhacetasaḥ
śokabhāreṇa cākrāntāḥ śayanaṁ na juhustadā

translations.english: And deprived of sense, and oppressed by the load of sorrow, the friends of Rāma forsook their rest.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वयोध्या रहिता महात्मना; पुरंदरेणेव मही सपर्वता
चचाल घोरं भयभारपीडिता; सनागयोधाश्वगणा ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
tatastvayodhyā rahitā mahātmanā; puraṁdareṇeva mahī saparvatā
cacāla ghoraṁ bhayabhārapīḍitā; sanāgayodhāśvagaṇā nanāda ca

translations.english: Like the Earth with her mountains bereft of Purandara, Ayodhya, bereft of Rama, shook, agitated by fear and grief; and the citizens with elephants and warriors uttered exclamations of distress.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्तु निर्यतस्तस्य रजोरूपमदृश्यत
नैवेक्ष्वाकुवरस्तावत्संजहारात्मचक्षुषी
verses.transliteration:
yāvattu niryatastasya rajorūpamadṛśyata
naivekṣvākuvarastāvatsaṁjahārātmacakṣuṣī

translations.english: So long as he could see the dust raised by the car of Rāma setting out for the forest, so long that best of the Ikşvāku race did not turn his eyes from that direction.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्राजा प्रियं पुत्रं पश्यत्यत्यन्तधार्मिकम्
तावद्व्यवर्धतेवास्य धरण्यां पुत्रदर्शने
verses.transliteration:
yāvadrājā priyaṁ putraṁ paśyatyatyantadhārmikam
tāvadvyavardhatevāsya dharaṇyāṁ putradarśane

translations.english: And so long as the king could discover his exceedingly virtuous and favourite son, so long he raised himself (on his toes) on the earth with the view of beholding him.

verses.sanskrit:
न पश्यति रजोऽप्यस्य यदा रामस्य भूमिपः
तदार्तश्च विषण्णश्च पपात धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
na paśyati rajo'pyasya yadā rāmasya bhūmipaḥ
tadārtaśca viṣaṇṇaśca papāta dharaṇītale

translations.english: When the ruler of earth could no longer perceive even the dust raised by Rāma's car, then pierced with sorrow, and in heaviness of heart, he fell down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य दक्षिणमन्वगात्कौसल्या बाहुमङ्गना
वामं चास्यान्वगात्पार्श्वं कैकेयी भरतप्रिया
verses.transliteration:
tasya dakṣiṇamanvagātkausalyā bāhumaṅganā
vāmaṁ cāsyānvagātpārśvaṁ kaikeyī bharatapriyā

translations.english: Then (raising him up), Kausalyā held his right arm and walked with him, while the slenderwaisted Kaikeyi walked by his left.

verses.sanskrit:
तां नयेन च संपन्नो धर्मेण निवयेन च
उवाच राजा कैकेयीं समीक्ष्य व्यथितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ nayena ca saṁpanno dharmeṇa nivayena ca
uvāca rājā kaikeyīṁ samīkṣya vyathitendriyaḥ

translations.english: Endowed with a sense of justice and with virtue and humility, the king with afflicted senses steadily eyeing Kaikeyī, thus spoke to her.

verses.sanskrit:
ये च त्वामुपजीवन्ति नाहं तेषां न ते मम
केवलार्थपरां हि त्वां त्यक्तधर्मां त्यजाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
ye ca tvāmupajīvanti nāhaṁ teṣāṁ na te mama
kevalārthaparāṁ hi tvāṁ tyaktadharmāṁ tyajāmyaham

translations.english: O Kaikeyī, that have decided for following sin, do you not touch my person, nor do I wish to see you. You are no wife of mine, not even a maid-servant of a friend sharing his good graces. I am none to those that subsist on your favour, nor are they anything to me. I renounce you who solely seek your interest and have abandoned virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
अगृह्णां यच्च ते पाणिमग्निं पर्यणयं च यत्
अनुजानामि तत्सर्वमस्मिँल्लोके परत्र च
verses.transliteration:
agṛhṇāṁ yacca te pāṇimagniṁ paryaṇayaṁ ca yat
anujānāmi tatsarvamasmi̐lloke paratra ca

translations.english: I renounce all the advantages pertaining either to this world or the next which I am entitled to by virtue of having obtained your hand and having made you circumambulate the sacrificial fire.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतश्चेत्प्रतीतः स्याद्राज्यं प्राप्येदमव्ययम्
यन्मे स दद्यात्पित्रर्थं मा मा तद्दत्तमागमत्
verses.transliteration:
bharataścetpratītaḥ syādrājyaṁ prāpyedamavyayam
yanme sa dadyātpitrarthaṁ mā mā taddattamāgamat

translations.english: If Bharata is satisfied with receiving this entire kingdom, let not what he spends on account of my funeral obsequies find its way to me.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रेणुसमुध्वस्तं तमुत्थाप्य नराधिपम्
न्यवर्तत तदा देवी कौसल्या शोककर्शिता
verses.transliteration:
atha reṇusamudhvastaṁ tamutthāpya narādhipam
nyavartata tadā devī kausalyā śokakarśitā

translations.english: Then raising the lord of men covered with dust, the noble Kausalyā pierced with grief, stopped (along with the monarch.)

verses.sanskrit:
हत्वेव ब्राह्मणं कामात्स्पृष्ट्वाग्निमिव पाणिना
अन्वतप्यत धर्मात्मा पुत्रं संचिन्त्य तापसम्
verses.transliteration:
hatveva brāhmaṇaṁ kāmātspṛṣṭvāgnimiva pāṇinā
anvatapyata dharmātmā putraṁ saṁcintya tāpasam

translations.english: The righteous one remembering Rāghava repented himself, as if he had slain a Brāhmaṇa through inordinate desire, or as if he had placed his hand in fire.

verses.sanskrit:
निवृत्यैव निवृत्यैव सीदतो रथवर्त्मसु
राज्ञो नातिबभौ रूपं ग्रस्तस्यांशुमतो यथा
verses.transliteration:
nivṛtyaiva nivṛtyaiva sīdato rathavartmasu
rājño nātibabhau rūpaṁ grastasyāṁśumato yathā

translations.english: Having stopped again and again, the visage of the monarch lamenting on beholding the track of the car, appeared dim like the Moon invaded by Rāhu,

verses.sanskrit:
विललाप च दुःखार्तः प्रियं पुत्रमनुस्मरन्
नगरान्तमनुप्राप्तं बुद्ध्वा पुत्रमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vilalāpa ca duḥkhārtaḥ priyaṁ putramanusmaran
nagarāntamanuprāptaṁ buddhvā putramathābravīt

translations.english: And stricken with grief, he lamented, remembering his beloved son, and thinking that by this time he had reached the precincts of the city, he broke out into the following.

verses.sanskrit:
वाहनानां च मुख्यानां वहतां तं ममात्मजम्
पदानि पथि दृश्यन्ते स महात्मा न दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
vāhanānāṁ ca mukhyānāṁ vahatāṁ taṁ mamātmajam
padāni pathi dṛśyante sa mahātmā na dṛśyate

translations.english: On the way are traced the foot-prints of those foremost of bearers that are carrying my son away; but that magnanimous one I do not find.

verses.sanskrit:
स नूनं क्वचिदेवाद्य वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः
काष्ठं वा यदि वाश्मानमुपधाय शयिष्यते
verses.transliteration:
sa nūnaṁ kvacidevādya vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ
kāṣṭhaṁ vā yadi vāśmānamupadhāya śayiṣyate

translations.english: And that meritorious son of mine, who, daubed with sandal, used to rest his head pleasantly upon a pillow, fanned by beauteous damsels decked in ornaments, will to-day surely take refuge underneath a tree, and lay his head on a wooden plank or a stone.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्थास्यति च मेदिन्याः कृपणः पांशुगुण्ठितः
विनिःश्वसन्प्रस्रवणात्करेणूनामिवर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
utthāsyati ca medinyāḥ kṛpaṇaḥ pāṁśuguṇṭhitaḥ
viniḥśvasanprasravaṇātkareṇūnāmivarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Covered with dust, he heaving sighs will rise from the ground in sad guise, like a leader of she-elephants rising from the side of a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रक्ष्यन्ति नूनं पुरुषा दीर्घबाहुं वनेचराः
राममुत्थाय गच्छन्तं लोकनाथमनाथवत्
verses.transliteration:
drakṣyanti nūnaṁ puruṣā dīrghabāhuṁ vanecarāḥ
rāmamutthāya gacchantaṁ lokanāthamanāthavat

translations.english: The rangers of the woods will now see the long-armed Rāma resembling the lord himself of the worlds, rising from the ground and going like one forlorn.

verses.sanskrit:
सकामा भव कैकेयि विधवा राज्यमावस
न हि तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं विना जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
sakāmā bhava kaikeyi vidhavā rājyamāvasa
na hi taṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ vinā jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: O Kaikeyi, do you realise your desire, do you becoming a widow, rule this kingdom. Without that best of men I cannot live.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं विलपन्राजा जनौघेनाभिसंवृतः
अपस्नात इवारिष्टं प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ vilapanrājā janaughenābhisaṁvṛtaḥ
apasnāta ivāriṣṭaṁ praviveśa purottamam

translations.english: Thus lamenting, the king surrounded by the multitude, like one that had performed his bath after death, entered that best of cities filled with people enfeebled and smitten with grief, with its streets thinned of men and its stalls closed.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्याया गृहं शीघ्रं राम मातुर्नयन्तु माम्
इति ब्रुवन्तं राजानमनयन्द्वारदर्शितः
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāyā gṛhaṁ śīghraṁ rāma māturnayantu mām
iti bruvantaṁ rājānamanayandvāradarśitaḥ

translations.english: When the king had spoken thus, the ushers taking him to Kausalyā's chamber, made his lie down in lowly plight.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तत्र प्रविष्टस्य कौसल्याया निवेशनम्
अधिरुह्यापि शयनं बभूव लुलितं मनः
verses.transliteration:
tatastatra praviṣṭasya kausalyāyā niveśanam
adhiruhyāpi śayanaṁ babhūva lulitaṁ manaḥ

translations.english: Having entered Kausalyā's apartment, the king having laid himself on the bed, was overwhelmed with emotion.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखिता बत तं कालं जीविष्यन्ति नरोत्तमाः
परिष्वजन्तो ये रामं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्
verses.transliteration:
sukhitā bata taṁ kālaṁ jīviṣyanti narottamāḥ
pariṣvajanto ye rāmaṁ drakṣyanti punarāgatam

translations.english: Beholding this, the puissant sovereign raising up his arm, burst out into lamentations, saying, “Ah! Rāma, you forsakes us both! Ah me! surely those blessed people are happy, who having passed this gap of time, will behold Rāma returned and will embrace him."

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वां पश्यामि कौसल्ये साधु मां पाणिना स्पृश
रामं मेऽनुगता दृष्टिरद्यापि न निवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
na tvāṁ paśyāmi kausalye sādhu māṁ pāṇinā spṛśa
rāmaṁ me'nugatā dṛṣṭiradyāpi na nivartate

translations.english: I do not perceive you, O Kausalyā. Do you touch me with your hand. My sight having followed Rāma does not return yet.

verses.sanskrit:
तं राममेवानुविचिन्तयन्तं; समीक्ष्य देवी शयने नरेन्द्रम्
उपोपविश्याधिकमार्तरूपा; विनिःश्वसन्ती विललाप कृच्छ्रम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rāmamevānuvicintayantaṁ; samīkṣya devī śayane narendram
upopaviśyādhikamārtarūpā; viniḥśvasantī vilalāpa kṛcchram

translations.english: Then seeing that foremost of men absorbed in the contemplation of Rāma, that noble dame sat by him, and afflicted with greater grief, began to indulge in sorrow,* sighing heavily. *Another text reads vinisvasantam, joining it to narendram, foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समीक्ष्य शयने सन्नं शोकेन पार्थिवम्
कौसल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता तमुवाच महीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samīkṣya śayane sannaṁ śokena pārthivam
kausalyā putraśokārtā tamuvāca mahīpatim

translations.english: Then seeing the king lying down stupified with grief, Kausalya, aggrieved for her son, spoke to the lord of earth, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवो नरशार्दूल विषमुप्त्वा द्विजिह्ववत्
विचरिष्यति कैकेयी निर्मुक्तेव हि पन्नगी
verses.transliteration:
rāghavo naraśārdūla viṣamuptvā dvijihvavat
vicariṣyati kaikeyī nirmukteva hi pannagī

translations.english: O best of men, having vented her venom upon Rāghava, the crooked Kaikeyi will go about like a she serpent that has cast off her slough.

verses.sanskrit:
विवास्य रामं सुभगा लब्धकामा समाहिता
त्रासयिष्यति मां भूयो दुष्टाहिरिव वेश्मनि
verses.transliteration:
vivāsya rāmaṁ subhagā labdhakāmā samāhitā
trāsayiṣyati māṁ bhūyo duṣṭāhiriva veśmani

translations.english: And that fortunate one having by her endeavours attained her end, will frighten me the more like a wicked serpent in one's house.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ स्म नगरे रामश्चरन्भैक्षं गृहे वसेत्
कामकारो वरं दातुमपि दासं ममात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
atha sma nagare rāmaścaranbhaikṣaṁ gṛhe vaset
kāmakāro varaṁ dātumapi dāsaṁ mamātmajam

translations.english: If Rāma had stayed in this city subsisting himself by alms, or had I made my son as Kaikeyi's slave, even that would have been preferable (before his retirement to the woods.)

verses.sanskrit:
पातयित्वा तु कैकेय्या रामं स्थानाद्यथेष्टतः
प्रदिष्टो रक्षसां भागः पर्वणीवाहिताग्निना
verses.transliteration:
pātayitvā tu kaikeyyā rāmaṁ sthānādyatheṣṭataḥ
pradiṣṭo rakṣasāṁ bhāgaḥ parvaṇīvāhitāgninā

translations.english: Like to the sacrificial share cast to the Rākşasas by the sacrificers on the occasions of Parvas that wielder of the bow, the mightyarmed Rāma, gifted with the gait of the prince of elephants, cast off by Kaikeyī, takes refuge in the forest in company with his wife and Laks mana.

verses.sanskrit:
वने त्वदृष्टदुःखानां कैकेय्यानुमते त्वया
त्यक्तानां वनवासाय का न्ववस्था भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vane tvadṛṣṭaduḥkhānāṁ kaikeyyānumate tvayā
tyaktānāṁ vanavāsāya kā nvavasthā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Despatched by you to the woods at the command of Kaikeyi, to what a plight will they, not inured to the privations of a forest-life, be reduced!

verses.sanskrit:
ते रत्नहीनास्तरुणाः फलकाले विवासिताः
कथं वत्स्यन्ति कृपणाः फलमूलैः कृताशनाः
verses.transliteration:
te ratnahīnāstaruṇāḥ phalakāle vivāsitāḥ
kathaṁ vatsyanti kṛpaṇāḥ phalamūlaiḥ kṛtāśanāḥ

translations.english: And bereft of elegant apparel, how will they of tender years, exiled in this time of enjoyment, pass their lives in misery, subsisting on fruits and roots!

verses.sanskrit:
अपीदानीं स कालः स्यान्मम शोकक्षयः शिवः
सभार्यं यत्सह भ्रात्रा पश्येयमिह राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
apīdānīṁ sa kālaḥ syānmama śokakṣayaḥ śivaḥ
sabhāryaṁ yatsaha bhrātrā paśyeyamiha rāghavam

translations.english: Will such a time present itself now that my grief removed and my desire attained, I shall here behold Rāghava along with his wife and brother?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वैवोपस्थितौ वीरौ कदायोध्या भविष्यति
यशस्विनी हृष्टजना सूच्छ्रितध्वजमालिनी
verses.transliteration:
śrutvaivopasthitau vīrau kadāyodhyā bhaviṣyati
yaśasvinī hṛṣṭajanā sūcchritadhvajamālinī

translations.english: When, hearing that those heroes have come, will Ayodhyā adorned with standards and garlands, attain fame, with her populace filled with joy?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा प्रेक्ष्य नरव्याघ्रावरण्यात्पुनरागतौ
नन्दिष्यति पुरी हृष्टा समुद्र इव पर्वणि
verses.transliteration:
kadā prekṣya naravyāghrāvaraṇyātpunarāgatau
nandiṣyati purī hṛṣṭā samudra iva parvaṇi

translations.english: When, seeing those foremost of men returned from the forest, will the city overflow with delight, like the ocean on the occasion of a Parva?

verses.sanskrit:
कदायोध्यां महाबाहुः पुरीं वीरः प्रवेक्ष्यति
पुरस्कृत्य रथे सीतां वृषभो गोवधूमिव
verses.transliteration:
kadāyodhyāṁ mahābāhuḥ purīṁ vīraḥ pravekṣyati
puraskṛtya rathe sītāṁ vṛṣabho govadhūmiva

translations.english: When will the mighty-armed hero enter the city of Ayodhyā, placing Sītā before him on the car, like to a bull having his bovine mate before him?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा प्राणिसहस्राणि राजमार्गे ममात्मजौ
लाजैरवकरिष्यन्ति प्रविशन्तावरिंदमौ
verses.transliteration:
kadā prāṇisahasrāṇi rājamārge mamātmajau
lājairavakariṣyanti praviśantāvariṁdamau

translations.english: When will people by thousands shower fried paddy upon my sons on the road, as those repressors of foes will enter the city?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा सुमनसः कन्या द्विजातीनां फलानि च
प्रदिशन्त्यः पुरीं हृष्टाः करिष्यन्ति प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
kadā sumanasaḥ kanyā dvijātīnāṁ phalāni ca
pradiśantyaḥ purīṁ hṛṣṭāḥ kariṣyanti pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: When accepting flowers from girls and fruits from Brahmanas, will they, filled with delight, go round the palace?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा परिणतो बुद्ध्या वयसा चामरप्रभः
अभ्युपैष्यति धर्मज्ञस्त्रिवर्ष इव मां ललन्
verses.transliteration:
kadā pariṇato buddhyā vayasā cāmaraprabhaḥ
abhyupaiṣyati dharmajñastrivarṣa iva māṁ lalan

translations.english: When with his intelligence ripened by time, although resembling a celestial in age, will that righteous-souled one come here, rejoicing people like a Trivarsa?* *Three consecutive showers, favourable tot he erops.

verses.sanskrit:
निःसंशयं मया मन्ये पुरा वीर कदर्यया
पातु कामेषु वत्सेषु मातॄणां शातिताः स्तनाः
verses.transliteration:
niḥsaṁśayaṁ mayā manye purā vīra kadaryayā
pātu kāmeṣu vatseṣu mātṝṇāṁ śātitāḥ stanāḥ

translations.english: Doubtless, O hero, formerly of vile ways that I was, I had cut off the paps of kine and thus prevented their calves hungering after their mothers' milk, from drinking it.

verses.sanskrit:
साहं गौरिव सिंहेन विवत्सा वत्सला कृता
कैकेय्या पुरुषव्याघ्र बालवत्सेव गौर्बलात्
verses.transliteration:
sāhaṁ gauriva siṁhena vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā
kaikeyyā puruṣavyāghra bālavatseva gaurbalāt

translations.english: And it is for this sin that, О foremost of men, have I, attached to my son, been forcibly deprived of him by Kaikeyi, like a cow deprived of her calf by a lion.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तावद्गुणैर्जुष्टं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्
एकपुत्रा विना पुत्रमहं जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
na hi tāvadguṇairjuṣṭaṁ sarvaśāstraviśāradam
ekaputrā vinā putramahaṁ jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: Having an only son, I dare not live without him endowed with every virtue and versed in every branch of learning.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे जीविते किंचित्सामर्थमिह कल्प्यते
अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियं पुत्रं महाबाहुं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi me jīvite kiṁcitsāmarthamiha kalpyate
apaśyantyāḥ priyaṁ putraṁ mahābāhuṁ mahābalam

translations.english: Not seeing my beloved son and the mighty Lakşmaņa, I cannot live at all.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं हि मां दीपयते समुत्थित;स्तनूजशोकप्रभवो हुताशनः
महीमिमां रश्मिभिरुत्तमप्रभो; यथा निदाघे भगवान्दिवाकरः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ hi māṁ dīpayate samutthita;stanūjaśokaprabhavo hutāśanaḥ
mahīmimāṁ raśmibhiruttamaprabho; yathā nidāghe bhagavāndivākaraḥ

translations.english: As in summer the divine Sun furnished with fierce rays burns this earth, even so this raging fire of grief of account of my son consumes me.

verses.sanskrit:
विलपन्तीं तथा तां तु कौसल्यां प्रमदोत्तमाम्
इदं धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यं सुमित्रा वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vilapantīṁ tathā tāṁ tu kausalyāṁ pramadottamām
idaṁ dharme sthitā dharmyaṁ sumitrā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: As that best of ladies, Kausalyā, was thus lamenting, Sumitrā ever abiding in virtue, spoke to her these words consistent with righteousness.

verses.sanskrit:
तवार्ये सद्गुणैर्युक्तः पुत्रः स पुरुषोत्तमः
किं ते विलपितेनैवं कृपणं रुदितेन वा
verses.transliteration:
tavārye sadguṇairyuktaḥ putraḥ sa puruṣottamaḥ
kiṁ te vilapitenaivaṁ kṛpaṇaṁ ruditena vā

translations.english: O worshipful one, your son is crowned with all qualities, and is the best of men. Why then do you bewail thus, or weep bitterly?

verses.sanskrit:
शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्शश्वत्प्रेत्य फलोदये
रामो धर्मे स्थितः श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन
verses.transliteration:
śiṣṭairācarite samyakśaśvatpretya phalodaye
rāmo dharme sthitaḥ śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadācana

translations.english: Since, O revered one, renouncing the kingdom, your mighty son wendeth (to the woods) with the view of fulfiling the intention of his high-souled and truthful sire, the worthy Rāma staying in the duty that is completely observed by the good and the performance of which always bringeth welfare in the next world, should by no means be lamented.

verses.sanskrit:
वर्तते चोत्तमां वृत्तिं लक्ष्मणोऽस्मिन्सदानघः
दयावान्सर्वभूतेषु लाभस्तस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
vartate cottamāṁ vṛttiṁ lakṣmaṇo'sminsadānaghaḥ
dayāvānsarvabhūteṣu lābhastasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: That sinless one, Laksmana, kind to all creatures, will minister to Rāma in the best way possible, and this is to the advantage of that high-souled one.

verses.sanskrit:
अरण्यवासे यद्दुःखं जानती वै सुखोचिता
अनुगच्छति वैदेही धर्मात्मानं तवात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
araṇyavāse yadduḥkhaṁ jānatī vai sukhocitā
anugacchati vaidehī dharmātmānaṁ tavātmajam

translations.english: And experiencing the hardships that come of living in the forest, Vaidehi deserving of happiness follows your righteous son.

verses.sanskrit:
कीर्तिभूतां पताकां यो लोके भ्रामयति प्रभुः
दमसत्यव्रतपरः किं न प्राप्तस्तवात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
kīrtibhūtāṁ patākāṁ yo loke bhrāmayati prabhuḥ
damasatyavrataparaḥ kiṁ na prāptastavātmajaḥ

translations.english: What is wanting to that maintainer of all, your son of subdued senses, intent upon truth and the observance of vows, who is spreading his banner of fame over the world?

verses.sanskrit:
व्यक्तं रामस्य विज्ञाय शौचं माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्
न गात्रमंशुभिः सूर्यः संतापयितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
vyaktaṁ rāmasya vijñāya śaucaṁ māhātmyamuttamam
na gātramaṁśubhiḥ sūryaḥ saṁtāpayitumarhati

translations.english: Acquainted with Rāma's manifest purity and high magnanimity, the Sun himself will not dare burn his body with his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
शिवः सर्वेषु कालेषु काननेभ्यो विनिःसृतः
राघवं युक्तशीतोष्णः सेविष्यति सुखोऽनिलः
verses.transliteration:
śivaḥ sarveṣu kāleṣu kānanebhyo viniḥsṛtaḥ
rāghavaṁ yuktaśītoṣṇaḥ seviṣyati sukho'nilaḥ

translations.english: And issuing from the woods at all hours, the delicious air impregnated with heat and cold will serve Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
शयानमनघं रात्रौ पितेवाभिपरिष्वजन्
रश्मिभिः संस्पृशञ्शीतैश्चन्द्रमा ह्लादयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
śayānamanaghaṁ rātrau pitevābhipariṣvajan
raśmibhiḥ saṁspṛśañśītaiścandramā hlādayiṣyati

translations.english: And when he will lie down at night, the Moon touching him with his beams and embracing him even like his own father, will gladden his heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ददौ चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि यस्मै ब्रह्मा महौजसे
दानवेन्द्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा तिमिध्वजसुतं रणे
verses.transliteration:
dadau cāstrāṇi divyāni yasmai brahmā mahaujase
dānavendraṁ hataṁ dṛṣṭvā timidhvajasutaṁ raṇe

translations.english: That hero of mighty energy on whom Brahma had conferred celestial weapons, seeing that foremost of the Dānavas, the son of Timidhvaja, slain in battle, that tiger-like one, relying on the native strength of his arms, will fearlessly abide in the forest as if in his own home.

verses.sanskrit:
पृथिव्या सह वैदेह्या श्रिया च पुरुषर्षभः
क्षिप्रं तिसृभिरेताभिः सह रामोऽभिषेक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
pṛthivyā saha vaidehyā śriyā ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ
kṣipraṁ tisṛbhiretābhiḥ saha rāmo'bhiṣekṣyate

translations.english: And that best of men, Räma, will soon be installed in the kingdom, in company with these three, the Earth, Vaidehī, and the goddess of victory.

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखजं विसृजन्त्यस्रं निष्क्रामन्तमुदीक्ष्य यम्
समुत्स्रक्ष्यसि नेत्राभ्यां क्षिप्रमानन्दजं पयः
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhajaṁ visṛjantyasraṁ niṣkrāmantamudīkṣya yam
samutsrakṣyasi netrābhyāṁ kṣipramānandajaṁ payaḥ

translations.english: And again seeing him returned and crowned with great auspiciousness, you will speedily shed the dew of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवादयमानं तं दृष्ट्वा ससुहृदं सुतम्
मुदाश्रु मोक्ष्यसे क्षिप्रं मेघलेकेव वार्षिकी
verses.transliteration:
abhivādayamānaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā sasuhṛdaṁ sutam
mudāśru mokṣyase kṣipraṁ meghalekeva vārṣikī

translations.english: Beholding your son surrounded by his friends, bowing to you, you will soon shed blissful tears, even like a rain-cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रस्ते वरदः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां पुनरागतः
कराभ्यां मृदुपीनाभ्यां चरणौ पीडयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
putraste varadaḥ kṣipramayodhyāṁ punarāgataḥ
karābhyāṁ mṛdupīnābhyāṁ caraṇau pīḍayiṣyati

translations.english: And soon will your son conferring boons, returning (to this place), press your feet with those soft and plump hands of his.

verses.sanskrit:
निशम्य तल्लक्ष्मणमातृवाक्यं; रामस्य मातुर्नरदेवपत्न्याः
सद्यः शरीरे विननाश शोकः; शरद्गतो मेघ इवाल्पतोयः
verses.transliteration:
niśamya tallakṣmaṇamātṛvākyaṁ; rāmasya māturnaradevapatnyāḥ
sadyaḥ śarīre vinanāśa śokaḥ; śaradgato megha ivālpatoyaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of Laksmana's mother, the wife of the best of men, Rāma's mother, had her sorrow destroyed in her person, even like and autumnal cloud surcharged with slight rain.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुरक्ता महात्मानं रामं सत्यपरक्रमम्
अनुजग्मुः प्रयान्तं तं वनवासाय मानवाः
verses.transliteration:
anuraktā mahātmānaṁ rāmaṁ satyaparakramam
anujagmuḥ prayāntaṁ taṁ vanavāsāya mānavāḥ

translations.english: The people, who yarned after Rāma having truth for prowess, followed him repairing to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
निवर्तितेऽपि च बलात्सुहृद्वर्गे च राजिनि
नैव ते संन्यवर्तन्त रामस्यानुगता रथम्
verses.transliteration:
nivartite'pi ca balātsuhṛdvarge ca rājini
naiva te saṁnyavartanta rāmasyānugatā ratham

translations.english: Even when the king in the interests of his son had with much ado restrained himself, these, following Răma's car, did not desist.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्यानिलयानां हि पुरुषाणां महायशाः
बभूव गुणसंपन्नः पूर्णचन्द्र इव प्रियः
verses.transliteration:
ayodhyānilayānāṁ hi puruṣāṇāṁ mahāyaśāḥ
babhūva guṇasaṁpannaḥ pūrṇacandra iva priyaḥ

translations.english: That illustrious one crowned with every perfection was dear to the inhabitants of Ayodhyā like to the full moon himself.

verses.sanskrit:
स याच्यमानः काकुत्स्थः स्वाभिः प्रकृतिभिस्तदा
कुर्वाणः पितरं सत्यं वनमेवान्वपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
sa yācyamānaḥ kākutsthaḥ svābhiḥ prakṛtibhistadā
kurvāṇaḥ pitaraṁ satyaṁ vanamevānvapadyata

translations.english: Although besought by the subjects, the truthful Käkutstha having pledged his word to his father, kept on going to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
या प्रीतिर्बहुमानश्च मय्ययोध्यानिवासिनाम्
मत्प्रियार्थं विशेषेण भरते सा निवेश्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
yā prītirbahumānaśca mayyayodhyānivāsinām
matpriyārthaṁ viśeṣeṇa bharate sā niveśyatām

translations.english: And affectionately eyeing them as if drinking them with his sight, Rāma touchingly addressed those subjects as if they were his own, The love and regard which the inhabitants of Ayodhyā have for me, let them, for pleasing me, extend in full measure towards Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि कल्याण चारित्रः कैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनः
करिष्यति यथावद्वः प्रियाणि च हितानि च
verses.transliteration:
sa hi kalyāṇa cāritraḥ kaikeyyānandavardhanaḥ
kariṣyati yathāvadvaḥ priyāṇi ca hitāni ca

translations.english: That enhancer of Kaikeyi's delight bearing an auspicious character, will duly compass your happiness and welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञानवृद्धो वयोबालो मृदुर्वीर्यगुणान्वितः
अनुरूपः स वो भर्ता भविष्यति भयापहः
verses.transliteration:
jñānavṛddho vayobālo mṛdurvīryaguṇānvitaḥ
anurūpaḥ sa vo bhartā bhaviṣyati bhayāpahaḥ

translations.english: Aged by virtue of his wisdom, although young in years, and mild albeit furnished with heroic virtue, that remover of fear will make a fit ruler for you. son

verses.sanskrit:
स हि राजगुणैर्युक्तो युवराजः समीक्षितः
अपि चापि मया शिष्टैः कार्यं वो भर्तृशासनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa hi rājaguṇairyukto yuvarājaḥ samīkṣitaḥ
api cāpi mayā śiṣṭaiḥ kāryaṁ vo bhartṛśāsanam

translations.english: Crowned with every regal virtue and selected as the heir-apparent (by the monarch), he is more meritorious by far than I am. I behove you to obey the order of your master.

verses.sanskrit:
न च तप्येद्यथा चासौ वनवासं गते मयि
महाराजस्तथा कार्यो मम प्रियचिकीर्षया
verses.transliteration:
na ca tapyedyathā cāsau vanavāsaṁ gate mayi
mahārājastathā kāryo mama priyacikīrṣayā

translations.english: And seeking my good, it beloves you to act so that when I shall have gone to the forest, the king may not grieve.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा यथा दाशरथिर्धर्ममेवास्थितोऽभवत्
तथा तथा प्रकृतयो रामं पतिमकामयन्
verses.transliteration:
yathā yathā dāśarathirdharmamevāsthito'bhavat
tathā tathā prakṛtayo rāmaṁ patimakāmayan

translations.english: But as Daśaratha's son was bringing home to the people that their duty lay in obeying the royal Mandata, they desried that even Rāma should rule them.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पेण पिहितं दीनं रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
चकर्षेव गुणैर्बद्ध्वा जनं पुनरिवासनम्
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpeṇa pihitaṁ dīnaṁ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
cakarṣeva guṇairbaddhvā janaṁ punarivāsanam

translations.english: Rāma in company with Sumitrā's attracted the inhabitants of the city subdued by his virtues, who stood with tears in their eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
ते द्विजास्त्रिविधं वृद्धा ज्ञानेन वयसौजसा
वयःप्रकम्पशिरसो दूरादूचुरिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
te dvijāstrividhaṁ vṛddhā jñānena vayasaujasā
vayaḥprakampaśiraso dūrādūcuridaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: The three kinds of the twice-born ones, viz., those old by virtue, respectively, of age, wisdom, and ascetic energy, the old folks with their heads shaking through length of years, cried from a distance.

verses.sanskrit:
वहन्तो जवना रामं भो भो जात्यास्तुरंगमाः
निवर्तध्वं न गन्तव्यं हिता भवत भर्तरि
उपवाह्यस्तु वो भर्ता नापवाह्यः पुराद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
vahanto javanā rāmaṁ bho bho jātyāsturaṁgamāḥ
nivartadhvaṁ na gantavyaṁ hitā bhavata bhartari
upavāhyastu vo bhartā nāpavāhyaḥ purādvanam

translations.english: O you fleet coursers boasting of exalted extraction that bear Rāma away, do you desist, do not go; do you do even what is for the good of your master.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमार्तप्रलापांस्तान्वृद्धान्प्रलपतो द्विजान्
अवेक्ष्य सहसा रामो रथादवततार ह
verses.transliteration:
evamārtapralāpāṁstānvṛddhānpralapato dvijān
avekṣya sahasā rāmo rathādavatatāra ha

translations.english: Suddenly seeing those old Brāhmaṇas thus lamenting distressfully, Rāma speedily descended from his car.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्भ्यामेव जगामाथ ससीतः सहलक्ष्मणः
संनिकृष्टपदन्यासो रामो वनपरायणः
verses.transliteration:
padbhyāmeva jagāmātha sasītaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
saṁnikṛṣṭapadanyāso rāmo vanaparāyaṇaḥ

translations.english: Along with Lakşmaņa and Sitā, Rāma bound for the forest, began to walk near them on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विजातींस्तु पदातींस्तान्रामश्चारित्रवत्सलः
न शशाक घृणाचक्षुः परिमोक्तुं रथेन सः
verses.transliteration:
dvijātīṁstu padātīṁstānrāmaścāritravatsalaḥ
na śaśāka ghṛṇācakṣuḥ parimoktuṁ rathena saḥ

translations.english: Endowed with kindness, that friend of the good, Rāma, could not by proceeding on his car bear to pare with the Brāhmaṇas that were following on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छन्तमेव तं दृष्ट्वा रामं संभ्रान्तमानसाः
ऊचुः परमसंतप्ता रामं वाक्यमिदं द्विजाः
verses.transliteration:
gacchantameva taṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ saṁbhrāntamānasāḥ
ūcuḥ paramasaṁtaptā rāmaṁ vākyamidaṁ dvijāḥ

translations.english: Seeing him thus going, the Brāhamaņas with agitated hearts, and burning in grief, addressed Rāma in these words.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण्यं कृत्स्नमेतत्त्वां ब्रह्मण्यमनुगच्छति
द्विजस्कन्धाधिरूढास्त्वामग्नयोऽप्यनुयान्त्यमी
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇyaṁ kṛtsnametattvāṁ brahmaṇyamanugacchati
dvijaskandhādhirūḍhāstvāmagnayo'pyanuyāntyamī

translations.english: The Brāhmaṇas in a body are following you ever seeking their good, and mounting on the shoulders of the regenerate ones, the (sacrificial) Fires are walking in your wake.

verses.sanskrit:
वाजपेयसमुत्थानि छत्राण्येतानि पश्य नः
पृष्ठतोऽनुप्रयातानि हंसानिव जलात्यये
verses.transliteration:
vājapeyasamutthāni chatrāṇyetāni paśya naḥ
pṛṣṭhato'nuprayātāni haṁsāniva jalātyaye

translations.english: And behold these raised umbrellas of ours got from the Vājapeya sacrifice, that like to autumnal clouds follow at your back.

verses.sanskrit:
अनवाप्तातपत्रस्य रश्मिसंतापितस्य ते
एभिश्छायां करिष्यामः स्वैश्छत्रैर्वाजपेयिकैः
verses.transliteration:
anavāptātapatrasya raśmisaṁtāpitasya te
ebhiśchāyāṁ kariṣyāmaḥ svaiśchatrairvājapeyikaiḥ

translations.english: With these umbrellas got at the Vājapeya sacrifice, we will afford shade to Rāma destitute of his own white umbrella, when he shall feel the heat of the (solar) rays.

verses.sanskrit:
या हि नः सततं बुद्धिर्वेदमन्त्रानुसारिणी
त्वत्कृते सा कृता वत्स वनवासानुसारिणी
verses.transliteration:
yā hi naḥ satataṁ buddhirvedamantrānusāriṇī
tvatkṛte sā kṛtā vatsa vanavāsānusāriṇī

translations.english: That intelligence of ours which ever follows the Vedic Mantras, is now, O child, ready to follow you to the forest in your interests.

verses.sanskrit:
हृदयेष्ववतिष्ठन्ते वेदा ये नः परं धनम्
वत्स्यन्त्यपि गृहेष्वेव दाराश्चारित्ररक्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
hṛdayeṣvavatiṣṭhante vedā ye naḥ paraṁ dhanam
vatsyantyapi gṛheṣveva dārāścāritrarakṣitāḥ

translations.english: That best of treasurers, the Vedas, resides in our bosoms; and our wives protected by their chastity shall abide in our homes.

verses.sanskrit:
न पुनर्निश्चयः कार्यस्त्वद्गतौ सुकृता मतिः
त्वयि धर्मव्यपेक्षे तु किं स्याद्धर्ममवेक्षितुम्
verses.transliteration:
na punarniścayaḥ kāryastvadgatau sukṛtā matiḥ
tvayi dharmavyapekṣe tu kiṁ syāddharmamavekṣitum

translations.english: As we have already made up our minds to follow you, it is useless to fix our hearts afresh. But if you overlooks virtues, what becomes of abiding by righteousness?* *Another reading is; What becomes of the virtue that we expect at your hands?

verses.sanskrit:
याचितो नो निवर्तस्व हंसशुक्लशिरोरुहैः
शिरोभिर्निभृताचार महीपतनपांशुलैः
verses.transliteration:
yācito no nivartasva haṁsaśuklaśiroruhaiḥ
śirobhirnibhṛtācāra mahīpatanapāṁśulaiḥ

translations.english: O you that are ever firm in virtue, we beseech you by humbling to the dust our heads covered with hair white-hued like cranes, do you desist.

verses.sanskrit:
बहूनां वितता यज्ञा द्विजानां य इहागताः
तेषां समाप्तिरायत्ता तव वत्स निवर्तने
verses.transliteration:
bahūnāṁ vitatā yajñā dvijānāṁ ya ihāgatāḥ
teṣāṁ samāptirāyattā tava vatsa nivartane

translations.english: These numerous Brāhmaṇas that have come hither have entered upon many a sacrifice. The completion of these, O child, depends upon your return.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्तिमन्ति हि भूतानि जंगमाजंगमानि च
याचमानेषु तेषु त्वं भक्तिं भक्तेषु दर्शय
verses.transliteration:
bhaktimanti hi bhūtāni jaṁgamājaṁgamāni ca
yācamāneṣu teṣu tvaṁ bhaktiṁ bhakteṣu darśaya

translations.english: All creatures mobile and immobile cherish you with high regard. All these beseech you. Do you show consideration to those that regard you.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुगंतुमशक्तास्त्वां मूलैरुद्धृतवेगिभिः
उन्नता वायुवेगेन विक्रोशन्तीव पादपाः
verses.transliteration:
anugaṁtumaśaktāstvāṁ mūlairuddhṛtavegibhiḥ
unnatā vāyuvegena vikrośantīva pādapāḥ

translations.english: Tall trees deprived of motion in consequence of being fast rooted to the earth and incapable of following you, are prohibiting you by sounding with the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
निश्चेष्टाहारसंचारा वृक्षैकस्थानविष्ठिताः
पक्षिणोऽपि प्रयाचन्ते सर्वभूतानुकम्पिनम्
verses.transliteration:
niśceṣṭāhārasaṁcārā vṛkṣaikasthānaviṣṭhitāḥ
pakṣiṇo'pi prayācante sarvabhūtānukampinam

translations.english: And birds staying upon trees and neither manifesting any motion nor seeking for their food, beseech you to have compassion upon all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विक्रोशतां तेषां द्विजातीनां निवर्तने
ददृशे तमसा तत्र वारयन्तीव राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vikrośatāṁ teṣāṁ dvijātīnāṁ nivartane
dadṛśe tamasā tatra vārayantīva rāghavam

translations.english: While the Brāhmaṇas were loudly demanding the return of Rāma, he found the darkness to descend as if forbidding him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तमसा तीरं रम्यमाश्रित्य राघवः
सीतामुद्वीक्ष्य सौमित्रिमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu tamasā tīraṁ ramyamāśritya rāghavaḥ
sītāmudvīkṣya saumitrimidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Then Rāghava pausing on the banks of the Tamasā, looked at Sītā and spoke to Sumitrā's son, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इयमद्य निशा पूर्वा सौमित्रे प्रस्थिता वनम्
वनवासस्य भद्रं ते स नोत्कण्ठितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
iyamadya niśā pūrvā saumitre prasthitā vanam
vanavāsasya bhadraṁ te sa notkaṇṭhitumarhasi

translations.english: O son of Sumitrā, this is the first night of our exile into the forest. From this day it behoveth you not, good betide you, to suffer your mind to grieve (by dwelling on past joys.)

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य शून्यान्यरण्यानि रुदन्तीव समन्ततः
यथानिलयमायद्भिर्निलीनानि मृगद्विजैः
verses.transliteration:
paśya śūnyānyaraṇyāni rudantīva samantataḥ
yathānilayamāyadbhirnilīnāni mṛgadvijaiḥ

translations.english: The empty forest resounding with the cries of beasts and birds returned to their abodes, covered with gloom, seems to weep on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यायोध्या तु नगरी राजधानी पितुर्मम
सस्त्रीपुंसा गतानस्माञ्शोचिष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
adyāyodhyā tu nagarī rājadhānī piturmama
sastrīpuṁsā gatānasmāñśociṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Doubtless to-day the men and women of Ayodhyā, the metropolis of my father, are bewailing us retired to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतः खलु धर्मात्मा पितरं मातरं च मे
धर्मार्थकामसहितैर्वाक्यैराश्वासयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
bharataḥ khalu dharmātmā pitaraṁ mātaraṁ ca me
dharmārthakāmasahitairvākyairāśvāsayiṣyati

translations.english: But surely the virtuous Bharata will console our father and mother with words fraught with virtuc, interest and profit.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्यानृशंसत्वं संचिन्त्याहं पुनः पुनः
नानुशोचामि पितरं मातरं चापि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
bharatasyānṛśaṁsatvaṁ saṁcintyāhaṁ punaḥ punaḥ
nānuśocāmi pitaraṁ mātaraṁ cāpi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: Reflecting again and again on Bharata's sincerity of soul, I do not, O mighty-armed one, bewail either my mother or my father.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया कार्यं नरव्याघ्र मामनुव्रजता कृतम्
अन्वेष्टव्या हि वैदेह्या रक्षणार्थे सहायता
verses.transliteration:
tvayā kāryaṁ naravyāghra māmanuvrajatā kṛtam
anveṣṭavyā hi vaidehyā rakṣaṇārthe sahāyatā

translations.english: foremost of men, that you have followed me in what is your duty. (If you had not done so), I should have to seek elsewhere for the protection of Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सौमित्रं सुमन्त्रमपि राघवः
अप्रमत्तस्त्वमश्वेषु भव सौम्येत्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu saumitraṁ sumantramapi rāghavaḥ
apramattastvamaśveṣu bhava saumyetyuvāca ha

translations.english: O Sumitrā's son, I will spend here this night, subsisting alone. Even this recommends itself to me, although the forest yields various kinds of fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽश्वान्सुमन्त्रः संयम्य सूर्येऽस्तं समुपागते
प्रभूतयवसान्कृत्वा बभूव प्रत्यनन्तरः
verses.transliteration:
so'śvānsumantraḥ saṁyamya sūrye'staṁ samupāgate
prabhūtayavasānkṛtvā babhūva pratyanantaraḥ

translations.english: Having said this to Sumitrā's son, Raghava spoke to Sumantra, saying, “O mild one, do you now heedfully tend the horses.” Then at sunset, fastening the horses, Sumantra fed them plentifully with grass, and then came back.

verses.sanskrit:
उपास्यतु शिवां संध्यां दृष्ट्वा रात्रिमुपस्थिताम्
रामस्य शयनं चक्रे सूतः सौमित्रिणा सह
verses.transliteration:
upāsyatu śivāṁ saṁdhyāṁ dṛṣṭvā rātrimupasthitām
rāmasya śayanaṁ cakre sūtaḥ saumitriṇā saha

translations.english: Then seeing the night arrived, the charioteer worshipped the beneficent Sandhyā, and then in company with Sumitrā's son, prepared Rāma's bed. on water

verses.sanskrit:
तां शय्यां तमसातीरे वीक्ष्य वृक्षदलैः कृताम्
रामः सौमित्रिणां सार्धं सभार्यः संविवेश ह
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ śayyāṁ tamasātīre vīkṣya vṛkṣadalaiḥ kṛtām
rāmaḥ saumitriṇāṁ sārdhaṁ sabhāryaḥ saṁviveśa ha

translations.english: And looking at that bed on the shores of the Tamasā surrounded by trees, Rāma along with his wife and the son of Sumitrā, lay down,

verses.sanskrit:
सभार्यं संप्रसुप्तं तं भ्रातरं वीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः
कथयामास सूताय रामस्य विविधान्गुणान्
verses.transliteration:
sabhāryaṁ saṁprasuptaṁ taṁ bhrātaraṁ vīkṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ
kathayāmāsa sūtāya rāmasya vividhānguṇān

translations.english: When Lakşmaņa found that Rāma afflicted with fatigue had slept together with his spouse, he began to speak to the charioteer concerning the various qualities of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
जाग्रतो ह्येव तां रात्रिं सौमित्रेरुदितो रविः
सूतस्य तमसातीरे रामस्य ब्रुवतो गुणान्
verses.transliteration:
jāgrato hyeva tāṁ rātriṁ saumitrerudito raviḥ
sūtasya tamasātīre rāmasya bruvato guṇān

translations.english: As remaining awake in the night, Sumitrā's son was engaged in expatiating to the charioteer on the virtues of Rāma on the banks of the Tamasă, the sun arose.

verses.sanskrit:
गोकुलाकुलतीरायास्तमसाया विदूरतः
अवसत्तत्र तां रात्रिं रामः प्रकृतिभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
gokulākulatīrāyāstamasāyā vidūrataḥ
avasattatra tāṁ rātriṁ rāmaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha

translations.english: Rāma abode that night along with the subjects at some distance from the banks of the Tamasā filled with kine.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्थाय तु महातेजाः प्रकृतीस्ता निशाम्य च
अब्रवीद्भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं पुण्यलक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
utthāya tu mahātejāḥ prakṛtīstā niśāmya ca
abravīdbhrātaraṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṁ puṇyalakṣaṇam

translations.english: Rising (from his bed), that highly energetic one, Rāma, viewing the subjects (asleep), addressed his brother Lakşmana graced with auspicious marks.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मद्व्यपेक्षान्सौमित्रे निरपेक्षान्गृहेष्वपि
वृक्षमूलेषु संसुप्तान्पश्य लक्ष्मण साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
asmadvyapekṣānsaumitre nirapekṣāngṛheṣvapi
vṛkṣamūleṣu saṁsuptānpaśya lakṣmaṇa sāmpratam

translations.english: O son of Sumitrā, these that for our sake have disregarded their own homes, are still asleep beneath the trees.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैते नियमं पौराः कुर्वन्त्यस्मन्निवर्तने
अपि प्राणानसिष्यन्ति न तु त्यक्ष्यन्ति निश्चयम्
verses.transliteration:
yathaite niyamaṁ paurāḥ kurvantyasmannivartane
api prāṇānasiṣyanti na tu tyakṣyanti niścayam

translations.english: These citizens have determined upon making me turn back from the forest, they would rather renounce their lives than give up their resolve.

verses.sanskrit:
यावदेव तु संसुप्तास्तावदेव वयं लघु
रथमारुह्य गच्छामः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्
verses.transliteration:
yāvadeva tu saṁsuptāstāvadeva vayaṁ laghu
rathamāruhya gacchāmaḥ panthānamakutobhayam

translations.english: Let us while they are asleep ascending on our car, swiftly go our way without fear of molestation.

verses.sanskrit:
अतो भूयोऽपि नेदानीमिक्ष्वाकुपुरवासिनः
स्वपेयुरनुरक्ता मां वृक्षमूलानि संश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
ato bhūyo'pi nedānīmikṣvākupuravāsinaḥ
svapeyuranuraktā māṁ vṛkṣamūlāni saṁśritāḥ

translations.english: Attached to me, the denizons of Ikşvāku's city will not again indulge in sleep underneath trees.

verses.sanskrit:
पौरा ह्यात्मकृताद्दुःखाद्विप्रमोच्या नृपात्मजैः
न तु खल्वात्मना योज्या दुःखेन पुरवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
paurā hyātmakṛtādduḥkhādvipramocyā nṛpātmajaiḥ
na tu khalvātmanā yojyā duḥkhena puravāsinaḥ

translations.english: A prince should deliver citizens from the calamity they bring upon themselves; but he should by no means drag them into those which he himself has brought on.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणो रामं साक्षाद्धर्ममिव स्थितम्
रोचते मे महाप्राज्ञ क्षिप्रमारुह्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
abravīllakṣmaṇo rāmaṁ sākṣāddharmamiva sthitam
rocate me mahāprājña kṣipramāruhyatāmiti

translations.english: Then Lakşmana spoke to Rāma like to manifest Virtue on earth, "O wise one, even this is relished also by me. Do you speedily ascend (the car.)"

verses.sanskrit:
सूतस्ततः संत्वरितः स्यन्दनं तैर्हयोत्तमैः
योजयित्वाथ रामाय प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
sūtastataḥ saṁtvaritaḥ syandanaṁ tairhayottamaiḥ
yojayitvātha rāmāya prāñjaliḥ pratyavedayat

translations.english: Thereupon the charioteer bestirring himself, yoking the excellent horses to the car, said to Rāma with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
मोहनार्थं तु पौराणां सूतं रामोऽब्रवीद्वचः
उदङ्मुखः प्रयाहि त्वं रथमास्थाय सारथे
verses.transliteration:
mohanārthaṁ tu paurāṇāṁ sūtaṁ rāmo'bravīdvacaḥ
udaṅmukhaḥ prayāhi tvaṁ rathamāsthāya sārathe

translations.english: But with the view of deluding the citizens, Rāma said to the charioteer, "O charioteer, do you ascending the car proceed northwards; and having proceeded swiftly for a while, do you turn the car. Do you carefully act so that the citizens nay not perceive this."

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे स सारथिः
प्रत्यागम्य च रामस्य स्यन्दनं प्रत्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā tathā cakre sa sārathiḥ
pratyāgamya ca rāmasya syandanaṁ pratyavedayat

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words, the charioteer did accordingly, and having returned said to Rāma to ascend the car.

verses.sanskrit:
तं स्यन्दनमधिष्ठाय राघवः सपरिच्छदः
शीघ्रगामाकुलावर्तां तमसामतरन्नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ syandanamadhiṣṭhāya rāghavaḥ saparicchadaḥ
śīghragāmākulāvartāṁ tamasāmatarannadīm
