translations.english: Ascending the car after equipping himself, Rāghava crossed the rapidly-rushing Tamasā abounding in eddies.

verses.sanskrit:
स संतीर्य महाबाहुः श्रीमाञ्शिवमकण्टकम्
प्रापद्यत महामार्गमभयं भयदर्शिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁtīrya mahābāhuḥ śrīmāñśivamakaṇṭakam
prāpadyata mahāmārgamabhayaṁ bhayadarśinām

translations.english: Having crossed (the stream), the auspicious and mighty-armed one came upon a safe and goodly-high way capable of inspiring even timid people with confidence.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पौरास्ते राघवो विना
शोकोपहतनिश्चेष्टा बभूवुर्हतचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
prabhātāyāṁ tu śarvaryāṁ paurāste rāghavo vinā
śokopahataniśceṣṭā babhūvurhatacetasaḥ

translations.english: When the night had departed an day dawned, the citizens not finding Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief and were deprived of their senses. were

verses.sanskrit:
शोकजाश्रुपरिद्यूना वीक्षमाणास्ततस्ततः
आलोकमपि रामस्य न पश्यन्ति स्म दुःखिताः
verses.transliteration:
śokajāśruparidyūnā vīkṣamāṇāstatastataḥ
ālokamapi rāmasya na paśyanti sma duḥkhitāḥ

translations.english: With tears of grief and afflicted with distress, they looked hither and thither, but they could not discover even the dust raised by Rāma's car.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मार्गानुसारेण गत्वा किंचित्क्षणं पुनः
मार्गनाशाद्विषादेन महता समभिप्लुतः
verses.transliteration:
tato mārgānusāreṇa gatvā kiṁcitkṣaṇaṁ punaḥ
mārganāśādviṣādena mahatā samabhiplutaḥ

translations.english: Then following for a while the track of the car, they, missing the track, became overwhelmed with woe.

verses.sanskrit:
रथस्य मार्गनाशेन न्यवर्तन्त मनस्विनः
किमिदं किं करिष्यामो दैवेनोपहता इति
verses.transliteration:
rathasya mārganāśena nyavartanta manasvinaḥ
kimidaṁ kiṁ kariṣyāmo daivenopahatā iti

translations.english: And then those intelligent ones came back by the track of the car. "What is this? What shall we do? We have been foiled by some supernatural agency."

verses.sanskrit:
ततो यथागतेनैव मार्गेण क्लान्तचेतसः
अयोध्यामगमन्सर्वे पुरीं व्यथितसज्जनाम्
verses.transliteration:
tato yathāgatenaiva mārgeṇa klāntacetasaḥ
ayodhyāmagamansarve purīṁ vyathitasajjanām

translations.english: Then they returned to the city of Ayodhyā with its good people oppressed with grief, by the self-same way by which they had come.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वं स्वं निलयमागम्य पुत्रदारैः समावृताः
अश्रूणि मुमुचुः सर्वे बाष्पेण पिहिताननाः
verses.transliteration:
svaṁ svaṁ nilayamāgamya putradāraiḥ samāvṛtāḥ
aśrūṇi mumucuḥ sarve bāṣpeṇa pihitānanāḥ

translations.english: Then with depressed spirits, and exceedingly afflicted, with tears flooding their eyes, smitten with mortal grief, the inhabitants of the city went back from Rāma to the city. And with their lives appearing as ready to go out, those unsteady ones came to their respective homes, and surrounded by their wives and sons, washed their faces with copious tears.

verses.sanskrit:
न चाहृष्यन्न चामोदन्वणिजो न प्रसारयन्
न चाशोभन्त पण्यानि नापचन्गृहमेधिनः
verses.transliteration:
na cāhṛṣyanna cāmodanvaṇijo na prasārayan
na cāśobhanta paṇyāni nāpacangṛhamedhinaḥ

translations.english: They forgot to rejoice or make merry, and the traders did not spread (their stores), and stalls did not grace the place, and the householders did not cook, and people did not rejoice on recovering lost property or gaining a profuse accession of wealth, and mothers did not feel any delight on beholding their first-born.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहे गृहे रुदन्त्यश्च भर्तारं गृहमागतम्
व्यगर्हयन्तो दुःखार्ता वाग्भिस्तोत्रैरिव द्विपान्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhe gṛhe rudantyaśca bhartāraṁ gṛhamāgatam
vyagarhayanto duḥkhārtā vāgbhistotrairiva dvipān

translations.english: And in every home females afflicted with woe, weeping child their husbands coming home, with the following words as (drivers) spur elephants with hooks.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु तेषां गृहैः कार्यं किं दारैः किं धनेन वा
पुत्रैर्वा किं सुखैर्वापि ये न पश्यन्ति राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu teṣāṁ gṛhaiḥ kāryaṁ kiṁ dāraiḥ kiṁ dhanena vā
putrairvā kiṁ sukhairvāpi ye na paśyanti rāghavam

translations.english: Of what use are their houses, and wives, and wealth, and sons, and comforts, to those who see not Rāghava (in their midst?)

verses.sanskrit:
एकः सत्पुरुषो लोके लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया
योऽनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थं रामं परिचरन्वने
verses.transliteration:
ekaḥ satpuruṣo loke lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
yo'nugacchati kākutsthaṁ rāmaṁ paricaranvane

translations.english: There is one only good man in this world even Lakşmaņa, who along with Sītā is following Käkutstha Rāma to the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
आपगाः कृतपुण्यास्ताः पद्मिन्यश्च सरांसि च
येषु स्नास्यति काकुत्स्थो विगाह्य सलिलं शुचि
verses.transliteration:
āpagāḥ kṛtapuṇyāstāḥ padminyaśca sarāṁsi ca
yeṣu snāsyati kākutstho vigāhya salilaṁ śuci

translations.english: Those streams, assemblage of lotuses, and pools are blessed by which bathing in the sacred waters, Kakutstha will pass.

verses.sanskrit:
शोभयिष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमटव्यो रम्यकाननाः
आपगाश्च महानूपाः सानुमन्तश्च पर्वताः
verses.transliteration:
śobhayiṣyanti kākutsthamaṭavyo ramyakānanāḥ
āpagāśca mahānūpāḥ sānumantaśca parvatāḥ

translations.english: And romantic forests and woods, watery expanses of mighty volume, and mountains with flat spaces, will grace Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
काननं वापि शैलं वा यं रामोऽभिगमिष्यति
प्रियातिथिमिव प्राप्तं नैनं शक्ष्यन्त्यनर्चितुम्
verses.transliteration:
kānanaṁ vāpi śailaṁ vā yaṁ rāmo'bhigamiṣyati
priyātithimiva prāptaṁ nainaṁ śakṣyantyanarcitum

translations.english: And forests and hills to which will repair Rāma cannot go without paying him homage like to a welcome guest.

verses.sanskrit:
विचित्रकुसुमापीडा बहुमञ्जरिधारिणः
अकाले चापि मुख्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च
दर्शयिष्यन्त्यनुक्रोशाद्गिरयो राममागतम्
verses.transliteration:
vicitrakusumāpīḍā bahumañjaridhāriṇaḥ
akāle cāpi mukhyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
darśayiṣyantyanukrośādgirayo rāmamāgatam

translations.english: And hills from regard will show to Rāma arrived there the choicest flowers and fruits even out of season and will supply him with fountains of pure water.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र रामो भयं नात्र नास्ति तत्र पराभवः
स हि शूरो महाबाहुः पुत्रो दशरथस्य च
verses.transliteration:
yatra rāmo bhayaṁ nātra nāsti tatra parābhavaḥ
sa hi śūro mahābāhuḥ putro daśarathasya ca

translations.english: And presenting him with many a charming fountain, trees will delight Rāma at the tops of mountains.* Where Rama is, there is nor fear or failure. That mighty-armed son of Dasaratha is heroic. Let us while he is yet ahead within a short distance of us, follow Rāghava. *The meaning is, Trees will please Rāghava by spreading for him a bed of leaves and flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा भवति नो दूरादनुगच्छाम राघवम्
पादच्छाया सुखा भर्तुस्तादृशस्य महात्मनः
स हि नाथो जनस्यास्य स गतिः स परायणम्
verses.transliteration:
purā bhavati no dūrādanugacchāma rāghavam
pādacchāyā sukhā bhartustādṛśasya mahātmanaḥ
sa hi nātho janasyāsya sa gatiḥ sa parāyaṇam

translations.english: Even the shadow of the feet of our master, so high-souled, would bring us happiness. He is the lord of all these, he is the refuge, he is the accomplishment of our religious duties.

verses.sanskrit:
वयं परिचरिष्यामः सीतां यूयं तु राघवम्
इति पौरस्त्रियो भर्तॄन्दुःखार्तास्तत्तदब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
vayaṁ paricariṣyāmaḥ sītāṁ yūyaṁ tu rāghavam
iti paurastriyo bhartṝnduḥkhārtāstattadabruvan

translations.english: We and you, will serve Sītā, and Rāghava. Thus afflicted with grief, the women of the city spoke to their husbands.

verses.sanskrit:
युष्माकं राघवोऽरण्ये योगक्षेमं विधास्यति
सीता नारीजनस्यास्य योगक्षेमं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yuṣmākaṁ rāghavo'raṇye yogakṣemaṁ vidhāsyati
sītā nārījanasyāsya yogakṣemaṁ kariṣyati

translations.english: In the forest Rāghava will attain for you the unattainable and protect what is attained; and Sītā being a female will do the same for these (women.)

verses.sanskrit:
को न्वनेनाप्रतीतेन सोत्कण्ठितजनेन च
संप्रीयेतामनोज्ञेन वासेन हृतचेतसा
verses.transliteration:
ko nvanenāpratītena sotkaṇṭhitajanena ca
saṁprīyetāmanojñena vāsena hṛtacetasā

translations.english: Who will take pleasure in residing in a dwelling where the heart dies within itself, which is devoid of delight, where the people are always agitated with anxiety and which is exceedingly disagreeable?

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्या यदि चेद्राज्यं स्यादधर्म्यमनाथवत्
न हि नो जीवितेनार्थः कुतः पुत्रैः कुतो धनैः
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyā yadi cedrājyaṁ syādadharmyamanāthavat
na hi no jīvitenārthaḥ kutaḥ putraiḥ kuto dhanaiḥ

translations.english: If this kingdom devolves on Kaikeyi it will be divested of all virtues and will be like to one without a master. And of what avail then is our life itself, not to speak of sons and wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
यया पुत्रश्च भर्ता च त्यक्तावैश्वर्यकारणात्
कं सा परिहरेदन्यं कैकेयी कुलपांसनी
verses.transliteration:
yayā putraśca bhartā ca tyaktāvaiśvaryakāraṇāt
kaṁ sā pariharedanyaṁ kaikeyī kulapāṁsanī

translations.english: Whom else will that stainer of her line, Kaikeyī, forsake now, who for the sake of wealth has forsaken her son and her lord?

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्या न वयं राज्ये भृतका निवसेमहि
जीवन्त्या जातु जीवन्त्यः पुत्रैरपि शपामहे
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyā na vayaṁ rājye bhṛtakā nivasemahi
jīvantyā jātu jīvantyaḥ putrairapi śapāmahe

translations.english: We swear by our sons that so long as Kaikeyi is alive, we living will never stay in her kingdom, although we may be maintained by her.

verses.sanskrit:
या पुत्रं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य प्रवासयति निर्घृणा
कस्तां प्राप्य सुखं जीवेदधर्म्यां दुष्टचारिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
yā putraṁ pārthivendrasya pravāsayati nirghṛṇā
kastāṁ prāpya sukhaṁ jīvedadharmyāṁ duṣṭacāriṇīm

translations.english: What happiness can be ours by living with that wicked and unrighteous one who lost to every sense of shame is bent upon exiling the son of the foremost of kings?

verses.sanskrit:
न हि प्रव्रजिते रामे जीविष्यति महीपतिः
मृते दशरथे व्यक्तं विलोपस्तदनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi pravrajite rāme jīviṣyati mahīpatiḥ
mṛte daśarathe vyaktaṁ vilopastadanantaram

translations.english: On Rāma retiring to the forest, the lord of earth will surely not live; and Dasaratha dying, it is evident everything will come to naught.

verses.sanskrit:
ते विषं पिबतालोड्य क्षीणपुण्याः सुदुर्गताः
राघवं वानुगच्छध्वमश्रुतिं वापि गच्छत
verses.transliteration:
te viṣaṁ pibatāloḍya kṣīṇapuṇyāḥ sudurgatāḥ
rāghavaṁ vānugacchadhvamaśrutiṁ vāpi gacchata

translations.english: Do you, your virtue exhausted, and oppressed with grief, pounding poison, take it, or follow Rāghava, or remove to such a place that the very name of Kaikeyī may not reach your ears.

verses.sanskrit:
मिथ्या प्रव्राजितो रामः सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः
भरते संनिषृष्टाः स्मः सौनिके पशवो यथा
verses.transliteration:
mithyā pravrājito rāmaḥ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
bharate saṁniṣṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ saunike paśavo yathā

translations.english: Rāma has been deceitfully exiled along with his wife and Lakşmaņa; and we are bound to Bharata like to a (sacrificial) beast before one that is to slaughter it.

verses.sanskrit:
तास्तथा विलपन्त्यस्तु नगरे नागरस्त्रियः
चुक्रुशुर्भृशसंतप्ता मृत्योरिव भयागमे
verses.transliteration:
tāstathā vilapantyastu nagare nāgarastriyaḥ
cukruśurbhṛśasaṁtaptā mṛtyoriva bhayāgame

translations.english: Thus lamenting in the city, the females thereof burning in grief became distressed like people stricken with panic on the occasion of a plague.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा स्त्रियो रामनिमित्तमातुरा; यथा सुते भ्रातरि वा विवासिते
विलप्य दीना रुरुदुर्विचेतसः; सुतैर्हि तासामधिको हि सोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
tathā striyo rāmanimittamāturā; yathā sute bhrātari vā vivāsite
vilapya dīnā rurudurvicetasaḥ; sutairhi tāsāmadhiko hi so'bhavat

translations.english: Distressed for the sake of Rāma as if it was a was son or a brother of theirs that was banished, the women weeping forlorn, lamented with senses lost; and Rāma was to them more than a son.

verses.sanskrit:
रामोऽपि रात्रिशेषेण तेनैव महदन्तरम्
जगाम पुरुषव्याघ्रः पितुराज्ञामनुस्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
rāmo'pi rātriśeṣeṇa tenaiva mahadantaram
jagāma puruṣavyāghraḥ piturājñāmanusmaran

translations.english: That best of men, Rāma, remembering his father's commanded cleared a large tract of country before the night terminated.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव गच्छतस्तस्य व्यपायाद्रजनी शिवा
उपास्य स शिवां संध्यां विषयान्तं व्यगाहत
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva gacchatastasya vyapāyādrajanī śivā
upāsya sa śivāṁ saṁdhyāṁ viṣayāntaṁ vyagāhata

translations.english: And as he went on, the auspicious night was spent. And then having offered up his devotions to the beneficent Sandhyā, Rāma entered into another country.

verses.sanskrit:
ग्रामान्विकृष्टसीमांस्तान्पुष्पितानि वनानि च
पश्यन्नतिययौ शीघ्रं शरैरिव हयोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
grāmānvikṛṣṭasīmāṁstānpuṣpitāni vanāni ca
paśyannatiyayau śīghraṁ śarairiva hayottamaiḥ

translations.english: And seeing villages having ploughed fields on their skirts, and powering woods, he by means of those excellent horses, proceeded very fast although seeming to go slowly.

verses.sanskrit:
शृण्वन्वाचो मनुष्याणां ग्रामसंवासवासिनाम्
राजानं धिग्दशरथं कामस्य वशमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
śṛṇvanvāco manuṣyāṇāṁ grāmasaṁvāsavāsinām
rājānaṁ dhigdaśarathaṁ kāmasya vaśamāgatam

translations.english: And as Rāma proceeded,* he heard the villagers speaking to each other, saying, Fie on king Dasaratha, who has yielded himself up to lust! *The N.W.P. text has an additional couplet:, How will that exalted lady, Janaka's daughter, ever engaged in enjoyment, bear misery?

verses.sanskrit:
हा नृशंसाद्य कैकेयी पापा पापानुबन्धिनी
तीक्ष्णा संभिन्नमर्यादा तीक्ष्णे कर्मणि वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
hā nṛśaṁsādya kaikeyī pāpā pāpānubandhinī
tīkṣṇā saṁbhinnamaryādā tīkṣṇe karmaṇi vartate

translations.english: Ah! the rebutless, fell and sinful Kaikeyi intent upon impiety, having put by her honour, has resolved upon an exceedingly atrocious deed, she that exiles into the woods such a virtuous son of the monarch, endowed with high wisdom, kind, and having his senses under control.* *The N.W.P. text has an additional line: And of the reprehensible Kaikeyi intent upon cruel deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वेदश्रुतिं नाम शिववारिवहां नदीम्
उत्तीर्याभिमुखः प्रायादगस्त्याध्युषितां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
tato vedaśrutiṁ nāma śivavārivahāṁ nadīm
uttīryābhimukhaḥ prāyādagastyādhyuṣitāṁ diśam

translations.english: Hearing these words of the villagers, that hero, the lord of Kosala, left Kosala behind him. Then crossing the river Vedaśruti of sacred waters, Rāma went in the direction of the quarter in which Agastya resided. (South)

verses.sanskrit:
गत्वा तु सुचिरं कालं ततः शीतजलां नदीम्
गोमतीं गोयुतानूपामतरत्सागरंगमाम्
verses.transliteration:
gatvā tu suciraṁ kālaṁ tataḥ śītajalāṁ nadīm
gomatīṁ goyutānūpāmataratsāgaraṁgamām

translations.english: Then proceeding for a good while, he crossed the cool flowing stream Gomati running in the direction of the ocean, with its banks filled with kine and inundating its edge.

verses.sanskrit:
गोमतीं चाप्यतिक्रम्य राघवः शीघ्रगैर्हयैः
मयूरहंसाभिरुतां ततार स्यन्दिकां नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
gomatīṁ cāpyatikramya rāghavaḥ śīghragairhayaiḥ
mayūrahaṁsābhirutāṁ tatāra syandikāṁ nadīm

translations.english: Having passed the Gomatī, Rāghava by means of fleet-coursing horses next crossed over the river Sandika resounding with the cries of cranes and peacocks.

verses.sanskrit:
स महीं मनुना राज्ञा दत्तामिक्ष्वाकवे पुरा
स्फीतां राष्ट्रावृतां रामो वैदेहीमन्वदर्शयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa mahīṁ manunā rājñā dattāmikṣvākave purā
sphītāṁ rāṣṭrāvṛtāṁ rāmo vaidehīmanvadarśayat

translations.english: Here Rāma showed to Vaidehi those flourishing regions that had formerly been conferred by king Manu on Ikşvāku, and which teemed with populous tracts.

verses.sanskrit:
सूत इत्येव चाभाष्य सारथिं तमभीक्ष्णशः
हंसमत्तस्वरः श्रीमानुवाच पुरुषर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
sūta ityeva cābhāṣya sārathiṁ tamabhīkṣṇaśaḥ
haṁsamattasvaraḥ śrīmānuvāca puruṣarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Then frequently addressing the charioteer, saying, "O Suta", that best of men furnished with grace and endowed with a voice like that of a mad swan, spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
कदाहं पुनरागम्य सरय्वाः पुष्पिते वने
मृगयां पर्याटष्यामि मात्रा पित्रा च संगतः
verses.transliteration:
kadāhaṁ punarāgamya sarayvāḥ puṣpite vane
mṛgayāṁ paryāṭaṣyāmi mātrā pitrā ca saṁgataḥ

translations.english: When shall I coming back, range a hunting the blossoming groves of the Sarayū, along with my father and mother?

verses.sanskrit:
नात्यर्थमभिकाङ्क्षामि मृगयां सरयूवने
रतिर्ह्येषातुला लोके राजर्षिगणसंमता
verses.transliteration:
nātyarthamabhikāṅkṣāmi mṛgayāṁ sarayūvane
ratirhyeṣātulā loke rājarṣigaṇasaṁmatā

translations.english: I do not so much long for hunting in the woods of the Sarayū; but a relish (for the pastime) is considered as beyond compare being held in esteem by the Rājarşis.

verses.sanskrit:
स तमध्वानमैक्ष्वाकः सूतं मधुरया गिरा
तं तमर्थमभिप्रेत्य ययौवाक्यमुदीरयन्
verses.transliteration:
sa tamadhvānamaikṣvākaḥ sūtaṁ madhurayā girā
taṁ tamarthamabhipretya yayauvākyamudīrayan

translations.english: Taking this subject, the descendant of Ikşvāku passed the way, addressing sweet words to the charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
विशालान्कोसलान्रम्यान्यात्वा लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गवेरपुरं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
viśālānkosalānramyānyātvā lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
āsasāda mahābāhuḥ śṛṅgaverapuraṁ prati

translations.english: Having passed the extensive and romantic Kosala, the intelligent elder brother of Lakşmaņa facing Ayodhyā said with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तामूर्मिकलिलावर्तामन्ववेक्ष्य महारथः
सुमन्त्रमब्रवीत्सूतमिहैवाद्य वसामहे
verses.transliteration:
tāmūrmikalilāvartāmanvavekṣya mahārathaḥ
sumantramabravītsūtamihaivādya vasāmahe

translations.english: And beholding (the river) with her surging eddies, that mighty car-warrior said to the charioteer, Sumantra, We will rest here to day.

verses.sanskrit:
अविदूरादयं नद्या बहुपुष्पप्रवालवान्
सुमहानिङ्गुदीवृक्षो वसामोऽत्रैव सारथे
verses.transliteration:
avidūrādayaṁ nadyā bahupuṣpapravālavān
sumahāniṅgudīvṛkṣo vasāmo'traiva sārathe

translations.english: There is hard by the river a gigantic Ingudī tree, bearing a profusion of flowers and fresh leaves. Here, O charioteer, will we stay to-day.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्षणश्च सुमन्त्रश्च बाढमित्येव राघवम्
उक्त्वा तमिङ्गुदीवृक्षं तदोपययतुर्हयैः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣaṇaśca sumantraśca bāḍhamityeva rāghavam
uktvā tamiṅgudīvṛkṣaṁ tadopayayaturhayaiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon saying to Rāghava, “Very well,” Lakşinana and Sumantra with the horses went to the Ingudi tree.

verses.sanskrit:
रामोऽभियाय तं रम्यं वृक्षमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः
रथादवातरत्तस्मात्सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
rāmo'bhiyāya taṁ ramyaṁ vṛkṣamikṣvākunandanaḥ
rathādavātarattasmātsabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: And reaching the tree, that descendant of Ikşvāku alighted from the car along with his wife and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रोऽप्यवतीर्यैव मोचयित्वा हयोत्तमान्
वृक्षमूलगतं राममुपतस्थे कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
sumantro'pyavatīryaiva mocayitvā hayottamān
vṛkṣamūlagataṁ rāmamupatasthe kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Then descending, Sumantra relieved those excellent horses, and with joined hands stood before Rāma seated at the foot of the tree.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र राजा गुहो नाम रामस्यात्मसमः सखा
निषादजात्यो बलवान्स्थपतिश्चेति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
tatra rājā guho nāma rāmasyātmasamaḥ sakhā
niṣādajātyo balavānsthapatiśceti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: There lived at the place a king named Guha, a friend to Răma, dear as his own self, a Nişāda by birth, powerful and famed as the lord of the Nişādas.

verses.sanskrit:
स श्रुत्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं रामं विषयमागतम्
वृद्धैः परिवृतोऽमात्यैर्ज्ञातिभिश्चाप्युपागतः
verses.transliteration:
sa śrutvā puruṣavyāghraṁ rāmaṁ viṣayamāgatam
vṛddhaiḥ parivṛto'mātyairjñātibhiścāpyupāgataḥ

translations.english: Hearing that thai foremost of men, Răma, had arrived at the place, he (Guha) surrounded by his aged counsellors and kindred came to him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निषादाधिपतिं दृष्ट्वा दूरादवस्थितम्
सह सौमित्रिणा रामः समागच्छद्गुहेन सः
verses.transliteration:
tato niṣādādhipatiṁ dṛṣṭvā dūrādavasthitam
saha saumitriṇā rāmaḥ samāgacchadguhena saḥ

translations.english: Seeing the lord of the Nişādhas at a distance, Rāma came up to him in company with Sumitra's son.

verses.sanskrit:
तमार्तः संपरिष्वज्य गुहो राघवमब्रवीत्
यथायोध्या तथेदं ते राम किं करवाणि ते
verses.transliteration:
tamārtaḥ saṁpariṣvajya guho rāghavamabravīt
yathāyodhyā tathedaṁ te rāma kiṁ karavāṇi te

translations.english: Thereat touched, Guha embracing Rāghava said to him, "O Rāma, as Ayodhyā this kingdom is to you. What shall I do for you?"

verses.sanskrit:
गुहमेव ब्रुवाणं तं राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह
अर्चिताश्चैव हृष्टाश्च भवता सर्वथा वयम्
verses.transliteration:
guhameva bruvāṇaṁ taṁ rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
arcitāścaiva hṛṣṭāśca bhavatā sarvathā vayam

translations.english: When Guha had said this, Rāghava answered him, saying, “We have been well received by you and are well pleased with you, since coming here on foot you have shown us affection."

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या त्वां गुह पश्यामि अरोगं सह बान्धवैः
अपि ते कूशलं राष्ट्रे मित्रेषु च धनेषु च
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā tvāṁ guha paśyāmi arogaṁ saha bāndhavaiḥ
api te kūśalaṁ rāṣṭre mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca

translations.english: Then pressing Guha hard with his arms, Rāma said, O Guha, it is by good luck that I see you whole along with your friends. Is your kingdom in peace both as regards your friends and the forest?

verses.sanskrit:
यत्त्विदं भवता किंचित्प्रीत्या समुपकल्पितम्
सर्वं तदनुजानामि न हि वर्ते प्रतिग्रहे
verses.transliteration:
yattvidaṁ bhavatā kiṁcitprītyā samupakalpitam
sarvaṁ tadanujānāmi na hi varte pratigrahe

translations.english: The things that you have presented me with out of love I accept but can not enjoy.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशचीराजिनधरं फलमूलाशनं च माम्
विद्धि प्रणिहितं धर्मे तापसं वनगोचरम्
verses.transliteration:
kuśacīrājinadharaṁ phalamūlāśanaṁ ca mām
viddhi praṇihitaṁ dharme tāpasaṁ vanagocaram

translations.english: Do you know me as assuming an ascetic mode of life in the woods, in which I am to wear Kusa and bark and live upon fruits and roots.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्वानां खादनेनाहमर्थी नान्येन केनचित्
एतावतात्रभवता भविष्यामि सुपूजितः
verses.transliteration:
aśvānāṁ khādanenāhamarthī nānyena kenacit
etāvatātrabhavatā bhaviṣyāmi supūjitaḥ

translations.english: So, with the single exception of the food for the horses, things require I none; and these horses being well kept, I shall consider myself as entertained by you.

verses.sanskrit:
एते हि दयिता राज्ञः पितुर्दशरथस्य मे
एतैः सुविहितैरश्वैर्भविष्याम्यहमर्चितः
verses.transliteration:
ete hi dayitā rājñaḥ piturdaśarathasya me
etaiḥ suvihitairaśvairbhaviṣyāmyahamarcitaḥ

translations.english: These are the favourites of my father, Dasaratha, and on these horses being well provided for, I shall be well received.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्वानां प्रतिपानं च खादनं चैव सोऽन्वशात्
गुहस्तत्रैव पुरुषांस्त्वरितं दीयतामिति
verses.transliteration:
aśvānāṁ pratipānaṁ ca khādanaṁ caiva so'nvaśāt
guhastatraiva puruṣāṁstvaritaṁ dīyatāmiti

translations.english: Thereupon Guha on the spot commanded the men, saying, Let the horses have without delay meats and drinks.

verses.sanskrit:
ततश्चीरोत्तरासङ्गः संध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्
जलमेवाददे भोज्यं लक्ष्मणेनाहृतं स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tataścīrottarāsaṅgaḥ saṁdhyāmanvāsya paścimām
jalamevādade bhojyaṁ lakṣmaṇenāhṛtaṁ svayam

translations.english: Then putting his sheet over his person, he (Rāma) performed his evening devotions. Having done this, he took as his sustenance the water that had been procured by Lakşmaņa himself.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य भूमौ शयानस्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य लक्ष्मणः
सभार्यस्य ततोऽभ्येत्य तस्थौ वृक्षमुपाश्रितः
verses.transliteration:
tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ
sabhāryasya tato'bhyetya tasthau vṛkṣamupāśritaḥ

translations.english: On Rāma having lain down on the ground along with his wife, Lakşmaņa washed their feet, and then remained stationed under the tree.

verses.sanskrit:
गुहोऽपि सह सूतेन सौमित्रिमनुभाषयन्
अन्वजाग्रत्ततो राममप्रमत्तो धनुर्धरः
verses.transliteration:
guho'pi saha sūtena saumitrimanubhāṣayan
anvajāgrattato rāmamapramatto dhanurdharaḥ

translations.english: Then bow in hand and with his wits about him, conversing with Sumitra's son along with the charioteer, Guha remained awake, watching Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा शयानस्य ततोऽस्य धीमतो; यशस्विनो दाशरथेर्महात्मनः
अदृष्टदुःखस्य सुखोचितस्य सा; तदा व्यतीयाय चिरेण शर्वरी
verses.transliteration:
tathā śayānasya tato'sya dhīmato; yaśasvino dāśarathermahātmanaḥ
adṛṣṭaduḥkhasya sukhocitasya sā; tadā vyatīyāya cireṇa śarvarī

translations.english: Thus the livelong night passed away with that illustrious, intelligent and high-souled son of Daśaratha, unacquainted with troubles and worthy of happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
तं जाग्रतमदम्भेन भ्रातुरर्थाय लक्ष्मणम्
गुहः संतापसंतप्तो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ jāgratamadambhena bhrāturarthāya lakṣmaṇam
guhaḥ saṁtāpasaṁtapto rāghavaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: As for the purpose of protecting his brother, Lakṣmaṇa was watching him out of sincere affection, Guha burning in grief addressed that descendant of Raghu, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता
प्रत्याश्वसिहि साध्वस्यां राजपुत्र यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadarthamupakalpitā
pratyāśvasihi sādhvasyāṁ rājaputra yathāsukham

translations.english: This O child, is the easeful bed that has been prepared for you. O prince, do you as you listen, lie down upon it.

verses.sanskrit:
उचितोऽयं जनः सर्वः क्लेशानां त्वं सुखोचितः
गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामः काकुत्स्थस्य वयं निशाम्
verses.transliteration:
ucito'yaṁ janaḥ sarvaḥ kleśānāṁ tvaṁ sukhocitaḥ
guptyarthaṁ jāgariṣyāmaḥ kākutsthasya vayaṁ niśām

translations.english: These (foresters) are inured to this hardship; but you are worthy of ease. We will wake up during the night for guarding Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि रामात्प्रियतरो ममास्ति भुवि कश्चन
ब्रवीम्येतदहं सत्यं सत्येनैव च ते शपे
verses.transliteration:
na hi rāmātpriyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaścana
bravīmyetadahaṁ satyaṁ satyenaiva ca te śape

translations.english: There is none on earth dearer to me than Răma. This I tell you truly and I swear by truth itself.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेऽस्मिन्सुमहद्यशः
धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थावाप्तिं च केवलाम्
verses.transliteration:
asya prasādādāśaṁse loke'sminsumahadyaśaḥ
dharmāvāptiṁ ca vipulāmarthāvāptiṁ ca kevalām

translations.english: Through his grace I hope in this world to attain high fame, and great religious merit as well as completely secure profit and pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया
रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणिः सर्वतो ज्ञातिभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ priyasakhaṁ rāmaṁ śayānaṁ saha sītayā
rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sarvato jñātibhiḥ saha

translations.english: I will bow in hand in company with my kindred adequately guard my dear friend reposing with Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मेऽविदितं किंचिद्वनेऽस्मिंश्चरतः सदा
चतुरङ्गं ह्यपि बलं सुमहत्प्रसहेमहि
verses.transliteration:
na hi me'viditaṁ kiṁcidvane'smiṁścarataḥ sadā
caturaṅgaṁ hyapi balaṁ sumahatprasahemahi

translations.english: Always ranging in this forest, nothing herein is unknown to me. I shall vanquish even any mighty body of fourfold forces (that may come up against us.)

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्तं तदोवाच रक्ष्यमाणास्त्वयानघ
नात्र भीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇastaṁ tadovāca rakṣyamāṇāstvayānagha
nātra bhītā vayaṁ sarve dharmamevānupaśyatā

translations.english: Thereupon Laksmana said, O sinless one, protected by you ever having your sight fixed on virtue, we do not fear to live in this place. But how with Dasaratha's son lying down on the ground along with Sītă can I indulge in sleep or what is the use of my living and enjoying happiness?

verses.sanskrit:
कथं दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया
शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितं वा सुखानि वा
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā
śakyā nidrā mayā labdhuṁ jīvitaṁ vā sukhāni vā

translations.english: How, Dasaratha's son sleeping on the earth with Sītā, can I attain sleep, or life, or happiness?

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्प्रव्रजितो राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति
विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
asminpravrajito rājā na ciraṁ vartayiṣyati
vidhavā medinī nūnaṁ kṣiprameva bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Him do you behold with ease asleep on the grass in company with Sītā, who was incapable of being borne in fight by the gods and the Asuras, and who obtained through Mantras and austerities and various endeavours, Dasaratha crowned with every auspicious mark, is the most meritorious son of the king. Rāma being banished, the king will not live long and the earth will shortly be widowed.

verses.sanskrit:
विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः
निर्घोषोपरतं तात मन्ये राजनिवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
vinadya sumahānādaṁ śrameṇoparatāḥ striyaḥ
nirghoṣoparataṁ tāta manye rājaniveśanam

translations.english: Having bewailed aloud, the women have, methinks, (by this time) ceased through fatigue, and the king's residence is still.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम
नाशंसे यदि जीवन्ति सर्वे ते शर्वरीमिमाम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama
nāśaṁse yadi jīvanti sarve te śarvarīmimām

translations.english: I can not hope that Kausalyā, the king, and my mother (Sumitrā) all those are yet alive.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवेदपि हि मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया
तद्दुःखं यत्तु कौसल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
jīvedapi hi me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā
tadduḥkhaṁ yattu kausalyā vīrasūrvinaśiṣyati

translations.english: If they are, it is for this night only. Even if my mother live looking up to Satrughna, yet this is my grief that that mother of a hero, Kausalyā will breathe her last.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुरक्तजनाकीर्णा सुखालोकप्रियावहा
राजव्यसनसंसृष्टा सा पुरी विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
anuraktajanākīrṇā sukhālokapriyāvahā
rājavyasanasaṁsṛṣṭā sā purī vinaśiṣyati

translations.english: And that palace filled with people attached to Rāma and flooded with the light of delight, will, visited with the calamity that will befall the king meet with destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्
राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
atikrāntamatikrāntamanavāpya manoratham
rājye rāmamanikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati

translations.english: Frustrated in his desire, my father, foiled in his endeavours to confer the kingdom on Rāma, will, exclaiming 'All is lost,' 'All is lost,' give up the ghost.

verses.sanskrit:
सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन्काले ह्युपस्थिते
प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति भूमिपम्
verses.transliteration:
siddhārthāḥ pitaraṁ vṛttaṁ tasminkāle hyupasthite
pretakāryeṣu sarveṣu saṁskariṣyanti bhūmipam

translations.english: Blessed are they that when the time shall come for the same, shall perform the funeral ceremonies of the king, my deceased sire.

verses.sanskrit:
आरामोद्यानसंपन्नां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्
सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम
verses.transliteration:
ārāmodyānasaṁpannāṁ samājotsavaśālinīm
sukhitā vicariṣyanti rājadhānīṁ piturmama

translations.english: They will happily range the capital of my father, furnished with fair looking terraces, with its highways laid out orderly, having lordly edifices and palatial residences, graced with excellent courtezans, abounding with cars, elephants and horses, resounding with the notes of trumpets, the abode of all auspiciousness, filled with portly and contented folks, rich in gardens and villas, and celebrating popular festivites.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयम्
निवृत्ते वनवासेऽस्मिन्नयोध्यां प्रविशेमहि
verses.transliteration:
api satyapratijñena sārdhaṁ kuśalinā vayam
nivṛtte vanavāse'sminnayodhyāṁ praviśemahi

translations.english: If we remain in peace, we shall returning from the forest with that one firm in promise, enter Ayodhyā?

verses.sanskrit:
परिदेवयमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः
तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी सात्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
paridevayamānasya duḥkhārtasya mahātmanaḥ
tiṣṭhato rājaputrasya śarvarī sātyavartata

translations.english: As the high-souled son of the king oppressed with grief was thus lamenting sitting up, the day broke.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा हि सत्यं ब्रुवति प्रजाहिते; नरेन्द्रपुत्रे गुरुसौहृदाद्गुहः
मुमोच बाष्पं व्यसनाभिपीडितो; ज्वरातुरो नाग इव व्यथातुरः
verses.transliteration:
tathā hi satyaṁ bruvati prajāhite; narendraputre gurusauhṛdādguhaḥ
mumoca bāṣpaṁ vyasanābhipīḍito; jvarāturo nāga iva vyathāturaḥ

translations.english: When that son of the foremost of men, intent on the welfare of the subjects had spoken thus truly, Guha, out of extreme affection for (Rāma), shed tears afflicted with grief and hurt like an elephant suffering from fever.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पृथु वृक्षा महायशाः
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
prabhātāyāṁ tu śarvaryāṁ pṛthu vṛkṣā mahāyaśāḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣaṇam

translations.english: When the morning broke, that illustrious one having a spacious chest, Rāma, addressed Sumitrā's son, Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks.

verses.sanskrit:
बर्हिणानां च निर्घोषः श्रूयते नदतां वने
तराम जाह्नवीं सौम्य शीघ्रगां सागरंगमाम्
verses.transliteration:
barhiṇānāṁ ca nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate nadatāṁ vane
tarāma jāhnavīṁ saumya śīghragāṁ sāgaraṁgamām

translations.english: This is the time of sunrise: the reverend Night has departed. O child, this gracefully sable-hued bird, the Coel, has began to warble, and I hear the cries of peacocks uttering notes in the woods. O amiable one, we will cross the Jāhnavī, fast rushing to the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञाय रामस्य वचः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः
गुहमामन्त्र्य सूतं च सोऽतिष्ठद्भ्रातुरग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
vijñāya rāmasya vacaḥ saumitrirmitranandanaḥ
guhamāmantrya sūtaṁ ca so'tiṣṭhadbhrāturagrataḥ

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words, that enhancer of the delight of friends, Sumitra's son, conveyed them to Guha and the charioteer; and then stood before his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कलापान्संनह्य खड्गौ बद्ध्वा च धन्विनौ
जग्मतुर्येन तौ गङ्गां सीतया सह राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kalāpānsaṁnahya khaḍgau baddhvā ca dhanvinau
jagmaturyena tau gaṅgāṁ sītayā saha rāghavau

translations.english: Then donning on their mail and equipped with their bows, quivers and swords, the Rāghavas along with Sītā descended to the Gangā.

verses.sanskrit:
राममेव तु धर्मज्ञमुपगम्य विनीतवत्
किमहं करवाणीति सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmameva tu dharmajñamupagamya vinītavat
kimahaṁ karavāṇīti sūtaḥ prāñjalirabravīt

translations.english: Then coming forward in humble guise before Rāma cognizant of virtue, the charioteer said with joined hands, "What shall I do (now)?"

verses.sanskrit:
निवर्तस्वेत्युवाचैनमेतावद्धि कृतं मम
यानं विहाय पद्भ्यां तु गमिष्यामो महावनम्
verses.transliteration:
nivartasvetyuvācainametāvaddhi kṛtaṁ mama
yānaṁ vihāya padbhyāṁ tu gamiṣyāmo mahāvanam

translations.english: “Do you” said he to the charioteer, "turn back, So far I have come (in obedience to the order of the monarch.) Now, renouncing the car, will I repair to the mighty forest on foot."

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं त्वभ्यनुज्ञातमवेक्ष्यार्तः स सारथिः
सुमन्त्रः पुरुषव्याघ्रमैक्ष्वाकमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ātmānaṁ tvabhyanujñātamavekṣyārtaḥ sa sārathiḥ
sumantraḥ puruṣavyāghramaikṣvākamidamabravīt

translations.english: Finding himself thus commanded, the charioteer, Sumantra grieved at heart spoke to that best of men, the descendant of Ikşvāku.

verses.sanskrit:
नातिक्रान्तमिदं लोके पुरुषेणेह केनचित्
तव सभ्रातृभार्यस्य वासः प्राकृतवद्वने
verses.transliteration:
nātikrāntamidaṁ loke puruṣeṇeha kenacit
tava sabhrātṛbhāryasya vāsaḥ prākṛtavadvane

translations.english: That Destiny owing to which you will have to pass your days in the forest like a low person, along with your brother and wife, has in this world been withstood by none.

verses.sanskrit:
न मन्ये ब्रह्मचर्येऽस्ति स्वधीते वा फलोदयः
मार्दवार्जवयोर्वापि त्वां चेद्व्यसनमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
na manye brahmacarye'sti svadhīte vā phalodayaḥ
mārdavārjavayorvāpi tvāṁ cedvyasanamāgatam

translations.english: I deem the Brahmacarya mode of life, or study, or meekness or sincerity as attended with no fruit, since you have come by calamity.

verses.sanskrit:
सह राघव वैदेह्या भ्रात्रा चैव वने वसन्
त्वं गतिं प्राप्स्यसे वीर त्रीँल्लोकांस्तु जयन्निव
verses.transliteration:
saha rāghava vaidehyā bhrātrā caiva vane vasan
tvaṁ gatiṁ prāpsyase vīra trī̐llokāṁstu jayanniva

translations.english: O Rāghava, living in the forest with Vaidehi and your brother, you, O Lord, attain a state (of supreme excellence), having, as it were, conquered the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
वयं खलु हता राम ये तयाप्युपवञ्चिताः
कैकेय्या वशमेष्यामः पापाया दुःखभागिनः
verses.transliteration:
vayaṁ khalu hatā rāma ye tayāpyupavañcitāḥ
kaikeyyā vaśameṣyāmaḥ pāpāyā duḥkhabhāginaḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, it is we, wretched that we are, that are undone, as we, deprived of your company, shall come under the sinful Kaikeyi expressing great misery.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवन्नात्म समं सुमन्त्रः सारथिस्तदा
दृष्ट्वा दुर गतं रामं दुःखार्तो रुरुदे चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvannātma samaṁ sumantraḥ sārathistadā
dṛṣṭvā dura gataṁ rāmaṁ duḥkhārto rurude ciram

translations.english: Having said this, the charioteer, Sumantra, seeing Rāma intent upon going to a distant land, wept for a long while in heaviness of heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु विगते बाष्पे सूतं स्पृष्टोदकं शुचिम्
रामस्तु मधुरं वाक्यं पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu vigate bāṣpe sūtaṁ spṛṣṭodakaṁ śucim
rāmastu madhuraṁ vākyaṁ punaḥ punaruvāca tam

translations.english: Then when he had dried up his tears, and sanctified himself by touching the water of the Gangā, Rāma again addressed the charioteer in sweet words, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां त्वया तुल्यं सुहृदं नोपलक्षये
यथा दशरथो राजा मां न शोचेत्तथा कुरु
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ tvayā tulyaṁ suhṛdaṁ nopalakṣaye
yathā daśaratho rājā māṁ na śocettathā kuru

translations.english: I do not find any one that is a friend of the sons of Ikşvāku like to you. Do you so act that king Dasaratha may not grieve (for me.)

verses.sanskrit:
शोकोपहत चेताश्च वृद्धश्च जगतीपतिः
काम भारावसन्नश्च तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते
verses.transliteration:
śokopahata cetāśca vṛddhaśca jagatīpatiḥ
kāma bhārāvasannaśca tasmādetadbravīmi te

translations.english: The lord of earth has been deprived of his senses by grief, has grown old, and is oppressed by the weight of desires (thwarted.) Therefore it is that I tell you this.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यदाज्ञापयेत्किंचित्स महात्मा महीपतिः
कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं कार्यं तदविकाङ्क्षया
verses.transliteration:
yadyadājñāpayetkiṁcitsa mahātmā mahīpatiḥ
kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmārthaṁ kāryaṁ tadavikāṅkṣayā

translations.english: Whatever that noble-minded lord of earth commands for the pleasure of Kaikeyi, should by us be done with alacrity.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदर्थं हि राज्यानि प्रशासति नरेश्वराः
यदेषां सर्वकृत्येषु मनो न प्रतिहन्यते
verses.transliteration:
etadarthaṁ hi rājyāni praśāsati nareśvarāḥ
yadeṣāṁ sarvakṛtyeṣu mano na pratihanyate

translations.english: It is for this that those lords of men, kings, govern, viz., that others may not thwart their purposes.)

verses.sanskrit:
तद्यथा स महाराजो नालीकमधिगच्छति
न च ताम्यति दुःखेन सुमन्त्र कुरु तत्तथा
verses.transliteration:
tadyathā sa mahārājo nālīkamadhigacchati
na ca tāmyati duḥkhena sumantra kuru tattathā

translations.english: O Sumantra, do you act so, that the mighty monarch may not come across anything unpleasant, or be attacked with chagrin through grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टदुःखं राजानं वृद्धमार्यं जितेन्द्रियम्
ब्रूयास्त्वमभिवाद्यैव मम हेतोरिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭaduḥkhaṁ rājānaṁ vṛddhamāryaṁ jitendriyam
brūyāstvamabhivādyaiva mama hetoridaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Do you saluting him for me say these words to the aged monarch who has his senses under complete control, and who has never seen misfortune before.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवाहमनुशोचामि लक्ष्मणो न च मैथिली
अयोध्यायाश्च्युताश्चेति वने वत्स्यामहेति वा
verses.transliteration:
naivāhamanuśocāmi lakṣmaṇo na ca maithilī
ayodhyāyāścyutāśceti vane vatsyāmaheti vā

translations.english: Neither I nor Lakşmaņa grieve for being ejected out of Ayodhyā, or that we shall have to abide in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दशसु वर्षेषु निवृत्तेषु पुनः पुनः
लक्ष्मणं मां च सीतां च द्रक्ष्यसि क्षिप्रमागतान्
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśasu varṣeṣu nivṛtteṣu punaḥ punaḥ
lakṣmaṇaṁ māṁ ca sītāṁ ca drakṣyasi kṣipramāgatān

translations.english: After these fourteen years have gone by, you will see Lakşmaņa, Sītā and myself come to you speedily.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं मातरं च सुमन्त्र मे
अन्याश्च देवीः सहिताः कैकेयीं च पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu rājānaṁ mātaraṁ ca sumantra me
anyāśca devīḥ sahitāḥ kaikeyīṁ ca punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Having thus, O Sumantra, in my name again and again spoken to the king, to iny mother and to Kaikeyi along with the other revered ladies, do you communicate to Kausalyā our welfare conveying to her at the same time Şītā's and Lakşmana's salutations to her feet as well those of myself who am her eldest son.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूयाश्च हि महाराजं भरतं क्षिप्रमानय
आगतश्चापि भरतः स्थाप्यो नृपमते पदे
verses.transliteration:
brūyāśca hi mahārājaṁ bharataṁ kṣipramānaya
āgataścāpi bharataḥ sthāpyo nṛpamate pade

translations.english: Do you also tell the king, 'Do you speedily bring Bharata; and when Bharata has come, let him be the invested with royalty.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतं च परिष्वज्य यौवराज्येऽभिषिच्य च
अस्मत्संतापजं दुःखं न त्वामभिभविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
bharataṁ ca pariṣvajya yauvarājye'bhiṣicya ca
asmatsaṁtāpajaṁ duḥkhaṁ na tvāmabhibhaviṣyati

translations.english: When you have embraced Bharata and installed him in the kingdom, you no longer be overpowered with grief on our account.'

verses.sanskrit:
भरतश्चापि वक्तव्यो यथा राजनि वर्तसे
तथा मातृषु वर्तेथाः सर्वास्वेवाविशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
bharataścāpi vaktavyo yathā rājani vartase
tathā mātṛṣu vartethāḥ sarvāsvevāviśeṣataḥ

translations.english: And tell Bharata, “As you bear yourself to the king so it behoves you to bear yourself to all your mothers, without making any distinction at hall. As Kaikeyi is unto you, so without distinction is Sumitrā.'

verses.sanskrit:
निवर्त्यमानो रामेण सुमन्त्रः शोककर्शितः
तत्सर्वं वचनं श्रुत्वा स्नेहात्काकुत्स्थमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
nivartyamāno rāmeṇa sumantraḥ śokakarśitaḥ
tatsarvaṁ vacanaṁ śrutvā snehātkākutsthamabravīt

translations.english: Told by Rāma to go back and instructed in this wise, Sumantra having heard everything, addressed Kākutstha from affection, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यदहं नोपचारेण ब्रूयां स्नेहादविक्लवः
भक्तिमानिति तत्तावद्वाक्यं त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
yadahaṁ nopacāreṇa brūyāṁ snehādaviklavaḥ
bhaktimāniti tattāvadvākyaṁ tvaṁ kṣantumarhasi

translations.english: It behoves you to forgive what I say plainly from affection, without letting myself by overwhelmed with emotion, and with due reverence for you. How can I, O child, without you return to that city, which seems as it afflicted with the grief incident to the loss of a son?

verses.sanskrit:
सराममपि तावन्मे रथं दृष्ट्वा तदा जनः
विना रामं रथं दृष्ट्वा विदीर्येतापि सा पुरी
verses.transliteration:
sarāmamapi tāvanme rathaṁ dṛṣṭvā tadā janaḥ
vinā rāmaṁ rathaṁ dṛṣṭvā vidīryetāpi sā purī

translations.english: Having then seen my car with Rāma on it, the hearts of the people and the palace will in all likelihood burst when they shall see it without Rāma. Surely the city will be distressed on beholding this empty car, like a host seeing car with its ro slain and the charioteer alone left in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
दूरेऽपि निवसन्तं त्वां मानसेनाग्रतः स्थितम्
चिन्तयन्त्योऽद्य नूनं त्वां निराहाराः कृताः प्रजाः
verses.transliteration:
dūre'pi nivasantaṁ tvāṁ mānasenāgrataḥ sthitam
cintayantyo'dya nūnaṁ tvāṁ nirāhārāḥ kṛtāḥ prajāḥ

translations.english: Thinking in their minds that you although actually at a great distance from them, are before them, the subjects (not finding you) will renounce food (and thus destroy themselves.)

verses.sanskrit:
आर्तनादो हि यः पौरैर्मुक्तस्तद्विप्रवासने
रथस्थं मां निशाम्यैव कुर्युः शतगुणं ततः
verses.transliteration:
ārtanādo hi yaḥ paurairmuktastadvipravāsane
rathasthaṁ māṁ niśāmyaiva kuryuḥ śataguṇaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: They will on seeing me with the car, burst out into lamentations exceeding a hundred times in bitterness those in which they indulged when you set out for the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं किं चापि वक्ष्यामि देवीं तव सुतो मया
नीतोऽसौ मातुलकुलं संतापं मा कृथा इति
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ kiṁ cāpi vakṣyāmi devīṁ tava suto mayā
nīto'sau mātulakulaṁ saṁtāpaṁ mā kṛthā iti

translations.english: Shall I say to the worshipful one, 'I have conveyed your son to the home of his maternal uncle. Do you not grieve.' I will never tell such a lie. Yet how can I speak this truth which is so very unpleasant?

verses.sanskrit:
मम तावन्नियोगस्थास्त्वद्बन्धुजनवाहिनः
कथं रथं त्वया हीनं प्रवक्ष्यन्ति हयोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
mama tāvanniyogasthāstvadbandhujanavāhinaḥ
kathaṁ rathaṁ tvayā hīnaṁ pravakṣyanti hayottamāḥ

translations.english: And ever abiding by my command and used to carry your friends, how can these excellent horses bear this car without you?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मे याचमानस्य त्यागमेव करिष्यसि
सरथोऽग्निं प्रवेक्ष्यामि त्यक्त मात्र इह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
yadi me yācamānasya tyāgameva kariṣyasi
saratho'gniṁ pravekṣyāmi tyakta mātra iha tvayā

translations.english: But if you forsake me who beseech you, I will as soon as left by you, enter into fire along with the car.

verses.sanskrit:
भविष्यन्ति वने यानि तपोविघ्नकराणि ते
रथेन प्रतिबाधिष्ये तानि सत्त्वानि राघव
verses.transliteration:
bhaviṣyanti vane yāni tapovighnakarāṇi te
rathena pratibādhiṣye tāni sattvāni rāghava

translations.english: I shall, O Rāghava, by means of this car, withstand all those impediments that shall present themselves against your ascetic austerities in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्कृतेन मया प्राप्तं रथ चर्या कृतं सुखम्
आशंसे त्वत्कृतेनाहं वनवासकृतं सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
tatkṛtena mayā prāptaṁ ratha caryā kṛtaṁ sukham
āśaṁse tvatkṛtenāhaṁ vanavāsakṛtaṁ sukham

translations.english: I have through your favour experienced the pleasure of driving the car. I expect at your hands the pleasure of living in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसीदेच्छामि तेऽरण्ये भवितुं प्रत्यनन्तरः
प्रीत्याभिहितमिच्छामि भव मे पत्यनन्तरः
verses.transliteration:
prasīdecchāmi te'raṇye bhavituṁ pratyanantaraḥ
prītyābhihitamicchāmi bhava me patyanantaraḥ

translations.english: Be you propitious. It is my wish to remain in the forest with you, and do you say, affectionately, 'Do you remain by my side.'

verses.sanskrit:
तव शुश्रूषणं मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन्
अयोध्यां देवलोकं वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tava śuśrūṣaṇaṁ mūrdhnā kariṣyāmi vane vasan
ayodhyāṁ devalokaṁ vā sarvathā prajahāmyaham

translations.english: Living in the forest, I will serve you with the crown of my head; and I will entirely renounce Ayodhyā or the celestial regions themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि शक्या प्रवेष्टुं सा मयायोध्या त्वया विना
राजधानी महेन्द्रस्य यथा दुष्कृतकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
na hi śakyā praveṣṭuṁ sā mayāyodhyā tvayā vinā
rājadhānī mahendrasya yathā duṣkṛtakarmaṇā

translations.english: Even as a doer of evil deeds cannot enter the metropolis of the mighty Indra, I am incapable of entering Ayodhyā without you.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे चापि हया वीर यदि ते वनवासिनः
परिचर्यां करिष्यन्ति प्राप्स्यन्ति परमां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
ime cāpi hayā vīra yadi te vanavāsinaḥ
paricaryāṁ kariṣyanti prāpsyanti paramāṁ gatim

translations.english: And these horses, O hero, will attain to a supreme state if your serve you during your abode in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
वनवासे क्षयं प्राप्ते ममैष हि मनोरथः
यदनेन रथेनैव त्वां वहेयं पुरीं पुनः
verses.transliteration:
vanavāse kṣayaṁ prāpte mamaiṣa hi manorathaḥ
yadanena rathenaiva tvāṁ vaheyaṁ purīṁ punaḥ

translations.english: This is my desire that the term of exile over, I may carry you back to the palace on this very car.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि सहितस्य त्वया वने
क्षणभूतानि यास्यन्ति शतशस्तु ततोऽन्यथा
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi sahitasya tvayā vane
kṣaṇabhūtāni yāsyanti śataśastu tato'nyathā

translations.english: Remaining with you in the forest the fourteen years will pass away dwindled into a moment, but without you, they shall the proportions of an hundred years. assume

verses.sanskrit:
भृत्यवत्सल तिष्ठन्तं भर्तृपुत्रगते पथि
भक्तं भृत्यं स्थितं स्थित्यां त्वं न मां हातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
bhṛtyavatsala tiṣṭhantaṁ bhartṛputragate pathi
bhaktaṁ bhṛtyaṁ sthitaṁ sthityāṁ tvaṁ na māṁ hātumarhasi

translations.english: O you bearing affection towards your servants, it does not behove you to forsake your servant having regard for you, ever abiding by the way that is wended by the son of his master, and observing the duties of his position.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधं दीनं याचमानं पुनः पुनः
रामो भृत्यानुकम्पी तु सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bahuvidhaṁ dīnaṁ yācamānaṁ punaḥ punaḥ
rāmo bhṛtyānukampī tu sumantramidamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma kind towards servants, said these words to Sumantra as he besought him thus humbly in various ways, O you that bear attachment to your master, I know that you regard me highly. But do you listen as to why I send you to the city from hence.

verses.sanskrit:
नगरीं त्वां गतं दृष्ट्वा जननी मे यवीयसी
कैकेयी प्रत्ययं गच्छेदिति रामो वनं गतः
verses.transliteration:
nagarīṁ tvāṁ gataṁ dṛṣṭvā jananī me yavīyasī
kaikeyī pratyayaṁ gacchediti rāmo vanaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Seeing you returned to the city, my youngest mother Kaikeyi will believe that Rāma has gone to the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
परितुष्टा हि सा देवि वनवासं गते मयि
राजानं नातिशङ्केत मिथ्यावादीति धार्मिकम्
verses.transliteration:
parituṣṭā hi sā devi vanavāsaṁ gate mayi
rājānaṁ nātiśaṅketa mithyāvādīti dhārmikam

translations.english: Then well pleased on my having repaired to the woods, she will not entertain any apprehension anent the righteous monarch, thinking that he is intruthful.

verses.sanskrit:
एष मे प्रथमः कल्पो यदम्बा मे यवीयसी
भरतारक्षितं स्फीतं पुत्रराज्यमवाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa me prathamaḥ kalpo yadambā me yavīyasī
bharatārakṣitaṁ sphītaṁ putrarājyamavāpnuyāt

translations.english: This is my first wish that my youngest mother may obtain her son's kingdom, prosperous and well protected by Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
मम प्रियार्थं राज्ञश्च सरथस्त्वं पुरीं व्रज
संदिष्टश्चासि यानर्थांस्तांस्तान्ब्रूयास्तथातथा
verses.transliteration:
mama priyārthaṁ rājñaśca sarathastvaṁ purīṁ vraja
saṁdiṣṭaścāsi yānarthāṁstāṁstānbrūyāstathātathā

translations.english: Do you, O Sumantra, bear yourself to the palace to compass the end of both the king and myself, and do you communicate in the desired way what I have said to the respective parties.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं सूतं सान्त्वयित्वा पुनः पुनः
गुहं वचनमक्लीबं रामो हेतुमदब्रवीत्
जटाः कृत्वा गमिष्यामि न्यग्रोधक्षीरमानय
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā vacanaṁ sūtaṁ sāntvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
guhaṁ vacanamaklībaṁ rāmo hetumadabravīt
jaṭāḥ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi nyagrodhakṣīramānaya

translations.english: Having said this to the charioteer and consoled him again and again, the energetic Rāma spoke to Guha the following words fraught with reason.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तदा चीरवसनौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ
अशोभेतामृषिसमौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tau tadā cīravasanau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau
aśobhetāmṛṣisamau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: And that mighty-armed chief of men wore matted locks. And those brothers Rāma and Lakş maņa dressed as mendicants, and wearing heads of matted hair, appeared like saints.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वैखानसं मार्गमास्थितः सहलक्ष्मणः
व्रतमादिष्टवान्रामः सहायं गुहमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato vaikhānasaṁ mārgamāsthitaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
vratamādiṣṭavānrāmaḥ sahāyaṁ guhamabravīt

translations.english: Then entering upon the Vānaprastha mode of life, Rāma along with Lakşmaņa assuming the vow of that life, observed to that adherent of his, Guha.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमत्तो बले कोशे दुर्गे जनपदे तथा
भवेथा गुह राज्यं हि दुरारक्षतमं मतम्
verses.transliteration:
apramatto bale kośe durge janapade tathā
bhavethā guha rājyaṁ hi durārakṣatamaṁ matam

translations.english: Do you, my friend, vigilantly protect the army, the exchequer, the fort and the provinces; for a kingdom demands all the exertions (of the king thereof).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं समनुज्ञाय गुहमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः
जगाम तूर्णमव्यग्रः सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ samanujñāya guhamikṣvākunandanaḥ
jagāma tūrṇamavyagraḥ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then taking the permission of Guha, the descendant of Ikşvāku, holding his soul in calmness, set out with his wife and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दृष्ट्वा नदीतीरे नावमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः
तितीर्षुः शीघ्रगां गङ्गामिदं लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dṛṣṭvā nadītīre nāvamikṣvākunandanaḥ
titīrṣuḥ śīghragāṁ gaṅgāmidaṁ lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing a boat at the river-side, that son of Ikşvāku desirous of crossing the swift-coursing Garigā, spoke these words.

verses.sanskrit:
आरोह त्वं नर व्याघ्र स्थितां नावमिमां शनैः
सीतां चारोपयान्वक्षं परिगृह्य मनस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
āroha tvaṁ nara vyāghra sthitāṁ nāvamimāṁ śanaiḥ
sītāṁ cāropayānvakṣaṁ parigṛhya manasvinīm

translations.english: Do you ascend, gently, O foremost of men, the boat that stay here, after the making the virtuous Sītā ascend by taking her by the hand.

verses.sanskrit:
स भ्रातुः शासनं श्रुत्वा सर्वमप्रतिकूलयन्
आरोप्य मैथिलीं पूर्वमारुरोहात्मवांस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhrātuḥ śāsanaṁ śrutvā sarvamapratikūlayan
āropya maithilīṁ pūrvamārurohātmavāṁstataḥ

translations.english: Hearing his brother's command, that strongwilled one, furthering everything, having made Mithila's daughter ascend, ascended himself.

verses.sanskrit:
अथारुरोह तेजस्वी स्वयं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
ततो निषादाधिपतिर्गुहो ज्ञातीनचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
athāruroha tejasvī svayaṁ lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
tato niṣādādhipatirguho jñātīnacodayat

translations.english: That energetic elder brother of Lakşmaņa next ascended himself. Then the lord of the Nişadas, Guha, incited his kinsfolk.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुज्ञाय सुमन्त्रं च सबलं चैव तं गुहम्
आस्थाय नावं रामस्तु चोदयामास नाविकान्
verses.transliteration:
anujñāya sumantraṁ ca sabalaṁ caiva taṁ guham
āsthāya nāvaṁ rāmastu codayāmāsa nāvikān

translations.english: Then telling Sumantra, Guha, and the forces, Rāma ascending the boat, ordered the boatmen (to proceed).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तैश्चोदिता सा नौः कर्णधारसमाहिता
शुभस्फ्यवेगाभिहता शीघ्रं सलिलमत्यगात्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaiścoditā sā nauḥ karṇadhārasamāhitā
śubhasphyavegābhihatā śīghraṁ salilamatyagāt

translations.english: Then the boat decked out by the heimsman, moved by them, and urged on by the pulls of the goodly roars, proceeded apace in the water.

verses.sanskrit:
मध्यं तु समनुप्राप्य भागीरथ्यास्त्वनिन्दिता
वैदेही प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तां नदीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
madhyaṁ tu samanuprāpya bhāgīrathyāstvaninditā
vaidehī prāñjalirbhūtvā tāṁ nadīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Having arrived at the middle of the Bhagirathi, that blameless one, Vaidehi, with joined hands, addressed the river, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रो दशरथस्यायं महाराजस्य धीमतः
निदेशं पालयत्वेनं गङ्गे त्वदभिरक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
putro daśarathasyāyaṁ mahārājasya dhīmataḥ
nideśaṁ pālayatvenaṁ gaṅge tvadabhirakṣitaḥ

translations.english: O Ganga, protected by you, may the son of the intelligent and mighty monarch, Dasaratha, execute the mandate (of the latter.)

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि समग्राण्युष्य कानने
भ्रात्रा सह मया चैव पुनः प्रत्यागमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi samagrāṇyuṣya kānane
bhrātrā saha mayā caiva punaḥ pratyāgamiṣyati

translations.english: Having spent complete fourteen years in the forest, he will return in company with his brother and myself.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वां देवि सुभगे क्षेमेण पुनरागता
यक्ष्ये प्रमुदिता गङ्गे सर्वकामसमृद्धये
verses.transliteration:
tatastvāṁ devi subhage kṣemeṇa punarāgatā
yakṣye pramuditā gaṅge sarvakāmasamṛddhaye

translations.english: Then, O worshipful one, O you of auspicious fortune, having returned safely, I will, O Gangā, worship you, you that crown every desire.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि त्रिपथगा देवि ब्रह्म लोकं समीक्षसे
भार्या चोदधिराजस्य लोकेऽस्मिन्संप्रदृश्यसे
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi tripathagā devi brahma lokaṁ samīkṣase
bhāryā codadhirājasya loke'sminsaṁpradṛśyase

translations.english: O you that wend in three ways, O revered one, you envelope the regions of Brahma. You appear in this world as the spouse of the Ocean-king.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वां देवि नमस्यामि प्रशंसामि च शोभने
प्राप्त राज्ये नरव्याघ्र शिवेन पुनरागते
verses.transliteration:
sā tvāṁ devi namasyāmi praśaṁsāmi ca śobhane
prāpta rājye naravyāghra śivena punarāgate

translations.english: I will, O respected one, bow down to you, O beauteous one, I will hymn you, when, with good fortune returned, the foremost of men has obtained the kingdom, I will to please you give away to Brāhmaṇas hundreds and thousands of kine, cloths, sapid rice, and vessels of wine by thousands, and pillaos.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा संभाषमाणा सा सीता गङ्गामनिन्दिता
दक्षिणा दक्षिणं तीरं क्षिप्रमेवाभ्युपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
tathā saṁbhāṣamāṇā sā sītā gaṅgāmaninditā
dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇaṁ tīraṁ kṣipramevābhyupāgamat

translations.english: Having thus addressed the Gangā, that blameless one ever obedient to her husband, swiftly went to the south bank (of the river).

verses.sanskrit:
तीरं तु समनुप्राप्य नावं हित्वा नरर्षभः
प्रातिष्ठत सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या च परंतपः
verses.transliteration:
tīraṁ tu samanuprāpya nāvaṁ hitvā nararṣabhaḥ
prātiṣṭhata saha bhrātrā vaidehyā ca paraṁtapaḥ

translations.english: Going to the (other) bank of the stream, that best of men, and subduer of foes stood along with his brother and Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्ठतोऽहं गमिष्यामि त्वां च सीतां च पालयन्
अद्य दुःखं तु वैदेही वनवासस्य वेत्स्यति
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭhato'haṁ gamiṣyāmi tvāṁ ca sītāṁ ca pālayan
adya duḥkhaṁ tu vaidehī vanavāsasya vetsyati

translations.english: We have not yet performed any of the arduous tasks. To day Vaidehi will know the grief of a life in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
गतं तु गङ्गापरपारमाशु; रामं सुमन्त्रः प्रततं निरीक्ष्य
अध्वप्रकर्षाद्विनिवृत्तदृष्टि;र्मुमोच बाष्पं व्यथितस्तपस्वी
verses.transliteration:
gataṁ tu gaṅgāparapāramāśu; rāmaṁ sumantraḥ pratataṁ nirīkṣya
adhvaprakarṣādvinivṛttadṛṣṭi;rmumoca bāṣpaṁ vyathitastapasvī

translations.english: On Rāma having speedily crossed the Gangā, the distressed Sumantra who had been gazing at him steadfastly, being no longer able to discern him, turned away his eyes and, overcome with grief, shed tears.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तत्र हत्वा चतुरो महामृगा;न्वराहमृश्यं पृषतं महारुरुम्
आदाय मेध्यं त्वरितं बुभुक्षितौ; वासाय काले ययतुर्वनस्पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tau tatra hatvā caturo mahāmṛgā;nvarāhamṛśyaṁ pṛṣataṁ mahārurum
ādāya medhyaṁ tvaritaṁ bubhukṣitau; vāsāya kāle yayaturvanaspatim

translations.english: And then the two (brothers) having slain the four kinds of beasts, viz., boars, rsyas, prsatas and maharurus,* and taking their flesh, in the evening took refuge under a mighty tree, feeling the demands of appetite. *Varieties of deer.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं वृक्षं समासाद्य संध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्
रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठ इति होवाच लक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ vṛkṣaṁ samāsādya saṁdhyāmanvāsya paścimām
rāmo ramayatāṁ śreṣṭha iti hovāca lakṣmaṇam

translations.english: Having taken refuge under the tree and performed his evening devotions, that foremost of those capable of charming others. Rāma, addressed Laksmana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्येयं प्रथमा रात्रिर्याता जनपदाद्बहिः
या सुमन्त्रेण रहिता तां नोत्कण्ठितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
adyeyaṁ prathamā rātriryātā janapadādbahiḥ
yā sumantreṇa rahitā tāṁ notkaṇṭhitumarhasi

translations.english: To day is the first night (which we must spend) outside the inhabited tracts without the company of Sumantra.. You ought not to suffer your mind to be uneasy on that score.

verses.sanskrit:
जागर्तव्यमतन्द्रिभ्यामद्य प्रभृति रात्रिषु
योगक्षेमो हि सीताया वर्तते लक्ष्मणावयोः
verses.transliteration:
jāgartavyamatandribhyāmadya prabhṛti rātriṣu
yogakṣemo hi sītāyā vartate lakṣmaṇāvayoḥ

translations.english: From to night forth, we shall have to guard her vigilantly, for, O Laksmana, the preservation of what she has as well as the securing to her of what she has not, rests with us.

verses.sanskrit:
रात्रिं कथंचिदेवेमां सौमित्रे वर्तयामहे
उपावर्तामहे भूमावास्तीर्य स्वयमार्जितैः
verses.transliteration:
rātriṁ kathaṁcidevemāṁ saumitre vartayāmahe
upāvartāmahe bhūmāvāstīrya svayamārjitaiḥ

translations.english: We will, O son of Sumitrā, anyhow pass the night; let us ourselves procuring (leaves) and spreading them on the ground, anyhow lie down on it.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु संविश्य मेदिन्यां महार्हशयनोचितः
इमाः सौमित्रये रामो व्याजहार कथाः शुभाः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu saṁviśya medinyāṁ mahārhaśayanocitaḥ
imāḥ saumitraye rāmo vyājahāra kathāḥ śubhāḥ

translations.english: Saying this, Rāma lying down on the ground although worthy of a costly bed, spoke these excellent words to Sumitrā's son.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रुवमद्य महाराजो दुःखं स्वपिति लक्ष्मण
कृतकामा तु कैकेयी तुष्टा भवितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
dhruvamadya mahārājo duḥkhaṁ svapiti lakṣmaṇa
kṛtakāmā tu kaikeyī tuṣṭā bhavitumarhati

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, surely the king sleeps uneasily to day, and Kaikeyi having attained her end ought to be satisfied.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हि देवी महाराजं कैकेयी राज्यकारणात्
अपि न च्यावयेत्प्राणान्दृष्ट्वा भरतमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
sā hi devī mahārājaṁ kaikeyī rājyakāraṇāt
api na cyāvayetprāṇāndṛṣṭvā bharatamāgatam

translations.english: Will not that revered lady, for the purpose of having Bharata established in the kingdom, take the king's life, when she shall see Bharata arrived?

verses.sanskrit:
अनाथश्चैव वृद्धश्च मया चैव विनाकृतः
किं करिष्यति कामात्मा कैकेय्या वशमागतः
verses.transliteration:
anāthaścaiva vṛddhaśca mayā caiva vinākṛtaḥ
kiṁ kariṣyati kāmātmā kaikeyyā vaśamāgataḥ

translations.english: Forlorn and old and deprived of me. I do not know what he will do, his soul possessed by desire, and having come under the influence of Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं व्यसनमालोक्य राज्ञश्च मतिविभ्रमम्
काम एवार्धधर्माभ्यां गरीयानिति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ vyasanamālokya rājñaśca mativibhramam
kāma evārdhadharmābhyāṁ garīyāniti me matiḥ

translations.english: Viewing this calamity that has overtaken us) and the disorder that has taken place in the senses of the monarch, I deem even lust as more potent than either virtue or interest.

verses.sanskrit:
को ह्यविद्वानपि पुमान्प्रमदायाः कृते त्यजेत्
छन्दानुवर्तिनं पुत्रं तातो मामिव लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
ko hyavidvānapi pumānpramadāyāḥ kṛte tyajet
chandānuvartinaṁ putraṁ tāto māmiva lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: O Lakşmana, what man is there ignorant though he be, who for the sake of a female forsake as my father has done me, his son following his foot-steps?

verses.sanskrit:
सुखी बत सभार्यश्च भरतः केकयीसुतः
मुदितान्कोसलानेको यो भोक्ष्यत्यधिराजवत्
verses.transliteration:
sukhī bata sabhāryaśca bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ
muditānkosalāneko yo bhokṣyatyadhirājavat

translations.english: Ah! Kaikeyi's son Bharata with his wife is really happy, he that enjoys the sole sovereignty of the delighted Kosalas.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि सर्वस्य राज्यस्य मुखमेकं भविष्यति
ताते च वयसातीते मयि चारण्यमाश्रिते
verses.transliteration:
sa hi sarvasya rājyasya mukhamekaṁ bhaviṣyati
tāte ca vayasātīte mayi cāraṇyamāśrite

translations.english: Now that our father has grown old and I have taken refuge in the forest, he will alone experience the supreme felicity in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थधर्मौ परित्यज्य यः काममनुवर्तते
एवमापद्यते क्षिप्रं राजा दशरथो यथा
verses.transliteration:
arthadharmau parityajya yaḥ kāmamanuvartate
evamāpadyate kṣipraṁ rājā daśaratho yathā

translations.english: He that renouncing interest and virtue, follows lust, speedily gets himself involved in troubles even like king Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये दशरथान्ताय मम प्रव्राजनाय च
कैकेयी सौम्य संप्राप्ता राज्याय भरतस्य च
verses.transliteration:
manye daśarathāntāya mama pravrājanāya ca
kaikeyī saumya saṁprāptā rājyāya bharatasya ca

translations.english: O amiable one, I think that Kaikeyi has been born for making an end of Dasaratha, sending me into exile, and conferring the kingdom on Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
अपीदानीं न कैकेयी सौभाग्यमदमोहिता
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च संप्रबाधेत मत्कृते
verses.transliteration:
apīdānīṁ na kaikeyī saubhāgyamadamohitā
kausalyāṁ ca sumitrāṁ ca saṁprabādheta matkṛte

translations.english: At present for impareing me pain, Kaikeyi intoxicated by the tide of good fortune, will afflict Kausalya and Sumitrā.

verses.sanskrit:
मा स्म मत्कारणाद्देवी सुमित्रा दुःखमावसेत्
अयोध्यामित एव त्वं काले प्रविश लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
mā sma matkāraṇāddevī sumitrā duḥkhamāvaset
ayodhyāmita eva tvaṁ kāle praviśa lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: Your mother, the reversed Sumitrā, will be smitten with grief on our account. Do you, Laks maņa, tomorrow morning repair to Ayodhyā:

verses.sanskrit:
अहमेको गमिष्यामि सीतया सह दण्डकान्
अनाथाया हि नाथस्त्वं कौसल्याया भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
ahameko gamiṣyāmi sītayā saha daṇḍakān
anāthāyā hi nāthastvaṁ kausalyāyā bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: I alone will go to Dandaka along with Sītā. You will be the protector of the helpless Kausalya.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुद्रकर्मा हि कैकेयी द्वेषादन्याय्यमाचरेत्
परिदद्या हि धर्मज्ञे भरते मम मातरम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣudrakarmā hi kaikeyī dveṣādanyāyyamācaret
paridadyā hi dharmajñe bharate mama mātaram

translations.english: Kaikeyi is surely mean-minded, she perpetrates wrongs from malice. O you cognizant of virtue, she may administer poison to my mother.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं जात्यन्तरे कस्मिं स्त्रियः पुत्रैर्वियोजिताः
जनन्या मम सौमित्रे तदप्येतदुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ jātyantare kasmiṁ striyaḥ putrairviyojitāḥ
jananyā mama saumitre tadapyetadupasthitam

translations.english: Surely, O child, in a former birth, women were bereft of their sons by my mother, O son of Sumitrā; and it is for this that this misfortune has befallen her.

verses.sanskrit:
मया हि चिरपुष्टेन दुःखसंवर्धितेन च
विप्रायुज्यत कौसल्या फलकाले धिगस्तु माम्
verses.transliteration:
mayā hi cirapuṣṭena duḥkhasaṁvardhitena ca
viprāyujyata kausalyā phalakāle dhigastu mām

translations.english: Having been brought up and reared with great pains by Kausalyä, I have left her at the time when her labours ought to have borne fruit, Fie on me.

verses.sanskrit:
मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज्जनयेत्पुत्रमीदृशम्
सौमित्रे योऽहमम्बाया दद्मि शोकमनन्तकम्
verses.transliteration:
mā sma sīmantinī kācijjanayetputramīdṛśam
saumitre yo'hamambāyā dadmi śokamanantakam

translations.english: Let on woman, O son of Sumitrā, gibe birth to a son like me who have imparted such infinite pain to my mother.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये प्रीतिविशिष्टा सा मत्तो लक्ष्मणसारिका
यस्यास्तच्छ्रूयते वाक्यं शुक पादमरेर्दश
verses.transliteration:
manye prītiviśiṣṭā sā matto lakṣmaṇasārikā
yasyāstacchrūyate vākyaṁ śuka pādamarerdaśa

translations.english: O Laksmana, I consider my mother's female parrot as more sharing her affection, since she is heard to say, 'O Śuka, do you bite the foot of the foe?

verses.sanskrit:
शोचन्त्याश्चाल्पभाग्याया न किंचिदुपकुर्वता
पुर्त्रेण किमपुत्राया मया कार्यमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
śocantyāścālpabhāgyāyā na kiṁcidupakurvatā
purtreṇa kimaputrāyā mayā kāryamariṁdama

translations.english: What am I, O repressor of foes, now to do for her, bewailing, of slender fortune, she that has not profited in the least by her son, and who stands in no further need of his good offices? Surely my unfortunate mother, Kausalyā, bereft of me, lies down on the ground, overwhelmed with woe, and plunged in an ocean of grief..

verses.sanskrit:
एको ह्यहमयोध्यां च पृथिवीं चापि लक्ष्मण
तरेयमिषुभिः क्रुद्धो ननु वीर्यमकारणम्
verses.transliteration:
eko hyahamayodhyāṁ ca pṛthivīṁ cāpi lakṣmaṇa
tareyamiṣubhiḥ kruddho nanu vīryamakāraṇam

translations.english: O Laksmana, enraged, I alone without doubt, can rid Ayodhyā, the Earth herself, by means of my arrows. But improper is the display of prowess for no reason,

verses.sanskrit:
अधर्मभय भीतश्च परलोकस्य चानघ
तेन लक्ष्मण नाद्याहमात्मानमभिषेचये
verses.transliteration:
adharmabhaya bhītaśca paralokasya cānagha
tena lakṣmaṇa nādyāhamātmānamabhiṣecaye

translations.english: O sinless one, I am afraid of unrighteousness and of the next life; and for this it is that, O Lakşmaņa, I do not install myself in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदन्यच्च करुणं विलप्य विजने बहु
अश्रुपूर्णमुखो रामो निशि तूष्णीमुपाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
etadanyacca karuṇaṁ vilapya vijane bahu
aśrupūrṇamukho rāmo niśi tūṣṇīmupāviśat

translations.english: Having in solitude for a long while piteously bewailed thus and in other ways, Rāma sat silent in the night with tears in his eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
विलप्योपरतं रामं गतार्चिषमिवानलम्
समुद्रमिव निर्वेगमाश्वासयत लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
vilapyoparataṁ rāmaṁ gatārciṣamivānalam
samudramiva nirvegamāśvāsayata lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa consoled Rāma spent with lamentation, like to fire deprived of its radiance or the ocean of its tide.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रुवमद्य पुरी राम अयोध्या युधिनां वर
निष्प्रभा त्वयि निष्क्रान्ते गतचन्द्रेव शर्वरी
verses.transliteration:
dhruvamadya purī rāma ayodhyā yudhināṁ vara
niṣprabhā tvayi niṣkrānte gatacandreva śarvarī

translations.english: Surely, O Rama, O foremost of warriors, on your having come out, the city of Ayodhyā is shorn of its splendour like the night deprived of the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतदौपयिकं राम यदिदं परितप्यसे
विषादयसि सीतां च मां चैव पुरुषर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
naitadaupayikaṁ rāma yadidaṁ paritapyase
viṣādayasi sītāṁ ca māṁ caiva puruṣarṣabha

translations.english: This is not fit that you should grieve; for thereby, O foremost of men, you make both Sītā and myself grieve.

verses.sanskrit:
न च सीता त्वया हीना न चाहमपि राघव
मुहूर्तमपि जीवावो जलान्मत्स्याविवोद्धृतौ
verses.transliteration:
na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na cāhamapi rāghava
muhūrtamapi jīvāvo jalānmatsyāvivoddhṛtau

translations.english: O Rāghava, deprived of you neither Sītā nor I can live for a moment, like fish taken out of water: without you.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तातं न शत्रुघ्नं न सुमित्रां परंतप
द्रष्टुमिच्छेयमद्याहं स्वर्गं वापि त्वया विना
verses.transliteration:
na hi tātaṁ na śatrughnaṁ na sumitrāṁ paraṁtapa
draṣṭumiccheyamadyāhaṁ svargaṁ vāpi tvayā vinā

translations.english: O repressor of foes, I wish to see neither my father, nor Satrughna, nor Sumitrā, nor heaven itself.

verses.sanskrit:
स लक्ष्मणस्योत्तम पुष्कलं वचो; निशम्य चैवं वनवासमादरात्
समाः समस्ता विदधे परंतपः; प्रपद्य धर्मं सुचिराय राघवः
verses.transliteration:
sa lakṣmaṇasyottama puṣkalaṁ vaco; niśamya caivaṁ vanavāsamādarāt
samāḥ samastā vidadhe paraṁtapaḥ; prapadya dharmaṁ sucirāya rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Lakşmaņa's excellent and appropriate words with which he gladly assumed a life in the woods, that subduer of foes, Rāghava, in the name of righteousness, at once fully granted him the permission to dwell with him for the entire fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु तस्मिन्महावृक्ष उषित्वा रजनीं शिवाम्
विमलेऽभ्युदिते सूर्ये तस्माद्देशात्प्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
te tu tasminmahāvṛkṣa uṣitvā rajanīṁ śivām
vimale'bhyudite sūrye tasmāddeśātpratasthire

translations.english: Having passed the auspicious night underneath that might tree, they, when the sun had risen in unclouded splendour, went away from that place.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र भागीरथी गङ्गा यमुनामभिवर्तते
जग्मुस्तं देशमुद्दिश्य विगाह्य सुमहद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
yatra bhāgīrathī gaṅgā yamunāmabhivartate
jagmustaṁ deśamuddiśya vigāhya sumahadvanam

translations.english: Then dividing into a mighty forest, they proceeded in the direction in which the Bhāgirathi Gangå meets with the Yamunā.

verses.sanskrit:
ते भूमिमागान्विविधान्देशांश्चापि मनोरमान्
अदृष्टपूर्वान्पश्यन्तस्तत्र तत्र यशस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
te bhūmimāgānvividhāndeśāṁścāpi manoramān
adṛṣṭapūrvānpaśyantastatra tatra yaśasvinaḥ

translations.english: Those illustrious ones went on, viewing at intervals various fields and delightful lands which they had never seen before.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाक्षेमेण गच्छन्स पश्यंश्च विविधान्द्रुमान्
निवृत्तमात्रे दिवसे रामः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
yathākṣemeṇa gacchansa paśyaṁśca vividhāndrumān
nivṛttamātre divase rāmaḥ saumitrimabravīt

translations.english: And going on beholding various kinds of blossoming trees, Rāma when the day had declined, spoke to Sumitrā's son saying.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयागमभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूममुन्नतम्
अग्नेर्भगवतः केतुं मन्ये संनिहितो मुनिः
verses.transliteration:
prayāgamabhitaḥ paśya saumitre dhūmamunnatam
agnerbhagavataḥ ketuṁ manye saṁnihito muniḥ

translations.english: O son of Sumitrā, do you behold the beautiful wreath of smoke that rises in front of Prayāga, sign of the worshipful Fire, and I infer some ascetic to be near.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं प्राप्ताः स्म संभेदं गङ्गायमुनयोर्वयम्
तथा हि श्रूयते शम्ब्दो वारिणा वारिघट्टितः
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ prāptāḥ sma saṁbhedaṁ gaṅgāyamunayorvayam
tathā hi śrūyate śambdo vāriṇā vārighaṭṭitaḥ

translations.english: For certain we have arrived at the confluence of the Gangā and the Yamunā; and it is for this that we hear the roar of the waters produced by the rushing of them.

verses.sanskrit:
दारूणि परिभिन्नानि वनजैरुपजीविभिः
भरद्वाजाश्रमे चैते दृश्यन्ते विविधा द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
dārūṇi paribhinnāni vanajairupajīvibhiḥ
bharadvājāśrame caite dṛśyante vividhā drumāḥ

translations.english: All these various trees with their wood hewn away by foresters are seen in the asylums.

verses.sanskrit:
धन्विनौ तौ सुखं गत्वा लम्बमाने दिवाकरे
गङ्गायमुनयोः संधौ प्रापतुर्निलयं मुनेः
verses.transliteration:
dhanvinau tau sukhaṁ gatvā lambamāne divākare
gaṅgāyamunayoḥ saṁdhau prāpaturnilayaṁ muneḥ

translations.english: Thus having proceeded at ease, you bowmen when the sun stood aslant, arrived in the vicinity of the ascetic's residence on the delta of the Yamunā and the Gangā.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्त्वाश्रममासाद्य त्रासयन्मृगपक्षिणः
गत्वा मुहूर्तमध्वानं भरद्वाजमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmastvāśramamāsādya trāsayanmṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
gatvā muhūrtamadhvānaṁ bharadvājamupāgamat

translations.english: Proceeding awhile on the way, Rāma, in presence of the asylum, came up to Bharadvāja's place, frightening beasts and birds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वाश्रममासाद्य मुनेर्दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणौ
सीतयानुगतौ वीरौ दूरादेवावतस्थतुः
verses.transliteration:
tatastvāśramamāsādya munerdarśanakāṅkṣiṇau
sītayānugatau vīrau dūrādevāvatasthatuḥ

translations.english: Arriving at the hermitage, the heroes desirous of seeing the ascetic, stood at a distance with Sītā behind them.

verses.sanskrit:
हुताग्निहोत्रं दृष्ट्वैव महाभागं कृताञ्जलिः
रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सीतया चाभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
hutāgnihotraṁ dṛṣṭvaiva mahābhāgaṁ kṛtāñjaliḥ
rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṁ sītayā cābhyavādayat

translations.english: And as soon as entering in, that exalted one saw that high-souled anchoret of accomplished vows, who had attained spiritual insight through austerities, sitting surrounded by his disciples after having finished the Agnihotra, Rāma with joined hands saluted him along with Sumitra's son and Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
पित्रा नियुक्ता भगवन्प्रवेष्यामस्तपोवनम्
धर्ममेवाचरिष्यामस्तत्र मूलफलाशनाः
verses.transliteration:
pitrā niyuktā bhagavanpraveṣyāmastapovanam
dharmamevācariṣyāmastatra mūlaphalāśanāḥ

translations.english: O revered one, commissioned by my father, I will enter the forest of asceticism, and there subsisting on fruits and roots will practise virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः
उपानयत धर्मात्मा गामर्घ्यमुदकं ततः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ
upānayata dharmātmā gāmarghyamudakaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of the intelligent prince, that righteous (ascetic) brought a bull* as well as Arghya and water and divers kinds of edibles consisting of wild fruits and roots. *When an eminent guest came to a person's house, as he offered madhuparka, with a bull which was killed for his entertainment

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य च तामर्चामुपविष्टं सराघवम्
भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं धर्मयुक्तमिदं तदा
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya ca tāmarcāmupaviṣṭaṁ sarāghavam
bharadvājo'bravīdvākyaṁ dharmayuktamidaṁ tadā

translations.english: Then paying homage to Rāma he proceeded by short stages, and asking him, Has your journey been a pleasant one?, the ascetic sat down. And when Rāghava had sat down after receiving the homage, Bharadvāja spoke to him these words fraught with virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
चिरस्य खलु काकुत्स्थ पश्यामि त्वामिहागतम्
श्रुतं तव मया चेदं विवासनमकारणम्
verses.transliteration:
cirasya khalu kākutstha paśyāmi tvāmihāgatam
śrutaṁ tava mayā cedaṁ vivāsanamakāraṇam

translations.english: O Kākutstha, I behold you come after a long time. I have heard of your causeless exile.

verses.sanskrit:
अवकाशो विविक्तोऽयं महानद्योः समागमे
पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च वसत्विह भगान्सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
avakāśo vivikto'yaṁ mahānadyoḥ samāgame
puṇyaśca ramaṇīyaśca vasatviha bhagānsukham

translations.english: This spot at the meeting of the mighty rivers is lonely, sacred and charming. Do you dwell here happily.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु वचनं भरद्वाजेन राघवः
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं रामः सर्वहिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu vacanaṁ bharadvājena rāghavaḥ
pratyuvāca śubhaṁ vākyaṁ rāmaḥ sarvahite rataḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by Bharadvāja, that descendant of Raghu, Rāma intent on the welfare of all, answered in auspicious words.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्नित आसन्नः पौरजानपदो जनः
आगमिष्यति वैदेहीं मां चापि प्रेक्षको जनः
अनेन कारणेनाहमिह वासं न रोचये
verses.transliteration:
bhagavannita āsannaḥ paurajānapado janaḥ
āgamiṣyati vaidehīṁ māṁ cāpi prekṣako janaḥ
anena kāraṇenāhamiha vāsaṁ na rocaye

translations.english: O reverend one, I apprehend that, living hard by, the inhabitants of the city and the provinces, thinking me as easily to be seen, will come to this asylum desirous of beholding me and Vaidehī. It is for this reason that living at this place does not recommended itself to me.

verses.sanskrit:
एकान्ते पश्य भगवन्नाश्रमस्थानमुत्तमम्
रमते यत्र वैदेही सुखार्हा जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
ekānte paśya bhagavannāśramasthānamuttamam
ramate yatra vaidehī sukhārhā janakātmajā

translations.english: Do you, O worshipful one, hit upon a retired and agreeable asylum where Janaka's daughter worthy of happiness, will pass her days pleasantly.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः
राघवस्य ततो वाक्यमर्थ ग्राहकमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā śubhaṁ vākyaṁ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ
rāghavasya tato vākyamartha grāhakamabravīt
