translations.english: Hearing this auspicious speech of Rāghava, that eminent anchoret Bharadvāja said these words calculated to serve Rāma's purpose.

verses.sanskrit:
गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितो वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः
चित्रकूट इति ख्यातो गन्धमादनसंनिभः
verses.transliteration:
golāṅgūlānucarito vānararkṣaniṣevitaḥ
citrakūṭa iti khyāto gandhamādanasaṁnibhaḥ

translations.english: Ten Krosas hence, my child, is the mountain where you shall dwell. it is inhabited by maharsis, and is sacred, and picturesque throughout, abounding in Golāngulas, monkeys, and bears, known by the name of Citrakuta, resembling Gandhamädana.

verses.sanskrit:
यावता चित्र कूटस्य नरः शृङ्गाण्यवेक्षते
कल्याणानि समाधत्ते न पापे कुरुते मनः
verses.transliteration:
yāvatā citra kūṭasya naraḥ śṛṅgāṇyavekṣate
kalyāṇāni samādhatte na pāpe kurute manaḥ

translations.english: On beholding the peaks of Citrakuța, one reaps welfare, and ignorance does not envelope one's mind.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषयस्तत्र बहवो विहृत्य शरदां शतम्
तपसा दिवमारूढाः कपालशिरसा सह
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣayastatra bahavo vihṛtya śaradāṁ śatam
tapasā divamārūḍhāḥ kapālaśirasā saha

translations.english: There innumerable saints with the hair of their heads rendered white like skulls, having spent hundreds of years, have through austerities ascended heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविविक्तमहं मन्ये तं वासं भवतः सुखम्
इह वा वनवासाय वस राम मया सह
verses.transliteration:
praviviktamahaṁ manye taṁ vāsaṁ bhavataḥ sukham
iha vā vanavāsāya vasa rāma mayā saha

translations.english: That solitary spot I deem as one which will make a happy residence for you. O Rāma, do you, for living out the term of your banishment, dwell either here or with me.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामं सर्वकामैस्तं भरद्वाजः प्रियातिथिम्
सभार्यं सह च भ्रात्रा प्रतिजग्राह धर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmaṁ sarvakāmaistaṁ bharadvājaḥ priyātithim
sabhāryaṁ saha ca bhrātrā pratijagrāha dharmavit

translations.english: Bharadvāja entertained his welcome guest, Rāma, along with his wife and brother by extending towards them every rite of hospitality.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य प्रयागे रामस्य तं महर्षिमुपेयुषः
प्रपन्ना रजनी पुण्या चित्राः कथयतः कथाः
verses.transliteration:
tasya prayāge rāmasya taṁ maharṣimupeyuṣaḥ
prapannā rajanī puṇyā citrāḥ kathayataḥ kathāḥ

translations.english: At Prayāga Rāma having obtained the company of that Maharși, and discoursing on a variety of sacred topics, the night came on.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभातायां रजन्यां तु भरद्वाजमुपागमत्
उवाच नरशार्दूलो मुनिं ज्वलिततेजसम्
verses.transliteration:
prabhātāyāṁ rajanyāṁ tu bharadvājamupāgamat
uvāca naraśārdūlo muniṁ jvalitatejasam

translations.english: When the night had passed away and day dawned, (Rāma) approached Bharadvāja, and that chief of men addressed that ascetic of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
शर्वरीं भवनन्नद्य सत्यशील तवाश्रमे
उषिताः स्मेह वसतिमनुजानातु नो भवान्
verses.transliteration:
śarvarīṁ bhavanannadya satyaśīla tavāśrame
uṣitāḥ smeha vasatimanujānātu no bhavān

translations.english: O reverend sire of truthful character, we have here in your asylum spent the night. Do you now permit us to set forward (for Citrakuta).

verses.sanskrit:
रात्र्यां तु तस्यां व्युष्टायां भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीदिदम्
मधुमूलफलोपेतं चित्रकूटं व्रजेति ह
verses.transliteration:
rātryāṁ tu tasyāṁ vyuṣṭāyāṁ bharadvājo'bravīdidam
madhumūlaphalopetaṁ citrakūṭaṁ vrajeti ha

translations.english: On Rāma having passed the night there, Bharadvāja spoke to him, “Do you race your steps to Citrakuța filled with delicious fruits and roots. I deem that, О mighty Rāma, as a fit abode for you, being, as it is, furnished with various kinds of trees, inhabited by crowds of Kinnars, resounding with the cries of peacocks, and frequented by gigantic elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र कुञ्जरयूथानि मृगयूथानि चाभितः
विचरन्ति वनान्तेषु तानि द्रक्ष्यसि राघव
verses.transliteration:
tatra kuñjarayūthāni mṛgayūthāni cābhitaḥ
vicaranti vanānteṣu tāni drakṣyasi rāghava

translations.english: Do you repair to the famed Citrakuţa, holy, fair to the view, and abounding in countless fruits and roots. And in those forests range herds of elephants and deer; and these, O Rāghava, you will behold. And ranging with Sītā rivers and rills and plateau's, caverns and fountains, your mind will experience delight.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टकोयष्टिककोकिलस्वनै;र्विनादितं तं वसुधाधरं शिवम्
मृगैश्च मत्तैर्बहुभिश्च कुञ्जरैः; सुरम्यमासाद्य समावसाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭakoyaṣṭikakokilasvanai;rvināditaṁ taṁ vasudhādharaṁ śivam
mṛgaiśca mattairbahubhiśca kuñjaraiḥ; suramyamāsādya samāvasāśramam

translations.english: Delighted with the notes of joyous Koyastivas and coels, and the cries of deer and coundess mad elephants, do you, arriving at the auspicious mountain, reside at the romantic asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
उषित्वा रजनीं तत्र राजपुत्रावरिंदमौ
महर्षिमभिवाद्याथ जग्मतुस्तं गिरिं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
uṣitvā rajanīṁ tatra rājaputrāvariṁdamau
maharṣimabhivādyātha jagmatustaṁ giriṁ prati

translations.english: Having spent the night there, those princes, repressors of their foes, after paying their obeisance to the Maharși, set out for the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रस्थितांश्चैव तान्प्रेक्ष्य पिता पुत्रानिवान्वगात्
ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुं वचनं स महामुनिः
verses.transliteration:
prasthitāṁścaiva tānprekṣya pitā putrānivānvagāt
tataḥ pracakrame vaktuṁ vacanaṁ sa mahāmuniḥ

translations.english: Seeing them about to set forth, that Maharși performed a propitiatory ceremony for them, even as a father does on behalf of the sons begot from his own loins.

verses.sanskrit:
अथासाद्य तु कालिन्दीं शीघ्रस्रोतसमापगाम्
तत्र यूयं प्लवं कृत्वा तरतांशुमतीं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
athāsādya tu kālindīṁ śīghrasrotasamāpagām
tatra yūyaṁ plavaṁ kṛtvā taratāṁśumatīṁ nadīm

translations.english: Arriving at the Kalindi running in a contrary direction, you will, O Rāghava, behold a goodly bathing place well-worn by foot-passengers. There constructing a raft, do you cross over the river who is the daughter of the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
स पन्थाश्चित्रकूटस्य गतः सुबहुशो मया
रम्यो मार्दवयुक्तश्च वनदावैर्विवर्जितः
इति पन्थानमावेद्य महर्षिः स न्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
sa panthāścitrakūṭasya gataḥ subahuśo mayā
ramyo mārdavayuktaśca vanadāvairvivarjitaḥ
iti panthānamāvedya maharṣiḥ sa nyavartata

translations.english: I went to Citrakuța many a time by that road, which is beautiful, sandy, and free from forestfire.

verses.sanskrit:
उपावृत्ते मुनौ तस्मिन्रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
कृतपुण्याः स्म सौमित्रे मुनिर्यन्नोऽनुकम्पते
verses.transliteration:
upāvṛtte munau tasminrāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
kṛtapuṇyāḥ sma saumitre muniryanno'nukampate

translations.english: On the ascetic turning away, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, “We had surely acquired religious merit, good betide you, since, the ascetic has shown compassion to us.

verses.sanskrit:
इति तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्रयित्वा मनस्विनौ
सीतामेवाग्रतः कृत्वा कालिन्दीं जग्मतुर्नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
iti tau puruṣavyāghrau mantrayitvā manasvinau
sītāmevāgrataḥ kṛtvā kālindīṁ jagmaturnadīm

translations.english: Having thus conversed with each other, those foremost of men endowed with intelligence, place Sītā in their front, proceeded towards the rive Kalindi.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ काष्ठसंघाटमथो चक्रतुः सुमहाप्लवम्
चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्त्वा सीतायाः सुखमानसम्
verses.transliteration:
tau kāṣṭhasaṁghāṭamatho cakratuḥ sumahāplavam
cakāra lakṣmaṇaśchittvā sītāyāḥ sukhamānasam

translations.english: Then with heaps of dry wild wood covered with grass, they constructed a large raft. And the puissant Lakşmaņa tearing twigs from the ratan and the rose-apple, made a comfortable seat for Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र श्रियमिवाचिन्त्यां रामो दाशरथिः प्रियाम्
ईषत्संलज्जमानां तामध्यारोपयत प्लवम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra śriyamivācintyāṁ rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyām
īṣatsaṁlajjamānāṁ tāmadhyāropayata plavam

translations.english: Then Dasaratha's son, Rāma, made his bashful wife (in power) inconceivable like to Śrī herself, ascend the raft, and carefully laid beside Vaidehī her attires and ornaments as well as the hoe and the basket.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्लवेनांशुमतीं शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम्
तीरजैर्बहुभिर्वृक्षैः संतेरुर्यमुनां नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ plavenāṁśumatīṁ śīghragāmūrmimālinīm
tīrajairbahubhirvṛkṣaiḥ saṁteruryamunāṁ nadīm

translations.english: And by means of that raft they crossed that fleet-coursing daughter of the Sun, heaving with billows, the river Yamunā with her banks abounding with innumerable trees.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तीर्णाः प्लवमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थाय यमुनावनात्
श्यामं न्यग्रोधमासेदुः शीतलं हरितच्छदम्
verses.transliteration:
te tīrṇāḥ plavamutsṛjya prasthāya yamunāvanāt
śyāmaṁ nyagrodhamāseduḥ śītalaṁ haritacchadam

translations.english: Then renouncing the raft, and passing by the woods adjoining the Yamunā, they came upon a banian Syāma by name, of cool shade and verdant foliage.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यां चैव पश्येयं सुमित्रां च यशस्विनीम्
इति सीताञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगछद्वनस्पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāṁ caiva paśyeyaṁ sumitrāṁ ca yaśasvinīm
iti sītāñjaliṁ kṛtvā paryagachadvanaspatim

translations.english: On coming to the banian, Vaidehī saluted it saying, “O mighty tree, I bow to you. May my husband fulfil his vow; and may we behold Kausalyā and the illustrious Sumitrā.” Having thus prayed with joined hands, the intelligent Sītā went away.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
बहून्मेध्यान्मृगान्हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने
verses.transliteration:
krośamātraṁ tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
bahūnmedhyānmṛgānhatvā ceraturyamunāvane

translations.english: And having proceeded just a Krosa, those brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, having killed many a sacred deer, began to range in the woods of the Yarnunā.

verses.sanskrit:
विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते; शुभे वने वारणवानरायुते
समं नदीवप्रमुपेत्य संमतं; निवासमाजग्मुरदीनदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite; śubhe vane vāraṇavānarāyute
samaṁ nadīvapramupetya saṁmataṁ; nivāsamājagmuradīnadarśanaḥ

translations.english: And having disported in the beautiful woods resounding with multitudes of peacocks and inhabited by elephants and monkeys, they looking as lively as ever, coming to the level banks of the river, took up their quarters there.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामवसुप्तमनन्तरम्
प्रबोधयामास शनैर्लक्ष्मणं रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
atha rātryāṁ vyatītāyāmavasuptamanantaram
prabodhayāmāsa śanairlakṣmaṇaṁ raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: When the night had been spent, that best of Raghus gently awakened Lakşmaņa from his light sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रे शृणु वन्यानां वल्गु व्याहरतां स्वनम्
संप्रतिष्ठामहे कालः प्रस्थानस्य परंतप
verses.transliteration:
saumitre śṛṇu vanyānāṁ valgu vyāharatāṁ svanam
saṁpratiṣṭhāmahe kālaḥ prasthānasya paraṁtapa

translations.english: O Sumiträ's son, do you hear the dulcet notes of the birds in the woods. Let us proceed. O repressor of foes, the time of our departure is present.

verses.sanskrit:
स सुप्तः समये भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणः प्रतिबोधितः
जहौ निद्रां च तन्द्रीं च प्रसक्तं च पथि श्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa suptaḥ samaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ
jahau nidrāṁ ca tandrīṁ ca prasaktaṁ ca pathi śramam

translations.english: Awakened at the proper time, Rāma's brother left off sleep and drowsiness and clinging fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
तत उत्थाय ते सर्वे स्पृष्ट्वा नद्याः शिवं जलम्
पन्थानमृषिणोद्दिष्टं चित्रकूटस्य तं ययुः
verses.transliteration:
tata utthāya te sarve spṛṣṭvā nadyāḥ śivaṁ jalam
panthānamṛṣiṇoddiṣṭaṁ citrakūṭasya taṁ yayuḥ

translations.english: Then they all arising touched the sacred waters of the river, and began to proceed on the way to Citrakuța inhabited by ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संप्रस्थितः काले रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁprasthitaḥ kāle rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
sītāṁ kamalapatrākṣīmidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Setting out in season with Sumitra's son, he of eyes resembling lotus-petais spoke these words to Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
आदीप्तानिव वैदेहि सर्वतः पुष्पितान्नगान्
स्वैः पुष्पैः किंशुकान्पश्य मालिनः शिशिरात्यये
verses.transliteration:
ādīptāniva vaidehi sarvataḥ puṣpitānnagān
svaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kiṁśukānpaśya mālinaḥ śiśirātyaye

translations.english: O Vaidehi, behold these flowering trees, the Kinsukas in spring appearing engarlanded with their own flowers, and as if flaming., Do you behold the Bhallatakas and Bilvas bending beneath their fruits and flowers, with no man to enjoy them. Surely, we: shall be able to live here.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य द्रोणप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि लक्ष्मण
मधूनि मधुकारीभिः संभृतानि नगे नगे
verses.transliteration:
paśya droṇapramāṇāni lambamānāni lakṣmaṇa
madhūni madhukārībhiḥ saṁbhṛtāni nage nage

translations.english: Behold, O Laksmana, these honeycombs measuring about a Droņa have been hung up on trees by the bees.

verses.sanskrit:
एष क्रोशति नत्यूहस्तं शिखी प्रतिकूजति
रमणीये वनोद्देशे पुष्पसंस्तरसंकटे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa krośati natyūhastaṁ śikhī pratikūjati
ramaṇīye vanoddeśe puṣpasaṁstarasaṁkaṭe

translations.english: In the charming woods overarched by flowers, the Datyuha cries, and is responded to by the peacock.

verses.sanskrit:
मातंगयूथानुसृतं पक्षिसंघानुनादितम्
चित्रकूटमिमं पश्य प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्
verses.transliteration:
mātaṁgayūthānusṛtaṁ pakṣisaṁghānunāditam
citrakūṭamimaṁ paśya pravṛddhaśikharaṁ girim

translations.english: Do you behold Citrakuta frequented by mad elephants and resonant with the voice of multitudes of birds, the mountain with its towering summits.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तौ पादचारेण गच्छन्तौ सह सीतया
रम्यमासेदतुः शैलं चित्रकूटं मनोरमम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastau pādacāreṇa gacchantau saha sītayā
ramyamāsedatuḥ śailaṁ citrakūṭaṁ manoramam

translations.english: Then they proceeding on foot along with Sītā, arrived at the charming and beautiful mountain Citrakuta.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु पर्वतमासाद्य नानापक्षिगणायुतम्
अयं वासो भवेत्तावदत्र सौम्य रमेमहि
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu parvatamāsādya nānāpakṣigaṇāyutam
ayaṁ vāso bhavettāvadatra saumya ramemahi

translations.english: Arriving at the mountain inhabited by birds of various kinds, abounding in fruits and roots, and furnished with watery expanses, (Răma) said.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणानय दारूणि दृढानि च वराणि च
कुरुष्वावसथं सौम्य वासे मेऽभिरतं मनः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇānaya dārūṇi dṛḍhāni ca varāṇi ca
kuruṣvāvasathaṁ saumya vāse me'bhirataṁ manaḥ

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, bring you wood good and strong. O amiable one, construct a dwelling. My mind is set upon staying here.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिर्विविधान्द्रुमान्
आजहार ततश्चक्रे पर्ण शालामरिं दम
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā saumitrirvividhāndrumān
ājahāra tataścakre parṇa śālāmariṁ dama

translations.english: Hearing his words, Sumitra's son procured woods of various descriptions, and then that subduer of foes reared a cottage thatched with leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्रूषमाणमेकाग्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
ऐणेयं मांसमाहृत्य शालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
śuśrūṣamāṇamekāgramidaṁ vacanamabravīt
aiṇeyaṁ māṁsamāhṛtya śālāṁ yakṣyāmahe vayam

translations.english: Procuring meat, we will worship the deity presiding over this dwelling. O Sumitrā's son, those who wish to live long, should pacify the household gods.

verses.sanskrit:
स लक्ष्मणः कृष्णमृगं हत्वा मेध्यं पतापवान्
अथ चिक्षेप सौमित्रिः समिद्धे जातवेदसि
verses.transliteration:
sa lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgaṁ hatvā medhyaṁ patāpavān
atha cikṣepa saumitriḥ samiddhe jātavedasi

translations.english: Then Lakşmana the son of Sumitrā endowed with vigour, having slain a sacred black deer, threw it into flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु पक्वं समाज्ञाय निष्टप्तं छिन्नशोणितम्
लक्ष्मणः पुरुषव्याघ्रमथ राघवमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu pakvaṁ samājñāya niṣṭaptaṁ chinnaśoṇitam
lakṣmaṇaḥ puruṣavyāghramatha rāghavamabravīt

translations.english: And seeing it well scorched and hot and free from blood, Lakşmaņa spoke to that foremost of men, Rāghava, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
तां वृक्षपर्णच्छदनां मनोज्ञां; यथाप्रदेशं सुकृतां निवाताम्
वासाय सर्वे विविशुः समेताः; सभां यथा देव गणाः सुधर्माम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ vṛkṣaparṇacchadanāṁ manojñāṁ; yathāpradeśaṁ sukṛtāṁ nivātām
vāsāya sarve viviśuḥ sametāḥ; sabhāṁ yathā deva gaṇāḥ sudharmām

translations.english: And as the celestials enter the hall entitled Sudharmă, they together with the view of dwelling in it, entered the mansion beautiful to behold, thatched with the leaves of trees, built at a convenient site, well-made, and keeping out the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
सुरम्यमासाद्य तु चित्रकूटं; नदीं च तां माल्यवतीं सुतीर्थाम्
ननन्द हृष्टो मृगपक्षिजुष्टां; जहौ च दुःखं पुरविप्रवासात्
verses.transliteration:
suramyamāsādya tu citrakūṭaṁ; nadīṁ ca tāṁ mālyavatīṁ sutīrthām
nananda hṛṣṭo mṛgapakṣijuṣṭāṁ; jahau ca duḥkhaṁ puravipravāsāt

translations.english: And having come to the charming Citrakuta and the river Mālyavatī furnished with excellent bathing places, and haunted by beasts and fowls, they rejoiced with glad hearts, and forsook the grief incident to their exile from the city.

verses.sanskrit:
कथयित्वा सुदुःखार्तः सुमन्त्रेण चिरं सह
रामे दक्षिण कूलस्थे जगाम स्वगृहं गुहः
verses.transliteration:
kathayitvā suduḥkhārtaḥ sumantreṇa ciraṁ saha
rāme dakṣiṇa kūlasthe jagāma svagṛhaṁ guhaḥ

translations.english: Having for a long time conversed with Sumantra, Guha distressed at heart on Rāma reaching the southern bank, retraced his steps homewards.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुज्ञातः सुमन्त्रोऽथ योजयित्वा हयोत्तमान्
अयोध्यामेव नगरीं प्रययौ गाढदुर्मनाः
verses.transliteration:
anujñātaḥ sumantro'tha yojayitvā hayottamān
ayodhyāmeva nagarīṁ prayayau gāḍhadurmanāḥ

translations.english: Learning from envoys at (Śrngaverapura) all about Rāma's visit to Bharadvāja at Prayāga and his reception (at Bharadvāja's place) as well as their destined journey (to Citrakuta), Sumantra, taking the permission (of Guha), yoked those excellent horses and with a heavy heart directed his course to the city of Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
स वनानि सुगन्धीनि सरितश्च सरांसि च
पश्यन्नतिययौ शीघ्रं ग्रामाणि नगराणि च
verses.transliteration:
sa vanāni sugandhīni saritaśca sarāṁsi ca
paśyannatiyayau śīghraṁ grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca

translations.english: And beholding perfumed woods and rivers and watery expanses and towns and villages, he eagerly proceeded on his way.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सायाह्नसमये तृतीयेऽहनि सारथिः
अयोध्यां समनुप्राप्य निरानन्दां ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sāyāhnasamaye tṛtīye'hani sārathiḥ
ayodhyāṁ samanuprāpya nirānandāṁ dadarśa ha

translations.english: And on the third day at dusk the charioteer arriving at Ayodhyā saw it bereft of happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्न सगजा साश्वा सजना सजनाधिपा
रामसंतापदुःखेन दग्धा शोकाग्निना पुरी
इति चिन्तापरः सूतस्त्वरितः प्रविवेश ह
verses.transliteration:
kaccinna sagajā sāśvā sajanā sajanādhipā
rāmasaṁtāpaduḥkhena dagdhā śokāgninā purī
iti cintāparaḥ sūtastvaritaḥ praviveśa ha

translations.english: And beholding it empty and still, Sumantra afflicted with exceeding sorrow, and overwhelmed with grief, thought, “Perhaps the city with her elephants and horses and men and king has been consumed by the fire of grief on account of Rāma."

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रमभियान्तं तं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
क्व राम इति पृच्छन्तः सूतमभ्यद्रवन्नराः
verses.transliteration:
sumantramabhiyāntaṁ taṁ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ
kva rāma iti pṛcchantaḥ sūtamabhyadravannarāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, people by hundreds and thousands rushed after the charioteer, Sumantra, asking, "Where is Rāma?”

verses.sanskrit:
दानयज्ञविवाहेषु समाजेषु महत्सु च
न द्रक्ष्यामः पुनर्जातु धार्मिकं राममन्तरा
verses.transliteration:
dānayajñavivāheṣu samājeṣu mahatsu ca
na drakṣyāmaḥ punarjātu dhārmikaṁ rāmamantarā

translations.english: We shall no longer see the righteous Rāma in the midst of mighty assemblies engaged in charity, sacrifice or nuptial rites.

verses.sanskrit:
किं समर्थं जनस्यास्य किं प्रियं किं सुखावहम्
इति रामेण नगरं पितृवत्परिपालितम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ samarthaṁ janasyāsya kiṁ priyaṁ kiṁ sukhāvaham
iti rāmeṇa nagaraṁ pitṛvatparipālitam

translations.english: What was necessary for this body? What was dear to them and what did they delight in?, (constantly revolving all this in his mind), Rāma ruled this city even as father.

verses.sanskrit:
वातायनगतानां च स्त्रीणामन्वन्तरापणम्
रामशोकाभितप्तानां शुश्राव परिदेवनम्
verses.transliteration:
vātāyanagatānāṁ ca strīṇāmanvantarāpaṇam
rāmaśokābhitaptānāṁ śuśrāva paridevanam

translations.english: Then proceeding past the stalls, Sumantra heard the lamentations of females at windows, burning in grief for Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजमार्गमध्येन सुमन्त्रः पिहिताननः
यत्र राजा दशरथस्तदेवोपययौ गृहम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājamārgamadhyena sumantraḥ pihitānanaḥ
yatra rājā daśarathastadevopayayau gṛham

translations.english: With his face muffled, Sumantra proceeded on the highway towards the palace of Daśaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽवतीर्य रथाच्छीघ्रं राजवेश्म प्रविश्य च
कक्ष्याः सप्ताभिचक्राम महाजनसमाकुलाः
verses.transliteration:
so'vatīrya rathācchīghraṁ rājaveśma praviśya ca
kakṣyāḥ saptābhicakrāma mahājanasamākulāḥ

translations.english: Swiftly alighting from the car and entering the royal residence, he went past seven apartments thronged with people.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दशरथस्त्रीणां प्रासादेभ्यस्ततस्ततः
रामशोकाभितप्तानां मन्दं शुश्राव जल्पितम्
verses.transliteration:
tato daśarathastrīṇāṁ prāsādebhyastatastataḥ
rāmaśokābhitaptānāṁ mandaṁ śuśrāva jalpitam

translations.english: Waxing still more aggrieved, the females looked at each other with their expansive and transparent eyes fast flooded with tears. And then he heard the talk, as toned down it proceeded from the royal mansions, of the wives of Dasaratha afflicted with grief for Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
सह रामेण निर्यातो विना राममिहागतः
सूतः किं नाम कौसल्यां शोचन्तीं प्रतिवक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
saha rāmeṇa niryāto vinā rāmamihāgataḥ
sūtaḥ kiṁ nāma kausalyāṁ śocantīṁ prativakṣyati

translations.english: Going in company with Rāma, and returning without him, what will the charioteer answer Kausalya bewailing (for her son)?

verses.sanskrit:
यथा च मन्ये दुर्जीवमेवं न सुकरं ध्रुवम्
आच्छिद्य पुत्रे निर्याते कौसल्या यत्र जीवति
verses.transliteration:
yathā ca manye durjīvamevaṁ na sukaraṁ dhruvam
ācchidya putre niryāte kausalyā yatra jīvati

translations.english: Surely life is miserable, yet is incapable of being renounced, since, although her son leaving (the installation) has gone away, yet Kausalyā still lives.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्य रूपं तु तद्वाक्यं राज्ञः स्त्रीणां निशामयन्
प्रदीप्तमिव शोकेन विवेश सहसा गृहम्
verses.transliteration:
satya rūpaṁ tu tadvākyaṁ rājñaḥ strīṇāṁ niśāmayan
pradīptamiva śokena viveśa sahasā gṛham

translations.english: Having heard those words of the queens, fraught with truth, Sumantra burning as it were in grief, at once entered the (next) apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रविश्याष्टमीं कक्ष्यां राजानं दीनमातुलम्
पुत्रशोकपरिद्यूनमपश्यत्पाण्डरे गृहे
verses.transliteration:
sa praviśyāṣṭamīṁ kakṣyāṁ rājānaṁ dīnamātulam
putraśokaparidyūnamapaśyatpāṇḍare gṛhe

translations.english: And entering the eighth apartment he beheld in a gloomy chamber the king distressed and in a pitiable plight, woe-begone for grief for his son.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिगम्य तमासीनं नरेन्द्रमभिवाद्य च
सुमन्त्रो रामवचनं यथोक्तं प्रत्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
abhigamya tamāsīnaṁ narendramabhivādya ca
sumantro rāmavacanaṁ yathoktaṁ pratyavedayat

translations.english: Thereupon presenting himself before the monarch, Sumantra saluted him and then conveyed to the king the words of Rāma as he had uttered them.

verses.sanskrit:
स तूष्णीमेव तच्छ्रुत्वा राजा विभ्रान्त चेतनः
मूर्छितो न्यपतद्भूमौ रामशोकाभिपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tūṣṇīmeva tacchrutvā rājā vibhrānta cetanaḥ
mūrchito nyapatadbhūmau rāmaśokābhipīḍitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing them silently, the monarch with his mind exceedingly wrought, dropped down to the ground in a swoon, afflicted with grief for Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽन्तःपुरमाविद्धं मूर्छिते पृथिवीपतौ
उद्धृत्य बाहू चुक्रोश नृपतौ पतिते क्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
tato'ntaḥpuramāviddhaṁ mūrchite pṛthivīpatau
uddhṛtya bāhū cukrośa nṛpatau patite kṣitau

translations.english: On the lord of earth swooning away and falling to the ground, the inmates of the inner apartment raising their burst into lamentations. arms of an

verses.sanskrit:
सुमित्रया तु सहिता कौसल्या पतितं पतिम्
उत्थापयामास तदा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sumitrayā tu sahitā kausalyā patitaṁ patim
utthāpayāmāsa tadā vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Kausalyā availing herself of the aid of Sumantra, raised up her fallen lord and addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इमं तस्य महाभाग दूतं दुष्करकारिणः
वनवासादनुप्राप्तं कस्मान्न प्रतिभाषसे
verses.transliteration:
imaṁ tasya mahābhāga dūtaṁ duṣkarakāriṇaḥ
vanavāsādanuprāptaṁ kasmānna pratibhāṣase

translations.english: This, O eminently virtuous one, is the envoy of that one an exceedingly arduous achievement returned from the forest. Why do you not accost him?

verses.sanskrit:
अद्येममनयं कृत्वा व्यपत्रपसि राघव
उत्तिष्ठ सुकृतं तेऽस्तु शोके न स्यात्सहायता
verses.transliteration:
adyemamanayaṁ kṛtvā vyapatrapasi rāghava
uttiṣṭha sukṛtaṁ te'stu śoke na syātsahāyatā

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, you are ashamed today, having done this wrong. Do you rise: merit be yours (arising from this act.) Let not your adherents come to naught (because of your sorrow).

verses.sanskrit:
देव यस्या भयाद्रामं नानुपृच्छसि सारथिम्
नेह तिष्ठति कैकेयी विश्रब्धं प्रतिभाष्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
deva yasyā bhayādrāmaṁ nānupṛcchasi sārathim
neha tiṣṭhati kaikeyī viśrabdhaṁ pratibhāṣyatām

translations.english: O worshipful one, she from fear of whom you do not speak to the charioteer, Kaikeyi, is not here. Do you therefore speak to him without fear.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तथोक्त्वा महाराजं कौसल्या शोकलालसा
धरण्यां निपपाताशु बाष्पविप्लुतभाषिणी
verses.transliteration:
sā tathoktvā mahārājaṁ kausalyā śokalālasā
dharaṇyāṁ nipapātāśu bāṣpaviplutabhāṣiṇī

translations.english: Having said this to the monarch, Kausalyā overwhelmed with grief, with her voice oppressed with the vapour begot of emotion, all on a sudden fell to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपतीं दृष्ट्वा कौसल्यां पतितां भुवि
पतिं चावेक्ष्य ताः सर्वाः सस्वरं रुरुदुः स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapatīṁ dṛṣṭvā kausalyāṁ patitāṁ bhuvi
patiṁ cāvekṣya tāḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṁ ruruduḥ striyaḥ

translations.english: Behoiding Kausalyā fallen on the ground bewailing, as also their husband, the ladies seated around, began to Lament,

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तमन्तःपुरनादमुत्थितं; समीक्ष्य वृद्धास्तरुणाश्च मानवाः
स्त्रियश्च सर्वा रुरुदुः समन्ततः; पुरं तदासीत्पुनरेव संकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastamantaḥpuranādamutthitaṁ; samīkṣya vṛddhāstaruṇāśca mānavāḥ
striyaśca sarvā ruruduḥ samantataḥ; puraṁ tadāsītpunareva saṁkulam

translations.english: Hearing the sounds of wailing arise from the inner apartment, old and young as well as females, set up lamentations all round; and the city was again filled with them.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्याश्वस्तो यदा राजा मोहात्प्रत्यागतः पुनः
अथाजुहाव तं सूतं रामवृत्तान्तकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
pratyāśvasto yadā rājā mohātpratyāgataḥ punaḥ
athājuhāva taṁ sūtaṁ rāmavṛttāntakāraṇāt

translations.english: When having been ministered to and when his senses has returned after the swoon, the king summoned Sumantra for hearing tidings of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा तु रजसा सूतं ध्वस्ताङ्गं समुपस्थितम्
अश्रुपूर्णमुखं दीनमुवाच परमार्तवत्
verses.transliteration:
rājā tu rajasā sūtaṁ dhvastāṅgaṁ samupasthitam
aśrupūrṇamukhaṁ dīnamuvāca paramārtavat

translations.english: Thereupon the charioteer with joined hands spoke to the mighty monarch, lamenting for Rāma, influenced by grief and sorrow, aged, burning in grief, like a newly-taken elephant, sighing heavily, plunged in thought, and resembling an elephant that is indisposed. Then the king like one exceedingly distressed, spoke to the charioteer, who had presented himself, covered over with dust, with tears starting from his eyes, and in pitiable guise.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व नु वत्स्यति धर्मात्मा वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः
सोऽत्यन्तसुखितः सूत किमशिष्यति राघवः
भूमिपालात्मजो भूमौ शेते कथमनाथवत्
verses.transliteration:
kva nu vatsyati dharmātmā vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ
so'tyantasukhitaḥ sūta kimaśiṣyati rāghavaḥ
bhūmipālātmajo bhūmau śete kathamanāthavat

translations.english: Where stays that righteous one, taking refuge under a tree? lapped in luxury, what, O charioteer, will Rāghava feed on?

verses.sanskrit:
यं यान्तमनुयान्ति स्म पदातिरथकुञ्जराः
स वत्स्यति कथं रामो विजनं वनमाश्रितः
verses.transliteration:
yaṁ yāntamanuyānti sma padātirathakuñjarāḥ
sa vatsyati kathaṁ rāmo vijanaṁ vanamāśritaḥ

translations.english: How is Rāma passing his days in the lone forest, he who when he went out used to be followed by foot-men and elephants?

verses.sanskrit:
व्यालैर्मृगैराचरितं कृष्णसर्पनिषेवितम्
कथं कुमारौ वैदेह्या सार्धं वनमुपस्थितौ
verses.transliteration:
vyālairmṛgairācaritaṁ kṛṣṇasarpaniṣevitam
kathaṁ kumārau vaidehyā sārdhaṁ vanamupasthitau

translations.english: How are the princes in company with Vaidehi living in the woods, ranged by serpents and beasts and inhabited by black snakes?

verses.sanskrit:
सुकुमार्या तपस्विन्या सुमन्त्र सह सीतया
राजपुत्रौ कथं पादैरवरुह्य रथाद्गतौ
verses.transliteration:
sukumāryā tapasvinyā sumantra saha sītayā
rājaputrau kathaṁ pādairavaruhya rathādgatau

translations.english: How, O Sumantra, having descended from the car, the princes along with the tender and unfortunate Sītā are proceeding on foot?

verses.sanskrit:
सिद्धार्थः खलु सूत त्वं येन दृष्टौ ममात्मजौ
वनान्तं प्रविशन्तौ तावश्विनाविव मन्दरम्
verses.transliteration:
siddhārthaḥ khalu sūta tvaṁ yena dṛṣṭau mamātmajau
vanāntaṁ praviśantau tāvaśvināviva mandaram

translations.english: O charioteer, surely you are blessed, for you have beheld my sons enter the forest, like the Asvins entering the Mandāra hill.

verses.sanskrit:
किमुवाच वचो रामः किमुवाच च लक्ष्मणः
सुमन्त्र वनमासाद्य किमुवाच च मैथिली
आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय
verses.transliteration:
kimuvāca vaco rāmaḥ kimuvāca ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
sumantra vanamāsādya kimuvāca ca maithilī
āsitaṁ śayitaṁ bhuktaṁ sūta rāmasya kīrtaya

translations.english: And what did Rāma say? And what did Laks mana? And, O Sumantra, arriving at the forest what did Mithila's daughter?

verses.sanskrit:
इति सूतो नरेन्द्रेण चोदितः सज्जमानया
उवाच वाचा राजानं सबाष्पपरिरब्धया
verses.transliteration:
iti sūto narendreṇa coditaḥ sajjamānayā
uvāca vācā rājānaṁ sabāṣpaparirabdhayā

translations.english: Thus urged by the king, the charioteer spoke to the king with his voice faltering and suppressed with the vapour of grief.

verses.sanskrit:
सूत मद्वचनात्तस्य तातस्य विदितात्मनः
शिरसा वन्दनीयस्य वन्द्यौ पादौ महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
sūta madvacanāttasya tātasya viditātmanaḥ
śirasā vandanīyasya vandyau pādau mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: O mighty monarch observing morality, Rāghava with joined hands and bowing down his head, said, “O charioteer, do you in my name salute with your head the feet of my high-souled sire worthy of being saluted, and famed (in the world).” And, O charioteer, do you in my name as each deserves salute the ladies of the inner apartment and communicate to them tidings of my health.

verses.sanskrit:
माता च मम कौसल्या कुशलं चाभिवादनम्
देवि देवस्य पादौ च देववत्परिपालय
verses.transliteration:
mātā ca mama kausalyā kuśalaṁ cābhivādanam
devi devasya pādau ca devavatparipālaya

translations.english: Having saluted my mother Kausalyā and conveyed to her news of my welfare, as well as of my unswerving adherence to morality, do you tell her these words, Do you remaining steady in virtue, at the proper hour bestir yourself in behalf of the chamber of sacrificial fire. And, O revered one, do you minister to the feet of that worshipful one, (the king), as if they were very deities.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतः कुशलं वाच्यो वाच्यो मद्वचनेन च
सर्वास्वेव यथान्यायं वृत्तिं वर्तस्व मातृषु
verses.transliteration:
bharataḥ kuśalaṁ vācyo vācyo madvacanena ca
sarvāsveva yathānyāyaṁ vṛttiṁ vartasva mātṛṣu

translations.english: Do you communicate to Bharata news of my welfare and say in my name, Do you behave properly with all your mothers.

verses.sanskrit:
वक्तव्यश्च महाबाहुरिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः
पितरं यौवराज्यस्थो राज्यस्थमनुपालय
verses.transliteration:
vaktavyaśca mahābāhurikṣvākukulanandanaḥ
pitaraṁ yauvarājyastho rājyasthamanupālaya

translations.english: And to that delight of the Ikṣvāku line do you further say, Having been installed as the heirapparent, be you, looking upon the king as the supreme authority in the state, obedient to him.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं मां महाराज ब्रुवन्नेव महायशाः
रामो राजीवताम्राक्षो भृशमश्रूण्यवर्तयत्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ māṁ mahārāja bruvanneva mahāyaśāḥ
rāmo rājīvatāmrākṣo bhṛśamaśrūṇyavartayat

translations.english: And shedding copious tears, he again addressed me, saying, Do you look upon my mother as on your own proud of her son. Having said this, the mighty-armed and illustrious Rāma furnished with eyes resembling lotus-petals, shed plenteous tears.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
केनायमपराधेन राजपुत्रो विवासितः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇastu susaṁkruddho niḥśvasanvākyamabravīt
kenāyamaparādhena rājaputro vivāsitaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa waxing wroth, breathing hard, said, For what fault of his has the Prince been banished?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि प्रव्राजितो रामो लोभकारणकारितम्
वरदाननिमित्तं वा सर्वथा दुष्कृतं कृतम्
रामस्य तु परित्यागे न हेतुमुपलक्षये
verses.transliteration:
yadi pravrājito rāmo lobhakāraṇakāritam
varadānanimittaṁ vā sarvathā duṣkṛtaṁ kṛtam
rāmasya tu parityāge na hetumupalakṣaye

translations.english: Whether Rāma has been exiled through Kaikeyi's lust for dominion or through the exigencies of the bestowal of the boon, there cannot be any doubt that the king has acted most unrighteously.

verses.sanskrit:
असमीक्ष्य समारब्धं विरुद्धं बुद्धिलाघवात्
जनयिष्यति संक्रोशं राघवस्य विवासनम्
verses.transliteration:
asamīkṣya samārabdhaṁ viruddhaṁ buddhilāghavāt
janayiṣyati saṁkrośaṁ rāghavasya vivāsanam

translations.english: The king through lack of sense has done herulessly what is opposed to morality; and this banishment of Rāma will but bring upon him woe here and hereafter.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तावन्महाराजे पितृत्वं नोपलक्षये
भ्राता भर्ता च बन्धुश्च पिता च मम राघवः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tāvanmahārāje pitṛtvaṁ nopalakṣaye
bhrātā bhartā ca bandhuśca pitā ca mama rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Fatherhood find I none in the monarch. My brother and feeder and friend and father is even Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वलोकप्रियं त्यक्त्वा सर्वलोकहिते रतम्
सर्वलोकोऽनुरज्येत कथं त्वानेन कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
sarvalokapriyaṁ tyaktvā sarvalokahite ratam
sarvaloko'nurajyeta kathaṁ tvānena karmaṇā

translations.english: Renouncing one that is universally dear, and that is ever engaged in the good of all, how by such an act will the king please the people?

verses.sanskrit:
जानकी तु महाराज निःश्वसन्ती तपस्विनी
भूतोपहतचित्तेव विष्ठिता विष्मृता स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
jānakī tu mahārāja niḥśvasantī tapasvinī
bhūtopahatacitteva viṣṭhitā viṣmṛtā sthitā

translations.english: O mighty monarch, Janaki also, unfortunate that she is, sighing heavily, stood wildered like one that had been possessed.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसना राजपुत्री यशस्विनी
तेन दुःखेन रुदती नैव मां किंचिदब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanā rājaputrī yaśasvinī
tena duḥkhena rudatī naiva māṁ kiṁcidabravīt

translations.english: And not having experienced any calamity before, the famed princes weeping because of this misfortune, told me nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्वीक्षमाणा भर्तारं मुखेन परिशुष्यता
मुमोच सहसा बाष्पं मां प्रयान्तमुदीक्ष्य सा
verses.transliteration:
udvīkṣamāṇā bhartāraṁ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
mumoca sahasā bāṣpaṁ māṁ prayāntamudīkṣya sā

translations.english: Looking up to her lord with a blank countenance, she suddenly let fall tears, perceiving the destruction of the subject.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव रामोऽश्रुमुखः कृताञ्जलिः; स्थितोऽभवल्लक्ष्मणबाहुपालितः
तथैव सीता रुदती तपस्विनी; निरीक्षते राजरथं तथैव माम्
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva rāmo'śrumukhaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ; sthito'bhavallakṣmaṇabāhupālitaḥ
tathaiva sītā rudatī tapasvinī; nirīkṣate rājarathaṁ tathaiva mām

translations.english: Thus said Rāma ministered to by Lakşmaņa, with a tearful countenance; and thus stood the unfortunate and weeping Sītå beholding the royal car and myself.

verses.sanskrit:
मम त्वश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि
उष्णमश्रु विमुञ्चन्तो रामे संप्रस्थिते वनम्
verses.transliteration:
mama tvaśvā nivṛttasya na prāvartanta vartmani
uṣṇamaśru vimuñcanto rāme saṁprasthite vanam

translations.english: On Rāma having gone to the forest, my horses as I turned away, did not proceed vigorously on the way, and shed warm tears. And having (done homage) to both the princes by joining my hands, I turned my back, bearing as best I could that load of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
गुहेव सार्धं तत्रैव स्थितोऽस्मि दिवसान्बहून्
आशया यदि मां रामः पुनः शब्दापयेदिति
verses.transliteration:
guheva sārdhaṁ tatraiva sthito'smi divasānbahūn
āśayā yadi māṁ rāmaḥ punaḥ śabdāpayediti

translations.english: Indulging in the hope that Rāma might again summon me by any of the envoys (of Guha left there), I stayed there with Guha for many days.

verses.sanskrit:
विषये ते महाराज रामव्यसनकर्शिताः
अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानः सपुष्पाङ्कुरकोरकाः
verses.transliteration:
viṣaye te mahārāja rāmavyasanakarśitāḥ
api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānaḥ sapuṣpāṅkurakorakāḥ

translations.english: In your dominions, O monarch, exercised by the calamity that has befallen Rāma, even trees bearing blossoms and buds and sprouts look sad; the rivers and pools and liquid lapses have their waters dried up; and the woods and groves have their foliage withered.

verses.sanskrit:
न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्याला न प्रसरन्ति च
रामशोकाभिभूतं तन्निष्कूजमभवद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
na ca sarpanti sattvāni vyālā na prasaranti ca
rāmaśokābhibhūtaṁ tanniṣkūjamabhavadvanam

translations.english: Creatures do not move and beasts of prey cease to range about; and the forest appears to be dumb, stupefied by grief on account of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च
नाद्य भान्त्यल्पगन्धीनि फलानि च यथा पुरम्
verses.transliteration:
jalajāni ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni sthalajāni ca
nādya bhāntyalpagandhīni phalāni ca yathā puram

translations.english: Streams containing lotuses with their leaves shrivelled, have their waters stained; and lotuses have their leaves burnt; and fished and (aquatic) birds have grown lean. And flowers both on land and water have been deprived of their freshness and fragrance; and they no longer retain their former condition.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविशन्तमयोध्यां मां न कश्चिदभिनन्दति
नरा राममपश्यन्तो निःश्वसन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
praviśantamayodhyāṁ māṁ na kaścidabhinandati
narā rāmamapaśyanto niḥśvasanti muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: When I entered Ayodhyā, none greeted me. And not seeing Rāma, the people sigh momentarily.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्म्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्य रथमागतम्
हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामादर्शनकर्शिताः
verses.transliteration:
harmyairvimānaiḥ prāsādairavekṣya rathamāgatam
hāhākārakṛtā nāryo rāmādarśanakarśitāḥ

translations.english: And from mansions, cars, and lordly edifices, ladies seeing the car come back, set up a chorus of 'Ah' and 'Alas,' afflicted with the absence of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः
अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्ते व्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
āyatairvimalairnetrairaśruvegapariplutaiḥ
anyonyamabhivīkṣante vyaktamārtatarāḥ striyaḥ

translations.english: And becoming more distressed that ever, the fair sex with their expansive and clear eyes filled with tears, began to eye each other indistinctly.

verses.sanskrit:
नामित्राणां न मित्राणामुदासीनजनस्य च
अहमार्ततया कंचिद्विशेषं नोपलक्षये
verses.transliteration:
nāmitrāṇāṁ na mitrāṇāmudāsīnajanasya ca
ahamārtatayā kaṁcidviśeṣaṁ nopalakṣaye

translations.english: And in consequence of the general grief that prevailed, I could not perceive any difference between friends and foes and persons indifferent.

verses.sanskrit:
निरानन्दा महाराज रामप्रव्राजनातुरा
कौसल्या पुत्रहीनेव अयोध्या प्रतिभाति मा
verses.transliteration:
nirānandā mahārāja rāmapravrājanāturā
kausalyā putrahīneva ayodhyā pratibhāti mā

translations.english: O mighty monarch, distressed in consequence of the exile of Rāma, men appear sunk in dejection, and elephants and horses are spiritless; and seized with cheerlessness, they utter doleful sounds and heave profound sighs. Ayodhyā appears to me joyless like Kausalyă deprived of her son.

verses.sanskrit:
सूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा वाचा परमदीनया
बाष्पोपहतया राजा तं सूतमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sūtasya vacanaṁ śrutvā vācā paramadīnayā
bāṣpopahatayā rājā taṁ sūtamidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of the charioteer, the king like an exceedingly forlorn, addressed the former in words lost in the vapour of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्या विनियुक्तेन पापाभिजनभावया
मया न मन्त्रकुशलैर्वृद्धैः सह समर्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyā viniyuktena pāpābhijanabhāvayā
mayā na mantrakuśalairvṛddhaiḥ saha samarthitam

translations.english: Exhorted by Kaikeyi of a sinful country, born in a sinful race and cherishing sinful designs, I did not take counsel with aged people capable of offering advice.

verses.sanskrit:
न सुहृद्भिर्न चामात्यैर्मन्त्रयित्वा न नैगमैः
मयायमर्थः संमोहात्स्त्रीहेतोः सहसा कृतः
verses.transliteration:
na suhṛdbhirna cāmātyairmantrayitvā na naigamaiḥ
mayāyamarthaḥ saṁmohātstrīhetoḥ sahasā kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Without consulting with friends or courtiers or persons versed in the Vedas, I have in the interest of a woman rashly done this thing through ignorance.

verses.sanskrit:
भवितव्यतया नूनमिदं वा व्यसनं महत्
कुलस्यास्य विनाशाय प्राप्तं सूत यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
bhavitavyatayā nūnamidaṁ vā vyasanaṁ mahat
kulasyāsya vināśāya prāptaṁ sūta yadṛcchayā

translations.english: Meseems, O charioteer, for the purpose of destroying this line entirely, this mighty disaster has surely befallen us through the influence of Destiny.

verses.sanskrit:
सूत यद्यस्ति ते किंचिन्मयापि सुकृतं कृतम्
त्वं प्रापयाशु मां रामं प्राणाः संत्वरयन्ति माम्
verses.transliteration:
sūta yadyasti te kiṁcinmayāpi sukṛtaṁ kṛtam
tvaṁ prāpayāśu māṁ rāmaṁ prāṇāḥ saṁtvarayanti mām

translations.english: O charioteer, if I have ever done you any good do you immediately take me to Rāma: my life urges me on (in this direction).

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यद्यापि ममैवाज्ञा निवर्तयतु राघवम्
न शक्ष्यामि विना राम मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
yadyadyāpi mamaivājñā nivartayatu rāghavam
na śakṣyāmi vinā rāma muhūrtamapi jīvitum

translations.english: Or let my command make Rāghava turn back. I cannot live for a moment without Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वापि महाबाहुर्गतो दूरं भविष्यति
मामेव रथमारोप्य शीघ्रं रामाय दर्शय
verses.transliteration:
atha vāpi mahābāhurgato dūraṁ bhaviṣyati
māmeva rathamāropya śīghraṁ rāmāya darśaya

translations.english: But if that mighty-armed one has proceeded far, do you placing me on a car speedily show me to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
वृत्तदंष्ट्रो महेष्वासः क्वासौ लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
यदि जीवामि साध्वेनं पश्येयं सह सीतया
verses.transliteration:
vṛttadaṁṣṭro maheṣvāsaḥ kvāsau lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
yadi jīvāmi sādhvenaṁ paśyeyaṁ saha sītayā

translations.english: Where is that elder brother of Lakşmaņa of a mighty bow, furnished with teeth resembling Kunda flowers? If I live so long, I will behold him in company with Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुमामुक्तमणिकुण्डलम्
रामं यदि न पश्यामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
lohitākṣaṁ mahābāhumāmuktamaṇikuṇḍalam
rāmaṁ yadi na paśyāmi gamiṣyāmi yamakṣayam

translations.english: What can be sadder than this, that reduced to such a pass, I cannot see here that descendant of Ikşvāku, Rāghava?

verses.sanskrit:
हा राम रामानुज हा हा वैदेहि तपस्विनी
न मां जानीत दुःखेन म्रियमाणमनाथवत्
दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयायं शोकसागरः
verses.transliteration:
hā rāma rāmānuja hā hā vaidehi tapasvinī
na māṁ jānīta duḥkhena mriyamāṇamanāthavat
dustaro jīvatā devi mayāyaṁ śokasāgaraḥ

translations.english: Ah Rāma! Ah you younger brother of Rāma! Ah you unfortunate Vaidehī! You do not know that I am through grief lamenting like one deserted.

verses.sanskrit:
इति विलपति पार्थिवे प्रनष्टे; करुणतरं द्विगुणं च रामहेतोः
वचनमनुनिशम्य तस्य देवी; भयमगमत्पुनरेव राममाता
verses.transliteration:
iti vilapati pārthive pranaṣṭe; karuṇataraṁ dviguṇaṁ ca rāmahetoḥ
vacanamanuniśamya tasya devī; bhayamagamatpunareva rāmamātā

translations.english: On the king swooning away lamenting, that exalted lady, Rāma's mother, hearing his words doubly bitter and more piteous than ever uttered for Rāma, was seized with fresh apprehension.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भूतोपसृष्टेव वेपमाना पुनः पुनः
धरण्यां गतसत्त्वेव कौसल्या सूतमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato bhūtopasṛṣṭeva vepamānā punaḥ punaḥ
dharaṇyāṁ gatasattveva kausalyā sūtamabravīt

translations.english: Then like one possessed by an evil spirit, and trembling again and again, Kausalyä lying down on the ground like one dead, spoke to the charioteer, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
नय मां यत्र काकुत्स्थः सीता यत्र च लक्ष्मणः
तान्विना क्षणमप्यत्र जीवितुं नोत्सहे ह्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
naya māṁ yatra kākutsthaḥ sītā yatra ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
tānvinā kṣaṇamapyatra jīvituṁ notsahe hyaham

translations.english: Do you take me where Kākutstha is and Sītā and Lakşınaņa: without them, I cannot live for a moment.

verses.sanskrit:
निवर्तय रथं शीघ्रं दण्डकान्नय मामपि
अथ तान्नानुगच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
nivartaya rathaṁ śīghraṁ daṇḍakānnaya māmapi
atha tānnānugacchāmi gamiṣyāmi yamakṣayam

translations.english: Do you without delay turn the car. Do you take me also to Dandaka. If I do not follow them, I shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यज शोकं च मोहं च संभ्रमं दुःखजं तथा
व्यवधूय च संतापं वने वत्स्यति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
tyaja śokaṁ ca mohaṁ ca saṁbhramaṁ duḥkhajaṁ tathā
vyavadhūya ca saṁtāpaṁ vane vatsyati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Thereat the cahrioteer with joined hands comforted that exalted lady with ready words faltering and choked with rising vapour, "Do you leave grief and sorrow and the violent emotion. Renouncing grief, Rāghava is living in the woods."

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामस्य पादौ परिचरन्वने
आराधयति धर्मज्ञः परलोकं जितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaścāpi rāmasya pādau paricaranvane
ārādhayati dharmajñaḥ paralokaṁ jitendriyaḥ

translations.english: And in the forest, the righteous Laksmara, having his senses under control, is ministering to Răma's feet and is thus adoring the gods for happiness in the next world.

verses.sanskrit:
विजनेऽपि वने सीता वासं प्राप्य गृहेष्विव
विस्रम्भं लभतेऽभीता रामे संन्यस्तमानसा
verses.transliteration:
vijane'pi vane sītā vāsaṁ prāpya gṛheṣviva
visrambhaṁ labhate'bhītā rāme saṁnyastamānasā

translations.english: And even in the lonely woods, Sītā as if remaining at home, having fixed her thoughts on Rāma, is living a life of love.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्या दैन्यं कृतं किंचित्सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्षये
उचितेव प्रवासानां वैदेही प्रतिभाति मा
verses.transliteration:
nāsyā dainyaṁ kṛtaṁ kiṁcitsusūkṣmamapi lakṣaye
uciteva pravāsānāṁ vaidehī pratibhāti mā

translations.english: And there appears not the least trace of any distress afflicting her; and Vaidehi seems to me as if she were meant (by Nature) for a life away from home.

verses.sanskrit:
नगरोपवनं गत्वा यथा स्म रमते पुरा
तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
nagaropavanaṁ gatvā yathā sma ramate purā
tathaiva ramate sītā nirjaneṣu vaneṣvapi

translations.english: And as forinerly going to urban villas she disported, she disports now even in the lonely forest.

verses.sanskrit:
बालेव रमते सीता बालचन्द्रनिभानना
रामा रामे ह्यदीनात्मा विजनेऽपि वने सती
verses.transliteration:
bāleva ramate sītā bālacandranibhānanā
rāmā rāme hyadīnātmā vijane'pi vane satī

translations.english: And although living in the lone forest, that one of a countenance resembling the infant moon, sports merrily like a girl, in the garden represented by Rāma's self.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्गतं हृदयं ह्यस्यास्तदधीनं च जीवितम्
अयोध्यापि भवेत्तस्या रामहीना तथा वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tadgataṁ hṛdayaṁ hyasyāstadadhīnaṁ ca jīvitam
ayodhyāpi bhavettasyā rāmahīnā tathā vanam

translations.english: Ayodhyā without Rāma would have seemed a wilderness to her whose heart is fixed on him and whose very life depends upon him.

verses.sanskrit:
पथि पृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च
गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान्विविधानपि
verses.transliteration:
pathi pṛcchati vaidehī grāmāṁśca nagarāṇi ca
gatiṁ dṛṣṭvā nadīnāṁ ca pādapānvividhānapi

translations.english: Vaidehī is now asking (Rāma) concerning the villages and towns (in their way); and observing various trees and the courses of the rivers, Jānaki, asking Råma Laksmana (for information), is learning all about them. And Sītā sports as she used to do in arbours stationed at the distance of only one krosa from Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्वना वातवेगेन संभ्रमेणातपेन च
न हि गच्छति वैदेह्याश्चन्द्रांशुसदृशी प्रभा
verses.transliteration:
adhvanā vātavegena saṁbhrameṇātapena ca
na hi gacchati vaidehyāścandrāṁśusadṛśī prabhā

translations.english: Neither through the fatigue of travel, nor the influence of the wind, nor excitement, nor the sun, has Vaidehi's lustre resembling the lunar light suffered any diminution.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं शतपत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम्
वदनं तद्वदान्याया वैदेह्या न विकम्पते
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ śatapatrasya pūrṇacandropamaprabham
vadanaṁ tadvadānyāyā vaidehyā na vikampate

translations.english: The countenance of that fair-speaking one resembling the lotus and comparable to the full moon in splendour, has not waxed pale.

verses.sanskrit:
अलक्तरसरक्ताभावलक्तरसवर्जितौ
अद्यापि चरणौ तस्याः पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ
verses.transliteration:
alaktarasaraktābhāvalaktarasavarjitau
adyāpi caraṇau tasyāḥ padmakośasamaprabhau

translations.english: Her feet now without your dye of the liquid lac, but naturally furnished with the roseate hue of the same, are gorgeous like lotus buds.

verses.sanskrit:
नूपुरोद्घुष्टहेलेव खेलं गच्छति भामिनी
इदानीमपि वैदेही तद्रागा न्यस्तभूषणा
verses.transliteration:
nūpurodghuṣṭaheleva khelaṁ gacchati bhāminī
idānīmapi vaidehī tadrāgā nyastabhūṣaṇā

translations.english: Still Vaidehī decked in ornaments from affection for Rāma, goes gracefully rebuking with her bangles the wavy gait (of cranes).

verses.sanskrit:
गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिंहं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता
नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता
verses.transliteration:
gajaṁ vā vīkṣya siṁhaṁ vā vyāghraṁ vā vanamāśritā
nāhārayati saṁtrāsaṁ bāhū rāmasya saṁśritā

translations.english: Supporting herself on Rāma's arm, Sītă arrived at the forest, is not inspired with fear on beholding either an elephant, or a lion, or a tiger.

verses.sanskrit:
न शोच्यास्ते न चात्मा ते शोच्यो नापि जनाधिपः
इदं हि चरितं लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
na śocyāste na cātmā te śocyo nāpi janādhipaḥ
idaṁ hi caritaṁ loke pratiṣṭhāsyati śāśvatam

translations.english: Therefore they are not to be bewailed, nor your own self, nor the lord of men. This history of Rāma will endure for ever in this world.

verses.sanskrit:
विधूय शोकं परिहृष्टमानसा; महर्षियाते पथि सुव्यवस्थिताः
वने रता वन्यफलाशनाः पितुः; शुभां प्रतिज्ञां परिपालयन्ति ते
verses.transliteration:
vidhūya śokaṁ parihṛṣṭamānasā; maharṣiyāte pathi suvyavasthitāḥ
vane ratā vanyaphalāśanāḥ pituḥ; śubhāṁ pratijñāṁ paripālayanti te

translations.english: Renouncing grief and with cheerful hearts, well established in the life led by the Maharşis, they living in the forest on wild fruits as their sustenance, are maintaining the noble promise of their sire.

verses.sanskrit:
तथापि सूतेन सुयुक्तवादिना; निवार्यमाणा सुतशोककर्शिता
न चैव देवी विरराम कूजिता;त्प्रियेति पुत्रेति च राघवेति च
verses.transliteration:
tathāpi sūtena suyuktavādinā; nivāryamāṇā sutaśokakarśitā
na caiva devī virarāma kūjitā;tpriyeti putreti ca rāghaveti ca

translations.english: Consoled by the truth-telling yet sweetspeeched charioteer, that lady oppressed with grief for her son, ceased not to wail loudly, "My beloved,” “My son," "Rāghava."

verses.sanskrit:
वनं गते धर्मपरे रामे रमयतां वरे
कौसल्या रुदती स्वार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vanaṁ gate dharmapare rāme ramayatāṁ vare
kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāramidamabravīt

translations.english: On that foremost of those capable of charming people, the righteous Rāma, repairing to the forest, Kausalyā crying in grief said to her husband.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यपित्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितं ते मयद्यशः
सानुक्रोशो वदान्यश्च प्रियवादी च राघवः
verses.transliteration:
yadyapitriṣu lokeṣu prathitaṁ te mayadyaśaḥ
sānukrośo vadānyaśca priyavādī ca rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Your great fame has spread over the three worlds; and the descendant of Raghu is kind, munificent and fair-speaking.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं नरवरश्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया
दुःखितौ सुखसंवृद्धौ वने दुःखं सहिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ naravaraśreṣṭha putrau tau saha sītayā
duḥkhitau sukhasaṁvṛddhau vane duḥkhaṁ sahiṣyataḥ

translations.english: Why then have you forsaken those foremost of men along with Sītā? Brought up in happiness, and now brought to misery, how can they bear it?

verses.sanskrit:
सा नूनं तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुखोचिता
कथमुष्णं च शीतं च मैथिली प्रसहिष्यते
verses.transliteration:
sā nūnaṁ taruṇī śyāmā sukumārī sukhocitā
kathamuṣṇaṁ ca śītaṁ ca maithilī prasahiṣyate

translations.english: How can the youthful daughter of Mithilā of slender make, tender, and deserving of happiness, bear heat and cold?

verses.sanskrit:
भुक्त्वाशनं विशालाक्षी सूपदंशान्वितं शुभम्
वन्यं नैवारमाहारं कथं सीतोपभोक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
bhuktvāśanaṁ viśālākṣī sūpadaṁśānvitaṁ śubham
vanyaṁ naivāramāhāraṁ kathaṁ sītopabhokṣyate

translations.english: Having formerly partaken of (excellent) rice with curries, how will Sita feed on wild rice?

verses.sanskrit:
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा शुभमनिन्दिता
कथं क्रव्यादसिंहानां शब्दं श्रोष्यत्यशोभनम्
verses.transliteration:
gītavāditranirghoṣaṁ śrutvā śubhamaninditā
kathaṁ kravyādasiṁhānāṁ śabdaṁ śroṣyatyaśobhanam

translations.english: Having heard excellent vocal and instrumental music, how will Sītă hear the frightful cries of carnivorous lions?

verses.sanskrit:
महेन्द्रध्वजसंकाशः क्व नु शेते महाभुजः
भुजं परिघसंकाशमुपधाय महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
mahendradhvajasaṁkāśaḥ kva nu śete mahābhujaḥ
bhujaṁ parighasaṁkāśamupadhāya mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Resembling the gonfalon of the great Indra, where sleeps the mighty-armed and exceedingly powerful Råma, making his arm like to a mace his pillow?

verses.sanskrit:
पद्मवर्णं सुकेशान्तं पद्मनिःश्वासमुत्तमम्
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वदनं पुष्करेक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
padmavarṇaṁ sukeśāntaṁ padmaniḥśvāsamuttamam
kadā drakṣyāmi rāmasya vadanaṁ puṣkarekṣaṇam

translations.english: When shall I behold Rāma's countenance hued like the lotus, with his hair ending beautifully (in curls), and his breath impregnated with the fine perfume of the lotus, and his eyes resembling lotus leaves?

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मे न संशयः
अपश्यन्त्या न तं यद्वै फलतीदं सहस्रधा
verses.transliteration:
vajrasāramayaṁ nūnaṁ hṛdayaṁ me na saṁśayaḥ
apaśyantyā na taṁ yadvai phalatīdaṁ sahasradhā

translations.english: Surely my heart, without doubt, is made of the essence of the thunderbolt, since not beholding him, it is not cracked in a thousand fragments.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि पञ्चदशे वर्षे राघवः पुनरेष्यति
जह्याद्राज्यं च कोशं च भरतेनोपभोक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
yadi pañcadaśe varṣe rāghavaḥ punareṣyati
jahyādrājyaṁ ca kośaṁ ca bharatenopabhokṣyate

translations.english: If after the expiration of the five and ten years, Rāghava does return, it does not appear likely that Bharata will renounce the kingdom and the exchequer.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तं राज्यं विशां पते
भ्राता ज्येष्ठा वरिष्ठाश्च किमर्थं नावमंस्यते
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktaṁ rājyaṁ viśāṁ pate
bhrātā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhāśca kimarthaṁ nāvamaṁsyate

translations.english: Why will not an elder brother and one who has sterling merits, O monarch, disregard a kingdom which has been thus enjoyed by his younger brother?

verses.sanskrit:
न परेणाहृतं भक्ष्यं व्याघ्रः खादितुमिच्छति
एवमेव नरव्याघ्रः परलीढं न मंस्यते
verses.transliteration:
na pareṇāhṛtaṁ bhakṣyaṁ vyāghraḥ khāditumicchati
evameva naravyāghraḥ paralīḍhaṁ na maṁsyate

translations.english: A tiger does not like to feed on food procured by others. Even so that tiger-like personage does not regard anything that has come to be tasted by another.

verses.sanskrit:
हविराज्यं पुरोडाशाः कुशा यूपाश्च खादिराः
नैतानि यातयामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनरध्वरे
verses.transliteration:
havirājyaṁ puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāśca khādirāḥ
naitāni yātayāmāni kurvanti punaradhvare

translations.english: Clarified butter, sacrificial cakes, Kusa, stakes of catechu having been used in one sacrifice cannot be used in another.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ह्यात्तमिदं राज्यं हृतसारां सुरामिव
नाभिमन्तुमलं रामो नष्टसोममिवाध्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā hyāttamidaṁ rājyaṁ hṛtasārāṁ surāmiva
nābhimantumalaṁ rāmo naṣṭasomamivādhvaram

translations.english: Even so this kingdom which has been already enjoyed, like to liquor deprived of its essence or a sacrifice whose soma has been eaten, cannot be accepted by Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवंविधमसत्कारं राघवो मर्षयिष्यति
बलवानिव शार्दूलो बालधेरभिमर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
naivaṁvidhamasatkāraṁ rāghavo marṣayiṣyati
balavāniva śārdūlo bāladherabhimarśanam

translations.english: Such an ill treatment Rāghava will not put up with, even as a powerful tiger cannot bear the rubbing of its tail (by another).

verses.sanskrit:
स तादृशः सिंहबलो वृषभाक्षो नरर्षभः
स्वयमेव हतः पित्रा जलजेनात्मजो यथा
verses.transliteration:
sa tādṛśaḥ siṁhabalo vṛṣabhākṣo nararṣabhaḥ
svayameva hataḥ pitrā jalajenātmajo yathā

translations.english: But such a man of men, possessed of leonine strength, and graced with the eyes of a bull, has been destroyed by his father, like a fish destroying his offspring.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विजाति चरितो धर्मः शास्त्रदृष्टः सनातनः
यदि ते धर्मनिरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते
verses.transliteration:
dvijāti carito dharmaḥ śāstradṛṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ
yadi te dharmanirate tvayā putre vivāsite

translations.english: If you had believed in the morality prescribed in the scriptures, and which is followed by the twice-born ones, you would not have banished your son. But disregarding such morality, you have banished your virtuous son.

verses.sanskrit:
गतिरेवाक्पतिर्नार्या द्वितीया गतिरात्मजः
तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजंश्चतुर्थी नेह विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
gatirevākpatirnāryā dvitīyā gatirātmajaḥ
tṛtīyā jñātayo rājaṁścaturthī neha vidyate

translations.english: One of the refuges of a woman is her husband, a second is her son, and a third is her relatives; and a fourth she has none.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र त्वं चैव मे नास्ति रामश्च वनमाश्रितः
न वनं गन्तुमिच्छामि सर्वथा हि हता त्वया
verses.transliteration:
tatra tvaṁ caiva me nāsti rāmaśca vanamāśritaḥ
na vanaṁ gantumicchāmi sarvathā hi hatā tvayā

translations.english: But you cease to be mine; and Rāma has been sent to the woods. I do not like to go into the forest; so I am entirely undone by you.

verses.sanskrit:
हतं त्वया राज्यमिदं सराष्ट्रं; हतस्तथात्मा सह मन्त्रिभिश्च
हता सपुत्रास्मि हताश्च पौराः; सुतश्च भार्या च तव प्रहृष्टौ
verses.transliteration:
hataṁ tvayā rājyamidaṁ sarāṣṭraṁ; hatastathātmā saha mantribhiśca
hatā saputrāsmi hatāśca paurāḥ; sutaśca bhāryā ca tava prahṛṣṭau

translations.english: This kingdom, your own kingdom, has been destroyed by you; destroyed are all along with the counsellors; destroyed am I with my son; and destroyed are the citizens: your son and your wife are alone delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां गिरं दारुणशब्दसंश्रितां; निशम्य राजापि मुमोह दुःखितः
ततः स शोकं प्रविवेश पार्थिवः; स्वदुष्कृतं चापि पुनस्तदास्मरत्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ giraṁ dāruṇaśabdasaṁśritāṁ; niśamya rājāpi mumoha duḥkhitaḥ
tataḥ sa śokaṁ praviveśa pārthivaḥ; svaduṣkṛtaṁ cāpi punastadāsmarat

translations.english: Hearing these words uttered in heart-rending accents, Dasaratha exceedingly distressed, became senseless. And being afflicted with grief, he again remembered his evil act.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं तु क्रुद्धया राजा राममात्रा सशोकया
श्रावितः परुषं वाक्यं चिन्तयामास दुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tu kruddhayā rājā rāmamātrā saśokayā
śrāvitaḥ paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ cintayāmāsa duḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Thus harshly addressed by the indignant mother of Rāma, the king aggrieved was plunged in thought. Having thought for a long while, that repressor of foes, the king, who had lost his senses through grief, regained consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रत्यभात्कर्म दुष्कृतम्
यदनेन कृतं पूर्वमज्ञानाच्छब्दवेधिना
verses.transliteration:
tasya cintayamānasya pratyabhātkarma duṣkṛtam
yadanena kṛtaṁ pūrvamajñānācchabdavedhinā

translations.english: As he was thinking, the sinful act which he had through ignorance formerly committed by means of the shaft which hits by sounds, rose up in his recollection,

verses.sanskrit:
अमनास्तेन शोकेन रामशोकेन च प्रभुः
दह्यमानस्तु शोकाभ्यां कौसल्यामाह भूपतिः
verses.transliteration:
amanāstena śokena rāmaśokena ca prabhuḥ
dahyamānastu śokābhyāṁ kausalyāmāha bhūpatiḥ

translations.english: Afflicted with this grief as well as that on account of Rāma, that lord, the king, burned in these two several griefs.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादये त्वां कौसल्ये रचितोऽयं मयाञ्जलिः
वत्सला चानृशंसा च त्वं हि नित्यं परेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
prasādaye tvāṁ kausalye racito'yaṁ mayāñjaliḥ
vatsalā cānṛśaṁsā ca tvaṁ hi nityaṁ pareṣvapi

translations.english: I deprecate your displeasure. O Kausalyä with joined hands. You are ever affectionate and did not treat harshly even enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्ता तु खलु नारीणां गुणवान्निर्गुणोऽपि वा
धर्मं विमृशमानानां प्रत्यक्षं देवि दैवतम्
verses.transliteration:
bhartā tu khalu nārīṇāṁ guṇavānnirguṇo'pi vā
dharmaṁ vimṛśamānānāṁ pratyakṣaṁ devi daivatam

translations.english: Verily to women cognizant of virtue, a husband, whether he has any merits or not, is a very deity.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वं धर्मपरा नित्यं दृष्टलोकपरावर
नार्हसे विप्रियं वक्तुं दुःखितापि सुदुःखितम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tvaṁ dharmaparā nityaṁ dṛṣṭalokaparāvara
nārhase vipriyaṁ vaktuṁ duḥkhitāpi suduḥkhitam

translations.english: Ever virtuous, you, that have seen both the virtuous and the vicious, although aggrieved, ought not to say anything unpleasant to me who am weighed down with woe.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वाक्यं करुणं राज्ञः श्रुत्वा दीनस्य भाषितम्
कौसल्या व्यसृजद्बाष्पं प्रणालीव नवोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
tadvākyaṁ karuṇaṁ rājñaḥ śrutvā dīnasya bhāṣitam
kausalyā vyasṛjadbāṣpaṁ praṇālīva navodakam

translations.english: Having heard these piteous words of the distressed king, Kausalyā uttered words even as a water-way lets out fresh accession of rain.

verses.sanskrit:
स मूद्र्ह्णि बद्ध्वा रुदती राज्ञः पद्ममिवाञ्जलिम्
संभ्रमादब्रवीत्त्रस्ता त्वरमाणाक्षरं वचः
verses.transliteration:
sa mūdrhṇi baddhvā rudatī rājñaḥ padmamivāñjalim
saṁbhramādabravīttrastā tvaramāṇākṣaraṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And weeping, she drew on her head the joined hands of the king resembling lotuses; and then flurried spoke these words hurriedly informed with extreme affection.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसीद शिरसा याचे भूमौ निततितास्मि ते
याचितास्मि हता देव हन्तव्याहं न हि त्वया
verses.transliteration:
prasīda śirasā yāce bhūmau nitatitāsmi te
yācitāsmi hatā deva hantavyāhaṁ na hi tvayā

translations.english: Be you propitious; I beseech with (bended) head. I bow to you, falling on the ground. O reverend one, besought by you, I shall be undone. I do not deserve to be forgiven by you.

verses.sanskrit:
नैषा हि सा स्त्री भवति श्लाघनीयेन धीमता
उभयोर्लोकयोर्वीर पत्या या संप्रसाद्यते
verses.transliteration:
naiṣā hi sā strī bhavati ślāghanīyena dhīmatā
ubhayorlokayorvīra patyā yā saṁprasādyate

translations.english: She cannot be reckoned a gentlewoman, who is propitiated by her intelligent husband, worthy of being extolled in both worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
जानामि धर्मं धर्मज्ञ त्वां जाने सत्यवादिनम्
पुत्रशोकार्तया तत्तु मया किमपि भाषितम्
verses.transliteration:
jānāmi dharmaṁ dharmajña tvāṁ jāne satyavādinam
putraśokārtayā tattu mayā kimapi bhāṣitam

translations.english: I know duty, O righteous one; I know that you are truth-telling. And it is because I was exceedingly distressed on account of my son that I spoke harshly to you.

verses.sanskrit:
शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्
शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः
verses.transliteration:
śoko nāśayate dhairyaṁ śoko nāśayate śrutam
śoko nāśayate sarvaṁ nāsti śokasamo ripuḥ

translations.english: Sorrow destroys patience, sorrow destroys knowledge of the scriptures, sorrow destroys every things; there is no enemy like to sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
शयमापतितः सोढुं प्रहरो रिपुहस्ततः
सोढुमापतितः शोकः सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि न शक्यते
verses.transliteration:
śayamāpatitaḥ soḍhuṁ praharo ripuhastataḥ
soḍhumāpatitaḥ śokaḥ susūkṣmo'pi na śakyate

translations.english: One can falling down bear ever beating from an enemy; but one cannot falling down bear ever so little sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
वनवासाय रामस्य पञ्चरात्रोऽद्य गण्यते
यः शोकहतहर्षायाः पञ्चवर्षोपमो मम
verses.transliteration:
vanavāsāya rāmasya pañcarātro'dya gaṇyate
yaḥ śokahataharṣāyāḥ pañcavarṣopamo mama

translations.english: This is the fifth night of the banishment of Rāma, as calculated by me; and to me rendered cheerless by sorrow, this interval has assumed the proportions of five years.

verses.sanskrit:
तं हि चिन्तयमानायाः शोकोऽयं हृदि वर्धते
अदीनामिव वेगेन समुद्रसलिलं महत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ hi cintayamānāyāḥ śoko'yaṁ hṛdi vardhate
adīnāmiva vegena samudrasalilaṁ mahat

translations.english: And fostered by thought on my part, this grief increases in my bosom, like the mighty waters of the ocean increased by the vehement discharge of rivers.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ प्रह्लादितो वाक्यैर्देव्या कौसल्यया नृपः
शोकेन च समाक्रान्तो निद्राया वशमेयिवान्
verses.transliteration:
atha prahlādito vākyairdevyā kausalyayā nṛpaḥ
śokena ca samākrānto nidrāyā vaśameyivān

translations.english: As Kausalyā was thus speaking auspiciously, the rays of the sun grew milder, and the night arrived. Cheered up by the words of Kausalya, the king overcome by grief, felt the influence of sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिबुद्धो मुहुर्तेन शोकोपहतचेतनः
अथ राजा दशरथः स चिन्तामभ्यपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
pratibuddho muhurtena śokopahatacetanaḥ
atha rājā daśarathaḥ sa cintāmabhyapadyata

translations.english: Starting in a moment from sleep, king Dasaratha deprived (almost) of his consciousness by grief, (again) became a prey to thought.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चैव विवासाद्वासवोपमम्
आविवेशोपसर्गस्तं तमः सूर्यमिवासुरम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇayoścaiva vivāsādvāsavopamam
āviveśopasargastaṁ tamaḥ sūryamivāsuram

translations.english: I consequence of the exile of Rāma and Laks mana, the king resembling Våsava was overpowered by grief, like the darkness of Rāhu enveloping the sun. was own

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा रजनीं षष्ठीं रामे प्रव्रजिते वनम्
अर्धरात्रे दशरथः संस्मरन्दुष्कृतं कृतम्
कौसल्यां पुत्रशोकार्तामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā rajanīṁ ṣaṣṭhīṁ rāme pravrajite vanam
ardharātre daśarathaḥ saṁsmaranduṣkṛtaṁ kṛtam
kausalyāṁ putraśokārtāmidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And on the sixth night after Rāma had repaired to the forest, the king Dasaratha, when it midnight, remembered his unrighteous act.

verses.sanskrit:
यदाचरति कल्याणि शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्
तदेव लभते भद्रे कर्ता कर्मजमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
yadācarati kalyāṇi śubhaṁ vā yadi vāśubham
tadeva labhate bhadre kartā karmajamātmanaḥ

translations.english: As are the actions of one, O auspicious one, whether good otherwise, the consequences, O gentle lady, reaped by the doer of them.

verses.sanskrit:
गुरु लाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्
दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते
verses.transliteration:
guru lāghavamarthānāmārambhe karmaṇāṁ phalam
doṣaṁ vā yo na jānāti sa bāla iti hocyate

translations.english: He that on the eve of beginning an action either relating to this world or the next, does not take into consideration the fact that actions entail consequences light or grave, disagreeable (or otherwise), is styled a child.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्चिदाम्रवणं छित्त्वा पलाशांश्च निषिञ्चति
पुष्पं दृष्ट्वा फले गृध्नुः स शोचति फलागमे
verses.transliteration:
kaścidāmravaṇaṁ chittvā palāśāṁśca niṣiñcati
puṣpaṁ dṛṣṭvā phale gṛdhnuḥ sa śocati phalāgame

translations.english: He that cutting down a mango grove, waters Palasa trees, beholding the flowers (blooming), will covet fruits; and grieve when their season arrives. The person that without apprehending (the principle of causation) rushed to action, grieves at the season of fruits, even like him that waters kinsuka trees (hewing down his mango grove). or are

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहमाम्रवणं छित्त्वा पलाशांश्च न्यषेचयम्
रामं फलागमे त्यक्त्वा पश्चाच्छोचामि दुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
so'hamāmravaṇaṁ chittvā palāśāṁśca nyaṣecayam
rāmaṁ phalāgame tyaktvā paścācchocāmi durmatiḥ

translations.english: And is this way, I fool that I am having hewn down my grove of mangoes and watered Palāsas, having renounced Räma in the season of fruit, is grieving in the end.

verses.sanskrit:
लब्धशब्देन कौसल्ये कुमारेण धनुष्मता
कुमारः शब्दवेधीति मया पापमिदं कृतम्
तदिदं मेऽनुसंप्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
labdhaśabdena kausalye kumāreṇa dhanuṣmatā
kumāraḥ śabdavedhīti mayā pāpamidaṁ kṛtam
tadidaṁ me'nusaṁprāptaṁ devi duḥkhaṁ svayaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: Having, O Kausalyā, earned the expression, 'The Prince can pierce his aim by sound alone,', I, a prince and bowman, did this offence.

verses.sanskrit:
संमोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद्भक्षितं विषम्
एवं ममाप्यविज्ञातं शब्दवेध्यमयं फलम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁmohādiha bālena yathā syādbhakṣitaṁ viṣam
evaṁ mamāpyavijñātaṁ śabdavedhyamayaṁ phalam

translations.english: Therefore, O noble dame, I have myself brought this misfortune on me, like a child who has eaten poison through ignorance.

verses.sanskrit:
देव्यनूढा त्वमभवो युवराजो भवाम्यहम्
ततः प्रावृडनुप्राप्ता मदकामविवर्धिनी
verses.transliteration:
devyanūḍhā tvamabhavo yuvarājo bhavāmyaham
tataḥ prāvṛḍanuprāptā madakāmavivardhinī

translations.english: O lady, you were then unwedded; and I was a youthful prince. And it was at this time that the rainy season increasing my desire set in.

verses.sanskrit:
उपास्यहि रसान्भौमांस्तप्त्वा च जगदंशुभिः
परेताचरितां भीमां रविराविशते दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
upāsyahi rasānbhaumāṁstaptvā ca jagadaṁśubhiḥ
paretācaritāṁ bhīmāṁ ravirāviśate diśam

translations.english: Drawing moisture from the ground and heated the earth by his rays, the Sun goes to the dreadful quarter whither repair the dead.

verses.sanskrit:
उष्णमन्तर्दधे सद्यः स्निग्धा ददृशिरे घनाः
ततो जहृषिरे सर्वे भेकसारङ्गबर्हिणः
verses.transliteration:
uṣṇamantardadhe sadyaḥ snigdhā dadṛśire ghanāḥ
tato jahṛṣire sarve bhekasāraṅgabarhiṇaḥ

translations.english: The heat was immediately dispelled, and the gelid clouds snowed themselves; and frogs and Sārangas and peacocks began to rejoice; and, finding it unpleasant, the feathered ones bathed and with the surface of their plumage shrunk up from the wet, took refuge in trees shaken by the wind and rain.

verses.sanskrit:
पतितेनाम्भसा छन्नः पतमानेन चासकृत्
आबभौ मत्तसारङ्गस्तोयराशिरिवाचलः
verses.transliteration:
patitenāmbhasā channaḥ patamānena cāsakṛt
ābabhau mattasāraṅgastoyarāśirivācalaḥ

translations.english: And the hill graced by maddened Sārangas, covered by showers falling simultaneously looked like a mass of waters.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्नतिसुखे काले धनुष्मानिषुमान्रथी
व्यायाम कृतसंकल्पः सरयूमन्वगां नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminnatisukhe kāle dhanuṣmāniṣumānrathī
vyāyāma kṛtasaṁkalpaḥ sarayūmanvagāṁ nadīm

translations.english: At such a sweet hour, I intent upon taking exercise, taking my bow and arrows and mounted on my car, sallied out for the river Sarayū, with the intention that I with my senses under control, should in the watery expense slay any buffalo, elephant, or any other beast that mighty have come there in the night.

verses.sanskrit:
अथान्धकारे त्वश्रौषं जले कुम्भस्य पर्यतः
अचक्षुर्विषये घोषं वारणस्येव नर्दतः
verses.transliteration:
athāndhakāre tvaśrauṣaṁ jale kumbhasya paryataḥ
acakṣurviṣaye ghoṣaṁ vāraṇasyeva nardataḥ

translations.english: And (coming there) while it was so dark that: nothing could be discovered, I heard sounds of a filling pitcher proceeding from the waters; resembling the roars of an elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र वागुषसि व्यक्ता प्रादुरासीद्वनौकसः
हा हेति पततस्तोये वागभूत्तत्र मानुषी
कथमस्मद्विधे शस्त्रं निपतेत्तु तपस्विनि
verses.transliteration:
tatra vāguṣasi vyaktā prādurāsīdvanaukasaḥ
hā heti patatastoye vāgabhūttatra mānuṣī
kathamasmadvidhe śastraṁ nipatettu tapasvini

translations.english: Thereupon from the spot whereto the sharpened shaft resembling a poisonous snake had been discharged by me in the twilight, proceeded cries of 'Oh' and 'Alas' uttered by a forester pierced to the quick by the arrow, and falling into the water. And when he had dropped down, words spoken by a human being became audible.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविविक्तां नदीं रात्रावुदाहारोऽहमागतः
इषुणाभिहतः केन कस्य वा किं कृतं मया
verses.transliteration:
praviviktāṁ nadīṁ rātrāvudāhāro'hamāgataḥ
iṣuṇābhihataḥ kena kasya vā kiṁ kṛtaṁ mayā

translations.english: Why does the weapon light upon me? I had come to this lone stream for procuring water.

verses.sanskrit:
जटाभारधरस्यैव वल्कलाजिनवाससः
को वधेन ममार्थी स्यात्किं वास्यापकृतं मया
verses.transliteration:
jaṭābhāradharasyaiva valkalājinavāsasaḥ
ko vadhena mamārthī syātkiṁ vāsyāpakṛtaṁ mayā

translations.english: By whom have I been wounded by this arrow? To whom have I done wrong? And how can the slaying of one like me bearing a load of matted locks, and wearing bark and deer-skin, who subsist on what the forest yields and never injures others, be sanctioned by the scriptures? Who can serve any purpose by slaying me? And how can I have injured such an one? Such a purposeless act cannot but end in evil.

verses.sanskrit:
तं गिरं करुणां श्रुत्वा मम धर्मानुकाङ्क्षिणः
कराभ्यां सशरं चापं व्यथितस्यापतद्भुवि
verses.transliteration:
taṁ giraṁ karuṇāṁ śrutvā mama dharmānukāṅkṣiṇaḥ
karābhyāṁ saśaraṁ cāpaṁ vyathitasyāpatadbhuvi

translations.english: Hearing his piteous words, I ever anxious to follow virtue, was exceedingly pained, and the bow with its arrow fixed fell down from my hand to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स मामुद्वीक्ष्य नेत्राभ्यां त्रस्तमस्वस्थचेतसम्
इत्युवाच वचः क्रूरं दिधक्षन्निव तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
sa māmudvīkṣya netrābhyāṁ trastamasvasthacetasam
ityuvāca vacaḥ krūraṁ didhakṣanniva tejasā

translations.english: Hearing in the night, the pathetic words of the saint thus lamenting, I became frightened, and was deprived of my senses through excess of grief. And coming to the quarter, I exceedingly unnerved and with an excited mind, discovered on the banks of the Sarayū an ascetic wounded with a shaft, with his matted locks scattered about, his pitcher of water lying by, his body smeared with blood and dust and afflicted by the dare. Gazing with his eyes at me who was extremely agitated and ill at ease, he said these words sternly, as if consuming me with his energy.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तवापकृतं राजन्वने निवसता मया
जिहीर्षुरम्भो गुर्वर्थं यदहं ताडितस्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tavāpakṛtaṁ rājanvane nivasatā mayā
jihīrṣurambho gurvarthaṁ yadahaṁ tāḍitastvayā

translations.english: What wrong, O monarch, had I residing in the woods done you, that coming to procure water for my parents, I have been thus afflicted by. you?

verses.sanskrit:
एकेन खलु बाणेन मर्मण्यभिहते मयि
द्वावन्धौ निहतौ वृद्धौ माता जनयिता च मे
verses.transliteration:
ekena khalu bāṇena marmaṇyabhihate mayi
dvāvandhau nihatau vṛddhau mātā janayitā ca me

translations.english: By piercing my marrow with a shaft, you have slain both my aged and blind father and mother.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ नूनं दुर्बलावन्धौ मत्प्रतीक्षौ पिपासितौ
चिरमाशाकृतां तृष्णां कष्टां संधारयिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
tau nūnaṁ durbalāvandhau matpratīkṣau pipāsitau
ciramāśākṛtāṁ tṛṣṇāṁ kaṣṭāṁ saṁdhārayiṣyataḥ

translations.english: Surely, they feeble and blind, who afflicted by thirst are remaining in expectation of me, will now bear (the stress and tension of) the expectation as well as the parching thirst.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं तपसो वास्ति फलयोगः श्रुतस्य वा
पिता यन्मां न जानाति शयानं पतितं भुवि
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ tapaso vāsti phalayogaḥ śrutasya vā
pitā yanmāṁ na jānāti śayānaṁ patitaṁ bhuvi

translations.english: Surely asceticism and study carry no fruit with them, since I lying low on the ground, my father knows nothing about it.

verses.sanskrit:
जानन्नपि च किं कुर्यादशक्तिरपरिक्रमः
भिद्यमानमिवाशक्तस्त्रातुमन्यो नगो नगम्
verses.transliteration:
jānannapi ca kiṁ kuryādaśaktiraparikramaḥ
bhidyamānamivāśaktastrātumanyo nago nagam

translations.english: And what could he do, even if he knew it, being as he is incapable and unable to go about? One tree cannot rescue another that is being battered (by the winds).

verses.sanskrit:
पितुस्त्वमेव मे गत्वा शीघ्रमाचक्ष्व राघव
न त्वामनुदहेत्क्रुद्धो वनं वह्निरिवैधितः
verses.transliteration:
pitustvameva me gatvā śīghramācakṣva rāghava
na tvāmanudahetkruddho vanaṁ vahnirivaidhitaḥ

translations.english: Do you, O descendant of Raghu, yourself going to my father, speedily inform of him this that has occurred. But take care that like a fire waxing furious consuming a woods, he in his ire do not burn you.

verses.sanskrit:
इयमेकपदी राजन्यतो मे पितुराश्रमः
तं प्रसादय गत्वा त्वं न त्वां स कुपितः शपेत्
verses.transliteration:
iyamekapadī rājanyato me piturāśramaḥ
taṁ prasādaya gatvā tvaṁ na tvāṁ sa kupitaḥ śapet

translations.english: This narrow way, O king, will lead you to my father's dwelling. Do you going there, pacify him, so that getting wroth he may not curse you.

verses.sanskrit:
विशल्यं कुरु मां राजन्मर्म मे निशितः शरः
रुणद्धि मृदु सोत्सेधं तीरमम्बुरयो यथा
verses.transliteration:
viśalyaṁ kuru māṁ rājanmarma me niśitaḥ śaraḥ
ruṇaddhi mṛdu sotsedhaṁ tīramamburayo yathā

translations.english: Do you (now), O king, take out the arrow. Your sharpened shaft afflicts my marrow, like the tide of a river wearing away a hollowheaving sand bank.

verses.sanskrit:
जलार्द्रगात्रं तु विलप्य कृच्छा;न्मर्मव्रणं संततमुच्छसन्तम्
ततः सरय्वां तमहं शयानं; समीक्ष्य भद्रे सुभृशं विषण्णः
verses.transliteration:
jalārdragātraṁ tu vilapya kṛcchā;nmarmavraṇaṁ saṁtatamucchasantam
tataḥ sarayvāṁ tamahaṁ śayānaṁ; samīkṣya bhadre subhṛśaṁ viṣaṇṇaḥ

translations.english: On beholding him with his body dripping with water, and mortally wounded, and breathing hard without respite, after he had bewailed his mortal wound, lying on the banks of the Sarayü, I lamented him and was, O gentle lady, greatly aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
तदज्ञानान्महत्पापं कृत्वा संकुलितेन्द्रियः
एकस्त्वचिन्तयं बुद्ध्या कथं नु सुकृतं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
tadajñānānmahatpāpaṁ kṛtvā saṁkulitendriyaḥ
ekastvacintayaṁ buddhyā kathaṁ nu sukṛtaṁ bhavet

translations.english: Having unwittingly committed that great sin, I, with my senses oppressed through grief, thought within myself as to how I could mend it.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं घटमादय पूर्णं परमवारिणा
आश्रमं तमहं प्राप्य यथाख्यातपथं गतः
