verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ ghaṭamādaya pūrṇaṁ paramavāriṇā
āśramaṁ tamahaṁ prāpya yathākhyātapathaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Then taking up the pitcher filled with excellent water, I went by the way mentioned and (at last) reached the asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्राहं दुर्बलावन्धौ वृद्धावपरिणायकौ
अपश्यं तस्य पितरौ लूनपक्षाविव द्विजौ
verses.transliteration:
tatrāhaṁ durbalāvandhau vṛddhāvapariṇāyakau
apaśyaṁ tasya pitarau lūnapakṣāviva dvijau

translations.english: There I found his aged, infirm, forlorn, parents, without any one to help them in moving about, like to birds whose wings have been severed, keeping up a talk about (their son) without experiencing any fatigue, and like helpless ones feeding on a hope which had been blasted by me.

verses.sanskrit:
पदशब्दं तु मे श्रुत्वा मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत
किं चिरायसि मे पुत्र पानीयं क्षिप्रमानय
verses.transliteration:
padaśabdaṁ tu me śrutvā munirvākyamabhāṣata
kiṁ cirāyasi me putra pānīyaṁ kṣipramānaya

translations.english: Hearing my footsteps, the ascetic said, “Why, my son, delay you? Bring the drink at once.

verses.sanskrit:
यन्निमित्तमिदं तात सलिले क्रीडितं त्वया
उत्कण्ठिता ते मातेयं प्रविश क्षिप्रमाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
yannimittamidaṁ tāta salile krīḍitaṁ tvayā
utkaṇṭhitā te māteyaṁ praviśa kṣipramāśramam

translations.english: Your mother, O child, was exceedingly anxious in consequence of your sporting in the waters. Do you speedily enter the asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्व्यलीकं कृतं पुत्र मात्रा ते यदि वा मया
न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं त्वया तात तपस्विना
verses.transliteration:
yadvyalīkaṁ kṛtaṁ putra mātrā te yadi vā mayā
na tanmanasi kartavyaṁ tvayā tāta tapasvinā

translations.english: O child, it behove you not to take to heart any unkind action that, O son, may have been done to you of high fame either by your mother or myself.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं गतिस्त्वगतीनां च चक्षुस्त्वं हीनचक्षुषाम्
समासक्तास्त्वयि प्राणाः किंचिन्नौ नाभिभाषसे
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ gatistvagatīnāṁ ca cakṣustvaṁ hīnacakṣuṣām
samāsaktāstvayi prāṇāḥ kiṁcinnau nābhibhāṣase

translations.english: You are the resource of these helpless ones; you are the eyes of these bereft of their sight. was Our lives are bound up with you. Why do not answer?'

verses.sanskrit:
मुनिमव्यक्तया वाचा तमहं सज्जमानया
हीनव्यञ्जनया प्रेक्ष्य भीतो भीत इवाब्रुवम्
verses.transliteration:
munimavyaktayā vācā tamahaṁ sajjamānayā
hīnavyañjanayā prekṣya bhīto bhīta ivābruvam

translations.english: Seeing the ascetic with a choked utterance indistinctly speaking thus with the letters not articulated clearly, I, dashed in spirits, yet concealing the real state of my mind by assuming a doughty tongue, communicated to him the danger that had befallen him in consequence of the calamity of his son:

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रियोऽहं दशरथो नाहं पुत्रो महात्मनः
सज्जनावमतं दुःखमिदं प्राप्तं स्वकर्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣatriyo'haṁ daśaratho nāhaṁ putro mahātmanaḥ
sajjanāvamataṁ duḥkhamidaṁ prāptaṁ svakarmajam

translations.english: I am a Ksatriya, Dasaratha (by name), and no son of yours, O magnanimous one. I have come by a misfortune in consequence of an act blamed by the good.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवंश्चापहस्तोऽहं सरयूतीरमागतः
जिघांसुः श्वापदं किंचिन्निपाने वागतं गजम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavaṁścāpahasto'haṁ sarayūtīramāgataḥ
jighāṁsuḥ śvāpadaṁ kiṁcinnipāne vāgataṁ gajam

translations.english: O revered one, desirous of killing some beast of prey, and elephant (or some other), come to the waters, I went to the banks of the Sarayū bow in hand.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र श्रुतो मया शब्दो जले कुम्भस्य पूर्यतः
द्विपोऽयमिति मत्वा हि बाणेनाभिहतो मया
verses.transliteration:
tatra śruto mayā śabdo jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ
dvipo'yamiti matvā hi bāṇenābhihato mayā

translations.english: Then hearing sounds from the water of a filling pitcher, I thought, This must be an elephant. I wounded it with a shaft. Next coming to the edge of the river, I saw an ascetic lying down on the ground almost deprived of life, with his heart pierced with an arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
स चोद्धृतेन बाणेन तत्रैव स्वर्गमास्थितः
भगवन्तावुभौ शोचन्नन्धाविति विलप्य च
verses.transliteration:
sa coddhṛtena bāṇena tatraiva svargamāsthitaḥ
bhagavantāvubhau śocannandhāviti vilapya ca

translations.english: And as soon as the arrow had been extracted, he ascended heaven, O reverend sir, lamenting and bewailing you, both grown old.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानाद्भवतः पुत्रः सहसाभिहतो मया
शेषमेवंगते यत्स्यात्तत्प्रसीदतु मे मुनिः
verses.transliteration:
ajñānādbhavataḥ putraḥ sahasābhihato mayā
śeṣamevaṁgate yatsyāttatprasīdatu me muniḥ

translations.english: It is through ignorance that I suddenly wounded your son. This having been past, do you favour me with telling me what is now to be done, O ascetic.

verses.sanskrit:
स तच्छ्रुत्वा वचः क्रूरं निःश्वसञ्शोककर्शितः
मामुवाच महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tacchrutvā vacaḥ krūraṁ niḥśvasañśokakarśitaḥ
māmuvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam

translations.english: With eyes flooded with tears, and well nigh deprived of his senses by grief, that highly energetic one said to me standing with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्येतदशुभं कर्म न स्म मे कथयेः स्वयम्
फलेन्मूर्धा स्म ते राजन्सद्यः शतसहस्रधा
verses.transliteration:
yadyetadaśubhaṁ karma na sma me kathayeḥ svayam
phalenmūrdhā sma te rājansadyaḥ śatasahasradhā

translations.english: If, O king, you had not of yourself immediately communicated to us this unpleasant news, your head would have been reduced to a thousand flaws.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रियेण वधो राजन्वानप्रस्थे विशेषतः
ज्ञानपूर्वं कृतः स्थानाच्च्यावयेदपि वज्रिणम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣatriyeṇa vadho rājanvānaprasthe viśeṣataḥ
jñānapūrvaṁ kṛtaḥ sthānāccyāvayedapi vajriṇam

translations.english: Not to speak of Kștriyas, I can even drag the very wielder of the thunderbolt himself from his position, if he knowingly kills one, in especial, that has assumed the Vånaprastha mode of life.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानाद्धि कृतं यस्मादिदं तेनैव जीवसि
अपि ह्यद्य कुलं नस्याद्राघवाणां कुतो भवान्
verses.transliteration:
ajñānāddhi kṛtaṁ yasmādidaṁ tenaiva jīvasi
api hyadya kulaṁ nasyādrāghavāṇāṁ kuto bhavān

translations.english: It is because you have done this through ignorance that you (still) live, else the race itself of the Rāghavas should be not, and where are you?

verses.sanskrit:
नय नौ नृप तं देशमिति मां चाभ्यभाषत
अद्य तं द्रष्टुमिच्छावः पुत्रं पश्चिमदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
naya nau nṛpa taṁ deśamiti māṁ cābhyabhāṣata
adya taṁ draṣṭumicchāvaḥ putraṁ paścimadarśanam

translations.english: He then said, 'Do you, o king, take us to the scene. To day will we look our last on our son besmeared with blood, his deer-skin garb falling off (from his body), lying senseless on the earth, and come under the subjection of the lord of righteousness.'

verses.sanskrit:
अथाहमेकस्तं देशं नीत्वा तौ भृशदुःखितौ
अस्पर्शयमहं पुत्रं तं मुनिं सह भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
athāhamekastaṁ deśaṁ nītvā tau bhṛśaduḥkhitau
asparśayamahaṁ putraṁ taṁ muniṁ saha bhāryayā

translations.english: Thereupon I alone taking them exceedingly disconsolate to the spot, made the ascetic and his wife touch their son.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ पुत्रमात्मनः स्पृष्ट्वा तमासाद्य तपस्विनौ
निपेततुः शरीरेऽस्य पिता चास्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tau putramātmanaḥ spṛṣṭvā tamāsādya tapasvinau
nipetatuḥ śarīre'sya pitā cāsyedamabravīt

translations.english: And having approached their son and touched him, ascetics fell on his person, and then his father addressed him thus.

verses.sanskrit:
न न्वहं ते प्रियः पुत्र मातरं पश्य धार्मिक
किं नु नालिङ्गसे पुत्र सुकुमार वचो वद
verses.transliteration:
na nvahaṁ te priyaḥ putra mātaraṁ paśya dhārmika
kiṁ nu nāliṅgase putra sukumāra vaco vada

translations.english: If, my son, you do not feel kindly to me, do you look up to your virtuous mother. And why, O son, do you not embrace me? Do you speak tender words.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य वापररात्रेऽहं श्रोष्यामि हृदयंगमम्
अधीयानस्य मधुरं शास्त्रं वान्यद्विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
kasya vāpararātre'haṁ śroṣyāmi hṛdayaṁgamam
adhīyānasya madhuraṁ śāstraṁ vānyadviśeṣataḥ

translations.english: At the small hours, form whom engaged in study, shall I hear the scriptures sweetly read in a way coming home to the listener's mind?

verses.sanskrit:
को मां संध्यामुपास्यैव स्नात्वा हुतहुताशनः
श्लाघयिष्यत्युपासीनः पुत्रशोकभयार्दितम्
verses.transliteration:
ko māṁ saṁdhyāmupāsyaiva snātvā hutahutāśanaḥ
ślāghayiṣyatyupāsīnaḥ putraśokabhayārditam

translations.english: Who, having performed his daily devotions and offered oblation to the sacrificial fire, will bathe me, afflicted with grief for my son?

verses.sanskrit:
कन्दमूलफलं हृत्वा को मां प्रियमिवातिथिम्
भोजयिष्यत्यकर्मण्यमप्रग्रहमनायकम्
verses.transliteration:
kandamūlaphalaṁ hṛtvā ko māṁ priyamivātithim
bhojayiṣyatyakarmaṇyamapragrahamanāyakam

translations.english: Who procuring Kandas, fruits and roots, will feed me like an welcome guest, incapable of and doing anything and furnishing provisions, and without any one to take care of myself.?

verses.sanskrit:
इमामन्धां च वृद्धां च मातरं ते तपस्विनीम्
कथं पुत्र भरिष्यामि कृपणां पुत्रगर्धिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
imāmandhāṁ ca vṛddhāṁ ca mātaraṁ te tapasvinīm
kathaṁ putra bhariṣyāmi kṛpaṇāṁ putragardhinīm

translations.english: And, my son, how will I maintain this blind ascetic mother of yours, proud of her son, who is passing her days in misery?

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ मा मा गमः पुत्र यमस्य सदनं प्रति
श्वो मया सह गन्तासि जनन्या च समेधितः
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha mā mā gamaḥ putra yamasya sadanaṁ prati
śvo mayā saha gantāsi jananyā ca samedhitaḥ

translations.english: Do you stay my son, in my behalf. Tomorrow you will go to Yama's mansion with me and your mother.

verses.sanskrit:
उभावपि च शोकार्तावनाथौ कृपणौ वने
क्षिप्रमेव गमिष्यावस्त्वया हीनौ यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
ubhāvapi ca śokārtāvanāthau kṛpaṇau vane
kṣiprameva gamiṣyāvastvayā hīnau yamakṣayam

translations.english: Distressed with grief and rendered miserable in the forest, both of us deprived of you shall soon repair to the abode of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वैवस्वतं दृष्ट्वा तं प्रवक्ष्यामि भारतीम्
क्षमतां धर्मराजो मे बिभृयात्पितरावयम्
verses.transliteration:
tato vaivasvataṁ dṛṣṭvā taṁ pravakṣyāmi bhāratīm
kṣamatāṁ dharmarājo me bibhṛyātpitarāvayam

translations.english: Seeing Vivasvata's son, I will say to him, Do you, O lord of justice forgive me, and let this my son, continue to maintain us, his parents.

verses.sanskrit:
अपापोऽसि यथा पुत्र निहतः पापकर्मणा
तेन सत्येन गच्छाशु ये लोकाः शस्त्रयोधिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
apāpo'si yathā putra nihataḥ pāpakarmaṇā
tena satyena gacchāśu ye lokāḥ śastrayodhinām

translations.english: You, my son, are sinless, although slain by this one who has done an unrighteous act; and by the force of this truth, do you repair to the world of warriors. Do you, O son, go the supreme way that is gone by heroes who without turning back from the fight, are slain in open encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
यां गतिं सगरः शैब्यो दिलीपो जनमेजयः
नहुषो धुन्धुमारश्च प्राप्तास्तां गच्छ पुत्रक
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ gatiṁ sagaraḥ śaibyo dilīpo janamejayaḥ
nahuṣo dhundhumāraśca prāptāstāṁ gaccha putraka

translations.english: Do you, O son, go the way that has been gone by Sagara and Saivya and Dilīpa and Janamejaya and Nahusa and Dhundhumāra.

verses.sanskrit:
गोसहस्रप्रदातॄणां या या गुरुभृतामपि
देहन्यासकृतां या च तां गतिं गच्छ पुत्रक
न हि त्वस्मिन्कुले जातो गच्छत्यकुशलां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
gosahasrapradātṝṇāṁ yā yā gurubhṛtāmapi
dehanyāsakṛtāṁ yā ca tāṁ gatiṁ gaccha putraka
na hi tvasminkule jāto gacchatyakuśalāṁ gatim

translations.english: Do you, O son, go the way that is gone by all creatures, even by ascetics engaged in the study of the Veda, by bestowers of lands, by those performing fire-sacrifices, by individuals each devoted to a single wife, men giving away a thousand kine, persons tending their preceptors, and individuals renouncing lives by fasting.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स कृपणं तत्र पर्यदेवयतासकृत्
ततोऽस्मै कर्तुमुदकं प्रवृत्तः सह भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa kṛpaṇaṁ tatra paryadevayatāsakṛt
tato'smai kartumudakaṁ pravṛttaḥ saha bhāryayā

translations.english: Having thus piteously wept, he along with his wife set about performing the watery rites on behalf of his son.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दिव्येन रूपेण मुनिपुत्रः स्वकर्मभिः
आश्वास्य च मुहूर्तं तु पितरौ वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu divyena rūpeṇa muniputraḥ svakarmabhiḥ
āśvāsya ca muhūrtaṁ tu pitarau vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon speedily assuming a celestial shape, the virtuous son of the ascetic by his own actions ascended heaven in company with Sakra.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थानमस्मि महत्प्राप्तो भवतोः परिचारणात्
भवन्तावपि च क्षिप्रं मम मूलमुपैष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
sthānamasmi mahatprāpto bhavatoḥ paricāraṇāt
bhavantāvapi ca kṣipraṁ mama mūlamupaiṣyataḥ

translations.english: I have attained a high state in consequence of having served you. Do you also without delay come to me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु दिव्येन विमानेन वपुष्मता
आरुरोह दिवं क्षिप्रं मुनिपुत्रो जितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu divyena vimānena vapuṣmatā
āruroha divaṁ kṣipraṁ muniputro jitendriyaḥ

translations.english: Having said this, the ascetic's son of restrained sense ascended heaven by means of an excellent and commodious car.

verses.sanskrit:
स कृत्वा तूदकं तूर्णं तापसः सह भार्यया
मामुवाच महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa kṛtvā tūdakaṁ tūrṇaṁ tāpasaḥ saha bhāryayā
māmuvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam

translations.english: Having performed the watery rites, the highly energetic ascetic along with his wife speedily said to me staying with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यैव जहि मां राजन्मरणे नास्ति मे व्यथा
यच्छरेणैकपुत्रं मां त्वमकार्षीरपुत्रकम्
verses.transliteration:
adyaiva jahi māṁ rājanmaraṇe nāsti me vyathā
yacchareṇaikaputraṁ māṁ tvamakārṣīraputrakam

translations.english: Do you, O monarch, slay me on the instant. I do not grieve to die', you have by your shaft rendered me who had an only son, absolutely sonless.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रव्यसनजं दुःखं यदेतन्मम साम्प्रतम्
एवं त्वं पुत्रशोकेन राजन्कालं करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
putravyasanajaṁ duḥkhaṁ yadetanmama sāmpratam
evaṁ tvaṁ putraśokena rājankālaṁ kariṣyasi

translations.english: Since this sorrow arising from the calamity that has befallen my son, is at present mine (through your instrumentality), I curse you. You shall even in this way find your death from grief born of separation from your son.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्मामागतं भद्रे तस्योदारस्य तद्वचः
यदहं पुत्रशोकेन संत्यक्ष्याम्यद्य जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
tasmānmāmāgataṁ bhadre tasyodārasya tadvacaḥ
yadahaṁ putraśokena saṁtyakṣyāmyadya jīvitam

translations.english: O exalted lady, even as a disease generated by one's taking rice with unhealthy curry, this danger is imminent in consequence of that act. O gentle one, the words of that noble-minded person are about to be verified in me.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्षुषा त्वां न पश्यामि स्मृतिर्मम विलुप्यते
दूता वैवस्वतस्यैते कौसल्ये त्वरयन्ति माम्
verses.transliteration:
cakṣuṣā tvāṁ na paśyāmi smṛtirmama vilupyate
dūtā vaivasvatasyaite kausalye tvarayanti mām

translations.english: But I do not see you with my eyes, and my memory fails. These envoys of Vivasvata's son, OKausalya, urge speed upon me.

verses.sanskrit:
अतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदहं जीवितक्षये
न हि पश्यामि धर्मज्ञं रामं सत्यपराक्यमम्
verses.transliteration:
atastu kiṁ duḥkhataraṁ yadahaṁ jīvitakṣaye
na hi paśyāmi dharmajñaṁ rāmaṁ satyaparākyamam

translations.english: What can be an object of greater regret than that I during my last moments cannot behold the righteous Rāma having truth for prowess?

verses.sanskrit:
न ते मनुष्या देवास्ते ये चारुशुभकुण्डलम्
मुखं द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य वर्षे पञ्चदशे पुनः
verses.transliteration:
na te manuṣyā devāste ye cāruśubhakuṇḍalam
mukhaṁ drakṣyanti rāmasya varṣe pañcadaśe punaḥ

translations.english: Those are not men, those are gods who in the fifteenth year shall again behold Rāma's countenance graced with elegant and burnished ear-rings.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणं सुभ्रु सुदंष्ट्रं चारुनासिकम्
धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य ताराधिपनिभं मुखम्
verses.transliteration:
padmapatrekṣaṇaṁ subhru sudaṁṣṭraṁ cārunāsikam
dhanyā drakṣyanti rāmasya tārādhipanibhaṁ mukham

translations.english: O you of graceful eye-brows, blessed are they who shall behold Rāma's countenance furnished with eyes resembling lotus-petals, with excellent teeth and a shapely nose, like to the lord of the stars himself.

verses.sanskrit:
निवृत्तवनवासं तमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्
द्रक्ष्यन्ति सुखिनो रामं शुक्रं मार्गगतं यथा
verses.transliteration:
nivṛttavanavāsaṁ tamayodhyāṁ punarāgatam
drakṣyanti sukhino rāmaṁ śukraṁ mārgagataṁ yathā

translations.english: Blessed are they that shall behold that fragrant face of his like to the autumnal moon, or the fullblown lotus. Thrice-blessed they who with delighted hearts, shall behold Rāma returned from the forest and come back to Ayodhyā, like to Sukra crowning the zenith?

verses.sanskrit:
अयमात्मभवः शोको मामनाथमचेतनम्
संसादयति वेगेन यथा कूलं नदीरयः
verses.transliteration:
ayamātmabhavaḥ śoko māmanāthamacetanam
saṁsādayati vegena yathā kūlaṁ nadīrayaḥ

translations.english: As the violence of a river wears away its banks, my grief occasioned through my own agency is destroying me, who am helpless and insensible.

verses.sanskrit:
हा राघव महाबाहो हा ममायास नाशन
राजा दशरथः शोचञ्जीवितान्तमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
hā rāghava mahābāho hā mamāyāsa nāśana
rājā daśarathaḥ śocañjīvitāntamupāgamat

translations.english: Having thus lamented in presence of Rāma's mother and Sumitrā, king Daſaratha breathed his last.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु दीनं कथयन्नराधिपः; प्रियस्य पुत्रस्य विवासनातुरः
गतेऽर्धरात्रे भृशदुःखपीडित;स्तदा जहौ प्राणमुदारदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu dīnaṁ kathayannarādhipaḥ; priyasya putrasya vivāsanāturaḥ
gate'rdharātre bhṛśaduḥkhapīḍita;stadā jahau prāṇamudāradarśanaḥ

translations.english: Thus that distressed lord of men, smitten with 1e exile of his beloved son, that one possessed fa gracious presence, when the night had been alf spent, wrought up with the violence of his notion, departed this life.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शुचिसमाचाराः पर्युपस्थान कोविदः
स्त्रीवर्षवरभूयिष्ठा उपतस्थुर्यथापुरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śucisamācārāḥ paryupasthāna kovidaḥ
strīvarṣavarabhūyiṣṭhā upatasthuryathāpuram

translations.english: And as on former occasions, men practising purity and well up in serving, with numerous women and eunuchs entered appearance.

verses.sanskrit:
हरिचन्दनसंपृक्तमुदकं काञ्चनैर्घटैः
आनिन्युः स्नानशिक्षाज्ञा यथाकालं यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
haricandanasaṁpṛktamudakaṁ kāñcanairghaṭaiḥ
āninyuḥ snānaśikṣājñā yathākālaṁ yathāvidhi

translations.english: Persons acquainted with the ceremonials connected with bath, according to the ordinance and in due time, in golden vessels brought water impregnated with Hair sandal powder.

verses.sanskrit:
मङ्गलालम्भनीयानि प्राशनीयानुपस्करान्
उपनिन्युस्तथाप्यन्याः कुमारी बहुलाः स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
maṅgalālambhanīyāni prāśanīyānupaskarān
upaninyustathāpyanyāḥ kumārī bahulāḥ striyaḥ

translations.english: Pure females together with many virgins brought kine &c, which were to be touched, Ganges water for sipping, mirrors, cloths, ornaments and other areicles.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ याः कोसलेन्द्रस्य शयनं प्रत्यनन्तराः
ताः स्त्रियस्तु समागम्य भर्तारं प्रत्यबोधयन्
verses.transliteration:
atha yāḥ kosalendrasya śayanaṁ pratyanantarāḥ
tāḥ striyastu samāgamya bhartāraṁ pratyabodhayan

translations.english: Those ladies that were beside the bed of the lord of Kosala, were consoling their husband.

verses.sanskrit:
ता वेपथुपरीताश्च राज्ञः प्राणेषु शङ्किताः
प्रतिस्रोतस्तृणाग्राणां सदृशं संचकम्पिरे
verses.transliteration:
tā vepathuparītāśca rājñaḥ prāṇeṣu śaṅkitāḥ
pratisrotastṛṇāgrāṇāṁ sadṛśaṁ saṁcakampire

translations.english: Thereupon apprehensive for the king's life, they began to tremble like a blade of grass on a torrent. Filled with doubts at sight of the king, the ladies at last concluded that what had been apprehended (by the monarch) had certainly taken place.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रचुक्रुशुर्दीनाः सस्वरं ता वराङ्गनाः
करेणव इवारण्ये स्थानप्रच्युतयूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pracukruśurdīnāḥ sasvaraṁ tā varāṅganāḥ
kareṇava ivāraṇye sthānapracyutayūthapāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon exceedingly distressed, those paragons of their sex, like she-elephants in the forest deprived of their leader of the herd, broke out into wailing.

verses.sanskrit:
तासामाक्रन्द शब्देन सहसोद्गतचेतने
कौसल्या च सुमित्राच त्यक्तनिद्रे बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration:
tāsāmākranda śabdena sahasodgatacetane
kausalyā ca sumitrāca tyaktanidre babhūvatuḥ

translations.english: At the sounds of their lamentations, both Kausalya and Sumitrā suddenly regaining consciousness, awoke from their sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च दृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्
हा नाथेति परिक्रुश्य पेततुर्धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
hā nātheti parikruśya petaturdharaṇītale

translations.english: And Kausalya and Sumitrā looking at the king and feeling him, fell down to the earth, exclaiming, "Ah lord.”

verses.sanskrit:
सा कोसलेन्द्रदुहिता वेष्टमाना महीतले
न बभ्राज रजोध्वस्ता तारेव गगनच्युता
verses.transliteration:
sā kosalendraduhitā veṣṭamānā mahītale
na babhrāja rajodhvastā tāreva gaganacyutā

translations.english: As the daughter of Kosala's lord rolled on the ground, she covered with dust did not appear in all her loveliness, like a star fallen from the sky to the earth below.

verses.sanskrit:
सद्यो निपतितानन्दं दीनविक्लवदर्शनम्
बभूव नरदेवस्य सद्म दिष्टान्तमीयुषः
verses.transliteration:
sadyo nipatitānandaṁ dīnaviklavadarśanam
babhūva naradevasya sadma diṣṭāntamīyuṣaḥ

translations.english: The mansion of the king became filled with people exceedingly excited and frightened, eager to know all about the matter, became filled with lamentations, with friends afflicted with distress, its joy instantaneously vanished, a scene of distress and dole.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीतमाज्ञाय तु पार्थिवर्षभं; यशस्विनं संपरिवार्य पत्नयः
भृशं रुदन्त्यः करुणं सुदुःखिताः; प्रगृह्य बाहू व्यलपन्ननाथवत्
verses.transliteration:
atītamājñāya tu pārthivarṣabhaṁ; yaśasvinaṁ saṁparivārya patnayaḥ
bhṛśaṁ rudantyaḥ karuṇaṁ suduḥkhitāḥ; pragṛhya bāhū vyalapannanāthavat

translations.english: Knowing that the lord of earth had departed, his wives surrounding that illustrious one, smitten with excess of sorrow and weeping bitterly and piteously, holding the king's hands indulged in lamentations, like forlorn ones.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी विविधं शोककर्शिता
उपगृह्य शिरो राज्ञः कैकेयीं प्रत्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇākṣī vividhaṁ śokakarśitā
upagṛhya śiro rājñaḥ kaikeyīṁ pratyabhāṣata

translations.english: Seeing the king had ascended heaven, like to a fire that has cooled, or an ocean deprived of its waters, or the sun shorn of his splendour, Kausalyā afflicted with woe, taking on her lap the head of the king, with tears in her eyes, said.

verses.sanskrit:
सकामा भव कैकेयि भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्
त्यक्त्वा राजानमेकाग्रा नृशंसे दुष्टचारिणि
verses.transliteration:
sakāmā bhava kaikeyi bhuṅkṣva rājyamakaṇṭakam
tyaktvā rājānamekāgrā nṛśaṁse duṣṭacāriṇi

translations.english: O Kaikeyī, attain you your wished: do you enjoy this kingdom rid of your thorn. O cruel one, O you of wicked ways, you that forsaking the king had set your heart (on having your son crowned), Rāma had gone away, forsaking me; and now my lord has ascended heaven. I can no longer bear to live, like one left lone in a wilderness by her companions.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तारं तं परित्यज्य का स्त्री दैवतमात्मनः
इच्छेज्जीवितुमन्यत्र कैकेय्यास्त्यक्तधर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
bhartāraṁ taṁ parityajya kā strī daivatamātmanaḥ
icchejjīvitumanyatra kaikeyyāstyaktadharmaṇaḥ

translations.english: What other woman except Kaikeyi lost to righteousness, having lost her deity, her lord, wishes to carry on existence in another's kingdom?

verses.sanskrit:
अनियोगे नियुक्तेन राज्ञा रामं विवासितम्
सभार्यं जनकः श्रुत्वा परितप्स्यत्यहं यथा
verses.transliteration:
aniyoge niyuktena rājñā rāmaṁ vivāsitam
sabhāryaṁ janakaḥ śrutvā paritapsyatyahaṁ yathā

translations.english: As a covetous person taking poison (through anger or some other passion), does not consider himself guilty, (so Kaikeyī) having done this evil through Manthara's incitement, does not bring her guilt home to her mind. It is through the instrumentality of the humpbacked woman that this race of the Rāghavas has been destroyed by Kaikeyi. Hearing that the king being made to do an unrighteous action, has banished Rāma together with his wife, king Janaka will be filled with grief as I have been.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः कमलपत्राक्षो जीवनाशमितो गतः
विदेहराजस्य सुता तहा सीता तपस्विनी
दुःखस्यानुचिता दुःखं वने पर्युद्विजिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣo jīvanāśamito gataḥ
videharājasya sutā tahā sītā tapasvinī
duḥkhasyānucitā duḥkhaṁ vane paryudvijiṣyati

translations.english: The fair daughter of Videha's king unworthy of hardship, in ascetic guise is leading a life of trouble and terror in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
नदतां भीमघोषाणां निशासु मृगपक्षिणाम्
निशम्य नूनं संस्त्रस्ता राघवं संश्रयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nadatāṁ bhīmaghoṣāṇāṁ niśāsu mṛgapakṣiṇām
niśamya nūnaṁ saṁstrastā rāghavaṁ saṁśrayiṣyati

translations.english: Hearing at night the dreadful roars of birds and beasts crying, she exceedingly frightened takes shelter with Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धश्चैवाल्पपुत्रश्च वैदेहीमनिचिन्तयन्
सोऽपि शोकसमाविष्टो ननु त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛddhaścaivālpaputraśca vaidehīmanicintayan
so'pi śokasamāviṣṭo nanu tyakṣyati jīvitam

translations.english: Old and having an only daughter, he revolving in his mind thoughts of Vaidehi, shall, smitten with grief, surely renounce his life. I ever faithful to my lord will die this very day, embracing this body; I will enter fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तां ततः संपरिष्वज्य विलपन्तीं तपस्विनीम्
व्यपनिन्युः सुदुःखार्तां कौसल्यां व्यावहारिकाः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tataḥ saṁpariṣvajya vilapantīṁ tapasvinīm
vyapaninyuḥ suduḥkhārtāṁ kausalyāṁ vyāvahārikāḥ

translations.english: As embracing the (dead) body, that unfortunate lady was bewailing, the courtiers had the distressed (queen) removed from there.

verses.sanskrit:
तैलद्रोण्यामथामात्याः संवेश्य जगतीपतिम्
राज्ञः सर्वाण्यथादिष्टाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
tailadroṇyāmathāmātyāḥ saṁveśya jagatīpatim
rājñaḥ sarvāṇyathādiṣṭāścakruḥ karmāṇyanantaram

translations.english: Then placing the corpse of the king in a (capacious) pan with oil, the courtiers performed the mourning rites of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
तैलद्रोण्यां तु सचिवैः शायितं तं नराधिपम्
हा मृतोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा स्त्रियस्ताः पर्यदेवयन्
verses.transliteration:
tailadroṇyāṁ tu sacivaiḥ śāyitaṁ taṁ narādhipam
hā mṛto'yamiti jñātvā striyastāḥ paryadevayan

translations.english: But well versed in everything, the counsellors, in the absence of his son, did not perform the funeral obsequies of the king; and therefore they placed his body stretched in the pan of oil. Alas! at length concluding it for certain that the king was dead, the ladies burst out into lamentaions.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहूनुद्यम्य कृपणा नेत्रप्रस्रवणैर्मुखैः
रुदन्त्यः शोकसंतप्ताः कृपणं पर्यदेवयन्
verses.transliteration:
bāhūnudyamya kṛpaṇā netraprasravaṇairmukhaiḥ
rudantyaḥ śokasaṁtaptāḥ kṛpaṇaṁ paryadevayan

translations.english: And raising their arms, with tears trickling down their faces, they in dire affliction and extremely exercised with grief, lamented.

verses.sanskrit:
निशानक्षत्रहीनेव स्त्रीव भर्तृविवर्जिता
पुरी नाराजतायोध्या हीना राज्ञा महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
niśānakṣatrahīneva strīva bhartṛvivarjitā
purī nārājatāyodhyā hīnā rājñā mahātmanā

translations.english: Like a night without stars, like a fair one forsaken by her husband, the city of Ayodhyā without the magnanimous monarch did not appear delightful as it had done before, with the populace filled with tears, the ladies uttering exclamations of distress, and the terraces and courts deserted.

verses.sanskrit:
गतप्रभा द्यौरिव भास्करं विना; व्यपेतनक्षत्रगणेव शर्वरी
पुरी बभासे रहिता महात्मना; न चास्रकण्ठाकुलमार्गचत्वरा
verses.transliteration:
gataprabhā dyauriva bhāskaraṁ vinā; vyapetanakṣatragaṇeva śarvarī
purī babhāse rahitā mahātmanā; na cāsrakaṇṭhākulamārgacatvarā

translations.english: And with her terraces overflowing with tears that flooded the throats of the mourners, the city appeared like the welkin without its splendour in the absence of the sun, or the night with the stars enveloped.

verses.sanskrit:
नराश्च नार्यश्च समेत्य संघशो; विगर्हमाणा भरतस्य मातरम्
तदा नगर्यां नरदेवसंक्षये; बभूवुरार्ता न च शर्म लेभिरे
verses.transliteration:
narāśca nāryaśca sametya saṁghaśo; vigarhamāṇā bharatasya mātaram
tadā nagaryāṁ naradevasaṁkṣaye; babhūvurārtā na ca śarma lebhire

translations.english: And on on the demise of that illustrious personage, in the city men and women in multitudes, censuring Bharata's mother, became extremely distressed, and did not attain peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीता शर्वरी दुःखं या नो वर्षशतोपमा
अस्मिन्पञ्चत्वमापन्ने पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवे
verses.transliteration:
atītā śarvarī duḥkhaṁ yā no varṣaśatopamā
asminpañcatvamāpanne putraśokena pārthive

translations.english: Then facing the royal priest, the eminent Vasistha, they said, "That night that had appeared like to an hundred years has at last been painfully passed.

verses.sanskrit:
उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ क्केकयेषु परंतपौ
पुरे राजगृहे रम्ये मातामहनिवेशने
verses.transliteration:
ubhau bharataśatrughnau kkekayeṣu paraṁtapau
pure rājagṛhe ramye mātāmahaniveśane

translations.english: The king racked by sorrow for his son having breathed his last, the mighty monarch has ascended heaven, Rāma has taken refuge in the woods, the energetic Lakşmaņa has gone with Rama, and does Bharata and Satrughna, repressors of foes, are staying in Kekaya in pleasant Rājagrha, the abode of their maternal grandfather.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणामिहाद्यैव कश्चिद्राजा विधीयताम्
अराजकं हि नो राष्ट्रं न विनाशमवाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāmihādyaiva kaścidrājā vidhīyatām
arājakaṁ hi no rāṣṭraṁ na vināśamavāpnuyāt

translations.english: Do you select some on this very day from the descendants of Ikşvāku, to be king here. Verily does a kingdom go to ruin, when without a king.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजले जनपदे विद्युन्माली महास्वनः
अभिवर्षति पर्जन्यो महीं दिव्येन वारिणा
verses.transliteration:
nārājale janapade vidyunmālī mahāsvanaḥ
abhivarṣati parjanyo mahīṁ divyena vāriṇā

translations.english: He that goes garlanded with lightning, and has a mighty voice, even the Cloud, does not with Skye shower drench the Earth in a kingdom without a king.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे बीजमुष्टिः प्रकीर्यते
नाराकके पितुः पुत्रो भार्या वा वर्तते वशे
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade bījamuṣṭiḥ prakīryate
nārākake pituḥ putro bhāryā vā vartate vaśe

translations.english: In a kingless kingdom no one sows corn. In a kingless kingdom the son does not obey his sire, or the wife her husband.

verses.sanskrit:
अराजके धनं नास्ति नास्ति भार्याप्यराजके
इदमत्याहितं चान्यत्कुतः सत्यमराजके
verses.transliteration:
arājake dhanaṁ nāsti nāsti bhāryāpyarājake
idamatyāhitaṁ cānyatkutaḥ satyamarājake

translations.english: A kingless kingdom possesses no wealth, and wives are hard to keep in such a place. This great fear attends a kingless country. And where is other morality (besides that detailed above) to be found at such a place?

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे कारयन्ति सभां नराः
उद्यानानि च रम्याणि हृष्टाः पुण्यगृहाणि च
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade kārayanti sabhāṁ narāḥ
udyānāni ca ramyāṇi hṛṣṭāḥ puṇyagṛhāṇi ca

translations.english: In a kingless country men do not form themselves into associations, nor do they, inspired with cheerfulness, make elegant gardens or sacred edifices.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे यज्ञशीला द्विजातयः
सत्राण्यन्वासते दान्ता ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade yajñaśīlā dvijātayaḥ
satrāṇyanvāsate dāntā brāhmaṇāḥ saṁśitavratāḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country, the twice-born ones do not celebrate sacrifices. In a kingless country, in mighty sacrifices wealthy Brāhmaṇas do not confer (on the officiating priests) the Dakșiņās (which they receive according to the ordinance).

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे प्रभूतनटनर्तकाः
उत्सवाश्च समाजाश्च वर्धन्ते राष्ट्रवर्धनाः
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade prabhūtanaṭanartakāḥ
utsavāśca samājāśca vardhante rāṣṭravardhanāḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country, neither neither social gatherings, nor festivities characterised by the presence of merry theatrical managers and performers, increase.

verses.sanskrit:
नारजके जनपदे सिद्धार्था व्यवहारिणः
कथाभिरनुरज्यन्ते कथाशीलाः कथाप्रियैः
verses.transliteration:
nārajake janapade siddhārthā vyavahāriṇaḥ
kathābhiranurajyante kathāśīlāḥ kathāpriyaiḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country disputants cannot decide their point; nor are persons given to hearing Puranic recitations pleased by those delighting in the practice.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे वाहनैः शीघ्रगामिभिः
नरा निर्यान्त्यरण्यानि नारीभिः सह कामिनः
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade vāhanaiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ
narā niryāntyaraṇyāni nārībhiḥ saha kāminaḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country pleasure-seeking people do not in company with females go to the woods by means of swift vehicles.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराकजे जनपदे धनवन्तः सुरक्षिताः
शेरते विवृत द्वाराः कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः
verses.transliteration:
nārākaje janapade dhanavantaḥ surakṣitāḥ
śerate vivṛta dvārāḥ kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country, the wealthy are not well protected; nor do shepherds and cultivators sleep with their doors open.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे वणिजो दूरगामिनः
गच्छन्ति क्षेममध्वानं बहुपुण्यसमाचिताः
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade vaṇijo dūragāminaḥ
gacchanti kṣemamadhvānaṁ bahupuṇyasamācitāḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country traders coming from distant lands, loaded with various kinds of merchandise, do not with safety go along the roads.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे चरत्येकचरो वशी
भावयन्नात्मनात्मानं यत्रसायंगृहो मुनिः
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade caratyekacaro vaśī
bhāvayannātmanātmānaṁ yatrasāyaṁgṛho muniḥ

translations.english: In a kingless country the ascetic with his subdued senses, himself his sole protector, who makes his quarters wherever evening overtakes him, cannot walk contemplating the Deity.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे योगक्षेमं प्रवर्तते
न चाप्यराजके सेना शत्रून्विषहते युधि
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade yogakṣemaṁ pravartate
na cāpyarājake senā śatrūnviṣahate yudhi

translations.english: In a kingless country, one cannot protect what one has, or procure what one has not. In a kingless country, the forces cannot bear the onslaught of the foe.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा ह्यनुदका नद्यो यथा वाप्यतृणं वनम्
अगोपाला यथा गावस्तथा राष्ट्रमराजकम्
verses.transliteration:
yathā hyanudakā nadyo yathā vāpyatṛṇaṁ vanam
agopālā yathā gāvastathā rāṣṭramarājakam

translations.english: Even as a river without water, a wood without grass, a herd of kine without a keeper, is a kingdom without a king.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराजके जनपदे स्वकं भवति कस्यचित्
मत्स्या इव नरा नित्यं भक्षयन्ति परस्परम्
verses.transliteration:
nārājake janapade svakaṁ bhavati kasyacit
matsyā iva narā nityaṁ bhakṣayanti parasparam

translations.english: In a kingless country a person hardly preserves his life; and like fishes people eat up one another.

verses.sanskrit:
येहि संभिन्नमर्यादा नास्तिकाश्छिन्नसंशयाः
तेऽपि भावाय कल्पन्ते राजदण्डनिपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
yehi saṁbhinnamaryādā nāstikāśchinnasaṁśayāḥ
te'pi bhāvāya kalpante rājadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ

translations.english: Even those heretics who having disregarded the dignity of social morality had met with chastisement at the hands of the king, their fear removed, give themselves airs.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो तम इवेदं स्यान्न प्रज्ञायेत किंचन
राजा चेन्न भवेँल्लोके विभजन्साध्वसाधुनी
verses.transliteration:
aho tama ivedaṁ syānna prajñāyeta kiṁcana
rājā cenna bhave̐lloke vibhajansādhvasādhunī

translations.english: If there were not a king in this world to adjudge fair and foul, darkness would overspread (the face of the earth) and people could not distinguish anything whatever. As the ocean keeps within its continent, we even while the monarch lived, did not disregard your words.

verses.sanskrit:
स नः समीक्ष्य द्विजवर्यवृत्तं; नृपं विना राज्यमरण्यभूतम्
कुमारमिक्ष्वाकुसुतं वदान्यं; त्वमेव राजानमिहाभिषिञ्चय
verses.transliteration:
sa naḥ samīkṣya dvijavaryavṛttaṁ; nṛpaṁ vinā rājyamaraṇyabhūtam
kumāramikṣvākusutaṁ vadānyaṁ; tvameva rājānamihābhiṣiñcaya

translations.english: Do you, O best of Brāhmaṇas, beholding our acts rendered nugatory, and this empire became a wilderness for want of a king, install that descendant of Ikşvāku or any other as king of this realm.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह
मित्रामात्यगणान्सर्वान्ब्राह्मणांस्तानिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
mitrāmātyagaṇānsarvānbrāhmaṇāṁstānidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Hearing their words, Vasiştha said to the Brāhmaṇas and the adherents and counsellors (of the king)

verses.sanskrit:
यदसौ मातुलकुले पुरे राजगृहे सुखी
भरतो वसति भ्रात्रा शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः
verses.transliteration:
yadasau mātulakule pure rājagṛhe sukhī
bharato vasati bhrātrā śatrughnena samanvitaḥ

translations.english: Bharata, on whom the king has conferred the kingdom, along with his brother Satrughna, is living happily in the house of his maternal uncle.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छीघ्रं जवना दूता गच्छन्तु त्वरितैर्हयैः
आनेतुं भ्रातरौ वीरौ किं समीक्षामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tacchīghraṁ javanā dūtā gacchantu tvaritairhayaiḥ
ānetuṁ bhrātarau vīrau kiṁ samīkṣāmahe vayam

translations.english: Let envoys by means of fleet coursers speedily repair thither and bring those heroic brothers. What shall we decide?

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छन्त्विति ततः सर्वे वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
gacchantviti tataḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaṁ vākyamabruvan
teṣāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt

translations.english: "Let them go", said all to Vasistha. Hearing their words, Vasistha spoke to them, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
एहि सिद्धार्थ विजय जयन्ताशोकनन्दन
श्रूयतामितिकर्तव्यं सर्वानेव ब्रवीमि वः
verses.transliteration:
ehi siddhārtha vijaya jayantāśokanandana
śrūyatāmitikartavyaṁ sarvāneva bravīmi vaḥ

translations.english: Come here, you Siddhārtha, and Vijaya, and Jayanta, and Asokanandana. Do you hear. I well tell you what you are to do.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरं राजगृहं गत्वा शीघ्रं शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः
त्यक्तशोकैरिदं वाच्यः शासनाद्भरतो मम
verses.transliteration:
puraṁ rājagṛhaṁ gatvā śīghraṁ śīghrajavairhayaiḥ
tyaktaśokairidaṁ vācyaḥ śāsanādbharato mama

translations.english: First going speedily to the royal residence by means of swift horses, do you, renouncing grief, by my order speak these words of mine to Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोहितस्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः
त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
purohitastvāṁ kuśalaṁ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ
tvaramāṇaśca niryāhi kṛtyamātyayikaṁ tvayā

translations.english: The priest as well as the counsellors have enquired after your welfare. Do you at once set out. A business is at hand that brooks no delay on your part.

verses.sanskrit:
मा चास्मै प्रोषितं रामं मा चास्मै पितरं मृतम्
भवन्तः शंसिषुर्गत्वा राघवाणामिमं क्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
mā cāsmai proṣitaṁ rāmaṁ mā cāsmai pitaraṁ mṛtam
bhavantaḥ śaṁsiṣurgatvā rāghavāṇāmimaṁ kṣayam

translations.english: But you must on no account communicate to him the exile of Rāma, or the demise of the monarch, or the destruction that has befallen the Raghu race through this occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि भूषणानि वराणि च
क्षिप्रमादाय राज्ञश्च भरतस्य च गच्छत
वसिष्ठेनाभ्यनुज्ञाता दूताः संत्वरिता ययुः
verses.transliteration:
kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca
kṣipramādāya rājñaśca bharatasya ca gacchata
vasiṣṭhenābhyanujñātā dūtāḥ saṁtvaritā yayuḥ

translations.english: Do you, speedily taking silk apparel and excellent ornaments for king Bharata, set off.

verses.sanskrit:
ते हस्तिन पुरे गङ्गां तीर्त्वा प्रत्यङ्मुखा ययुः
पाञ्चालदेशमासाद्य मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्
verses.transliteration:
te hastina pure gaṅgāṁ tīrtvā pratyaṅmukhā yayuḥ
pāñcāladeśamāsādya madhyena kurujāṅgalam

translations.english: Then crossing the Gangā at Hastināpura, and arriving at Pāñcāla, they proceeded west ward through Kurujāngala.

verses.sanskrit:
ते प्रसन्नोदकां दिव्यां नानाविहगसेविताम्
उपातिजग्मुर्वेगेन शरदण्डां जनाकुलाम्
verses.transliteration:
te prasannodakāṁ divyāṁ nānāvihagasevitām
upātijagmurvegena śaradaṇḍāṁ janākulām

translations.english: And they darted past the Saradanda overflowing with delightful water, beautiful, and haunted by fowls of various kinds.

verses.sanskrit:
निकूलवृक्षमासाद्य दिव्यं सत्योपयाचनम्
अभिगम्याभिवाद्यं तं कुलिङ्गां प्राविशन्पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
nikūlavṛkṣamāsādya divyaṁ satyopayācanam
abhigamyābhivādyaṁ taṁ kuliṅgāṁ prāviśanpurīm

translations.english: Then on the western bank of the stream, coming upon a tree called Satyopayācana presided by a deity, and bowing down to the tree and going round it, they entered the city of Kulinga.

verses.sanskrit:
ते श्रान्तवाहना दूता विकृष्टेन सता पथा
गिरि व्रजं पुर वरं शीघ्रमासेदुरञ्जसा
verses.transliteration:
te śrāntavāhanā dūtā vikṛṣṭena satā pathā
giri vrajaṁ pura varaṁ śīghramāsedurañjasā

translations.english: And with their vehicles fatigued, the ambassadors, on account of the great distance of the way; speedily reached that best of cities, Girivraja.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तुः प्रियार्थं कुलरक्षणार्थं; भर्तुश्च वंशस्य परिग्रहार्थम्
अहेडमानास्त्वरया स्म दूता; रात्र्यां तु ते तत्पुरमेव याताः
verses.transliteration:
bhartuḥ priyārthaṁ kularakṣaṇārthaṁ; bhartuśca vaṁśasya parigrahārtham
aheḍamānāstvarayā sma dūtā; rātryāṁ tu te tatpurameva yātāḥ

translations.english: And for pleasing their master, for the preservation of the people, and enabling Bharata to assume the reins of government, those envoys, casting aside negligence, swiftly entered the city in the night.

verses.sanskrit:
यामेव रात्रिं ते दूताः प्रविशन्ति स्म तां पुरीम्
भरतेनापि तां रात्रिं स्वप्नो दृष्टोऽयमप्रियः
verses.transliteration:
yāmeva rātriṁ te dūtāḥ praviśanti sma tāṁ purīm
bharatenāpi tāṁ rātriṁ svapno dṛṣṭo'yamapriyaḥ

translations.english: The very same night that the envoys entered the city, Bharata saw an evil dream.

verses.sanskrit:
व्युष्टामेव तु तां रात्रिं दृष्ट्वा तं स्वप्नमप्रियम्
पुत्रो राजाधिराजस्य सुभृशं पर्यतप्यत
verses.transliteration:
vyuṣṭāmeva tu tāṁ rātriṁ dṛṣṭvā taṁ svapnamapriyam
putro rājādhirājasya subhṛśaṁ paryatapyata

translations.english: And seeing that evil dream during the short hours, the son of that king of kings exceedingly burned in grief.

verses.sanskrit:
तप्यमानं समाज्ञाय वयस्याः प्रियवादिनः
आयासं हि विनेष्यन्तः सभायां चक्रिरे कथाः
verses.transliteration:
tapyamānaṁ samājñāya vayasyāḥ priyavādinaḥ
āyāsaṁ hi vineṣyantaḥ sabhāyāṁ cakrire kathāḥ

translations.english: And finding him aggrieved, his sweet. speeched associates, endeavouring to chase the heaviness, began to converse on a variety of subjects.

verses.sanskrit:
वादयन्ति तथा शान्तिं लासयन्त्यपि चापरे
नाटकान्यपरे प्राहुर्हास्यानि विविधानि च
verses.transliteration:
vādayanti tathā śāntiṁ lāsayantyapi cāpare
nāṭakānyapare prāhurhāsyāni vividhāni ca

translations.english: Some played on instruments; some for the purpose of pacifying his mind, danced (the courtezans); others performed scenes variously fraught with the sentiment of mirth.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैर्महात्मा भरतः सखिभिः प्रिय वादिभिः
गोष्ठीहास्यानि कुर्वद्भिर्न प्राहृष्यत राघवः
verses.transliteration:
sa tairmahātmā bharataḥ sakhibhiḥ priya vādibhiḥ
goṣṭhīhāsyāni kurvadbhirna prāhṛṣyata rāghavaḥ

translations.english: But although his friends intending to ally his agitation set about enacting passages calculated to amuse family circles, that magnanimous descendant of Raghu did not indulge in laughter.

verses.sanskrit:
तमब्रवीत्प्रियसखो भरतं सखिभिर्वृतम्
सुहृद्भिः पर्युपासीनः किं सखे नानुमोदसे
verses.transliteration:
tamabravītpriyasakho bharataṁ sakhibhirvṛtam
suhṛdbhiḥ paryupāsīnaḥ kiṁ sakhe nānumodase

translations.english: Then a dear friend addressed Bharata, as he sat surrounded by his friends, “Surrounded by your friends, why do you not, my friend, join in the mirth?"

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्ने पितरमद्राक्षं मलिनं मुक्तमूर्धजम्
पतन्तमद्रिशिखरात्कलुषे गोमये ह्रदे
verses.transliteration:
svapne pitaramadrākṣaṁ malinaṁ muktamūrdhajam
patantamadriśikharātkaluṣe gomaye hrade

translations.english: Thus asked by his friend, Bharata answered, “Listen why this depression has overtaken me. In a dream I beheld my father, pale, with his hair loosely flowing about, plunging from the summit of a mountain into a dirty pool filled with cowdung.”

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवमानश्च मे दृष्टः स तस्मिन्गोमयह्रदे
पिबन्नञ्जलिना तैलं हसन्निव मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
plavamānaśca me dṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmingomayahrade
pibannañjalinā tailaṁ hasanniva muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: And I saw him floating on a sink of cowdung, and yet with a momentary laugh drinking oil by means of his joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तिलोदनं भुक्त्वा पुनः पुनरधःशिराः
तैलेनाभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्गस्तैलमेवावगाहत
verses.transliteration:
tatastilodanaṁ bhuktvā punaḥ punaradhaḥśirāḥ
tailenābhyaktasarvāṅgastailamevāvagāhata

translations.english: Then feeding on rice mixed with sesame, he again and again hanging his head down, dives into oil with his limbs rubbed with oil.

verses.sanskrit:
अवदीर्णां च पृथिवीं शुष्कांश्च विविधान्द्रुमान्
अहं पश्यामि विध्वस्तान्सधूमांश्चैव पार्वतान्
verses.transliteration:
avadīrṇāṁ ca pṛthivīṁ śuṣkāṁśca vividhāndrumān
ahaṁ paśyāmi vidhvastānsadhūmāṁścaiva pārvatān

translations.english: And in my dream I saw the ocean dried up, and the moon fallen on the earth, and the earth as if invaded by enfolding darkness, and the tusk of the elephant on which the monarch rides falling in fragments, and flaming fire suddenly extinguished, and the earth rent, and the trees withered, and all the mountains belching smoke.

verses.sanskrit:
पीठे कार्ष्णायसे चैनं निषण्णं कृष्णवाससम्
प्रहसन्ति स्म राजानं प्रमदाः कृष्णपिङ्गलाः
verses.transliteration:
pīṭhe kārṣṇāyase cainaṁ niṣaṇṇaṁ kṛṣṇavāsasam
prahasanti sma rājānaṁ pramadāḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalāḥ

translations.english: I saw the king seated on a sable seat of iron, clad in a sable garb; and women black and yellow beating him.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वरमाणश्च धर्मात्मा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः
रथेन खरयुक्तेन प्रयातो दक्षिणामुखः
verses.transliteration:
tvaramāṇaśca dharmātmā raktamālyānulepanaḥ
rathena kharayuktena prayāto dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ

translations.english: And bearing a garland of red flowers, with his body daubed with red sandal, he was fast proceeding to the south in a car yoked with asses.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेतन्मया दृष्टमिमां रात्रिं भयावहाम्
अहं रामोऽथ वा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
evametanmayā dṛṣṭamimāṁ rātriṁ bhayāvahām
ahaṁ rāmo'tha vā rājā lakṣmaṇo vā mariṣyati

translations.english: This was the dream that I saw this terrible night. Either I, or Rama, or the king, or Lakşmaņa is to breathe our last.

verses.sanskrit:
नरो यानेन यः स्वप्ने खरयुक्तेन याति हि
अचिरात्तस्य धूमाग्रं चितायां संप्रदृश्यते
एतन्निमित्तं दीनोऽहं तन्न वः प्रतिपूजये
verses.transliteration:
naro yānena yaḥ svapne kharayuktena yāti hi
acirāttasya dhūmāgraṁ citāyāṁ saṁpradṛśyate
etannimittaṁ dīno'haṁ tanna vaḥ pratipūjaye

translations.english: The smoke of the funeral pyre of him will be shortly visible that goes in the car yoked with asses. It is for this reason that I am poor of spirit, and that I do not respond to your words. Further, my throat is parched, and my mind ill at ease.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां हि दुःस्वप्नगतिं निशाम्य ता;मनेकरूपामवितर्कितां पुरा
भयं महत्तद्धृदयान्न याति मे; विचिन्त्य राजानमचिन्त्यदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ hi duḥsvapnagatiṁ niśāmya tā;manekarūpāmavitarkitāṁ purā
bhayaṁ mahattaddhṛdayānna yāti me; vicintya rājānamacintyadarśanam

translations.english: Bringing to mind this various-looking dream which I had not thought of before, and remembering the king of incomprehensible presence, this fear goes not from my heart.

verses.sanskrit:
भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नं दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः
प्रविश्यासह्यपरिखं रम्यं राजगृहं पुरम्
verses.transliteration:
bharate bruvati svapnaṁ dūtāste klāntavāhanāḥ
praviśyāsahyaparikhaṁ ramyaṁ rājagṛhaṁ puram

translations.english: Bharata was speaking thus when the envoys with their vehicles fatigued, entered the splendid royal residence surrounded by a strong rampart.

verses.sanskrit:
समागम्य तु राज्ञा च राजपुत्रेण चार्चिताः
राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु तमूचुर्भरतं वचः
verses.transliteration:
samāgamya tu rājñā ca rājaputreṇa cārcitāḥ
rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tamūcurbharataṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Presenting themselves before the king, they, well received by him as well as the prince, bowed down to the feet of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोहितस्त्वा कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः
त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
purohitastvā kuśalaṁ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ
tvaramāṇaśca niryāhi kṛtyamātyayikaṁ tvayā

translations.english: Then they addressed Bharata, saying, The priest and the counsellors have enquired after your welfare. Do you set out speedily. A business is on hand that Brooke no delay on your part.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्र विंशतिकोट्यस्तु नृपतेर्मातुलस्य ते
दशकोट्यस्तु संपूर्णास्तथैव च नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
atra viṁśatikoṭyastu nṛpatermātulasya te
daśakoṭyastu saṁpūrṇāstathaiva ca nṛpātmaja

translations.english: Twenty Kotis are intended for the king and complete ten for your maternal uncle, O son of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सर्वं स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज्जने
दूतानुवाच भरतः कामैः संप्रतिपूज्य तान्
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya ca tatsarvaṁ svanuraktaḥ suhṛjjane
dūtānuvāca bharataḥ kāmaiḥ saṁpratipūjya tān

translations.english: Taking all these, Bharata attached to his relatives, made the articles over to them; and receiving the envoys with goodly gifts, spoke to them.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्सुकुशली राजा पिता दशरथो मम
कच्चिच्चारागता रामे लक्ष्मणे वा महात्मनि
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsukuśalī rājā pitā daśaratho mama
kacciccārāgatā rāme lakṣmaṇe vā mahātmani

translations.english: Is my father, king Dasaratha, well? And is it well with Rama and the high-souled Laksmana?

verses.sanskrit:
आर्या च धर्मनिरता धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी
अरोगा चापि कौसल्या माता रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
āryā ca dharmaniratā dharmajñā dharmadarśinī
arogā cāpi kausalyā mātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: And is the mother of the intelligent Rāma, the revered Kausalyā, conversant with virtue and ever practising it, well?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्सुमित्रा धर्मज्ञा जननी लक्ष्मणस्य या
शत्रुघ्नस्य च वीरस्य सारोगा चापि मध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsumitrā dharmajñā jananī lakṣmaṇasya yā
śatrughnasya ca vīrasya sārogā cāpi madhyamā

translations.english: Is the virtuous Sumitrā, mother of Lakşmaņa and of the heroic Śatrughna, well?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मकामा सदा चण्डी क्रोधना प्राज्ञमानिनी
अरोगा चापि कैकेयी माता मे किमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
ātmakāmā sadā caṇḍī krodhanā prājñamāninī
arogā cāpi kaikeyī mātā me kimuvāca ha

translations.english: And that wrathful one ever intent on her interest and setting immense store by her wisdom, my mother Kaikeyī, is it also well with her?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते दूता भरतेन महात्मना
ऊचुः संप्रश्रितं वाक्यमिदं तं भरतं तदा
कुशलास्ते नरव्याघ्र येषां कुशलमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāstu te dūtā bharatena mahātmanā
ūcuḥ saṁpraśritaṁ vākyamidaṁ taṁ bharataṁ tadā
kuśalāste naravyāghra yeṣāṁ kuśalamicchasi

translations.english: Thus addressed by the magnanimous Bharata, the envoys spoke to him these humble and brief words.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतश्चापि तान्दूतानेवमुक्तोऽभ्यभाषत
आपृच्छेऽहं महाराजं दूताः संत्वरयन्ति माम्
verses.transliteration:
bharataścāpi tāndūtānevamukto'bhyabhāṣata
āpṛcche'haṁ mahārājaṁ dūtāḥ saṁtvarayanti mām

translations.english: Thus addressed, Bharata said to the envoys, “Let me tell the king that the envoys are urging speed on me.”

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तान्दूतान्भरतः पार्थिवात्मजः
दूतैः संचोदितो वाक्यं मातामहमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu tāndūtānbharataḥ pārthivātmajaḥ
dūtaiḥ saṁcodito vākyaṁ mātāmahamuvāca ha

translations.english: Having said this, that son of the king, Bharata, communicated to his maternal grand-father what the envoys had told him.

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्पितुर्गमिष्यामि सकाशं दूतचोदितः
पुनरप्यहमेष्यामि यदा मे त्वं स्मरिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
rājanpiturgamiṣyāmi sakāśaṁ dūtacoditaḥ
punarapyahameṣyāmi yadā me tvaṁ smariṣyasi

translations.english: Asked by the envoys, I shall, O monarch, go to my father. I shall come again whenever you will remember me.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतेनैवमुक्तस्तु नृपो मातामहस्तदा
तमुवाच शुभं वाक्यं शिरस्याघ्राय राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
bharatenaivamuktastu nṛpo mātāmahastadā
tamuvāca śubhaṁ vākyaṁ śirasyāghrāya rāghavam

translations.english: Thus accosted by Bharata, his maternal grandfather, the king, smelling Bharata's head, spoke these auspicious words to that descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छ तातानुजाने त्वां कैकेयी सुप्रजास्त्वया
मातरं कुशलं ब्रूयाः पितरं च परंतप
verses.transliteration:
gaccha tātānujāne tvāṁ kaikeyī suprajāstvayā
mātaraṁ kuśalaṁ brūyāḥ pitaraṁ ca paraṁtapa

translations.english: Go, my child; I permit you. Kaikeyi is mother of a worthy son through you. Do you O subduer of foes, communicate our welfare to both your father and your mother.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोहितं च कुशलं ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमाः
तौ च तात महेष्वासौ भ्रातरु रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
purohitaṁ ca kuśalaṁ ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ
tau ca tāta maheṣvāsau bhrātaru rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Do you likewise communicate the same to the priest and the other principal Brāhmaṇas; as also, my child, to those mighty bowmen, the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मै हस्त्युत्तमांश्चित्रान्कम्बलानजिनानि च
अभिसत्कृत्य कैकेयो भरताय धनं ददौ
verses.transliteration:
tasmai hastyuttamāṁścitrānkambalānajināni ca
abhisatkṛtya kaikeyo bharatāya dhanaṁ dadau

translations.english: Then honouring Bharata, king Kekaya conferred on Bharata wealth consisting of choice elephants maintained (at the palace) and woollen sheets and deerskins.

verses.sanskrit:
रुक्म निष्कसहस्रे द्वे षोडशाश्वशतानि च
सत्कृत्य कैकेयी पुत्रं केकयो धनमादिशत्
verses.transliteration:
rukma niṣkasahasre dve ṣoḍaśāśvaśatāni ca
satkṛtya kaikeyī putraṁ kekayo dhanamādiśat

translations.english: Honouring the son of Kaikeyi, Kekaya gave him two thousand nishkas and six hundred: horses.

verses.sanskrit:
तथामात्यानभिप्रेतान्विश्वास्यांश्च गुणान्वितान्
ददावश्वपतिः शीघ्रं भरतायानुयायिनः
verses.transliteration:
tathāmātyānabhipretānviśvāsyāṁśca guṇānvitān
dadāvaśvapatiḥ śīghraṁ bharatāyānuyāyinaḥ

translations.english: And for following Bharata, Aśvapati without delay assigned a number of goodly, trustworthy, and qualified courtiers.

verses.sanskrit:
ऐरावतानैन्द्रशिरान्नागान्वै प्रियदर्शनान्
खराञ्शीघ्रान्सुसंयुक्तान्मातुलोऽस्मै धनं ददौ
verses.transliteration:
airāvatānaindraśirānnāgānvai priyadarśanān
kharāñśīghrānsusaṁyuktānmātulo'smai dhanaṁ dadau

translations.english: Bharata's maternal uncle conferred on Bharata wealth in the shape of graceful elephants sprung in the īrāvat mountain and the country called Indrasira; as well as fleet and well-broken horses.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःपुरेऽतिसंवृद्धान्व्याघ्रवीर्यबलान्वितान्
दंष्ट्रायुधान्महाकायाञ्शुनश्चोपायनं ददौ
verses.transliteration:
antaḥpure'tisaṁvṛddhānvyāghravīryabalānvitān
daṁṣṭrāyudhānmahākāyāñśunaścopāyanaṁ dadau

translations.english: The king presented him with dogs brought up in the inner apartment, resembling tigers in strength and prowess, furnished with teeth representing weapons, and large of body.

verses.sanskrit:
स मातामहमापृच्छ्य मातुलं च युधाजितम्
रथमारुह्य भरतः शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
sa mātāmahamāpṛcchya mātulaṁ ca yudhājitam
rathamāruhya bharataḥ śatrughnasahito yayau

translations.english: Then after speaking with his maternal grandfather and uncle, Yudhajit, Bharata ascending a car, set out with Satrughna.

verses.sanskrit:
रथान्मण्डलचक्रांश्च योजयित्वा परःशतम्
उष्ट्रगोश्वखरैर्भृत्या भरतं यान्तमन्वयुः
verses.transliteration:
rathānmaṇḍalacakrāṁśca yojayitvā paraḥśatam
uṣṭragośvakharairbhṛtyā bharataṁ yāntamanvayuḥ

translations.english: Thereat servants by means of an hundred cars, furnished with circular wheels, and yoked with camels, oxen, horses, and asses, followed Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
बलेन गुप्तो भरतो महात्मा; सहार्यकस्यात्मसमैरमात्यैः
आदाय शत्रुघ्नमपेतशत्रु;र्गृहाद्ययौ सिद्ध इवेन्द्रलोकात्
verses.transliteration:
balena gupto bharato mahātmā; sahāryakasyātmasamairamātyaiḥ
ādāya śatrughnamapetaśatru;rgṛhādyayau siddha ivendralokāt

translations.english: Protected by the forces and the courtiers of his maternal grandfather dear to him like his ownself, the magnanimous Bharata who had his foes removed, taking with him his brother, Śatrughna, departed from the abode (of the king), like Siddha issuing from the regions of Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्राङ्मुखो राजगृहादभिनिर्याय वीर्यवान्
ह्रादिनीं दूरपारां च प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम्
शतद्रूमतरच्छ्रीमान्नदीमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
sa prāṅmukho rājagṛhādabhiniryāya vīryavān
hrādinīṁ dūrapārāṁ ca pratyaksrotastaraṅgiṇīm
śatadrūmataracchrīmānnadīmikṣvākunandanaḥ

translations.english: Issuing from the palace, the blazing Bharata endowed with prowess went in an easterly direction, and seeing before him the river called Sudāmā, crossed it. Then the auspicious descendant of Iksvāku crossed the broad Hrādinſ coursing westwards, as also the river Satadru.

verses.sanskrit:
एलधाने नदीं तीर्त्वा प्राप्य चापरपर्पटान्
शिलामाकुर्वतीं तीर्त्वा आग्नेयं शल्यकर्तनम्
verses.transliteration:
eladhāne nadīṁ tīrtvā prāpya cāparaparpaṭān
śilāmākurvatīṁ tīrtvā āgneyaṁ śalyakartanam

translations.english: Then crossing a river at Eladhana,' and coming to Aparaparvata”, he crossed the Sila? and the Akurvatī, and arrived at Agneya* and Salyakarsanam. 1. Some read Eladhani. 2. Some read Apharaparyata. 3. The river, according to some is so named because it transforms the surrounding objects to stone. 4. Some make Agneya an epithet to Salyakarsana, meaning, relating to the south-east.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यसंधः शुचिः श्रीमान्प्रेक्षमाणः शिलावहाम्
अत्ययात्स महाशैलान्वनं चैत्ररथं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
satyasaṁdhaḥ śuciḥ śrīmānprekṣamāṇaḥ śilāvahām
atyayātsa mahāśailānvanaṁ caitrarathaṁ prati

translations.english: And having purified himself and seen Silavaha,' that one of truthful purposes passed the Mahacailas,' and entered the forest of Caitraratha. 1. According to Tirtha, Silavaha is a strcam having Āgneya on one side and Salyakarşaņa on the other. 2. Lit, mighty mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
वेगिनीं च कुलिङ्गाख्यां ह्रादिनीं पर्वतावृताम्
यमुनां प्राप्य संतीर्णो बलमाश्वासयत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
veginīṁ ca kuliṅgākhyāṁ hrādinīṁ parvatāvṛtām
yamunāṁ prāpya saṁtīrṇo balamāśvāsayattadā

translations.english: Next crossing the rapid river Kulingā and the Hrādinſ surrounded by hills, as well as the Yamunā, he ordered the forces to halt.

verses.sanskrit:
शीतीकृत्य तु गात्राणि क्लान्तानाश्वास्य वाजिनः
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च प्रायादादाय चोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
śītīkṛtya tu gātrāṇi klāntānāśvāsya vājinaḥ
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca prāyādādāya codakam

translations.english: Then cooling the limbs of the fatigued horses (with water) and refreshing them, Bharata himself bathed there and drank of the water; and then resumed the march, furnished with the water. Then the gentle prince by means of an excellent car, like to the wind-god himself, entered the mighty forest inhabited by various races of men.

verses.sanskrit:
तोरणं दक्षिणार्धेन जम्बूप्रस्थमुपागमत्
वरूथं च ययौ रम्यं ग्रामं दशरथात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
toraṇaṁ dakṣiṇārdhena jambūprasthamupāgamat
varūthaṁ ca yayau ramyaṁ grāmaṁ daśarathātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then proceeding by the south of Toraņa, he came to Jambuprastha. Then Dasaratha's son went to the beautiful village of Varūtha.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र रम्ये वने वासं कृत्वासौ प्राङ्मुखो ययौ
उद्यानमुज्जिहानायाः प्रियका यत्र पादपाः
verses.transliteration:
tatra ramye vane vāsaṁ kṛtvāsau prāṅmukho yayau
udyānamujjihānāyāḥ priyakā yatra pādapāḥ

translations.english: Having for a while stayed at that romantic wood, he proceeded eastwards, and presented himself at the villa of Ujjihānāya, where abound trees (called) Priyaka.

verses.sanskrit:
सालांस्तु प्रियकान्प्राप्य शीघ्रानास्थाय वाजिनः
अनुज्ञाप्याथ भरतो वाहिनीं त्वरितो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
sālāṁstu priyakānprāpya śīghrānāsthāya vājinaḥ
anujñāpyātha bharato vāhinīṁ tvarito yayau

translations.english: Coming to the Priyakas, Bharata speedily yoking the horses, set out without delay, issuing his orders to the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यानानि हि सायाह्ने क्रीडित्वोपरतैर्नरैः
समन्ताद्विप्रधावद्भिः प्रकाशन्ते ममान्यदा
verses.transliteration:
udyānāni hi sāyāhne krīḍitvoparatairnaraiḥ
samantādvipradhāvadbhiḥ prakāśante mamānyadā

translations.english: The gardens where from persons having sported in the evening used to rush out (at day break) wear a different aspect now. Forsaken by the pleasure-seekers, the garden appear to weep.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यत्र यानैर्दृश्यन्ते न गजैर्न च वाजिभिः
निर्यान्तो वाभियान्तो वा नरमुख्या यथापुरम्
verses.transliteration:
na hyatra yānairdṛśyante na gajairna ca vājibhiḥ
niryānto vābhiyānto vā naramukhyā yathāpuram

translations.english: O charioteer, the city appears to me like a wilderness. And I do not as formerly behold the flower of the city leaving or entering her on cars or elephants or horses.

verses.sanskrit:
अनिष्टानि च पापानि पश्यामि विविधानि च
निमित्तान्यमनोज्ञानि तेन सीदति ते मनः
verses.transliteration:
aniṣṭāni ca pāpāni paśyāmi vividhāni ca
nimittānyamanojñāni tena sīdati te manaḥ

translations.english: I witness various evil, unsightly, and unpleasant* omens, and hence my mind is depressed. *The commentator renders amongnani, inauspicious. I venture to differ from him.,

verses.sanskrit:
द्वारेण वैजयन्तेन प्राविशच्छ्रान्तवाहनः
द्वाःस्थैरुत्थाय विजयं पृष्टस्तैः सहितो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
dvāreṇa vaijayantena prāviśacchrāntavāhanaḥ
dvāḥsthairutthāya vijayaṁ pṛṣṭastaiḥ sahito yayau

translations.english: And Bharata having his vehicles fatigued, entered by the Vaijayanta* gate, and went on, followed by the gate-keepers, who enquired after his welfare. *Vijayantena. Another meaning is, By the gate resembling that of Indra's palace.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वनेकाग्रहृदयो द्वाःस्थं प्रत्यर्च्य तं जनम्
सूतमश्वपतेः क्लान्तमब्रवीत्तत्र राघवः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvanekāgrahṛdayo dvāḥsthaṁ pratyarcya taṁ janam
sūtamaśvapateḥ klāntamabravīttatra rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Then courteously telling the warders to desist, he with an agitated heart spoke to the tired charioteer of Aśvapati, “O sinless one, why have I been brought in this haste without any (adequate) reason?" My heart apprehended some evil; and my disposition gives way.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुता नो यादृशाः पूर्वं नृपतीनां विनाशने
आकारास्तानहं सर्वानिह पश्यामि सारथे
verses.transliteration:
śrutā no yādṛśāḥ pūrvaṁ nṛpatīnāṁ vināśane
ākārāstānahaṁ sarvāniha paśyāmi sārathe

translations.english: O charioteer, I see around me all those signs which I had heard told as occurring on the occasion of he death of monarchs.

verses.sanskrit:
मलिनं चाश्रुपूर्णाक्षं दीनं ध्यानपरं कृशम्
सस्त्री पुंसं च पश्यामि जनमुत्कण्ठितं पुरे
verses.transliteration:
malinaṁ cāśrupūrṇākṣaṁ dīnaṁ dhyānaparaṁ kṛśam
sastrī puṁsaṁ ca paśyāmi janamutkaṇṭhitaṁ pure

translations.english: And in temples and Caityas birds and beasts appear dispirited. And in the city I behold men and women pale and woe-begone and emaciated and anxious, with tears filling their eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतः सूतं तं दीनमानसः
तान्यनिष्टान्ययोध्यायां प्रेक्ष्य राजगृहं ययौ
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā bharataḥ sūtaṁ taṁ dīnamānasaḥ
tānyaniṣṭānyayodhyāyāṁ prekṣya rājagṛhaṁ yayau

translations.english: Having said this to the charioteer, Bharata, beholding these inauspicious sights, entered the palace of the king with a depressed heart.

verses.sanskrit:
तां शून्यशृङ्गाटकवेश्मरथ्यां; रजोरुणद्वारकपाटयन्त्राम्
दृष्ट्वा पुरीमिन्द्रपुरी प्रकाशां; दुःखेन संपूर्णतरो बभूव
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ śūnyaśṛṅgāṭakaveśmarathyāṁ; rajoruṇadvārakapāṭayantrām
dṛṣṭvā purīmindrapurī prakāśāṁ; duḥkhena saṁpūrṇataro babhūva

translations.english: Beholding the city resembling the city of Indra, with her crossings and houses and roads void of people, and the doors and hinges covered with dust, Bharata was filled with greater grief.

verses.sanskrit:
बहूनि पश्यन्मनसोऽप्रियाणि; यान्यन्न्यदा नास्य पुरे बभूवुः
अवाक्शिरा दीनमना नहृष्टः; पितुर्महात्मा प्रविवेश वेश्म
verses.transliteration:
bahūni paśyanmanaso'priyāṇi; yānyannyadā nāsya pure babhūvuḥ
avākśirā dīnamanā nahṛṣṭaḥ; piturmahātmā praviveśa veśma

translations.english: And witnessing many unpleasant things which he had never seen during the life of the monarch, that high-souled one entered the mansion of his father, bending his head, depressed in spirits, and with his mind extremely aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
अपश्यंस्तु ततस्तत्र पितरं पितुरालये
जगाम भरतो द्रष्टुं मातरं मातुरालये
verses.transliteration:
apaśyaṁstu tatastatra pitaraṁ piturālaye
jagāma bharato draṣṭuṁ mātaraṁ māturālaye

translations.english: Not having seen his father in his father's quarters, Bharata went to his mother's apartment for seeing her. *The text is evidently corrupt. From the sequel it appears that Bharata has not seen the king at that time. That commentator, however, passes over the point in silence, which is to be accounted for by the slovenliness of the way of though characterising the Sanskrit commentators in general. An English commentator would have considered the matter as of very great importance, but his Hindu brother takes it quietly, and passes on with indifference.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुप्राप्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा कैकेयी प्रोषितं सुतम्
उत्पपात तदा हृष्टा त्यक्त्वा सौवर्णमानसम्
verses.transliteration:
anuprāptaṁ tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā kaikeyī proṣitaṁ sutam
utpapāta tadā hṛṣṭā tyaktvā sauvarṇamānasam

translations.english: On seeing her son before her after his sojourn from home, Kaikeyi delighted, rose up from her golden seat.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रविश्यैव धर्मात्मा स्वगृहं श्रीविवर्जितम्
भरतः प्रेक्ष्य जग्राह जनन्याश्चरणौ शुभौ
verses.transliteration:
sa praviśyaiva dharmātmā svagṛhaṁ śrīvivarjitam
bharataḥ prekṣya jagrāha jananyāścaraṇau śubhau

translations.english: On entering his own quarter which he found deprived of grace, the virtuous Bharata took hold of his mother's auspicious feet.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मूर्ध्नि समुपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनम्
अङ्के भरतमारोप्य प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ mūrdhni samupāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinam
aṅke bharatamāropya praṣṭuṁ samupacakrame

translations.english: Then smelling the crown of his head and embracing him and taking that illustrious one on her lap, Kaikeyi addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य ते कतिचिद्रात्र्यश्च्युतस्यार्यकवेश्मनः
अपि नाध्वश्रमः शीघ्रं रथेनापततस्तव
verses.transliteration:
adya te katicidrātryaścyutasyāryakaveśmanaḥ
api nādhvaśramaḥ śīghraṁ rathenāpatatastava

translations.english: How many days hence did you leave the residence of the revered one? Have you felt any fatigue on the way incident to the car proceeding swiftly?

verses.sanskrit:
आर्यकस्ते सुकुशलो युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव
प्रवासाच्च सुखं पुत्र सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
āryakaste sukuśalo yudhājinmātulastava
pravāsācca sukhaṁ putra sarvaṁ me vaktumarhasi

translations.english: And is the revered one will, and your maternal uncle, Yuddhajit? And, my son, have you passed your time pleasantly during your sojourn? It behoves you to tell me all this.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं पृष्ठस्तु कैकेय्या प्रियं पार्थिवनन्दनः
आचष्ट भरतः सर्वं मात्रे राजीवलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ pṛṣṭhastu kaikeyyā priyaṁ pārthivanandanaḥ
ācaṣṭa bharataḥ sarvaṁ mātre rājīvalocanaḥ

translations.english: Thus asked that son of the king, Bharata, furnished with eyes resembling lotuses, told his mother that all was well.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य मे सप्तमी रात्रिश्च्युतस्यार्यकवेश्मनः
अम्बायाः कुशली तातो युधाजिन्मातुलश्च मे
verses.transliteration:
adya me saptamī rātriścyutasyāryakaveśmanaḥ
ambāyāḥ kuśalī tāto yudhājinmātulaśca me

translations.english: Seven nights hence I took leave of that revered one's residence. My mother's sire is well, as also my maternal uncle, Yuddhajit.

verses.sanskrit:
राजवाक्यहरैर्दूतैस्त्वर्यमाणोऽहमागतः
यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि तदम्बा वक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
rājavākyaharairdūtaistvaryamāṇo'hamāgataḥ
yadahaṁ praṣṭumicchāmi tadambā vaktumarhasi

translations.english: My vehicles had got tired in consequence of bearing the wealth and jewels which that subduer of foes, the king, had bestowed on me. And it is for this reason that I have come in advance of them. Urged by the royal emissaries, I have come here so swiftly. But it behoves my mother to tell me what I wish to ask.

verses.sanskrit:
शून्योऽयं शयनीयस्ते पर्यङ्को हेमभूषितः
न चायमिक्ष्वाकुजनः प्रहृष्टः प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
śūnyo'yaṁ śayanīyaste paryaṅko hemabhūṣitaḥ
na cāyamikṣvākujanaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratibhāti me

translations.english: This sleeping bedstead of yours adorned with gold is empty. I do not see the race of Ikşvāku in their usual good spirits.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा भवति भूयिष्ठमिहाम्बाया निवेशने
तमहं नाद्य पश्यामि द्रष्टुमिच्छन्निहागतः
verses.transliteration:
rājā bhavati bhūyiṣṭhamihāmbāyā niveśane
tamahaṁ nādya paśyāmi draṣṭumicchannihāgataḥ

translations.english: The king generally remains in this apartment of my mother. But coming here with the desire of seeing him, I do not today find him at this place.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्ग्रहीष्ये चरणौ तं ममाख्याहि पृच्छतः
आहोस्विदम्ब ज्येष्ठायाः कौसल्याया निवेशने
verses.transliteration:
piturgrahīṣye caraṇau taṁ mamākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
āhosvidamba jyeṣṭhāyāḥ kausalyāyā niveśane

translations.english: I would take the feet of my father. Do you tell me who ask you. Is he in the apartment of my eldest mother, Kausalya?

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रत्युवाच कैकेयी प्रियवद्घोरमप्रियम्
अजानन्तं प्रजानन्ती राज्यलोभेन मोहिता
या गतिः सर्वभूतानां तां गतिं ते पिता गतः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ pratyuvāca kaikeyī priyavadghoramapriyam
ajānantaṁ prajānantī rājyalobhena mohitā
yā gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ tāṁ gatiṁ te pitā gataḥ

translations.english: Blinded by the lust of dominion, and looking upon that as desirable (to Bharata) which was exceedingly disagreeable (to him), Kaikeyi replied to him, who did not know what had transpired.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं धर्माभिजनवाञ्शुचिः
पपात सहसा भूमौ पितृशोकबलार्दितः
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā bharato vākyaṁ dharmābhijanavāñśuciḥ
papāta sahasā bhūmau pitṛśokabalārditaḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words, Bharata of pure ways sprung from a righteous race, smite with the vehemence of sorrow on account of his father, suddenly fell down to the earth. And exclaiming in the anguish of spirit and in the excess of grief, the words, "Ah me! I am undone!" that mightyarmed one endowed with prowess, fell down, tossing about his arms.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शोकेन संवीतः पितुर्मरणदुःखितः
विललाप महातेजा भ्रान्ताकुलितचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śokena saṁvītaḥ piturmaraṇaduḥkhitaḥ
vilalāpa mahātejā bhrāntākulitacetanaḥ

translations.english: Then, overwhelmed with and distressed at the death of his father, that highly sorrow energetic one, with his senses distracted, indulged in lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्सुरुचिरं भाति पितुर्मे शयनं पुरा
तदिदं न विभात्यद्य विहीनं तेन धीमता
verses.transliteration:
etatsuruciraṁ bhāti piturme śayanaṁ purā
tadidaṁ na vibhātyadya vihīnaṁ tena dhīmatā

translations.english: This bed of my father used to look like the speckless welkin at night crowned with the moon, after the clouds have gone off. But to-day, deprived of that intellignet one, it ceases to shine, like the firmament without the moon or the sea devoid of its waters.

verses.sanskrit:
तमार्तं देवसंकाशं समीक्ष्य पतितं भुवि
उत्थापयित्वा शोकार्तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tamārtaṁ devasaṁkāśaṁ samīkṣya patitaṁ bhuvi
utthāpayitvā śokārtaṁ vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing that one resembling a celestial fallen to the earth, stricken with sorrow, like to a bough of the Sāla that had been severed in the wood by an axe, his mother raising up he distressed son like a mad elephant or the sun or the moon, addressed him.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे राजपुत्र महायशः
त्वद्विधा न हि शोचन्ति सन्तः सदसि संमताः
verses.transliteration:
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kiṁ śeṣe rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
tvadvidhā na hi śocanti santaḥ sadasi saṁmatāḥ

translations.english: Arise, arise. Why do you lie down, O illustrious son of the king? Persons like you having their senses under perfect control, and approved by men of culture, do not grieve.

verses.sanskrit:
स रुदत्या चिरं कालं भूमौ विपरिवृत्य च
जननीं प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa rudatyā ciraṁ kālaṁ bhūmau viparivṛtya ca
jananīṁ pratyuvācedaṁ śokairbahubhirāvṛtaḥ

translations.english: Having wept for a long while with his body rolling on the earth, Bharata afflicted with manifold grief, answered his mother, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिषेक्ष्यति रामं तु राजा यज्ञं नु यक्ष्यति
इत्यहं कृतसंकल्पो हृष्टो यात्रामयासिषम्
verses.transliteration:
abhiṣekṣyati rāmaṁ tu rājā yajñaṁ nu yakṣyati
ityahaṁ kṛtasaṁkalpo hṛṣṭo yātrāmayāsiṣam

translations.english: The king will install Rāma and celebrate a sacrifice' concluding this for certain, I had joyfully gone from hence.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं ह्यन्यथा भूतं व्यवदीर्णं मनो मम
पितरं यो न पश्यामि नित्यं प्रियहिते रतम्
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ hyanyathā bhūtaṁ vyavadīrṇaṁ mano mama
pitaraṁ yo na paśyāmi nityaṁ priyahite ratam

translations.english: But it has fallen out otherwise. That I do not behold my father ever engaged in the dear welfare (of his subjects) cleaves my heart mother.

verses.sanskrit:
अम्ब केनात्यगाद्राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते
धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
amba kenātyagādrājā vyādhinā mayyanāgate
dhanyā rāmādayaḥ sarve yaiḥ pitā saṁskṛtaḥ svayam

translations.english: Of what ailment has the king breathed his last during my absence? Blessed are Rāma and others who have personally performed my sire's last rites.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं मां महाराजः प्राप्तं जानाति कीर्तिमान्
उपजिघ्रेद्धि मां मूर्ध्नि तातः संनम्य सत्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ māṁ mahārājaḥ prāptaṁ jānāti kīrtimān
upajighreddhi māṁ mūrdhni tātaḥ saṁnamya satvaram

translations.english: Surely the renowned monarch does not know that I have come. (If he had done so), pressing down my head, my father would at once have smelt it.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः
येन मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति
verses.transliteration:
kva sa pāṇiḥ sukhasparśastātasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
yena māṁ rajasā dhvastamabhīkṣṇaṁ parimārjati

translations.english: Where is now the soft hand of that energetic one which used to rub my person when it was covered with dust?

verses.sanskrit:
यो मे भ्राता पिता बन्धुर्यस्य दासोऽस्मि धीमतः
तस्य मां शीघ्रमाख्याहि रामस्याक्लिष्ट कर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
yo me bhrātā pitā bandhuryasya dāso'smi dhīmataḥ
tasya māṁ śīghramākhyāhi rāmasyākliṣṭa karmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Do you now without delay convey the news of my arrival to the vigorous Rāma, who is at once my father, brother and friend, and whose beloved servant I am.

verses.sanskrit:
पिता हि भवति ज्येष्ठो धर्ममार्यस्य जानतः
तस्य पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि स हीदानीं गतिर्मम
verses.transliteration:
pitā hi bhavati jyeṣṭho dharmamāryasya jānataḥ
tasya pādau grahīṣyāmi sa hīdānīṁ gatirmama

translations.english: The eldest brother of one that is noble and cognisant of morality, becomes his father. I shall take hold of his feet: he is now my refuge.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्ये किमब्रवीद्राजा पिता मे सत्यविक्रमः
पश्चिमं साधु संदेशमिच्छामि श्रोतुमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ārye kimabravīdrājā pitā me satyavikramaḥ
paścimaṁ sādhu saṁdeśamicchāmi śrotumātmanaḥ

translations.english: And, O noble lady, what did that virtuous one cognizant of virtue, that pre-eminently pious one, firm in his vow, and having truth for prowess, even my father, say? I wish to hear news concerning us relative to the last moments of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
इति पृष्टा यथातत्त्वं कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
रामेति राजा विलपन्हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च
स महात्मा परं लोकं गतो गतिमतां वरः
verses.transliteration:
iti pṛṣṭā yathātattvaṁ kaikeyī vākyamabravīt
rāmeti rājā vilapanhā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
sa mahātmā paraṁ lokaṁ gato gatimatāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: Thus asked, Kaikeyi related all as it had happened, saying, “Bewailing 'Ah Rama!' 'Ah Sita!' “Ah Laksmana!' that magnanimous one, the foremost of those that have attained to excellent state (after death), has gone to the next world coming under the law of time.

verses.sanskrit:
सिद्धार्थास्तु नरा राममागतं सीतया सह
लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्
verses.transliteration:
siddhārthāstu narā rāmamāgataṁ sītayā saha
lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābāhuṁ drakṣyanti punarāgatam

translations.english: Your father like a mighty elephant fast bound with a cord, said to me these words during his last moments, "Blessed are they that shall see Rāma and the mighty-armed Lakşmaņa returned along with Sītā.”

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विषसादैव द्वितीया प्रियशंसनात्
विषण्णवदनो भूत्वा भूयः पप्रच्छ मातरम्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā viṣasādaiva dvitīyā priyaśaṁsanāt
viṣaṇṇavadano bhūtvā bhūyaḥ papraccha mātaram

translations.english: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending a second misfortune was deeply moved; and with a sad countenance, he again asked his mother.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व चेदानीं स धर्मात्मा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया च समं गतः
verses.transliteration:
kva cedānīṁ sa dharmātmā kausalyānandavardhanaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca samaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Where has gone that righteous-souled one, the enchancer of Kausalya's joy, along with Laks maņa and Sītā?

verses.sanskrit:
तथा पृष्टा यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
मातास्य युगपद्वाक्यं विप्रियं प्रियशङ्कया
verses.transliteration:
tathā pṛṣṭā yathātattvamākhyātumupacakrame
mātāsya yugapadvākyaṁ vipriyaṁ priyaśaṅkayā

translations.english: Thus questioned, his mother at the same time duly said in words which although highly unwelcome, she took as agreeable to Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि राजसुतः पुत्र चीरवासा महावनम्
दण्डकान्सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणानुचरो गतः
verses.transliteration:
sa hi rājasutaḥ putra cīravāsā mahāvanam
daṇḍakānsaha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇānucaro gataḥ

translations.english: O son, that son of the king wearing bark has repaired to the forest of Dandaka, along with Vaidehi and followed by Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्त्रस्तो भ्रातुश्चारित्रशङ्कया
स्वस्य वंशस्य माहात्म्यात्प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā bharatastrasto bhrātuścāritraśaṅkayā
svasya vaṁśasya māhātmyātpraṣṭuṁ samupacakrame
