translations.english: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending some moral lapse on the part of his brother from the dignity of his race, asked in agitation.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्न ब्राह्मणवधं हृतं रामेण कस्यचित्
कच्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः
verses.transliteration:
kaccinna brāhmaṇavadhaṁ hṛtaṁ rāmeṇa kasyacit
kaccinnāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṁsitaḥ

translations.english: Has Rāma deprived any Brāhmaṇa of his wealth? Or has he wronged any innocent person, whether rich or poor?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्न परदारान्वा राजपुत्रोऽभिमन्यते
कस्मात्स दण्डकारण्ये भ्रूणहेव विवासितः
verses.transliteration:
kaccinna paradārānvā rājaputro'bhimanyate
kasmātsa daṇḍakāraṇye bhrūṇaheva vivāsitaḥ

translations.english: Has the fancy of the prince gone after the wife of another? For what reason has brother Rāma been banished?

verses.sanskrit:
अथास्य चपला माता तत्स्वकर्म यथातथम्
तेनैव स्त्रीस्वभावेन व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
athāsya capalā mātā tatsvakarma yathātatham
tenaiva strīsvabhāvena vyāhartumupacakrame

translations.english: Thereat his volatile mother, influenced by her feminine nature, related faithfully to him her own doings.

verses.sanskrit:
न ब्राह्मणधनं किंचिद्धृतं रामेण कस्यचित्
कश्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः
न रामः परदारांश्च चक्षुर्भ्यामपि पश्यति
verses.transliteration:
na brāhmaṇadhanaṁ kiṁciddhṛtaṁ rāmeṇa kasyacit
kaścinnāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṁsitaḥ
na rāmaḥ paradārāṁśca cakṣurbhyāmapi paśyati

translations.english: Rāma has deprived no Brāhmaṇa of his property, nor has any innocent person rich or otherwise been wronged by him, nor does he ever with his eyes look at the wife of another.

verses.sanskrit:
मया तु पुत्र श्रुत्वैव रामस्यैवाभिषेचनम्
याचितस्ते पिता राज्यं रामस्य च विवासनम्
verses.transliteration:
mayā tu putra śrutvaiva rāmasyaivābhiṣecanam
yācitaste pitā rājyaṁ rāmasya ca vivāsanam

translations.english: O son, as soon as I heard of Råma's (coming) installation, I asked for the kingdom to be conferred on you, and Rāma to be banished.

verses.sanskrit:
स स्ववृत्तिं समास्थाय पिता ते तत्तथाकरोत्
रामश्च सहसौमित्रिः प्रेषितः सह सीतया
verses.transliteration:
sa svavṛttiṁ samāsthāya pitā te tattathākarot
rāmaśca sahasaumitriḥ preṣitaḥ saha sītayā

translations.english: Thereupon, he, staying by his promise, did accordingly: Rāma has been banished along with Sumitrā's son and Sītā. Not seeing his beloved son, the illustrious lord of earth, stricken by grief on his account, has breathed his last.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया त्विदानीं धर्मज्ञ राजत्वमवलम्ब्यताम्
त्वत्कृते हि मया सर्वमिदमेवंविधं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
tvayā tvidānīṁ dharmajña rājatvamavalambyatām
tvatkṛte hi mayā sarvamidamevaṁvidhaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: Do you now, O you cognizant of duty, take charge of the kingdom. I have done all this in your interests.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्पुत्र शीघ्रं विधिना विधिज्ञै;र्वसिष्ठमुख्यैः सहितो द्विजेन्द्रैः
संकाल्य राजानमदीनसत्त्व;मात्मानमुर्व्यामभिषेचयस्व
verses.transliteration:
tatputra śīghraṁ vidhinā vidhijñai;rvasiṣṭhamukhyaiḥ sahito dvijendraiḥ
saṁkālya rājānamadīnasattva;mātmānamurvyāmabhiṣecayasva

translations.english: Having with the help of the principal Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, duly performed the funeral obsequies of the king, do you, without suffering your energy to depart, install yourself in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु पितरं वृत्तं भ्रातरु च विवासितौ
भरतो दुःखसंतप्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu pitaraṁ vṛttaṁ bhrātaru ca vivāsitau
bharato duḥkhasaṁtapta idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing of his father's death and the exile of his brothers, Bharata burning in grief, said these words.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नुण्कार्यं हतस्येह मम राज्येन शोचतः
विहीनस्याथ पित्रा च भ्रात्रा पितृसमेन च
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nuṇkāryaṁ hatasyeha mama rājyena śocataḥ
vihīnasyātha pitrā ca bhrātrā pitṛsamena ca

translations.english: Deprived of my father as well as my brother like to a father, what shall I bewailing them and undone by you do with the kingdom?

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखे मे दुःखमकरोर्व्रणे क्षारमिवादधाः
राजानं प्रेतभावस्थं कृत्वा रामं च तापसम्
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhe me duḥkhamakarorvraṇe kṣāramivādadhāḥ
rājānaṁ pretabhāvasthaṁ kṛtvā rāmaṁ ca tāpasam

translations.english: You, like one throwing alkali on a sore, have, by bringing about the death of the king and making Rāma an ascetic, heaped grief on grief.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलस्य त्वमभावाय कालरात्रिरिवागता
अङ्गारमुपगूह्य स्म पिता मे नावबुद्धवान्
verses.transliteration:
kulasya tvamabhāvāya kālarātririvāgatā
aṅgāramupagūhya sma pitā me nāvabuddhavān

translations.english: You have come like the fatal night for the destruction of this race. Not under-standing it, my father embraced live coal.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिते
दुष्करं यदि जीवेतां प्राप्य त्वां जननीं मम
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putraśokābhipīḍite
duṣkaraṁ yadi jīvetāṁ prāpya tvāṁ jananīṁ mama

translations.english: Afflicted with grief for their son, even if Kausalya and Sumitrā live, it will be hard for them to do so in the presence of you, my mother.

verses.sanskrit:
ननु त्वार्योऽपि धर्मात्मा त्वयि वृत्तिमनुत्तमाम्
वर्तते गुरुवृत्तिज्ञो यथा मातरि वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
nanu tvāryo'pi dharmātmā tvayi vṛttimanuttamām
vartate guruvṛttijño yathā mātari vartate

translations.english: Surely the noble and virtuous Råma, well knowing his duties towards his superiors, regards you as highly as he does his own mother.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ज्येष्ठा हि मे माता कौसल्या दीर्घदर्शिनी
त्वयि धर्मं समास्थाय भगिन्यामिव वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
tathā jyeṣṭhā hi me mātā kausalyā dīrghadarśinī
tvayi dharmaṁ samāsthāya bhaginyāmiva vartate

translations.english: In the same way, my eldest mother, the farsighted Kausalyā, doing her duties by you, bears herself like a sister.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः पुत्रं कृतात्मानं चीरवल्कलवाससम्
प्रस्थाप्य वनवासाय कथं पापे न शोचसि
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ putraṁ kṛtātmānaṁ cīravalkalavāsasam
prasthāpya vanavāsāya kathaṁ pāpe na śocasi

translations.english: Why, O sinful one, having sent to the woods her magnanimous son, clad in bark, do you not grieve?

verses.sanskrit:
अपापदर्शिनं शूरं कृतात्मानं यशस्विनम्
प्रव्राज्य चीरवसनं किं नु पश्यसि कारणम्
verses.transliteration:
apāpadarśinaṁ śūraṁ kṛtātmānaṁ yaśasvinam
pravrājya cīravasanaṁ kiṁ nu paśyasi kāraṇam

translations.english: Having exiled the famous and heroic Rāma seeing no sin, clad in bark, what benefit do you perceive as yours?

verses.sanskrit:
लुब्धाया विदितो मन्ये न तेऽहं राघवं प्रति
तथा ह्यनर्थो राज्यार्थं त्वया नीतो महानयम्
verses.transliteration:
lubdhāyā vidito manye na te'haṁ rāghavaṁ prati
tathā hyanartho rājyārthaṁ tvayā nīto mahānayam

translations.english: I deem that you did not know how very highly I regarded Rāghava; and therefore it is that you have brought this mighty calamity.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि पुरुषव्याघ्रावपश्यन्रामलक्ष्मणौ
केन शक्तिप्रभावेन राज्यं रक्षितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi puruṣavyāghrāvapaśyanrāmalakṣmaṇau
kena śaktiprabhāvena rājyaṁ rakṣitumutsahe

translations.english: Not seeing those chiefs of men, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, by virtue of whose energy can I venture to rule the kingdom?

verses.sanskrit:
तं हि नित्यं महाराजो बलवन्तं महाबलः
अपाश्रितोऽभूद्धर्मात्मा मेरुर्मेरुवनं यथा
verses.transliteration:
taṁ hi nityaṁ mahārājo balavantaṁ mahābalaḥ
apāśrito'bhūddharmātmā merurmeruvanaṁ yathā

translations.english: The monarch was ever protected by that powerful one possessed of mighty energy, as Meru is protected by its forest.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं कथमिमं भारं महाधुर्यसमुद्यतम्
दम्यो धुरमिवासाद्य सहेयं केन चौजसा
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ kathamimaṁ bhāraṁ mahādhuryasamudyatam
damyo dhuramivāsādya saheyaṁ kena caujasā

translations.english: Like a calf burdened with a load capable of being borne by a mighty ox, by what energy shall I bear this burden which was borne by an exceedingly strong person?

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा मे भवेच्छक्तिर्योगैर्बुद्धिबलेन वा
सकामां न करिष्यामि त्वामहं पुत्रगर्धिनीम्
निवर्तयिष्यामि वनाद्भ्रातरं स्वजनप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā me bhavecchaktiryogairbuddhibalena vā
sakāmāṁ na kariṣyāmi tvāmahaṁ putragardhinīm
nivartayiṣyāmi vanādbhrātaraṁ svajanapriyam

translations.english: And even if this strength be mine through yoga or vigour of intellect, I will not crown with success the hopes of you, proud of your son.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतो महात्मा; प्रियेतरैर्वाक्यगणैस्तुदंस्ताम्
शोकातुरश्चापि ननाद भूयः; सिंहो यथा पर्वतगह्वरस्थः
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā bharato mahātmā; priyetarairvākyagaṇaistudaṁstām
śokāturaścāpi nanāda bhūyaḥ; siṁho yathā parvatagahvarasthaḥ

translations.english: The high-souled Bharata afflicted (his mother) with multitudes of words causing pain; and distressed with grief, emitted sounds like to a lion in the cave of Mandāra.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तथा गर्हयित्वा तु मातरं भरतस्तदा
रोषेण महताविष्टः पुनरेवाब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tathā garhayitvā tu mātaraṁ bharatastadā
roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭaḥ punarevābravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: Having thus reproved his mother in great wrath, Bharata said again.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्याद्भ्रंशस्व कैकेयि नृशंसे दुष्टचारिणि
परित्यक्ता च धर्मेण मा मृतं रुदती भव
verses.transliteration:
rājyādbhraṁśasva kaikeyi nṛśaṁse duṣṭacāriṇi
parityaktā ca dharmeṇa mā mṛtaṁ rudatī bhava

translations.english: Do you bear yourself from this kingdom, O heartless and wicked Kaikeyī. Having been lost to righteousness, do not you lament me dead.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु तेऽदूषयद्राजा रामो वा भृशधार्मिकः
ययोर्मृत्युर्विवासश्च त्वत्कृते तुल्यमागतौ
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu te'dūṣayadrājā rāmo vā bhṛśadhārmikaḥ
yayormṛtyurvivāsaśca tvatkṛte tulyamāgatau

translations.english: What qualities of yours were taxed by the king or the exceedingly virtuous Rāma, that both of them simultaneously have come by death and exile respectively through your agency?

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रूणहत्यामसि प्राप्ता कुलस्यास्य विनाशनात्
कैकेयि नरकं गच्छ मा च भर्तुः सलोकताम्
verses.transliteration:
bhrūṇahatyāmasi prāptā kulasyāsya vināśanāt
kaikeyi narakaṁ gaccha mā ca bhartuḥ salokatām

translations.english: O Kaikeyī, you have been guilty of homicide in consequence of the destruction of this race. Do you go to hell, never to the world attained by my father.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्त्वया हीदृशं पापं कृतं घोरेण कर्मणा
सर्वलोकप्रियं हित्वा ममाप्यापादितं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
yattvayā hīdṛśaṁ pāpaṁ kṛtaṁ ghoreṇa karmaṇā
sarvalokapriyaṁ hitvā mamāpyāpāditaṁ bhayam

translations.english: Since, renouncing Rāma dear to all, you have committed this sin by your grim act and brought me into fear.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वत्कृते मे पिता वृत्तो रामश्चारण्यमाश्रितः
अयशो जीवलोके च त्वयाहं प्रतिपादितः
verses.transliteration:
tvatkṛte me pitā vṛtto rāmaścāraṇyamāśritaḥ
ayaśo jīvaloke ca tvayāhaṁ pratipāditaḥ

translations.english: Through you has my father met with his end, and Rāma has taken refuge in the woods; and it is through you that I have come to ignominy among all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
मातृरूपे ममामित्रे नृशंसे राज्यकामुके
न तेऽहमभिभाष्योऽस्मि दुर्वृत्ते पतिघातिनि
verses.transliteration:
mātṛrūpe mamāmitre nṛśaṁse rājyakāmuke
na te'hamabhibhāṣyo'smi durvṛtte patighātini

translations.english: O you enemy of mine in the guise of a mother! O fell one! O you that covetest the kingdom! do you not speak to me, O wicked wretch!

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या मम मातरः
दुःखेन महताविष्टास्त्वां प्राप्य कुलदूषिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāścānyā mama mātaraḥ
duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭāstvāṁ prāpya kuladūṣiṇīm

translations.english: O slayer of your husband! it is because of you, stainer of your race, that Kausalyā, Sumiträ, and other mothers of mine have been overwhelmed with a mighty sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्प्रधानासि तत्पापं मयि पित्रा विनाकृते
भ्रातृभ्यां च परित्यक्ते सर्वलोकस्य चाप्रिये
verses.transliteration:
yatpradhānāsi tatpāpaṁ mayi pitrā vinākṛte
bhrātṛbhyāṁ ca parityakte sarvalokasya cāpriye

translations.english: You are never the daughter of the pious and intelligent Aśvapati, you are a Rākṣasī born in that race, you that have destroyed my father's race, inasmuch as the virtuous and heroic Rāma ever observing truth has been sent to the woods and my father has ascended heaven through your agency; inasmuch as you that have perpetrated this arch offence, have laid this sin on me, who have been forsaken by my sire, renounced by my brothers, and come by universal disfavour.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्यां धर्मसंयुक्तां वियुक्तां पापनिश्चये
कृत्वा कं प्राप्स्यसे त्वद्य लोकं निरयगामिनी
verses.transliteration:
kausalyāṁ dharmasaṁyuktāṁ viyuktāṁ pāpaniścaye
kṛtvā kaṁ prāpsyase tvadya lokaṁ nirayagāminī

translations.english: O you of sinful ways, having separated the virtuous Kausalya (from her son), what world, O you that repairest to hell, shall be your portion?

verses.sanskrit:
किं नावबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतं बन्धुसंश्रयम्
ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं रामं कौसल्यायात्मसंभवम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nāvabudhyase krūre niyataṁ bandhusaṁśrayam
jyeṣṭhaṁ pitṛsamaṁ rāmaṁ kausalyāyātmasaṁbhavam

translations.english: Does you not, O tortuous one, know that that one sprung from Kucalya's, self, my eldest brother Räma, who is like a father to me, has ever been the refuge of his friends?

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गजः पुत्रो हृदयाच्चापि जायते
तस्मात्प्रियतरो मातुः प्रियत्वान्न तु बान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
aṅgapratyaṅgajaḥ putro hṛdayāccāpi jāyate
tasmātpriyataro mātuḥ priyatvānna tu bāndhavaḥ

translations.english: A son born from all the limbs of his mother, comes out from her heart, and therefore it is that he is far dearer to his mother, albeit her friends are dear to her.* *Angapratyangaja: at., born from the limbs principal and minor. The commentator recounts the face, the breast, the abdomen, the hands and the feet as constituting the former; and eyes, fingers, etc., as the latter.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्यदा किल धर्मज्ञा सुरभिः सुरसंमता
वहमानौ ददर्शोर्व्यां पुत्रौ विगतचेतसौ
verses.transliteration:
anyadā kila dharmajñā surabhiḥ surasaṁmatā
vahamānau dadarśorvyāṁ putrau vigatacetasau

translations.english: Once on a time, it is related by persons cognizant of morality, Surabhi regarded by the celestials, beheld two of her sons toiling on earth and seeming to be deprived of their senses.

verses.sanskrit:
तावर्धदिवसे श्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रौ महीतले
रुरोद पुत्र शोकेन बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
tāvardhadivase śrāntau dṛṣṭvā putrau mahītale
ruroda putra śokena bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā

translations.english: And, when the day had been half spent, seeing her sons fatigued on earth, she stricken with grief for them, began to weep with tears flooding her eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
अधस्ताद्व्रजतस्तस्याः सुरराज्ञो महात्मनः
बिन्दवः पतिता गात्रे सूक्ष्माः सुरभिगन्धिनः
verses.transliteration:
adhastādvrajatastasyāḥ surarājño mahātmanaḥ
bindavaḥ patitā gātre sūkṣmāḥ surabhigandhinaḥ

translations.english: And it came to pass that as the magnanimous sovereign of the celestials was passing below, her fine and fragrant tear drops fell on his person.

verses.sanskrit:
तां दृष्ट्वा शोकसंतप्तां वज्रपाणिर्यशस्विनीम्
इन्द्रः प्राञ्जलिरुद्विग्नः सुरराजोऽब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dṛṣṭvā śokasaṁtaptāṁ vajrapāṇiryaśasvinīm
indraḥ prāñjalirudvignaḥ surarājo'bravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that illustrious one burning in grief, the wielder of the thunder-bolt, Indra the lord of the celestials, waxing anxious, with joined hands said.

verses.sanskrit:
भयं कच्चिन्न चास्मासु कुतश्चिद्विद्यते महत्
कुतो निमित्तः शोकस्ते ब्रूहि सर्वहितैषिणि
verses.transliteration:
bhayaṁ kaccinna cāsmāsu kutaścidvidyate mahat
kuto nimittaḥ śokaste brūhi sarvahitaiṣiṇi

translations.english: Is there any great danger in any quarter? Do you, O you that are intent on the welfare of all, say, whence is this grief of yours?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सुरभिः सुरराजेन धीमता
पत्युवाच ततो धीरा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदा
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu surabhiḥ surarājena dhīmatā
patyuvāca tato dhīrā vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradā

translations.english: Thus addressed by the intelligent king of the celestials, that one well skilled in speech, the sedate Surabhi answered.

verses.sanskrit:
शान्तं पातं न वः किंचित्कुतश्चिदमराधिप
अहं तु मग्नौ शोचामि स्वपुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ
verses.transliteration:
śāntaṁ pātaṁ na vaḥ kiṁcitkutaścidamarādhipa
ahaṁ tu magnau śocāmi svaputrau viṣame sthitau

translations.english: Auspiciousness, O lord of celestials! No sin is yours. But I mourn my sons fallen into evil plight, having seen them lean, distressed, and burnt by the rays of the sun, Balivardas afflicted by the wicked-minded ploughman.

verses.sanskrit:
मम कायात्प्रसूतौ हि दुःखितौ भार पीडितौ
यौ दृष्ट्वा परितप्येऽहं नास्ति पुत्रसमः प्रियः
verses.transliteration:
mama kāyātprasūtau hi duḥkhitau bhāra pīḍitau
yau dṛṣṭvā paritapye'haṁ nāsti putrasamaḥ priyaḥ

translations.english: Seeing those that have been born of my body, cast down and in trouble, I grieve: there is none that is dear like to a son.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्याः पुत्र सहस्राणि सापि शोचति कामधुक्
किं पुनर्या विना रामं कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yasyāḥ putra sahasrāṇi sāpi śocati kāmadhuk
kiṁ punaryā vinā rāmaṁ kausalyā vartayiṣyati

translations.english: Even that one yielding whatever is asked, auspicious, crowned with the choicest virtues,। although having all natural functions, showing equal kindness to all, and of unequalled character, who maintain all creatures, she who has a thousand sons, grieves (for her sons). How can then Kausalyā carry on existence without Rāma?

verses.sanskrit:
एकपुत्रा च साध्वी च विवत्सेयं त्वया कृता
तस्मात्त्वं सततं दुःखं प्रेत्य चेह च लप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
ekaputrā ca sādhvī ca vivatseyaṁ tvayā kṛtā
tasmāttvaṁ satataṁ duḥkhaṁ pretya ceha ca lapsyase

translations.english: Chaste and having an only son, that lady has through you been separated from her son, (like a cow separated from her calf). For this, you will always have to suffer misery alike in this world and the next.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं ह्यपचितिं भ्रातुः पितुश्च सकलामिमाम्
वर्धनं यशसश्चापि करिष्यामि न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hyapacitiṁ bhrātuḥ pituśca sakalāmimām
vardhanaṁ yaśasaścāpi kariṣyāmi na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: I shall for my part completely minister to my brother and father, and shall without doubt, increase my fame.

verses.sanskrit:
आनाययित्वा तनयं कौसल्याया महाद्युतिम्
स्वयमेव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनं मुनिनिषेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
ānāyayitvā tanayaṁ kausalyāyā mahādyutim
svayameva pravekṣyāmi vanaṁ muniniṣevitam

translations.english: Bringing hither the mighty-armed lord of Kosala endowed with immense strength, I myself will repair to the forest inhabited by ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
इति नाग इवारण्ये तोमराङ्कुशचोदितः
पपात भुवि संक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः
verses.transliteration:
iti nāga ivāraṇye tomarāṅkuśacoditaḥ
papāta bhuvi saṁkruddho niḥśvasanniva pannagaḥ

translations.english: Grieving thus, Bharata, like an elephant in the forest afflicted with a tomara or ankusa,* fell to the earth sighing like an enraged snake. *Names of instruments.

verses.sanskrit:
संरक्तनेत्रः शिथिलाम्बरस्तदा; विधूतसर्वाभरणः परंतपः
बभूव भूमौ पतितो नृपात्मजः; शचीपतेः केतुरिवोत्सवक्षये
verses.transliteration:
saṁraktanetraḥ śithilāmbarastadā; vidhūtasarvābharaṇaḥ paraṁtapaḥ
babhūva bhūmau patito nṛpātmajaḥ; śacīpateḥ keturivotsavakṣaye

translations.english: With his eyes reddened, and his cloth falling off, and his ornaments cast away, that subduer of foes, the king's son fallen on the earth, resembled a banner of Sakra after the festival is over.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव क्रोशतस्तस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः
कौसल्या शब्दमाज्ञाय सुमित्रामिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva krośatastasya bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
kausalyā śabdamājñāya sumitrāmidamabravīt

translations.english: As the high-souled Bharata was thus wailing, Kausalyā recognizing his voice spoke to Sumitra.

verses.sanskrit:
आगतः क्रूरकार्यायाः कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः
तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भरतं दीर्घदर्शिनम्
verses.transliteration:
āgataḥ krūrakāryāyāḥ kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ
tamahaṁ draṣṭumicchāmi bharataṁ dīrghadarśinam

translations.english: Come is Bharata, the son of that one of crooked ways. I am desirous of seeing the farsighted Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु रामानुजश्चापि शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा
प्रतस्थे भरतो यत्र कौसल्याया निवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu rāmānujaścāpi śatrughnasahitastadā
pratasthe bharato yatra kausalyāyā niveśanam

translations.english: Having said this to Sumitrā, that one emaciated and with a pallid countenance, trembling and almost deprived of sensation, went to where Bharata, was. And it came to pass that the king's son, Bharata, along with Śatrughna had just then by the way that led to the same, been proceeding to Kausalyā's quarter.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शत्रुघ्नभरतौ कौसल्यां प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितौ
पर्यष्वजेतां दुःखार्तां पतितां नष्टचेतनाम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śatrughnabharatau kausalyāṁ prekṣya duḥkhitau
paryaṣvajetāṁ duḥkhārtāṁ patitāṁ naṣṭacetanām

translations.english: Then Śatrughna and Bharata seeing the aggrieved Kausalyā, embraced the stricken and fallen lady wellnigh deprived of her senses. Thereupon, weeping from grief, the noble and intelligent Kausalyà exceedingly afflicted, embracing them as they indulged in sorrow, said to Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं कौसल्या भृशदुःखिता
इदं ते राज्यकामस्य राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्
संप्राप्तं बत कैकेय्या शीघ्रं क्रूरेण कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
bharataṁ pratyuvācedaṁ kausalyā bhṛśaduḥkhitā
idaṁ te rājyakāmasya rājyaṁ prāptamakaṇṭakam
saṁprāptaṁ bata kaikeyyā śīghraṁ krūreṇa karmaṇā

translations.english: Thus have you, that had desired the kingdom, received it rid of its thorn. Alas! it has been speedily obtained through the crooked act of Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रस्थाप्य चीरवसनं पुत्रं मे वनवासिनम्
कैकेयी कं गुणं तत्र पश्यति क्रूरदर्शिनी
verses.transliteration:
prasthāpya cīravasanaṁ putraṁ me vanavāsinam
kaikeyī kaṁ guṇaṁ tatra paśyati krūradarśinī

translations.english: What is the good that is perceived by Kaikeyi of tortuous sight in sending away my son clad in bark to the woods?

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं मामपि कैकेयी प्रस्थापयितुमर्हति
हिरण्यनाभो यत्रास्ते सुतो मे सुमहायशाः
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṁ māmapi kaikeyī prasthāpayitumarhati
hiraṇyanābho yatrāste suto me sumahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: It behoves Kaikeyi to send me also speedily to where is staying my illustrious son furnished with a gold-gleaming navel.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा स्वयमेवाहं सुमित्रानुचरा सुखम्
अग्निहोत्रं पुरस्कृत्य प्रस्थास्ये यत्र राघवः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā svayamevāhaṁ sumitrānucarā sukham
agnihotraṁ puraskṛtya prasthāsye yatra rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Or first performing the fire-sacrifice, I followed by Sumitrā, will myself happily seek the way by which Rāghava (has gone to the woods).

verses.sanskrit:
कामं वा स्वयमेवाद्य तत्र मां नेतुमर्हसि
यत्रासौ पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तप्यते मे तपः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ vā svayamevādya tatra māṁ netumarhasi
yatrāsau puruṣavyāghrastapyate me tapaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Or it behoves you to yourself bring me to the place where that foremost of men, my son, is performing austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं हि तव विस्तीर्णं धनधान्यसमाचितम्
हस्त्यश्वरथसंपूर्णं राज्यं निर्यातितं तया
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ hi tava vistīrṇaṁ dhanadhānyasamācitam
hastyaśvarathasaṁpūrṇaṁ rājyaṁ niryātitaṁ tayā

translations.english: This spacious kingdom abounding in corn and wealth, and filled with elephants, horses, and cars, is yours, having been conferred on you (by Kaikeyi).

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपमानां तां भरतः प्राञ्जलिस्तदा
कौसल्यां प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृताम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapamānāṁ tāṁ bharataḥ prāñjalistadā
kausalyāṁ pratyuvācedaṁ śokairbahubhirāvṛtām

translations.english: Exceedingly agitated, he fell at Kausalya's feet, lamenting much, and well nigh deprived of his Bharata then regained his consciousness, and with joined hands answered Kausalya lamenting thus and overcome with excess of sorrow, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकिल्बिषम्
विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थिरां जानासि राघवे
verses.transliteration:
ārye kasmādajānantaṁ garhase māmakilbiṣam
vipulāṁ ca mama prītiṁ sthirāṁ jānāsi rāghave

translations.english: O noble lady, what for do you censure me who am without sin and who know nothing of this? You know that profuse is my delight in Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
कृता शास्त्रानुगा बुद्धिर्मा भूत्तस्य कदाचन
सत्यसंधः सतां श्रेष्ठो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtā śāstrānugā buddhirmā bhūttasya kadācana
satyasaṁdhaḥ satāṁ śreṣṭho yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May the sense of him never follow scripture, that had approved the exile into the woods of that foremost of the good, the noble Rāma intent senses. on truth!

verses.sanskrit:
प्रैष्यं पापीयसां यातु सूर्यं च प्रति मेहतु
हन्तु पादेन गां सुप्तां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
praiṣyaṁ pāpīyasāṁ yātu sūryaṁ ca prati mehatu
hantu pādena gāṁ suptāṁ yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May such a person as had approved the exile to the woods of the noble one undergo servitude at the hands of the sinful, answer the calls of nature facing the Sun, and kick a sleeping cow with his feet!

verses.sanskrit:
कारयित्वा महत्कर्म भर्ता भृत्यमनर्थकम्
अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
kārayitvā mahatkarma bhartā bhṛtyamanarthakam
adharmo yo'sya so'syāstu yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods come by the sin that is reaped by a master who withholds salary from servants after the ceremony is over!

verses.sanskrit:
परिपालयमानस्य राज्ञो भूतानि पुत्रवत्
ततस्तु द्रुह्यतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
paripālayamānasya rājño bhūtāni putravat
tatastu druhyatāṁ pāpaṁ yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May that one that had approved the exile of the noble Rāma to the woods, be guilty of the sin that is his that injures a sovereign engaged in ruling his subjects like sons!

verses.sanskrit:
बलिषड्भागमुद्धृत्य नृपस्यारक्षतः प्रजाः
अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
baliṣaḍbhāgamuddhṛtya nṛpasyārakṣataḥ prajāḥ
adharmo yo'sya so'syāstu yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May the person that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, reap the sin of his that having taken a sixth pare of their incomes, does not protect his subjects!

verses.sanskrit:
संश्रुत्य च तपस्विभ्यः सत्रे वै यज्ञदक्षिणाम्
तां विप्रलपतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
saṁśrutya ca tapasvibhyaḥ satre vai yajñadakṣiṇām
tāṁ vipralapatāṁ pāpaṁ yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, come by the demerit that is his that denies Dakșiņās to ascetics in a sacrifice, after having promised them the same!

verses.sanskrit:
हस्त्यश्वरथसंबाधे युद्धे शस्त्रसमाकुले
मा स्म कार्षीत्सतां धर्मं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
hastyaśvarathasaṁbādhe yuddhe śastrasamākule
mā sma kārṣītsatāṁ dharmaṁ yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of the noble one, never discharge the duty of the good in the field thronged with elephants and horses and cars, and bristling with arms!

verses.sanskrit:
उपदिष्टं सुसूक्ष्मार्थं शास्त्रं यत्नेन धीमता
स नाशयतु दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
upadiṣṭaṁ susūkṣmārthaṁ śāstraṁ yatnena dhīmatā
sa nāśayatu duṣṭātmā yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May the wicked wight that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods bring to naught the subtle scriptural knowledge which has been carefully taught him by his intelligent preceptor!

verses.sanskrit:
पायसं कृसरं छागं वृथा सोऽश्नातु निर्घृणः
गुरूंश्चाप्यवजानातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
pāyasaṁ kṛsaraṁ chāgaṁ vṛthā so'śnātu nirghṛṇaḥ
gurūṁścāpyavajānātu yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May that one void of aversion, that had approved of the exile of the noble one to the woods feed on Payasa, Krsara, and goat's flesh, which have not been offered in sacrifice; and may he insult his spiritual precept.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रैर्दारैश्च भृत्यैश्च स्वगृहे परिवारितः
स एको मृष्टमश्नातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
putrairdāraiśca bhṛtyaiśca svagṛhe parivāritaḥ
sa eko mṛṣṭamaśnātu yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one, eat alone in his home, although surrounded by sons and wives and servitors!

verses.sanskrit:
राजस्त्रीबालवृद्धानां वधे यत्पापमुच्यते
भृत्यत्यागे च यत्पापं तत्पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
rājastrībālavṛddhānāṁ vadhe yatpāpamucyate
bhṛtyatyāge ca yatpāpaṁ tatpāpaṁ pratipadyatām

translations.english: And may he come by the sin that is reaped by slaying a king, a woman, a boy, or an old man, or by renouncing those who have claims on his maintenance!

verses.sanskrit:
उभे संध्ये शयानस्य यत्पापं परिकल्प्यते
तच्च पापं भवेत्तस्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
ubhe saṁdhye śayānasya yatpāpaṁ parikalpyate
tacca pāpaṁ bhavettasya yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one bear the sin that is his that serves a thirsty soul with deceit.

verses.sanskrit:
यदग्निदायके पापं यत्पापं गुरुतल्पगे
मित्रद्रोहे च यत्पापं तत्पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
yadagnidāyake pāpaṁ yatpāpaṁ gurutalpage
mitradrohe ca yatpāpaṁ tatpāpaṁ pratipadyatām

translations.english: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of that noble one, come by the demerit that is his who sleeps during both the twilight's! May he reap the sin that is reaped by an incendiary or him that Leith with his preceptor's wife; or him that wrongs his friend!

verses.sanskrit:
देवतानां पितॄणां च माता पित्रोस्तथैव च
मा स्म कार्षीत्स शुश्रूषां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
devatānāṁ pitṝṇāṁ ca mātā pitrostathaiva ca
mā sma kārṣītsa śuśrūṣāṁ yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: May he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, never serve the gods or the manes of the ancestors or his father and mother!

verses.sanskrit:
सतां लोकात्सतां कीर्त्याः सज्जुष्टात्कर्मणस्तथा
भ्रश्यतु क्षिप्रमद्यैव यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः
verses.transliteration:
satāṁ lokātsatāṁ kīrtyāḥ sajjuṣṭātkarmaṇastathā
bhraśyatu kṣipramadyaiva yasyāryo'numate gataḥ

translations.english: may he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, be speedily shut out from the world of the good, from their fame, and from their acts!

verses.sanskrit:
विहीनां पतिपुत्राभ्यां कौसल्यां पार्थिवात्मजः
एवमाश्वसयन्नेव दुःखार्तो निपपात ह
verses.transliteration:
vihīnāṁ patiputrābhyāṁ kausalyāṁ pārthivātmajaḥ
evamāśvasayanneva duḥkhārto nipapāta ha

translations.english: Having thus consoled Kausalyā bereft of her son and husband, the prince afflicted with distress fell down.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु शपथैः कष्टैः शपमानमचेतनम्
भरतं शोकसंतप्तं कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu śapathaiḥ kaṣṭaiḥ śapamānamacetanam
bharataṁ śokasaṁtaptaṁ kausalyā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Then Kausalyā addressed the aggrieved Bharaia (well-nigh) deprived of his senses, swearing strong oaths, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
मम दुःखमिदं पुत्र भूयः समुपजायते
शपथैः शपमानो हि प्राणानुपरुणत्सि मे
verses.transliteration:
mama duḥkhamidaṁ putra bhūyaḥ samupajāyate
śapathaiḥ śapamāno hi prāṇānuparuṇatsi me

translations.english: O son, it grieves me more that you are afflicting my heart by taking oaths.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या न चलितो धर्मादात्मा ते सहलक्ष्मणः
वत्स सत्यप्रतिज्ञो मे सतां लोकानवाप्स्यसि
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā na calito dharmādātmā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
vatsa satyapratijño me satāṁ lokānavāpsyasi

translations.english: Lucky it is that graced with auspicious marks, you swerves not from virtue. My child, for this reason you will attain the regions of pious person, drawing into her lap Bharata attached to his brother, and embracing the mighty armed one, gave way to grief.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः
मोहाच्च शोकसंरोधाद्बभूव लुलितं मनः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapamānasya duḥkhārtasya mahātmanaḥ
mohācca śokasaṁrodhādbabhūva lulitaṁ manaḥ

translations.english: And bewailing thus, the mind of the high souled (Bharata) wrought with sorrow, was overcome with the burden of grief.

verses.sanskrit:
लालप्यमानस्य विचेतनस्य; प्रनष्टबुद्धेः पतितस्य भूमौ
मुहुर्मुहुर्निःश्वसतश्च दीर्घं; सा तस्य शोकेन जगाम रात्रिः
verses.transliteration:
lālapyamānasya vicetanasya; pranaṣṭabuddheḥ patitasya bhūmau
muhurmuhurniḥśvasataśca dīrghaṁ; sā tasya śokena jagāma rātriḥ

translations.english: And fallen the ground, lamenting, senseless, with his intellect overpowered, and momentarily heaving sighs, Bharata passed away night in grief.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवं शोकसंतप्तं भरतं केकयीसुतम्
उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठवागृषिः
verses.transliteration:
tamevaṁ śokasaṁtaptaṁ bharataṁ kekayīsutam
uvāca vadatāṁ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhavāgṛṣiḥ

translations.english: As Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi was thus burning in grief, that foremost of those skilled in speech, the saint Vasistha, endowed with excellence of language, said.

verses.sanskrit:
अलं शोकेन भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः
प्राप्तकालं नरपतेः कुरु संयानमुत्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
alaṁ śokena bhadraṁ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
prāptakālaṁ narapateḥ kuru saṁyānamuttaram

translations.english: Do not weep, good betide you, O illustrious prince. Do you perform the funereal rites of the departed king.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भरतो धारणां गतः
प्रेतकार्याणि सर्वाणि कारयामास धर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā bharato dhāraṇāṁ gataḥ
pretakāryāṇi sarvāṇi kārayāmāsa dharmavit

translations.english: Hearing Vasistha's words, Bharata cognisant of duty, bowed down to the ground and despatched the ministers for performing the last rites.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेश्य शयने चाग्र्ये नानारत्नपरिष्कृते
ततो दशरथं पुत्रो विललाप सुदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
niveśya śayane cāgrye nānāratnapariṣkṛte
tato daśarathaṁ putro vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: And raising from under the oil the body of the king with a sallow countenance, and appearing to be asleep. Bharata placed it on the ground upon a couch in front adorned with various gems. Then overwhelmed with grief, Dasaratha's son bewailed him thus.

verses.sanskrit:
किं ते व्यवसितं राजन्प्रोषिते मय्यनागते
विवास्य रामं धर्मज्ञं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ te vyavasitaṁ rājanproṣite mayyanāgate
vivāsya rāmaṁ dharmajñaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam

translations.english: O king, what was it that you had intended to do, I absent and away from home, by banishing righteous Rāma and the powerful Lakşmana?

verses.sanskrit:
क्व यास्यसि महाराज हित्वेमं दुःखितं जनम्
हीनं पुरुषसिंहेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
kva yāsyasi mahārāja hitvemaṁ duḥkhitaṁ janam
hīnaṁ puruṣasiṁhena rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā

translations.english: Whither wend you, O mighty monarch, forsaking these aggrieved people, who have already been deprived of the lion like Rāma energetic in action?

verses.sanskrit:
योगक्षेमं तु ते राजन्कोऽस्मिन्कल्पयिता पुरे
त्वयि प्रयाते स्वस्तात रामे च वनमाश्रिते
verses.transliteration:
yogakṣemaṁ tu te rājanko'sminkalpayitā pure
tvayi prayāte svastāta rāme ca vanamāśrite

translations.english: O father, you having ascended heaven and Rāma having taken refuge in the woods, who now in this city of yours shall protect what the people possess and secure to them what they have not?

verses.sanskrit:
विधवा पृथिवी राजंस्त्वया हीना न राजते
हीनचन्द्रेव रजनी नगरी प्रतिभाति माम्
verses.transliteration:
vidhavā pṛthivī rājaṁstvayā hīnā na rājate
hīnacandreva rajanī nagarī pratibhāti mām

translations.english: Widowed in consequence of losing you, this earth does not look graceful. The city appears to me like the night deprived of the Moon

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपमानं तं भरतं दीनमानसम्
अब्रवीद्वचनं भूयो वसिष्ठस्तु महानृषिः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapamānaṁ taṁ bharataṁ dīnamānasam
abravīdvacanaṁ bhūyo vasiṣṭhastu mahānṛṣiḥ

translations.english: As Bharata was lamenting thus in dejected mood, the mighty ascetic Vasiştha again addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेतकार्याणि यान्यस्य कर्तव्यानि विशाम्पतेः
तान्यव्यग्रं महाबाहो क्रियतामविचारितम्
verses.transliteration:
pretakāryāṇi yānyasya kartavyāni viśāmpateḥ
tānyavyagraṁ mahābāho kriyatāmavicāritam

translations.english: O mighty armed one, do you without indulging in any reflections, perform those funeral ceremonies of the monarch which ought to be performed.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति भरतो वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्याभिपूज्य तत्
ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यांस्त्वरयामास सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
tatheti bharato vākyaṁ vasiṣṭhasyābhipūjya tat
ṛtvikpurohitācāryāṁstvarayāmāsa sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon honouring his words by saying, "So be it,” he urged speed upon all the Rtvigs, priests, and Acāryas.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वग्रतो नरेन्द्रस्य अग्न्यगाराद्बहिष्कृताः
ऋत्विग्भिर्याजकैश्चैव ते ह्रियन्ते यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
ye tvagrato narendrasya agnyagārādbahiṣkṛtāḥ
ṛtvigbhiryājakaiścaiva te hriyante yathāvidhi

translations.english: And then those that had brought the king's corpse out side from the fire chamber, instructed by the Rtvigs and priests according to the ordinance began to offer oblations into the fire.

verses.sanskrit:
शिबिलायामथारोप्य राजानं गतचेतनम्
बाष्पकण्ठा विमनसस्तमूहुः परिचारकाः
verses.transliteration:
śibilāyāmathāropya rājānaṁ gatacetanam
bāṣpakaṇṭhā vimanasastamūhuḥ paricārakāḥ

translations.english: Next placing the king deprived of life on a car, the servants with their throats oppressed with vapour and with their minds weighed down with dejection carried him.

verses.sanskrit:
हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च वासांसि विविधानि च
प्रकिरन्तो जना मार्गं नृपतेरग्रतो ययुः
verses.transliteration:
hiraṇyaṁ ca suvarṇaṁ ca vāsāṁsi vividhāni ca
prakiranto janā mārgaṁ nṛpateragrato yayuḥ

translations.english: And scattering gold and silver and various kinds of cloth, on the way people went in front of the king.

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धानुच्चावचांश्चान्यांस्तत्र दत्त्वाथ भूमिपम्
ततः संवेशयामासुश्चितामध्ये तमृत्विजः
verses.transliteration:
gandhānuccāvacāṁścānyāṁstatra dattvātha bhūmipam
tataḥ saṁveśayāmāsuścitāmadhye tamṛtvijaḥ

translations.english: Others procuring sandal, aguru and other sarala, padmaka and devadari, cast it (on the earth). And drawing near the king there, Rtvigs laid various other fragrant substances on the funeral pile.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा हुताशनं हुत्वा जेपुस्तस्य तदर्त्विजः
जगुश्च ते यथाशास्त्रं तत्र सामानि सामगाः
verses.transliteration:
tathā hutāśanaṁ hutvā jepustasya tadartvijaḥ
jaguśca te yathāśāstraṁ tatra sāmāni sāmagāḥ

translations.english: Then offering oblations into the fire, the Rtvigs began to recite japa; and as laid down in the scriptures, Sāma-singers chanted Sämans.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसव्यं चापि तं चक्रुरृत्विजोऽग्निचितं नृपम्
स्त्रियश्च शोकसंतप्ताः कौसल्या प्रमुखास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
prasavyaṁ cāpi taṁ cakrurṛtvijo'gnicitaṁ nṛpam
striyaśca śokasaṁtaptāḥ kausalyā pramukhāstadā

translations.english: By means of litters and other conveyances, each mounted according to her rank, the wives of the king went out from the city, surrounded by aged men. And Rtvijas went round the corpse on the king who performed many sacrifices leaving it on the left side.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चीनामिव नारीणां निनादस्तत्र शुश्रुवे
आर्तानां करुणं काले क्रोशन्तीनां सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
krauñcīnāmiva nārīṇāṁ ninādastatra śuśruve
ārtānāṁ karuṇaṁ kāle krośantīnāṁ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And kindling with grief, the females also headed by Kausalyā (circumambulated the pyre). And then there was heard the wail of women distressed with grief weeping piteously by thousands like to Krauñcis.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रुदन्त्यो विवशा विलप्य च पुनः पुनः
यानेभ्यः सरयूतीरमवतेरुर्वराङ्गनाः
verses.transliteration:
tato rudantyo vivaśā vilapya ca punaḥ punaḥ
yānebhyaḥ sarayūtīramavaterurvarāṅganāḥ

translations.english: Weeping again and again with their sense lost, the wives of the king alighted from the car on the banks of the Sarayu.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतोदकं ते भरतेन सार्धं; नृपाङ्गना मन्त्रिपुरोहिताश्च
पुरं प्रविश्याश्रुपरीतनेत्रा; भूमौ दशाहं व्यनयन्त दुःखम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtodakaṁ te bharatena sārdhaṁ; nṛpāṅganā mantripurohitāśca
puraṁ praviśyāśruparītanetrā; bhūmau daśāhaṁ vyanayanta duḥkham

translations.english: Having performed the watery rites, the wives of the monarch as well as the counsellors and priests, in company with Bharata entering the city with tears in their eyes, spent ten days* in mourning lying down on the ground. *The Smrti: lays down twelve days of mourning for kings, and sixteen for Khatriyas. Parasara, however, fixes ten days for Ksatriyas in general.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दशाहेऽतिगते कृतशौचो नृपात्मजः
द्वादशेऽहनि संप्राप्ते श्राद्धकर्माण्यकारयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato daśāhe'tigate kṛtaśauco nṛpātmajaḥ
dvādaśe'hani saṁprāpte śrāddhakarmāṇyakārayat

translations.english: When the ten days had gone by, the king's son, his uncleanness (consequent on the demise of his father) removed, performed the sraddha on the twelfth day.

verses.sanskrit:
दासीदासं च यानं च वेश्मानि सुमहान्ति च
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुत्रो राज्ञस्तस्यौर्ध्वदैहिकम्
verses.transliteration:
dāsīdāsaṁ ca yānaṁ ca veśmāni sumahānti ca
brāhmaṇebhyo dadau putro rājñastasyaurdhvadaihikam

translations.english: On the occasion on the ceremonies for the welfare of the departed Spirit, the son of the king conferred on Brāhmaṇas wealth and gems, and rice in abundance, and herds of goats, and silver in profusion, and countless kine, and maidservants and man-servants, and vehicles and spacious mansions.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ त्रयोदशे
विललाप महाबाहुर्भरतः शोकमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prabhātasamaye divase'tha trayodaśe
vilalāpa mahābāhurbharataḥ śokamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And on the thirteenth day, the long armed Bharata, overwhelmed with grief, burst into lamentation.

verses.sanskrit:
तात यस्मिन्निषृष्टोऽहं त्वया भ्रातरि राघवे
तस्मिन्वनं प्रव्रजिते शून्ये त्यक्तोऽस्म्यहं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
tāta yasminniṣṛṣṭo'haṁ tvayā bhrātari rāghave
tasminvanaṁ pravrajite śūnye tyakto'smyahaṁ tvayā

translations.english: And coming to the foot of the funeral pyre for gathering the bones of the departed, he overcome with grief, with his throat obstructed with the sounds of lamentation, said, “my father, on brother Rāma, to whom I had been consigned by you, having gone to the forest, I have been cast by you into vacancy.

verses.sanskrit:
यथागतिरनाथायाः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो वनम्
तामम्बां तात कौसल्यां त्यक्त्वा त्वं क्व गतो नृप
verses.transliteration:
yathāgatiranāthāyāḥ putraḥ pravrājito vanam
tāmambāṁ tāta kausalyāṁ tyaktvā tvaṁ kva gato nṛpa

translations.english: My father, forsaking forlorn mother Kausalya, whose stay her son, had gone to the forest, where have you gone, Oking?

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा भस्मारुणं तच्च दग्धास्थिस्थानमण्डलम्
पितुः शरीर निर्वाणं निष्टनन्विषसाद ह
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā bhasmāruṇaṁ tacca dagdhāsthisthānamaṇḍalam
pituḥ śarīra nirvāṇaṁ niṣṭananviṣasāda ha

translations.english: Seeing the spot where lay the bones of his father mixed with ashes and embers Bharata looking at the place where occurred the dissolution of his father's fame, carried away by emotion, indulged in sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दृष्ट्वा रुदन्दीनः पपात धरणीतले
उत्थाप्यमानः शक्रस्य यन्त्र ध्वज इव च्युतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dṛṣṭvā rudandīnaḥ papāta dharaṇītale
utthāpyamānaḥ śakrasya yantra dhvaja iva cyutaḥ

translations.english: And seeing this, he exceedingly distressed, crying fell down to the ground. And raised up (by others) he looked like an uplifted banner of Sakra bound to an engine.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिपेतुस्ततः सर्वे तस्यामात्याः शुचिव्रतम्
अन्तकाले निपतितं ययातिमृषयो यथा
verses.transliteration:
abhipetustataḥ sarve tasyāmātyāḥ śucivratam
antakāle nipatitaṁ yayātimṛṣayo yathā

translations.english: His counsellors rushed towards that one of pure vows, like the saints making towards Yayati as he was falling on the extinction of his merit.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नश्चापि भरतं दृष्ट्वा शोकपरिप्लुतम्
विसंज्ञो न्यपतद्भूमौ भूमिपालमनुस्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnaścāpi bharataṁ dṛṣṭvā śokapariplutam
visaṁjño nyapatadbhūmau bhūmipālamanusmaran

translations.english: Seeing Bharata plunged in grief, Satrughna remembering the king, fell down to the ground deprived of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
उन्मत्त इव निश्चेता विललाप सुदुःखितः
स्मृत्वा पितुर्गुणाङ्गानि तानि तानि तदा तदा
verses.transliteration:
unmatta iva niścetā vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ
smṛtvā piturguṇāṅgāni tāni tāni tadā tadā

translations.english: And devoid of sense and like a madman, he in grief of heart began to lament remembering all the virtues of his father again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्थरा प्रभवस्तीव्रः कैकेयीग्राहसंकुलः
वरदानमयोऽक्षोभ्योऽमज्जयच्छोकसागरः
verses.transliteration:
mantharā prabhavastīvraḥ kaikeyīgrāhasaṁkulaḥ
varadānamayo'kṣobhyo'majjayacchokasāgaraḥ

translations.english: This terrible sea of grief owing its origin to Mantharā, containing its ferocious aquatic animal in the shape of Kaikeyī, and incapable of being disturbed in consequence of the bestowal of the boon drowns (us).

verses.sanskrit:
सुकुमारं च बालं च सततं लालितं त्वया
क्व तात भरतं हित्वा विलपन्तं गतो भवान्
verses.transliteration:
sukumāraṁ ca bālaṁ ca satataṁ lālitaṁ tvayā
kva tāta bharataṁ hitvā vilapantaṁ gato bhavān

translations.english: O father, where have you gone, leaving the tender and youthful Bharata fondled by you, to lament (your loss).

verses.sanskrit:
ननु भोज्येषु पानेषु वस्त्रेष्वाभरणेषु च
प्रवारयसि नः सर्वांस्तन्नः कोऽद्य करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nanu bhojyeṣu pāneṣu vastreṣvābharaṇeṣu ca
pravārayasi naḥ sarvāṁstannaḥ ko'dya kariṣyati

translations.english: You did use to confer on us eatables and drinkable and attires and ornaments. Who will now do so?

verses.sanskrit:
अवदारण काले तु पृथिवी नावदीर्यते
विहीना या त्वया राज्ञा धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
avadāraṇa kāle tu pṛthivī nāvadīryate
vihīnā yā tvayā rājñā dharmajñena mahātmanā

translations.english: Deprived of you, the high souled king cognisant of duty, the earth albeit her time of riving is come, is not yet riven.

verses.sanskrit:
पितरि स्वर्गमापन्ने रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते
किं मे जीवित सामर्थ्यं प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
pitari svargamāpanne rāme cāraṇyamāśrite
kiṁ me jīvita sāmarthyaṁ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam

translations.english: My father having gone to heaven and Rāma having sought the woods, how can I live? I will enter fire.

verses.sanskrit:
हीनो भ्रात्रा च पित्रा च शून्यामिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्
अयोध्यां न प्रवेक्ष्यामि प्रवेक्ष्यामि तपोवनम्
verses.transliteration:
hīno bhrātrā ca pitrā ca śūnyāmikṣvākupālitām
ayodhyāṁ na pravekṣyāmi pravekṣyāmi tapovanam

translations.english: Bereft of my brother and sire, I will not enter the empty Ayodhyā governed by the Ikşvākus. I will repair to the forest of asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोर्विलपितं श्रुत्वा व्यसनं चान्ववेक्ष्य तत्
भृशमार्ततरा भूयः सर्व एवानुगामिनः
verses.transliteration:
tayorvilapitaṁ śrutvā vyasanaṁ cānvavekṣya tat
bhṛśamārtatarā bhūyaḥ sarva evānugāminaḥ

translations.english: Hearing his lamentations and seeing that disaster, all the followers became all the more distressed.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विषण्णौ श्रान्तौ च शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ
धरण्यां संव्यचेष्टेतां भग्नशृङ्गाविवर्षभौ
verses.transliteration:
tato viṣaṇṇau śrāntau ca śatrughnabharatāvubhau
dharaṇyāṁ saṁvyaceṣṭetāṁ bhagnaśṛṅgāvivarṣabhau

translations.english: Then depressed and exhausted, both Šatrughna and Bharata rolled on the earth like two bulls with their horns fractured,

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रकृतिमान्वैद्यः पितुरेषां पुरोहितः
वसिष्ठो भरतं वाक्यमुत्थाप्य तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prakṛtimānvaidyaḥ pitureṣāṁ purohitaḥ
vasiṣṭho bharataṁ vākyamutthāpya tamuvāca ha

translations.english: Then the all-knowing priest of their father possessed of sterling worth, Vasistha, raising Bharata, said to him.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः
तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
trīṇi dvandvāni bhūteṣu pravṛttānyaviśeṣataḥ
teṣu cāparihāryeṣu naivaṁ bhavitumarhati

translations.english: Three couples* pertain in especial to all creatures and these being inevitable, you ought not to bear yourself thus. *Hunger and thirst, ignorance and grief, sickness and death.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रश्चापि शत्रुघ्नमुत्थाप्याभिप्रसाद्य च
श्रावयामास तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतभवाभवौ
verses.transliteration:
sumantraścāpi śatrughnamutthāpyābhiprasādya ca
śrāvayāmāsa tattvajñaḥ sarvabhūtabhavābhavau

translations.english: And Sumantra also versed in the nature of things, raising up Šatrughna and pacifying him, discoursed the birth and heath of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्थितौ तौ नरव्याघ्रौ प्रकाशेते यशस्विनौ
वर्षातपपरिक्लिन्नौ पृथगिन्द्रध्वजाविव
verses.transliteration:
utthitau tau naravyāghrau prakāśete yaśasvinau
varṣātapapariklinnau pṛthagindradhvajāviva

translations.english: Being raised up, those renowned chiefs of men looked like Indra's banner stained by shine and shower.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्रूणि परिमृद्नन्तौ रक्ताक्षौ दीनभाषिणौ
अमात्यास्त्वरयन्ति स्म तनयौ चापराः क्रियाः
verses.transliteration:
aśrūṇi parimṛdnantau raktākṣau dīnabhāṣiṇau
amātyāstvarayanti sma tanayau cāparāḥ kriyāḥ

translations.english: And as the princes stood there shedding tears, with reddened eyes, and speaking sadly, the courers urged nem on in behalf of the rites that remained.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्र यात्रां समीहन्तं शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः
भरतं शोकसंतप्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atra yātrāṁ samīhantaṁ śatrughno lakṣmaṇānujaḥ
bharataṁ śokasaṁtaptamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Then ſatrughna, the younger brother of Lakşmaņa spoke to Bharata burning in grief as he was revolving in his mind the (intended) journey (to Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
गतिर्यः सर्वभूतानां दुःखे किं पुनरात्मनः
स रामः सत्त्व संपन्नः स्त्रिया प्रव्राजितो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
gatiryaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ duḥkhe kiṁ punarātmanaḥ
sa rāmaḥ sattva saṁpannaḥ striyā pravrājito vanam

translations.english: Need it be said that Rāma is the refuge both of himself and all creatures in trouble? That Rāma possessed of strength has been exiled into the woods by a woman!

verses.sanskrit:
बलवान्वीर्य संपन्नो लक्ष्मणो नाम योऽप्यसौ
किं न मोचयते रामं कृत्वापि पितृनिग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
balavānvīrya saṁpanno lakṣmaṇo nāma yo'pyasau
kiṁ na mocayate rāmaṁ kṛtvāpi pitṛnigraham

translations.english: And powerful and having prowess, why did not Laksmana deliver Rāma by checking our father?

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वमेव तु निग्राह्यः समवेक्ष्य नयानयौ
उत्पथं यः समारूढो नार्या राजा वशं गतः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvameva tu nigrāhyaḥ samavekṣya nayānayau
utpathaṁ yaḥ samārūḍho nāryā rājā vaśaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: The king bent upon following an unrighteous course through the influence of a woman, should, the justice or otherwise of the measure being fully weighed, at the very outset have been checked.

verses.sanskrit:
इति संभाषमाणे तु शत्रुघ्ने लक्ष्मणानुजे
प्राग्द्वारेऽभूत्तदा कुब्जा सर्वाभरणभूषिता
verses.transliteration:
iti saṁbhāṣamāṇe tu śatrughne lakṣmaṇānuje
prāgdvāre'bhūttadā kubjā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā

translations.english: As Lakşmaņa's younger brother Satrughna was speaking thus, appeared there at the door in front the hump backed one adorned with every kind of ornament, with her body besmeared with sandal paste, wearing regal apparel, and variously decked out with a variety of ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
तां समीक्ष्य तदा द्वाःस्थो भृशं पापस्य कारिणीम्
गृहीत्वाकरुणं कुब्जां शत्रुघ्नाय न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ samīkṣya tadā dvāḥstho bhṛśaṁ pāpasya kāriṇīm
gṛhītvākaruṇaṁ kubjāṁ śatrughnāya nyavedayat

translations.english: At that time seeing that one of horrible misdeeds, (Bharata) who stood near the door, seizing the hump backed one ruthlessly, took her to Satrughna, and said.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्याः कृते वने रामो न्यस्तदेहश्च वः पिता
सेयं पापा नृशंसा च तस्याः कुरु यथामति
verses.transliteration:
yasyāḥ kṛte vane rāmo nyastadehaśca vaḥ pitā
seyaṁ pāpā nṛśaṁsā ca tasyāḥ kuru yathāmati

translations.english: That one through whom Rāma has gone to the wood and our father has renounced his body this is that wicked and remorseless one. Do you deal with her as you like.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नश्च तदाज्ञाय वचनं भृशदुःखितः
अन्तःपुरचरान्सर्वानित्युवाच धृतव्रतः
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnaśca tadājñāya vacanaṁ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
antaḥpuracarānsarvānityuvāca dhṛtavrataḥ

translations.english: At Bharata's command Satrughna observing vows waxing exceedingly aggrieved, addressed all the inmates of the inner apartment, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
तीव्रमुत्पादितं दुःखं भ्रातॄणां मे तथा पितुः
यया सेयं नृशंसस्य कर्मणः फलमश्नुताम्
verses.transliteration:
tīvramutpāditaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhrātṝṇāṁ me tathā pituḥ
yayā seyaṁ nṛśaṁsasya karmaṇaḥ phalamaśnutām

translations.english: This one has occasioned intense misery to my father and brothers Let her now take the fruit of her fell deed.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता च तेनाशु सखी जनसमावृता
गृहीता बलवत्कुब्जा सा तद्गृहमनादयत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā ca tenāśu sakhī janasamāvṛtā
gṛhītā balavatkubjā sā tadgṛhamanādayat

translations.english: Having said this, he furiously fell upon the hump backed one surrounded by her maids. Thereupon she with her cries made the chamber resound.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुभृश संतप्तस्तस्याः सर्वः सखीजनः
क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय शत्रुघ्नं व्यपलायत सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ subhṛśa saṁtaptastasyāḥ sarvaḥ sakhījanaḥ
kruddhamājñāya śatrughnaṁ vyapalāyata sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Concluding Śatrughna fired with rage, her associates extremely pained, fled away in all directions.

verses.sanskrit:
अमन्त्रयत कृत्स्नश्च तस्याः सर्वसखीजनः
यथायं समुपक्रान्तो निःशेषं नः करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
amantrayata kṛtsnaśca tasyāḥ sarvasakhījanaḥ
yathāyaṁ samupakrānto niḥśeṣaṁ naḥ kariṣyati

translations.english: Then her companions in a body took counsel of each other, saying, “considering the way in which he has entered upon it, he will annihilate us quite."

verses.sanskrit:
सानुक्रोशां वदान्यां च धर्मज्ञां च यशस्विनीम्
कौसल्यां शरणं यामः सा हि नोऽस्तु ध्रुवा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
sānukrośāṁ vadānyāṁ ca dharmajñāṁ ca yaśasvinīm
kausalyāṁ śaraṇaṁ yāmaḥ sā hi no'stu dhruvā gatiḥ

translations.english: Let us therefore seek the protection of the tender hearted generous, pious and illustrious Kausalyā. Even she is our sure refuge.

verses.sanskrit:
स च रोषेण ताम्राक्षः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुतापनः
विचकर्ष तदा कुब्जां क्रोशन्तीं पृथिवीतले
verses.transliteration:
sa ca roṣeṇa tāmrākṣaḥ śatrughnaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
vicakarṣa tadā kubjāṁ krośantīṁ pṛthivītale

translations.english: Overpowered with rage, that chastiser of foes, Śatrughna, dragged the shrieking hump backed one to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या ह्याकृष्यमाणाया मन्थरायास्ततस्ततः
चित्रं बहुविधं भाण्डं पृथिव्यां तद्व्यशीर्यत
verses.transliteration:
tasyā hyākṛṣyamāṇāyā mantharāyāstatastataḥ
citraṁ bahuvidhaṁ bhāṇḍaṁ pṛthivyāṁ tadvyaśīryata

translations.english: As Mantharā was pushed this way and that, her various ornaments were scattered over the floor.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन भाण्डेन संकीर्णं श्रीमद्राजनिवेशनम्
अशोभत तदा भूयः शारदं गगनं यथा
verses.transliteration:
tena bhāṇḍena saṁkīrṇaṁ śrīmadrājaniveśanam
aśobhata tadā bhūyaḥ śāradaṁ gaganaṁ yathā

translations.english: And strewn with those ornaments, the graceful chamber of the palace looked like the autumnal firmament.

verses.sanskrit:
स बली बलवत्क्रोधाद्गृहीत्वा पुरुषर्षभः
कैकेयीमभिनिर्भर्त्स्य बभाषे परुषं वचः
verses.transliteration:
sa balī balavatkrodhādgṛhītvā puruṣarṣabhaḥ
kaikeyīmabhinirbhartsya babhāṣe paruṣaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And that foremost of men possessed of strength holding her, began to reprove Kaikeyī with harsh speech.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्वाक्यैः परुषैर्दुःखैः कैकेयी भृशदुःखिता
शत्रुघ्न भयसंत्रस्ता पुत्रं शरणमागता
verses.transliteration:
tairvākyaiḥ paruṣairduḥkhaiḥ kaikeyī bhṛśaduḥkhitā
śatrughna bhayasaṁtrastā putraṁ śaraṇamāgatā

translations.english: Extremely hurt by those rough words, Kaikeyi terrified on account of Satrughna, took refuge with her son.

verses.sanskrit:
तां प्रेक्ष्य भरतः क्रुद्धं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्
अवध्याः सर्वभूतानां प्रमदाः क्षम्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ prekṣya bharataḥ kruddhaṁ śatrughnamidamabravīt
avadhyāḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ pramadāḥ kṣamyatāmiti

translations.english: Thereupon casting his eyes on Satrughna, Bharata said, “A woman is incapable of being slain by any. Do you therefore excuse her.”

verses.sanskrit:
हन्यामहमिमां पापां कैकेयीं दुष्टचारिणीम्
यदि मां धार्मिको रामो नासूयेन्मातृघातकम्
verses.transliteration:
hanyāmahamimāṁ pāpāṁ kaikeyīṁ duṣṭacāriṇīm
yadi māṁ dhārmiko rāmo nāsūyenmātṛghātakam

translations.english: I myself would have slain this wicked Kaikeyi of impious deeds, if the righteous Rāma should not be displeased with me on account of my slaying my mother.

verses.sanskrit:
इमामपि हतां कुब्जां यदि जानाति राघवः
त्वां च मां चैव धर्मात्मा नाभिभाषिष्यते ध्रुवम्
verses.transliteration:
imāmapi hatāṁ kubjāṁ yadi jānāti rāghavaḥ
tvāṁ ca māṁ caiva dharmātmā nābhibhāṣiṣyate dhruvam

translations.english: If Rāghava knows that the hump-backed one has been slain, he sure' will speak neither with you nor me.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः
न्यवर्तत ततो रोषात्तां मुमोच च मन्थराम्
verses.transliteration:
bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā śatrughno lakṣmaṇānujaḥ
nyavartata tato roṣāttāṁ mumoca ca mantharām

translations.english: Hearing Bharata's words, Satrughna, younger brother to Lakşmaņa, refrained from that wrong and set free the hump-backed woman in a swoon.

verses.sanskrit:
सा पादमूले कैकेय्या मन्थरा निपपात ह
निःश्वसन्ती सुदुःखार्ता कृपणं विललाप च
verses.transliteration:
sā pādamūle kaikeyyā mantharā nipapāta ha
niḥśvasantī suduḥkhārtā kṛpaṇaṁ vilalāpa ca

translations.english: Thereat, sighing hard in exceeding grief, Mantharā flung herself and Kaikeyi's feet, weeping piteously.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नविक्षेपविमूढसंज्ञां; समीक्ष्य कुब्जां भरतस्य माता
शनैः समाश्वासयदार्तरूपां; क्रौञ्चीं विलग्नामिव वीक्षमाणाम्
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnavikṣepavimūḍhasaṁjñāṁ; samīkṣya kubjāṁ bharatasya mātā
śanaiḥ samāśvāsayadārtarūpāṁ; krauñcīṁ vilagnāmiva vīkṣamāṇām

translations.english: Seeing the hump-backed one deprived of her senses in consequence of the pushing she had received at the hands of Satrughna, Bharata's mother consoled that distressed woman, who appeared like a Krauñci that had been entrapped.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ चतुर्दशे
समेत्य राजकर्तारो भरतं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prabhātasamaye divase'tha caturdaśe
sametya rājakartāro bharataṁ vākyamabruvan

translations.english: Then on the morning of the fourteenth day, the ministers of the king assembled addressed Bharata in the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
गतो दशरथः स्वर्गं यो नो गुरुतरो गुरुः
रामं प्रव्राज्य वै ज्येष्ठं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
gato daśarathaḥ svargaṁ yo no gurutaro guruḥ
rāmaṁ pravrājya vai jyeṣṭhaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam

translations.english: Having exiled his eldest son and the exceedingly strong Lakşmaņa, Dasaratha who was the superior of our superiors has gone to heaven. Do you, therefore, O illustrious prince, become our king. Having been permitted by the king you will commit no fault (by doing so), as this kingdom is without a master.

verses.sanskrit:
आभिषेचनिकं सर्वमिदमादाय राघव
प्रतीक्षते त्वां स्वजनः श्रेणयश्च नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
ābhiṣecanikaṁ sarvamidamādāya rāghava
pratīkṣate tvāṁ svajanaḥ śreṇayaśca nṛpātmaja

translations.english: O Raghava, having procured all these necessaries for the installation, the counsellor and othe, as well as the citizens wait, О king's son.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं गृहाण भरत पितृपैतामहं महत्
अभिषेचय चात्मानं पाहि चास्मान्नरर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ gṛhāṇa bharata pitṛpaitāmahaṁ mahat
abhiṣecaya cātmānaṁ pāhi cāsmānnararṣabha

translations.english: Do you, O Bharata, take charge of this secure kingdom bequeathed by your father and grandfather. Do you, O foremost of men, have yourself sprinkled, and rule over us.

verses.sanskrit:
आभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं कृत्वा सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम्
भरतस्तं जनं सर्वं प्रत्युवाच धृतव्रतः
verses.transliteration:
ābhiṣecanikaṁ bhāṇḍaṁ kṛtvā sarvaṁ pradakṣiṇam
bharatastaṁ janaṁ sarvaṁ pratyuvāca dhṛtavrataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, having gone round all the things procured for the sprinkling, Bharata from in his vows addressed those persons, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठस्य राजता नित्यमुचिता हि कुलस्य नः
नैवं भवन्तो मां वक्तुमर्हन्ति कुशला जनाः
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhasya rājatā nityamucitā hi kulasya naḥ
naivaṁ bhavanto māṁ vaktumarhanti kuśalā janāḥ

translations.english: In our line it is ever fit for the first-born alone to perform the task of government. It does not behove you who are wise to say so to me.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः पूर्वो हि नो भ्राता भविष्यति महीपतिः
अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि वर्षाणि नव पञ्च च
verses.transliteration:
rāmaḥ pūrvo hi no bhrātā bhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ
ahaṁ tvaraṇye vatsyāmi varṣāṇi nava pañca ca

translations.english: Certainly Rāma our eldest brother shall become the king; and I will abide in the forest for five all nine years.

verses.sanskrit:
युज्यतां महती सेना चतुरङ्गमहाबला
आनयिष्याम्यहं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरं राघवं वनात्
verses.transliteration:
yujyatāṁ mahatī senā caturaṅgamahābalā
ānayiṣyāmyahaṁ jyeṣṭhaṁ bhrātaraṁ rāghavaṁ vanāt

translations.english: Do you array the grand and mighty my consisting of fourfold forces. I will bring back from the forest my eldest brother Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
आभिषेचनिकं चैव सर्वमेतदुपस्कृतम्
पुरस्कृत्य गमिष्यामि रामहेतोर्वनं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
ābhiṣecanikaṁ caiva sarvametadupaskṛtam
puraskṛtya gamiṣyāmi rāmahetorvanaṁ prati

translations.english: And taking all these necessaries for the investiture in front, I will go in the direction of the forest for Rāma. And sprinkling that chief of men on the spot, I will placing him in our front, bring Rāma back, like to fire brought in from the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
न सकामा करिष्यामि स्वमिमां मातृगन्धिनीम्
वने वत्स्याम्यहं दुर्गे रामो राजा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
na sakāmā kariṣyāmi svamimāṁ mātṛgandhinīm
vane vatsyāmyahaṁ durge rāmo rājā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: I will never fulfil the desire of this lady proud of her son. I will inhabit the impracticable woods, and Rāma shall become the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रियतां शिल्पिभिः पन्थाः समानि विषमाणि च
रक्षिणश्चानुसंयान्तु पथि दुर्गविचारकाः
verses.transliteration:
kriyatāṁ śilpibhiḥ panthāḥ samāni viṣamāṇi ca
rakṣiṇaścānusaṁyāntu pathi durgavicārakāḥ

translations.english: Let workmen lay out level roads in uneven tracts; and let those men that are adepts in threading places difficult to pass through, follow us.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं संभाषमाणं तं रामहेतोर्नृपात्मजम्
प्रत्युवाच जनः सर्वः श्रीमद्वाक्यमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ saṁbhāṣamāṇaṁ taṁ rāmahetornṛpātmajam
pratyuvāca janaḥ sarvaḥ śrīmadvākyamanuttamam

translations.english: When the prince had spoken thus in behalf of Rāma, all those persons answered him in these excellent words.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ते भाषमाणस्य पद्मा श्रीरुपतिष्ठताम्
यस्त्वं ज्येष्ठे नृपसुते पृथिवीं दातुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ te bhāṣamāṇasya padmā śrīrupatiṣṭhatām
yastvaṁ jyeṣṭhe nṛpasute pṛthivīṁ dātumicchasi

translations.english: For saying this, may Lakşmi seated on the lotus remain at they side; inasmuch you wish to confer the earth on the eldest son of the monarch!

verses.sanskrit:
अनुत्तमं तद्वचनं नृपात्मज; प्रभाषितं संश्रवणे निशम्य च
प्रहर्षजास्तं प्रति बाष्पबिन्दवो; निपेतुरार्यानननेत्रसंभवाः
verses.transliteration:
anuttamaṁ tadvacanaṁ nṛpātmaja; prabhāṣitaṁ saṁśravaṇe niśamya ca
praharṣajāstaṁ prati bāṣpabindavo; nipeturāryānananetrasaṁbhavāḥ

translations.english: Hearing that graceful speech of the king's son, tear-drops. begot of delight began to trickle from their eyes and adorned those noble countenances.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊचुस्ते वचनमिदं निशम्य हृष्टाः; सामात्याः सपरिषदो वियातशोकाः
पन्थानं नरवरभक्तिमाञ्जनश्च; व्यादिष्टस्तव वचनाच्च शिल्पिवर्गः
verses.transliteration:
ūcuste vacanamidaṁ niśamya hṛṣṭāḥ; sāmātyāḥ sapariṣado viyātaśokāḥ
panthānaṁ naravarabhaktimāñjanaśca; vyādiṣṭastava vacanācca śilpivargaḥ

translations.english: Their grief removed, with cheerful hearts, the counsellors, courtiers, and others hearing that speech (of the prince), said, “O best of men, according to your order artizans as well as people cherishing a high regard for you have been directed to lay out a read."

verses.sanskrit:
स तु हर्षात्तमुद्देशं जनौघो विपुलः प्रयान्
अशोभत महावेगः सागरस्येव पर्वणि
verses.transliteration:
sa tu harṣāttamuddeśaṁ janaugho vipulaḥ prayān
aśobhata mahāvegaḥ sāgarasyeva parvaṇi

translations.english: And as the mighty throng began to proceed, it resembled the swell of the sea on the occasion of a parva.

verses.sanskrit:
ते स्ववारं समास्थाय वर्त्मकर्माणि कोविदाः
करणैर्विविधोपेतैः पुरस्तात्संप्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
te svavāraṁ samāsthāya vartmakarmāṇi kovidāḥ
karaṇairvividhopetaiḥ purastātsaṁpratasthire

translations.english: And number of men skilled in roadconstructing went before furnished with various implements.

verses.sanskrit:
लतावल्लीश्च गुल्मांश्च स्थाणूनश्मन एव च
जनास्ते चक्रिरे मार्गं छिन्दन्तो विविधान्द्रुमान्
verses.transliteration:
latāvallīśca gulmāṁśca sthāṇūnaśmana eva ca
janāste cakrire mārgaṁ chindanto vividhāndrumān

translations.english: And hewing away boughs, plants and shrubs and woody projections, stones, and diverse trees, they went on preparing a road.

verses.sanskrit:
अवृक्षेषु च देशेषु केचिद्वृक्षानरोपयन्
केचित्कुठारैष्टङ्कैश्च दात्रैश्छिन्दन्क्वचित्क्वचित्
verses.transliteration:
avṛkṣeṣu ca deśeṣu kecidvṛkṣānaropayan
kecitkuṭhāraiṣṭaṅkaiśca dātraiśchindankvacitkvacit

translations.english: They set up trees where there were none, and at places they felled trees by means of axes, tankas, and daos, others possessed of greater strength and more powerful, with their hands uprooted masses of Vīrana and here and there levelled a rising ground. And other filled up with dust wells and capacious hollows, and speedily levelled deep places all around.

verses.sanskrit:
बबन्धुर्बन्धनीयांश्च क्षोद्यान्संचुक्षुदुस्तदा
बिभिदुर्भेदनीयांश्च तांस्तान्देशान्नरास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
babandhurbandhanīyāṁśca kṣodyānsaṁcukṣudustadā
bibhidurbhedanīyāṁśca tāṁstāndeśānnarāstadā

translations.english: And those men threw bridges wherever they became necessary, and broke the earth wherever such a process was required, and excavated whenever such a process was required, and excavated whenever it was necessary.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिरेणैव कालेन परिवाहान्बहूदकान्
चक्रुर्बहुविधाकारान्सागरप्रतिमान्बहून्
उदपानान्बहुविधान्वेदिका परिमण्डितान्
verses.transliteration:
acireṇaiva kālena parivāhānbahūdakān
cakrurbahuvidhākārānsāgarapratimānbahūn
udapānānbahuvidhānvedikā parimaṇḍitān

translations.english: In a short time, they made places poor of water overflow with many and various expanses resembling the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
ससुधाकुट्टिमतलः प्रपुष्पितमहीरुहः
मत्तोद्घुष्टद्विजगणः पताकाभिरलंकृतः
verses.transliteration:
sasudhākuṭṭimatalaḥ prapuṣpitamahīruhaḥ
mattodghuṣṭadvijagaṇaḥ patākābhiralaṁkṛtaḥ

translations.english: And the way of the army, furnished with pavements of bricks and clay, with trees bearing blossoms, eloquent with the tunes of birds, decorated with pennons, sprinkled with sandal showers, and garnished with flowers of various kinds, looked exceedingly beautiful, like to the way of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
आज्ञाप्याथ यथाज्ञप्ति युक्तास्तेऽधिकृता नराः
रमणीयेषु देशेषु बहुस्वादुफलेषु च
verses.transliteration:
ājñāpyātha yathājñapti yuktāste'dhikṛtā narāḥ
ramaṇīyeṣu deśeṣu bahusvāduphaleṣu ca

translations.english: Then having received the command of Bharata, the men that were in charge of the tents, ordered (the workmen) to pitch the tents, and when they had been pitched at a romantic spot filled with tasteful fruits, in consonance with the injunction of the high-souled Bharata, the men decorated splendidly the tents which themselves were like the ornaments of the road.

verses.sanskrit:
नक्षत्रेषु प्रशस्तेषु मुहूर्तेषु च तद्विदः
निवेशं स्थापयामासुर्भरतस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
nakṣatreṣu praśasteṣu muhūrteṣu ca tadvidaḥ
niveśaṁ sthāpayāmāsurbharatasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Under an auspicious star and at a favourable hour, men well up in the work set the encampment of the high-souled Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
विसर्पद्भिरिवाकाशे विटङ्काग्रविमानकैः
समुच्छ्रितैर्निवेशास्ते बभुः शक्रपुरोपमाः
verses.transliteration:
visarpadbhirivākāśe viṭaṅkāgravimānakaiḥ
samucchritairniveśāste babhuḥ śakrapuropamāḥ

translations.english: And the tents surrounded by an entrenchment paved with dust, containing images made of sapphires, graced with goodly thoroughfares, lined with edifices, encircled by towers and walls, decorated with streamers, having wellmade high-ways, and appearing like celestial daises and containing stately mansions dovecotes, resembled the metropolis of Śakra himself.

verses.sanskrit:
सचन्द्रतारागणमण्डितं यथा; नभःक्षपायाममलं विराजते
नरेन्द्रमार्गः स तथा व्यराजत; क्रमेण रम्यः शुभशिल्पिनिर्मितः
verses.transliteration:
sacandratārāgaṇamaṇḍitaṁ yathā; nabhaḥkṣapāyāmamalaṁ virājate
narendramārgaḥ sa tathā vyarājata; krameṇa ramyaḥ śubhaśilpinirmitaḥ

translations.english: And passing by the Jāhnavi abounding in various trees and woods, of cool and crystal waters, and filled with mighty fishes, that way of the chief of men constructed by artizans, looked more and more lovely as it proceeded, as the unclouded sky looks beautiful at night, adorned with innumerable stars.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नान्दीमुखीं रात्रिं भरतं सूतमागधाः
तुष्टुवुर्वाग्विशेषज्ञाः स्तवैर्मङ्गलसंहितैः
verses.transliteration:
tato nāndīmukhīṁ rātriṁ bharataṁ sūtamāgadhāḥ
tuṣṭuvurvāgviśeṣajñāḥ stavairmaṅgalasaṁhitaiḥ

translations.english: Then seeing that the night in which had been performed the auspicious preliminary ceremonies, was about to be spent, eulogists and genealogists hymned Bharata with consecrated hymns.

verses.sanskrit:
सुवर्णकोणाभिहतः प्राणदद्यामदुन्दुभिः
दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च शतशो वाद्यांश्चोच्चावचस्वरान्
verses.transliteration:
suvarṇakoṇābhihataḥ prāṇadadyāmadundubhiḥ
dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṁśca śataśo vādyāṁścoccāvacasvarān

translations.english: And then sounded the kettle-drum, beaten by a golden stick, announcing the departure of the night; and people sounded conchs and other instruments by hundreds furnished with soft and loud sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
स तूर्य घोषः सुमहान्दिवमापूरयन्निव
भरतं शोकसंतप्तं भूयः शोकैररन्ध्रयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tūrya ghoṣaḥ sumahāndivamāpūrayanniva
bharataṁ śokasaṁtaptaṁ bhūyaḥ śokairarandhrayat

translations.english: And as if filling the heavens, those powerful blasts of the trumpet repeatedly rendered Bharata burning in grief the more aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो प्रबुद्धो भरतस्तं घोषं संनिवर्त्य च
नाहं राजेति चाप्युक्त्वा शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato prabuddho bharatastaṁ ghoṣaṁ saṁnivartya ca
nāhaṁ rājeti cāpyuktvā śatrughnamidamabravīt

translations.english: Then awaking and silencing those sounds with saying, “I am not the king," he said to Satrughna.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य शत्रुघ्न कैकेय्या लोकस्यापकृतं महत्
विसृज्य मयि दुःखानि राजा दशरथो गतः
verses.transliteration:
paśya śatrughna kaikeyyā lokasyāpakṛtaṁ mahat
visṛjya mayi duḥkhāni rājā daśaratho gataḥ

translations.english: Behold, O Satrughna, in what a mighty wrong the people are engaged, on account of Kaikeyi. The king Dasaratha has gone away throwing down on me (the burthen of) this misery.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैषा धर्मराजस्य धर्ममूला महात्मनः
परिभ्रमति राजश्रीर्नौरिवाकर्णिका जले
verses.transliteration:
tasyaiṣā dharmarājasya dharmamūlā mahātmanaḥ
paribhramati rājaśrīrnaurivākarṇikā jale

translations.english: The royal grace founded in righteousness of that magnanimous and virtuous monarch is wandering even like a boat on water having no helmsman.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं भरतं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं विचेतनम्
कृपणं रुरुदुः सर्वाः सस्वरं योषितस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ bharataṁ prekṣya vilapantaṁ vicetanam
kṛpaṇaṁ ruruduḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṁ yoṣitastadā

translations.english: Seeing Bharata lamenting thus senseless, the ladies afflicted with sorrow began to wail in winsome accents.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तस्मिन्विलपति वसिष्ठो राजधर्मवित्
सभामिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य प्रविवेश महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
tathā tasminvilapati vasiṣṭho rājadharmavit
sabhāmikṣvākunāthasya praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: As Bharata was mourning thus, the highly famous and virtuous Vasistha accompanied by his disciples entered the court of the Ikşvāku king: built of entire gold, charming, dazzling with gems and gold: like to Sudharmä its. Sitting down on a golden seat furnished with a elegant cover, that one versed in all the Vedas commanded the envoys, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियान्योधानमात्यान्गणबल्लभान्
क्षिप्रमानयताव्यग्राः कृत्यमात्ययिकं हि नः
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇānkṣatriyānyodhānamātyāngaṇaballabhān
kṣipramānayatāvyagrāḥ kṛtyamātyayikaṁ hi naḥ

translations.english: Do you speedily with collected minds bring hither Brāhmaṇas and Kștriyas and warriors and counsellors and generals of forces and Satrughna with the other princes, and the famous Bharata and Yuddhajit* and Sumantra and others that are engaged in our welfare. *One of the counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हलहलाशब्दो महान्समुदपद्यत
रथैरश्वैर्गजैश्चापि जनानामुपगच्छताम्
verses.transliteration:
tato halahalāśabdo mahānsamudapadyata
rathairaśvairgajaiścāpi janānāmupagacchatām

translations.english: Then there arose a mighty hubbub occasioned by people coming up in cars, horses and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भरतमायान्तं शतक्रतुमिवामराः
प्रत्यनन्दन्प्रकृतयो यथा दशरथं तथा
verses.transliteration:
tato bharatamāyāntaṁ śatakratumivāmarāḥ
pratyanandanprakṛtayo yathā daśarathaṁ tathā

translations.english: When Bharata arrived, the subjects rejoiced as they used to rejoice on Daſaratha's arrival; and as rejoiced the immortals on the arrival of him of an hundred sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit:
ह्रद इव तिमिनागसंवृतः; स्तिमितजलो मणिशङ्खशर्करः
दशरथसुतशोभिता सभा; सदशरथेव बभौ यथा पुरा
verses.transliteration:
hrada iva timināgasaṁvṛtaḥ; stimitajalo maṇiśaṅkhaśarkaraḥ
daśarathasutaśobhitā sabhā; sadaśaratheva babhau yathā purā

translations.english: And then the court resembling a moveless ocean containing whales and serpents,* and gems and conchs and gold-mines, being graced with the presence of Dasaratha's son, looked splendid as it formerly did with that of Dasaratha himself. *Nāga may also mean hypopotamus.

verses.sanskrit:
तामार्यगणसंपूर्णां भरतः प्रग्रहां सभाम्
ददर्श बुद्धिसंपन्नः पूर्णचन्द्रां निशामिव
verses.transliteration:
tāmāryagaṇasaṁpūrṇāṁ bharataḥ pragrahāṁ sabhām
dadarśa buddhisaṁpannaḥ pūrṇacandrāṁ niśāmiva

translations.english: And then the intelligent Bharata surveyed that assembly filled with noble, and worthy personages, resembling the night of the full moon.

verses.sanskrit:
आसनानि यथान्यायमार्याणां विशतां तदा
अदृश्यत घनापाये पूर्णचन्द्रेव शर्वरी
verses.transliteration:
āsanāni yathānyāyamāryāṇāṁ viśatāṁ tadā
adṛśyata ghanāpāye pūrṇacandreva śarvarī

translations.english: And that splendid assembly filled with learned people looked like he night of the full moon after the clouds have dispersed.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञस्तु प्रकृतीः सर्वाः समग्राः प्रेक्ष्य धर्मवित्
इदं पुरोहितो वाक्यं भरतं मृदु चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rājñastu prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ samagrāḥ prekṣya dharmavit
idaṁ purohito vākyaṁ bharataṁ mṛdu cābravīt

translations.english: And seeing all the subjects of the sovereign gathered together, the priest cognizant of virtue softly spoke to Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
तात राजा दशरथः स्वर्गतो धर्ममाचरन्
धन धान्यवतीं स्फीतां प्रदाय पृथिवीं तव
verses.transliteration:
tāta rājā daśarathaḥ svargato dharmamācaran
dhana dhānyavatīṁ sphītāṁ pradāya pṛthivīṁ tava

translations.english: Your child, leaving to you this prosperous carth abounding in corn and wealth, king Dasaratha having performed his duties, has gone to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्तथा सत्यधृतिः सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्
नाजहात्पितुरादेशं शशी ज्योत्स्नामिवोदितः
verses.transliteration:
rāmastathā satyadhṛtiḥ satāṁ dharmamanusmaran
nājahātpiturādeśaṁ śaśī jyotsnāmivoditaḥ

translations.english: And Rāma of truthful character observing the virtue of the righteous has not set aside his father's commands. even as the risen moon does not renounce the moonlight.

verses.sanskrit:
उदीच्याश्च प्रतीच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च केवलाः
कोट्यापरान्ताः सामुद्रा रत्नान्यभिहरन्तु ते
verses.transliteration:
udīcyāśca pratīcyāśca dākṣiṇātyāśca kevalāḥ
koṭyāparāntāḥ sāmudrā ratnānyabhiharantu te

translations.english: Loved by the courtiers, do you, having been installed, enjoy this kingdom conferred on you by your father and mother, rid of its thorn. Let princes throned as well as those without thrones, from east, and west, north and south, and also persons ranging the sea, procure countless gems (for presenting them to you.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं शोकेनाभिपरिप्लुतः
जगाम मनसा रामं धर्मज्ञो धर्मकाङ्क्षया
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā bharato vākyaṁ śokenābhipariplutaḥ
jagāma manasā rāmaṁ dharmajño dharmakāṅkṣayā

translations.english: Hearing this speech, Bharata cognizant of virtue, filled with sorrow, mentally repaired to Rāma desirous of reaping merit.

verses.sanskrit:
स बाष्पकलया वाचा कलहंसस्वरो युवा
विललाप सभामध्ये जगर्हे च पुरोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa bāṣpakalayā vācā kalahaṁsasvaro yuvā
vilalāpa sabhāmadhye jagarhe ca purohitam

translations.english: Then in words choked with the melodious voice of a swan, lamented and taxed the priest, in the midst of the assembly.

verses.sanskrit:
चरितब्रह्मचर्यस्य विद्या स्नातस्य धीमतः
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य को राज्यं मद्विधो हरेत्
verses.transliteration:
caritabrahmacaryasya vidyā snātasya dhīmataḥ
dharme prayatamānasya ko rājyaṁ madvidho haret

translations.english: Who like myself ever deprives one that has led a Brahmacharya mode of life, that is endowed with understanding and performed his bath after having acquired learning, and that is always intent on righteousness, of one's kingdom?

verses.sanskrit:
कथं दशरथाज्जातो भवेद्राज्यापहारकः
राज्यं चाहं च रामस्य धर्मं वक्तुमिहार्हसि
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ daśarathājjāto bhavedrājyāpahārakaḥ
rājyaṁ cāhaṁ ca rāmasya dharmaṁ vaktumihārhasi

translations.english: How begot of Dasaratha, shall I deprive Rāma of his kingdom. It behove you to speak righteousness before this assembly.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठश्च धर्मात्मा दिलीपनहुषोपमः
लब्धुमर्हति काकुत्स्थो राज्यं दशरथो यथा
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaśca dharmātmā dilīpanahuṣopamaḥ
labdhumarhati kākutstho rājyaṁ daśaratho yathā

translations.english: First-born, and foremost in merit, righteoussouled, and comparable to Dilipa and Nahuşa, Kākutstha deserves the kingdom, just as Dasaratha did.

verses.sanskrit:
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यं कुर्यां पापमहं यदि
इक्ष्वाकूणामहं लोके भवेयं कुलपांसनः
verses.transliteration:
anāryajuṣṭamasvargyaṁ kuryāṁ pāpamahaṁ yadi
ikṣvākūṇāmahaṁ loke bhaveyaṁ kulapāṁsanaḥ
