verses.transliteration:
surāṁ surāpāḥ pibata pāyasaṁ ca bubhukśitāḥ
māṁsani ca sumedhyāni bhakṣyantāṁ yāvadicchatha

translations.english: Let wine-drinkers drink wine, the hungry eat Pāyasa, and those that are inclined to it, feed on clean meat.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्साद्य स्नापयन्ति स्म नदीतीरेषु वल्गुषु
अप्येकमेकं पुरुषं प्रमदाः सत्प चाष्ट च
verses.transliteration:
utsādya snāpayanti sma nadītīreṣu valguṣu
apyekamekaṁ puruṣaṁ pramadāḥ satpa cāṣṭa ca

translations.english: And every seven or eight females taking a man, bathed him on the lovely banks of the rivers.

verses.sanskrit:
संवहन्त्यः समापेतुर्नार्यो रुचिरलोचनाः
परिमृज्य तथान्योन्यं पाययन्ति वराङ्गनाः
verses.transliteration:
saṁvahantyaḥ samāpeturnāryo ruciralocanāḥ
parimṛjya tathānyonyaṁ pāyayanti varāṅganāḥ

translations.english: And damsels furnished with expansive eyes, having wiped the persons (of the bathers), pressed their legs, and those magnificent women made them drink (wine).

verses.sanskrit:
हयान्गजान्खरानुष्ट्रांस्तथैव सुरभेः सुतान्
इक्षूंश्च मधुजालांश्च भोजयन्ति स्म वाहनान्
इक्ष्वाकुवरयोधानां चोदयन्तो महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
hayāngajānkharānuṣṭrāṁstathaiva surabheḥ sutān
ikṣūṁśca madhujālāṁśca bhojayanti sma vāhanān
ikṣvākuvarayodhānāṁ codayanto mahābalāḥ

translations.english: And some persons possessed of mighty strength, being directed thereto, fed the bearers of the foremost Ikşvāku warriors with sugercanes, honey, and fried paddy.

verses.sanskrit:
नाश्वबन्धोऽश्वमाजानान्न गजं कुञ्जरग्रहः
मत्तप्रमत्तमुदिता चमूः सा तत्र संबभौ
verses.transliteration:
nāśvabandho'śvamājānānna gajaṁ kuñjaragrahaḥ
mattapramattamuditā camūḥ sā tatra saṁbabhau

translations.english: And the groom forgot his horse, and the elephant-keeper his elephant: that army there became transported with wine and exhilaration.

verses.sanskrit:
तर्पिता सर्वकामैस्ते रक्तचन्दनरूषिताः
अप्सरोगणसंयुक्ताः सैन्या वाचमुदैरयन्
verses.transliteration:
tarpitā sarvakāmaiste raktacandanarūṣitāḥ
apsarogaṇasaṁyuktāḥ sainyā vācamudairayan

translations.english: And sumptuously entertained with every enjoyment, with their bodies decked with red sandal, the soldiery in the company of bevies of Apsaras, exclaimed.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवायोध्यां गमिष्यामो न गमिष्याम दण्डकान्
कुशलं भरतस्यास्तु रामस्यास्तु तथा सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
naivāyodhyāṁ gamiṣyāmo na gamiṣyāma daṇḍakān
kuśalaṁ bharatasyāstu rāmasyāstu tathā sukham

translations.english: To Ayodhyā will we not go, nor yet to Dandaka. Peace be to Bharata, and may Rāma reap happiness!

verses.sanskrit:
इति पादातयोधाश्च हस्त्यश्वारोहबन्धकाः
अनाथास्तं विधिं लब्ध्वा वाचमेतामुदैरयन्
verses.transliteration:
iti pādātayodhāśca hastyaśvārohabandhakāḥ
anāthāstaṁ vidhiṁ labdhvā vācametāmudairayan

translations.english: Thus did footmen and the riders and keepers of elephants and horses, as well as others, having experienced such a state, utter words.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रहृष्टा विनेदुस्ते नरास्तत्र सहस्रशः
भरतस्यानुयातारः स्वर्गेऽयमिति चाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
saṁprahṛṣṭā vineduste narāstatra sahasraśaḥ
bharatasyānuyātāraḥ svarge'yamiti cābruvan

translations.english: And men by thousand, exceedinly delighted, sent up shouts. And saying. “This is heaven,” the retiune of Bharata, the soldiers, began to dance and laugh and sing; and bearing garlands, they on all sides rushed by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भुक्तवतां तेषां तदन्नममृतोपमम्
दिव्यानुद्वीक्ष्य भक्ष्यांस्तानभवद्भक्षणे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
tato bhuktavatāṁ teṣāṁ tadannamamṛtopamam
divyānudvīkṣya bhakṣyāṁstānabhavadbhakṣaṇe matiḥ

translations.english: And beholding the inviting viands resembling ambrosia, they although already fed, became desirous of eating once again.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेष्याश्चेट्यश्च वध्वश्च बलस्थाश्चापि सर्वशः
बभूवुस्ते भृशं तृप्ताः सर्वे चाहतवाससः
verses.transliteration:
preṣyāśceṭyaśca vadhvaśca balasthāścāpi sarvaśaḥ
babhūvuste bhṛśaṁ tṛptāḥ sarve cāhatavāsasaḥ

translations.english: And wearing new clothes, all the servants, and maids, and females of the household, became exceedingly well pleased.

verses.sanskrit:
कुञ्जराश्च खरोष्ट्रश्च गोश्वाश्च मृगपक्षिणः
बभूवुः सुभृतास्तत्र नान्यो ह्यन्यमकल्पयत्
verses.transliteration:
kuñjarāśca kharoṣṭraśca gośvāśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
babhūvuḥ subhṛtāstatra nānyo hyanyamakalpayat

translations.english: And elephants, and asses, camels, kine and horses, and beats and birds, being fed their fill, did not hunger after anything else.

verses.sanskrit:
नाशुक्लवासास्तत्रासीत्क्षुधितो मलिनोऽपि वा
रजसा ध्वस्तकेशो वा नरः कश्चिददृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
nāśuklavāsāstatrāsītkṣudhito malino'pi vā
rajasā dhvastakeśo vā naraḥ kaścidadṛśyata

translations.english: And there appeared no one who wore a soiled habit, or who was hungry, or melancholy, or whose hair was covered with dust.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पध्वजवतीः पूर्णाः शुक्लस्यान्नस्य चाभितः
ददृशुर्विस्मितास्तत्र नरा लौहीः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
puṣpadhvajavatīḥ pūrṇāḥ śuklasyānnasya cābhitaḥ
dadṛśurvismitāstatra narā lauhīḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And the people with wonder beheld before them vessels of precious metals by thousands graceful with chaplets of flowers, filled with essences of fruits and fragrant soups and curries and the flesh of goats and bears, and white rice.

verses.sanskrit:
बभूवुर्वनपार्श्वेषु कूपाः पायसकर्दमाः
ताश्च कामदुघा गावो द्रुमाश्चासन्मधुश्च्युतः
verses.transliteration:
babhūvurvanapārśveṣu kūpāḥ pāyasakardamāḥ
tāśca kāmadughā gāvo drumāścāsanmadhuścyutaḥ

translations.english: And there were on the skirts of the wood wells having Pāyasa for their slime; and the kine yeilded whatever was asked and all the trees dropped honey.

verses.sanskrit:
वाप्यो मैरेयपूर्णाश्च मृष्टमांसचयैर्वृताः
प्रतप्तपिठरैश्चापि मार्गमायूरकौक्कुटैः
verses.transliteration:
vāpyo maireyapūrṇāśca mṛṣṭamāṁsacayairvṛtāḥ
prataptapiṭharaiścāpi mārgamāyūrakaukkuṭaiḥ

translations.english: And the tanks were filled with Maireya as well as with clean hot meat of dear, peacocks, and cocks, dressed in pans.

verses.sanskrit:
पात्रीणां च सहस्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च
स्थाल्यः कुम्भ्यः करम्भ्यश्च दधिपूर्णाः सुसंस्कृताः
यौवनस्थस्य गौरस्य कपित्थस्य सुगन्धिनः
verses.transliteration:
pātrīṇāṁ ca sahasrāṇi śātakumbhamayāni ca
sthālyaḥ kumbhyaḥ karambhyaśca dadhipūrṇāḥ susaṁskṛtāḥ
yauvanasthasya gaurasya kapitthasya sugandhinaḥ

translations.english: And there were pitchers and water-pots and cleaned vessels for churning curd, filled with the same. And there were tanks of savoury and yellow butter-milk, well-tempered. And there were tanks filled with Rasāla;* and others filled with milk, and with sugar. *A preparation of butter-milk.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिपानह्रदान्पूर्णान्खरोष्ट्रगजवाजिनाम्
अवगाह्य सुतीर्थांश्च ह्रदान्सोत्पल पुष्करान्
verses.transliteration:
pratipānahradānpūrṇānkharoṣṭragajavājinām
avagāhya sutīrthāṁśca hradānsotpala puṣkarān

translations.english: And they saw reservoirs for asses, camels, elephants, and horses, with easy descents, filled with water to assist their digestion; and pools furnished with lotuses, of the hue of the firmament, with transparent water, comfortable for ablutions; and tender (plots of) grass all around coloured like blue lapises, to serve as pasture for beasts.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यस्मयन्त मनुष्यास्ते स्वप्नकल्पं तदद्भुतम्
दृष्ट्वातिथ्यं कृतं तादृग्भरतस्य महर्षिणा
verses.transliteration:
vyasmayanta manuṣyāste svapnakalpaṁ tadadbhutam
dṛṣṭvātithyaṁ kṛtaṁ tādṛgbharatasya maharṣiṇā

translations.english: Witnessing the wonderful hospitality provided by the Maharşi Bharadvāja, like to a vision, the men marvelled.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं रममाणानां देवानामिव नन्दने
भरद्वाजाश्रमे रम्ये सा रात्रिर्व्यत्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ ramamāṇānāṁ devānāmiva nandane
bharadvājāśrame ramye sā rātrirvyatyavartata

translations.english: Thus entertained like to celestials in Nandana, they passed the night at the hermitage of Bharadvāja.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिजग्मुश्च ता नद्यो गन्धर्वाश्च यथागतम्
भरद्वाजमनुज्ञाप्य ताश्च सर्वा वराङ्गनाः
verses.transliteration:
pratijagmuśca tā nadyo gandharvāśca yathāgatam
bharadvājamanujñāpya tāśca sarvā varāṅganāḥ

translations.english: Then taking the permission of Bharadvāja, all the Gandharvas as well as the superb damsels went away as they had come.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव मत्ता मदिरोत्कटा नरा;स्तथैव दिव्यागुरुचन्दनोक्षिताः
तथैव दिव्या विविधाः स्रगुत्तमाः; पृथक्प्रकीर्णा मनुजैः प्रमर्दिताः
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva mattā madirotkaṭā narā;stathaiva divyāgurucandanokṣitāḥ
tathaiva divyā vividhāḥ sraguttamāḥ; pṛthakprakīrṇā manujaiḥ pramarditāḥ

translations.english: And the men remained intoxicated and highly inebriate with the liquor, their persons daubed with goodly aguru and sandal; and the various elegant garlands beautiful to behold, lay by themselves all around, crushed by the people.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तां रजनीमुष्य भरतः सपरिच्छदः
कृतातिथ्यो भरद्वाजं कामादभिजगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
tatastāṁ rajanīmuṣya bharataḥ saparicchadaḥ
kṛtātithyo bharadvājaṁ kāmādabhijagāma ha

translations.english: Having passed that night, Bharata having been entertained along with his family, appeared before Bharadvāja, desirous (of seeing Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
तमृषिः पुरुषव्याघ्रं प्रेक्ष्य प्राञ्जलिमागतम्
हुताग्निहोत्रो भरतं भरद्वाजोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tamṛṣiḥ puruṣavyāghraṁ prekṣya prāñjalimāgatam
hutāgnihotro bharataṁ bharadvājo'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Seeing that foremost of men (standing) with joined hands, Bharadvāja, who had just finished his fire-sacrifice, said.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदत्र सुखा रात्रिस्तवास्मद्विषये गता
समग्रस्ते जनः कच्चिदातिथ्ये शंस मेऽनघ
verses.transliteration:
kaccidatra sukhā rātristavāsmadviṣaye gatā
samagraste janaḥ kaccidātithye śaṁsa me'nagha

translations.english: Have you passed the night pleasantly at our place? And have all your men been pleased with our hospitality? Do you tell me this O sinless one. we

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाचाञ्जलिं कृत्वा भरतोऽभिप्रणम्य च
आश्रमादभिनिष्क्रन्तमृषिमुत्तम तेजसम्
verses.transliteration:
tamuvācāñjaliṁ kṛtvā bharato'bhipraṇamya ca
āśramādabhiniṣkrantamṛṣimuttama tejasam

translations.english: Thereupon, Bharata bowing down, with joined hands said to that ascetic of excellent energy, as he had issued out of his hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
अपेतक्लमसंतापाः सुभक्ष्याः सुप्रतिश्रयाः
अपि प्रेष्यानुपादाय सर्वे स्म सुसुखोषिताः
verses.transliteration:
apetaklamasaṁtāpāḥ subhakṣyāḥ supratiśrayāḥ
api preṣyānupādāya sarve sma susukhoṣitāḥ

translations.english: O reverend Sire, I along with all my forces and vehicles have passed (the night) happily. I have been full well entertained by you, o worshipful one possessed of power. And with our languor and heat removed, all sumptuously feasted and comfortably quartered, have passed (the night) agreeably along with our servants.

verses.sanskrit:
आमन्त्रयेऽहं भगवन्कामं त्वामृषिसत्तम
समीपं प्रस्थितं भ्रातुर्मैरेणेक्षस्व चक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
āmantraye'haṁ bhagavankāmaṁ tvāmṛṣisattama
samīpaṁ prasthitaṁ bhrāturmaireṇekṣasva cakṣuṣā

translations.english: Now, O best of ascetics, I beseech you to look with a propitious eye on me who am bound for my brother's place.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्रमं तस्य धर्मज्ञ धार्मिकस्य महात्मनः
आचक्ष्व कतमो मार्गः कियानिति च शंस मे
verses.transliteration:
āśramaṁ tasya dharmajña dhārmikasya mahātmanaḥ
ācakṣva katamo mārgaḥ kiyāniti ca śaṁsa me

translations.english: And tell me, O you cognizant of morality, how far is it to that high-souled righteous one's asylm, and by what way (shall I reach there)?

verses.sanskrit:
इति पृष्टस्तु भरतं भ्रातृदर्शनलालसम्
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा भरद्वाजो महातपाः
verses.transliteration:
iti pṛṣṭastu bharataṁ bhrātṛdarśanalālasam
pratyuvāca mahātejā bharadvājo mahātapāḥ

translations.english: When Bharata eager to see his brother had asked thus, the highly energetic Bharadvāja of rigid austerities answered.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतार्धतृतीयेषु योजनेष्वजने वने
चित्रकूटो गिरिस्तत्र रम्यनिर्दरकाननः
verses.transliteration:
bharatārdhatṛtīyeṣu yojaneṣvajane vane
citrakūṭo giristatra ramyanirdarakānanaḥ

translations.english: O Bharata, two and a half Yojanas hence, embossed in a tenantless wood is the mountain Citrakuta, charming with rocks and woods.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरं पार्श्वमासाद्य तस्य मन्दाकिनी नदी
पुष्पितद्रुमसंछन्ना रम्यपुष्पितकानना
verses.transliteration:
uttaraṁ pārśvamāsādya tasya mandākinī nadī
puṣpitadrumasaṁchannā ramyapuṣpitakānanā

translations.english: On its northern border flows the river Mandākinſ, covered with flowering trees and with blossoming woods. Beyond the stream is the mountain Citrakuta. There is their thatched cottage, my child; there they abide for certain.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणेनैव मार्गेण सव्यदक्षिणमेव च
गजवाजिरथाकीर्णां वाहिनीं वाहिनीपते
वाहयस्व महाभाग ततो द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇenaiva mārgeṇa savyadakṣiṇameva ca
gajavājirathākīrṇāṁ vāhinīṁ vāhinīpate
vāhayasva mahābhāga tato drakṣyasi rāghavam

translations.english: Proceeding by the southern way, do you with your forces composed of elephants and horses, O master of the army, turn to the left, O exalted one, and go southwards. By doing so, you will be able to see Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयाणमिति च श्रुत्वा राजराजस्य योषितः
हित्वा यानानि यानार्हा ब्राह्मणं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
prayāṇamiti ca śrutvā rājarājasya yoṣitaḥ
hitvā yānāni yānārhā brāhmaṇaṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: Hearing of their departure, the wives of that king of kings, leaving their cars, albeit worthy of them, gathered round the Brāhmaṇa.

verses.sanskrit:
वेपमाना कृशा दीना सह देव्या सुमन्त्रिया
कौसल्या तत्र जग्राह कराभ्यां चरणौ मुनेः
verses.transliteration:
vepamānā kṛśā dīnā saha devyā sumantriyā
kausalyā tatra jagrāha karābhyāṁ caraṇau muneḥ

translations.english: Lean and trembling and in woeful guise, Kausalyā along with the noble Sumitrā, with her hands took the feet of the ascetic.

verses.sanskrit:
असमृद्धेन कामेन सर्वलोकस्य गर्हिता
कैकेयी तस्य जग्राह चरणौ सव्यपत्रपा
verses.transliteration:
asamṛddhena kāmena sarvalokasya garhitā
kaikeyī tasya jagrāha caraṇau savyapatrapā

translations.english: Depised universally because of her unrighteous desire, Kaikeyi also bashfully took hold of his feet and, having circumambulated the mighty and venerable anchoret, stood near Bharata in dejection of spirits.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पप्रच्छ भरतं भरद्वाजो दृढव्रतः
विशेषं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि मातॄणां तव राघव
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ papraccha bharataṁ bharadvājo dṛḍhavrataḥ
viśeṣaṁ jñātumicchāmi mātṝṇāṁ tava rāghava

translations.english: Then the mighty ascetic Bharadvāja asked Bharata, “O descendant of Raghu, I wish to know particularly about your mothers."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो भरद्वाजेन धार्मिकः
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यं वचनकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu bharato bharadvājena dhārmikaḥ
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā vākyaṁ vacanakovidaḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by Bharadvāja, the pious Bharata deft in speech said with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
एषा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्
कौसल्या सुषुवे रामं धातारमदितिर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
eṣā taṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ siṁhavikrāntagāminam
kausalyā suṣuve rāmaṁ dhātāramaditiryathā

translations.english: O reverend sir, she whom you behold depressed and emaciated through grief and fasting, resembling a very goddess, is the noble Queen of my father. This one, Kausalyā, it is that gave birth to that chief of men, having the powerful gait of a lion, Rāma, even as Aditi gave birth to Dhātā.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्यास्तौ सुतौ देव्याः कुमारौ देववर्णिनौ
उभौ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ वीरौ सत्यपराक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
etasyāstau sutau devyāḥ kumārau devavarṇinau
ubhau lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau vīrau satyaparākramau

translations.english: She that stands at her left hand, in dejected guise, is the noble Sumitrā afflicted with sorrow, the second wife of the monarch, like a Karņikāra bough in a forest, with all its blossoms shrivelled up. The sons of this exalted lady are the youthful and heroic Lakşmaņa and ſatrughna, having truth for their prowess, and resembling celestials in shape.

verses.sanskrit:
ऐश्वर्यकामां कैकेयीमनार्यामार्यरूपिणीम्
ममैतां मातरं विद्धि नृशंसां पापनिश्चयाम्
यतोमूलं हि पश्यामि व्यसनं महदात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
aiśvaryakāmāṁ kaikeyīmanāryāmāryarūpiṇīm
mamaitāṁ mātaraṁ viddhi nṛśaṁsāṁ pāpaniścayām
yatomūlaṁ hi paśyāmi vyasanaṁ mahadātmanaḥ

translations.english: And her in consequence of whose act those foremost of men have come by crushing misfortune, and the king Dasaratha has gone to heaven, deprived of his son, wrathful and proud of her good fortune, setting her heart of wealth, Kaikeyi, dishonourable, although endowed with the semblance of honour, do you know this wicked one intent on sin as my mother. In her do I perceive the root of my mighty misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा नरशार्दूलो बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा
स निशश्वास ताम्राक्षो क्रुद्धो नाग इवासकृत्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā naraśārdūlo bāṣpagadgadayā girā
sa niśaśvāsa tāmrākṣo kruddho nāga ivāsakṛt

translations.english: Having said this, with his words choked with emotion, that best of men with his eyes reddened, sighed like an enraged serpent.

verses.sanskrit:
भरद्वाजो महर्षिस्तं ब्रुवन्तं भरतं तदा
प्रत्युवाच महाबुद्धिरिदं वचनमर्थवत्
verses.transliteration:
bharadvājo maharṣistaṁ bruvantaṁ bharataṁ tadā
pratyuvāca mahābuddhiridaṁ vacanamarthavat

translations.english: As Bharata was speaking thus, the great ascetic Bharadvāja gifted with high understanding and knowing interest, answered Bharata, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न दोषेणावगन्तव्या कैकेयी भरत त्वया
रामप्रव्राजनं ह्येतत्सुखोदर्कं भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
na doṣeṇāvagantavyā kaikeyī bharata tvayā
rāmapravrājanaṁ hyetatsukhodarkaṁ bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O Bharata, you ought not to cast any blame on Kaikeyī. This banishment of the king (Rāma), shall be for the good (of all).

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्य तु संसिद्धः कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम्
आमन्त्र्य भरतः सैन्यं युज्यतामित्यचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
abhivādya tu saṁsiddhaḥ kṛtvā cainaṁ pradakṣiṇam
āmantrya bharataḥ sainyaṁ yujyatāmityacodayat

translations.english: Thus blest, Bharata saluted the ascetic and went round him, and then summoning the soldiery, said, “Yoke,"

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वाजिरथान्युक्त्वा दिव्यान्हेमपरिष्क्रितान्
अध्यारोहत्प्रयाणार्थी बहून्बहुविधो जनः
verses.transliteration:
tato vājirathānyuktvā divyānhemapariṣkritān
adhyārohatprayāṇārthī bahūnbahuvidho janaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, getting ready excellent steeds and cars decked with gold, many people mounted, with the intention of departing.

verses.sanskrit:
गजकन्यागजाश्चैव हेमकक्ष्याः पताकिनः
जीमूता इव घर्मान्ते सघोषाः संप्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
gajakanyāgajāścaiva hemakakṣyāḥ patākinaḥ
jīmūtā iva gharmānte saghoṣāḥ saṁpratasthire

translations.english: And male and female elephants with golden chains round their necks, and furnished with banners, with the sounds (of bells), proceeded, like clouds at the end of the summer season.

verses.sanskrit:
विविधान्यपि यानानि महानि च लघूनि च
प्रययुः सुमहार्हाणि पादैरेव पदातयः
verses.transliteration:
vividhānyapi yānāni mahāni ca laghūni ca
prayayuḥ sumahārhāṇi pādaireva padātayaḥ

translations.english: And then proceeded various kinds of cars great and light of movement and of high value; and the infantry went on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ यानप्रवेकैस्तु कौसल्याप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः
रामदर्शनकाङ्क्षिण्यः प्रययुर्मुदितास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
atha yānapravekaistu kausalyāpramukhāḥ striyaḥ
rāmadarśanakāṅkṣiṇyaḥ prayayurmuditāstadā

translations.english: And on a magnificent car went the ladies headed by Kausalyā, with delighted hearts, eager to see Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
स चार्कतरुणाभासां नियुक्तां शिबिकां शुभाम्
आस्थाय प्रययौ श्रीमान्भरतः सपरिच्छदः
verses.transliteration:
sa cārkataruṇābhāsāṁ niyuktāṁ śibikāṁ śubhām
āsthāya prayayau śrīmānbharataḥ saparicchadaḥ

translations.english: And ascending an elegant car resembling the infant sun or moon, driven by charioteers, went the graceful Bharata well attired.

verses.sanskrit:
सा प्रयाता महासेना गजवाजिरथाकुला
दक्षिणां दिशमावृत्य महामेघ इवोत्थितः
वनानि तु व्यतिक्रम्य जुष्टानि मृगपक्षिभिः
verses.transliteration:
sā prayātā mahāsenā gajavājirathākulā
dakṣiṇāṁ diśamāvṛtya mahāmegha ivotthitaḥ
vanāni tu vyatikramya juṣṭāni mṛgapakṣibhiḥ

translations.english: And that mighty host abounding with horses and elephants proceeded, blocking up the southern quarter, like a colossal cloud arisen (in the sky), leaving behind on the other bank of the Gangā woods inhabited by birds and beasts, and coursing by rivers mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
सा संप्रहृष्टद्विपवाजियोधा; वित्रासयन्ती मृगपक्षिसंघान्
महद्वनं तत्प्रविगाहमाना; रराज सेना भरतस्य तत्र
verses.transliteration:
sā saṁprahṛṣṭadvipavājiyodhā; vitrāsayantī mṛgapakṣisaṁghān
mahadvanaṁ tatpravigāhamānā; rarāja senā bharatasya tatra

translations.english: And composed of numbers of elephants and horses in high spirits, that army of Bharata, frightening multitudes of beasts and birds, dived into that mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तया महत्या यायिन्या ध्वजिन्या वनवासिनः
अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ताः सयूथाः संप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
tayā mahatyā yāyinyā dhvajinyā vanavāsinaḥ
arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthāḥ saṁpradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Afflicted by the mighty force on its way with banners (displayed), those inhabitants of the woods, leaders of elephant-herds, took to their heels in company with the herds themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षाः पृषतसंघाश्च रुरवश्च समन्ततः
दृश्यन्ते वनराजीषु गिरिष्वपि नदीषु च
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṁghāśca ruravaśca samantataḥ
dṛśyante vanarājīṣu giriṣvapi nadīṣu ca

translations.english: And bears and Prsatas and Rurus were on all sides seen in the forest-ways, and on hills and rivers.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्रतस्थे धर्मात्मा प्रीतो दशरथात्मजः
वृतो महत्या नादिन्या सेनया चतुरङ्गया
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁpratasthe dharmātmā prīto daśarathātmajaḥ
vṛto mahatyā nādinyā senayā caturaṅgayā

translations.english: And that virtuous son of Dasaratha with a glad heart held on this way, surrounded by that vast army consisting of fourfold forces, raising a tremendous uproar.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरौघनिभा सेना भरतस्य महात्मनः
महीं संछादयामास प्रावृषि द्यामिवाम्बुदः
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraughanibhā senā bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
mahīṁ saṁchādayāmāsa prāvṛṣi dyāmivāmbudaḥ

translations.english: And that army of the high-souled Bharata resembling the waves of the ocean, covered the earth quite, as clouds in the rainy season cover the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
तुरंगौघैरवतता वारणैश्च महाजवैः
अनालक्ष्या चिरं कालं तस्मिन्काले बभूव भूः
verses.transliteration:
turaṁgaughairavatatā vāraṇaiśca mahājavaiḥ
anālakṣyā ciraṁ kālaṁ tasminkāle babhūva bhūḥ

translations.english: And filled with steeds and mighty elephants, the earth at that time for a long while remained invisible.

verses.sanskrit:
स यात्वा दूरमध्वानं सुपरिश्रान्त वाहनः
उवाच भरतः श्रीमान्वसिष्ठं मन्त्रिणां वरम्
verses.transliteration:
sa yātvā dūramadhvānaṁ supariśrānta vāhanaḥ
uvāca bharataḥ śrīmānvasiṣṭhaṁ mantriṇāṁ varam

translations.english: And having proceeded a long way, the graceful Bharata, with his bearers extremely tired, said these words to that foremost of counsellors, Vasistha.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशं लक्ष्यते रूपं यथा चैव श्रुतं मया
व्यक्तं प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśaṁ lakṣyate rūpaṁ yathā caiva śrutaṁ mayā
vyaktaṁ prāptāḥ sma taṁ deśaṁ bharadvājo yamabravīt

translations.english: From appearances, and from what I had heard, it is evident that we have arrived at that region which Bharadvāja had told us of.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं गिरिश्चित्रकूटस्तथा मन्दाकिनी नदी
एतत्प्रकाशते दूरान्नीलमेघनिभं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ giriścitrakūṭastathā mandākinī nadī
etatprakāśate dūrānnīlameghanibhaṁ vanam

translations.english: This is the mountain Citrakuta and that the river Mandakinī. And from a distance this forest appears like dark clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरेः सानूनि रम्याणि चित्रकूटस्य संप्रति
वारणैरवमृद्यन्ते मामकैः पर्वतोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
gireḥ sānūni ramyāṇi citrakūṭasya saṁprati
vāraṇairavamṛdyante māmakaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ

translations.english: And now our elephants resembling hills afflict the romantic sides of Citrakuta.

verses.sanskrit:
मुञ्चन्ति कुसुमान्येते नगाः पर्वतसानुषु
नीला इवातपापाये तोयं तोयधरा घनाः
verses.transliteration:
muñcanti kusumānyete nagāḥ parvatasānuṣu
nīlā ivātapāpāye toyaṁ toyadharā ghanāḥ

translations.english: And the trees scatter blossoms over the sides of the mountain, even as after summer sable clouds pour down showers.

verses.sanskrit:
किन्नराचरितोद्देशं पश्य शत्रुघ्न पर्वतम्
हयैः समन्तादाकीर्णं मकरैरिव सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
kinnarācaritoddeśaṁ paśya śatrughna parvatam
hayaiḥ samantādākīrṇaṁ makarairiva sāgaram

translations.english: O Śatrughna, behold the realms inhabited by Kinnaras, scattered with steeds, like the main with makaras.

verses.sanskrit:
एते मृगगणा भान्ति शीघ्रवेगाः प्रचोदिताः
वायुप्रविद्धाः शरदि मेघराज्य इवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
ete mṛgagaṇā bhānti śīghravegāḥ pracoditāḥ
vāyupraviddhāḥ śaradi megharājya ivāmbare

translations.english: And these herds of deer furnished with celerity, being urged on, roam about like masses of clouds in the sky in autumn, propelled by the winds.

verses.sanskrit:
कुर्वन्ति कुसुमापीडाञ्शिरःसु सुरभीनमी
मेघप्रकाशैः फलकैर्दाक्षिणात्या यथा नराः
verses.transliteration:
kurvanti kusumāpīḍāñśiraḥsu surabhīnamī
meghaprakāśaiḥ phalakairdākṣiṇātyā yathā narāḥ

translations.english: And like the people of the south, these warriors bearing shields resembling clouds, are adorning their heads with ornaments of perfumed blossoms.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्कूजमिव भूत्वेदं वनं घोरप्रदर्शनम्
अयोध्येव जनाकीर्णा संप्रति प्रतिभाति मा
verses.transliteration:
niṣkūjamiva bhūtvedaṁ vanaṁ ghorapradarśanam
ayodhyeva janākīrṇā saṁprati pratibhāti mā

translations.english: And this forest, although void of men and dreadful in appearance, at present appears to me like Ayodhyā teeming with people.

verses.sanskrit:
खुरैरुदीरितो रेणुर्दिवं प्रच्छाद्य तिष्ठति
तं वहत्यनिलः शीघ्रं कुर्वन्निव मम प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
khurairudīrito reṇurdivaṁ pracchādya tiṣṭhati
taṁ vahatyanilaḥ śīghraṁ kurvanniva mama priyam

translations.english: The dust raised by the hoofs (of horses) stands covering the sky: anon the wind bearing it away, compasses my pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
स्यन्दनांस्तुरगोपेतान्सूतमुख्यैरधिष्ठितान्
एतान्संपततः शीघ्रं पश्य शत्रुघ्न कानने
verses.transliteration:
syandanāṁsturagopetānsūtamukhyairadhiṣṭhitān
etānsaṁpatataḥ śīghraṁ paśya śatrughna kānane

translations.english: And, O Satrughna, see how fast these cars yoked with steeds and driven by skilful charioteers, are proceeding in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
एतान्वित्रासितान्पश्य बर्हिणः प्रियदर्शनान्
एतमाविशतः शैलमधिवासं पतत्रिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
etānvitrāsitānpaśya barhiṇaḥ priyadarśanān
etamāviśataḥ śailamadhivāsaṁ patatriṇām

translations.english: And behold these beauteous peacocks, which, being frightened, take refuge in the mountain, the home of feathered tribes.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिमात्रमयं देशो मनोज्ञः प्रतिभाति मा
तापसानां निवासोऽयं व्यक्तं स्वर्गपथो यथा
verses.transliteration:
atimātramayaṁ deśo manojñaḥ pratibhāti mā
tāpasānāṁ nivāso'yaṁ vyaktaṁ svargapatho yathā

translations.english: This country appears to me exceedingly lovely. This abode of the ascetics is like to the way to heaven itself.

verses.sanskrit:
मृगा मृगीभिः सहिता बहवः पृषता वने
मनोज्ञ रूपा लक्ष्यन्ते कुसुमैरिव चित्रितः
verses.transliteration:
mṛgā mṛgībhiḥ sahitā bahavaḥ pṛṣatā vane
manojña rūpā lakṣyante kusumairiva citritaḥ

translations.english: Male and female deer and Prşatas in the forest, beautiful to look at, appear as if variegated with flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु सैन्याः प्रतिष्ठन्तां विचिन्वन्तु च काननम्
यथा तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ दृश्येते रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
sādhu sainyāḥ pratiṣṭhantāṁ vicinvantu ca kānanam
yathā tau puruṣavyāghrau dṛśyete rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Now let the soldiers go advisedly and search this forest, so that they light upon those chiefs of men, Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा पुरुषाः शस्त्रपाणयः
विविशुस्तद्वनं शूरा धूमं च ददृशुस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā puruṣāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ
viviśustadvanaṁ śūrā dhūmaṁ ca dadṛśustataḥ

translations.english: Hearing Bharata's speech, persons with weapons in their hands, plunged into the forest, and those heroes presently discovered the top of a (column of) smoke.

verses.sanskrit:
ते समालोक्य धूमाग्रमूचुर्भरतमागताः
नामनुष्ये भवत्यग्निर्व्यक्तमत्रैव राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
te samālokya dhūmāgramūcurbharatamāgatāḥ
nāmanuṣye bhavatyagnirvyaktamatraiva rāghavau

translations.english: Having seen the top of the (column of) smoke, they came before Bharata and said, "Fire cannot exist where there is no man present. Therefore it is evident that even here are those descendants of Raghu.”

verses.sanskrit:
अथ नात्र नरव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ परंतपौ
अन्ये रामोपमाः सन्ति व्यक्तमत्र तपस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
atha nātra naravyāghrau rājaputrau paraṁtapau
anye rāmopamāḥ santi vyaktamatra tapasvinaḥ

translations.english: But if those foremost of men, those subduers of their enemies, the princes, be not here, there are others, being ascetics, resembling Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्तेषां वचनं साधु संमतम्
सैन्यानुवाच सर्वांस्तानमित्रबलमर्दनः
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā bharatasteṣāṁ vacanaṁ sādhu saṁmatam
sainyānuvāca sarvāṁstānamitrabalamardanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing their words acceptable to the pious, that afflicter of hostile ranks, Bharata, said to the entire army.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्ता भवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तु नेतो गन्तव्यमग्रतः
अहमेव गमिष्यामि सुमन्त्रो गुरुरेव च
verses.transliteration:
yattā bhavantastiṣṭhantu neto gantavyamagrataḥ
ahameva gamiṣyāmi sumantro gurureva ca

translations.english: Do you carefully stay here: do not proceed further. I myself will go, and Sumantra and Dhrti.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तास्ततः सर्वे तत्र तस्थुः समन्ततः
भरतो यत्र धूमाग्रं तत्र दृष्टिं समादधत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāstataḥ sarve tatra tasthuḥ samantataḥ
bharato yatra dhūmāgraṁ tatra dṛṣṭiṁ samādadhat

translations.english: Thus desired, the troops remained all about that place. Bharata went away, keeping his gaze fixed in the direction of the top of the column of) smoke.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यवस्थिता या भरतेन सा चमू;र्निरीक्षमाणापि च धूममग्रतः
बभूव हृष्टा नचिरेण जानती; प्रियस्य रामस्य समागमं तदा
verses.transliteration:
vyavasthitā yā bharatena sā camū;rnirīkṣamāṇāpi ca dhūmamagrataḥ
babhūva hṛṣṭā nacireṇa jānatī; priyasya rāmasya samāgamaṁ tadā

translations.english: Desired by Bharata to halt, that army, looking in the direction of the smoke, rejoiced soon on learning that the beloved Rāma had arrived (at that place).

verses.sanskrit:
दीर्घकालोषितस्तस्मिन्गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः
विदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन्स्वं च चित्तं विलोभयन्
verses.transliteration:
dīrghakāloṣitastasmingirau girivanapriyaḥ
videhyāḥ priyamākāṅkṣansvaṁ ca cittaṁ vilobhayan

translations.english: Having spent a long time in that mountain, that lover of hills and woods, Dasaratha's son resembling an immortal, anxious to pleasure Vaidehī as well as to please his own mind, showed the variegated Citrakuța to his wife, like Purandara to Sacī.

verses.sanskrit:
न राज्याद्भ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः
मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम्
verses.transliteration:
na rājyādbhraṁśanaṁ bhadre na suhṛdbhirvinābhavaḥ
mano me bādhate dṛṣṭvā ramaṇīyamimaṁ girim

translations.english: O gentle one, neither deprivation of the kingdom nor separation from friends afflicts my mind on beholding this romantic mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्येममचलं भद्रे नानाद्विजगणायुतम्
शिखरैः खमिवोद्विद्धैर्धातुमद्भिर्विभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
paśyemamacalaṁ bhadre nānādvijagaṇāyutam
śikharaiḥ khamivodviddhairdhātumadbhirvibhūṣitam

translations.english: My gentle one, look but at the hill abounding with flocks of various birds, adorned with summits cleaving the welkin and teeming with mineral substances,

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्यार्ककेतुकाभाश्च केचिज्ज्योती रसप्रभाः
विराजन्तेऽचलेन्द्रस्य देशा धातुविभूषिताः
verses.transliteration:
puṣyārkaketukābhāśca kecijjyotī rasaprabhāḥ
virājante'calendrasya deśā dhātuvibhūṣitāḥ

translations.english: And some pares of this monarch of mountains are like silver, and some are blood-red, and some yellow like the hue of Mañjiștha, and some lustrous like sapphires, and some shining like blossoms or crystal or Ketakas, and some blazing like stars or mercury, and some digit in mineral substances.

verses.sanskrit:
नानामृगगणद्वीपितरक्ष्वृक्षगणैर्वृतः
अदुष्टैर्भात्ययं शैलो बहुपक्षिसमाकुलः
verses.transliteration:
nānāmṛgagaṇadvīpitarakṣvṛkṣagaṇairvṛtaḥ
aduṣṭairbhātyayaṁ śailo bahupakṣisamākulaḥ

translations.english: And the mountain shines, being filled with divers beasts and multitudes of innocuous tigers, hyenas and bears, and thronged with innumerable birds.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पवद्भिः फलोपेतैश्छायावद्भिर्मनोरमैः
एवमादिभिराकीर्णः श्रियं पुष्यत्ययं गिरिः
verses.transliteration:
puṣpavadbhiḥ phalopetaiśchāyāvadbhirmanoramaiḥ
evamādibhirākīrṇaḥ śriyaṁ puṣyatyayaṁ giriḥ

translations.english: And overspread with mangos, tose-apples, and Asanas, and Lodhras,* Piyālas, jacks, Ankolas, and Bhavyatinisas, and Bilvas, and Tindukas, and bamboos, Kasmaris, Aristas, and Varanas, and Madhukas, sesames, and jujubes, and Amalakas, Nipas, canes, Dhanvanas, and citrons, all in full flower, and bearing fruits, umbrageous and charming, the mountain attains an accession of loveliness. *Symplocos racemosa.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पश्येमान्कामहर्षणान्
किन्नरान्द्वंद्वशो भद्रे रममाणान्मनस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
śailaprastheṣu ramyeṣu paśyemānkāmaharṣaṇān
kinnarāndvaṁdvaśo bhadre ramamāṇānmanasvinaḥ

translations.english: And, you gentle one, on the picturesque plateou of the hill behold these intelligent couples of Kinnaras engaged in sport at spots yeilding every enjoyment and look at their swords hung up on the boughs. And see the gorgeous apparel of Vidyadharis, as well as the charming regions in which they sport.

verses.sanskrit:
जलप्रपातैरुद्भेदैर्निष्यन्दैश्च क्वचित्क्वचित्
स्रवद्भिर्भात्ययं शैलः स्रवन्मद इव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
jalaprapātairudbhedairniṣyandaiśca kvacitkvacit
sravadbhirbhātyayaṁ śailaḥ sravanmada iva dvipaḥ

translations.english: And like an elephant dropping the temporal juice, this hill appears beautiful with cascades, fountains and riles, flowing here and there.

verses.sanskrit:
गुहासमीरणो गन्धान्नानापुष्पभवान्वहन्
घ्राणतर्पणमभ्येत्य कं नरं न प्रहर्षयेत्
verses.transliteration:
guhāsamīraṇo gandhānnānāpuṣpabhavānvahan
ghrāṇatarpaṇamabhyetya kaṁ naraṁ na praharṣayet

translations.english: Whom does not the breeze laden with the perfumes of many a flower, soothing the sense of smell, fill with delight?

verses.sanskrit:
यदीह शरदोऽनेकास्त्वया सार्धमनिन्दिते
लक्ष्मणेन च वत्स्यामि न मां शोकः प्रधक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadīha śarado'nekāstvayā sārdhamanindite
lakṣmaṇena ca vatsyāmi na māṁ śokaḥ pradhakṣyati

translations.english: If, O blameless one, I dwell (here) for many years with you as well as Lakşmaņa, grief cannot overcome me.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुपुष्पफले रम्ये नानाद्विजगणायुते
विचित्रशिखरे ह्यस्मिन्रतवानस्मि भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
bahupuṣpaphale ramye nānādvijagaṇāyute
vicitraśikhare hyasminratavānasmi bhāmini

translations.english: O damsel, I take delight in this picturesque peak abounding in flowers and fruits, and frequented by various birds.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन वनवासेन मया प्राप्तं फलद्वयम्
पितुश्चानृणता धर्मे भरतस्य प्रियं तथा
verses.transliteration:
anena vanavāsena mayā prāptaṁ phaladvayam
pituścānṛṇatā dharme bharatasya priyaṁ tathā

translations.english: By this banishment of mine, I have gained two things, my father has maintained his truth in religion, and Bharata has obtained his dear interest.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह
पश्यन्ती विविधान्भावान्मनोवाक्कायसंयतान्
verses.transliteration:
vaidehi ramase kacciccitrakūṭe mayā saha
paśyantī vividhānbhāvānmanovākkāyasaṁyatān

translations.english: O daughter of Videha, are you being pleased on viewing along with me on Citrakuța, various objects grateful to mind, speech and body?

verses.sanskrit:
इदमेवामृतं प्राहू राज्ञां राजर्षयः परे
वनवासं भवार्थाय प्रेत्य मे प्रपितामहाः
verses.transliteration:
idamevāmṛtaṁ prāhū rājñāṁ rājarṣayaḥ pare
vanavāsaṁ bhavārthāya pretya me prapitāmahāḥ

translations.english: O queen, this abode in the forest like to ambrosia has been declared by those royal saints, my ancestors, as working out one's emancipation after death.

verses.sanskrit:
शिलाः शैलस्य शोभन्ते विशालाः शतशोऽभितः
बहुला बहुलैर्वर्णैर्नीलपीतसितारुणैः
verses.transliteration:
śilāḥ śailasya śobhante viśālāḥ śataśo'bhitaḥ
bahulā bahulairvarṇairnīlapītasitāruṇaiḥ

translations.english: The giant crags of the mountain grace the place all round by hundreds; many and varioushued, blue and yellow and pale and red.

verses.sanskrit:
निशि भान्त्यचलेन्द्रस्य हुताशनशिखा इव
ओषध्यः स्वप्रभा लक्ष्म्या भ्राजमानाः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
niśi bhāntyacalendrasya hutāśanaśikhā iva
oṣadhyaḥ svaprabhā lakṣmyā bhrājamānāḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: In the night, the annual herbs by thousands growing on this foremost of hills, shine and become visible by their own lustre, like flames of fire.

verses.sanskrit:
केचित्क्षयनिभा देशाः केचिदुद्यानसंनिभाः
केचिदेकशिला भान्ति पर्वतस्यास्य भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
kecitkṣayanibhā deśāḥ kecidudyānasaṁnibhāḥ
kecidekaśilā bhānti parvatasyāsya bhāmini

translations.english: And, O lady, some parts of the mountain appear like dwellings, and some like gardens, and some, again, consist of single rocks (capable of accommodating numbers of men).

verses.sanskrit:
भित्त्वेव वसुधां भाति चित्रकूटः समुत्थितः
चित्रकूटस्य कूटोऽसौ दृश्यते सर्वतः शिवः
verses.transliteration:
bhittveva vasudhāṁ bhāti citrakūṭaḥ samutthitaḥ
citrakūṭasya kūṭo'sau dṛśyate sarvataḥ śivaḥ

translations.english: And Citrakuța looks as if it had arisen, riving the earth; and the fair front of Citrakuța can be perceived from every point.

verses.sanskrit:
कुष्ठपुंनागतगरभूर्जपत्रोत्तरच्छदान्
कामिनां स्वास्तरान्पश्य कुशेशयदलायुतान्
verses.transliteration:
kuṣṭhapuṁnāgatagarabhūrjapatrottaracchadān
kāmināṁ svāstarānpaśya kuśeśayadalāyutān

translations.english: behold the beds of pleasure-seekers, consisting of the petals of lotuses, with Sthagaras, Punāgas and Bhūrjapatras for their coverlets.

verses.sanskrit:
मृदिताश्चापविद्धाश्च दृश्यन्ते कमलस्रजः
कामिभिर्वनिते पश्य फलानि विविधानि च
verses.transliteration:
mṛditāścāpaviddhāśca dṛśyante kamalasrajaḥ
kāmibhirvanite paśya phalāni vividhāni ca

translations.english: And, my wife, behold these lotus-garlands have been crushed and scattered; and the various fruits have been partaken of.

verses.sanskrit:
वस्वौकसारां नलिनीमत्येतीवोत्तरान्कुरून्
पर्वतश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ बहुमूलफलोदकः
verses.transliteration:
vasvaukasārāṁ nalinīmatyetīvottarānkurūn
parvataścitrakūṭo'sau bahumūlaphalodakaḥ

translations.english: The mountain Citrakuța abounding in fruits and roots and waters, surpasses Kuvera's capital Śakra's city or the north Kurus.

verses.sanskrit:
इमं तु कालं वनिते विजह्रिवां;स्त्वया च सीते सह लक्ष्मणेन च
रतिं प्रपत्स्ये कुलधर्मवर्धिनीं; सतां पथि स्वैर्नियमैः परैः स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
imaṁ tu kālaṁ vanite vijahrivāṁ;stvayā ca sīte saha lakṣmaṇena ca
ratiṁ prapatsye kuladharmavardhinīṁ; satāṁ pathi svairniyamaiḥ paraiḥ sthitaḥ

translations.english: My wife, O Sītā, if in consonance with my own excellent rules, I can, remaining in the path of the pious, pleasantly pass this time along with yourself and Lakşmaņa, then I shall attain the happiness resulting from observing the duties of one's race. or

verses.sanskrit:
अथ शैलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेश्वरः
अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
atha śailādviniṣkramya maithilīṁ kosaleśvaraḥ
adarśayacchubhajalāṁ ramyāṁ mandākinīṁ nadīm

translations.english: Then going out of the mountain, the Lord of Kosala showed to Mithila's daughter the charming stream Mandākini of excellent waters.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां चारुचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
विदेहराजस्य सुतां रामो राजीवलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca varārohāṁ cārucandranibhānanām
videharājasya sutāṁ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ

translations.english: And Rāma, furnished with eyes resembling lotuses, addressed the daughter of king Videha, transcendentally beautiful, with a countenance like the fair moon, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाविधैस्तीररुहैर्वृतां पुष्पफलद्रुमैः
राजन्तीं राजराजस्य नलिनीमिव सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
nānāvidhaistīraruhairvṛtāṁ puṣpaphaladrumaiḥ
rājantīṁ rājarājasya nalinīmiva sarvataḥ

translations.english: Behold the river Mandākini, having variegated islets; beautiful; frequented by ducks and cranes; and filled with flowers; covered with diverse trees bearing fruits and flowers; and looking graceful all round like Saughandhikā herself of Kuvera.

verses.sanskrit:
मृगयूथनिपीतानि कलुषाम्भांसि साम्प्रतम्
तीर्थानि रमणीयानि रतिं संजनयन्ति मे
verses.transliteration:
mṛgayūthanipītāni kaluṣāmbhāṁsi sāmpratam
tīrthāni ramaṇīyāni ratiṁ saṁjanayanti me

translations.english: And the waters rendered muddy in consequence of herds of deer drinking of them, as well as the graceful descents to the river, fill me with pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
जटाजिनधराः काले वल्कलोत्तरवाससः
ऋषयस्त्ववगाहन्ते नदीं मन्दाकिनीं प्रिये
verses.transliteration:
jaṭājinadharāḥ kāle valkalottaravāsasaḥ
ṛṣayastvavagāhante nadīṁ mandākinīṁ priye

translations.english: And, my beloved sages wearing matted locks and deer-skins, with barks for their sheets, are in season performing their ablutions in the river Mandakini.

verses.sanskrit:
आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते नियमादूर्ध्वबाहवः
एतेऽपरे विशालाक्षि मुनयः संशितव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
ādityamupatiṣṭhante niyamādūrdhvabāhavaḥ
ete'pare viśālākṣi munayaḥ saṁśitavratāḥ

translations.english: And observing rules, persons raising up their arms, are worshipping the sun, and, O you of expansive eyes, after these appear ascetics following vows, (engaged if Tapa)

verses.sanskrit:
मारुतोद्धूत शिखरैः प्रनृत्त इव पर्वतः
पादपैः पत्रपुष्पाणि सृजद्भिरभितो नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
mārutoddhūta śikharaiḥ pranṛtta iva parvataḥ
pādapaiḥ patrapuṣpāṇi sṛjadbhirabhito nadīm

translations.english: And the hill seems to dance on the wind swaying the tops of tree; and on both sides of the river, the trees are crowned with flowers and leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्मणिनिकाशोदां कच्चित्पुलिनशालिनीम्
कच्चित्सिद्धजनाकीर्णां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
kaccinmaṇinikāśodāṁ kaccitpulinaśālinīm
kaccitsiddhajanākīrṇāṁ paśya mandākinīṁ nadīm

translations.english: And behold the river Mandakini, somewhere with its waters resembling pearls, and somewhere with islets, and somewhere filled with persons who have attained emancipation.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्धूतान्वायुना पश्य विततान्पुष्पसंचयान्
पोप्लूयमानानपरान्पश्य त्वं जलमध्यगान्
verses.transliteration:
nirdhūtānvāyunā paśya vitatānpuṣpasaṁcayān
poplūyamānānaparānpaśya tvaṁ jalamadhyagān

translations.english: O you of slender waist, behold these hosts of flowers spreading along, and others dipping themselves (in the stream).

verses.sanskrit:
तांश्चातिवल्गु वचसो रथाङ्गाह्वयना द्विजाः
अधिरोहन्ति कल्याणि निष्कूजन्तः शुभा गिरः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁścātivalgu vacaso rathāṅgāhvayanā dvijāḥ
adhirohanti kalyāṇi niṣkūjantaḥ śubhā giraḥ

translations.english: And, O auspicious one, behold these sweetthroated birds, the Chakravākas, getting upon the islets, uttering pleasant notes.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शनं चित्रकूटस्य मन्दाकिन्याश्च शोभने
अधिकं पुरवासाच्च मन्ये च तव दर्शनात्
verses.transliteration:
darśanaṁ citrakūṭasya mandākinyāśca śobhane
adhikaṁ puravāsācca manye ca tava darśanāt

translations.english: Methinks, O beauteous one, the sight of Citrakuta and of Mandakini is even more delightful than life in the metropolis, or the sight of your own self.

verses.sanskrit:
विधूतकलुषैः सिद्धैस्तपोदमशमान्वितैः
नित्यविक्षोभित जलां विहाहस्व मया सह
verses.transliteration:
vidhūtakaluṣaiḥ siddhaistapodamaśamānvitaiḥ
nityavikṣobhita jalāṁ vihāhasva mayā saha

translations.english: Do you like to her companion perform your bath with me in this stream, whose waters are perpetually stirred by emancipated ones, furnished with asceticism, self-restraint, and control over the senses, who have had their sins removed.

verses.sanskrit:
सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दकिनीमिमाम्
कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
sakhīvacca vigāhasva sīte mandakinīmimām
kamalānyavamajjantī puṣkarāṇi ca bhāmini

translations.english: Do you, O Sītā, perform your ablutions in the Mandākinī, scattering at the sometime, O girl, red and white lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं पौरजनवद्व्यालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम्
मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ paurajanavadvyālānayodhyāmiva parvatam
manyasva vanite nityaṁ sarayūvadimāṁ nadīm

translations.english: Do you, my wife, always consider the wild animals as citizens, the mountain as Ayodhyā, and this stream as the Sarayū.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्चैव धर्मात्मा मन्निदेशे व्यवस्थितः
त्वं चानुकूला वैदेहि प्रीतिं जनयथो मम
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaścaiva dharmātmā mannideśe vyavasthitaḥ
tvaṁ cānukūlā vaidehi prītiṁ janayatho mama

translations.english: The virtuous Lakşmaņa is ever obedient to my commands; and, O Videha's daughter, you also are favourable to me.

verses.sanskrit:
उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं मधुमूलफलाशनः
नायोध्यायै न राज्याय स्पृहयेऽद्य त्वया सह
verses.transliteration:
upaspṛśaṁstriṣavaṇaṁ madhumūlaphalāśanaḥ
nāyodhyāyai na rājyāya spṛhaye'dya tvayā saha

translations.english: This causes delight in my heart. Bathing thrice (in this river), and living on tasteful fruits and roots, I in your company do not today wish either for Ayodhyā or royalty.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां हि रम्यां गजयूथलोलितां; निपीततोयां गजसिंहवानरैः
सुपुष्पितैः पुष्पधरैरलंकृतां; न सोऽस्ति यः स्यान्न गतक्रमः सुखी
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ hi ramyāṁ gajayūthalolitāṁ; nipītatoyāṁ gajasiṁhavānaraiḥ
supuṣpitaiḥ puṣpadharairalaṁkṛtāṁ; na so'sti yaḥ syānna gatakramaḥ sukhī

translations.english: Bathing in this beauteous stream agitated by herds of elephants, whose waters are drunk by elephants, lions and monkeys, which is graced with flowers, and which is decked with multitudes of blossoms, there is not one who has not his fatigue removed, and who does not feel exhilarated.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव रामो बहुसंगतं वचः; प्रिया सहायः सरितं प्रति ब्रुवन्
चचार रम्यं नयनाञ्जनप्रभं; स चित्रकूटं रघुवंशवर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
itīva rāmo bahusaṁgataṁ vacaḥ; priyā sahāyaḥ saritaṁ prati bruvan
cacāra ramyaṁ nayanāñjanaprabhaṁ; sa citrakūṭaṁ raghuvaṁśavardhanaḥ

translations.english: Having thus along with his beloved one, spoken variously regarding the stream, that perpetuator of the Raghu race, began to range the charming Citrakuța, resembling the collyrium in hue.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तत्रासतस्तस्य भरतस्योपयायिनः
सैन्य रेणुश्च शब्दश्च प्रादुरास्तां नभः स्पृशौ
verses.transliteration:
tathā tatrāsatastasya bharatasyopayāyinaḥ
sainya reṇuśca śabdaśca prādurāstāṁ nabhaḥ spṛśau

translations.english: This clean meat tastes sweet, having been roasted in fire. The righteous Rāghava was thus seated in company with Sītā, when Bharata's followers came there. And filling the heavens, there arose clouds of dust raised by the army as well as an uproar.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे त्रस्ताः शब्देन महता ततः
अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ताः सयूथा दुद्रुवुर्दिशः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare trastāḥ śabdena mahatā tataḥ
arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthā dudruvurdiśaḥ

translations.english: And at this time mad leaders of elephant-herds accompanied by the latter, scared by the terrible tumult, scudded on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं सैन्यसमुद्भूतं शब्दं शुश्रव राघवः
तांश्च विप्रद्रुतान्सर्वान्यूथपानन्ववैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ sainyasamudbhūtaṁ śabdaṁ śuśrava rāghavaḥ
tāṁśca vipradrutānsarvānyūthapānanvavaikṣata

translations.english: And Rāghava heard the noise raised by the army; and also saw all those leaders of elephantherds scampering away.

verses.sanskrit:
तांश्च विद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा तं च श्रुत्वा स निःस्वनम्
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁśca vidravato dṛṣṭvā taṁ ca śrutvā sa niḥsvanam
uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ dīptatejasam

translations.english: And having seen them running away and heard that hubbub, Rāma spoke to Sumitrā's son, Lakşmaņa of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा वा राजमात्रो वा मृगयामटते वने
अन्यद्वा श्वापदं किंचित्सौमित्रे ज्ञातुमर्हसि
सर्वमेतद्यथातत्त्वमचिराज्ज्ञातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
rājā vā rājamātro vā mṛgayāmaṭate vane
anyadvā śvāpadaṁ kiṁcitsaumitre jñātumarhasi
sarvametadyathātattvamacirājjñātumarhasi

translations.english: Ha! Lakşmaņa, in whom Şumitrā has been blest with a worthy son, hark! A tremendous and dreadful uproar resembling the rumbling of clouds is being heard; and in the woods and mighty forest, deer and buffaloes and herds of elephants being accompanied by lions are suddenly scampering away in all directions. O Sumitrā's son, it behoves you to learn whether any king or prince is hunting in the forest, or any ferocious beast is (ravaging the woods).

verses.sanskrit:
स लक्ष्मणः संत्वरितः सालमारुह्य पुष्पितम्
प्रेक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वाः पूर्वां दिशमवैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
sa lakṣmaṇaḥ saṁtvaritaḥ sālamāruhya puṣpitam
prekṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvāḥ pūrvāṁ diśamavaikṣata

translations.english: Thereat, hurriedly ascending a flowering Säla tree, Laksmana surveying all sides, fixed his gaze on the east. to

verses.sanskrit:
उदङ्मुखः प्रेक्षमाणो ददर्श महतीं चमूम्
रथाश्वगजसंबाधां यत्तैर्युक्तां पदातिभिः
verses.transliteration:
udaṅmukhaḥ prekṣamāṇo dadarśa mahatīṁ camūm
rathāśvagajasaṁbādhāṁ yattairyuktāṁ padātibhiḥ

translations.english: And viewing the east, he discovered a mighty army, abounding with elephants, horses and cars, and consisting of equipped infantry.

verses.sanskrit:
तामश्वगजसंपूर्णां रथध्वजविभूषिताम्
शशंस सेनां रामाय वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāmaśvagajasaṁpūrṇāṁ rathadhvajavibhūṣitām
śaśaṁsa senāṁ rāmāya vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon, Lakşmaņa communicated Rāma tidings concerning that army filled with elephants and steeds, and decked with cars and streamers; and spoke to Rāma, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निं संशमयत्वार्यः सीता च भजतां गुहाम्
सज्यं कुरुष्व चापं च शरांश्च कवचं तथा
verses.transliteration:
agniṁ saṁśamayatvāryaḥ sītā ca bhajatāṁ guhām
sajyaṁ kuruṣva cāpaṁ ca śarāṁśca kavacaṁ tathā

translations.english: O noble one, do you put out the fire; and let Sītā go into the cave. And do you string your bow and make ready the arrows and don on your mail.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रामः पुरुषव्याघ्रो लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाच ह
अङ्गावेक्षस्व सौमित्रे कस्यैतां मन्यसे चमूम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rāmaḥ puruṣavyāghro lakṣmaṇaṁ pratyuvāca ha
aṅgāvekṣasva saumitre kasyaitāṁ manyase camūm

translations.english: Thereat, Rāma-chief of men, answered Lakş mana, saying O son of Sumitra, do you (first) ascertain whom this host belongs to.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्क्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्माणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
दिधक्षन्निव तां सेनां रुषितः पावको यथा
verses.transliteration:
evamukktastu rāmeṇa lakṣmāṇo vākyamabravīt
didhakṣanniva tāṁ senāṁ ruṣitaḥ pāvako yathā

translations.english: Thus accosted by Rama, Laksmana, as if consuming that army by his wrath resembling fire, said.

verses.sanskrit:
संपन्नं राज्यमिच्छंस्तु व्यक्तं प्राप्याभिषेचनम्
आवां हन्तुं समभ्येति कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpannaṁ rājyamicchaṁstu vyaktaṁ prāpyābhiṣecanam
āvāṁ hantuṁ samabhyeti kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Having got himself installed, Kaikeyi's son, Bharata, anxious to render his royalty perfectly safe, is coming hither for the purpose of slaying us both.

verses.sanskrit:
एष वै सुमहाञ्श्रीमान्विटपी संप्रकाशते
विराजत्युद्गतस्कन्धः कोविदार ध्वजो रथे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa vai sumahāñśrīmānviṭapī saṁprakāśate
virājatyudgataskandhaḥ kovidāra dhvajo rathe

translations.english: Yonder is seen the graceful tree. By the same apr-ars on the car the Kovidāra standard, having a shining top.

verses.sanskrit:
भजन्त्येते यथाकाममश्वानारुह्य शीघ्रगान्
एते भ्राजन्ति संहृष्टा गजानारुह्य सादिनः
verses.transliteration:
bhajantyete yathākāmamaśvānāruhya śīghragān
ete bhrājanti saṁhṛṣṭā gajānāruhya sādinaḥ

translations.english: And men riding swift coursers are at their riders, riding on elephants, are also cheerfully directing their course hither.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतधनुषौ चावां गिरिं वीर श्रयावहे
अथ वेहैव तिष्ठावः संनद्धावुद्यतायुधौ
अपि नौ वशमागच्छेत्कोविदारध्वजो रणे
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītadhanuṣau cāvāṁ giriṁ vīra śrayāvahe
atha vehaiva tiṣṭhāvaḥ saṁnaddhāvudyatāyudhau
api nau vaśamāgacchetkovidāradhvajo raṇe

translations.english: Let us, O hero, taking our bows, station ourselves on this hill. I will (to day) see Bharata, for whom we have come by this mighty misfortune. Or let us rather remain where we are accoutred in mail and with our arms ready. Shall he of the Kovidāra banner in conflict come under our sway? O hero, we have met with that foe of ours for whom, O Rāghava, you, Sītā and myself have (experienced such misery), for whom, O Rāghava, you have been cast off from the entire kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्य वधे दोषं नाहं पश्यामि राघव
पूर्वापकारिणां त्यागे न ह्यधर्मो विधीयते
एतस्मिन्निहते कृत्स्नामनुशाधि वसुंधराम्
verses.transliteration:
bharatasya vadhe doṣaṁ nāhaṁ paśyāmi rāghava
pūrvāpakāriṇāṁ tyāge na hyadharmo vidhīyate
etasminnihate kṛtsnāmanuśādhi vasuṁdharām

translations.english: Surely, Bharata should be slain by me. O Rāghava, fault find I none in slaying Bharata; slaying a former wronger, one does not reap unrighteousness. O Raghava, there is religious merit to be reaped by slaying Bharata, who had formerly done us wrong.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य पुत्रं हतं संख्ये कैकेयी राज्यकामुका
मया पश्येत्सुदुःखार्ता हस्तिभग्नमिव द्रुमम्
verses.transliteration:
adya putraṁ hataṁ saṁkhye kaikeyī rājyakāmukā
mayā paśyetsuduḥkhārtā hastibhagnamiva drumam

translations.english: On this one being slain, you will rule the entire earth. To day shall Kaikeyi lusting after the kingdom, with grief behold her son slain in battle by me, like a tree riven by an elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेयीं च वधिष्यामि सानुबन्धां सबान्धवाम्
कलुषेणाद्य महता मेदिनी परिमुच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyīṁ ca vadhiṣyāmi sānubandhāṁ sabāndhavām
kaluṣeṇādya mahatā medinī parimucyatām

translations.english: I will also kill Kaikeyi along (with the humpbacked one, and her friends. Let the earth today be freed from foul sins.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्येमं संयतं क्रोधमसत्कारं च मानद
मोक्ष्यामि शत्रुसैन्येषु कक्षेष्विव हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
adyemaṁ saṁyataṁ krodhamasatkāraṁ ca mānada
mokṣyāmi śatrusainyeṣu kakṣeṣviva hutāśanam

translations.english: To day will I, O bestower of honour, vent my restrained ire and bad blood upon the hostile hosts, like fire set to a heap of hay.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यैतच्चित्रकूटस्य काननं निशितैः शरैः
भिन्दञ्शत्रुशरीराणि करिष्ये शोणितोक्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
adyaitaccitrakūṭasya kānanaṁ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
bhindañśatruśarīrāṇi kariṣye śoṇitokṣitam

translations.english: To day with sharpened shafts will I cut the bodies of the hostile hosts and drench the woods of Citrakuta with their blood.

verses.sanskrit:
शरैर्निर्भिन्नहृदयान्कुञ्जरांस्तुरगांस्तथा
श्वापदाः परिकर्षन्तु नराश्च निहतान्मया
verses.transliteration:
śarairnirbhinnahṛdayānkuñjarāṁsturagāṁstathā
śvāpadāḥ parikarṣantu narāśca nihatānmayā

translations.english: The ferocious beasts shall drag away elephants and steeds and men slaughtered by me with arrows penetrating into their hearts.

verses.sanskrit:
शराणां धनुषश्चाहमनृणोऽस्मि महावने
ससैन्यं भरतं हत्वा भविष्यामि न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
śarāṇāṁ dhanuṣaścāhamanṛṇo'smi mahāvane
sasainyaṁ bharataṁ hatvā bhaviṣyāmi na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: I will, without doubt, in this forest pay the debt I owe to my bow and arrows, by slaying Bharata together with all his forces.

verses.sanskrit:
सुसंरब्धं तु सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं क्रोधमूर्छितम्
रामस्तु परिसान्त्व्याथ वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
susaṁrabdhaṁ tu saumitriṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ krodhamūrchitam
rāmastu parisāntvyātha vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Pacifying Sumitrā's son, Laksmana, transported with rage and eager for encounter, Rama addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किमत्र धनुषा कार्यमसिना वा सचर्मणा
महेष्वासे महाप्राज्ञे भरते स्वयमागते
verses.transliteration:
kimatra dhanuṣā kāryamasinā vā sacarmaṇā
maheṣvāse mahāprājñe bharate svayamāgate

translations.english: When the mighty Bharata possessed of high spirits has himself come here, what is the use of the bow or the sword or the shield?

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तकालं यदेषोऽस्मान्भरतो द्रष्टुमिच्छति
अस्मासु मनसाप्येष नाहितं किंचिदाचरेत्
verses.transliteration:
prāptakālaṁ yadeṣo'smānbharato draṣṭumicchati
asmāsu manasāpyeṣa nāhitaṁ kiṁcidācaret

translations.english: And the season being fit. meet it is that Bharata should see us. He does not even in thought act against us.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा न किम्
ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं योऽत्र शङ्कसे
verses.transliteration:
vipriyaṁ kṛtapūrvaṁ te bharatena kadā na kim
īdṛśaṁ vā bhayaṁ te'dya bharataṁ yo'tra śaṅkase

translations.english: Has ere this Bharata done you any bad turn? Or did he tell you any thing so alarming that today you stand in fear of him?

verses.sanskrit:
न हि ते निष्ठुरं वाच्यो भरतो नाप्रियं वचः
अहं ह्यप्रियमुक्तः स्यां भरतस्याप्रिये कृते
verses.transliteration:
na hi te niṣṭhuraṁ vācyo bharato nāpriyaṁ vacaḥ
ahaṁ hyapriyamuktaḥ syāṁ bharatasyāpriye kṛte

translations.english: Certainly you ought not to say cruel or unpleasant words in relation to Bharata, if wrong be done to Bharata, I shall consider myself as wornged.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं नु पुत्राः पितरं हन्युः कस्यांचिदापदि
भ्राता वा भ्रातरं हन्यात्सौमित्रे प्राणमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ nu putrāḥ pitaraṁ hanyuḥ kasyāṁcidāpadi
bhrātā vā bhrātaraṁ hanyātsaumitre prāṇamātmanaḥ

translations.english: Do sons, in times of peril, ever slay their father, or brothers their brother like to their life, O son of Sumitrā?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि राज्यस्य हेतोस्त्वमिमां वाचं प्रभाषसे
वक्ष्यामि भरतं दृष्ट्वा राज्यमस्मै प्रदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
yadi rājyasya hetostvamimāṁ vācaṁ prabhāṣase
vakṣyāmi bharataṁ dṛṣṭvā rājyamasmai pradīyatām

translations.english: If you speak thus for the sake of the monarchy, on seeing Bharata, I will say to him, "Make over the kingdom to this one/"

verses.sanskrit:
उच्यमानो हि भरतो मया लक्ष्मण तत्त्वतः
राज्यमस्मै प्रयच्छेति बाढमित्येव वक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ucyamāno hi bharato mayā lakṣmaṇa tattvataḥ
rājyamasmai prayaccheti bāḍhamityeva vakṣyati

translations.english: Earnestly exhorted by me, saying, “Do you place the kingdom in his hands', he will say, "Very well'."

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्तो धर्मशीलेन भ्रात्रा तस्य हिते रतः
लक्ष्मणः प्रविवेशेव स्वानि गात्राणि लज्जया
verses.transliteration:
tathokto dharmaśīlena bhrātrā tasya hite rataḥ
lakṣmaṇaḥ praviveśeva svāni gātrāṇi lajjayā

translations.english: Thus addressed by his brother of a virtuous disposition, Laksmana ever engaged in Rama's good, from shame seemed to enter into his body.

verses.sanskrit:
व्रीडितं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह
एष मन्ये महाबाहुरिहास्मान्द्रष्टुमागतः
verses.transliteration:
vrīḍitaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
eṣa manye mahābāhurihāsmāndraṣṭumāgataḥ

translations.english: And finding Lakşmaņa overcome with shame, Rāghava replied, I think that mighty-armed one has come hither to see us; or I take it for certain that, considering that we are fit for ease only, and taking our banishment to heart, he will take us home.

verses.sanskrit:
वनवासमनुध्याय गृहाय प्रतिनेष्यति
इमां वाप्येश वैदेहीमत्यन्तसुखसेविनीम्
verses.transliteration:
vanavāsamanudhyāya gṛhāya pratineṣyati
imāṁ vāpyeśa vaidehīmatyantasukhasevinīm

translations.english: Or it may be that graceful descendant of Raghu, my father, will go away, taking form the forest Videha's daughter brought up in the lap of luxury.

verses.sanskrit:
एतौ तौ संप्रकाशेते गोत्रवन्तौ मनोरमौ
वायुवेगसमौ वीर जवनौ तुरगोत्तमौ
verses.transliteration:
etau tau saṁprakāśete gotravantau manoramau
vāyuvegasamau vīra javanau turagottamau

translations.english: There are seen these graceful and well-bred steeds, courageous, swift, and furnished with the speed of the wind, the best of horses.

verses.sanskrit:
स एष सुमहाकायः कम्पते वाहिनीमुखे
नागः शत्रुंजयो नाम वृद्धस्तातस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
sa eṣa sumahākāyaḥ kampate vāhinīmukhe
nāgaḥ śatruṁjayo nāma vṛddhastātasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: And this huge elephant belonging to our aged sire, named Satrunjaya, proceeds in the van of the army.

verses.sanskrit:
अवतीर्य तु सालाग्रात्तस्मात्स समितिंजयः
लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः
verses.transliteration:
avatīrya tu sālāgrāttasmātsa samitiṁjayaḥ
lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā tasthau rāmasya pārśvataḥ

translations.english: Do you descend from the top of the tree, O Laksmana. Do my bidding. Thus did the righteous Rāma accosts Sumitra's Descending from the top of the Sāla tree, that conqueror in battles, Lakşmaņa, stood by Rāma with joined hands. son.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतेनाथ संदिष्टा संमर्दो न भवेदिति
समन्तात्तस्य शैलस्य सेनावासमकल्पयत्
verses.transliteration:
bharatenātha saṁdiṣṭā saṁmardo na bhavediti
samantāttasya śailasya senāvāsamakalpayat

translations.english: Commanded by Bharata, Let not (Rāma's asylum) by trampled by the forces, the army took up its quarters at a distance from the hill.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्यर्धमिक्ष्वाकुचमूर्योजनं पर्वतस्य सा
पार्श्वे न्यविशदावृत्य गजवाजिरथाकुला
verses.transliteration:
adhyardhamikṣvākucamūryojanaṁ parvatasya sā
pārśve nyaviśadāvṛtya gajavājirathākulā

translations.english: And the Ikşvāku host filled with elephants and steeds covering half a Yojana, encamped at the side of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
सा चित्रकूटे भरतेन सेना; धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य विधूय दर्पम्
प्रसादनार्थं रघुनन्दनस्य; विरोचते नीतिमता प्रणीता
verses.transliteration:
sā citrakūṭe bharatena senā; dharmaṁ puraskṛtya vidhūya darpam
prasādanārthaṁ raghunandanasya; virocate nītimatā praṇītā

translations.english: And keeping morality in their fore-front, and renouncing pride, the disciplined forces schooled by Bharata in view of pleasing that descendant of Raghu (Rāma), stayed in Citrakuța.

verses.sanskrit:
निविष्ट मात्रे सैन्ये तु यथोद्देशं विनीतवत्
भरतो भ्रातरं वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
niviṣṭa mātre sainye tu yathoddeśaṁ vinītavat
bharato bhrātaraṁ vākyaṁ śatrughnamidamabravīt

translations.english: Having stationed his troops, that best of men, the master, became anxious to go on foot to the Käkutstha honouring his superiors. And the forces having with humility took up the quarters assigned, Bharata addressed his brother, Satrughna, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं वनमिदं सौम्य नरसंघैः समन्ततः
लुब्धैश्च सहितैरेभिस्त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṁ vanamidaṁ saumya narasaṁghaiḥ samantataḥ
lubdhaiśca sahitairebhistvamanveṣitumarhasi

translations.english: O mild one, it behoves you at once to search this forest all round in company with a large body of men as well as these Nişadas.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्न रामं द्रक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मणं वा महाबलम्
वैदेहीं वा महाभागां न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvanna rāmaṁ drakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṁ vā mahābalam
vaidehīṁ vā mahābhāgāṁ na me śāntirbhaviṣyati

translations.english: So long as I do not see Răma, or the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, or the highly exalted daughter of Videha, I shall not attain peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्न चन्द्रसंकाशं द्रक्ष्यामि शुभमाननम्
भ्रातुः पद्मपलाशाक्षं न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvanna candrasaṁkāśaṁ drakṣyāmi śubhamānanam
bhrātuḥ padmapalāśākṣaṁ na me śāntirbhaviṣyati

translations.english: And so long as I do not see that face of his fair as the moon, with eyes expansive like lotuses, I shall not attain peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्न चरणौ भ्रातुः पार्थिव व्यञ्जनान्वितौ
शिरसा धारयिष्यामि न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvanna caraṇau bhrātuḥ pārthiva vyañjanānvitau
śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi na me śāntirbhaviṣyati

translations.english: So long as I do not take on my head those feet of my brother bearing royal marks, I shall not attain peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्न राज्ये राज्यार्हः पितृपैतामहे स्थितः
अभिषेकजलक्लिन्नो न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvanna rājye rājyārhaḥ pitṛpaitāmahe sthitaḥ
abhiṣekajalaklinno na me śāntirbhaviṣyati

translations.english: So long as established in the kingdom of his father and grandfather, that one worthy of the monarchy is not sprinkled with the water on installation, I shall not attain peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतकृत्या महाभागा वैदेही जनकात्मजा
भर्तारं सागरान्तायाः पृथिव्या यानुगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
kṛtakṛtyā mahābhāgā vaidehī janakātmajā
bhartāraṁ sāgarāntāyāḥ pṛthivyā yānugacchati

translations.english: Blessed is Vaidehī, the eminently virtuous daughter of Janaka, who follows the lord of this Earth bounded by the seas.

verses.sanskrit:
सुभगश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ गिरिराजोपमो गिरिः
यस्मिन्वसति काकुत्स्थः कुबेर इवनन्दने
verses.transliteration:
subhagaścitrakūṭo'sau girirājopamo giriḥ
yasminvasati kākutsthaḥ kubera ivanandane

translations.english: This Citrakuța is fortunate, this hill like to the monarch of mountains, in which resides Kākutstha, like Kuvera in Nandana.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतकार्यमिदं दुर्गं वनं व्यालनिषेवितम्
यदध्यास्ते महातेजा रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtakāryamidaṁ durgaṁ vanaṁ vyālaniṣevitam
yadadhyāste mahātejā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: And blessed is this deep forest inhabited by ferocious animals, where abide the great king Rāma, the foremost of those bearing arms.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा भरतः पुरुषर्षभः
पद्भ्यामेव महातेजाः प्रविवेश महद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahātejā bharataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
padbhyāmeva mahātejāḥ praviveśa mahadvanam

translations.english: Having said this, that best of men, the mightyarmed and highly energetic Bharata, on foot entered the vast forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स तानि द्रुमजालानि जातानि गिरिसानुषु
पुष्पिताग्राणि मध्येन जगाम वदतां वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāni drumajālāni jātāni girisānuṣu
puṣpitāgrāṇi madhyena jagāma vadatāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: And that best of speakers went over the mountain-side through ranks of blossoming trees.

verses.sanskrit:
स गिरेश्चित्रकूटस्य सालमासाद्य पुष्पितम्
रामाश्रमगतस्याग्नेर्ददर्श ध्वजमुच्छ्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa gireścitrakūṭasya sālamāsādya puṣpitam
rāmāśramagatasyāgnerdadarśa dhvajamucchritam

translations.english: Then swiftly ascending a Sāla on Citrakuta, he descried the high column of smoke belonging to Răma's asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरतः श्रीमान्मुमोद सहबान्धवः
अत्र राम इति ज्ञात्वा गतः पारमिवाम्भसः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmānmumoda sahabāndhavaḥ
atra rāma iti jñātvā gataḥ pāramivāmbhasaḥ

translations.english: Having seen this, like one that has crossed over the ocean, the graceful Bharata, concluding that Rāma was there, rejoiced exceedingly along with his friends.

verses.sanskrit:
स चित्रकूटे तु गिरौ निशाम्य; रामाश्रमं पुण्यजनोपपन्नम्
गुहेन सार्धं त्वरितो जगाम; पुनर्निवेश्यैव चमूं महात्मा
verses.transliteration:
sa citrakūṭe tu girau niśāmya; rāmāśramaṁ puṇyajanopapannam
guhena sārdhaṁ tvarito jagāma; punarniveśyaiva camūṁ mahātmā

translations.english: Having heard that Rama's asylum containing pious people lay in Citrakuta, that high-souled one again stationing his forces, speedily went (in that direction), accompanied by Guha.

verses.sanskrit:
निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा
जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुघ्नमनुदर्शयन्
verses.transliteration:
niviṣṭāyāṁ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastadā
jagāma bhrātaraṁ draṣṭuṁ śatrughnamanudarśayan

translations.english: Having quartered his forces, Bharata eager (to go to Rāma's place), went to see his brother, showing to Satrughna the signs of Rāma's abode being in the vicinity.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिं वसिष्ठं संदिश्य मातॄर्मे शीघ्रमानय
इति तरितमग्रे स जागम गुरुवत्सलः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣiṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ saṁdiśya mātṝrme śīghramānaya
iti taritamagre sa jāgama guruvatsalaḥ

translations.english: And having desired Vasistha, saying, “Bring my mothers without delay," that one attached to his superiors went before.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शतुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत
रामदार्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च
verses.transliteration:
sumantrastvapi śatughnamadūrādanvapadyata
rāmadārśanajastarṣo bharatasyeva tasya ca

translations.english: And eager to see Rāma even like Bharata himself, Sumantra followed Bharata at a short distance.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालयसंस्थिताम्
भ्रातुः पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālayasaṁsthitām
bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭīṁ śrīmānuṭajaṁ ca dadarśa ha

translations.english: As Bharata passed on, he observed a neat cottage of leaves stationed among the asylums of anchorets, furnished with a portion having a wall with a door.

verses.sanskrit:
शालायास्त्वग्रतस्तस्या ददर्श भरतस्तदा
काष्टानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्यवचितानि च
verses.transliteration:
śālāyāstvagratastasyā dadarśa bharatastadā
kāṣṭāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyavacitāni ca

translations.english: Before the cottage, Bharata saw fuel broken up, and flowers gathered. And he saw at places signs of Kuśa and bark set up on trees when Rāma and Lakşmaņa (first) arrived at their asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
ददर्श च वने तस्मिन्महतः संचयान्कृतान्
मृगाणां महिषाणां च करीषैः शीतकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
dadarśa ca vane tasminmahataḥ saṁcayānkṛtān
mṛgāṇāṁ mahiṣāṇāṁ ca karīṣaiḥ śītakāraṇāt

translations.english: And in that habitation, Bharata saw great heaps of dry dung of deer and buffaloes, gathered for preventing cold.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छनेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान्भरतस्तदा
शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
gacchaneva mahābāhurdyutimānbharatastadā
śatrughnaṁ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṁśca sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: As he proceeded, the intelligent and mightyarmed Bharata with a cheerful heart remarked to Śatrughna and all the courtiers.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्
नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमितः
verses.transliteration:
manye prāptāḥ sma taṁ deśaṁ bharadvājo yamabravīt
nātidūre hi manye'haṁ nadīṁ mandākinīmitaḥ

translations.english: I conceive, we have reached the tract that was mentioned by Bharadvāja. Hard by this spot, I fancy, is the river Mandākini.

verses.sanskrit:
उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्
अभिज्ञानकृतः पन्था विकाले गन्तुमिच्छता
verses.transliteration:
uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam
abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantumicchatā

translations.english: On high are barks set up by Lakşmaņa. Having to pass by the way at unusual hours, (Laksmana) has marked it with signs.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्
शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ codāttadantānāṁ kuñjarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām

translations.english: On the side of the hill is the way by which long-tusked elephants pass to and fro with vehemence, roaring at each other.

verses.sanskrit:
यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसाः सततं वने
तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूमः संकुलः कृष्टवर्त्मनः
verses.transliteration:
yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasāḥ satataṁ vane
tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ saṁkulaḥ kṛṣṭavartmanaḥ

translations.english: Here is seen the dense and dark smoke of that which the anchorets are ever anxious to preserve in the forest, fire.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्
आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टो महर्षिमिव राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
atrāhaṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ gurusatkārakāriṇam
āryaṁ drakṣyāmi saṁhṛṣṭo maharṣimiva rāghavam

translations.english: Even here shall I with a delighted heart see that foremost of men, the noble Rāghava resembling a Maharși, ever engaged in serving his superiors.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तं तु चित्रकूटं स राघवः
मन्दाकिनीमनुप्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha gatvā muhūrtaṁ tu citrakūṭaṁ sa rāghavaḥ
mandākinīmanuprāptastaṁ janaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Then going to Citrakuta, that descendant of Raghu, coming to the Mandakini, said to the men.

verses.sanskrit:
जगत्यां पुरुषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रतः
जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिन्मे जन्म सजीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
jagatyāṁ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ
janendro nirjanaṁ prāpya dhinme janma sajīvitam

translations.english: That foremost of men in all the world, the lord of all, coming into seclusion, is in his yoga posture. O fie upon my birth and my life!

verses.sanskrit:
मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युतिः
सरान्कामान्परित्यज्य वने वसति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
matkṛte vyasanaṁ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ
sarānkāmānparityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: For me, having come by misfortune, and renounced every comfort, the effulgent lord of men, Rāghava, is dwelling in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
इति लोकसमाक्रुष्टः पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्
रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीतायाश्च पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
iti lokasamākruṣṭaḥ pādeṣvadya prasādayan
rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyāśca punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: I shall be taxed of men on the score. To-day (first) pacifying him, I will fall at the feet of Rāma as well as of Sitã and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स विलपंस्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः
ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa vilapaṁstasminvane daśarathātmajaḥ
dadarśa mahatīṁ puṇyāṁ parṇaśālāṁ manoramām

translations.english: Having thus bewailed, Dasaratha's son saw a splendid, charming, and holy dwelling in that forest, composed of leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरतः श्रीमान्दुःखमोहपरिप्लुतः
अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरतः कैकयीसुतः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmānduḥkhamohapariplutaḥ
abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ

translations.english: And seeing him, overwhelmed with grief and affliction, the righteous and graceful son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, rushed (towards him).

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा च विललापार्तो बाष्पसंदिग्धया गिरा
अशक्नुवन्धारयितुं धैर्याद्वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā ca vilalāpārto bāṣpasaṁdigdhayā girā
aśaknuvandhārayituṁ dhairyādvacanamabravīt

translations.english: And soon as Bharata saw Rāma, he, exceedingly distressed, broke out into lamentations in words choked with sorrow. And incapable of holding himself in patience, he said.

verses.sanskrit:
यः संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद्युक्त उपासितुम्
वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीनः सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रजः
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ saṁsadi prakṛtibhirbhavedyukta upāsitum
vanyairmṛgairupāsīnaḥ so'yamāste mamāgrajaḥ

translations.english: That elder brother of mine, who (seated) in court should be surrounded by the subjects intent upon paying him homage, is now surrounded by wild deer.

verses.sanskrit:
वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचितः
मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन्
verses.transliteration:
vāsobhirbahusāhasrairyo mahātmā purocitaḥ
mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran

translations.english: He that used to adorn his person with attire worth many thousands (of things), engaged in observing morality, is clad in deer-skin.

verses.sanskrit:
अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्राः सुमनसस्तदा
सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं सहते राघवः कथम्
verses.transliteration:
adhārayadyo vividhāścitrāḥ sumanasastadā
so'yaṁ jaṭābhāramimaṁ sahate rāghavaḥ katham

translations.english: Why does he that always wore variegated blossoms, Rāghava, bears this burthen of matted locks?

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य यज्ञैर्यथादिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य संचयः
शरीर क्लेशसंभूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते
verses.transliteration:
yasya yajñairyathādiṣṭairyukto dharmasya saṁcayaḥ
śarīra kleśasaṁbhūtaṁ sa dharmaṁ parimārgate

translations.english: He who is worthy of acquiring religious merit by celebrating sacrifices according to the ordinance, is now following morality by afflicting his person.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्
मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते
verses.transliteration:
candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam
malena tasyāṅgamidaṁ kathamāryasya sevyate

translations.english: How is the person of that one whose body used to be daubed with costly sandal, covered with dust.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्निमित्तमिदं दुःखं प्राप्तो रामः सुखोचितः
धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
mannimittamidaṁ duḥkhaṁ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ
dhigjīvitaṁ nṛśaṁsasya mama lokavigarhitam

translations.english: It is for me that Rama, although deserving of comfort, has come by this misfortune. Wicked that I am, fie upon my life despised of men!

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं विलपन्दीनः प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कजः
पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ vilapandīnaḥ prasvinnamukhapaṅkajaḥ
pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan

translations.english: Thus lamenting in woeful guise, with the lotus of his countenance covered with sweat, Bharata coming at Rāma's feet, fell at them bewailing.

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबलः
उक्त्वार्येति सकृद्दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किंचन
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābalaḥ
uktvāryeti sakṛddīnaṁ punarnovāca kiṁcana

translations.english: And inflamed with grief, the exceedingly powerful prince Bharata, having in distress of spirit uttered, O noble one, again said nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पापिहित कण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्
आर्येत्येवाभिसंक्रुश्य व्याहर्तुं नाशकत्ततः
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpāpihita kaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṁ yaśasvinam
āryetyevābhisaṁkruśya vyāhartuṁ nāśakattataḥ

translations.english: And beholding the illustrious Rāma, Bharata with his utterance choked with emotion, exclaimed, O noble one, and was unable to say anything further.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव; समीयतू राजसुतावरण्ये
दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च; यथाम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva; samīyatū rājasutāvaraṇye
divākaraścaiva niśākaraśca; yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām

translations.english: Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्पार्थिवान्वारणयूथपाभा;न्समागतांस्तत्र महत्यरण्ये
वनौकसस्तेऽपि समीक्ष्य सर्वे;ऽप्यश्रूण्यमुञ्चन्प्रविहाय हर्षम्
verses.transliteration:
tānpārthivānvāraṇayūthapābhā;nsamāgatāṁstatra mahatyaraṇye
vanaukasaste'pi samīkṣya sarve;'pyaśrūṇyamuñcanpravihāya harṣam

translations.english: And beholding those kings resembling leaders of elephant-herds met together in that mighty forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears. forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व नु तेऽभूत्पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागतः
न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
kva nu te'bhūtpitā tāta yadaraṇyaṁ tvamāgataḥ
na hi tvaṁ jīvatastasya vanamāgantumarhasi

translations.english: Where was your father, child, that you have come to the forest? It certainly behoves you not to come to the forest while he is living.

verses.sanskrit:
चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम्
दुष्प्रतीकमरण्येऽस्मिन्किं तात वनमागतः
verses.transliteration:
cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrādbharatamāgatam
duṣpratīkamaraṇye'sminkiṁ tāta vanamāgataḥ

translations.english: Ah! I see you come from far after a long time. Why, my child, have you come to this gloomy forest?

verses.sanskrit:
