कच्चिद्दशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसंगरः
राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्ता धर्मनिश्चयः
verses.transliteration:
kacciddaśaratho rājā kuśalī satyasaṁgaraḥ
rājasūyāśvamedhānāmāhartā dharmaniścayaḥ

translations.english: Is that truthful one, that performer of Rajasüya and Aśvamedha, ever devoted to righteousness, king Dasaratha, well?

verses.sanskrit:
स कच्चिद्ब्राह्मणो विद्वान्धर्मनित्यो महाद्युतिः
इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते
verses.transliteration:
sa kaccidbrāhmaṇo vidvāndharmanityo mahādyutiḥ
ikṣvākūṇāmupādhyāyo yathāvattāta pūjyate

translations.english: My child, is that exceedingly effulgent and learned Brāhmaṇa ever steady in morality, the priest of the Iksvākus, duly honoured?

verses.sanskrit:
तात कच्चिच्च कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती
सुखिनी कच्चिदार्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी
verses.transliteration:
tāta kaccicca kausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī
sukhinī kaccidāryā ca devī nandati kaikayī

translations.english: And, my child, are Kausalyā, and Sumitrā having a son, in happiness? And is the noble Kaikeyi in spirits?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिद्विनय संपन्नः कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुतः
अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहितः
verses.transliteration:
kaccidvinaya saṁpannaḥ kulaputro bahuśrutaḥ
anasūyuranudraṣṭā satkṛtaste purohitaḥ

translations.english: And is that one, sprung from a mighty line, humble and versed in various lore, your priest, who performs every ceremony, who bears no ill will, and whose gaze is ever fixed upon our welfare, honoured?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजुः
हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा
verses.transliteration:
kaccidagniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimānṛjuḥ
hutaṁ ca hoṣyamāṇaṁ ca kāle vedayate sadā

translations.english: Do intelligent and sincere people cognizant of the rules, look after the sacrificial fire? And do they regularly inform you of the proper seasons for performing the fire-sacrifice?

verses.sanskrit:
इष्वस्त्रवरसंपन्नमर्थशास्त्रविशारदम्
सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
iṣvastravarasaṁpannamarthaśāstraviśāradam
sudhanvānamupādhyāyaṁ kaccittvaṁ tāta manyase

translations.english: And do not disregard the preceptor Sudhanvā versed in excellent arms whether inspired with mantras or not, and accomplished in the knowledge of polity?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदात्म समाः शूराः श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः
कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
kaccidātma samāḥ śūrāḥ śrutavanto jitendriyāḥ
kulīnāśceṅgitajñāśca kṛtāste tāta mantriṇaḥ

translations.english: And, my child, have you employed as your controlled, well-born, and understanding signs, who are like your own self?

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव
सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यैः शास्त्रकोविदैः
verses.transliteration:
mantro vijayamūlaṁ hi rājñāṁ bhavati rāghava
susaṁvṛto mantradharairamātyaiḥ śāstrakovidaiḥ

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, counsel well kept by clever councillors versed in lore, is the root of victory with kings.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषि कच्चित्काले विबुध्यसे
कच्चिंश्चापररात्रिषु चिन्तयस्यर्थनैपुणम्
verses.transliteration:
kaccinnidrāvaśaṁ naiṣi kaccitkāle vibudhyase
kacciṁścāpararātriṣu cintayasyarthanaipuṇam

translations.english: You have not come under the sway of sleep? and you awake at the proper hour? And do you during the short hours revolve the means of acquiring wealth?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह
कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति
verses.transliteration:
kaccinmantrayase naikaḥ kaccinna bahubhiḥ saha
kaccitte mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṁ na paridhāvati

translations.english: And you did not take counsel either with yourself alone, or (on the other hand) with a multiplicity of counsellors? and your counsel does not range the kingdom (i.e. does not take air)?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम्
क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव
verses.transliteration:
kaccidarthaṁ viniścitya laghumūlaṁ mahodayam
kṣipramārabhase kartuṁ na dīrghayasi rāghava

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, having determined upon a course costing small effort but fraught with a mighty result, you set about it sharply and delay not?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्तु सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुनः
विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्तव्यानि पार्थिवाः
verses.transliteration:
kaccittu sukṛtānyeva kṛtarūpāṇi vā punaḥ
viduste sarvakāryāṇi na kartavyāni pārthivāḥ

translations.english: Do the (auxiliary) kings know only those acts of yours that have been accomplished or those that are well nigh so, and not those that you intend to set yours hand to?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्न तर्कैर्युक्त्वा वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिताः
त्वया वा तव वामात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
kaccinna tarkairyuktvā vā ye cāpyaparikīrtitāḥ
tvayā vā tava vāmātyairbudhyate tāta mantritam

translations.english: Do others through inference or appearances come at a knowledge of your counsels, although undivulged to others by yourself or your counsellors; and (do you and your ministers) attain to a knowledge of others' counsels?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्सहस्रान्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्
पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्यान्निःश्रेयसं महत्
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsahasrānmūrkhāṇāmekamicchasi paṇḍitam
paṇḍito hyarthakṛcchreṣu kuryānniḥśreyasaṁ mahat

translations.english: And passing by a thousand dunces, do you set your heart on having a single wise man? In times of pecuniary stress, a wise man stands in excellent stead.

verses.sanskrit:
सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां यद्युपास्ते महीपतिः
अथ वाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता
verses.transliteration:
sahasrāṇyapi mūrkhāṇāṁ yadyupāste mahīpatiḥ
atha vāpyayutānyeva nāsti teṣu sahāyatā

translations.english: And although a king might be surrounded by a thousand or ten thousand fools, yet he can count upon no assistance (at their hands).

verses.sanskrit:
एकोऽप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षणः
राजानं राजमात्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
eko'pyamātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇaḥ
rājānaṁ rājamātraṁ vā prāpayenmahatīṁ śriyam

translations.english: And a single able counsellor, intelligent, heroic, and sagacious, bring great prosperity upon a king or a prince.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्मुख्या महत्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमाः
जघन्याश्च जघन्येषु भृत्याः कर्मसु योजिताः
verses.transliteration:
kaccinmukhyā mahatsveva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ
jaghanyāśca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ

translations.english: And, my child, do you employ the best servants upon the best offices, the middling upon middling, and the worst upon the worst?

verses.sanskrit:
अमात्यानुपधातीतान्पितृपैतामहाञ्शुचीन्
श्रेष्ठाञ्श्रेष्ठेषु कच्चित्त्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु
verses.transliteration:
amātyānupadhātītānpitṛpaitāmahāñśucīn
śreṣṭhāñśreṣṭheṣu kaccittvaṁ niyojayasi karmasu

translations.english: And did you employ upon the most worthy offices counsellors who are above bribery, who have served your father and grand-father, and who are pure?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजकाः पतितं यथा
उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
kaccittvāṁ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitaṁ yathā
ugrapratigrahītāraṁ kāmayānamiva striyaḥ

translations.english: Do the priests scorn you like a fallen one, even as females do those lascivious folks who use force towards the former?

verses.sanskrit:
उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसंदूषणे रतम्
शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स वध्यते
verses.transliteration:
upāyakuśalaṁ vaidyaṁ bhṛtyasaṁdūṣaṇe ratam
śūramaiśvaryakāmaṁ ca yo na hanti sa vadhyate

translations.english: He that does not slay a physician skilled in ways and means, a servant given to enlisting the sympathies of his fellow-servants against his master, or a hero that covets riches, is slain (by them).

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च धृतिमान्मतिमाञ्शुचिः
कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्षः सेनापतिः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
kacciddhṛṣṭaśca śūraśca dhṛtimānmatimāñśuciḥ
kulīnaścānuraktaśca dakṣaḥ senāpatiḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: And had you chosen for your general one that is confident, is endowed with intelligence and fortitude, sprung in a respectable race, and attached and able?

verses.sanskrit:
बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युद्धविशारदाः
दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्य मानिताः
verses.transliteration:
balavantaśca kaccitte mukhyā yuddhaviśāradāḥ
dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntāstvayā satkṛtya mānitāḥ

translations.english: And do you practically honour your foremost warriors possessed of prowess, who have already given evidence of their manliness?

verses.sanskrit:
कचिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्
संप्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे
verses.transliteration:
kacidbalasya bhaktaṁ ca vetanaṁ ca yathocitam
saṁprāptakālaṁ dātavyaṁ dadāsi na vilambase

translations.english: And do you at the proper time grant your soldiers what you should, provision and pay; and do not delay in doing this?

verses.sanskrit:
कालातिक्रमणे ह्येव भक्त वेतनयोर्भृताः
भर्तुः कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सोऽनर्थः सुमहान्स्मृतः
verses.transliteration:
kālātikramaṇe hyeva bhakta vetanayorbhṛtāḥ
bhartuḥ kupyanti duṣyanti so'narthaḥ sumahānsmṛtaḥ

translations.english: If the proper time for granting provision and pay be passed, the servants get wroth with their master and tax him; and great is the evil that springs herefrom.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्सर्वेऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्राः प्रधानतः
कच्चित्प्राणांस्तवार्थेषु संत्यजन्ति समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsarve'nuraktāstvāṁ kulaputrāḥ pradhānataḥ
kaccitprāṇāṁstavārtheṣu saṁtyajanti samāhitāḥ

translations.english: And are the principal descendants of our race attached to you; and are they, when enlisted on your side with concentrated minds, ready to lay down their lives?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान्दक्षिणः प्रतिभानवान्
यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डितः
verses.transliteration:
kaccijjānapado vidvāndakṣiṇaḥ pratibhānavān
yathoktavādī dūtaste kṛto bharata paṇḍitaḥ

translations.english: O Bharata, are your spies persons coming from the provinces, and learned, upright, endowed with presence of mind, representing the truth, and possessed of wisdon?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च
त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकैः
verses.transliteration:
kaccidaṣṭādaśānyeṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca
tribhistribhiravijñātairvetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ

translations.english: And do you acquire intelligence of the expedients, eighteen* in respect of others, and fifteen in respect of the own self, by means of every three spies appointed in connection with each of these expedients, men quite ignorant of each other's counsels? *1. Minister. 2. Priest. 3. Heir-apparent. 4. General. 5. Warder. 6. Gatekeeper of the inner-apartment. 7. Jailer. 8. Treasurer. 9. Conveyer of the royal orders. 10. Pleaders. 11. Judges. 12. Members of the council. 13. Distributor of pay and provision to the army. 14. Journeymen. 15. Justice of the peace. 16. Protector of the frontiers of the kingdom. 17. Magistrate. 18. Guards of rivers, hills, and fortresses.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान्प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा
दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्तसे रिपुसूदन
verses.transliteration:
kaccidvyapāstānahitānpratiyātāṁśca sarvadā
durbalānanavajñāya vartase ripusūdana

translations.english: And do you not contemn those. weak ones that, O destroyer of your. foes, having been expelled, have come again (to you)?

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः
बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते
verses.transliteration:
dharmaśāstreṣu mukhyeṣu vidyamāneṣu durbudhāḥ
buddhimānvīkṣikīṁ prāpya nirarthaṁ pravadanti te

translations.english: And, my child, you did not minister to atheistical Brāhmaṇas? These childish persons proud of their learning are only fit for bringing evils upon others. While there are excellent scriptures, these people of subtle intellects, having acquired a knowledge of dialectics, speak vanities.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः स्वकर्मनिरतैः सदा
जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामात्यैः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ svakarmanirataiḥ sadā
jitendriyairmahotsāhairvṛtāmātyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: My child, do you protect the prosperous and renowned Ayodhyā, inhabited formerly by our heroic predecessors; bearing a true name; having strong gates; filled with elephants, steeds, and cars; thronged by thousands; with noble Brāhmaṇas, Kștriyas and Vaisyas breathing high spirits, and with their senses controlled, each engaged in his own task; abounding in people learned in the Veda; and surrounded with palatial mansions of various shapes?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्ते दयिताः सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः
वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते
verses.transliteration:
kaccitte dayitāḥ sarve kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ
vārtāyāṁ saṁśritastāta loko hi sukhamedhate

translations.english: And do agriculturists and cow herds find favour in your sight? And remaining in their respective vocations, do they enjoy happiness?

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम्
रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ guptiparīhāraiḥ kaccitte bharaṇaṁ kṛtam
rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ

translations.english: And do you maintain them by securing to them what they wish for and removing from them what they wish away? All the dwellers in his dominions should be protected by the king.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्स्त्रियः सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिताः
कच्चिन्न श्रद्दधास्यासां कच्चिद्गुह्यं न भाषसे
verses.transliteration:
kaccitstriyaḥ sāntvayasi kaccittāśca surakṣitāḥ
kaccinna śraddadhāsyāsāṁ kaccidguhyaṁ na bhāṣase

translations.english: And do you conciliate the females; and are they well protected by you? And do you not regard them; and do you not open to them your mind?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि
कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम्
उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्रो महापथे
verses.transliteration:
kaccinnāgavanaṁ guptaṁ kuñjarāṇāṁ ca tṛpyasi
kacciddarśayase nityaṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ vibhūṣitam
utthāyotthāya pūrvāhṇe rājaputro mahāpathe

translations.english: And do you show yourself daily in the court, well robed? And rising in the morning, do you show yourself in the high-ways?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः
यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsarvāṇi durgāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakaiḥ
yantraiśca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurdharaiḥ

translations.english: Are all the forts furnished with wealth, corn, arms water, machines, artisans, and bowmen?

verses.sanskrit:
आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित्कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः
अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव
verses.transliteration:
āyaste vipulaḥ kaccitkaccidalpataro vyayaḥ
apātreṣu na te kaccitkośo gacchati rāghava

translations.english: And are your incomings great and outgoings slender? And, O Raghu's descendant, you do not give away your coffers to the undeserving?

verses.sanskrit:
देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थे ब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च
योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्ययः
verses.transliteration:
devatārthe ca pitrarthe brāhmaṇābhyāgateṣu ca
yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccidgacchati te vyayaḥ

translations.english: And did you spend your wealth in the interests of the deities, or the pitris, or the Brāhmaṇas who have come to you, or warriors, or friends?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदार्यो विशुद्धात्मा क्षारितश्चोरकर्मणा
अपृष्टः शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्बध्यते शुचिः
verses.transliteration:
kaccidāryo viśuddhātmā kṣāritaścorakarmaṇā
apṛṣṭaḥ śāstrakuśalairna lobhādbadhyate śuciḥ

translations.english: If any respectable, pure-spirited and clean person happen to be accused by some one of theft or other crimes, do you from covetousness punish him without first having him tried by persons versed in scripture?

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टः सकारणः
कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītaścaiva pṛṣṭaśca kāle dṛṣṭaḥ sakāraṇaḥ
kaccinna mucyate coro dhanalobhānnararṣabha

translations.english: And, O best of men, is a thief, that has been caught, interrogated (as to his guilt), and found with the stolen property on his person, set free (by your men) from motives of gain.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुगतस्य च राघव
अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः
verses.transliteration:
vyasane kaccidāḍhyasya dugatasya ca rāghava
arthaṁ virāgāḥ paśyanti tavāmātyā bahuśrutāḥ

translations.english: And do your counsellors, o descendant of Raghu, accomplished in various lore, uninfluenced by greed, consider the conduct of both the rich and the poor involved in peril?

verses.sanskrit:
यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यस्राणि राघव
तानि पुत्रपशून्घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः
verses.transliteration:
yāni mithyābhiśastānāṁ patantyasrāṇi rāghava
tāni putrapaśūnghnanti prītyarthamanuśāsataḥ

translations.english: O son of the Raghu race, the tears of those who have been falsely charged with any offence, (and who have failed to obtain justice), dropping, destroy the sons as well as the beasts of the ruler that minds his own comfort only.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिद्वृधांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यमुख्यांश्च राघव
दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे
verses.transliteration:
kaccidvṛdhāṁśca bālāṁśca vaidyamukhyāṁśca rāghava
dānena manasā vācā tribhiretairbubhūṣase

translations.english: And do you with these three, gifts, mind and word, try to win over aged people, boys, physicians, and the principal ones?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान्देवतातिथीन्
चैत्यांश्च सर्वान्सिद्धार्थान्ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि
verses.transliteration:
kaccidgurūṁśca vṛddhāṁśca tāpasāndevatātithīn
caityāṁśca sarvānsiddhārthānbrāhmaṇāṁśca namasyasi

translations.english: And do you salute spiritual preceptors, aged persons, ascetics, gods, guests, Caityas, emancipated one, and Brāhmaṇās?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्मं धर्मं धर्मेण वा पुनः
उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन न विबाधसे
verses.transliteration:
kaccidarthena vā dharmaṁ dharmaṁ dharmeṇa vā punaḥ
ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena na vibādhase

translations.english: And you do not oppose righteousness by interest, or interest by virtue, or both by desire, intent on gratifying the senses?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर
विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान्भरत सेवसे
verses.transliteration:
kaccidarthaṁ ca dharmaṁ ca kāmaṁ ca jayatāṁ vara
vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvānbharata sevase

translations.english: And, O foremost of conquerors, do you, O you cognisant of time, in season resorting to interest, desire, and virtue respectively, attain them, O bestower of boons?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणाः शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदः
आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदैः सह
verses.transliteration:
kaccitte brāhmaṇāḥ śarma sarvaśāstrārthakovidaḥ
āśaṁsante mahāprājña paurajānapadaiḥ saha

translations.english: And do Brāhmaṇas versed in all religious lore and knowing interest, together with the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces wish for your happiness, O highly wise one?

verses.sanskrit:
नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्
अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्
verses.transliteration:
nāstikyamanṛtaṁ krodhaṁ pramādaṁ dīrghasūtratām
adarśanaṁ jñānavatāmālasyaṁ pañcavṛttitām

translations.english: Atheism, untruthfulness, inattention, anger, procrastination, companionship with evil persons, indolence, gratification of the senses, consultation with a single person concerning the needs of a kingdom, taking counsel with those that are cognisant of evils alone, omission to take in hand a task that has been decided upon, divulgence of counsel, non-commencement of a course in the morning, and marching against all the foes at one and the same time, have you eschewed these ten and four faults?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्स्वादुकृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव
कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्यः संप्रयच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
kaccitsvādukṛtaṁ bhojyameko nāśnāsi rāghava
kaccidāśaṁsamānebhyo mitrebhyaḥ saṁprayacchasi

translations.english: And, O son of Raghu, you do not alone partake of sapid meats yourself alone? And do you share them with those friends who expect it?

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह
किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
kiṁ me dharmādvihīnasya rājadharmaḥ kariṣyati

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words, Bharata answered, Deprived of the kingdom in consequence of my posteriority in point of birth, what does regard for morality avail me?

verses.sanskrit:
शाश्वतोऽयं सदा धर्मः स्थितोऽस्मासु नरर्षभ
ज्येष्ठ पुत्रे स्थिते राजन्न कनीयान्भवेन्नृपः
verses.transliteration:
śāśvato'yaṁ sadā dharmaḥ sthito'smāsu nararṣabha
jyeṣṭha putre sthite rājanna kanīyānbhavennṛpaḥ

translations.english: O best of men, even this morality has ever been established with reference to us, viz., that the eldest son of the king existing, a younger one cannot be the king.

verses.sanskrit:
स समृद्धां मया सार्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव
अभिषेचय चात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय नः
verses.transliteration:
sa samṛddhāṁ mayā sārdhamayodhyāṁ gaccha rāghava
abhiṣecaya cātmānaṁ kulasyāsya bhavāya naḥ

translations.english: Do you, therefore, O Rāghava go along with me to the prosperous Ayodhya; and get yourself ir stalled there for the behoof of our race.

verses.sanskrit:
राजानं मानुषं प्राहुर्देवत्वे संमतो मम
यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम्
verses.transliteration:
rājānaṁ mānuṣaṁ prāhurdevatve saṁmato mama
yasya dharmārthasahitaṁ vṛttamāhuramānuṣam

translations.english: Although a king observing interest and virtue, and who towers above average humanity, has been called a mortal, yet to me he is a very deity.

verses.sanskrit:
केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्यमाश्रिते
दिवमार्य गतो राजा यायजूकः सतां मतः
verses.transliteration:
kekayasthe ca mayi tu tvayi cāraṇyamāśrite
divamārya gato rājā yāyajūkaḥ satāṁ mataḥ

translations.english: While I was in Kekaya and you was in the forest that intelligent monarch honoured of the good, given to celebrating sacrifices, ascended heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितुः
अहं चायं च शत्रुघ्नः पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ
verses.transliteration:
uttiṣṭha puruṣavyāghra kriyatāmudakaṁ pituḥ
ahaṁ cāyaṁ ca śatrughnaḥ pūrvameva kṛtodakau

translations.english: O foremost of men, do you arise, and offer water to the spirit of our sire. Śatrughna and I have ere this offered water to (the departed).

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियेण किल दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव
अक्षय्यं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितुः प्रियः
verses.transliteration:
priyeṇa kila dattaṁ hi pitṛlokeṣu rāghava
akṣayyaṁ bhavatītyāhurbhavāṁścaiva pituḥ priyaḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, anything offered to the (manes of the) ancestors by a beloved descendant, conduces to their eternal behoof; and you the favourite of our father.

verses.sanskrit:
तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्
राघवो भरतेनोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ śrutvā karuṇāṁ vācaṁ piturmaraṇasaṁhitām
rāghavo bharatenoktāṁ babhūva gatacetanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those piteous words uttered by Bharata in connection with the demise of their father, Rāghava was deprived of his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
वाग्वज्रं भरतेनोक्तममनोज्ञं परंतपः
प्रगृह्य बाहू रामो वै पुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः
वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह
verses.transliteration:
vāgvajraṁ bharatenoktamamanojñaṁ paraṁtapaḥ
pragṛhya bāhū rāmo vai puṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ
vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha

translations.english: On that thunder-bolt of a speech being uttered by Bharata, like to a (real) thunder-bolt hurled in battle by the enemy of the Dānavas (Indra), that subduer of foes, Rāma, stretching his arms, fell down to the earth, like a blossoming tree that has been hewn by an axe.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा हि पतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम्
कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā hi patitaṁ rāmaṁ jagatyāṁ jagatīpatim
kūlaghātapariśrāntaṁ prasuptamiva kuñjaram

translations.english: Seeing that lord of the world and mighty bowman, Rāma, fallen, like a sleeping elephant fatigued with turning up earth with its tusks, his brothers exercised with sorrow, broke out into lamentations, and along with Videha's daughter began to sprinkle water (on his face).

verses.sanskrit:
स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामास्रमुत्सृजन्
उपाक्रामत काकुत्स्थः कृपणं बहुभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu saṁjñāṁ punarlabdhvā netrābhyāmāsramutsṛjan
upākrāmata kākutsthaḥ kṛpaṇaṁ bahubhāṣitum

translations.english: Then regaining his consciousness, Kākutstha shedding tears from his eyes, distressfully addressed himself to speech.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु तस्य मया कार्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मना
यो मृतो मम शोकेन न मया चापि संस्कृतः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu tasya mayā kāryaṁ durjātena mahātmanā
yo mṛto mama śokena na mayā cāpi saṁskṛtaḥ

translations.english: What shall I do with Ayodhyā, my sire having gone the way ordained by the gods? And who will govern her, now that she has been deprived of that foremost of monarchs? Of fruitless birth that I am, what can I do for that magnanimous one? And of him that renounced his life from grief on my account I have not even performed the last rites.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो भरत सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वयानघ
शत्रुघेण च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृतः
verses.transliteration:
aho bharata siddhārtho yena rājā tvayānagha
śatrugheṇa ca sarveṣu pretakṛtyeṣu satkṛtaḥ

translations.english: Ah! Bharata, you, O sinless one, are blessed, since by you as well as by Satrughna have been performed all the funeral rites of the king.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्प्रधानामनेकाग्रं नरेन्द्रेण विनाकृताम्
निवृत्तवनवासोऽपि नायोध्यां गन्तुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
niṣpradhānāmanekāgraṁ narendreṇa vinākṛtām
nivṛttavanavāso'pi nāyodhyāṁ gantumutsahe

translations.english: To Ayodhyā, bereft of the monarch, having none to preside over her destinies, and many rulers, will I not return even when the term of my abode in the woods has been passed.

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायां परंतप
को नु शासिष्यति पुनस्ताते लोकान्तरं गते
verses.transliteration:
samāptavanavāsaṁ māmayodhyāyāṁ paraṁtapa
ko nu śāsiṣyati punastāte lokāntaraṁ gate

translations.english: My father having gone to the other world, who, O subduer of enemies, will again counsel me when, my stay in the forest being over, I shall have returned to Ayodhyā?

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्
वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
purā prekṣya suvṛttaṁ māṁ pitā yānyāha sāntvayan
vākyāni tāni śroṣyāmi kutaḥ karṇasukhānyaham

translations.english: And from whom shall I hear those words grateful to the ear, which my father gratifying me used to speak to me when I happened to do something well?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा स भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघवः
उवाच शोकसंतप्तः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā sa bharataṁ bhāryāmabhyetya rāghavaḥ
uvāca śokasaṁtaptaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanām

translations.english: Having thus addressed Bharata, Rāghava burning in grief spoke to his wife, with her countenance resembling the full moon, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुरः पित्रा हीनोऽसि लक्ष्मण
भरतो दुःखमाचष्टे स्वर्गतं पृथिवीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sīte mṛtaste śvaśuraḥ pitrā hīno'si lakṣmaṇa
bharato duḥkhamācaṣṭe svargataṁ pṛthivīpatim

translations.english: O Sītā, your father-in-law is dead and, O Laks inana, you are fatherless. Bharata has communicated to me that sad intelligence that our father has ascended heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदन्तीं जनकात्मजाम्
उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दुःखितो दुःखितं वचः
verses.transliteration:
sāntvayitvā tu tāṁ rāmo rudantīṁ janakātmajām
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṁ tatra duḥkhito duḥkhitaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, pacifying the weeping daughter of Janaka, Rama moved with grief, spoke to the distressed Laksmana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम्
जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ānayeṅgudipiṇyākaṁ cīramāhara cottaram
jalakriyārthaṁ tātasya gamiṣyāmi mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Do you bring Ingudi fruits as well as a piece of new bark. I will go to perform the watery rites of our high-souled sire.

verses.sanskrit:
सीता पुरस्ताद्व्रजतु त्वमेनामभितो व्रज
अहं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामि गतिर्ह्येषा सुदारुणा
verses.transliteration:
sītā purastādvrajatu tvamenāmabhito vraja
ahaṁ paścādgamiṣyāmi gatirhyeṣā sudāruṇā

translations.english: Let Sītā go first. do you follow her. I shall go last. Even this is the course of those in mourning.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः
मृदुर्दान्तश्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढ भक्तिमान्
verses.transliteration:
tato nityānugasteṣāṁ viditātmā mahāmatiḥ
mṛdurdāntaśca śāntaśca rāme ca dṛḍha bhaktimān

translations.english: Then that magnanimous one, having a knowledge of the soul, mild, graceful, capable of controlling his senses, steady in his regard for Rāma, and ever following him, Sumantra, in company with those sons of the auspicious river, Mandakini.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्
सिषिचुस्तूदकं राज्ञे तत एतद्भवत्विति
verses.transliteration:
śīghrasrotasamāsādya tīrthaṁ śivamakardamam
siṣicustūdakaṁ rājñe tata etadbhavatviti

translations.english: Then those illustrious ones, having in distress arrived at the river Mandākini, Mandākini, having convenient descents, charming, ever furnished with blossomag woods, and of rapid currents; and approached it descents, goodly and void of mud, offered water to the monarch, uttering, “May this be so!"

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम्
पितृलोकगतस्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु
verses.transliteration:
etatte rājaśārdūla vimalaṁ toyamakṣayam
pitṛlokagatasyādya maddattamupatiṣṭhatu

translations.english: The protector of the earth (Rama), holding water with his joined hands, facing the south, said weeping, “O foremost of monarchs, may this clear water knowing no deterioration, reach you, who have gone to the world of the ancestral manes.!"

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मन्दाकिनी तीरात्प्रत्युत्तीर्य स राघवः
पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निवापं भ्रातृभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
tato mandākinī tīrātpratyuttīrya sa rāghavaḥ
pituścakāra tejasvī nivāpaṁ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha

translations.english: Then drawing nigh to the marge of the Mandākinī, the energetic Rāghava along with his brothers, offered the Pinda to his father.

verses.sanskrit:
ऐङ्गुदं बदरीमिश्रं पिण्याकं दर्भसंस्तरे
न्यस्य रामः सुदुःखार्तो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
aiṅgudaṁ badarīmiśraṁ piṇyākaṁ darbhasaṁstare
nyasya rāmaḥ suduḥkhārto rudanvacanamabravīt

translations.english: And placing the Ingudi Pinda mixed with jujube on a bed of darbha, Rāma crying in distress, said.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं भुङ्क्ष्व महाराजप्रीतो यदशना वयम्
यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ bhuṅkṣva mahārājaprīto yadaśanā vayam
yadannaḥ puruṣo bhavati tadannāstasya devatāḥ

translations.english: O mighty monarch! do you well pleased feed on this, which we also live upon. That which is the fare of an individual, is also the fare of his divinities.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपतिः
परिजग्राह पाणिभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ parṇakuṭīdvāramāsādya jagatīpatiḥ
parijagrāha pāṇibhyāmubhau bharatalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Then that forernost of men ascending the bank of the stream by the self-same way, got up on the charming side of the hill. And having arrived at the gate of the cottage of leaves, that lord of the earth held both Bharata and Laksmana with his hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात्प्रतिश्रुत्काभवद्गिरौ
भ्रातॄणां सह वैदेह्या सिंहानां नर्दतामिव
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tu rudatāṁ śabdātpratiśrutkābhavadgirau
bhrātṝṇāṁ saha vaidehyā siṁhānāṁ nardatāmiva

translations.english: And there the hill reverberated at the sounds raised by the brothers wailing along with Vaidehi; like to lions roaring.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दं त्रस्ता भरतसैनिकाः
अब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरतः संगतो ध्रुवम्
तेषामेव महाञ्शब्दः शोचतां पितरं मृतम्
verses.transliteration:
vijñāya tumulaṁ śabdaṁ trastā bharatasainikāḥ
abruvaṁścāpi rāmeṇa bharataḥ saṁgato dhruvam
teṣāmeva mahāñśabdaḥ śocatāṁ pitaraṁ mṛtam

translations.english: And perceiving the loud uproar of those mighty ones engaged in offering water to their sire, indulging in lamentations, the army of Bharata became agitated. And they said, “For certain Bharata has met with Rāma; and this mighty noise proceeds from them, as they are bitterly mourning their deceased sire.”

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वासान्परित्यज्य तं सर्वेऽभिमुखाः स्वनम्
अप्येक मनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानं प्रधाविताः
verses.transliteration:
atha vāsānparityajya taṁ sarve'bhimukhāḥ svanam
apyeka manaso jagmuryathāsthānaṁ pradhāvitāḥ

translations.english: Thereat leaving aside their vehicles, they with one mind, rushed towards the spot wherefrom proceeded the uproar.

verses.sanskrit:
हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलंकृतैः
सुकुमारास्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययुः
verses.transliteration:
hayairanye gajairanye rathairanye svalaṁkṛtaiḥ
sukumārāstathaivānye padbhireva narā yayuḥ

translations.english: And of those that were tender, some went on horses, and some on elephants, and some on ornamented chariots, while others went on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिरप्रोषितं रामं चिरविप्रोषितं यथा
द्रष्टुकामो जनः सर्वो जगाम सहसाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
aciraproṣitaṁ rāmaṁ ciraviproṣitaṁ yathā
draṣṭukāmo janaḥ sarvo jagāma sahasāśramam

translations.english: And eager to behold Rāma staying away for a short time though seeming to do so for a long period, all the men at once went to the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातॄणां त्वरितास्ते तु द्रष्टुकामाः समागमम्
ययुर्बहुविधैर्यानैः खुरनेमिसमाकुलैः
verses.transliteration:
bhrātṝṇāṁ tvaritāste tu draṣṭukāmāḥ samāgamam
yayurbahuvidhairyānaiḥ khuranemisamākulaiḥ

translations.english: And desirous of witnessing the meeting of the brothers (with Rāma), they with all despatch proceeded by means of various vehicles consisting of beasts and cars.

verses.sanskrit:
सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानैः खुरनेमिसमाहता
मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे
verses.transliteration:
sā bhūmirbahubhiryānaiḥ khuranemisamāhatā
mumoca tumulaṁ śabdaṁ dyaurivābhrasamāgame

translations.english: And the ground trodden by the wheels of innumerable cars, emitted loud sounds, like those emitted by the sky on clouds gathering.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः
आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनं ततः
verses.transliteration:
tena vitrāsitā nāgāḥ kareṇuparivāritāḥ
āvāsayanto gandhena jagmuranyadvanaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: And frightened by the uproar, elephants accompanied by female ones, perfuming all sides (by the fragrance of temporal juice), went to another forest.

verses.sanskrit:
वराहमृगसिंहाश्च महिषाः सर्क्षवानराः
व्याघ्र गोकर्णगवया वित्रेषुः पृषतैः सह
verses.transliteration:
varāhamṛgasiṁhāśca mahiṣāḥ sarkṣavānarāḥ
vyāghra gokarṇagavayā vitreṣuḥ pṛṣataiḥ saha

translations.english: And boars, and deer, and lions, and buffaloes, and Srmaras, and tigers, and Gokarnas, Gavayas and Prşatas were stricken with panic.

verses.sanskrit:
रथाङ्गसाह्वा नत्यूहा हंसाः कारण्डवाः प्लवाः
तथा पुंस्कोकिलाः क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः
verses.transliteration:
rathāṅgasāhvā natyūhā haṁsāḥ kāraṇḍavāḥ plavāḥ
tathā puṁskokilāḥ krauñcā visaṁjñā bhejire diśaḥ

translations.english: And wild with alarm, Chakravakas, and swans, and Natyuhas, and Plavas, and Karandavas, and male coels, and Kraunchas, fled away in all directions.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकाशं पक्षिभिर्वृतम्
मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयं प्रबभौ तदा
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena vitrastairākāśaṁ pakṣibhirvṛtam
manuṣyairāvṛtā bhūmirubhayaṁ prababhau tadā

translations.english: And the welkin was enveloped by birds frightened by the noise, as the earth was covered by men, and both the sky and the land then gave out great effulgence.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्नरान्बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान्समीक्ष्याथ सुदुःखितान्
पर्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञः पितृवन्मातृवच्च सः
verses.transliteration:
tānnarānbāṣpapūrṇākṣānsamīkṣyātha suduḥkhitān
paryaṣvajata dharmajñaḥ pitṛvanmātṛvacca saḥ

translations.english: Seeing those men oppressed with grief with their eyes filled with tears, that one cognizant of virtue like fathers and mothers, embraced those that deserved it.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्र कांश्चित्परिषस्वजे नरा;न्नराश्च केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन्
चकार सर्वान्सवयस्यबान्धवा;न्यथार्हमासाद्य तदा नृपात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatra kāṁścitpariṣasvaje narā;nnarāśca kecittu tamabhyavādayan
cakāra sarvānsavayasyabāndhavā;nyathārhamāsādya tadā nṛpātmajaḥ

translations.english: And he embraced some persons; and some offered him salutations. And the king's son, as each deserved, properly received them along with their friends and equals in age.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स तेषां रुदतां महात्मनां; भुवं च खं चानुविनादयन्स्वनः
गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च संततं; मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिमो विशुश्रुवे
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa teṣāṁ rudatāṁ mahātmanāṁ; bhuvaṁ ca khaṁ cānuvinādayansvanaḥ
guhā girīṇāṁ ca diśaśca saṁtataṁ; mṛdaṅgaghoṣapratimo viśuśruve

translations.english: And the sounds, produced by those high souled persons lamenting, resounding the earth and the sky, and the mountain-caverns, and all the cardinal points, were heard like peals of Mrdangas. And the sounds, produced by those high souled persons lamenting, resounding the earth and the sky, and the mountain-caverns, and all the cardinal points, were heard like peals of Mrdangas.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठः पुरतः कृत्वा दारान्दशरथस्य च
अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षितः
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhaḥ purataḥ kṛtvā dārāndaśarathasya ca
abhicakrāma taṁ deśaṁ rāmadarśanatarṣitaḥ

translations.english: Desirous of seeing Rama, Vasistha, taking before him the wives of Dasaratha, proceeded towards the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
राजपत्न्यश्च गच्छन्त्यो मन्दं मन्दाकिनीं प्रति
ददृशुस्तत्र तत्तीर्थं रामलक्ष्मणसेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
rājapatnyaśca gacchantyo mandaṁ mandākinīṁ prati
dadṛśustatra tattīrthaṁ rāmalakṣmaṇasevitam

translations.english: And as the wives of the king were going slowly by the Mandākinī, they discovered the landing-place which was used by Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता
सुमित्रामब्रवीद्दीना याश्चान्या राजयोषितः
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇena mukhena pariśuṣyatā
sumitrāmabravīddīnā yāścānyā rājayoṣitaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Kausalyä, with her eyes filled with tears and her countenance rendered pale, observed to the forlorn Sumitra as well as the other wives of the king, sacred like to a first wife, in this forest this is the landing-place of those unfortunate ones of untiring energy, who had been deprived of the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
इतः सुमित्रे पुत्रस्ते सदा जलमतन्द्रितः
स्वयं हरति सौमित्रिर्मम पुत्रस्य कारणात्
verses.transliteration:
itaḥ sumitre putraste sadā jalamatandritaḥ
svayaṁ harati saumitrirmama putrasya kāraṇāt

translations.english: From here, O Sumitrā, does your son, Saumitri, ever vigilant, personally procure water for my son.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सा ददर्श महीतले
पितुरिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं न्यस्तमायतलोचना
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu sā dadarśa mahītale
pituriṅgudipiṇyākaṁ nyastamāyatalocanā

translations.english: That lady of expansive eyes happened to see on the earth the Ingudī piņņa, which had been placed by Rāma for his sire on the darbha with their tops pointing south-wards.

verses.sanskrit:
तं भूमौ पितुरार्तेन न्यस्तं रामेण वीक्ष्य सा
उवाच देवी कौसल्या सर्वा दशरथस्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ bhūmau piturārtena nyastaṁ rāmeṇa vīkṣya sā
uvāca devī kausalyā sarvā daśarathastriyaḥ

translations.english: Seeing this, which had been placed on the ground by Rāma disconsolate for his sire, the noble Kausaly, addressed all the wives of Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
इदमिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः
राघवेण पितुर्दत्तं पश्यतैतद्यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
idamikṣvākunāthasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
rāghaveṇa piturdattaṁ paśyataitadyathāvidhi

translations.english: Do you behold this that has been duly offered to the high-souled descendant of Raghu, lord of the Ikşvāku race, by Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य देवसमानस्य पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः
नैतदौपयिकं मन्ये भुक्तभोगस्य भोजनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya devasamānasya pārthivasya mahātmanaḥ
naitadaupayikaṁ manye bhuktabhogasya bhojanam

translations.english: Do not deem this as fit fare for that magnanimous monarch resembling a celestial, who had enjoyed every luxury (in life).

verses.sanskrit:
चतुरन्तां महीं भुक्त्वा महेन्द्र सदृशो भुवि
कथमिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं स भुङ्क्ते वसुधाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
caturantāṁ mahīṁ bhuktvā mahendra sadṛśo bhuvi
kathamiṅgudipiṇyākaṁ sa bhuṅkte vasudhādhipaḥ

translations.english: Having enjoyed this earth bounded by the four seas, how can that. lord of the world, resembling on earth the mighty Indra, feed on this Ingudī pinda?

verses.sanskrit:
अतो दुःखतरं लोके न किंचित्प्रतिभाति मा
यत्र रामः पितुर्दद्यादिङ्गुदीक्षोदमृद्धिमान्
verses.transliteration:
ato duḥkhataraṁ loke na kiṁcitpratibhāti mā
yatra rāmaḥ piturdadyādiṅgudīkṣodamṛddhimān

translations.english: Nothing appears to me more deplorable in this world than this that the auspicious Rāma has offered an Ingudi cake to his father.

verses.sanskrit:
रामेणेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं पितुर्दत्तं समीक्ष्य मे
कथं दुःखेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा
verses.transliteration:
rāmeṇeṅgudipiṇyākaṁ piturdattaṁ samīkṣya me
kathaṁ duḥkhena hṛdayaṁ na sphoṭati sahasradhā

translations.english: Seeing the Ingudi pinda offered by Rāma to his father, why does not my heart break into a thousand shivers?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमार्तां सपत्न्यस्ता जग्मुराश्वास्य तां तदा
ददृशुश्चाश्रमे रामं स्वर्गाच्च्युतमिवामरम्
verses.transliteration:
evamārtāṁ sapatnyastā jagmurāśvāsya tāṁ tadā
dadṛśuścāśrame rāmaṁ svargāccyutamivāmaram

translations.english: Then those that were co-wives with her, consoled the distressed Kausalyā; and, (entering the asylum), beheld Rāma like an immortal dropped from the celestial regions.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वभोगैः परित्यक्तं राम संप्रेक्ष्य मातरः
आर्ता मुमुचुरश्रूणि सस्वरं शोककर्शिताः
verses.transliteration:
sarvabhogaiḥ parityaktaṁ rāma saṁprekṣya mātaraḥ
ārtā mumucuraśrūṇi sasvaraṁ śokakarśitāḥ

translations.english: Seeing Rāma, who had been deprived of every comfort, his mothers, overwhelmed with grief and distress, began to shed tears, lamenting.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां रामः समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणाञ्शुभान्
मातॄणां मनुजव्याघ्रः सर्वासां सत्यसंगरः
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ rāmaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇāñśubhān
mātṝṇāṁ manujavyāghraḥ sarvāsāṁ satyasaṁgaraḥ

translations.english: Raising his mothers, that foremost of men, Rāma, true to his promise, took hold of those lotus feet of theirs.

verses.sanskrit:
ताः पाणिभिः सुखस्पर्शैर्मृद्वङ्गुलितलैः शुभैः
प्रममार्जू रजः पृष्ठाद्रामस्यायतलोचनाः
verses.transliteration:
tāḥ pāṇibhiḥ sukhasparśairmṛdvaṅgulitalaiḥ śubhaiḥ
pramamārjū rajaḥ pṛṣṭhādrāmasyāyatalocanāḥ

translations.english: And those ones furnished with expansive eyes, (on their turn) by means of their fair hands of delicious feed furnished with soft fingers and palms, fell to rubbing the dust off Rāma's back.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रिरपि ताः सर्वा मातॄः संप्रेक्ष्य दुःखितः
अभ्यवादयतासक्तं शनै रामादनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
saumitrirapi tāḥ sarvā mātṝḥ saṁprekṣya duḥkhitaḥ
abhyavādayatāsaktaṁ śanai rāmādanantaram

translations.english: After Rāma had done, Sumitrā's son also, seeing all his mothers, with sorrow gently paid his reverence to them with affection.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन्सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रियः
वृत्तिं दशरथाज्जाते लक्ष्मणे शुभलक्षणे
verses.transliteration:
yathā rāme tathā tasminsarvā vavṛtire striyaḥ
vṛttiṁ daśarathājjāte lakṣmaṇe śubhalakṣaṇe

translations.english: Thereat, as they had treated Rāma, all the ladies treated that one sprung from Daśaratha, Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतापि चरणांस्तासामुपसंगृह्य दुःखिता
श्वश्रूणामश्रुपूर्णाक्षी सा बभूवाग्रतः स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
sītāpi caraṇāṁstāsāmupasaṁgṛhya duḥkhitā
śvaśrūṇāmaśrupūrṇākṣī sā babhūvāgrataḥ sthitā

translations.english: Sītă also with her eyes filled with tears, law, stood before them in distressful guise.

verses.sanskrit:
तां परिष्वज्य दुःखार्तां माता दुहितरं यथा
वनवासकृशां दीनां कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ pariṣvajya duḥkhārtāṁ mātā duhitaraṁ yathā
vanavāsakṛśāṁ dīnāṁ kausalyā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Embracing that woeful one in banishment, even as a mother does her daughter, Kausalya, smitten with grief, said.

verses.sanskrit:
विदेहराजस्य सुता स्नुषा दशरथस्य च
रामपत्नी कथं दुःखं संप्राप्ता निर्जने वने
verses.transliteration:
videharājasya sutā snuṣā daśarathasya ca
rāmapatnī kathaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṁprāptā nirjane vane

translations.english: The daughter of Videha's King, and the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, and the wife of Rāma himself, why does such a lady undergo misery in the lone forest?

verses.sanskrit:
मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाश्रयम्
भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसंभवः
verses.transliteration:
mukhaṁ te prekṣya māṁ śoko dahatyagnirivāśrayam
bhṛśaṁ manasi vaidehi vyasanāraṇisaṁbhavaḥ

translations.english: O Vaidehi, beholding your face like to a lotus heated under the sun, or a lily that has been crushed, or like to gold covered with dust, or the moon enveloped by clouds, grief begot of this vortex of disaster that is in my mind, fiercely burns me, as fire consume a structure.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रुवन्त्यामेवमार्तायां जनन्यां भरताग्रजः
पादावासाद्य जग्राह वसिष्ठस्य स राघवः
verses.transliteration:
bruvantyāmevamārtāyāṁ jananyāṁ bharatāgrajaḥ
pādāvāsādya jagrāha vasiṣṭhasya sa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: As his wretched mother was thus speaking, Bharata's elder brother, Räghava, approaching, took the feet of Vasiştha.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोहितस्याग्निसमस्य तस्य वै; बृहस्पतेरिन्द्र इवामराधिपः
प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजसः; सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघवः
verses.transliteration:
purohitasyāgnisamasya tasya vai; bṛhaspaterindra ivāmarādhipaḥ
pragṛhya pādau susamṛddhatejasaḥ; sahaiva tenopaviveśa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Having taken hold of the feet of the priest resembling a flame, and of accumulated energy, like to that lord of the immortals, Indra, taking the feet of Bșhaspati, Rāghava sat down with him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो जघन्यं सहितैः स मन्त्रिभिः; पुरप्रधानैश्च सहैव सैनिकैः
जनेन धर्मज्ञतमेन धर्मवा;नुपोपविष्टो भरतस्तदाग्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
tato jaghanyaṁ sahitaiḥ sa mantribhiḥ; purapradhānaiśca sahaiva sainikaiḥ
janena dharmajñatamena dharmavā;nupopaviṣṭo bharatastadāgrajam

translations.english: Then behind them (Rāma and Vasistha), along with his own counsellors, and principal citizens, and generals, and persons of eminent piety, sat the virtuous Bharata in the presence of his elder brother.

verses.sanskrit:
उपोपविष्टस्तु तदा स वीर्यवां;स्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम्
श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरतः कृताञ्जलि;र्यथा महेन्द्रः प्रयतः प्रजापतिम्
verses.transliteration:
upopaviṣṭastu tadā sa vīryavāṁ;stapasviveṣeṇa samīkṣya rāghavam
śriyā jvalantaṁ bharataḥ kṛtāñjali;ryathā mahendraḥ prayataḥ prajāpatim

translations.english: Seeing Raghava in the guise of an ascetic, flaming in grace, the exceedingly powerful Bharata with joined palms sat down in company with his brother, like the great Indra of controlled faculties in presence of Prajāpati.

verses.sanskrit:
किमेष वाक्यं भरतोऽद्य राघवं; प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति
इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो; बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा
verses.transliteration:
kimeṣa vākyaṁ bharato'dya rāghavaṁ; praṇamya satkṛtya ca sādhu vakṣyati
itīva tasyāryajanasya tattvato; babhūva kautūhalamuttamaṁ tadā

translations.english: "What will Bharata, having bowed to Rāghava and paid him homage, will say to him?", this intense curiosity arose in (the mind of) all the noble persons present there.

verses.sanskrit:
स राघवः सत्यधृतिश्च लक्ष्मणो; महानुभावो भरतश्च धार्मिकः
वृताः सुहृद्भिश्च विरेजुरध्वरे; यथा सदस्यैः सहितास्त्रयोऽग्नयः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāghavaḥ satyadhṛtiśca lakṣmaṇo; mahānubhāvo bharataśca dhārmikaḥ
vṛtāḥ suhṛdbhiśca virejuradhvare; yathā sadasyaiḥ sahitāstrayo'gnayaḥ

translations.english: And Rāghava having truth and forbearance, and Lakşmaņa endowed with magnanimity, and Bharata possessed of righteousness, surrounded by their friends, appeared (there) like to the three fires surrounded by Sadasyas.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु रामः समाश्वास्य भ्रातरं गुरुवत्सलम्
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu rāmaḥ samāśvāsya bhrātaraṁ guruvatsalam
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā praṣṭuṁ samupacakrame

translations.english: Knowing Bharata as devoted to his superior Răma along with his brother Lakşmaņa, asked him.

verses.sanskrit:
यन्निमित्तमिमं देशं कृष्णाजिनजटाधरः
हित्वा राज्यं प्रविष्टस्त्वं तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
yannimittamimaṁ deśaṁ kṛṣṇājinajaṭādharaḥ
hitvā rājyaṁ praviṣṭastvaṁ tatsarvaṁ vaktumarhasi

translations.english: What for is this (visit of yours to the woods)? I wish to hear as clearly related by you the reason why clad in blackdeerskin and wearing matted locks, you, leaving your kingdom, have come to these regions. It behoves you to tell me all this.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः केकयीपुत्रः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना
प्रगृह्य बलवद्भूयः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ kekayīputraḥ kākutsthena mahātmanā
pragṛhya balavadbhūyaḥ prāñjalirvākyamabravīt

translations.english: Thus accosted by the high-souled Kākutstha, Kaikeyi's son, suppressing his grief by a strong effort, with joined hands said.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्यं तातः परित्यज्य कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
गतः स्वर्गं महाबाहुः पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
āryaṁ tātaḥ parityajya kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
gataḥ svargaṁ mahābāhuḥ putraśokābhipīḍitaḥ

translations.english: O noble one, forsaking us all, our father possessed of mighty arms, having performed this terrible task, in consequence of being urged by a woman, my mother Kaikeyi, has gone to heaven afflicted with grief on account of his son, O repressor of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
सा राज्यफलमप्राप्य विधवा शोककर्शिता
पतिष्यति महाघोरे निरये जननी मम
verses.transliteration:
sā rājyaphalamaprāpya vidhavā śokakarśitā
patiṣyati mahāghore niraye jananī mama

translations.english: And she has committed a signal sin capable of destroying her fame. And without obtaining the kingdom which she had coveted as the fruit of her action, a widow tried with grief, my mother will fall into a terrible hell.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
अभिषिञ्चस्व चाद्यैव राज्येन मघवानिव
verses.transliteration:
tasya me dāsabhūtasya prasādaṁ kartumarhasi
abhiṣiñcasva cādyaiva rājyena maghavāniva

translations.english: Now it behoves you to extend your favour to me who have become your slave. Do you this very day get yourself installed in the kingdom, like to Indra himself.

verses.sanskrit:
इमाः प्रकृतयः सर्वा विधवा मातुरश्च याः
त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्ताः प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
imāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā vidhavā māturaśca yāḥ
tvatsakāśamanuprāptāḥ prasādaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: All these subjects and our widowed mothers have come to you. It behoves you to show your favour to them.

verses.sanskrit:
तदानुपूर्व्या युक्तं च युक्तं चात्मनि मानद
राज्यं प्राप्नुहि धर्मेण सकामान्सुहृदः कुरु
verses.transliteration:
tadānupūrvyā yuktaṁ ca yuktaṁ cātmani mānada
rājyaṁ prāpnuhi dharmeṇa sakāmānsuhṛdaḥ kuru

translations.english: You are the first-born; and meet it is that you should get yourself installed, O bestower of honour. Therefore do you receive the kingdom righteously and fulfil the desire of your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
एभिश्च सचिवैः सार्धं शिरसा याचितो मया
भ्रातुः शिष्यस्य दासस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ebhiśca sacivaiḥ sārdhaṁ śirasā yācito mayā
bhrātuḥ śiṣyasya dāsasya prasādaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: And like the autumnal Night on having the unclouded moon, let the entire Earth cease to be a widow on having you counsellors. It behoves you to show your favour to your brother, disciple, and slave.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं शाश्वतं पित्र्यं सर्वं सचिवमण्डलम्
पूजितं पुरुषव्याघ्र नातिक्रमितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ śāśvataṁ pitryaṁ sarvaṁ sacivamaṇḍalam
pūjitaṁ puruṣavyāghra nātikramitumutsahe

translations.english: Therefore, O chief of men, you ought not to pass by this honoured band of ancestral ministers, who have always been serving this race.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुः सबाष्पः केकयीसुतः
रामस्य शिरसा पादौ जग्राह भरतः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahābāhuḥ sabāṣpaḥ kekayīsutaḥ
rāmasya śirasā pādau jagrāha bharataḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Having said this, with tears flooding his eyes, the mighty-armed son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, again took Rāma's feet on this head.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः
भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ mattamiva mātaṅgaṁ niḥśvasantaṁ punaḥ punaḥ
bhrātaraṁ bharataṁ rāmaḥ pariṣvajyedamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma embracing his brother Bharata resembling a mad elephant, and sighing again and again, said.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलीनः सत्त्वसंपन्नस्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः
राज्यहेतोः कथं पापमाचरेत्त्वद्विधो जनः
verses.transliteration:
kulīnaḥ sattvasaṁpannastejasvī caritavrataḥ
rājyahetoḥ kathaṁ pāpamācarettvadvidho janaḥ

translations.english: Of a high race, possessed of strength, endowed with energy, and vowed to sterling worth of character, how can one like me commit sin for the sake of dominion?

verses.sanskrit:
न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरि सूदन
न चापि जननीं बाल्यात्त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
na doṣaṁ tvayi paśyāmi sūkṣmamapyari sūdana
na cāpi jananīṁ bālyāttvaṁ vigarhitumarhasi

translations.english: Fault find I none ever so small in you, you destroyer of foes. Nor does it become you from puerility to tax your mother.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्पितरि धर्मज्ञ गौरवं लोकसत्कृते
तावद्धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ जनन्यामपि गौरवम्
verses.transliteration:
yāvatpitari dharmajña gauravaṁ lokasatkṛte
tāvaddharmabhṛtāṁ śreṣṭha jananyāmapi gauravam

translations.english: O you conversant with morality, O foremost of those observing righteousness, in respect of virtuous conduct a mother should be as much regarded (by a son) as a father is.

verses.sanskrit:
एताभ्यां धर्मशीलाभ्यां वनं गच्छेति राघव
माता पितृभ्यामुक्तोऽहं कथमन्यत्समाचरे
verses.transliteration:
etābhyāṁ dharmaśīlābhyāṁ vanaṁ gaccheti rāghava
mātā pitṛbhyāmukto'haṁ kathamanyatsamācare

translations.english: How can I, O descendant of Rāghava, having been told by my righteous father and mother, 'Go to the woods', act otherwise?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया राज्यमयोध्यायां प्राप्तव्यं लोकसत्कृतम्
वस्तव्यं दण्डकारण्ये मया वल्कलवाससा
verses.transliteration:
tvayā rājyamayodhyāyāṁ prāptavyaṁ lokasatkṛtam
vastavyaṁ daṇḍakāraṇye mayā valkalavāsasā

translations.english: You ought to receive the kingdom, Ayodhyā, honoured of men; and I ought to dwell in Dandaka dressed in bark.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं कृत्वा महाराजो विभागं लोकसंनिधौ
व्यादिश्य च महातेजा दिवं दशरथो गतः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ kṛtvā mahārājo vibhāgaṁ lokasaṁnidhau
vyādiśya ca mahātejā divaṁ daśaratho gataḥ

translations.english: Having made this division of duties in the presence of all, and also enjoined this, the mighty monarch, Dasaratha, has ascended heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
स च प्रमाणं धर्मात्मा राजा लोकगुरुस्तव
पित्रा दत्तं यथाभागमुपभोक्तुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
sa ca pramāṇaṁ dharmātmā rājā lokagurustava
pitrā dattaṁ yathābhāgamupabhoktuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: That superior of all, even the virtuous king, is your evidence. It behoves you to enjoy that which has been assigned to you by your sire.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश समाः सौम्य दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः
उपभोक्ष्ये त्वहं दत्तं भागं पित्रा महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa samāḥ saumya daṇḍakāraṇyamāśritaḥ
upabhokṣye tvahaṁ dattaṁ bhāgaṁ pitrā mahātmanā

translations.english: And, O mild one, taking refuge in the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years, I will act the part that has been set apart for me by my magnanimous father.

verses.sanskrit:
यदब्रवीन्मां नरलोकसत्कृतः; पिता महात्मा विबुधाधिपोपमः
तदेव मन्ये परमात्मनो हितं; न सर्वलोकेश्वरभावमव्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
yadabravīnmāṁ naralokasatkṛtaḥ; pitā mahātmā vibudhādhipopamaḥ
tadeva manye paramātmano hitaṁ; na sarvalokeśvarabhāvamavyayam

translations.english: What has been assigned to me by that one respected by all men, my high-souled father resembling the lord of celestials himself, is my prime good; the masterdom of all the worlds I would decline (should it be opposed to the will of my sire).

verses.sanskrit:
रजन्यां सुप्रभातायां भ्रातरस्ते सुहृद्वृताः
मन्दाकिन्यां हुतं जप्यं कृत्वा राममुपागमन्
verses.transliteration:
rajanyāṁ suprabhātāyāṁ bhrātaraste suhṛdvṛtāḥ
mandākinyāṁ hutaṁ japyaṁ kṛtvā rāmamupāgaman

translations.english: As those foremost of persons surrounded by their friends indulged in lamentations, the night passed away in grief. On the night being succeeded by an auspicious morning, those brothers surrounded by their friends, having performed Homa and Japa on the Mandākinī, returned to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तूष्णीं ते समुपासीना न कश्चित्किंचिदब्रवीत्
भरतस्तु सुहृन्मध्ये रामवचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tūṣṇīṁ te samupāsīnā na kaścitkiṁcidabravīt
bharatastu suhṛnmadhye rāmavacanamabravīt

translations.english: And sitting silent, no one said anything. Then Bharata addressed Rāma in the midst of those friends, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्त्विता मामिका माता दत्तं राज्यमिदं मम
तद्ददामि तवैवाहं भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्
verses.transliteration:
sāntvitā māmikā mātā dattaṁ rājyamidaṁ mama
taddadāmi tavaivāhaṁ bhuṅkṣva rājyamakaṇṭakam

translations.english: My mother was (first) pacified (by grant to the kingdom.) The kingdom is (now) mine. I grant the same to you. Do you enjoy the kingdom rid of its thorns.

verses.sanskrit:
महतेवाम्बुवेगेन भिन्नः सेतुर्जलागमे
दुरावारं त्वदन्येन राज्यखण्डमिदं महत्
verses.transliteration:
mahatevāmbuvegena bhinnaḥ seturjalāgame
durāvāraṁ tvadanyena rājyakhaṇḍamidaṁ mahat

translations.english: Like to a dyke forced by a torrent during the rains, this mighty monarchy is difficult of being protected save by you.

verses.sanskrit:
गतिं खर इवाश्वस्य तार्क्ष्यस्येव पतत्रिणः
अनुगन्तुं न शक्तिर्मे गतिं तव महीपते
verses.transliteration:
gatiṁ khara ivāśvasya tārkṣyasyeva patatriṇaḥ
anugantuṁ na śaktirme gatiṁ tava mahīpate

translations.english: As a mule is incapable of imitating the course of a horse, or as birds, that of Tarksya, I, O Lord of earth, lack the strength to imitate you.

verses.sanskrit:
सुजीवं नित्यशस्तस्य यः परैरुपजीव्यते
राम तेन तु दुर्जीवं यः परानुपजीवति
verses.transliteration:
sujīvaṁ nityaśastasya yaḥ parairupajīvyate
rāma tena tu durjīvaṁ yaḥ parānupajīvati

translations.english: O Rāma, ever happy is the life of him that others depend upon for subsistence: unhappy is the life of the person that depends upon others for support.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेणयस्त्वां महाराज पश्यन्त्वग्र्याश्च सर्वशः
प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं राज्ये स्थितमरिंदमम्
verses.transliteration:
śreṇayastvāṁ mahārāja paśyantvagryāśca sarvaśaḥ
pratapantamivādityaṁ rājye sthitamariṁdamam

translations.english: Let the principal orders, O monarch, behold you, represser of foes, established in the kingdom, like the powerful sun himself.

verses.sanskrit:
तवानुयाने काकुत्ष्ठ मत्ता नर्दन्तु कुञ्जराः
अन्तःपुर गता नार्यो नन्दन्तु सुसमाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
tavānuyāne kākutṣṭha mattā nardantu kuñjarāḥ
antaḥpura gatā nāryo nandantu susamāhitāḥ

translations.english: O Kākutstha, let mad elephants roar, with the view of following you; and let the women of the inner apartments with concentrated rainds utter jubilation.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य साध्वित्यमन्यन्त नागरा विविधा जनाः
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामं प्रत्यनुयाचतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya sādhvityamanyanta nāgarā vividhā janāḥ
bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaṁ pratyanuyācataḥ

translations.english: On hearing the words of Bharata, who was beseeching Rāma, many of the citizens expressed their approbation by exclaiming, “Excellent well!"

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवं दुःखितं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं यशस्विनम्
रामः कृतात्मा भरतं समाश्वासयदात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
tamevaṁ duḥkhitaṁ prekṣya vilapantaṁ yaśasvinam
rāmaḥ kṛtātmā bharataṁ samāśvāsayadātmavān

translations.english: Seeing the illustrious Bharata aggrieved and engaged in lamentation, the calm and considerate Rāma consoled him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
नात्मनः कामकारोऽस्ति पुरुषोऽयमनीश्वरः
इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति
verses.transliteration:
nātmanaḥ kāmakāro'sti puruṣo'yamanīśvaraḥ
itaścetarataścainaṁ kṛtāntaḥ parikarṣati

translations.english: No creature is endowed with the power of exercising any control over the course of events, man has no independent status (in nature).

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ
saṁyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṁ ca jīvitam

translations.english: The Destroyer draw him both here and hereafter. Those that increase, are destined to deteriorate; those that go upward, ultimately fall, those that come together, separate in the end; and life at length meet with death.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा फलानं पक्वानां नान्यत्र पतनाद्भयम्
एवं नरस्य जातस्य नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्
verses.transliteration:
yathā phalānaṁ pakvānāṁ nānyatra patanādbhayam
evaṁ narasya jātasya nānyatra maraṇādbhayam

translations.english: As a ripe fruit has no other fear than fall, so man who is born, has no other fear than death.

verses.sanskrit:
यथागारं दृढस्थूणं जीर्णं भूत्वावसीदति
तथावसीदन्ति नरा जरामृत्युवशं गताः
verses.transliteration:
yathāgāraṁ dṛḍhasthūṇaṁ jīrṇaṁ bhūtvāvasīdati
tathāvasīdanti narā jarāmṛtyuvaśaṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: Even as a stout-pillared edifice, getting dilapidated, waxes weak, so men coming under the sway of decrepitude and death, get enfeebled.

verses.sanskrit:
अहोरात्राणि गच्छन्ति सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह
आयूंषि क्षपयन्त्याशु ग्रीष्मे जलमिवांशवः
verses.transliteration:
ahorātrāṇi gacchanti sarveṣāṁ prāṇināmiha
āyūṁṣi kṣapayantyāśu grīṣme jalamivāṁśavaḥ

translations.english: In this world, days and nights pass away with creatures, and speedily impair their lives, even as in summer the rays (of the sun) (dry up) the waters.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानमनुशोच त्वं किमन्यमनुशोचसि
आयुस्ते हीयते यस्य स्थितस्य च गतस्य च
verses.transliteration:
ātmānamanuśoca tvaṁ kimanyamanuśocasi
āyuste hīyate yasya sthitasya ca gatasya ca

translations.english: Do you therefore deplore yourself. Why do you lament any thing else? Every one's life is decreasing, whether he sits or moves.

verses.sanskrit:
सहैव मृत्युर्व्रजति सह मृत्युर्निषीदति
गत्वा सुदीर्घमध्वानं सह मृत्युर्निवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
sahaiva mṛtyurvrajati saha mṛtyurniṣīdati
gatvā sudīrghamadhvānaṁ saha mṛtyurnivartate

translations.english: Death goes with one, sits down with one, and after having gone a long way, returns with one.

verses.sanskrit:
गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ताः श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः
जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्
verses.transliteration:
gātreṣu valayaḥ prāptāḥ śvetāścaiva śiroruhāḥ
jarayā puruṣo jīrṇaḥ kiṁ hi kṛtvā prabhāvayet

translations.english: The person is filled with folds in the skin, the hair has grown hoary, the individual is enfeebled because of age, by doing what, can be prevent this?

verses.sanskrit:
नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमिते रवौ
आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
nandantyudita āditye nandantyastamite ravau
ātmano nāvabudhyante manuṣyā jīvitakṣayam

translations.english: People rejoice on the rising of the sun; they feel delighted at the approach of night, but they do not understand that their lives have (meanwhile) been shortened.

verses.sanskrit:
हृष्यन्त्यृतुमुखं दृष्ट्वा नवं नवमिहागतम्
ऋतूनां परिवर्तेन प्राणिनां प्राणसंक्षयः
verses.transliteration:
hṛṣyantyṛtumukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā navaṁ navamihāgatam
ṛtūnāṁ parivartena prāṇināṁ prāṇasaṁkṣayaḥ

translations.english: People are exhilarated at the commencement of a new season of novel fashion; creatures get their lives shortened at the change of season.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च
समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bhāryāśca putrāśca jñātayaśca vasūni ca
sametya vyavadhāvanti dhruvo hyeṣāṁ vinābhavaḥ

translations.english: As on the mighty ocean, one piece of wood comes in contact with another; so, a person, having been in association with another, is separated from him in time. In this way, wives and sons and kindred and wealth, having been in association, go away; their separation is certain.

verses.sanskrit:
नात्र कश्चिद्यथा भावं प्राणी समभिवर्तते
तेन तस्मिन्न सामर्थ्यं प्रेतस्यास्त्यनुशोचतः
verses.transliteration:
nātra kaścidyathā bhāvaṁ prāṇī samabhivartate
tena tasminna sāmarthyaṁ pretasyāstyanuśocataḥ

translations.english: There exists not one in this world that can change one's nature as received. A person lamenting a dead individual, has no power to prevent his own death.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः
अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवतामिति
verses.transliteration:
yathā hi sārthaṁ gacchantaṁ brūyātkaścitpathi sthitaḥ
ahamapyāgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhato bhavatāmiti

translations.english: As while one is proceeding on a road, another stationed by the way, says, 'I too will go in your wake,' even so, the way that has been followed by our predecessors, (must be followed as well by us.) Why should people mourn for deceased relatives), when they are themselves subject to the fate that knows no turning? (Perceiving the destruction of) life declining, like to a current that never turns back, one should engage his soul in happiness; for all men are said to be born for the same.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मात्मा स शुभैः कृत्स्नैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः
धूतपापो गतः स्वर्गं पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
dharmātmā sa śubhaiḥ kṛtsnaiḥ kratubhiścāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
dhūtapāpo gataḥ svargaṁ pitā naḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ

translations.english: My child, our righteous sire, who, after having performed excellent and entire sacrifices, accompanied with Dakșiņās, has repaired to heaven, honoured of he good, should not be mourned.* *The N.W.P. text has seven additional lines here, wanting in the other texts:, “That lord of the earth, our father Dasaratha, has gone to heaven. On account of having adequately maintained his servants and governed his subjects, and virtuously given away wealth, our sire has gone to heaven. And by virtue of supremely excellent and desirable acts, and sacrifices accompanied with Dakşiņā, that master of this world, our father Dasaratha, has ascended heaven. And having celebrated many sacrifices and enjoyed luxuries, that lord of the earth, having attained a goodly age, has gone to heaven."

verses.sanskrit:
भृत्यानां भरणात्सम्यक्प्रजानां परिपालनात्
अर्थादानाच्च धार्मेण पिता नस्त्रिदिवं गतः
verses.transliteration:
bhṛtyānāṁ bharaṇātsamyakprajānāṁ paripālanāt
arthādānācca dhārmeṇa pitā nastridivaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Having renounced his human frame wasted and worn out with age, our father has attained celestial state, which exists in the regions of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्यमरिंदम
तत्त्वयापि सदा मान्यं स वै बन्धुः स नः पिता
verses.transliteration:
na mayā śāsanaṁ tasya tyaktuṁ nyāyyamariṁdama
tattvayāpi sadā mānyaṁ sa vai bandhuḥ sa naḥ pitā

translations.english: O subduer foes, it is not proper for me to pass by his orders. So they are also worthy of being honoured by you. He is our friend and father.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु विरते रामे वचनमर्थवत्
उवाच भरतश्चित्रं धार्मिको धार्मिकं वचः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu virate rāme vacanamarthavat
uvāca bharataścitraṁ dhārmiko dhārmikaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: On Rāma having stopped after speaking these pregnant words, the virtuous Bharata addressed the righteous Rāma attached to him subjects in an excellent speech on the banks of the Mandākinī, saying, “O vanquisher of foes, who is there is this world like to you?"

verses.sanskrit:
को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृशस्त्वमरिंदम
न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा न प्रहर्षयेत्
verses.transliteration:
ko hi syādīdṛśo loke yādṛśastvamariṁdama
na tvāṁ pravyathayedduḥkhaṁ prītirvā na praharṣayet

translations.english: Pain does not afflict you, nor does pleasure exhilarate. Yourself the exemplar of even aged people, you refer to them on doubtful point (of morality).

verses.sanskrit:
यस्यैष बुद्धिलाभः स्यात्परितप्येत केन सः
स एवं व्यसनं प्राप्य न विषीदितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
yasyaiṣa buddhilābhaḥ syātparitapyeta kena saḥ
sa evaṁ vyasanaṁ prāpya na viṣīditumarhati

translations.english: ‘Living like to dead and existing like to nonexisting', what shall make a person that has attained this intellectual state, grieve?

verses.sanskrit:
अमरोपमसत्त्वस्त्वं महात्मा सत्यसंगरः
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च बुद्धिमांश्चासि राघव
verses.transliteration:
amaropamasattvastvaṁ mahātmā satyasaṁgaraḥ
sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca buddhimāṁścāsi rāghava

translations.english: You resemble, O Rāghava, the god in strength, and are magnanimous, and truthful in promise, and know every thing and are endued with intelligence, Calamity, however unbearable it may be, should not overpower a person like yourself furnished with such virtues and cognizant of life and death.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रोषिते मयि यत्पापं मात्रा मत्कारणात्कृतम्
क्षुद्रया तदनिष्टं मे प्रसीदतु भवान्मम
verses.transliteration:
proṣite mayi yatpāpaṁ mātrā matkāraṇātkṛtam
kṣudrayā tadaniṣṭaṁ me prasīdatu bhavānmama

translations.english: The sin that in my absence from home has been perpetrated by my mean-minded mother does not find favour in my sight. Be you therefore propitious to me.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मबन्धेन बद्धोऽस्मि तेनेमां नेह मातरम्
हन्मि तीव्रेण दण्डेन दण्डार्हां पापकारिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
dharmabandhena baddho'smi tenemāṁ neha mātaram
hanmi tīvreṇa daṇḍena daṇḍārhāṁ pāpakāriṇīm

translations.english: I am bound by the fetters of religion. For this it is that I do not by a severe penalty slay my wicked mother deserving of chastisement.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं दशरथाज्जातः शुद्धाभिजनकर्मणः
जानन्धर्ममधर्मिष्ठं कुर्यां कर्म जुगुप्सितम्
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ daśarathājjātaḥ śuddhābhijanakarmaṇaḥ
jānandharmamadharmiṣṭhaṁ kuryāṁ karma jugupsitam

translations.english: How having sprung from Dasaratha of righteous deeds and born of immaculate race, and knowing virtue and vice, can I commit such a reprehensible action?

verses.sanskrit:
गुरुः क्रियावान्वृद्धश्च राजा प्रेतः पितेति च
तातं न परिगर्हेयं दैवतं चेति संसदि
verses.transliteration:
guruḥ kriyāvānvṛddhaśca rājā pretaḥ piteti ca
tātaṁ na parigarheyaṁ daivataṁ ceti saṁsadi

translations.english: Dasaratha is our superior, of meritorious acts, aged our king, a departed spirit, and our father, it is on account of this that I do not censure our father who is a deity to us.

verses.sanskrit:
को हि धर्मार्थयोर्हीनमीदृशं कर्म किल्बिषम्
स्त्रियाः प्रियचिकीर्षुः सन्कुर्याद्धर्मज्ञ धर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
ko hi dharmārthayorhīnamīdṛśaṁ karma kilbiṣam
striyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ sankuryāddharmajña dharmavit

translations.english: O cognizant of virtue, what virtuous person conversant in morality, should, seeking the pleasure of his wife, commit such a sinful act devoid of both righteousness and interest?

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तकाले हि भूतानि मुह्यन्तीति पुराश्रुतिः
राज्ञैवं कुर्वता लोके प्रत्यक्षा सा श्रुतिः कृता
verses.transliteration:
antakāle hi bhūtāni muhyantīti purāśrutiḥ
rājñaivaṁ kurvatā loke pratyakṣā sā śrutiḥ kṛtā

translations.english: 'Creatures, as their end approaches, lose their sense this ancient adage has been illustrated in the world by the course the king has taken.

verses.sanskrit:
साध्वर्थमभिसंधाय क्रोधान्मोहाच्च साहसात्
तातस्य यदतिक्रान्तं प्रत्याहरतु तद्भवान्
verses.transliteration:
sādhvarthamabhisaṁdhāya krodhānmohācca sāhasāt
tātasya yadatikrāntaṁ pratyāharatu tadbhavān

translations.english: Do you, intent upon bringing about good, redeem the wrong that has been done by our sire through anger, ignorance and recklessness.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्हि समतिक्रान्तं पुत्रो यः साधु मन्यते
तदपत्यं मतं लोके विपरीतमतोऽन्यथा
verses.transliteration:
piturhi samatikrāntaṁ putro yaḥ sādhu manyate
tadapatyaṁ mataṁ loke viparītamato'nyathā

translations.english: The son that repair the wrong done by his father by acting contrary to the latter is in this world considered really a son; but not he that acts otherwise.

verses.sanskrit:
तदपत्यं भवानस्तु मा भवान्दुष्कृतं पितुः
अभिपत्तत्कृतं कर्म लोके धीरविगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
tadapatyaṁ bhavānastu mā bhavānduṣkṛtaṁ pituḥ
abhipattatkṛtaṁ karma loke dhīravigarhitam

translations.english: Be you that (real) son (of the monarch). Do you not approve the action of your father, since what he has done is divorced from righteousness and is blameworthy.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेयीं मां च तातं च सुहृदो बान्धवांश्च नः
पौरजानपदान्सर्वांस्त्रातु सर्वमिदं भवान्
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyīṁ māṁ ca tātaṁ ca suhṛdo bāndhavāṁśca naḥ
paurajānapadānsarvāṁstrātu sarvamidaṁ bhavān

translations.english: Do you rescue all these, Kaikeyī, myself, my father, our friends and adherents, and the whole body of the citizens as well as the inhabitants of the provinces.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व चारण्यं क्व च क्षात्रं क्व जटाः क्व च पालनम्
ईदृशं व्याहतं कर्म न भवान्कर्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
kva cāraṇyaṁ kva ca kṣātraṁ kva jaṭāḥ kva ca pālanam
īdṛśaṁ vyāhataṁ karma na bhavānkartumarhati

translations.english: Where is the forest? And where is Ksatriya morality? Where are matted locks? And where is your government of the country? It behoves you not to act in such an untoward way.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ क्लेशजमेव त्वं धर्मं चरितुमिच्छसि
धर्मेण चतुरो वर्णान्पालयन्क्लेशमाप्नुहि
verses.transliteration:
atha kleśajameva tvaṁ dharmaṁ caritumicchasi
dharmeṇa caturo varṇānpālayankleśamāpnuhi

translations.english: But if you be bent upon practising this austere morality, do you undergo this trouble, after having righteously ruled the four orders.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमाश्रमम्
आहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
caturṇāmāśramāṇāṁ hi gārhasthyaṁ śreṣṭhamāśramam
āhurdharmajña dharmajñāstaṁ kathaṁ tyaktumarhasi

translations.english: O you cognizant of morality, those versed in duty say that of the four modes of life, the life of the householder is the foremost. Why then do you wish to renounce the same?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतेन बालः स्थानेन जन्मना भवतो ह्यहम्
स कथं पालयिष्यामि भूमिं भवति तिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
śrutena bālaḥ sthānena janmanā bhavato hyaham
sa kathaṁ pālayiṣyāmi bhūmiṁ bhavati tiṣṭhati

translations.english: I am inferior to you in learning, in position, and in birth. How can I then govern the earth, you existing?

verses.sanskrit:
हीनबुद्धिगुणो बालो हीनः स्थानेन चाप्यहम्
भवता च विना भूतो न वर्तयितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
hīnabuddhiguṇo bālo hīnaḥ sthānena cāpyaham
bhavatā ca vinā bhūto na vartayitumutsahe

translations.english: Void of sense and quality, a body, and inferior to you in point of years, I, deprived of you, can not live.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं निखिलमव्यग्रं पित्र्यं राज्यमकण्टकम्
अनुशाधि स्वधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ सह बान्धवैः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ nikhilamavyagraṁ pitryaṁ rājyamakaṇṭakam
anuśādhi svadharmeṇa dharmajña saha bāndhavaiḥ

translations.english: O you cognizant of morality, do you, along with your friends, according to your proper morality rule this entire ancestral kingdom rid of its thorns and enjoying tranquillity.

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव त्वाभिषिञ्चन्तु धर्मज्ञ सह बान्धवैः
ऋत्विजः सवसिष्ठाश्च मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रकोविदाः
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva tvābhiṣiñcantu dharmajña saha bāndhavaiḥ
ṛtvijaḥ savasiṣṭhāśca mantravanmantrakovidāḥ

translations.english: Even here, O you cognizant of the Mantras, let all the subjects and the Rtvijas with Vasiștha, versed in the Mantras, install you.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिषिक्तस्त्वमस्माभिरयोध्यां पालने व्रज
विजित्य तरसा लोकान्मरुद्भिरिव वासवः
verses.transliteration:
abhiṣiktastvamasmābhirayodhyāṁ pālane vraja
vijitya tarasā lokānmarudbhiriva vāsavaḥ

translations.english: Having been installed, go to Ayodhyā for the purpose of governing it, having with our assistance conquered your enemies by they strength, like Vāsava conquering (his foes) with the help of the Maruts.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकुर्वन्दुर्हृदः साधु निर्दहन्
सुहृदस्तर्पयन्कामैस्त्वमेवात्रानुशाधि माम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṇāni trīṇyapākurvandurhṛdaḥ sādhu nirdahan
suhṛdastarpayankāmaistvamevātrānuśādhi mām

translations.english: Having freed yourself from the threefold debts, do you govern me, repressing your foes, and propitiating your friends with every gratification.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यार्य मुदिताः सन्तु सुहृदस्तेऽभिषेचने
अद्य भीताः पालयन्तां दुर्हृदस्ते दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
adyārya muditāḥ santu suhṛdaste'bhiṣecane
adya bhītāḥ pālayantāṁ durhṛdaste diśo daśa

translations.english: O noble one, to-day let your friends rejoice in consequence of your coronation. To day let those that intend to do you harm, being frightened, fly to the ten cardinal points.

verses.sanskrit:
आक्रोशं मम मातुश्च प्रमृज्य पुरुषर्षभ
अद्य तत्र भवन्तं च पितरं रक्ष किल्बिषात्
verses.transliteration:
ākrośaṁ mama mātuśca pramṛjya puruṣarṣabha
adya tatra bhavantaṁ ca pitaraṁ rakṣa kilbiṣāt

translations.english: O foremost of men, wiping out the disgrace of my mother, do you emancipate our sire from sin.

verses.sanskrit:
शिरसा त्वाभियाचेऽहं कुरुष्व करुणां मयि
बान्धवेषु च सर्वेषु भूतेष्विव महेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
śirasā tvābhiyāce'haṁ kuruṣva karuṇāṁ mayi
bāndhaveṣu ca sarveṣu bhūteṣviva maheśvaraḥ

translations.english: I beseech you with bent head. Be you merciful to me, to all our friends, and, O great lord, to all creatures in general.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा पृष्ठतः कृत्वा वनमेव भवानितः
गमिष्यति गमिष्यामि भवता सार्धमप्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā vanameva bhavānitaḥ
gamiṣyati gamiṣyāmi bhavatā sārdhamapyaham

translations.english: But, if disregarding my solicitations, you wend from here to the forest, I shall go along with you.

verses.sanskrit:
तथापि रामो भरतेन ताम्यत; प्रसाद्यमानः शिरसा महीपतिः
न चैव चक्रे गमनाय सत्त्ववा;न्मतिं पितुस्तद्वचने प्रतिष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
tathāpi rāmo bharatena tāmyata; prasādyamānaḥ śirasā mahīpatiḥ
na caiva cakre gamanāya sattvavā;nmatiṁ pitustadvacane pratiṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: Although thus besought and propitiated by Bharata with bent head, that lord of the earth, Rāma, possessed of strength, established in the words of his father, did not decide for going.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्भुतं स्थैर्यमवेक्ष्य राघवे; समं जनो हर्षमवाप दुःखितः
न यात्ययोध्यामिति दुःखितोऽभव;त्स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वमवेक्ष्य हर्षितः
verses.transliteration:
tadadbhutaṁ sthairyamavekṣya rāghave; samaṁ jano harṣamavāpa duḥkhitaḥ
na yātyayodhyāmiti duḥkhito'bhava;tsthirapratijñatvamavekṣya harṣitaḥ

translations.english: Witnessing that wonderful firmness in Rāghava, the people were at one and the same time delighted and depressed. They were aggrieved because he would not go to Ayodhyā; they rejoiced on seeing his firm resolution.

verses.sanskrit:
तमृत्विजो नैगमयूथवल्लभा;स्तथा विसंज्ञाश्रुकलाश्च मातरः
तथा ब्रुवाणं भरतं प्रतुष्टुवुः; प्रणम्य रामं च ययाचिरे सह
verses.transliteration:
tamṛtvijo naigamayūthavallabhā;stathā visaṁjñāśrukalāśca mātaraḥ
tathā bruvāṇaṁ bharataṁ pratuṣṭuvuḥ; praṇamya rāmaṁ ca yayācire saha

translations.english: Then the Rtvijas, the citizens, and their leaders, and the mothers with their senses lost and with tears in their eyes, extolled Bharata as he was speaking thus; and, bowing down to Rāma, they directed their solicitations together.

verses.sanskrit:
पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तु भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
प्रत्युवच ततः श्रीमाञ्ज्ञातिमध्येऽतिसत्कृतः
verses.transliteration:
punarevaṁ bruvāṇaṁ tu bharataṁ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
pratyuvaca tataḥ śrīmāñjñātimadhye'tisatkṛtaḥ
