translations.english: As Bharata was again ng in this strain, his graceful elder brother, having been highly honoured, answered Bharata in the midst of his relatives, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं यत्त्वमेवमभाषथाः
जातः पुत्रो दशरथात्कैकेय्यां राजसत्तमात्
verses.transliteration:
upapannamidaṁ vākyaṁ yattvamevamabhāṣathāḥ
jātaḥ putro daśarathātkaikeyyāṁ rājasattamāt

translations.english: Having been born as a son to Daśaratha, foremost of monarchs, by Kaikeyſ, this speech of yours is worthy of you.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा भ्रातः पिता नः स मातरं ते समुद्वहन्
मातामहे समाश्रौषीद्राज्यशुल्कमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
purā bhrātaḥ pitā naḥ sa mātaraṁ te samudvahan
mātāmahe samāśrauṣīdrājyaśulkamanuttamam

translations.english: O brother, formerly when our father espoused the hand of your mother, he promised her the kingdom as her marriage portion.

verses.sanskrit:
देवासुरे च संग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिवः
संप्रहृष्टो ददौ राजा वरमाराधितः प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
devāsure ca saṁgrāme jananyai tava pārthivaḥ
saṁprahṛṣṭo dadau rājā varamārādhitaḥ prabhuḥ

translations.english: Then on the occasion of the war between the gods and the Asuras, that master, the king, well pleased (with her), being besought, granted her a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सा संप्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी
अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sā saṁpratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī
ayācata naraśreṣṭhaṁ dvau varau varavarṇinī

translations.english: Having been thus promised, that virtuous lady, your illustrious mother, O foremost of men, asked for two boons (of the king), viz., your enthronement, O best of men, and my banishment. Thus besought by her, the king conferred on her the boon.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन पित्राहमप्यत्र नियुक्तः पुरुषर्षभ
चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वरदानिकम्
verses.transliteration:
tena pitrāhamapyatra niyuktaḥ puruṣarṣabha
caturdaśa vane vāsaṁ varṣāṇi varadānikam

translations.english: And, you foremost of men, I have been enjoyed by my sire to stay in the woods for fourteen years, in consequence of his having granted her the boon.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वितः
शीतया चाप्रतिद्वन्द्वः सत्यवादे स्थितः पितुः
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ vanamidaṁ prāpto nirjanaṁ lakṣmaṇānvitaḥ
śītayā cāpratidvandvaḥ satyavāde sthitaḥ pituḥ

translations.english: And, having, in company with Laksmana and Sītā, come to the lone forest, I in humble guise am staying in the truthful speech of my father.

verses.sanskrit:
भवानपि तथेत्येव पितरं सत्यवादिनम्
कर्तुमर्हति राजेन्द्रं क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचनात्
verses.transliteration:
bhavānapi tathetyeva pitaraṁ satyavādinam
kartumarhati rājendraṁ kṣipramevābhiṣecanāt

translations.english: You too, you foremost of kings, should in the same way speedily render our father truthful, by getting yourself installed.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋणान्मोचय राजानं मत्कृते भरत प्रभुम्
पितरं त्राहि धर्मज्ञ मातरं चाभिनन्दय
verses.transliteration:
ṛṇānmocaya rājānaṁ matkṛte bharata prabhum
pitaraṁ trāhi dharmajña mātaraṁ cābhinandaya

translations.english: O Bharata, for my sake, do you free that lord, the king, from his debts. Do you, O you cognizant of morality, deliver our father and gladden your mother.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयते हि पुरा तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विनी
गयेन यजमानेन गयेष्वेव पितॄन्प्रति
verses.transliteration:
śrūyate hi purā tāta śrutirgītā yaśasvinī
gayena yajamānena gayeṣveva pitṝnprati

translations.english: O child, we hear that in Gaya, formerly the famous Gaya, engaged in a sacrifice, chanted this Vedic hymn, for pleasing his departed ancestors.

verses.sanskrit:
पुं नाम्ना नरकाद्यस्मात्पितरं त्रायते सुतः
तस्मात्पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः पितॄन्यत्पाति वा सुतः
verses.transliteration:
puṁ nāmnā narakādyasmātpitaraṁ trāyate sutaḥ
tasmātputra iti proktaḥ pitṝnyatpāti vā sutaḥ

translations.english: Since a son delivers his sire form the hell named Put, a son goes by the appellation of putra, he protecting his (departed) ancestors in every way.

verses.sanskrit:
एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुताः
तेषां वै समवेतानामपि कश्चिद्गयां व्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā guṇavanto bahuśrutāḥ
teṣāṁ vai samavetānāmapi kaścidgayāṁ vrajet

translations.english: One should wish for many sons crowned with qualities and versed in various lore, for the chance is that one at least of these may repair to Gayā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं राजर्षयः सर्वे प्रतीता राजनन्दन
तस्मात्त्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात्प्रभो
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ rājarṣayaḥ sarve pratītā rājanandana
tasmāttrāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṁ narakātprabho

translations.english: O son of the Raghu race, the Rājarşis have delivered their decision on the point. Therefore, you foremost of men, do you, O lord, rescue your sire from hell.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्यां गच्छ भरत प्रकृतीरनुरञ्जय
शत्रुघ्न सहितो वीर सह सर्वैर्द्विजातिभिः
verses.transliteration:
ayodhyāṁ gaccha bharata prakṛtīranurañjaya
śatrughna sahito vīra saha sarvairdvijātibhiḥ

translations.english: O Bharata, go to Ayodhyā, and please the subjects, in company with Śatrughna, O hero, and all the regenerate ones.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवेक्ष्ये दण्डकारण्यमहमप्यविलम्बयन्
आभ्यां तु सहितो राजन्वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च
verses.transliteration:
pravekṣye daṇḍakāraṇyamahamapyavilambayan
ābhyāṁ tu sahito rājanvaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca

translations.english: I also, O hero, without delay shall have to enter the forest of Dandaka in company with Lakşmaņa and Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं राजा भव भरत स्वयं नराणां; वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम्
गच्छ त्वं पुरवरमद्य संप्रहृष्टः; संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान्प्रवेक्ष्ये
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ rājā bhava bharata svayaṁ narāṇāṁ; vanyānāmahamapi rājarāṇmṛgāṇām
gaccha tvaṁ puravaramadya saṁprahṛṣṭaḥ; saṁhṛṣṭastvahamapi daṇḍakānpravekṣye

translations.english: O Bharata, be you yourself the monarch of men. I shall become the king of kings of deer. Go you to that foremost of cities with a glad heart: with a glad heart will I enter Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
छायां ते दिनकरभाः प्रबाधमानं; वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम्
एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां; छायां तामतिशयिनीं सुखं श्रयिष्ये
verses.transliteration:
chāyāṁ te dinakarabhāḥ prabādhamānaṁ; varṣatraṁ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām
eteṣāmahamapi kānanadrumāṇāṁ; chāyāṁ tāmatiśayinīṁ sukhaṁ śrayiṣye

translations.english: O Bharata, let the umbrella barring out the rays of the sun, afford cool shade to your head: I shall happily seek the dense shade of these forest trees.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नः कुशलमतिस्तु ते सहायः; सौमित्रिर्मम विदितः प्रधानमित्रम्
चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं; सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषादम्
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnaḥ kuśalamatistu te sahāyaḥ; saumitrirmama viditaḥ pradhānamitram
catvārastanayavarā vayaṁ narendraṁ; satyasthaṁ bharata carāma mā viṣādam

translations.english: Śatrughna endued with cleverness is your helper: Sumitrā's son is well known as my best friend. We four worthy sons of that foremost of monarchs will keep him established in truth, O Bharata. Let not your mind despond.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्वासयन्तं भरतं जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः
उवाच रामं धर्मज्ञं धर्मापेतमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
āśvāsayantaṁ bharataṁ jābālirbrāhmaṇottamaḥ
uvāca rāmaṁ dharmajñaṁ dharmāpetamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: As Rāma cognizant of righteousness was thus encouraging Bharata, Jābāli, best of Brāhmaṇas, addressed him in words divorced from morality, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु राघव मा भूत्ते बुद्धिरेवं निरर्थका
प्राकृतस्य नरस्येव आर्य बुद्धेस्तपस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
sādhu rāghava mā bhūtte buddhirevaṁ nirarthakā
prākṛtasya narasyeva ārya buddhestapasvinaḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, endowed with a noble understanding and leading a life of asceticism, do not suffer your intellect to entertain inanities, like any low person.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्माता पिता चेति राम सज्जेत यो नरः
उन्मत्त इव स ज्ञेयो नास्ति काचिद्धि कस्यचित्
verses.transliteration:
tasmānmātā pitā ceti rāma sajjeta yo naraḥ
unmatta iva sa jñeyo nāsti kāciddhi kasyacit

translations.english: Who is whose friend? And to what is one entitled and by virtue of what relation? And who is such? Since a creature is born alone and dies alone, a person that cherishes his father and mother with affection, must, O Rāma, be looked upon as a madman.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु
आवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः
verses.transliteration:
evameva manuṣyāṇāṁ pitā mātā gṛhaṁ vasu
āvāsamātraṁ kākutstha sajjante nātra sajjanāḥ

translations.english: No individual has any one (in the world). As on the eve of setting out for another country, a person stays somewhere (outside the village he lives in), and the next day goes away, renouncing that abode, even such are a man's father and mother, house and wealth. O Kākutstha, worthy people never bear affection towards a mere abode.

verses.sanskrit:
पित्र्यं राज्यं समुत्सृज्य स नार्हति नरोत्तम
आस्थातुं कापथं दुःखं विषमं बहुकण्टकम्
verses.transliteration:
pitryaṁ rājyaṁ samutsṛjya sa nārhati narottama
āsthātuṁ kāpathaṁ duḥkhaṁ viṣamaṁ bahukaṇṭakam

translations.english: Therefore, O best of men, leaving your ancestral kingdom, you ought not to abide in the disagreeable forest filled with dangers and difficulties.

verses.sanskrit:
समृद्धायामयोध्यायामात्मानमभिषेचय
एकवेणीधरा हि त्वां नगरी संप्रतीक्षते
verses.transliteration:
samṛddhāyāmayodhyāyāmātmānamabhiṣecaya
ekaveṇīdharā hi tvāṁ nagarī saṁpratīkṣate

translations.english: Do you get yourself sprinkled in the prosperous Ayodhyā. The city expects you wearing a single woven braid.

verses.sanskrit:
राजभोगाननुभवन्महार्हान्पार्थिवात्मज
विहर त्वमयोध्यायां यथा शक्रस्त्रिविष्टपे
verses.transliteration:
rājabhogānanubhavanmahārhānpārthivātmaja
vihara tvamayodhyāyāṁ yathā śakrastriviṣṭape

translations.english: O king's son, enjoying costly regal pleasures, do you sport in Ayodhyā, like Sakra in the celestial regions.

verses.sanskrit:
न ते कश्चिद्दशरतःस्त्वं च तस्य न कश्चन
अन्यो राजा त्वमन्यश्च तस्मात्कुरु यदुच्यते
verses.transliteration:
na te kaściddaśarataḥstvaṁ ca tasya na kaścana
anyo rājā tvamanyaśca tasmātkuru yaducyate

translations.english: Dasaratha is none to you, and you too are none's to Dasaratha. He is quite other than your sire; and you have no connection with him. Therefore, do you act as I tell you.

verses.sanskrit:
गतः स नृपतिस्तत्र गन्तव्यं यत्र तेन वै
प्रवृत्तिरेषा मर्त्यानां त्वं तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
gataḥ sa nṛpatistatra gantavyaṁ yatra tena vai
pravṛttireṣā martyānāṁ tvaṁ tu mithyā vihanyase

translations.english: The king has gone the way he should. This is the nature of all creatures. But you for naught deny yourself (the manliness of monarchical power).

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थधर्मपरा ये ये तांस्ताञ्शोचामि नेतरान्
ते हि दुःखमिह प्राप्य विनाशं प्रेत्य भेजिरे
verses.transliteration:
arthadharmaparā ye ye tāṁstāñśocāmi netarān
te hi duḥkhamiha prāpya vināśaṁ pretya bhejire

translations.english: Those that disregarding interest are devoted to virtue, do I mourn, and not others; for having suffered misery here, they in the end meet with extinction.

verses.sanskrit:
अष्टका पितृदैवत्यमित्ययं प्रसृतो जनः
अन्नस्योपद्रवं पश्य मृतो हि किमशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
aṣṭakā pitṛdaivatyamityayaṁ prasṛto janaḥ
annasyopadravaṁ paśya mṛto hi kimaśiṣyati

translations.english: People engage in Aştaka* in behalf of ancestors and deities. Behold the waste of edibles. Does any dead person feed? *The lunar days and months for propitiating the manes.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि भुक्तमिहान्येन देहमन्यस्य गच्छति
दद्यात्प्रवसतः श्राद्धं न तत्पथ्यशनं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
yadi bhuktamihānyena dehamanyasya gacchati
dadyātpravasataḥ śrāddhaṁ na tatpathyaśanaṁ bhavet

translations.english: If food partaken by one is transferred to the body of another, offer Śrāddha to one going to a distant and, that shall serve for his provender on the way.

verses.sanskrit:
दानसंवनना ह्येते ग्रन्था मेधाविभिः कृताः
यजस्व देहि दीक्षस्व तपस्तप्यस्व संत्यज
verses.transliteration:
dānasaṁvananā hyete granthā medhāvibhiḥ kṛtāḥ
yajasva dehi dīkṣasva tapastapyasva saṁtyaja

translations.english: Works (on morality) enjoining, Worship,' 'Give away,' 'Be initiated,' 'Observe rites,' "Renounce', have been composed by intelligent persons, for inducing people to be charitable.

verses.sanskrit:
स नास्ति परमित्येव कुरु बुद्धिं महामते
प्रत्यक्षं यत्तदातिष्ठ परोक्षं पृष्ठतः कुरु
verses.transliteration:
sa nāsti paramityeva kuru buddhiṁ mahāmate
pratyakṣaṁ yattadātiṣṭha parokṣaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru

translations.english: O magnanimous one, assure yourself there is no hereafter. Do you remain grounded in the evident, turning your back on what is beyond our ken.

verses.sanskrit:
सतां बुद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वलोकनिदर्शिनीम्
राज्यं त्वं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भरतेन प्रसादितः
verses.transliteration:
satāṁ buddhiṁ puraskṛtya sarvalokanidarśinīm
rājyaṁ tvaṁ pratigṛhṇīṣva bharatena prasāditaḥ

translations.english: Placing in front the intellect of the good, and approved by all, do you, propitiated by Bharata, accept the monarchy.

verses.sanskrit:
जाबालेस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यात्मनां वरः
उवाच परया युक्त्या स्वबुद्ध्या चाविपन्नया
verses.transliteration:
jābālestu vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ satyātmanāṁ varaḥ
uvāca parayā yuktyā svabuddhyā cāvipannayā

translations.english: Hearing Jāvāli's words, Rāma having truth for prowess, by help of an exceedingly subtle intellect uninfluenced (under the exhortations of that sage), said.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्मे प्रियकामार्थं वचनं यदिहोक्तवान्
अकार्यं कार्यसंकाशमपथ्यं पथ्यसंमितम्
verses.transliteration:
bhavānme priyakāmārthaṁ vacanaṁ yadihoktavān
akāryaṁ kāryasaṁkāśamapathyaṁ pathyasaṁmitam

translations.english: What you, wishing for my welfare, have dwelt upon, though wearing the guise of a good action, is really not such; and though appearing to be beneficent, is really calculated to entail misery.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्मर्यादस्तु पुरुषः पापाचारसमन्वितः
मानं न लभते सत्सु भिन्नचारित्रदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
nirmaryādastu puruṣaḥ pāpācārasamanvitaḥ
mānaṁ na labhate satsu bhinnacāritradarśanaḥ

translations.english: The person that with his sinful acts sticking to him, walk astray, as well as he that hold up (to others) different patterns of character (from those recommended by scripture), does not win honour with the good.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्
चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्
verses.transliteration:
kulīnamakulīnaṁ vā vīraṁ puruṣamāninam
cāritrameva vyākhyāti śuciṁ vā yadi vāśucim

translations.english: One's character (fashioned according to scripture) shows whether one is high-born or base, heroic or vainly priding himself on his manliness, pure or impure.

verses.sanskrit:
अनार्यस्त्वार्यसंकाशः शौचाद्धीनस्तथा शुचिः
लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुःशीलः शीलवानिव
verses.transliteration:
anāryastvāryasaṁkāśaḥ śaucāddhīnastathā śuciḥ
lakṣaṇyavadalakṣaṇyo duḥśīlaḥ śīlavāniva

translations.english: (But by adopting the code of conduct inculcated by you), a mean character may appear as a noble one, one bereft of purity may appear pure, an inauspicious individual may seem auspicious, and one of vile ways may appear honest.

verses.sanskrit:
अधर्मं धर्मवेषेण यदीमं लोकसंकरम्
अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
adharmaṁ dharmaveṣeṇa yadīmaṁ lokasaṁkaram
abhipatsye śubhaṁ hitvā kriyāvidhivivarjitam

translations.english: If I adopt this unrighteous course, calculated to produce confusion of castes, and do acts not recognized by scripture, I shall, renouncing good, have to reap only evil. Then what man possessed of consciousness and capable of discriminating between right and wrong, shall honour me, given to wicked ways and deserving of universal reprehension?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य यास्याम्यहं वृत्तं केन वा स्वर्गमाप्नुयाम्
अनया वर्तमानोऽहं वृत्त्या हीनप्रतिज्ञया
verses.transliteration:
kasya yāsyāmyahaṁ vṛttaṁ kena vā svargamāpnuyām
anayā vartamāno'haṁ vṛttyā hīnapratijñayā

translations.english: Whose is this course (that you asked me to follow)? And by what way shall I attain heaven, by following the present course, which would make me give up my vow?

verses.sanskrit:
कामवृत्तस्त्वयं लोकः कृत्स्नः समुपवर्तते
यद्वृत्ताः सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ताः सन्ति हि प्रजाः
verses.transliteration:
kāmavṛttastvayaṁ lokaḥ kṛtsnaḥ samupavartate
yadvṛttāḥ santi rājānastadvṛttāḥ santi hi prajāḥ

translations.english: When I have (first) myself set up desire as my standard of action, the entire body of the people shall follow me: subjects take to the ways that have been adopted by their sovereigns.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यमेवानृशंस्यं च राजवृत्तं सनातनम्
तस्मात्सत्यात्मकं राज्यं सत्ये लोकः प्रतिष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
satyamevānṛśaṁsyaṁ ca rājavṛttaṁ sanātanam
tasmātsatyātmakaṁ rājyaṁ satye lokaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: This eternal regal morality founded in kindness towards the subjects, is verily true. Hence a kingdom is essentially based upon truth; and this world itself is established in truth.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च सत्यमेव हि मेनिरे
सत्यवादी हि लोकेऽस्मिन्परमं गच्छति क्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣayaścaiva devāśca satyameva hi menire
satyavādī hi loke'sminparamaṁ gacchati kṣayam

translations.english: Saints and celestials for certain regard truth alone. In this world a truthful person attains the regions of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्विजन्ते यथा सर्पान्नरादनृतवादिनः
धर्मः सत्यं परो लोके मूलं स्वर्गस्य चोच्यते
verses.transliteration:
udvijante yathā sarpānnarādanṛtavādinaḥ
dharmaḥ satyaṁ paro loke mūlaṁ svargasya cocyate

translations.english: Untruthful persons harass people as much as serpents. In this world virtue, which is said to be the root of everything, is itself established in truth.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्मा समाश्रिता
सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम्
verses.transliteration:
satyameveśvaro loke satyaṁ padmā samāśritā
satyamūlāni sarvāṇi satyānnāsti paraṁ padam

translations.english: In this world, truth is the Lord; in truth is established righteousness. Everything has truth for its basis. No condition is superior to truth.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्तमिष्टं हुतं चैव तप्तानि च तपांसि च
वेदाः सत्यप्रतिष्ठानास्तस्मात्सत्यपरो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
dattamiṣṭaṁ hutaṁ caiva taptāni ca tapāṁsi ca
vedāḥ satyapratiṣṭhānāstasmātsatyaparo bhavet

translations.english: The Veda, which inculcates gift, sacrifice homa, and asceticism, is based on truth. I never or

verses.sanskrit:
एकः पालयते लोकमेकः पालयते कुलम्
मज्जत्येको हि निरय एकः स्वर्गे महीयते
verses.transliteration:
ekaḥ pālayate lokamekaḥ pālayate kulam
majjatyeko hi niraya ekaḥ svarge mahīyate

translations.english: One protects men, another his family; one is plunged in hell, another is honoured in heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं पितुर्निदेशं तु किमर्थं नानुपालये
सत्यप्रतिश्रवः सत्यं सत्येन समयीकृतः
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ piturnideśaṁ tu kimarthaṁ nānupālaye
satyapratiśravaḥ satyaṁ satyena samayīkṛtaḥ

translations.english: Why should I not then obey the mandate of my father? My father was of truthful promise and of righteous ways and with the object of observing his promise, he laid on me this (for faithful performance).

verses.sanskrit:
नैव लोभान्न मोहाद्वा न चाज्ञानात्तमोन्वितः
सेतुं सत्यस्य भेत्स्यामि गुरोः सत्यप्रतिश्रवः
verses.transliteration:
naiva lobhānna mohādvā na cājñānāttamonvitaḥ
setuṁ satyasya bhetsyāmi guroḥ satyapratiśravaḥ

translations.english: Having promised to my superior with an oath, shall through covetousness forgetfulness or pride rive the bridge of truth.

verses.sanskrit:
असत्यसंधस्य सतश्चलस्यास्थिरचेतसः
नैव देवा न पितरः प्रतीच्छन्तीति नः श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
asatyasaṁdhasya sataścalasyāsthiracetasaḥ
naiva devā na pitaraḥ pratīcchantīti naḥ śrutam

translations.english: We have heard that the gods and the Pitrs do not accept offerings from one inclined to untruth, or who is unsteady and of volatile faculties.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्यगात्ममिमं धर्मं सत्यं पश्याम्यहं स्वयम्
भारः सत्पुरुषाचीर्णस्तदर्थमभिनन्द्यते
verses.transliteration:
pratyagātmamimaṁ dharmaṁ satyaṁ paśyāmyahaṁ svayam
bhāraḥ satpuruṣācīrṇastadarthamabhinandyate

translations.english: This duty of maintaining truth, whose influence radiates all over one's soul, I certainly find to be the prime one; and this burthen has (ere this) been borne by worthy people. And it is for this that I reverence the same.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षात्रं धर्ममहं त्यक्ष्ये ह्यधर्मं धर्मसंहितम्
क्षुद्रौर्नृशंसैर्लुब्धैश्च सेवितं पापकर्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
kṣātraṁ dharmamahaṁ tyakṣye hyadharmaṁ dharmasaṁhitam
kṣudraurnṛśaṁsairlubdhaiśca sevitaṁ pāpakarmabhiḥ

translations.english: I abjure that Ksatriya morality which, wearing the garb of righteousness, is in fact impiety, and which is pursued by the low-minded, or the wicked, or the covetous, or the sinful.

verses.sanskrit:
कायेन कुरुते पापं मनसा संप्रधार्य च
अनृतं जिह्वया चाह त्रिविधं कर्म पातकम्
verses.transliteration:
kāyena kurute pāpaṁ manasā saṁpradhārya ca
anṛtaṁ jihvayā cāha trividhaṁ karma pātakam

translations.english: A person commits a sin by means of his physique, but after he has accurately cast it in his mind; and he has also spoken an untruth with his tongue. Thus a sin is threefold.

verses.sanskrit:
भूमिः कीर्तिर्यशो लक्ष्मीः पुरुषं प्रार्थयन्ति हि
स्वर्गस्थं चानुबध्नन्ति सत्यमेव भजेत तत्
verses.transliteration:
bhūmiḥ kīrtiryaśo lakṣmīḥ puruṣaṁ prārthayanti hi
svargasthaṁ cānubadhnanti satyameva bhajeta tat

translations.english: The earth and fame and renown and auspiciousness pay court to the truthful person. The good follow truth, therefore even truth is to be sought by all).

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेष्ठं ह्यनार्यमेव स्याद्यद्भवानवधार्य माम्
आह युक्तिकरैर्वाक्यैरिदं भद्रं कुरुष्व ह
verses.transliteration:
śreṣṭhaṁ hyanāryameva syādyadbhavānavadhārya mām
āha yuktikarairvākyairidaṁ bhadraṁ kuruṣva ha

translations.english: Therefore the seemingly excellent thing that you, after having well ascertained it, have said to me in words informed with reason, 'You had rather do this', appears to me wanting in nobility.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं ह्यहं प्रतिज्ञाय वनवासमिमं गुरोः
भरतस्य करिष्यामि वचो हित्वा गुरोर्वचः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ hyahaṁ pratijñāya vanavāsamimaṁ guroḥ
bharatasya kariṣyāmi vaco hitvā gurorvacaḥ

translations.english: How, after having promised to my superior this exile of mine, shall I act up to Bharata's words, setting aside those of my superior?

verses.sanskrit:
स्थिरा मया प्रतिज्ञाता प्रतिज्ञा गुरुसंनिधौ
प्रहृष्टमानसा देवी कैकेयी चाभवत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
sthirā mayā pratijñātā pratijñā gurusaṁnidhau
prahṛṣṭamānasā devī kaikeyī cābhavattadā

translations.english: I having remained firm in the promise I had made to my superior, that noble lady, Kaikeyi, became exceedingly delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
वनवासं वसन्नेवं शुचिर्नियतभोजनः
मूलैः पुष्पैः फलैः पुण्यैः पितॄन्देवांश्च तर्पयन्
verses.transliteration:
vanavāsaṁ vasannevaṁ śucirniyatabhojanaḥ
mūlaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pitṝndevāṁśca tarpayan

translations.english: Living in the forest, pure, with regulated fare, I shall, propitiating the gods and the Pits with fruits, flowers and roots, (fulfil my vow).

verses.sanskrit:
संतुष्टपञ्चवर्गोऽहं लोकयात्रां प्रवर्तये
अकुहः श्रद्दधानः सन्कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
saṁtuṣṭapañcavargo'haṁ lokayātrāṁ pravartaye
akuhaḥ śraddadhānaḥ sankāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Satisfying the five classes,* I shall, retaining my simplicity and my religious faith and being able to distinguish between right and wrong, pass away the term (of banishment). * Prakrāmam, The commentator says that the word means, Cāndrāyaṇa and other rites.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मभूमिमिमां प्राप्य कर्तव्यं कर्म यच्छुभम्
अग्निर्वायुश्च सोमश्च कर्मणां फलभागिनः
verses.transliteration:
karmabhūmimimāṁ prāpya kartavyaṁ karma yacchubham
agnirvāyuśca somaśca karmaṇāṁ phalabhāginaḥ

translations.english: Having come to this scene of action, one should do that which is proper. Even Agni and Vāyu and Soma reap the fruits of their own acts.

verses.sanskrit:
शतं क्रतूनामाहृत्य देवराट्त्रिदिवं गतः
तपांस्युग्राणि चास्थाय दिवं याता महर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
śataṁ kratūnāmāhṛtya devarāṭtridivaṁ gataḥ
tapāṁsyugrāṇi cāsthāya divaṁ yātā maharṣayaḥ

translations.english: Having acquired the appellation of Satakratu, the sovereign of the celestials has gone to heaven; and, having performed rigid austerities, the Maharșis have attained the celestial regions.'

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यं च धर्मं च पराक्रमं च; भूतानुकम्पां प्रियवादितां च
द्विजातिदेवातिथिपूजनं च; पन्थानमाहुस्त्रिदिवस्य सन्तः
verses.transliteration:
satyaṁ ca dharmaṁ ca parākramaṁ ca; bhūtānukampāṁ priyavāditāṁ ca
dvijātidevātithipūjanaṁ ca; panthānamāhustridivasya santaḥ

translations.english: Truth, righteousness, prowess, kindness to creatures, fair spokeness, and worship of the twice-born ones, gods and guests, these have by the pious been styled the ways to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मे रताः सत्पुरुषैः समेता;स्तेजस्विनो दानगुणप्रधानाः
अहिंसका वीतमलाश्च लोके; भवन्ति पूज्या मुनयः प्रधानाः
verses.transliteration:
dharme ratāḥ satpuruṣaiḥ sametā;stejasvino dānaguṇapradhānāḥ
ahiṁsakā vītamalāśca loke; bhavanti pūjyā munayaḥ pradhānāḥ

translations.english: Therefore those Brahmanas, a men, who have spared life and in other ways practised morality, and have also given away in charity, performed austerities and served others, (perform sacrifices in consonance with Vedas). And principal ascetics engaged in religion, surrounded by the good, possessed of energy, having charity for their foremost attribute, void of envy, and their hearts free from all stain, are honoured in this world.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय रामं तु वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह
जाबालिरपि जानीते लोकस्यास्य गतागतिम्
निवर्तयितुकामस्तु त्वामेतद्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kruddhamājñāya rāmaṁ tu vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
jābālirapi jānīte lokasyāsya gatāgatim
nivartayitukāmastu tvāmetadvākyamabravīt

translations.english: Knowing that Rāma was wroth, Vasiştha said, Jābāli knows the departure of the creature to the next world and their return thence.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां लोकसमुत्पत्तिं लोकनाथ निबोध मे
सर्वं सलिलमेवासीत्पृथिवी यत्र निर्मिता
ततः समभवद्ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूर्दैवतैः सह
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ lokasamutpattiṁ lokanātha nibodha me
sarvaṁ salilamevāsītpṛthivī yatra nirmitā
tataḥ samabhavadbrahmā svayambhūrdaivataiḥ saha

translations.english: Water was everywhere. The earth was constructed therein. Then sprang the self-create Brahmā along with all the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
स वराहस्ततो भूत्वा प्रोज्जहार वसुंधराम्
असृजच्च जगत्सर्वं सह पुत्रैः कृतात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
sa varāhastato bhūtvā projjahāra vasuṁdharām
asṛjacca jagatsarvaṁ saha putraiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ

translations.english: Having become a boar, he raised up the earth, and along with his sons of subdued souls created everything.

verses.sanskrit:
आकाशप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्ययः
तस्मान्मरीचिः संजज्ञे मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
ākāśaprabhavo brahmā śāśvato nitya avyayaḥ
tasmānmarīciḥ saṁjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Brahma eternal, existing through all time and incapable of decay, sprang from the sky. From him Marici came into being, and Kaśyapa is Marici's son.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्येयं प्रथमं दत्ता समृद्धा मनुना मही
तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम्
verses.transliteration:
yasyeyaṁ prathamaṁ dattā samṛddhā manunā mahī
tamikṣvākumayodhyāyāṁ rājānaṁ viddhi pūrvakam

translations.english: Vivasvat drew his birth from Kaśyapa, and Manu from Vivasvat. Manu was formerly known as Prajāpati. Ikṣvāku is son to Manu; and this world was first conferred upon Ikşvāku by Manu. Do you know Ikşvāku as the first kind in Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुतः श्रीमान्कुक्षिरेवेति विश्रुतः
कुक्षेरथात्मजो वीरो विकुक्षिरुदपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākostu sutaḥ śrīmānkukṣireveti viśrutaḥ
kukṣerathātmajo vīro vikukṣirudapadyata

translations.english: The graceful Kukşi is known as the son of Iksvāku. And, O hero, Kuksi's son was Vikuksi.

verses.sanskrit:
विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजा बाणः पुत्रः प्रतापवान्
बाणस्य तु महाबाहुरनरण्यो महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
vikukṣestu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān
bāṇasya tu mahābāhuranaraṇyo mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Vikukși had the powerful Bāņa possessed of exceeding energy for his son. Bāna had the mighty-armed Anaranya of high austerities for his son.

verses.sanskrit:
नानावृष्टिर्बभूवास्मिन्न दुर्भिक्षं सतां वरे
अनरण्ये महाराजे तस्करो वापि कश्चन
verses.transliteration:
nānāvṛṣṭirbabhūvāsminna durbhikṣaṁ satāṁ vare
anaraṇye mahārāje taskaro vāpi kaścana

translations.english: During the time of that foremost of righteous person, the monarch Anaranya, drought or famine did not occur (in Ayodhyā); nor were there any thieves at that time.

verses.sanskrit:
अनरण्यान्महाबाहुः पृथू राजा बभूव ह
तस्मात्पृथोर्महाराजस्त्रिशङ्कुरुदपद्यत
स सत्यवचनाद्वीरः सशरीरो दिवं गतः
verses.transliteration:
anaraṇyānmahābāhuḥ pṛthū rājā babhūva ha
tasmātpṛthormahārājastriśaṅkurudapadyata
sa satyavacanādvīraḥ saśarīro divaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: O mighty king, from Anaranya sprang king Pșthu. From Pệthu sprang Trišanku of mighty energy.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिशङ्कोरभवत्सूनुर्धुन्धुमारो महायशाः
धुन्धुमारान्महातेजा युवनाश्वो व्यजायत
verses.transliteration:
triśaṅkorabhavatsūnurdhundhumāro mahāyaśāḥ
dhundhumārānmahātejā yuvanāśvo vyajāyata

translations.english: This hero by virtue of his truth telling went to heaven in person. Trisanku had the famous Dhundhumāra for his son; and from Dhundhumāra Yuvanāśva born. Yuvanāśva's son was the handsome Māndhătā; was and from Māndhātā Susandhi came into being. Susandhi had two sons; Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतात्तु महाबाहोरसितो नाम जायत
यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रवः
हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च शूराश्च शशबिन्दवः
verses.transliteration:
bharatāttu mahābāhorasito nāma jāyata
yasyaite pratirājāna udapadyanta śatravaḥ
haihayāstālajaṅghāśca śūrāśca śaśabindavaḥ

translations.english: Dhruvasandhi had the illustrious Bharata, destroyer of foes (for his son) From Bharata sprang Asita, to whom sprang these hostile kings as foes, Haihayas, Tālajanghas and Sasabindus, heroes all.

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्तु सर्वान्प्रतिव्यूह्य युद्धे राजा प्रवासितः
स च शैलवरे रम्ये बभूवाभिरतो मुनिः
द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुतिः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstu sarvānprativyūhya yuddhe rājā pravāsitaḥ
sa ca śailavare ramye babhūvābhirato muniḥ
dve cāsya bhārye garbhiṇyau babhūvaturiti śrutiḥ

translations.english: Having engaged with them in battle, the king was excited (by them). And on the romantic Himavat, he become engaged in asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
भार्गवश्च्यवनो नाम हिमवन्तमुपाश्रितः
तमृषिं समुपागम्य कालिन्दी त्वभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
bhārgavaścyavano nāma himavantamupāśritaḥ
tamṛṣiṁ samupāgamya kālindī tvabhyavādayat

translations.english: Bhrgu's son named Cyavana was at that time staying in Himavat. Appearing before the sage, Kalindi saluted him.

verses.sanskrit:
सपत्न्या तु गरस्तस्यै दत्तो गर्भजिघांसया
गरेण सह तेनैव जातः स सगरोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sapatnyā tu garastasyai datto garbhajighāṁsayā
gareṇa saha tenaiva jātaḥ sa sagaro'bhavat

translations.english: And because her co-wife, had given her poison for destroying her foetus, and as in consequence of this, he had come in contact with poison, he came to be allied Sagara.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा सगरो नाम यः समुद्रमखानयत्
इष्ट्वा पर्वणि वेगेन त्रासयन्तमिमाः प्रजाः
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā sagaro nāma yaḥ samudramakhānayat
iṣṭvā parvaṇi vegena trāsayantamimāḥ prajāḥ

translations.english: The name of that king is Sagara, who having been initiated in a sacrifice excavated the ocean, frightening the people with the vehemence of his operations.

verses.sanskrit:
असमञ्जस्तु पुत्रोऽभूत्सगरस्येति नः श्रुतम्
जीवन्नेव स पित्रा तु निरस्तः पापकर्मकृत्
verses.transliteration:
asamañjastu putro'bhūtsagarasyeti naḥ śrutam
jīvanneva sa pitrā tu nirastaḥ pāpakarmakṛt

translations.english: Asamañja is known to have been the son of Sagara. This wicked man while yet in life, was banished by his father.

verses.sanskrit:
अंशुमानिति पुत्रोऽभूदसमञ्जस्य वीर्यवान्
दिलीपोंऽशुमतः पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथः
verses.transliteration:
aṁśumāniti putro'bhūdasamañjasya vīryavān
dilīpoṁ'śumataḥ putro dilīpasya bhagīrathaḥ

translations.english: Asamanja's son was the puissant Ansumat. Dilipa is the son of Ansumat and Dilipa's son is Bhagiratha.

verses.sanskrit:
भगीरथात्ककुत्स्थस्तु काकुत्स्था येन तु स्मृताः
ककुत्स्थस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूद्रघुर्येन तु राघवः
verses.transliteration:
bhagīrathātkakutsthastu kākutsthā yena tu smṛtāḥ
kakutsthasya tu putro'bhūdraghuryena tu rāghavaḥ

translations.english: From Bhagiratha sprang Kakutstha; from whom the Kākutsthas came to be well known. Kakutstha had Raghu for his son; after whom have been named the Rāghavas.

verses.sanskrit:
रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्धः पुरुषादकः
कल्माषपादः सौदास इत्येवं प्रथितो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
raghostu putrastejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
kalmāṣapādaḥ saudāsa ityevaṁ prathito bhuvi

translations.english: Raghu's son is the energetic Pravědha, who are human beings. He is known on earth under such names as Kalmāşapāda, Saudāsa.

verses.sanskrit:
कल्माषपादपुत्रोऽभूच्छङ्खणस्त्विति विश्रुतः
यस्तु तद्वीर्यमासाद्य सहसेनो व्यनीनशत्
verses.transliteration:
kalmāṣapādaputro'bhūcchaṅkhaṇastviti viśrutaḥ
yastu tadvīryamāsādya sahaseno vyanīnaśat

translations.english: We have heard that Kalmāșapāda's son was Śarkhaņa, who having been endowed with prowess, found destruction along with his forces.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खणस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूच्छूरः श्रीमान्सुदर्शनः
सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्ण अग्निवर्षस्य शीघ्रगः
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhaṇasya tu putro'bhūcchūraḥ śrīmānsudarśanaḥ
sudarśanasyāgnivarṇa agnivarṣasya śīghragaḥ

translations.english: Sarkhana's son was the beautiful and heroic Sudarśana. Sudarśana's son was Agnivarṇa and Agnivarna's, Sighraga.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुकः
प्रशुश्रुकस्य पुत्रोऽभूदम्बरीषो महाद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
śīghragasya maruḥ putro maroḥ putraḥ praśuśrukaḥ
praśuśrukasya putro'bhūdambarīṣo mahādyutiḥ

translations.english: Śighraga's son was Maru, and Maru's Praśuśruva. Praśuśruva's son the magnanimous Ambarisa.

verses.sanskrit:
अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोऽभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः
नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः
verses.transliteration:
ambarīṣasya putro'bhūnnahuṣaḥ satyavikramaḥ
nahuṣasya ca nābhāgaḥ putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ

translations.english: Ambarīşa's son was Nahuşa having truth for his prowess. Nahușa's son was the exceedingly virtuous Nābhaga.

verses.sanskrit:
अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ
अजस्य चैव धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
ajaśca suvrataścaiva nābhāgasya sutāvubhau
ajasya caiva dharmātmā rājā daśarathaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Nābhāga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata. Aja's son was the virtuous king Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ज्येष्ठोऽसि दायादो राम इत्यभिविश्रुतः
तद्गृहाण स्वकं राज्यमवेक्षस्व जगन्नृप
verses.transliteration:
tasya jyeṣṭho'si dāyādo rāma ityabhiviśrutaḥ
tadgṛhāṇa svakaṁ rājyamavekṣasva jagannṛpa

translations.english: His eldest son are you celebrated under the name of Rāma. Do you receive your own kingdom and look after the world.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां हि सर्वेषां राजा भवति पूर्वजः
पूर्वजे नावरः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो राज्येऽभिषिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ hi sarveṣāṁ rājā bhavati pūrvajaḥ
pūrvaje nāvaraḥ putro jyeṣṭho rājye'bhiṣicyate

translations.english: Among the Ikșwākus, the first born becomes the sovereign. The first born existing, an inferior son cannot be installed in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
स राघवाणां कुलधर्ममात्मनः; सनातनं नाद्य विहातुमर्हसि
प्रभूतरत्नामनुशाधि मेदिनीं; प्रभूतराष्ट्रां पितृवन्महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāghavāṇāṁ kuladharmamātmanaḥ; sanātanaṁ nādya vihātumarhasi
prabhūtaratnāmanuśādhi medinīṁ; prabhūtarāṣṭrāṁ pitṛvanmahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: It therefore does not today behove you to depart from the ever existing morality of the descendants of Raghu. Do you rule this earth filled with gems, and furnished with high fame, do you like to a father govern her containing many kingdoms.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठस्तु तदा राममुक्त्वा राजपुरोहितः
अब्रवीद्धर्मसंयुक्तं पुनरेवापरं वचः
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhastu tadā rāmamuktvā rājapurohitaḥ
abravīddharmasaṁyuktaṁ punarevāparaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Having thus addressed Rāma, the royal priest Vasiștha again spoke to him words fraught with righteousness, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरुषस्येह जातस्य भवन्ति गुरवस्त्रयः
आचार्यश्चैव काकुत्स्थ पिता माता च राघव
verses.transliteration:
puruṣasyeha jātasya bhavanti guravastrayaḥ
ācāryaścaiva kākutstha pitā mātā ca rāghava

translations.english: To a man born there are three superiors, viz, the preceptor, O Kakutstha, and father and mother, O Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
पिता ह्येनं जनयति पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ
प्रज्ञां ददाति चाचार्यस्तस्मात्स गुरुरुच्यते
verses.transliteration:
pitā hyenaṁ janayati puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha
prajñāṁ dadāti cācāryastasmātsa gururucyate

translations.english: Oforemost of men, the father begets a person, the preceptor imparts wisdom and therefore is he called a superior.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेऽहं पितुराचार्यस्तव चैव परंतप
मम त्वं वचनं कुर्वन्नातिवर्तेः सतां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa te'haṁ piturācāryastava caiva paraṁtapa
mama tvaṁ vacanaṁ kurvannātivarteḥ satāṁ gatim

translations.english: I, O subduer of foes, have been the preceptor of both yourself and your father. By doing what I say, you will not lose the state of the righteous.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धाया धर्मशीलाया मातुर्नार्हस्यवर्तितुम्
अस्यास्तु वचनं कुर्वन्नातिवर्तेः सतां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛddhāyā dharmaśīlāyā māturnārhasyavartitum
asyāstu vacanaṁ kurvannātivarteḥ satāṁ gatim

translations.english: These courtiers of yours, these relatives, and these kings;, by protecting them virtuously you will not lose the state of the righteous. It does not behove you to disregard the words of your aged and virtuous mother. By doing her bidding you will not lose the state of the righteous.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्य वचः कुर्वन्याचमानस्य राघव
आत्मानं नातिवर्तेस्त्वं सत्यधर्मपराक्रम
verses.transliteration:
bharatasya vacaḥ kurvanyācamānasya rāghava
ātmānaṁ nātivartestvaṁ satyadharmaparākrama

translations.english: O Rāghava, by acting as Bharata, who is soliciting you, says, you having the morality of truth for your prowess, will not be frustrated of the state of the pious.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं मधुरमुक्तस्तु गुरुणा राघवः स्वयम्
प्रत्युवाच समासीनं वसिष्ठं पुरुषर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ madhuramuktastu guruṇā rāghavaḥ svayam
pratyuvāca samāsīnaṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ puruṣarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Thus sweetly addressed by his preceptor personally, that foremost of men, Rāghava, replied to Vasistha, seated with him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यन्मातापितरौ वृत्तं तनये कुरुतः सदा
न सुप्रतिकरं तत्तु मात्रा पित्रा च यत्कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
yanmātāpitarau vṛttaṁ tanaye kurutaḥ sadā
na supratikaraṁ tattu mātrā pitrā ca yatkṛtam

translations.english: What his father and mother always do in behalf of their son, and what they effect by way of provision and sleep and clothing and constant sweet speech, and sport, is difficult of being repaid.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि राजा जनयिता पिता दशरथो मम
आज्ञातं यन्मया तस्य न तन्मिथ्या भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sa hi rājā janayitā pitā daśaratho mama
ājñātaṁ yanmayā tasya na tanmithyā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Therefore, what my father, king Dasaratha has commanded me to do, must not be falsified.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण भरतः प्रत्यनन्तरम्
उवाच परमोदारः सूतं परमदुर्मनाः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa bharataḥ pratyanantaram
uvāca paramodāraḥ sūtaṁ paramadurmanāḥ

translations.english: Rāma having said this, the broad-breasted Bharata, extremely depressed spoke to the charioteer who was by, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाहारो निरालोको धनहीनो यथा द्विजः
शेष्ये पुरस्ताच्छालाया यावन्न प्रतियास्यति
verses.transliteration:
anāhāro nirāloko dhanahīno yathā dvijaḥ
śeṣye purastācchālāyā yāvanna pratiyāsyati

translations.english: O charioteer, do you speedily spread Kuša on the ground here. I will remain near the noble one until he be kindly disposed (towards me). Even as a twice born one deprived of his wealth Leith down (at the door of an unrighteous person), eschewing food and in darkness, will I lie down in front of this cottage, until he betakes himself back (to Ayodhyā)

verses.sanskrit:
स तु राममवेक्षन्तं सुमन्त्रं प्रेक्ष्य दुर्मनाः
कुशोत्तरमुपस्थाप्य भूमावेवास्तरत्स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu rāmamavekṣantaṁ sumantraṁ prekṣya durmanāḥ
kuśottaramupasthāpya bhūmāvevāstaratsvayam

translations.english: Then with a dispirited heart finding Sumantra looking up to Rāma, Bharata himself spread Kuśa and lay down upon it.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच महातेजा रामो राजर्षिसत्तमाः
किं मां भरत कुर्वाणं तात प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca mahātejā rāmo rājarṣisattamāḥ
kiṁ māṁ bharata kurvāṇaṁ tāta pratyupavekṣyasi

translations.english: To him spoke that foremost of Rājarşis, the highly energetic Rāma, O Bharata, my dear brother, what have I done that you have down by me?

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणो ह्येकपार्श्वेन नरान्रोद्धुमिहार्हति
न तु मूर्धावसिक्तानां विधिः प्रत्युपवेशने
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇo hyekapārśvena narānroddhumihārhati
na tu mūrdhāvasiktānāṁ vidhiḥ pratyupaveśane

translations.english: It is a Brāhmaṇa who alone can obstruct a person by lying down beside him; but there is no rule by which a member of the military class* can lie down (in this wise). *Murdhabhisikta, Murdha, the head; Abhisikta, sprinkled; kings being consecrated by having poured on their heads, while seated on a throne, prepared for the purpose, water from some sacred stream, mixed with honey, clarified butter, and spirituous liquor, as well as two sorts of grass and sprouts of corn; the term applies to the Kșetriya as identified with the king, the duties of royalty belonging specially to the military caste.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल हित्वैतद्दारुणं व्रतम्
पुरवर्यामितः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां याहि राघव
verses.transliteration:
uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla hitvaitaddāruṇaṁ vratam
puravaryāmitaḥ kṣipramayodhyāṁ yāhi rāghava

translations.english: O best of men, arise, renouncing this difficult vow; and, O descendant of Raghu, do you from hence take yourself to that best of cities, Ayodhyā,

verses.sanskrit:
आसीनस्त्वेव भरतः पौरजानपदं जनम्
उवाच सर्वतः प्रेक्ष्य किमार्यं नानुशासथ
verses.transliteration:
āsīnastveva bharataḥ paurajānapadaṁ janam
uvāca sarvataḥ prekṣya kimāryaṁ nānuśāsatha

translations.english: Being seated, Bharata, eyeing the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces, remarked, What for do you not solicit the noble one?

verses.sanskrit:
ते तमूचुर्महात्मानं पौरजानपदा जनाः
काकुत्स्थमभिजानीमः सम्यग्वदति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
te tamūcurmahātmānaṁ paurajānapadā janāḥ
kākutsthamabhijānīmaḥ samyagvadati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon the citizens and the dwellers of the provinces answered that high-souled one, saying, We perceive that the descendant of Raghu says to Kākutstha what is fit; and this exceedingly virtuous one stay by the words of his sire. Therefore we are incapable of suddenly saying anything.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामाज्ञाय वचनं रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
एवं निबोध वचनं सुहृदां धर्मचक्षुषाम्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmājñāya vacanaṁ rāmo vacanamabravīt
evaṁ nibodha vacanaṁ suhṛdāṁ dharmacakṣuṣām

translations.english: Hearing their speech, Rāma said, “Listen to the words of these friends having morality for their vision."

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्चैवोभयं श्रुत्वा सम्यक्संपश्य राघव
उत्तिष्ठ त्वं महाबाहो मां च स्पृश तथोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
etaccaivobhayaṁ śrutvā samyaksaṁpaśya rāghava
uttiṣṭha tvaṁ mahābāho māṁ ca spṛśa tathodakam

translations.english: And, O scion of the Raghu race, hearing their utterances as regards both yourself and me, do you decide. Arise, you mighty-armed one. Touch me and then water.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोत्थाय जलं स्पृष्ट्वा भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
शृण्वन्तु मे परिषदो मन्त्रिणः श्रेणयस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
athotthāya jalaṁ spṛṣṭvā bharato vākyamabravīt
śṛṇvantu me pariṣado mantriṇaḥ śreṇayastathā

translations.english: Thereat arising, Bharata, having touched water, said, You courtiers, and you ministers, listen to me! I did not wish for my paternal kingdom; nor did I sway my mother (towards obtaining the same); nor did I know that the exceedingly righteous Rāghava was to seek the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि त्ववश्यं वस्तव्यं कर्तव्यं च पितुर्वचः
अहमेव निवत्स्यामि चतुर्दश वने समाः
verses.transliteration:
yadi tvavaśyaṁ vastavyaṁ kartavyaṁ ca piturvacaḥ
ahameva nivatsyāmi caturdaśa vane samāḥ

translations.english: But if he must dwell here, and thus act out the mandate of our father, I also will abide in the forest for fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मात्मा तस्य तथ्येन भ्रातुर्वाक्येन विस्मितः
उवाच रामः संप्रेक्ष्य पौरजानपदं जनम्
verses.transliteration:
dharmātmā tasya tathyena bhrāturvākyena vismitaḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ saṁprekṣya paurajānapadaṁ janam

translations.english: Astonished at the determination of Bharata, the righteous Rāma eyeing the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces, said.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रीतमाहितं क्रीतं यत्पित्रा जीवता मम
न तल्लोपयितुं शक्यं मया वा भरतेन वा
verses.transliteration:
vikrītamāhitaṁ krītaṁ yatpitrā jīvatā mama
na tallopayituṁ śakyaṁ mayā vā bharatena vā

translations.english: Neither Bharata nor I can annual any sale or pledge or purchase effected by our father during his life.

verses.sanskrit:
उपधिर्न मया कार्यो वनवासे जुगुप्सितः
युक्तमुक्तं च कैकेय्या पित्रा मे सुकृतं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
upadhirna mayā kāryo vanavāse jugupsitaḥ
yuktamuktaṁ ca kaikeyyā pitrā me sukṛtaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: Therefore I ought not to accept any substitute for living in the woods, who can but contribute to my censure. Kaikeyi has spoken what is proper; and my father has acted well.

verses.sanskrit:
जानामि भरतं क्षान्तं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्
सर्वमेवात्र कल्याणं सत्यसंधे महात्मनि
verses.transliteration:
jānāmi bharataṁ kṣāntaṁ gurusatkārakāriṇam
sarvamevātra kalyāṇaṁ satyasaṁdhe mahātmani

translations.english: I know Bharata to be forgiving, and given to serving superiors. Everything in that high-souled one intent on truth appear beneficial.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन धर्मशीलेन वनात्प्रत्यागतः पुनः
भ्रात्रा सह भविष्यामि पृथिव्याः पतिरुत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
anena dharmaśīlena vanātpratyāgataḥ punaḥ
bhrātrā saha bhaviṣyāmi pṛthivyāḥ patiruttamaḥ

translations.english: Having returned from the forest, I will in company with this brother of virtuous character become the worthy master of this earth.

verses.sanskrit:
वृतो राजा हि कैकेय्या मया तद्वचनं कृतम्
अनृतान्मोचयानेन पितरं तं महीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛto rājā hi kaikeyyā mayā tadvacanaṁ kṛtam
anṛtānmocayānena pitaraṁ taṁ mahīpatim

translations.english: The king having been made by Kaikeyi to consent (to her proposal, I have done as she told me. Do you by acting in the way calculated to free that lord of the earth, our father (from the debt of promise), do so. company with this brother of virtuous character become the worthy master of this earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तमप्रतिमतेजोभ्यां भ्रातृभ्यां रोमहर्षणम्
विस्मिताः संगमं प्रेक्ष्य समवेता महर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
tamapratimatejobhyāṁ bhrātṛbhyāṁ romaharṣaṇam
vismitāḥ saṁgamaṁ prekṣya samavetā maharṣayaḥ

translations.english: Observing the meeting of the two brothers of unparalleled energy, capable of making one's hair stand on end, the Maharsis struck with surprise came to the scene.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तर्हितास्त्वृषिगणाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
तौ भ्रातरौ महात्मानौ काकुत्स्थौ प्रशशंसिरे
verses.transliteration:
antarhitāstvṛṣigaṇāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
tau bhrātarau mahātmānau kākutsthau praśaśaṁsire

translations.english: And remaining invisible, the ascetics, Siddhas and prime saints admired those brothers, the virtuous Käkutsthas.

verses.sanskrit:
स धन्यो यस्य पुत्रौ द्वौ धर्मज्ञौ धर्मविक्रमौ
श्रुत्वा वयं हि संभाषामुभयोः स्पृहयामहे
verses.transliteration:
sa dhanyo yasya putrau dvau dharmajñau dharmavikramau
śrutvā vayaṁ hi saṁbhāṣāmubhayoḥ spṛhayāmahe

translations.english: Blessed is he whose sons these, two cognizant of virtue and having truth for prowess are. Having heard their converse, we are delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वृषिगणाः क्षिप्रं दशग्रीववधैषिणः
भरतं राजशार्दूलमित्यूचुः संगता वचः
verses.transliteration:
tatastvṛṣigaṇāḥ kṣipraṁ daśagrīvavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
bharataṁ rājaśārdūlamityūcuḥ saṁgatā vacaḥ

translations.english: Then the saints, desirous of the destruction of the ten-headed one, having become unanimous, speedily addressed that foremost of monarchs, Bharata, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
कुले जात महाप्राज्ञ महावृत्त महायशः
ग्राह्यं रामस्य वाक्यं ते पितरं यद्यवेक्षसे
verses.transliteration:
kule jāta mahāprājña mahāvṛtta mahāyaśaḥ
grāhyaṁ rāmasya vākyaṁ te pitaraṁ yadyavekṣase

translations.english: Born in an illustrious line, endued with high wisdom, of high character and high fame, you should accept Rāma's words, in you have a care for the happiness of your sire.

verses.sanskrit:
सदानृणमिमं रामं वयमिच्छामहे पितुः
अनृणत्वाच्च कैकेय्याः स्वर्गं दशरथो गतः
verses.transliteration:
sadānṛṇamimaṁ rāmaṁ vayamicchāmahe pituḥ
anṛṇatvācca kaikeyyāḥ svargaṁ daśaratho gataḥ

translations.english: We wish that Rāma may always act truthfully in respect of his father. By virtue of this truth connected with Kaikeyi, Dasaratha has gone to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं गन्धर्वाः समहर्षयः
राजर्षयश्चैव तथा सर्वे स्वां स्वां गतिं गताः
verses.transliteration:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṁ gandharvāḥ samaharṣayaḥ
rājarṣayaścaiva tathā sarve svāṁ svāṁ gatiṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: Having said this, the Gandharvas, Maharsis, and Rājarșis each went to his proper quarter.

verses.sanskrit:
ह्लादितस्तेन वाक्येन शुभेन शुभदर्शनः
रामः संहृष्टवदनस्तानृषीनभ्यपूजयत्
verses.transliteration:
hlāditastena vākyena śubhena śubhadarśanaḥ
rāmaḥ saṁhṛṣṭavadanastānṛṣīnabhyapūjayat

translations.english: Having paid homage to those saints, Rāma possessed of a gracious presence, hearing their words, was filled with joy, and looked lovely with his delightful countenance.

verses.sanskrit:
स्रस्तगात्रस्तु भरतः स वाचा सज्जमानया
कृताञ्जलिरिदं वाक्यं राघवं पुनरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
srastagātrastu bharataḥ sa vācā sajjamānayā
kṛtāñjaliridaṁ vākyaṁ rāghavaṁ punarabravīt

translations.english: But with his frame agitated (with emotion), Bharata with joined hands again addressed Rāghava in words faltering (with feeling).

verses.sanskrit:
राजधर्ममनुप्रेक्ष्य कुलधर्मानुसंततिम्
कर्तुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ मम मातुश्च याचनाम्
verses.transliteration:
rājadharmamanuprekṣya kuladharmānusaṁtatim
kartumarhasi kākutstha mama mātuśca yācanām

translations.english: O Rāma, taking into account the morality of this race, it behoves you to act in accordance with the solicitations of my mother (and yours).

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षितुं सुमहद्राज्यमहमेकस्तु नोत्सहे
पौरजानपदांश्चापि रक्तान्रञ्जयितुं तथा
verses.transliteration:
rakṣituṁ sumahadrājyamahamekastu notsahe
paurajānapadāṁścāpi raktānrañjayituṁ tathā

translations.english: I do not venture to govern this vast kingdom alone, or please the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces attached to you.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञातयश्च हि योधाश्च मित्राणि सुहृदश्च नः
त्वामेव प्रतिकाङ्क्षन्ते पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकाः
verses.transliteration:
jñātayaśca hi yodhāśca mitrāṇi suhṛdaśca naḥ
tvāmeva pratikāṅkṣante parjanyamiva karṣakāḥ

translations.english: And as husbandmen remain expecting rain, our kindred, and warriors and friends and adherents wait in expectation of you.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं राज्यं महाप्राज्ञ स्थापय प्रतिपद्य हि
शक्तिमानसि काकुत्स्थ लोकस्य परिपालने
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ rājyaṁ mahāprājña sthāpaya pratipadya hi
śaktimānasi kākutstha lokasya paripālane

translations.english: O exceedingly wise one, accepting the kingdom, do you place it in the hands of some person. O Kākutstha, whomsoever you will chose for performing this office, will surely prove strong enough to govern the people.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा न्यपतद्भ्रातुः पादयोर्भरतस्तदा
भृशं संप्रार्थयामास राममेवं प्रियं वदः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā nyapatadbhrātuḥ pādayorbharatastadā
bhṛśaṁ saṁprārthayāmāsa rāmamevaṁ priyaṁ vadaḥ

translations.english: Having said this, Bharata fell at his brother's feet; and sweetly addressing him, O Rāghava, solicited him once again.

verses.sanskrit:
तमङ्के भ्रातरं कृत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
श्यामं नलिनपत्राक्षं मत्तहंसस्वरः स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tamaṅke bhrātaraṁ kṛtvā rāmo vacanamabravīt
śyāmaṁ nalinapatrākṣaṁ mattahaṁsasvaraḥ svayam

translations.english: Taking on his lap that sable-hued on furnished with eyes resembling lotus-leaves, Rāma with a voice like that of a mad swan, spoke to (Bharata).

verses.sanskrit:
आगता त्वामियं बुद्धिः स्वजा वैनयिकी च या
भृशमुत्सहसे तात रक्षितुं पृथिवीमपि
verses.transliteration:
āgatā tvāmiyaṁ buddhiḥ svajā vainayikī ca yā
bhṛśamutsahase tāta rakṣituṁ pṛthivīmapi

translations.english: You have at length attained the mental attitude that is natural and that also comes of the training one receives at the hands of his preceptor. And brother you venture greatly to protect the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अमात्यैश्च सुहृद्भिश्च बुद्धिमद्भिश्च मन्त्रिभिः
सर्वकार्याणि संमन्त्र्य सुमहान्त्यपि कारय
verses.transliteration:
amātyaiśca suhṛdbhiśca buddhimadbhiśca mantribhiḥ
sarvakāryāṇi saṁmantrya sumahāntyapi kāraya

translations.english: Taking counsel with courtiers, adherents and intelligent ministers, do you achieve grand tasks.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद्वा हिमवान्वा हिमं त्यजेत्
अतीयात्सागरो वेलां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmīścandrādapeyādvā himavānvā himaṁ tyajet
atīyātsāgaro velāṁ na pratijñāmahaṁ pituḥ

translations.english: Even if beauty forsake the moon, or Himavat his snow, or the ocean overleaps its shores, I shall not forsake the promise of my sire.

verses.sanskrit:
कामाद्वा तात लोभाद्वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्
न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्
verses.transliteration:
kāmādvā tāta lobhādvā mātrā tubhyamidaṁ kṛtam
na tanmanasi kartavyaṁ vartitavyaṁ ca mātṛvat

translations.english: My brother, you ought not to cherish in your mind what your mother incited by covetousness or affection for you has done; and you should act by her as one should by one's mother.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं भरतः कौसल्यासुतमब्रवीत्
तेजसादित्यसंकाशं प्रतिपच्चन्द्रदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ bharataḥ kausalyāsutamabravīt
tejasādityasaṁkāśaṁ pratipaccandradarśanam

translations.english: When Rāma resembling the sun in energy and like the moon of Pratipat in appearance, had said this, Bharata said to the son of Kausalya.

verses.sanskrit:
अधिरोहार्य पादाभ्यां पादुके हेमभूषिते
एते हि सर्वलोकस्य योगक्षेमं विधास्यतः
verses.transliteration:
adhirohārya pādābhyāṁ pāduke hemabhūṣite
ete hi sarvalokasya yogakṣemaṁ vidhāsyataḥ

translations.english: O noble one, do you take off your feet your sandals adorned with gold. These shall protect what the people have got and secure to you what they lack.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽधिरुह्य नरव्याघ्रः पादुके ह्यवरुह्य च
प्रायच्छत्सुमहातेजा भरताय महात्मने
verses.transliteration:
so'dhiruhya naravyāghraḥ pāduke hyavaruhya ca
prāyacchatsumahātejā bharatāya mahātmane

translations.english: Thereupon taking off his sandals, that highly energetic one gave them to the magnanimous Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
स पादुके ते भरतः प्रतापवा;न्स्वलंकृते संपरिगृह्य धर्मवित्
प्रदक्षिणं चैव चकार राघवं; चकार चैवोत्तमनागमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
sa pāduke te bharataḥ pratāpavā;nsvalaṁkṛte saṁparigṛhya dharmavit
pradakṣiṇaṁ caiva cakāra rāghavaṁ; cakāra caivottamanāgamūrdhani

translations.english: Then accepting those burnished and garnished sandals, Bharata versed in morality circumabulated Rāghava, and placed the sandals on the head of an excellent elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
अथानुपूर्व्यात्प्रतिपूज्य तं जनं; गुरूंश्च मन्त्रिप्रकृतीस्तथानुजौ
व्यसर्जयद्राघववंशवर्धनः; स्थितः स्वधर्मे हिमवानिवाचलः
verses.transliteration:
athānupūrvyātpratipūjya taṁ janaṁ; gurūṁśca mantriprakṛtīstathānujau
vyasarjayadrāghavavaṁśavardhanaḥ; sthitaḥ svadharme himavānivācalaḥ

translations.english: Then having one by one honoured that assembly, and his preceptor and the counsellors, and the subjects and his younger brothers, perpetuator of the Raghu race, steady in his own duty like. Himavat itself, took leave of them.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मातरो बाष्पगृहीतकण्ठो; दुःखेन नामन्त्रयितुं हि शेकुः
स त्वेव मातॄरभिवाद्य सर्वा; रुदन्कुटीं स्वां प्रविवेश रामः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ mātaro bāṣpagṛhītakaṇṭho; duḥkhena nāmantrayituṁ hi śekuḥ
sa tveva mātṝrabhivādya sarvā; rudankuṭīṁ svāṁ praviveśa rāmaḥ

translations.english: His mothers with their throats invaded by the vapour of grief could not from distress of heart say ought to him. And Rāma also having paid homage to all of them, weeping entered his own cottage.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शिरसि कृत्वा तु पादुके भरतस्तदा
आरुरोह रथं हृष्टः शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śirasi kṛtvā tu pāduke bharatastadā
āruroha rathaṁ hṛṣṭaḥ śatrughnena samanvitaḥ

translations.english: Then taking the pair of sandals on his head, Bharata in company with Śatrughna well pleased, ascended the car.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिश्च दृढव्रतः
अग्रतः प्रययुः सर्वे मन्त्रिणो मन्त्रपूजिताः
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭho vāmadevaśca jābāliśca dṛḍhavrataḥ
agrataḥ prayayuḥ sarve mantriṇo mantrapūjitāḥ

translations.english: And Vasiştha, and Vāmadeva and Jāvāli steady his vow as well as the minister, honoured on account of their counsels, went before.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्दाकिनीं नदीं रम्यां प्राङ्मुखास्ते ययुस्तदा
प्रदक्षिणं च कुर्वाणाश्चित्रकूटं महागिरिम्
verses.transliteration:
mandākinīṁ nadīṁ ramyāṁ prāṅmukhāste yayustadā
pradakṣiṇaṁ ca kurvāṇāścitrakūṭaṁ mahāgirim

translations.english: And going round the charming Mandākinī, they went eastwards, circumambulating (at the same time) the mighty hill, Citrakuta.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्यन्धातुसहस्राणि रम्याणि विविधानि च
प्रययौ तस्य पार्श्वेन ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
paśyandhātusahasrāṇi ramyāṇi vividhāni ca
prayayau tasya pārśvena sasainyo bharatastadā

translations.english: And beholding various kinds of beautiful minerals by thousand. Bharata accompanied by his army went by the side (of the hill).

verses.sanskrit:
अदूराच्चित्रकूटस्य ददर्श भरतस्तदा
आश्रमं यत्र स मुनिर्भरद्वाजः कृतालयः
verses.transliteration:
adūrāccitrakūṭasya dadarśa bharatastadā
āśramaṁ yatra sa munirbharadvājaḥ kṛtālayaḥ

translations.english: At a short distance from Citrakuța, Bharata beheld the spot where the ascetic Bharadvāja had built his habitation.

verses.sanskrit:
स तमाश्रममागम्य भरद्वाजस्य बुद्धिमान्
अवतीर्य रथात्पादौ ववन्दे कुलनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tamāśramamāgamya bharadvājasya buddhimān
avatīrya rathātpādau vavande kulanandanaḥ

translations.english: Approaching the asylum, the puissant Bharata descended from the car, and the son of Raghu then paid homage to the saint's feet.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हृष्टो भरद्वाजो भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
अपि कृत्यं कृतं तात रामेण च समागतम्
verses.transliteration:
tato hṛṣṭo bharadvājo bharataṁ vākyamabravīt
api kṛtyaṁ kṛtaṁ tāta rāmeṇa ca samāgatam

translations.english: Thereat Bharadvāja well pleased said, Have you, my child, on meeting with Rama, done what it behoved you to do?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो भरद्वाजेन धीमता
प्रत्युवाच भरद्वाजं भरतो धर्मवत्सलः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu bharato bharadvājena dhīmatā
pratyuvāca bharadvājaṁ bharato dharmavatsalaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the intelligent Bharadvāja, Bharata attached to righteousness answered the former, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
स याच्यमानो गुरुणा मया च दृढविक्रमः
राघवः परमप्रीतो वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa yācyamāno guruṇā mayā ca dṛḍhavikramaḥ
rāghavaḥ paramaprīto vasiṣṭhaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Solicited by our preceptor as well as by myself, Rāghava of steady prowess highly pleased spoke to Vasiștha.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुः प्रतिज्ञां तामेव पालयिष्यामि तत्त्वतः
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि य प्रतिज्ञा पितुर्मम
verses.transliteration:
pituḥ pratijñāṁ tāmeva pālayiṣyāmi tattvataḥ
caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi ya pratijñā piturmama

translations.english: I would faithfully perform my father's promise for fourteen years; for even this is the promise of my father.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो महाप्राज्ञो वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं राघवं वचनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
evamukto mahāprājño vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
vākyajño vākyakuśalaṁ rāghavaṁ vacanaṁ mahat

translations.english: Thus accosted, the eminently wise Vasiștha skilled in speech replied to Rāghava in these pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit:
एते प्रयच्छ संहृष्टः पादुके हेमभूषिते
अयोध्यायां महाप्राज्ञ योगक्षेमकरे तव
verses.transliteration:
ete prayaccha saṁhṛṣṭaḥ pāduke hemabhūṣite
ayodhyāyāṁ mahāprājña yogakṣemakare tava

translations.english: Do you well pleased confer (on Bharata) your sandals decked in gold. Thereby, exceedingly wise one, you will be able to protect what the people have and secure to them what they have not.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन राघवः प्राङ्मुखः स्थितः
पादुके हेमविकृते मम राज्याय ते ददौ
verses.transliteration:
evamukto vasiṣṭhena rāghavaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ sthitaḥ
pāduke hemavikṛte mama rājyāya te dadau

translations.english: Thus addressed by Vasiştha, Rāghava facing the east, conferred on me his sandals decked in gold, in order that I mighty carry on the government of the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
निवृत्तोऽहमनुज्ञातो रामेण सुमहात्मना
अयोध्यामेव गच्छामि गृहीत्वा पादुके शुभे
verses.transliteration:
nivṛtto'hamanujñāto rāmeṇa sumahātmanā
ayodhyāmeva gacchāmi gṛhītvā pāduke śubhe

translations.english: Commanded by the magnanimous Rāma, I retrace my steps. I will go to Ayodhyā, taking the sandals along with me.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः
भरद्वाजः शुभतरं मुनिर्वाक्यमुदाहरत्
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā śubhaṁ vākyaṁ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
bharadvājaḥ śubhataraṁ munirvākyamudāharat

translations.english: Hearing these auspicious words of the highsouled Bharata, the ascetic Bharadvāja said to Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतच्चित्रं नरव्याघ्र शीलवृत्तवतां वर
यदार्यं त्वयि तिष्ठेत्तु निम्ने वृष्टिमिवोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
naitaccitraṁ naravyāghra śīlavṛttavatāṁ vara
yadāryaṁ tvayi tiṣṭhettu nimne vṛṣṭimivodakam

translations.english: It is no wonder that Rāma has acted nobly by you, foremost among men and possessed of an (excellent) character and disposition, even as water poured out, flow downwards.

verses.sanskrit:
अमृतः स महाबाहुः पिता दशरथस्तव
यस्य त्वमीदृशः पुत्रो धर्मात्मा धर्मवत्सलः
verses.transliteration:
amṛtaḥ sa mahābāhuḥ pitā daśarathastava
yasya tvamīdṛśaḥ putro dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ

translations.english: Your father Dasaratha has become freed from his debts, since he has a son like to you, righteous and attached to virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
तमृषिं तु महात्मानमुक्तवाक्यं कृताञ्जलिः
आमन्त्रयितुमारेभे चरणावुपगृह्य च
verses.transliteration:
tamṛṣiṁ tu mahātmānamuktavākyaṁ kṛtāñjaliḥ
āmantrayitumārebhe caraṇāvupagṛhya ca

translations.english: When the ascetic had said this, Bharata with joined palms paid his respects to that highly wise one, by taking hold of his feet.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा भरद्वाजं पुनः पुनः
भरतस्तु ययौ श्रीमानयोध्यां सह मन्त्रिभिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṁ kṛtvā bharadvājaṁ punaḥ punaḥ
bharatastu yayau śrīmānayodhyāṁ saha mantribhiḥ

translations.english: And after having again and again gone round Bharadvāja, the graceful Bharata went to Ayodhyā accompanied by his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
यानैश्च शकटैश्चैव हयैश्नागैश्च सा चमूः
पुनर्निवृत्ता विस्तीर्णा भरतस्यानुयायिनी
verses.transliteration:
yānaiśca śakaṭaiścaiva hayaiśnāgaiśca sā camūḥ
punarnivṛttā vistīrṇā bharatasyānuyāyinī

translations.english: And returning by means of cars and carts, horses and elephants, that army marching in the wake of Bharata, spread wide.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते यमुनां दिव्यां नदीं तीर्त्वोर्मिमालिनीम्
ददृशुस्तां पुनः सर्वे गङ्गां शिवजलां नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
tataste yamunāṁ divyāṁ nadīṁ tīrtvormimālinīm
dadṛśustāṁ punaḥ sarve gaṅgāṁ śivajalāṁ nadīm

translations.english: And after having crossed the beautiful river Yamunā flowing in waves, they again beheld the river Gangā of auspicious waters.

verses.sanskrit:
तां रम्यजलसंपूर्णां संतीर्य सह बान्धवः
शृङ्गवेरपुरं रम्यं प्रविवेश ससैनिकः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ ramyajalasaṁpūrṇāṁ saṁtīrya saha bāndhavaḥ
śṛṅgaverapuraṁ ramyaṁ praviveśa sasainikaḥ

translations.english: And having along with his friend crossed over that river filled with beautiful waters, Bharata together with his army entered the charming city of Srigavera.

verses.sanskrit:
शृङ्गवेरपुराद्भूय अयोध्यां संददर्श ह
भरतो दुःखसंतप्तः सारथिं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śṛṅgaverapurādbhūya ayodhyāṁ saṁdadarśa ha
bharato duḥkhasaṁtaptaḥ sārathiṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: And from the city of Śộngava he went to Ayodhyā and again beheld it. And seeing Ayodhyā bereft of his father and mother, Bharata burning in grief, said to the charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
सारथे पश्य विध्वस्ता अयोध्या न प्रकाशते
निराकारा निरानन्दा दीना प्रतिहतस्वना
verses.transliteration:
sārathe paśya vidhvastā ayodhyā na prakāśate
nirākārā nirānandā dīnā pratihatasvanā

translations.english: O charioteer, behold that Ayodhyā, which shorn of its splendour and decorations, and plunged in grief, forlorn and silent, does not appear delightful.

verses.sanskrit:
स्निग्धगम्भीरघोषेण स्यन्दनेनोपयान्प्रभुः
अयोध्यां भरतः क्षिप्रं प्रविवेश महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
snigdhagambhīraghoṣeṇa syandanenopayānprabhuḥ
ayodhyāṁ bharataḥ kṣipraṁ praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Arriving by means of a car emitting a low and solemn sound, that lord, the highly famous Bharata speedily entered Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
राहुशत्रोः प्रियां पत्नीं श्रिया प्रज्वलितप्रभाम्
ग्रहेणाभ्युत्थितेनैकां रोहिणीमिव पीडिताम्
verses.transliteration:
rāhuśatroḥ priyāṁ patnīṁ śriyā prajvalitaprabhām
graheṇābhyutthitenaikāṁ rohiṇīmiva pīḍitām

translations.english: Ranged by cats and owls, with the doors of the people's dwellings remaining closed; like a night enveloped in darkness gloomy; and invisible; resembling the beloved wife of Rāhu's enemy, Rohini, brilliant with the lustre of the latter, when she is forlorn in consequence of her lover being afflicted by that planet.

verses.sanskrit:
अल्पोष्णक्षुब्धसलिलां घर्मोत्तप्तविहंगमाम्
लीनमीनझषग्राहां कृशां गिरिनदीमिव
verses.transliteration:
alpoṣṇakṣubdhasalilāṁ gharmottaptavihaṁgamām
līnamīnajhaṣagrāhāṁ kṛśāṁ girinadīmiva

translations.english: Like to a mountain stream shrunk up, having its waters turbid and slightly heated, and its fowls burning in the heat; and with its fishes, alligators and other aquatic animals rendered lean.

verses.sanskrit:
विधूमामिव हेमाभामध्वराग्निसमुत्थिताम्
हविरभ्युक्षितां पश्चाच्छिखां विप्रलयं गताम्
verses.transliteration:
vidhūmāmiva hemābhāmadhvarāgnisamutthitām
havirabhyukṣitāṁ paścācchikhāṁ vipralayaṁ gatām

translations.english: Resembling a flame of fire devoid of smoke and streaming up in golden splendour, next sprinkled with clarified butter, and lastly appearing with its crest extinguished.

verses.sanskrit:
विध्वस्तकवचां रुग्णगजवाजिरथध्वजाम्
हतप्रवीरामापन्नां चमूमिव महाहवे
verses.transliteration:
vidhvastakavacāṁ rugṇagajavājirathadhvajām
hatapravīrāmāpannāṁ camūmiva mahāhave

translations.english: With armour scattered all round, and sick elephants and horses and cars and standards, and heroes lying dead, in distress.

verses.sanskrit:
सफेनां सस्वनां भूत्वा सागरस्य समुत्थिताम्
प्रशान्तमारुतोद्धूतां जलोर्मिमिव निःस्वनाम्
verses.transliteration:
saphenāṁ sasvanāṁ bhūtvā sāgarasya samutthitām
praśāntamārutoddhūtāṁ jalormimiva niḥsvanām

translations.english: Like to an army in a mighty encounter; resembling the silent ripples of the ocean raised by the gentle breeze which ere now (in the shapes of surges) were heaving, brimming over with foam and sending forth roars.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्तां यज्ञायुधैः सर्वैरभिरूपैश्च याजकैः
सुत्याकाले विनिर्वृत्ते वेदिं गतरवामिव
verses.transliteration:
tyaktāṁ yajñāyudhaiḥ sarvairabhirūpaiśca yājakaiḥ
sutyākāle vinirvṛtte vediṁ gataravāmiva

translations.english: Like a silent dais after the sacrifice is over, without the sacrificial appurtenances, without worthy priests.

verses.sanskrit:
गोष्ठमध्ये स्थितामार्तामचरन्तीं नवं तृणम्
गोवृषेण परित्यक्तां गवां पत्नीमिवोत्सुकाम्
verses.transliteration:
goṣṭhamadhye sthitāmārtāmacarantīṁ navaṁ tṛṇam
govṛṣeṇa parityaktāṁ gavāṁ patnīmivotsukām

translations.english: Like to the wife of a youthful ox, exercised with anxiety on having been forsaken by her favourite ox, staying in distress in a pen, abstaining from fresh grass.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभाकरालैः सुस्निग्धैः प्रज्वलद्भिरिवोत्तमैः
वियुक्तां मणिभिर्जात्यैर्नवां मुक्तावलीमिव
verses.transliteration:
prabhākarālaiḥ susnigdhaiḥ prajvaladbhirivottamaiḥ
viyuktāṁ maṇibhirjātyairnavāṁ muktāvalīmiva

translations.english: Like to a string of new pearls divorced from noble, mild-gleaming rubies and other excellent gems.

verses.sanskrit:
सहसा चलितां स्थानान्महीं पुण्यक्षयाद्गताम्
संहृतद्युतिविस्तारां तारामिव दिवश्च्युताम्
verses.transliteration:
sahasā calitāṁ sthānānmahīṁ puṇyakṣayādgatām
saṁhṛtadyutivistārāṁ tārāmiva divaścyutām

translations.english: Like a star on the expiration of its virtue, moving from its place and dislodged from heaven, dropping to the earth with its brightness contracted.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पनद्धां वसन्तान्ते मत्तभ्रमरशालिनीम्
द्रुतदावाग्निविप्लुष्टां क्लान्तां वनलतामिव
verses.transliteration:
puṣpanaddhāṁ vasantānte mattabhramaraśālinīm
drutadāvāgnivipluṣṭāṁ klāntāṁ vanalatāmiva

translations.english: Like a blossoming creeper at the end of spring with maddened Bhramaras* suddenly rendered nerveless in consequence of being caught by a forest fire. *Black bees.

verses.sanskrit:
संमूढनिगमां सर्वां संक्षिप्तविपणापणाम्
प्रच्छन्नशशिनक्षत्रां द्यामिवाम्बुधरैर्वृताम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁmūḍhanigamāṁ sarvāṁ saṁkṣiptavipaṇāpaṇām
pracchannaśaśinakṣatrāṁ dyāmivāmbudharairvṛtām

translations.english: With her merchants plunged in grief, and her shops and stalls closed; like the welkin covered with clouds, and having its moon and stars hid.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षीणपानोत्तमैर्भिन्नैः शरावैरभिसंवृताम्
हतशौण्डामिवाकाशे पानभूमिमसंस्कृताम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣīṇapānottamairbhinnaiḥ śarāvairabhisaṁvṛtām
hataśauṇḍāmivākāśe pānabhūmimasaṁskṛtām

translations.english: Like an unclean, uncovered spot used for drinking, with all the wine drained, and scattered with broken bowls, and with the tipplers lying dead.

verses.sanskrit:
विपुलां विततां चैव युक्तपाशां तरस्विनाम्
भूमौ बाणैर्विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां ज्यामिवायुधात्
verses.transliteration:
vipulāṁ vitatāṁ caiva yuktapāśāṁ tarasvinām
bhūmau bāṇairviniṣkṛttāṁ patitāṁ jyāmivāyudhāt

translations.english: Like to a reservoir with its terrace riven, filled with broken pots, and lying with its pillars crushed; like a long strong bow-string fixed on a bow furnished with nooses, falling off the bow to the ground, being snapped in consequence of the pressure of the arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
सहसा युद्धशौण्डेन हयारोहेण वाहिताम्
निक्षिप्तभाण्डामुत्सृष्टां किशोरीमिव दुर्बलाम्
verses.transliteration:
sahasā yuddhaśauṇḍena hayāroheṇa vāhitām
nikṣiptabhāṇḍāmutsṛṣṭāṁ kiśorīmiva durbalām

translations.english: Like a mare, suddenly urged on by a rider skilled in battle, lying (on the ground), having been slain by the hostile forces.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्तु रथस्थः सञ्श्रीमान्दशरथात्मजः
वाहयन्तं रथश्रेष्ठं सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
bharatastu rathasthaḥ sañśrīmāndaśarathātmajaḥ
vāhayantaṁ rathaśreṣṭhaṁ sārathiṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: That son of Dasaratha, the beauteous Bharata, while proceeding on his car, addressed the charioteer as he drove that best of cars, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु खल्वद्य गम्भीरो मूर्छितो न निशम्यते
यथापुरमयोध्यायां गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu khalvadya gambhīro mūrchito na niśamyate
yathāpuramayodhyāyāṁ gītavāditraniḥsvanaḥ

translations.english: Why do I not hear as formerly the solemn sounds of song and instrumental music spreading on all sides in Ayodhyā?

verses.sanskrit:
वारुणीमदगन्धाश्च माल्यगन्धश्च मूर्छितः
धूपितागरुगन्धश्च न प्रवाति समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
vāruṇīmadagandhāśca mālyagandhaśca mūrchitaḥ
dhūpitāgarugandhaśca na pravāti samantataḥ

translations.english: And there does not breathe around the aroma of liquor, or the perfume of garlands, or the incense of aguru and sandal.

verses.sanskrit:
यानप्रवरघोषश्च स्निग्धश्च हयनिःस्वनः
प्रमत्तगजनादश्च महांश्च रथनिःस्वनः
नेदानीं श्रूयते पुर्यामस्यां रामे विवासिते
verses.transliteration:
yānapravaraghoṣaśca snigdhaśca hayaniḥsvanaḥ
pramattagajanādaśca mahāṁśca rathaniḥsvanaḥ
nedānīṁ śrūyate puryāmasyāṁ rāme vivāsite

translations.english: And on Rāma being banished, in this city is not heard the mild neighing of steeds, the rattle of vehicles, the roar of mad elephants, or the mighty clatter of arms.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुणैश्चारु वेषैश्च नरैरुन्नतगामिभिः
संपतद्भिरयोध्यायां न विभान्ति महापथाः
verses.transliteration:
taruṇaiścāru veṣaiśca narairunnatagāmibhiḥ
saṁpatadbhirayodhyāyāṁ na vibhānti mahāpathāḥ

translations.english: And the highways shall be graced with young people elegantly attired and bearing themselves bravely in Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधं जल्पन्विवेश वसतिं पितुः
तेन हीनां नरेन्द्रेण सिंहहीनां गुहामिव
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bahuvidhaṁ jalpanviveśa vasatiṁ pituḥ
tena hīnāṁ narendreṇa siṁhahīnāṁ guhāmiva

translations.english: Having said this in grief, Bharata in company with the charioteer entered Ayodhyā and immediately went to the residence of his father, bereft of that foremost of men, like a cavern bereft of its lion.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निक्षिप्य मातॄः स अयोध्यायां दृढव्रतः
भरतः शोकसंतप्तो गुरूनिदमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato nikṣipya mātṝḥ sa ayodhyāyāṁ dṛḍhavrataḥ
bharataḥ śokasaṁtapto gurūnidamathābravīt

translations.english: Having placed his mothers in Ayodhyā, Bharata steady in his vow, kindling in grief, said preceptors.

verses.sanskrit:
नन्दिग्रामं गमिष्यामि सर्वानामन्त्रयेऽद्य वः
तत्र दुःखमिदं सर्वं सहिष्ये राघवं विना
verses.transliteration:
nandigrāmaṁ gamiṣyāmi sarvānāmantraye'dya vaḥ
tatra duḥkhamidaṁ sarvaṁ sahiṣye rāghavaṁ vinā

translations.english: I shall go to Nandigrāma, and therefore greet you all. There I shall suffer all this grief on account of Rāma's absence.

verses.sanskrit:
गतश्च हि दिवं राजा वनस्थश्च गुरुर्मम
रामं प्रतीक्षे राज्याय स हि राजा महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
gataśca hi divaṁ rājā vanasthaśca gururmama
rāmaṁ pratīkṣe rājyāya sa hi rājā mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: The king has gone to heaven, and my superior is staying in the woods. I shall remain in expectation of Rāma, assuming the reins of government. Verily that illustrious one is the king.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः
अब्रुवन्मन्त्रिणः सर्वे वसिष्ठश्च पुरोहितः
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā śubhaṁ vākyaṁ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
abruvanmantriṇaḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaśca purohitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing this excellent speech of the highsouled Bharata the counsellors as well as the priest Vasiştha said.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं श्लाघनीयं च यदुक्तं भरत त्वया
वचनं भ्रातृवात्सल्यादनुरूपं तवैव तत्
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ ślāghanīyaṁ ca yaduktaṁ bharata tvayā
vacanaṁ bhrātṛvātsalyādanurūpaṁ tavaiva tat

translations.english: What, О Bharata, influenced by affection for your brother you say, is worthy of you and is highly commendable.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यं ते बन्धुलुब्धस्य तिष्ठतो भ्रातृसौहृदे
आर्यमार्गं प्रपन्नस्य नानुमन्येत कः पुमान्
verses.transliteration:
nityaṁ te bandhulubdhasya tiṣṭhato bhrātṛsauhṛde
āryamārgaṁ prapannasya nānumanyeta kaḥ pumān

translations.english: Who will not endorse what has fallen from you, ever engaged in serving your friends, established in fraternal love, and who have entered upon a noble course?

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिणां वचनं श्रुत्वा यथाभिलषितं प्रियम्
अब्रवीत्सारथिं वाक्यं रथो मे युज्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
mantriṇāṁ vacanaṁ śrutvā yathābhilaṣitaṁ priyam
abravītsārathiṁ vākyaṁ ratho me yujyatāmiti

translations.english: Having heard the words of the counsellors acceptable and welcome, Bharata said to the charioteer, Do you yoke my car.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टवदनः सर्वा मातॄः समभिवाद्य सः
आरुरोह रथं श्रीमाञ्शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ sarvā mātṝḥ samabhivādya saḥ
āruroha rathaṁ śrīmāñśatrughnena samanvitaḥ

translations.english: Then with a cheerful countenance having spoken to his mothers, that graceful one ascended the car in company with Satrughna.

verses.sanskrit:
आरुह्य तु रथं शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ
ययतुः परमप्रीतौ वृतौ मन्त्रिपुरोहितैः
verses.transliteration:
āruhya tu rathaṁ śīghraṁ śatrughnabharatāvubhau
yayatuḥ paramaprītau vṛtau mantripurohitaiḥ

translations.english: Having swiftly ascended the car, both Satrughna and Bharata, right glad at heart, set out surrounded by counsellors and priests.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रतो पुरवस्तत्र वसिष्ठ प्रमुखा द्विजाः
प्रययुः प्राङ्मुखाः सर्वे नन्दिग्रामो यतोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
agrato puravastatra vasiṣṭha pramukhā dvijāḥ
prayayuḥ prāṅmukhāḥ sarve nandigrāmo yato'bhavat

translations.english: And going ahead, all the preceptors headed by Vasiştha proceeded eastwards, in which direction lay Nandigrāma.

verses.sanskrit:
बलं च तदनाहूतं गजाश्वरथसंकुलम्
प्रययौ भरते याते सर्वे च पुरवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
balaṁ ca tadanāhūtaṁ gajāśvarathasaṁkulam
prayayau bharate yāte sarve ca puravāsinaḥ

translations.english: And the forces, filled with elephants and horses and cars, although not called, set out on Bharata proceeding, as well as all the citizens.

verses.sanskrit:
रथस्थः स तु धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः
नन्दिग्रामं ययौ तूर्णं शिरस्याधाय पादुके
verses.transliteration:
rathasthaḥ sa tu dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
nandigrāmaṁ yayau tūrṇaṁ śirasyādhāya pāduke

translations.english: And ascending the car, the virtuous Bharata attached to his brother, speedily went to Nandigrāma, holding the sandals (of Rāma) on his head.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु भरतः क्षिप्रं नन्दिग्रामं प्रविश्य सः
अवतीर्य रथात्तूर्णं गुरूनिदमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tatastu bharataḥ kṣipraṁ nandigrāmaṁ praviśya saḥ
avatīrya rathāttūrṇaṁ gurūnidamuvāca ha

translations.english: Then entering Nandigrāma in a short time, Bharata swiftly alighted from the car and addressed his preceptors, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्राज्यं मम भ्रात्रा दत्तं संन्यासवत्स्वयम्
योगक्षेमवहे चेमे पादुके हेमभूषिते
तमिमं पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
etadrājyaṁ mama bhrātrā dattaṁ saṁnyāsavatsvayam
yogakṣemavahe ceme pāduke hemabhūṣite
tamimaṁ pālayiṣyāmi rāghavāgamanaṁ prati

translations.english: This monarchy has been consigned to me as a trust; and these gold-decked sandals shall carry on the work of government, protecting what the people have and securing to them what they have not.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं संयोजयित्वा तु राघवस्य पुनः स्वयम्
चरणौ तौ तु रामस्य द्रक्ष्यामि सहपादुकौ
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṁ saṁyojayitvā tu rāghavasya punaḥ svayam
caraṇau tau tu rāmasya drakṣyāmi sahapādukau

translations.english: Again speedily putting these sandals on Raghava's feet, I shall behold them with the sandals on.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निक्षिप्तभारोऽहं राघवेण समागतः
निवेद्य गुरवे राज्यं भजिष्ये गुरुवृत्तिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tato nikṣiptabhāro'haṁ rāghaveṇa samāgataḥ
nivedya gurave rājyaṁ bhajiṣye guruvṛttitām
