translations.english: On Rāghava coming (back), I shall, my burden being cast upon him, making over the kingdom to him, engage myself in serving my superior.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवाय च संन्यासं दत्त्वेमे वरपादुके
राज्यं चेदमयोध्यां च धूतपापो भवामि च
verses.transliteration:
rāghavāya ca saṁnyāsaṁ dattveme varapāduke
rājyaṁ cedamayodhyāṁ ca dhūtapāpo bhavāmi ca

translations.english: And having rendered to Rāghava the trust in the shape of these sandals, this kingdom, and Ayodhyā, I shall be washed form my sin.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिप्रयाते भरते वसन्रामस्तपोवने
लक्षयामास सोद्वेगमथौत्सुक्यं तपस्विनाम्
verses.transliteration:
pratiprayāte bharate vasanrāmastapovane
lakṣayāmāsa sodvegamathautsukyaṁ tapasvinām

translations.english: On Bharata having returned, while Rāma was dwelling in the woods, he noticed affright among the ascetics, added to a desire to remove to another place.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तत्र चित्रकूटस्य पुरस्तात्तापसाश्रमे
राममाश्रित्य निरतास्तानलक्षयदुत्सुकान्
verses.transliteration:
ye tatra citrakūṭasya purastāttāpasāśrame
rāmamāśritya niratāstānalakṣayadutsukān

translations.english: And those ascetic that were living happily in the asylum in Citrakuța, relying upon Rāma (for their protection), he found to be wrought up with anxiety.

verses.sanskrit:
नयनैर्भृकुटीभिश्च रामं निर्दिश्य शङ्किताः
अन्योन्यमुपजल्पन्तः शनैश्चक्रुर्मिथः कथाः
verses.transliteration:
nayanairbhṛkuṭībhiśca rāmaṁ nirdiśya śaṅkitāḥ
anyonyamupajalpantaḥ śanaiścakrurmithaḥ kathāḥ

translations.english: And by means of signs by the eye and contractions of the brow, they, afflicted with fear, were, alluding to Răma, slowly speaking to each other.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामौत्सुक्यमालक्ष्य रामस्त्वात्मनि शङ्कितः
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमृषिं कुलपतिं ततः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmautsukyamālakṣya rāmastvātmani śaṅkitaḥ
kṛtāñjaliruvācedamṛṣiṁ kulapatiṁ tataḥ

translations.english: Perceiving their anxiety, Rāma apprehensive of himself, with joined hands addressed the patriarchal ascetic, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न कच्चिद्भगवन्किंचित्पूर्ववृत्तमिदं मयि
दृश्यते विकृतं येन विक्रियन्ते तपस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
na kaccidbhagavankiṁcitpūrvavṛttamidaṁ mayi
dṛśyate vikṛtaṁ yena vikriyante tapasvinaḥ

translations.english: O reverend one, do you find me deviating from the path of former sovereigns, or acting contrary to their practice, which has perplexed (the minds of) these ascetics?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमादाच्चरितं कच्चित्किंचिन्नावरजस्य मे
लक्ष्मणस्यर्षिभिर्दृष्टं नानुरूपमिवात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
pramādāccaritaṁ kaccitkiṁcinnāvarajasya me
lakṣmaṇasyarṣibhirdṛṣṭaṁ nānurūpamivātmanaḥ

translations.english: Have the sages seen my younger (brother), the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, do anything from inadvertence that in unworthy of him?

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिच्छुश्रूषमाणा वः शुश्रूषणपरा मयि
प्रमदाभ्युचितां वृत्तिं सीता युक्तं न वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
kaccicchuśrūṣamāṇā vaḥ śuśrūṣaṇaparā mayi
pramadābhyucitāṁ vṛttiṁ sītā yuktaṁ na vartate

translations.english: Does not Sītā engaged in serving you, having to serve me, now minister to you as a woman should?

verses.sanskrit:
अथर्षिर्जरया वृद्धस्तपसा च जरां गतः
वेपमान इवोवाच रामं भूतदयापरम्
verses.transliteration:
atharṣirjarayā vṛddhastapasā ca jarāṁ gataḥ
vepamāna ivovāca rāmaṁ bhūtadayāparam

translations.english: Thereat a certain aged and decrepit ascetic, with his frame trembling said to Rāma ever kind towards creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
कुतः कल्याणसत्त्वायाः कल्याणाभिरतेस्तथा
चलनं तात वैदेह्यास्तपस्विषु विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
kutaḥ kalyāṇasattvāyāḥ kalyāṇābhiratestathā
calanaṁ tāta vaidehyāstapasviṣu viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: Where is the falling off of that one of excellent character, engaged in offices of beneficence,-more specially with reference to ascetics?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वन्निमित्तमिदं तावत्तापसान्प्रति वर्तते
रक्षोभ्यस्तेन संविग्नाः कथयन्ति मिथः कथाः
verses.transliteration:
tvannimittamidaṁ tāvattāpasānprati vartate
rakṣobhyastena saṁvignāḥ kathayanti mithaḥ kathāḥ

translations.english: This fear arising from Rākşasas afflicts the ascetics because of you; and they, extremely agitated, converse with each other (on the subject).

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं यदा प्रभृति ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रमे तात वर्तसे
तदा प्रभृति रक्षांसि विप्रकुर्वन्ति तापसान्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ yadā prabhṛti hyasminnāśrame tāta vartase
tadā prabhṛti rakṣāṁsi viprakurvanti tāpasān

translations.english: A Rākşasa named Khara, a younger brother of Rāvana, has been harassing the ascetics dwelling in Janasthāna. And Dhrsta also a fearless and wicked Rākṣasa feeding on human beings, and the unrighteous Avalipta, cannot bear you, my child. As long, my child, as you have been residing in this asylum, the Rākşasas have been plaguing the ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शयन्ति हि बीभत्सैः क्रूरैर्भीषणकैरपि
नाना रूपैर्विरूपैश्च रूपैरसुखदर्शनैः
verses.transliteration:
darśayanti hi bībhatsaiḥ krūrairbhīṣaṇakairapi
nānā rūpairvirūpaiśca rūpairasukhadarśanaiḥ

translations.english: And they show themselves sometimes in disgusting shapes, sometimes in horrible and dreadful ones, in various frightful forms capable of frightening folks. And they throw execrable and unclean things among the anchorets, and torment those that happen to come before them.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु तेष्वाश्रमस्थानेष्वबुद्धमवलीय च
रमन्ते तापसांस्तत्र नाशयन्तोऽल्पचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
teṣu teṣvāśramasthāneṣvabuddhamavalīya ca
ramante tāpasāṁstatra nāśayanto'lpacetasaḥ

translations.english: And they take delight in approaching asylums unperceived, and slaughtering ascetics, after having bound them by means of their arms.

verses.sanskrit:
अपक्षिपन्ति स्रुग्भाण्डानग्नीन्सिञ्चन्ति वारिणा
कलशांश्च प्रमृद्नन्ति हवने समुपस्थिते
verses.transliteration:
apakṣipanti srugbhāṇḍānagnīnsiñcanti vāriṇā
kalaśāṁśca pramṛdnanti havane samupasthite

translations.english: And on the occasion of sacrifices, they throw away the vessels containing sacrificial articles, pour water on the sacrificial fire and break vessels containing water.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्दुरात्मभिराविष्टानाश्रमान्प्रजिहासवः
गमनायान्यदेशस्य चोदयन्त्यृषयोऽद्य माम्
verses.transliteration:
tairdurātmabhirāviṣṭānāśramānprajihāsavaḥ
gamanāyānyadeśasya codayantyṛṣayo'dya mām

translations.english: Eager to renounce this asylum infested by those wicked ones, and removing to another place, the sages today have been exhorting me (on the subject).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्पुरा राम शारीरामुपहिंसां तपस्विषु
दर्शयति हि दुष्टास्ते त्यक्ष्याम इममाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tatpurā rāma śārīrāmupahiṁsāṁ tapasviṣu
darśayati hi duṣṭāste tyakṣyāma imamāśramam

translations.english: And, O Rama, ere this, those wicked ones have slain ascetics. Therefore would renounce this asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुमूलफलं चित्रमविदूरादितो वनम्
पुराणाश्रममेवाहं श्रयिष्ये सगणः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
bahumūlaphalaṁ citramavidūrādito vanam
purāṇāśramamevāhaṁ śrayiṣye sagaṇaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Not far from here is a picturesque wood abounding in fruits and roots. Thither shall I betake myself together with my own folks.

verses.sanskrit:
खरस्त्वय्यपि चायुक्तं पुरा तात प्रवर्तते
सहास्माभिरितो गच्छ यदि बुद्धिः प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
kharastvayyapi cāyuktaṁ purā tāta pravartate
sahāsmābhirito gaccha yadi buddhiḥ pravartate

translations.english: Khara shall also annoy you. If you think it proper, go hence in company with us. we

verses.sanskrit:
सकलत्रस्य संदेहो नित्यं यत्तस्य राघव
समर्थस्यापि हि सतो वासो दुःख इहाद्य ते
verses.transliteration:
sakalatrasya saṁdeho nityaṁ yattasya rāghava
samarthasyāpi hi sato vāso duḥkha ihādya te

translations.english: O Rāghava, although you are vigilant, able, and in all ways capable, it would be unpleasant for you to dwell here now in doubt.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तवन्तं रामस्तं राजपुत्रस्तपस्विनम्
न शशाकोत्तरैर्वाक्यैरवरोद्धुं समुत्सुकम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktavantaṁ rāmastaṁ rājaputrastapasvinam
na śaśākottarairvākyairavaroddhuṁ samutsukam

translations.english: When the anxious ascetic had said this, Rāma could not console him by his words.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिनन्द्य समापृच्छ्य समाधाय च राघवम्
स जगामाश्रमं त्यक्त्वा कुलैः कुलपतिः सह
verses.transliteration:
abhinandya samāpṛcchya samādhāya ca rāghavam
sa jagāmāśramaṁ tyaktvā kulaiḥ kulapatiḥ saha

translations.english: Then having paid homage to Rāma, and spoken to him and encouraged Rāghava, the patriach ascetic renouncing the asylum, went away along with his own people.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः संसाध्य त्वृषिगणमनुगमना;द्देशात्तस्माच्चित्कुलपतिमभिवाद्यर्षिम्
सम्यक्प्रीतैस्तैरनुमत उपदिष्टार्थः; पुण्यं वासाय स्वनिलयमुपसंपेदे
verses.transliteration:
rāmaḥ saṁsādhya tvṛṣigaṇamanugamanā;ddeśāttasmāccitkulapatimabhivādyarṣim
samyakprītaistairanumata upadiṣṭārthaḥ; puṇyaṁ vāsāya svanilayamupasaṁpede

translations.english: And Rāma having (for a time) followed the sage who was departing from that place, and having paid him respects, being permitted by them, well-pleased, and advised (as to what it behoved him to do), came to his quarters reposing there.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्रमं त्वृषिविरहितं प्रभुः; क्षणमपि न जहौ स राघवः
राघवं हि सततमनुगता;स्तापसाश्चर्षिचरितधृतगुणाः
verses.transliteration:
āśramaṁ tvṛṣivirahitaṁ prabhuḥ; kṣaṇamapi na jahau sa rāghavaḥ
rāghavaṁ hi satatamanugatā;stāpasāścarṣicaritadhṛtaguṇāḥ

translations.english: (Thenceforth) Rāghava never for a moment left that asylum forsaken by the sages., Rāghava having such qualities in his character as were likely to stand the sages in stead, the ascetics (that remained behind) ever followed Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्त्वपयातेषु तपस्विषु विचिन्तयन्
न तत्रारोचयद्वासं कारणैर्बहुभिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
rāghavastvapayāteṣu tapasviṣu vicintayan
na tatrārocayadvāsaṁ kāraṇairbahubhistadā

translations.english: When the ascetics had gone away, Rāghava reflected (as to his stay at that place); and from diverse reasons, he did not relish remaining there any further.

verses.sanskrit:
इह मे भरतो दृष्टो मातरश्च सनागराः
सा च मे स्मृतिरन्वेति तान्नित्यमनुशोचतः
verses.transliteration:
iha me bharato dṛṣṭo mātaraśca sanāgarāḥ
sā ca me smṛtiranveti tānnityamanuśocataḥ

translations.english: Here have I seen Bharata and my mother in company with the citizens. Overwhelmed with grief on my account, they ever recur to my memory.

verses.sanskrit:
स्कन्धावारनिवेशेन तेन तस्य महात्मनः
हयहस्तिकरीषैश्च उपमर्दः कृतो भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
skandhāvāraniveśena tena tasya mahātmanaḥ
hayahastikarīṣaiśca upamardaḥ kṛto bhṛśam

translations.english: And in consequence of the troops of that highsouled one having quartered here as well as the dung discharged by his elephants and horses, this place has got exceedingly dirty.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादन्यत्र गच्छाम इति संचिन्त्य राघवः
प्रातिष्ठत स वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च संगतः
verses.transliteration:
tasmādanyatra gacchāma iti saṁcintya rāghavaḥ
prātiṣṭhata sa vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca saṁgataḥ

translations.english: Therefore will I go to another quarter. Having settled this in his mind, Rāghava departed along with Videha's daughter and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽत्रेराश्रममासाद्य तं ववन्दे महायशाः
तं चापि भगवानत्रिः पुत्रवत्प्रत्यपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
so'trerāśramamāsādya taṁ vavande mahāyaśāḥ
taṁ cāpi bhagavānatriḥ putravatpratyapadyata

translations.english: And having arrived at Atri's asylum, that renowned one paid obeisance (to the sage); and the reverend Atri also on his pare received Rāma asason.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयमातिथ्यमादिश्य सर्वमस्य सुसत्कृतम्
सौमित्रिं च महाभागां सीतां च समसान्त्वयत्
verses.transliteration:
svayamātithyamādiśya sarvamasya susatkṛtam
saumitriṁ ca mahābhāgāṁ sītāṁ ca samasāntvayat

translations.english: And having personally given Rāma respectful reception and entertainment, the ascetic regarded the exalted Lakşmaņa and Sītā with a gracious eye.

verses.sanskrit:
पत्नीं च तमनुप्राप्तां वृद्धामामन्त्र्य सत्कृताम्
सान्त्वयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वभूतहिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
patnīṁ ca tamanuprāptāṁ vṛddhāmāmantrya satkṛtām
sāntvayāmāsa dharmajñaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ

translations.english: And his aged wife having come there, Atri greeted her; and after she had been paid homage, the sage cognizant of virtue ever engaged in the good of all creatures, gladdened her (by presenting Sītā to her.) And that best of sages said to the pious female ascetic, Anasüyā, engaged in offices of virtue, “Do you accept Videha's daughter."

verses.sanskrit:
तामिमां सर्वभूतानां नमस्कार्यां यशस्विनीम्
अभिगच्छतु वैदेही वृद्धामक्रोधनां सदा
verses.transliteration:
tāmimāṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ namaskāryāṁ yaśasvinīm
abhigacchatu vaidehī vṛddhāmakrodhanāṁ sadā

translations.english: Let Vaidehī always resort to this aged ascetic devoid of anger, who is worthy of being bowed down to by all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं तथेत्युक्त्वा स राघवः
सीतामुवाच धर्मज्ञामिदं वचनमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ tamṛṣiṁ tathetyuktvā sa rāghavaḥ
sītāmuvāca dharmajñāmidaṁ vacanamuttamam

translations.english: When the saint had spoken thus, Rāghava saying, “So be it," turned his eyes to Sītā, and thus spoke to that one knowing morality.

verses.sanskrit:
राजपुत्रि श्रुतं त्वेतन्मुनेरस्य समीरितम्
श्रेयोऽर्थमात्मनः शीघ्रमभिगच्छ तपस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
rājaputri śrutaṁ tvetanmunerasya samīritam
śreyo'rthamātmanaḥ śīghramabhigaccha tapasvinīm

translations.english: O princess, you have heard what has been uttered by the ascetic. For the sake of your own welfare, do you speedily resort to the female anchoret. Do you without delay resort to the ascetic Anasuya, who is worthy of being associated with, and who has by virtue of her acts attained renown among men.f

verses.sanskrit:
सीता त्वेतद्वचः श्रुत्वा राघवस्य हितैषिणी
तामत्रिपत्नीं धर्मज्ञामभिचक्राम मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
sītā tvetadvacaḥ śrutvā rāghavasya hitaiṣiṇī
tāmatripatnīṁ dharmajñāmabhicakrāma maithilī

translations.english: Hearing these words of Rāghava Mithila's daughter, the illustrious Sītā, drew near the righteous wife of Atri.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु सीता महाभागामनसूयां पतिव्रताम्
अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रा स्वं नाम समुदाहरत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu sītā mahābhāgāmanasūyāṁ pativratām
abhyavādayadavyagrā svaṁ nāma samudāharat

translations.english: Thereupon Sītā, announcing her name, saluted the pious and chaste Anasuyā old with slackened joints, with folds all over her skin, and her hair hoary from age, whose frame shook perpetually, like a plantain-leaf in the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्य च वैदेही तापसीं तामनिन्दिताम्
बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा हृष्टा पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्
verses.transliteration:
abhivādya ca vaidehī tāpasīṁ tāmaninditām
baddhāñjalipuṭā hṛṣṭā paryapṛcchadanāmayam

translations.english: Having paid homage to that ascetic with her senses subdued, Vaidehi glad at heart, with joined hands, enquired after her welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सीतां महाभागां दृष्ट्वा तां धर्मचारिणीम्
सान्त्वयन्त्यब्रवीद्धृष्टा दिष्ट्या धर्ममवेक्षसे
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sītāṁ mahābhāgāṁ dṛṣṭvā tāṁ dharmacāriṇīm
sāntvayantyabravīddhṛṣṭā diṣṭyā dharmamavekṣase

translations.english: Seeing the virtuous Sītā engaged in righteous acts, the old lady consoling her, said "By luck it is that you regard righteousness."

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा ज्ञातिजनं सीते मानमृद्धिं च मानिनि
अवरुद्धं वने रामं दिष्ट्या त्वमनुगच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
tyaktvā jñātijanaṁ sīte mānamṛddhiṁ ca mānini
avaruddhaṁ vane rāmaṁ diṣṭyā tvamanugacchasi

translations.english: O Sita, having left your kindred, and banishing pride, you have o honoured lady, followed Rāma staying in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा पापो वा यदि वाशुभः
यासां स्त्रीणां प्रियो भर्ता तासां लोका महोदयाः
verses.transliteration:
nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vāśubhaḥ
yāsāṁ strīṇāṁ priyo bhartā tāsāṁ lokā mahodayāḥ

translations.english: They that love their husbands, whether living in the city or the forest, whether well or ill disposed towards them, attain great state.

verses.sanskrit:
दुःशीलः कामवृत्तो वा धनैर्वा परिवर्जितः
स्त्रीणामार्य स्वभावानां परमं दैवतं पतिः
verses.transliteration:
duḥśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā dhanairvā parivarjitaḥ
strīṇāmārya svabhāvānāṁ paramaṁ daivataṁ patiḥ

translations.english: Wicked, ur libidinous, or indigent, a husband is a supreme deity to a wife of noble character.

verses.sanskrit:
नातो विशिष्टं पश्यामि बान्धवं विमृशन्त्यहम्
सर्वत्र योग्यं वैदेहि तपः कृतमिवाव्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
nāto viśiṣṭaṁ paśyāmi bāndhavaṁ vimṛśantyaham
sarvatra yogyaṁ vaidehi tapaḥ kṛtamivāvyayam

translations.english: Than the husband a greater friend find I none, O Vaidehī, who is worthy of being served both in this world and the next, and who is like imperishable asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वेवमवगच्छन्ति गुण दोषमसत्स्त्रियः
कामवक्तव्यहृदया भर्तृनाथाश्चरन्ति याः
verses.transliteration:
na tvevamavagacchanti guṇa doṣamasatstriyaḥ
kāmavaktavyahṛdayā bhartṛnāthāścaranti yāḥ

translations.english: But bad women whose hearts hunger after carnality, and who lord over their husbands, do not get acquainted with the virtues and demerits (of their husbands); and range at their will.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्नुवन्त्ययशश्चैव धर्मभ्रंशं च मैथिलि
अकार्य वशमापन्नाः स्त्रियो याः खलु तद्विधाः
verses.transliteration:
prāpnuvantyayaśaścaiva dharmabhraṁśaṁ ca maithili
akārya vaśamāpannāḥ striyo yāḥ khalu tadvidhāḥ

translations.english: O Mithilā's daughter, surely women of this sort who are given to doing evil acts, reap infamy and fall off from righteousness.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वद्विधास्तु गुणैर्युक्ता दृष्टलोकपरावराः
स्त्रियः स्वर्गे चरिष्यन्ति यथा पुण्यकृतस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
tvadvidhāstu guṇairyuktā dṛṣṭalokaparāvarāḥ
striyaḥ svarge cariṣyanti yathā puṇyakṛtastathā

translations.english: But worthy women like you furnished with excellence, see a superior and better world, and range the celestial regions, like pious people.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वेवमुक्ता वैदेही अनसूयानसूयया
प्रतिपूज्य वचो मन्दं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
sā tvevamuktā vaidehī anasūyānasūyayā
pratipūjya vaco mandaṁ pravaktumupacakrame

translations.english: Thus addressed by Anasūyā, Vaidehī devoid of malice, honouring her words, began, “That you should instruct me is no wonder in you."

verses.sanskrit:
नैतदाश्चर्यमार्याया यन्मां त्वमनुभाषसे
विदितं तु ममाप्येतद्यथा नार्याः पतिर्गुरुः
verses.transliteration:
naitadāścaryamāryāyā yanmāṁ tvamanubhāṣase
viditaṁ tu mamāpyetadyathā nāryāḥ patirguruḥ

translations.english: I know that a woman's spiritual guide is her husband. Even if a husband should be poor and of a disreputable character, he should be ungiudgingly obeyed by the like of me. one

verses.sanskrit:
किं पुनर्यो गुणश्लाघ्यः सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रियः
स्थिरानुरागो धर्मात्मा मातृवर्ती पितृ प्रियः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ punaryo guṇaślāghyaḥ sānukrośo jitendriyaḥ
sthirānurāgo dharmātmā mātṛvartī pitṛ priyaḥ

translations.english: And to be said of one that is crowned with qualities, kind, self-controlled, of steady affection, righteous-souled, and who is dear as a father or a mother?

verses.sanskrit:
यां वृत्तिं वर्तते रामः कौसल्यायां महाबलः
तामेव नृपनारीणामन्यासामपि वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ vṛttiṁ vartate rāmaḥ kausalyāyāṁ mahābalaḥ
tāmeva nṛpanārīṇāmanyāsāmapi vartate

translations.english: The exceedingly strong Rāma bear himself towards the other wives of the monarch as he does towards Kausalyā herself.

verses.sanskrit:
सकृद्दृष्टास्वपि स्त्रीषु नृपेण नृपवत्सलः
मातृवद्वर्तते वीरो मानमुत्सृज्य धर्मवित्
verses.transliteration:
sakṛddṛṣṭāsvapi strīṣu nṛpeṇa nṛpavatsalaḥ
mātṛvadvartate vīro mānamutsṛjya dharmavit

translations.english: Renouncing sense of self-importance that heroic conversant with righteousness, devoted to his king, regards as his mothers those on whom the monarch once cast his eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
आगच्छन्त्याश्च विजनं वनमेवं भयावहम्
समाहितं हि मे श्वश्र्वा हृदये यत्स्थितं मम
verses.transliteration:
āgacchantyāśca vijanaṁ vanamevaṁ bhayāvaham
samāhitaṁ hi me śvaśrvā hṛdaye yatsthitaṁ mama

translations.english: What my mother-in-law instructed me at the time that I was leaving for the lonely and fearful forest, is constantly present in my mind.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणिप्रदानकाले च यत्पुरा त्वग्निसंनिधौ
अनुशिष्टा जनन्यास्मि वाक्यं तदपि मे धृतम्
verses.transliteration:
prāṇipradānakāle ca yatpurā tvagnisaṁnidhau
anuśiṣṭā jananyāsmi vākyaṁ tadapi me dhṛtam

translations.english: And what also my mother taught me in presence of fire on the occasion of the bestowal of my hand, is also remembered by me.

verses.sanskrit:
नवीकृतं तु तत्सर्वं वाक्यैस्ते धर्मचारिणि
पतिशुश्रूषणान्नार्यास्तपो नान्यद्विधीयते
verses.transliteration:
navīkṛtaṁ tu tatsarvaṁ vākyaiste dharmacāriṇi
patiśuśrūṣaṇānnāryāstapo nānyadvidhīyate

translations.english: And, O you engaged in acts of righteousness, I have not forgotten the words that my relatives said to me, viz, the asceticism of a woman is ministering to her husband. They did not teach any thing else.

verses.sanskrit:
सावित्री पतिशुश्रूषां कृत्वा स्वर्गे महीयते
तथा वृत्तिश्च याता त्वं पतिशुश्रूषया दिवम्
verses.transliteration:
sāvitrī patiśuśrūṣāṁ kṛtvā svarge mahīyate
tathā vṛttiśca yātā tvaṁ patiśuśrūṣayā divam

translations.english: Having served her lord. Sāvitri is highly honoured in heaven; and you also, following the same course, by virtue of having served your husband, has secured heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
वरिष्ठा सर्वनारीणामेषा च दिवि देवता
रोहिणी च विना चन्द्रं मुहूर्तमपि दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
variṣṭhā sarvanārīṇāmeṣā ca divi devatā
rohiṇī ca vinā candraṁ muhūrtamapi dṛśyate

translations.english: And this foremost of females, this goddess of heaven, Rohiņi, is not seen for a moment without the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
एवंविधाश्च प्रवराः स्त्रियो भर्तृदृढव्रताः
देवलोके महीयन्ते पुण्येन स्वेन कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
evaṁvidhāśca pravarāḥ striyo bhartṛdṛḍhavratāḥ
devaloke mahīyante puṇyena svena karmaṇā

translations.english: And prime women of this sort, firm in their husbands, are highly respected in the celestial regions by virtue of their pious acts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽनसूया संहृष्टा श्रुत्वोक्तं सीतया वचः
शिरस्याघ्राय चोवाच मैथिलीं हर्षयन्त्युत
verses.transliteration:
tato'nasūyā saṁhṛṣṭā śrutvoktaṁ sītayā vacaḥ
śirasyāghrāya covāca maithilīṁ harṣayantyuta

translations.english: Hearing Sītā's words, Anasuyā, exceedingly delighted, smelling her head, spoke thus, pleasing Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
नियमैर्विविधैराप्तं तपो हि महदस्ति मे
तत्संश्रित्य बलं सीते छन्दये त्वां शुचिव्रते
verses.transliteration:
niyamairvividhairāptaṁ tapo hi mahadasti me
tatsaṁśritya balaṁ sīte chandaye tvāṁ śucivrate

translations.english: By observing restrictions, I have earned great asceticism. By resorting to that energy, I would, O Sīta, confer a boon upon you, O you of pure vows.

verses.sanskrit:
उपपन्नं च युक्तं च वचनं तव मैथिलि
प्रीता चास्म्युचितं किं ते करवाणि ब्रवीहि मे
कृतमित्यब्रवीत्सीता तपोबलसमन्विताम्
verses.transliteration:
upapannaṁ ca yuktaṁ ca vacanaṁ tava maithili
prītā cāsmyucitaṁ kiṁ te karavāṇi bravīhi me
kṛtamityabravītsītā tapobalasamanvitām

translations.english: O Maithili, your words are just and proper. I am well pleased (with you). Tell me, O Sītā, what good shall I do you?

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वेवमुक्ता धर्मज्ञा तया प्रीततराभवत्
सफलं च प्रहर्षं ते हन्त सीते करोम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tvevamuktā dharmajñā tayā prītatarābhavat
saphalaṁ ca praharṣaṁ te hanta sīte karomyaham

translations.english: Thus accosted, that one cognizant of virtue, was still more pleased, and said, “I am exceedingly pleased (with your words). I will attain a desire of mine."

verses.sanskrit:
मया दत्तमिदं सीते तव गात्राणि शोभयेत्
अनुरूपमसंक्लिष्टं नित्यमेव भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
mayā dattamidaṁ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet
anurūpamasaṁkliṣṭaṁ nityameva bhaviṣyati

translations.english: This noble and grand garland, this apparel, these ornaments, and this precious paste for adorning the person, presented by me, let these, O Sītā, grace your person. These, worthy of you will never be tarnished.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गरागेण दिव्येन लिप्ताङ्गी जनकात्मजे
शोभयिष्यामि भर्तारं यथा श्रीर्विष्णुमव्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgarāgeṇa divyena liptāṅgī janakātmaje
śobhayiṣyāmi bhartāraṁ yathā śrīrviṣṇumavyayam

translations.english: O daughter of Janaka, daubing your person with this excellent paint, you will grace your husband even as Śrī does the undeteriorating Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सीता प्रीतिदानं यशस्विनी
श्लिष्टाञ्जलिपुटा धीरा समुपास्त तपोधनाम्
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya ca tatsītā prītidānaṁ yaśasvinī
śliṣṭāñjalipuṭā dhīrā samupāsta tapodhanām

translations.english: Thereupon Mithila's daughter accepted those things presented to her out of love, viz., the apparel, the paint, the ornaments and the garland. Having accepted those accepted those presents conferred on her from love, that illustrious one, Sītā, quietly sat beside the female ascetic with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा सीतामुपासीनामनसूया दृढव्रता
वचनं प्रष्टुमारेभे कथां कांचिदनुप्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā sītāmupāsīnāmanasūyā dṛḍhavratā
vacanaṁ praṣṭumārebhe kathāṁ kāṁcidanupriyām

translations.english: Then as Sītā was sitting, Anasūyā firm in vow asked her concerning a thing that was near her heart, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयंवरे किल प्राप्ता त्वमनेन यशस्विना
राघवेणेति मे सीते कथा श्रुतिमुपागता
verses.transliteration:
svayaṁvare kila prāptā tvamanena yaśasvinā
rāghaveṇeti me sīte kathā śrutimupāgatā

translations.english: I have heard, O Sītā, that you were won by the renowned Rāghava on the occasion of a selfchoice.

verses.sanskrit:
तां कथां श्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेण च मैथिलि
यथानुभूतं कार्त्स्न्येन तन्मे त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ kathāṁ śrotumicchāmi vistareṇa ca maithili
yathānubhūtaṁ kārtsnyena tanme tvaṁ vaktumarhasi

translations.english: O Maithili, that story I should like to hear, related at length. It therefore, behoves you to relate that to me in detail.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा सीता तां ततो धर्मचारिणीम्
श्रूयतामिति चोक्त्वा वै कथयामास तां कथाम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā sītā tāṁ tato dharmacāriṇīm
śrūyatāmiti coktvā vai kathayāmāsa tāṁ kathām

translations.english: Thus address, Sītā, saying to the ascetic engaged in pious acts, "Listen!" began to tell the story.

verses.sanskrit:
मिथिलाधिपतिर्वीरो जनको नाम धर्मवित्
क्षत्रधर्मण्यभिरतो न्यायतः शास्ति मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
mithilādhipatirvīro janako nāma dharmavit
kṣatradharmaṇyabhirato nyāyataḥ śāsti medinīm

translations.english: Mithila's lord, the heroic Janaka, justly rule the earth, engaged in observing the duties of Ks atriyas.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य लाङ्गलहस्तस्य कर्षतः क्षेत्रमण्डलम्
अहं किलोत्थिता भित्त्वा जगतीं नृपतेः सुता
verses.transliteration:
tasya lāṅgalahastasya karṣataḥ kṣetramaṇḍalam
ahaṁ kilotthitā bhittvā jagatīṁ nṛpateḥ sutā

translations.english: As he was ploughing a plain intended for a sacrifice, I rose from under the earth; and (in this sense) I am the daughter of that king.

verses.sanskrit:
स मां दृष्ट्वा नरपतिर्मुष्टिविक्षेपतत्परः
पांशु गुण्ठित सर्वाङ्गीं विस्मितो जनकोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa māṁ dṛṣṭvā narapatirmuṣṭivikṣepatatparaḥ
pāṁśu guṇṭhita sarvāṅgīṁ vismito janako'bhavat

translations.english: Tending me, with my body covered with dust, Janaka, engaged in throwing handfuls of dust (to level hollow spots), was struck with amazement.

verses.sanskrit:
अनपत्येन च स्नेहादङ्कमारोप्य च स्वयम्
ममेयं तनयेत्युक्त्वा स्नेहो मयि निपातितः
verses.transliteration:
anapatyena ca snehādaṅkamāropya ca svayam
mameyaṁ tanayetyuktvā sneho mayi nipātitaḥ

translations.english: Being childless, he took me on his lap from affection, and saying, 'This is my daughter', conceived affection for me.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षे च वागुक्ताप्रतिमा मानुषी किल
एवमेतन्नरपते धर्मेण तनया तव
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣe ca vāguktāpratimā mānuṣī kila
evametannarapate dharmeṇa tanayā tava

translations.english: Then there were uttered words in the welkin, resembling those of a human being,! 'O king, in all righteousness, this is your daughter'.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा पिता मे मिथिलाधिपः
अवाप्तो विपुलामृद्धिं मामवाप्य नराधिपः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā pitā me mithilādhipaḥ
avāpto vipulāmṛddhiṁ māmavāpya narādhipaḥ

translations.english: Then well-pleased, my righteous father, the king, lord of Mithilā, receiving me, attained mighty good fortune.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्त्वा चास्मीष्टवद्देव्यै ज्येष्ठायै पुण्यकर्मणा
तया संभाविता चास्मि स्निग्धया मातृसौहृदात्
verses.transliteration:
dattvā cāsmīṣṭavaddevyai jyeṣṭhāyai puṇyakarmaṇā
tayā saṁbhāvitā cāsmi snigdhayā mātṛsauhṛdāt

translations.english: Consigned to the pious eldest noble one (queen), desirous of having offspring, I was brought up by that mild lady, with the tenderness of a mother.

verses.sanskrit:
पतिसंयोगसुलभं वयो दृष्ट्वा तु मे पिता
चिन्तामभ्यगमद्दीनो वित्तनाशादिवाधनः
verses.transliteration:
patisaṁyogasulabhaṁ vayo dṛṣṭvā tu me pitā
cintāmabhyagamaddīno vittanāśādivādhanaḥ

translations.english: (In time) seeing me fit for the company of a husband, my father in distress was plunged in thought, like a poor man that has lost his wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशाच्चापकृष्टाच्च लोके कन्यापिता जनात्
प्रधर्षणामवाप्नोति शक्रेणापि समो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśāccāpakṛṣṭācca loke kanyāpitā janāt
pradharṣaṇāmavāpnoti śakreṇāpi samo bhuvi

translations.english: Even if the father of a girl be like to ſakra himself on earth he reaps odium at the hands of his equals and inferiors.

verses.sanskrit:
तां धर्षणामदूरस्थां संदृश्यात्मनि पार्थिवः
चिन्न्तार्णवगतः पारं नाससादाप्लवो यथ
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dharṣaṇāmadūrasthāṁ saṁdṛśyātmani pārthivaḥ
cinntārṇavagataḥ pāraṁ nāsasādāplavo yatha

translations.english: Perceiving this obloquy at a short distance, the king was plunged in a sea of anxiety, but could not cross it, like one that has no raft.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोनिजां हि मां ज्ञात्वा नाध्यगच्छत्स चिन्तयन्
सदृशं चानुरूपं च महीपालः पतिं मम
verses.transliteration:
ayonijāṁ hi māṁ jñātvā nādhyagacchatsa cintayan
sadṛśaṁ cānurūpaṁ ca mahīpālaḥ patiṁ mama

translations.english: Knowing me as unborn from any female vessel, the lord of earth reflecting upon it, could not come upon a suitable and fit husband for me.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बुद्धिरियं जाता चिन्तयानस्य संततम्
स्वयं वरं तनूजायाः करिष्यामीति धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya buddhiriyaṁ jātā cintayānasya saṁtatam
svayaṁ varaṁ tanūjāyāḥ kariṣyāmīti dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Then as he reflected, this thought occurred to him 'I will righteously celebrate the self-choice of my daughters'.

verses.sanskrit:
महायज्ञे तदा तस्य वरुणेन महात्मना
दत्तं धनुर्वरं प्रीत्या तूणी चाक्षय्य सायकौ
verses.transliteration:
mahāyajñe tadā tasya varuṇena mahātmanā
dattaṁ dhanurvaraṁ prītyā tūṇī cākṣayya sāyakau

translations.english: In the great sacrifice of Daksa, the highsouled Varuna had well-pleased conferred on Devarata an excellent bow with inexhaustible arrows and a couple of quivers.

verses.sanskrit:
असंचाल्यं मनुष्यैश्च यत्नेनापि च गौरवात्
तन्न शक्ता नमयितुं स्वप्नेष्वपि नराधिपाः
verses.transliteration:
asaṁcālyaṁ manuṣyaiśca yatnenāpi ca gauravāt
tanna śaktā namayituṁ svapneṣvapi narādhipāḥ

translations.english: Incapable of being moved on account of its weight, the kings could not even dream of bending the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्धनुः प्राप्य मे पित्रा व्याहृतं सत्यवादिना
समवाये नरेन्द्राणां पूर्वमामन्त्र्य पार्थिवान्
verses.transliteration:
taddhanuḥ prāpya me pitrā vyāhṛtaṁ satyavādinā
samavāye narendrāṇāṁ pūrvamāmantrya pārthivān

translations.english: Having obtained the bow, my truthful father said, 'No fear!' inviting at the same time the kings to an assembly of sovereigns.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं च धनुरुद्यम्य सज्यं यः कुरुते नरः
तस्य मे दुहिता भार्या भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ ca dhanurudyamya sajyaṁ yaḥ kurute naraḥ
tasya me duhitā bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: He that, raising the bow, shall string it, shall doubtless receive my daughter for his wife.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्च दृष्ट्वा धनुःश्रेष्ठं गौरवाद्गिरिसंनिभम्
अभिवाद्य नृपा जग्मुरशक्तास्तस्य तोलने
verses.transliteration:
tacca dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṁ gauravādgirisaṁnibham
abhivādya nṛpā jagmuraśaktāstasya tolane

translations.english: Seeing that best of bows in weight resembling a hill, the kings saluting it, go away, unable to move it.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा मम पित्रा सुपूजितः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
viśvāmitrastu dharmātmā mama pitrā supūjitaḥ

translations.english: It came to pass that after a long time, this highly effulgent Rāghava came to witness the sacrifice in company with Viśvāmitra. And Rāma having truth for his prowess, and the righteous Viśvāmitra were respectfully received by my sire.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रोवाच पितरं तत्र राघवो रामलक्ष्मणौ
सुतौ दशरथस्येमौ धनुर्दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणौ
इत्युक्तस्तेन विप्रेण तद्धनुः समुपानयत्
verses.transliteration:
provāca pitaraṁ tatra rāghavo rāmalakṣmaṇau
sutau daśarathasyemau dhanurdarśanakāṅkṣiṇau
ityuktastena vipreṇa taddhanuḥ samupānayat

translations.english: Then Viśvāmitra said to my father, 'The descendants of Raghu, sons of Daśaratha, Rāma and Lakşmaņa are anxious to behold the bow.'

verses.sanskrit:
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तदानम्य स वीर्यवान्
ज्यां समारोप्य झटिति पूरयामास वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tadānamya sa vīryavān
jyāṁ samāropya jhaṭiti pūrayāmāsa vīryavān

translations.english: Thereupon, in the twinkling of an eye, bending it, the powerful (Raghava) stringed the bow and drew it.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन पूरयता वेगान्मध्ये भग्नं द्विधा धनुः
तस्य शब्दोऽभवद्भीमः पतितस्याशनेरिव
verses.transliteration:
tena pūrayatā vegānmadhye bhagnaṁ dvidhā dhanuḥ
tasya śabdo'bhavadbhīmaḥ patitasyāśaneriva

translations.english: And as he drew it vehemently, it broke in the middle in twain. And the sound of it was dreadful like to the bursting of a thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं तत्र रामाय पित्रा सत्याभिसंधिना
उद्यता दातुमुद्यम्य जलभाजनमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ tatra rāmāya pitrā satyābhisaṁdhinā
udyatā dātumudyamya jalabhājanamuttamam

translations.english: Then raising an excellent vessel of water, my truthful father prepared to bestow me on Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
दीयमानां न तु तदा प्रतिजग्राह राघवः
अविज्ञाय पितुश्छन्दमयोध्याधिपतेः प्रभोः
verses.transliteration:
dīyamānāṁ na tu tadā pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ
avijñāya pituśchandamayodhyādhipateḥ prabhoḥ

translations.english: And bestowed on Rāghava, I was accepted of him, after he had consulted the wish of his father, that lord, the master of Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः श्वशुरमामन्त्र्य वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्
मम पित्रा अहं दत्ता रामाय विदितात्मने
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śvaśuramāmantrya vṛddhaṁ daśarathaṁ nṛpam
mama pitrā ahaṁ dattā rāmāya viditātmane

translations.english: And inviting my father-in-law, the old king Dasaratha, my father bestowed me on Rāma having knowledge of self.

verses.sanskrit:
मम चैवानुजा साध्वी ऊर्मिला प्रियदर्शना
भार्यार्थे लक्ष्मणस्यापि दत्ता पित्रा मम स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
mama caivānujā sādhvī ūrmilā priyadarśanā
bhāryārthe lakṣmaṇasyāpi dattā pitrā mama svayam

translations.english: And my father bestowed on Lakşmaņa for his wife, my younger sister, the beauteous and chaste Urmila.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं दत्तास्मि रामाय तदा तस्मिन्स्वयं वरे
अनुरक्ता च धर्मेण पतिं वीर्यवतां वरम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ dattāsmi rāmāya tadā tasminsvayaṁ vare
anuraktā ca dharmeṇa patiṁ vīryavatāṁ varam

translations.english: Thus was I bestowed on Rāma on the occasion of that self-choice. And ever since I have been devoted to my husband, the foremost of those possessing prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
अनसूया तु धर्मज्ञा श्रुत्वा तां महतीं कथाम्
पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्यां शिरस्याघ्राय मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṁ mahatīṁ kathām
paryaṣvajata bāhubhyāṁ śirasyāghrāya maithilīm

translations.english: Having heard this grand story, Anasāyā cognizant of righteousness, smelling the head of Mithilā's daughter, embraced Sītā with her arms.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यक्ताक्षरपदं चित्रं भाषितं मधुरं त्वया
यथा स्वयंवरं वृत्तं तत्सर्वं हि श्रुतं मया
verses.transliteration:
vyaktākṣarapadaṁ citraṁ bhāṣitaṁ madhuraṁ tvayā
yathā svayaṁvaraṁ vṛttaṁ tatsarvaṁ hi śrutaṁ mayā

translations.english: I have heard all that you, describing the selfchoice, have spoken sweetly and beautifully in articulated letters and feet.

verses.sanskrit:
दिवसं प्रति कीर्णानामाहारार्थं पतत्रिणाम्
संध्याकाले निलीनानां निद्रार्थं श्रूयते ध्वनिः
verses.transliteration:
divasaṁ prati kīrṇānāmāhārārthaṁ patatriṇām
saṁdhyākāle nilīnānāṁ nidrārthaṁ śrūyate dhvaniḥ

translations.english: O sweet-speeched one, I have been delighted with your narration. But ushering in the auspicious night, the graceful Sun has set. And there are heard the notes of feathered ones, which, after having gone about in search of food, are resting now for the purpose of sleeping.

verses.sanskrit:
एते चाप्यभिषेकार्द्रा मुनयः फलशोधनाः
सहिता उपवर्तन्ते सलिलाप्लुतवल्कलाः
verses.transliteration:
ete cāpyabhiṣekārdrā munayaḥ phalaśodhanāḥ
sahitā upavartante salilāplutavalkalāḥ

translations.english: And these ascetics having bathed, are wending their way in a body, carrying waterpitchers, their barks drenched with water.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु हुतेषु विधिपुर्वकम्
कपोताङ्गारुणो धूमो दृश्यते पवनोद्धतः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu huteṣu vidhipurvakam
kapotāṅgāruṇo dhūmo dṛśyate pavanoddhataḥ

translations.english: The smoke arising from the fire-sacrifice duly performed by the ascetics, reddish like the hue of the pigeon's neck, is seen, wafted by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
अल्पपर्णा हि तरवो घनीभूताः समन्ततः
विप्रकृष्टेऽपि ये देशे न प्रकाशन्ति वै दिशः
verses.transliteration:
alpaparṇā hi taravo ghanībhūtāḥ samantataḥ
viprakṛṣṭe'pi ye deśe na prakāśanti vai diśaḥ

translations.english: And trees of spare foliage appear dense (on all sides); and distance is no longer perceptible.

verses.sanskrit:
रजनी रससत्त्वानि प्रचरन्ति समन्ततः
तपोवनमृगा ह्येते वेदितीर्थेषु शेरते
verses.transliteration:
rajanī rasasattvāni pracaranti samantataḥ
tapovanamṛgā hyete veditīrtheṣu śerate

translations.english: And animals ranging in the night are going about all round; and those deer of the asylum are reposing on the daises.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रवृत्ता निशा सीते नक्षत्रसमलंकृता
ज्योत्स्ना प्रावरणश्चन्द्रो दृश्यतेऽभ्युदितोऽम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
saṁpravṛttā niśā sīte nakṣatrasamalaṁkṛtā
jyotsnā prāvaraṇaścandro dṛśyate'bhyudito'mbare

translations.english: O Sītā, the night crested by the stars has arrived; and, veiled in moonlight, appears the moon in the heavens.

verses.sanskrit:
गम्यतामनुजानामि रामस्यानुचरी भव
कथयन्त्या हि मधुरं त्वयाहं परितोषिता
verses.transliteration:
gamyatāmanujānāmi rāmasyānucarī bhava
kathayantyā hi madhuraṁ tvayāhaṁ paritoṣitā

translations.english: Go you; I permit you. Do you seek the society of Rāma. I have been pleased with your sweet converse.

verses.sanskrit:
अलंकुरु च तावत्त्वं प्रत्यक्षं मम मैथिलि
प्रीतिं जनय मे वत्स दिव्यालंकारशोभिनी
verses.transliteration:
alaṁkuru ca tāvattvaṁ pratyakṣaṁ mama maithili
prītiṁ janaya me vatsa divyālaṁkāraśobhinī

translations.english: O daughter of Mithilā, do you deck yourself before me. Do you thus please me, my child, you that look beautiful with excellent ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तदा समलंकृत्य सीता सुरसुतोपमा
प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्यै रामं त्वभिमुखी ययौ
verses.transliteration:
sā tadā samalaṁkṛtya sītā surasutopamā
praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmaṁ tvabhimukhī yayau

translations.english: Thereat, having adorned herself, Sītā, resembling the daughter of a celestial, bowing down to the feet (of the female ascetic), directed her steps towards Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु भूषितां सीतां ददर्श वदतां वरः
राघवः प्रीतिदानेन तपस्विन्या जहर्ष च
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu bhūṣitāṁ sītāṁ dadarśa vadatāṁ varaḥ
rāghavaḥ prītidānena tapasvinyā jaharṣa ca

translations.english: And that best of speakers, Raghava, saw Sita, decked with the ornaments affectionately presented by the ascetic; and he rejoiced thereat.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यवेदयत्ततः सर्वं सीता रामाय मैथिली
प्रीतिदानं तपस्विन्या वसनाभरणस्रजाम्
verses.transliteration:
nyavedayattataḥ sarvaṁ sītā rāmāya maithilī
prītidānaṁ tapasvinyā vasanābharaṇasrajām

translations.english: Then Mithila's daughter, Sita, related to Rama all about her having been affectionately presented by the ascetic with attire, ornaments and the garland.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टस्त्वभवद्रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः
मैथिल्याः सत्क्रियां दृष्ट्वा मानुषेषु सुदुर्लभाम्
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭastvabhavadrāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahārathaḥ
maithilyāḥ satkriyāṁ dṛṣṭvā mānuṣeṣu sudurlabhām

translations.english: Thereupon, witnessing the honour that had been accorded to Maithili, rare among men, Rāma became well pleased, as also that mighty car-warrior, Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तां सर्वरीं प्रीतः पुण्यां शशिनिभाननः
अर्चितस्तापसैः सिद्धैरुवास रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
tatastāṁ sarvarīṁ prītaḥ puṇyāṁ śaśinibhānanaḥ
arcitastāpasaiḥ siddhairuvāsa raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: Then Raghu's son, ministered to by the ascetic, happily spent the delightful night there, with her face resembling the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामभिषिच्य हुताग्निकान्
आपृच्छेतां नरव्याघ्रौ तापसान्वनगोचरान्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ rātryāṁ vyatītāyāmabhiṣicya hutāgnikān
āpṛcchetāṁ naravyāghrau tāpasānvanagocarān

translations.english: On the night having passed away, those foremost of men, after performing their ablutions, enquired of the ascetics performing fire sacrifices, who lived in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तावूचुस्ते वनचरास्तापसा धर्मचारिणः
वनस्य तस्य संचारं राक्षसैः समभिप्लुतम्
verses.transliteration:
tāvūcuste vanacarāstāpasā dharmacāriṇaḥ
vanasya tasya saṁcāraṁ rākṣasaiḥ samabhiplutam

translations.english: Thereat the righteous ascetics ranging the forest said that all the sides of the forest were infested by Rākşasas. “Ferocious beasts feasting on blood, and Rākşasas, O Rāghava, living on human beings, wearing various shapes, abide in this mighty forest."

verses.sanskrit:
एष पन्था महर्षीणां फलान्याहरतां वने
अनेन तु वनं दुर्गं गन्तुं राघव ते क्षमम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa panthā maharṣīṇāṁ phalānyāharatāṁ vane
anena tu vanaṁ durgaṁ gantuṁ rāghava te kṣamam

translations.english: This is the path of the Maharșis, who procure fruits in the forest. By this way you will be able to enter the impracticable wild, O Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव तैः प्राञ्जलिभिस्तपस्विभि;र्द्विजैः कृतस्वस्त्ययनः परंतपः
वनं सभार्यः प्रविवेश राघवः; सलक्ष्मणः सूर्य इवाभ्रमण्डलम्
verses.transliteration:
itīva taiḥ prāñjalibhistapasvibhi;rdvijaiḥ kṛtasvastyayanaḥ paraṁtapaḥ
vanaṁ sabhāryaḥ praviveśa rāghavaḥ; salakṣmaṇaḥ sūrya ivābhramaṇḍalam

translations.english: Thus addressed by the ascetic twice-born ones, and having been blessed by them, that repressor of foes, Rāghava, entered the forest in company with his wife and Lakşmaņa, like the sun entering a mass of clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्ब्रह्मभवनप्रख्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्
ब्रह्मविद्भिर्महाभागैर्ब्राह्मणैरुपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
tadbrahmabhavanaprakhyaṁ brahmaghoṣanināditam
brahmavidbhirmahābhāgairbrāhmaṇairupaśobhitam

translations.english: Beholding that collection of asylums belonging to the ascetics, resembling the regions of Brahmă, resonant with the voices of Vedic recitations; and grateful; with highly pious Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas, the exceedingly energetic and graceful Rāghava entered the same, having first unstrung his mighty bow.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तं सोममिवोद्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणः
मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जानाः प्रत्यगृह्णन्दृढव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
te taṁ somamivodyantaṁ dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇaḥ
maṅgalāni prayuñjānāḥ pratyagṛhṇandṛḍhavratāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, seeing the righteous Rāma resembling the moon risen, as well as Lakşmaņa and the illustrious Vaidehī, those. Maharsis endued with spiritual intuition, came forward (to meet the incomers); and, having uttered benedictions, those persons of rigid VOWS, received them.

verses.sanskrit:
रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम्
ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
rūpasaṁhananaṁ lakṣmīṁ saukumāryaṁ suveṣatām
dadṛśurvismitākārā rāmasya vanavāsinaḥ

translations.english: And those dwellers of the wood, struck with wonder, beheld Rāma's tender grace and loveliness and elegance of dress.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेहीं लक्ष्मणं रामं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव
आश्चर्यभूतान्ददृशुः सर्वे ते वनचारिणः
verses.transliteration:
vaidehīṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ rāmaṁ netrairanimiṣairiva
āścaryabhūtāndadṛśuḥ sarve te vanacāriṇaḥ

translations.english: And struck with astonishment, those inhabitants of the woods of pre-eminent piety saw Vaidehī, Lakşmaņa and Rāma, with winkless eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्रैनं हि महाभागाः सर्वभूतहिते रताः
अतिथिं पर्णशालायां राघवं संन्यवेशयन्
verses.transliteration:
atrainaṁ hi mahābhāgāḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
atithiṁ parṇaśālāyāṁ rāghavaṁ saṁnyaveśayan

translations.english: And those persons of exalted virtue, engaged in the welfare of all creatures, made Rāghava, their guest, sit down in their thatched cottage.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामस्य सत्कृत्य विधिना पावकोपमाः
आजह्रुस्ते महाभागाः सलिलं धर्मचारिणः
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmasya satkṛtya vidhinā pāvakopamāḥ
ājahruste mahābhāgāḥ salilaṁ dharmacāriṇaḥ

translations.english: Then, having received Rāma respectfully according to scriptural prescription, those virtuous ones of eminent piety, resembling fire, procured water (for Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं भवता रक्ष्या भवद्विषयवासिनः
नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा त्वं नो राजा जनेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ bhavatā rakṣyā bhavadviṣayavāsinaḥ
nagarastho vanastho vā tvaṁ no rājā janeśvaraḥ

translations.english: And we, being in your dominions, ought to be protected by you. Whether living in the city or in the woods, you, lord of men, are our sovereign.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यस्तदण्डा वयं राजञ्जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः
रक्षितव्यास्त्वया शश्वद्गर्भभूतास्तपोधनाः
verses.transliteration:
nyastadaṇḍā vayaṁ rājañjitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ
rakṣitavyāstvayā śaśvadgarbhabhūtāstapodhanāḥ

translations.english: We have renounced chastising others; and, O monarch, we have conquered our anger, and subdued our passions. Therefore, even as a child in its mother's womb (should be protected by her), should we be protected by you."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मूलैः पुष्पैर्वन्यैश्च राघवम्
अन्यैश्च विविधाहारैः सलक्ष्मणमपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā phalairmūlaiḥ puṣpairvanyaiśca rāghavam
anyaiśca vividhāhāraiḥ salakṣmaṇamapūjayan

translations.english: Having said this, they entertained Rāghava, along with Laksmana, with fruits and roots and flowers and diverse other edibles procurable in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
तथान्ये तापसाः सिद्धा रामं वैश्वानरोपमाः
न्यायवृत्ता यथान्यायं तर्पयामासुरीश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
tathānye tāpasāḥ siddhā rāmaṁ vaiśvānaropamāḥ
nyāyavṛttā yathānyāyaṁ tarpayāmāsurīśvaram

translations.english: In the same way, other ascetics of accomplished purposes, living lives of integrity, duly pleased that lord, Rāma, resembling Vaisvānara.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतातिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति
आमन्त्र्य स मुनीन्सर्वान्वनमेवान्वगाहत
verses.transliteration:
kṛtātithyo'tha rāmastu sūryasyodayanaṁ prati
āmantrya sa munīnsarvānvanamevānvagāhata

translations.english: Having received the homage of the ascetics, Rāma about sun-rise, having greeted them all, entered into the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं शार्दूलवृकसेवितम्
ध्वस्तवृक्षलतागुल्मं दुर्दर्श सलिलाशयम्
verses.transliteration:
nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṁ śārdūlavṛkasevitam
dhvastavṛkṣalatāgulmaṁ durdarśa salilāśayam

translations.english: And Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, saw the heart of the forest abounding in various kinds of beasts, ranged by bears and tigers, with its trees and shrubs torn and trampled, its pools turbid, and its birds crying.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धः प्रजाः काल इवान्तकः
स कृत्वा भैरवं नादं चालयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
abhyadhāvatsusaṁkruddhaḥ prajāḥ kāla ivāntakaḥ
sa kṛtvā bhairavaṁ nādaṁ cālayanniva medinīm

translations.english: Having seen Rāma and Laksmana as well as Sītā the daughter of Mithilā, he growing angry, rushed (against them), like the Destroyer himself rushing against creatures at the universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गेनादाय वैदेहीमपक्रम्य ततोऽब्रवीत्
युवां जटाचीरधरौ सभार्यौ क्षीणजीवितौ
verses.transliteration:
aṅgenādāya vaidehīmapakramya tato'bravīt
yuvāṁ jaṭācīradharau sabhāryau kṣīṇajīvitau

translations.english: Uttering a dreadful yell, and, as if making the earth tremble, he took Vaidehi on his waist, and, going a little distance, said, “O you wearing bark and matted locks, O you of feeble strength, that accompanied by your (common) wife, have entered the forest of Dandaka, bearing bows and arrows and scimitars, why, being ascetics, do you wish to associate with a (single) woman?

verses.sanskrit:
चरामि सायुधो नित्यमृषिमांसानि भक्षयन्
इयं नारी वरारोहा मम भर्या भविष्यति
युवयोः पापयोश्चाहं पास्यामि रुधिरं मृधे
verses.transliteration:
carāmi sāyudho nityamṛṣimāṁsāni bhakṣayan
iyaṁ nārī varārohā mama bharyā bhaviṣyati
yuvayoḥ pāpayoścāhaṁ pāsyāmi rudhiraṁ mṛdhe

translations.english: You wicked wretches, you imf.ous wights, who are you that bring disgrace upon ascetics? I am a Rākṣasa, Virādha by name. This forest is my fastness. Accoutred in arms, I range (here), feeding on the flesh of ascetics. This transcendentally beauteous one shall be my wife. And in battle I shall drink your blood, wretches that you are.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो धृष्टं विराधस्य दुरात्मनः
श्रुत्वा सगर्वितं वाक्यं संभ्रान्ता जनकात्मजा
सीता प्रावेपतोद्वेगात्प्रवाते कदली यथा
verses.transliteration:
tasyaivaṁ bruvato dhṛṣṭaṁ virādhasya durātmanaḥ
śrutvā sagarvitaṁ vākyaṁ saṁbhrāntā janakātmajā
sītā prāvepatodvegātpravāte kadalī yathā

translations.english: Hearing the wicked and vaunting speech of the impious Virādha, as he said this, Janaka's daughter, Sītā, began to tremble from fear, like a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
तां दृष्ट्वा राघवः सीतां विराधाङ्कगतां शुभाम्
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītāṁ virādhāṅkagatāṁ śubhām
abravīllakṣmaṇaṁ vākyaṁ mukhena pariśuṣyatā

translations.english: Seeing the graceful Sītā on the waist of Virādha, Rāghava with a blank countenance said to Laksmana,

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य सौम्य नरेन्द्रस्य जनकस्यात्मसंभवाम्
मम भार्यां शुभाचारां विराधाङ्के प्रवेशिताम्
अत्यन्त सुखसंवृद्धां राजपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
paśya saumya narendrasya janakasyātmasaṁbhavām
mama bhāryāṁ śubhācārāṁ virādhāṅke praveśitām
atyanta sukhasaṁvṛddhāṁ rājaputrīṁ yaśasvinīm

translations.english: O amiable one, behold the daughter of king Janaka, my wife of pure ways, an illustrious princess brought up in luxury, on Virādha's waist.

verses.sanskrit:
या न तुष्यति राज्येन पुत्रार्थे दीर्घदर्शिनी
ययाहं सर्वभूतानां हितः प्रस्थापितो वनम्
अद्येदानीं सकामा सा या माता मम मध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
yā na tuṣyati rājyena putrārthe dīrghadarśinī
yayāhaṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ hitaḥ prasthāpito vanam
adyedānīṁ sakāmā sā yā mātā mama madhyamā

translations.english: Lakşmaņa, what had been wished for by Kaikeyi with reference to us, (has taken place), and the dear boon (that she had asked) has born fruit. That far-sighted lady, my second mother, who had not been satisfied with having secured the kingdom in the interests of her son, and by whom I that was dear to her above all other creatures, had been banished to the woods, has to-day her wishes crowned with success.

verses.sanskrit:
परस्पर्शात्तु वैदेह्या न दुःखतरमस्ति मे
पितुर्विनाशात्सौमित्रे स्वराज्यहरणात्तथा
verses.transliteration:
parasparśāttu vaidehyā na duḥkhataramasti me
piturvināśātsaumitre svarājyaharaṇāttathā

translations.english: O Sumitra's son, nothing can impart to me greater anguish than the touching of Vaidehi by another, which surpasses my father's demise and my having been deprived of the kingdom.”'

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे बाष्पशोकपरिप्लुते
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvati kākutsthe bāṣpaśokapariplute
abravīllakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho ruddho nāga iva śvasan

translations.english: As Kākutstha with his eyes flooded with tears was speaking thus, Lakşmaņa flying into a rage, spoke like to a confined elephant:

verses.sanskrit:
अनाथ इव भूतानां नाथस्त्वं वासवोपमः
मया प्रेष्येण काकुत्स्थ किमर्थं परितप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
anātha iva bhūtānāṁ nāthastvaṁ vāsavopamaḥ
mayā preṣyeṇa kākutstha kimarthaṁ paritapsyase

translations.english: Why do you, O Kākutstha, being the lord of all creatures and resembling Väsava himself, and also backed by myself, your servant, grieve like one forlorn?

verses.sanskrit:
शरेण निहतस्याद्य मया क्रुद्धेन रक्षसः
विराधस्य गतासोर्हि मही पास्यति शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
śareṇa nihatasyādya mayā kruddhena rakṣasaḥ
virādhasya gatāsorhi mahī pāsyati śoṇitam

translations.english: The earth shall drink the gore of this Rākşasa, Virādha, when deprived of life, after he has been slain with a shaft by my angry self.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यकामे मम क्रोधो भरते यो बभूव ह
तं विराधे विमोक्ष्यामि वज्री वज्रमिवाचले
verses.transliteration:
rājyakāme mama krodho bharate yo babhūva ha
taṁ virādhe vimokṣyāmi vajrī vajramivācale

translations.english: That ire of mine which I had conceived against Bharata hankering after the kingdom, will I discharge on Virādha; even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt hurls his weapon at a hi!l.

verses.sanskrit:
मम भुजबलवेगवेगितः; पततु शरोऽस्य महान्महोरसि
व्यपनयतु तनोश्च जीवितं; पततु ततश्च महीं विघूर्णितः
verses.transliteration:
mama bhujabalavegavegitaḥ; patatu śaro'sya mahānmahorasi
vyapanayatu tanośca jīvitaṁ; patatu tataśca mahīṁ vighūrṇitaḥ

translations.english: Let my mighty arrow acquiring velocity from the speed imparted to it through the energy of my arms, light on his huge breast, and force his life from forth his body; and let him whirling (at length) fall down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोवाच पुनर्वाक्यं विराधः पूरयन्वनम्
आत्मानं पृच्छते ब्रूतं कौ युवां क्व गमिष्यथः
verses.transliteration:
athovāca punarvākyaṁ virādhaḥ pūrayanvanam
ātmānaṁ pṛcchate brūtaṁ kau yuvāṁ kva gamiṣyathaḥ

translations.english: Then Virādha again spoke filling the forest, Do you tell me who ask you, who are you and whither are you going? The North-West Provinces text has additional Sloka: Having said this, the graceful Lakşmaņa spoke to Virādha as if jestingly, Who are you that coming to the forest, are ranging it pleasantly?-

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रियो वृत्तसंपन्नौ विद्धि नौ वनगोचरौ
त्वां तु वेदितुमिच्छावः कस्त्वं चरसि दण्डकान्
verses.transliteration:
kṣatriyo vṛttasaṁpannau viddhi nau vanagocarau
tvāṁ tu veditumicchāvaḥ kastvaṁ carasi daṇḍakān

translations.english: Thereupon, the highly energetic Rāma answered the Rākşasa with a flaming face, when he had thus asked (Rāma) that he belonged to the Iksvaku race. Know us that are in the forest, for Kșatriyas of respectable character. I also am anxious of knowing who you are, wandering in the Dandakas.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच विराधस्तु रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्
हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते राजन्निबोध मम राघव
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca virādhastu rāmaṁ satyaparākramam
hanta vakṣyāmi te rājannibodha mama rāghava

translations.english: Virădha answered Råma having truth for his prowess, Ah! I will tell you, O king. Do you,O Răghava understand!

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रः किल जयस्याहं माता मम शतह्रदा
विराध इति मामाहुः पृथिव्यां सर्वराक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
putraḥ kila jayasyāhaṁ mātā mama śatahradā
virādha iti māmāhuḥ pṛthivyāṁ sarvarākṣasāḥ

translations.english: I am son of Java, and my mother is Satahradā. All the Rāksasas of the earth have called me Virādha.

verses.sanskrit:
तपसा चापि मे प्राप्ता ब्रह्मणो हि प्रसादजा
शस्त्रेणावध्यता लोकेऽच्छेद्याभेद्यत्वमेव च
verses.transliteration:
tapasā cāpi me prāptā brahmaṇo hi prasādajā
śastreṇāvadhyatā loke'cchedyābhedyatvameva ca

translations.english: Having gratified Brahmă by my asceticism, IⓇreceived (this boon) that none in the world would be able to slay me by mangling my body with weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रामः प्रत्युवाचेदं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
राक्षसं विकृताकारं विराधं पापचेतसं
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rāmaḥ pratyuvācedaṁ kopasaṁraktalocanaḥ
rākṣasaṁ vikṛtākāraṁ virādhaṁ pāpacetasaṁ

translations.english: Forsaking this fair one, do you, renouncing all hope (of either recovering her or vanquishing me), speedily flee away to that place whence you had come; else I shall deprive you of your lives. Thereat, Rāma with his eyes reddened through wrath replied to that Rākşasa of a deformed shape, the wicked Viradha.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुद्र धिक्त्वां तु हीनार्थं मृत्युमन्वेषसे ध्रुवम्
रणे संप्राप्स्यसे तिष्ठ न मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
kṣudra dhiktvāṁ tu hīnārthaṁ mṛtyumanveṣase dhruvam
raṇe saṁprāpsyase tiṣṭha na me jīvangamiṣyasi

translations.english: Little! shame on you of base purposes! You surely seek your own death; and (death) you shall get in battle. Stay! You escapist me not with life.

verses.sanskrit:
धनुषा ज्यागुणवता सप्तबाणान्मुमोच ह
रुक्मपुङ्खान्महावेगान्सुपर्णानिलतुल्यगान्
verses.transliteration:
dhanuṣā jyāguṇavatā saptabāṇānmumoca ha
rukmapuṅkhānmahāvegānsuparṇānilatulyagān

translations.english: Then stringing his bow, Rāma, speedily aiming at the Rākşasa, pierced him with sharpened shafts; and (then) from his bow-string let go seven shafts, having their feathered parts plaited with good, furnished with great velocity, and coursing like Suparna or the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शरीरं विराधस्य भित्त्वा बर्हिणवाससः
निपेतुः शोणितादिग्धा धरण्यां पावकोपमाः
verses.transliteration:
te śarīraṁ virādhasya bhittvā barhiṇavāsasaḥ
nipetuḥ śoṇitādigdhā dharaṇyāṁ pāvakopamāḥ

translations.english: Thereat, resembling flames, those arrows furnished with peacocks, feathers, pierced. Viradha's body, and fell to the earth, covered with blood.

verses.sanskrit:
स विनद्य महानादं शूलं शक्रध्वजोपमम्
प्रगृह्याशोभत तदा व्यात्तानन इवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
sa vinadya mahānādaṁ śūlaṁ śakradhvajopamam
pragṛhyāśobhata tadā vyāttānana ivāntakaḥ

translations.english: And sending forth a mighty roar, he took up a dart resembling the banner of Sakra and he then appeared like the Destroyer* with opening mouth.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छूलं वज्रसंकाशं गगने ज्वलनोपमम्
द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां चिच्छेद रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः
verses.transliteration:
tacchūlaṁ vajrasaṁkāśaṁ gagane jvalanopamam
dvābhyāṁ śarābhyāṁ ciccheda rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: That best of those bearing arms cut off with two arrows that dart resembling the thunder-bolt and flaming in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रौद्रस्य सौमित्रिर्बाहुं सव्यं बभञ्ज ह
रामस्तु दक्षिणं बाहुं तरसा तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tasya raudrasya saumitrirbāhuṁ savyaṁ babhañja ha
rāmastu dakṣiṇaṁ bāhuṁ tarasā tasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: And Sumitra's son broke his left arm; while Rāma at once broke the Rākşasa's right one.

verses.sanskrit:
स भग्नबाहुः संविग्नो निपपाताशु राक्षसः
धरण्यां मेघसंकाशो वज्रभिन्न इवाचलः
इदं प्रोवाच काकुत्स्थं विराधः पुरुषर्षभम्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhagnabāhuḥ saṁvigno nipapātāśu rākṣasaḥ
dharaṇyāṁ meghasaṁkāśo vajrabhinna ivācalaḥ
idaṁ provāca kākutsthaṁ virādhaḥ puruṣarṣabham

translations.english: On his arms being broken, the Raksasa resembling a mass of clouds, growing weak, sank down on the ground in a swoon, like a hill riven by the thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
कौसल्या सुप्रजास्तात रामस्त्वं विदितो मया
वैदेही च महाभागा लक्ष्मणश्च महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
kausalyā suprajāstāta rāmastvaṁ vidito mayā
vaidehī ca mahābhāgā lakṣmaṇaśca mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Now I know you that are Rāma, the worthy Son of Kausalyā, my child; as well as the highly virtuous Vaidehi and the renowned Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिशापादहं घोरां प्रविष्टो राक्षसीं तनुम्
तुम्बुरुर्नाम गन्धर्वः शप्तो वैश्वरणेन हि
verses.transliteration:
abhiśāpādahaṁ ghorāṁ praviṣṭo rākṣasīṁ tanum
tumbururnāma gandharvaḥ śapto vaiśvaraṇena hi

translations.english: By virtue of a curse, I entered this dreadful Räkşasi form, I a Gandharva, having been cursed by Vaisravaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसाद्यमानश्च मया सोऽब्रवीन्मां महायशाः
यदा दाशरथी रामस्त्वां वधिष्यति संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
prasādyamānaśca mayā so'bravīnmāṁ mahāyaśāḥ
yadā dāśarathī rāmastvāṁ vadhiṣyati saṁyuge

translations.english: Being propitiated by me, that greatly famous one said, 'When Rāma the son of Dasaratha, shall slay you in encounter, you, attaining your natural condition, shall repair to the celestial regions.'

verses.sanskrit:
तदा प्रकृतिमापन्नो भवान्स्वर्गं गमिष्यति
इति वैश्रवणो राजा रम्भासक्तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tadā prakṛtimāpanno bhavānsvargaṁ gamiṣyati
iti vaiśravaṇo rājā rambhāsaktamuvāca ha

translations.english: Getting wroth, he cursed me, who had been absent; and thus did king Vaiśravaņa address me, who had conceived love for Rambhā.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुपस्थीयमानो मां संक्रुद्धो व्यजहार ह
तव प्रसादान्मुक्तोऽहमभिशापात्सुदारुणात्
भवनं स्वं गमिष्यामि स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु परंतप
verses.transliteration:
anupasthīyamāno māṁ saṁkruddho vyajahāra ha
tava prasādānmukto'hamabhiśāpātsudāruṇāt
bhavanaṁ svaṁ gamiṣyāmi svasti vo'stu paraṁtapa

translations.english: Through your grace have I been freed from this fearful curse, I shall (now) repair to heaven. Hail, O repressor of foes!

verses.sanskrit:
तं क्षिप्रमभिगच्छ त्वं स ते श्रेयो विधास्यति
अवटे चापि मां राम निक्षिप्य कुशली व्रज
verses.transliteration:
taṁ kṣipramabhigaccha tvaṁ sa te śreyo vidhāsyati
avaṭe cāpi māṁ rāma nikṣipya kuśalī vraja

translations.english: Half a Yojana hence, my child, dwells the righteous and potent Maharși, Śarabharga, resembling the Sun. Seek him speedily: he will bring about your good. Casting me (into this pit) in the wood, do you, O Rama, peacefully go your way. Even this is the eternal usage of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं विराधः शरपीडितः
बभूव स्वर्गसंप्राप्तो न्यस्तदेहो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu kākutsthaṁ virādhaḥ śarapīḍitaḥ
babhūva svargasaṁprāpto nyastadeho mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Those that die in the forest, attain eternal regions. Having said this to Kākutstha, the mighty Viradha, afflicted with arrows, having his body deposited (in the pit), attained heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मुक्तकण्ठमुत्क्षिप्य शङ्कुकर्णं महास्वनम्
विराधं प्राक्षिपच्छ्वभ्रे नदन्तं भैरवस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ muktakaṇṭhamutkṣipya śaṅkukarṇaṁ mahāsvanam
virādhaṁ prākṣipacchvabhre nadantaṁ bhairavasvanam

translations.english: Then when his throat had been freed (Laks maņa) cast into the pit Virādha having ears resembling javelins, sending loud and dreadful sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तौ काञ्चनचित्रकार्मुकौ; निहत्य रक्षः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम्
विजह्रतुस्तौ मुदितौ महावने; दिवि स्थितौ चन्द्रदिवाकराविव
verses.transliteration:
tatastu tau kāñcanacitrakārmukau; nihatya rakṣaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm
vijahratustau muditau mahāvane; divi sthitau candradivākarāviva

translations.english: Having thrown him into the hole in the earth, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, their fear being removed, and covered the Rākṣasa with rocks. And having slain the Rākşasa and taken Mithila's daughter, those ones having bows decked in gold, being delighted, rejoiced in that mighty forest, like the sun and the moon seated in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
हत्वा तु तं भीमबलं विराधं राक्षसं वने
ततः सीतां परिष्वज्य समाश्वास्य च वीर्यवान्
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणां रामो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसं
verses.transliteration:
hatvā tu taṁ bhīmabalaṁ virādhaṁ rākṣasaṁ vane
tataḥ sītāṁ pariṣvajya samāśvāsya ca vīryavān
abravīllakṣmaṇāṁ rāmo bhrātaraṁ dīptatejasaṁ

translations.english: Having in the forest slain the Rākṣasa Virādha possessed of tremendous strength, Rāma endued with prowess, embracing and cheering Sītā, spoke to his brother Lakşınaņa of flaming energy, saying, This dense forest is hard to live in; nor are reacquainted with the was of the wood. Therefore will we speedily repair to the ascetic Sarabhanga. Thereupon Rāghava set out for the hermitage of Sarabhanga.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य देवप्रभावस्य तपसा भावितात्मनः
समीपे शरभङ्गस्य ददर्श महदद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya devaprabhāvasya tapasā bhāvitātmanaḥ
samīpe śarabhaṅgasya dadarśa mahadadbhutam

translations.english: And Rāma beheld a mighty wonder near that one of celestial virtue, who had purified his soul through asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
विभ्राजमानं वपुषा सूर्यवैश्वानरोपमम्
असंस्पृशन्तं वसुधां ददर्श विबुधेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
vibhrājamānaṁ vapuṣā sūryavaiśvānaropamam
asaṁspṛśantaṁ vasudhāṁ dadarśa vibudheśvaram

translations.english: He saw the lord of the celestials, possessed of a resplendent person, resembling in effulgence the sun or Vaisvanara-mounted on a superb car (saw) him that is followed by all the celestials, stationed in the sky, not touching the earth, adorned in luminous ornaments-the god dressed in a clean appear!

verses.sanskrit:
हरिभिर्वाजिभिर्युक्तमन्तरिक्षगतं रथम्
ददर्शादूरतस्तस्य तरुणादित्यसंनिभम्
verses.transliteration:
haribhirvājibhiryuktamantarikṣagataṁ ratham
dadarśādūratastasya taruṇādityasaṁnibham

translations.english: Worshipped by many a high-should personage dressed in the same way. And from a distance, (Rāma) saw the car stationed in the sky yoked with green steeds-resembling the infant sun;

verses.sanskrit:
पाण्डुराभ्रघनप्रख्यं चन्द्रमण्डलसंनिभम्
अपश्यद्विमलं छत्रं चित्रमाल्योपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
pāṇḍurābhraghanaprakhyaṁ candramaṇḍalasaṁnibham
apaśyadvimalaṁ chatraṁ citramālyopaśobhitam

translations.english: And he saw the spotless umbrella possessing the beauty of a mass of white clouds, resembling the lunar disc, and graced with variegated wreaths.

verses.sanskrit:
चामरव्यजने चाग्र्ये रुक्मदण्डे महाधने
गृहीते वननारीभ्यां धूयमाने च मूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
cāmaravyajane cāgrye rukmadaṇḍe mahādhane
gṛhīte vananārībhyāṁ dhūyamāne ca mūrdhani

translations.english: And his (Indira's) head was being fanned by two chowris, costly and furnished with golden handles, held by two magnificent damsels; and innumerable Gandharvas and Siddhas and prime sages were hymning the celestial stationed in the welkin. And seeing Sarabhanga engaged in converse with Satakratu, Rāma said to Laksmana (the following words). And pointing out the car, Rāma showed the wonder to his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा शतक्रतुं तत्र रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
ये हयाः पुरुहूतस्य पुरा शक्रस्य नः श्रुताः
अन्तरिक्षगता दिव्यास्त इमे हरयो ध्रुवम्
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā śatakratuṁ tatra rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
ye hayāḥ puruhūtasya purā śakrasya naḥ śrutāḥ
antarikṣagatā divyāsta ime harayo dhruvam

translations.english: The steeds standing in the sky are for certain those of which we had formerly heard as beionging to Sakra of many sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे च पुरुषव्याघ्र ये तिष्ठन्त्यभितो रथम्
शतं शतं कुण्डलिनो युवानः खड्गपाणयः
verses.transliteration:
ime ca puruṣavyāghra ye tiṣṭhantyabhito ratham
śataṁ śataṁ kuṇḍalino yuvānaḥ khaḍgapāṇayaḥ

translations.english: And, you foremost of men, these youths envisioning (the celestial) by hundreds, wearing earrings, and bearing swords in their hands, are broad of chest, have arms resembling bludgeons in size, and are clad in crimson vesture, like to tigers incapable of being approached.

verses.sanskrit:
उरोदेशेषु सर्वेषां हारा ज्वलनसंनिभाः
रूपं बिभ्रति सौमित्रे पञ्चविंशतिवार्षिकम्
verses.transliteration:
urodeśeṣu sarveṣāṁ hārā jvalanasaṁnibhāḥ
rūpaṁ bibhrati saumitre pañcaviṁśativārṣikam

translations.english: Over the breasts of all appear chains of blazing sheen; and, O son of Sumitrā, their beauty appears that of five and twenty.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्धि किल देवानां वयो भवति नित्यदा
यथेमे पुरुषव्याघ्रा दृश्यन्ते प्रियदर्शनाः
verses.transliteration:
etaddhi kila devānāṁ vayo bhavati nityadā
yatheme puruṣavyāghrā dṛśyante priyadarśanāḥ

translations.english: And even this is the ever-enduring age of the celestials, as these foremost of men of sweet looks appear.

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव सह वैदेह्या मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ लक्ष्मण
यावज्जनाम्यहं व्यक्तं क एष द्युतिमान्रथे
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva saha vaidehyā muhūrtaṁ tiṣṭha lakṣmaṇa
yāvajjanāmyahaṁ vyaktaṁ ka eṣa dyutimānrathe

translations.english: O Laksmana, stay here awhile with Vaidehi, so long as I do not gather who it is that is in the effulgent car.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमुक्त्वा सौमित्रिमिहैव स्थीयतामिति
अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थः शरभङ्गाश्रमं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
tamevamuktvā saumitrimihaiva sthīyatāmiti
abhicakrāma kākutsthaḥ śarabhaṅgāśramaṁ prati

translations.english: Saying to Sumitrās son, Stay here, Kākutstha bent his steps towards Sarabhaiga's asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समभिगच्छन्तं प्रेक्ष्य रामं शचीपतिः
शरभङ्गमनुज्ञाप्य विबुधानिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samabhigacchantaṁ prekṣya rāmaṁ śacīpatiḥ
śarabhaṅgamanujñāpya vibudhānidamabravīt

translations.english: And seeing Rāma approach, Saci's lord, taking Sarabhanga's permission, addressed the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
इहोपयात्यसौ रामो यावन्मां नाभिभाषते
निष्ठां नयत तावत्तु ततो मां द्रष्टुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
ihopayātyasau rāmo yāvanmāṁ nābhibhāṣate
niṣṭhāṁ nayata tāvattu tato māṁ draṣṭumarhati

translations.english: Rāma is coming hither. Do you set out for another place, ere he yet addresses me. He is not fit to behold me (now.)

verses.sanskrit:
जितवन्तं कृतार्थं च द्रष्टाहमचिरादिमम्
कर्म ह्यनेन कर्तव्यं महदन्यैः सुदुष्करम्
verses.transliteration:
jitavantaṁ kṛtārthaṁ ca draṣṭāhamacirādimam
karma hyanena kartavyaṁ mahadanyaiḥ suduṣkaram

translations.english: When he shall have vanquished (his foe in fight) and won success, shall I readily show myself to him. He shall have to achieve an act incapable of being achieved by others.

verses.sanskrit:
इति वज्री तमामन्त्र्य मानयित्वा च तापसं
रथेन हरियुक्तेन ययौ दिवमरिंदमः
verses.transliteration:
iti vajrī tamāmantrya mānayitvā ca tāpasaṁ
rathena hariyuktena yayau divamariṁdamaḥ

translations.english: Then rendering homage to that anchorite and conversing with him, the wielder of the thunderbolt-subduer of enemies-repaired to heaven in a car yoked with steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयाते तु सहस्राक्षे राघवः सपरिच्छदः
अग्निहोत्रमुपासीनं शरभङ्गमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
prayāte tu sahasrākṣe rāghavaḥ saparicchadaḥ
agnihotramupāsīnaṁ śarabhaṅgamupāgamat

translations.english: When the thousand-eyed one had gone away, Rāghava accompanied by his companions appeared before Sarabhanga in the (Agni-hotra) chamber.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पादौ च संगृह्य रामः सीता च लक्ष्मणः
निषेदुस्तदनुज्ञाता लब्धवासा निमन्त्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya pādau ca saṁgṛhya rāmaḥ sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
niṣedustadanujñātā labdhavāsā nimantritāḥ

translations.english: Taking his feet, Rāma, Sītā and Lakşmaņa sat down with the permission of the ascetic, who received them and set apart quarters for them.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शक्रोपयानं तु पर्यपृच्छत्स राघवः
शरभङ्गश्च तत्सर्वं राघवाय न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śakropayānaṁ tu paryapṛcchatsa rāghavaḥ
śarabhaṅgaśca tatsarvaṁ rāghavāya nyavedayat

translations.english: Then Rāghava questioned (the sage) concerning the visit of Sakra; and Sarabhanga related everything to Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
मामेष वरदो राम ब्रह्मलोकं निनीषति
जितमुग्रेण तपसा दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
māmeṣa varado rāma brahmalokaṁ ninīṣati
jitamugreṇa tapasā duṣprāpamakṛtātmabhiḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, this bestower of boons wishes to take me to the regions of Brahmā. I have conquered them, incapable of being attained by persons that have not schooled themselves, by virtue of fierce austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं ज्ञात्वा नरव्याघ्र वर्तमानमदूरतः
ब्रह्मलोकं न गच्छामि त्वामदृष्ट्वा प्रियातिथिम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ jñātvā naravyāghra vartamānamadūrataḥ
brahmalokaṁ na gacchāmi tvāmadṛṣṭvā priyātithim

translations.english: O chief of men, knowing that you were near, I became anxious to go to the minor celestial regions and the supreme heaven (of Brahmā), after I had seen you, righteous and high-souled, who are my dear guest now.

verses.sanskrit:
समागम्य गमिष्यामि त्रिदिवं देवसेवितम्
अक्षया नरशार्दूल जिता लोका मया शुभाः
ब्राह्म्याश्च नाकपृष्ठ्याश्च प्रतिगृह्णीष्व मामकान्
verses.transliteration:
samāgamya gamiṣyāmi tridivaṁ devasevitam
akṣayā naraśārdūla jitā lokā mayā śubhāḥ
brāhmyāśca nākapṛṣṭhyāśca pratigṛhṇīṣva māmakān

translations.english: O foremost of men, having had a meeting with you, a high-souled prince of righteous nature, I have for aye attained the excellent regions of Brahmã and Nākaprştha. Do you receive them as pertaining to me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो नरव्याघ्रः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः
ऋषिणा शरभङ्गेन राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamukto naravyāghraḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
ṛṣiṇā śarabhaṅgena rāghavo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Thus addressed by the sage, Sarabhanga, that best of men, Rāghava, versed in every branch of learning, said.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमेवाहरिष्यामि सर्वाँल्लोकान्महामुने
आवासं त्वहमिच्छामि प्रदिष्टमिह कानने
verses.transliteration:
ahamevāhariṣyāmi sarvā̐llokānmahāmune
āvāsaṁ tvahamicchāmi pradiṣṭamiha kānane

translations.english: O mighty anchorite, I shall acquire all those regions myself. I now wish that you may direct me as to my abode in this forest.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु शक्रतुल्यबलेन वै
शरभङ्गो महाप्राज्ञः पुनरेवाब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
rāghaveṇaivamuktastu śakratulyabalena vai
śarabhaṅgo mahāprājñaḥ punarevābravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by Rāghava resembling Sakra in strength, the eminently wise Sarabhanga again said,

verses.sanskrit:
सुतीक्ष्णमभिगच्छ त्वं शुचौ देशे तपस्विनम्
रमणीये वनोद्देशे स ते वासं विधास्यति
verses.transliteration:
sutīkṣṇamabhigaccha tvaṁ śucau deśe tapasvinam
ramaṇīye vanoddeśe sa te vāsaṁ vidhāsyati

translations.english: O Rāma, follow this Mandākini flowing among flowers, which (here runs in an opposite direction to her usual course; and then will you reach there.

verses.sanskrit:
एष पन्था नरव्याघ्र मुहूर्तं पश्य तात माम्
यावज्जहामि गात्राणि जीर्णं त्वचमिवोरगः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa panthā naravyāghra muhūrtaṁ paśya tāta mām
yāvajjahāmi gātrāṇi jīrṇaṁ tvacamivoragaḥ

translations.english: This is your course, you best of men. Do you now, my child, for a space look at me; while I leave of my limbs, even as a serpent renounces its slough.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽग्निं स समाधाय हुत्वा चाज्येन मन्त्रवित्
शरभङ्गो महातेजाः प्रविवेश हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'gniṁ sa samādhāya hutvā cājyena mantravit
śarabhaṅgo mahātejāḥ praviveśa hutāśanam

translations.english: Then preparing a.fire and with Mantras a offering obiations into it, the exceedingly energetic Sarabhanga entered into the fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रोमाणि केशांश्च ददाहाग्निर्महात्मनः
जीर्णं त्वचं तथास्थीनि यच्च मांसं च शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya romāṇi keśāṁśca dadāhāgnirmahātmanaḥ
jīrṇaṁ tvacaṁ tathāsthīni yacca māṁsaṁ ca śoṇitam

translations.english: The fire consumed the down, hair, old skin, bones, flesh and blood of that high-souled one.

verses.sanskrit:
स च पावकसंकाशः कुमारः समपद्यत
उत्थायाग्निचयात्तस्माच्छरभङ्गो व्यरोचत
verses.transliteration:
sa ca pāvakasaṁkāśaḥ kumāraḥ samapadyata
utthāyāgnicayāttasmāccharabhaṅgo vyarocata

translations.english: (Anon) Śarabharga became youth resembling fire; and rising from the flame, he appeared splendid.

verses.sanskrit:
स लोकानाहिताग्नीनामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्
देवानां च व्यतिक्रम्य ब्रह्मलोकं व्यरोहत
verses.transliteration:
sa lokānāhitāgnīnāmṛṣīṇāṁ ca mahātmanām
devānāṁ ca vyatikramya brahmalokaṁ vyarohata

translations.english: And proceeding past the regions of highsouled sages sacrificing with fire, as well as of the celestials, he ascended those of Brahmā.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुण्यकर्मा भुवने द्विजर्षभः; पितामहं सानुचरं ददर्श ह
पितामहश्चापि समीक्ष्य तं द्विजं; ननन्द सुस्वागतमित्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sa puṇyakarmā bhuvane dvijarṣabhaḥ; pitāmahaṁ sānucaraṁ dadarśa ha
pitāmahaścāpi samīkṣya taṁ dvijaṁ; nananda susvāgatamityuvāca ha

translations.english: That one of pious acts done on earth-that best of the twice-born the grandfather, in company with his followers. And the grand-father also, beholding that Brahmana, rejoiced greatly, and said-Hail! race-saw

verses.sanskrit:
शरभङ्गे दिवं प्राप्ते मुनिसंघाः समागताः
अभ्यगच्छन्त काकुत्स्थं रामं ज्वलिततेजसं
verses.transliteration:
śarabhaṅge divaṁ prāpte munisaṁghāḥ samāgatāḥ
abhyagacchanta kākutsthaṁ rāmaṁ jvalitatejasaṁ

translations.english: After Sarabhanga had ascended heaven, ascetics in bodies, assembled together, presented themselves before Kākutstha, Rāma of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिगम्य च धर्मज्ञा रामं धर्मभृतां वरम्
ऊचुः परमधर्मज्ञमृषिसंघाः समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
abhigamya ca dharmajñā rāmaṁ dharmabhṛtāṁ varam
ūcuḥ paramadharmajñamṛṣisaṁghāḥ samāhitāḥ

translations.english: And coming before Rāma, the foremost of those practising righteousness, those sages conversant with morality, met in a body, said to that pre-eminently virtuous one,

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमिक्ष्वाकुकुलस्यास्य पृथिव्याश्च महारथः
प्रधानश्चासि नाथश्च देवानां मघवानिव
verses.transliteration:
tvamikṣvākukulasyāsya pṛthivyāśca mahārathaḥ
pradhānaścāsi nāthaśca devānāṁ maghavāniva

translations.english: A mighty car-warrior, you are the foremost person of the lkshvāku race and the world; as well as their lord, even as Maghavān is the lord of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्रुतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु यशसा विक्रमेण च
पितृव्रतत्वं सत्यं च त्वयि धर्मश्च पुष्कलः
verses.transliteration:
viśrutastriṣu lokeṣu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca
pitṛvratatvaṁ satyaṁ ca tvayi dharmaśca puṣkalaḥ

translations.english: Famous over the three worlds in high worth and prowess, in you are found truth and virtue in profusion and obedience to the mandate of your sire.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वामासाद्य महात्मानं धर्मज्ञं धर्मवत्सलम्
अर्थित्वान्नाथ वक्ष्यामस्तच्च नः क्षन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tvāmāsādya mahātmānaṁ dharmajñaṁ dharmavatsalam
arthitvānnātha vakṣyāmastacca naḥ kṣantumarhasi

translations.english: O lord, it behoves you cognizant of virtue and attached to it, to forgive us for what we as suiters say to you.

verses.sanskrit:
अधार्मस्तु महांस्तात भवेत्तस्य महीपतेः
यो हरेद्बलिषड्भागं न च रक्षति पुत्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
adhārmastu mahāṁstāta bhavettasya mahīpateḥ
yo haredbaliṣaḍbhāgaṁ na ca rakṣati putravat

translations.english: The sin, O lord, of that monarch is mighty that take a sixth part of the subjects' incomes, but dose not protect them as sons.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्नोति शाश्वतीं राम कीर्तिं स बहुवार्षिकीम्
ब्रह्मणः स्थानमासाद्य तत्र चापि महीयते
verses.transliteration:
prāpnoti śāśvatīṁ rāma kīrtiṁ sa bahuvārṣikīm
brahmaṇaḥ sthānamāsādya tatra cāpi mahīyate

translations.english: But he that, setting his heart on protecting the people, dose ever carefully protect all the inhabitants of his dominions, like his own life or like his son dearer to him than life itself, repeat, O Rāma, enduring renown extending over many years, and (at length) attaining the regions of Brahmā, is glorified there.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्करोति परं धर्मं मुनिर्मूलफलाशनः
तत्र राज्ञश्चतुर्भागः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः
verses.transliteration:
yatkaroti paraṁ dharmaṁ munirmūlaphalāśanaḥ
tatra rājñaścaturbhāgaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ

translations.english: The king that protect his subjects righteously, is entitled to a fourth part of the great religious merit that is reaped by an ascetic subsisting on fruits and roots.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽयं ब्राह्मणभूयिष्ठो वानप्रस्थगणो महान्
त्वन्नाथोऽनाथवद्राम राक्षसैर्वध्यते भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
so'yaṁ brāhmaṇabhūyiṣṭho vānaprasthagaṇo mahān
tvannātho'nāthavadrāma rākṣasairvadhyate bhṛśam
