verses.transliteration:
tau tu tenābhyanujñātau kṛtapādābhivandanau
tadāśramātpañcavaṭīṁ jagmatuḥ saha sītayā

translations.english: Then, having saluted his feet, they, taking the saint's permission, set out along with Sītā for the hermitage of Pañcavați.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतचापौ तु नराधिपात्मजौ; विषक्ततूणी समरेष्वकातरौ
यथोपदिष्टेन पथा महर्षिणा; प्रजग्मतुः पञ्चवटीं समाहितौ
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītacāpau tu narādhipātmajau; viṣaktatūṇī samareṣvakātarau
yathopadiṣṭena pathā maharṣiṇā; prajagmatuḥ pañcavaṭīṁ samāhitau

translations.english: And, taking their bows and quivers those sons of the king, of undiminished martial virtue, with intent minds bent their course to Pañcavați by the way laid down by the Maharși.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ पञ्चवटीं गच्छन्नन्तरा रघुनन्दनः
आससाद महाकायं गृध्रं भीमपराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
atha pañcavaṭīṁ gacchannantarā raghunandanaḥ
āsasāda mahākāyaṁ gṛdhraṁ bhīmaparākramam

translations.english: As he was proceeding to Pancavati, Raghu's son saw a huge-bodied vulture of terrible prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा तौ महाभागौ वनस्थं रामलक्ष्मणौ
मेनाते राक्षसं पक्षिं ब्रुवाणौ को भवानिति
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tau mahābhāgau vanasthaṁ rāmalakṣmaṇau
menāte rākṣasaṁ pakṣiṁ bruvāṇau ko bhavāniti

translations.english: And seeing him in the forest, the exalted Rāma and Lakşmaņa, as they were conversing with each other, knowing the bird to be (in reality) a Raksasa, asked him, saying, Who are you?

verses.sanskrit:
स तौ मधुरया वाचा सौम्यया प्रीणयन्निव
उवाच वत्स मां विद्धि वयस्यं पितुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tau madhurayā vācā saumyayā prīṇayanniva
uvāca vatsa māṁ viddhi vayasyaṁ piturātmanaḥ

translations.english: There-upon, in soft and sweet words, he, pleasing them, said, My child, know me for a friend of your father.'

verses.sanskrit:
स तं पितृसखं बुद्ध्वा पूजयामास राघवः
स तस्य कुलमव्यग्रमथ पप्रच्छ नाम च
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ pitṛsakhaṁ buddhvā pūjayāmāsa rāghavaḥ
sa tasya kulamavyagramatha papraccha nāma ca

translations.english: Knowing him to be a friend of his sire, Rāghava paid him homage, and enquired for his name and lineage.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा कुलमात्मानमेव च
आचचक्षे द्विजस्तस्मै सर्वभूतसमुद्भवम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā kulamātmānameva ca
ācacakṣe dvijastasmai sarvabhūtasamudbhavam

translations.english: Hearing Rama's words, he mentioned his own lineage, and related the origin of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वकाले महाबाहो ये प्रजापतयोऽभवन्
तान्मे निगदतः सर्वानादितः शृणु राघव
verses.transliteration:
pūrvakāle mahābāho ye prajāpatayo'bhavan
tānme nigadataḥ sarvānāditaḥ śṛṇu rāghava

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, I shall describe (to you) from the very beginning the (history of) those that were Prajāpatis in days of yore.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थाणुर्मरीचिरत्रिश्च क्रतुश्चैव महाबलः
पुलस्त्यश्चाङ्गिराश्चैव प्रचेताः पुलहस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
sthāṇurmarīciratriśca kratuścaiva mahābalaḥ
pulastyaścāṅgirāścaiva pracetāḥ pulahastathā

translations.english: Listen, O Raghava. Of these, the first is Kardama, then Vikrta, and then Sesa, Sansraya, the powerful Bahuputra, Sthanu, Marici, Atri, the mighty Kratu, Pulastya, Aigiri, Praceta, Pulaha, Daksa, Vivasvat, Aristanemi, O Rāghava, and the exceedingly energetic Kasyapa. These had the west.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतेस्तु दक्षस्य बभूवुरिति नः श्रुतम्
षष्टिर्दुहितरो राम यशस्विन्यो महायशः
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatestu dakṣasya babhūvuriti naḥ śrutam
ṣaṣṭirduhitaro rāma yaśasvinyo mahāyaśaḥ

translations.english: The Prajāpati Dakşa, it has been heard by us, O Rāma, had sixty famous and illustrious daughters.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्यपः प्रतिजग्राह तासामष्टौ सुमध्यमाः
अदितिं च दितिं चैव दनूमपि च कालकाम्
verses.transliteration:
kaśyapaḥ pratijagrāha tāsāmaṣṭau sumadhyamāḥ
aditiṁ ca ditiṁ caiva danūmapi ca kālakām

translations.english: Of these Kaśyapa wed eight, with elegant waists; Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālikā, Tamră, Krodhavāśa, Manu and Analā.

verses.sanskrit:
कालका च महाबाहो शेषास्त्वमनसोऽभवन्
अदित्यां जज्ञिरे देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशदरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
kālakā ca mahābāho śeṣāstvamanaso'bhavan
adityāṁ jajñire devāstrayastriṁśadariṁdama

translations.english: Thereat, Aditi, O Raina, Diti, Danu, and Kalika*, O mighty-armed one, consented, the rest were of another mind. *Some text:-Kalaka.

verses.sanskrit:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा अश्विनौ च परंतप
दितिस्त्वजनयत्पुत्रान्दैत्यांस्तात यशस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau ca paraṁtapa
ditistvajanayatputrāndaityāṁstāta yaśasvinaḥ

translations.english: And of Aditi were born thirty-three deities, O repressor of your foes, viz., the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Asvinas, O subduer of enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामियं वसुमती पुरासीत्सवनार्णवा
दनुस्त्वजनयत्पुत्रमश्वग्रीवमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmiyaṁ vasumatī purāsītsavanārṇavā
danustvajanayatputramaśvagrīvamariṁdama

translations.english: And, my child, Diti gave birth to those sons, the renowned Daityas. Formerly, this earth girt with seas was in the possession of these.

verses.sanskrit:
नरकं कालकं चैव कालकापि व्यजायत
क्रौञ्चीं भासीं तथा श्येनीं धृतराष्ट्रीं तथा शुकीम्
verses.transliteration:
narakaṁ kālakaṁ caiva kālakāpi vyajāyata
krauñcīṁ bhāsīṁ tathā śyenīṁ dhṛtarāṣṭrīṁ tathā śukīm

translations.english: And Tāmrā gave birth to these five daughters celebrated in the world, Kraunci, Bhāsi, Syeni, Dhrtarastri, and Suki.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्रवाकांश्च भद्रं ते विजज्ञे सापि भामिनी
शुकी नतां विजज्ञे तु नताया विनता सुता
verses.transliteration:
cakravākāṁśca bhadraṁ te vijajñe sāpi bhāminī
śukī natāṁ vijajñe tu natāyā vinatā sutā

translations.english: And Krauncī gave birth to the Ulūkas, and Bhāsī, to Bhāsas, and Śyeni to hawks and vultures possessed of energy; and Dhịtarāştri to swans, all kinds of Kalahansas, and Cakravākas, and that damsel, Suki, to Natā And Vinatā was Natā's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
मातङ्गीमथ शार्दूलीं श्वेतां च सुरभीं तथा
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नां सुरसां कद्रुकामपि
verses.transliteration:
mātaṅgīmatha śārdūlīṁ śvetāṁ ca surabhīṁ tathā
sarvalakṣaṇasaṁpannāṁ surasāṁ kadrukāmapi

translations.english: And Krodhavasā, O Rāma, brought forth ten daughters viz., Mrgi, Mrgamanda, Hari, Bhadramadā, Mātangi, Śårdūlī, Śvetā, Surabhi crowned with every (auspicious mark), Surasā and Kadrukā.

verses.sanskrit:
अपत्यं तु मृगाः सर्वे मृग्या नरवरोत्तम
ऋष्काश्च मृगमन्दायाः सृमराश्चमरास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
apatyaṁ tu mṛgāḥ sarve mṛgyā naravarottama
ṛṣkāśca mṛgamandāyāḥ sṛmarāścamarāstathā

translations.english: You foremost of the best of men, Mrgi's sons were all the deer, and those of Mſgamandã were bears, Srmaras and Camaras.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्विरावतीं नाम जज्ञे भद्रमदा सुताम्
तस्यास्त्वैरावतः पुत्रो लोकनाथो महागजः
verses.transliteration:
tatastvirāvatīṁ nāma jajñe bhadramadā sutām
tasyāstvairāvataḥ putro lokanātho mahāgajaḥ

translations.english: And Bhadramadā bore one daughter, Irāvati. And Irāvati's son is the mighty elephant; who is the lord of the worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्याश्च हरयोऽपत्यं वानराश्च तपस्विनः
गोलाङ्गूलांश्च शार्दूली व्याघ्रांश्चाजनयत्सुतान्
verses.transliteration:
haryāśca harayo'patyaṁ vānarāśca tapasvinaḥ
golāṅgūlāṁśca śārdūlī vyāghrāṁścājanayatsutān

translations.english: And Hari's sons are lions and the nimble monkeys. And Śārdúlí brought forth as her sons, Golāngūlas, and tigers; and the offspring of Matangi were mad elephants, O best of men. And Śvetā, O Kākutstha, gave birth to the elephants of the cardinal points.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दुहितरौ राम सुरभिर्देव्यजायत
रोहिणीं नाम भद्रं ते गन्धर्वीं च यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
tato duhitarau rāma surabhirdevyajāyata
rohiṇīṁ nāma bhadraṁ te gandharvīṁ ca yaśasvinīm

translations.english: O Rāma, then, Surabhi gave birth to two daughters-the famous Rohini, and Gandharvi.

verses.sanskrit:
रोहिण्यजनयद्गा वै गन्धर्वी वाजिनः सुतान्
सुरसाजनयन्नागान्राम कद्रूश्च पन्नगान्
verses.transliteration:
rohiṇyajanayadgā vai gandharvī vājinaḥ sutān
surasājanayannāgānrāma kadrūśca pannagān

translations.english: Rohini produced kine, and the sons of Gandharvī are horses. And Surasā, O Rāma, gave birth to Nāgas, and Kadru to Pannagas.

verses.sanskrit:
मनुर्मनुष्याञ्जनयत्कश्यपस्य महात्मनः
ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियान्वैश्याञ्शूद्रांश्च मनुजर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
manurmanuṣyāñjanayatkaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ
brāhmaṇānkṣatriyānvaiśyāñśūdrāṁśca manujarṣabha

translations.english: Kāśyapa's other wife Manu begot mankind-Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras.

verses.sanskrit:
मुखतो ब्राह्मणा जाता उरसः क्षत्रियास्तथा
ऊरुभ्यां जज्ञिरे वैश्याः पद्भ्यां शूद्रा इति श्रुतिः
verses.transliteration:
mukhato brāhmaṇā jātā urasaḥ kṣatriyāstathā
ūrubhyāṁ jajñire vaiśyāḥ padbhyāṁ śūdrā iti śrutiḥ

translations.english: From the mouth, it is known sprang Brahmanas, from the breast, Ksatriya, from the thighs, Vaisyas, and from the feet, Sudras.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वान्पुण्यफलान्वृक्षाननलापि व्यजायत
विनता च शुकी पौत्री कद्रूश्च सुरसा स्वसा
verses.transliteration:
sarvānpuṇyaphalānvṛkṣānanalāpi vyajāyata
vinatā ca śukī pautrī kadrūśca surasā svasā

translations.english: And Anală produced all trees bearing sacred fruits. Vinatā (was) Śuki' grand-daughter, and Kadru, Surasā's aunt.

verses.sanskrit:
कद्रूर्नागसहस्क्रं तु विजज्ञे धरणीधरम्
द्वौ पुत्रौ विनतायास्तु गरुडोऽरुण एव च
verses.transliteration:
kadrūrnāgasahaskraṁ tu vijajñe dharaṇīdharam
dvau putrau vinatāyāstu garuḍo'ruṇa eva ca

translations.english: And Kadru gave birth to a thousand Nāgas with the holder of the Earth. And Vinatā brought forth two sons-Garuda and Aruna.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्माज्जातोऽहमरुणात्संपातिश्च ममाग्रजः
जटायुरिति मां विद्धि श्येनीपुत्रमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
tasmājjāto'hamaruṇātsaṁpātiśca mamāgrajaḥ
jaṭāyuriti māṁ viddhi śyenīputramariṁdama

translations.english: An from Aruņa sprang myself and my elder brother Sampāti subduer of enemies, know me for Jatayu, the son of Syeni.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं वाससहायस्ते भविष्यामि यदीच्छसि
सीतां च तात रक्षिष्ये त्वयि याते सलक्ष्मणे
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ vāsasahāyaste bhaviṣyāmi yadīcchasi
sītāṁ ca tāta rakṣiṣye tvayi yāte salakṣmaṇe

translations.english: If you will, I shall become your help during your abode (in the woods). And, O child, I shall protect Sītā when you shall go out along with Laksimana.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुषं तु प्रतिपूज्य राघवो; मुदा परिष्वज्य च संनतोऽभवत्
पितुर्हि शुश्राव सखित्वमात्मवा;ञ्जटायुषा संकथितं पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyuṣaṁ tu pratipūjya rāghavo; mudā pariṣvajya ca saṁnato'bhavat
piturhi śuśrāva sakhitvamātmavā;ñjaṭāyuṣā saṁkathitaṁ punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: There Rāghava paying homage to Jațāyu, and embracing him jcyfully, bent low; and that selfpossessed one listened to the story of Jațāyu's friendship with his father, as related by him repeatedly.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्र सीतां परिदाय मैथिलीं; सहैव तेनातिबलेन पक्षिणा
जगाम तां पञ्चवटीं सलक्ष्मणो; रिपून्दिधक्षञ्शलभानिवानलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatra sītāṁ paridāya maithilīṁ; sahaiva tenātibalena pakṣiṇā
jagāma tāṁ pañcavaṭīṁ salakṣmaṇo; ripūndidhakṣañśalabhānivānalaḥ

translations.english: Then consigning to that bird of exceeding strength, Mithila's daughter, Sita, Rama accompanied by Lakşmana went to Pañcavatī, destroying his foes and protecting the worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पञ्चवटीं गत्वा नानाव्यालमृगायुताम्
उवाच भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसं
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pañcavaṭīṁ gatvā nānāvyālamṛgāyutām
uvāca bhrātaraṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṁ dīptatejasaṁ

translations.english: Then repairing to Pañcavațī filled with various animals and beasts of prey, Rāma remarked to his brother Laksmana of flaming energy,

verses.sanskrit:
आगताः स्म यथोद्दिष्टममुं देशं महर्षिणा
अयं पञ्चवटी देशः सौम्य पुष्पितकाननः
verses.transliteration:
āgatāḥ sma yathoddiṣṭamamuṁ deśaṁ maharṣiṇā
ayaṁ pañcavaṭī deśaḥ saumya puṣpitakānanaḥ

translations.english: (Now) we have come to the place to which we had been directed by the ascetic This, O amiable one, is Pañcavați furnished with blossoming woods.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वतश्चार्यतां दृष्टिः कानने निपुणो ह्यसि
आश्रमः कतरस्मिन्नो देशे भवति संमतः
verses.transliteration:
sarvataścāryatāṁ dṛṣṭiḥ kānane nipuṇo hyasi
āśramaḥ katarasminno deśe bhavati saṁmataḥ

translations.english: Do you cast your eyes around this forest, and (ascertain) what spot shall suit our asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
रमते यत्र वैदेही त्वमहं चैव लक्ष्मण
तादृशो दृश्यतां देशः संनिकृष्टजलाशयः
verses.transliteration:
ramate yatra vaidehī tvamahaṁ caiva lakṣmaṇa
tādṛśo dṛśyatāṁ deśaḥ saṁnikṛṣṭajalāśayaḥ

translations.english: Do you find out such a place in the vicinity of a tank where yourself Sītā and I may dwell happily, which is graced with the garniture of woods and delightful with liquid lapses, and whose neighbourhood yields fuel, flowers, Kuća and water.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्मणः संयताञ्जलिः
सीता समक्षं काकुत्स्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa lakmaṇaḥ saṁyatāñjaliḥ
sītā samakṣaṁ kākutsthamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thus addressed by Rāma. Lakşmaņa with joined hands, said to Kākutstha in the presence of Sītā,

verses.sanskrit:
परवानस्मि काकुत्स्थ त्वयि वर्षशतं स्थिते
स्वयं तु रुचिरे देशे क्रियतामिति मां वद
verses.transliteration:
paravānasmi kākutstha tvayi varṣaśataṁ sthite
svayaṁ tu rucire deśe kriyatāmiti māṁ vada

translations.english: O Kákutstha, even if I were to stay with you for an hundred years, I shall remain your servant. Thyself selecting some beauteous spot do you tell me-'Construct (an asylum)'.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं रुचिरमाक्रम्य देशमाश्रमकर्मणि
हस्ते गृहीत्वा हस्तेन रामः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ ruciramākramya deśamāśramakarmaṇi
haste gṛhītvā hastena rāmaḥ saumitrimabravīt

translations.english: Well pleased with the words of Lakşınana, that highly effulgent one, after dure reflection, selected a site having every recommendation. Going to that romantic spot for rearing an asylum, Rama, taking the hand of Sumitra's son in his, said to him.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं देशः समः श्रीमान्पुष्पितैर्तरुभिर्वृतः
इहाश्रमपदं सौम्य यथावत्कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ deśaḥ samaḥ śrīmānpuṣpitairtarubhirvṛtaḥ
ihāśramapadaṁ saumya yathāvatkartumarhasi

translations.english: This place is level, graceful and surrounded with blossoming trees. Do you duly construct an asylum at this spot.

verses.sanskrit:
इयमादित्यसंकाशैः पद्मैः सुरभिगन्धिभिः
अदूरे दृश्यते रम्या पद्मिनी पद्मशोभिता
verses.transliteration:
iyamādityasaṁkāśaiḥ padmaiḥ surabhigandhibhiḥ
adūre dṛśyate ramyā padminī padmaśobhitā

translations.english: Hard by is seen a beautiful pool, embellished with lotuses, resembling the sun, and breathing balmy perfume.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाख्यातमगस्त्येन मुनिना भावितात्मना
इयं गोदावरी रम्या पुष्पितैस्तरुभिर्वृता
verses.transliteration:
yathākhyātamagastyena muninā bhāvitātmanā
iyaṁ godāvarī ramyā puṣpitaistarubhirvṛtā

translations.english: And, as told by that pure-hearted ascetic, Agastya, this is the graceful Godåvarī, bordered by flowering trees; swarming with swans and Kārandavas, delighted with Cakravākas, thronged with herds of deer,* not far, yet not so very near.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं पुण्यमिदं मेध्यमिदं बहुमृगद्विजम्
इह वत्स्याम सौमित्रे सार्धमेतेन पक्षिणा
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ puṇyamidaṁ medhyamidaṁ bahumṛgadvijam
iha vatsyāma saumitre sārdhametena pakṣiṇā

translations.english: This spot is sacred-this spot is charmingthis spot abounds in beasts and birds. Here will I dwell, O Sumitra's son, in company with this birds.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
अचिरेणाश्रमं भ्रातुश्चकार सुमहाबलः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
acireṇāśramaṁ bhrātuścakāra sumahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the exceedingly powerful Lakşmaņa, slayer of hostile heroes, in a short time raised as asylum for his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान्नदीं गोदावरीं तदा
स्नात्वा पद्मानि चादाय सफलः पुनरागतः
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmānnadīṁ godāvarīṁ tadā
snātvā padmāni cādāya saphalaḥ punarāgataḥ

translations.english: And then going to the river Godāvarī, the lovely Lakşmana, performing his bath, and securing lotuses and fruits, came back (to the asylum).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुष्पबलिं कृत्वा शान्तिं च स यथाविधि
दर्शयामास रामाय तदाश्रमपदं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ puṣpabaliṁ kṛtvā śāntiṁ ca sa yathāvidhi
darśayāmāsa rāmāya tadāśramapadaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: Then offering flowers, and duly performing rites for the peace (of the habitation), Lakşmaņa showed the asylum which he had made to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं दृष्ट्वा कृतं सौम्यमाश्रमं सह सीतया
राघवः पर्णशालायां हर्षमाहारयत्परम्
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ dṛṣṭvā kṛtaṁ saumyamāśramaṁ saha sītayā
rāghavaḥ parṇaśālāyāṁ harṣamāhārayatparam

translations.english: Seeing the beautiful asylum along with Sitā, Rāghava experienced high raptures.

verses.sanskrit:
सुसंहृष्टः परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां लक्ष्मणं तदा
अतिस्निग्धं च गाढं च वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
susaṁhṛṣṭaḥ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ tadā
atisnigdhaṁ ca gāḍhaṁ ca vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: And joyfully embracing Lakṣmaṇa with his arms, Rāma said these exceedingly calm and solemn words.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रीतोऽस्मि ते महत्कर्म त्वया कृतमिदं प्रभो
प्रदेयो यन्निमित्तं ते परिष्वङ्गो मया कृतः
verses.transliteration:
prīto'smi te mahatkarma tvayā kṛtamidaṁ prabho
pradeyo yannimittaṁ te pariṣvaṅgo mayā kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Pleased am I with you. You have done a great deed, my brother; for which I have granted you my embrace by way of reward.

verses.sanskrit:
भावज्ञेन कृतज्ञेन धर्मज्ञेन च लक्ष्मण
त्वया पुत्रेण धर्मात्मा न संवृत्तः पिता मम
verses.transliteration:
bhāvajñena kṛtajñena dharmajñena ca lakṣmaṇa
tvayā putreṇa dharmātmā na saṁvṛttaḥ pitā mama

translations.english: While you, his son skilled in reading thought, grateful, and cognizant of righteousness are alive, O Laksmana, my father is not dead.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं लक्ष्मणमुक्त्वा तु राघवो लक्ष्मिवर्धनः
तस्मिन्देशे बहुफले न्यवसत्स सुखं वशी
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ lakṣmaṇamuktvā tu rāghavo lakṣmivardhanaḥ
tasmindeśe bahuphale nyavasatsa sukhaṁ vaśī

translations.english: Having said this to Lakşmana, Rāghava— the enhancer of auspiciousness experiencing felicity, began to dwell happily in that region filled with fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
कंचित्कालं स धर्मात्मा सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च
अन्वास्यमानो न्यवसत्स्वर्गलोके यथामरः
verses.transliteration:
kaṁcitkālaṁ sa dharmātmā sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
anvāsyamāno nyavasatsvargaloke yathāmaraḥ

translations.english: And ministered to by Sītā and Lakşmaņa that righteous one lived there, like the immortals in heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
वसतस्तस्य तु सुखं राघवस्य महात्मनः
शरद्व्यपाये हेमन्त ऋतुरिष्टः प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
vasatastasya tu sukhaṁ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
śaradvyapāye hemanta ṛturiṣṭaḥ pravartate

translations.english: As the high-souled Rāghava was dwelling there peacefully, after autumn had departed, the welcome winter commenced.

verses.sanskrit:
स कदाचित्प्रभातायां शर्वर्यां रघुनन्दनः
प्रययावभिषेकार्थं रम्यां गोदावरीं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
sa kadācitprabhātāyāṁ śarvaryāṁ raghunandanaḥ
prayayāvabhiṣekārthaṁ ramyāṁ godāvarīṁ nadīm

translations.english: And it came to pass that once on a time, when the night had passed away and day broke, that son of Raghu went to the romantic river Godāvarī for performing his bath.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रह्वः कलशहस्तस्तं सीतया सह वीर्यवान्
पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजन्भ्राता सौमित्रिरिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
prahvaḥ kalaśahastastaṁ sītayā saha vīryavān
pṛṣṭhato'nuvrajanbhrātā saumitriridamabravīt

translations.english: And as the humble son of Sumitrā Rāma's puissant brother bearing a water pitcher in his hand was following Rāma along with Sītā at his back, the former said to Rāma,

verses.sanskrit:
अयं स कालः संप्राप्तः प्रियो यस्ते प्रियंवद
अलंकृत इवाभाति येन संवत्सरः शुभः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ sa kālaḥ saṁprāptaḥ priyo yaste priyaṁvada
alaṁkṛta ivābhāti yena saṁvatsaraḥ śubhaḥ

translations.english: O sweet-speeched one, now is come that season which you have ever held dear; and as if decorated by which comes on the entire auspicious year.

verses.sanskrit:
नीहारपरुषो लोकः पृथिवी सस्यमालिनी
जलान्यनुपभोग्यानि सुभगो हव्यवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
nīhāraparuṣo lokaḥ pṛthivī sasyamālinī
jalānyanupabhogyāni subhago havyavāhanaḥ

translations.english: Now people have their persons rendered rough from dew; the earth is replenished with com; water is difficult of being used; and fire becomes enjoyable.

verses.sanskrit:
नवाग्रयणपूजाभिरभ्यर्च्य पितृदेवताः
कृताग्रयणकाः काले सन्तो विगतकल्मषाः
verses.transliteration:
navāgrayaṇapūjābhirabhyarcya pitṛdevatāḥ
kṛtāgrayaṇakāḥ kāle santo vigatakalmaṣāḥ

translations.english: And men having worshipped the gods and the Pitſis by celebrating Āgrayana on the occasion of partaking new rice, have at this season, their sins purged off.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राज्यकामा जनपदाः संपन्नतरगोरसाः
विचरन्ति महीपाला यात्रार्थं विजिगीषवः
verses.transliteration:
prājyakāmā janapadāḥ saṁpannataragorasāḥ
vicaranti mahīpālā yātrārthaṁ vijigīṣavaḥ

translations.english: The provinces overflow with food, and abound in milk and articles prepared therefrom; and kings bent on conquest, range about for surveying thein.

verses.sanskrit:
सेवमाने दृढं सूर्ये दिशमन्तकसेविताम्
विहीनतिलकेव स्त्री नोत्तरा दिक्प्रकाशते
verses.transliteration:
sevamāne dṛḍhaṁ sūrye diśamantakasevitām
vihīnatilakeva strī nottarā dikprakāśate

translations.english: And on the sun having veered steadily to the quarter presided over by the Destroyer*, the north appears like a female without her tilaka. ** *i.e.-The South, **A mark made with coloured earth's or unguents upon the forehead and between the eye-brows either by way of ornament or a sectarial distinction.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या हिमकोशाढ्यो दूरसूर्यश्च साम्प्रतम्
यथार्थनामा सुव्यक्तं हिमवान्हिमवान्गिरिः
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā himakośāḍhyo dūrasūryaśca sāmpratam
yathārthanāmā suvyaktaṁ himavānhimavāngiriḥ

translations.english: Naturally abounding in snow, and now having the sun at a great distance, the mountain Himavān+ justly bear that name. Himavan means having snow.-T

verses.sanskrit:
अत्यन्तसुखसंचारा मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखाः
दिवसाः सुभगादित्याश्छायासलिलदुर्भगाः
verses.transliteration:
atyantasukhasaṁcārā madhyāhne sparśataḥ sukhāḥ
divasāḥ subhagādityāśchāyāsaliladurbhagāḥ

translations.english: At midday the days are delightful to a degree to range in, feel highly agreeable, and have pleasant suns; while shade and water are uncomfortable.

verses.sanskrit:
मृदुसूर्याः सनीहाराः पटुशीताः समारुताः
शून्यारण्या हिमध्वस्ता दिवसा भान्ति साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
mṛdusūryāḥ sanīhārāḥ paṭuśītāḥ samārutāḥ
śūnyāraṇyā himadhvastā divasā bhānti sāmpratam

translations.english: The days now have mild suns, are covered with dew severely cold, with the forests remaining idle, and the lotuses destroyed by frost.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्योत्स्ना तुषारमलिना पौर्णमास्यां न राजते
सीतेव चातपश्यामा लक्ष्यते न तु शोभते
verses.transliteration:
jyotsnā tuṣāramalinā paurṇamāsyāṁ na rājate
sīteva cātapaśyāmā lakṣyate na tu śobhate

translations.english: And now at night people cannot lie down in unsheltered places; and the nights are inferred from the presence of Pusya And at night the atmosphere (being covered with vapour) looks brown; and it is bitter cold then; and the hours are long And the good fortune of the Moon has fallen to the Sun; and the disc of the former is reddish with vapour; and like to a glass breathed upon, it dose not shine clearly. And the moonlight furnished by vapour dose not appear pleasant; and like Sītā pallid because of exposure to) sunshine, is perceptible, but dose not look beauteous,

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या शीतलस्पर्शो हिमविद्धश्च साम्प्रतम्
प्रवाति पश्चिमो वायुः काले द्विगुणशीतलः
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā śītalasparśo himaviddhaśca sāmpratam
pravāti paścimo vāyuḥ kāle dviguṇaśītalaḥ

translations.english: And at this season the western wind naturally of gelid feel, being permeated at present with cold, Flows with ouble coldness.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पच्छन्नान्यरण्यानि यवगोधूमवन्ति च
शोभन्तेऽभ्युदिते सूर्ये नदद्भिः क्रौञ्चसारसैः
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpacchannānyaraṇyāni yavagodhūmavanti ca
śobhante'bhyudite sūrye nadadbhiḥ krauñcasārasaiḥ

translations.english: And the forests enveloped in mist, and stocked with wheat and barley, look brilliant at sunrise, with Krauñcas and cranes crying (in chorus).

verses.sanskrit:
खर्जूरपुष्पाकृतिभिः शिरोभिः पूर्णतण्डुलैः
शोभन्ते किं चिदालम्बाः शालयः कनकप्रभाः
verses.transliteration:
kharjūrapuṣpākṛtibhiḥ śirobhiḥ pūrṇataṇḍulaiḥ
śobhante kiṁ cidālambāḥ śālayaḥ kanakaprabhāḥ

translations.english: Golden-hued paddy slightly inclined, appear graceful, with their heads like to date-flowers filled with rice.

verses.sanskrit:
मयूखैरुपसर्पद्भिर्हिमनीहारसंवृतैः
दूरमभ्युदितः सूर्यः शशाङ्क इव लक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
mayūkhairupasarpadbhirhimanīhārasaṁvṛtaiḥ
dūramabhyuditaḥ sūryaḥ śaśāṅka iva lakṣyate

translations.english: And the sun although high advanced. yet having its rays covered with thick mist, appear like the moon,

verses.sanskrit:
अग्राह्यवीर्यः पूर्वाह्णे मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखः
संरक्तः किंचिदापाण्डुरातपः शोभते क्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
agrāhyavīryaḥ pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne sparśataḥ sukhaḥ
saṁraktaḥ kiṁcidāpāṇḍurātapaḥ śobhate kṣitau

translations.english: And feeble at the first part of the day, and of agreeable touch at mid-day, the sunshine, being surcharged with mist, appear polish over the face of the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यायनिपातेन किंचित्प्रक्लिन्नशाद्वला
वनानां शोभते भूमिर्निविष्टतरुणातपा
verses.transliteration:
avaśyāyanipātena kiṁcitpraklinnaśādvalā
vanānāṁ śobhate bhūmirniviṣṭataruṇātapā

translations.english: And in the woods, swards covered with green grass, and with dew-drops on it, look handsome on the morning sun brightening it up.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यायतमोनद्धा नीहारतमसावृताः
प्रसुप्ता इव लक्ष्यन्ते विपुष्पा वनराजयः
verses.transliteration:
avaśyāyatamonaddhā nīhāratamasāvṛtāḥ
prasuptā iva lakṣyante vipuṣpā vanarājayaḥ

translations.english: And the rows of trees, shorn of their blossoms, on being enveloped with dew at night and mist at morn, look as if they were fast asleep.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पसंछन्नसलिला रुतविज्ञेयसारसाः
हिमार्द्रवालुकैस्तीरैः सरितो भान्ति साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpasaṁchannasalilā rutavijñeyasārasāḥ
himārdravālukaistīraiḥ sarito bhānti sāmpratam

translations.english: And the streams appear with their waters enveloped in vapour and the cranes, perceived through their cries, and their banks having their sands wet.

verses.sanskrit:
तुषारपतनाच्चैव मृदुत्वाद्भास्करस्य च
शैत्यादगाग्रस्थमपि प्रायेण रसवज्जलम्
verses.transliteration:
tuṣārapatanāccaiva mṛdutvādbhāskarasya ca
śaityādagāgrasthamapi prāyeṇa rasavajjalam

translations.english: What on account of the snow-fall, what of the mildness of the sun, and what through the cold, water even when it is on a mountain top, tastes sweet.

verses.sanskrit:
जराजर्जरितैः पर्णैः शीर्णकेसरकर्णिकैः
नालशेषा हिमध्वस्ता न भान्ति कमलाकराः
verses.transliteration:
jarājarjaritaiḥ parṇaiḥ śīrṇakesarakarṇikaiḥ
nālaśeṣā himadhvastā na bhānti kamalākarāḥ

translations.english: And lotuses afflicted by the cold, with the stalks only left, and with their petals dropping down and their pericarps and filaments shrivelled up, do not appear beautiful.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिंस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्र काले दुःखसमन्वितः
तपश्चरति धर्मात्मा त्वद्भक्त्या भरतः पुरे
verses.transliteration:
asmiṁstu puruṣavyāghra kāle duḥkhasamanvitaḥ
tapaścarati dharmātmā tvadbhaktyā bharataḥ pure

translations.english: O foremost of men, at this season, influenced by regard for you, Bharata undergoing affliction of spirit, is performing mortification's in the city.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा राज्यं च मानं च भोगांश्च विविधान्बहून्
तपस्वी नियताहारः शेते शीते महीतले
verses.transliteration:
tyaktvā rājyaṁ ca mānaṁ ca bhogāṁśca vividhānbahūn
tapasvī niyatāhāraḥ śete śīte mahītale

translations.english: And forsaking kingdom, and dignity, and the many and various enjoyments, Bharata practising asceticism and restraining himself in respect of food, in this winter lie down on the bare earth.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपि वेलामिमां नूनमभिषेकार्थमुद्यतः
वृतः प्रकृतिभिर्नित्यं प्रयाति सरयूं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
so'pi velāmimāṁ nūnamabhiṣekārthamudyataḥ
vṛtaḥ prakṛtibhirnityaṁ prayāti sarayūṁ nadīm

translations.english: He also for certain, at this hour of the day, surrounded by this subjects, daily wend to the river Sarayū for performing his ablutions.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धः सुकुमारो हिमार्दितः
कथं त्वपररात्रेषु सरयूमवगाहते
verses.transliteration:
atyantasukhasaṁvṛddhaḥ sukumāro himārditaḥ
kathaṁ tvapararātreṣu sarayūmavagāhate

translations.english: Brought up in luxury, and exceedingly tender, how can he, afflicted with cold, perforim his ablutions in the Sarayū during the latter part of the night?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियाभिभाषी मधुरो दीर्घबाहुररिंदमः
संत्यज्य विविधान्सौख्यानार्यं सर्वात्मनाश्रितः
verses.transliteration:
priyābhibhāṣī madhuro dīrghabāhurariṁdamaḥ
saṁtyajya vividhānsaukhyānāryaṁ sarvātmanāśritaḥ

translations.english: Of eyes resembling lotus petals, grey-hued, endued with grace, with a navel depressed, and mighty, Bharata understand righteousness, is truth-speaking, of restrained senses (in respect of other' wives) and also of subdued senses. And he speak fair, and is sweet-tempered, and longarmed and the vanquisher of foes. And renouncing various pleasures, he has devoted himself to the noble one.

verses.sanskrit:
जितः स्वर्गस्तव भ्रात्रा भरतेन महात्मना
वनस्थमपि तापस्ये यस्त्वामनुविधीयते
verses.transliteration:
jitaḥ svargastava bhrātrā bharatena mahātmanā
vanasthamapi tāpasye yastvāmanuvidhīyate

translations.english: Your high-souled brother has secured heaven, since he, resorting to asceticism, is iinitating you that resident in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
न पित्र्यमनुवर्न्तन्ते मातृकं द्विपदा इति
ख्यातो लोकप्रवादोऽयं भरतेनान्यथाकृतः
verses.transliteration:
na pitryamanuvarntante mātṛkaṁ dvipadā iti
khyāto lokapravādo'yaṁ bharatenānyathākṛtaḥ

translations.english: The saying that people follow their mother and not their father, is falsified in the case of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्ता दशरथो यस्याः साधुश्च भरतः सुतः
कथं नु साम्बा कैकेयी तादृशी क्रूरदर्शिनी
verses.transliteration:
bhartā daśaratho yasyāḥ sādhuśca bharataḥ sutaḥ
kathaṁ nu sāmbā kaikeyī tādṛśī krūradarśinī

translations.english: How can mother Kaikeyī, whose husband is Daśaratha and son the righteous Bharata, have such crooked way?

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं लक्ष्मणे वाक्यं स्नेहाद्ब्रुवति धार्मिके
परिवादं जनन्यास्तमसहन्राघवोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ lakṣmaṇe vākyaṁ snehādbruvati dhārmike
parivādaṁ jananyāstamasahanrāghavo'bravīt

translations.english: As the virtuous Lakṣmaṇa was speaking thus from affection, Rāghava, not bearing the blame cast upon his mother (Kaikeyi), said, My brother, you should by no means, tax our second mother. Do you talk of that lord of the Ikşvāku race, Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
निश्चितापि हि मे बुद्धिर्वनवासे दृढव्रता
भरतस्नेहसंतप्ता बालिशीक्रियते पुनः
verses.transliteration:
niścitāpi hi me buddhirvanavāse dṛḍhavratā
bharatasnehasaṁtaptā bāliśīkriyate punaḥ

translations.english: Albeit my mind is firm as regards my sojourn in the woods, yet is my mind unsteady, being inflained with affection for Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं विलपंस्तत्र प्राप्य गोदावरीं नदीम्
चक्रेऽभिषेकं काकुत्स्थः सानुजः सह सीतया
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ vilapaṁstatra prāpya godāvarīṁ nadīm
cakre'bhiṣekaṁ kākutsthaḥ sānujaḥ saha sītayā

translations.english: Having bewailed thus, Kākutstha, coming to the river Godāvarī, there performed his ablutions in company with his younger brother and Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
तर्पयित्वाथ सलिलैस्ते पितॄन्दैवतानि च
स्तुवन्ति स्मोदितं सूर्यं देवताश्च समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
tarpayitvātha salilaiste pitṝndaivatāni ca
stuvanti smoditaṁ sūryaṁ devatāśca samāhitāḥ

translations.english: Then having offered his adorations with water to the gods and the pitrs, those sinless ones hymned the risen sun as well as the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
कृताभिषेकः स रराज रामः; सीताद्वितीयः सह लक्ष्मणेन
कृताभिषेकस्त्वगराजपुत्र्या; रुद्रः सनन्दिर्भगवानिवेशः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtābhiṣekaḥ sa rarāja rāmaḥ; sītādvitīyaḥ saha lakṣmaṇena
kṛtābhiṣekastvagarājaputryā; rudraḥ sanandirbhagavāniveśaḥ

translations.english: Having with Sītā as the second and Laksmana, performed his bath. Rama looked beautiful like that lord the reverend Rudra in company with Nandi and the daughter of the king of mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
कृताभिषेको रामस्तु सीता सौमित्रिरेव च
तस्माद्गोदावरीतीरात्ततो जग्मुः स्वमाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtābhiṣeko rāmastu sītā saumitrireva ca
tasmādgodāvarītīrāttato jagmuḥ svamāśramam

translations.english: Having bathed, Rāma Sītā and Sumitrā's son went to their own asylum from the banks of the Godāvarī.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्रमं तमुपागम्य राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः
कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकं कर्म पर्णशालामुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
āśramaṁ tamupāgamya rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṁ karma parṇaśālāmupāgamat

translations.english: Arriving at the asylum, Rāghava along with Lakşmana, performing his morning devotions, entered the cottage.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामः पर्णशालायामासीनः सह सीतया
विरराज महाबाहुश्चित्रया चन्द्रमा इव
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा चकार विविधाः कथाः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmaḥ parṇaśālāyāmāsīnaḥ saha sītayā
virarāja mahābāhuścitrayā candramā iva
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā cakāra vividhāḥ kathāḥ

translations.english: And honoured of the Maharsis, Rāma happily dwelt in that cottage; and seated with Sītā that mighty-armed one looked like the moon in conjunction with Citrā. And he carried on various converse with his brother Lakşınana.

verses.sanskrit:
राममिन्दीवरश्यामं कन्दर्पसदृशप्रभम्
बभूवेन्द्रोपमं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसी काममोहिता
verses.transliteration:
rāmamindīvaraśyāmaṁ kandarpasadṛśaprabham
babhūvendropamaṁ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī kāmamohitā

translations.english: And beholding Rāma dark-blue like the lotus, and becoming like Kandarpa himself, and resembling Indra, the Rākşasi was maddened with desire.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमुखं दुर्मुखी रामं वृत्तमध्यं महोदरी
विशालाक्षं विरूपाक्षी सुकेशं ताम्रमूर्धजा
verses.transliteration:
sumukhaṁ durmukhī rāmaṁ vṛttamadhyaṁ mahodarī
viśālākṣaṁ virūpākṣī sukeśaṁ tāmramūrdhajā

translations.english: Rāma graced with beauteous continence, that Raksasi had a hideous face; Ráma had a slender waist, she had a huge abdomen; he had expansive eyes, she had terrible eyes; he was gifted with an elegant head of hair, she had coppery hair; Rāma was of a dear presence, she was of an unsightly presence; Rāma had a sonorous voice, she had a hideous voice.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियरूपं विरूपा सा सुस्वरं भैरवस्वना
तरुणं दारुणा वृद्धा दक्षिणं वामभाषिणी
verses.transliteration:
priyarūpaṁ virūpā sā susvaraṁ bhairavasvanā
taruṇaṁ dāruṇā vṛddhā dakṣiṇaṁ vāmabhāṣiṇī

translations.english: Rāma was youthful, the Rākşasi was an old hag; Rāma had mellifluous accents, she had was a harsh accents; Rāma was ever abiding by justice, she was unruly; Rāma was handsome, she was ugly.

verses.sanskrit:
जटी तापसरूपेण सभार्यः शरचापधृक्
आगतस्त्वमिमं देशं कथं राक्षससेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
jaṭī tāpasarūpeṇa sabhāryaḥ śaracāpadhṛk
āgatastvamimaṁ deśaṁ kathaṁ rākṣasasevitam

translations.english: That Rākşasī being wrought up with passion addressed Rāma saying Wearing matted locks, and equipped with bows and arrows, why hast you along with your wife come to this region haunted by Rākșasas? It behove you to say "what the object of your visit is."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या शूर्पणख्या परंतपः
ऋजुबुद्धितया सर्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rākṣasyā śūrpaṇakhyā paraṁtapaḥ
ṛjubuddhitayā sarvamākhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: Thus accosted by the Rākṣasī, Śūrpanakhă, that subduer of his foes from sincerity of disposition began to relate everything;

verses.sanskrit:
आसीद्दशरथो नाम राजा त्रिदशविक्रमः
तस्याहमग्रजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
āsīddaśaratho nāma rājā tridaśavikramaḥ
tasyāhamagrajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ

translations.english: There was a king named Dasaratha endued with the prowess of a celestial. I am his eldest son known among men by the name of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातायं लक्ष्मणो नाम यवीयान्मामनुव्रतः
इयं भार्या च वैदेही मम सीतेति विश्रुता
verses.transliteration:
bhrātāyaṁ lakṣmaṇo nāma yavīyānmāmanuvrataḥ
iyaṁ bhāryā ca vaidehī mama sīteti viśrutā

translations.english: This is my younger brother (named) Laks inana, (ever)serving me. This is my wife, known by the name of Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
नियोगात्तु नरेन्द्रस्य पितुर्मातुश्च यन्त्रितः
धर्मार्थं धर्मकाङ्क्षी च वनं वस्तुमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
niyogāttu narendrasya piturmātuśca yantritaḥ
dharmārthaṁ dharmakāṅkṣī ca vanaṁ vastumihāgataḥ

translations.english: Commanded by my father and mother, I in obedience their mandate, desirous of acquiring religious merits, have for the purpose of securing righteousness, come to the forest for dwelling here.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां तु वेदितुमिच्छामि कथ्यतां कासि कस्य वा
इह वा किंनिमित्तं त्वमागता ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ tu veditumicchāmi kathyatāṁ kāsi kasya vā
iha vā kiṁnimittaṁ tvamāgatā brūhi tattvataḥ

translations.english: I also am anxious to know you. Whose daughter are you? And what is your name, and what your lineage? Possessed of a captivating form, you appear to me as a Rākşasī. Tell me truly why you have come here. to

verses.sanskrit:
साब्रवीद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसी मदनार्दिता
श्रूयतां राम वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वार्थं वचनं मम
verses.transliteration:
sābravīdvacanaṁ śrutvā rākṣasī madanārditā
śrūyatāṁ rāma vakṣyāmi tattvārthaṁ vacanaṁ mama

translations.english: Hearing these words the Rákşasi, afflicted with lust said, Listen, O Rāma. I will relate everything truly. I am a Räkșasī, capable of wearing shapes at will. My name in Śūrpanakhā.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी कामरूपिणी
अरण्यं विचरामीदमेका सर्वभयंकरा
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ śūrpaṇakhā nāma rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī
araṇyaṁ vicarāmīdamekā sarvabhayaṁkarā

translations.english: Striking terror into the hearts of all, I range this forest alone. My brother is named Ravana* You may have heard of him.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा न तु राक्षसचेष्टितः
प्रख्यातवीर्यौ च रणे भ्रातरौ खरदूषणौ
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā na tu rākṣasaceṣṭitaḥ
prakhyātavīryau ca raṇe bhrātarau kharadūṣaṇau

translations.english: My brother Råvana is a valiant son of Viśravā if you have heard of him. And he that is given to long sleep-the mighty Kumbhakarna, the righteous Vibhīşaņa, who never serves the Rākşasas, and the brothers Khara and Düşaņa renowned in conflict (are also my brothers).

verses.sanskrit:
तानहं समतिक्रान्ता राम त्वापूर्वदर्शनात्
समुपेतास्मि भावेन भर्तारं पुरुषोत्तमम्
चिराय भव भर्ता मे सीतया किं करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tānahaṁ samatikrāntā rāma tvāpūrvadarśanāt
samupetāsmi bhāvena bhartāraṁ puruṣottamam
cirāya bhava bhartā me sītayā kiṁ kariṣyasi

translations.english: O Rāma, I have surpassed them all (in prowess). At first sight of you, I approach you, you best of men, as iny husband, with (feelings of) love.

verses.sanskrit:
विकृता च विरूपा च न सेयं सदृशी तव
अहमेवानुरूपा ते भार्यारूपेण पश्य माम्
verses.transliteration:
vikṛtā ca virūpā ca na seyaṁ sadṛśī tava
ahamevānurūpā te bhāryārūpeṇa paśya mām

translations.english: Deformed and unsightly, she is not worthy of you. I am fit for you. Do you look upon me as a wife.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्
अनेन सह ते भ्रात्रा भक्षयिष्यामि मानुषीम्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ virūpāmasatīṁ karālāṁ nirṇatodarīm
anena saha te bhrātrā bhakṣayiṣyāmi mānuṣīm

translations.english: This unsightly, grim unchaste and human one with me, with a lean abdomen, will I devour up, along with this brother of yours.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाणि वनानि विविधानि च
पश्यन्सह मया कान्त दण्डकान्विचरिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ parvataśṛṅgāṇi vanāni vividhāni ca
paśyansaha mayā kānta daṇḍakānvicariṣyasi

translations.english: Then having your wish, in company you will range the Daņdakas, surveying the various mountain summits and forests.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्तः काकुत्स्थः प्रहस्य मदिरेक्षणाम्
इदं वचनमारेभे वक्तुं वाक्यविशारदः
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktaḥ kākutsthaḥ prahasya madirekṣaṇām
idaṁ vacanamārebhe vaktuṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed, Kākutstha having charming eyes, well skilled in speech, with a smile, began to speak thus. with me, with a lean abdomen, will I devour up, along with this brother of yours.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु शूर्पणखां रामः कामपाशावपाशिताम्
स्वेच्छया श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्मितपूर्वमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu śūrpaṇakhāṁ rāmaḥ kāmapāśāvapāśitām
svecchayā ślakṣṇayā vācā smitapūrvamathābravīt

translations.english: With a smile, Rāma jestingly addressed Śūrpanakhā who had been ensnared in the noose of love, in soft words.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतदारोऽस्मि भवति भार्येयं दयिता मम
त्वद्विधानां तु नारीणां सुदुःखा ससपत्नता
verses.transliteration:
kṛtadāro'smi bhavati bhāryeyaṁ dayitā mama
tvadvidhānāṁ tu nārīṇāṁ suduḥkhā sasapatnatā

translations.english: Gentle one, I am already wedded; this is my beloved wife. To females like to you co-wifehood is exceedingly miserable.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुजस्त्वेष मे भ्राता शीलवान्प्रियदर्शनः
श्रीमानकृतदारश्च लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
anujastveṣa me bhrātā śīlavānpriyadarśanaḥ
śrīmānakṛtadāraśca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān

translations.english: This young brother of mine is good-looking, and is of an excellent character; he is graceful, and is still unwived. The powerful one is named Laksmana. He has not yet tested the pleasures of a wife's company, and is desirous of having a spouse. And he is youthful and of an inviting presence. He will become a fit husband for you, considering this your beauty.

verses.sanskrit:
एनं भज विशालाक्षि भर्तारं भ्रातरं मम
असपत्ना वरारोहे मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा
verses.transliteration:
enaṁ bhaja viśālākṣi bhartāraṁ bhrātaraṁ mama
asapatnā varārohe merumarkaprabhā yathā

translations.english: O you of expansive eyes, seek this brother of mine as your husband, even as the solar beam seeks Meru. (By doing so), You O supremely beautiful damsel, will not have to fear a co-wife.

verses.sanskrit:
इति रामेण सा प्रोक्ता राक्षसी काममोहिता
विसृज्य रामं सहसा ततो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
iti rāmeṇa sā proktā rākṣasī kāmamohitā
visṛjya rāmaṁ sahasā tato lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: Having been thus addressed by Rāma, the Rākṣasī intoxicated with lust, at once leaving Rāma, spoke to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य रूपस्य ते युक्ता भार्याहं वरवर्णिनी
मया सह सुखं सर्वान्दण्डकान्विचरिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
asya rūpasya te yuktā bhāryāhaṁ varavarṇinī
mayā saha sukhaṁ sarvāndaṇḍakānvicariṣyasi

translations.english: I am fit to be your wife possessed of transcendental grace, having regard to this beauty of yours. And with me you will happily range these Dandakas.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्री राक्षस्या वाक्यकोविदः
ततः शूर्पणखीं स्मित्वा लक्ष्मणो युक्तमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu saumitrī rākṣasyā vākyakovidaḥ
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhīṁ smitvā lakṣmaṇo yuktamabravīt

translations.english: Thus accosted by the Räkşasi, Sumitrā's son, Lakşmana versed in speech, with a smile appropriately observed to Śūrpanakhā,

verses.sanskrit:
कथं दासस्य मे दासी भार्या भवितुमिच्छसि
सोऽहमार्येण परवान्भ्रात्रा कमलवर्णिनि
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ dāsasya me dāsī bhāryā bhavitumicchasi
so'hamāryeṇa paravānbhrātrā kamalavarṇini

translations.english: Why wish you to be the servant of me who am a servant myself*? O lotus-hued one, I am dependant on my noble brother. The text is difficult to render literally:—Why wish you to be the female servant of me who am myself a male servant.

verses.sanskrit:
समृद्धार्थस्य सिद्धार्था मुदितामलवर्णिनी
आर्यस्य त्वं विशालाक्षि भार्या भव यवीयसी
verses.transliteration:
samṛddhārthasya siddhārthā muditāmalavarṇinī
āryasya tvaṁ viśālākṣi bhāryā bhava yavīyasī

translations.english: O you of expansive eyes, be you securing the sumimum bonum, with a joyful heart, become, O superbly beautiful wench, the younger wife of the noble one of great good fortune.

verses.sanskrit:
एतां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्
भार्यां वृद्धां परित्यज्य त्वामेवैष भजिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ virūpāmasatīṁ karālāṁ nirṇatodarīm
bhāryāṁ vṛddhāṁ parityajya tvāmevaiṣa bhajiṣyati

translations.english: Renouncing this frightful, unchaste, hideous, old wife possessed of a lean abdomen; he will devote himself to you.

verses.sanskrit:
को हि रूपमिदं श्रेष्ठं संत्यज्य वरवर्णिनि
मानुषेषु वरारोहे कुर्याद्भावं विचक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
ko hi rūpamidaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ saṁtyajya varavarṇini
mānuṣeṣu varārohe kuryādbhāvaṁ vicakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: O paragon among damsels, O supremely charming lady, what man possessed of discernment, passing by such grace, would bear affliction to a human female?

verses.sanskrit:
इति सा लक्ष्मणेनोक्ता कराला निर्णतोदरी
मन्यते तद्वचः सत्यं परिहासाविचक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
iti sā lakṣmaṇenoktā karālā nirṇatodarī
manyate tadvacaḥ satyaṁ parihāsāvicakṣaṇā

translations.english: Thus accosted by Lakşmaņa, that hideous one having a lean abdomen being incapable of understanding jest, took his words as true.

verses.sanskrit:
सा रामं पर्णशालायामुपविष्टं परंतपम्
सीतया सह दुर्धर्षमब्रवीत्काममोहिता
verses.transliteration:
sā rāmaṁ parṇaśālāyāmupaviṣṭaṁ paraṁtapam
sītayā saha durdharṣamabravītkāmamohitā

translations.english: Thereupon as that subduer of enemies, the irrepressible Rāma, was seated in the cottage in company with Sītā, the Rākşasī, transported with lust, said to him.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्
वृद्धां भार्यामवष्टभ्य न मां त्वं बहु मन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ virūpāmasatīṁ karālāṁ nirṇatodarīm
vṛddhāṁ bhāryāmavaṣṭabhya na māṁ tvaṁ bahu manyase

translations.english: Forsaking this deformed, unchaste, horrible old wife of yours possessed of a lean abdomen, you do not regard me.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्येमां भक्षयिष्यामि पश्यतस्तव मानुषीम्
त्वया सह चरिष्यामि निःसपत्ना यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
adyemāṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmi paśyatastava mānuṣīm
tvayā saha cariṣyāmi niḥsapatnā yathāsukham

translations.english: To-day, you looking on, I shall eat up this human female. And I shall, rid of a co-wife, happily range with you.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा मृगशावाक्षीमलातसदृशेक्षणा
अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धा महोल्का रोहिणीमिव
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā mṛgaśāvākṣīmalātasadṛśekṣaṇā
abhyadhāvatsusaṁkruddhā maholkā rohiṇīmiva

translations.english: Having said this, even as a mighty meteor strike Rohiņī, that one having eyes resembling live coals, waxing exceedingly enraged, rushed towards that (damsel) with the eyes of a doe.

verses.sanskrit:
तां मृत्युपाशप्रतिमामापतन्तीं महाबलः
निगृह्य रामः कुपितस्ततो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ mṛtyupāśapratimāmāpatantīṁ mahābalaḥ
nigṛhya rāmaḥ kupitastato lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon, hindering the Rākṣasi resembling the noose of death, as she was rushing on, the mighty Rāma, growing wroth said to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रूरैरनार्यैः सौमित्रे परिहासः कथंचन
न कार्यः पश्य वैदेहीं कथंचित्सौम्य जीवतीम्
verses.transliteration:
krūrairanāryaiḥ saumitre parihāsaḥ kathaṁcana
na kāryaḥ paśya vaidehīṁ kathaṁcitsaumya jīvatīm

translations.english: O Saumitri (Sumitrā's son), what is the good of jesting with a base and wicked one? No use of doing it. Look, I amiable one, Vaidehi (Videha's daughter) is well nigh dead.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां विरूपामसतीमतिमत्तां महोदरीम्
राक्षसीं पुरुषव्याघ्र विरूपयितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ virūpāmasatīmatimattāṁ mahodarīm
rākṣasīṁ puruṣavyāghra virūpayitumarhasi

translations.english: It behoves you, O foremost of men, to deform this frightful, unchaste Rākşasī of a huge abdomen, transported with lust.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तो लक्ष्मणस्तस्याः क्रुद्धो रामस्य पश्यतः
उद्धृत्य खड्गं चिच्छेद कर्णनासं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
ityukto lakṣmaṇastasyāḥ kruddho rāmasya paśyataḥ
uddhṛtya khaḍgaṁ ciccheda karṇanāsaṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thus desired the exceedingly strong Laksmana, fired with wrath, taking out his sword, in the sight of Rāma, cut off her nose and ears.

verses.sanskrit:
निकृत्तकर्णनासा तु विस्वरं सा विनद्य च
यथागतं प्रदुद्राव घोरा शूर्पणखा वनम्
verses.transliteration:
nikṛttakarṇanāsā tu visvaraṁ sā vinadya ca
yathāgataṁ pradudrāva ghorā śūrpaṇakhā vanam

translations.english: Her ears and nose cut off, the terrible Śūrpanakhā, uttering frightful cries, fled a main into the forest whence she had come.

verses.sanskrit:
सा विरूपा महाघोरा राक्षसी शोणितोक्षिता
ननाद विविधान्नादान्यथा प्रावृषि तोयदः
verses.transliteration:
sā virūpā mahāghorā rākṣasī śoṇitokṣitā
nanāda vividhānnādānyathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ

translations.english: And being deformed, and covered with gore, the dreadful Rākşasī sent up many a roar, like clouds rumbling in the rains.

verses.sanskrit:
सा विक्षरन्ती रुधिरं बहुधा घोरदर्शना
प्रगृह्य बाहू गर्जन्ती प्रविवेश महावनम्
verses.transliteration:
sā vikṣarantī rudhiraṁ bahudhā ghoradarśanā
pragṛhya bāhū garjantī praviveśa mahāvanam

translations.english: And bleeding profusely, the grimvisaged Rākṣasī, lifting up her arms, and roaring, entered the mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सा राक्षससंघसंवृतं; खरं जनस्थानगतं विरूपिता
उपेत्य तं भ्रातरमुग्रतेजसं; पपात भूमौ गगनाद्यथाशनिः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sā rākṣasasaṁghasaṁvṛtaṁ; kharaṁ janasthānagataṁ virūpitā
upetya taṁ bhrātaramugratejasaṁ; papāta bhūmau gaganādyathāśaniḥ

translations.english: Then having been deformed, (the Rākşasī) approaching, her brother of fierce energy, Khara, come to Janasthāna, (seated surrounded by numbers of Raksasas), fell down to the earth, even as the thunderbolt bursts from the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सभार्यं भयमोहमूर्छिता; सलक्ष्मणं राघवमागतं वनम्
विरूपणं चात्मनि शोणितोक्षिता; शशंस सर्वं भगिनी खरस्य सा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sabhāryaṁ bhayamohamūrchitā; salakṣmaṇaṁ rāghavamāgataṁ vanam
virūpaṇaṁ cātmani śoṇitokṣitā; śaśaṁsa sarvaṁ bhaginī kharasya sā

translations.english: Then that sister of Khara, bathed in blood, and deprived of her senses through fright, related all about Räma's arrival at the forest along with Lakşmaņa and his own wife, as well as the forest along with Lakşmana and his own wife, as well as the circumstances connected with her being deformed.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तथा पतितां दृष्ट्वा विरूपां शोणितोक्षिताम्
भगिनीं क्रोधसंतप्तः खरः पप्रच्छ राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tathā patitāṁ dṛṣṭvā virūpāṁ śoṇitokṣitām
bhaginīṁ krodhasaṁtaptaḥ kharaḥ papraccha rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Seeing his sister deformed, and covered with blood, fallen on the ground, the Raksasa, Khara, fired with wrath asked her.

verses.sanskrit:
बलविक्रमसंपन्ना कामगा कामरूपिणी
इमामवस्थां नीता त्वं केनान्तकसमा गता
verses.transliteration:
balavikramasaṁpannā kāmagā kāmarūpiṇī
imāmavasthāṁ nītā tvaṁ kenāntakasamā gatā

translations.english: Endowed with strength and prowess, ranging about at will, wearing shapes at pleasure, and resembling the destroyer himself, going to whom hast you come by this condition?

verses.sanskrit:
देवगन्धर्वभूतानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्
कोऽयमेवं महावीर्यस्त्वां विरूपां चकार ह
verses.transliteration:
devagandharvabhūtānāmṛṣīṇāṁ ca mahātmanām
ko'yamevaṁ mahāvīryastvāṁ virūpāṁ cakāra ha

translations.english: Who among the gods, Gandharvas or creatures or the light souled saints is of such mighty energy as to have deformed you?

verses.sanskrit:
न हि पश्याम्यहं लोके यः कुर्यान्मम विप्रियम्
अन्तरेन सहस्राक्षं महेन्द्रं पाकशासनम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi paśyāmyahaṁ loke yaḥ kuryānmama vipriyam
antarena sahasrākṣaṁ mahendraṁ pākaśāsanam

translations.english: In this world I do not see him that would do me: wrong, not even the mighty Indra, the thousand eyed tamer of the demon Pāka.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्याहं मार्गणैः प्राणानादास्ये जीवितान्तकैः
सलिले क्षीरमासक्तं निष्पिबन्निव सारसः
verses.transliteration:
adyāhaṁ mārgaṇaiḥ prāṇānādāsye jīvitāntakaiḥ
salile kṣīramāsaktaṁ niṣpibanniva sārasaḥ

translations.english: a crane Even as afflicted with thirst appropriate milk mixed in water (leaving the latter out), so by means of fleet an lifedestroying shafts I will among the immortals take the life of that chastiser. The frothy blood of whom, having his marrow pierced (by me) and slain by me in battle, dose the Earth wish to drink?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य पत्ररथाः कायान्मांसमुत्कृत्य संगताः
प्रहृष्टा भक्षयिष्यन्ति निहतस्य मया रणे
verses.transliteration:
kasya patrarathāḥ kāyānmāṁsamutkṛtya saṁgatāḥ
prahṛṣṭā bhakṣayiṣyanti nihatasya mayā raṇe

translations.english: Tearing off flesh from the corpse of whom slain by me in conflict, shall the birds so joyfully feed on it?

verses.sanskrit:
तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः
मयापकृष्टं कृपणं शक्तास्त्रातुं महाहवे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ na devā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
mayāpakṛṣṭaṁ kṛpaṇaṁ śaktāstrātuṁ mahāhave

translations.english: Him, whom I shall wrong mightily, neither the gods, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Piśācas, nor the Rākşasas, will be able to rescue in fierce encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
उपलभ्य शनैः संज्ञां तं मे शंसितुमर्हसि
येन त्वं दुर्विनीतेन वने विक्रम्य निर्जिता
verses.transliteration:
upalabhya śanaiḥ saṁjñāṁ taṁ me śaṁsitumarhasi
yena tvaṁ durvinītena vane vikramya nirjitā

translations.english: Recovering by degrees your sense, it behoves you to tell me what individual it was of execrable character, who by his prowess, half humbled you in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
इति भ्रातुर्वचः श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धस्य च विशेषतः
ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यं सबाष्पमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
iti bhrāturvacaḥ śrutvā kruddhasya ca viśeṣataḥ
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyaṁ sabāṣpamidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing these words of his brother, who was under the influence of extreme rage, Sūrpanakhā with tears in her eyes, said.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुणी रूपसंपन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता
दृष्टा तत्र मया नारी तयोर्मध्ये सुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
taruṇī rūpasaṁpannā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
dṛṣṭā tatra mayā nārī tayormadhye sumadhyamā

translations.english: And between them I saw there a youthful female furnished with grace, and having a dainty waist; adorned with every kind of ornament.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यामुभाभ्यां संभूय प्रमदामधिकृत्य ताम्
इमामवस्थां नीताहं यथानाथासती तथा
verses.transliteration:
tābhyāmubhābhyāṁ saṁbhūya pramadāmadhikṛtya tām
imāmavasthāṁ nītāhaṁ yathānāthāsatī tathā

translations.english: And it is on account of this feinale that I have like one unchaste and uncared for, have come by this condition at their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याश्चानृजुवृत्तायास्तयोश्च हतयोरहम्
सफेनं पातुमिच्छामि रुधिरं रणमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
tasyāścānṛjuvṛttāyāstayośca hatayoraham
saphenaṁ pātumicchāmi rudhiraṁ raṇamūrdhani

translations.english: Nor I wish in the midst of encounter to drink the frothy blood of that crooked one as well as those two slain (in battle).

verses.sanskrit:
एष मे प्रथमः कामः कृतस्तात त्वया भवेत्
तस्यास्तयोश्च रुधिरं पिबेयमहमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa me prathamaḥ kāmaḥ kṛtastāta tvayā bhavet
tasyāstayośca rudhiraṁ pibeyamahamāhave

translations.english: Let this my prime wish be crowned there with fruition. her and their blood will I drink in dreadful conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
इति तस्यां ब्रुवाणायां चतुर्दश महाबलान्
व्यादिदेश खरः क्रुद्धो राक्षसानन्तकोपमान्
verses.transliteration:
iti tasyāṁ bruvāṇāyāṁ caturdaśa mahābalān
vyādideśa kharaḥ kruddho rākṣasānantakopamān

translations.english: As she said this, Khara wrought up with boundless passion, said, Two human beings accoutred in arins, and wearing bark and dark deer-skins have in company with a female entered this deep Dandaka forest. Do you returni, after slaying them, as well as that wicked one. And this sister of mine will drink their blood.

verses.sanskrit:
मनोरथोऽयमिष्टोऽस्या भगिन्या मम राक्षसाः
शीघ्रं संपद्यतां गत्वा तौ प्रमथ्य स्वतेजसा
verses.transliteration:
manoratho'yamiṣṭo'syā bhaginyā mama rākṣasāḥ
śīghraṁ saṁpadyatāṁ gatvā tau pramathya svatejasā

translations.english: You Rākşasas, even this is my sister's dear desire. Repairing thither, specdily accomplish this, bearing them down by your native might.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश
तत्र जग्मुस्तया सार्धं घना वातेरिता यथा
verses.transliteration:
iti pratisamādiṣṭā rākṣasāste caturdaśa
tatra jagmustayā sārdhaṁ ghanā vāteritā yathā

translations.english: Thus commissioned, those fourteen Räksasas set out there like clouds driven by the winds, accompanied by Śürpanakhā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखा घोरा राघवाश्रममागता
रक्षसामाचचक्षे तौ भ्रातरौ सह सीतया
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā ghorā rāghavāśramamāgatā
rakṣasāmācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā

translations.english: Then the grim Śūrpanakhā, coming to Rāghava's asylum pointed out to the Rākşasas those brother in company with Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
ते रामं पर्णशालायामुपविष्टं महाबलम्
ददृशुः सीतया सार्धं वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च
verses.transliteration:
te rāmaṁ parṇaśālāyāmupaviṣṭaṁ mahābalam
dadṛśuḥ sītayā sārdhaṁ vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca

translations.english: And they saw the mighty Rāma seated in the cottage in company with Sītā, and ministered to by Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमानागतां तां च राक्षसीम्
अब्रवीद्भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसं
verses.transliteration:
tāndṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmānāgatāṁ tāṁ ca rākṣasīm
abravīdbhrātaraṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṁ dīptatejasaṁ

translations.english: And seeing her, as well as the Rākşasas who had come, Rāma remarked to his brother, Lakşınaņa of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
मुहूर्तं भव सौमित्रे सीतायाः प्रत्यनन्तरः
इमानस्या वधिष्यामि पदवीमागतानिह
verses.transliteration:
muhūrtaṁ bhava saumitre sītāyāḥ pratyanantaraḥ
imānasyā vadhiṣyāmi padavīmāgatāniha

translations.english: O Sumitrā's son, do you for a while guard Sītā. I shall slay these that have come to this asylum here.

verses.sanskrit:
वाक्यमेतत्ततः श्रुत्वा रामस्य विदितात्मनः
तथेति लक्ष्मणो वाक्यं रामस्य प्रत्यपूजयत्
verses.transliteration:
vākyametattataḥ śrutvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
tatheti lakṣmaṇo vākyaṁ rāmasya pratyapūjayat

translations.english: Hearing these words of Rāma versed in the knowledge of self, Lakşmaņa honoured his speech by saying, So be it.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवोऽपि महच्चापं चामीकरविभूषितम्
चकार सज्यं धर्मात्मा तानि रक्षांसि चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavo'pi mahaccāpaṁ cāmīkaravibhūṣitam
cakāra sajyaṁ dharmātmā tāni rakṣāṁsi cābravīt

translations.english: And the righteous Rāghava strung his mighty bow decked with gold; and addressed the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रौ दशरथस्यावां भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
प्रविष्टौ सीतया सार्धं दुश्चरं दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
putrau daśarathasyāvāṁ bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
praviṣṭau sītayā sārdhaṁ duścaraṁ daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: We that have entered into this untraceable forest of Dandaka in company with Sītā are the sons of Dasaratha, the brothers, Rama and Lakşmana. Why do you intend to do injury to us. Subsisting on fruits and roots, having our senses under control, carrying on asceticism and leading a Brahmacarya life, we are passing our days in the forest of Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
युष्मान्पापात्मकान्हन्तुं विप्रकारान्महावने
ऋषीणां तु नियोगेन प्राप्तोऽहं सशरासनः
verses.transliteration:
yuṣmānpāpātmakānhantuṁ viprakārānmahāvane
ṛṣīṇāṁ tu niyogena prāpto'haṁ saśarāsanaḥ

translations.english: It is do destroy you, wicked, and troublesome that I equipped with the bow have come here at the desire of the saints.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठतैवात्र संतुष्टा नोपसर्पितुमर्हथ
यदि प्राणैरिहार्थो वो निवर्तध्वं निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭhataivātra saṁtuṣṭā nopasarpitumarhatha
yadi prāṇairihārtho vo nivartadhvaṁ niśācarāḥ

translations.english: Stay there content you should not move further. If you have a care for your lives, desist, you rangers of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश
ऊचुर्वाचं सुसंक्रुद्धा ब्रह्मघ्नः शूलपाणयः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rākṣasāste caturdaśa
ūcurvācaṁ susaṁkruddhā brahmaghnaḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of his, those fourteen grim Rākşasas bearing darts in their hands, exceedingly enraged, with their eyes reddened, breathing high spirits, harshly said to the sweetspeeched Rāma, having his eyes reddened whose prowess they had not seen before.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधमुत्पाद्य नो भर्तुः खरस्य सुमहात्मनः
त्वमेव हास्यसे प्राणानद्यास्माभिर्हतो युधि
verses.transliteration:
krodhamutpādya no bhartuḥ kharasya sumahātmanaḥ
tvameva hāsyase prāṇānadyāsmābhirhato yudhi

translations.english: Having excited there our lord. the high-souled Khara, it is you that shal: lose your life no later than this day, being slain by us in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
का हि ते शक्तिरेकस्य बहूनां रणमूर्धनि
अस्माकमग्रतः स्थातुं किं पुनर्योद्धुमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
kā hi te śaktirekasya bahūnāṁ raṇamūrdhani
asmākamagrataḥ sthātuṁ kiṁ punaryoddhumāhave

translations.english: What power hast you, being one to stay before us many in the field, what shall I say of your coping with us in conflict?

verses.sanskrit:
एभिर्बाहुप्रयुक्तैर्नः परिघैः शूलपट्टिशैः
प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यसि वीर्यं च धनुश्च करपीडितम्
verses.transliteration:
ebhirbāhuprayuktairnaḥ parighaiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśaiḥ
prāṇāṁstyakṣyasi vīryaṁ ca dhanuśca karapīḍitam

translations.english: In consequence of the parighas (iron-clubs), darts, and pattisas (a kind of sharp-edged sword) discharged by our arms, you will surely lose your life, along with your prowess, and this bow which you press with your hand.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा संरब्धा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश
उद्यतायुधनिस्त्रिंशा राममेवाभिदुद्रुवुः
चिक्षिपुस्तानि शूलानि राघवं प्रति दुर्जयम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā saṁrabdhā rākṣasāste caturdaśa
udyatāyudhanistriṁśā rāmamevābhidudruvuḥ
cikṣipustāni śūlāni rāghavaṁ prati durjayam

translations.english: Having said this in wrath, those fourteen Rākşasas, uplifting their weapons and daggers rushed towards Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि शूलानि काकुत्स्थः समस्तानि चतुर्दश
तावद्भिरेव चिच्छेद शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः
verses.transliteration:
tāni śūlāni kākutsthaḥ samastāni caturdaśa
tāvadbhireva ciccheda śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: And discharged darts at the invincible Rāghava. Thereupon Kākutstha by means of shafts decked with gold, cut off those fourteen darts of theirs.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीत्वा धनुरायम्य लक्ष्यानुद्दिश्य राक्षसान्
मुमोच राघवो बाणान्वज्रानिव शतक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītvā dhanurāyamya lakṣyānuddiśya rākṣasān
mumoca rāghavo bāṇānvajrāniva śatakratuḥ

translations.english: Seeing this, that exceedingly cnergetic one, waxing highly enraged, look out fourteen darts with many golden arrows, whetted on stone, resembling the sun. And even as Satakratu hurls the thunder bolt, Rāghava drawing his bow and taking his aim at the Rākşasas, let go those shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ते भित्त्वा रक्षसां वेगाद्वक्षांसि रुधिराप्लुताः
विनिष्पेतुस्तदा भूमौ न्यमज्जन्ताशनिस्वनाः
verses.transliteration:
te bhittvā rakṣasāṁ vegādvakṣāṁsi rudhirāplutāḥ
viniṣpetustadā bhūmau nyamajjantāśanisvanāḥ

translations.english: And those Rākşasas, their breasts pierced with vehemence, and themselves bathed in blood, fell down to the carth, like snakes dropping down from an ant hill.

verses.sanskrit:
ते भिन्नहृदया भूमौ छिन्नमूला इव द्रुमाः
निपेतुः शोणितार्द्राङ्गा विकृता विगतासवः
verses.transliteration:
te bhinnahṛdayā bhūmau chinnamūlā iva drumāḥ
nipetuḥ śoṇitārdrāṅgā vikṛtā vigatāsavaḥ

translations.english: And with their breasts pierced, they, dripping with blood, deformed and deprived of their lives, lay on the ground like trees whose roots have been severed.

verses.sanskrit:
सा नदन्ती महानादं जवाच्छूर्पणखा पुनः
उपगम्य खरं सा तु किंचित्संशुष्क शोणिता
पपात पुनरेवार्ता सनिर्यासेव वल्लरी
verses.transliteration:
sā nadantī mahānādaṁ javācchūrpaṇakhā punaḥ
upagamya kharaṁ sā tu kiṁcitsaṁśuṣka śoṇitā
papāta punarevārtā saniryāseva vallarī

translations.english: Seeing them fallen-on the ground, the Rākşasī, beyond herself in wrath, approaching Khara, with her blood a little dried up, again in distressful guise threw herself on the earth, like a plant exuding gum.

verses.sanskrit:
निपातितान्प्रेक्ष्य रणे तु राक्षसा;न्प्रधाविता शूर्पणखा पुनस्ततः
वधं च तेषां निखिलेन रक्षसां; शशंस सर्वं भगिनी खरस्य सा
verses.transliteration:
nipātitānprekṣya raṇe tu rākṣasā;npradhāvitā śūrpaṇakhā punastataḥ
vadhaṁ ca teṣāṁ nikhilena rakṣasāṁ; śaśaṁsa sarvaṁ bhaginī kharasya sā

translations.english: Seeing those Rākşasas slain in battle, Śūrpanakhā again hastened (to his brother); and the sister of Khara, related in detail the slaughter of those Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुनः पतितां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधाच्छूर्पणखां खरः
उवाच व्यक्तता वाचा तामनर्थार्थमागताम्
verses.transliteration:
sa punaḥ patitāṁ dṛṣṭvā krodhācchūrpaṇakhāṁ kharaḥ
uvāca vyaktatā vācā tāmanarthārthamāgatām

translations.english: Seeing Sūrpanakhă again lying on the ground, Khara in anger spoke out to that one, who had come to bring on evil.

verses.sanskrit:
मया त्विदानीं शूरास्ते राक्षसा रुधिराशनाः
त्वत्प्रियार्थं विनिर्दिष्टाः किमर्थं रुद्यते पुनः
verses.transliteration:
mayā tvidānīṁ śūrāste rākṣasā rudhirāśanāḥ
tvatpriyārthaṁ vinirdiṣṭāḥ kimarthaṁ rudyate punaḥ

translations.english: I had but recently commissioned for your behoof those heroic Rākşasas living on flesh. Why then do you again weep?

verses.sanskrit:
भक्ताश्चैवानुरक्ताश्च हिताश्च मम नित्यशः
घ्नन्तोऽपि न निहन्तव्या न न कुर्युर्वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
bhaktāścaivānuraktāśca hitāśca mama nityaśaḥ
ghnanto'pi na nihantavyā na na kuryurvaco mama

translations.english: Bearing regard and attached to me, and ever engaged in my welfare, they, assailed by others, are incapable of being slain; nor do they not obey my orders.

verses.sanskrit:
किमेतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि कारणं यत्कृते पुनः
हा नाथेति विनर्दन्ती सर्पवद्वेष्टसे क्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
kimetacchrotumicchāmi kāraṇaṁ yatkṛte punaḥ
hā nātheti vinardantī sarpavadveṣṭase kṣitau

translations.english: What can it be? I would hear of the occasion owing to which again, crying ‘Ah lord,' you roll on the earth like a serpent.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाथवद्विलपसि किं नु नाथे मयि स्थिते
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ मा भैषीर्वैक्लव्यं त्यज्यतामिह
verses.transliteration:
anāthavadvilapasi kiṁ nu nāthe mayi sthite
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha mā bhaiṣīrvaiklavyaṁ tyajyatāmiha

translations.english: Why do you be weep like one forlorn, while I your lord, am living? Arise! Arise! Do not fear, cast off your stupor.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्ता दुर्धर्षा खरेण परिसान्त्विता
विमृज्य नयने सास्रे खरं भ्रातरमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktā durdharṣā khareṇa parisāntvitā
vimṛjya nayane sāsre kharaṁ bhrātaramabravīt

translations.english: Thus addressed, and consoled by Khara, that irrepressible one, wiping her eyes, spoke to Khara.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेषिताश्च त्वया शूरा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश
निहन्तुं राघवं घोरा मत्प्रियार्थं सलक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
preṣitāśca tvayā śūrā rākṣasāste caturdaśa
nihantuṁ rāghavaṁ ghorā matpriyārthaṁ salakṣmaṇam

translations.english: And you also had despatched fourteen heroic Rākṣasas, for my hehoof, for slaying the terrific Rāghava along with Lakşmaņa. But all those, bearing ill will (towards Rāma), bearing darts and pattiśas in their hands, have been slain in conflict by means of weapons penetrating into the vitals.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्भूमौ पतितान्दृष्ट्वा क्षणेनैव महाबलान्
रामस्य च महत्कर्म महांस्त्रासोऽभवन्मम
verses.transliteration:
tānbhūmau patitāndṛṣṭvā kṣaṇenaiva mahābalān
rāmasya ca mahatkarma mahāṁstrāso'bhavanmama

translations.english: Seeing those possessed of great speed, in a moment laid low on the ground, as well as (witnessing) Rāma's mighty deed, great fear has taken possession of me.

verses.sanskrit:
विषादनक्राध्युषिते परित्रासोर्मिमालिनि
किं मां न त्रायसे मग्नां विपुले शोकसागरे
verses.transliteration:
viṣādanakrādhyuṣite paritrāsormimālini
kiṁ māṁ na trāyase magnāṁ vipule śokasāgare

translations.english: O ranger of the night, I am afraid, and agitated, and cast down. I have (at length) found in you a refuge, seeing fear on all sides. Will you not rescue me who am sinking in this ocean of grief, having sorrow for its alligators and affright for billows?

verses.sanskrit:
एते च निहता भूमौ रामेण निशितैः शरैः
ये च मे पदवीं प्राप्ता राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः
verses.transliteration:
ete ca nihatā bhūmau rāmeṇa niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
ye ca me padavīṁ prāptā rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ

translations.english: And these Rākşasas, living on flesh who had arrived at that place, have been slain by Rāma with sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
मयि ते यद्यनुक्रोशो यदि रक्षःसु तेषु च
रामेण यदि शक्तिस्ते तेजो वास्ति निशाचर
दण्डकारण्यनिलयं जहि राक्षसकण्टकम्
verses.transliteration:
mayi te yadyanukrośo yadi rakṣaḥsu teṣu ca
rāmeṇa yadi śaktiste tejo vāsti niśācara
daṇḍakāraṇyanilayaṁ jahi rākṣasakaṇṭakam

translations.english: If you have any kindness for me as well as those sons of Rākşasas* and, O ranger of night, if you have strength and energy to cope with Rāma, do you kill this thorn of the Rákşasas, who has set up his dwelling in the forest of Dandaka. Another reading is that enemy of mine.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि रामं ममामित्रमद्य त्वं न वधिष्यसि
तव चैवाग्रतः प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि निरपत्रपा
verses.transliteration:
yadi rāmaṁ mamāmitramadya tvaṁ na vadhiṣyasi
tava caivāgrataḥ prāṇāṁstyakṣyāmi nirapatrapā

translations.english: If you do not to-day slay that destroyer of foes, Rāma, I shall banishing shame, give up my life in your very presence.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्ध्याहमनुपश्यामि न त्वं रामस्य संयुगे
स्थातुं प्रतिमुखे शक्तः सचापस्य महारणे
verses.transliteration:
buddhyāhamanupaśyāmi na tvaṁ rāmasya saṁyuge
sthātuṁ pratimukhe śaktaḥ sacāpasya mahāraṇe

translations.english: Meseems, you backed by your forecast are incapable of staying in battle before Rāma in high encounter. Some texts-(Rāma) equipped with the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
अपयाहि जनस्थानात्त्वरितः सहबान्धवः
निःसत्त्वस्याल्पवीर्यस्य वासस्ते कीदृशस्त्विह
verses.transliteration:
apayāhi janasthānāttvaritaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ
niḥsattvasyālpavīryasya vāsaste kīdṛśastviha

translations.english: You plume yourself on being a hero; but are really none such. Prowess has been falsely attributed to you. Go off from Janasthāna without delay, along with your friends. O stainer of your line, do you in battle slay those foolhardy ones. But if you fail in slaying those human beings, Rama and Laksmana, then how can you void of strength and of slender prowess, stay here?

verses.sanskrit:
रामतेजोऽभिभूतो हि त्वं क्षिप्रं विनशिष्यसि
स हि तेजःसमायुक्तो रामो दशरथात्मजः
भ्राता चास्य महावीर्यो येन चास्मि विरूपिता
verses.transliteration:
rāmatejo'bhibhūto hi tvaṁ kṣipraṁ vinaśiṣyasi
sa hi tejaḥsamāyukto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
bhrātā cāsya mahāvīryo yena cāsmi virūpitā

translations.english: Overcome by the energy of Rāma, you shall speedily meet with destruction Dasaratha's son, Rāma, you shall speedily meet with destruction. Dasaratha's son, is endued with energy. His brother is possessed of high vigour by whom I have come to be deformed.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमाधर्षितः शूरः शूर्पणख्या खरस्तदा
उवाच रक्षसां मध्ये खरः खरतरं वचः
verses.transliteration:
evamādharṣitaḥ śūraḥ śūrpaṇakhyā kharastadā
uvāca rakṣasāṁ madhye kharaḥ kharataraṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: On being thus taunted by Śūrpanakha, Khara spoke these sharp words in the midst of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तवापमानप्रभवः क्रोधोऽयमतुलो मम
न शक्यते धारयितुं लवणाम्भ इवोत्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
tavāpamānaprabhavaḥ krodho'yamatulo mama
na śakyate dhārayituṁ lavaṇāmbha ivotthitam

translations.english: Arising from this your humiliating censure, my wrath is beyond compare. I can not bear it, like salt-water cast on a sore.

verses.sanskrit:
न रामं गणये वीर्यान्मानुषं क्षीणजीवितम्
आत्मा दुश्चरितैः प्राणान्हतो योऽद्य विमोक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
na rāmaṁ gaṇaye vīryānmānuṣaṁ kṣīṇajīvitam
ātmā duścaritaiḥ prāṇānhato yo'dya vimokṣyati

translations.english: From my prowess I count not Rāma who is a human being possessed of a frail life him who slain by me shall to-day in consequence of his misdeed give up existence.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पः संह्रियतामेष संभ्रमश्च विमुच्यताम्
अहं रामः सह भ्रात्रा नयामि यमसादनम्
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpaḥ saṁhriyatāmeṣa saṁbhramaśca vimucyatām
ahaṁ rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā nayāmi yamasādanam

translations.english: Restrain your tears, and remove your fear. I shall despatch a Rāma along with his brother to the abode of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
परश्वधहतस्याद्य मन्दप्राणस्य भूतले
रामस्य रुधिरं रक्तमुष्णं पास्यसि राक्षसि
verses.transliteration:
paraśvadhahatasyādya mandaprāṇasya bhūtale
rāmasya rudhiraṁ raktamuṣṇaṁ pāsyasi rākṣasi

translations.english: You shall O Rākşasī, quaff on the ground the hot blood of Rāma of evil life, slain by my axe.

verses.sanskrit:
सा प्रहृष्ट्वा वचः श्रुत्वा खरस्य वदनाच्च्युतम्
प्रशशंस पुनर्मौर्ख्याद्भ्रातरं रक्षसां वरम्
verses.transliteration:
sā prahṛṣṭvā vacaḥ śrutvā kharasya vadanāccyutam
praśaśaṁsa punarmaurkhyādbhrātaraṁ rakṣasāṁ varam

translations.english: Overjoyed on hearing the words that dropped from Khara's mouth, she again through fickleness extolled that foremost of Rākşasas, her brother.

verses.sanskrit:
तया परुषितः पूर्वं पुनरेव प्रशंसितः
अब्रवीद्दूषणं नाम खरः सेनापतिं तदा
verses.transliteration:
tayā paruṣitaḥ pūrvaṁ punareva praśaṁsitaḥ
abravīddūṣaṇaṁ nāma kharaḥ senāpatiṁ tadā

translations.english: At first reprimanded by her and then praised, Khara spoke to is general, named Dusana.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि मम चित्तानुवर्तिनाम्
रक्षसीं भीमवेगानां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi mama cittānuvartinām
rakṣasīṁ bhīmavegānāṁ samareṣvanivartinām

translations.english: Do you, O gentle one, array fourteen thousand of those those Rākṣasas, gifted with furious vehemence, ever following my wish, who never turn away froin the field; who are hued like to purple clouds, who revel in cruelty*, and who are elated (in consequence of their prowess). *The North-West Province's text has some additional sloka:-Dreadful, wearing forms at will, possessing the pride of the lion, having large mouth, high-souled, revelling in cruelty, endued with strength, of fierce energy.

verses.sanskrit:
उपस्थापय मे क्षिप्रं रथं सौम्य धनूंषि च
शरांश्च चित्रान्खड्गांश्च शक्तीश्च विविधाः शिताः
verses.transliteration:
upasthāpaya me kṣipraṁ rathaṁ saumya dhanūṁṣi ca
śarāṁśca citrānkhaḍgāṁśca śaktīśca vividhāḥ śitāḥ

translations.english: And you gentle one, do you at once bring my car as well as my bows, and pasty coloured arrows and scimitars, and darts, and various whetted javelins.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रे निर्यातुमिच्छामि पौलस्त्यानां महात्मनाम्
वधार्थं दुर्विनीतस्य रामस्य रणकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
agre niryātumicchāmi paulastyānāṁ mahātmanām
vadhārthaṁ durvinītasya rāmasya raṇakovidaḥ

translations.english: O you versed in warfare, for slaying this haughty Rāma, I go in the very fore-front of the high-souled Paulastyas. Lit.-Pulastya's The Rākşasas commonly descended from Pulastya.

verses.sanskrit:
इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य सूर्यवर्णं महारथम्
सदश्वैः शबलैर्युक्तमाचचक्षेऽथ दूषणः
verses.transliteration:
iti tasya bruvāṇasya sūryavarṇaṁ mahāratham
sadaśvaiḥ śabalairyuktamācacakṣe'tha dūṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: As he said this, Dūşaņa brought his great car hued like the sun, yoked with excellent steeds of various colours. sons. were

verses.sanskrit:
मत्स्यैः पुष्पैर्द्रुमैः शैलैश्चन्द्रसूर्यैश्च काञ्चनैः
माङ्गल्यैः पक्षिसंघैश्च ताराभिश्च समावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
matsyaiḥ puṣpairdrumaiḥ śailaiścandrasūryaiśca kāñcanaiḥ
māṅgalyaiḥ pakṣisaṁghaiśca tārābhiśca samāvṛtam

translations.english: Thereupon in a passion Khara ascended that car resembling a peak of Meru, embellished with burnished-gold, furnished with golden wheels, open; having its pole studded with lapises; surrounded with fishes and flowers and trees and stones, and the sun and the moon and gold, and auspicious articles; and swarms of birds, and stars; having streamers and swords; garnished with bells; and yoked with superb coursers.

verses.sanskrit:
खरस्तु तान्महेष्वासान्घोरचर्मायुधध्वजान्
निर्यातेत्यब्रवीद्दृष्ट्वा रथस्थः सर्वराक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
kharastu tānmaheṣvāsānghoracarmāyudhadhvajān
niryātetyabravīddṛṣṭvā rathasthaḥ sarvarākṣasān

translations.english: Beholding that mighty army consisting of cars and arms and pennons, Khara as well as Dūşana, said to that multitude of Rākşasas, March forth!

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्त्वभिद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसान्भीमविक्रमान्
खरस्यापि रथः किंचिज्जगाम तदनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstvabhidravato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānbhīmavikramān
kharasyāpi rathaḥ kiṁcijjagāma tadanantaram

translations.english: Seeing those Rākṣasas of dreadful forms rushing out, Khara's car remaining a little away (from the press), proceeded after a short space.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ताञ्शबलानश्वांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषितान्
खरस्य मतमाज्ञाय सारथिः समचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastāñśabalānaśvāṁstaptakāñcanabhūṣitān
kharasya matamājñāya sārathiḥ samacodayat

translations.english: Then taking the perinission of Khara, the charioteer drove at speed those powerful steeds decked in shining gold.

verses.sanskrit:
स चोदितो रथः शीघ्रं खरस्य रिपुघातिनः
शब्देनापूरयामास दिशश्च प्रतिशस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
sa codito rathaḥ śīghraṁ kharasya ripughātinaḥ
śabdenāpūrayāmāsa diśaśca pratiśastathā

translations.english: And driven with speed, the car of Khara. slayer of foes, filled all directions with its rattle.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवृद्धमन्युस्तु खरः खरस्वनो; रिपोर्वधार्थं त्वरितो यथान्तकः
अचूचुदत्सारथिमुन्नदन्पुन;र्महाबलो मेघ इवाश्मवर्षवान्
verses.transliteration:
pravṛddhamanyustu kharaḥ kharasvano; riporvadhārthaṁ tvarito yathāntakaḥ
acūcudatsārathimunnadanpuna;rmahābalo megha ivāśmavarṣavān

translations.english: Khara, fired with wrath, and having piercing voice, hastening to destroy his enemy like the destroyer himself, again urged his charioteer with roars, like a mighty cloud showering down stones.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्प्रयातं बलं घोरमशिवं शोणितोदकम्
अभ्यवर्षन्महामेघस्तुमुलो गर्दभारुणः
verses.transliteration:
tatprayātaṁ balaṁ ghoramaśivaṁ śoṇitodakam
abhyavarṣanmahāmeghastumulo gardabhāruṇaḥ

translations.english: As those terrible and inauspicious forces were marching on, a mighty sable cloud with dreadful sounds began to shower down blood.

verses.sanskrit:
निपेतुस्तुरगास्तस्य रथयुक्ता महाजवाः
समे पुष्पचिते देशे राजमार्गे यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
nipetusturagāstasya rathayuktā mahājavāḥ
same puṣpacite deśe rājamārge yadṛcchayā

translations.english: The steeds yoked to his (Khara's) car, gifted with great celerity, dropped down all of a sudden on the level high ways strewn with blossoms.

verses.sanskrit:
श्यामं रुधिरपर्यन्तं बभूव परिवेषणम्
अलातचक्रप्रतिमं प्रतिगृह्य दिवाकरम्
verses.transliteration:
śyāmaṁ rudhiraparyantaṁ babhūva pariveṣaṇam
alātacakrapratimaṁ pratigṛhya divākaram

translations.english: A dark circle bordered with red, resembling that of charcoal, appeared in the vicinity of the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो ध्वजमुपागम्य हेमदण्डं समुच्छ्रितम्
समाक्रम्य महाकायस्तस्थौ गृध्रः सुदारुणः
verses.transliteration:
tato dhvajamupāgamya hemadaṇḍaṁ samucchritam
samākramya mahākāyastasthau gṛdhraḥ sudāruṇaḥ

translations.english: And a frightful vulture, having a huge body, approaching the banner, sat upon the upraised golden flag-staff.

verses.sanskrit:
जनस्थानसमीपे च समाक्रम्य खरस्वनाः
विस्वरान्विविधांश्चक्रुर्मांसादा मृगपक्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
