janasthānasamīpe ca samākramya kharasvanāḥ
visvarānvividhāṁścakrurmāṁsādā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: And beasts and birds having shrill voices, living on flesh, remaining near Janasthāna, emitted various dissonant notes. And in the quarter lighted up by the sun, fierce jackals having mighty voices, in dreadful cries presaged evil to the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभिन्नगिरिसंकाशास्तोयशोषितधारिणः
आकाशं तदनाकाशं चक्रुर्भीमा बलाहकाः
verses.transliteration:
prabhinnagirisaṁkāśāstoyaśoṣitadhāriṇaḥ
ākāśaṁ tadanākāśaṁ cakrurbhīmā balāhakāḥ

translations.english: And terrific clouds surcharged with water and blood, and resembling elephants with rent temples, enveloped the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
बभूव तिमिरं घोरमुद्धतं रोमहर्षणम्
दिशो वा विदिशो वापि सुव्यक्तं न चकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
babhūva timiraṁ ghoramuddhataṁ romaharṣaṇam
diśo vā vidiśo vāpi suvyaktaṁ na cakāśire

translations.english: And a dense darkness appeared, capable of making one's hair stand on end, and no quarter was distinctly visible.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षतजार्द्रसवर्णाभा संध्याकालं विना बभौ
खरस्याभिमुखं नेदुस्तदा घोरा मृगाः खगाः
verses.transliteration:
kṣatajārdrasavarṇābhā saṁdhyākālaṁ vinā babhau
kharasyābhimukhaṁ nedustadā ghorā mṛgāḥ khagāḥ

translations.english: And out of season, there appeared evening hued like a cloth soaked in blood. And facing Khara, terrible beasts and birds set up cries.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्याशिवकरा युद्धे शिवा घोरनिदर्शनाः
नेदुर्बलस्याभिमुखं ज्वालोद्गारिभिराननैः
verses.transliteration:
nityāśivakarā yuddhe śivā ghoranidarśanāḥ
nedurbalasyābhimukhaṁ jvālodgāribhirānanaiḥ

translations.english: Kankas, Gomayas and vultures, portending fear, began to cry. Ever inauspicious in war, jackals presaging evil, with their mouths belching forth flame, howled in the face of the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
कबन्धः परिघाभासो दृश्यते भास्करान्तिके
जग्राह सूर्यं स्वर्भानुरपर्वणि महाग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
kabandhaḥ parighābhāso dṛśyate bhāskarāntike
jagrāha sūryaṁ svarbhānuraparvaṇi mahāgrahaḥ

translations.english: And comets, resembling parighas appeared beside the sun. That mighty planet Svarbhānu seized the sun when there was no parva. And the winds blew violently; and the sun was without lustre.

verses.sanskrit:
संलीनमीनविहगा नलिन्यः पुष्पपङ्कजाः
तस्मिन्क्षणे बभूवुश्च विना पुष्पफलैर्द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
saṁlīnamīnavihagā nalinyaḥ puṣpapaṅkajāḥ
tasminkṣaṇe babhūvuśca vinā puṣpaphalairdrumāḥ

translations.english: And at that hour the trees were shorn of fruits and flowers; and without wind there arose dust dusky like clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
उल्काश्चापि सनिर्घोषा निपेतुर्घोरदर्शनाः
प्रचचाल मही चापि सशैलवनकानना
verses.transliteration:
ulkāścāpi sanirghoṣā nipeturghoradarśanāḥ
pracacāla mahī cāpi saśailavanakānanā

translations.english: And the parrots uttered wild notes-cīcīkūci. And meteors of terrific aspects fell with loud noises.

verses.sanskrit:
खरस्य च रथस्थस्य नर्दमानस्य धीमतः
प्राकम्पत भुजः सव्यः खरश्चास्यावसज्जत
verses.transliteration:
kharasya ca rathasthasya nardamānasya dhīmataḥ
prākampata bhujaḥ savyaḥ kharaścāsyāvasajjata

translations.english: And the earth with her mountains, woods, and forests, shook. And as the intelligent Khara was roaring from his car, his left arm shook, and his voice fell, and as he surveyed around, his eyes moistened, and his head ached; yet through ignorance, he did not desist.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्समीक्ष्य महोत्पातानुत्थितान्रोमहर्षणान्
अब्रवीद्राक्षसान्सर्वान्प्रहसन्स खरस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tānsamīkṣya mahotpātānutthitānromaharṣaṇān
abravīdrākṣasānsarvānprahasansa kharastadā

translations.english: Witnessing these mighty portents capable of making one's hair stand on end, Khara with a laugh, addressed the whole body of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवं तं बलोत्सिक्तं भ्रातरं चापि लक्ष्मणम्
अहत्वा सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नोपावर्तितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaṁ taṁ balotsiktaṁ bhrātaraṁ cāpi lakṣmaṇam
ahatvā sāyakaistīkṣṇairnopāvartitumutsahe

translations.english: Even as a strong person from prowess counts not a weak one, I do not dwell upon all these mighty portents, dreadful to behold, that have appeared. Even the stars will I bring down from heaven with my sharp shafts; and even Death will I engaged, bring to mortality. Without slaying Rāghava puffed up with pride as well as Laksmana, by means of sharp weapons, I return not (from the conflict).

verses.sanskrit:
सकामा भगिनी मेऽस्तु पीत्वा तु रुधिरं तयोः
यन्निमित्तं तु रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्य विपर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
sakāmā bhaginī me'stu pītvā tu rudhiraṁ tayoḥ
yannimittaṁ tu rāmasya lakṣmaṇasya viparyayaḥ

translations.english: Let that sister of mine, for whom Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa have had sense perverted, attain her desire, by drinking their blood..

verses.sanskrit:
न क्वचित्प्राप्तपूर्वो मे संयुगेषु पराजयः
युष्माकमेतत्प्रत्यक्षं नानृतं कथयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
na kvacitprāptapūrvo me saṁyugeṣu parājayaḥ
yuṣmākametatpratyakṣaṁ nānṛtaṁ kathayāmyaham

translations.english: I had never before met with defeat in conflict. You have witnessed it. I do not speak a falsehood.

verses.sanskrit:
देवराजमपि क्रुद्धो मत्तैरावतयायिनम्
वज्रहस्तं रणे हन्यां किं पुनस्तौ च मानुषौ
verses.transliteration:
devarājamapi kruddho mattairāvatayāyinam
vajrahastaṁ raṇe hanyāṁ kiṁ punastau ca mānuṣau

translations.english: Wrought up with rage, I shall slay in fight the sovereign of the celestials himself, going on his mad Airāvata, with the thunderbolt in his hand, what shall I say of those two, who are human beings?

verses.sanskrit:
सा तस्य गर्जितं श्रुत्वा राक्षसस्य महाचमूः
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे मृत्युपाशावपाशिता
verses.transliteration:
sā tasya garjitaṁ śrutvā rākṣasasya mahācamūḥ
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe mṛtyupāśāvapāśitā

translations.english: Entangled in the noose of death, that mighty army of the Rākşasas hearing his challenge, experienced boundless enthusiasm.

verses.sanskrit:
समेयुश्च महात्मानो युद्धदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः
ऋषयो देवगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च सह चारणैः
verses.transliteration:
sameyuśca mahātmāno yuddhadarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
ṛṣayo devagandharvāḥ siddhāśca saha cāraṇaiḥ

translations.english: Then the high-souled gods and Gandharvas, Siddhas and Cāranas came there, with the intention of witnessing the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
जयतां राघवो युद्धे पौलस्त्यान्रजनीचरान्
चक्रा हस्तो यथा युद्धे सर्वानसुरपुंगवान्
verses.transliteration:
jayatāṁ rāghavo yuddhe paulastyānrajanīcarān
cakrā hasto yathā yuddhe sarvānasurapuṁgavān

translations.english: Welfare to those cows, and Brāhmanas, and those that are prized by the worlds! As the discus-handed Vişņu vanquished the foremost Asuras, may Rāghava rout in battle those rangers of the night, the progeny of Pulastya!

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्चान्यच्च बहुशो ब्रुवाणाः परमर्षयः
ददृशुर्वाहिनीं तेषां राक्षसानां गतायुषाम्
verses.transliteration:
etaccānyacca bahuśo bruvāṇāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
dadṛśurvāhinīṁ teṣāṁ rākṣasānāṁ gatāyuṣām

translations.english: And saying this as well as various other things, the supreme saints and the celestials stationed in the sky conceiving curiosity (as to the issue of the conflict), beheld the host of those Rākşasas, whose days had been numbered.

verses.sanskrit:
श्येन गामी पृथुग्रीवो यज्ञशत्रुर्विहंगमः
दुर्जयः करवीराक्षः परुषः कालकार्मुकः
verses.transliteration:
śyena gāmī pṛthugrīvo yajñaśatrurvihaṁgamaḥ
durjayaḥ karavīrākṣaḥ paruṣaḥ kālakārmukaḥ

translations.english: Then impetuously Khara issued in his car from the van of the army*. And these twelve endowed with exceeding prowess, viz., Syenagāmí, Prthusyama, Yajñaśatru, Vihangama, Durjaya, Karavirāksa, Parusa, Kālakärmuka, Hemamāli, Mahāmāli, Sarpāsya, and Rudhirāśana posted themselves around Khara. The N.W.P. text has a different stoka. And seeing him come out on the ground, they themselves came out.

verses.sanskrit:
महाकपालः स्थूलाक्षः प्रमाथी त्रिशिरास्तथा
चत्वार एते सेनाग्र्या दूषणं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयुः
verses.transliteration:
mahākapālaḥ sthūlākṣaḥ pramāthī triśirāstathā
catvāra ete senāgryā dūṣaṇaṁ pṛṣṭhato'nvayuḥ

translations.english: And Mahākapāla, Sthūlākṣa, Pramātha and Trisirā—These four going before the forces, went at the back of Dūşaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
सा भीमवेगा समराभिकामा; सुदारुणा राक्षसवीर सेना
तौ राजपुत्रौ सहसाभ्युपेता; मालाग्रहाणामिव चन्द्रसूर्यौ
verses.transliteration:
sā bhīmavegā samarābhikāmā; sudāruṇā rākṣasavīra senā
tau rājaputrau sahasābhyupetā; mālāgrahāṇāmiva candrasūryau

translations.english: Then as the planets dart towards the sun and moon, that heroic and dreadful army of Rākşasas, eager for victory suddenly rushed towards the princes with great vehemence.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्रमं प्रति याते तु खरे खरपराक्रमे
तानेवौत्पातिकान्रामः सह भ्रात्रा ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
āśramaṁ prati yāte tu khare kharaparākrame
tānevautpātikānrāmaḥ saha bhrātrā dadarśa ha

translations.english: When Khara of fierce prowess had come to the asylum Rāma in company with his brother saw all those evil prognostics.

verses.sanskrit:
तानुत्पातान्महाघोरानुत्थितान्रोमहर्षणान्
प्रजानामहितान्दृष्ट्वा वाक्यं लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tānutpātānmahāghorānutthitānromaharṣaṇān
prajānāmahitāndṛṣṭvā vākyaṁ lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: And beholding those dreadful portents, Rāma exceedingly distressed, apprehending some calamity to the Rākşasas, observed to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
इमान्पश्य महाबाहो सर्वभूतापहारिणः
समुत्थितान्महोत्पातान्संहर्तुं सर्वराक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
imānpaśya mahābāho sarvabhūtāpahāriṇaḥ
samutthitānmahotpātānsaṁhartuṁ sarvarākṣasān

translations.english: O mighty armed one, behold these great presages that have taken place, capable of annihilating all beings, and which have taken place, capable of annihilating all beings, and which have for their object the utter extermination of the Raksasas!

verses.sanskrit:
अमी रुधिरधारास्तु विसृजन्तः खरस्वनान्
व्योम्नि मेघा विवर्तन्ते परुषा गर्दभारुणाः
verses.transliteration:
amī rudhiradhārāstu visṛjantaḥ kharasvanān
vyomni meghā vivartante paruṣā gardabhāruṇāḥ

translations.english: Yonder threatening clouds of asinine sable, showering down blood and uttering loud sounds are ranging the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
सधूमाश्च शराः सर्वे मम युद्धाभिनन्दिनः
रुक्मपृष्ठानि चापानि विवेष्टन्ते च लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
sadhūmāśca śarāḥ sarve mama yuddhābhinandinaḥ
rukmapṛṣṭhāni cāpāni viveṣṭante ca lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: And, O discerning one, rejoicing at the prospect of my fight, all these arrows emit smoke, and my bows plaited on the back with gold, are restless.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशा इह कूजन्ति पक्षिणो वनचारिणः
अग्रतो नो भयं प्राप्तं संशयो जीवितस्य च
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśā iha kūjanti pakṣiṇo vanacāriṇaḥ
agrato no bhayaṁ prāptaṁ saṁśayo jīvitasya ca

translations.english: Meseems from the noise of the wild birds that impending on us is danger and uncertainty to life.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रहारस्तु सुमहान्भविष्यति न संशयः
अयमाख्याति मे बाहुः स्फुरमाणो मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
saṁprahārastu sumahānbhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ
ayamākhyāti me bāhuḥ sphuramāṇo muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: Without doubt, there shall take place a mighty conflict. At this critical time, my arin shaking momentarily, betokens, O hero, victory to us, and defeat to the enemy. And your face appear pleasant with a delightful lustre.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यतानां हि युद्धार्थं येषां भवति लक्ष्मणः
निष्प्रभं वदनं तेषां भवत्यायुः परिक्षयः
verses.transliteration:
udyatānāṁ hi yuddhārthaṁ yeṣāṁ bhavati lakṣmaṇaḥ
niṣprabhaṁ vadanaṁ teṣāṁ bhavatyāyuḥ parikṣayaḥ

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, the pallid face of those that prepare for conflict, auger shortening of life.

verses.sanskrit:
अनागतविधानं तु कर्तव्यं शुभमिच्छता
आपदं शङ्कमानेन पुरुषेण विपश्चिता
verses.transliteration:
anāgatavidhānaṁ tu kartavyaṁ śubhamicchatā
āpadaṁ śaṅkamānena puruṣeṇa vipaścitā

translations.english: A considerate person that wishes for his welfare, apprehending peril, should prevent disaster ere it arrives.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्माद्गृहीत्वा वैदेहीं शरपाणिर्धनुर्धरः
गुहामाश्रयशैलस्य दुर्गां पादपसंकुलाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasmādgṛhītvā vaidehīṁ śarapāṇirdhanurdharaḥ
guhāmāśrayaśailasya durgāṁ pādapasaṁkulām

translations.english: Therefore bearing arrows in your hand, and equipped with your bow, do you, taking Videha's daughter, take refuge in the mountain cavern, covered with trees and difficult of access.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिकूलितुमिच्छामि न हि वाक्यमिदं त्वया
शापितो मम पादाभ्यां गम्यतां वत्स माचिरम्
verses.transliteration:
pratikūlitumicchāmi na hi vākyamidaṁ tvayā
śāpito mama pādābhyāṁ gamyatāṁ vatsa māciram

translations.english: That you should act contrary to my words, is what I do not wish. Swearing by my feet, go you without delay, my brother.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया
शरानादाय चापं च गुहां दुर्गां समाश्रयत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
śarānādāya cāpaṁ ca guhāṁ durgāṁ samāśrayat

translations.english: Thus accosted by Rama, Laksmana, taking arrows and a bow, took refuge in an inaccessible cave along with Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्प्रविष्टे तु गुहां लक्ष्मणे सह सीतया
हन्त निर्युक्तमित्युक्त्वा रामः कवचमाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
tasminpraviṣṭe tu guhāṁ lakṣmaṇe saha sītayā
hanta niryuktamityuktvā rāmaḥ kavacamāviśat

translations.english: Thereupon, saying, Ah! we have spoken it sharp, Rāma put on his mail. And adorned with that mail resembling fire Rāma appeared in the dark like a mighty flame streaming up.

verses.sanskrit:
स चापमुद्यम्य महच्छरानादाय वीर्यवान्
बभूवावस्थितस्तत्र ज्यास्वनैः पूरयन्दिशः
verses.transliteration:
sa cāpamudyamya mahaccharānādāya vīryavān
babhūvāvasthitastatra jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayandiśaḥ

translations.english: And uplifting his bow, and taking his arrows, that powerful one stood there, feeling all directions with the twangs of his bow-string.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
एकश्च रामो धर्मात्मा कथं युद्धं भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
ekaśca rāmo dharmātmā kathaṁ yuddhaṁ bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Having said this, they again spoke, eyeing one another, There are fourteen thousand of the Rākşasas of dreadful deed while the righteous Rāma is single. How can fight take place (between two such parties)?

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ताः श्वापदा वनचारिणः
दुद्रुवुर्यत्र निःशब्दं पृष्ठतो नावलोकयन्
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena vitrastāḥ śvāpadā vanacāriṇaḥ
dudruvuryatra niḥśabdaṁ pṛṣṭhato nāvalokayan

translations.english: The universal uproar filled that (entire) forest. Scared and terrified at the hubbub the rangers of the wood fle: to quarters free from noise; nor did they cast their eyes backward.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्वनीकं महावेगं रामं समुपसर्पत
घृतनानाप्रहरणं गम्भीरं सागरोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
tattvanīkaṁ mahāvegaṁ rāmaṁ samupasarpata
ghṛtanānāpraharaṇaṁ gambhīraṁ sāgaropamam

translations.english: And that army resembling the ocean, and rife with sounds, equipped with various weapons, with furious speed came towards Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
रामोऽपि चारयंश्चक्षुः सर्वतो रणपण्डितः
ददर्श खरसैन्यं तद्युद्धाभिमुखमुद्यतम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmo'pi cārayaṁścakṣuḥ sarvato raṇapaṇḍitaḥ
dadarśa kharasainyaṁ tadyuddhābhimukhamudyatam

translations.english: And Rāma also versed in warfare, casting his eyes around, found the forces of Khara ready for fight. Another text:-The holder of Pinaka.

verses.sanskrit:
वितत्य च धनुर्भीमं तूण्याश्चोद्धृत्य सायकान्
क्रोधमाहारयत्तीव्रं वधार्थं सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
vitatya ca dhanurbhīmaṁ tūṇyāścoddhṛtya sāyakān
krodhamāhārayattīvraṁ vadhārthaṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: Then stretching his dreadful bow, and swiftly taking out shafts, (Rāma) for compassing the destruction of the entire body of the Rākşasas, waxed furiously enraged. And like to the flaming fire at the universal dissolution, he, growing wroth, was incapable of being looked i at.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य क्रुद्धस्य रूपं तु रामस्य ददृशे तदा
दक्षस्येव क्रतुं हन्तुमुद्यतस्य पिनाकिनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya kruddhasya rūpaṁ tu rāmasya dadṛśe tadā
dakṣasyeva kratuṁ hantumudyatasya pinākinaḥ

translations.english: And seeing him filled with energy, the sylvan deities were extremely pained*. And the aspect of the enraged Rāma appeared like that of the holder of Pināka, intent upon destroying Dakşa's sacrifice. Another reading is:-The sylvan deities fled away.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा सगुणं चापमुद्यम्य खरनिःस्वनम्
रामस्याभिमुखं सूतं चोद्यतामित्यचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā saguṇaṁ cāpamudyamya kharaniḥsvanam
rāmasyābhimukhaṁ sūtaṁ codyatāmityacodayat

translations.english: Coming to the asylum, Khara in company with those that went before him, saw that slayer of foes, the enraged Rāma, holding his bow. And seeing him, Khara possessing a shrill voice, raising his bow, commanded to the charioteer to drive towards Rāma, Drive on!

verses.sanskrit:
स खरस्याज्ञया सूतस्तुरगान्समचोदयत्
यत्र रामो महाबाहुरेको धुन्वन्धनुः स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
sa kharasyājñayā sūtasturagānsamacodayat
yatra rāmo mahābāhureko dhunvandhanuḥ sthitaḥ

translations.english: At Khara's command, the charioteer drove the steeds to where the mighty—arined Rāma stood alone, holding his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु निष्पतितं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे ते रजनीचराः
नर्दमाना महानादं सचिवाः पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu niṣpatitaṁ dṛṣṭvā sarve te rajanīcarāḥ
nardamānā mahānādaṁ sacivāḥ paryavārayan

translations.english: And seeing him (Khara) entered the field, all those rangers of the night-the counsellers-uttering mighty shouts, cnvironed him round.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेषां यातुधानानां मध्ये रतो गतः खरः
बभूव मध्ये ताराणां लोहिताङ्ग इवोदितः
verses.transliteration:
sa teṣāṁ yātudhānānāṁ madhye rato gataḥ kharaḥ
babhūva madhye tārāṇāṁ lohitāṅga ivoditaḥ

translations.english: Khara stationed on his car in the midst of Rākşasas appeared like red bodied one risen in the midst of the stars.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं भीमधन्वानं क्रुद्धाः सर्वे निशाचराः
रामं नानाविधैः शस्त्रैरभ्यवर्षन्त दुर्जयम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ bhīmadhanvānaṁ kruddhāḥ sarve niśācarāḥ
rāmaṁ nānāvidhaiḥ śastrairabhyavarṣanta durjayam

translations.english: Then all the rangers of the night, waxing exceeding wroth, showered various weapons on that terrible bowman, the invincible Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
मुद्गरैरायसैः शूलैः प्रासैः खड्गैः परश्वधैः
राक्षसाः समरे रामं निजघ्नू रोषतत्पराः
verses.transliteration:
mudgarairāyasaiḥ śūlaiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
rākṣasāḥ samare rāmaṁ nijaghnū roṣatatparāḥ

translations.english: And wrought up with rage, the Rākṣasas in battle assailed him with iron clubs, and darts, and prāsas, and swords, and axes.

verses.sanskrit:
ते बलाहकसंकाशा महानादा महाबलाः
अभ्यधावन्त काकुत्स्थं रामं युद्धे जिघांसवः
verses.transliteration:
te balāhakasaṁkāśā mahānādā mahābalāḥ
abhyadhāvanta kākutsthaṁ rāmaṁ yuddhe jighāṁsavaḥ

translations.english: And resembling clouds (in hue), the exceedingly strong Rākṣasas, having huge bodies, darted towards Kākutstha by means of steeds and cars.

verses.sanskrit:
ते रामे शरवर्षाणि व्यसृजन्रक्षसां गुणाः
शैलेन्द्रमिव धाराभिर्वर्षमाणा महाधनाः
verses.transliteration:
te rāme śaravarṣāṇi vyasṛjanrakṣasāṁ guṇāḥ
śailendramiva dhārābhirvarṣamāṇā mahādhanāḥ

translations.english: And mounted on elephants resembling mountain-peaks, numbers of Rākṣasas, intent upon staying Rāma in battle, showered arrows on him, as mighty clouds pour down showers on the monarch of mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः परिवृतो घोरै राघवो रक्षसां गणैः
तिथिष्विव महादेवो वृतः पारिषदां गणैः
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ parivṛto ghorai rāghavo rakṣasāṁ gaṇaiḥ
tithiṣviva mahādevo vṛtaḥ pāriṣadāṁ gaṇaiḥ

translations.english: Rāma was hemmed in by all those fiercelooking Raksasas, even as in the evening Mahādeva is surrounded by his courtiers.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि मुक्तानि शस्त्राणि यातुधानैः स राघवः
प्रतिजग्राह विशिखैर्नद्योघानिव सागरः
verses.transliteration:
tāni muktāni śastrāṇi yātudhānaiḥ sa rāghavaḥ
pratijagrāha viśikhairnadyoghāniva sāgaraḥ

translations.english: And as the ocean resisted the tide of a river, Rāghava by means of arrow resist the weapons discharged by the Yātudhānas.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः प्रहरणैर्घोरैर्भिन्नगात्रो न विव्यथे
रामः प्रदीप्तैर्बहुभिर्वज्रैरिव महाचलः
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ praharaṇairghorairbhinnagātro na vivyathe
rāmaḥ pradīptairbahubhirvajrairiva mahācalaḥ

translations.english: As a mighty mountain, assailed by the thunderbolt, dose not feel pain, Rāma, having his person pierced by terrible flaming weapons, did not feel pain.

verses.sanskrit:
स विद्धः क्षतजादिग्धः सर्वगात्रेषु राघवः
बभूव रामः संध्याभ्रैर्दिवाकर इवावृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa viddhaḥ kṣatajādigdhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāghavaḥ
babhūva rāmaḥ saṁdhyābhrairdivākara ivāvṛtaḥ

translations.english: And pierced, and with his person covered with blood, Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, resembled the sun enveloped in evening clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
विषेदुर्देवगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
एकं सहस्त्रैर्बहुभिस्तदा दृष्ट्वा समावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
viṣedurdevagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
ekaṁ sahastrairbahubhistadā dṛṣṭvā samāvṛtam

translations.english: And seeing him single, surrounded by many thousand, the Gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and supreme saints became sorrowful.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामः सुसंक्रुद्धो मण्डलीकृतकार्मुकः
ससर्ज निशितान्बाणाञ्शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmaḥ susaṁkruddho maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ
sasarja niśitānbāṇāñśataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Then Rama getting enraged, bringing his bow to a circle, discharged sharpened shafts by hundreds and by thousands. And as if in sport, Rāma in the conflict shot irresistible (shafts) furnished with Kanka feathers, and decked with gold, irresistible, capable of inflicting extreme pain, and resembling the noose of Death.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शराः शत्रुसैन्येषु मुक्ता रामेण लीलया
आददू रक्षसां प्राणान्पाशाः कालकृता इव
verses.transliteration:
te śarāḥ śatrusainyeṣu muktā rāmeṇa līlayā
ādadū rakṣasāṁ prāṇānpāśāḥ kālakṛtā iva

translations.english: And sportively discharged by Rāma, those arrows deprived the Rākṣasas of their lives, like the noose forged by death.

verses.sanskrit:
भित्त्वा राक्षसदेहांस्तांस्ते शरा रुधिराप्लुताः
अन्तरिक्षगता रेजुर्दीप्ताग्निसमतेजसः
verses.transliteration:
bhittvā rākṣasadehāṁstāṁste śarā rudhirāplutāḥ
antarikṣagatā rejurdīptāgnisamatejasaḥ

translations.english: And piercing the persons of the Rākşasas, those arrows, soaked in blood, going up to the sky, appeared with the splendour of flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
असंख्येयास्तु रामस्य सायकाश्चापमण्डलात्
विनिष्पेतुरतीवोग्रा रक्षः प्राणापहारिणः
verses.transliteration:
asaṁkhyeyāstu rāmasya sāyakāścāpamaṇḍalāt
viniṣpeturatīvogrā rakṣaḥ prāṇāpahāriṇaḥ

translations.english: And innumerable shafts, exceedingly fierce, capable of depriving the Rāksasas of their lives, were let go from the circle of his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्धनूंषि ध्वजाग्राणि वर्माणि च शिरांसि च
बहून्सहस्ताभरणानूरून्करिकरोपमान्
verses.transliteration:
tairdhanūṁṣi dhvajāgrāṇi varmāṇi ca śirāṁsi ca
bahūnsahastābharaṇānūrūnkarikaropamān

translations.english: And with those Rāma severed bows, in baitle by hundreds and by thousands and flag ends, and shields, and mail, and many arms with embellished hands, resembling the trunks of elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नालीकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णाग्रैश्च विकर्णिभिः
भीममार्तस्वरं चक्रुर्भिद्यमाना निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
tato nālīkanārācaistīkṣṇāgraiśca vikarṇibhiḥ
bhīmamārtasvaraṁ cakrurbhidyamānā niśācarāḥ

translations.english: And cut off with nālīkas (steel-pointed arrows) and, nārācas (arrows wholly made of steel), and sharp-pointed vikarnas (barbed arrows), the rangers of the night uttered dreadful howls of distress.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सैन्यं निशितैर्बाणैरर्दितं मर्मभेदिभिः
रामेण न सुखं लेभे शुष्कं वनमिवाग्निना
verses.transliteration:
tatsainyaṁ niśitairbāṇairarditaṁ marmabhedibhiḥ
rāmeṇa na sukhaṁ lebhe śuṣkaṁ vanamivāgninā

translations.english: And like a withered wood afflicted by fire, that host harassed by the various marrowpiercing* shafts shot by Rāma, did not attain ease. Another reading is, sharpened.

verses.sanskrit:
केचिद्भीमबलाः शूराः शूलान्खड्गान्परश्वधान्
चिक्षिपुः परमक्रुद्धा रामाय रजनीचराः
verses.transliteration:
kecidbhīmabalāḥ śūrāḥ śūlānkhaḍgānparaśvadhān
cikṣipuḥ paramakruddhā rāmāya rajanīcarāḥ

translations.english: And some heroic rangers of the night possessed of great strength, waxing furious, threw at Rāma rrāsas, and darts and axes. Another reading: remaining before Rāma, threw powerful weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि बाणैर्महाबाहुः शस्त्राण्यावार्य राघवः
जहार समरे प्राणांश्चिच्छेद च शिरोधरान्
verses.transliteration:
tāni bāṇairmahābāhuḥ śastrāṇyāvārya rāghavaḥ
jahāra samare prāṇāṁściccheda ca śirodharān

translations.english: Thereupon resisting by means of shafts those weapons of theirs, the mighty-armed Rāma endued with prowess, took their lives in the conflict, and cut off the heads (of warriors).

verses.sanskrit:
अवशिष्टाश्च ये तत्र विषण्णाश्च निशाचराः
खरमेवाभ्यधावन्त शरणार्थं शरार्दिताः
verses.transliteration:
avaśiṣṭāśca ye tatra viṣaṇṇāśca niśācarāḥ
kharamevābhyadhāvanta śaraṇārthaṁ śarārditāḥ

translations.english: And having their heads, and shields and bowstrings, severed, they fell as fall on the earth trees thrown down by blasts froin the wings of Suparņa*. Those rangers of the night that remained there, wounded by arrows, and losing heart, fled with speed to Khara, to seek his protection. *Lit.-Of fair feather. A name of Garuda.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्सर्वान्पुनरादाय समाश्वास्य च दूषणः
अभ्यधावत काकुत्स्थं क्रुद्धो रुद्रमिवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
tānsarvānpunarādāya samāśvāsya ca dūṣaṇaḥ
abhyadhāvata kākutsthaṁ kruddho rudramivāntakaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, encouraging them, Dāsana, taking his bow, ran furiously in high rage against Răma, like the enraged Destroyer himself,

verses.sanskrit:
निवृत्तास्तु पुनः सर्वे दूषणाश्रयनिर्भयाः
राममेवाभ्यधावन्त सालतालशिलायुधाः
verses.transliteration:
nivṛttāstu punaḥ sarve dūṣaṇāśrayanirbhayāḥ
rāmamevābhyadhāvanta sālatālaśilāyudhāḥ

translations.english: And rallied again (by Dāsana) and, their fear dispelled through their having founded refuge with him, they armed with sālas, tālas, and crags, darted against Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बभूवाद्भुतं युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम्
रामस्यास्य महाघोरं पुनस्तेषां च रक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
tadbabhūvādbhutaṁ yuddhaṁ tumulaṁ romaharṣaṇam
rāmasyāsya mahāghoraṁ punasteṣāṁ ca rakṣasām

translations.english: And the Räkşasas discharged vollies of trees and crags. And capable of making one's hair stand on end, that battle was dreadful and furious and now on the side of Rāma and now again on: that of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्द्रुमाणां शिलानां च वर्षं प्राणहरं महत्
प्रतिजग्राह धर्मात्मा राघवस्तीक्ष्णसायकैः
verses.transliteration:
taddrumāṇāṁ śilānāṁ ca varṣaṁ prāṇaharaṁ mahat
pratijagrāha dharmātmā rāghavastīkṣṇasāyakaiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon by means of shafts the righteous Rāghava resisted that mighty destructive shower of trees and stones.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य च तद्वरं निमीलित इवर्षभः
रामः क्रोधं परं भेजे वधार्थं सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya ca tadvaraṁ nimīlita ivarṣabhaḥ
rāmaḥ krodhaṁ paraṁ bheje vadhārthaṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: Resisting that shower, Rāma with his eyes staring and resembling a bull, flew into a great rage, for the purpose of slaying the whole body of Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टः प्रदीप्त इव तेजसा
शरैरभ्यकिरत्सैन्यं सर्वतः सहदूषणम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ pradīpta iva tejasā
śarairabhyakiratsainyaṁ sarvataḥ sahadūṣaṇam

translations.english: Then influenced by wrath, and flaming in energy, he on all sides covered the army along with Düşana with arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
वेष्टितं काञ्चनैः पट्टैर्देवसैन्याभिमर्दनम्
आयसैः शङ्कुभिस्तीक्ष्णैः कीर्णं परवसोक्षिताम्
verses.transliteration:
veṣṭitaṁ kāñcanaiḥ paṭṭairdevasainyābhimardanam
āyasaiḥ śaṅkubhistīkṣṇaiḥ kīrṇaṁ paravasokṣitām

translations.english: His bow cut off, his steeds together with the charioteer slain, and himself deprived of his car, he (Dūşana) took a parigha resembling a mountain peak, able to me one's down stand on end plated with gold, capable of afflicting celestial hosts, studded with sharp iron sankus, and graced with the fal of foes;-of the touch of a thunder-bolt, able to pierce the persons of enemies*. The text may also mean able to rend the cities of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शं परगोपुरदारणम्
तं महोरगसंकाशं प्रगृह्य परिघं रणे
दूषणोऽभ्यपतद्रामं क्रूरकर्मा निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
vajrāśanisamasparśaṁ paragopuradāraṇam
taṁ mahoragasaṁkāśaṁ pragṛhya parighaṁ raṇe
dūṣaṇo'bhyapatadrāmaṁ krūrakarmā niśācaraḥ

translations.english: And taking up in that encounter the parigha (an iron club) resembling a mighty snake, that ranger of the night of cruel deeds Duşaņa, rushed towards Rāina.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याभिपतमानस्य दूषणस्य स राघवः
द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां चिच्छेद सहस्ताभरणौ भुजौ
verses.transliteration:
tasyābhipatamānasya dūṣaṇasya sa rāghavaḥ
dvābhyāṁ śarābhyāṁ ciccheda sahastābharaṇau bhujau

translations.english: And as Dūsuņa was rushing forward, Rāghava by means of a couple of shafts cut off his two arms with the ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रष्टस्तस्य महाकायः पपात रणमूर्धनि
परिघश्छिन्नहस्तस्य शक्रध्वज इवाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
bhraṣṭastasya mahākāyaḥ papāta raṇamūrdhani
parighaśchinnahastasya śakradhvaja ivāgrataḥ

translations.english: And the huge parigha (an iron club) escaping from (Dusana's grasp) fell forward on the field like the banner of Sakra.

verses.sanskrit:
स कराभ्यां विकीर्णाभ्यां पपात भुवि दूषणः
विषाणाभ्यां विशीर्णाभ्यां मनस्वीव महागजः
verses.transliteration:
sa karābhyāṁ vikīrṇābhyāṁ papāta bhuvi dūṣaṇaḥ
viṣāṇābhyāṁ viśīrṇābhyāṁ manasvīva mahāgajaḥ

translations.english: And like a nighty elephant whose husks have fallen off, Dūşana, on his arms having been severed, fell down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तं पतितं भूमौ दूषणं निहतं रणे
साधु साध्विति काकुत्स्थं सर्वभूतान्यपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā taṁ patitaṁ bhūmau dūṣaṇaṁ nihataṁ raṇe
sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṁ sarvabhūtānyapūjayan

translations.english: Seeing Dūşaņa down on the ground, and slain in battle, all creatures, saying, ''well done! well done!" paid homage to Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धास्त्रयः सेनाग्रयायिनः
संहत्याभ्यद्रवन्रामं मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः
महाकपालः स्थूलाक्षः प्रमाथी च महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare kruddhāstrayaḥ senāgrayāyinaḥ
saṁhatyābhyadravanrāmaṁ mṛtyupāśāvapāśitāḥ
mahākapālaḥ sthūlākṣaḥ pramāthī ca mahābalaḥ

translations.english: In the meantime, three generals, getting wioth, being entrapped in the noose of death, rushed against Rāma in a body, viz; Mahakapāla, Stūlākșa, and the mighty Pramāthī the Rāksasa, Mahākapäla, upraising a large dart, and Sthulaksa, taking a pattisa, and Pramāthi all axe.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वैवापततस्तांस्तु राघवः सायकैः शितैः
तीक्ष्णाग्रैः प्रतिजग्राह संप्राप्तानतिथीनिव
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvaivāpatatastāṁstu rāghavaḥ sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ
tīkṣṇāgraiḥ pratijagrāha saṁprāptānatithīniva

translations.english: And as Rāghava beheld them advance, he resisted them by means of sharp and keen-edged shafts, even as one receives guests that have come.

verses.sanskrit:
महाकपालस्य शिरश्चिच्छेद रघुनङ्गनः
असंख्येयैस्तु बाणौघैः प्रममाथ प्रमाथिनम्
verses.transliteration:
mahākapālasya śiraściccheda raghunaṅganaḥ
asaṁkhyeyaistu bāṇaughaiḥ pramamātha pramāthinam

translations.english: And Raghu's son split Mahākapāla's head, afflicted Pramăthſ with countless shafts, and lodged the eyes of Sthūlāksya with sharp shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पावकसंकाशैर्हेमवज्रविभूषितैः
जघनशेषं तेजस्वी तस्य सैन्यस्य सायकैः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pāvakasaṁkāśairhemavajravibhūṣitaiḥ
jaghanaśeṣaṁ tejasvī tasya sainyasya sāyakaiḥ

translations.english: Threat with shafts resembling fire, and decked with diamonds and with gold, (Rāma) possessed of energy destroyed the rest of his (Khara's) forces.

verses.sanskrit:
ते रुक्मपुङ्खा विशिखाः सधूमा इव पावकाः
निजघ्नुस्तानि रक्षांसि वज्रा इव महाद्रुमान्
verses.transliteration:
te rukmapuṅkhā viśikhāḥ sadhūmā iva pāvakāḥ
nijaghnustāni rakṣāṁsi vajrā iva mahādrumān

translations.english: And as the thunderbolt slay the mighty, Asuras, those shafts studded with gold, and like to smoking fire, slew those Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षसां तु शतं रामः शतेनैकेन कर्णिना
सहस्रं च सहस्रेण जघान रणमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
rakṣasāṁ tu śataṁ rāmaḥ śatenaikena karṇinā
sahasraṁ ca sahasreṇa jaghāna raṇamūrdhani

translations.english: And in the field Rāma slew an hundred Rāks asa with an hundred Karnis, and a thousand (again) with a thousand.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्भिन्नवर्माभरणाश्छिन्नभिन्नशरासनाः
निपेतुः शोणितादिग्धा धरण्यां रजनीचराः
verses.transliteration:
tairbhinnavarmābharaṇāśchinnabhinnaśarāsanāḥ
nipetuḥ śoṇitādigdhā dharaṇyāṁ rajanīcarāḥ

translations.english: And, their armour and ornaments severed, and their bows broken in shivers, those rangers of the night fell down on the earth, bathed in blood.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्मुक्तकेशैः समरे पतितैः शोणितोक्षितैः
आस्तीर्णा वसुधा कृत्स्ना महावेदिः कुशैरिव
verses.transliteration:
tairmuktakeśaiḥ samare patitaiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ
āstīrṇā vasudhā kṛtsnā mahāvediḥ kuśairiva

translations.english: And as a spacious dais is covered with Kusa, the entire field was scattered with the Rākṣasas fallen in battle with hair dishevelled, and covered with blood.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षणेन तु महाघोरं वनं निहतराक्षसं
बभूव निरय प्रख्यं मांसशोणितकर्दमम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣaṇena tu mahāghoraṁ vanaṁ nihatarākṣasaṁ
babhūva niraya prakhyaṁ māṁsaśoṇitakardamam

translations.english: And at that time that fearful forest, with the Rākṣasas slaughtered, and with its clay mired with flesh and blood, resembled hell itself.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
हतान्येकेन रामेण मानुषेण पदातिना
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
hatānyekena rāmeṇa mānuṣeṇa padātinā

translations.english: Fourteen thousand Rākṣasas of dreadful deeds were slain by Rāma single, a human being, fighting, (moreover) on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सैन्यस्य सर्वस्य खरः शेषो महारथः
राक्षसस्त्रिशिराश्चैव रामश्च रिपुसूदनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya sainyasya sarvasya kharaḥ śeṣo mahārathaḥ
rākṣasastriśirāścaiva rāmaśca ripusūdanaḥ

translations.english: And the remnant of his (Khara's) forces were that mighty car-warrior, Khara himself, and the Raksasa, Trisirā; and (on the other side) was that destroyer of foes-Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तद्भीमबलं महाहवे; समीक्ष्य रामेण हतं बलीयसा
रथेन रामं महता खरस्ततः; समाससादेन्द्र इवोद्यताशनिः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu tadbhīmabalaṁ mahāhave; samīkṣya rāmeṇa hataṁ balīyasā
rathena rāmaṁ mahatā kharastataḥ; samāsasādendra ivodyatāśaniḥ

translations.english: Then seeing that dreadful army destroyed in terrible conflict by the mighty Rāma, Khara ascending a great car, advanced before Rāma, like Indra with the upraised thunderbolt. Then seeing that dreadful army destroyed in terrible conflict by the mighty Rāma, Khara ascending a great car, advanced before Rāma, like Indra with the upraised thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
खरं तु रामाभिमुखं प्रयान्तं वाहिनीपतिः
राक्षसस्त्रिशिरा नाम संनिपत्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kharaṁ tu rāmābhimukhaṁ prayāntaṁ vāhinīpatiḥ
rākṣasastriśirā nāma saṁnipatyedamabravīt

translations.english: As Khara was advancing before Rāma, that leader of the army named Triſirā, approaching him, said.

verses.sanskrit:
मां नियोजय विक्रान्त संनिवर्तस्व साहसात्
पश्य रामं महाबाहुं संयुगे विनिपातितम्
verses.transliteration:
māṁ niyojaya vikrānta saṁnivartasva sāhasāt
paśya rāmaṁ mahābāhuṁ saṁyuge vinipātitam

translations.english: Do you employ me, who am possessed of prowess, and yourself desist from this rashness. Behold the mighty-armed Rāma brought down in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यमायुधं चाहमालभे
यथा रामं वधिष्यामि वधार्हं सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
pratijānāmi te satyamāyudhaṁ cāhamālabhe
yathā rāmaṁ vadhiṣyāmi vadhārhaṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: I swear (to you) truly; I touch this weapon, (to say) that I will stay Rāma, who deserves to be slain by all the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं वास्य रणे मृत्युरेष वा समरे मम
विनिवर्त्य रणोत्साहं मुहूर्तं प्राश्निको भव
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ vāsya raṇe mṛtyureṣa vā samare mama
vinivartya raṇotsāhaṁ muhūrtaṁ prāśniko bhava

translations.english: Either I shall prove his death in battle, or he shall prove mine. Restraining your martial ardour, do you for a while become a witness.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टो वा हते रामे जनस्थानं प्रयास्यसि
मयि वा निहते रामं संयुगायोपयास्यसि
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭo vā hate rāme janasthānaṁ prayāsyasi
mayi vā nihate rāmaṁ saṁyugāyopayāsyasi

translations.english: Either, joyed in consequence of Rāma being slain, you shall repair to Janasthāna; or I being slain you shall enter the field (against him).

verses.sanskrit:
खरस्त्रिशिरसा तेन मृत्युलोभात्प्रसादितः
गच्छ युध्येत्यनुज्ञातो राघवाभिमुखो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
kharastriśirasā tena mṛtyulobhātprasāditaḥ
gaccha yudhyetyanujñāto rāghavābhimukho yayau

translations.english: Thus satisfied by Trisirā, from his desire to meet with death, the latter, on being permitted with Go, proceeded towards Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिशिराश्च रथेनैव वाजियुक्तेन भास्वता
अभ्यद्रवद्रणे रामं त्रिशृङ्ग इव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
triśirāśca rathenaiva vājiyuktena bhāsvatā
abhyadravadraṇe rāmaṁ triśṛṅga iva parvataḥ

translations.english: And like a hill with three sumınits, Trisirā rushed towards Rāma on an effulgent car yoked with steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
शरधारा समूहान्स महामेघ इवोत्सृजन्
व्यसृजत्सदृशं नादं जलार्द्रस्येव दुन्दुभेः
verses.transliteration:
śaradhārā samūhānsa mahāmegha ivotsṛjan
vyasṛjatsadṛśaṁ nādaṁ jalārdrasyeva dundubheḥ

translations.english: And as a mighty cloud pours down shower, (Trisirā) discharging vollies of shafts, uttered a roar resembling the sound of a wet kettledrum.

verses.sanskrit:
आगच्छन्तं त्रिशिरसं राक्षसं प्रेक्ष्य राघवः
धनुषा प्रतिजग्राह विधुन्वन्सायकाञ्शितान्
verses.transliteration:
āgacchantaṁ triśirasaṁ rākṣasaṁ prekṣya rāghavaḥ
dhanuṣā pratijagrāha vidhunvansāyakāñśitān

translations.english: And seeing that the Rākşasa Trisirã was advancing, Raghava resisted (his attack) by discharging sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्रहारस्तुमुलो राम त्रिशिरसोर्महान्
बभूवातीव बलिनोः सिंहकुञ्जरयोरिव
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprahārastumulo rāma triśirasormahān
babhūvātīva balinoḥ siṁhakuñjarayoriva

translations.english: And that encounter of those exceedingly powerful ones, Rāma and Triſiră was fierce, like to that between a lion and an elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्रिशिरसा बाणैर्ललाटे ताडितस्त्रिभिः
अमर्षी कुपितो रामः संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastriśirasā bāṇairlalāṭe tāḍitastribhiḥ
amarṣī kupito rāmaḥ saṁrabdhamidamabravīt

translations.english: Then struck on the forehead by a brace of shafts shot by Trisirā, the wrathful Rāma enraged, and inflamed with anger, said.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो विक्रमशूरस्य राक्षसस्येदृशं बलम्
पुष्पैरिव शरैर्यस्य ललाटेऽस्मि परिक्षतः
ममापि प्रतिगृह्णीष्व शरांश्चापगुणच्युतान्
verses.transliteration:
aho vikramaśūrasya rākṣasasyedṛśaṁ balam
puṣpairiva śarairyasya lalāṭe'smi parikṣataḥ
mamāpi pratigṛhṇīṣva śarāṁścāpaguṇacyutān

translations.english: Ah! such is the strength of the heroic Rākşasas! I have been wounded in the forehead with shafts resembling flowers. Do you also take the arrows shot from my bow.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु संरब्धः शरानाशीविषोपमान्
त्रिशिरो वक्षसि क्रुद्धो निजघान चतुर्दश
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu saṁrabdhaḥ śarānāśīviṣopamān
triśiro vakṣasi kruddho nijaghāna caturdaśa

translations.english: Saying this, (Rāma) enraged, and influenced by wrath, wounded Trisiră in the breast with fourteen arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्भिस्तुरगानस्य शरैः संनतपर्वभिः
न्यपातयत तेजस्वी चतुरस्तस्य वाजिनः
verses.transliteration:
caturbhisturagānasya śaraiḥ saṁnataparvabhiḥ
nyapātayata tejasvī caturastasya vājinaḥ

translations.english: And that energetic one by means of four shafts having their joints bent, brought down his four steeds. And by means of eight arrows (Rāma) laid low the charioteer from the front of the car.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हतरथात्तस्मादुत्पतन्तं निशाचरम्
बिभेद रामस्तं बाणैर्हृदये सोऽभवज्जडः
verses.transliteration:
tato hatarathāttasmādutpatantaṁ niśācaram
bibheda rāmastaṁ bāṇairhṛdaye so'bhavajjaḍaḥ

translations.english: And Rāma with a shaft severed his upraised standard. Then as that ranger of the night was descending from his broken car, Rāma pierced his breast with arrows, and thereat he was stupified.

verses.sanskrit:
सायकैश्चाप्रमेयात्मा सामर्षस्तस्य रक्षसः
शिरांस्यपातयत्त्रीणि वेगवद्भिस्त्रिभिः शतैः
verses.transliteration:
sāyakaiścāprameyātmā sāmarṣastasya rakṣasaḥ
śirāṁsyapātayattrīṇi vegavadbhistribhiḥ śataiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, that one of immeasurable prowess, out of anger by means of three shafts possessed of celerity, brought down Trisira's three heads.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूमौ शोणितोद्गारी रामबाणाभिपीडितः
न्यपतत्पतितैः पूर्वं स्वशिरोभिर्निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūmau śoṇitodgārī rāmabāṇābhipīḍitaḥ
nyapatatpatitaiḥ pūrvaṁ svaśirobhirniśācaraḥ

translations.english: And that ranger of the night present in the field, afflicted by the shafts of Rāma, after his heads had fallen first, fell, vomiting smoking gore.

verses.sanskrit:
हतशेषास्ततो भग्ना राक्षसाः खरसंश्रयाः
द्रवन्ति स्म न तिष्ठन्ति व्याघ्रत्रस्ता मृगा इव
verses.transliteration:
hataśeṣāstato bhagnā rākṣasāḥ kharasaṁśrayāḥ
dravanti sma na tiṣṭhanti vyāghratrastā mṛgā iva

translations.english: And the Räksasas remaining after the rest had been slain, belonging to Khara's original forces losing heart, began to flee like deer terrified at a hunter.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्खरो द्रवतो दृष्ट्वा निवर्त्य रुषितः स्वयम्
राममेवाभिदुद्राव राहुश्चन्द्रमसं यथा
verses.transliteration:
tānkharo dravato dṛṣṭvā nivartya ruṣitaḥ svayam
rāmamevābhidudrāva rāhuścandramasaṁ yathā

translations.english: And seeing them fly, Khara waxing wroth, swiftly making them desist, darted towards Ráma, like Rāhu darting towards the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
निहतं दूषणं दृष्ट्वा रणे त्रिशिरसा सह
खरस्याप्यभवत्त्रासो दृष्ट्वा रामस्य विक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
nihataṁ dūṣaṇaṁ dṛṣṭvā raṇe triśirasā saha
kharasyāpyabhavattrāso dṛṣṭvā rāmasya vikramam

translations.english: Seeing Düşaņa slain in fight along with Trisiră, Khara, witnessing Rāma's prowess, was filled with fear.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं सैन्यमविषह्यं महाबलम्
हतमेकेन रामेण दूषणस्त्रिशिरा अपि
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṁ sainyamaviṣahyaṁ mahābalam
hatamekena rāmeṇa dūṣaṇastriśirā api

translations.english: Seeing that irresistible Raksasa host-even Düşaņa and Triſirā-slain by the mighty Rāma alone, and seeing the great courage that was made in the army, that Raksasa, Khara, was seized with despondency. Then as Namuci advances against Väsava, Khara stretching his powerful bow, advanced against Răma.

verses.sanskrit:
विकृष्य बलवच्चापं नाराचान्रक्तभोजनान्
खरश्चिक्षेप रामाय क्रुद्धानाशीविषानिव
verses.transliteration:
vikṛṣya balavaccāpaṁ nārācānraktabhojanān
kharaścikṣepa rāmāya kruddhānāśīviṣāniva

translations.english: Khara hurled at Rāma nārācas revelling in blood, resembling infuriated venomous snakes.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्यां विधुन्वन्सुबहुशः शिक्षयास्त्राणि दर्शयन्
चचार समरे मार्गाञ्शरै रथगतः खरः
verses.transliteration:
jyāṁ vidhunvansubahuśaḥ śikṣayāstrāṇi darśayan
cacāra samare mārgāñśarai rathagataḥ kharaḥ

translations.english: Repeatedly twanging his twanging his bow, Khara, mounted on his car, began to range the field, displaying his weapons through his acquired skill.

verses.sanskrit:
स सर्वाश्च दिशो बाणैः प्रदिशश्च महारथः
पूरयामास तं दृष्ट्वा रामोऽपि सुमहद्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
sa sarvāśca diśo bāṇaiḥ pradiśaśca mahārathaḥ
pūrayāmāsa taṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmo'pi sumahaddhanuḥ

translations.english: And that mighty car-warrior covered all sides with his shafts. And secing this, Rāma of a tremendous bow with shafts incapable of being borne, and resembling tongues of flaming fire, entirely enveloped the welkin, even as a cloud pour down showers.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बभूव शितैर्बाणैः खररामविसर्जितैः
पर्याकाशमनाकाशं सर्वतः शरसंकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
tadbabhūva śitairbāṇaiḥ khararāmavisarjitaiḥ
paryākāśamanākāśaṁ sarvataḥ śarasaṁkulam

translations.english: With the sharpened shafts shot by Khara and Rāma, the entire firmament on all sides was thronged.

verses.sanskrit:
शरजालावृतः सूर्यो न तदा स्म प्रकाशते
अन्योन्यवधसंरम्भादुभयोः संप्रयुध्यतोः
verses.transliteration:
śarajālāvṛtaḥ sūryo na tadā sma prakāśate
anyonyavadhasaṁrambhādubhayoḥ saṁprayudhyatoḥ

translations.english: And as each enraged was engaged in coping with the other, the sun, enveloped in a net-work of shafts, did not appear.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नालीकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णाग्रैश्च विकर्णिभिः
आजघान रणे रामं तोत्रैरिव महाद्विपम्
verses.transliteration:
tato nālīkanārācaistīkṣṇāgraiśca vikarṇibhiḥ
ājaghāna raṇe rāmaṁ totrairiva mahādvipam

translations.english: As a mighty elephant is struck with the goad, Rāma in the conflict attacked (his opponent) with nalikas and nārācas and sharp-pointed vikarna.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रथस्थं धनुष्पाणिं राक्षसं पर्यवस्थितम्
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि पाशहस्तमिवान्तकम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rathasthaṁ dhanuṣpāṇiṁ rākṣasaṁ paryavasthitam
dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni pāśahastamivāntakam

translations.english: And as that Rākşasa sat on his car, bow in hand, all creatures saw him, as if he were the very destroyer with the noose in his hand.

verses.sanskrit:
तं सिंहमिव विक्रान्तं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्
दृष्ट्वा नोद्विजते रामः सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा
verses.transliteration:
taṁ siṁhamiva vikrāntaṁ siṁhavikrāntagāminam
dṛṣṭvā nodvijate rāmaḥ siṁhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṁ yathā

translations.english: Seeing that one powerful like the lion, and gifted with the vigorous gait of the lion, Rāma was not moved, as a lion seeing a puny deer (is not moved).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सूर्यनिकाशेन रथेन महता खरः
आससाद रणे रामं पतङ्ग इव पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sūryanikāśena rathena mahatā kharaḥ
āsasāda raṇe rāmaṁ pataṅga iva pāvakam

translations.english: And then as an insect falls into a flame, Khara mounting a mighty car, resembling the sun, approached Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽस्य सशरं चापं मुष्टिदेशे महात्मनः
खरश्चिच्छेद रामस्य दर्शयन्पाणिलाघवम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'sya saśaraṁ cāpaṁ muṣṭideśe mahātmanaḥ
kharaściccheda rāmasya darśayanpāṇilāghavam

translations.english: And, displaying his lightness of hand, Khara severed the bow of the magnanimous Rāma, with the arrow (fixed on it) at the place where it is grasped.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुनस्त्वपरान्सप्त शरानादाय वर्मणि
निजघान रणे क्रुद्धः शक्राशनिसमप्रभान्
verses.transliteration:
sa punastvaparānsapta śarānādāya varmaṇi
nijaghāna raṇe kruddhaḥ śakrāśanisamaprabhān

translations.english: Then taking up seven other shafts, resplendent like the thunderbolt of Sakra, Khara, enraged, sent them into (Rāma's) main-joints, and then afflicting Rāma of unparalleled energy with a thousand shafts, Khara sent up in that conflict a loud shout.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तत्प्रहतं बाणैः खरमुक्तैः सुपर्वभिः
पपात कवचं भूमौ रामस्यादित्यवर्चसः
verses.transliteration:
tatastatprahataṁ bāṇaiḥ kharamuktaiḥ suparvabhiḥ
papāta kavacaṁ bhūmau rāmasyādityavarcasaḥ

translations.english: And riven by the shafts discharged by Khara, Rāma's mail resembling the sun fell to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरैरर्पितः क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु राघवः
रराज समरे रामो विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्
verses.transliteration:
sa śarairarpitaḥ kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāghavaḥ
rarāja samare rāmo vidhūmo'gniriva jvalan

translations.english: And pierced with those arrow, all over his body, and inflamed with rage, Rāghava appeared in the field, like a smokeless flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गम्भीरनिर्ह्रादं रामः शत्रुनिबर्हणः
चकारान्ताय स रिपोः सज्यमन्यन्महद्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
tato gambhīranirhrādaṁ rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
cakārāntāya sa ripoḥ sajyamanyanmahaddhanuḥ

translations.english: Then that destroyer of foes, Rāma, for compassing the end of his enemy, stringed another mighty bow, sending forth solemn sounds, the redoubtable Vaisnava bow that had been conferred on him by the Maharşi.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कनकपुङ्खैस्तु शरैः संनतपर्वभिः
चिच्छेद रामः संक्रुद्धः खरस्य समरे ध्वजम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kanakapuṅkhaistu śaraiḥ saṁnataparvabhiḥ
ciccheda rāmaḥ saṁkruddhaḥ kharasya samare dhvajam

translations.english: And uplifting that superior bow, Rāma rushed against Khara. Then with shafts having bent knots and golden feathers, Rāma, wrought up with rage, severed in battle Khara's standard.

verses.sanskrit:
स दर्शनीयो बहुधा विच्छिन्नः काञ्चनो ध्वजः
जगाम धरणीं सूर्यो देवतानामिवाज्ञया
verses.transliteration:
sa darśanīyo bahudhā vicchinnaḥ kāñcano dhvajaḥ
jagāma dharaṇīṁ sūryo devatānāmivājñayā

translations.english: And on that exceedingly graceful golden standard being hewn down it seemed as if the sun dropped to the earth at the behest of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
तं चतुर्भिः खरः क्रुद्धो रामं गात्रेषु मार्गणैः
विव्याध हृदि मर्मज्ञो मातङ्गमिव तोमरैः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ caturbhiḥ kharaḥ kruddho rāmaṁ gātreṣu mārgaṇaiḥ
vivyādha hṛdi marmajño mātaṅgamiva tomaraiḥ

translations.english: And thereat Khara, understanding the import of things, fired with wrath, pierced Rāma's breast with five arrows, like one striking an elephant with a goad.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामो बहुभिर्बाणैः खरकार्मुकनिःसृतैः
विद्धो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गो बभूव रुषितो भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmo bahubhirbāṇaiḥ kharakārmukaniḥsṛtaiḥ
viddho rudhirasiktāṅgo babhūva ruṣito bhṛśam

translations.english: Rāma on being pierced with a good many shafts discharged from Khara's bow, and having his body bathed in blood, was highly wroth.

verses.sanskrit:
स धनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः प्रगृह्य परमाहवे
मुमोच परमेष्वासः षट्शरानभिलक्षितान्
verses.transliteration:
sa dhanurdhanvināṁ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya paramāhave
mumoca parameṣvāsaḥ ṣaṭśarānabhilakṣitān

translations.english: Thereupon that foremost of bowmen, and wielder of a mighty bow, taking six shafts, let them go, after aiming at them.

verses.sanskrit:
शिरस्येकेन बाणेन द्वाभ्यां बाह्वोरथार्पयत्
त्रिभिश्चन्द्रार्धवक्त्रैश्च वक्षस्यभिजघान ह
verses.transliteration:
śirasyekena bāṇena dvābhyāṁ bāhvorathārpayat
tribhiścandrārdhavaktraiśca vakṣasyabhijaghāna ha

translations.english: And with one shaft he pierced Khara's head, with two his arms, and with three arrows headed like half-moons, Rāma wounded Khara in the chest.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिभिस्त्रिवेणुं बलवान्द्वाभ्यामक्षं महाबलः
द्वादशेन तु बाणेन खरस्य सशरं धनुः
छित्त्वा वज्रनिकाशेन राघवः प्रहसन्निव
त्रयोदशेनेन्द्रसमो बिभेद समरे खरम्
verses.transliteration:
tribhistriveṇuṁ balavāndvābhyāmakṣaṁ mahābalaḥ
dvādaśena tu bāṇena kharasya saśaraṁ dhanuḥ
chittvā vajranikāśena rāghavaḥ prahasanniva
trayodaśenendrasamo bibheda samare kharam

translations.english: Then that highly energetic one, influenced by anger, assailed the Räkşasa with thirteen närācas whetted on stone and with one that exceedingly powerful one, cut the yoke of the car, with four the four steeds, with the sixth the head of Khara's charioteer, with three the stout trivenu of the car, with two the wheel, and with the twelfth, severing as if in sport Khara's bow with his hand*, with the thirteenth, resembling the thunder-bolt pierced Khara in the encounter. Another text reads: with the arrow set.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभग्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः
गदापाणिरवप्लुत्य तस्थौ भूमौ खरस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
prabhagnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ
gadāpāṇiravaplutya tasthau bhūmau kharastadā

translations.english: Then with his bow shattered, deprived of his car, (Khara) having his horses slain as well as his charioteer killed, taking a mace in his hand leaped to the ground, and stood there.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्कर्म रामस्य महारथस्य; समेत्य देवाश्च महर्षयश्च
अपूजयन्प्राञ्जलयः प्रहृष्टा;स्तदा विमानाग्रगताः समेताः
verses.transliteration:
tatkarma rāmasya mahārathasya; sametya devāśca maharṣayaśca
apūjayanprāñjalayaḥ prahṛṣṭā;stadā vimānāgragatāḥ sametāḥ

translations.english: And the celestials and Maharsis exceedingly rejoiced, assembled in the welkin in a body, and with joined hands extolled that feat of that mighty car-warrior Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
खरं तु विरथं रामो गदापाणिमवस्थितम्
मृदुपूर्वं महातेजाः परुषं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kharaṁ tu virathaṁ rāmo gadāpāṇimavasthitam
mṛdupūrvaṁ mahātejāḥ paruṣaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And to Khara deprived of his car standing with a mace in his hand, that exceedingly energetic one, Rāma, precluding his speech with mildness, spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
लोभात्पापानि कुर्वाणः कामाद्वा यो न बुध्यते
भ्रष्टः पश्यति तस्यान्तं ब्राह्मणी करकादिव
verses.transliteration:
lobhātpāpāni kurvāṇaḥ kāmādvā yo na budhyate
bhraṣṭaḥ paśyati tasyāntaṁ brāhmaṇī karakādiva

translations.english: People delightedly behold the end of him that doing an action either from covetousness or desire, dose not like a Brāhmaṇi swallowing a Karakā, see the consequence thereof.

verses.sanskrit:
वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तापसान्धर्मचारिणः
किं नु हत्वा महाभागान्फलं प्राप्स्यसि राक्षस
verses.transliteration:
vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tāpasāndharmacāriṇaḥ
kiṁ nu hatvā mahābhāgānphalaṁ prāpsyasi rākṣasa

translations.english: What, O Rākṣasa, do you gain by slaughtering exceedingly pious ascetics engaged in righteous acts, living in the forest of Dandaka?

verses.sanskrit:
न चिरं पापकर्माणः क्रूरा लोकजुगुप्सिताः
ऐश्वर्यं प्राप्य तिष्ठन्ति शीर्णमूला इव द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
na ciraṁ pāpakarmāṇaḥ krūrā lokajugupsitāḥ
aiśvaryaṁ prāpya tiṣṭhanti śīrṇamūlā iva drumāḥ

translations.english: Like to trees whose roots have been reduced, cruel persons, execrated of men, who perpetrate iniquitous acts, do not exist long.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं लभते कर्ता फलं पापस्य कर्मणः
घोरं पर्यागते काले द्रुमः पुष्पमिवार्तवम्
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ labhate kartā phalaṁ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
ghoraṁ paryāgate kāle drumaḥ puṣpamivārtavam

translations.english: As a tree puts forth blossoms in season, the doer of sinful deeds, at the hour (of repentance) inevitably reaps their fruit in the shape of dreadful anguish (of the spirit).

verses.sanskrit:
नचिरात्प्राप्यते लोके पापानां कर्मणां फलम्
सविषाणामिवान्नानां भुक्तानां क्षणदाचर
verses.transliteration:
nacirātprāpyate loke pāpānāṁ karmaṇāṁ phalam
saviṣāṇāmivānnānāṁ bhuktānāṁ kṣaṇadācara

translations.english: O ranger of night, as the effect of having taken rice mixed with poison, appears without delay, even so also people readily reap the fruit of their own acts.

verses.sanskrit:
पापमाच्चरतां घोरं लोकस्याप्रियमिच्छताम्
अहमासादितो राजा प्राणान्हन्तुं निशाचर
verses.transliteration:
pāpamāccaratāṁ ghoraṁ lokasyāpriyamicchatām
ahamāsādito rājā prāṇānhantuṁ niśācara

translations.english: O ranger of the night, it is to take the lives of the perpetrators of dreadful sins, who wish ill to men, that I the king have come.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य हि त्वां मया मुक्ताः शराः काञ्चनभूषणाः
विदार्य निपतिष्यन्ति वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः
verses.transliteration:
adya hi tvāṁ mayā muktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
vidārya nipatiṣyanti valmīkamiva pannagāḥ

translations.english: Today the gold-decked arrows discharged by ine, piercing (your body), shall enter into the carth, cleaving it, like serpents falling into an ant-hill.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वया दण्डकारण्ये भक्षिता धर्मचारिणः
तानद्य निहतः संख्ये ससैन्योऽनुगमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
ye tvayā daṇḍakāraṇye bhakṣitā dharmacāriṇaḥ
tānadya nihataḥ saṁkhye sasainyo'nugamiṣyasi

translations.english: Slain in battle, you shall in company with your army, follow those people practising piety, whom you have devoured in the Dandaka forest.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य त्वां निहतं बाणैः पश्यन्तु परमर्षयः
निरयस्थं विमानस्था ये त्वया हिंसिताः पुरा
verses.transliteration:
adya tvāṁ nihataṁ bāṇaiḥ paśyantu paramarṣayaḥ
nirayasthaṁ vimānasthā ye tvayā hiṁsitāḥ purā

translations.english: Today let those great saints, who had formerly been slain by you, stationed in the sky, behold you slain (in turn) with my arrows, and inhabiting hell.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहर त्वं यथाकामं कुरु यत्नं कुलाधम
अद्य ते पातयिष्यामि शिरस्तालफलं यथा
verses.transliteration:
prahara tvaṁ yathākāmaṁ kuru yatnaṁ kulādhama
adya te pātayiṣyāmi śirastālaphalaṁ yathā

translations.english: Do you strike as you like. And youl that are of an odious race, do you put forth your energy. Today I will bring down your head, even as a palm falls to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण क्रुद्धः संरक्तलोचनः
प्रत्युवाच ततो रामं प्रहसन्क्रोधमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa kruddhaḥ saṁraktalocanaḥ
pratyuvāca tato rāmaṁ prahasankrodhamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Khara enraged and beyond himself with passion, with eyes reddened, replied.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राकृतान्राक्षसान्हत्वा युद्धे दशरथात्मज
आत्मना कथमात्मानमप्रशस्यं प्रशंससि
verses.transliteration:
prākṛtānrākṣasānhatvā yuddhe daśarathātmaja
ātmanā kathamātmānamapraśasyaṁ praśaṁsasi

translations.english: O son of Dasaratha, why having slain inferior Rākṣasas in battle, do you praise yourself without reason?

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तो वा ये भवन्ति नरर्षभाः
कथयन्ति न ते किंचित्तेजसा स्वेन गर्विताः
verses.transliteration:
vikrāntā balavanto vā ye bhavanti nararṣabhāḥ
kathayanti na te kiṁcittejasā svena garvitāḥ

translations.english: Those foremost of men that are puissant and powerful, do not, inflated with their energy, mouth (their own consequence).

verses.sanskrit:
प्राकृतास्त्वकृतात्मानो लोके क्षत्रियपांसनाः
निरर्थकं विकत्थन्ते यथा राम विकत्थसे
verses.transliteration:
prākṛtāstvakṛtātmāno loke kṣatriyapāṁsanāḥ
nirarthakaṁ vikatthante yathā rāma vikatthase

translations.english: It is the mean-minded Kșatriyas of impure hearts that magnify themselves among men, even as you, O Rama,do.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलं व्यपदिशन्वीरः समरे कोऽभिधास्यति
मृत्युकाले हि संप्राप्ते स्वयमप्रस्तवे स्तवम्
verses.transliteration:
kulaṁ vyapadiśanvīraḥ samare ko'bhidhāsyati
mṛtyukāle hi saṁprāpte svayamaprastave stavam

translations.english: What hero, when the hour of his death has approached, publishes in the field his own lofty lineage and sings his own hymn.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा तु लघुत्वं ते कत्थनेन विदर्शितम्
सुवर्णप्रतिरूपेण तप्तेनेव कुशाग्निना
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā tu laghutvaṁ te katthanena vidarśitam
suvarṇapratirūpeṇa tapteneva kuśāgninā

translations.english: As brass wearing the semblance of gold, displays its own defect on being heated*, with a fire lit with Kusa, so you have betrayed your own lightness by this speech of yours. i.c. becomes dusky, (Ramanuja).

verses.sanskrit:
न तु मामिह तिष्ठन्तं पश्यसि त्वं गदाधरम्
धराधरमिवाकम्प्यं पर्वतं धातुभिश्चितम्
verses.transliteration:
na tu māmiha tiṣṭhantaṁ paśyasi tvaṁ gadādharam
dharādharamivākampyaṁ parvataṁ dhātubhiścitam

translations.english: You do not see me staying here mace in hand, like a moveless mountain dyed in metals, bearing mobile and immobile things.

verses.sanskrit:
पर्याप्तोऽहं गदापाणिर्हन्तुं प्राणान्रणे तव
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पाशहस्त इवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
paryāpto'haṁ gadāpāṇirhantuṁ prāṇānraṇe tava
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṁ pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ

translations.english: I can, mace in hand, deprive you and the three worlds to boot clean of your lives, like the very Destroyer with the noose in his hand.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं बह्वपि वक्तव्यं त्वयि वक्ष्यामि न त्वहम्
अस्तं गच्छेद्धि सविता युद्धविघ्रस्ततो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ bahvapi vaktavyaṁ tvayi vakṣyāmi na tvaham
astaṁ gaccheddhi savitā yuddhavighrastato bhavet

translations.english: But I will not parley much with you as much as I could wish: the sun is going to set, and our fight shall be interrupted.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि राक्षसानां हतानि ते
त्वद्विनाशात्करोम्यद्य तेषामश्रुप्रमार्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rākṣasānāṁ hatāni te
tvadvināśātkaromyadya teṣāmaśrupramārjanam

translations.english: Fourteen thousand Räksasas have been slaughtered by you. I will for their deaths wipe their tears to-day.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा परमक्रुद्धस्तां गदां परमाङ्गदाम्
खरश्चिक्षेप रामाय प्रदीप्तामशनिं यथा
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā paramakruddhastāṁ gadāṁ paramāṅgadām
kharaścikṣepa rāmāya pradīptāmaśaniṁ yathā

translations.english: Saying this Khara, highly enraged, hurled his mace+ provided with golden rings at Rāma, like to the blazing thunderbolt. Another reading is, plaited with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
खरबाहुप्रमुक्ता सा प्रदीप्ता महती गदा
भस्मवृक्षांश्च गुल्मांश्च कृत्वागात्तत्समीपतः
verses.transliteration:
kharabāhupramuktā sā pradīptā mahatī gadā
bhasmavṛkṣāṁśca gulmāṁśca kṛtvāgāttatsamīpataḥ

translations.english: Thereat, reducing to ashes trees and shrubs, that mighty flaming mace, discharged by Khara's arm, fell before Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
तामापतन्तीं ज्वलितां मृत्युपाशोपमां गदा
अन्तरिक्षगतां रामश्चिच्छेद बहुधा शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tāmāpatantīṁ jvalitāṁ mṛtyupāśopamāṁ gadā
antarikṣagatāṁ rāmaściccheda bahudhā śaraiḥ

translations.english: And Rāma severed in many fragments that mighty mace, resembling the noose of Death, as ascending the welkin, it was coming down.

verses.sanskrit:
सा विशीर्णा शरैर्भिन्ना पपात धरणीतले
गदामन्त्रौषधिबलैर्व्यालीव विनिपातिता
verses.transliteration:
sā viśīrṇā śarairbhinnā papāta dharaṇītale
gadāmantrauṣadhibalairvyālīva vinipātitā

translations.english: Thereupon, like a she-serpent brought down by force of incantations, the mace fell to the earth shattered and riven.

verses.sanskrit:
भित्त्वा तु तां गदां बाणै राघवो धर्मवत्सलः
स्मयमानः खरं वाक्यं संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
bhittvā tu tāṁ gadāṁ bāṇai rāghavo dharmavatsalaḥ
smayamānaḥ kharaṁ vākyaṁ saṁrabdhamidamabravīt

translations.english: Cutting off the mace with his shafts, Rāghava attached to righteousness with a smile said to Khara these angry words.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते बलसर्वस्वं दर्शितं राक्षसाधम
शक्तिहीनतरो मत्तो वृथा त्वमुपगर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
etatte balasarvasvaṁ darśitaṁ rākṣasādhama
śaktihīnataro matto vṛthā tvamupagarjitam

translations.english: You vile of Rākșasas, this is the utmost of your might, which you have displayed.

verses.sanskrit:
एषा बाणविनिर्भिन्ना गदा भूमितलं गता
अभिधानप्रगल्भस्य तव प्रत्ययघातिनी
verses.transliteration:
eṣā bāṇavinirbhinnā gadā bhūmitalaṁ gatā
abhidhānapragalbhasya tava pratyayaghātinī

translations.english: Rendered more nerveless at my hands, in vain do you storm. Riven by my shafts, your mace, belonging to you who are prolix in the matter of vocabulary, destroying your confidence, has sought the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्त्वयोक्तं विनष्टानामिदमश्रुप्रमार्जनम्
राक्षसानां करोमीति मिथ्या तदपि ते वचः
verses.transliteration:
yattvayoktaṁ vinaṣṭānāmidamaśrupramārjanam
rākṣasānāṁ karomīti mithyā tadapi te vacaḥ

translations.english: And what you had said, will wipe the tears of the Rākşasas that have been slain, has also proved false.

verses.sanskrit:
नीचस्य क्षुद्रशीलस्य मिथ्यावृत्तस्य रक्षसः
प्राणानपहरिष्यामि गरुत्मानमृतं यथा
verses.transliteration:
nīcasya kṣudraśīlasya mithyāvṛttasya rakṣasaḥ
prāṇānapahariṣyāmi garutmānamṛtaṁ yathā

translations.english: As Garuda stole ambrosia, will I deprive you, O Rāksasa, who are base, of a mean disposition and a false character, of your life.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य ते भिन्नकण्ठस्य फेनबुद्बुदभूषितम्
विदारितस्य मद्बाणैर्मही पास्यति शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
adya te bhinnakaṇṭhasya phenabudbudabhūṣitam
vidāritasya madbāṇairmahī pāsyati śoṇitam

translations.english: To day the earth shall drink the blood vitiated with foamy bubbles, of you, having your throat severed, and riven by my shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
पांसुरूषितसर्वाङ्गः स्रस्तन्यस्तभुजद्वयः
स्वप्स्यसे गां समाश्लिष्य दुर्लभां प्रमदामिव
verses.transliteration:
pāṁsurūṣitasarvāṅgaḥ srastanyastabhujadvayaḥ
svapsyase gāṁ samāśliṣya durlabhāṁ pramadāmiva

translations.english: Having all your body covered with dust, and your two arms lopped off, you shall, difficult to win, take your nap, embracing the earth, like a damsel difficult to win.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवृद्धनिद्रे शयिते त्वयि राक्षसपांसने
भविष्यन्त्यशरण्यानां शरण्या दण्डका इमे
verses.transliteration:
pravṛddhanidre śayite tvayi rākṣasapāṁsane
bhaviṣyantyaśaraṇyānāṁ śaraṇyā daṇḍakā ime

translations.english: On you, disgrace of Raksasas, lying down, and being fast asleep, this Dandaka shall be refuge of those that shall resort to it for shelter.

verses.sanskrit:
जनस्थाने हतस्थाने तव राक्षसमच्छरैः
निर्भया विचरिष्यन्ति सर्वतो मुनयो वने
verses.transliteration:
janasthāne hatasthāne tava rākṣasamaccharaiḥ
nirbhayā vicariṣyanti sarvato munayo vane

translations.english: O Rākşasa, in your Janasthāna, with its (Rāks asas) slain by my shafts, ascetics shall fearlessly go about in the wood.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य विप्रसरिष्यन्ति राक्षस्यो हतबान्धवाः
बाष्पार्द्रवदना दीना भयादन्यभयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
adya viprasariṣyanti rākṣasyo hatabāndhavāḥ
bāṣpārdravadanā dīnā bhayādanyabhayāvahāḥ

translations.english: Today Rākṣasas, capable of exciting fear in others, rendered forlorn and with their friends slain, shall from fear, with their faces wet with tears, fly (this place).

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य शोकरसज्ञास्ता भविष्यन्ति निशाचर
अनुरूपकुलाः पत्न्यो यासां त्वं पतिरीदृशः
verses.transliteration:
adya śokarasajñāstā bhaviṣyanti niśācara
anurūpakulāḥ patnyo yāsāṁ tvaṁ patirīdṛśaḥ

translations.english: To day your wives whose husband are you of such a nature, and who are of a like lineage (with yourself), shall experience the sentiment of sorrow, and be deprived of their all.

verses.sanskrit:
नृशंसशील क्षुद्रात्मन्नित्यं ब्राह्मणकण्टक
त्वत्कृते शङ्कितैरग्नौ मुनिभिः पात्यते हविः
verses.transliteration:
nṛśaṁsaśīla kṣudrātmannityaṁ brāhmaṇakaṇṭaka
tvatkṛte śaṅkitairagnau munibhiḥ pātyate haviḥ

translations.english: You of a cruel disposition, you of ignoble soul, you that are aye a thorn (in the side) of Brāhmanas, it is for you that ascetics, frightened and dispirited, have so long been pouring the clarified butter.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमभिसंरब्धं ब्रुवाणं राघवं रणे
खरो निर्भर्त्सयामास रोषात्खरतर स्वनः
verses.transliteration:
tamevamabhisaṁrabdhaṁ bruvāṇaṁ rāghavaṁ raṇe
kharo nirbhartsayāmāsa roṣātkharatara svanaḥ

translations.english: As Rāghava, influenced by anger, said this in the field, Khara f. wrath, with accents rendered harsher, fell to censuring (Rāma),

verses.sanskrit:
दृढं खल्ववलिप्तोऽसि भयेष्वपि च निर्भयः
वाच्यावाच्यं ततो हि त्वं मृत्युवश्यो न बुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
dṛḍhaṁ khalvavalipto'si bhayeṣvapi ca nirbhayaḥ
vācyāvācyaṁ tato hi tvaṁ mṛtyuvaśyo na budhyase

translations.english: You are wondrous proud; and you are fearless albeit fear is present to you. And come under the sway of Death, you do not understand what should be said and what left unspoken.

verses.sanskrit:
कालपाशपरिक्षिप्ता भवन्ति पुरुषा हि ये
कार्याकार्यं न जानन्ति ते निरस्तषडिन्द्रियाः
verses.transliteration:
kālapāśaparikṣiptā bhavanti puruṣā hi ye
kāryākāryaṁ na jānanti te nirastaṣaḍindriyāḥ

translations.english: Those persons that have been fast bound by the noose of death, do not in consequence of their senses having ceased to perform their functions, discern what is proper and what improper.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामं संरुध्य भृकुटिं ततः
स ददर्श महासालमविदूरे निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rāmaṁ saṁrudhya bhṛkuṭiṁ tataḥ
sa dadarśa mahāsālamavidūre niśācaraḥ

translations.english: Saying this to Rāma, that ranger of the night (Khara), pursing his brows, espied a mighty Sāla hard by. And looking about him on all sides in the field for a weapon, he uprooted it, biting his Nether lip.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समुत्क्षिप्य बाहुभ्यां विनर्दित्वा महाबलः
राममुद्दिश्य चिक्षेप हतस्त्वमिति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samutkṣipya bāhubhyāṁ vinarditvā mahābalaḥ
rāmamuddiśya cikṣepa hatastvamiti cābravīt

translations.english: And raising up the tree with his arms, and uttering a roar, that exceedingly powerful one aiming at Rāma discharged it, exclaiming, Dead you are.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं बाणौघैश्छित्त्वा रामः प्रतापवान्
रोषमाहारयत्तीव्रं निहन्तुं समरे खरम्
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ bāṇaughaiśchittvā rāmaḥ pratāpavān
roṣamāhārayattīvraṁ nihantuṁ samare kharam

translations.english: And as it descended, the puissant Rāma cut it off by means of a multitude of shafts, got into a mighty rage for the purpose of slaying Khara is battle.

verses.sanskrit:
जातस्वेदस्ततो रामो रोषाद्रक्तान्तलोचनः
निर्बिभेद सहस्रेण बाणानां समरे खरम्
verses.transliteration:
jātasvedastato rāmo roṣādraktāntalocanaḥ
nirbibheda sahasreṇa bāṇānāṁ samare kharam

translations.english: Then Rāma perspiring, with eyes reddened in wrath, pierced Khara in battle with a thousand shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बाणान्तराद्रक्तं बहु सुस्राव फेनिलम्
गिरेः प्रस्रवणस्येव तोयधारापरिस्रवः
verses.transliteration:
tasya bāṇāntarādraktaṁ bahu susrāva phenilam
gireḥ prasravaṇasyeva toyadhārāparisravaḥ

translations.english: And blood mixed with froth gushed by the sides of the shafts, like torrents flowing from fountain in a hill* stupefied in battle by the shafts shot by Rāina, and maddened by the smell of blood Khara furiously inade for Rāma. The text varies slightly in other texts.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं संरब्धं कृतास्त्रो रुधिराप्लुतम्
अपसर्पत्प्रतिपदं किंचित्त्वरितविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ saṁrabdhaṁ kṛtāstro rudhirāplutam
apasarpatpratipadaṁ kiṁcittvaritavikramaḥ

translations.english: And as he (Khara) was rushing on, bathed with blood, Rāma cquipped with arms, suddenly summoning his strength walked backward two or three paces.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पावकसंकाशं बधाय समरे शरम्
खरस्य रामो जग्राह ब्रह्मदण्डमिवापरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pāvakasaṁkāśaṁ badhāya samare śaram
kharasya rāmo jagrāha brahmadaṇḍamivāparam

translations.english: Then with the view of bringing about (Khara's end) Rāma took up in the conflict an arrow resembling fire or another weapon of Brahmã himself.

verses.sanskrit:
स तद्दत्तं मघवता सुरराजेन धीमता
संदधे च स धर्मात्मा मुमोच च खरं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
sa taddattaṁ maghavatā surarājena dhīmatā
saṁdadhe ca sa dharmātmā mumoca ca kharaṁ prati

translations.english: And that righteous one shot at Khara, that (arrow), which had been conferred on him by the intelligent Maghavān.

verses.sanskrit:
स विमुक्तो महाबाणो निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः
रामेण धनुरुद्यम्य खरस्योरसि चापतत्
verses.transliteration:
sa vimukto mahābāṇo nirghātasamaniḥsvanaḥ
rāmeṇa dhanurudyamya kharasyorasi cāpatat

translations.english: And discharged by Rāma from his bent bow, that mighty arrow with the roaring of the thunderbolt fell at Khara's breast.

verses.sanskrit:
स पपात खरो भूमौ दह्यमानः शराग्निना
रुद्रेणैव विनिर्दग्धः श्वेतारण्ये यथान्धकः
verses.transliteration:
sa papāta kharo bhūmau dahyamānaḥ śarāgninā
rudreṇaiva vinirdagdhaḥ śvetāraṇye yathāndhakaḥ

translations.english: And burning in the fire of the arrow, Khara fell down on the earth, like the giant Andakha* in the forest of Svetā, consumed by Rudra. The Asura Andhaka was slain in the forest of Svetă by Rudra. This is related in the Purāṇas. Another reading is Svetarayge yathantaka like the Destroyer in the forest of Svetā. Sva, according to the Kūrma Purāņa Uttara Khanda, in the Kalanyara hill, by a kick with his left leg. slew the Destroyer, engaged in penance's, who had come to kill the Rajarsi Svetā, who was a great votary of Siva.

verses.sanskrit:
स वृत्र इव वज्रेण फेनेन नमुचिर्यथा
बलो वेन्द्राशनिहतो निपपात हतः खरः
verses.transliteration:
sa vṛtra iva vajreṇa phenena namuciryathā
balo vendrāśanihato nipapāta hataḥ kharaḥ

translations.english: And threat Khara slain fell down like Vritra slain by the thunder-bolt, or Namuci by foam, or Bala by Indra's Ašani. Namuci was slain by a thunder-bolt laid over with foam.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राजर्षयः सर्वे संगताः परमर्षयः
सभाज्य मुदिता राममिदं वचनमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tato rājarṣayaḥ sarve saṁgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
sabhājya muditā rāmamidaṁ vacanamabruvan

translations.english: Saying this all the deities went to from where they had come. Then the Rājarşis in company with supreme saints, with Agastya (at their head), gladly paying homage to Rāma, said the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदर्थं महातेजा महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः
शरभङ्गाश्रमं पुण्यमाजगाम पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
etadarthaṁ mahātejā mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
śarabhaṅgāśramaṁ puṇyamājagāma puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: It is for this that the chastiser of Pāka, the great Indra, Purandra, had paid a visit to the sacred asylum of Sarabhanga. And the Maharşis had dextrously brought you to this place, for compassing the destruction of those foes-the wicked Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं नः कृतं कार्यं त्वया दशरथात्मज
सुखं धर्मं चरिष्यन्ति दण्डकेषु महर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ naḥ kṛtaṁ kāryaṁ tvayā daśarathātmaja
sukhaṁ dharmaṁ cariṣyanti daṇḍakeṣu maharṣayaḥ

translations.english: And it is owing to this, that, O son of Dasaratha, you have performed this mighty deed. (Now) the Maharsis will carry on their proper pious offices in the Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया
गिरिदुर्गाद्विनिष्क्रम्य संविवेशाश्रमं सुखी
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare vīro lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
giridurgādviniṣkramya saṁviveśāśramaṁ sukhī

translations.english: After this, that hero, Laksmana, accompanied with Sītā came out of the mountain cavern, and joyfully entered the asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामस्तु विजयी पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः
प्रविवेशाश्रमं वीरो लक्ष्मणेनाभिवादितः
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmastu vijayī pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
praviveśāśramaṁ vīro lakṣmaṇenābhivāditaḥ

translations.english: Then the victorious and heroic, Rāma, honoured by the Maharsis, entered the asylum, worshipped by Lakṣmaṇa.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुहन्तारं महर्षीणां सुखावहम्
बभूव हृष्टा वैदेही भर्तारं परिषस्वजे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā śatruhantāraṁ maharṣīṇāṁ sukhāvaham
babhūva hṛṣṭā vaidehī bhartāraṁ pariṣasvaje

translations.english: And seeing that destroyer of foes, and bringer of coinfort to the Maharsis, her husband, Vaidehi embraced him. And seeing the multitudes of Raksasas siain, Janaka's daughter, beholding the undeteriorating Rāma, ministered to him with supreme joy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखा दृष्ट्वा सहस्राणि चतुर्दश
हतान्येकेन रामेण रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā dṛṣṭvā sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
hatānyekena rāmeṇa rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām

translations.english: Seeing fourteen thousands of Rākşasas of dreadful deeds, together with Duşaņa, and Khara, and Trisirā, slain in battle by Rāma single-handed, that one resembling clouds, Śūrpanakhā, again fell to send up mighty sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
सा दृष्ट्वा कर्म रामस्य कृतमन्यैः सुदुष्करम्
जगाम परमौद्विग्ना लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
sā dṛṣṭvā karma rāmasya kṛtamanyaiḥ suduṣkaram
jagāma paramaudvignā laṅkāṁ rāvaṇapālitām

translations.english: And witnessing Rāma's deeds, incapable of being performed by others, she, extremely agitated, went to Lankā, ruled by Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
आसीनं सूर्यसंकाशे काञ्चने परमासने
रुक्मवेदिगतं प्राज्यं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
āsīnaṁ sūryasaṁkāśe kāñcane paramāsane
rukmavedigataṁ prājyaṁ jvalantamiva pāvakam

translations.english: And she saw the effulgent Rāvaņa in front of his palace, surrounded by his counsellors, like Vāsava surrounded by the Maruts; scated on a supreme golden seat resembling the sun, and like to a flaming fire on a golden dais kept alive by sacrificial offerings.

verses.sanskrit:
देवासुरविमर्देषु वज्राशनिकृतव्रणम्
ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
devāsuravimardeṣu vajrāśanikṛtavraṇam
airāvataviṣāṇāgrairutkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasaṁ

translations.english: Unconquerable by high-souled saints, celestials, Gandharvas and all creatures; terrible like the Destroyer with his mouth wide open; his persons containing scars* of wounds inflicted by the thunder bolt and the lightings, in the war between the gods and Asuras; his breast bearing marks of attacks made by Airāvata with the ends of his tusks. *This reminds one of Milton: of Belzebub, he says, His person Deep scars of thunder had intrenched-Par, Lost-Book I.

verses.sanskrit:
विंशद्भुजं दशग्रीवं दर्शनीयपरिच्छदम्
विशालवक्षसं वीरं राजलक्ष्मणलक्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
viṁśadbhujaṁ daśagrīvaṁ darśanīyaparicchadam
viśālavakṣasaṁ vīraṁ rājalakṣmaṇalakṣitam

translations.english: Having twenty hands, and ten heads, wearing elegant attire; broad breasted; heroic; marked with royal signs; (in hue) resembling cool lapises; embellished. in ornaments of burnished gold; having goodly hands, white teeth, and a huge face resembling a hill.

verses.sanskrit:
अक्षोभ्याणां समुद्राणां क्षोभणं क्षिप्रकारिणम्
क्षेप्तारं पर्वताग्राणां सुराणां च प्रमर्दनम्
verses.transliteration:
akṣobhyāṇāṁ samudrāṇāṁ kṣobhaṇaṁ kṣiprakāriṇam
kṣeptāraṁ parvatāgrāṇāṁ surāṇāṁ ca pramardanam

translations.english: Even him who in the war of the gods had been assailed an hundred ways with the descent of Viş ņu's discus; whose body had been cut with all the weapons of the celestials; (him). who furiously disturbs the deep incapable of being disturbed; uproots mountain summits, and tramples over gods, the destroyer of righteousness, and the violator of other's wives.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरीं भोगवतीं गत्वा पराजित्य च वासुकिम्
तक्षकस्य प्रियां भार्यां पराजित्य जहार यः
verses.transliteration:
purīṁ bhogavatīṁ gatvā parājitya ca vāsukim
takṣakasya priyāṁ bhāryāṁ parājitya jahāra yaḥ

translations.english: The employer of all celestial arms, and the disturber of sacrifics-who going to the city of Bhogavatī, and vanquishing Vāsuki, had carried off Taksa's beloved wife.

verses.sanskrit:
कैलासं पर्वतं गत्वा विजित्य नरवाहनम्
विमानं पुष्पकं तस्य कामगं वै जहार यः
verses.transliteration:
kailāsaṁ parvataṁ gatvā vijitya naravāhanam
vimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ tasya kāmagaṁ vai jahāra yaḥ

translations.english: Who, going to Kailasa, and defeating him having for his vehicle a human being, had carried of the car Puspaka coursing at every where at will;

verses.sanskrit:
वनं चैत्ररथं दिव्यं नलिनीं नन्दनं वनम्
विनाशयति यः क्रोधाद्देवोद्यानानि वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
vanaṁ caitrarathaṁ divyaṁ nalinīṁ nandanaṁ vanam
vināśayati yaḥ krodhāddevodyānāni vīryavān

translations.english: Who endued with prowess had devastated the divine Caitraratha grove, the tank (situated there) and the Nandana wood, as well as the gardens of the gods;

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रसूर्यौ महाभागावुत्तिष्ठन्तौ परंतपौ
निवारयति बाहुभ्यां यः शैलशिखरोपमः
verses.transliteration:
candrasūryau mahābhāgāvuttiṣṭhantau paraṁtapau
nivārayati bāhubhyāṁ yaḥ śailaśikharopamaḥ

translations.english: And, who, himself resembling a mountain summit, had by means of his upraised arms, obstructed the rising of these repressor of foes the exalted Sun and Moon;

verses.sanskrit:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने
पुरा स्वयम्भुवे धीरः शिरांस्युपजहार यः
verses.transliteration:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptvā mahāvane
purā svayambhuve dhīraḥ śirāṁsyupajahāra yaḥ

translations.english: Who, possessed of calmness, having formerly for ten thousand years carried on asceticism in the mighty forest, offered his own heads to the self create one;

verses.sanskrit:
देवदानवगन्धर्वपिशाचपतगोरगैः
अभयं यस्य संग्रामे मृत्युतो मानुषादृते
verses.transliteration:
devadānavagandharvapiśācapatagoragaiḥ
abhayaṁ yasya saṁgrāme mṛtyuto mānuṣādṛte

translations.english: Who in conflict fears, not death from either gods or Dānavas or Gandharvas, or Piśācas or birds or serpents, from none save human beings;

verses.sanskrit:
