मन्त्ररभितुष्टं पुण्यमध्वरेषु द्विजातिभिः
हविर्धानेषु यः सोममुपहन्ति महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
mantrarabhituṣṭaṁ puṇyamadhvareṣu dvijātibhiḥ
havirdhāneṣu yaḥ somamupahanti mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Who, possessed of prodigious strength, forcibly takes away the clarified butter sanctified with mantras from the sacrificial ground;

verses.sanskrit:
आप्तयज्ञहरं क्रूरं ब्रह्मघ्नं दुष्टचारिणम्
कर्कशं निरनुक्रोशं प्रजानामहिते रतम्
रावणं सर्वभूतानां सर्वलोकभयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
āptayajñaharaṁ krūraṁ brahmaghnaṁ duṣṭacāriṇam
karkaśaṁ niranukrośaṁ prajānāmahite ratam
rāvaṇaṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ sarvalokabhayāvaham

translations.english: The destroyer of sacrifices about to be completed; of villainous nature; the slaughterer of Brahmanas; of cruel deeds; harsh and kindles, and ever bent on doing evil to all creatures;

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसी भ्रातरं क्रूरं सा ददर्श महाबलम्
तं दिव्यवस्त्राभरणं दिव्यमाल्योपशोभितम्
राक्षसेन्द्रं महाभागं पौलस्त्य कुलनन्दनम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasī bhrātaraṁ krūraṁ sā dadarśa mahābalam
taṁ divyavastrābharaṇaṁ divyamālyopaśobhitam
rākṣasendraṁ mahābhāgaṁ paulastya kulanandanam

translations.english: And railing furiously at all creatures; the inspirer of fear in all beings. And the Räkşasas beheld her exceedingly powerful and cruel brother, wearing gorgeous apparel and ornaments, and decked in a glorious garland, seated, like the Destroyer at the time (of dissolution) ready (to destroy); the exalted chief of Rākşasas; the delight of the race of Paulastya. Stupefied with fear, the Rākşasī, approaching that destroyer of foes, Rāvana, surrounded by his counsellors, said these words.

verses.sanskrit:
तमब्रवीद्दीप्तविशाललोचनं; प्रदर्शयित्वा भयमोहमूर्छिता
सुदारुणं वाक्यमभीतचारिणी; महात्मना शूर्पणखा विरूपिता
verses.transliteration:
tamabravīddīptaviśālalocanaṁ; pradarśayitvā bhayamohamūrchitā
sudāruṇaṁ vākyamabhītacāriṇī; mahātmanā śūrpaṇakhā virūpitā

translations.english: And transported with fear and desire, Śūrpanakhā, given to fearlessly ranging every where, who had been deformed by that highsouled one, showing (her mutilation), addressed these harsh words to Rāvana of flaming and expansive eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखा दीना रावणं लोकरावणम्
अमात्यमध्ये संक्रुद्धा परुषं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā dīnā rāvaṇaṁ lokarāvaṇam
amātyamadhye saṁkruddhā paruṣaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Then the woe began Śūrpanakhā, in high wrath spoke harshly in the midst of the courtiers, to Rāvana, given to railing loudly against all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमत्तः कामभोगेषु स्वैरवृत्तो निरङ्कुशः
समुत्पन्नं भयं घोरं बोद्धव्यं नावबुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
pramattaḥ kāmabhogeṣu svairavṛtto niraṅkuśaḥ
samutpannaṁ bhayaṁ ghoraṁ boddhavyaṁ nāvabudhyase

translations.english: Intoxicated with enjoyments, acting as you will, and without any control whatever, you do not see that a dreadful disaster is impending.

verses.sanskrit:
सक्तं ग्राम्येषु भोगेषु कामवृत्तं महीपतिम्
लुब्धं न बहु मन्यन्ते श्मशानाग्निमिव प्रजाः
verses.transliteration:
saktaṁ grāmyeṣu bhogeṣu kāmavṛttaṁ mahīpatim
lubdhaṁ na bahu manyante śmaśānāgnimiva prajāḥ

translations.english: The subjects do not esteem a monarch that is given to sensual enjoyments, in intent upon satisfying his lust and is covetous like the fire in a cemetery.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयं कार्याणि यः काले नानुतिष्ठति पार्थिवः
स तु वै सह राज्येन तैश्च कार्यैर्विनश्यति
verses.transliteration:
svayaṁ kāryāṇi yaḥ kāle nānutiṣṭhati pārthivaḥ
sa tu vai saha rājyena taiśca kāryairvinaśyati

translations.english: The king that dose not act at the proper time, finds destruction along with his kingdom and acts.

verses.sanskrit:
अयुक्तचारं दुर्दर्शमस्वाधीनं नराधिपम्
वर्जयन्ति नरा दूरान्नदीपङ्कमिव द्विपाः
verses.transliteration:
ayuktacāraṁ durdarśamasvādhīnaṁ narādhipam
varjayanti narā dūrānnadīpaṅkamiva dvipāḥ

translations.english: Even as elephants shun the muddy river, do people shun from a distance, the ruler that dose not send cut spies, who show now himself (to his subjects), and who had lost his independence.

verses.sanskrit:
ये न रक्षन्ति विषयमस्वाधीना नराधिपः
ते न वृद्ध्या प्रकाशन्ते गिरयः सागरे यथा
verses.transliteration:
ye na rakṣanti viṣayamasvādhīnā narādhipaḥ
te na vṛddhyā prakāśante girayaḥ sāgare yathā

translations.english: Like to rocks in the sea, those monarchs that do not administer their dominions, that are not dependent, do not prosper.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मवद्भिर्विगृह्य त्वं देवगन्धर्वदानवैः
अयुक्तचारश्चपलः कथं राजा भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
ātmavadbhirvigṛhya tvaṁ devagandharvadānavaiḥ
ayuktacāraścapalaḥ kathaṁ rājā bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: Having incurred the hostility of the gods, the Dānavas and the Gandharvas of subdued souls and senses, how can you, who are fickle, and hast not employed spies, become the king?

verses.sanskrit:
येषां चारश्च कोशश्च नयश्च जयतां वर
अस्वाधीना नरेन्द्राणां प्राकृतैस्ते जनैः समाः
verses.transliteration:
yeṣāṁ cāraśca kośaśca nayaśca jayatāṁ vara
asvādhīnā narendrāṇāṁ prākṛtaiste janaiḥ samāḥ

translations.english: O you best of conquerors, those kings whose spies, exchequer and morality are not free, are like the common head.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्पश्यन्ति दूरस्थान्सर्वानर्थान्नराधिपाः
चारेण तस्मादुच्यन्ते राजानो दीर्घचक्षुषः
verses.transliteration:
yasmātpaśyanti dūrasthānsarvānarthānnarādhipāḥ
cāreṇa tasmāducyante rājāno dīrghacakṣuṣaḥ

translations.english: It is because kings know distant dangers through spies, therefore they are styled farsighted.

verses.sanskrit:
अयुक्तचारं मन्ये त्वां प्राकृतैः सचिवैर्वृतम्
स्वजनं च जनस्थानं हतं यो नावबुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
ayuktacāraṁ manye tvāṁ prākṛtaiḥ sacivairvṛtam
svajanaṁ ca janasthānaṁ hataṁ yo nāvabudhyase

translations.english: I believe you have no spies, and that your counsellors are common folks, since although Janasthāna with your kinsman is destroyed, yet you take it not to heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषीणामभयं दत्तं कृतक्षेमाश्च दण्डकाः
धर्षितं च जनस्थानं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣīṇāmabhayaṁ dattaṁ kṛtakṣemāśca daṇḍakāḥ
dharṣitaṁ ca janasthānaṁ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā

translations.english: Fourteen thousands of Raksasas of dreadful deeds, with Khara and Dūşana, have all been slain by Rāma single-handed; Rāma of untiring energy has inspired the saints with courage; the Dandakas have been benefited; and Janasthāna had been harassed.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं तु लुब्धः प्रमत्तश्च पराधीनश्च रावण
विषये स्वे समुत्पन्नं भयं यो नावबुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ tu lubdhaḥ pramattaśca parādhīnaśca rāvaṇa
viṣaye sve samutpannaṁ bhayaṁ yo nāvabudhyase

translations.english: But you, covetous and intoxicated and in the power of others, do not understand that a great danger is over-hanging (you).

verses.sanskrit:
तीक्ष्णमल्पप्रदातारं प्रमत्तं गर्वितं शठम्
व्यसने सर्वभूतानि नाभिधावन्ति पार्थिवम्
verses.transliteration:
tīkṣṇamalpapradātāraṁ pramattaṁ garvitaṁ śaṭham
vyasane sarvabhūtāni nābhidhāvanti pārthivam

translations.english: People do not in times of peril assist a sovereign that is wrathful, stingy, intoxicated, haughty and deceitful.

verses.sanskrit:
नानुतिष्ठति कार्याणि भयेषु न बिभेति च
क्षिप्रं राज्याच्च्युतो दीनस्तृणैस्तुल्यो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nānutiṣṭhati kāryāṇi bhayeṣu na bibheti ca
kṣipraṁ rājyāccyuto dīnastṛṇaistulyo bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Even his own kindred slay a sovereign that sets immense store by his own self, is of light worth, regards himself highly, and irascible. They do not serve him; nor do they fear when he intimidates them. Such an one is speedily dethroned; and reduced to poverty and becomes like a straw.

verses.sanskrit:
शुष्ककाष्ठैर्भवेत्कार्यं लोष्टैरपि च पांसुभिः
न तु स्थानात्परिभ्रष्टैः कार्यं स्याद्वसुधाधिपैः
verses.transliteration:
śuṣkakāṣṭhairbhavetkāryaṁ loṣṭairapi ca pāṁsubhiḥ
na tu sthānātparibhraṣṭaiḥ kāryaṁ syādvasudhādhipaiḥ

translations.english: Even dry wood may serve a purpose; or stone, or dust; but no purpose is capable of being served by a sovereign that has been cast off his place.

verses.sanskrit:
उपभुक्तं यथा वासः स्रजो वा मृदिता यथा
एवं राज्यात्परिभ्रष्टः समर्थोऽपि निरर्थकः
verses.transliteration:
upabhuktaṁ yathā vāsaḥ srajo vā mṛditā yathā
evaṁ rājyātparibhraṣṭaḥ samartho'pi nirarthakaḥ

translations.english: Like a cloth that has been worn, like a garland that has been trodden, a king that had been dethroned, although able, is of no consequence.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमत्तश्च यो राजा सर्वज्ञो विजितेन्द्रियः
कृतज्ञो धर्मशीलश्च स राजा तिष्ठते चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
apramattaśca yo rājā sarvajño vijitendriyaḥ
kṛtajño dharmaśīlaśca sa rājā tiṣṭhate ciram

translations.english: But a king that keeps his wits about him, understands everything, is of controlled senses, and grateful, and of virtuous character, endure for ever.

verses.sanskrit:
नयनाभ्यां प्रसुप्तोऽपि जागर्ति नयचक्षुषा
व्यक्तक्रोधप्रसादश्च स राजा पूज्यते जनैः
verses.transliteration:
nayanābhyāṁ prasupto'pi jāgarti nayacakṣuṣā
vyaktakrodhaprasādaśca sa rājā pūjyate janaiḥ

translations.english: That king is honoured by men; that sleeping with his eyes, is awake as respects his eye of duty, and (the effects of) whose anger and favour, are seen (by all).

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं तु रावणदुर्बुद्धिर्गुणैरेतैर्विवर्जितः
यस्य तेऽविदितश्चारै रक्षसां सुमहान्वधः
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ tu rāvaṇadurbuddhirguṇairetairvivarjitaḥ
yasya te'viditaścārai rakṣasāṁ sumahānvadhaḥ

translations.english: But, you Rāvana, who hast not by means of spies; acquainted yourself with the slaughter of Rākşasas, are of evil understanding and bereft of all these virtues.

verses.sanskrit:
परावमन्ता विषयेषु संगतो; नदेश कालप्रविभाग तत्त्ववित्
अयुक्तबुद्धिर्गुणदोषनिश्चये; विपन्नराज्यो न चिराद्विपत्स्यते
verses.transliteration:
parāvamantā viṣayeṣu saṁgato; nadeśa kālapravibhāga tattvavit
ayuktabuddhirguṇadoṣaniścaye; vipannarājyo na cirādvipatsyate

translations.english: Given to disgracing others, ignorant of the proper distribution of time and place*, and never taking care to distinguish merits and defects,: you, your kingdom being in danger, will speedily meet with disaster. The commentator, is silent here. the meaning evidently is, you do not discern the where and when of things.

verses.sanskrit:
इति स्वदोषान्परिकीर्तितांस्तया; समीक्ष्य बुद्ध्या क्षणदाचरेश्वरः
धनेन दर्पेण बलेन चान्वितो; विचिन्तयामास चिरं स रावणः
verses.transliteration:
iti svadoṣānparikīrtitāṁstayā; samīkṣya buddhyā kṣaṇadācareśvaraḥ
dhanena darpeṇa balena cānvito; vicintayāmāsa ciraṁ sa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: On his vices having been thus celebrated by her (Surpanakhā), that lord of the rangers of night, Råvaņa, musing awhile, was long plunged in thought.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखां क्रुद्धां ब्रुवतीं परुषं वचः
अमात्यमध्ये संक्रुद्धः परिपप्रच्छ रावणः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāṁ kruddhāṁ bruvatīṁ paruṣaṁ vacaḥ
amātyamadhye saṁkruddhaḥ paripapraccha rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Seeing Śūrpanakhā speak harsh words in the midst of the courtiers, Ravana, being enraged, asked her.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्च रामः कथं वीर्यः किं रूपः किं पराक्रमः
किमर्थं दण्डकारण्यं प्रविष्टश्च सुदुश्चरम्
verses.transliteration:
kaśca rāmaḥ kathaṁ vīryaḥ kiṁ rūpaḥ kiṁ parākramaḥ
kimarthaṁ daṇḍakāraṇyaṁ praviṣṭaśca suduścaram

translations.english: Who is Rāma? And what is his prowess? And what his form? And what his power? And why had he entered the forest of Dandaka, difficult to range?

verses.sanskrit:
आयुधं किं च रामस्य निहता येन राक्षसाः
खरश्च निहतं संख्ये दूषणस्त्रिशिरास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
āyudhaṁ kiṁ ca rāmasya nihatā yena rākṣasāḥ
kharaśca nihataṁ saṁkhye dūṣaṇastriśirāstathā

translations.english: And what Rāma's weapons, by means of which he had slain the Rākşasas?. And Khara has been slain in battle, and Dūşaņa and Trisirā.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्ता राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसी क्रोधमूर्छिता
ततो रामं यथान्यायमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
ityuktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā
tato rāmaṁ yathānyāyamākhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: Do you, O you of a pleasing person, tell me the truth. And who had deformed you?

verses.sanskrit:
दीर्घबाहुर्विशालाक्षश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरः
कन्दर्पसमरूपश्च रामो दशरथात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
dīrghabāhurviśālākṣaścīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraḥ
kandarpasamarūpaśca rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the lord of the Rākṣasas, the Raksasi, transported with rage, commenced to duly narrate all about Rāma. Rāma the son of Dasaratha is long-armed, of expansive eyes, clad in bark and dark deer-skin, and like Kandarpa in grace.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्रचापनिभं चापं विकृष्य कनकाङ्गदम्
दीप्तान्क्षिपति नाराचान्सर्पानिव महाविषान्
verses.transliteration:
śakracāpanibhaṁ cāpaṁ vikṛṣya kanakāṅgadam
dīptānkṣipati nārācānsarpāniva mahāviṣān

translations.english: And drawing a bow resembling that of Sakra, decked with golden rings, he discharges blazing nāracas, like to serpents of virulent poison.

verses.sanskrit:
अमर्षी दुर्जयो जेता विक्रान्तो बुद्धिमान्बली
रामस्य दक्षिणे बाहुर्नित्यं प्राणो बहिष्चरः
verses.transliteration:
amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimānbalī
rāmasya dakṣiṇe bāhurnityaṁ prāṇo bahiṣcaraḥ

translations.english: His brother is endued with mighty energy, and in merit, is of equal prowess, and he is devoted to his brother, and bear him regard; the puissant one is named Laksmana. And wrathful and invincible and victorious, and powerful, and intelligent and mighty, (he) is Rāma's right-arı-his life ranging externally.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य तु विशालाक्षी धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनी
सीता नाम वरारोहा वैदेही तनुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya tu viśālākṣī dharmapatnī yaśasvinī
sītā nāma varārohā vaidehī tanumadhyamā

translations.english: Of the lustre of burnished gold, with her finger nails reddish and projecting, and graceful, that surpassingly lovely wench is named Sītā—the slender-waisted daughter of Videha.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव देवी न गन्धर्वा न यक्षी न च किंनरी
तथारूपा मया नारी दृष्टपूर्वा महीतले
verses.transliteration:
naiva devī na gandharvā na yakṣī na ca kiṁnarī
tathārūpā mayā nārī dṛṣṭapūrvā mahītale

translations.english: And neither a goddess, nor a Gandharvi, nor a Yaksi, nor a Kinnari, had I seen before on earth, possessed of such beauty.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य सीता भवेद्भार्या यं च हृष्टा परिष्वजेत्
अतिजीवेत्स सर्वेषु लोकेष्वपि पुरंदरात्
verses.transliteration:
yasya sītā bhavedbhāryā yaṁ ca hṛṣṭā pariṣvajet
atijīvetsa sarveṣu lokeṣvapi puraṁdarāt

translations.english: He that shall have Sītā for his spouse, and who shall be warmly embraced by her, shall live longer in the world than the Lord of celestials himself.

verses.sanskrit:
सा सुशीला वपुःश्लाघ्या रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि
तवानुरूपा भार्या सा त्वं च तस्यास्तथा पतिः
verses.transliteration:
sā suśīlā vapuḥślāghyā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi
tavānurūpā bhāryā sā tvaṁ ca tasyāstathā patiḥ

translations.english: That good-natured girl, unparalleled on earth in loveliness, who can well pride herself on her person, is a worthy wife for you, and you too are a fit husband for her.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु विस्तीर्णजघनां पीनोत्तुङ्गपयोधराम्
भार्यार्थे तु तवानेतुमुद्यताहं वराननाम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu vistīrṇajaghanāṁ pīnottuṅgapayodharām
bhāryārthe tu tavānetumudyatāhaṁ varānanām

translations.english: It is to bring over for you that one of spacious hips, and a high and well-developed bust, that I had put forth my endeavours. But, O mightyarmed one I have been disfigured by the wicked Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु दृष्ट्वाद्य वैदेहीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
मन्मथस्य शराणां च त्वं विधेयो भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu dṛṣṭvādya vaidehīṁ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
manmathasya śarāṇāṁ ca tvaṁ vidheyo bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: As soon as you have seen Vaidehi having a countenance resembling the full moon, you shall be afflicted with the shafts of Cupid.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि तस्यामभिप्रायो भार्यार्थे तव जायते
शीघ्रमुद्ध्रियतां पादो जयार्थमिह दक्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
yadi tasyāmabhiprāyo bhāryārthe tava jāyate
śīghramuddhriyatāṁ pādo jayārthamiha dakṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: If it is your purpose to have her for your wife, at once stretch forth your right leg. for attaining success.

verses.sanskrit:
रोचते यदि ते वाक्यं ममैतद्राक्षसेश्वर
क्रियतां निर्विशङ्केन वचनं मम राघव
verses.transliteration:
rocate yadi te vākyaṁ mamaitadrākṣaseśvara
kriyatāṁ nirviśaṅkena vacanaṁ mama rāghava

translations.english: If, O lord of Raksasas, you relish my speech, do you then, O Ravana, without fear, do as I tell you.

verses.sanskrit:
निशम्य रामेण शरैरजिह्मगै;र्हताञ्जनस्थानगतान्निशाचरान्
खरं च बुद्ध्वा निहतं च दूषणं; त्वमद्य कृत्यं प्रतिपत्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
niśamya rāmeṇa śarairajihmagai;rhatāñjanasthānagatānniśācarān
kharaṁ ca buddhvā nihataṁ ca dūṣaṇaṁ; tvamadya kṛtyaṁ pratipattumarhasi

translations.english: Hearing that Rāma by means of straight coursing shafts, has slain the Rākşasas that had gone to Janasthāna, and seeing Khara and Düşaņa, killed, do you ascertaining your course, adopt it.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यं तच्छ्रुत्वा रोमहर्षणम्
सचिवानभ्यनुज्ञाय कार्यं बुद्ध्वा जगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyaṁ tacchrutvā romaharṣaṇam
sacivānabhyanujñāya kāryaṁ buddhvā jagāma ha

translations.english: Hearing those words of Śūrpanakhā, able to make one's hair stand on end, (Ravana) ascertaining his course after issuing his orders to this counsellors, departed.

verses.sanskrit:
इति कर्तव्यमित्येव कृत्वा निश्चयमात्मनः
स्थिरबुद्धिस्ततो रम्यां यानशालां जगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
iti kartavyamityeva kṛtvā niścayamātmanaḥ
sthirabuddhistato ramyāṁ yānaśālāṁ jagāma ha

translations.english: And proposing to himself that act, weighing its good and evil, considering his capacity or Otherwise, and (finally) determining his purpose, Rāvana with a fixed mird went to the handsome stable.

verses.sanskrit:
यानशालां ततो गत्वा प्रच्छन्नं राक्षसाधिपः
सूतं संचोदयामास रथः संयुज्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
yānaśālāṁ tato gatvā pracchannaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
sūtaṁ saṁcodayāmāsa rathaḥ saṁyujyatāmiti

translations.english: And going to the stable in disguise, the lord of the Rākṣasasas commanded the charioteer, saying, Yoke the car.:

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः क्षणेनैव सारथिर्लघुविक्रमः
रथं संयोजयामास तस्याभिमतमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ kṣaṇenaiva sārathirlaghuvikramaḥ
rathaṁ saṁyojayāmāsa tasyābhimatamuttamam

translations.english: Thus asked, the charioteer possessed of fleet vigour, in a trice, yoked an excellent car after his heart.

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनं रथमास्थाय कामगं रत्नभूषितम्
पिशाचवदनैर्युक्तं खरैः कनकभूषणैः
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanaṁ rathamāsthāya kāmagaṁ ratnabhūṣitam
piśācavadanairyuktaṁ kharaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: And ascending the car coursing at will, made of gold and garnished with spectral faces as well as arrow decked with gold, resembling a mass of clouds, the graceful ruler of the Rākşasasyounger brother to the Lord of wealth proceeded in that noiseless (vehicle), past the lord of rivers and streams.

verses.sanskrit:
दशास्यो विंशतिभुजो दर्शनीय परिच्छदः
त्रिदशारिर्मुनीन्द्रघ्नो दशशीर्ष इवाद्रिराट्
verses.transliteration:
daśāsyo viṁśatibhujo darśanīya paricchadaḥ
tridaśārirmunīndraghno daśaśīrṣa ivādrirāṭ

translations.english: And with chouris of white hair, and a white umbrella, having ten-faces, resembling (in hue) cool lapises, wearing ornaments of polished gold, possessed of ten mouths, and twenty arms, clad in elegant apparel, the foe of the celestials, and slayer of the foremost ascetics-having huge heads like to the monarch of mountains, the lord of the Rākşasas, mounted on that chariot coursing at will, appeared beautiful like as mass of clouds in the sky, with cranes, in the midst of lighting.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्याभरणमाल्याभिर्दिव्यरूपाभिरावृतम्
क्रीडा रतिविधिज्ञाभिरप्सरोभिः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
divyābharaṇamālyābhirdivyarūpābhirāvṛtam
krīḍā ratividhijñābhirapsarobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Swarming with females, divinely beautiful, delight with gorgeous ornaments and garlands, and Apsarās skilled in sport by thousands; frequented by the wives of the celestials, and honoured by graceful girls; ranged by multitudes of deities and Dänavas, feeding on ambrosia; abounding with swans, Krauncas, and frogs, echoing to (the cries of) cranes; containing stones resembling the lapis, and mild and cool by the influence of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
पाण्डुराणि विशालानि दिव्यमाल्ययुतानि च
तूर्यगीताभिजुष्टानि विमानानि समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
pāṇḍurāṇi viśālāni divyamālyayutāni ca
tūryagītābhijuṣṭāni vimānāni samantataḥ

translations.english: And as he proceeded, the younger brother of the Lord of wealth, saw on all sides spacious cars capable of coursing at will, sable, furnished with fair garlands, and resounding with trumpet notes, and Gandharvas and Apsaras.

verses.sanskrit:
समन्ताद्यस्य ताः शाखाः शतयोजनमायताः
यस्य हस्तिनमादाय महाकायं च कच्चपम्
भक्षार्थं गरुडः शाखामाजगाम महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
samantādyasya tāḥ śākhāḥ śatayojanamāyatāḥ
yasya hastinamādāya mahākāyaṁ ca kaccapam
bhakṣārthaṁ garuḍaḥ śākhāmājagāma mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And there he saw a fig tree, hued like clouds, surrounded by ascetics; its branches stretched around an hundred Yojanas, and the exceedingly powerful Garuda had ascended one of its boughs, taking an elephant and a huge tortoise, for the purpose of devouring them.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तां सहसा शाखां भारेण पतगोत्तमः
सुपर्णः पर्णबहुलां बभञ्जाथ महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tāṁ sahasā śākhāṁ bhāreṇa patagottamaḥ
suparṇaḥ parṇabahulāṁ babhañjātha mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And that best of birds, the powerful Suparņa by his weight suddenly broke a branch containing full many leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र वैखानसा माषा वालखिल्या मरीचिपाः
अजा बभूवुर्धूम्राश्च संगताः परमर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
tatra vaikhānasā māṣā vālakhilyā marīcipāḥ
ajā babhūvurdhūmrāśca saṁgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ

translations.english: And it came to pass that Vaikhānasas, Māşas, Valakhilyas, Maricipas, Ayas, and Dhumras, saints of the highest order-had assembled there.

verses.sanskrit:
एकपादेन धर्मात्मा भक्षयित्वा तदामिषम्
निषादविषयं हत्वा शाखया पतगोत्तमः
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे मोक्षयित्वा महामुनीन्
verses.transliteration:
ekapādena dharmātmā bhakṣayitvā tadāmiṣam
niṣādaviṣayaṁ hatvā śākhayā patagottamaḥ
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe mokṣayitvā mahāmunīn

translations.english: Thereat, moved by commiseration (for the ascetics), the virtuous Garuda, taking with proinptitude the broken bough measuring an hundred Yojanas as well as the elephant and the tortoise, by one leg, at length eating up the animals, and by means of the bough, exterminating the country of the Nişādas-that best of birds attained unequalled delight in consequence of having rescued the mighty ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेनैव प्रहर्षेण द्विगुणीकृतविक्रमः
अमृतानयनार्थं वै चकार मतिमान्मतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tenaiva praharṣeṇa dviguṇīkṛtavikramaḥ
amṛtānayanārthaṁ vai cakāra matimānmatim

translations.english: Thereat, attaining double energy by virtue of that delight, that intelligent one set his heart on bringing ambrosia.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोजालानि निर्मथ्य भित्त्वा रत्नगृहं वरम्
महेन्द्रभवनाद्गुप्तमाजहारामृतं ततः
verses.transliteration:
ayojālāni nirmathya bhittvā ratnagṛhaṁ varam
mahendrabhavanādguptamājahārāmṛtaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: And tearing off the iron links of the network, and bursting into the repository of gem, he carried away secreted ambrosia from the residence of the great Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
तं महर्षिगणैर्जुष्टं सुपर्णकृतलक्षणम्
नाम्ना सुभद्रं न्यग्रोधं ददर्श धनदानुजः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ maharṣigaṇairjuṣṭaṁ suparṇakṛtalakṣaṇam
nāmnā subhadraṁ nyagrodhaṁ dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ

translations.english: Kubera's younger brother beheld this fig tree, named Suparna had left his mark.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु गत्वा परं पारं समुद्रस्य नदीपतेः
ददर्शाश्रममेकान्ते पुण्ये रम्ये वनान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu gatvā paraṁ pāraṁ samudrasya nadīpateḥ
dadarśāśramamekānte puṇye ramye vanāntare

translations.english: Then repairing to the other shore of that lord of rivers, the ocean, Rāvana saw an asylum lying in the forest in a charming and sacred recess.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र कृष्णाजिनधरं जटावल्कलधारिणम्
ददर्श नियताहारं मारीचं नाम राक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
tatra kṛṣṇājinadharaṁ jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam
dadarśa niyatāhāraṁ mārīcaṁ nāma rākṣasaṁ

translations.english: And there he saw a Rākṣasa, named Mārīca, clad in a dark deer-skin, bearing a head of matted locks, subsisting on restricted fare.

verses.sanskrit:
स रावणः समागम्य विधिवत्तेन रक्षसा
ततः पश्चादिदं वाक्यमब्रवीद्वाक्यकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāvaṇaḥ samāgamya vidhivattena rakṣasā
tataḥ paścādidaṁ vākyamabravīdvākyakovidaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by Mārica, the highly energetic Ravana, versed in speech, said.

verses.sanskrit:
मारीच श्रूयतां तात वचनं मम भाषतः
आर्तोऽस्मि मम चार्तस्य भवान्हि परमा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
mārīca śrūyatāṁ tāta vacanaṁ mama bhāṣataḥ
ārto'smi mama cārtasya bhavānhi paramā gatiḥ

translations.english: O Mărîca, hearken to me, my child, as I relate (everything to you). I am distressed and in this distress of mine, you are certainly my great refuge.

verses.sanskrit:
जानीषे त्वं जनस्थानं भ्राता यत्र खरो मम
दूषणश्च महाबाहुः स्वसा शूर्पणखा च मे
verses.transliteration:
jānīṣe tvaṁ janasthānaṁ bhrātā yatra kharo mama
dūṣaṇaśca mahābāhuḥ svasā śūrpaṇakhā ca me

translations.english: You know Janasthāna, where lives my brother Khara, and the mighty-armed Dusana, and my sister, sūrpanakhă; as also that Räksasa subsisting on (human) flesh, the long armed Trisirā, and many other heroic night rangers besides, of high enthusiasm in battlesRākşasas, who had been living there at my command, troubling in the mighty forest the ascetics carrying on their pious offices.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
शूराणां लब्धलक्षाणां खरचित्तानुवर्तिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
śūrāṇāṁ labdhalakṣāṇāṁ kharacittānuvartinām

translations.english: And fourteen thousands of Rākşasas of dreadful deeds, heroic, high-spirited, Raksasas possessed of exceeding prowess; while residing in Janasthåna of late, clad in mail and equipped with various weapons, headed, by Khara, met with Rāma in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
पित्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन सभार्यः क्षीणजीवितः
स हन्ता तस्य सैन्यस्य रामः क्षत्रियपांसनः
verses.transliteration:
pitrā nirastaḥ kruddhena sabhāryaḥ kṣīṇajīvitaḥ
sa hantā tasya sainyasya rāmaḥ kṣatriyapāṁsanaḥ

translations.english: Having been expelled by his enraged sire, that disgrace of Kșatriyas, the weak Rāma, living in company with his wife has effected the destruction of this army.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया ह्यहं सहायेन पार्श्वस्थेन महाबल
भ्रातृभिश्च सुरान्युद्धे समग्रान्नाभिचिन्तये
verses.transliteration:
tvayā hyahaṁ sahāyena pārśvasthena mahābala
bhrātṛbhiśca surānyuddhe samagrānnābhicintaye

translations.english: Be you my help in it. For certain, O exceedingly strong one, if you help me at my side, if my brothers also back me, I do not think much of all the celestials. Therefore, be you my help; for, you are capable, O Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सहायो भव त्वं मे समर्थो ह्यसि राक्षस
वीर्ये युद्धे च दर्पे च न ह्यस्ति सदृशस्तव
verses.transliteration:
tatsahāyo bhava tvaṁ me samartho hyasi rākṣasa
vīrye yuddhe ca darpe ca na hyasti sadṛśastava

translations.english: In prowess in battle, and in indomitableness, there is none like you. You are a mighty hero commanding resources, and conversant with potent illusory displays.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदर्थमहं प्राप्तस्त्वत्समीपं निशाचर
शृणु तत्कर्म साहाय्ये यत्कार्यं वचनान्मम
verses.transliteration:
etadarthamahaṁ prāptastvatsamīpaṁ niśācara
śṛṇu tatkarma sāhāyye yatkāryaṁ vacanānmama

translations.english: Taking this to my heart, I have come to you, O ranger of the night. Do you listen as to the business in which by my command you are to help ime.

verses.sanskrit:
सौवर्णस्त्वं मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजतबिन्दुभिः
आश्रमे तस्य रामस्य सीतायाः प्रमुखे चर
verses.transliteration:
sauvarṇastvaṁ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ
āśrame tasya rāmasya sītāyāḥ pramukhe cara

translations.english: Becoming a golden deer, marked with silver spots, do you range about in Rāma's asylum in presence of Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां तु निःसंशयं सीता दृष्ट्वा तु मृगरूपिणम्
गृह्यतामिति भर्तारं लक्ष्मणं चाभिधास्यति
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ tu niḥsaṁśayaṁ sītā dṛṣṭvā tu mṛgarūpiṇam
gṛhyatāmiti bhartāraṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ cābhidhāsyati

translations.english: Seeing you helpless, in the shape of a deer, Sītā will say to her lord and Lakşmaņa also, Do you catch it.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तयोरपाये तु शून्ये सीतां यथासुखम्
निराबाधो हरिष्यामि राहुश्चन्द्रप्रभामिव
verses.transliteration:
tatastayorapāye tu śūnye sītāṁ yathāsukham
nirābādho hariṣyāmi rāhuścandraprabhāmiva

translations.english: When they shall have departed, I shall carry off from the empty asylum, Sītã without let, like Rāhu depriving the Moon of his splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पश्चात्सुखं रामे भार्याहरणकर्शिते
विस्रब्धं प्रहरिष्यामि कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paścātsukhaṁ rāme bhāryāharaṇakarśite
visrabdhaṁ prahariṣyāmi kṛtārthenāntarātmanā

translations.english: Then when Rāma shall be sore afflicted because of the carrying off of his wife, I shall easily, crowning my soul with success, safely bear away Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रामकथां श्रुत्वा मारीचस्य महात्मनः
शुष्कं समभवद्वक्त्रं परित्रस्तो बभूव च
verses.transliteration:
tasya rāmakathāṁ śrutvā mārīcasya mahātmanaḥ
śuṣkaṁ samabhavadvaktraṁ paritrasto babhūva ca

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words, the face of the highsouled Mārīca became blank and he was seized with apprehension.

verses.sanskrit:
स रावणं त्रस्तविषण्णचेता; महावने रामपराक्रमज्ञः
कृताञ्जलिस्तत्त्वमुवाच वाक्यं; हितं च तस्मै हितमात्मनश्च
verses.transliteration:
sa rāvaṇaṁ trastaviṣaṇṇacetā; mahāvane rāmaparākramajñaḥ
kṛtāñjalistattvamuvāca vākyaṁ; hitaṁ ca tasmai hitamātmanaśca

translations.english: And alarmed because of Rāvana, with his mind depressed, Mārīca who well knew Rāma's prowess in the forest, with joined hands in agitation spoke words lending to his own as well as Rāvana's welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो मारीचो राक्षसेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā rākṣasendrasya vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
pratyuvāca mahāprājño mārīco rākṣaseśvaram

translations.english: Hearing the words of that sovereign of the Rākşasas, the highly energetic Mārica, skilled in speech, answered the Raksasa chief.

verses.sanskrit:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः
अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः
verses.transliteration:
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṁ priyavādinaḥ
apriyasya ca pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ

translations.english: O king, the speaker of soft words is common, but the speaker and the listener of unwelcome though beneficial words are rarities.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं बुध्यसे रामं महावीर्यं गुणोन्नतम्
अयुक्तचारश्चपलो महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ budhyase rāmaṁ mahāvīryaṁ guṇonnatam
ayuktacāraścapalo mahendravaruṇopamam

translations.english: Volatile, and employing no spies, you surely do not understand the exceedingly powerful Rāma towering high in virtues, and resembling the illustrious Indra or Varuņa himself.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि स्वस्ति भवेत्तात सर्वेषां भुवि रक्षसाम्
अपि रामो न संक्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
api svasti bhavettāta sarveṣāṁ bhuvi rakṣasām
api rāmo na saṁkruddhaḥ kuryāllokamarākṣasaṁ

translations.english: I shall be well, me child, if Rāma fired with rage, do not render all the world bereft of Rākşasas;

verses.sanskrit:
अपि ते जीवितान्ताय नोत्पन्ना जनकात्मजा
अपि सीता निमित्तं च न भवेद्व्यसनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
api te jīvitāntāya notpannā janakātmajā
api sītā nimittaṁ ca na bhavedvyasanaṁ mahat

translations.english: If Janaka's daughter has not sprung to compass your destruction, if a dreadful disaster do not befall you because of Sītā,

verses.sanskrit:
अपि त्वामीश्वरं प्राप्य कामवृत्तं निरङ्कुशम्
न विनश्येत्पुरी लङ्का त्वया सह सराक्षसा
verses.transliteration:
api tvāmīśvaraṁ prāpya kāmavṛttaṁ niraṅkuśam
na vinaśyetpurī laṅkā tvayā saha sarākṣasā

translations.english: And if having obtained for her lord you that are wilful and wicked, the city of Lankā with you and the Rākṣasas do not meet with utter extermination.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वद्विधः कामवृत्तो हि दुःशीलः पापमन्त्रितः
आत्मानं स्वजनं राष्ट्रं स राजा हन्ति दुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
tvadvidhaḥ kāmavṛtto hi duḥśīlaḥ pāpamantritaḥ
ātmānaṁ svajanaṁ rāṣṭraṁ sa rājā hanti durmatiḥ

translations.english: The sovereign who is wicked, whimsical and of evil intent like you, bring about his own destruction as well as that of his kingdom and relatives.

verses.sanskrit:
न च पित्रा परित्यक्तो नामर्यादः कथंचन
न लुब्धो न च दुःशीलो न च क्षत्रियपांसनः
verses.transliteration:
na ca pitrā parityakto nāmaryādaḥ kathaṁcana
na lubdho na ca duḥśīlo na ca kṣatriyapāṁsanaḥ

translations.english: Rāma, the enhancer of Kausalyā's delight had not been abandoned by his father, nor is he devoid of propriety of conduct; he is not avaricious, wicked nor the destroyer of Kaşatriya race.

verses.sanskrit:
न च धर्मगुणैर्हीनैः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः
न च तीक्ष्णो हि भूतानां सर्वेषां च हिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
na ca dharmaguṇairhīnaiḥ kausalyānandavardhanaḥ
na ca tīkṣṇo hi bhūtānāṁ sarveṣāṁ ca hite rataḥ

translations.english: He does not lack religious merits or accomplishments, nor is he of a harsh temperament and intent on causing misery to creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं पितुर्दशरथस्य च
हित्वा राज्यं च भोगांश्च प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmārthaṁ piturdaśarathasya ca
hitvā rājyaṁ ca bhogāṁśca praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: Finding his truthful sire imposed on by Kaikeyi he has sojourned to woods. For compassing the welfare of his father Dasaratha and Kaikeyi he has entered the forest of Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
न रामः कर्कशस्तात नाविद्वान्नाजितेन्द्रियः
अनृतं न श्रुतं चैव नैव त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
na rāmaḥ karkaśastāta nāvidvānnājitendriyaḥ
anṛtaṁ na śrutaṁ caiva naiva tvaṁ vaktumarhasi

translations.english: Rāma, O my child is not harsh or foolish; nor has he not control over his senses. Far from speaking untruth he does not know false stories even.

verses.sanskrit:
रामो विग्रहवान्धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानामिव वासवः
verses.transliteration:
rāmo vigrahavāndharmaḥ sādhuḥ satyaparākramaḥ
rājā sarvasya lokasya devānāmiva vāsavaḥ

translations.english: It did not behove you therefore to use such improper language towards him. he is an incarnation of virtue, pious and truthful, and lord of all men as Vāsava of all celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं त्वं तस्य वैदेहीं रक्षितां स्वेन तेजसा
इच्छसि प्रसभं हर्तुं प्रभामिव विवस्वतः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ tvaṁ tasya vaidehīṁ rakṣitāṁ svena tejasā
icchasi prasabhaṁ hartuṁ prabhāmiva vivasvataḥ

translations.english: How does you then wish to carry away by force his Vaidehī, protected by virtue of her own chastity, like to the rays of Sun?

verses.sanskrit:
शरार्चिषमनाधृष्यं चापखड्गेन्धनं रणे
रामाग्निं सहसा दीप्तं न प्रवेष्टुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
śarārciṣamanādhṛṣyaṁ cāpakhaḍgendhanaṁ raṇe
rāmāgniṁ sahasā dīptaṁ na praveṣṭuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: It did not behove you to enter that fire of Rāma who has arrows for rays and bow and scimitar for fuel. It did not behove you,

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं सुखं च संत्यज्य जीवितं चेष्टमात्मनः
नात्यासादयितुं तात रामान्तकमिहार्हसि
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ sukhaṁ ca saṁtyajya jīvitaṁ ceṣṭamātmanaḥ
nātyāsādayituṁ tāta rāmāntakamihārhasi

translations.english: O Rāvana, to approach Räma renouncing your kingdom, happiness and love of life, who is like to death itself and has bow for his widened and flaming mouth, and arrows for his rays and who is irrepressible, of mighty prowess, holding bows and arrows and repulsing the forces of the enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमेयं हि तत्तेजो यस्य सा जनकात्मजा
न त्वं समर्थस्तां हर्तुं रामचापाश्रयां वने
verses.transliteration:
aprameyaṁ hi tattejo yasya sā janakātmajā
na tvaṁ samarthastāṁ hartuṁ rāmacāpāśrayāṁ vane

translations.english: Incomparable is his power; daughter of Janaka is his wife and lives in the forest confiding in the mighty strength of his bow; you shall not be able to carry her away.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणेभ्योऽपि प्रियतरा भार्या नित्यमनुव्रता
दीप्तस्येव हुताशस्य शिखा सीता सुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
prāṇebhyo'pi priyatarā bhāryā nityamanuvratā
dīptasyeva hutāśasya śikhā sītā sumadhyamā

translations.english: She is the beloved wife of that best of men having a leonine chest—and he holds his wife dearer than his life and is ever attached to her.

verses.sanskrit:
किमुद्यमं व्यर्थमिमं कृत्वा ते राक्षसाधिप
दृष्टश्चेत्त्वं रणे तेन तदन्तं तव जीवितम्
जीवितं च सुखं चैव राज्यं चैव सुदुर्लभम्
verses.transliteration:
kimudyamaṁ vyarthamimaṁ kṛtvā te rākṣasādhipa
dṛṣṭaścettvaṁ raṇe tena tadantaṁ tava jīvitam
jīvitaṁ ca sukhaṁ caiva rājyaṁ caiva sudurlabham

translations.english: Of what avail is this vain attempt O Rākşasa chief? No sooner Rāma shall see you in the battle you shall meet with your end.

verses.sanskrit:
दोषाणां च गुणानां च संप्रधार्य बलाबलम्
आत्मनश्च बलं ज्ञात्वा राघवस्य च तत्त्वतः
हितं हि तव निश्चित्य क्षमं त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
doṣāṇāṁ ca guṇānāṁ ca saṁpradhārya balābalam
ātmanaśca balaṁ jñātvā rāghavasya ca tattvataḥ
hitaṁ hi tava niścitya kṣamaṁ tvaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: Hard it is to attain life, happiness and kingdom, so it behoved you to act properly, after consulting with your ministers headed by Vibhīşaņa, judging Rāma's merits and demerits and ascertaining his and your own strength and as well as your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु मन्ये तव न क्षमं रणे; समागमं कोसलराजसूनुना
इदं हि भूयः शृणु वाक्यमुत्तमं; क्षमं च युक्तं च निशाचराधिप
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu manye tava na kṣamaṁ raṇe; samāgamaṁ kosalarājasūnunā
idaṁ hi bhūyaḥ śṛṇu vākyamuttamaṁ; kṣamaṁ ca yuktaṁ ca niśācarādhipa

translations.english: Methinks your approaching conflict with the son of the Kosala chief forebodes no good to you; hear again therefore O prince of the night rangers, words sensible and lending to your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
कदाचिदप्यहं वीर्यात्पर्यटन्पृथिवीमिमाम्
बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्पर्वतोपमः
verses.transliteration:
kadācidapyahaṁ vīryātparyaṭanpṛthivīmimām
balaṁ nāgasahasrasya dhārayanparvatopamaḥ

translations.english: Once on a time I was engaged in travelling all over the earth. I had in my body, resembling a huge mountain, the strength of a thousand Nagas.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलजीमूतसंकाशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः
भयं लोकस्य जनयन्किरीटी परिघायुधः
व्यचरं दण्डकारण्यमृषिमांसानि भक्षयन्
verses.transliteration:
nīlajīmūtasaṁkāśastaptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ
bhayaṁ lokasya janayankirīṭī parighāyudhaḥ
vyacaraṁ daṇḍakāraṇyamṛṣimāṁsāni bhakṣayan

translations.english: I had parigha in my hands, crown on my head and golden ear-rings on my ears and my body was of a dark blue colour like that of a cloud. Causing fright to the people I used to wander through the forest of Dandaka and live upon the flesh of the Rsis.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रोऽथ धर्मात्मा मद्वित्रस्तो महामुनिः
स्वयं गत्वा दशरथं नरेन्द्रमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
viśvāmitro'tha dharmātmā madvitrasto mahāmuniḥ
svayaṁ gatvā daśarathaṁ narendramidamabravīt

translations.english: The pious ascetic Viśvāmitra being afraid of me went in person to the king Dasaratha and said,

verses.sanskrit:
अयं रक्षतु मां रामः पर्वकाले समाहितः
मारीचान्मे भयं घोरं समुत्पन्नं नरेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ rakṣatu māṁ rāmaḥ parvakāle samāhitaḥ
mārīcānme bhayaṁ ghoraṁ samutpannaṁ nareśvara

translations.english: When I shall remain absorbed in meditation on the occasion of Parva, let Rāma protect me O king, Truly am I afraid of this Mārīca.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्तो धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्तदा
प्रत्युवाच महाभागं विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamukto dharmātmā rājā daśarathastadā
pratyuvāca mahābhāgaṁ viśvāmitraṁ mahāmunim

translations.english: Being thus addressed by the ascetic the virtuous-souled king Dasaratha replied.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊन षोडश वर्षोऽयमकृतास्त्रश्च राघवः
कामं तु मम यत्सैन्यं मया सह गमिष्यति
बधिष्यामि मुनिश्रेष्ठ शत्रुं तव यथेप्सितम्
verses.transliteration:
ūna ṣoḍaśa varṣo'yamakṛtāstraśca rāghavaḥ
kāmaṁ tu mama yatsainyaṁ mayā saha gamiṣyati
badhiṣyāmi muniśreṣṭha śatruṁ tava yathepsitam

translations.english: Rāghava is still under twelve years of age and had not been well disciplined in military arts. But I have soldiers enough, and if permitted by you, O you best of ascetics, I shall with my fourfold forces kill your enemies, the rangers of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स मुनिस्तमादाय नृपात्मजम्
जगाम परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रः स्वमाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā sa munistamādāya nṛpātmajam
jagāma paramaprīto viśvāmitraḥ svamāśramam

translations.english: Saying this the ascetic Viśvāmitra being pleased went to his asylum along with Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तदा दण्डकारण्ये यज्ञमुद्दिश्य दीक्षितम्
बभूवावस्थितो रामश्चित्रं विस्फारयन्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tadā daṇḍakāraṇye yajñamuddiśya dīkṣitam
babhūvāvasthito rāmaścitraṁ visphārayandhanuḥ

translations.english: After-words having been initiated for the sacrifice in the forest of Dandaka Rāma having unstrung his mighty bow came to the ascetic to protect the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
अजातव्यञ्जनः श्रीमान्बालः श्यामः शुभेक्षणः
एकवस्त्रधरो धन्वी शिखी कनकमालया
verses.transliteration:
ajātavyañjanaḥ śrīmānbālaḥ śyāmaḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ
ekavastradharo dhanvī śikhī kanakamālayā

translations.english: He had a gold chain round his neck, a crest on his head and a bow in his hands; he had a pair of beautiful eyes, and only one piece of cloth; his countenance was of green hue and exquisite beauty and even then moustaches or other signs of manhood did not appear on his face.

verses.sanskrit:
शोभयन्दण्डकारण्यं दीप्तेन स्वेन तेजसा
अदृश्यत तदा रामो बालचन्द्र इवोदितः
verses.transliteration:
śobhayandaṇḍakāraṇyaṁ dīptena svena tejasā
adṛśyata tadā rāmo bālacandra ivoditaḥ

translations.english: Beautifying the entire forest of Dandaka with his own splendour Rāma appeared like the newly risen moon.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं मेघसंकाशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः
बली दत्तवरो दर्पादाजगाम तदाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ meghasaṁkāśastaptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ
balī dattavaro darpādājagāma tadāśramam

translations.english: Thereupon I resembling a cloud and having golden ear locks entered the asylum being proud of my power on account of the boons offered to me by Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन दृष्टः प्रविष्टोऽहं सहसैवोद्यतायुधः
मां तु दृष्ट्वा धनुः सज्यमसंभ्रान्तश्चकार ह
verses.transliteration:
tena dṛṣṭaḥ praviṣṭo'haṁ sahasaivodyatāyudhaḥ
māṁ tu dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥ sajyamasaṁbhrāntaścakāra ha

translations.english: Seeing me enter he took up his dart and attached string to his bow with proper care.

verses.sanskrit:
अवजानन्नहं मोहाद्बालोऽयमिति राघवम्
विश्वामित्रस्य तां वेदिमध्यधावं कृतत्वरः
verses.transliteration:
avajānannahaṁ mohādbālo'yamiti rāghavam
viśvāmitrasya tāṁ vedimadhyadhāvaṁ kṛtatvaraḥ

translations.english: Being under the influence of sheer foolishness I passed by him as a child and darted towards the sacrificial alter of Viśvāmitra.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन मुक्तस्ततो बाणः शितः शत्रुनिबर्हणः
तेनाहं ताडितः क्षिप्तः समुद्रे शतयोजने
verses.transliteration:
tena muktastato bāṇaḥ śitaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
tenāhaṁ tāḍitaḥ kṣiptaḥ samudre śatayojane

translations.english: Thereupon he wounded me with a sharpened sword capable of doing away with the enemies and threw me away into the ocean situated at a distance of hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य शरवेगेन निरस्तो भ्रान्तचेतनः
पातितोऽहं तदा तेन गम्भीरे सागराम्भसि
प्राप्य संज्ञां चिरात्तात लङ्कां प्रति गतः पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya śaravegena nirasto bhrāntacetanaḥ
pātito'haṁ tadā tena gambhīre sāgarāmbhasi
prāpya saṁjñāṁ cirāttāta laṅkāṁ prati gataḥ purīm

translations.english: He had no mind of killing me then and for this he saved my life. I was thrown however into the deep ocean being hindered by the velocity of his arrows and having lost my consciousness. Regaining my sense after a long while I returned to the city of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमस्मि तदा मुक्तः सहायास्ते निपातिताः
अकृतास्त्रेण रामेण बालेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
evamasmi tadā muktaḥ sahāyāste nipātitāḥ
akṛtāstreṇa rāmeṇa bālenākliṣṭakarmaṇā

translations.english: Myself saved thus, my followers however all killed by Rāma of unwearied activity though a mere child and a novice in the are of warfare.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं यदि रामेण विग्रहम्
करिष्यस्यापदं घोरां क्षिप्रं प्राप्य नशिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tanmayā vāryamāṇastvaṁ yadi rāmeṇa vigraham
kariṣyasyāpadaṁ ghorāṁ kṣipraṁ prāpya naśiṣyasi

translations.english: It is for this that I do prevent you; you shall be overwhelmed with calamities and meet with destruction if do you engage yourself in battle with him. In vain shall you bring about the affliction of the mirthful and sportive Rākşasas ever witnessing social festivities.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्म्यप्रासादसंबाधां नानारत्नविभूषिताम्
द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं पुरीं लङ्कां विनष्टां मैथिलीकृते
verses.transliteration:
harmyaprāsādasaṁbādhāṁ nānāratnavibhūṣitām
drakṣyasi tvaṁ purīṁ laṅkāṁ vinaṣṭāṁ maithilīkṛte

translations.english: And in vain shall you for Sītā compass the destruction of the city of Lankā, adorned with diverse jewels and filled with golden edifices.

verses.sanskrit:
अकुर्वन्तोऽपि पापानि शुचयः पापसंश्रयात्
परपापैर्विनश्यन्ति मत्स्या नागह्रदे यथा
verses.transliteration:
akurvanto'pi pāpāni śucayaḥ pāpasaṁśrayāt
parapāpairvinaśyanti matsyā nāgahrade yathā

translations.english: Pious men living with a vicious man, 'meet with destruction for his sins, though they themselves do not commit any misdeed, like to fish (devoured by Garuda) living in a lake where snakes dwell.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्यचन्दनदिग्धाङ्गान्दिव्याभरणभूषितान्
द्रक्ष्यस्यभिहतान्भूमौ तव दोषात्तु राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
divyacandanadigdhāṅgāndivyābharaṇabhūṣitān
drakṣyasyabhihatānbhūmau tava doṣāttu rākṣasān

translations.english: Thus shall you witness that for your own folly the rangers of the night, adorned with celestial ornaments and having their body pasted with sandal, have been killed and brought down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
हृतदारान्सदारांश्च दशविद्रवतो दिशः
हतशेषानशरणान्द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं निशाचरान्
verses.transliteration:
hṛtadārānsadārāṁśca daśavidravato diśaḥ
hataśeṣānaśaraṇāndrakṣyasi tvaṁ niśācarān

translations.english: And they deprived of shelter have fled away to different directions, some with their wives and some alone, having their wives carried away (by the enemies).

verses.sanskrit:
शरजालपरिक्षिप्तामग्निज्वालासमावृताम्
प्रदग्धभवनां लङ्कां द्रक्ष्यसि त्वमसंशयम्
verses.transliteration:
śarajālaparikṣiptāmagnijvālāsamāvṛtām
pradagdhabhavanāṁ laṅkāṁ drakṣyasi tvamasaṁśayam

translations.english: You shall further observe that all edifices of Lankā being enveloped with arrows and flaming fire have been burnt down to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमदानां सहस्राणि तव राजन्परिग्रहः
भव स्वदारनिरतः स्वकुलं रक्षराक्षस
verses.transliteration:
pramadānāṁ sahasrāṇi tava rājanparigrahaḥ
bhava svadāranirataḥ svakulaṁ rakṣarākṣasa

translations.english: There is no greater sin on earth than carrying away another's wife. There are thousand ladies in your seraglio O king. Being attached to your wives do you preserve the race of the Rākşasas, your own line, your wished for life, kingdom, wealth and dignity.

verses.sanskrit:
मानं वृद्धिं च राज्यं च जीवितं चेष्टमात्मनः
यदीच्छसि चिरं भोक्तुं मा कृथा राम विप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
mānaṁ vṛddhiṁ ca rājyaṁ ca jīvitaṁ ceṣṭamātmanaḥ
yadīcchasi ciraṁ bhoktuṁ mā kṛthā rāma vipriyam

translations.english: Do not bring about Rāma's mischief if do you wish to live happily with your wives and friends.

verses.sanskrit:
निवार्यमाणः सुहृदा मया भृशं; प्रसह्य सीतां यदि धर्षयिष्यसि
गमिष्यसि क्षीणबलः सबान्धवो; यमक्षयं रामशरात्तजीवितः
verses.transliteration:
nivāryamāṇaḥ suhṛdā mayā bhṛśaṁ; prasahya sītāṁ yadi dharṣayiṣyasi
gamiṣyasi kṣīṇabalaḥ sabāndhavo; yamakṣayaṁ rāmaśarāttajīvitaḥ

translations.english: I am your friend and do ask you again and again to desist (from your evil intention); if do you encroach upon Sītā surely shall you along with your kinsmen go to the abode of Yama being enfeebled by the arrows of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमस्मि तदा मुक्तः कथंचित्तेन संयुगे
इदानीमपि यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणुष्व यदुत्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
evamasmi tadā muktaḥ kathaṁcittena saṁyuge
idānīmapi yadvṛttaṁ tacchṛṇuṣva yaduttaram

translations.english: I Was however somehow saved by Rāma in that conflict. Listen what happened afterwards.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाभ्यामहं द्वाभ्यामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः
सहितो मृगरूपाभ्यां प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasābhyāmahaṁ dvābhyāmanirviṇṇastathā kṛtaḥ
sahito mṛgarūpābhyāṁ praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: I was not humbled even by the danger of my life. Once again I entered the forest of Dandaka accompanied by two Rākşasas assuming the shape of deer.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निहोत्रेषु तीर्थेषु चैत्यवृक्षेषु रावण
अत्यन्तघोरो व्यचरंस्तापसांस्तान्प्रधर्षयन्
verses.transliteration:
agnihotreṣu tīrtheṣu caityavṛkṣeṣu rāvaṇa
atyantaghoro vyacaraṁstāpasāṁstānpradharṣayan

translations.english: I had a flaming tongue, huge teeth, sharpened horns and lived on the flesh of ascetics. Assuming such a terrible appearance I began to traverse with great vehemence the Tīrtha, Agnihotri and the place of worship; eating the flesh and drinking the blood of the ascetics after killing them I began to hinder all religious services.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिमांसाशनः क्रूरस्त्रासयन्वनगोचरान्
तदा रुधिरमत्तोऽहं व्यचरं दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣimāṁsāśanaḥ krūrastrāsayanvanagocarān
tadā rudhiramatto'haṁ vyacaraṁ daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: I had a most ugly figure and was maddened with drinking blood, and all the animals of the forest were exceedingly frightened at me.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेहीं च महाभागां लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्
तापसं नियताहारं सर्वभूतहिते रतम्
verses.transliteration:
vaidehīṁ ca mahābhāgāṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahāratham
tāpasaṁ niyatāhāraṁ sarvabhūtahite ratam

translations.english: While I was thus traversing the forest of Dandaka throwing obstacles in the way of religious services I saw the pious ascetic Răma living on a restricted fare, the honoured Sītā and the mighty Lakşmaņa, taking recourse to asceticism, moderate in eating and ever engaged in the welfare of created beings.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्यधावं सुसंक्रुद्धस्तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो मृगाकृतिः
जिघांसुरकृतप्रज्ञस्तं प्रहारमनुस्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
abhyadhāvaṁ susaṁkruddhastīkṣṇaśṛṅgo mṛgākṛtiḥ
jighāṁsurakṛtaprajñastaṁ prahāramanusmaran

translations.english: Remembering his former enmity and aggrandisement, I, being extremely wrathful, in my deer shape and with my sharpened horns, darted towards him with a view to kill him, considering through my ignorance the effulgent Rāma as none other but an ascetic living in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
ते बाणा वज्रसंकाशाः सुघोरा रक्तभोजनाः
आजग्मुः सहिताः सर्वे त्रयः संनतपर्वणः
verses.transliteration:
te bāṇā vajrasaṁkāśāḥ sughorā raktabhojanāḥ
ājagmuḥ sahitāḥ sarve trayaḥ saṁnataparvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then stringing his huge bow he darted three sharpened arrows at me. Those three terrible arrows with bent knots resembling thunderbolts, killing enemies and drinking blood and having the motion of Garuda and air, coalescing with each other came before us.

verses.sanskrit:
पराक्रमज्ञो रामस्य शठो दृष्टभयः पुरा
समुत्क्रान्तस्ततो मुक्तस्तावुभौ राक्षसौ हतौ
verses.transliteration:
parākramajño rāmasya śaṭho dṛṣṭabhayaḥ purā
samutkrāntastato muktastāvubhau rākṣasau hatau

translations.english: Wicked as I am, I was fully aware of his prowess having been frightened by him on a former occasion, and so I saved myself by escaping, but those two Raksasas were killed.

verses.sanskrit:
शरेण मुक्तो रामस्य कथंचित्प्राप्य जीवितम्
इह प्रव्राजितो युक्तस्तापसोऽहं समाहितः
verses.transliteration:
śareṇa mukto rāmasya kathaṁcitprāpya jīvitam
iha pravrājito yuktastāpaso'haṁ samāhitaḥ

translations.english: O Rāvana, any how saved from the arrows of Rāma and having got my life back I have resorted to the life of an ascetic and have been carrying on asceticism here being absorbed in Yoga.

verses.sanskrit:
वृक्षे वृक्षे हि पश्यामि चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरम्
गृहीतधनुषं रामं पाशहस्तमिवान्तकम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛkṣe vṛkṣe hi paśyāmi cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaram
gṛhītadhanuṣaṁ rāmaṁ pāśahastamivāntakam

translations.english: From that very day I see Rāma wearing bark and deerskin even in the very trees before me like to Death with the noose in his hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि रामसहस्राणि भीतः पश्यामि रावण
रामभूतमिदं सर्वमरण्यं प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
api rāmasahasrāṇi bhītaḥ paśyāmi rāvaṇa
rāmabhūtamidaṁ sarvamaraṇyaṁ pratibhāti me

translations.english: Terrified as I am I always see thousands of Rāma around me. Me seems the entire forest is inhabited by Rāma only.

verses.sanskrit:
राममेव हि पश्यामि रहिते राक्षसेश्वर
दृष्ट्वा स्वप्नगतं राममुद्भ्रमामि विचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
rāmameva hi paśyāmi rahite rākṣaseśvara
dṛṣṭvā svapnagataṁ rāmamudbhramāmi vicetanaḥ

translations.english: O king of Räksasas, I see Rāma even in the quarter where there is no Rāma. Seeing him in my dreams even I look around like one awaken.

verses.sanskrit:
रकारादीनि नामानि रामत्रस्तस्य रावण
रत्नानि च रथाश्चैव त्रासं संजनयन्ति मे
verses.transliteration:
rakārādīni nāmāni rāmatrastasya rāvaṇa
ratnāni ca rathāścaiva trāsaṁ saṁjanayanti me

translations.english: O Rāvana what more shall I speak to you, I am so much afraid of Rāma that such words as Ratna (jewel), Ratha (chariot) which begin with the letter Ra administer consternation to me.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तस्य प्रभावज्ञो न युद्धं तेन ते क्षमम्
रणे रामेण युध्यस्व क्षमां वा कुरु राक्षस
न ते रामकथा कार्या यदि मां द्रष्टुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tasya prabhāvajño na yuddhaṁ tena te kṣamam
raṇe rāmeṇa yudhyasva kṣamāṁ vā kuru rākṣasa
na te rāmakathā kāryā yadi māṁ draṣṭumicchasi

translations.english: O Rāvana, whether do you fight with Rāma or not, do not mention him to me if do you wish to see me.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं वचो बन्धुहितार्थिना मया; यथोच्यमानं यदि नाभिपत्स्यसे
सबान्धवस्त्यक्ष्यसि जीवितं रणे; हतोऽद्य रामेण शरैरजिह्मगैः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ vaco bandhuhitārthinā mayā; yathocyamānaṁ yadi nābhipatsyase
sabāndhavastyakṣyasi jīvitaṁ raṇe; hato'dya rāmeṇa śarairajihmagaiḥ

translations.english: You are my friend; it is for this and for your welfare that I speak this truth to you. If do you not follow my words, yourself with all your kinsmen, shall be slain in battle by Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
मारीचेन तु तद्वाक्यं क्षमं युक्तं च रावणः
उक्तो न प्रतिजग्राह मर्तुकाम इवौषधम्
verses.transliteration:
mārīcena tu tadvākyaṁ kṣamaṁ yuktaṁ ca rāvaṇaḥ
ukto na pratijagrāha martukāma ivauṣadham

translations.english: As a person desirous of meeting with his end dose not take medicine, Ravana, the king of night-rangers paid no heed to the appropriate and sound words of Márica skilled in speech, foreboding good to him.

verses.sanskrit:
तं पथ्यहितवक्तारं मारीचं राक्षसाधिपः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यमयुक्तं कालचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ pathyahitavaktāraṁ mārīcaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyamayuktaṁ kālacoditaḥ

translations.english: Moreover he addressed him with the following harsh words.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्किलैतदयुक्तार्थं मारीच मयि कथ्यते
वाक्यं निष्फलमत्यर्थं बीजमुप्तमिवोषरे
verses.transliteration:
yatkilaitadayuktārthaṁ mārīca mayi kathyate
vākyaṁ niṣphalamatyarthaṁ bījamuptamivoṣare

translations.english: O, Marica, what you have spoken to me, shall bear no fruit like to seeds sown into a desertland.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वद्वाक्यैर्न तु मां शक्यं भेत्तुं रामस्य संयुगे
पापशीलस्य मूर्खस्य मानुषस्य विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
tvadvākyairna tu māṁ śakyaṁ bhettuṁ rāmasya saṁyuge
pāpaśīlasya mūrkhasya mānuṣasya viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: I shall not be frightened thereby to fight with that foolish Rāma—a human being of vicious deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्यक्त्वा सुहृदो राज्यं मातरं पितरं तथा
स्त्रीवाक्यं प्राकृतं श्रुत्वा वनमेकपदे गतः
verses.transliteration:
yastyaktvā suhṛdo rājyaṁ mātaraṁ pitaraṁ tathā
strīvākyaṁ prākṛtaṁ śrutvā vanamekapade gataḥ

translations.english: Surely shall I before you take away from that Rāma the destroyer of Khara his favourite wife, at whose words he has sojourned into woods renouncing his father mother, kingdom and friends.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं मे निश्चिता बुद्धिर्हृदि मारीच वर्तते
न व्यावर्तयितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ me niścitā buddhirhṛdi mārīca vartate
na vyāvartayituṁ śakyā sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: I have made this firm resolution in my mind O, Marica; even Indra, with the celestials and Asuras shall not be able to shake it.

verses.sanskrit:
दोषं गुणं वा संपृष्टस्त्वमेवं वक्तुमर्हसि
अपायं वाप्युपायं वा कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चये
verses.transliteration:
doṣaṁ guṇaṁ vā saṁpṛṣṭastvamevaṁ vaktumarhasi
apāyaṁ vāpyupāyaṁ vā kāryasyāsya viniścaye

translations.english: It would have been proper for you to give vent to these expressions had I but asked you for advice to ascertain my duty, the propriety or impropriety of my action its way or losses,

verses.sanskrit:
संपृष्टेन तु वक्तव्यं सचिवेन विपश्चिता
उद्यताञ्जलिना राज्ञो य इच्छेद्भूतिमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpṛṣṭena tu vaktavyaṁ sacivena vipaścitā
udyatāñjalinā rājño ya icchedbhūtimātmanaḥ

translations.english: A wise counsellor who wishes prosperity to himself should always communicate to his master his desire with joined hands whenever asked to do so.

verses.sanskrit:
वाक्यमप्रतिकूलं तु मृदुपूर्वं शुभं हितम्
उपचारेण युक्तं च वक्तव्यो वसुधाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
vākyamapratikūlaṁ tu mṛdupūrvaṁ śubhaṁ hitam
upacāreṇa yuktaṁ ca vaktavyo vasudhādhipaḥ

translations.english: It is always proper to speak before monarchs such pleasant and favourable words as are intended for the welfare of the master and are sanctioned by the royal etiquette.

verses.sanskrit:
सावमर्दं तु यद्वाक्यं मारीच हितमुच्यते
नाभिनन्दति तद्राजा मानार्हो मानवर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
sāvamardaṁ tu yadvākyaṁ mārīca hitamucyate
nābhinandati tadrājā mānārho mānavarjitam

translations.english: A respectable king dose not receive with good grace friendly words even when they are expressed disre.pectfully.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चरूपाणि राजानो धारयन्त्यमितौजसः
अग्नेरिन्द्रस्य सोमस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च
औष्ण्यं तथा विक्रमं च सौम्यं दण्डं प्रसन्नताम्
verses.transliteration:
pañcarūpāṇi rājāno dhārayantyamitaujasaḥ
agnerindrasya somasya yamasya varuṇasya ca
auṣṇyaṁ tathā vikramaṁ ca saumyaṁ daṇḍaṁ prasannatām

translations.english: Sovereigns of superb prowess assume the semblance of five deities–Agni, Indra, Moon, Yama, and Varuna. Powerful kings, O Ranger of the night, assume haughtiness, power, a placid look and contentment and administer punishment to the wicked.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्यागतं मां दौरात्म्यात्परुषं वदसीदृशम्
गुणदोषौ न पृच्छामि क्षमं चात्मनि राक्षस
अस्मिंस्तु स भवान्कृत्ये साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
abhyāgataṁ māṁ daurātmyātparuṣaṁ vadasīdṛśam
guṇadoṣau na pṛcchāmi kṣamaṁ cātmani rākṣasa
asmiṁstu sa bhavānkṛtye sāhāyyaṁ kartumarhati

translations.english: They are to be adored and honoured therefore on all occasions. You are ignorant of kingly morality and fully absorbed in illusion. It is for this that you do out of your wickedness of heart address me your guest with these harsh words. I do not ask you, O, Raksasa about the propriety (of my conduct) or about my welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
सौवर्णस्त्वं मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजतबिन्दुभिः
प्रलोभयित्वा वैदेहीं यथेष्टं गन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
sauvarṇastvaṁ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ
pralobhayitvā vaidehīṁ yatheṣṭaṁ gantumarhasi

translations.english: Listen what you shall have to do at my request in my aid; assuming the shape of a deer having golden skin painted with silvery drops do you proceed to the asylum of Rāma, and ranging at large before Vaidehī do you after captivating her take your wished-for way.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां तु मायामृगं दृष्ट्वा काञ्चनं जातविस्मया
आनयैनमिति क्षिप्रं रामं वक्ष्यति मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ tu māyāmṛgaṁ dṛṣṭvā kāñcanaṁ jātavismayā
ānayainamiti kṣipraṁ rāmaṁ vakṣyati maithilī

translations.english: Vaidehi, being struck with wonder seeing you a golden deer capable of illusions, shall request Rāma to get you soon for her.

verses.sanskrit:
अपक्रान्ते च काकुत्स्थे लक्ष्मणे च यथासुखम्
आनयिष्यामि वैदेहीं सहस्राक्षः शचीमिव
verses.transliteration:
apakrānte ca kākutsthe lakṣmaṇe ca yathāsukham
ānayiṣyāmi vaidehīṁ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīmiva

translations.english: When both Rāma and Laksmana shall go elsewhere in this way, I shall to my felicity carry away Vaidehī like to the thousand-eyed deity carrying away Sací.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं कृत्वा त्विदं कार्यं यथेष्टं गच्छ राक्षस
राज्यस्यार्धं प्रदास्यामि मारीच तव सुव्रत
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ kṛtvā tvidaṁ kāryaṁ yatheṣṭaṁ gaccha rākṣasa
rājyasyārdhaṁ pradāsyāmi mārīca tava suvrata

translations.english: O Rākşasa, do you go wherever you like after doing this. I shall confer on you, O Mārīca, half of my kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छ सौम्य शिवं मार्गं कार्यस्यास्य विवृद्धये
प्राप्य सीतामयुद्धेन वञ्चयित्वा तु राघवम्
लङ्कां प्रति गमिष्यामि कृतकार्यः सह त्वया
verses.transliteration:
gaccha saumya śivaṁ mārgaṁ kāryasyāsya vivṛddhaye
prāpya sītāmayuddhena vañcayitvā tu rāghavam
laṅkāṁ prati gamiṣyāmi kṛtakāryaḥ saha tvayā

translations.english: Acquiring Sītā without any conflict, after imposing upon Rāma I shall return to Lankā successful along with you.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्कार्यमवश्यं मे बलादपि करिष्यसि
राज्ञो हि प्रतिकूलस्थो न जातु सुखमेधते
verses.transliteration:
etatkāryamavaśyaṁ me balādapi kariṣyasi
rājño hi pratikūlastho na jātu sukhamedhate

translations.english: I shall kill you, O Mārīca, if do you not obey my behest. I shall compel you to do this. No body can attain to prosperity and happiness, acting against his sovereign's will.

verses.sanskrit:
आसाद्य तं जीवितसंशयस्ते; मृत्युर्ध्रुवो ह्यद्य मया विरुध्य
एतद्यथावत्परिगृह्य बुद्ध्या; यदत्र पथ्यं कुरु तत्तथा त्वम्
verses.transliteration:
āsādya taṁ jīvitasaṁśayaste; mṛtyurdhruvo hyadya mayā virudhya
etadyathāvatparigṛhya buddhyā; yadatra pathyaṁ kuru tattathā tvam

translations.english: Truly shall you risk your life if you approaches Rāma, but you shall meet with sure destruction if do you act against my will. Consider about it, and do what you think proper.

verses.sanskrit:
आज्ञप्तो राजवद्वाक्यं प्रतिकूलं निशाचरः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं मारीचो राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
ājñapto rājavadvākyaṁ pratikūlaṁ niśācaraḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ mārīco rākṣasādhipam

translations.english: Being thus commended by Rāvana like a king to act against his will Mārica fearlessly addressed the lord of the Rākṣasas with the following bold words.

verses.sanskrit:
केनायमुपदिष्टस्ते विनाशः पापकर्मणा
सपुत्रस्य सराष्ट्रस्य सामात्यस्य निशाचर
verses.transliteration:
kenāyamupadiṣṭaste vināśaḥ pāpakarmaṇā
saputrasya sarāṣṭrasya sāmātyasya niśācara

translations.english: What person of impious deeds has advised you ( ranger of the night thus in order to exterminate you with your kingdom, counsellors and children?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्त्वया सुखिना राजन्नाभिनन्दति पापकृत्
केनेदमुपदिष्टं ते मृत्युद्वारमुपायतः
verses.transliteration:
kastvayā sukhinā rājannābhinandati pāpakṛt
kenedamupadiṣṭaṁ te mṛtyudvāramupāyataḥ

translations.english: Who of a vicious heart, O King, dose not feel himself happy at your welfare? Who has pointed out to you the way of your death under the cover of your means?

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रवस्तव सुव्यक्तं हीनवीर्या निशाचर
इच्छन्ति त्वां विनश्यन्तमुपरुद्धं बलीयसा
verses.transliteration:
śatravastava suvyaktaṁ hīnavīryā niśācara
icchanti tvāṁ vinaśyantamuparuddhaṁ balīyasā

translations.english: O Ranger of night surely do your weak enemies wish to bring about your destruction by making you enter into a conflict with a powerful man.

verses.sanskrit:
केनेदमुपदिष्टं ते क्षुद्रेणाहितवादिना
यस्त्वामिच्छति नश्यन्तं स्वकृतेन निशाचर
verses.transliteration:
kenedamupadiṣṭaṁ te kṣudreṇāhitavādinā
yastvāmicchati naśyantaṁ svakṛtena niśācara

translations.english: What little-minded man of evil intent has counselled you thus? O Ranger of night, really do they desire that you do bring destruction upon yourself by your own actions.

verses.sanskrit:
वध्याः खलु न हन्यन्ते सचिवास्तव रावण
ये त्वामुत्पथमारूढं न निगृह्णन्ति सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
vadhyāḥ khalu na hanyante sacivāstava rāvaṇa
ye tvāmutpathamārūḍhaṁ na nigṛhṇanti sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: You do not exterminate your counsellors O Rāvana, albeit they are worthy of being destroyed. For they do not prevent these entirely from your evil course.

verses.sanskrit:
अमात्यैः कामवृत्तो हि राजा कापथमाश्रितः
निग्राह्यः सर्वथा सद्भिर्न निग्राह्यो निगृह्यसे
verses.transliteration:
amātyaiḥ kāmavṛtto hi rājā kāpathamāśritaḥ
nigrāhyaḥ sarvathā sadbhirna nigrāhyo nigṛhyase

translations.english: Wise counsellors do always restrain a king who wends a vicious track being guided by his impulses and passions; but about you they are quite unmindful, though you should by every means be brought under restraint.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च यशश्च जयतां वर
स्वामिप्रसादात्सचिवाः प्राप्नुवन्ति निशाचर
verses.transliteration:
dharmamarthaṁ ca kāmaṁ ca yaśaśca jayatāṁ vara
svāmiprasādātsacivāḥ prāpnuvanti niśācara

translations.english: O you the best of conquerors, O you the ranger of high, ministers by the grace of their sovereign attain virtue, wealth, desires and fame.

verses.sanskrit:
विपर्यये तु तत्सर्वं व्यर्थं भवति रावण
व्यसनं स्वामिवैगुण्यात्प्राप्नुवन्तीतरे जनाः
verses.transliteration:
viparyaye tu tatsarvaṁ vyarthaṁ bhavati rāvaṇa
vyasanaṁ svāmivaiguṇyātprāpnuvantītare janāḥ

translations.english: But those objects are never attained O Rāvana when they are not in good odour with their sovereign; moreover the subjects meet with dangers when he is devoid of all qualities.

verses.sanskrit:
राजमूलो हि धर्मश्च जयश्च जयतां वर
तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु रक्षितव्यो नराधिपः
verses.transliteration:
rājamūlo hi dharmaśca jayaśca jayatāṁ vara
tasmātsarvāsvavasthāsu rakṣitavyo narādhipaḥ

translations.english: O you the best of conquerors, the king is the root of virtue and fame to the subjects; he should therefore be always protected by them.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं पालयितुं शक्यं न तीक्ष्णेन निशाचर
न चापि प्रतिकूलेन नाविनीतेन राक्षस
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ pālayituṁ śakyaṁ na tīkṣṇena niśācara
na cāpi pratikūlena nāvinītena rākṣasa

translations.english: O ranger of night, proud kings of cruel temperament, acting against the subjects can never administer their kingdoms.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तीक्ष्णमन्त्राः सचिवा भज्यन्ते सह तेन वै
विषमेषु रथाः शीघ्रं मन्दसारथयो यथा
verses.transliteration:
ye tīkṣṇamantrāḥ sacivā bhajyante saha tena vai
viṣameṣu rathāḥ śīghraṁ mandasārathayo yathā

translations.english: So do the ministers of cruel counsel meet with their end like to a chariot driven into a wild track by an unskilled charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
बहवः साधवो लोके युक्तधर्ममनुष्ठिताः
परेषामपराधेन विनष्टाः सपरिच्छदाः
verses.transliteration:
bahavaḥ sādhavo loke yuktadharmamanuṣṭhitāḥ
pareṣāmaparādhena vinaṣṭāḥ saparicchadāḥ

translations.english: Many persons pious and devoted to asceticism on this earth have met with destruction for another's misdeeds.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वामिना प्रतिकूलेन प्रजास्तीक्ष्णेन रावण
रक्ष्यमाणा न वर्धन्ते मेषा गोमायुना यथा
verses.transliteration:
svāminā pratikūlena prajāstīkṣṇena rāvaṇa
rakṣyamāṇā na vardhante meṣā gomāyunā yathā

translations.english: Verily the subjects, O Ravana, can never expect to prosper under the regime of hotnatured sovereigns acting against their subjects like to deer under the protection of a jackal.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं विनशिष्यन्ति सर्वे रावण राक्षसाः
येषां त्वं कर्कशो राजा दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ vinaśiṣyanti sarve rāvaṇa rākṣasāḥ
yeṣāṁ tvaṁ karkaśo rājā durbuddhirajitendriyaḥ

translations.english: O Rāvana, surely shall all the Räkşasas meet with death, who have such a stupid, harsh and lustful person like you for their king.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं काकतालीयं घोरमासादितं त्वया
अत्र किं शोभनं यत्त्वं ससैन्यो विनशिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ kākatālīyaṁ ghoramāsāditaṁ tvayā
atra kiṁ śobhanaṁ yattvaṁ sasainyo vinaśiṣyasi

translations.english: I shall not be the least sorry if I do meet with a sudden accident—what I do deplore most is that you shall meet in no time with destruction along with your soldiery.

verses.sanskrit:
मां निहत्य तु रामोऽसौ नचिरात्त्वां वधिष्यति
अनेन कृतकृत्योऽस्मि म्रिये यदरिणा हतः
verses.transliteration:
māṁ nihatya tu rāmo'sau nacirāttvāṁ vadhiṣyati
anena kṛtakṛtyo'smi mriye yadariṇā hataḥ

translations.english: Compassing my end Rāma shall exterminate you in no time and blessed I shall be being killed by an enemy in the conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शनादेव रामस्य हतं मामुपधारय
आत्मानं च हतं विद्धि हृत्वा सीतां सबान्धवम्
verses.transliteration:
darśanādeva rāmasya hataṁ māmupadhāraya
ātmānaṁ ca hataṁ viddhi hṛtvā sītāṁ sabāndhavam

translations.english: Surely do you know that no sooner shall I see Rāma I shall be done away with; you shall carrying away Sītā meet with your end along with your kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit:
आनयिष्यसि चेत्सीतामाश्रमात्सहितो मया
नैव त्वमसि नैवाहं नैव लङ्का न राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
ānayiṣyasi cetsītāmāśramātsahito mayā
naiva tvamasi naivāhaṁ naiva laṅkā na rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: And if do you bring Şītā with me from the asylum, none shall be saved, me, yourself, the city of Lankā and the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
निवार्यमाणस्तु मया हितैषिणा; न मृष्यसे वाक्यमिदं निशाचर
परेतकल्पा हि गतायुषो नरा; हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्
verses.transliteration:
nivāryamāṇastu mayā hitaiṣiṇā; na mṛṣyase vākyamidaṁ niśācara
paretakalpā hi gatāyuṣo narā; hitaṁ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhirīritam

translations.english: You do not relish my words O ranger of the night though prevented by me, who wishes you welfare; those men who range on the verge of death, well-nigh finishing the term of their existence do not receive with good grace the counsels of friends.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु परुषं मारीचो रावणं ततः
गच्छावेत्यब्रवीद्दीनो भयाद्रात्रिंचरप्रभोः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu paruṣaṁ mārīco rāvaṇaṁ tataḥ
gacchāvetyabravīddīno bhayādrātriṁcaraprabhoḥ

translations.english: Speaking these harsh words to Rāvana, Mārīca being afraid of him said, We shall both go.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टश्चाहं पुनस्तेन शरचापासिधारिणा
मद्वधोद्यतशस्त्रेण विनष्टं जीवितं च मे
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭaścāhaṁ punastena śaracāpāsidhāriṇā
madvadhodyataśastreṇa vinaṣṭaṁ jīvitaṁ ca me

translations.english: Surely shall I be deprived of my life b, (Rāma) taking up his scimitar and having a bow and arrows in his hands, if I go before hiin again.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तु कर्तुं मया शक्यमेवं त्वयि दुरात्मनि
एष गच्छाम्यहं तात स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु निशाचर
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tu kartuṁ mayā śakyamevaṁ tvayi durātmani
eṣa gacchāmyahaṁ tāta svasti te'stu niśācara

translations.english: You are vicious-souled, what can I do for you? be you crowned with success O ranger of the night, I shall go.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टस्त्वभवत्तेन वचनेन स राक्षसः
परिष्वज्य सुसंश्लिष्टमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭastvabhavattena vacanena sa rākṣasaḥ
pariṣvajya susaṁśliṣṭamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: The Lord of Rākşasas being pleased with Mārīca's words embraced him warmly and said,

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छौण्डीर्ययुक्तं ते मच्छन्दादिव भाषितम्
इदानीमसि मारीचः पूर्वमन्यो निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
etacchauṇḍīryayuktaṁ te macchandādiva bhāṣitam
idānīmasi mārīcaḥ pūrvamanyo niśācaraḥ

translations.english: This is worthy of your heroism that you have addressed yourself to act after my desire. You were another Raksasa before and have now become true Mārīca.

verses.sanskrit:
आरुह्यतामयं शीघ्रं खगो रत्नविभूषितः
मया सह रथो युक्तः पिशाचवदनैः खरैः
verses.transliteration:
āruhyatāmayaṁ śīghraṁ khago ratnavibhūṣitaḥ
mayā saha ratho yuktaḥ piśācavadanaiḥ kharaiḥ

translations.english: Do you now with me ascend this chariot coursing in the air, crested with jewels and driven by asses having faces of a demon.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रावणमारीचौ विमानमिव तं रथम्
आरुह्य ययतुः शीघ्रं तस्मादाश्रममण्डलात्
verses.transliteration:
tato rāvaṇamārīcau vimānamiva taṁ ratham
āruhya yayatuḥ śīghraṁ tasmādāśramamaṇḍalāt

translations.english: Thereupon Tārakā's son assented to Rāvana's words, and both of them ascending the chariot like to a heavenly car set out for the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव तत्र पश्यन्तौ पत्तनानि वनानि च
गिरींश्च सरितः सर्वा राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva tatra paśyantau pattanāni vanāni ca
girīṁśca saritaḥ sarvā rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca

translations.english: And beholding diverse towns, forests, mountains, rivers, kingdoms and cities they reached the forest of Dandaka and the asylum of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अवतीर्य रथात्तस्मात्ततः काञ्चनभूषणात्
हस्ते गृहीत्वा मारीचं रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
avatīrya rathāttasmāttataḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāt
haste gṛhītvā mārīcaṁ rāvaṇo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And descending now from the golden car the lord of Rākşasas together with Mārīca beheld Răma's asylum. Taking him (Mārīca) by the hand Ravana spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्रामाश्रमपदं दृश्यते कदलीवृतम्
क्रियतां तत्सखे शीघ्रं यदर्थं वयमागताः
verses.transliteration:
etadrāmāśramapadaṁ dṛśyate kadalīvṛtam
kriyatāṁ tatsakhe śīghraṁ yadarthaṁ vayamāgatāḥ

translations.english: There stands the asylum of Rāma surrounded by palm trees. Do you do that for which we have come here.

verses.sanskrit:
स रावणवचः श्रुत्वा मारीचो राक्षसस्तदा
मृगो भूत्वाश्रमद्वारि रामस्य विचचार ह
verses.transliteration:
sa rāvaṇavacaḥ śrutvā mārīco rākṣasastadā
mṛgo bhūtvāśramadvāri rāmasya vicacāra ha

translations.english: Hearing the words of Rāvaņa, the Rāksasa Mārīca assuming the wonderful shape of a (golden) deer began to range at large before Rama's hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रलोभनार्थं वैदेह्या नानाधातुविचित्रितम्
विचरन्गच्छते सम्यक्शाद्वलानि समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
pralobhanārthaṁ vaidehyā nānādhātuvicitritam
vicarangacchate samyakśādvalāni samantataḥ

translations.english: And in no time the Rākşasa assumed the shape of a beautiful deer. To tempt Vaidehī that ranger of the night, assuming a beautiful countenance painted with diverse metals, illumining the beautiful forest and Rāma's asylum with its beauty, and ranging at large on the green field and living on grass, began to

verses.sanskrit:
रूप्यबिन्दुशतैश्चित्रो भूत्वा च प्रियदर्शनः
विटपीनां किसलयान्भङ्क्त्वादन्विचचार ह
verses.transliteration:
rūpyabinduśataiścitro bhūtvā ca priyadarśanaḥ
viṭapīnāṁ kisalayānbhaṅktvādanvicacāra ha

translations.english: That one of lively presence having its body painted with hundreds of silver drops and living on twigs of trees began to range in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
कदलीगृहकं गत्वा कर्णिकारानितस्ततः
समाश्रयन्मन्दगतिः सीतासंदर्शनं तदा
verses.transliteration:
kadalīgṛhakaṁ gatvā karṇikārānitastataḥ
samāśrayanmandagatiḥ sītāsaṁdarśanaṁ tadā

translations.english: Sometimes walking into the plantain house, sometimes walking around the forest of Karņikā, sometimes coming within the compass of Sītā's vision, that best of deer having its back painted with gold began to range slowly around the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
पुनर्गत्वा निवृत्तश्च विचचार मृगोत्तमः
गत्वा मुहूर्तं त्वरया पुनः प्रतिनिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
punargatvā nivṛttaśca vicacāra mṛgottamaḥ
gatvā muhūrtaṁ tvarayā punaḥ pratinivartate

translations.english: It began to walk at pleasure near Rāma's asylum. Sometimes going, sometimes stopping, at one time running very swiftly and receding the next moment, that best of deer began to range at large.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रीडंश्च पुनर्भूमौ पुनरेव निषीदति
आश्रमद्वारमागम्य मृगयूथानि गच्छति
verses.transliteration:
vikrīḍaṁśca punarbhūmau punareva niṣīdati
āśramadvāramāgamya mṛgayūthāni gacchati

translations.english: Sometimes playing around, sometimes lying on earth and sometimes following the deer-herd having come within the thresh hold of the asylum and then followed again by them that Rākṣasa assuming the form of a deer came back to see Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
परिभ्रमति चित्राणि मण्डलानि विनिष्पतन्
समुद्वीक्ष्य च सर्वे तं मृगा येऽन्ये वनेचराः
verses.transliteration:
paribhramati citrāṇi maṇḍalāni viniṣpatan
samudvīkṣya ca sarve taṁ mṛgā ye'nye vanecarāḥ

translations.english: He then began to range at large in the beautiful forest (extending far and wide). Seeing him other forest-deer came (by hiin) and smelling him fled away into different quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
उपगम्य समाघ्राय विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश
राक्षसः सोऽपि तान्वन्यान्मृगान्मृगवधे रतः
verses.transliteration:
upagamya samāghrāya vidravanti diśo daśa
rākṣasaḥ so'pi tānvanyānmṛgānmṛgavadhe rataḥ

translations.english: That Raksasa, though expert in killing deer, did not eat them up, though touching, in order to hide his real self.

verses.sanskrit:
कुसुमापचये व्यग्रा पादपानत्यवर्तत
कर्णिकारानशोकांश्च चूटांश्च मदिरेक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
kusumāpacaye vyagrā pādapānatyavartata
karṇikārānaśokāṁśca cūṭāṁśca madirekṣaṇā

translations.english: In the meantime Vaidehī, of auspicious looks whose eyes inebriate like wine, being engaged in plucking flowers, was going sometimes to the Karņikā grove and sometimes to the mango grove.

verses.sanskrit:
कुसुमान्यपचिन्वन्ती चचार रुचिरानना
अनर्हारण्यवासस्य सा तं रत्नमयं मृगम्
मुक्तामणिविचित्राङ्गं ददर्श परमाङ्गना
verses.transliteration:
kusumānyapacinvantī cacāra rucirānanā
anarhāraṇyavāsasya sā taṁ ratnamayaṁ mṛgam
muktāmaṇivicitrāṅgaṁ dadarśa paramāṅganā

translations.english: That best of women, ever inured to living in the forest and possessed of a graceful countenance, walking and plucking flowers, saw that jewelled deer, having its body diversified with pearls and diamonds,

verses.sanskrit:
तं वै रुचिरदण्तौष्ठं रूप्यधातुतनूरुहम्
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयना सस्नेहं समुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vai ruciradaṇtauṣṭhaṁ rūpyadhātutanūruham
vismayotphullanayanā sasnehaṁ samudaikṣata

translations.english: It had beautiful teeth and lips and had its down resembling silver. She began to behold with affection and with her eyes expanded with surprise.

verses.sanskrit:
स च तां रामदयितां पश्यन्मायामयो मृगः
विचचार ततस्तत्र दीपयन्निव तद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa ca tāṁ rāmadayitāṁ paśyanmāyāmayo mṛgaḥ
vicacāra tatastatra dīpayanniva tadvanam

translations.english: That illusive deer seeing Rāma's wife began to inove around as if lighting up that forest (with the fire of its beauty).

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं दृष्ट्वा तं नानारत्नमयं मृगम्
विस्मयं परमं सीता जगाम जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭapūrvaṁ dṛṣṭvā taṁ nānāratnamayaṁ mṛgam
vismayaṁ paramaṁ sītā jagāma janakātmajā

translations.english: Beholding that deer ornamented with diverse jewels, and the like of which she had never seen before, the daughter of Janaka was struck with immense wonder. Beholding that deer ornamented with diverse jewels, and the like of which she had never seen before, the daughter of Janaka was struck with immense wonder.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तं संप्रेक्ष्य सुश्रोणी कुसुमानि विचिन्वती
हेमराजतवर्णाभ्यां पार्श्वाभ्यामुपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
sā taṁ saṁprekṣya suśroṇī kusumāni vicinvatī
