hemarājatavarṇābhyāṁ pārśvābhyāmupaśobhitam

translations.english: Beholding that deer with its sides painted with gold and silver, while collecting flowers, Sītā, having blameless limbs and beautiful hips and having the colour of her body like that of pure gold became immensely pleased and called aloud her husband and Lakşmaņa with scimitars in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तयाहूतौ नरव्याघ्रौ वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ
वीक्षमाणौ तु तं देशं तदा ददृशतुर्मृगम्
verses.transliteration:
tayāhūtau naravyāghrau vaidehyā rāmalakṣmaṇau
vīkṣamāṇau tu taṁ deśaṁ tadā dadṛśaturmṛgam

translations.english: Having called (her husband) again and again in this strain she continued beholding that deer. Being thus called by the daughter of the king of Videha those two best of men Rāma and Laks maņa, casting their looks around beheld that deer.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्कमानस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत्
तमेवैनमहं मन्ये मारीचं राक्षसं मृगम्
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkamānastu taṁ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇo rāmamabravīt
tamevainamahaṁ manye mārīcaṁ rākṣasaṁ mṛgam

translations.english: Seeing him Lakşmana, struck with fear, said Me-thinks, this deer is the Raksasa Marica.

verses.sanskrit:
चरन्तो मृगयां हृष्टाः पापेनोपाधिना वने
अनेन निहता राम राजानः कामरूपिणा
verses.transliteration:
caranto mṛgayāṁ hṛṣṭāḥ pāpenopādhinā vane
anena nihatā rāma rājānaḥ kāmarūpiṇā

translations.english: This vicious Mārīca, O Rāma, assuming the shape of a deer oftentimes kills at pleasure the kings who come here a-hunting.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य मायाविदो मायामृगरूपमिदं कृतम्
भानुमत्पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसंनिभम्
verses.transliteration:
asya māyāvido māyāmṛgarūpamidaṁ kṛtam
bhānumatpuruṣavyāghra gandharvapurasaṁnibham

translations.english: He is cognizant of illusions, by virtue of which he has assumed this shape, O best of men; its countenance is perfectly fine like the abode of Gandharvas and resplendent like the Sun; there is no such jewelled deer on earth. O Rāghava, O Lord of earth, there is no doubt that this is nothing but illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं काकुत्स्थं प्रतिवार्य शुचिस्मिता
उवाच सीता संहृष्टा छद्मना हृतचेतना
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ kākutsthaṁ prativārya śucismitā
uvāca sītā saṁhṛṣṭā chadmanā hṛtacetanā

translations.english: When Lakşınaņa spoke thus Sītā with a pure smile being under the influence of enchantment contradicted him, and being pleased said

verses.sanskrit:
आर्यपुत्राभिरामोऽसौ मृगो हरति मे मनः
आनयैनं महाबाहो क्रीडार्थं नो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
āryaputrābhirāmo'sau mṛgo harati me manaḥ
ānayainaṁ mahābāho krīḍārthaṁ no bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O son of the worshipful Sire, this deer has attracted my mind, get it for me, pray, O you of mighty arms: it shall be an object of sport for us.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षाः पृषतसंघाश्च वानराः किंनरास्तथा
विचरन्ति महाबाहो रूपश्रेष्ठा महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṁghāśca vānarāḥ kiṁnarāstathā
vicaranti mahābāho rūpaśreṣṭhā mahābalāḥ

translations.english: Many a beautiful deer range at large in the vicinity of our hermitage such as Camaras, Srmaras, Rksas, Prsatas, Vanaras and Kinnaras. They are all very beautiful and of mighty strength; but O Prince, I have never seen before the like of this deer. In energy, strength and beauty it stands above all deer.

verses.sanskrit:
नानावर्णविचित्राङ्गो रत्नबिन्दुसमाचितः
द्योतयन्वनमव्यग्रं शोभते शशिसंनिभः
verses.transliteration:
nānāvarṇavicitrāṅgo ratnabindusamācitaḥ
dyotayanvanamavyagraṁ śobhate śaśisaṁnibhaḥ

translations.english: Its cntire body is diversified with various colours, nay, it is a jewel itself. It moves before me beautifying the forest with its resplendence, like to Moon himself.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो रूपमहो लक्ष्मीः स्वरसंपच्च शोभना
मृगोऽद्भुतो विचित्रोऽसौ हृदयं हरतीव मे
verses.transliteration:
aho rūpamaho lakṣmīḥ svarasaṁpacca śobhanā
mṛgo'dbhuto vicitro'sau hṛdayaṁ haratīva me

translations.english: Ah! what beauty, what beautiful a lustre, how musical a voice, this wonderful deer of variegated countenance, has indeed captivated my heart!

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ग्रहणमभ्येति जीवन्नेव मृगस्तव
आश्चर्यभूतं भवति विस्मयं जनयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi grahaṇamabhyeti jīvanneva mṛgastava
āścaryabhūtaṁ bhavati vismayaṁ janayiṣyati

translations.english: If can you get by this deer alive, O what wonder, what surprise!

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्तवनवासानां राज्यस्थानां च नः पुनः
अन्तःपुरविभूषार्थो मृग एष भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
samāptavanavāsānāṁ rājyasthānāṁ ca naḥ punaḥ
antaḥpuravibhūṣārtho mṛga eṣa bhaviṣyati

translations.english: When shall we regain our kingdom after the expire of the term of our banishment, this deer shall beautify the interior of our palace.

verses.sanskrit:
भरतस्यार्यपुत्रस्य श्वश्रूणां मम च प्रभो
मृगरूपमिदं दिव्यं विस्मयं जनयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
bharatasyāryaputrasya śvaśrūṇāṁ mama ca prabho
mṛgarūpamidaṁ divyaṁ vismayaṁ janayiṣyati

translations.english: O Lord, truly shall this celestial deer create surprise in Bharata, yourself, me and my mothers-in-law.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवन्न यदि तेऽभ्येति ग्रहणं मृगसत्तमः
अजिनं नरशार्दूल रुचिरं मे भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
jīvanna yadi te'bhyeti grahaṇaṁ mṛgasattamaḥ
ajinaṁ naraśārdūla ruciraṁ me bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O best of men, if can you not get hold of it alive its skin shall also look very beautiful (to us).

verses.sanskrit:
निहतस्यास्य सत्त्वस्य जाम्बूनदमयत्वचि
शष्पबृस्यां विनीतायामिच्छाम्यहमुपासितुम्
verses.transliteration:
nihatasyāsya sattvasya jāmbūnadamayatvaci
śaṣpabṛsyāṁ vinītāyāmicchāmyahamupāsitum

translations.english: Spreading on Kuća the skin of this golden deer when killed do I wish to invoke the Almighty.

verses.sanskrit:
कामवृत्तमिदं रौद्रं स्त्रीणामसदृशं मतम्
वपुषा त्वस्य सत्त्वस्य विस्मयो जनितो मम
verses.transliteration:
kāmavṛttamidaṁ raudraṁ strīṇāmasadṛśaṁ matam
vapuṣā tvasya sattvasya vismayo janito mama

translations.english: It looks (no doubt) unseemly and terrible and smacks of wilfulness, on the part of a wife to command her husband in this way, but I am sunk in surprise seeing the countenance of the deer.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन काञ्चनरोम्णा तु मणिप्रवरशृङ्गिणा
तरुणादित्यवर्णेन नक्षत्रपथवर्चसा
बभूव राघवस्यापि मनो विस्मयमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
tena kāñcanaromṇā tu maṇipravaraśṛṅgiṇā
taruṇādityavarṇena nakṣatrapathavarcasā
babhūva rāghavasyāpi mano vismayamāgatam

translations.english: Rāma's heart was struck with surprise beholding that wonderful deer having its down resembling gold, horns resembling exquisitely finc diamonds, colour like that of the newly risen Sun, and resplendence like that of the orbit of the planets. Being enchanted by its beauty and spurred on by Sītā's words, Raghava pleased, spoke to his younger brother.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्याः स्पृहां मृगगतामिमाम्
रूपश्रेष्ठतया ह्येष मृगोऽद्य न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ spṛhāṁ mṛgagatāmimām
rūpaśreṣṭhatayā hyeṣa mṛgo'dya na bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Behold, O Laksmana, it has immensely excited Vaidehi's desire. On account of its exquisite beauty it shall loose its life to-day.

verses.sanskrit:
न वने नन्दनोद्देशे न चैत्ररथसंश्रये
कुतः पृथिव्यां सौमित्रे योऽस्य कश्चित्समो मृगः
verses.transliteration:
na vane nandanoddeśe na caitrarathasaṁśraye
kutaḥ pṛthivyāṁ saumitre yo'sya kaścitsamo mṛgaḥ

translations.english: It has its equal no where on the earth-neither in the celestial garden nor in the Caitraratha forest.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिलोमानुलोमाश्च रुचिरा रोमराजयः
शोभन्ते मृगमाश्रित्य चित्राः कनकबिन्दुभिः
verses.transliteration:
pratilomānulomāśca rucirā romarājayaḥ
śobhante mṛgamāśritya citrāḥ kanakabindubhiḥ

translations.english: The hairs of its body being arranged in regular and contrary courses and being painted with golden drops do indeed look very beautiful.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्यास्य जृम्भमाणस्य दीप्तामग्निशिखोपमाम्
जिह्वां मुखान्निःसरन्तीं मेघादिव शतह्रदाम्
verses.transliteration:
paśyāsya jṛmbhamāṇasya dīptāmagniśikhopamām
jihvāṁ mukhānniḥsarantīṁ meghādiva śatahradām

translations.english: Do you see, while expanding its inouth, its tongue comes out resembling flaming fire like to a thunder-bolt reaving the mass of clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
मसारगल्वर्कमुखः शङ्खमुक्तानिभोदरः
कस्य नामानिरूप्योऽसौ न मनो लोभयेन्मृगः
verses.transliteration:
masāragalvarkamukhaḥ śaṅkhamuktānibhodaraḥ
kasya nāmānirūpyo'sau na mano lobhayenmṛgaḥ

translations.english: Its face is like a glass made of a best blue sapphire, its belly resembling a conch and pearl, and it is very difficult to ascertain its shapes. Beholding it who is there (on earth) whose heart is not enamoured?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य रूपमिदं दृष्ट्वा जाम्बूनदमयप्रभम्
नानारत्नमयं दिव्यं न मनो विस्मयं व्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
kasya rūpamidaṁ dṛṣṭvā jāmbūnadamayaprabham
nānāratnamayaṁ divyaṁ na mano vismayaṁ vrajet

translations.english: Its beauty resembles the rays of gold and is variegated with diverse hues of jewels. Whose heart is not enveloped with surprise beholding such a celestial beauty, O Laksmana?

verses.sanskrit:
मांसहेतोरपि मृगान्विहारार्थं च धन्विनः
घ्नन्ति लक्ष्मण राजानो मृगयायां महावने
verses.transliteration:
māṁsahetorapi mṛgānvihārārthaṁ ca dhanvinaḥ
ghnanti lakṣmaṇa rājāno mṛgayāyāṁ mahāvane

translations.english: Princes, with bows in their hands, while-a hunting in a deep forest destroy deer either for flesh or for sport.

verses.sanskrit:
धनानि व्यवसायेन विचीयन्ते महावने
धातवो विविधाश्चापि मणिरत्नसुवर्णिनः
verses.transliteration:
dhanāni vyavasāyena vicīyante mahāvane
dhātavo vividhāścāpi maṇiratnasuvarṇinaḥ

translations.english: Moreover while engaged in sporting they collect many a jewel and various metals as gold and silver, in the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सारमखिलं नॄणां धनं निचयवर्धनम्
मनसा चिन्तितं सर्वं यथा शुक्रस्य लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
tatsāramakhilaṁ nṝṇāṁ dhanaṁ nicayavardhanam
manasā cintitaṁ sarvaṁ yathā śukrasya lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: There is not the least doubt that these wild riches filling up their coffers are comparatively far better (than the wealth acquired by other sources) like to the objects of enjoyment, enjoyed at their fancy by the people inhabiting the celestial region.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थी येनार्थकृत्येन संव्रजत्यविचारयन्
तमर्थमर्थशास्त्रज्ञः प्राहुरर्थ्याश्च लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
arthī yenārthakṛtyena saṁvrajatyavicārayan
tamarthamarthaśāstrajñaḥ prāhurarthyāśca lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: The object which persons desirous of acquiring wealth follow without any discretion in their actions, is the true definition of wealth given by the political economists.

verses.sanskrit:
न कादली न प्रियकी न प्रवेणी न चाविकी
भवेदेतस्य सदृशी स्पर्शनेनेति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
na kādalī na priyakī na praveṇī na cāvikī
bhavedetasya sadṛśī sparśaneneti me matiḥ

translations.english: Vaidehi of slender waist desire to sit with me on the exquisitely fine golden skin of this gem of a deer, me-seems no deer skin is so comfortable to touch as this neither the skin of Kādali, Priyaki, Praveni nor of Caviki.

verses.sanskrit:
एष चैव मृगः श्रीमान्यश्च दिव्यो नभश्चरः
उभावेतौ मृगौ दिव्यौ तारामृगमहीमृगौ
verses.transliteration:
eṣa caiva mṛgaḥ śrīmānyaśca divyo nabhaścaraḥ
ubhāvetau mṛgau divyau tārāmṛgamahīmṛgau

translations.english: Truly handsome in this deer and the one that range in the welkin, indeed these two deer only are celestial—the one that range in the sky* (Mrgasirā) and this that range on earth. This refers to Mrgaşiră, the fifth lunar constellation which resembles a deer.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि वायं तथा यन्मां भवेद्वदसि लक्ष्मण
मायैषा राक्षसस्येति कर्तव्योऽस्य वधो मया
verses.transliteration:
yadi vāyaṁ tathā yanmāṁ bhavedvadasi lakṣmaṇa
māyaiṣā rākṣasasyeti kartavyo'sya vadho mayā

translations.english: And if it be a Raksasa's illusion as you say, O Laksmana, then it must be killed by me.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन हि नृशंसेन मारीचेनाकृतात्मना
वने विचरता पूर्वं हिंसिता मुनिपुंगवाः
verses.transliteration:
etena hi nṛśaṁsena mārīcenākṛtātmanā
vane vicaratā pūrvaṁ hiṁsitā munipuṁgavāḥ

translations.english: This cruel vicious-souled Mārica made away with many eminent ascetics, while travelling in the forest; and this Räkşasa assuming the shape of an illusive deer destroyed many kings-mighty archers while a-hunting in this forest; it is for this that this deer must be killed.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरस्तादिह वातापिः परिभूय तपस्विनः
उदरस्थो द्विजान्हन्ति स्वगर्भोऽश्वतरीमिव
verses.transliteration:
purastādiha vātāpiḥ paribhūya tapasvinaḥ
udarastho dvijānhanti svagarbho'śvatarīmiva

translations.english: Formerly this Vātăpi entering into the womb of twice-born ones used to come out reaving them like to the embryo of a mule. The name of an Asur devoured by Agastya.

verses.sanskrit:
स कदाचिच्चिराल्लोके आससाद महामुनिम्
अगस्त्यं तेजसा युक्तं भक्ष्यस्तस्य बभूव ह
verses.transliteration:
sa kadāciccirālloke āsasāda mahāmunim
agastyaṁ tejasā yuktaṁ bhakṣyastasya babhūva ha

translations.english: Once on a time this Vātāpi approached the eminent saint Agastya and was devoured by him.

verses.sanskrit:
समुत्थाने च तद्रूपं कर्तुकामं समीक्ष्य तम्
उत्स्मयित्वा तु भगवान्वातापिमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
samutthāne ca tadrūpaṁ kartukāmaṁ samīkṣya tam
utsmayitvā tu bhagavānvātāpimidamabravīt

translations.english: After the Šrāddha ceremony had been over, finding that Bātāpi desirous of assuming the shape of a Rākṣasa the great saint Agastya said smiling.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयाविगण्य वातापे परिभूताश्च तेजसा
जीवलोके द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तस्मादसि जरां गतः
verses.transliteration:
tvayāvigaṇya vātāpe paribhūtāśca tejasā
jīvaloke dvijaśreṣṭhāstasmādasi jarāṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Being blinded with your prowess O Vātāpi, you have destroyed many eminent twice-born ones on this earth and for this that I do digest you.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं तन्न भवेद्रक्षो वातापिरिव लक्ष्मण
मद्विधं योऽतिमन्येत धर्मनित्यं जितेन्द्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tanna bhavedrakṣo vātāpiriva lakṣmaṇa
madvidhaṁ yo'timanyeta dharmanityaṁ jitendriyam

translations.english: Truly that Raksasa, O, Laksmana who wish to surpass one like me who has controlled his senses and is ever engaged in pious offices shall meet with his end like to this Vātāpi.

verses.sanskrit:
भवेद्धतोऽयं वातापिरगस्त्येनेव मा गतिः
इह त्वं भव संनद्धो यन्त्रितो रक्ष मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
bhaveddhato'yaṁ vātāpiragastyeneva mā gatiḥ
iha tvaṁ bhava saṁnaddho yantrito rakṣa maithilīm

translations.english: Therefore this Mārīca approaching me shall be killed by me like to Vātāpi being devoured by Agastya. Do you therefore vigilantly protect Vaidehi with mail and armours on.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्यामायत्तमस्माकं यत्कृत्यं रघुनन्दन
अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ग्रहीष्याम्यथ वा मृगम्
verses.transliteration:
asyāmāyattamasmākaṁ yatkṛtyaṁ raghunandana
ahamenaṁ vadhiṣyāmi grahīṣyāmyatha vā mṛgam

translations.english: It is our prime duty, O descendant of Raghu, to protect Jānaki. I shall either kill this deer or shall get hold of it.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्गच्छामि सौमित्रे मृगमानयितुं द्रुतम्
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेहीं मृगत्वचि गतस्पृहाम्
verses.transliteration:
yāvadgacchāmi saumitre mṛgamānayituṁ drutam
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehīṁ mṛgatvaci gataspṛhām

translations.english: Look, O Laksmana, Vaidehi is extremely anxious to get the skin of this deer I shall therefore proceed at once, O son of Sumitrā, to catch this deer.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वचा प्रधानया ह्येष मृगोऽद्य न भविष्यति
अप्रमत्तेन ते भाव्यमाश्रमस्थेन सीतया
verses.transliteration:
tvacā pradhānayā hyeṣa mṛgo'dya na bhaviṣyati
apramattena te bhāvyamāśramasthena sītayā

translations.english: The skin of this deer is the best of its kind; for certain shall it loose its life today. As long as I do not kill this deer, O Lakşmaņa, do you with Sītā remain with vigilance in this asylum. I shall in no time come back with its skin after killing in with one arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणेनातिबलेन पक्षिणा; जटायुषा बुद्धिमता च लक्ष्मण
भवाप्रमत्तः प्रतिगृह्य मैथिलीं; प्रतिक्षणं सर्वत एव शङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇenātibalena pakṣiṇā; jaṭāyuṣā buddhimatā ca lakṣmaṇa
bhavāpramattaḥ pratigṛhya maithilīṁ; pratikṣaṇaṁ sarvata eva śaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: Do you stay here, O Lakşmaņa, with Jānakī in constant fear and vigilance, along with the mighty Jațāyu, intelligent and ever engaged in pious offices.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु तं समादिश्य भ्रातरं रघुनन्दनः
बबन्धासिं महातेजा जाम्बूनदमयत्सरुम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu taṁ samādiśya bhrātaraṁ raghunandanaḥ
babandhāsiṁ mahātejā jāmbūnadamayatsarum

translations.english: Having thus directed his brother, the highly energetic son of Raghu equipped himself with his gold-hilted scimitar.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्रिविणतं चापमादायात्मविभूषणम्
आबध्य च कलापौ द्वौ जगामोदग्रविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tatastriviṇataṁ cāpamādāyātmavibhūṣaṇam
ābadhya ca kalāpau dvau jagāmodagravikramaḥ

translations.english: And girding himself with his bow bent at three places, which served him ornament,—as well as a couple of quivers, that one of fierce energy sallied out.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वञ्चयानो राजेन्द्रमापतन्तं निरीक्ष्य वै
बभूवान्तर्हितस्त्रासात्पुनः संदर्शनेऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vañcayāno rājendramāpatantaṁ nirīkṣya vai
babhūvāntarhitastrāsātpunaḥ saṁdarśane'bhavat

translations.english: Seeing that foremost of monarchs approach, that best of beasts from fear disappeared; and then again showed himself. as an

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शनादर्शनेनैव सोऽपाकर्षत राघवम्
आसीत्क्रुद्धस्तु काकुत्स्थो विवशस्तेन मोहितः
verses.transliteration:
darśanādarśanenaiva so'pākarṣata rāghavam
āsītkruddhastu kākutstho vivaśastena mohitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Rāma, eagerly anxious to secure the deer, being foiled by the deer, and in consequence growing enraged, wearied out, rested under a shadow, on a sward.

verses.sanskrit:
अथावतस्थे सुश्रान्तश्छायामाश्रित्य शाद्वले
मृगैः परिवृतो वन्यैरदूरात्प्रत्यदृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
athāvatasthe suśrāntaśchāyāmāśritya śādvale
mṛgaiḥ parivṛto vanyairadūrātpratyadṛśyata

translations.english: And that ranger of the night, wearing the form of a deer, maddening Rāma, discovered himself (again) at a distance surrounded by (other) deer,

verses.sanskrit:
स भृशं मृगरूपस्य विनिर्भिद्य शरोत्तमः
मारीचस्यैव हृदयं विभेदाशनिसंनिभः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhṛśaṁ mṛgarūpasya vinirbhidya śarottamaḥ
mārīcasyaiva hṛdayaṁ vibhedāśanisaṁnibhaḥ

translations.english: And that best of arrows, like to a thunderbolt, deeply pierced the breast of Mārīca, wearing the shape of a deer.

verses.sanskrit:
तालमात्रमथोत्पत्य न्यपतत्स शरातुरः
व्यनदद्भैरवं नादं धरण्यामल्पजीवितः
म्रियमाणस्तु मारीचो जहौ तां कृत्रिमां तनुम्
verses.transliteration:
tālamātramathotpatya nyapatatsa śarāturaḥ
vyanadadbhairavaṁ nādaṁ dharaṇyāmalpajīvitaḥ
mriyamāṇastu mārīco jahau tāṁ kṛtrimāṁ tanum

translations.english: Thereat bounding up high as a palmyra palm, that one whose saws had almost run out, uttered terrible sounds, lying on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन मर्मणि निर्विद्धः शरेणानुपमेन हि
मृगरूपं तु तत्त्यक्त्वा राक्षसं रूपमात्मनः
चक्रे स सुमहाकायो मारीचो जीवितं त्यजन्
verses.transliteration:
tena marmaṇi nirviddhaḥ śareṇānupamena hi
mṛgarūpaṁ tu tattyaktvā rākṣasaṁ rūpamātmanaḥ
cakre sa sumahākāyo mārīco jīvitaṁ tyajan

translations.english: And pierced to the marrow by that peerless shaft, Marica, renouncing his deer form, resumed his Rākşasa lineaments; and giving up his life attaining a huge person, considering the time had come (for availing himself of the advice tendered by Rāvana), began to cry with the voice of Rāghava, Ah Sita! Ah Laksmana!

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं भूमौ राक्षसं घोरदर्शनम्
जगाम मनसा सीतां लक्ष्मणस्य वचः स्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā patitaṁ bhūmau rākṣasaṁ ghoradarśanam
jagāma manasā sītāṁ lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ smaran

translations.english: And seeing that grim-visaged Rākşasa lying low on the ground, with his person bathed in blood, and rolling hither and thither, Rāma proceeded towards the asylum thinking of Sītā and revolving within himself Laksmana's words.

verses.sanskrit:
हा सीते लक्ष्मणेत्येवमाक्रुश्य तु महास्वरम्
ममार राक्षसः सोऽयं श्रुत्वा सीता कथं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
hā sīte lakṣmaṇetyevamākruśya tu mahāsvaram
mamāra rākṣasaḥ so'yaṁ śrutvā sītā kathaṁ bhavet

translations.english: Mārīca has given up his ghost exclaiming aloud Ah! Sītā, Ah! Laksmana. I do not know what shall Sītā do hearing the cry? And what shall the mighty-armed Laksmana do?

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्च महाबाहुः कामवस्थां गमिष्यति
इति संचिन्त्य धर्मात्मा रामो हृष्टतनूरुहः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaśca mahābāhuḥ kāmavasthāṁ gamiṣyati
iti saṁcintya dharmātmā rāmo hṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ

translations.english: While pondering thus the hairs of the virtuous-souled Rāma stood on their end. Killing that Räkşasa assuming the shape of a deer and hearing his terrible cry Rāma was overwhelmed with fear arising out of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य पृषतं चान्यं मांसमादाय राघवः
त्वरमाणो जनस्थानं ससाराभिमुखस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
nihatya pṛṣataṁ cānyaṁ māṁsamādāya rāghavaḥ
tvaramāṇo janasthānaṁ sasārābhimukhastadā

translations.english: Thereupon killing a deer and taking its flesh he hastened towards Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्तस्वरं तु तं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय सदृशं वने
उवाच लक्ष्मणं सीता गच्छ जानीहि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
ārtasvaraṁ tu taṁ bharturvijñāya sadṛśaṁ vane
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṁ sītā gaccha jānīhi rāghavam

translations.english: Hearing that cry in the forest resembling her husband's voice Sítā spake to Laksmana saying Do you go and learn what has befallen Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे जीवितं स्थाने हृदयं वावतिष्ठते
क्रोशतः परमार्तस्य श्रुतः शब्दो मया भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi me jīvitaṁ sthāne hṛdayaṁ vāvatiṣṭhate
krośataḥ paramārtasya śrutaḥ śabdo mayā bhṛśam

translations.english: He is crying aloud in pitiable accents; hearing them my life and soul are incapable of remaining any longer in their proper places.

verses.sanskrit:
आक्रन्दमानं तु वने भ्रातरं त्रातुमर्हसि
तं क्षिप्रमभिधाव त्वं भ्रातरं शरणैषिणम्
verses.transliteration:
ākrandamānaṁ tu vane bhrātaraṁ trātumarhasi
taṁ kṣipramabhidhāva tvaṁ bhrātaraṁ śaraṇaiṣiṇam

translations.english: It behoveth you to save your brother who is crying aloud in the forest; do you immediately repair hence to save him, who is in need of your help. He has been over-powered by the Rākşasas like to a bullock brought under the power of a lion, Remembering the behest of Rāma, Laks maņa did not go, though accosted thus by Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्वमस्यामवस्थायां भ्रातरं नाभिपद्यसे
इच्छसि त्वं विनश्यन्तं रामं लक्ष्मण मत्कृते
verses.transliteration:
yastvamasyāmavasthāyāṁ bhrātaraṁ nābhipadyase
icchasi tvaṁ vinaśyantaṁ rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇa matkṛte

translations.english: Extremely mortified, the daughter of Janaka spake to him saying O Son of Sumitra, you are an enemy to Rāma, in the grab of a brother. You did not proceed for the relief of they brother who has been reduced to such a plight.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यसनं ते प्रियं मन्ये स्नेहो भ्रातरि नास्ति ते
तेन तिष्ठसि विस्रब्धस्तमपश्यन्महाद्युतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vyasanaṁ te priyaṁ manye sneho bhrātari nāsti te
tena tiṣṭhasi visrabdhastamapaśyanmahādyutim

translations.english: Truely being under the influence of lust for me you did not follow Rāghava! For this you did welcome Rāma's disaster; you have no affection for him.

verses.sanskrit:
किं हि संशयमापन्ने तस्मिन्निह मया भवेत्
कर्तव्यमिह तिष्ठन्त्या यत्प्रधानस्त्वमागतः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ hi saṁśayamāpanne tasminniha mayā bhavet
kartavyamiha tiṣṭhantyā yatpradhānastvamāgataḥ

translations.english: For this it is that you did sit here without anxiety not seeing the highly effulgent (Rāma). Råma, following whom you have repaired to this forest, being in danger, of what avail is life to me.?'

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणं वैदेहीं बाष्पशोकपरिप्लुताम्
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणस्त्रस्तां सीतां मृगवधूमिव
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇaṁ vaidehīṁ bāṣpaśokapariplutām
abravīllakṣmaṇastrastāṁ sītāṁ mṛgavadhūmiva

translations.english: Vaidehī speaking thus being influenced by sorrow, and with tears in her eyes, like to a deer, Laksmana spoke to her.

verses.sanskrit:
देवि देवमनुष्येषु गन्धर्वेषु पतत्रिषु
राक्षसेषु पिशाचेषु किंनरेषु मृगेषु च
verses.transliteration:
devi devamanuṣyeṣu gandharveṣu patatriṣu
rākṣaseṣu piśāceṣu kiṁnareṣu mṛgeṣu ca

translations.english: Worshipful madam! Celestials, Danavas, Gandharvas, Raksasas, Pisacas, men, Kinnaras, animals, or birds, there is none among them, who can withstand Rāghava, who equals the lord of celestials in warfare. In fact there is none who can do away with Ráma in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
अनिवार्यं बलं तस्य बलैर्बलवतामपि
त्रिभिर्लोकैः समुद्युक्तैः सेश्वरैः सामरैरपि
verses.transliteration:
anivāryaṁ balaṁ tasya balairbalavatāmapi
tribhirlokaiḥ samudyuktaiḥ seśvaraiḥ sāmarairapi

translations.english: It does not behove you therefore to accost me thus. Nor do I dare leave you here alone in this forest without Rāma. Even the mighty heroes, as the Lord of celestials, cannot subdue his prowess with all their strength. Even the Almighty Himself, with the celestials and the three world, cannot defeat him. Do you therefore renounce grief and console theyself.

verses.sanskrit:
न स तस्य स्वरो व्यक्तं न कश्चिदपि दैवतः
गन्धर्वनगरप्रख्या माया सा तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
na sa tasya svaro vyaktaṁ na kaścidapi daivataḥ
gandharvanagaraprakhyā māyā sā tasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: Sooner shall your husband return killing the best of deer. It is not his voice nor one sent by any deity. It is but an illusion of that Rākşasa (Mārīca).

verses.sanskrit:
न्यासभूतासि वैदेहि न्यस्ता मयि महात्मना
रामेण त्वं वरारोहे न त्वां त्यक्तुमिहोत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
nyāsabhūtāsi vaidehi nyastā mayi mahātmanā
rāmeṇa tvaṁ varārohe na tvāṁ tyaktumihotsahe

translations.english: O Vaidehī, you have been left to my charge by the high-souled (Rama)-I therefore do not dare leave you behind, O you the jewel of a damsel.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतवैराश्च कल्याणि वयमेतैर्निशाचरैः
खरस्य निधने देवि जनस्थानवधं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
kṛtavairāśca kalyāṇi vayametairniśācaraiḥ
kharasya nidhane devi janasthānavadhaṁ prati

translations.english: We have made these night-rangers our enemies. For compassing the destruction of Khara, O worshipful one, and devastating Janasthāna, Rākṣasas oftentimes use improper words to us in this extensive forest.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसा विधिना वाचो विसृजन्ति महावने
हिंसाविहारा वैदेहि न चिन्तयितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasā vidhinā vāco visṛjanti mahāvane
hiṁsāvihārā vaidehi na cintayitumarhasi

translations.english: O Vaidehī, to create mischief to the pious is the only amusement of these Rākşasas-you shoudst not therefore be anxious for this.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्ता तु क्रुद्धा संरक्तलोचना
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यवादिनम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇenaivamuktā tu kruddhā saṁraktalocanā
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ satyavādinam

translations.english: Being thus addressed by him her eyes were reddened with ire, and she spake these harsh words to the truthful Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अनार्य करुणारम्भ नृशंस कुलपांसन
अहं तव प्रियं मन्ये तेनैतानि प्रभाषसे
verses.transliteration:
anārya karuṇārambha nṛśaṁsa kulapāṁsana
ahaṁ tava priyaṁ manye tenaitāni prabhāṣase

translations.english: O cruel one! O you the destroyer of your line! it is a disgrace to you that you wishest to protect me (killing Răma). Methinks, this mighty disaster of Rāma is welcome to you, or else why should you seeing this, speak thus, O Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतच्चित्रं सपत्नेषु पापं लक्ष्मण यद्भवेत्
त्वद्विधेषु नृशंसेषु नित्यं प्रच्छन्नचारिषु
verses.transliteration:
naitaccitraṁ sapatneṣu pāpaṁ lakṣmaṇa yadbhavet
tvadvidheṣu nṛśaṁseṣu nityaṁ pracchannacāriṣu

translations.english: It is not a wonder that an evil desire lurks in you who are a hypocrite and a cruel-hearted cnemy.

verses.sanskrit:
सुदुष्टस्त्वं वने राममेकमेकोऽनुगच्छसि
मम हेतोः प्रतिच्छन्नः प्रयुक्तो भरतेन वा
verses.transliteration:
suduṣṭastvaṁ vane rāmamekameko'nugacchasi
mama hetoḥ praticchannaḥ prayukto bharatena vā

translations.english: Verily are you a monster of wickedness, that Rāma repairing to woods, you have, being lustful for me, followed him alone. Or hast you been engaged by Bharata to act thus?

verses.sanskrit:
कथमिन्दीवरश्यामं रामं पद्मनिभेक्षणम्
उपसंश्रित्य भर्तारं कामयेयं पृथग्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
kathamindīvaraśyāmaṁ rāmaṁ padmanibhekṣaṇam
upasaṁśritya bhartāraṁ kāmayeyaṁ pṛthagjanam

translations.english: But your or Bharata's intention shall not be satisfied, O Saumitre. How shall I desire another man after serving the lotus-eyed Rāma of dark blue hue as my husband?

verses.sanskrit:
समक्षं तव सौमित्रे प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्ये न संशयः
रामं विना क्षणमपि न हि जीवामि भूतले
verses.transliteration:
samakṣaṁ tava saumitre prāṇāṁstyakṣye na saṁśayaḥ
rāmaṁ vinā kṣaṇamapi na hi jīvāmi bhūtale

translations.english: I shall renounce my life before you, therefore, O Laksmana; without Rāma I shall not maintain my being for a moment on this earth.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं सीतया सोमहर्षणम्
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणः सीतां प्राञ्जलिर्विजितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ sītayā somaharṣaṇam
abravīllakṣmaṇaḥ sītāṁ prāñjalirvijitendriyaḥ

translations.english: Hearing these brazen words of Sītā, capable of making one's down stand on end, the selfcontrolled Lakşmaņa with joined hands spake to her saying You are a very Goddess to me, I therefore dare not answer you.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरं नोत्सहे वक्तुं दैवतं भवती मम
वाक्यमप्रतिरूपं तु न चित्रं स्त्रीषु मैथिलि
verses.transliteration:
uttaraṁ notsahe vaktuṁ daivataṁ bhavatī mama
vākyamapratirūpaṁ tu na citraṁ strīṣu maithili

translations.english: What you have spoken, O Maithelee, is nothing surprising-for fernales. Such is the nature of womankind on this earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वभावस्त्वेष नारीणामेषु लोकेषु दृश्यते
विमुक्तधर्माश्चपलास्तीक्ष्णा भेदकराः स्त्रियः
verses.transliteration:
svabhāvastveṣa nārīṇāmeṣu lokeṣu dṛśyate
vimuktadharmāścapalāstīkṣṇā bhedakarāḥ striyaḥ

translations.english: Women by nature are crooked, fickle, devoid of religious knowledge, and bring about difference between father and sons. O Vaidehi, O daughter of Janaka, truly am I incapable of putting up with these words of yours. They have pierced through both of my ears like a heated Nāraca.

verses.sanskrit:
धिक्त्वामद्य प्रणश्य त्वं यन्मामेवं विशङ्कसे
स्त्रीत्वाद्दुष्टस्वभावेन गुरुवाक्ये व्यवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
dhiktvāmadya praṇaśya tvaṁ yanmāmevaṁ viśaṅkase
strītvādduṣṭasvabhāvena guruvākye vyavasthitam

translations.english: However the deities ranging in this woodland are my witnesses—may they hear you. I spoke what was fair and have been thus addressed by you with these harsh words. I do always obey my superior's commands. Fie on you! Your destruction is near at hand that do you suspect me, being influenced' by this womanish nature. I shall go where Kākutstha is, may good betide you, O you the best of damsel!

verses.sanskrit:
निमित्तानि हि घोराणि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे
अपि त्वां सह रामेण पश्येयं पुनरागतः
verses.transliteration:
nimittāni hi ghorāṇi yāni prādurbhavanti me
api tvāṁ saha rāmeṇa paśyeyaṁ punarāgataḥ

translations.english: May the deities of the forest protect you, O you of expansive eyes! many a bad omen appear before me. My I see you again when I shall come back with Rāina.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्ता तु रुदती जनकात्मजा
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं तीव्रं बाष्पपरिप्लुता
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇenaivamuktā tu rudatī janakātmajā
pratyuvāca tato vākyaṁ tīvraṁ bāṣpapariplutā

translations.english: Being thus accosted by Lakşmaņa the daughter of Janaka replied weeping and being bathed in tears.

verses.sanskrit:
गोदावरीं प्रवेक्ष्यामि विना रामेण लक्ष्मण
आबन्धिष्येऽथ वा त्यक्ष्ये विषमे देहमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
godāvarīṁ pravekṣyāmi vinā rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇa
ābandhiṣye'tha vā tyakṣye viṣame dehamātmanaḥ

translations.english: Without Rama, O Laksmana, I shall drink virulent poison, enter fire or dive into the Godāverī. I shall destroy this body either by hanging or by falling down from the top of a high object. I shall never be able to touch another man but Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
इति लक्ष्मणमाक्रुश्य सीता दुःखसमन्विता
पाणिभ्यां रुदती दुःखादुदरं प्रजघान ह
verses.transliteration:
iti lakṣmaṇamākruśya sītā duḥkhasamanvitā
pāṇibhyāṁ rudatī duḥkhādudaraṁ prajaghāna ha

translations.english: Speaking thus to Lakşmaņa, Sītā, being enveloped with grief, weeping, struck her belly* with her hands. Properly it should be Struck her breast. But it has a special significance here, i.e.-she would not be satisfied until her belly be filled with all the Raksasas salin.तामार्तरूपां विमना रुदन्ती

verses.sanskrit:
तामार्तरूपां विमना रुदन्तीं; सौमित्रिरालोक्य विशालनेत्राम्
आश्वासयामास न चैव भर्तु;स्तं भ्रातरं किंचिदुवाच सीता
verses.transliteration:
tāmārtarūpāṁ vimanā rudantīṁ; saumitrirālokya viśālanetrām
āśvāsayāmāsa na caiva bhartu;staṁ bhrātaraṁ kiṁciduvāca sītā

translations.english: Seeing the daughter of Janaka of expansive eyes weep thus in pitiable accents, Lakşmaņa losing his attention began to console her.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सीतामभिवाद्य लक्ष्मणः; कृताञ्जलिः किंचिदभिप्रणम्य
अवेक्षमाणो बहुशश्च मैथिलीं; जगाम रामस्य समीपमात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sītāmabhivādya lakṣmaṇaḥ; kṛtāñjaliḥ kiṁcidabhipraṇamya
avekṣamāṇo bahuśaśca maithilīṁ; jagāma rāmasya samīpamātmavān

translations.english: Afterwards the pure-hearted Laksmana, having control over his senses, saluting Sītā with clasped palms and bending low a little proceeded where Rāma was, casting again and again his glance upon her as he went.

verses.sanskrit:
तया परुषमुक्तस्तु कुपितो राघवानुजः
स विकाङ्क्षन्भृशं रामं प्रतस्थे नचिरादिव
verses.transliteration:
tayā paruṣamuktastu kupito rāghavānujaḥ
sa vikāṅkṣanbhṛśaṁ rāmaṁ pratasthe nacirādiva

translations.english: Having been addressed with those harsh words the younger brother of Rāghava, enraged, proceeded at once, being anxious to see Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तदासाद्य दशग्रीवः क्षिप्रमन्तरमास्थितः
अभिचक्राम वैदेहीं परिव्राजकरूपधृक्
verses.transliteration:
tadāsādya daśagrīvaḥ kṣipramantaramāsthitaḥ
abhicakrāma vaidehīṁ parivrājakarūpadhṛk

translations.english: Thereupon the ten-necked one, availing of this opportunity came before Vaidehī assuming the semblance of a mendicant.

verses.sanskrit:
श्लक्ष्णकाषायसंवीतः शिखी छत्री उपानही
वामे चांसेऽवसज्याथ शुभे यष्टिकमण्डलू
परिव्राजकरूपेण वैदेहीं समुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
ślakṣṇakāṣāyasaṁvītaḥ śikhī chatrī upānahī
vāme cāṁse'vasajyātha śubhe yaṣṭikamaṇḍalū
parivrājakarūpeṇa vaidehīṁ samupāgamat

translations.english: Wearing a soft silken cloth, with a lock of hair on his head with an umbrella and shoes and having on his left shoulder a rod and kamandalu the highly powerful one assuming the appearance of a wandering devotee carrying three long bamboo staves appeared before Vaidehi in the forest when there was none of the brothers by her.

verses.sanskrit:
तामपश्यत्ततो बालां राजपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम्
रोहिणीं शशिना हीनां ग्रहवद्भृशदारुणः
verses.transliteration:
tāmapaśyattato bālāṁ rājaputrīṁ yaśasvinīm
rohiṇīṁ śaśinā hīnāṁ grahavadbhṛśadāruṇaḥ

translations.english: He saw there the young and pious daughter of the king like to an evening void of both sun and moon and as the highly terrible Rahu eyes Rohini forsaken by Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रस्रोताश्च तं दृष्ट्वा वीक्षन्तं रक्तलोचनम्
स्तिमितं गन्तुमारेभे भयाद्गोदावरी नदी
verses.transliteration:
śīghrasrotāśca taṁ dṛṣṭvā vīkṣantaṁ raktalocanam
stimitaṁ gantumārebhe bhayādgodāvarī nadī

translations.english: Seeing that terrible one the doer of evil deeds, the trees of Janasthāna did not move nor the wind did blow. Seeing him eye Sītā with his blood-red eyes, the fast streaming river Godāverī even slackened its course out of fear.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य त्वन्तरं प्रेप्सुर्दशग्रीवस्तदन्तरे
उपतस्थे च वैदेहीं भिक्षुरूपेण रावणः
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya tvantaraṁ prepsurdaśagrīvastadantare
upatasthe ca vaidehīṁ bhikṣurūpeṇa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: In the mean time the Ten-necked Rävana, enquiring about Rāma's weak points appeared before Vaidehī in the guise of a mendicant.

verses.sanskrit:
अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण भर्तारमनुशोचतीम्
अभ्यवर्तत वैदेहीं चित्रामिव शनैश्चरः
verses.transliteration:
abhavyo bhavyarūpeṇa bhartāramanuśocatīm
abhyavartata vaidehīṁ citrāmiva śanaiścaraḥ

translations.english: Like to Sani approaching citră, that impious one, assuming the appearance of a pious man like a well covered with grass, approached Vaidehī who was bewailing her husband.

verses.sanskrit:
स पापो भव्यरूपेण तृणैः कूप इवावृतः
अतिष्ठत्प्रेक्ष्य वैदेहीं रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
sa pāpo bhavyarūpeṇa tṛṇaiḥ kūpa ivāvṛtaḥ
atiṣṭhatprekṣya vaidehīṁ rāmapatnīṁ yaśasvinīm

translations.english: And seeing that pious spouse of Rāma-Vaidehi, Ravana stood before her.

verses.sanskrit:
शुभां रुचिरदन्तौष्ठीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
आसीनां पर्णशालायां बाष्पशोकाभिपीडिताम्
verses.transliteration:
śubhāṁ ruciradantauṣṭhīṁ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
āsīnāṁ parṇaśālāyāṁ bāṣpaśokābhipīḍitām

translations.english: Her lips and teeth were extremely fine, her face resembled the full moon and her eyes were like lotus-petals. She had a yellow siiken cloth on and sat in the thatched cottage, overwhelmed with grief and bathed in tears.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पीतकौशेयवासिनीम्
अभ्यगच्छत वैदेहीं दुष्टचेता निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ padmapalāśākṣīṁ pītakauśeyavāsinīm
abhyagacchata vaidehīṁ duṣṭacetā niśācaraḥ

translations.english: And that ranger of the night with a pleased heart approached Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
तामुत्तमां त्रिलोकानां पद्महीनामिव श्रियम्
विभ्राजमानां वपुषा रावणः प्रशशंस ह
verses.transliteration:
tāmuttamāṁ trilokānāṁ padmahīnāmiva śriyam
vibhrājamānāṁ vapuṣā rāvaṇaḥ praśaśaṁsa ha

translations.english: Seeing her that lord of Rākṣasas was pierced with the shafts of passion. And speaking highly of her, surpassing in beauty the three worlds and resembling by the excellence of her own person the very goddess of wealth herself Rāvana uttering the name of God spake to her,

verses.sanskrit:
का त्वं काञ्चनवर्णाभे पीतकौशेयवासिनि
कमलानां शुभां मालां पद्मिनीव च बिभ्रती
verses.transliteration:
kā tvaṁ kāñcanavarṇābhe pītakauśeyavāsini
kamalānāṁ śubhāṁ mālāṁ padminīva ca bibhratī

translations.english: O you having the colour of gold and silver, O you wearing silken cloth, O you appearing like a lotus wearing a garland of lotus-petals, O you of beautiful countenance!

verses.sanskrit:
ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिः शुभा लक्ष्मीरप्सरा वा शुभानने
भूतिर्वा त्वं वरारोहे रतिर्वा स्वैरचारिणी
verses.transliteration:
hrīḥ śrīḥ kīrtiḥ śubhā lakṣmīrapsarā vā śubhānane
bhūtirvā tvaṁ varārohe ratirvā svairacāriṇī

translations.english: Are you Bashfulness, Beauty, Fame, Wealth, Apsarā, Dignity or Rati herself who is ranging at will in this forest?

verses.sanskrit:
समाः शिखरिणः स्निग्धाः पाण्डुरा दशनास्तव
विशाले विमले नेत्रे रक्तान्ते कृष्णतारके
verses.transliteration:
samāḥ śikhariṇaḥ snigdhāḥ pāṇḍurā daśanāstava
viśāle vimale netre raktānte kṛṣṇatārake

translations.english: All your teeth are equal having their tops like to the buds of Kunda flower, beautiful and yellow. Your eyes are expansive, clear, of bloody hue, and having black pupils. Your hip is fleshy and spacious. Your thighs are like those of elephants, round, fleshy and perfectly strong.

verses.sanskrit:
पीनोन्नतमुखौ कान्तौ स्निग्धतालफलोपमौ
मणिप्रवेकाभरणौ रुचिरौ ते पयोधरौ
verses.transliteration:
pīnonnatamukhau kāntau snigdhatālaphalopamau
maṇipravekābharaṇau rucirau te payodharau

translations.english: Your nipples are bulky, pointed, highly captivating like cold palm fruits, beautiful and ornamented with diverse jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
चारुस्मिते चारुदति चारुनेत्रे विलासिनि
मनो हरसि मे रामे नदीकूलमिवाम्भसा
verses.transliteration:
cārusmite cārudati cārunetre vilāsini
mano harasi me rāme nadīkūlamivāmbhasā

translations.english: O you of beautiful smile! O you of beautiful teeth! O you of beautiful eyes! O fine damsel, you did carry away my heart like to a river carrying away its banks by its stream.

verses.sanskrit:
करान्तमितमध्यासि सुकेशी संहतस्तनी
नैव देवी न गन्धर्वी न यक्षी न च किंनरी
verses.transliteration:
karāntamitamadhyāsi sukeśī saṁhatastanī
naiva devī na gandharvī na yakṣī na ca kiṁnarī

translations.english: The lock of your hair is exquisitely fine, your breast very close and your waist is so thin that they may be got round even by fingers. There is none so beautiful like you-a Goddess, a Gandharvi, a Yaksi or a Kinnari.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवंरूपा मया नारी दृष्टपूर्वा महीतले
इह वासश्च कान्तारे चित्तमुन्माथयन्ति मे
verses.transliteration:
naivaṁrūpā mayā nārī dṛṣṭapūrvā mahītale
iha vāsaśca kāntāre cittamunmāthayanti me

translations.english: I had never seen before on this earth a damsel so beautiful as you. This your beauty the best on earth, your youth, your grace and your abode in the forest do agitate my mind. So it is well for you to come (with me); it does not behove you to remain here.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रासादाग्र्याणि रम्याणि नगरोपवनानि च
संपन्नानि सुगन्धीनि युक्तान्याचरितुं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
prāsādāgryāṇi ramyāṇi nagaropavanāni ca
saṁpannāni sugandhīni yuktānyācarituṁ tvayā

translations.english: This is the abode of terrible Rākşasas wearing shapes at will. Picturesque palaces, prosperous cities and sweet-smelling gardens are worthy of your abode.

verses.sanskrit:
वरं माल्यं वरं पानं वरं वस्त्रं च शोभने
भर्तारं च वरं मन्ये त्वद्युक्तमसितेक्षणे
verses.transliteration:
varaṁ mālyaṁ varaṁ pānaṁ varaṁ vastraṁ ca śobhane
bhartāraṁ ca varaṁ manye tvadyuktamasitekṣaṇe

translations.english: O you of dark-blue eyes, fine is your garland, fine is the sinell of your person and fine is your apparel-me-thinks fine is your husband too.

verses.sanskrit:
का त्वं भवसि रुद्राणां मरुतां वा शुचिस्मिते
वसूनां वा वरारोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे
verses.transliteration:
kā tvaṁ bhavasi rudrāṇāṁ marutāṁ vā śucismite
vasūnāṁ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me

translations.english: O you of pure smile! whom do you belong to?-Rudras, Marutas, or Vasus-Meseems, O fine damsel you are a very gooddes.

verses.sanskrit:
नेह गच्छन्ती गन्धर्वा न देवा न च किंनराः
राक्षसानामयं वासः कथं नु त्वमिहागता
verses.transliteration:
neha gacchantī gandharvā na devā na ca kiṁnarāḥ
rākṣasānāmayaṁ vāsaḥ kathaṁ nu tvamihāgatā

translations.english: No one comes here—the Gandharvas, the celestials or Kinnaras; this is an abode of the Rākşasa how do you come here.

verses.sanskrit:
इह शाखामृगाः सिंहा द्वीपिव्याघ्रमृगास्तथा
ऋक्षास्तरक्षवः कङ्काः कथं तेभ्यो न बिभ्यसे
verses.transliteration:
iha śākhāmṛgāḥ siṁhā dvīpivyāghramṛgāstathā
ṛkṣāstarakṣavaḥ kaṅkāḥ kathaṁ tebhyo na bibhyase

translations.english: Are you not afraid of these monkeys, lions, tigers, wolves bears, herons and hyenas?

verses.sanskrit:
मदान्वितानां घोराणां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्
कथमेका महारण्ये न बिभेषि वनानने
verses.transliteration:
madānvitānāṁ ghorāṇāṁ kuñjarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
kathamekā mahāraṇye na bibheṣi vanānane

translations.english: Alone in this forest, are you not afraid of these terrible elephants of fierce motion and maddened with the exuding of their temporal juice?

verses.sanskrit:
कासि कस्य कुतश्च त्वं किंनिमित्तं च दण्डकान्
एका चरसि कल्याणि घोरान्राक्षससेवितान्
verses.transliteration:
kāsi kasya kutaśca tvaṁ kiṁnimittaṁ ca daṇḍakān
ekā carasi kalyāṇi ghorānrākṣasasevitān

translations.english: Who are you? Whose wife? What for do you range alone in this forest of Dandaka frequented by terrible Rākşasas?

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रशस्ता वैदेही रावणेन दुरात्मना
द्विजातिवेषेण हि तं दृष्ट्वा रावणमागतम्
सर्वैरतिथिसत्कारैः पूजयामास मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
iti praśastā vaidehī rāvaṇena durātmanā
dvijātiveṣeṇa hi taṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇamāgatam
sarvairatithisatkāraiḥ pūjayāmāsa maithilī

translations.english: Thus addressed was Vaidehĩ by the vicious souled Rāvana. Seeing him come under the guise of a twice-born one, Maithelee worshipped him with diverse articles necessary for serving a guest.

verses.sanskrit:
उपानीयासनं पूर्वं पाद्येनाभिनिमन्त्र्य च
अब्रवीत्सिद्धमित्येव तदा तं सौम्यदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
upānīyāsanaṁ pūrvaṁ pādyenābhinimantrya ca
abravītsiddhamityeva tadā taṁ saumyadarśanam

translations.english: Offering him a seat first and afterwards inviting him to wash his feet she said to that one of placid look cooked rice is ready.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विजातिवेषेण समीक्ष्य मैथिली; तमागतं पात्रकुसुम्भधारिणम्
अशक्यमुद्द्वेष्टुमुपायदर्शना;न्न्यमन्त्रयद्ब्राह्मणवद्यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
dvijātiveṣeṇa samīkṣya maithilī; tamāgataṁ pātrakusumbhadhāriṇam
aśakyamuddveṣṭumupāyadarśanā;nnyamantrayadbrāhmaṇavadyathāgatam

translations.english: Seeing Rāvaņa approach with Kamandalu and wearing a red cloth under the guise of a Brāhmana, Maithelee could not pass by him any way, and considering him a twice-born one by various signs invited him as if a Brāhmana,

verses.sanskrit:
इयं बृसी ब्राह्मण काममास्यता;मिदं च पाद्यं प्रतिगृह्यतामिति
इदं च सिद्धं वनजातमुत्तमं; त्वदर्थमव्यग्रमिहोपभुज्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ bṛsī brāhmaṇa kāmamāsyatā;midaṁ ca pādyaṁ pratigṛhyatāmiti
idaṁ ca siddhaṁ vanajātamuttamaṁ; tvadarthamavyagramihopabhujyatām

translations.english: O Brāhmana, do you sit on this seat facing the right; do you take this water to wash your feet); do you enjoy these well-cooked eatables growing in the forest and intended for you.

verses.sanskrit:
निमन्त्र्यमाणः प्रतिपूर्णभाषिणीं; नरेन्द्रपत्नीं प्रसमीक्ष्य मैथिलीम्
प्रहस्य तस्या हरणे धृतं मनः; समर्पयामास वधाय रावणः
verses.transliteration:
nimantryamāṇaḥ pratipūrṇabhāṣiṇīṁ; narendrapatnīṁ prasamīkṣya maithilīm
prahasya tasyā haraṇe dhṛtaṁ manaḥ; samarpayāmāsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Jānakí the wife of Lord of men inviting him thus, Ravana, casting a look upon her, addressed himself for his own destruction, to carry her away.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुवेषं मृगया गतं पतिं; प्रतीक्षमाणा सहलक्ष्मणं तदा
निरीक्षमाणा हरितं ददर्श त;न्महद्वनं नैव तु रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suveṣaṁ mṛgayā gataṁ patiṁ; pratīkṣamāṇā sahalakṣmaṇaṁ tadā
nirīkṣamāṇā haritaṁ dadarśa ta;nmahadvanaṁ naiva tu rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: She was anxiously expecting the return of Rāma who had gone a-hunting with Lakşmaņa; she looked around and beheld but on all sides the spacious yellow forest-land-~-there was neither Rāma nor Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेन तु वैदेही तदा पृष्टा जिहीर्षुणा
परिव्राजकरूपेण शशंसात्मानमात्मना
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇena tu vaidehī tadā pṛṣṭā jihīrṣuṇā
parivrājakarūpeṇa śaśaṁsātmānamātmanā

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Rāvaņa under the guise of a mendicant, desirous of carrying her away Vaidehī thought within herself.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणश्चातिथिश्चैष अनुक्तो हि शपेत माम्
इति ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु सीता वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇaścātithiścaiṣa anukto hi śapeta mām
iti dhyātvā muhūrtaṁ tu sītā vacanamabravīt

translations.english: This person is my guest and a Brahmin; he may curse me if I do not speak to him. Thinking this for a moment Sītā said.

verses.sanskrit:
दुहिता जनकस्याहं मैथिलस्य महात्मनः
सीता नाम्नास्मि भद्रं ते रामभार्या द्विजोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
duhitā janakasyāhaṁ maithilasya mahātmanaḥ
sītā nāmnāsmi bhadraṁ te rāmabhāryā dvijottama

translations.english: May good betide you! I am the daughter of the high-souled Janaka, the king of Mithilā, the beloved Queen of Rāma and my name is Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
संवत्सरं चाध्युषिता राघवस्य निवेशने
भुञ्जाना मानुषान्भोगान्सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी
verses.transliteration:
saṁvatsaraṁ cādhyuṣitā rāghavasya niveśane
bhuñjānā mānuṣānbhogānsarvakāmasamṛddhinī

translations.english: Dwelling in the palace of Ikşäkus for twelve years, I enjoyed many things passing human and had all my desires satisfied.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संवत्सरादूर्ध्वं सममन्यत मे पतिम्
अभिषेचयितुं रामं समेतो राजमन्त्रिभिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁvatsarādūrdhvaṁ samamanyata me patim
abhiṣecayituṁ rāmaṁ sameto rājamantribhiḥ

translations.english: On the thirteenth year king (Dasaratha) counselled with his ministers about the installation of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्संभ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने
कैकेयी नाम भर्तारं ममार्या याचते वरम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminsaṁbhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasyābhiṣecane
kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṁ mamāryā yācate varam

translations.english: Accordingly everything necessary for the installation being made ready, KaikeyI, one of my mothers-in-law, begged of her husband a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य तु कैकेयी श्वशुरं सुकृतेन मे
मम प्रव्राजनं भर्तुर्भरतस्याभिषेचनम्
द्वावयाचत भर्तारं सत्यसंधं नृपोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya tu kaikeyī śvaśuraṁ sukṛtena me
mama pravrājanaṁ bharturbharatasyābhiṣecanam
dvāvayācata bhartāraṁ satyasaṁdhaṁ nṛpottamam

translations.english: Bringing my father-in-law under control by means of her virtuous deeds, Kaikeyi begged, of that truthful, best of monarchs, two boons namely the exile of my husband into woods and the installation of Bharata,

verses.sanskrit:
नाद्य भोक्ष्ये न च स्वप्स्ये न पास्येऽहं कदाचन
एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
nādya bhokṣye na ca svapsye na pāsye'haṁ kadācana
eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yadyabhiṣicyate

translations.english: And said-I shall never eat, drink or sleep and (if Rāma be installed) I shall end my life.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणां कैकेयीं श्वशुरो मे स मानदः
अयाचतार्थैरन्वर्थैर्न च याच्ञां चकार सा
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇāṁ kaikeyīṁ śvaśuro me sa mānadaḥ
ayācatārthairanvarthairna ca yācñāṁ cakāra sā

translations.english: Kaikeyī speaking thus, that lord of earth, my father-in-law begged her to accept diverse riches; but Kaikeyi did not agree.

verses.sanskrit:
मम भर्ता महातेजा वयसा पञ्चविंशकः
रामेति प्रथितो लोके गुणवान्सत्यवाक्शुचिः
विशालाक्षो महाबाहुः सर्वभूतहिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
mama bhartā mahātejā vayasā pañcaviṁśakaḥ
rāmeti prathito loke guṇavānsatyavākśuciḥ
viśālākṣo mahābāhuḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ

translations.english: My husband is known all over the world under the name of Rāma he is truthful, goodnatured, of pure character, ever engaged in the welfare of all created beings, of mighty-arms and expansive eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिषेकाय तु पितुः समीपं राममागतम्
कैकेयी मम भर्तारमित्युवाच द्रुतं वचः
verses.transliteration:
abhiṣekāya tu pituḥ samīpaṁ rāmamāgatam
kaikeyī mama bhartāramityuvāca drutaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: When Rāma came to his father for being installed Kaikeyi spoke to my husband the following cruel words.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया तु खलु वस्तव्यं नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च
वने प्रव्रज काकुत्स्थ पितरं मोचयानृतात्
verses.transliteration:
tvayā tu khalu vastavyaṁ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
vane pravraja kākutstha pitaraṁ mocayānṛtāt

translations.english: Do you hear, O Rāghava, how I have been ordered by your Sire. This kingdom, rid of thorns is to be conferred of Bharata, and you shall have to sojourn into woods for years nine and five. Do you therefore repair to forest, O Kākutstha and save your Sire from untruth.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेत्युवाच तां रामः कैकेयीमकुतोभयः
चकार तद्वचस्तस्या मम भर्ता दृढव्रतः
verses.transliteration:
tathetyuvāca tāṁ rāmaḥ kaikeyīmakutobhayaḥ
cakāra tadvacastasyā mama bhartā dṛḍhavrataḥ

translations.english: Whereto Rāma fearlessly replied 'So be it!' Hearing her words my husband of firm vows acted accordingly.

verses.sanskrit:
दद्यान्न प्रतिगृह्णीयात्सत्यब्रूयान्न चानृतम्
एतद्ब्राह्मण रामस्य व्रतं ध्रुवमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
dadyānna pratigṛhṇīyātsatyabrūyānna cānṛtam
etadbrāhmaṇa rāmasya vrataṁ dhruvamanuttamam

translations.english: He always maketh gifts and taketh none. He always speaketh truth and never telleth an untruth. This is his best observance O Brāhmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य भ्राता तु वैमात्रो लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्
रामस्य पुरुषव्याघ्रः सहायः समरेऽरिहा
verses.transliteration:
tasya bhrātā tu vaimātro lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
rāmasya puruṣavyāghraḥ sahāyaḥ samare'rihā

translations.english: His half-brother named Lakşmaņa is of mighty prowess. That best of men is Rāma's help and the destroyer of foes in battle. That brother of his named Lakşmaņa is of firm resolution and given to asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
स भ्राता लक्ष्मणो नाम धर्मचारी दृढव्रतः
अन्वगच्छद्धनुष्पाणिः प्रव्रजन्तं मया सह
verses.transliteration:
sa bhrātā lakṣmaṇo nāma dharmacārī dṛḍhavrataḥ
anvagacchaddhanuṣpāṇiḥ pravrajantaṁ mayā saha

translations.english: With a bow in hand he has followed (Rama) flying as an exile to woods along with me. Thus that one (Rāma) of firm resolution and ever engaged in pious offices wearing matted hair and assuming the semblance of an ascetic has entered this forest of Dandaka along with myself and his younger brother,

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवत्यां सीतायां रामपत्न्यां महाबलः
प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं तीव्रं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvatyāṁ sītāyāṁ rāmapatnyāṁ mahābalaḥ
pratyuvācottaraṁ tīvraṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: Sītā the wife of Rāma speaking thus, the mighty Lord of Rākşasas-Rävana replied with these harsh words,

verses.sanskrit:
येन वित्रासिता लोकाः सदेवासुरपन्नगाः
अहं स रावणो नाम सीते रक्षोगणेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
yena vitrāsitā lokāḥ sadevāsurapannagāḥ
ahaṁ sa rāvaṇo nāma sīte rakṣogaṇeśvaraḥ

translations.english: O Sītā I am that Rāvaņa, the lord of Rākşasas, whoin fear the celestials, Asuras and human beings.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां तु काञ्चनवर्णाभां दृष्ट्वा कौशेयवासिनीम्
रतिं स्वकेषु दारेषु नाधिगच्छाम्यनिन्दिते
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ tu kāñcanavarṇābhāṁ dṛṣṭvā kauśeyavāsinīm
ratiṁ svakeṣu dāreṣu nādhigacchāmyanindite

translations.english: O you of blameless beauty, seeing you of golden hue and wearing silk cloth I do not relish my own wives.

verses.sanskrit:
बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणामाहृतानामितस्ततः
सर्वासामेव भद्रं ते ममाग्रमहिषी भव
verses.transliteration:
bahvīnāmuttamastrīṇāmāhṛtānāmitastataḥ
sarvāsāmeva bhadraṁ te mamāgramahiṣī bhava

translations.english: I have brought many a beautiful damsel from various quarters, do you become my foremost Queen among them.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्का नाम समुद्रस्य मध्ये मम महापुरी
सागरेण परिक्षिप्ता निविष्टा गिरिमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
laṅkā nāma samudrasya madhye mama mahāpurī
sāgareṇa parikṣiptā niviṣṭā girimūrdhani

translations.english: That great city in the midst of the ocean, Larkā, encircled on all sides by the sea and situated on the summit of a hill, is my capital.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र सीते मया सार्धं वनेषु विचरिष्यसि
न चास्यारण्यवासस्य स्पृहयिष्यसि भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
tatra sīte mayā sārdhaṁ vaneṣu vicariṣyasi
na cāsyāraṇyavāsasya spṛhayiṣyasi bhāmini

translations.english: There shall you with me, O Sītā, walk in gardens, and thus you shall no more long for living in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चदास्यः सहस्राणि सर्वाभरणभूषिताः
सीते परिचरिष्यन्ति भार्या भवसि मे यदि
verses.transliteration:
pañcadāsyaḥ sahasrāṇi sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
sīte paricariṣyanti bhāryā bhavasi me yadi

translations.english: If you did become my wife, O Sītā, five thousand maid-servants decorated with divers ornaments shall serve you.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेनैवमुक्ता तु कुपिता जनकात्मजा
प्रत्युवाचानवद्याङ्गी तमनादृत्य राक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇenaivamuktā tu kupitā janakātmajā
pratyuvācānavadyāṅgī tamanādṛtya rākṣasaṁ

translations.english: That blameless daughter of Janaka, being thus addressed by Ravana, was highly enraged, and, passing by him, replied.

verses.sanskrit:
महागिरिमिवाकम्प्यं महेन्द्रसदृशं पतिम्
महोदधिमिवाक्षोभ्यमहं राममनुव्रता
verses.transliteration:
mahāgirimivākampyaṁ mahendrasadṛśaṁ patim
mahodadhimivākṣobhyamahaṁ rāmamanuvratā

translations.english: I am a dependant of Rāma, who is incapable of being, shaken, like to a mighty mountain, incapable of being agitated, like to a vast ocean, and resembling Mahendra in effulgence.

verses.sanskrit:
महाबाहुं महोरस्कं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्
नृसिंहं सिंहसंकाशमहं राममनुव्रता
verses.transliteration:
mahābāhuṁ mahoraskaṁ siṁhavikrāntagāminam
nṛsiṁhaṁ siṁhasaṁkāśamahaṁ rāmamanuvratā

translations.english: I am a dependant of that lion among men, Rāma, of mighty arms, of a spacious breast an treading like a lion.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्णचन्द्राननं वीरं राजवत्सं जितेन्द्रियम्
पृथुकीर्तिं महाबाहुमहं राममनुव्रता
verses.transliteration:
pūrṇacandrānanaṁ vīraṁ rājavatsaṁ jitendriyam
pṛthukīrtiṁ mahābāhumahaṁ rāmamanuvratā

translations.english: I am a dependant of that son of a king, Rāma, of mighty arms, having control over his passions, whose face resembles the full moon and whose fame has spread far and wide over the earth.36

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं पुनर्जम्बुकः सिंहीं मामिहेच्छसि दुर्लभाम्
नाहं शक्या त्वया स्प्रष्टुमादित्यस्य प्रभा यथा
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ punarjambukaḥ siṁhīṁ māmihecchasi durlabhām
nāhaṁ śakyā tvayā spraṣṭumādityasya prabhā yathā

translations.english: Why do you being a tiger wish for a she-lion? You shall not be able to touch me like to the rays of the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
पादपान्काञ्चनान्नूनं बहून्पश्यसि मन्दभाक्
राघवस्य प्रियां भार्यां यस्त्वमिच्छसि रावण
verses.transliteration:
pādapānkāñcanānnūnaṁ bahūnpaśyasi mandabhāk
rāghavasya priyāṁ bhāryāṁ yastvamicchasi rāvaṇa

translations.english: O you wretched Rākşasa, when you have desired to steal away Raghhava's beloved spouse, surely do you see these trees (before you) as made of gold.

verses.sanskrit:
अक्षिसूच्या प्रमृजसि जिह्वया लेढि च क्षुरम्
राघवस्य प्रियां भार्यामधिगन्तुं त्वमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
akṣisūcyā pramṛjasi jihvayā leḍhi ca kṣuram
rāghavasya priyāṁ bhāryāmadhigantuṁ tvamicchasi

translations.english: Do you wish to uproot the teeth from the mouth of a lion, that enemy of deer, or from that of a serpent? Do you wish to clasp with your hands the Mandara hill, or do you wish to walk in peace after drinking poison? Do you wish to rub your eyes with pins and lick a razor with your tongue?

verses.sanskrit:
अवसज्य शिलां कण्ठे समुद्रं तर्तुमिच्छसि
सूर्या चन्द्रमसौ चोभौ प्राणिभ्यां हर्तुमिच्छसि
यो रामस्य प्रियां भार्यां प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
avasajya śilāṁ kaṇṭhe samudraṁ tartumicchasi
sūryā candramasau cobhau prāṇibhyāṁ hartumicchasi
yo rāmasya priyāṁ bhāryāṁ pradharṣayitumicchasi

translations.english: You did wish to swim across an ocean, having a rock tied to your neck. You did wish to get at the Sun and Moon, to bind a flaming fire with a piece of cloth and walk through iron-spikes, as you have wished to come by the worthy spouse of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव तद्वाक्यमदुष्टभावा; सुदृष्टमुक्त्वा रजनीचरं तम्
गात्रप्रकम्पाद्व्यथिता बभूव; वातोद्धता सा कदलीव तन्वी
verses.transliteration:
itīva tadvākyamaduṣṭabhāvā; sudṛṣṭamuktvā rajanīcaraṁ tam
gātraprakampādvyathitā babhūva; vātoddhatā sā kadalīva tanvī

translations.english: Addressing those words to that wicked ranger of the night, that innocent ($ītā) shook like a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
तां वेपमानामुपलक्ष्य सीतां; स रावणो मृत्युसमप्रभावः
कुलं बलं नाम च कर्म चात्मनः; समाचचक्षे भयकारणार्थम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ vepamānāmupalakṣya sītāṁ; sa rāvaṇo mṛtyusamaprabhāvaḥ
kulaṁ balaṁ nāma ca karma cātmanaḥ; samācacakṣe bhayakāraṇārtham

translations.english: There upon Rāvaņa, like to Death in prowess, trembling, began to relate to her with a view to frighten (her) his race, power, name and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवत्यां सीतायां संरब्धः परुषाक्षरम्
ललाटे भ्रुकुटीं कृत्वा रावणः प्रत्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvatyāṁ sītāyāṁ saṁrabdhaḥ paruṣākṣaram
lalāṭe bhrukuṭīṁ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha

translations.english: After Sītā had spoken these harsh words, Rāvana, enraged, with a frown, replied.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्राता वैश्रवणस्याहं सापत्न्यो वरवर्णिनि
रावणो नाम भद्रं ते दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātā vaiśravaṇasyāhaṁ sāpatnyo varavarṇini
rāvaṇo nāma bhadraṁ te daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān

translations.english: O you of a beatiful countenance, I am the step-brother of the Lord of wealth and my name is the mighty Ten-necked Rāvana May good betide you!

verses.sanskrit:
येन वैश्रवणो भ्राता वैमात्रः कारणान्तरे
द्वन्द्वमासादितः क्रोधाद्रणे विक्रम्य निर्जितः
verses.transliteration:
yena vaiśravaṇo bhrātā vaimātraḥ kāraṇāntare
dvandvamāsāditaḥ krodhādraṇe vikramya nirjitaḥ

translations.english: Like to people fearing Death, the celestials, Gandharvas, Piśāchas, Pannagas and Serpents fly in diverse directions being frightened by me. I have subdued by my prowess, my step-brother, the Lord of wealth in a conflict, quarrelling with him for some reason.

verses.sanskrit:
मद्भयार्तः परित्यज्य स्वमधिष्ठानमृद्धिमत्
कैलासं पर्वतश्रेष्ठमध्यास्ते नरवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
madbhayārtaḥ parityajya svamadhiṣṭhānamṛddhimat
kailāsaṁ parvataśreṣṭhamadhyāste naravāhanaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, that one carried by men, renouncing out of my fear this wealthy abode of Lankā, has been living on that Lord of mountains, Kailāśa.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य तत्पुष्पकं नाम विमानं कामगं शुभम्
वीर्यादावर्जितं भद्रे येन यामि विहायसं
verses.transliteration:
yasya tatpuṣpakaṁ nāma vimānaṁ kāmagaṁ śubham
vīryādāvarjitaṁ bhadre yena yāmi vihāyasaṁ

translations.english: O you auspicious one, by virtue of my prowess I have taken away that beautiful chariot of his called Puspaka. Ascending that chariot you shall travei by the ethereal route.

verses.sanskrit:
मम संजातरोषस्य मुखं दृष्ट्वैव मैथिलि
विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्ताः सुराः शक्रपुरोगमाः
verses.transliteration:
mama saṁjātaroṣasya mukhaṁ dṛṣṭvaiva maithili
vidravanti paritrastāḥ surāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ

translations.english: O Maithilee, when I am excited with ire, Indra and other celestials at the mere sight of my countenance fly away in divers directions out of fear.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र तिष्ठाम्यहं तत्र मारुतो वाति शङ्कितः
तीव्रांशुः शिशिरांशुश्च भयात्संपद्यते रविः
verses.transliteration:
yatra tiṣṭhāmyahaṁ tatra māruto vāti śaṅkitaḥ
tīvrāṁśuḥ śiśirāṁśuśca bhayātsaṁpadyate raviḥ

translations.english: Wherever I live, the Wind bloweth cautiously and the Sun (of piercing rays) out of fear for me appeareth in the welkin like the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्कम्पपत्रास्तरवो नद्यश्च स्तिमितोदकाः
भवन्ति यत्र यत्राहं तिष्ठामि च चरामि च
verses.transliteration:
niṣkampapatrāstaravo nadyaśca stimitodakāḥ
bhavanti yatra yatrāhaṁ tiṣṭhāmi ca carāmi ca

translations.english: What shall I say more? Wherever I live, even the leaves of the trees do not flutter and the currents of the rivers are stopped.

verses.sanskrit:
मम पारे समुद्रस्य लङ्का नाम पुरी शुभा
संपूर्णा राक्षसैर्घोरैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती
verses.transliteration:
mama pāre samudrasya laṅkā nāma purī śubhā
saṁpūrṇā rākṣasairghorairyathendrasyāmarāvatī

translations.english: Beyond the ocean stands my beautiful capital Larikā like to Indra's Amaravati, (the capital of the Lord of celestials), guarded on all sides by the terrible night-rangers and encircled by yellow walls.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राकारेण परिक्षिप्ता पाण्डुरेण विराजिता
हेमकक्ष्या पुरी रम्या वैदूर्यमय तोरणा
verses.transliteration:
prākāreṇa parikṣiptā pāṇḍureṇa virājitā
hemakakṣyā purī ramyā vaidūryamaya toraṇā

translations.english: That beautiful city has gate-ways of ornamented and jewelled arches and golden apartinents.

verses.sanskrit:
हस्त्यश्वरथसंभाधा तूर्यनादविनादिता
सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैः संकुलोद्यानशोभिता
verses.transliteration:
hastyaśvarathasaṁbhādhā tūryanādavināditā
sarvakāmaphalairvṛkṣaiḥ saṁkulodyānaśobhitā

translations.english: It is filled with clephants, horses and chariots, always resounds with the sounds of bugles, and is beautified with gardens having divers trees of wished-for fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र त्वं वसती सीते राजपुत्रि मया सह
न स्रमिष्यसि नारीणां मानुषीणां मनस्विनि
verses.transliteration:
tatra tvaṁ vasatī sīte rājaputri mayā saha
na sramiṣyasi nārīṇāṁ mānuṣīṇāṁ manasvini

translations.english: O Sītā, O you the daughter of a king, in this city shall you dwell with me. O large-minded damsel, you shall never think of earthly women.

verses.sanskrit:
भुञ्जाना मानुषान्भोगान्दिव्यांश्च वरवर्णिनि
न स्मरिष्यसि रामस्य मानुषस्य गतायुषः
verses.transliteration:
bhuñjānā mānuṣānbhogāndivyāṁśca varavarṇini
na smariṣyasi rāmasya mānuṣasya gatāyuṣaḥ

translations.english: O you of an exquisite countenance, enjoying these many things passing human, you shall not any more think of Rāma a human being of brief existence.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन किं भ्रष्टराज्येन रामेण गतचेतसा
करिष्यसि विशालाक्षि तापसेन तपस्विना
verses.transliteration:
tena kiṁ bhraṣṭarājyena rāmeṇa gatacetasā
kariṣyasi viśālākṣi tāpasena tapasvinā

translations.english: Placing his beloved son on the throne, king Dasaratha has sent away his eldest son of weak prowess into the woods. O you of expansive eyes, what shall you do with that wretched ascetic Rāma who has been deprived of his kingdom?

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वराक्षसभर्तारं कामात्स्वयमिहागतम्
न मन्मथशराविष्टं प्रत्याख्यातुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
sarvarākṣasabhartāraṁ kāmātsvayamihāgatam
na manmathaśarāviṣṭaṁ pratyākhyātuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: I am the lord of the whole world of Rākşasas; being pierced by the shafts of Kāma have I come by you. It does not behave you therefore to pass by me.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्याख्याय हि मां भीरु परितापं गमिष्यसि
चरणेनाभिहत्येव पुरूरवसमुर्वशी
verses.transliteration:
pratyākhyāya hi māṁ bhīru paritāpaṁ gamiṣyasi
caraṇenābhihatyeva purūravasamurvaśī

translations.english: O timid damsel, truly shall you repent afterwards if you did disregard me, like to Urvasi kicking Pururavā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही क्रुद्धा संरक्तलोचना
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं रहिते राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu vaidehī kruddhā saṁraktalocanā
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ rahite rākṣasādhipam

translations.english: Rāma is a human being and is not even equal to a finger of mine in battle. By your good luck have I come to you-do you give yourself up to me, O you of a beautiful countenance. Being thus addressed by him, Vaidehi exceedingly wroth and with blood-red eyes spoke to that Lord of Rākşasas in the lonely forest, these bold words.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं वैश्रवणं देवं सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्
भ्रातरं व्यपदिश्य त्वमशुभं कर्तुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ vaiśravaṇaṁ devaṁ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam
bhrātaraṁ vyapadiśya tvamaśubhaṁ kartumicchasi

translations.english: How do you wish to perpetrate such an impious deed after introducing as your brother that highly worshipful Kubera adored by all the deities.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं विनशिष्यन्ति सर्वे रावण राक्षसाः
येषां त्वं कर्कशो राजा दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ vinaśiṣyanti sarve rāvaṇa rākṣasāḥ
yeṣāṁ tvaṁ karkaśo rājā durbuddhirajitendriyaḥ

translations.english: All the Rākşasas shall surely die, O Rāvana whose lord are you, foolish, cruel and under the control of your passions.

verses.sanskrit:
अपहृत्य शचीं भार्यां शक्यमिन्द्रस्य जीवितुम्
न तु रामस्य भार्यां मामपनीयास्ति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
apahṛtya śacīṁ bhāryāṁ śakyamindrasya jīvitum
na tu rāmasya bhāryāṁ māmapanīyāsti jīvitam

translations.english: One can breathe on this earth carrying away Indra's wife, Śacī—but stealing me, the wife of Rāma, no body shall be able to live in peace.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवेच्चिरं वज्रधरस्य हस्ता;च्छचीं प्रधृष्याप्रतिरूपरूपाम्
न मादृशीं राक्षसधर्षयित्वा; पीतामृतस्यापि तवास्ति मोक्षः
verses.transliteration:
jīvecciraṁ vajradharasya hastā;cchacīṁ pradhṛṣyāpratirūparūpām
na mādṛśīṁ rākṣasadharṣayitvā; pītāmṛtasyāpi tavāsti mokṣaḥ

translations.english: O Räkşasa, it might be possible for one to live on this earth treating contemptuously the wife of the holder of thunder-bolt, but insulting me none shall escape the hands of Death even if he drinketh nectar.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्
हस्ते हस्तं समाहत्य चकार सुमहद्वपुः
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān
haste hastaṁ samāhatya cakāra sumahadvapuḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of Sītā the highly powerful Ten necked one striking his hands together, increased his body too high.

verses.sanskrit:
स मैथिलीं पुनर्वाक्यं बभाषे च ततो भृशम्
नोन्मत्तया श्रुतौ मन्ये मम वीर्यपराक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
sa maithilīṁ punarvākyaṁ babhāṣe ca tato bhṛśam
nonmattayā śrutau manye mama vīryaparākramau

translations.english: Thereupon, that one skilled in speech again spake to Maithili, Methinks you have run mad. Have you not heard of my valour and prowess?

verses.sanskrit:
उद्वहेयं भुजाभ्यां तु मेदिनीमम्बरे स्थितः
आपिबेयं समुद्रं च मृत्युं हन्यां रणे स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
udvaheyaṁ bhujābhyāṁ tu medinīmambare sthitaḥ
āpibeyaṁ samudraṁ ca mṛtyuṁ hanyāṁ raṇe sthitaḥ

translations.english: Stationing myself in the welkin I can with my hands raise up the earth. I can drink up the waters of the ocean. And engaged in conflict I can destroy Death itself

verses.sanskrit:
अर्कं रुन्ध्यां शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विभिन्द्यां हि महीतलम्
कामरूपिणमुन्मत्ते पश्य मां कामदं पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
arkaṁ rundhyāṁ śaraistīkṣṇairvibhindyāṁ hi mahītalam
kāmarūpiṇamunmatte paśya māṁ kāmadaṁ patim

translations.english: With my sharpened shafts I can pierce the Sun and cut asunder the earth. You are mad with your beauty. Do you look upon me, who am capable of illusions.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तवतस्तस्य रावणस्य शिखिप्रभे
क्रुद्धस्य हरिपर्यन्ते रक्ते नेत्रे बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktavatastasya rāvaṇasya śikhiprabhe
kruddhasya hariparyante rakte netre babhūvatuḥ

translations.english: When he had spoken thus, his yellow eyes became blood-red with rage and assumed the, semblance of flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
सद्यः सौम्यं परित्यज्य भिक्षुरूपं स रावणः
स्वं रूपं कालरूपाभं भेजे वैश्रवणानुजः
verses.transliteration:
sadyaḥ saumyaṁ parityajya bhikṣurūpaṁ sa rāvaṇaḥ
svaṁ rūpaṁ kālarūpābhaṁ bheje vaiśravaṇānujaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Răvana, the younger brother of the Lord of wealth, changing his placid countenance, instantly assumed his own terrible shape resembling that of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
संरक्तनयनः क्रोधाज्जीमूतनिचयप्रभः
रक्ताम्बरधरस्तस्थौ स्त्रीरत्नं प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁraktanayanaḥ krodhājjīmūtanicayaprabhaḥ
raktāmbaradharastasthau strīratnaṁ prekṣya maithilīm

translations.english: Leaving aside the semblance of a mendicant, that lord of Raksasas, Ravana, increasing in bulk, assumed his own shape. And wearing a blood-red cloth he stood there fixing his look upon that jewel of a damsel–Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यदि भर्तारमिच्छसि
मामाश्रय वरारोहे तवाहं सदृशः पतिः
verses.transliteration:
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṁ yadi bhartāramicchasi
māmāśraya varārohe tavāhaṁ sadṛśaḥ patiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Rāvaņa spake to Mathili like to the rays of the sun, having a head of black hair and wearing apparel and ornaments, saying, O you fine damsel, if you did wish to have a husband known all over the world, do you surrender yourself to me.

verses.sanskrit:
मां भजस्व चिराय त्वमहं श्लाघ्यस्तव प्रियः
नैव चाहं क्वचिद्भद्रे करिष्ये तव विप्रियम्
त्यज्यतां मानुषो भावो मयि भावः प्रणीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
māṁ bhajasva cirāya tvamahaṁ ślāghyastava priyaḥ
naiva cāhaṁ kvacidbhadre kariṣye tava vipriyam
tyajyatāṁ mānuṣo bhāvo mayi bhāvaḥ praṇīyatām

translations.english: I am a worthy husband for you. Do you serve me for ever, your praiseworthy husband. O fine lady, I hall never do what you did not like.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्याच्च्युतमसिद्धार्थं रामं परिमितायुषम्
कैर्गुणैरनुरक्तासि मूढे पण्डितमानिनि
verses.transliteration:
rājyāccyutamasiddhārthaṁ rāmaṁ parimitāyuṣam
kairguṇairanuraktāsi mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini

translations.english: Renouncing your attachment for a man, do you place your love in me. O foolish girl, worthy of being adored by the learned, for what quality are you attached to Rāma of a limited life, who has been deprived of his kingdom and has his desire frustrated, and who of an evil intent, has, at the words of his wife, renouncing his kingdom and kinsmen, been living in this forest-the abode of voracious animals.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं वाक्यं प्रियार्हां प्रियवादिनीम्
जग्राह रावणः सीतां बुधः खे रोहिणीमिव
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā maithilīṁ vākyaṁ priyārhāṁ priyavādinīm
jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ sītāṁ budhaḥ khe rohiṇīmiva

translations.english: Speaking thus to Maithili, sweet-speeched and worthy of being sweetly addressed, that highly wicked Raksasa, Rāvaņa, being exercised with lust, approached towards Sītā and got hold of her, like to Budha holding Rohinī in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
वामेन सीतां पद्माक्षीं मूर्धजेषु करेण सः
ऊर्वोस्तु दक्षिणेनैव परिजग्राह पाणिना
verses.transliteration:
vāmena sītāṁ padmākṣīṁ mūrdhajeṣu kareṇa saḥ
ūrvostu dakṣiṇenaiva parijagrāha pāṇinā

translations.english: With his left hand he held her, having eyes like to lotus-petals, by the hair, and with his right hand got hold of her thighs.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गाभं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रं महाभुजम्
प्राद्रवन्मृत्युसंकाशं भयार्ता वनदेवताः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṁ tīkṣṇadaṁṣṭraṁ mahābhujam
prādravanmṛtyusaṁkāśaṁ bhayārtā vanadevatāḥ

translations.english: Seeing Rāvaņa of sharpened teeth, and mighty arms, resembling the summit of a mountain and like to death itself, the deities of the forest became highly terrified and fled in different directions.

verses.sanskrit:
स च मायामयो दिव्यः खरयुक्तः खरस्वनः
प्रत्यदृश्यत हेमाङ्गो रावणस्य महारथः
verses.transliteration:
sa ca māyāmayo divyaḥ kharayuktaḥ kharasvanaḥ
pratyadṛśyata hemāṅgo rāvaṇasya mahārathaḥ

translations.english: Instantly appeared there the celestial car of Ravana, decked in gold, drawn by asses and making a terrible sound.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तां परुषैर्वाक्यैरभितर्ज्य महास्वनः
अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीं रथमारोपयत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tatastāṁ paruṣairvākyairabhitarjya mahāsvanaḥ
aṅkenādāya vaidehīṁ rathamāropayattadā

translations.english: Thereupon, that one emmiting terrible accents, remonstrated with Vaidehī in harsh words and clasping her ascended the car.

verses.sanskrit:
सा गृहीतातिचुक्रोश रावणेन यशस्विनी
रामेति सीता दुःखार्ता रामं दूरगतं वने
verses.transliteration:
sā gṛhītāticukrośa rāvaṇena yaśasvinī
rāmeti sītā duḥkhārtā rāmaṁ dūragataṁ vane

translations.english: The virtuous Sīta, being thus caught by Ravana, began to cry aloud, addressing Rama, who had gone away to a distant forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तामकामां स कामार्तः पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव
विवेष्टमानामादाय उत्पपाथाथ रावणः
verses.transliteration:
tāmakāmāṁ sa kāmārtaḥ pannagendravadhūmiva
viveṣṭamānāmādāya utpapāthātha rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Rāvaņa, racked with lust, rose high up with her like to the wife of a Pannaga, though she tried her best (to get rid of him), for she was not in the least attached to him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सा राक्षसेन्द्रेण ह्रियमाणा विहायसा
भृशं चुक्रोश मत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्ता यथातुरा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sā rākṣasendreṇa hriyamāṇā vihāyasā
bhṛśaṁ cukrośa matteva bhrāntacittā yathāturā

translations.english: Being thus carried away by the ethereal track by that Lord of Rākṣasas, Sītā began to cry aloud, like one mad, distressed and of deranged senses.

verses.sanskrit:
हा लक्ष्मण महाबाहो गुरुचित्तप्रसादक
ह्रियमाणां न जानीषे रक्षसा कामरूपिणा
verses.transliteration:
hā lakṣmaṇa mahābāho gurucittaprasādaka
hriyamāṇāṁ na jānīṣe rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā

translations.english: Ah! mighty Laksmana, ever ministering to the satisfaction of your superiors, do you not know that I have been stolen away by a Rākṣasa assuming shapes at will?

verses.sanskrit:
जीवितं सुखमर्थांश्च धर्महेतोः परित्यजन्
ह्रियमाणामधर्मेण मां राघव न पश्यसि
verses.transliteration:
jīvitaṁ sukhamarthāṁśca dharmahetoḥ parityajan
hriyamāṇāmadharmeṇa māṁ rāghava na paśyasi

translations.english: O Rāghava, for virtue have you renounced your life, happiness and wealth,-do you not see that I have been carried away by one of mighty iniquity?

verses.sanskrit:
ननु नामाविनीतानां विनेतासि परंतप
कथमेवंविधं पापं न त्वं शाधि हि रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
nanu nāmāvinītānāṁ vinetāsi paraṁtapa
kathamevaṁvidhaṁ pāpaṁ na tvaṁ śādhi hi rāvaṇam

translations.english: O you the subduer of foes, you did always control the rebellious,-why do you not punish such a vicious Rākşasa?

verses.sanskrit:
ननु सद्योऽविनीतस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्
कालोऽप्यङ्गी भवत्यत्र सस्यानामिव पक्तये
verses.transliteration:
nanu sadyo'vinītasya dṛśyate karmaṇaḥ phalam
kālo'pyaṅgī bhavatyatra sasyānāmiva paktaye

translations.english: The vicious do not instantaneously meet with the fruits of their actions, as for corn to ripen requires the assistance of time.

verses.sanskrit:
स कर्म कृतवानेतत्कालोपहतचेतनः
जीवितान्तकरं घोरं रामाद्व्यसनमाप्नुहि
verses.transliteration:
sa karma kṛtavānetatkālopahatacetanaḥ
jīvitāntakaraṁ ghoraṁ rāmādvyasanamāpnuhi

translations.english: For this iniquitous deed, which you have perpetrated, availing of the time and losing your sense, you shall meet with a mighty disaster from Rāma, bringing about your end.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्तेदानीं सकामा तु कैकेयी बान्धवैः सह
ह्रियेयं धर्मकामस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
hantedānīṁ sakāmā tu kaikeyī bāndhavaiḥ saha
hriyeyaṁ dharmakāmasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinaḥ

translations.english: Ah! being the virtuous wife of the virtuous and far-famed Rāma, I have been stolen away. Now has the desire of Kaikeyi and other relations been fulfilled.

verses.sanskrit:
आमन्त्रये जनस्थानं कर्णिकारांश्च पुष्पितान्
क्षिप्रं रामाय शंसध्वं सीतां हरति रावणः
verses.transliteration:
āmantraye janasthānaṁ karṇikārāṁśca puṣpitān
kṣipraṁ rāmāya śaṁsadhvaṁ sītāṁ harati rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: I invoke this Janasthāna and these flowery Karnikās to tell Rāma that Rāvana has stolen away Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
हंससारससंघुष्टां वन्दे गोदावरीं नदीम्
क्षिप्रं रामाय शंसध्वं सीतां हरति रावणः
verses.transliteration:
haṁsasārasasaṁghuṣṭāṁ vande godāvarīṁ nadīm
kṣipraṁ rāmāya śaṁsadhvaṁ sītāṁ harati rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: I invoke you, O Godāvarī, having swans and cranes sporting in your stream, to tell Ráma that Rāvana has stolen away Sītã.

verses.sanskrit:
दैवतानि च यान्त्यस्मिन्वने विविधपादपे
नमस्करोम्यहं तेभ्यो भर्तुः शंसत मां हृताम्
verses.transliteration:
daivatāni ca yāntyasminvane vividhapādape
namaskaromyahaṁ tebhyo bhartuḥ śaṁsata māṁ hṛtām

translations.english: I salute and invoke the deities that live in this forest of many trees to tell my husband of my being stolen away (by Ravana).

verses.sanskrit:
ह्रियमाणां प्रियां भर्तुः प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम्
विवशापहृता सीता रावणेनेति शंसत
verses.transliteration:
hriyamāṇāṁ priyāṁ bhartuḥ prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasīm
vivaśāpahṛtā sītā rāvaṇeneti śaṁsata

translations.english: I do seek the refuge of all deer, birds and other animals that live in this forest, and may they all cominunicate to Rāma the news of his dear spouse being carried away, and tell him that Sītā, losing her control, has been stolen away by Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
विदित्वा मां महाबाहुरमुत्रापि महाबलः
आनेष्यति पराक्रम्य वैवस्वतहृतामपि
verses.transliteration:
viditvā māṁ mahābāhuramutrāpi mahābalaḥ
āneṣyati parākramya vaivasvatahṛtāmapi

translations.english: Even if I am taken away by Yama, and if the mighty-armed Rāma is apprised of it, surely shall he bring me back by the display of his prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
रामाय तु यथातत्त्वं जटायो हरणं मम
लक्ष्मणाय च तत्सर्वमाख्यातव्यमशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
rāmāya tu yathātattvaṁ jaṭāyo haraṇaṁ mama
lakṣmaṇāya ca tatsarvamākhyātavyamaśeṣataḥ

translations.english: Do you relate to Rāma and to Lakşmaņa everything about my being carried away from the beginning to the end.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शब्दमवसुप्तस्य जटायुरथ शुश्रुवे
निरैक्षद्रावणं क्षिप्रं वैदेहीं च ददर्श सः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śabdamavasuptasya jaṭāyuratha śuśruve
niraikṣadrāvaṇaṁ kṣipraṁ vaidehīṁ ca dadarśa saḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words Jațāyu, who lay buried in a deep slumber, awoke and beheld both Rāvana and Janaki.

verses.sanskrit:
