ततः पर्वतकूटाभस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डः खगोत्तमः
वनस्पतिगतः श्रीमान्व्याजहार शुभां गिरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ parvatakūṭābhastīkṣṇatuṇḍaḥ khagottamaḥ
vanaspatigataḥ śrīmānvyājahāra śubhāṁ giram

translations.english: There-at the lord of birds resting on the tree, having a big sharp beak like to the summit of a hill, addressed these soft words to Rāvana,

verses.sanskrit:
दशग्रीवस्थितो धर्मे पुराणे सत्यसंश्रयः
जटायुर्नाम नाम्नाहं गृध्रराजो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
daśagrīvasthito dharme purāṇe satyasaṁśrayaḥ
jaṭāyurnāma nāmnāhaṁ gṛdhrarājo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: O brother Ten-necked one, I am conversant with Purāņas, of truthful vows and abide by religion. It does not behove you to perpetrate such an iniquitous deed before me. I am Jātayu, the mighty lord of vultures.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः
लोकानां च हिते युक्तो रामो दशरथात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
rājā sarvasya lokasya mahendravaruṇopamaḥ
lokānāṁ ca hite yukto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ

translations.english: Daśaratha's son Rāma is the lord of all men like to Mahendra and Varuņa. He is ever engaged in the welfare of all men.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैषा लोकनाथस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनी
सीता नाम वरारोहा यां त्वं हर्तुमिहेच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
tasyaiṣā lokanāthasya dharmapatnī yaśasvinī
sītā nāma varārohā yāṁ tvaṁ hartumihecchasi

translations.english: This exquisitely beautiful and far-famed Sītā whom you are about to steal away, is the married wife of that lord of men.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं राजा स्थितो धर्मे परदारान्परामृशेत्
रक्षणीया विशेषेण राजदारा महाबलः
निवर्तय मतिं नीचां परदाराभिमर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ rājā sthito dharme paradārānparāmṛśet
rakṣaṇīyā viśeṣeṇa rājadārā mahābalaḥ
nivartaya matiṁ nīcāṁ paradārābhimarśanam

translations.english: How do you yourself being a monarch and engaged in the royal office of maintaining subjects, carry away by stealth another's wife? O you of mighty prowess, you should specially protect the wives of kings. Do you therefore control your base inclination of oppressing another's wife. A hero does never perform what bring calumny upon himself. It becometh every individual to save another's wife from the touch of a second man like to his own wife.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थं वा यदि वा कामं शिष्टाः शास्त्रेष्वनागतम्
व्यवस्यन्त्यनु राजानं धर्मं पौरस्त्यनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
arthaṁ vā yadi vā kāmaṁ śiṣṭāḥ śāstreṣvanāgatam
vyavasyantyanu rājānaṁ dharmaṁ paurastyanandana

translations.english: O son of Paulastya, at the instance of the king mild subjects perform many an action conducing to virtue, wealth and desire, though not mentioned in the Šāstras.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा धर्मश्च कामश्च द्रव्याणां चोत्तमो निधिः
धर्मः शुभं वा पापं वा राजमूलं प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
rājā dharmaśca kāmaśca dravyāṇāṁ cottamo nidhiḥ
dharmaḥ śubhaṁ vā pāpaṁ vā rājamūlaṁ pravartate

translations.english: The king is the virtue, the king is the desire and the king is the prime jewel of all subjects. Virtue, desire or sin-every thing ariseth from the king.

verses.sanskrit:
पापस्वभावश्चपलः कथं त्वं रक्षसां वर
ऐश्वर्यमभिसंप्राप्तो विमानमिव दुष्कृती
verses.transliteration:
pāpasvabhāvaścapalaḥ kathaṁ tvaṁ rakṣasāṁ vara
aiśvaryamabhisaṁprāpto vimānamiva duṣkṛtī

translations.english: O you the best of Rākṣasas, you are vicious and unsteady; how have you come by riches like to a sinner attaining to the abode of celestials?

verses.sanskrit:
कामस्वभावो यो यस्य न स शक्यः प्रमार्जितुम्
न हि दुष्टात्मनामार्य मा वसत्यालये चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
kāmasvabhāvo yo yasya na sa śakyaḥ pramārjitum
na hi duṣṭātmanāmārya mā vasatyālaye ciram

translations.english: A vicious person can never relinquish his sinful habits—virtue does never reside in the abodes of impious persons.

verses.sanskrit:
विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा रामो महाबलः
नापराध्यति धर्मात्मा कथं तस्यापराध्यसि
verses.transliteration:
viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā rāmo mahābalaḥ
nāparādhyati dharmātmā kathaṁ tasyāparādhyasi

translations.english: The mighty and the virtuous-souled Rāma has committed nothing wrong in your city or your dominions. Why do you then commit wrong by him?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि शूर्पणखाहेतोर्जनस्थानगतः खरः
अतिवृत्तो हतः पूर्वं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
yadi śūrpaṇakhāhetorjanasthānagataḥ kharaḥ
ativṛtto hataḥ pūrvaṁ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā

translations.english: Though the wicked Khara of Janasthāna has been slain by him on Sūrpanakhā's account, yet how is he to blame for it do you truly speak.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्र ब्रूहि यथासत्यं को रामस्य व्यतिक्रमः
यस्य त्वं लोकनाथस्य हृत्वा भार्यां गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
atra brūhi yathāsatyaṁ ko rāmasya vyatikramaḥ
yasya tvaṁ lokanāthasya hṛtvā bhāryāṁ gamiṣyasi

translations.english: Khara of Janasthāna is highly wicked and if Rāma of blameless actions has killed him on Surpanakha's account how is he to blame? Why do you then carry away the wife of that lord of men?

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं विसृज वैदेहीं मा त्वा घोरेण चक्षुषा
दहेद्दहन भूतेन वृत्रमिन्द्राशनिर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṁ visṛja vaidehīṁ mā tvā ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā
daheddahana bhūtena vṛtramindrāśaniryathā

translations.english: Do you soon leave off Vaidehī. Like to Indra burning down Vịtrāsura, Rāma, looking with his terrible eyes like flaming fire, shall reduce you to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्पमाशीविषं बद्ध्वा वस्त्रान्ते नावबुध्यसे
ग्रीवायां प्रतिमुक्तं च कालपाशं न पश्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sarpamāśīviṣaṁ baddhvā vastrānte nāvabudhyase
grīvāyāṁ pratimuktaṁ ca kālapāśaṁ na paśyasi

translations.english: Do you not understand that you have tied with cloth a virulent serpent? Do you not see that you have placed around your neck the noose of death?

verses.sanskrit:
स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्
तदन्नमुपभोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhāraḥ saumya bhartavyo yo naraṁ nāvasādayet
tadannamupabhoktavyaṁ jīryate yadanāmayam

translations.english: It is always proper to carry such a weight as does not exhaust (him who carries); it is always proper to take such a food as does not cause illness.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्कृत्वा न भवेद्धर्मो न कीर्तिर्न यशो भुवि
शरीरस्य भवेत्खेदः कस्तत्कर्म समाचरेत्
verses.transliteration:
yatkṛtvā na bhaveddharmo na kīrtirna yaśo bhuvi
śarīrasya bhavetkhedaḥ kastatkarma samācaret

translations.english: Who engageth himself in such an action as does not confer virtue, fame or glory, but bring about physical affliction only?

verses.sanskrit:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि मम जातस्य रावण
पितृपैतामहं राज्यं यथावदनुतिष्ठतः
verses.transliteration:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi mama jātasya rāvaṇa
pitṛpaitāmahaṁ rājyaṁ yathāvadanutiṣṭhataḥ

translations.english: O Rāvana, I am sixty thousand years old and have been administering regularly my ancestral kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धोऽहं त्वं युवा धन्वी सरथः कवची शरी
तथाप्यादाय वैदेहीं कुशली न गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
vṛddho'haṁ tvaṁ yuvā dhanvī sarathaḥ kavacī śarī
tathāpyādāya vaidehīṁ kuśalī na gamiṣyasi

translations.english: Old though I am, you shall not be able to carry away with safety Jānakī in my presence, young, accoutred in mails as you are with bow and arrows in your hands and ascending a car.

verses.sanskrit:
न शक्तस्त्वं बलाद्धर्तुं वैदेहीं मम पश्यतः
हेतुभिर्न्यायसंयुक्तैर्ध्रुवां वेदश्रुतीमिव
verses.transliteration:
na śaktastvaṁ balāddhartuṁ vaidehīṁ mama paśyataḥ
hetubhirnyāyasaṁyuktairdhruvāṁ vedaśrutīmiva

translations.english: As it is not easy to destroy, by the reasonings of Logic, Vedas and Śrutis containing eternal and immutable truths, so you shall not be able to carry away Vaidehi by force before me.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ रावण
शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथापूर्वं खरस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
yudhyasva yadi śūro'si muhūrtaṁ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa
śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathāpūrvaṁ kharastathā

translations.english: If you are a hero do you fight. Or do you wait for a moment, O Rāvana, you shall also embrace the earth like to Khara.

verses.sanskrit:
असकृत्संयुगे येन निहता दैत्यदानवाः
नचिराच्चीरवासास्त्वां रामो युधि वधिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
asakṛtsaṁyuge yena nihatā daityadānavāḥ
nacirāccīravāsāstvāṁ rāmo yudhi vadhiṣyati

translations.english: Soon shall Rāma clad in bark destroy you in the battle field, who had many a time and oft destroyed in conflict the celestials and Dānavas.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं गतौ दूरं नृपात्मजौ
क्षिप्रं त्वं नश्यसे नीच तयोर्भीतो न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu śakyaṁ mayā kartuṁ gatau dūraṁ nṛpātmajau
kṣipraṁ tvaṁ naśyase nīca tayorbhīto na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: These two princes Rāma and Lakşmaņa are at a distance, what shall I do now? O vile being, undoubtedly shall you, terrified, be destroyed by thein.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे जीवमानस्य नयिष्यसि शुभामिमाम्
सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीं रामस्य महषीं प्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi me jīvamānasya nayiṣyasi śubhāmimām
sītāṁ kamalapatrākṣīṁ rāmasya mahaṣīṁ priyām

translations.english: Myself drawing my breath you shall not be able to carry away this beloved queen of Rāma, the pure-natured Sitä having eyes resembling lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं तु मया कार्यं प्रियं तस्य महात्मनः
जीवितेनापि रामस्य तथा दशरथस्य च
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ tu mayā kāryaṁ priyaṁ tasya mahātmanaḥ
jīvitenāpi rāmasya tathā daśarathasya ca

translations.english: It is my duty to do good to the high-souled Rāma and Dasaratha even at the sacrifice of my life.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठ दशग्रीव मुहूर्तं पश्य रावण
युद्धातिथ्यं प्रदास्यामि यथाप्राणं निशाचर
वृन्तादिव फलं त्वां तु पातयेयं रथोत्तमात्
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭha daśagrīva muhūrtaṁ paśya rāvaṇa
yuddhātithyaṁ pradāsyāmi yathāprāṇaṁ niśācara
vṛntādiva phalaṁ tvāṁ tu pātayeyaṁ rathottamāt

translations.english: Do you stand, O ten-necked one. Behold for a moment. O Ravana, I shall throw you headlong from this car, like to a fruit from its stalk. O ranger of the night, even to my utmost might I will render you hospitality in encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
संरक्तनयनः कोपात्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः
राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिदुद्राव पतगेन्द्रममर्षणः
verses.transliteration:
saṁraktanayanaḥ kopāttaptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ
rākṣasendro'bhidudrāva patagendramamarṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: While Jatayu, the king of birds, spake this, Rāvana, the lord of Rākşasas, wearing pendants made of pure gold, having his eyes reddened with ire, darted towards him.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्रहारस्तुमुलस्तयोस्तस्मिन्महावने
बभूव वातोद्धतयोर्मेघयोर्गगने यथा
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprahārastumulastayostasminmahāvane
babhūva vātoddhatayormeghayorgagane yathā

translations.english: Thereupon they began a terrible conflict in the welkin, like to clouds driven by wind.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बभूवाद्भुतं युद्धं गृध्रराक्षसयोस्तदा
सपक्षयोर्माल्यवतोर्महापर्वतयोरिव
verses.transliteration:
tadbabhūvādbhutaṁ yuddhaṁ gṛdhrarākṣasayostadā
sapakṣayormālyavatormahāparvatayoriva

translations.english: There occurred a mighty conflict between Jatayu, the lord of vultures, and Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, like to two Malyavān* hills supplies with wings. A mountainous range described as one of the smaller mountains of India proper, lying eastward of mount Meru.—

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नालीकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णाग्रैश्च विकर्णिभिः
अभ्यवर्षन्महाघोरैर्गृध्रराजं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tato nālīkanārācaistīkṣṇāgraiśca vikarṇibhiḥ
abhyavarṣanmahāghorairgṛdhrarājaṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Răvaņa began to shower continually terrible and sharpened pikes, iron arrows and Vikarnis upon the mighty lord of vultures.

verses.sanskrit:
स तानि शरजालानि गृध्रः पत्ररथेश्वरः
जटायुः प्रतिजग्राह रावणास्त्राणि संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
sa tāni śarajālāni gṛdhraḥ patraratheśvaraḥ
jaṭāyuḥ pratijagrāha rāvaṇāstrāṇi saṁyuge

translations.english: Jatayu, the king of birds, began to withstand in conflict the arrows and weapons darted by Rāvana, and wounded Rāvana's person with his feet supplies with sharpened talons.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यः पूर्णमुक्तैरजिह्मगैः
बिभेद निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गृध्रं घोरैः शिलीमुखैः
verses.transliteration:
sa tairbāṇairmahāvīryaḥ pūrṇamuktairajihmagaiḥ
bibheda niśitaistīkṣṇairgṛdhraṁ ghoraiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, to destroy his enemy, that mighty hero, the Ten-necked Ravana, being exercised with ire, took up ten terrible arrows like to the sceptre of Death, and stretching the bow to the full he shot those straight-coursing sharpened shafts at Jatayu, the king of birds.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसरथे पश्यञ्जानकीं बाष्पलोचनाम्
अचिन्तयित्वा बाणांस्तान्राक्षसं समभिद्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasarathe paśyañjānakīṁ bāṣpalocanām
acintayitvā bāṇāṁstānrākṣasaṁ samabhidravat

translations.english: Beholding Jānaki with tears in her eyes in that Raksasa's car, Jatayu, the king of birds, disregarding those arrows, darted towards Rāvana, and with his feet broke asunder his bow with the arrows, adorned with pearls and diamonds.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्चाग्निसदृशं दीप्तं रावणस्य शरावरम्
पक्षाभ्यां च महातेजा व्यधुनोत्पतगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
taccāgnisadṛśaṁ dīptaṁ rāvaṇasya śarāvaram
pakṣābhyāṁ ca mahātejā vyadhunotpatageśvaraḥ

translations.english: Pushing away these arrows by the wind of his wings, he again snapped that mighty bow with his feet, and with a stroke of his wings shattered Rāvaņa's flaming shield like to burning fire.

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनोरश्छदान्दिव्यान्पिशाचवदनान्खरान्
तांश्चास्य जवसंपन्नाञ्जघान समरे बली
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanoraśchadāndivyānpiśācavadanānkharān
tāṁścāsya javasaṁpannāñjaghāna samare balī

translations.english: Thereupon moving away with the wind of his wings Rāvana's blazing cuirass resembling flaming fire, Jațāyu in that conflict made away with his fleet-coursing asses having the faces of demons.

verses.sanskrit:
वरं त्रिवेणुसंपन्नं कामगं पावकार्चिषम्
मणिहेमविचित्राङ्गं बभञ्ज च महारथम्
पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतीकाशं छत्रं च व्यजनैः सह
verses.transliteration:
varaṁ triveṇusaṁpannaṁ kāmagaṁ pāvakārciṣam
maṇihemavicitrāṅgaṁ babhañja ca mahāratham
pūrṇacandrapratīkāśaṁ chatraṁ ca vyajanaiḥ saha

translations.english: Next crumbling into pieces with his impetus the mighty chariot of Rāvana, coursing at will, flaming like fire having steps studded with jewels, and a wooden pole, and throwing down the umbrella and chowris like to the full moon along with the Rākşasas engaged in carrying them, the effulgent and mighty lord of birds shattered the head of the charioteer with the strokes of his beak.

verses.sanskrit:
स भग्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः
अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीं पपात भुवि रावणः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhagnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ
aṅkenādāya vaidehīṁ papāta bhuvi rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Having his bow snapped and deprived of his car, horses and charioteer, Rāvana fell down to the earth, taking Vaidehi on his lap.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भूमौ रावणं भग्नवाहनम्
साधु साध्विति भूतानि गृध्रराजमपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṁ bhūmau rāvaṇaṁ bhagnavāhanam
sādhu sādhviti bhūtāni gṛdhrarājamapūjayan

translations.english: Beholding Rāvaņa fallen on the ground and of broken conveyance, all creatures praised the king of vultures again and again and worshipped him.

verses.sanskrit:
परिश्रान्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा जरया पक्षियूथपम्
उत्पपात पुनर्हृष्टो मैथिलीं गृह्य रावणः
verses.transliteration:
pariśrāntaṁ tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā jarayā pakṣiyūthapam
utpapāta punarhṛṣṭo maithilīṁ gṛhya rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, finding the lord of birds worn out on account of his old age, Ravana, highly encouraged, again rose high up in the welkin, taking Maithill with him.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रहृष्टं निधायाङ्के गच्छन्तं जनकात्मजाम्
गृध्रराजः समुत्पत्य जटायुरिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prahṛṣṭaṁ nidhāyāṅke gacchantaṁ janakātmajām
gṛdhrarājaḥ samutpatya jaṭāyuridamabravīt

translations.english: He had all his weapons broken in the conflict, and had but his dagger left to him. beholding him proceed thus pleased, taking the daughter of Janaka on his lap, all his weapons having been lost, with his sword alone left, the mighty and powerful lord of vultures, Jațāyu, rose up and, darting towards Rāvana, resisted him and said,

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रसंस्पर्शबाणस्य भार्यां रामस्य रावण
अल्पबुद्धे हरस्येनां वधाय खलु रक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
vajrasaṁsparśabāṇasya bhāryāṁ rāmasya rāvaṇa
alpabuddhe harasyenāṁ vadhāya khalu rakṣasām

translations.english: O Rāvana of feeble sense, it is for the destruction of the whole line of Rākşasas that you carries away this spouse of Răma, having arrows like to thunderbolts.

verses.sanskrit:
समित्रबन्धुः सामात्यः सबलः सपरिच्छदः
विषपानं पिबस्येतत्पिपासित इवोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
samitrabandhuḥ sāmātyaḥ sabalaḥ saparicchadaḥ
viṣapānaṁ pibasyetatpipāsita ivodakam

translations.english: Like one thirsty drinking water, you do address yourself to drinking poison along with your friends, courtiers, four-fold forces, servants and relatives.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुबन्धमजानन्तः कर्मणामविचक्षणाः
शीघ्रमेव विनश्यन्ति यथा त्वं विनशिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
anubandhamajānantaḥ karmaṇāmavicakṣaṇāḥ
śīghrameva vinaśyanti yathā tvaṁ vinaśiṣyasi

translations.english: Foolish persons unaware of the fruit of their actions, meet in a short time with their own destruction, so shall you very soon meet with your own end.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे
वधाय बडिशं गृह्य सामिषं जलजो यथा
verses.transliteration:
baddhastvaṁ kālapāśena kva gatastasya mokṣyase
vadhāya baḍiśaṁ gṛhya sāmiṣaṁ jalajo yathā

translations.english: You have been bound up by the noose of Death; and, proceeding whither, shall you save yourself, like to fish eating up baits with hooks for their own destruction?

verses.sanskrit:
न हि जातु दुराधर्षौ काकुत्स्थौ तव रावण
धर्षणं चाश्रमस्यास्य क्षमिष्येते तु राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
na hi jātu durādharṣau kākutsthau tava rāvaṇa
dharṣaṇaṁ cāśramasyāsya kṣamiṣyete tu rāghavau

translations.english: O Rāvana, it is beyond your power to defeat the Kakutsthas. They shall not forgive you for this your encroachment upon their asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा त्वया कृतं कर्म भीरुणा लोकगर्हितम्
तस्कराचरितो मार्गो नैष वीरनिषेवितः
verses.transliteration:
yathā tvayā kṛtaṁ karma bhīruṇā lokagarhitam
taskarācarito mārgo naiṣa vīraniṣevitaḥ

translations.english: What have been perpetrated by you coward, is blamed by all, and is the way taken recourse to by thieves and not by heroes.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ रावण
शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथा भ्राता खरस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
yudhyasva yadi śūro'si muhūrtaṁ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa
śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathā bhrātā kharastathā

translations.english: Do you fight. O Ravana, if you are a hero, or wait for a moment and you shall lie down on the earth like to your brother Khara.

verses.sanskrit:
परेतकाले पुरुषो यत्कर्म प्रतिपद्यते
विनाशायात्मनोऽधर्म्यं प्रतिपन्नोऽसि कर्म तत्
verses.transliteration:
paretakāle puruṣo yatkarma pratipadyate
vināśāyātmano'dharmyaṁ pratipanno'si karma tat

translations.english: Truly have you for your own destruction engaged yourself in these impious acts, which are perpetrated by men on the eve of their death.

verses.sanskrit:
पापानुबन्धो वै यस्य कर्मणः को नु तत्पुमान्
कुर्वीत लोकाधिपतिः स्वयम्भूर्भगवानपि
verses.transliteration:
pāpānubandho vai yasya karmaṇaḥ ko nu tatpumān
kurvīta lokādhipatiḥ svayambhūrbhagavānapi

translations.english: What person do that which lead solely into sin? neither the lord of celestials nor the selfcreate Deity do engage in such an action.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथा गृध्रराजेन क्लिश्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः
अमर्षस्फुरितौष्ठः सन्प्राकम्पत स राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
sa tathā gṛdhrarājena kliśyamāno muhurmuhuḥ
amarṣasphuritauṣṭhaḥ sanprākampata sa rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Being thus afflicted again and again by the king of vultures, the Răkşasa shook, with his lips quivering in anger.

verses.sanskrit:
संपरिष्वज्य वैदेहीं वामेनाङ्केन रावणः
तलेनाभिजघानार्तो जटायुं क्रोधमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpariṣvajya vaidehīṁ vāmenāṅkena rāvaṇaḥ
talenābhijaghānārto jaṭāyuṁ krodhamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: Beside himself with anger, Ravana, holding Jānaki fast by her left flank, struck Jațāyu with his palms.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुस्तमतिक्रम्य तुण्डेनास्य खराधिपः
वामबाहून्दश तदा व्यपाहरदरिंदमः
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyustamatikramya tuṇḍenāsya kharādhipaḥ
vāmabāhūndaśa tadā vyapāharadariṁdamaḥ

translations.english: Jatayu, the subduer of foes, bearing the strokes, tore into pieces his ten left arms with his beak.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रुद्धो दशक्रीवः सीतामुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान्
मुष्टिभ्यां चरणाभ्यां च गृध्रराजमपोथयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kruddho daśakrīvaḥ sītāmutsṛjya vīryavān
muṣṭibhyāṁ caraṇābhyāṁ ca gṛdhrarājamapothayat

translations.english: The mighty Ten-necked one, leaving aside Sitä, out of anger bore down Jațāyu with his fists and feet.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मुहूर्तं संग्रामो बभूवातुलवीर्ययोः
राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य पक्षिणां प्रवरस्य च
verses.transliteration:
tato muhūrtaṁ saṁgrāmo babhūvātulavīryayoḥ
rākṣasānāṁ ca mukhyasya pakṣiṇāṁ pravarasya ca

translations.english: Thereupon arose a mighty conflict between the lord of vultures and the lord of Rākṣasas of incomparable prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य व्यायच्छमानस्य रामस्यार्थेऽथ रावणः
पक्षौ पादौ च पार्श्वौ च खड्गमुद्धृत्य सोऽच्छिनत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya vyāyacchamānasya rāmasyārthe'tha rāvaṇaḥ
pakṣau pādau ca pārśvau ca khaḍgamuddhṛtya so'cchinat

translations.english: Jațāyu addressing himself to displaying his prowess for the benefit of Rāma, Rāvaņa taking out his dagger, cut off his two wings, two legs and two sides.

verses.sanskrit:
स छिन्नपक्षः सहसा रक्षसा रौद्रकर्मणा
निपपात हतो गृध्रो धरण्यामल्पजीवितः
verses.transliteration:
sa chinnapakṣaḥ sahasā rakṣasā raudrakarmaṇā
nipapāta hato gṛdhro dharaṇyāmalpajīvitaḥ

translations.english: The ranger of the night of cruel deeds having şundered his wings, the king of vultures approaching well-nigh the verge of death, fell। down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं भूमौ क्षतजार्द्रं जटायुषम्
अभ्यधावत वैदेही स्वबन्धुमिव दुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā patitaṁ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṁ jaṭāyuṣam
abhyadhāvata vaidehī svabandhumiva duḥkhitā

translations.english: Beholding him fallen on the ground with his person bathed in blood, Sītā became exceedingly aggrieved and darted towards him like to a friend.

verses.sanskrit:
तं नीलजीमूतनिकाशकल्पं; सुपाण्डुरोरस्कमुदारवीर्यम्
ददर्श लङ्काधिपतिः पृथिव्यां; जटायुषं शान्तमिवाग्निदावम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ nīlajīmūtanikāśakalpaṁ; supāṇḍuroraskamudāravīryam
dadarśa laṅkādhipatiḥ pṛthivyāṁ; jaṭāyuṣaṁ śāntamivāgnidāvam

translations.english: The lord of Lankā beheld Jațāyu, fallen on the ground, resembling sable clouds, having a yellow breast and of exceeding prowess, like to an extinguished forest-fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तं पत्ररथं महीतले; निपातितं रावणवेगमर्दितम्
पुनः परिष्वज्य शशिप्रभानना; रुरोद सीता जनकात्मजा तदा
verses.transliteration:
tatastu taṁ patrarathaṁ mahītale; nipātitaṁ rāvaṇavegamarditam
punaḥ pariṣvajya śaśiprabhānanā; ruroda sītā janakātmajā tadā

translations.english: Then Sītā the daughter of Janaka, having a moon-like countenance began lamenting, clasping with her hands Jațāyu, crushed and fallen on the ground by the vehemence of Rāvana's prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु ताराधिपमुखी रावणेन समीक्ष्य तम्
गृध्रराजं विनिहतं विललाप सुदुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
sā tu tārādhipamukhī rāvaṇena samīkṣya tam
gṛdhrarājaṁ vinihataṁ vilalāpa suduḥkhitā

translations.english: Beholding the king of vultures slain by Rāvana, that one possessed of a face fair as the moon, stricken with grief, broke out into lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
निमित्तं लक्षणज्ञानं शकुनिस्वरदर्शनम्
अवश्यं सुखदुःखेषु नराणां प्रतिदृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
nimittaṁ lakṣaṇajñānaṁ śakunisvaradarśanam
avaśyaṁ sukhaduḥkheṣu narāṇāṁ pratidṛśyate

translations.english: Throbbings of the eyes or other parts of the body, dreams, seeing birds or hearing their voice, are found to augur happiness or misery to men.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं राम जानासि महद्व्यसनमात्मजः
धावन्ति नूनं काकुत्स्थ मदर्थं मृगपक्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ rāma jānāsi mahadvyasanamātmajaḥ
dhāvanti nūnaṁ kākutstha madarthaṁ mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: And, O Rāma, although birds and beasts are scampering away before you on my account, you under-stand not the mighty mishap that has befallen you.

verses.sanskrit:
त्राहि मामद्य काकुत्स्थ लक्ष्मणेति वराङ्गना
सुसंत्रस्ता समाक्रन्दच्छृण्वतां तु यथान्तिके
verses.transliteration:
trāhi māmadya kākutstha lakṣmaṇeti varāṅganā
susaṁtrastā samākrandacchṛṇvatāṁ tu yathāntike

translations.english: O Kākutstha, O Laksmana, save me! Thus did that best of females, afflicted with fear, bewail; and those near (her) heard her lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
तां क्लिष्टमाल्याभरणां विलपन्तीमनाथवत्
अभ्यधावत वैदेहीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ kliṣṭamālyābharaṇāṁ vilapantīmanāthavat
abhyadhāvata vaidehīṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, that lord of the Rākşasas, Rāvana, darted towards Vaidehi, who, with a faded wreath for her ornament, was bewailing in forlorn guise.

verses.sanskrit:
तां लतामिव वेष्टन्तीमालिङ्गन्तीं महाद्रुमान्
मुञ्च मुञ्चेति बहुशः प्रवदन्राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ latāmiva veṣṭantīmāliṅgantīṁ mahādrumān
muñca muñceti bahuśaḥ pravadanrākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: Exclaiming repeatedly, Leave off! Leave off, the lord of the Rākşasas got at her, as she was clasping a mighty trees as if it were a creeper.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति रामेण रहितां वने
जीवितान्ताय केशेषु जग्राहान्तकसंनिभः
verses.transliteration:
krośantīṁ rāma rāmeti rāmeṇa rahitāṁ vane
jīvitāntāya keśeṣu jagrāhāntakasaṁnibhaḥ

translations.english: And as she, bereft of the company of Răma in the wilderness, was wailing, saying, O Rāma, O Rāma, that one resembling the Destroyer himself, with the view of compassing his own end, seized her by her hair. On Vaidehi being thus outraged, this entire world consisting of mobile and immobile objects, had its nature altered. A dense darkness enveloped (everything).

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा सीतां परामृष्टां दीनां दिव्येन चक्षुषा
कृतं कार्यमिति श्रीमान्व्याजहार पितामहः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā sītāṁ parāmṛṣṭāṁ dīnāṁ divyena cakṣuṣā
kṛtaṁ kāryamiti śrīmānvyājahāra pitāmahaḥ

translations.english: And the air did not breathe there; and the sun grew dim. Espying with his divine vision that Sītā was overcome, that Deity, the graceful Great-father exclaimed, Our work is accomplished.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टा व्यथिताश्चासन्सर्वे ते परमर्षयः
दृष्ट्वा सीतां परामृष्टां दण्डकारण्यवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭā vyathitāścāsansarve te paramarṣayaḥ
dṛṣṭvā sītāṁ parāmṛṣṭāṁ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinaḥ

translations.english: And seeing Sītā overpowered, the supreme saints inhabiting the Dandaka forest, concluding the destruction of Rāvaņa to be as good as accomplished without much ado, became at once delighted and aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तां राम रामेति रुदन्तीं लक्ष्मणेति च
जगामाकाशमादाय रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tāṁ rāma rāmeti rudantīṁ lakṣmaṇeti ca
jagāmākāśamādāya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: As she went on weeping with ( Rāma, O Lakşmaņa, Rāvana-lord of Rākşasas—taking her, coursed through the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तप्ताभरणसर्वाङ्गी पीतकौशेयवासनी
रराज राजपुत्री तु विद्युत्सौदामनी यथा
verses.transliteration:
taptābharaṇasarvāṅgī pītakauśeyavāsanī
rarāja rājaputrī tu vidyutsaudāmanī yathā

translations.english: And then the king's daughter hued like molten gold, clad in a yellow silken cloth, looked exceedingly beautiful like to lighting.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्धूतेन च वस्त्रेण तस्याः पीतेन रावणः
अधिकं परिबभ्राज गिरिर्दीप इवाग्निना
verses.transliteration:
uddhūtena ca vastreṇa tasyāḥ pītena rāvaṇaḥ
adhikaṁ paribabhrāja girirdīpa ivāgninā

translations.english: And on her yellow cloth streaming up, Rāvaņa looked surpassingly graceful like a hill aflame with fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः परमकल्याण्यास्ताम्राणि सुरभीणि च
पद्मपत्राणि वैदेह्या अभ्यकीर्यन्त रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ paramakalyāṇyāstāmrāṇi surabhīṇi ca
padmapatrāṇi vaidehyā abhyakīryanta rāvaṇam

translations.english: And coppery fragrant lotus-leaves belonging to the eminently auspicious Vaidehī showered upon Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः कौशेयमुद्धूतमाकाशे कनकप्रभम्
बभौ चादित्यरागेण ताम्रमभ्रमिवातपे
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ kauśeyamuddhūtamākāśe kanakaprabham
babhau cādityarāgeṇa tāmramabhramivātape

translations.english: And her gold-glowing silken cloth, flying in the air, appeared like clouds coloured by the sunken sun.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तद्विमलं वक्त्रमाकाशे रावणाङ्कगम्
न रराज विना रामं विनालमिव पङ्कजम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstadvimalaṁ vaktramākāśe rāvaṇāṅkagam
na rarāja vinā rāmaṁ vinālamiva paṅkajam

translations.english: And her blameless countenance on Rāvana's lap in the sky did not appear beauteous without Rāma, like a lotus without its stalk;

verses.sanskrit:
बभूव जलदं नीलं भित्त्वा चन्द्र इवोदितः
सुललाटं सुकेशान्तं पद्मगर्भाभमव्रणम्
शुक्लैः सुविमलैर्दन्तैः प्रभावद्भिरलंकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
babhūva jaladaṁ nīlaṁ bhittvā candra ivoditaḥ
sulalāṭaṁ sukeśāntaṁ padmagarbhābhamavraṇam
śuklaiḥ suvimalairdantaiḥ prabhāvadbhiralaṁkṛtam

translations.english: It appeared like the moon risen tearing away dark clouds. And in the aerial regions her countenance on Rāvana's lap furnished with a fair forehead and graceful hair glowing like the interior of a lotus, without scars, graced with white, shining, stainless teeth, having excellent eyes, lovely like the moon, having a shapely nose, a rubeous upper lip, wearing the splendour of gold in the sky, that captivating countenance of hers in consequence of her weeping, and of being stained with tears, as also owing to the violence it had undergone at the hands of the lord of Rākşasas,-did not appear beautiful without Rāma' like the moon risen during the day.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हेमवर्णा नीलाङ्गं मैथिली राक्षसाधिपम्
शुशुभे काञ्चनी काञ्ची नीलं मणिमिवाश्रिता
verses.transliteration:
sā hemavarṇā nīlāṅgaṁ maithilī rākṣasādhipam
śuśubhe kāñcanī kāñcī nīlaṁ maṇimivāśritā

translations.english: And furnished with the hue of gold, Mithila's daughter beside the dark-bodied lord of the Rākşasas, looked like a golden girth round a sable elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
सा पद्मगौरी हेमाभा रावणं जनकात्मजा
विद्युद्घनमिवाविश्य शुशुभे तप्तभूषणा
verses.transliteration:
sā padmagaurī hemābhā rāvaṇaṁ janakātmajā
vidyudghanamivāviśya śuśubhe taptabhūṣaṇā

translations.english: Janaka's daughter, yellow-hued like lotus, having the lustre of gold-and adorned with shining ornaments, coming in contact with Rāvana, appeared like lightning embosomed among clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या भूषणघोषेण वैदेह्या राक्षसाधिपः
बभूव विमलो नीलः सघोष इव तोयदः
verses.transliteration:
tasyā bhūṣaṇaghoṣeṇa vaidehyā rākṣasādhipaḥ
babhūva vimalo nīlaḥ saghoṣa iva toyadaḥ

translations.english: And in consequence of Vaidehi's ornaments sending sounds, the lord of Rākşasas resembled an entirely dark rumbling cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तमाङ्गच्युता तस्याः पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः
सीताया ह्रियमाणायाः पपात धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
uttamāṅgacyutā tasyāḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ
sītāyā hriyamāṇāyāḥ papāta dharaṇītale

translations.english: As Sītā was being borne away, showers of blossoms, falling off from her head, were scattered all around on the earth beneath.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु रावणवेगेन पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः
समाधूता दशग्रीवं पुनरेवाभ्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
sā tu rāvaṇavegena puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ
samādhūtā daśagrīvaṁ punarevābhyavartata

translations.english: And that blossoms shower all around, drawn up by the vehemence of the ten-headed Rāvana, again alighted beside him.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्यवर्तत पुष्पाणां धारा वैश्रवणानुजम्
नक्षत्रमालाविमला मेरुं नगमिवोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
abhyavartata puṣpāṇāṁ dhārā vaiśravaṇānujam
nakṣatramālāvimalā meruṁ nagamivottamam

translations.english: And the showers of blossoms scattered around Vaisravana's younger brother, looked like rows of burning stars round the foremost of mountains*. Sumerus

verses.sanskrit:
चरणान्नूपुरं भ्रष्टं वैदेह्या रत्नभूषितम्
विद्युन्मण्डलसंकाशं पपात मधुरस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
caraṇānnūpuraṁ bhraṣṭaṁ vaidehyā ratnabhūṣitam
vidyunmaṇḍalasaṁkāśaṁ papāta madhurasvanam

translations.english: And the bangles studded with gems, loosened. from Vaidehi's feet, fell on the earth, like the lighting circle. Instead of On the earth-some texts have [bangles] sweet-sounding.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुप्रवालरक्ता सा नीलाङ्गं राक्षसेश्वरम्
प्राशोभयत वैदेही गजं कष्येव काञ्चनी
verses.transliteration:
tarupravālaraktā sā nīlāṅgaṁ rākṣaseśvaram
prāśobhayata vaidehī gajaṁ kaṣyeva kāñcanī

translations.english: O hue like the light red of tender twigs, Vaidehi set off the dark-bodied lord of Rākşasas, as does a golden cover an elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
तां महोल्कामिवाकाशे दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा
जहाराकाशमाविश्य सीतां वैश्रवणानुजः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ maholkāmivākāśe dīpyamānāṁ svatejasā
jahārākāśamāviśya sītāṁ vaiśravaṇānujaḥ

translations.english: Vaisravana's younger brother carried away Sītā, who, like a mighty meteor, filled the heavens with her splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तान्यग्निवर्णानि भूषणानि महीतले
सघोषाण्यवकीर्यन्त क्षीणास्तारा इवाम्बरात्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstānyagnivarṇāni bhūṣaṇāni mahītale
saghoṣāṇyavakīryanta kṣīṇāstārā ivāmbarāt

translations.english: And like stars of exhausted religious merit dropping down from the sky, her fiery ornaments began to fall to the earth with sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः स्तनान्तराद्भ्रष्टो हारस्ताराधिपद्युतिः
वैदेह्या निपतन्भाति गङ्गेव गगनाच्च्युता
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ stanāntarādbhraṣṭo hārastārādhipadyutiḥ
vaidehyā nipatanbhāti gaṅgeva gaganāccyutā

translations.english: And the chain of the splendour of the moon, removed from Vaidehi's breast, falling down, shone like the Gangā dropping from the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पात वाताभिहता नानाद्विज गणायुताः
मा भैरिति विधूताग्रा व्याजह्रुरिव पादपाः
verses.transliteration:
utpāta vātābhihatā nānādvija gaṇāyutāḥ
mā bhairiti vidhūtāgrā vyājahruriva pādapāḥ

translations.english: The trees filled with various fowls, with their tops waving because of the wind blowing on high and swaying them, seemed to say, No fear, [to Sita.]

verses.sanskrit:
नलिन्यो ध्वस्तकमलास्त्रस्तमीनजले चराः
सखीमिव गतोत्साहां शोचन्तीव स्म मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
nalinyo dhvastakamalāstrastamīnajale carāḥ
sakhīmiva gatotsāhāṁ śocantīva sma maithilīm

translations.english: And the pools with their lotuses faded and their fishes agitated, seemed to sorrow for the desponding daughter of Mithilā as for their friend.

verses.sanskrit:
समन्तादभिसंपत्य सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विजाः
अन्वधावंस्तदा रोषात्सीताच्छायानुगामिनः
verses.transliteration:
samantādabhisaṁpatya siṁhavyāghramṛgadvijāḥ
anvadhāvaṁstadā roṣātsītācchāyānugāminaḥ

translations.english: And following Sītā's shadow, lions, and tigers, and other beasts and birds, rushed from all sides in wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
जलप्रपातास्रमुखाः शृङ्गैरुच्छ्रितबाहवः
सीतायां ह्रियमाणायां विक्रोशन्तीव पर्वताः
verses.transliteration:
jalaprapātāsramukhāḥ śṛṅgairucchritabāhavaḥ
sītāyāṁ hriyamāṇāyāṁ vikrośantīva parvatāḥ

translations.english: And the mountains, with their faces washed with water-falls representing tears, and their summits resembling uplifted arms, seemed to lament for Sītă, as she was being carried away.

verses.sanskrit:
ह्रियमाणां तु वैदेहीं दृष्ट्वा दीनो दिवाकरः
प्रविध्वस्तप्रभः श्रीमानासीत्पाण्डुरमण्डलः
verses.transliteration:
hriyamāṇāṁ tu vaidehīṁ dṛṣṭvā dīno divākaraḥ
pravidhvastaprabhaḥ śrīmānāsītpāṇḍuramaṇḍalaḥ

translations.english: And beholding Vaidehỉ carried away, the glorious Sun, oppressed with sadness, had his rays dimmed and his disc darkened.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सर्वाणि भूतानि गणशः पर्यदेवयन्
वित्रस्तका दीनमुखा रुरुदुर्मृगपोतकाः
verses.transliteration:
iti sarvāṇi bhūtāni gaṇaśaḥ paryadevayan
vitrastakā dīnamukhā rurudurmṛgapotakāḥ

translations.english: Virtue is not; and where is truth? And there is neither sincerity nor kindness, in a case in which Rāvana is carrying away Rāma's Vaidehī; thus did all creatures lament in numbers. And the young of deer, afflicted with fear, wept with woe-began faces.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्वीक्ष्योद्वीक्ष्य नयनैरास्रपाताविलेक्षणाः
सुप्रवेपितगात्राश्च बभूवुर्वनदेवताः
verses.transliteration:
udvīkṣyodvīkṣya nayanairāsrapātāvilekṣaṇāḥ
supravepitagātrāśca babhūvurvanadevatāḥ

translations.english: And the sylvan deities, looking up now and again with eyes betokening fear, had their persons all in a tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
अवेक्षमाणां बहुषो वैदेहीं धरणीतलम्
स तामाकुलकेशान्तां विप्रमृष्टविशेषकाम्
जहारात्मविनाशाय दशग्रीवो मनस्विनाम्
verses.transliteration:
avekṣamāṇāṁ bahuṣo vaidehīṁ dharaṇītalam
sa tāmākulakeśāntāṁ vipramṛṣṭaviśeṣakām
jahārātmavināśāya daśagrīvo manasvinām

translations.english: headed one carried away the intelligent Vaidehī, bewailing bitterly, Sītā, who had come by such misfortune, sweet-voiced, crying, O Lakşmaņa O Rāma, and casting glances on the ground many time and oft, the ends of her hair waving and her tilika wiped out.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सा चारुदती शुचिस्मिता; विनाकृता बन्धुजनेन मैथिली
अपश्यती राघवलक्ष्मणावुभौ; विवर्णवक्त्रा भयभारपीडिता
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sā cārudatī śucismitā; vinākṛtā bandhujanena maithilī
apaśyatī rāghavalakṣmaṇāvubhau; vivarṇavaktrā bhayabhārapīḍitā

translations.english: Then oppressed with the load of fear, Sītā of luminous smiles, Mithila's daughter, bereft of her friends-not beholding either Rāma or Lakşmaņa, became pale of countenance.

verses.sanskrit:
खमुत्पतन्तं तं दृष्ट्वा मैथिली जनकात्मजा
दुःखिता परमोद्विग्ना भये महति वर्तिनी
verses.transliteration:
khamutpatantaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā maithilī janakātmajā
duḥkhitā paramodvignā bhaye mahati vartinī

translations.english: Seeing him fly up into the air, Janaka's daughter, Maithili, became aggrieved and exceedingly agitated, and great was the fear that possessed her.

verses.sanskrit:
रोषरोदनताम्राक्षी भीमाक्षं राक्षसाधिपम्
रुदती करुणं सीता ह्रियमाणेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
roṣarodanatāmrākṣī bhīmākṣaṁ rākṣasādhipam
rudatī karuṇaṁ sītā hriyamāṇedamabravīt

translations.english: Her eyes expressing rage, weeping and fright, Sītā, as she was being carried away, weeping piteously, spoke to the grim-eyed lord of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
न व्यपत्रपसे नीच कर्मणानेन रावण
ज्ञात्वा विरहितां यो मां चोरयित्वा पलायसे
verses.transliteration:
na vyapatrapase nīca karmaṇānena rāvaṇa
jñātvā virahitāṁ yo māṁ corayitvā palāyase

translations.english: Do you not, O base wretch, O Ravana, feel shame on account of this act-you, who, knowing that I was alone fly away, carrying me?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयैव नूनं दुष्टात्मन्भीरुणा हर्तुमिच्छता
ममापवाहितो भर्ता मृगरूपेण मायया
यो हि मामुद्यतस्त्रातुं सोऽप्ययं विनिपातितः
verses.transliteration:
tvayaiva nūnaṁ duṣṭātmanbhīruṇā hartumicchatā
mamāpavāhito bhartā mṛgarūpeṇa māyayā
yo hi māmudyatastrātuṁ so'pyayaṁ vinipātitaḥ

translations.english: Coward that you are, you it was, who, desirous of carrying me off, by the shape of a deer, had, by your (powers of] illusion taken away my lord.

verses.sanskrit:
परमं खलु ते वीर्यं दृश्यते राक्षसाधम
विश्राव्य नामधेयं हि युद्धे नास्ति जिता त्वया
verses.transliteration:
paramaṁ khalu te vīryaṁ dṛśyate rākṣasādhama
viśrāvya nāmadheyaṁ hi yuddhe nāsti jitā tvayā

translations.english: Great, forsooth, is found to be your might, you vilest of Rākşasas, in that you have carried me off; by simply declaring your name, but have not won me in war. Why do you not, O execrable one, take shame to yourself, having perpetrated such a heinous act-having carried off another's wife in the absence of her husband?

verses.sanskrit:
कथयिष्यन्ति लोकेषु पुरुषाः कर्म कुत्सितम्
सुनृशंसमधर्मिष्ठं तव शौण्डीर्यमानिनः
verses.transliteration:
kathayiṣyanti lokeṣu puruṣāḥ karma kutsitam
sunṛśaṁsamadharmiṣṭhaṁ tava śauṇḍīryamāninaḥ

translations.english: This fell and foul ict of yours fraught with unrighteousness, heroic persons shall bruit about the world.

verses.sanskrit:
धिक्ते शौर्यं च सत्त्वं च यत्त्वया कथितं तदा
कुलाक्रोशकरं लोके धिक्ते चारित्रमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
dhikte śauryaṁ ca sattvaṁ ca yattvayā kathitaṁ tadā
kulākrośakaraṁ loke dhikte cāritramīdṛśam

translations.english: Fie on your heroism and your truth, of which you did speak at that time; and fie also on this character of yours, calculated to sully your line in this world.

verses.sanskrit:
किं शक्यं कर्तुमेवं हि यज्जवेनैव धावसि
मुहूर्तमपि तिष्ठस्व न जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ śakyaṁ kartumevaṁ hi yajjavenaiva dhāvasi
muhūrtamapi tiṣṭhasva na jīvanpratiyāsyasi

translations.english: What can I do (to you), as you proceed with speed? But stay you for a moment; and you shall not return with life.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि चक्षुःपथं प्राप्य तयोः पार्थिवपुत्रयोः
ससैन्योऽपि समर्तःस्त्वं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi cakṣuḥpathaṁ prāpya tayoḥ pārthivaputrayoḥ
sasainyo'pi samartaḥstvaṁ muhūrtamapi jīvitum

translations.english: Should you come within the range of the vision of those sons of the king, you could not, although you should happen to be accompanied with your army, live for a moment.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वं तयोः शरस्पर्शं सोढुं शक्तः कथंचन
वने प्रज्वलितस्येव स्पर्शमग्नेर्विहंगमः
verses.transliteration:
na tvaṁ tayoḥ śarasparśaṁ soḍhuṁ śaktaḥ kathaṁcana
vane prajvalitasyeva sparśamagnervihaṁgamaḥ

translations.english: Even as a bird cannot bear the touch of a flaming fire in a forest, you can never bear the touch of their arrows. Effecting your own welfare, do you, O Ravana, leave me.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु कृत्वात्मनः पथ्यं साधु मां मुञ्च रावण
मत्प्रधर्षणरुष्टो हि भ्रात्रा सह पतिर्मम
विधास्यति विनाशाय त्वं मां यदि न मुञ्चसि
verses.transliteration:
sādhu kṛtvātmanaḥ pathyaṁ sādhu māṁ muñca rāvaṇa
matpradharṣaṇaruṣṭo hi bhrātrā saha patirmama
vidhāsyati vināśāya tvaṁ māṁ yadi na muñcasi

translations.english: If you do not let me go, iny husband along with his brother would strive for your destruction. As intent upon sensual enjoyment, you endeavour to ravish me, this very endeavour of yours O mean wight, shall come to naught.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यहं तमपश्यन्ती भर्तारं विबुधोपमम्
उत्सहे शत्रुवशगा प्राणान्धारयितुं चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
na hyahaṁ tamapaśyantī bhartāraṁ vibudhopamam
utsahe śatruvaśagā prāṇāndhārayituṁ ciram

translations.english: Not beholding my lord resembling a celestial, I cannot, come under the sway of my enemy, bear to live long.

verses.sanskrit:
न नूनं चात्मनः श्रेयः पथ्यं वा समवेक्षसे
मृत्युकाले यथा मर्त्यो विपरीतानि सेवते
verses.transliteration:
na nūnaṁ cātmanaḥ śreyaḥ pathyaṁ vā samavekṣase
mṛtyukāle yathā martyo viparītāni sevate

translations.english: As one dwelling on earth perceives objects in their reversed relations at the time of one's death SO you do not perceive what is for your good or profit. Those moribund do not relish what would do them good.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि त्वमीदृशं कृत्वा तस्यालीकं महात्मनः
धारितुं शक्ष्यसि चिरं विषं पीत्वेव निर्घृणः
verses.transliteration:
na hi tvamīdṛśaṁ kṛtvā tasyālīkaṁ mahātmanaḥ
dhārituṁ śakṣyasi ciraṁ viṣaṁ pītveva nirghṛṇaḥ

translations.english: But, O shameless one, like a person that has drunk poison, having done this wrong to that high-souled one, you with not be able to save yourself. O Rāvana, you are fast fettered in the noose of Death.

verses.sanskrit:
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण विना भ्रातरमाहवे
राक्षसा निहता येन सहस्राणि चतुर्दश
verses.transliteration:
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa vinā bhrātaramāhave
rākṣasā nihatā yena sahasrāṇi caturdaśa

translations.english: Having done this foul turn to that high-souled one, repairing whither, shall you obtain respite? Shall not that strong and heroic Rāghava, skilled in all weapons, who without his brother, in the twinkling of an eye, in battle slew fourteen thousand Rākṣasas, slay you, who carries away his beloved wife?

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्चान्यच्च परुषं वैदेही रावणाङ्कगा
भयशोकसमाविष्टा करुणं विललाप ह
verses.transliteration:
etaccānyacca paruṣaṁ vaidehī rāvaṇāṅkagā
bhayaśokasamāviṣṭā karuṇaṁ vilalāpa ha

translations.english: Thus and in other ways, Videha's daughter, lying on the lap of Rāvana, overwhelmed with fear and grief, indulged in piteous lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा भृशार्तां बहु चैव भाषिणीं; विललाप पूर्वं करुणं च भामिनीम्
जहार पापस्तरुणीं विवेष्टतीं; नृपात्मजामागतगात्रवेपथुम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā bhṛśārtāṁ bahu caiva bhāṣiṇīṁ; vilalāpa pūrvaṁ karuṇaṁ ca bhāminīm
jahāra pāpastaruṇīṁ viveṣṭatīṁ; nṛpātmajāmāgatagātravepathum

translations.english: And the wicked (Rävaņa) with a shaking frame carried away the daughter of the king extremely distressed, speaking much, and speaking piteously, uttering lamentations, and putting forth endeavours (to free herself.) saw

verses.sanskrit:
ह्रियमाणा तु वैदेही कंचिन्नाथमपश्यती
ददर्श गिरिशृङ्गस्थान्पञ्चवानरपुंगवान्
verses.transliteration:
hriyamāṇā tu vaidehī kaṁcinnāthamapaśyatī
dadarśa giriśṛṅgasthānpañcavānarapuṁgavān

translations.english: Carried away (by Ravana), Vaidehi, not finding any defender, five principal monkeys stationed on the top of a hill.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां मध्ये विशालाक्षी कौशेयं कनकप्रभम्
उत्तरीयं वरारोहा शुभान्याभरणानि च
मुमोच यदि रामाय शंसेयुरिति मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ madhye viśālākṣī kauśeyaṁ kanakaprabham
uttarīyaṁ varārohā śubhānyābharaṇāni ca
mumoca yadi rāmāya śaṁseyuriti maithilī

translations.english: Thereat, that lady of expansive eyes and surpassing charms, in the hope that they might convey the intelligence to Rāma, flung off in their midst her gold-gleaming silken sheet, and elegant ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
पिङ्गाक्षास्तां विशालाक्षीं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव
विक्रोशन्तीं तदा सीतां ददृशुर्वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
piṅgākṣāstāṁ viśālākṣīṁ netrairanimiṣairiva
vikrośantīṁ tadā sītāṁ dadṛśurvānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: But the Ten headed one owing to hurry did not observe the throwing of the cloth along with the ornaments. Those foremost of monkeys having tawny eyes observes with winkless eyes the large-eyed Sītā as she was giving way to grief.

verses.sanskrit:
स च पम्पामतिक्रम्य लङ्कामभिमुखः पुरीम्
जगाम रुदतीं गृह्य मैथिलीं राक्षसेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa ca pampāmatikramya laṅkāmabhimukhaḥ purīm
jagāma rudatīṁ gṛhya maithilīṁ rākṣaseśvaraḥ

translations.english: The lord of Rākşasas, passing beyond Pampā, directed his course towards the city of Lankā, taking Mithilā's daughter along with him, indulging lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
तां जहार सुसंहृष्टो रावणो मृत्युमात्मनः
उत्सङ्गेनैव भुजगीं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रां महाविषाम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ jahāra susaṁhṛṣṭo rāvaṇo mṛtyumātmanaḥ
utsaṅgenaiva bhujagīṁ tīkṣṇadaṁṣṭrāṁ mahāviṣām

translations.english: Experiencing the height of delight, Rāvana ravished her, taking her on his lap like a sharp-toothed serpent of virulent poison.

verses.sanskrit:
वनानि सरितः शैलान्सरांसि च विहायसा
स क्षिप्रं समतीयाय शरश्चापादिव च्युतः
verses.transliteration:
vanāni saritaḥ śailānsarāṁsi ca vihāyasā
sa kṣipraṁ samatīyāya śaraścāpādiva cyutaḥ

translations.english: And speedily, like an arrow shot from a bow, he, coursing the welkin, left behind woods and streams and mountains and pieces of water.

verses.sanskrit:
तिमिनक्रनिकेतं तु वरुणालयमक्षयम्
सरितां शरणं गत्वा समतीयाय सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
timinakraniketaṁ tu varuṇālayamakṣayam
saritāṁ śaraṇaṁ gatvā samatīyāya sāgaram

translations.english: Coming to the abode of Varuņa, that refuge of rivers, the exhaustless ocean—the home of whales and alligators, he crossed over it.

verses.sanskrit:
संभ्रमात्परिवृत्तोर्मी रुद्धमीनमहोरगः
वैदेह्यां ह्रियमाणायां बभूव वरुणालयः
verses.transliteration:
saṁbhramātparivṛttormī ruddhamīnamahoragaḥ
vaidehyāṁ hriyamāṇāyāṁ babhūva varuṇālayaḥ

translations.english: In consequence of the carrying away of Vaidehi, Varuna's abode, from grief, had all its waves stilled and its fishes and mighty snakes inert.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षगता वाचः ससृजुश्चारणास्तदा
एतदन्तो दशग्रीव इति सिद्धास्तदाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣagatā vācaḥ sasṛjuścāraṇāstadā
etadanto daśagrīva iti siddhāstadābruvan

translations.english: And the Cāranas uttered in the heavens these words, O Ten-headed one, this is your end. Thus did the Siddhas then say.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु सीतां विवेष्टन्तीमङ्केनादाय रावणः
प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां रूपिणीं मृत्युमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu sītāṁ viveṣṭantīmaṅkenādāya rāvaṇaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ laṅkāṁ rūpiṇīṁ mṛtyumātmanaḥ

translations.english: And taking Sītā on his lap, representing his own Death, who endeavoured (to liberate herself). Rāvana entered the city of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिगम्य पुरीं लङ्कां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्
संरूढकक्ष्या बहुलं स्वमन्तःपुरमाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
so'bhigamya purīṁ laṅkāṁ suvibhaktamahāpathām
saṁrūḍhakakṣyā bahulaṁ svamantaḥpuramāviśat

translations.english: And entering the city of Lankā, vast, with all its highways well-arranged, and with people thronging its gates, he entered his own inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र तामसितापाङ्गीं शोकमोहपरायणाम्
निदधे रावणः सीतां मयो मायामिवासुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra tāmasitāpāṅgīṁ śokamohaparāyaṇām
nidadhe rāvaṇaḥ sītāṁ mayo māyāmivāsurīm

translations.english: Then Rāvana set Sītā there, having eyes with dark outer corners, exercised with grief and dole; as if Máyā had set his own Asura Illusion (in his own palace).

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च दशग्रीवः पिशाचीर्घोरदर्शनाः
यथा नैनां पुमान्स्त्री वा सीतां पश्यत्यसंमतः
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca daśagrīvaḥ piśācīrghoradarśanāḥ
yathā naināṁ pumānstrī vā sītāṁ paśyatyasaṁmataḥ

translations.english: Then the Ten-headed one spoke to some female friends of terrible visages, Let no man or woman behold Sītā without my permission.

verses.sanskrit:
मुक्तामणिसुवर्णानि वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च
यद्यदिच्छेत्तदेवास्या देयं मच्छन्दतो यथा
verses.transliteration:
muktāmaṇisuvarṇāni vastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca
yadyadicchettadevāsyā deyaṁ macchandato yathā

translations.english: And I command that, should she ask for pearls, or rubies, or gold, or apparel, or ornaments, the same should be rendered to her.

verses.sanskrit:
या च वक्ष्यति वैदेहीं वचनं किंचिदप्रियम्
अज्ञानाद्यदि वा ज्ञानान्न तस्या जीवितं प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
yā ca vakṣyati vaidehīṁ vacanaṁ kiṁcidapriyam
ajñānādyadi vā jñānānna tasyā jīvitaṁ priyam

translations.english: She that, whether knowingly or unknowingly should say anything unpleasant to Vaidehī, would hold her life cheap.

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्त्वा राक्षसीस्तास्तु राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्
निष्क्रम्यान्तःपुरात्तस्मात्किं कृत्यमिति चिन्तयन्
ददर्शाष्टौ महावीर्यान्राक्षसान्पिशिताशनान्
verses.transliteration:
tathoktvā rākṣasīstāstu rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
niṣkramyāntaḥpurāttasmātkiṁ kṛtyamiti cintayan
dadarśāṣṭau mahāvīryānrākṣasānpiśitāśanān

translations.english: Heaving said this to the Rākşasis, the puissant lord of the Rākṣasas, went out of the inner apartment, and thought within himself as to what was to be done (next). And he saw eight flesheating Rākşasas of wondrous prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
स तान्दृष्ट्वा महावीर्यो वरदानेन मोहितः
उवाचैतानिदं वाक्यं प्रशस्य बलवीर्यतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāndṛṣṭvā mahāvīryo varadānena mohitaḥ
uvācaitānidaṁ vākyaṁ praśasya balavīryataḥ

translations.english: And seeing them, the exceedingly powerful. (Ravana), blinded by the bestowal of the boon, after extolling their strength and heroism, addressed them.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रोष्यतां जनस्थाने शून्ये निहतराक्षसे
पौरुषं बलमाश्रित्य त्रासमुत्सृज्य दूरतः
verses.transliteration:
tatroṣyatāṁ janasthāne śūnye nihatarākṣase
pauruṣaṁ balamāśritya trāsamutsṛjya dūrataḥ

translations.english: Equipped with various weapons, do you speedily take yourself to Janasthāna-that field of carnage-which ere this contained the abode of Khara; and casting off fear at a distance, do you sojourn in vacant Janasthāna with all its Raksasas slain (by Rama).

verses.sanskrit:
बलं हि सुमहद्यन्मे जनस्थाने निवेशितम्
सदूषणखरं युद्धे हतं तद्रामसायकैः
verses.transliteration:
balaṁ hi sumahadyanme janasthāne niveśitam
sadūṣaṇakharaṁ yuddhe hataṁ tadrāmasāyakaiḥ

translations.english: A great many troops endued with exceeding prowess, who had been posted in Janasthāna, have, along with Düşana and Khara, been slain by the shafts of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रोधो ममापूर्वो धैर्यस्योपरि वर्धते
वैरं च सुमहज्जातं रामं प्रति सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ krodho mamāpūrvo dhairyasyopari vardhate
vairaṁ ca sumahajjātaṁ rāmaṁ prati sudāruṇam

translations.english: Hence unprecedented is my wrath, towering above my patience; and great and fierce also is the hostility I have conceived against Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्यातयितुमिच्छामि तच्च वैरमहं रिपोः
न हि लप्स्याम्यहं निद्रामहत्वा संयुगे रिपुम्
verses.transliteration:
niryātayitumicchāmi tacca vairamahaṁ ripoḥ
na hi lapsyāmyahaṁ nidrāmahatvā saṁyuge ripum

translations.english: I wish to avenge myself on my mighty enemy. Sleep find I none without slaying my foe in fight. Slaying that slayer of Khara and Dūşaņa, Rāma, I shall attain delight like to that attained by a pauper on gaining riches.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमादाच्च गन्तव्यं सर्वैरेव निशाचरैः
कर्तव्यश्च सदा यत्नो राघवस्य वधं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
apramādācca gantavyaṁ sarvaireva niśācaraiḥ
kartavyaśca sadā yatno rāghavasya vadhaṁ prati

translations.english: Staying in Janasthāna, you shall gather true information touching Rāma as to what he is about. Repair all you rangers of the night carefully, and strive yourselves always for slaying Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
युष्माकं हि बलज्ञोऽहं बहुशो रणमूर्धनि
अतश्चास्मिञ्जनस्थाने मया यूयं नियोजिताः
verses.transliteration:
yuṣmākaṁ hi balajño'haṁ bahuśo raṇamūrdhani
ataścāsmiñjanasthāne mayā yūyaṁ niyojitāḥ

translations.english: I have been well acquainted with your strength in many a field, and it is for this that I set you in Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रियं वाक्यमुपेत्य राक्षसा; महार्थमष्टावभिवाद्य रावणम्
विहाय लङ्कां सहिताः प्रतस्थिरे; यतो जनस्थानमलक्ष्यदर्शनाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ priyaṁ vākyamupetya rākṣasā; mahārthamaṣṭāvabhivādya rāvaṇam
vihāya laṅkāṁ sahitāḥ pratasthire; yato janasthānamalakṣyadarśanāḥ

translations.english: Hearing these agreeable and weighty words of Ravana, those Raksasas, bowing down to Rāvana, left Lankā, and in a body invisible proceeded in the direction of Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सीतामुपलभ्य रावणः; सुसंप्रहृष्टः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम्
प्रसज्य रामेण च वैरमुत्तमं; बभूव मोहान्मुदितः स राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sītāmupalabhya rāvaṇaḥ; susaṁprahṛṣṭaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm
prasajya rāmeṇa ca vairamuttamaṁ; babhūva mohānmuditaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Having obtained Mithilā's daughter, Rāvaņa experienced great joy in establishing her (in his own house); and having created high hostility with Rāma, Rāvana through blindness rejoiced greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
संदिश्य राक्षसान्घोरान्रावणोऽष्टौ महाबलान्
आत्मानं बुद्धिवैक्लव्यात्कृतकृत्यममन्यत
verses.transliteration:
saṁdiśya rākṣasānghorānrāvaṇo'ṣṭau mahābalān
ātmānaṁ buddhivaiklavyātkṛtakṛtyamamanyata

translations.english: Having commissioned those eight terrible and mighty Rākşasas, Rāvana, in consequence of perversion of sense, considered himself as crowned with success.

verses.sanskrit:
स चिन्तयानो वैदेहीं कामबाणसमर्पितः
प्रविवेश गृहं रम्यं सीतां द्रष्टुमभित्वरन्
verses.transliteration:
sa cintayāno vaidehīṁ kāmabāṇasamarpitaḥ
praviveśa gṛhaṁ ramyaṁ sītāṁ draṣṭumabhitvaran

translations.english: And brooding over Vaidehi, he, sore pierced by the shafts of Kāma, hastily entered his charming mansion, with the intention of secing Sitā.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां शोकभारावपीडिताम्
वायुवेगैरिवाक्रान्तां मज्जन्तीं नावमर्णवे
verses.transliteration:
aśrupūrṇamukhīṁ dīnāṁ śokabhārāvapīḍitām
vāyuvegairivākrāntāṁ majjantīṁ nāvamarṇave

translations.english: And entering that apartment, Rāvana-lord of Rākşasas-saw the distressed Sītā in the midst of the Raksasas, with a tearful countenance, oppressed with a load of grief, like to a bark sinking in the ocean through the violence of the winds; like to a doe separated from the herd of deer, and surrounded by dogs.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्यदुन्दुभिनिर्ह्रादं तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणम्
सोपानं काञ्चनं चित्रमारुरोह तया सह
verses.transliteration:
divyadundubhinirhrādaṁ taptakāñcanatoraṇam
sopānaṁ kāñcanaṁ citramāruroha tayā saha

translations.english: Rāvana in company with Şītā ascended the beautiful golden stairs, resounding with the sounds of kettle-drums and embellished with ornaments of burnished gold.

verses.sanskrit:
दान्तका राजताश्चैव गवाक्षाः प्रियदर्शनाः
हेमजालावृताश्चासंस्तत्र प्रासादपङ्क्तयः
verses.transliteration:
dāntakā rājatāścaiva gavākṣāḥ priyadarśanāḥ
hemajālāvṛtāścāsaṁstatra prāsādapaṅktayaḥ

translations.english: And those loftily edifices had excellent windows made of vory and silver, and covered with golden nets.

verses.sanskrit:
सुधामणिविचित्राणि भूमिभागानि सर्वशः
दशग्रीवः स्वभवने प्रादर्शयत मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
sudhāmaṇivicitrāṇi bhūmibhāgāni sarvaśaḥ
daśagrīvaḥ svabhavane prādarśayata maithilīm

translations.english: The ground all over was decorated with ambrosia and gems. The Ten-headed one in his own mansion showed to Maithilī large tanks and pools covered with various kinds of flowers. (All this) Rāvaņa showed to Sítā overmastered by sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शयित्वा तु वैदेहीं कृत्स्नं तद्भवनोत्तमम्
उवाच वाक्यं पापात्मा रावणो जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
darśayitvā tu vaidehīṁ kṛtsnaṁ tadbhavanottamam
uvāca vākyaṁ pāpātmā rāvaṇo janakātmajām

translations.english: And after having showed to Vaidehi the whole of that good lie of mansions, that wicked one, with the intention of tempting Sītā, spoke to her.

verses.sanskrit:
दशराक्षसकोट्यश्च द्वाविंशतिरथापराः
वर्जयित्वा जरा वृद्धान्बालांश्च रजनीचरान्
verses.transliteration:
daśarākṣasakoṭyaśca dvāviṁśatirathāparāḥ
varjayitvā jarā vṛddhānbālāṁśca rajanīcarān

translations.english: O Sītā, leaving out old men and boys, I am the lord of thirty two crore of night-rangers of terrible deeds. And a thousand come forward whenever required for any service.

verses.sanskrit:
यदिदं राज्यतन्त्रं मे त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्
जीवितं च विशालाक्षि त्वं मे प्राणैर्गरीयसी
verses.transliteration:
yadidaṁ rājyatantraṁ me tvayi sarvaṁ pratiṣṭhitam
jīvitaṁ ca viśālākṣi tvaṁ me prāṇairgarīyasī

translations.english: If such is my sovereignty, all this is established in you, O large-eyed lady, as well as my life. You are dearer to me than life.

verses.sanskrit:
बहूनां स्त्रीसहस्राणां मम योऽसौ परिग्रहः
तासां त्वमीश्वरी सीते मम भार्या भव प्रिये
verses.transliteration:
bahūnāṁ strīsahasrāṇāṁ mama yo'sau parigrahaḥ
tāsāṁ tvamīśvarī sīte mama bhāryā bhava priye

translations.english: O Sītā, be you the mistress of those numerous excellent women who are my wives. Dear, be you my wife.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु किं तेऽन्यया बुद्ध्या रोचयस्व वचो मम
भजस्व माभितप्तस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
sādhu kiṁ te'nyayā buddhyā rocayasva vaco mama
bhajasva mābhitaptasya prasādaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: This is for your good. Why should you act otherwise? Do you relish my speech. Do you bend your mind towards me. It behoves you to favour me, who am burning in the heat of desire).

verses.sanskrit:
परिक्षिप्ता समुद्रेण लङ्केयं शतयोजना
नेयं धर्षयितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
parikṣiptā samudreṇa laṅkeyaṁ śatayojanā
neyaṁ dharṣayituṁ śakyā sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: This Larkă measuring an hundred Yojanas girt round by the ocean, is incapable of being harassed by the celestials themselves headed by Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
न देवेषु न यक्षेषु न गन्धर्वेषु नर्षिषु
अहं पश्यामि लोकेषु यो मे वीर्यसमो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
na deveṣu na yakṣeṣu na gandharveṣu narṣiṣu
ahaṁ paśyāmi lokeṣu yo me vīryasamo bhavet

translations.english: Neither among the celestials nor Yakşãs nor Gandharvas nor Serpents, find I any one that can match me in prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तापसेन गतायुषा
किं करिष्यसि रामेण मानुषेणाल्पतेजसा
verses.transliteration:
rājyabhraṣṭena dīnena tāpasena gatāyuṣā
kiṁ kariṣyasi rāmeṇa mānuṣeṇālpatejasā

translations.english: What will you do with Rāma a human being of short life, poor, of small prowess, practising mendicancy?

verses.sanskrit:
भजस्व सीते मामेव भर्ताहं सदृशस्तव
यौवनं ह्यध्रुवं भीरु रमस्वेह मया सह
verses.transliteration:
bhajasva sīte māmeva bhartāhaṁ sadṛśastava
yauvanaṁ hyadhruvaṁ bhīru ramasveha mayā saha

translations.english: O Sītā, bend your mind to me. I am a fit husband for you. O timed one, youth is uncertain. Sport with me here.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शने मा कृथा बुद्धिं राघवस्य वरानने
कास्य शक्तिरिहागन्तुमपि सीते मनोरथैः
verses.transliteration:
darśane mā kṛthā buddhiṁ rāghavasya varānane
kāsya śaktirihāgantumapi sīte manorathaiḥ

translations.english: And, O you of a handsome countenance, do not wish for the sight of Rāghava. O Sītā, what power has he to come hither even in thought?

verses.sanskrit:
न शक्यो वायुराकाशे पाशैर्बद्धं महाजवः
दीप्यमानस्य वाप्यग्नेर्ग्रहीतुं विमलां शिखाम्
verses.transliteration:
na śakyo vāyurākāśe pāśairbaddhaṁ mahājavaḥ
dīpyamānasya vāpyagnergrahītuṁ vimalāṁ śikhām

translations.english: None can fetter the exceedingly fleet wind in the sky, or hold the bright flame of a burning fire.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां न तं पश्यामि शोभने
विक्रमेण नयेद्यस्त्वां मद्बाहुपरिपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṁ na taṁ paśyāmi śobhane
vikrameṇa nayedyastvāṁ madbāhuparipālitām

translations.english: O beauteous one, in these three worlds I find no one that can by his might carry you away, who are protected by my arms.

verses.sanskrit:
दुष्कृतं यत्पुरा कर्म वनवासेन तद्गतम्
यश्च ते सुकृतो धर्मस्तस्येह फलमाप्नुहि
verses.transliteration:
duṣkṛtaṁ yatpurā karma vanavāsena tadgatam
yaśca te sukṛto dharmastasyeha phalamāpnuhi

translations.english: Laving your limbs with water, do you gratify me. The evil that you had done, has been expiated by your life in the forest: now do you reap the fruit of your good deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
इह सर्वाणि माल्यानि दिव्यगन्धानि मैथिलि
भूषणानि च मुख्यानि तानि सेव मया सह
verses.transliteration:
iha sarvāṇi mālyāni divyagandhāni maithili
bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni tāni seva mayā saha

translations.english: Here are garlands furnished with divine fragrance, and, O Maithili, superb ornaments. Enjoy you all those along with me.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पकं नाम सुश्रोणि भ्रातुर्वैश्रवणस्य मे
विमानं रमणीयं च तद्विमानं मनोजवम्
verses.transliteration:
puṣpakaṁ nāma suśroṇi bhrāturvaiśravaṇasya me
vimānaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ ca tadvimānaṁ manojavam

translations.english: O you of shapely hips, the car called Pușpaka, resembling the sun, which (formerly) belonged to my brother Vaiśravaņa, was through my prowess won by me in fight. And vast and beautiful is that car furnished with the speed of the mind. Do you, O Sītā, at your pleasure sport on it along with me.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकार्तं तु वरारोहे न भ्राजति वरानने
अलं व्रीडेन वैदेहि धर्मलोप कृतेन ते
verses.transliteration:
śokārtaṁ tu varārohe na bhrājati varānane
alaṁ vrīḍena vaidehi dharmalopa kṛtena te

translations.english: Your face stainless and lovely to look at, resembling the lotus, dose not, O you of a comely countenance, O magnificent damsel, appear beautiful in consequence of your being exercised with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादं कुरु मे क्षिप्रं वश्यो दासोऽहमस्मि ते
नेमाः शून्या मया वाचः शुष्यमाणेन भाषिताः
verses.transliteration:
prasādaṁ kuru me kṣipraṁ vaśyo dāso'hamasmi te
nemāḥ śūnyā mayā vācaḥ śuṣyamāṇena bhāṣitāḥ

translations.english: These tender feet of yours I press upon my heads. Do you speedily show your favour to me. I am your slave (ever) obedient to you.

verses.sanskrit:
न चापि रावणः कांचिन्मूर्ध्ना स्त्रीं प्रणमेत ह
एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
na cāpi rāvaṇaḥ kāṁcinmūrdhnā strīṁ praṇameta ha
evamuktvā daśagrīvo maithilīṁ janakātmajām

translations.english: Let not these words of mine spoken by me under the withering influence of love prove fruitless. Rāvana has never bowed his head to any female. Having said this, the Ten-headed one, come under the subjection of the Destroyer, looked upon Maithili, Janaka's daughter (as his own) saying, She is mine.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तथोक्ता तु वैदेही निर्भया शोककर्षिता
तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा रावणं प्रत्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarṣitā
tṛṇamantarataḥ kṛtvā rāvaṇaṁ pratyabhāṣata

translations.english: Having been thus addressed, Vaidehī unaffected by fear, although exercised with grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Rāvana, answered him.

verses.sanskrit:
रामो नाम स धर्मात्मा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः
दीर्घबाहुर्विशालाक्षो दैवतं स पतिर्मम
verses.transliteration:
rāmo nāma sa dharmātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
dīrghabāhurviśālākṣo daivataṁ sa patirmama

translations.english: There was a king named Dasaratha, the bridge of righteousness, like to a mountain, ever bearing regard towards the truth, and renowned among men, whose son is Rāghava. He is named Rāma, and is righteous-souled and celebrated over the three worlds. he is long-armed, of expansive eyes, like to a celestial—he is my husband.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातः सिंहस्कन्धो महाद्युतिः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा यस्ते प्राणां हरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ kule jātaḥ siṁhaskandho mahādyutiḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā yaste prāṇāṁ hariṣyati

translations.english: Born in the race of the Ikşvākus, the has the shoulders of a lion and is possessed of exceeding effulgence-the same that along with his brother, Laksmana, shall take your life. If you had wronged me forcibly in his presence, you would have slain in battle in Janasthāna even as Khara.

verses.sanskrit:
य एते राक्षसाः प्रोक्ता घोररूपा महाबलाः
राघवे निर्विषाः सर्वे सुपर्णे पन्नगा यथा
verses.transliteration:
ya ete rākṣasāḥ proktā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ
rāghave nirviṣāḥ sarve suparṇe pannagā yathā

translations.english: All the mighty Rākşasas of grim visages, whom you have extolled (before me), shall be deprived of their venom before Rāma, as serpents are before Suparna,

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ज्याविप्रमुक्तास्ते शराः काञ्चनभूषणाः
शरीरं विधमिष्यन्ति गङ्गाकूलमिवोर्मयः
verses.transliteration:
tasya jyāvipramuktāste śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
śarīraṁ vidhamiṣyanti gaṅgākūlamivormayaḥ

translations.english: The shafts decorated with gold shot by the bow-string of Rāghava, shall pierce their bodies, as the waves of the Ganga (beat against) her banks.

verses.sanskrit:
असुरैर्वा सुरैर्वा त्वं यद्यवधोऽसि रावण
उत्पाद्य सुमहद्वैरं जीवंस्तस्य न मोक्ष्यसे
verses.transliteration:
asurairvā surairvā tvaṁ yadyavadho'si rāvaṇa
utpādya sumahadvairaṁ jīvaṁstasya na mokṣyase

translations.english: Although, O Rāvana, you may be incapable of being slain either by the gods or the Asuras, yet having roused the high hostility of Rāghava, you will not be able to liberate your life.

verses.sanskrit:
स ते जीवितशेषस्य राघवोऽन्तकरो बली
पशोर्यूपगतस्येव जीवितं तव दुर्लभम्
verses.transliteration:
sa te jīvitaśeṣasya rāghavo'ntakaro balī
paśoryūpagatasyeva jīvitaṁ tava durlabham

translations.english: The strong Rāghava will compass the end of what remains of your life. Like the life of a beast tied to the sacrificial stake, your own is incapable of being reclaimed.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि पश्येत्स रामस्त्वां रोषदीप्तेन चक्षुषा
रक्षस्त्वमद्य निर्दग्धो गच्छेः सद्यः पराभवम्
verses.transliteration:
yadi paśyetsa rāmastvāṁ roṣadīptena cakṣuṣā
rakṣastvamadya nirdagdho gaccheḥ sadyaḥ parābhavam

translations.english: Should Rāma look at you with eyes aglow with anger, you, O Raksasa, would be consumed even as Manmatha was by, Rudra.

verses.sanskrit:
यश्चन्द्रं नभसो भूमौ पातयेन्नाशयेत वा
सागरं शोषयेद्वापि स सीतां मोचयेदिह
verses.transliteration:
yaścandraṁ nabhaso bhūmau pātayennāśayeta vā
sāgaraṁ śoṣayedvāpi sa sītāṁ mocayediha

translations.english: He who is able to bring down the Moon or destroy him, and to drink up the ocean dry, will surely liberate Sītā from here.

verses.sanskrit:
गतायुस्त्वं गतश्रीको गतसत्त्वो गतेन्द्रियः
लङ्का वैधव्यसंयुक्ता त्वत्कृतेन भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
gatāyustvaṁ gataśrīko gatasattvo gatendriyaḥ
laṅkā vaidhavyasaṁyuktā tvatkṛtena bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Your days are numbered, and auspiciousness has bidden you adieu. You are shorn of strength, and your senses have been dulled. And it is owing to you that Larkā shall be subject to widowhood.

verses.sanskrit:
न ते पापमिदं कर्म सुखोदर्कं भविष्यति
याहं नीता विना भावं पतिपार्श्वात्त्वया वनात्
verses.transliteration:
na te pāpamidaṁ karma sukhodarkaṁ bhaviṣyati
yāhaṁ nītā vinā bhāvaṁ patipārśvāttvayā vanāt

translations.english: That you by force have for naught carried me away from the side of my husband-this sinful act can never conduce to your felicity.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि दैवतसंयुक्तो मम भर्ता महाद्युतिः
निर्भयो वीर्यमाश्रित्य शून्ये वसति दण्डके
verses.transliteration:
sa hi daivatasaṁyukto mama bhartā mahādyutiḥ
nirbhayo vīryamāśritya śūnye vasati daṇḍake

translations.english: That exceedingly effulgent lord of mine along with my husband's younger brother, summoning up their energy, is fearlessly dwelling in the vacant Dandaka.

verses.sanskrit:
स ते दर्पं बलं वीर्यमुत्सेकं च तथाविधम्
अपनेष्यति गात्रेभ्यः शरवर्षेण संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
sa te darpaṁ balaṁ vīryamutsekaṁ ca tathāvidham
apaneṣyati gātrebhyaḥ śaravarṣeṇa saṁyuge

translations.english: By means of an arrowy shower in conflict, he will take your prowess and strength, your hauteur and wickedness out of your person,

verses.sanskrit:
यदा विनाशो भूतानां दृश्यते कालचोदितः
तदा कार्ये प्रमाद्यन्ति नराः कालवशं गताः
verses.transliteration:
yadā vināśo bhūtānāṁ dṛśyate kālacoditaḥ
tadā kārye pramādyanti narāḥ kālavaśaṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: When urged by the Destroyer, the destruction of creatures is perceptible, then, coming under the sway of the Destroyer, men become careless in their actions.

verses.sanskrit:
मां प्रधृष्य स ते कालः प्राप्तोऽयं रक्षसाधम
आत्मनो राक्षसानां च वधायान्तःपुरस्य च
verses.transliteration:
māṁ pradhṛṣya sa te kālaḥ prāpto'yaṁ rakṣasādhama
ātmano rākṣasānāṁ ca vadhāyāntaḥpurasya ca

translations.english: Having outraged me, you, O worst of Rāks asas your time come; for compassing your own destruction as well as that of the Rākşasas and those dwelling in your inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
न शक्या यज्ञमध्यस्था वेदिः स्रुग्भाण्ड मण्डिता
द्विजातिमन्त्रसंपूता चण्डालेनावमर्दितुम्
verses.transliteration:
na śakyā yajñamadhyasthā vediḥ srugbhāṇḍa maṇḍitā
dvijātimantrasaṁpūtā caṇḍālenāvamarditum

translations.english: A Candāla cannot tread the dais reared the midst of a sacrifice beauteous with ladies, and vessels, and sanctified by the twice-born ones.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं शरीरं निःसंज्ञं बन्ध वा घातयस्व वा
नेदं शरीरं रक्ष्यं मे जीवितं वापि राक्षस
न हि शक्ष्याम्युपक्रोशं पृथिव्यां दातुमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ śarīraṁ niḥsaṁjñaṁ bandha vā ghātayasva vā
nedaṁ śarīraṁ rakṣyaṁ me jīvitaṁ vāpi rākṣasa
na hi śakṣyāmyupakrośaṁ pṛthivyāṁ dātumātmanaḥ

translations.english: Do you either bind or destroy this body deprived of sensation. This body will I not protect, nor yet this life, O Rāvana;

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही क्रोद्धात्सुपरुषं वचः
रावणं मैथिली तत्र पुनर्नोवाच किंचन
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu vaidehī kroddhātsuparuṣaṁ vacaḥ
rāvaṇaṁ maithilī tatra punarnovāca kiṁcana

translations.english: And I shall not be able to bring blame on myself in this world. having said these harsh words in wrath, Videha's daughter, Janaki, did not there again say anything to Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं रोमहर्षणम्
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां भयसंदर्शनं वचः
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā paruṣaṁ romaharṣaṇam
pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṁ bhayasaṁdarśanaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Sita's words, harsh and calculated to make one's down stand on end, Rāvana answered her in words tending to excite one's apprehension,

verses.sanskrit:
शृणु मैथिलि मद्वाक्यं मासान्द्वादश भामिनि
कालेनानेन नाभ्येषि यदि मां चारुहासिनि
ततस्त्वां प्रातराशार्थं सूदाश्छेत्स्यन्ति लेशशः
verses.transliteration:
śṛṇu maithili madvākyaṁ māsāndvādaśa bhāmini
kālenānena nābhyeṣi yadi māṁ cāruhāsini
tatastvāṁ prātarāśārthaṁ sūdāśchetsyanti leśaśaḥ

translations.english: Hear, O Maithili, my words. O damsel if, O you of sweet smiles, within this time you do not turn yourself to me, the cooks shall cut you off in pieces to serve my morning mcal.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणः शत्रुरावणः
राक्षसीश्च ततः क्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
rākṣasīśca tataḥ kruddha idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Having herself spoken thus, Ravana-challenger of foes-growing exceedingly wroth, addressed the Rākşasis in these words,

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रमेवं हि राक्षस्यो विकृता घोरदर्शनाः
दर्पमस्या विनेष्यन्तु मांसशोणितभोजनाः
verses.transliteration:
śīghramevaṁ hi rākṣasyo vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ
darpamasyā vineṣyantu māṁsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ

translations.english: You frightful Rākşasīs terrible to behold, subsisting on flesh and gore, do you at once crush her pride.

verses.sanskrit:
वचनादेव तास्तस्य विकृता घोरदर्शनाः
कृतप्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा मैथिलीं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
vacanādeva tāstasya vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ
kṛtaprāñjalayo bhūtvā maithilīṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: As soon as he had said this, those frightful and terrible Rākṣasīs with joined hands encircled Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
स ताः प्रोवाच राजा तु रावणो घोरदर्शनः
प्रचाल्य चरणोत्कर्षैर्दारयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tāḥ provāca rājā tu rāvaṇo ghoradarśanaḥ
pracālya caraṇotkarṣairdārayanniva medinīm

translations.english: Then the grim-visaged king Ravana, as if riving the earth by his tread, proceeding a pace or two, said,

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकवनिकामध्ये मैथिली नीयतामिति
तत्रेयं रक्ष्यतां गूढमुष्माभिः परिवारिता
verses.transliteration:
aśokavanikāmadhye maithilī nīyatāmiti
tatreyaṁ rakṣyatāṁ gūḍhamuṣmābhiḥ parivāritā

translations.english: Do you take Maithilī to the wood of Asokas. There surrounding her, do you secretly guard her; and there (sometimes) by storming, and (at other) by means of soft speech, do you all strive to bring Mithila's daughter, like a wild female elephant, under your sway.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैर्नानापुष्पफलैर्वृताम्
सर्वकालमदैश्चापि द्विजैः समुपसेविताम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvakāmaphalairvṛkṣairnānāpuṣpaphalairvṛtām
sarvakālamadaiścāpi dvijaiḥ samupasevitām

translations.english: Thus commanded by Rāvana, those Rākşasis taking Maithili along with them, went to the Asoka wood, abounding with trees granting every desire, and filled with various kinds of fruits and flowers, and frequented by fowls fraught with juices at all seasons.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु शोकपरीताङ्गी मैथिली जनकात्मजा
राक्षसी वशमापन्ना व्याघ्रीणां हरिणी यथा
verses.transliteration:
sā tu śokaparītāṅgī maithilī janakātmajā
rākṣasī vaśamāpannā vyāghrīṇāṁ hariṇī yathā

translations.english: And as a doe comes under the subjection of tigresses, Janaka's daughter, Maithili, her frame worked up with grief, came under the sway of the Raksasis.

verses.sanskrit:
न विन्दते तत्र तु शर्म मैथिली; विरूपनेत्राभिरतीव तर्जिता
पतिं स्मरन्ती दयितं च देवरं; विचेतनाभूद्भयशोकपीडिता
verses.transliteration:
na vindate tatra tu śarma maithilī; virūpanetrābhiratīva tarjitā
patiṁ smarantī dayitaṁ ca devaraṁ; vicetanābhūdbhayaśokapīḍitā

translations.english: And greatly up-braided by the fierce eyes (of the Raksasis), Maithili did not know repose; and, afflicted with grief and fear, she, remembering her beloved lord along with Lakşmaņa swooned away.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसं मृगरूपेण चरन्तं कामरूपिणम्
निहत्य रामो मारीचं तूर्णं पथि न्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasaṁ mṛgarūpeṇa carantaṁ kāmarūpiṇam
nihatya rāmo mārīcaṁ tūrṇaṁ pathi nyavartata

translations.english: Killing the Rākṣasa, Mārīca assuming shapes at will and ranging in the shape of a deer, Rāma vended speedily his way.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य संत्वरमाणस्य द्रष्टुकामस्य मैथिलीम्
क्रूरस्वरोऽथ गोमायुर्विननादास्य पृष्ठतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya saṁtvaramāṇasya draṣṭukāmasya maithilīm
krūrasvaro'tha gomāyurvinanādāsya pṛṣṭhataḥ

translations.english: And as he hurried himself, eager to behold Maithilī, jackals began to howl hideously at his back.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य स्वरमाज्ञाय दारुणं रोमहर्षणम्
चिन्तयामास गोमायोः स्वरेण परिशङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya svaramājñāya dāruṇaṁ romaharṣaṇam
cintayāmāsa gomāyoḥ svareṇa pariśaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing their harsh cries, capable of making one's hair stand on end, Rāma struck with fear at the voices of the jackals, became filled with alarm.

verses.sanskrit:
अशुभं बत मन्येऽहं गोमायुर्वाश्यते यथा
स्वस्ति स्यादपि वैदेह्या राक्षसैर्भक्षणं विना
verses.transliteration:
aśubhaṁ bata manye'haṁ gomāyurvāśyate yathā
svasti syādapi vaidehyā rākṣasairbhakṣaṇaṁ vinā

translations.english: Ah! I consider this as inauspicious—that these jackals are crying. Escaping being devoured by the Raksasas, may fair fortune befall Vaidehi!

verses.sanskrit:
स सौमित्रिः स्वरं श्रुत्वा तां च हित्वाथ मैथिलीम्
तयैव प्रहितः क्षिप्रं मत्सकाशमिहैष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sa saumitriḥ svaraṁ śrutvā tāṁ ca hitvātha maithilīm
tayaiva prahitaḥ kṣipraṁ matsakāśamihaiṣyati

translations.english: If Laksmana should have heard the cries which Mārica, knowing my voice, and fixing on the means of harming me, uttered in the form of a deer, Saumitrī, hearing that voice, leaving Mithila's daughter and commissioned by herself, must have come near me.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसैः सहितैर्नूनं सीताया ईप्सितो वधः
काञ्चनश्च मृगो भूत्वा व्यपनीयाश्रमात्तु माम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasaiḥ sahitairnūnaṁ sītāyā īpsito vadhaḥ
kāñcanaśca mṛgo bhūtvā vyapanīyāśramāttu mām

translations.english: Surely, the Rākṣasas in a body are desirous of slaying Sitä. Becoming a golden deer, Mārica, having allured me far, transformed himself into a Rākşasa, as soon as he had been struck with my shafts; and exclaimed, 'Ah! Laksmana, slain am I.'

verses.sanskrit:
अपि स्वस्ति भवेद्द्वाभ्यां रहिताभ्यां मया वने
जनस्थाननिमित्तं हि कृतवैरोऽस्मि राक्षसैः
निमित्तानि च घोराणि दृश्यन्तेऽद्य बहूनि च
verses.transliteration:
api svasti bhaveddvābhyāṁ rahitābhyāṁ mayā vane
janasthānanimittaṁ hi kṛtavairo'smi rākṣasaiḥ
nimittāni ca ghorāṇi dṛśyante'dya bahūni ca

translations.english: It is doubtless, we having left (Sītā, whether all is well with her. I having raised the hostility of the Räksasas for the sake of Janasthāna;

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं चिन्तयन्रामः श्रुत्वा गोमायुनिःस्वनम्
आत्मनश्चापनयनं मृगरूपेण रक्षसा
आजगाम जनस्थानं राघवः परिशङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ cintayanrāmaḥ śrutvā gomāyuniḥsvanam
ātmanaścāpanayanaṁ mṛgarūpeṇa rakṣasā
ājagāma janasthānaṁ rāghavaḥ pariśaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: Rāghava went back to Janasthāna, alarmed in consequence of his having been drawn away by the Raksasa in the form of a dear.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दीनमानसं दीनमासेदुर्मृगपक्षिणः
सव्यं कृत्वा महात्मानं घोरांश्च ससृजुः स्वरान्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dīnamānasaṁ dīnamāsedurmṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
savyaṁ kṛtvā mahātmānaṁ ghorāṁśca sasṛjuḥ svarān

translations.english: And birds and beasts approached that highsouled one distressed and depressed in spirit; and staying on his left set up frightful cries.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि महाघोराणि राघवः
ततो लक्षणमायान्तं ददर्श विगतप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
tāni dṛṣṭvā nimittāni mahāghorāṇi rāghavaḥ
tato lakṣaṇamāyāntaṁ dadarśa vigataprabham

translations.english: As he was witnessing the exceedingly dreadful signs, Rāghava saw Lakşmaņa coming with a lacklustre (countenance); and Lakşmaņa came up to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
संजगर्हेऽथ तं भ्राता जेष्ठो लक्ष्मणमागतम्
विहाय सीतां विजने वने राक्षससेविते
