verses.transliteration:
saṁjagarhe'tha taṁ bhrātā jeṣṭho lakṣmaṇamāgatam
vihāya sītāṁ vijane vane rākṣasasevite

translations.english: And depressed in spirit, he was rendered still more sad by that one who, afflicted with depression shared his sorrow. And, seeing that (Laksmana) bad come, leaving Sita in that solitary wood frequented by Rākşasas, his brother fell to reprimanding him.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीत्वा च करं सव्यं लक्ष्मणं रघुनन्दनः
उवाच मधुरोदर्कमिदं परुषमार्तवत्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītvā ca karaṁ savyaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ raghunandanaḥ
uvāca madhurodarkamidaṁ paruṣamārtavat

translations.english: And taking Lakşmaņa's left hand, the son of Raghu in extreme distress sweetly spoke these rough words,

verses.sanskrit:
अहो लक्ष्मण गर्ह्यं ते कृतं यत्त्वं विहाय ताम्
सीतामिहागतः सौम्य कच्चित्स्वस्ति भवेदिति
verses.transliteration:
aho lakṣmaṇa garhyaṁ te kṛtaṁ yattvaṁ vihāya tām
sītāmihāgataḥ saumya kaccitsvasti bhavediti

translations.english: Alas! Laksmana, you have committed a censurable.,act; leaving Sita, O mild one, you have come hither. Is it well with her?

verses.sanskrit:
न मेऽस्ति संशयो वीर सर्वथा जनकात्मजा
विनष्टा भक्षिता वाप राक्षसैर्वनचारिभिः
verses.transliteration:
na me'sti saṁśayo vīra sarvathā janakātmajā
vinaṣṭā bhakṣitā vāpa rākṣasairvanacāribhiḥ

translations.english: I make no doubt, O hero, but that Janaka's daughter has either been slain or devoured by Rākṣasas ranging the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
अशुभान्येव भूयिष्ठं यथा प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे
अपि लक्ष्मण सीतायाः सामग्र्यं प्राप्नुयावहे
verses.transliteration:
aśubhānyeva bhūyiṣṭhaṁ yathā prādurbhavanti me
api lakṣmaṇa sītāyāḥ sāmagryaṁ prāpnuyāvahe

translations.english: And, considering the many omens that take place before me, O Laksmana, I do not know whether we shall light upon welfare of Janaka's daughter Sita being alive, O best of men.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं हि रक्षोमृगसंनिकाशं; प्रलोभ्य मां दूरमनुप्रयातम्
हतं कथंचिन्महता श्रमेण; स राक्षसोऽभून्म्रियमाण एव
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ hi rakṣomṛgasaṁnikāśaṁ; pralobhya māṁ dūramanuprayātam
hataṁ kathaṁcinmahatā śrameṇa; sa rākṣaso'bhūnmriyamāṇa eva

translations.english: This Rākşasa, who, wearing the shape of a deer, and, alluring me, had drawn me far, has in some sort been slain by me wiih much ado; and he became a Rāksasa at the time of his death.

verses.sanskrit:
मनश्च मे दीनमिहाप्रहृष्टं; चक्षुश्च सव्यं कुरुते विकारम्
असंशयं लक्ष्मण नास्ति सीता; हृता मृता वा पथि वर्तते वा
verses.transliteration:
manaśca me dīnamihāprahṛṣṭaṁ; cakṣuśca savyaṁ kurute vikāram
asaṁśayaṁ lakṣmaṇa nāsti sītā; hṛtā mṛtā vā pathi vartate vā

translations.english: Yet my mind is poor and cheerless; and my left eye throbs. Doubtless, O Laksmana, Sita is not, she is either carried away, or dead, or is wandering on the way. SECITION 58

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं दीनं शून्ये दशरथात्मजः
पर्यपृच्छत धर्मात्मा वैदेहीमागतं विना
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṁ dīnaṁ śūnye daśarathātmajaḥ
paryapṛcchata dharmātmā vaidehīmāgataṁ vinā

translations.english: Seeing Lakşmana cast down, cheerless, and come without Vaidehī, the righteous son of Dasaratha, asked him.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रस्थितं दण्डकारण्यं या मामनुजगाम ह
क्व सा लक्ष्मण वैदेही यां हित्वा त्वमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
prasthitaṁ daṇḍakāraṇyaṁ yā māmanujagāma ha
kva sā lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yāṁ hitvā tvamihāgataḥ

translations.english: Where, O Laksmana is that Vaidehi, who has followed me to the Dandaka forest, and leaving whom you have come hither?

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यभ्रष्टस्य दीनस्य दण्डकान्परिधावतः
क्व सा दुःखसहाया मे वैदेही तनुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
rājyabhraṣṭasya dīnasya daṇḍakānparidhāvataḥ
kva sā duḥkhasahāyā me vaidehī tanumadhyamā

translations.english: Where is that one of a slender waist, who is the help in trouble of me, deprived of my kingdom, dispirited, and running about the Dandakas?

verses.sanskrit:
यां विना नोत्सहे वीर मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्
क्व सा प्राणसहाया मे सीता सुरसुतोपमा
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ vinā notsahe vīra muhūrtamapi jīvitum
kva sā prāṇasahāyā me sītā surasutopamā

translations.english: Without whom, O hero, I cannot live for a moment-where is that life's help of me Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial?

verses.sanskrit:
पतित्वममराणां वा पृथिव्याश्चापि लक्ष्मण
विना तां तपनीयाभां नेच्छेयं जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
patitvamamarāṇāṁ vā pṛthivyāścāpi lakṣmaṇa
vinā tāṁ tapanīyābhāṁ neccheyaṁ janakātmajām

translations.english: O Laksmana, without Janaka's daughter (hued) like burning gold, I covet not the sovereignty of the celestials or the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिज्जीवति वैदेही प्राणैः प्रियतरा मम
कच्चित्प्रव्राजनं सौम्य न मे मिथ्या भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
kaccijjīvati vaidehī prāṇaiḥ priyatarā mama
kaccitpravrājanaṁ saumya na me mithyā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Is Vaidehī, dearer to me than my life still living? Shall this exile of mine be of no avail?

verses.sanskrit:
सीतानिमित्तं सौमित्रे मृते मयि गते त्वयि
कच्चित्सकामा सुखिता कैकेयी सा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sītānimittaṁ saumitre mṛte mayi gate tvayi
kaccitsakāmā sukhitā kaikeyī sā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O Sumitrā's son, on my dying for Sītā and your returning (to the city). shall Kaikeyi have her desire, and attain felicity; and shall Kausalyā, her son dead, and herself wearing the guise of a female mendicant, humbly wait upon Kaikeyi when she shall have succeeded in obtaining the kingdom for her son?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि जीवति वैदेही गमिष्याम्याश्रमं पुनः
सुवृत्ता यदि वृत्ता सा प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
yadi jīvati vaidehī gamiṣyāmyāśramaṁ punaḥ
suvṛttā yadi vṛttā sā prāṇāṁstyakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: If Vaidehī live, I will then return to the asylum; but O Lakşmaņa, if that one of excellent character should happen to be dead, I will also renounce my life.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मामाश्रमगतं वैदेही नाभिभाषते
पुनः प्रहसिता सीता विनशिष्यामि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
yadi māmāśramagataṁ vaidehī nābhibhāṣate
punaḥ prahasitā sītā vinaśiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: If, O Laksmana, Vaidehi ever precluding her speech with a smile should not speak to me when I arrive at the asylum, I shall give up my life.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूहि लक्ष्मण वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा
त्वयि प्रमत्ते रक्षोभिर्भक्षिता वा तपस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
brūhi lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā
tvayi pramatte rakṣobhirbhakṣitā vā tapasvinī

translations.english: tell me, O Laksmana, whether Do you Videha's daughter live or not; or whether, in consequence of your acting heedlessly, that forlorn wench has been devoured by Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकुमारी च बाला च नित्यं चादुःखदर्शिनी
मद्वियोगेन वैदेही व्यक्तं शोचति दुर्मनाः
verses.transliteration:
sukumārī ca bālā ca nityaṁ cāduḥkhadarśinī
madviyogena vaidehī vyaktaṁ śocati durmanāḥ

translations.english: Of a tender frame, and a mere girl, Vaidehi, never having experienced unhappiness being cast down, surely weep for my separation.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा रक्षसा तेन जिह्मेन सुदुरात्मना
वदता लक्ष्मणेत्युच्चैस्तवापि जनितं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā rakṣasā tena jihmena sudurātmanā
vadatā lakṣmaṇetyuccaistavāpi janitaṁ bhayam

translations.english: When that exceedingly wicked Rākşasa cried, Lakşmaņa at the top of his voice, was you also seized with fear?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतश्च शङ्के वैदेह्या स स्वरः सदृशो मम
त्रस्तया प्रेषितस्त्वं च द्रष्टुं मां शीघ्रमागतः
verses.transliteration:
śrutaśca śaṅke vaidehyā sa svaraḥ sadṛśo mama
trastayā preṣitastvaṁ ca draṣṭuṁ māṁ śīghramāgataḥ

translations.english: And I apprehend that voice resembling mine was heard by Vaidehī; and, despatched by her from fear, you may have come hither swiftly to see* me. Some texts-to rescue me.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा तु कृतं कष्टं सीतामुत्सृजता वने
प्रतिकर्तुं नृशंसानां रक्षसां दत्तमन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā tu kṛtaṁ kaṣṭaṁ sītāmutsṛjatā vane
pratikartuṁ nṛśaṁsānāṁ rakṣasāṁ dattamantaram

translations.english: You have every way acted unwisely in having left Şītā alone in the wood. By this you have afforded opportunity to the cruel Rākşasas to repair the mischief (I have done them).

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखिताः खरघातेन राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः
तैः सीता निहता घोरैर्भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhitāḥ kharaghātena rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
taiḥ sītā nihatā ghorairbhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: The Rākşasas subsisting flesh are aggrieved because of Khara having been slain; and now, without doubt, those terrible ones have slain Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
अहोऽस्मि व्यसने मग्नः सर्वथा रिपुनाशन
किं त्विदानीं करिष्यामि शङ्के प्राप्तव्यमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
aho'smi vyasane magnaḥ sarvathā ripunāśana
kiṁ tvidānīṁ kariṣyāmi śaṅke prāptavyamīdṛśam

translations.english: Alas! absolutely sunk am I in peril, O destroyer of foes. What shall I do now? I fear such an event was appointed for me.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सीतां वरारोहां चिन्तयन्नेव राघवः
आजगाम जनस्थानं त्वरया सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
iti sītāṁ varārohāṁ cintayanneva rāghavaḥ
ājagāma janasthānaṁ tvarayā sahalakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thus thinking of Sītā, paragon among women, Rāghava hastily went to Janasthāna in company with Laksmana. on

verses.sanskrit:
विगर्हमाणोऽनुजमार्तरूपं; क्षुधा श्रमाच्चैव पिपासया च
विनिःश्वसञ्शुष्कमुखो विषण्णः; प्रतिश्रयं प्राप्य समीक्ष्य शून्यम्
verses.transliteration:
vigarhamāṇo'nujamārtarūpaṁ; kṣudhā śramāccaiva pipāsayā ca
viniḥśvasañśuṣkamukho viṣaṇṇaḥ; pratiśrayaṁ prāpya samīkṣya śūnyam

translations.english: Taking to task his younger brother of distressed visage, Rāma, afflicted with hunger and thirst, and dejected in spirits, sighing heavily with a countenance turned pale, entered the asylum and found it vacant.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वमाश्रमं संप्रविगाह्य वीरो; विहारदेशाननुसृत्य कांश्चित्
एतत्तदित्येव निवासभूमौ; प्रहृष्टरोमा व्यथितो बभूव
verses.transliteration:
svamāśramaṁ saṁpravigāhya vīro; vihāradeśānanusṛtya kāṁścit
etattadityeva nivāsabhūmau; prahṛṣṭaromā vyathito babhūva

translations.english: And entering his own asylum that hero went to the play-grounds (of Sītā) and remembering the sporting ground (of Sītā) in that abode, he was filled with grief and his down stood on end.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाश्रमादुपावृत्तमन्तरा रघुनन्दनः
परिपप्रच्छ सौमित्रिं रामो दुःखार्दितः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
athāśramādupāvṛttamantarā raghunandanaḥ
paripapraccha saumitriṁ rāmo duḥkhārditaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Then coming out of the hermitage, Raghu's descendant, Rāma, after a while, from grief, spoke these words to the son of Sumitrā,

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच किमर्थं त्वमागतोऽपास्य मैथिलीम्
यदा सा तव विश्वासाद्वने विहरिता मया
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca kimarthaṁ tvamāgato'pāsya maithilīm
yadā sā tava viśvāsādvane viharitā mayā

translations.english: When confiding myself in you, I had left Maithilī with you in the wood, why then did you go out, leaving her behind?

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वैवाभ्यागतं त्वां मे मैथिलीं त्यज्य लक्ष्मण
शङ्कमानं महत्पापं यत्सत्यं व्यथितं मनः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvaivābhyāgataṁ tvāṁ me maithilīṁ tyajya lakṣmaṇa
śaṅkamānaṁ mahatpāpaṁ yatsatyaṁ vyathitaṁ manaḥ

translations.english: O Laksmana, directly I saw you approach, renouncing Maithilī, my mind, apprehending great wrong, became really aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
स्फुरते नयनं सव्यं बाहुश्च हृदयं च मे
दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मण दूरे त्वां सीताविरहितं पथि
verses.transliteration:
sphurate nayanaṁ savyaṁ bāhuśca hṛdayaṁ ca me
dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇa dūre tvāṁ sītāvirahitaṁ pathi

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, seeing you coming at a distance, renouncing her, my left eye and arm as well as my heart keep throbbing.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः
भूयो दुःखसमाविष्टो दुःखितं राममब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu saumitrirlakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
bhūyo duḥkhasamāviṣṭo duḥkhitaṁ rāmamabravīt

translations.english: Thus accosted, Laksmana having auspicious signs, afflicted with great grief, said to the aggrieved Rāma,

verses.sanskrit:
न स्वयं कामकारेण तां त्यक्त्वाहमिहागतः
प्रचोदितस्तयैवोग्रैस्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
na svayaṁ kāmakāreṇa tāṁ tyaktvāhamihāgataḥ
pracoditastayaivograistvatsakāśamihāgataḥ

translations.english: I have not come hither, of my own accord, renouncing Sītā; but I have come to you, having been urged thereto by herself with rudeness.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्येणेव परिक्रुष्टं हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च
परित्राहीति यद्वाक्यं मैथिल्यास्तच्छ्रुतिं गतम्
verses.transliteration:
āryeṇeva parikruṣṭaṁ hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
paritrāhīti yadvākyaṁ maithilyāstacchrutiṁ gatam

translations.english: The cries of O Laksimana, save me, as if uttered by the master, came to the ears of Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तमार्तस्वरं श्रुत्वा तव स्नेहेन मैथिली
गच्छ गच्छेति मामाह रुदन्ती भयविह्वला
verses.transliteration:
sā tamārtasvaraṁ śrutvā tava snehena maithilī
gaccha gaccheti māmāha rudantī bhayavihvalā

translations.english: Hearing those distressful accents, Maithili from affection [for you], breaking out into lamentations, and overwhelmed with fear, spoke to me, Off, off.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रचोद्यमानेन मया गच्छेति बहुशस्तया
प्रत्युक्ता मैथिली वाक्यमिदं त्वत्प्रत्ययान्वितम्
verses.transliteration:
pracodyamānena mayā gaccheti bahuśastayā
pratyuktā maithilī vākyamidaṁ tvatpratyayānvitam

translations.english: On being repeatedly urged, with Go, answered Maithili in these words, tending to inspire her confidence.

verses.sanskrit:
न तत्पश्याम्यहं रक्षो यदस्य भयमावहेत्
निर्वृता भव नास्त्येतत्केनाप्येवमुदाहृतम्
verses.transliteration:
na tatpaśyāmyahaṁ rakṣo yadasya bhayamāvahet
nirvṛtā bhava nāstyetatkenāpyevamudāhṛtam

translations.english: I do not see such a Rākṣasa, as can excite his fear. Do you desist. These cries do not come from him; but must have been uttered by someone else.

verses.sanskrit:
विगर्हितं च नीचं च कथमार्योऽभिधास्यति
त्राहीति वचनं सीते यस्त्रायेत्त्रिदशानपि
verses.transliteration:
vigarhitaṁ ca nīcaṁ ca kathamāryo'bhidhāsyati
trāhīti vacanaṁ sīte yastrāyettridaśānapi

translations.english: How can he that can rescue the celestials themselves, utter, O Sītā, such a blame-worthy and base word as-save me?

verses.sanskrit:
किंनिमित्तं तु केनापि भ्रातुरालम्ब्य मे स्वरम्
विस्वरं व्याहृतं वाक्यं लक्ष्मण त्राहि मामिति
न भवत्या व्यथा कार्या कुनारीजनसेविता
verses.transliteration:
kiṁnimittaṁ tu kenāpi bhrāturālambya me svaram
visvaraṁ vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ lakṣmaṇa trāhi māmiti
na bhavatyā vyathā kāryā kunārījanasevitā

translations.english: Some one for some purpose, assuming my brother's voice, is crying-O Laksmana, save me.

verses.sanskrit:
अलं वैक्लव्यमालम्ब्य स्वस्था भव निरुत्सुका
न चास्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु पुमान्यो राघवं रणे
जातो वा जायमानो वा संयुगे यः पराजयेत्
verses.transliteration:
alaṁ vaiklavyamālambya svasthā bhava nirutsukā
na cāsti triṣu lokeṣu pumānyo rāghavaṁ raṇe
jāto vā jāyamāno vā saṁyuge yaḥ parājayet

translations.english: Do not be over-whelmed; and banish your anxiety. There breathes no person, nor yet shall there be born any one in these three worlds who in the field shall vanquish Rāghava in fight. Rāghava is incapable of being beaten in battle by the very gods headed by Indra.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही परिमोहितचेतना
उवाचाश्रूणि मुञ्चन्ती दारुणं मामिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu vaidehī parimohitacetanā
uvācāśrūṇi muñcantī dāruṇaṁ māmidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed (by me) Vaidehi, deprived of her sense, shedding tears, spoke to me these cruel words,

verses.sanskrit:
भावो मयि तवात्यर्थं पाप एव निवेशितः
विनष्टे भ्रातरि प्राप्ते न च त्वं मामवाप्स्यसि
verses.transliteration:
bhāvo mayi tavātyarthaṁ pāpa eva niveśitaḥ
vinaṣṭe bhrātari prāpte na ca tvaṁ māmavāpsyasi

translations.english: You cherish the vile idea that on your brother perishing, you shall come by me; but me you shall never have.

verses.sanskrit:
संकेताद्भरतेन त्वं रामं समनुगच्छसि
क्रोशन्तं हि यथात्यर्थं नैनमभ्यवपद्यसे
verses.transliteration:
saṁketādbharatena tvaṁ rāmaṁ samanugacchasi
krośantaṁ hi yathātyarthaṁ nainamabhyavapadyase

translations.english: As you do not go to him albeit he is crying loudly (for help), you follow Rāma in consonance with a hint from Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
रिपुः प्रच्छन्नचारी त्वं मदर्थमनुगच्छसि
राघवस्यान्तरप्रेप्सुस्तथैनं नाभिपद्यसे
verses.transliteration:
ripuḥ pracchannacārī tvaṁ madarthamanugacchasi
rāghavasyāntaraprepsustathainaṁ nābhipadyase

translations.english: A foe going about in disguise, you follow Rāma for my sake, prying into Rāghava's draw backs; and it is for this that you do not go (to him)?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो हि वैदेह्या संरब्धो रक्तलोचनः
क्रोधात्प्रस्फुरमाणौष्ठ आश्रमादभिनिर्गतः
verses.transliteration:
evamukto hi vaidehyā saṁrabdho raktalocanaḥ
krodhātprasphuramāṇauṣṭha āśramādabhinirgataḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by Vaidehi, I, with eyes reddened in wrath, and my nether lip swollen in ire, rushed out of the asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं सौमित्रिं रामः संतापमोहितः
अब्रवीद्दुष्कृतं सौम्य तां विना यत्त्वमागतः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ saumitriṁ rāmaḥ saṁtāpamohitaḥ
abravīdduṣkṛtaṁ saumya tāṁ vinā yattvamāgataḥ

translations.english: When Saumitri had spoken thus, Rāma transported by grief; said to Laksmana, O gentle one, you have done wrong in having come out hither without her.

verses.sanskrit:
जानन्नपि समर्थं मां रक्षसां विनिवारणे
अनेन क्रोधवाक्येन मैथिल्या निःसृतो भवान्
verses.transliteration:
jānannapi samarthaṁ māṁ rakṣasāṁ vinivāraṇe
anena krodhavākyena maithilyā niḥsṛto bhavān

translations.english: Although you knew (full well) that I was able to withstand the Rākşasas, yet did you sally out at the angry words of Mithila's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि ते परितुष्यामि त्यक्त्वा यद्यासि मैथिलीम्
क्रुद्धायाः परुषं श्रुत्वा स्त्रिया यत्त्वमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
na hi te parituṣyāmi tyaktvā yadyāsi maithilīm
kruddhāyāḥ paruṣaṁ śrutvā striyā yattvamihāgataḥ

translations.english: I am not pleased with you that hearing her harsh speech spoken in wrath, you have come hither, leaving Vaidehi behind.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा त्वपनीतं ते सीतया यत्प्रचोदितः
क्रोधस्य वशमागम्य नाकरोः शासनं मम
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā tvapanītaṁ te sītayā yatpracoditaḥ
krodhasya vaśamāgamya nākaroḥ śāsanaṁ mama

translations.english: You have every way done wrong in not acting out my mandate in consequence of being urged by Sītā, and under the influence of indignation.

verses.sanskrit:
असौ हि राक्षसः शेते शरेणाभिहतो मया
मृगरूपेण येनाहमाश्रमादपवादितः
verses.transliteration:
asau hi rākṣasaḥ śete śareṇābhihato mayā
mṛgarūpeṇa yenāhamāśramādapavāditaḥ

translations.english: That Rākṣasa lie low, being wounded by my shafts—that had drawn me away from the asylum wearing the form of a deer.

verses.sanskrit:
विकृष्य चापं परिधाय सायकं; सलील बाणेन च ताडितो मया
मार्गीं तनुं त्यज्य च विक्लवस्वरो; बभूव केयूरधरः स राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
vikṛṣya cāpaṁ paridhāya sāyakaṁ; salīla bāṇena ca tāḍito mayā
mārgīṁ tanuṁ tyajya ca viklavasvaro; babhūva keyūradharaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: I hit him stretching my brow slightly and fixing the shaft on it; when, renouncing his deerform he became a Rākṣasa wearing a bracelet and began to emit distressful shrieks.

verses.sanskrit:
शराहतेनैव तदार्तया गिरा; स्वरं ममालम्ब्य सुदूरसंश्रवम्
उदाहृतं तद्वचनं सुदारुणं; त्वमागतो येन विहाय मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
śarāhatenaiva tadārtayā girā; svaraṁ mamālambya sudūrasaṁśravam
udāhṛtaṁ tadvacanaṁ sudāruṇaṁ; tvamāgato yena vihāya maithilīm

translations.english: Wounded by my shaft, he, assuming my voice, and in accents capable of being heard from far, uttered those dreadful words fraught with dole, hearing which, you have come hither, renouncing Mithilā's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
भृशमाव्रजमानस्य तस्याधोवामलोचनम्
प्रास्फुरच्चास्खलद्रामो वेपथुश्चास्य जायते
verses.transliteration:
bhṛśamāvrajamānasya tasyādhovāmalocanam
prāsphuraccāskhaladrāmo vepathuścāsya jāyate

translations.english: As Rāma went on, his feet failed him, his left eye to beat, and a trembling came over his frame.

verses.sanskrit:
उपालक्ष्य निमित्तानि सोऽशुभानि मुहुर्मुहुः
अपि क्षेमं तु सीताया इति वै व्याजहार ह
verses.transliteration:
upālakṣya nimittāni so'śubhāni muhurmuhuḥ
api kṣemaṁ tu sītāyā iti vai vyājahāra ha

translations.english: Seeing again and again all these signs, he continually kept on asking (Lakşmaņa), Is it well with Sita?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वरमाणो जगामाथ सीतादर्शनलालसः
शून्यमावसथं दृष्ट्वा बभूवोद्विग्नमानसः
verses.transliteration:
tvaramāṇo jagāmātha sītādarśanalālasaḥ
śūnyamāvasathaṁ dṛṣṭvā babhūvodvignamānasaḥ

translations.english: Eager to behold Sītā, he proceeded fast; but finding the abode empty, he was filled with anxiety.

verses.sanskrit:
ददर्श पर्णशालां च रहितां सीतया तदा
श्रिया विरहितां ध्वस्तां हेमन्ते पद्मिनीमिव
verses.transliteration:
dadarśa parṇaśālāṁ ca rahitāṁ sītayā tadā
śriyā virahitāṁ dhvastāṁ hemante padminīmiva

translations.english: And proceeding with swiftness, throwing about his limbs, Raghu's son began to survey all around the hut. He then found it empty of Sītā, like to a tank in evil plight and bereft of lotuses-during the winter.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रकीर्णाजिनकुशं विप्रविद्धबृसीकटम्
दृष्ट्वा शून्योटजस्थानं विललाप पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
viprakīrṇājinakuśaṁ vipraviddhabṛsīkaṭam
dṛṣṭvā śūnyoṭajasthānaṁ vilalāpa punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: And seeing the cottage empty, with its trees as if sorrowing, and its flowers faded, and its beasts and birds sunk in gloom, shorn of grace, worn out, forsaken by the sylvan deities, strewn with deer-skins and Kusa, and twists of Kasa, he wept again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
हृता मृता वा नष्टा वा भक्षिता वा भविष्यति
निलीनाप्यथ वा भीरुरथ वा वनमाश्रिता
verses.transliteration:
hṛtā mṛtā vā naṣṭā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati
nilīnāpyatha vā bhīruratha vā vanamāśritā

translations.english: Has the timid one been carried off, or is she dead, or has any one eaten her up, or has she vanished (from the earth), or has she gone to the wood, or has she gone to cull flowers and fruits, or has she gone to the pool for procuring water, or has she repaired to the river?

verses.sanskrit:
यत्नान्मृगयमाणस्तु नाससाद वने प्रियाम्
शोकरक्तेक्षणः शोकादुन्मत्त इव लक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
yatnānmṛgayamāṇastu nāsasāda vane priyām
śokaraktekṣaṇaḥ śokādunmatta iva lakṣyate

translations.english: Although he searched his beloved one carefully, yet he failed to find her out in the wood-land. And that graceful one with his eyes reddened with grief, seemed like a maniac

verses.sanskrit:
वृक्षाद्वृक्षं प्रधावन्स गिरींश्चापि नदीन्नदीम्
बभूव विलपन्रामः शोकपङ्कार्णवप्लुतः
verses.transliteration:
vṛkṣādvṛkṣaṁ pradhāvansa girīṁścāpi nadīnnadīm
babhūva vilapanrāmaḥ śokapaṅkārṇavaplutaḥ

translations.english: He rushed from tree to tree, and bewailing being sunk in an ocean of grief traversed all the rivers and mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्ति कच्चित्त्वया दृष्टा सा कदम्बप्रिया प्रिया
कदम्ब यदि जानीषे शंस सीतां शुभाननाम्
verses.transliteration:
asti kaccittvayā dṛṣṭā sā kadambapriyā priyā
kadamba yadi jānīṣe śaṁsa sītāṁ śubhānanām

translations.english: O Kadamba, have you seen where is that one fond of Kadamba groves? If know you this do you tell me of Sītā having an auspicious countenance. O Bilva, tell me pray, if you have seen her, wearing silken cloth, resembling cool leaves and having breast like to Bilva fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वार्जुन शंस त्वं प्रियां तामर्जुनप्रियाम्
जनकस्य सुता भीरुर्यदि जीवति वा न वा
verses.transliteration:
atha vārjuna śaṁsa tvaṁ priyāṁ tāmarjunapriyām
janakasya sutā bhīruryadi jīvati vā na vā

translations.english: Or, O Aryunā, she was very fond of you, tell me if live that daughter of Janaka of slender frame.

verses.sanskrit:
ककुभः ककुभोरुं तां व्यक्तं जानाति मैथिलीम्
लतापल्लवपुष्पाढ्यो भाति ह्येष वनस्पतिः
verses.transliteration:
kakubhaḥ kakubhoruṁ tāṁ vyaktaṁ jānāti maithilīm
latāpallavapuṣpāḍhyo bhāti hyeṣa vanaspatiḥ

translations.english: This Kakubha know for certain about Maithilī having thighs like to Kakubha. You stands beautifully that Vanaspati being enveloped with creepers flowers and leaves and filled with the hum of Bhramaras. Surely dose this Tilaka know about her who was fond of her.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकशोकापनुद शोकोपहतचेतसं
त्वन्नामानं कुरु क्षिप्रं प्रियासंदर्शनेन माम्
verses.transliteration:
aśokaśokāpanuda śokopahatacetasaṁ
tvannāmānaṁ kuru kṣipraṁ priyāsaṁdarśanena mām

translations.english: O Asoka, who dose remove sorrows, do you make good your name by making me, who am exercised with grief, see instantly my beloved (spouse).

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ताल त्वया दृष्टा पक्वतालफलस्तनी
कथयस्व वरारोहां कारुष्यं यदि ते मयि
verses.transliteration:
yadi tāla tvayā dṛṣṭā pakvatālaphalastanī
kathayasva varārohāṁ kāruṣyaṁ yadi te mayi

translations.english: O Tāla, if you have any pity on me do you tell me whether you have beheld that fair damsel having breast resembling ripe Tāla fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दृष्टा त्वया सीता जम्बुजाम्बूनदप्रभा
प्रियां यदि विजानीषे निःशङ्कं कथयस्व मे
verses.transliteration:
yadi dṛṣṭā tvayā sītā jambujāmbūnadaprabhā
priyāṁ yadi vijānīṣe niḥśaṅkaṁ kathayasva me

translations.english: Do you tell me without fear, O Jāmbu, if you have seen my dear one resembling in hue the river Jāmbu.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा मृगशावाक्षीं मृग जानासि मैथिलीम्
मृगविप्रेक्षणी कान्ता मृगीभिः सहिता भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā mṛgaśāvākṣīṁ mṛga jānāsi maithilīm
mṛgaviprekṣaṇī kāntā mṛgībhiḥ sahitā bhavet

translations.english: Again addressed he the diverse animals-O dear, know you for certain about Janakī having the eyes of a doe; is she engaged in play with the does?

verses.sanskrit:
गज सा गजनासोरुर्यदि दृष्टा त्वया भवेत्
तां मन्ये विदितां तुभ्यमाख्याहि वरवारण
verses.transliteration:
gaja sā gajanāsoruryadi dṛṣṭā tvayā bhavet
tāṁ manye viditāṁ tubhyamākhyāhi varavāraṇa

translations.english: O elephant, methinks you do know about the daughter of Janaka having thighs resembling your trunk; pray tell me if you have beheld her.

verses.sanskrit:
शार्दूल यदि सा दृष्टा प्रिया चन्द्रनिभानना
मैथिली मम विस्रब्धः कथयस्व न ते भयम्
verses.transliteration:
śārdūla yadi sā dṛṣṭā priyā candranibhānanā
maithilī mama visrabdhaḥ kathayasva na te bhayam

translations.english: O tiger, fearlessly do you relate to me if you have seen my beloved Maithilī, having a countenance resembling Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
किं धावसि प्रिये नूनं दृष्टासि कमलेक्षणे
वृक्षेणाच्छाद्य चात्मानं किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ dhāvasi priye nūnaṁ dṛṣṭāsi kamalekṣaṇe
vṛkṣeṇācchādya cātmānaṁ kiṁ māṁ na pratibhāṣase

translations.english: O dear! O you having eyes like to lotuses! why do you fly away? Surely have I seen you. Why do you not address me hiding yourself behind the tree?

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठ वरारोहे न तेऽस्ति करुणा मयि
नात्यर्थं हास्यशीलासि किमर्थं मामुपेक्षसे
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭha varārohe na te'sti karuṇā mayi
nātyarthaṁ hāsyaśīlāsi kimarthaṁ māmupekṣase

translations.english: Wait, wait, O you fair damsel, you have no compassion for me! Never had you mock me before in this way! Why do you neglect me now?

verses.sanskrit:
पीतकौशेयकेनासि सूचिता वरवर्णिनि
धावन्त्यपि मया दृष्टा तिष्ठ यद्यस्ति सौहृदम्
verses.transliteration:
pītakauśeyakenāsi sūcitā varavarṇini
dhāvantyapi mayā dṛṣṭā tiṣṭha yadyasti sauhṛdam

translations.english: O exquisitely fair damsel, truly have I found you out from this your yellow silken cloth. I have seen you flying away. Stand if you have any love for me.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव सा नूनमथ वा हिंसिता चारुहासिनी
कृच्छ्रं प्राप्तं हि मां नूनं यथोपेक्षितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
naiva sā nūnamatha vā hiṁsitā cāruhāsinī
kṛcchraṁ prāptaṁ hi māṁ nūnaṁ yathopekṣitumarhati

translations.english: Or, O you having a sweet smile, you are not she; truly you have been killed or else you would not have neglected me at this time of dire affliction.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यक्तं सा भक्षिता बाला राक्षसैः पिशिताशनैः
विभज्याङ्गानि सर्वाणि मया विरहिता प्रिया
verses.transliteration:
vyaktaṁ sā bhakṣitā bālā rākṣasaiḥ piśitāśanaiḥ
vibhajyāṅgāni sarvāṇi mayā virahitā priyā

translations.english: True it is that she has been devoured in my absence by the Rākşasas living on flesh having torn into pieces her limbs.

verses.sanskrit:
कोमला विलपन्त्यास्तु कान्ताया भक्षिता शुभा
नूनं विक्षिप्यमाणौ तौ बाहू पल्लवकोमलौ
verses.transliteration:
komalā vilapantyāstu kāntāyā bhakṣitā śubhā
nūnaṁ vikṣipyamāṇau tau bāhū pallavakomalau

translations.english: Her arms were tender like leaves and adorned with various ornaments; truly have the Rākşasas eaten them up, shaken as they were, by throwing them here and there.

verses.sanskrit:
सार्थेनेव परित्यक्ता भक्षिता बहुबान्धवा
हा लक्ष्मण महाबाहो पश्यसि त्वं प्रियां क्वचित्
verses.transliteration:
sārtheneva parityaktā bhakṣitā bahubāndhavā
hā lakṣmaṇa mahābāho paśyasi tvaṁ priyāṁ kvacit

translations.english: Alas! did I leave her alone only to be devoured by the Rākşasas? And she has been eaten up like one weak and helpless albeit she has many friends.

verses.sanskrit:
हा प्रिये क्व गता भद्रे हा सीतेति पुनः पुनः
इत्येवं विलपन्रामः परिधावन्वनाद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
hā priye kva gatā bhadre hā sīteti punaḥ punaḥ
ityevaṁ vilapanrāmaḥ paridhāvanvanādvanam

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, O you of mighty-arms, have you seen where my dear wife is? O dear! O Sītā! where have you gone? bewailing again and again in this strain Rāma began to range the forest. Sometimes leaping, sometimes walking in an uncertain direction, again and again he looked like one void of sense.

verses.sanskrit:
स वनानि नदीः शैलान्गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च
काननानि च वेगेन भ्रमत्यपरिसंस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
sa vanāni nadīḥ śailāngiriprasravaṇāni ca
kānanāni ca vegena bhramatyaparisaṁsthitaḥ

translations.english: And again intent on searching Sītā he furiously engaged in traversing the rivers, mountains, fountains and the woods. he could not wait patiently anywhere.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा स गत्वा विपुलं महद्वनं; परीत्य सर्वं त्वथ मैथिलीं प्रति
अनिष्ठिताशः स चकार मार्गणे; पुनः प्रियायाः परमं परिश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā sa gatvā vipulaṁ mahadvanaṁ; parītya sarvaṁ tvatha maithilīṁ prati
aniṣṭhitāśaḥ sa cakāra mārgaṇe; punaḥ priyāyāḥ paramaṁ pariśramam

translations.english: Entering a vast forest he searched every nook and corner for Maithilī; his desire was not satisfied and he again engaged with great labour in the finding out of his dear spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्ट्वा तत्र वैदेहीं संनिरीक्ष्य च सर्वशः
उवाच रामः प्राक्रुश्य प्रगृह्य रुचिरौ भुजौ
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭvā tatra vaidehīṁ saṁnirīkṣya ca sarvaśaḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ prākruśya pragṛhya rucirau bhujau

translations.english: Beholding the hermitage and cottage desolate and the seats strewn here and there, Rāma the son of Dasaratha looked around. And finding Sītā nowhere he raised up his beautiful arm and broke out into lamentations.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व नु लक्ष्मण वैदेही कं वा देशमितो गता
केनाहृता वा सौमित्रे भक्षिता केन वा प्रिया
verses.transliteration:
kva nu lakṣmaṇa vaidehī kaṁ vā deśamito gatā
kenāhṛtā vā saumitre bhakṣitā kena vā priyā

translations.english: O Laksmana where is Sītā? Where has she gone hence? O Saumitri, who has carried away my dear one or who has devoured her?

verses.sanskrit:
वृष्केणावार्य यदि मां सीते हसितुमिच्छसि
अलं ते हसितेनाद्य मां भजस्व सुदुःखितम्
verses.transliteration:
vṛṣkeṇāvārya yadi māṁ sīte hasitumicchasi
alaṁ te hasitenādya māṁ bhajasva suduḥkhitam

translations.english: O Sītā, if wish you to mock me, hiding yourself behind the tree, enough-~-enough it is-console me who am exercised with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
यैः सह क्रीडसे सीते विश्वस्तैर्मृगपोतकैः
एते हीनास्त्वया सौम्ये ध्यायन्त्यस्राविलेक्षणाः
verses.transliteration:
yaiḥ saha krīḍase sīte viśvastairmṛgapotakaiḥ
ete hīnāstvayā saumye dhyāyantyasrāvilekṣaṇāḥ

translations.english: O pleasant Sītā, without you these faithful little deer have engaged in meditation being bathed in tears.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं प्रतिज्ञां संश्रुत्य मया त्वमभियोजितः
अपूरयित्वा तं कालं मत्सकाशमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ pratijñāṁ saṁśrutya mayā tvamabhiyojitaḥ
apūrayitvā taṁ kālaṁ matsakāśamihāgataḥ

translations.english: Without Sita I shall not breathe, O Laksmana. A mighty grief has overtaken me in consequence of her being carried away. My father the monarch shall surely behold me in the next world and ask me 'I engaged you in the observance of a vow; without fulfilling that, why have you come here?

verses.sanskrit:
कामवृत्तमनार्यं मां मृषावादिनमेव च
धिक्त्वामिति परे लोके व्यक्तं वक्ष्यति मे पिता
verses.transliteration:
kāmavṛttamanāryaṁ māṁ mṛṣāvādinameva ca
dhiktvāmiti pare loke vyaktaṁ vakṣyati me pitā

translations.english: O shame on you!' For certain shall my father address me with these words relating to my passionate, false and base conduct.

verses.sanskrit:
विवशं शोकसंतप्तं दीनं भग्नमनोरथम्
मामिहोत्सृज्य करुणं कीर्तिर्नरमिवानृजुम्
verses.transliteration:
vivaśaṁ śokasaṁtaptaṁ dīnaṁ bhagnamanoratham
māmihotsṛjya karuṇaṁ kīrtirnaramivānṛjum

translations.english: All my desires have now been baffled and I have lost all control over myself and have been exercised with grief. O fine damsel, O you of slender waist, where do you repair leaving me behind like to fame renouncing a person of vicious nature?

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव विलपन्रामः सीतादर्शनलालसः
न ददर्श सुदुःखार्तो राघवो जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
itīva vilapanrāmaḥ sītādarśanalālasaḥ
na dadarśa suduḥkhārto rāghavo janakātmajām

translations.english: Without you I shall renounce my own life. Being desirous of seeing Sītā, Rāma afflicted with grief began to bewail in this strain, but did not behold the daughter of Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
अनासादयमानं तं सीतां दशरथात्मजम्
पङ्कमासाद्य विपुलं सीदन्तमिव कुञ्जरम्
लक्ष्मणो राममत्यर्थमुवाच हितकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
anāsādayamānaṁ taṁ sītāṁ daśarathātmajam
paṅkamāsādya vipulaṁ sīdantamiva kuñjaram
lakṣmaṇo rāmamatyarthamuvāca hitakāmyayā

translations.english: Being sunk in grief on Sītā's account he became worn out like to an elephant fallen in mud.' Thereat for his well being, Laksmana spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
सरितं वापि संप्राप्ता मीनवञ्जुरसेविताम्
वित्रासयितुकामा वा लीना स्यात्कानने क्वचित्
जिज्ञासमाना वैदेही त्वां मां च पुरुषर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
saritaṁ vāpi saṁprāptā mīnavañjurasevitām
vitrāsayitukāmā vā līnā syātkānane kvacit
jijñāsamānā vaidehī tvāṁ māṁ ca puruṣarṣabha

translations.english: O you of mighty intellect-do not grieve. Do you put forth your endeavours along with me. There is that high hill, O hero, containing many a cave. Maithilī who is fond of ranging the forest and ever delight in beholding the flowery woods, must have entered therein or have gone to the watering-place blooming with flowers and lot''ses. She Las gone to the river abounding in fish and Vañjulas or has hidden herself somewhere in the forest to frighten us and to know, O best of men, how we can search her out. O you of great beauty, let us soon engage in quest of her.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौहार्दाल्लक्ष्मणेन समाहितः
सह सौमित्रिणा रामो विचेतुमुपचक्रमे
तौ वनानि गिरींश्चैव सरितश्च सरांसि च
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu sauhārdāllakṣmaṇena samāhitaḥ
saha saumitriṇā rāmo vicetumupacakrame
tau vanāni girīṁścaiva saritaśca sarāṁsi ca

translations.english: O Kākutstha, if think you that she is somewhere in this forest, we shall leave no quarter untried. Do you not grieve. After Laks maņa had spoken thus out of fraternal affection, Rāma, with a composed heart, set out along with him in quest of Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
नेह पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीं पर्वते शुभे
ततो दुःखाभिसंतप्तो लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
neha paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīṁ parvate śubhe
tato duḥkhābhisaṁtapto lakṣmaṇo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Ranging the entire forest of Dandaka, Laks mana, sore distressed, spoke to his brother of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा विष्णुर्महाबाहुर्बलिं बद्ध्वा महीमिमाम्
एवमुक्तस्तु वीरेण लक्ष्मणेन स राघवः
verses.transliteration:
yathā viṣṇurmahābāhurbaliṁ baddhvā mahīmimām
evamuktastu vīreṇa lakṣmaṇena sa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Surely shall you come by Maithilī the daughter of Janaka like to the mighty armed Viş ņu obtaining this earth after having bound Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच दीनया वाचा दुःखाभिहतचेतनः
वनं सर्वं सुविचितं पद्मिन्यः फुल्लपङ्कजाः
verses.transliteration:
uvāca dīnayā vācā duḥkhābhihatacetanaḥ
vanaṁ sarvaṁ suvicitaṁ padminyaḥ phullapaṅkajāḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed by the heroic Lakşmaņa, Rāghava, greatly afflicted with sorrow, replied in piteous accents.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिश्चायं महाप्राज्ञ बहुकन्दरनिर्झरः
न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीं प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम्
verses.transliteration:
giriścāyaṁ mahāprājña bahukandaranirjharaḥ
na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṁ prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasīm

translations.english: O you of mighty intellect I have searched every nook of this forest, this pool abounding in blown lotuses, and this mountain containing many a cave and fountain; but nowhere have I seen Vaidehi dearer than my life.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स विलपन्रामः सीताहरणकर्शितः
दीनः शोकसमाविष्टो मुहूर्तं विह्वलोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa vilapanrāmaḥ sītāharaṇakarśitaḥ
dīnaḥ śokasamāviṣṭo muhūrtaṁ vihvalo'bhavat

translations.english: Thus bewailing Rāma, racked with sorrow consequent on Sītā being carried away, became poorly and afflicted with grief and swooned away for sometime.

verses.sanskrit:
स विह्वलितसर्वाङ्गो गतबुद्धिर्विचेतनः
विषसादातुरो दीनो निःश्वस्याशीतमायतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo gatabuddhirvicetanaḥ
viṣasādāturo dīno niḥśvasyāśītamāyatam

translations.english: He lost his sense and his whole frame was worked with grief. Being greatly anxious and breathless he sighed hot and fast and began to lament.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुशः स तु निःश्वस्य रामो राजीवलोचनः
हा प्रियेति विचुक्रोश बहुशो बाष्पगद्गदः
verses.transliteration:
bahuśaḥ sa tu niḥśvasya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
hā priyeti vicukrośa bahuśo bāṣpagadgadaḥ

translations.english: And sobbing again and again the lotus-eyed Rāma bewailed with his voice choked with the vapour of grief, exclaiming “Ah Sītā!”

verses.sanskrit:
तं सान्त्वयामास ततो लक्ष्मणः प्रियबान्धवः
बहुप्रकारं धर्मज्ञः प्रश्रितः प्रश्रिताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ sāntvayāmāsa tato lakṣmaṇaḥ priyabāndhavaḥ
bahuprakāraṁ dharmajñaḥ praśritaḥ praśritāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Thereat his dear brother Lakşmaņa, aggrieved, consoled him with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादृत्य तु तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणौष्ठपुटच्युतम्
अपश्यंस्तां प्रियां सीतां प्राक्रोशत्स पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
anādṛtya tu tadvākyaṁ lakṣmaṇauṣṭhapuṭacyutam
apaśyaṁstāṁ priyāṁ sītāṁ prākrośatsa punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: But passing by the words dropping from Laks mana's lips Rāma again and again bewailed not beholding his dear Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
स दीनो दीनया वाचा लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
शीघ्रं लक्ष्मण जानीहि गत्वा गोदावरीं नदीम्
अपि गोदावरीं सीता पद्मान्यानयितुं गता
verses.transliteration:
sa dīno dīnayā vācā lakṣmaṇaṁ vākyamabravīt
śīghraṁ lakṣmaṇa jānīhi gatvā godāvarīṁ nadīm
api godāvarīṁ sītā padmānyānayituṁ gatā

translations.english: Rāma stricken with grief spoke to Lakşmaņa the following piteous words saying, O Laks mana, do you speedily repair to the river Godaverſ and learn if Sītā has gone there to fetch lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः पुनरेव हि
नदीं गोदावरीं रम्यां जगाम लघुविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ punareva hi
nadīṁ godāvarīṁ ramyāṁ jagāma laghuvikramaḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Rāma, the quickpaced Lakşmaņa went to the pleasant stream Godaveri.

verses.sanskrit:
तां लक्ष्मणस्तीर्थवतीं विचित्वा राममब्रवीत्
नैनां पश्यामि तीर्थेषु क्रोशतो न शृणोति मे
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ lakṣmaṇastīrthavatīṁ vicitvā rāmamabravīt
naināṁ paśyāmi tīrtheṣu krośato na śṛṇoti me

translations.english: Reconnoitring full well the river containing many a watering-place Lakşmaņa spoke to Rāma saying, Searched have I all the watering-places but have found her nowhere-anon I cried aloud but she did not hear.

verses.sanskrit:
कं नु सा देशमापन्ना वैदेही क्लेशनाशिनी
न हि तं वेद्मि वै राम यत्र सा तनुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
kaṁ nu sā deśamāpannā vaidehī kleśanāśinī
na hi taṁ vedmi vai rāma yatra sā tanumadhyamā

translations.english: I cannot trace whither has Vaidehi of slender waist repaired ever assuaging our mental affliction.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दीनः संताप मोहितः
रामः समभिचक्राम स्वयं गोदावरीं नदीम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dīnaḥ saṁtāpa mohitaḥ
rāmaḥ samabhicakrāma svayaṁ godāvarīṁ nadīm

translations.english: Hearing Laksmana's words, Rāma, aggrieved and overwhelmed with sorrow repaired in person to the river Godāverī.

verses.sanskrit:
भूतानि राक्षसेन्द्रेण वधार्हेण हृतामपि
न तां शशंसू रामाय तथा गोदावरी नदी
verses.transliteration:
bhūtāni rākṣasendreṇa vadhārheṇa hṛtāmapi
na tāṁ śaśaṁsū rāmāya tathā godāvarī nadī

translations.english: Arriving there cried he where is Şītā? Neither did the world of creatures nor the river Godāvarī apprise Rāma of Sītā's being carried away by the Lord of Rākşasas worthy of being slain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रचोदिता भूतैः शंसास्मै तां प्रियामिति
न च साभ्यवदत्सीतां पृष्टा रामेण शोचिता
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pracoditā bhūtaiḥ śaṁsāsmai tāṁ priyāmiti
na ca sābhyavadatsītāṁ pṛṣṭā rāmeṇa śocitā

translations.english: Thinking of the terrible figure and monstrous action of that vicious-souled Råvaņa, that river did not dare relate to him anything about Sītā, albeit appointed by the creatures to relate the story concerning her and accosted by Răma in piteous accents.

verses.sanskrit:
निराशस्तु तया नद्या सीताया दर्शने कृतः
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं सीतादर्शनकर्शितः
verses.transliteration:
nirāśastu tayā nadyā sītāyā darśane kṛtaḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṁ sītādarśanakarśitaḥ

translations.english: Being thus disappointed by the river in beholding Sītā, Răma racked with her separation spoke to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु लक्ष्मण वक्ष्यामि समेत्य जनकं वचः
मातरं चैव वैदेह्या विना तामहमप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu lakṣmaṇa vakṣyāmi sametya janakaṁ vacaḥ
mātaraṁ caiva vaidehyā vinā tāmahamapriyam

translations.english: O you of auspicious looks, this river Godāvarī dose give no reply. But O Laksmana, returning without her what shall I say to Janaka and Vaidehi's mother?

verses.sanskrit:
या मे राज्यविहीनस्य वने वन्येन जीवतः
सर्वं व्यपनयच्छोकं वैदेही क्व नु सा गता
verses.transliteration:
yā me rājyavihīnasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ
sarvaṁ vyapanayacchokaṁ vaidehī kva nu sā gatā

translations.english: Where has that Vaidehi gone who used to assuage my grief who had been deprived of kingdom and living in this forest on wild fruits and vegetables? Nights shall appear too long to me, keeping late liquors being deprived of my kinsmen and relatives and not beholding Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
गोदावरीं जनस्थानमिमं प्रस्रवणं गिरिम्
सर्वाण्यनुचरिष्यामि यदि सीता हि दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
godāvarīṁ janasthānamimaṁ prasravaṇaṁ girim
sarvāṇyanucariṣyāmi yadi sītā hi dṛśyate

translations.english: I can range this Mandakini, this Janasthāna and this Pasravana hill if I can find Sītā there.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं संभाषमाणौ तावन्योन्यं भ्रातरावुभौ
वसुंधरायां पतितं पुष्पमार्गमपश्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ saṁbhāṣamāṇau tāvanyonyaṁ bhrātarāvubhau
vasuṁdharāyāṁ patitaṁ puṣpamārgamapaśyatām

translations.english: While proceeding thus, conversing with each other the two brothers beheld some flowers scattered on the high-way.

verses.sanskrit:
तां पुष्पवृष्टिं पतितां दृष्ट्वा रामो महीतले
उवाच लक्ष्मणं वीरो दुःखितो दुःखितं वचः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ puṣpavṛṣṭiṁ patitāṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahītale
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṁ vīro duḥkhito duḥkhitaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Beholding a collection of flowers scattered on earth, Rāma, exceedingly sorry, spoke to Laks mana in piteous accents.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिजानामि पुष्पाणि तानीमामीह लक्ष्मण
अपिनद्धानि वैदेह्या मया दत्तानि कानने
verses.transliteration:
abhijānāmi puṣpāṇi tānīmāmīha lakṣmaṇa
apinaddhāni vaidehyā mayā dattāni kānane

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, I have come to know that these are the flowers of the forest I gave Vaidehī; with these she decorated her hair.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणं पुरुषर्षभम्
क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीद्गिरिं तत्र सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahābāhurlakṣmaṇaṁ puruṣarṣabham
kruddho'bravīdgiriṁ tatra siṁhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṁ yathā

translations.english: Having spoken these words to Lakşmaņa, the best of men, the virtuous-souled Rāma, of mighty arms, addressed the mountain in front of him containing many fountains.

verses.sanskrit:
तां हेमवर्णां हेमाभां सीतां दर्शय पर्वत
यावत्सानूनि सर्वाणि न ते विध्वंसयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ hemavarṇāṁ hemābhāṁ sītāṁ darśaya parvata
yāvatsānūni sarvāṇi na te vidhvaṁsayāmyaham

translations.english: Exceedingly wroth he accosted the mountain like to a lion addressing a little deer, saying Show me my graceful Sītā hued like gold before I crush down your summits. Being thus addressed by Rāma on Maithili's account the mountain did not show him Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
मम बाणाग्निनिर्दग्धो भस्मीभूतो भविष्यसि
असेव्यः सततं चैव निस्तृणद्रुमपल्लवः
verses.transliteration:
mama bāṇāgninirdagdho bhasmībhūto bhaviṣyasi
asevyaḥ satataṁ caiva nistṛṇadrumapallavaḥ

translations.english: Again addressed him Rāma—You shall by the fire of my arrows, be reduced to ashes-your twigs and leaves shall be totally destroyed and no one shall resort to you.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां वा सरितं चाद्य शोषयिष्यामि लक्ष्मण
यदि नाख्याति मे सीतामद्य चन्द्रनिभाननाम्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ vā saritaṁ cādya śoṣayiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
yadi nākhyāti me sītāmadya candranibhānanām

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, I shall dry up this river Godāvari if it tell me not about Sītā having a moon-like countenance.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स रुषितो रामो दिधक्षन्निव चक्षुषा
ददर्श भूमौ निष्क्रान्तं राक्षसस्य पदं महत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa ruṣito rāmo didhakṣanniva cakṣuṣā
dadarśa bhūmau niṣkrāntaṁ rākṣasasya padaṁ mahat

translations.english: Rāma, exceedingly wroth, cast his looks around as if desiring to burn everything with his eyes and beheld footprints of the Räkşasas on the earth as well as those of Sītā moving wildly hither and thither, terrified and desirous to see Rāma, while pursued by the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स समीक्ष्य परिक्रान्तं सीताया राक्षसस्य च
संभ्रान्तहृदयो रामः शशंस भ्रातरं प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
sa samīkṣya parikrāntaṁ sītāyā rākṣasasya ca
saṁbhrāntahṛdayo rāmaḥ śaśaṁsa bhrātaraṁ priyam

translations.english: Beholding these foot marks, the snapped bow, the quiver and the chariot broken into many pieces, Rāma, terrified spoke to his dear brother.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्याः शीर्णाः कनकबिन्दवः
भूषणानां हि सौमित्रे माल्यानि विविधानि च
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ śīrṇāḥ kanakabindavaḥ
bhūṣaṇānāṁ hi saumitre mālyāni vividhāni ca

translations.english: Behold O, Laksmana, the remnants of Vaidehi's golden ornaments, strewn hither and thither, and diverse garlands.

verses.sanskrit:
तप्तबिन्दुनिकाशैश्च चित्रैः क्षतजबिन्दुभिः
आवृतं पश्य सौमित्रे सर्वतो धरणीतलम्
verses.transliteration:
taptabindunikāśaiśca citraiḥ kṣatajabindubhiḥ
āvṛtaṁ paśya saumitre sarvato dharaṇītalam

translations.english: Behold O Saumitrī, the earth covered with drops of blood resembling golden drops.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये लक्ष्मण वैदेही राक्षसैः कामरूपिभिः
भित्त्वा भित्त्वा विभक्ता वा भक्षिता वा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
manye lakṣmaṇa vaidehī rākṣasaiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
bhittvā bhittvā vibhaktā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Methinks, O Laksmana, Vaidehi has been devoured by the Rākşasas assuming shapes at will, having sundered her in pieces.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य निमित्तं वैदेह्या द्वयोर्विवदमानयोः
बभूव युद्धं सौमित्रे घोरं राक्षसयोरिह
verses.transliteration:
tasya nimittaṁ vaidehyā dvayorvivadamānayoḥ
babhūva yuddhaṁ saumitre ghoraṁ rākṣasayoriha

translations.english: O Saumitrī, there took place a terrible conflict between the Rākṣasas, fighting with each other on Sita's account.

verses.sanskrit:
मुक्तामणिचितं चेदं तपनीयविभूषितम्
धरण्यां पतितं सौम्य कस्य भग्नं महद्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
muktāmaṇicitaṁ cedaṁ tapanīyavibhūṣitam
dharaṇyāṁ patitaṁ saumya kasya bhagnaṁ mahaddhanuḥ

translations.english: O gentle one, whose is this snapped bow lying on the breast of the earth adorned and crested with pearls and diamonds?

verses.sanskrit:
दीप्तपावकसंकाशो द्युतिमान्समरध्वजः
अपविद्धश्च भग्नश्च कस्य सांग्रामिको रथः
verses.transliteration:
dīptapāvakasaṁkāśo dyutimānsamaradhvajaḥ
apaviddhaśca bhagnaśca kasya sāṁgrāmiko rathaḥ

translations.english: Whose is this shattered war-car lying upset on the ground and broken flag resembling in lustre the burning gold?

verses.sanskrit:
रथाक्षमात्रा विशिखास्तपनीयविभूषणाः
कस्येमेऽभिहता बाणाः प्रकीर्णा घोरकर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
rathākṣamātrā viśikhāstapanīyavibhūṣaṇāḥ
kasyeme'bhihatā bāṇāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Whose are these terrible arrows feathered in gold, measuring four-hundred fingers, lying without blades on earth?

verses.sanskrit:
वैरं शतगुणं पश्य ममेदं जीवितान्तकम्
सुघोरहृदयैः सौम्य राक्षसैः कामरूपिभिः
verses.transliteration:
vairaṁ śataguṇaṁ paśya mamedaṁ jīvitāntakam
sughorahṛdayaiḥ saumya rākṣasaiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ

translations.english: These foot-marks must be some Raksasa's. I made these Rākşasas my fatal enemies, assuming shapes at will and of crooked hearts.

verses.sanskrit:
हृता मृता वा सीता हि भक्षिता वा तपस्विनी
न धर्मस्त्रायते सीतां ह्रियमाणां महावने
verses.transliteration:
hṛtā mṛtā vā sītā hi bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī
na dharmastrāyate sītāṁ hriyamāṇāṁ mahāvane

translations.english: Poor Sītā must have been either dead, carried away by them or devoured. Virtue did not save her from being carried away in this mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्षितायां हि वैदेह्यां हृतायामपि लक्ष्मण
के हि लोके प्रियं कर्तुं शक्ताः सौम्य ममेश्वराः
verses.transliteration:
bhakṣitāyāṁ hi vaidehyāṁ hṛtāyāmapi lakṣmaṇa
ke hi loke priyaṁ kartuṁ śaktāḥ saumya mameśvarāḥ

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, while virtue did not protect Janakī being devoured or taken away by stealth, what person else gifted with heavenly power, on this earth shall bring about my well-being?

verses.sanskrit:
कर्तारमपि लोकानां शूरं करुणवेदिनम्
अज्ञानादवमन्येरन्सर्वभूतानि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
kartāramapi lokānāṁ śūraṁ karuṇavedinam
ajñānādavamanyeransarvabhūtāni lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: For this it is that people through ignorance disregard the ever kind Almighty-the lord of creatures and the best of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
मृदुं लोकहिते युक्तं दान्तं करुणवेदिनम्
निर्वीर्य इति मन्यन्ते नूनं मां त्रिदशेश्वराः
verses.transliteration:
mṛduṁ lokahite yuktaṁ dāntaṁ karuṇavedinam
nirvīrya iti manyante nūnaṁ māṁ tridaśeśvarāḥ

translations.english: Truly shall the celestials regard me as one devoid of prowess, who am mild-tempered, kind, ever engaged in the welfare of the humanity, and have controlled all my senses.

verses.sanskrit:
मां प्राप्य हि गुणो दोषः संवृत्तः पश्य लक्ष्मण
अद्यैव सर्वभूतानां रक्षसामभवाय च
संहृत्यैव शशिज्योत्स्नां महान्सूर्य इवोदितः
verses.transliteration:
māṁ prāpya hi guṇo doṣaḥ saṁvṛttaḥ paśya lakṣmaṇa
adyaiva sarvabhūtānāṁ rakṣasāmabhavāya ca
saṁhṛtyaiva śaśijyotsnāṁ mahānsūrya ivoditaḥ

translations.english: Observe, O Laksmana, obtaining me as the stay these accomplishments have been turned into so many blemishes. Truly shall my prowess manifest itself to-day overshadowing all my other accomplishments for the destruction of the Rākşasas and all created beings like to the rising of the Sun casting the Moon into shade on the day of dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव यक्षा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः
किंनरा वा मनुष्या वा सुखं प्राप्स्यन्ति लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
naiva yakṣā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
kiṁnarā vā manuṣyā vā sukhaṁ prāpsyanti lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: None shall enjoy felicity, O Lakşmaņa,-Yaksas, Gandharvas, Pisacas, Raksasas, Kinnaras, or human beings.

verses.sanskrit:
ममास्त्रबाणसंपूर्णमाकाशं पश्य लक्ष्मण
निःसंपातं करिष्यामि ह्यद्य त्रैलोक्यचारिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
mamāstrabāṇasaṁpūrṇamākāśaṁ paśya lakṣmaṇa
niḥsaṁpātaṁ kariṣyāmi hyadya trailokyacāriṇām

translations.english: Today shall the welkin be filled up with my arrows. Motionless shall I make all the animals inhabiting the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
नाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्ति सर्वभूतानि लक्ष्मण
मम चापगुणान्मुक्तैर्बाणजालैर्निरन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
nākāśamutpatiṣyanti sarvabhūtāni lakṣmaṇa
mama cāpaguṇānmuktairbāṇajālairnirantaram

translations.english: None shall be able to range the welkin. Behold O Lakşmaņa, being perpetually crushed down by my arrows shot off my bow, the world shall be disturbed and dislodged and the animals and birds shall be confused and destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
आकर्णपूर्णैरिषुभिर्जीवलोकं दुरावरैः
करिष्ये मैथिलीहेतोरपिशाचमराक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
ākarṇapūrṇairiṣubhirjīvalokaṁ durāvaraiḥ
kariṣye maithilīhetorapiśācamarākṣasaṁ

translations.english: Stretching the bow to my ears I shall make the world, for Sita's sake, void of Pisacas and Raks asas with my arrows incapable of being withstood by created beings.

verses.sanskrit:
मम रोषप्रयुक्तानां सायकानां बलं सुराः
द्रक्ष्यन्त्यद्य विमुक्तानाममर्षाद्दूरगामिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
mama roṣaprayuktānāṁ sāyakānāṁ balaṁ surāḥ
drakṣyantyadya vimuktānāmamarṣāddūragāminām

translations.english: To-day shall the celestials behold the power of my arrows coursing a long distance shot through my ire.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव देवा न दैतेया न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः
भविष्यन्ति मम क्रोधात्त्रैलोक्ये विप्रणाशिते
verses.transliteration:
naiva devā na daiteyā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
bhaviṣyanti mama krodhāttrailokye vipraṇāśite

translations.english: Three worlds, destroyed on account of my wrath, celestials, Sanavas, Pisacas or Raks asas,-none shall be saved.

verses.sanskrit:
देवदानवयक्षाणां लोका ये रक्षसामपि
बहुधा निपतिष्यन्ति बाणौघैः शकुलीकृताः
निर्मर्यादानिमाँल्लोकान्करिष्याम्यद्य सायकैः
verses.transliteration:
devadānavayakṣāṇāṁ lokā ye rakṣasāmapi
bahudhā nipatiṣyanti bāṇaughaiḥ śakulīkṛtāḥ
nirmaryādānimā̐llokānkariṣyāmyadya sāyakaiḥ

translations.english: The dwellings of the celestials, Asuras, Yaks as and Rākşasas shall fall down sundered by my arrows into diverse pieces.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा जरा यथा मृत्युर्यथाकालो यथाविधिः
नित्यं न प्रतिहन्यन्ते सर्वभूतेषु लक्ष्मण
तथाहं क्रोधसंयुक्तो न निवार्योऽस्म्यसंशयम्
verses.transliteration:
yathā jarā yathā mṛtyuryathākālo yathāvidhiḥ
nityaṁ na pratihanyante sarvabhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa
tathāhaṁ krodhasaṁyukto na nivāryo'smyasaṁśayam

translations.english: O Lakşınaņa none shall be able to withstand me, who am inflamed with rage, as debility consequent on old age, death, time, duty are incapable of being averted from their destined ends by the animals.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरेव मे चारुदतीमनिन्दितां; दिशन्ति सीतां यदि नाद्य मैथिलीम्
सदेवगन्धर्वमनुष्य पन्नगं; जगत्सशैलं परिवर्तयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
pureva me cārudatīmaninditāṁ; diśanti sītāṁ yadi nādya maithilīm
sadevagandharvamanuṣya pannagaṁ; jagatsaśailaṁ parivartayāmyaham

translations.english: I shall bring about a mighty revolution in the world containing the celestials Gandharvas, human beings, Pannagas and the mountains, if I do not get back, in her pristine beauty, my Sītā, the daughter of the King of Mithilā.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं संक्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा रामं स लक्ष्मणः
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭapūrvaṁ saṁkruddhaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ mukhena pariśuṣyatā

translations.english: Rāma highly aggrieved on account of Sīta's being carried away, addressing himself to destroy the world like to the fire of dissolution and casting his look, sighing again and again, upon the stringed bow like to Mahadeva desirous of burning down the whole world at the time of dissolution, Laksmana, having his countenance dried up, beholding his rage not seen before, began with folded hands.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा भूत्वा मृदुर्दान्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः
न क्रोधवशमापन्नः प्रकृतिं हातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
purā bhūtvā mṛdurdāntaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
na krodhavaśamāpannaḥ prakṛtiṁ hātumarhasi

translations.english: Ere this you had been gently, self-controlled and engaged in the welfare of all beings. It dose not behove you now to renounce your natural temper being influenced by ire.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रे लक्ष्णीः प्रभा सूर्ये गतिर्वायौ भुवि क्षमा
एतच्च नियतं सर्वं त्वयि चानुत्तमं यशः
verses.transliteration:
candre lakṣṇīḥ prabhā sūrye gatirvāyau bhuvi kṣamā
etacca niyataṁ sarvaṁ tvayi cānuttamaṁ yaśaḥ

translations.english: Ever manifested itself in you, glory Par excellence like to splendour in the Moon, lustre in the Sun, motion in the wind and forgiveness in the Earth.

verses.sanskrit:
न तु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः
केन वा कस्य वा हेतोः सायुधः सपरिच्छदः
verses.transliteration:
na tu jānāmi kasyāyaṁ bhagnaḥ sāṁgrāmiko rathaḥ
kena vā kasya vā hetoḥ sāyudhaḥ saparicchadaḥ

translations.english: It become you not to devastate the whole world for the crime of an individual being. Methinks for certain, this shattered car must be the property of an individual person, not of many.

verses.sanskrit:
खुरनेमिक्षतश्चायं सिक्तो रुधिरबिन्दुभिः
देशो निवृत्तसंग्रामः सुघोरः पार्थिवात्मज
verses.transliteration:
khuranemikṣataścāyaṁ sikto rudhirabindubhiḥ
deśo nivṛttasaṁgrāmaḥ sughoraḥ pārthivātmaja

translations.english: But I do not know whose is this car with yokes and dresses and what for it has been shattered? Behold, O you the son of a King this terrible spot bathed in blood and raked with hoofs and wheels. Surely here took place a conflict. O you the foremost of those skilled in speech, it appear from these signs that this skirmish did take place with one, not with two. Here are not to be seen the foot-marks of a large army. It therefore dose not behove you to destroy the whole world for one's individual offence.

verses.sanskrit:
नैकस्य तु कृते लोकान्विनाशयितुमर्हसि
युक्तदण्डा हि मृदवः प्रशान्ता वसुधाधिपाः
verses.transliteration:
naikasya tu kṛte lokānvināśayitumarhasi
yuktadaṇḍā hi mṛdavaḥ praśāntā vasudhādhipāḥ

translations.english: Kings, gentle and mild by nature, do always administer punishment, proportionate to the amount of offence. You are always the stay and the best refuge of all animals.

verses.sanskrit:
सरितः सागराः शैला देवगन्धर्वदानवाः
नालं ते विप्रियं कर्तुं दीक्षितस्येव साधवः
verses.transliteration:
saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā devagandharvadānavāḥ
nālaṁ te vipriyaṁ kartuṁ dīkṣitasyeva sādhavaḥ

translations.english: Who shall think well, O Raghava, of the destruction of your wife? The celestials, Danavas, Gandharvas, rivers, seas, and mountains-none can act unfriendly by you as the learned priests cannot act improperly towards those initiated by them.

verses.sanskrit:
येन राजन्हृता सीता तमन्वेषितुमर्हसि
मद्द्वितीयो धनुष्पाणिः सहायैः परमर्षिभिः
verses.transliteration:
yena rājanhṛtā sītā tamanveṣitumarhasi
maddvitīyo dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sahāyaiḥ paramarṣibhiḥ

translations.english: It is your duty, O king with bow in hand to search out the person who has carried away Sītā, along with me and the devotees.

verses.sanskrit:
न चेत्साम्ना प्रदास्यन्ति पत्नीं ते त्रिदशेश्वराः
कोसलेन्द्र ततः पश्चात्प्राप्तकालं करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
na cetsāmnā pradāsyanti patnīṁ te tridaśeśvarāḥ
kosalendra tataḥ paścātprāptakālaṁ kariṣyasi

translations.english: Explore shall we, with great care, the seas, the forest, the mountains, the fearful caves, the pools and the abodes of the celestials and Gandharvas until we find out the person who has carried away your wife. If the celestials do not return you peacefully your wife, O Lord of Kosala, you shall adopt imeasures, befitting the occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
शीलेन साम्ना विनयेन सीतां; नयेन न प्राप्स्यसि चेन्नरेन्द्र
ततः समुत्सादय हेमपुङ्खै;र्महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैः शरौघैः
verses.transliteration:
śīlena sāmnā vinayena sītāṁ; nayena na prāpsyasi cennarendra
tataḥ samutsādaya hemapuṅkhai;rmahendravajrapratimaiḥ śaraughaiḥ

translations.english: You shall then uproot the whole world, O lord of men, with your gold-feathered arrows resembling the thunderbolt of Mahendra, if you do not come by your wife by resorting to good conduct, self-control, lowliness and polity.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सौमित्रिराश्वास्य मुहूर्तादिव लक्ष्मणः
रामं संबोधयामास चरणौ चाभिपीडयन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saumitrirāśvāsya muhūrtādiva lakṣmaṇaḥ
rāmaṁ saṁbodhayāmāsa caraṇau cābhipīḍayan

translations.english: Rāma bewailing thus like one helpless being stricken with grief, overwhelmed with sorrow and losing control over himself, Lakşmaņa touched his feet and consoling him instantly began.

verses.sanskrit:
महता तपसा राम महता चापि कर्मणा
राज्ञा दशरथेनासील्लब्धोऽमृतमिवामरैः
verses.transliteration:
mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā cāpi karmaṇā
rājñā daśarathenāsīllabdho'mṛtamivāmaraiḥ

translations.english: By constant asceticism and manifold pious observances king Dasaratha obtained you like to the celestials obtaining ambrosia.

verses.sanskrit:
तव चैव गुणैर्बद्धस्त्वद्वियोगान्महीपतिः
राजा देवत्वमापन्नो भरतस्य यथा श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
tava caiva guṇairbaddhastvadviyogānmahīpatiḥ
rājā devatvamāpanno bharatasya yathā śrutam

translations.english: As I have heard from Bharata, king Dasaratha died for your separation, attached as he was to you for your accomplishments.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दुःखमिदं प्राप्तं काकुत्स्थ न सहिष्यसे
प्राकृतश्चाल्पसत्त्वश्च इतरः कः सहिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi duḥkhamidaṁ prāptaṁ kākutstha na sahiṣyase
prākṛtaścālpasattvaśca itaraḥ kaḥ sahiṣyati

translations.english: O Kākutstha, if do you not bear patiently this impending peril what little-minded person else shall bear it?

verses.sanskrit:
लोकस्वभाव एवैष ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः
गतः शक्रेण सालोक्यमनयस्तं समस्पृशत्
verses.transliteration:
lokasvabhāva evaiṣa yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ
gataḥ śakreṇa sālokyamanayastaṁ samaspṛśat

translations.english: This is the nature of men. Yayati, the son of king Nahusa, though attained to the state of celestials, was however thrown down for an iniquitous deed.

verses.sanskrit:
महर्षयो वसिष्ठस्तु यः पितुर्नः पुरोहितः
अह्ना पुत्रशतं जज्ञे तथैवास्य पुनर्हतम्
verses.transliteration:
maharṣayo vasiṣṭhastu yaḥ piturnaḥ purohitaḥ
ahnā putraśataṁ jajñe tathaivāsya punarhatam

translations.english: The hundred sons, that had been born to our ancestral priest Vasiştha, were all killed in one day.

verses.sanskrit:
या चेयं जगतो माता देवी लोकनमस्कृता
अस्याश्च चलनं भूमेर्दृश्यते सत्यसंश्रव
verses.transliteration:
yā ceyaṁ jagato mātā devī lokanamaskṛtā
asyāśca calanaṁ bhūmerdṛśyate satyasaṁśrava

translations.english: O lord of Kosala, even Vasumati, the mother of the world, adored of all beings, meet with misery consequent upon earth-quake.

verses.sanskrit:
यौ चेमौ जगतां नेत्रे यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्
आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ
verses.transliteration:
yau cemau jagatāṁ netre yatra sarvaṁ pratiṣṭhitam
ādityacandrau grahaṇamabhyupetau mahābalau

translations.english: Even the mighty Sun and Moon witness eclipse who are the eyes of the world and the very images of virtue and in whom the whole world is stationed.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमहान्त्यपि भूतानि देवाश्च पुरुषर्षभ
न दैवस्य प्रमुञ्चन्ति सर्वभूतानि देहिनः
verses.transliteration:
sumahāntyapi bhūtāni devāśca puruṣarṣabha
na daivasya pramuñcanti sarvabhūtāni dehinaḥ

translations.english: O you best of men, what of insignificant beings cased in this frail body, even the mighty creatures and celestials are subject to the influence of destiny.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्रादिष्वपि देवेषु वर्तमानौ नयानयौ
श्रूयेते नरशार्दूल न त्वं व्यथितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
śakrādiṣvapi deveṣu vartamānau nayānayau
śrūyete naraśārdūla na tvaṁ vyathitumarhasi

translations.english: I have heard, O best of men, even the celestials headed by Indra are subject to happiness or misery. So it dose not behove you to bewail thus.

verses.sanskrit:
नष्टायामपि वैदेह्यां हृतायामपि चानघ
शोचितुं नार्हसे वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
naṣṭāyāmapi vaidehyāṁ hṛtāyāmapi cānagha
śocituṁ nārhase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, it become you not to lament like an ordinary person even if Janakí is dead or has been carried away.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वद्विधा हि न शोचन्ति सततं सत्यदर्शिनः
सुमहत्स्वपि कृच्छ्रेषु रामानिर्विण्णदर्शणाः
verses.transliteration:
tvadvidhā hi na śocanti satataṁ satyadarśinaḥ
sumahatsvapi kṛcchreṣu rāmānirviṇṇadarśaṇāḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, persons, highly experienced and ascertaining right or wrong without being moved, do not lament even in the face of mighty perils.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्वतो हि नरश्रेष्ठ बुद्ध्या समनुचिन्तय
बुद्ध्या युक्ता महाप्राज्ञा विजानन्ति शुभाशुभे
verses.transliteration:
tattvato hi naraśreṣṭha buddhyā samanucintaya
buddhyā yuktā mahāprājñā vijānanti śubhāśubhe

translations.english: O you best of men, do you, after due consideration, ascertain what is proper or improper; persons of your vast wisdom are cognizant of the right or wrong by dint of their understanding.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टगुणदोषाणामधृतानां च कर्मणाम्
नान्तरेण क्रियां तेषां फलमिष्टं प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭaguṇadoṣāṇāmadhṛtānāṁ ca karmaṇām
nāntareṇa kriyāṁ teṣāṁ phalamiṣṭaṁ pravartate

translations.english: Without proper exercise, actions, of unknown merit and uncertain issue do not bear fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
मामेव हि पुरा वीर त्वमेव बहुषोऽन्वशाः
अनुशिष्याद्धि को नु त्वामपि साक्षाद्बृहस्पतिः
verses.transliteration:
māmeva hi purā vīra tvameva bahuṣo'nvaśāḥ
anuśiṣyāddhi ko nu tvāmapi sākṣādbṛhaspatiḥ

translations.english: O hero, many a time and oft ere this, you had given me the self-same counsel. Who is capable of counselling you who are the very preceptor of the gods?

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया
शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं संबोधयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
buddhiśca te mahāprājña devairapi duranvayā
śokenābhiprasuptaṁ te jñānaṁ saṁbodhayāmyaham

translations.english: O you of great intellect, even the celestials cannot measure your mental acumen. Greatly benumbed is your wisdom with the slumber of grief, and I am to rouse it.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्यं च मानुषं चैवमात्मनश्च पराक्रमम्
इक्ष्वाकुवृषभावेक्ष्य यतस्व द्विषतां बधे
verses.transliteration:
divyaṁ ca mānuṣaṁ caivamātmanaśca parākramam
ikṣvākuvṛṣabhāvekṣya yatasva dviṣatāṁ badhe

translations.english: O you the best of lkşvākus, do you engage in the destruction of your foes considering well your celestial and human prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
किं ते सर्वविनाशेन कृतेन पुरुषर्षभ
तमेव तु रिपुं पापं विज्ञायोद्धर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ te sarvavināśena kṛtena puruṣarṣabha
tameva tu ripuṁ pāpaṁ vijñāyoddhartumarhasi

translations.english: O you best of men, what necessity have you to destroy the whole world? Do you rescue Sītā after finding out your vicious enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वजोऽप्युक्तमात्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेन सुभाषितम्
सारग्राही महासारं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvajo'pyuktamātrastu lakṣmaṇena subhāṣitam
sāragrāhī mahāsāraṁ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ

translations.english: After Laksmana had spoken these highly sound and pleasant words, Rāma, ever taking to what is sound, accepted them.

verses.sanskrit:
संनिगृह्य महाबाहुः प्रवृद्धं कोपमात्मनः
अवष्टभ्य धनुश्चित्रं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁnigṛhya mahābāhuḥ pravṛddhaṁ kopamātmanaḥ
avaṣṭabhya dhanuścitraṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon that one, of mighty arms, slaking his flaming ire and reclining himself upon his beautiful bow, addressed Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
किं करिष्यावहे वत्स क्व वा गच्छाव लक्ष्मण
केनोपायेन पश्येयं सीतामिति विचिन्तय
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ kariṣyāvahe vatsa kva vā gacchāva lakṣmaṇa
kenopāyena paśyeyaṁ sītāmiti vicintaya

translations.english: Do you ponder over, O brother, where shall we repair, what shall we do and by what means shall we come by Sītā?

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसैर्बहुभिः कीर्णं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्
सन्तीह गिरिदुर्गाणि निर्दराः कन्दराणि च
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasairbahubhiḥ kīrṇaṁ nānādrumalatāyutam
santīha giridurgāṇi nirdarāḥ kandarāṇi ca

translations.english: Whereto Lakşmaņa replied saying to the highly aggrieved Råma, It is proper for you to search this Janasthāna filled with a multitude of Rākṣasas and covered with diverse trees and creepers. Here are many strongholds in the midst of mountains, clefts of rocks, many caves and numerous cavities filled with various animals.

verses.sanskrit:
गुहाश्च विविधा घोरा नानामृगगणाकुलाः
आवासाः किंनराणां च गन्धर्वभवनानि च
verses.transliteration:
guhāśca vividhā ghorā nānāmṛgagaṇākulāḥ
āvāsāḥ kiṁnarāṇāṁ ca gandharvabhavanāni ca

translations.english: Many are the abodes here belonging to the Kinnaras and Gandharvas. Do you, along with me, search all these places. Great men, of your calibre, do remain unagitated even in the midst of difficulties like to mountains never shaken by the velocity of the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धो रामः शरं घोरं संधाय धनुषि क्षुरम्
ततः पर्वतकूटाभं महाभागं द्विजोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
kruddho rāmaḥ śaraṁ ghoraṁ saṁdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
tataḥ parvatakūṭābhaṁ mahābhāgaṁ dvijottamam

translations.english: Hearing these words, Rāma, enraged, fixing sharp and terrible arrows to his bow, began to range the forest with Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
ददर्श पतितं भूमौ क्षतजार्द्रं जटायुषम्
तं दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गाभं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
अनेन सीता वैदेही भक्षिता नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
dadarśa patitaṁ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṁ jaṭāyuṣam
taṁ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
anena sītā vaidehī bhakṣitā nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon he beheld, fallen on ground, having his person bathed in blood, the king of birds-Jatayu, resembling a mountain peak, and spoke to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
गृध्ररूपमिदं व्यक्तं रक्षो भ्रमति काननम्
भक्षयित्वा विशालाक्षीमास्ते सीतां यथासुखम्
एनं वधिष्ये दीप्ताग्रैर्घोरैर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः
verses.transliteration:
gṛdhrarūpamidaṁ vyaktaṁ rakṣo bhramati kānanam
bhakṣayitvā viśālākṣīmāste sītāṁ yathāsukham
enaṁ vadhiṣye dīptāgrairghorairbāṇairajihmagaiḥ

translations.english: This Rākşasa has been reposing at ease after devouring that one of expansive eyes; I shall kill him with terrible straight coursing arrows, having flaming points.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वाभ्यपतद्गृध्रं संधाय धनुषि क्षुरम्
क्रुद्धो रामः समुद्रान्तां चालयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvābhyapatadgṛdhraṁ saṁdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
kruddho rāmaḥ samudrāntāṁ cālayanniva medinīm

translations.english: Fixing sharpened shafts to his bow, Rāma, enraged, darted towards the vulture, as if moving the sea-girt earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दीनदीनया वाचा सफेनं रुधिरं वमन्
अभ्यभाषत पक्षी तु रामं दशरथात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dīnadīnayā vācā saphenaṁ rudhiraṁ vaman
abhyabhāṣata pakṣī tu rāmaṁ daśarathātmajam

translations.english: Vomiting frothy blood Jațāyu, the king of vultures, spoke to Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
यामोषधिमिवायुष्मन्नन्वेषसि महावने
सा देवी मम च प्राणा रावणेनोभयं हृतम्
verses.transliteration:
yāmoṣadhimivāyuṣmannanveṣasi mahāvane
sā devī mama ca prāṇā rāvaṇenobhayaṁ hṛtam

translations.english: O you of long life, that goddess, whom you have been searching in this vast forest like to Os adhi, and my life have been carried away by Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया विरहिता देवी लक्ष्मणेन च राघव
ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन बलीयसा
verses.transliteration:
tvayā virahitā devī lakṣmaṇena ca rāghava
hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇena balīyasā

translations.english: I saw her, O Rāghava, carried away stealthily by the powerful Rāvaņa, in your absence as well as that of Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतामभ्यवपन्नोऽहं रावणश्च रणे मया
विध्वंसितरथच्छत्रः पातितो धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
sītāmabhyavapanno'haṁ rāvaṇaśca raṇe mayā
vidhvaṁsitarathacchatraḥ pātito dharaṇītale

translations.english: Myself nearing Sītā, for her rescue, O Lord, Rāvaņa was thrown down on earth by me in conflict having his car and umbrella shattered.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदस्य धनुर्भग्नमेतदस्य शरावरम्
अयमस्य रणे राम भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः
verses.transliteration:
etadasya dhanurbhagnametadasya śarāvaram
ayamasya raṇe rāma bhagnaḥ sāṁgrāmiko rathaḥ

translations.english: This is his snapped bow and these are his broken shafts. And this is his war-car, O Rāma shattered in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
परिश्रान्तस्य मे पक्षौ छित्त्वा खड्गेन रावणः
सीतामादाय वैदेहीमुत्पपात विहायसं
रक्षसा निहतं पूर्व्म न मां हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ
sītāmādāya vaidehīmutpapāta vihāyasaṁ
rakṣasā nihataṁ pūrvma na māṁ hantuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: This is his charioteer lying on earth being killed by the velocity of my wings. Having sundered my wings with his dagger, who had been exhausted, Rāvana taking Sītā, rose high up in the welkin. It behove you not to kill me who had been wounded before by the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्तस्य तु विज्ञाय सीतासक्तां प्रियां कथाम्
गृध्रराजं परिष्वज्य रुरोद सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
rāmastasya tu vijñāya sītāsaktāṁ priyāṁ kathām
gṛdhrarājaṁ pariṣvajya ruroda sahalakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing from him pleasant words relating to Sītā, Rāma, leaving aside, instantly, his mighty bow, embraced him, and rolling on earth having lost self-control through grief, began to lament with Lakşmaņa. Though highly composed by nature, he was overwhelmed with doubled grief.

verses.sanskrit:
एकमेकायने दुर्गे निःश्वसन्तं कथंचन
समीक्ष्य दुःखितो रामः सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ekamekāyane durge niḥśvasantaṁ kathaṁcana
samīkṣya duḥkhito rāmaḥ saumitrimidamabravīt

translations.english: And beholding Jațāyu, sigh again and again and breathing with difficulty in a helpless plight, Rāma, highly aggrieved, spoke to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्याद्भ्रंशो वने वासः सीता नष्टा हतो द्विजः
ईदृशीयं ममालक्ष्मीर्निर्दहेदपि पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
rājyādbhraṁśo vane vāsaḥ sītā naṣṭā hato dvijaḥ
īdṛśīyaṁ mamālakṣmīrnirdahedapi pāvakam

translations.english: I have lost my kingdom and have been living in this forest. My Sītā has been carried away and this bird has been killed (on my account). This misfortune of mine can burn even the very fire.

verses.sanskrit:
संपूर्णमपि चेदद्य प्रतरेयं महोदधिम्
सोऽपि नूनं ममालक्ष्म्या विशुष्येत्सरितां पतिः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpūrṇamapi cedadya pratareyaṁ mahodadhim
so'pi nūnaṁ mamālakṣmyā viśuṣyetsaritāṁ patiḥ

translations.english: If for assuaging my grief I do enter the mighty ocean, verily shall that misfortune dry up even that lord of rivers.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्त्यभाग्यतरो लोके मत्तोऽस्मिन्सचराचरे
येनेयं महती प्राप्ता मया व्यसनवागुरा
verses.transliteration:
nāstyabhāgyataro loke matto'sminsacarācare
yeneyaṁ mahatī prāptā mayā vyasanavāgurā

translations.english: There is none so unfortunate as I, throughout this earth, mobile or immobile, and it is for this bad luck that I have confronted this mighty disaster.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं पितृवयस्यो मे गृध्रराजो जरान्वितः
शेते विनिहतो भूमौ मम भाग्यविपर्ययात्
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ pitṛvayasyo me gṛdhrarājo jarānvitaḥ
śete vinihato bhūmau mama bhāgyaviparyayāt

translations.english: This mighty king of vultures is our father's friend and he Leith on earth, killed through the evil turn of my fortune.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा बहुशो राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः
जटायुषं च पस्पर्श पितृस्नेहं निदर्शयन्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā bahuśo rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
jaṭāyuṣaṁ ca pasparśa pitṛsnehaṁ nidarśayan

translations.english: Uttering these and various other words, Rāghava, along with Lakşmaņa touched his body manifesting his paternal affection.

verses.sanskrit:
निकृत्तपक्षं रुधिरावसिक्तं; तं गृध्रराजं परिरभ्य रामः
क्व मैथिलि प्राणसमा ममेति; विमुच्य वाचं निपपात भूमौ
verses.transliteration:
nikṛttapakṣaṁ rudhirāvasiktaṁ; taṁ gṛdhrarājaṁ parirabhya rāmaḥ
kva maithili prāṇasamā mameti; vimucya vācaṁ nipapāta bhūmau

translations.english: Embracing the king of vultures, bathed in blood, having its wings cut off, Rāghava, fell on the ground, exclaiming where has Maithili gone like to my life?

verses.sanskrit:
जटायो यदि शक्नोषि वाक्यं व्याहरितुं पुनः
सीतामाख्याहि भद्रं ते वधमाख्याहि चात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyo yadi śaknoṣi vākyaṁ vyāharituṁ punaḥ
sītāmākhyāhi bhadraṁ te vadhamākhyāhi cātmanaḥ

translations.english: May good betide you, O Jatayu; if you are capable of speaking again, do you relate how Sītā has been carried away and you have been killed.

verses.sanskrit:
किंनिमित्तोऽहरत्सीतां रावणस्तस्य किं मया
अपराद्धं तु यं दृष्ट्वा रावणेन हृता प्रिया
verses.transliteration:
kiṁnimitto'haratsītāṁ rāvaṇastasya kiṁ mayā
aparāddhaṁ tu yaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena hṛtā priyā

translations.english: Why has Rāvaņa taken away by stealth the worshipful Jānki? What offence did I commit by him that he has carried away my dear one?

verses.sanskrit:
कथं तच्चन्द्रसंकाशं मुखमासीन्मनोहरम्
सीतया कानि चोक्तानि तस्मिन्काले द्विजोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ taccandrasaṁkāśaṁ mukhamāsīnmanoharam
sītayā kāni coktāni tasminkāle dvijottama

translations.english: O you best of birds, how looked the moonlike, pleasant countenance of Sītā at the time of her being carried away? What did she speak then?

verses.sanskrit:
कथंवीर्यः कथंरूपः किंकर्मा स च राक्षसः
क्व चास्य भवनं तात ब्रूहि मे परिपृच्छतः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁvīryaḥ kathaṁrūpaḥ kiṁkarmā sa ca rākṣasaḥ
kva cāsya bhavanaṁ tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ

translations.english: What is the prowess, appearance and action of that Raksasa? Where dose he live, O reverend Sir? Pray tell me, I do ask you.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुद्वीक्ष्याथ दीनात्मा विलपन्तमनन्तरम्
वाचातिसन्नया रामं जटायुरिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tamudvīkṣyātha dīnātmā vilapantamanantaram
vācātisannayā rāmaṁ jaṭāyuridamabravīt

translations.english: Beholding Rāma, lament like one helpless, the virtuous-souled Jațăyu spoke in faltering accents.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हृता राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन विहायसा
मायामास्थाय विपुलां वातदुर्दिनसंकुलाम्
verses.transliteration:
sā hṛtā rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena vihāyasā
māyāmāsthāya vipulāṁ vātadurdinasaṁkulām

translations.english: Sītā has been carried away by Rāvana, the lord of Rākşasas, creating a mighty illusion producing wind and showers.

verses.sanskrit:
परिश्रान्तस्य मे तात पक्षौ छित्त्वा निशाचरः
सीतामादाय वैदेहीं प्रयातो दक्षिणा मुखः
verses.transliteration:
pariśrāntasya me tāta pakṣau chittvā niśācaraḥ
sītāmādāya vaidehīṁ prayāto dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ

translations.english: O darling, myself being worn out that nightranger, having sundered my wings, fled away with Sītā to the southerly direction.

verses.sanskrit:
उपरुध्यन्ति मे प्राणा दृष्टिर्भ्रमति राघव
पश्यामि वृक्षान्सौवर्णानुशीरकृतमूर्धजान्
verses.transliteration:
uparudhyanti me prāṇā dṛṣṭirbhramati rāghava
paśyāmi vṛkṣānsauvarṇānuśīrakṛtamūrdhajān

translations.english: O Rāghava, my life is about to expire, my eye-sight has grown of mistaken perception, I see trees before me made of gold having hair resembling Usira.

verses.sanskrit:
येन याति मुहूर्तेन सीतामादाय रावणः
विप्रनष्टं धनं क्षिप्रं तत्स्वामिप्रतिपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
yena yāti muhūrtena sītāmādāya rāvaṇaḥ
vipranaṣṭaṁ dhanaṁ kṣipraṁ tatsvāmipratipadyate

translations.english: Rāvana has taken away Sītā at a moment when a person regains soon his lost property. O Kākutstha, this moment is called Vindya, which Rāvana has not been able to perceive. (At this moment) the person who takes away (a thing) is soon destroyed like to a fish devouring a hook. This refers to Jatāyu's astrological knowledge. Vindya is derived from the root Vid-to gain.
