Thus this moment is favourable to the laser and unfavourable to the taker. Hence Rāvana carrying away Sītā at this moment shall meet with destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
न च त्वया व्यथा कार्या जनकस्य सुतां प्रति
वैदेह्या रंस्यसे क्षिप्रं हत्वा तं राक्षसं रणे
verses.transliteration:
na ca tvayā vyathā kāryā janakasya sutāṁ prati
vaidehyā raṁsyase kṣipraṁ hatvā taṁ rākṣasaṁ raṇe

translations.english: Do not therefore entertain the least doubt about your coming by Janakī. Destroying him at the head of the battle you shall soon sport with Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
असंमूढस्य गृध्रस्य रामं प्रत्यनुभाषतः
आस्यात्सुस्राव रुधिरं म्रियमाणस्य सामिषम्
verses.transliteration:
asaṁmūḍhasya gṛdhrasya rāmaṁ pratyanubhāṣataḥ
āsyātsusrāva rudhiraṁ mriyamāṇasya sāmiṣam

translations.english: Thereupon flesh and gore began to come out of the mouth of Jatayu, the king of vultures, not loosing his sense even while treading the verge of death.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रो विश्रवसः साक्षाद्भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च
इत्युक्त्वा दुर्लभान्प्राणान्मुमोच पतगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
putro viśravasaḥ sākṣādbhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca
ityuktvā durlabhānprāṇānmumoca patageśvaraḥ

translations.english: Thereupon the king of birds gave up his dear life uttering only-Rāvana is the son of Visravā and brother to Vaisravana (the lord of wealth).

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूहि ब्रूहीति रामस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कृताञ्जलेः
त्यक्त्वा शरीरं गृध्रस्य जग्मुः प्राणा विहायसं
verses.transliteration:
brūhi brūhīti rāmasya bruvāṇasya kṛtāñjaleḥ
tyaktvā śarīraṁ gṛdhrasya jagmuḥ prāṇā vihāyasaṁ

translations.english: Rāma again and again addressed him with joined palms saying, Do you speak! Do you speak. And instantly Jatayu's vital spark rose up in the sky, leaving his bodily frame.

verses.sanskrit:
स निक्षिप्य शिरो भूमौ प्रसार्य चरणौ तदा
विक्षिप्य च शरीरं स्वं पपात धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
sa nikṣipya śiro bhūmau prasārya caraṇau tadā
vikṣipya ca śarīraṁ svaṁ papāta dharaṇītale

translations.english: Thereupon the king of vultures fell down on the earth by stretching forth his legs, body and head on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तं गृध्रं प्रेक्ष्य ताम्राक्षं गतासुमचलोपमम्
रामः सुबहुभिर्दुःखैर्दीनः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ gṛdhraṁ prekṣya tāmrākṣaṁ gatāsumacalopamam
rāmaḥ subahubhirduḥkhairdīnaḥ saumitrimabravīt

translations.english: Beholding the vulture dead, of huge proportions, resembling a hill and having red eyes, Rama, aggrieved, spoke piteously to Saumitri.

verses.sanskrit:
बहूनि रक्षसां वासे वर्षाणि वसता सुखम्
अनेन दण्डकारण्ये विचीर्णमिह पक्षिणा
verses.transliteration:
bahūni rakṣasāṁ vāse varṣāṇi vasatā sukham
anena daṇḍakāraṇye vicīrṇamiha pakṣiṇā

translations.english: Living happily, for years, in this forest of Dandaka inhabited by the Rākşasas, Jațāyu has, at last, given up his life.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेकवार्षिको यस्तु चिरकालं समुत्थितः
सोऽयमद्य हतः शेते कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
anekavārṣiko yastu cirakālaṁ samutthitaḥ
so'yamadya hataḥ śete kālo hi duratikramaḥ

translations.english: He lived for a long time, of an uplifted person, and has now laid low on the earth. None can withstand the course of destiny.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण गृध्रोऽयमुपकारी हतश्च मे
सीतामभ्यवपन्नो वै रावणेन बलीयसा
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa gṛdhro'yamupakārī hataśca me
sītāmabhyavapanno vai rāvaṇena balīyasā

translations.english: Observe, O Laksmana, this vulture for my benefaction, has been killed by the powerful Rāvaņa in his attempt to rescue Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
गृध्रराज्यं परित्यज्य पितृपैतामहं महत्
मम हेतोरयं प्राणान्मुमोच पतगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
gṛdhrarājyaṁ parityajya pitṛpaitāmahaṁ mahat
mama hetorayaṁ prāṇānmumoca patageśvaraḥ

translations.english: For me, has this Lord of birds, breathed his last, renouncing his large ancestral kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वत्र खलु दृश्यन्ते साधवो धर्मचारिणः
शूराः शरण्याः सौमित्रे तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
sarvatra khalu dṛśyante sādhavo dharmacāriṇaḥ
śūrāḥ śaraṇyāḥ saumitre tiryagyonigateṣvapi

translations.english: In every status of animal creation, the heroic, the righteous and the honest, affording refuge to all, are to be found, even among the birds.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताहरणजं दुःखं न मे सौम्य तथागतम्
यथा विनाशो गृध्रस्य मत्कृते च परंतप
verses.transliteration:
sītāharaṇajaṁ duḥkhaṁ na me saumya tathāgatam
yathā vināśo gṛdhrasya matkṛte ca paraṁtapa

translations.english: I do not feel so much affliction, O hero, for Sītā's ravishment as I do for this vulture, who has been killed for me.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा दशरथः श्रीमान्यथा मम मया यशाः
पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च तथायं पतगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
rājā daśarathaḥ śrīmānyathā mama mayā yaśāḥ
pūjanīyaśca mānyaśca tathāyaṁ patageśvaraḥ

translations.english: Like to the highly famous, effulgent king Dasaratha, this King of birds is worthy of being adored and worshipped by me.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रे हर काष्ठानि निर्मथिष्यामि पावकम्
गृध्रराजं दिधक्षामि मत्कृते निधनं गतम्
verses.transliteration:
saumitre hara kāṣṭhāni nirmathiṣyāmi pāvakam
gṛdhrarājaṁ didhakṣāmi matkṛte nidhanaṁ gatam

translations.english: O Saumitri, do you bring fuels; I shall produce fire there-with and burn the dead body of this king of birds who has been killed on my account.

verses.sanskrit:
नाथं पतगलोकस्य चितामारोपयाम्यहम्
इमं धक्ष्यामि सौमित्रे हतं रौद्रेण रक्षसा
verses.transliteration:
nāthaṁ patagalokasya citāmāropayāmyaham
imaṁ dhakṣyāmi saumitre hataṁ raudreṇa rakṣasā

translations.english: Placing on a funeral pile, I shall cremate, O Saumitrī, the dead body of this king of birds who has been destroyed by the grim-visaged Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
या गतिर्यज्ञशीलानामाहिताग्नेश्च या गतिः
अपरावर्तिनां या च या च भूमिप्रदायिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
yā gatiryajñaśīlānāmāhitāgneśca yā gatiḥ
aparāvartināṁ yā ca yā ca bhūmipradāyinām

translations.english: Being consecrated and commanded by me, do you, O highly powerful king of birds, attain to that excellent state of existence, which is reached by persons ever performing pious observance, by Āhilāgnis by heroes who are not afraid of entering a battle-field and by persons who confer grants of land.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा चितां दीप्तामारोप्य पतगेश्वरम्
ददाह रामो धर्मात्मा स्वबन्धुमिव दुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā citāṁ dīptāmāropya patageśvaram
dadāha rāmo dharmātmā svabandhumiva duḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Saying this the virtuous-souled Rāma, afflicted with sorrow, burned the body of the king of birds, placing it on the funeral pile, like to his own kinsman.

verses.sanskrit:
रोहिमांसानि चोद्धृत्य पेशीकृत्वा महायशाः
शकुनाय ददौ रामो रम्ये हरितशाद्वले
verses.transliteration:
rohimāṁsāni coddhṛtya peśīkṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ
śakunāya dadau rāmo ramye haritaśādvale

translations.english: Entering the forest with Saumitrī, Rāma gifted with prowess, killed plump high deer and stretched forth grass and twigs for offering oblation to that bird. Taking off the flesh of those high deer and clustering it, Rāma, of great renown, offered it to the vultures in that pleasant forest-land, abounding in green grass.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तत्प्रेतस्य मर्त्यस्य कथयन्ति द्विजातयः
तत्स्वर्गगमनं तस्य क्षिप्रं रामो जजाप ह
verses.transliteration:
yattatpretasya martyasya kathayanti dvijātayaḥ
tatsvargagamanaṁ tasya kṣipraṁ rāmo jajāpa ha

translations.english: Thereupon for his speedy arrival at the abode of celestials, Rāma recited those Mantras which are being uttered by the twice-born ones.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गोदावरीं गत्वा नदीं नरवरात्मजौ
उदकं चक्रतुस्तस्मै गृध्रराजाय तावुभौ
verses.transliteration:
tato godāvarīṁ gatvā nadīṁ naravarātmajau
udakaṁ cakratustasmai gṛdhrarājāya tāvubhau

translations.english: Afterwards repairing to the river Godāverī the two princes offered water to that kingly vulture.

verses.sanskrit:
स गृध्रराजः कृतवान्यशस्करं; सुदुष्करं कर्म रणे निपातितः
महर्षिकल्पेन च संस्कृतस्तदा; जगाम पुण्यां गतिमात्मनः शुभाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa gṛdhrarājaḥ kṛtavānyaśaskaraṁ; suduṣkaraṁ karma raṇe nipātitaḥ
maharṣikalpena ca saṁskṛtastadā; jagāma puṇyāṁ gatimātmanaḥ śubhām

translations.english: Having been killed in battle for an arduous but glorious work, that king of vultures, consecrated by the ascetic-like Rāma, attained to an excellent state.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वैवमुदकं तस्मै प्रस्थितौ राघवौ तदा
अवेक्षन्तौ वने सीतां पश्चिमां जग्मतुर्दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvaivamudakaṁ tasmai prasthitau rāghavau tadā
avekṣantau vane sītāṁ paścimāṁ jagmaturdiśam

translations.english: Having offered him the gift of water, those two descendants of Raghu wended their way in that forest in quest of Sītā and proceeded towards the south-west*. In this sloka west is mentioned and in the next one there is reference to their turning to the south and hence west here refers to south-west.

verses.sanskrit:
तां दिशं दक्षिणां गत्वा शरचापासिधारिणौ
अविप्रहतमैक्ष्वाकौ पन्थानं प्रतिपेदतुः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ diśaṁ dakṣiṇāṁ gatvā śaracāpāsidhāriṇau
aviprahatamaikṣvākau panthānaṁ pratipedatuḥ

translations.english: Then turning to the south, with bow and arrows in hand, they reached a track not wended by the people.

verses.sanskrit:
गुल्मैर्वृक्षैश्च बहुभिर्लताभिश्च प्रवेष्टितम्
आवृतं सर्वतो दुर्गं गहनं घोरदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
gulmairvṛkṣaiśca bahubhirlatābhiśca praveṣṭitam
āvṛtaṁ sarvato durgaṁ gahanaṁ ghoradarśanam

translations.english: It was a ghastly, impenetrable forest, covered on all sides with groves, trees and creepers,

verses.sanskrit:
व्यतिक्रम्य तु वेगेन गृहीत्वा दक्षिणां दिशम्
सुभीमं तन्महारण्यं व्यतियातौ महाबलौ
verses.transliteration:
vyatikramya tu vegena gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṁ diśam
subhīmaṁ tanmahāraṇyaṁ vyatiyātau mahābalau

translations.english: Proceeding by the southerly direction, those two mighty ones, passed hastily by that terrible, dreary forest.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परं जनस्थानात्त्रिक्रोशं गम्य राघवौ
क्रौञ्चारण्यं विविशतुर्गहनं तौ महौजसौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paraṁ janasthānāttrikrośaṁ gamya rāghavau
krauñcāraṇyaṁ viviśaturgahanaṁ tau mahaujasau

translations.english: Thereupon, the highly effulgent descendants of Raghu entered the dense forest of Krauñca, situated at a distance of six miles from Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
नानामेघघनप्रख्यं प्रहृष्टमिव सर्वतः
नानावर्णैः शुभैः पुष्पैर्मृगपक्षिगणैर्युतम्
verses.transliteration:
nānāmeghaghanaprakhyaṁ prahṛṣṭamiva sarvataḥ
nānāvarṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ puṣpairmṛgapakṣigaṇairyutam

translations.english: It was a dense forest like to a collection of clouds, as if smiling on all sides blooming with charming flowers of diverse hues and frequented by various animals and birds.

verses.sanskrit:
दिदृक्षमाणौ वैदेहीं तद्वनं तौ विचिक्यतुः
तत्र तत्रावतिष्ठन्तौ सीताहरणकर्शितौ
verses.transliteration:
didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīṁ tadvanaṁ tau vicikyatuḥ
tatra tatrāvatiṣṭhantau sītāharaṇakarśitau

translations.english: Waiting for sometime here and there they, exercised with Sītā's ravishment, explored the entire forest in quest of Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्तु महातेजाः सत्त्ववाञ्शीलवाञ्शुचिः
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसं
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇastu mahātejāḥ sattvavāñśīlavāñśuciḥ
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ bhrātaraṁ dīptatejasaṁ

translations.english: There upon the highly effulgent and truthful Laksmana, possessing a pure character, spoke, with folded hands, to his brother of flaming energy.

verses.sanskrit:
स्पन्दते मे दृढं बाहुरुद्विग्नमिव मे मनः
प्रायशश्चाप्यनिष्टानि निमित्तान्युपलक्षये
verses.transliteration:
spandate me dṛḍhaṁ bāhurudvignamiva me manaḥ
prāyaśaścāpyaniṣṭāni nimittānyupalakṣaye

translations.english: My left arm is throbbing, my mind is filled with anxiety and I perceive before me many a bad omen. Do you put on your habiliments, O worshipful one, and act by what I say for your well-being. Methinks from these bad omens some calamity shall soon befall us.

verses.sanskrit:
एष वञ्चुलको नाम पक्षी परमदारुणः
आवयोर्विजयं युद्धे शंसन्निव विनर्दति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa vañculako nāma pakṣī paramadāruṇaḥ
āvayorvijayaṁ yuddhe śaṁsanniva vinardati

translations.english: O Rāma, this terrible bird Vanjulaka is emitting fearful cries as if announcing our victory in the conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोरन्वेषतोरेवं सर्वं तद्वनमोजसा
संजज्ञे विपुलः शब्दः प्रभञ्जन्निव तद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tayoranveṣatorevaṁ sarvaṁ tadvanamojasā
saṁjajñe vipulaḥ śabdaḥ prabhañjanniva tadvanam

translations.english: Thereupon while they began to explore the entire forest with their prowess there arose a terrible sound as if breaking down the wood.

verses.sanskrit:
संवेष्टितमिवात्यर्थं गहनं मातरिश्वना
वनस्य तस्य शब्दोऽभूद्दिवमापूरयन्निव
verses.transliteration:
saṁveṣṭitamivātyarthaṁ gahanaṁ mātariśvanā
vanasya tasya śabdo'bhūddivamāpūrayanniva

translations.english: The forest was enveloped on all sides with a mighty wind and everywhere was audible a roar filling the wood-land.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शब्दं काङ्क्षमाणस्तु रामः कक्षे सहानुजः
ददर्श सुमहाकायं राक्षसं विपुलोरसं
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śabdaṁ kāṅkṣamāṇastu rāmaḥ kakṣe sahānujaḥ
dadarśa sumahākāyaṁ rākṣasaṁ vipulorasaṁ

translations.english: With a view to ascertain whence the sound proceeded, Rāma, with a dagger in hand, along with his younger brother, espied a Rākşasha of huge proportions, having big thighs.

verses.sanskrit:
आसेदतुस्ततस्तत्र तावुभौ प्रमुखे स्थितम्
विवृद्धमशिरोग्रीवं कबन्धमुदरे मुखम्
verses.transliteration:
āsedatustatastatra tāvubhau pramukhe sthitam
vivṛddhamaśirogrīvaṁ kabandhamudare mukham

translations.english: The two brothers beheld that Rākşasa stationed before them, having a huge body, devoid of head and neck and therefore a headless demon and having its mouth on its belly.

verses.sanskrit:
रोमभिर्निचितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्महागिरिमिवोच्छ्रितम्
नीलमेघनिभं रौद्रं मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
romabhirnicitaistīkṣṇairmahāgirimivocchritam
nīlameghanibhaṁ raudraṁ meghastanitaniḥsvanam

translations.english: Its body resembled a huge mountain and was covered with sharpened down; its look was terrible like to sable cloud and its roar resembled the muttering where of.

verses.sanskrit:
महापक्ष्मेण पिङ्गेन विपुलेनायतेन च
एकेनोरसि घोरेण नयनेनाशुदर्शिना
verses.transliteration:
mahāpakṣmeṇa piṅgena vipulenāyatena ca
ekenorasi ghoreṇa nayanenāśudarśinā

translations.english: Its one terrible, expansive eye, seeing all, was on the fore-head placed on its breast and shone forth like to the flaming fire and it had huge yellow eye-lashes. Its mouth was greatly widened and covered with rows of huge teeth and it was again and again licking that terrible mouth.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरौ भुजौ विकुर्वाणमुभौ योजनमायतौ
कराभ्यां विविधान्गृह्य ऋष्कान्पक्षिगणान्मृगान्
verses.transliteration:
ghorau bhujau vikurvāṇamubhau yojanamāyatau
karābhyāṁ vividhāngṛhya ṛṣkānpakṣigaṇānmṛgān

translations.english: And stretching forth its two huge arms extending over a Yojana it was devouring bears, lions and deer. It was catching and throwing with its huge hands many an animal, bird and bear.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तौ समतिक्रम्य क्रोशमात्रे ददर्शतुः
महान्तं दारुणं भीमं कबन्धं भुजसंवृतम्
verses.transliteration:
atha tau samatikramya krośamātre dadarśatuḥ
mahāntaṁ dāruṇaṁ bhīmaṁ kabandhaṁ bhujasaṁvṛtam

translations.english: Hindering the way-fare it was awaiting those two brothers. And proceeding a Krosa, they espied that fearful, grim-visaged, headless demon, hindering all creatures with its arms, terrible-looking and appearing like a kabandha from its very situation,

verses.sanskrit:
स महाबाहुरत्यर्थं प्रसार्य विपुलौ भुजौ
जग्राह सहितावेव राघवौ पीडयन्बलात्
verses.transliteration:
sa mahābāhuratyarthaṁ prasārya vipulau bhujau
jagrāha sahitāveva rāghavau pīḍayanbalāt

translations.english: Thereupon that one, of huge arms, stretching them forth, got hold of those two descendants of Raghu crushing them with its strength.

verses.sanskrit:
खड्गिनौ दृढधन्वानौ तिग्मतेजौ महाभुजौ
भ्रातरौ विवशं प्राप्तौ कृष्यमाणौ महाबलौ
verses.transliteration:
khaḍginau dṛḍhadhanvānau tigmatejau mahābhujau
bhrātarau vivaśaṁ prāptau kṛṣyamāṇau mahābalau

translations.english: Those two highly powerful brothers, of mighty arms, with daggers and bows in their hands, were assailed and got hold of by that Raksasha.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरं देशमिमं प्राप्तौ मम भक्षावुपस्थितौ
वदतं कार्यमिह वां किमर्थं चागतौ युवाम्
verses.transliteration:
ghoraṁ deśamimaṁ prāptau mama bhakṣāvupasthitau
vadataṁ kāryamiha vāṁ kimarthaṁ cāgatau yuvām

translations.english: Who are you two youthful figures having the neck of a bull and with mighty daggers and bows in your hands? Arriving in this fearful place you have by chance come within the compass of my vision. Tell me now what have you to do here, and what for have you come? I have been waiting here being hungry, and you have come here having daggers and bows with arrows in your hands like to two oxen having sharpened horns. Nearing me quickly, it will be hard for you to draw your vital breath.

verses.sanskrit:
कृच्छ्रात्कृच्छ्रतरं प्राप्य दारुणं सत्यविक्रम
व्यसनं जीवितान्ताय प्राप्तमप्राप्य तां प्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛcchrātkṛcchrataraṁ prāpya dāruṇaṁ satyavikrama
vyasanaṁ jīvitāntāya prāptamaprāpya tāṁ priyām

translations.english: Hearing those words of the vicious-souled Kabandha, Rāma having his countenance dried up, bespoke Laksmana-O you, having truth for your prowess, again and again, greater and worse calamities have been threatening us. We have already met with a dire disaster leading to our death, consequent on my separation from my dear one.

verses.sanskrit:
कालस्य सुमहद्वीर्यं सर्वभूतेषु लक्ष्मण
त्वां च मां च नरव्याघ्र व्यसनैः पश्य मोहितौ
नातिभारोऽस्ति दैवस्य सर्वभुतेषु लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
kālasya sumahadvīryaṁ sarvabhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa
tvāṁ ca māṁ ca naravyāghra vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitau
nātibhāro'sti daivasya sarvabhuteṣu lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: Mighty is the course of Destiny in all creatures, O Lakşmaņa. Do you O best of men, behold even yourself and me stricken with calamity. But O Lakşmaņa it is not very difficult for destiny to afflict all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च कृतास्त्राश्च रणाजिरे
कालाभिपन्नाः सीदन्ति यथा वालुकसेतवः
verses.transliteration:
śūrāśca balavantaśca kṛtāstrāśca raṇājire
kālābhipannāḥ sīdanti yathā vālukasetavaḥ

translations.english: Under the influence of destiny even the mighty heroes, well habited in armours are distressed like to a bridge of sands.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणो दृढसत्यविक्रमो; महायशा दाशरथिः प्रतापवान्
अवेक्ष्य सौमित्रिमुदग्रविक्रमं; स्थिरां तदा स्वां मतिमात्मनाकरोत्
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇo dṛḍhasatyavikramo; mahāyaśā dāśarathiḥ pratāpavān
avekṣya saumitrimudagravikramaṁ; sthirāṁ tadā svāṁ matimātmanākarot

translations.english: Addressing these words to Saumitrī, the resolute, powerful and highly famous son of Dasaratha, having truth for his prowess, composed himself by dint of his own understanding.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तु तत्र स्थितौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
बाहुपाशपरिक्षिप्तौ कबन्धो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tau tu tatra sthitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
bāhupāśaparikṣiptau kabandho vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Beholding both the brothers, Rāma and Laks maņa, clasping each other with their arms, the headless demon spoke:

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठतः किं नु मां दृष्ट्वा क्षुधार्तं क्षत्रियर्षभौ
आहारार्थं तु संदिष्टौ दैवेन गतचेतसौ
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭhataḥ kiṁ nu māṁ dṛṣṭvā kṣudhārtaṁ kṣatriyarṣabhau
āhārārthaṁ tu saṁdiṣṭau daivena gatacetasau

translations.english: O two best of Ksatryas, are you waiting here beholding me hungry? O you having lost your sense, you have been chosen by Destiny as my food.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो वाक्यं प्राप्तकालं हितं तदा
उवाचार्तिसमापन्नो विक्रमे कृतनिश्चयः
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā lakṣmaṇo vākyaṁ prāptakālaṁ hitaṁ tadā
uvācārtisamāpanno vikrame kṛtaniścayaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words Laksmana, sore, distressed and determined to display his valour, addressed Rāma with words worthy of being said on that occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां च मां च पुरा तूर्णमादत्ते राक्षसाधमः
तस्मादसिभ्यामस्याशु बाहू छिन्दावहे गुरू
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ ca māṁ ca purā tūrṇamādatte rākṣasādhamaḥ
tasmādasibhyāmasyāśu bāhū chindāvahe gurū

translations.english: This vile Rākṣasa shall seize both of us; let us sunder soon its two huge arms with our daggers.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तौ देशकालज्ञौ खड्गाभ्यामेव राघवौ
अच्छिन्दतां सुसंहृष्टौ बाहू तस्यांसदेशयोः
verses.transliteration:
tatastau deśakālajñau khaḍgābhyāmeva rāghavau
acchindatāṁ susaṁhṛṣṭau bāhū tasyāṁsadeśayoḥ

translations.english: Thereat Rāma and Lakşmana, cognizant of time and place, pleased+, sundered its arms off its shoulders with their daggers. They were pleased because they cut off its arms with ease like to the trunks of a plantain tree.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणो दक्षिणं बाहुमसक्तमसिना ततः
चिच्छेद रामो वेगेन सव्यं वीरस्तु लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇaṁ bāhumasaktamasinā tataḥ
ciccheda rāmo vegena savyaṁ vīrastu lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Rāma, stationed on the right side cut off in no time its right arm with his dagger and the heroic Laksmana, the left one. It may mean also expert.

verses.sanskrit:
स पपात महाबाहुश्छिन्नबाहुर्महास्वनः
खं च गां च दिशश्चैव नादयञ्जलदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
sa papāta mahābāhuśchinnabāhurmahāsvanaḥ
khaṁ ca gāṁ ca diśaścaiva nādayañjalado yathā

translations.english: Having got its arms dissevered, the terriblevoiced, Kabandha, of huge arms, roaring like to the muttering of clouds and resounding the heaven, earth and all the quarters, fell flat on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
स निकृत्तौ भुजौ दृष्ट्वा शोणितौघपरिप्लुतः
दीनः पप्रच्छ तौ वीरौ कौ युवामिति दानवः
verses.transliteration:
sa nikṛttau bhujau dṛṣṭvā śoṇitaughapariplutaḥ
dīnaḥ papraccha tau vīrau kau yuvāmiti dānavaḥ

translations.english: Beholding both its arms cut off, the demon, with its person bathed in blood, asked them poorly Who are you?

verses.sanskrit:
इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः
शशंस तस्य काकुत्स्थं कबन्धस्य महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
iti tasya bruvāṇasya lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
śaśaṁsa tasya kākutsthaṁ kabandhasya mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Being thus accosted by Kabandha, the mighty Lakşmana, gifted with auspicious marks, spoke to it, about Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
अयमिक्ष्वाकुदायादो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
अस्यैवावरजं विद्धि भ्रातरं मां च लक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
ayamikṣvākudāyādo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
asyaivāvarajaṁ viddhi bhrātaraṁ māṁ ca lakṣmaṇam

translations.english: He is a descendant of the Ikşvākus known on earth by the name of Rāma, and know me as his younger brother, by name-Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य देवप्रभावस्य वसतो विजने वने
रक्षसापहृता भार्या यामिच्छन्ताविहागतौ
verses.transliteration:
asya devaprabhāvasya vasato vijane vane
rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā yāmicchantāvihāgatau

translations.english: Being thwarted by mother (Kaikeyi) in his accession of kingdom, he, renouncing all, has fled as an exile to woods, and has, along with me and his spouse, been ranging this forest. While living in the dense forest the wife of Răma, effulgent like to the celestials has been ravished by a Raksasa. Searching her, have we come here.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं तु को वा किमर्थं वा कबन्ध सदृशो वने
आस्येनोरसि दीप्तेन भग्नजङ्घो विचेष्टसे
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ tu ko vā kimarthaṁ vā kabandha sadṛśo vane
āsyenorasi dīptena bhagnajaṅgho viceṣṭase

translations.english: Who are you? And what for are you ranging this forest like to a headless demon, having your thighs broken and your flaming face placed on your breast?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः कबन्धस्तु लक्ष्मणेनोत्तरं वचः
उवाच परमप्रीतस्तदिन्द्रवचनं स्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ kabandhastu lakṣmaṇenottaraṁ vacaḥ
uvāca paramaprītastadindravacanaṁ smaran

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa with these goodly words, Kabandha, pleased, recollecting the words of Indra, bespoke him,

verses.sanskrit:
स्वागतं वां नरव्याघ्रौ दिष्ट्या पश्यामि चाप्यहम्
दिष्ट्या चेमौ निकृत्तौ मे युवाभ्यां बाहुबन्धनौ
verses.transliteration:
svāgataṁ vāṁ naravyāghrau diṣṭyā paśyāmi cāpyaham
diṣṭyā cemau nikṛttau me yuvābhyāṁ bāhubandhanau

translations.english: O two best of men, you are welcome! By my good luck it is that I do behold you. By my good fortune you have dissevered my shoulders today.

verses.sanskrit:
विरूपं यच्च मे रूपं प्राप्तं ह्यविनयाद्यथा
तन्मे शृणु नरव्याघ्र तत्त्वतः शंसतस्तव
verses.transliteration:
virūpaṁ yacca me rūpaṁ prāptaṁ hyavinayādyathā
tanme śṛṇu naravyāghra tattvataḥ śaṁsatastava

translations.english: Do you hear; I shall relate truly to you how have I, by my haughtiness, come by this unsightly shape.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा राम महाबाहो महाबलपराक्रम
रूपमासीन्ममाचिन्त्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्
यथा सोमस्य शक्रस्य सूर्यस्य च यथा वपुः
verses.transliteration:
purā rāma mahābāho mahābalaparākrama
rūpamāsīnmamācintyaṁ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
yathā somasya śakrasya sūryasya ca yathā vapuḥ

translations.english: O Mighty armed Rāma of great prowess, formerly my beauty, beyond conception, was known all over the three worlds, like to the beauty of the Sun, the Moon and Indra. I used to frighten everywhere the ascetics living in the forest by turning this my beauty into a terrific form.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स्थूलशिरा नाम महर्षिः कोपितो मया
संचिन्वन्विविधं वन्यं रूपेणानेन धर्षितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sthūlaśirā nāma maharṣiḥ kopito mayā
saṁcinvanvividhaṁ vanyaṁ rūpeṇānena dharṣitaḥ

translations.english: Once on a time assuming this terrible shape I assailed and enraged the great ascetic Sthulasira collecting diverse wild fruits. Thereupon he imprecated curses upon me.

verses.sanskrit:
स मया याचितः क्रुद्धः शापस्यान्तो भवेदिति
अभिशापकृतस्येति तेनेदं भाषितं वचः
verses.transliteration:
sa mayā yācitaḥ kruddhaḥ śāpasyānto bhavediti
abhiśāpakṛtasyeti tenedaṁ bhāṣitaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Do you retain this ghastly shape hated of all mankind. Upon my praying to that angry ascetic for my relief from that curse, he said.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा छित्त्वा भुजौ रामस्त्वां दहेद्विजने वने
तदा त्वं प्राप्स्यसे रूपं स्वमेव विपुलं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
yadā chittvā bhujau rāmastvāṁ dahedvijane vane
tadā tvaṁ prāpsyase rūpaṁ svameva vipulaṁ śubham

translations.english: You shall regain your stalwart and beautiful shape when you shall be burnt by Rāma in a dense forest having got your arms dissevered by him.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि तपसोग्रेण पितामहमतोषयम्
दीर्घमायुः स मे प्रादात्ततो मां विभ्रमोऽस्पृशत्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi tapasogreṇa pitāmahamatoṣayam
dīrghamāyuḥ sa me prādāttato māṁ vibhramo'spṛśat

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, know me to be the beautiful son of Danu. Through Indra's curse in the battle field I have been metamorphosed into my present shape. After I had pleased him with hard austerites, the Grand-Father of the celestials conferred on me a long life. And therefore I was inflamed with pride assailed Indra in a conflict, thinking within me, 'I have gained a long life-what can Indra do me?'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बाहुप्रमुक्तेन वज्रेण शतपर्वणा
सक्थिनी च शिरश्चैव शरीरे संप्रवेशितम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya bāhupramuktena vajreṇa śataparvaṇā
sakthinī ca śiraścaiva śarīre saṁpraveśitam

translations.english: Thereupon by his thunderbolt, having hundred edges hurled off his hands, my thighs were shattered and my head thrusted into my body.

verses.sanskrit:
स मया याच्यमानः सन्नानयद्यमसादनम्
पितामहवचः सत्यं तदस्त्विति ममाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa mayā yācyamānaḥ sannānayadyamasādanam
pitāmahavacaḥ satyaṁ tadastviti mamābravīt

translations.english: Myself praying for the close of my life, he did not despatch me to the abode of Yama. He only said May the words of the Grand Sire prove true.'

verses.sanskrit:
अनाहारः कथं शक्तो भग्नसक्थिशिरोमुखः
वज्रेणाभिहतः कालं सुदीर्घमपि जीवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
anāhāraḥ kathaṁ śakto bhagnasakthiśiromukhaḥ
vajreṇābhihataḥ kālaṁ sudīrghamapi jīvitum

translations.english: Where to I replied 'How shall I live long without any food, being smitten by you having a thunderbolt in your hand, and having my head, thighs and mouth crushed down?' Thereat Indra made my hands extending over a Yojana and placed my mouth, having sharpened teeth, on my belly.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां समाकृष्य वनेचरान्
सिंहद्विपमृगव्याघ्रान्भक्षयामि समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ bhujābhyāṁ dīrghābhyāṁ samākṛṣya vanecarān
siṁhadvipamṛgavyāghrānbhakṣayāmi samantataḥ

translations.english: Thenceforth, stretching out my long arms I used to devour all lions, tigers, wolves and deer ranging the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु मामब्रवीदिन्द्रो यदा रामः सलक्ष्मणः
छेत्स्यते समरे बाहू तदा स्वर्गं गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sa tu māmabravīdindro yadā rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
chetsyate samare bāhū tadā svargaṁ gamiṣyasi

translations.english: Indra said to me, 'You shall attain to heaven when Rāma, along with Laksmana, shall cut off your arms in a battle.'

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि मतिसाचिव्यं करिष्यामि नरर्षभ
मित्रं चैवोपदेक्ष्यामि युवाभ्यां संस्कृतोऽग्निना
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi matisācivyaṁ kariṣyāmi nararṣabha
mitraṁ caivopadekṣyāmi yuvābhyāṁ saṁskṛto'gninā

translations.english: Being cremated by you, I shall counsel you best and tell you with whom you should contract friendship.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दनुना तेन राघवः
इदं जगाद वचनं लक्ष्मणस्योपशृण्वतः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu dharmātmā danunā tena rāghavaḥ
idaṁ jagāda vacanaṁ lakṣmaṇasyopaśṛṇvataḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Danu, the virtuoussouled Rāghva spoke before listening Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेन हृता सीता मम भार्या यशस्विनी
निष्क्रान्तस्य जनस्थानात्सह भ्रात्रा यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā mama bhāryā yaśasvinī
niṣkrāntasya janasthānātsaha bhrātrā yathāsukham

translations.english: My renowned spouse Sītā was easily ravished by Rāvaņa after I had gone out of Janasthana along with my brother. I know that Raksasa's name only—but do not know his whereabouts, his figure and his prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकार्तानामनाथानामेवं विपरिधावताम्
कारुण्यं सदृशं कर्तुमुपकारे च वर्तताम्
verses.transliteration:
śokārtānāmanāthānāmevaṁ viparidhāvatām
kāruṇyaṁ sadṛśaṁ kartumupakāre ca vartatām

translations.english: It behove you to show proper compassion for us, who have been stricken with grief, who are helpless, have been ranging this forest in this way and are, ever engaged in the well-being of others*. This sloka may be rendered in another way:Do you continue benefiting us by showing proper compassion for us, who are stricken with grief helpless and ranging the forest in this way. We have however adopted here the commentator Rāmāņaya's explanation.

verses.sanskrit:
काष्ठान्यानीय शुष्काणि काले भग्नानि कुञ्जरैः
भक्ष्यामस्त्वां वयं वीर श्वभ्रे महति कल्पिते
verses.transliteration:
kāṣṭhānyānīya śuṣkāṇi kāle bhagnāni kuñjaraiḥ
bhakṣyāmastvāṁ vayaṁ vīra śvabhre mahati kalpite

translations.english: O, hero, we shall burn you after collecting all the branches that have been broken down by the elephants and dried up in time, and digging a big trench.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं सीतां समाचक्ष्व येन वा यत्र वा हृता
कुरु कल्याणमत्यर्थं यदि जानासि तत्त्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ sītāṁ samācakṣva yena vā yatra vā hṛtā
kuru kalyāṇamatyarthaṁ yadi jānāsi tattvataḥ

translations.english: Do you tell us who has carried away Sītā? And where? If do you know it truly do you perform us this good service.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण वाक्यं दनुरनुत्तमम्
प्रोवाच कुशलो वक्तुं वक्तारमपि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa vākyaṁ danuranuttamam
provāca kuśalo vaktuṁ vaktāramapi rāghavam

translations.english: Thereat the Rākşasa, skilled in speech, spoke to Rāghava, addressing him thus.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्यमस्ति न मे ज्ञानं नाभिजानामि मैथिलीम्
यस्तां ज्ञास्यति तं वक्ष्ये दग्धः स्वं रूपमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
divyamasti na me jñānaṁ nābhijānāmi maithilīm
yastāṁ jñāsyati taṁ vakṣye dagdhaḥ svaṁ rūpamāsthitaḥ

translations.english: I am not gifted with divine fore-sight and therefore do not know where Maithilī is. I shall let you know of him who shall be able to tell you all about her, after I resume my original shape, being burnt (by you). I shall furthermore tell you, O Rāma, who knows that Räksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
अदग्धस्य हि विज्ञातुं शक्तिरस्ति न मे प्रभो
राक्षसं तं महावीर्यं सीता येन हृता तव
verses.transliteration:
adagdhasya hi vijñātuṁ śaktirasti na me prabho
rākṣasaṁ taṁ mahāvīryaṁ sītā yena hṛtā tava

translations.english: Without being burnt I am incapable of being cognizant of that highly powerful Rākṣasa who has carried away your Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञानं हि महद्भ्रष्टं शापदोषेण राघव
स्वकृतेन मया प्राप्तं रूपं लोकविगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
vijñānaṁ hi mahadbhraṣṭaṁ śāpadoṣeṇa rāghava
svakṛtena mayā prāptaṁ rūpaṁ lokavigarhitam

translations.english: By the influence of curse, I have lost my foresight and by my own improper actions I have been transformed into this ugly figure.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तु यावन्न यात्यस्तं सविता श्रान्तवाहनः
तावन्मामवटे क्षिप्त्वा दह राम यथाविधि
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tu yāvanna yātyastaṁ savitā śrāntavāhanaḥ
tāvanmāmavaṭe kṣiptvā daha rāma yathāvidhi

translations.english: Do you cremate me according to the prescribed rites after throwing me into the ditch before the sun, with his worn out carriers descends into the western horizon.

verses.sanskrit:
दग्धस्त्वयाहमवटे न्यायेन रघुनन्दन
वक्ष्यामि तमहं वीर यस्तं ज्ञास्यति राक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
dagdhastvayāhamavaṭe nyāyena raghunandana
vakṣyāmi tamahaṁ vīra yastaṁ jñāsyati rākṣasaṁ

translations.english: Being burnt by you in the ditch, with due ceremonials, O descendant of Raghu, I shall inention, to you, one who knows that Rāksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन सख्यं च कर्तव्यं न्याय्यवृत्तेन राघव
कल्पयिष्यति ते प्रीतः साहाय्यं लघुविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tena sakhyaṁ ca kartavyaṁ nyāyyavṛttena rāghava
kalpayiṣyati te prītaḥ sāhāyyaṁ laghuvikramaḥ

translations.english: O Raghava, O fleet-footed hero, do you contract friendship with him gifted with good qualities and he shall assist you.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तस्यास्त्यविज्ञातं त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव
सर्वान्परिसृतो लोकान्पुरा वै कारणान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
na hi tasyāstyavijñātaṁ triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
sarvānparisṛto lokānpurā vai kāraṇāntare

translations.english: There is nothing unknown to him, O Rāghava is the three worlds. Formerly for some reasons he had travelled all over them.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तौ तु तौ वीरौ कबन्धेन नरेश्वरौ
गिरिप्रदरमासाद्य पावकं विससर्जतुः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktau tu tau vīrau kabandhena nareśvarau
giripradaramāsādya pāvakaṁ visasarjatuḥ

translations.english: After Kabandha had spoken thus, the two best of men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa took him to a mountain-cave and placed on fire.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्तु महोल्काभिर्ज्वलिताभिः समन्ततः
चितामादीपयामास सा प्रजज्वाल सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇastu maholkābhirjvalitābhiḥ samantataḥ
citāmādīpayāmāsa sā prajajvāla sarvataḥ

translations.english: Laksmana kindled the funeral pile, which was ablaze on all sides. Thereupon the fire began to burn down slowly the huge and corpulent body of Kabandha like to a lump of clarified butter.

verses.sanskrit:
स विधूय चितामाशु विधूमोऽग्निरिवोत्थितः
अरजे वाससी विभ्रन्मालां दिव्यां महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa vidhūya citāmāśu vidhūmo'gnirivotthitaḥ
araje vāsasī vibhranmālāṁ divyāṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Afterwards the highly powerful demon, shaking the funeral pile, rose up quickly like a smokeless flame of fire, wearing a clean cloth and a celestial garland.

verses.sanskrit:
विमाने भास्वरे तिष्ठन्हंसयुक्ते यशस्करे
प्रभया च महातेजा दिशो दश विराजयन्
verses.transliteration:
vimāne bhāsvare tiṣṭhanhaṁsayukte yaśaskare
prabhayā ca mahātejā diśo daśa virājayan

translations.english: And the graceful demon, wearing an unsullied cloth and having all its limbs crested with diverse ornaments, rose from the pile high up in the welkin with a delighted heart. Thereupon mounting on a famed car, brilliant and drawn by swans* and lighting up all the quarters with the effulgence of his person, that highly powerful one, stationing himself in the heaven, addressed Rāma. By virtue of the pious observances performed by him in his previous existence and for his being burnt by Rāma that celestial car appeared there.

verses.sanskrit:
राम षड्युक्तयो लोके याभिः सर्वं विमृश्यते
परिमृष्टो दशान्तेन दशाभागेन सेव्यते
verses.transliteration:
rāma ṣaḍyuktayo loke yābhiḥ sarvaṁ vimṛśyate
parimṛṣṭo daśāntena daśābhāgena sevyate

translations.english: Do you hear truly, O Rāghava, of the means by which you shall come by Sīta. There are six expedients. O Rāma, by virtue of which kings acquire all objects. He, in whom misfortune has culminated, should seek the company of one such+. The six expedients are as follow—(1) Sandhi, peace. (2) Vigraha war-fare. (3) Yāna, military expedition against an enemy. (4) Asana-halting. (5) Daidhibhava-sowing dissension. (6) Samaşraya seeking protection. This is a moral law referring to the sixth to or expedient, to be resorted by the kings-namely Samasrarya seeking protection.

verses.sanskrit:
दशाभागगतो हीनस्त्वं राम सहलक्ष्मणः
यत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तं त्वया दारप्रधर्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
daśābhāgagato hīnastvaṁ rāma sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
yatkṛte vyasanaṁ prāptaṁ tvayā dārapradharṣaṇam

translations.english: You have, O Rāma along with Laksmana, met with the culmination of misfortune and for which you have been assailed with such a disaster as the ravishment of your spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
तदवश्यं त्वया कार्यः स सुहृत्सुहृदां वर
अकृत्वा न हि ते सिद्धिमहं पश्यामि चिन्तयन्
verses.transliteration:
tadavaśyaṁ tvayā kāryaḥ sa suhṛtsuhṛdāṁ vara
akṛtvā na hi te siddhimahaṁ paśyāmi cintayan

translations.english: O you best of my friends, it behove you, therefore to make friends with such a person. Or else I do not find any means for your success.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयतां राम वक्ष्यामि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः
भ्रात्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन वालिना शक्रसूनुना
verses.transliteration:
śrūyatāṁ rāma vakṣyāmi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
bhrātrā nirastaḥ kruddhena vālinā śakrasūnunā

translations.english: Do you hear, O Rāma, what I relate. There live with four monkeys a heroic, self-controlled monkey by name Sugrīva, on that best of mountains Rşyamūka, situated on the banks of the lake Pampā, being driven by his enraged brother Vāli, the son of Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
वयस्यं तं कुरु क्षिप्रमितो गत्वाद्य राघव
अद्रोहाय समागम्य दीप्यमाने विभावसौ
verses.transliteration:
vayasyaṁ taṁ kuru kṣipramito gatvādya rāghava
adrohāya samāgamya dīpyamāne vibhāvasau

translations.english: Do you proceed soon, O hero, to Sugriva of mighty prowess, and repairing hence even to-day do you contract friendship with him, taking vow in the presence of flaming fire* that you shall not envy each other. This refers to the the oriental custom of performing every sacred rite in the presence of fire as witness. The Hindus regard the fire with sacred reverence and for this in all their social and religious ceremonials fire plays, a very prominent and sacred part.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्तौ ह्यद्य युवां कर्तुं कार्यं तस्य चिकीर्षितम्
कृतार्थो वाकृतार्थो वा कृत्यं तव करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
śaktau hyadya yuvāṁ kartuṁ kāryaṁ tasya cikīrṣitam
kṛtārtho vākṛtārtho vā kṛtyaṁ tava kariṣyati

translations.english: Despise not that kingly monkey Sugrīva, because he is grateful, capable of assuming shapes at will, seeking protection and powerful. You too are able to accomplish his wished-for object.

verses.sanskrit:
न तस्याविदितं लोके किंचिदस्ति हि राघव
यावत्सूर्यः प्रतपति सहस्रांशुररिंदम
verses.transliteration:
na tasyāviditaṁ loke kiṁcidasti hi rāghava
yāvatsūryaḥ pratapati sahasrāṁśurariṁdama

translations.english: There is no place under the sun of many rays, O Rāghava, O slayer of foes, unknown to him.

verses.sanskrit:
स नदीर्विपुलाञ्शैलान्गिरिदुर्गाणि कन्दरान्
अन्विष्य वानरैः सार्धं पत्नीं तेऽधिगमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sa nadīrvipulāñśailāngiridurgāṇi kandarān
anviṣya vānaraiḥ sārdhaṁ patnīṁ te'dhigamiṣyati

translations.english: Exploring, with all his monkeys, the rivers, huge mountains, strongholds and caves, he shall learn about your spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरांश्च महाकायान्प्रेषयिष्यति राघव
दिशो विचेतुं तां सीतां त्वद्वियोगेन शोचतीम्
verses.transliteration:
vānarāṁśca mahākāyānpreṣayiṣyati rāghava
diśo vicetuṁ tāṁ sītāṁ tvadviyogena śocatīm

translations.english: He shall search that exquisitely fine damsel Maithili in Ravana's abode, bewailing on your separation, and to find her out he shall despatch, O Rāghava, many a monkey of huge proportions to various quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
स मेरुशृङ्गाग्रगतामनिन्दितां; प्रविश्य पातालतलेऽपि वाश्रिताम्
प्लवंगमानां प्रवरस्तव प्रियां; निहत्य रक्षांसि पुनः प्रदास्यति
verses.transliteration:
sa meruśṛṅgāgragatāmaninditāṁ; praviśya pātālatale'pi vāśritām
plavaṁgamānāṁ pravarastava priyāṁ; nihatya rakṣāṁsi punaḥ pradāsyati

translations.english: Whether on the summit of the mount Meru or in the region under the earth, that lord of monkeys, shall give you back your blameless spouse, killing all the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
निदर्शयित्वा रामाय सीतायाः प्रतिपादने
वाक्यमन्वर्थमर्थज्ञः कबन्धः पुनरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
nidarśayitvā rāmāya sītāyāḥ pratipādane
vākyamanvarthamarthajñaḥ kabandhaḥ punarabravīt

translations.english: Having pointed out to Rāma the expedient for finding out Sītā the wise Kabandha began with the following significant words.

verses.sanskrit:
अशर्करामविभ्रंशां समतीर्थमशैवलाम्
राम संजातवालूकां कमलोत्पलशोभिताम्
verses.transliteration:
aśarkarāmavibhraṁśāṁ samatīrthamaśaivalām
rāma saṁjātavālūkāṁ kamalotpalaśobhitām

translations.english: O heroes, ranging from forest to forest, from high mountains to hillocks, you shall get at the lake Pampā, void of gravels and acquatic plants and hence there is no danger of falling down to the people, having level watering-places, covered with sands and blooming with red and white lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र हंसाः प्लवाः क्रौञ्चाः कुरराश्चैव राघव
वल्गुस्वरा निकूजन्ति पम्पासलिलगोचराः
verses.transliteration:
tatra haṁsāḥ plavāḥ krauñcāḥ kurarāścaiva rāghava
valgusvarā nikūjanti pampāsalilagocarāḥ

translations.english: There emit forth musical notes, swans, frogs, cranes and ospreys sporting in the lake Pampā. They are not filled with terror in view of human beings, inexperienced as they are in the matter of destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थूलान्गिरिगुहाशय्यान्वराहान्वनचारिणः
अपां लोभादुपावृत्तान्वृषभानिव नर्दतः
रूपान्वितांश्च पम्पायां द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं नरोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
sthūlāngiriguhāśayyānvarāhānvanacāriṇaḥ
apāṁ lobhādupāvṛttānvṛṣabhāniva nardataḥ
rūpānvitāṁśca pampāyāṁ drakṣyasi tvaṁ narottama

translations.english: And you too, O best of men, shall behold those fat monkeys, who had drunk water, roaring like to oxen appearing on the banks of a river to drink water.

verses.sanskrit:
सायाह्ने विचरन्राम विटपी माल्यधारिणः
शीतोदकं च पम्पायां दृष्ट्वा शोकं विहास्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sāyāhne vicaranrāma viṭapī mālyadhāriṇaḥ
śītodakaṁ ca pampāyāṁ dṛṣṭvā śokaṁ vihāsyasi

translations.english: And rambling in the evening, you shall assuage your grief beholding the pleasant water of Pampā and blossoming trees.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां तु धर्मे स्थिता नित्यं सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्
दृष्ट्वा देवोपमं राम स्वर्गलोकं गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ tu dharme sthitā nityaṁ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam
dṛṣṭvā devopamaṁ rāma svargalokaṁ gamiṣyati

translations.english: Even at the present day, O Kakutstha, there live an immortal mendicant woman, by name Savari, who had waited in attendance upon those departed ones. Beholding you, O Rāma, who are adored of all creatures like to the Deity Himself, that mendicant woman, ever engaged in pious observances, shall attain to the abode of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्राम पम्पायास्तीरमाश्रित्य पश्चिमम्
आश्रमस्थानमतुलं गुह्यं काकुत्स्थ पश्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tatastadrāma pampāyāstīramāśritya paścimam
āśramasthānamatulaṁ guhyaṁ kākutstha paśyasi

translations.english: O Rāma, turning to the western bank of Pampa, you shall, O Kakutstha, behold the incomparable and secret asylum of Matanga.

verses.sanskrit:
न तत्राक्रमितुं नागाः शक्नुवन्ति तमाश्रमम्
ऋषेस्तस्य मतङ्गस्य विधानात्तच्च काननम्
verses.transliteration:
na tatrākramituṁ nāgāḥ śaknuvanti tamāśramam
ṛṣestasya mataṅgasya vidhānāttacca kānanam

translations.english: Fearing the divine authority of that great ascetic Matanga, the elephants, though there are many, dare not cross the threshold of his asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्नन्दनसंकाशे देवारण्योपमे वने
नानाविहगसंकीर्णे रंस्यसे राम निर्वृतः
verses.transliteration:
tasminnandanasaṁkāśe devāraṇyopame vane
nānāvihagasaṁkīrṇe raṁsyase rāma nirvṛtaḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, this forest is widely known as Matanga wood. You shall sport, O Rāma, with a delighted heart in that forest resembling the celestial garden-Nandana and filled with various birds.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋष्यमूकस्तु पम्पायाः पुरस्तात्पुष्पितद्रुमः
सुदुःखारोहणो नाम शिशुनागाभिरक्षितः
उदारो ब्रह्मणा चैव पूर्वकाले विनिर्मितः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣyamūkastu pampāyāḥ purastātpuṣpitadrumaḥ
suduḥkhārohaṇo nāma śiśunāgābhirakṣitaḥ
udāro brahmaṇā caiva pūrvakāle vinirmitaḥ

translations.english: There stands in front of Pampă the highly inaccessible mount Rşyamūka, ornamented with many a blossoming tree and guarded on all sides by little serpents. That mount is highly munificent. It was created by Brahmā in the days of yore.

verses.sanskrit:
शयानः पुरुषो राम तस्य शैलस्य मूर्धनि
यत्स्वप्ने लभते वित्तं तत्प्रबुद्धोऽधिगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
śayānaḥ puruṣo rāma tasya śailasya mūrdhani
yatsvapne labhate vittaṁ tatprabuddho'dhigacchati

translations.english: A person, sleeping on the summit of that hill and dreaming of an accession of wealth, really gets at it after the dream is over. A perpetrator of iniquitous deeds and engaged in impious observances ascending that hill, the Rākṣasas seize upon him, asleep, and bruise him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽपि शिशुनागानामाक्रन्दः श्रूयते महान्
क्रीडतां राम पम्पायां मतङ्गारण्यवासिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'pi śiśunāgānāmākrandaḥ śrūyate mahān
krīḍatāṁ rāma pampāyāṁ mataṅgāraṇyavāsinām

translations.english: You shall hear the terrible roar of the young elephants ranging in the asylum of Matanga, situated on the banks of Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
सिक्ता रुधिरधाराभिः संहत्य परमद्विपाः
प्रचरन्ति पृथक्कीर्णा मेघवर्णास्तरस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
siktā rudhiradhārābhiḥ saṁhatya paramadvipāḥ
pracaranti pṛthakkīrṇā meghavarṇāstarasvinaḥ

translations.english: You shall furthermore observe many a quickly moving, infuriated elephant, resembling clouds in hue and with red temporal juice oozing out of their heads, roaming here and there sometimes separately and again in a band. Those mighty elephants, roaming the forest, return to their woody homes, drinking the pleasant, pure and sweet smelling water of Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
राम तस्य तु शैलस्य महती शोभते गुहा
शिलापिधाना काकुत्स्थ दुःखं चास्याः प्रवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
rāma tasya tu śailasya mahatī śobhate guhā
śilāpidhānā kākutstha duḥkhaṁ cāsyāḥ praveśanam

translations.english: There is a huge cave, O Rāma, in that mountain, covered on all sides with rocks and where it is very hard to enter.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या गुहायाः प्राग्द्वारे महाञ्शीतोदको ह्रदः
बहुमूलफलो रम्यो नानानगसमावृतः
verses.transliteration:
tasyā guhāyāḥ prāgdvāre mahāñśītodako hradaḥ
bahumūlaphalo ramyo nānānagasamāvṛtaḥ

translations.english: At the entrance of that cave lies a beautiful, wide lake of cool water, hedged on all sides with trees abounding in fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां वसति सुग्रीवश्चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
कदाचिच्छिखरे तस्य पर्वतस्यावतिष्ठते
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ vasati sugrīvaścaturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
kadācicchikhare tasya parvatasyāvatiṣṭhate

translations.english: There live with other monkeys the virtuoussouled Sugrīva, who sometimes reside on the summit of the hill.

verses.sanskrit:
कबन्धस्त्वनुशास्यैवं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
स्रग्वी भास्करवर्णाभः खे व्यरोचत वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
kabandhastvanuśāsyaivaṁ tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
sragvī bhāskaravarṇābhaḥ khe vyarocata vīryavān

translations.english: Having thus addressed Rāma and Lakşmaņa, Kabandha, highly powerful resembling the sun in effulgence and wearing garlands appeared beautiful on the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु खस्थं महाभागं कबन्धं रामलक्ष्मणौ
प्रस्थितौ त्वं व्रजस्वेति वाक्यमूचतुरन्तिकात्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu khasthaṁ mahābhāgaṁ kabandhaṁ rāmalakṣmaṇau
prasthitau tvaṁ vrajasveti vākyamūcaturantikāt

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, preparing to proceed spoke to that great one stationed in the sky, saying, Do you go'

verses.sanskrit:
गम्यतां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमिति तावब्रवीच्च सः
सुप्रीतौ तावनुज्ञाप्य कबन्धः प्रस्थितस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
gamyatāṁ kāryasiddhyarthamiti tāvabravīcca saḥ
suprītau tāvanujñāpya kabandhaḥ prasthitastadā

translations.english: Whereto Kabandha replied, saying Do you proceed to make good your end and bidding them adieu, who were well pleased, departed.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्कबन्धः प्रतिपद्य रूपं; वृतः श्रिया भास्करतुल्यदेहः
निदर्शयन्राममवेक्ष्य खस्थः; सख्यं कुरुष्वेति तदाभ्युवाच
verses.transliteration:
sa tatkabandhaḥ pratipadya rūpaṁ; vṛtaḥ śriyā bhāskaratulyadehaḥ
nidarśayanrāmamavekṣya khasthaḥ; sakhyaṁ kuruṣveti tadābhyuvāca

translations.english: Regaining his pristine beauty and shining in grace and effulgence that Kabandha, who was on the sky, fixing his looks upon Rāma, and pointing out to him his way, said Do you make friends with (Sugrīva).

verses.sanskrit:
तौ कबन्धेन तं मार्गं पम्पाया दर्शितं वने
आतस्थतुर्दिशं गृह्य प्रतीचीं नृवरात्मजौ
verses.transliteration:
tau kabandhena taṁ mārgaṁ pampāyā darśitaṁ vane
ātasthaturdiśaṁ gṛhya pratīcīṁ nṛvarātmajau

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, sons of a kingly father, passing along the way, pointed out by Kabandha, leading to the lake Pampā, proceeded towards the West.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ शैलेष्वाचितानेकान्क्षौद्रकल्पफलद्रुमान्
वीक्षन्तौ जग्मतुर्द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tau śaileṣvācitānekānkṣaudrakalpaphaladrumān
vīkṣantau jagmaturdraṣṭuṁ sugrīvaṁ rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: They wending their way desirous of seeing Sugrīva, there came within the compass of their vision many trees, grown on the summits of the mountains, blossoming with flowers and abounding in fruits tasting sweet like to honey.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ पुष्करिण्याः पम्पायास्तीरमासाद्य पश्चिमम्
अपश्यतां ततस्तत्र शबर्या रम्यमाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tau puṣkariṇyāḥ pampāyāstīramāsādya paścimam
apaśyatāṁ tatastatra śabaryā ramyamāśramam

translations.english: Passing the night on the summit of a hill those two descendants of Raghu arrived at the western bank of Pampā and espied the pleasant asylum of Savari.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तमाश्रममासाद्य द्रुमैर्बहुभिरावृतम्
सुरम्यमभिवीक्षन्तौ शबरीमभ्युपेयतुः
verses.transliteration:
tau tamāśramamāsādya drumairbahubhirāvṛtam
suramyamabhivīkṣantau śabarīmabhyupeyatuḥ

translations.english: Getting at that charming hermitage covered on all sides with trees and casting their looks around they beheld that female mendicant-Savari.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तु दृष्ट्वा तदा सिद्धा समुत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः
पादौ जग्राह रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
tau tu dṛṣṭvā tadā siddhā samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
pādau jagrāha rāmasya lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ

translations.english: No sooner had that one of perfect asceticism beheld those highly intelligent Rāma and Laks maņa than she rose up with folded hands and touching their feet offered them duly water for washing their feet and mouth. Thereupon Rāma spoke to that female ascetic, engaged in religious services.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्ते नियतः कोप आहारश्च तपोधने
कच्चित्ते नियमाः प्राप्ताः कच्चित्ते मनसः सुखम्
कच्चित्ते गुरुशुश्रूषा सफला चारुभाषिणि
verses.transliteration:
kaccitte niyataḥ kopa āhāraśca tapodhane
kaccitte niyamāḥ prāptāḥ kaccitte manasaḥ sukham
kaccitte guruśuśrūṣā saphalā cārubhāṣiṇi

translations.english: O you of sweet accents, have you got all hindrances to asceticism removed? Is your asceticism growing stronger every day? O you having asceticism for your wealth, have you restricted your anger and fare? Have you observed the commandments and attained to mental felicity? Have your attendance upon your spiritual guide born fruits?

verses.sanskrit:
रामेण तापसी पृष्ठा सा सिद्धा सिद्धसंमता
शशंस शबरी वृद्धा रामाय प्रत्युपस्थिता
verses.transliteration:
rāmeṇa tāpasī pṛṣṭhā sā siddhā siddhasaṁmatā
śaśaṁsa śabarī vṛddhā rāmāya pratyupasthitā

translations.english: Being thus accosted by Rāma that old Savarī, of accomplished asceticism and recognised by the Siddhas, approaching Rāma spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
चित्रकूटं त्वयि प्राप्ते विमानैरतुलप्रभैः
इतस्ते दिवमारूढा यानहं पर्यचारिषम्
verses.transliteration:
citrakūṭaṁ tvayi prāpte vimānairatulaprabhaiḥ
itaste divamārūḍhā yānahaṁ paryacāriṣam

translations.english: On your setting foot on the mount Citrakūta, the ascetics whom I served, ascending celestial cars of incomparable lustre, departed to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
स ते प्रतिग्रहीतव्यः सौमित्रिसहितोऽतिथिः
तं च दृष्ट्वा वराँल्लोकानक्षयांस्त्वं गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sa te pratigrahītavyaḥ saumitrisahito'tithiḥ
taṁ ca dṛṣṭvā varā̐llokānakṣayāṁstvaṁ gamiṣyasi

translations.english: Those great ascetics, cognizant of virtue, said to me, Rāma shall come to your holy asylum. Do you receive with great reverence that guest together with Laksmana. On beholding him, you shall attain to that best land of the celestials whence none return.

verses.sanskrit:
मया तु विविधं वन्यं संचितं पुरुषर्षभ
तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसंभवम्
verses.transliteration:
mayā tu vividhaṁ vanyaṁ saṁcitaṁ puruṣarṣabha
tavārthe puruṣavyāghra pampāyāstīrasaṁbhavam

translations.english: O best of men, I was thus told by those great ascetics, and for you I have collected various wild fruits growing on the banks of Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा शबर्या शबरीमिदम्
राघवः प्राह विज्ञाने तां नित्यमबहिष्कृताम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ sa dharmātmā śabaryā śabarīmidam
rāghavaḥ prāha vijñāne tāṁ nityamabahiṣkṛtām

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Savarī, the virtuoussouled Raghava spoke to her conversant with the knowledge of past and future.

verses.sanskrit:
दनोः सकाशात्तत्त्वेन प्रभावं ते महात्मनः
श्रुतं प्रत्यक्षमिच्छामि संद्रष्टुं यदि मन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
danoḥ sakāśāttattvena prabhāvaṁ te mahātmanaḥ
śrutaṁ pratyakṣamicchāmi saṁdraṣṭuṁ yadi manyase

translations.english: I have heard from Danu, in truth, about your divine authority as well as that of your spiritual guides. If you purpose so I wish to witness it with my own eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा रामवक्त्राद्विनिःसृतम्
शबरी दर्शयामास तावुभौ तद्वनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
etattu vacanaṁ śrutvā rāmavaktrādviniḥsṛtam
śabarī darśayāmāsa tāvubhau tadvanaṁ mahat

translations.english: Hearing those accents dropping from Rāma's lips, Sabarī showing to them the vast forest said.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य मेघघनप्रख्यं मृगपक्षिसमाकुलम्
मतङ्गवनमित्येव विश्रुतं रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
paśya meghaghanaprakhyaṁ mṛgapakṣisamākulam
mataṅgavanamityeva viśrutaṁ raghunandana

translations.english: Do you behold, O Rāghava, this forest, crowded with deer and birds resembling a dense cloud. This forest is known as Matanga's wood.

verses.sanskrit:
इह ते भावितात्मानो गुरवो मे महाद्युते
जुहवांश्चक्रिरे तीर्थं मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रपूजितम्
verses.transliteration:
iha te bhāvitātmāno guravo me mahādyute
juhavāṁścakrire tīrthaṁ mantravanmantrapūjitam

translations.english: Here in this forest the pure-souled preceptors sacrificed to fire their persons consecrated by the Mantras as Mantra itself.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं प्रत्यक्स्थली वेदी यत्र ते मे सुसत्कृताः
पुष्पोपहारं कुर्वन्ति श्रमादुद्वेपिभिः करैः
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ pratyaksthalī vedī yatra te me susatkṛtāḥ
puṣpopahāraṁ kurvanti śramādudvepibhiḥ karaiḥ

translations.english: This is that alter Pratyaksthalī, ascending which my worshipful preceptors used to offer flowers to the deities with hands trembling with toil,

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तपः प्रभावेन पश्याद्यापि रघूत्तम
द्योतयन्ति दिशः सर्वाः श्रिया वेद्योऽतुलप्रभाः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tapaḥ prabhāvena paśyādyāpi raghūttama
dyotayanti diśaḥ sarvāḥ śriyā vedyo'tulaprabhāḥ

translations.english: Behold, O best of Raghus, this alter of incomparable beauty, by virtue of their asceticism, has been still shedding its lustre on all the sides.

verses.sanskrit:
अशक्नुवद्भिस्तैर्गन्तुमुपवासश्रमालसैः
चिन्तितेऽभ्यागतान्पश्य समेतान्सप्त सागरान्
verses.transliteration:
aśaknuvadbhistairgantumupavāsaśramālasaiḥ
cintite'bhyāgatānpaśya sametānsapta sāgarān

translations.english: Behold, again, the seven seas have appeared here in conjunction, at their very thought, worn out with fast and therefore incapable of moving on.

verses.sanskrit:
कृताभिषेकैस्तैर्न्यस्ता वल्कलाः पादपेष्विह
अद्यापि न विशुष्यन्ति प्रदेशे रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
kṛtābhiṣekaistairnyastā valkalāḥ pādapeṣviha
adyāpi na viśuṣyanti pradeśe raghunandana

translations.english: Even those barks, which they used to place on these trees after ablution have not yet been dried up.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्स्नं वनमिदं दृष्टं श्रोतव्यं च श्रुतं त्वया
तदिच्छाम्यभ्यनुज्ञाता त्यक्तुमेतत्कलेवरम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtsnaṁ vanamidaṁ dṛṣṭaṁ śrotavyaṁ ca śrutaṁ tvayā
tadicchāmyabhyanujñātā tyaktumetatkalevaram

translations.english: You have observed this entire forest and heard every thing worth hearing. I purpose now to renounce my body being commanded by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामिच्छाम्यहं गन्तुं समीपं भावितात्मनाम्
मुनीनामाश्रंमो येषामहं च परिचारिणी
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmicchāmyahaṁ gantuṁ samīpaṁ bhāvitātmanām
munīnāmāśraṁmo yeṣāmahaṁ ca paricāriṇī

translations.english: I wish to approach those pure-souled ascetics, whom I used to wait upon, and whom these asylums belong to.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मिष्ठं तु वचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः
अनुजानामि गच्छेति प्रहृष्टवदनोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
dharmiṣṭhaṁ tu vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
anujānāmi gaccheti prahṛṣṭavadano'bravīt

translations.english: Hearing with Lakşmaņa the speech of the pious one, Rāma gained an excess of joy and exclaiming, Wonderful it is!

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र ते सुकृतात्मानो विहरन्ति महर्षयः
तत्पुण्यं शबरीस्थानं जगामात्मसमाधिना
verses.transliteration:
yatra te sukṛtātmāno viharanti maharṣayaḥ
tatpuṇyaṁ śabarīsthānaṁ jagāmātmasamādhinā

translations.english: By virtue of her devout meditation, Savarī repaired to that holy region where dwelt her spiritual preceptors-the pure-hearted ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयित्वा तु धर्मात्मा प्रभावं तं महात्मनाम्
हितकारिणमेकाग्रं लक्ष्मणं राघवोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
cintayitvā tu dharmātmā prabhāvaṁ taṁ mahātmanām
hitakāriṇamekāgraṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ rāghavo'bravīt

translations.english: After Savarī had repaired to heaven by virtue of her divine prowess, Rāma with his brother Lakşmaņa began to ponder over the pious influence of those great ascetics. Thinking within himself about the divine authority of those great ones, the virtuous-souled Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, devoted and ever engaged in his well-being.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टोऽयमाश्रमः सौम्य बह्वाश्चर्यः कृतात्मनाम्
विश्वस्तमृगशार्दूलो नानाविहगसेवितः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭo'yamāśramaḥ saumya bahvāścaryaḥ kṛtātmanām
viśvastamṛgaśārdūlo nānāvihagasevitaḥ

translations.english: Beheld have I, O gentle one, the wondrous asylum of the pure-souled ascetics filled with diverse birds and tigers rambling friendly with antelopes.

verses.sanskrit:
सप्तानां च समुद्राणामेषु तीर्थेषु लक्ष्मण
उपस्पृष्टं च विधिवत्पितरश्चापि तर्पिताः
verses.transliteration:
saptānāṁ ca samudrāṇāmeṣu tīrtheṣu lakṣmaṇa
upaspṛṣṭaṁ ca vidhivatpitaraścāpi tarpitāḥ

translations.english: O Laksmana, we have performed ablutions in the sacred waters of these seven seas and offered oblations to our manes. Our misfortunes have ended and prosperity has appeared and my mind is now filled with ecstasy of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
हृदये हि नरव्याघ्र शुभमाविर्भविष्यति
तदागच्छ गमिष्यावः पम्पां तां प्रियदर्शनाम्
verses.transliteration:
hṛdaye hi naravyāghra śubhamāvirbhaviṣyati
tadāgaccha gamiṣyāvaḥ pampāṁ tāṁ priyadarśanām

translations.english: Me-thinks, O best of men, auspiciousness shall soon appear to us; do you come, therefore, we shall proceed towards the picturesque lake Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यमूको गिरिर्यत्र नातिदूरे प्रकाशते
यस्मिन्वसति धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवोंऽशुमतः सुतः
नित्यं वालिभयात्त्रस्तश्चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyamūko giriryatra nātidūre prakāśate
yasminvasati dharmātmā sugrīvoṁ'śumataḥ sutaḥ
nityaṁ vālibhayāttrastaścaturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ

translations.english: You appear in view, at no distance, the mount Rşyamūka. Here dwells with four monkeys, the virtuous-souled Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
अभित्वरे च तं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्
तदधीनं हि मे सौम्य सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्
verses.transliteration:
abhitvare ca taṁ draṣṭuṁ sugrīvaṁ vānararṣabham
tadadhīnaṁ hi me saumya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam

translations.english: Surya's son, in constant fear of Vāli. I am in a hurry to behold Sugrīva the best of monkeys, for my business—Sītā's quest-is entirely at his hands.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणं तं रामं सौमित्रिरिदमब्रवीत्
गच्छावस्त्वरितं तत्र ममापि त्वरते मनः
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇaṁ taṁ rāmaṁ saumitriridamabravīt
gacchāvastvaritaṁ tatra mamāpi tvarate manaḥ

translations.english: Unto the heroic Rāma, speaking thus Saumitrī said. Let us depart soon, I am in haste too.

verses.sanskrit:
समीक्षमाणः पुष्पाढ्यं सर्वतो विपुलद्रुमम्
कोयष्टिभिश्चार्जुनकैः शतपत्रैश्च कीचकैः
एतैश्चान्यैश्च विविधैर्नादितं तद्वनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
samīkṣamāṇaḥ puṣpāḍhyaṁ sarvato vipuladrumam
koyaṣṭibhiścārjunakaiḥ śatapatraiśca kīcakaiḥ
etaiścānyaiśca vividhairnāditaṁ tadvanaṁ mahat

translations.english: Issuing out of Matanga's asylum, the mighty Rāma, lord of men, repaired with Lakşmaņa to the lake Pampā. Exercised with grief, he arrived at the bank of that best lakes, beholding (as he passed along), various trees and pools, the mighty forest covered on all sides with huge trees and flowers and resounding with the noise of lapwings, peacocks, woodpeckers and various other birds and rattling of the bamboo's.

verses.sanskrit:
सखीभिरिव युक्ताभिर्लताभिरनुवेष्टिताम्
किंनरोरगगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षससेविताम्
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णां शीतवारिनिधिं शुभाम्
verses.transliteration:
sakhībhiriva yuktābhirlatābhiranuveṣṭitām
kiṁnaroragagandharvayakṣarākṣasasevitām
nānādrumalatākīrṇāṁ śītavārinidhiṁ śubhām

translations.english: It was adorned on all sides with Tilakas, Aśokas, Punnāgas, Uddālas and Bakulas. It was lake girt on all sides with picturesque gardens, having its waters undulating beautifully and transparent like to crystal, and covered all around with soft sands. It was filled with fish and tortoise, adorned with trees on its banks, encircled with creepers embracing her like companions and frequented by Gandharvas, Kinnaras, serpents, Yaksas and Raksasas. It was covered with trees and creepers of various kind, of cool water, and enveloped with beauty.

verses.sanskrit:
मालतीकुन्दगुल्मैश्च भण्डीरैर्निचुलैस्तथा
अशोकैः सप्तपर्णैश्च केतकैरतिमुक्तकैः
अन्यैश्च विविधैर्वृक्षैः प्रमदेवोपशोभिताम्
verses.transliteration:
mālatīkundagulmaiśca bhaṇḍīrairniculaistathā
aśokaiḥ saptaparṇaiśca ketakairatimuktakaiḥ
anyaiśca vividhairvṛkṣaiḥ pramadevopaśobhitām

translations.english: There stands on its bank the mount R$ yamūka, abounding in various metals and covered with trees of variegated flowers as mentioned before (by Kabandha).

verses.sanskrit:
हरिरृक्षरजो नाम्नः पुत्रस्तस्य महात्मनः
अध्यास्ते तं महावीर्यः सुग्रीव इति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
harirṛkṣarajo nāmnaḥ putrastasya mahātmanaḥ
adhyāste taṁ mahāvīryaḥ sugrīva iti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: There dwell the famous lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, the heroic son of the great Rkşarajā.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवमभिगच्छ त्वं वानरेन्द्रं नरर्षभ
इत्युवाच पुनर्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvamabhigaccha tvaṁ vānarendraṁ nararṣabha
ityuvāca punarvākyaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ satyavikramam

translations.english: O best of men, do you approach the chief of monkeys. Rāma, having truth for his prowess, again spoke to Laksmana, saying, O Laksmana, how shall I live without Sitā, who have been deprived of my kingdom, who am poorly and have Sītā for my life?

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महद्वर्त्म च दूरसंक्रमं; क्रमेण गत्वा प्रविलोकयन्वनम्
ददर्श पम्पां शुभदर्श कानना;मनेकनानाविधपक्षिसंकुलाम्
verses.transliteration:
tato mahadvartma ca dūrasaṁkramaṁ; krameṇa gatvā pravilokayanvanam
dadarśa pampāṁ śubhadarśa kānanā;manekanānāvidhapakṣisaṁkulām

translations.english: Proceeding slowly, observing the forest, Rāma beheld and entered with Lakşmaņa Pampā, girt on all sides with beautiful woods and filled with a multitude of diverse birds.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां पुष्करिणीं गत्वा पद्मोत्पलझषाकुलाम्
रामः सौमित्रिसहितो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ puṣkariṇīṁ gatvā padmotpalajhaṣākulām
rāmaḥ saumitrisahito vilalāpākulendriyaḥ

translations.english: Repairing with Lakşmaņa to the lake Pampā filled with red and while lotuses and fish Rāma having his senses agitated began to lament.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य दृष्ट्वैव तां हर्षादिन्द्रियाणि चकम्पिरे
स कामवशमापन्नः सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya dṛṣṭvaiva tāṁ harṣādindriyāṇi cakampire
sa kāmavaśamāpannaḥ saumitrimidamabravīt

translations.english: And beholding there that lake, his senses were stirred with delight. Troubled with passion he spoke to Saumitri saying,

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाः काननं शुभदर्शनम्
यत्र राजन्ति शैलाभा द्रुमाः सशिखरा इव
verses.transliteration:
saumitre paśya pampāyāḥ kānanaṁ śubhadarśanam
yatra rājanti śailābhā drumāḥ saśikharā iva

translations.english: Observe again, O son of Sumitra, the picturesque wood-land around the lake, where trees, crowned with large branches resembling the summits of a mountain, appear like so many hills.

verses.sanskrit:
मां तु शोकाभिसंतप्तमाधयः पीडयन्ति वै
भरतस्य च दुःखेन वैदेह्या हरणेन च
verses.transliteration:
māṁ tu śokābhisaṁtaptamādhayaḥ pīḍayanti vai
bharatasya ca duḥkhena vaidehyā haraṇena ca

translations.english: Mental agony arising from Sītā's ravishment and Bharata's grief, have been grinding me who am already stricken with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
अधिकं प्रविभात्येतन्नीलपीतं तु शाद्वलम्
द्रुमाणां विविधैः पुष्पैः परिस्तोमैरिवार्पितम्
verses.transliteration:
adhikaṁ pravibhātyetannīlapītaṁ tu śādvalam
drumāṇāṁ vividhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ paristomairivārpitam

translations.english: This green common, chequered with yellow and blue, appeared of enhanced beauty by the various flowers of the trees as if covered with a blanket of diverse hues.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखानिलोऽयं सौमित्रे कालः प्रचुरमन्मथः
गन्धवान्सुरभिर्मासो जातपुष्पफलद्रुमः
verses.transliteration:
sukhānilo'yaṁ saumitre kālaḥ pracuramanmathaḥ
gandhavānsurabhirmāso jātapuṣpaphaladrumaḥ

translations.english: The tops of the trees rich with flowery bunches are gnarled with creepers of blossoming tips. Now has appeared, O Saumitri, the fragrant spring of pleasant breezes, when greatly prevail the influence of Cupid and the trees are graced with fruits and flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य रूपाणि सौमित्रे वनानां पुष्पशालिनाम्
सृजतां पुष्पवर्षाणि वर्षं तोयमुचामिव
verses.transliteration:
paśya rūpāṇi saumitre vanānāṁ puṣpaśālinām
sṛjatāṁ puṣpavarṣāṇi varṣaṁ toyamucāmiva

translations.english: Behold, O Saumitri, the beauty of the flowery woods, showering flowers like to clouds pouring forth rain.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः
वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति गाम्
verses.transliteration:
prastareṣu ca ramyeṣu vividhāḥ kānanadrumāḥ
vāyuvegapracalitāḥ puṣpairavakiranti gām

translations.english: Various trees growing on rock surfaces, moved by the wind have been scattering flowers on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
मारुतः सुखं संस्पर्शे वाति चन्दनशीतलः
षट्पदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु
verses.transliteration:
mārutaḥ sukhaṁ saṁsparśe vāti candanaśītalaḥ
ṣaṭpadairanukūjadbhirvaneṣu madhugandhiṣu

translations.english: Violently shaken by wind the trees in this nectar-smelling forest are sounding as it were with the hum of bees.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पुष्पवद्भिर्मनोरमैः
संसक्तशिखरा शैला विराजन्ति महाद्रुमैः
verses.transliteration:
giriprastheṣu ramyeṣu puṣpavadbhirmanoramaiḥ
saṁsaktaśikharā śailā virājanti mahādrumaiḥ

translations.english: Hillocks over-topped with picturesque and flowery trees stand beautifully on this mountainous expanse.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पिताग्रांश्च पश्येमान्कर्णिकारान्समन्ततः
हाटकप्रतिसंछन्नान्नरान्पीताम्बरानिव
verses.transliteration:
puṣpitāgrāṁśca paśyemānkarṇikārānsamantataḥ
hāṭakapratisaṁchannānnarānpītāmbarāniva

translations.english: Behold, the Karņikāras covered with flowers appear on all sides like to human beings decorated with golden ornaments and wearing yellow cloths.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं वसन्तः सौमित्रे नानाविहगनादितः
सीतया विप्रहीणस्य शोकसंदीपनो मम
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ vasantaḥ saumitre nānāvihaganāditaḥ
sītayā viprahīṇasya śokasaṁdīpano mama

translations.english: This spring, O Saumitri, sounded by the musical notes of the birds of different spacies has been kindling my grief who am without Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
मां हि शोकसमाक्रान्तं संतापयति मन्मथः
हृष्टः प्रवदमानश्च समाह्वयति कोकिलः
verses.transliteration:
māṁ hi śokasamākrāntaṁ saṁtāpayati manmathaḥ
hṛṣṭaḥ pravadamānaśca samāhvayati kokilaḥ

translations.english: Cupid has been smiting me the more who am stricken with grief, and the cuckoos have been defying me, displaying their mirth, O Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
एष दात्यूहको हृष्टो रम्ये मां वननिर्झरे
प्रणदन्मन्मथाविष्टं शोचयिष्यति लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
eṣa dātyūhako hṛṣṭo ramye māṁ vananirjhare
praṇadanmanmathāviṣṭaṁ śocayiṣyati lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: At the pleasant fountains the delighted Dátyūahas with their warblings have been afflicting me who am possessed by Cupid.

verses.sanskrit:
विमिश्रा विहगाः पुम्भिरात्मव्यूहाभिनन्दिताः
भृङ्गराजप्रमुदिताः सौमित्रे मधुरस्वराः
verses.transliteration:
vimiśrā vihagāḥ pumbhirātmavyūhābhinanditāḥ
bhṛṅgarājapramuditāḥ saumitre madhurasvarāḥ

translations.english: O Saumitri, birds and bees of melodious notes accompanied by their co-mates and delighted with their mutual companionship are on the banks of this lake.

verses.sanskrit:
मां हि सा मृगशावाक्षी चिन्ताशोकबलात्कृतम्
संतापयति सौमित्रे क्रूरश्चैत्रवनानिलः
verses.transliteration:
māṁ hi sā mṛgaśāvākṣī cintāśokabalātkṛtam
saṁtāpayati saumitre krūraścaitravanānilaḥ

translations.english: That one having the eyes of a fawn and ruthless vernal breeze, O Saumitri, have been oppressing me who am overpowered with anxiety and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
शिखिनीभिः परिवृता मयूरा गिरिसानुषु
मन्मथाभिपरीतस्य मम मन्मथवर्धनाः
verses.transliteration:
śikhinībhiḥ parivṛtā mayūrā girisānuṣu
manmathābhiparītasya mama manmathavardhanāḥ

translations.english: These maddened peacocks encircled by the pea-hens, have been aggravating my amorous desire who am already possessed by the Cupid.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्णम नृत्यन्तं मयूरमुपनृत्यति
शिखिनी मन्मथार्तैषा भर्तारं गिरिसानुषु
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣṇama nṛtyantaṁ mayūramupanṛtyati
śikhinī manmathārtaiṣā bhartāraṁ girisānuṣu

translations.english: Observe, O Laksmana, there dance with her dancing mate on the mountainous expanse, the pea-hen, troubled with amorous sentiments.

verses.sanskrit:
मयूरस्य वने नूनं रक्षसा न हृता प्रिया
मम त्वयं विना वासः पुष्पमासे सुदुःसहः
verses.transliteration:
mayūrasya vane nūnaṁ rakṣasā na hṛtā priyā
mama tvayaṁ vinā vāsaḥ puṣpamāse suduḥsahaḥ

translations.english: Surely the Rākşasa has not brought my dear one in this forest of peacocks and therefore they dance with their mates in this picturesque forest land.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण पुष्पाणि निष्फलानि भवन्ति मे
पुष्पभारसमृद्धानां वनानां शिशिरात्यये
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa puṣpāṇi niṣphalāni bhavanti me
puṣpabhārasamṛddhānāṁ vanānāṁ śiśirātyaye

translations.english: Behold, O Laksmana, In this season of spring flowers of this forest rich in their load of flowers are of no avail to me. These pleasant flowers of the trees have been uselessly falling on the earth along with the swarms of black bees.

verses.sanskrit:
वदन्ति रावं मुदिताः शकुनाः संघशः कलम्
आह्वयन्त इवान्योन्यं कामोन्मादकरा मम
verses.transliteration:
vadanti rāvaṁ muditāḥ śakunāḥ saṁghaśaḥ kalam
āhvayanta ivānyonyaṁ kāmonmādakarā mama

translations.english: The birds exciting my desire have been delightedly warbling in flocks as if welcoming each other.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं परवशा सीता सापि शोचत्यहं यथा
श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी मृदुभाषा च मे प्रिया
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ paravaśā sītā sāpi śocatyahaṁ yathā
śyāmā padmapalāśākṣī mṛdubhāṣā ca me priyā

translations.english: Surely shall my dear wife of a slender make, having eyes like lotus-petals and of sweet accents renounce her life at the appearance of this spring?

verses.sanskrit:
एष पुष्पवहो वायुः सुखस्पर्शो हिमावहः
तां विचिन्तयतः कान्तां पावकप्रतिमो मम
verses.transliteration:
eṣa puṣpavaho vāyuḥ sukhasparśo himāvahaḥ
tāṁ vicintayataḥ kāntāṁ pāvakapratimo mama

translations.english: This cool breeze of a pleasant touch, carrying the fragrance of flowers appears like a fire-brand to me who am thinking of my spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
तां विनाथ विहंगोऽसौ पक्षी प्रणदितस्तदा
वायसः पादपगतः प्रहृष्टमभिनर्दति
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ vinātha vihaṁgo'sau pakṣī praṇaditastadā
vāyasaḥ pādapagataḥ prahṛṣṭamabhinardati

translations.english: This bird set up a cry in the sky at that time* and now in the absence of Sītā, that crow, sitting on the tree is crying delightedly. This refers to the time when Rāma was united with Sītā i.e. at the time of his wedding, At that time the bird, flying up in the sky set up an inauspicious cry indicating that in no distant time he should be separated form her; and now his sitting on the tree and cawing delightedly indicated that he should soon be re-united with her.

verses.sanskrit:
एष वै तत्र वैदेह्या विहगः प्रतिहारकः
पक्षी मां तु विशालाक्ष्याः समीपमुपनेष्यति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa vai tatra vaidehyā vihagaḥ pratihārakaḥ
pakṣī māṁ tu viśālākṣyāḥ samīpamupaneṣyati

translations.english: This bird flying up in the sky brought about Sītā's ravishment and this bird shall take me to her having expansive eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण संनादं वने मदविवर्धनम्
पुष्पिताग्रेषु वृक्षेषु द्विजानामुपकूजताम्
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa saṁnādaṁ vane madavivardhanam
puṣpitāgreṣu vṛkṣeṣu dvijānāmupakūjatām

translations.english: Hear, O Laksmana, the maddening notes of those birds sitting on the tops of the flowery trees and setting up their melody.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाश्चित्रासु वनराजिषु
नलिनानि प्रकाशन्ते जले तरुणसूर्यवत्
verses.transliteration:
saumitre paśya pampāyāścitrāsu vanarājiṣu
nalināni prakāśante jale taruṇasūryavat

translations.english: Behold, O Saumitri, O foremost of men, the Kinnaras are ranging at large in this variegated forest land on the banks of Pampā. Behold, O Lakşmaņa, here the fragrant red lotuses are shedding forth their splendour like to the newly risen sun.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्रवाकयुता नित्यं चित्रप्रस्थवनान्तरा
मातङ्गमृगयूथैश्च शोभते सलिलार्थिभिः
verses.transliteration:
cakravākayutā nityaṁ citraprasthavanāntarā
mātaṅgamṛgayūthaiśca śobhate salilārthibhiḥ

translations.english: Here appear beautifully the lake Pampā of transparent water, filled with blue and fragrant lotuses, swans and Kõrandavas and abounding in red lotuses like to the virgin rays of the sun and having their filaments crushed by the bees. And the beautiful woods around the lake have been manifesting their beauty, filled with Cakravākas and the herds of elephants and deer desirous of drinking water.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्मकोशपलाशानि द्रष्टुं दृष्टिर्हि मन्यते
सीताया नेत्रकोशाभ्यां सदृशानीति लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
padmakośapalāśāni draṣṭuṁ dṛṣṭirhi manyate
sītāyā netrakośābhyāṁ sadṛśānīti lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: My eyes pant for beholding those lotus-petals, O Lakṣmaṇa, because of their resemblance with Sītā's eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्मकेसरसंसृष्टो वृक्षान्तरविनिःसृतः
निःश्वास इव सीताया वाति वायुर्मनोहरः
verses.transliteration:
padmakesarasaṁsṛṣṭo vṛkṣāntaraviniḥsṛtaḥ
niḥśvāsa iva sītāyā vāti vāyurmanoharaḥ

translations.english: Issuing out of the trees and touching the filaments, the pleasant wind is blowing like to Sita's breath.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पाया दक्षिणे गिरिसानुनि
पुष्पितां कर्णिकारस्य यष्टिं परमशोभनाम्
verses.transliteration:
saumitre paśya pampāyā dakṣiṇe girisānuni
puṣpitāṁ karṇikārasya yaṣṭiṁ paramaśobhanām

translations.english: Behold O Lakşmaņa, the flowery branches of the Karņikāras on the summits of the mountain situated on the southern bank of Pampā.

verses.sanskrit:
अधिकं शैलराजोऽयं धातुभिस्तु विभूषितः
विचित्रं सृजते रेणुं वायुवेगविघट्टितम्
verses.transliteration:
adhikaṁ śailarājo'yaṁ dhātubhistu vibhūṣitaḥ
vicitraṁ sṛjate reṇuṁ vāyuvegavighaṭṭitam

translations.english: This prince of mountains, beautified with various metals, has been throwing up dusts of diverse colours driven by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिप्रस्थास्तु सौमित्रे सर्वतः संप्रपुष्पितैः
निष्पत्रैः सर्वतो रम्यैः प्रदीपा इव कुंशुकैः
verses.transliteration:
giriprasthāstu saumitre sarvataḥ saṁprapuṣpitaiḥ
niṣpatraiḥ sarvato ramyaiḥ pradīpā iva kuṁśukaiḥ

translations.english: O Saumitri, these mountainous expanses are burning in beauty with blossoming and beautiful Kinsukas void of leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
विविधा विविधैः पुष्पैस्तैरेव नगसानुषु
विकीर्णैः पीतरक्ताभाः सौमित्रे प्रस्तराः कृताः
verses.transliteration:
vividhā vividhaiḥ puṣpaistaireva nagasānuṣu
vikīrṇaiḥ pītaraktābhāḥ saumitre prastarāḥ kṛtāḥ

translations.english: O Saumitri, the mountainous levels variegated with flowers of different species, are appearing like to beds.

verses.sanskrit:
हिमान्ते पश्य सौमित्रे वृक्षाणां पुष्पसंभवम्
पुष्पमासे हि तरवः संघर्षादिव पुष्पिताः
verses.transliteration:
himānte paśya saumitre vṛkṣāṇāṁ puṣpasaṁbhavam
puṣpamāse hi taravaḥ saṁgharṣādiva puṣpitāḥ

translations.english: Behold O Saumitri, the origination of flowers in the trees at the expiry of the winter. The trees as if viewing with each other, have blossomed in this season of flowers. The trees, O Lakşmaņa, with bees humming around and with flowery branches are as if welcoming each other.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य शीतजलां चेमां सौमित्रे पुष्करायुताम्
चक्रवाकानुचरितां कारण्डवनिषेविताम्
प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च संपूर्णां वराहमृगसेविताम्
verses.transliteration:
paśya śītajalāṁ cemāṁ saumitre puṣkarāyutām
cakravākānucaritāṁ kāraṇḍavaniṣevitām
plavaiḥ krauñcaiśca saṁpūrṇāṁ varāhamṛgasevitām

translations.english: O Saumitri, behold this Pampā of cool water, enveloped on all sides with lotuses, and frequented by Cakravākas, Karandavas, Krauñcas, Plavas and high deer.

verses.sanskrit:
दीपयन्तीव मे कामं विविधा मुदिता द्विजाः
श्यामां चन्द्रमुखीं स्मृत्वा प्रियां पद्मनिभेक्षणाम्
verses.transliteration:
dīpayantīva me kāmaṁ vividhā muditā dvijāḥ
śyāmāṁ candramukhīṁ smṛtvā priyāṁ padmanibhekṣaṇām

translations.english: The beauty of Pampā has been further enhanced by the birds carolling. Diverse delighted birds have been exciting my passion, reminding me of my dear spouse, of blameless countenance, having a moon like face and eyes resembling lotus-petals.

verses.sanskrit:
पय सानुषु चित्रेषु मृगीभिः सहितान्मृगान्
मां पुनर्मृगशावाक्ष्या वैदेह्या विरहीकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
paya sānuṣu citreṣu mṛgībhiḥ sahitānmṛgān
māṁ punarmṛgaśāvākṣyā vaidehyā virahīkṛtam
