translations.english: Behold on the yonder mountainous expanse of various colours, stags sporting with hinds and myself on the other hand forsaken by Vaidehi having eyes resembling those of an antelope.

verses.sanskrit:
निरीक्षमाणः सहसा महात्मा; सर्वं वनं निर्झरकन्दरं च
उद्विग्नचेताः सह लक्ष्मणेन; विचार्य दुःखोपहतः प्रतस्थे
verses.transliteration:
nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā mahātmā; sarvaṁ vanaṁ nirjharakandaraṁ ca
udvignacetāḥ saha lakṣmaṇena; vicārya duḥkhopahataḥ pratasthe

translations.english: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, stricken with grief passed along beholding the forestland, fountains, caves and revolving aside (the 'pregnant words of Laksmana).

verses.sanskrit:
तावृष्यमूकं सहितौ प्रयातौ; सुग्रीवशाखामृगसेवितं तम्
त्रस्तास्तु दृष्ट्वा हरयो बभूवु;र्महौजसौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ तौ
verses.transliteration:
tāvṛṣyamūkaṁ sahitau prayātau; sugrīvaśākhāmṛgasevitaṁ tam
trastāstu dṛṣṭvā harayo babhūvu;rmahaujasau rāghavalakṣmaṇau tau

translations.english: Espying the highly powerful Rāma and Lakş mana there, monkeys, terrified, entered into that holy and pleasant asylum, a worthy refuge and having its inside always frequented by them.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महात्मानौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
वरायुधधरौ वीरौ सुग्रीवः शङ्कितोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahātmānau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
varāyudhadharau vīrau sugrīvaḥ śaṅkito'bhavat

translations.english: Beholding those two high-souled brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa, heroic and with great scimitars in their hands, Sugrīva became terrified.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्विग्नहृदयः सर्वा दिशः समवलोकयन्
न व्यतिष्ठत कस्मिंश्चिद्देशे वानरपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
udvignahṛdayaḥ sarvā diśaḥ samavalokayan
na vyatiṣṭhata kasmiṁściddeśe vānarapuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: That best of monkeys, of a disturbed mind, cast his looks around and could not stand (patiently) at any place.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव चक्रे मनः स्थाने वीक्षमाणो महाबलौ
कपेः परमभीतस्य चित्तं व्यवससाद ह
verses.transliteration:
naiva cakre manaḥ sthāne vīkṣamāṇo mahābalau
kapeḥ paramabhītasya cittaṁ vyavasasāda ha

translations.english: Beholding those two of great prowess he could not make up his mind to remain there and the heart of that terrified monkey, sank.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयित्वा स धर्मात्मा विमृश्य गुरुलाघवम्
सुग्रीवः परमोद्विग्नः सर्वैरनुचरैः सह
verses.transliteration:
cintayitvā sa dharmātmā vimṛśya gurulāghavam
sugrīvaḥ paramodvignaḥ sarvairanucaraiḥ saha

translations.english: Pondering over what is more and what is less important the virtuous-souled Sugrīva became highly anxious along with that monkey-herd.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स सचिवेभ्यस्तु सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः
शशंस परमोद्विग्नः पश्यंस्तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa sacivebhyastu sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ
śaśaṁsa paramodvignaḥ paśyaṁstau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Beholding Rāma and Laksmana, Sugriva, the king of monkeys, greatly exercised with anxiety spoke to his counsellors, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
एतौ वनमिदं दुर्गं वालिप्रणिहितौ ध्रुवम्
छद्मना चीरवसनौ प्रचरन्ताविहागतौ
verses.transliteration:
etau vanamidaṁ durgaṁ vālipraṇihitau dhruvam
chadmanā cīravasanau pracarantāvihāgatau

translations.english: Forsooth, these two heroes, in false guises and wearing bark, despatched by Vāli, have come here traversing the forest stronghold.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुग्रीवसचिवा दृष्ट्वा परमधन्विनौ
जग्मुर्गिरितटात्तस्मादन्यच्छिखरमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sugrīvasacivā dṛṣṭvā paramadhanvinau
jagmurgiritaṭāttasmādanyacchikharamuttamam

translations.english: Beholding these two mighty archers the counsellors of Sugriva, quitting that mountainous expanse proceeded to another best of hills.

verses.sanskrit:
ते क्षिप्रमभिगम्याथ यूथपा यूथपर्षभम्
हरयो वानरश्रेष्ठं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
te kṣipramabhigamyātha yūthapā yūthaparṣabham
harayo vānaraśreṣṭhaṁ parivāryopatasthire

translations.english: Thereupon proceeding quickly the commanders of various monkey herds stood encircling the king of monkeys and the chief of · leaders.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शाखामृगाः सर्वे प्लवमाना महाबलाः
बभञ्जुश्च नगांस्तत्र पुष्पितान्दुर्गसंश्रितान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śākhāmṛgāḥ sarve plavamānā mahābalāḥ
babhañjuśca nagāṁstatra puṣpitāndurgasaṁśritān

translations.english: The monkeys thus sharing in the misery and happiness (of their chief) proceeded jumping from hill to hill shaking the summits thereof, with the velocity (of their persons). Thereupon those mighty monkeys, jumping, broke down the flowery trees of that stronghold.

verses.sanskrit:
आप्लवन्तो हरिवराः सर्वतस्तं महागिरिम्
मृगमार्जारशार्दूलांस्त्रासयन्तो ययुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
āplavanto harivarāḥ sarvatastaṁ mahāgirim
mṛgamārjāraśārdūlāṁstrāsayanto yayustadā

translations.english: Those best of monkeys, springing all around that mighty hill, proceeded terrifying the deer, the wild cats and the tigers.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुग्रीवसचिवाः पर्वतेन्द्रं समाश्रिताः
संगम्य कपिमुख्येन सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः स्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sugrīvasacivāḥ parvatendraṁ samāśritāḥ
saṁgamya kapimukhyena sarve prāñjalayaḥ sthitāḥ

translations.english: Stationed on that best of mountains the ministers of Sugrīva, coming in the front of that monkey-chief, stood with clasped palms.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं भयसंत्रस्तं वालिकिल्बिषशङ्कितम्
उवाच हनुमान्वाक्यं सुग्रीवं वाक्यकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ bhayasaṁtrastaṁ vālikilbiṣaśaṅkitam
uvāca hanumānvākyaṁ sugrīvaṁ vākyakovidaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Hanumān, skilled in speech, spoke to Sugrīva, terrified and afraid of Vāli's wicked wiles.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मादुद्विग्नचेतास्त्वं प्रद्रुतो हरिपुंगव
तं क्रूरदर्शनं क्रूरं नेह पश्यामि वालिनम्
verses.transliteration:
yasmādudvignacetāstvaṁ pradruto haripuṁgava
taṁ krūradarśanaṁ krūraṁ neha paśyāmi vālinam

translations.english: I do not behold, O best of monkeys, that wicked Vāli of terrible looks, afraid of whom you had fled away and for whom you are anxious.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्तव भयं सौम्य पूर्वजात्पापकर्मणः
स नेह वाली दुष्टात्मा न ते पश्याम्यहं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
yasmāttava bhayaṁ saumya pūrvajātpāpakarmaṇaḥ
sa neha vālī duṣṭātmā na te paśyāmyahaṁ bhayam

translations.english: I do not observe here, O gentle one, the wicked-souled Väli your elder brother of impious actions and whom you do fear and I do not perceive any terror proceeding from him.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवंगम
लघुचित्ततयात्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ
verses.transliteration:
aho śākhāmṛgatvaṁ te vyaktameva plavaṁgama
laghucittatayātmānaṁ na sthāpayasi yo matau

translations.english: O monkey-chief, truly manifest is your monkey-hood and it is through your lightheartedness that you are incapable of fixing your soul.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिविज्ञानसंपन्न इङ्गितैः सर्वमाचर
न ह्यबुद्धिं गतो राजा सर्वभूतानि शास्ति हि
verses.transliteration:
buddhivijñānasaṁpanna iṅgitaiḥ sarvamācara
na hyabuddhiṁ gato rājā sarvabhūtāni śāsti hi

translations.english: Gifted with intellect and knowledge do you perforin all by means of gestures. A king void of sense cannot govern all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्तु शुभं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सर्वं हनूमतः
ततः शुभतरं वाक्यं हनूमन्तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvastu śubhaṁ vākyaṁ śrutvā sarvaṁ hanūmataḥ
tataḥ śubhataraṁ vākyaṁ hanūmantamuvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing those pregnant words of Hanumār in its entirety, Sugrīva addressed to Hanumān in better accents.

verses.sanskrit:
दीर्घबाहू विशालाक्षौ शरचापासिधारिणौ
कस्य न स्याद्भयं दृष्ट्वा एतौ सुरसुतोपमौ
verses.transliteration:
dīrghabāhū viśālākṣau śaracāpāsidhāriṇau
kasya na syādbhayaṁ dṛṣṭvā etau surasutopamau

translations.english: Who is not terrified beholding those two mighty armed heroes, having expansive eyes, with bows, arrow, and daggers in their hands like to two sons of a celestial?

verses.sanskrit:
वालिप्रणिहितावेतौ शङ्केऽहं पुरुषोत्तमौ
राजानो बहुमित्राश्च विश्वासो नात्र हि क्षमः
verses.transliteration:
vālipraṇihitāvetau śaṅke'haṁ puruṣottamau
rājāno bahumitrāśca viśvāso nātra hi kṣamaḥ

translations.english: Methinks these two best of men have been despatched by Vali. Kings have many friends. And it is not proper for me to place confidence in them.

verses.sanskrit:
अरयश्च मनुष्येण विज्ञेयाश्छन्नचारिणः
विश्वस्तानामविश्वस्ताश्छिद्रेषु प्रहरन्ति हि
verses.transliteration:
arayaśca manuṣyeṇa vijñeyāśchannacāriṇaḥ
viśvastānāmaviśvastāśchidreṣu praharanti hi

translations.english: People should know that enemies, always treacherous by nature, range under false guises. And those foes, availing of their credulity, bring about their destruction whenever opportunity presents itself.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्येषु वाली मेधावी राजानो बहुदर्शनाः
भवन्ति परहन्तारस्ते ज्ञेयाः प्राकृतैर्नरैः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtyeṣu vālī medhāvī rājāno bahudarśanāḥ
bhavanti parahantāraste jñeyāḥ prākṛtairnaraiḥ

translations.english: Vāli is eminently expert in despatching business. Monarchs, cognizant of many a wily expedient, bring about others' destruction. It is proper to discern them by means of disguised spies.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ त्वया प्राकृतेनैव गत्वा ज्ञेयौ प्लवंगम
शङ्कितानां प्रकारैश्च रूपव्याभाषणेन च
verses.transliteration:
tau tvayā prākṛtenaiva gatvā jñeyau plavaṁgama
śaṅkitānāṁ prakāraiśca rūpavyābhāṣaṇena ca

translations.english: O monkey, do you proceed under a false guise and come by their intentions, examining them aright by their countenances, gestures and words.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्षयस्व तयोर्भावं प्रहृष्टमनसौ यदि
विश्वासयन्प्रशंसाभिरिङ्गितैश्च पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣayasva tayorbhāvaṁ prahṛṣṭamanasau yadi
viśvāsayanpraśaṁsābhiriṅgitaiśca punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Do you ascertain their intention. If do you find them delighted, secure their confidence in my favour by eulogising me again and again and giving out to them my views.

verses.sanskrit:
ममैवाभिमुखं स्थित्वा पृच्छ त्वं हरिपुंगव
प्रयोजनं प्रवेशस्य वनस्यास्य धनुर्धरौ
verses.transliteration:
mamaivābhimukhaṁ sthitvā pṛccha tvaṁ haripuṁgava
prayojanaṁ praveśasya vanasyāsya dhanurdharau

translations.english: O best of monkeys, do you ask them why they have entered this forest, if you do perceive that these two archers are pure souled.

verses.sanskrit:
शुद्धात्मानौ यदि त्वेतौ जानीहि त्वं प्लवंगम
व्याभाषितैर्वा रूपैर्वा विज्ञेया दुष्टतानयोः
verses.transliteration:
śuddhātmānau yadi tvetau jānīhi tvaṁ plavaṁgama
vyābhāṣitairvā rūpairvā vijñeyā duṣṭatānayoḥ

translations.english: O monkey, if you determine the fairness and unfairness of their purpose, their wickedness should be discovered by means of their gestures and conversation.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं कपिराजेन संदिष्टो मारुतात्मजः
चकार गमने बुद्धिं यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ kapirājena saṁdiṣṭo mārutātmajaḥ
cakāra gamane buddhiṁ yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Being commanded by that chief of monkeys, the son of Maruta purposed to approach Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेति संपूज्य वचस्तु तस्य; कपेः सुभीतस्य दुरासदस्य
महानुभावो हनुमान्ययौ तदा; स यत्र रामोऽतिबलश्च लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
tatheti saṁpūjya vacastu tasya; kapeḥ subhītasya durāsadasya
mahānubhāvo hanumānyayau tadā; sa yatra rāmo'tibalaśca lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Assenting to the words of the terrified and unconquerable Sugriva and saying 'Be it so, Hanumān, the high-souled monkey proceeded where the heroic Râma was with Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
वचो विज्ञाय हनुमान्सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
पर्वतादृश्यमूकात्तु पुप्लुवे यत्र राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
vaco vijñāya hanumānsugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
parvatādṛśyamūkāttu pupluve yatra rāghavau

translations.english: Understanding the words of the high-souled Sugrīva, Hanumān, proceeded, springing, from the mount Rsyamūka, towards the descendants of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणौ वीरौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ
अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरौ देवलोकादिवागतौ
verses.transliteration:
padmapatrekṣaṇau vīrau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau
anyonyasadṛśau vīrau devalokādivāgatau

translations.english: Having eyes resembling lotus-petals, heroic, wearing matted locks, resembling each other, have you come here from the celestial region?

verses.sanskrit:
सिंहस्कन्धौ महासत्त्वौ समदाविव गोवृषौ
आयताश्च सुवृत्ताश्च बाहवः परिघोत्तमाः
सर्वभूषणभूषार्हाः किमर्थं न विभूषितः
verses.transliteration:
siṁhaskandhau mahāsattvau samadāviva govṛṣau
āyatāśca suvṛttāśca bāhavaḥ parighottamāḥ
sarvabhūṣaṇabhūṣārhāḥ kimarthaṁ na vibhūṣitaḥ

translations.english: Of a spacious breast, heroic, you two men possess the exterior of gods. It appears as the Sun and the Moon have come down to the earth of their own accord. Having leonine shoulders, gifted with high energy, stout like to plump bulls and human albeit looking like celestials, why are not your long, round arms, resembling Parighas and deserving all ornaments adorned? Methinks you two are perfectly able to protect this entire earth, filled with forests and oceans, and intersected by the mountains Vindhya and Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे च धनुषी चित्रे श्लक्ष्णे चित्रानुलेपने
प्रकाशेते यथेन्द्रस्य वज्रे हेमविभूषिते
verses.transliteration:
ime ca dhanuṣī citre ślakṣṇe citrānulepane
prakāśete yathendrasya vajre hemavibhūṣite

translations.english: These your painted and smooth bows appear like to the thunder-bolts of Indra adorned with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
संपूर्णा निशितैर्बाणैर्तूणाश्च शुभदर्शनाः
जीवितान्तकरैर्घोरैर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पन्नगैः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpūrṇā niśitairbāṇairtūṇāśca śubhadarśanāḥ
jīvitāntakarairghorairjvaladbhiriva pannagaiḥ

translations.english: And these beautiful quivers are filled to the brim with sharpened and deadly shafts like to flaming fire and serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
महाप्रमाणौ विपुलौ तप्तहाटकभूषितौ
खड्गावेतौ विराजेते निर्मुक्तभुजगाविव
verses.transliteration:
mahāpramāṇau vipulau taptahāṭakabhūṣitau
khaḍgāvetau virājete nirmuktabhujagāviva

translations.english: And these two daggers, of mighty proportions, furnished with burning gold, appear like to serpents, let loose.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवो नाम धर्मात्मा कश्चिद्वानरयूथपः
वीरो विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा जगद्भ्रमति दुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvo nāma dharmātmā kaścidvānarayūthapaḥ
vīro vinikṛto bhrātrā jagadbhramati duḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Why do you not answer me accosting you thus? A certain heroic and virtuous monkeychief, by name Sugrīva, has been journeying on this carth, distressed at heart, being driven away by his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
राज्ञा वानरमुख्यानां हनुमान्नाम वानरः
verses.transliteration:
prāpto'haṁ preṣitastena sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
rājñā vānaramukhyānāṁ hanumānnāma vānaraḥ

translations.english: I have come here being despatched by that high-souled Sugriva-my name is Hanuman, the foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
भिक्षुरूपप्रतिच्छन्नं सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया
ऋश्यमूकादिह प्राप्तं कामगं कामरूपिणम्
verses.transliteration:
bhikṣurūpapraticchannaṁ sugrīvapriyakāmyayā
ṛśyamūkādiha prāptaṁ kāmagaṁ kāmarūpiṇam

translations.english: That virtuous souled Sugrīva desires to make friends with you. And know me to be his counsellor-a monkey, the son of Pavana, ranging every where at my will, coming here, under the guise of a mendicant, from the mount Rsymuka, for the welfare of Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमांस्तौ वीरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
वाक्यज्ञौ वाक्यकुशलः पुनर्नोवाच किंचन
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu hanumāṁstau vīrau rāmalakṣmaṇau
vākyajñau vākyakuśalaḥ punarnovāca kiṁcana

translations.english: Having addressed thus those two heroes-Rama and Laksmana, Hanuman, conversant with words and skilled in speech, did not speak again.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
प्रहृष्टवदनः श्रीमान्भ्रातरं पार्श्वतः स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā vacastasya rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrīmānbhrātaraṁ pārśvataḥ sthitam

translations.english: Hearing those words, the effulgent Rāma, with a delighted countenance, spoke to his younger brother, Laksmana-~-sitting by him.

verses.sanskrit:
सचिवोऽयं कपीन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
तमेव काङ्क्षमाणस्य ममान्तिकमुपागतः
verses.transliteration:
sacivo'yaṁ kapīndrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
tameva kāṅkṣamāṇasya mamāntikamupāgataḥ

translations.english: He is the counsellor of the high-souled Sugriva, the lord of monkeys and has approached me, soliciting my friendship in his (Sugriva's) favour.

verses.sanskrit:
तमभ्यभाष सौमित्रे सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्
वाक्यज्ञं मधुरैर्वाक्यैः स्नेहयुक्तमरिंदमम्
verses.transliteration:
tamabhyabhāṣa saumitre sugrīvasacivaṁ kapim
vākyajñaṁ madhurairvākyaiḥ snehayuktamariṁdamam

translations.english: Do you welcome, with pleasant words, O Saumitri, this monkey-Sugrīva's minister, the subduer of foes, affectionate and skilled in speech.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टो हनुमान्कृत्यवानिति तद्वचः
श्रुत्वा मधुरसंभाषं सुग्रीवं मनसा गतः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭo hanumānkṛtyavāniti tadvacaḥ
śrutvā madhurasaṁbhāṣaṁ sugrīvaṁ manasā gataḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words (of Rāma) and learning his amicable feeling (in relation to Sugrīva) as also, seeing that Rāma was willing to assist Sugrīva, Hanuman, getting exceedingly delighted, remembered Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
भव्यो राज्यागमस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
यदयं कृत्यवान्प्राप्तः कृत्यं चैतदुपागतम्
verses.transliteration:
bhavyo rājyāgamastasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
yadayaṁ kṛtyavānprāptaḥ kṛtyaṁ caitadupāgatam

translations.english: Since this one of successful acts has been come by and also this business is in hand, the high-souled Sugrīva will most probably obtain the monarchy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परमसंहृष्टो हनूमान्प्लवगर्षभः
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं रामं वाक्यविशारदः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paramasaṁhṛṣṭo hanūmānplavagarṣabhaḥ
pratyuvāca tato vākyaṁ rāmaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ

translations.english: Then transported with joy, that foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, in these words, replied to Rāma, deft in speech, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
किमर्थं त्वं वनं घोरं पम्पाकाननमण्डितम्
आगतः सानुजो दुर्गं नानाव्यालमृगायुतम्
verses.transliteration:
kimarthaṁ tvaṁ vanaṁ ghoraṁ pampākānanamaṇḍitam
āgataḥ sānujo durgaṁ nānāvyālamṛgāyutam

translations.english: Why is it, thất accompanied with your younger brother, have you come to this dense and trackless forest, garnished with the woodlands of Pampā, and filled with various kinds of ferocious beasts?

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो रामचोदितः
आचचक्षे महात्मानं रामं दशरथात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā lakṣmaṇo rāmacoditaḥ
ācacakṣe mahātmānaṁ rāmaṁ daśarathātmajam

translations.english: Hearing those words of his, Laksmana, directed by Råma, informed (Hanumān) of all about Rama, the son of Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा दशरथो नाम द्युतिमान्धर्मवत्सलः
तस्यायं पूर्वजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
rājā daśaratho nāma dyutimāndharmavatsalaḥ
tasyāyaṁ pūrvajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ

translations.english: And he celebrated Agniştoma and other sacrifices with presents (to Brāhmaṇas). This one is his eldest son, named Rama, famous among men.

verses.sanskrit:
शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां पितुर्निर्देशपारगः
वीरो दशरथस्यायं पुत्राणां गुणवत्तरः
verses.transliteration:
śaraṇyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ piturnirdeśapāragaḥ
vīro daśarathasyāyaṁ putrāṇāṁ guṇavattaraḥ

translations.english: He is the refuge of all creatures, and competent to carry out the injunctions of his father. The eldest son of Dasaratha, he is foremost of all his sons in merit.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्याद्भ्रष्टो वने वस्तुं मया सार्धमिहागतः
भार्यया च महातेजाः सीतयानुगतो वशी
दिनक्षये महातेजाः प्रभयेव दिवाकरः
verses.transliteration:
rājyādbhraṣṭo vane vastuṁ mayā sārdhamihāgataḥ
bhāryayā ca mahātejāḥ sītayānugato vaśī
dinakṣaye mahātejāḥ prabhayeva divākaraḥ

translations.english: And, O highly exalted one, this one of subdued senses is followed by his wife Sītā even as the decline of day the exceedingly effulgent Sun is followed by (his spouse) Splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमस्यावरो भ्राता गुणैर्दास्यमुपागतः
कृतज्ञस्य बहुज्ञस्य लक्ष्मणो नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
ahamasyāvaro bhrātā guṇairdāsyamupāgataḥ
kṛtajñasya bahujñasya lakṣmaṇo nāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: I am the younger brother of this one endued with gratitude and of various lore. Subdued by his virtues, I, Laksimana by name, have dedicated myself to his service.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षसापहृता भार्या रहिते कामरूपिणा
तच्च न ज्ञायते रक्षः पत्नी येनास्य सा हृता
verses.transliteration:
rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā rahite kāmarūpiṇā
tacca na jñāyate rakṣaḥ patnī yenāsya sā hṛtā

translations.english: Worthy of happiness, homage, and intent upon the welfare of all beings, deprived of wealth and living in the forest, he has his wife carried off by a Rākşasa, wearing shapes at will. Nor have we yet (been able) to ascertain who is that Rākşasa that has carried off his wife.

verses.sanskrit:
स ज्ञास्यति महावीर्यस्तव भार्यापहारिणम्
एवमुक्त्वा दनुः स्वर्गं भ्राजमानो गतः सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
sa jñāsyati mahāvīryastava bhāryāpahāriṇam
evamuktvā danuḥ svargaṁ bhrājamāno gataḥ sukham

translations.english: A son of Diti named Danu, had, by virtue of an imprecation, undergone Raksasa-hood. He it is who had related to us all about the capable Sugrīva.—That exceedingly puissant one shall have a knowledge of the ravisher of your wife? Having said this, Danu beaming (with a halo) went to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः
अहं चैव हि रामश्च सुग्रीवं शरणं गतौ
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ
ahaṁ caiva hi rāmaśca sugrīvaṁ śaraṇaṁ gatau

translations.english: Thus have 1 related to you all as it fell out. Both Rāma and myself have saught the shelter of Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
एष दत्त्वा च वित्तानि प्राप्य चानुत्तमं यशः
लोकनाथः पुरा भूत्वा सुग्रीवं नाथमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa dattvā ca vittāni prāpya cānuttamaṁ yaśaḥ
lokanāthaḥ purā bhūtvā sugrīvaṁ nāthamicchati

translations.english: Having given away profuse wealth and attained high fame, this one who formerly was the lord of the worlds, now wishes to make Sugrīva his master.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकाभिभूते रामे तु शोकार्ते शरणं गते
कर्तुमर्हति सुग्रीवः प्रसादं सह यूथपैः
verses.transliteration:
śokābhibhūte rāme tu śokārte śaraṇaṁ gate
kartumarhati sugrīvaḥ prasādaṁ saha yūthapaiḥ

translations.english: On Rāma being overwhelmed with sorrow, tried by grief, and having come under his refuge,' it behoveth Sugrīva along with the leaders of bands to show favour to Rāma?

verses.sanskrit:
ईदृशा बुद्धिसंपन्ना जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः
द्रष्टव्या वानरेन्द्रेण दिष्ट्या दर्शनमागताः
verses.transliteration:
īdṛśā buddhisaṁpannā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ
draṣṭavyā vānarendreṇa diṣṭyā darśanamāgatāḥ

translations.english: When Sumitrā's son shedding tears had spoken thus, that one skilled in speech, Hanumān, answered in these words, 'Persons of such a stamp, endued with understanding, of controlled anger and subdued senses, should be seen by the master of monkeys, and such come within one's ken through blessed luck.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि राज्याच्च विभ्रष्टः कृतवैरश्च वालिना
हृतदारो वने त्रस्तो भ्रात्रा विनिकृतो भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
sa hi rājyācca vibhraṣṭaḥ kṛtavairaśca vālinā
hṛtadāro vane trasto bhrātrā vinikṛto bhṛśam

translations.english: He also has been driven out of his kingdom, and has incurred the hostility of Vali. And his wife torn away from him, he dwelleth in this wood, in fear, having been exceedingly harassed by his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
करिष्यति स साहाय्यं युवयोर्भास्करात्मजः
सुग्रीवः सह चास्माभिः सीतायाः परिमार्गणे
verses.transliteration:
kariṣyati sa sāhāyyaṁ yuvayorbhāskarātmajaḥ
sugrīvaḥ saha cāsmābhiḥ sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe

translations.english: That son of the Sun, Sugriva, along with us, will help you in seeking out Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा हनुमाञ्श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा
बभाषे सोऽभिगच्छामः सुग्रीवमिति राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā hanumāñślakṣṇaṁ madhurayā girā
babhāṣe so'bhigacchāmaḥ sugrīvamiti rāghavam

translations.english: Having said these sweet and hurried words, Hanuman said to Rāghava, 'I will (now) repair to Sugriva.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं धर्मात्मा हनूमन्तं स लक्ष्मणः
प्रतिपूज्य यथान्यायमिदं प्रोवाच राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ dharmātmā hanūmantaṁ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
pratipūjya yathānyāyamidaṁ provāca rāghavam

translations.english: When Hanumān had said this, the righteous Lakşmaņa duly paying homage to the former, addressed Rāghava, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
कपिः कथयते हृष्टो यथायं मारुतात्मजः
कृत्यवान्सोऽपि संप्राप्तः कृतकृत्योऽसि राघव
verses.transliteration:
kapiḥ kathayate hṛṣṭo yathāyaṁ mārutātmajaḥ
kṛtyavānso'pi saṁprāptaḥ kṛtakṛtyo'si rāghava

translations.english: From the glad way in which this son of the god of the wind is speaking, it appears that he also seeks your service; and, arriving (at this region) you also, Rāghava, have reaped success.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसन्नमुखवर्णश्च व्यक्तं हृष्टश्च भाषते
नानृतं वक्ष्यते वीरो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
prasannamukhavarṇaśca vyaktaṁ hṛṣṭaśca bhāṣate
nānṛtaṁ vakṣyate vīro hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: He speaketh openly with a delightful light in his countenance; and cheerfulness. (It seems) that the heroic Hanuman, son to the God of wind does not speak anything that is false.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स तु महाप्राज्ञो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
जगामादाय तौ वीरौ हरिराजाय राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa tu mahāprājño hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
jagāmādāya tau vīrau harirājāya rāghavau

translations.english: Then that vastly wise one Hanumān the son of the wind god departed, taking with him the heroic descendants of Raghu, for (presenting them) to the monarch of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु विपुल यशाः कपिप्रवीरः; पवनसुतः कृतकृत्यवत्प्रहृष्टः
गिरिवरमुरुविक्रमः प्रयातः; स शुभमतिः सह रामलक्ष्मणाभ्याम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vipula yaśāḥ kapipravīraḥ; pavanasutaḥ kṛtakṛtyavatprahṛṣṭaḥ
girivaramuruvikramaḥ prayātaḥ; sa śubhamatiḥ saha rāmalakṣmaṇābhyām

translations.english: Then the heroic monkey, the son of the windgod, of wide fame, and great prowess, with his mind perfectly pure, considering himself as crowned with success, and experiencing exceeding delight, arrived at that best of mountains in company with Rāma and Laks mana.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यमूकात्तु हनुमान्गत्वा तं मलयं गिरम्
आचचक्षे तदा वीरौ कपिराजाय राघवौ
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyamūkāttu hanumāngatvā taṁ malayaṁ giram
ācacakṣe tadā vīrau kapirājāya rāghavau

translations.english: Having departed from Rşyamuka, and arrived at the Malaya hill, Hanumān informed the king of monkeys of (the arrival of) the descendants of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं रामो महाप्राज्ञः संप्राप्तो दृढविक्रमः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा रामोऽयं सत्यविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ rāmo mahāprājñaḥ saṁprāpto dṛḍhavikramaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmo'yaṁ satyavikramaḥ

translations.english: O exceedingly wise one, this one that has come here is Rāma having truth for his prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो रामो दशरथात्मजः
धर्मे निगदितश्चैव पितुर्निर्देशपालकः
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ kule jāto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
dharme nigaditaścaiva piturnirdeśapālakaḥ

translations.english: This is Rāma having truth for his prowess, in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa. Rāma the son of Dasaratha, is born in the race of the Ikş wākus. Ever doing the will of his sire, he has been sent hither, in order that his father's verity may stand in tact.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्य वसतोऽरण्ये नियतस्य महात्मनः
रक्षसापहृता भार्या स त्वां शरणमागतः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāsya vasato'raṇye niyatasya mahātmanaḥ
rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā sa tvāṁ śaraṇamāgataḥ

translations.english: While that high-souled one having his senses under control was dwelling in the woods, his wife was carried off by Rāvana; and he (Rāma) has (in consequence) sought your protection.

verses.sanskrit:
राजसूयाश्वमेधैश्च वह्निर्येनाभितर्पितः
दक्षिणाश्च तथोत्सृष्टा गावः शतसहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
rājasūyāśvamedhaiśca vahniryenābhitarpitaḥ
dakṣiṇāśca tathotsṛṣṭā gāvaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Raima, who has come to the forest, is the son of him who has propitiated Fire with Rājasuyas and horse sacrifices,-dispensing Dakshinas and kine by hundreds and thousands-and who has governed the earth by asceticism and truthful speech. His son Rāma has come to the forest through a woman.

verses.sanskrit:
भवता सख्यकामौ तौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
प्रतिगृह्यार्चयस्वेमौ पूजनीयतमावुभौ
verses.transliteration:
bhavatā sakhyakāmau tau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
pratigṛhyārcayasvemau pūjanīyatamāvubhau

translations.english: Do you, granting an interview to the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-both of them worthy of homage-who pe eager for your friendship, receive them respectfully.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्धर्मविनीतश्च विक्रान्तः सर्ववत्सलः
आख्याता वायुपुत्रेण तत्त्वतो मे भवद्गुणाः
verses.transliteration:
bhavāndharmavinītaśca vikrāntaḥ sarvavatsalaḥ
ākhyātā vāyuputreṇa tattvato me bhavadguṇāḥ

translations.english: Hearing Hanuman's words, Sugrīva-lord of monkeys, becoming visible (at his will), gladly spoke to Rāghava, sir, you are versed in morality, and bear love towards all. The son of the wind-god has faithfully described your virtues to me.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्ममैवैष सत्कारो लाभश्चैवोत्तमः प्रभो
यत्त्वमिच्छसि सौहार्दं वानरेण मया सह
verses.transliteration:
tanmamaivaiṣa satkāro lābhaścaivottamaḥ prabho
yattvamicchasi sauhārdaṁ vānareṇa mayā saha

translations.english: That you, O lord, are anxious to contract friendship with me who am a monkey does me honour and is my gain.

verses.sanskrit:
रोचते यदि वा सख्यं बाहुरेष प्रसारितः
गृह्यतां पाणिना पाणिर्मर्यादा वध्यतां ध्रुवा
verses.transliteration:
rocate yadi vā sakhyaṁ bāhureṣa prasāritaḥ
gṛhyatāṁ pāṇinā pāṇirmaryādā vadhyatāṁ dhruvā

translations.english: If you relish friendship with me, do you take this stretched arm and my hand with yours, and bind yourself fast with a vow.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम्
संप्रहृष्टमना हस्तं पीडयामास पाणिना
हृद्यं सौहृदमालम्ब्य पर्यष्वजत पीडितम्
verses.transliteration:
etattu vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam
saṁprahṛṣṭamanā hastaṁ pīḍayāmāsa pāṇinā
hṛdyaṁ sauhṛdamālambya paryaṣvajata pīḍitam

translations.english: Hearing these sweet words of Sugrīva, (Rāma) exceedingly delighted, pressed Sugrīva's hand with his. And contracting friendship with Surgrīva, Rāma experiencing great joy embraced him warmly.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हनूमान्संत्यज्य भिक्षुरूपमरिंदमः
काष्ठयोः स्वेन रूपेण जनयामास पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
tato hanūmānsaṁtyajya bhikṣurūpamariṁdamaḥ
kāṣṭhayoḥ svena rūpeṇa janayāmāsa pāvakam

translations.english: Then that subduer of foes, Hanumān, leaving off the guise of a beggar, in his native shape produced a fire with two pieces of wood.

verses.sanskrit:
दीप्यमानं ततो वह्निं पुष्पैरभ्यर्च्य सत्कृतम्
तयोर्मध्ये तु सुप्रीतो निदधे सुसमाहितः
verses.transliteration:
dīpyamānaṁ tato vahniṁ puṣpairabhyarcya satkṛtam
tayormadhye tu suprīto nidadhe susamāhitaḥ

translations.english: Then worshipping that flaming fire with flowers, he, well pleased, carefully placed it between them (Rāma and Sugrīva). Then Sugrīva and Rāghava went round the fire; and (thus) were fastened in friendship.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुप्रीत मनसौ तावुभौ हरिराघवौ
अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तौ न तृप्तिमुपजग्मतुः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suprīta manasau tāvubhau harirāghavau
anyonyamabhivīkṣantau na tṛptimupajagmatuḥ

translations.english: And with delighted hearts, both of them-the monkey and Rāghava began to gaze at each other, yet they did not feel satiated.

verses.sanskrit:
अयमाख्याति मे राम सचिवो मन्त्रिसत्तमः
हनुमान्यन्निमित्तं त्वं निर्जनं वनमागतः
verses.transliteration:
ayamākhyāti me rāma sacivo mantrisattamaḥ
hanumānyannimittaṁ tvaṁ nirjanaṁ vanamāgataḥ

translations.english: Sugrīva well pleased again addressed Rāghava, the son of Raghu, saying, O Rāma, this servant of thine, foremost of my counsellors, Hanumān, has related (to me), the reason of your arrival in this lone forest.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया वियुक्ता रुदती लक्ष्मणेन च धीमता
अन्तरं प्रेप्सुना तेन हत्वा गृध्रं जटायुषम्
verses.transliteration:
tvayā viyuktā rudatī lakṣmaṇena ca dhīmatā
antaraṁ prepsunā tena hatvā gṛdhraṁ jaṭāyuṣam

translations.english: Your wife, Maithili, daughter to Janaka, separated from you as well as the intelligent Laksmana, and weeping (in consequence) was carried off by a Rākṣa. Seeing for opportunities of doing mischief that Rākşa, having slain Jațáyu, has caused to you the grief that comes of separation from one's wife.

verses.sanskrit:
भार्यावियोगजं दुःखं नचिरात्त्वं विमोक्ष्यसे
अहं तामानयिष्यामि नष्टां वेदश्रुतिं यथा
verses.transliteration:
bhāryāviyogajaṁ duḥkhaṁ nacirāttvaṁ vimokṣyase
ahaṁ tāmānayiṣyāmi naṣṭāṁ vedaśrutiṁ yathā

translations.english: But you with soon be relieved from the sorrow that comes of separation from one's wife. Her will I bring like to the ravished Devasruti.

verses.sanskrit:
रसातले वा वर्तन्तीं वर्तन्तीं वा नभस्तले
अहमानीय दास्यामि तव भार्यामरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
rasātale vā vartantīṁ vartantīṁ vā nabhastale
ahamānīya dāsyāmi tava bhāryāmariṁdama

translations.english: O repressor of foes, whether she be in the nether regions or under the sky, I will, bringing your wife, make her over to you.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं तथ्यं मम वचस्त्वमवेहि च राघव
त्यज शोकं महाबाहो तां कान्तामानयामि ते
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ tathyaṁ mama vacastvamavehi ca rāghava
tyaja śokaṁ mahābāho tāṁ kāntāmānayāmi te

translations.english: O Rāghava, know my words to be true. O mighty-armed one, like to poison, your wife is incapable of being digested even by the gods and Asuras with Indra (at their head). O mightyarmed one, leave off sorrow, I will bring back your beloved.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोशन्ती राम रामेति लक्ष्मणेति च विस्वरम्
स्फुरन्ती रावणस्याङ्के पन्नगेन्द्रवधूर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca visvaram
sphurantī rāvaṇasyāṅke pannagendravadhūryathā

translations.english: From guess I find that it was doubtless Mithilā's daughter whom I saw when she was being carried away by that Räksa of terrific deeds. She was crying, Rama, Laksmana, Laks maņa,' and in the lap of Răvaņa she looked like the wife of the Snake-chief.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मना पञ्चमं मां हि दृष्ट्वा शैलतटे स्थितम्
उत्तरीयं तया त्यक्तं शुभान्याभरणानि च
verses.transliteration:
ātmanā pañcamaṁ māṁ hi dṛṣṭvā śailataṭe sthitam
uttarīyaṁ tayā tyaktaṁ śubhānyābharaṇāni ca

translations.english: Seeing me along with my four counsellors stationed at the hill, she dropped down her scarf and her ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यस्माभिर्गृहीतानि निहितानि च राघव
आनयिष्याम्यहं तानि प्रत्यभिज्ञातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tānyasmābhirgṛhītāni nihitāni ca rāghava
ānayiṣyāmyahaṁ tāni pratyabhijñātumarhasi

translations.english: All these, O Rāghava, I have taken and kept (with me). I will bring them. It behoveth you to recognise them.

verses.sanskrit:
तमब्रवीत्ततो रामः सुग्रीवं प्रियवादिनम्
आनयस्व सखे शीघ्रं किमर्थं प्रविलम्बसे
verses.transliteration:
tamabravīttato rāmaḥ sugrīvaṁ priyavādinam
ānayasva sakhe śīghraṁ kimarthaṁ pravilambase

translations.english: There upon Rāma spoke to the sweetspeeched Sugrīva, 'Bring (them), at once, my friend. Why did you tarry?'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः शैलस्य गहनां गुहाम्
प्रविवेश ततः शीघ्रं राघवप्रियकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu sugrīvaḥ śailasya gahanāṁ guhām
praviveśa tataḥ śīghraṁ rāghavapriyakāmyayā

translations.english: Having been thus addressed, Sugrīva swiftly entered a deep cavern in the mountain, with the view of doing what was dear to Rāghava. Then taking the scarf as well as the ornaments. Look at this, (Saying this) the monkey held them before Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गृहीत्वा तद्वासः शुभान्याभरणानि च
अभवद्बाष्पसंरुद्धो नीहारेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
tato gṛhītvā tadvāsaḥ śubhānyābharaṇāni ca
abhavadbāṣpasaṁruddho nīhāreṇeva candramāḥ

translations.english: Taking the sheet and the ornaments, (Rama) had his ayes filled with tears, like the moon covered by the dew.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतास्नेहप्रवृत्तेन स तु बाष्पेण दूषितः
हा प्रियेति रुदन्धैर्यमुत्सृज्य न्यपतत्क्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
sītāsnehapravṛttena sa tu bāṣpeṇa dūṣitaḥ
hā priyeti rudandhairyamutsṛjya nyapatatkṣitau

translations.english: From affection for Sītā, (Rāma,) his eyes filled with tears, deprived of patience, fell down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
हृदि कृत्वा स बहुशस्तमलंकारमुत्तमम्
निशश्वास भृशं सर्पो बिलस्थ इव रोषितः
verses.transliteration:
hṛdi kṛtvā sa bahuśastamalaṁkāramuttamam
niśaśvāsa bhṛśaṁ sarpo bilastha iva roṣitaḥ

translations.english: And placing the elegant ornaments on his bosom, he sighed again and again, like an enraged serpent in a hole.

verses.sanskrit:
अविच्छिन्नाश्रुवेगस्तु सौमित्रिं वीक्ष्य पार्श्वतः
परिदेवयितुं दीनं रामः समुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
avicchinnāśruvegastu saumitriṁ vīkṣya pārśvataḥ
paridevayituṁ dīnaṁ rāmaḥ samupacakrame

translations.english: Seeing Sumitrā's son at his side, Rāma shedding ceaseless tears, began to lament piteously,

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्या संत्यक्तं ह्रियमाणया
उत्तरीयमिदं भूमौ शरीराद्भूषणानि च
verses.transliteration:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyā saṁtyaktaṁ hriyamāṇayā
uttarīyamidaṁ bhūmau śarīrādbhūṣaṇāni ca

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, behold this scarf and these ornaments which Vaidehī, while being carried away, let fall from her person to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
शाद्वलिन्यां ध्रुवं भूम्यां सीतया ह्रियमाणया
उत्सृष्टं भूषणमिदं तथारूपं हि दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
śādvalinyāṁ dhruvaṁ bhūmyāṁ sītayā hriyamāṇayā
utsṛṣṭaṁ bhūṣaṇamidaṁ tathārūpaṁ hi dṛśyate

translations.english: Surely Sītā, while being ravished, let these fall on a sward, for these remain as before.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूहि सुग्रीव कं देशं ह्रियन्ती लक्षिता त्वया
रक्षसा रौद्ररूपेण मम प्राणसमा प्रिया
verses.transliteration:
brūhi sugrīva kaṁ deśaṁ hriyantī lakṣitā tvayā
rakṣasā raudrarūpeṇa mama prāṇasamā priyā

translations.english: Thereupon Rāghava said these words to Sugriva, Tell me, O Sugriva, at what place didst you see Sītā, while she, dear to me as life, was taken away by the fierce-looking Raksasas?

verses.sanskrit:
क्व वा वसति तद्रक्षो महद्व्यसनदं मम
यन्निमित्तमहं सर्वान्नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
kva vā vasati tadrakṣo mahadvyasanadaṁ mama
yannimittamahaṁ sarvānnāśayiṣyāmi rākṣasān

translations.english: Where does that Rākṣa, who has brought on this high peril, and for whom I will slay all the Rākşasas, live?

verses.sanskrit:
हरता मैथिलीं येन मां च रोषयता भृशम्
आत्मनो जीवितान्ताय मृत्युद्वारमपावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
haratā maithilīṁ yena māṁ ca roṣayatā bhṛśam
ātmano jīvitāntāya mṛtyudvāramapāvṛtam

translations.english: He, that has carried off Mithila's daughter, and roused my wrath, has certainly for his own end, opened the door of death.

verses.sanskrit:
मम दयिततमा हृता वना;द्रजनिचरेण विमथ्य येन सा
कथय मम रिपुं तमद्य वै; प्रवगपते यमसंनिधिं नयामि
verses.transliteration:
mama dayitatamā hṛtā vanā;drajanicareṇa vimathya yena sā
kathaya mama ripuṁ tamadya vai; pravagapate yamasaṁnidhiṁ nayāmi

translations.english: Tell me all about that ranger of the night, that deceitfully has carried away my dearest wife from the forest. My foe, O lord of monkey will I to-day send to the neighbourhood of Yāma.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो रामेणार्तेन वानरः
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं सबाष्पं बाष्पगद्गदः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu sugrīvo rāmeṇārtena vānaraḥ
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ sabāṣpaṁ bāṣpagadgadaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the aggrieved Rāma, the monkey, Sugriva, his accents obstructed by vapour and his eyes filled with tears, said with joined hands,

verses.sanskrit:
न जाने निलयं तस्य सर्वथा पापरक्षसः
सामर्थ्यं विक्रमं वापि दौष्कुलेयस्य वा कुलम्
verses.transliteration:
na jāne nilayaṁ tasya sarvathā pāparakṣasaḥ
sāmarthyaṁ vikramaṁ vāpi dauṣkuleyasya vā kulam

translations.english: I do not know the hidden abode of that exceedingly wicked Raksasa,-nor do l know his heroism and prowess, or the lineage of that one sprung from a vicious race.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यं तु प्रतिजानामि त्यज शोकमरिंदम
करिष्यामि तथा यत्नं यथा प्राप्स्यसि मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
satyaṁ tu pratijānāmi tyaja śokamariṁdama
kariṣyāmi tathā yatnaṁ yathā prāpsyasi maithilīm

translations.english: O vanquisher of foes, leave off sorrowing. I promise to you truly, I will exert so that you mayst obtain Maithilī.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं सगणं हत्वा परितोष्यात्मपौरुषम्
तथास्मि कर्ता नचिराद्यथा प्रीतो भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaṁ sagaṇaṁ hatvā paritoṣyātmapauruṣam
tathāsmi kartā nacirādyathā prīto bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: Slaying Rāvaņa with his hosts, and putting forth my manliness capable of pleasing others, I will speedily act so that you mayst be pleased.

verses.sanskrit:
अलं वैक्लव्यमालम्ब्य धैर्यमात्मगतं स्मर
त्वद्विधानां न सदृशमीदृशं बुद्धिलाघवम्
verses.transliteration:
alaṁ vaiklavyamālambya dhairyamātmagataṁ smara
tvadvidhānāṁ na sadṛśamīdṛśaṁ buddhilāghavam

translations.english: Do not be overwhelmed with grief: summon the fortitude that is in you. Such lightness of sense does not become persons like you.

verses.sanskrit:
मयापि व्यसनं प्राप्तं भार्या हरणजं महत्
न चाहमेवं शोचामि न च धैर्यं परित्यजे
verses.transliteration:
mayāpi vyasanaṁ prāptaṁ bhāryā haraṇajaṁ mahat
na cāhamevaṁ śocāmi na ca dhairyaṁ parityaje

translations.english: I also have experienced mighty disaster arising out of separation from my wife; but I do not weep in this wise,-nor do I forsake my fortitude.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं तामनुशोचामि प्राकृतो वानरोऽपि सन्
महात्मा च विनीतश्चा किं पुनर्धृतिमान्भवान्
verses.transliteration:
nāhaṁ tāmanuśocāmi prākṛto vānaro'pi san
mahātmā ca vinītaścā kiṁ punardhṛtimānbhavān

translations.english: A despicable monkey as I am, I do not grieve for her,-and what again shall I say of one that is magnanimous, endued with meekness and firmness, and great?

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पमापतितं धैर्यान्निग्रहीतुं त्वमर्हसि
मर्यादां सत्त्वयुक्तानां धृतिं नोत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpamāpatitaṁ dhairyānnigrahītuṁ tvamarhasi
maryādāṁ sattvayuktānāṁ dhṛtiṁ notsraṣṭumarhasi

translations.english: It behoveth you to restrain your falling tears by patience. It behoveth you not to resign that patience which is the dignity of persons possessed of the quality of goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यसने वार्थ कृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे
विमृशन्वै स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान्नावसीदति
verses.transliteration:
vyasane vārtha kṛcchre vā bhaye vā jīvitāntage
vimṛśanvai svayā buddhyā dhṛtimānnāvasīdati

translations.english: Persons endued with firmness of understanding by help of their intellect, do not in calamity consequent on separation from dear ones, or on the occasion of loss of wealth, or of fear arising from thieves, wild beasts, etc., or of loss of life itself, lose their self-possession.

verses.sanskrit:
बालिशस्तु नरो नित्यं वैक्लव्यं योऽनुवर्तते
स मज्जत्यवशः शोके भाराक्रान्तेव नौर्जले
verses.transliteration:
bāliśastu naro nityaṁ vaiklavyaṁ yo'nuvartate
sa majjatyavaśaḥ śoke bhārākrānteva naurjale

translations.english: He that is senseless as well as he that suffers himself to be overwhelmed with grief, losing all control over self, drown themselves in sorrow like a boat bearing a heavy load in water.

verses.sanskrit:
एषोऽञ्जलिर्मया बद्धः प्रणयात्त्वां प्रसादये
पौरुषं श्रय शोकस्य नान्तरं दातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
eṣo'ñjalirmayā baddhaḥ praṇayāttvāṁ prasādaye
pauruṣaṁ śraya śokasya nāntaraṁ dātumarhasi

translations.english: I soothe you from the love I bear towards you. Do you have recourse to manliness. It does not behove you to let grief overcome you.

verses.sanskrit:
ये शोकमनुवर्तन्ते न तेषां विद्यते सुखम्
तेजश्च क्षीयते तेषां न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
ye śokamanuvartante na teṣāṁ vidyate sukham
tejaśca kṣīyate teṣāṁ na tvaṁ śocitumarhasi

translations.english: Those that indulge in sorrow, know no happiness; and their virtue* goeth out of them. Therefore it behoveth you not to grieve. In the sense of energy.

verses.sanskrit:
हितं वयस्य भावेन ब्रूहि नोपदिशामि ते
वयस्यतां पूजयन्मे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
hitaṁ vayasya bhāvena brūhi nopadiśāmi te
vayasyatāṁ pūjayanme na tvaṁ śocitumarhasi

translations.english: In the spirit of a friend I tell what is for your good: I do not instruct you. Honour the amity I bear towards you. It behoveth you not to weep.

verses.sanskrit:
मधुरं सान्त्वितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण स राघवः
मुखमश्रुपरिक्लिन्नं वस्त्रान्तेन प्रमार्जयत्
verses.transliteration:
madhuraṁ sāntvitastena sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ
mukhamaśrupariklinnaṁ vastrāntena pramārjayat

translations.english: Thus sweetly consoled by Sugrīva, Rāghava with the end of his cloth wiped his face tarnished with tears.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिष्ठस्तु काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीववचनात्प्रभुः
संपरिष्वज्य सुग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtiṣṭhastu kākutsthaḥ sugrīvavacanātprabhuḥ
saṁpariṣvajya sugrīvamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And after that lord, Kakutstha, had recovered his natural state through the words of Sugrīva he embraced Sugrīva and addressed him, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
कर्तव्यं यद्वयस्येन स्निग्धेन च हितेन च
अनुरूपं च युक्तं च कृतं सुग्रीव तत्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
kartavyaṁ yadvayasyena snigdhena ca hitena ca
anurūpaṁ ca yuktaṁ ca kṛtaṁ sugrīva tattvayā

translations.english: O Sugriva, that which, pleasing and profitable, proper and fit, ought to be done by a friend, has been done by you.

verses.sanskrit:
एष च प्रकृतिष्ठोऽहमनुनीतस्त्वया सखे
दुर्लभो हीदृशो बन्धुरस्मिन्काले विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa ca prakṛtiṣṭho'hamanunītastvayā sakhe
durlabho hīdṛśo bandhurasminkāle viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: Solicited by you, I have, O friend, regained my natural tone of mind. Such a friend is rare, specially at such a time.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तु यत्नस्त्वया कार्यो मैथिल्याः परिमार्गणे
राक्षसस्य च रौद्रस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tu yatnastvayā kāryo maithilyāḥ parimārgaṇe
rākṣasasya ca raudrasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ

translations.english: But you should strive to trace Maithili as well as bring about the destruction of that fierce Räks asa, the impious Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
मया च यदनुष्ठेयं विस्रब्धेन तदुच्यताम्
वर्षास्विव च सुक्षेत्रे सर्वं संपद्यते तव
verses.transliteration:
mayā ca yadanuṣṭheyaṁ visrabdhena taducyatām
varṣāsviva ca sukṣetre sarvaṁ saṁpadyate tava

translations.english: Do you also without reserve say what I shall have to do for you. Like corn sown in a fertile field in the rainy season, every concern of thine shall attain success.

verses.sanskrit:
मया च यदिदं वाक्यमभिमानात्समीरितम्
तत्त्वया हरिशार्दूल तत्त्वमित्युपधार्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
mayā ca yadidaṁ vākyamabhimānātsamīritam
tattvayā hariśārdūla tattvamityupadhāryatām

translations.english: O best of monkeys, do you verily consider as true the words that I have uttered through affection.

verses.sanskrit:
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन
एतत्ते प्रतिजानामि सत्येनैव शपामि ते
verses.transliteration:
anṛtaṁ noktapūrvaṁ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
etatte pratijānāmi satyenaiva śapāmi te

translations.english: Falsehoods have I never spoken before, nor will I ever say one (in future). This I promise to you. I swear by truth itself.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवो वानरैः सचिवैः सह
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञातं विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvo vānaraiḥ sacivaiḥ saha
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā pratijñātaṁ viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: Hearing Rāghava's words, and in special his promise, Sugrīva felt exceedingly delighted along with this monkey ministers.

verses.sanskrit:
महानुभावस्य वचो निशम्य; हरिर्नराणामृषभस्य तस्य
कृतं स मेने हरिवीर मुख्य;स्तदा स्वकार्यं हृदयेन विद्वान्
verses.transliteration:
mahānubhāvasya vaco niśamya; harirnarāṇāmṛṣabhasya tasya
kṛtaṁ sa mene harivīra mukhya;stadā svakāryaṁ hṛdayena vidvān

translations.english: Hearing the words of that illustrious monarch of kings, that hero-greatest of monkeys-considered and felt in his heart as if his work had already been accomplished.

verses.sanskrit:
परितुष्टस्तु सुग्रीवस्तेन वाक्येन वानरः
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रजं राममिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
parituṣṭastu sugrīvastena vākyena vānaraḥ
lakṣmaṇasyāgrajaṁ rāmamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Sugrīva, rejoiced at the words of Rāma, said to that hero, the elder brother of Laksmana; who was well pleased.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथाहमनुग्राह्यो देवतानामसंशयः
उपपन्नगुणोपेतः सखा यस्य भवान्मम
verses.transliteration:
sarvathāhamanugrāhyo devatānāmasaṁśayaḥ
upapannaguṇopetaḥ sakhā yasya bhavānmama

translations.english: I am, without doubt, worthy of being favoured by the gods, since you accomplished and furnished with virtues are my friend.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्यं खलु भवेद्राम सहायेन त्वयानघ
सुरराज्यमपि प्राप्तुं स्वराज्यं किं पुनः प्रभो
verses.transliteration:
śakyaṁ khalu bhavedrāma sahāyena tvayānagha
surarājyamapi prāptuṁ svarājyaṁ kiṁ punaḥ prabho

translations.english: By your help, O Rama, one can, O sinless one, obtain the kingdom of the celestials,-what is to be said of one's kingdom, O lord?

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं सभाज्यो बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव राघव
यस्याग्निसाक्षिकं मित्रं लब्धं राघववंशजम्
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ sabhājyo bandhūnāṁ suhṛdāṁ caiva rāghava
yasyāgnisākṣikaṁ mitraṁ labdhaṁ rāghavavaṁśajam

translations.english: I, who have, in the presence of Fire, gained for my friend (you) sprung from the Rāghava race, am, O Rāghava worthy of being honoured by my friends and relations.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमप्यनुरूपस्ते वयस्यो ज्ञास्यसे शनैः
न तु वक्तुं समर्थोऽहं स्वयमात्मगतान्गुणान्
verses.transliteration:
ahamapyanurūpaste vayasyo jñāsyase śanaiḥ
na tu vaktuṁ samartho'haṁ svayamātmagatānguṇān

translations.english: You also shall by and by learn that I am a fit friend for you; but I can not speak to you of the qualities that abide in me.

verses.sanskrit:
महात्मनां तु भूयिष्ठं त्वद्विधानां कृतात्मनाम्
निश्चला भवति प्रीतिर्धैर्यमात्मवतामिव
verses.transliteration:
mahātmanāṁ tu bhūyiṣṭhaṁ tvadvidhānāṁ kṛtātmanām
niścalā bhavati prītirdhairyamātmavatāmiva

translations.english: O free one, the felicity of high-souled and self-governed friends like you abounds and is enduring.

verses.sanskrit:
रजतं वा सुवर्णं वा वस्त्राण्याभरणानि वा
अविभक्तानि साधूनामवगच्छन्ति साधवः
verses.transliteration:
rajataṁ vā suvarṇaṁ vā vastrāṇyābharaṇāni vā
avibhaktāni sādhūnāmavagacchanti sādhavaḥ

translations.english: Pious friends look upon the silver, and gold, and the elegant ornaments of pious friends as common property.

verses.sanskrit:
आढ्यो वापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा
निर्दोषो वा सदोषो वा वयस्यः परमा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
āḍhyo vāpi daridro vā duḥkhitaḥ sukhito'pi vā
nirdoṣo vā sadoṣo vā vayasyaḥ paramā gatiḥ

translations.english: Whether rich or poor, happy or miserable, good or bad, a friend is the greatest refuge (of his friend).

verses.sanskrit:
धनत्यागः सुखत्यागो देहत्यागोऽपि वा पुनः
वयस्यार्थे प्रवर्तन्ते स्नेहं दृष्ट्वा तथाविधम्
verses.transliteration:
dhanatyāgaḥ sukhatyāgo dehatyāgo'pi vā punaḥ
vayasyārthe pravartante snehaṁ dṛṣṭvā tathāvidham

translations.english: Witnessing such affection, people can, O sinless one, forsake wealth, comfort, and even their native land for the sake of their friends.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तथेत्यब्रवीद्रामः सुग्रीवं प्रियवादिनम्
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो लक्ष्म्या वासवस्येव धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
tattathetyabravīdrāmaḥ sugrīvaṁ priyavādinam
lakṣmaṇasyāgrato lakṣmyā vāsavasyeva dhīmataḥ

translations.english: There at the graceful Rāma, in front of the intelligent Lakşmaņa resembling Väsava, said to Sugriva of a pleasing presence,-It is even so.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
सुग्रीवः सर्वतश्चक्षुर्वने लोलमपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmaṁ sthitaṁ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam
sugrīvaḥ sarvataścakṣurvane lolamapātayat

translations.english: The next day seeing Rāma as well as the mighty Lakşmaņa seated on the ground, Sugrīva briskly cast his eyes about the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श ततः सालमविदूरे हरीश्वरः
सुपुष्पमीषत्पत्राढ्यं भ्रमरैरुपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa tataḥ sālamavidūre harīśvaraḥ
supuṣpamīṣatpatrāḍhyaṁ bhramarairupaśobhitam

translations.english: And hard by that lord of monkeys discovered a Sāla tree, bearing a few beautiful blossoms, with its wealth of foliage, decked by black bees.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैकां पर्णबहुलां भङ्क्त्वा शाखां सुपुष्पिताम्
सालस्यास्तीर्य सुग्रीवो निषसाद सराघवः
verses.transliteration:
tasyaikāṁ parṇabahulāṁ bhaṅktvā śākhāṁ supuṣpitām
sālasyāstīrya sugrīvo niṣasāda sarāghavaḥ

translations.english: Then spreading a beautifully blossoming spray of Sala, full of foliage, Sugriva made an awning and sat down with Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तावासीनौ ततो दृष्ट्वा हनूमानपि लक्ष्मणम्
सालशाखां समुत्पाट्य विनीतमुपवेशयत्
verses.transliteration:
tāvāsīnau tato dṛṣṭvā hanūmānapi lakṣmaṇam
sālaśākhāṁ samutpāṭya vinītamupaveśayat

translations.english: Seeing them seated, Hanumān breaking off a branch of śāla, humbly made Lakşmaņa sit down.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवः श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा
उवाच प्रणयाद्रामं हर्षव्याकुलिताक्षरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ ślakṣṇaṁ madhurayā girā
uvāca praṇayādrāmaṁ harṣavyākulitākṣaram

translations.english: Next Sugriva, feeling high rapture, with his eyes expanded with joy, answered Rāma blandly in sweet words.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा चराम्येष भयार्दितः
ऋश्यमूकं गिरिवरं हृतभार्यः सुदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ vinikṛto bhrātrā carāmyeṣa bhayārditaḥ
ṛśyamūkaṁ girivaraṁ hṛtabhāryaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Wronged by my brother, I deprived of my wife and exceedingly distressed, and exercised with fear, live in this foremost of mountains, Rs yamuka.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं त्रस्तो भये मग्नो वसाम्युद्भ्रान्तचेतनः
वालिना निकृतो भ्रात्रा कृतवैरश्च राघव
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ trasto bhaye magno vasāmyudbhrāntacetanaḥ
vālinā nikṛto bhrātrā kṛtavairaśca rāghava

translations.english: O Rāghava, my senses wildered, having been oppressed by Vāli, and having incurred his enmity, I am afflicted with fear, and tormented with fright.

verses.sanskrit:
वालिनो मे भयार्तस्य सर्वलोकाभयंकर
ममापि त्वमनाथस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
vālino me bhayārtasya sarvalokābhayaṁkara
mamāpi tvamanāthasya prasādaṁ kartumarhasi

translations.english: O you, that remove the fear of all creatures, it behove you who am tormented by fear and am helpless, to extend your favour to me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः
प्रत्युवाच स काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीवं प्रहसन्निव
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu tejasvī dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ
pratyuvāca sa kākutsthaḥ sugrīvaṁ prahasanniva

translations.english: Thus accosted, that ever energetic one knowing righteousness and devoted to it, Kākutstha, smiling, said to Sugrīva,

verses.sanskrit:
उपकारफलं मित्रमपकारोऽरिलक्षणम्
अद्यैव तं हनिष्यामि तव भार्यापहारिणम्
verses.transliteration:
upakāraphalaṁ mitramapakāro'rilakṣaṇam
adyaiva taṁ haniṣyāmi tava bhāryāpahāriṇam

translations.english: Benefits make friends, while injuries denote enemies. Even this very day will I slay him that has deprived you of your wife.

verses.sanskrit:
कङ्कपत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना महेन्द्राशनिसंनिभाः
सुपर्वाणः सुतीक्ष्णाग्रा सरोषा भुजगा इव
verses.transliteration:
kaṅkapatrapraticchannā mahendrāśanisaṁnibhāḥ
suparvāṇaḥ sutīkṣṇāgrā saroṣā bhujagā iva

translations.english: O exalted one, these feathered shafts of exceeding energy, sprung from the Kārtikeya forest, decked with gold, furnished with the plumes of the Kanka, resembling the thunderbolt of the great Indra, having smooth knots, and sharp heads, are like enraged serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातृसंज्ञममित्रं ते वालिनं कृतकिल्बिषम्
शरैर्विनिहतं पश्य विकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātṛsaṁjñamamitraṁ te vālinaṁ kṛtakilbiṣam
śarairvinihataṁ paśya vikīrṇamiva parvatam

translations.english: You shall behold your brother and enemy, who is named Vāli slain by my shafts, and lying like a dislodged hill.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinīpatiḥ
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt

translations.english: Hearing Rāghava's words, Sugrīva-lord of host-felt excess of joy and exclaimed, Excellent well! Excellent well!

verses.sanskrit:
रामशोकाभिभूतोऽहं शोकार्तानां भवान्गतिः
वयस्य इति कृत्वा हि त्वय्यहं परिदेवये
verses.transliteration:
rāmaśokābhibhūto'haṁ śokārtānāṁ bhavāngatiḥ
vayasya iti kṛtvā hi tvayyahaṁ paridevaye

translations.english: O Rāma, overwhelmed am I by grief. You are the succour of those afflicted with sorrow. Having made you my friend, I express to you my grief.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि पाणिप्रदानेन वयस्यो सोऽग्निसाक्षिकः
कृतः प्राणैर्बहुमतः सत्येनापि शपाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi pāṇipradānena vayasyo so'gnisākṣikaḥ
kṛtaḥ prāṇairbahumataḥ satyenāpi śapāmyaham

translations.english: I have, in the presence of Fire by giving you my hand, made you my friend. You are dearer to me than life itself. This I swear to you by Truth.

verses.sanskrit:
वयस्य इति कृत्वा च विस्रब्धं प्रवदाम्यहम्
दुःखमन्तर्गतं यन्मे मनो दहति नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
vayasya iti kṛtvā ca visrabdhaṁ pravadāmyaham
duḥkhamantargataṁ yanme mano dahati nityaśaḥ

translations.english: Having made you my friend, I inspired with confidence am unbosoming myself to you. The sorrow, that is in my heart, is constantly enfeebling my mind.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं बाष्पदूषितलोचनः
बाष्पोपहतया वाचा नोच्चैः शक्नोति भाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṁ bāṣpadūṣitalocanaḥ
bāṣpopahatayā vācā noccaiḥ śaknoti bhāṣitum

translations.english: Having proceeded thus far, he, his eyes filled with tears and his words faltering because of vapour, could not speak aloud.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पवेगं तु सहसा नदीवेगमिवागतम्
धारयामास धैर्येण सुग्रीवो रामसंनिधौ
verses.transliteration:
bāṣpavegaṁ tu sahasā nadīvegamivāgatam
dhārayāmāsa dhairyeṇa sugrīvo rāmasaṁnidhau

translations.english: Sugrīva suddenly restrained, before Rāma, the force of tears, like to the tide of a river.

verses.sanskrit:
संनिगृह्य तु तं बाष्पं प्रमृज्य नयने शुभे
विनिःश्वस्य च तेजस्वी राघवं पुनरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁnigṛhya tu taṁ bāṣpaṁ pramṛjya nayane śubhe
viniḥśvasya ca tejasvī rāghavaṁ punarabravīt

translations.english: Having restrained his tears and wiped his fair eyes, that energetic one, sighing heavily, again went on,

verses.sanskrit:
पुराहं वलिना राम राज्यात्स्वादवरोपितः
परुषाणि च संश्राव्य निर्धूतोऽस्मि बलीयसा
verses.transliteration:
purāhaṁ valinā rāma rājyātsvādavaropitaḥ
paruṣāṇi ca saṁśrāvya nirdhūto'smi balīyasā

translations.english: Formerly, O Rāma, I was deprived of my kingdom and reproached in harsh language by the strong Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
हृता भार्या च मे तेन प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी
सुहृदश्च मदीया ये संयता बन्धनेषु ते
verses.transliteration:
hṛtā bhāryā ca me tena prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī
suhṛdaśca madīyā ye saṁyatā bandhaneṣu te

translations.english: He also took away my wife dearer to me than life; and my friends have been imprisoned and been bound.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्नवांश्च सुदुष्टात्मा मद्विनाशाय राघव
बहुशस्तत्प्रयुक्ताश्च वानरा निहता मया
verses.transliteration:
yatnavāṁśca suduṣṭātmā madvināśāya rāghava
bahuśastatprayuktāśca vānarā nihatā mayā

translations.english: That wicked wight, O Rāghava, seeks my life. Many monkeys commissioned by him have been slain by me.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्कया त्वेतया चाहं दृष्ट्वा त्वामपि राघव
नोपसर्पाम्यहं भीतो भये सर्वे हि बिभ्यति
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkayā tvetayā cāhaṁ dṛṣṭvā tvāmapi rāghava
nopasarpāmyahaṁ bhīto bhaye sarve hi bibhyati

translations.english: It was, O Rāghava, in consequence of this fear that when I (first) saw you, I did not come out. This is all the fear that oppresses me.

verses.sanskrit:
केवलं हि सहाया मे हनुमत्प्रमुखास्त्विमे
अतोऽहं धारयाम्यद्य प्राणान्कृच्छ्र गतोऽपि सन्
verses.transliteration:
kevalaṁ hi sahāyā me hanumatpramukhāstvime
ato'haṁ dhārayāmyadya prāṇānkṛcchra gato'pi san

translations.english: My adherents are only these headed by Hanumān. It is for this that although reduced to the greatest straits I have been able to preserve my life.

verses.sanskrit:
एते हि कपयः स्निग्धा मां रक्षन्ति समन्ततः
सह गच्छन्ति गन्तव्ये नित्यं तिष्ठन्ति च स्थिते
verses.transliteration:
ete hi kapayaḥ snigdhā māṁ rakṣanti samantataḥ
saha gacchanti gantavye nityaṁ tiṣṭhanti ca sthite

translations.english: These affectionate apes protect me on all sides. They go when I go, and stay when I stay.

verses.sanskrit:
संक्षेपस्त्वेष मे राम किमुक्त्वा विस्तरं हि ते
स मे ज्येष्ठो रिपुर्भ्राता वाली विश्रुतपौरुषः
verses.transliteration:
saṁkṣepastveṣa me rāma kimuktvā vistaraṁ hi te
sa me jyeṣṭho ripurbhrātā vālī viśrutapauruṣaḥ

translations.english: Why should I expatiate? In brief, Vāli my elder brother, famed for his prowess, is my foe.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्विनाशाद्धि मे दुःखं प्रनष्टं स्यादनन्तरम्
सुखं मे जीवितं चैव तद्विनाशनिबन्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
tadvināśāddhi me duḥkhaṁ pranaṣṭaṁ syādanantaram
sukhaṁ me jīvitaṁ caiva tadvināśanibandhanam

translations.english: Even by his death my present pain would be removed. Both my life and my happiness are bound up with his death.

verses.sanskrit:
एष मे राम शोकान्तः शोकार्तेन निवेदितः
दुःखितोऽदुःखितो वापि सख्युर्नित्यं सखा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa me rāma śokāntaḥ śokārtena niveditaḥ
duḥkhito'duḥkhito vāpi sakhyurnityaṁ sakhā gatiḥ

translations.english: I have, O Rāma, communicated to you, the way in which my grief might be removed. Whether in joy or in sorrow, a friend is the refuge of his friend.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वैतच्च वचो रामः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्
किंनिमित्तमभूद्वैरं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvaitacca vaco rāmaḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt
kiṁnimittamabhūdvairaṁ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words, Rāma said to Sugrīva, What for arose hostility between yourself and Vāli? I wish to hear this (related) faithfully.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखं हि कारणं श्रुत्वा वैरस्य तव वानर
आनन्तर्यं विधास्यामि संप्रधार्य बलाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
sukhaṁ hi kāraṇaṁ śrutvā vairasya tava vānara
ānantaryaṁ vidhāsyāmi saṁpradhārya balābalam

translations.english: Having learnt the cause of your hostility, and ascertained your strength and weakness, I will, O monkey, understanding the irritation that has ensued, compass your happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
बलवान्हि ममामर्षः श्रुत्वा त्वामवमानितम्
वर्धते हृदयोत्कम्पी प्रावृड्वेग इवाम्भसः
verses.transliteration:
balavānhi mamāmarṣaḥ śrutvā tvāmavamānitam
vardhate hṛdayotkampī prāvṛḍvega ivāmbhasaḥ

translations.english: Great is my wrath, on hearing you disgraced; and like a down-pour in the rainy season my ire increases, shaking my very heart.

verses.sanskrit:
हृष्टः कथय विस्रब्धो यावदारोप्यते धनुः
सृष्टश्च हि मया बाणो निरस्तश्च रिपुस्तव
verses.transliteration:
hṛṣṭaḥ kathaya visrabdho yāvadāropyate dhanuḥ
sṛṣṭaśca hi mayā bāṇo nirastaśca ripustava

translations.english: Do you cheerfully and confidingly speak while I fix the string to my bow. As soon as my shaft is off, your foe is beaten.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu sugrīvaḥ kākutsthena mahātmanā
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the high-souled Käkutstha, Sugrīva, along with the four (other) monkeys, experienced exceeding delight.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहृष्टवदनः सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणाग्रजे
वैरस्य कारणं तत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ sugrīvo lakṣmaṇāgraje
vairasya kāraṇaṁ tattvamākhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: Then with a cheerful countenance, Sugrīva began to unfold to Lakşmaņa's elder brother the cause of their hostility.

verses.sanskrit:
वाली नाम मम भ्राता ज्येष्ठः शत्रुनिषूदनः
पितुर्बहुमतो नित्यं मम चापि तथा पुरा
verses.transliteration:
vālī nāma mama bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ śatruniṣūdanaḥ
piturbahumato nityaṁ mama cāpi tathā purā

translations.english: My elder brother named Väli-destroyer of foes, was formerly highly, honoured both by my father and myself.

verses.sanskrit:
पितर्युपरतेऽस्माकं ज्येष्ठोऽयमिति मन्त्रिभिः
कपीनामीश्वरो राज्ये कृतः परमसंमतः
verses.transliteration:
pitaryuparate'smākaṁ jyeṣṭho'yamiti mantribhiḥ
kapīnāmīśvaro rājye kṛtaḥ paramasaṁmataḥ

translations.english: At the death of our father, the counsellors, saying,-This is the eldest son', made him, who was well loved (of all), lord of the monkeys in the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं प्रशासतस्तस्य पितृपैतामहं महत्
अहं सर्वेषु कालेषु प्रणतः प्रेष्यवत्स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ praśāsatastasya pitṛpaitāmahaṁ mahat
ahaṁ sarveṣu kāleṣu praṇataḥ preṣyavatsthitaḥ

translations.english: While he was governing the kingdom which had belonged to his father and grand-father, I, at all times, in humiliation, remained like a servant.

verses.sanskrit:
मायावी नाम तेजस्वी पूर्वजो दुन्दुभेः सुतः
तेन तस्य महद्वैरं स्त्रीकृतं विश्रुतं पुरा
verses.transliteration:
māyāvī nāma tejasvī pūrvajo dundubheḥ sutaḥ
tena tasya mahadvairaṁ strīkṛtaṁ viśrutaṁ purā

translations.english: There was one endued with energy, named Māyāvi. He was the eldest son of Dunduvī. Formerly there arose a mighty hostility between himself and Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु सुप्ते जने रात्रौ किष्किन्धाद्वारमागतः
नर्दति स्म सुसंरब्धो वालिनं चाह्वयद्रणे
verses.transliteration:
sa tu supte jane rātrau kiṣkindhādvāramāgataḥ
nardati sma susaṁrabdho vālinaṁ cāhvayadraṇe

translations.english: It came to pass that one night when all had fallen asleep, (Māyāvi) coming to Kişkindhā, began to emit roars in great wrath, and challenged Väli to an encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसुप्तस्तु मम भ्राता नर्दितं भैरवस्वनम्
श्रुत्वा न ममृषे वाली निष्पपात जवात्तदा
verses.transliteration:
prasuptastu mama bhrātā narditaṁ bhairavasvanam
śrutvā na mamṛṣe vālī niṣpapāta javāttadā

translations.english: My brother, who was fast asleep, hearing those dreadful yells, could not bear them; but at once rushed out vehemently.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वै निःसृतः क्रोधात्तं हन्तुमसुरोत्तमम्
वार्यमाणस्ततः स्त्रीभिर्मया च प्रणतात्मना
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vai niḥsṛtaḥ krodhāttaṁ hantumasurottamam
vāryamāṇastataḥ strībhirmayā ca praṇatātmanā

translations.english: And as he rushed out in wrath, for the purpose of slaying that foremost of Asuras, he was opposed by his wives as well as myself, who humbled himself before him.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु निर्धूय सर्वान्नो निर्जगाम महाबलः
ततोऽहमपि सौहार्दान्निःसृतो वालिना सह
verses.transliteration:
sa tu nirdhūya sarvānno nirjagāma mahābalaḥ
tato'hamapi sauhārdānniḥsṛto vālinā saha

translations.english: But moving them aside, that exceedingly powerful one sallied out. Thereupon out of affection I also went out with Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु मे भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा मां च दूरादवस्थितम्
असुरो जातसंत्रासः प्रदुद्राव तदा भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu me bhrātaraṁ dṛṣṭvā māṁ ca dūrādavasthitam
asuro jātasaṁtrāsaḥ pradudrāva tadā bhṛśam

translations.english: And seeing my brother and me present from a distance, the Asura, seized with a panic, fled with speed.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्द्रवति संत्रस्ते ह्यावां द्रुततरं गतौ
प्रकाशोऽपि कृतो मार्गश्चन्द्रेणोद्गच्छता तदा
verses.transliteration:
tasmindravati saṁtraste hyāvāṁ drutataraṁ gatau
prakāśo'pi kṛto mārgaścandreṇodgacchatā tadā

translations.english: And as he was rushing on in fear and when we had proceeded further, the moon arising, discovered the way.

verses.sanskrit:
स तृणैरावृतं दुर्गं धरण्या विवरं महत्
प्रविवेशासुरो वेगादावामासाद्य विष्ठितौ
verses.transliteration:
sa tṛṇairāvṛtaṁ durgaṁ dharaṇyā vivaraṁ mahat
praviveśāsuro vegādāvāmāsādya viṣṭhitau

translations.english: And the Asura, coming by a capacious and impregnable hole covered with grass (on the surface), entered it amain; and we remained there.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रविष्टं रिपुं दृष्ट्वा बिलं रोषवशं गतः
मामुवाच तदा वाली वचनं क्षुभितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ praviṣṭaṁ ripuṁ dṛṣṭvā bilaṁ roṣavaśaṁ gataḥ
māmuvāca tadā vālī vacanaṁ kṣubhitendriyaḥ

translations.english: Seeing his enemy enter the hole, Vāli, overcome by anger, and with his senses agitated, spoke to me, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
इह त्वं तिष्ठ सुग्रीव बिलद्वारि समाहितः
यावदत्र प्रविश्याहं निहन्मि समरे रिपुम्
verses.transliteration:
iha tvaṁ tiṣṭha sugrīva biladvāri samāhitaḥ
yāvadatra praviśyāhaṁ nihanmi samare ripum

translations.english: Do you, O Sugriva, carefully stay at the mouth of the hole, while I entering in, slay my foe in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
मया त्वेतद्वचः श्रुत्वा याचितः स परंतप
शापयित्वा च मां पद्भ्यां प्रविवेश बिलं तदा
verses.transliteration:
mayā tvetadvacaḥ śrutvā yācitaḥ sa paraṁtapa
śāpayitvā ca māṁ padbhyāṁ praviveśa bilaṁ tadā

translations.english: Hearing his speech, that subduer of foes was besought by me (for permission to enter the cave along with him). But making me swear by touching his feet he entered the cave.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य प्रविष्टस्य बिलं साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः
स्थितस्य च मम द्वारि स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
tasya praviṣṭasya bilaṁ sāgraḥ saṁvatsaro gataḥ
sthitasya ca mama dvāri sa kālo vyatyavartata

translations.english: After he had entered the cave, and as I remained at its mouth, a space of over a complete year rolled away.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु नष्टं तं ज्ञात्वा स्नेहादागतसंभ्रमः
भ्रातरं न हि पश्यामि पापशङ्कि च मे मनः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu naṣṭaṁ taṁ jñātvā snehādāgatasaṁbhramaḥ
bhrātaraṁ na hi paśyāmi pāpaśaṅki ca me manaḥ

translations.english: And seized with sorrow (I reflected), 'As I do not see my brother, he must be lost—and my mind was alarmed, apprehending his death.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य बिलात्तस्माद्विनिःसृतम्
सफेनं रुधिरं रक्तमहं दृष्ट्वा सुदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
atha dīrghasya kālasya bilāttasmādviniḥsṛtam
saphenaṁ rudhiraṁ raktamahaṁ dṛṣṭvā suduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: After a long time, I saw frothy blood issuing from the cave. There at I was greatly aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
नर्दतामसुराणां च ध्वनिर्मे श्रोत्रमागतः
निरस्तस्य च संग्रामे क्रोशतो निःस्वनो गुरोः
verses.transliteration:
nardatāmasurāṇāṁ ca dhvanirme śrotramāgataḥ
nirastasya ca saṁgrāme krośato niḥsvano guroḥ

translations.english: And roars of Asuras also reached my ears; but I could not hear the cries of my superior, engaged in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं त्ववगतो बुद्ध्या चिह्नैस्तैर्भ्रातरं हतम्
पिधाय च बिलद्वारं शिलया गिरिमात्रया
शोकार्तश्चोदकं कृत्वा किष्किन्धामागतः सखे
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tvavagato buddhyā cihnaistairbhrātaraṁ hatam
pidhāya ca biladvāraṁ śilayā girimātrayā
śokārtaścodakaṁ kṛtvā kiṣkindhāmāgataḥ sakhe

translations.english: And from these signs concluding my brother to be slain, I, closing the mouth of the cavern with a crag, huge as a hill, and afflicted with grief, after performing his watery rites, came (back) to Kiskindha, O my friend. And although I carefully concealed (the matter), the counsellors heard it all.

verses.sanskrit:
मानयंस्तं महात्मानं यथावच्चाभ्यवादयम्
उक्ताश्च नाशिषस्तेन संतुष्टेनान्तरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
mānayaṁstaṁ mahātmānaṁ yathāvaccābhyavādayam
uktāśca nāśiṣastena saṁtuṣṭenāntarātmanā

translations.english: Having slain his foe, he then entered his city; and I, honouring that high-souled one, duly saluted him. He withal did not with a glad heart utter his benediction.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टं संरब्धं तमुपागतम्
अहं प्रसादयां चक्रे भ्रातरं प्रियकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaṁ saṁrabdhaṁ tamupāgatam
ahaṁ prasādayāṁ cakre bhrātaraṁ priyakāmyayā

translations.english: Then wishing for my welfare I strove to propitiate my angry brother, wrought up with wrath, who was seated (there).

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्यासि कुशली प्राप्तो निहतश्च त्वया रिपुः
अनाथस्य हि मे नाथस्त्वमेकोऽनाथनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyāsi kuśalī prāpto nihataśca tvayā ripuḥ
anāthasya hi me nāthastvameko'nāthanandanaḥ

translations.english: By good luck it is that you had come off safely; and that you had slain the foe. O you that rejoicest the forlorn, you are the only protector of me who am helpless.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं बहुशलाकं ते पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्
छत्रं सवालव्यजनं प्रतीच्छस्व मयोद्यतम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ bahuśalākaṁ te pūrṇacandramivoditam
chatraṁ savālavyajanaṁ pratīcchasva mayodyatam

translations.english: I hold this. umbrella furnished with many ribs, resembling the moon risen; as well as this chowrī containing hair,—do you accept my service.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमेव राजा मानार्हः सदा चाहं यथापुरा
न्यासभूतमिदं राज्यं तव निर्यातयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tvameva rājā mānārhaḥ sadā cāhaṁ yathāpurā
nyāsabhūtamidaṁ rājyaṁ tava niryātayāmyaham

translations.english: You are the king, O worthy of honour; and I am, as before, ever (your servant). I was entrusted with regal power in consequence of your absence. This kingdom consisting of courtiers and citizens, remains now rid of its thorns. It was established in me as a trust. And I protected it as such.

verses.sanskrit:
मा च रोषं कृथाः सौम्य मयि शत्रुनिबर्हण
याचे त्वां शिरसा राजन्मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
mā ca roṣaṁ kṛthāḥ saumya mayi śatrunibarhaṇa
yāce tvāṁ śirasā rājanmayā baddho'yamañjaliḥ

translations.english: Do not get wroth, O miid one, O destroyer of foes, I beseech you with bent head, and, O king, with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
बलादस्मि समागम्य मन्त्रिभिः पुरवासिभिः
राजभावे नियुक्तोऽहं शून्यदेशजिगीषया
verses.transliteration:
balādasmi samāgamya mantribhiḥ puravāsibhiḥ
rājabhāve niyukto'haṁ śūnyadeśajigīṣayā

translations.english: With the view of preventing any one to wish to conquer this kingdom vacant (of its ruler the citizens and counsellors unanimously, by force, entrusted me with regal authority.

verses.sanskrit:
स्निग्धमेवं ब्रुवाणं मां स तु निर्भर्त्स्य वानरः
धिक्त्वामिति च मामुक्त्वा बहु तत्तदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
snigdhamevaṁ bruvāṇaṁ māṁ sa tu nirbhartsya vānaraḥ
dhiktvāmiti ca māmuktvā bahu tattaduvāca ha

translations.english: As I said this softly, the monkey reproaching me, said to me 'Fie on you,' and censured me greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतीश्च समानीय मन्त्रिणश्चैव संमतान्
मामाह सुहृदां मध्ये वाक्यं परमगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtīśca samānīya mantriṇaścaiva saṁmatān
māmāha suhṛdāṁ madhye vākyaṁ paramagarhitam

translations.english: And bringing together the subjects and favourite counsellors, spoke to me, before friends, highly improper words.

verses.sanskrit:
विदितं वो यथा रात्रौ मायावी स महासुरः
मां समाह्वयत क्रूरो युद्धाकाङ्क्षी सुदुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
viditaṁ vo yathā rātrau māyāvī sa mahāsuraḥ
māṁ samāhvayata krūro yuddhākāṅkṣī sudurmatiḥ

translations.english: “You know that formerly one night the mighty Asura Mayavi, getting' enraged, challenged me (to a fight) desirous of an encounter with me.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्गर्जितं श्रुत्वा निःसृतोऽहं नृपालयात्
अनुयातश्च मां तूर्णमयं भ्राता सुदारुणः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadgarjitaṁ śrutvā niḥsṛto'haṁ nṛpālayāt
anuyātaśca māṁ tūrṇamayaṁ bhrātā sudāruṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing his speech I sallied out of the palace, and was followed by this horrible brother of mine.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दृष्ट्वैव मां रात्रौ सद्वितीयं महाबलः
प्राद्रवद्भयसंत्रस्तो वीक्ष्यावां तमनुद्रुतौ
अनुद्रुतस्तु वेगेन प्रविवेश महाबिलम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dṛṣṭvaiva māṁ rātrau sadvitīyaṁ mahābalaḥ
prādravadbhayasaṁtrasto vīkṣyāvāṁ tamanudrutau
anudrutastu vegena praviveśa mahābilam

translations.english: Thereat seeing me with one to assist me, and finding that we had come upon him, that mighty Asura, fled, seized with fear. And fleeing on, he (at length) swiftly entered a huge hole.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रविष्टं विदित्वा तु सुघोरं सुमहद्बिलम्
अयमुक्तोऽथ मे भ्राता मया तु क्रूरदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ praviṣṭaṁ viditvā tu sughoraṁ sumahadbilam
ayamukto'tha me bhrātā mayā tu krūradarśanaḥ

translations.english: Knowing that he had entered that dreadful and large cave, I spoke to my brother of a crooked presence.

verses.sanskrit:
अहत्वा नास्ति मे शक्तिः प्रतिगन्तुमितः पुरीम्
बिलद्वारि प्रतीक्ष त्वं यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
ahatvā nāsti me śaktiḥ pratigantumitaḥ purīm
biladvāri pratīkṣa tvaṁ yāvadenaṁ nihanmyaham

translations.english: Without slaying (this Asura) I cannot return to the palace. Do you wait at the mouth of the cave while I slay him.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थितोऽयमिति मत्वा तु प्रविष्टोऽहं दुरासदम्
तं च मे मार्गमाणस्य गतः संवत्सरस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
sthito'yamiti matvā tu praviṣṭo'haṁ durāsadam
taṁ ca me mārgamāṇasya gataḥ saṁvatsarastadā

translations.english: This one is stationed here-thinking thus, I entered that inaccessible cave. And as I searched (for the Asura), one entire year passed away.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दृष्टो मया शत्रुरनिर्वेदाद्भयावहः
निहतश्च मया तत्र सोऽसुरो बन्धुभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dṛṣṭo mayā śatruranirvedādbhayāvahaḥ
nihataśca mayā tatra so'suro bandhubhiḥ saha

translations.english: That wicked wight who had roused my alarm in consequence of his disappearance, was (at length) slain by me in one day, along with his friends.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्यात्तु प्रवृत्तेन रुधिरौघेण तद्बिलम्
पूर्णमासीद्दुराक्रामं स्तनतस्तस्य भूतले
verses.transliteration:
tasyāsyāttu pravṛttena rudhiraugheṇa tadbilam
pūrṇamāsīddurākrāmaṁ stanatastasya bhūtale

translations.english: Then as he emitted yells in the subterranean region, the cave was filled with his blood and it became difficult to come out of it.

verses.sanskrit:
सूदयित्वा तु तं शत्रुं विक्रान्तं दुन्दुभेः सुतम्
निष्क्रामन्नेव पश्यामि बिलस्य पिहितं मुखम्
verses.transliteration:
sūdayitvā tu taṁ śatruṁ vikrāntaṁ dundubheḥ sutam
niṣkrāmanneva paśyāmi bilasya pihitaṁ mukham

translations.english: Having with ease slain my powerful foe, I could not find the outlet of the cavern, its mouth having been closed.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रोशमानस्य तु मे सुग्रीवेति पुनः पुनः
यदा प्रतिवचो नास्ति ततोऽहं भृशदुःखितः
verses.transliteration:
vikrośamānasya tu me sugrīveti punaḥ punaḥ
yadā prativaco nāsti tato'haṁ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ

translations.english: Then as I again and again cried Sugrīva, Sugrīva, I became exceedingly sorry for not receiving any reply.

verses.sanskrit:
पादप्रहारैस्तु मया बहुशस्तद्विदारितम्
ततोऽहं तेन निष्क्रम्य यथा पुनरुपागतः
verses.transliteration:
pādaprahāraistu mayā bahuśastadvidāritam
tato'haṁ tena niṣkramya yathā punarupāgataḥ

translations.english: Thereat I threw down the stone after striking it many times with my legs. Then coming out by its mouth, I have come to this city.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रानेनास्मि संरुद्धो राज्यं मार्गयतात्मनः
सुग्रीवेण नृशंसेन विस्मृत्य भ्रातृसौहृदम्
verses.transliteration:
tatrānenāsmi saṁruddho rājyaṁ mārgayatātmanaḥ
sugrīveṇa nṛśaṁsena vismṛtya bhrātṛsauhṛdam

translations.english: Seeking my kingdom, the crafty Sugrīva had shut me up there forgetting fraternal love.'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु मां तत्र वस्त्रेणैकेन वानरः
तदा निर्वासयामास वाली विगतसाध्वसः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu māṁ tatra vastreṇaikena vānaraḥ
tadā nirvāsayāmāsa vālī vigatasādhvasaḥ

translations.english: Saying this, that monkey, the shameless Vali, exiled me with a single cloth on.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यमूकं गिरिवरं भार्याहरणदुःखितः
प्रविष्टोऽस्मि दुराधर्षं वालिनः कारणान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyamūkaṁ girivaraṁ bhāryāharaṇaduḥkhitaḥ
praviṣṭo'smi durādharṣaṁ vālinaḥ kāraṇāntare

translations.english: O Rāghava, I have been discomfited by him, and been deprived of my wife. And from fear of him, I have wandered over the whole earth having forest and seas. And aggrieved in consequence of my having been deprived of my wife. I have (at length) entered this best of mountains, Rsyamuka, which for a certain reason* is incapable of being approached by Vali. *In consequence of Matanga's curse.
