verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं वैरानुकथनं महत्
अनागसा मया प्राप्तं व्यसनं पश्य राघव
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ vairānukathanaṁ mahat
anāgasā mayā prāptaṁ vyasanaṁ paśya rāghava

translations.english: Thus have I mentioned to you the great cause of this hostility, O Rāghava, innocent as I am, I have come by this mighty misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
वालिनस्तु भयार्तस्य सर्वलोकाभयंकर
कर्तुमर्हसि मे वीर प्रसादं तस्य निग्रहात्
verses.transliteration:
vālinastu bhayārtasya sarvalokābhayaṁkara
kartumarhasi me vīra prasādaṁ tasya nigrahāt

translations.english: O you that inspirest the fear of all creatures, by chastising Vāli it behoveth you to grant your grace to me, who am tormented with fear in connection with Vali, O hero.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः स तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्मसंहितम्
वचनं वक्तुमारेभे सुग्रीवं प्रहसन्निव
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ sa tejasvī dharmajño dharmasaṁhitam
vacanaṁ vaktumārebhe sugrīvaṁ prahasanniva

translations.english: Thus accosted, that energetic one knowing righteousness, smiling, began to address Sugrīva in words fraught with morality.

verses.sanskrit:
अमोघाः सूर्यसंकाशा ममेमे निशिताः शराः
तस्मिन्वालिनि दुर्वृत्ते पतिष्यन्ति रुषान्विताः
verses.transliteration:
amoghāḥ sūryasaṁkāśā mameme niśitāḥ śarāḥ
tasminvālini durvṛtte patiṣyanti ruṣānvitāḥ

translations.english: These sharpened shafts of mine, resembling the sun, and never missing, shall furiously fall upon the wicked Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्तं न हि पश्येयं तव भार्यापहारिणम्
तावत्स जीवेत्पापात्मा वाली चारित्रदूषकः
verses.transliteration:
yāvattaṁ na hi paśyeyaṁ tava bhāryāpahāriṇam
tāvatsa jīvetpāpātmā vālī cāritradūṣakaḥ

translations.english: So long as you did not see that stealer of your wife, so long only shall the impious Väli of vile character, live.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानुमानात्पश्यामि मग्नं त्वां शोकसागरे
त्वामहं तारयिष्यामि कामं प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलम्
verses.transliteration:
ātmānumānātpaśyāmi magnaṁ tvāṁ śokasāgare
tvāmahaṁ tārayiṣyāmi kāmaṁ prāpsyasi puṣkalam

translations.english: By what I myself feel, I see that you had sunk in a sea of sorrow. But I will deliver you; and you shall attain both your wife as well as this kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षपौरुषवर्धनम्
सुग्रीवः पूजयां चक्रे राघवं प्रशशंस च
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā harṣapauruṣavardhanam
sugrīvaḥ pūjayāṁ cakre rāghavaṁ praśaśaṁsa ca

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words capable of enhancing joy and manliness, Sugrīva highly honoured the former and extolled him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
असंशयं प्रज्वलितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्मातिगैः शरैः
त्वं दहेः कुपितो लोकान्युगान्त इव भास्करः
verses.transliteration:
asaṁśayaṁ prajvalitaistīkṣṇairmarmātigaiḥ śaraiḥ
tvaṁ daheḥ kupito lokānyugānta iva bhāskaraḥ

translations.english: Enraged, you, with your sharp and flaming shafts, capable of piercing into the vitals, canst burn up the worlds, like the sun at the universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
वालिनः पौरुषं यत्तद्यच्च वीर्यं धृतिश्च या
तन्ममैकमनाः श्रुत्वा विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
vālinaḥ pauruṣaṁ yattadyacca vīryaṁ dhṛtiśca yā
tanmamaikamanāḥ śrutvā vidhatsva yadanantaram

translations.english: Heedfully hearing from me of Vali's strength, prowess and fortitude, do you afterwards, ascertain what is fit.

verses.sanskrit:
समुद्रात्पश्चिमात्पूर्वं दक्षिणादपि चोत्तरम्
क्रामत्यनुदिते सूर्ये वाली व्यपगतक्लमः
verses.transliteration:
samudrātpaścimātpūrvaṁ dakṣiṇādapi cottaram
krāmatyanudite sūrye vālī vyapagataklamaḥ

translations.english: Before the sun rises, Vāli can easily range the ocean from west to east and from south to north.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्राण्यारुह्य शैलानां शिखराणि महान्त्यपि
ऊर्ध्वमुत्क्षिप्य तरसा प्रतिगृह्णाति वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
agrāṇyāruhya śailānāṁ śikharāṇi mahāntyapi
ūrdhvamutkṣipya tarasā pratigṛhṇāti vīryavān

translations.english: Ascending the tops of mountains, Vāli possessed of prowess throws up their summits, and then again swiftly holds them.

verses.sanskrit:
बहवः सारवन्तश्च वनेषु विविधा द्रुमाः
वालिना तरसा भग्ना बलं प्रथयतात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
bahavaḥ sāravantaśca vaneṣu vividhā drumāḥ
vālinā tarasā bhagnā balaṁ prathayatātmanaḥ

translations.english: And displaying his strength, Vāli vehemently crushes in the woods various stout trees.

verses.sanskrit:
महिषो दुन्दुभिर्नाम कैलासशिखरप्रभः
बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयामास वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
mahiṣo dundubhirnāma kailāsaśikharaprabhaḥ
balaṁ nāgasahasrasya dhārayāmāsa vīryavān

translations.english: There was one assuming the shape of buffalo named Dundubhi, resembling in splendour the summit of Kailasa. That one possessed of prowess had the strength of an hundred elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
वीर्योत्सेकेन दुष्टात्मा वरदानाच्च मोहितः
जगाम स महाकायः समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vīryotsekena duṣṭātmā varadānācca mohitaḥ
jagāma sa mahākāyaḥ samudraṁ saritāṁ patim

translations.english: That wicked one of a gigantic body inflated by his prowess and blinded by the boon he had received once went to that lord of streams—the Sea.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊर्मिमन्तमतिक्रम्य सागरं रत्नसंचयम्
मम युद्धं प्रयच्छेति तमुवाच महार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
ūrmimantamatikramya sāgaraṁ ratnasaṁcayam
mama yuddhaṁ prayaccheti tamuvāca mahārṇavam

translations.english: Passing beyond the Sea, with waves upon him, and containing heaps of gemsji e said to the mighty deep-Grant me battle.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समुद्रो धर्मात्मा समुत्थाय महाबलः
अब्रवीद्वचनं राजन्नसुरं कालचोदितम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samudro dharmātmā samutthāya mahābalaḥ
abravīdvacanaṁ rājannasuraṁ kālacoditam

translations.english: Thereat the righteous-souled and mighty Ocean arose and, O king, said these words to that Asura, who had been urged by Death.

verses.sanskrit:
समर्थो नास्मि ते दातुं युद्धं युद्धविशारद
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि यस्ते युद्धं प्रदास्यति
verses.transliteration:
samartho nāsmi te dātuṁ yuddhaṁ yuddhaviśārada
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi yaste yuddhaṁ pradāsyati

translations.english: O you that are skilled in fight, I am not competent to offer you fight; but lister to me who will tell you who shall offer the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलराजो महारण्ये तपस्विशरणं परम्
शंकरश्वशुरो नाम्ना हिमवानिति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
śailarājo mahāraṇye tapasviśaraṇaṁ param
śaṁkaraśvaśuro nāmnā himavāniti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: There is a monarch of mountains in a mighty forest,—the great refuge of asceticism, the worker of the weal (of all), an Asura, celebrated by the name of Himavān containing great cascades and furnished with many fountains and caves. He can compass your incomparable pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तस्य गिरेः श्वेता गजेन्द्रविपुलाः शिलाः
चिक्षेप बहुधा भूमौ दुन्दुभिर्विननाद च
verses.transliteration:
tatastasya gireḥ śvetā gajendravipulāḥ śilāḥ
cikṣepa bahudhā bhūmau dundubhirvinanāda ca

translations.english: Concluding that the ocean was afraid, that foremost of Asuras, presented himself in the wood of Himavān, like a shaft shot from a bow. Thereupon Dundhubhi began to throw down many white crags resembling the foremost of elephants; and sent up shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः श्वेताम्बुदाकारः सौम्यः प्रीतिकराकृतिः
हिमवानब्रवीद्वाक्यं स्व एव शिखरे स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śvetāmbudākāraḥ saumyaḥ prītikarākṛtiḥ
himavānabravīdvākyaṁ sva eva śikhare sthitaḥ

translations.english: Then resembling white clouds, mild and possessed of a pleasing shape, Himavan, stationed on the summit, spoke,

verses.sanskrit:
क्लेष्टुमर्हसि मां न त्वं दुन्दुभे धर्मवत्सल
रणकर्मस्वकुशलस्तपस्विशरणं ह्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
kleṣṭumarhasi māṁ na tvaṁ dundubhe dharmavatsala
raṇakarmasvakuśalastapasviśaraṇaṁ hyaham

translations.english: O Dundhubhi, O you that are attached to righteousness, it behoveth you not to distress me. I am the refuge of all those ascetics who are not expert in military arts.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा गिरिराजस्य धीमतः
उवाच दुन्दुभिर्वाक्यं क्रोधात्संरक्तलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā girirājasya dhīmataḥ
uvāca dundubhirvākyaṁ krodhātsaṁraktalocanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of that intelligent lord of mountains Dundhubhi, with reddened eyes, said.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि युद्धेऽसमर्थस्त्वं मद्भयाद्वा निरुद्यमः
तमाचक्ष्व प्रदद्यान्मे योऽद्य युद्धं युयुत्सतः
verses.transliteration:
yadi yuddhe'samarthastvaṁ madbhayādvā nirudyamaḥ
tamācakṣva pradadyānme yo'dya yuddhaṁ yuyutsataḥ

translations.english: Afraid of me and hence void of energy if you are incapable of fighting with me, do you name him who is ready to fight with me who am desirous of entering into conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
हिमवानब्रवीद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वाक्यविशारदः
अनुक्तपूर्वं धर्मात्मा क्रोधात्तमसुरोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
himavānabravīdvākyaṁ śrutvā vākyaviśāradaḥ
anuktapūrvaṁ dharmātmā krodhāttamasurottamam

translations.english: Hearing these words the virtuous-souled Himavān, skilled in speech, spoke to that great Asura, exercised with ire.

verses.sanskrit:
वाली नाम महाप्राज्ञः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः
अध्यास्ते वानरः श्रीमान्किष्किन्धामतुलप्रभाम्
verses.transliteration:
vālī nāma mahāprājñaḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ
adhyāste vānaraḥ śrīmānkiṣkindhāmatulaprabhām

translations.english: O greatly wise one, there lives in Kişkindhā, of incomparable beauty, the mighty and highly graceful monkey—the son of Sakra, by name Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
स समर्थो महाप्राज्ञस्तव युद्धविशारदः
द्वन्द्वयुद्धं महद्दातुं नमुचेरिव वासवः
verses.transliteration:
sa samartho mahāprājñastava yuddhaviśāradaḥ
dvandvayuddhaṁ mahaddātuṁ namuceriva vāsavaḥ

translations.english: That mighty wise one, skilled in warfare, is capable of fighting with you on equal terms like to Namuci with Vasava.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शीघ्रमभिगच्छ त्वं यदि युद्धमिहेच्छसि
स हि दुर्धर्षणो नित्यं शूरः समरकर्मणि
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śīghramabhigaccha tvaṁ yadi yuddhamihecchasi
sa hi durdharṣaṇo nityaṁ śūraḥ samarakarmaṇi

translations.english: Do you speedily repair to him if did you wish for a conflict. He is always expert in military exploits and is hard to repress.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा हिमवतो वाक्यं क्रोधाविष्टः स दुन्दुभिः
जगाम तां पुरीं तस्य किष्किन्धां वालिनस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā himavato vākyaṁ krodhāviṣṭaḥ sa dundubhiḥ
jagāma tāṁ purīṁ tasya kiṣkindhāṁ vālinastadā

translations.english: Hearing Himavān's Himavān's words, Dundhubhi, inflamed with ire, went to Kişkindhā—Vāli's capital.

verses.sanskrit:
धारयन्माहिषं रूपं तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो भयावहः
प्रावृषीव महामेघस्तोयपूर्णो नभस्तले
verses.transliteration:
dhārayanmāhiṣaṁ rūpaṁ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo bhayāvahaḥ
prāvṛṣīva mahāmeghastoyapūrṇo nabhastale

translations.english: Assuming the figure of a terrible buffalo, with sharpened horns like to a cloud big with water, ranging on the sky in the rainy season, and approaching the gate of Kişkindhā that highly powerful one set up a terrible roar, shaking the earth like to the sound of a kettle-drum.

verses.sanskrit:
समीपजान्द्रुमान्भञ्जन्वसुधां दारयन्खुरैः
विषाणेनोल्लेखन्दर्पात्तद्द्वारं द्विरदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
samīpajāndrumānbhañjanvasudhāṁ dārayankhuraiḥ
viṣāṇenollekhandarpāttaddvāraṁ dvirado yathā

translations.english: Like to an elephant he felled, out of haughtiness, the trees around, and rent the earth with his hoofs scraping it with his horns.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःपुरगतो वाली श्रुत्वा शब्दममर्षणः
निष्पपात सह स्त्रीभिस्ताराभिरिव चन्द्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
antaḥpuragato vālī śrutvā śabdamamarṣaṇaḥ
niṣpapāta saha strībhistārābhiriva candramāḥ

translations.english: Vāli was in the female-apartment at that time, and unable to bear the sound came out with his wives like to the Moon with stars.

verses.sanskrit:
मितं व्यक्ताक्षरपदं तमुवाच स दुन्दुभिम्
हरीणामीश्वरो वाली सर्वेषां वनचारिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
mitaṁ vyaktākṣarapadaṁ tamuvāca sa dundubhim
harīṇāmīśvaro vālī sarveṣāṁ vanacāriṇām

translations.english: Thereupon thạt lord of monkeys and other wild anànals, spoke openly to Dundhubhi, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
किमर्थं नगरद्वारमिदं रुद्ध्वा विनर्दसि
दुन्दुभे विदितो मेऽसि रक्ष प्राणान्महाबल
verses.transliteration:
kimarthaṁ nagaradvāramidaṁ ruddhvā vinardasi
dundubhe vidito me'si rakṣa prāṇānmahābala

translations.english: O Dundhubhi, obstructing this my city-gate, why did you set up a terrible roar? Did you know my mighty strength? Do you save your own life.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्य धीमतः
उवाच दुन्दुभिर्वाक्यं क्रोधात्संरक्तलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vānarendrasya dhīmataḥ
uvāca dundubhirvākyaṁ krodhātsaṁraktalocanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of that intelligent lord of monkeys, Dundhubhi, with reddened eyes spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वं स्त्रीसंनिधौ वीर वचनं वक्तुमर्हसि
मम युद्धं प्रयच्छ त्वं ततो ज्ञास्यामि ते बलम्
verses.transliteration:
na tvaṁ strīsaṁnidhau vīra vacanaṁ vaktumarhasi
mama yuddhaṁ prayaccha tvaṁ tato jñāsyāmi te balam

translations.english: O hero, it becomes you not to speak thus before your wives. Do you enter into conflict with me and your prowess shall be ascertained thereafter.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा धारयिष्यामि क्रोधमद्य निशामिमाम्
गृह्यतामुदयः स्वैरं कामभोगेषु वानर
verses.transliteration:
atha vā dhārayiṣyāmi krodhamadya niśāmimām
gṛhyatāmudayaḥ svairaṁ kāmabhogeṣu vānara

translations.english: Or I shall suppress my wrath for this night and do you, O monkey, enjoy till the rise of the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि मत्तं प्रमत्तं वा सुप्तं वा रहितं भृशम्
हन्यात्स भ्रूणहा लोके त्वद्विधं मदमोहितम्
verses.transliteration:
yo hi mattaṁ pramattaṁ vā suptaṁ vā rahitaṁ bhṛśam
hanyātsa bhrūṇahā loke tvadvidhaṁ madamohitam

translations.english: He, who destroyeth a person who is given up to drinking, reckless, emaciated and deprived of weapons, and one like you, sunk in the abyss of voluptuousness, committeth the sin consequent upon the destruction of an embryo,

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रहस्याब्रवीन्मन्दं क्रोधात्तमसुरोत्तमम्
विसृज्य ताः स्त्रियः सर्वास्ताराप्रभृतिकास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
sa prahasyābravīnmandaṁ krodhāttamasurottamam
visṛjya tāḥ striyaḥ sarvāstārāprabhṛtikāstadā

translations.english: Where to replied Vāli, laughing, to that wicked lord of Asuras, leaving aside all his wives, headed by Tārā.

verses.sanskrit:
मत्तोऽयमिति मा मंस्था यद्यभीतोऽसि संयुगे
मदोऽयं संप्रहारेऽस्मिन्वीरपानं समर्थ्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
matto'yamiti mā maṁsthā yadyabhīto'si saṁyuge
mado'yaṁ saṁprahāre'sminvīrapānaṁ samarthyatām

translations.english: If you are not afraid of fighting, do not consider me as one given up to drinking only. Do you regard this my attachment as a draught in this conflict, to be drunk by the heroes.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमुक्त्वा संक्रुद्धो मालामुत्क्षिप्य काञ्चनीम्
पित्रा दत्तां महेन्द्रेण युद्धाय व्यवतिष्ठत
verses.transliteration:
tamevamuktvā saṁkruddho mālāmutkṣipya kāñcanīm
pitrā dattāṁ mahendreṇa yuddhāya vyavatiṣṭhata

translations.english: Saying this, Vāli, taking his golden garland, conferred on him by his father Mahendra, addressed himself for the conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
विषाणयोर्गृहीत्वा तं दुन्दुभिं गिरिसंनिभम्
वाली व्यापातयां चक्रे ननर्द च महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
viṣāṇayorgṛhītvā taṁ dundubhiṁ girisaṁnibham
vālī vyāpātayāṁ cakre nanarda ca mahāsvanam

translations.english: Holding him by the horns, Vāli, that lord of monkeys, setting up a terrible roar, hurled Dundhubhi resembling a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
युद्धे प्राणहरे तस्मिन्निष्पिष्टो दुन्दुभिस्तदा
श्रोत्राभ्यामथ रक्तं तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः
पपात च महाकायः क्षितौ पञ्चत्वमागतः
verses.transliteration:
yuddhe prāṇahare tasminniṣpiṣṭo dundubhistadā
śrotrābhyāmatha raktaṁ tu tasya susrāva pātyataḥ
papāta ca mahākāyaḥ kṣitau pañcatvamāgataḥ

translations.english: There was a profusion of blood falling from the ears of that one crushed down. Thereupon that one of mighty arms fell down to the earth and breathed his last.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तोलयित्वा बाहुभ्यां गतसत्त्वमचेतनम्
चिक्षेप वेगवान्वाली वेगेनैकेन योजनम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tolayitvā bāhubhyāṁ gatasattvamacetanam
cikṣepa vegavānvālī vegenaikena yojanam

translations.english: And taking up with his arms that lifeless one, the mighty Vāli hurled him with great force at distance of a Yojana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य वेगप्रविद्धस्य वक्त्रात्क्षतजबिन्दवः
प्रपेतुर्मारुतोत्क्षिप्ता मतङ्गस्याश्रमं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
tasya vegapraviddhasya vaktrātkṣatajabindavaḥ
prapeturmārutotkṣiptā mataṅgasyāśramaṁ prati

translations.english: While thus thrown down by force, drops of blood, falling from his mouth, driven by the wind, fell upon the asylum of the great Saint Matanga.

verses.sanskrit: स महर्षिं समासाद्य याचते स्म कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration: sa maharṣiṁ samāsādya yācate sma kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words, Vāli approached that great ascetic and solicited him with folded hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याप्रवेशं ज्ञात्वाहमिदं राम महावनम्
विचरामि सहामात्यो विषादेन विवर्जितः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāpraveśaṁ jñātvāhamidaṁ rāma mahāvanam
vicarāmi sahāmātyo viṣādena vivarjitaḥ

translations.english: O Lord of men, afraid of the curse that monkey chief purposed to repair to the mount Rş yamuka. Knowing for certain, O Rāma, that he shall not enter this forest, I have been living here with my ministers, devoid of fear and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
एषोऽस्थिनिचयस्तस्य दुन्दुभेः संप्रकाशते
वीर्योत्सेकान्निरस्तस्य गिरिकूटनिभो महान्
verses.transliteration:
eṣo'sthinicayastasya dundubheḥ saṁprakāśate
vīryotsekānnirastasya girikūṭanibho mahān

translations.english: Here is the collection of Dundhuvi's bones, killed on account of his own haughtiness, resembling a huge mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे च विपुलाः सालाः सप्त शाखावलम्बिनः
यत्रैकं घटते वाली निष्पत्रयितुमोजसा
verses.transliteration:
ime ca vipulāḥ sālāḥ sapta śākhāvalambinaḥ
yatraikaṁ ghaṭate vālī niṣpatrayitumojasā

translations.english: These are the seven huge Sāla trees, clothed in branches, which Vāli could simultaneously divest of leaves by virtue of his prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदस्यासमं वीर्यं मया राम प्रकाशितम्
कथं तं वालिनं हन्तुं समरे शक्ष्यसे नृप
verses.transliteration:
etadasyāsamaṁ vīryaṁ mayā rāma prakāśitam
kathaṁ taṁ vālinaṁ hantuṁ samare śakṣyase nṛpa

translations.english: I have related to you, O Rāma, the incomparable prowess of his. Do you tell me now, O hero, how canst you destroy him in the conflict?

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
राघवो दुन्दुभेः कायं पादाङ्गुष्ठेन लीलया
तोलयित्वा महाबाहुश्चिक्षेप दशयोजनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
rāghavo dundubheḥ kāyaṁ pādāṅguṣṭhena līlayā
tolayitvā mahābāhuścikṣepa daśayojanam

translations.english: Having thus addressed Sugrīva and consoling him, the highly powerful Raghava, of mighty arms-Laksmana's elder brother, lifting up easily with his thumb the dried frame of that Asura-Dundhubhi-hurled it at a distance of ten Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्तं दृष्ट्वा ततः कायं सुग्रीवः पुनरब्रवीत्
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो राममिदं वचनमर्थवत्
verses.transliteration:
kṣiptaṁ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ kāyaṁ sugrīvaḥ punarabravīt
lakṣmaṇasyāgrato rāmamidaṁ vacanamarthavat

translations.english: Beholding that Asura's body thrown thus, Sugrīva, again addressed to the heroic Rāma, before Lakşmaņa and the monkey herd, the following pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्द्रः समांसप्रत्यग्रः क्षिप्तः कायः पुरा सखे
लघुः संप्रति निर्मांसस्तृणभूतश्च राघव
नात्र शक्यं बलं ज्ञातुं तव वा तस्य वाधिकम्
verses.transliteration:
ārdraḥ samāṁsapratyagraḥ kṣiptaḥ kāyaḥ purā sakhe
laghuḥ saṁprati nirmāṁsastṛṇabhūtaśca rāghava
nātra śakyaṁ balaṁ jñātuṁ tava vā tasya vādhikam

translations.english: Friend, formerly this body was wet and corpulent, and it was thrown with great difficulty by my brother Vāli, mad with voluptuousness.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्च वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवेण सुभाषितम्
प्रत्ययार्थं महातेजा रामो जग्राह कार्मुकम्
verses.transliteration:
etacca vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīveṇa subhāṣitam
pratyayārthaṁ mahātejā rāmo jagrāha kārmukam

translations.english: Hearing those pleasant words of Sugrīva, the highly effulgent Rāma, to create his confidence, took up his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
स गृहीत्वा धनुर्घोरं शरमेकं च मानदः
सालानुद्दिश्य चिक्षेप ज्यास्वनैः पूरयन्दिशः
verses.transliteration:
sa gṛhītvā dhanurghoraṁ śaramekaṁ ca mānadaḥ
sālānuddiśya cikṣepa jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayandiśaḥ

translations.english: That one, conferring honours upon others, holding his terrible bow and a shaft, darted it towards the Sāla, filling all the quarters with a sound,

verses.sanskrit:
स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणः स्वर्णपरिष्कृतः
भित्त्वा सालान्गिरिप्रस्थे सप्त भूमिं विवेश ह
verses.transliteration:
sa visṛṣṭo balavatā bāṇaḥ svarṇapariṣkṛtaḥ
bhittvā sālāngiriprasthe sapta bhūmiṁ viveśa ha

translations.english: The arrow, clear as the gold itself, hurled by that one of mighty strength, perforating the trees, entered into the mountainous expanse and the sevenfold regions of the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टस्तु मुहूर्तेन रसां भित्त्वा महाजवः
निष्पत्य च पुनस्तूर्णं स्वतूणीं प्रविवेश ह
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭastu muhūrtena rasāṁ bhittvā mahājavaḥ
niṣpatya ca punastūrṇaṁ svatūṇīṁ praviveśa ha

translations.english: And that shaft, gifted with wonderful velocity, piercing all the trees entered again into the quiver.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्दृष्ट्वा सप्त निर्भिन्नान्सालान्वानरपुंगवः
रामस्य शरवेगेन विस्मयं परमं गतः
verses.transliteration:
tāndṛṣṭvā sapta nirbhinnānsālānvānarapuṁgavaḥ
rāmasya śaravegena vismayaṁ paramaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Having beheld those seven trees bored by Rāma's arrow, that monkey chief attained to an excess of surprise.

verses.sanskrit:
स मूर्ध्ना न्यपतद्भूमौ प्रलम्बीकृतभूषणः
सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो राघवाय कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
sa mūrdhnā nyapatadbhūmau pralambīkṛtabhūṣaṇaḥ
sugrīvaḥ paramaprīto rāghavāya kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Sugrīva, exceedingly glad, and delighted with his actions, bowing down his head on the earth and stretching his ornamented person on the ground, addressed with clasped hands, that heroic descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं चोवाच धर्मज्ञं कर्मणा तेन हर्षितः
रामं सर्वास्त्रविदुषां श्रेष्ठं शूरमवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ covāca dharmajñaṁ karmaṇā tena harṣitaḥ
rāmaṁ sarvāstraviduṣāṁ śreṣṭhaṁ śūramavasthitam

translations.english: Rāma, the foremost of those conversant with religious lore, with the following pious words.

verses.sanskrit:
सेन्द्रानपि सुरान्सर्वांस्त्वं बाणैः पुरुषर्षभ
समर्थः समरे हन्तुं किं पुनर्वालिनं प्रभो
verses.transliteration:
sendrānapi surānsarvāṁstvaṁ bāṇaiḥ puruṣarṣabha
samarthaḥ samare hantuṁ kiṁ punarvālinaṁ prabho

translations.english: O best of men, O lord, what of Vali, you are capable of destroying with your arrows, in the conflict, even the celestials headed by Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
येन सप्त महासाला गिरिर्भूमिश्च दारिताः
बाणेनैकेन काकुत्स्थ स्थाता ते को रणाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
yena sapta mahāsālā girirbhūmiśca dāritāḥ
bāṇenaikena kākutstha sthātā te ko raṇāgrataḥ

translations.english: O Kākutstha, who can stand before you in a battle, who has pierced the seven trees, and the mountain, and the earth with one arrow?

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य मे विगतः शोकः प्रीतिरद्य परा मम
सुहृदं त्वां समासाद्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
adya me vigataḥ śokaḥ prītiradya parā mama
suhṛdaṁ tvāṁ samāsādya mahendravaruṇopamam

translations.english: Obtaining you as my friend like to Mahendra and Varuņa, my grief has been removed and I have attained to an excess of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
तमद्यैव प्रियार्थं मे वैरिणं भ्रातृरूपिणम्
वालिनं जहि काकुत्स्थ मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
tamadyaiva priyārthaṁ me vairiṇaṁ bhrātṛrūpiṇam
vālinaṁ jahi kākutstha mayā baddho'yamañjaliḥ

translations.english: Do you, O Kākutstha, even to-day destroy, for my welfare, my brother Vāli. This I do pray to you with folded hands.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामः परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणानुमतं वचः
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmaḥ pariṣvajya sugrīvaṁ priyadarśanam
pratyuvāca mahāprājño lakṣmaṇānumataṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon embracing Sugrīva, of a pleasant countenance and like to Lakşmaņa, the highly wise Rāma spoke to him, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माद्गच्छाम किष्किन्धां क्षिप्रं गच्छ त्वमग्रतः
गत्वा चाह्वय सुग्रीव वालिनं भ्रातृगन्धिनम्
verses.transliteration:
asmādgacchāma kiṣkindhāṁ kṣipraṁ gaccha tvamagrataḥ
gatvā cāhvaya sugrīva vālinaṁ bhrātṛgandhinam

translations.english: Soon shall we repair to Kiskindha.-Do you go before, O Sugriva, and invite your false brother, Vali, to battle.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम्
वृक्षैरात्मानमावृत्य व्यतिष्ठन्गहने वने
verses.transliteration:
sarve te tvaritaṁ gatvā kiṣkindhāṁ vālinaḥ purīm
vṛkṣairātmānamāvṛtya vyatiṣṭhangahane vane

translations.english: They all, repairing quickly to Kiskindha, Vāli's capital stood waiting in the dense forest, hiding themselves behind the trees.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवो व्यनदद्घोरं वालिनो ह्वानकारणात्
गाढं परिहितो वेगान्नादैर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvo vyanadadghoraṁ vālino hvānakāraṇāt
gāḍhaṁ parihito vegānnādairbhindannivāmbaram

translations.english: With a view to call Vāli, Sugrīva, tying fast his cloth (around the waist) set up a terrible roar, as if rending the sky (therewith).

verses.sanskrit:
तं श्रुत्वा निनदं भ्रातुः क्रुद्धो वाली महाबलः
निष्पपात सुसंरब्धो भास्करोऽस्ततटादिव
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śrutvā ninadaṁ bhrātuḥ kruddho vālī mahābalaḥ
niṣpapāta susaṁrabdho bhāskaro'stataṭādiva

translations.english: Hearing the terrible uproar of his brother, the mighty Vāli, highly angered, issued out of his city, like to the Sun from the western shores (where he sets).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुतुमुलं युद्धं वालिसुग्रीवयोरभूत्
गगने ग्रहयोर्घोरं बुधाङ्गारकयोरिव
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sutumulaṁ yuddhaṁ vālisugrīvayorabhūt
gagane grahayorghoraṁ budhāṅgārakayoriva

translations.english: Thereupon there arose a mighty conflict between Vāli and Sugrīva like to the planets Mercury and Mars fighting with each other on the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तलैरशनिकल्पैश्च वज्रकल्पैश्च मुष्टिभिः
जघ्नतुः समरेऽन्योन्यं भ्रातरौ क्रोधमूर्छितौ
verses.transliteration:
talairaśanikalpaiśca vajrakalpaiśca muṣṭibhiḥ
jaghnatuḥ samare'nyonyaṁ bhrātarau krodhamūrchitau

translations.english: The two brothers, exercised with ire, struck each other with palms like to Asani and with fists resembling adamant.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामो धनुष्पाणिस्तावुभौ समुदीक्ष्य तु
अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरावुभौ देवाविवाश्विनौ
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇistāvubhau samudīkṣya tu
anyonyasadṛśau vīrāvubhau devāvivāśvinau

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma, with bow in hand, beheld those two heroes resembling each other, like to two Aświns.

verses.sanskrit:
यन्नावगच्छत्सुग्रीवं वालिनं वापि राघवः
ततो न कृतवान्बुद्धिं मोक्तुमन्तकरं शरम्
verses.transliteration:
yannāvagacchatsugrīvaṁ vālinaṁ vāpi rāghavaḥ
tato na kṛtavānbuddhiṁ moktumantakaraṁ śaram

translations.english: And Rāghava did not discharge that mortal shaft until he could perfectly ascertain who was Vāli and who was Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भग्नः सुग्रीवस्तेन वालिना
अपश्यन्राघवं नाथमृश्यमूकं प्रदुद्रुवे
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare bhagnaḥ sugrīvastena vālinā
apaśyanrāghavaṁ nāthamṛśyamūkaṁ pradudruve

translations.english: In the mean time, being defeated by Vāli, Sugrīva fled away and not beholding Rāghava, proceeded towards Rșyamuka.

verses.sanskrit:
क्लान्तो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः
वालिनाभिद्रुतः क्रोधात्प्रविवेश महावनम्
verses.transliteration:
klānto rudhirasiktāṅgaḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtaḥ
vālinābhidrutaḥ krodhātpraviveśa mahāvanam

translations.english: And wearied, worn out with blows, and having his person bathed in blood, he, followed by Vāli, angered, entered that mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रविष्टं वनं दृष्ट्वा वाली शापभयात्ततः
मुक्तो ह्यसि त्वमित्युक्त्वा स निवृत्तो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ praviṣṭaṁ vanaṁ dṛṣṭvā vālī śāpabhayāttataḥ
mukto hyasi tvamityuktvā sa nivṛtto mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Beholding him enter that forest, the highly powerful Vâli could not pursue him there for fear of the curse but said:-You are released today

verses.sanskrit:
राघवोऽपि सह भ्रात्रा सह चैव हनूमता
तदेव वनमागच्छत्सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavo'pi saha bhrātrā saha caiva hanūmatā
tadeva vanamāgacchatsugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ

translations.english: And Rāghava too, with his brother and Hanumān, entered that forest, where the monkey chief Sugrīva was.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समीक्ष्यागतं रामं सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणम्
ह्रीमान्दीनमुवाचेदं वसुधामवलोकयन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samīkṣyāgataṁ rāmaṁ sugrīvaḥ sahalakṣmaṇam
hrīmāndīnamuvācedaṁ vasudhāmavalokayan

translations.english: Beholding Rāma approach with Lakşmaņa, Sugrīva, stricken with shame and casting his looks on the earth, addressed him poorly, with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
आह्वयस्वेति मामुक्त्वा दर्शयित्वा च विक्रमम्
वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किमिदानीं त्वया कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
āhvayasveti māmuktvā darśayitvā ca vikramam
vairiṇā ghātayitvā ca kimidānīṁ tvayā kṛtam

translations.english: Accosting me with 'do you call (Vāli),' displaying your valour and making me struck by the enemy, what improper, conduct have you shown by me? You should have spoken me then truly, O Rāghava,-I shall not destroy Vali and I would not have gone there.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चैवं ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
करुणं दीनया वाचा राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya caivaṁ bruvāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
karuṇaṁ dīnayā vācā rāghavaḥ punarabravīt

translations.english: The high-souled Sugrīva speaking thus poorly, Rāghava again spoke to him, saying:

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीव श्रूयतां तातः क्रोधश्च व्यपनीयताम्
कारणं येन बाणोऽयं न मया स विसर्जितः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīva śrūyatāṁ tātaḥ krodhaśca vyapanīyatām
kāraṇaṁ yena bāṇo'yaṁ na mayā sa visarjitaḥ

translations.english: Do you hear, O Sugriva, O worshipful one, why I did not discharge my arrow then.

verses.sanskrit:
अलंकारेण वेषेण प्रमाणेन गतेन च
त्वं च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम्
verses.transliteration:
alaṁkāreṇa veṣeṇa pramāṇena gatena ca
tvaṁ ca sugrīva vālī ca sadṛśau sthaḥ parasparam

translations.english: By ornaments, dress, stature and movements yourself and Vali are just the same, O Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वरेण वर्चसा चैव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर
विक्रमेण च वाक्यैश्च व्यक्तिं वां नोपलक्षये
verses.transliteration:
svareṇa varcasā caiva prekṣitena ca vānara
vikrameṇa ca vākyaiśca vyaktiṁ vāṁ nopalakṣaye

translations.english: By voice, by words, by looks or by valour, O monkey, I could not make out any distinction.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं रूपसादृश्यान्मोहितो वानरोत्तम
नोत्सृजामि महावेगं शरं शत्रुनिबर्हणम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ rūpasādṛśyānmohito vānarottama
notsṛjāmi mahāvegaṁ śaraṁ śatrunibarhaṇam

translations.english: O best of monkeys, being thus surprised by the similarity of your countenances I could not discharge that foe-destroying and quick-coursing shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
एतन्मुहूर्ते तु मया पश्य वालिनमाहवे
निरस्तमिषुणैकेन वेष्टमानं महीतले
verses.transliteration:
etanmuhūrte tu mayā paśya vālinamāhave
nirastamiṣuṇaikena veṣṭamānaṁ mahītale

translations.english: And do you behold even, in this very moment, Vāli, moving restlessly on the breast of the earth, wounded by my shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिज्ञानं कुरुष्व त्वमात्मनो वानरेश्वर
येन त्वामभिजानीयां द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतम्
verses.transliteration:
abhijñānaṁ kuruṣva tvamātmano vānareśvara
yena tvāmabhijānīyāṁ dvandvayuddhamupāgatam

translations.english: Do you make some mark on your person, O lord of monkeys, by which I shall be able to recognize you when engaged in a duel (with your brother).

verses.sanskrit:
गजपुष्पीमिमां फुल्लामुत्पाट्य शुभलक्षणाम्
कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठेऽस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
gajapuṣpīmimāṁ phullāmutpāṭya śubhalakṣaṇām
kuru lakṣmaṇa kaṇṭhe'sya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, plucking this auspicious Gaja flower, do you put it round the neck of the highsouled Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गिरितटे जातामुत्पाट्य कुसुमायुताम्
लक्ष्मणो गजपुष्पीं तां तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato giritaṭe jātāmutpāṭya kusumāyutām
lakṣmaṇo gajapuṣpīṁ tāṁ tasya kaṇṭhe vyasarjayat

translations.english: Thereat that highly graceful one with the garland around his neck appeared like to a cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
विभ्राजमानो वपुषा रामवाक्यसमाहितः
जगाम सह रामेण किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
vibhrājamāno vapuṣā rāmavākyasamāhitaḥ
jagāma saha rāmeṇa kiṣkindhāṁ vālipālitām

translations.english: And appearing in a graceful person and attentive to Rāma's words he again entered Kiş kindhā with him.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यमूकात्स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धां लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
जगाम सहसुग्रीवो वालिविक्रमपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyamūkātsa dharmātmā kiṣkindhāṁ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
jagāma sahasugrīvo vālivikramapālitām

translations.english: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, along with Sugrīva, proceeded from the mount Rșyamuka to Kiskindha, maintained by Vali's prowess, raising up his gold crested mighty bow and taking his battle arrows like to Aditya.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रतस्तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः
सुग्रीवः संहतग्रीवो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
agratastu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
sugrīvaḥ saṁhatagrīvo lakṣmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ

translations.english: The mighty Sugrīva, bending low, proceeded before the high-souled Rama and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्ठतो हनुमान्वीरो नलो नीलश्च वानरः
तारश्चैव महातेजा हरियूथप यूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭhato hanumānvīro nalo nīlaśca vānaraḥ
tāraścaiva mahātejā hariyūthapa yūthapāḥ

translations.english: They were followed by the heroic Hanumān, the mighty Nala and Neela, and the highly powerful Tārā, the leader of the monkey herd.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्दराणि च शैलांश्च निर्झराणि गुहास्तथा
शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीश्च प्रियदर्शनाः
verses.transliteration:
kandarāṇi ca śailāṁśca nirjharāṇi guhāstathā
śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīśca priyadarśanāḥ

translations.english: They beheld as they proceeded, trees, lowered down with the weight of flowers, rivers of clear water flowing to the ocean, mountain hollows, hills, caves, cavities, and principal peaks and charming rills.

verses.sanskrit:
कारण्डैः सारसैर्हंसैर्वञ्जूलैर्जलकुक्कुटैः
चक्रवाकैस्तथा चान्यैः शकुनैः प्रतिनादितान्
verses.transliteration:
kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasairhaṁsairvañjūlairjalakukkuṭaiḥ
cakravākaistathā cānyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān

translations.english: They. beheld on their way, pools filled with water clear as Baidurya and beautified with lotuses-full blown and buds, and resounded with the cries of Kārandhabas, swans, geese, Banculas, water-fowls, Cakravākas, and various other birds.

verses.sanskrit:
मृदुशष्पाङ्कुराहारान्निर्भयान्वनगोचरान्
चरतः सर्वतोऽपश्यन्स्थलीषु हरिणान्स्थितान्
verses.transliteration:
mṛduśaṣpāṅkurāhārānnirbhayānvanagocarān
carataḥ sarvato'paśyansthalīṣu hariṇānsthitān

translations.english: They surveyed all around in the forest-land, deer ranging fearlessly at large and grazing on tender grass.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तु गच्छतां तत्र त्वरितं रघुनन्दनः
द्रुमषण्डं वनं दृष्ट्वा रामः सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tu gacchatāṁ tatra tvaritaṁ raghunandanaḥ
drumaṣaṇḍaṁ vanaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt

translations.english: They proceeding quickly, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, beholding the forest filled with trees, spoke to Sugrīva, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किमेतज्ज्ञातुमिच्छामि सखे कौतूहलं मम
कौतूहलापनयनं कर्तुमिच्छाम्यहं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
kimetajjñātumicchāmi sakhe kautūhalaṁ mama
kautūhalāpanayanaṁ kartumicchāmyahaṁ tvayā

translations.english: These trees skirted by plantain groves, dense as a collection of clouds, appear as clouds in the sky. Great is my curiosity, O friend, to learn what are these. 'And I wish to have my curiosity removed by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः
गच्छन्नेवाचचक्षेऽथ सुग्रीवस्तन्महद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
gacchannevācacakṣe'tha sugrīvastanmahadvanam

translations.english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva began to describe that great forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामेवं प्रभावेन द्रुमप्राकारसंवृतम्
आश्रमं सुदुराधर्षमपि सेन्द्रैः सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmevaṁ prabhāvena drumaprākārasaṁvṛtam
āśramaṁ sudurādharṣamapi sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: By virtue of their asceticism, this asylum is walled by trees and incapable of being conquered even by Indra, the celestials and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
पक्षिणो वर्जयन्त्येतत्तथान्ये वनचारिणः
विशन्ति मोहाद्येऽप्यत्र निवर्तन्ते न ते पुनः
verses.transliteration:
pakṣiṇo varjayantyetattathānye vanacāriṇaḥ
viśanti mohādye'pyatra nivartante na te punaḥ

translations.english: Birds or other wild animals do not enter this asylum; whoever entereth this by mistake never returneth.

verses.sanskrit:
विभूषणरवाश्चात्र श्रूयन्ते सकलाक्षराः
तूर्यगीतस्वनाश्चापि गन्धो दिव्यश्च राघव
verses.transliteration:
vibhūṣaṇaravāścātra śrūyante sakalākṣarāḥ
tūryagītasvanāścāpi gandho divyaśca rāghava

translations.english: There is audible, O Rāghava, the sound of the dressing of Apsarās, their sweet-winged accents and that of their music and drums; and herçin pervadeth the celestial fragrance.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रेताग्नयोऽपि दीप्यन्ते धूमो ह्येष प्रदृश्यते
वेष्टयन्निव वृक्षाग्रान्कपोताङ्गारुणो घनः
verses.transliteration:
tretāgnayo'pi dīpyante dhūmo hyeṣa pradṛśyate
veṣṭayanniva vṛkṣāgrānkapotāṅgāruṇo ghanaḥ

translations.english: Here burneth the fire Tretā; and the smoke and cloud sable like to the wings of a pigeon envelope the tops of the trees.

verses.sanskrit:
कुरु प्रणामं धर्मात्मंस्तान्समुद्दिश्य राघवः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रयतः संयताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
kuru praṇāmaṁ dharmātmaṁstānsamuddiśya rāghavaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṁyatāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Do you, O Rāghava, O virtuous-souled one, make obeisance to them along with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, with concentrated heart and folded palms.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रणमन्ति हि ये तेषामृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्
न तेषामशुभं किंचिच्छरीरे राम दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
praṇamanti hi ye teṣāmṛṣīṇāṁ bhāvitātmanām
na teṣāmaśubhaṁ kiṁciccharīre rāma dṛśyate

translations.english: There resteth no sin in their persons, O Rāma, who bow to those self-controlled Saints.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामः सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन कृताञ्जलिः
समुद्दिश्य महात्मानस्तानृषीनभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāñjaliḥ
samuddiśya mahātmānastānṛṣīnabhyavādayat

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma, along with his younger brother Lakşmaņa, made obeisance to those high-souled ones.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्य च धर्मात्मा रामो भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः
सुग्रीवो वानराश्चैव जग्मुः संहृष्टमानसाः
verses.transliteration:
abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
sugrīvo vānarāścaiva jagmuḥ saṁhṛṣṭamānasāḥ

translations.english: Having paid homage (to the sacred memory of those great ones) the virtuous-souled Rāma his (younger) brother Laksmana, Sugriva and other monkeys, proceeded with delighted hearts.

verses.sanskrit:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं तस्मात्सप्तजनाश्रमात्
ददृशुस्तां दुराधर्षां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
te gatvā dūramadhvānaṁ tasmātsaptajanāśramāt
dadṛśustāṁ durādharṣāṁ kiṣkindhāṁ vālipālitām

translations.english: And wending a distant way from that hermitage of the seven great ones, they beheld Kişkindhä, hard to conquer and occupied by Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्
वृक्षैरात्मानमावृत्य व्यतिष्ठन्गहने वने
verses.transliteration:
sarve te tvaritaṁ gatvā kiṣkindhāṁ vālipālitām
vṛkṣairātmānamāvṛtya vyatiṣṭhangahane vane

translations.english: Thereupon proceeding quickly to Kişkindhā, Väli's capital—they all stood waiting in that dense forest, hiding themselves under the trees.

verses.sanskrit:
विचार्य सर्वतो दृष्टिं कानने काननप्रियः
सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः क्रोधमाहारयद्भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
vicārya sarvato dṛṣṭiṁ kānane kānanapriyaḥ
sugrīvo vipulagrīvaḥ krodhamāhārayadbhṛśam

translations.english: Casting his looks all around in the forest, Sugrīva, having a huge neck and fond of woods, became exceedingly enraged.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स निनदं घोरं कृत्वा युद्धाय चाह्वयत्
परिवारैः परिवृतो नादैर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa ninadaṁ ghoraṁ kṛtvā yuddhāya cāhvayat
parivāraiḥ parivṛto nādairbhindannivāmbaram

translations.english: Setting up a terrible uproar and rending the sky with his cry (Sugrīva) encircled by his kinsmen, invited (Vāli) to battle.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ बालार्कसदृशो दृप्तसिंहगतिस्तदा
दृष्ट्वा रामं क्रियादक्षं सुग्रीवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha bālārkasadṛśo dṛptasiṁhagatistadā
dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ kriyādakṣaṁ sugrīvo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon roaring like to a huge cloud, preceded by a mighty wind, Sugrīva, gifted with leonine motion and resembling the newly risen Sun, finding Rāma expert in business, spoke to him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
हरिवागुरया व्याप्तं तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणाम्
प्राप्ताः स्म ध्वजयन्त्राढ्यां किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
harivāgurayā vyāptaṁ taptakāñcanatoraṇām
prāptāḥ sma dhvajayantrāḍhyāṁ kiṣkindhāṁ vālinaḥ purīm

translations.english: You have reached Kiskindhā, Vāli's capital, adorned with gold, filled with pennons and instruments and surrounded by monkeys. Do you make good your promise, O hero, you hadst made before to encompass the destruction of Vāli like to the season making the creepers filled with fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण स राघवः
तमथोवाच सुग्रीवं वचनं शत्रुसूदनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu dharmātmā sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ
tamathovāca sugrīvaṁ vacanaṁ śatrusūdanaḥ

translations.english: Being thus accosted by Sugrīva, the virtuoussouled Rāghava, the slayer of foes, addressed him with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
कृताभिज्ञान चिह्नस्त्वमनया गजसाह्वया
विपरीत इवाकाशे सूर्यो नक्षत्र मालया
verses.transliteration:
kṛtābhijñāna cihnastvamanayā gajasāhvayā
viparīta ivākāśe sūryo nakṣatra mālayā

translations.english: Uprooting the Gaja creeper, Laksmana, has placed it around your neck as an emblem (to distinguish you). You does appear beautiful, O hero, with this creeper around your neck like to the sun on the sky engarlanded by the stars.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य वालिसमुत्थं ते भयं वैरं च वानर
एकेनाहं प्रमोक्ष्यामि बाणमोक्षेण संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
adya vālisamutthaṁ te bhayaṁ vairaṁ ca vānara
ekenāhaṁ pramokṣyāmi bāṇamokṣeṇa saṁyuge

translations.english: I shall, O monkey, by the discharge of one shaft in the conflict, destroy your fear and enmity proceeding from Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
मम दर्शय सुग्रीववैरिणं भ्रातृरूपिणम्
वाली विनिहतो यावद्वने पांसुषु वेष्टते
verses.transliteration:
mama darśaya sugrīvavairiṇaṁ bhrātṛrūpiṇam
vālī vinihato yāvadvane pāṁsuṣu veṣṭate

translations.english: Do you show me, O Sugriva, your enemy, in the guise of a brother. Wounded (by my shaft) Vāli shall roll in the dust in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्तो जीवन्स विनिवर्तते
ततो दोषेण मा गच्छेत्सद्यो गर्हेच्च मा भवान्
verses.transliteration:
yadi dṛṣṭipathaṁ prāpto jīvansa vinivartate
tato doṣeṇa mā gacchetsadyo garhecca mā bhavān

translations.english: If regaining his life he comes in your view, do you leave this field, showering abuses upon me. more

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्यक्षं सप्त ते साला मया बाणेन दारिताः
ततो वेत्सि बलेनाद्य बालिनं निहतं मया
verses.transliteration:
pratyakṣaṁ sapta te sālā mayā bāṇena dāritāḥ
tato vetsi balenādya bālinaṁ nihataṁ mayā

translations.english: You didst behold seven Talas riven by a single shaft of mine and do you therefore consider Vāli destroyed to-day by my prowess in the conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
जितकाशी जयश्लाघी त्वया चाधर्षितः पुरात्
निष्पतिष्यत्यसंगेन वाली स प्रियसंयुगः
verses.transliteration:
jitakāśī jayaślāghī tvayā cādharṣitaḥ purāt
niṣpatiṣyatyasaṁgena vālī sa priyasaṁyugaḥ

translations.english: He has subdued his breath, is proud of victory and fond of warfare; you could not repress him before. Forsooth that Vāli shall come out, leaving the company (of his wives). Hearing the war cry of his enemy, he shall never put up with it, specially, as he boasteth of his prowess before his wives.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु रामवचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो हेमपिङ्गलः
ननर्द क्रूरनादेन विनिर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu rāmavacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo hemapiṅgalaḥ
nanarda krūranādena vinirbhindannivāmbaram

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's words. Sugrīva, having a gold-yellow hue, set up a terrible roar, as if riving the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य शब्देन वित्रस्ता गावो यान्ति हतप्रभाः
राजदोषपरामृष्टाः कुलस्त्रिय इवाकुलाः
verses.transliteration:
tasya śabdena vitrastā gāvo yānti hataprabhāḥ
rājadoṣaparāmṛṣṭāḥ kulastriya ivākulāḥ

translations.english: Terrified by that sound, the kine, losing their countenance do move hither and thither like to damsels, oppressed on account of their kings' neglecting (to protect them).

verses.sanskrit:
द्रवन्ति च मृगाः शीघ्रं भग्ना इव रणे हयाः
पतन्ति च खगा भूमौ क्षीणपुण्या इव ग्रहाः
verses.transliteration:
dravanti ca mṛgāḥ śīghraṁ bhagnā iva raṇe hayāḥ
patanti ca khagā bhūmau kṣīṇapuṇyā iva grahāḥ

translations.english: And the deer fly away like to the horses defeated in a warfare. And the birds fall down on the earth, like to planets, losing their purity.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स जीमूतगणप्रणादो; नादं व्यमुञ्चत्त्वरया प्रतीतः
सूर्यात्मजः शौर्यविवृद्धतेजाः; सरित्पतिर्वानिलचञ्चलोर्मिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa jīmūtagaṇapraṇādo; nādaṁ vyamuñcattvarayā pratītaḥ
sūryātmajaḥ śauryavivṛddhatejāḥ; saritpatirvānilacañcalormiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon confiding in Rāma's words, that son, of Suryya (Sun) having his energy enhanced by means of his prowess resembling the ocean agitated by the wind, began to roar like to cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तस्य निनादं तं सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
शुश्रावान्तःपुरगतो वाली भ्रातुरमर्षणः
verses.transliteration:
atha tasya ninādaṁ taṁ sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
śuśrāvāntaḥpuragato vālī bhrāturamarṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: While residing in the female apartment, Vāli heard the uproar of that high-souled Sugriva-his wrathful brother.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु तस्य निनदं सर्वभूतप्रकम्पनम्
मदश्चैकपदे नष्टः क्रोधश्चापतितो महान्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu tasya ninadaṁ sarvabhūtaprakampanam
madaścaikapade naṣṭaḥ krodhaścāpatito mahān

translations.english: And hearing that mighty roar, shaking the whole world of creation, his pride was in no time, crushed and he attained to an excess of ire.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु रोषपरीताङ्गो वाली संध्यातपप्रभः
उपरक्त इवादित्यः सद्यो निष्प्रभतां गतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu roṣaparītāṅgo vālī saṁdhyātapaprabhaḥ
uparakta ivādityaḥ sadyo niṣprabhatāṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, Vāli, having a golden hue, greatly exercised with wrath, instantly lost the effulgence of his person like to the sun possessed by Rāhu.

verses.sanskrit:
वाली दंष्ट्रा करालस्तु क्रोधाद्दीप्ताग्निसंनिभः
भात्युत्पतितपद्माभः समृणाल इव ह्रदः
verses.transliteration:
vālī daṁṣṭrā karālastu krodhāddīptāgnisaṁnibhaḥ
bhātyutpatitapadmābhaḥ samṛṇāla iva hradaḥ

translations.english: And looking terrible by his teeth and having eyes resembling burning fire in consequence of ire he appeared like to a pond, having the lotuses thereof uprooted with their stalks and fibres.

verses.sanskrit:
शब्दं दुर्मर्षणं श्रुत्वा निष्पपात ततो हरिः
वेगेन चरणन्यासैर्दारयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
śabdaṁ durmarṣaṇaṁ śrutvā niṣpapāta tato hariḥ
vegena caraṇanyāsairdārayanniva medinīm

translations.english: And hearing that unbearable sound, the 'monkey, issued out speedily, as if riving the earth with his foot marks.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु तारा परिष्वज्य स्नेहाद्दर्शितसौहृदा
उवाच त्रस्तसंभ्रान्ता हितोदर्कमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu tārā pariṣvajya snehāddarśitasauhṛdā
uvāca trastasaṁbhrāntā hitodarkamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Embracing him warmly and showing her affection, Tara, afraid and mortified, addressed him with the following words, presaging his future welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदी वेगमिवागतम्
शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज भुक्तामिव स्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
sādhu krodhamimaṁ vīra nadī vegamivāgatam
śayanādutthitaḥ kālyaṁ tyaja bhuktāmiva srajam

translations.english: Do you renounce, O hero, this your ire, coming like the course of a river, like to one, leaving aside the garland, which he used in the night, after rising from bed.

verses.sanskrit:
सहसा तव निष्क्रामो मम तावन्न रोचते
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि यन्निमित्तं निवार्यसे
verses.transliteration:
sahasā tava niṣkrāmo mama tāvanna rocate
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi yannimittaṁ nivāryase

translations.english: O monkey chief, do you engage with him in conflict, tomorrow. O hero, your enemy is very insignificant and hence there will be no deterioration on your part. Your hastily issuing out does not please me; do you hear, why I do prevent you.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वमापतितः क्रोधात्स त्वामाह्वयते युधि
निष्पत्य च निरस्तस्ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvamāpatitaḥ krodhātsa tvāmāhvayate yudhi
niṣpatya ca nirastaste hanyamāno diśo gataḥ

translations.english: Formerly this Sugrīva invited you angrily to battle and being defeated and wounded by you fled away.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया तस्य निरस्तस्य पीडितस्य विशेषतः
इहैत्य पुनराह्वानं शङ्कां जनयतीव मे
verses.transliteration:
tvayā tasya nirastasya pīḍitasya viśeṣataḥ
ihaitya punarāhvānaṁ śaṅkāṁ janayatīva me

translations.english: That one, who had been defeated and harassed by you formerly, is now calling you. Indeed it has excited my fear.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्पश्च व्यवसायश्च यादृशस्तस्य नर्दतः
निनादस्य च संरम्भो नैतदल्पं हि कारणम्
verses.transliteration:
darpaśca vyavasāyaśca yādṛśastasya nardataḥ
ninādasya ca saṁrambho naitadalpaṁ hi kāraṇam

translations.english: His pride, his energy, and his terrible uproar do indicate that there is nothing insignificant (at the bottom).

verses.sanskrit:
नासहायमहं मन्ये सुग्रीवं तमिहागतम्
अवष्टब्धसहायश्च यमाश्रित्यैष गर्जति
verses.transliteration:
nāsahāyamahaṁ manye sugrīvaṁ tamihāgatam
avaṣṭabdhasahāyaśca yamāśrityaiṣa garjati

translations.english: I do not think Sugrīva has come here without any to assist him. Forsooth he has taken shelter of some body, and securing which he has been setting up such a terrible uproar.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या निपुणश्चैव बुद्धिमांश्चैव वानरः
अपरीक्षितवीर्येण सुग्रीवः सह नैष्यति
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā nipuṇaścaiva buddhimāṁścaiva vānaraḥ
aparīkṣitavīryeṇa sugrīvaḥ saha naiṣyati

translations.english: That monkey is clever by nature and gifted with intellect. And Sugrīva shall not desire friendship with any one without having a test of his prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वमेव मया वीर श्रुतं कथयतो वचः
अङ्गदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामि त्वा हितं वचः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvameva mayā vīra śrutaṁ kathayato vacaḥ
aṅgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi tvā hitaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Hearken, O hero, I shall relate to you today, the auspicious words, I heard ere this, from the prince Angada.

verses.sanskrit:
तव भ्रातुर्हि विख्यातः सहायो रणकर्कशः
रामः परबलामर्दी युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tava bhrāturhi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇakarkaśaḥ
rāmaḥ parabalāmardī yugāntāgnirivotthitaḥ

translations.english: To accomplish Sugrīva's welfare, those two heroes, hard to repress, have come here. He is the main stay of your brother in the battle. Rāma has sprung up like to the fire of dissolution and is the repressor of enemy's prowess. He is the refuge of the saints and the prime shelter of the afflicted.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानसंपन्नो निदेशो निरतः पितुः
धातूनामिव शैलेन्द्रो गुणानामाकरो महान्
verses.transliteration:
jñānavijñānasaṁpanno nideśo nirataḥ pituḥ
dhātūnāmiva śailendro guṇānāmākaro mahān

translations.english: He is the protector of those grinded by their enemies and is the only possessor of fame. He is gifted with knowledge and intellect and ever abideth by his sire's commandments,

verses.sanskrit:
तत्क्षमं न विरोधस्ते सह तेन महात्मना
दुर्जयेनाप्रमेयेन रामेण रणकर्मसु
verses.transliteration:
tatkṣamaṁ na virodhaste saha tena mahātmanā
durjayenāprameyena rāmeṇa raṇakarmasu

translations.english: Like to Himālaya, the king of mountains, containing diverse metals, he is the mine of various accomplishments. It does not behove you therefore to enter into conflict with that high-souled Răma, incomparable in prowess and hard to conquer in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
शूर वक्ष्यामि ते किंचिन्न चेच्छाम्यभ्यसूयितुम्
श्रूयतां क्रियतां चैव तव वक्ष्यामि यद्धितम्
verses.transliteration:
śūra vakṣyāmi te kiṁcinna cecchāmyabhyasūyitum
śrūyatāṁ kriyatāṁ caiva tava vakṣyāmi yaddhitam

translations.english: Hearken, O hero, I desire to speak something more-I do not wish to excite your wrath. Do you instantly confer upon Sugrīva, the dignity of heir apparent (to your throne). O hero, O king, do not quarrel with your younger brother.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि ते क्षमं मन्ये तव रामेण सौहृदम्
सुग्रीवेण च संप्रीतिं वैरमुत्सृज्य दूरतः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi te kṣamaṁ manye tava rāmeṇa sauhṛdam
sugrīveṇa ca saṁprītiṁ vairamutsṛjya dūrataḥ

translations.english: I do consider it your welfare to contract friendship with Rāma and regain Sugrīva's affections, renouncing all your inimical feelings.

verses.sanskrit:
लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः
तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते
verses.transliteration:
lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyāneṣa vānaraḥ
tatra vā sannihastho vā sarvathā bandhureva te

translations.english: This your younger brother, even when remaining at a distance, should always be maintained by you. Whether by you, or at a distance, he is always your best friend—I do not find his equal on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ते मत्प्रियं कार्यं यदि चावैषि मां हिताम्
याच्यमानः प्रयत्नेन साधु वाक्यं कुरुष्व मे
verses.transliteration:
yadi te matpriyaṁ kāryaṁ yadi cāvaiṣi māṁ hitām
yācyamānaḥ prayatnena sādhu vākyaṁ kuruṣva me

translations.english: If you does wish to go by my desire, if you does regard me as your well-wisher, do you perform what I do request you for your welfare. Be pleased and hear my beneficial words.

verses.sanskrit:
तामेवं ब्रुवतीं तारां ताराधिपनिभाननाम्
वाली निर्भर्त्सयामास वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tāmevaṁ bruvatīṁ tārāṁ tārādhipanibhānanām
vālī nirbhartsayāmāsa vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: After Tārā, having a moon-like countenance, had spoken thus, Vāli, remonstrated with her and said.

verses.sanskrit:
गर्जतोऽस्य च संरम्भं भ्रातुः शत्रोर्विशेषतः
मर्षयिष्याम्यहं केन कारणेन वरानने
verses.transliteration:
garjato'sya ca saṁrambhaṁ bhrātuḥ śatrorviśeṣataḥ
marṣayiṣyāmyahaṁ kena kāraṇena varānane

translations.english: O you of exquisite loveliness, my brother, and specially my enemy, is roaring lowly and haughtily-and how shall I put up with it?

verses.sanskrit:
अधर्षितानां शूराणां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्
धर्षणामर्षणं भीरु मरणादतिरिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
adharṣitānāṁ śūrāṇāṁ samareṣvanivartinām
dharṣaṇāmarṣaṇaṁ bhīru maraṇādatiricyate

translations.english: O timid damsel, heroes, who have never been defeated and have never fled away from the battle field, had rather meet with death than put up with this ignominy.

verses.sanskrit:
सोढुं न च समर्थोऽहं युद्धकामस्य संयुगे
सुग्रीवस्य च संरम्भं हीनग्रीवस्य गर्जतः
verses.transliteration:
soḍhuṁ na ca samartho'haṁ yuddhakāmasya saṁyuge
sugrīvasya ca saṁrambhaṁ hīnagrīvasya garjataḥ

translations.english: I am incapable of bearing this proud uproar of Sugrīva, having a defective neck and desirous of entering into conflict with me.

verses.sanskrit:
न च कार्यो विषादस्ते राघवं प्रति मत्कृते
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च कथं पापं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
na ca kāryo viṣādaste rāghavaṁ prati matkṛte
dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca kathaṁ pāpaṁ kariṣyati

translations.english: Fearing danger from Rāghava, you needst not entertain any anxiety on my account. Why shall that virtuous-souled and grateful Rāma perpetrate iniquity?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतियोत्स्याम्यहं गत्वा सुग्रीवं जहि संभ्रमम्
दर्पं चास्य विनेष्यामि न च प्राणैर्विमोक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
pratiyotsyāmyahaṁ gatvā sugrīvaṁ jahi saṁbhramam
darpaṁ cāsya vineṣyāmi na ca prāṇairvimokṣyate

translations.english: Do you therefore return with my other wives. Why do you follow me again? You have already shown your friendship and respect for me. I shall repairing thither, only fight with Sugrīva. I shall crush down his pride and not destroy him.

verses.sanskrit:
शापितासि मम प्राणैर्निवर्तस्व जयेन च
अहं जित्वा निवर्तिष्ये तमलं भ्रातरं रणे
verses.transliteration:
śāpitāsi mama prāṇairnivartasva jayena ca
ahaṁ jitvā nivartiṣye tamalaṁ bhrātaraṁ raṇe

translations.english: By my life, do you go back with the other members of my household, I shall only return after bringing about the discomfiture of my brother in the battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु तारा परिष्वज्य वालिनं प्रियवादिनी
चकार रुदती मन्दं दक्षिणा सा प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu tārā pariṣvajya vālinaṁ priyavādinī
cakāra rudatī mandaṁ dakṣiṇā sā pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: Thereupon, Tārā, dextrous and of sweet accents, embracing Väli, went round him, with tears trickling from her eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्वा मन्त्रवद्विजयैषिणी
अन्तःपुरं सह स्त्रीभिः प्रविष्टा शोकमोहिता
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ svastyayanaṁ kṛtvā mantravadvijayaiṣiṇī
antaḥpuraṁ saha strībhiḥ praviṣṭā śokamohitā

translations.english: Having performed Sastayana or the ceremony of benediction, that one gifted with a knowledge of Mantras, and desirous of Vāli's success, went, overwhelmed with grief, to the inner-apartment in the company of other females.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टायां तु तारायां सह स्त्रीभिः स्वमालयम्
नगरान्निर्ययौ क्रुद्धो महासर्प इव श्वसन्
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭāyāṁ tu tārāyāṁ saha strībhiḥ svamālayam
nagarānniryayau kruddho mahāsarpa iva śvasan

translations.english: After Tārā had departed to her own quarters with her female companions, he issued out of the city sighing like an enraged serpent.

verses.sanskrit:
स निःश्वस्य महावेगो वाली परमरोषणः
सर्वतश्चारयन्दृष्टिं शत्रुदर्शनकाङ्क्षया
verses.transliteration:
sa niḥśvasya mahāvego vālī paramaroṣaṇaḥ
sarvataścārayandṛṣṭiṁ śatrudarśanakāṅkṣayā

translations.english: And the quick-paced Vali, exceedingly wroth, sighing, cast his looks around with a view to behold his enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श ततः श्रीमान्सुग्रीवं हेमपिङ्गलम्
सुसंवीतमवष्टब्धं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa tataḥ śrīmānsugrīvaṁ hemapiṅgalam
susaṁvītamavaṣṭabdhaṁ dīpyamānamivānalam

translations.english: And that highly effulgent one espied Sugrīva, having a golden yellow hue, tightly clothed, standing firm on the earth and shining like to burning gold.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं दृष्ट्वा महावीर्यं सुग्रीवं पर्यवस्थितम्
गाढं परिदधे वासो वाली परमरोषणः
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryaṁ sugrīvaṁ paryavasthitam
gāḍhaṁ paridadhe vāso vālī paramaroṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: And beholding Sugrīva stationed thus, the greatly enraged Vāli, of mighty arms, put on his clothes tightly well.

verses.sanskrit:
स वाली गाढसंवीतो मुष्टिमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
सुग्रीवमेवाभिमुखो ययौ योद्धुं कृतक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
sa vālī gāḍhasaṁvīto muṣṭimudyamya vīryavān
sugrīvamevābhimukho yayau yoddhuṁ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Highly powerful and closely habited, he, clinching his fists, proceeded towards Sugriva, and waited for the action.

verses.sanskrit:
श्लिष्टमुष्टिं समुद्यम्य संरब्धतरमागतः
सुग्रीवोऽपि समुद्दिश्य वालिनं हेममालिनम्
verses.transliteration:
śliṣṭamuṣṭiṁ samudyamya saṁrabdhataramāgataḥ
sugrīvo'pi samuddiśya vālinaṁ hemamālinam

translations.english: Sugrīva too, clinching his fist and exceedingly wroth, proceeded towards Vāli, wearing a golden garland.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वाली क्रोधताम्राक्षः सुग्रीवं रणपण्डितम्
आपतन्तं महावेगमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vālī krodhatāmrākṣaḥ sugrīvaṁ raṇapaṇḍitam
āpatantaṁ mahāvegamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And beholding Sugrīva, adept in warfare having his eyes reddened with ire, advance quickly, Vāli spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
एष मुष्टिर्मया बद्धो गाढः सुनिहिताङ्गुलिः
मया वेगविमुक्तस्ते प्राणानादाय यास्यति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa muṣṭirmayā baddho gāḍhaḥ sunihitāṅguliḥ
mayā vegavimuktaste prāṇānādāya yāsyati

translations.english: Behold, I have clinched this terrible fist, arranging close my fingers; and one blow from me will take away your life.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः क्रुद्धो वालिनमब्रवीत्
तवैव च हरन्प्राणान्मुष्टिः पततु मूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu sugrīvaḥ kruddho vālinamabravīt
tavaiva ca haranprāṇānmuṣṭiḥ patatu mūrdhani

translations.english: Being accosted thus by Vāli, Sugrīva, exercised with wrath, spoke to him, saying,—This my fist shall strike you on your head taking away your life.

verses.sanskrit:
ताडितस्तेन संक्रुद्धः समभिक्रम्य वेगतः
अभवच्छोणितोद्गारी सोत्पीड इव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
tāḍitastena saṁkruddhaḥ samabhikramya vegataḥ
abhavacchoṇitodgārī sotpīḍa iva parvataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon being struck by Vāli, waxing worth and approaching him quickly he began to vomit out gore like to a mountain having springs.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवेण तु निःसंगं सालमुत्पाट्य तेजसा
गात्रेष्वभिहतो वाली वज्रेणेव महागिरिः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīveṇa tu niḥsaṁgaṁ sālamutpāṭya tejasā
gātreṣvabhihato vālī vajreṇeva mahāgiriḥ

translations.english: And Vāli too was struck down by Sugrīva, fearlessly taking up a Sāla tree, like to a mountain clapped by a thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वाली प्रचरितः सालताडनविह्वलः
गुरुभारसमाक्रान्ता सागरे नौरिवाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vālī pracaritaḥ sālatāḍanavihvalaḥ
gurubhārasamākrāntā sāgare naurivābhavat

translations.english: Being thus smitten by the tree and overwhelmed with the strike of Sāla he was troubled like to a heavily laden boat in the midst of an ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ भीमबलविक्रान्तौ सुपर्णसमवेगिनौ
प्रवृद्धौ घोरवपुषौ चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
tau bhīmabalavikrāntau suparṇasamaveginau
pravṛddhau ghoravapuṣau candrasūryāvivāmbare

translations.english: And these (two brothers) gifted with mighty strength and prowess and motion of Suparna, and having huge persons fought with each other like to the Sun and Moon on the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
वालिना भग्नदर्पस्तु सुग्रीवो मन्दविक्रमः
वालिनं प्रति सामर्षो दर्शयामास लाघवम्
verses.transliteration:
vālinā bhagnadarpastu sugrīvo mandavikramaḥ
vālinaṁ prati sāmarṣo darśayāmāsa lāghavam

translations.english: And having his pride crushed down by Väli and strength greatly reduced, Sugrīva in anger pointed him out to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो धनुषि संधाय शरमाशीविषोपमम्
राघवेण महाबाणो वालिवक्षसि पातितः
verses.transliteration:
tato dhanuṣi saṁdhāya śaramāśīviṣopamam
rāghaveṇa mahābāṇo vālivakṣasi pātitaḥ

translations.english: And fixing on his bow an arrow resembling a serpent, he stretched it like to Death drawing out his cycle of time.

verses.sanskrit: वेगेनाभिहतो वाली निपपात महीतले
verses.transliteration: vegenābhihato vālī nipapāta mahītale

translations.english: Being wounded by that shaft that highly powerful chief of monkeys, gifted with prowess fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोक्षितः शोणिततोयविस्रवैः; सुपुष्पिताशोक इवानिलोद्धतः
विचेतनो वासवसूनुराहवे; प्रभ्रंशितेन्द्रध्वजवत्क्षितिं गतः
verses.transliteration:
athokṣitaḥ śoṇitatoyavisravaiḥ; supuṣpitāśoka ivāniloddhataḥ
vicetano vāsavasūnurāhave; prabhraṁśitendradhvajavatkṣitiṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon being bathed in blood that son of Vasava, fell senseless on the ground, in the conflict like to a blossoming Asoka growing on a hill and Sakra's banner struck down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरेणाभिहतो रामेण रणकर्कशः
पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्त इव पादपः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śareṇābhihato rāmeṇa raṇakarkaśaḥ
papāta sahasā vālī nikṛtta iva pādapaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Vāli, adept in warfare, wounded by Rāma's shaft, fell down to the ground like to a felled tree.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूमौ न्यस्तसर्वाङ्गस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः
अपतद्देवराजस्य मुक्तरश्मिरिव ध्वजः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūmau nyastasarvāṅgastaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇaḥ
apataddevarājasya muktaraśmiriva dhvajaḥ

translations.english: Ornamented with burning gold, he stretched the whole length of his person on the ground like to the banner of the Lord of celestials, loosened and thrown (off the chariot).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्निपतिते भूमौ हर्यृषाणां गणेश्वरे
नष्टचन्द्रमिव व्योम न व्यराजत भूतलम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminnipatite bhūmau haryṛṣāṇāṁ gaṇeśvare
naṣṭacandramiva vyoma na vyarājata bhūtalam

translations.english: That lord of monkeys being levelled to the ground, his kingdom appeared like to the sky, shorn of the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
भूमौ निपतितस्यापि तस्य देहं महात्मनः
न श्रीर्जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
bhūmau nipatitasyāpi tasya dehaṁ mahātmanaḥ
na śrīrjahāti na prāṇā na tejo na parākramaḥ

translations.english: Though struck down to the earth, neither vitality, effulgence nor prowess did renounce the body of that high-souled one.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्रदत्ता वरा माला काञ्चनी रत्नभूषिता
दधार हरिमुख्यस्य प्राणांस्तेजः श्रियं च सा
verses.transliteration:
śakradattā varā mālā kāñcanī ratnabhūṣitā
dadhāra harimukhyasya prāṇāṁstejaḥ śriyaṁ ca sā

translations.english: That excellent gold and jewel-crested garland conferred on him by Sakra maintained the vitality, effulgence and prowess of that lord of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स तया मालया वीरो हैमया हरियूथपः
संध्यानुगतपर्यन्तः पयोधर इवाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tayā mālayā vīro haimayā hariyūthapaḥ
saṁdhyānugataparyantaḥ payodhara ivābhavat

translations.english: Being adorned with that golden garland, that heroic lord, of monkey-herds, appeared like to an evening cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य माला च देहश्च मर्मघाती च यः शरः
त्रिधेव रचिता लक्ष्मीः पतितस्यापि शोभते
verses.transliteration:
tasya mālā ca dehaśca marmaghātī ca yaḥ śaraḥ
tridheva racitā lakṣmīḥ patitasyāpi śobhate

translations.english: Though felled to the ground, his beauty appeared as if divided into three, namely, his garland, his body and the shaft piercing his heart.

verses.sanskrit:
तदस्त्रं तस्य वीरस्य स्वर्गमार्गप्रभावनम्
रामबाणासनक्षिप्तमावहत्परमां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tadastraṁ tasya vīrasya svargamārgaprabhāvanam
rāmabāṇāsanakṣiptamāvahatparamāṁ gatim

translations.english: The arrow thrown off Răma's bow pointing out to him the way to the celestial region, became an excellent means to that hero.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा राघवं वाली लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं परुषं धर्मसंहितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṁ vālī lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam
abravītpraśritaṁ vākyaṁ paruṣaṁ dharmasaṁhitam

translations.english: And beholding that highly powerful Rāghava and Laksmana, Vāli addressed them with the following bold and pious words.

verses.sanskrit:
पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा को नु प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः
यदहं युद्धसंरब्धस्त्वत्कृते निधनं गतः
verses.transliteration:
parāṅmukhavadhaṁ kṛtvā ko nu prāptastvayā guṇaḥ
yadahaṁ yuddhasaṁrabdhastvatkṛte nidhanaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: What merit have you reaped by destroying me, who was not engaged in fight with you? I was exercised with ire, being engaged in conflict (with another person) and for you I have met with destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
सानुक्रोशो महोत्साहः समयज्ञो दृढव्रतः
इति ते सर्वभूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
sānukrośo mahotsāhaḥ samayajño dṛḍhavrataḥ
iti te sarvabhūtāni kathayanti yaśo bhuvi

translations.english: People speak highly of you, O Rāma, on this earth, describing you as coming of a high family, gifted with manliness and prowess, ever engaged in the welfare of your subjects, compassionate, energetic, of firm resolution and knowing time.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्गुणान्संप्रधार्याहमग्र्यं चाभिजनं तव
तारया प्रतिषिद्धः सन्सुग्रीवेण समागतः
verses.transliteration:
tānguṇānsaṁpradhāryāhamagryaṁ cābhijanaṁ tava
tārayā pratiṣiddhaḥ sansugrīveṇa samāgataḥ

translations.english: And knowing your high pedigree, and all these your accomplishments I approached Sugrīva with a hostile intention, albeit prevented by Tārā.

verses.sanskrit:
न मामन्येन संरब्धं प्रमत्तं वेद्धुमर्हसि
इति मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना बभूवादर्शने तव
verses.transliteration:
na māmanyena saṁrabdhaṁ pramattaṁ veddhumarhasi
iti me buddhirutpannā babhūvādarśane tava

translations.english: Before I saw you I had thought within myself:-'Forsooth Rāma shall not destroy me, engaged as I am with another person and hence not prepared to fight with him.'

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वां विनिहतात्मानं धर्मध्वजमधार्मिकम्
जाने पापसमाचारं तृणैः कूपमिवावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
na tvāṁ vinihatātmānaṁ dharmadhvajamadhārmikam
jāne pāpasamācāraṁ tṛṇaiḥ kūpamivāvṛtam

translations.english: I do now know you as one who has spoliated his soul through impious actions, feigning religion while in truth an irreligious person, resorting to all vicious deeds, like to a well crusted with grass, unrighteous while passing under the clock of honesty and religion like to a hidden fire.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रतीतः प्रियदर्शनः
लिङ्गमप्यस्ति ते राजन्दृश्यते धर्मसंहितम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ narādhipateḥ putraḥ pratītaḥ priyadarśanaḥ
liṅgamapyasti te rājandṛśyate dharmasaṁhitam

translations.english: I have not done you any wrong either in your kingdom or in your city. Nor have I passed by you. Why have you then destroyed me, who am a monkey ranging always in the woods, living on fruits and roots and who have come here to fight with another person? It appears that you are of a kingly father and of a graceful countenance. And, O king, there are marks of piety on your person.

verses.sanskrit:
कः क्षत्रियकुले जातः श्रुतवान्नष्टसंशयः
धर्मलिङ्ग प्रतिच्छन्नः क्रूरं कर्म समाचरेत्
verses.transliteration:
kaḥ kṣatriyakule jātaḥ śrutavānnaṣṭasaṁśayaḥ
dharmaliṅga praticchannaḥ krūraṁ karma samācaret

translations.english: Who, born in the race of Kșatriyas, versed in religious lore, having his doubts removed and marks of piety on his person, perpetrates such an iniquitous deed?

verses.sanskrit:
राम राजकुले जातो धर्मवानिति विश्रुतः
अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण किमर्थं परिधावसि
verses.transliteration:
rāma rājakule jāto dharmavāniti viśrutaḥ
abhavyo bhavyarūpeṇa kimarthaṁ paridhāvasi

translations.english: You are born in the family of Raghus and known all over the world as being pious. Being clothed in righteousness why did you commit such an unrighteous act?

verses.sanskrit:
साम दानं क्षमा धर्मः सत्यं धृतिपराक्रमौ
पार्थिवानां गुणा राजन्दण्डश्चाप्यपकारिषु
verses.transliteration:
sāma dānaṁ kṣamā dharmaḥ satyaṁ dhṛtiparākramau
pārthivānāṁ guṇā rājandaṇḍaścāpyapakāriṣu

translations.english: Chastisement, charity, forgiveness, piety, truthfulness firmness, prowess and the punishment of the iniquitous are the virtues of a king, O prince.

verses.sanskrit:
वयं वनचरा राम मृगा मूलफलाशनाः
एषा प्रकृतिरस्माकं पुरुषस्त्वं नरेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
vayaṁ vanacarā rāma mṛgā mūlaphalāśanāḥ
eṣā prakṛtirasmākaṁ puruṣastvaṁ nareśvaraḥ

translations.english: We are, O Rama, wild beasts ranging in the forest and living on roots and fruits-our nature is such—but you are a man, O king.

verses.sanskrit:
भूमिर्हिरण्यं रूप्यं च निग्रहे कारणानि च
तत्र कस्ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा
verses.transliteration:
bhūmirhiraṇyaṁ rūpyaṁ ca nigrahe kāraṇāni ca
tatra kaste vane lobho madīyeṣu phaleṣu vā

translations.english: Land, gold and silver are the causes of dissension. But who is there who is avaricious enough to get by our forest habitations and fruits?

verses.sanskrit:
नयश्च विनयश्चोभौ निग्रहानुग्रहावपि
राजवृत्तिरसंकीर्णा न नृपाः कामवृत्तयः
verses.transliteration:
nayaśca vinayaścobhau nigrahānugrahāvapi
rājavṛttirasaṁkīrṇā na nṛpāḥ kāmavṛttayaḥ

translations.english: The royal virtue consists in humbly and freely administering discipline, favour and punishment. Kings by no means, should follow their whims.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं तु कामप्रधानश्च कोपनश्चानवस्थितः
राजवृत्तैश्च संकीर्णः शरासनपरायणः
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ tu kāmapradhānaśca kopanaścānavasthitaḥ
rājavṛttaiśca saṁkīrṇaḥ śarāsanaparāyaṇaḥ

translations.english: But you are angry and unsteady by nature, capricious, perfectly narrow-minded in the discharge of your royal duties and did use your bow and shaft: (any where and every time).

verses.sanskrit:
न तेऽस्त्यपचितिर्धर्मे नार्थे बुद्धिरवस्थिता
इन्द्रियैः कामवृत्तः सन्कृष्यसे मनुजेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
na te'styapacitirdharme nārthe buddhiravasthitā
indriyaiḥ kāmavṛttaḥ sankṛṣyase manujeśvara

translations.english: You have no attachment for virtue, no comprehension of right things and are always guided by your passions albeit you are a lord of men.

verses.sanskrit:
हत्वा बाणेन काकुत्स्थ मामिहानपराधिनम्
किं वक्ष्यसि सतां मध्ये कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्
verses.transliteration:
hatvā bāṇena kākutstha māmihānaparādhinam
kiṁ vakṣyasi satāṁ madhye karma kṛtvā jugupsitam

translations.english: O Kākutstha, destroying me sinless, with your shaft and perpetrating such a disgraceful act, how shall you relate it to the pious.

verses.sanskrit:
राजहा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नश्चोरः प्राणिवधे रतः
नास्तिकः परिवेत्ता च सर्वे निरयगामिनः
verses.transliteration:
rājahā brahmahā goghnaścoraḥ prāṇivadhe rataḥ
nāstikaḥ parivettā ca sarve nirayagāminaḥ

translations.english: Those, who commit treason, destroy Brahmins and kine, who are thieves and always engaged in the destruction of animals, and who are atheists and marry before their elder brothers are married, do all go to hell.

verses.sanskrit:
अधार्यं चर्म मे सद्भी रोमाण्यस्थि च वर्जितम्
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि त्वद्विधैर्धर्मचारिभिः
verses.transliteration:
adhāryaṁ carma me sadbhī romāṇyasthi ca varjitam
abhakṣyāṇi ca māṁsāni tvadvidhairdharmacāribhiḥ

translations.english: And there is not the least doubt about it. My skin is not worthy of your touch and my bones and hairs should always be avoided by the virtuous. And my flesh is not worthy of being eaten by persons of your piety.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्च पञ्चनखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण राघव
शल्यकः श्वाविधो गोधा शशः कूर्मश्च पञ्चमः
verses.transliteration:
pañca pañcanakhā bhakṣyā brahmakṣatreṇa rāghava
śalyakaḥ śvāvidho godhā śaśaḥ kūrmaśca pañcamaḥ

translations.english: A hedge-hog a porcupine, an iguana, a hare and a tortoise these five animals only, having five toes, are worthy of being eaten by the Ks atryas and Brahmins, O Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
चर्म चास्थि च मे राजन्न स्पृशन्ति मनीषिणः
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि सोऽहं पञ्चनखो हतः
verses.transliteration:
carma cāsthi ca me rājanna spṛśanti manīṣiṇaḥ
abhakṣyāṇi ca māṁsāni so'haṁ pañcanakho hataḥ

translations.english: The wise, O Rāma, do not touch my skin and bones and my flesh is not worthy of being taken-I am that (monkey) having five toes who have been killed by you.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया नाथेन काकुत्स्थ न सनाथा वसुंधरा
प्रमदा शीलसंपन्ना धूर्तेन पतिता यथा
verses.transliteration:
tvayā nāthena kākutstha na sanāthā vasuṁdharā
pramadā śīlasaṁpannā dhūrtena patitā yathā

translations.english: O Kākutstha, the Earth has got you as her husband like to a good natured damsel being wedded to a husband who has forsaken his own religion.

verses.sanskrit:
शठो नैकृतिकः क्षुद्रो मिथ्या प्रश्रितमानसः
कथं दशरथेन त्वं जातः पापो महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
śaṭho naikṛtikaḥ kṣudro mithyā praśritamānasaḥ
kathaṁ daśarathena tvaṁ jātaḥ pāpo mahātmanā

translations.english: How are you, who are wicked, narrowminded, a liar and ever intent upon bringing about others' misfortune, born of the loins of the high-souled Dasaratha?

verses.sanskrit:
छिन्नचारित्र्यकक्ष्येण सतां धर्मातिवर्तिना
त्यक्तधर्माङ्कुशेनाहं निहतो रामहस्तिना
verses.transliteration:
chinnacāritryakakṣyeṇa satāṁ dharmātivartinā
tyaktadharmāṅkuśenāhaṁ nihato rāmahastinā

translations.english: I have been killed by an elephant-Rāma, disregarding the virtue of the pious, breaking the chord of character, and neglecting the goad of religion.

verses.sanskrit:
दृश्यमानस्तु युध्येथा मया युधि नृपात्मज
अद्य वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येस्त्वं निहतो मया
verses.transliteration:
dṛśyamānastu yudhyethā mayā yudhi nṛpātmaja
adya vaivasvataṁ devaṁ paśyestvaṁ nihato mayā

translations.english: O son of a king, hadst you fought with me openly you wouldst have, forsooth, seen the abode of Death being killed by me.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयादृश्येन तु रणे निहतोऽहं दुरासदः
प्रसुप्तः पन्नगेनेव नरः पानवशं गतः
verses.transliteration:
tvayādṛśyena tu raṇe nihato'haṁ durāsadaḥ
prasuptaḥ pannageneva naraḥ pānavaśaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, like to a serpent destroying persons asleep, you, that are under the control of vice, have killed me, who am hard to repress, keeping yourself out of my sight in the battle.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवप्रियकामेन यदहं निहतस्त्वया
कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्यां तेऽनिहतं रावणं रणे
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvapriyakāmena yadahaṁ nihatastvayā
kaṇṭhe baddhvā pradadyāṁ te'nihataṁ rāvaṇaṁ raṇe

translations.english: I have been killed by you, desirous of encompassing Sugrīva's well being. Hadst you apprized me of your object before, I would have got you your Maithili in the course of a day, and brought, by the neck, that vicious-souled Raks asa-Rāvaņa, the ravisher of your spouse with out putting an end to his life in the battle.

verses.sanskrit:
न्यस्तां सागरतोये वा पाताले वापि मैथिलीम्
जानयेयं तवादेशाच्छ्वेतामश्वतरीमिव
verses.transliteration:
nyastāṁ sāgaratoye vā pātāle vāpi maithilīm
jānayeyaṁ tavādeśācchvetāmaśvatarīmiva

translations.english: Whether in the deep ocean or in the region under the earth, I shall bring your Maithili like to an Asyatar* Here is an allusion. A prince of Daityas, named Hayagriva, stole the Vedas at the end of Kalpa; in the recovery of them he was slain by Vişnu after his descent as Matshya.

verses.sanskrit:
युक्तं यत्प्रप्नुयाद्राज्यं सुग्रीवः स्वर्गते मयि
अयुक्तं यदधर्मेण त्वयाहं निहतो रणे
verses.transliteration:
yuktaṁ yatprapnuyādrājyaṁ sugrīvaḥ svargate mayi
ayuktaṁ yadadharmeṇa tvayāhaṁ nihato raṇe

translations.english: It is perfectly proper that Sugrīva shall inherit my kingdom on my ascension to heaven. And it is equally improper that I have been viciously killed by you in the battle.

verses.sanskrit:
काममेवंविधं लोकः कालेन विनियुज्यते
क्षमं चेद्भवता प्राप्तमुत्तरं साधु चिन्त्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
kāmamevaṁvidhaṁ lokaḥ kālena viniyujyate
kṣamaṁ cedbhavatā prāptamuttaraṁ sādhu cintyatām

translations.english: Every one in time meets with death and hence there is nothing to be sorry for me. But do you think of a proper reply you shall give to the people (when asked about the cause of my destruction).

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा परिशुष्कवक्त्रः; शराभिघाताद्व्यथितो महात्मा
समीक्ष्य रामं रविसंनिकाशं; तूष्णीं बभूवामरराजसूनुः
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā pariśuṣkavaktraḥ; śarābhighātādvyathito mahātmā
samīkṣya rāmaṁ ravisaṁnikāśaṁ; tūṣṇīṁ babhūvāmararājasūnuḥ

translations.english: Having said this, that high-souled Son of monkey-chief, greatly distressed being wounded by (Rāma's) shaft and having his countenance dried up, became silent, fixing his look upon Rāma, resembling the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्
परुषं वालिना रामो निहतेन विचेतसा
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ praśritaṁ vākyaṁ dharmārthasahitaṁ hitam
paruṣaṁ vālinā rāmo nihatena vicetasā

translations.english: And thus Rāma was addressed by Vāli, wounded and senseless, with those modest, pious and auspicious words. And being thus reproached he spoke to that excellent lord of monkeys, gifted with virtue and other accomplishments, resembling the Sun shorn of its lustre, a cloud which has already discharged its waters and fire extinguished.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च समयं चापि लौकिकम्
अविज्ञाय कथं बाल्यान्मामिहाद्य विगर्हसे
verses.transliteration:
