translations.english: Having thus addressed Hanumān, Rāma spoke to Sugriva, saying:-Conversant with customs as you are, do you install this generous and heroic Angada, gifted with gifted with prowess and honouring customs, as the heir-apparent of the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वोऽयं वार्षिको मासः श्रावणः सलिलागमः
प्रवृत्ताः सौम्य चत्वारो मासा वार्षिकसंज्ञिताः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvo'yaṁ vārṣiko māsaḥ śrāvaṇaḥ salilāgamaḥ
pravṛttāḥ saumya catvāro māsā vārṣikasaṁjñitāḥ

translations.english: O gentle one, this month of Sravana, which is the first of those four months which make up the rainy season, has set in and this is not the time therefore enter your auspicious city and I shall live in this mountain along with Lakṣmaṇa.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं गिरिगुहा रम्या विशाला युक्तमारुता
प्रभूतसलिला सौम्य प्रभूतकमलोत्पला
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ giriguhā ramyā viśālā yuktamārutā
prabhūtasalilā saumya prabhūtakamalotpalā

translations.english: Pleasant indeed is this mountain cave, spacious, filled with air, water and many lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
कार्तिके समनुप्राप्ते त्वं रावणवधे यत
एष नः समयः सौम्य प्रविश त्वं स्वमालयम्
अभिषिञ्चस्व राज्ये च सुहृदः संप्रहर्षय
verses.transliteration:
kārtike samanuprāpte tvaṁ rāvaṇavadhe yata
eṣa naḥ samayaḥ saumya praviśa tvaṁ svamālayam
abhiṣiñcasva rājye ca suhṛdaḥ saṁpraharṣaya

translations.english: You shall engage in endeavours to bring about the destruction of Rāvana, after Kārtika sets in. This is not the proper time, O gentle one, and do you enter your own city. And being installed on the throne do you enhance the joy of your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
इति रामाभ्यनुज्ञातः सुग्रीवो वानरर्षभः
प्रविवेश पुरीं रम्यां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
iti rāmābhyanujñātaḥ sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ ramyāṁ kiṣkindhāṁ vālipālitām

translations.english: Being thus commanded by Rāma, Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys entered the pleasant city of Kiskindha, reared by Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वानरसहस्राणि प्रविष्टं वानरेश्वरम्
अभिवाद्य प्रहृष्टानि सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vānarasahasrāṇi praviṣṭaṁ vānareśvaram
abhivādya prahṛṣṭāni sarvataḥ paryavārayan

translations.english: Encircling that lord of monkeys thousands of them entered the city.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वा दृष्ट्वा हरिगणेश्वरम्
प्रणम्य मूर्ध्ना पतिता वसुधायां समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā harigaṇeśvaram
praṇamya mūrdhnā patitā vasudhāyāṁ samāhitāḥ

translations.english: Beholding the lord of monkeys, the subjects bowed to him, lowering their heads on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवः प्रकृतीः सर्वाः संभाष्योत्थाप्य वीर्यवान्
भ्रातुरन्तःपुरं सौम्यं प्रविवेश महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvaḥ prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ saṁbhāṣyotthāpya vīryavān
bhrāturantaḥpuraṁ saumyaṁ praviveśa mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Welcoming the subjects and raising them up; the highly powerful Sugrīva entered the pleasant inner apartment of his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविश्य त्वभिनिष्क्रान्तं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्
अभ्यषिञ्चन्त सुहृदः सहस्राक्षमिवामराः
verses.transliteration:
praviśya tvabhiniṣkrāntaṁ sugrīvaṁ vānararṣabham
abhyaṣiñcanta suhṛdaḥ sahasrākṣamivāmarāḥ

translations.english: On his entering the city, his friends installed the highly powerful foremost of monkeys-Sugrīva, on the throne like to the celestials placing the thousand-eyed Deity (on the kingdom).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते वानरश्रेष्ठं यथाकालं यथाविधि
रत्नैर्वस्त्रैश्च भक्ष्यैश्च तोषयित्वा द्विजर्षभान्
verses.transliteration:
tataste vānaraśreṣṭhaṁ yathākālaṁ yathāvidhi
ratnairvastraiśca bhakṣyaiśca toṣayitvā dvijarṣabhān

translations.english: Thereupon those monkeys pleased the foremost of twice-born ones with jewels clothes and eatables, with a view to install that best of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कुशपरिस्तीर्णं समिद्धं जातवेदसं
मन्त्रपूतेन हविषा हुत्वा मन्त्रविदो जनाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kuśaparistīrṇaṁ samiddhaṁ jātavedasaṁ
mantrapūtena haviṣā hutvā mantravido janāḥ

translations.english: And these conversant with mantras threw clarified butter, sanctified by mantras, into flaming fire burning on a Kusa bed.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य तु वचः कुर्वन्सुग्रीवो हरिपुंगवः
अङ्गदं संपरिष्वज्य यौवराज्येऽभिषेचयत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya tu vacaḥ kurvansugrīvo haripuṁgavaḥ
aṅgadaṁ saṁpariṣvajya yauvarājye'bhiṣecayat

translations.english: Abiding by Rama's words, Sugriva, the lord of monkeys, embracing Angada conferred on him the heir-apparentship of the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदे चाभिषिक्ते तु सानुक्रोशाः प्लवंगमाः
साधु साध्विति सुग्रीवं महात्मानोऽभ्यपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgade cābhiṣikte tu sānukrośāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
sādhu sādhviti sugrīvaṁ mahātmāno'bhyapūjayan

translations.english: Angada being thus installed, those best of monkeys, highly delighted adored the highsouled Sugrīva, extolling him again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा पताकाध्वजशोभिता
बभूव नगरी रम्या क्षिकिन्धा गिरिगह्वरे
verses.transliteration:
hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā patākādhvajaśobhitā
babhūva nagarī ramyā kṣikindhā girigahvare

translations.english: The city of Kiskindhā, filled with stoutly built people and adorned with pennons and flags, appeared beautiful in the mountain cave.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेद्य रामाय तदा महात्मने; महाभिषेकं कपिवाहिनीपतिः
रुमां च भार्यां प्रतिलभ्य वीर्यवा;नवाप राज्यं त्रिदशाधिपो यथा
verses.transliteration:
nivedya rāmāya tadā mahātmane; mahābhiṣekaṁ kapivāhinīpatiḥ
rumāṁ ca bhāryāṁ pratilabhya vīryavā;navāpa rājyaṁ tridaśādhipo yathā

translations.english: Communicating to the high-souled Rāma the news of installation the highly powerful lord of monkey hosts (Sugrīva) getting back his wife Rumā, regained the kingdom like to the lord of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिषिक्ते तु सुग्रीवे प्रविष्टे वानरे गुहाम्
आजगाम सह भ्रात्रा रामः प्रस्रवणं गिरिम्
verses.transliteration:
abhiṣikte tu sugrīve praviṣṭe vānare guhām
ājagāma saha bhrātrā rāmaḥ prasravaṇaṁ girim

translations.english: On Sugrīva being installed and the monkeys entering the cave, Rāma, along with his younger brother, got at the Prasravana hill, resounded with the noise of tigers and deer, filled with terrible lions, covered with diverse trees, creepers and bowers, inhabited by bears, monkeys, Gopucyas and cats, resembling a collection of clouds and always auspicious.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य शैलस्य शिखरे महतीमायतां गुहाम्
प्रत्यगृह्णत वासार्थं रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
verses.transliteration:
tasya śailasya śikhare mahatīmāyatāṁ guhām
pratyagṛhṇata vāsārthaṁ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha

translations.english: Rāma, along with Saumitri, selected for his habitation, a spacious cave, situated on the summit of that hill.

verses.sanskrit:
अवसत्तत्र धर्मात्मा राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः
बहुदृश्यदरीकुञ्जे तस्मिन्प्रस्रवणे गिरौ
verses.transliteration:
avasattatra dharmātmā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
bahudṛśyadarīkuñje tasminprasravaṇe girau

translations.english: Having said this, Rāghava, along with Laks maņa, dwelt in that Prasravana hill abounding in caves and bowers.

verses.sanskrit:
सुसुखेऽपि बहुद्रव्ये तस्मिन्हि धरणीधरे
वसतस्तस्य रामस्य रतिरल्पापि नाभवत्
हृतां हि भार्यां स्मरतः प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम्
verses.transliteration:
susukhe'pi bahudravye tasminhi dharaṇīdhare
vasatastasya rāmasya ratiralpāpi nābhavat
hṛtāṁ hi bhāryāṁ smarataḥ prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasīm

translations.english: He did not attain to a best felicity although he lived in that pleasant hill filled with many things.

verses.sanskrit:
उदयाभ्युदितं दृष्ट्वा शशाङ्कं च विशेषतः
आविवेश न तं निद्रा निशासु शयनं गतम्
verses.transliteration:
udayābhyuditaṁ dṛṣṭvā śaśāṅkaṁ ca viśeṣataḥ
āviveśa na taṁ nidrā niśāsu śayanaṁ gatam

translations.english: Pondering over the ravishment of his spouse, dearer than his life, beholding the setting of the Sun in particular, he did not go to sleep, although he laid himself on the bed in the night.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्समुत्थेन शोकेन बाष्पोपहतचेतसं
तं शोचमानं काकुत्स्थं नित्यं शोकपरायणम्
तुल्यदुःखोऽब्रवीद्भ्राता लक्ष्मणोऽनुनयन्वचः
verses.transliteration:
tatsamutthena śokena bāṣpopahatacetasaṁ
taṁ śocamānaṁ kākutsthaṁ nityaṁ śokaparāyaṇam
tulyaduḥkho'bravīdbhrātā lakṣmaṇo'nunayanvacaḥ

translations.english: His younger brother Laksmana, equally aggrieved, spoke to Kākutstha, thus bewailing being exercised with grief and almost beside himself with sorrow, consequent upon Sita's bereavement, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अलं वीर व्यथां गत्वा न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
शोचतो ह्यवसीदन्ति सर्वार्था विदितं हि ते
verses.transliteration:
alaṁ vīra vyathāṁ gatvā na tvaṁ śocitumarhasi
śocato hyavasīdanti sarvārthā viditaṁ hi te

translations.english: It does not behove you to lament thus, being exercised with grief—it is not unknown to you that people, thus bewailing do exhaust themselves by and by.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्क्रियापरो लोके भवान्देवपरायणः
आस्तिको धर्मशीलश्च व्यवसायी च राघव
verses.transliteration:
bhavānkriyāparo loke bhavāndevaparāyaṇaḥ
āstiko dharmaśīlaśca vyavasāyī ca rāghava

translations.english: O Rāghava, you are devoted to pious actions and the services of the Deity in this world-and pious, energetic and did believe in the existence of God.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यव्यवसितः शत्रुं राक्षसं तं विशेषतः
समर्थस्त्वं रणे हन्तुं विक्रमैर्जिह्मकारिणम्
verses.transliteration:
na hyavyavasitaḥ śatruṁ rākṣasaṁ taṁ viśeṣataḥ
samarthastvaṁ raṇe hantuṁ vikramairjihmakāriṇam

translations.english: Without being persevering you shall not be able to destroy in conflict your enemy—that terrible, wily Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
समुन्मूलय शोकं त्वं व्यवसायं स्थिरं कुरु
ततः सपरिवारं तं निर्मूलं कुरु राक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
samunmūlaya śokaṁ tvaṁ vyavasāyaṁ sthiraṁ kuru
tataḥ saparivāraṁ taṁ nirmūlaṁ kuru rākṣasaṁ

translations.english: Do you renounce your grief and take recourse to energy and you shall be able to slay that Rākş asa with all his family.

verses.sanskrit:
पृथिवीमपि काकुत्स्थ ससागरवनाचलाम्
परिवर्तयितुं शक्तः किमङ्ग पुन रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
pṛthivīmapi kākutstha sasāgaravanācalām
parivartayituṁ śaktaḥ kimaṅga puna rāvaṇam

translations.english: What of the destruction of Rāvana, you are O Kākutstha. capable of uprooting the earth with oceans, forest and hills.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु खलु ते वीर्यं प्रसुप्तं प्रतिबोधये
दीप्तैराहुतिभिः काले भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu khalu te vīryaṁ prasuptaṁ pratibodhaye
dīptairāhutibhiḥ kāle bhasmacchannamivānalam

translations.english: I, too, am exciting your latent energy like to fire hidden in ashes with oblations.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं प्रतिपूज्य हितं शुभम्
राघवः सुहृदं स्निग्धमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇasya tu tadvākyaṁ pratipūjya hitaṁ śubham
rāghavaḥ suhṛdaṁ snigdhamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Welcoming the auspicious and well-meaning accents of Lakşmaņa, Raghava again spoke to him the following affectionate words. when you

verses.sanskrit:
वाच्यं यदनुरक्तेन स्निग्धेन च हितेन च
सत्यविक्रम युक्तेन तदुक्तं लक्ष्मण त्वया
verses.transliteration:
vācyaṁ yadanuraktena snigdhena ca hitena ca
satyavikrama yuktena taduktaṁ lakṣmaṇa tvayā

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, truly do your words become you, affectionate, devoted, truthful and intent in my welfare as you are.

verses.sanskrit:
एष शोकः परित्यक्तः सर्वकार्यावसादकः
विक्रमेष्वप्रतिहतं तेजः प्रोत्साहयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa śokaḥ parityaktaḥ sarvakāryāvasādakaḥ
vikrameṣvapratihataṁ tejaḥ protsāhayāmyaham

translations.english: Renouncing this grief standing in the way of all business, I shail call forth, the more, this my energy on the occasion of displaying my prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षेऽहमियं प्रावृडुपस्थिता
ततः सराष्ट्रं सगणं राक्षसं तं निहन्म्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
śaratkālaṁ pratīkṣe'hamiyaṁ prāvṛḍupasthitā
tataḥ sarāṣṭraṁ sagaṇaṁ rākṣasaṁ taṁ nihanmyaham

translations.english: Rains have set in and do you wait for the autumn shall encompass the destruction of Rāvana with his kingdom and kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit:
नियम्य कोपं प्रतिपाल्यतां शर;त्क्षमस्व मासांश्चतुरो मया सह
वसाचलेऽस्मिन्मृगराजसेविते; संवर्धयञ्शत्रुवधे समुद्यतः
verses.transliteration:
niyamya kopaṁ pratipālyatāṁ śara;tkṣamasva māsāṁścaturo mayā saha
vasācale'sminmṛgarājasevite; saṁvardhayañśatruvadhe samudyataḥ

translations.english: Subduing your wrath, and awaiting the autumn, do you with me spend these four months in this hill filled with deer, capable as you are of encompassing the destruction of your enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
स तदा वालिनं हत्वाह्सुग्रीवमभिषिच्य च
वसन्माल्यवतः पृष्टे रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tadā vālinaṁ hatvāhsugrīvamabhiṣicya ca
vasanmālyavataḥ pṛṣṭe rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon encompassing the destruction of Vāli, installing Sugrīva and dwelling on the summit of the Mālyabana hill, Rāma spoke to Laksmana, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अयं स कालः संप्राप्तः समयोऽद्य जलागमः
संपश्य त्वं नभो मेघैः संवृतं गिरिसंनिभैः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ sa kālaḥ saṁprāptaḥ samayo'dya jalāgamaḥ
saṁpaśya tvaṁ nabho meghaiḥ saṁvṛtaṁ girisaṁnibhaiḥ

translations.english: This is the time the beginning of the rainy season-do you behold the sky enveloped with clouds resembling so many hills.

verses.sanskrit:
नव मास धृतं गर्भं भास्कारस्य गभस्तिभिः
पीत्वा रसं समुद्राणां द्यौः प्रसूते रसायनम्
verses.transliteration:
nava māsa dhṛtaṁ garbhaṁ bhāskārasya gabhastibhiḥ
pītvā rasaṁ samudrāṇāṁ dyauḥ prasūte rasāyanam

translations.english: The sky, drinking the liquid contents of the ocean through the rays of the Sun, and being enceinite for nine months, is giving birth to showers.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्यमम्बरमारुह्य मेघसोपानपङ्क्तिभिः
कुटजार्जुनमालाभिरलंकर्तुं दिवाकरम्
verses.transliteration:
śakyamambaramāruhya meghasopānapaṅktibhiḥ
kuṭajārjunamālābhiralaṁkartuṁ divākaram

translations.english: Ascending the sky by the steps of clouds, one can ornameni the Sun with garlands of Kutajas and Arjunas.

verses.sanskrit:
संध्यारागोत्थितैस्ताम्रैरन्तेष्वधिकपाण्डुरैः
स्निग्धैरभ्रपटच्छदैर्बद्धव्रणमिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁdhyārāgotthitaistāmrairanteṣvadhikapāṇḍuraiḥ
snigdhairabhrapaṭacchadairbaddhavraṇamivāmbaram

translations.english: Like to a wound covered with a torn cloth, the sky is enveloped with cool clouds, coppery with the rays of the setting Sun, and yellow at another end.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्दमारुतनिःश्वासं संध्याचन्दनरञ्जितम्
आपाण्डुजलदं भाति कामातुरमिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
mandamārutaniḥśvāsaṁ saṁdhyācandanarañjitam
āpāṇḍujaladaṁ bhāti kāmāturamivāmbaram

translations.english: The sky, having mild breezes as its breath, sprinkled with sandal-like evening rays and covered with yellow clouds, is appearing as it were like one stricken with amour.

verses.sanskrit:
एषा धर्मपरिक्लिष्टा नववारिपरिप्लुता
सीतेव शोकसंतप्ता मही बाष्पं विमुञ्चति
verses.transliteration:
eṣā dharmaparikliṣṭā navavāripariplutā
sīteva śokasaṁtaptā mahī bāṣpaṁ vimuñcati

translations.english: The earth, afflicted with perspiration and filled with new water, is emitting forth vapour like to Sitā racked with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
मेघोदरविनिर्मुक्ताः कह्लारसुखशीतलाः
शक्यमञ्जलिभिः पातुं वाताः केतकिगन्धिनः
verses.transliteration:
meghodaravinirmuktāḥ kahlārasukhaśītalāḥ
śakyamañjalibhiḥ pātuṁ vātāḥ ketakigandhinaḥ

translations.english: Ketaka smelling breezes may be drunk up in the cavity formed by putting the hands together, like to cold water discharged off the clouds and mixed with camphor.

verses.sanskrit:
एष फुल्लार्जुनः शैलः केतकैरधिवासितः
सुग्रीव इव शान्तारिर्धाराभिरभिषिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
eṣa phullārjunaḥ śailaḥ ketakairadhivāsitaḥ
sugrīva iva śāntārirdhārābhirabhiṣicyate

translations.english: This hill, having blown Arjunas and Ketakas and rid of its enemies like to Sugriva, has been bathed with showers.

verses.sanskrit:
मेघकृष्णाजिनधरा धारायज्ञोपवीतिनः
मारुतापूरितगुहाः प्राधीता इव पर्वताः
verses.transliteration:
meghakṛṣṇājinadharā dhārāyajñopavītinaḥ
mārutāpūritaguhāḥ prādhītā iva parvatāḥ

translations.english: These hillocks, having clouds for dark deerskins, heavy showers for sacred threads and having caves filled with air, are appearing like so many Brahmins who have finished their studies.

verses.sanskrit:
कशाभिरिव हैमीभिर्विद्युद्भिरिव ताडितम्
अन्तःस्तनितनिर्घोषं सवेदनमिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
kaśābhiriva haimībhirvidyudbhiriva tāḍitam
antaḥstanitanirghoṣaṁ savedanamivāmbaram

translations.english: The sky, being struck by thunders like to so many golden lashes, is, as if, groaning under a deep mental agony.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलमेघाश्रिता विद्युत्स्फुरन्ती प्रतिभाति मे
स्फुरन्ती रावणस्याङ्के वैदेहीव तपस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
nīlameghāśritā vidyutsphurantī pratibhāti me
sphurantī rāvaṇasyāṅke vaidehīva tapasvinī

translations.english: Methinks, the lighting, shining by the violet clouds, is appearing like to the poor Vaidehi at the lap of Rävaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
इमास्ता मन्मथवतां हिताः प्रतिहता दिशः
अनुलिप्ता इव घनैर्नष्टग्रहनिशाकराः
verses.transliteration:
imāstā manmathavatāṁ hitāḥ pratihatā diśaḥ
anuliptā iva ghanairnaṣṭagrahaniśākarāḥ

translations.english: These quarters, enveloped with clouds and having therefore the Moon and stars hidden, are indeed very pleasant to those who are under the influence of Cupid

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचिद्बाष्पाभिसंरुद्धान्वर्षागमसमुत्सुकान्
कुटजान्पश्य सौमित्रे पुष्टितान्गिरिसानुषु
मम शोकाभिभूतस्य कामसंदीपनान्स्थितान्
verses.transliteration:
kvacidbāṣpābhisaṁruddhānvarṣāgamasamutsukān
kuṭajānpaśya saumitre puṣṭitāngirisānuṣu
mama śokābhibhūtasya kāmasaṁdīpanānsthitān

translations.english: Behold, O Saumitri, on the summits of the hill the flowery Kuțajas enveloped with the vapour arising out of the earth, gladdened at the approach of the rainy season and exciting my amour who am stricken with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
रजः प्रशान्तं सहिमोऽद्य वायु;र्निदाघदोषप्रसराः प्रशान्ताः
स्थिता हि यात्रा वसुधाधिपानां; प्रवासिनो यान्ति नराः स्वदेशान्
verses.transliteration:
rajaḥ praśāntaṁ sahimo'dya vāyu;rnidāghadoṣaprasarāḥ praśāntāḥ
sthitā hi yātrā vasudhādhipānāṁ; pravāsino yānti narāḥ svadeśān

translations.english: (In this season) the dust is watered, the air is saturated with dews, all the evils of the summer are stopped, the kings no longer proceed on royal marches and those journeying in a foreign land return their native homes.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रस्थिता मानसवासलुब्धाः; प्रियान्विताः संप्रति चक्रवाकः
अभीक्ष्णवर्षोदकविक्षतेषु; यानानि मार्गेषु न संपतन्ति
verses.transliteration:
saṁprasthitā mānasavāsalubdhāḥ; priyānvitāḥ saṁprati cakravākaḥ
abhīkṣṇavarṣodakavikṣateṣu; yānāni mārgeṣu na saṁpatanti

translations.english: The Cakravākas along with their mates are proceeding, being desirous to live in the Mänasa Sarovara, and in consequence of incessant rains, chariots and other conveyances cannot pass along the wayfares.

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचित्प्रकाशं क्वचिदप्रकाशं; नभः प्रकीर्णाम्बुधरं विभाति
क्वचित्क्वचित्पर्वतसंनिरुद्धं; रूपं यथा शान्तमहार्णवस्य
verses.transliteration:
kvacitprakāśaṁ kvacidaprakāśaṁ; nabhaḥ prakīrṇāmbudharaṁ vibhāti
kvacitkvacitparvatasaṁniruddhaṁ; rūpaṁ yathā śāntamahārṇavasya

translations.english: Somewhere hidden, somewhere open, the sky, covered with clouds, appears like a vast ocean, being encircled here and there with hills.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रितं सर्जकदम्बपुष्पै;र्नवं जलं पर्वतधातुताम्रम्
मयूरकेकाभिरनुप्रयातं; शैलापगाः शीघ्रतरं वहन्ति
verses.transliteration:
vyāmiśritaṁ sarjakadambapuṣpai;rnavaṁ jalaṁ parvatadhātutāmram
mayūrakekābhiranuprayātaṁ; śailāpagāḥ śīghrataraṁ vahanti

translations.english: There speedily pass by the hill streams, being resounded with the cries of peacocks, carrying with the current Sarja and Kadamba flowers and having their coppery contents mixed with the metals of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
रसाकुलं षट्पदसंनिकाशं; प्रभुज्यते जम्बुफलं प्रकामम्
अनेकवर्णं पवनावधूतं; भूमौ पतत्याम्रफलं विपक्वम्
verses.transliteration:
rasākulaṁ ṣaṭpadasaṁnikāśaṁ; prabhujyate jambuphalaṁ prakāmam
anekavarṇaṁ pavanāvadhūtaṁ; bhūmau patatyāmraphalaṁ vipakvam

translations.english: People (in this season) live upon Inany a sweet rose-apple; and ripe mangoes, of diverse colours, being shaken by the wind, fall on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्युत्पताकाः सबलाक मालाः; शैलेन्द्रकूटाकृतिसंनिकाशाः
गर्जन्ति मेघाः समुदीर्णनादा; मत्तगजेन्द्रा इव संयुगस्थः
verses.transliteration:
vidyutpatākāḥ sabalāka mālāḥ; śailendrakūṭākṛtisaṁnikāśāḥ
garjanti meghāḥ samudīrṇanādā; mattagajendrā iva saṁyugasthaḥ

translations.english: The clouds, resembling the summits of a mountain, having lightnings for pennons and cranes for garlands, are muttering like to infuriated elephants in a field of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
मेघाभिकामी परिसंपतन्ती; संमोदिता भाति बलाकपङ्क्तिः
वातावधूता वरपौण्डरीकी; लम्बेव माला रचिताम्बरस्य
verses.transliteration:
meghābhikāmī parisaṁpatantī; saṁmoditā bhāti balākapaṅktiḥ
vātāvadhūtā varapauṇḍarīkī; lambeva mālā racitāmbarasya

translations.english: And rows of cranes, fond of clouds, rising up in the sky, delighted and moved by the wind, are appearing like a garland of white lotuses, spread along the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
निद्रा शनैः केशवमभ्युपैति; द्रुतं नदी सागरमभ्युपैति
हृष्टा बलाका घनमभ्युपैति; कान्ता सकामा प्रियमभ्युपैति
verses.transliteration:
nidrā śanaiḥ keśavamabhyupaiti; drutaṁ nadī sāgaramabhyupaiti
hṛṣṭā balākā ghanamabhyupaiti; kāntā sakāmā priyamabhyupaiti

translations.english: (In this part of the year) sleep is gradually overcoming the great God Nārāyaṇa, the river is flowing speedily towards the ocean, the delighted cranes are approaching the clouds and the damsels are proceeding towards their lovers.

verses.sanskrit:
जाता वनान्ताः शिखिसुप्रनृत्ता; जाताः कदम्बाः सकदम्बशाखाः
जाता वृषा गोषु समानकामा; जाता मही सस्यवनाभिरामा
verses.transliteration:
jātā vanāntāḥ śikhisupranṛttā; jātāḥ kadambāḥ sakadambaśākhāḥ
jātā vṛṣā goṣu samānakāmā; jātā mahī sasyavanābhirāmā

translations.english: The peacocks are dancing at the forest skirts, the Kadamba trees are covered with flowers, the bulls have become attached to her and the earth has become charming with corns and forests.

verses.sanskrit:
वहन्ति वर्षन्ति नदन्ति भान्ति; ध्यायन्ति नृत्यन्ति समाश्वसन्ति
नद्यो घना मत्तगजा वनान्ताः; प्रियाविनीहाः शिखिनः प्लवंगाः
verses.transliteration:
vahanti varṣanti nadanti bhānti; dhyāyanti nṛtyanti samāśvasanti
nadyo ghanā mattagajā vanāntāḥ; priyāvinīhāḥ śikhinaḥ plavaṁgāḥ

translations.english: The rivers are flowing by; the clouds are discharging waters; the infuriated elephants are emitting terrible roars; the forest-lands are growing more charming; persons, separated from their wives, are growing more anxious; the peacocks are dancing with delight and the monkeys are greatly comforted for Sugrīva's attaining to the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहर्षिताः केतकपुष्पगन्ध;माघ्राय हृष्टा वननिर्झरेषु
प्रपात शब्दाकुलिता गजेन्द्राः; सार्धं मयूरैः समदा नदन्ति
verses.transliteration:
praharṣitāḥ ketakapuṣpagandha;māghrāya hṛṣṭā vananirjhareṣu
prapāta śabdākulitā gajendrāḥ; sārdhaṁ mayūraiḥ samadā nadanti

translations.english: By the fountains in he forests, the infuriated elephants delighted with the fragrance of the Ketaka flowers and maddened with the noise of the water falls, are emitting terrible roars along with the peacocks.

verses.sanskrit:
धारानिपातैरभिहन्यमानाः; कदम्बशाखासु विलम्बमानाः
क्षणार्जितं पुष्परसावगाढं; शनैर्मदं षट्चरणास्त्यजन्ति
verses.transliteration:
dhārānipātairabhihanyamānāḥ; kadambaśākhāsu vilambamānāḥ
kṣaṇārjitaṁ puṣparasāvagāḍhaṁ; śanairmadaṁ ṣaṭcaraṇāstyajanti

translations.english: The black bees, resorting to the branches of the Kadamba trees and overwhelmed with showers, are, as if, slowly discharging their temporal juice-namely the honey of flowers collected by them ere while.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गारचूर्णोत्करसंनिकाशैः; फलैः सुपर्याप्त रसैः समृद्धैः
जम्बूद्रुमाणां प्रविभान्ति शाखा; निलीयमाना इव षट्पदौघैः
verses.transliteration:
aṅgāracūrṇotkarasaṁnikāśaiḥ; phalaiḥ suparyāpta rasaiḥ samṛddhaiḥ
jambūdrumāṇāṁ pravibhānti śākhā; nilīyamānā iva ṣaṭpadaughaiḥ

translations.english: The branches of rose-apple trees containing enough of fruits like to a collection of char coal are so appearing as if the black bees are drinking the juice thereof.

verses.sanskrit:
तडित्पताकाभिरलंकृताना;मुदीर्णगम्भीरमहारवाणाम्
विभान्ति रूपाणि बलाहकानां; रणोद्यतानामिव वारणानाम्
verses.transliteration:
taḍitpatākābhiralaṁkṛtānā;mudīrṇagambhīramahāravāṇām
vibhānti rūpāṇi balāhakānāṁ; raṇodyatānāmiva vāraṇānām

translations.english: The dense clouds, ornamented with pennonlike lightnings and emitting terrible roars, are appearing like so many elephants, mad after fighting.

verses.sanskrit:
मार्गानुगः शैलवनानुसारी; संप्रस्थितो मेघरवं निशम्य
युद्धाभिकामः प्रतिनागशङ्की; मत्तो गजेन्द्रः प्रतिसंनिवृत्तः
verses.transliteration:
mārgānugaḥ śailavanānusārī; saṁprasthito megharavaṁ niśamya
yuddhābhikāmaḥ pratināgaśaṅkī; matto gajendraḥ pratisaṁnivṛttaḥ

translations.english: The infuriated lord of elephants, following in the track and ranging in the hills and forests hearing the muttering of clouds and taking it for the uproar of another elephant, has turned back, with a view to enter into conflict with him.

verses.sanskrit:
मुक्तासकाशं सलिलं पतद्वै; सुनिर्मलं पत्रपुटेषु लग्नम्
हृष्टा विवर्णच्छदना विहंगाः; सुरेन्द्रदत्तं तृषिताः पिबन्ति
verses.transliteration:
muktāsakāśaṁ salilaṁ patadvai; sunirmalaṁ patrapuṭeṣu lagnam
hṛṣṭā vivarṇacchadanā vihaṁgāḥ; surendradattaṁ tṛṣitāḥ pibanti

translations.english: The birds, having their wings discoloured, being wet with water, delighted and thirsty, are drinking the drops of clear water, falling on leaves and discharged by the Lord of celestials*. *According to Hindu mythology Indra is the god of rains.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलेषु नीला नववारिपूर्णा; मेघेषु मेघाः प्रविभान्ति सक्ताः
दवाग्निदग्धेषु दवाग्निदग्धाः; शैलेषु शैला इव बद्धमूलाः
verses.transliteration:
nīleṣu nīlā navavāripūrṇā; megheṣu meghāḥ pravibhānti saktāḥ
davāgnidagdheṣu davāgnidagdhāḥ; śaileṣu śailā iva baddhamūlāḥ

translations.english: Clouds, big with new waters coming in, contact with violet ones are appearing as such; and sometimes, touching the hills brunt by forest-fire, are appearing like deep-rooted hills.

verses.sanskrit:
मत्ता गजेन्द्रा मुदिता गवेन्द्रा; वनेषु विश्रान्ततरा मृगेन्द्राः
रम्या नगेन्द्रा निभृता नगेन्द्राः; प्रक्रीडितो वारिधरैः सुरेन्द्रः
verses.transliteration:
mattā gajendrā muditā gavendrā; vaneṣu viśrāntatarā mṛgendrāḥ
ramyā nagendrā nibhṛtā nagendrāḥ; prakrīḍito vāridharaiḥ surendraḥ

translations.english: (In this season) the elephants are infuriated, the bulls are delighted, the lions have grown more powerful, the hills are charming-the kings are devoid of all active pursuits, are the Lord of celestials is engaged in sport with clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
वृत्ता यात्रा नरेन्द्राणां सेना प्रतिनिवर्तते
वैराणि चैव मार्गाश्च सलिलेन समीकृताः
verses.transliteration:
vṛttā yātrā narendrāṇāṁ senā pratinivartate
vairāṇi caiva mārgāśca salilena samīkṛtāḥ

translations.english: The royal marches are all stopped, and the soldiers, who have already marched are waiting in the way-hostility and wayfares have been equally blockaded by water.

verses.sanskrit:
मासि प्रौष्ठपदे ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणानां विवक्षताम्
अयमध्यायसमयः सामगानामुपस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
māsi prauṣṭhapade brahma brāhmaṇānāṁ vivakṣatām
ayamadhyāyasamayaḥ sāmagānāmupasthitaḥ

translations.english: This month of Bhādra is the time of studying for those Brahmins, who chant Sāma Vedas.

verses.sanskrit:
निवृत्तकर्मायतनो नूनं संचितसंचयः
आषाढीमभ्युपगतो भरतः कोषकाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
nivṛttakarmāyatano nūnaṁ saṁcitasaṁcayaḥ
āṣāḍhīmabhyupagato bharataḥ koṣakādhipaḥ

translations.english: Having roofed all his houses and stored up his food, Bharata, the king of Kosala has set upon the performance of Așara sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनमापूर्यमाणायाः सरय्वा वधते रयः
मां समीक्ष्य समायान्तमयोध्याया इव स्वनः
verses.transliteration:
nūnamāpūryamāṇāyāḥ sarayvā vadhate rayaḥ
māṁ samīkṣya samāyāntamayodhyāyā iva svanaḥ

translations.english: The river Saraju is now brimful with water. Seeing me return as if Ayodhyā herself is making a delightful noise.

verses.sanskrit:
इमाः स्फीतगुणा वर्षाः सुग्रीवः सुखमश्नुते
विजितारिः सदारश्च राज्ये महति च स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
imāḥ sphītaguṇā varṣāḥ sugrīvaḥ sukhamaśnute
vijitāriḥ sadāraśca rājye mahati ca sthitaḥ

translations.english: Clearly manifest are now all the signs of the rainy season and Sugrīva, rid of his enemies, established on the vast kingdom, and regaining his wives, has attained to best felicity.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु हृतदारश्च राज्याच्च महतश्च्युतः
नदीकूलमिव क्लिन्नमवसीदामि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu hṛtadāraśca rājyācca mahataścyutaḥ
nadīkūlamiva klinnamavasīdāmi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: And I am, O Laksmana, waning every day like to the banks of a river, being separated from my spouse and deprived of my vast kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकश्च मम विस्तीर्णो वर्षाश्च भृशदुर्गमाः
रावणश्च महाञ्शत्रुरपारं प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
śokaśca mama vistīrṇo varṣāśca bhṛśadurgamāḥ
rāvaṇaśca mahāñśatrurapāraṁ pratibhāti me

translations.english: Immense is my grief, inaccessible is this rainy season and mighty is my enemy, Ravana; methinks it is impossible for me to bring about the discomfiture of my foe.

verses.sanskrit:
अयात्रां चैव दृष्ट्वेमां मार्गांश्च भृशदुर्गमान्
प्रणते चैव सुग्रीवे न मया किंचिदीरितम्
verses.transliteration:
ayātrāṁ caiva dṛṣṭvemāṁ mārgāṁśca bhṛśadurgamān
praṇate caiva sugrīve na mayā kiṁcidīritam

translations.english: Owing to the unfitness of the season (for marching against my foe) and the wayfares being inaccessible, I cannot possibly request Sugrīva (to march) although he is prepared to abide by my mandate.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि चातिपरिक्लिष्टं चिराद्दारैः समागतम्
आत्मकार्यगरीयस्त्वाद्वक्तुं नेच्छामि वानरम्
verses.transliteration:
api cātiparikliṣṭaṁ cirāddāraiḥ samāgatam
ātmakāryagarīyastvādvaktuṁ necchāmi vānaram

translations.english: Moreover after a good deal of affliction he has regained his wives, and my service is of very great difficulty; so I do not wish to request that monkey-chief now.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयमेव हि विश्रम्य ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम्
उपकारं च सुग्रीवो वेत्स्यते नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
svayameva hi viśramya jñātvā kālamupāgatam
upakāraṁ ca sugrīvo vetsyate nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Forsooth, shall Sugrīva think of the benefits (he has received from me) after enjoying rest for sometime, when the time for action shall arrive.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्कालप्रतीक्षोऽहं स्थितोऽस्मि शुभलक्षण
सुग्रीवस्य नदीनां च प्रसादमनुपालयन्
verses.transliteration:
tasmātkālapratīkṣo'haṁ sthito'smi śubhalakṣaṇa
sugrīvasya nadīnāṁ ca prasādamanupālayan

translations.english: Therefore I shall, O Laksmana, live here, awaiting the pleasure of Sugrīva and the clear currents of the rivers (the autumn).

verses.sanskrit:
उपकारेण वीरो हि प्रतिकारेण युज्यते
अकृतज्ञोऽप्रतिकृतो हन्ति सत्त्ववतां मनः
verses.transliteration:
upakāreṇa vīro hi pratikāreṇa yujyate
akṛtajño'pratikṛto hanti sattvavatāṁ manaḥ

translations.english: Heroes receiving benefits, do always return them. The ungrateful lose the good wishes of the great ones.

verses.sanskrit:
अथैवमुक्तः प्रणिधाय लक्ष्मणः; कृताञ्जलिस्तत्प्रतिपूज्य भाषितम्
उवाच रामं स्वभिराम दर्शनं; प्रदर्शयन्दर्शनमात्मनः शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
athaivamuktaḥ praṇidhāya lakṣmaṇaḥ; kṛtāñjalistatpratipūjya bhāṣitam
uvāca rāmaṁ svabhirāma darśanaṁ; pradarśayandarśanamātmanaḥ śubham

translations.english: Being thus accosted, Laksmana, with folded hands, respecting highly his words, spoke to the graceful Rāma, pointing out his own welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
यथोक्तमेतत्तव सर्वमीप्सितं; नरेन्द्र कर्ता नचिराद्धरीश्वरः
शरत्प्रतीक्षः क्षमतामिमं भवा;ञ्जलप्रपातं रिपुनिग्रहे धृतः
verses.transliteration:
yathoktametattava sarvamīpsitaṁ; narendra kartā nacirāddharīśvaraḥ
śaratpratīkṣaḥ kṣamatāmimaṁ bhavā;ñjalaprapātaṁ ripunigrahe dhṛtaḥ

translations.english: Forsooth shall that lord of monkeys carry out all your wishes. Do you therefore spend here the rainy season, awaiting the autumn.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं प्राप्तं यशश्चैव कौली श्रीरभिवर्थिता
मित्राणां संग्रहः शेषस्तद्भवान्कर्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ prāptaṁ yaśaścaiva kaulī śrīrabhivarthitā
mitrāṇāṁ saṁgrahaḥ śeṣastadbhavānkartumarhati

translations.english: You have attained your kingdom, fame, and your vast ancestral wealth. It now behoveth you to perform your duties by your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि मित्रेषु कालज्ञः सततं साधु वर्तते
तस्य राज्यं च कीर्तिश्च प्रतापश्चाभिवर्धते
verses.transliteration:
yo hi mitreṣu kālajñaḥ satataṁ sādhu vartate
tasya rājyaṁ ca kīrtiśca pratāpaścābhivardhate

translations.english: Truly does his kingdom, fame and prowess increase who is cognizant of the seasonableness of time and does good to his friends.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य कोशश्च दण्डश्च मित्राण्यात्मा च भूमिप
समवेतानि सर्वाणि स राज्यं महदश्नुते
verses.transliteration:
yasya kośaśca daṇḍaśca mitrāṇyātmā ca bhūmipa
samavetāni sarvāṇi sa rājyaṁ mahadaśnute

translations.english: O king, truly does he attain to a vast kingdom, who has the same wealth, soldiery and body with his friends.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्भवान्वृत्तसंपन्नः स्थितः पथि निरत्यये
मित्रार्थमभिनीतार्थं यथावत्कर्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
tadbhavānvṛttasaṁpannaḥ sthitaḥ pathi niratyaye
mitrārthamabhinītārthaṁ yathāvatkartumarhati

translations.english: It becometh you, therefore, who are crowned with a good character, and who did wend a blameless track, to work out your friend's well being (as promised by you).

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु कालव्यतीतेषु मित्रकार्येषु वर्तते
स कृत्वा महतोऽप्यर्थान्न मित्रार्थेन युज्यते
verses.transliteration:
yastu kālavyatīteṣu mitrakāryeṣu vartate
sa kṛtvā mahato'pyarthānna mitrārthena yujyate

translations.english: He, who engage in his friend's service after the proper season is over, does nothing to his well-being, though he performs a great thing.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रियतां राघवस्यैतद्वैदेह्याः परिमार्गणम्
तदिदं वीर कार्यं ते कालातीतमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
kriyatāṁ rāghavasyaitadvaidehyāḥ parimārgaṇam
tadidaṁ vīra kāryaṁ te kālātītamariṁdama

translations.english: O slayer of foes, soon shall the time for performing your friend's service, be over; do you therefore encompass Rāghava's good, namely the searching out of Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
न च कालमतीतं ते निवेदयति कालवित्
त्वरमाणोऽपि सन्प्राज्ञस्तव राजन्वशानुगः
verses.transliteration:
na ca kālamatītaṁ te nivedayati kālavit
tvaramāṇo'pi sanprājñastava rājanvaśānugaḥ

translations.english: o king, Rāma, conversant with the scasonableness of time and wise as he is, is not inforining you of it, though the proper time is past; and though he is in hurry, he is waiting for you.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलस्य केतुः स्फीतस्य दीर्घबन्धुश्च राघवः
अप्रमेयप्रभावश्च स्वयं चाप्रतिमो गुणैः
verses.transliteration:
kulasya ketuḥ sphītasya dīrghabandhuśca rāghavaḥ
aprameyaprabhāvaśca svayaṁ cāpratimo guṇaiḥ

translations.english: Rāghava, as well as Lakşmaņa, who are the instruments of your attaining to this vast kingdom, and your friends for so long a time, are persons of incomparable prowess by virtue of their unequalled accomplishments. He has already performed your service, and it behoveth you now, O lord of monkeys, to command the foremost of monkeys to engage in his service.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तावद्भवेत्कालो व्यतीतश्चोदनादृते
चोदितस्य हि कार्यस्य भवेत्कालव्यतिक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
na hi tāvadbhavetkālo vyatītaścodanādṛte
coditasya hi kāryasya bhavetkālavyatikramaḥ

translations.english: T To engage, out of season, in a service, uncalled for, is not blameable; but to defer the performance of an action in proper time after promising is indeed an object of censure.

verses.sanskrit:
अकर्तुरपि कार्यस्य भवान्कर्ता हरीश्वर
किं पुनः प्रतिकर्तुस्ते राज्येन च धनेन च
verses.transliteration:
akarturapi kāryasya bhavānkartā harīśvara
kiṁ punaḥ pratikartuste rājyena ca dhanena ca

translations.english: O lord of monkeys, you did engage even in the service of one who does you no good, then why shall you not engage in the benefit of Rāma who has favoured you by encompassing the destruction (of Vāli) and securing for you your kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्तिमानसि विक्रान्तो वानरर्ष्क गणेश्वर
कर्तुं दाशरथेः प्रीतिमाज्ञायां किं नु सज्जसे
verses.transliteration:
śaktimānasi vikrānto vānararṣka gaṇeśvara
kartuṁ dāśaratheḥ prītimājñāyāṁ kiṁ nu sajjase

translations.english: O lord of monkeys and bears, truly you are gifted with prowess and strength, why did you not prepare yourself for satisfying Dāśarathee's commands?

verses.sanskrit:
कामं खलु शरैर्शक्तः सुरासुरमहोरगान्
वशे दाशरथिः कर्तुं त्वत्प्रतिज्ञां तु काङ्क्षते
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ khalu śarairśaktaḥ surāsuramahoragān
vaśe dāśarathiḥ kartuṁ tvatpratijñāṁ tu kāṅkṣate

translations.english: Dāśarathee himself is capable of subduing the celestials, Asuras and great serpents-he is simply awaiting the fulfilment of your promise.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणत्यागाविशङ्केन कृतं तेन तव प्रियम्
तस्य मार्गाम वैदेहीं पृथिव्यामपि चाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
prāṇatyāgāviśaṅkena kṛtaṁ tena tava priyam
tasya mārgāma vaidehīṁ pṛthivyāmapi cāmbare

translations.english: He has performed a great service at the risk of his life-we shall therefore find out Vaidehī whether she is in this earth or in the welkin,

verses.sanskrit:
न देवा न च गन्धर्वा नासुरा न मरुद्गणाः
न च यक्षा भयं तस्य कुर्युः किमुत राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
na devā na ca gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
na ca yakṣā bhayaṁ tasya kuryuḥ kimuta rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: Even the celestials, Dānavas, Gandharabas, Asuras, Mārutas, Yakşas are afraid of him in the battle-field-what of the insignificant Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेवं शक्तियुक्तस्य पूर्वं प्रियकृतस्तथा
रामस्यार्हसि पिङ्गेश कर्तुं सर्वात्मना प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
tadevaṁ śaktiyuktasya pūrvaṁ priyakṛtastathā
rāmasyārhasi piṅgeśa kartuṁ sarvātmanā priyam

translations.english: O lord of monkeys, it therefore behoveth you to do good by all means to the powerful Rāma, who benefited you before.

verses.sanskrit:
नाधस्तादवनौ नाप्सु गतिर्नोपरि चाम्बरे
कस्यचित्सज्जतेऽस्माकं कपीश्वर तवाज्ञया
verses.transliteration:
nādhastādavanau nāpsu gatirnopari cāmbare
kasyacitsajjate'smākaṁ kapīśvara tavājñayā

translations.english: O lord of monkeys, who is there among us, who shall not at your command proceed to: water, sky or the region under the earth?

verses.sanskrit:
तदाज्ञापय कः किं ते कृते वसतु कुत्रचित्
हरयो ह्यप्रधृष्यास्ते सन्ति कोट्यग्रतोऽनघ
verses.transliteration:
tadājñāpaya kaḥ kiṁ te kṛte vasatu kutracit
harayo hyapradhṛṣyāste santi koṭyagrato'nagha

translations.english: O blameless one, there are more than one koți of invincible monkeys under you, do you command, who shall proceed and to what quarter?

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा काले साधुनिवेदितम्
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसंपन्नश्चकार मतिमुत्तमाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā kāle sādhuniveditam
sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṁpannaścakāra matimuttamām

translations.english: Hearing these words of Hanumān, said on a very proper occasion, the intelligent Sugrīva, made up his mind for a worthy end.

verses.sanskrit:
स संदिदेशाभिमतं नीलं नित्यकृतोद्यमम्
दिक्षु सर्वासु सर्वेषां सैन्यानामुपसंग्रहे
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁdideśābhimataṁ nīlaṁ nityakṛtodyamam
dikṣu sarvāsu sarveṣāṁ sainyānāmupasaṁgrahe

translations.english: Thereupon the highly intelligent Sugrīva ordered the ever active Neela, to collect soldiers from various quarters. Do you so arrange as all my hosts and soldiers with their commanders soon come here.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वन्तपालाः प्लवगाः शीघ्रगा व्यवसायिनः
समानयन्तु ते सैन्यं त्वरिताः शासनान्मम
स्वयं चानन्तरं सैन्यं भवानेवानुपश्यतु
verses.transliteration:
ye tvantapālāḥ plavagāḥ śīghragā vyavasāyinaḥ
samānayantu te sainyaṁ tvaritāḥ śāsanānmama
svayaṁ cānantaraṁ sainyaṁ bhavānevānupaśyatu

translations.english: Do you soon bring here at my behest all the energetic and quick-coursing monkeys and commanders spreading their conquests to the end of the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिपञ्चरात्रादूर्ध्वं यः प्राप्नुयान्नेह वानरः
तस्य प्राणान्तिको दण्डो नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration:
tripañcarātrādūrdhvaṁ yaḥ prāpnuyānneha vānaraḥ
tasya prāṇāntiko daṇḍo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā

translations.english: (After their arrival) do you yourself inspect and count all those monkeys. He who shall not reach here within fifteen days shall be punished with the loss of his life.

verses.sanskrit:
हरींश्च वृद्धानुपयातु साङ्गदो; भवान्ममाज्ञामधिकृत्य निश्चिताम्
इति व्यवस्थां हरिपुंगवेश्वरो; विधाय वेश्म प्रविवेश वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
harīṁśca vṛddhānupayātu sāṅgado; bhavānmamājñāmadhikṛtya niścitām
iti vyavasthāṁ haripuṁgaveśvaro; vidhāya veśma praviveśa vīryavān

translations.english: There is no need of scrutinizing my orders. Abiding by my order, do you see along with Angada all the elderly monkeys. having thus arranged, that best of monkeys entered the inner apartment.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु संज्ञामुपागम्य मुहूर्तान्मतिमान्पुनः
मनःस्थामपि वैदेहीं चिन्तयामास राघवः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu saṁjñāmupāgamya muhūrtānmatimānpunaḥ
manaḥsthāmapi vaidehīṁ cintayāmāsa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: And regaining his sense after sometime, the highly intelligent king-Räghava began to think of Vaidehĩ although always present in his mind.

verses.sanskrit:
आसीनः पर्वतस्याग्रे हेमधातुविभूषिते
शारदं गगनं दृष्ट्व जगाम मनसा प्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
āsīnaḥ parvatasyāgre hemadhātuvibhūṣite
śāradaṁ gaganaṁ dṛṣṭva jagāma manasā priyām

translations.english: And beholding the clear sky void of lightnings and clouds and filled with the noise of Sārasas, Rāghava began to lament piteously, stationing himself on the summit of the hill ornamented with metals of golden hue. And beholding the autumnal sky he engaged in the meditation of his beloved spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
सारसारवसंनादैः सारसारवनादिनी
याश्रमे रमते बाला साद्य मे रमते कथम्
verses.transliteration:
sārasāravasaṁnādaiḥ sārasāravanādinī
yāśrame ramate bālā sādya me ramate katham

translations.english: How shall that Sarasa-voiced damsel be pleased to-day, who, while sporting in the hermitage, used to warble like Sārasas, to invite them.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पितांश्चासनान्दृष्ट्वा काञ्चनानिव निर्मलान्
कथं स रमते बाला पश्यन्ती मामपश्यती
verses.transliteration:
puṣpitāṁścāsanāndṛṣṭvā kāñcanāniva nirmalān
kathaṁ sa ramate bālā paśyantī māmapaśyatī

translations.english: Beholding Asana trees, as if covered with golden flowers and not beholding me how shall that damsel be pleased?

verses.sanskrit:
या पुरा कलहंसानां स्वरेण कलभाषिणी
बुध्यते चारुसर्वाङ्गी साद्य मे बुध्यते कथम्
verses.transliteration:
yā purā kalahaṁsānāṁ svareṇa kalabhāṣiṇī
budhyate cārusarvāṅgī sādya me budhyate katham

translations.english: How that exquisitely fine damsel having a sweet voice shall be pleased to-day, who used formerly to awake at the sounds of the drakes.?

verses.sanskrit:
निःस्वनं चक्रवाकानां निशम्य सहचारिणाम्
पुण्डरीकविशालाक्षी कथमेषा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
niḥsvanaṁ cakravākānāṁ niśamya sahacāriṇām
puṇḍarīkaviśālākṣī kathameṣā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Hearing the noise of her companionsCakravākas, how shali that one, of expansive eyes resembling lotuses, live?

verses.sanskrit:
सरांसि सरितो वापीः काननानि वनानि च
तां विना मृगशावाक्षीं चरन्नाद्य सुखं लभे
verses.transliteration:
sarāṁsi sarito vāpīḥ kānanāni vanāni ca
tāṁ vinā mṛgaśāvākṣīṁ carannādya sukhaṁ labhe

translations.english: Without her having the eyes of a fawn, I do not attain to felicity to-day, ranging at large by ponds, streams, pools and in forests and woods.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि तां मद्वियोगाच्च सौकुमार्याच्च भामिनीम्
न दूरं पीडयेत्कामः शरद्गुणनिरन्तरः
verses.transliteration:
api tāṁ madviyogācca saukumāryācca bhāminīm
na dūraṁ pīḍayetkāmaḥ śaradguṇanirantaraḥ

translations.english: Forsooth shall Cupid excited by the approach of the autumn, distress her the more on account of my separation and her personal charms.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमादि नरश्रेष्ठो विललाप नृपात्मजः
विहंग इव सारङ्गः सलिलं त्रिदशेश्वरात्
verses.transliteration:
evamādi naraśreṣṭho vilalāpa nṛpātmajaḥ
vihaṁga iva sāraṅgaḥ salilaṁ tridaśeśvarāt

translations.english: Thus bewailed that best son of a king like to the bird Sāranga soliciting water from the lord of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
ततश्चञ्चूर्य रम्येषु फलार्थी गिरिसानुषु
ददर्श पर्युपावृत्तो लक्ष्मीवाँल्लक्ष्मणोऽग्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
tataścañcūrya ramyeṣu phalārthī girisānuṣu
dadarśa paryupāvṛtto lakṣmīvā̐llakṣmaṇo'grajam

translations.english: And the graceful Lakşmaņa, returning from the picturesque mountain-summits where he had sojourned in quest of fruits, beheld his elder brother.

verses.sanskrit:
तं चिन्तया दुःसहया परीतं; विसंज्ञमेकं विजने मनस्वी
भ्रातुर्विषादात्परितापदीनः; समीक्ष्य सौमित्रिरुवाच रामम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ cintayā duḥsahayā parītaṁ; visaṁjñamekaṁ vijane manasvī
bhrāturviṣādātparitāpadīnaḥ; samīkṣya saumitriruvāca rāmam

translations.english: And beholding in that lonely forest his brother, racked with anxious thoughts hard to bear and almost beside himself (with grief) the high-minded Saumitri, prompted by his brother's grief, spoke to him very poorly, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किमार्य कामस्य वशंगतेन; किमात्मपौरुष्यपराभवेन
अयं सदा संहृइयते समाधिः; किमत्र योगेन निवर्तितेन
verses.transliteration:
kimārya kāmasya vaśaṁgatena; kimātmapauruṣyaparābhavena
ayaṁ sadā saṁhṛiyate samādhiḥ; kimatra yogena nivartitena

translations.english: O worshipful one, what have you perpetrated by placing yourself under the control of passions and defeating your manliness? Your deep and devout meditation has been purloined by your grief; and it is by religious contemplation that your grief shall be terminated now.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रियाभियोगं मनसः प्रसादं; समाधियोगानुगतं च कालम्
सहायसामर्थ्यमदीनसत्त्व; स्वकर्महेतुं च कुरुष्व हेतुम्
verses.transliteration:
kriyābhiyogaṁ manasaḥ prasādaṁ; samādhiyogānugataṁ ca kālam
sahāyasāmarthyamadīnasattva; svakarmahetuṁ ca kuruṣva hetum

translations.english: O brother, after going through the ceremonies of bathing and so forth, and acquiring peace, do you bring all your time under your control by virtue of the concentration of soul; and being of unmitigated strength do you resort to power and help, the key-notes for the accomplishment of your great object.

verses.sanskrit:
न जानकी मानववंशनाथ; त्वया सनाथा सुलभा परेण
न चाग्निचूडां ज्वलितामुपेत्य; न दह्यते वीरवरार्ह कश्चित्
verses.transliteration:
na jānakī mānavavaṁśanātha; tvayā sanāthā sulabhā pareṇa
na cāgnicūḍāṁ jvalitāmupetya; na dahyate vīravarārha kaścit

translations.english: O lord of men, Jānakī, husbanded by you, is not capable of being easily possessed by others. O hero who getting at a flame of fire, does not burn himself?

verses.sanskrit:
सलक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणमप्रधृष्यं; स्वभावजं वाक्यमुवाच रामः
हितं च पथ्यं च नयप्रसक्तं; ससामधर्मार्थसमाहितं च
verses.transliteration:
salakṣmaṇaṁ lakṣmaṇamapradhṛṣyaṁ; svabhāvajaṁ vākyamuvāca rāmaḥ
hitaṁ ca pathyaṁ ca nayaprasaktaṁ; sasāmadharmārthasamāhitaṁ ca

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, gifted with royal marks, addressing him with natural and resolute words and saying:—What you had said, is sound, well-meaning, sanctioned by polity and speaks of piety, wealth and forgiveness. It should therefore, without the least doubt, be performed by me. It behoveth me to engage in contemplation about the eternal truth regarding the Deity and in ascetic observances. Oh else O Prince, it is not proper to think of the fruits of a difficult, highly developed and energetic action.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ पद्मपलाशाक्षीं मैथिलीमनुचिन्तयन्
उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामो मुखेन परिशुष्यता
verses.transliteration:
atha padmapalāśākṣīṁ maithilīmanucintayan
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṁ rāmo mukhena pariśuṣyatā

translations.english: Thereupon thinking of Maithelee, having eyes resembling lotus-petals, Rāma spoke to Laks mana with dried countenance.

verses.sanskrit:
तर्पयित्वा सहस्राक्षः सलिलेन वसुंधराम्
निर्वर्तयित्वा सस्यानि कृतकर्मा व्यवस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tarpayitvā sahasrākṣaḥ salilena vasuṁdharām
nirvartayitvā sasyāni kṛtakarmā vyavasthitaḥ

translations.english: Having satisfied the earth with a profuse discharge of water, produced crops and thus finished his work, the thousand eyed Deity is sitting silent.

verses.sanskrit:
स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषाः शैलद्रुमपुरोगमाः
विसृज्य सलिलं मेघाः परिश्रान्ता नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
snigdhagambhīranirghoṣāḥ śailadrumapurogamāḥ
visṛjya salilaṁ meghāḥ pariśrāntā nṛpātmaja

translations.english: O son of a king, the clouds, muttering a long and deep sound and approaching the hills and frees, are calmed having discharged their liquid contents.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामः श्यामीकृत्वा दिशो दश
विमदा इव मातङ्गाः शान्तवेगाः पयोधराः
verses.transliteration:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ śyāmīkṛtvā diśo daśa
vimadā iva mātaṅgāḥ śāntavegāḥ payodharāḥ

translations.english: Having made the ten quarters dark blue, the clouds, resembling blue lotuses, have become calm, like to elephants without temporal juice.

verses.sanskrit:
जलगर्भा महावेगाः कुटजार्जुनगन्धिनः
चरित्वा विरताः सौम्य वृष्टिवाताः समुद्यताः
verses.transliteration:
jalagarbhā mahāvegāḥ kuṭajārjunagandhinaḥ
caritvā viratāḥ saumya vṛṣṭivātāḥ samudyatāḥ

translations.english: O gentle one, high gales accompanied with rains, big with water and fragrant with Kutaja and Arjuna flowers being driven before hither and thither, have now become silent.

verses.sanskrit:
घनानां वारणानां च मयूराणां च लक्ष्मण
नादः प्रस्रवणानां च प्रशान्तः सहसानघ
verses.transliteration:
ghanānāṁ vāraṇānāṁ ca mayūrāṇāṁ ca lakṣmaṇa
nādaḥ prasravaṇānāṁ ca praśāntaḥ sahasānagha

translations.english: O innocent Laksmana, the sounds of clouds, elephants, peacocks, and fountains, have been all stopped.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवृष्टा महामेघैर्निर्मलाश्चित्रसानवः
अनुलिप्ता इवाभान्ति गिरयश्चन्द्ररश्मिभिः
verses.transliteration:
abhivṛṣṭā mahāmeghairnirmalāścitrasānavaḥ
anuliptā ivābhānti girayaścandraraśmibhiḥ

translations.english: Hills, having variegated summits, being washed by dense clouds and thus free from dirt and impurities, do appear elegant being sprinkled by the rays of the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शयन्ति शरन्नद्यः पुलिनानि शनैः शनैः
नवसंगमसव्रीडा जघनानीव योषितः
verses.transliteration:
darśayanti śarannadyaḥ pulināni śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
navasaṁgamasavrīḍā jaghanānīva yoṣitaḥ

translations.english: The rivers in this season of autumn have been gradually showing their banks.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसन्नसलिलाः सौम्य कुररीभिर्विनादिताः
चक्रवाकगणाकीर्णा विभान्ति सलिलाशयाः
verses.transliteration:
prasannasalilāḥ saumya kurarībhirvināditāḥ
cakravākagaṇākīrṇā vibhānti salilāśayāḥ

translations.english: O you of excellent looks, the ponds in this season) appear exquisitely fine, being filled with Kurara birds and Cakravākas.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यबद्धवैराणां जिगीषूणां नृपात्मज
उद्योगसमयः सौम्य पार्थिवानामुपस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
anyonyabaddhavairāṇāṁ jigīṣūṇāṁ nṛpātmaja
udyogasamayaḥ saumya pārthivānāmupasthitaḥ

translations.english: O son of king, this is the time of preparation for inimical kings, desirous of defeating one another.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं सा प्रथमा यात्रा पार्थिवानां नृपात्मज
न च पश्यामि सुग्रीवमुद्योगं वा तथाविधम्
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ sā prathamā yātrā pārthivānāṁ nṛpātmaja
na ca paśyāmi sugrīvamudyogaṁ vā tathāvidham

translations.english: O son of king, this is the best time for royal marches, but I do not find Sugrīva preparing himself for that end.

verses.sanskrit:
चत्वारो वार्षिका मासा गता वर्षशतोपमाः
मम शोकाभितप्तस्य सौम्य सीतामपश्यतः
verses.transliteration:
catvāro vārṣikā māsā gatā varṣaśatopamāḥ
mama śokābhitaptasya saumya sītāmapaśyataḥ

translations.english: Stricken as I am with grief, these four months, the season of rains, appeared to me like a hundred year, not beholding Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियाविहीने दुःखार्ते हृतराज्ये विवासिते
कृपां न कुरुते राजा सुग्रीवो मयि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
priyāvihīne duḥkhārte hṛtarājye vivāsite
kṛpāṁ na kurute rājā sugrīvo mayi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: O Laksmana, Sugriva, is not inclined to show any commiseration towards me, who am separated from my beloved spouse, deprived of my kingdom, banished and stricken with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाथो हृतराज्योऽयं रावणेन च धर्षितः
दीनो दूरगृहः कामी मां चैव शरणं गतः
verses.transliteration:
anātho hṛtarājyo'yaṁ rāvaṇena ca dharṣitaḥ
dīno dūragṛhaḥ kāmī māṁ caiva śaraṇaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Regarding me as one without any to back him, deprived of his kingdom, insulted my Rāvaņa, wretched, of a distant land, under the influence of amour and therefore seeking his help, (Sugrīva has not felt pity for me).

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येतैः कारणैः सौम्य सुग्रीवस्य दुरात्मनः
अहं वानरराजस्य परिभूतः परंतप
verses.transliteration:
ityetaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saumya sugrīvasya durātmanaḥ
ahaṁ vānararājasya paribhūtaḥ paraṁtapa

translations.english: O subduer of foes, O you of excellent looks, for these reasons, I have been insulted by that vicious-souled king of monkeys-Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
स कालं परिसंख्याय सीतायाः परिमार्गणे
कृतार्थः समयं कृत्वा दुर्मतिर्नावबुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
sa kālaṁ parisaṁkhyāya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe
kṛtārthaḥ samayaṁ kṛtvā durmatirnāvabudhyate

translations.english: Having appointed the time time to institute enquiries about Sītā, that wicked-minded one has now forgot it on the accession of his new dignity.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं प्रविश्य च किष्किन्धां ब्रूहि वानरपुंगवम्
मूर्खं ग्राम्य सुखे सक्तं सुग्रीवं वचनान्मम
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ praviśya ca kiṣkindhāṁ brūhi vānarapuṁgavam
mūrkhaṁ grāmya sukhe saktaṁ sugrīvaṁ vacanānmama

translations.english: Do you therefore repair to Kişkindhā and speak of me to that stupid lord of monkeys Sugriva, addicted to rural enjoyments.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थिनामुपपन्नानां पूर्वं चाप्युपकारिणाम्
आशां संश्रुत्य यो हन्ति स लोके पुरुषाधमः
verses.transliteration:
arthināmupapannānāṁ pūrvaṁ cāpyupakāriṇām
āśāṁ saṁśrutya yo hanti sa loke puruṣādhamaḥ

translations.english: And do you tell him-'He, who breaks his promise made to a powerful benefactor who solicits his favour, is regarded by people as vile.

verses.sanskrit:
शुभं वा यदि वा पापं यो हि वाक्यमुदीरितम्
सत्येन परिगृह्णाति स वीरः पुरुषोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
śubhaṁ vā yadi vā pāpaṁ yo hi vākyamudīritam
satyena parigṛhṇāti sa vīraḥ puruṣottamaḥ

translations.english: He is a true hero and an excellent person who verifies his words whether good or bad.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतार्था ह्यकृतार्थानां मित्राणां न भवन्ति ये
तान्मृतानपि क्रव्यादः कृतघ्नान्नोपभुञ्जते
verses.transliteration:
kṛtārthā hyakṛtārthānāṁ mitrāṇāṁ na bhavanti ye
tānmṛtānapi kravyādaḥ kṛtaghnānnopabhuñjate

translations.english: Ungrateful they are who do not, after attaining their ends, engage in the service of those of their friends who have not accomplished their objects; even those living on raw flesh do not feed on their gore after their death.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं काञ्चनपृष्ठस्य विकृष्टस्य मया रणे
द्रष्टुमिच्छन्ति चापस्य रूपं विद्युद्गणोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ kāñcanapṛṣṭhasya vikṛṣṭasya mayā raṇe
draṣṭumicchanti cāpasya rūpaṁ vidyudgaṇopamam

translations.english: And ask him if he wishes to behold in battlefield the golden bow resembling a lightning.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरं ज्यातलनिर्घोषं क्रुद्धस्य मम संयुगे
निर्घोषमिव वज्रस्य पुनः संश्रोतुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
ghoraṁ jyātalanirghoṣaṁ kruddhasya mama saṁyuge
nirghoṣamiva vajrasya punaḥ saṁśrotumicchati

translations.english: And ask him more, if he wishes to hear the terrible twang of my bow resembling the noise of thunder, when I am enraged in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
काममेवंगतेऽप्यस्य परिज्ञाते पराक्रमे
त्वत्सहायस्य मे वीर न चिन्ता स्यान्नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
kāmamevaṁgate'pyasya parijñāte parākrame
tvatsahāyasya me vīra na cintā syānnṛpātmaja

translations.english: O hero, O son of a king, when apprised of my prowess assisted by you, will he not recapitulate in his mind (that he may be destroyed by us like to Vali)?

verses.sanskrit:
यदर्थमयमारम्भः कृतः परपुरंजय
समयं नाभिजानाति कृतार्थः प्लवगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
yadarthamayamārambhaḥ kṛtaḥ parapuraṁjaya
samayaṁ nābhijānāti kṛtārthaḥ plavageśvaraḥ

translations.english: O conqueror of enemies' cities, does not that lord of monkeys, after accomplishing his object, think of the conditions under which our friendship was contracted?

verses.sanskrit:
वर्षासमयकालं तु प्रतिज्ञाय हरीश्वरः
व्यतीतांश्चतुरो मासान्विहरन्नावबुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
varṣāsamayakālaṁ tu pratijñāya harīśvaraḥ
vyatītāṁścaturo māsānviharannāvabudhyate

translations.english: Does not that lord of monkeys think that he has spent four months in enjoyments, having promised and appointed the season, after rains, (for making) enquiries about Sītā?

verses.sanskrit:
सामात्यपरिषत्क्रीडन्पानमेवोपसेवते
शोकदीनेषु नास्मासु सुग्रीवः कुरुते दयाम्
verses.transliteration:
sāmātyapariṣatkrīḍanpānamevopasevate
śokadīneṣu nāsmāsu sugrīvaḥ kurute dayām

translations.english: Does not Sugrīva feel pity for us, who are racked with sorrow, being addicted to drinking with friends and counsellors?

verses.sanskrit:
उच्यतां गच्छ सुग्रीवस्त्वया वत्स महाबल
मम रोषस्य यद्रूपं ब्रूयाश्चैनमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
ucyatāṁ gaccha sugrīvastvayā vatsa mahābala
mama roṣasya yadrūpaṁ brūyāścainamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: Do you go, O hero, O you of mighty strength and relate to Sugrīva these my angry words.

verses.sanskrit:
न च संकुचितः पन्था येन वाली हतो गतः
समये तिष्ठ सुग्रीवमा वालिपथमन्वगाः
verses.transliteration:
na ca saṁkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ
samaye tiṣṭha sugrīvamā vālipathamanvagāḥ

translations.english: 'O Sugriva, do not neglect your promise and wend your way trodden by Vāli.

verses.sanskrit:
एक एव रणे वाली शरेण निहतो मया
त्वां तु सत्यादतिक्रान्तं हनिष्यामि सबान्धवम्
verses.transliteration:
eka eva raṇe vālī śareṇa nihato mayā
tvāṁ tu satyādatikrāntaṁ haniṣyāmi sabāndhavam

translations.english: I killed Vāli only with my shaft in the battlefield; but if you did deviate from the path of truth I shall destroy you along with your kinsmen and relatives.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेवं विहिते कार्ये यद्धितं पुरुषर्षभ
तत्तद्ब्रूहि नरश्रेष्ठ त्वर कालव्यतिक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tadevaṁ vihite kārye yaddhitaṁ puruṣarṣabha
tattadbrūhi naraśreṣṭha tvara kālavyatikramaḥ

translations.english: O you best of men, do you speedily relate to him all those benefits which we shall reap by his actions, for the proper season is well-nigh past.

verses.sanskrit:
कुरुष्व सत्यं मयि वानरेश्वर; प्रतिश्रुतं धर्ममवेक्ष्य शाश्वतम्
मा वालिनं प्रेत्य गतो यमक्षयं; त्वमद्य पश्येर्मम चोदितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
kuruṣva satyaṁ mayi vānareśvara; pratiśrutaṁ dharmamavekṣya śāśvatam
mā vālinaṁ pretya gato yamakṣayaṁ; tvamadya paśyermama coditaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: O best of monkeys, do you carry out your promise remembering the eternal existence of virtue. Do you not behold the spirit of Väli in the abode of Death, being killed by the shaft discharged by me.

verses.sanskrit:
स पूर्वजं तीव्रविवृद्धकोपं; लालप्यमानं प्रसमीक्ष्य दीनम्
चकार तीव्रां मतिमुग्रतेजा; हरीश्वरमानववंशनाथः
verses.transliteration:
sa pūrvajaṁ tīvravivṛddhakopaṁ; lālapyamānaṁ prasamīkṣya dīnam
cakāra tīvrāṁ matimugratejā; harīśvaramānavavaṁśanāthaḥ

translations.english: Beholding his elder brother thus enraged and bewailing, the fiery-spirited Laksmana, the best of men, became enraged with Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
स कामिनं दीनमदीनसत्त्वः; शोकाभिपन्नं समुदीर्णकोपम्
नरेन्द्रसूनुर्नरदेवपुत्रं; रामानुजः पूर्वजमित्युवाच
verses.transliteration:
sa kāminaṁ dīnamadīnasattvaḥ; śokābhipannaṁ samudīrṇakopam
narendrasūnurnaradevaputraṁ; rāmānujaḥ pūrvajamityuvāca

translations.english: Lakşmaņa again addressed his high-minded elder brother, the son of a king, influenced by passion, stricken with grief, and poorly, with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
न वानरः स्थास्यति साधुवृत्ते; न मंस्यते कार्यफलानुषङ्गान्
न भक्ष्यते वानरराज्यलक्ष्मीं; तथा हि नाभिक्रमतेऽस्य बुद्धिः
verses.transliteration:
na vānaraḥ sthāsyati sādhuvṛtte; na maṁsyate kāryaphalānuṣaṅgān
na bhakṣyate vānararājyalakṣmīṁ; tathā hi nābhikramate'sya buddhiḥ

translations.english: That monkey shall not follow the actions of the pious, shall not think of the great fruit (the accession of kingdom) reaped by our friendship; kingdom because he has not the right understanding to make good his promise.

verses.sanskrit:
मतिक्षयाद्ग्राम्यसुखेषु सक्त;स्तव प्रसादाप्रतिकारबुद्धिः
हतोऽग्रजं पश्यतु वालिनं स; न राज्यमेवं विगुणस्य देयम्
verses.transliteration:
matikṣayādgrāmyasukheṣu sakta;stava prasādāpratikārabuddhiḥ
hato'grajaṁ paśyatu vālinaṁ sa; na rājyamevaṁ viguṇasya deyam

translations.english: Owing to the wane of his understanding in consequence of your favour he is addicted to rural enjoyments and has forgot to return your benefits. O hero, killed let him espy his elder brother Vāli. It is not proper to confer kingdom upon that wicked-minded one.

verses.sanskrit:
न धारये कोपमुदीर्णवेगं; निहन्मि सुग्रीवमसत्यमद्य
हरिप्रवीरैः सह वालिपुत्रो; नरेन्द्रपत्न्या विचयं करोतु
verses.transliteration:
na dhāraye kopamudīrṇavegaṁ; nihanmi sugrīvamasatyamadya
haripravīraiḥ saha vāliputro; narendrapatnyā vicayaṁ karotu

translations.english: I am unable to bear the outburst of my ire forsooth shall I kill today, that liar Sugrīva. May the son of Vāli with other principal monkeys engage in quest of that daughter of a king.

verses.sanskrit:
तमात्तबाणासनमुत्पतन्तं; निवेदितार्थं रणचण्डकोपम्
उवच रामः परवीरहन्ता; स्ववेक्षितं सानुनयं च वाक्यम्
verses.transliteration:
tamāttabāṇāsanamutpatantaṁ; niveditārthaṁ raṇacaṇḍakopam
uvaca rāmaḥ paravīrahantā; svavekṣitaṁ sānunayaṁ ca vākyam

translations.english: Beholding him rise up from the seat with bow in his hand and greatly wrought up with anger and hearing him thus announce his intention about the destruction of Sugriva, Rama, the slayer of foes, spoke to him the following humble words worthy of being spoken on that occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि वै त्वद्विधो लोके पापमेवं समाचरेत्
पापमार्येण यो हन्ति स वीरः पुरुषोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
na hi vai tvadvidho loke pāpamevaṁ samācaret
pāpamāryeṇa yo hanti sa vīraḥ puruṣottamaḥ

translations.english: Persons like you on this earth do not perpetrate the crime of destroying their friends. He is truly a great hero and an excellent person who subdues anger by his right understanding, O Lakṣmaṇa, it is not proper for you to bring about the destruction of your friend, do you follow your former friendship and good feelings.

verses.sanskrit:
सामोपहितया वाचा रूक्षाणि परिवर्जयन्
वक्तुमर्हसि सुग्रीवं व्यतीतं कालपर्यये
verses.transliteration:
sāmopahitayā vācā rūkṣāṇi parivarjayan
vaktumarhasi sugrīvaṁ vyatītaṁ kālaparyaye

translations.english: Avoiding harsh words do you address Sugrīva, who has violated his promise, with soothing words.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽ ग्रजेनानुशिष्टार्थो यथावत्पुरुषर्षभः
प्रविवेश पुरीं वीरो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
verses.transliteration:
so' grajenānuśiṣṭārtho yathāvatpuruṣarṣabhaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ vīro lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā

translations.english: Being thus duly counselled by his elder brother, that best of men, the heroic Laks maņa-the slayer of foes, entered the city.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शुभमतिः प्राज्ञो भ्रातुः प्रियहिते रतः
लक्ष्मणः प्रतिसंरब्धो जगाम भवनं कपेः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śubhamatiḥ prājño bhrātuḥ priyahite rataḥ
lakṣmaṇaḥ pratisaṁrabdho jagāma bhavanaṁ kapeḥ

translations.english: Thereupon the highly intelligent Lakşmaņa of right understanding, and ever intent upon the welfare of his brother, taking up a bow like to Indra's, resembling the summit of a hill and terrible as Death himself, entered, wrought up with ire, the abode of the king of monkeys like the hill Mandāra.

verses.sanskrit:
यथोक्तकारी वचनमुत्तरं चैव सोत्तरम्
बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या मत्त्वा रामानुजस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
yathoktakārī vacanamuttaraṁ caiva sottaram
bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā mattvā rāmānujastadā

translations.english: Intelligent like Bșhaspati and ever abiding by his elder brother's behest, Laksmana, revolving in his mind what he should say as well as Sugrīva's answers, and enveloped with the fire of anger arising from the excitement of his brother's amour, and therefore displeased, proceeded quick as air.

verses.sanskrit:
शिलाश्च शकलीकुर्वन्पद्भ्यां गज इवाशुगः
दूरमेकपदं त्यक्त्वा ययौ कार्यवशाद्द्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
śilāśca śakalīkurvanpadbhyāṁ gaja ivāśugaḥ
dūramekapadaṁ tyaktvā yayau kāryavaśāddrutam

translations.english: And on he proceeded, felling down by his velocity, Sāla, Tāla, and Aśvakarņa trees, throwing aside the mountain summits and other trees, breaking rocks into pieces with his feet and striding very quickly like to a fleet-coursing elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
तामपश्यद्बलाकीर्णां हरिराजमहापुरीम्
दुर्गामिक्ष्वाकुशार्दूलः किष्किन्धां गिरिसंकटे
verses.transliteration:
tāmapaśyadbalākīrṇāṁ harirājamahāpurīm
durgāmikṣvākuśārdūlaḥ kiṣkindhāṁ girisaṁkaṭe

translations.english: And that best of Ikşwakus, beheld that splendid city of the king of monkeys hard to enter, surrounded by monkey-herds, and mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
रोषात्प्रस्फुरमाणौष्ठः सुग्रीवं प्रति कल्ष्मणः
ददर्श वानरान्भीमान्किष्किन्धाया बहिश्चरान्
verses.transliteration:
roṣātprasphuramāṇauṣṭhaḥ sugrīvaṁ prati kalṣmaṇaḥ
dadarśa vānarānbhīmānkiṣkindhāyā bahiścarān

translations.english: And having his lips swollen with anger for Sugrīva, Lakşmaņa beheld the terrible monkeys walking outside the city.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलशृङ्गाणि शतशः प्रवृद्धांश्च महीरुहान्
जगृहुः कुञ्जरप्रख्या वानराः पर्वतान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
śailaśṛṅgāṇi śataśaḥ pravṛddhāṁśca mahīruhān
jagṛhuḥ kuñjaraprakhyā vānarāḥ parvatāntare

translations.english: Beholding that best of men-Laksmana, the monkeys resembling elephants entered the mountainous stronghold and took up the summits of the hill and huge trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्गृहीतप्रहरणान्हरीन्दृष्ट्वा तु लक्ष्मणः
बभूव द्विगुणं क्रुद्धो बह्विन्धन इवानलः
verses.transliteration:
tāngṛhītapraharaṇānharīndṛṣṭvā tu lakṣmaṇaḥ
babhūva dviguṇaṁ kruddho bahvindhana ivānalaḥ

translations.english: And observing them armed, Lakṣmaṇa was doubly inflamed with anger like to fire kindled with fuels.

verses.sanskrit:
तं ते भयपरीताङ्गाः क्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा प्लवंगमाः
कालमृत्युयुगान्ताभं शतशो विद्रुता दिशः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ te bhayaparītāṅgāḥ kruddhaṁ dṛṣṭvā plavaṁgamāḥ
kālamṛtyuyugāntābhaṁ śataśo vidrutā diśaḥ

translations.english: Beholding Lakṣmaṇa, highly enraged, terrible as Death himself at the time of dissolution, the monkeys, stricken with fear, fled away, by hundreds, into various quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुग्रीवभवनं प्रविश्य हरिपुंगवाः
क्रोधमागमनं चैव लक्ष्मणस्य न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sugrīvabhavanaṁ praviśya haripuṁgavāḥ
krodhamāgamanaṁ caiva lakṣmaṇasya nyavedayan

translations.english: Thereat those foremost of monkeys, entering the palace of Sugrīva, communicated to him, Laksmana's ire and approach.

verses.sanskrit:
तारया सहितः कामी सक्तः कपिवृषो रहः
न तेषां कपिवीराणां शुश्राव वचनं तदा
verses.transliteration:
tārayā sahitaḥ kāmī saktaḥ kapivṛṣo rahaḥ
na teṣāṁ kapivīrāṇāṁ śuśrāva vacanaṁ tadā

translations.english: That amorous chief of monkeys, attached to Tārā, paid no heed to the words of those foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सचिवसंदिष्टा हरयो रोमहर्षणाः
गिरिकुञ्जरमेघाभा नगर्या निर्ययुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sacivasaṁdiṣṭā harayo romaharṣaṇāḥ
girikuñjarameghābhā nagaryā niryayustadā

translations.english: Thereupon those terrible monkeys, resembling hills, elephants and clouds, went out of the city being commanded by the minister.

verses.sanskrit:
दशनागबलाः केचित्केचिद्दशगुणोत्तराः
केचिन्नागसहस्रस्य बभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
daśanāgabalāḥ kecitkeciddaśaguṇottarāḥ
kecinnāgasahasrasya babhūvustulyavikramāḥ

translations.english: Some of them had sharpened teeth and nails, some were grim-visaged, some had teeth like those of tigers, some had the strength of ten elephants, some had the strength of hundred elephants and some had that of thousand elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्स्नां हि कपिभिर्व्याप्तां द्रुमहस्तैर्महाबलैः
अपश्यल्लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धः किष्किन्धां तां दुरासदम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtsnāṁ hi kapibhirvyāptāṁ drumahastairmahābalaiḥ
apaśyallakṣmaṇaḥ kruddhaḥ kiṣkindhāṁ tāṁ durāsadam

translations.english: Thereupon Laksmana, angry, espied the city of Kiskindhă, hard to enter and surrounded by mighty monkeys with trees in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते हरयः सर्वे प्राकारपरिखान्तरात्
निष्क्रम्योदग्रसत्त्वास्तु तस्थुराविष्कृतं तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataste harayaḥ sarve prākāraparikhāntarāt
niṣkramyodagrasattvāstu tasthurāviṣkṛtaṁ tadā

translations.english: And getting over the ditch around the city walls, those terrible-looking monkeys stationed themselves openly.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्य प्रमादं च पूर्वजं चार्तमात्मवान्
बुद्ध्वा कोपवशं वीरः पुनरेव जगाम सः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvasya pramādaṁ ca pūrvajaṁ cārtamātmavān
buddhvā kopavaśaṁ vīraḥ punareva jagāma saḥ

translations.english: And meditating upon Sugrīva's error and his brother's interest, the self-controlled Laksmana, heroic, proceeded on wards.

verses.sanskrit:
स दीर्घोष्णमहोच्छ्वासः कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
बभूव नरशार्दूलसधूम इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
sa dīrghoṣṇamahocchvāsaḥ kopasaṁraktalocanaḥ
babhūva naraśārdūlasadhūma iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: Sighing hot and hard, that best of men-Laks maņa, with reddened eyes appeared like to smoky fire.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणशल्यस्फुरज्जिह्वः सायकासनभोगवान्
स्वतेजोविषसंघातः पञ्चास्य इव पन्नगः
verses.transliteration:
bāṇaśalyasphurajjihvaḥ sāyakāsanabhogavān
svatejoviṣasaṁghātaḥ pañcāsya iva pannagaḥ

translations.english: He appeared like to a terrible serpent of five mouths having the top of the arrow for his tongue, the bow for his expanded hood and his own prowess for the poison.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं नागेन्द्रमिव कोपितम्
समासाद्याङ्गदस्त्रासाद्विषादमगमद्भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dīptamiva kālāgniṁ nāgendramiva kopitam
samāsādyāṅgadastrāsādviṣādamagamadbhṛśam

translations.english: Beholding him like the flaming fire of dissolution and enraged lord of serpents, Angada, out of fear, became exceedingly sorry.

verses.sanskrit:
एष रामानुजः प्राप्तस्त्वत्सकाशमरिंदमः
भ्रातुर्व्यसनसंतप्तो द्वारि तिष्ठति लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa rāmānujaḥ prāptastvatsakāśamariṁdamaḥ
bhrāturvyasanasaṁtapto dvāri tiṣṭhati lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon the far-famed Laksmana, having his eyes reddened with ire, spoke to Argada, saying-0 child, do you inform Sugriva of my arrival. O conqueror of foes, do you tell him:-'Laksmana, the younger brother of Rama, being stricken with grief on account his brother's disaster, has come to you and is waiting at the gate. If it pleaseth you, do you make good your promise.' Saying these words do you speedily return, O my child, O conqueror of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शोकाविष्टोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्
पितुः समीपमागम्य सौमित्रिरयमागतः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā śokāviṣṭo'ṅgado'bravīt
pituḥ samīpamāgamya saumitrirayamāgataḥ

translations.english: Hearing Laksmana's words, Angada overwhelmed with grief, approaching his uncle said-'Saumitree has arrived here.'

verses.sanskrit:
ते महौघनिभं दृष्ट्वा वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्
सिंहनादं समं चक्रुर्लक्ष्मणस्य समीपतः
verses.transliteration:
te mahaughanibhaṁ dṛṣṭvā vajrāśanisamasvanam
siṁhanādaṁ samaṁ cakrurlakṣmaṇasya samīpataḥ

translations.english: They, approaching Lakşmaņa began to set up a terrible roar like to thunder and resembling the uproar of lions and the noise of water-falls.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन महता प्रत्यबुध्यत वानरः
मदविह्वलताम्राक्षो व्याकुलस्रग्विभूषणः
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena mahatā pratyabudhyata vānaraḥ
madavihvalatāmrākṣo vyākulasragvibhūṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: By that terrible sound awoke that monkeychief, having coppery eyes, agitated, adorned with garlands and possessed by liquor.

verses.sanskrit:
प्लक्षश्चैव प्रभावश्च मन्त्रिणावर्थधर्मयोः
वक्तुमुच्चावचं प्राप्तं लक्ष्मणं तौ शशंसतुः
verses.transliteration:
plakṣaścaiva prabhāvaśca mantriṇāvarthadharmayoḥ
vaktumuccāvacaṁ prāptaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ tau śaśaṁsatuḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of Angada, the tow counsellors of Sugrīva, intelligent and of magnificent looks, along with him, approached that lord of monkeys. And those two ministers Yaksa and Prabhava, to give him proper counsels, informed (that monkey-chief) of the arrival of Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
स एष राघवभ्राता लक्ष्मणो वाक्यसारथिः
व्यवसाय रथः प्राप्तस्तस्य रामस्य शासनात्
verses.transliteration:
sa eṣa rāghavabhrātā lakṣmaṇo vākyasārathiḥ
vyavasāya rathaḥ prāptastasya rāmasya śāsanāt

translations.english: That Laksmana, Raghava's brother, having words for his charioteer, and perseverance for his chariot, has approached you at his brother's command.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य मूर्ध्ना प्रणम्य त्वं सपुत्रः सह बन्धुभिः
राजंस्तिष्ठ स्वसमये भव सत्यप्रतिश्रवः
verses.transliteration:
tasya mūrdhnā praṇamya tvaṁ saputraḥ saha bandhubhiḥ
rājaṁstiṣṭha svasamaye bhava satyapratiśravaḥ

translations.english: And do you, O king, with a composed heart, perform what the virtuous-souled Rāma has ordered you to do and thus fulfil your promise.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सचिवैः सह
लक्ष्मणं कुपितं श्रुत्वा मुमोचासनमात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha
lakṣmaṇaṁ kupitaṁ śrutvā mumocāsanamātmavān

translations.english: Hearing the words of Angada as well as of Laksmana's wrath, the self-controlled Sugriva along with his counsellors, left his seat.

verses.sanskrit:
सचिवानब्रवीद्वाक्यं निश्चित्य गुरुलाघवम्
मन्त्रज्ञान्मन्त्रकुशलो मन्त्रेषु परिनिष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
sacivānabravīdvākyaṁ niścitya gurulāghavam
mantrajñānmantrakuśalo mantreṣu pariniṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: Ascertaining the weight and lightness of the present occasion, that one, expert in counsels and abiding by their advice spoke to the expert counsellors, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न मे दुर्व्याहृतं किंचिन्नापि मे दुरनुष्ठितम्
लक्ष्मणो राघवभ्राता क्रुद्धः किमिति चिन्तये
verses.transliteration:
na me durvyāhṛtaṁ kiṁcinnāpi me duranuṣṭhitam
lakṣmaṇo rāghavabhrātā kruddhaḥ kimiti cintaye

translations.english: I have not done him any wrong, nor have I spoken to him any improper word. I do not know why Rāghava's brother Laksmana has become offended with me.

verses.sanskrit:
असुहृद्भिर्ममामित्रैर्नित्यमन्तरदर्शिभिः
मम दोषानसंभूताञ्श्रावितो राघवानुजः
verses.transliteration:
asuhṛdbhirmamāmitrairnityamantaradarśibhiḥ
mama doṣānasaṁbhūtāñśrāvito rāghavānujaḥ

translations.english: Lakşmaņa has been falsely apprised of my imaginary weakness by my enemies, always looking to my dark sides.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्र तावद्यथाबुद्धि सर्वैरेव यथाविधि
भवद्भिर्निश्चयस्तस्य विज्ञेयो निपुणं शनैः
verses.transliteration:
atra tāvadyathābuddhi sarvaireva yathāvidhi
bhavadbhirniścayastasya vijñeyo nipuṇaṁ śanaiḥ

translations.english: It behoveth you all, to ascertain now speedily according to your knowledge and right understanding (the cause of Laksmana's wrath).

verses.sanskrit:
न खल्वस्ति मम त्रासो लक्ष्मणान्नापि राघवात्
मित्रं त्वस्थान कुपितं जनयत्येव संभ्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
na khalvasti mama trāso lakṣmaṇānnāpi rāghavāt
mitraṁ tvasthāna kupitaṁ janayatyeva saṁbhramam

translations.english: I do not fear Lakşmaņa or Rāghava; but friends enraged without any cause do invariable produce fear.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा सुकरं मित्रं दुष्करं परिपालनम्
अनित्यत्वात्तु चित्तानां प्रीतिरल्पेऽपि भिद्यते
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā sukaraṁ mitraṁ duṣkaraṁ paripālanam
anityatvāttu cittānāṁ prītiralpe'pi bhidyate

translations.english: It is easy to contract friendship but very difficult to sustain it; for owing to the fickleness of our minds, a very slight cause bring about separation.

verses.sanskrit:
अतोनिमित्तं त्रस्तोऽहं रामेण तु महात्मना
यन्ममोपकृतं शक्यं प्रतिकर्तुं न तन्मया
verses.transliteration:
atonimittaṁ trasto'haṁ rāmeṇa tu mahātmanā
yanmamopakṛtaṁ śakyaṁ pratikartuṁ na tanmayā

translations.english: I have not done him any good proportionate to what the high-souled Rāma had done for me; and it is for this reason that I am afraid of him.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान्हरिपुंगवः
उवाच स्वेन तर्केण मध्ये वानरमन्त्रिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīveṇaivamuktastu hanumānharipuṁgavaḥ
uvāca svena tarkeṇa madhye vānaramantriṇām

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Sugrīva-Hanumān, the foremost of monkey-counsellors spoke, according to his own understanding, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा नैतदाश्चर्यं यत्त्वं हरिगणेश्वर
न विस्मरसि सुस्निग्धमुपकारकृतं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā naitadāścaryaṁ yattvaṁ harigaṇeśvara
na vismarasi susnigdhamupakārakṛtaṁ śubham

translations.english: It is no wonder, O lord of monkeys, that you had not forgot the unexpected benefit, (you hadst received at the hands of Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा प्रणयात्क्रुद्धो राघवो नात्र संशयः
भ्रातरं स प्रहितवाँल्लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā praṇayātkruddho rāghavo nātra saṁśayaḥ
bhrātaraṁ sa prahitavā̐llakṣmaṇaṁ lakṣmivardhanam

translations.english: To encompass your well-being, Vali, powerful as the Lord of celestials, was fearlessly destroyed by the heroic Rāghava. There is not the least doubt, that Rāghava, out of love, is enraged with you, and has despatched his younger brother Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of prosperity.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं प्रमत्तो न जानीषे कालं कलविदां वर
फुल्लसप्तच्छदश्यामा प्रवृत्ता तु शरच्छिवा
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ pramatto na jānīṣe kālaṁ kalavidāṁ vara
phullasaptacchadaśyāmā pravṛttā tu śaracchivā

translations.english: O you foremost of those conversant with time, the auspicious autumn, green with Saptchada flowers, has set in and you, given up to enjoyments, does not perceive it.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्मल ग्रहनक्षत्रा द्यौः प्रनष्टबलाहका
प्रसन्नाश्च दिशः सर्वाः सरितश्च सरांसि च
verses.transliteration:
nirmala grahanakṣatrā dyauḥ pranaṣṭabalāhakā
prasannāśca diśaḥ sarvāḥ saritaśca sarāṁsi ca

translations.english: The sky, having the clouds removed, is full of clear stars and planets. The quarters, the ponds and rivers are all clear.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तमुद्योगकालं तु नावैषि हरिपुंगव
त्वं प्रमत्त इति व्यक्तं लक्ष्मणोऽयमिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
prāptamudyogakālaṁ tu nāvaiṣi haripuṁgava
tvaṁ pramatta iti vyaktaṁ lakṣmaṇo'yamihāgataḥ

translations.english: O best of monkeys, finding you forgetful, Lakṣmaṇa has come here to inform you that the proper time has arrived.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्
वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ārtasya hṛtadārasya paruṣaṁ puruṣāntarāt
vacanaṁ marṣaṇīyaṁ te rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Do you patiently hear all these harsh words of the high-souled Rāma, racked with sorrow and separated from his spouse, which Laksmana, shall relate to you.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतापराधस्य हि ते नान्यत्पश्याम्यहं क्षमम्
अन्तरेणाञ्जलिं बद्ध्वा लक्ष्मणस्य प्रसादनात्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtāparādhasya hi te nānyatpaśyāmyahaṁ kṣamam
antareṇāñjaliṁ baddhvā lakṣmaṇasya prasādanāt

translations.english: You have acted improperly towards him, and I do not find any thing tending to your welfare but your satisfying Lakşmana with folded hands.

verses.sanskrit:
नियुक्तैर्मन्त्रिभिर्वाच्यो अवश्यं पार्थिवो हितम्
अत एव भयं त्यक्त्वा ब्रवीम्यवधृतं वचः
verses.transliteration:
niyuktairmantribhirvācyo avaśyaṁ pārthivo hitam
ata eva bhayaṁ tyaktvā bravīmyavadhṛtaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: The kings should be addressed with auspicious words by their counsellors always ministering to them proper counsels. And it is for this reason, I am addressing you with these sound words.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिक्रुद्धः समर्थो हि चापमुद्यम्य राघवः
