ततः समुद्रमासाद्य संप्रधार्यार्थनिश्चयम्
अगस्त्येनान्तरे तत्र सागरे विनिवेशितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samudramāsādya saṁpradhāryārthaniścayam
agastyenāntare tatra sāgare viniveśitaḥ

translations.english: Then arriving at the main, you shall ascertain your ability or otherwise of crossing the same. In the bosom of the deep there, Agastya has placed that foremost of mountains-the charming Mahendra, having picturesque plateaus; golden, and beautiful,-with a portion of it sunk in the great ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाविधैर्नगैः फुल्लैर्लताभिश्चोपशोभितम्
देवर्षियक्षप्रवरैरप्सरोभिश्च सेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
nānāvidhairnagaiḥ phullairlatābhiścopaśobhitam
devarṣiyakṣapravarairapsarobhiśca sevitam

translations.english: For aye, He of a thousand eyes at Parvas visiteth this mountain embellished by various blossoming trees and creepers; beauteous with divinities, and saints, and the foremost Yaksas and Apsarās; thronged by numbers of Siddhas and Chāraṇas; and of surpassing loveliness.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वीपस्तस्यापरे पारे शतयोजनमायतः
अगम्यो मानुषैर्दीप्तस्तं मार्गध्वं समन्ततः
तत्र सर्वात्मना सीता मार्गितव्या विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
dvīpastasyāpare pāre śatayojanamāyataḥ
agamyo mānuṣairdīptastaṁ mārgadhvaṁ samantataḥ
tatra sarvātmanā sītā mārgitavyā viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: On its other shore is an island extending over an hundred Yojanas, inaccessible to men*, and of splendid aspect. Do you explore it all round. There, in particular, you must every way search for Sita. *Because, says the commentator,. of the profusion of gold in it.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि देशस्तु वध्यस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
राक्षसाधिपतेर्वासः सहस्राक्षसमद्युतेः
verses.transliteration:
sa hi deśastu vadhyasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
rākṣasādhipatervāsaḥ sahasrākṣasamadyuteḥ

translations.english: That country belongs to the impious Rāvana, worthy of being slain—the lord of Raksasas, like to the thousand-eyed (deity) in splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य मध्ये तस्य तु राक्षसी
अङ्गारकेति विख्याता छायामाक्षिप्य भोजिनी
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇasya samudrasya madhye tasya tu rākṣasī
aṅgāraketi vikhyātā chāyāmākṣipya bhojinī

translations.english: In the midst of the Southern sea belonging to him (Ravana), there is a Raksasi, named Angāraketi, who procureth her pray by casting her shadow.

verses.sanskrit:
तमतिक्रम्य लक्ष्मीवान्समुद्रे शतयोजने
गिरिः पुष्पितको नाम सिद्धचारणसेवितः
verses.transliteration:
tamatikramya lakṣmīvānsamudre śatayojane
giriḥ puṣpitako nāma siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ

translations.english: In the sea extending over an hundred Yojanas, a lovely hill, named Puspitaka, the abode of Siddhas and Chăraņas; resembling the rays of the sun or the moon,-resting on the waters of the ocean, looks splendid, piercing the heavens with its giant peaks. Of this (mountain), there is a particular golden summit, which the sun approaches. It is incapable of being beheld by the ungrateful or the atheistical.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्
शरणं काञ्चनं दिव्यं नानारत्नविभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra yojanavistāramucchritaṁ daśayojanam
śaraṇaṁ kāñcanaṁ divyaṁ nānāratnavibhūṣitam

translations.english: There is the hill named Kunjara, grateful both to the eye and the mind, where Viśvakarmā had built the abode of Agastya*. There (rises) that stately golden pile, adorned with various gems, extending over one Yojana, and ten in height. *i.e. in that hill.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र भोगवती नाम सर्पाणामालयः पुरी
विशालरथ्या दुर्धर्षा सर्वतः परिरक्षिता
रक्षिता पन्नगैर्घोरैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाविषैः
verses.transliteration:
tatra bhogavatī nāma sarpāṇāmālayaḥ purī
viśālarathyā durdharṣā sarvataḥ parirakṣitā
rakṣitā pannagairghoraistīkṣṇadaṁṣṭrairmahāviṣaiḥ

translations.english: In it also there is that palace, which is the abode of snakes; having spacious ways, i incapable of being captured, guarded around, and protected by dreadful snakes and sharptoothed serpents of virulent poison; where dwelleth Vāsuki, the exceedingly terrible king of snakes. Proceeding heedfully, you must explore that Bhogavatī palace; also whatever concealed place may lie there.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ते पृथिव्या दुर्धर्षास्तत्र स्वर्गजितः स्थिताः
ततः परं न वः सेव्यः पितृलोकः सुदारुणः
राजधानी यमस्यैषा कष्टेन तमसावृता
verses.transliteration:
ante pṛthivyā durdharṣāstatra svargajitaḥ sthitāḥ
tataḥ paraṁ na vaḥ sevyaḥ pitṛlokaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
rājadhānī yamasyaiṣā kaṣṭena tamasāvṛtā

translations.english: And there reside persons who have won the heavenly regions. After that are the awful regions of the ancestral manes, which you must not approach. This is the metropolis of Yama, covered by deep gloom.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावदेव युष्माभिर्वीरा वानरपुंगवाः
शक्यं विचेतुं गन्तुं वा नातो गतिमतां गतिः
verses.transliteration:
etāvadeva yuṣmābhirvīrā vānarapuṁgavāḥ
śakyaṁ vicetuṁ gantuṁ vā nāto gatimatāṁ gatiḥ

translations.english: You heroic monkey chiefs, you can seek thus far. Further there is no course for those endued with motion.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वमेतत्समालोक्य यच्चान्यदपि दृश्यते
गतिं विदित्वा वैदेह्याः संनिवर्तितमर्हथ
verses.transliteration:
sarvametatsamālokya yaccānyadapi dṛśyate
gatiṁ viditvā vaidehyāḥ saṁnivartitamarhatha

translations.english: Having examined all these, as well others that may come within your ken, it behoves you, after having ascertained Vaidehi's course, to return (hither).

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु मासान्निवृत्तोऽग्रे दृष्टा सीतेति वक्ष्यति
मत्तुल्यविभवो भोगैः सुखं स विहरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yastu māsānnivṛtto'gre dṛṣṭā sīteti vakṣyati
mattulyavibhavo bhogaiḥ sukhaṁ sa vihariṣyati

translations.english: He that, returning within a month, shall say,—I have seen Sītā,' shall pass his days in happiness, enjoying affluence like mine own and indulging all pleasures.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रियतरो नास्ति मम प्राणाद्विशेषतः
कृतापराधो बहुशो मम बन्धुर्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ priyataro nāsti mama prāṇādviśeṣataḥ
kṛtāparādho bahuśo mama bandhurbhaviṣyati

translations.english: He shall be dearer to me than life itself, and none dearer (to me) that he; and although he might commit innumerable wrongs, still should he become my friend.

verses.sanskrit:
अमितबलपराक्रमा भवन्तो; विपुलगुणेषु कुलेषु च प्रसूताः
मनुजपतिसुतां यथा लभध्वं; तदधिगुणं पुरुषार्थमारभध्वम्
verses.transliteration:
amitabalaparākramā bhavanto; vipulaguṇeṣu kuleṣu ca prasūtāḥ
manujapatisutāṁ yathā labhadhvaṁ; tadadhiguṇaṁ puruṣārthamārabhadhvam

translations.english: Possessed of immeasurable strength and prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered. prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिजालावृतां दुर्गां मार्गित्वा पश्चिमां दिशम्
ततः पश्चिममासाद्य समुद्रं द्रष्टुमर्हथ
तिमि नक्रायुत जलमक्षोभ्यमथ वानरः
verses.transliteration:
girijālāvṛtāṁ durgāṁ mārgitvā paścimāṁ diśam
tataḥ paścimamāsādya samudraṁ draṣṭumarhatha
timi nakrāyuta jalamakṣobhyamatha vānaraḥ

translations.english: There having explored tracts resembling deserts, and cold cliffs towering high, and the West, covered with mountain ranges, and extremely difficult of access,-and proceeding at a little more to the west, it behoves you a view of the sea. And proceeding on, you monkeys, you shall see (the ocean), whose waters abound in whales and alligators, you monkeys.* Then the apes shall sport in tracts covered by Ketakas, and dense with Tamālas and woods of coconuts. There shall you look for $ītā and the mansion of Rāvana, *The grammar of these slokas is exceedingly vicious; and it has cost the Translator no small amount of labour to assign the necessary logical nexus in a good many praces:

verses.sanskrit:
अवन्तीमङ्गलोपां च तथा चालक्षितं वनम्
राष्ट्राणि च विशालानि पत्तनानि ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
avantīmaṅgalopāṁ ca tathā cālakṣitaṁ vanam
rāṣṭrāṇi ca viśālāni pattanāni tatastataḥ

translations.english: In hills and woods on the shores of the sea; and (explore) Muracipattana, and the delightful Jațāpura, and Avantī, and Angalepā, as well as in the wood (called) Alaksita, and spacious monarchies, and emporiums.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य प्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सिंहाः पक्षगमाः स्थिताः
तिमिमत्स्यगजांश्चैव नीडान्यारोपयन्ति ते
verses.transliteration:
tasya prastheṣu ramyeṣu siṁhāḥ pakṣagamāḥ sthitāḥ
timimatsyagajāṁścaiva nīḍānyāropayanti te

translations.english: There is a mighty mountain where the Sindhu falls into the sea, Somagiri by name; having an hundred summits and tall trees. In its plateaus there are certain birds (called) Sinhas. These lift up to their nests whales and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि नीडानि सिंहानां गिरिशृङ्गगताश्च ये
दृप्तास्तृप्ताश्च मातङ्गास्तोयदस्वननिःस्वनाः
विचरन्ति विशालेऽस्मिंस्तोयपूर्णे समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tāni nīḍāni siṁhānāṁ giriśṛṅgagatāśca ye
dṛptāstṛptāśca mātaṅgāstoyadasvananiḥsvanāḥ
vicaranti viśāle'smiṁstoyapūrṇe samantataḥ

translations.english: The proud elephants carried to the nests and remaining on the summits of the mountain, possessing the roar of clouds, having been gratified (with food), range around this extensive table-land filled with water.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य शृङ्गं दिवस्पर्शं काञ्चनं चित्रपादपम्
सर्वमाशु विचेतव्यं कपिभिः कामरूपिभिः
verses.transliteration:
tasya śṛṅgaṁ divasparśaṁ kāñcanaṁ citrapādapam
sarvamāśu vicetavyaṁ kapibhiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ

translations.english: The monkeys, capable of wearing shapes at will, should swiftly search its golden summit towering to the sky and filled with graceful trees.

verses.sanskrit:
कोटिं तत्र समुद्रे तु काञ्चनीं शतयोजनम्
दुर्दर्शां परियात्रस्य गता द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः
verses.transliteration:
koṭiṁ tatra samudre tu kāñcanīṁ śatayojanam
durdarśāṁ pariyātrasya gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ

translations.english: Proceeding further, the monkeys shall behold the golden summit of Pāriyātra rising from the sea and extending over an hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
कोट्यस्तत्र चतुर्विंशद्गन्धर्वाणां तरस्विनाम्
वसन्त्यग्निनिकाशानां घोराणां कामरूपिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
koṭyastatra caturviṁśadgandharvāṇāṁ tarasvinām
vasantyagninikāśānāṁ ghorāṇāṁ kāmarūpiṇām

translations.english: There dwell all around in a body four and twenty kotis of ascetic Gandharvas, resembling fire, dreadful, practicising impiety, and like to flames of fire.

verses.sanskrit:
नात्यासादयितव्यास्ते वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः
नादेयं च फलं तस्माद्देशात्किंचित्प्लवंगमैः
verses.transliteration:
nātyāsādayitavyāste vānarairbhīmavikramaiḥ
nādeyaṁ ca phalaṁ tasmāddeśātkiṁcitplavaṁgamaiḥ

translations.english: The monkeys of dreadful prowess should not present themselves before those, nor should they take any fruits from that country.

verses.sanskrit:
दुरासदा हि ते वीराः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः
फलमूलानि ते तत्र रक्षन्ते भीमविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
durāsadā hi te vīrāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ
phalamūlāni te tatra rakṣante bhīmavikramāḥ

translations.english: Those heroes are hard to approach; and they are truthful and possessed of great might. And there they of dreadful prowess stow away their fruits and roots.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र यत्नश्च कर्तव्यो मार्गितव्या च जानकी
न हि तेभ्यो भयं किंचित्कपित्वमनुवर्तताम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra yatnaśca kartavyo mārgitavyā ca jānakī
na hi tebhyo bhayaṁ kiṁcitkapitvamanuvartatām

translations.english: There you should heedfully search for Jānakī. you have no fear whatever from them; do you only follow your native nature as monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्भागे समुद्रस्य चक्रवान्नाम पर्वतः
तत्र चक्रं सहस्रारं निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
caturbhāge samudrasya cakravānnāma parvataḥ
tatra cakraṁ sahasrāraṁ nirmitaṁ viśvakarmaṇā

translations.english: On the fourth side of the Ocean is a mountain named Cakravān. There Viśvakarmā forged the discus (called) Sahasrāra.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र पञ्चजनं हत्वा हयग्रीवं च दानवम्
आजहार ततश्चक्रं शङ्खं च पुरुषोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
tatra pañcajanaṁ hatvā hayagrīvaṁ ca dānavam
ājahāra tataścakraṁ śaṅkhaṁ ca puruṣottamaḥ

translations.english: There, slaying Panchajana and the Dānava, Hayagriva*, the best of male beings obtained the discus as well as the conch. *Lit. horse-necked.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सानुषु चित्रेषु विशालासु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: There do you everywhere search for Rāvana along with Vaidehi in the beautiful plateaus and huge caves.

verses.sanskrit:
योजनानि चतुःषष्टिर्वराहो नाम पर्वतः
सुवर्णशृङ्गः सुश्रीमानगाधे वरुणालये
verses.transliteration:
yojanāni catuḥṣaṣṭirvarāho nāma parvataḥ
suvarṇaśṛṅgaḥ suśrīmānagādhe varuṇālaye

translations.english: Sunk in the depths of the sea, is a very great mountain named Varāha, having golden peaks and measuring four and sixty yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र प्राग्ज्योतिषं नाम जातरूपमयं पुरम्
यस्मिन्वस्ति दुष्टात्मा नरको नाम गुहासु च
verses.transliteration:
tatra prāgjyotiṣaṁ nāma jātarūpamayaṁ puram
yasminvasti duṣṭātmā narako nāma guhāsu ca

translations.english: In it is a city named Prāgjyotişa, all of gold. There dwells the wicked Dänava named Naraka.* *i.e. in the Varadha hill.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सानुषु चित्रेषु विशालासु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: In those beautiful plateous and huge caves, you should everywhere search for Rāvana with Videha's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्रं काञ्चनान्तरनिर्दरः
पर्वतः सर्वसौवर्णो धारा प्रस्रवणायुतः
verses.transliteration:
tamatikramya śailendraṁ kāñcanāntaranirdaraḥ
parvataḥ sarvasauvarṇo dhārā prasravaṇāyutaḥ

translations.english: Passing beyond that foremost of mountains, whose sight betrays the secret of its bowels being freighted with gold, (you shall come upon) the mountain Sarvasauvarna, furnished with fountains and cascades.

verses.sanskrit:
तं गजाश्च वराहाश्च सिंहा व्याघ्राश्च सर्वतः
अभिगर्जन्ति सततं तेन शब्देन दर्पिताः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ gajāśca varāhāśca siṁhā vyāghrāśca sarvataḥ
abhigarjanti satataṁ tena śabdena darpitāḥ

translations.english: Coming to it, elephants, and boars, and lions, and tigers, on all sides roar ceaselessly, wrought up by the echoes their own cries have produced.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्हरिहयः श्रीमान्महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः
अभिषिक्तः सुरै राजा मेघवान्नाम पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
tasminharihayaḥ śrīmānmahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
abhiṣiktaḥ surai rājā meghavānnāma parvataḥ

translations.english: This is the mountain named Megha, where the graceful green-horsed vanquisher of Pāka, Mahendra, was installed king by the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुणादित्यवर्णानि भ्राजमानानि सर्वतः
जातरूपमयैर्वृक्षैः शोभितानि सुपुष्पितैः
verses.transliteration:
taruṇādityavarṇāni bhrājamānāni sarvataḥ
jātarūpamayairvṛkṣaiḥ śobhitāni supuṣpitaiḥ

translations.english: Having passed by that mountain protected by Mahendra, you shall repair to sixty thousand hills of gold; in hue like the infant sun, and blazing on all sides and embellished by blossoming golden trees,

verses.sanskrit:
तेनैवमुक्तः शैलेन्द्रः सर्व एव त्वदाश्रयाः
मत्प्रसादाद्भविष्यन्ति दिवारात्रौ च काञ्चनाः
verses.transliteration:
tenaivamuktaḥ śailendraḥ sarva eva tvadāśrayāḥ
matprasādādbhaviṣyanti divārātrau ca kāñcanāḥ

translations.english: In the midst of them is established as king, Meru, best of mountains, formerly the Sun being well pleased, conferred a boon on this mountain, and he addressed the mountain, saying,—'By my grace all the hills that are under your protection, shall be golden day and night; and also those gods Gandharvas and Dānvas that shall dwell in you, shall be filled with reverence for me and to the boot attain a golden glory.'

verses.sanskrit:
आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ति तैश्च सूर्योऽभिपूजितः
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानामस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
ādityamupatiṣṭhanti taiśca sūryo'bhipūjitaḥ
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāmastaṁ gacchati parvatam

translations.english: Coming to the excellent mountain Meru. Viśvadevas, the Vasus, the Maruts and the celestials, adore the Sun in the western twilight. Adored by them, the Sun, becoming invisible, repaireth to the Setting hill*. The commentator remarks: Although not expressly stated, it is implied that the islands to the west of it are also to be searched.

verses.sanskrit:
योजनानां सहस्राणि दशतानि दिवाकरः
मुहूर्तार्धेन तं शीघ्रमभियाति शिलोच्चयम्
verses.transliteration:
yojanānāṁ sahasrāṇi daśatāni divākaraḥ
muhūrtārdhena taṁ śīghramabhiyāti śiloccayam

translations.english: In half a muhurta, the Sun swiftly passes over this (mountain), measuring, as it does, ten thousand Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
शोभितं तरुभिश्चित्रैर्नानापक्षिसमाकुलैः
निकेतं पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
śobhitaṁ tarubhiścitrairnānāpakṣisamākulaiḥ
niketaṁ pāśahastasya varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: On its peak rises an edifice; resembling the sun (in splendour); consisting of palatial mansions built by Viśvakarmā; and graced by goodly trees rife with various birds,-the residence of the high-souled Varuna, bearing the noose in his hand.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरा मेरुमस्तं च तालो दशशिरा महान्
जातरूपमयः श्रीमान्भ्राजते चित्रवेदिकः
verses.transliteration:
antarā merumastaṁ ca tālo daśaśirā mahān
jātarūpamayaḥ śrīmānbhrājate citravedikaḥ

translations.english: Between Meru and the Setting hill, towers a tall palm having ten heads. Golden and graceful, it shineth on a variegated dais.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु सर्वेषु दुर्गेषु सरःसु च सरित्सु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
teṣu sarveṣu durgeṣu saraḥsu ca saritsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: In all these, difficult of access, as also in rivers and tanks, you should thoroughly search for Rāvana along with Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र तिष्ठति धर्मात्मा तपसा स्वेन भावितः
मेरुसावर्णिरित्येव ख्यातो वै ब्रह्मणा समः
verses.transliteration:
yatra tiṣṭhati dharmātmā tapasā svena bhāvitaḥ
merusāvarṇirityeva khyāto vai brahmaṇā samaḥ

translations.english: There dwells there the righteous and famous Merusāvarani, sanctified by virtue of his own ascesticism, and like to Brahmā himself*. *Like to Prajāpati dwelling by Mahameru.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रष्टव्यो मेरुसावर्णिर्महर्षिः सूर्यसंनिभः
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ प्रवृत्तिं मैथिलीं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
praṣṭavyo merusāvarṇirmaharṣiḥ sūryasaṁnibhaḥ
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau pravṛttiṁ maithilīṁ prati

translations.english: Bowing down your heads to the earth, you should ask the Maharși Merusăvarņi, resembling the sun, touching Mithila's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावज्जीवलोकस्य भास्करो रजनीक्षये
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वमस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
etāvajjīvalokasya bhāskaro rajanīkṣaye
kṛtvā vitimiraṁ sarvamastaṁ gacchati parvatam

translations.english: On the departure of night, the sun dispels the darkness of the world to this extent, and then enters the Setting hill.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावद्वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुंगवाः
अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्
verses.transliteration:
etāvadvānaraiḥ śakyaṁ gantuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ
abhāskaramamaryādaṁ na jānīmastataḥ param

translations.english: You foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are able to proceed thus far. Beyond this, of what is sunless and boundless I know nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च
अस्तं पर्वतमासाद्य पूर्णे मासे निवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
adhigamya tu vaidehīṁ nilayaṁ rāvaṇasya ca
astaṁ parvatamāsādya pūrṇe māse nivartata

translations.english: Having come to Vaidehi and Rāvana's mansions, and arrived at the Setting-hill, do you return of the month being complete.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन्वध्यो भवेन्मम
सहैव शूरो युष्माभिः श्वशुरो मे गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ūrdhvaṁ māsānna vastavyaṁ vasanvadhyo bhavenmama
sahaiva śūro yuṣmābhiḥ śvaśuro me gamiṣyati

translations.english: You must not stay above a month; and if you do, you must be slain by me. And along with you goeth that hero, my father-in-law.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रोतव्यं सर्वमेतस्य भवद्भिर्दिष्ट कारिभिः
गुरुरेष महाबाहुः श्वशुरो मे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
śrotavyaṁ sarvametasya bhavadbhirdiṣṭa kāribhiḥ
gurureṣa mahābāhuḥ śvaśuro me mahābalaḥ

translations.english: You, abiding by his orders, should listen to all that he sayeth. My mighty-armed father-in-law, gifted with great strength, is my spiritual preceptor.

verses.sanskrit:
भवन्तश्चापि विक्रान्ताः प्रमाणं सर्वकर्मसु
प्रमाणमेनं संस्थाप्य पश्यध्वं पश्चिमां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
bhavantaścāpi vikrāntāḥ pramāṇaṁ sarvakarmasu
pramāṇamenaṁ saṁsthāpya paśyadhvaṁ paścimāṁ diśam

translations.english: All of you possessed of prowess, yourselves certainly constitute the measure whereby to ascertain the wisdom or otherwise of a course. Making this one also into a measure, survey the western quarter. Having requited the good that has been done to us, we shall attain our end.

verses.sanskrit:
अतोऽन्यदपि यत्किंचित्कार्यस्यास्य हितं भवेत्
संप्रधार्य भवद्भिश्च देशकालार्थसंहितम्
verses.transliteration:
ato'nyadapi yatkiṁcitkāryasyāsya hitaṁ bhavet
saṁpradhārya bhavadbhiśca deśakālārthasaṁhitam

translations.english: De you also determine what else is agreeable (to Rāma), and in consonance with place, season and profit, should be performed by you in the matter of this business.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुषेण प्रमुखाः प्लवंगमाः; सुग्रीववाक्यं निपुणं निशम्य
आमन्त्र्य सर्वे प्लवगाधिपं ते; जग्मुर्दिशं तां वरुणाभिगुप्ताम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suṣeṇa pramukhāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ; sugrīvavākyaṁ nipuṇaṁ niśamya
āmantrya sarve plavagādhipaṁ te; jagmurdiśaṁ tāṁ varuṇābhiguptām

translations.english: Then those monkeys-the monkey-chiefs headed by Sușeņa, having heard Sugrīva's deft speech, set out for the quarter protected by Varuna.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संदिश्य सुग्रीवः श्वशुरं पश्चिमां दिशम्
वीरं शतबलिं नाम वानरं वानरर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁdiśya sugrīvaḥ śvaśuraṁ paścimāṁ diśam
vīraṁ śatabaliṁ nāma vānaraṁ vānararṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Having directed his father-in-law to proceed to the West, that best to monkeys, the allknowing king Sugrīva, lord of apes, then spoke to the heroic monkey, named Satavala, words fraught with good to himself as well as to Rāma,

verses.sanskrit:
वृतः शतसहस्रेण त्वद्विधानां वनौकसाम्
वैवस्वत सुतैः सार्धं प्रतिष्ठस्व स्वमन्त्रिभिः
verses.transliteration:
vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa tvadvidhānāṁ vanaukasām
vaivasvata sutaiḥ sārdhaṁ pratiṣṭhasva svamantribhiḥ

translations.english: Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of rangers of the forest like yourself, in company with the offspring of Yama as well as the counsellors in a body, do you, O you possessed of prowess, entering the northern quarter furnished with the Himaśaila, search everywhere for the illustrious spouse of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्कार्ये विनिवृत्ते कृते दाशरथेः प्रिये
ऋणान्मुक्ता भविष्यामः कृतार्थार्थविदां वराः
verses.transliteration:
asminkārye vinivṛtte kṛte dāśaratheḥ priye
ṛṇānmuktā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṛtārthārthavidāṁ varāḥ

translations.english: Having performed this task satisfactorily, and brought about what is dear to Dasaratha's son, we shall, O best of those that achieve success, be freed from our debts.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतं हि प्रियमस्माकं राघवेण महात्मना
तस्य चेत्प्रतिकारोऽस्ति सफलं जीवितं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtaṁ hi priyamasmākaṁ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
tasya cetpratikāro'sti saphalaṁ jīvitaṁ bhavet

translations.english: The high-souled Rāghava had done us good. If we can serve him in turn, our life shall be crowned with success.

verses.sanskrit:
एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय दृश्यते जानकी यथा
तथा भवद्भिः कर्तव्यमस्मत्प्रियहितैषिभिः
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ buddhiṁ samāsthāya dṛśyate jānakī yathā
tathā bhavadbhiḥ kartavyamasmatpriyahitaiṣibhiḥ

translations.english: Pondering this, those that are engaged in our welfare, should so act that Jānaki may be discovered.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं हि सर्वभूतानां मान्यस्तु नरसत्तमः
अस्मासु चागतप्रीती रामः परपुरंजयः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ hi sarvabhūtānāṁ mānyastu narasattamaḥ
asmāsu cāgataprītī rāmaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ

translations.english: And this foremost of men is worthy of being honoured by all creatures; and Rāmacaptor of hostile capitals—has also found delight in us.

verses.sanskrit:
इमानि वनदुर्गाणि नद्यः शैलान्तराणि च
भवन्तः परिमार्गंस्तु बुद्धिविक्रमसंपदा
verses.transliteration:
imāni vanadurgāṇi nadyaḥ śailāntarāṇi ca
bhavantaḥ parimārgaṁstu buddhivikramasaṁpadā

translations.english: Endowed with sense and prowess, do you explore these many inaccessible places, rivers and mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र म्लेच्छान्पुलिन्दांश्च शूरसेनांस्तथैव च
प्रस्थालान्भरतांश्चैव कुरूंश्च सह मद्रकैः
verses.transliteration:
tatra mlecchānpulindāṁśca śūrasenāṁstathaiva ca
prasthālānbharatāṁścaiva kurūṁśca saha madrakaiḥ

translations.english: Having searched there Mlechās, Pulindas, Surasensas, Prasthalas, Bharatas, Kurus, and Madrakas, and Varadas, as well as the cities of Kambojas, Yavanas and Sakas, do you explore Himavān.

verses.sanskrit:
लोध्रपद्मकषण्डेषु देवदारुवनेषु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्य मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
lodhrapadmakaṣaṇḍeṣu devadāruvaneṣu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehya mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: And in tracts of Lodhras and Padmakas, and in Devadāru woods* do you search thoroughly for Ravana along with Videha's daughter. *Belonging, according to the commentator, to Himavān.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सोमाश्रमं गत्वा देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्
कालं नाम महासानुं पर्वतं तं गमिष्यथ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ somāśramaṁ gatvā devagandharvasevitam
kālaṁ nāma mahāsānuṁ parvataṁ taṁ gamiṣyatha

translations.english: Then, coming upon the hermitage of Soma, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, do you repair to the mountain called kāla possessing spacious plateaus,

verses.sanskrit:
महत्सु तस्य शृङ्गेषु निर्दरेषु गुहासु च
विचिनुध्वं महाभागां रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्
verses.transliteration:
mahatsu tasya śṛṅgeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
vicinudhvaṁ mahābhāgāṁ rāmapatnīṁ yaśasvinīm

translations.english: In those mighty mountains, as also in others and in their caves, do you search for that exalted lady, the blameless wife of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्रं हेमवर्गं महागिरिम्
ततः सुदर्शनं नाम पर्वतं गन्तुमर्हथ
verses.transliteration:
tamatikramya śailendraṁ hemavargaṁ mahāgirim
tataḥ sudarśanaṁ nāma parvataṁ gantumarhatha

translations.english: Having passed beyond that mighty mountain containing gold in its womb, it behoves you to go to the mountain called Sudarsana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य काननषण्डेषु निर्दरेषु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tasya kānanaṣaṇḍeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: In its golden tracts, fountains and caves, do you search for Rāvaņa along with Videha's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
तमतिक्रम्य चाकाशं सर्वतः शतयोजनम्
अपर्वतनदी वृक्षं सर्वसत्त्वविवर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
tamatikramya cākāśaṁ sarvataḥ śatayojanam
aparvatanadī vṛkṣaṁ sarvasattvavivarjitam

translations.english: Going beyond it, (you come upon) a vacant land, measuring an hundred Yojanas, without mountains, or rivers, or trees; and void of all living beings.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु शीघ्रमतिक्रम्य कान्तारं रोमहर्षणम्
कैलासं पाण्डुरं शैलं प्राप्य हृष्टा भविष्यथ
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu śīghramatikramya kāntāraṁ romaharṣaṇam
kailāsaṁ pāṇḍuraṁ śailaṁ prāpya hṛṣṭā bhaviṣyatha

translations.english: Speedily passing that desert land capable of making one's hair stand on end, you shall feel delighted, on coming to the pale Kailasa.

verses.sanskrit:
विशाला नलिनी यत्र प्रभूतकमलोत्पला
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा अप्सरोगणसेविता
verses.transliteration:
viśālā nalinī yatra prabhūtakamalotpalā
haṁsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā apsarogaṇasevitā

translations.english: There (you will behold) the charming mansion of Kuvera, resembling pale clouds, of burnished gold, built by Viśvakarmā; where (lies) the spacious tank overflowing with lotuses and lilies, thronged with swans and Kāraņdavas, and frequented by troops of Apsarās.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र वैश्रवणो राजा सर्वभूतनमस्कृतः
धनदो रमते श्रीमान्गुह्यकैः सह यक्षराट्
verses.transliteration:
tatra vaiśravaṇo rājā sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ
dhanado ramate śrīmānguhyakaiḥ saha yakṣarāṭ

translations.english: There king Vaiśravana, the lord of Yakşas, bowed down to by all creatures,-the graceful giver of riches—sporteth along with the Guhyakas.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चन्द्रनिकशेषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tasya candranikaśeṣu parvateṣu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ

translations.english: In the offshoots belonging to Kailasa resembling the moon, as also in their caverns, do you thoroughly search for Rāvaņa in company with Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चं तु गिरिमासाद्य बिलं तस्य सुदुर्गमम्
अप्रमत्तैः प्रवेष्टव्यं दुष्प्रवेशं हि तत्स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration:
krauñcaṁ tu girimāsādya bilaṁ tasya sudurgamam
apramattaiḥ praveṣṭavyaṁ duṣpraveśaṁ hi tatsmṛtam

translations.english: And coming to the Kruncha mountain, you should, having your wits about you, enter its inaccessible cavern; for that is well known as difficult of entrance.

verses.sanskrit:
वसन्ति हि महात्मानस्तत्र सूर्यसमप्रभाः
देवैरप्यर्चिताः सम्यग्देवरूपा महर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
vasanti hi mahātmānastatra sūryasamaprabhāḥ
devairapyarcitāḥ samyagdevarūpā maharṣayaḥ

translations.english: There dwell certain Maharsis, high-souled, of effulgence resembling that of the sun-complete god-like shapes,—who are sought by the deities themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चस्य तु गुहाश्चान्याः सानूनि शिखराणि च
निर्दराश्च नितम्बाश्च विचेतव्यास्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
krauñcasya tu guhāścānyāḥ sānūni śikharāṇi ca
nirdarāśca nitambāśca vicetavyāstatastataḥ

translations.english: And you should thoroughly explore the other caves of Krauncha, its plateaus and peaks; its passes and sides.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चस्य शिखरं चापि निरीक्ष्य च ततस्ततः
अवृक्षं कामशैलं च मानसं विहगालयम्
verses.transliteration:
krauñcasya śikharaṁ cāpi nirīkṣya ca tatastataḥ
avṛkṣaṁ kāmaśailaṁ ca mānasaṁ vihagālayam

translations.english: (Then is) the treeless Manasa-abode of birds-the scene of Kāma's austerities. Way there is none for creatures, or for gods, or for Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चं गिरिमतिक्रम्य मैनाको नाम पर्वतः
मयस्य भवनं तत्र दानवस्य स्वयं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
krauñcaṁ girimatikramya maināko nāma parvataḥ
mayasya bhavanaṁ tatra dānavasya svayaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: are That also must be explored by you, that mountain with plains and plateous. Going beyond Krauncha, (you shall see) the mountain, named Maināka.

verses.sanskrit:
मैनाकस्तु विचेतव्यः ससानुप्रस्थकन्दरः
स्त्रीणामश्वमुखीनां च निकेतास्तत्र तत्र तु
verses.transliteration:
mainākastu vicetavyaḥ sasānuprasthakandaraḥ
strīṇāmaśvamukhīnāṁ ca niketāstatra tatra tu

translations.english: There is the residence of the Danvava, Maya, reared by himself. Mainaka also with its plains, plateaus and woods must be searched by you.

verses.sanskrit:
वन्द्यास्ते तु तपःसिद्धास्तापसा वीतकल्मषाः
प्रष्टव्याश्चापि सीतायाः प्रवृत्तं विनयान्वितैः
verses.transliteration:
vandyāste tu tapaḥsiddhāstāpasā vītakalmaṣāḥ
praṣṭavyāścāpi sītāyāḥ pravṛttaṁ vinayānvitaiḥ

translations.english: There are all over, the homes of females with faces resembling those of horses. Going beyond that part, (you shall come to) the asylum inhabited by Siddhas; where ascetics—Vālakhilyas, Siddhas and Vaikhānasas. Saluting those Siddhas, who have been cleansed of their sins on account of their asceticism, you should in humble guise ask them concerning Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
हेमपुष्करसंछन्नं तत्र वैखानसं सरः
तरुणादित्यसंकाशैर्हंसैर्विचरितं शुभैः
verses.transliteration:
hemapuṣkarasaṁchannaṁ tatra vaikhānasaṁ saraḥ
taruṇādityasaṁkāśairhaṁsairvicaritaṁ śubhaiḥ

translations.english: There is the Vaikhānasa tank filled with golden lotuses; and ranged by graceful cranes of the hue of the infant sun.

verses.sanskrit:
औपवाह्यः कुबेरस्य सर्वभौम इति स्मृतः
गजः पर्येति तं देशं सदा सह करेणुभिः
verses.transliteration:
aupavāhyaḥ kuberasya sarvabhauma iti smṛtaḥ
gajaḥ paryeti taṁ deśaṁ sadā saha kareṇubhiḥ

translations.english: Kuvera's vehicle, the elephant known (by the name of) Sārvabhauma, ever rangeth that country in company with she-elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
गभस्तिभिरिवार्कस्य स तु देशः प्रकाशते
विश्राम्यद्भिस्तपः सिद्धैर्देवकल्पैः स्वयम्प्रभैः
verses.transliteration:
gabhastibhirivārkasya sa tu deśaḥ prakāśate
viśrāmyadbhistapaḥ siddhairdevakalpaiḥ svayamprabhaiḥ

translations.english: Going beyond that expanse of water, (you come upon) a sky void of stars, and where the sun and the moon have been put out; and that land is visible by the rays, as if of the sun, proceeding from (the persons of) self-luminous, god-like ones, who are reposing there, after achieving success in austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु देशमतिक्रम्य शैलोदा नाम निम्नगा
उभयोस्तीरयोर्यस्याः कीचका नाम वेणवः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu deśamatikramya śailodā nāma nimnagā
ubhayostīrayoryasyāḥ kīcakā nāma veṇavaḥ

translations.english: Leaving behind that region, (you come to) a stream named Sailoda. On its both banks are bamboos named Kīcaka.

verses.sanskrit:
ते नयन्ति परं तीरं सिद्धान्प्रत्यानयन्ति च
उत्तराः कुरवस्तत्र कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रियाः
verses.transliteration:
te nayanti paraṁ tīraṁ siddhānpratyānayanti ca
uttarāḥ kuravastatra kṛtapuṇyapratiśriyāḥ

translations.english: These take the Siddhas to the other shore and bring them back again. There (are seen the northern Kurus, the abode of those that have acquired religious merit.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः काञ्चनपद्माभिः पद्मिनीभिः कृतोदकाः
नीलवैदूर्यपत्राढ्या नद्यस्तत्र सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kāñcanapadmābhiḥ padminībhiḥ kṛtodakāḥ
nīlavaidūryapatrāḍhyā nadyastatra sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And there are tanks there with their waters crowned with golden lotuses. There are rivers by thousands with copious blue lapis leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्तोत्पलवनैश्चात्र मण्डिताश्च हिरण्मयैः
तरुणादित्यसदृशैर्भान्ति तत्र जलाशयाः
verses.transliteration:
raktotpalavanaiścātra maṇḍitāśca hiraṇmayaiḥ
taruṇādityasadṛśairbhānti tatra jalāśayāḥ

translations.english: And the pools here, resembling the tender sun, are embellished with assemblages of golden red lotuses.

verses.sanskrit:
महार्हमणिपत्रैश्च काञ्चनप्रभ केसरैः
नीलोत्पलवनैश्चित्रैः स देशः सर्वतोवृतः
verses.transliteration:
mahārhamaṇipatraiśca kāñcanaprabha kesaraiḥ
nīlotpalavanaiścitraiḥ sa deśaḥ sarvatovṛtaḥ

translations.english: And that tract is every where filled with costly gems, and jewels, and woods of blue lotuses, having filaments splendid like gold; and with round pearls and costly jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिर्मणिभिश्च महाधनैः
उद्भूतपुलिनास्तत्र जातरूपैश्च निम्नगाः
verses.transliteration:
nistulābhiśca muktābhirmaṇibhiśca mahādhanaiḥ
udbhūtapulināstatra jātarūpaiśca nimnagāḥ

translations.english: And the rivers there have islets covered with gold; and are crowded with lovely hills of gold, bright as fire, furnished with all kinds of precious stones.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यपुष्पफलाश्चात्र नगाः पत्ररथाकुलाः
दिव्यगन्धरसस्पर्शाः सर्वकामान्स्रवन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
nityapuṣpaphalāścātra nagāḥ patrarathākulāḥ
divyagandharasasparśāḥ sarvakāmānsravanti ca

translations.english: And the trees there, thronged with birds, bear flowers and fruits daily; and, charged with savoury juices, publishing superb perfumes, and of delicious feel, they confer every wish.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाकाराणि वासांसि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः
मुक्तावैदूर्यचित्राणि भूषणानि तथैव च
verses.transliteration:
nānākārāṇi vāsāṁsi phalantyanye nagottamāḥ
muktāvaidūryacitrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni tathaiva ca

translations.english: Other excellent trees bring forth attires of divers kinds, and ornaments decked with pearls and lapises,-coveted alike by males and females*. *The present text, according to Kataka, drops a sloka, whose last line is, Beings possessed of powerful effulgence, sport here always in company with females.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रीणां यान्यनुरूपाणि पुरुषाणां तथैव च
सर्वर्तुसुखसेव्यानि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
strīṇāṁ yānyanurūpāṇi puruṣāṇāṁ tathaiva ca
sarvartusukhasevyāni phalantyanye nagottamāḥ

translations.english: And other excellent trees bear fruits fit to be partaken at all seasons. And other excellent trees bring forth precious beds dight with costly jewels and furnished with variegated covers.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रियश्च गुणसंपन्ना रूपयौवनलक्षिताः
गन्धर्वाः किंनरा सिद्धा नागा विद्याधरास्तथा
रमन्ते सहितास्तत्र नारीभिर्भास्करप्रभाः
verses.transliteration:
striyaśca guṇasaṁpannā rūpayauvanalakṣitāḥ
gandharvāḥ kiṁnarā siddhā nāgā vidyādharāstathā
ramante sahitāstatra nārībhirbhāskaraprabhāḥ

translations.english: And other trees bring forth charming wreaths, and costly drinks, and various kinds of viands. And females adorned with every accomplishment, and endowed with youth and beauty, and Gandharvas and Kinnaras, and Siddhas and Nāgas and Vidyādharas, of blazing splendour, ceaselessly sport there in company with females.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे सुकृतकर्माणः सर्वे रतिपरायणाः
सर्वे कामार्थसहिता वसन्ति सह योषितः
verses.transliteration:
sarve sukṛtakarmāṇaḥ sarve ratiparāyaṇāḥ
sarve kāmārthasahitā vasanti saha yoṣitaḥ

translations.english: And all of righteous deeds, and all engaged in amorous disports, and all furnished with desire and profit,-dwell in that place in association with their females.

verses.sanskrit:
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषः सोत्कृष्टहसितस्वनः
श्रूयते सततं तत्र सर्वभूतमनोहरः
verses.transliteration:
gītavāditranirghoṣaḥ sotkṛṣṭahasitasvanaḥ
śrūyate satataṁ tatra sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ

translations.english: And there are continually heard there the sounds of instruments and the voice of song mixed with sweet hilarious laughter, capable of taking all crcatures.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र नामुदितः कश्चिन्नास्ति कश्चिदसत्प्रियः
अहन्यहनि वर्धन्ते गुणास्तत्र मनोरमाः
verses.transliteration:
tatra nāmuditaḥ kaścinnāsti kaścidasatpriyaḥ
ahanyahani vardhante guṇāstatra manoramāḥ

translations.english: No one is depressed there; nor does any one there want any desirable object; and day after day the delightful qualities find their development there.

verses.sanskrit:
समतिक्रम्य तं देशमुत्तरस्तोयसां निधिः
तत्र सोमगिरिर्नाम मध्ये हेममयो महान्
verses.transliteration:
samatikramya taṁ deśamuttarastoyasāṁ nidhiḥ
tatra somagirirnāma madhye hemamayo mahān

translations.english: Passing beyond that is the Northern ocean. In the bosom (of the deep) is the mountain named Somagiri, golden and of great dimensions.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु देशो विसूर्योऽपि तस्य भासा प्रकाशते
सूर्यलक्ष्म्याभिविज्ञेयस्तपसेव विवस्वता
verses.transliteration:
sa tu deśo visūryo'pi tasya bhāsā prakāśate
sūryalakṣmyābhivijñeyastapaseva vivasvatā

translations.english: Albeit without the sun, yet through the brightness of the Soma mountain, the land shines forth with all the loveliness and reality of one warmed by the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवानपि विश्वात्मा शम्भुरेकादशात्मकः
ब्रह्मा वसति देवेशो ब्रह्मर्षिपरिवारितः
verses.transliteration:
bhagavānapi viśvātmā śambhurekādaśātmakaḥ
brahmā vasati deveśo brahmarṣiparivāritaḥ

translations.english: There that Soul of the Universe, the adorable Sambhu, fraught with the spirits of the eleven Rudras-that lord of the gods-Brahmā.dwelleth, surrounded by the Brahmarsis.

verses.sanskrit:
न कथंचन गन्तव्यं कुरूणामुत्तरेण वः
अन्येषामपि भूतानां नातिक्रामति वै गतिः
verses.transliteration:
na kathaṁcana gantavyaṁ kurūṇāmuttareṇa vaḥ
anyeṣāmapi bhūtānāṁ nātikrāmati vai gatiḥ

translations.english: You cannot proceed to the north of the Kurus; nor is there way in that region for any other creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हि सोमगिरिर्नाम देवानामपि दुर्गमः
तमालोक्य ततः क्षिप्रमुपावर्तितुमर्हथ
verses.transliteration:
sā hi somagirirnāma devānāmapi durgamaḥ
tamālokya tataḥ kṣipramupāvartitumarhatha

translations.english: And that mountain is named Soma, incapable of being entered even by the gods, Sighting this you should speedily turn back.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावद्वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुंगवाः
अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्
verses.transliteration:
etāvadvānaraiḥ śakyaṁ gantuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ
abhāskaramamaryādaṁ na jānīmastataḥ param

translations.english: You foremost of monkey, the monkeys are competent to proceed thus far. Beyond that, of regions sunless and limitless I know nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वमेतद्विचेतव्यं यन्मया परिकीर्तितम्
यदन्यदपि नोक्तं च तत्रापि क्रियतां मतिः
verses.transliteration:
sarvametadvicetavyaṁ yanmayā parikīrtitam
yadanyadapi noktaṁ ca tatrāpi kriyatāṁ matiḥ

translations.english: You should search all these which I have described (to you); and you should also turn your attention to others besides, which I have omitted to mention.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृतं दाशरथेर्महत्प्रियं; महत्तरं चापि ततो मम प्रियम्
कृतं भविष्यत्यनिलानलोपमा; विदेहजा दर्शनजेन कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛtaṁ dāśarathermahatpriyaṁ; mahattaraṁ cāpi tato mama priyam
kṛtaṁ bhaviṣyatyanilānalopamā; videhajā darśanajena karmaṇā

translations.english: You that are comparable to the wind or fire, by accomplishing the work of beholding Videha's daughter, you will do what is held as exceedingly dear to Daśaratha's son as well as highly grateful to me.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृतार्थाः सहिताः सबान्धवा; मयार्चिताः सर्वगुणैर्मनोरमैः
चरिष्यथोर्वीं प्रतिशान्तशत्रवः; सहप्रिया भूतधराः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛtārthāḥ sahitāḥ sabāndhavā; mayārcitāḥ sarvaguṇairmanoramaiḥ
cariṣyathorvīṁ pratiśāntaśatravaḥ; sahapriyā bhūtadharāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Then, having achieved success, do you, along with your friends, honoured by me, and crowned with every virtue, you monkeys, with your enemies slain, range the earth in company with your wives,-the support of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
विशेषेण तु सुग्रीवो हनुमत्यर्थमुक्तवान्
स हि तस्मिन्हरिश्रेष्ठे निश्चितार्थोऽर्थसाधने
verses.transliteration:
viśeṣeṇa tu sugrīvo hanumatyarthamuktavān
sa hi tasminhariśreṣṭhe niścitārtho'rthasādhane

translations.english: Sugrīva had declared his conviction that he relied particularly upon Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
न भूमौ नान्तरिक्षे वा नाम्बरे नामरालये
नाप्सु वा गतिसंगं ते पश्यामि हरिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
na bhūmau nāntarikṣe vā nāmbare nāmarālaye
nāpsu vā gatisaṁgaṁ te paśyāmi haripuṁgava

translations.english: O foremost of monkeys, neither on the earth, nor in the sky', nor in the etherial regions, nor yet in water, find I any obstacle to your course. 1. Antariksa-regions above the earth in which the birds fly. 2. Ambara— Upper air.

verses.sanskrit:
सासुराः सहगन्धर्वाः सनागनरदेवताः
विदिताः सर्वलोकास्ते ससागरधराधराः
verses.transliteration:
sāsurāḥ sahagandharvāḥ sanāganaradevatāḥ
viditāḥ sarvalokāste sasāgaradharādharāḥ

translations.english: The entire worlds with Asuras, and Gandharvas, and Nāgas, and men, and gods, with oceans, and the earth and the regions beneath—are well known to you.

verses.sanskrit:
गतिर्वेगश्च तेजश्च लाघवं च महाकपे
पितुस्ते सदृशं वीर मारुतस्य महौजसः
verses.transliteration:
gatirvegaśca tejaśca lāghavaṁ ca mahākape
pituste sadṛśaṁ vīra mārutasya mahaujasaḥ

translations.english: And your motion, vehemence, energy and fleetness, are, O hero, O mighty ape, even like those of your sire, the powerful wind god; and there exists no creature on earth that is like to you in energy. Therefore do you bethink you how Sītā may be recovered.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वय्येव हनुमन्नस्ति बलं बुद्धिः पराक्रमः
देशकालानुवृत्तश्च नयश्च नयपण्डित
verses.transliteration:
tvayyeva hanumannasti balaṁ buddhiḥ parākramaḥ
deśakālānuvṛttaśca nayaśca nayapaṇḍita

translations.english: Even in you, O you versed in policy, are strength, and wit, and courage, and policy, and conduct in consonance with season and place.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कार्यसमासंगमवगम्य हनूमति
विदित्वा हनुमन्तं च चिन्तयामास राघवः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kāryasamāsaṁgamavagamya hanūmati
viditvā hanumantaṁ ca cintayāmāsa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, understanding that success in the task depended upon Hanumān, and also knowing what Hanumān was, Rāghava reflected,

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा निश्चितार्थोऽयं हनूमति हरीश्वरः
निश्चितार्थतरश्चापि हनूमान्कार्यसाधने
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā niścitārtho'yaṁ hanūmati harīśvaraḥ
niścitārthataraścāpi hanūmānkāryasādhane

translations.english: This lord of monkeys is every way confident concerning Hanumān; and Hanumān himself is even more confident of achieving success in the work.

verses.sanskrit:
तदेवं प्रस्थितस्यास्य परिज्ञातस्य कर्मभिः
भर्त्रा परिगृहीतस्य ध्रुवः कार्यफलोदयः
verses.transliteration:
tadevaṁ prasthitasyāsya parijñātasya karmabhiḥ
bhartrā parigṛhītasya dhruvaḥ kāryaphalodayaḥ

translations.english: He that has been tested by his deed, and who has been considered worthiest by his master, having veen commissioned in this business,-success in the work is certain.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समीक्ष्य महातेजा व्यवसायोत्तरं हरिम्
कृतार्थ इव संवृत्तः प्रहृष्टेन्द्रियमानसः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samīkṣya mahātejā vyavasāyottaraṁ harim
kṛtārtha iva saṁvṛttaḥ prahṛṣṭendriyamānasaḥ

translations.english: Then beholding that monkey who was the fittest for the task, that exceedingly energetic senses one, (Rāma), with his mind and exhilarated, considering himself as already crowned with success, felt the excess of joy.

verses.sanskrit:
ददौ तस्य ततः प्रीतः स्वनामाङ्कोपशोभितम्
अङ्गुलीयमभिज्ञानं राजपुत्र्याः परंतपः
verses.transliteration:
dadau tasya tataḥ prītaḥ svanāmāṅkopaśobhitam
aṅgulīyamabhijñānaṁ rājaputryāḥ paraṁtapaḥ

translations.english: And well pleased, that subduer of enemies handed to Hanuman a ring inscribed with his name, as a sign to the king's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ चिह्नेन जनकात्मजा
मत्सकाशादनुप्राप्तमनुद्विग्नानुपश्यति
verses.transliteration:
anena tvāṁ hariśreṣṭha cihnena janakātmajā
matsakāśādanuprāptamanudvignānupaśyati

translations.english: By this sign, O foremost of monkeys, Janaka's daughter will be able to see you fearlessly, as one that has come from me.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यवसायश्च ते वीर सत्त्वयुक्तश्च विक्रमः
सुग्रीवस्य च संदेशः सिद्धिं कथयतीव मे
verses.transliteration:
vyavasāyaśca te vīra sattvayuktaśca vikramaḥ
sugrīvasya ca saṁdeśaḥ siddhiṁ kathayatīva me

translations.english: Your firmness, O hero, and sterling prowess, as well as Sugrīva's saying, tell me greatly of success.

verses.sanskrit:
स तद्गृह्य हरिश्रेष्ठः स्थाप्य मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
वन्दित्वा चरणौ चैव प्रस्थितः प्लवगोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
sa tadgṛhya hariśreṣṭhaḥ sthāpya mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
vanditvā caraṇau caiva prasthitaḥ plavagottamaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, taking that (ring), and raising his joined palms to his head, that foremost and best of monkeys, saluting (Rāma's) feet, went away.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्प्रकर्षन्हरिणां बलं मह;द्बभूव वीरः पवनात्मजः कपि
गताम्बुदे व्योम्नि विशुद्धमण्डलः; शशीव नक्षत्रगणोपशोभितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatprakarṣanhariṇāṁ balaṁ maha;dbabhūva vīraḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapi
gatāmbude vyomni viśuddhamaṇḍalaḥ; śaśīva nakṣatragaṇopaśobhitaḥ

translations.english: Then taking with him that mighty host of monkeys, that hero, the son of the wind, resembled the moon of bright disc in the sky, garnished by the stars, after the clouds have departed.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिबलबलमाश्रितस्तवाहं; हरिवरविक्रमविक्रमैरनल्पैः
पवनसुत यथाभिगम्यते सा; जनकसुता हनुमंस्तथा कुरुष्व
verses.transliteration:
atibalabalamāśritastavāhaṁ; harivaravikramavikramairanalpaiḥ
pavanasuta yathābhigamyate sā; janakasutā hanumaṁstathā kuruṣva

translations.english: O you of excessive strength! I take refuge in your mighty. O you endowed with the prowess of the foremost of lions! do you, O son of the Wind, O Hanuman, exert yourself so, summoning the great strength you are master of, that we may obtain Janaka's daughter.* The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rāma and Sugrīva. But I think, it would fit Rāma's lips to a nicely. The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rāma and Sugrīva. But I think, it would fit Rāma's lips to a nicely.

verses.sanskrit:
तदुग्रशासनं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय हरिपुंगवाः
शलभा इव संछाद्य मेदिनीं संप्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
tadugraśāsanaṁ bharturvijñāya haripuṁgavāḥ
śalabhā iva saṁchādya medinīṁ saṁpratasthire

translations.english: The monkey-chiefs, knowing the stern command of their lord should search in all these places. Then, covering up the earth like locusts, they marched away.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः प्रस्रवणे तस्मिन्न्यवसत्सहलक्ष्मणः
प्रतीक्षमाणस्तं मासं यः सीताधिगमे कृतः
verses.transliteration:
rāmaḥ prasravaṇe tasminnyavasatsahalakṣmaṇaḥ
pratīkṣamāṇastaṁ māsaṁ yaḥ sītādhigame kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Expecting tidings of Sītä, Rāma remained that month in the vicinity of that cascade, in company with Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरां तु दिशं रम्यां गिरिराजसमावृताम्
प्रतस्थे सहसा वीरो हरिः शतबलिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
uttarāṁ tu diśaṁ ramyāṁ girirājasamāvṛtām
pratasthe sahasā vīro hariḥ śatabalistadā

translations.english: And that heroic monkey Satavali swiftly set out for the northern regions covered by the monarch of mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्चिमां तु दिशं घोरां सुषेणः प्लवगेश्वरः
प्रतस्थे हरिशार्दूलो भृशं वरुणपालिताम्
verses.transliteration:
paścimāṁ tu diśaṁ ghorāṁ suṣeṇaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
pratasthe hariśārdūlo bhṛśaṁ varuṇapālitām

translations.english: And that leader of monkey herds, Vinata, proceeded towards the estern quarter. And that monkey, Hanumān-leader of monkeyherds in company with Tārā, Angada and others, went to the South, inhabited by Agastya. And that lord of monkeys, Suşeņa, lion among monkeys, went to the terrible western quarter, protected by Varuna.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सर्वा दिशो राजा चोदयित्वा यथा तथम्
कपिसेना पतीन्मुख्यान्मुमोद सुखितः सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sarvā diśo rājā codayitvā yathā tatham
kapisenā patīnmukhyānmumoda sukhitaḥ sukham

translations.english: Then, having properly despatched (his forces) in all directions, that general of the monkey hosts, being pleased, gave himself up to sport.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं संचोदिताः सर्वे राज्ञा वानरयूथपाः
स्वां स्वां दिशमभिप्रेत्य त्वरिताः संप्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ saṁcoditāḥ sarve rājñā vānarayūthapāḥ
svāṁ svāṁ diśamabhipretya tvaritāḥ saṁpratasthire

translations.english: Thus despatched by the king, the monkeychiefs proceeded apace respectively towards their destined quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येकैकं तदा तत्र वानरा बलदर्पिताः
ऊचुश्च वचनं तस्मिन्हरिराजस्य संनिधौ
verses.transliteration:
ityekaikaṁ tadā tatra vānarā baladarpitāḥ
ūcuśca vacanaṁ tasminharirājasya saṁnidhau

translations.english: Thus did the apes proud of their strength, severally speak in presence of the sovereign of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
गतेषु वानरेन्द्रेषु रामः सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्
कथं भवान्विनाजीते सर्वं वै मण्डलं भुवः
verses.transliteration:
gateṣu vānarendreṣu rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt
kathaṁ bhavānvinājīte sarvaṁ vai maṇḍalaṁ bhuvaḥ

translations.english: On the monkey-chiefs having departed, Rāma said to Sugrīva, How is it that you know all the quarters of this earth?'

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्तु ततो राममुवाच प्रणतात्मवान्
श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये विस्तरेण नरर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvastu tato rāmamuvāca praṇatātmavān
śrūyatāṁ sarvamākhyāsye vistareṇa nararṣabha

translations.english: Thereupon, the self-controlled Sugrīva, bowing low, said to Rāma, Do you listen to my words. I shall relate everything.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा विवेश महिषो मलयस्य गुहां प्रति
विवेश वाली तत्रापि मलयं तज्जिघांसया
verses.transliteration:
tadā viveśa mahiṣo malayasya guhāṁ prati
viveśa vālī tatrāpi malayaṁ tajjighāṁsayā

translations.english: When Vāli pursued the Dānava Dundubhi, wearing the form of a buffalo towards the Malaya mountain, Mahișa entered a cave of that mountain. And Vali also, desirous of slaying the Asura, entered Malaya.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं तत्र निक्षिप्तो गुहाद्वारिविनीतवत्
न च निष्क्रमते वाली तदा संवत्सरे गते
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ tatra nikṣipto guhādvārivinītavat
na ca niṣkramate vālī tadā saṁvatsare gate

translations.english: And I was made to stand at the mouth in humble guise; nor did Väli issue out, although a good year rolled away.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्षतजवेगेन आपुपूरे तदा बिलम्
तदहं विस्मितो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातृशोकविषार्दितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṣatajavegena āpupūre tadā bilam
tadahaṁ vismito dṛṣṭvā bhrātṛśokaviṣārditaḥ

translations.english: Then the cave became filled with blood gushing out vehemently. Seeing this, I became amazed, and exercised with the poison of grief of accountri my brother.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाहं कृतबुद्धिस्तु सुव्यक्तं निहतो गुरुः
शिलापर्वतसंकाशा बिलद्वारि मया कृता
अशक्नुवन्निष्क्रमितुं महिषो विनशेदिति
verses.transliteration:
athāhaṁ kṛtabuddhistu suvyaktaṁ nihato guruḥ
śilāparvatasaṁkāśā biladvāri mayā kṛtā
aśaknuvanniṣkramituṁ mahiṣo vinaśediti

translations.english: And I, losing my sense, thought that my superior had for certain been slain. And I placed 7 crag huge as a hill at the mouth of the cave. took to my

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहमागां किष्किन्धां निराशस्तस्य जीविते
राज्यं च सुमहत्प्राप्तं तारा च रुमया सह
मित्रैश्च सहितस्तत्र वसामि विगतज्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tato'hamāgāṁ kiṣkindhāṁ nirāśastasya jīvite
rājyaṁ ca sumahatprāptaṁ tārā ca rumayā saha
mitraiśca sahitastatra vasāmi vigatajvaraḥ

translations.english: And obtaining the spacious kingdom along with Tãrã and Umā, I began to pass my days in peace in company with his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
स मां जिघांसुर्दुष्टात्मा वाली प्रव्यथितेन्द्रियः
परिलाकयते क्रोधाद्धावन्तं सचिवैः सह
verses.transliteration:
sa māṁ jighāṁsurduṣṭātmā vālī pravyathitendriyaḥ
parilākayate krodhāddhāvantaṁ sacivaiḥ saha

translations.english: Then came that foremost of monkeys, having slain him (Mahisa). Thereupon I, influenced by fear, in consideration of his dignity, made over to him his monarchy. But Vali, his senses exercised with sorrow, anxious to slay me, in company with his counsellors, pursued me, who heels.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं वालिना तेन सानुबन्धः प्रधावितः
नदीश्च विविधाः पश्यन्वनानि नगराणि च
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ vālinā tena sānubandhaḥ pradhāvitaḥ
nadīśca vividhāḥ paśyanvanāni nagarāṇi ca

translations.english: Hotly pursued and chased by Vāli, I surveyed various streams and woods and cities. And I surveyed the earth like the hoof-print of a cow, or the image reflected from a mirror, or a firebrand whirled (in the air).* *The commentator remarks that like the hoof-print of a cow expresses the case with which Sugrīva travelled the earth; like a fire brand whirled conveys his vehement speed; and like the image reflected on a mirror signifies the lucidity of his perception.

verses.sanskrit:
इदानीं मे स्मृतं राजन्यथा वाली हरीश्वरः
मतङ्गेन तदा शप्तो ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रममण्डले
verses.transliteration:
idānīṁ me smṛtaṁ rājanyathā vālī harīśvaraḥ
mataṅgena tadā śapto hyasminnāśramamaṇḍale

translations.english: 'O king, now, I remember me how that lord of monkeys, Vāli, was cursed by Matanga in this very hermitage. If Vāli enters (into this asylum), his head becomes cleft in hundred.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पर्वतमासाद्य ऋश्यमूकं नृपात्मज
न विवेश तदा वाली मतङ्गस्य भयात्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ parvatamāsādya ṛśyamūkaṁ nṛpātmaja
na viveśa tadā vālī mataṅgasya bhayāttadā

translations.english: There shall dwell happily without anxiety.' O king's son, thereupon, we went to the Rișyamuka mountain, nor did then Vāli enter we there from fear of Matanga.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं मया तदा राजन्प्रत्यक्षमुपलक्षितम्
पृथिवीमण्डलं कृत्स्नं गुहामस्म्यागतस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ mayā tadā rājanpratyakṣamupalakṣitam
pṛthivīmaṇḍalaṁ kṛtsnaṁ guhāmasmyāgatastataḥ

translations.english: Thus, O king, did I actually see all the world. And from that place I came to this cave.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शनार्थं तु वैदेह्याः सर्वतः कपियूथपाः
व्यादिष्टाः कपिराजेन यथोक्तं जग्मुरञ्जसा
verses.transliteration:
darśanārthaṁ tu vaidehyāḥ sarvataḥ kapiyūthapāḥ
vyādiṣṭāḥ kapirājena yathoktaṁ jagmurañjasā

translations.english: The principal monkeys, having been ordered by the monkey-king, speedily went in all directions to their destinations for the purpose of seeing Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
सरांसि सरितः कक्षानाकाशं नगराणि च
नदीदुर्गांस्तथा शैलान्विचिन्वन्ति समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
sarāṁsi saritaḥ kakṣānākāśaṁ nagarāṇi ca
nadīdurgāṁstathā śailānvicinvanti samantataḥ

translations.english: And on all sides they explore watery expanses, and streams, and lawns, and commons, and cities, and tracts rendered impassable by torrents.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवेण समाख्यातान्सर्वे वानरयूथपाः
प्रदेशान्प्रविचिन्वन्ति सशैलवनकाननान्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīveṇa samākhyātānsarve vānarayūthapāḥ
pradeśānpravicinvanti saśailavanakānanān

translations.english: And the leaders of monkey-herds search all those countries, countries, described described by Sugrīva,-containing mountains, woods and forests.

verses.sanskrit:
विचिन्त्य दिवसं सर्वे सीताधिगमने धृताः
समायान्ति स्म मेदिन्यां निशाकालेशु वानराः
verses.transliteration:
vicintya divasaṁ sarve sītādhigamane dhṛtāḥ
samāyānti sma medinyāṁ niśākāleśu vānarāḥ

translations.english: Engaged during the day in search of Sītā, at night the monkeys seek the ground (for sleep).

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वर्तुकांश्च देशेषु वानराः सफलान्द्रुमान्
आसाद्य रजनीं शय्यां चक्रुः सर्वेष्वहःसु ते
verses.transliteration:
sarvartukāṁśca deśeṣu vānarāḥ saphalāndrumān
āsādya rajanīṁ śayyāṁ cakruḥ sarveṣvahaḥsu te

translations.english: In every place, by day coming to trees aye enjoying every season, and crowned with fruits, the monkeys prepared their beds at night.* *The sense is rather obscure, it being difficult to understand the relation their beds bore to the neighbouring trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तदहः प्रथमं कृत्वा मासे प्रस्रवणं गताः
कपिराजेन संगम्य निराशाः कपियूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
tadahaḥ prathamaṁ kṛtvā māse prasravaṇaṁ gatāḥ
kapirājena saṁgamya nirāśāḥ kapiyūthapāḥ

translations.english: Counting that day* as the first, the principal monkeys, after the month had run out, resigning all hope, came to the Fountain and met with the monkey-king. *i.e. the day of their departure.

verses.sanskrit:
विचित्य तु दिशं पूर्वां यथोक्तां सचिवैः सह
अदृष्ट्वा विनतः सीतामाजगाम महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
vicitya tu diśaṁ pūrvāṁ yathoktāṁ sacivaiḥ saha
adṛṣṭvā vinataḥ sītāmājagāma mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And having explored the Eastern regions, as directed, the exceedingly strong Vinata not having been able to see Sītā, came back, in company with his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरां तु दिशं सर्वां विचित्य स महाकपिः
आगतः सह सैन्येन वीरः शतबलिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
uttarāṁ tu diśaṁ sarvāṁ vicitya sa mahākapiḥ
āgataḥ saha sainyena vīraḥ śatabalistadā

translations.english: And then that mighty ape, Satavali, daunted in spirits, arrived with his forces, after having searched all through the North.

verses.sanskrit:
सुषेणः पश्चिमामाशां विचित्य सह वानरैः
समेत्य मासे संपूर्णे सुग्रीवमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
suṣeṇaḥ paścimāmāśāṁ vicitya saha vānaraiḥ
sametya māse saṁpūrṇe sugrīvamupacakrame

translations.english: And having searched the West in company with his monkeys, Sușeņa, on the month being complete, presented himself before Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रस्रवणपृष्ठस्थं समासाद्याभिवाद्य च
आसीनं सह रामेण सुग्रीवमिदमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prasravaṇapṛṣṭhasthaṁ samāsādyābhivādya ca
āsīnaṁ saha rāmeṇa sugrīvamidamabruvan

translations.english: And coming to Sugrīva seated along with Rāma behind the Fountain, and saluting the former, Susena said to Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
गहनेषु च देशेषु दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च
सत्त्वान्यतिप्रमाणानि विचितानि हतानि च
ये चैव गहना देशा विचितास्ते पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
gahaneṣu ca deśeṣu durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
sattvānyatipramāṇāni vicitāni hatāni ca
ye caiva gahanā deśā vicitāste punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Searched have been all the mountains, and deep woods, and streams, and islands embosomed in the ocean, and the various provinces. And also searched have been all the caves which have been described by you; and searched have been all the groves entertwined with plants; and thickets; and difficult and uneven grounds. And huge animals have been sought out and slain (by us). And all the impracticable places we have explored again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
उदारसत्त्वाभिजनो महात्मा; स मैथिलीं द्रक्ष्यति वानरेन्द्रः
दिशं तु यामेव गता तु सीता; तामास्थितो वायुसुतो हनूमान्
verses.transliteration:
udārasattvābhijano mahātmā; sa maithilīṁ drakṣyati vānarendraḥ
diśaṁ tu yāmeva gatā tu sītā; tāmāsthito vāyusuto hanūmān

translations.english: O lord of monkeys, possessed of great strength and nobly born, it is Hanumān who will be able to ascertain the whereabouts of Mithila's daughter. And the Wind's son, Hanumān, has followed even the has by which Sītā has gone.

verses.sanskrit:
सहताराङ्गदाभ्यां तु गत्वा स हनुमान्कपिः
सुग्रीवेण यथोद्दिष्टं तं देशमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
sahatārāṅgadābhyāṁ tu gatvā sa hanumānkapiḥ
sugrīveṇa yathoddiṣṭaṁ taṁ deśamupacakrame

translations.english: The monkey Hanumān in company with Tārā and Angada swiftly set out for the quarter assigned by Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्वेषमाणास्ते सर्वे वानराः सर्वतो दिशम्
न सीतां ददृशुर्वीरा मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
anveṣamāṇāste sarve vānarāḥ sarvato diśam
na sītāṁ dadṛśurvīrā maithilīṁ janakātmajām

translations.english: And having proceeded far along with all those foremost of monkeys, he explored the caves and woods of Vindhya; spots inaccessible in consequence of streams intervening in front of mountains; and tanks; and tracts filled with trees; and various mountains rife with wild trees. And having searched in all directions, the monkeys could not find Maithilī, Janaka's daughter Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
स्निग्धपत्राः स्थले यत्र पद्मिन्यः फुल्लपङ्कजाः
प्रेक्षणीयाः सुगन्धाश्च भ्रमरैश्चापि वर्जिताः
verses.transliteration:
snigdhapatrāḥ sthale yatra padminyaḥ phullapaṅkajāḥ
prekṣaṇīyāḥ sugandhāśca bhramaraiścāpi varjitāḥ

translations.english: And there are there neither trees, nor annual plants, nor creepers, nor herbs,-and in that place there are no pleasant pools, with cool leaves, and filled with blown lotuses, and it has been renounced by the black-bees.

verses.sanskrit:
कण्डुर्नाम महाभागः सत्यवादी तपोधनः
महर्षिः परमामर्षी नियमैर्दुष्प्रधर्षणः
verses.transliteration:
kaṇḍurnāma mahābhāgaḥ satyavādī tapodhanaḥ
maharṣiḥ paramāmarṣī niyamairduṣpradharṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: There dwelleth a Maharași, Kandu by name, an eminently pious, and truthful ascetic, irascible, and irrepressible because of his practice of self-discipline.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तस्मिन्वने पुत्रो बालको दशवार्षिकः
प्रनष्टो जीवितान्ताय क्रुद्धस्तत्र महामुनिः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tasminvane putro bālako daśavārṣikaḥ
pranaṣṭo jīvitāntāya kruddhastatra mahāmuniḥ

translations.english: In that wood his son, a boy of ten years, his sands having run out, breathed his last; and it is for this that the mighty ascetic has come under the influence of passion.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन धर्मात्मना शप्तं कृत्स्नं तत्र महद्वनम्
अशरण्यं दुराधर्षं मृगपक्षिविवर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
tena dharmātmanā śaptaṁ kṛtsnaṁ tatra mahadvanam
aśaraṇyaṁ durādharṣaṁ mṛgapakṣivivarjitam

translations.english: And cursed by that high-souled one, the entire mighty forest has become unfit to harbour (any creatures); difficult of entrance; and devoid of birds and beasts.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ते काननान्तांस्तु गिरीणां कन्दराणि च
प्रभवानि नदीनांच विचिन्वन्ति समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya te kānanāntāṁstu girīṇāṁ kandarāṇi ca
prabhavāni nadīnāṁca vicinvanti samāhitāḥ

translations.english: They carefully search the skirts of its woods, mountain-caves, and the sources of its streams. And those high-souled ones, devoted to the good of Sugrīva, did not find Janaka's daughter, or her ravisher, Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
ते प्रविश्य तु तं भीमं लतागुल्मसमावृतम्
ददृशुः क्रूरकर्माणमसुरं सुरनिर्भयम्
verses.transliteration:
te praviśya tu taṁ bhīmaṁ latāgulmasamāvṛtam
dadṛśuḥ krūrakarmāṇamasuraṁ suranirbhayam

translations.english: And entering (into a wood), they saw a terrible Asura, concealed by the shrubs and plants-of dreadful deeds, and cherishing no fear even of the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा वनरा घोरं स्थितं शैलमिवापरम्
गाढं परिहिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तं पर्वतोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā vanarā ghoraṁ sthitaṁ śailamivāparam
gāḍhaṁ parihitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā taṁ parvatopamam

translations.english: And seeing that dreadful Asura, seated like a hill, and resembling a mountain, they all tightened their cloths,

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपि तान्वानरान्सर्वान्नष्टाः स्थेत्यब्रवीद्बली
अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो मुष्टिमुद्यम्य संहितम्
verses.transliteration:
so'pi tānvānarānsarvānnaṣṭāḥ sthetyabravīdbalī
abhyadhāvata saṁkruddho muṣṭimudyamya saṁhitam

translations.english: And that strong one also, saying to the monkeys, Destroyed are you, and uplifting his clenched fist, rushed after them in rage.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं सहसा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदस्तदा
रावणोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा तलेनाभिजघान ह
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ sahasā vāliputro'ṅgadastadā
rāvaṇo'yamiti jñātvā talenābhijaghāna ha

translations.english: And as he darted suddenly, Angada, the son of Vali, knowing, This is Ravana, administered to him a slap.

verses.sanskrit:
स वालिपुत्राभिहतो वक्त्राच्छोणितमुद्वमन्
असुरो न्यपतद्भूमौ पर्यस्त इव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa vāliputrābhihato vaktrācchoṇitamudvaman
asuro nyapatadbhūmau paryasta iva parvataḥ

translations.english: Struck by Vāli's son, that Asura, his mouth vomiting blood, fell down to the earth like a hill toppled down. And on his having breathed his last, the monkeys, elated with victory, thoroughly searched that mountain cavern.

verses.sanskrit:
विचितं तु ततः कृत्वा सर्वे ते काननं पुनः
अन्यदेवापरं घोरं विविशुर्गिरिगह्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
vicitaṁ tu tataḥ kṛtvā sarve te kānanaṁ punaḥ
anyadevāparaṁ ghoraṁ viviśurgirigahvaram

translations.english: And when they had satisfied themselves that the cave had been searched all through, the dwellers of the woods entered another fearful mountain cavern.

verses.sanskrit:
ते विचिन्त्य पुनः खिन्ना विनिष्पत्य समागताः
एकान्ते वृक्षमूले तु निषेदुर्दीनमानसाः
verses.transliteration:
te vicintya punaḥ khinnā viniṣpatya samāgatāḥ
ekānte vṛkṣamūle tu niṣedurdīnamānasāḥ

translations.english: And after having searched (that place) also, they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree. they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाङ्गदस्तदा सर्वान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत्
परिश्रान्तो महाप्राज्ञः समाश्वास्य शनैर्वचः
verses.transliteration:
athāṅgadastadā sarvānvānarānidamabravīt
pariśrānto mahāprājñaḥ samāśvāsya śanairvacaḥ

translations.english: Then the eminently wise Angada, fatigued, spoke to all the monkeys, cheering them.

verses.sanskrit:
वनानि गिरयो नद्यो दुर्गाणि गहनानि च
दर्यो गिरिगुहाश्चैव विचिता नः समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
vanāni girayo nadyo durgāṇi gahanāni ca
daryo giriguhāścaiva vicitā naḥ samantataḥ

translations.english: Woods, and mountains, and rivers, and impenetrable wilds, and valleys, and mountain caverns have been thoroughly searched. But Jānakī we have failed to find anywhere,—or that wicked wight, the Rākṣasa that has ravished Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
कालश्च नो महान्यातः सुग्रीवश्चोग्रशासनः
तस्माद्भवन्तः सहिता विचिन्वन्तु समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
kālaśca no mahānyātaḥ sugrīvaścograśāsanaḥ
tasmādbhavantaḥ sahitā vicinvantu samantataḥ

translations.english: We have spent a great part of the term that had been assigned by Sugrīva of stern commands. Therefore, banishing languor, sadness, and invading drowsiness, do you together search all round.

verses.sanskrit:
विहाय तन्द्रीं शोकं च निद्रां चैव समुत्थिताम्
विचिनुध्वं यथा सीतां पश्यामो जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
vihāya tandrīṁ śokaṁ ca nidrāṁ caiva samutthitām
vicinudhvaṁ yathā sītāṁ paśyāmo janakātmajām

translations.english: Do you so search Sītā, that she may be found out (by us). High spirits, ability and forwardness in action, are said to conduce to success. Therefore it is that I speak thus to you.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यापीदं वनं दुर्गं विचिन्वन्तु वनौकसः
खेदं त्यक्त्वा पुनः सर्वं वनमेतद्विचीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
adyāpīdaṁ vanaṁ durgaṁ vicinvantu vanaukasaḥ
khedaṁ tyaktvā punaḥ sarvaṁ vanametadvicīyatām

translations.english: You dwellers of the wood, do you to day rummage this impenetrable wood; renouncing grief, do you again search through this forest.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं क्रियमाणस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्
अलं निर्वेदमागम्य न हि नो मलिनं क्षमम्
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ kriyamāṇasya dṛśyate karmaṇaḥ phalam
alaṁ nirvedamāgamya na hi no malinaṁ kṣamam

translations.english: Those who act, for certain behold the fruit of their endeavours; but if people once give way to grief, they cannot again attain vigour.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवः क्रोधनो राजा तीक्ष्णदण्डश्च वानराः
भेतव्यं तस्य सततं रामस्य च महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvaḥ krodhano rājā tīkṣṇadaṇḍaśca vānarāḥ
bhetavyaṁ tasya satataṁ rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: You monkeys, king Sugrīva is irascible; and inflicteth sharp punishments. He should be always feared, as also the magnanimous Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
हितार्थमेतदुक्तं वः क्रियतां यदि रोचते
उच्यतां वा क्षमं यन्नः सर्वेषामेव वानराः
verses.transliteration:
hitārthametaduktaṁ vaḥ kriyatāṁ yadi rocate
ucyatāṁ vā kṣamaṁ yannaḥ sarveṣāmeva vānarāḥ

translations.english: I tell you this for your good. Act accordingly, if you list. And do you also express what else you are capable of.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वचनं गन्धमादनः
उवाचाव्यक्तया वाचा पिपासा श्रमखिन्नया
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā vacanaṁ gandhamādanaḥ
uvācāvyaktayā vācā pipāsā śramakhinnayā

translations.english: Hearing Angada's words Gandhamādana said in candid words faint from thirst and fatigue,

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं खलु वो वाक्यमङ्गदो यदुवाच ह
हितं चैवानुकूलं च क्रियतामस्य भाषितम्
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ khalu vo vākyamaṅgado yaduvāca ha
hitaṁ caivānukūlaṁ ca kriyatāmasya bhāṣitam

translations.english: What Angada has said to us is worthy of him, and is beneficial and good. Do you follow his speech.

verses.sanskrit:
यथोद्दिष्ठानि सर्वाणि सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
विचिन्वन्तु वनं सर्वे गिरिदुर्गाणि सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
yathoddiṣṭhāni sarvāṇi sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
vicinvantu vanaṁ sarve giridurgāṇi sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Let us afresh search hills, caves and rocks, vacant forests and mountain cascades,-in accordance with what the high-souled Sugrīva has laid down. Let all in a body rummage the wood, and the mountain caverns.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समुत्थाय पुनर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः
विन्ध्यकाननसंकीर्णां विचेरुर्दक्षिणां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samutthāya punarvānarāste mahābalāḥ
vindhyakānanasaṁkīrṇāṁ vicerurdakṣiṇāṁ diśam

translations.english: There rising up, the mighty monkeys again began to range the South close with forests belonging to Vindhya.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शारदाभ्रप्रतिमं श्रीमद्रजतपर्वतम्
शृङ्गवन्तं दरीवन्तमधिरुह्य च वानराः
verses.transliteration:
te śāradābhrapratimaṁ śrīmadrajataparvatam
śṛṅgavantaṁ darīvantamadhiruhya ca vānarāḥ

translations.english: And the monkeys ascended the Silvern Hill resembling the autumnal welkin, graceful, and furnished with summits and valleys.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र लोध्रवनं रम्यं सप्तपर्णवनानि च
विचिन्वन्तो हरिवराः सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
tatra lodhravanaṁ ramyaṁ saptaparṇavanāni ca
vicinvanto harivarāḥ sītādarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: And eager to behold Sītā, those excellent monkeys began to search the Lodhra wood, and the Saptaparņa forests.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याग्रमधिरूढास्ते श्रान्ता विपुलविक्रमाः
न पश्यन्ति स्म वैदेहीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāgramadhirūḍhāste śrāntā vipulavikramāḥ
na paśyanti sma vaidehīṁ rāmasya mahiṣīṁ priyām

translations.english: And ascending its top*, those ones endued with immense prowess, experiencing fatigue, could not find Vaidehi, the beloved spouse of Rama. *i.e. the top of the Silvern Hill.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु दृष्टिगतं कृत्वा तं शैलं बहुकन्दरम्
अवारोहन्त हरयो वीक्षमाणाः समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
te tu dṛṣṭigataṁ kṛtvā taṁ śailaṁ bahukandaram
avārohanta harayo vīkṣamāṇāḥ samantataḥ

translations.english: And having surveyed that hill having many a grot, so far as the eye could range, the monkeys looking all round, descended (the eminence).

verses.sanskrit:
अवरुह्य ततो भूमिं श्रान्ता विगतचेतसः
स्थित्वा मुहूर्तं तत्राथ वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
avaruhya tato bhūmiṁ śrāntā vigatacetasaḥ
sthitvā muhūrtaṁ tatrātha vṛkṣamūlamupāśritāḥ

translations.english: And having descended to the earth, the monkeys, bewildered, and losing their consciousness, rested for a while at the foot of a tree.

verses.sanskrit:
ते मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्ताः किंचिद्भग्नपरिश्रमाः
पुनरेवोद्यताः कृत्स्नां मार्गितुं दक्षिणां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
te muhūrtaṁ samāśvastāḥ kiṁcidbhagnapariśramāḥ
punarevodyatāḥ kṛtsnāṁ mārgituṁ dakṣiṇāṁ diśam

translations.english: And their fatigue having gone off a little, the monkeys, having been refreshed for a while, again prepared to explore the whole South.

verses.sanskrit:
हनुमत्प्रमुखास्ते तु प्रस्थिताः प्लवगर्षभाः
विन्ध्यमेवादितस्तावद्विचेरुस्ते समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
hanumatpramukhāste tu prasthitāḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
vindhyamevāditastāvadviceruste samantataḥ

translations.english: And the monkey chiefs, headed by Hanumān, having set out (on the search), began to range all through Vindhya.

verses.sanskrit:
सिंहशार्दूलजुष्टाश्च गुहाश्च परितस्तथा
विषमेषु नगेन्द्रस्य महाप्रस्रवणेषु च
verses.transliteration:
siṁhaśārdūlajuṣṭāśca guhāśca paritastathā
viṣameṣu nagendrasya mahāprasravaṇeṣu ca

translations.english: The monkey, Hanumān, in company with Tārā and Angada searcheth the caves and woods of Vindhya, caverns all around haunted by lions and tigers, and in vast inaccessible cascades in that foremost of mountains.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां तत्रैव वसतां स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration: teṣāṁ tatraiva vasatāṁ sa kālo vyatyavartata

translations.english: And they came to the south-western summit of the inountain. And when they sojourned there, their (appointed) term had not expired.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि देशो दुरन्वेषो गुहा गहनवान्महान्
तत्र वायुसुतः सर्वं विचिनोति स्म पर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa hi deśo duranveṣo guhā gahanavānmahān
tatra vāyusutaḥ sarvaṁ vicinoti sma parvatam

translations.english: And that spacious country, consisting as it did, of caves and grots and woods, was difficult to search. And there the wind-god's offspring searched all over the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्बिलमासाद्य सुगन्धि दुरतिक्रमम्
विस्मयव्यग्रमनसो बभूवुर्वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
tatastadbilamāsādya sugandhi duratikramam
vismayavyagramanaso babhūvurvānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And drawing nigh to that fragrant and inaccessible cave, those superior monkeys were struck with amaze, and became eager (to enter into it).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पर्वतकूटाभो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
अब्रवीद्वानरान्सर्वान्कान्तार वनकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ parvatakūṭābho hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
abravīdvānarānsarvānkāntāra vanakovidaḥ

translations.english: And with their minds filled with doubt, those vigorous foremost of monkeys gladly approached that cave; abounding in diverse animals, resembling the residence of the lord of Daityas, dazzling, and dreadful, and impenetrable on all sides. Then Hanuman the son of the wind-god, possessed of the splendour of a mountain-summit, cognizant of woods and forests, said to the grim-visaged apes,

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिजालावृतान्देशान्मार्गित्वा दक्षिणां दिशम्
वयं सर्वे परिश्रान्ता न च पश्यामि मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
girijālāvṛtāndeśānmārgitvā dakṣiṇāṁ diśam
vayaṁ sarve pariśrāntā na ca paśyāmi maithilīm

translations.english: Having explored the South, (containing) countries enveloped with mountain chains, we have all got fatigued, but we have failed to find Mithila's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माच्चापि बिलाद्धंसाः क्रौञ्चाश्च सह सारसैः
जलार्द्राश्चक्रवाकाश्च निष्पतन्ति स्म सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
asmāccāpi bilāddhaṁsāḥ krauñcāśca saha sārasaiḥ
jalārdrāścakravākāśca niṣpatanti sma sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: And from yonder cave come out swarms of and and kraunchas and chakravākas, drenched with water. For certain here is a well or a watery expanse. And at the mouth of the cave there are these cool trees.'

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तस्मिन्बिले दुर्गे नानापादपसंकुले
अन्योन्यं संपरिष्वज्य जग्मुर्योजनमन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastasminbile durge nānāpādapasaṁkule
anyonyaṁ saṁpariṣvajya jagmuryojanamantaram

translations.english: And those foremost of monkeys rushed into the cavity; and beheld displayed (before them) an excellent and charming scene. And embracing each other in that fearful cave rife with various trees, they passed over an hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
ते नष्टसंज्ञास्तृषिताः संभ्रान्ताः सलिलार्थिनः
परिपेतुर्बिले तस्मिन्कंचित्कालमतन्द्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
te naṣṭasaṁjñāstṛṣitāḥ saṁbhrāntāḥ salilārthinaḥ
paripeturbile tasminkaṁcitkālamatandritāḥ

translations.english: And deprived of their sense, and tried with thirst, and bewildered, and thirsting for water, they for a time vigilantly descended in darkness down the cave. And emaciated, with woebegone faces, and spent, those monkeys despairing of their lives, (at last) saw light.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं देशमागम्य सौम्यं वितिमिरं वनम्
ददृशुः काञ्चनान्वृक्षान्दीप्तवैश्वानरप्रभान्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ deśamāgamya saumyaṁ vitimiraṁ vanam
dadṛśuḥ kāñcanānvṛkṣāndīptavaiśvānaraprabhān

translations.english: Those mild ones, coming to a spot free from darkness, saw golden trees, possessed of the brightness of flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तपनीयगवाक्षाणि मुक्ताजालावृतानि च
हैमराजतभौमानि वैदूर्यमणिमन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
tapanīyagavākṣāṇi muktājālāvṛtāni ca
haimarājatabhaumāni vaidūryamaṇimanti ca

translations.english: And the monkeys saw there golden as well as silvern vehicles, and elegant dwellings all round veiled with nets of pearls; having golden balconys; with their grounds paved with gold and silver; and furnished with lapis lazulis.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हनूमान्गिरिसंनिकाशः; कृताञ्जलिस्तामभिवाद्य वृद्धाम्
पप्रच्छ का त्वं भवनं बिलं च; रत्नानि चेमानि वदस्व कस्य
verses.transliteration:
tato hanūmāngirisaṁnikāśaḥ; kṛtāñjalistāmabhivādya vṛddhām
papraccha kā tvaṁ bhavanaṁ bilaṁ ca; ratnāni cemāni vadasva kasya

translations.english: And-Hanumān like to a hill, bowing down to the old women with joined hands, asked her, saying,-Who are you? And tell me, to whom belong this edifice and the cave as well as all these jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा हनुमांस्तत्र पुनः कृष्णाजिनाम्बराम्
अब्रवीत्तां महाभागां तापसीं धर्मचारिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā hanumāṁstatra punaḥ kṛṣṇājināmbarām
abravīttāṁ mahābhāgāṁ tāpasīṁ dharmacāriṇīm

translations.english: Having said this to that female clad in a piece of black deer-skin, Hanumān asked that highly religious ascetic practising pious offices,

verses.sanskrit:
महद्धिरण्या विवरं प्रविष्टाः स्म पिपासिताः
इमांस्त्वेवं विधान्भावान्विविधानद्भुतोपमान्
दृष्ट्वा वयं प्रव्यथिताः संभ्रान्ता नष्टचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
mahaddhiraṇyā vivaraṁ praviṣṭāḥ sma pipāsitāḥ
imāṁstvevaṁ vidhānbhāvānvividhānadbhutopamān
dṛṣṭvā vayaṁ pravyathitāḥ saṁbhrāntā naṣṭacetasaḥ

translations.english: Having rashly entered this cave enveloped in gloom, we have been exercised with hunger and thirst; and are extremely faint.
