And, having entered this mighty cave underneath the earth, we have become thirsty. And, seeing all these wonderful phenomena, we have become afflicted, and bewildered; and have lost our sense. To whom belong these golden trees resembling the infantine sun;

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनानि विमानानि राजतानि गृहाणि च
तपनीय गवाक्षाणि मणिजालावृतानि च
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāni vimānāni rājatāni gṛhāṇi ca
tapanīya gavākṣāṇi maṇijālāvṛtāni ca

translations.english: And the pure fruits and roots, and the houses and vehicles of gold and silver,-veiled in networks of jewels, and furnished with golden windows? And by whose energy are these golden trees (here), bearing flowers, crowned with fruits, grateful to the sight, and breathing rich odour?

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनानि च पद्मानि जातानि विमले जले
कथं मत्स्याश्च सौवर्णा चरन्ति सह कच्छपैः
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāni ca padmāni jātāni vimale jale
kathaṁ matsyāśca sauvarṇā caranti saha kacchapaiḥ

translations.english: And golden lotuses spring in in lucent water,-how golden fishes are discovered in it along with tortoises! Have these sprung from your power; or do they owe their existence to the ascetic energy of any other? It behoves you to relate all this to us who are ignorant of everything.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता तापसी धर्मचारिणी
प्रत्युवाच हनूमन्तं सर्वभूतहिते रता
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā hanumatā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī
pratyuvāca hanūmantaṁ sarvabhūtahite ratā

translations.english: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the female ascetic practising righteousness, and engaged in the welfare of all beings, replied to Hanumān,

verses.sanskrit:
मयो नाम महातेजा मायावी दानवर्षभः
तेनेदं निर्मितं सर्वं मायया काञ्चनं वनम्
verses.transliteration:
mayo nāma mahātejā māyāvī dānavarṣabhaḥ
tenedaṁ nirmitaṁ sarvaṁ māyayā kāñcanaṁ vanam

translations.english: O foremost of monkeys, there is one, named Maya, spreader of illusions. By him has this entire golden grove been constructed through his wonderful power of construction.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा दानवमुख्यानां विश्वकर्मा बभूव ह
येनेदं काञ्चनं दिव्यं निर्मितं भवनोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
purā dānavamukhyānāṁ viśvakarmā babhūva ha
yenedaṁ kāñcanaṁ divyaṁ nirmitaṁ bhavanottamam

translations.english: He that as reared this excellent golden grove, and this charming mansion, was formerly the Viśvakarmā* of the principal Dänavas. *The name of the celestial architect.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने
पितामहाद्वरं लेभे सर्वमौशसनं धनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptvā mahāvane
pitāmahādvaraṁ lebhe sarvamauśasanaṁ dhanam

translations.english: Having for a thousand years thousand years practised austerities in this vast forest, he obtained a boon from the Great-father,-in virtue of which he had attained consummate mastery in his art, as well as absolute control over the materials required therein.

verses.sanskrit:
विधाय सर्वं बलवान्सर्वकामेश्वरस्तदा
उवास सुखितः कालं कंचिदस्मिन्महावने
verses.transliteration:
vidhāya sarvaṁ balavānsarvakāmeśvarastadā
uvāsa sukhitaḥ kālaṁ kaṁcidasminmahāvane

translations.english: Having accomplished everything, that powerful one, commanding every enjoyment, for a time happily dwelt in this mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तमप्सरसि हेमायां सक्तं दानवपुंगवम्
विक्रम्यैवाशनिं गृह्य जघानेशः पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
tamapsarasi hemāyāṁ saktaṁ dānavapuṁgavam
vikramyaivāśaniṁ gṛhya jaghāneśaḥ puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: Then he, happening to conceive a passion for an Apsara, Hema (by name), Purandara, vigorously wielding his thunder-bolt, struck him dead.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं च ब्रह्मणा दत्तं हेमायै वनमुत्तमम्
शाश्वतः कामभोगश्च गृहं चेदं हिरण्मयम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ ca brahmaṇā dattaṁ hemāyai vanamuttamam
śāśvataḥ kāmabhogaśca gṛhaṁ cedaṁ hiraṇmayam

translations.english: Then Brahmä conferred on Hemā this fine forest and this golden mansion, with the perpetual privilege of enjoying every pleasure herein.

verses.sanskrit:
दुहिता मेरुसावर्णेरहं तस्याः स्वयं प्रभा
इदं रक्षामि भवनं हेमाया वानरोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
duhitā merusāvarṇerahaṁ tasyāḥ svayaṁ prabhā
idaṁ rakṣāmi bhavanaṁ hemāyā vānarottama

translations.english: I, Svayamprabhā by name,-the daughter of Merusāvarņi, guard this house of Hemā, O foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
मम प्रियसखी हेमा नृत्तगीतविशारदा
तया दत्तवरा चास्मि रक्षामि भवनोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
mama priyasakhī hemā nṛttagītaviśāradā
tayā dattavarā cāsmi rakṣāmi bhavanottamam

translations.english: Hemā, skilled in dance and song, is my dear friend. having received her blessing, I guard this vast forest.

verses.sanskrit:
किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोः कान्ताराणि प्रपद्यथ
कथं चेदं वनं दुर्गं युष्माभिरुपलक्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ kāryaṁ kasya vā hetoḥ kāntārāṇi prapadyatha
kathaṁ cedaṁ vanaṁ durgaṁ yuṣmābhirupalakṣitam

translations.english: What is your errand? And why is it that you have arrived at these lone woods? And how have you managed to see this inaccessible forest?

verses.sanskrit:
इमान्यभ्यवहार्याणि मूलानि च फलानि च
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च पानीयं सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हथ
verses.transliteration:
imānyabhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
bhuktvā pītvā ca pānīyaṁ sarvaṁ me vaktumarhatha

translations.english: Having partaken of these fruits and roots intended for use, and drunk, do you detail all this to me.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तानब्रवीत्सर्वान्विश्रान्तान्हरियूथपान्
इदं वचनमेकाग्रा तापसी धर्मचारिणी
verses.transliteration:
atha tānabravītsarvānviśrāntānhariyūthapān
idaṁ vacanamekāgrā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī

translations.english: Then to all the monkey-chiefs, after they had rested, the female ascetic, engaged in righteous practices, eagerly said these words,

verses.sanskrit:
वानरा यदि वः खेदः प्रनष्टः फलभक्षणात्
यदि चैतन्मया श्राव्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
vānarā yadi vaḥ khedaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ phalabhakṣaṇāt
yadi caitanmayā śrāvyaṁ śrotumicchāmi kathyatām

translations.english: You monkeys, if your pain has gone off in consequence of the fare of fruits which you have partaken, and also if it be fit to be heard by me, I would listen to your narration.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
आर्जवेन यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstadvacanaṁ śrutvā hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
ārjavena yathātattvamākhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: Hearing her words, Hanumān, the son of the wind-god, in all candour began to relate everything faithfully.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया
तस्य भार्या जनस्थानाद्रावणेन हृता बलात्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
tasya bhāryā janasthānādrāvaṇena hṛtā balāt

translations.english: The Sovereign of all this world, resembling Mahendra or Varuna, Rāma, the graceful son of Dasaratha, entered the woods of Dandaka, in company with his brother, Laksmana, as well as his spouse, Vaidehi. His wife has been forcibly carried of by Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
अगस्त्यचरितामाशां दक्षिणां यमरक्षिताम्
सहैभिर्वानरैर्मुख्यैरङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
agastyacaritāmāśāṁ dakṣiṇāṁ yamarakṣitām
sahaibhirvānarairmukhyairaṅgadapramukhairvayam

translations.english: His friend is that heroic king, the monkey named Sugrīva. By that monarch of the foremnost monkeys have we been despatched (hither). And we have, joining company with these prime monkeys headed by Angada, come to the South, protected by Yama, and inhabited by Agastya.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं सहिताः सर्वे राक्षसं कामरूपिणम्
सीतया सह वैदेह्या मार्गध्वमिति चोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaṁ sahitāḥ sarve rākṣasaṁ kāmarūpiṇam
sītayā saha vaidehyā mārgadhvamiti coditāḥ

translations.english: And we have been commissioned, 'Do you all search for the Rākşasa Rāvana, wearing forms at will, along with Videha's daughter, Sītā.'

verses.sanskrit:
विचित्य तु वयं सर्वे समग्रां दक्षिणां दिशम्
बुभुक्षिताः परिश्रान्ता वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
vicitya tu vayaṁ sarve samagrāṁ dakṣiṇāṁ diśam
bubhukṣitāḥ pariśrāntā vṛkṣamūlamupāśritāḥ

translations.english: Having searched through the forest as well as the ocean on the South, we becoming hungry, sat down at the foot of a tree.

verses.sanskrit:
विवर्णवदनाः सर्वे सर्वे ध्यानपरायणाः
नाधिगच्छामहे पारं मग्नाश्चिन्तामहार्णवे
verses.transliteration:
vivarṇavadanāḥ sarve sarve dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ
nādhigacchāmahe pāraṁ magnāścintāmahārṇave

translations.english: And with pallid countenance, we all, absorbed in thought, sank in a wide sea of anxiety, which we could not cross.

verses.sanskrit:
चारयन्तस्ततश्चक्षुर्दृष्टवन्तो महद्बिलम्
लतापादपसंछन्नं तिमिरेण समावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
cārayantastataścakṣurdṛṣṭavanto mahadbilam
latāpādapasaṁchannaṁ timireṇa samāvṛtam

translations.english: And casting our eyes around, we spyed a huge cave covered with trees and plants and enveloped in gloom.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माद्धंसा जलक्लिन्नाः पक्षैः सलिलरेणुभिः
कुरराः सारसाश्चैव निष्पतन्ति पतत्रिणः
साध्वत्र प्रविशामेति मया तूक्ताः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
asmāddhaṁsā jalaklinnāḥ pakṣaiḥ salilareṇubhiḥ
kurarāḥ sārasāścaiva niṣpatanti patatriṇaḥ
sādhvatra praviśāmeti mayā tūktāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: And (it came to pass that) from this (cave) came out swans, drenched with water, with drops of water on their wings,-and plumed kuravas and cranes.

verses.sanskrit:
आतिथ्यधर्मदत्तानि मूलानि च फलानि च
अस्माभिरुपभुक्तानि बुभुक्षापरिपीडितैः
verses.transliteration:
ātithyadharmadattāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca
asmābhirupabhuktāni bubhukṣāparipīḍitaiḥ

translations.english: Having come to you, hungry, and exhausted, we, who had been sore tried by hunger, have been entertained with fruits and roots, agreeably to the code regulating hospitality.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्त्वया रक्षिताः सर्वे म्रियमाणा बुभुक्षया
ब्रूहि प्रत्युपकारार्थं किं ते कुर्वन्तु वानराः
verses.transliteration:
yattvayā rakṣitāḥ sarve mriyamāṇā bubhukṣayā
brūhi pratyupakārārthaṁ kiṁ te kurvantu vānarāḥ

translations.english: And as you had saved the monkeys, who were weary and suffering from hunger, tell (me),-what benefit shall the monkeys do you in return?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सर्वज्ञा वानरैस्तैः स्वयंप्रभा
प्रत्युवाच ततः सर्वानिदं वानरयूथपम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sarvajñā vānaraistaiḥ svayaṁprabhā
pratyuvāca tataḥ sarvānidaṁ vānarayūthapam

translations.english: Thus addressed by the apes, the all-knowing Svayamprabhā replied to the monkey-chiefs, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषां परितुष्टास्मि वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
चरन्त्या मम धर्मेण न कार्यमिह केनचित्
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣāṁ parituṣṭāsmi vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
carantyā mama dharmeṇa na kāryamiha kenacit

translations.english: Well pleased am I with the fast-footing monkeys. But by one engaged in your duties, there is no work that is desiderated.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः शुभं वाक्यं तापस्या धर्मसंहितम्
उवाच हनुमान्वाक्यं तामनिन्दितचेष्टिताम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ śubhaṁ vākyaṁ tāpasyā dharmasaṁhitam
uvāca hanumānvākyaṁ tāmaninditaceṣṭitām

translations.english: Thus accosted in excellent words fraught with asceticism and righteousness Hanumān spoke to that one of faultless eyes, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नाः स्मः सर्वे वै धर्मचारिणि
यः कृतः समयोऽस्माकं सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
स तु कालो व्यतिक्रान्तो बिले च परिवर्तताम्
verses.transliteration:
śaraṇaṁ tvāṁ prapannāḥ smaḥ sarve vai dharmacāriṇi
yaḥ kṛtaḥ samayo'smākaṁ sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
sa tu kālo vyatikrānto bile ca parivartatām

translations.english: We all take refuge in you, practising piety. the term that had been fixed by the high-souled Sugrīva in respect of us, shall all be spent in this cave. Therefore it behoveth you to deliver us from this place.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्सुग्रीववचनादतिक्रान्तान्गतायुषः
त्रातुमर्हसि नः सर्वान्सुग्रीवभयशङ्कितान्
verses.transliteration:
tasmātsugrīvavacanādatikrāntāngatāyuṣaḥ
trātumarhasi naḥ sarvānsugrīvabhayaśaṅkitān

translations.english: It behove you to save us, exercised with fear for Sugriva,-who, happening to override Sugriva's command, shall lose our lives. And, further, O you that practisest righteousness, great is the task that is to be performed by us.

verses.sanskrit:
महच्च कार्यमस्माभिः कर्तव्यं धर्मचारिणि
तच्चापि न कृतं कार्यमस्माभिरिह वासिभिः
verses.transliteration:
mahacca kāryamasmābhiḥ kartavyaṁ dharmacāriṇi
taccāpi na kṛtaṁ kāryamasmābhiriha vāsibhiḥ

translations.english: But if we stay here, that work of ours shall remain unaccomplished.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता तापसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
जीवता दुष्करं मन्ये प्रविष्टेन निवर्तितुम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā hanumatā tāpasī vākyamabravīt
jīvatā duṣkaraṁ manye praviṣṭena nivartitum

translations.english: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the ascetic said, Once entering, hard it is for any one to return (hence) alive. But by the potency of my asceticism acquired through self-discipline, I shall deliver all the monkeys from this den.

verses.sanskrit:
निमीलयत चक्षूंषि सर्वे वानरपुंगवाः
न हि निष्क्रमितुं शक्यमनिमीलितलोचनैः
verses.transliteration:
nimīlayata cakṣūṁṣi sarve vānarapuṁgavāḥ
na hi niṣkramituṁ śakyamanimīlitalocanaiḥ

translations.english: You foremost of monkeys, do you close your eyes. No one is able to issue out of this place without closing one's eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संमीलिताः सर्वे सुकुमाराङ्गुलैः करैः
सहसा पिदधुर्दृष्टिं हृष्टा गमनकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁmīlitāḥ sarve sukumārāṅgulaiḥ karaiḥ
sahasā pidadhurdṛṣṭiṁ hṛṣṭā gamanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: Then they, eagerly desirous of going out, closed their sight* with their hands furnished with tender fingers. *The text has nimilitah—and thus they closed their eyes. This redundant epithet has been left out in the translation, as it would render the version extremely awkward.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरास्तु महात्मानो हस्तरुद्धमुखास्तदा
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण बिलादुत्तारितास्तया
verses.transliteration:
vānarāstu mahātmāno hastaruddhamukhāstadā
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa bilāduttāritāstayā

translations.english: The magnanimous monkeys, with their faces covered with their palms, were in the twinkling of an eye, liberated from the den by her.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तान्वानरान्सर्वांस्तापसी धर्मचारिणी
निःसृतान्विषमात्तस्मात्समाश्वास्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastānvānarānsarvāṁstāpasī dharmacāriṇī
niḥsṛtānviṣamāttasmātsamāśvāsyedamabravīt

translations.english: And then the pious anchoret spoke to them there. And when they had come out of the fearful den, cheering them up, she said,

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु गमिष्यामि भवनं वानरर्षभाः
इत्युक्त्वा तद्बिलं श्रीमत्प्रविवेश स्वयंप्रभा
verses.transliteration:
svasti vo'stu gamiṣyāmi bhavanaṁ vānararṣabhāḥ
ityuktvā tadbilaṁ śrīmatpraviveśa svayaṁprabhā

translations.english: This is the fair Vindhya mountain filled with various trees and herbs. This is the Praśravaņa hill; and this is the great deep. Fair Fortune! I go to my abode, you foremost of monkeys. Having spokea thus, Svayamprabhā entered that captivating cave.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते ददृशुर्घोरं सागरं वरुणालयम्
अपारमभिगर्जन्तं घोरैरूर्मिभिराकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
tataste dadṛśurghoraṁ sāgaraṁ varuṇālayam
apāramabhigarjantaṁ ghorairūrmibhirākulam

translations.english: Then they saw the ocean—abode of Varuņashoreless, resounding, rife with dreadful billows.

verses.sanskrit:
मयस्य माया विहितं गिरिदुर्गं विचिन्वताम्
तेषां मासो व्यतिक्रान्तो यो राज्ञा समयः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
mayasya māyā vihitaṁ giridurgaṁ vicinvatām
teṣāṁ māso vyatikrānto yo rājñā samayaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Exploring the mountain fateness of Maya*, they spent the month that had been set by the king. *Named Rhiksavila.

verses.sanskrit:
विन्ध्यस्य तु गिरेः पादे संप्रपुष्पितपादपे
उपविश्य महाभागाश्चिन्तामापेदिरे तदा
verses.transliteration:
vindhyasya tu gireḥ pāde saṁprapuṣpitapādape
upaviśya mahābhāgāścintāmāpedire tadā

translations.english: Then sitting down at the foot of the Vindhya mountain, containing blossoming trees, at that time* those high-souled ones indulged-in reflections. *i.e. at the beginning of winter.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुष्पातिभाराग्राँल्लताशतसमावृतान्
द्रुमान्वासन्तिकान्दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्भयशङ्किताः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ puṣpātibhārāgrā̐llatāśatasamāvṛtān
drumānvāsantikāndṛṣṭvā babhūvurbhayaśaṅkitāḥ

translations.english: Beholding vernal trees bending beneath the load of flowers, and environed by hundreds of plants, they were inspired with apprehension.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वसन्तमनुप्राप्तं प्रतिवेद्य परस्परम्
नष्टसंदेशकालार्था निपेतुर्धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
te vasantamanuprāptaṁ prativedya parasparam
naṣṭasaṁdeśakālārthā nipeturdharaṇītale

translations.english: And each knowing that spring had appeared, they, the term appointed for their task having run out, dropped down on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु सिंहर्षभ स्कन्धः पीनायतभुजः कपिः
युवराजो महाप्राज्ञ अङ्गदो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu siṁharṣabha skandhaḥ pīnāyatabhujaḥ kapiḥ
yuvarājo mahāprājña aṅgado vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Thereat, with bland words properly honouring the aged apes and the rest dwelling in the woods, that monkey having the shoulders of a lion or a bull, and plump and broad arms-the youthful prince Angada, endowed with high wisdom, spoke,

verses.sanskrit:
शासनात्कपिराजस्य वयं सर्वे विनिर्गताः
मासः पूर्णो बिलस्थानां हरयः किं न बुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
śāsanātkapirājasya vayaṁ sarve vinirgatāḥ
māsaḥ pūrṇo bilasthānāṁ harayaḥ kiṁ na budhyate

translations.english: We have come out at the mandate of the monarch of monkeys. While we sojourned in the cave, a full month had passed away, you monkeys. Why do you not understand this? We set out, engaging that our term of search should reach no further than the end of Kärtika;* but that has expired. Now, what next is to be done? *October.

verses.sanskrit:
तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः स्वामिभावे व्यवस्थितः
न क्षमिष्यति नः सर्वानपराधकृतो गतान्
verses.transliteration:
tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ svāmibhāve vyavasthitaḥ
na kṣamiṣyati naḥ sarvānaparādhakṛto gatān

translations.english: Naturally stern, Sugrīva, established as our master, shall not forgive us, when we repair there, after having transgressed thus.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रवृत्तौ च सीतायाः पापमेव करिष्यति
तस्मात्क्षममिहाद्यैव प्रायोपविशनं हि नः
verses.transliteration:
apravṛttau ca sītāyāḥ pāpameva kariṣyati
tasmātkṣamamihādyaiva prāyopaviśanaṁ hi naḥ

translations.english: Sītā not having been found out, Sugrīva, for certain, shall commit this sin.* Therefore it is fit that, forsaking our sons, and wives, and wealth, and homes, we this very day sit down to starve ourselves to death. *i.e. slay us.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च धनानि च गृहाणि च
यावन्न घातयेद्राजा सर्वान्प्रतिगतानितः
वधेनाप्रतिरूपेण श्रेयान्मृत्युरिहैव नः
verses.transliteration:
tyaktvā putrāṁśca dārāṁśca dhanāni ca gṛhāṇi ca
yāvanna ghātayedrājā sarvānpratigatānitaḥ
vadhenāpratirūpeṇa śreyānmṛtyurihaiva naḥ

translations.english: Death at this place is preferable to the unequal punishment (we must meet with at the hands of Sugriva).

verses.sanskrit:
न चाहं यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवेणाभिषेचितः
नरेन्द्रेणाभिषिक्तोऽस्मि रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
na cāhaṁ yauvarājyena sugrīveṇābhiṣecitaḥ
narendreṇābhiṣikto'smi rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā

translations.english: And, further, I have not been installed heirapparent by Sugrīva: I have been sprinkled by that foremost of kings, Rāma of untiring energy.

verses.sanskrit:
स पूर्वं बद्धवैरो मां राजा दृष्ट्वा व्यतिक्रमम्
घातयिष्यति दण्डेन तीक्ष्णेन कृतनिश्चयः
verses.transliteration:
sa pūrvaṁ baddhavairo māṁ rājā dṛṣṭvā vyatikramam
ghātayiṣyati daṇḍena tīkṣṇena kṛtaniścayaḥ

translations.english: Entertaining enmity against me of old, the king, seeing this lapse, must be firmly determined to take my life by means of a severe sentence.

verses.sanskrit:
किं मे सुहृद्भिर्व्यसनं पश्यद्भिर्जीवितान्तरे
इहैव प्रायमासिष्ये पुण्ये सागररोधसि
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ me suhṛdbhirvyasanaṁ paśyadbhirjīvitāntare
ihaiva prāyamāsiṣye puṇye sāgararodhasi

translations.english: What is the use of suffering my friends to look on my disaster at the last moment of my existence? Therefore even on this sacred shore of the sea shall I sit down to starve myself.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा कुमारेण युवराजेन भाषितम्
सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः करुणं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā kumāreṇa yuvarājena bhāṣitam
sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ karuṇaṁ vākyamabruvan

translations.english: Hearing the tender prince speak thus, all those principal monkeys pathetically observed,

verses.sanskrit:
तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः प्रियासक्तश्च राघवः
अदृष्टायां च वैदेह्यां दृष्ट्वास्मांश्च समागतान्
verses.transliteration:
tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ priyāsaktaśca rāghavaḥ
adṛṣṭāyāṁ ca vaidehyāṁ dṛṣṭvāsmāṁśca samāgatān

translations.english: Sugrīva is harsh by nature, and Rāghava loveth his wife dearly. The time appointed having passed by, seeing us (come) without attaining success in the task, and seeing us arrive without obtaining a sight of Vaidehi, (Sugrīva) shall certainly slay us from the desire of doing what is agreeable to Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवंगमानां तु भयार्दितानां; श्रुत्वा वचस्तार इदं बभाषे
अलं विषादेन बिलं प्रविश्य; वसाम सर्वे यदि रोचते वः
verses.transliteration:
plavaṁgamānāṁ tu bhayārditānāṁ; śrutvā vacastāra idaṁ babhāṣe
alaṁ viṣādena bilaṁ praviśya; vasāma sarve yadi rocate vaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the speeches of the monkeys afflicted with fear, Tārā said,-No use of indulging in grief. If you relish it, let us all entering the cave, dwell there.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं हि माया विहितं सुदुर्गमं; प्रभूतवृक्षोदकभोज्यपेयम्
इहास्ति नो नैव भयं पुरंदरा;न्न राघवाद्वानरराजतोऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ hi māyā vihitaṁ sudurgamaṁ; prabhūtavṛkṣodakabhojyapeyam
ihāsti no naiva bhayaṁ puraṁdarā;nna rāghavādvānararājato'pi vā

translations.english: This place abounding in flowers and waters, meats and drinks,—which has been brought forth by the power of ilusion, is incapable of being approached. Here we have no fear from Purandara, or Rāghava, or the king of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वाङ्गदस्यापि वचोऽनुकूल;मूचुश्च सर्वे हरयः प्रतीताः
यथा न हन्येम तथाविधान;मसक्तमद्यैव विधीयतां नः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvāṅgadasyāpi vaco'nukūla;mūcuśca sarve harayaḥ pratītāḥ
yathā na hanyema tathāvidhāna;masaktamadyaiva vidhīyatāṁ naḥ

translations.english: Hearing the welcome words of Angada, the monkeys,-being convinced, said,-Do you this very day so order that we may not be slain.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा ब्रुवति तारे तु ताराधिपतिवर्चसि
अथ मेने हृतं राज्यं हनुमानङ्गदेन तत्
verses.transliteration:
tathā bruvati tāre tu tārādhipativarcasi
atha mene hṛtaṁ rājyaṁ hanumānaṅgadena tat

translations.english: When Tārā, bright as the moon, had spoken thus, Hanumān felt as if Angada had already deprived (Sugrīva) of his kingdom.* The sense is very obscure. One meaning is: Hanumān thought that Argada acquiescing in what Tārā had said, must remain there,-and ultimately endeavour to wrest the kingdom from Sugriva. Another meaning is: Hanumān conceived that remaining there in peace, Angada would consider his position as enviable as if he had extorted the kingdom from Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
बृहस्पतिसमं बुद्ध्या विक्रमे सदृशं पितुः
शुश्रूषमाणं तारस्य शुक्रस्येव पुरंदरम्
verses.transliteration:
bṛhaspatisamaṁ buddhyā vikrame sadṛśaṁ pituḥ
śuśrūṣamāṇaṁ tārasya śukrasyeva puraṁdaram

translations.english: Hanumān deemned Vāli's son as endowed with intelligence consisting of eight elements; with power of four kinds; and the four and ten virtues; as ever fraught with energy, strength and prowess; as growing in grace like the moon during the lighted fortnight; as resembling Brhaspati in intelligence; and in prowess, his own sire; and as ever listening to. Tārā's counsels, as Purandara listens to the counsels of Sukra.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तुरर्थे परिश्रान्तं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्
अभिसंधातुमारेभे हनुमानङ्गदं ततः
verses.transliteration:
bharturarthe pariśrāntaṁ sarvaśāstraviśāradam
abhisaṁdhātumārebhe hanumānaṅgadaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: And Hanumān versed in all branches of learning, finding Angada backward in the affair of his master, began inspire him with fear.* *Touching Tārā.

verses.sanskrit:
स चतुर्णामुपायानां तृतीयमुपवर्णयन्
भेदयामास तान्सर्वान्वानरान्वाक्यसंपदा
verses.transliteration:
sa caturṇāmupāyānāṁ tṛtīyamupavarṇayan
bhedayāmāsa tānsarvānvānarānvākyasaṁpadā

translations.english: He, wealthy in words, laying under contribution the second of the four means,* had created division among those monkeys. *Referred to above.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु सर्वेषु भिन्नेषु ततोऽभीषयदङ्गदम्
भीषणैर्बहुभिर्वाक्यैः कोपोपायसमन्वितैः
verses.transliteration:
teṣu sarveṣu bhinneṣu tato'bhīṣayadaṅgadam
bhīṣaṇairbahubhirvākyaiḥ kopopāyasamanvitaiḥ

translations.english: On their being divided, he (Hanuman) set about raising Angada's apprehension by various fear-fraught speech, referring to punishments.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं समर्थतरः पित्रा युद्धे तारेय वै धुरम्
दृढं धारयितुं शक्तः कपिराज्यं यथा पिता
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ samarthataraḥ pitrā yuddhe tāreya vai dhuram
dṛḍhaṁ dhārayituṁ śaktaḥ kapirājyaṁ yathā pitā

translations.english: O Tārā's son, you are for certain more capable of fight than even your sire; and you are also able to hold the monkey-kingdom as firmly as he.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यमस्थिरचित्ता हि कपयो हरिपुंगव
नाज्ञाप्यं विषहिष्यन्ति पुत्रदारान्विना त्वया
verses.transliteration:
nityamasthiracittā hi kapayo haripuṁgava
nājñāpyaṁ viṣahiṣyanti putradārānvinā tvayā

translations.english: But, O foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are always inconstant in character. Bereft of their wives and sons, they shall not bear your behest.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां नैते ह्यनुयुञ्जेयुः प्रत्यक्षं प्रवदामि ते
यथायं जाम्बवान्नीलः सुहोत्रश्च महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ naite hyanuyuñjeyuḥ pratyakṣaṁ pravadāmi te
yathāyaṁ jāmbavānnīlaḥ suhotraśca mahākapiḥ

translations.english: They shall never take to you. This I tell you in presence of all. And I will tell you what. You neither by the virtues of conciliation, charity and the rest, nor by chastisement, shall succeed in drawing to your side this Jāmbavān, or Nīla, or the mighty ape Suhotra, or myself.

verses.sanskrit:
विगृह्यासनमप्याहुर्दुर्बलेन बलीयसः
आत्मरक्षाकरस्तस्मान्न विगृह्णीत दुर्बलः
verses.transliteration:
vigṛhyāsanamapyāhurdurbalena balīyasaḥ
ātmarakṣākarastasmānna vigṛhṇīta durbalaḥ

translations.english: A strong one wronging another that is weak, can live; therefore a weak person anxious for self-preservation, should never wrong (a strong individual).

verses.sanskrit:
यां चेमां मन्यसे धात्रीमेतद्बिलमिति श्रुतम्
एतल्लक्ष्मणबाणानामीषत्कार्यं विदारणे
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ cemāṁ manyase dhātrīmetadbilamiti śrutam
etallakṣmaṇabāṇānāmīṣatkāryaṁ vidāraṇe

translations.english: You considerest that this cave may serve for your protectress,* having heard of it (said by Tārā); but to rive the same is but light work for the shafts of Laksmana. *The word meaning cave is feminine in Sanskrit.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वल्पं हि कृतमिन्द्रेण क्षिपता ह्यशनिं पुरा
लक्ष्मणो निशितैर्बाणैर्भिन्द्यात्पत्रपुटं यथा
लक्ष्मणस्य च नाराचा बहवः सन्ति तद्विधाः
verses.transliteration:
svalpaṁ hi kṛtamindreṇa kṣipatā hyaśaniṁ purā
lakṣmaṇo niśitairbāṇairbhindyātpatrapuṭaṁ yathā
lakṣmaṇasya ca nārācā bahavaḥ santi tadvidhāḥ

translations.english: Formerly this was cleft a little by Indra, with his thunderbolt hurled (against it);* but now Lakṣmaṇa would pierce it like a leaf-stalk, by means of his keen arrows. *The commentator interprets the passage differently: Formerly Indra did a little damage herein-i.e. merely slew Maya, the architect of the mansion. This is ingenuity. I give the plain sense.

verses.sanskrit:
अवस्थाने यदैव त्वमासिष्यसि परंतप
तदैव हरयः सर्वे त्यक्ष्यन्ति कृतनिश्चयाः
verses.transliteration:
avasthāne yadaiva tvamāsiṣyasi paraṁtapa
tadaiva harayaḥ sarve tyakṣyanti kṛtaniścayāḥ

translations.english: O subduer of enemies, soon as you shall set up here, the monkeys, making up their minds, shall forsake you.

verses.sanskrit:
स्मरन्तः पुत्रदाराणां नित्योद्विग्ना बुभुक्षिताः
खेदिता दुःखशय्याभिस्त्वां करिष्यन्ति पृष्ठतः
verses.transliteration:
smarantaḥ putradārāṇāṁ nityodvignā bubhukṣitāḥ
kheditā duḥkhaśayyābhistvāṁ kariṣyanti pṛṣṭhataḥ

translations.english: Remembering their wives and sons, ever anxious (on account of Sugrīva, pining for domestic happiness, ad aggrieved (at their pitiable plight), they shall turn their backs upon you.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं हीनः सुहृद्भिश्च हितकामैश्च बन्धुभिः
तृणादपि भृशोद्विग्नः स्पन्दमानाद्भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ hīnaḥ suhṛdbhiśca hitakāmaiśca bandhubhiḥ
tṛṇādapi bhṛśodvignaḥ spandamānādbhaviṣyasi

translations.english: Then forsaken by the kindred as well as friends seeking your welfare, you shall be struck with affright even at a quaking blade of grass. If you make head (against Sugriva), the sharpened shafts of Laksmana, terrible, of exceeding impetuosity and mighty vehemence, and incapable of being baffled, shall be eager to slay you.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माभिस्तु गतं सार्धं विनीतवदुपस्थितम्
आनुपूर्व्यात्तु सुग्रीवो राज्ये त्वां स्थापयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
asmābhistu gataṁ sārdhaṁ vinītavadupasthitam
ānupūrvyāttu sugrīvo rājye tvāṁ sthāpayiṣyati

translations.english: On the contrary, if you in humble guise present yourself (before him) along with us, he shall-establish you in the kingdom, in consideration of your being the next heir.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मकामः पितृव्यस्ते प्रीतिकामो दृढव्रतः
शुचिः सत्यप्रतिज्ञश्च ना त्वां जातु जिघांसति
verses.transliteration:
dharmakāmaḥ pitṛvyaste prītikāmo dṛḍhavrataḥ
śuciḥ satyapratijñaśca nā tvāṁ jātu jighāṁsati

translations.english: A righteous sovereign, steady in vow, clean, and truthful in promise, your uncle, who cherishes affection for you shall not by any mears chastise. Ju.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियकामश्च ते मातुस्तदर्थं चास्य जीवितम्
तस्यापत्यं च नास्त्यन्यत्तस्मादङ्गद गम्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
priyakāmaśca te mātustadarthaṁ cāsya jīvitam
tasyāpatyaṁ ca nāstyanyattasmādaṅgada gamyatām

translations.english: He loves your mother, and his life is for her; and she has no other son. Therefore, O Angada, go along with us.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं प्रश्रितं धर्मसंहितम्
स्वामिसत्कारसंयुक्तमङ्गदो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā hanumato vākyaṁ praśritaṁ dharmasaṁhitam
svāmisatkārasaṁyuktamaṅgado vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Hanuman's speech, uttered meekly, fraught with morality, and reflecting honour upon Sugriva, Angada said,

verses.sanskrit:
स्थैर्यं सर्वात्मना शौचमानृशंस्यमथार्जवम्
विक्रमैश्चैव धैर्यं च सुग्रीवे नोपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
sthairyaṁ sarvātmanā śaucamānṛśaṁsyamathārjavam
vikramaiścaiva dhairyaṁ ca sugrīve nopapadyate

translations.english: Firmness, and mental sanctity, mercy, candour, prowess, and patience, are not in Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य यो भार्यां जीवितो महिषीं प्रियाम्
धर्मेण मातरं यस्तु स्वीकरोति जुगुप्सितः
verses.transliteration:
bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya yo bhāryāṁ jīvito mahiṣīṁ priyām
dharmeṇa mātaraṁ yastu svīkaroti jugupsitaḥ

translations.english: He that, while her son is living, appropriateth the beloved queen of his elder brother, mother to him by morality, is hated (of all beings). How can he that could cover up the mouth of the cave, when he had been desired by his brother gone on martial mission, to guard the same,—(how can he) know morality?

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यात्पाणिगृहीतश्च कृतकर्मा महायशाः
विस्मृतो राघवो येन स कस्य सुकृतं स्मरेत्
verses.transliteration:
satyātpāṇigṛhītaśca kṛtakarmā mahāyaśāḥ
vismṛto rāghavo yena sa kasya sukṛtaṁ smaret

translations.english: Whose good office remembereth he who could forget the renowned Räghava himself of mighty deeds, after having, in the name of truth, taken his hand? How can he reap religious merit that directed us to search Sītā here, from fear of Laksmana, and not from fear of unrighteousness?

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्पापे कृतघ्ने तु स्मृतिहीने चलात्मनि
आर्यः को विश्वसेज्जातु तत्कुलीनो जिजीविषुः
verses.transliteration:
tasminpāpe kṛtaghne tu smṛtihīne calātmani
āryaḥ ko viśvasejjātu tatkulīno jijīviṣuḥ

translations.english: What noble person, in especial, sprung in his race, shall any longer repose confidence in that impious one of unstable soul who has run amuck of morality?

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ये पुत्रं प्रतिष्ठाप्य सगुणो निर्गुणोऽपि वा
कथं शत्रुकुलीनं मां सुग्रीवो जीवयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rājye putraṁ pratiṣṭhāpya saguṇo nirguṇo'pi vā
kathaṁ śatrukulīnaṁ māṁ sugrīvo jīvayiṣyati

translations.english: Meritorious or otherwise, how can Sugriva, having installed in the kingdom me, son (of his enemy) and the enemy sprung in his race, suffer me to live?

verses.sanskrit:
भिन्नमन्त्रोऽपराद्धश्च हीनशक्तिः कथं ह्यहम्
किष्किन्धां प्राप्य जीवेयमनाथ इव दुर्बलः
verses.transliteration:
bhinnamantro'parāddhaśca hīnaśaktiḥ kathaṁ hyaham
kiṣkindhāṁ prāpya jīveyamanātha iva durbalaḥ

translations.english: How can I, whose counsels have been revealed, who have transgressed, and who have been deprived of my power, repairing to Kiş kindhā like one forlorn and feeble, live?

verses.sanskrit:
उपांशुदण्डेन हि मां बन्धनेनोपपादयेत्
शठः क्रूरो नृशंसश्च सुग्रीवो राज्यकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
upāṁśudaṇḍena hi māṁ bandhanenopapādayet
śaṭhaḥ krūro nṛśaṁsaśca sugrīvo rājyakāraṇāt

translations.english: For the sake of his kingdom, Sugrīva, wily, cunning and cruel, shall put me in solitary confinement.

verses.sanskrit:
बन्धनाच्चावसादान्मे श्रेयः प्रायोपवेशनम्
अनुजानीत मां सर्वे गृहान्गच्छन्तु वानराः
verses.transliteration:
bandhanāccāvasādānme śreyaḥ prāyopaveśanam
anujānīta māṁ sarve gṛhāngacchantu vānarāḥ

translations.english: For me fasting to death is better than being confined-and suffering the consequent misery. Do you grant me your permission; and go to your homes, you monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं वः प्रतिजानामि न गमिष्याम्यहं पुरीम्
इहैव प्रायमासिष्ये श्रेयो मरणमेव मे
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ vaḥ pratijānāmi na gamiṣyāmyahaṁ purīm
ihaiva prāyamāsiṣye śreyo maraṇameva me

translations.english: I vow before you, to the palace I will never repair. At this very spot will I fast for death; as death is good for me.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवादनपूर्वं तु राजा कुशलमेव च
वाच्यस्ततो यवीयान्मे सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
abhivādanapūrvaṁ tu rājā kuśalameva ca
vācyastato yavīyānme sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ

translations.english: Bowing to the king as well as to the powerful Rāghava, you should communicate my wellbeing to Sugriva— lord of my health and peace to my mother Umā.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या प्रियपुत्रा सा सानुक्रोशा तपस्विनी
विनष्टं मामिह श्रुत्वा व्यक्तं हास्यति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā priyaputrā sā sānukrośā tapasvinī
vinaṣṭaṁ māmiha śrutvā vyaktaṁ hāsyati jīvitam

translations.english: It behoves you also to console my mother, Tārā. Naturally fond of her son, and overflowing with tenderness, that lorn one, hearing of my apes-and death at this place, shall certainly renounce her life. Having said this, Angada, saluting the elders, with a woebegone face entered the earth covered with grass.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य संविशतस्तत्र रुदन्तो वानरर्षभाः
नयनेभ्यः प्रमुमुचुरुष्णं वै वारिदुःखिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya saṁviśatastatra rudanto vānararṣabhāḥ
nayanebhyaḥ pramumucuruṣṇaṁ vai vāriduḥkhitāḥ

translations.english: When he had entered, those foremost monkeys, stricken with sorrow, weeping shed warm tears from their eyes. And censuring Sugrīva and praising Vāli, they, surrounding Angada, determined to starve themselves to death.

verses.sanskrit:
मतं तद्वालिपुत्रस्य विज्ञाय प्लवगर्षभाः
उपस्पृश्योदकं सर्वे प्राङ्मुखाः समुपाविशन्
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु उदक्तीरं समाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
mataṁ tadvāliputrasya vijñāya plavagarṣabhāḥ
upaspṛśyodakaṁ sarve prāṅmukhāḥ samupāviśan
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu udaktīraṁ samāśritāḥ

translations.english: Taking to heart the speech of Väli's son, those prime monkeys, sipping water, sat down facing the East. And sitting on the edge of the water on grass pointing to the south, the foremost monkeys, wishing for surcease, thought within themselves,-Even this is fit for us.

verses.sanskrit: स संविशद्भिर्बहुभिर्महीधरो; महाद्रिकूटप्रमितैः प्लवंगमैः
verses.transliteration: sa saṁviśadbhirbahubhirmahīdharo; mahādrikūṭapramitaiḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ

translations.english: When those monkeys resembling mountainsummits had entered in, they set up cries, which, like to the rumbling of clouds, making the sky resound, made that mountain with its rills reverberate.

verses.sanskrit:
उपविष्टास्तु ते सर्वे यस्मिन्प्रायं गिरिस्थले
हरयो गृध्रराजश्च तं देशमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
upaviṣṭāstu te sarve yasminprāyaṁ giristhale
harayo gṛdhrarājaśca taṁ deśamupacakrame

translations.english: When the monkeys had been seated in that mountain, with the intention of putting a period to their existence through fasting a king of vultures happened to come to that quarter. And that long-lived bird was named Sampāti, the beautiful brother of Jaţāyu, famous for his strength and prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्दरादभिनिष्क्रम्य स विन्ध्यस्य महागिरेः
उपविष्टान्हरीन्दृष्ट्वा हृष्टात्मा गिरमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kandarādabhiniṣkramya sa vindhyasya mahāgireḥ
upaviṣṭānharīndṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭātmā giramabravīt

translations.english: Issuing from a cavern of the mighty mountain Vindhya, he, seeing the monkeys seated, well pleased, said.

verses.sanskrit:
विधिः किल नरं लोके विधानेनानुवर्तते
यथायं विहितो भक्ष्यश्चिरान्मह्यमुपागतः
verses.transliteration:
vidhiḥ kila naraṁ loke vidhānenānuvartate
yathāyaṁ vihito bhakṣyaścirānmahyamupāgataḥ

translations.english: Verily man reapeth the fruit of his former acts; and therefore it is that this food ordained to that end, comes to me after a long time. I shall feed on these monkeys, one by one, slaying them one after another. Eyeing those apes, the bird expressed himself thus.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भक्षलुब्धस्य पक्षिणः
अङ्गदः परमायस्तो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā bhakṣalubdhasya pakṣiṇaḥ
aṅgadaḥ paramāyasto hanūmantamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing this speech of the bird coveting his food, Argada faintly spoke to Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य सीतापदेशेन साक्षाद्वैवस्वतो यमः
इमं देशमनुप्राप्तो वानराणां विपत्तये
verses.transliteration:
paśya sītāpadeśena sākṣādvaivasvato yamaḥ
imaṁ deśamanuprāpto vānarāṇāṁ vipattaye

translations.english: Behold! through Sita's simplicity* this onethe very son of the Sun, Yama-has come to this place, to exterminate the monkeys. *Another reading is Gridhra padesana— through the vultur's cunning. This the commentator consider as preferrable.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य न कृतं कार्यं राज्ञो न च वचः कृतम्
हरीणामियमज्ञाता विपत्तिः सहसागता
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya na kṛtaṁ kāryaṁ rājño na ca vacaḥ kṛtam
harīṇāmiyamajñātā vipattiḥ sahasāgatā

translations.english: Rāma's work has not been done; nor the royal mandate. And this disaster has arrived unthought of by the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेह्याः प्रियकामेन कृतं कर्म जटायुषा
गृध्रराजेन यत्तत्र श्रुतं वस्तदशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
vaidehyāḥ priyakāmena kṛtaṁ karma jaṭāyuṣā
gṛdhrarājena yattatra śrutaṁ vastadaśeṣataḥ

translations.english: You have in detail heard all that, inspired with the desire of doing what is good to Vaidehi, that king of vultures, Jatayu, did here.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि तिर्यग्योनिगतान्यपि
प्रियं कुर्वन्ति रामस्य त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्यथा वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni tiryagyonigatānyapi
priyaṁ kurvanti rāmasya tyaktvā prāṇānyathā vayam

translations.english: In this way, all creatures, even the brute species, compass the welfare of Rāma, renouncing their lives, as we do.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवार्थे परिश्रान्ता वयं संत्यक्तजीविताः
कान्ताराणि प्रपन्नाः स्म न च पश्याम मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavārthe pariśrāntā vayaṁ saṁtyaktajīvitāḥ
kāntārāṇi prapannāḥ sma na ca paśyāma maithilīm

translations.english: Therefore the righteous Jațãyu, of his own accord laying down his life, has done the pleasure of Rāma. We also, overcome with fatigue and (almost) dying, have come to this forest; but Mithila's daughter we find not.

verses.sanskrit:
स सुखी गृध्रराजस्तु रावणेन हतो रणे
मुक्तश्च सुग्रीवभयाद्गतश्च परमां गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa sukhī gṛdhrarājastu rāvaṇena hato raṇe
muktaśca sugrīvabhayādgataśca paramāṁ gatim

translations.english: Happy is that king of vultures, having been slain by Rāvaņa in battle. He has got quit of the fear of Sugrīva, and has also attained supreme state.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुषो विनाशेन राज्ञो दशरथस्य च
हरणेन च वैदेह्याः संशयं हरयो गताः
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyuṣo vināśena rājño daśarathasya ca
haraṇena ca vaidehyāḥ saṁśayaṁ harayo gatāḥ

translations.english: In consequence of the death of Jațāyu and that of king Dasaratha, as well as owing to the ravishment of Vaidehi, (the lives of) the monkeys have come into jeopardy.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वासामरण्ये सह सीतया
राघवस्य च बाणेन वालिनश्च तथा वधः
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇayorvāsāmaraṇye saha sītayā
rāghavasya ca bāṇena vālinaśca tathā vadhaḥ

translations.english: Rama's and Laksmana's abode in the forest with Sītā, Rāghava's slaying of Vāli with a shaft, the slaughter of innumerable Räksasas by the enraged Rama, and (finally) this mishap-all these owe their origin to the bestowal of the boon on Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तु श्रुत्वा तदा वाक्यमङ्गदस्य मुखोद्गतम्
अब्रवीद्वचनं गृध्रस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डो महास्वनः
verses.transliteration:
tattu śrutvā tadā vākyamaṅgadasya mukhodgatam
abravīdvacanaṁ gṛdhrastīkṣṇatuṇḍo mahāsvanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words that issued from Angada's mouth, the sharp-beaked and high-toned vulture, said,

verses.sanskrit:
कोऽयं गिरा घोषयति प्राणैः प्रियतरस्य मे
जटायुषो वधं भ्रातुः कम्पयन्निव मे मनः
verses.transliteration:
ko'yaṁ girā ghoṣayati prāṇaiḥ priyatarasya me
jaṭāyuṣo vadhaṁ bhrātuḥ kampayanniva me manaḥ

translations.english: Who is it that, making my mind tremble, speak of the death of my brother, Jațāyu, dearer to me than life.

verses.sanskrit:
कथमासीज्जनस्थाने युद्धं राक्षसगृध्रयोः
नामधेयमिदं भ्रातुश्चिरस्याद्य मया श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
kathamāsījjanasthāne yuddhaṁ rākṣasagṛdhrayoḥ
nāmadheyamidaṁ bhrātuścirasyādya mayā śrutam

translations.english: How happened in Janasthāna the fight between the Rākṣasa and the vulture? It is after a long time that to-day I hear the name of my brother.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुर्जटायुषस्तस्य जनस्थाननिवासिनः
तस्यैव च मम भ्रातुः सखा दशरथः कथम्
यस्य रामः प्रियः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो गुरुजनप्रियः
verses.transliteration:
bhrāturjaṭāyuṣastasya janasthānanivāsinaḥ
tasyaiva ca mama bhrātuḥ sakhā daśarathaḥ katham
yasya rāmaḥ priyaḥ putro jyeṣṭho gurujanapriyaḥ

translations.english: I wish to alight from this mountain-fastness. I have been well pleased by listening after a long time to the celebration of the virtues of my younger brother, cognizant of qualities and worthy of being extolled by reason of his prowess. You foremost of monkeys, I wish to hear of the destruction of Jaţāyu, who dwelt in Janasthāna. And how could Dasaratha, whose beloved eldest son is Rāma, dear to his superiors, be the friend of my brother?

verses.sanskrit:
सूर्यांशुदग्धपक्षत्वान्न शक्नोमि विसर्पितुम्
इच्छेयं पर्वतादस्मादवतर्तुमरिंदमाः
verses.transliteration:
sūryāṁśudagdhapakṣatvānna śaknomi visarpitum
iccheyaṁ parvatādasmādavatartumariṁdamāḥ

translations.english: I can not move in consequence of my wings having been burnt by the solar rays. But I wish that you may take me down from this mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकाद्भ्रष्टस्वरमपि श्रुत्वा ते हरियूथपाः
श्रद्दधुर्नैव तद्वाक्यं कर्मणा तस्य शङ्किताः
verses.transliteration:
śokādbhraṣṭasvaramapi śrutvā te hariyūthapāḥ
śraddadhurnaiva tadvākyaṁ karmaṇā tasya śaṅkitāḥ

translations.english: Hearing his accents faltering through grief, the leaders of monkey-herds, alarmed by his action*, did not repose confidence in his speech. Karmaņā (instru.) by his action. The commentator explains: alarmed by his speech about eating up the monkeys. The passage is

verses.sanskrit:
ते प्रायमुपविष्टास्तु दृष्ट्वा गृध्रं प्लवंगमाः
चक्रुर्बुद्धिं तदा रौद्रां सर्वान्नो भक्षयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
te prāyamupaviṣṭāstu dṛṣṭvā gṛdhraṁ plavaṁgamāḥ
cakrurbuddhiṁ tadā raudrāṁ sarvānno bhakṣayiṣyati

translations.english: Seated for the purpose of fasting to death, the monkeys, seeing the vulture, with terror thought within themselves, he shall eat us all up.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा प्रायमासीनान्यदि नो भक्षयिष्यति
कृतकृत्या भविष्यामः क्षिप्रं सिद्धिमितो गताः
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā prāyamāsīnānyadi no bhakṣayiṣyati
kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṁ siddhimito gatāḥ

translations.english: If he eat us up, who have sat down to fast to death, we shall secure success, and speedily attain our end.

verses.sanskrit:
एतां बुद्धिं ततश्चक्रुः सर्वे ते वानरर्षभाः
अवतार्य गिरेः शृङ्गाद्गृध्रमाहाङ्गदस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ buddhiṁ tataścakruḥ sarve te vānararṣabhāḥ
avatārya gireḥ śṛṅgādgṛdhramāhāṅgadastadā

translations.english: Then those monkey-chiefs resolved thus. And descending from the summit of the mountain, Angada spoke to the vulture,

verses.sanskrit:
बभूवुर्क्षरजो नाम वानरेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्
ममार्यः पार्थिवः पक्षिन्धार्मिकौ तस्य चात्मजौ
verses.transliteration:
babhūvurkṣarajo nāma vānarendraḥ pratāpavān
mamāryaḥ pārthivaḥ pakṣindhārmikau tasya cātmajau

translations.english: There was a lord of monkeys named Riksaraja, endowed with prowess. That king, O bird, was my grandsire. He had two virtuous sons, exceedingly powerful both-Vāli and Sugriva. My father, Vali, was famed in the world for his deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा कृत्स्नस्य जगत इक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान्प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
rājā kṛtsnasya jagata ikṣvākūṇāṁ mahārathaḥ
rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmānpraviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: It came to pass that mighty monarch of all this earth, descendant of the Ikṣwākus, the great and graceful car warrior, Rāma, son to Dasaratha, intent upon the injunction of his sire, resorting to the path of righteousness, entered the woods of Dandaka in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa and his wife Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं विरथं कृत्वा स्थापयित्वा च मैथिलीम्
परिश्रान्तश्च वृद्धश्च रावणेन हतो रणे
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaṁ virathaṁ kṛtvā sthāpayitvā ca maithilīm
pariśrāntaśca vṛddhaśca rāvaṇena hato raṇe

translations.english: His spouse was forcibly carried away from Janasthāna. And the friend of Rāma's father, the king of vultures, named Jatayu, saw Videha's daughter, Sītā, as she was being carried away in the sky. And after having thrown down Rāvana from his car, and placed Maithili on the ground, (that vulture) old and overcome with fatigue was (at length) slain by Ravana in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं गृध्रो हतस्तेन रावणेन बहीयसा
संस्कृतश्चापि रामेण गतश्च गतिमुत्तमाम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ gṛdhro hatastena rāvaṇena bahīyasā
saṁskṛtaścāpi rāmeṇa gataśca gatimuttamām

translations.english: Thus slain by the powerful Rāvana, the vulture, having had his funereal obsequies performed by Rama. (himself), has attained excellent state.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मम पितृव्येण सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
चकार राघवः सख्यं सोऽवधीत्पितरं मम
verses.transliteration:
tato mama pitṛvyeṇa sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
cakāra rāghavaḥ sakhyaṁ so'vadhītpitaraṁ mama

translations.english: Then Rāghava made friends with my uncle, the high-souled Sugrīva; and he also slew my sire.

verses.sanskrit:
माम पित्रा विरुद्धो हि सुग्रीवः सचिवैः सह
निहत्य वालिनं रामस्ततस्तमभिषेचयत्
verses.transliteration:
māma pitrā viruddho hi sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha
nihatya vālinaṁ rāmastatastamabhiṣecayat

translations.english: My father had debarred Sugrīva from the kingdom along with his counsellors; but Rāma, having slain Vāli, installed him (Sugrīva).

verses.sanskrit:
स राज्ये स्थापितस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः
राजा वानरमुख्यानां येन प्रस्थापिता वयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājye sthāpitastena sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
rājā vānaramukhyānāṁ yena prasthāpitā vayam

translations.english: And established in the monarchy by him (Rāma), Sugriva is (now) the master of the monkeys and king of all the foremost monkeys. By him have we been sent.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं रामप्रयुक्तास्तु मार्गमाणास्ततस्ततः
वैदेहीं नाधिगच्छामो रात्रौ सूर्यप्रभामिव
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ rāmaprayuktāstu mārgamāṇāstatastataḥ
vaidehīṁ nādhigacchāmo rātrau sūryaprabhāmiva

translations.english: Despatched hither by Rāma, we have searched for Sītā all round, but Vaidehī we have not found, as one does not find the solar splendour at night.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं दण्दकारण्यं विचित्य सुसमाहिताः
अज्ञानात्तु प्रविष्टाः स्म धरण्या विवृतं बिलम्
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ daṇdakāraṇyaṁ vicitya susamāhitāḥ
ajñānāttu praviṣṭāḥ sma dharaṇyā vivṛtaṁ bilam

translations.english: It came to pass that, having heedfully explored the Dandaka forest, we through ignorance entered a cave lying open before.

verses.sanskrit:
मयस्य माया विहितं तद्बिलं च विचिन्वताम्
व्यतीतस्तत्र नो मासो यो राज्ञा सामयः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
mayasya māyā vihitaṁ tadbilaṁ ca vicinvatām
vyatītastatra no māso yo rājñā sāmayaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: That cave, you must know, was constructed by the illusive energy of Maya. And there we spent a month the term which had been fixed by the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं कपिराजस्य सर्वे वचनकारिणः
कृतां संस्थामतिक्रान्ता भयात्प्रायमुपास्महे
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ kapirājasya sarve vacanakāriṇaḥ
kṛtāṁ saṁsthāmatikrāntā bhayātprāyamupāsmahe

translations.english: Doing the behests of the king of monkeys, we, having overstayed the terms which had been appointed, have from fear sat here down for the purpose of fasting to death.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धे तस्मिंस्तु काकुत्स्थे सुग्रीवे च सलक्ष्मणे
गतानामपि सर्वेषां तत्र नो नास्ति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
kruddhe tasmiṁstu kākutsthe sugrīve ca salakṣmaṇe
gatānāmapi sarveṣāṁ tatra no nāsti jīvitam

translations.english: On that Kākutstha being wrought up with wrath, as well as Sugrīva together with Lakş maņa, we, repairing thither, shall lose our lives.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः करुणं वाक्यं वानरैस्त्यक्तजीवितैः
सबाष्पो वानरान्गृध्रः प्रत्युवाच महास्वनः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ karuṇaṁ vākyaṁ vānaraistyaktajīvitaiḥ
sabāṣpo vānarāngṛdhraḥ pratyuvāca mahāsvanaḥ

translations.english: When the monkeys, whose lives had well nigh departed out of them, had spoken these piteous words, the vulture, in solemn accents, with tears in his eyes, said to the monkeys,

verses.sanskrit:
यवीयान्मम स भ्राता जटायुर्नाम वानराः
यमाख्यात हतं युद्धे रावणेन बलीयसा
verses.transliteration:
yavīyānmama sa bhrātā jaṭāyurnāma vānarāḥ
yamākhyāta hataṁ yuddhe rāvaṇena balīyasā

translations.english: You monkeys, you have said that my younger brother, named Jaţāyu, has been slain in battle by the powerful Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
वृद्धभावादपक्षत्वाच्छृण्वंस्तदपि मर्षये
न हि मे शक्तिरद्यास्ति भ्रातुर्वैरविमोक्षणे
verses.transliteration:
vṛddhabhāvādapakṣatvācchṛṇvaṁstadapi marṣaye
na hi me śaktiradyāsti bhrāturvairavimokṣaṇe

translations.english: On account of my age and want of wings, I, although hearing this, bear it. Nor have I strength to-day to clear scores touching my brother's enmity.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते स चाहं च जयैषिणौ
आदित्यमुपयातौ स्वो ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्
verses.transliteration:
purā vṛtravadhe vṛtte sa cāhaṁ ca jayaiṣiṇau
ādityamupayātau svo jvalantaṁ raśmimālinam

translations.english: Formerly, while engaged in the destruction of Vrtra, he and I, burning for victory, soared in the sky near the flaming sun, garlanded by glory. Thence impetuously wheeling round, we went to the celestial regions along the etherial way. And it came to pass that, coming midway of the sun, Jațāyu was faint.

verses.sanskrit:
तमहं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सूर्यरश्मिभिरर्दितम्
पक्षाभ्यं छादयामास स्नेहात्परमविह्वलम्
verses.transliteration:
tamahaṁ bhrātaraṁ dṛṣṭvā sūryaraśmibhirarditam
pakṣābhyaṁ chādayāmāsa snehātparamavihvalam

translations.english: Witnessing my brother severely struck by the solar rays and exceedingly stupefied, I from affection shadowed him with my wings.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्दग्धपक्षः पतितो विन्ध्येऽहं वानरोत्तमाः
अहमस्मिन्वसन्भ्रातुः प्रवृत्तिं नोपलक्षये
verses.transliteration:
nirdagdhapakṣaḥ patito vindhye'haṁ vānarottamāḥ
ahamasminvasanbhrātuḥ pravṛttiṁ nopalakṣaye

translations.english: Thereat, my pinions scathed, I dropped down on Vindhya, you foremost of monkeys; and staying here, I could not know the circumstances that have befallen my brother.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुषस्त्वेवमुक्तो भ्रात्रा संपातिना तदा
युवराजो महाप्राज्ञः प्रत्युवाचाङ्गदस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyuṣastvevamukto bhrātrā saṁpātinā tadā
yuvarājo mahāprājñaḥ pratyuvācāṅgadastadā

translations.english: Thus addressed by Jatāyu's brother, Sampāti, the eminently wise prince Angada answered,

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुषो यदि भ्राता श्रुतं ते गदितं मया
आख्याहि यदि जानासि निलयं तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyuṣo yadi bhrātā śrutaṁ te gaditaṁ mayā
ākhyāhi yadi jānāsi nilayaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: 'If you are indeed the brother of Jațāyu, having heard what I have related, tell (us) if you know touching the abode of that Rākşasa. Tell us if you know anent that short-sighted worst of Raksasas, Ravana, whether staying far or near.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा ज्येष्ठो भ्राता जटायुषः
आत्मानुरूपं वचनं वानरान्संप्रहर्षयन्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīnmahātejā jyeṣṭho bhrātā jaṭāyuṣaḥ
ātmānurūpaṁ vacanaṁ vānarānsaṁpraharṣayan

translations.english: Thereat, rejoicing the monkeys, the exceedingly energetic elder brother of Jațāyu spoke words worthy of him.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्दग्धपक्षो गृध्रोऽहं गतवीर्यः प्लवंगमाः
वाङ्मात्रेण तु रामस्य करिष्ये साह्यमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
nirdagdhapakṣo gṛdhro'haṁ gatavīryaḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
vāṅmātreṇa tu rāmasya kariṣye sāhyamuttamam

translations.english: You monkeys, my pinions have been burnt; and I am a vulture shorn of strength. Therefore I will help Rāma well by my words.

verses.sanskrit:
जानामि वारुणाल्लोकान्विष्णोस्त्रैविक्रमानपि
देवासुरविमर्दांश्च अमृतस्य च मन्थनम्
verses.transliteration:
jānāmi vāruṇāllokānviṣṇostraivikramānapi
devāsuravimardāṁśca amṛtasya ca manthanam

translations.english: I know the realms of Varuna, and Visnu's Trivikrama* worlds, the wars of the gods and Asuras, and the churning for ambrosia. *i.e. the worlds enveloped by his three steps during his Dwarf incarnation.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य यदिदं कार्यं कर्तव्यं प्रथमं मया
जरया च हृतं तेजः प्राणाश्च शिथिला मम
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya yadidaṁ kāryaṁ kartavyaṁ prathamaṁ mayā
jarayā ca hṛtaṁ tejaḥ prāṇāśca śithilā mama

translations.english: And albeit age has deprived me of energy, and albeit my life hangs loosely on me, yet, if this is Rāma's work, it should be done by me first.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुणी रूपसंपन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता
ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
taruṇī rūpasaṁpannā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇena durātmanā

translations.english: I have seen a youthful and beautiful female, adorned with all ornaments, carried away by the wicked Rāvana,

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोशन्ती राम रामेति लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी
भूषणान्यपविध्यन्ती गात्राणि च विधुन्वती
verses.transliteration:
krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca bhāminī
bhūṣaṇānyapavidhyantī gātrāṇi ca vidhunvatī

translations.english: The lady (all the while) crying, 'O Rāma!' 'O Rāma!' '0 Lakşmaņa! And And taking her ornaments from her person, she was throwing them on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
सूर्यप्रभेव शैलाग्रे तस्याः कौशेयमुत्तमम्
असिते राक्षसे भाति यथा वा तडिदम्बुदे
verses.transliteration:
sūryaprabheva śailāgre tasyāḥ kauśeyamuttamam
asite rākṣase bhāti yathā vā taḍidambude

translations.english: Her silken cloth seemed like the solar splendour on the summit of a mountain; and herself beside the sable Rākşasa, looked like the lightning in the welkin (beside clouds).

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु सीतामहं मन्ये रामस्य परिकीर्तनात्
श्रूयतां मे कथयतो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu sītāmahaṁ manye rāmasya parikīrtanāt
śrūyatāṁ me kathayato nilayaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: From your relation of Rāma, I conclude that she must be Sītā. Now listen to me as I tell you about the abode of that Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रो विश्रवसः साक्षाद्भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च
अध्यास्ते नगरीं लङ्कां रावणो नाम राकसः
verses.transliteration:
putro viśravasaḥ sākṣādbhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca
adhyāste nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ rāvaṇo nāma rākasaḥ

translations.english: Son to Viśravana and brother to Vaiśravaņa, the Rākşasa named Rāvana resides in the city of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्राप्य सागरस्यान्तं संपूर्णं शतयोजनम्
आसाद्य दक्षिणं कूलं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁprāpya sāgarasyāntaṁ saṁpūrṇaṁ śatayojanam
āsādya dakṣiṇaṁ kūlaṁ tato drakṣyatha rāvaṇam

translations.english: As the end of the ocean after a full hundred Yojanas, arriving at its southern shore, you shall see Rāvana in Laņkā, protected by ocean from all sides. You monkeys, do you hie thither speedily with vigour.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रैव त्वरिताः क्षिप्रं विक्रमध्वं प्लवंगमाः
ज्ञानेन खलु पश्यामि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागमिष्यथ
verses.transliteration:
tatraiva tvaritāḥ kṣipraṁ vikramadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ
jñānena khalu paśyāmi dṛṣṭvā pratyāgamiṣyatha

translations.english: I perceive by my knowledge that having seen (that place) you shall come back. The first course belongs to forktailed shrikes and others living on grain.

verses.sanskrit:
बलवीर्योपपन्नानां रूपयौवनशालिनाम्
षष्ठस्तु पन्था हंसानां वैनतेयगतिः परा
वैनतेयाच्च नो जन्म सर्वेषां वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
balavīryopapannānāṁ rūpayauvanaśālinām
ṣaṣṭhastu panthā haṁsānāṁ vainateyagatiḥ parā
vainateyācca no janma sarveṣāṁ vānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: The second, to those that live on animals and fruits; the third is ranged by Bhāşas; the fourth by Krunchas, Kuvaras and hawks; the fifth by vultures; the sixth belongs to swans endowed with youth and beauty; and the next to the Vainateyas. We have derived or origin from Vainateya. *Aruna, son to Vinata.

verses.sanskrit:
गर्हितं तु कृतं कर्म येन स्म पिशिताशनाः
इहस्थोऽहं प्रपश्यामि रावणं जानकीं तथा
verses.transliteration:
garhitaṁ tu kṛtaṁ karma yena sma piśitāśanāḥ
ihastho'haṁ prapaśyāmi rāvaṇaṁ jānakīṁ tathā

translations.english: Resting here, I see Ravana and Janaki. We have excellent Sauparana' clairvoyance. *Clairvoyance attained by success in knowledge respecting the spiritual Golden eyes. Thus far the commentator. We leave the abstruse point to the apostles of theosophy and spiritism for illucidation.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माकमपि सौवर्णं दिव्यं चक्षुर्बलं तथा
तस्मादाहारवीर्येण निसर्गेण च वानराः
आयोजनशतात्साग्राद्वयं पश्याम नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
asmākamapi sauvarṇaṁ divyaṁ cakṣurbalaṁ tathā
tasmādāhāravīryeṇa nisargeṇa ca vānarāḥ
āyojanaśatātsāgrādvayaṁ paśyāma nityaśaḥ

translations.english: For this reason, as well as owing to the energy consequent on our feeding on certain kinds of flesh, we, you monkeys, can see a little further than an hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माकं विहिता वृत्तिर्निसार्गेण च दूरतः
विहिता पादमूले तु वृत्तिश्चरणयोधिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
asmākaṁ vihitā vṛttirnisārgeṇa ca dūrataḥ
vihitā pādamūle tu vṛttiścaraṇayodhinām

translations.english: Therefore (the Deity) has ordained such food for us as are fraught with the power of making one see from a great distance. And the abode of cocks and others being underneath trees, their sight is limited to the extent which they require to see.

verses.sanskrit:
समुद्रं नेतुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वरुणालयम्
प्रदास्याम्युदकं भ्रातुः स्वर्गतस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
samudraṁ netumicchāmi bhavadbhirvaruṇālayam
pradāsyāmyudakaṁ bhrātuḥ svargatasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Do you look about for means to cross over the salt waters. Having met with Vaidehi, do you, having achieved success, come back. I wish to be taken by you to the ocean-abode of Varuna. I will offer water to (the manes of) my highsouled brother, who has gone to heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नीत्वा तु तं देशं तीरे नदनदीपतेः
निर्दग्धपक्षं संपातिं वानराः सुमहौजसः
verses.transliteration:
tato nītvā tu taṁ deśaṁ tīre nadanadīpateḥ
nirdagdhapakṣaṁ saṁpātiṁ vānarāḥ sumahaujasaḥ

translations.english: Thereat those heroes, the monkeys possessed of exceeding energy, carried to the destined spot on the shore of the ocean, Sampāti, whose wings had been scathed. Then carrying that lord of vultures back to the self-same place, the monkeys, furnished with information (concerning Sītā), experienced great joy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तदमृतास्वादं गृध्रराजेन भाषितम्
निशम्य वदतो हृष्टास्ते वचः प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
tatastadamṛtāsvādaṁ gṛdhrarājena bhāṣitam
niśamya vadato hṛṣṭāste vacaḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: Then hearing that ambrosial speech of the vulture-king, the monkey-chiefs, being delighted, kept on parleying (on that topic).

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवान्वै हरिश्रेष्ठः सह सर्वैः प्लवंगमैः
भूतलात्सहसोत्थाय गृध्रराजानमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavānvai hariśreṣṭhaḥ saha sarvaiḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ
bhūtalātsahasotthāya gṛdhrarājānamabravīt

translations.english: Then Jāmbavān-foremost of monkeystogether with all the monkeys, arising suddenly from the ground, spoke to the vulture-king, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
क्व सीता केन वा दृष्टा को वा हरति मैथिलीम्
तदाख्यातु भवान्सर्वं गतिर्भव वनौकसाम्
verses.transliteration:
kva sītā kena vā dṛṣṭā ko vā harati maithilīm
tadākhyātu bhavānsarvaṁ gatirbhava vanaukasām

translations.english: Where is Sītā? By whom has she been seen? And who has carried away Mithila's daughter? Do you tell us all about this, and (thus) prove the path of these rangers of the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
को दाशरथिबाणानां वज्रवेगनिपातिनाम्
स्वयं लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां न चिन्तयति विक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
ko dāśarathibāṇānāṁ vajraveganipātinām
svayaṁ lakṣmaṇamuktānāṁ na cintayati vikramam

translations.english: Who is there that does not take heed of the force of Dasarathi's* and Laksmana's arrows, speeding with the vehemence of thunder? *Lit. Dasaratha's son. The term is applied in especial to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स हरीन्प्रीतिसंयुक्तान्सीता श्रुतिसमाहितान्
पुनराश्वासयन्प्रीत इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa harīnprītisaṁyuktānsītā śrutisamāhitān
punarāśvāsayanprīta idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thereat, cheering up those monkeys, who had risen from their attitudes of fasting, and who were all attention to hear news concerning Sītā, he (Sampāti), well pleased, said these words,

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयतामिह वैदेह्या यथा मे हरणं श्रुतम्
येन चापि ममाख्यातं यत्र चायतलोचना
verses.transliteration:
śrūyatāmiha vaidehyā yathā me haraṇaṁ śrutam
yena cāpi mamākhyātaṁ yatra cāyatalocanā

translations.english: Listen as to how I came to know of the ravishment of Vaidehī, Sītā, at this place; and who it was that told me where that one of expansive eyes is.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमस्मिन्गिरौ दुर्गे बहुयोजनमायते
चिरान्निपतितो वृद्धः क्षीणप्राणपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
ahamasmingirau durge bahuyojanamāyate
cirānnipatito vṛddhaḥ kṣīṇaprāṇaparākramaḥ

translations.english: For a long time I lay here, old, and of feeble life and energy. that best of birds, my son named Supārswa, coming to me, at the proper hour maintained me with food.

verses.sanskrit:
तीक्ष्णकामास्तु गन्धर्वास्तीक्ष्णकोपा भुजंगमाः
मृगाणां तु भयं तीक्ष्णं ततस्तीक्ष्णक्षुधा वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tīkṣṇakāmāstu gandharvāstīkṣṇakopā bhujaṁgamāḥ
mṛgāṇāṁ tu bhayaṁ tīkṣṇaṁ tatastīkṣṇakṣudhā vayam

translations.english: Gandharvas exceedingly lascivious; serpents are exceedingly wrathful; fear is excessive in deer; and we have excessive hunger.

verses.sanskrit:
स कदाचित्क्षुधार्तस्य मम चाहारकाङ्क्षिणः
गतसूर्योऽहनि प्राप्तो मम पुत्रो ह्यनामिषः
verses.transliteration:
sa kadācitkṣudhārtasya mama cāhārakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
gatasūryo'hani prāpto mama putro hyanāmiṣaḥ

translations.english: Once on a time my son, going forth about sunrise to procure food for me who was suffering from hunger and (accordingly) eager for it, came back in the evening without any flesh. are

verses.sanskrit:
स ममाहारसंरोधात्पीडितः प्रीतिवर्धनः
अनुमान्य यथातत्त्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa mamāhārasaṁrodhātpīḍitaḥ prītivardhanaḥ
anumānya yathātattvamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hurt (by my speech uttered) in consequence of my non-receipt of food, that enhancer of my joy, asking my forgiveness, said these words fraught with fact,

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तात यथाकालमामिषार्थी खमाप्लुतः
महेन्द्रस्य गिरेर्द्वारमावृत्य च समास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tāta yathākālamāmiṣārthī khamāplutaḥ
mahendrasya girerdvāramāvṛtya ca samāsthitaḥ

translations.english: 'Father, taking to my wings at the proper time for procuring flesh, I (went) and stood, obstructing the pass of the Mahendra mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र सत्त्वसहस्राणां सागरान्तरचारिणाम्
पन्थानमेकोऽध्यवसं संनिरोद्धुमवाङ्मुखः
verses.transliteration:
tatra sattvasahasrāṇāṁ sāgarāntaracāriṇām
panthānameko'dhyavasaṁ saṁniroddhumavāṅmukhaḥ

translations.english: There stood I looking down, obstructing the way of thousands of creatures ranging the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र कश्चिन्मया दृष्टः सूर्योदयसमप्रभाम्
स्त्रियमादाय गच्छन्वै भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः
verses.transliteration:
tatra kaścinmayā dṛṣṭaḥ sūryodayasamaprabhām
striyamādāya gacchanvai bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ

translations.english: There I saw somebody resembling a mass of crushed collyrium, going away, taking a female resembling the rising sun in splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहमभ्यवहारार्थी तौ दृष्ट्वा कृतनिश्चयः
तेन साम्ना विनीतेन पन्थानमभियाचितः
verses.transliteration:
so'hamabhyavahārārthī tau dṛṣṭvā kṛtaniścayaḥ
tena sāmnā vinītena panthānamabhiyācitaḥ

translations.english: Seeing them I had made up my mind that they should serve for your fare, when he humbly in a pacific manner begged for way.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि सामोपपन्नानां प्रहर्ता विद्यते क्वचित्
नीचेष्वपि जनः कश्चित्किमङ्ग बत मद्विधः
verses.transliteration:
na hi sāmopapannānāṁ prahartā vidyate kvacit
nīceṣvapi janaḥ kaścitkimaṅga bata madvidhaḥ

translations.english: Even among the mean, there is none on earth that can slay people who assume a mild attitude. What shall I say, alas! of superior ones like myself?

verses.sanskrit:
स यातस्तेजसा व्योम संक्षिपन्निव वेगतः
अथाहं खे चरैर्भूतैरभिगम्य सभाजितः
verses.transliteration:
sa yātastejasā vyoma saṁkṣipanniva vegataḥ
athāhaṁ khe carairbhūtairabhigamya sabhājitaḥ

translations.english: And summoning celerity, he went on as if pushing off the sky by his energy. Then the rangers of the air and other beings worshipped me.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या जीवसि तातेति अब्रुवन्मां महर्षयः
कथंचित्सकलत्रोऽसौ गतस्ते स्वस्त्यसंशयम्
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā jīvasi tāteti abruvanmāṁ maharṣayaḥ
kathaṁcitsakalatro'sau gataste svastyasaṁśayam

translations.english: And the Maharsis said to me,-By luck it is that Sītā is still living' — he together with a female, having passed by you, certainly augurs good fortune to you. 1. The commentator supplies the elipsis thus,-Coming within your ken by fuck, Sītā is living. 2. The passage is obscure. The commentator has glossed over this sloka, and the meaning is lone the clear for his explanation.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्ततोऽहं तैः सिद्धैः परमशोभनैः
स च मे रावणो राजा रक्षसां प्रतिवेदितः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastato'haṁ taiḥ siddhaiḥ paramaśobhanaiḥ
sa ca me rāvaṇo rājā rakṣasāṁ prativeditaḥ

translations.english: Then those eminently handsome Siddhas spoke thus to me.-This is Ravana, the king of the Rākşasas, said they to me.

verses.sanskrit:
एतमर्थं समग्रं मे सुपार्श्वः प्रत्यवेदयत्
तच्छ्रुत्वापि हि मे बुद्धिर्नासीत्काचित्पराक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
etamarthaṁ samagraṁ me supārśvaḥ pratyavedayat
tacchrutvāpi hi me buddhirnāsītkācitparākrame

translations.english: I (stood), beholding the wife of Rama, son to Dasaratha,—throwing off her ornaments and silken apparel, overwhelmed by might of sorrow, with hair dishevelled crying out the names of Rāma and Lakşmaņa. This O father, is the reason of my passing the time.' That best of those skilled in speech, Suparswa, said all this to me. Even hearing of this, I could not think of putting forth prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
अपक्षो हि कथं पक्षी कर्म किंचिदुपक्रमेत्
यत्तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं वाग्बुद्धिगुणवर्तिना
verses.transliteration:
apakṣo hi kathaṁ pakṣī karma kiṁcidupakramet
yattu śakyaṁ mayā kartuṁ vāgbuddhiguṇavartinā

translations.english: How can a bird bereft of wings, undertake any thing? But listen! I will tell you as to what I am capable of through speech, intellect and merit, and what you can exèrt your manliness in.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयतां तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि भवतां पौरुषाश्रयम्
वाङ्मतिभ्यां हि सार्वेषां करिष्यामि प्रियं हि वः
यद्धि दाशरथेः कार्यं मम तन्नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
śrūyatāṁ tatpravakṣyāmi bhavatāṁ pauruṣāśrayam
vāṅmatibhyāṁ hi sārveṣāṁ kariṣyāmi priyaṁ hi vaḥ
yaddhi dāśaratheḥ kāryaṁ mama tannātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: I will do what is agreeable to you by my words and my and my intention. That which is Dasarathi's work is also mine. Of this there is no doubt.

verses.sanskrit:
ते भवन्तो मतिश्रेष्ठा बलवन्तो मनस्विनः
सहिताः कपिराजेन देवैरपि दुरासदाः
verses.transliteration:
te bhavanto matiśreṣṭhā balavanto manasvinaḥ
sahitāḥ kapirājena devairapi durāsadāḥ

translations.english: You, foremost in intelligence, strong, intellectual, and incapable of being overcome by the gods themselves, have been despatched by the monarch of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणबाणाश्च निशिताः कङ्कपत्रिणः
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पर्याप्तास्त्राणनिग्रहे
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇabāṇāśca niśitāḥ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṁ paryāptāstrāṇanigrahe

translations.english: Rama's and Laksmana's shafts furnished with the feathers of the Kanka, are competent to afflict or save the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं खलु दशग्रीवस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः
भवतां तु समर्थानां न किंचिदपि दुष्करम्
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ khalu daśagrīvastejobalasamanvitaḥ
bhavatāṁ tu samarthānāṁ na kiṁcidapi duṣkaram

translations.english: And although the Ten-necked one is endowed with strength and energy, yet to you who are competent, nothing is hard to accomplish.

verses.sanskrit:
तदलं कालसंगेन क्रियतां बुद्धिनिश्चयः
न हि कर्मसु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः
verses.transliteration:
tadalaṁ kālasaṁgena kriyatāṁ buddhiniścayaḥ
na hi karmasu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ

translations.english: There is no need of delay. Make up 'yo minds. Persons like you do not give way to laziness in enterprise.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृतोदकं स्नातं तं गृध्रं हरियूथपाः
उपविष्टा गिरौ दुर्गे परिवार्य समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛtodakaṁ snātaṁ taṁ gṛdhraṁ hariyūthapāḥ
upaviṣṭā girau durge parivārya samantataḥ

translations.english: When the vulture had offered oblations of water to the manes of his deceased brother and finished his ablutions, the monkey-chiefs sat down in that charming mountain, surrounding him.

verses.sanskrit:
तमङ्गदमुपासीनं तैः सर्वैर्हरिभिर्वृतम्
जनितप्रत्ययो हर्षात्संपातिः पुनरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tamaṅgadamupāsīnaṁ taiḥ sarvairharibhirvṛtam
janitapratyayo harṣātsaṁpātiḥ punarabravīt

translations.english: And inspired with confidence in the words of the Nisakara), Sampati, from delight, said to Angada, who was seated, surrounded by all the monkeys.'

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा निःशब्दमेकाग्राः शृण्वन्तु हरयो मम
तत्त्वं संकीर्तयिष्यामि यथा जानामि मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā niḥśabdamekāgrāḥ śṛṇvantu harayo mama
tattvaṁ saṁkīrtayiṣyāmi yathā jānāmi maithilīm

translations.english: Remaining silent, do you, you monkeys, heedfully hear what I say. I will tell you truly how I came to know Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य विन्ध्यस्य शिखरे पतितोऽस्मि पुरा वने
सूर्यातपपरीताङ्गो निर्दग्धः सूर्यरश्मिभिः
verses.transliteration:
asya vindhyasya śikhare patito'smi purā vane
sūryātapaparītāṅgo nirdagdhaḥ sūryaraśmibhiḥ

translations.english: My body being affected by solar heat, and my wings burnt by the rays of the sun, O sinless one, I formerly fell to this summit of Vindhya.

verses.sanskrit:
लब्धसंज्ञस्तु षड्रात्राद्विवशो विह्वलन्निव
वीक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वा नाभिजानामि किंचन
verses.transliteration:
labdhasaṁjñastu ṣaḍrātrādvivaśo vihvalanniva
vīkṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvā nābhijānāmi kiṁcana

translations.english: On regaining my senses after six nights, during which I was insensible, I looked around in bewilderment, but could not recognise anything whatever.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सागराञ्शैलान्नदीः सर्वाः सरांसि च
वनान्यटविदेशांश्च समीक्ष्य मतिरागमत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sāgarāñśailānnadīḥ sarvāḥ sarāṁsi ca
vanānyaṭavideśāṁśca samīkṣya matirāgamat

translations.english: Then closely viewing oceans and mountains, rivers and tanks, and woods and countries, my thoughts came back to me.

verses.sanskrit:
हृष्टपक्षिगणाकीर्णः कन्दरान्तरकूटवान्
दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे विन्ध्योऽयमिति निश्चितः
verses.transliteration:
hṛṣṭapakṣigaṇākīrṇaḥ kandarāntarakūṭavān
dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre vindhyo'yamiti niścitaḥ

translations.english: Seeing this place abounding in cheerful birds, containing woods and crested with summits, I for certain concluded it to be Vindhya on the shores of the Southern sea.

verses.sanskrit:
आसीच्चात्राश्रमं पुण्यं सुरैरपि सुपूजितम्
ऋषिर्निशाकरो नाम यस्मिन्नुग्रतपाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
āsīccātrāśramaṁ puṇyaṁ surairapi supūjitam
ṛṣirniśākaro nāma yasminnugratapābhavat

translations.english: And here lay a sacred asylum, honoured even by the celestials, and here dwelt a saint named Niśākara, of fierce austerities.

verses.sanskrit:
अष्टौ वर्षसहस्राणि तेनास्मिन्नृषिणा विना
वसतो मम धर्मज्ञाः स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे
verses.transliteration:
aṣṭau varṣasahasrāṇi tenāsminnṛṣiṇā vinā
vasato mama dharmajñāḥ svargate tu niśākare

translations.english: After Niśākara cognizant of virtue had gone to heaven, I bereft of that saint, passed eight thousand years in this mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
अवतीर्य च विन्ध्याग्रात्कृच्छ्रेण विषमाच्छनैः
तीक्ष्णदर्भां वसुमतीं दुःखेन पुनरागतः
verses.transliteration:
avatīrya ca vindhyāgrātkṛcchreṇa viṣamācchanaiḥ
tīkṣṇadarbhāṁ vasumatīṁ duḥkhena punarāgataḥ

translations.english: Descending with difficulty from the uneven top of Vindhya, I again came* to the earth covered with sharp-pointed grass. *While the saint was staying here.

verses.sanskrit:
तमृषिं द्रष्टु कामोऽस्मि दुःखेनाभ्यागतो भृशम्
जटायुषा मया चैव बहुशोऽभिगतो हि सः
verses.transliteration:
tamṛṣiṁ draṣṭu kāmo'smi duḥkhenābhyāgato bhṛśam
jaṭāyuṣā mayā caiva bahuśo'bhigato hi saḥ

translations.english: I was eager to see the saint; and (therefore), with much ado I came to him; and Jatāyu and myself saw that saint many a time and oft.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याश्रमपदाभ्याशे ववुर्वाताः सुगन्धिनः
वृक्षो नापुष्पितः कश्चिदफलो वा न दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
tasyāśramapadābhyāśe vavurvātāḥ sugandhinaḥ
vṛkṣo nāpuṣpitaḥ kaścidaphalo vā na dṛśyate

translations.english: A fragrant breeze blew about the hermitage; and no tree was found that did not bear flowers and fruits.

verses.sanskrit:
उपेत्य चाश्रमं पुण्यं वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः
द्रष्टुकामः प्रतीक्षे च भगवन्तं निशाकरम्
verses.transliteration:
upetya cāśramaṁ puṇyaṁ vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ
draṣṭukāmaḥ pratīkṣe ca bhagavantaṁ niśākaram

translations.english: Approaching the holy asylum, I, desirous of beholding the worshipful Niśākara, waited at the foot of a tree.

verses.sanskrit:
अथापश्यमदूरस्थमृषिं ज्वलिततेजसं
कृताभिषेकं दुर्धर्षमुपावृत्तमुदङ्मुखम्
verses.transliteration:
athāpaśyamadūrasthamṛṣiṁ jvalitatejasaṁ
kṛtābhiṣekaṁ durdharṣamupāvṛttamudaṅmukham

translations.english: Then at a distance I saw the saint, flaming in energy and irrepressible,-returning northwards.

verses.sanskrit:
तमृक्षाः सृमरा व्याघ्राः सिंहा नागाः सरीसृपाः
परिवार्योपगच्छन्ति दातारं प्राणिनो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tamṛkṣāḥ sṛmarā vyāghrāḥ siṁhā nāgāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ
parivāryopagacchanti dātāraṁ prāṇino yathā

translations.english: As creatures gather round a giver, bears and Srimaras, tigers lions, and various reptiles, were going along, surrounding him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्राप्तमृषिं ज्ञात्वा तानि सत्त्वानि वै ययुः
प्रविष्टे राजनि यथा सर्वं सामात्यकं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prāptamṛṣiṁ jñātvā tāni sattvāni vai yayuḥ
praviṣṭe rājani yathā sarvaṁ sāmātyakaṁ balam

translations.english: And knowing that the saint had arrived (at his home), the animals went away, as go away forces together with counsellors, when the sovereign has entered (his palace).

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिस्तु दृष्ट्वा मां तुष्टः प्रविष्टश्चाश्रमं पुनः
मुहूर्तमात्रान्निष्क्रम्य ततः कार्यमपृच्छत
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣistu dṛṣṭvā māṁ tuṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaścāśramaṁ punaḥ
muhūrtamātrānniṣkramya tataḥ kāryamapṛcchata

translations.english: The saint was glad on seeing me. Then reentering his asylum for a short space, he came out and enquired for my mission.

verses.sanskrit:
सौम्य वैकल्यतां दृष्ट्वा रोंणां ते नावगम्यते
अग्निदग्धाविमौ पक्षौ त्वक्चैव व्रणिता तव
verses.transliteration:
saumya vaikalyatāṁ dṛṣṭvā roṁṇāṁ te nāvagamyate
agnidagdhāvimau pakṣau tvakcaiva vraṇitā tava

translations.english: O mild one, in consequence of your feathers having undergone alteration, I cannot recognise you. Your two wings have been blasted by fire; and your powers in your frail frame are in the same condition).

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ गृध्रौ दृष्टपूर्वौ मे मातरिश्वसमौ जवे
गृध्राणां चैव राजानौ भ्रातरौ कामरूपिणौ
verses.transliteration:
dvau gṛdhrau dṛṣṭapūrvau me mātariśvasamau jave
gṛdhrāṇāṁ caiva rājānau bhrātarau kāmarūpiṇau

translations.english: After time I saw two vultures like to wind in speed,-kings of vultures, brothers, wearing shapes at will.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठस्त्वं तु च संपातिर्जटायुरनुजस्तव
मानुषं रूपमास्थाय गृह्णीतां चरणौ मम
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhastvaṁ tu ca saṁpātirjaṭāyuranujastava
mānuṣaṁ rūpamāsthāya gṛhṇītāṁ caraṇau mama

translations.english: You are I know, elder, O Sampati; and Jatayu is younger to you. Assuming human forms, you had taken hold of my feet.

verses.sanskrit:
किं ते व्याधिसमुत्थानं पक्षयोः पतनं कथम्
दण्डो वायं धृतः केन सर्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ te vyādhisamutthānaṁ pakṣayoḥ patanaṁ katham
daṇḍo vāyaṁ dhṛtaḥ kena sarvamākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ

translations.english: Now, what ailment has attacked you? And why have your plumes fallen off? And who has dealt this punishment to you? Do you tell all this to me, who am asking you.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्दारुणं कर्म दुष्करं साहसात्कृतम्
आचचक्षे मुनेः सर्वं सूर्यानुगमनं तथा
verses.transliteration:
tatastaddāruṇaṁ karma duṣkaraṁ sāhasātkṛtam
ācacakṣe muneḥ sarvaṁ sūryānugamanaṁ tathā

translations.english: Thereat Sampāti related to the ascetic all about his fearful, arduous, and rash act of following up the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्व्रणयुक्तत्वाल्लज्जया चाकुलेन्द्रियः
परिश्रान्तो न शक्नोमि वचनं परिभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavanvraṇayuktatvāllajjayā cākulendriyaḥ
pariśrānto na śaknomi vacanaṁ paribhāṣitum

translations.english: O reverend sire, in consequence of my body suffering from sores, I, my senses bewildered from shame, and myself fatigued, cannot utter words.

verses.sanskrit:
कैलासशिखरे बद्ध्वा मुनीनामग्रतः पणम्
रविः स्यादनुयातव्यो यावदस्तं महागिरिम्
verses.transliteration:
kailāsaśikhare baddhvā munīnāmagrataḥ paṇam
raviḥ syādanuyātavyo yāvadastaṁ mahāgirim

translations.english: From pride for power of flight, I and Jatayu, being intoxicated by conceit, began to voyage the sky afar off, with the view of testing each other's prowess, binding ourselves by the vow that we would follow the Sun so long as he did not enter that mighty Setting mountain,-and appear before the ascetics on the summit of Kailāsa.

verses.sanskrit:
अथावां युगपत्प्राप्तावपश्याव महीतले
रथचक्रप्रमाणानि नगराणि पृथक्पृथक्
verses.transliteration:
athāvāṁ yugapatprāptāvapaśyāva mahītale
