rathacakrapramāṇāni nagarāṇi pṛthakpṛthak

translations.english: And simultaneously plunging into the serial deep) we saw on the earth beneath separate cities resembling car-wheels; and here the sound of musical instruments, and there the tinklings of ornaments. And (at places) we beheld many a damsel clad in red attire, engaged in singing.

verses.sanskrit:
तूर्णमुत्पत्य चाकाशमादित्यपथमास्थितौ
आवामालोकयावस्तद्वनं शाद्वलसंस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
tūrṇamutpatya cākāśamādityapathamāsthitau
āvāmālokayāvastadvanaṁ śādvalasaṁsthitam

translations.english: And swiftly darting up into the sky and approaching the path of the Sun, we saw a wood interspersed with swards.

verses.sanskrit:
उपलैरिव संछन्ना दृश्यते भूः शिलोच्चयैः
आपगाभिश्च संवीता सूत्रैरिव वसुंधरा
verses.transliteration:
upalairiva saṁchannā dṛśyate bhūḥ śiloccayaiḥ
āpagābhiśca saṁvītā sūtrairiva vasuṁdharā

translations.english: We saw the earth covered with crags and masses of rocks, and intersected by streams resembling threads.

verses.sanskrit:
तीव्रस्वेदश्च खेदश्च भयं चासीत्तदावयोः
समाविशत मोहश्च मोहान्मूर्छा च दारुणा
verses.transliteration:
tīvrasvedaśca khedaśca bhayaṁ cāsīttadāvayoḥ
samāviśata mohaśca mohānmūrchā ca dāruṇā

translations.english: Himavān, and Vindhya, and that mighty mountain, Meru, appeared on the earth like elephants in a tank. Then we began to sweat, and to be filled with regret; and fear seized us both. And we became bewildered; and fainted away frightfully.* *Consequent on Jațāyu having dropped down.

verses.sanskrit:
न दिग्विज्ञायते याम्या नागेन्या न च वारुणी
युगान्ते नियतो लोको हतो दग्ध इवाग्निना
verses.transliteration:
na digvijñāyate yāmyā nāgenyā na ca vāruṇī
yugānte niyato loko hato dagdha ivāgninā

translations.english: We knew not the south, or the west, or the quarter presided over by Fire;' and the world that was still burning at the end of a Yuga, appeared (to us) as if it had been consumed quite.? 1. South-east. 2. The passage is obscure. This is however, all the explanation that the commentator has to give.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्नेन महता भूयो रविः समवलोकितः
तुल्यः पृथ्वीप्रमाणेन भास्करः प्रतिभाति नौ
verses.transliteration:
yatnena mahatā bhūyo raviḥ samavalokitaḥ
tulyaḥ pṛthvīpramāṇena bhāskaraḥ pratibhāti nau

translations.english: My mind, combined with my eyes waxed feebler. And then fixing with might and main my eyes as well as my mind (on the sun), I could by a violent exercise of my energy behold the sun. And the sun shining, appeared to us like the earth in extent.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायुर्मामनापृच्छ्य निपपात महीं ततः
तं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमाकाशादात्मानं मुक्तवानहम्
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyurmāmanāpṛcchya nipapāta mahīṁ tataḥ
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇamākāśādātmānaṁ muktavānaham

translations.english: Then, without asking me Jațāyu dropped to the earth. Seeing him, I at once descended form the sky and Jațāyu and not burnt in consequence of having been shielded by my wings. And scathed through the agitation* I fell through the serial way. I guessed that Jațāyu fell in Janasthāna. And I myself, my wings blasted, and rendered inert, fell on Vindhya. *Rāmanuya comments: the confusion seized them as the sun was midway. They lost all ense of direction. The faint succeeded.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्येन हीनो भ्रात्रा च पक्षाभ्यां विक्रमेण च
सर्वथा मर्तुमेवेच्छन्पतिष्ये शिखराद्गिरेः
verses.transliteration:
rājyena hīno bhrātrā ca pakṣābhyāṁ vikrameṇa ca
sarvathā martumevecchanpatiṣye śikharādgireḥ

translations.english: Deprived of my kingdom, and my brother, and my wings, and my prowess, I wishing to put a period to my existence, will hurl myself headlong from this summit of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठमरुदं दुःखितो भृशम्
अथ ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु भगवानिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā muniśreṣṭhamarudaṁ duḥkhito bhṛśam
atha dhyātvā muhūrtaṁ tu bhagavānidamabravīt

translations.english: Having said this to that foremost of ascetics, I smitten with grief, began to weep. Thereat, after, reflecting for a while, that reverend one said,

verses.sanskrit:
पक्षौ च ते प्रपक्षौ च पुनरन्यौ भविष्यतः
चक्षुषी चैव प्राणाश्च विक्रमश्च बलं च ते
verses.transliteration:
pakṣau ca te prapakṣau ca punaranyau bhaviṣyataḥ
cakṣuṣī caiva prāṇāśca vikramaśca balaṁ ca te

translations.english: Your wings together with two smaller ones shall grow again; as also your sight, energy, prowess and strength.

verses.sanskrit:
पुराणे सुमहत्कार्यं भविष्यं हि मया श्रुतम्
दृष्टं मे तपसा चैव श्रुत्वा च विदितं मम
verses.transliteration:
purāṇe sumahatkāryaṁ bhaviṣyaṁ hi mayā śrutam
dṛṣṭaṁ me tapasā caiva śrutvā ca viditaṁ mama

translations.english: Having heard of it, and also seen it through ascetic power, I know that a great deed is going to take place.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा दशरथो नाम कश्चिदिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः
तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा रामो नाम भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rājā daśaratho nāma kaścidikṣvākunandanaḥ
tasya putro mahātejā rāmo nāma bhaviṣyati

translations.english: There shall be a king named Daſaratha, increaser of the Ikşwāku race. He shall have a son, named Rāma, endowed with exceeding energy.

verses.sanskrit:
अरण्यं च सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन गमिष्यति
तस्मिन्नर्थे नियुक्तः सन्पित्रा सत्यपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
araṇyaṁ ca saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena gamiṣyati
tasminnarthe niyuktaḥ sanpitrā satyaparākramaḥ

translations.english: He (Rāma) shall repair to the forest in company with his brother, Laksmana; that one having truth for prowess, having commissioned to that effect by his sire.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृतो रावणो नाम तस्या भार्यां हरिष्यति
राक्षसेन्द्रो जनस्थानादवध्यः सुरदानवैः
verses.transliteration:
nairṛto rāvaṇo nāma tasyā bhāryāṁ hariṣyati
rākṣasendro janasthānādavadhyaḥ suradānavaiḥ

translations.english: A friend named Rāvana, the lord of Rākşasas, incapable of being slain by either the gods or the Dāvanas, shall carry off his Rāma's) spouse in Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
सा च कामैः प्रलोभ्यन्ती भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च मैथिली
न भोक्ष्यति महाभागा दुःखमग्ना यशस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
sā ca kāmaiḥ pralobhyantī bhakṣyairbhojyaiśca maithilī
na bhokṣyati mahābhāgā duḥkhamagnā yaśasvinī

translations.english: And albeit tempted by viands and objects of enjoyment and desire, the famous and highly virtuous one, plunged in grief, shall not pertake of those things.

verses.sanskrit:
परमान्नं तु वैदेह्या ज्ञात्वा दास्यति वासवः
यदन्नममृतप्रख्यं सुराणामपि दुर्लभम्
verses.transliteration:
paramānnaṁ tu vaidehyā jñātvā dāsyati vāsavaḥ
yadannamamṛtaprakhyaṁ surāṇāmapi durlabham

translations.english: And knowing that Videha's daughter (has been fasting for many a day), Vāsava shall offer Vaidehī pāyasa like to ambrosia, difficult of being procured even by the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
तदन्नं मैथिली प्राप्य विज्ञायेन्द्रादिदं त्विति
अग्रमुद्धृत्य रामाय भूतले निर्वपिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tadannaṁ maithilī prāpya vijñāyendrādidaṁ tviti
agramuddhṛtya rāmāya bhūtale nirvapiṣyati

translations.english: Receiving that food, Maithili, knowing that it has come from Indra,* took up a little of it from the surface, and dropped it to the earth for Rāma. *From the fact of the food not touching the earth, and other signs. It is humorous to read the explanation of the commentator as to the reason of Indra's supplying Sītā with food. If Sītā remained fasting, Rāvana would forego his attachment for Vaidehi, on seeing her altered appearance; and thus his destruction could not take place. Further, if he saw Sītā retaining her former loveliness, he could conclude that Sītā, as also Rāma, were superhuman character, and that as such they could not be agents for his destruction according to the prophecy Rāvana shall be slain by a human being. This inducing him to persist in his bellicose attitude towards Rāma, would being down ruin upon his head.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि जीवति मे भर्ता लक्ष्मणेन सह प्रभुः
देवत्वं गतयोर्वापि तयोरन्नमिदं त्विति
verses.transliteration:
yadi jīvati me bhartā lakṣmaṇena saha prabhuḥ
devatvaṁ gatayorvāpi tayorannamidaṁ tviti

translations.english: Whether my husband as well as his younger brother live, or they have attained godhead, let this food serve for them.

verses.sanskrit:
एष्यन्त्यन्वेषकास्तस्या रामदूताः प्लवंगमाः
आख्येया राममहिषी त्वया तेभ्यो विहंगम
verses.transliteration:
eṣyantyanveṣakāstasyā rāmadūtāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
ākhyeyā rāmamahiṣī tvayā tebhyo vihaṁgama

translations.english: Rāma's envoys, having been despatched thither.* shall come hither. You should relate to them all the facts connected with the queen of Rāma. *For going to Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा तु न गन्तव्यमीदृशः क्व गमिष्यसि
देशकालौ प्रतीक्षस्व पक्षौ त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā tu na gantavyamīdṛśaḥ kva gamiṣyasi
deśakālau pratīkṣasva pakṣau tvaṁ pratipatsyase

translations.english: Do not by any means go hence; and in this case, whither, again, wilt you repair? Do you stay here for season and place. You shall regain your wings.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्
इहस्थस्त्वं तु लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
utsaheyamahaṁ kartumadyaiva tvāṁ sapakṣakam
ihasthastvaṁ tu lokānāṁ hitaṁ kāryaṁ kariṣyasi

translations.english: I could this very day furnish you with wings. But, by staying here in this condition, you wilt be able to compass the welfare of the worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयापि खलु तत्कार्यं तयोश्च नृपपुत्रयोः
ब्राह्मणानां सुराणां च मुनीनां वासवस्य च
verses.transliteration:
tvayāpi khalu tatkāryaṁ tayośca nṛpaputrayoḥ
brāhmaṇānāṁ surāṇāṁ ca munīnāṁ vāsavasya ca

translations.english: Even you shall do that act in behalf of those sons of the king, of the Brāhmanas, of the spiritual preceptors, of the ascetics, and of Vasava.

verses.sanskrit:
इच्छाम्यहमपि द्रष्टुं भ्रातरु रामलक्ष्मणौ
नेच्छे चिरं धारयितुं प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्ये कलेवरम्
verses.transliteration:
icchāmyahamapi draṣṭuṁ bhrātaru rāmalakṣmaṇau
necche ciraṁ dhārayituṁ prāṇāṁstyakṣye kalevaram

translations.english: I also am desirous of beholding the brothers, Rāma and Laksmana. I do not wish to hold this life long. I would renounce my life.' That Maharși, conversant with the nature of things, told me this.'

verses.sanskrit:
एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्वाक्यविशारदः
मां प्रशस्याभ्यनुज्ञाप्य प्रविष्टः स स्वमाश्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
etairanyaiśca bahubhirvākyairvākyaviśāradaḥ
māṁ praśasyābhyanujñāpya praviṣṭaḥ sa svamāśramam

translations.english: Having praised me with these and many other words, and bidden me adieu that one skilled in speech, entered his own habitation.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्दरात्तु विसर्पित्वा पर्वतस्य शनैः शनैः
अहं विन्ध्यं समारुह्य भवतः प्रतिपालये
verses.transliteration:
kandarāttu visarpitvā parvatasya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
ahaṁ vindhyaṁ samāruhya bhavataḥ pratipālaye

translations.english: Issuing out gently from the cave of that mountain, I, ascending Vindhya, was expecting you.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य त्वेतस्य कालस्य साग्रं वर्षशतं गतम्
देशकालप्रतीक्षोऽस्मि हृदि कृत्वा मुनेर्वचः
verses.transliteration:
adya tvetasya kālasya sāgraṁ varṣaśataṁ gatam
deśakālapratīkṣo'smi hṛdi kṛtvā munervacaḥ

translations.english: The space covered by the time intervening between then and to-day is a little over an hundred years;* and laying up in my heart the speech of that ascetic I have been awaiting season and place. *The commentator says the period is one hundred and eight years.

verses.sanskrit:
महाप्रस्थानमासाद्य स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे
मां निर्दहति संतापो वितर्कैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्
verses.transliteration:
mahāprasthānamāsādya svargate tu niśākare
māṁ nirdahati saṁtāpo vitarkairbahubhirvṛtam

translations.english: Setting out on his great journey, on Niśākara having gone to heaven, I distracted with various thoughts, have been consumed by grief. For the loss of my plumage.-

verses.sanskrit:
उत्थितां मरणे बुद्धिं मुनि वाक्यैर्निवर्तये
बुद्धिर्या तेन मे दत्ता प्राणसंरक्षणाय तु
सा मेऽपनयते दुःखं दीप्तेवाग्निशिखा तमः
verses.transliteration:
utthitāṁ maraṇe buddhiṁ muni vākyairnivartaye
buddhiryā tena me dattā prāṇasaṁrakṣaṇāya tu
sā me'panayate duḥkhaṁ dīptevāgniśikhā tamaḥ

translations.english: My rising intention of doing away with myself I have suppressed in consideration of the words of the ascetic. The reason which he had imparted to me for preserving my life, has removed my pains even as a flaming fire (dispels darkness).

verses.sanskrit:
बुध्यता च मया वीर्यं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
पुत्रः संतर्जितो वाग्भिर्न त्राता मैथिली कथम्
verses.transliteration:
budhyatā ca mayā vīryaṁ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
putraḥ saṁtarjito vāgbhirna trātā maithilī katham

translations.english: And knowing the prowess of the impious Rāvana, I said in rage to my son, versed in speech,-'Hearing her lamentation, and knowing them bereft of Sītā, why didst you not deliver her?'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या विलपितं श्रुत्वा तौ च सीता विनाकृतौ
न मे दशरथस्नेहात्पुत्रेणोत्पादितं प्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyā vilapitaṁ śrutvā tau ca sītā vinākṛtau
na me daśarathasnehātputreṇotpāditaṁ priyam

translations.english: My son did not do this good office to Daſaratha, influenced by affection for him.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य संपातेर्वानरैः सह
उत्पेततुस्तदा पक्षौ समक्षं वनचारिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tvevaṁ bruvāṇasya saṁpātervānaraiḥ saha
utpetatustadā pakṣau samakṣaṁ vanacāriṇām

translations.english: As he was speaking thus in the midst of the monkeys, his wings sprang up in presence of the rangers of the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा स्वां तनुं पक्षैरुद्गतैररुणच्छदैः
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे वानरांश्चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā svāṁ tanuṁ pakṣairudgatairaruṇacchadaiḥ
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe vānarāṁścedamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon, seeing his person furnished with grown pinions hued like the infant sun, he experienced incomparable raptures, and addressed the monkeys, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
निशाकरस्य महर्षेः प्रभावादमितात्मनः
आदित्यरश्मिनिर्दग्धौ पक्षौ मे पुनरुत्थितौ
verses.transliteration:
niśākarasya maharṣeḥ prabhāvādamitātmanaḥ
ādityaraśminirdagdhau pakṣau me punarutthitau

translations.english: By the grace of that Rājarși of immeasurable energy, my wings, which had been burnt up by the rays of the sun, have grown again.

verses.sanskrit:
यौवने वर्तमानस्य ममासीद्यः पराक्रमः
तमेवाद्यावगच्छामि बलं पौरुषमेव च
verses.transliteration:
yauvane vartamānasya mamāsīdyaḥ parākramaḥ
tamevādyāvagacchāmi balaṁ pauruṣameva ca

translations.english: To-day I have got back) the strength and prowess which I possessed while my youth was yet present.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा क्रियतां यत्नः सीतामधिगमिष्यथ
पक्षलाभो ममायं वः सिद्धिप्रत्यय कारकः
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā kriyatāṁ yatnaḥ sītāmadhigamiṣyatha
pakṣalābho mamāyaṁ vaḥ siddhipratyaya kārakaḥ

translations.english: Do you strive every way. You shall meet with Sītā. And my getting (back) my wings inspires (us) with confidence as to success.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा तान्हरीन्सर्वान्संपातिः पततां वरः
उत्पपात गिरेः शृङ्गाज्जिज्ञासुः खगमो गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā tānharīnsarvānsaṁpātiḥ patatāṁ varaḥ
utpapāta gireḥ śṛṅgājjijñāsuḥ khagamo gatim

translations.english: Having said this to all the monkeys, that ranger of the sky and best of birds. Sampāti, anxious to ascertain his power of flight, flew up from the mountain summits.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतिसंहृष्टमानसाः
बभूवुर्हरिशार्दूला विक्रमाभ्युदयोन्मुखाः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā prītisaṁhṛṣṭamānasāḥ
babhūvurhariśārdūlā vikramābhyudayonmukhāḥ

translations.english: Hearing his words, those powerful monkeys, with vigour (enhanced, seeing success before them, felt the height of joy.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ पवनसमानविक्रमाः; प्लवगवराः प्रतिलब्ध पौरुषाः
अभिजिदभिमुखां दिशं ययु;र्जनकसुता परिमार्गणोन्मुखाः
verses.transliteration:
atha pavanasamānavikramāḥ; plavagavarāḥ pratilabdha pauruṣāḥ
abhijidabhimukhāṁ diśaṁ yayu;rjanakasutā parimārgaṇonmukhāḥ

translations.english: Then those foremost of monkeys, in vigour resembling the Wind, getting occasion for displaying their prowess, intent upon searching the Janaka's daughter, set forward towards the quarter crested by Abhijit.* * Abhijitabhimukhan (acc.) Abhijit—the name of a star. Abhijit may also mean-he who is to be conquered. Then the sense would be the region in which Rāvana was.

verses.sanskrit:
आख्याता गृध्रराजेन समुत्पत्य प्लवंगमाः
संगताः प्रीतिसंयुक्ता विनेदुः सिंहविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
ākhyātā gṛdhrarājena samutpatya plavaṁgamāḥ
saṁgatāḥ prītisaṁyuktā vineduḥ siṁhavikramāḥ

translations.english: Having heard all this related to them by the vulture-king, the monkeys possessing the strength of lions, filled with delight, bounded and set up a roar.

verses.sanskrit:
संपातेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयो रावणक्षयम्
हृष्टाः सागरमाजग्मुः सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpātervacanaṁ śrutvā harayo rāvaṇakṣayam
hṛṣṭāḥ sāgaramājagmuḥ sītādarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing from Sampāti that Rāvana was to be slain, the monkeys growing glad, came to the ocean, with the desire of seeing Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिक्रम्य तु तं देशं ददृशुर्भीमविक्रमाः
कृत्स्नं लोकस्य महतः प्रतिबिम्बमिव स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
abhikramya tu taṁ deśaṁ dadṛśurbhīmavikramāḥ
kṛtsnaṁ lokasya mahataḥ pratibimbamiva sthitam

translations.english: Coming to that country, these ones processing dreadful prowess, beheld (the sea) reflecting the image of this entire mighty world.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य समासाद्योत्तरां दिशम्
संनिवेशं ततश्चक्रुः सहिता वानरोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇasya samudrasya samāsādyottarāṁ diśam
saṁniveśaṁ tataścakruḥ sahitā vānarottamāḥ

translations.english: Arriving at the northern side of the Southern sea, those exceedingly powerful heroic monkeys took up their quarters there.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसुप्तमिव चान्यत्र क्रीडन्तमिव चान्यतः
क्वचित्पर्वतमात्रैश्च जलराशिभिरावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
prasuptamiva cānyatra krīḍantamiva cānyataḥ
kvacitparvatamātraiśca jalarāśibhirāvṛtam

translations.english: Seeing the sea, here as if asleep, there, as if playful, and at another place with surges measuring mountains; and thronged with the foremost Dānavas inhabiting the nether regions; and capable of causing one's hair to stand on end, those powerful monkeys were seized with sadness.

verses.sanskrit:
आकाशमिव दुष्पारं सागरं प्रेक्ष्य वानराः
विषेदुः सहसा सर्वे कथं कार्यमिति ब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
ākāśamiva duṣpāraṁ sāgaraṁ prekṣya vānarāḥ
viṣeduḥ sahasā sarve kathaṁ kāryamiti bruvan

translations.english: Seeing the sea, incapable of being crossed even as the sky, all the monkeys began to lament, saying,-What is to be done?

verses.sanskrit:
विषण्णां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा सागरस्य निरीक्षणात्
आश्वासयामास हरीन्भयार्तान्हरिसत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
viṣaṇṇāṁ vāhinīṁ dṛṣṭvā sāgarasya nirīkṣaṇāt
āśvāsayāmāsa harīnbhayārtānharisattamaḥ

translations.english: That best of monkeys-(Angada), seeing the army cast down because of the sight of the sea, began to comfort the monkeys, afflicted with fear.

verses.sanskrit:
न निषादेन नः कार्यं विषादो दोषवत्तरः
विषादो हन्ति पुरुषं बालं क्रुद्ध इवोरगः
verses.transliteration:
na niṣādena naḥ kāryaṁ viṣādo doṣavattaraḥ
viṣādo hanti puruṣaṁ bālaṁ kruddha ivoragaḥ

translations.english: We should not indulge in grief. Grief is injurious.-Grief destroys a person even as a wrathful serpent does a boy.

verses.sanskrit:
विषादोऽयं प्रसहते विक्रमे पर्युपस्थिते
तेजसा तस्य हीनस्य पुरुषार्थो न सिध्यति
verses.transliteration:
viṣādo'yaṁ prasahate vikrame paryupasthite
tejasā tasya hīnasya puruṣārtho na sidhyati

translations.english: He that, when the time is come for displaying his prowess, indulges in sorrow, growing weak in energy, fails to attain his objects.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामङ्गदो वानरैः सह
हरिवृद्धैः समागम्य पुनर्मन्त्रममन्त्रयत्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ rātryāṁ vyatītāyāmaṅgado vānaraiḥ saha
harivṛddhaiḥ samāgamya punarmantramamantrayat

translations.english: That night having passed away, Angada in company with the monkeys, joined by the old ones, again took counsel with them.

verses.sanskrit:
सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी परिवार्याङ्गदं बभौ
वासवं परिवार्येव मरुतां वाहिनी स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
sā vānarāṇāṁ dhvajinī parivāryāṅgadaṁ babhau
vāsavaṁ parivāryeva marutāṁ vāhinī sthitā

translations.english: That monkey-host surrounding Angada, resembled the host of Maruts environing Vasava.

verses.sanskrit:
कोऽन्यस्तां वानरीं सेनां शक्तः स्तम्भयितुं भवेत्
अन्यत्र वालितनयादन्यत्र च हनूमतः
verses.transliteration:
ko'nyastāṁ vānarīṁ senāṁ śaktaḥ stambhayituṁ bhavet
anyatra vālitanayādanyatra ca hanūmataḥ

translations.english: Who save Väli's son (stationed) at one place and at another Hanumān, could be capable of stilling that force?

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तान्हरिवृद्धांश्च तच्च सैन्यमरिंदमः
अनुमान्याङ्गदः श्रीमान्वाक्यमर्थवदब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastānharivṛddhāṁśca tacca sainyamariṁdamaḥ
anumānyāṅgadaḥ śrīmānvākyamarthavadabravīt

translations.english: Then saluting the elders as well as army, the-graceful Angada-repressor of foes-~-spoke words fraught with sense,

verses.sanskrit:
क इदानीं महातेजा लङ्घयिष्यति सागरम्
कः करिष्यति सुग्रीवं सत्यसंधमरिंदमम्
verses.transliteration:
ka idānīṁ mahātejā laṅghayiṣyati sāgaram
kaḥ kariṣyati sugrīvaṁ satyasaṁdhamariṁdamam

translations.english: What person, endued with exceeding energy, shall now leap over the main? Who shall serve that subduer of enemies, Sugrīva, ever intent on truth?

verses.sanskrit:
को वीरो योजनशतं लङ्घयेत प्लवंगमाः
इमांश्च यूथपान्सर्वान्मोचयेत्को महाभयात्
verses.transliteration:
ko vīro yojanaśataṁ laṅghayeta plavaṁgamāḥ
imāṁśca yūthapānsarvānmocayetko mahābhayāt

translations.english: What monkey can leap over an hundred Yojanas? Who shall deliver leaders of herds from a mighty fear?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्य प्रसादाद्दारांश्च पुत्रांश्चैव गृहाणि च
इतो निवृत्ताः पश्येम सिद्धार्थाः सुखिनो वयम्
verses.transliteration:
kasya prasādāddārāṁśca putrāṁścaiva gṛhāṇi ca
ito nivṛttāḥ paśyema siddhārthāḥ sukhino vayam

translations.english: By whose favour shall we, crowned with success and rendered happy, returning from this place, shall behold our wives and our son, and our homes?

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा न कश्चित्किंचिदब्रवीत्
स्तिमितेवाभवत्सर्वा सा तत्र हरिवाहिनी
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā na kaścitkiṁcidabravīt
stimitevābhavatsarvā sā tatra harivāhinī

translations.english: By whose favour shall we joyfully meet Rama, and the mighty Laksmana, and that dweller in the woods, Sugrīva? If any monkey among you is competent to bound over the deep, let him at once confer on us Dakșină in the shape of deliverance from fear. Hearing Angada's speech, none said anything, And that host off monkeys wavered.

verses.sanskrit:
पुनरेवाङ्गदः प्राह तान्हरीन्हरिसत्तमः
सर्वे बलवतां श्रेष्ठा भवन्तो दृढविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
punarevāṅgadaḥ prāha tānharīnharisattamaḥ
sarve balavatāṁ śreṣṭhā bhavanto dṛḍhavikramāḥ

translations.english: Then that foremost of monkeys addressed those monkeys, saying-All of you are the foremost of strong ones, and of steady prowess. And you have sprung in blameless lines, and are ever honoured (by the king).

verses.sanskrit: ब्रुवध्वं यस्य या शक्तिर्गमने प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration: bruvadhvaṁ yasya yā śaktirgamane plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And yet no one of you can promise to undertake this journey? You best of monkeys, unfold your respective powers in bounding.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽङ्गदवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते वानरोत्तमाः
स्वं स्वं गतौ समुत्साहमाहुस्तत्र यथाक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'ṅgadavacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānarottamāḥ
svaṁ svaṁ gatau samutsāhamāhustatra yathākramam

translations.english: Hearing Angada's speech, those foremost monkeys one after another began to speak, touching their respective competence in coursing.

verses.sanskrit:
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव सुषेणो जाम्बवांस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
maindaśca dvividaścaiva suṣeṇo jāmbavāṁstathā

translations.english: Gaja, and Gavākṣa, and Gavaya, and Sarabha, and Gandhamādana, and Mainda, and Dwivida, and Angada, and Jāmbavān.

verses.sanskrit:
आबभाषे गजस्तत्र प्लवेयं दशयोजनम्
गवाक्षो योजनान्याह गमिष्यामीति विंशतिम्
verses.transliteration:
ābabhāṣe gajastatra plaveyaṁ daśayojanam
gavākṣo yojanānyāha gamiṣyāmīti viṁśatim

translations.english: Gaja said, “I can leap over ten Yojanas," and Gavaksa said, "I shall go twenty Yojanas."

verses.sanskrit:
गवयो वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह
त्रिंशतं तु गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
gavayo vānarastatra vānarāṁstānuvāca ha
triṁśataṁ tu gamiṣyāmi yojanānāṁ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: There monkey Sarabha said to those monkeys, “You monkey, I shall go thirty Yojanas."

verses.sanskrit:
शरभो वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह
चत्वारिंशद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
śarabho vānarastatra vānarāṁstānuvāca ha
catvāriṁśadgamiṣyāmi yojanānāṁ na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: And the monkey, Rhishava, said to those monkeys,-"I shall, without doubt, go forty Yojanas."

verses.sanskrit:
वानरांस्तु महातेजा अब्रवीद्गन्धमादनः
योजनानां गमिष्यामि पञ्चाशत्तु न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
vānarāṁstu mahātejā abravīdgandhamādanaḥ
yojanānāṁ gamiṣyāmi pañcāśattu na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: And the exceedingly energetic monkey, Gandhamädana, said, I shall for certain go fifty Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
मैन्दस्तु वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह
योजनानां परं षष्टिमहं प्लवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
maindastu vānarastatra vānarāṁstānuvāca ha
yojanānāṁ paraṁ ṣaṣṭimahaṁ plavitumutsahe

translations.english: And the monkey Mainda said to the monkeys there, I shall undertake to leap over sixty Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तत्र महातेजा द्विविदः प्रत्यभाषत
गमिष्यामि न संदेहः सप्ततिं योजनान्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastatra mahātejā dvividaḥ pratyabhāṣata
gamiṣyāmi na saṁdehaḥ saptatiṁ yojanānyaham

translations.english: And then the highly energetic Dwivida said,-I Shall, for certain, go seventy Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
सुषेणस्तु हरिश्रेष्ठः प्रोक्तवान्कपिसत्तमान्
अशीतिं योजनानां तु प्लवेयं प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
suṣeṇastu hariśreṣṭhaḥ proktavānkapisattamān
aśītiṁ yojanānāṁ tu plaveyaṁ plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And the highly powerful Suşena, possessed of strength-foremost of monkeys said—I declare that in motion I am equal to eighty Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां कथयतां तत्र सर्वांस्ताननुमान्य च
ततो वृद्धतमस्तेषां जाम्बवान्प्रत्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ kathayatāṁ tatra sarvāṁstānanumānya ca
tato vṛddhatamasteṣāṁ jāmbavānpratyabhāṣata

translations.english: As they were speaking thus,' the oldest of them all, Jambavān, saluting them answered.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वमस्माकमप्यासीत्कश्चिद्गतिपराक्रमः
ते वयं वयसः पारमनुप्राप्ताः स्म साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
pūrvamasmākamapyāsītkaścidgatiparākramaḥ
te vayaṁ vayasaḥ pāramanuprāptāḥ sma sāmpratam

translations.english: Formerly we had power of motion. But now we have waxed exceeding old. Although this is so, yet we can not overlook this, as both Rama and the monkey-king (by sending us) have become sure of success. At present do you understand the course that is ours. I shall go ninety Yojanas. There is no doubt whatever about this.

verses.sanskrit:
तांश्च सर्वान्हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवान्पुनरब्रवीत्
न खल्वेतावदेवासीद्गमने मे पराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁśca sarvānhariśreṣṭhāñjāmbavānpunarabravīt
na khalvetāvadevāsīdgamane me parākramaḥ

translations.english: Jāmbavān said this to those choice monkeys. But (formerly) my prowess in leaping was forsooth not such.* Of old in the sacrifice of Virocana's son, the external Lord Visnu, when he had covered the entire universe with three steps, was circumambulated by me. *i.e. it was greater.

verses.sanskrit:
स इदानीमहं वृद्धः प्लवने मन्दविक्रमः
यौवने च तदासीन्मे बलमप्रतिमं परैः
verses.transliteration:
sa idānīmahaṁ vṛddhaḥ plavane mandavikramaḥ
yauvane ca tadāsīnme balamapratimaṁ paraiḥ

translations.english: But I who was all this, have waxed old, and my vigour sits feebly upon me. In my youth, ever, my strength was exceeding great and incomparable.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रत्येतावतीं शक्तिं गमने तर्कयाम्यहम्
नैतावता च संसिद्धिः कार्यस्यास्य भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
saṁpratyetāvatīṁ śaktiṁ gamane tarkayāmyaham
naitāvatā ca saṁsiddhiḥ kāryasyāsya bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Now I can only by my own energy, course thus far. But has a bound shall not bring success on our undertaking.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोत्तरमुदारार्थमब्रवीदङ्गदस्तदा
अनुमान्य महाप्राज्ञो जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिम्
verses.transliteration:
athottaramudārārthamabravīdaṅgadastadā
anumānya mahāprājño jāmbavantaṁ mahākapim

translations.english: After this, saluting the mighty monkey, Jāmbavān, the wise Angada spoke straight sense, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अहमेतद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां शतं महत्
निवर्तने तु मे शक्तिः स्यान्न वेति न निश्चितम्
verses.transliteration:
ahametadgamiṣyāmi yojanānāṁ śataṁ mahat
nivartane tu me śaktiḥ syānna veti na niścitam

translations.english: I can go over this mighty hundred Yojanas; but there is no certainty as to my answer of returning.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं शतसहस्रं वा न ह्येष विधिरुच्यते
योजनानां भवाञ्शक्तो गन्तुं प्रतिनिवर्तितुम्
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ śatasahasraṁ vā na hyeṣa vidhirucyate
yojanānāṁ bhavāñśakto gantuṁ pratinivartitum

translations.english: Thereat, Jāmbavān, cognizant of speech, said to that foremost of monkeys,-0 foremost of leonine as, we know your power of motion, you are capable of ursing a hundred thousand Yojanas, as well as of coming back. But we say that even this is what is fit.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि प्रेषयिता तत स्वामी प्रेष्यः कथंचन
भवतायं जनः सर्वः प्रेष्यः प्लवगसत्तम
verses.transliteration:
na hi preṣayitā tata svāmī preṣyaḥ kathaṁcana
bhavatāyaṁ janaḥ sarvaḥ preṣyaḥ plavagasattama

translations.english: My child, ore master must on no account be commanded by his servants. foremost of monkeys, all these should be commanded your you.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्कलत्रमस्माकं स्वामिभावे व्यवस्थितः
स्वामी कलत्रं सैन्यस्य गतिरेषा परंतप
verses.transliteration:
bhavānkalatramasmākaṁ svāmibhāve vyavasthitaḥ
svāmī kalatraṁ sainyasya gatireṣā paraṁtapa

translations.english: You are our spouse, and (at the same time) occuying the position of our husband. The master is the spouse if the army. This is the way of the world.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्कलत्रवत्तात प्रतिपाल्यः सदा भवान्
अपि चैतस्य कार्यस्य भवान्मूलमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
tasmātkalatravattāta pratipālyaḥ sadā bhavān
api caitasya kāryasya bhavānmūlamariṁdama

translations.english: O repressor of oes! O subduer of enemies, you are the root of this business. Therefore, my child, you should always be maintained by us like a wife.

verses.sanskrit:
मूलमर्थस्य संरक्ष्यमेष कार्यविदां नयः
मूले हि सति सिध्यन्ति गुणाः पुष्पफलादयः
verses.transliteration:
mūlamarthasya saṁrakṣyameṣa kāryavidāṁ nayaḥ
mūle hi sati sidhyanti guṇāḥ puṣpaphalādayaḥ

translations.english: The root of any work must be preserved. This is the policy of those versed in business. The root existing, all the virtues, obtaining fruit, certainly meet with success.

verses.sanskrit:
गुरुश्च गुरुपुत्रश्च त्वं हि नः कपिसत्तम
भवन्तमाश्रित्य वयं समर्था ह्यर्थसाधने
verses.transliteration:
guruśca guruputraśca tvaṁ hi naḥ kapisattama
bhavantamāśritya vayaṁ samarthā hyarthasādhane

translations.english: You, O you having truth for prowess are the instrument of this undertaking, and, O subduer of enemies, furnished with sense and vigour, you are the occasion herein. And, O foremost of monkeys, you are both our superior, and our superior's son; and resorting to you we are enabled to accomplish our object.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तवाक्यं महाप्राज्ञं जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः
प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वाक्यं वालिसूनुरथाङ्गदः
verses.transliteration:
uktavākyaṁ mahāprājñaṁ jāmbavantaṁ mahākapiḥ
pratyuvācottaraṁ vākyaṁ vālisūnurathāṅgadaḥ

translations.english: Threat that mighty monkey, Angada, son to Vali, answered the exceedingly wise Jambavan, when he had spoken,

verses.sanskrit:
यदि नाहं गमिष्यामि नान्यो वानरपुंगवः
पुनः खल्विदमस्माभिः कार्यं प्रायोपवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
yadi nāhaṁ gamiṣyāmi nānyo vānarapuṁgavaḥ
punaḥ khalvidamasmābhiḥ kāryaṁ prāyopaveśanam

translations.english: If I go not, nor any other powerful monkey, then we should for certain again sit ourselves down to fast to death.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यकृत्वा हरिपतेः संदेशं तस्य धीमतः
तत्रापि गत्वा प्राणानां पश्यामि परिरक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
na hyakṛtvā haripateḥ saṁdeśaṁ tasya dhīmataḥ
tatrāpi gatvā prāṇānāṁ paśyāmi parirakṣaṇam

translations.english: Without doing the mandate of the intelligent lord of monkeys, we, repairing thither, shall not behold ourselves alive.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि प्रसादे चात्यर्थं कोपे च हरिरीश्वरः
अतीत्य तस्य संदेशं विनाशो गमने भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
sa hi prasāde cātyarthaṁ kope ca harirīśvaraḥ
atītya tasya saṁdeśaṁ vināśo gamane bhavet

translations.english: He is extreme both in showing favour and in anger. Disregarding his order, we shall, going there, meet with destruction. And his ire shall, not take any other course.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्यथा ह्यस्य कार्यस्य न भवत्यन्यथा गतिः
तद्भवानेव दृष्टार्थः संचिन्तयितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
tadyathā hyasya kāryasya na bhavatyanyathā gatiḥ
tadbhavāneva dṛṣṭārthaḥ saṁcintayitumarhati

translations.english: Therefore it behoves you, cap of seeing issues, to reflect.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽङ्गदेन तदा वीरः प्रत्युक्तः प्लवगर्षभः
जाम्बवानुत्तरं वाक्यं प्रोवाचेदं ततोऽङ्गदम्
verses.transliteration:
so'ṅgadena tadā vīraḥ pratyuktaḥ plavagarṣabhaḥ
jāmbavānuttaraṁ vākyaṁ provācedaṁ tato'ṅgadam

translations.english: Thus addressed by Angada that powerful and heroic monkey Jāmbavān answered Angada in excellent words, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य ते वीर कार्यस्य न किंचित्परिहीयते
एष संचोदयाम्येनं यः कार्यं साधयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
asya te vīra kāryasya na kiṁcitparihīyate
eṣa saṁcodayāmyenaṁ yaḥ kāryaṁ sādhayiṣyati

translations.english: That. business, O hero, say most moult a feather. I shall despatch even him who's bring about success.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रतीतं प्लवतां वरिष्ठ;मेकान्तमाश्रित्य सुखोपविष्टम्
संचोदयामास हरिप्रवीरो; हरिप्रवीरं हनुमन्तमेव
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pratītaṁ plavatāṁ variṣṭha;mekāntamāśritya sukhopaviṣṭam
saṁcodayāmāsa haripravīro; haripravīraṁ hanumantameva

translations.english: Then that heroic monkey ordered foremost of monkeys, the highly heroic monkey Hanuman who stood apart, convinced (of the wisdom of Jambavān decision).

verses.sanskrit:
अनेकशतसाहस्रीं विषण्णां हरिवाहिनीम्
जाम्बवान्समुदीक्ष्यैवं हनुमन्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
anekaśatasāhasrīṁ viṣaṇṇāṁ harivāhinīm
jāmbavānsamudīkṣyaivaṁ hanumantamathābravīt

translations.english: Surveying the monkey-host consisting of many hundred and thousand,-crest-fallen, Jämbavān thus spoke to Hanumān,

verses.sanskrit:
वीर वानरलोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविदां वर
तूष्णीमेकान्तमाश्रित्य हनुमन्किं न जल्पसि
verses.transliteration:
vīra vānaralokasya sarvaśāstravidāṁ vara
tūṣṇīmekāntamāśritya hanumankiṁ na jalpasi

translations.english: O hero among the monkey-multitude, O be of those versed in all branches of learning, staying apart silent, why did you not speak?

verses.sanskrit:
हनुमन्हरिराजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो ह्यसि
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि तेजसा च बलेन च
verses.transliteration:
hanumanharirājasya sugrīvasya samo hyasi
rāmalakṣmaṇayoścāpi tejasā ca balena ca

translations.english: O Hanuman, you are alil in energy and strength, equal to Sugriva, monarch monkeys, and to Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रौ वैनतेयो महाबलः
गरुत्मानिव विख्यात उत्तमः सर्वपक्षिणाम्
verses.transliteration:
ariṣṭaneminaḥ putrau vainateyo mahābalaḥ
garutmāniva vikhyāta uttamaḥ sarvapakṣiṇām

translations.english: Aristanemi's son the mighty Vainateya,* famous by the cognomen of Garutmā, is the foremost of birds. *Offspring of Vinatā, Garura's mother.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः
भुजगानुद्धरन्पक्षी महावेगो महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
bahuśo hi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sāgare sa mahābalaḥ
bhujagānuddharanpakṣī mahāvego mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Many a time and oft. I have see that exceedingly powerful, mighty-armed one, endowed with strength of will,-raise up serpents in the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
पक्षयोर्यद्बलं तस्य तावद्भुजबलं तव
विक्रमश्चापि वेगश्च न ते तेनापहीयते
verses.transliteration:
pakṣayoryadbalaṁ tasya tāvadbhujabalaṁ tava
vikramaścāpi vegaśca na te tenāpahīyate

translations.english: The strength that is in his wings, is equal to the might and virtues your arm.

verses.sanskrit:
बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिसत्तम
विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न बुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
balaṁ buddhiśca tejaśca sattvaṁ ca harisattama
viśiṣṭaṁ sarvabhūteṣu kimātmānaṁ na budhyase

translations.english: Your energy and prowess are not surpassed by him And your strength, and your understanding, your energy, and your vigour, O foremost of monkeys, (is known among all creatures). Why did not you prepare yourself furnished with everything that is noble or great, (for this feat)?

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या वस्त्रं विशालाक्ष्याः पीतं रक्तदशं शुभम्
स्थितायाः पर्वतस्याग्रे मारुतोऽपहरच्छनैः
verses.transliteration:
tasyā vastraṁ viśālākṣyāḥ pītaṁ raktadaśaṁ śubham
sthitāyāḥ parvatasyāgre māruto'paharacchanaiḥ

translations.english: It came moss that as that one of expansive eyes was standing on the mit of the mount, the Wind gently stole away her elegant bow cloth with crimson skirts.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां भुजाभ्यां पीनाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः
मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ bhujābhyāṁ pīnābhyāṁ paryaṣvajata mārutaḥ
manmathāviṣṭasarvāṅgo gatātmā tāmaninditām

translations.english: He had a sight of her and fine face, together with her well-developed breasts. As soon as the Wind saw that illustrious one of spacious and slender waist, and whose every limb was lovely,-was amain overcome by desire. And all his frame sessed by Manmatha, and deprived of self, the Wind emced that blameless one by means of his long arms.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु तत्रैव संभ्रान्ता सुवृत्ता वाक्यमब्रवीत्
एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
sā tu tatraiva saṁbhrāntā suvṛttā vākyamabravīt
ekapatnīvratamidaṁ ko nāśayitumicchati

translations.english: There influenced by fear, that one of excellent vows said,-no is it that desireth to lay violent hands upon my chastity?

verses.sanskrit:
अञ्जनाया वचः श्रुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत
न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्
verses.transliteration:
añjanāyā vacaḥ śrutvā mārutaḥ pratyabhāṣata
na tvāṁ hiṁsāmi suśroṇi mā bhūtte subhage bhayam

translations.english: Hearing Anjana's words, the Wind answered, do not wrong you, O you of shapely hips. Let not her enter your heart.

verses.sanskrit:
मनसास्मि गतो यत्त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनि
वीर्यवान्बुद्धिसंपन्नः पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
manasāsmi gato yattvāṁ pariṣvajya yaśasvini
vīryavānbuddhisaṁpannaḥ putrastava bhaviṣyati

translations.english: As, O famous damsel, by embracing the, I have mentally entered into your womb, you shall her a son, intelligent and endued with prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्युत्थितं ततः सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने
फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्यपतो दिवम्
verses.transliteration:
abhyutthitaṁ tataḥ sūryaṁ bālo dṛṣṭvā mahāvane
phalaṁ ceti jighṛkṣustvamutplutyābhyapato divam

translations.english: In that mighty forest, you, a child, desirous of eating, seeing the sun risen, and taking on to be a fruit, sprang up and leaped into the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाथ योजनानां महाकपे
तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं ततो गतः
verses.transliteration:
śatāni trīṇi gatvātha yojanānāṁ mahākape
tejasā tasya nirdhūto na viṣādaṁ tato gataḥ

translations.english: O mighty monkey, going three thousand Yojanas, you, struck by as energy, didst not feel poverty of spirit.

verses.sanskrit:
तावदापततस्तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे
क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं क्रोधाविष्टेन धीमता
verses.transliteration:
tāvadāpatatastūrṇamantarikṣaṁ mahākape
kṣiptamindreṇa te vajraṁ krodhāviṣṭena dhīmatā

translations.english: And, seeing you shing through the heavens, O mighty monkey, Indra, owing wrath, hurled his thunder-bolt at you.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत
ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्त्यते
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śailāgraśikhare vāmo hanurabhajyata
tato hi nāmadheyaṁ te hanumāniti kīrtyate

translations.english: Thereat, breaking your left jaw, you (didst fall) on the mountain From this circumstance, your name has been known Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वां निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहः स्वयम्
त्रैलोक्ये भृशसंक्रुद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः
verses.transliteration:
tatastvāṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā vāyurgandhavahaḥ svayam
trailokye bhṛśasaṁkruddho na vavau vai prabhañjanaḥ

translations.english: Witnessing you beaten back, that bearer of fumes himself, the Wind, that breaketh everything before in wrath did not blow through the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
संभ्रान्ताश्च सुराः सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति
प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः
verses.transliteration:
saṁbhrāntāśca surāḥ sarve trailokye kṣubhite sati
prasādayanti saṁkruddhaṁ mārutaṁ bhuvaneśvarāḥ

translations.english: Thereat, all gods-lords of the universeinfluenced by fear in consequence of the triune world waxing agitated, began to path the wrathful Wind.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ
अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम
verses.transliteration:
prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyaṁ varaṁ dadau
aśastravadhyatāṁ tāta samare satyavikrama

translations.english: And on the Wind being mollified, Bra conferred on him a boon, saying,–O child, O you of prowess, (your son) shall be incapable of being slain in be by means of weapons.'

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च
सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
vajrasya ca nipātena virujaṁ tvāṁ samīkṣya ca
sahasranetraḥ prītātmā dadau te varamuttamam

translations.english: And seeing him sustain (serious) injury consequent on the impact of the thunder. He of a thousand eyes, pleased in his soul, also confer on (you) and excellent boon, O lord, saying, 'Your death: take place according to your will.' *Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं ते भूयादिति वै प्रभो
स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
svacchandataśca maraṇaṁ te bhūyāditi vai prabho
sa tvaṁ kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīmavikramaḥ

translations.english: You, endowed with drawful vigour, are the son of Kesarī by his wife; and, resemble the Wind in energy, you had sprung from his loins.

verses.sanskrit:
वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवानस्मासु साम्प्रतम्
दाक्ष्यविक्रमसंपन्नः पक्षिराज इवापरः
verses.transliteration:
vayamadya gataprāṇā bhavānasmāsu sāmpratam
dākṣyavikramasaṁpannaḥ pakṣirāja ivāparaḥ

translations.english: The are the son of the Wind, my child-equal to him in power of leaping. Now we are without our lives. And you, endowed with dexterity and vigour, and like another I of the monkeys,+ are before us. *Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
trivikrame mayā tāta saśailavanakānanā
triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī parikrāntā pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: On the occasion of Vişnu enveloping the earth with three steps, I, O child, had circa ambulated the earth with her mountains, woods and fore one and twenty times.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा चौषधयोऽस्माभिः संचिता देवशासनात्
निष्पन्नममृतं याभिस्तदासीन्नो महद्बलम्
verses.transliteration:
tadā cauṣadhayo'smābhiḥ saṁcitā devaśāsanāt
niṣpannamamṛtaṁ yābhistadāsīnno mahadbalam

translations.english: Then, commissioned by the gods, had gathered annuals, which (bcing cast on the deep), cat ambrosia to come out after churning. At that time, god was our strength.

verses.sanskrit:
स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः
साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान्सर्वगुणान्वितः
verses.transliteration:
sa idānīmahaṁ vṛddhaḥ parihīnaparākramaḥ
sāmprataṁ kālamasmākaṁ bhavānsarvaguṇānvitaḥ

translations.english: But now I have grown old, and prowess has left me. At present we have you, furnish with every virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्तः प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि
त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामेयं सर्वा वानरवाहिनी
verses.transliteration:
tadvijṛmbhasva vikrāntaḥ plavatāmuttamo hyasi
tvadvīryaṁ draṣṭukāmeyaṁ sarvā vānaravāhinī

translations.english: Therefore, possessed of vigour, do I bestir yourself, and bound over (the main). You are the qualified of all. This entire monkey host is eager to bell your prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्
परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन्या गतिस्तव
verses.transliteration:
uttiṣṭha hariśārdūla laṅghayasva mahārṇavam
parā hi sarvabhūtānāṁ hanumanyā gatistava

translations.english: O redoubtable monkey, do you arise! leap over the mighty ocean. Your motion, Hanumān, asseth that of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
विषाण्णा हरयः सर्वे हनुमन्किमुपेक्षसे
विक्रमस्व महावेगो विष्णुस्त्रीन्विक्रमानिव
verses.transliteration:
viṣāṇṇā harayaḥ sarve hanumankimupekṣase
vikramasva mahāvego viṣṇustrīnvikramāniva

translations.english: All the monkeys are depressed. O Hanuman, did you overlook this? Put forth your you endowed with mighty vehemence, like Vişnu sing over the three worlds in three steps.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु वै जाम्बवताभिचोदितः; प्रतीतवेगः पवनात्मजः कपिः
प्रहर्षयंस्तां हरिवीर वाहिनीं; चकार रूपं महदात्मनस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tatastu vai jāmbavatābhicoditaḥ; pratītavegaḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ
praharṣayaṁstāṁ harivīra vāhinīṁ; cakāra rūpaṁ mahadātmanastadā

translations.english: Exhorted by foremost of monkeys, that one famed for has speech, that key, the offspring of the Wind-god, gladdening the monkey-chiefs, wore (a fit) shape for crossing the ocean.* *Another epithet of Hanumān, Pavanātmaja-son to the Wind?? on the score of Redundency.

verses.sanskrit:
संस्तूयमानो हनुमान्व्यवर्धत महाबलः
समाविध्य च लाङ्गूलं हर्षाच्च बलमेयिवान्
verses.transliteration:
saṁstūyamāno hanumānvyavardhata mahābalaḥ
samāvidhya ca lāṅgūlaṁ harṣācca balameyivān

translations.english: And, struck with amazement, they, (staying) all round, joyfully gazed (at him); even as creatures beheld Nārāyaṇa, then stretching forth his three steps, he prepared him (for the succeeding feat). And, eulogized by them, the odorous mighty Hanuman increased; and, flourishing his tail me joy, attained strength.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य सर्वैर्वानरपुंगवैः
तेजसापूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya saṁstūyamānasya sarvairvānarapuṁgavaiḥ
tejasāpūryamāṇasya rūpamāsīdanuttamam

translations.english: As, extolled by the principal derly monkeys, he became fraught with effulgence, his beauty as great..

verses.sanskrit:
यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृद्धो गिरिगह्वरे
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तथा संप्रति जृम्भते
verses.transliteration:
yathā vijṛmbhate siṁho vivṛddho girigahvare
mārutasyaurasaḥ putrastathā saṁprati jṛmbhate

translations.english: As a lion fills himself with vigour in an open we, so the son of the Wind-god filled himself with energy.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः
अम्बरीषोपमं दीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
aśobhata mukhaṁ tasya jṛmbhamāṇasya dhīmataḥ
ambarīṣopamaṁ dīptaṁ vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: The face of him, as that intelligent one was filling, himself has force was aflame like a frying-pan, or like to themeless fire.

verses.sanskrit:
हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात्संप्रहृष्टतनूरुहः
अभिवाद्य हरीन्वृद्धान्हनुमानिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
harīṇāmutthito madhyātsaṁprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ
abhivādya harīnvṛddhānhanumānidamabravīt

translations.english: Rising in the midst of the monkeys, Hanumān has his down standing on end through joy, saluting the monkeys, said,

verses.sanskrit:
अरुजन्पर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः
बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः
verses.transliteration:
arujanparvatāgrāṇi hutāśanasakho'nilaḥ
balavānaprameyaśca vāyurākāśagocaraḥ

translations.english: Wind, the friend of Fire, shattereth summits; and, [ever blowing in the eye of the sky, he is possessed of strength, and is of immeasure (might). Begot from his loins, I am the son of fast-coursing and high-souled Wind, coursing swiftly am his equal in all these accomplishments.* *i.e. pertaining to leaping.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे
समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्
verses.transliteration:
bāhuvegapraṇunnena sāgareṇāhamutsahe
samāplāvayituṁ lokaṁ saparvatanadīhradam

translations.english: I without once stopping, circumambulate the extensive heaven-cleaving mountain, Meru, for a thousand tin And, dashing the ocean with my arms, I can del the world with its mountains, rivers and lakes.

verses.sanskrit:
ममोरुजङ्घावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः
संमूर्छितमहाग्राहः समुद्रो वरुणालयः
verses.transliteration:
mamorujaṅghāvegena bhaviṣyati samutthitaḥ
saṁmūrchitamahāgrāhaḥ samudro varuṇālayaḥ

translations.english: Las by the force of my legs and thighs, that abode of Varuņa the sea, out which have sprung the ferocious aqua animals, overleaps its continents.

verses.sanskrit:
पन्नगाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेवितम्
वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
pannagāśanamākāśe patantaṁ pakṣisevitam
vainateyamahaṁ śaktaḥ parigantuṁ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And for once that lor birds, Vinata's offspring, living on serpents, courseth through the welkin, I can course through it a thousand times.

verses.sanskrit:
उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्
अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
udayātprasthitaṁ vāpi jvalantaṁ raśmimālinam
anastamitamādityamabhigantuṁ samutsahe

translations.english: And can touch the flaming effulgent Sun ere, beginning his jour from the Rising hill, he ascends the Setting hill. And, foremost of monkeys, I can, fiercely rushing on, come as without touching the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्
सागरं क्षोभयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
utsaheyamatikrāntuṁ sarvānākāśagocarān
sāgaraṁ kṣobhayiṣyāmi dārayiṣyāmi medinīm

translations.english: And I can bound beyound's and planets, suck up the oceans, and rive the earth. And a monkey, I can, leaping, crush mountains; and, leaping can drain the mighty ocean dry.

verses.sanskrit:
लतानां वीरुधां पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः
अनुयास्यति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा
भविष्यति हि मे पन्थाः स्वातेः पन्था इवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
latānāṁ vīrudhāṁ puṣpaṁ pādapānāṁ ca sarvaśaḥ
anuyāsyati māmadya plavamānaṁ vihāyasā
bhaviṣyati hi me panthāḥ svāteḥ panthā ivāmbare

translations.english: When I shall learing the sky, flowers from various shrubs and trees shall follow me to-day.

verses.sanskrit:
चरन्तं घोरमाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्तमेव च
द्रक्ष्यन्ति निपतन्तं च सर्वभूतानि वानराः
verses.transliteration:
carantaṁ ghoramākāśamutpatiṣyantameva ca
drakṣyanti nipatantaṁ ca sarvabhūtāni vānarāḥ

translations.english: And then my course, flecked with flowers), resemble even they sky (studded with stars). And, monkeys, then all creatures shall see me now ranging through the profound firmament, now shooting up, and now descending (on the other shore).

verses.sanskrit:
विधमिष्यामि जीमूतान्कम्पयिष्यामि पर्वतान्
सागरं क्षोभयिष्यामि प्लवमानः समाहितः
verses.transliteration:
vidhamiṣyāmi jīmūtānkampayiṣyāmi parvatān
sāgaraṁ kṣobhayiṣyāmi plavamānaḥ samāhitaḥ

translations.english: Resembling Mahāmeru, me shall behold, you monkeys, making my way, covering up sky, as if devouring up the heavens. I shall, leaping concentrating my energy, scatter the clouds, shake the I and suck up the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
वैनतेयस्य वा शक्तिर्मम वा मारुतस्य वा
ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाबलम्
न हि भूतं प्रपश्यामि यो मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
vainateyasya vā śaktirmama vā mārutasya vā
ṛte suparṇarājānaṁ mārutaṁ vā mahābalam
na hi bhūtaṁ prapaśyāmi yo māṁ plutamanuvrajet

translations.english: The strength of Vinata's son the Wind-god's, or mine, (surpasses that of every creature). None save the sovereign of birds, or the exceeding mighty Wind, can follow me in flight.

verses.sanskrit:
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण निरालम्भनमम्बरम्
सहसा निपतिष्यामि घनाद्विद्युदिवोत्थिता
verses.transliteration:
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa nirālambhanamambaram
sahasā nipatiṣyāmi ghanādvidyudivotthitā

translations.english: In the twing an eye I shall spread through the unsupported lightning darting from clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
भविष्यति हि मे रूपं प्लवमानस्य सागरम्
विष्णोः प्रक्रममाणस्य तदा त्रीन्विक्रमानिव
verses.transliteration:
bhaviṣyati hi me rūpaṁ plavamānasya sāgaram
viṣṇoḥ prakramamāṇasya tadā trīnvikramāniva

translations.english: And at the time of leaping over the ocean, my form shall resemble that of the energizing Vişņu, when He had assumed the triune energy.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्ध्या चाहं प्रपश्यामि मनश्चेष्टा च मे तथा
अहं द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं प्रमोदध्वं प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
buddhyā cāhaṁ prapaśyāmi manaśceṣṭā ca me tathā
ahaṁ drakṣyāmi vaidehīṁ pramodadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: I perceive through my intelligence, (and my mental motion tallies), that I shall behold Vaidehi. Therefore, you monkeys, rejoice.

verses.sanskrit:
मारुतस्य समो वेगे गरुडस्य समो जवे
अयुतं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामीति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
mārutasya samo vege garuḍasya samo jave
ayutaṁ yojanānāṁ tu gamiṣyāmīti me matiḥ

translations.english: In vehemence like to Garura, I shall, I conceive, go an Ayuta yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
वासवस्य सवज्रस्य ब्रह्मणो वा स्वयम्भुवः
विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तादमृतं तदिहानये
लङ्कां वापि समुत्क्षिप्य गच्छेयमिति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
vāsavasya savajrasya brahmaṇo vā svayambhuvaḥ
vikramya sahasā hastādamṛtaṁ tadihānaye
laṅkāṁ vāpi samutkṣipya gaccheyamiti me matiḥ

translations.english: I can, suddenly summoning energy, bring hither ambrosia from the very grasp of Vāsava or Brahmā himself. I shall leap sheer over Lankā. Even this is my impression.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवं वानरश्रेष्ठं गर्जन्तममितौजसं
उवाच परिसंहृष्टो जाम्बवान्हरिसत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
tamevaṁ vānaraśreṣṭhaṁ garjantamamitaujasaṁ
uvāca parisaṁhṛṣṭo jāmbavānharisattamaḥ

translations.english: Filled with delight, the monkeys there amazed see that foremost of monkeys, endued with immeasurable might, storming.

verses.sanskrit:
वीर केसरिणः पुत्र वेगवन्मारुतात्मज
ज्ञातीनां विपुलं शोकस्त्वया तात प्रणाशितः
verses.transliteration:
vīra kesariṇaḥ putra vegavanmārutātmaja
jñātīnāṁ vipulaṁ śokastvayā tāta praṇāśitaḥ

translations.english: O hero! O son of Kesari! O offspring of the Wind! the huge sorrow of your kindred has, my child, been destroyed by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तव कल्याणरुचयः कपिमुख्याः समागताः
मङ्गलं कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं करिष्यन्ति समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
tava kalyāṇarucayaḥ kapimukhyāḥ samāgatāḥ
maṅgalaṁ kāryasiddhyarthaṁ kariṣyanti samāhitāḥ

translations.english: These foremost of monkeys assembled, who wish for your welfare, shall, with intent mind, perform acts tending to your weal,-so that you mayst succeed in your undertaking.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषीणां च प्रसादेन कपिवृद्धमतेन च
गुरूणां च प्रसादेन प्लवस्व त्वं महार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣīṇāṁ ca prasādena kapivṛddhamatena ca
gurūṇāṁ ca prasādena plavasva tvaṁ mahārṇavam

translations.english: By the grace of the saints, and with the permission of the aged monkeys, and by the blessing of the superiors, do you bound over the mighty main.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थास्यामश्चैकपादेन यावदागमनं तव
त्वद्गतानि च सर्वेषां जीवितानि वनौकसाम्
verses.transliteration:
sthāsyāmaścaikapādena yāvadāgamanaṁ tava
tvadgatāni ca sarveṣāṁ jīvitāni vanaukasām

translations.english: Till you return, we shall stay on one leg. The lives of all these rangers of the forest shall go along with you. *i.e. practise austerities on your behalf.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु हरिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच वनौकसः
नेयं मम मही वेगं प्लवने धारयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tatastu hariśārdūlastānuvāca vanaukasaḥ
neyaṁ mama mahī vegaṁ plavane dhārayiṣyati

translations.english: Then that tiger-like monkey said to those rangers of the woods, None in this world would be able to sustain my impetus in the act of bounding.

verses.sanskrit:
एतानि हि नगस्यास्य शिलासंकटशालिनः
शिखराणि महेन्द्रस्य स्थिराणि च महान्ति च
verses.transliteration:
etāni hi nagasyāsya śilāsaṁkaṭaśālinaḥ
śikharāṇi mahendrasya sthirāṇi ca mahānti ca

translations.english: Here are these summits, firm and spacious, of this mountain, Mahendra, thronged with crags. I shall rush forward from these summits of Mahendra, interspersed with trees and adorned with masses of ore.

verses.sanskrit:
एतानि मम निष्पेषं पादयोः पततां वराः
प्लवतो धारयिष्यन्ति योजनानामितः शतम्
verses.transliteration:
etāni mama niṣpeṣaṁ pādayoḥ patatāṁ varāḥ
plavato dhārayiṣyanti yojanānāmitaḥ śatam

translations.english: As I leap over a hundred Yojanas, these mighty summits shall sustain my impetus.

verses.sanskrit:
पादाभ्यां पीडितस्तेन महाशैलो महात्मना
ररास सिंहाभिहतो महान्मत्त इव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
pādābhyāṁ pīḍitastena mahāśailo mahātmanā
rarāsa siṁhābhihato mahānmatta iva dvipaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, hurt by the arms of that high-souled one, the mighty mountain began to cry,* like a mighty mad elephant tormented by a lion. *Through the voices of the animals inhabiting it.

verses.sanskrit:
मुमोच सलिलोत्पीडान्विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः
वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः
verses.transliteration:
mumoca salilotpīḍānviprakīrṇaśiloccayaḥ
vitrastamṛgamātaṅgaḥ prakampitamahādrumaḥ

translations.english: And water rushed out of masses of rocks scattered around. And that mighty mountain had its deer and elephants afflicted with affright; and its giant trees shaken; and its spacious uplands deserted by various Gandharva couples engaged in drinking and dalliance, and by birds-flying away, and by bevies of Vidyadharas; and its huge serpents distressed, and its cliffs and peaks toppling down.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषिभिस्त्रास संभ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानः शिलोच्चयः
सीदन्महति कान्तारे सार्थहीन इवाध्वगः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣibhistrāsa saṁbhrāntaistyajyamānaḥ śiloccayaḥ
sīdanmahati kāntāre sārthahīna ivādhvagaḥ

translations.english: With its serpents hissing, with their bodies half issuing (from their holes), the mountain seemed as if it shone with pennons displayed. And the heap of crags forsaken by saints exercised with fear and agitation, looked doleful, like a wayfarer left in a vast forest by his companions.

verses.sanskrit:
स वेगवान्वेगसमाहितात्मा; हरिप्रवीरः परवीरहन्ता
मनः समाधाय महानुभावो; जगाम लङ्कां मनसा मनस्वी
verses.transliteration:
sa vegavānvegasamāhitātmā; haripravīraḥ paravīrahantā
manaḥ samādhāya mahānubhāvo; jagāma laṅkāṁ manasā manasvī

translations.english: That intelligent, magnanimous and heroic monkey-destroyer of hostile heroes, endowed with speed, concentrating his soul on his energy, mentally went to Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः
इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि
verses.transliteration:
tato rāvaṇanītāyāḥ sītāyāḥ śatrukarśanaḥ
iyeṣa padamanveṣṭuṁ cāraṇācarite pathi

translations.english: Hanumăn then resolved to travel through the air or the path of Cāraņas (heavens), in quest of Jānaki who had taken away by Rävaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विजान्वित्रासयन्धीमानुरसा पादपान्हरन्
मृगांश्च सुबहून्निघ्नन्प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी
verses.transliteration:
dvijānvitrāsayandhīmānurasā pādapānharan
mṛgāṁśca subahūnnighnanpravṛddha iva kesarī

translations.english: Then he, wise and mighty monkey walked over the earth, green with grass, with irresistible steps. At that time, he brushed aside all animals like a lion and crushed down many trees, and thereby scared away the feathered denizens of the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयम्भुवे
भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa sūryāya mahendrāya pavanāya svayambhuve
bhūtebhyaścāñjaliṁ kṛtvā cakāra gamane matim

translations.english: After this, he bowed down to the Sun, Indra, Svayambhu, Wind-god, and all beings with joined palms and then facing the west he saluted his father and then began to increase in dimension like the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवंगप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः
ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु
verses.transliteration:
plavaṁgapravarairdṛṣṭaḥ plavane kṛtaniścayaḥ
vavṛdhe rāmavṛddhyarthaṁ samudra iva parvasu

translations.english: The foremost of the Vānaras at this stared at him, he swelled in size for the purpose of Rāma as the ocean swells on the full-moon days.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्प्रमाण शरीरः सँल्लिलङ्घयिषुरर्णवम्
बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
niṣpramāṇa śarīraḥ sa̐llilaṅghayiṣurarṇavam
bāhubhyāṁ pīḍayāmāsa caraṇābhyāṁ ca parvatam

translations.english: Hanumān got ready for crossing the ocean having grown his body immensely. He caught hold tightly of the mountain with his hands and feet.

verses.sanskrit:
तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः
जज्वलुः पावकोद्दीप्ता विभिदुश्च सहस्रधा
verses.transliteration:
tāstadā saviṣairdaṣṭāḥ kupitaistairmahāśilāḥ
jajvaluḥ pāvakoddīptā vibhiduśca sahasradhā

translations.english: Big rocks bit by those snakes crumbled into pieces and those fragments began to burn with fire-like venom.

verses.sanskrit:
यानि चौषधजालानि तस्मिञ्जातानि पर्वते
विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्
verses.transliteration:
yāni cauṣadhajālāni tasmiñjātāni parvate
viṣaghnānyapi nāgānāṁ na śekuḥ śamituṁ viṣam

translations.english: Although there were many medical herbs, capable of counteracting poison, which had sprung up on that mountain, could not neutralise that poison of the snakes.

verses.sanskrit:
रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन्कर्म दुष्करम्
समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्राप्तुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
rāmārthaṁ vānarārthaṁ ca cikīrṣankarma duṣkaram
samudrasya paraṁ pāraṁ duṣprāpaṁ prāptumicchati

translations.english: Looking like a mountain, the hermits thought about Hanumān, son of wind-god, undertaken for the benefit of Rāma and Vānaras in general, and blessed that he would be able to cross the ocean, the abode of Varuņa easily.

verses.sanskrit:
दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः
ननाद च महानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः
verses.transliteration:
dudhuve ca sa romāṇi cakampe cācalopamaḥ
nanāda ca mahānādaṁ sumahāniva toyadaḥ

translations.english: Meanwhile the fire-like mighty hero trembled in his limbs and his hairs stood on their ends, and he roared like the rumbling of a cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य लाङ्गूलमाविद्धमतिवेगस्य पृष्ठतः
ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः
verses.transliteration:
tasya lāṅgūlamāviddhamativegasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
dadṛśe garuḍeneva hriyamāṇo mahoragaḥ

translations.english: He lashed his roundish tail covered with down and again on his back just to get ready for the spring. It seemed as if Garuda, the king of the birds, was flying off with a huge snake.

verses.sanskrit:
संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्
तेजः सत्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
saṁhṛtya ca bhujau śrīmāṁstathaiva ca śirodharām
tejaḥ sattvaṁ tathā vīryamāviveśa sa vīryavān

translations.english: The monkey firmly planted his arins like bolts, on the mountain; then crouched at the waist and contracted his legs. Contracting his arms, neck and abdomen He, the glorious and powerful Hanumān then, mustered his strengh.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्भ्यां दृढमवस्थानं कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः
निकुञ्च्य कर्णौ हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन्महाबलः
वानरान्वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
padbhyāṁ dṛḍhamavasthānaṁ kṛtvā sa kapikuñjaraḥ
nikuñcya karṇau hanumānutpatiṣyanmahābalaḥ
vānarānvānaraśreṣṭha idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: He looked up to survey the distance, he suspended his breath in the heart while looking into sky. Then doing firm his feet and contracting his ears in order to spring, addressing other Vanaras, mighty Hanuman said.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लङ्कायां जनकात्मजाम्
अनेनैव हि वेगेन गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi drakṣyāmi yadi tāṁ laṅkāyāṁ janakātmajām
anenaiva hi vegena gamiṣyāmi surālayam

translations.english: I shall reach Lankā with the velocity of wind, just like an arrow shot by Rāma and if I do not find Jānakī there I shall, at the same speed, go to the region of the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्यामि कृतश्रमः
बद्ध्वा राक्षसराजानमानयिष्यामि रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
yadi vā tridive sītāṁ na drakṣyāmi kṛtaśramaḥ
baddhvā rākṣasarājānamānayiṣyāmi rāvaṇam

translations.english: If I do not see Sītā in heaven even after exerting myself, I shall bring Ravana, the ruler of Raksasas, in bondage. At anyway with success, I shall come with Sītā or then I shall bring Lankā uprooting it with Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः
उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu hanumānvānarānvānarottamaḥ
utpapātātha vegena vegavānavicārayan

translations.english: With these words, Hanumān who was full of vigour, sprang into the air accounted himself like a compeer of Garuda. As he flew up with vehemence, trees growing on the mountain, were uprooted from all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः
हनुमान्पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
supuṣpitāgrairbahubhiḥ pādapairanvitaḥ kapiḥ
hanumānparvatākāro babhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ

translations.english: Hanumān thus being covered with buds and blossoms looked like a hill lit up with glowworms. Then the heavy trees being deprived of their flowers by the velocity of the flight began to drop down into the sea like mountains bode, afflicted with the fear of Mahendra.

verses.sanskrit:
स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः
शुशुभे मेघसंकाशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa nānākusumaiḥ kīrṇaḥ kapiḥ sāṅkurakorakaiḥ
śuśubhe meghasaṁkāśaḥ khadyotairiva parvataḥ

translations.english: And strewn with various sprouts and buds and blossoms, the monkey resembling a mass of clouds, looked lovely like a bill filled with glowworms.

verses.sanskrit:
विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः
अवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
vimuktāstasya vegena muktvā puṣpāṇi te drumāḥ
avaśīryanta salile nivṛttāḥ suhṛdo yathā

translations.english: And uprooted by the force of his rush, mose trees, their flowers fallen off, plunged into the sea, like friends returning to their homes (after having accompanied their friend some way).

verses.sanskrit:
लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद्विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत्
द्रुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्
verses.transliteration:
laghutvenopapannaṁ tadvicitraṁ sāgare'patat
drumāṇāṁ vividhaṁ puṣpaṁ kapivāyusamīritam

translations.english: And blown by the wind caused by the a monkey, the various variegated flowers of the trees the consequence of their lightness, showered down on the sea. And covered with heaps of fragrant flowers of diverse hues, the monkey resembled a mass of clouds embellished by lines of lightning

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ
पर्वताग्राद्विनिष्क्रान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ
verses.transliteration:
tasyāmbaragatau bāhū dadṛśāte prasāritau
parvatāgrādviniṣkrāntau pañcāsyāviva pannagau

translations.english: The waters of the ocean) strewn with blossoms carried off by his motion, operated like the sky garnished with charming stars (cresting the same). His arms stretched in the sky, seemed like five-hooded snakes issuing from mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोर्मिजालं महार्णवम्
पिपासुरिव चाकाशं ददृशे स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
pibanniva babhau cāpi sormijālaṁ mahārṇavam
pipāsuriva cākāśaṁ dadṛśe sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: He appeared as if he was drinking up the mightily deep with its multitudes of waves, or as if that redoubtable monkey was desirous of sucking up the sky itself.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः
नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ
verses.transliteration:
tasya vidyutprabhākāre vāyumārgānusāriṇaḥ
nayane viprakāśete parvatasthāvivānalau

translations.english: As he coursed the orbit of air, his eyes flashing like lightning, resembled two craters a glow on a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले
चक्षुषी संप्रकशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविव स्थितौ
verses.transliteration:
piṅge piṅgākṣamukhyasya bṛhatī parimaṇḍale
cakṣuṣī saṁprakaśete candrasūryāviva sthitau

translations.english: And the eyes of that foremost of tawny-hued ones resembled the sun and the moon stationed in a vast yellow aureola.

verses.sanskrit:
लाङ्गलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते
अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितः
verses.transliteration:
lāṅgalaṁ ca samāviddhaṁ plavamānasya śobhate
ambare vāyuputrasya śakradhvaja ivocchritaḥ

translations.english: Beside his coppery nose, his face looked coppery, as looks the solar disc on the approach of eve. And the uplifted tail of the Wind-god's offspring engaged in bounding, appeared beautiful in the sky like the raised standard of Sakra.

verses.sanskrit:
लाङ्गूलचक्रेण महाञ्शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः
व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः
verses.transliteration:
lāṅgūlacakreṇa mahāñśukladaṁṣṭro'nilātmajaḥ
vyarocata mahāprājñaḥ pariveṣīva bhāskaraḥ

translations.english: The exceedingly wise son of the Wind, Hanumān, having white teeth, with his tail coiled up, looked handsome like the sun with his disc.

verses.sanskrit:
स्फिग्देशेनाभिताम्रेण रराज स महाकपिः
महता दारितेनेव गिरिर्गैरिकधातुना
verses.transliteration:
sphigdeśenābhitāmreṇa rarāja sa mahākapiḥ
mahatā dāriteneva girirgairikadhātunā

translations.english: On account of his waist being deeply coppery that mighty monkey appeared like a mountain running, mighty torrent mixed with minerals and red chalk.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्
कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमूत इव गर्जति
verses.transliteration:
tasya vānarasiṁhasya plavamānasya sāgaram
kakṣāntaragato vāyurjīmūta iva garjati

translations.english: The wind that had got into the armpits of that leonine monkey who was crossing over the main, roar like clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
खे यथा निपतत्युल्का उत्तरान्ताद्विनिःसृता
दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः
verses.transliteration:
khe yathā nipatatyulkā uttarāntādviniḥsṛtā
dṛśyate sānubandhā ca tathā sa kapikuñjaraḥ

translations.english: As a meteor consisting of many smaller ones, darting from above fall down (to the earth), rushed on that foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
पतत्पतंगसंकाशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः
प्रवृद्ध इव मातंगः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया
verses.transliteration:
patatpataṁgasaṁkāśo vyāyataḥ śuśubhe kapiḥ
pravṛddha iva mātaṁgaḥ kakṣyayā badhyamānayā

translations.english: Then that stalwart monkey resembling the careering sun, resembled a mad elephant fettered by the middle, whose bulk has increased immensely.

verses.sanskrit:
उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण छायया चावगाढया
सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत्तदा कपिः
verses.transliteration:
upariṣṭāccharīreṇa chāyayā cāvagāḍhayā
sāgare mārutāviṣṭā naurivāsīttadā kapiḥ

translations.english: As he coursed above, on account of the reflection cast by his body (on the boson of the deep), the monkey* by his progress, looked link a bark swayed by the breeze. *Under water.

verses.sanskrit:
यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः
स स तस्याङ्गवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
yaṁ yaṁ deśaṁ samudrasya jagāma sa mahākapiḥ
sa sa tasyāṅgavegena sonmāda iva lakṣyate

translations.english: And wherever that mighty monkey went about the sea, the state of things appeared to undergo a violent convulsion owing to impetus imparted by his body.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरस्योर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्ष्मणाम्
अभिघ्नंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
sāgarasyormijālānāmurasā śailavarṣmaṇām
abhighnaṁstu mahāvegaḥ pupluve sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: That mighty monkey possessed of exceeding speed rushed on, raising multitudes of surges on the sea by his breast resembling rock.

verses.sanskrit:
कपिवातश्च बलवान्मेघवातश्च निःसृतः
सागरं भीमनिर्घोषं कम्पयामासतुर्भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
kapivātaśca balavānmeghavātaśca niḥsṛtaḥ
sāgaraṁ bhīmanirghoṣaṁ kampayāmāsaturbhṛśam

translations.english: And the wind begot of the monkey as well as that of the clouds, issuing out, made the dreadsounding ocean roll violently.

verses.sanskrit:
विकर्षन्नूर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि
अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान्गणयन्निव
verses.transliteration:
vikarṣannūrmijālāni bṛhanti lavaṇāmbhasi
atyakrāmanmahāvegastaraṅgāngaṇayanniva

translations.english: Pushing up multitudes of high-heaving billows from the salt waters, that tiger-like monkey rushed on separating earth and heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवमानं समीक्ष्याथ भुजङ्गाः सागरालयाः
व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्णमिति मेनिरे
verses.transliteration:
plavamānaṁ samīkṣyātha bhujaṅgāḥ sāgarālayāḥ
vyomni taṁ kapiśārdūlaṁ suparṇamiti menire

translations.english: And sea-serpents, seeing that tiger-like monkey proceeding in the sky, took him for Suparna himself.

verses.sanskrit:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता
छाया वानरसिंहस्य जले चारुतराभवत्
verses.transliteration:
daśayojanavistīrṇā triṁśadyojanamāyatā
chāyā vānarasiṁhasya jale cārutarābhavat

translations.english: The shadow the leonine monkey, measuring ten Yojanas in width and thirty in length, seemed the handsome in consequence of his speed.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी
तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि
verses.transliteration:
śvetābhraghanarājīva vāyuputrānugāminī
tasya sā śuśubhe chāyā vitatā lavaṇāmbhasi

translations.english: That shadow resembling masses of white clouds, rallying on the salt waters and following the wind-god's son, seemed exceedingly beautiful. on more

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवगं त्वरितं तदा
ववृषुः पुष्पवर्षाणि देवगन्धर्वदानवाः
verses.transliteration:
plavamānaṁ tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā plavagaṁ tvaritaṁ tadā
vavṛṣuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi devagandharvadānavāḥ

translations.english: Beholding that monkey engaged in bounding with celerity, gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas began to strew blossoms (on him).

verses.sanskrit:
तताप न हि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरेश्वरम्
सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये
verses.transliteration:
tatāpa na hi taṁ sūryaḥ plavantaṁ vānareśvaram
siṣeve ca tadā vāyū rāmakāryārthasiddhaye

translations.english: As he was leaping, the Sun did not burn him; and the Wind ministered to him, for the success of Rāma's work.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं प्लवमानं विहायसा
जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो महौजसं
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣayastuṣṭuvuścainaṁ plavamānaṁ vihāyasā
jaguśca devagandharvāḥ praśaṁsanto mahaujasaṁ

translations.english: And the saints hymned his praises, as he was leaping on in the sky. And applauding the ranger of forests, they raised the voice of song.

verses.sanskrit:
नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विबुधाः खगाः
प्रेक्ष्याकाशे कपिवरं सहसा विगतक्लमम्
verses.transliteration:
nāgāśca tuṣṭuvuryakṣā rakṣāṁsi vibudhāḥ khagāḥ
prekṣyākāśe kapivaraṁ sahasā vigataklamam

translations.english: Nagas and Yaksas, and various (races of) Raksasas, eulogized (him), on beholding that tiger-like monkey, Hanumān, in the act of bounding.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति
इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी चिन्तयामास सागरः
verses.transliteration:
tasminplavagaśārdūle plavamāne hanūmati
ikṣvākukulamānārthī cintayāmāsa sāgaraḥ

translations.english: Hanumān, that lord of monkeys, being engaged in the act of bounding, the Ocean, who sought to do honour to the race of Ikşvāku within himself.

verses.sanskrit:
साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमतः
करिष्यामि भविष्यामि सर्ववाच्यो विवक्षताम्
verses.transliteration:
sāhāyyaṁ vānarendrasya yadi nāhaṁ hanūmataḥ
kariṣyāmi bhaviṣyāmi sarvavācyo vivakṣatām

translations.english: He said himself, ‘Truly shall I be blamed of all persons if I do not assist this lord of monkeys-Hanumān.'

verses.sanskrit:
अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धितः
इक्ष्वाकुसचिवश्चायं नावसीदितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
ahamikṣvākunāthena sagareṇa vivardhitaḥ
ikṣvākusacivaścāyaṁ nāvasīditumarhati

translations.english: Reared I have been by Sagara, the foremost of the race of the Ikşvākus and this monkey is their counsellor. It therefore dose not behove me to tire him out.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः
शेषं च मयि विश्रान्तः सुखेनातिपतिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tathā mayā vidhātavyaṁ viśrameta yathā kapiḥ
śeṣaṁ ca mayi viśrāntaḥ sukhenātipatiṣyati

translations.english: It become me to do that by which the monkey may take rest in me and, relieved, may happily traverse the remaining way.

verses.sanskrit:
इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वीं समुद्रश्छन्नमम्भसि
हिरण्यनाभं मैनाकमुवाच गिरिसत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
iti kṛtvā matiṁ sādhvīṁ samudraśchannamambhasi
hiraṇyanābhaṁ mainākamuvāca girisattamam

translations.english: Having arrived at this wholesome resolution, the Ocean spake upto that best of mountains, Maināka, hued in gold and situate in the waters, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमिहासुरसंघानां पातालतलवासिनाम्
देवराज्ञा गिरिश्रेष्ठ परिघः संनिवेशितः
verses.transliteration:
tvamihāsurasaṁghānāṁ pātālatalavāsinām
devarājñā giriśreṣṭha parighaḥ saṁniveśitaḥ

translations.english: O lord, you had been placed here by the king of celestials as an outer gate against the Asuras inhabiting the region under the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमेषां ज्ञातवीर्याणां पुनरेवोत्पतिष्यताम्
पातालस्याप्रमेयस्य द्वारमावृत्य तिष्ठसि
verses.transliteration:
tvameṣāṁ jñātavīryāṇāṁ punarevotpatiṣyatām
pātālasyāprameyasya dvāramāvṛtya tiṣṭhasi

translations.english: You too, from then, had been waiting at this gate, unapproachable by the Asuras, rising up again and again and whose prowess is wellknown (to the Lord of celestials)

verses.sanskrit:
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैलवर्धितुम्
तस्मात्संचोदयामि त्वामुत्तिष्ठ नगसत्तम
verses.transliteration:
tiryagūrdhvamadhaścaiva śaktiste śailavardhitum
tasmātsaṁcodayāmi tvāmuttiṣṭha nagasattama

translations.english: O mountain, you are capable of expanding yourself upwards, downwards and on they sides. I do command you therefore, O best of mountains, to rise up.

verses.sanskrit:
स एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वामुपर्येति वीर्यवान्
हनूमान्रामकार्यार्थं भीमकर्मा खमाप्लुतः
verses.transliteration:
sa eṣa kapiśārdūlastvāmuparyeti vīryavān
hanūmānrāmakāryārthaṁ bhīmakarmā khamāplutaḥ

translations.english: That best of monkeys, the energetic Hanumān, the performer of mighty deeds, engaged in Rāma's service, worn out with fatigue, wait above you. Beholding the exhaustion of that leader of monkeys, it behove you to rise up.

verses.sanskrit:
हिरण्यनाभो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः
उत्पपात जलात्तूर्णं महाद्रुमलतायुतः
verses.transliteration:
hiraṇyanābho maināko niśamya lavaṇāmbhasaḥ
utpapāta jalāttūrṇaṁ mahādrumalatāyutaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the speech of the Ocean, the golden mountain Maināka, covered with tall trees and creepers, rose up instantly from his watery bed.

verses.sanskrit:
स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवात्युत्थितस्तदा
यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीप्तरश्मिर्दिवाकरः
verses.transliteration:
sa sāgarajalaṁ bhittvā babhūvātyutthitastadā
yathā jaladharaṁ bhittvā dīptaraśmirdivākaraḥ

translations.english: Like to the Sun of bright rays rising out of the watery expanse, he uplifted himself from the Ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिंनरमहोरगैः
आदित्योदयसंकाशैरालिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
śātakumbhamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ sakiṁnaramahoragaiḥ
ādityodayasaṁkāśairālikhadbhirivāmbaram

translations.english: The sky was as if cleft by these golden summits like to the rising of the Sun, inhabited by Kinnaras and large Serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य जाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गैः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः
आकाशं शस्त्रसंकाशमभवत्काञ्चनप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya jāmbūnadaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ parvatasya samutthitaiḥ
ākāśaṁ śastrasaṁkāśamabhavatkāñcanaprabham

translations.english: To golden summits of that mountain being thus lifted up, the dark-blue sky assumed the golden hue. And by those highly resplendent golden peaks that best of mountains assumed the brilliance of a thousand suns.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुत्थितमसंगेन हनूमानग्रतः स्थितम्
मध्ये लवणतोयस्य विघ्नोऽयमिति निश्चितः
verses.transliteration:
tamutthitamasaṁgena hanūmānagrataḥ sthitam
madhye lavaṇatoyasya vighno'yamiti niścitaḥ
