translations.english: Beholding before him that up-heaved mountain in the midst of the salt Ocean Hanumān regarded it, as a barrier for aye.

verses.sanskrit:
स तमुच्छ्रितमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः
उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tamucchritamatyarthaṁ mahāvego mahākapiḥ
urasā pātayāmāsa jīmūtamiva mārutaḥ

translations.english: Like to Wind dispersing clouds, that mighty monkey with great velocity crushed down those up-lifted peaks with his breast.

verses.sanskrit:
स तदा पातितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः
बुद्ध्वा तस्य कपेर्वेगं जहर्ष च ननन्द च
verses.transliteration:
sa tadā pātitastena kapinā parvatottamaḥ
buddhvā tasya kapervegaṁ jaharṣa ca nananda ca

translations.english: Being thus crushed down by that monkey, the best of mountains, being apprized of his prowess, began to shout with joy.

verses.sanskrit:
तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समवस्थितम्
प्रीतो हृष्टमना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम्
मानुषं धरयन्रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tamākāśagataṁ vīramākāśe samavasthitam
prīto hṛṣṭamanā vākyamabravītparvataḥ kapim
mānuṣaṁ dharayanrūpamātmanaḥ śikhare sthitaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, with a glad heart assuming the semblance of a man ånd stationing himself upon his own summit, that mountain-chief addressed Hanumān, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
दुष्करं कृतवान्कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम
निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु विश्रमस्व यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
duṣkaraṁ kṛtavānkarma tvamidaṁ vānarottama
nipatya mama śṛṅgeṣu viśramasva yathāsukham

translations.english: O best of monkeys, forsooth had you been engaged in this arduous task. Coming down on my peak do you take rest.

verses.sanskrit:
राघावस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः
स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः
verses.transliteration:
rāghāvasya kule jātairudadhiḥ parivardhitaḥ
sa tvāṁ rāmahite yuktaṁ pratyarcayati sāgaraḥ

translations.english: This ocean was reared by one born in the family of Raghus. And beholding you engaged on Rāma's behoof he is worshipping you.

verses.sanskrit:
कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः
सोऽयं तत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वत्तः संमानमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
kṛte ca pratikartavyameṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
so'yaṁ tatpratikārārthī tvattaḥ saṁmānamarhati

translations.english: The best and everlasting virtue consists in returning benefits to one who has benefited us. Bent on returning benefits to Raghu's race, he deserve respect from you.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः
योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः
तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति
verses.transliteration:
tvannimittamanenāhaṁ bahumānātpracoditaḥ
yojanānāṁ śataṁ cāpi kapireṣa samāplutaḥ
tava sānuṣu viśrāntaḥ śeṣaṁ prakramatāmiti

translations.english: And to welcome you properly I have been despatched by him with the message-traversing over a hundred yojans this monkey has been worn out with fatigue; let him voyage to the remaining way after resting for a while on your summit.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ त्वं हरिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्
तदिदं गन्धवत्स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु
तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽनुगमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha tvaṁ hariśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām
tadidaṁ gandhavatsvādu kandamūlaphalaṁ bahu
tadāsvādya hariśreṣṭha viśrānto'nugamiṣyasi

translations.english: Do you therefore, O best of monkeys, remain here and take rest. And feasting on these many fragrant and sweet fruits and roots, O foremost of monkeys, do you relieve yourself of the toil and proceed.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्माकमपि संबन्धः कपिमुख्यस्त्वयास्ति वै
प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
asmākamapi saṁbandhaḥ kapimukhyastvayāsti vai
prakhyātastriṣu lokeṣu mahāguṇaparigrahaḥ

translations.english: O leader of monkeys, my relation with you is replete with many virtues and known all over the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज
तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर
verses.transliteration:
vegavantaḥ plavanto ye plavagā mārutātmaja
teṣāṁ mukhyatamaṁ manye tvāmahaṁ kapikuñjara

translations.english: O Son of Maruta, O best of monkeys, I know you to be the foremost of all monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिथिः किल पूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता
धर्मं जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनर्यादृशो भवान्
verses.transliteration:
atithiḥ kila pūjārhaḥ prākṛto'pi vijānatā
dharmaṁ jijñāsamānena kiṁ punaryādṛśo bhavān

translations.english: Even an ordinary guest should be adored by him who abide by virtue, what of you great as you are?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः
पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi devavariṣṭhasya mārutasya mahātmanaḥ
putrastasyaiva vegena sadṛśaḥ kapikuñjara

translations.english: O you lion among monkeys, you are the son of Māruta, the foremost of celestials and are his equal in speed.

verses.sanskrit:
पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञ पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः
तस्मात्त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्
verses.transliteration:
pūjite tvayi dharmajña pūjāṁ prāpnoti mārutaḥ
tasmāttvaṁ pūjanīyo me śṛṇu cāpyatra kāraṇam

translations.english: You that are conversant with virtue, being worshipped, Maruta himself receive offerings. You are therefore worth of my adoration. Hearken, there is another reason for it.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन्
तेऽपि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडानिलवेगिनः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvaṁ kṛtayuge tāta parvatāḥ pakṣiṇo'bhavan
te'pi jagmurdiśaḥ sarvā garuḍānilaveginaḥ

translations.english: O worshipful one, in olden times, the mountains, gifted with wings, began to range all quarters with velocity like to Garuda.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसंघाः सहर्षिभिः
भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया
verses.transliteration:
tatasteṣu prayāteṣu devasaṁghāḥ saharṣibhiḥ
bhūtāni ca bhayaṁ jagmusteṣāṁ patanaśaṅkayā

translations.english: They moving thus, the celestials, the ascetics, and all creatures became almost faint with fear of their falling down.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः
पक्षांश्चिच्छेद वज्रेण तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kruddhaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ parvatānāṁ śatakratuḥ
pakṣāṁściccheda vajreṇa tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Highly enraged therefore, the thousand-eyed Deity, the performer of hundred sacrifices, hundred with his thunderbolt, the wings of hundreds and thousands of them.

verses.sanskrit:
स मामुपगतः क्रुद्धो वज्रमुद्यम्य देवराट्
ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः श्वसनेन महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
sa māmupagataḥ kruddho vajramudyamya devarāṭ
tato'haṁ sahasā kṣiptaḥ śvasanena mahātmanā

translations.english: When with his thunderbolt, the Lord of celestials, wroth, approached me, I was all on a sudden thrown down by the high-souled Wind.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिँल्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम
गुप्तपक्षः समग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
asmi̐llavaṇatoye ca prakṣiptaḥ plavagottama
guptapakṣaḥ samagraśca tava pitrābhirakṣitaḥ

translations.english: O best of monkeys I was these cast done in this salt ocean and preserved unhurt by your ancestors having my wings hid.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्यो हि मम मारुतः
त्वया मे ह्येष संबन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः
verses.transliteration:
tato'haṁ mānayāmi tvāṁ mānyo hi mama mārutaḥ
tvayā me hyeṣa saṁbandhaḥ kapimukhya mahāguṇaḥ

translations.english: I shall therefore adore you and you are object of my worship O Maruta! And this my relation with you, O foremost of monkeys, is pregnant with many virtues.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च
प्रीतिं प्रीतमना कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महाकपे
verses.transliteration:
asminnevaṁgate kārye sāgarasya mamaiva ca
prītiṁ prītamanā kartuṁ tvamarhasi mahākape

translations.english: The time for returning benefits having arrived, O high-souled one, it behove you to afford me and the ocean, satisfaction with a blessed heart.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण कपिसत्तम
प्रीतिं च बहुमन्यस्व प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्
verses.transliteration:
śramaṁ mokṣaya pūjāṁ ca gṛhāṇa kapisattama
prītiṁ ca bahumanyasva prīto'smi tava darśanāt

translations.english: best of monkeys, relieve yourself of the fatigue and accept my affectionate offering, who am worthy of your respect. For his relationship with Wind whose son was Pitupanthānam-the text means "his father's path”-Wind being Hanumān's father the passage means-"aerial way."-Happy am I to see you. *Wrath in consequence of his inability to accept his offerings.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत्
प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ kapiśreṣṭhastaṁ nagottamamabravīt
prīto'smi kṛtamātithyaṁ manyureṣo'panīyatām

translations.english: Being thus accosted by Maināka, the best of mountains, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys said, saying: Pleased am I and you had shown me enough of hospitality. Do you give up your wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वरते कार्यकालो मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते
प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरा
verses.transliteration:
tvarate kāryakālo me ahaścāpyativartate
pratijñā ca mayā dattā na sthātavyamihāntarā

translations.english: Business wants me to go soon and the time is well-nigh spent. Besides I have promised that I shall not halt at any intermediate place.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुंगवः
जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान्प्रहसन्निव
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā pāṇinā śailamālabhya haripuṁgavaḥ
jagāmākāśamāviśya vīryavānprahasanniva

translations.english: Thereupon touching the hill with his hand that highly energetic monkey wended, smiling his aerial way. Ocean

verses.sanskrit:
स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः
पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरनिलात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa parvatasamudrābhyāṁ bahumānādavekṣitaḥ
pūjitaścopapannābhirāśīrbhiranilātmajaḥ

translations.english: Thereat the and the mountain respectfully looked towards him and adored and welcomed him with blessings worthy of the occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोर्ध्वं दूरमुत्पत्य हित्वा शैलमहार्णवौ
पितुः पन्थानमास्थाय जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
athordhvaṁ dūramutpatya hitvā śailamahārṇavau
pituḥ panthānamāsthāya jagāma vimale'mbare

translations.english: Leaving the mountain and the ocean and rising his up, he proceeded in the clear welkin traversing the aerial way.

verses.sanskrit:
भूयश्चोर्ध्वगतिं प्राप्य गिरिं तमवलोकयन्
वायुसूनुर्निरालम्बे जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
bhūyaścordhvagatiṁ prāpya giriṁ tamavalokayan
vāyusūnurnirālambe jagāma vimale'mbare

translations.english: Rising high up and casting his look down on the hill, that foremost of monkeys proceeded by the unsupported aerial track.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
प्रशशंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
taddvitīyaṁ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram
praśaśaṁsuḥ surāḥ sarve siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ

translations.english: Beholding this singularly arduous work of Hanumān the celestials, the Siddhas and the ascetics all praised him.

verses.sanskrit:
देवताश्चाभवन्हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा
काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः
verses.transliteration:
devatāścābhavanhṛṣṭāstatrasthāstasya karmaṇā
kāñcanasya sunābhasya sahasrākṣaśca vāsavaḥ

translations.english: All the celestials and others living on its summit, were highly pleased with the mountain arrayed in gold and having beautiful sides.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच वचनं धीमान्परितोषात्सगद्गदम्
सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
uvāca vacanaṁ dhīmānparitoṣātsagadgadam
sunābhaṁ parvataśreṣṭhaṁ svayameva śacīpatiḥ

translations.english: And the thousand-eyed Vásava was also pleased. And greatly pleased that highly intelligent Saci's lord, himself, addressed that best of mountains having picturesque sides, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
हिरण्यनाभशैलेन्द्रपरितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम्
अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि तिष्ठ सौम्य यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
hiraṇyanābhaśailendraparituṣṭo'smi te bhṛśam
abhayaṁ te prayacchāmi tiṣṭha saumya yathāsukham

translations.english: Greatly delighted am I, O lord of mountains, O you having golden peaks. 'No fear' I do declare to you. Proceedest you therefore, at your ease, O gently one!

verses.sanskrit:
साह्यं कृतं ते सुमहद्विक्रान्तस्य हनूमतः
क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भयस्य भये सति
verses.transliteration:
sāhyaṁ kṛtaṁ te sumahadvikrāntasya hanūmataḥ
kramato yojanaśataṁ nirbhayasya bhaye sati

translations.english: Greatly had you hoped Hanumān, crossin fearlessly an unceasingly, over hundred yojanas so that he might not fall in danger.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्यैष हि दौत्येन याति दाशरथेर्हरिः
सत्क्रियां कुर्वता शक्या तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
rāmasyaiṣa hi dautyena yāti dāśaratherhariḥ
satkriyāṁ kurvatā śakyā toṣito'smi dṛḍhaṁ tvayā

translations.english: This monkey, is going in the interests of Rāma, Dasaratha's son—and you had welcomed him to the best of your mighty. Therefore I am greatly pleased with you.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहर्षमलभद्विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः
देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ praharṣamalabhadvipulaṁ parvatottamaḥ
devatānāṁ patiṁ dṛṣṭvā parituṣṭaṁ śatakratum

translations.english: Beholding that lord of celestials the performer of an hundred sacrifices, highly gratified, that best of mountains attained to an excess of joy.

verses.sanskrit:
स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा
हनूमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
sa vai dattavaraḥ śailo babhūvāvasthitastadā
hanūmāṁśca muhūrtena vyaticakrāma sāgaram

translations.english: Having received boons (from Indra) the Mountain occupied again its pristine place. And Hanumān in a short time crossed over the main.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
अब्रुवन्सूर्यसंकाशां सुरसां नागमातरम्
verses.transliteration:
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
abruvansūryasaṁkāśāṁ surasāṁ nāgamātaram

translations.english: Thereupon the celestial along with Gandharvas, Siddhas and the ascetics, spake to Surasā the mother of serpents, resembling the Sun, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि
हनूमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ vātātmajaḥ śrīmānplavate sāgaropari
hanūmānnāma tasya tvaṁ muhūrtaṁ vighnamācara

translations.english: The highly effulgent son of Wind named Hanumān is crossing over the main. You are required to throw obstacles in his way for a while.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्
दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभःस्पृशम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasaṁ rūpamāsthāya sughoraṁ parvatopamam
daṁṣṭrākarālaṁ piṅgākṣaṁ vaktraṁ kṛtvā nabhaḥspṛśam

translations.english: Assuming therefore the semblance of a terrible, grim-visaged Rāksasa, resembling a huge mountain and having terrible teeth and a face with coppery eyes, do you touch the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम्
त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषदं वा गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
balamicchāmahe jñātuṁ bhūyaścāsya parākramam
tvāṁ vijeṣyatyupāyena viṣadaṁ vā gamiṣyati

translations.english: We are anxious to learn if he defeat you by some means or comes by grief."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता
समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā devī daivatairabhisatkṛtā
samudramadhye surasā bibhratī rākṣasaṁ vapuḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed the worshipful Surasā, having been honoured by the celestials, deformed and horrible and capable of exciting the fear of all beings, and obstructing Hanumān as he was coursing on, said.

verses.sanskrit:
मम भक्षः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ
अहं त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम्
verses.transliteration:
mama bhakṣaḥ pradiṣṭastvamīśvarairvānararṣabha
ahaṁ tvāṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmi praviśedaṁ mamānanam

translations.english: O foremost of monkeys, you had been ordained as my fare by the gods themselves. I will eat you up, do you enter my mouth.

verses.sanskrit:
रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
rāmo dāśarathirnāma praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā

translations.english: Thus accosted by Surasā, (Hanumān) with a glad countenance, said, Rama, son to Dasaratha, had entered the Dandaka forest in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa, and his wife, Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्य कार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः
तस्य सीता हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी
verses.transliteration:
asya kāryaviṣaktasya baddhavairasya rākṣasaiḥ
tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī

translations.english: He having created hostility with the Rākṣasas, his illustrious wife, Sītā, while he was engrossed in some work, was carried away by Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामशासनात्
कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साह्यं विषयवासिनि
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ sakāśaṁ dūto'haṁ gamiṣye rāmaśāsanāt
kartumarhasi rāmasya sāhyaṁ viṣayavāsini

translations.english: At Rāma's command, I go to her as his envoy. It behove you, living in (Rāma's) dominions, to lend him your help.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्
आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते
verses.transliteration:
atha vā maithilīṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ cākliṣṭakāriṇam
āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṁ satyaṁ pratiśṛṇomi te

translations.english: Or having seen Mithila's daughter, as well as Rāma of untiring deeds, I will enter your mouth. This I promise you truly."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी
अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेन्मां कश्चिदेष वरो मम
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā hanumatā surasā kāmarūpiṇī
abravīnnātivartenmāṁ kaścideṣa varo mama

translations.english: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Surasā, capable of wearing forms at will, said, “None shall pass me without being devoured by me, even this is the boon that I have received."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुंगवः
अब्रवीत्कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ surasayā kruddho vānarapuṁgavaḥ
abravītkuru vai vaktraṁ yena māṁ viṣahiṣyase

translations.english: Thus addressed by Surasā, that foremost of monkeys, waxing wroth, said, “Extend your mouth so, that you may contain me." Having said this to Surasā, having her mouth measuring ten yojanas, Hanumān enlarged himself as many yojanas. Thereat-Surasā enlarged her mouth twenty yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यं चास्तु वचस्तव
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭo'smi hi te vaktraṁ dākṣāyaṇi namo'stu te
gamiṣye yatra vaidehī satyaṁ cāstu vacastava

translations.english: O descendant of Dakşa, I have entered into your mouth. I bow down to you. I will repair to where Vaidehi is Your boon has proved trve.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव
अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā vadanānmuktaṁ candraṁ rāhumukhādiva
abravītsurasā devī svena rūpeṇa vānaram

translations.english: Seeing him out of her mouth like the Moon out of the mouth of Rāhu, the venerable Surasā spoke to the monkey in her native form, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्
समानय च वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
arthasiddhyai hariśreṣṭha gaccha saumya yathāsukham
samānaya ca vaidehīṁ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā

translations.english: For compassing your end, go, O foremost of monkeys, O mild one, at yours ease. And bringing to Vaidehī tidings touching the highsouled Rāghava do you meet her.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
साधु साध्विति भूतानि प्रशशंसुस्तदा हरिम्
verses.transliteration:
tattṛtīyaṁ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram
sādhu sādhviti bhūtāni praśaśaṁsustadā harim

translations.english: Witnessing that third act* The third feat, remarks Rāmānuja, is Hanuman's issuing out of Surasā's mouth. The preceding two are not mentioned. — of Hanumān's hard to perform, all beings extolled the monkey exclaiming, "Excellent! Excellent!" *A kind of also or agallochum.-Wilson.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुशः सेविते वीरैर्विद्याधरगणैर्वरैः
कपिना कृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
bahuśaḥ sevite vīrairvidyādharagaṇairvaraiḥ
kapinā kṛṣyamāṇāni mahābhrāṇi cakāśire

translations.english: And colossal clouds scattered by the monkey, pale and crimson and blue and mangistha-hued, looked exceedingly lovely.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः
प्रावृषीन्दुरिवाभाति निष्पतन्प्रविशंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
praviśannabhrajālāni niṣpataṁśca punaḥ punaḥ
prāvṛṣīndurivābhāti niṣpatanpraviśaṁstadā

translations.english: Again and again entering into the clouds and emerging out of them, he resembled the Moon during the rains now entering into clouds) and now issuing out of them.

verses.sanskrit:
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी
मनसा चिन्तयामास प्रवृद्धा कामरूपिणी
verses.transliteration:
plavamānaṁ tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā siṁhikā nāma rākṣasī
manasā cintayāmāsa pravṛddhā kāmarūpiṇī

translations.english: And it came to pass that beholding him in the act of bounding, a Rākşasi named Sinhikā, of great age, and capable of wearing forms at will, thought herself.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य दीर्घस्य कालस्य भविष्याम्यहमाशिता
इदं हि मे महत्सत्त्वं चिरस्य वशमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
adya dīrghasya kālasya bhaviṣyāmyahamāśitā
idaṁ hi me mahatsattvaṁ cirasya vaśamāgatam

translations.english: Today after a long lapse of time I shall have my fare. This mighty creature has after a long time come within my power.

verses.sanskrit:
कपिराज्ञा यदाख्यातं सत्त्वमद्भुतदर्शनम्
छायाग्राहि महावीर्यं तदिदं नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
kapirājñā yadākhyātaṁ sattvamadbhutadarśanam
chāyāgrāhi mahāvīryaṁ tadidaṁ nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that one of a distorted countenance, the wind-god's son thought, This one is, without doubt, the creature of wonderful form, possessed of exceeding prowess, given to securing its prey by means of its shadow, which had been described by the monkey-king.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां बुद्ध्वार्थतत्त्वेन सिंहिकां मतिमान्कपिः
व्यवर्धत महाकायः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ buddhvārthatattvena siṁhikāṁ matimānkapiḥ
vyavardhata mahākāyaḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ

translations.english: And concluding her to be Sinhikā from her act, the intelligent monkey attaining a gigantic body, increased himself, like a mass of clouds during the rains.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सा कायमुद्वीक्ष्य वर्धमानं महाकपेः
वक्त्रं प्रसारयामास पातालाम्बरसंनिभम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya sā kāyamudvīkṣya vardhamānaṁ mahākapeḥ
vaktraṁ prasārayāmāsa pātālāmbarasaṁnibham

translations.english: Seeing the enlarged body of the mighty monkey, she extended her mouth measuring the sky and the nether regions. And roaring like to a mass of clouds, she rushed against the monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श ततस्तस्या विकृतं सुमहन्मुखम्
कायमात्रं च मेधावी मर्माणि च महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa tatastasyā vikṛtaṁ sumahanmukham
kāyamātraṁ ca medhāvī marmāṇi ca mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, that intelligent and mighty monkey marked her deformed and huge mouth, her body and its asticulated members.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्या विवृते वक्त्रे वज्रसंहननः कपिः
संक्षिप्य मुहुरात्मानं निष्पपात महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasyā vivṛte vaktre vajrasaṁhananaḥ kapiḥ
saṁkṣipya muhurātmānaṁ niṣpapāta mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And the redoubtable monkey hard as the thunderbolt, contracting himself in a moment, threw himself into her mouth.

verses.sanskrit:
आस्ये तस्या निमज्जन्तं ददृशुः सिद्धचारणाः
ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा
verses.transliteration:
āsye tasyā nimajjantaṁ dadṛśuḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ
grasyamānaṁ yathā candraṁ pūrṇaṁ parvaṇi rāhuṇā

translations.english: And the Siddhas and Chāraņas saw him sink in her mouth, as the full Moon is taken by Rāhu during a Parva.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तस्य नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्माण्युत्कृत्य वानरः
उत्पपाताथ वेगेन मनःसंपातविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tatastasya nakhaistīkṣṇairmarmāṇyutkṛtya vānaraḥ
utpapātātha vegena manaḥsaṁpātavikramaḥ

translations.english: Then tearing her limits by means of his sharp claws, the monkey, endowed with the celerity of thought, vehemently sprang forward.

verses.sanskrit:
तां हतां वानरेणाशु पतितां वीक्ष्य सिंहिकाम्
भूतान्याकाशचारीणि तमूचुः प्लवगर्षभम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ hatāṁ vānareṇāśu patitāṁ vīkṣya siṁhikām
bhūtānyākāśacārīṇi tamūcuḥ plavagarṣabham

translations.english: And seeing Sinhikā speedily slain by the monkey, and fallen, creatures ranging the sky addressed that foremost of monkeys, saying,

verses.sanskrit:
भीममद्य कृतं कर्म महत्सत्त्वं त्वया हतम्
साधयार्थमभिप्रेतमरिष्टं प्लवतां वर
verses.transliteration:
bhīmamadya kṛtaṁ karma mahatsattvaṁ tvayā hatam
sādhayārthamabhipretamariṣṭaṁ plavatāṁ vara

translations.english: Terrible is the deed that you had performed to day. Mighty was the creature that has been slaughtered by you. Compass you yours wishedfor end without let, О foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव
धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्यं स कर्मसु न सीदति
verses.transliteration:
yasya tvetāni catvāri vānarendra yathā tava
dhṛtirdṛṣṭirmatirdākṣyaṁ sa karmasu na sīdati

translations.english: He, O chief of monkeys, that, like you, is endowed with endurance, sharp sightedness, sense, and ability, dose not feel depressed in action.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः संभावितः पूज्यः प्रतिपन्नप्रयोजनः
जगामाकाशमाविश्य पन्नगाशनवत्कपिः
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ saṁbhāvitaḥ pūjyaḥ pratipannaprayojanaḥ
jagāmākāśamāviśya pannagāśanavatkapiḥ

translations.english: Honoured by these and wished well as to his purpose, that monkey, worthy of being honoured, set out, enveloping the sky, like him that subsist on serpents.* *Garuda.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तभूयिष्ठ पारस्तु सर्वतः प्रतिलोकयन्
योजनानां शतस्यान्ते वनराजिं ददर्श सः
verses.transliteration:
prāptabhūyiṣṭha pārastu sarvataḥ pratilokayan
yojanānāṁ śatasyānte vanarājiṁ dadarśa saḥ

translations.english: And it came to pass that as he had almost arrived at the other shore (of the ocean), he looking about on all sides at the end of an hundred yojanas saw a range of woods.

verses.sanskrit:
ददर्श च पतन्नेव विविधद्रुमभूषितम्
द्वीपं शाखामृगश्रेष्ठो मलयोपवनानि च
verses.transliteration:
dadarśa ca patanneva vividhadrumabhūṣitam
dvīpaṁ śākhāmṛgaśreṣṭho malayopavanāni ca

translations.english: As he went on, that best of monkeys saw an island decked with diverse trees, and groves pertaining Malaya.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरं सागरानूपान्सागरानूपजान्द्रुमान्
सागरस्य च पत्नीनां मुखान्यपि विलोकयन्
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraṁ sāgarānūpānsāgarānūpajāndrumān
sāgarasya ca patnīnāṁ mukhānyapi vilokayan

translations.english: He surveyed the sea, and lands bordering thereon, and trees growing on the sea shore, and the countenance of the spouses of the Sea.

verses.sanskrit:
स महामेघसंकाशं समीक्ष्यात्मानमात्मना
निरुन्धन्तमिवाकाशं चकार मतिमान्मतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa mahāmeghasaṁkāśaṁ samīkṣyātmānamātmanā
nirundhantamivākāśaṁ cakāra matimānmatim

translations.english: Surveying his own person resembling a mighty mass of clouds, and as if closing up the sky, that self-possessed one ascertained his course of action.

verses.sanskrit:
कायवृद्धिं प्रवेगं च मम दृष्ट्वैव राक्षसाः
मयि कौतूहलं कुर्युरिति मेने महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
kāyavṛddhiṁ pravegaṁ ca mama dṛṣṭvaiva rākṣasāḥ
mayi kautūhalaṁ kuryuriti mene mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Soon as the Rākṣasas shall behold my enlarged body and the vehemence of my motion, they shall be seized with curiosity concerning me.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसंनिभम्
पुनः प्रकृतिमापेदे वीतमोह इवात्मवान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śarīraṁ saṁkṣipya tanmahīdharasaṁnibham
punaḥ prakṛtimāpede vītamoha ivātmavān

translations.english: Thus thought that magnanimous one. Thereat diminishing that person of his resembling a mountain, that self-possessed one, purged on ignorance, resumed his natural shape.

verses.sanskrit:
स चारुनानाविधरूपधारी; परं समासाद्य समुद्रतीरम्
परैरशक्यप्रतिपन्नरूपः; समीक्षितात्मा समवेक्षितार्थः
verses.transliteration:
sa cārunānāvidharūpadhārī; paraṁ samāsādya samudratīram
parairaśakyapratipannarūpaḥ; samīkṣitātmā samavekṣitārthaḥ

translations.english: Thus wearing various graceful forms, that one, acting after reflection, having come to the other shore of the ocean incapable of being reached by others, on looking over his (immensely magnified person), reduced his body (to its former size).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स लम्बस्य गिरेः समृद्धे; विचित्रकूटे निपपात कूटे
सकेतकोद्दालकनालिकेरे; महाद्रिकूटप्रतिमो महात्मा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa lambasya gireḥ samṛddhe; vicitrakūṭe nipapāta kūṭe
saketakoddālakanālikere; mahādrikūṭapratimo mahātmā

translations.english: That high-souled one resembling a cloudy pavilion, alighted on the (foremost) summit of the splendid mountain, Samva; crested with picturesque peaks; and abounding in ketakas, uddalakas and cocoanuts.

verses.sanskrit:
स सागरं दानवपन्नगायुतं; बलेन विक्रम्य महोर्मिमालिनम्
निपत्य तीरे च महोदधेस्तदा; ददर्श लङ्काममरावतीमिव
verses.transliteration:
sa sāgaraṁ dānavapannagāyutaṁ; balena vikramya mahormimālinam
nipatya tīre ca mahodadhestadā; dadarśa laṅkāmamarāvatīmiva

translations.english: Having by main force bounded over the ocean heaving with surges, and rife with Dānavas and Pannagas, he alighting on the shore of the mighty main, beheld Lankā like to Amarāvati.

verses.sanskrit:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः
त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
sa sāgaramanādhṛṣyamatikramya mahābalaḥ
trikūṭaśikhare laṅkāṁ sthitāṁ svastho dadarśa ha

translations.english: Having crossed over the ocean incapable of being repressed, that one endowed with great strength, staying at the plateau of Chitrakūta, and having refreshed himself, cast his eyes on Laukā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पवर्षेण वीर्यवान्
अभिवृष्टः स्थितस्तत्र बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pādapamuktena puṣpavarṣeṇa vīryavān
abhivṛṣṭaḥ sthitastatra babhau puṣpamayo yathā

translations.english: And covered with showers of blossoms poured down by the trees, that monkey possessed of prowess then appeared there like Puspamaya.* *A monkey so named.

verses.sanskrit:
योजनानां शतं श्रीमांस्तीर्त्वाप्युत्तमविक्रमः
अनिश्वसन्कपिस्तत्र न ग्लानिमधिगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
yojanānāṁ śataṁ śrīmāṁstīrtvāpyuttamavikramaḥ
aniśvasankapistatra na glānimadhigacchati

translations.english: Having cleared an hundred Yoyanas, that monkey gifted with first-rate prowess, did not heave sighs or feel any fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
शतान्यहं योजनानां क्रमेयं सुबहून्यपि
किं पुनः सागरस्यान्तं संख्यातं शतयोजनम्
verses.transliteration:
śatānyahaṁ yojanānāṁ krameyaṁ subahūnyapi
kiṁ punaḥ sāgarasyāntaṁ saṁkhyātaṁ śatayojanam

translations.english: I am competent to bound over many hundreds of Yojanas. What then is this end of the ocean measuring an hundred Yojanas only?

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठः प्लवतामपि चोत्तमः
जगाम वेगवाँल्लङ्कां लङ्घयित्वा महोदधिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vīryavatāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ plavatāmapi cottamaḥ
jagāma vegavā̐llaṅkāṁ laṅghayitvā mahodadhim

translations.english: That foremost of those endowed with energy and the prime of monkeys, gifted with speed, went to Laikā,* having crossed over the mighty main. *Descending, remarks the commentator, from the mountain-summit.

verses.sanskrit:
शाद्वलानि च नीलानि गन्धवन्ति वनानि च
गण्डवन्ति च मध्येन जगाम नगवन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
śādvalāni ca nīlāni gandhavanti vanāni ca
gaṇḍavanti ca madhyena jagāma nagavanti ca

translations.english: Seeing blue lawns, and perfumed woods, replete with honey and filled with mountains, he held his way by the central thoroughfare.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलांश्च तरुसंछन्नान्वनराजीश्च पुष्पिताः
अभिचक्राम तेजस्वी हनुमान्प्लवगर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
śailāṁśca tarusaṁchannānvanarājīśca puṣpitāḥ
abhicakrāma tejasvī hanumānplavagarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: That foremost of monkeys, the energetic Hanumān, went by hills filled with trees, and ranges of blossoming woods.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्मिन्नचले तिष्ठन्वनान्युपवनानि च
स नगाग्रे च तां लङ्कां ददर्श पवनात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasminnacale tiṣṭhanvanānyupavanāni ca
sa nagāgre ca tāṁ laṅkāṁ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ

translations.english: And stationing himself in that mountain, the offspring of the Wind-god beheld woods and groves and Lankā established at the brow of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
पालितां राक्षसेन्द्रेण निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा
प्लवमानामिवाकाशे ददर्श हनुमान्पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
pālitāṁ rākṣasendreṇa nirmitāṁ viśvakarmaṇā
plavamānāmivākāśe dadarśa hanumānpurīm

translations.english: And that graceful monkey saw Lankā situated on the top of the mountain, filled with splendid yellow-white palaces, like to a city stationed in the sky ruled by the lord of Rākşasas and reared by Viśvakarmā himself. And the monkey, Hanumān, beheld Lankā, as if moving in the sky: with her walls furnished with daises for her hips, the immense waters and woods for her cloth, Śataghnīs and darts for her hair ends: and pennons on her walls for earrings, built as if by the agency of the Mind; and constructed by Viśvakarmā himself.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वारमुत्तरमासाद्य चिन्तयामास वानरः
कैलासशिखरप्रख्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्
ध्रियमाणमिवाकाशमुच्छ्रितैर्भवनोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
dvāramuttaramāsādya cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ
kailāsaśikharaprakhyamālikhantamivāmbaram
dhriyamāṇamivākāśamucchritairbhavanottamaiḥ

translations.english: And arriving at the Northern gate resembling the mansion of Kailāsa, and cleaving, as it were, the welkin, and as if holding the firmament with lofty and glorious edifices, and observing the sea; his dreadful enemy, Ravana; the city teeming with poisonous snakes, as well as the method of defence (displayed in it)-the monkeys reflected, Even if the monkeys came here, they should fail to achieve success; for Lankā is incapable of being taken in battle by the celestials themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां तु विषमां दुर्गां लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्
प्राप्यापि स महाबाहुः किं करिष्यति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ tu viṣamāṁ durgāṁ laṅkāṁ rāvaṇapālitām
prāpyāpi sa mahābāhuḥ kiṁ kariṣyati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Even if the mighty-armed Rāghava should reach this terrible-looking and impregnable Lankā reared by Rāvana, what could he do?

verses.sanskrit:
अवकाशो न सान्त्वस्य राक्षसेष्वभिगम्यते
न दानस्य न भेदस्य नैव युद्धस्य दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
avakāśo na sāntvasya rākṣaseṣvabhigamyate
na dānasya na bhedasya naiva yuddhasya dṛśyate

translations.english: Opportunity find I none either for conciliation with the Raksasas, or for (winning them over) by gifts, or for sowing dissensions among them, or for conquering them in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्णामेव हि गतिर्वानराणां महात्मनाम्
वालिपुत्रस्य नीलस्य मम राज्ञश्च धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
caturṇāmeva hi gatirvānarāṇāṁ mahātmanām
vāliputrasya nīlasya mama rājñaśca dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Of all the monkeys, four only endowed with (exceptional) celerity, viz., Vāli's son, Nīla, the intelligent king, and myself, heave the power to come over here.

verses.sanskrit:
यावज्जानामि वैदेहीं यदि जीवति वा न वा
तत्रैव चिन्तयिष्यामि दृष्ट्वा तां जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
yāvajjānāmi vaidehīṁ yadi jīvati vā na vā
tatraiva cintayiṣyāmi dṛṣṭvā tāṁ janakātmajām

translations.english: When I have ascertained whether Vaidehī is alive or not, I shall, after interviewing Janaka's daughter, think about this.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः
गिरिशृङ्गे स्थितस्तस्मिन्रामस्याभ्युदये रतः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa muhūrtaṁ kapikuñjaraḥ
giriśṛṅge sthitastasminrāmasyābhyudaye rataḥ

translations.english: Then that elephantine monkey, stationed on the summit of that mountain, for a while bethought himself as the success of Rāma.* *About rescuing his wife.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन रूपेण मया न शक्या रक्षसां पुरी
प्रवेष्टुं राक्षसैर्गुप्ता क्रूरैर्बलसमन्वितैः
verses.transliteration:
anena rūpeṇa mayā na śakyā rakṣasāṁ purī
praveṣṭuṁ rākṣasairguptā krūrairbalasamanvitaiḥ

translations.english: I cannot in this form succeed in entering the city of the Rākşasas, guarded by wily and powerful Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
उग्रौजसो महावीर्यो बलवन्तश्च राक्षसाः
वञ्चनीया मया सर्वे जानकीं परिमार्गिता
verses.transliteration:
ugraujaso mahāvīryo balavantaśca rākṣasāḥ
vañcanīyā mayā sarve jānakīṁ parimārgitā

translations.english: I should, while engaged in searching for Jānaki, deceive all the strong and highly energetic Rākşasas gifted with prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्येण रूपेण रात्रौ लङ्का पुरी मया
प्रवेष्टुं प्राप्तकालं मे कृत्यं साधयितुं महत्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣyālakṣyeṇa rūpeṇa rātrau laṅkā purī mayā
praveṣṭuṁ prāptakālaṁ me kṛtyaṁ sādhayituṁ mahat

translations.english: For attaining this mighty object, it behove me to enter Lankā at night in a shape invisible yet well suited to the end in view.

verses.sanskrit:
तां पुरीं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः
हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ purīṁ tādṛśīṁ dṛṣṭvā durādharṣāṁ surāsuraiḥ
hanūmāṁścintayāmāsa viniḥśvasya muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: Beholding the city in that state, difficult of being subdued by the celestials and Asuras (combined), Hanumān, sighing moment arily, thought within himself,

verses.sanskrit:
केनोपायेन पश्येयं मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम्
अदृष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
kenopāyena paśyeyaṁ maithilīṁ janakātmajām
adṛṣṭo rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena durātmanā

translations.english: How can I, without being discovered by the impious lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, succeed in seeing Janaka's daughter, Maithili?

verses.sanskrit:
न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं रामस्य विदितात्मनः
एकामेकश्च पश्येयं रहिते जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
na vinaśyetkathaṁ kāryaṁ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
ekāmekaśca paśyeyaṁ rahite janakātmajām

translations.english: How can the work of Rāma cognizant of self (be so managed that it) may not be brought to naught? How can I see Janaka's daughter singly in secret?

verses.sanskrit:
भूताश्चार्थो विपद्यन्ते देशकालविरोधिताः
विक्लवं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा
verses.transliteration:
bhūtāścārtho vipadyante deśakālavirodhitāḥ
viklavaṁ dūtamāsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā

translations.english: Works, almost accomplished, when entrusted to an inconsiderate emissary, are generally spoiled, out of season and out of place, like to darkness driven by the appearance of the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिर्निश्चितापि न शोभते
घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः
verses.transliteration:
arthānarthāntare buddhirniścitāpi na śobhate
ghātayanti hi kāryāṇi dūtāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ

translations.english: All those works, which are generally taken in hand after duly deliberating over their propriety and impropriety, are generally spoiled by those emissaries who are proud of their learing.

verses.sanskrit:
न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं वैक्लव्यं न कथं भवेत्
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
na vinaśyetkathaṁ kāryaṁ vaiklavyaṁ na kathaṁ bhavet
laṅghanaṁ ca samudrasya kathaṁ nu na vṛthā bhavet

translations.english: How can I so manage that my business may not suffer? How can I avoid recklessness? How can my bounding over the deep bear fruit?

verses.sanskrit:
मयि दृष्टे तु रक्षोभी रामस्य विदितात्मनः
भवेद्व्यर्थमिदं कार्यं रावणानर्थमिच्छतः
verses.transliteration:
mayi dṛṣṭe tu rakṣobhī rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
bhavedvyarthamidaṁ kāryaṁ rāvaṇānarthamicchataḥ

translations.english: On my being seen by the Rākşasas, the work of Rāma cognizant of self, desirous of the destruction of Ravana, shall be marred.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि शक्यं क्वचित्स्थातुमविज्ञातेन राक्षसैः
अपि राक्षसरूपेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्
verses.transliteration:
na hi śakyaṁ kvacitsthātumavijñātena rākṣasaiḥ
api rākṣasarūpeṇa kimutānyena kenacit

translations.english: Even if I wear a Rākşasa form, I cannot anywhere remain undiscovered by the Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
वायुरप्यत्र नाज्ञातश्चरेदिति मतिर्मम
न ह्यस्त्यविदितं किंचिद्राक्षसानां बलीयसाम्
verses.transliteration:
vāyurapyatra nājñātaścarediti matirmama
na hyastyaviditaṁ kiṁcidrākṣasānāṁ balīyasām

translations.english: What shall I say of any other form? Even the wind, I conceive dose not stray here, unperceived. Nothing whatever is here that is unknown to the Räkşasas of redoubtable deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
इहाहं यदि तिष्ठामि स्वेन रूपेण संवृतः
विनाशमुपयास्यामि भर्तुरर्थश्च हीयते
verses.transliteration:
ihāhaṁ yadi tiṣṭhāmi svena rūpeṇa saṁvṛtaḥ
vināśamupayāsyāmi bharturarthaśca hīyate

translations.english: Should I stay here embodied in my native form, I shall come by destruction; and the interest also of my master shall suffer.

verses.sanskrit:
तदहं स्वेन रूपेण रजन्यां ह्रस्वतां गतः
लङ्कामभिपतिष्यामि राघवस्यार्थसिद्धये
verses.transliteration:
tadahaṁ svena rūpeṇa rajanyāṁ hrasvatāṁ gataḥ
laṅkāmabhipatiṣyāmi rāghavasyārthasiddhaye

translations.english: Therefore, diminishing myself, I shall at night, for compassing the welfare of Rāghava, enter Lankā is my own form.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य पुरीं रात्रौ प्रविश्य सुदुरासदाम्
विचिन्वन्भवनं सर्वं द्रक्ष्यामि जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya purīṁ rātrau praviśya sudurāsadām
vicinvanbhavanaṁ sarvaṁ drakṣyāmi janakātmajām

translations.english: Entering at night Råvaņa's capital difficult of access, I shall, obtaining entry into every dwelling seek Janaka's daughter.'

verses.sanskrit:
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमान्सूर्यस्यास्तमयं कपिः
आचकाङ्क्षे तदा वीरा वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः
पृषदंशकमात्रः सन्बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
iti saṁcintya hanumānsūryasyāstamayaṁ kapiḥ
ācakāṅkṣe tadā vīrā vaidehyā darśanotsukaḥ
pṛṣadaṁśakamātraḥ sanbabhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ

translations.english: Having made up his mind thus, the heroic Hanumān, extremely eager to see Vaidehi, wished for the setting of the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदोषकाले हनुमांस्तूर्णमुत्पत्य वीर्यवान्
प्रविवेश पुरीं रम्यां सुविभक्तमहापथम्
verses.transliteration:
pradoṣakāle hanumāṁstūrṇamutpatya vīryavān
praviveśa purīṁ ramyāṁ suvibhaktamahāpatham

translations.english: At dusk, the powerful Hanumān, springing up, entered the charming city of Lankā with its well divided highways; furnished with rows of edifices having golden pillars, and net-works, resembling the metropolis of the Gandharvas.

verses.sanskrit:
सप्तभौमाष्टभौमैश्च स ददर्श महापुरीम्
तलैः स्फाटिकसंपूर्णैः कार्तस्वरविभूषितैः
verses.transliteration:
saptabhaumāṣṭabhaumaiśca sa dadarśa mahāpurīm
talaiḥ sphāṭikasaṁpūrṇaiḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitaiḥ

translations.english: He saw that splendid city containing sevenstoried and eight-storied edifices, studded with crystal and adorned with gold. And the dwellings of the Rākṣasas were embellished with these (ornaments).

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनानि विचित्राणि तोरणानि च रक्षसाम्
लङ्कामुद्द्योतयामासुः सर्वतः समलंकृताम्
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāni vicitrāṇi toraṇāni ca rakṣasām
laṅkāmuddyotayāmāsuḥ sarvataḥ samalaṁkṛtām

translations.english: And graceful golden gateways belonging to the Rākṣasas everywhere lent splendour to Lankā adorned all over.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्त्यामद्भुताकारां दृष्ट्वा लङ्कां महाकपिः
आसीद्विषण्णो हृष्टश्च वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः
verses.transliteration:
acintyāmadbhutākārāṁ dṛṣṭvā laṅkāṁ mahākapiḥ
āsīdviṣaṇṇo hṛṣṭaśca vaidehyā darśanotsukaḥ

translations.english: Beholding Lankā, wonderful and of inconceivable loveliness, the mighty monkey, desirous of beholding Vaidehī, became depressed and delighted at the same time.

verses.sanskrit:
स पाण्डुरोद्विद्धविमानमालिनीं; महार्हजाम्बूनदजालतोरणाम्
यशस्विनां रावणबाहुपालितां; क्षपाचरैर्भीमबलैः समावृताम्
verses.transliteration:
sa pāṇḍurodviddhavimānamālinīṁ; mahārhajāmbūnadajālatoraṇām
yaśasvināṁ rāvaṇabāhupālitāṁ; kṣapācarairbhīmabalaiḥ samāvṛtām

translations.english: And he (entered Lankā) engarlanded with yellow edifices joined together, with the ornamented arches of her gateways furnished with nets of precious gold; famed (all over the world); ruled by the arm of Ravana, and vigilantly guarded by night-rangers of dreadful strength.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रोऽपि साचिव्यमिवास्य कुर्वं;स्तारागणैर्मध्यगतो विराजन्
ज्योत्स्नावितानेन वितत्य लोक;मुत्तिष्ठते नैकसहस्ररश्मिः
verses.transliteration:
candro'pi sācivyamivāsya kurvaṁ;stārāgaṇairmadhyagato virājan
jyotsnāvitānena vitatya loka;muttiṣṭhate naikasahasraraśmiḥ

translations.english: As if ministering to him,* the Moon furnished with many thousands of rays arose with the stars in the midst of the sky, spreading lunar light over all creatures. * Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खप्रभं क्षीरमृणालवर्ण;मुद्गच्छमानं व्यवभासमानम्
ददर्श चन्द्रं स कपिप्रवीरः; पोप्लूयमानं सरसीव हंसं
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhaprabhaṁ kṣīramṛṇālavarṇa;mudgacchamānaṁ vyavabhāsamānam
dadarśa candraṁ sa kapipravīraḥ; poplūyamānaṁ sarasīva haṁsaṁ

translations.english: And that heroic monkey behold the Moon possessing the sheen of a conch, and hued like milk or the lotus-stalk, arisen and afloat (in the welkin), like a swan swimming in a tank.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रौञ्चबर्हिणसंघुष्टे राजहंसनिषेवितैः
तूर्याभरणनिर्घोषैः सर्वतः प्रतिनादिताम्
verses.transliteration:
krauñcabarhiṇasaṁghuṣṭe rājahaṁsaniṣevitaiḥ
tūryābharaṇanirghoṣaiḥ sarvataḥ pratināditām

translations.english: Resounding with Krauñca as and peacocks; frequented by swans, and everywhere resonant with the sounds of trumpets and ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
वस्वोकसाराप्रतिमां समीक्ष्य नगरीं ततः
खमिवोत्पतितां लङ्कां जहर्ष हनुमान्कपिः
verses.transliteration:
vasvokasārāpratimāṁ samīkṣya nagarīṁ tataḥ
khamivotpatitāṁ laṅkāṁ jaharṣa hanumānkapiḥ

translations.english: And then beholding the city Lankā, resembling Vasvokasāra,* and appearing to mount to the welkin, the monkey Hanumān was filled with rapture. *Alaka.

verses.sanskrit:
तां समीक्ष्य पुरीं लङ्कां राक्षसाधिपतेः शुभाम्
अनुत्तमामृद्धियुतां चिन्तयामास वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ samīkṣya purīṁ laṅkāṁ rākṣasādhipateḥ śubhām
anuttamāmṛddhiyutāṁ cintayāmāsa vīryavān

translations.english: And seeing the delightful,. divine and prosperous city of Lankā belonging to the lord of Rākşasas, that one endowed with prowess thought within himself,

verses.sanskrit:
नेयमन्येन नगरी शक्या धर्षयितुं बलात्
रक्षिता रावणबलैरुद्यतायुधधारिभिः
verses.transliteration:
neyamanyena nagarī śakyā dharṣayituṁ balāt
rakṣitā rāvaṇabalairudyatāyudhadhāribhiḥ

translations.english: This city protected by the forces of Rãvaņa with their hands holding upraised arms, is incapable of being forcibly subdued by any other.

verses.sanskrit:
कुमुदाङ्गदयोर्वापि सुषेणस्य महाकपेः
प्रसिद्धेयं भवेद्भूमिर्मैन्दद्विविदयोरपि
verses.transliteration:
kumudāṅgadayorvāpi suṣeṇasya mahākapeḥ
prasiddheyaṁ bhavedbhūmirmaindadvividayorapi

translations.english: This place can be easily entered by Kumuda, and Angada, as well as by that mighty monkey, Suşeņa; and also by Mainda and Dvivida. And there is way also for the offspring of the Sun, and that monkey, Kuśaparva, as well as of that foremost of monkeys, Rksya, and myself."

verses.sanskrit:
समीक्ष्य तु महाबाहो राघवस्य पराक्रमम्
लक्ष्मणस्य च विक्रान्तमभवत्प्रीतिमान्कपिः
verses.transliteration:
samīkṣya tu mahābāho rāghavasya parākramam
lakṣmaṇasya ca vikrāntamabhavatprītimānkapiḥ

translations.english: Having witnessed the prowess of Rāghava, as well as the vigour of Lakşmaņa, the monkey was filled with joy.

verses.sanskrit:
तां रत्नवसनोपेतां कोष्ठागारावतंसकाम्
यन्त्रागारस्तनीमृद्धां प्रमदामिव भूषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ ratnavasanopetāṁ koṣṭhāgārāvataṁsakām
yantrāgārastanīmṛddhāṁ pramadāmiva bhūṣitām

translations.english: And that redoubtable monkey beheld the metropolis of the monarch of the Räkşasas; having for her cloth the sea; for her pendants, cow-stalls and stables; for her breasts, turrets mounted on the walls for discharging missils, decked out like a damsel; with her darkness dispelled by bright lights and the mighty monkey son to the Wind-god was met by the city in her native shape.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टः सत्त्वसंपन्नो निशायां मारुतात्मजः
स महापथमास्थाय मुक्तापुष्पविराजितम्
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭaḥ sattvasaṁpanno niśāyāṁ mārutātmajaḥ
sa mahāpathamāsthāya muktāpuṣpavirājitam

translations.english: Entering in by night, the offspring of the Wind-god furnished with strength, proceeded along the high-way strewn with blossoms.

verses.sanskrit:
हसितोद्घुष्टनिनदैस्तूर्यघोष पुरः सरैः
वज्राङ्कुशनिकाशैश्च वज्रजालविभूषितैः
गृहमेधैः पुरी रम्या बभासे द्यौरिवाम्बुदैः
verses.transliteration:
hasitodghuṣṭaninadaistūryaghoṣa puraḥ saraiḥ
vajrāṅkuśanikāśaiśca vajrajālavibhūṣitaiḥ
gṛhamedhaiḥ purī ramyā babhāse dyaurivāmbudaiḥ

translations.english: The monkey held his way in the charming city of Lankā, resounding with grateful sounds mixed with laughter, and ringing with trumpet blasts. And with multitudes of mansions marked with the thunderbolt and the hook, and adorned with diamond windows, the charming metropolis looked splendid, like the welkin with clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजज्वाल तदा लङ्का रक्षोगणगृहैः शुभैः
सिताभ्रसदृशैश्चित्रैः पद्मस्वस्तिकसंस्थितैः
वर्धमानगृहैश्चापि सर्वतः सुविभाषितैः
verses.transliteration:
prajajvāla tadā laṅkā rakṣogaṇagṛhaiḥ śubhaiḥ
sitābhrasadṛśaiścitraiḥ padmasvastikasaṁsthitaiḥ
vardhamānagṛhaiścāpi sarvataḥ suvibhāṣitaiḥ

translations.english: Then Lankā, with handsome and variegated mansions of Rākṣasas, resembling white clouds and arranged like lotus-leaves; and adorned on all sides with structures superscribed 'Vardhamāna,' shone forth in all it glory.

verses.sanskrit:
तां चित्रमाल्याभरणां कपिराजहितंकरः
राघवार्थं चरञ्श्रीमान्ददर्श च ननन्द च
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ citramālyābharaṇāṁ kapirājahitaṁkaraḥ
rāghavārthaṁ carañśrīmāndadarśa ca nananda ca

translations.english: And that graceful one serving in the interests of the king of monkeys, ranging for Rāma's behoof, beheld (Lankā) adorned with variegated wreaths; and was highly delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्राव मधुरं गीतं त्रिस्थानस्वरभूषितम्
स्त्रीणां मदसमृद्धानां दिवि चाप्सरसामिव
verses.transliteration:
śuśrāva madhuraṁ gītaṁ tristhānasvarabhūṣitam
strīṇāṁ madasamṛddhānāṁ divi cāpsarasāmiva

translations.english: Moving from house to house, that foremost of monkeys observed on all sides various dwellings of diverse forms and colour, and heard charming songs chanted in the three octaves* by damsels maddened with amour, resembling celestial Apsaras. *The three octaves referred to are Mandra or the base tone, Madhyma or the middle tone, and Tara or the high tone. These constitute the entire diapason of Hindu Music..

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्राव काञ्चीनिनादं नूपुराणां च निःस्वनम्
सोपाननिनदांश्चैव भवनेषु महात्मनम्
आस्फोटितनिनादांश्च क्ष्वेडितांश्च ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
śuśrāva kāñcīninādaṁ nūpurāṇāṁ ca niḥsvanam
sopānaninadāṁścaiva bhavaneṣu mahātmanam
āsphoṭitaninādāṁśca kṣveḍitāṁśca tatastataḥ

translations.english: He also heard the jingling of zones and the clash of bangles; and sounds of footsteps on stairs of edifices belonging to high-souled ones; and sounds proceeding from clapping hands; and the roaring of lions here and there.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वाध्याय निरतांश्चैव यातुधानान्ददर्श सः
रावणस्तवसंयुक्तान्गर्जतो राक्षसानपि
verses.transliteration:
svādhyāya niratāṁścaiva yātudhānāndadarśa saḥ
rāvaṇastavasaṁyuktāngarjato rākṣasānapi

translations.english: And (Hanumān) heard there in the mansions of the Rākṣas, Mantras recited by persons engaged therein, and those occupied in Vaidika studies.

verses.sanskrit:
राजमार्गं समावृत्य स्थितं रक्षोबलं महत्
ददर्श मध्यमे गुल्मे राक्षसस्य चरान्बहून्
verses.transliteration:
rājamārgaṁ samāvṛtya sthitaṁ rakṣobalaṁ mahat
dadarśa madhyame gulme rākṣasasya carānbahūn

translations.english: And (Hanumān) saw goblins and Rākşasas storming and eulogizing Rāvana; and mighty swarms of Rākṣas stationed, covering the highway.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्तिवृक्षायुधांश्चैव पट्टिशाशनिधारिणः
क्षेपणीपाशहस्तांश्च ददर्श स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
śaktivṛkṣāyudhāṁścaiva paṭṭiśāśanidhāriṇaḥ
kṣepaṇīpāśahastāṁśca dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: And (Hanuman) saw also various weapons; and those having for their arms darts and vrikshas, or bearing patticas and asanis, or having Kshepanis* and nooses in their hands, saw that mighty monkey, or wearing wreaths, or having their persons daubed with pastes, or adorned with nobel ornaments, or clad in various kinds of raiment; and many a one ranging wherever he listed. *A short arrow thrown from the hand, or shot

verses.sanskrit:
भूषितं रुचिरद्वारं मत्तैश्च मृगपक्षिभिः
राक्षसाधिपतेर्गुप्तमाविवेश गृहं कपिः
verses.transliteration:
bhūṣitaṁ ruciradvāraṁ mattaiśca mṛgapakṣibhiḥ
rākṣasādhipaterguptamāviveśa gṛhaṁ kapiḥ

translations.english: The monkey entered the palace protected by the Rākṣasa chief, guarded by maddened beasts and birds, and thousands of gobbling endowed with exceeding great prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
हंसो यथा राजतपञ्जुरस्थः; सिंहो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः
वीरो यथा गर्वितकुञ्जरस्थ;श्चन्द्रोऽपि बभ्राज तथाम्बरस्थः
verses.transliteration:
haṁso yathā rājatapañjurasthaḥ; siṁho yathā mandarakandarasthaḥ
vīro yathā garvitakuñjarastha;ścandro'pi babhrāja tathāmbarasthaḥ

translations.english: Like a swan in a silver cage, like a lion in a cave in Mandara, like a hero on a haughty elephant, appeared the Moon in the middle of the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थितः ककुद्मानिव तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो; महाचलः श्वेत इवोच्चशृङ्गः
हस्तीव जाम्बूनदबद्धशृङ्गो; विभाति चन्द्रः परिपूर्णशृङ्गः
verses.transliteration:
sthitaḥ kakudmāniva tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo; mahācalaḥ śveta ivoccaśṛṅgaḥ
hastīva jāmbūnadabaddhaśṛṅgo; vibhāti candraḥ paripūrṇaśṛṅgaḥ

translations.english: the Moon resembled a sharp-horned bull, or a mighty white-hued hill with towering summits, or an elephant with his horns plated with gold. And with (the mark of) the horn.* *The sun. It is a planet in Hindu cosmogony.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकाशचन्द्रोदयनष्टदोषः; प्रवृद्धरक्षः पिशिताशदोषः
रामाभिरामेरितचित्तदोषः; स्वर्गप्रकाशो भगवान्प्रदोषः
verses.transliteration:
prakāśacandrodayanaṣṭadoṣaḥ; pravṛddharakṣaḥ piśitāśadoṣaḥ
rāmābhirāmeritacittadoṣaḥ; svargaprakāśo bhagavānpradoṣaḥ

translations.english: And now appeared the revered Mid-night, chasing away darkness with the Moon displayed, when flesh-eating (Raksasas) lend full liberty to their vicious appetite for flesh; and when disputes between lovers cease, and which bring down heaven itself.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्त्री स्वनाः कर्णसुखाः प्रवृत्ताः; स्वपन्ति नार्यः पतिभिः सुवृत्ताः
नक्तंचराश्चापि तथा प्रवृत्ता; विहर्तुमत्यद्भुतरौद्रवृत्ताः
verses.transliteration:
tantrī svanāḥ karṇasukhāḥ pravṛttāḥ; svapanti nāryaḥ patibhiḥ suvṛttāḥ
naktaṁcarāścāpi tathā pravṛttā; vihartumatyadbhutaraudravṛttāḥ

translations.english: The sounds of strings sweet to the ear spread around; females sleep besides their husbands; and night-rangers, given to astounding and terrible acts, are, in the same way, out, indulging in their sports.

verses.sanskrit:
मत्तप्रमत्तानि समाकुलानि; रथाश्वभद्रासनसंकुलानि
वीरश्रिया चापि समाकुलानि; ददर्श धीमान्स कपिः कुलानि
verses.transliteration:
mattapramattāni samākulāni; rathāśvabhadrāsanasaṁkulāni
vīraśriyā cāpi samākulāni; dadarśa dhīmānsa kapiḥ kulāni

translations.english: The intelligent monkey saw mansions crowded with (Raksasas), some inebriate with wine and other with wealth, and abounding in cars and horses and golden seats; and fraught with the grace got of heroism.

verses.sanskrit:
परस्परं चाधिकमाक्षिपन्ति; भुजांश्च पीनानधिविक्षिपन्ति
मत्तप्रलापानधिविक्षिपन्ति; मत्तानि चान्योन्यमधिक्षिपन्ति
verses.transliteration:
parasparaṁ cādhikamākṣipanti; bhujāṁśca pīnānadhivikṣipanti
mattapralāpānadhivikṣipanti; mattāni cānyonyamadhikṣipanti

translations.english: And (Raksasas) were parleying, moving about their plump arms, railing at each other; and throwing intemperate speeches at each other.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षांसि वक्षांसि च विक्षिपन्ति; गात्राणि कान्तासु च विक्षिपन्ति
ददर्श कान्ताश्च समालपन्ति; तथापरास्तत्र पुनः स्वपन्ति
verses.transliteration:
rakṣāṁsi vakṣāṁsi ca vikṣipanti; gātrāṇi kāntāsu ca vikṣipanti
dadarśa kāntāśca samālapanti; tathāparāstatra punaḥ svapanti

translations.english: (Hanumān saw) Raksasas striking at their chests (by way of challenge). sinking on the persons of their beloved, wearing diverse habiliments, or stretching their tough bows.

verses.sanskrit:
महागजैश्चापि तथा नदद्भिः; सूपूजितैश्चापि तथा सुसद्भिः
रराज वीरैश्च विनिःश्वसद्भि;र्ह्रदो भुजङ्गैरिव निःश्वसद्भिः
verses.transliteration:
mahāgajaiścāpi tathā nadadbhiḥ; sūpūjitaiścāpi tathā susadbhiḥ
rarāja vīraiśca viniḥśvasadbhi;rhrado bhujaṅgairiva niḥśvasadbhiḥ

translations.english: And with gigantic elephants roaring, (the place), honoured by pious persons, with its heroes heaving sighs looked exceedingly beautiful like a lake in which serpents are sighing forth.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिप्रधानान्रुचिराभिधाना;न्संश्रद्दधानाञ्जगतः प्रधानान्
नानाविधानान्रुचिराभिधाना;न्ददर्श तस्यां पुरि यातुधानान्
verses.transliteration:
buddhipradhānānrucirābhidhānā;nsaṁśraddadhānāñjagataḥ pradhānān
nānāvidhānānrucirābhidhānā;ndadarśa tasyāṁ puri yātudhānān

translations.english: In that apartment (Hanumān) saw persons of commanding understandings, endowed with a tongue, instinct with the spirit of reverence-the foremost men of all this world, and bearing euphonious appellations, and clad in diverse attires.

verses.sanskrit:
ननन्द दृष्ट्वा स च तान्सुरूपा;न्नानागुणानात्मगुणानुरूपान्
विद्योतमानान्स च तान्सुरूपा;न्ददर्श कांश्चिच्च पुनर्विरूपान्
verses.transliteration:
nananda dṛṣṭvā sa ca tānsurūpā;nnānāguṇānātmaguṇānurūpān
vidyotamānānsa ca tānsurūpā;ndadarśa kāṁścicca punarvirūpān

translations.english: And beholding those well-formed people, whose conduct was of a piece with their many virtues, (Hanumān) rejoiced exceedingly. And he saw some having beautiful forms, and others deformed, and both possessed of splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वरार्हाः सुविशुद्धभावा;स्तेषां स्त्रियस्तत्र महानुभावाः
प्रियेषु पानेषु च सक्तभावा; ददर्श तारा इव सुप्रभावाः
verses.transliteration:
tato varārhāḥ suviśuddhabhāvā;steṣāṁ striyastatra mahānubhāvāḥ
priyeṣu pāneṣu ca saktabhāvā; dadarśa tārā iva suprabhāvāḥ

translations.english: And (Hanumān) saw there their wives worthy of noble ornaments and endowed with eminent beauty; of spotless character; possessing great potency; like to stars in point of excellency of conduct, displaying side-glances and other tokens of dalliance, engaged in dear driking.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रिया ज्वलन्तीस्त्रपयोपगूढा; निशीथकाले रमणोपगूढाः
ददर्श काश्चित्प्रमदोपगूढा; यथा विहंगाः कुसुमोपगूडाः
verses.transliteration:
śriyā jvalantīstrapayopagūḍhā; niśīthakāle ramaṇopagūḍhāḥ
dadarśa kāścitpramadopagūḍhā; yathā vihaṁgāḥ kusumopagūḍāḥ

translations.english: At dead of night Hanuman saw some females blazing in beauty affected simultaneously with bashfulness and bliss, on being embraced by their paramours, like birds embracing their mates.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्याः पुनर्हर्म्यतलोपविष्टा;स्तत्र प्रियाङ्केषु सुखोपविष्टाः
भर्तुः प्रिया धर्मपरा निविष्टा; ददर्श धीमान्मनदाभिविष्टाः
verses.transliteration:
anyāḥ punarharmyatalopaviṣṭā;statra priyāṅkeṣu sukhopaviṣṭāḥ
bhartuḥ priyā dharmaparā niviṣṭā; dadarśa dhīmānmanadābhiviṣṭāḥ

translations.english: The sensible Hanumān saw there other females scated in stately halls, lying in happiness on the laps of their lovers, beloved of their lords-intent on virtue, married women, under the influence of Madana.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रावृताः काञ्चनराजिवर्णाः; काश्चित्परार्ध्यास्तपनीयवर्णाः
पुनश्च काश्चिच्छशलक्ष्मवर्णाः; कान्तप्रहीणा रुचिराङ्गवर्णाः
verses.transliteration:
aprāvṛtāḥ kāñcanarājivarṇāḥ; kāścitparārdhyāstapanīyavarṇāḥ
punaśca kāścicchaśalakṣmavarṇāḥ; kāntaprahīṇā rucirāṅgavarṇāḥ

translations.english: Hanumān saw some without sheets, like to golden streaks, paragons among women of the hue of molten gold, and some of a moon-like complexion, endued with lovelines, bereft of their beloved.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रियान्प्राप्य मनोऽभिरामा;न्सुप्रीतियुक्ताः प्रसमीक्ष्य रामाः
गृहेषु हृष्टाः परमाभिरामा; हरिप्रवीरः स ददर्श रामाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ priyānprāpya mano'bhirāmā;nsuprītiyuktāḥ prasamīkṣya rāmāḥ
gṛheṣu hṛṣṭāḥ paramābhirāmā; haripravīraḥ sa dadarśa rāmāḥ

translations.english: That exceedingly heroic monkey saw females in their homes experiencing the height of joy in the company of their beloved dear to their souls; charming with blossoms; filled with gladness; and enchaining the hearts of their lords with their loveiness

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रप्रकाशाश्च हि वक्त्रमाला; वक्राक्षिपक्ष्माश्च सुनेत्रमालाः
विभूषणानां च ददर्श मालाः; शतह्रदानामिव चारुमालाः
verses.transliteration:
candraprakāśāśca hi vaktramālā; vakrākṣipakṣmāśca sunetramālāḥ
vibhūṣaṇānāṁ ca dadarśa mālāḥ; śatahradānāmiva cārumālāḥ

translations.english: And Hanumān saw crowds of faces like to the Moon displayed, with elegant eyes furnished with lovely lashes, and side-long looks; an multitudes of ornaments resembling beautiful lines of lighting.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वेव सीतां परमाभिजातां; पथि स्थिते राजकुले प्रजाताम्
लतां प्रफुल्लामिव साधुजातां; ददर्श तन्वीं मनसाभिजाताम्
verses.transliteration:
na tveva sītāṁ paramābhijātāṁ; pathi sthite rājakule prajātām
latāṁ praphullāmiva sādhujātāṁ; dadarśa tanvīṁ manasābhijātām

translations.english: But Hanumān saw not Sītā, of the highest lineage, ever abiding by the way of righteousness; born in a royal line, like to a delightful and well-begot plant, of a slender frame, sprung from the mind (of Brahmä himself);

verses.sanskrit:
स निकामं विनामेषु विचरन्कामरूपधृक्
विचचार कपिर्लङ्कां लाघवेन समन्वितः
verses.transliteration:
sa nikāmaṁ vināmeṣu vicarankāmarūpadhṛk
vicacāra kapirlaṅkāṁ lāghavena samanvitaḥ

translations.english: Wending about at will on the roofs of sevenstoried edifices, that monkey capable of assuming any form that he chose, began Lankā with speed.

verses.sanskrit:
आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान्राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्
प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन भास्वरेणाभिसंवृतम्
verses.transliteration:
āsasādātha lakṣmīvānrākṣasendraniveśanam
prākāreṇārkavarṇena bhāsvareṇābhisaṁvṛtam

translations.english: And (at length) that auspicious one arrived at the mansion of the Rākṣasa chief, surrounded by a shining wall hued like the Sun;

verses.sanskrit:
तद्राजगुणसंपन्नं मुख्यैश्च वरचन्दनैः
भेरीमृदङ्गाभिरुतं शङ्खघोषविनादितम्
verses.transliteration:
tadrājaguṇasaṁpannaṁ mukhyaiśca varacandanaiḥ
bherīmṛdaṅgābhirutaṁ śaṅkhaghoṣavināditam

translations.english: Resonant with trumpets and drums; and ringing with the blares of conchs; where the ever adored offspring of the Parvas was always worshipped by the Rākşasas;

verses.sanskrit:
महात्मानो महद्वेश्म महारत्नपरिच्छदम्
महाजनसमाकीर्णं ददर्श स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
mahātmāno mahadveśma mahāratnaparicchadam
mahājanasamākīrṇaṁ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Solemn like the sea; and resounding like the ocean itself, the mighty mansion of the highsouled (Rāvana); clad in costly jewels; scattered with precious gems-as that mighty monkey beheld (Ravana's residence), he set about searching for Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
विराजमानं वपुषा गजाश्वरथसंकुलम्
लङ्काभरणमित्येव सोऽमन्यत महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
virājamānaṁ vapuṣā gajāśvarathasaṁkulam
laṅkābharaṇamityeva so'manyata mahākapiḥ

translations.english: That mighty monkey concluded, “This is the ornament of Larikā bodied forth beautifully to the view, covered with elephants, steeds and chariots."

verses.sanskrit:
गृहाद्गृहं राक्षसानामुद्यानानि च वानरः
वीक्षमाणो ह्यसंत्रस्तः प्रासादांश्च चचार सः
verses.transliteration:
gṛhādgṛhaṁ rākṣasānāmudyānāni ca vānaraḥ
vīkṣamāṇo hyasaṁtrastaḥ prāsādāṁśca cacāra saḥ

translations.english: And that monkey with a calm mind, eyeing (all round), ranged one house from another, and gardens, and stately piles.

verses.sanskrit:
अवप्लुत्य महावेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम्
ततोऽन्यत्पुप्लुवे वेश्म महापार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
avaplutya mahāvegaḥ prahastasya niveśanam
tato'nyatpupluve veśma mahāpārśvasya vīryavān

translations.english: Then that one endowed with wondrous motion, with a bound entered Prahasta's palace; and then with another, that (monkey) possessed of energy entered the into of Mahaparcwa.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ मेघप्रतीकाशं कुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम्
विभीषणस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
atha meghapratīkāśaṁ kumbhakarṇaniveśanam
vibhīṣaṇasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Then that inighty monkey entered into the abode of Kumbhakarna, resembling a mass of clouds; and thereafter that of Vibhisana;

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरस्य च तथा विरूपाक्षस्य चैव हि
विद्युज्जिह्वस्य भवनं विद्युन्मालेस्तथैव च
वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
mahodarasya ca tathā virūpākṣasya caiva hi
vidyujjihvasya bhavanaṁ vidyunmālestathaiva ca
vajradaṁṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: And then that of Mahodara, and then that of Virupaksha; and then the abode of Vidyujjibha, and then that of Vidyunmala;

verses.sanskrit:
शुकस्य च महावेगः सारणस्य च धीमतः
तथा चेन्द्रजितो वेश्म जगाम हरियूथपः
verses.transliteration:
śukasya ca mahāvegaḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
tathā cendrajito veśma jagāma hariyūthapaḥ

translations.english: And then that mighty monkey with a bound entered into the abode of Vahudanshtra. And then that leader of monkey-bands gifted with great speed leapt into the abode of Suka, and next into that of the intelligent Sarana.

verses.sanskrit:
जम्बुमालेः सुमालेश्च जगाम हरियूथपः
रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च
verses.transliteration:
jambumāleḥ sumāleśca jagāma hariyūthapaḥ
raśmiketośca bhavanaṁ sūryaśatrostathaiva ca

translations.english: And thus, next into that of Indrajit, and that foremost of monkeys went to the mansion of Jambumāla, and of Sumāla,

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु तेषु महार्हेषु भवनेषु महायशाः
तेषामृद्धिमतामृद्धिं ददर्श स महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
teṣu teṣu mahārheṣu bhavaneṣu mahāyaśāḥ
teṣāmṛddhimatāmṛddhiṁ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ

translations.english: In those costly mansions and dwellings, that famous one, that foremost of monkeys, burnt all the wealth of those affluent persons.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषां समतिक्रम्य भवनानि समन्ततः
आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान्राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣāṁ samatikramya bhavanāni samantataḥ
āsasādātha lakṣmīvānrākṣasendraniveśanam

translations.english: Having bounded over the mansions of all situated around, that blessed with one auspiciousness, at length came to the very mansion of the monarch of the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्योपशायिन्यो ददर्श हरिसत्तमः
विचरन्हरिशार्दूलो राक्षसीर्विकृतेक्षणाः
शूलमुद्गरहस्ताश्च शक्तो तोमरधारिणीः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasyopaśāyinyo dadarśa harisattamaḥ
vicaranhariśārdūlo rākṣasīrvikṛtekṣaṇāḥ
śūlamudgarahastāśca śakto tomaradhāriṇīḥ

translations.english: That tiger-like monkey-the best of his speciesranging around, saw Rākṣasis of frightful eyes, alternately mounting sentry over the couch of Rāvana-bearing darts and maces in their hands, and equipped with javelins and clubs.

verses.sanskrit:
सहस्रं वाहिनीस्तत्र जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः
हेमजालैरविच्छिन्नास्तरुणादित्यसंनिभाः
verses.transliteration:
sahasraṁ vāhinīstatra jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtāḥ
hemajālairavicchinnāstaruṇādityasaṁnibhāḥ

translations.english: That monkey, son to the Wind-god, saw in the mansion of the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, hosts by thousands; and cars of various forms of glittering gold, furnished all over with golden net-works, resembling the risen sun.

verses.sanskrit:
लतागृहाणि चित्राणि चित्रशालागृहाणि च
क्रीडागृहाणि चान्यानि दारुपर्वतकानपि
verses.transliteration:
latāgṛhāṇi citrāṇi citraśālāgṛhāṇi ca
krīḍāgṛhāṇi cānyāni dāruparvatakānapi

translations.english: And graceful grots; and picture galleries; and sporting saloons, mountains composed of wood, captivating structures dedicated to dalliance, and dwellings for day-dalliance,' saw he in the mansion of the Raksasa monarch. 1. Designed for sport. — 2. The conception of day-dalliance met with in Vidya Sundara of Bharata Chandra Roy, the Bengali poet, is found to have first originated with Vālimiki.

verses.sanskrit:
स मन्दरतलप्रख्यं मयूरस्थानसंकुलम्
ध्वजयष्टिभिराकीर्णं ददर्श भवनोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa mandaratalaprakhyaṁ mayūrasthānasaṁkulam
dhvajayaṣṭibhirākīrṇaṁ dadarśa bhavanottamam

translations.english: He beheld that charming mansion resembling Mandara, filled with places for peacocks* thronged with pennons and flagstaffs, a very mine of countless gems, a field of treasures spread around, where persons of intrepid calmness were engaged in acts tending to the safety of the treasures, resembling the mansion herself of Kubera. *Sportive peacocks.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्चिर्भिश्चापि रत्नानां तेजसा रावणस्य च
विरराजाथ तद्वेश्म रश्मिमानिव रश्मिभिः
verses.transliteration:
arcirbhiścāpi ratnānāṁ tejasā rāvaṇasya ca
virarājātha tadveśma raśmimāniva raśmibhiḥ

translations.english: On account of the lustre shed by the genes, as well as the energy of Rāvana himself, that mansion appeared splendid like the rayfurnished Sun in all his glory.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बूनदमयान्येव शयनान्यासनानि च
भाजनानि च शुभ्राणि ददर्श हरियूथपः
verses.transliteration:
jāmbūnadamayānyeva śayanānyāsanāni ca
bhājanāni ca śubhrāṇi dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ

translations.english: And the chief of monkey-bands saw bedsteads and seat of gold and white vessels.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रासादसंघातयुतं स्त्रीरत्नशतसंकुलम्
सुव्यूढकक्ष्यं हनुमान्प्रविवेश महागृहम्
verses.transliteration:
prāsādasaṁghātayutaṁ strīratnaśatasaṁkulam
suvyūḍhakakṣyaṁ hanumānpraviveśa mahāgṛham

translations.english: Hanumān entered the mighty mansion, filled with gemmed cans; charming; free from impediments; resembling the mansion herself of Kama, like the abode of Kubera, resonant with the sounds of bangles and the tinklings of zones, as well as with the beat of mridanga hides and other eloquent musical instruments; with palaces close on each other; thronged with hundreds of females (like to) jewels; and containing capacious enclosures. 1. Spirituous liquor distilled from the blossoms of the Bassia latifolia. According to some, a spirit distilled from grapes. 2. Spirit distilled from sugar or molasses. filled with gemmed cans; charming; free from impediments; resembling the mansion herself of Kama, like the abode of Kubera, resonant with the sounds of bangles and the tinklings of zones, as well as with the beat of mridanga hides and other eloquent musical instruments; with palaces close on each other; thronged with hundreds of females (like to) jewels; and containing capacious enclosures. 1. Spirituous liquor distilled from the blossoms of the Bassia latifolia. According to some, a spirit distilled from grapes. 2. Spirit distilled from sugar or molasses.

verses.sanskrit:
स वेश्मजालं बलवान्ददर्श; व्यासक्तवैदूर्यसुवर्णजालम्
यथा महत्प्रावृषि मेघजालं; विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहंगजालम्
verses.transliteration:
sa veśmajālaṁ balavāndadarśa; vyāsaktavaidūryasuvarṇajālam
yathā mahatprāvṛṣi meghajālaṁ; vidyutpinaddhaṁ savihaṁgajālam

translations.english: And that one endowed with strength saw that row of structures fitted up with golden windows, studded with lapis lazulis, and containing birds; like to a mass of clouds in a season of great rains, crowned with lightning, and fraught with fowls.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेशनानां विविधाश्च शालाः; प्रधानशङ्खायुधचापशालाः
मनोहराश्चापि पुनर्विशाला; ददर्श वेश्माद्रिषु चन्द्रशालाः
verses.transliteration:
niveśanānāṁ vividhāśca śālāḥ; pradhānaśaṅkhāyudhacāpaśālāḥ
manoharāścāpi punarviśālā; dadarśa veśmādriṣu candraśālāḥ

translations.english: He saw various structures close to one another to which excellent conchs, arms and bows lent lustre; as well as huge and splendid towers belonging to edifices resembling mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहाणि नानावसुराजितानि; देवासुरैश्चापि सुपूजितानि
सर्वैश्च दोषैः परिवर्जितानि; कपिर्ददर्श स्वबलार्जितानि
verses.transliteration:
gṛhāṇi nānāvasurājitāni; devāsuraiścāpi supūjitāni
sarvaiśca doṣaiḥ parivarjitāni; kapirdadarśa svabalārjitāni

translations.english: The monkey beheld mansions, treasuring various kinds of wealth, which were held in regard by both gods and Asuras, devoid of every defect; and which had been won (by Rāvana) through his own might.* Swavalenarjitam. Another meaning is: (mansions) into which Hanumān found entry through his own might.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि प्रयत्नाभिसमाहितानि; मयेन साक्षादिव निर्मितानि
महीतले सर्वगुणोत्तराणि; ददर्श लङ्काधिपतेर्गृहाणि
verses.transliteration:
tāni prayatnābhisamāhitāni; mayena sākṣādiva nirmitāni
mahītale sarvaguṇottarāṇi; dadarśa laṅkādhipatergṛhāṇi

translations.english: And (Hanumān) saw the mansions of the lord of Lankā, located in strict conformity with aesthetic laws, appearing as if they had been constructed by Maya himself, which had on the earth beneath every excellence.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा नगाग्रं बहुधातुचित्रं; यथा नभश्च ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम्
ददर्श युक्तीकृतमेघचित्रं; विमानरत्नं बहुरत्नचित्रम्
verses.transliteration:
yathā nagāgraṁ bahudhātucitraṁ; yathā nabhaśca grahacandracitram
dadarśa yuktīkṛtameghacitraṁ; vimānaratnaṁ bahuratnacitram

translations.english: And (Hanumān) saw the car variegated with countless gems; like unto the top of a mountain variegated with innumerable metals; or like the firmament with the moon and the planets, or like clouds of diverse hues fused into a homogeneous whole.

verses.sanskrit:
मही कृता पर्वतराजिपूर्णा; शैलाः कृता वृक्षवितानपूर्णाः
वृक्षाः कृताः पुष्पवितानपूर्णाः; पुष्पं कृतं केसरपत्रपूर्णम्
verses.transliteration:
mahī kṛtā parvatarājipūrṇā; śailāḥ kṛtā vṛkṣavitānapūrṇāḥ
vṛkṣāḥ kṛtāḥ puṣpavitānapūrṇāḥ; puṣpaṁ kṛtaṁ kesarapatrapūrṇam

translations.english: The place in the car designed as the seat of the many, was filled with rows of hills,* Composed of gold and gems. Its hills were filled with trees; its trees were filled flowers; and (finally) its flowers were filled with leaves and filaments.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतानि वेश्मानि च पाण्डुराणि; तथा सुपुष्पा अपि पुष्करिण्यः
पुनश्च पद्मानि सकेसराणि; धन्यानि चित्राणि तथा वनानि
verses.transliteration:
kṛtāni veśmāni ca pāṇḍurāṇi; tathā supuṣpā api puṣkariṇyaḥ
punaśca padmāni sakesarāṇi; dhanyāni citrāṇi tathā vanāni

translations.english: And (in it), where white mansions were reared, there were tank's filed with fair flowers; and lotuses furnished with filaments; and picturesque woods; and liquid lapses.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पाह्वयं नाम विराजमानं; रत्नप्रभाभिश्च विवर्धमानम्
वेश्मोत्तमानामपि चोच्चमानं; महाकपिस्तत्र महाविमानम्
verses.transliteration:
puṣpāhvayaṁ nāma virājamānaṁ; ratnaprabhābhiśca vivardhamānam
veśmottamānāmapi coccamānaṁ; mahākapistatra mahāvimānam

translations.english: And the mighty monkey beheld there the great chariot going after the name of Pushpa, appearing beautiful, wheeling round in the splendour of the gems—which had surpassed cven the cars pertaining to the abodes of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
कृताश्च वैदूर्यमया विहंगा; रूप्यप्रवालैश्च तथा विहंगाः
चित्राश्च नानावसुभिर्भुजंगा; जात्यानुरूपास्तुरगाः शुभाङ्गाः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtāśca vaidūryamayā vihaṁgā; rūpyapravālaiśca tathā vihaṁgāḥ
citrāśca nānāvasubhirbhujaṁgā; jātyānurūpāsturagāḥ śubhāṅgāḥ

translations.english: And in that car) were birds made of lapis lazulis; and (other) birds composed of silver and coral; and variegated serpents made of various precious metals; and fair-bodied steeds resembling those of superior breeds; and there were constructed birds having graceful mouths; and fair, tapering, playful and contracted plumage, bearing blossoms made of coral and gold, like to the very plumage of Kama himself.

verses.sanskrit:
नियुज्यमानाश्च गजाः सुहस्ताः; सकेसराश्चोत्पलपत्रहस्ताः
बभूव देवी च कृता सुहस्ता; लक्ष्मीस्तथा पद्मिनि पद्महस्ता
verses.transliteration:
niyujyamānāśca gajāḥ suhastāḥ; sakesarāścotpalapatrahastāḥ
babhūva devī ca kṛtā suhastā; lakṣmīstathā padmini padmahastā

translations.english: There were elephants possessed of graceful trunks, bearing filaments; and with their trunks bearing lotus leaves, engaged in showering water on Lakshmi); as well as the goddess, made with fair arms, seated on a pool with a lotus in her hand.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव तद्गृहमभिगम्य शोभनं; सविस्मयो नगमिव चारुशोभनम्
पुनश्च तत्परमसुगन्धि सुन्दरं; हिमात्यये नगमिव चारुकन्दरम्
verses.transliteration:
itīva tadgṛhamabhigamya śobhanaṁ; savismayo nagamiva cāruśobhanam
punaśca tatparamasugandhi sundaraṁ; himātyaye nagamiva cārukandaram

translations.english: Thus entering that graceful mansion, like to a mountain containing charming caverns, (Hanumān) was seized with wonderment. And once again (entering that charming mansion), like to a taking and fragrant tree during spring furnished with holes, Hanumān was seized with wonderment.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स तां कपिरभिपत्य पूजितां; चरन्पुरीं दशमुखबाहुपालिताम्
अदृश्य तां जनकसुतां सुपूजितां; सुदुःखितां पतिगुणवेगनिर्जिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa tāṁ kapirabhipatya pūjitāṁ; caranpurīṁ daśamukhabāhupālitām
adṛśya tāṁ janakasutāṁ supūjitāṁ; suduḥkhitāṁ patiguṇaveganirjitām

translations.english: Then ranging by bounds that honoured city ruled by the arms of the Ten faced one, he, not finding the highly regarded and extremely distressed daughter of Janaka, who had won over her grief by contemplating the virtues of her lord, (was affected with sorrow).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तदा बहुविधभावितात्मनः; कृतात्मनो जनकसुतां सुवर्त्मनः
अपश्यतोऽभवदतिदुःखितं मनः; सुचक्षुषः प्रविचरतो महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
tatastadā bahuvidhabhāvitātmanaḥ; kṛtātmano janakasutāṁ suvartmanaḥ
apaśyato'bhavadatiduḥkhitaṁ manaḥ; sucakṣuṣaḥ pravicarato mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: And, not seeing Janaka's daughter, then the heart of that high-souled one, honoured for his character by the entire world, of schooled self, ever ranging by the way chiming in with morality, and having the scriptures for his eyesight, as he ranged about, was oppressed with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्धयोजनविस्तीर्णमायतं योजनं हि तत्
भवनं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बहुप्रासादसंकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
ardhayojanavistīrṇamāyataṁ yojanaṁ hi tat
bhavanaṁ rākṣasendrasya bahuprāsādasaṁkulam

translations.english: And located within that excellent mansion, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, saw a superior and grand structure, stainless and spacious; half a Yojana in width and one in lenght, belonging to the lord of the Rākşasas, and abounding with many a palace.

verses.sanskrit:
मार्गमाणस्तु वैदेहीं सीतामायतलोचनाम्
सर्वतः परिचक्राम हनूमानरिसूदनः
verses.transliteration:
mārgamāṇastu vaidehīṁ sītāmāyatalocanām
sarvataḥ paricakrāma hanūmānarisūdanaḥ

translations.english: Searching for Videha's daughter, the large eyed Sītā, that slayer of enemies, Hanumān, ranged all through (this edifice).

verses.sanskrit:
चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च
परिक्षिप्तमसंबाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः
verses.transliteration:
caturviṣāṇairdviradaistriviṣāṇaistathaiva ca
parikṣiptamasaṁbādhaṁ rakṣyamāṇamudāyudhaiḥ

translations.english: Hanumān beheld the goodly edifice where the Rāksasas used to dwell in common. And (at length) that one came upon the mansion itself of the lord of Rākşasas, having three-tusked and four-tusked elephants, and protected by persons with upraised arms, and covering a capacious area.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम्
आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasībhiśca patnībhī rāvaṇasya niveśanam
āhṛtābhiśca vikramya rājakanyābhirāvṛtam

translations.english: And (Hanumān beheld) the residence of Rāvana thronged with his Rākṣasi wives, as well as with princesses forcibly brought thither (by him), like to the sea teeming with alligators and Makaras, abounding in timingilas and fishes and snakes, and agitated by the force of the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च
तादृशी तद्विशिष्टा वा ऋद्धी रक्षो गृहेष्विह
verses.transliteration:
yā ca rājñaḥ kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca
tādṛśī tadviśiṣṭā vā ṛddhī rakṣo gṛheṣviha

translations.english: The same enchanting splendour that is in Vaiśravaņa or the ray-riding Moon, remained ever constant and abiding in, Rāvana's abode. And the prosperity of king Kubera, or Yama, or Varuna, was here present in the house of the Rākşas, or even surpassed by the prosperity (of Rāvana).

verses.sanskrit:
