ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा
विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
brahmaṇo'rthe kṛtaṁ divyaṁ divi yadviśvakarmaṇā
vimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ nāma sarvaratnavibhūṣitam

translations.english: In the midst of that mansion the Wind-god's offspring found another.* excellently constructed, having innumerable mad elephants; that noble car embellished with all gems, entitled Pushpaka, which had been constructed in heaven by Viśvakarmă for Brahmā himself. *The car Puspaka, according to Tirtha, whose view is accepted by Rāmānuja. According to Kataka, Vesma means a bedchamber of husband and wife.

verses.sanskrit:
परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात्
कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
pareṇa tapasā lebhe yatkuberaḥ pitāmahāt
kuberamojasā jitvā lebhe tadrākṣaseśvaraḥ

translations.english: Which Kubera obtained for the Great-father through high austerities, and which, vanquishing Kubera by his prowess, the Rākṣasa chief god possession of.

verses.sanskrit:
स गन्धस्तं महासत्त्वं बन्धुर्बन्धुमिवोत्तमम्
इत एहीत्युवाचेव तत्र यत्र स रावणः
verses.transliteration:
sa gandhastaṁ mahāsattvaṁ bandhurbandhumivottamam
ita ehītyuvāceva tatra yatra sa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: And stationed thereon, Hanumān smelt the rich odour of viands and drinks that was spreading on all sides; and like one dear friend smelling another, he also smelt the mighty Air, impregnated with aroma, which seemed like embodied Odour. And (the Air) said to Hanumãn, "Come here, where that Rāvana is." 'i.e. on Puspaka.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वर्गोऽयं देवलोकोऽयमिन्द्रस्येयं पुरी भवेत्
सिद्धिर्वेयं परा हि स्यादित्यमन्यत मारुतिः
verses.transliteration:
svargo'yaṁ devaloko'yamindrasyeyaṁ purī bhavet
siddhirveyaṁ parā hi syādityamanyata mārutiḥ

translations.english: This must be svarga, or the region of the immortals, or the city of Amarāvatī, or the supreme Siddhit thought the Wind-god's offspring Svarga is the region where persons reap the fruit of Jyotishtoma, etc. Siddhi is Illusion spread by Gandharvas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रध्यायत इवापश्यत्प्रदीपांस्तत्र काञ्चनान्
धूर्तानिव महाधूर्तैर्देवनेन पराजितान्
verses.transliteration:
pradhyāyata ivāpaśyatpradīpāṁstatra kāñcanān
dhūrtāniva mahādhūrtairdevanena parājitān

translations.english: And he saw the golden lamps (shorn of their brightness),* like to gamblers worsted at dice by others exceedingly skilful, and, in consequence, plunged in thought. * By the superior splendour of Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
दीपानां च प्रकाशेन तेजसा रावणस्य च
अर्चिर्भिर्भूषणानां च प्रदीप्तेत्यभ्यमन्यत
verses.transliteration:
dīpānāṁ ca prakāśena tejasā rāvaṇasya ca
arcirbhirbhūṣaṇānāṁ ca pradīptetyabhyamanyata

translations.english: And (Hanumān) conceived that (Rāvana's sleeping apartment) was in a conflagration, on account of the display of the lamps, Rāvana's energy, and the splendour of the ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽपश्यत्कुथासीनं नानावर्णाम्बरस्रजम्
सहस्रं वरनारीणां नानावेषविभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'paśyatkuthāsīnaṁ nānāvarṇāmbarasrajam
sahasraṁ varanārīṇāṁ nānāveṣavibhūṣitam

translations.english: And when the night had been half spent, (Hanuman) saw thousands of superb dames, adorned in various attires, and bearing apparels of diverse hues, and wreaths, who having given up sport, and come under the influence of wine and sleep, were fast asleep on woollen sheets.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्प्रसुप्तं विरुरुचे निःशब्दान्तरभूषणम्
निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरं यथा पद्मवनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
tatprasuptaṁ viruruce niḥśabdāntarabhūṣaṇam
niḥśabdahaṁsabhramaraṁ yathā padmavanaṁ mahat

translations.english: And in consequence of the silence that reigned (in the apartment) embellished with (ornaments), it resembled a large lotus-grove, where the swans and the black bees are silent.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां संवृतदन्तानि मीलिताक्षाणि मारुतिः
अपश्यत्पद्मगन्धीनि वदनानि सुयोषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ saṁvṛtadantāni mīlitākṣāṇi mārutiḥ
apaśyatpadmagandhīni vadanāni suyoṣitām

translations.english: And the Wind-god's offspring beheld the countenance of those beauteous women, with closed eyes, having their lashes shut through languor; and odorous with lotus-perfume.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रबुद्धानीव पद्मानि तासां भूत्वा क्षपाक्षये
पुनःसंवृतपत्राणि रात्राविव बभुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
prabuddhānīva padmāni tāsāṁ bhūtvā kṣapākṣaye
punaḥsaṁvṛtapatrāṇi rātrāviva babhustadā

translations.english: And their faces appeared like lotuses blowing on the expire of night and closing their petals by night.

verses.sanskrit:
इति वामन्यत श्रीमानुपपत्त्या महाकपिः
मेने हि गुणतस्तानि समानि सलिलोद्भवैः
verses.transliteration:
iti vāmanyata śrīmānupapattyā mahākapiḥ
mene hi guṇatastāni samāni salilodbhavaiḥ

translations.english: “These lotus-faces like to very lotuses themselves, ever the six-footed ones* seek once and again.” Thus thought with discrimination the graceful, mighty. monkey; and on account of their perfections, he confessed those countenances to be equal to water-sprung (lotuses). * Şatpadā—six-footed—a name of the black bee. "Salitodbhavas, water spiung—a name of the lotus.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिः स्त्रीभिर्विराजिता
शारदीव प्रसन्ना द्यौस्ताराभिरभिशोभिता
verses.transliteration:
sā tasya śuśubhe śālā tābhiḥ strībhirvirājitā
śāradīva prasannā dyaustārābhirabhiśobhitā

translations.english: And that apartment, in consequence of being graced by those women, appeared splendid, like the autumnal, complacent sky decorated with the stars.

verses.sanskrit:
स च ताभिः परिवृतः शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः
यथा ह्युडुपतिः श्रीमांस्ताराभिरभिसंवृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa ca tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ
yathā hyuḍupatiḥ śrīmāṁstārābhirabhisaṁvṛtaḥ

translations.english: And surrounded by them, the Rākṣasa chief resembled the fair Moon encircled by the stars.

verses.sanskrit:
याश्च्यवन्तेऽम्बरात्ताराः पुण्यशेषसमावृताः
इमास्ताः संगताः कृत्स्ना इति मेने हरिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
yāścyavante'mbarāttārāḥ puṇyaśeṣasamāvṛtāḥ
imāstāḥ saṁgatāḥ kṛtsnā iti mene haristadā

translations.english: “Those stars that drop from the firmament on their virtue deteriorating, have assembled here in a body," thus thought the monkey at that time.

verses.sanskrit:
ताराणामिव सुव्यक्तं महतीनां शुभार्चिषाम्
प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च विरेजुस्तत्र योषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tārāṇāmiva suvyaktaṁ mahatīnāṁ śubhārciṣām
prabhāvarṇaprasādāśca virejustatra yoṣitām

translations.english: And the shine, form, and splendour of those females resembled, forsooth those of magnificently displayed, noble and lustrous stars.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यावृत्तगुरुपीनस्रक्प्रकीर्णवरभूषणाः
पानव्यायामकालेषु निद्रापहृतचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
vyāvṛttagurupīnasrakprakīrṇavarabhūṣaṇāḥ
pānavyāyāmakāleṣu nidrāpahṛtacetasaḥ

translations.english: And on account of their having been bereft of consciousness through sleep, induced by fatigue brought on by drink (and dance), their hair was dishevelled, and their full wreaths and goodly ornaments lay scattered about.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यावृत्ततिलकाः काश्चित्काश्चिदुद्भ्रान्तनूपुराः
पार्श्वे गलितहाराश्च काश्चित्परमयोषितः
verses.transliteration:
vyāvṛttatilakāḥ kāścitkāścidudbhrāntanūpurāḥ
pārśve galitahārāśca kāścitparamayoṣitaḥ

translations.english: And some of those paragons had got their beauty-spots, smudged; and some, their bangles loosening off, some, their chains running to one side.

verses.sanskrit:
मुखा हारवृताश्चान्याः काश्चित्प्रस्रस्तवाससः
व्याविद्धरशना दामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
mukhā hāravṛtāścānyāḥ kāścitprasrastavāsasaḥ
vyāviddharaśanā dāmāḥ kiśorya iva vāhitāḥ

translations.english: And others had their pearl necklaces burst, and their cloths getting away (from their persons), and the chains of their zones straying irregularly; resembling way-worn mares.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकुण्डलधराश्चान्या विच्छिन्नमृदितस्रजः
गजेन्द्रमृदिताः फुल्ला लता इव महावने
verses.transliteration:
sukuṇḍaladharāścānyā vicchinnamṛditasrajaḥ
gajendramṛditāḥ phullā latā iva mahāvane

translations.english: And others again were without their ear-rings, and had their garlands torn and crushed; and resembled blossoming creepers, trodden down in a vast forest by mighty elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च हाराः कासांचिदुत्कटाः
हंसा इव बभुः सुप्ताः स्तनमध्येषु योषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
candrāṁśukiraṇābhāśca hārāḥ kāsāṁcidutkaṭāḥ
haṁsā iva babhuḥ suptāḥ stanamadhyeṣu yoṣitām

translations.english: And the pearl chains of some shining females resembling moon beams, having got topsy-turvy, was lying like sleeping swans between the breasts of the damsels.

verses.sanskrit:
अपरासां च वैदूर्याः कादम्बा इव पक्षिणः
हेमसूत्राणि चान्यासां चक्रवाका इवाभवन्
verses.transliteration:
aparāsāṁ ca vaidūryāḥ kādambā iva pakṣiṇaḥ
hemasūtrāṇi cānyāsāṁ cakravākā ivābhavan

translations.english: And the lapis chains of some resembled water-crows;* and the fine golden chains turned upside down of other appeared like ruddy geese. *Kadamba-a drake; or, according to some, a teal; a gander; or the species gallinula porphyria.

verses.sanskrit:
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः
आपगा इव ता रेजुर्जघनैः पुलिनैरिव
verses.transliteration:
haṁsakāraṇḍavākīrṇāścakravākopaśobhitāḥ
āpagā iva tā rejurjaghanaiḥ pulinairiva

translations.english: And those ladies resembled rivers having hips for banks; containing swans and Karandavas, and beautified with ruddy geese.

verses.sanskrit:
किङ्किणीजालसंकाशास्ता हेमविपुलाम्बुजाः
भावग्राहा यशस्तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इवाबभुः
verses.transliteration:
kiṅkiṇījālasaṁkāśāstā hemavipulāmbujāḥ
bhāvagrāhā yaśastīrāḥ suptā nadya ivābabhuḥ

translations.english: Those sleeping females appeared like streams; having Kinkiņis for their ripples; and large gold lotuses;* marks* of amorous encounter on their persons for ferocious aquatic animals; and perfections,** for their banks. 'i.e. the faces of the females are meant. Another meaning is, gold for large lotuses. *Vilasa, may also mean arch displays by way of ecquetry. **Yasa, according to some, here means grace.

verses.sanskrit:
मृदुष्वङ्गेषु कासांचित्कुचाग्रेषु च संस्थिताः
बभूवुर्भूषणानीव शुभा भूषणराजयः
verses.transliteration:
mṛduṣvaṅgeṣu kāsāṁcitkucāgreṣu ca saṁsthitāḥ
babhūvurbhūṣaṇānīva śubhā bhūṣaṇarājayaḥ

translations.english: On the tender frames, as well as on the tops of the breasts, of graceful scratches consequent pressure, appeared like ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
अंशुकान्ताश्च कासांचिन्मुखमारुतकम्पिताः
उपर्युपरि वक्त्राणां व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
aṁśukāntāśca kāsāṁcinmukhamārutakampitāḥ
uparyupari vaktrāṇāṁ vyādhūyante punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: The scarf-ends of some stirred by the air that some on was blowing about their faces, flapped on them again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
ताः पाताका इवोद्धूताः पत्नीनां रुचिरप्रभाः
नानावर्णसुवर्णानां वक्त्रमूलेषु रेजिरे
verses.transliteration:
tāḥ pātākā ivoddhūtāḥ patnīnāṁ ruciraprabhāḥ
nānāvarṇasuvarṇānāṁ vaktramūleṣu rejire

translations.english: At the nether part of the faces of Rāvana's wives, they (the scarf-ends) appeared beauteous like uplifted streamers of exceeding elegance, composed of many-hued golden yarn.

verses.sanskrit:
ववल्गुश्चात्र कासांचित्कुण्डलानि शुभार्चिषाम्
मुखमारुतसंसर्गान्मन्दं मन्दं सुयोषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
vavalguścātra kāsāṁcitkuṇḍalāni śubhārciṣām
mukhamārutasaṁsargānmandaṁ mandaṁ suyoṣitām

translations.english: The ear-rings of some dames possessed of a pleasant sheen, stirred by the air that was breathing about their faces, were undulating gently.

verses.sanskrit:
शर्करासवगन्धः स प्रकृत्या सुरभिः सुखः
तासां वदननिःश्वासः सिषेवे रावणं तदा
verses.transliteration:
śarkarāsavagandhaḥ sa prakṛtyā surabhiḥ sukhaḥ
tāsāṁ vadananiḥśvāsaḥ siṣeve rāvaṇaṁ tadā

translations.english: The sweet breath of their faces, naturally fragrani, and redolent of sugar and asava, was then rogaling Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणाननशङ्काश्च काश्चिद्रावणयोषितः
मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनामुपाजिघ्रन्पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇānanaśaṅkāśca kāścidrāvaṇayoṣitaḥ
mukhāni sma sapatnīnāmupājighranpunaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Out of fear sprung from sleep and intoxication, some of Rāvana's wives were again and again smelling the faces of those, co-wives with them, taking the faces to belong to Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्यर्थं सक्तमनसो रावणे ता वरस्त्रियः
अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनां प्रियमेवाचरंस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
atyarthaṁ saktamanaso rāvaṇe tā varastriyaḥ
asvatantrāḥ sapatnīnāṁ priyamevācaraṁstadā

translations.english: From their hearts being firmly fixed on Ravana, those excellent women, having their sense of separateness removed, (albeit thus dealt with), did what was dear to them.* *The sense is very imperspicusous only by reason of he unskilful use of the pronouns. The damsels kissed did not resent the act; but kissed the kissers in turn.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहूनुपनिधायान्याः पारिहार्य विभूषिताः
अंशुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदास्तत्र शिश्यिरे
verses.transliteration:
bāhūnupanidhāyānyāḥ pārihārya vibhūṣitāḥ
aṁśukāni ca ramyāṇi pramadāstatra śiśyire

translations.english: Other females, making their gay scarf-ends (for their sheets), and making their arms, their pillows, were lying down there.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्या वक्षसि चान्यस्यास्तस्याः काचित्पुनर्भुजम्
अपरा त्वङ्कमन्यस्यास्तस्याश्चाप्यपरा भुजौ
verses.transliteration:
anyā vakṣasi cānyasyāstasyāḥ kācitpunarbhujam
aparā tvaṅkamanyasyāstasyāścāpyaparā bhujau

translations.english: And some were lying on others' bosoms; and others again, on the arms of the latter. And some lay on the laps of others; and others, again, on the breasts of the latter.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊरुपार्श्वकटीपृष्ठमन्योन्यस्य समाश्रिताः
परस्परनिविष्टाङ्ग्यो मदस्नेहवशानुगाः
verses.transliteration:
ūrupārśvakaṭīpṛṣṭhamanyonyasya samāśritāḥ
parasparaniviṣṭāṅgyo madasnehavaśānugāḥ

translations.english: They reposed on each other's thighs, flanks, waists, and backs; and coming under the influence of wine and amour, they lay on each other's persons.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यस्याङ्गसंस्पर्शात्प्रीयमाणाः सुमध्यमाः
एकीकृतभुजाः सर्वाः सुषुपुस्तत्र योषितः
verses.transliteration:
anyonyasyāṅgasaṁsparśātprīyamāṇāḥ sumadhyamāḥ
ekīkṛtabhujāḥ sarvāḥ suṣupustatra yoṣitaḥ

translations.english: Those females having elegant waists, receiving pleasure from the contact with others' persons, were sleeping there, with their hands fastened by each other.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यभुजसूत्रेण स्त्रीमालाग्रथिता हि सा
मालेव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्तषट्पदा
verses.transliteration:
anyonyabhujasūtreṇa strīmālāgrathitā hi sā
māleva grathitā sūtre śuśubhe mattaṣaṭpadā

translations.english: That garland of females strung by the threads of their hands, appeared beauteous, like a real wreath strung on a thread, with maddened black bees (seated thereon).

verses.sanskrit:
लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात्
अन्योन्यमालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम्
verses.transliteration:
latānāṁ mādhave māsi phullānāṁ vāyusevanāt
anyonyamālāgrathitaṁ saṁsaktakusumoccayam

translations.english: That multitude of females in a mediey appeared like an assemblage of blooming plants in the month of Caitra,* with its wreaths formed in consequence of their coming in contact with one another, and of its clusters touching each other, on account of the breeze blowing; with the plants encircling the graceful (necks of the trees), and rife with Bhramaras chasing each other. 'March-April.

verses.sanskrit:
उचितेष्वपि सुव्यक्तं न तासां योषितां तदा
विवेकः शक्य आधातुं भूषणाङ्गाम्बरस्रजाम्
verses.transliteration:
uciteṣvapi suvyaktaṁ na tāsāṁ yoṣitāṁ tadā
vivekaḥ śakya ādhātuṁ bhūṣaṇāṅgāmbarasrajām

translations.english: Although the ornaments of those women wearing ornaments, attires and wreaths, were put on proper places; yet (on account of the profusion of the ornaments themselves, as well as because of the circumstance of the dames sleeping, * it was difficult to ascertain which ornament belonged to one damsel and which to another. *In consequence also, remarks the commentator, of the uniformity running through the ornaments, as well as of the close contact of the persons of the ladies.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणे सुखसंविष्टे ताः स्त्रियो विविधप्रभाः
ज्वलन्तः काञ्चना दीपाः प्रेक्षन्तानिमिषा इव
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇe sukhasaṁviṣṭe tāḥ striyo vividhaprabhāḥ
jvalantaḥ kāñcanā dīpāḥ prekṣantānimiṣā iva

translations.english: It seemed as if, Rāvana having attained rest (through sleep), the flaming golden lamps furnished with various rays, were gazing at the girls with winkless eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
राजर्षिपितृदैत्यानां गन्धर्वाणां च योषितः
रक्षसां चाभवन्कन्यास्तस्य कामवशं गताः
verses.transliteration:
rājarṣipitṛdaityānāṁ gandharvāṇāṁ ca yoṣitaḥ
rakṣasāṁ cābhavankanyāstasya kāmavaśaṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: Daughters of Rajarsis, of Vipras, of Daityas, of Gandharvas, and of Rākşasas, having come under the influence of desire, had become his wives.

verses.sanskrit:
न तत्र काचित्प्रमदा प्रसह्य; वीर्योपपन्नेन गुणेन लब्धा
न चान्यकामापि न चान्यपूर्वा; विना वरार्हां जनकात्मजां तु
verses.transliteration:
na tatra kācitpramadā prasahya; vīryopapannena guṇena labdhā
na cānyakāmāpi na cānyapūrvā; vinā varārhāṁ janakātmajāṁ tu

translations.english: There was no woman there, who had been won by force by (Rāvana), possessed as he was of prowess; but they had all been subdued by his qualities. And save the surpassingly worthy daughter of Janaka, no female (had been brought), who had set her heart on another, or who had known any other before.

verses.sanskrit:
न चाकुलीना न च हीनरूपा; नादक्षिणा नानुपचार युक्ता
भार्याभवत्तस्य न हीनसत्त्वा; न चापि कान्तस्य न कामनीया
verses.transliteration:
na cākulīnā na ca hīnarūpā; nādakṣiṇā nānupacāra yuktā
bhāryābhavattasya na hīnasattvā; na cāpi kāntasya na kāmanīyā

translations.english: There was none who, being his wife, was not of high extraction; none who was defective in grace; none who was not an object of desire of her lover.

verses.sanskrit:
बभूव बुद्धिस्तु हरीश्वरस्य; यदीदृशी राघवधर्मपत्नी
इमा यथा राक्षसराजभार्याः; सुजातमस्येति हि साधुबुद्धेः
verses.transliteration:
babhūva buddhistu harīśvarasya; yadīdṛśī rāghavadharmapatnī
imā yathā rākṣasarājabhāryāḥ; sujātamasyeti hi sādhubuddheḥ

translations.english: as The lord of monkeys endowed with uprightness of sense, thought, “If the righteously wedded wife of Rāghava were one of the wives of the king of the Rākṣasas, it would well for him."

verses.sanskrit:
पुनश्च सोऽचिन्तयदार्तरूपो; ध्रुवं विशिष्टा गुणतो हि सीता
अथायमस्यां कृतवान्महात्मा; लङ्केश्वरः कष्टमनार्यकर्म
verses.transliteration:
punaśca so'cintayadārtarūpo; dhruvaṁ viśiṣṭā guṇato hi sītā
athāyamasyāṁ kṛtavānmahātmā; laṅkeśvaraḥ kaṣṭamanāryakarma

translations.english: Again reflected he, “Sītā is crowned with chastity and other virtues; and the powerful lord of Lankā, assuming an illusory form, has with much ado perpetrated this ignominious act.” as The lord of monkeys endowed with uprightness of sense, thought, “If the righteously wedded wife of Rāghava were one of the wives of the king of the Rākṣasas, it would well for him."

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम्
अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान्ददर्श शयनासनम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra divyopamaṁ mukhyaṁ sphāṭikaṁ ratnabhūṣitam
avekṣamāṇo hanumāndadarśa śayanāsanam

translations.english: And there Hanumán employed in looking around saw a grand dais made of crystal; and embellished with jewels; comparable to one belonging to the celestial regions; furnished with superb and costly sofas, having their parts painted and composed of ivory, gold, and lapis lazulis; with highly precious canopies.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चैकतमे देशे सोऽग्र्यमाल्यविभूषितम्
ददर्श पाण्डुरं छत्रं ताराधिपतिसंनिभम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya caikatame deśe so'gryamālyavibhūṣitam
dadarśa pāṇḍuraṁ chatraṁ tārādhipatisaṁnibham

translations.english: At one place thereof he saw a white umbrella, adorned with beautiful wreaths, resembling the lord of the stars himself.

verses.sanskrit:
परमास्तरणास्तीर्णमाविकाजिनसंवृतम्
दामभिर्वरमाल्यानां समन्तादुपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration:
paramāstaraṇāstīrṇamāvikājinasaṁvṛtam
dāmabhirvaramālyānāṁ samantādupaśobhitam

translations.english: Around which persons kept waving with their hands chowris furnished with hair;* rife with perfumes of various kinds; odorous with rich dhupa, spread with excellent sheets; covered with the skins of rams; and decked on all sides with chaplets of gorgeous flowers. *The commentator throws out a conjecture that artificial figures are here meant; which mechanically performed the function herein assigned to them.

verses.sanskrit:
निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं रावणं वानरोत्तमः
आसाद्य परमोद्विग्नः सोऽपासर्पत्सुभीतवत्
verses.transliteration:
niḥśvasantaṁ yathā nāgaṁ rāvaṇaṁ vānarottamaḥ
āsādya paramodvignaḥ so'pāsarpatsubhītavat

translations.english: Respiring like a (hissing) serpent.* And reaching there, Hanumān, waxing wondrous agitated, shrank back, as if in fear. And then arriving at the staircase, the mighty monkey, stationing himself on a dais in the middle of the stairs, gazed at the inebriate, Raksasa, resembling a tiger. 'The commentator, however, interprets: like an elephant. Serpent is, I fancy, a happy rendering of Nāga.

verses.sanskrit:
शुशुभे राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स्वपतः शयनोत्तमम्
गन्धहस्तिनि संविष्टे यथाप्रस्रवणं महत्
verses.transliteration:
śuśubhe rākṣasendrasya svapataḥ śayanottamam
gandhahastini saṁviṣṭe yathāprasravaṇaṁ mahat

translations.english: As the sovereign of the Rākșasas was sleeping, his graceful bed resembled a grand cascade, beside which stands an elephant breathing odour.

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धौ च ददर्श स महात्मनः
विक्षिप्तौ राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भुजाविन्द्रध्वजोपमौ
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāṅgadanaddhau ca dadarśa sa mahātmanaḥ
vikṣiptau rākṣasendrasya bhujāvindradhvajopamau

translations.english: Hanuman saw the arms of the huge-bodied lord of Raksasas, fastened with bracelets, stretched (there), like to the banners of Indra;

verses.sanskrit:
ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरापीडितकृतव्रणौ
वज्रोल्लिखितपीनांसौ विष्णुचक्रपरिक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
airāvataviṣāṇāgrairāpīḍitakṛtavraṇau
vajrollikhitapīnāṁsau viṣṇucakraparikṣitau

translations.english: Which had been wounded by the tusk-ends of Airāvata, whose plump parts had been riven by vajra; and which had been torn by the discus of Visnu;

verses.sanskrit:
संहतौ परिघाकारौ वृत्तौ करिकरोपमौ
विक्षिप्तौ शयने शुभ्रे पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ
verses.transliteration:
saṁhatau parighākārau vṛttau karikaropamau
vikṣiptau śayane śubhre pañcaśīrṣāvivoragau

translations.english: Well developed; having equal and elegant parts; with hard joints; fraught with strength; with thumbs having nails bearing auspicious marks; having rings (on the fingers); covered; formed like bludgeons; round; resembling the trunks of elephants; cast on the white bed like to five-hooded serpents;

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तमस्त्रीविमृदितौ गन्धोत्तमनिषेवितौ
यक्षपन्नगगन्धर्वदेवदानवराविणौ
verses.transliteration:
uttamastrīvimṛditau gandhottamaniṣevitau
yakṣapannagagandharvadevadānavarāviṇau

translations.english: Smeared and adorned with cool, fragrant, and excellent sandal resembling the blood of hares; pressed by paragons; odorous with incense; resisting (in battle) Yaksas, and Pannagas, Gandharvas, gods and Dānavas.

verses.sanskrit:
ददर्श स कपिस्तस्य बाहू शयनसंस्थितौ
मन्दरस्यान्तरे सुप्तौ महार्ही रुषिताविव
verses.transliteration:
dadarśa sa kapistasya bāhū śayanasaṁsthitau
mandarasyāntare suptau mahārhī ruṣitāviva

translations.english: That monkey saw his arms resting on the bed, like to two beautiful and mighty serpents sleeping in the entrails of Mandara.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसाधिपः
शुशुभेऽचलसंकाशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः
verses.transliteration:
tābhyāṁ sa paripūrṇābhyāṁ bhujābhyāṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
śuśubhe'calasaṁkāśaḥ śṛṅgābhyāmiva mandaraḥ

translations.english: With his two plump arms, ihat lord of Rākşasas appeared like to the hill Mandara with its two huge summits.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य राक्षससिंहस्य निश्चक्राम मुखान्महान्
शयानस्य विनिःश्वासः पूरयन्निव तद्गृहम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya rākṣasasiṁhasya niścakrāma mukhānmahān
śayānasya viniḥśvāsaḥ pūrayanniva tadgṛham

translations.english: And breath bearing the aroma of the mango, and the Punnāga, the sweet scent of the Bakula, the savour of viands fraught with the six kinds of tastes, and the perfume of wines, came out of the mighty mouth of the sovereign of the Rākşasas, filling as it were, that entire chamber.

verses.sanskrit:
पादमूलगताश्चापि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः
पत्नीः स प्रियभार्यस्य तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे
verses.transliteration:
pādamūlagatāścāpi dadarśa sumahātmanaḥ
patnīḥ sa priyabhāryasya tasya rakṣaḥpatergṛhe

translations.english: He (Hanumān) also saw in the mansion of the Rākşas chief, the wives of that huge bodied one dear to his wives, lying at his feet.

verses.sanskrit:
शशिप्रकाशवदना वरकुण्डलभूषिताः
अम्लानमाल्याभरणा ददर्श हरियूथपः
verses.transliteration:
śaśiprakāśavadanā varakuṇḍalabhūṣitāḥ
amlānamālyābharaṇā dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ

translations.english: That protector of monkey-bands saw them, having countenances resembling the Moon displayed; decked out with elegant ear-rings; bearing unfading garlands* by way of ornamentation; lying on the arms and lap of the lord of the Räksasa. *i.e. celestial females.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रवैदूर्यगर्भाणि श्रवणान्तेषु योषिताम्
ददर्श तापनीयानि कुण्डलान्यङ्गदानि च
verses.transliteration:
vajravaidūryagarbhāṇi śravaṇānteṣu yoṣitām
dadarśa tāpanīyāni kuṇḍalānyaṅgadāni ca

translations.english: The monkey saw women bearing noble ornaments, lying down. And he saw golden bracelets and ear-rings at the nether ends of the women's ears, set with diamonds and lapises.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां चन्द्रोपमैर्वक्त्रैः शुभैर्ललितकुण्डलैः
विरराज विमानं तन्नभस्तारागणैरिव
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ candropamairvaktraiḥ śubhairlalitakuṇḍalaiḥ
virarāja vimānaṁ tannabhastārāgaṇairiva

translations.english: With their fair countenances resembling the Moon, graced with comely ear-rings, that terrace looked beautiful, like the welking embellished with stars.

verses.sanskrit:
मदव्यायामखिन्नास्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य योषितः
तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु प्रसुप्तास्तनुमध्यमाः
verses.transliteration:
madavyāyāmakhinnāstā rākṣasendrasya yoṣitaḥ
teṣu teṣvavakāśeṣu prasuptāstanumadhyamāḥ

translations.english: The slender-waisted wives of the sovereign of the Rākşasas, overcome with languor consequent on drink and amorous encounter, were fast asleep at the very places where they were seated.

verses.sanskrit:
काचिद्वीणां परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता संप्रकाशते
महानदीप्रकीर्णेव नलिनी पोतमाश्रिता
verses.transliteration:
kācidvīṇāṁ pariṣvajya prasuptā saṁprakāśate
mahānadīprakīrṇeva nalinī potamāśritā

translations.english: Another was seen asleep, embracing a Vīņā, like a lotus with spreading petals, resting by the side of a raft.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्या कक्षगतेनैव मड्डुकेनासितेक्षणा
प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बालपुत्रेव वत्सला
verses.transliteration:
anyā kakṣagatenaiva maḍḍukenāsitekṣaṇā
prasuptā bhāminī bhāti bālaputreva vatsalā

translations.english: And another dark-eyed which was asleep with her mudduka* on her lap, like a loving mother having a boy. *A kind of musical instrument.

verses.sanskrit:
पटहं चारुसर्वाङ्गी पीड्य शेते शुभस्तनी
चिरस्य रमणं लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्येव कामिनी
verses.transliteration:
paṭahaṁ cārusarvāṅgī pīḍya śete śubhastanī
cirasya ramaṇaṁ labdhvā pariṣvajyeva kāminī

translations.english: Another damsel possessed of graceful limbs and a shapely bust, was lying down, hugging her kettle-drum, like a woman embracing her lover obtained after a long time.

verses.sanskrit:
काचिदंशं परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमललोचना
निद्रावशमनुप्राप्ता सहकान्तेव भामिनी
verses.transliteration:
kācidaṁśaṁ pariṣvajya suptā kamalalocanā
nidrāvaśamanuprāptā sahakānteva bhāminī

translations.english: And another girl of restrained self, given to dancing, had come under the sway of sleep embracing her vipanci* like a female sleeping with her lover. *A kind of Vina.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्या कनकसंकाशैर्मृदुपीनैर्मनोरमैः
मृदङ्गं परिपीड्याङ्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्तलोचना
verses.transliteration:
anyā kanakasaṁkāśairmṛdupīnairmanoramaiḥ
mṛdaṅgaṁ paripīḍyāṅgaiḥ prasuptā mattalocanā

translations.english: Another having inebriate eyes, was fast asleep, embracing her mridanga with her charming, plump, and tender limbs, resembling gold.

verses.sanskrit:
भुजपार्श्वान्तरस्थेन कक्षगेण कृशोदरी
पणवेन सहानिन्द्या सुप्ता मदकृतश्रमा
verses.transliteration:
bhujapārśvāntarasthena kakṣageṇa kṛśodarī
paṇavena sahānindyā suptā madakṛtaśramā

translations.english: Another female of faultless features, endued with a slender frame, having been overcome by lassitude consequent on drink, was asleep, with her panava on the ends of her lower garment, held fast with her hands.

verses.sanskrit:
डिण्डिमं परिगृह्यान्या तथैवासक्तडिण्डिमा
प्रसुप्ता तरुणं वत्समुपगूह्येव भामिनी
verses.transliteration:
ḍiṇḍimaṁ parigṛhyānyā tathaivāsaktaḍiṇḍimā
prasuptā taruṇaṁ vatsamupagūhyeva bhāminī

translations.english: Another woman was sleeping soundly, embracing her dindima,* with another, bound at her back; like a female taking both her lover and her child. *A kind of musical instrument.

verses.sanskrit:
काचिदाडम्बरं नारी भुजसंभोगपीडितम्
कृत्वा कमलपत्राक्षी प्रसुप्ता मदमोहिता
verses.transliteration:
kācidāḍambaraṁ nārī bhujasaṁbhogapīḍitam
kṛtvā kamalapatrākṣī prasuptā madamohitā

translations.english: Another damsel having eyes resembling lotuspetals, having come under the influence of liquor, was asleep, firmly holding her aramvara' with her hands. A kind of musical instrument.

verses.sanskrit:
कलशीमपविद्ध्यान्या प्रसुप्ता भाति भामिनी
वसन्ते पुष्पशबला मालेव परिमार्जिता
verses.transliteration:
kalaśīmapaviddhyānyā prasuptā bhāti bhāminī
vasante puṣpaśabalā māleva parimārjitā

translations.english: Another woman, intoxicated by wine, was discovered asleep, with her water-vessel upset; and, in consequence, appearing like a wellwashed variegated wreath in spring.

verses.sanskrit:
पाणिभ्यां च कुचौ काचित्सुवर्णकलशोपमौ
उपगूह्याबला सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिता
verses.transliteration:
pāṇibhyāṁ ca kucau kācitsuvarṇakalaśopamau
upagūhyābalā suptā nidrābalaparājitā

translations.english: Another, coming under the masterdom of slumber, was sleeping, holding with her hands her twin breasts resembling golden jars.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्या कमलपत्राक्षी पूर्णेन्दुसदृशानना
अन्यामालिङ्ग्य सुश्रोणी प्रसुप्ता मदविह्वला
verses.transliteration:
anyā kamalapatrākṣī pūrṇendusadṛśānanā
anyāmāliṅgya suśroṇī prasuptā madavihvalā

translations.english: And another lotus-eyed and moon-faced fair one, coming under the governance of slumber, (was asleep), embracing another furnished with shapely hips.

verses.sanskrit:
आतोद्यानि विचित्राणि परिष्वज्य वरस्त्रियः
निपीड्य च कुचैः सुप्ताः कामिन्यः कामुकानिव
verses.transliteration:
ātodyāni vicitrāṇi pariṣvajya varastriyaḥ
nipīḍya ca kucaiḥ suptāḥ kāminyaḥ kāmukāniva

translations.english: And eminently beautiful dames were asleep, embracing musical instruments; like wenches pressing lustful (lovers), with their breasts.

verses.sanskrit:
मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम्
विभूषयन्तीमिव च स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
muktāmaṇisamāyuktairbhūṣaṇaiḥ suvibhūṣitām
vibhūṣayantīmiva ca svaśriyā bhavanottamam

translations.english: That monkey saw that lady, endued with beauty, lying down apart in an excellent bed; adorned with ornaments containing pearls and jewels; and as if decorating that charming mansion with her grace.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्भूषितां मारुतात्मजः
तर्कयामास सीतेति रूपयौवनसंपदा
हर्षेण महता युक्तो ननन्द हरियूथपः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ dṛṣṭvā mahābāhurbhūṣitāṁ mārutātmajaḥ
tarkayāmāsa sīteti rūpayauvanasaṁpadā
harṣeṇa mahatā yukto nananda hariyūthapaḥ

translations.english: The monkey saw there the yellow-hued Mandodarī, having the splendour of gold; the object of (Rāvana's) desire; beautiful exceedingly, the mistress of the inner apartment, lying down. And seeing (Mandodarī) adorned with ornaments, the offspring of the Wind-god guessed. This one endowed with the wealth of youth and beauty mighty be Sītā. And demonstrating great joy, that leader of monkeybands rejoiced exceedingly.

verses.sanskrit:
आस्फोटयामास चुचुम्ब पुच्छं; ननन्द चिक्रीड जगौ जगाम
स्तम्भानरोहन्निपपात भूमौ; निदर्शयन्स्वां प्रकृतिं कपीनाम्
verses.transliteration:
āsphoṭayāmāsa cucumba pucchaṁ; nananda cikrīḍa jagau jagāma
stambhānarohannipapāta bhūmau; nidarśayansvāṁ prakṛtiṁ kapīnām

translations.english: Thereat, (Hanumăn) struck at his arms with his hands, kissed his tail, exhibited signs of glee, frolicked, sang, darted towards the pillars, shoot up to the top thereof, and jumbed down to the earth, manifesting his monkey-nature.

verses.sanskrit:
अवधूय च तां बुद्धिं बभूवावस्थितस्तदा
जगाम चापरां चिन्तां सीतां प्रति महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
avadhūya ca tāṁ buddhiṁ babhūvāvasthitastadā
jagāma cāparāṁ cintāṁ sītāṁ prati mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Then resigning that line of thought, that mighty monkey, regaining his equanimity, set out in another direction of thought touching Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुमर्हति भामिनी
न भोक्तुं नाप्यलंकर्तुं न पानमुपसेवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
na rāmeṇa viyuktā sā svaptumarhati bhāminī
na bhoktuṁ nāpyalaṁkartuṁ na pānamupasevitum

translations.english: Separated from Rāma, that lady is incapable of sleeping, or eating, or decorating (her person), or drinking.

verses.sanskrit:
नान्यं नरमुपस्थातुं सुराणामपि चेश्वरम्
न हि रामसमः कश्चिद्विद्यते त्रिदशेष्वपि
अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य पानभूमौ चचार सः
verses.transliteration:
nānyaṁ naramupasthātuṁ surāṇāmapi ceśvaram
na hi rāmasamaḥ kaścidvidyate tridaśeṣvapi
anyeyamiti niścitya pānabhūmau cacāra saḥ

translations.english: She is incapable of associating with any other person, although he were the sovereign of the celestials himself. And even in all heaven there is none who is equal to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रीडितेनापराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथा पराः
नृत्तेन चापराः क्लान्ताः पानविप्रहतास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
krīḍitenāparāḥ klāntā gītena ca tathā parāḥ
nṛttena cāparāḥ klāntāḥ pānaviprahatāstathā

translations.english: Some were tired out with sporting; some with singing; some with dancing; and some were fast asleep through intoxication.

verses.sanskrit:
देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना
रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः
verses.transliteration:
deśakālābhiyuktena yuktavākyābhidhāyinā
ratābhiratasaṁsuptaṁ dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ

translations.english: That leader of monkey bands saw (women) versed in season and place, and understanding the meanings of words consonant with season and place.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः
गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ madhye mahābāhuḥ śuśubhe rākṣaseśvaraḥ
goṣṭhe mahati mukhyānāṁ gavāṁ madhye yathā vṛṣaḥ

translations.english: In the midst of them all, the lord of the Rāks asas looked splendid like an ox in a spacious stall in the midst of stately kine.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतः स्वयम्
करेणुभिर्यथारण्यं परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasendraḥ śuśubhe tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ svayam
kareṇubhiryathāraṇyaṁ parikīrṇo mahādvipaḥ

translations.english: Surrounded by them, the Rākṣasa chief appeared beautiful like a gigantic elephant in a forest, surrounded by female elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च भागशः
तत्र न्यस्तानि मांसानि पानभूमौ ददर्श सः
verses.transliteration:
mṛgāṇāṁ mahiṣāṇāṁ ca varāhāṇāṁ ca bhāgaśaḥ
tatra nyastāni māṁsāni pānabhūmau dadarśa saḥ

translations.english: In the abode of the huge-bodied Rākşasa chief, that tiger like monkey saw that place of drinking, furnished with every object of desire.

verses.sanskrit:
पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि
कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
pānabhājanavikṣiptaiḥ phalaiśca vividhairapi
kṛtapuṣpopahārā bhūradhikaṁ puṣyati śriyam

translations.english: With large and costly stray bangles and bracelests; and scattered cans, and diverse kinds of fruit; and wreaths of flowers, the pavement attained exceeding beauty.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तैः सुश्लिष्टैः शयनासनैः
पानभूमिर्विना वह्निं प्रदीप्तेवोपलक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration:
tatra tatra ca vinyastaiḥ suśliṣṭaiḥ śayanāsanaiḥ
pānabhūmirvinā vahniṁ pradīptevopalakṣyate

translations.english: And with elegantly jointed bedsteads, arranged (around), the scene of wassail appeared aflame without fire.

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृतसुरा अपि
शर्करासवमाध्वीकाः पुष्पासवफलासवाः
वासचूर्णैश्च विविधैर्मृष्टास्तैस्तैः पृथक्पृथक्
verses.transliteration:
divyāḥ prasannā vividhāḥ surāḥ kṛtasurā api
śarkarāsavamādhvīkāḥ puṣpāsavaphalāsavāḥ
vāsacūrṇaiśca vividhairmṛṣṭāstaistaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak

translations.english: With meat consisting of many ingredients, fraught with diverse tastes, seasoned with many substances, and dressed by skilful cooks, arranged separately in the scene of revel; and with noble and pleasant wines, natural and artifical, asavas from sugar; and Madhvika' and āsavas from flowers and fruits; and impregnated separately with different kinds of fragrant dust, the pavement, furnished with innumerable garlands, surrounded with golden water vessels and crystal bowls, and golden water-pots, looked exceedingly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit:
राजतेषु च कुम्भेषु जाम्बूनदमयेषु च
पानश्रेष्ठं तदा भूरि कपिस्तत्र ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
rājateṣu ca kumbheṣu jāmbūnadamayeṣu ca
pānaśreṣṭhaṁ tadā bhūri kapistatra dadarśa ha

translations.english: The monkey saw that foremost of all places set apart for drinking, containing silver and golden jars.

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचिदर्धावशेषाणि क्वचित्पीतानि सर्वशः
क्वचिन्नैव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
kvacidardhāvaśeṣāṇi kvacitpītāni sarvaśaḥ
kvacinnaiva prapītāni pānāni sa dadarśa ha

translations.english: That mighty monkey saw golden wine-vessels studded with gems, all filled with wine; and some with half full of liquor, some with their wine entirely exhausted, and some full of liquor.

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचिद्भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान्क्वचित्पानानि भागशः
क्वचिदन्नावशेषाणि पश्यन्वै विचचार ह
verses.transliteration:
kvacidbhakṣyāṁśca vividhānkvacitpānāni bhāgaśaḥ
kvacidannāvaśeṣāṇi paśyanvai vicacāra ha

translations.english: And (at some spots) he saw various kinds of viands, and at other wines ranged in rows, and at others the wine-vessels remaining half full.

verses.sanskrit:
शयनान्यत्र नारीणां शून्यानि बहुधा पुनः
परस्परं समाश्लिष्य काश्चित्सुप्ता वराङ्गनाः
verses.transliteration:
śayanānyatra nārīṇāṁ śūnyāni bahudhā punaḥ
parasparaṁ samāśliṣya kāścitsuptā varāṅganāḥ

translations.english: There were many bedsteads belonging to fair ones, remaining vacant; and at some places excellent women were sleeping touching each other.

verses.sanskrit:
काचिच्च वस्त्रमन्यस्या अपहृत्योपगुह्य च
उपगम्याबला सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिता
verses.transliteration:
kācicca vastramanyasyā apahṛtyopaguhya ca
upagamyābalā suptā nidrābalaparājitā

translations.english: And at one place, a female, borne down by the force of sleep, forcibly possessing herself of another's cloth, and wrapping herself there with, went to the bed of that one, and was indulging in sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
तासामुच्छ्वासवातेन वस्त्रं माल्यं च गात्रजम्
नात्यर्थं स्पन्दते चित्रं प्राप्य मन्दमिवानिलम्
verses.transliteration:
tāsāmucchvāsavātena vastraṁ mālyaṁ ca gātrajam
nātyarthaṁ spandate citraṁ prāpya mandamivānilam

translations.english: And with their breath, their variegated wreaths and the cloth on their persons were stirring gently, as if with a mild-blowing breeze.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर्मधुरसस्य च
विविधस्य च माल्यस्य पुष्पस्य विविधस्य च
verses.transliteration:
candanasya ca śītasya śīdhormadhurasasya ca
vividhasya ca mālyasya puṣpasya vividhasya ca

translations.english: Laden with the odours of cool sandal, and of sweet-tasting Sidhu; and of diverse wreaths and flowers, and with perfumes of various kinds, and entranced with (the aroma) of sandals suitable for use after ablution, and of dhupas, the air, impregnated with excellent scent, was there breathing around the car Puşpaka.

verses.sanskrit:
श्यामावदातास्तत्रान्याः काश्चित्कृष्णा वराङ्गनाः
काश्चित्काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये
verses.transliteration:
śyāmāvadātāstatrānyāḥ kāścitkṛṣṇā varāṅganāḥ
kāścitkāñcanavarṇāṅgyaḥ pramadā rākṣasālaye

translations.english: And in the residence of the Rākşas, there were some wenches sable, yet exceedingly witching; and some were dark-hued; and the frames of some were of a golden brilliance.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम्
पद्मिनीनां प्रसुप्तानां रूपमासीद्यथैव हि
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ nidrāvaśatvācca madanena vimūrchitam
padminīnāṁ prasuptānāṁ rūpamāsīdyathaiva hi

translations.english: Their beauty, in consequence of their coming under the governance of sleep, and their being bereft of their senses by Madana, resembled that of lotuses in a sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं सर्वमशेषेण रावणान्तःपुरं कपिः
ददर्श सुमहातेजा न ददर्श च जानकीम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sarvamaśeṣeṇa rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṁ kapiḥ
dadarśa sumahātejā na dadarśa ca jānakīm

translations.english: Thus that highly energetic monkey saw everything thoroughly in the inner apartment of Ravana, but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
निरीक्षमाणश्च ततस्ताः स्त्रियः स महाकपिः
जगाम महतीं चिन्तां धर्मसाध्वसशङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
nirīkṣamāṇaśca tatastāḥ striyaḥ sa mahākapiḥ
jagāma mahatīṁ cintāṁ dharmasādhvasaśaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: Seeing those females, that mighty monkey, apprehending loss of righteousness, was seized with an exceeding great fear.

verses.sanskrit:
परदारावरोधस्य प्रसुप्तस्य निरीक्षणम्
इदं खलु ममात्यर्थं धर्मलोपं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
paradārāvarodhasya prasuptasya nirīkṣaṇam
idaṁ khalu mamātyarthaṁ dharmalopaṁ kariṣyati

translations.english: Beholding a female, who is the religiously wedded wife of another, while she is asleep, verily cause loss of righteousness. *And therefore presumably incapable of taking care of herself.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे परदाराणां दृष्टिर्विषयवर्तिनी
अयं चात्र मया दृष्टः परदारपरिग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
na hi me paradārāṇāṁ dṛṣṭirviṣayavartinī
ayaṁ cātra mayā dṛṣṭaḥ paradāraparigrahaḥ

translations.english: My sight surely never seek other's wives; but I have beheld this one that has ravished another's spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य प्रादुरभूच्चिन्तापुनरन्या मनस्विनः
निश्चितैकान्तचित्तस्य कार्यनिश्चयदर्शिनी
verses.transliteration:
tasya prādurabhūccintāpunaranyā manasvinaḥ
niścitaikāntacittasya kāryaniścayadarśinī

translations.english: That intelligent one, intent on attaining a knowledge of things capable of being arrived at on grounds of judgement, again reflected effectively as to his course of action.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं दृष्ट्वा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावणस्त्रियः
न तु मे मनसः किंचिद्वैकृत्यमुपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ dṛṣṭvā mayā sarvā viśvastā rāvaṇastriyaḥ
na tu me manasaḥ kiṁcidvaikṛtyamupapadyate

translations.english: All these unsuspecting wives of Rāvana have been beheld by me; yet there are no signs that my mind has undergone any alteration.

verses.sanskrit:
मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषामिन्द्रियाणां प्रवर्तते
शुभाशुभास्ववस्थासु तच्च मे सुव्यवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
mano hi hetuḥ sarveṣāmindriyāṇāṁ pravartate
śubhāśubhāsvavasthāsu tacca me suvyavasthitam

translations.english: In respect of the enlistment of the senses on behalf of any course of action good or evil, it is verily mind which is the cause; and herein my mind is righteously disposed.

verses.sanskrit:
नान्यत्र हि मया शक्या वैदेही परिमार्गितुम्
स्त्रियो हि स्त्रीषु दृश्यन्ते सदा संपरिमार्गणे
verses.transliteration:
nānyatra hi mayā śakyā vaidehī parimārgitum
striyo hi strīṣu dṛśyante sadā saṁparimārgaṇe

translations.english: I could not search for Vaidehī elsewhere; for in the matter of search, people always search for women even among women.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिस्तस्यां तत्परिमार्ग्यते
न शक्यं प्रमदा नष्टा मृगीषु परिमार्गितुम्
verses.transliteration:
yasya sattvasya yā yonistasyāṁ tatparimārgyate
na śakyaṁ pramadā naṣṭā mṛgīṣu parimārgitum

translations.english: People search for creatures among the species to which they happen to belong: none scarchets for a lost lady among female deer.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं मार्गितं तावच्छुद्धेन मनसा मया
रावणान्तःपुरं सरं दृश्यते न च जानकी
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ mārgitaṁ tāvacchuddhena manasā mayā
rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṁ saraṁ dṛśyate na ca jānakī

translations.english: Therefore have I with a pure heart explored the entire inner apartment of Rāvana; but Janaka's daughter I see not.

verses.sanskrit:
देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च वीर्यवान्
अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान्नैवापश्यत जानकीम्
verses.transliteration:
devagandharvakanyāśca nāgakanyāśca vīryavān
avekṣamāṇo hanumānnaivāpaśyata jānakīm

translations.english: Hanumān endowed with prowess saw the daughters of gods, and Yaksa, and Nagas; but he saw not Jānaki.

verses.sanskrit:
तामपश्यन्कपिस्तत्र पश्यंश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः
अपक्रम्य तदा वीरः प्रध्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tāmapaśyankapistatra paśyaṁścānyā varastriyaḥ
apakramya tadā vīraḥ pradhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: And not seeing her, that hero, having beheld other magnificent dames, coming out of that place, set about searching for Sītā (afresh).

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य वानरो; लतागृहांश्चित्रगृहान्निशागृहान्
जगाम सीतां प्रति दर्शनोत्सुको; न चैव तां पश्यति चारुदर्शनाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya madhye bhavanasya vānaro; latāgṛhāṁścitragṛhānniśāgṛhān
jagāma sītāṁ prati darśanotsuko; na caiva tāṁ paśyati cārudarśanām

translations.english: Remaining in that mansion, (Hanuman) desirous of getting a sight of Sītā graced with a fair presence, went into bowers, and picture galleries, and night-houses;* but her he did not find. *Intended for stay at night.

verses.sanskrit:
स चिन्तयामास ततो महाकपिः; प्रियामपश्यन्रघुनन्दनस्य ताम्
ध्रुवं नु सीता म्रियते यथा न मे; विचिन्वतो दर्शनमेति मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
sa cintayāmāsa tato mahākapiḥ; priyāmapaśyanraghunandanasya tām
dhruvaṁ nu sītā mriyate yathā na me; vicinvato darśanameti maithilī

translations.english: And not finding the beloved (spouse) of Raghu's son that mighty monkey reflected, “Surely Sītā is not alive, for although I have searched (through and through), yet Mithila's daughter I have failed to find."

verses.sanskrit:
सा राक्षसानां प्रवरेण बाला; स्वशीलसंरक्षण तत्परा सती
अनेन नूनं प्रतिदुष्टकर्मणा; हता भवेदार्यपथे परे स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
sā rākṣasānāṁ pravareṇa bālā; svaśīlasaṁrakṣaṇa tatparā satī
anena nūnaṁ pratiduṣṭakarmaṇā; hatā bhavedāryapathe pare sthitā

translations.english: That girl solicitous for the preservation of her chastity, and staying in the prime path of virtuous woman, that chaste one has, for certain, been slain by this chief of the Rākṣasas, (ever) finding delight in iniquity.

verses.sanskrit:
विरूपरूपा विकृता विवर्चसो; महानना दीर्घविरूपदर्शनाः
समीक्ष्य सा राक्षसराजयोषितो; भयाद्विनष्टा जनकेश्वरात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
virūparūpā vikṛtā vivarcaso; mahānanā dīrghavirūpadarśanāḥ
samīkṣya sā rākṣasarājayoṣito; bhayādvinaṣṭā janakeśvarātmajā

translations.english: Seeing the wives of the Rākṣasa inonarch, of frightful forms, monstrous; of lurid hue; having huge faces; with large horrid eyes, the daughter of Janaka has given up the ghost from fright.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतामदृष्ट्वा ह्यनवाप्य पौरुषं; विहृत्य कालं सह वानरैश्चिरम्
न मेऽस्ति सुग्रीवसमीपगा गतिः; सुतीक्ष्णदण्डो बलवांश्च वानरः
verses.transliteration:
sītāmadṛṣṭvā hyanavāpya pauruṣaṁ; vihṛtya kālaṁ saha vānaraiściram
na me'sti sugrīvasamīpagā gatiḥ; sutīkṣṇadaṇḍo balavāṁśca vānaraḥ

translations.english: Failing to see Sītā, and (thereby) annulling my prowess, and having long spent the appointed space in company with the monkeys, way have I none to present myself before Sugrīva, that monkey being puissant and given to meting out sharp chastisement.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टमन्तःपुरं सर्वं दृष्ट्वा रावणयोषितः
न सीता दृश्यते साध्वी वृथा जातो मम श्रमः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭamantaḥpuraṁ sarvaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇayoṣitaḥ
na sītā dṛśyate sādhvī vṛthā jāto mama śramaḥ

translations.english: Having searched the inner apartment through, and seen the wives of the Rākṣasa, I do not see the chaste Sită. Therefore vain is the trouble that I take.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु मां वानराः सर्वे गतं वक्ष्यन्ति संगताः
गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किं कृतं तद्वदस्व नः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu māṁ vānarāḥ sarve gataṁ vakṣyanti saṁgatāḥ
gatvā tatra tvayā vīra kiṁ kṛtaṁ tadvadasva naḥ

translations.english: What, alas! shall the monkeys assembled tell me when I shall go (to them)? 'O hero, tell us what you have done, repairing there.'

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्ट्वा किं प्रवक्ष्यामि तामहं जनकात्मजाम्
ध्रुवं प्रायमुपेष्यन्ति कालस्य व्यतिवर्तने
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭvā kiṁ pravakṣyāmi tāmahaṁ janakātmajām
dhruvaṁ prāyamupeṣyanti kālasya vyativartane

translations.english: And not having seen Janaka's daughter, what shall I answer? The term fixed (by Sugrīva) having been past, certainly meet it is that I should fast to death.

verses.sanskrit:
किं वा वक्ष्यति वृद्धश्च जाम्बवानङ्गदश्च सः
गतं पारं समुद्रस्य वानराश्च समागताः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ vā vakṣyati vṛddhaśca jāmbavānaṅgadaśca saḥ
gataṁ pāraṁ samudrasya vānarāśca samāgatāḥ

translations.english: And what shall the aged Jambhavan, and what shall Angada, say? And what, again, shall the assembled monkeys say to me when I shall have crossed over the main.

verses.sanskrit:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्
भूयस्तावद्विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlamanirvedaḥ paraṁ sukham
bhūyastāvadviceṣyāmi na yatra vicayaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: But perseverance is the source of good fortune; and perseverance bring about supreme happiness. Search again I will, where I have not yet searched.

verses.sanskrit:
अनिर्वेदो हि सततं सर्वार्थेषु प्रवर्तकः
करोति सफलं जन्तोः कर्म यच्च करोति सः
verses.transliteration:
anirvedo hi satataṁ sarvārtheṣu pravartakaḥ
karoti saphalaṁ jantoḥ karma yacca karoti saḥ

translations.english: Perseverance, for certain, ever bring people to all profitable objects. Whatever one dose with vigour, bear fruit.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादनिर्वेद कृतं यत्नं चेष्टेऽहमुत्तमम्
अदृष्टांश्च विचेष्यामि देशान्रावणपालितान्
verses.transliteration:
tasmādanirveda kṛtaṁ yatnaṁ ceṣṭe'hamuttamam
adṛṣṭāṁśca viceṣyāmi deśānrāvaṇapālitān

translations.english: Therefore will I put forth fresh dear efforts vigorously. I will search such places held by Rāvana as I have not yet seen.

verses.sanskrit:
चतुरङ्गुलमात्रोऽपि नावकाशः स विद्यते
रावणान्तःपुरे तस्मिन्यं कपिर्न जगाम सः
verses.transliteration:
caturaṅgulamātro'pi nāvakāśaḥ sa vidyate
rāvaṇāntaḥpure tasminyaṁ kapirna jagāma saḥ

translations.english: There was not even space measuring four fingers in that inner apartment of Rāvana, to which the monkey did not repair.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राकरान्तररथ्याश्च वेदिकश्चैत्यसंश्रयाः
श्वभ्राश्च पुष्करिण्यश्च सर्वं तेनावलोकितम्
verses.transliteration:
prākarāntararathyāśca vedikaścaityasaṁśrayāḥ
śvabhrāśca puṣkariṇyaśca sarvaṁ tenāvalokitam

translations.english: And he saw the abodes of the nobility, the daises, the trees by the crossings, the holes, and the tanks.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षस्यो विविधाकारा विरूपा विकृतास्तथा
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सा जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasyo vividhākārā virūpā vikṛtāstathā
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sā janakātmajā

translations.english: And Hanumān saw there Räksasas of various forms, frightful and deformed; but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
रूपेणाप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्याधर स्त्रियः
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु राघवनन्दिनी
verses.transliteration:
rūpeṇāpratimā loke varā vidyādhara striyaḥ
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu rāghavanandinī

translations.english: Hanuman there the the foremost and beautiful wives of Vidyadharas; but he saw not Rāghava's beloved Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
नागकन्या वरारोहाः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा
verses.transliteration:
nāgakanyā varārohāḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sītā sumadhyamā

translations.english: Hanumān saw there transcendentally beautiful women, daughter of Nāgas, having countenances resembling the moon; but he saw not Janaka's daughter. saw

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमथ्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण नागकन्या बलाद्धृताः
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न सा जनकनन्दिनी
verses.transliteration:
pramathya rākṣasendreṇa nāgakanyā balāddhṛtāḥ
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na sā janakanandinī

translations.english: And Hanumān saw there daughter of Nāgas forcibly brought by the lord of the Rākşasas; but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपश्यंस्तां महाबाहुः पश्यंश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः
विषसाद महाबाहुर्हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
so'paśyaṁstāṁ mahābāhuḥ paśyaṁścānyā varastriyaḥ
viṣasāda mahābāhurhanūmānmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: Having seen other beauteous females, and not seeing her, the mighty-armed son of the Windgod was oppressed with sandness.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्योगं वानरेन्द्राणं प्लवनं सागरस्य च
व्यर्थं वीक्ष्यानिलसुतश्चिन्तां पुनरुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
udyogaṁ vānarendrāṇaṁ plavanaṁ sāgarasya ca
vyarthaṁ vīkṣyānilasutaścintāṁ punarupāgamat

translations.english: Seeing that the endeavours of the monarch of monkeys, as well as the bounding over the main, had come to nought, the offspring of the Windgod was plunged in thought.

verses.sanskrit:
अवतीर्य विमानाच्च हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
चिन्तामुपजगामाथ शोकोपहतचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
avatīrya vimānācca hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
cintāmupajagāmātha śokopahatacetanaḥ

translations.english: Descending from the aerial car, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, his senses deprived by sorrow, was again wrought up with anxiety.

verses.sanskrit:
विमानात्तु सुसंक्रम्य प्राकारं हरियूथपः
हनूमान्वेगवानासीद्यथा विद्युद्घनान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
vimānāttu susaṁkramya prākāraṁ hariyūthapaḥ
hanūmānvegavānāsīdyathā vidyudghanāntare

translations.english: Alighting from the car, Hanumān possessed of vigorous activity, leader of monkeybands-nearing the wall, looked like lightning within a mass of clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
संपरिक्रम्य हनुमान्रावणस्य निवेशनान्
अदृष्ट्वा जानकीं सीतामब्रवीद्वचनं कपिः
verses.transliteration:
saṁparikramya hanumānrāvaṇasya niveśanān
adṛṣṭvā jānakīṁ sītāmabravīdvacanaṁ kapiḥ

translations.english: And having gone round the mansions of Ravana, and not seeing Janaki, the monkey Hanuman said,

verses.sanskrit:
भूयिष्ठं लोडिता लङ्का रामस्य चरता प्रियम्
न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीं सीतां सर्वाङ्गशोभनाम्
verses.transliteration:
bhūyiṣṭhaṁ loḍitā laṅkā rāmasya caratā priyam
na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṁ sītāṁ sarvāṅgaśobhanām

translations.english: Striving after Rāma's welfare, I have again searched through Lankā; but I do not see Vaidehi's daughter, Janaki, having all her limbs endeued with loveliness.

verses.sanskrit:
पल्वलानि तटाकानि सरांसि सरितस्तथा
नद्योऽनूपवनान्ताश्च दुर्गाश्च धरणीधराः
लोडिता वसुधा सर्वा न च पश्यामि जानकीम्
verses.transliteration:
palvalāni taṭākāni sarāṁsi saritastathā
nadyo'nūpavanāntāśca durgāśca dharaṇīdharāḥ
loḍitā vasudhā sarvā na ca paśyāmi jānakīm

translations.english: And I have explored pools, and watery expanses, and tanks, and rivers, and streams, and marshes, and and woods, and citadels, and mountains, yea, all this earth; but Janaki I do not fimd.

verses.sanskrit:
इह संपातिना सीता रावणस्य निवेशने
आख्याता गृध्रराजेन न च पश्यामि तामहम्
verses.transliteration:
iha saṁpātinā sītā rāvaṇasya niveśane
ākhyātā gṛdhrarājena na ca paśyāmi tāmaham

translations.english: The vulture-king Sampati had told that Sītā was in the mansion of Rāvaņa. But why do I not see her (here)?

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु सीताथ वैदेही मैथिली जनकात्मजा
उपतिष्ठेत विवशा रावणं दुष्टचारिणम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu sītātha vaidehī maithilī janakātmajā
upatiṣṭheta vivaśā rāvaṇaṁ duṣṭacāriṇam

translations.english: Or dose Maithili Sītā, daughter to Janaka, sprung in the Vaidehī line, forcibly carried off (by Rāvaņa), and completely in his power, abide by the mandate (of that monarch)?

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रमुत्पततो मन्ये सीतामादाय रक्षसः
बिभ्यतो रामबाणानामन्तरा पतिता भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kṣipramutpatato manye sītāmādāya rakṣasaḥ
bibhyato rāmabāṇānāmantarā patitā bhavet

translations.english: I conceive that while taking Sītā, the Rākşasa darted upward, he being influenced by fear of Rāma's shafts; (and accordingly losing control over his movements), she fell off by the way.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा ह्रियमाणायाः पथि सिद्धनिषेविते
मन्ये पतितमार्याया हृदयं प्रेक्ष्य सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā hriyamāṇāyāḥ pathi siddhaniṣevite
manye patitamāryāyā hṛdayaṁ prekṣya sāgaram

translations.english: Or I fancy that while that noble lady was being carried away along the way ranged by Siddhas, she lost her life on beholding the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्योरुवेगेन भुजाभ्यां पीडितेन च
तया मन्ये विशालाक्ष्या त्यक्तं जीवितमार्यया
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasyoruvegena bhujābhyāṁ pīḍitena ca
tayā manye viśālākṣyā tyaktaṁ jīvitamāryayā

translations.english: Or I think that on account of the vehement spced assumed by Rāvana, and also oppressed with his arms, that large-eyed noble lady has been bereft of her life.

verses.sanskrit:
उपर्युपरि वा नूनं सागरं क्रमतस्तदा
विवेष्टमाना पतिता समुद्रे जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
uparyupari vā nūnaṁ sāgaraṁ kramatastadā
viveṣṭamānā patitā samudre janakātmajā

translations.english: For certain, while (Ravana) was soaring higher and higher, Janaka's daughter, rolling (on the car), dropped down into the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पत्नीभिरसितेक्षणा
अदुष्टा दुष्टभावाभिर्भक्षिता सा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
atha vā rākṣasendrasya patnībhirasitekṣaṇā
aduṣṭā duṣṭabhāvābhirbhakṣitā sā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Alas! trying to preserve her chastity, the forlorn Sītā, practising self-mortification, has been devoured by this abject-minded Rāvana. Or that darkeyed innocent one, has been eaten up by the wives of the Rākşasa chief, actuated by wicked motives.* *Jealously, according to the commentator.

verses.sanskrit:
संपूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम्
रामस्य ध्यायती वक्त्रं पञ्चत्वं कृपणा गता
verses.transliteration:
saṁpūrṇacandrapratimaṁ padmapatranibhekṣaṇam
rāmasya dhyāyatī vaktraṁ pañcatvaṁ kṛpaṇā gatā

translations.english: (Ever) contemplating Rāma's countenance, resembling the full Moon, with eyes like lotusleaves, she, exercised with sorrow, has breathed her last.

verses.sanskrit:
हा राम लक्ष्मणेत्येव हायोध्येति च मैथिली
विलप्य बहु वैदेही न्यस्तदेहा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
hā rāma lakṣmaṇetyeva hāyodhyeti ca maithilī
vilapya bahu vaidehī nyastadehā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Bewailing much with exclamations of 'Oh Rama and Laksmana!' 'Ah Ayodhya!' that lady Vaidehi has renounced her body.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा निहिता मन्ये रावणस्य निवेशने
नूनं लालप्यते मन्दं पञ्जरस्थेव शारिका
verses.transliteration:
atha vā nihitā manye rāvaṇasya niveśane
nūnaṁ lālapyate mandaṁ pañjarastheva śārikā

translations.english: Or secretly kept in Rāvana's mansion, that girl, like a female parrot in a cage, is weeping bitterly.

verses.sanskrit:
जनकस्य कुले जाता रामपत्नी सुमध्यमा
कथमुत्पलपत्राक्षी रावणस्य वशं व्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
janakasya kule jātā rāmapatnī sumadhyamā
kathamutpalapatrākṣī rāvaṇasya vaśaṁ vrajet

translations.english: How can the slender-waisted wife of Rāma, born in the race of Janaka, furnished with eyes resembling lotus petals, come under the sway of Ravana?

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टा वा प्रनष्टा वा मृता वा जनकात्मजा
रामस्य प्रियभार्यस्य न निवेदयितुं क्षमम्
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭā vā pranaṣṭā vā mṛtā vā janakātmajā
rāmasya priyabhāryasya na nivedayituṁ kṣamam

translations.english: I shall not be able to say of Rāma's beloved wife that she has been sullied, or that I have seen her, or yet that she is dead. To say this is censurable; not to say it is also such. *This is evidently the sense, having regard to the preceding sloku, although the commentator gives the apparent meaning of vinastha perished.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेद्यमाने दोषः स्याद्दोषः स्यादनिवेदने
कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यं विषमं प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
nivedyamāne doṣaḥ syāddoṣaḥ syādanivedane
kathaṁ nu khalu kartavyaṁ viṣamaṁ pratibhāti me

translations.english: What is my course? I find myself in a false position. Things having drifted to this pass, what should I say, now that the time has come?'

verses.sanskrit:
यदि सीतामदृष्ट्वाहं वानरेन्द्रपुरीमितः
गमिष्यामि ततः को मे पुरुषार्थो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi sītāmadṛṣṭvāhaṁ vānarendrapurīmitaḥ
gamiṣyāmi tataḥ ko me puruṣārtho bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Thus thinking, Hanumān again reflected, "If without seeing Sītā, I repair to the abode of the lord of monkeys, what then shall I gain as the object of my exertions?

verses.sanskrit:
ममेदं लङ्घनं व्यर्थं सागरस्य भविष्यति
प्रवेशश्चिव लङ्काया राक्षसानां च दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
mamedaṁ laṅghanaṁ vyarthaṁ sāgarasya bhaviṣyati
praveśaściva laṅkāyā rākṣasānāṁ ca darśanam

translations.english: This my bounding over the main comes to nought; as also my entry into Lank, and the sight of the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
किं वा वक्ष्यति सुग्रीवो हरयो व समागताः
किष्किन्धां समनुप्राप्तौ तौ वा दशरथात्मजौ
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ vā vakṣyati sugrīvo harayo va samāgatāḥ
kiṣkindhāṁ samanuprāptau tau vā daśarathātmajau

translations.english: And what shall Sugrīva say? Or the assembled monkeys; or those twin sons of Dasaratha; to me when I shall have come to Kiskindhā?

verses.sanskrit:
गत्वा तु यदि काकुत्स्थं वक्ष्यामि परमप्रियम्
न दृष्टेति मया सीता ततस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
gatvā tu yadi kākutsthaṁ vakṣyāmi paramapriyam
na dṛṣṭeti mayā sītā tatastyakṣyanti jīvitam

translations.english: If going there, I should say a harsh speech to Kākutstha-'I have not seen Sitā'-he shall renounce his life.

verses.sanskrit:
परुषं दारुणं क्रूरं तीक्ष्णमिन्द्रियतापनम्
सीतानिमित्तं दुर्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा स न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
paruṣaṁ dāruṇaṁ krūraṁ tīkṣṇamindriyatāpanam
sītānimittaṁ durvākyaṁ śrutvā sa na bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Hearing harsh, terrible, unsufferable, fierce and foul words concerning Sītă, calculated to set the senses on fire, he shall not exist.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तु कृच्छ्रगतं दृष्ट्वा पञ्चत्वगतमानसं
भृशानुरक्तो मेधावी न भविष्यति लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tu kṛcchragataṁ dṛṣṭvā pañcatvagatamānasaṁ
bhṛśānurakto medhāvī na bhaviṣyati lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Seeing him come under misery, with his mind expiring, the intelligent Laksmana, firmly attached (to Rāma), shall also cease to exist.

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टौ भ्रातरौ श्रुत्वा भरतोऽपि मरिष्यति
भरतं च मृतं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुघ्नो न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭau bhrātarau śrutvā bharato'pi mariṣyati
bharataṁ ca mṛtaṁ dṛṣṭvā śatrughno na bhaviṣyati

translations.english: And hearing that his two brothers are dead, Bharata also shall give up existence. And seeing Bharata dead, Śatrughna shall also renounce his life.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रान्मृतान्समीक्ष्याथ न भविष्यन्ति मातरः
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
putrānmṛtānsamīkṣyātha na bhaviṣyanti mātaraḥ
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: And beholding their sons dead, their mothers, Kausalya, Sumitra and kaikayi, shall, certainly, resign their lives,

verses.sanskrit:
कृतज्ञः सत्यसंधश्च सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः
रामं तथा गतं दृष्ट्वा ततस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtajñaḥ satyasaṁdhaśca sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ
rāmaṁ tathā gataṁ dṛṣṭvā tatastyakṣyanti jīvitam

translations.english: Seeing Rāma in that plight, the lord of the monkeys, Sugrīva, grateful and having his heart fast fixed in truth, shall give up his life.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्मना व्यथिता दीना निरानन्दा तपस्विनी
पीडिता भर्तृशोकेन रुमा त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
durmanā vyathitā dīnā nirānandā tapasvinī
pīḍitā bhartṛśokena rumā tyakṣyati jīvitam

translations.english: Rumā, aggrieved, heart-wrung, distressed and bereft of happiness and assuming the garb of a female ascetic, because of grief for her husband, shall resign her existence.

verses.sanskrit:
वालिजेन तु दुःखेन पीडिता शोककर्शिता
पञ्चत्वगमने राज्ञस्तारापि न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vālijena tu duḥkhena pīḍitā śokakarśitā
pañcatvagamane rājñastārāpi na bhaviṣyati

translations.english: And oppressed with grief arising from Vāli, and weighed down by sorrow, the queen Tārā, also, resolving on death shall cease to exist.

verses.sanskrit:
मातापित्रोर्विनाशेन सुग्रीव व्यसनेन च
कुमारोऽप्यङ्गदः कस्माद्धारयिष्यति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
mātāpitrorvināśena sugrīva vyasanena ca
kumāro'pyaṅgadaḥ kasmāddhārayiṣyati jīvitam

translations.english: In consequence of the death of his father and mother and the calamity befalling Sugrīva, the prince Angada also shall next forego his existence.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्त्वेनानुप्रदानेन मानेन च यशस्विना
लालिताः कपिराजेन प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति वानराः
verses.transliteration:
sāntvenānupradānena mānena ca yaśasvinā
lālitāḥ kapirājena prāṇāṁstyakṣyanti vānarāḥ

translations.english: The dwellers of the woods overwhelmed with grief got of (the decease of) their master, shall strike at their heads with their clenched fists and hands. And the monkeys affectionately cherished by the famous lord of the monkeys with soothing words gifts and regard, shall resign there lives.

verses.sanskrit:
न वनेषु न शैलेषु न निरोधेषु वा पुनः
क्रीडामनुभविष्यन्ति समेत्य कपिकुञ्जराः
verses.transliteration:
na vaneṣu na śaileṣu na nirodheṣu vā punaḥ
krīḍāmanubhaviṣyanti sametya kapikuñjarāḥ

translations.english: No more in woods, and rocks, or secret spots, shall the foremost monkeys, assembled together, indulge in sports.

verses.sanskrit:
सपुत्रदाराः सामात्या भर्तृव्यसनपीडिताः
शैलाग्रेभ्यः पतिष्यन्ति समेत्य विषमेषु च
verses.transliteration:
saputradārāḥ sāmātyā bhartṛvyasanapīḍitāḥ
śailāgrebhyaḥ patiṣyanti sametya viṣameṣu ca

translations.english: They, along with their sons and wives, and counsellors, distressed on account the disaster that has overtaken their master, shall fall from the tops of mountains down to places even or uneven.

verses.sanskrit:
विषमुद्बन्धनं वापि प्रवेशं ज्वलनस्य वा
उपवासमथो शस्त्रं प्रचरिष्यन्ति वानराः
verses.transliteration:
viṣamudbandhanaṁ vāpi praveśaṁ jvalanasya vā
upavāsamatho śastraṁ pracariṣyanti vānarāḥ

translations.english: The monkeys shall take poison, or hang themselves, or enter into flaming fire, or fast, or fall on their own weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरमारोदनं मन्ये गते मयि भविष्यति
इक्ष्वाकुकुलनाशश्च नाशश्चैव वनौकसाम्
verses.transliteration:
ghoramārodanaṁ manye gate mayi bhaviṣyati
ikṣvākukulanāśaśca nāśaścaiva vanaukasām

translations.english: I fancy that a loud wailing shall arise on my return (to that place); and the race of Iksvāku as well as the rangets of the woods shall meet with destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं नैव गमिष्यामि किष्किन्धां नगरीमितः
न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं मैथिलीं विना
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ naiva gamiṣyāmi kiṣkindhāṁ nagarīmitaḥ
na hi śakṣyāmyahaṁ draṣṭuṁ sugrīvaṁ maithilīṁ vinā

translations.english: Therefore I will not repair hence to the city of Kiskindhā; nor can I see Sugrīva without Mithila's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
हस्तादानो मुखादानो नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः
वानप्रस्थो भविष्यामि अदृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
hastādāno mukhādāno niyato vṛkṣamūlikaḥ
vānaprastho bhaviṣyāmi adṛṣṭvā janakātmajām

translations.english: On my not going there and staying here, those righteous-souled Maharathas as well as the fastfleeting monkeys, shall preserve their lives through hope (of hearing tidings concerning Sītā). And not having seen Janaka's daughter, I will lead the Vānaprastha mode of life, partaking (of fruits) falling into my hands or mouth, restraining my senses, and staying at the foot of trees.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरानूपजे देशे बहुमूलफलोदके
चितां कृत्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि समिद्धमरणीसुतम्
verses.transliteration:
sāgarānūpaje deśe bahumūlaphalodake
citāṁ kṛtvā pravekṣyāmi samiddhamaraṇīsutam

translations.english: Preparing a funereal pile on a tract bordering on the sea, abounding in fruits, and flowers, and water, I will enter into flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
उपविष्टस्य वा सम्यग्लिङ्गिनं साधयिष्यतः
शरीरं भक्षयिष्यन्ति वायसाः श्वापदानि च
verses.transliteration:
upaviṣṭasya vā samyagliṅginaṁ sādhayiṣyataḥ
śarīraṁ bhakṣayiṣyanti vāyasāḥ śvāpadāni ca

translations.english: As I sit to fast, and for effecting the separation of self from my body and centring my identity in the spirit crows and beasts of prey shall feed on my body.

verses.sanskrit:
इदमप्यृषिभिर्दृष्टं निर्याणमिति मे मतिः
सम्यगापः प्रवेक्ष्यामि न चेत्पश्यामि जानकीम्
verses.transliteration:
idamapyṛṣibhirdṛṣṭaṁ niryāṇamiti me matiḥ
samyagāpaḥ pravekṣyāmi na cetpaśyāmi jānakīm

translations.english: I think the sages have enjoyed another way of exit. I shall, failing to see Janaki, enter into water.

verses.sanskrit:
सुजातमूला सुभगा कीर्तिमालायशस्विनी
प्रभग्ना चिररात्रीयं मम सीतामपश्यतः
verses.transliteration:
sujātamūlā subhagā kīrtimālāyaśasvinī
prabhagnā cirarātrīyaṁ mama sītāmapaśyataḥ

translations.english: My illustrious and exalted garland of fame, begot of excellent acts, has perished for good in consequence of my not seeing Sītā.* *Tirtha reads chiraratriyam for chiraratrya. Then the sense is. This illustrious live-long fairrooted and auspicious night crowned with a garland of fame, has borne no fruit, in consequence of my not seeing Sītă. The commentator, I presume, refines a little too much.

verses.sanskrit:
तापसो वा भविष्यामि नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः
नेतः प्रतिगमिष्यामि तामदृष्ट्वासितेक्षणाम्
verses.transliteration:
tāpaso vā bhaviṣyāmi niyato vṛkṣamūlikaḥ
netaḥ pratigamiṣyāmi tāmadṛṣṭvāsitekṣaṇām

translations.english: Or restraining myself, I shall become an ascetic living underneath trees; but return I will not, without obtaining a sight of that dark-eyed damsel.

verses.sanskrit:
यदीतः प्रतिगच्छामि सीतामनधिगम्य ताम्
अङ्गदः सहितैः सर्वैर्वानरैर्न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadītaḥ pratigacchāmi sītāmanadhigamya tām
aṅgadaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvairvānarairna bhaviṣyati

translations.english: If I return without seeing Sītā, all the monkeys with Angada shall cease to exist.

verses.sanskrit:
विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन्प्राप्नोति भद्रकम्
तस्मात्प्राणान्धरिष्यामि ध्रुवो जीवति संगमः
verses.transliteration:
vināśe bahavo doṣā jīvanprāpnoti bhadrakam
tasmātprāṇāndhariṣyāmi dhruvo jīvati saṁgamaḥ

translations.english: Incalculable are the ills of my putting a period to my existence; (on the other hand) if I live, I imay come by good. Therefore my life I will maintain. If I live, it may conduce to happiness."

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधं दुःखं मनसा धारयन्मुहुः
नाध्यगच्छत्तदा पारं शोकस्य कपिकुञ्जरः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bahuvidhaṁ duḥkhaṁ manasā dhārayanmuhuḥ
nādhyagacchattadā pāraṁ śokasya kapikuñjaraḥ

translations.english: Having thus indulged in a variety of harassing thoughts in his mind, that foremost of monkeys could not cross over to the other shore (of the sea of distress).

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं वा वधिष्यामि दशग्रीवं महाबलम्
काममस्तु हृता सीता प्रत्याचीर्णं भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaṁ vā vadhiṣyāmi daśagrīvaṁ mahābalam
kāmamastu hṛtā sītā pratyācīrṇaṁ bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Then summoning energy, that elephantine monkey endued with fortitude reflected, Or I shall slay the Ten-necked Rāvaņa possessed of great strength. Sītā has been carried off; but by this I shall avenge myself.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वैनं समुत्क्षिप्य उपर्युपरि सागरम्
रामायोपहरिष्यामि पशुं पशुपतेरिव
verses.transliteration:
atha vainaṁ samutkṣipya uparyupari sāgaram
rāmāyopahariṣyāmi paśuṁ paśupateriva

translations.english: Or throwing him repeatedly into the sea, I (shall take him) and present him to Rāma, even as one presents a beast to Pasupat." 'An appellation of Siva-lit. lord of beasts-in allusion to animal sacrifices to Śiva.

verses.sanskrit:
इति चिन्ता समापन्नः सीतामनधिगम्य ताम्
ध्यानशोका परीतात्मा चिन्तयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
iti cintā samāpannaḥ sītāmanadhigamya tām
dhyānaśokā parītātmā cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: Reflecting thus, the monkey, not finding Sītā, agitated with sorrow and anxiety, thought.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्सीतां न पश्यामि रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्
तावदेतां पुरीं लङ्कां विचिनोमि पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
yāvatsītāṁ na paśyāmi rāmapatnīṁ yaśasvinīm
tāvadetāṁ purīṁ laṅkāṁ vicinomi punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: So long as I do not find the illustrious spouse of Rāma, Sītā, I will explore the city of Lankā again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
संपाति वचनाच्चापि रामं यद्यानयाम्यहम्
अपश्यन्राघवो भार्यां निर्दहेत्सर्ववानरान्
verses.transliteration:
saṁpāti vacanāccāpi rāmaṁ yadyānayāmyaham
apaśyanrāghavo bhāryāṁ nirdahetsarvavānarān

translations.english: If in consonance with Sampat's speech, I bring Rāma hither, Rāghava, not seeing his wife, shall burn all the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव नियताहारो वत्स्यामि नियतेन्द्रियः
न मत्कृते विनश्येयुः सर्वे ते नरवानराः
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva niyatāhāro vatsyāmi niyatendriyaḥ
na matkṛte vinaśyeyuḥ sarve te naravānarāḥ

translations.english: (Therefore) even here I shall stay, restraining my fare and mortifying my senses. All those principal monkeys ought not to lose their lives because of any act to which I may commit myself.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकवनिका चापि महतीयं महाद्रुमा
इमामभिगमिष्यामि न हीयं विचिता मया
verses.transliteration:
aśokavanikā cāpi mahatīyaṁ mahādrumā
imāmabhigamiṣyāmi na hīyaṁ vicitā mayā

translations.english: This is the Asoka wood, extensive and containing mighty trees. This I shall explore, as it has not yet been searched by me.

verses.sanskrit:
वसून्रुद्रांस्तथादित्यानश्विनौ मरुतोऽपि च
नमस्कृत्वा गमिष्यामि रक्षसां शोकवर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
vasūnrudrāṁstathādityānaśvinau maruto'pi ca
namaskṛtvā gamiṣyāmi rakṣasāṁ śokavardhanaḥ

translations.english: And saluting the Vasus, the Rudras, the Aditya, the twin Asvins, (and Rāma and Laks mana), I enhancing the sorrow of the Raksas, shall go into it.

verses.sanskrit:
जित्वा तु राक्षसान्देवीमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दिनीम्
संप्रदास्यामि रामाया यथासिद्धिं तपस्विने
verses.transliteration:
jitvā tu rākṣasāndevīmikṣvākukulanandinīm
saṁpradāsyāmi rāmāyā yathāsiddhiṁ tapasvine

translations.english: Having vanquished the Rākşas, I will bestow on Rāma the lady of the Ikşvāku race like the fruit of asceticism conferred on an ascetic.

verses.sanskrit:
नमोऽस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय; देव्यै च तस्यै जनकात्मजायै
नमोऽस्तु रुद्रेन्द्रयमानिलेभ्यो; नमोऽस्तु चन्द्रार्कमरुद्गणेभ्यः
verses.transliteration:
namo'stu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya; devyai ca tasyai janakātmajāyai
namo'stu rudrendrayamānilebhyo; namo'stu candrārkamarudgaṇebhyaḥ

translations.english: Having thus reflected for a space, the mightyarmed offspring of the Wind-god, his senses agitated with anxiety, arose. “I bow to Rāma with Lakşmaņa, and to the revered daughter of Janaka, I bow to Rudra, and Indra, and Yama, and Wind-god, and I bow to the Moon, to Fire and to the Maruts."

verses.sanskrit:
स तेभ्यस्तु नमस्कृत्वा सुग्रीवाय च मारुतिः
दिशः सर्वाः समालोक्य अशोकवनिकां प्रति
verses.transliteration:
sa tebhyastu namaskṛtvā sugrīvāya ca mārutiḥ
diśaḥ sarvāḥ samālokya aśokavanikāṁ prati

translations.english: Having bowed to them all, as also to Sugrīva, the offspring of the Wind-god, surveying all he cardinal points, mentally entered the Asoka wood.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा मनसा पूर्वमशोकवनिकां शुभाम्
उत्तरं चिन्तयामास वानरो मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā manasā pūrvamaśokavanikāṁ śubhām
uttaraṁ cintayāmāsa vānaro mārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: Having mentally entered the Asoka wood, that monkey, son to the Wind-god, reflected as to what he should do next.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रुवं तु रक्षोबहुला भविष्यति वनाकुला
अशोकवनिका चिन्त्या सर्वसंस्कारसंस्कृता
verses.transliteration:
dhruvaṁ tu rakṣobahulā bhaviṣyati vanākulā
aśokavanikā cintyā sarvasaṁskārasaṁskṛtā

translations.english: The sacred Asoka wood, sanctified with every purifying rite and abounding in woods, needs must be full of Rāksas.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षिणश्चात्र विहिता नूनं रक्षन्ति पादपान्
भगवानपि सर्वात्मा नातिक्षोभं प्रवायति
verses.transliteration:
rakṣiṇaścātra vihitā nūnaṁ rakṣanti pādapān
bhagavānapi sarvātmā nātikṣobhaṁ pravāyati

translations.english: And warders, directed there to, forsooth, protect the trees, and that worshipful Soul of the universe does not breathe here vigorously.

verses.sanskrit:
संक्षिप्तोऽयं मयात्मा च रामार्थे रावणस्य च
सिद्धिं मे संविधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षिगणास्त्विह
verses.transliteration:
saṁkṣipto'yaṁ mayātmā ca rāmārthe rāvaṇasya ca
siddhiṁ me saṁvidhāsyanti devāḥ sarṣigaṇāstviha

translations.english: I contract my person in the interests of Rāma, and in order that Rāvana may not see me. May all the deities along with the saints confer success on me.

verses.sanskrit:
तदुन्नसं पाण्डुरदन्तमव्रणं; शुचिस्मितं पद्मपलाशलोचनम्
द्रक्ष्ये तदार्यावदनं कदा न्वहं; प्रसन्नताराधिपतुल्यदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
tadunnasaṁ pāṇḍuradantamavraṇaṁ; śucismitaṁ padmapalāśalocanam
drakṣye tadāryāvadanaṁ kadā nvahaṁ; prasannatārādhipatulyadarśanam

translations.english: When shall I behold the blameless face of that noble lady, with its protruding nose; having luminous smiles, having eyes resembling lotuspetals; and bright as the complacent lord of stars?

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुद्रेण पापेन नृशंसकर्मणा; सुदारुणालांकृतवेषधारिणा
बलाभिभूता अबला तपस्विनी; कथं नु मे दृष्टपथेऽद्य सा भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kṣudreṇa pāpena nṛśaṁsakarmaṇā; sudāruṇālāṁkṛtaveṣadhāriṇā
balābhibhūtā abalā tapasvinī; kathaṁ nu me dṛṣṭapathe'dya sā bhavet

translations.english: Ah! today how shall feeble forlorn one that has been borne down by the force of the mean, abject and grim-visaged (Ravana), fierce yet wearing (at the time of the rape), a dress tending to inspire confidence, come in my sight?

verses.sanskrit:
स मुहूर्तमिव ध्यत्वा मनसा चाधिगम्य ताम्
अवप्लुतो महातेजाः प्राकारं तस्य वेश्मनः
verses.transliteration:
sa muhūrtamiva dhyatvā manasā cādhigamya tām
avapluto mahātejāḥ prākāraṁ tasya veśmanaḥ

translations.english: Having reflected for a while and mentally met with her, that highly energetic one leapt from the wall of Rāvana's mansion on to that (of the Asoka wood).

verses.sanskrit:
सालानशोकान्भव्यांश्च चम्पकांश्च सुपुष्पितान्
उद्दालकान्नागवृक्षांश्चूतान्कपिमुखानपि
verses.transliteration:
sālānaśokānbhavyāṁśca campakāṁśca supuṣpitān
uddālakānnāgavṛkṣāṁścūtānkapimukhānapi

translations.english: All his frame filled with delight, that mighty monkey, stationed on the wall, saw various trees having their tops furnished with flowers through spring and the other seasons, salas and Asokas, bhavyas, champakas, uddalakas, and Nāgas, and those bearing fruits resembling the mouths of monkeys; and those relative to mango woods, with hundreds of plants. And (Hanuman) leapt into the garden like an arrow let go from the bow string.

verses.sanskrit:
मार्गमाणो वरारोहां राजपुत्रीमनिन्दिताम्
सुखप्रसुप्तान्विहगान्बोधयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
mārgamāṇo varārohāṁ rājaputrīmaninditām
sukhaprasuptānvihagānbodhayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: As he was searching for that surpassingly beautiful and blameless daughter of the king, that monkey awakened the monkeys that were sleeping sweetly..

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पतद्भिर्द्विजगणैः पक्षैः सालाः समाहताः
अनेकवर्णा विविधा मुमुचुः पुष्पवृष्टयः
verses.transliteration:
utpatadbhirdvijagaṇaiḥ pakṣaiḥ sālāḥ samāhatāḥ
anekavarṇā vividhā mumucuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ

translations.english: And blown against by the wind caused by the wings of the birds as they flew upwards, various and variegated trees showered down blossoms.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पावकीर्णः शुशुभे हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
अशोकवनिकामध्ये यथा पुष्पमयो गिरिः
verses.transliteration:
puṣpāvakīrṇaḥ śuśubhe hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
aśokavanikāmadhye yathā puṣpamayo giriḥ
