translations.english: Like to a sinner unworthy of praying for final emancipation, it dose not behove you to expect to come by me. Devoted to one husband I shall never perpetrate such an iniquitous act.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणं तं यशस्विनी
राक्षसं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भूयो वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu vaidehī rāvaṇaṁ taṁ yaśasvinī
rākṣasaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhūyo vacanamabravīt

translations.english: I am born in a high and have been married in a pious family. Having accosted Rāvana thus, the well-known Vaidehi, turning her back, again spake to him, saying. "I should not live with you since I am another's wife and chaste."

verses.sanskrit:
नाहमौपयिकी भार्या परभार्या सती तव
साधु धर्ममवेक्षस्व साधु साधुव्रतं चर
verses.transliteration:
nāhamaupayikī bhāryā parabhāryā satī tava
sādhu dharmamavekṣasva sādhu sādhuvrataṁ cara

translations.english: Have your eyes always on religion and do you follow in the track of piety. Like to yours own wives, others are worthy of being protected by you, O ranger of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
अतुष्टं स्वेषु दारेषु चपलं चलितेन्द्रियम्
नयन्ति निकृतिप्रज्ञां परदाराः पराभवम्
verses.transliteration:
atuṣṭaṁ sveṣu dāreṣu capalaṁ calitendriyam
nayanti nikṛtiprajñāṁ paradārāḥ parābhavam

translations.english: Making an example of you, do you enjoy with your own wives. Forsooth those vicious-minded, those of agitated senses, who are not satisfied with their own wives, are brought to misery by others' wives.

verses.sanskrit:
इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे
वचो मिथ्या प्रणीतात्मा पथ्यमुक्तं विचक्षणैः
verses.transliteration:
iha santo na vā santi sato vā nānuvartase
vaco mithyā praṇītātmā pathyamuktaṁ vicakṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: Or the considerate people have spoken the truth, but you, for the destruction of the race of the Raksasas, considering that false, had not followed it.

verses.sanskrit:
अकृतात्मानमासाद्य राजानमनये रतम्
समृद्धानि विनश्यन्ति राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च
verses.transliteration:
akṛtātmānamāsādya rājānamanaye ratam
samṛddhāni vinaśyanti rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca

translations.english: Wealth, kingdom and cities-all are brought to naught when they are placed at the hands of a vicious and illiterate king.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेयं त्वां समासाद्य लङ्का रत्नौघ संकुला
अपराधात्तवैकस्य नचिराद्विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tatheyaṁ tvāṁ samāsādya laṅkā ratnaugha saṁkulā
aparādhāttavaikasya nacirādvinaśiṣyati

translations.english: Obtaining you, (therefore) as her king and for your folly only, this city of Lankā, abounding in jewels, shall soon be ruined.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वकृतैर्हन्यमानस्य रावणादीर्घदर्शिनः
अभिनन्दन्ति भूतानि विनाशे पापकर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
svakṛtairhanyamānasya rāvaṇādīrghadarśinaḥ
abhinandanti bhūtāni vināśe pāpakarmaṇaḥ

translations.english: O Rāvana, every one delight in the destruction of that inconsiderate being, who bring about his own destruction and is engaged in the perpetration of evil deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं त्वां पापकर्माणं वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः
दिष्ट्यैतद्व्यसनं प्राप्तो रौद्र इत्येव हर्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tvāṁ pāpakarmāṇaṁ vakṣyanti nikṛtā janāḥ
diṣṭyaitadvyasanaṁ prāpto raudra ityeva harṣitāḥ

translations.english: In this way, yourself, the perpetrator of vicious acts, meeting with your end, those persons who had been tyrannised by you, shall, delightedly, say, “Oh! blessed are we since this terrible (Raksasa) has met with his end."

verses.sanskrit:
शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा
अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण प्रभा यथा
verses.transliteration:
śakyā lobhayituṁ nāhamaiśvaryeṇa dhanena vā
ananyā rāghaveṇāhaṁ bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā

translations.english: With wealth or riches you shall not be able to tempt me. As the rays of the sun belong to him, so I am Rāghava's only.

verses.sanskrit:
उपधाय भुजं तस्य लोकनाथस्य सत्कृतम्
कथं नामोपधास्यामि भुजमन्यस्य कस्यचित्
verses.transliteration:
upadhāya bhujaṁ tasya lokanāthasya satkṛtam
kathaṁ nāmopadhāsyāmi bhujamanyasya kasyacit

translations.english: Having laid my head on the beautiful arms of that lord of men, how shall I place it again on another's?

verses.sanskrit:
अहमौपयिकी भार्या तस्यैव वसुधापतेः
व्रतस्नातस्य विप्रस्य विद्येव विदितात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ahamaupayikī bhāryā tasyaiva vasudhāpateḥ
vratasnātasya viprasya vidyeva viditātmanaḥ

translations.english: Like the knowledge of one God monopolized by the Brāhmaṇas only, I am the spouse of that lord of earth only, cognisant of higher truths and marrying me according to the pious ceremonials.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्
वने वाशितया सार्धं करेण्वेव गजाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
sādhu rāvaṇa rāmeṇa māṁ samānaya duḥkhitām
vane vāśitayā sārdhaṁ kareṇveva gajādhipam

translations.english: to May good betide you, O Rāvaņa. Do you take me to Rāma, stricken with grief as I am, like to a she-elephant anxiously waiting in the forest brought to the lord of elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
मित्रमौपयिकं कर्तुं रामः स्थानं परीप्सता
वधं चानिच्छता घोरं त्वयासौ पुरुषर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
mitramaupayikaṁ kartuṁ rāmaḥ sthānaṁ parīpsatā
vadhaṁ cānicchatā ghoraṁ tvayāsau puruṣarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: It behove you to make friends with Rāma, that best of men, if do you desire to maintain your empire and do not wish to bring about your own destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
वर्जयेद्वज्रमुत्सृष्टं वर्जयेदन्तकश्चिरम्
त्वद्विधं न तु संक्रुद्धो लोकनाथः स राघवः
verses.transliteration:
varjayedvajramutsṛṣṭaṁ varjayedantakaściram
tvadvidhaṁ na tu saṁkruddho lokanāthaḥ sa rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Thunderbolt, even, when hurled, may leave you, Death himself may overlook you-but there is no safety for you, if Rāghava, the lord of men is enraged.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्
शतक्रतुविसृष्टस्य निर्घोषमशनेरिव
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya dhanuṣaḥ śabdaṁ śroṣyasi tvaṁ mahāsvanam
śatakratuvisṛṣṭasya nirghoṣamaśaneriva

translations.english: You shall hear the terrible sound of the twang of Rāma's bow, like to the sound of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra. Soon shall arrows, bearing the names of Rāma and Lakşmaņa and having fiery heads like those of snakes, alight here.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षांसि परिनिघ्नन्तः पुर्यामस्यां समन्ततः
असंपातं करिष्यन्ति पतन्तः कङ्कवाससः
verses.transliteration:
rakṣāṁsi parinighnantaḥ puryāmasyāṁ samantataḥ
asaṁpātaṁ kariṣyanti patantaḥ kaṅkavāsasaḥ

translations.english: And covered with Kanka leaves they shall undoubtedly cover the whole city and devastate it by destroying all the Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसेन्द्रमहासर्पान्स रामगरुडो महान्
उद्धरिष्यति वेगेन वैनतेय इवोरगान्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasendramahāsarpānsa rāmagaruḍo mahān
uddhariṣyati vegena vainateya ivoragān

translations.english: Like to Garuda pulling up the snakes, the Garuda like Rāma shall pull up your snake-like Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अपनेष्यति मां भर्ता त्वत्तः शीघ्रमरिंदमः
असुरेभ्यः श्रियं दीप्तां विष्णुस्त्रिभिरिव क्रमैः
verses.transliteration:
apaneṣyati māṁ bhartā tvattaḥ śīghramariṁdamaḥ
asurebhyaḥ śriyaṁ dīptāṁ viṣṇustribhiriva kramaiḥ

translations.english: Like to Vişņu recovering the effulgent Śrī (the Goddess of wealth) from the Asuras, by crossing over the three worlds with three foot-steps, my husband, the conqueror of foes, shall recover me from you.

verses.sanskrit:
जनस्थाने हतस्थाने निहते रक्षसां बले
अशक्तेन त्वया रक्षः कृतमेतदसाधु वै
verses.transliteration:
janasthāne hatasthāne nihate rakṣasāṁ bale
aśaktena tvayā rakṣaḥ kṛtametadasādhu vai

translations.english: Janasthāna has been devastated, the host of Rākṣasas has been killed, and you had been disabled. Truly you had perpetrated an impious deed.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया
शक्यं संदर्शने स्थातुं शुना शार्दूलयोरिव
verses.transliteration:
na hi gandhamupāghrāya rāmalakṣmaṇayostvayā
śakyaṁ saṁdarśane sthātuṁ śunā śārdūlayoriva

translations.english: O Rākṣasa, those two lions among men going out to enquire about the illusive deer, I was ravished by you, entering the empty hermitage O vile wight. And like to a dog incapable of standing before a tiger, it would have been impossible for you, to wait there in the presence of Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ते विग्रहे ताभ्यां युगग्रहणमस्थिरम्
वृत्रस्येवेन्द्रबाहुभ्यां बाहोरेकस्य निग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
tasya te vigrahe tābhyāṁ yugagrahaṇamasthiram
vṛtrasyevendrabāhubhyāṁ bāhorekasya nigrahaḥ

translations.english: If do you engage in conflict with them, your wealth and friends shall be of no avail to you (and you shall be discomfited) like to onehanded Asura Vſtra by the two handed Indra.* *The allusion is-the mighty Asura Vrtra fought with Indra for a long time even after he had his one hand chopped off.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
तोयमल्पमिवादित्यः प्राणानादास्यते शरैः
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṁ tava sa nātho me rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
toyamalpamivādityaḥ prāṇānādāsyate śaraiḥ

translations.english: Soon shall my husband, with the assistance of Lakşmaņa, draw out your life with arrows, like to the sun drying up, by his rays, shallow water.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथ वालयं; सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः
असंशयं दाशरथेर्न मोक्ष्यसे; महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव
verses.transliteration:
giriṁ kuberasya gato'tha vālayaṁ; sabhāṁ gato vā varuṇasya rājñaḥ
asaṁśayaṁ dāśaratherna mokṣyase; mahādrumaḥ kālahato'śaneriva

translations.english: Whether do you repair to the abode of Kubera, or whether do you, terrified, take refuge to the assembly of Varuna, you shall, for certain, be destroyed by the son of Dasaratha, like to a mighty tree broken down by thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं राक्षसाधिपः
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां विप्रियं प्रियदर्शनाम्
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā paruṣaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṁ vipriyaṁ priyadarśanām

translations.english: Hearing those harsh accents, that lord of Rākṣasas, replied to Sītā, of comely presence, with the following unpleasant words.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा
यथा यथा प्रियं वक्ता परिभूतस्तथा तथा
verses.transliteration:
yathā yathā sāntvayitā vaśyaḥ strīṇāṁ tathā tathā
yathā yathā priyaṁ vaktā paribhūtastathā tathā

translations.english: It is generally found on earth that the more a woman is courted by a man, the more she is brought under his influence, (But for you) the more kindly I have been behaving towards you, the more roughly I have been treated.

verses.sanskrit:
संनियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः
द्रवतो मार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः
verses.transliteration:
saṁniyacchati me krodhaṁ tvayi kāmaḥ samutthitaḥ
dravato mārgamāsādya hayāniva susārathiḥ

translations.english: Truly dose my love for you keep in control the wrath like to a good charioteer restraining the swerving steed.

verses.sanskrit:
वामः कामो मनुष्याणां यस्मिन्किल निबध्यते
जने तस्मिंस्त्वनुक्रोशः स्नेहश्च किल जायते
verses.transliteration:
vāmaḥ kāmo manuṣyāṇāṁ yasminkila nibadhyate
jane tasmiṁstvanukrośaḥ snehaśca kila jāyate

translations.english: O mighty is amour to men, for on whom this amour fall, albeit she is an object of wrath, becomes an object of kindness and affection.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मात्कारणान्न तां घतयामि वरानने
वधार्हामवमानार्हां मिथ्याप्रव्रजिते रताम्
verses.transliteration:
etasmātkāraṇānna tāṁ ghatayāmi varānane
vadhārhāmavamānārhāṁ mithyāpravrajite ratām

translations.english: O you of fair countenance, it is for this reason, that I do not destroy you, although you, who are engaged in false asceticism, are worthy of being killed and dishonoured. do you

verses.sanskrit:
परुषाणि हि वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम्
तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः
verses.transliteration:
paruṣāṇi hi vākyāni yāni yāni bravīṣi mām
teṣu teṣu vadho yuktastava maithili dāruṇaḥ

translations.english: O Maithili, for each and every one of all those harsh words which you had used by me, deserve death.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेहीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
क्रोधसंरम्भसंयुक्तः सीतामुत्तरमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu vaidehīṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
krodhasaṁrambhasaṁyuktaḥ sītāmuttaramabravīt

translations.english: Having spoken thus to Vaidehi, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, having his wrath subdued, again bespake Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ मासौ रक्षितव्यौ मे योऽवधिस्ते मया कृतः
ततः शयनमारोह मम त्वं वरवर्णिनि
verses.transliteration:
dvau māsau rakṣitavyau me yo'vadhiste mayā kṛtaḥ
tataḥ śayanamāroha mama tvaṁ varavarṇini

translations.english: I shall wait for those two months, of which I have made a contract, after which you shall have to share my bed. O you of a comely presence.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वाभ्यामूर्ध्वं तु मासाभ्यां भर्तारं मामनिच्छतीम्
मम त्वां प्रातराशार्थमारभन्ते महानसे
verses.transliteration:
dvābhyāmūrdhvaṁ tu māsābhyāṁ bhartāraṁ māmanicchatīm
mama tvāṁ prātarāśārthamārabhante mahānase

translations.english: Even then if you do refuse to regard me as your husband, my cooks shall mince your limbs with steel and serve you for my morning meal.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तर्ज्यमानां संप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण जानकीम्
देवगन्धर्वकन्यास्ता विषेदुर्विपुलेक्षणाः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tarjyamānāṁ saṁprekṣya rākṣasendreṇa jānakīm
devagandharvakanyāstā viṣedurvipulekṣaṇāḥ

translations.english: Beholding the lord of Rākşasas remonstrate with the daughter of Janaka is this wise, the daughters of the celestials and Gandharvas became exceedingly sorry.

verses.sanskrit:
ओष्ठप्रकारैरपरा नेत्रवक्त्रैस्तथापराः
सीतामाश्वासयामासुस्तर्जितां तेन रक्षसा
verses.transliteration:
oṣṭhaprakārairaparā netravaktraistathāparāḥ
sītāmāśvāsayāmāsustarjitāṁ tena rakṣasā

translations.english: Some with lips, some with eyes, and some with gestures of their faces, they all consoled Sita, thus distressed by that Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभिराश्वासिता सीता रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं वृत्तशौण्डीर्यगर्वितम्
verses.transliteration:
tābhirāśvāsitā sītā rāvaṇaṁ rākṣasādhipam
uvācātmahitaṁ vākyaṁ vṛttaśauṇḍīryagarvitam

translations.english: Thus consoled by them, and being proud of her good conduct and her husband's heroism, Sītā thus addressed Rāvana, the lord of Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं न ते जनः कश्चिदसिन्निःश्रेयसे स्थितः
निवारयति यो न त्वां कर्मणोऽस्माद्विगर्हितात्
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ na te janaḥ kaścidasinniḥśreyase sthitaḥ
nivārayati yo na tvāṁ karmaṇo'smādvigarhitāt

translations.english: Forsooth there is no person in this city who desire your welfare and therefore prevent you from such an impious deed.

verses.sanskrit:
मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः
त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसापि कः
verses.transliteration:
māṁ hi dharmātmanaḥ patnīṁ śacīmiva śacīpateḥ
tvadanyastriṣu lokeṣu prārthayenmanasāpi kaḥ

translations.english: Who is there in the three worlds, who even desire me in mind, who am the spouse of the virtuous souled (Rāma) like to Indra's Sacī.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः
उक्तवानसि यत्पापं क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasādhama rāmasya bhāryāmamitatejasaḥ
uktavānasi yatpāpaṁ kva gatastasya mokṣyase

translations.english: O you the vilest of the Rākşasas, for using those vicious words towards the spouse of Rāma, of immeasured prowess, repairing whither shall you escape vengeance?

verses.sanskrit:
यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश्च सहितौ वने
तथा द्विरदवद्रामस्त्वं नीच शशवत्स्मृतः
verses.transliteration:
yathā dṛptaśca mātaṅgaḥ śaśaśca sahitau vane
tathā dviradavadrāmastvaṁ nīca śaśavatsmṛtaḥ

translations.english: Like to an infuriated elephant encountering a hare in the forest, you shall O Vile! a hare as you are, meet with that elephant-like Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वमिक्ष्वाकुनाथं वै क्षिपन्निह न लज्जसे
चक्षुषो विषयं तस्य न तावदुपगच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
sa tvamikṣvākunāthaṁ vai kṣipanniha na lajjase
cakṣuṣo viṣayaṁ tasya na tāvadupagacchasi

translations.english: You are not ashamed of railing that lord of Ikşvākus, so long as dose you not come within his ken.

verses.sanskrit:
इमे ते नयने क्रूरे विरूपे कृष्णपिङ्गले
क्षितौ न पतिते कस्मान्मामनार्यनिरीक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
ime te nayane krūre virūpe kṛṣṇapiṅgale
kṣitau na patite kasmānmāmanāryanirīkṣitaḥ

translations.english: O base! why do not your grim, terrible, coppery eyes, looking so viciously at me, fall down on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं स्नुषां दशरथस्य च
कथं व्याहरतो मां ते न जिह्वा पाप शीर्यते
verses.transliteration:
tasya dharmātmanaḥ patnīṁ snuṣāṁ daśarathasya ca
kathaṁ vyāharato māṁ te na jihvā pāpa śīryate

translations.english: O vicious wretch, I am the spouse of that virtuous-souled (Rāma) and daughter-in-law of Dasaratha—using these vile words towards me, why dose not your tongue fall off?

verses.sanskrit:
असंदेशात्तु रामस्य तपसश्चानुपालनात्
न त्वां कुर्मि दशग्रीव भस्म भस्मार्हतेजसा
verses.transliteration:
asaṁdeśāttu rāmasya tapasaścānupālanāt
na tvāṁ kurmi daśagrīva bhasma bhasmārhatejasā

translations.english: O Ten-necked one, I can instantly reduce you to ashes but for Rāma's mandate and my ascetic observances.

verses.sanskrit:
नापहर्तुमहं शक्या तस्य रामस्य धीमतः
विधिस्तव वधार्थाय विहितो नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration:
nāpahartumahaṁ śakyā tasya rāmasya dhīmataḥ
vidhistava vadhārthāya vihito nātra saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: You could not have ravished me in the presence of the highly intelligent Rāma. And undoubtedly for your destruction this has been brought about by God.

verses.sanskrit:
शूरेण धनदभ्राता बलैः समुदितेन च
अपोह्य रामं कस्माद्धि दारचौर्यं त्वया कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
śūreṇa dhanadabhrātā balaiḥ samuditena ca
apohya rāmaṁ kasmāddhi dāracauryaṁ tvayā kṛtam

translations.english: You are heroic and Kubera's brother and great in prowess, why didst you then take me by stealth after despatching Rāma away from the hermitage?”

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
विवृत्य नयने क्रूरे जानकीमन्ववैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
vivṛtya nayane krūre jānakīmanvavaikṣata

translations.english: Hearing those words of Sītā, Rāvana, the lord of Rāksasas, whirling his grim eyes, looked towards the daughter of Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलजीमूतसंकाशो महाभुजशिरोधरः
सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान्दीप्तजिह्वोग्रलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
nīlajīmūtasaṁkāśo mahābhujaśirodharaḥ
siṁhasattvagatiḥ śrīmāndīptajihvogralocanaḥ

translations.english: He was like to a mass of blue clouds and his arms and necks were long and spacious. He was gifted with elephantine gaits and his tongues and eyes were sharp and flaming.

verses.sanskrit:
चलाग्रमकुटः प्रांशुश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्तप्ताङ्गदविभूषणः
verses.transliteration:
calāgramakuṭaḥ prāṁśuścitramālyānulepanaḥ
raktamālyāmbaradharastaptāṅgadavibhūṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: The top of his crown was shaking and he had charming garland around his neck and his person sprinkled with paste. He had crimson-coloured garlands and clothes on and his charming arms were adorned with ornaments. Encircled with a sword-belt around his waist he appeared like to Mandara, entwined by a snake at the time of the churning of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
तरुणादित्यवर्णाभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितः
रक्तपल्लवपुष्पाभ्यामशोकाभ्यामिवाचलः
verses.transliteration:
taruṇādityavarṇābhyāṁ kuṇḍalābhyāṁ vibhūṣitaḥ
raktapallavapuṣpābhyāmaśokābhyāmivācalaḥ

translations.english: And adorned with a pair of Kundalas (A kind of ornament worn on ears.) resembling the newly risen Sun he looked like a hill covered with two Asoka trees enveloped with crimson flowers and leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
अवेक्षमाणो वैदेहीं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजंग इव निःश्वसन्
verses.transliteration:
avekṣamāṇo vaidehīṁ kopasaṁraktalocanaḥ
uvāca rāvaṇaḥ sītāṁ bhujaṁga iva niḥśvasan

translations.english: And having his eyes red hot with ire, sighing again and again like to a snake and casting his looks upon Sītā, Rāvaņa addressed her again, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अनयेनाभिसंपन्नमर्थहीनमनुव्रते
नाशयाम्यहमद्य त्वां सूर्यः संध्यामिवौजसा
verses.transliteration:
anayenābhisaṁpannamarthahīnamanuvrate
nāśayāmyahamadya tvāṁ sūryaḥ saṁdhyāmivaujasā

translations.english: O you following asceticism, this your vow is without any meaning and beyond the pale of morality. Even shall I destroy you today like to the Sun dispelling darkness with his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः
संदिदेश ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā maithilīṁ rājā rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
saṁdideśa tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīrghoradarśanāḥ

translations.english: Having thus addressed Maithili, the inimical king Rāvaņa cast his looks towards the grimvisaged Rākşasīs.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रतिसमादिश्य राक्षसेन्द्रः पुनः पुनः
काममन्युपरीतात्मा जानकीं पर्यतर्जयत्
verses.transliteration:
iti pratisamādiśya rākṣasendraḥ punaḥ punaḥ
kāmamanyuparītātmā jānakīṁ paryatarjayat

translations.english: And having ordered thus again and again, that lord of Rākşasas, stricken with amour and ire, addressed Sītā, roaring fiercely.

verses.sanskrit:
उपगम्य ततः क्षिप्रं राक्षसी धान्यमालिनी
परिष्वज्य दशग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
upagamya tataḥ kṣipraṁ rākṣasī dhānyamālinī
pariṣvajya daśagrīvamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon approaching speedily and embracing the Ten-necked one, one Rākşasī named Dhānyamālīnī bespoke him.

verses.sanskrit:
मया क्रीड महाराजसीतया किं तवानया
अकामां कामयानस्य शरीरमुपतप्यते
इच्छन्तीं कामयानस्य प्रीतिर्भवति शोभना
verses.transliteration:
mayā krīḍa mahārājasītayā kiṁ tavānayā
akāmāṁ kāmayānasya śarīramupatapyate
icchantīṁ kāmayānasya prītirbhavati śobhanā

translations.english: Again he who desire for an unwilling dame burn his own person—and he who desire for a willing damsel, attain excess of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या समुत्क्षिप्तस्ततो बली
ज्वलद्भास्करवर्णाभं प्रविवेश निवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rākṣasyā samutkṣiptastato balī
jvaladbhāskaravarṇābhaṁ praviveśa niveśanam

translations.english: Having said this, the Rākşasī took away Rāvana by force. And that Rākşasa too, resembling a mass of clouds, laughing, turned back.

verses.sanskrit:
देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च तास्ततः
परिवार्य दशग्रीवं विविशुस्तद्गृहोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
devagandharvakanyāśca nāgakanyāśca tāstataḥ
parivārya daśagrīvaṁ viviśustadgṛhottamam

translations.english: And encircling Rāvana those daughters of celestials Gandharvas and Nāgas, entered into an excellent abode.

verses.sanskrit:
स मैथिलीं धर्मपरामवस्थितां; प्रवेपमानां परिभर्त्स्य रावणः
विहाय सीतां मदनेन मोहितः; स्वमेव वेश्म प्रविवेश भास्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
sa maithilīṁ dharmaparāmavasthitāṁ; pravepamānāṁ paribhartsya rāvaṇaḥ
vihāya sītāṁ madanena mohitaḥ; svameva veśma praviveśa bhāsvaram

translations.english: And having remonstrated with and left behind, the firm and pious Sīta with a trembling person, Rāvana, possessed by amour entered into his own palace.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः
संदिश्य च ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्निर्जगाम ह
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā maithilīṁ rājā rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
saṁdiśya ca tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīrnirjagāma ha

translations.english: Having spoken thus Maithili and commanded the host of the Räksasīs, Rāvana, a terror to his enemies, went away.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्क्रान्ते राक्षसेन्द्रे तु पुनरन्तःपुरं गते
राक्षस्यो भीमरूपास्ताः सीतां समभिदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
niṣkrānte rākṣasendre tu punarantaḥpuraṁ gate
rākṣasyo bhīmarūpāstāḥ sītāṁ samabhidudruvuḥ

translations.english: And after that lord of Rākşasas had gone away and entered his inner apartment, the hideous Rākşasīs drew near Sitä.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
परं परुषया वाचा वैदेहीमिदमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sītāmupāgamya rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
paraṁ paruṣayā vācā vaidehīmidamabruvan

translations.english: And approaching Sītā that terrible host, almost faint with ire, addressed Vaidehī with the following harsh words.

verses.sanskrit:
पौलस्त्यस्य वरिष्ठस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः
दशग्रीवस्य भार्यात्वं सीते न बहु मन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
paulastyasya variṣṭhasya rāvaṇasya mahātmanaḥ
daśagrīvasya bhāryātvaṁ sīte na bahu manyase

translations.english: You do not regard it highly, Sītā, that you shall become the chosen wife of that highsouled, and great Ravana, the Ten-necked son of Paulastya.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वेकजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
आमन्त्र्य क्रोधताम्राक्षी सीतां करतलोदरीम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastvekajaṭā nāma rākṣasī vākyamabravīt
āmantrya krodhatāmrākṣī sītāṁ karatalodarīm

translations.english: Thereupon another Rākṣasī named Ekjatä, with eyes rendered coppery with ire, addressing Sītā, having a small navel, said.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतीनां षण्णां तु चतुर्थो यः प्रजापतिः
मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुलस्त्य इति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatīnāṁ ṣaṇṇāṁ tu caturtho yaḥ prajāpatiḥ
mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ pulastya iti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: Pulastya is the fourth of the six Prajāpatīs, (Prajāpatis are the lords of the created being first created by Brahmā.) a mind-born son of Brahmā and celebrated in the world.

verses.sanskrit:
पुलस्त्यस्य तु तेजस्वी महर्षिर्मानसः सुतः
नाम्ना स विश्रवा नाम प्रजापतिसमप्रभः
verses.transliteration:
pulastyasya tu tejasvī maharṣirmānasaḥ sutaḥ
nāmnā sa viśravā nāma prajāpatisamaprabhaḥ

translations.english: The glorious ascetic, by name Vishravā was the mind-born son to Pulastya, effulgent like to Prajāpatis.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पुत्रो विशालाक्षि रावणः शत्रुरावणः
तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि
मयोक्तं चारुसर्वाङ्गि वाक्यं किं नानुमन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
tasya putro viśālākṣi rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
tasya tvaṁ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitumarhasi
mayoktaṁ cārusarvāṅgi vākyaṁ kiṁ nānumanyase

translations.english: O large-eyed damsel! Of Visravā came Rāvana terrible to his enemies. And it behove you to become the consort of that lord of Raksasas. Scorn not the words I say to you, O you of comely presence.”

verses.sanskrit:
येन देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवराजश्च निर्जितः
तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
yena devāstrayastriṁśaddevarājaśca nirjitaḥ
tasya tvaṁ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitumarhasi

translations.english: Thereupon another Rākşasī named Harijatā, having the eyes of a cat, and whirling them with ire, said It become you to be the wife of that lord of Rākşasas who smote the thirty three celestials and their lord in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
वीर्योत्सिक्तस्य शूरस्य संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः
बलिनो वीर्ययुक्तस्या भार्यात्वं किं न लप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
vīryotsiktasya śūrasya saṁgrāmeṣvanivartinaḥ
balino vīryayuktasyā bhāryātvaṁ kiṁ na lapsyase

translations.english: Do you not desire to be his wife, who is heroic, of indomitable prowess and who dose not turn back in battle?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः
सर्वासां च महाभागां त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः
verses.transliteration:
priyāṁ bahumatāṁ bhāryāṁ tyaktvā rājā mahābalaḥ
sarvāsāṁ ca mahābhāgāṁ tvāmupaiṣyati rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: And turning away in scorn from his beloved wife, highly esteemed, the mighty king Ravana, desire for you. And leaving his inner apartment enriched with thousand of females and adorned with various jewels, Rāvana shall adore you.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सर्वसमृद्धस्या रावणस्य महात्मनः
किमर्थं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्यात्वं नेच्छसेऽधमे
verses.transliteration:
tasya sarvasamṛddhasyā rāvaṇasya mahātmanaḥ
kimarthaṁ rākṣasendrasya bhāryātvaṁ necchase'dhame

translations.english: And then followed another Rākşasī by name Vikatā, “The king, who by his terrible prowess subdued the Gandharvas (Heavenly singers and musicians who belong to the heaven of Indra.) and Nāgas, (Serpent-gods who dwell in the regions under the carth.) in battle, has stood by you. O foolish damsel, why do you not wish to be the consort of that high-souled lord of Rākşasas-Rāvana, gifted with wealth and riches."

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य च मारुतः
न वाति स्मायतापाङ्गे किं त्वं तस्य न तिष्ठसि
verses.transliteration:
yasya sūryo na tapati bhīto yasya ca mārutaḥ
na vāti smāyatāpāṅge kiṁ tvaṁ tasya na tiṣṭhasi

translations.english: Then followed another Rākşaşī named Durmukhi. “Why dose you not approach him, O you having expansive eyes, by whose fear, the sun dose not shine, and the wind dose not blow."

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य नैरृतराजस्य राजराजस्य भामिनि
किं त्वं न कुरुषे बुद्धिं भार्यार्थे रावणस्य हि
verses.transliteration:
tasya nairṛtarājasya rājarājasya bhāmini
kiṁ tvaṁ na kuruṣe buddhiṁ bhāryārthe rāvaṇasya hi

translations.english: O dame, why do you not wish to be the consort of Rāvana, the lord of Rākṣasas, at whose command the trees shower blossoms and the hills and clouds pour down water. Why do you not make up your mind to be the wife of Rāvana?

verses.sanskrit:
साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवि कथितं साधु भामिनि
गृहाण सुस्मिते वाक्यमन्यथा न भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sādhu te tattvato devi kathitaṁ sādhu bhāmini
gṛhāṇa susmite vākyamanyathā na bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: O damsel, O worshipful dame, we have spoken thus for your welfare. Do you comply with our request or you shall surely die. CECTION 24

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः
परुषं परुषा नार्य ऊचुस्ता वाक्यमप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sītāmupāgamya rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ
paruṣaṁ paruṣā nārya ūcustā vākyamapriyam

translations.english: Thereupon all those Rākşasīs, having terrible faces again and again pursued Sitä with reproaches rough and rude.

verses.sanskrit:
किं त्वमन्तःपुरे सीते सर्वभूतमनोहरे
महार्हशयनोपेते न वासमनुमन्यसे
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tvamantaḥpure sīte sarvabhūtamanohare
mahārhaśayanopete na vāsamanumanyase

translations.english: Why do you not desire, O Sītā, to live in his inner apartment, liked by all and abounding in costly bed-steads.

verses.sanskrit:
मानुषी मानुषस्यैव भार्यात्वं बहु मन्यसे
प्रत्याहर मनो रामान्न त्वं जातु भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
mānuṣī mānuṣasyaiva bhāryātvaṁ bahu manyase
pratyāhara mano rāmānna tvaṁ jātu bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: O woman, you regardest highly to be the wife of a man. Do you turn back from Rāma-your desire shall never be satisfied.

verses.sanskrit:
मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने
राज्याद्भ्रष्टमसिद्धार्थं विक्लवं तमनिन्दिते
verses.transliteration:
mānuṣī mānuṣaṁ taṁ tu rāmamicchasi śobhane
rājyādbhraṣṭamasiddhārthaṁ viklavaṁ tamanindite

translations.english: You are a woman, O you of comely presence, and therefore dose your fancy cling to Rāma, O you of a blameless countenance, who is a man, deprived of his kingdom, overwhelmed with disasters and has his desires frustrated.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा सीता पद्मनिभेक्षणा
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasīnāṁ vacaḥ śrutvā sītā padmanibhekṣaṇā
netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāmidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of those Rākşasīs, the lotus-eyed Sītā, with her eyes full of tears said.

verses.sanskrit:
यदिदं लोकविद्विष्टमुदाहरथ संगताः
नैतन्मनसि वाक्यं मे किल्बिषं प्रतितिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
yadidaṁ lokavidviṣṭamudāharatha saṁgatāḥ
naitanmanasi vākyaṁ me kilbiṣaṁ pratitiṣṭhati

translations.english: What you have all said and which is against human usage and vicious, dose not find place in my mind.

verses.sanskrit:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
दीनो वा राज्यहीनो वा यो मे भर्ता स मे गुरुः
verses.transliteration:
na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitumarhati
kāmaṁ khādata māṁ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
dīno vā rājyahīno vā yo me bhartā sa me guruḥ

translations.english: A woman can never be the wife of a Räksasa. Eat ine up if you will, I shall never follow your words.

verses.sanskrit:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
भर्त्सयन्ति स्म परुषैर्वाक्यै रावणचोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
bhartsayanti sma paruṣairvākyai rāvaṇacoditāḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of Sītā, all those Rākşasīs despatched by Rāvana, almost beside themselves with ire, again covered her with reproaches rough and rude.

verses.sanskrit:
अवलीनः स निर्वाक्यो हनुमाञ्शिंशपाद्रुमे
सीतां संतर्जयन्तीस्ता राक्षसीरशृणोत्कपिः
verses.transliteration:
avalīnaḥ sa nirvākyo hanumāñśiṁśapādrume
sītāṁ saṁtarjayantīstā rākṣasīraśṛṇotkapiḥ

translations.english: Hanumān remained all along speechless and hidden on the ſinsapā tree. And that monkey heard all those demons remonstrate with Sītā in this way.

verses.sanskrit:
तामभिक्रम्य संरब्धा वेपमानां समन्ततः
भृशं संलिलिहुर्दीप्तान्प्रलम्बदशनच्छदान्
verses.transliteration:
tāmabhikramya saṁrabdhā vepamānāṁ samantataḥ
bhṛśaṁ saṁlilihurdīptānpralambadaśanacchadān

translations.english: Those, influenced with ire, approached the trembling Sītā and encircling her, licked again and again their long a burning lips.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊचुश्च परमक्रुद्धाः प्रगृह्याशु परश्वधान्
नेयमर्हति भर्तारं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
ūcuśca paramakruddhāḥ pragṛhyāśu paraśvadhān
neyamarhati bhartāraṁ rāvaṇaṁ rākṣasādhipam

translations.english: Taking up instantly spears, they exceedingly wroth, menaced her, saying— "she is not worthy of having Rāvana, the lord of the Rākşasas, as her lord."

verses.sanskrit:
सा भर्त्स्यमाना भीमाभी राक्षसीभिर्वरानना
सा बाष्पमपमार्जन्ती शिंशपां तामुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
sā bhartsyamānā bhīmābhī rākṣasībhirvarānanā
sā bāṣpamapamārjantī śiṁśapāṁ tāmupāgamat

translations.english: Being thus remonstrated with by those terrible Raksasis, that excellent damsel, shedding tears, neared the ſinsapa tree.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तां शिंशपां सीता राक्षसीभिः समावृता
अभिगम्य विशालाक्षी तस्थौ शोकपरिप्लुता
verses.transliteration:
tatastāṁ śiṁśapāṁ sītā rākṣasībhiḥ samāvṛtā
abhigamya viśālākṣī tasthau śokapariplutā

translations.english: The large eyed Sītā, encircled by the Rākşasīs, remained there sunk in grief. And all those hideous demons, showered reproaches, from all sides, on her, greatly reduced, of a poorly countenance, and wearing a soiled cloth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तां विनता नाम राक्षसी भीमदर्शना
अब्रवीत्कुपिताकारा कराला निर्णतोदरी
verses.transliteration:
tatastāṁ vinatā nāma rākṣasī bhīmadarśanā
abravītkupitākārā karālā nirṇatodarī

translations.english: Thereupon a grim-visaged demon, angry, having hideous teeth and a huge belly extending downwards, by name Vinatā, spoke, saying:

verses.sanskrit:
सीते पर्याप्तमेतावद्भर्तृस्नेहो निदर्शितः
सर्वत्रातिकृतं भद्रे व्यसनायोपकल्पते
verses.transliteration:
sīte paryāptametāvadbhartṛsneho nidarśitaḥ
sarvatrātikṛtaṁ bhadre vyasanāyopakalpate

translations.english: O Sītā, you had shown enough of attachment towards your husband. But, O gentle dame, excess of any thing tends to evil.

verses.sanskrit:
परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः
ममापि तु वचः पथ्यं ब्रुवन्त्याः कुरु मैथिलि
verses.transliteration:
parituṣṭāsmi bhadraṁ te mānuṣaste kṛto vidhiḥ
mamāpi tu vacaḥ pathyaṁ bruvantyāḥ kuru maithili

translations.english: We are satisfied. And may good betide you! You had acted worthily like a woman. do you hear, O Maithili, what I say for your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणं त्यागशीलं च सर्वस्य प्रियवादिनम्
मानुषं कृपणं रामं त्यक्त्वा रावणमाश्रय
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇaṁ tyāgaśīlaṁ ca sarvasya priyavādinam
mānuṣaṁ kṛpaṇaṁ rāmaṁ tyaktvā rāvaṇamāśraya

translations.english: Do you accept, Rāvana, the lord of the Rākşasa host, as your husband. He withstands powerfully his enemies like to Vāsava, the lord of the celestials, charitable, kind to all, and sweet-speeched. And forsaking Rāma, a poor wight, do you take Rāvana (as your husband)

verses.sanskrit:
दिव्याङ्गरागा वैदेहि दिव्याभरणभूषिता
अद्य प्रभृति सर्वेषां लोकानामीश्वरी भव
अग्नेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शचीवेन्द्रस्य शोभने
verses.transliteration:
divyāṅgarāgā vaidehi divyābharaṇabhūṣitā
adya prabhṛti sarveṣāṁ lokānāmīśvarī bhava
agneḥ svāhā yathā devī śacīvendrasya śobhane

translations.english: Having your person sprinkled with celestial paste and adorned with excellent ornaments, do you from today O Vaidehī, O you of comely presence, become the queen of all the worlds, like to Sachee of the lord of the celestials and svāhā (An exclamation used in making an oblation to the Gods. A personification of the preceding as the wife of fire and Goddess presiding over burnt offerings.) of the fire. What shall you do with Rama, O Vaidehi, poor and of limited life?

verses.sanskrit:
एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि
अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सर्वास्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
etaduktaṁ ca me vākyaṁ yadi tvaṁ na kariṣyasi
asminmuhūrte sarvāstvāṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmahe vayam

translations.english: This is what I say and if do you not follow it we shall all instantly banquet on you.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्या तु विकटा नाम लम्बमानपयोधरा
अब्रवीत्कुपिता सीतां मुष्टिमुद्यम्य गर्जती
verses.transliteration:
anyā tu vikaṭā nāma lambamānapayodharā
abravītkupitā sītāṁ muṣṭimudyamya garjatī

translations.english: Thereupon another Rākşasi named Vikață. having her breast hanging long, exercised with ire, and clinching her fist, addressed, roaring, Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
बहून्यप्रतिरूपाणि वचनानि सुदुर्मते
अनुक्रोशान्मृदुत्वाच्च सोढानि तव मैथिलि
न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरस्कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
bahūnyapratirūpāṇi vacanāni sudurmate
anukrośānmṛdutvācca soḍhāni tava maithili
na ca naḥ kuruṣe vākyaṁ hitaṁ kālapuraskṛtam

translations.english: O foolish daughter of the king of Mithilā, we have put up with all your foolish words only out of compassion, and because you are a feeble being.

verses.sanskrit:
आनीतासि समुद्रस्य पारमन्यैर्दुरासदम्
रावणान्तःपुरं घोरं प्रविष्टा चासि मैथिलि
verses.transliteration:
ānītāsi samudrasya pāramanyairdurāsadam
rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṁ ghoraṁ praviṣṭā cāsi maithili

translations.english: It will not lead to your well-being if you do not hear our words. You had been brought here, the other side of the ocean, difficult of being approached by others. You had come within the terrible abode of Rāvana O Maithili, and had been shut up in his room guarded by us all.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य गृहे रुधा अस्माभिस्तु सुरक्षिता
न त्वां शक्तः परित्रातुमपि साक्षात्पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya gṛhe rudhā asmābhistu surakṣitā
na tvāṁ śaktaḥ paritrātumapi sākṣātpuraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: And even, Purandara's (Another name of Indra-the lord of the celestials.) self cannot save yoll. Do you therefore hear, O Maithili, my well-mcaning words.

verses.sanskrit:
भज प्रीतिं प्रहर्षं च त्यजैतां नित्यदैन्यताम्
सीते राक्षसराजेन सह क्रीड यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
bhaja prītiṁ praharṣaṁ ca tyajaitāṁ nityadainyatām
sīte rākṣasarājena saha krīḍa yathāsukham

translations.english: Why do you shed tears? Renounce your useless grief. Do you become happy and delighted, renouncing your continued melancholy.

verses.sanskrit:
जानासि हि यथा भीरु स्त्रीणां यौवनमध्रुवम्
यावन्न ते व्यतिक्रामेत्तावत्सुखमवाप्नुहि
verses.transliteration:
jānāsi hi yathā bhīru strīṇāṁ yauvanamadhruvam
yāvanna te vyatikrāmettāvatsukhamavāpnuhi

translations.english: Do you sport, O Sītā, at your pleasure, with the lord of the Rākşasas. We know, for certain, O timid damsel, that the youth of the females, is very transient.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रीसहस्राणि ते सप्त वशे स्थास्यन्ति सुन्दरि
रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
strīsahasrāṇi te sapta vaśe sthāsyanti sundari
rāvaṇaṁ bhaja bhartāraṁ bhartāraṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: And so long as your youth dose not fade, do you pass your days happily, O you having inebriate eyes, with the lord of Rākşasas, in picturesque gardens, and mountain forests. Do you take, O fair damsel, Ravana, the lord of the Rākşasas, for your husband, and thousands of females shall be placed at your service.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि
यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत्करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
utpāṭya vā te hṛdayaṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmi maithili
yadi me vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ na yathāvatkariṣyasi

translations.english: If do you not follow, what I say, O Maithili, I shall taking out your heart, banquet on it.

verses.sanskrit:
निवेद्यतां ततो राज्ञे मानुषी सा मृतेति ह
नात्र कश्चन संदेहः खादतेति स वक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nivedyatāṁ tato rājñe mānuṣī sā mṛteti ha
nātra kaścana saṁdehaḥ khādateti sa vakṣyati

translations.english: Thereupon another Rākşasī named Praghasă and-"I shall grind the throat of this cruel woman. What are you doing, sitting here? You shall then relate to the king that the woman is dead. And undoubtedly he shall say 'Do you eat her up."

verses.sanskrit:
विभजाम ततः सर्वा विवादो मे न रोचते
पेयमानीयतां क्षिप्रं माल्यं च विविधं बहु
verses.transliteration:
vibhajāma tataḥ sarvā vivādo me na rocate
peyamānīyatāṁ kṣipraṁ mālyaṁ ca vividhaṁ bahu

translations.english: And thereupon another Räkşasi named Ajāmukhi said, “I do not like quarrels. Let us all divide her into equal portions. Bring soon our favourite drink and various garlands."

verses.sanskrit:
सुरा चानीयतां क्षिप्रं सर्वशोकविनाशिनी
मानुषं मांसमासाद्य नृत्यामोऽथ निकुम्भिलाम्
verses.transliteration:
surā cānīyatāṁ kṣipraṁ sarvaśokavināśinī
mānuṣaṁ māṁsamāsādya nṛtyāmo'tha nikumbhilām

translations.english: Then followed another Rākşasí by name Śūrpanakha, I do fully concur with what Ajāmukhi has said. Bring soon wine, the remover of all griefs. Banqueting on human flesh I shall dance before the queen Nikumbhilă.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं संभर्त्स्यमाना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्धैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ saṁbhartsyamānā sā sītā surasutopamā
rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhirdhairyamutsṛjya roditi

translations.english: Being thus threatened by those grim-visaged Rākṣasīs Sītā, resembling the daughter of a celestial, renouncing patience, began to weep.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु
राक्षसीनामसौम्यानां रुरोद जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
tathā tāsāṁ vadantīnāṁ paruṣaṁ dāruṇaṁ bahu
rākṣasīnāmasaumyānāṁ ruroda janakātmajā

translations.english: Those hideous Rākşasīs thus threatening her with reproaches rude and rough, the daughter of the king Janaka began to weep.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही राक्षसीभिर्मनस्विनी
उवाच परमत्रस्ता बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu vaidehī rākṣasībhirmanasvinī
uvāca paramatrastā bāṣpagadgadayā girā

translations.english: And being thus addressed by those Rākşasīs, Vaidehi, of subdued soul, being greatly terrified, said, having her voice choked with vapour.

verses.sanskrit:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
verses.transliteration:
na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitumarhati
kāmaṁ khādata māṁ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ

translations.english: A woman cannot be the wife of a Rākşasa. Eat me up if you will, I will never follow your words.

verses.sanskrit:
सा राक्षसी मध्यगता सीता सुरसुतोपमा
न शर्म लेभे दुःखार्ता रावणेन च तर्जिता
verses.transliteration:
sā rākṣasī madhyagatā sītā surasutopamā
na śarma lebhe duḥkhārtā rāvaṇena ca tarjitā

translations.english: And being surrounded by the Rākṣasīs and threatened by Rāvana, Sītă, resembling the daughter of a celestial, stricken with grief, could not console herself.

verses.sanskrit:
वेपते स्माधिकं सीता विशन्तीवाङ्गमात्मनः
वने यूथपरिभ्रष्टा मृगी कोकैरिवार्दिता
verses.transliteration:
vepate smādhikaṁ sītā viśantīvāṅgamātmanaḥ
vane yūthaparibhraṣṭā mṛgī kokairivārditā

translations.english: And trembling, she shrank from their presence like to a strayed fawn surrounded by wolves.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वशोकस्य विपुलां शाखामालम्ब्य पुष्पिताम्
चिन्तयामास शोकेन भर्तारं भग्नमानसा
verses.transliteration:
sā tvaśokasya vipulāṁ śākhāmālambya puṣpitām
cintayāmāsa śokena bhartāraṁ bhagnamānasā

translations.english: And resorting to a flowery branch of an Asoka tree, she sunk in grief, thought upon her lord.

verses.sanskrit:
सा स्नापयन्ती विपुलौ स्तनौ नेत्रजलस्रवैः
चिन्तयन्ती न शोकस्य तदान्तमधिगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
sā snāpayantī vipulau stanau netrajalasravaiḥ
cintayantī na śokasya tadāntamadhigacchati

translations.english: With tears she bathed her beautiful breast and oppressed with woe, she could not reach the other bank of the ocean of grief.

verses.sanskrit:
सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा
राक्षसीनां भयत्रस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sā vepamānā patitā pravāte kadalī yathā
rākṣasīnāṁ bhayatrastā vivarṇavadanābhavat

translations.english: Like a plantain tree shaken by the breeze, she shook and fell down trembling (on the earth). And being afraid of the Rākşasīs, her cheeks forsook their native hue.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्या सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्याः सीतया तदा
ददृशे कम्पिनी वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती
verses.transliteration:
tasyā sā dīrghavipulā vepantyāḥ sītayā tadā
dadṛśe kampinī veṇī vyālīva parisarpatī

translations.english: And herself trembling, her pretty long lock of hair also shook and appeared like a serpent moving this way and that.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्राहमाभिः क्रूराभी राक्षसीभिरिहार्दिता
जीवामि हीना रामेण मुहूर्तमपि दुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
yatrāhamābhiḥ krūrābhī rākṣasībhirihārditā
jīvāmi hīnā rāmeṇa muhūrtamapi duḥkhitā

translations.english: Or else I would not have lived for a moment, separated from Rama and oppressed by the Raksasis as I am.

verses.sanskrit:
एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत्
समुद्रमध्ये नौ पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता
verses.transliteration:
eṣālpapuṇyā kṛpaṇā vinaśiṣyāmyanāthavat
samudramadhye nau pūrṇā vāyuvegairivāhatā

translations.english: Limited is my virtue, and therefore I am to die the death of a poor deserted thing like to a bark driven by the blast in the midst of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तारं तमपश्यन्ती राक्षसीवशमागता
सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा
verses.transliteration:
bhartāraṁ tamapaśyantī rākṣasīvaśamāgatā
sīdāmi khalu śokena kūlaṁ toyahataṁ yathā

translations.english: Debarred from my husband's sight and tortured by the hideous demons, I shall sink, oppressed with woes, like to the banks of a river, washed by the water.

verses.sanskrit:
तं पद्मदलपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्
धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ padmadalapatrākṣaṁ siṁhavikrāntagāminam
dhanyāḥ paśyanti me nāthaṁ kṛtajñaṁ priyavādinam

translations.english: Oh blest are they who have been resting their eyes upon my grateful and sweet-speeched lord of leonine gaits, having eyes resembling lotus petals!

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना
तीष्क्णं विषमिवास्वाद्य दुर्लभं मम जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvathā tena hīnāyā rāmeṇa viditātmanā
tīṣkṇaṁ viṣamivāsvādya durlabhaṁ mama jīvitam

translations.english: And separated from Rāma of subdued soul, it is as difficult for me to breathe as for him who has drank up virulent poison.

verses.sanskrit:
कीदृशं तु मया पापं पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्
येनेदं प्राप्यते दुःखं मया घोरं सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
kīdṛśaṁ tu mayā pāpaṁ purā dehāntare kṛtam
yenedaṁ prāpyate duḥkhaṁ mayā ghoraṁ sudāruṇam

translations.english: What mighty iniquity had I perpetrated in my previous existence that I have met with this terrible disaster!

verses.sanskrit:
जीवितं त्यक्तुमिच्छामि शोकेन महता वृता
राक्षसीभिश्च रक्षन्त्या रामो नासाद्यते मया
verses.transliteration:
jīvitaṁ tyaktumicchāmi śokena mahatā vṛtā
rākṣasībhiśca rakṣantyā rāmo nāsādyate mayā

translations.english: I wish to renounce my life under this load of grief-but alas! I am surrounded by the Raks asis and cannot meet Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं धिगस्तु परवश्यताम्
न शक्यं यत्परित्यक्तुमात्मच्छन्देन जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
dhigastu khalu mānuṣyaṁ dhigastu paravaśyatām
na śakyaṁ yatparityaktumātmacchandena jīvitam

translations.english: Oh! cursed is this subject human life, that they cannot renounce it even at their pleasure!

verses.sanskrit:
उन्मत्तेव प्रमत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्तेव शोचती
उपावृत्ता किशोरीव विवेष्टन्ती महीतले
verses.transliteration:
unmatteva pramatteva bhrāntacitteva śocatī
upāvṛttā kiśorīva viveṣṭantī mahītale

translations.english: Saying this, the daughter of the king Janaka, bathed her countenance with tears and hanging down her head began to lament. And she began to roll on the earth like to a colt as if she was mad, possessed by a devil and had lost her sense.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्याप्रमत्तस्य रक्षसा कामरूपिणा
रावणेन प्रमथ्याहमानीता क्रोशती बलात्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasyāpramattasya rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā
rāvaṇena pramathyāhamānītā krośatī balāt

translations.english: I, the spouse of Rāma, who was drawn away at a distance by the Rākşasa (Mārīca) assuming shapes at will, was seized and borne away by Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसी वशमापन्ना भर्त्यमाना सुदारुणम्
चिन्तयन्ती सुदुःखार्ता नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasī vaśamāpannā bhartyamānā sudāruṇam
cintayantī suduḥkhārtā nāhaṁ jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: A captive of the Rākşasis, subject to their terrible threats and taunts, sunk in grief and anxiety, I desire not to keep my life.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे जीवितेनार्थो नैवार्थैर्न च भूषणैः
वसन्त्या राक्षसी मध्ये विना रामं महारथम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi me jīvitenārtho naivārthairna ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
vasantyā rākṣasī madhye vinā rāmaṁ mahāratham

translations.english: Of what avail are wealth, ornament and life to me, who am living in the midst of the Răkşasas and separated from Ráma, of the mighty car?

verses.sanskrit:
धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं याहं तेन विना कृता
मुहूर्तमपि रक्षामि जीवितं पापजीविता
verses.transliteration:
dhiṅmāmanāryāmasatīṁ yāhaṁ tena vinā kṛtā
muhūrtamapi rakṣāmi jīvitaṁ pāpajīvitā

translations.english: Woe to me! who am unchaste and vile and my life is vicious, since breathe I still in the absence of my lord.

verses.sanskrit:
चरणेनापि सव्येन न स्पृशेयं निशाचरम्
रावणं किं पुनरहं कामयेयं विगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
caraṇenāpi savyena na spṛśeyaṁ niśācaram
rāvaṇaṁ kiṁ punarahaṁ kāmayeyaṁ vigarhitam

translations.english: What of fixing my fancy on that night-ranger Rāvaņa, my meaner foot even shall not touch him?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्याख्यातं न जानाति नात्मानं नात्मनः कुलम्
यो नृशंस स्वभावेन मां प्रार्थयितुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
pratyākhyātaṁ na jānāti nātmānaṁ nātmanaḥ kulam
yo nṛśaṁsa svabhāvena māṁ prārthayitumicchati

translations.english: That (demon) who is courting me in this terrible way, does not know himself, his own race and that I loathe him so much.

verses.sanskrit:
छिन्ना भिन्ना विभक्ता वा दीप्ते वाग्नौ प्रदीपिता
रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वश्चिरम्
verses.transliteration:
chinnā bhinnā vibhaktā vā dīpte vāgnau pradīpitā
rāvaṇaṁ nopatiṣṭheyaṁ kiṁ pralāpena vaściram

translations.english: What more shall I speak to you, I shall never consent to Rāvana's prayer, I might be rent from limb to limb or burnt in fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ख्यातः प्राज्ञः कृतज्ञश्च सानुक्रोशश्च राघवः
सद्वृत्तो निरनुक्रोशः शङ्के मद्भाग्यसंक्षयात्
verses.transliteration:
khyātaḥ prājñaḥ kṛtajñaśca sānukrośaśca rāghavaḥ
sadvṛtto niranukrośaḥ śaṅke madbhāgyasaṁkṣayāt

translations.english: Rāghava is grateful, true, wise and kind. I fear it is through my ill-luck that he dose not feel pity for me.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां जनस्थाने सहस्राणि चतुर्दश
येनैकेन निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ janasthāne sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
yenaikena nirastāni sa māṁ kiṁ nābhipadyate

translations.english: Will he not take me back who alone slew the thousands of the Rākşasas in Janasthāna?

verses.sanskrit:
निरुद्धा रावणेनाहमल्पवीर्येण रक्षसा
समर्थः खलु मे भर्ता रावणं हन्तुमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
niruddhā rāvaṇenāhamalpavīryeṇa rakṣasā
samarthaḥ khalu me bhartā rāvaṇaṁ hantumāhave

translations.english: I have been captured by Rāvana, a Rākşasa of feeble prowess. Forsooth my lord is capable of slaying this Rāvana in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
विराधो दण्डकारण्ये येन राक्षसपुंगवः
रणे रामेण निहतः स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
virādho daṇḍakāraṇye yena rākṣasapuṁgavaḥ
raṇe rāmeṇa nihataḥ sa māṁ kiṁ nābhipadyate

translations.english: Will not that Rāma regain me, by whom was killed in the forest of Dandaka, Virādha, the foremost of the Rākṣasa crew?

verses.sanskrit:
कामं मध्ये समुद्रस्य लङ्केयं दुष्प्रधर्षणा
न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधी ह विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ madhye samudrasya laṅkeyaṁ duṣpradharṣaṇā
na tu rāghavabāṇānāṁ gatirodhī ha vidyate

translations.english: Although situated in the midst of the ocean, Lankā is unapproachable by others, but Raghava's arrows shall also reach here.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु तत्कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः
रक्षसापहृतां भार्यामिष्टां नाभ्यवपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu tatkāraṇaṁ yena rāmo dṛḍhaparākramaḥ
rakṣasāpahṛtāṁ bhāryāmiṣṭāṁ nābhyavapadyate

translations.english: (I am at a loss to ascertain) why Rāma of firm prowess, dose not regain me, his beloved spouse who have been borne away by the Räkşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
जानन्नपि हि तेजस्वी धर्षणां मर्षयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ihasthāṁ māṁ na jānīte śaṅke lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
jānannapi hi tejasvī dharṣaṇāṁ marṣayiṣyati

translations.english: Methinks Rāma dose not know that I am here, or else, powerful as he is, he would not have put up with this insult.

verses.sanskrit:
हृतेति योऽधिगत्वा मां राघवाय निवेदयेत्
गृध्रराजोऽपि स रणे रावणेन निपातितः
verses.transliteration:
hṛteti yo'dhigatvā māṁ rāghavāya nivedayet
gṛdhrarājo'pi sa raṇe rāvaṇena nipātitaḥ

translations.english: That lord of vultures, who could have informed Rāghava, of my being born away by the Rākṣasa, was killed by Rāvana in the battle.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतं कर्म महत्तेन मां तदाभ्यवपद्यता
तिष्ठता रावणद्वन्द्वे वृद्धेनापि जटायुषा
verses.transliteration:
kṛtaṁ karma mahattena māṁ tadābhyavapadyatā
tiṣṭhatā rāvaṇadvandve vṛddhenāpi jaṭāyuṣā

translations.english: O great was the work done by him, who, old as he was, for my sake, addressed himself to bring about Rāvana's destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मामिह जानीयाद्वर्तमानां स राघवः
अद्य बाणैरभिक्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
yadi māmiha jānīyādvartamānāṁ sa rāghavaḥ
adya bāṇairabhikruddhaḥ kuryāllokamarākṣasaṁ

translations.english: If Rāghava could know that I was here, he, exceedingly wroth, would have cleared the earth with his arrows, of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
विधमेच्च पुरीं लङ्कां शोषयेच्च महोदधिम्
रावणस्य च नीचस्य कीर्तिं नाम च नाशयेत्
verses.transliteration:
vidhamecca purīṁ laṅkāṁ śoṣayecca mahodadhim
rāvaṇasya ca nīcasya kīrtiṁ nāma ca nāśayet

translations.english: He would have then burnt down the city of Lankā, dried up the deep and blotted out the name and fame of Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निहतनथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे
यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः
अन्विष्य रक्षसां लङ्कां कुर्याद्रामः सलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
tato nihatanathānāṁ rākṣasīnāṁ gṛhe gṛhe
yathāhamevaṁ rudatī tathā bhūyo na saṁśayaḥ
anviṣya rakṣasāṁ laṅkāṁ kuryādrāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: And from each ruined home would have risen the Rākşasa widow's groans and cries like to those of mine.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूतमपि जीवति
चिता धूमाकुलपथा गृध्रमण्डलसंकुला
अचिरेण तु लङ्केयं श्मशानसदृशी भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
na hi tābhyāṁ ripurdṛṣṭo muhūtamapi jīvati
citā dhūmākulapathā gṛdhramaṇḍalasaṁkulā
acireṇa tu laṅkeyaṁ śmaśānasadṛśī bhavet

translations.english: And in no time, shall Lankā, assume the appearance of a cremation ground, having all her high ways enveloped with smoke issuing out of the funeral pyres, and filled with vultures.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिरेणैव कालेन प्राप्स्याम्येव मनोरथम्
दुष्प्रस्थानोऽयमाख्याति सर्वेषां वो विपर्ययः
verses.transliteration:
acireṇaiva kālena prāpsyāmyeva manoratham
duṣprasthāno'yamākhyāti sarveṣāṁ vo viparyayaḥ

translations.english: And soon shall this desire of mine be fulfilled. All these words of mine do sound improbable now but they all indicate your misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशानि तु दृश्यन्ते लङ्कायामशुभानि तु
अचिरेणैव कालेन भविष्यति हतप्रभा
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśāni tu dṛśyante laṅkāyāmaśubhāni tu
acireṇaiva kālena bhaviṣyati hataprabhā

translations.english: Besides from these bad omens, that are to be seen here, it appear, that Lankä shall soon be shorn of her grace.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधिपे
शोषं यास्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ laṅkā hate pāpe rāvaṇe rākṣasādhipe
śoṣaṁ yāsyati durdharṣā pramadā vidhavā yathā

translations.english: The lord of the Rākşasas, the vicious Rāvana being killed, forsooth shall Lankā, divested of wealth, appear like a widow.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्योत्सवसमृद्धा च नष्टभर्त्री सराक्षसा
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का नष्टभर्त्री यथाङ्गना
verses.transliteration:
puṣyotsavasamṛddhā ca naṣṭabhartrī sarākṣasā
bhaviṣyati purī laṅkā naṣṭabhartrī yathāṅganā

translations.english: This Lankā, which is now full of pious ceremonies, shall, on the death of the Rākṣasas and their master, appear like a husbandless woman.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं राक्षसकन्यानां रुदन्तीनां गृहे गृहे
श्रोष्यामि नचिरादेव दुःखार्तानामिह ध्वनिम्
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ rākṣasakanyānāṁ rudantīnāṁ gṛhe gṛhe
śroṣyāmi nacirādeva duḥkhārtānāmiha dhvanim

translations.english: For certain, shall I soon hear the cries and groans in every house, of the daughters of the Rākşasas worn with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्धकारा हतद्योता हतराक्षसपुंगवा
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का निर्दग्धा रामसायकैः
verses.transliteration:
sāndhakārā hatadyotā hatarākṣasapuṁgavā
bhaviṣyati purī laṅkā nirdagdhā rāmasāyakaiḥ

translations.english: If that heroic Rāma, having dark-blue eyes, comes to know that I am in the abode of the Rākşasas, the city of Lankā shall be burnt down with his arrows and shall be stricken with darkness and shorn of grace and all the foremost of the Rākşasas shall be destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन तु नृशंसेन रावणेनाधमेन मे
समयो यस्तु निर्दिष्टस्तस्य कालोऽयमागतः
verses.transliteration:
anena tu nṛśaṁsena rāvaṇenādhamena me
samayo yastu nirdiṣṭastasya kālo'yamāgataḥ

translations.english: The time which was appointed by the vile and cruel Rāvana, has arrived.

verses.sanskrit:
अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैरृताः पापकारिणः
अधर्मात्तु महोत्पातो भविष्यति हि साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
akāryaṁ ye na jānanti nairṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ
adharmāttu mahotpāto bhaviṣyati hi sāmpratam

translations.english: And that vicious wretch has resolved to destroy me now. There is no crime which cannot be perpetrated by those vicious demons.

verses.sanskrit:
नैते धर्मं विजानन्ति राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः
ध्रुवं मां प्रातराशार्थे राक्षसः कल्पयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
naite dharmaṁ vijānanti rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
dhruvaṁ māṁ prātarāśārthe rākṣasaḥ kalpayiṣyati

translations.english: Mighty is the disaster that shall arise on account of this crime—the Räkşasas who live on flesh do not know what virtue is.

verses.sanskrit:
साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं विना प्रियदर्शनम्
रामं रक्तान्तनयनमपश्यन्ती सुदुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
sāhaṁ kathaṁ kariṣyāmi taṁ vinā priyadarśanam
rāmaṁ raktāntanayanamapaśyantī suduḥkhitā

translations.english: Forsooth shall the Raksasa serve me for his morning meal. What shall I do without my lord of comely presence?

verses.sanskrit:
यदि कश्चित्प्रदाता मे विषस्याद्य भवेदिह
क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येयं पतिना विना
verses.transliteration:
yadi kaścitpradātā me viṣasyādya bhavediha
kṣipraṁ vaivasvataṁ devaṁ paśyeyaṁ patinā vinā

translations.english: Debarred from my husband's presence, stricken with grief and not beholding Rāma, having dark-blue eyes, I shall soon meet with death.

verses.sanskrit:
नाजानाज्जीवतीं रामः स मां लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
जानन्तौ तौ न कुर्यातां नोर्व्यां हि मम मार्गणम्
verses.transliteration:
nājānājjīvatīṁ rāmaḥ sa māṁ lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
jānantau tau na kuryātāṁ norvyāṁ hi mama mārgaṇam

translations.english: Rāma, the elder brother of Bharata, dose not know that I am still alive or else he and Lakşmaņa would have ransacked the whole world for me.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
देवलोकमितो यातस्त्यक्त्वा देहं महीतले
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ mamaiva śokena sa vīro lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
devalokamito yātastyaktvā dehaṁ mahītale

translations.english: Or renouncing his body on this earth for my grief, the heroic elder brother of Lakşmaņa, has repaired to the celestial region.

verses.sanskrit:
धन्या देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
मम पश्यन्ति ये नाथं रामं राजीवलोचनम्
verses.transliteration:
dhanyā devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
mama paśyanti ye nāthaṁ rāmaṁ rājīvalocanam

translations.english: Blessed the celestials, Gandharvas, Siddhās and mighty ascetics who are beholding my heroic lotus-eyed Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा न हि तस्यार्थे धर्मकामस्य धीमतः
मया रामस्य राजर्षेर्भार्यया परमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā na hi tasyārthe dharmakāmasya dhīmataḥ
mayā rāmasya rājarṣerbhāryayā paramātmanaḥ

translations.english: Or that highly intelligent royal ascetic desirous of securing piety and freed from the troubles of life, has no need of a wife like me.

verses.sanskrit:
दृश्यमाने भवेत्प्रीतः सौहृदं नास्त्यपश्यतः
नाशयन्ति कृतघ्रास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
dṛśyamāne bhavetprītaḥ sauhṛdaṁ nāstyapaśyataḥ
nāśayanti kṛtaghrāstu na rāmo nāśayiṣyati

translations.english: Or people have fancy for what they see and are which disappear as soon as the object is out of sight. The ungrateful are capable of renouncing their love, but not Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु मे न गुणाः केचित्किं वा भाग्य क्षयो हि मे
याहं सीता वरार्हेण हीना रामेण भामिनी
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu me na guṇāḥ kecitkiṁ vā bhāgya kṣayo hi me
yāhaṁ sītā varārheṇa hīnā rāmeṇa bhāminī

translations.english: Or there might be some folly in me. Or on the wane of my good luck have been separated from the excellent Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयो मे जीवितान्मर्तुं विहीना या महात्मना
रामादक्लिष्टचारित्राच्छूराच्छत्रुनिबर्हणात्
verses.transliteration:
śreyo me jīvitānmartuṁ vihīnā yā mahātmanā
rāmādakliṣṭacāritrācchūrācchatrunibarhaṇāt

translations.english: Death is more preferable to me than life since. I have been separated from the high-souled heroic Rāma, of unblemished character and the slayer of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा न्यस्तशस्त्रौ तौ वने मूलफलाशनौ
भ्रातरौ हि नर श्रेष्ठौ चरन्तौ वनगोचरौ
verses.transliteration:
atha vā nyastaśastrau tau vane mūlaphalāśanau
bhrātarau hi nara śreṣṭhau carantau vanagocarau

translations.english: Or those two brothers, the foremost of men, laying aside their weapons, and living on fruits and roots, have been wandering in the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना
छद्मना घातितौ शूरौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
atha vā rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena durātmanā
chadmanā ghātitau śūrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Or those two heroic brothers Rāma and Laksmana, have been, by treachery, put to death, by the vicious-souled Rāvana, the lord of Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
साहमेवंगते काले मर्तुमिच्छामि सर्वथा
न च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन्दुःखेऽपि वर्तति
verses.transliteration:
sāhamevaṁgate kāle martumicchāmi sarvathā
na ca me vihito mṛtyurasminduḥkhe'pi vartati

translations.english: At this time of distress, I do with all my heart long for death, (but alas!) even death is not approaching me is this my misery.

verses.sanskrit:
धन्याः खलु महात्मानो मुनयः सत्यसंमताः
जितात्मानो महाभागा येषां न स्तः प्रियाप्रिये
verses.transliteration:
dhanyāḥ khalu mahātmāno munayaḥ satyasaṁmatāḥ
jitātmāno mahābhāgā yeṣāṁ na staḥ priyāpriye

translations.english: Oh blessed are those high-souled, great ascetics abiding by truth and having their senses in control, who have no objects of love or displeasure.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियान्न संभवेद्दुःखमप्रियादधिकं भयम्
ताभ्यां हि ये वियुज्यन्ते नमस्तेषां महात्मनाम्
verses.transliteration:
priyānna saṁbhavedduḥkhamapriyādadhikaṁ bhayam
tābhyāṁ hi ye viyujyante namasteṣāṁ mahātmanām

translations.english: They are not distressed with misery for their objects of love or grief for them whom they do not love. They are freed from them and I do bow to those high-souled ones.

verses.sanskrit:
साहं त्यक्ता प्रियेणेह रामेण विदितात्मना
प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि पापस्य रावणस्य गता वशम्
verses.transliteration:
sāhaṁ tyaktā priyeṇeha rāmeṇa viditātmanā
prāṇāṁstyakṣyāmi pāpasya rāvaṇasya gatā vaśam

translations.english: Being forsaken by the beloved Rāma, knowing his ownself, and brought under the control of Ravana, I shall renounce my life.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्ताः सीतया घोरं राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
काश्चिज्जग्मुस्तदाख्यातुं रावणस्य तरस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktāḥ sītayā ghoraṁ rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
kāścijjagmustadākhyātuṁ rāvaṇasya tarasvinaḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed angrily by Sītā, some of those Raksasis, beside themselves with ire, proceeded to relate this to the vicious-souled Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो घोरदर्शनाः
पुनः परुषमेकार्थमनर्थार्थमथाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sītāmupāgamya rākṣasyo ghoradarśanāḥ
punaḥ paruṣamekārthamanarthārthamathābruvan

translations.english: And approaching Sītā those grim-visaged demons again addressed her with words rude and rough.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्तेदानीं तवानार्ये सीते पापविनिश्चये
राक्षस्यो भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसमेतद्यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
hantedānīṁ tavānārye sīte pāpaviniścaye
rākṣasyo bhakṣayiṣyanti māṁsametadyathāsukham

translations.english: O vile Sītă, O you bent on committing sin, we Rākşasīs shall today devour your flesh to the best of our satisfaction.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतां ताभिरनार्याभिर्दृष्ट्वा संतर्जितां तदा
राक्षसी त्रिजटावृद्धा शयाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sītāṁ tābhiranāryābhirdṛṣṭvā saṁtarjitāṁ tadā
rākṣasī trijaṭāvṛddhā śayānā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Beholding those vile demons threaten Sītā, a Raksasa matron, wise and old, named, Trijata cried.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं खादतानार्या न सीतां भक्षयिष्यथ
जनकस्य सुतामिष्टां स्नुषां दशरथस्य च
verses.transliteration:
ātmānaṁ khādatānāryā na sītāṁ bhakṣayiṣyatha
janakasya sutāmiṣṭāṁ snuṣāṁ daśarathasya ca

translations.english: O vile demons, do youeat your own persons (The proper expression, I think, should be-“Eat me.” The commentator Rāmānuja explains Atmanam as your own bodies.) but do not devour Sītā, the daughter of Janaka and the esteemed daughter-in-law of the king Dasaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुणो रोमहर्षणः
राक्षसानामभावाय भर्तुरस्या भवाय च
verses.transliteration:
svapno hyadya mayā dṛṣṭo dāruṇo romaharṣaṇaḥ
rākṣasānāmabhāvāya bharturasyā bhavāya ca

translations.english: I dreamt a terrible dream last night which made my down stand on their end. And in that dream I foresaw the overthrow of the Rāksasa race and the conquest of her husband.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तास्त्रिजटया राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
सर्वा एवाब्रुवन्भीतास्त्रिजटां तामिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāstrijaṭayā rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
sarvā evābruvanbhītāstrijaṭāṁ tāmidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And being thus addressed by Trijatā, those demons, exercised with wrath and terrified, accosted her with the following words.

verses.sanskrit:
तासां श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राक्षसीनां मुखोद्गतम्
उवाच वचनं काले त्रिजटास्वप्नसंश्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ śrutvā tu vacanaṁ rākṣasīnāṁ mukhodgatam
uvāca vacanaṁ kāle trijaṭāsvapnasaṁśritam

translations.english: "Do you relate (to us) what sort of dream didst you dream last night." And hearing those words proceeding from the mouths of the Rākşasīs, Trijatā began to describe the dream she had at the latter end of the night,

verses.sanskrit:
गजदन्तमयीं दिव्यां शिबिकामन्तरिक्षगाम्
युक्तां वाजिसहस्रेण स्वयमास्थाय राघवः
verses.transliteration:
gajadantamayīṁ divyāṁ śibikāmantarikṣagām
yuktāṁ vājisahasreṇa svayamāsthāya rāghavaḥ

translations.english: I saw Rāma, wearing garlands and clothed in white, ride in a celestial chariot, along with Lakşmaņa, made of ivory, traversing the etherial regions and drawn by a hundred steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्ने चाद्य मया दृष्टा सीता शुक्लाम्बरावृता
सागरेण परिक्षिप्तं श्वेतपर्वतमास्थिता
रामेण संगता सीता भास्करेण प्रभा यथा
verses.transliteration:
svapne cādya mayā dṛṣṭā sītā śuklāmbarāvṛtā
sāgareṇa parikṣiptaṁ śvetaparvatamāsthitā
rāmeṇa saṁgatā sītā bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā

translations.english: I saw in my dream to-night, that Sītā, clad in the purest white, appearing on a snow-white hill beaten by the waves of the ocean, had at last met Rāma, like to light joined to the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवश्च मया दृष्टश्चतुर्दन्तं महागजम्
आरूढः शैलसंकाशं चचार सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaśca mayā dṛṣṭaścaturdantaṁ mahāgajam
ārūḍhaḥ śailasaṁkāśaṁ cacāra sahalakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: I again saw Rāma and Lakşmaņa appear in effulgence, seated on a huge elephant, having four tusks and resembling a bull.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा
शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरौ जानकीं पर्युपस्थितौ
verses.transliteration:
tatastau naraśārdūlau dīpyamānau svatejasā
śuklamālyāmbaradharau jānakīṁ paryupasthitau

translations.english: Thereupon those two (brothers), resplendent like to the Sun by their own effulgence, and wearing white garlands and clothes, appeared near Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तुरङ्कात्समुत्पत्य ततः कमललोचना
चन्द्रसूर्यौ मया दृष्टा पाणिभ्यां परिमार्जती
verses.transliteration:
bharturaṅkātsamutpatya tataḥ kamalalocanā
candrasūryau mayā dṛṣṭā pāṇibhyāṁ parimārjatī

translations.english: And the lotus-eyed Jānakī, on the top of the hill situate on the welkin, first fell on the lap of her husband and then stationed herself on the neck of the elephant guided by her husband. Then I saw Sītā rubbing the Sun and the Moon with her two hands.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यामास्थितः स गजोत्तमः
सीतया च विशालाक्ष्या लङ्काया उपरि स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tatastābhyāṁ kumārābhyāmāsthitaḥ sa gajottamaḥ
sītayā ca viśālākṣyā laṅkāyā upari sthitaḥ

translations.english: Then that best of the elephants, with those two princes and the large eyed Sītā on him, stood high above Lanka. I again saw Rāma, clad in white, and adorned with garlands, ride along with Lakşmaņa in a chariot drawn by eight white bullocks.

verses.sanskrit:
विमानात्पुष्पकादद्य रावणः पतितो भुवि
कृष्यपाणः स्त्रिया दृष्टो मुण्डः कृष्णाम्बरः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
vimānātpuṣpakādadya rāvaṇaḥ patito bhuvi
kṛṣyapāṇaḥ striyā dṛṣṭo muṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇāmbaraḥ punaḥ

translations.english: I saw Ravana too, shaved and shorn, besmeared with oil, wearing a crimson cloth, drinking honey, wearing a garland of Karavīra flowers, fall down on earth from the flowery chariot.

verses.sanskrit:
रथेन खरयुक्तेन रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः
प्रयातो दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टः कर्दमं ह्रदम्
verses.transliteration:
rathena kharayuktena raktamālyānulepanaḥ
prayāto dakṣiṇāmāśāṁ praviṣṭaḥ kardamaṁ hradam

translations.english: And dragged by a woman, shaved, wearing a red cloth and garlands and sprinkled with crimson paste, Rāvana was again seen by me riding in a chariot drawn by asses. And quaffing oil, laughing and dancing, that one of agitated senses, forgetting himself sped on the chariot to the South. (In the south is the region of Yama, the God of Death and hence his going to the south is not an auspicious sign.)

verses.sanskrit:
समाजश्च महान्वृत्तो गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः
पिबतां रक्तमाल्यानां रक्षसां रक्तवाससाम्
verses.transliteration:
samājaśca mahānvṛtto gītavāditraniḥsvanaḥ
pibatāṁ raktamālyānāṁ rakṣasāṁ raktavāsasām

translations.english: And there was audible in the large assembly sound of music and stringed instruments. And all the Rākşasa wearing crimson clothes and garlands, were quaffing oil, I saw the royal and picturesque city Lankā with her steeds, cars and elephants, drowned in the ocean, having her gateways and ornamented arches broken.

verses.sanskrit:
पीत्व तैलं प्रनृत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः
लङ्कायां भस्मरूक्षायां सर्वा राक्षसयोषितः
verses.transliteration:
pītva tailaṁ pranṛttāśca prahasantyo mahāsvanāḥ
laṅkāyāṁ bhasmarūkṣāyāṁ sarvā rākṣasayoṣitaḥ

translations.english: And in Lanka, covered with dust, Raksasa women laughing and making terrible sound, were engaged in quaffing oil.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे सर्वे राक्षसपुंगवाः
रक्तं निवसनं गृह्य प्रविष्टा गोमयह्रदे
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇādayaśceme sarve rākṣasapuṁgavāḥ
raktaṁ nivasanaṁ gṛhya praviṣṭā gomayahrade

translations.english: I saw all the leading Raksasas-Kumbhakarņā and others, dark-hued and wearing crimson clothes, emerged in an abyss of cow dung.

verses.sanskrit:
अपगच्छत नश्यध्वं सीतामाप्नोति राघवः
घातयेत्परमामर्षी सर्वैः सार्धं हि राक्षसैः
verses.transliteration:
apagacchata naśyadhvaṁ sītāmāpnoti rāghavaḥ
ghātayetparamāmarṣī sarvaiḥ sārdhaṁ hi rākṣasaiḥ

translations.english: Do youtherefore fly at some distance, and will find that Rāghava shall regain Sītā. And exercised with ire he shall destroy you all along with the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां वनवासमनुव्रताम्
भर्त्सितां तर्जितां वापि नानुमंस्यति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
priyāṁ bahumatāṁ bhāryāṁ vanavāsamanuvratām
bhartsitāṁ tarjitāṁ vāpi nānumaṁsyati rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Rāghava shall never brook, his esteemed and beloved spouse, living in the forest, being taunted and threatened by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तदलं क्रूरवाक्यैर्वः सान्त्वमेवाभिधीयताम्
अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्धि मम रोचते
verses.transliteration:
tadalaṁ krūravākyairvaḥ sāntvamevābhidhīyatām
abhiyācāma vaidehīmetaddhi mama rocate

translations.english: No more with rough words therefore; do you console the lady and humbly pray her to forgive you. This I think proper.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्या ह्येवं विधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायाः प्रदृश्यते
सा दुःखैर्बहुभिर्मुक्ता प्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
yasyā hyevaṁ vidhaḥ svapno duḥkhitāyāḥ pradṛśyate
sā duḥkhairbahubhirmuktā priyaṁ prāpnotyanuttamam

translations.english: Surely shall she, divested of misfortune, he reconciled to her beloved and excellent husband, regarding whom, in her misery, I have dreamt such a dream.

verses.sanskrit:
भर्त्सितामपि याचध्वं राक्षस्यः किं विवक्षया
राघवाद्धि भयं घोरं राक्षसानामुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
bhartsitāmapi yācadhvaṁ rākṣasyaḥ kiṁ vivakṣayā
rāghavāddhi bhayaṁ ghoraṁ rākṣasānāmupasthitam

translations.english: YouRaksasis! You have threatened her, do youimplore her forgiveness—no more with harsh words. Forsooth, from Rāghava shall proceed the mighty disaster of the Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रणिपात प्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा
अलमेषा परित्रातुं राक्षस्यो महतो भयात्
verses.transliteration:
praṇipāta prasannā hi maithilī janakātmajā
alameṣā paritrātuṁ rākṣasyo mahato bhayāt

translations.english: If Maithili, the daughter of the king Janaka, be pleased with you (for your imploring her forgiveness) you might be saved from the mighty disaster.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि चास्या विशालाक्ष्या न किंचिदुपलक्षये
विरुद्धमपि चाङ्गेषु सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
api cāsyā viśālākṣyā na kiṁcidupalakṣaye
viruddhamapi cāṅgeṣu susūkṣmamapi lakṣmaṇam

translations.english: I do not perceive any inauspicious mark on the person of this large-eyed dame. It appears from the paleness of her countenance that she has been overcome by misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
छाया वैगुण्य मात्रं तु शङ्के दुःखमुपस्थितम्
अदुःखार्हामिमां देवीं वैहायसमुपस्थिताम्
verses.transliteration:
chāyā vaiguṇya mātraṁ tu śaṅke duḥkhamupasthitam
aduḥkhārhāmimāṁ devīṁ vaihāyasamupasthitām

translations.english: And I saw in my dreams) this worshipful damsel, unworthy of any misfortune, stationed in the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थसिद्धिं तु वैदेह्याः पश्याम्यहमुपस्थिताम्
राक्षसेन्द्रविनाशं च विजयं राघवस्य च
verses.transliteration:
arthasiddhiṁ tu vaidehyāḥ paśyāmyahamupasthitām
rākṣasendravināśaṁ ca vijayaṁ rāghavasya ca

translations.english: Verily I do perceive, before me, the satisfaction of Vaidehi's end, the destruction of the lord of the Rākşasas and the conquest of Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
ईषच्च हृषितो वास्या दक्षिणाया ह्यदक्षिणः
अकस्मादेव वैदेह्या बाहुरेकः प्रकम्पते
verses.transliteration:
īṣacca hṛṣito vāsyā dakṣiṇāyā hyadakṣiṇaḥ
akasmādeva vaidehyā bāhurekaḥ prakampate

translations.english: Behold! there, her left eye, spacious, as a lotus-petals, is dancing to hear this pleasant dream announcing the satisfaction of her own end. And her left arm is also dancing with joy, all on a sudden.

verses.sanskrit:
करेणुहस्तप्रतिमः सव्यश्चोरुरनुत्तमः
वेपन्सूचयतीवास्या राघवं पुरतः स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
kareṇuhastapratimaḥ savyaścoruranuttamaḥ
vepansūcayatīvāsyā rāghavaṁ purataḥ sthitam

translations.english: And her excellent beautiful left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, is also dancing as if indicating, that she shall at no distant date, be reconciled to Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
पक्षी च शाखा निलयं प्रविष्टः; पुनः पुनश्चोत्तमसान्त्ववादी
सुखागतां वाचमुदीरयाणः; पुनः पुनश्चोदयतीव हृष्टः
verses.transliteration:
pakṣī ca śākhā nilayaṁ praviṣṭaḥ; punaḥ punaścottamasāntvavādī
sukhāgatāṁ vācamudīrayāṇaḥ; punaḥ punaścodayatīva hṛṣṭaḥ

translations.english: And the birds, again and again, entering their nests, and highly delighted are pouring forth their notes announcing the advent of a happy occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
सा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचो निशम्य; तद्रावणस्याप्रियमप्रियार्ता
सीता वितत्रास यथा वनान्ते; सिंहाभिपन्ना गजराजकन्या
verses.transliteration:
sā rākṣasendrasya vaco niśamya; tadrāvaṇasyāpriyamapriyārtā
sītā vitatrāsa yathā vanānte; siṁhābhipannā gajarājakanyā

translations.english: Hearing those unpleasant words of Rāvana, the lord of Rāksasas, Sītā, racked with sorrow on account of her husband, became terrified, like to a she-elephant, worsted by a lion on the skirt of a forest.

verses.sanskrit:
सा राक्षसी मध्यगता च भीरु;र्वाग्भिर्भृशं रावणतर्जिता च
कान्तारमध्ये विजने विसृष्टा; बालेव कन्या विललाप सीता
verses.transliteration:
sā rākṣasī madhyagatā ca bhīru;rvāgbhirbhṛśaṁ rāvaṇatarjitā ca
kāntāramadhye vijane visṛṣṭā; bāleva kanyā vilalāpa sītā

translations.english: Threatened by Rāvana and encircled by the Rākşasīs, that timid damsel bewailed like a girl cast off in a lonely forest.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यं बतेदं प्रवदन्ति लोके; नाकालमृत्युर्भवतीति सन्तः
यत्राहमेवं परिभर्त्स्यमाना; जीवामि किंचित्क्षणमप्यपुण्या
verses.transliteration:
satyaṁ batedaṁ pravadanti loke; nākālamṛtyurbhavatīti santaḥ
yatrāhamevaṁ paribhartsyamānā; jīvāmi kiṁcitkṣaṇamapyapuṇyā

translations.english: Truly the sages say that death in this world dose not come untimely. Or else would I have, vicious as I am, lived for a moment, being thus sorely threatened.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखाद्विहीनं बहुदुःखपूर्ण;मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे
विदीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाद्य; वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य
verses.transliteration:
sukhādvihīnaṁ bahuduḥkhapūrṇa;midaṁ tu nūnaṁ hṛdayaṁ sthiraṁ me
vidīryate yanna sahasradhādya; vajrāhataṁ śṛṅgamivācalasya

translations.english: Forsooth, my mind, divested of happiness and full of misery, is firin or else why is it not broken in sunder like to the summit of a hill clapped by a thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवास्ति नूनं मम दोषमत्र; वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य
भावं न चास्याहमनुप्रदातु;मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय
verses.transliteration:
naivāsti nūnaṁ mama doṣamatra; vadhyāhamasyāpriyadarśanasya
bhāvaṁ na cāsyāhamanupradātu;malaṁ dvijo mantramivādvijāya

translations.english: Nor am I to blame for this. I am worthy of being killed by this demon of uncomely presence. As a Brāhmaṇa cannot impart instructions in Vedas to the people of other castes so I shall not confer my mind on Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं ममाङ्गान्यचिरादनार्यः; शस्त्रैः शितैश्छेत्स्यति राक्षसेन्द्रः
तस्मिन्ननागच्छति लोकनाथे; गर्भस्थजन्तोरिव शल्यकृन्तः
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ mamāṅgānyacirādanāryaḥ; śastraiḥ śitaiśchetsyati rākṣasendraḥ
tasminnanāgacchati lokanāthe; garbhasthajantoriva śalyakṛntaḥ

translations.english: If that lord of the people dose not come within the appointed time, forsooth shall that vile lord, of the Rākşasas, mince my limbs with his arrows like to a surgeon cutting off the limbs of an embryo. (This passage clearly indicates that there were proficient and skilled surgeons at the time when Rāmāyaṇa was written.)

verses.sanskrit:
