दुःखं बतेदं मम दुःखिताया; मासौ चिरायाभिगमिष्यतो द्वौ
बद्धस्य वध्यस्य यथा निशान्ते; राजापराधादिव तस्करस्य
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhaṁ batedaṁ mama duḥkhitāyā; māsau cirāyābhigamiṣyato dvau
baddhasya vadhyasya yathā niśānte; rājāparādhādiva taskarasya

translations.english: Two months shall pass away in no time and I shall have to suffer the pain of death, overwhelmed with sorrow as I am, like to a thief, confined in stocks, at the command of the sovereign to receive death the next morning.

verses.sanskrit:
हा राम हा लक्ष्मण हा सुमित्रे; हा राम मातः सह मे जनन्या
एषा विपद्याम्यहमल्पभाग्या; महार्णवे नौरिव मूढ वाता
verses.transliteration:
hā rāma hā lakṣmaṇa hā sumitre; hā rāma mātaḥ saha me jananyā
eṣā vipadyāmyahamalpabhāgyā; mahārṇave nauriva mūḍha vātā

translations.english: O Rama! O Laksmana! O Sumitra! O Rama's mother! O my mothers! I am worsted in this ocean of grief, like to a bark, driven hither and thither by the blast, in the midst of an ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य; सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रौ
नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात्तौ; सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन
verses.transliteration:
tarasvinau dhārayatā mṛgasya; sattvena rūpaṁ manujendraputrau
nūnaṁ viśastau mama kāraṇāttau; siṁharṣabhau dvāviva vaidyutena

translations.english: Verily for me, those two powerful, lion-like sons of the king, have been killed by (this demon) effulgent like the lightning and assuming the semblance of a deer.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं स कालो मृगरूपधारी; मामल्पभाग्यां लुलुभे तदानीम्
यत्रार्यपुत्रं विससर्ज मूढा; रामानुजं लक्ष्मणपूर्वकं च
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ sa kālo mṛgarūpadhārī; māmalpabhāgyāṁ lulubhe tadānīm
yatrāryaputraṁ visasarja mūḍhā; rāmānujaṁ lakṣmaṇapūrvakaṁ ca

translations.english: Unfortunate as I am, forsooth I was tempted then by death wearing the shape of a deer and thus foolishly lost Rāma and Lakşmana, the sons of the worshipful sire.

verses.sanskrit:
हा राम सत्यव्रत दीर्घवाहो; हा पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमानवक्त्र
हा जीवलोकस्य हितः प्रियश्च; वध्यां न मां वेत्सि हि राक्षसानाम्
verses.transliteration:
hā rāma satyavrata dīrghavāho; hā pūrṇacandrapratimānavaktra
hā jīvalokasya hitaḥ priyaśca; vadhyāṁ na māṁ vetsi hi rākṣasānām

translations.english: O Rāma, O you of truthful vows, O you of long arms, O you having the countenance of a full moon! O my life! engaged as you are in the welfare of the people, do you not perceive that I am about to be killed by the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अनन्यदेवत्वमियं क्षमा च; भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे
पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदं; कृतं कृतघ्नेष्विव मानुषाणाम्
verses.transliteration:
ananyadevatvamiyaṁ kṣamā ca; bhūmau ca śayyā niyamaśca dharme
pativratātvaṁ viphalaṁ mamedaṁ; kṛtaṁ kṛtaghneṣviva mānuṣāṇām

translations.english: Alas! this my devotedness to my husband, my forgiveness, my lying down on the bare earth, my observance of religious vows, my wife-like virtues, are lost like to service done for an ungrateful wight.

verses.sanskrit:
मोघो हि धर्मश्चरितो ममायं; तथैकपत्नीत्वमिदं निरर्थम्
या त्वां न पश्यामि कृशा विवर्णा; हीना त्वया संगमने निराशा
verses.transliteration:
mogho hi dharmaścarito mamāyaṁ; tathaikapatnītvamidaṁ nirartham
yā tvāṁ na paśyāmi kṛśā vivarṇā; hīnā tvayā saṁgamane nirāśā

translations.english: In vain are my pious rites, and in vain is my devotedness to my husband since I do not behold you, am pale and feeble in your absence and have given up all hopes of seeing you.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्निर्देशं नियमेन कृत्वा; वनान्निवृत्तश्चरितव्रतश्च
स्त्रीभिस्तु मन्ये विपुलेक्षणाभिः; संरंस्यसे वीतभयः कृतार्थः
verses.transliteration:
piturnirdeśaṁ niyamena kṛtvā; vanānnivṛttaścaritavrataśca
strībhistu manye vipulekṣaṇābhiḥ; saṁraṁsyase vītabhayaḥ kṛtārthaḥ

translations.english: And duly satisfying your sire's command, and returning successfully from the forest, you shall fearlessly sport with many a damsel having large eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु राम त्वयि जातकामा; चिरं विनाशाय निबद्धभावा
मोघं चरित्वाथ तपोव्रतं च; त्यक्ष्यामि धिग्जीवितमल्पभाग्या
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu rāma tvayi jātakāmā; ciraṁ vināśāya nibaddhabhāvā
moghaṁ caritvātha tapovrataṁ ca; tyakṣyāmi dhigjīvitamalpabhāgyā

translations.english: (But for me) O Rama, I was for my own destruction, devoted, soul and heart, to you. Oh! fruitless is my asceticism and wifely virtue! Oh fie on me! I shall renounce this my unfortunate life.

verses.sanskrit:
सा जीवितं क्षिप्रमहं त्यजेयं; विषेण शस्त्रेण शितेन वापि
विषस्य दाता न तु मेऽस्ति कश्चि;च्छस्त्रस्य वा वेश्मनि राक्षसस्य
verses.transliteration:
sā jīvitaṁ kṣipramahaṁ tyajeyaṁ; viṣeṇa śastreṇa śitena vāpi
viṣasya dātā na tu me'sti kaści;cchastrasya vā veśmani rākṣasasya

translations.english: I desire to do away speedily with my being by means of poison or a sharp weapon. But there is no one in this city of the Rākşasas, who bring me this poison or weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव सीता बहुधा विलप्य; सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती
प्रवेपमाना परिशुष्कवक्त्रा; नगोत्तमं पुष्पितमाससाद
verses.transliteration:
itīva sītā bahudhā vilapya; sarvātmanā rāmamanusmarantī
pravepamānā pariśuṣkavaktrā; nagottamaṁ puṣpitamāsasāda

translations.english: Bewailing thus in various accents, and remembering Rāma with all her heart, Sītā, having her countenance dried up, and trembling, got at the biggest tree enveloped with flowers. And thinking thus, Sītā, stricken with grief, took up in her hand, her braid of hair and thought—"I shall soon hang myself with this braid and reach the abode of Death."

verses.sanskrit:
शोकानिमित्तानि तदा बहूनि; धैर्यार्जितानि प्रवराणि लोके
प्रादुर्निमित्तानि तदा बभूवुः; पुरापि सिद्धान्युपलक्षितानि
verses.transliteration:
śokānimittāni tadā bahūni; dhairyārjitāni pravarāṇi loke
prādurnimittāni tadā babhūvuḥ; purāpi siddhānyupalakṣitāni

translations.english: And that one of tender person reached the tree, and holding a branch, began to think of Rama, Laksmana, and the glory of her race. And on her person were perceived many auspicious marks, well-known in the world, removing grief, fostering patience and announcing the advent of future welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
तथागतां तां व्यथितामनिन्दितां; व्यपेतहर्षां परिदीनमानसाम्
शुभां निमित्तानि शुभानि भेजिरे; नरं श्रिया जुष्टमिवोपजीविनः
verses.transliteration:
tathāgatāṁ tāṁ vyathitāmaninditāṁ; vyapetaharṣāṁ paridīnamānasām
śubhāṁ nimittāni śubhāni bhejire; naraṁ śriyā juṣṭamivopajīvinaḥ

translations.english: Like to servants waiting upon a wealthy person various auspicious omens waited upon Sītā of a blameless and comely person, racked with grief and divested of joy.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः शुभं वाममरालपक्ष्म; राजीवृतं कृष्णविशालशुक्लम्
प्रास्पन्दतैकं नयनं सुकेश्या; मीनाहतं पद्ममिवाभिताम्रम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ śubhaṁ vāmamarālapakṣma; rājīvṛtaṁ kṛṣṇaviśālaśuklam
prāspandataikaṁ nayanaṁ sukeśyā; mīnāhataṁ padmamivābhitāmram

translations.english: And the large left eye of that dame having graceful hairs, having dark pupils, white ends and thick eye-lashes, began to dance like a lotus shaken by a fish.

verses.sanskrit:
भुजश्च चार्वञ्चितपीनवृत्तः; परार्ध्य कालागुरुचन्दनार्हः
अनुत्तमेनाध्युषितः प्रियेण; चिरेण वामः समवेपताशु
verses.transliteration:
bhujaśca cārvañcitapīnavṛttaḥ; parārdhya kālāgurucandanārhaḥ
anuttamenādhyuṣitaḥ priyeṇa; cireṇa vāmaḥ samavepatāśu

translations.english: And her beautiful, round, plump left hand, which, ere this, sprinkled with costly aguru and sandal, used to serve for a pillow to Rāma, began to dance now again and again after a long time.

verses.sanskrit:
गजेन्द्रहस्तप्रतिमश्च पीन;स्तयोर्द्वयोः संहतयोः सुजातः
प्रस्पन्दमानः पुनरूरुरस्या; रामं पुरस्तात्स्थितमाचचक्षे
verses.transliteration:
gajendrahastapratimaśca pīna;stayordvayoḥ saṁhatayoḥ sujātaḥ
praspandamānaḥ punarūrurasyā; rāmaṁ purastātsthitamācacakṣe

translations.english: And her well built plump left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, dancing, announced that she would soon behold Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
शुभं पुनर्हेमसमानवर्ण;मीषद्रजोध्वस्तमिवामलाक्ष्याः
वासः स्थितायाः शिखराग्रदन्त्याः; किंचित्परिस्रंसत चारुगात्र्याः
verses.transliteration:
śubhaṁ punarhemasamānavarṇa;mīṣadrajodhvastamivāmalākṣyāḥ
vāsaḥ sthitāyāḥ śikharāgradantyāḥ; kiṁcitparisraṁsata cārugātryāḥ

translations.english: And the gold-hued cloth, now covered with dust, of that damsel of a comely person, having teeth like pomegranate seeds, slipped a little off its place.

verses.sanskrit:
एतैर्निमित्तैरपरैश्च सुभ्रूः; संबोधिता प्रागपि साधुसिद्धैः
वातातपक्लान्तमिव प्रनष्टं; वर्षेण बीजं प्रतिसंजहर्ष
verses.transliteration:
etairnimittairaparaiśca subhrūḥ; saṁbodhitā prāgapi sādhusiddhaiḥ
vātātapaklāntamiva pranaṣṭaṁ; varṣeṇa bījaṁ pratisaṁjaharṣa

translations.english: And being enlivened by those and various other auspicious omens, she attained joy like to a seed, spoiled by the wind and the sun, growing afresh in the rainy season.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः पुनर्बिम्बफलोपमौष्ठं; स्वक्षिभ्रुकेशान्तमरालपक्ष्म
वक्त्रं बभासे सितशुक्लदंष्ट्रं; राहोर्मुखाच्चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ punarbimbaphalopamauṣṭhaṁ; svakṣibhrukeśāntamarālapakṣma
vaktraṁ babhāse sitaśukladaṁṣṭraṁ; rāhormukhāccandra iva pramuktaḥ

translations.english: And her countenance, having lips red as Bimba fruits, beautiful eyes, eye-brows extending to ears, curling eye-lashes and white teeth, again appeared graceful like to the Moon released from the full grasp of Rahu. (Like the Moon when full eclipse is just over-In mythology Rāhu is the son of Sinika, a Daitya, with the tail of a dragon whose head was severed from-his body by Vişnu, but being immortal this head and tail retained their separate existence and being transferred to the stellar sphere, became the authors of eclipses.)

verses.sanskrit:
सा वीतशोका व्यपनीततन्द्री; शान्तज्वरा हर्षविबुद्धसत्त्वा
अशोभतार्या वदनेन शुक्ले; शीतान्शुना रात्रिरिवोदितेन
verses.transliteration:
sā vītaśokā vyapanītatandrī; śāntajvarā harṣavibuddhasattvā
aśobhatāryā vadanena śukle; śītānśunā rātririvoditena

translations.english: Her grief and exhaustion were removed. sorrow was pacified and her heart was filled with joy. And she with her countenance appeared beautiful like a lunar night beautified by the rays of the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
हनुमानपि विक्रान्तः सर्वं शुश्राव तत्त्वतः
सीतायास्त्रिजटायाश्च राक्षसीनां च तर्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
hanumānapi vikrāntaḥ sarvaṁ śuśrāva tattvataḥ
sītāyāstrijaṭāyāśca rākṣasīnāṁ ca tarjanam

translations.english: And the powerful Hanumān, heard from the beginning to the end (the bewailings) of Sitā, the story to Trijatā's dream and the threats of the Rākşasīs.

verses.sanskrit:
अवेक्षमाणस्तां देवीं देवतामिव नन्दने
ततो बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
avekṣamāṇastāṁ devīṁ devatāmiva nandane
tato bahuvidhāṁ cintāṁ cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: And beholding the worshipful damsel, living in the forest of Asoka, like to a celestial damsel in the garden of Nandana, the monkey-entered in a maze of anxious thoughts.

verses.sanskrit:
यां कपीनां सहस्राणि सुबहून्ययुतानि च
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सेयमासादिता मया
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ kapīnāṁ sahasrāṇi subahūnyayutāni ca
dikṣu sarvāsu mārgante seyamāsāditā mayā

translations.english: At length my watchful eyes have seen her, whom have been seeking in vain, the thousands and millions of the monkeys in all directions and quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
चारेण तु सुयुक्तेन शत्रोः शक्तिमवेक्षिता
गूढेन चरता तावदवेक्षितमिदं मया
verses.transliteration:
cāreṇa tu suyuktena śatroḥ śaktimavekṣitā
gūḍhena caratā tāvadavekṣitamidaṁ mayā

translations.english: Truly have I seen her today, engaged as I have been as a spy to estimate the strength of the enemy and am ranging secretly everywhere. I have seen minutely the city of the Rākşasas, and the strength of Rāvana the lord of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
युक्तं तस्याप्रमेयस्य सर्वसत्त्वदयावतः
समाश्वासयितुं भार्यां पतिदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
yuktaṁ tasyāprameyasya sarvasattvadayāvataḥ
samāśvāsayituṁ bhāryāṁ patidarśanakāṅkṣiṇīm

translations.english: It now remains to console the spouse of Rāma of incomparable power, and kind to all, who pants for her lord.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमाश्वासयाम्येनां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
अदृष्टदुःखां दुःखस्य न ह्यन्तमधिगच्छतीम्
verses.transliteration:
ahamāśvāsayāmyenāṁ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
adṛṣṭaduḥkhāṁ duḥkhasya na hyantamadhigacchatīm

translations.english: I shall console this damsel, having the countenance of the full moon, who had never seen grief before, and who shall not soon reach its end.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहमिमां देवीं शोकोपहतचेतनाम्
अनाश्वास्य गमिष्यामि दोषवद्गमनं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
yadi hyahamimāṁ devīṁ śokopahatacetanām
anāśvāsya gamiṣyāmi doṣavadgamanaṁ bhavet

translations.english: And if I go away without soothing this chaste lady, who is almost senseless with grief, I shall be blamed of neglect of duty.

verses.sanskrit:
गते हि मयि तत्रेयं राजपुत्री यशस्विनी
परित्राणमविन्दन्ती जानकी जीवितं त्यजेत्
verses.transliteration:
gate hi mayi tatreyaṁ rājaputrī yaśasvinī
paritrāṇamavindantī jānakī jīvitaṁ tyajet

translations.english: And if I go away, the royal daughter, the famed Janaki, finding no means of safety, shall, for certain, renounce her life.

verses.sanskrit:
मया च स महाबाहुः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः
समाश्वासयितुं न्याय्यः सीतादर्शनलालसः
verses.transliteration:
mayā ca sa mahābāhuḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ
samāśvāsayituṁ nyāyyaḥ sītādarśanalālasaḥ

translations.english: She is worthy of being consoled like to the great armed (Rāma) having the countenance of the full-moon and anxious to behold Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
निशाचरीणां प्रत्यक्षमक्षमं चाभिभाषणम्
कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यमिदं कृच्छ्र गतो ह्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
niśācarīṇāṁ pratyakṣamakṣamaṁ cābhibhāṣaṇam
kathaṁ nu khalu kartavyamidaṁ kṛcchra gato hyaham

translations.english: It is not proper to speak before the Rākşasas-What shall I do them? I am in very great difficulty.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन रात्रिशेषेण यदि नाश्वास्यते मया
सर्वथा नास्ति संदेहः परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
anena rātriśeṣeṇa yadi nāśvāsyate mayā
sarvathā nāsti saṁdehaḥ parityakṣyati jīvitam

translations.english: If I do not console her at this later end of the night, surely shall she renounce her life.

verses.sanskrit:
रामश्च यदि पृच्छेन्मां किं मां सीताब्रवीद्वचः
किमहं तं प्रतिब्रूयामसंभाष्य सुमध्यमाम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmaśca yadi pṛcchenmāṁ kiṁ māṁ sītābravīdvacaḥ
kimahaṁ taṁ pratibrūyāmasaṁbhāṣya sumadhyamām

translations.english: How shall I answer Rāma, without consoling Sītā of comely stature, when he will ask me “What message from my Sītā?”

verses.sanskrit:
सीतासंदेशरहितं मामितस्त्वरया गतम्
निर्दहेदपि काकुत्स्थः क्रुद्धस्तीव्रेण चक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
sītāsaṁdeśarahitaṁ māmitastvarayā gatam
nirdahedapi kākutsthaḥ kruddhastīvreṇa cakṣuṣā

translations.english: And if I speedily repair hence without any information regarding Sītā, surely shall Kākuthutha scorci me lifeless with the fire of his angry eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि चेद्योजयिष्यामि भर्तारं रामकारणात्
व्यर्थमागमनं तस्य ससैन्यस्य भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi cedyojayiṣyāmi bhartāraṁ rāmakāraṇāt
vyarthamāgamanaṁ tasya sasainyasya bhaviṣyati

translations.english: And if I urge my lord the king (Vibhīşaņa) to bring his hosts here for Rāma, in vain shall be his toil. (For before that Sītā shall renounce her life.)

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरं त्वहमासाद्य राक्षसीनामिह स्थितः
शनैराश्वासयिष्यामि संतापबहुलामिमाम्
verses.transliteration:
antaraṁ tvahamāsādya rākṣasīnāmiha sthitaḥ
śanairāśvāsayiṣyāmi saṁtāpabahulāmimām

translations.english: And seizing the occasion when she shall be free from her demoniac guards, I shall console her in her dire distress.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं ह्यतितनुश्चैव वनरश्च विशेषतः
वाचं चोदाहरिष्यामि मानुषीमिह संस्कृताम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hyatitanuścaiva vanaraśca viśeṣataḥ
vācaṁ codāhariṣyāmi mānuṣīmiha saṁskṛtām

translations.english: And a puny monkey as I am, I shall speak in Sanskrit (The language refined by the strict rules of grammar) which men delight to use.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि वाचं प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिरिव संस्कृताम्
रावणं मन्यमाना मां सीता भीता भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi vācaṁ pradāsyāmi dvijātiriva saṁskṛtām
rāvaṇaṁ manyamānā māṁ sītā bhītā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: And if I speak Sanskrit like a Brāhmaṇa, Sītā shall be terrified considering me Råvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्
मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता
verses.transliteration:
avaśyameva vaktavyaṁ mānuṣaṁ vākyamarthavat
mayā sāntvayituṁ śakyā nānyatheyamaninditā

translations.english: Must I therefore use the language of a common man or else I shall not be able to console the dame of a blameless person. (This passage clearly indicates that Sanskrit if not spoken by men, and women of the upper classes of the time when Rāmāyaṇa was written, was at least understood by them, and was commonly spoken by men of priestly class and other educated persons")

verses.sanskrit:
सेयमालोक्य मे रूपं जानकी भाषितं तथा
रक्षोभिस्त्रासिता पूर्वं भूयस्त्रासं गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
seyamālokya me rūpaṁ jānakī bhāṣitaṁ tathā
rakṣobhistrāsitā pūrvaṁ bhūyastrāsaṁ gamiṣyati

translations.english: And beholding my monkey shape and hearing my human language she might be afraid again, terrified as she had been before by the band of the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो जातपरित्रासा शब्दं कुर्यान्मनस्विनी
जानमाना विशालाक्षी रावणं कामरूपिणम्
verses.transliteration:
tato jātaparitrāsā śabdaṁ kuryānmanasvinī
jānamānā viśālākṣī rāvaṇaṁ kāmarūpiṇam

translations.english: And considering me Rāvaņa wearing shapes at will, that large-eyed and high-minded dame, shall cry piteously for help.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतया च कृते शब्दे सहसा राक्षसीगणः
नानाप्रहरणो घोरः समेयादन्तकोपमः
verses.transliteration:
sītayā ca kṛte śabde sahasā rākṣasīgaṇaḥ
nānāpraharaṇo ghoraḥ sameyādantakopamaḥ

translations.english: And Sītā making a sudden noise, those terrible Rākṣasīs resembling Death himself and arined with various weapons, shall at once arrive there.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मां संपरिक्षिप्य सर्वतो विकृताननाः
वधे च ग्रहणे चैव कुर्युर्यत्नं यथाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
tato māṁ saṁparikṣipya sarvato vikṛtānanāḥ
vadhe ca grahaṇe caiva kuryuryatnaṁ yathābalam

translations.english: And thereupon casting their looks all around and finding me out, those highly powerful and grim-viasged demons shall try to kill or catch ine.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मां शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम्
दृष्ट्वा विपरिधावन्तं भवेयुर्भयशङ्किताः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ māṁ śākhāḥ praśākhāśca skandhāṁścottamaśākhinām
dṛṣṭvā viparidhāvantaṁ bhaveyurbhayaśaṅkitāḥ

translations.english: Beholding me leap from branch to branch and trunk to trunk of big trees they shall be greatly alarmed.

verses.sanskrit:
मम रूपं च संप्रेक्ष्य वनं विचरतो महत्
राक्षस्यो भयवित्रस्ता भवेयुर्विकृताननाः
verses.transliteration:
mama rūpaṁ ca saṁprekṣya vanaṁ vicarato mahat
rākṣasyo bhayavitrastā bhaveyurvikṛtānanāḥ

translations.english: And espying my appearance while ranging in the forest, those Rākşasīs greatly terrified, shall fill the wood with their wild shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कुर्युः समाह्वानं राक्षस्यो रक्षसामपि
राक्षसेन्द्रनियुक्तानां राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशने
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kuryuḥ samāhvānaṁ rākṣasyo rakṣasāmapi
rākṣasendraniyuktānāṁ rākṣasendraniveśane

translations.english: Then they shall call (to their assistance) all those Rākşasīs engaged in guarding the abode of the lord of the Rāksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शूलशरनिस्त्रिंश विविधायुधपाणयः
आपतेयुर्विमर्देऽस्मिन्वेगेनोद्विग्नकारिणः
verses.transliteration:
te śūlaśaranistriṁśa vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ
āpateyurvimarde'sminvegenodvignakāriṇaḥ

translations.english: They, greatly agitated, shall with vehemence arrive here, armed with dirts, arrow, scimitars and various other weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
संक्रुद्धस्तैस्तु परितो विधमन्रक्षसां बलम्
शक्नुयं न तु संप्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः
verses.transliteration:
saṁkruddhastaistu parito vidhamanrakṣasāṁ balam
śaknuyaṁ na tu saṁprāptuṁ paraṁ pāraṁ mahodadheḥ

translations.english: Being surrounded by them on all sides, If I do kill that host of demons, tired, I shall not be able to bound over the main.

verses.sanskrit:
मां वा गृह्णीयुराप्लुत्य बहवः शीघ्रकारिणः
स्यादियं चागृहीतार्था मम च ग्रहणं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
māṁ vā gṛhṇīyurāplutya bahavaḥ śīghrakāriṇaḥ
syādiyaṁ cāgṛhītārthā mama ca grahaṇaṁ bhavet

translations.english: And if that host of skilled demons, succeed in making me a captive, too shall be in their hands and Sītā shall remain ignorant of my object.

verses.sanskrit:
हिंसाभिरुचयो हिंस्युरिमां वा जनकात्मजाम्
विपन्नं स्यात्ततः कार्यं रामसुग्रीवयोरिदम्
verses.transliteration:
hiṁsābhirucayo hiṁsyurimāṁ vā janakātmajām
vipannaṁ syāttataḥ kāryaṁ rāmasugrīvayoridam

translations.english: Or the Rākşasas, pernicious as they are, shall kill the daughter of Janaka, and there shall the great work of Rāma and Sugrīva, be spoiled.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्देशे नष्टमार्गेऽस्मिन्राक्षसैः परिवारिते
सागरेण परिक्षिप्ते गुप्ते वसति जानकी
verses.transliteration:
uddeśe naṣṭamārge'sminrākṣasaiḥ parivārite
sāgareṇa parikṣipte gupte vasati jānakī

translations.english: And Jānakī live in this secret place, girt by the ocean, guarded on all sides by the Raksasas, difficult of being got at and having all avenues to it shut up.

verses.sanskrit:
विशस्ते वा गृहीते वा रक्षोभिर्मयि संयुगे
नान्यं पश्यामि रामस्य सहायं कार्यसाधने
verses.transliteration:
viśaste vā gṛhīte vā rakṣobhirmayi saṁyuge
nānyaṁ paśyāmi rāmasya sahāyaṁ kāryasādhane

translations.english: If I am killed or captured by Rākşasas in battle, I do not find any who can help Rāma in his enterprise.

verses.sanskrit:
विमृशंश्च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं लङ्घयेत महोदधिम्
verses.transliteration:
vimṛśaṁśca na paśyāmi yo hate mayi vānaraḥ
śatayojanavistīrṇaṁ laṅghayeta mahodadhim

translations.english: Myself killed, I do not find any monkey who can leap a hundred leagues across the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं हन्तुं समर्थोऽस्मि सहस्राण्यपि रक्षसाम्
न तु शक्ष्यामि संप्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ hantuṁ samartho'smi sahasrāṇyapi rakṣasām
na tu śakṣyāmi saṁprāptuṁ paraṁ pāraṁ mahodadheḥ

translations.english: I am capable of destroying thousands of Rākşasas, but I shall not then be able to get at the other shore of the great ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते
कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात्प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्
verses.transliteration:
asatyāni ca yuddhāni saṁśayo me na rocate
kaśca niḥsaṁśayaṁ kāryaṁ kuryātprājñaḥ sasaṁśayam

translations.english: Victory or defeat is uncertain in a battle-I do not (therefore) like to engage in such an uncertain (act). What wise man merges certainty in uncertainly?

verses.sanskrit:
एष दोषो महान्हि स्यान्मम सीताभिभाषणे
प्राणत्यागश्च वैदेह्या भवेदनभिभाषणे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa doṣo mahānhi syānmama sītābhibhāṣaṇe
prāṇatyāgaśca vaidehyā bhavedanabhibhāṣaṇe

translations.english: It is a great sin in me (I own) to talk with Sita-But she will die if I do not talk with her.

verses.sanskrit:
भूताश्चार्था विनश्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः
विक्लवं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा
verses.transliteration:
bhūtāścārthā vinaśyanti deśakālavirodhitāḥ
viklavaṁ dūtamāsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā

translations.english: Action on the very eve of success, on being obstructed by adverse season and place, and through the agency of unreflecting envoys come to nought, even as darkness is dispelled on sunrise.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिर्निश्चितापि न शोभते
घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः
verses.transliteration:
arthānarthāntare buddhirniścitāpi na śobhate
ghātayanti hi kāryāṇi dūtāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ

translations.english: In respect of what should he undertaken and what not, even the certain decision (of a master assisted by his counsellors), because of a heedless messenger, dose not appear in all its beauty: messengers (foolish) yet proud of their knowledge, bring every business to nought.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं नु खलु वाक्यं मे शृणुयान्नोद्विजेत च
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमांश्चकार मतिमान्मतिम्
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ nu khalu vākyaṁ me śṛṇuyānnodvijeta ca
iti saṁcintya hanumāṁścakāra matimānmatim

translations.english: What shall I do, by which my work is not injured, I am not blamed of foolishness and my crossing over the main dose not become fruitless? What shall I do so that Sītā might listen to me without being terrified? Thinking over this, the intelligent Hanumān arrived at a conclusion.

verses.sanskrit:
राममक्लिष्टकर्माणं स्वबन्धुमनुकीर्तयन्
नैनामुद्वेजयिष्यामि तद्बन्धुगतमानसाम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmamakliṣṭakarmāṇaṁ svabandhumanukīrtayan
naināmudvejayiṣyāmi tadbandhugatamānasām

translations.english: I shall not disturb her, speaking (all on a sudden) about Rāma of unwearied actions, dear to her and to whom.

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः
शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākūṇāṁ variṣṭhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
śubhāni dharmayuktāni vacanāni samarpayan

translations.english: She is firmly attached. Uttering the name of Rāma, the foremost of the Ikşvākus, and of subdued soul and lauding his piety and fame in sweet accents, I shall so manage that Sītā might hear and believe them.

verses.sanskrit:
इति स बहुविधं महानुभावो; जगतिपतेः प्रमदामवेक्षमाणः
मधुरमवितथं जगाद वाक्यं; द्रुमविटपान्तरमास्थितो हनूमान्
verses.transliteration:
iti sa bahuvidhaṁ mahānubhāvo; jagatipateḥ pramadāmavekṣamāṇaḥ
madhuramavitathaṁ jagāda vākyaṁ; drumaviṭapāntaramāsthito hanūmān

translations.english: Beholding the spouse of that high-souled lord of the earth and engaging in this train of thoughts, Hanumān, stationed on a branch of the tree, spoke the following sweet words.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयित्व महाकपिः
संश्रवे मधुरं वाक्यं वैदेह्या व्याजहार ह
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bahuvidhāṁ cintāṁ cintayitva mahākapiḥ
saṁśrave madhuraṁ vākyaṁ vaidehyā vyājahāra ha

translations.english: Meditating thus the highly intelligent monkey speh in accents, sweet and in such a tone as they mighty be, heard by Vaidehī.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिनाम्
पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिरृजुरासीन्महायशाः
चक्रवर्तिकुले जातः पुरंदरसमो बले
verses.transliteration:
rājā daśaratho nāma rathakuñjaravājinām
puṇyaśīlo mahākīrtirṛjurāsīnmahāyaśāḥ
cakravartikule jātaḥ puraṁdarasamo bale

translations.english: There reigned a noble and pious king named Dasaratha, highly glorious among the Ikşvākus, the lord of the warrior-cars, steeds and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
पार्थिवव्यञ्जनैर्युक्तः पृथुश्रीः पार्थिवर्षभः
पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तयां विश्रुतः सुखदः सुखी
verses.transliteration:
pārthivavyañjanairyuktaḥ pṛthuśrīḥ pārthivarṣabhaḥ
pṛthivyāṁ caturantayāṁ viśrutaḥ sukhadaḥ sukhī

translations.english: Devoid of envy, high-minded, kind, having truth for his prowess, the foremost of the Ikşvāku race, wealthy and the enhancer of wealth; gifted with royal marks; highly beautiful; the foremost of the kings; famous all over the world of many occans; the conferrer of happiness and himself happy.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठस्ताराधिपनिभाननः
रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya putraḥ priyo jyeṣṭhastārādhipanibhānanaḥ
rāmo nāma viśeṣajñaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām

translations.english: His eldest and most beloved son was the Moon-bright Rāma, wise and the foremost of those who know the science of the bended bow.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य स्वजनस्यापि रक्षिता
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य च परंतपः
verses.transliteration:
rakṣitā svasya vṛttasya svajanasyāpi rakṣitā
rakṣitā jīvalokasya dharmasya ca paraṁtapaḥ

translations.english: He was the protector of his own character, of his own kinsmen, of the whole world of creation and of virtue and subduer of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सत्याभिसंधस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात्पितुः
सभार्यः सह च भ्रात्रा वीरः प्रव्रजितो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya satyābhisaṁdhasya vṛddhasya vacanātpituḥ
sabhāryaḥ saha ca bhrātrā vīraḥ pravrajito vanam

translations.english: And banished by his old and truthful sire's commands, that hero, along with his wife and brother (Laksmana) repaired to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन तत्र महारण्ये मृगयां परिधावता
जनस्थानवधं श्रुत्वा हतौ च खरदूषणौ
ततस्त्वमर्षापहृता जानकी रावणेन तु
verses.transliteration:
tena tatra mahāraṇye mṛgayāṁ paridhāvatā
janasthānavadhaṁ śrutvā hatau ca kharadūṣaṇau
tatastvamarṣāpahṛtā jānakī rāvaṇena tu

translations.english: And having heard of the destruction of the Rākşasas of Janasthāna and of Khara and Duşaņa, the illusive Rāvana, assuming shapes at will, beguiling Rāma, it the forest, stole away his consort-the Janaka's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मीं विनिश्चिताम्
अश्रौषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया
verses.transliteration:
yathārūpāṁ yathāvarṇāṁ yathālakṣmīṁ viniścitām
aśrauṣaṁ rāghavasyāhaṁ seyamāsāditā mayā

translations.english: I have at last got her. And such were the form, grace and the marks that Rāghava mentioned to me. Having said this, the foremost of the monkeys ceased.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सा वक्रकेशान्ता सुकेशी केशसंवृतम्
उन्नम्य वदनं भीरुः शिंशपावृक्षमैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sā vakrakeśāntā sukeśī keśasaṁvṛtam
unnamya vadanaṁ bhīruḥ śiṁśapāvṛkṣamaikṣata

translations.english: And greatly wondered was Sītā hearing those words. Thereupon that timid dame, having good curling hair, raising up her face covered with hairs, looked up to the Singshapă tree.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च तथाप्यधस्ता;न्निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्य बुद्धिम्
ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपतेरमात्यं; वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tiryagūrdhvaṁ ca tathāpyadhastā;nnirīkṣamāṇā tamacintya buddhim
dadarśa piṅgādhipateramātyaṁ; vātātmajaṁ sūryamivodayastham

translations.english: And looking around her and upwards, she beheld, like to the rising sun, the Wind god's son, gifted with inconceivable intellect, the minister of the king of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा
सा ददर्श कपिं तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śākhāntare līnaṁ dṛṣṭvā calitamānasā
sā dadarśa kapiṁ tatra praśritaṁ priyavādinam

translations.english: And beholding that tawny-coloured monkey like to a mass of lightnings and wearing a white cloth, hidden on the tree Sītā's mind was greatly agitated. And she saw there the humble, sweetspeeched monkey, appearing graceful like to a collection of full-blown Asoka flowers and having eyes resembling burning gold.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदुपस्थितम्
मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी
verses.transliteration:
sā tu dṛṣṭvā hariśreṣṭhaṁ vinītavadupasthitam
maithilī cintayāmāsa svapno'yamiti bhāminī

translations.english: And observing that foremost of the monkeys, sitting humbly, that daughter of the king of Mithilā, again greatly amazed, thought.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तं समीक्ष्यैव भृशं विसंज्ञा; गतासुकल्पेव बभूव सीता
चिरेण संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य चैव; विचिन्तयामास विशालनेत्रा
verses.transliteration:
sā taṁ samīkṣyaiva bhṛśaṁ visaṁjñā; gatāsukalpeva babhūva sītā
cireṇa saṁjñāṁ pratilabhya caiva; vicintayāmāsa viśālanetrā

translations.english: And beholding him Sītā was almost out of breath with fear. And regaining soon her sense the large-eyed damsel again thought.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नो मयायं विकृतोऽद्य दृष्टः; शाखामृगः शास्त्रगणैर्निषिद्धः
स्वस्त्यस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय; तथा पितुर्मे जनकस्य राज्ञः
verses.transliteration:
svapno mayāyaṁ vikṛto'dya dṛṣṭaḥ; śākhāmṛgaḥ śāstragaṇairniṣiddhaḥ
svastyastu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya; tathā piturme janakasya rājñaḥ

translations.english: I have seen a very inauspicious dream to-dayto see a monkey in a dream is reckoned inauspicious by the sages. May good betide Rāma, Lakşmaņa and my Sire the king of Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नोऽपि नायं न हि मेऽस्ति निद्रा; शोकेन दुःखेन च पीडितायाः
सुखं हि मे नास्ति यतोऽस्मि हीना; तेनेन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन
verses.transliteration:
svapno'pi nāyaṁ na hi me'sti nidrā; śokena duḥkhena ca pīḍitāyāḥ
sukhaṁ hi me nāsti yato'smi hīnā; tenendupūrṇapratimānanena

translations.english: It is not dream, I have not slept, worn with grief and trouble as I am. Apart form my lord having the countenance of the full-moon, I have no happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि तस्याद्य मनो भवेन; संपीडिता तद्गतसर्वभावा
विचिन्तयन्ती सततं तमेव; तथैव पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi tasyādya mano bhavena; saṁpīḍitā tadgatasarvabhāvā
vicintayantī satataṁ tameva; tathaiva paśyāmi tathā śṛṇomi

translations.english: And therefore his form appearing in my mind is distressing me to-day, who am entirely sunk in his thoughts. And thinking of him always I see him before me and hear his words.

verses.sanskrit:
मनोरथः स्यादिति चिन्तयामि; तथापि बुद्ध्या च वितर्कयामि
किं कारणं तस्य हि नास्ति रूपं; सुव्यक्तरूपश्च वदत्ययं माम्
verses.transliteration:
manorathaḥ syāditi cintayāmi; tathāpi buddhyā ca vitarkayāmi
kiṁ kāraṇaṁ tasya hi nāsti rūpaṁ; suvyaktarūpaśca vadatyayaṁ mām

translations.english: Methinks this is but a phantom of the mind. And thinking this I still behold the same. But an imaginary object can never have a form. And I still find a distinct form addressing me.

verses.sanskrit:
नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये सवज्रिणे; स्वयम्भुवे चैव हुताशनाय
अनेन चोक्तं यदिदं ममाग्रतो; वनौकसा तच्च तथास्तु नान्यथा
verses.transliteration:
namo'stu vācaspataye savajriṇe; svayambhuve caiva hutāśanāya
anena coktaṁ yadidaṁ mamāgrato; vanaukasā tacca tathāstu nānyathā

translations.english: Be glory to Vācaspati, Indra, the self existent Brahmā, the lord of fire and may they so grant that the creature who has spoken before me, be real and not imaginary.

verses.sanskrit:
तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा
verses.transliteration:
tāmabravīnmahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
śirasyañjalimādhāya sītāṁ madhurayā girā

translations.english: Thereupon coming down from the tree, Hanumān, the highly effulgent son of Wind, having a coral-red countenance and attired in a humble guise, approached Sītā and joining reverentially his palms, addressed her with the following sweet words.

verses.sanskrit:
किमर्थं तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्रवति शोकजम्
पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम्
verses.transliteration:
kimarthaṁ tava netrābhyāṁ vāri sravati śokajam
puṇḍarīkapalāśābhyāṁ viprakīrṇamivodakam

translations.english: Who are you, O you having eyes like lotus petals and wearing a soiled silken cloth, who are waiting there holding a branch of the tree? Why are the tears of sorrow flowing from your eyes like to drops of water falling from lotus petals?

verses.sanskrit:
का त्वं भवसि रुद्राणां मरुतां वा वरानने
वसूनां वा वरारोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे
verses.transliteration:
kā tvaṁ bhavasi rudrāṇāṁ marutāṁ vā varānane
vasūnāṁ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me

translations.english: Who are you, O most fair of face, among the celestials, Asuras, Nāgas, Gandharvas, Rāks asas, and Yaksas and Kinnaras? Do the Rudra's (The Rudras are manifestations of Śiva) claim your birth O you fair damsel,? Or the swift gods who ride the storm? Or the Vasus? (A kind of demi-gods of whom six are enumerated viz., Dhava, Druva. Soma or the Moon, Visnu, Anila or wind, Anala or fire, Prabhusa and Prabhava) You appear to me as of a celestial race.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुधालयात्
रोहिणी ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठा सर्वगुणान्विता
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu candramasā hīnā patitā vibudhālayāt
rohiṇī jyotiṣāṁ śreṣṭhā śreṣṭhā sarvaguṇānvitā

translations.english: Are you Rohiņā, the best and most accomplished of the stars, who, left from the Moon, has fallen down from the abode of the celestials?

verses.sanskrit:
कोपाद्वा यदि वा मोहाद्भर्तारमसितेक्षणा
वसिष्ठं कोपयित्वा त्वं नासि कल्याण्यरुन्धती
verses.transliteration:
kopādvā yadi vā mohādbhartāramasitekṣaṇā
vasiṣṭhaṁ kopayitvā tvaṁ nāsi kalyāṇyarundhatī

translations.english: Who are you O blessed dame, O you having blameless eyes? Are you, O lotus-eyed damsel, the blessed Arundhuti, who has fled in wrath or jealous pride form the side of her lord (Vasistha)?

verses.sanskrit:
को नौ पुत्रः पिता भ्रात भर्ता वा ते सुमध्यमे
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं गतं त्वमनुशोचसि
verses.transliteration:
ko nau putraḥ pitā bhrāta bhartā vā te sumadhyame
asmāllokādamuṁ lokaṁ gataṁ tvamanuśocasi

translations.english: Or O lovely damsel, who is the son, father, brother or husband gone from this world for whom you are weeping?

verses.sanskrit:
व्यञ्जनानि हि ते यानि लक्षणानि च लक्षये
महिषी भूमिपालस्य राजकन्यासि मे मता
verses.transliteration:
vyañjanāni hi te yāni lakṣaṇāni ca lakṣaye
mahiṣī bhūmipālasya rājakanyāsi me matā

translations.english: Yet by your tears and sighs, by the earth you are treading and by calling on a monarch's name it appears that you are not a celestial. (The celestials never shed tears nor touch the ground when they walk.) But from the marks on your person it appear that you are either the consort or the daughter of a king.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेन जनस्थानाद्बलादपहृता यदि
सीता त्वमसि भद्रं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇena janasthānādbalādapahṛtā yadi
sītā tvamasi bhadraṁ te tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ

translations.english: Are you that Sītā, I do ask you, who had been stolen and borne away by Rāvana from Janasthāna? May good betide you!

verses.sanskrit:
सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रामकीर्तनहर्षिता
उवाच वाक्यं वैदेही हनूमन्तं द्रुमाश्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tasya vacanaṁ śrutvā rāmakīrtanaharṣitā
uvāca vākyaṁ vaidehī hanūmantaṁ drumāśritam

translations.english: Hearing those words of Hanumān and greatly delighted at Rāma's name, Vaidehī spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
दुहिता जनकस्याहं वैदेहस्य महात्मनः
सीता च नाम नाम्नाहं भार्या रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
duhitā janakasyāhaṁ vaidehasya mahātmanaḥ
sītā ca nāma nāmnāhaṁ bhāryā rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: I am the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, knowing his own self, the foremost of the kings of the world and the slayer of the enemy's host, and the daughter of Janaka the high-souled king of Vaideha. My name is Sītā and I am the consort of the highly intelligent Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
समा द्वादश तत्राहं राघवस्य निवेशने
भुञ्जाना मानुषान्भोगान्सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी
verses.transliteration:
samā dvādaśa tatrāhaṁ rāghavasya niveśane
bhuñjānā mānuṣānbhogānsarvakāmasamṛddhinī

translations.english: I lived twelve years in Rāghava's abode, enjoying every earthly comfort and satisfying every desire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्येनेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्
अभिषेचयितुं राजा सोपाध्यायः प्रचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tatastrayodaśe varṣe rājyenekṣvākunandanam
abhiṣecayituṁ rājā sopādhyāyaḥ pracakrame

translations.english: And at the beginning of the thirteenth year the king, advised by his priest, arranged for the installation of the descendant of Ikşvākus (Rāma) on the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्संभ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने
कैकेयी नाम भर्तारं देवी वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasminsaṁbhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasyābhiṣecane
kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṁ devī vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And while the articles for the installation were being collected, the queen Kaikeyi addressed her lord saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न पिबेयं न खादेयं प्रत्यहं मम भोजनम्
एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
na pibeyaṁ na khādeyaṁ pratyahaṁ mama bhojanam
eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yadyabhiṣicyate

translations.english: I shall not drink or eat for days and this shall be the end of my existence if Räma be installed.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तदुक्तं त्वया वाक्यं प्रीत्या नृपतिसत्तम
तच्चेन्न वितथं कार्यं वनं गच्छतु राघवः
verses.transliteration:
yattaduktaṁ tvayā vākyaṁ prītyā nṛpatisattama
taccenna vitathaṁ kāryaṁ vanaṁ gacchatu rāghavaḥ

translations.english: If you do not wish to falsify the vow (This refers to the vow which Dasaratha made to Kaikeyſ at the time of the war going on between the celestials and the Asuras) you made to me,O best of kings, let Rāma then repair to the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा सत्यवाग्देव्या वरदानमनुस्मरन्
मुमोह वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्याः क्रूरमप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā satyavāgdevyā varadānamanusmaran
mumoha vacanaṁ śrutvā kaikeyyāḥ krūramapriyam

translations.english: The monarch was truthful and remembering his vow and hearing the unpleasant and vile words of Kaikeyi lost himself (in grief).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु स्थविरो राजा सत्यधर्मे व्यवस्थितः
ज्येष्ठं यशस्विनं पुत्रं रुदन्राज्यमयाचत
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sthaviro rājā satyadharme vyavasthitaḥ
jyeṣṭhaṁ yaśasvinaṁ putraṁ rudanrājyamayācata

translations.english: Thereupon the old king abiding by truth, weeping, begged of his eldest son, the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
स पितुर्वचनं श्रीमानभिषेकात्परं प्रियम्
मनसा पूर्वमासाद्य वाचा प्रतिगृहीतवान्
verses.transliteration:
sa piturvacanaṁ śrīmānabhiṣekātparaṁ priyam
manasā pūrvamāsādya vācā pratigṛhītavān

translations.english: The graceful Räma killed his sire's command more than the installation, and resolving within him, promised to obey his words.

verses.sanskrit:
दद्यान्न प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न ब्रूयत्किंचिदप्रियम्
अपि जीवितहेतोर्हि रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
dadyānna pratigṛhṇīyānna brūyatkiṁcidapriyam
api jīvitahetorhi rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ

translations.english: Rāma, having truth for his prowess, never, for his life, takes back what her gives, never speaks an untruth and always speaks truth.

verses.sanskrit:
स विहायोत्तरीयाणि महार्हाणि महायशाः
विसृज्य मनसा राज्यं जनन्यै मां समादिशत्
verses.transliteration:
sa vihāyottarīyāṇi mahārhāṇi mahāyaśāḥ
visṛjya manasā rājyaṁ jananyai māṁ samādiśat

translations.english: Leaving aside his costly attire, the highly glorious (Rāma) renounced with all his heart the kingdom and gave me over to his mother.

verses.sanskrit:
साहं तस्याग्रतस्तूर्णं प्रस्थिता वनचारिणी
न हि मे तेन हीनाया वासः स्वर्गेऽपि रोचते
verses.transliteration:
sāhaṁ tasyāgratastūrṇaṁ prasthitā vanacāriṇī
na hi me tena hīnāyā vāsaḥ svarge'pi rocate

translations.english: But myself wearing the garb of an ascetic, repaired speedily before him. Separated from him, I do not like to live even in the celestial region.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रागेव तु महाभागः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः
पूर्वजस्यानुयात्रार्थे द्रुमचीरैरलंकृतः
verses.transliteration:
prāgeva tu mahābhāgaḥ saumitrirmitranandanaḥ
pūrvajasyānuyātrārthe drumacīrairalaṁkṛtaḥ

translations.english: The great son of Sumitrā, the enhancer of friends' joys, to follow his elder brother, dressed himself in bark and kusa.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं भर्तुरादेशं बहु मान्यदृढव्रताः
प्रविष्टाः स्म पुराद्दृष्टं वनं गम्भीरदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ bharturādeśaṁ bahu mānyadṛḍhavratāḥ
praviṣṭāḥ sma purāddṛṣṭaṁ vanaṁ gambhīradarśanam

translations.english: Thus abiding by our sire's behest, and taking firm vows we entered a dreary forest never seen before.

verses.sanskrit:
वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तस्याहममितौजसः
रक्षसापहृता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना
verses.transliteration:
vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tasyāhamamitaujasaḥ
rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena durātmanā

translations.english: While that one, of unmitigated effulgence was thus living in the forest of Dandaka, I, his consort, was stolen by the vicious-souled Rākşasa—Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ मासौ तेन मे कालो जीवितानुग्रहः कृतः
ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां ततस्त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
dvau māsau tena me kālo jīvitānugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ
ūrdhvaṁ dvābhyāṁ tu māsābhyāṁ tatastyakṣyāmi jīvitam

translations.english: He has kindly allowed me two months respite after which I shall be slain.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं रामस्य संदेशाद्देवि दूतस्तवागतः
वैदेहि कुशली रामस्त्वां च कौशलमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ rāmasya saṁdeśāddevi dūtastavāgataḥ
vaidehi kuśalī rāmastvāṁ ca kauśalamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing those words of Sītā stricken with grief, Hanumān, the foremost of the monkeys, replied in soothing words, O worshipful lady, by Rāma's decree I come as a messenger to these. He is sale and sound, O Vaidehi, and has asked of your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
यो ब्राह्ममस्त्रं वेदांश्च वेद वेदविदां वरः
स त्वां दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
yo brāhmamastraṁ vedāṁśca veda vedavidāṁ varaḥ
sa tvāṁ dāśarathī rāmo devi kauśalamabravīt

translations.english: O worshipful dame, Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, the master of the Vedas, and the foremost of those conversant with Vedas has enquired of your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजा भर्तुस्तेऽनुचरः प्रियः
कृतवाञ्शोकसंतप्तः शिरसा तेऽभिवादनम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaśca mahātejā bhartuste'nucaraḥ priyaḥ
kṛtavāñśokasaṁtaptaḥ śirasā te'bhivādanam

translations.english: And the highly effulgent Lakşmaņa, the beloved follower of your husband, worn with grief, bows his reverential head to you.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तयोः कुशलं देवी निशम्य नरसिंहयोः
प्रीतिसंहृष्टसर्वाङ्गी हनूमान्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sā tayoḥ kuśalaṁ devī niśamya narasiṁhayoḥ
prītisaṁhṛṣṭasarvāṅgī hanūmāntamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing of the welfare of those two lions among men, the worshipful dame, with all her frame worked up with rapture, again spake to Hanumān, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
कल्याणी बत गथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मे
एहि जीवन्तमानदो नरं वर्षशतादपि
verses.transliteration:
kalyāṇī bata gatheyaṁ laukikī pratibhāti me
ehi jīvantamānado naraṁ varṣaśatādapi

translations.english: Verily the wise saw of the people appears to me to be true that once in a hundred years true joy appears to a living man.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः समागमे तस्मिन्प्रीतिरुत्पादिताद्भुता
परस्परेण चालापं विश्वस्तौ तौ प्रचक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ samāgame tasminprītirutpāditādbhutā
paraspareṇa cālāpaṁ viśvastau tau pracakratuḥ

translations.english: Sītā, at that time, attained such a wonderful joy, as would have been acquired by her in the company (of Rama and Laksmana). And they confidingly conversed with each other.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान्हरियूथपः
सीतायाः शोकदीनायाः समीपमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstadvacanaṁ śrutvā hanūmānhariyūthapaḥ
sītāyāḥ śokadīnāyāḥ samīpamupacakrame

translations.english: Hearing those words of $ītā, racked with sorrow, Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god drew a little nearer to her.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा यथा समीपं स हनूमानुपसर्पति
तथा तथा रावणं सा तं सीता परिशङ्कते
verses.transliteration:
yathā yathā samīpaṁ sa hanūmānupasarpati
tathā tathā rāvaṇaṁ sā taṁ sītā pariśaṅkate

translations.english: The more Hanumān approached her the more Sītā suspected him as Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो धिग्धिक्कृतमिदं कथितं हि यदस्य मे
रूपान्तरमुपागम्य स एवायं हि रावणः
verses.transliteration:
aho dhigdhikkṛtamidaṁ kathitaṁ hi yadasya me
rūpāntaramupāgamya sa evāyaṁ hi rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Alas! Alas! why have I spoken to him? It is the Rāvaņa, who has appeared again in a new disguise.

verses.sanskrit:
तामशोकस्य शाखां सा विमुक्त्वा शोककर्शिता
तस्यामेवानवद्याङ्गी धरण्यां समुपाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
tāmaśokasya śākhāṁ sā vimuktvā śokakarśitā
tasyāmevānavadyāṅgī dharaṇyāṁ samupāviśat

translations.english: And leaving off the Asoka branch, that one having a blameless person, overwhelmed with grief, sat down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अवन्दत महाबाहुस्ततस्तां जनकात्मजाम्
सा चैनं भयवित्रस्ता भूयो नैवाभ्युदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
avandata mahābāhustatastāṁ janakātmajām
sā cainaṁ bhayavitrastā bhūyo naivābhyudaikṣata

translations.english: In the meantime the mighty-armed monkey bowed to Janaka's daughter, but she, worked up with fear, did not cast again her looks towards him.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानं तु सीता शशिनिभानना
अब्रवीद्दीर्घमुच्छ्वस्य वानरं मधुरस्वरा
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā vandamānaṁ tu sītā śaśinibhānanā
abravīddīrghamucchvasya vānaraṁ madhurasvarā

translations.english: Beholding him bow to her, Sítā, having a moon-like countenance, sighing, spoke to that monkey in sweet accents.

verses.sanskrit:
मायां प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वं रावणः स्वयम्
उत्पादयसि मे भूयः संतापं तन्न शोभनम्
verses.transliteration:
māyāṁ praviṣṭo māyāvī yadi tvaṁ rāvaṇaḥ svayam
utpādayasi me bhūyaḥ saṁtāpaṁ tanna śobhanam

translations.english: If you are that Ravana's self, who, changing your shape by magic art, want to distress me again— this your vile deed dose not behove you.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वं परित्यज्य रूपं यः परिव्राजकरूपधृत्
जनस्थाने मया दृष्टस्त्वं स एवासि रावणः
verses.transliteration:
svaṁ parityajya rūpaṁ yaḥ parivrājakarūpadhṛt
janasthāne mayā dṛṣṭastvaṁ sa evāsi rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: You are surely that Rāvana, whom I saw at Janasthāna, in a mendicant's guise, renouncing his own shape.

verses.sanskrit:
उपवासकृशां दीनां कामरूप निशाचर
संतापयसि मां भूयः संतापं तन्न शोभनम्
verses.transliteration:
upavāsakṛśāṁ dīnāṁ kāmarūpa niśācara
saṁtāpayasi māṁ bhūyaḥ saṁtāpaṁ tanna śobhanam

translations.english: O night-ranger, O you wearing shapes at will! it dose not behove you to distress me who am poorly and famished with fasts.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि रामस्य दूतस्त्वमागतो भद्रमस्तु ते
पृच्छामि त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ प्रिया राम कथा हि मे
verses.transliteration:
yadi rāmasya dūtastvamāgato bhadramastu te
pṛcchāmi tvāṁ hariśreṣṭha priyā rāma kathā hi me

translations.english: And may good betide you if you are Rāma's messenger. I do ask you, O foremost of monkeys, something about Rāma that is pleasant to me.

verses.sanskrit:
गुणान्रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर
चित्तं हरसि मे सौम्य नदीकूलं यथा रयः
verses.transliteration:
guṇānrāmasya kathaya priyasya mama vānara
cittaṁ harasi me saumya nadīkūlaṁ yathā rayaḥ

translations.english: O monkey, do you relate the glories of my dear Rama. You are (thus) shaking my mind O gentle one, like to water breaking down the banks of a river.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो स्वप्नस्य सुखता याहमेवं चिराहृता
प्रेषितं नाम पश्यामि राघवेण वनौकसं
verses.transliteration:
aho svapnasya sukhatā yāhamevaṁ cirāhṛtā
preṣitaṁ nāma paśyāmi rāghaveṇa vanaukasaṁ

translations.english: Alas! this dream has afforded me immense pleasure since, I, who have been separated from my lord for so long a time, have beheld this monkey sent by Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहं वीरं राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्
पश्येयं नावसीदेयं स्वप्नोऽपि मम मत्सरी
verses.transliteration:
svapne'pi yadyahaṁ vīraṁ rāghavaṁ sahalakṣmaṇam
paśyeyaṁ nāvasīdeyaṁ svapno'pi mama matsarī

translations.english: I do not sink even if I can behold in dream the heroic Raghava. along with Laksmana-but dream even is Jealous of my well-being.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं स्वप्नमिमं मन्ये स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा हि वानरम्
न शक्योऽभ्युदयः प्राप्तुं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयो मम
verses.transliteration:
nāhaṁ svapnamimaṁ manye svapne dṛṣṭvā hi vānaram
na śakyo'bhyudayaḥ prāptuṁ prāptaścābhyudayo mama

translations.english: Nor do I regard this as dream. To behold a monkey in a dream dose not lead to prosperity whereas I have attained it. (Here prosperity means joy-Sītā attained an immense treasure of joy on beholding Rāma's messengerHanumãn.)

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु स्याच्चित्तमोहोऽयं भवेद्वातगतिस्त्वियम्
उन्मादजो विकारो वा स्यादियं मृगतृष्णिका
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu syāccittamoho'yaṁ bhavedvātagatistviyam
unmādajo vikāro vā syādiyaṁ mṛgatṛṣṇikā

translations.english: Or is it mental derangement? Or have I been possessed by a devil? Or have I run mad? Or is it the sultry vapour noating over sands and appearing at a distance like water?

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा नायमुन्मादो मोहोऽप्युन्मादलक्ष्मणः
संबुध्ये चाहमात्मानमिमं चापि वनौकसं
verses.transliteration:
atha vā nāyamunmādo moho'pyunmādalakṣmaṇaḥ
saṁbudhye cāhamātmānamimaṁ cāpi vanaukasaṁ

translations.english: No, it is not madness-for derangement of mind is the sign of madness, I have not lost sense and I do distinctly perceive me and the monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
एतां बुद्धिं तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनुमध्यमा
न प्रतिव्याजहाराथ वानरं जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ buddhiṁ tadā kṛtvā sītā sā tanumadhyamā
na prativyājahārātha vānaraṁ janakātmajā

translations.english: Thinking thus in many a way and ascertaining the strength of the monkey and the Rākṣasa) Sītā took him for the lord of the Raksasas, wearing shapes at will. And having arrived at this decision, Janaka's daughter-Sītā, ceased from talking with that monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतायाश्चिन्तितं बुद्ध्वा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
श्रोत्रानुकूलैर्वचनैस्तदा तां संप्रहर्षयत्
verses.transliteration:
sītāyāścintitaṁ buddhvā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
śrotrānukūlairvacanaistadā tāṁ saṁpraharṣayat

translations.english: And apprised of Sītā's thought, Hanumān, the Wind-god's son, (replied) in words sweet to her and enhancing her delight.

verses.sanskrit:
आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तः शशी यथा
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा
verses.transliteration:
āditya iva tejasvī lokakāntaḥ śaśī yathā
rājā sarvasya lokasya devo vaiśravaṇo yathā

translations.english: Bright as the sun that lights the sky and dear as the moon to every eye, he pleases all his subjects with bounties like to those of as Vaisravana. (Another name of Kubera, the god of gold.)

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः
सत्यवादी मधुरवाग्देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
vikrameṇopapannaśca yathā viṣṇurmahāyaśāḥ
satyavādī madhuravāgdevo vācaspatiryathā

translations.english: He is gifted with prowess like to the greatly famed Vişnu, truthful and sweet-speeched like to Vacaspati. (The god of speech)

verses.sanskrit:
रूपवान्सुभगः श्रीमान्कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्
स्थानक्रोधप्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः
बाहुच्छायामवष्टब्धो यस्य लोको महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
rūpavānsubhagaḥ śrīmānkandarpa iva mūrtimān
sthānakrodhaprahartā ca śreṣṭho loke mahārathaḥ
bāhucchāyāmavaṣṭabdho yasya loko mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Graceful, grateful to the eye and beautiful like to Kandarva's (Cupid or the god of love in Hindu mythology described the most beautiful of the celestials) Self, he displays his wrath in a proper quarter-the foremost of men and of a mighty car.

verses.sanskrit:
अपकृष्याश्रमपदान्मृगरूपेण राघवम्
शून्ये येनापनीतासि तस्य द्रक्ष्यसि यत्फलम्
verses.transliteration:
apakṛṣyāśramapadānmṛgarūpeṇa rāghavam
śūnye yenāpanītāsi tasya drakṣyasi yatphalam

translations.english: The whole world of creation (live safe) in the shadow of the arms of that high-souled one. You shall soon see the consequences he shall reap by whom, assuming the shape of a dear, Rāghava was taken away from the hermitage and you wert stolen away from that lonely place.

verses.sanskrit:
नचिराद्रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान्
रोषप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः
verses.transliteration:
nacirādrāvaṇaṁ saṁkhye yo vadhiṣyati vīryavān
roṣapramuktairiṣubhirjvaladbhiriva pāvakaiḥ

translations.english: And soon shall that powerful (hero) destroy Ravana in the battle, with fiery arrows, discharged angrily.

verses.sanskrit:
तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूतस्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः
त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्तः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tenāhaṁ preṣito dūtastvatsakāśamihāgataḥ
tvadviyogena duḥkhārtaḥ sa tvāṁ kauśalamabravīt

translations.english: I have been sent by him as a messenger to you. Worn with grief in your separation he has enquired of your welfare, as well the highly effulgent Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of Sumitrā's joy, bowing reverentially to you.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य च सखा देवि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः
राजा वानरमुख्यानां स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya ca sakhā devi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
rājā vānaramukhyānāṁ sa tvāṁ kauśalamabravīt

translations.english: The king of monkey host, by name SugrīvaRama's friend, has also enquired of your welfare, O worshipful dame. Rāma, Sugrīva and Laksmana, have you always in their minds.

verses.sanskrit:
नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्
मध्ये वानरकोटीनां सुग्रीवं चामितौजसं
verses.transliteration:
nacirāddrakṣyase rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahāratham
madhye vānarakoṭīnāṁ sugrīvaṁ cāmitaujasaṁ

translations.english: Blessed are we, O Vaidehi, that you do still live, subject as you are to the Raksasis. You shall soon behold Rāma, and Lakşmaņa of a mighty car, and Sugrīva of unmitigated prowess in the midst of the million of monkey hosts. I am Sugrīva's minister, by name Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पदन्यासं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
त्वां द्रष्टुमुपयातोऽहं समाश्रित्य पराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā mūrdhni padanyāsaṁ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
tvāṁ draṣṭumupayāto'haṁ samāśritya parākramam

translations.english: I have entered this city of Lankā after crossing over the great main. And by means of my prowess and placing my feet on the head of the vicious-souled Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहमस्मि तथा देवि यथा मामवगच्छसि
विशङ्का त्यज्यतामेषा श्रद्धत्स्व वदतो मम
verses.transliteration:
nāhamasmi tathā devi yathā māmavagacchasi
viśaṅkā tyajyatāmeṣā śraddhatsva vadato mama

translations.english: I have come here to see you I am not he (Ravana) for whom you are taking me, O worshipful dame. Do you renounce your suspicion and rely on my words.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु राम कथां श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानरर्षभात्
उवाच वचनं सान्त्वमिदं मधुरया गिरा
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu rāma kathāṁ śrutvā vaidehī vānararṣabhāt
uvāca vacanaṁ sāntvamidaṁ madhurayā girā

translations.english: Hearing the tale of Rāma from that best of monkeys, Vaidehī, spoke in sweet accents, soft and low.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथं जानासि लक्ष्मणम्
वानराणां नराणां च कथमासीत्समागमः
verses.transliteration:
kva te rāmeṇa saṁsargaḥ kathaṁ jānāsi lakṣmaṇam
vānarāṇāṁ narāṇāṁ ca kathamāsītsamāgamaḥ

translations.english: Where didst you meet Rāma, how didst you come to know Lakşmaņa? How did the monkeys and men meet on terms of brother-hood?

verses.sanskrit:
यानि रामस्य लिङ्गानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर
तानि भूयः समाचक्ष्व न मां शोकः समाविशेत्
verses.transliteration:
yāni rāmasya liṅgāni lakṣmaṇasya ca vānara
tāni bhūyaḥ samācakṣva na māṁ śokaḥ samāviśet

translations.english: Do you again relate to me, O monkey, the regal signs that deck the persons of Rāma and Lakşmaņa-and I shall then relinquish all grief.

verses.sanskrit:
कीदृशं तस्य संस्थानं रूपं रामस्य कीदृशम्
कथमूरू कथं बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे
verses.transliteration:
kīdṛśaṁ tasya saṁsthānaṁ rūpaṁ rāmasya kīdṛśam
kathamūrū kathaṁ bāhū lakṣmaṇasya ca śaṁsa me

translations.english: Do you relate to me the form and grace of Rāma, his thighs and arms and as well as those of Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु वैदेह्या हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
ततो रामं यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu vaidehyā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
tato rāmaṁ yathātattvamākhyātumupacakrame

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Vaidehi, Hanuman, the Wind-god's son, began to give an exact description of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च यानि वै
लक्षितानि विशालाक्षि वदतः शृणु तानि मे
verses.transliteration:
yāni rāmasya cihnāni lakṣmaṇasya ca yāni vai
lakṣitāni viśālākṣi vadataḥ śṛṇu tāni me

translations.english: If do you, by my good luck, O Vaidehi, O you having eyes like lotus-petals, knowing me (as his messenger) ask me to describe your lord's person as well as that of Lakşmaņa, I shall relate them to you. Do you hear, O large-eyed dame, what regal signs I have marked on the persons of Rama and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः कमलपत्राक्षः सर्वभूतमनोहरः
रूपदाक्षिण्यसंपन्नः प्रसूतो जनकात्मजे
verses.transliteration:
rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ
rūpadākṣiṇyasaṁpannaḥ prasūto janakātmaje

translations.english: O daughter of Janaka, Rāma has eyes like lotus-petals and a countenance resembling the full-moon and is gifted with great beauty and goodness.

verses.sanskrit:
तेजसादित्यसंकाशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः
बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः
verses.transliteration:
tejasādityasaṁkāśaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ
bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā yaśasā vāsavopamaḥ

translations.english: In effulgence he is like the Sun, in patience like the earth, in intellect like BỊhaspati (The god of wisdom) and in fame like Vāsava. (The lord of celestials) He is the protector of the world of creation and his own kinsmen. He follows right in all his ways and never swerves from his royal duties and is the slayer of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
रामो भामिनि लोकस्य चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता
मर्यादानां च लोकस्य कर्ता कारयिता च सः
verses.transliteration:
rāmo bhāmini lokasya cāturvarṇyasya rakṣitā
maryādānāṁ ca lokasya kartā kārayitā ca saḥ

translations.english: O dame, he upholds the dignity of the people of four-castes— he confers honours on the people and preserves them.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्चिष्मानर्चितोऽत्यर्थं ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितः
साधूनामुपकारज्ञः प्रचारज्ञश्च कर्मणाम्
verses.transliteration:
arciṣmānarcito'tyarthaṁ brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ
sādhūnāmupakārajñaḥ pracārajñaśca karmaṇām

translations.english: He is worshipped by all like the Sun, observes ascetic vows, know well the time when the saints should be honoured and is conversant with the nature and procedure of actions.

verses.sanskrit:
राजविद्याविनीतश्च ब्राह्मणानामुपासिता
श्रुतवाञ्शीलसंपन्नो विनीतश्च परंतपः
verses.transliteration:
rājavidyāvinītaśca brāhmaṇānāmupāsitā
śrutavāñśīlasaṁpanno vinītaśca paraṁtapaḥ

translations.english: He is well acquainted with royal duties and abode by the commandments of the Brāhmaṇas is wise, gifted with a good character, humble and the slayer of foes.

verses.sanskrit:
यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च वेदविद्भिः सुपूजितः
धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च वेदाङ्गेषु च निष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
yajurvedavinītaśca vedavidbhiḥ supūjitaḥ
dhanurvede ca vede ca vedāṅgeṣu ca niṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: He is the master of Yajurvedas and is adored by those who are well-versed in Vedas—is proficient in the science of bended bow, Vedas and Vedāngas. (A sacred science considered as subordinate to and in some sense a part of the Vedas six sciences come under this denimination-Siksha (pronunciation); Kalp. (religious rite) Vyakarana (grammar) Chandas (prosody) Jyotis (astronomy) and and Nirukti explanation of difficult words.)

verses.sanskrit:
विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवः शुभाननः
गूढजत्रुः सुताम्राक्षो रामो देवि जनैः श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
vipulāṁso mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvaḥ śubhānanaḥ
gūḍhajatruḥ sutāmrākṣo rāmo devi janaiḥ śrutaḥ

translations.english: He is broad-shouldered, large-armed, has a conch-like neck and a beautiful countenance. His throat is plump and his eyes are red-and he is famed all over the world under the name of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोषः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्
समः समविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः
verses.transliteration:
dundubhisvananirghoṣaḥ snigdhavarṇaḥ pratāpavān
samaḥ samavibhaktāṅgo varṇaṁ śyāmaṁ samāśritaḥ

translations.english: He has the voice of a bugle, is of a cool hue and highly powerful, has equally proportioned limbs and a green colour.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिस्थिरस्त्रिप्रलम्बश्च त्रिसमस्त्रिषु चोन्नतः
त्रिवलीवांस्त्र्यवणतश्चतुर्व्यङ्गस्त्रिशीर्षवान्
verses.transliteration:
tristhirastripralambaśca trisamastriṣu connataḥ
trivalīvāṁstryavaṇataścaturvyaṅgastriśīrṣavān

translations.english: His three limbs (thigh, fist and wrist) are hard and three others (brow arins and scrotum) are long; and three (tops of the hairs, scrotums and knee-joints) equal and three (navel, abdomen and breast) high. And three (the angles of the or three are cool and three (voice, navel and gait) are grave.

verses.sanskrit:
महौष्ठहनुनासश्च पञ्चस्निग्धोऽष्टवंशवान्
दशपद्मो दशबृहत्त्रिभिर्व्याप्तो द्विशुक्लवान्
षडुन्नतो नवतनुस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति राघवः
verses.transliteration:
mahauṣṭhahanunāsaśca pañcasnigdho'ṣṭavaṁśavān
daśapadmo daśabṛhattribhirvyāpto dviśuklavān
ṣaḍunnato navatanustribhirvyāpnoti rāghavaḥ

translations.english: His belly and throat have three folds of skin. The sole of the foot, the lines thereon and the nipples are equally bended. His neck, eyes and back are short. He has three locks of hair on his head. He has four lines on his thumb indicating his proficiency in the four Vedas. His body is four hands tall; arms, thighs and checks are plump; eye-brows, the hollows of the nose, eyes, ears, lips, nipples; wrists, knee-joints, scrotums, hips, hands feet are all equally proportioned. Four teeth by the side of each row, are gifted with auspicious marks of the Gästras. His gaits are like those of a lion, tiger, elephant or a bull. His lips and jaws are fleshy and elevated. His nose is long; words, countenance, nails, down and skin are all cool; his two arms, two little fingers, two thighs and two legs are long; his face, eyes, mouth tongue, lips; palate, nipples, nails and feet are like lotuses, his breast, forehead, neck, arms, navel feet, back and ears are spacious. He is gifted with grace, fame and effulgence. His paternal and maternal race are pure. His armpit, belly, breasts, nose, shoulders and forehead are high; his fingers, hairs, down, nails, skin, beard, eye-sight and intellect are thin and sharp. Rāghava, with a due division of his time is engaged in acquiring piety, wealth emancipation and desires,

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यधर्मपरः श्रीमान्संग्रहानुग्रहे रतः
देशकालविभागज्ञः सर्वलोकप्रियंवदः
verses.transliteration:
satyadharmaparaḥ śrīmānsaṁgrahānugrahe rataḥ
deśakālavibhāgajñaḥ sarvalokapriyaṁvadaḥ

translations.english: He is truthful and graceful, amasses wealth and thereby protects his subjects. He is cognisant of the divisions of time and country and dear to all.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्राता च तस्य द्वैमात्रः सौमित्रिरपराजितः
अनुरागेण रूपेण गुणैश्चैव तथाविधः
verses.transliteration:
bhrātā ca tasya dvaimātraḥ saumitriraparājitaḥ
anurāgeṇa rūpeṇa guṇaiścaiva tathāvidhaḥ

translations.english: His step brother Saumitri is gifted with incomparable prowess and is his equal in attachment, beauty and accomplishments.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे तु बहुपादपसंकुले
भ्रातुर्भार्यार्तमासीनं सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛśyamūkasya pṛṣṭhe tu bahupādapasaṁkule
bhrāturbhāryārtamāsīnaṁ sugrīvaṁ priyadarśanam

translations.english: And ranging the earth for you they beheld Sugriva, of comely presence, the lord of monkeys, at the foot of the mount Rsyamūka covered with trees, banished by his elder brother and resorting there in his fear.

verses.sanskrit:
वयं तु हरिराजं तं सुग्रीवं सत्यसंगरम्
परिचर्यामहे राज्यात्पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्
verses.transliteration:
vayaṁ tu harirājaṁ taṁ sugrīvaṁ satyasaṁgaram
paricaryāmahe rājyātpūrvajenāvaropitam

translations.english: We wears serving that truthful Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, driven from the kingdom by his elder brother.

verses.sanskrit:
स तौ दृष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्रौ धन्विनौ वानरर्षभः
अभिप्लुतो गिरेस्तस्य शिखरं भयमोहितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tau dṛṣṭvā naravyāghrau dhanvinau vānararṣabhaḥ
abhipluto girestasya śikharaṁ bhayamohitaḥ

translations.english: Beholding those two best of men, wearing bark and with bows in their hands, that best of monkeys, stricken with fear, leaped above and stationed himself on the crest of the hill.

verses.sanskrit:
तावहं पुरुषव्याघ्रौ सुग्रीववचनात्प्रभू
रूपलक्षणसंपन्नौ कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tāvahaṁ puruṣavyāghrau sugrīvavacanātprabhū
rūpalakṣaṇasaṁpannau kṛtāñjalirupasthitaḥ

translations.english: He then sent me to them. And thereupon by Sugrīva's decree I, approached with joined palms, those two foremost of men gifted with beauty and royal marks.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ परिज्ञाततत्त्वार्थौ मया प्रीतिसमन्वितौ
पृष्ठमारोप्य तं देशं प्रापितौ पुरुषर्षभौ
verses.transliteration:
tau parijñātatattvārthau mayā prītisamanvitau
pṛṣṭhamāropya taṁ deśaṁ prāpitau puruṣarṣabhau

translations.english: They were pleased by me, being informed of the real facts. And then placing those two best of men on my back I arrived at the top of the hill and communicated the truth to the high-souled Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र तौ कीर्तिसंपन्नौ हरीश्वरनरेश्वरौ
परस्परकृताश्वासौ कथया पूर्ववृत्तया
verses.transliteration:
tatra tau kīrtisaṁpannau harīśvaranareśvarau
parasparakṛtāśvāsau kathayā pūrvavṛttayā

translations.english: And conversing with each other those two lords of men and monkeys attained great delight. And they consoled each other narrating their respective misfortunes.

verses.sanskrit:
तं ततः सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
स्त्रीहेतोर्वालिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तमुरु तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tataḥ sāntvayāmāsa sugrīvaṁ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
strīhetorvālinā bhrātrā nirastamuru tejasā

translations.english: And Rāma then consoled Sugrīva, driven away by his greatly powerful elder brother Vāli on his wife's account.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वन्नाशजं शोकं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः
लक्ष्मणो वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastvannāśajaṁ śokaṁ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
lakṣmaṇo vānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayat

translations.english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa related to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, the grief, of Rāma of unwearied actions, in consequence of your being borne away (by Rāvana).

verses.sanskrit:
स श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेनेरितं वचः
तदासीन्निष्प्रभोऽत्यर्थं ग्रहग्रस्त इवांशुमान्
verses.transliteration:
sa śrutvā vānarendrastu lakṣmaṇeneritaṁ vacaḥ
tadāsīnniṣprabho'tyarthaṁ grahagrasta ivāṁśumān

translations.english: And hearing Laksmana's words, the lord of monkeys became pale, like to the radiant Sun possessed by Rāhu.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वद्गात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया
यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले
verses.transliteration:
tatastvadgātraśobhīni rakṣasā hriyamāṇayā
yānyābharaṇajālāni pātitāni mahītale

translations.english: And collecting all those ornaments which were thrown off by you on the earth when you were borne away, the leaders of the monkey hosts, delighted brought them before Räma. But they could not make out your whereabouts.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यङ्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहुविधं ततः
तेन देवप्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
tānyaṅke darśanīyāni kṛtvā bahuvidhaṁ tataḥ
tena devaprakāśena devena paridevitam

translations.english: All those ornaments, which were handed over to Rāma, were collected by me when they fell tinkling on the ground, Rāma being beside himself with grief. And placing them on his lap, the god-like Rāma bewailed in various accents.

verses.sanskrit:
शयितं च चिरं तेन दुःखार्तेन महात्मना
मयापि विविधैर्वाक्यैः कृच्छ्रादुत्थापितः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
śayitaṁ ca ciraṁ tena duḥkhārtena mahātmanā
mayāpi vividhairvākyaiḥ kṛcchrādutthāpitaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: They inflamed the more Dasarathi's (Son of Dasaratha-Rāma) grief. And being overwhelmed with grief that high-souled one laid himself low on the ground. And consoling him in various words, I raised him up again.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि दृष्ट्वा महार्हाणि दर्शयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः
राघवः सहसौमित्रिः सुग्रीवे स न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
tāni dṛṣṭvā mahārhāṇi darśayitvā muhurmuhuḥ
rāghavaḥ sahasaumitriḥ sugrīve sa nyavedayat

translations.english: Looking again and again with Saumitri, at those costly ornaments, Rāghava handed them over to Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
स तवादर्शनादार्ये राघवः परितप्यते
महता ज्वलता नित्यमग्निनेवाग्निपर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tavādarśanādārye rāghavaḥ paritapyate
mahatā jvalatā nityamagninevāgniparvataḥ

translations.english: Rāghava burns in grief, O worshipful dame, in your absence, like to a volcanic mountain burning with a perpetual fire.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वत्कृते तमनिद्रा च शोकश्चिन्ता च राघवम्
तापयन्ति महात्मानमग्न्यगारमिवाग्नयः
verses.transliteration:
tvatkṛte tamanidrā ca śokaścintā ca rāghavam
tāpayanti mahātmānamagnyagāramivāgnayaḥ

translations.english: For you, sleeplessness, grief and anxiety are distressing Rāghava like to three fires, (The aggregate of the three fires maintained by the Brāhmaṇa house-holder) burning down the fire temple.

verses.sanskrit:
तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः प्रविचाल्यते
महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः
verses.transliteration:
tavādarśanaśokena rāghavaḥ pravicālyate
mahatā bhūmikampena mahāniva śiloccayaḥ

translations.english: Rāghava is moved by your separation like to a huge mountain shaken by a terrible earth-quake.

verses.sanskrit:
कानानानि सुरम्याणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च
चरन्न रतिमाप्नोति त्वमपश्यन्नृपात्मजे
verses.transliteration:
kānānāni suramyāṇi nadīprasravaṇāni ca
caranna ratimāpnoti tvamapaśyannṛpātmaje

translations.english: O daughter of a king, he is ranging at large in many a beautiful forest, river and fountain-but he finds delight nowhere.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वां मनुजशार्दूलः क्षिप्रं प्राप्स्यति राघवः
समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं जनकात्मजे
verses.transliteration:
sa tvāṁ manujaśārdūlaḥ kṣipraṁ prāpsyati rāghavaḥ
samitrabāndhavaṁ hatvā rāvaṇaṁ janakātmaje

translations.english: O daughter of the king Janaka bringing about the destruction of Rāvaņa, with all his kith and kin, Rāghava, the foremost of men, shall soon regain you.

verses.sanskrit:
सहितौ रामसुग्रीवावुभावकुरुतां तदा
समयं वालिनं हन्तुं तव चान्वेषणं तथा
verses.transliteration:
sahitau rāmasugrīvāvubhāvakurutāṁ tadā
samayaṁ vālinaṁ hantuṁ tava cānveṣaṇaṁ tathā

translations.english: Thus Rāma and Sugrīva entered into a friendly covenant, to encompass Vali's destruction and to institute enquiries about you.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निहत्य तरसा रामो वालिनमाहवे
सर्वर्क्षहरिसंघानां सुग्रीवमकरोत्पतिम्
verses.transliteration:
tato nihatya tarasā rāmo vālinamāhave
sarvarkṣaharisaṁghānāṁ sugrīvamakarotpatim

translations.english: And destroying Vāli by his prowess in battle, Rāma made Sugrīva king over all monkeys and bears.

verses.sanskrit:
रामसुग्रीवयोरैक्यं देव्येवं समजायत
हनूमन्तं च मां विद्धि तयोर्दूतमिहागतम्
verses.transliteration:
rāmasugrīvayoraikyaṁ devyevaṁ samajāyata
hanūmantaṁ ca māṁ viddhi tayordūtamihāgatam

translations.english: In this way, O dame, the alliance between Rāma and Sugrīva was made. And know me as Hanumān, their messenger who has come to you.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वराज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवः समनीय महाहरीन्
त्वदर्थं प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान्
verses.transliteration:
svarājyaṁ prāpya sugrīvaḥ samanīya mahāharīn
tvadarthaṁ preṣayāmāsa diśo daśa mahābalān

translations.english: Regaining his kingdom, Sugrīva summoned all the mighty monkeys and despatched them in various quarters in quest of you.

verses.sanskrit:
आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महौजसः
अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशाः सर्वतः प्रस्थिता महीम्
verses.transliteration:
ādiṣṭā vānarendreṇa sugrīveṇa mahaujasaḥ
adrirājapratīkāśāḥ sarvataḥ prasthitā mahīm

translations.english: The highly powerful monkeys, resembling mountains, commanded by that lord of monkeys, proceeded to all the regions of the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदो नाम लक्ष्मीवान्वालिसूनुर्महाबलः
प्रस्थितः कपिशार्दूलस्त्रिभागबलसंवृतः
verses.transliteration:
aṅgado nāma lakṣmīvānvālisūnurmahābalaḥ
prasthitaḥ kapiśārdūlastribhāgabalasaṁvṛtaḥ

translations.english: Own I am one of them And the beautiful and mighty son of Vali, by name Angada, has proceeded with three armies under him.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां नो विप्रनष्टानां विन्ध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे
भृशं शोकपरीतनामहोरात्रगणा गताः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ no vipranaṣṭānāṁ vindhye parvatasattame
bhṛśaṁ śokaparītanāmahorātragaṇā gatāḥ

translations.english: Many were the days and nights that we spent, overwhelmed with grief and having lost our way on that best of mountains Vindhya.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं कार्यनैराश्यात्कालस्यातिक्रमेण च
भयाच्च कपिराजस्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ kāryanairāśyātkālasyātikrameṇa ca
bhayācca kapirājasya prāṇāṁstyaktuṁ vyavasthitāḥ

translations.english: We gave up all our hopes for the accomplishment of our end and our appointed time was well-nigh spent. And in fear of that lord of monkeys we addressed ourselves to put au end to our live.

verses.sanskrit:
विचित्य वनदुर्गाणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च
अनासाद्य पदं देव्याः प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
vicitya vanadurgāṇi giriprasravaṇāni ca
anāsādya padaṁ devyāḥ prāṇāṁstyaktuṁ vyavasthitāḥ

translations.english: Ranging the mountain strongholds, rivers and fountains and not finding your reverence, we were ready to do away with our existence.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां नः स्वामिसंदेशान्निराशानां मुमूर्षताम्
कार्यहेतोरिवायातः शकुनिर्वीर्यवान्महान्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ naḥ svāmisaṁdeśānnirāśānāṁ mumūrṣatām
kāryahetorivāyātaḥ śakunirvīryavānmahān

translations.english: O Vaidehī, mentioning your rape, the destruction of Vāli in that way, our fastings and Jatayu's death. While we were thus waiting, ready for death and giving up all hopes for the fulfilment of our master's behest, there appeared, as if the cause of our success, the mighty and powerful vulture, the brother of Jațãyu, by name Sampati.

verses.sanskrit:
यवीयान्केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च विनाशितः
एतदाख्यातुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
yavīyānkena me bhrātā hataḥ kva ca vināśitaḥ
etadākhyātumicchāmi bhavadbhirvānarottamāḥ

translations.english: Hearing of the destruction of his brother, he in wrath, said-'By whom and where has my younger brother been killed? I wish to hear this from you, the foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदोऽकथयत्तस्य जनस्थाने महद्वधम्
रक्षसा भीमरूपेण त्वामुद्दिश्य यथातथम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgado'kathayattasya janasthāne mahadvadham
rakṣasā bhīmarūpeṇa tvāmuddiśya yathātatham

translations.english: Angada related to him verily Jațāyu's destruction at Janasthāna, for you, by that grimvisaged Rākṣasa.

verses.sanskrit:
जटायोस्तु वधं श्रुत्वा दुःखितः सोऽरुणात्मजः
त्वामाह स वरारोहे वसन्तीं रावणालये
verses.transliteration:
jaṭāyostu vadhaṁ śrutvā duḥkhitaḥ so'ruṇātmajaḥ
tvāmāha sa varārohe vasantīṁ rāvaṇālaye

translations.english: Hearing of Jatayu's death, Aruna's son became afflicted with sorrow and informed us, O you exquisitely fine damsel, of your stay in the abode of Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा संपातेः प्रीतिवर्धनम्
अङ्गदप्रमुखाः सर्वे ततः संप्रस्थिता वयम्
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहा हृष्टास्तुष्टाः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā saṁpāteḥ prītivardhanam
aṅgadapramukhāḥ sarve tataḥ saṁprasthitā vayam
tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhā hṛṣṭāstuṣṭāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of Sampāti, enhancing our delight, we all, headed by Angada, left that place. And leaping from the crest of Vindhya mountain we reached the excellent brink of the Ocean. Being greatly anxious to behold you and delighted, those plump monkeys headed by Angada, arrived at the banks of the main.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्का चापि मया रात्रौ प्रविष्टा राक्षसाकुला
रावणश्च मया दृष्टस्त्वं च शोकनिपीडिता
verses.transliteration:
laṅkā cāpi mayā rātrau praviṣṭā rākṣasākulā
rāvaṇaśca mayā dṛṣṭastvaṁ ca śokanipīḍitā

translations.english: And worked up with a strong desire to see you, they again engaged in anxious thought. And beholding the ocean, the monkey hosts lost their heart. And removing their fear, I leaped a hundred leagues across the deep and entered Lankā, at night, infested with demons. I have seen Rāvana, and you stricken with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथावृत्तमनिन्दिते
अभिभाषस्व मां देवि दूतो दाशरथेरहम्
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ yathāvṛttamanindite
abhibhāṣasva māṁ devi dūto dāśaratheraham

translations.english: O you of a blameless person, I have related all to you in regular order. Do you speak to me, O worshipful dame, I am Dasarathi's messenger.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं मां रामकृतोद्योगं त्वन्निमित्तमिहागतम्
सुग्रीव सचिवं देवि बुध्यस्व पवनात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ māṁ rāmakṛtodyogaṁ tvannimittamihāgatam
sugrīva sacivaṁ devi budhyasva pavanātmajam

translations.english: Do you know me as the Wind-god's son, the counsellor of Sugrīva, who am engaged in Rāma's service and have come here for you.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशली तव काकुत्स्थः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः
गुरोराराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणश्च सुलक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
kuśalī tava kākutsthaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṁ varaḥ
gurorārādhane yukto lakṣmaṇaśca sulakṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: It is all well with your Kākuthstha, the foremost of those using weapons, as well as with Laksmana, O worshipful dame, gifted with auspicious marks, engaged in the worship of his superiors and in the well being of your lord.

verses.sanskrit:
मयेयमसहायेन चरता कामरूपिणा
दक्षिणा दिगनुक्रान्ता त्वन्मार्गविचयैषिणा
verses.transliteration:
mayeyamasahāyena caratā kāmarūpiṇā
dakṣiṇā diganukrāntā tvanmārgavicayaiṣiṇā
