translations.english: And soon shall you behold the assembled heroic monkeys, endowed with the prowess of lions and tigers, and the splendour of the monarch of monkeys, and having nails and teeth for their arms.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु
नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामार्ये यूथान्यनेकशः
verses.transliteration:
śailāmbudanikāśānāṁ laṅkāmalayasānuṣu
nardatāṁ kapimukhyānāmārye yūthānyanekaśaḥ

translations.english: And you shall, O noble one, behold innumerable companies of choice monkeys, resembling hills and clouds, roaring on the plateaus of Malaya in Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु मर्मणि घोरेण ताडितो मन्मथेषुणा
न शर्म लभते रामः सिंहार्दित इव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu marmaṇi ghoreṇa tāḍito manmatheṣuṇā
na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṁhārdita iva dvipaḥ

translations.english: Like an elephant tormented by a lion, Rāma afflicted in the vitals by the dreadful shafts of Manmatha, dose not attain ease.

verses.sanskrit:
मा रुदो देवि शोकेन मा भूत्ते मनसोऽप्रियम्
शचीव पथ्या शक्रेण भर्त्रा नाथवती ह्यसि
verses.transliteration:
mā rudo devi śokena mā bhūtte manaso'priyam
śacīva pathyā śakreṇa bhartrā nāthavatī hyasi

translations.english: Do not weep, exalted one, in sorrow. Let not fear take possession of your heart! Even as Sacī meet with Sakra, shall you, O auspicious one, meet with your lord.

verses.sanskrit:
रामाद्विशिष्टः कोऽन्योऽस्ति कश्चित्सौमित्रिणा समः
अग्निमारुतकल्पौ तौ भ्रातरौ तव संश्रयौ
verses.transliteration:
rāmādviśiṣṭaḥ ko'nyo'sti kaścitsaumitriṇā samaḥ
agnimārutakalpau tau bhrātarau tava saṁśrayau

translations.english: Who is greater than Rāma? And who is equal to Saumitri? (i.e. Sumitra's son, Laksmana) And these brothers resembling Fire and the Wind, are your help.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्मिंश्चिरं वत्स्यसि देवि देशे; रक्षोगणैरध्युषितोऽतिरौद्रे
न ते चिरादागमनं प्रियस्य; क्षमस्व मत्संगमकालमात्रम्
verses.transliteration:
nāsmiṁściraṁ vatsyasi devi deśe; rakṣogaṇairadhyuṣito'tiraudre
na te cirādāgamanaṁ priyasya; kṣamasva matsaṁgamakālamātram

translations.english: O revered one, you will not have to dwell long in this extremely dreadful place inhabited by the Rākşasas. The arrival of your beloved one is not distant. Just remain expecting (as best you may), during the time that elapses between this and my meeting with Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य वायुसूनोर्महात्मनः
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं सीता सुरसुतोपमा
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu vacanaṁ tasya vāyusūnormahātmanaḥ
uvācātmahitaṁ vākyaṁ sītā surasutopamā

translations.english: Hearing the speech of the high-souled offspring of the Wind-god, Sītā resembling a daughter of the celestials, said in words fraught with her welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वां दृष्ट्वा प्रियवक्तारं संप्रहृष्यामि वानर
अर्धसंजातसस्येव वृष्टिं प्राप्य वसुंधरा
verses.transliteration:
tvāṁ dṛṣṭvā priyavaktāraṁ saṁprahṛṣyāmi vānara
ardhasaṁjātasasyeva vṛṣṭiṁ prāpya vasuṁdharā

translations.english: Even as the Earth with corn half-way towards harvest is gladdened on receipt of showers, have I, O monkey, been gladdened on seeing you that speakest sweetly.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गात्रैः शोकाभिकर्शितैः
संस्पृशेयं सकामाहं तथा कुरु दयां मयि
verses.transliteration:
yathā taṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ gātraiḥ śokābhikarśitaiḥ
saṁspṛśeyaṁ sakāmāhaṁ tathā kuru dayāṁ mayi

translations.english: Do you so dispense your kindness to me that, with my desire attained, I may touch that tigerlike one with my body reduced by grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिज्ञानं च रामस्य दत्तं हरिगणोत्तम
क्षिप्तामीषिकां काकस्य कोपादेकाक्षिशातनीम्
verses.transliteration:
abhijñānaṁ ca rāmasya dattaṁ harigaṇottama
kṣiptāmīṣikāṁ kākasya kopādekākṣiśātanīm

translations.english: O foremost of monkeys, present this sign to Rāma, and tell him also for a sign that he had in ire hurled the dart which destroyed a single eye of the crow.

verses.sanskrit:
मनःशिलायास्तिकलो गण्डपार्श्वे निवेशितः
त्वया प्रनष्टे तिलके तं किल स्मर्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
manaḥśilāyāstikalo gaṇḍapārśve niveśitaḥ
tvayā pranaṣṭe tilake taṁ kila smartumarhasi

translations.english: And tell him also, (Sītă wishes Hanuman to use her own language to Rama) 'On my (first) tilaka having been wiped out, you didst paint beside my cheek another cheek another made of red arsenic—this you You remember.

verses.sanskrit:
स वीर्यवान्कथं सीतां हृतां समनुमन्यसे
वसन्तीं रक्षसां मध्ये महेन्द्रवरुणोपम
verses.transliteration:
sa vīryavānkathaṁ sītāṁ hṛtāṁ samanumanyase
vasantīṁ rakṣasāṁ madhye mahendravaruṇopama

translations.english: Why, O you endowed with prowess, resembling Indra the Great or Varuņa, do you disregard the ravished Sītā, sitting in the midst of Raksasa?

verses.sanskrit:
एष चूडामणिर्दिव्यो मया सुपरिरक्षितः
एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ
verses.transliteration:
eṣa cūḍāmaṇirdivyo mayā suparirakṣitaḥ
etaṁ dṛṣṭvā prahṛṣyāmi vyasane tvāmivānagha

translations.english: This jewel for the head I had preserved with care. In my misfortune, O sinless one, I used to inspire cheerfulness by a sight a sight of this, resembling yourself.

verses.sanskrit:
एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान्मया ते वारिसंभवः
अतः परं न शक्ष्यामि जीवितुं शोकलालसा
verses.transliteration:
eṣa niryātitaḥ śrīmānmayā te vārisaṁbhavaḥ
ataḥ paraṁ na śakṣyāmi jīvituṁ śokalālasā

translations.english: This graceful water-sprung (gem) I part from. Hereafter, overwhelmed with grief, I shall not be able to live.

verses.sanskrit:
असह्यानि च दुःखानि वाचश्च हृदयच्छिदः
राक्षसीनां सुघोराणां त्वत्कृते मर्षयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
asahyāni ca duḥkhāni vācaśca hṛdayacchidaḥ
rākṣasīnāṁ sughorāṇāṁ tvatkṛte marṣayāmyaham

translations.english: For you only do I bear insufferable miseries, heart-cleaving speech, and companionship with Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
धारयिष्यामि मासं तु जीवितं शत्रुसूदन
मासादूर्ध्वं न जीविष्ये त्वया हीना नृपात्मज
verses.transliteration:
dhārayiṣyāmi māsaṁ tu jīvitaṁ śatrusūdana
māsādūrdhvaṁ na jīviṣye tvayā hīnā nṛpātmaja

translations.english: O destroyer of enemies, for a month longer will I maintain being. Beyond that, О king's son, bereft of you, I will not live.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरो राक्षसराजोऽयं दृष्टिश्च न सुखा मयि
त्वां च श्रुत्वा विपद्यन्तं न जीवेयमहं क्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
ghoro rākṣasarājo'yaṁ dṛṣṭiśca na sukhā mayi
tvāṁ ca śrutvā vipadyantaṁ na jīveyamahaṁ kṣaṇam

translations.english: This Raksasa king is dreadful. (This being so), if I hear you tarrying, I would not live for a moment.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साश्रुभाषितम्
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
vaidehyā vacanaṁ śrutvā karuṇaṁ sāśrubhāṣitam
athābravīnmahātejā hanumānmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Vaidehi's speech pathetic and uttered with tears, the highly energetic Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, said.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे
रामे शोकाभिभूते तु लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते
verses.transliteration:
tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape
rāme śokābhibhūte tu lakṣmaṇaḥ paritapyate

translations.english: My revered one, I swear to you by truth itself that Rāma neglect every business because of grief for you. And Rāma being over-whelmed with woe, Laksmana burn in grief.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टा कथंचिद्भवती न कालः परिशोचितुम्
इमं मुहूर्तं दुःखानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭā kathaṁcidbhavatī na kālaḥ pariśocitum
imaṁ muhūrtaṁ duḥkhānāmantaṁ drakṣyasi bhāmini

translations.english: Now that I have succeeded in seeing you after no end of ado, this is no time for lamentation. O fair one, this very moment you shall witness the end of your woe.

verses.sanskrit:
तावुभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रावनिन्दितौ
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
tāvubhau puruṣavyāghrau rājaputrāvaninditau
tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhau laṅkāṁ bhasmīkariṣyataḥ

translations.english: Those blameless princes-foremost of men, gathering courage from my sight of you shall reduce Lankā to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
हत्वा तु समरे क्रूरं रावणं सह बान्धवम्
राघवौ त्वां विशालाक्षि स्वां पुरीं प्रापयिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
hatvā tu samare krūraṁ rāvaṇaṁ saha bāndhavam
rāghavau tvāṁ viśālākṣi svāṁ purīṁ prāpayiṣyataḥ

translations.english: O you of expansive eyes, slaying in battle Rāvana along with his friends, Raghu's, sons shall take you back to their own palace.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते
प्रीतिसंजननं तस्य भूयस्त्वं दातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
yattu rāmo vijānīyādabhijñānamanindite
prītisaṁjananaṁ tasya bhūyastvaṁ dātumarhasi

translations.english: Now, O faultless lady, you ought to give me such a sign as Rāma shall certainly recognise, and as shall more please him by far.

verses.sanskrit:
साब्रवीद्दत्तमेवेह मयाभिज्ञानमुत्तमम्
एतदेव हि रामस्य दृष्ट्वा मत्केशभूषणम्
श्रद्धेयं हनुमन्वाक्यं तव वीर भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sābravīddattameveha mayābhijñānamuttamam
etadeva hi rāmasya dṛṣṭvā matkeśabhūṣaṇam
śraddheyaṁ hanumanvākyaṁ tava vīra bhaviṣyati

translations.english: “Ah!” (answered Sītā), "I have already furnished you with an excellent sign. This ornament,. Hanuman, when carefully examined by Rāma, O hero, shall render your words credible."

verses.sanskrit:
स तं मणिवरं गृह्य श्रीमान्प्लवगसत्तमः
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीं गमनायोपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ maṇivaraṁ gṛhya śrīmānplavagasattamaḥ
praṇamya śirasā devīṁ gamanāyopacakrame

translations.english: Thereupon, taking that best of gems, that graceful foremost of monkeys, bowing down the head to that exalted one, prepared to depart.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुत्पातकृतोत्साहमवेक्ष्य हरिपुंगवम्
वर्धमानं महावेगमुवाच जनकात्मजा
अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा
verses.transliteration:
tamutpātakṛtotsāhamavekṣya haripuṁgavam
vardhamānaṁ mahāvegamuvāca janakātmajā
aśrupūrṇamukhī dīnā bāṣpagadgadayā girā

translations.english: Seeing that monkey-leader intent upon leaping up, and surcharged with energy, with his person enlarged, Janaka's daughter, with a tearful countenance, spake in woe-begone guise, her accents choked with the vapour of grief,

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमन्सिंहसंकाशौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान्ब्रूया अनामयम्
verses.transliteration:
hanūmansiṁhasaṁkāśau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
sugrīvaṁ ca sahāmātyaṁ sarvānbrūyā anāmayam

translations.english: O Hanumān, communicate tidings of my good health to those lion-like brothers, Rāma and Laksmana, to' Sugriva along with his counsellors, and to all (the monkeys).

verses.sanskrit:
यथा च स महाबाहुर्मां तारयति राघवः
अस्माद्दुःखाम्बुसंरोधात्तत्समाधातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
yathā ca sa mahābāhurmāṁ tārayati rāghavaḥ
asmādduḥkhāmbusaṁrodhāttatsamādhātumarhasi

translations.english: And it behove you so to compass things that the mighty-armed Rāghava may rescue me from this sea of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
इमं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं; रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं; शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर
verses.transliteration:
imaṁ ca tīvraṁ mama śokavegaṁ; rakṣobhirebhiḥ paribhartsanaṁ ca
brūyāstu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṁ; śivaśca te'dhvāstu haripravīra

translations.english: Do you, going to Rāma, make known to him the fierce current of my grief, as well as the railing of these Rākşasas. Good fortune be your portion, you exceedingly heroic monkey!

verses.sanskrit:
स राजपुत्र्या प्रतिवेदितार्थः; कपिः कृतार्थः परिहृष्टचेताः
तदल्पशेषं प्रसमीक्ष्य कार्यं; दिशं ह्युदीचीं मनसा जगाम
verses.transliteration:
sa rājaputryā prativeditārthaḥ; kapiḥ kṛtārthaḥ parihṛṣṭacetāḥ
tadalpaśeṣaṁ prasamīkṣya kāryaṁ; diśaṁ hyudīcīṁ manasā jagāma

translations.english: Thus furnished with the intentions of the princess, the monkey, having gained his object, and, growing exceedingly exhilarated in his heart, reviewed the small work that yet remained for him, became bent upon proceeding to the north.

verses.sanskrit:
स च वाग्भिः प्रशस्ताभिर्गमिष्यन्पूजितस्तया
तस्माद्देशादपक्रम्य चिन्तयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
sa ca vāgbhiḥ praśastābhirgamiṣyanpūjitastayā
tasmāddeśādapakramya cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: Having been honoured by her (Sītā) in excellent words, the monkey proceeding, left that place, thinking.

verses.sanskrit:
अल्पशेषमिदं कार्यं दृष्टेयमसितेक्षणा
त्रीनुपायानतिक्रम्य चतुर्थ इह दृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
alpaśeṣamidaṁ kāryaṁ dṛṣṭeyamasitekṣaṇā
trīnupāyānatikramya caturtha iha dṛśyate

translations.english: A small work it is that remains. Beheld have I this dark-eyed lady. Passing by three means, I see that I shali have to resort to the fourth.

verses.sanskrit:
न साम रक्षःसु गुणाय कल्पते; न दनमर्थोपचितेषु वर्तते
न भेदसाध्या बलदर्पिता जनाः; पराक्रमस्त्वेष ममेह रोचते
verses.transliteration:
na sāma rakṣaḥsu guṇāya kalpate; na danamarthopaciteṣu vartate
na bhedasādhyā baladarpitā janāḥ; parākramastveṣa mameha rocate

translations.english: No treaty with Rākşasa can answer the end. Neither can gifts prevail with the wealthy. Nor is it possible to sow dissensions among persons proud of their strength. Then, display of prowess appear to me applicable in this case.

verses.sanskrit:
न चास्य कार्यस्य पराक्रमादृते; विनिश्चयः कश्चिदिहोपपद्यते
हृतप्रवीरास्तु रणे हि राक्षसाः; कथंचिदीयुर्यदिहाद्य मार्दवम्
verses.transliteration:
na cāsya kāryasya parākramādṛte; viniścayaḥ kaścidihopapadyate
hṛtapravīrāstu raṇe hi rākṣasāḥ; kathaṁcidīyuryadihādya mārdavam

translations.english: Without resorting to prowess, way find I none for ensuring success in this matter. If the Rākşasa find their foremost heroes fallen in battle, they may temper their (martial ardour).

verses.sanskrit:
कार्ये कर्मणि निर्दिष्टो यो बहून्यपि साधयेत्
पूर्वकार्यविरोधेन स कार्यं कर्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
kārye karmaṇi nirdiṣṭo yo bahūnyapi sādhayet
pūrvakāryavirodhena sa kāryaṁ kartumarhati

translations.english: He that, having compassed his (principal) purpose, accomplishes many more without marring the prime one, is entitled to act.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्येकः साधको हेतुः स्वल्पस्यापीह कर्मणः
यो ह्यर्थं बहुधा वेद स समर्थोऽर्थसाधने
verses.transliteration:
na hyekaḥ sādhako hetuḥ svalpasyāpīha karmaṇaḥ
yo hyarthaṁ bahudhā veda sa samartho'rthasādhane

translations.english: He that dose a small work, is certainly not a worker, he it is that know to bring about success in diverse ways, is along capable of securing the same. (The commentator explains this passage thus:"He that by great pains accomplishes a small work, cannot be a great actor; but he that bring about his end in a variety of ways through the minimum of effort, in the actor.")

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव तावत्कृतनिश्चयो ह्यहं; यदि व्रजेयं प्लवगेश्वरालयम्
परात्मसंमर्द विशेषतत्त्ववि;त्ततः कृतं स्यान्मम भर्तृशासनम्
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva tāvatkṛtaniścayo hyahaṁ; yadi vrajeyaṁ plavageśvarālayam
parātmasaṁmarda viśeṣatattvavi;ttataḥ kṛtaṁ syānmama bhartṛśāsanam

translations.english: Although my sole commission was to effect this much, (i.e. see Sita) yet if I repair to the abode of the lord of monkeys after having ascertained the strength of our ownselves and that of the foe in the field, then I shall have done the mandate of my master.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं नु खल्वद्य भवेत्सुखागतं; प्रसह्य युद्धं मम राक्षसैः सह
तथैव खल्वात्मबलं च सारव;त्समानयेन्मां च रणे दशाननः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ nu khalvadya bhavetsukhāgataṁ; prasahya yuddhaṁ mama rākṣasaiḥ saha
tathaiva khalvātmabalaṁ ca sārava;tsamānayenmāṁ ca raṇe daśānanaḥ

translations.english: How can my arrival (at this place) be made to bring forth good fruit? How can I forcibly bring on engagement with the Rākşasas? And how can the Ten-necked one in battle be made to form a just estimate of the respective strength of myself and his forces?

verses.sanskrit:
इदं विध्वंसयिष्यामि शुष्कं वनमिवानलः
अस्मिन्भग्ने ततः कोपं करिष्यति स रावणः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ vidhvaṁsayiṣyāmi śuṣkaṁ vanamivānalaḥ
asminbhagne tataḥ kopaṁ kariṣyati sa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: This grove of the fell (fiend) resembling Nandana itself, containing various trees and plants, and captivating to eye and heart, will i destroy; even as fire destroy a dry wood. This grove being ravaged, Rāvana shall get into a fury.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महत्साश्वमहारथद्विपं; बलं समानेष्वपि राक्षसाधिपः
त्रिशूलकालायसपट्टिशायुधं; ततो महद्युद्धमिदं भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tato mahatsāśvamahārathadvipaṁ; balaṁ samāneṣvapi rākṣasādhipaḥ
triśūlakālāyasapaṭṭiśāyudhaṁ; tato mahadyuddhamidaṁ bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Then the Raksasa monarch shall summon up an army consisting of herse, elephants, and mighty cars, equipped with tridents, iron axes and other arms, and mighty shall be the encounter that shall take place.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु तैः संयति चण्डविक्रमैः; समेत्य रक्षोभिरसंगविक्रमः
निहत्य तद्रावणचोदितं बलं; सुखं गमिष्यामि कपीश्वरालयम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu taiḥ saṁyati caṇḍavikramaiḥ; sametya rakṣobhirasaṁgavikramaḥ
nihatya tadrāvaṇacoditaṁ balaṁ; sukhaṁ gamiṣyāmi kapīśvarālayam

translations.english: And I with unpaired prowess battling with those terrific Rākşasa, and annihilating that host despatched by Rāvana, shall merrily journey to the abode of the monkey king.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मारुतवत्क्रुद्धो मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः
ऊरुवेगेन महता द्रुमान्क्षेप्तुमथारभत्
verses.transliteration:
tato mārutavatkruddho mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ
ūruvegena mahatā drumānkṣeptumathārabhat

translations.english: Then furious like the Wind, the offspring of the Wind-god possessed of dreadful prowess set about knocking down the trees with impetuous violence.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्धनुमान्वीरो बभञ्ज प्रमदावनम्
मत्तद्विजसमाघुष्टं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaddhanumānvīro babhañja pramadāvanam
mattadvijasamāghuṣṭaṁ nānādrumalatāyutam

translations.english: Then that hero, Hanumān, devastated that garden of the damsels, resounding with the roars of mad elephants, and filled with diverse trees and shrubs.

verses.sanskrit:
लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्च नाशितै;र्महोरगैर्व्यालमृगैश्च निर्धुतैः
शिलागृहैरुन्मथितैस्तथा गृहैः; प्रनष्टरूपं तदभून्महद्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
latāgṛhaiścitragṛhaiśca nāśitai;rmahoragairvyālamṛgaiśca nirdhutaiḥ
śilāgṛhairunmathitaistathā gṛhaiḥ; pranaṣṭarūpaṁ tadabhūnmahadvanam

translations.english: And that magnificent wood, with its arbours and its picture-galleries destroyed, and its ferocious animals, beasts and birds crying in distressful accents, and its rocky structures and other mansions broken down, was bereft of its loveliness.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य कृत्वार्थपतेर्महाकपि;र्महद्व्यलीकं मनसो महात्मनः
युयुत्सुरेको बहुभिर्महाबलैः; श्रिया ज्वलंस्तोरणमाश्रितः कपिः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya kṛtvārthapatermahākapi;rmahadvyalīkaṁ manaso mahātmanaḥ
yuyutsureko bahubhirmahābalaiḥ; śriyā jvalaṁstoraṇamāśritaḥ kapiḥ

translations.english: Then having done what was wondrous disagreeable to the mind of the magnanimous lord of the world, that monkey desirous of coping alone with a vast host, stood by the main entrance, flaming in effulgence.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पक्षिनिनादेन वृक्षभङ्गस्वनेन च
बभूवुस्त्राससंभ्रान्ताः सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pakṣininādena vṛkṣabhaṅgasvanena ca
babhūvustrāsasaṁbhrāntāḥ sarve laṅkānivāsinaḥ

translations.english: Then on account of the cries of birds and the sounds of breaking trees, all the denizons of Lankā were seized with trepidation in consequence of fright.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्रुताश्च भयत्रस्ता विनेदुर्मृगपक्षुणः
रक्षसां च निमित्तानि क्रूराणि प्रतिपेदिरे
verses.transliteration:
vidrutāśca bhayatrastā vinedurmṛgapakṣuṇaḥ
rakṣasāṁ ca nimittāni krūrāṇi pratipedire

translations.english: And agitated with fear, birds and beasts hurried (on all sides); and omens boding evil to the, Raksasas, began to appear (everywhere).

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गतायां निद्रायां राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः
तद्वनं ददृशुर्भग्नं तं च वीरं महाकपिम्
verses.transliteration:
tato gatāyāṁ nidrāyāṁ rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ
tadvanaṁ dadṛśurbhagnaṁ taṁ ca vīraṁ mahākapim

translations.english: And grim-visaged Rākṣasīs, awaking from their sleep, saw that wood devastated, and that heroic mighty monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
स ता दृष्ट्व महाबाहुर्महासत्त्वो महाबलः
चकार सुमहद्रूपं राक्षसीनां भयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tā dṛṣṭva mahābāhurmahāsattvo mahābalaḥ
cakāra sumahadrūpaṁ rākṣasīnāṁ bhayāvaham

translations.english: And observing them, that mighty-armed and powerful monkey endowed with immense strength, magnified his dimension, capable of striking terror into the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं गिरिसंकाशमतिकायं महाबलम्
राक्षस्यो वानरं दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुर्जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ girisaṁkāśamatikāyaṁ mahābalam
rākṣasyo vānaraṁ dṛṣṭvā papracchurjanakātmajām

translations.english: Beholding that exceedingly strong monkey resembling a mountain, the Räkşasīs asked Janaka's daughter, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
आचक्ष्व नो विशालाक्षि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्
संवादमसितापाङ्गे त्वया किं कृतवानयम्
verses.transliteration:
ācakṣva no viśālākṣi mā bhūtte subhage bhayam
saṁvādamasitāpāṅge tvayā kiṁ kṛtavānayam

translations.english: Who is this? And whence, and wherefore has he come here? And why did he carry on converse with you? Tell us this, you of expansive eyes. O lucky one, entertain no fear. And, O you having eyes with dark outer corners, what is the talk that this one has held with you?

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीत्तदा साध्वी सीता सर्वाङ्गशोभना
रक्षसां कामरूपाणां विज्ञाने मम का गतिः
verses.transliteration:
athābravīttadā sādhvī sītā sarvāṅgaśobhanā
rakṣasāṁ kāmarūpāṇāṁ vijñāne mama kā gatiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, the chaste Sītā, having all her parts perfect, answered, “What is my power to read Rākṣasas capable of wearing forms at will? ”

verses.sanskrit:
यूयमेवास्य जानीत योऽयं यद्वा करिष्यति
अहिरेव अहेः पादान्विजानाति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
yūyamevāsya jānīta yo'yaṁ yadvā kariṣyati
ahireva aheḥ pādānvijānāti na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: You know who he is and what he does. Serpents, without doubt, know the way of serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमप्यस्य भीतास्मि नैनं जानामि कोऽन्वयम्
वेद्मि राक्षसमेवैनं कामरूपिणमागतम्
verses.transliteration:
ahamapyasya bhītāsmi nainaṁ jānāmi ko'nvayam
vedmi rākṣasamevainaṁ kāmarūpiṇamāgatam

translations.english: And, furthermore, I am very much frightened, nor know I who that one is. I take him to be a Rākşasa, who has come here through his capacity to put on any shape.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यो विद्रुता द्रुतम्
स्थिताः काश्चिद्गताः काश्चिद्रावणाय निवेदितुम्
verses.transliteration:
vaidehyā vacanaṁ śrutvā rākṣasyo vidrutā drutam
sthitāḥ kāścidgatāḥ kāścidrāvaṇāya niveditum

translations.english: Hearing Vaidehi's words, the Raksasis swiftly took to their heels. Some remained, and some departed to inform Rāvana of the matter.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य समीपे तु राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः
विरूपं वानरं भीममाख्यातुमुपचक्रमुः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya samīpe tu rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ
virūpaṁ vānaraṁ bhīmamākhyātumupacakramuḥ

translations.english: And before Rāvana, the Rākṣasīs of deformed visage informed him of the hideous and dreadful monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकवनिका मध्ये राजन्भीमवपुः कपिः
सीतया कृतसंवादस्तिष्ठत्यमितविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
aśokavanikā madhye rājanbhīmavapuḥ kapiḥ
sītayā kṛtasaṁvādastiṣṭhatyamitavikramaḥ

translations.english: O king, in the heart of the aśoka wood there is a monkey of a terrific body, who, possessed of immeasurable might, stay, after having carried on a conversation with Jānakī.

verses.sanskrit:
न च तं जानकी सीता हरिं हरिणलोचणा
अस्माभिर्बहुधा पृष्टा निवेदयितुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
na ca taṁ jānakī sītā hariṁ hariṇalocaṇā
asmābhirbahudhā pṛṣṭā nivedayitumicchati

translations.english: Nor, albeit questioned by us many a time and oft, dose Janaka's daughter, Sītā, having the eyes of a deer, intend to tell us who the monkey is.

verses.sanskrit:
वासवस्य भवेद्दूतो दूतो वैश्रवणस्य वा
प्रेषितो वापि रामेण सीतान्वेषणकाङ्क्षया
verses.transliteration:
vāsavasya bhaveddūto dūto vaiśravaṇasya vā
preṣito vāpi rāmeṇa sītānveṣaṇakāṅkṣayā

translations.english: He may be the emissary of Vāsava, or of Vaiśravaņa; or he may have been sent by Rāma himself from eagerness to get at the whereabouts of Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
न तत्र कश्चिदुद्देशो यस्तेन न विनाशितः
यत्र सा जानकी सीता स तेन न विनाशितः
verses.transliteration:
na tatra kaściduddeśo yastena na vināśitaḥ
yatra sā jānakī sītā sa tena na vināśitaḥ

translations.english: And he it is that, wearing a wonderful form, has destroyed your charming arbour of the interior, filled with beasts of various kinds-And quarter there is none which has not been destroyer by him; and only that place where the exalted Jänakī is, remain uninjured by him.

verses.sanskrit:
जानकीरक्षणार्थं वा श्रमाद्वा नोपलभ्यते
अथ वा कः श्रमस्तस्य सैव तेनाभिरक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
jānakīrakṣaṇārthaṁ vā śramādvā nopalabhyate
atha vā kaḥ śramastasya saiva tenābhirakṣitā

translations.english: Whether for preserving Jānakī, or from fatigue—it dose not appear. But what is his fatigue? She it is that has been preserved by him.

verses.sanskrit:
चारुपल्लवपत्राढ्यं यं सीता स्वयमास्थिता
प्रवृद्धः शिंशपावृक्षः स च तेनाभिरक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
cārupallavapatrāḍhyaṁ yaṁ sītā svayamāsthitā
pravṛddhaḥ śiṁśapāvṛkṣaḥ sa ca tenābhirakṣitaḥ

translations.english: And that overgrown Sinsapă tree, affluent with elegant foliage, under which Sītā herself has (always rested), has been spared by him.

verses.sanskrit:
मनःपरिगृहीतां तां तव रक्षोगणेश्वर
कः सीतामभिभाषेत यो न स्यात्त्यक्तजीवितः
verses.transliteration:
manaḥparigṛhītāṁ tāṁ tava rakṣogaṇeśvara
kaḥ sītāmabhibhāṣeta yo na syāttyaktajīvitaḥ

translations.english: It behove you to order sharp chastisement to be inflicted on that one of a fierce form, who, having carried on converse with Sītā, has laid your wood waste. Who, O Sovereign of the Rākşasas, that has not his life served from him, converse with Sītā, who has captivated your heart?"

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
हुतागिरिव जज्वाल कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasīnāṁ vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
hutāgiriva jajvāla kopasaṁvartitekṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the speeches of the Rākṣasīs, Rāvaņa, lord of Raksasas, with his eyes rolling in rage, flamed up like the fire of a funeral pyre.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मनः सदृशाञ्शूरान्किंकरान्नाम राक्षसान्
व्यादिदेश महातेजा निग्रहार्थं हनूमतः
verses.transliteration:
ātmanaḥ sadṛśāñśūrānkiṁkarānnāma rākṣasān
vyādideśa mahātejā nigrahārthaṁ hanūmataḥ

translations.english: And that highly energetic one ordered his heroic servants, resembling himself, to punish Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं किंकराणां तरस्विनाम्
निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्कूटमुद्गरपाणयः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmaśītisāhasraṁ kiṁkarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
niryayurbhavanāttasmātkūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ

translations.english: And from that mansion speedily issued eighty thousand of those retainers, carrying in their hands maces and mallets. (Kūța-hammer. The commentator, however, says that it means a weapon resembling a hammer.)

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरा महादंष्ट्रा घोररूपा महाबलाः
युद्धाभिमनसः सर्वे हनूमद्ग्रहणोन्मुखाः
verses.transliteration:
mahodarā mahādaṁṣṭrā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ
yuddhābhimanasaḥ sarve hanūmadgrahaṇonmukhāḥ

translations.english: Having huge bellies, and large teeth, of dreadful form, and possessed of unwieldy strength, all eager to engage in the conflict and take Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
ते कपिं तं समासाद्य तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्
अभिपेतुर्महावेगाः पतङ्गा इव पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
te kapiṁ taṁ samāsādya toraṇasthamavasthitam
abhipeturmahāvegāḥ pataṅgā iva pāvakam

translations.english: Having come near that monkey staying at the main entrance, those swelling spirits rushed on, even as insects rush into a flame.

verses.sanskrit:
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः
आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं शरैरादित्यसंनिभैः
verses.transliteration:
te gadābhirvicitrābhiḥ parighaiḥ kāñcanāṅgadaiḥ
ājaghnurvānaraśreṣṭhaṁ śarairādityasaṁnibhaiḥ

translations.english: And equipped with variegated maces, and bludgeons, and golden Angadas, (A bracelet worn on the upper arm) and arrows resembling the Sun, they approached that foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमानपि तेजस्वी श्रीमान्पर्वतसंनिभः
क्षितावाविध्य लाङ्गूलं ननाद च महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
hanūmānapi tejasvī śrīmānparvatasaṁnibhaḥ
kṣitāvāvidhya lāṅgūlaṁ nanāda ca mahāsvanam

translations.english: And the graceful and energetic Hanumān also, resembling a hill, flourishing his tail over the ground, sent up tremendous roars.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य संनादशब्देन तेऽभवन्भयशङ्किताः
ददृशुश्च हनूमन्तं संध्यामेघमिवोन्नतम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya saṁnādaśabdena te'bhavanbhayaśaṅkitāḥ
dadṛśuśca hanūmantaṁ saṁdhyāmeghamivonnatam

translations.english: They were struck with affright at his roars; and they beheld Hanumān elevated as an evening cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वामिसंदेशनिःशङ्कास्ततस्ते राक्षसाः कपिम्
चित्रैः प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
svāmisaṁdeśaniḥśaṅkāstataste rākṣasāḥ kapim
citraiḥ praharaṇairbhīmairabhipetustatastataḥ

translations.english: And now knowing for certain that the monkey had been despatched by his master, the Rākṣasas commenced assailing him with various kinds of dire arms.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः परिवृतः शूरैः सर्वतः स महाबलः
आससादायसं भीमं परिघं तोरणाश्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ sarvataḥ sa mahābalaḥ
āsasādāyasaṁ bhīmaṁ parighaṁ toraṇāśritam

translations.english: Environed on all sides by those heroes, that exceedingly powerful one, staying by the main entrance, look up a terrific bolt.

verses.sanskrit: स तं परिघमादाय जघान रजनीचरान्
verses.transliteration: sa taṁ parighamādāya jaghāna rajanīcarān

translations.english: And taking that bolt, like Vinatā's offspring handing a darting serpent, he slew those rangers of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
स पन्नगमिवादाय स्फुरन्तं विनतासुतः
विचचाराम्बरे वीरः परिगृह्य च मारुतिः
verses.transliteration:
sa pannagamivādāya sphurantaṁ vinatāsutaḥ
vicacārāmbare vīraḥ parigṛhya ca mārutiḥ

translations.english: And grasping (the bolt), the Wind-god' son began to range the welkin and destroy (the Rākşasas) like the thousand-eyed (deity) slaughtering Daityas with his thunder-bold.

verses.sanskrit:
स हत्वा राक्षसान्वीरः किंकरान्मारुतात्मजः
युद्धाकाङ्क्षी पुनर्वीरस्तोरणं समुपस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
sa hatvā rākṣasānvīraḥ kiṁkarānmārutātmajaḥ
yuddhākāṅkṣī punarvīrastoraṇaṁ samupasthitaḥ

translations.english: And having slain those Rākṣasas, who where the retainers of Rāvaņa, the heroic offspring of the Wind-god-foremost of heroes-desirous of fight, stood at the gate.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तस्माद्भयान्मुक्ताः कतिचित्तत्र राक्षसाः
निहतान्किंकरान्सर्वान्रावणाय न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
tatastasmādbhayānmuktāḥ katicittatra rākṣasāḥ
nihatānkiṁkarānsarvānrāvaṇāya nyavedayan

translations.english: Then certain Räkşasas, getting off from the field in fear, informed Rāvana of the destruction of all his servants.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसानां निहतं महाबलं; निशम्य राजा परिवृत्तलोचनः
समादिदेशाप्रतिमं पराक्रमे; प्रहस्तपुत्रं समरे सुदुर्जयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasānāṁ nihataṁ mahābalaṁ; niśamya rājā parivṛttalocanaḥ
samādideśāpratimaṁ parākrame; prahastaputraṁ samare sudurjayam

translations.english: Hearing that a mighty host of the Rākṣasas had been slain, the king, with his eyes whirling in ire, ordered Prahasta's son of incomparable prowess, and invincible in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स किंकरान्हत्वा हनूमान्ध्यानमास्थितः
वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः
तस्मात्प्रासादमप्येवमिमं विध्वंसयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa kiṁkarānhatvā hanūmāndhyānamāsthitaḥ
vanaṁ bhagnaṁ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ
tasmātprāsādamapyevamimaṁ vidhvaṁsayāmyaham

translations.english: Having slaughtered the servants, Hanumān, having reflected awhile, thought, “I have broken down the wood; but have not destroyed the edifice dedicated to the deities of the Rākşasas.”

verses.sanskrit:
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमान्मनसा दर्शयन्बलम्
चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्
आरुरोह हरिश्रेष्ठो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
iti saṁcintya hanumānmanasā darśayanbalam
caityaprāsādamāplutya meruśṛṅgamivonnatam
āruroha hariśreṣṭho hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, this very day will I demolish this structure. Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, displaying his strength, bounded to the Caitya (A building designed for deities) building, elevated like a summit of Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रधृष्य च दुर्धर्षश्चैत्यप्रासादमुन्नतम्
हनूमान्प्रज्वलँल्लक्ष्म्या पारियात्रोपमोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁpradhṛṣya ca durdharṣaścaityaprāsādamunnatam
hanūmānprajvala̐llakṣmyā pāriyātropamo'bhavat

translations.english: Having broken down that superb edifice, the irrepressible Hanuman, flaming in auspiciousness, resembled (the mountain) Pāriyatra.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूत्वा तु महाकायो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
धृष्टमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūtvā tu mahākāyo hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
dhṛṣṭamāsphoṭayāmāsa laṅkāṁ śabdena pūrayan

translations.english: And attaining mighty proportions, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, brandished his tail, filling Lankā with sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता श्रोत्रघातिना
पेतुर्विहंगा गगनादुच्चैश्चेदमघोषयत्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāsphoṭitaśabdena mahatā śrotraghātinā
peturvihaṁgā gaganāduccaiścedamaghoṣayat

translations.english: At the sounds of his flourishing, as well as with those resounding ones set up by himself, birds began to drop down from the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा विमानस्थश्चैत्यस्थान्हरिपुंगवः
ननाद भीमनिर्ह्रादो रक्षसां जनयन्भयम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā vimānasthaścaityasthānharipuṁgavaḥ
nanāda bhīmanirhrādo rakṣasāṁ janayanbhayam

translations.english: Having spoken thus, that one of a prodigious person, seated on the Caitya, emitted tremendous roars, striking terror into the Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन महता चैत्यपालाः शतं ययुः
गृहीत्वा विविधानस्त्रान्प्रासान्खड्गान्परश्वधान्
विसृजन्तो महाक्षया मारुतिं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena mahatā caityapālāḥ śataṁ yayuḥ
gṛhītvā vividhānastrānprāsānkhaḍgānparaśvadhān
visṛjanto mahākṣayā mārutiṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: In consequence of that mighty cry, an hundred guards attached to the Caitya sallied out, taking various weapons-bearded darts, scimitars and axes; and they surrounded the Wind-god's offspring, as he went on increasing his body.

verses.sanskrit:
आवर्त इव गङ्गायास्तोयस्य विपुलो महान्
परिक्षिप्य हरिश्रेष्ठं स बभौ रक्षसां गणः
verses.transliteration:
āvarta iva gaṅgāyāstoyasya vipulo mahān
parikṣipya hariśreṣṭhaṁ sa babhau rakṣasāṁ gaṇaḥ

translations.english: Those numbers of Rākşasa, encountering that best of monkeys, resumbled an extensive and mighty whirlpool in the Gangā.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रासादस्य महांस्तस्य स्तम्भं हेमपरिष्कृतम्
उत्पाटयित्वा वेगेन हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
ततस्तं भ्रामयामास शतधारं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
prāsādasya mahāṁstasya stambhaṁ hemapariṣkṛtam
utpāṭayitvā vegena hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
tatastaṁ bhrāmayāmāsa śatadhāraṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, the Wind-god's son, the mighty Hanumān, (Mārutatmaja-son to the Wind-god, left out on the score of redundency) waxing enraged, violently uprooting a huge pillar of the edifice, plated with gold, and having an hundred borders, began to whirl it (in the air). (The reader is powerfully reminded of a like feat of Manoah's son-'the Herculean Samson') And the fire generated there thus, burnt down the entire edifice.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसशतं हत्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान्
अन्तरिक्षस्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasaśataṁ hatvā vajreṇendra ivāsurān
antarikṣasthitaḥ śrīmānidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing that edifice in flames, the graceful monkey-leader, having slain having slain the hundred Rākṣasas, like Indra slaying Asuras with this thunderbolt, remaining in the sky, said,

verses.sanskrit:
मादृशानां सहस्राणि विसृष्टानि महात्मनाम्
बलिनां वानरेन्द्राणां सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
mādṛśānāṁ sahasrāṇi visṛṣṭāni mahātmanām
balināṁ vānarendrāṇāṁ sugrīvavaśavartinām

translations.english: Thousands of strong, high-souled and foremost monkeys like myself, having been created, and remaining under the command of Sugriva, including ourselves as well as other monkeys—are ranging all over the world.

verses.sanskrit:
शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटीभिरयुतैरपि
आगमिष्यति सुग्रीवः सर्वेषां वो निषूदनः
verses.transliteration:
śataiḥ śatasahasraiśca koṭībhirayutairapi
āgamiṣyati sugrīvaḥ sarveṣāṁ vo niṣūdanaḥ

translations.english: Surrounded with monkeys of this sort, having nails and teeth for their arms, in hundreds and thousands and koțis and ayutas, come our Sugrīva, the slayer of all (foes).

verses.sanskrit:
नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न यूयं न च रावणः
यस्मादिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन बद्धं वैरं महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
neyamasti purī laṅkā na yūyaṁ na ca rāvaṇaḥ
yasmādikṣvākunāthena baddhaṁ vairaṁ mahātmanā

translations.english: Neither this city of Lanka, nor you, nor yet Rāvaņa, shall exist, having created hostility with that high-souled hero of the Ikşvāku race.

verses.sanskrit:
संदिष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रहस्तस्य सुतो बली
जम्बुमाली महादंष्ट्रो निर्जगाम धनुर्धरः
verses.transliteration:
saṁdiṣṭo rākṣasendreṇa prahastasya suto balī
jambumālī mahādaṁṣṭro nirjagāma dhanurdharaḥ

translations.english: Commanded by the lord of Rākṣasas, Prahasta's son, the powerful Jambumali, having large teeth, went out bow in hand.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरः स्रग्वी रुचिरकुण्डलः
महान्विवृत्तनयनश्चण्डः समरदुर्जयः
verses.transliteration:
raktamālyāmbaradharaḥ sragvī rucirakuṇḍalaḥ
mahānvivṛttanayanaścaṇḍaḥ samaradurjayaḥ

translations.english: He wore a red wreath and attire, with a rings; and he was huge, and terrible, with his eyes whirling, invincible in encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
धनुः शक्रधनुः प्रख्यं महद्रुचिरसायकम्
विस्फारयाणो वेगेन वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
dhanuḥ śakradhanuḥ prakhyaṁ mahadrucirasāyakam
visphārayāṇo vegena vajrāśanisamasvanam

translations.english: He impetuously stretched a graceful bow, resembling the bow of Sakra, and roaring like vajra and the thounderbolt. (For distinction between the two, vide ante).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य विस्फारघोषेण धनुषो महता दिशः
प्रदिशश्च नभश्चैव सहसा समपूर्यत
verses.transliteration:
tasya visphāraghoṣeṇa dhanuṣo mahatā diśaḥ
pradiśaśca nabhaścaiva sahasā samapūryata

translations.english: The entire welkin, and all sides and quarters, were suddenly filled with the mighty sounds of that bow as it was being stretched.

verses.sanskrit:
रथेन खरयुक्तेन तमागतमुदीक्ष्य सः
हनूमान्वेगसंपन्नो जहर्ष च ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
rathena kharayuktena tamāgatamudīkṣya saḥ
hanūmānvegasaṁpanno jaharṣa ca nanāda ca

translations.english: Seeing him approaching in a car yoked with asses, Hanumān endowed with vigour both rejoiced and shouted.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तोरणविटङ्कस्थं हनूमन्तं महाकपिम्
जम्बुमाली महाबाहुर्विव्याध निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ toraṇaviṭaṅkasthaṁ hanūmantaṁ mahākapim
jambumālī mahābāhurvivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, the highly energetic Jambumālī pierced with whetted shafts that mighty monkey, Hanumāna, who as seated on an awry plank at the gate serving as a perch for pigeons. (This is all that I can make of the commentator's gloss on toranavitanka.)

verses.sanskrit:
अर्धचन्द्रेण वदने शिरस्येकेन कर्णिना
बाह्वोर्विव्याध नाराचैर्दशभिस्तं कपीश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
ardhacandreṇa vadane śirasyekena karṇinā
bāhvorvivyādha nārācairdaśabhistaṁ kapīśvaram

translations.english: He pierced that lord of monkey's face with half-moon (shaped) arrows, his head with one having its head made like a hook and his arms with ten nārācas. (Iron arrows).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तच्छुशुभे ताम्रं शरेणाभिहतं मुखम्
शरदीवाम्बुजं फुल्लं विद्धं भास्कररश्मिना
verses.transliteration:
tasya tacchuśubhe tāmraṁ śareṇābhihataṁ mukham
śaradīvāmbujaṁ phullaṁ viddhaṁ bhāskararaśminā

translations.english: And pierced by the arrows, his coppery face looked beautiful like a blown autumnal red lotus shot at by the solar rays.

verses.sanskrit:
चुकोप बाणाभिहतो राक्षसस्य महाकपिः
ततः पार्श्वेऽतिविपुलां ददर्श महतीं शिलाम्
verses.transliteration:
cukopa bāṇābhihato rākṣasasya mahākapiḥ
tataḥ pārśve'tivipulāṁ dadarśa mahatīṁ śilām

translations.english: And his naturally red countenance being painted with blood, looked lovely like a majestic red lotus in the sky, washed with the honey of the red Asoka. Wounded by the shafts, the redoubted grew enraged. And he espied a huge and gigantic crag beside him. Thereat, at once uprooting it, that one endowed with celerity and strength hurled it (at his foe).

verses.sanskrit:
विपन्नं कर्म तद्दृष्ट्वा हनूमांश्चण्डविक्रमः
सालं विपुलमुत्पाट्य भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
vipannaṁ karma taddṛṣṭvā hanūmāṁścaṇḍavikramaḥ
sālaṁ vipulamutpāṭya bhrāmayāmāsa vīryavān

translations.english: And the enraged Rākṣasa opposed it by ten shafts. Witnessing his action rendered fruitless, the energetic Hanumān of terrific prowess, uprooting a large Sāla, began to whirl it in the air).

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रामयन्तं कपिं दृष्ट्वा सालवृक्षं महाबलम्
चिक्षेप सुबहून्बाणाञ्जम्बुमाली महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
bhrāmayantaṁ kapiṁ dṛṣṭvā sālavṛkṣaṁ mahābalam
cikṣepa subahūnbāṇāñjambumālī mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the exceedingly strong monkey whirling the Sāla tree, the highly powerful Jambumālī dischanged a many shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
सालं चतुर्भिर्चिच्छेद वानरं पञ्चभिर्भुजे
उरस्येकेन बाणेन दशभिस्तु स्तनान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
sālaṁ caturbhirciccheda vānaraṁ pañcabhirbhuje
urasyekena bāṇena daśabhistu stanāntare

translations.english: He severed the Sāla by means of four shafts, and wounded the monkey in the arm with five, in the chest, with one, and with ten, between the teast.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरैः पूरिततनुः क्रोधेन महता वृतः
तमेव परिघं गृह्य भ्रामयामास वेगितः
verses.transliteration:
sa śaraiḥ pūritatanuḥ krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ
tameva parighaṁ gṛhya bhrāmayāmāsa vegitaḥ

translations.english: With his body covered all over with shafts, (Hanumān) getting into a furious passion, taking up the same bolt, again began to swing it with rapidity.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिवेगोऽतिवेगेन भ्रामयित्वा बलोत्कटः
परिघं पातयामास जम्बुमालेर्महोरसि
verses.transliteration:
ativego'tivegena bhrāmayitvā balotkaṭaḥ
parighaṁ pātayāmāsa jambumālermahorasi

translations.english: That terrific one gifted with exceeding impetuosity, having whirled the bolt with wondrous rapidity, let it light upon Jambumāli's spacious breast.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चैव शिरो नास्ति न बाहू न च जानुनी
न धनुर्न रथो नाश्वास्तत्रादृश्यन्त नेषवः
verses.transliteration:
tasya caiva śiro nāsti na bāhū na ca jānunī
na dhanurna ratho nāśvāstatrādṛśyanta neṣavaḥ

translations.english: And (non) there was neither seen there his head, nor his arms, nor his thighs, nor his bow, nor his car, nor his steeds, nor his arrows at that place.

verses.sanskrit:
स हतस्तरसा तेन जम्बुमाली महारथः
पपात निहतो भूमौ चूर्णिताङ्गविभूषणः
verses.transliteration:
sa hatastarasā tena jambumālī mahārathaḥ
papāta nihato bhūmau cūrṇitāṅgavibhūṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: That mighty car-warrior, Jambumālī, speedily slain, fell down to the earth, like a tree whose trunk has been crushed.

verses.sanskrit:
जम्बुमालिं च निहतं किंकरांश्च महाबलान्
चुक्रोध रावणः श्रुत्वा कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
verses.transliteration:
jambumāliṁ ca nihataṁ kiṁkarāṁśca mahābalān
cukrodha rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā kopasaṁraktalocanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Jambumāli as well as his exceedingly powerful servants slaughtered, Rāvana became transported with anger, and his eyes became reddened in wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
स रोषसंवर्तितताम्रलोचनः; प्रहस्तपुत्रे निहते महाबले
अमात्यपुत्रानतिवीर्यविक्रमा;न्समादिदेशाशु निशाचरेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa roṣasaṁvartitatāmralocanaḥ; prahastaputre nihate mahābale
amātyaputrānativīryavikramā;nsamādideśāśu niśācareśvaraḥ

translations.english: On the mighty-son of Prahasta having been slain, the lord of the night-rangers, with his reddened eyes rolling in rage, speedily commanded the of his counsellors, endowed with vast energy and prowess, (to encounter Hanumān in battle). sons

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणः सुताः
निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्त सप्तार्चिवर्चसः
verses.transliteration:
tataste rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇaḥ sutāḥ
niryayurbhavanāttasmātsapta saptārcivarcasaḥ

translations.english: Then ordered by the lord of Rākşasas, the sons of his counsellors, seven (in number) in splendour reseinbling fire, issued forth that mansion.

verses.sanskrit:
ते परस्परसंघर्षास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः
अभिपेतुर्हनूमन्तं तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
te parasparasaṁgharṣāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
abhipeturhanūmantaṁ toraṇasthamavasthitam

translations.english: And vieing with each other in eagerness, those (warriors) decked in ornaments of polished gold, confronted Hanumān staying at the gate.

verses.sanskrit:
सृजन्तो बाणवृष्टिं ते रथगर्जितनिःस्वनाः
वृष्टिमन्त इवाम्भोदा विचेरुर्नैरृतर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
sṛjanto bāṇavṛṣṭiṁ te rathagarjitaniḥsvanāḥ
vṛṣṭimanta ivāmbhodā vicerurnairṛtarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And with their cars sending roars, the Rākşasas, pouring showers of shafts, ranged (the field), resembling clouds during the rainy season.

verses.sanskrit:
अवकीर्णस्ततस्ताभिर्हनूमाञ्शरवृष्टिभिः
अभवत्संवृताकारः शैलराडिव वृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration:
avakīrṇastatastābhirhanūmāñśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
abhavatsaṁvṛtākāraḥ śailarāḍiva vṛṣṭibhiḥ

translations.english: Covered with those arrowy showers, Hanuman had his person concealed, like the monarch of mountains hidden by a downpour.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरान्वञ्चयामास तेषामाशुचरः कपिः
रथवेगांश्च वीराणां विचरन्विमलेऽम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
sa śarānvañcayāmāsa teṣāmāśucaraḥ kapiḥ
rathavegāṁśca vīrāṇāṁ vicaranvimale'mbare

translations.english: That swift-speeding monkey, coursing the cloudless sky, evaded those shafts of those heroes, as well as the impetuosity of their cars.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः क्रीडन्धनुष्मद्भिर्व्योम्नि वीरः प्रकाशते
धनुष्मद्भिर्यथा मेघैर्मारुतः प्रभुरम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ krīḍandhanuṣmadbhirvyomni vīraḥ prakāśate
dhanuṣmadbhiryathā meghairmārutaḥ prabhurambare

translations.english: That hero, playing pranks with those bowmen, appeared like the masterful Wind playing tricks with the bow-bearing clouds. (i.e. having the iris.)

verses.sanskrit:
स कृत्वा निनदं घोरं त्रासयंस्तां महाचमूम्
चकार हनुमान्वेगं तेषु रक्षःसु वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
sa kṛtvā ninadaṁ ghoraṁ trāsayaṁstāṁ mahācamūm
cakāra hanumānvegaṁ teṣu rakṣaḥsu vīryavān

translations.english: Sending up a dreadful shout, and thereby filling that vast host with fright, the energetic Hanumān rushed on that Rākşasa army.

verses.sanskrit:
तलेनाभिहनत्कांश्चित्पादैः कांश्चित्परंतपः
मुष्टिनाभ्यहनत्कांश्चिन्नखैः कांश्चिद्व्यदारयत्
verses.transliteration:
talenābhihanatkāṁścitpādaiḥ kāṁścitparaṁtapaḥ
muṣṭinābhyahanatkāṁścinnakhaiḥ kāṁścidvyadārayat

translations.english: That subduer of enemies slew some with slaps, and some he rived with nails, and some he killed by blows, and others with (the pressure of) his chest. And some dropped down on the ground at the very same spot at the sounds that he emitted.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेष्ववपन्नेषु भूमौ निपतितेषु च
तत्सैन्यमगमत्सर्वं दिशो दशभयार्दितम्
verses.transliteration:
tatasteṣvavapanneṣu bhūmau nipatiteṣu ca
tatsainyamagamatsarvaṁ diśo daśabhayārditam

translations.english: And on their being slain or falling on the earth, that army, afflicted with affright, began to fly in all directions.

verses.sanskrit:
विनेदुर्विस्वरं नागा निपेतुर्भुवि वाजिनः
भग्ननीडध्वजच्छत्रैर्भूश्च कीर्णाभवद्रथैः
verses.transliteration:
vinedurvisvaraṁ nāgā nipeturbhuvi vājinaḥ
bhagnanīḍadhvajacchatrairbhūśca kīrṇābhavadrathaiḥ

translations.english: The elephants roared in frightful tones, and the steeds fell down on the earth. And the Earth was covered with broken boxes, flag-staffs, and umbrellas, (belonging to the cars), as also with the cars themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
स तान्प्रवृद्धान्विनिहत्य राक्षसा;न्महाबलश्चण्डपराक्रमः कपिः
युयुत्सुरन्यैः पुनरेव राक्षसै;स्तदेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tānpravṛddhānvinihatya rākṣasā;nmahābalaścaṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ
yuyutsuranyaiḥ punareva rākṣasai;stadeva vīro'bhijagāma toraṇam

translations.english: Having slain those overgrown Rākşasas, that exceedingly powerful and heroic monkey of terrific power, desirous of again coping with other Rākşasas, retraced his steps to the selfsame entrance.

verses.sanskrit:
हतान्मन्त्रिसुतान्बुद्ध्वा वानरेण महात्मना
रावणः संवृताकारश्चकार मतिमुत्तमाम्
verses.transliteration:
hatānmantrisutānbuddhvā vānareṇa mahātmanā
rāvaṇaḥ saṁvṛtākāraścakāra matimuttamām

translations.english: Learning that the sons of the counsellors had been slain by the high-souled monkey, the Tennecked one suppressing the apprehension that was in his heart, restored the balance of his mind.

verses.sanskrit:
संदिदेश दशग्रीवो वीरान्नयविशारदान्
हनूमद्ग्रहणे व्यग्रान्वायुवेगसमान्युधि
verses.transliteration:
saṁdideśa daśagrīvo vīrānnayaviśāradān
hanūmadgrahaṇe vyagrānvāyuvegasamānyudhi

translations.english: He directed five of the foremost leaders of his forces, the heroic Virūpaksa Yupakşa, the Rāks asa Durdharsa, Praghasa, and Bhasakarma, versed in polity, endowed with the speed of the Wind in conflict and alert on every occasion, to take Hanumān captive.

verses.sanskrit:
यात सेनाग्रगाः सर्वे महाबलपरिग्रहाः
सवाजिरथमातङ्गाः स कपिः शास्यतामिति
verses.transliteration:
yāta senāgragāḥ sarve mahābalaparigrahāḥ
savājirathamātaṅgāḥ sa kapiḥ śāsyatāmiti

translations.english: You generals, do youtaking mighty host with steeds, elephants and cars, chastise that monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तैश्च खलु भाव्यं स्यात्तमासाद्य वनालयम्
कर्म चापि समाधेयं देशकालविरोधितम्
verses.transliteration:
yattaiśca khalu bhāvyaṁ syāttamāsādya vanālayam
karma cāpi samādheyaṁ deśakālavirodhitam

translations.english: And coming to that dweller of the woods, youhad better act heedfully, and should accomplish this work in consonance with place and season.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यहं तं कपिं मन्ये कर्मणा प्रतितर्कयन्
सर्वथा तन्महद्भूतं महाबलपरिग्रहम्
भवेदिन्द्रेण वा सृष्टमस्मदर्थं तपोबलात्
verses.transliteration:
na hyahaṁ taṁ kapiṁ manye karmaṇā pratitarkayan
sarvathā tanmahadbhūtaṁ mahābalaparigraham
bhavedindreṇa vā sṛṣṭamasmadarthaṁ tapobalāt

translations.english: Having regard to his acts, I do not take him to be a monkey. He is a great being endowed with extraordinary prowess every way.

verses.sanskrit:
वाली च सह सुग्रीवो जाम्बवांश्च महाबलः
नीलः सेनापतिश्चैव ये चान्ये द्विविदादयः
verses.transliteration:
vālī ca saha sugrīvo jāmbavāṁśca mahābalaḥ
nīlaḥ senāpatiścaiva ye cānye dvividādayaḥ

translations.english: This monkey of deliberate prowess should not be disregarded by you. I have seen (There is a word sighra, soon-in this Śloka, of which I fail to perceive the relation) monkeys of immense prowess, Vāli with Sugrīva and the exceedingly powerful Jāmbavāna, and Nīla the general, and others with Dwivida at their head.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव तेषां गतिर्भीमा न तेजो न पराक्रमः
न मतिर्न बलोत्साहो न रूपपरिकल्पनम्
verses.transliteration:
naiva teṣāṁ gatirbhīmā na tejo na parākramaḥ
na matirna balotsāho na rūpaparikalpanam

translations.english: Their speed is not dreadful, nor their energy, nor their prowess, nor their intelligence, nor their strength, nor their courage, nor their capacity to change shapes.

verses.sanskrit:
महत्सत्त्वमिदं ज्ञेयं कपिरूपं व्यवस्थितम्
प्रयत्नं महदास्थाय क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
mahatsattvamidaṁ jñeyaṁ kapirūpaṁ vyavasthitam
prayatnaṁ mahadāsthāya kriyatāmasya nigrahaḥ

translations.english: Therefore you should know him as some great being staying in the form of a monkey. Exerting yourself to the uttermost, do you chastise him.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः ससुरासुरमानवाः
भवतामग्रतः स्थातुं न पर्याप्ता रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ lokāstrayaḥ sendrāḥ sasurāsuramānavāḥ
bhavatāmagrataḥ sthātuṁ na paryāptā raṇājire

translations.english: These three worlds combined, with Indra, celestials and mortals, are incapable of long staying before you in the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तथापि तु नयज्ञेन जयमाकाङ्क्षता रणे
आत्मा रक्ष्यः प्रयत्नेन युद्धसिद्धिर्हि चञ्चला
verses.transliteration:
tathāpi tu nayajñena jayamākāṅkṣatā raṇe
ātmā rakṣyaḥ prayatnena yuddhasiddhirhi cañcalā

translations.english: Still a person versed in polity, albeit anxious to secure victory in battle, should carefully preserve self, as success in war is unstable.

verses.sanskrit:
ते स्वामिवचनं सर्वे प्रतिगृह्य महौजसः
समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा हुताशसमतेजसः
verses.transliteration:
te svāmivacanaṁ sarve pratigṛhya mahaujasaḥ
samutpeturmahāvegā hutāśasamatejasaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, they, possessed of the energy of fire, accepting the words of their master, rushed forth vehemendy, accompanied with cars, mad elephants, fleet steeds, sharp and whetted weapons, and forces of all kinds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं ददृशुर्वीरा दीप्यमानं महाकपिम्
रश्मिमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं स्वतेजोरश्मिमालिनम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ dadṛśurvīrā dīpyamānaṁ mahākapim
raśmimantamivodyantaṁ svatejoraśmimālinam

translations.english: Then those heroes saw that effulgent mighty monkey, shining in his native splendour, like to the risen sun, possessed of great strength and immense speed, and magnanimity of mind, seated at the gate.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समीक्ष्यैव ते सर्वे दिक्षु सर्वास्ववस्थिताः
तैस्तैः प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samīkṣyaiva te sarve dikṣu sarvāsvavasthitāḥ
taistaiḥ praharaṇairbhīmairabhipetustatastataḥ

translations.english: And soon as they saw him, they, frightened at his appearance, assailed him with their respective terrible weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पञ्चायसास्तीक्ष्णाः सिताः पीतमुखाः शराः
शिरस्त्युत्पलपत्राभा दुर्धरेण निपातिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya pañcāyasāstīkṣṇāḥ sitāḥ pītamukhāḥ śarāḥ
śirastyutpalapatrābhā durdhareṇa nipātitāḥ

translations.english: And Durdhasa discharged at Hanumān's head five white iron (This may rather look an incongruous mixture of images; but the iron arrows may have been silvered over) arrows with yellow heads, and possessing the lustre of lotus-leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः पञ्चभिराविद्धः शरैः शिरसि वानरः
उत्पपात नदन्व्योम्नि दिशो दश विनादयन्
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ pañcabhirāviddhaḥ śaraiḥ śirasi vānaraḥ
utpapāta nadanvyomni diśo daśa vinādayan

translations.english: Having been pierced in the head with those shafts, the monkey, roaring, leapt into the sky inaking the ten cardinal points resound.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु दुर्धरो वीरः सरथः सज्जकार्मुकः
किरञ्शरशतैर्नैकैरभिपेदे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu durdharo vīraḥ sarathaḥ sajjakārmukaḥ
kirañśaraśatairnaikairabhipede mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Then the exceedingly powerful and heroic Durdhara mounted on a car, with his bow stringed, came forward showering innumerable arrows by hundreds.

verses.sanskrit:
स कपिर्वारयामास तं व्योम्नि शरवर्षिणम्
वृष्टिमन्तं पयोदान्ते पयोदमिव मारुतः
verses.transliteration:
sa kapirvārayāmāsa taṁ vyomni śaravarṣiṇam
vṛṣṭimantaṁ payodānte payodamiva mārutaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, even as the wind drive away rainpouring clouds at the end of the rainy season, the monkey, remaining in the sky, resisted (his antagonist) as he kept on pouring his shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्द्यमानस्ततस्तेन दुर्धरेणानिलात्मजः
चकार निनदं भूयो व्यवर्धत च वेगवान्
verses.transliteration:
ardyamānastatastena durdhareṇānilātmajaḥ
cakāra ninadaṁ bhūyo vyavardhata ca vegavān

translations.english: And sore beset by Durdhara, the Wind-god's son again emitted cries, and that puissant one also increased himself.

verses.sanskrit:
स दूरं सहसोत्पत्य दुर्धरस्य रथे हरिः
निपपात महावेगो विद्युद्राशिर्गिराविव
verses.transliteration:
sa dūraṁ sahasotpatya durdharasya rathe hariḥ
nipapāta mahāvego vidyudrāśirgirāviva

translations.english: Then darting far up in the air, the monkey suddenly descended on the car of Durdhara with extreme vehemence, like to a mass of lightning alighting on a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं मथिताष्टाश्वं रथं भग्नाक्षकूवरम्
विहाय न्यपतद्भूमौ दुर्धरस्त्यक्तजीवितः
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ mathitāṣṭāśvaṁ rathaṁ bhagnākṣakūvaram
vihāya nyapatadbhūmau durdharastyaktajīvitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat his eight steeds getting mangled, and the wheels and pole of his car having been broken, Durdhara leaving the car, fell down to the earth, deprived of life.

verses.sanskrit:
तं विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भुवि
संजातरोषौ दुर्धर्षावुत्पेततुररिंदमौ
verses.transliteration:
taṁ virūpākṣayūpākṣau dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṁ bhuvi
saṁjātaroṣau durdharṣāvutpetaturariṁdamau

translations.english: Seeing him down on the earth, those irrepressible subduers of enemies, Virūpaksa and Yupaksa, waxing wroth, sprang up.

verses.sanskrit:
स ताभ्यां सहसोत्पत्य विष्ठितो विमलेऽम्बरे
मुद्गराभ्यां महाबाहुर्वक्षस्यभिहतः कपिः
verses.transliteration:
sa tābhyāṁ sahasotpatya viṣṭhito vimale'mbare
mudgarābhyāṁ mahābāhurvakṣasyabhihataḥ kapiḥ

translations.english: And springing up suddenly, they by means of maces, dealt blows on the chest of the monkey, who was staying in the unclouded sky.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोर्वेगवतोर्वेगं विनिहत्य महाबलः
निपपात पुनर्भूमौ सुपर्णसमविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tayorvegavatorvegaṁ vinihatya mahābalaḥ
nipapāta punarbhūmau suparṇasamavikramaḥ

translations.english: Thereat resisting the furious rush of those gifted with ebullient erergy, that exceedingly powerful one descended to the earth with the violence of the Fair-feathered (bird).* (Suparna-a name of Garuda.)

verses.sanskrit:
स सालवृक्षमासाद्य समुत्पाट्य च वानरः
तावुभौ राक्षसौ वीरौ जघान पवनात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa sālavṛkṣamāsādya samutpāṭya ca vānaraḥ
tāvubhau rākṣasau vīrau jaghāna pavanātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then getting at and uprooting a sāla tree, that monkey, the Wind-god's offspring, slew both of those heroic Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स ताभ्यां विक्षतैर्गात्रैरसृग्दिग्धतनूरुहः
अभवद्वानरः क्रुद्धो बालसूर्यसमप्रभः
verses.transliteration:
sa tābhyāṁ vikṣatairgātrairasṛgdigdhatanūruhaḥ
abhavadvānaraḥ kruddho bālasūryasamaprabhaḥ

translations.english: And with his limbs wounded by them, and his hair wetted with blood, that monkey resembling in splendour the infant sun, grew furiously enraged.

verses.sanskrit:
समुत्पाट्य गिरेः शृङ्गं समृगव्यालपादपम्
जघान हनुमान्वीरो राक्षसौ कपिकुञ्जरः
verses.transliteration:
samutpāṭya gireḥ śṛṅgaṁ samṛgavyālapādapam
jaghāna hanumānvīro rākṣasau kapikuñjaraḥ

translations.english: That elephantine monkey, the heroic Hanumān, uprooting a mountain-peak with beasts, snakes, and trees (in it), slew those Raksasas; and, crushed by that mountainsummit, they were reduced to powder.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेष्ववसन्नेषु सेनापतिषु पञ्चसु
बलं तदवशेषं तु नाशयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
tatasteṣvavasanneṣu senāpatiṣu pañcasu
balaṁ tadavaśeṣaṁ tu nāśayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: On those five generals having fallen, the monkey slew the remaining forces.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्वैरश्वान्गजैर्नागान्योधैर्योधान्रथै रथान्
स कपिर्नाशयामास सहस्राक्ष इवासुरान्
verses.transliteration:
aśvairaśvāngajairnāgānyodhairyodhānrathai rathān
sa kapirnāśayāmāsa sahasrākṣa ivāsurān

translations.english: As the thousand-eyed Deity destroyed Asuras, the monkey destroyed steeds with steeds, elephants with elephants, warriors with warriors, and cars with cars.

verses.sanskrit:
हतैर्नागैश्च तुरगैर्भग्नाक्षैश्च महारथैः
हतैश्च राक्षसैर्भूमी रुद्धमार्गा समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
hatairnāgaiśca turagairbhagnākṣaiśca mahārathaiḥ
hataiśca rākṣasairbhūmī ruddhamārgā samantataḥ

translations.english: And with horses and elephants, swift steeds, with broken wheels and mighty cars, and Raksasas slain, all the ways were blocked up.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कपिस्तान्ध्वजिनीपतीन्रणे; निहत्य वीरान्सबलान्सवाहनान्
तदेव वीरः परिगृह्य तोरणं; कृतक्षणः काल इव प्रजाक्षये
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kapistāndhvajinīpatīnraṇe; nihatya vīrānsabalānsavāhanān
tadeva vīraḥ parigṛhya toraṇaṁ; kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye

translations.english: Having destroyed in battle the heroic generals with all their forces and vehicles, that hero in the same way rested at the gate like Kāla himself engaged in destroying people when he has gained respite. Having destroyed in battle the heroic generals with all their forces and vehicles, that hero in the same way rested at the gate like Kāla himself engaged in destroying people when he has gained respite.

verses.sanskrit:
सेनापतीन्पञ्च स तु प्रमापिता;न्हनूमता सानुचरान्सवाहनान्
समीक्ष्य राजा समरोद्धतोन्मुखं; कुमारमक्षं प्रसमैक्षताक्षतम्
verses.transliteration:
senāpatīnpañca sa tu pramāpitā;nhanūmatā sānucarānsavāhanān
samīkṣya rājā samaroddhatonmukhaṁ; kumāramakṣaṁ prasamaikṣatākṣatam

translations.english: Hearing that the five generals had been slain by Hanumān alone with their vehicles and followers, the king, gazing at prince Aksa, who was ready and eager to go to battle, commanded him to take the field.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य दृष्ट्यर्पणसंप्रचोदितः; प्रतापवान्काञ्चनचित्रकार्मुकः
समुत्पपाताथ सदस्युदीरितो; द्विजातिमुख्यैर्हविषेव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya dṛṣṭyarpaṇasaṁpracoditaḥ; pratāpavānkāñcanacitrakārmukaḥ
samutpapātātha sadasyudīrito; dvijātimukhyairhaviṣeva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: That puissant one of a bow decked with gold, on being commanded (by Rāvana) with a glance started up, like to fire on being fed by clarified butter by foremost regenerate persons on the sacrificial ground.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महद्बालदिवाकरप्रभं; प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालसंततम्
रथां समास्थाय ययौ स वीर्यवा;न्महाहरिं तं प्रति नैरृतर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
tato mahadbāladivākaraprabhaṁ; prataptajāmbūnadajālasaṁtatam
rathāṁ samāsthāya yayau sa vīryavā;nmahāhariṁ taṁ prati nairṛtarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: That best of Naiſtas (Rākṣasas) possessed of prowess, ascending a car resembling the infant sun in effulgence, and surrounded all round with networks of burnished gold, sallied forth in quest of that mighty monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
स पूरयन्खं च महीं च साचलां; तुरंगमतङ्गमहारथस्वनैः
बलैः समेतैः स हि तोरणस्थितं; समर्थमासीनमुपागमत्कपिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa pūrayankhaṁ ca mahīṁ ca sācalāṁ; turaṁgamataṅgamahārathasvanaiḥ
balaiḥ sametaiḥ sa hi toraṇasthitaṁ; samarthamāsīnamupāgamatkapim

translations.english: And filling the firmament and the earth containing mountains with sounds proceeding from steeds, elephants and mighty cars, he, accompanied by his forces, presented himself before the capable monkey, who was seated at the gate.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं समासाद्य हरिं हरीक्षणो; युगान्तकालाग्निमिव प्रजाक्षये
अवस्थितं विस्मितजातसंभ्रमः; समैक्षताक्षो बहुमानचक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ samāsādya hariṁ harīkṣaṇo; yugāntakālāgnimiva prajākṣaye
avasthitaṁ vismitajātasaṁbhramaḥ; samaikṣatākṣo bahumānacakṣuṣā

translations.english: Coming before the monkey, Akşa, having the gaze of a lion, with eyes betokening regard, gazed at Hanumān resembling the Fire on the occasion of the universal dissolution at the end of a Yuga, intent on destroying creatures, and who was seated and was influenced alike by surprise and regard.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य वेगं च कपेर्महात्मनः; पराक्रमं चारिषु पार्थिवात्मजः
विचारयन्खं च बलं महाबलो; हिमक्षये सूर्य इवाभिवर्धते
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya vegaṁ ca kapermahātmanaḥ; parākramaṁ cāriṣu pārthivātmajaḥ
vicārayankhaṁ ca balaṁ mahābalo; himakṣaye sūrya ivābhivardhate

translations.english: And seriously considering the impetuosity of the high-souled monkey as well as his prowess in relation to a foe, as also his own strength, he increased in strength) like the Sun on the expiration of a Yuga.

verses.sanskrit:
स जातमन्युः प्रसमीक्ष्य विक्रमं; स्थिरः स्थितः संयति दुर्निवारणम्
समाहितात्मा हनुमन्तमाहवे; प्रचोदयामास शरैस्त्रिभिः शितैः
verses.transliteration:
sa jātamanyuḥ prasamīkṣya vikramaṁ; sthiraḥ sthitaḥ saṁyati durnivāraṇam
samāhitātmā hanumantamāhave; pracodayāmāsa śaraistribhiḥ śitaiḥ

translations.english: And growing enraged, (Aksa), staying calmly in the field, with concentrated soul, challenged Hanumān difficult to resist in conflict and of prowess worthy to witness, with three whetted shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कपिं तं प्रसमीक्ष्य गर्वितं; जितश्रमं शत्रुपराजयोर्जितम्
अवैक्षताक्षः समुदीर्णमानसः; सबाणपाणिः प्रगृहीतकार्मुकः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kapiṁ taṁ prasamīkṣya garvitaṁ; jitaśramaṁ śatruparājayorjitam
avaikṣatākṣaḥ samudīrṇamānasaḥ; sabāṇapāṇiḥ pragṛhītakārmukaḥ

translations.english: And finding the monkey proud and untiring, capable of vanquishing his foe, and possessed of exalted spirits, Akșa took up his bow and held his arrows in his hands.

verses.sanskrit:
स हेमनिष्काङ्गदचारुकुण्डलः; समाससादाशु पराक्रमः कपिम्
तयोर्बभूवाप्रतिमः समागमः; सुरासुराणामपि संभ्रमप्रदः
verses.transliteration:
sa hemaniṣkāṅgadacārukuṇḍalaḥ; samāsasādāśu parākramaḥ kapim
tayorbabhūvāpratimaḥ samāgamaḥ; surāsurāṇāmapi saṁbhramapradaḥ

translations.english: And wearing a golden corslet, Angadas, and earrings, and possessed of fiery vigour, he closed with the monkey; and their meeting was something unparalleled on this earth, and was calculated to raise the respect (Sambhramaprada according to Rāmānuja means, capable of exciting fear) even of the celestials and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
ररास भूमिर्न तताप भानुमा;न्ववौ न वायुः प्रचचाल चाचलः
कपेः कुमारस्य च वीक्ष्य संयुगं; ननाद च द्यौरुदधिश्च चुक्षुभे
verses.transliteration:
rarāsa bhūmirna tatāpa bhānumā;nvavau na vāyuḥ pracacāla cācalaḥ
kapeḥ kumārasya ca vīkṣya saṁyugaṁ; nanāda ca dyaurudadhiśca cukṣubhe

translations.english: And witnessing the mighty conflict of the prince and the monkey, Earth emitted cries, and the Sun did not burn, and the Wind did not blow, and the mountains shook, and the welkin sounded, and the main was vexed.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स वीरः सुमुखान्पतत्रिणः; सुवर्णपुङ्खान्सविषानिवोरगान्
समाधिसंयोगविमोक्षतत्त्ववि;च्छरानथ त्रीन्कपिमूर्ध्न्यपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa vīraḥ sumukhānpatatriṇaḥ; suvarṇapuṅkhānsaviṣānivoragān
samādhisaṁyogavimokṣatattvavi;ccharānatha trīnkapimūrdhnyapātayat

translations.english: That hero, skilled in aiming, fixing and discharging arrows, shot at the monkey's head three fine-headed feathered shafts plated with gold near the feathers, and resembling venomous serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः शरैर्मूर्ध्नि समं निपातितैः; क्षरन्नसृग्दिग्धविवृत्तलोचनः
नवोदितादित्यनिभः शरांशुमा;न्व्यराजतादित्य इवांशुमालिकः
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ śarairmūrdhni samaṁ nipātitaiḥ; kṣarannasṛgdigdhavivṛttalocanaḥ
navoditādityanibhaḥ śarāṁśumā;nvyarājatāditya ivāṁśumālikaḥ

translations.english: And with his rolling eyes washed with blood in consequence of the shafts having alighted at his head, Hanumān, resembling a new-risen Sun having arrows for its rays, looked splendid like the light-engarlanded Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स पिङ्गाधिपमन्त्रिसत्तमः; समीक्ष्य तं राजवरात्मजं रणे
उदग्रचित्रायुधचित्रकार्मुकं; जहर्ष चापूर्यत चाहवोन्मुखः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa piṅgādhipamantrisattamaḥ; samīkṣya taṁ rājavarātmajaṁ raṇe
udagracitrāyudhacitrakārmukaṁ; jaharṣa cāpūryata cāhavonmukhaḥ

translations.english: Seeing in battle that son of the foremost of monarchs, with his excellent weapons upraised and his beautiful bow, that best of the counsellors of the lord of monkeys, rejoiced, and intent on encounter, increased himself.

verses.sanskrit:
स मन्दराग्रस्थ इवांशुमाली; विवृद्धकोपो बलवीर्यसंयुतः
कुमारमक्षं सबलं सवाहनं; ददाह नेत्राग्निमरीचिभिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
sa mandarāgrastha ivāṁśumālī; vivṛddhakopo balavīryasaṁyutaḥ
kumāramakṣaṁ sabalaṁ savāhanaṁ; dadāha netrāgnimarīcibhistadā

translations.english: And with his ire heightened, that one endowed with energy and prowess, like to the ray-decorated (Sun) on the crest of Mandara,* The Sun is on Mandara in mid-day: therefore the meridian Sun is meant here, began to burn with the fiery rays of his eyes, Akşa, along with his forces and vehicles.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स बाणासनशक्रकार्मुकः; शरप्रवर्षो युधि राक्षसाम्बुदः
शरान्मुमोचाशु हरीश्वराचले; बलाहको वृष्टिमिवाचलोत्तमे
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa bāṇāsanaśakrakārmukaḥ; śarapravarṣo yudhi rākṣasāmbudaḥ
śarānmumocāśu harīśvarācale; balāhako vṛṣṭimivācalottame

translations.english: As a mass of clouds shower rain on a high hill, the arrow-showering Rākşasa resembling clouds, having the bow for his rain-bow, discharged shafts at that foremost of monkeys, representing a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कपिस्तं रणचण्डविक्रमं; विवृद्धतेजोबलवीर्यसायकम्
कुमारमक्षं प्रसमीक्ष्य संयुगे; ननाद हर्षाद्घनतुल्यविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kapistaṁ raṇacaṇḍavikramaṁ; vivṛddhatejobalavīryasāyakam
kumāramakṣaṁ prasamīkṣya saṁyuge; nanāda harṣādghanatulyavikramaḥ

translations.english: Then the monkey, having sounds like those of clouds, beholding in battle Akşa of terrific prowess in conflict, and strong in energy, strength and shafts, sent up shouts from elation of spirits.

verses.sanskrit:
स बालभावाद्युधि वीर्यदर्पितः; प्रवृद्धमन्युः क्षतजोपमेक्षणः
समाससादाप्रतिमं रणे कपिं; गजो महाकूपमिवावृतं तृणैः
verses.transliteration:
sa bālabhāvādyudhi vīryadarpitaḥ; pravṛddhamanyuḥ kṣatajopamekṣaṇaḥ
samāsasādāpratimaṁ raṇe kapiṁ; gajo mahākūpamivāvṛtaṁ tṛṇaiḥ

translations.english: As an elephant approach a deep pit covered over with grass, (Aksa) from a spirit of childishness elated in conflict with his prowess, with his ire heightened, and eyes resembling blood, drew near the monkey in the fleld.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेन बाणैः प्रसभं निपातितै;श्चकार नादं घननादनिःस्वनः
समुत्पपाताशु नभः स मारुति;र्भुजोरुविक्षेपण घोरदर्शनः
verses.transliteration:
sa tena bāṇaiḥ prasabhaṁ nipātitai;ścakāra nādaṁ ghananādaniḥsvanaḥ
samutpapātāśu nabhaḥ sa māruti;rbhujoruvikṣepaṇa ghoradarśanaḥ

translations.english: As Akşa went on hastily pouring shafts, that one uttering roars resembling the rumbling of clouds, looking terrible in consequence of his arms and thighs flung about, darted into the sky with exuberant energy.

verses.sanskrit:
समुत्पतन्तं समभिद्रवद्बली; स राक्षसानां प्रवरः प्रतापवान्
रथी रथश्रेष्ठतमः किरञ्शरैः; पयोधरः शैलमिवाश्मवृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration:
samutpatantaṁ samabhidravadbalī; sa rākṣasānāṁ pravaraḥ pratāpavān
rathī rathaśreṣṭhatamaḥ kirañśaraiḥ; payodharaḥ śailamivāśmavṛṣṭibhiḥ

translations.english: As he leapt up, that strong and powerful one-foremost of Raksasas-that car-warrior and the best of choice car warriors-rushed at (Hanuman), showering arrows on him, like a cloud showering hail-stones on a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
स ताञ्शरांस्तस्य विमोक्षयन्कपि;श्चचार वीरः पथि वायुसेविते
शरान्तरे मारुतवद्विनिष्पत;न्मनोजवः संयति चण्डविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāñśarāṁstasya vimokṣayankapi;ścacāra vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite
śarāntare mārutavadviniṣpata;nmanojavaḥ saṁyati caṇḍavikramaḥ

translations.english: And dashing in the midst of the arrows like the wind, and thus baffling them, the heroic monkey of dreadful 'prowess in conflict, and endowed with the speed of thought, began to range the path of the air.

verses.sanskrit:
तमात्तबाणासनमाहवोन्मुखं; खमास्तृणन्तं विविधैः शरोत्तमैः
अवैक्षताक्षं बहुमानचक्षुषा; जगाम चिन्तां च स मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
tamāttabāṇāsanamāhavonmukhaṁ; khamāstṛṇantaṁ vividhaiḥ śarottamaiḥ
avaikṣatākṣaṁ bahumānacakṣuṣā; jagāma cintāṁ ca sa mārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: And witness Akșa with regardful eyes, as that one intent on contest, taking his bow, was covering the sky with various excellent arrows, the Wind-god's offspring was plunged in thought.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरैर्भिन्नभुजान्तरः कपिः; कुमारवर्येण महात्मना नदन्
महाभुजः कर्मविशेषतत्त्ववि;द्विचिन्तयामास रणे पराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śarairbhinnabhujāntaraḥ kapiḥ; kumāravaryeṇa mahātmanā nadan
mahābhujaḥ karmaviśeṣatattvavi;dvicintayāmāsa raṇe parākramam

translations.english: Wounded in the arm with shafts by that highsouled, noble prince, that mighty-armed one, capable of adequately appreciating the nature of actions, thought on (Aksa's) prowess in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
अबालवद्बालदिवाकरप्रभः; करोत्ययं कर्म महन्महाबलः
न चास्य सर्वाहवकर्मशोभिनः; प्रमापणे मे मतिरत्र जायते
verses.transliteration:
abālavadbāladivākaraprabhaḥ; karotyayaṁ karma mahanmahābalaḥ
na cāsya sarvāhavakarmaśobhinaḥ; pramāpaṇe me matiratra jāyate

translations.english: This exceedingly powerful one, endowed with the splendour of the infant sun, is doing dire deeds incapable of being done by a boy; and I am loth to slay one that has shown himself equal to every martial feat.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं महात्मा च महांश्च वीर्यतः; समाहितश्चातिसहश्च संयुगे
असंशयं कर्मगुणोदयादयं; सनागयक्षैर्मुनिभिश्च पूजितः
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ mahātmā ca mahāṁśca vīryataḥ; samāhitaścātisahaśca saṁyuge
asaṁśayaṁ karmaguṇodayādayaṁ; sanāgayakṣairmunibhiśca pūjitaḥ

translations.english: This one is high-souled, mighty in energy, of concentrated self, and capable of bearing extreme hardships in war; without doubt, by virtue of his actions, he is worthy of being honoured by Nagas, Yaksas and ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
पराक्रमोत्साहविवृद्धमानसः; समीक्षते मां प्रमुखागतः स्थितः
पराक्रमो ह्यस्य मनांसि कम्पये;त्सुरासुराणामपि शीघ्रकारिणः
verses.transliteration:
parākramotsāhavivṛddhamānasaḥ; samīkṣate māṁ pramukhāgataḥ sthitaḥ
parākramo hyasya manāṁsi kampaye;tsurāsurāṇāmapi śīghrakāriṇaḥ

translations.english: With his mind braced by prowess and hope, that foremost of heroes eye me staying in the fore-front. The prowess of this light-handed (one), I were, make even the hearts of the celestials and Asuras tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
न खल्वयं नाभिभवेदुपेक्षितः; पराक्रमो ह्यस्य रणे विवर्धते
प्रमापणं त्वेव ममास्य रोचते; न वर्धमानोऽग्निरुपेक्षितुं क्षमः
verses.transliteration:
na khalvayaṁ nābhibhavedupekṣitaḥ; parākramo hyasya raṇe vivardhate
pramāpaṇaṁ tveva mamāsya rocate; na vardhamāno'gnirupekṣituṁ kṣamaḥ

translations.english: If I disregard him, he shall certainly vanquish me, for his prowess in battle increase (fast). Therefore I must even slay him: it is not proper to suffer an increasing fire.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रवेगं तु परस्य तर्कय;न्स्वकर्मयोगं च विधाय वीर्यवान्
चकार वेगं तु महाबलस्तदा; मतिं च चक्रेऽस्य वधे महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
iti pravegaṁ tu parasya tarkaya;nsvakarmayogaṁ ca vidhāya vīryavān
cakāra vegaṁ tu mahābalastadā; matiṁ ca cakre'sya vadhe mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Thus reflecting on the strength of his foe and having ascertained his line of action, that puissant one endowed with great strength, summoned energy and set his heart on slaying him (his antagonist).

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य तानष्टहयान्महाजवा;न्समाहितान्भारसहान्विवर्तने
जघान वीरः पथि वायुसेविते; तलप्रहालैः पवनात्मजः कपिः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya tānaṣṭahayānmahājavā;nsamāhitānbhārasahānvivartane
jaghāna vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite; talaprahālaiḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ

translations.english: And remaining in the path coursed by the air, that heroic monkey, the offspring of the Windgod, with his slaps slew his eight powerful and excellent steeds, capable of bearing pressure and trained to diverse circular movements.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तलेनाभिहतो महारथः; स तस्य पिङ्गाधिपमन्त्रिनिर्जितः
स भग्ननीडः परिमुक्तकूबरः; पपात भूमौ हतवाजिरम्बरात्
verses.transliteration:
tatastalenābhihato mahārathaḥ; sa tasya piṅgādhipamantrinirjitaḥ
sa bhagnanīḍaḥ parimuktakūbaraḥ; papāta bhūmau hatavājirambarāt

translations.english: And successfully assailed by the councillor of that lord of monkey, the car with its seat smashed, and its pole broken, and deprived of its steeds, fell to the earth from the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं परित्यज्य महारथो रथं; सकार्मुकः खड्गधरः खमुत्पतत्
तपोऽभियोगादृषिरुग्रवीर्यवा;न्विहाय देहं मरुतामिवालयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ parityajya mahāratho rathaṁ; sakārmukaḥ khaḍgadharaḥ khamutpatat
tapo'bhiyogādṛṣirugravīryavā;nvihāya dehaṁ marutāmivālayam

translations.english: Thereat, forsaking that car, the mighty car warrior sprang up into sky with his bow and holding his sabre, and (resembled) an ascetic of fierce energy consequent on austerities, going up to heaven, renouncing his body.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कपिस्तं विचरन्तमम्बरे; पतत्रिराजानिलसिद्धसेविते
समेत्य तं मारुतवेगविक्रमः; क्रमेण जग्राह च पादयोर्दृढम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kapistaṁ vicarantamambare; patatrirājānilasiddhasevite
sametya taṁ mārutavegavikramaḥ; krameṇa jagrāha ca pādayordṛḍham

translations.english: Then the monkey possessed of the energy and vigour of the Wind, approaching him as he was ranging the air coursed by the king of birds, the Wind and the Siddhas, at length fast caught hold of his legs.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं समाविध्य सहस्रशः कपि;र्महोरगं गृह्य इवाण्डजेश्वरः
मुमोच वेगात्पितृतुल्यविक्रमो; महीतले संयति वानरोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ samāvidhya sahasraśaḥ kapi;rmahoragaṁ gṛhya ivāṇḍajeśvaraḥ
mumoca vegātpitṛtulyavikramo; mahītale saṁyati vānarottamaḥ

translations.english: As the foremost of birds, Garuda taking a mighty serpent, whirls it, that foremost of monkeys, resembling his sire in prowess, whirling Akşa in the conflict, violently dropped him on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स भग्नबाहूरुकटीशिरो धरः; क्षरन्नसृन्निर्मथितास्थिलोचनः
स भिन्नसंधिः प्रविकीर्णबन्धनो; हतः क्षितौ वायुसुतेन राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhagnabāhūrukaṭīśiro dharaḥ; kṣarannasṛnnirmathitāsthilocanaḥ
sa bhinnasaṁdhiḥ pravikīrṇabandhano; hataḥ kṣitau vāyusutena rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: And with his arms, thighs and chest crushed, bleeding, (having his bones and eyes smashed, his joints riven, and his tendons snapped, the Rākṣasa lay on the earth, slain by the offspring of the Wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
महर्षिभिश्चक्रचरैर्महाव्रतैः; समेत्य भूतैश्च सयक्षपन्नगैः
सुरैश्च सेन्द्रैर्भृशजातविस्मयै;र्हते कुमारे स कपिर्निरीक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
maharṣibhiścakracarairmahāvrataiḥ; sametya bhūtaiśca sayakṣapannagaiḥ
suraiśca sendrairbhṛśajātavismayai;rhate kumāre sa kapirnirīkṣitaḥ

translations.english: And tormenting him (Akşa) on the earth, that mighty monkey caused great fright to the ruler of the Rākşasas; and he was gazed at by the assembled Maharsis and the orbit-coursing ones and all beings with Yakşas and Pannāgas, come to see him. And on the prince being slain, that monkey was gazed at by the celestials with Indra, who had been seized with extreme wonderment.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य तं वज्रसुतोपमप्रभं; कुमारमक्षं क्षतजोपमेक्षणम्
तदेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणं; कृतक्षणः काल इव प्रजाक्षये
verses.transliteration:
nihatya taṁ vajrasutopamaprabhaṁ; kumāramakṣaṁ kṣatajopamekṣaṇam
tadeva vīro'bhijagāma toraṇaṁ; kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye

translations.english: And having slain in battle prince Akşa resembling a son of the celestials and possessed of blood-red eyes, the hero (again) neared the same gate, and waited there like Kāla bent upon destroying all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु रक्षोऽधिपतिर्महात्मा; हनूमताक्षे निहते कुमारे
मनः समाधाय तदेन्द्रकल्पं; समादिदेशेन्द्रजितं स रोषात्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu rakṣo'dhipatirmahātmā; hanūmatākṣe nihate kumāre
manaḥ samādhāya tadendrakalpaṁ; samādideśendrajitaṁ sa roṣāt

translations.english: On prince Akşa having been slain by Hanumān, the magnanimous monarch of the Rākṣasas, wrought up by wrath, repressing his feelings, ordered Indrajit resembling a celestial, (to take the against the foe.)

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमस्त्रविच्छस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठः; सुरासुराणामपि शोकदाता
सुरेषु सेन्द्रेषु च दृष्टकर्मा; पितामहाराधनसंचितास्त्रः
verses.transliteration:
tvamastravicchastrabhṛtāṁ variṣṭhaḥ; surāsurāṇāmapi śokadātā
sureṣu sendreṣu ca dṛṣṭakarmā; pitāmahārādhanasaṁcitāstraḥ

translations.english: You are the foremost of those bearing arms; and you had afflicted even the gods and Asuras (in bat.s); your deeds have been witnessed by the celestials with Indra; and you had procured a weapon (viz. the Brahma weapon) even from the Great-father.

verses.sanskrit:
