तवास्त्रबलमासाद्य नासुरा न मरुद्गणाः
न कश्चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु संयुगे न गतश्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tavāstrabalamāsādya nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
na kaścittriṣu lokeṣu saṁyuge na gataśramaḥ

translations.english: And coping (in conflict) with your might of arms, all the celestials with the Maruts, headed by the lord of celestials himself, could not stay in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
भुजवीर्याभिगुप्तश्च तपसा चाभिरक्षितः
देशकालविभागज्ञस्त्वमेव मतिसत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
bhujavīryābhiguptaśca tapasā cābhirakṣitaḥ
deśakālavibhāgajñastvameva matisattamaḥ

translations.english: There is none in these three worlds (save yourself), who dose not come under the influence of fatigue in battle. And you are preserved by the prowess of your arms, and protected also by your ascetic merit; and being skilled in the knowledge of season and place, you, methinks, are the foremost of them all in intelligence.

verses.sanskrit:
न तेऽस्त्यशक्यं समरेषु कर्मणा; न तेऽस्त्यकार्यं मतिपूर्वमन्त्रणे
न सोऽस्ति कश्चित्त्रिषु संग्रहेषु वै; न वेद यस्तेऽस्त्रबलं बलं च ते
verses.transliteration:
na te'styaśakyaṁ samareṣu karmaṇā; na te'styakāryaṁ matipūrvamantraṇe
na so'sti kaścittriṣu saṁgraheṣu vai; na veda yaste'strabalaṁ balaṁ ca te

translations.english: There is no deed which you cannot perform in the field; and there is nothing in counsel capable of being arrived at by arguing on the lines prescribed by the scriptures, which you are not equal to; and there is none in all the three worlds who dose not know your strength and prowess in arms.

verses.sanskrit:
ममानुरूपं तपसो बलं च ते; पराक्रमश्चास्त्रबलं च संयुगे
न त्वां समासाद्य रणावमर्दे; मनः श्रमं गच्छति निश्चितार्थम्
verses.transliteration:
mamānurūpaṁ tapaso balaṁ ca te; parākramaścāstrabalaṁ ca saṁyuge
na tvāṁ samāsādya raṇāvamarde; manaḥ śramaṁ gacchati niścitārtham

translations.english: And your ascetic energy is like to mine, as well as your prowess and mighty in arms in battle. And having you in the conflict, my mind assured (of victory), dose not experience sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
निहता इंकराः सर्वे जम्बुमाली च राक्षसः
अमात्यपुत्रा वीराश्च पञ्च सेनाग्रयायिनः
verses.transliteration:
nihatā iṁkarāḥ sarve jambumālī ca rākṣasaḥ
amātyaputrā vīrāśca pañca senāgrayāyinaḥ

translations.english: Slain have been all the servants, as also Jambumālī, and those five generals, the heroic sons of my councillors, and the swelling forces including steeds, elephants and cars.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं हि दृष्ट्वा मतिमन्महद्बलं; कपेः प्रभावं च पराक्रमं च
त्वमात्मनश्चापि समीक्ष्य सारं; कुरुष्व वेगं स्वबलानुरूपम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ hi dṛṣṭvā matimanmahadbalaṁ; kapeḥ prabhāvaṁ ca parākramaṁ ca
tvamātmanaścāpi samīkṣya sāraṁ; kuruṣva vegaṁ svabalānurūpam

translations.english: And low Leith Sahodara, and prince Akşa has also been slain. O destroyer of foes, my mind did not feel the same confidence in them that I do in you. (According to another reading, the meaning would be:-"O best of warriors, do you, considering your own strength and that of the enemy, so exert yourself that he may no longer inflict terrible losses on our army.” (Tirtha)) And seeing this mighty host slain, as well as the prowess and energy of the monkey, and the taking into consideration your own strength, do you put forth your energy according to your strength.

verses.sanskrit:
बलावमर्दस्त्वयि संनिकृष्टे; यथा गते शाम्यति शान्तशत्रौ
तथा समीक्ष्यात्मबलं परं च; समारभस्वास्त्रविदां वरिष्ठ
verses.transliteration:
balāvamardastvayi saṁnikṛṣṭe; yathā gate śāmyati śāntaśatrau
tathā samīkṣyātmabalaṁ paraṁ ca; samārabhasvāstravidāṁ variṣṭha

translations.english: On nearing the scene (of conflict), do you, O foremost of those bearing arms, seeing yours own strength and that of the foe, so exert yourself that the latter, (now) resting quietly in consequence of having created a carnage-(on the hostile hosts), may wax enfeebled. (Another meaning is: Looking on yourself, and (not on my forces), as constituting my main stay, put forth your prowess.)

verses.sanskrit:
न खल्वियं मतिः श्रेष्ठा यत्त्वां संप्रेषयाम्यहम्
इयं च राजधर्माणां क्षत्रस्य च मतिर्मता
verses.transliteration:
na khalviyaṁ matiḥ śreṣṭhā yattvāṁ saṁpreṣayāmyaham
iyaṁ ca rājadharmāṇāṁ kṣatrasya ca matirmatā

translations.english: O foremost of intelligent ones, (that I send you to battle) is certainly not proper; yet this course of action is endorsed by Kșatriyas and those following the morality of kings.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाशस्त्रैश्च संग्रामे वैशारद्यमरिंदम
अवश्यमेव बोद्धव्यं काम्यश्च विजयो रणे
verses.transliteration:
nānāśastraiśca saṁgrāme vaiśāradyamariṁdama
avaśyameva boddhavyaṁ kāmyaśca vijayo raṇe

translations.english: O subduer of enemies, one should be versed in various branches of learning as well as be masterful in war. (According to a different reading, the meaning would be, “You are competent to fight agreeably to the rules.") He that craves victory in fight, should be acquainted with various branches of knowledge. (The śloka is very difficult and incapable of interpretation without at places meanings being read into it.)

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पितुस्तद्वचनं निशम्य; प्रदक्षिणं दक्षसुतप्रभावः
चकार भर्तारमदीनसत्त्वो; रणाय वीरः प्रतिपन्नबुद्धिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pitustadvacanaṁ niśamya; pradakṣiṇaṁ dakṣasutaprabhāvaḥ
cakāra bhartāramadīnasattvo; raṇāya vīraḥ pratipannabuddhiḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of his father, (Indrajit) gifted with celestial prowess, determined to fight, instantly circumambulated him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तैः स्वगणैरिष्टैरिन्द्रजित्प्रतिपूजितः
युद्धोद्धतकृतोत्साहः संग्रामं प्रतिपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
tatastaiḥ svagaṇairiṣṭairindrajitpratipūjitaḥ
yuddhoddhatakṛtotsāhaḥ saṁgrāmaṁ pratipadyata

translations.english: Excited with desire for fight and worked up with energy, Indrajit, eulogised by the friendly Rākşasas, set out for battle.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रीमान्पद्मपलाशाक्षो राक्षसाधिपतेः सुतः
निर्जगाम महातेजाः समुद्र इव पर्वसु
verses.transliteration:
śrīmānpadmapalāśākṣo rākṣasādhipateḥ sutaḥ
nirjagāma mahātejāḥ samudra iva parvasu

translations.english: And that highly effulgent and graceful son of the lord of the Rākşasas, having expansive eyes resembling lotus-petals, issued out like to the rising of the ocean during a parva. (A name given to certain days in the lunar month at the full and change at the moon, and the 8th and 11th of each hall month.)

verses.sanskrit:
स पक्षि राजोपमतुल्यवेगै;र्व्यालैश्चतुर्भिः सिततीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैः
रथं समायुक्तमसंगवेगं; समारुरोहेन्द्रजिदिन्द्रकल्पः
verses.transliteration:
sa pakṣi rājopamatulyavegai;rvyālaiścaturbhiḥ sitatīkṣṇadaṁṣṭraiḥ
rathaṁ samāyuktamasaṁgavegaṁ; samārurohendrajidindrakalpaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon Indrajit of unbearable prowess, equal to the lord of the celestials, ascended a car drawn by four horses, having sharpened teeth and resembling Garuda in velocity.

verses.sanskrit:
स रथी धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः शस्त्रज्ञोऽस्त्रविदां वरः
रथेनाभिययौ क्षिप्रं हनूमान्यत्र सोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rathī dhanvināṁ śreṣṭhaḥ śastrajño'stravidāṁ varaḥ
rathenābhiyayau kṣipraṁ hanūmānyatra so'bhavat

translations.english: And that master of a car and foremost of bowmen, conversant with the use of all weapons-the best of those using swords proceeded soon in his car where Hanumān was.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य रथनिर्घोषं ज्यास्वनं कार्मुकस्य च
निशम्य हरिवीरोऽसौ संप्रहृष्टतरोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya rathanirghoṣaṁ jyāsvanaṁ kārmukasya ca
niśamya harivīro'sau saṁprahṛṣṭataro'bhavat

translations.english: And hearing the sound of his car and the twang of his bow, that heroic monkey attained an excess of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमहच्चापमादाय शितशल्यांश्च सायकान्
हनूमन्तमभिप्रेत्य जगाम रणपण्डितः
verses.transliteration:
sumahaccāpamādāya śitaśalyāṁśca sāyakān
hanūmantamabhipretya jagāma raṇapaṇḍitaḥ

translations.english: And taking up a bow and sharpened darts, Indrajit, versed in the rules of war, proceeded towards Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिंस्ततः संयति जातहर्षे; रणाय निर्गच्छति बाणपाणौ
दिशश्च सर्वाः कलुषा बभूवु;र्मृगाश्च रौद्रा बहुधा विनेदुः
verses.transliteration:
tasmiṁstataḥ saṁyati jātaharṣe; raṇāya nirgacchati bāṇapāṇau
diśaśca sarvāḥ kaluṣā babhūvu;rmṛgāśca raudrā bahudhā vineduḥ

translations.english: And as he issued out for battle, greatly delighted, with arrows in his hands, all the quar'ers becai.e dark, and jackals began to set up terrible cries.

verses.sanskrit:
समागतास्तत्र तु नागयक्षा; महर्षयश्चक्रचराश्च सिद्धाः
नभः समावृत्य च पक्षिसंघा; विनेदुरुच्चैः परमप्रहृष्टाः
verses.transliteration:
samāgatāstatra tu nāgayakṣā; maharṣayaścakracarāśca siddhāḥ
nabhaḥ samāvṛtya ca pakṣisaṁghā; vineduruccaiḥ paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ

translations.english: There arrived the Nāgas, the Yakşas, the Maharsis, the planets, and the Siddhās, and the birds, covering the the welkin, and, greatly delighted, began to make a noise.

verses.sanskrit:
आयन्तं सरथं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमिन्द्रजितं कपिः
विननाद महानादं व्यवर्धत च वेगवान्
verses.transliteration:
āyantaṁ sarathaṁ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇamindrajitaṁ kapiḥ
vinanāda mahānādaṁ vyavardhata ca vegavān

translations.english: Beholding that car having a flag like that of Indra, approach very quickly, the monkey began to emit terrible roars and increase himself.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्तु रथं दिव्यमास्थितश्चित्रकार्मुकः
धनुर्विस्फारयामास तडिदूर्जितनिःस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
indrajittu rathaṁ divyamāsthitaścitrakārmukaḥ
dhanurvisphārayāmāsa taḍidūrjitaniḥsvanam

translations.english: And Indrajit too, seated on the celestial car and having a painted bow, began to stretch it, emitting a sound resembling that of thunder.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समेतावतितीक्ष्णवेगौ; महाबलौ तौ रणनिर्विशङ्कौ
कपिश्च रक्षोऽधिपतेश्च पुत्रः; सुरासुरेन्द्राविव बद्धवैरौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sametāvatitīkṣṇavegau; mahābalau tau raṇanirviśaṅkau
kapiśca rakṣo'dhipateśca putraḥ; surāsurendrāviva baddhavairau

translations.english: Thereupon closed in conflict those two greatly powerful (heroes)gifted with swift movements and fearless in battle—the monkey, and the son of the lord of Rākṣasas, like to the lords of celestials and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य वीरस्य महारथस्या; धनुष्मतः संयति संमतस्य
शरप्रवेगं व्यहनत्प्रवृद्ध;श्चचार मार्गे पितुरप्रमेयः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya vīrasya mahārathasyā; dhanuṣmataḥ saṁyati saṁmatasya
śarapravegaṁ vyahanatpravṛddha;ścacāra mārge pituraprameyaḥ

translations.english: And baffling the shafts of that hero of a mighty car, an accomplished bowman and a finished warrior, the immeasurably powerful monkey increasing himself began to range in the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरानायततीक्ष्णशल्या;न्सुपत्रिणः काञ्चनचित्रपुङ्खान्
मुमोच वीरः परवीरहन्ता; सुसंततान्वज्रनिपातवेगान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śarānāyatatīkṣṇaśalyā;nsupatriṇaḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhān
mumoca vīraḥ paravīrahantā; susaṁtatānvajranipātavegān

translations.english: Thereupon the heroic (Indrajit)-slayer of foes-began to discharge incessantly shafts, large, sharp, well-feathered, painted in gold and swift-coursing like to thunder.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य तत्स्यन्दननिःस्वनं च; मृदङ्गभेरीपटहस्वनं च
विकृष्यमाणस्य च कार्मुकस्य; निशम्य घोषं पुनरुत्पपात
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya tatsyandananiḥsvanaṁ ca; mṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahasvanaṁ ca
vikṛṣyamāṇasya ca kārmukasya; niśamya ghoṣaṁ punarutpapāta

translations.english: And hearing again the noise of his car, the sounds of drums, bugles, and war-drums, and the twangs of the bow, he again leaped up in the sky).

verses.sanskrit:
शराणामन्तरेष्वाशु व्यवर्तत महाकपिः
हरिस्तस्याभिलक्षस्य मोक्षयँल्लक्ष्यसंग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
śarāṇāmantareṣvāśu vyavartata mahākapiḥ
haristasyābhilakṣasya mokṣaya̐llakṣyasaṁgraham

translations.english: And baffling the aim of (Indrajit), who had always an eye on it, that great monkey ranged at a distance from those shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
शराणामग्रतस्तस्य पुनः समभिवर्तत
प्रसार्य हस्तौ हनुमानुत्पपातानिलात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
śarāṇāmagratastasya punaḥ samabhivartata
prasārya hastau hanumānutpapātānilātmajaḥ

translations.english: And again facing the arrows and stretching his hands, the Wind-god's son again leaped up.

verses.sanskrit:
तावुभौ वेगसंपन्नौ रणकर्मविशारदौ
सर्वभूतमनोग्राहि चक्रतुर्युद्धमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tāvubhau vegasaṁpannau raṇakarmaviśāradau
sarvabhūtamanogrāhi cakraturyuddhamuttamam

translations.english: And those two heroes, gifted with swift movements and versed in the art of war, engaged in a combat, admired by all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमतो वेद न राक्षसोऽन्तरं; न मारुतिस्तस्य महात्मनोऽन्तरम्
परस्परं निर्विषहौ बभूवतुः; समेत्य तौ देवसमानविक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
hanūmato veda na rākṣaso'ntaraṁ; na mārutistasya mahātmano'ntaram
parasparaṁ nirviṣahau babhūvatuḥ; sametya tau devasamānavikramau

translations.english: And Hanuman could not find out the shortcomings of the Rākşasa, nor could that highsouled one detect the weak points of the son of the Wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु लक्ष्ये स विहन्यमाने; शरेषु मोघेषु च संपतत्सु
जगाम चिन्तां महतीं महात्मा; समाधिसंयोगसमाहितात्मा
verses.transliteration:
tatastu lakṣye sa vihanyamāne; śareṣu mogheṣu ca saṁpatatsu
jagāma cintāṁ mahatīṁ mahātmā; samādhisaṁyogasamāhitātmā

translations.english: And these two gifted with celestial prowess, engaged in conflict, became unbearable to each other. And seeing him unhurt though aimed at with infallible arrows, the high-souled (Indrajit), controlling his senses, engaged in deep and devout meditation (According Hindu philosophy, one by virtue of yoga and selfcontrol can realise many great things which are beyond ordinary human conception. Beholding to Human unhurt though assailed incessantly with terrible shafts, Indrajit at once jumped at the conclusion that he must be a great spirit in a monkey-form. To realise who he in reality was, he gagged in yoga or devout meditation) (to realise the true identity of Hanumān).

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मतिं राक्षसराजसूनु;श्चकार तस्मिन्हरिवीरमुख्ये
अवध्यतां तस्य कपेः समीक्ष्य; कथं निगच्छेदिति निग्रहार्थम्
verses.transliteration:
tato matiṁ rākṣasarājasūnu;ścakāra tasminharivīramukhye
avadhyatāṁ tasya kapeḥ samīkṣya; kathaṁ nigacchediti nigrahārtham

translations.english: Thereupon, that son of the lord of Rākşasas pinned his thoughts upon that foremost of monkeys, and finding him incapable of being slain, he began to devise plans how he could be bound.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पैतामहां वीरः सोऽस्त्रमस्त्रविदां वरः
संदधे सुमहातेजास्तं हरिप्रवरं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paitāmahāṁ vīraḥ so'stramastravidāṁ varaḥ
saṁdadhe sumahātejāstaṁ haripravaraṁ prati

translations.english: And that hero, foremost of those versed in the use of weapons, discharged at that best of monkeys the highly powerful weapon conferred on him by Brahmă, the Great-father of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अवध्योऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा तमस्त्रेणास्त्रतत्त्ववित्
निजग्राह महाबाहुर्मारुतात्मजमिन्द्रजित्
verses.transliteration:
avadhyo'yamiti jñātvā tamastreṇāstratattvavit
nijagrāha mahābāhurmārutātmajamindrajit

translations.english: And knowing him incapable of being slain, Indrajit conversant with the use of weapons, bound that large-armed son of the Wind-god with that weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन बद्धस्ततोऽस्त्रेण राक्षसेन स वानरः
अभवन्निर्विचेष्टश्च पपात च महीतले
verses.transliteration:
tena baddhastato'streṇa rākṣasena sa vānaraḥ
abhavannirviceṣṭaśca papāta ca mahītale

translations.english: And being bound up by that Rākşasa with the weapon, the monkey became motionless and fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽथ बुद्ध्वा स तदास्त्रबन्धं; प्रभोः प्रभावाद्विगताल्पवेगः
पितामहानुग्रहमात्मनश्च; विचिन्तयामास हरिप्रवीरः
verses.transliteration:
tato'tha buddhvā sa tadāstrabandhaṁ; prabhoḥ prabhāvādvigatālpavegaḥ
pitāmahānugrahamātmanaśca; vicintayāmāsa haripravīraḥ

translations.english: And thinking that he was bound up with a Brahma weapon, he did not feel the least pain in consequence of Brahmā's blessing.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स्वायम्भुवैर्मन्त्रैर्ब्रह्मास्त्रमभिमन्त्रितम्
हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास वरदानं पितामहात्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ svāyambhuvairmantrairbrahmāstramabhimantritam
hanūmāṁścintayāmāsa varadānaṁ pitāmahāt

translations.english: And that heroic monkey began to think of the boons conferred on him by the Great-father of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
स वीर्यमस्त्रस्य कपिर्विचार्य; पितामहानुग्रहमात्मनश्च
विमोक्षशक्तिं परिचिन्तयित्वा; पितामहाज्ञामनुवर्तते स्म
verses.transliteration:
sa vīryamastrasya kapirvicārya; pitāmahānugrahamātmanaśca
vimokṣaśaktiṁ paricintayitvā; pitāmahājñāmanuvartate sma

translations.english: And thinking that the weapon was conferred by the Self-create and consecrated by sacred Mantras, Hanuman began to think of boons conferred by the Great-father. “In consequence of the power of the Lord of creation I am incapable of extricating myself from these bonds." (Knowing this by means of devout mediation, he reflected again)-“This has been ordained by Him, and I must put up with this pain for sometime.” Revolving well the power of the weapon, the boon of the Great-father, and his own prowess to extricate himself from bonds, the monkey followed the Great-father's behest.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रेणापि हि बद्धस्य भयं मम न जायते
पितामहमहेन्द्राभ्यां रक्षितस्यानिलेन च
verses.transliteration:
astreṇāpi hi baddhasya bhayaṁ mama na jāyate
pitāmahamahendrābhyāṁ rakṣitasyānilena ca

translations.english: I do not fear though bound by this weapon, since I am being protected by Brahmā, Indra and the Wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
ग्रहणे चापि रक्षोभिर्महन्मे गुणदर्शनम्
राक्षसेन्द्रेण संवादस्तस्माद्गृह्णन्तु मां परे
verses.transliteration:
grahaṇe cāpi rakṣobhirmahanme guṇadarśanam
rākṣasendreṇa saṁvādastasmādgṛhṇantu māṁ pare

translations.english: It will be better if I am carried off by the Rākşasas, for I shall reap very great benefit by my conversation with the lord of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स निश्चितार्थः परवीरहन्ता; समीक्ष्य करी विनिवृत्तचेष्टः
परैः प्रसह्याभिगतैर्निगृह्य; ननाद तैस्तैः परिभर्त्स्यमानः
verses.transliteration:
sa niścitārthaḥ paravīrahantā; samīkṣya karī vinivṛttaceṣṭaḥ
paraiḥ prasahyābhigatairnigṛhya; nanāda taistaiḥ paribhartsyamānaḥ

translations.english: "Therefore let the enemies carry me." Having resolved this, the considerate (monkey)-slayer of foes—remained motionless. And being ruthlessly bound by the foes and remonstrated with by them, he began to moan piteously.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा निर्विचेष्टमरिंदमम्
बबन्धुः शणवल्कैश्च द्रुमचीरैश्च संहतैः
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ rākṣasā dṛṣṭvā nirviceṣṭamariṁdamam
babandhuḥ śaṇavalkaiśca drumacīraiśca saṁhataiḥ

translations.english: And beholding that slayer of foes motionless, the Rakşasas bound him up with cotton and bark.

verses.sanskrit:
स रोचयामास परैश्च बन्धनं; प्रसह्य वीरैरभिनिग्रहं च
कौतूहलान्मां यदि राक्षसेन्द्रो; द्रष्टुं व्यवस्येदिति निश्चितार्थः
verses.transliteration:
sa rocayāmāsa paraiśca bandhanaṁ; prasahya vīrairabhinigrahaṁ ca
kautūhalānmāṁ yadi rākṣasendro; draṣṭuṁ vyavasyediti niścitārthaḥ

translations.english: And he gladly allowed himself to be tied up and rebuked by his enemies, thinking that he might converse with the lord of the Rākşasas, if he, out of curiosity, should like to see him.

verses.sanskrit:
स बद्धस्तेन वल्केन विमुक्तोऽस्त्रेण वीर्यवान्
अस्त्रबन्धः स चान्यं हि न बन्धमनुवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
sa baddhastena valkena vimukto'streṇa vīryavān
astrabandhaḥ sa cānyaṁ hi na bandhamanuvartate

translations.english: Being bound with bark, that powerful (monkey) got himself freed from the binding of the weapon, for the binding force of a Brahma weapon becomes null when there is any other binding.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो महत्कर्म कृतं निरर्थकं; न राक्षसैर्मन्त्रगतिर्विमृष्टा
पुनश्च नास्त्रे विहतेऽस्त्रमन्य;त्प्रवर्तते संशयिताः स्म सर्वे
verses.transliteration:
aho mahatkarma kṛtaṁ nirarthakaṁ; na rākṣasairmantragatirvimṛṣṭā
punaśca nāstre vihate'stramanya;tpravartate saṁśayitāḥ sma sarve

translations.english: Beholding that best of monkeys tied up with bark and liberated from the binding of the weapon Indrajit reflected that the binding force of the Brahma weapon became powerless when there was any other binding. “Alas, (those Räkşas) have rendered my mighty deed fruitless. They know not the action of Mantras. (That the action of a Brahma mantra upon one is multified if one is bound physically) And on the Brahma weapon being baffled, any other weapon cannot effect anything; and thus we thus we have all been placed in a critical predicament."

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रेण हनुमान्मुक्तो नात्मानमवबुध्यते
कृष्यमाणस्तु रक्षोभिस्तैश्च बन्धैर्निपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
astreṇa hanumānmukto nātmānamavabudhyate
kṛṣyamāṇastu rakṣobhistaiśca bandhairnipīḍitaḥ

translations.english: On being released from the weapon, Hanumān did not betray any signs of his liberation, albeit he was pulled by the Rākşasas and pained by the bonds they had bound him with. And the monkey, Hanumān, was pulled by those cruel Rākṣasas having fatal boxes, in the direction of the lord of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अथेन्द्रजित्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य मुक्त;मस्त्रेण बद्धं द्रुमचीरसूत्रैः
व्यदर्शयत्तत्र महाबलं तं; हरिप्रवीरं सगणाय राज्ञे
verses.transliteration:
athendrajittaṁ prasamīkṣya mukta;mastreṇa baddhaṁ drumacīrasūtraiḥ
vyadarśayattatra mahābalaṁ taṁ; haripravīraṁ sagaṇāya rājñe

translations.english: Seeing (Hanuman) freed from the (Brahma) weapon yet bound by the bark of trees, he (Indrajit) showed the exceedingly powerful and highly heroic monkey to the king along with his adherents.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं बद्धं कपिवरोत्तमम्
राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ mattamiva mātaṅgaṁ baddhaṁ kapivarottamam
rākṣasā rākṣasendrāya rāvaṇāya nyavedayan

translations.english: And the Rākṣasas related to the ruler of Rākșas everything touching that foremost of choice monkeys, resembling a mad elephant who was in bonds.

verses.sanskrit:
कोऽयं कस्य कुतो वापि किं कार्यं को व्यपाश्रयः
इति राक्षसवीराणां तत्र संजज्ञिरे कथाः
verses.transliteration:
ko'yaṁ kasya kuto vāpi kiṁ kāryaṁ ko vyapāśrayaḥ
iti rākṣasavīrāṇāṁ tatra saṁjajñire kathāḥ

translations.english: “Who is he? And whose son? And where from? And what's his errand? And by whom is he backed?” Thus did the heroic Rākşasas converse on beholding Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीत्य मार्गं सहसा महात्मा; स तत्र रक्षोऽधिपपादमूले
ददर्श राज्ञः परिचारवृद्धा;न्गृहं महारत्नविभूषितं च
verses.transliteration:
atītya mārgaṁ sahasā mahātmā; sa tatra rakṣo'dhipapādamūle
dadarśa rājñaḥ paricāravṛddhā;ngṛhaṁ mahāratnavibhūṣitaṁ ca

translations.english: And others said, "Kill him," "Burn him," "Eat him up". The Raksasas, growing enraged, thus said to each other. Having passed some way, that magnanimous one saw there old servants sitting at the feet of the lord of Rākşasas, as well as a mansion embellished with countless jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श महातेजा रावणः कपिसत्तमम्
रक्षोभिर्विकृताकारैः कृष्यमाणमितस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ kapisattamam
rakṣobhirvikṛtākāraiḥ kṛṣyamāṇamitastataḥ

translations.english: And the exceedingly energetic Rāvana saw that foremost of monkeys dragged hither and thither by Rākṣasas of frightful forms.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाधिपतिं चापि ददर्श कपिसत्तमः
तेजोबलसमायुक्तं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasādhipatiṁ cāpi dadarśa kapisattamaḥ
tejobalasamāyuktaṁ tapantamiva bhāskaram

translations.english: And that best of monkeys too saw that lord of Rākşasas, endowed with strength and energy and resembling the resplendent sun.

verses.sanskrit:
स रोषसंवर्तितताम्रदृष्टि;र्दशाननस्तं कपिमन्ववेक्ष्य
अथोपविष्टान्कुलशीलवृद्धा;न्समादिशत्तं प्रति मन्त्रमुख्यान्
verses.transliteration:
sa roṣasaṁvartitatāmradṛṣṭi;rdaśānanastaṁ kapimanvavekṣya
athopaviṣṭānkulaśīlavṛddhā;nsamādiśattaṁ prati mantramukhyān

translations.english: And with his reddened eyes rolling, the tennecked one, gazing at that monkey, ordered his principal counsellors, boasting of high pedigree and noble character, (to interrogate the incomer).

verses.sanskrit:
यथाक्रमं तैः स कपिश्च पृष्टः; कार्यार्थमर्थस्य च मूलमादौ
निवेदयामास हरीश्वरस्य; दूतः सकाशादहमागतोऽस्मि
verses.transliteration:
yathākramaṁ taiḥ sa kapiśca pṛṣṭaḥ; kāryārthamarthasya ca mūlamādau
nivedayāmāsa harīśvarasya; dūtaḥ sakāśādahamāgato'smi

translations.english: And by turns questioned by them as to his mission and purpose, as well as the fundamental occasion (of his in road), that foremost of monkeys replied, “A messenger, I come (from Sugriva.)"

verses.sanskrit:
अपश्यद्राक्षसपतिं हनूमानतितेजसं
विष्ठितं मेरुशिखरे सतोयमिव तोयदम्
verses.transliteration:
apaśyadrākṣasapatiṁ hanūmānatitejasaṁ
viṣṭhitaṁ meruśikhare satoyamiva toyadam

translations.english: Hanumān beheld the immensely energetic lord of Rākşasas surrounded (on all sides by his advisers), like a cloud containing water on a summit of Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः संपीड्यमानोऽपि रक्षोभिर्भीमविक्रमैः
विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रक्षोऽधिपमवैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ saṁpīḍyamāno'pi rakṣobhirbhīmavikramaiḥ
vismayaṁ paramaṁ gatvā rakṣo'dhipamavaikṣata

translations.english: Undergoing exceeding trouble at the hands of the Rākṣasa of dreadful prowess, (Hanumān) struck with mighty amaze, gazed at the lord of Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्राजमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा हनुमान्राक्षसेश्वरम्
मनसा चिन्तयामास तेजसा तस्य मोहितः
verses.transliteration:
bhrājamānaṁ tato dṛṣṭvā hanumānrākṣaseśvaram
manasā cintayāmāsa tejasā tasya mohitaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the sovereign of Rākşasas, appearing splendid, Hanuman, bewildered by his effulgence, mentally reflected.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यधर्मो न बलवान्स्यादयं राक्षसेश्वरः
स्यादयं सुरलोकस्य सशक्रस्यापि रक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
yadyadharmo na balavānsyādayaṁ rākṣaseśvaraḥ
syādayaṁ suralokasya saśakrasyāpi rakṣitā

translations.english: Ah! the form! Ah! the patience! Ah! the strength! Ah! the splendour! Ah! the entire auspiciousness of the king of Rākşasas! If the lord of Rākṣasas were not impious to the height, this one could well be the protector themselves of the celestial regions with Śakra.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन बिभ्यति खल्वस्माल्लोकाः सामरदानवाः
अयं ह्युत्सहते क्रुद्धः कर्तुमेकार्णवं जगत्
verses.transliteration:
tena bibhyati khalvasmāllokāḥ sāmaradānavāḥ
ayaṁ hyutsahate kruddhaḥ kartumekārṇavaṁ jagat

translations.english: But in consequence of the fell and remorseless acts of this one, which are the aversion of very one, all the worlds with gods and demons hold him in fear. This one, being angered, dares to convert this earth into one entire ocean." Beholding the potency of the Rākṣasa king of immeasurable prowess, the intelligent monkey thus indulged in a variety of thought.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुद्वीक्ष्य महाबाहुः पिङ्गाक्षं पुरतः स्थितम्
रोषेण महताविष्टो रावणो लोकरावणः
verses.transliteration:
tamudvīkṣya mahābāhuḥ piṅgākṣaṁ purataḥ sthitam
roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭo rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the tawny-eyed one staying before him, the mighty-armed Ravana, affrighter of (the worlds), was overwhelmed with fierce wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा रोषताम्राक्षः प्रहस्तं मन्त्रिसत्तमम्
कालयुक्तमुवाचेदं वचो विपुलमर्थवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā roṣatāmrākṣaḥ prahastaṁ mantrisattamam
kālayuktamuvācedaṁ vaco vipulamarthavat

translations.english: And with his eyes coppery with rage, the king asked his foreniost counsellor Prahasta, in words fraught with sense and suiting the season,

verses.sanskrit:
दुरात्मा पृच्छ्यतामेष कुतः किं वास्य कारणम्
वनभङ्गे च कोऽस्यार्थो राक्षसीनां च तर्जने
verses.transliteration:
durātmā pṛcchyatāmeṣa kutaḥ kiṁ vāsya kāraṇam
vanabhaṅge ca ko'syārtho rākṣasīnāṁ ca tarjane

translations.english: Ask this wicked-minded one, whence is he? And what led him to ravage the grove, and what was his object in brow-beating the Rākşasas? And what has been his purpose in entering my metropolis incapable of being subdued; and what for did he also fight (with my retainers?) Do you ask the wicked-minded one about this.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्तो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते न भीः कार्या त्वया कपे
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasto vākyamabravīt
samāśvasihi bhadraṁ te na bhīḥ kāryā tvayā kape

translations.english: Hearing Ravana's speech, Prahasta said, “Take heart! Fair fortune to you! You need not be alarmed, O monkey."

verses.sanskrit:
यदि तावत्त्वमिन्द्रेण प्रेषितो रावणालयम्
तत्त्वमाख्याहि मा ते भूद्भयं वानर मोक्ष्यसे
verses.transliteration:
yadi tāvattvamindreṇa preṣito rāvaṇālayam
tattvamākhyāhi mā te bhūdbhayaṁ vānara mokṣyase

translations.english: If you had been sent to Rāvana's residence by Indra, tell us truly everything. Let no fear, O imonkey, be yours. You shall be liberated.

verses.sanskrit:
विष्णुना प्रेषितो वापि दूतो विजयकाङ्क्षिणा
न हि ते वानरं तेजो रूपमात्रं तु वानरम्
verses.transliteration:
viṣṇunā preṣito vāpi dūto vijayakāṅkṣiṇā
na hi te vānaraṁ tejo rūpamātraṁ tu vānaram

translations.english: If you belong to Vaisravana, or to Yama, or to Varuņa, and had entered into this city of ours disguising (your proper shape), or if you had been despatched by Vişnu burning for victory, (tell us this truly). Your prowess is certainly not hat of a monkey, your form alone is that of a monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो हरिवरस्तदा रक्षोगणेश्वरम्
अब्रवीन्नास्मि शक्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य वा
verses.transliteration:
evamukto harivarastadā rakṣogaṇeśvaram
abravīnnāsmi śakrasya yamasya varuṇasya vā

translations.english: Unfold this (to us) faithfully, O monkey, and you shall get (back) your liberty. But if you should say aught untruthful, your life shall pay dear for it. Or tell us wherefore you had entered into Rāvana's mansion. Thus addressed then that foremost of monkeys said to the lord of Rāks asas, “I am not Sakra's, nor Yama's, nor Varuna's. I have no friendship with Dhanada, (Lit.-giver of wealth-a designation of Kubera) nor have I been despatched by Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः प्राप्ता बलिनो युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः
रक्षणार्थं च देहस्य प्रतियुद्धा मया रणे
verses.transliteration:
tataste rākṣasāḥ prāptā balino yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
rakṣaṇārthaṁ ca dehasya pratiyuddhā mayā raṇe

translations.english: This is my race; and I have come hither a monkey for obtaining a, sight of the Rākṣasa chief. And it is to attain a sight of the Rākṣasa lord that I have destroyed his peerless grove; and it is for this that, the powerful Rākşasas seeking for fight, I for the preservation of my person have resisted them in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रपाशैर्न शक्योऽहं बद्धुं देवासुरैरपि
पितामहादेव वरो ममाप्येषोऽभ्युपागतः
verses.transliteration:
astrapāśairna śakyo'haṁ baddhuṁ devāsurairapi
pitāmahādeva varo mamāpyeṣo'bhyupāgataḥ

translations.english: I am incapable of being slain with weapons even by the celestials and the Asuras themselves. This boon I also (like yourself) happen to have received from the Great-father.

verses.sanskrit:
राजानं द्रष्टुकामेन मयास्त्रमनुवर्तितम्
विमुक्तो अहमस्त्रेण राक्षसैस्त्वतिपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
rājānaṁ draṣṭukāmena mayāstramanuvartitam
vimukto ahamastreṇa rākṣasaistvatipīḍitaḥ

translations.english: It is because I was desirous of seeing the king that I have suffered this weapon to restrain me. Although the Rākşasas have brought me (hither thus), yet I am free from any weapon (restraining me).

verses.sanskrit:
दूतोऽहमिति विज्ञेयो राघवस्यामितौजसः
श्रूयतां चापि वचनं मम पथ्यमिदं प्रभो
verses.transliteration:
dūto'hamiti vijñeyo rāghavasyāmitaujasaḥ
śrūyatāṁ cāpi vacanaṁ mama pathyamidaṁ prabho

translations.english: I come near you on a certain business of Rāma. Knowing me for a messenger of Rāghava endowed with measureless prowess, do you, O lord, listen to my words, calculated to work your profit.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समीक्ष्य महासत्त्वं सत्त्ववान्हरिसत्तमः
वाक्यमर्थवदव्यग्रस्तमुवाच दशाननम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samīkṣya mahāsattvaṁ sattvavānharisattamaḥ
vākyamarthavadavyagrastamuvāca daśānanam

translations.english: Seeing the Ten-necked one of mighty energy, that foremost of monkeys, endued with strength, calmly spoke to him words containing sense,

verses.sanskrit:
अहं सुग्रीवसंदेशादिह प्राप्तस्तवालयम्
राक्षसेन्द्र हरीशस्त्वां भ्राता कुशलमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ sugrīvasaṁdeśādiha prāptastavālayam
rākṣasendra harīśastvāṁ bhrātā kuśalamabravīt

translations.english: I have come to you at you command of Sugriva, O lord of Raksasas. Your brother, the king of monkeys, enquires after your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुः शृणु समादेशं सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
धर्मार्थोपहितं वाक्यमिह चामुत्र च क्षमम्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātuḥ śṛṇu samādeśaṁ sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
dharmārthopahitaṁ vākyamiha cāmutra ca kṣamam

translations.english: Listen to the desire of your brother, the highsouled Sugrīva, and his words fraught with righteous sense and capable of working one's good here and hercafter.

verses.sanskrit:
राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्
पितेव बन्धुर्लोकस्य सुरेश्वरसमद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
rājā daśaratho nāma rathakuñjaravājimān
piteva bandhurlokasya sureśvarasamadyutiḥ

translations.english: King Dasaratha, master of cars and elephants and steeds, is the friend of all like to their father, and is furnished with the splendour of the sovereign of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठस्तस्य महाबाहुः पुत्रः प्रियकरः प्रभुः
पितुर्निदेशान्निष्क्रान्तः प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhastasya mahābāhuḥ putraḥ priyakaraḥ prabhuḥ
piturnideśānniṣkrāntaḥ praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam

translations.english: His eldest son, mighty-armed, and masterful, the darling (of his sire), has, in accordance with his father's order, entered the forest of Dandaka with his brother Lakşmaņa and his wife Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य भार्या वने नष्टा सीता पतिमनुव्रता
वैदेहस्य सुता राज्ञो जनकस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
tasya bhāryā vane naṣṭā sītā patimanuvratā
vaidehasya sutā rājño janakasya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: His name is Rāma, and he is exceedingly energetic, and ever abide on the path of virtue. His spouse, the celebrated Sītā, daughter to Vaideha, the high-souled king Janaka, either died or was carried off in Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
स मार्गमाणस्तां देवीं राजपुत्रः सहानुजः
ऋश्यमूकमनुप्राप्तः सुग्रीवेण च संगतः
verses.transliteration:
sa mārgamāṇastāṁ devīṁ rājaputraḥ sahānujaḥ
ṛśyamūkamanuprāptaḥ sugrīveṇa ca saṁgataḥ

translations.english: Seeking for that exalted lady, the king's son, accompanied by this younger brother, arriving at Rşyamūka, met with Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तेन प्रतिज्ञातं सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्
सुग्रीवस्यापि रामेण हरिराज्यं निवेदितम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tena pratijñātaṁ sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam
sugrīvasyāpi rāmeṇa harirājyaṁ niveditam

translations.english: And Sugrīva promised that he would undertake the search for Sītă, and Rāma (on his part promised) that he would confer on Sugrīva the kingdom of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेन मृधे हत्वा राजपुत्रेण वालिनम्
सुग्रीवः स्थापितो राज्ये हर्यृक्षाणां गणेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tatastena mṛdhe hatvā rājaputreṇa vālinam
sugrīvaḥ sthāpito rājye haryṛkṣāṇāṁ gaṇeśvaraḥ

translations.english: And, thereupon, slaying Vāli in battle, the king's son established Sugrīva as the lord of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स सीतामार्गणे व्यग्रः सुग्रीवः सत्यसंगरः
हरीन्संप्रेषयामास दिशः सर्वा हरीश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa sītāmārgaṇe vyagraḥ sugrīvaḥ satyasaṁgaraḥ
harīnsaṁpreṣayāmāsa diśaḥ sarvā harīśvaraḥ

translations.english: And, thereupon, the lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, true to his vow, eager for searching Sītā, despatched monkeys in all directions.

verses.sanskrit:
तां हरीणां सहस्राणि शतानि नियुतानि च
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते अधश्चोपरि चाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ harīṇāṁ sahasrāṇi śatāni niyutāni ca
dikṣu sarvāsu mārgante adhaścopari cāmbare

translations.english: And thousands and hundreds and niyutas of monkeys are exploring all sides, below and above in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
वैनतेय समाः केचित्केचित्तत्रानिलोपमाः
असंगगतयः शीघ्रा हरिवीरा महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
vainateya samāḥ kecitkecittatrānilopamāḥ
asaṁgagatayaḥ śīghrā harivīrā mahābalāḥ

translations.english: Some are like Vinata's offspring, (Garuda) and some like the Wind; their Course is incapable of being resisted; and those heroic monkeys are endued with strength and celerity.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु हनुमान्नाम मारुतस्यौरसः सुतः
सीतायास्तु कृते तूर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्
समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वैव तां दिदृक्षुरिहागतः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu hanumānnāma mārutasyaurasaḥ sutaḥ
sītāyāstu kṛte tūrṇaṁ śatayojanamāyatam
samudraṁ laṅghayitvaiva tāṁ didṛkṣurihāgataḥ

translations.english: I, Hanumān my name, am the son of the Wind-god. For Sitã, I, desirous of seeing her, have come hither, bounding over the main measuring a full hundred Yojanas. And as I was roving, I came to see Janaka's daughter in your house.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्भवान्दृष्टधर्मार्थस्तपः कृतपरिग्रहः
परदारान्महाप्राज्ञ नोपरोद्धुं त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tadbhavāndṛṣṭadharmārthastapaḥ kṛtaparigrahaḥ
paradārānmahāprājña noparoddhuṁ tvamarhasi

translations.english: You are cognisant of righteousness and interest, and had attained prosperity through your asceticism. Therefore, O eminently wise one, you ought not to confine another's wife.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि धर्मविरुद्धेषु बह्वपायेषु कर्मसु
मूलघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः
verses.transliteration:
na hi dharmaviruddheṣu bahvapāyeṣu karmasu
mūlaghātiṣu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ

translations.english: Actions opposed to righteousness, and bringing on countless evils, and causing extermination, ill become persons of your sort.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्च लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां रामकोपानुवर्तिनाम्
शराणामग्रतः स्थातुं शक्तो देवासुरेष्वपि
verses.transliteration:
kaśca lakṣmaṇamuktānāṁ rāmakopānuvartinām
śarāṇāmagrataḥ sthātuṁ śakto devāsureṣvapi

translations.english: Who is there even among celestials and Asuras that is competent to stay before the shafts shot by Lakşmaņa and Rāma in wrath?

verses.sanskrit:
न चापि त्रिषु लोकेषु राजन्विद्येत कश्चन
राघवस्य व्यलीकं यः कृत्वा सुखमवाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
na cāpi triṣu lokeṣu rājanvidyeta kaścana
rāghavasya vyalīkaṁ yaḥ kṛtvā sukhamavāpnuyāt

translations.english: There is none, O king, in all the three worlds, that is capable of attaining ease, after inflicting injury on Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्रिकालहितं वाक्यं धर्म्यमर्थानुबन्धि च
मन्यस्व नरदेवाय जानकी प्रतिदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
tattrikālahitaṁ vākyaṁ dharmyamarthānubandhi ca
manyasva naradevāya jānakī pratidīyatām

translations.english: Treading the path of virtue and profit, do you pay heed to my speech fraught with good for three times; (Present, past, and future) and do you return Jānaki to that foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टा हीयं मया देवी लब्धं यदिह दुर्लभम्
उत्तरं कर्म यच्छेषं निमित्तं तत्र राघवः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭā hīyaṁ mayā devī labdhaṁ yadiha durlabham
uttaraṁ karma yaccheṣaṁ nimittaṁ tatra rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Seen have I this exalted lady, which was difficult to compass. As for what remain to be done, Rāma himself shall bring it about.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्षितेयं मया सीता तथा शोकपरायणा
गृह्य यां नाभिजानासि पञ्चास्यामिव पन्नगीम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣiteyaṁ mayā sītā tathā śokaparāyaṇā
gṛhya yāṁ nābhijānāsi pañcāsyāmiva pannagīm

translations.english: That Sītā I have beheld overwhelmed with grief, whom, albeit resembling a five-hooded serpent in your mansion, you know not.

verses.sanskrit:
नेयं जरयितुं शक्या सासुरैरमरैरपि
विषसंसृष्टमत्यर्थं भुक्तमन्नमिवौजसा
verses.transliteration:
neyaṁ jarayituṁ śakyā sāsurairamarairapi
viṣasaṁsṛṣṭamatyarthaṁ bhuktamannamivaujasā

translations.english: And even as food thoroughly mixed with poison, being taken, is incapable of being digested, this one is incapable of being subdued even by the celestials and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
तपःसंतापलब्धस्ते योऽयं धर्मपरिग्रहः
न स नाशयितुं न्याय्य आत्मप्राणपरिग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
tapaḥsaṁtāpalabdhaste yo'yaṁ dharmaparigrahaḥ
na sa nāśayituṁ nyāyya ātmaprāṇaparigrahaḥ

translations.english: It is not proper to destroy religious merit reaped by undergoing extreme mortification, as well as access of life attained by the same means). (By such an iniquitous act as this.)

verses.sanskrit:
अवध्यतां तपोभिर्यां भवान्समनुपश्यति
आत्मनः सासुरैर्देवैर्हेतुस्तत्राप्ययं महान्
verses.transliteration:
avadhyatāṁ tapobhiryāṁ bhavānsamanupaśyati
ātmanaḥ sāsurairdevairhetustatrāpyayaṁ mahān

translations.english: You deem yourself by virtue of your asceticism incapable of being destroyed by the celestials and Asuras; and herein your great merit (incident to they austerities) is the cause.

verses.sanskrit:
मानुषो राघवो राजन्सुग्रीवश्च हरीश्वरः
तस्मात्प्राणपरित्राणं कथं राजन्करिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
mānuṣo rāghavo rājansugrīvaśca harīśvaraḥ
tasmātprāṇaparitrāṇaṁ kathaṁ rājankariṣyasi

translations.english: But Sugrīva is not a god or a Yakṣa or a Rākşasa. Rāghava, O king, is a mortal and Sugrīva is the lord of monkeys. How can you, O king, save your-life from them.

verses.sanskrit:
न तु धर्मोपसंहारमधर्मफलसंहितम्
तदेव फलमन्वेति धर्मश्चाधर्मनाशनः
verses.transliteration:
na tu dharmopasaṁhāramadharmaphalasaṁhitam
tadeva phalamanveti dharmaścādharmanāśanaḥ

translations.english: He that, confiding in his strength, commit himself to foul proceedings, cannot count upon his righteous deeds, but his evil ones follow him.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तं धर्मफलं तावद्भवता नात्र संशयः
फलमस्याप्यधर्मस्य क्षिप्रमेव प्रपत्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
prāptaṁ dharmaphalaṁ tāvadbhavatā nātra saṁśayaḥ
phalamasyāpyadharmasya kṣiprameva prapatsyase

translations.english: Virtue destroy vice, (yet vice like yours destroy all virtue). (The parenthetical part is the commentator's filling in of the deficiency in the sentiment) You, without doubt, had obtained the fruit of your righteousness, and the fruit also of this iniquity you shall reap without delay.

verses.sanskrit:
जनस्थानवधं बुद्ध्वा बुद्ध्वा वालिवधं तथा
रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च बुध्यस्व हितमात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
janasthānavadhaṁ buddhvā buddhvā vālivadhaṁ tathā
rāmasugrīvasakhyaṁ ca budhyasva hitamātmanaḥ

translations.english: And taking to heart the carnage in Janasthāna and the slaying of Vāli as well as the friendship of Rāma with Sugrīva, do you understand yours own good.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं खल्वहमप्येकः सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम्
लङ्कां नाशयितुं शक्तस्तस्यैष तु विनिश्चयः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ khalvahamapyekaḥ savājirathakuñjarām
laṅkāṁ nāśayituṁ śaktastasyaiṣa tu viniścayaḥ

translations.english: I, alone that I am, can at my will destroy Lankā with her steeds and elephants and cars; but he whose envoy I am has not yet decided on this point.

verses.sanskrit:
रामेण हि प्रतिज्ञातं हर्यृक्षगणसंनिधौ
उत्सादनममित्राणां सीता यैस्तु प्रधर्षिता
verses.transliteration:
rāmeṇa hi pratijñātaṁ haryṛkṣagaṇasaṁnidhau
utsādanamamitrāṇāṁ sītā yaistu pradharṣitā

translations.english: Rāma has in presence of the tawny-eyed (ones) forsooth promised the annihilation of the foe by whom Sītā has been sore oppressed.

verses.sanskrit:
अपकुर्वन्हि रामस्य साक्षादपि पुरंदरः
न सुखं प्राप्नुयादन्यः किं पुनस्त्वद्विधो जनः
verses.transliteration:
apakurvanhi rāmasya sākṣādapi puraṁdaraḥ
na sukhaṁ prāpnuyādanyaḥ kiṁ punastvadvidho janaḥ

translations.english: On wronging Rāma, Purandara himself cannot escape scot-free, what shall I say of persons like you?

verses.sanskrit:
यां सीतेत्यभिजानासि येयं तिष्ठति ते वशे
कालरात्रीति तां विद्धि सर्वलङ्काविनाशिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ sītetyabhijānāsi yeyaṁ tiṣṭhati te vaśe
kālarātrīti tāṁ viddhi sarvalaṅkāvināśinīm

translations.english: Her-whom you know as Sītā staying in yours abode-know her for the Fatal Night that shall bring destruction down on all Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
तदलं कालपाशेन सीता विग्रहरूपिणा
स्वयं स्कन्धावसक्तेन क्षममात्मनि चिन्त्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
tadalaṁ kālapāśena sītā vigraharūpiṇā
svayaṁ skandhāvasaktena kṣamamātmani cintyatām

translations.english: Therefore, beware of yourself turning about your neck the fatal noose in the shape of Sītā! Do you rather study your welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतायास्तेजसा दग्धां रामकोपप्रपीडिताम्
दह्यमनामिमां पश्य पुरीं साट्टप्रतोलिकाम्
verses.transliteration:
sītāyāstejasā dagdhāṁ rāmakopaprapīḍitām
dahyamanāmimāṁ paśya purīṁ sāṭṭapratolikām

translations.english: You shall behold this city crowned with edifices and stalls, in flames fed by the wrath of Rāma, and consumed by the energy of Şītā.

verses.sanskrit:
स सौष्ठवोपेतमदीनवादिनः; कपेर्निशम्याप्रतिमोऽप्रियं वचः
दशाननः कोपविवृत्तलोचनः; समादिशत्तस्य वधं महाकपेः
verses.transliteration:
sa sauṣṭhavopetamadīnavādinaḥ; kaperniśamyāpratimo'priyaṁ vacaḥ
daśānanaḥ kopavivṛttalocanaḥ; samādiśattasya vadhaṁ mahākapeḥ

translations.english: Hearing the distasteful yet excellent speech of the bold and matchless monkey, the ten-necked one, with his eyes whirling in wrath, ordered the destruction of that mighty monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरस्य महात्मनः
आज्ञापयद्वधं तस्य रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vānarasya mahātmanaḥ
ājñāpayadvadhaṁ tasya rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of the high-souled monkey, Răvaņa, bereft of his senses by wrath, ordered that he should be put to death.

verses.sanskrit:
वधे तस्य समाज्ञप्ते रावणेन दुरात्मना
निवेदितवतो दौत्यं नानुमेने विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
vadhe tasya samājñapte rāvaṇena durātmanā
niveditavato dautyaṁ nānumene vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: On the death of that one who had proclaimed his own position of being an envoy, having been ordered by the wicked-minded Ravana, Vibhisana did not agree (with the decision).

verses.sanskrit:
तं रक्षोऽधिपतिं क्रुद्धं तच्च कार्यमुपस्थितम्
विदित्वा चिन्तयामास कार्यं कार्यविधौ स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rakṣo'dhipatiṁ kruddhaṁ tacca kāryamupasthitam
viditvā cintayāmāsa kāryaṁ kāryavidhau sthitaḥ

translations.english: And knowing that the lord of Rākşasas was wroth and that affair (The destruction of Hanuman) was at hand, Vibhisana, resolved to act according to justice, began to reflect as to what was to be done.

verses.sanskrit:
निश्चितार्थस्ततः साम्नापूज्य शत्रुजिदग्रजम्
उवाच हितमत्यर्थं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
verses.transliteration:
niścitārthastataḥ sāmnāpūjya śatrujidagrajam
uvāca hitamatyarthaṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ

translations.english: Having arrived at a decision, that one skilled in speech, paying homage to that conqueror of foes, his elder brother, spoke to him in words eminently good. “O lord of Rākṣasas, forgive me and renounce your wrath." (The commentator says, the passage means, ‘Give up your promise (to slay Hanumãn) and abate your anger.) Extend your favour to me, and hear these words of mine. Lords of the earth, endowed with integrity and knowing high and low, never put messengers to death,

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्धर्मविरुद्धं च लोकवृत्तेश्च गर्हितम्
तव चासदृशं वीर कपेरस्य प्रमापणम्
verses.transliteration:
rājandharmaviruddhaṁ ca lokavṛtteśca garhitam
tava cāsadṛśaṁ vīra kaperasya pramāpaṇam

translations.english: The taking the monkey's life, O king, is opposed to morality and repugnant to social usage; and it is also unworthy of yourself.

verses.sanskrit:
असंशयं शत्रुरयं प्रवृद्धः; कृतं ह्यनेनाप्रियमप्रमेयम्
न दूतवध्यां प्रवदन्ति सन्तो; दूतस्य दृष्टा बहवो हि दण्डाः
verses.transliteration:
asaṁśayaṁ śatrurayaṁ pravṛddhaḥ; kṛtaṁ hyanenāpriyamaprameyam
na dūtavadhyāṁ pravadanti santo; dūtasya dṛṣṭā bahavo hi daṇḍāḥ

translations.english: Surely this is an overgrown enemy; and he has perpetrated immense injury (to us). But say the good, envoys are not to be slain, albeit many are the punishments that have been assigned for messengers.

verses.sanskrit:
वैरूप्यामङ्गेषु कशाभिघातो; मौण्ड्यं तथा लक्ष्मणसंनिपातः
एतान्हि दूते प्रवदन्ति दण्डा;न्वधस्तु दूतस्य न नः श्रुतोऽपि
verses.transliteration:
vairūpyāmaṅgeṣu kaśābhighāto; mauṇḍyaṁ tathā lakṣmaṇasaṁnipātaḥ
etānhi dūte pravadanti daṇḍā;nvadhastu dūtasya na naḥ śruto'pi

translations.english: Disfigurement of the body, strips, shaving of the head, one of these or all combined, these are said to be the punishments that should be inflicted on envoys. But I have not heard of the punishment of death being a penalty of the envoy. as

verses.sanskrit:
कथं च धर्मार्थविनीतबुद्धिः; परावरप्रत्ययनिश्चितार्थः
भवद्विधः कोपवशे हि तिष्ठे;त्कोपं नियच्छन्ति हि सत्त्ववन्तः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ ca dharmārthavinītabuddhiḥ; parāvarapratyayaniścitārthaḥ
bhavadvidhaḥ kopavaśe hi tiṣṭhe;tkopaṁ niyacchanti hi sattvavantaḥ

translations.english: Why dose one like you, having one's intelligence rendered meek respects righteousness and profit, and capable of proceeding on certain decisions on the merits or otherwise of things, come under the sway of passion? Those possessed of power never give way to anger.

verses.sanskrit:
न धर्मवादे न च लोकवृत्ते; न शास्त्रबुद्धिग्रहणेषु वापि
विद्येत कश्चित्तव वीरतुल्य;स्त्वं ह्युत्तमः सर्वसुरासुराणाम्
verses.transliteration:
na dharmavāde na ca lokavṛtte; na śāstrabuddhigrahaṇeṣu vāpi
vidyeta kaścittava vīratulya;stvaṁ hyuttamaḥ sarvasurāsurāṇām

translations.english: Neither in religious discussion, nor in social concernis, nor in appropriating the right sense of the scriptures, is there any that can approach you, O hero-Verily you are the foremost among celestials and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
न चाप्यस्य कपेर्घाते कंचित्पश्याम्यहं गुणम्
तेष्वयं पात्यतां दण्डो यैरयं प्रेषितः कपिः
verses.transliteration:
na cāpyasya kaperghāte kaṁcitpaśyāmyahaṁ guṇam
teṣvayaṁ pātyatāṁ daṇḍo yairayaṁ preṣitaḥ kapiḥ

translations.english: Nor do I see any good that may likely accrue to us from the slaying of this monkey. Let your vengeance descend those that have despatched the monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
साधुर्वा यदि वासाधुर्परैरेष समर्पितः
ब्रुवन्परार्थं परवान्न दूतो वधमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
sādhurvā yadi vāsādhurparaireṣa samarpitaḥ
bruvanparārthaṁ paravānna dūto vadhamarhati

translations.english: Whether honest or otherwise, this one has been commissioned by others. Advocating interest not his own and identifying himself with another, an envoy dose not merit the being put to death.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्नास्य वधे यत्नः कार्यः परपुरंजय
भवान्सेन्द्रेषु देवेषु यत्नमास्थातुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
tasmānnāsya vadhe yatnaḥ kāryaḥ parapuraṁjaya
bhavānsendreṣu deveṣu yatnamāsthātumarhati

translations.english: O king, if this one be slain, no other skyranger whatever would show himself tous. Threfore, O captor of hostile capitals, do not seek to slay this one. You should spend yourself on celestials with Indra (at their head).

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्विनष्टे न हि दूतमन्यं; पश्यामि यस्तौ नरराजपुत्रौ
युद्धाय युद्धप्रियदुर्विनीता;वुद्योजयेद्दीर्घपथावरुद्धौ
verses.transliteration:
asminvinaṣṭe na hi dūtamanyaṁ; paśyāmi yastau nararājaputrau
yuddhāya yuddhapriyadurvinītā;vudyojayeddīrghapathāvaruddhau

translations.english: On his being killed, another see I not who, O you that love warfare, can move those haughty sons of a king to take up arms against you.

verses.sanskrit:
पराक्रमोत्साहमनस्विनां च; सुरासुराणामपि दुर्जयेन
त्वया मनोनन्दन नैरृतानां; युद्धायतिर्नाशयितुं न युक्ता
verses.transliteration:
parākramotsāhamanasvināṁ ca; surāsurāṇāmapi durjayena
tvayā manonandana nairṛtānāṁ; yuddhāyatirnāśayituṁ na yuktā

translations.english: And, O bringer-in of joy to the heart, it is not proper for you, invincible to celestials and Asuras gifted with prowess, high spirits and intelligence, to disappoint the Nairtas (as to their eagerness for encounter).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो महाबलः
देशकालहितं वाक्यं भ्रातुरुत्तममब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā daśagrīvo mahābalaḥ
deśakālahitaṁ vākyaṁ bhrāturuttamamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing those words of his, the high-souled ten-necked one spoke to his brother a speech consonant to season and place,

verses.sanskrit:
सम्यगुक्तं हि भवता दूतवध्या विगर्हिता
अवश्यं तु वधादन्यः क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
samyaguktaṁ hi bhavatā dūtavadhyā vigarhitā
avaśyaṁ tu vadhādanyaḥ kriyatāmasya nigrahaḥ

translations.english: Properly had you spoken, to slay a messenger is improper. But let him be punished with any chastisement save slaying.

verses.sanskrit:
कपीनां किल लाङ्गूलमिष्टं भवति भूषणम्
तदस्य दीप्यतां शीघ्रं तेन दग्धेन गच्छतु
verses.transliteration:
kapīnāṁ kila lāṅgūlamiṣṭaṁ bhavati bhūṣaṇam
tadasya dīpyatāṁ śīghraṁ tena dagdhena gacchatu

translations.english: Certainly the tail is a darling ornament to a monkey. Therefore let his tail be set on fire anon; and this having been consumed, let him go away.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पश्यन्त्विमं दीनमङ्गवैरूप्यकर्शितम्
समित्रा ज्ञातयः सर्वे बान्धवाः ससुहृज्जनाः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paśyantvimaṁ dīnamaṅgavairūpyakarśitam
samitrā jñātayaḥ sarve bāndhavāḥ sasuhṛjjanāḥ

translations.english: Then shall his best friends and kindred and acquaintances see him crest-fallen, with his person deformed.

verses.sanskrit:
आज्ञापयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः पुरं सर्वं सचत्वरम्
लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन रक्षोभिः परिणीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
ājñāpayadrākṣasendraḥ puraṁ sarvaṁ sacatvaram
lāṅgūlena pradīptena rakṣobhiḥ pariṇīyatām

translations.english: The lord of Rākşasas ordered, With his tail in flames, let this one be taken all round Lankā containing terraces.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसाः कोपकर्कशाः
वेष्टन्ते तस्य लाङ्गूलं जीर्णैः कार्पासिकैः पटैः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rākṣasāḥ kopakarkaśāḥ
veṣṭante tasya lāṅgūlaṁ jīrṇaiḥ kārpāsikaiḥ paṭaiḥ

translations.english: Hearing his words, the Raksasas, cruel through wrath, cover up his (Hanumān's) tail with worn pieces of cotton cloth.

verses.sanskrit:
संवेष्ट्यमाने लाङ्गूले व्यवर्धत महाकपिः
शुष्कमिन्धनमासाद्य वनेष्विव हुताशनः
verses.transliteration:
saṁveṣṭyamāne lāṅgūle vyavardhata mahākapiḥ
śuṣkamindhanamāsādya vaneṣviva hutāśanaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, even as fire in a forest increase on getting dry fuel, the mighty monkey grew in dimensions on his tail being wrapped up.

verses.sanskrit:
लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन राक्षसांस्तानपातयत्
रोषामर्षपरीतात्मा बालसूर्यसमाननः
verses.transliteration:
lāṅgūlena pradīptena rākṣasāṁstānapātayat
roṣāmarṣaparītātmā bālasūryasamānanaḥ

translations.english: Having soaked (the cloth) in oil, they set fire to it. Thereat with his soul overpowered with rage and hatred, and his countenance like the risen sun, he lashed them with his flaming tail.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूयः संगतैः क्रूरै राकसैर्हरिसत्तमः
निबद्धः कृतवान्वीरस्तत्कालसदृशीं मतिम्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūyaḥ saṁgataiḥ krūrai rākasairharisattamaḥ
nibaddhaḥ kṛtavānvīrastatkālasadṛśīṁ matim

translations.english: And those-rangers of the night-those Rākşasas-old and young and females-again bringing that foremost of monkey, grew exceedingly glad.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं खलु न मे शक्ता निबधस्यापि राक्षसाः
छित्त्वा पाशान्समुत्पत्य हन्यामहमिमान्पुनः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ khalu na me śaktā nibadhasyāpi rākṣasāḥ
chittvā pāśānsamutpatya hanyāmahamimānpunaḥ

translations.english: That hero (being bound), entertained a purpose in harmony with the season. "Albeit bound, the Rākşasas cannot forsooth cope with me. Snapping these bonds, I shall, darting up, again slaughter these."

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषामेव पर्याप्तो राक्षसानामहं युधि
किं तु रामस्य प्रीत्यर्थं विषहिष्येऽहमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
sarveṣāmeva paryāpto rākṣasānāmahaṁ yudhi
kiṁ tu rāmasya prītyarthaṁ viṣahiṣye'hamīdṛśam

translations.english: I can slay all these Rākşasas in battle; but I suffer this (maltreatment) for not marring the (pure delight) Rāma shall derive from my deed.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्का चरयितव्या मे पुनरेव भवेदिति
रात्रौ न हि सुदृष्टा मे दुर्गकर्मविधानतः
अवश्यमेव द्रष्टव्या मया लङ्का निशाक्षये
verses.transliteration:
laṅkā carayitavyā me punareva bhavediti
rātrau na hi sudṛṣṭā me durgakarmavidhānataḥ
avaśyameva draṣṭavyā mayā laṅkā niśākṣaye

translations.english: I shall once more range around Lankā. Let this be so. At night I could not satisfactorily examine the fortifications.* (Another meaning is:-lts places inaccessible on account of works.)

verses.sanskrit:
कामं बन्धैश्च मे भूयः पुच्छस्योद्दीपनेन च
पीडां कुर्वन्तु रक्षांसि न मेऽस्ति मनसः श्रमः
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ bandhaiśca me bhūyaḥ pucchasyoddīpanena ca
pīḍāṁ kurvantu rakṣāṁsi na me'sti manasaḥ śramaḥ

translations.english: For certain, by me is to be beheld Lankā when night has departed. Let them bind me anew. The Rākşasas pain me by setting fire to my tail; but my mind dose not tire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते संवृताकारं सत्त्ववन्तं महाकपिम्
परिगृह्य ययुर्हृष्टा राक्षसाः कपिकुञ्जरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataste saṁvṛtākāraṁ sattvavantaṁ mahākapim
parigṛhya yayurhṛṣṭā rākṣasāḥ kapikuñjaram

translations.english: Then the Raksasas, rejoicing greatly, went off, taking that mighty monkey endowed with strength, an elephant (in prowess) among monkeys. And blowing conchs and trumpets, and bruiting it abroad by various actions, (Publishing Hanuman's penalty) those Raksasas of cruel deeds took (Hanumān) about the city (of Lankā).

verses.sanskrit:
चत्वरेषु चतुष्केषु राजमार्गे तथैव च
घोषयन्ति कपिं सर्वे चारीक इति राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
catvareṣu catuṣkeṣu rājamārge tathaiva ca
ghoṣayanti kapiṁ sarve cārīka iti rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: And on terraces and highways the Rākṣasas proclaim the monkey, saying, “This is a spy.'

verses.sanskrit:
दीप्यमाने ततस्तस्य लाङ्गूलाग्रे हनूमतः
राक्षस्यस्ता विरूपाक्ष्यः शंसुर्देव्यास्तदप्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
dīpyamāne tatastasya lāṅgūlāgre hanūmataḥ
rākṣasyastā virūpākṣyaḥ śaṁsurdevyāstadapriyam

translations.english: On Hanumān's tail being in flames, Rākṣasīs of frightful eyes related to that exalted lady (Sītā) tidings of this great mishap.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्वया कृतसंवादः सीते ताम्रमुखः कपिः
लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन स एष परिणीयते
verses.transliteration:
yastvayā kṛtasaṁvādaḥ sīte tāmramukhaḥ kapiḥ
lāṅgūlena pradīptena sa eṣa pariṇīyate

translations.english: O Sītā, the copper-faced monkey with whom you hadst held talk, is being led around with his tail flaming,

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं क्रूरमात्मापहरणोपमम्
वैदेही शोकसंतप्ता हुताशनमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tadvacanaṁ krūramātmāpaharaṇopamam
vaidehī śokasaṁtaptā hutāśanamupāgamat

translations.english: Hearing these cruel words, like to loss of life, Vaidehi, burning in grief, approached the Fire.

verses.sanskrit:
मङ्गलाभिमुखी तस्य सा तदासीन्महाकपेः
उपतस्थे विशालाक्षी प्रयता हव्यवाहनम्
verses.transliteration:
maṅgalābhimukhī tasya sā tadāsīnmahākapeḥ
upatasthe viśālākṣī prayatā havyavāhanam

translations.english: And wishing for the welfare of the mighty monkey, that large eyed lady with an intent mind began to pray to that bearer of sacrificial offerings,

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यस्ति पतिशुश्रूषा यद्यस्ति चरितं तपः
यदि चास्त्येकपत्नीत्वं शीतो भव हनूमतः
verses.transliteration:
yadyasti patiśuśrūṣā yadyasti caritaṁ tapaḥ
yadi cāstyekapatnītvaṁ śīto bhava hanūmataḥ

translations.english: If I have served my lord, if I bear a character, if I have ascetic merit, if I have been the wife of one alone, then prove you cool to Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तीक्ष्णार्चिरव्यग्रः प्रदक्षिणशिखोऽनलः
जज्वाल मृगशावाक्ष्याः शंसन्निव शिवं कपेः
verses.transliteration:
tatastīkṣṇārciravyagraḥ pradakṣiṇaśikho'nalaḥ
jajvāla mṛgaśāvākṣyāḥ śaṁsanniva śivaṁ kapeḥ

translations.english: Thereat, as if communicating the welfare of the monkey to that one having eyes like those of a young deer, the Fire flamed up. And Hanumān's sire, albeit furnished with fire and a tail, blew ice-cold before that worshipful one, breathing health (to Hanumān).

verses.sanskrit:
दह्यमाने च लाङ्गूले चिन्तयामास वानरः
प्रदीप्तोऽग्निरयं कस्मान्न मां दहति सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
dahyamāne ca lāṅgūle cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ
pradīpto'gnirayaṁ kasmānna māṁ dahati sarvataḥ

translations.english: On his tail flaming, the monkey reflected, "This fire is flaming. Why dose it not then burn me all over"?

verses.sanskrit:
दृश्यते च महाज्वालः करोति च न मे रुजम्
शिशिरस्येव संपातो लाङ्गूलाग्रे प्रतिष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
dṛśyate ca mahājvālaḥ karoti ca na me rujam
śiśirasyeva saṁpāto lāṅgūlāgre pratiṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: I see it of exceeding brightness yet it pain me not. (On the contrary), at the end of my tail it seem like a mass of ice.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा तदिदं व्यक्तं यद्दृष्टं प्लवता मया
रामप्रभावादाश्चर्यं पर्वतः सरितां पतौ
verses.transliteration:
atha vā tadidaṁ vyaktaṁ yaddṛṣṭaṁ plavatā mayā
rāmaprabhāvādāścaryaṁ parvataḥ saritāṁ patau

translations.english: Or this is clearly due to Rāma's power, even like the wonder (that I witnessed) while bounding over the main-the mountain under the lord of streams. (Mainaka)

verses.sanskrit:
यदि तावत्समुद्रस्य मैनाकस्य च धीमथ
रामार्थं संभ्रमस्तादृक्किमग्निर्न करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadi tāvatsamudrasya mainākasya ca dhīmatha
rāmārthaṁ saṁbhramastādṛkkimagnirna kariṣyati

translations.english: If the Ocean and the intelligent Maināka could show such regard for Råma, what may not the Fire do (for him?)

verses.sanskrit:
सीतायाश्चानृशंस्येन तेजसा राघवस्य च
पितुश्च मम सख्येन न मां दहति पावकः
verses.transliteration:
sītāyāścānṛśaṁsyena tejasā rāghavasya ca
pituśca mama sakhyena na māṁ dahati pāvakaḥ

translations.english: Fire dose not burn me for Sītā's (absolute) goodness, for Rāghava's prowess, and for (his friendship with my sire.

verses.sanskrit:
भूयः स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः
उत्पपाताथ वेगेन ननाद च महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
bhūyaḥ sa cintayāmāsa muhūrtaṁ kapikuñjaraḥ
utpapātātha vegena nanāda ca mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Thereat that vehement and mighty monkey snapped his bonds, and furiously springing into the sky, the terrible monkey uttered a shout. anon one

verses.sanskrit:
पुरद्वारं ततः श्रीमाञ्शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्
विभक्तरक्षःसंबाधमाससादानिलात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
puradvāraṁ tataḥ śrīmāñśailaśṛṅgamivonnatam
vibhaktarakṣaḥsaṁbādhamāsasādānilātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then the graceful son of the Wind-god arrived at the gate of the city resembling a hill, where Rākşasas there were none.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूत्वा शैलसंकाशः क्षणेन पुनरात्मवान्
ह्रस्वतां परमां प्राप्तो बन्धनान्यवशातयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūtvā śailasaṁkāśaḥ kṣaṇena punarātmavān
hrasvatāṁ paramāṁ prāpto bandhanānyavaśātayat

translations.english: After having attained the magnitude of a mountain, that self-controlled diminished himself and cast off his bonds. And having freed himself, the graceful one again became mountain-like.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं गृह्य महाबाहुः कालायसपरिष्कृतम्
रक्षिणस्तान्पुनः सर्वान्सूदयामास मारुतिः
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ gṛhya mahābāhuḥ kālāyasapariṣkṛtam
rakṣiṇastānpunaḥ sarvānsūdayāmāsa mārutiḥ

translations.english: And eyeing around, he saw a bolt standing against the gate. And that mighty-armed one, the Wind-god's son, taking up that bolt of burnished iron, again slaughtered the guards.

verses.sanskrit:
स तान्निहत्वा रणचण्डविक्रमः; समीक्षमाणः पुनरेव लङ्काम्
प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलकृतार्चिमाली; प्रकाशतादित्य इवांशुमाली
verses.transliteration:
sa tānnihatvā raṇacaṇḍavikramaḥ; samīkṣamāṇaḥ punareva laṅkām
pradīptalāṅgūlakṛtārcimālī; prakāśatāditya ivāṁśumālī

translations.english: Having slain the warders, that one of terrific prowess crowned with a luminous wreath forged from his flaming tail, and appearing like the sun garlanded with glory, once again cast his eyes over Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
वीक्षमाणस्ततो लङ्कां कपिः कृतमनोरथः
वर्धमानसमुत्साहः कार्यशेषमचिन्तयत्
verses.transliteration:
vīkṣamāṇastato laṅkāṁ kapiḥ kṛtamanorathaḥ
vardhamānasamutsāhaḥ kāryaśeṣamacintayat

translations.english: Casting his eyes on Lankā, the monkey, his wish attained, increasing his person and bursting with spirits, considered as to how to give the coup de grace to his exertions.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु खल्वविशिष्टं मे कर्तव्यमिह साम्प्रतम्
यदेषां रक्षसां भूयः संतापजननं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu khalvaviśiṣṭaṁ me kartavyamiha sāmpratam
yadeṣāṁ rakṣasāṁ bhūyaḥ saṁtāpajananaṁ bhavet

translations.english: What recently is to done by me here to finish this business, that may afflict them the more?

verses.sanskrit:
वनं तावत्प्रमथितं प्रकृष्टा राक्षसा हताः
बलैकदेशः क्षपितः शेषं दुर्गविनाशनम्
verses.transliteration:
vanaṁ tāvatpramathitaṁ prakṛṣṭā rākṣasā hatāḥ
balaikadeśaḥ kṣapitaḥ śeṣaṁ durgavināśanam

translations.english: I have ravaged the wood, and slain the choice Rākşasas, and destroyed by main force a portion of the army. Now it remains to demolish the fortifications.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्गे विनाशिते कर्म भवेत्सुखपरिश्रमम्
अल्पयत्नेन कार्येऽस्मिन्मम स्यात्सफलः श्रमः
verses.transliteration:
durge vināśite karma bhavetsukhapariśramam
alpayatnena kārye'sminmama syātsaphalaḥ śramaḥ

translations.english: On the fortifications being destroyed, my work shall nave its toils crowned with joy. By undergoing slight labour in this business, I shall have my pains furnished with fruit.

verses.sanskrit:
यो ह्ययं मम लाङ्गूले दीप्यते हव्यवाहनः
अस्य संतर्पणं न्याय्यं कर्तुमेभिर्गृहोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
yo hyayaṁ mama lāṅgūle dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ
asya saṁtarpaṇaṁ nyāyyaṁ kartumebhirgṛhottamaiḥ

translations.english: That bearer of sacrificial offerings (Vide ante) who flame on my tail, it is my duty to propitiate him with these excellent edifices.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलः सविद्युदिव तोयदः
भवनाग्रेषु लङ्काया विचचार महाकपिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pradīptalāṅgūlaḥ savidyudiva toyadaḥ
bhavanāgreṣu laṅkāyā vicacāra mahākapiḥ

translations.english: Thereat that mighty monkey, with his tail aglow, and resembling a cloud (luminous) with lightning, began to range before the dwellings in Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वसनेन च संयोगादतिवेगो महाबलः
कालाग्निरिव जज्वाल प्रावर्धत हुताशनः
verses.transliteration:
śvasanena ca saṁyogādativego mahābalaḥ
kālāgniriva jajvāla prāvardhata hutāśanaḥ

translations.english: And assisted by the wind, that highly powerful and vehement one (Fire) flaimed up, like fire at the wreck of all, and the fire attained energy.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि काञ्चनजालानि मुक्तामणिमयानि च
भवनान्यवशीर्यन्त रत्नवन्ति महान्ति च
verses.transliteration:
tāni kāñcanajālāni muktāmaṇimayāni ca
bhavanānyavaśīryanta ratnavanti mahānti ca

translations.english: The wind spreading the flaming fire all round those dwellings, those mansions furnished with golden networks; and containing pearls and gems; enjewelled and magnificent, were shorn of their splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्तारजतसंहितान्
विचित्रान्भवनाद्धातून्स्यन्दमानान्ददर्श सः
verses.transliteration:
vajravidrumavaidūryamuktārajatasaṁhitān
vicitrānbhavanāddhātūnsyandamānāndadarśa saḥ

translations.english: And he (Hanuman) saw various kinds of metals, mixed with diamonds, and coral, and lapises and pearls and silver, running down in streams from the mansions.

verses.sanskrit:
नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां तृणानां च यथा तथा
हनूमान्राक्षसेन्द्राणां वधे किंचिन्न तृप्यति
verses.transliteration:
nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṁ tṛṇānāṁ ca yathā tathā
hanūmānrākṣasendrāṇāṁ vadhe kiṁcinna tṛpyati

translations.english: And as Fire is not cloyed with wood and straw, Hanumān never at all felt satiety on slaying those foremost of Räkşasas. And the Earth could not contain the Rākşasas slain by Hanumăn.

verses.sanskrit:
हुताशनज्वालसमावृता सा; हतप्रवीरा परिवृत्तयोधा
हनूमातः क्रोधबलाभिभूता; बभूव शापोपहतेव लङ्का
verses.transliteration:
hutāśanajvālasamāvṛtā sā; hatapravīrā parivṛttayodhā
hanūmātaḥ krodhabalābhibhūtā; babhūva śāpopahateva laṅkā

translations.english: And with the flames encircling her, and her foremost heroes fallen, and her warriors destroyed, Lankā, overcome by the might of Hanumān's wrath, became as if she had been blighted by an imprecation.

verses.sanskrit:
ससंभ्रमं त्रस्तविषण्णराक्षसां; समुज्ज्वलज्ज्वालहुताशनाङ्किताम्
ददर्श लङ्कां हनुमान्महामनाः; स्वयम्भुकोपोपहतामिवावनिम्
verses.transliteration:
sasaṁbhramaṁ trastaviṣaṇṇarākṣasāṁ; samujjvalajjvālahutāśanāṅkitām
dadarśa laṅkāṁ hanumānmahāmanāḥ; svayambhukopopahatāmivāvanim

translations.english: Then the mighty-minded Hanumān beheld the Rākşasas in terror and trepidation and cast down, and Lankā marked by fire and bright flames, even as the Self-sprung eye the world destroyed by his rage.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसांस्तान्सुबहूंश्च हत्वा; वनं च भङ्क्त्वा बहुपादपं तत्
विसृज्य रक्षो भवनेषु चाग्निं; जगाम रामं मनसा महात्मा
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasāṁstānsubahūṁśca hatvā; vanaṁ ca bhaṅktvā bahupādapaṁ tat
visṛjya rakṣo bhavaneṣu cāgniṁ; jagāma rāmaṁ manasā mahātmā

translations.english: And destroying many a Rākṣasa, felling many trees in the forest and setting fire to the houses of the Raksasas, the high-souled (monkey) became engaged in thoughts touching Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्कां समस्तां संदीप्य लाङ्गूलाग्निं महाकपिः
निर्वापयामास तदा समुद्रे हरिसत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
laṅkāṁ samastāṁ saṁdīpya lāṅgūlāgniṁ mahākapiḥ
nirvāpayāmāsa tadā samudre harisattamaḥ

translations.english: And having consumed ihe city of Lankä, the great monkey quenched the fire of his tail in the Ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
संदीप्यमानां विध्वस्तां त्रस्तरक्षो गणां पुरीम्
अवेक्ष्य हानुमाँल्लङ्कां चिन्तयामास वानरः
verses.transliteration:
saṁdīpyamānāṁ vidhvastāṁ trastarakṣo gaṇāṁ purīm
avekṣya hānumā̐llaṅkāṁ cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ

translations.english: Beholding Lankā burnt down and devastated and the demons terrified, the monkey Hanumān began to reflect.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याभूत्सुमहांस्त्रासः कुत्सा चात्मन्यजायत
लङ्कां प्रदहता कर्म किंस्वित्कृतमिदं मया
verses.transliteration:
tasyābhūtsumahāṁstrāsaḥ kutsā cātmanyajāyata
laṅkāṁ pradahatā karma kiṁsvitkṛtamidaṁ mayā

translations.english: And worked up with fear and remorse, he reflected, “What a mighty iniquity have I perpetrated by burning down Lankā of my own accord.

verses.sanskrit:
धन्यास्ते पुरुषश्रेष्ठ ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्
निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा
verses.transliteration:
dhanyāste puruṣaśreṣṭha ye buddhyā kopamutthitam
nirundhanti mahātmāno dīptamagnimivāmbhasā

translations.english: Blessed are those high-souled ones who control their wrath by dint of their own good sense, like to fire quenched by water.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दग्धा त्वियं लङ्का नूनमार्यापि जानकी
दग्धा तेन मया भर्तुर्हतं कार्यमजानता
verses.transliteration:
yadi dagdhā tviyaṁ laṅkā nūnamāryāpi jānakī
dagdhā tena mayā bharturhataṁ kāryamajānatā

translations.english: Forsooth has the worshipful Jảnaki been burnt, since the whole city of Lankā has been devastated with fire. And she being burnt, foolishly have I spoilt the work of my master.

verses.sanskrit:
यदर्थमयमारम्भस्तत्कार्यमवसादितम्
मया हि दहता लङ्कां न सीता परिरक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
yadarthamayamārambhastatkāryamavasāditam
mayā hi dahatā laṅkāṁ na sītā parirakṣitā

translations.english: I have defeated the great object for which I have laboured so much. In burning down Lankā, I have not saved Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
ईषत्कार्यमिदं कार्यं कृतमासीन्न संशयः
तस्य क्रोधाभिभूतेन मया मूलक्षयः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
īṣatkāryamidaṁ kāryaṁ kṛtamāsīnna saṁśayaḥ
tasya krodhābhibhūtena mayā mūlakṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: To have burnt down Lankā is assuredly a trifle, but in my ire I have lost my great object. Forsooth has Janaki been consumed, since I behold no spot in Lankā which is not made desolate with fire-in fact the whole city has been reduced to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते
लङ्कायाः कश्चिदुद्देशः सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭā jānakī vyaktaṁ na hyadagdhaḥ pradṛśyate
laṅkāyāḥ kaściduddeśaḥ sarvā bhasmīkṛtā purī

translations.english: I was not the least flurried at it. Forsooth has Jānaki been destroyed for behold I nothing in Lankā which has not been burnt down— indeed the whole city has been reduced to ashes. For certain have I burnt down Sītă while burning the city Lankā-and I have thus baffled the great work of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि तद्विहतं कार्यं मया प्रज्ञाविपर्ययात्
इहैव प्राणसंन्यासो ममापि ह्यतिरोचते
verses.transliteration:
yadi tadvihataṁ kāryaṁ mayā prajñāviparyayāt
ihaiva prāṇasaṁnyāso mamāpi hyatirocate

translations.english: As I have committed such an injury under the influence of my perverse understanding, it behave me to relinquish my life here.

verses.sanskrit:
किमग्नौ निपताम्यद्य आहोस्विद्वडवामुखे
शरीरमाहो सत्त्वानां दद्मि सागरवासिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
kimagnau nipatāmyadya āhosvidvaḍavāmukhe
śarīramāho sattvānāṁ dadmi sāgaravāsinām

translations.english: I shall jump into this flame or into a submarine fire, or I shall resign my mortal frame to the animals that infest the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं हि जीवता शक्यो मया द्रष्टुं हरीश्वरः
तौ वा पुरुषशार्दूलौ कार्यसर्वस्वघातिना
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ hi jīvatā śakyo mayā draṣṭuṁ harīśvaraḥ
tau vā puruṣaśārdūlau kāryasarvasvaghātinā

translations.english: For, living, I shall not be able to face that lord of monkeys, and how shall I, having spoilt their work utterly, show myself to those foremost of men?

verses.sanskrit:
मया खलु तदेवेदं रोषदोषात्प्रदर्शितम्
प्रथितं त्रिषु लोकेषु कपितमनवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
mayā khalu tadevedaṁ roṣadoṣātpradarśitam
prathitaṁ triṣu lokeṣu kapitamanavasthitam

translations.english: I have through my culpable passion furnished an illustration of the reckless monkey-nature, which is well known over the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
धिगस्तु राजसं भावमनीशमनवस्थितम्
ईश्वरेणापि यद्रागान्मया सीता न रक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
dhigastu rājasaṁ bhāvamanīśamanavasthitam
īśvareṇāpi yadrāgānmayā sītā na rakṣitā

translations.english: Fie on this activity, born of (the quality of) passion, which is the source of incompetence and rashness; since although capable, I did not protect Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टायां तु सीतायां तावुभौ विनशिष्यतः
तयोर्विनाशे सुग्रीवः सबन्धुर्विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭāyāṁ tu sītāyāṁ tāvubhau vinaśiṣyataḥ
tayorvināśe sugrīvaḥ sabandhurvinaśiṣyati

translations.english: On Sītā having met with destruction, both of them (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) shall cease to exist; and on their ceasing to exist, Sugrīva shall die along with his friends.

verses.sanskrit:
एतदेव वचः श्रुत्वा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः
धर्मात्मा सहशत्रुघ्नः कथं शक्ष्यति जीवितुम्
verses.transliteration:
etadeva vacaḥ śrutvā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
dharmātmā sahaśatrughnaḥ kathaṁ śakṣyati jīvitum

translations.english: Hearing these tidings, how shall the righteous Bharata, attached to his brother (Rāma), along with Satrughna, live?

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकुवंशे धर्मिष्ठे गते नाशमसंशयम्
भविष्यन्ति प्रजाः सर्वाः शोकसंतापपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
ikṣvākuvaṁśe dharmiṣṭhe gate nāśamasaṁśayam
bhaviṣyanti prajāḥ sarvāḥ śokasaṁtāpapīḍitāḥ

translations.english: And on the virtuous Ikşvāku race being extinct, without doubt, all the subjects shall be overwhelmed with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
तदहं भाग्यरहितो लुप्तधर्मार्थसंग्रहः
रोषदोषपरीतात्मा व्यक्तं लोकविनाशनः
verses.transliteration:
tadahaṁ bhāgyarahito luptadharmārthasaṁgrahaḥ
roṣadoṣaparītātmā vyaktaṁ lokavināśanaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, I of crust luck has had my harvest of virtue and profit taken away; and being under the influence of baleful passion, I am the cause of the destruction of creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
इति चिन्तयतस्तस्य निमित्तान्युपपेदिरे
पूरमप्युपलब्धानि साक्षात्पुनरचिन्तयत्
verses.transliteration:
iti cintayatastasya nimittānyupapedire
pūramapyupalabdhāni sākṣātpunaracintayat

translations.english: As he was reflecting thus, he bethought him of auspicious omens which he had witnessed since.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा चारुसर्वाङ्गी रक्षिता स्वेन तेजसा
न नशिष्यति कल्याणी नाग्निरग्नौ प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
atha vā cārusarvāṅgī rakṣitā svena tejasā
na naśiṣyati kalyāṇī nāgniragnau pravartate

translations.english: Or it may be that one of charming limbs has been preserved by her proper energy. The blessed one may not have met with her end, for fire dose burn fire.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि धर्मान्मनस्तस्य भार्याममिततेजसः
स्वचारित्राभिगुप्तां तां स्प्रष्टुमर्हति पावकः
verses.transliteration:
na hi dharmānmanastasya bhāryāmamitatejasaḥ
svacāritrābhiguptāṁ tāṁ spraṣṭumarhati pāvakaḥ

translations.english: Fire should not touch the spouse of that virtuous one of immeasurable energy, who is protected by her own character.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं रामप्रभावेन वैदेह्याः सुकृतेन च
यन्मां दहनकर्मायं नादहद्धव्यवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ rāmaprabhāvena vaidehyāḥ sukṛtena ca
yanmāṁ dahanakarmāyaṁ nādahaddhavyavāhanaḥ

translations.english: And that bearer of sacrificial offerings has not burnt me, is owing to Rāma's power and the virtue of Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणां भरतादीनां भ्रातॄणां देवता च या
रामस्य च मनःकान्ता सा कथं विनशिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇāṁ bharatādīnāṁ bhrātṝṇāṁ devatā ca yā
rāmasya ca manaḥkāntā sā kathaṁ vinaśiṣyati

translations.english: Why should she that is a very goddess to the three brothers, Bharata and the others, and that has enchanted the mind of Rāma, meet with destruction?

verses.sanskrit:
यद्वा दहनकर्मायं सर्वत्र प्रभुरव्ययः
न मे दहति लाङ्गूलं कथमार्यां प्रधक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yadvā dahanakarmāyaṁ sarvatra prabhuravyayaḥ
na me dahati lāṅgūlaṁ kathamāryāṁ pradhakṣyati

translations.english: When that everywhere unspent Lord, having burning for his office, has not consumed my tail, why should he burn the exalted lady?

verses.sanskrit:
तपसा सत्यवाक्येन अनन्यत्वाच्च भर्तरि
अपि सा निर्दहेदग्निं न तामग्निः प्रधक्ष्यति
verses.transliteration:
tapasā satyavākyena ananyatvācca bhartari
api sā nirdahedagniṁ na tāmagniḥ pradhakṣyati

translations.english: By virtue of her asceticism, veracity, and devotion to her lord she it is that can consume Fire, but Fire cannot burn her.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथा चिन्तयंस्तत्र देव्या धर्मपरिग्रहम्
शुश्राव हनुमान्वाक्यं चारणानां महात्मनाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tathā cintayaṁstatra devyā dharmaparigraham
śuśrāva hanumānvākyaṁ cāraṇānāṁ mahātmanām

translations.english: And as Hanumān was thinking of the magnitude of that revered lady's religious merit, he heard the converse there of high-souled Caranas.

verses.sanskrit:
अहो खलु कृतं कर्म दुर्विषह्यं हनूमता
अग्निं विसृजताभीक्ष्णं भीमं राक्षससद्मनि
verses.transliteration:
aho khalu kṛtaṁ karma durviṣahyaṁ hanūmatā
agniṁ visṛjatābhīkṣṇaṁ bhīmaṁ rākṣasasadmani

translations.english: Ah! hard is the feat that Hanumān has forsooth achieved. He has created a terrific and fierce conflagration in the abode of the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
दग्धेयं नगरी लङ्का साट्टप्राकारतोरणा
जानकी न च दग्धेति विस्मयोऽद्भुत एव नः
verses.transliteration:
dagdheyaṁ nagarī laṅkā sāṭṭaprākāratoraṇā
jānakī na ca dagdheti vismayo'dbhuta eva naḥ

translations.english: The females of Rākşasa accompanied by boys and old folks, are flying amain; and in consequence of the hubbub it seems as if (Lankā) is in lamentation through her mountaincaverns. Burnt is this city of Lankā with her turrets, walls and gate-ways; and we are astonished that Jānakī is not burnt.

verses.sanskrit:
स निमित्तैश्च दृष्टार्थैः कारणैश्च महागुणैः
ऋषिवाक्यैश्च हनुमानभवत्प्रीतमानसः
verses.transliteration:
sa nimittaiśca dṛṣṭārthaiḥ kāraṇaiśca mahāguṇaiḥ
ṛṣivākyaiśca hanumānabhavatprītamānasaḥ

translations.english: And what through the auspicious omens that he had witnessed, and what through the speech of the saints, Hanumān was delighted (beyond measure).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कपिः प्राप्तमनोरथार्थ;स्तामक्षतां राजसुतां विदित्वा
प्रत्यक्षतस्तां पुनरेव दृष्ट्वा; प्रतिप्रयाणाय मतिं चकार
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kapiḥ prāptamanorathārtha;stāmakṣatāṁ rājasutāṁ viditvā
pratyakṣatastāṁ punareva dṛṣṭvā; pratiprayāṇāya matiṁ cakāra

translations.english: Then the monkey, with his end attained, knowing that the king's daughter was unhurt, became bent upon returning after seeing her once again.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु शिंशपामूले जानकीं पर्यवस्थिताम्
अभिवाद्याब्रवीद्दिष्ट्या पश्यामि त्वामिहाक्षताम्
verses.transliteration:
