सेतुरत्र यथा वध्येद्यथा पश्येम तां पुरीम्
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य तथा त्वं कुरु राघव
verses.transliteration:
seturatra yathā vadhyedyathā paśyema tāṁ purīm
tasya rākṣasarājasya tathā tvaṁ kuru rāghava

translations.english: Do you, O Rāghava, so order matters that a bridge may be constructed (over the main), and that we may behold the palace of the Rākşasa monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तां हि पुरीं लङ्कां त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिताम्
हतं च रावणं युद्धे दर्शनादुपधारय
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā tāṁ hi purīṁ laṅkāṁ trikūṭaśikhare sthitām
hataṁ ca rāvaṇaṁ yuddhe darśanādupadhāraya

translations.english: We having seen the city of Lankā, established on the summit of Triküța, do you for certain conclude Răvaņa as slain in battle immediately after (we see her).

verses.sanskrit:
सेतुबद्धः समुद्रे च यावल्लङ्का समीपतः
सर्वं तीर्णं च वै सैन्यं जितमित्युपधार्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
setubaddhaḥ samudre ca yāvallaṅkā samīpataḥ
sarvaṁ tīrṇaṁ ca vai sainyaṁ jitamityupadhāryatām

translations.english: When the bridge over the ocean has been constructed up to near Laňkä, and when my forces have crossed (over the sea), consider victory as secured. As these monkeys are heroic in fight, and able to wear forms at will, O king, do not let your intellect get stupefied and thus mar all interests. In this world, sorrow berefts people of their prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टे वा प्रनष्टे वा शोकः सर्वार्थनाशनः
त्वं तु बुद्धिमतां श्रेष्ठः सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदः
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭe vā pranaṣṭe vā śokaḥ sarvārthanāśanaḥ
tvaṁ tu buddhimatāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvaśāstrārthakovidaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, the foremost of intelligent persons, and conversant with every lore, you should along with councillors like me, strive to beat they foe.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतधनुषो यस्ते तिष्ठेदभिमुखो रणे
वानरेषु समासक्तं न ते कार्यं विपत्स्यते
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītadhanuṣo yaste tiṣṭhedabhimukho raṇe
vānareṣu samāsaktaṁ na te kāryaṁ vipatsyate

translations.english: Find I none in the three worlds, O Rāghava, who can stay in fight before you equipped with your bow,

verses.sanskrit:
अचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे सीतां तीर्त्वा सागरमक्षयम्
तदलं शोकमालम्ब्य क्रोधमालम्ब भूपते
verses.transliteration:
acirāddrakṣyase sītāṁ tīrtvā sāgaramakṣayam
tadalaṁ śokamālambya krodhamālamba bhūpate

translations.english: Your business entrusted to these monkeys shall not (anyway) suffer. And soon, crossing over the boundless main, you shall behold Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
निश्चेष्टाः क्षत्रिया मन्दाः सर्वे चण्डस्य बिभ्यति
लङ्गनार्थं च घोरस्य समुद्रस्य नदीपतेः
verses.transliteration:
niśceṣṭāḥ kṣatriyā mandāḥ sarve caṇḍasya bibhyati
laṅganārthaṁ ca ghorasya samudrasya nadīpateḥ

translations.english: Therefore, O king, renounce your sorrow, and call up wrath. Those Ksatriyas that conceive no anger in respect of their enemies, have their activity annulled; and all fear furious persons.

verses.sanskrit:
सहास्माभिरिहोपेतः सूक्ष्मबुद्धिर्विचारय
इमे हि समरे शूरा हरयः कामरूपिणः
verses.transliteration:
sahāsmābhirihopetaḥ sūkṣmabuddhirvicāraya
ime hi samare śūrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ

translations.english: Drawing nigh to us, do you, gifted with acute intelligence, cast about for crossing over the dreadful deep, lord of streams, along with us.

verses.sanskrit:
तानरीन्विधमिष्यन्ति शिलापादपवृष्टिभिः
कथंचित्परिपश्यामस्ते वयं वरुणालयम्
verses.transliteration:
tānarīnvidhamiṣyanti śilāpādapavṛṣṭibhiḥ
kathaṁcitparipaśyāmaste vayaṁ varuṇālayam

translations.english: These monkeys, heroic and capable of assuming in fight forms at will, shall slaughter those foes by showering rocks and trees.

verses.sanskrit: किमुक्त्वा बहुधा चापि सर्वथा विजयी भवान्
verses.transliteration: kimuktvā bahudhā cāpi sarvathā vijayī bhavān

translations.english: And what is the use of dilating? Every way you shall prove victorious. And I see omens, and my mind is filled with delight.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत्परमार्थवित्
प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumatparamārthavit
pratijagrāha kākutstho hanūmantamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing Sugrīva's speech, reasonable and fraught with high sense, Kākutstha accorded his assent to it and spoke to Hanumān, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
तरसा सेतुबन्धेन सागरोच्छोषणेन वा
सर्वथा सुसमर्थोऽस्मि सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने
verses.transliteration:
tarasā setubandhena sāgarocchoṣaṇena vā
sarvathā susamartho'smi sāgarasyāsya laṅghane

translations.english: By asceticism, or constructing a bridge, or drying up the ocean, competent every way am I for crossing over this ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
कति दुर्गाणि दुर्गाया लङ्कायास्तद्ब्रवीहि मे
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्सर्वं दर्शनादिव वानर
verses.transliteration:
kati durgāṇi durgāyā laṅkāyāstadbravīhi me
jñātumicchāmi tatsarvaṁ darśanādiva vānara

translations.english: Of impracticable places, tell me how many there are in (Lankā), which are incapable of being come at.

verses.sanskrit:
बलस्य परिमाणं च द्वारदुर्गक्रियामपि
गुप्ति कर्म च लङ्काया रक्षसां सदनानि च
verses.transliteration:
balasya parimāṇaṁ ca dvāradurgakriyāmapi
gupti karma ca laṅkāyā rakṣasāṁ sadanāni ca

translations.english: O monkey, as you have seen personally, I wish to get acquainted with all this. And you have at your leisure duly noticed in Lankā the nur.ber of the army, the inaccessibility (or otherwise) of the gates, the defence of Lankā, and the dwellings of the Rākşasas. Do you faithfully relate this to me, for you are observant.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टा मुदिता लङ्का मत्तद्विपसमाकुला
महती रथसंपूर्णा रक्षोगणसमाकुला
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭā muditā laṅkā mattadvipasamākulā
mahatī rathasaṁpūrṇā rakṣogaṇasamākulā

translations.english: Lankā, filled with mad elephants, ever rejoice. She is great, thronging with cars and inhabited by Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
दृढबद्धकवाटानि महापरिघवन्ति च
द्वाराणि विपुलान्यस्याश्चत्वारि सुमहान्ति च
verses.transliteration:
dṛḍhabaddhakavāṭāni mahāparighavanti ca
dvārāṇi vipulānyasyāścatvāri sumahānti ca

translations.english: Her doors are firmly established and furnished with massy bolts. And she has four wide and giant gates.

verses.sanskrit:
वप्रेषूपलयन्त्राणि बलवन्ति महान्ति च
आगतं परसैन्यं तैस्तत्र प्रतिनिवार्यते
verses.transliteration:
vapreṣūpalayantrāṇi balavanti mahānti ca
āgataṁ parasainyaṁ taistatra pratinivāryate

translations.english: (At those gates) are powerful and large arms, stones, and engines, whereby a hostile host approaching, is opposed.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वारेषु संस्कृता भीमाः कालायसमयाः शिताः
शतशो रोचिता वीरैः शतघ्न्यो रक्षसां गणैः
verses.transliteration:
dvāreṣu saṁskṛtā bhīmāḥ kālāyasamayāḥ śitāḥ
śataśo rocitā vīraiḥ śataghnyo rakṣasāṁ gaṇaiḥ

translations.english: At the entrances are arrayed and set in order by bands of heroic Rākşasas, hundreds of dreadful sharp iron sataghnis.* *A kind of fire-arms, or ancient Hindu rocket; or a stone set round with sharp iron spikes. According to Rāmānuja, a sort of mace about two yards in length, with spikes.

verses.sanskrit:
सौवर्णश्च महांस्तस्याः प्राकारो दुष्प्रधर्षणः
मणिविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्ताविचरितान्तरः
verses.transliteration:
sauvarṇaśca mahāṁstasyāḥ prākāro duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ
maṇividrumavaidūryamuktāvicaritāntaraḥ

translations.english: She has a mighty impassable golden wall, having its side emblazoned in the centre with costly stones, coral, lapises and pearls.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वतश्च महाभीमाः शीततोया महाशुभाः
अगाधा ग्राहवत्यश्च परिखा मीनसेविताः
verses.transliteration:
sarvataśca mahābhīmāḥ śītatoyā mahāśubhāḥ
agādhā grāhavatyaśca parikhā mīnasevitāḥ

translations.english: Round about is a moat, exceedingly dreadful, with cool water, eminently grand, fathomless, containing ferocious aquatic animals, and inhabited by fishes.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वारेषु तासां चत्वारः संक्रमाः परमायताः
यन्त्रैरुपेता बहुभिर्महद्भिर्दृढसंधिभिः
verses.transliteration:
dvāreṣu tāsāṁ catvāraḥ saṁkramāḥ paramāyatāḥ
yantrairupetā bahubhirmahadbhirdṛḍhasaṁdhibhiḥ

translations.english: At the gates are four broad bridges, furnished with machines and many rows of grand structures.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रायन्ते संक्रमास्तत्र परसैन्यागमे सति
यन्त्रैस्तैरवकीर्यन्ते परिखासु समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
trāyante saṁkramāstatra parasainyāgame sati
yantraistairavakīryante parikhāsu samantataḥ

translations.english: On the approach of hostile forces, their attack is repulsed by these machines, and they are thrown into the ditch.

verses.sanskrit:
एकस्त्वकम्प्यो बलवान्संक्रमः सुमहादृढः
काञ्चनैर्बहुभिः स्तम्भैर्वेदिकाभिश्च शोभितः
verses.transliteration:
ekastvakampyo balavānsaṁkramaḥ sumahādṛḍhaḥ
kāñcanairbahubhiḥ stambhairvedikābhiśca śobhitaḥ

translations.english: One among these bridges is immovable, strong and fast established; adorned with golden pillars and daises.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयं प्रकृतिसंपन्नो युयुत्सू राम रावणः
उत्थितश्चाप्रमत्तश्च बलानामनुदर्शने
verses.transliteration:
svayaṁ prakṛtisaṁpanno yuyutsū rāma rāvaṇaḥ
utthitaścāpramattaśca balānāmanudarśane

translations.english: O Rāma, albeit Rāvaņa hunger for fight, yet is he calm; and he is vigilant and ever engaged in superintending his army.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्का पुरी निरालम्बा देवदुर्गा भयावहा
नादेयं पार्वतं वन्यं कृत्रिमं च चतुर्विधम्
verses.transliteration:
laṅkā purī nirālambā devadurgā bhayāvahā
nādeyaṁ pārvataṁ vanyaṁ kṛtrimaṁ ca caturvidham

translations.english: And dreadful and resembling a celestial citadel, Lankā cannot be ascended by means of any support. She has fortresses composed of streams, those of hills, and artificial ones of four kinds.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थिता पारे समुद्रस्य दूरपारस्य राघव
नौपथश्चापि नास्त्यत्र निरादेशश्च सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sthitā pāre samudrasya dūrapārasya rāghava
naupathaścāpi nāstyatra nirādeśaśca sarvataḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, she is situated on the other shore of the ocean having its limit far away. And way there is none even for barks, and all sides are destitute of division.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलाग्रे रचिता दुर्गा सा पूर्देवपुरोपमा
वाजिवारणसंपूर्णा लङ्का परमदुर्जया
verses.transliteration:
śailāgre racitā durgā sā pūrdevapuropamā
vājivāraṇasaṁpūrṇā laṅkā paramadurjayā

translations.english: That citadel is built on the mountain's brow; and, resembling the metropolis of the immortals, the exceedingly invincible Larkā is filled with horses and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
परिघाश्च शतघ्न्यश्च यन्त्राणि विविधानि च
शोभयन्ति पुरीं लङ्कां रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
parighāśca śataghnyaśca yantrāṇi vividhāni ca
śobhayanti purīṁ laṅkāṁ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ

translations.english: And a moat and sataghnís and various engines adorn the city of Lankā, belonging to the wicked Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
अयुतं रक्षसामत्र पश्चिमद्वारमाश्रितम्
शूलहस्ता दुराधर्षाः सर्वे खड्गाग्रयोधिनः
verses.transliteration:
ayutaṁ rakṣasāmatra paścimadvāramāśritam
śūlahastā durādharṣāḥ sarve khaḍgāgrayodhinaḥ

translations.english: And an ayuta of Raksasas, dart-handed, hard to subdue, and all fighting at the front with their swords-protect the Eastern gate.

verses.sanskrit:
नियुतं रक्षसामत्र दक्षिणद्वारमाश्रितम्
चतुरङ्गेण सैन्येन योधास्तत्राप्यनुत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
niyutaṁ rakṣasāmatra dakṣiṇadvāramāśritam
caturaṅgeṇa sainyena yodhāstatrāpyanuttamāḥ

translations.english: And a lac of Rākşasas with a fourfold force, and with the flower of the soldiery-protect the Southern gate.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयुतं रक्षसामत्र पूर्वद्वारं समाश्रितम्
चर्मखड्गधराः सर्वे तथा सर्वास्त्रकोविदाः
verses.transliteration:
prayutaṁ rakṣasāmatra pūrvadvāraṁ samāśritam
carmakhaḍgadharāḥ sarve tathā sarvāstrakovidāḥ

translations.english: And a prayuta of Rākṣasas, bearing swords and shields, and skilled in all arms, protect the Western gate.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्बुदं रक्षसामत्र उत्तरद्वारमाश्रितम्
रथिनश्चाश्ववाहाश्च कुलपुत्राः सुपूजिताः
verses.transliteration:
arbudaṁ rakṣasāmatra uttaradvāramāśritam
rathinaścāśvavāhāśca kulaputrāḥ supūjitāḥ

translations.english: And an arbuda of Rākṣasas protect the Northern gate. And car-warriors and horsemenpersons honoured and sprung from noble linesby hundreds and thousands,tand irrepressible goblins and koțis of Rākşasas, protect the garrison.

verses.sanskrit:
ते मया संक्रमा भग्नाः परिखाश्चावपूरिताः
दग्धा च नगरी लङ्का प्राकाराश्चावसादिताः
verses.transliteration:
te mayā saṁkramā bhagnāḥ parikhāścāvapūritāḥ
dagdhā ca nagarī laṅkā prākārāścāvasāditāḥ

translations.english: I have broken down the bridges and filled up the entrenchment. I have burnt that city of Lankā and laid the wall low.

verses.sanskrit:
येन केन तु मार्गेण तराम वरुणालयम्
हतेति नगरी लङ्कां वानरैरवधार्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
yena kena tu mārgeṇa tarāma varuṇālayam
hateti nagarī laṅkāṁ vānarairavadhāryatām

translations.english: Let us by any way whatever cross over Varuna's abode. Do you take it for certain that the city of Lankā is subdued by the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदो द्विविदो मैन्दो जाम्बवान्पनसो नलः
नीलः सेनापतिश्चैव बलशेषेण किं तव
verses.transliteration:
aṅgado dvivido maindo jāmbavānpanaso nalaḥ
nīlaḥ senāpatiścaiva balaśeṣeṇa kiṁ tava

translations.english: What is the use of your reckoning the rest? Aigada, Dvivida, Mainda, Jambavan, Panasa, Nala, and the general, Nīla, bounding and reaching Răvana's abode, and riving the same consisting of woods and hills, moat and gateway, walls and dwellings, shall, O Rāghava, bring (hither) Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं बलानां सर्वसंग्रहम्
मुहूर्तेन तु युक्तेन प्रस्थानमभिरोचय
verses.transliteration:
evamājñāpaya kṣipraṁ balānāṁ sarvasaṁgraham
muhūrtena tu yuktena prasthānamabhirocaya

translations.english: If this be so,* do you order the entire body of the army to be brought; and do you set out at the proper hour. *Ebam ajnápaya: Ramanuja reads sense into this passage. If you wishes the principal monkeys to go, bring them; if you wish the whole host to march, call it hither, and march at the auspicious moment.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं यथावदनुपूर्वशः
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā hanūmato vākyaṁ yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ
tato'bravīnmahātejā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Hanumăn's speech duly from the beginning, the exceedingly energetic Rāma having truth for this prowess, said.

verses.sanskrit:
यां निवेदयसे लङ्कां पुरीं भीमस्य रक्षसः
क्षिप्रमेनां वधिष्यामि सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते
verses.transliteration:
yāṁ nivedayase laṅkāṁ purīṁ bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ
kṣipramenāṁ vadhiṣyāmi satyametadbravīmi te

translations.english: What you say 'I shall speedily destroy the city of this dreadful Raksasa,' is true, I tell you.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रयाणमभिरोचये
युक्तो मुहूर्तो विजयः प्राप्तो मध्यं दिवाकरः
verses.transliteration:
asminmuhūrte sugrīva prayāṇamabhirocaye
yukto muhūrto vijayaḥ prāpto madhyaṁ divākaraḥ

translations.english: Therefore, at this very moment arrange for Sugrīva's march. The Sun has attained his meridian at this proper moment, capable of conferring victory.* *The moment is named abhijit.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तरा फल्गुनी ह्यद्य श्वस्तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यते
अभिप्रयाम सुग्रीव सर्वानीकसमावृताः
verses.transliteration:
uttarā phalgunī hyadya śvastu hastena yokṣyate
abhiprayāma sugrīva sarvānīkasamāvṛtāḥ

translations.english: To-day the Northern Phālguni (is in the ascendant); and to-morrow the moon shall be in conjunction with Hasta.* O Sugriva, shall we set our, surrounded by the entire host? *Hastā sprung from Punarvasu is the star of doom, portending death to Rāvana. The Northern Phālguni, is Sita's natal star. The expedition begun during the influence of this star, augurs deliverance to Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
निमित्तानि च धन्यानि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे
निहत्य रावणं सीतामानयिष्यामि जानकीम्
verses.transliteration:
nimittāni ca dhanyāni yāni prādurbhavanti me
nihatya rāvaṇaṁ sītāmānayiṣyāmi jānakīm

translations.english: The omens I witness, augur, that, having slain Ravana, I shall bring back Janaki.

verses.sanskrit:
उपरिष्टाद्धि नयनं स्फुरमाणमिदं मम
विजयं समनुप्राप्तं शंसतीव मनोरथम्
verses.transliteration:
upariṣṭāddhi nayanaṁ sphuramāṇamidaṁ mama
vijayaṁ samanuprāptaṁ śaṁsatīva manoratham

translations.english: The upper lid of my eye throb; and it betook that my desire has indeed been had.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रे यातु बलस्यास्य नीलो मार्गमवेक्षितुम्
वृतः शतसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
verses.transliteration:
agre yātu balasyāsya nīlo mārgamavekṣitum
vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām

translations.english: Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of fast-speeding monkeys, let Nīla go ahead of this force, for surveying the route.

verses.sanskrit:
फलमूलवता नील शीतकाननवारिणा
पथा मधुमता चाशु सेनां सेनापते नय
verses.transliteration:
phalamūlavatā nīla śītakānanavāriṇā
pathā madhumatā cāśu senāṁ senāpate naya

translations.english: O Nīla, do you, O general, expeditiously take the army by a path furnished with fruits and roots, having cool waters of the woods, and replenished with honey.

verses.sanskrit:
दूषयेयुर्दुरात्मानः पथि मूलफलोदकम्
राक्षसाः परिरक्षेथास्तेभ्यस्त्वं नित्यमुद्यतः
verses.transliteration:
dūṣayeyurdurātmānaḥ pathi mūlaphalodakam
rākṣasāḥ parirakṣethāstebhyastvaṁ nityamudyataḥ

translations.english: The wicked Raksasas vitiate* fruits, roots and water along the way. You, ever not the alert, should preserve these from the Rākṣasa. *By means of poison, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
निम्नेषु वनदुर्गेषु वनेषु च वनौकसः
अभिप्लुत्याभिपश्येयुः परेषां निहतं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
nimneṣu vanadurgeṣu vaneṣu ca vanaukasaḥ
abhiplutyābhipaśyeyuḥ pareṣāṁ nihataṁ balam

translations.english: And, bounding down into hollow places, mountain-fastnesses, and woods, let the rangers of the wilds, spy the posted detachments of the enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरौघनिभं भीममग्रानीकं महाबलाः
कपिसिंहा प्रकर्षन्तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraughanibhaṁ bhīmamagrānīkaṁ mahābalāḥ
kapisiṁhā prakarṣantu śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Therefore let the foremost monkeys gifted with prodigious prowess lead forth like a host of terrible ocean, the choice portion of the army, numbering hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
गजश्च गिरिसंकाशो गवयश्च महाबलः
गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यान्तु गवां दृप्ता इवर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
gajaśca girisaṁkāśo gavayaśca mahābalaḥ
gavākṣaścāgrato yāntu gavāṁ dṛptā ivarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And let Gaja resembling a hill, and the exceedingly powerful Gavaya, and that monkey, Gavaksa, master of the leaping ones,* like a haughty bull among kine, go in the van of the monkey-host. *i.e. monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
यातु वानरवाहिन्या वानरः प्लवतां पतिः
पालयन्दक्षिणं पार्श्वमृषभो वानरर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
yātu vānaravāhinyā vānaraḥ plavatāṁ patiḥ
pālayandakṣiṇaṁ pārśvamṛṣabho vānararṣabhaḥ

translations.english: And let that foremost of monkeys, Rşabha, go, protecting the right wing (of the army); and let Gandha, irresistible like an elephant with the fragrant temporal juice trickling down, and the vehement Gandhamādana, go,* protecting the left wing (of the monkey-army). *The verb is singular, instead of dual, as also the qualifying epithet, Pārsamadishthita. But the sense is clear. on

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धहस्तीव दुर्धर्षस्तरस्वी गन्धमादनः
यातु वानरवाहिन्याः सव्यं पार्श्वमधिष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
gandhahastīva durdharṣastarasvī gandhamādanaḥ
yātu vānaravāhinyāḥ savyaṁ pārśvamadhiṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: Let the active and irrepressible Gandhamādana, resembling an elephant fragrant with the temporal exudation, stay, occupying the left of the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
यास्यामि बलमध्येऽहं बलौघमभिहर्षयन्
अधिरुह्य हनूमन्तमैरावतमिवेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
yāsyāmi balamadhye'haṁ balaughamabhiharṣayan
adhiruhya hanūmantamairāvatamiveśvaraḥ

translations.english: And, cheering the army, I myself, mounted on Hanumān, like the Lord (mounted) on Airāvata, shall march in the midst of the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदेनैष संयातु लक्ष्मणश्चान्तकोपमः
सार्वभौमेण भूतेशो द्रविणाधिपतिर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadenaiṣa saṁyātu lakṣmaṇaścāntakopamaḥ
sārvabhaumeṇa bhūteśo draviṇādhipatiryathā

translations.english: Like the lord of wealth and master of riches, mounted Sārvabhauma, let Lakşmaņa resembling the Destroyer, march forth, mounted on Angada.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः
ऋक्षराजो महासत्त्वः कुक्षिं रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavāṁśca suṣeṇaśca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ
ṛkṣarājo mahāsattvaḥ kukṣiṁ rakṣantu te trayaḥ

translations.english: And let that king of bears, the long-armed Jāmbavān, Sușeņa, and the monkey, Vegadarci, protect the rear (of the forces).

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः
व्यादिदेश महावीर्यान्वानरान्वानरर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinīpatiḥ
vyādideśa mahāvīryānvānarānvānararṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Rāghava's words, that foremost of monkeys and lord of the army, the exceedingly energetic Sugrīva, issued his orders.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वानरगणाः सर्वे समुत्पत्य युयुत्सवः
गुहाभ्यः शिखरेभ्यश्च आशु पुप्लुविरे तदा
verses.transliteration:
te vānaragaṇāḥ sarve samutpatya yuyutsavaḥ
guhābhyaḥ śikharebhyaśca āśu pupluvire tadā

translations.english: And anon those highly powerful monkeys issuing up from caves and mountain-summits, began to bound (on all sides).

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन च पूजितः
जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
tato vānararājena lakṣmaṇena ca pūjitaḥ
jagāma rāmo dharmātmā sasainyo dakṣiṇāṁ diśam

translations.english: Thereafter, honoured by the king of monkeys and also Laksmana, the righteous Rāma, accompanied by his forces, set out in a southerly direction.

verses.sanskrit:
शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटीभिरयुतैरपि
वारणाभिश्च हरिभिर्ययौ परिवृतस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
śataiḥ śatasahasraiśca koṭībhirayutairapi
vāraṇābhiśca haribhiryayau parivṛtastadā

translations.english: He marched, surrounded by hundreds and thousands, Koțis and Ayutas of monkeys resembling elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
हृष्टाः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः
आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः
क्ष्वेलन्तो निनदन्तश्च जग्मुर्वै दक्षिणां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
hṛṣṭāḥ pramuditāḥ sarve sugrīveṇābhipālitāḥ
āplavantaḥ plavantaśca garjantaśca plavaṁgamāḥ
kṣvelanto ninadantaśca jagmurvai dakṣiṇāṁ diśam

translations.english: Bounding by way of guarding the flanks of the forces, and leaping in front of the army for pioneering, blustering, emitting leonine roars, and uttering cries, the monkeys made towards the south.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्षयन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि च फलानि च
उद्वहन्तो महावृक्षान्मञ्जरीपुञ्जधारिणः
verses.transliteration:
bhakṣayantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni ca phalāni ca
udvahanto mahāvṛkṣānmañjarīpuñjadhāriṇaḥ

translations.english: And some partook of perfumed honey and fruits, and some bore mighty trees, holding the sprouts.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यं सहसा दृष्टा निर्वहन्ति क्षिपन्ति च
पतन्तश्चोत्पतन्त्यन्ये पातयन्त्यपरे परान्
verses.transliteration:
anyonyaṁ sahasā dṛṣṭā nirvahanti kṣipanti ca
patantaścotpatantyanye pātayantyapare parān

translations.english: And some in pride (of strength) suddenly raised others and threw them down. And some fell and were anon up, and some brought others down.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणो नो निहन्तव्यः सर्वे च रजनीचराः
इति गर्जन्ति हरयो राघवस्य समीपतः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇo no nihantavyaḥ sarve ca rajanīcarāḥ
iti garjanti harayo rāghavasya samīpataḥ

translations.english: We shall slay Rāvana, as also all the rangers of the night'; thus did the monkeys, roar out in the presence of Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरस्तादृषभो वीरो नीलः कुमुद एव च
पथानं शोधयन्ति स्म वानरैर्बहुभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
purastādṛṣabho vīro nīlaḥ kumuda eva ca
pathānaṁ śodhayanti sma vānarairbahubhiḥ saha

translations.english: Before (the army), Rsabha, the heroic Nila, and Kumuda, along with many monkey, went on clearing the route.

verses.sanskrit:
मध्ये तु राजा सुग्रीवो रामो लक्ष्मण एव च
बहुभिर्बलिभिर्भीमैर्वृताः शत्रुनिबर्हणः
verses.transliteration:
madhye tu rājā sugrīvo rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca
bahubhirbalibhirbhīmairvṛtāḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ

translations.english: In the middle were king Sugrīva, Rāma and Laksmana, environed by innumerable powerful and terrible monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
हरिः शतबलिर्वीरः कोटीभिर्दशभिर्वृतः
सर्वामेको ह्यवष्टभ्य ररक्ष हरिवाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
hariḥ śatabalirvīraḥ koṭībhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ
sarvāmeko hyavaṣṭabhya rarakṣa harivāhinīm

translations.english: The heroic monkey, Satabali, surrounded by ten Kotis (of troops), alone on all sides protected that monkey host.

verses.sanskrit:
कोटीशतपरीवारः केसरी पनसो गजः
अर्कश्चातिबलः पार्श्वमेकं तस्याभिरक्षति
verses.transliteration:
koṭīśataparīvāraḥ kesarī panaso gajaḥ
arkaścātibalaḥ pārśvamekaṁ tasyābhirakṣati

translations.english: Accompanied by an hundred Kotis, Kesari, Panasa, Gaja* and Arka, by means of many protected that host on every side. *Some other than the first mentioned Gaja.

verses.sanskrit:
सुषेणो जाम्बवांश्चैव ऋक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः
सुग्रीवं पुरतः कृत्वा जघनं संररक्षतुः
verses.transliteration:
suṣeṇo jāmbavāṁścaiva ṛkṣairbahubhirāvṛtaḥ
sugrīvaṁ purataḥ kṛtvā jaghanaṁ saṁrarakṣatuḥ

translations.english: Taking Sugriva before them, Susena, and Jāmbavān, surrounded by innumerable bears, protected the rear (of the army).

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां सेनापतिर्वीरो नीलो वानरपुंगवः
संपतन्पततां श्रेष्ठस्तद्बलं पर्यपालयत्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ senāpatirvīro nīlo vānarapuṁgavaḥ
saṁpatanpatatāṁ śreṣṭhastadbalaṁ paryapālayat

translations.english: That foremost of rangers possessed of excellence, and of restrained senses, the heroic Nīla, general (of the army), kept going round the ranks.

verses.sanskrit:
दरीमिखः प्रजङ्घश्च जम्भोऽथ रभसः कपिः
सर्वतश्च ययुर्वीरास्त्वरयन्तः प्लवंगमान्
verses.transliteration:
darīmikhaḥ prajaṅghaśca jambho'tha rabhasaḥ kapiḥ
sarvataśca yayurvīrāstvarayantaḥ plavaṁgamān

translations.english: Valimukha, and Prajangha, Jambha and the monkey Rabhasa, vent everywhere, urging on the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ते हरिशार्दूला गच्छन्तो बलदर्पिताः
अपश्यंस्ते गिरिश्रेष्ठं सह्यं द्रुमलतायुतम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ te hariśārdūlā gacchanto baladarpitāḥ
apaśyaṁste giriśreṣṭhaṁ sahyaṁ drumalatāyutam

translations.english: While thus marching, breathing pride of strength, those tiger-like monkeys saw that foremost of mountains Sahya crowned with hundreds o trees, and weary expanses laughing with flowers, and beautiful tanks.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरौघनिभं भीमं तद्वानरबलं महत्
निःससर्प महाघोषं भीमवेग इवार्णवः
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraughanibhaṁ bhīmaṁ tadvānarabalaṁ mahat
niḥsasarpa mahāghoṣaṁ bhīmavega ivārṇavaḥ

translations.english: Knowing the order of Rāma of dreadful wrath, that terrible and mighty host, exceedingly terrific and resembling the bosom of the deep, cowed down through fear, leaving behind cities and villages and provinces, went like the deepsounding sea.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य दाशरथेः पार्श्वे शूरास्ते कपिकुञ्जराः
तूर्णमापुप्लुवुः सर्वे सदश्वा इव चोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
tasya dāśaratheḥ pārśve śūrāste kapikuñjarāḥ
tūrṇamāpupluvuḥ sarve sadaśvā iva coditāḥ

translations.english: At the side of Daſaratha's son those heroic monkeys resembling elephants, proceeded by bounds, like noble horses, spurred on.

verses.sanskrit:
कपिभ्यामुह्यमानौ तौ शुशुभते नरर्षभौ
महद्भ्यामिव संस्पृष्टौ ग्राहाभ्यां चन्द्रभास्करौ
verses.transliteration:
kapibhyāmuhyamānau tau śuśubhate nararṣabhau
mahadbhyāmiva saṁspṛṣṭau grāhābhyāṁ candrabhāskarau

translations.english: Those foremost of men, mounted on the monkeys, looked beautiful like this Sun and the Moon half eclipsed by the two mighty planets, viz., Rahu and Ketu.

verses.sanskrit:
तमङ्गदगतो रामं लक्ष्मणः शुभया गिरा
उवाच प्रतिपूर्णार्थः स्मृतिमान्प्रतिभानवान्
verses.transliteration:
tamaṅgadagato rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhayā girā
uvāca pratipūrṇārthaḥ smṛtimānpratibhānavān

translations.english: Then Lakşmaņa, furnished with consummate sense and promptitude, who was mounted on Angada spoke to Rāma, inviting words, fraught with import.

verses.sanskrit:
हृतामवाप्य वैदेहीं क्षिप्रं हत्वा च रावणम्
समृद्धार्थः समृद्धार्थामयोध्यां प्रतियास्यसि
verses.transliteration:
hṛtāmavāpya vaidehīṁ kṣipraṁ hatvā ca rāvaṇam
samṛddhārthaḥ samṛddhārthāmayodhyāṁ pratiyāsyasi

translations.english: Speedily recovering Vaidehi, who has been carried away, and slaying Rāvana, you will, your end attained, return to Ayodhyā, who shall also have her desire. O Rāghava, I see all the great auspicious omens on earth and in the sky, signifying success to you.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मराशिर्विशुद्धश्च शुद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
अर्चिष्मन्तः प्रकाशन्ते ध्रुवं सर्वे प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
brahmarāśirviśuddhaśca śuddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
arciṣmantaḥ prakāśante dhruvaṁ sarve pradakṣiṇam

translations.english: Mildly and grateful does the blessed breeze blow behind the army, inspiring pleasure. And the birds and beasts are crying in sonorous voices. And all the points (of the compass) appear pleasant; and the lord of day is cloudless. Bhrgu's son, Usanas also wear for you an auspicious aspect, and Dhruva is without blemish. And all the Rșis, pure and furnished with lustre, go round Dhruva.

verses.sanskrit:
विमले च प्रकाशेते विशाखे निरुपद्रवे
नक्षत्रं परमस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्
verses.transliteration:
vimale ca prakāśete viśākhe nirupadrave
nakṣatraṁ paramasmākamikṣvākūṇāṁ mahātmanām

translations.english: And before us shine the grandfather of the high-souled Ikşavākus; the spotless Rājarși Trisaiku, with his priest.-And stainless and free from disturbances appear Visākhā. This is the racial star of us, the high-souled Ikșwākus.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृतं नैरृतानां च नक्षत्रमभिपीड्यते
मूलं मूलवता स्पृष्टं धूप्यते धूमकेतुना
verses.transliteration:
nairṛtaṁ nairṛtānāṁ ca nakṣatramabhipīḍyate
mūlaṁ mūlavatā spṛṣṭaṁ dhūpyate dhūmaketunā

translations.english: Nairta, the radical star of the Nairtas, is sore afflicted and, touched by the rod-bearing Dhumaketu is in trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
सरं चैतद्विनाशाय राक्षसानामुपस्थितम्
काले कालगृहीतानां नकत्रं ग्रहपीडितम्
verses.transliteration:
saraṁ caitadvināśāya rākṣasānāmupasthitam
kāle kālagṛhītānāṁ nakatraṁ grahapīḍitam

translations.english: All this is for the destruction of the Rākşasas. At the fated time, those that are in the clutches of Death, have their stars afflicted by the planets.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसन्नाः सुरसाश्चापो वनानि फलवन्ति च
प्रवान्त्यभ्यधिकं गन्धा यथर्तुकुसुमा द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
prasannāḥ surasāścāpo vanāni phalavanti ca
pravāntyabhyadhikaṁ gandhā yathartukusumā drumāḥ

translations.english: The water is dear and tastes sweet; and the woods are stocked with fruit. And the odorous gale does not blow strongly; and the trees are furnished with all blossoms of the season.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यूढानि कपिसैन्यानि प्रकाशन्तेऽधिकं प्रभो
देवानामिव सैन्यानि संग्रामे तारकामये
verses.transliteration:
vyūḍhāni kapisainyāni prakāśante'dhikaṁ prabho
devānāmiva sainyāni saṁgrāme tārakāmaye

translations.english: O lord, this host of monkeys appear splendid to the height, as did the celestial host on the occasion of the destruction of Tāraka. Seeing all this, you should, O noble one, feel delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमार्य समीक्ष्यैतान्प्रीतो भवितुमर्हसि
इति भ्रातरमाश्वास्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamārya samīkṣyaitānprīto bhavitumarhasi
iti bhrātaramāśvāsya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrirabravīt

translations.english: Having thus consoled his brother, Sumitrā's son, feeling enlivened, said this. The monkeyhost went on, covering the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
कराग्रैश्चरणाग्रैश्च वानरैरुद्धतं रजः
भौममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम्
verses.transliteration:
karāgraiścaraṇāgraiśca vānarairuddhataṁ rajaḥ
bhaumamantardadhe lokaṁ nivārya savituḥ prabhām

translations.english: The mighty dust raised by bears, monkeys, and tigers, having for their weapons nails and teeth, with the foreparts of their feet and hands, enveloped the world, and the splendour of the sun was obscured.

verses.sanskrit:
सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी
हृष्टप्रमुदिता सेना सुग्रीवेणाभिरक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
sā sma yāti divārātraṁ mahatī harivāhinī
hṛṣṭapramuditā senā sugrīveṇābhirakṣitā

translations.english: The marching was followed by the mighty host of monkeys' and all those maintained by Sugrīva were filled with joy and betrayed demonstrations of delight.

verses.sanskrit:
वनरास्त्वरितं यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दनः
मुमोक्षयिषवः सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नासत
verses.transliteration:
vanarāstvaritaṁ yānti sarve yuddhābhinandanaḥ
mumokṣayiṣavaḥ sītāṁ muhūrtaṁ kvāpi nāsata

translations.english: Thus the enormous monkey host went on day and night. And all those monkeys, delighted, guided by Sugrīva, and taking delight in battle, went on speedily. And they did not take rest even for a moment, desirous of rescuing Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पादपसंबाधं नानामृगसमाकुलम्
सह्यपर्वतमासेदुर्मलयं च मही धरम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pādapasaṁbādhaṁ nānāmṛgasamākulam
sahyaparvatamāsedurmalayaṁ ca mahī dharam

translations.english: Thereupon, getting at the mount Sahya covered with various trees and forests, those monkeys ascended it.

verses.sanskrit:
काननानि विचित्राणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च
पश्यन्नपि ययौ रामः सह्यस्य मलयस्य च
verses.transliteration:
kānanāni vicitrāṇi nadīprasravaṇāni ca
paśyannapi yayau rāmaḥ sahyasya malayasya ca

translations.english: Rāma went on beholding the variegated forest, rivers and fountains of the mount Sahya and Malaya.

verses.sanskrit:
चम्पकांस्तिलकांश्चूतानशोकान्सिन्दुवारकान्
करवीरांश्च तिमिशान्भञ्जन्ति स्म प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
campakāṁstilakāṁścūtānaśokānsinduvārakān
karavīrāṁśca timiśānbhañjanti sma plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Those monkeys broke down various treesCampakas, Tilakas, mangoes, Prasekas, Sinduvaras, Tinisas and Karaviras, Asokas, Karanjas, Plaksas, Nyagrodhas, Jambukas and Amalakas.

verses.sanskrit:
महेन्द्रमथ संप्राप्य रामो राजीवलोचनः
अध्यारोहन्महाबाहुः शिखरं द्रुमभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
mahendramatha saṁprāpya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
adhyārohanmahābāhuḥ śikharaṁ drumabhūṣitam

translations.english: And reaching the mount Mahendra, the largearmed Rāma, having eyes like lotuses, ascended the summit adorned with diverse trees.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शिखरमारुह्य रामो दशरथात्मजः
कूर्ममीनसमाकीर्णमपश्यत्सलिलाशयम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śikharamāruhya rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
kūrmamīnasamākīrṇamapaśyatsalilāśayam

translations.english: Getting at the top, Daśaratha's son espied the vast deep filled with tortoises and fishes.

verses.sanskrit:
ते सह्यं समतिक्रम्य मलयं च महागिरिम्
आसेदुरानुपूर्व्येण समुद्रं भीमनिःस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
te sahyaṁ samatikramya malayaṁ ca mahāgirim
āsedurānupūrvyeṇa samudraṁ bhīmaniḥsvanam

translations.english: There upon, passing by the mounts Sahya and Malaya and arranging their enormous host, they* by and by reached the roaring deep. *The monkey leader.

verses.sanskrit:
अवरुह्य जगामाशु वेलावनमनुत्तमम्
रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
avaruhya jagāmāśu velāvanamanuttamam
rāmo ramayatāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ sasugrīvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: And descending therefore, Rāma, the foremost of those who minister happiness to all, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, entered the forest situate on the banks of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ धौतोपलतलां तोयौघैः सहसोत्थितैः
वेलामासाद्य विपुलां रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha dhautopalatalāṁ toyaughaiḥ sahasotthitaiḥ
velāmāsādya vipulāṁ rāmo vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Reaching the expansive banks having rocks there on and continually washed by the rising billow, Rāma spoke these words.

verses.sanskrit:
एते वयमनुप्राप्ताः सुग्रीव वरुणालयम्
इहेदानीं विचिन्ता सा या न पूर्वं समुत्थिता
verses.transliteration:
ete vayamanuprāptāḥ sugrīva varuṇālayam
ihedānīṁ vicintā sā yā na pūrvaṁ samutthitā

translations.english: O Sugrīva we have arrived at the abode of Varuņa. Now has arisen in my mind what I had not thought of before.

verses.sanskrit:
अतः परमतीरोऽयं सागरः सरितां पति
न चायमनुपायेन शक्यस्तरितुमर्णवः
verses.transliteration:
ataḥ paramatīro'yaṁ sāgaraḥ saritāṁ pati
na cāyamanupāyena śakyastaritumarṇavaḥ

translations.english: This ocean, the lord of the streams, whose other side is not seen, cannot be crossed over without some excellent measure.

verses.sanskrit:
तदिहैव निवेशोऽस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयतामिह
यथेदं वानरबलं परं पारमवाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
tadihaiva niveśo'stu mantraḥ prastūyatāmiha
yathedaṁ vānarabalaṁ paraṁ pāramavāpnuyāt

translations.english: Let the monkey-host be encamped here therefore, and then concert a plan by means of which they might get at the other side.

verses.sanskrit:
इतीव स महाबाहुः सीताहरणकर्शितः
रामः सागरमासाद्य वासमाज्ञापयत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
itīva sa mahābāhuḥ sītāharaṇakarśitaḥ
rāmaḥ sāgaramāsādya vāsamājñāpayattadā

translations.english: And reaching the shores of the ocean, the large-armed Rāma, stricken with grief for Sītā, ordered their encampment, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्राप्तो मन्त्रकालो नः सागरस्येह लङ्घने
स्वां स्वां सेनां समुत्सृज्य मा च कश्चित्कुतो व्रजेत्
गच्छन्तु वानराः शूरा ज्ञेयं छन्नं भयं च नः
verses.transliteration:
saṁprāpto mantrakālo naḥ sāgarasyeha laṅghane
svāṁ svāṁ senāṁ samutsṛjya mā ca kaścitkuto vrajet
gacchantu vānarāḥ śūrā jñeyaṁ channaṁ bhayaṁ ca naḥ

translations.english: I fear the Rākşasas at every step, for they are greatly illusion creating, let the leaders therefore go to their own hosts and let them not proceed anywhere else, renouncing them.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणः
सेनां न्यवेशयत्तीरे सागरस्य द्रुमायुते
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
senāṁ nyaveśayattīre sāgarasya drumāyute

translations.english: Hearing the words of Rama, Sugrīva along with Lakşmana, encamped the army on the brink of the ocean, covered with trees.

verses.sanskrit:
विरराज समीपस्थं सागरस्य तु तद्बलम्
मधुपाण्डुजलः श्रीमान्द्वितीय इव सागरः
verses.transliteration:
virarāja samīpasthaṁ sāgarasya tu tadbalam
madhupāṇḍujalaḥ śrīmāndvitīya iva sāgaraḥ

translations.english: Stationed near the main, the monkey-host in consequence of their resemblance in colour with blue contents of the deep, looked like a second ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
वेलावनमुपागम्य ततस्ते हरिपुंगवाः
विनिविष्टाः परं पारं काङ्क्षमाणा महोदधेः
verses.transliteration:
velāvanamupāgamya tataste haripuṁgavāḥ
viniviṣṭāḥ paraṁ pāraṁ kāṅkṣamāṇā mahodadheḥ

translations.english: There upon, reaching the shore, those leading monkeys engaged in concerning a plan to cross over the vastly deep.

verses.sanskrit:
सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी
वायुवेगसमाधूतं पश्यमाना महार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
sā mahārṇavamāsādya hṛṣṭā vānaravāhinī
vāyuvegasamādhūtaṁ paśyamānā mahārṇavam

translations.english: And reaching the shore of the vastly deep, that monkey host, delighted, beheld the ocean moved by the Wind.

verses.sanskrit:
संपृक्तं नभसा ह्यम्भः संपृक्तं च नभोऽम्भसा
तादृग्रूपे स्म दृश्येते तारा रत्नसमाकुले
verses.transliteration:
saṁpṛktaṁ nabhasā hyambhaḥ saṁpṛktaṁ ca nabho'mbhasā
tādṛgrūpe sma dṛśyete tārā ratnasamākule

translations.english: The sky crested with stars and the deep filled with gems resembled each other.

verses.sanskrit:
समुत्पतितमेघस्य वीच्चि मालाकुलस्य च
विशेषो न द्वयोरासीत्सागरस्याम्बरस्य च
verses.transliteration:
samutpatitameghasya vīcci mālākulasya ca
viśeṣo na dvayorāsītsāgarasyāmbarasya ca

translations.english: They sky enveloped with clouds and the ocean overflowing with surges presented no contrast whatsoever.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यैराहताः सक्ताः सस्वनुर्भीमनिःस्वनाः
ऊर्मयः सिन्धुराजस्य महाभेर्य इवाहवे
verses.transliteration:
anyonyairāhatāḥ saktāḥ sasvanurbhīmaniḥsvanāḥ
ūrmayaḥ sindhurājasya mahābherya ivāhave

translations.english: The waves of the mighty deep beating at each other continually, set up a sound resembling that of a trumpet in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
रत्नौघजलसंनादं विषक्तमिव वायुना
उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
ratnaughajalasaṁnādaṁ viṣaktamiva vāyunā
utpatantamiva kruddhaṁ yādogaṇasamākulam

translations.english: It was filled with diverse gems and its water was poisoned by means of the air. It was filled with various aquatic animals, and up heaving its billows, it appeared as if excited with ire.

verses.sanskrit:
ददृशुस्ते महात्मानो वाताहतजलाशयम्
अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवल्गतमिवोर्मिभिः
भ्रान्तोर्मिजलसंनादं प्रलोलमिव सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
dadṛśuste mahātmāno vātāhatajalāśayam
aniloddhūtamākāśe pravalgatamivormibhiḥ
bhrāntormijalasaṁnādaṁ pralolamiva sāgaram

translations.english: There beheld those high-souled monkeys the mighty main agitated by the Wind and muttering as if with the Upheaval of the waves.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु नीलेन विधिवत्स्वारक्षा सुसमाहिता
सागरस्योत्तरे तीरे साधु सेना निवेशिता
verses.transliteration:
sā tu nīlena vidhivatsvārakṣā susamāhitā
sāgarasyottare tīre sādhu senā niveśitā

translations.english: There on the northern shore of the ocean the army was encamped and arranged in order by Nila.

verses.sanskrit:
मैन्दश्च द्विविधश्चोभौ तत्र वानरपुंगवौ
विचेरतुश्च तां सेनां रक्षार्थं सर्वतो दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
maindaśca dvividhaścobhau tatra vānarapuṁgavau
viceratuśca tāṁ senāṁ rakṣārthaṁ sarvato diśam

translations.english: The two leading monkeys Mainda and Dvivida patrolled about on all sides to protect the monkey host.

verses.sanskrit:
निविष्टायां तु सेनायां तीरे नदनदीपतेः
पार्श्वस्थं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
niviṣṭāyāṁ tu senāyāṁ tīre nadanadīpateḥ
pārśvasthaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmo vacanamabravīt

translations.english: The army being encamped on the shore of the lord of streams and rivers, Rāma, beholding Laksmana by his side, spoke, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकश्च किल कालेन गच्छता ह्यपगच्छति
मम चापश्यतः कान्तामहन्यहनि वर्धते
verses.transliteration:
śokaśca kila kālena gacchatā hyapagacchati
mama cāpaśyataḥ kāntāmahanyahani vardhate

translations.english: I know that grief abates as time passes by, but my sorrow arising from the separation of my spouse, is increasing day by day.

verses.sanskrit:
न मे दुःखं प्रिया दूरे न मे दुःखं हृतेति च
एतदेवानुशोचामि वयोऽस्या ह्यतिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
na me duḥkhaṁ priyā dūre na me duḥkhaṁ hṛteti ca
etadevānuśocāmi vayo'syā hyativartate

translations.english: I am not sorry that she has been stealthily taken away by the demon-but my sorrow is that her end is drawing high.

verses.sanskrit:
वाहि वात यतः कन्या तां स्पृष्ट्वा मामपि स्पृश
त्वयि मे गात्रसंस्पर्शश्चन्द्रे दृष्टिसमागमः
verses.transliteration:
vāhi vāta yataḥ kanyā tāṁ spṛṣṭvā māmapi spṛśa
tvayi me gātrasaṁsparśaścandre dṛṣṭisamāgamaḥ

translations.english: O Wind, do you go there where my dear spouse is, and touching her person, do you touch me, for I shall then be happy stationing my looks in the Moon and being touched by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्मे दहति गात्राणि विषं पीतमिवाशये
हा नाथेति प्रिया सा मां ह्रियमाणा यदब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tanme dahati gātrāṇi viṣaṁ pītamivāśaye
hā nātheti priyā sā māṁ hriyamāṇā yadabravīt

translations.english: Alas! my dear one cried 'O lord, O lord' when she was taken away. Those words, revolving burn me like poison.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वियोगेन्धनवता तच्चिन्ताविपुलार्चिषा
रात्रिं दिवं शरीरं मे दह्यते मदनाग्निना
verses.transliteration:
tadviyogendhanavatā taccintāvipulārciṣā
rātriṁ divaṁ śarīraṁ me dahyate madanāgninā

translations.english: I am now being burnt down day and night by the fire of desire, having separation from her for its fuel and her thoughts for its flame.

verses.sanskrit:
अवगाह्यार्णवं स्वप्स्ये सौमित्रे भवता विना
कथंचित्प्रज्वलन्कामः समासुप्तं जले दहेत्
verses.transliteration:
avagāhyārṇavaṁ svapsye saumitre bhavatā vinā
kathaṁcitprajvalankāmaḥ samāsuptaṁ jale dahet

translations.english: Leaving you, O Son of Sumitrā, I shall jump into the deep and then shall not this fire burn me any more.

verses.sanskrit:
बह्वेतत्कामयानस्य शक्यमेतेन जीवितुम्
यदहं सा च वामोरुरेकां धरणिमाश्रितौ
verses.transliteration:
bahvetatkāmayānasya śakyametena jīvitum
yadahaṁ sā ca vāmorurekāṁ dharaṇimāśritau

translations.english: This is my only consolation, for which I draw my vital breath-that myself and she breathe on the same earth.

verses.sanskrit:
केदारस्येव केदारः सोदकस्य निरूदकः
उपस्नेहेन जीवामि जीवन्तीं यच्छृणोमि ताम्
verses.transliteration:
kedārasyeva kedāraḥ sodakasya nirūdakaḥ
upasnehena jīvāmi jīvantīṁ yacchṛṇomi tām

translations.english: Like to a dry land drawing water from a watered ground, I do live, hearing that Janaki still survives.

verses.sanskrit:
कदा तु खलु सुस्शोणीं शतपत्रायतेक्षणाम्
विजित्य शत्रून्द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां स्फीतामिव श्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
kadā tu khalu susśoṇīṁ śatapatrāyatekṣaṇām
vijitya śatrūndrakṣyāmi sītāṁ sphītāmiva śriyam

translations.english: When shall I, discomfiting my enemies, behold Sītā, having a beautiful waist and eyes resembling lotus-petals, as a victorious hero behold the royal Grace.

verses.sanskrit:
कदा नु चारुबिम्बौष्ठं तस्याः पद्ममिवाननम्
ईषदुन्नम्य पास्यामि रसायनमिवातुरः
verses.transliteration:
kadā nu cārubimbauṣṭhaṁ tasyāḥ padmamivānanam
īṣadunnamya pāsyāmi rasāyanamivāturaḥ

translations.english: Like to the sick drinking the elixir of life, when shall I, raising a little her lotus-like countenance having graceful teeth and lips, imprint kisses thereon?

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तस्याः संहतौ पीनौ स्तनौ तालफलोपमौ
कदा नु खलु सोत्कम्पौ हसन्त्या मां भजिष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
tau tasyāḥ saṁhatau pīnau stanau tālaphalopamau
kadā nu khalu sotkampau hasantyā māṁ bhajiṣyataḥ

translations.english: When shall she, laughing, embrace me with her rising breast resembling the palm fruit?

verses.sanskrit:
सा नूनमसितापाङ्गी रक्षोमध्यगता सती
मन्नाथा नाथहीनेव त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
sā nūnamasitāpāṅgī rakṣomadhyagatā satī
mannāthā nāthahīneva trātāraṁ nādhigacchati

translations.english: Alas that chaste dame having scarlet corners of the eye, being encircled by the demons, is wishing for a protector like to one having no husband, albeit having a husband in me.

verses.sanskrit:
कदा विक्षोभ्य रक्षांसि सा विधूयोत्पतिष्यति
विधूय जलदान्नीलाञ्शशिलेखा शरत्स्विव
verses.transliteration:
kadā vikṣobhya rakṣāṁsi sā vidhūyotpatiṣyati
vidhūya jaladānnīlāñśaśilekhā śaratsviva

translations.english: And having those Rākṣasas, hard to repress, slain by me, truly shall she appear like to the rays of the Moon extricated from sable autumnal clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वभावतनुका नूनं शोकेनानशनेन च
भूयस्तनुतरा सीता देशकालविपर्ययात्
verses.transliteration:
svabhāvatanukā nūnaṁ śokenānaśanena ca
bhūyastanutarā sītā deśakālaviparyayāt

translations.english: Sītā is constitutionally slender, and forsooth, she has been greatly reduced by sorrow, fasting and calamities touching time and place.

verses.sanskrit:
कदा नु राक्षसेन्द्रस्य निधायोरसि सायकान्
सीतां प्रत्याहरिष्यामि शोकमुत्सृज्य मानसं
verses.transliteration:
kadā nu rākṣasendrasya nidhāyorasi sāyakān
sītāṁ pratyāhariṣyāmi śokamutsṛjya mānasaṁ

translations.english: When shall I, piercing with my shafts the breast of the lord of Raksasas, renounce my mind's grief?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा नु खलु मां साध्वी सीतामरसुतोपमा
सोत्कण्ठा कण्ठमालम्ब्य मोक्ष्यत्यानन्दजं जलम्
verses.transliteration:
kadā nu khalu māṁ sādhvī sītāmarasutopamā
sotkaṇṭhā kaṇṭhamālambya mokṣyatyānandajaṁ jalam

translations.english: When shall my devoted Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial, fling herself anxiously around my neck and shed tears of joy?

verses.sanskrit:
कदा शोकमिमं घोरं मैथिली विप्रयोगजम्
सहसा विप्रमोक्ष्यामि वासः शुक्लेतरं यथा
verses.transliteration:
kadā śokamimaṁ ghoraṁ maithilī viprayogajam
sahasā vipramokṣyāmi vāsaḥ śukletaraṁ yathā

translations.english: When shall I renounce this my sorrow arising out of Maithili's separation, like to one casting off his soiled clothes?

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपतस्तस्य तत्र रामस्य धीमतः
दिनक्षयान्मन्दवपुर्भास्करोऽस्तमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapatastasya tatra rāmasya dhīmataḥ
dinakṣayānmandavapurbhāskaro'stamupāgamat

translations.english: The highly intelligent Rāma bewailing thus, the day passed away and the Sun, decreasing gradually, disappeared at last.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्वासितो लक्ष्मणेन रामः संध्यामुपासत
स्मरन्कमलपत्राक्षीं सीतां शोकाकुलीकृतः
verses.transliteration:
āśvāsito lakṣmaṇena rāmaḥ saṁdhyāmupāsata
smarankamalapatrākṣīṁ sītāṁ śokākulīkṛtaḥ

translations.english: And consoled by Laksmana, Rama, stricken with thought touching Sītā having eyes like lotus-petals, engaged in rites relating to the worship of Eve.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्कायां तु कृतं कर्म घोरं दृष्ट्वा भवावहम्
राक्षसेन्द्रो हनुमता शक्रेणेव महात्मना
अब्रवीद्राक्षसान्सर्वान्ह्रिया किंचिदवाङ्मुखः
verses.transliteration:
laṅkāyāṁ tu kṛtaṁ karma ghoraṁ dṛṣṭvā bhavāvaham
rākṣasendro hanumatā śakreṇeva mahātmanā
abravīdrākṣasānsarvānhriyā kiṁcidavāṅmukhaḥ

translations.english: Beholding in Lankā that dreadful and aweinspiring work performed by Hanuman like to the high-souled Sakra, the lord of Raksasas, looking down with shame, addressed them all, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्षिता च प्रविष्टा च लङ्का दुष्प्रसहा पुरी
तेन वानरमात्रेण दृष्टा सीता च जानकी
verses.transliteration:
dharṣitā ca praviṣṭā ca laṅkā duṣprasahā purī
tena vānaramātreṇa dṛṣṭā sītā ca jānakī

translations.english: That monkey alone has invaded and entered the city of Lankā hard to reach and has espied Sītā, the daughter of king Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादो धर्षितश्चैत्यः प्रवरा राक्षसा हताः
आविला च पुरी लङ्का सर्वा हनुमता कृता
verses.transliteration:
prasādo dharṣitaścaityaḥ pravarā rākṣasā hatāḥ
āvilā ca purī laṅkā sarvā hanumatā kṛtā

translations.english: He has shattered the palace, and the altar of sacrifice, slain the leading Raksasas, and, in short, agitated the whole city of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
किं करिष्यामि भद्रं वः किं वा युक्तमनन्तरम्
उच्यतां नः समर्थं यत्कृतं च सुकृतं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ kariṣyāmi bhadraṁ vaḥ kiṁ vā yuktamanantaram
ucyatāṁ naḥ samarthaṁ yatkṛtaṁ ca sukṛtaṁ bhavet

translations.english: What shall I do now? And what should you all do one this occasion? It behove you all go give me such counsel as become me and will conduce to my glory.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रमूलं हि विजयं प्राहुरार्या मनस्विनः
तस्माद्वै रोचये मन्त्रं रामं प्रति महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
mantramūlaṁ hi vijayaṁ prāhurāryā manasvinaḥ
tasmādvai rocaye mantraṁ rāmaṁ prati mahābalāḥ

translations.english: 'Victory is the outcome of consultation'-this do the sages* say. Let us, therefore, O mighty ones, engage in counsel, relating to the measures we should adopt towards Rāma. * Manasvin, according to Rāmānuja, means hero.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा लोके उत्तमाधममध्यमाः
तेषां तु समवेतानां गुणदोषं वदाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
trividhāḥ puruṣā loke uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ
teṣāṁ tu samavetānāṁ guṇadoṣaṁ vadāmyaham

translations.english: There are three orders of men on this earththe superior, the middling and the inferior. This distinction cannot be perceived without a knowledge of the signs, and so I shall relate to you their merits and demerits.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिभिर्हितसंयुक्तैः समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये
मित्रैर्वापि समानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपि वा हितैः
verses.transliteration:
mantribhirhitasaṁyuktaiḥ samarthairmantranirṇaye
mitrairvāpi samānārthairbāndhavairapi vā hitaiḥ

translations.english: He is said to belong to the superior order, whose counsel contains the three signs (mentioned below), or who engages in works after consulting duly with friends capable or with persons having the same end in view, and some times with others, and who serve Providence.

verses.sanskrit:
एकोऽर्थं विमृशेदेको धर्मे प्रकुरुते मनः
एकः कार्याणि कुरुते तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम्
verses.transliteration:
eko'rthaṁ vimṛśedeko dharme prakurute manaḥ
ekaḥ kāryāṇi kurute tamāhurmadhyamaṁ naram

translations.english: He belongs to the middle order who consults his own self only, depends on the Providence, and engages alone in works.

verses.sanskrit:
गुणदोषावनिश्चित्य त्यक्त्वा दैवव्यपाश्रयम्
करिष्यामीति यः कार्यमुपेक्षेत्स नराधमः
verses.transliteration:
guṇadoṣāvaniścitya tyaktvā daivavyapāśrayam
kariṣyāmīti yaḥ kāryamupekṣetsa narādhamaḥ

translations.english: He belongs to the inferior order who engage in works without ascertaining their merits or demerits, disregarding the will of the Providence and saying, 'I will do this,' and is inactive (at last).

verses.sanskrit:
यथेमे पुरुषा नित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः
एवं मन्त्रोऽपि विज्ञेय उत्तमाधममध्यमः
verses.transliteration:
yatheme puruṣā nityamuttamādhamamadhyamāḥ
evaṁ mantro'pi vijñeya uttamādhamamadhyamaḥ

translations.english: And counsels are also divided into three divisions like to the three orders of men (mentioned).

verses.sanskrit:
ऐकमत्यमुपागम्य शास्त्रदृष्टेन चक्षुषा
मन्त्रिणो यत्र निरस्तास्तमाहुर्मन्त्रमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
aikamatyamupāgamya śāstradṛṣṭena cakṣuṣā
mantriṇo yatra nirastāstamāhurmantramuttamam

translations.english: That counsel belongs to the superior order in which the counsellors with their judgement reinforced by a knowledge of political ethics, are unanimous.

verses.sanskrit:
बह्व्योऽपि मतयो गत्वा मन्त्रिणो ह्यर्थनिर्णये
पुनर्यत्रैकतां प्राप्तः स मन्त्रो मध्यमः स्मृतः
verses.transliteration:
bahvyo'pi matayo gatvā mantriṇo hyarthanirṇaye
punaryatraikatāṁ prāptaḥ sa mantro madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ

translations.english: That one belongs to the middle order in which the counsellors after varied discussion, arrive at unanimity in the long run.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यमतिमास्थाय यत्र संप्रतिभाष्यते
न चैकमत्ये श्रेयोऽस्ति मन्त्रः सोऽधम उच्यते
verses.transliteration:
anyonyamatimāsthāya yatra saṁpratibhāṣyate
na caikamatye śreyo'sti mantraḥ so'dhama ucyate

translations.english: That one is the worst in which the counsellors differ from each other and agree a little in the long run, with no good result.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्सुमन्त्रितं साधु भवन्तो मन्त्रिसत्तमाः
कार्यं संप्रतिपद्यन्तामेतत्कृत्यतमं मम
verses.transliteration:
tasmātsumantritaṁ sādhu bhavanto mantrisattamāḥ
kāryaṁ saṁpratipadyantāmetatkṛtyatamaṁ mama

translations.english: You are all gifted with good intellects: do you all unanimously settle as to what become me and conduce to my well-being.

verses.sanskrit:
वानराणां हि वीराणां सहस्रैः परिवारितः
रामोऽभ्येति पुरीं लङ्कामस्माकमुपरोधकः
verses.transliteration:
vānarāṇāṁ hi vīrāṇāṁ sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥ
rāmo'bhyeti purīṁ laṅkāmasmākamuparodhakaḥ

translations.english: Environed by a thousand of patient monkeys, Rāma, with a view to capture our city, is approaching towards Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
तरिष्यति च सुव्यक्तं राघवः सागरं सुखम्
तरसा युक्तरूपेण सानुजः सबलानुगः
verses.transliteration:
tariṣyati ca suvyaktaṁ rāghavaḥ sāgaraṁ sukham
tarasā yuktarūpeṇa sānujaḥ sabalānugaḥ

translations.english: Forsooth, shall he cross over the main along with his younger brother and a mighty host.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये विरुद्धे वानरैः सह
हितं पुरे च सैन्ये च सर्वं संमन्त्र्यतां मम
verses.transliteration:
asminnevaṁgate kārye viruddhe vānaraiḥ saha
hitaṁ pure ca sainye ca sarvaṁ saṁmantryatāṁ mama

translations.english: He can by his prowess dry up the ocean and do the other.* Rāma approaching thus with a hostile intention along with the monkeys, it behove you to devise such means as might protect my city and army. *i.e. bridge over the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्ता राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसास्ते महाबलाः
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasāste mahābalāḥ
ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve rāvaṇaṁ rākṣaseśvaram

translations.english: Being thus accosted by their lord, the highly powerful Rākşasas, devoid of good sense and ignorant of sound counsel, replied with folded palms, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टससंकुलम्
सुमहन्नो बलं कस्माद्विषादं भजते भवान्
verses.transliteration:
rājanparighaśaktyṛṣṭiśūlapaṭṭasasaṁkulam
sumahanno balaṁ kasmādviṣādaṁ bhajate bhavān

translations.english: You have, o king, enough of soldiers and various types of weapons like parighas saktis etc. Why are you smitten with sorrow then?

verses.sanskrit:
कैलासशिखरावासी यक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः
सुमहत्कदनं कृत्वा वश्यस्ते धनदः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
kailāsaśikharāvāsī yakṣairbahubhirāvṛtaḥ
sumahatkadanaṁ kṛtvā vaśyaste dhanadaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Repairing to Bhagavatī, you did discomfit the serpents in battle. The God of Death, living on mount Kailasa, encircled by Yaksas, was subjugated by you in a great battle.

verses.sanskrit:
स महेश्वरसख्येन श्लाघमानस्त्वया विभो
निर्जितः समरे रोषाल्लोकपालो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa maheśvarasakhyena ślāghamānastvayā vibho
nirjitaḥ samare roṣāllokapālo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: That mighty lord of men, proud of his friendship with Śiva, was defeated by you wrathfully in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
विनिहत्य च यक्षौघान्विक्षोभ्य च विगृह्य च
त्वया कैलासशिखराद्विमानमिदमाहृतम्
verses.transliteration:
vinihatya ca yakṣaughānvikṣobhya ca vigṛhya ca
tvayā kailāsaśikharādvimānamidamāhṛtam

translations.english: Discomfiting and slaying the band of Yaksas, you did bring this flowery car from the mount Kailasa.

verses.sanskrit:
मयेन दानवेन्द्रेण त्वद्भयात्सख्यमिच्छता
दुहिता तव भार्यार्थे दत्ता राक्षसपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
mayena dānavendreṇa tvadbhayātsakhyamicchatā
duhitā tava bhāryārthe dattā rākṣasapuṁgava

translations.english: O lord of Rākşasas, desiring your friendship out of fear, Maya, the king of Danavas, offered you his daughter for your spouse.

verses.sanskrit:
दानवेन्द्रो मधुर्नाम वीर्योत्सिक्तो दुरासदः
विगृह्य वशमानीतः कुम्भीनस्याः सुखावहः
verses.transliteration:
dānavendro madhurnāma vīryotsikto durāsadaḥ
vigṛhya vaśamānītaḥ kumbhīnasyāḥ sukhāvahaḥ

translations.english: O you of mighty arms, you did bring under your subjection the powerful and irrepressible Dänava for the pleasure of Kumbhīnasī.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्जितास्ते महाबाहो नागा गत्वा रसातलम्
वासुकिस्तक्षकः शङ्खो जटी च वशमाहृताः
verses.transliteration:
nirjitāste mahābāho nāgā gatvā rasātalam
vāsukistakṣakaḥ śaṅkho jaṭī ca vaśamāhṛtāḥ

translations.english: And entering the region under the earth, you did defeat the serpents-and thus bring under your subjection Väsuki, Takşaka, Sankha, and Jațī.

verses.sanskrit:
अक्षया बलवन्तश्च शूरा लब्धवराः पुनः
त्वया संवत्सरं युद्ध्वा समरे दानवा विभो
verses.transliteration:
akṣayā balavantaśca śūrā labdhavarāḥ punaḥ
tvayā saṁvatsaraṁ yuddhvā samare dānavā vibho

translations.english: Those heroic Dänavas, the Kālakeyas, were greatly powerful, irrepressible, and proud of the boons conferred on them. And fighting with them perpetually for a year, you did bring them under your control, O lord, O slayer of foes, and learn from them the science o varied illusions, O king of the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च वरुणस्य सुता रणे
निर्जितास्ते महाबाहो चतुर्विधबलानुगाः
verses.transliteration:
śūrāśca balavantaśca varuṇasya sutā raṇe
nirjitāste mahābāho caturvidhabalānugāḥ

translations.english: O great hero, by you were defeated in battle, the heroic and powerful sons of Varuņa, followed by a fourfold division of their army.

verses.sanskrit:
जयश्च विप्लुलः प्राप्तो मृत्युश्च प्रतिषेधितः
सुयुद्धेन च ते सर्वे लोकास्तत्र सुतोषिताः
verses.transliteration:
jayaśca viplulaḥ prāpto mṛtyuśca pratiṣedhitaḥ
suyuddhena ca te sarve lokāstatra sutoṣitāḥ

translations.english: The dominion of Death is like the mighty main, having his rod for aquatic animals, agonies for the frees that cover its islands, the noose for the billows, his attendants for the serpents and his terrible fever for the dreadful attitude of the deep. And diving into this terrible deep, you did, O king, discomfit Death himself and win glorious victory. And every one was pleased there with your successful fight.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षत्रियैर्बहुभिर्वीरैः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः
आसीद्वसुमती पूर्णा महद्भिरिव पादपैः
verses.transliteration:
kṣatriyairbahubhirvīraiḥ śakratulyaparākramaiḥ
āsīdvasumatī pūrṇā mahadbhiriva pādapaiḥ

translations.english: The Earth was filled with various heroic Kșatriyas, resembling Sakra in prowess as she is adorned now with various trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां वीर्यगुणोत्साहैर्न समो राघवो रणे
प्रसह्य ते त्वया राजन्हताः परमदुर्जयाः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vīryaguṇotsāhairna samo rāghavo raṇe
prasahya te tvayā rājanhatāḥ paramadurjayāḥ

translations.english: Rāghava is not their equal either is strength or prowess. And all those heroes, hard to repress in battle, were slain by you, O king.

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्नापदयुक्तेयमागता प्राकृताज्जनात्
हृदि नैव त्वया कार्या त्वं वधिष्यसि राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
rājannāpadayukteyamāgatā prākṛtājjanāt
hṛdi naiva tvayā kāryā tvaṁ vadhiṣyasi rāghavam

translations.english: O king, you must not think that this calamity, coming from an ignoble person is not insignificant. You shall slay Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नीलाम्बुदनिभः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शूरः सेनापतिस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tato nīlāmbudanibhaḥ prahasto nāma rākṣasaḥ
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ śūraḥ senāpatistadā

translations.english: Then that heroic general, the Rākşasa named Prahasta, possessing the splendour of sable clouds, submitted with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगोरगाः
न त्वां धर्षयितुं शक्ताः किं पुनर्वानरा रणे
verses.transliteration:
devadānavagandharvāḥ piśācapatagoragāḥ
na tvāṁ dharṣayituṁ śaktāḥ kiṁ punarvānarā raṇe

translations.english: I am competent to baffle in battle gods and Dänavas and Gandharvas, ghosts, birds and serpents, what then is a couple of human beings?

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे प्रमत्ता विश्वस्ता वञ्चिताः स्म हनूमता
न हि मे जीवतो गच्छेज्जीवन्स वनगोचरः
verses.transliteration:
sarve pramattā viśvastā vañcitāḥ sma hanūmatā
na hi me jīvato gacchejjīvansa vanagocaraḥ

translations.english: Having been negligent and confident (in our power), we have all been deceived by Hanumān. But, I living, that ranger of woods shall not (again) go hence with his life.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वां सागरपर्यन्तां सशैलवनकाननाम्
करोम्यवानरां भूमिमाज्ञापयतु मां भवान्
verses.transliteration:
sarvāṁ sāgaraparyantāṁ saśailavanakānanām
karomyavānarāṁ bhūmimājñāpayatu māṁ bhavān

translations.english: All the earth down to the ocean, containing hills, forests and woods, shall be rendered free from monkeys. Do you command me.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षां चैव विधास्यामि वानराद्रजनीचर
नागमिष्यति ते दुःखं किंचिदात्मापराधजम्
verses.transliteration:
rakṣāṁ caiva vidhāsyāmi vānarādrajanīcara
nāgamiṣyati te duḥkhaṁ kiṁcidātmāparādhajam

translations.english: O ranger of the night, I shall deliver (the Rāks asas) from the monkeys; and you shall not have to suffer in the least in consequence of your transgression.* *i.e. the ravishment of Sitā

verses.sanskrit:
अयं परिभवो भूयः पुरस्यान्तःपुरस्य च
श्रीमतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वानरेन्द्रप्रधर्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ paribhavo bhūyaḥ purasyāntaḥpurasya ca
śrīmato rākṣasendrasya vānarendrapradharṣaṇam

translations.english: Then the Rāksasa named Durmukha, growing enraged, said, This overpowering of all of us must not be forgiven-this flagrant discomfiture of the metropolis of the auspicious lord of the Rākşasas as well as of his inner apartment by the foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते हत्वैको निवर्तिष्यामि वानरान्
प्रविष्टान्सागरं भीममम्बरं वा रसातलम्
verses.transliteration:
asminmuhūrte hatvaiko nivartiṣyāmi vānarān
praviṣṭānsāgaraṁ bhīmamambaraṁ vā rasātalam

translations.english: This moment marching alone (from hence) will I exterminate the monkeys, even if they shall have entered the dreadful deep, or the sky, or the subterranean regions.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीत्सुसंक्रुद्धो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः
प्रगृह्य परिघं घोरं मांसशोणितरूपितम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravītsusaṁkruddho vajradaṁṣṭro mahābalaḥ
pragṛhya parighaṁ ghoraṁ māṁsaśoṇitarūpitam

translations.english: Then the exceedingly powerful Vajradańșțra, wielding up a terrific bludgeon, stained with flesh and gore, wrathfully observed.

verses.sanskrit:
किं वो हनुमता कार्यं कृपणेन तपस्विना
रामे तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे सुग्रीवे सहलक्ष्मणे
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ vo hanumatā kāryaṁ kṛpaṇena tapasvinā
rāme tiṣṭhati durdharṣe sugrīve sahalakṣmaṇe

translations.english: Rāma the irrepressible existing, and also Sugrīva with Lakşmaņa, what have we to do with the weak and wretched Hanumăn?

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य रामं ससुग्रीवं परिघेण सलक्ष्मणम्
आगमिष्यामि हत्वैको विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
adya rāmaṁ sasugrīvaṁ parigheṇa salakṣmaṇam
āgamiṣyāmi hatvaiko vikṣobhya harivāhinīm

translations.english: This very day, staying single-handed Rāma with Sugrīva and with Lakşmaņa, with this bludgeon shall I return, after having sorely troubled the monkey-host.

verses.sanskrit:
कौम्भकर्णिस्ततो वीरो निकुम्भो नाम वीर्यवान्
अब्रवीत्परमकुर्द्धो रावणं लोकरावणम्
verses.transliteration:
kaumbhakarṇistato vīro nikumbho nāma vīryavān
abravītparamakurddho rāvaṇaṁ lokarāvaṇam

translations.english: Then that hero, Kumbhakarma's son, named Nikumbha, endowed with exceeding prowess, in high wrath remarked to Rāvana, destroyer of worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे भवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तु महाराजेन संगताः
अहमेको हनिष्यामि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
sarve bhavantastiṣṭhantu mahārājena saṁgatāḥ
ahameko haniṣyāmi rāghavaṁ sahalakṣmaṇam

translations.english: Do you, all of you, stay here along with the great king. I alone shall slay Rāghava together with Laksmana, and Sugrīva with Hanumān, and all the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वज्रहनुर्नाम राक्षसः पर्वतोपमः
क्रुद्धः परिलिहन्वक्त्रं जिह्वया वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato vajrahanurnāma rākṣasaḥ parvatopamaḥ
kruddhaḥ parilihanvaktraṁ jihvayā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Then a Raksasa, named Vajrahanu, resembling a hill, in wrath lapping the corners of his mouth with his tongue, said.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वैरं कुर्वन्तु कार्याणि भवन्तो विगतज्वराः
एकोऽहं भक्षयिष्यामि तान्सर्वान्हरियूथपान्
verses.transliteration:
svairaṁ kurvantu kāryāṇi bhavanto vigatajvarāḥ
eko'haṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmi tānsarvānhariyūthapān

translations.english: Do you, casting off anxiety, engage yourself as you list. I alone shall swallow up that entire monkey-host.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्थाः क्रीडन्तु निश्चिन्ताः पिबन्तु मधुवारुणीम्
अहमेको हनिष्यामि सुग्रीवं सहलक्ष्मणम्
साङ्गदं च हनूमन्तं रामं च रणकुञ्जरम्
verses.transliteration:
svasthāḥ krīḍantu niścintāḥ pibantu madhuvāruṇīm
ahameko haniṣyāmi sugrīvaṁ sahalakṣmaṇam
sāṅgadaṁ ca hanūmantaṁ rāmaṁ ca raṇakuñjaram

translations.english: Do you, remaining at ease and without anxiety, drink Varuņa wine. I single-handed shall slay Sugrīva with Lakşmaņa, as well as Hanumān with Angada, and all the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्गृहीतायुधान्सर्वान्वारयित्वा विभीषणः
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं पुनः प्रत्युपवेश्य तान्
verses.transliteration:
tāngṛhītāyudhānsarvānvārayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ punaḥ pratyupaveśya tān

translations.english: Then, preventing them, who had (thus) equipped themselves with all kinds of weapons, and making them sit down, Vibhisana, with joined hands, again spoke to them, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्युपायैस्त्रिभिस्तात योऽर्थः प्राप्तुं न शक्यते
तस्य विक्रमकालांस्तान्युक्तानाहुर्मनीषिणः
verses.transliteration:
apyupāyaistribhistāta yo'rthaḥ prāptuṁ na śakyate
tasya vikramakālāṁstānyuktānāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: The wise have asserted that an appeal to prowess should be resorted to anent a business then only when the end sought cannot be attained through the three (other) means. Prowess produce fruit only in respect of welladvised action directed while carefully watching (enemies) that are negligent, or captive, or under Divine affliction.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रमत्तं कथं तं तु विजिगीषुं बले स्थितम्
जितरोषं दुराधर्षं प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छथ
verses.transliteration:
apramattaṁ kathaṁ taṁ tu vijigīṣuṁ bale sthitam
jitaroṣaṁ durādharṣaṁ pradharṣayitumicchatha

translations.english: But why do you intend to discomfit (Rāma), who is vigilant, who desire victory, who is strong in the Divine strength, who has subdued passion, and who is hard to subdue?

verses.sanskrit:
बलान्यपरिमेयानि वीर्याणि च निशाचराः
परेषां सहसावज्ञा न कर्तव्या कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
balānyaparimeyāni vīryāṇi ca niśācarāḥ
pareṣāṁ sahasāvajñā na kartavyā kathaṁcana

translations.english: Who had in this world ever thought of or reasoned at ɔut Hanuman's career over the dreadful deep, the lord of streams and rivers? O rangers of the night, the strength and prowess (of the foe) being immeasurable, you should by no means recklessly disregard him.

verses.sanskrit:
किं च राक्षसराजस्य रामेणापकृतं पुरा
आजहार जनस्थानाद्यस्य भार्यां यशस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ ca rākṣasarājasya rāmeṇāpakṛtaṁ purā
ājahāra janasthānādyasya bhāryāṁ yaśasvinaḥ

translations.english: And what was the wrong that formerly had been done by Rāma to the king of the Rākşasas, that he has carried off from Janasthāna the spouse of that illustrious one?

verses.sanskrit:
खरो यद्यतिवृत्तस्तु रामेण निहतो रणे
अवश्यं प्राणिनां प्राणा रक्षितव्या यथा बलम्
verses.transliteration:
kharo yadyativṛttastu rāmeṇa nihato raṇe
avaśyaṁ prāṇināṁ prāṇā rakṣitavyā yathā balam

translations.english: If Khara, who had trespassed into regions not his own, has buen slain in battle by Rāma, surely a creature should to the best of his might preserve his life.

verses.sanskrit:
एतन्निमित्तं वैदेही भयं नः सुमहद्भवेत्
आहृता सा परित्याज्या कलहार्थे कृते न किम्
verses.transliteration:
etannimittaṁ vaidehī bhayaṁ naḥ sumahadbhavet
āhṛtā sā parityājyā kalahārthe kṛte na kim

translations.english: It is for this great fear that exercise us on the score of Vaidehi owing its existence to this,* that she, having been ravished, should (now) be given up. What is the use of acting so that quarrel may be the consequence? *The feeling of revenge for the slaughter of Khara and the rest.

verses.sanskrit:
न नः क्षमं वीर्यवता तेन धर्मानुवर्तिना
वैरं निरर्थकं कर्तुं दीयतामस्य मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
na naḥ kṣamaṁ vīryavatā tena dharmānuvartinā
vairaṁ nirarthakaṁ kartuṁ dīyatāmasya maithilī

translations.english: And (Rama), possessed of prowess, yet ever abiding by morality, is incapable of initiating hostilities for no purpose. Therefore, do you give him his Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
यावन्न सगजां साश्वां बहुरत्नसमाकुलाम्
पुरीं दारयते बाणैर्दीयतामस्य मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
yāvanna sagajāṁ sāśvāṁ bahuratnasamākulām
purīṁ dārayate bāṇairdīyatāmasya maithilī

translations.english: And before, he by means of his shafts rive this city together with her elephants and steeds, overflowing with countless gems, do you give him his Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्सुघोरा महती दुर्धर्षा हरिवाहिनी
नावस्कन्दति नो लङ्कां तावत्सीता प्रदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
yāvatsughorā mahatī durdharṣā harivāhinī
nāvaskandati no laṅkāṁ tāvatsītā pradīyatām

translations.english: And before the dreadful, irrepressible and mighty monkey-host block up this Lankā of ours, do you give (back) Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
विनश्येद्धि पुरी लङ्का शूराः सर्वे च राक्षसाः
रामस्य दयिता पत्नी न स्वयं यदि दीयते
verses.transliteration:
vinaśyeddhi purī laṅkā śūrāḥ sarve ca rākṣasāḥ
rāmasya dayitā patnī na svayaṁ yadi dīyate

translations.english: This city of Lankā shall perish as also all the heroic Rākṣasas, if you did not yourself make over Rāma's spouse to him.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादये त्वां बन्धुत्वात्कुरुष्व वचनं मम
हितं पथ्यं त्वहं ब्रूमि दीयतामस्य मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
prasādaye tvāṁ bandhutvātkuruṣva vacanaṁ mama
hitaṁ pathyaṁ tvahaṁ brūmi dīyatāmasya maithilī

translations.english: I exert myself to pleasure you, because of the fraternity (that subsist between us). Do what I say. I say what is truth and what also is for your good. Do you render (back) Rama's Maithili.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा शरत्सूर्यमरीचिसंनिभा;न्नवाग्रपुङ्खान्सुदृढान्नृपात्मजः
सृजत्यमोघान्विशिखान्वधाय ते; प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
purā śaratsūryamarīcisaṁnibhā;nnavāgrapuṅkhānsudṛḍhānnṛpātmajaḥ
sṛjatyamoghānviśikhānvadhāya te; pradīyatāṁ dāśarathāya maithilī

translations.english: Ere yet the king's son, for compassing your destruction, shower sure shafts resembling the rays of the autumnal Sun, having shining heads and feathered parts, and exceedingly hard, do you render Maithili to son of Daſaratha.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यजस्व कोपं सुखधर्मनाशनं; भजस्व धर्मं रतिकीर्तिवर्धनम्
प्रसीद जीवेम सपुत्रबान्धवाः; प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
tyajasva kopaṁ sukhadharmanāśanaṁ; bhajasva dharmaṁ ratikīrtivardhanam
prasīda jīvema saputrabāndhavāḥ; pradīyatāṁ dāśarathāya maithilī

translations.english: Forsake your wrath at once, which destroy happiness and virtue; and follow righteousness, which enhance enjoyment and fame. Be you propitious, so that we may live (at ease) along with our sons and relatives. Render (back) Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

verses.sanskrit:
सुनिविष्टं हितं वाक्यमुक्तवन्तं विभीषणम्
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं रावणः कालचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
suniviṣṭaṁ hitaṁ vākyamuktavantaṁ vibhīṣaṇam
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ

translations.english: Vibhīşaņa addressing him with these excellent and auspicious words, fraught with high sense, Rāvaņa, impelled by Death, again spoke in harsh accents.

verses.sanskrit:
वसेत्सह सपत्नेन क्रुद्धेनाशीविषेण वा
न तु मित्रप्रवादेन संवसेच्छत्रुसेविना
verses.transliteration:
vasetsaha sapatnena kruddhenāśīviṣeṇa vā
na tu mitrapravādena saṁvasecchatrusevinā

translations.english: It is better to live with open enemies or enraged serpents than with those who pass for friends but are in reality foes.

verses.sanskrit:
जानामि शीलं ज्ञातीनां सर्वलोकेषु राक्षस
हृष्यन्ति व्यसनेष्वेते ज्ञातीनां ज्ञातयः सदा
verses.transliteration:
jānāmi śīlaṁ jñātīnāṁ sarvalokeṣu rākṣasa
hṛṣyanti vyasaneṣvete jñātīnāṁ jñātayaḥ sadā

translations.english: I know well the nature of kinsmen, in all the worlds, O Raksasas, one takes delight in another's misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रधानं साधकं वैद्यं धर्मशीलं च राक्षस
ज्ञातयो ह्यवमन्यन्ते शूरं परिभवन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
pradhānaṁ sādhakaṁ vaidyaṁ dharmaśīlaṁ ca rākṣasa
jñātayo hyavamanyante śūraṁ paribhavanti ca

translations.english: The kinsmen, O Raksasa, generally disregard him who is their king, * protects the kingdom, educated and pious-and they always try to discomfit him, if he be a heroe. *On account of the priority of his birth,

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यमन्योन्यसंहृष्टा व्यसनेष्वाततायिनः
प्रच्छन्नहृदया घोरा ज्ञातयस्तु भयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
nityamanyonyasaṁhṛṣṭā vyasaneṣvātatāyinaḥ
pracchannahṛdayā ghorā jñātayastu bhayāvahāḥ

translations.english: These terrible enemies-the kinsmen, hypocrite as they are, always take delight in one another's calamity.

verses.sanskrit:
नाग्निर्नान्यानि शस्त्राणि न नः पाशा भयावहाः
घोराः स्वार्थप्रयुक्तास्तु ज्ञातयो नो भयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
nāgnirnānyāni śastrāṇi na naḥ pāśā bhayāvahāḥ
ghorāḥ svārthaprayuktāstu jñātayo no bhayāvahāḥ

translations.english: Hear, I shall relate what elephants, in yore, spoke beholding some persons with noose in hand-We do not fear, fire, weapons, or even the terrible noose-we fear only the dreadful kinsmen, blinded with selfishness.

verses.sanskrit:
उपायमेते वक्ष्यन्ति ग्रहणे नात्र संशयः
कृत्स्नाद्भयाज्ज्ञातिभयं सुकष्टं विदितं च नः
verses.transliteration:
upāyamete vakṣyanti grahaṇe nātra saṁśayaḥ
kṛtsnādbhayājjñātibhayaṁ sukaṣṭaṁ viditaṁ ca naḥ

translations.english: They alone unfold the means of our detection, there is not the least doubt about it. Fear from kinsmen is therefore known as the worst of all fears.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्यते गोषु संपन्नं विद्यते ब्राह्मणे दमः
विद्यते स्त्रीषु चापल्यं विद्यते ज्ञातितो भयम्
verses.transliteration:
vidyate goṣu saṁpannaṁ vidyate brāhmaṇe damaḥ
vidyate strīṣu cāpalyaṁ vidyate jñātito bhayam

translations.english: In kine there is milk, in kinsmen, there is fear, in women there is fickleness, and in Brahmanas, there is asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नेष्टमिदं सौम्य यदहं लोकसत्कृतः
ऐश्वर्यमभिजातश्च रिपूणां मूर्ध्नि च स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tato neṣṭamidaṁ saumya yadahaṁ lokasatkṛtaḥ
aiśvaryamabhijātaśca ripūṇāṁ mūrdhni ca sthitaḥ

translations.english: It does not please you, I fancy, O gentle one, that I am honoured of the three worlds, the lord of riches, and the subduer of my foes.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्यस्त्वेवंविधं ब्रूयाद्वाक्यमेतन्निशाचर
अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते न भवेत्त्वां तु धिक्कुलपांसनम्
verses.transliteration:
anyastvevaṁvidhaṁ brūyādvākyametanniśācara
asminmuhūrte na bhavettvāṁ tu dhikkulapāṁsanam

translations.english: Fie you, O night ranger, O you that bring disgrace on the family. Had any one else spoken thus he would have ceased to live by this time.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं न्यायवादी विभीषणः
उत्पपात गदापाणिश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ nyāyavādī vibhīṣaṇaḥ
utpapāta gadāpāṇiścaturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ

translations.english: Being thus accosted harshly, Vibhisana, speaking truth, rose up along with four Rākṣasas having maces in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च तदा वाक्यं जातक्रोधो विभीषणः
अन्तरिक्षगतः श्रीमान्भ्रातरं राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca tadā vākyaṁ jātakrodho vibhīṣaṇaḥ
antarikṣagataḥ śrīmānbhrātaraṁ rākṣasādhipam

translations.english: There upon, rising up in the welkin, the graceful brother Vibhisana, worked up with ire, addressed the lord of Rāshasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं भ्रातासि मे राजन्ब्रूहि मां यद्यदिच्छसि
इदं तु परुषं वाक्यं न क्षमाम्यनृतं तव
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ bhrātāsi me rājanbrūhi māṁ yadyadicchasi
idaṁ tu paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ na kṣamāmyanṛtaṁ tava

translations.english: You are mistaken, O king. Do you speak what you wish, you are my elder brother, adorable like to father-you did not follow the track of virtue. I cannot tolerate the harsh accents of you, my elder brother.

verses.sanskrit:
सुनीतं हितकामेन वाक्यमुक्तं दशानन
न गृह्णन्त्यकृतात्मानः कालस्य वशमागताः
verses.transliteration:
sunītaṁ hitakāmena vākyamuktaṁ daśānana
na gṛhṇantyakṛtātmānaḥ kālasya vaśamāgatāḥ

translations.english: For your welfare I spoke those w ell-meaning words, O Ten-necked one, but you did not pay heed to them being brought under the control of Death.

verses.sanskrit:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः
अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः
verses.transliteration:
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṁ priyavādinaḥ
apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ

translations.english: O king, many are the persons who speak sweet words. hit rare are they who can speak and near anpalatable but well-meaning words.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धं कालस्य पाशेन सर्वभूतापहारिणा
न नश्यन्तमुपेक्षेयं प्रदीप्तं शरणं यथा
verses.transliteration:
baddhaṁ kālasya pāśena sarvabhūtāpahāriṇā
na naśyantamupekṣeyaṁ pradīptaṁ śaraṇaṁ yathā

translations.english: How can I disregard your death like to a burning house bound as you are by the noose of Death, the destroyer of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
दीप्तपावकसंकाशैः शितैः काञ्चनभूषणैः
न त्वामिच्छाम्यहं द्रष्टुं रामेण निहतं शरैः
verses.transliteration:
dīptapāvakasaṁkāśaiḥ śitaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ
na tvāmicchāmyahaṁ draṣṭuṁ rāmeṇa nihataṁ śaraiḥ

translations.english: I do not wish to behold you slain by the well sharpened shafts of Rāma, feathered in gold and resembling the flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च कृतास्त्राश्च रणाजिरे
कालाभिपन्ना सीदन्ति यथा वालुकसेतवः
verses.transliteration:
śūrāśca balavantaśca kṛtāstrāśca raṇājire
kālābhipannā sīdanti yathā vālukasetavaḥ

translations.english: Even the heroic and powerful persons, well versed in the use of weapons, wear away like sands in battle, being attracted by Death.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीं चेमां सराक्षसाम्
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना
verses.transliteration:
ātmānaṁ sarvathā rakṣa purīṁ cemāṁ sarākṣasām
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sukhī bhava mayā vinā
