translations.english: You are worshipful to me, do you forgive me for what I have said for your welfare. Do you protect yourself and this city, abounding in Raksasas. May good betide you! I am going away and do you be happy without me.

verses.sanskrit:
निवार्यमाणस्य मया हितैषिणा; न रोचते ते वचनं निशाचर
परीतकाला हि गतायुषो नरा; हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्
verses.transliteration:
nivāryamāṇasya mayā hitaiṣiṇā; na rocate te vacanaṁ niśācara
parītakālā hi gatāyuṣo narā; hitaṁ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhirīritam

translations.english: What, I spoke to you, O ranger of the night, to prevent you, for your welfare, did not please you. Persons, whose lease of life is well-nigh expired, do not pay heed to the well-meaning words of their friends.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणं रावणानुजः
आजगाम मुहूर्तेन यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ rāvaṇaṁ rāvaṇānujaḥ
ājagāma muhūrtena yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Having addressed Rāvana with these harsh words, his younger brother, reached in no time, where Rāma along with Lakṣmaṇa was.

verses.sanskrit:
तं मेरुशिखराकारं दीप्तामिव शतह्रदाम्
गगनस्थं महीस्थास्ते ददृशुर्वानराधिपाः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ meruśikharākāraṁ dīptāmiva śatahradām
gaganasthaṁ mahīsthāste dadṛśurvānarādhipāḥ

translations.english: The leading monkeys, stationed on earth, espied him on the welkin, resembling in size the summit of the mount Meru, and burning like lightning in the effulgence of his own person.

verses.sanskrit:
तमात्मपञ्चमं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः
वानरैः सह दुर्धर्षश्चिन्तयामास बुद्धिमान्
verses.transliteration:
tamātmapañcamaṁ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
vānaraiḥ saha durdharṣaścintayāmāsa buddhimān

translations.english: Beholding him along with four counsellors, the highly intelligent Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, engaged in meditation along with them.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं तु वानरांस्तानुवाच ह
हनूमत्प्रमुखान्सर्वानिदं वचनमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
cintayitvā muhūrtaṁ tu vānarāṁstānuvāca ha
hanūmatpramukhānsarvānidaṁ vacanamuttamam

translations.english: And meditating for a while, he spoke to the monkeys headed by Hanuman the following excellent words.

verses.sanskrit:
एष सर्वायुधोपेतश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः
राक्षसोऽभ्येति पश्यध्वमस्मान्हन्तुं न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa sarvāyudhopetaścaturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
rākṣaso'bhyeti paśyadhvamasmānhantuṁ na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Behold, there comes a Rākşasa, armed with various weapons and followed by four demons to slay us and there is not the least doubt about it.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते वानरोत्तमाः
सालानुद्यम्य शैलांश्च इदं वचनमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānarottamāḥ
sālānudyamya śailāṁśca idaṁ vacanamabruvan

translations.english: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the excellent monkeys, taking up huge trees and crages, bespoke him.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रं व्यादिश नो राजन्वधायैषां दुरात्मनाम्
निपतन्तु हताश्चैते धरण्यामल्पजीविताः
verses.transliteration:
śīghraṁ vyādiśa no rājanvadhāyaiṣāṁ durātmanām
nipatantu hatāścaite dharaṇyāmalpajīvitāḥ

translations.english: Do you order us, O king, to destroy these vicious-souled demons. These shall crush them to death, limited as is the tenure of their life.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां संभाषमाणानामन्योन्यं स विभीषणः
उत्तरं तीरमासाद्य खस्थ एव व्यतिष्ठत
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ saṁbhāṣamāṇānāmanyonyaṁ sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
uttaraṁ tīramāsādya khastha eva vyatiṣṭhata

translations.english: They addressing each other in this wise, Vibhīşaņa descended from the sky on the northern shore.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच च महाप्राज्ञः स्वरेण महता महान्
सुग्रीवं तांश्च संप्रेक्ष्य खस्थ एव विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
uvāca ca mahāprājñaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān
sugrīvaṁ tāṁśca saṁprekṣya khastha eva vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: And beholdings Sugrīva and all others stationed near him, the highly intelligent Vibhīşaņa accosted them, at the highest pitch of his voice, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणो नाम दुर्वृत्तो राक्षसो राक्षसेश्वरः
तस्याहमनुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇo nāma durvṛtto rākṣaso rākṣaseśvaraḥ
tasyāhamanujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ

translations.english: There lives a Raksasa, named Ravana, the lord of demons, and perpetrator of many iniquitous deeds. I am his younger brother known as Vibhişaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन सीता जनस्थानाद्धृता हत्वा जटायुषम्
रुद्ध्वा च विवशा दीना राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
tena sītā janasthānāddhṛtā hatvā jaṭāyuṣam
ruddhvā ca vivaśā dīnā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā

translations.english: By him, slaying the vulture Jatayu, was carried away Sītā from Janasthana. She is imprisoned, brought under his sway, poorly, and being well guarded by the Rakşasees.

verses.sanskrit:
तमहं हेतुभिर्वाक्यैर्विविधैश्च न्यदर्शयम्
साधु निर्यात्यतां सीता रामायेति पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tamahaṁ hetubhirvākyairvividhaiśca nyadarśayam
sādhu niryātyatāṁ sītā rāmāyeti punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: With various well meaning words and reasonings I pointed out to him, the necessity of rendering back Sītā to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
स च न प्रतिजग्राह रावणः कालचोदितः
उच्यमानो हितं वाक्यं विपरीत इवौषधम्
verses.transliteration:
sa ca na pratijagrāha rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ
ucyamāno hitaṁ vākyaṁ viparīta ivauṣadham

translations.english: And Ravana, possessed by Death, paid no heed to my well-meaning words, like to one, lying on the brink of death, neglecting the administration of medicine.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं परुषितस्तेन दासवच्चावमानितः
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च राघवं शरणं गतः
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ paruṣitastena dāsavaccāvamānitaḥ
tyaktvā putrāṁśca dārāṁśca rāghavaṁ śaraṇaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Being reviled by him and treated harshly like a menial, I have come to seek Rāghava's shelter, renouncing my children and wives.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वलोकशरण्याय राघवाय महात्मने
निवेदयत मां क्षिप्रं विभीषणमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvalokaśaraṇyāya rāghavāya mahātmane
nivedayata māṁ kṣipraṁ vibhīṣaṇamupasthitam

translations.english: Do you soon mention to the high-souled Rāghava, the refuge of all creatures, that Vibhīşaņa has arrived.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो लघुविक्रमः
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो रामं संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
etattu vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvo laghuvikramaḥ
lakṣmaṇasyāgrato rāmaṁ saṁrabdhamidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing those words the quick-paced Sugrīva, excited with ire, spoke to Rāma, before Laksmana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्यानुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः
चतुर्भिः सह रक्षोभिर्भवन्तं शरणं गतः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasyānujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ
caturbhiḥ saha rakṣobhirbhavantaṁ śaraṇaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Ravana's younger brother, known Vibilisana, uc come here with four Raksasas, to seck your shelter.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेन प्रणिहितं तमवेहि विभीषणम्
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये क्षमं क्षमवतां वर
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇena praṇihitaṁ tamavehi vibhīṣaṇam
tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye kṣamaṁ kṣamavatāṁ vara

translations.english: O you the foremost of forgiving persons, I consider this Vibhīşaņa, who has been despatched by Ravana, worthy of being slain. as

verses.sanskrit:
बध्यतामेष तीव्रेण दण्डेन सचिवैः सह
रावणस्य नृशंसस्य भ्राता ह्येष विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
badhyatāmeṣa tīvreṇa daṇḍena sacivaiḥ saha
rāvaṇasya nṛśaṁsasya bhrātā hyeṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Being impelled by his wicked intention and commissioned by Rävaņa, this Rākşasa has come here and secretly by virtue of his illusive powers he shall slay you, O innocent one, when you shall place confidence in him.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं रामं संरब्धो वाहिनीपतिः
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं ततो मौनमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu taṁ rāmaṁ saṁrabdho vāhinīpatiḥ
vākyajño vākyakuśalaṁ tato maunamupāgamat

translations.english: Having thus accosted Rāma, skilled in the are of speech, that lord of the army, Sugriva, well versed in speech, became silent.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा रामो महाबलः
समीपस्थानुवाचेदं हनूमत्प्रमुखान्हरीन्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvasya tu tadvākyaṁ śrutvā rāmo mahābalaḥ
samīpasthānuvācedaṁ hanūmatpramukhānharīn

translations.english: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the mighty Rāma spoke to the monkeys, near him, headed by Hanumān, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यदुक्तं कपिराजेन रावणावरजं प्रति
वाक्यं हेतुमदत्यर्थं भवद्भिरपि तच्छ्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
yaduktaṁ kapirājena rāvaṇāvarajaṁ prati
vākyaṁ hetumadatyarthaṁ bhavadbhirapi tacchrutam

translations.english: You have all heard, the words well grounded in reason, the lord of monkeys has said, regarding Rāvana's younger brother.

verses.sanskrit:
सुहृदा ह्यर्थकृच्छेषु युक्तं बुद्धिमता सता
समर्थेनापि संदेष्टुं शाश्वतीं भूतिमिच्छता
verses.transliteration:
suhṛdā hyarthakṛccheṣu yuktaṁ buddhimatā satā
samarthenāpi saṁdeṣṭuṁ śāśvatīṁ bhūtimicchatā

translations.english: It behove him, who desires for perpetual wealth, and is intelligent and capable of giving sound counsels, to advise his friends in difficult matters.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं परिपृष्टास्ते स्वं स्वं मतमतन्द्रिताः
सोपचारं तदा राममूचुर्हितचिकीर्षवः
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ paripṛṣṭāste svaṁ svaṁ matamatandritāḥ
sopacāraṁ tadā rāmamūcurhitacikīrṣavaḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Rāma (to minister to him best counsels) all those monkeys, intent upon encompassing his well-being, gave out their respective opinions.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञातं नास्ति ते किंचित्त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव
आत्मानं पूजयन्राम पृच्छस्यस्मान्सुहृत्तया
verses.transliteration:
ajñātaṁ nāsti te kiṁcittriṣu lokeṣu rāghava
ātmānaṁ pūjayanrāma pṛcchasyasmānsuhṛttayā

translations.english: O Rāghava, there is nothing beyond your knowledge in the three worlds. It is only to show your respect towards us; O Răma, that you did accost us in this wise.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि सत्यव्रतः शूरो धार्मिको दृढविक्रमः
परीक्ष्य कारा स्मृतिमान्निसृष्टात्मा सुहृत्सु च
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi satyavrataḥ śūro dhārmiko dṛḍhavikramaḥ
parīkṣya kārā smṛtimānnisṛṣṭātmā suhṛtsu ca

translations.english: You are of truthful vows, heroic, pious, of firm prowess, discriminating, recollecting and having implicit confidence in your friends.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादेकैकशस्तावद्ब्रुवन्तु सचिवास्तव
हेतुतो मतिसंपन्नाः समर्थाश्च पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tasmādekaikaśastāvadbruvantu sacivāstava
hetuto matisaṁpannāḥ samarthāśca punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Let the intelligent and capable counsellors deliver their reasonable opinions to you.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्ते राघवायाथ मतिमानङ्गदोऽग्रतः
विभीषणपरीक्षार्थमुवाच वचनं हरिः
verses.transliteration:
ityukte rāghavāyātha matimānaṅgado'grataḥ
vibhīṣaṇaparīkṣārthamuvāca vacanaṁ hariḥ

translations.english: They speaking thus to Rāghava, the intelligent monkey Angada, spoke as follows for sounding the intention of Vibhīşaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रोः सकाशात्संप्राप्तः सर्वथा शङ्क्य एव हि
विश्वासयोग्यः सहसा न कर्तव्यो विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
śatroḥ sakāśātsaṁprāptaḥ sarvathā śaṅkya eva hi
viśvāsayogyaḥ sahasā na kartavyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: We should always suspect him since he has come from the side of our enemies, and should not, all on a sudden, place confidence in him.

verses.sanskrit:
छादयित्वात्मभावं हि चरन्ति शठबुद्धयः
प्रहरन्ति च रन्ध्रेषु सोऽनर्थः सुमहान्भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
chādayitvātmabhāvaṁ hi caranti śaṭhabuddhayaḥ
praharanti ca randhreṣu so'narthaḥ sumahānbhavet

translations.english: The wicked-minded always move about hiding their real self, and bring about peoples' calamity, taking advantage of their weak points. And great is the disaster thereof.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थानर्थौ विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायं भजेत ह
गुणतः संग्रहं कुर्याद्दोषतस्तु विसर्जयेत्
verses.transliteration:
arthānarthau viniścitya vyavasāyaṁ bhajeta ha
guṇataḥ saṁgrahaṁ kuryāddoṣatastu visarjayet

translations.english: It is always proper to engage in actions, considering what is right and what is wrong. Virtues should always be gathered and vices abondoned.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दोषो महांस्तस्मिंस्त्यज्यतामविशङ्कितम्
गुणान्वापि बहूञ्ज्ञात्वा संग्रहः क्रियतां नृप
verses.transliteration:
yadi doṣo mahāṁstasmiṁstyajyatāmaviśaṅkitam
guṇānvāpi bahūñjñātvā saṁgrahaḥ kriyatāṁ nṛpa

translations.english: Do you renounce him unhesitatingly, if did you find in him a source of a great calamity and do you embrace him if did you find him crowned with many virtues.

verses.sanskrit:
शरभस्त्वथ निश्चित्य सार्थं वचनमब्रवीत्
क्षिप्रमस्मिन्नरव्याघ्र चारः प्रतिविधीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
śarabhastvatha niścitya sārthaṁ vacanamabravīt
kṣipramasminnaravyāghra cāraḥ pratividhīyatām

translations.english: There upon followed Sarava with words fraught with high import, best of men, do you speedily despatch emissaries to sound Vibhis ana.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रणिधाय हि चारेण यथावत्सूक्ष्मबुद्धिना
परीक्ष्य च ततः कार्यो यथान्यायं परिग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
praṇidhāya hi cāreṇa yathāvatsūkṣmabuddhinā
parīkṣya ca tataḥ kāryo yathānyāyaṁ parigrahaḥ

translations.english: If did you, sounding him well through the instrumentality of sharp spies, find him friendly, do you win him over to your side.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवांस्त्वथ संप्रेक्ष्य शास्त्रबुद्ध्या विचक्षणः
वाक्यं विज्ञापयामास गुणवद्दोषवर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavāṁstvatha saṁprekṣya śāstrabuddhyā vicakṣaṇaḥ
vākyaṁ vijñāpayāmāsa guṇavaddoṣavarjitam

translations.english: There upon the wise Jāmbavān, arriving at conclusions by virtue of his knowledge of Šāstras, began with words, void of defects.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धवैराच्च पापाच्च राक्षसेन्द्राद्विभीषणः
अदेश काले संप्राप्तः सर्वथा शङ्क्यतामयम्
verses.transliteration:
baddhavairācca pāpācca rākṣasendrādvibhīṣaṇaḥ
adeśa kāle saṁprāptaḥ sarvathā śaṅkyatāmayam

translations.english: Surely does Vibhīşaņa come from the vicious lord of Räkşasas, dead set against us and has arrived at such a bad piace and in such a bad hour. We should always fear him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मैन्दस्तु संप्रेक्ष्य नयापनयकोविदः
वाक्यं वचनसंपन्नो बभाषे हेतुमत्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
tato maindastu saṁprekṣya nayāpanayakovidaḥ
vākyaṁ vacanasaṁpanno babhāṣe hetumattaram

translations.english: There upon followed Mainda, conversant with what is right and wrong, after due deliberation, with words pregnant with words pregnant with reason.

verses.sanskrit:
वचनं नाम तस्यैष रावणस्य विभीषणः
पृच्छ्यतां मधुरेणायं शनैर्नरवरेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
vacanaṁ nāma tasyaiṣa rāvaṇasya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
pṛcchyatāṁ madhureṇāyaṁ śanairnaravareśvara

translations.english: He is Rāvana's younger brother, by name Vibhīşana. Let the lord of men ask him every thing at first in sweet words.

verses.sanskrit:
भावमस्य तु विज्ञाय ततस्तत्त्वं करिष्यसि
यदि दृष्टो न दुष्टो वा बुद्धिपूर्वं नरर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
bhāvamasya tu vijñāya tatastattvaṁ kariṣyasi
yadi dṛṣṭo na duṣṭo vā buddhipūrvaṁ nararṣabha

translations.english: Do you first ascertain, O foremost of men, with what intention he has come evil or good and then settle what course to adopt.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ संस्कारसंपन्नो हनूमान्सचिवोत्तमः
उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमर्थवन्मधुरं लघु
verses.transliteration:
atha saṁskārasaṁpanno hanūmānsacivottamaḥ
uvāca vacanaṁ ślakṣṇamarthavanmadhuraṁ laghu

translations.english: There upon spoke Hanumān, the foremost of the counsellors and well versed in Šāstras, in accents sweet, glorious and fraught with a high value.

verses.sanskrit:
न भवन्तं मतिश्रेष्ठं समर्थं वदतां वरम्
अतिशाययितुं शक्तो बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
na bhavantaṁ matiśreṣṭhaṁ samarthaṁ vadatāṁ varam
atiśāyayituṁ śakto bṛhaspatirapi bruvan

translations.english: Even Brhaspati, (the lord of speech) cannot excel you, capaable,* gifted with the best of intellect and foremost of those skilled in the are of speech, as you are. *Capable to ascertain the truth of all Sastras.

verses.sanskrit:
न वादान्नापि संघर्षान्नाधिक्यान्न च कामतः
वक्ष्यामि वचनं राजन्यथार्थं रामगौरवात्
verses.transliteration:
na vādānnāpi saṁgharṣānnādhikyānna ca kāmataḥ
vakṣyāmi vacanaṁ rājanyathārthaṁ rāmagauravāt

translations.english: And what I know I speak, o king. I do so, in the interest of Rāma's work and not impelled by my skill in the are of speech, by the pride of being a counsellor, by the vanity of being gifted with a high intellect or by the desire of speaking for its own sake.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थानर्थनिमित्तं हि यदुक्तं सचिवैस्तव
तत्र दोषं प्रपश्यामि क्रिया न ह्युपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
arthānarthanimittaṁ hi yaduktaṁ sacivaistava
tatra doṣaṁ prapaśyāmi kriyā na hyupapadyate

translations.english: What your counsellors have said for ascertaining the good or evil intention of Vibhīş aņa appear to me as most defective and productive of no consequence whatever. It is impossible to sound him without any command.* *To command to relate for what he has come.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋते नियोगात्सामर्थ्यमवबोद्धुं न शक्यते
सहसा विनियोगो हि दोषवान्प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
ṛte niyogātsāmarthyamavaboddhuṁ na śakyate
sahasā viniyogo hi doṣavānpratibhāti me

translations.english: And even to command him now for the same appears to me as improper.

verses.sanskrit:
चारप्रणिहितं युक्तं यदुक्तं सचिवैस्तव
अर्थस्यासंभवात्तत्र कारणं नोपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
cārapraṇihitaṁ yuktaṁ yaduktaṁ sacivaistava
arthasyāsaṁbhavāttatra kāraṇaṁ nopapadyate

translations.english: And as regards the despatch of spies, anent what you have been advised by your ministers, I do not observe any utility.

verses.sanskrit:
अदेश काले संप्राप्त इत्ययं यद्विभीषणः
विवक्षा चात्र मेऽस्तीयं तां निबोध यथा मति
verses.transliteration:
adeśa kāle saṁprāpta ityayaṁ yadvibhīṣaṇaḥ
vivakṣā cātra me'stīyaṁ tāṁ nibodha yathā mati

translations.english: And what little I have thought of, I have something to say (regarding Jambaban's proposal) that Vibhīşaņa has arrived at such a bad place and in such an evil hour.

verses.sanskrit:
दौरात्म्यं रावणे दृष्ट्वा विक्रमं च तथा त्वयि
युक्तमागमनं तस्य सदृशं तस्य बुद्धितः
verses.transliteration:
daurātmyaṁ rāvaṇe dṛṣṭvā vikramaṁ ca tathā tvayi
yuktamāgamanaṁ tasya sadṛśaṁ tasya buddhitaḥ

translations.english: He has really come to a very good place and in a very good hour. And truly has he performed a becoming and sensille action by coming here after duly ascertaining that Rāvana is a vicious wight and you are a pious person-he is full of vices-you are gifted with many virtues-he is tyrannical and you are powerful.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञातरूपैः पुरुषैः स राजन्पृच्छ्यतामिति
यदुक्तमत्र मे प्रेक्षा काचिदस्ति समीक्षिता
verses.transliteration:
ajñātarūpaiḥ puruṣaiḥ sa rājanpṛcchyatāmiti
yaduktamatra me prekṣā kācidasti samīkṣitā

translations.english: And what they have said, O king, as regards sounding him through secret spies, appear to me as one requiring great wisdom.

verses.sanskrit:
पृच्छ्यमानो विशङ्केत सहसा बुद्धिमान्वचः
तत्र मित्रं प्रदुष्येत मिथ्यपृष्टं सुखागतम्
verses.transliteration:
pṛcchyamāno viśaṅketa sahasā buddhimānvacaḥ
tatra mitraṁ praduṣyeta mithyapṛṣṭaṁ sukhāgatam

translations.english: An intelligent man, when questioned by any suddenly, suspects many things. And if the newcomer be a friend and has come here for his own happiness, how greatly shall his mind be changed by such a course?

verses.sanskrit:
अशक्यः सहसा राजन्भावो वेत्तुं परस्य वै
अन्तः स्वभावैर्गीतैस्तैर्नैपुण्यं पश्यता भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
aśakyaḥ sahasā rājanbhāvo vettuṁ parasya vai
antaḥ svabhāvairgītaistairnaipuṇyaṁ paśyatā bhṛśam

translations.english: Besides by a sudden questioning it is impossible to ascertain the intention of a foreigner. Do you therefore yourself accost him and determine, by his voice, his secret motive.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वस्य ब्रुवतो जातु लक्ष्यते दुष्टभावता
प्रसन्नं वदनं चापि तस्मान्मे नास्ति संशयः
verses.transliteration:
na tvasya bruvato jātu lakṣyate duṣṭabhāvatā
prasannaṁ vadanaṁ cāpi tasmānme nāsti saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: I did not however mark anything of his wickedness while he spoke; rather I did observe signs of gladness on his countenance. So I do not suspect him.

verses.sanskrit:
अशङ्कितमतिः स्वस्थो न शठः परिसर्पति
न चास्य दुष्टा वाक्चापि तस्मान्नास्तीह संशयः
verses.transliteration:
aśaṅkitamatiḥ svastho na śaṭhaḥ parisarpati
na cāsya duṣṭā vākcāpi tasmānnāstīha saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: The wily can never come fearless and undisturbed. Nor were his words cunning. So I do not suspect him.

verses.sanskrit:
आकारश्छाद्यमानोऽपि न शक्यो विनिगूहितुम्
बलाद्धि विवृणोत्येव भावमन्तर्गतं नृणाम्
verses.transliteration:
ākāraśchādyamāno'pi na śakyo vinigūhitum
balāddhi vivṛṇotyeva bhāvamantargataṁ nṛṇām

translations.english: It is not very easy to hide one's real nature. It manifests itself by force.

verses.sanskrit:
देशकालोपपन्नं च कार्यं कार्यविदां वर
सफलं कुरुते क्षिप्रं प्रयोगेणाभिसंहितम्
verses.transliteration:
deśakālopapannaṁ ca kāryaṁ kāryavidāṁ vara
saphalaṁ kurute kṣipraṁ prayogeṇābhisaṁhitam

translations.english: So this action of Vibhīşana is not out of place or season. When accomplished it shall redound to his own interest.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्योगं तव संप्रेक्ष्य मिथ्यावृत्तं च रावणम्
वालिनश्च वधं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवं चाभिषेचितम्
verses.transliteration:
udyogaṁ tava saṁprekṣya mithyāvṛttaṁ ca rāvaṇam
vālinaśca vadhaṁ śrutvā sugrīvaṁ cābhiṣecitam

translations.english: Considering well your preparations for war and Ravana's vain conduct, hearing of Vah's destruction and Sugrīva's installation on the throne he has, impelled by his good sense, come here, desirous of gaining the kingdom. Taking these into account, it seems prudent to take him to our side.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाशक्ति मयोक्तं तु राक्षसस्यार्जवं प्रति
त्वं प्रमाणं तु शेषस्य श्रुत्वा बुद्धिमतां वर
verses.transliteration:
yathāśakti mayoktaṁ tu rākṣasasyārjavaṁ prati
tvaṁ pramāṇaṁ tu śeṣasya śrutvā buddhimatāṁ vara

translations.english: O you the foremost of the intelligent, I have spok thus considering him sincere. It now behove you to perform what you think proper.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ रामः प्रसन्नात्मा श्रुत्वा वायुसुतस्य ह
प्रत्यभाषत दुर्धर्षः श्रुतवानात्मनि स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
atha rāmaḥ prasannātmā śrutvā vāyusutasya ha
pratyabhāṣata durdharṣaḥ śrutavānātmani sthitam

translations.english: Hearing those words of the Wind-god's son, the irrepressible Rāma, conversant with all the Šāstras, replied, with words expressing his own opinion.

verses.sanskrit:
ममापि तु विवक्षास्ति काचित्प्रति विभीषणम्
श्रुतमिच्छामि तत्सर्वं भवद्भिः श्रेयसि स्थितैः
verses.transliteration:
mamāpi tu vivakṣāsti kācitprati vibhīṣaṇam
śrutamicchāmi tatsarvaṁ bhavadbhiḥ śreyasi sthitaiḥ

translations.english: I have also thought of some thing regarding Vibhisana. I wish you all, interested in my wellbeing, to hear that.

verses.sanskrit:
मित्रभावेन संप्राप्तं न त्यजेयं कथंचन
दोषो यद्यपि तस्य स्यात्सतामेतदगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
mitrabhāvena saṁprāptaṁ na tyajeyaṁ kathaṁcana
doṣo yadyapi tasya syātsatāmetadagarhitam

translations.english: (Vibhīşaņa) has come here as friend so I cannot forsake him by any means. And even if he has come with any evil intent it is not culpable for the pious to afford him shelter.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः
प्रत्यभाषत काकुत्स्थं सौहार्देनाभिचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
pratyabhāṣata kākutsthaṁ sauhārdenābhicoditaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of Rāma, Sugriva, the lords of those who go bounding, over-flowing with friendliness, bespake Kākutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
किमत्र चित्रं धर्मज्ञ लोकनाथशिखामणे
यत्त्वमार्यं प्रभाषेथाः सत्त्ववान्सपथे स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
kimatra citraṁ dharmajña lokanāthaśikhāmaṇe
yattvamāryaṁ prabhāṣethāḥ sattvavānsapathe sthitaḥ

translations.english: What wonder is there that you wouldst speak these auspicious words, O you the foremost of kings, conversant with morality, gifted with prowess and ever treading the pious track as you are.

verses.sanskrit:
मम चाप्यन्तरात्मायं शुद्धिं वेत्ति विभीषणम्
अनुमनाच्च भावाच्च सर्वतः सुपरीक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
mama cāpyantarātmāyaṁ śuddhiṁ vetti vibhīṣaṇam
anumanācca bhāvācca sarvataḥ suparīkṣitaḥ

translations.english: Truly does my inner self regard Vibhīşana as devoid of any wicked intention. He has been well sounded by signs and gestures.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्क्षिप्रं सहास्माभिस्तुल्यो भवतु राघव
विभीषणो महाप्राज्ञः सखित्वं चाभ्युपैतु नः
verses.transliteration:
tasmātkṣipraṁ sahāsmābhistulyo bhavatu rāghava
vibhīṣaṇo mahāprājñaḥ sakhitvaṁ cābhyupaitu naḥ

translations.english: And let the greatly wise Vibhīşaņa, O Rāghava, be placed on an equal footing with us and gain our friendship.

verses.sanskrit:
स सुग्रीवस्य तद्वाक्यं रामः श्रुत्वा विमृश्य च
ततः शुभतरं वाक्यमुवाच हरिपुंगवम्
verses.transliteration:
sa sugrīvasya tadvākyaṁ rāmaḥ śrutvā vimṛśya ca
tataḥ śubhataraṁ vākyamuvāca haripuṁgavam

translations.english: Hearing the words of Sugrīva, and weighing them, Rāma again addressed the foremost of monkeys with more reasonable accents.

verses.sanskrit:
सुदुष्टो वाप्यदुष्टो वा किमेष रजनीचरः
सूक्ष्ममप्यहितं कर्तुं ममाशक्तः कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
suduṣṭo vāpyaduṣṭo vā kimeṣa rajanīcaraḥ
sūkṣmamapyahitaṁ kartuṁ mamāśaktaḥ kathaṁcana

translations.english: Wicked or other wise, whatever this nightranger may be, he shall not be able to do me the least mischief.

verses.sanskrit:
पिशाचान्दानवान्यक्षान्पृथिव्यां चैव राक्षसान्
अङ्गुल्यग्रेण तान्हन्यामिच्छन्हरिगणेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
piśācāndānavānyakṣānpṛthivyāṁ caiva rākṣasān
aṅgulyagreṇa tānhanyāmicchanharigaṇeśvara

translations.english: Piśācas, Dānavas, Yakşas or all the Rākşasas on earth, I can slay them all, if I like, with the tips of my fingers, O you the lord of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रूयते हि कपोतेन शत्रुः शरणमागतः
अर्चितश्च यथान्यायं स्वैश्च मांसैर्निमन्त्रितः
verses.transliteration:
śrūyate hi kapotena śatruḥ śaraṇamāgataḥ
arcitaśca yathānyāyaṁ svaiśca māṁsairnimantritaḥ

translations.english: I have heard of a pigeon adoring and entertaining with its own flesh, an enemy who took its shelter.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि तं प्रतिजग्राह भार्या हर्तारमागतम्
कपोतो वानरश्रेष्ठ किं पुनर्मद्विधो जनः
verses.transliteration:
sa hi taṁ pratijagrāha bhāryā hartāramāgatam
kapoto vānaraśreṣṭha kiṁ punarmadvidho janaḥ

translations.english: While a pigeon received so friendly its enemy, the slayer of its mate, how can I then act otherwise, O foremost of the monkeys?

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषेः कण्वस्य पुत्रेण कण्डुना परमर्षिणा
शृणु गाथां पुरा गीतां धर्मिष्ठां सत्यवादिना
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣeḥ kaṇvasya putreṇa kaṇḍunā paramarṣiṇā
śṛṇu gāthāṁ purā gītāṁ dharmiṣṭhāṁ satyavādinā

translations.english: Do you hear, I shall relate, a sacred story, narrated by the great ascetic, the truthful Kandu, son of the ascetic Kanyā.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धाञ्जलिपुटं दीनं याचन्तं शरणागतम्
न हन्यादानृशंस्यार्थमपि शत्रुं परं पत
verses.transliteration:
baddhāñjalipuṭaṁ dīnaṁ yācantaṁ śaraṇāgatam
na hanyādānṛśaṁsyārthamapi śatruṁ paraṁ pata

translations.english: o slayer of foes, even a wicked-minded enemy, if he, with folded palms and a poor heart, crave for your shelter, should not be slain.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्तो वा यदि वा दृप्तः परेषां शरणं गतः
अरिः प्राणान्परित्यज्य रक्षितव्यः कृतात्मना
verses.transliteration:
ārto vā yadi vā dṛptaḥ pareṣāṁ śaraṇaṁ gataḥ
ariḥ prāṇānparityajya rakṣitavyaḥ kṛtātmanā

translations.english: If an enemy, proud or terrified, seek shelter in affright, he should be saved by a great man even at the risk of his own life.

verses.sanskrit:
स चेद्भयाद्वा मोहाद्वा कामाद्वापि न रक्षति
स्वया शक्त्या यथातत्त्वं तत्पापं लोकगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa cedbhayādvā mohādvā kāmādvāpi na rakṣati
svayā śaktyā yathātattvaṁ tatpāpaṁ lokagarhitam

translations.english: One, who from fear, ignorance or wilfully does not protect him who seek his shelter, perpetrate a mighty iniquity, blamed of all.

verses.sanskrit:
विनष्टः पश्यतस्तस्य रक्षिणः शरणागतः
आदाय सुकृतं तस्य सर्वं गच्छेदरक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
vinaṣṭaḥ paśyatastasya rakṣiṇaḥ śaraṇāgataḥ
ādāya sukṛtaṁ tasya sarvaṁ gacchedarakṣitaḥ

translations.english: When a person is slain before him whose shelter he has taken he take away all the virtues of his protector.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं दोषो महानत्र प्रपन्नानामरक्षणे
अस्वर्ग्यं चायशस्यं च बलवीर्यविनाशनम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ doṣo mahānatra prapannānāmarakṣaṇe
asvargyaṁ cāyaśasyaṁ ca balavīryavināśanam

translations.english: So great is the sin in not affording shelter to those who seek for it; it stands in the way of going to heaven, brings in calumny and destroys the strength and prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
करिष्यामि यथार्थं तु कण्डोर्वचनमुत्तमम्
धर्मिष्ठं च यशस्यं च स्वर्ग्यं स्यात्तु फलोदये
verses.transliteration:
kariṣyāmi yathārthaṁ tu kaṇḍorvacanamuttamam
dharmiṣṭhaṁ ca yaśasyaṁ ca svargyaṁ syāttu phalodaye

translations.english: I shall therefore follow the excellent words of Kaņdu-leading to piety, fame and the attainment of the abode of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद्व्रतं मम
verses.transliteration:
sakṛdeva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate
abhayaṁ sarvabhūtebhyo dadāmyetadvrataṁ mama

translations.english: I always declare 'no fear' to all creatures, whenever any, approaching me, says, 'I am thine' and seek my shelter. Even this is my pious observance.

verses.sanskrit:
आनयैनं हरिश्रेष्ठ दत्तमस्याभयं मया
विभीषणो वा सुग्रीव यदि वा रावणः स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
ānayainaṁ hariśreṣṭha dattamasyābhayaṁ mayā
vibhīṣaṇo vā sugrīva yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam

translations.english: O Sugrīva, O foremost of monkeys, do you soon bring him here, whether he be Rāvaņa or Vibhisana and I shall declare to him 'no fear'.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सुग्रीववचो निशम्य त;द्धरीश्वरेणाभिहितं नरेश्वरः
विभीषणेनाशु जगाम संगमं; पतत्रिराजेन यथा पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sugrīvavaco niśamya ta;ddharīśvareṇābhihitaṁ nareśvaraḥ
vibhīṣaṇenāśu jagāma saṁgamaṁ; patatrirājena yathā puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, the king of men (Rāma) made instantly friends with Vibhīşaņa, like to the conqueror of enemies' cities making friends with the king of birds.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवेणाभये दत्ते संनतो रावणानुजः
खात्पपातावनिं हृष्टो भक्तैरनुचरैः सह
verses.transliteration:
rāghaveṇābhaye datte saṁnato rāvaṇānujaḥ
khātpapātāvaniṁ hṛṣṭo bhaktairanucaraiḥ saha

translations.english: Rāghava thus declaring to him 'no fear' Ravana's younger brother, the greatly wise Vibhișana, bending low his head, cast his looks on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च तदा रामं वाक्यं तत्र विभीषणः
धर्मयुक्तं च युक्तं च साम्प्रतं संप्रहर्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca tadā rāmaṁ vākyaṁ tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ
dharmayuktaṁ ca yuktaṁ ca sāmprataṁ saṁpraharṣaṇam

translations.english: Descending from the welkin with his devoted attendants the virtuous-souled Vibhisana, delighted, bowed to Rāma. And thereupon touching his feet along with four Rākşasas, Vibhisana addressed Rama, with words, fraught with piety, befitting the occasion and conducing to pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
परित्यक्ता मया लङ्का मित्राणि च धनानि च
भवद्गतं मे राज्यं च जीवितं च सुखानि च
verses.transliteration:
parityaktā mayā laṅkā mitrāṇi ca dhanāni ca
bhavadgataṁ me rājyaṁ ca jīvitaṁ ca sukhāni ca

translations.english: I am Rāvana's younger brother and have been greatly insulted by him. I have therefore come to seek your shelter, the refuge of all creatures, abandoning Lanka and renouncing my friends and riches. My kingdom, life and happiness are all at your disposal.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां वधे साह्यं लङ्कायाश्च प्रधर्षणे
करिष्यामि यथाप्राणं प्रवेक्ष्यामि च वाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ vadhe sāhyaṁ laṅkāyāśca pradharṣaṇe
kariṣyāmi yathāprāṇaṁ pravekṣyāmi ca vāhinīm

translations.english: I shall lend you my might in slaying the Raksasas and devastating the city of Larkā, and shall be in the midst of Rāvana's army.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणं रामस्तु परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं प्रीतः समुद्राज्जलमानय
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇaṁ rāmastu pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam
abravīllakṣmaṇaṁ prītaḥ samudrājjalamānaya

translations.english: There upon, embracing Vibhīşaņa, who spoke thus, Rama, delighted, said to Laksmana, Omy brother, do you bring water from the ocean. Sprinkling the greatly wise Vibhișana, I shall make him at once the king of the Rākşasas, o confrere of honour; for I am greatly pleased with him.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिरभ्यषिञ्चद्विभीषणम्
मध्ये वानरमुख्यानां राजानं रामशासनात्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu saumitrirabhyaṣiñcadvibhīṣaṇam
madhye vānaramukhyānāṁ rājānaṁ rāmaśāsanāt

translations.english: Being thus addressed, Saumitri, at the command of the king, anointed Vibhișana and made him the king of the Räkşasas in the presence of the monkey host.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रसादं तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा सद्यः प्लवंगमाः
प्रचुक्रुशुर्महानादान्साधु साध्विति चाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prasādaṁ tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
pracukruśurmahānādānsādhu sādhviti cābruvan

translations.english: Beholding Rāma's kindness (towards Vibhīş ana), the monkeys eulogized the high-souled one, exclaiming “Excellent! Excellent!”

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च हनूमांश्च सुग्रीवश्च विभीषणम्
कथं सागरमक्षोभ्यं तराम वरुणालयम्
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca hanūmāṁśca sugrīvaśca vibhīṣaṇam
kathaṁ sāgaramakṣobhyaṁ tarāma varuṇālayam

translations.english: Thereupon, Hanumān and Sugrīva addressed Vibhisana, saying, Do you tell us how we shall cross over the main-the abode of Varuņa, along with the host of the highly powerful monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
उपायैरभिगच्छामो यथा नदनदीपतिम्
तराम तरसा सर्वे ससैन्या वरुणालयम्
verses.transliteration:
upāyairabhigacchāmo yathā nadanadīpatim
tarāma tarasā sarve sasainyā varuṇālayam

translations.english: Do you inform us of the means by which we may cross over, along with our army, the lord of rivers and streams-the abode of Varuna."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मज्ञः प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः
समुद्रं राघवो राजा शरणं गन्तुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu dharmajñaḥ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
samudraṁ rāghavo rājā śaraṇaṁ gantumarhati

translations.english: Being thus addressed, the virtuous-souled Vibhisana replied, "It behovth the king, Rāghava, to seek refuge from the Ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
खानितः सगरेणायमप्रमेयो महोदधिः
कर्तुमर्हति रामस्य ज्ञातेः कार्यं महोदधिः
verses.transliteration:
khānitaḥ sagareṇāyamaprameyo mahodadhiḥ
kartumarhati rāmasya jñāteḥ kāryaṁ mahodadhiḥ

translations.english: This measureless deep was dug out by (the king) Sagara.* And the great ocean shall surely help Rāma belonging to Sagara's race. *Sagara was a sovereign of Ayodhyā, belonging to the same family with Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विभीषणेनोक्ते राक्षसेन विपश्चिता
प्रकृत्या धर्मशीलस्य राघवस्याप्यरोचत
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vibhīṣaṇenokte rākṣasena vipaścitā
prakṛtyā dharmaśīlasya rāghavasyāpyarocata

translations.english: Being thus accosted by the wise Rākşasa, Vibhīşaņa. Sugrīva reached where Rāma with Laksmana was.

verses.sanskrit:
स लक्ष्मणं महातेजाः सुग्रीवं च हरीश्वरम्
सत्क्रियार्थं क्रियादक्षः स्मितपूर्वमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sa lakṣmaṇaṁ mahātejāḥ sugrīvaṁ ca harīśvaram
satkriyārthaṁ kriyādakṣaḥ smitapūrvamuvāca ha

translations.english: And those words pleased Răma, pious by nature. And the highly effulgent (hero) requested, smiling, the active Lakşmaņa and the monkey-chief Sugrīva to collect necessaries for his adoration.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवः पण्डितो नित्यं भवान्मन्त्रविचक्षणः
उभाभ्यां संप्रधार्यार्यं रोचते यत्तदुच्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvaḥ paṇḍito nityaṁ bhavānmantravicakṣaṇaḥ
ubhābhyāṁ saṁpradhāryāryaṁ rocate yattaducyatām

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, this counsel of Vibhīşaņa appear to me as most sound. Sugrīva is a ways greatly wise, and you are greatly proficient in counsel. Do you, holding a conference, intimate to me what you think becoming."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तौ तु तौ वीरावुभौ सुग्रीवलक्ष्मणौ
समुदाचार संयुक्तमिदं वचनमूचतुः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktau tu tau vīrāvubhau sugrīvalakṣmaṇau
samudācāra saṁyuktamidaṁ vacanamūcatuḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed, those two heroes-Lakşmaņa and Sugriva, spoke respectfully the following words fraught with propriety.

verses.sanskrit:
किमर्थं नो नरव्याघ्र न रोचिष्यति राघव
विभीषणेन यत्तूक्तमस्मिन्काले सुखावहम्
verses.transliteration:
kimarthaṁ no naravyāghra na rociṣyati rāghava
vibhīṣaṇena yattūktamasminkāle sukhāvaham

translations.english: Why shall not the well-meaning words of Vibhīşaņa expressed now, please us O Rāghava, O you best of men?

verses.sanskrit:
अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुं घोरेऽस्मिन्वरुणालये
लङ्का नासादितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
abaddhvā sāgare setuṁ ghore'sminvaruṇālaye
laṅkā nāsādituṁ śakyā sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: Without constructing a bridge over the deep, the terrible abode of Varuņa, even the celestials and their lord (India) cannot get at the city of Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्य शूरस्य यथार्थं क्रियतां वचः
अलं कालात्ययं कृत्वा समुद्रोऽयं नियुज्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇasya śūrasya yathārthaṁ kriyatāṁ vacaḥ
alaṁ kālātyayaṁ kṛtvā samudro'yaṁ niyujyatām

translations.english: Do you act on the genuine counsel of the heroic Vibhisana, and without losing time, do you engage the Ocean for this work, so that we may with our army proceed to the city protected by Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः कुशास्तीर्णे तीरे नदनदीपतेः
संविवेश तदा रामो वेद्यामिव हुताशनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ kuśāstīrṇe tīre nadanadīpateḥ
saṁviveśa tadā rāmo vedyāmiva hutāśanaḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed Räma reached the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, covered with Kusa, like to fire getting into the sacrificial dais.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रामस्य सुप्तस्य कुशास्तीर्णे महीतले
नियमादप्रमत्तस्य निशास्तिस्रोऽतिचक्रमुः
verses.transliteration:
tasya rāmasya suptasya kuśāstīrṇe mahītale
niyamādapramattasya niśāstisro'ticakramuḥ

translations.english: As Rāma slept on the earth on Kuśa spread over, without ever swerving from the rule, three nights passed away.

verses.sanskrit:
न च दर्शयते मन्दस्तदा रामस्य सागरः
प्रयतेनापि रामेण यथार्हमभिपूजितः
verses.transliteration:
na ca darśayate mandastadā rāmasya sāgaraḥ
prayatenāpi rāmeṇa yathārhamabhipūjitaḥ

translations.english: me. And while spending three nights, Rāma, learned in polity and attached to virtue, prayed to that lord of streams-the Ocean. Yet the wicked Ocean, albeit adored according to his deserts by Rāma with his mind concentrated, did not show himself.

verses.sanskrit:
समुद्रस्य ततः क्रुद्धो रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः
समीपस्थमुवाचेदं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
samudrasya tataḥ kruddho rāmo raktāntalocanaḥ
samīpasthamuvācedaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣmaṇam

translations.english: Thereat Răma grew enraged and had the corners of his eyes crimsoned; and he spank to Laksmana of auspicious marks, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता
असामर्थ्यं फलन्त्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः
verses.transliteration:
praśamaśca kṣamā caiva ārjavaṁ priyavāditā
asāmarthyaṁ phalantyete nirguṇeṣu satāṁ guṇāḥ

translations.english: Behold the hauteur of the Ocean in not presenting himself before Calmness, forbearance, candour, and soft speech-these virtues of the good are by the insolent taken for the effects of incompetency.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मप्रशंसिनं दुष्टं धृष्टं विपरिधावकम्
सर्वत्रोत्सृष्टदण्डं च लोकः सत्कुरुते नरम्
verses.transliteration:
ātmapraśaṁsinaṁ duṣṭaṁ dhṛṣṭaṁ viparidhāvakam
sarvatrotsṛṣṭadaṇḍaṁ ca lokaḥ satkurute naram

translations.english: The person' that is self-laudatory, wicked and badly-bold, publish his own praise and met out chastisement everywhere, is honoured in the world. 1. The word, however, is naram (ac.), man. 2. i.e. indiscriminately.

verses.sanskrit:
न साम्ना शक्यते कीर्तिर्न साम्ना शक्यते यशः
प्राप्तुं लक्ष्मण लोकेऽस्मिञ्जयो वा रणमूधनि
verses.transliteration:
na sāmnā śakyate kīrtirna sāmnā śakyate yaśaḥ
prāptuṁ lakṣmaṇa loke'smiñjayo vā raṇamūdhani

translations.english: By moderation one cannot attain celebrity, by moderation one cannot attain fame, and, O Lakşmaņa, in this world by moderation one cannot attain victory on the edge of battle.* *Ranamārdhani, 'The perilous edge of battle when it raged.'

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य मद्बाणनिर्भिन्नैर्मकरैर्मकरालयम्
निरुद्धतोयं सौमित्रे प्लवद्भिः पश्य सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
adya madbāṇanirbhinnairmakarairmakarālayam
niruddhatoyaṁ saumitre plavadbhiḥ paśya sarvataḥ

translations.english: See, O Sumitrā's son, the abode of Makaras, with his waters obstructed all around with Makaras destroyed by my shafts. O Laksmana, see the bodies here of serpents, and the huge on bodies of mighty fishes, and the trunks of elephants, torn by my arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
सशङ्खशुक्तिका जालं समीनमकरं शरैः
अद्य युद्धेन महता समुद्रं परिशोषये
verses.transliteration:
saśaṅkhaśuktikā jālaṁ samīnamakaraṁ śaraiḥ
adya yuddhena mahatā samudraṁ pariśoṣaye

translations.english: To day in terrible battle will I dry up the Ocean with conchs and oysters, and fishes and Makaras.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षमया हि समायुक्तं मामयं मकरालयः
असमर्थं विजानाति धिक्क्षमामीदृशे जने
verses.transliteration:
kṣamayā hi samāyuktaṁ māmayaṁ makarālayaḥ
asamarthaṁ vijānāti dhikkṣamāmīdṛśe jane

translations.english: This abode of Makaras take me, who is forbearing, to be incompetent. Fie forbearance towards such as he! In consequence of my moderation, Ocean show not his own form. O Saumitri, bring you my bow, my arrows resembling venomous snakes. I will dry up the Ocean, and the monkeys shall go over on foot.

verses.sanskrit:
वेलासु कृतमर्यादं सहसोर्मिसमाकुलम्
निर्मर्यादं करिष्यामि सायकैर्वरुणालयम्
verses.transliteration:
velāsu kṛtamaryādaṁ sahasormisamākulam
nirmaryādaṁ kariṣyāmi sāyakairvaruṇālayam

translations.english: Being angered, today, albeit incapable of being agitated, will I agitate the deep. And by means of my shafts will I make Varuna's abode, surging with a thousand billows and having his dignity maintained by his shores, overleep his continents. And I will agitate the deep harbouring numbers of mighty Dānavas.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा धनुष्पाणिः क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः
बभूव रामो दुर्धर्षो युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā dhanuṣpāṇiḥ krodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ
babhūva rāmo durdharṣo yugāntāgniriva jvalan

translations.english: Having spoken you, Rāma, equipped with his bow, with his eyes dilated in wrath, became exceedingly irrepressible, like to the flaming fire at the final dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
संपीड्य च धनुर्घोरं कम्पयित्वा शरैर्जगत्
मुमोच विशिखानुग्रान्वज्राणीव शतक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
saṁpīḍya ca dhanurghoraṁ kampayitvā śarairjagat
mumoca viśikhānugrānvajrāṇīva śatakratuḥ

translations.english: And straining his dreadful bow, making the earth shake, tremulously, he let fly fierce shafts like him of an hundred sacrifices hurling his thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
ते ज्वलन्तो महावेगास्तेजसा सायकोत्तमाः
प्रविशन्ति समुद्रस्य सलिलं त्रस्तपन्नगम्
verses.transliteration:
te jvalanto mahāvegāstejasā sāyakottamāḥ
praviśanti samudrasya salilaṁ trastapannagam

translations.english: Thereat, flaming up, those vehement choice shafts surcharged with energy, enter into the waters of the sea, with its serpents afflicted with fear.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वेगः समुद्रस्य सनक्रमकरो महान्
संबभूव महाघोरः समारुतरवस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tato vegaḥ samudrasya sanakramakaro mahān
saṁbabhūva mahāghoraḥ samārutaravastadā

translations.english: Then great and exceedingly dreadful was the motion of the sea, with fishes and Makaras, and with the roar of the winds (blowing there).

verses.sanskrit:
महोर्मिमालाविततः शङ्खशुक्तिसमाकुलः
सधूमपरिवृत्तोर्मिः सहसाभून्महोदधिः
verses.transliteration:
mahormimālāvitataḥ śaṅkhaśuktisamākulaḥ
sadhūmaparivṛttormiḥ sahasābhūnmahodadhiḥ

translations.english: On a sudden the mighty deep was heaving with mighty surges, with conchs scattered about, and a smoke (enveloped) the ocean; and the billows became visible on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यथिताः पन्नगाश्चासन्दीप्तास्या दीप्तलोचनाः
दानवाश्च महावीर्याः पातालतलवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
vyathitāḥ pannagāścāsandīptāsyā dīptalocanāḥ
dānavāśca mahāvīryāḥ pātālatalavāsinaḥ

translations.english: The serpents were distressed, with their faces flaming and their eyes aglow; as well as the Dānavas of terrific energy, and the dwellers of the nether spheres.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊर्मयः सिन्धुराजस्य सनक्रमकरास्तदा
विन्ध्यमन्दरसंकाशाः समुत्पेतुः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
ūrmayaḥ sindhurājasya sanakramakarāstadā
vindhyamandarasaṁkāśāḥ samutpetuḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Billows of the sovran Ocean, resembling Vindhya or Mandara, containing crocodiles and Makaras, sprang up by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
आघूर्णिततरङ्गौघः संभ्रान्तोरगराक्षसः
उद्वर्तित महाग्राहः संवृत्तः सलिलाशयः
verses.transliteration:
āghūrṇitataraṅgaughaḥ saṁbhrāntoragarākṣasaḥ
udvartita mahāgrāhaḥ saṁvṛttaḥ salilāśayaḥ

translations.english: Varuņa's abode had its surges whirling its serpents and Räkşasas seized with affright, and its ferocious aquatic animals borne all around; and it sent forth sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मध्यात्समुद्रस्य सागरः स्वयमुत्थितः
उदयन्हि महाशैलान्मेरोरिव दिवाकरः
पन्नगैः सह दीप्तास्यैः समुद्रः प्रत्यदृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
tato madhyātsamudrasya sāgaraḥ svayamutthitaḥ
udayanhi mahāśailānmeroriva divākaraḥ
pannagaiḥ saha dīptāsyaiḥ samudraḥ pratyadṛśyata

translations.english: Then from forth the mid-sea arose Ocean himself, even as the maker of day rise from the mighty ascending-hill, Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरः समतिक्रम्य पूर्वमामन्त्र्य वीर्यवान्
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं शरपाणिनम्
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraḥ samatikramya pūrvamāmantrya vīryavān
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṁ rāghavaṁ śarapāṇinam

translations.english: And approaching the arrow-showering Rāma, and greeting him fair, Ocean spoke to him with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च राघवः
स्वभावे सौम्य तिष्ठन्ति शाश्वतं मार्गमाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
pṛthivī vāyurākāśamāpo jyotiśca rāghavaḥ
svabhāve saumya tiṣṭhanti śāśvataṁ mārgamāśritāḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, earth, air, sky, water and light, these, O mild one, retaining their eternal course, maintain their (respective) nature.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्स्वभावो ममाप्येष यदगाधोऽहमप्लवः
विकारस्तु भवेद्राध एतत्ते प्रवदाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tatsvabhāvo mamāpyeṣa yadagādho'hamaplavaḥ
vikārastu bhavedrādha etatte pravadāmyaham

translations.english: Mine also is that nature whereby I am fathomless and incapable of being crossed. The reverse of this is the having a bottom. And for this reason I speak to you (concerning the means).

verses.sanskrit:
न कामान्न च लोभाद्वा न भयात्पार्थिवात्मज
ग्राहनक्राकुलजलं स्तम्भयेयं कथंचन
verses.transliteration:
na kāmānna ca lobhādvā na bhayātpārthivātmaja
grāhanakrākulajalaṁ stambhayeyaṁ kathaṁcana

translations.english: O king's son, not from desire, covetousness, or fear, or anger, can I anywise deprive my waters abounding in alligators of their (perpetual) motion.

verses.sanskrit:
विधास्ये राम येनापि विषहिष्ये ह्यहं तथा
ग्राहा न प्रहरिष्यन्ति यावत्सेना तरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vidhāsye rāma yenāpi viṣahiṣye hyahaṁ tathā
grāhā na prahariṣyanti yāvatsenā tariṣyati

translations.english: I will tell you how you will pass (over me); or and I will bear it. And no ferocious aquatic animals shall do wrong so long as your forces have not crossed. And, O Rāma, I will make as it were firm land for the crossing over of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
एष सेतुं महोत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः
तमहं धारयिष्यामि तथा ह्येष यथा पिता
verses.transliteration:
eṣa setuṁ mahotsāhaḥ karotu mayi vānaraḥ
tamahaṁ dhārayiṣyāmi tathā hyeṣa yathā pitā

translations.english: O mild one, this one is named Nala, son to Viśvakarmā. He has received a boon from his sire. Visvakarma's son is well pleased with you. Let this monkey, surcharged with exhuberant spirits, build a bridge over me. I will hold that up. This one is as his sire.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वोदधिर्नष्टः समुत्थाय नलस्ततः
अब्रवीद्वानरश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं रामं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvodadhirnaṣṭaḥ samutthāya nalastataḥ
abravīdvānaraśreṣṭho vākyaṁ rāmaṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Having delivered himself thus, Ocean disappeared. Then that foremost of monkeys, Nala, arising, spoke to the mighty Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं सेतुं करिष्यामि विस्तीर्णे वरुणालये
पितुः सामर्थ्यमास्थाय तत्त्वमाह महोदधिः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ setuṁ kariṣyāmi vistīrṇe varuṇālaye
pituḥ sāmarthyamāsthāya tattvamāha mahodadhiḥ

translations.english: Resorting to my sire's skill, I will build a bridge over the spacious abode of Makaras. The mighty Ocean has spoken justly.

verses.sanskrit:
मम मातुर्वरो दत्तो मन्दरे विश्वकर्मणा
औरसस्तस्य पुत्रोऽहं सदृशो विश्वकर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
mama māturvaro datto mandare viśvakarmaṇā
aurasastasya putro'haṁ sadṛśo viśvakarmaṇā

translations.english: (Formerly) in Mandara, Visvakarma had conferred a boon on my mother: 'O exalted one, your son shall be like me.

verses.sanskrit:
न चाप्यहमनुक्तो वै प्रब्रूयामात्मनो गुणान्
काममद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुंगवाः
verses.transliteration:
na cāpyahamanukto vai prabrūyāmātmano guṇān
kāmamadyaiva badhnantu setuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ

translations.english: I also am capable of constructing a bridge over Varuna's abode. Therefore this very day let the foremost monkeys construct the bridge.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो निसृष्टरामेण सर्वतो हरियूथपाः
अभिपेतुर्महारण्यं हृष्टाः शतसहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tato nisṛṣṭarāmeṇa sarvato hariyūthapāḥ
abhipeturmahāraṇyaṁ hṛṣṭāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Then directed by Rāma, the principal monkeys with alacrity entered the mighty forest in hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
ते नगान्नगसंकाशाः शाखामृगगणर्षभाः
बभञ्जुर्वानरास्तत्र प्रचकर्षुश्च सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
te nagānnagasaṁkāśāḥ śākhāmṛgagaṇarṣabhāḥ
babhañjurvānarāstatra pracakarṣuśca sāgaram

translations.english: Themselves resembling mountains, the foremost of the monkeys began to break down trees and draw them towards the Ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
बिल्वकैः सप्तपर्णैश्च कर्णिकारैश्च पुष्पितैः
चूतैश्चाशोकवृक्षैश्च सागरं समपूरयन्
verses.transliteration:
bilvakaiḥ saptaparṇaiśca karṇikāraiśca puṣpitaiḥ
cūtaiścāśokavṛkṣaiśca sāgaraṁ samapūrayan

translations.english: The monkeys filled the Ocean with Sālas, and Ašvakarņas, dhavas, bamboo's and kutajas, arjunas, palms, tilakas, tinicas, billakas, saptaparnas, and blossoming karnikāras, mangoes, and asoka trees.

verses.sanskrit:
समूलांश्च विमूलांश्च पादपान्हरिसत्तमाः
इन्द्रकेतूनिवोद्यम्य प्रजह्रुर्हरयस्तरून्
verses.transliteration:
samūlāṁśca vimūlāṁśca pādapānharisattamāḥ
indraketūnivodyamya prajahrurharayastarūn

translations.english: And those monkeys the foremost of their species-began to gather the trees, some with their roots, and some without them, carrying them like Indra's ensign.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रक्षिप्यमाणैरचलैः सहसा जलमुद्धतम्
समुत्पतितमाकाशमपासर्पत्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
prakṣipyamāṇairacalaiḥ sahasā jalamuddhatam
samutpatitamākāśamapāsarpattatastataḥ

translations.english: And on rocks being plunged into the waters, the latter, suddenly swelling up, mounted to the welkin, and again subsided.

verses.sanskrit:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्
नलश्चक्रे महासेतुं मध्ये नदनदीपतेः
verses.transliteration:
daśayojanavistīrṇaṁ śatayojanamāyatam
nalaścakre mahāsetuṁ madhye nadanadīpateḥ

translations.english: And (the trees) dropping (into the deep), vexed it all around. And some took lines (for insuring straightness to the bridge). And at the middle of the lord of rivers and streams, Nala made a grand bridge measuring an hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
शिलानां क्षिप्यमाणानां शैलानां तत्र पात्यताम्
बभूव तुमुलः शब्दस्तदा तस्मिन्महोदधौ
verses.transliteration:
śilānāṁ kṣipyamāṇānāṁ śailānāṁ tatra pātyatām
babhūva tumulaḥ śabdastadā tasminmahodadhau

translations.english: And tremendous was the tumult that arose of crags thrown and rocks toppled down into the mighty deep.

verses.sanskrit:
स नलेन कृतः सेतुः सागरे मकरालये
शुशुभे सुभगः श्रीमान्स्वातीपथ इवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
sa nalena kṛtaḥ setuḥ sāgare makarālaye
śuśubhe subhagaḥ śrīmānsvātīpatha ivāmbare

translations.english: That bridge built by force over the abode of makaras, looked graceful and splendid like the Milky way in the firmament.

verses.sanskrit: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
verses.transliteration: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ

translations.english: Then the deities and Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the prime saints, appearing in the heavens, stood there, eager to behold this wonder.

verses.sanskrit:
आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः
तमचिन्त्यमसह्यं च अद्भुतं लोमहर्षणम्
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि सागरे सेतुबन्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
āplavantaḥ plavantaśca garjantaśca plavaṁgamāḥ
tamacintyamasahyaṁ ca adbhutaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni sāgare setubandhanam

translations.english: The monkeys, leaping and bounding and roaring, as well as all creatures, beheld that building of the bridge the ocean, on inconceivable, and marvellous, displaying skill past thought and capable of making one's hair stand on end.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि कोटिसहस्राणि वानराणां महौजसाम्
बध्नन्तः सागरे सेतुं जग्मुः पारं महोदधेः
verses.transliteration:
tāni koṭisahasrāṇi vānarāṇāṁ mahaujasām
badhnantaḥ sāgare setuṁ jagmuḥ pāraṁ mahodadheḥ

translations.english: And those thousands of Koțis of exceeding vigour, having constructed the bridge over the ocean, went over to the other shore of the mighty main.

verses.sanskrit:
विशालः सुकृतः श्रीमान्सुभूमिः सुसमाहितः
अशोभत महासेतुः सीमन्त इव सागरे
verses.transliteration:
viśālaḥ sukṛtaḥ śrīmānsubhūmiḥ susamāhitaḥ
aśobhata mahāsetuḥ sīmanta iva sāgare

translations.english: And spacious, skilfully constructed, graceful, well-paved and nicely finished, the great bridge appeared like the line where the hair has been parted on the Ocean's head.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परे समुद्रस्य गदापाणिर्विभीषणः
परेषामभिघतार्थमतिष्ठत्सचिवैः सह
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pare samudrasya gadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ
pareṣāmabhighatārthamatiṣṭhatsacivaiḥ saha

translations.english: Then on the other shore of the ocean, Bibhisbana with the view of opposing foes (that might advance), stationed himself mace in hand, along with some councilors.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रतस्तस्य सैन्यस्य श्रीमान्रामः सलक्ष्मणः
जगाम धन्वी धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण समन्वितः
verses.transliteration:
agratastasya sainyasya śrīmānrāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
jagāma dhanvī dharmātmā sugrīveṇa samanvitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat the graceful and righteous Rāma along with Laksmana, equipped with his bow, set out in the van of the army in company with Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ये मध्येन गच्छन्ति पार्श्वतोऽन्ये प्लवंगमाः
सलिले प्रपतन्त्यन्ये मार्गमन्ये न लेभिरे
केचिद्वैहायस गताः सुपर्णा इव पुप्लुवुः
verses.transliteration:
anye madhyena gacchanti pārśvato'nye plavaṁgamāḥ
salile prapatantyanye mārgamanye na lebhire
kecidvaihāyasa gatāḥ suparṇā iva pupluvuḥ

translations.english: And some monkeys proceeded along the middle, and some plunged into the deep, and some went by the road. And some coursed through the air, bounding up bird-like.

verses.sanskrit:
घोषेण महता घोषं सागरस्य समुच्छ्रितम्
भीममन्तर्दधे भीमा तरन्ती हरिवाहिनी
verses.transliteration:
ghoṣeṇa mahatā ghoṣaṁ sāgarasya samucchritam
bhīmamantardadhe bhīmā tarantī harivāhinī

translations.english: That dreadful array of monkeys crossing over, with its mighty uproar drowned the dreadful roar of the deep, which had been arising.

verses.sanskrit:
वानराणां हि सा तीर्णा वाहिनी नल सेतुना
तीरे निविविशे राज्ञा बहुमूलफलोदके
verses.transliteration:
vānarāṇāṁ hi sā tīrṇā vāhinī nala setunā
tīre niviviśe rājñā bahumūlaphalodake

translations.english: On the monkey-host having crossed by the bridge of Nala, the king stationed it on the shore abounding in fruits, roots, and water.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्भुतं राघव कर्म दुष्करं; समीक्ष्य देवाः सह सिद्धचारणैः
उपेत्य रामं सहिता महर्षिभिः; समभ्यषिञ्चन्सुशुभैर्जलैः पृथक्
verses.transliteration:
tadadbhutaṁ rāghava karma duṣkaraṁ; samīkṣya devāḥ saha siddhacāraṇaiḥ
upetya rāmaṁ sahitā maharṣibhiḥ; samabhyaṣiñcansuśubhairjalaiḥ pṛthak

translations.english: Beholding that work of Rāghava incapable of being performed the deities together with the Siddhas and Caranas, and the Maharsis, suddenly presenting themselves before Rāma, sprinkled him one by one with sacred water, and said.

verses.sanskrit:
जयस्व शत्रून्नरदेव मेदिनीं; ससागरां पालय शाश्वतीः समाः
इतीव रामं नरदेवसत्कृतं; शुभैर्वचोभिर्विविधैरपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
jayasva śatrūnnaradeva medinīṁ; sasāgarāṁ pālaya śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
itīva rāmaṁ naradevasatkṛtaṁ; śubhairvacobhirvividhairapūjayan

translations.english: May you be victorious, O human-divine one! Rule you the Earth eternally! Thus in various auspicious words, did they pay homage to that one honoured by the Brāhmanas, Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
सबले सागरं तीर्णे रामे दशरथात्मजे
अमात्यौ रावणः श्रीमानब्रवीच्छुकसारणौ
verses.transliteration:
sabale sāgaraṁ tīrṇe rāme daśarathātmaje
amātyau rāvaṇaḥ śrīmānabravīcchukasāraṇau

translations.english: On Dasaratha's son, Rama, having crossed the Ocean with his forces, the graceful Răvaņa addressed his two counsellors, Suka and Sarana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
समग्रं सागरं तीर्णं दुस्तरं वानरं बलम्
अभूतपूर्वं रामेण सागरे सेतुबन्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
samagraṁ sāgaraṁ tīrṇaṁ dustaraṁ vānaraṁ balam
abhūtapūrvaṁ rāmeṇa sāgare setubandhanam

translations.english: The crossing the entire ocean incapable of being crossed, by the monkey-forces, and the building over the sea of the bridge by Rāma, all this had never happened before.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरे सेतुबन्धं तु न श्रद्दध्यां कथंचन
अवश्यं चापि संख्येयं तन्मया वानरं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
sāgare setubandhaṁ tu na śraddadhyāṁ kathaṁcana
avaśyaṁ cāpi saṁkhyeyaṁ tanmayā vānaraṁ balam

translations.english: The construction of a bridge over the ocean cannot at all command credence. But (however it be), I must enumerate the monkey-hosts.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टौ राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ
हरिरूपधरौ वीरौ प्रविष्टौ वानरं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
iti pratisamādiṣṭau rākṣasau śukasāraṇau
harirūpadharau vīrau praviṣṭau vānaraṁ balam

translations.english: Being thus commissioned, these heroes, the Raksasas, Suka and Sarana, assuming monkeyshapes, entered into the hosts of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्वानरं सैन्यमचिन्त्यं लोमहर्षणम्
संख्यातुं नाध्यगच्छेतां तदा तौ शुकसारणौ
verses.transliteration:
tatastadvānaraṁ sainyamacintyaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
saṁkhyātuṁ nādhyagacchetāṁ tadā tau śukasāraṇau

translations.english: But Suka and Sāraṇa could not number that army of monkeys, incomprehensible and capable of making people's hair stand on end.

verses.sanskrit:
तरमाणं च तीर्णं च तर्तुकामं च सर्वशः
निविष्टं निविशच्चैव भीमनादं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
taramāṇaṁ ca tīrṇaṁ ca tartukāmaṁ ca sarvaśaḥ
niviṣṭaṁ niviśaccaiva bhīmanādaṁ mahābalam

translations.english: The forces were on mountain-tops, by fountains and in caves. And those rangers of the night beheld those forces, some having already crossed, and some crossing, and some intent on doing so, and some having sat down and some sitting that mighty army sending terrific roars, that ocean of hosts incapable of being disturbed.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ ददर्श महातेजाः प्रच्छन्नौ च विभीषणः
आचचक्षेऽथ रामाय गृहीत्वा शुकसारणौ
लङ्कायाः समनुप्राप्तौ चारौ परपुरंजयौ
verses.transliteration:
tau dadarśa mahātejāḥ pracchannau ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
ācacakṣe'tha rāmāya gṛhītvā śukasāraṇau
laṅkāyāḥ samanuprāptau cārau parapuraṁjayau

translations.english: As they remained thus disguised, they were discovered by Vibhisana. Thereat, taking them captive, he unfolded (the fact) to Rama, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ दृष्ट्वा व्यथितौ रामं निराशौ जीविते तदा
कृताञ्जलिपुटौ भीतौ वचनं चेदमूचतुः
verses.transliteration:
tau dṛṣṭvā vyathitau rāmaṁ nirāśau jīvite tadā
kṛtāñjalipuṭau bhītau vacanaṁ cedamūcatuḥ

translations.english: Seeing Ráma, they were greatly afflicted, and, despairing of their lives and exercised with fear, with joined hands, said.

verses.sanskrit:
आवामिहागतौ सौम्य रावणप्रहितावुभौ
परिज्ञातुं बलं कृत्स्नं तवेदं रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
āvāmihāgatau saumya rāvaṇaprahitāvubhau
parijñātuṁ balaṁ kṛtsnaṁ tavedaṁ raghunandana

translations.english: O placid one, commanded by Ravana, we have come here, O son of Raghu, for the purpose of gathering information concerning this army.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथात्मजः
अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्वाक्यं सर्वभूतहिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
tayostadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
abravītprahasanvākyaṁ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ

translations.english: Hearing their speech, Rāma, son to Dasaratha, ever engaged in the welfare of all beings, laughing, remarked.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दृष्टं बलं कृत्स्नं वयं वा सुसमीक्षिताः
यथोक्तं वा कृतं कार्यं छन्दतः प्रतिगम्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
yadi dṛṣṭaṁ balaṁ kṛtsnaṁ vayaṁ vā susamīkṣitāḥ
yathoktaṁ vā kṛtaṁ kāryaṁ chandataḥ pratigamyatām

translations.english: If you have heedfully noted this entire array, or if you have done what you had been commanded to do, return in peace.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविश्य नगरीं लङ्कां भवद्भ्यां धनदानुजः
वक्तव्यो रक्षसां राजा यथोक्तं वचनं मम
verses.transliteration:
praviśya nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ bhavadbhyāṁ dhanadānujaḥ
vaktavyo rakṣasāṁ rājā yathoktaṁ vacanaṁ mama

translations.english: Entering the extensive Lankā, you should say to the king-younger brother to the Dispenser of riches-the words which I utter.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्बलं च समाश्रित्य सीतां मे हृतवानसि
तद्दर्शय यथाकामं ससैन्यः सहबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
yadbalaṁ ca samāśritya sītāṁ me hṛtavānasi
taddarśaya yathākāmaṁ sasainyaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ

translations.english: That force relying on which you have carried away my Sita, do you as you wish, along with your forces and friends, display the same.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वःकाले नगरीं लङ्कां सप्राकारां सतोरणाम्
राक्षसं च बलं पश्य शरैर्विध्वंसितं मया
verses.transliteration:
śvaḥkāle nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ saprākārāṁ satoraṇām
rākṣasaṁ ca balaṁ paśya śarairvidhvaṁsitaṁ mayā

translations.english: On the morning of the morrow behold the city of Larikā with her wall and gates, as well as the hosts of Räkşasas, destroyed by me with my shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरं रोषमहं मोक्ष्ये बलं धारय रावण
श्वःकाले वज्रवान्वज्रं दानवेष्विव वासवः
verses.transliteration:
ghoraṁ roṣamahaṁ mokṣye balaṁ dhāraya rāvaṇa
śvaḥkāle vajravānvajraṁ dānaveṣviva vāsavaḥ

translations.english: As Väsava equipped with the thunder-bolt hurled the same amidst the Dänavas, will I, O Rāvana, on the morning of the morrow pour down my dreadful ire upon you along with your forces.

verses.sanskrit:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टौ राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ
आगम्य नगरीं लङ्कामब्रूतां राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.transliteration:
iti pratisamādiṣṭau rākṣasau śukasāraṇau
āgamya nagarīṁ laṅkāmabrūtāṁ rākṣasādhipam

translations.english: Thus directed (by Rama), those Raksasas, Śuka and Säraņa, having saluted the righteous Raghava with 'Victory!,' came (back) to Lanka and spoke to the lord of Rākşasas, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणगृहीतौ तु वधार्हौ राक्षसेश्वर
दृष्ट्वा धर्मात्मना मुक्तौ रामेणामिततेजसा
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇagṛhītau tu vadhārhau rākṣaseśvara
dṛṣṭvā dharmātmanā muktau rāmeṇāmitatejasā

translations.english: O lord of Rākşasas, having been taken by Vibhīşaņa for the purpose of being slain, we came to be seen by the righteous-souled Rāma of immeasurable energy, and (finally) were liberated (by him).

verses.sanskrit:
एते शक्ताः पुरीं लङ्कां सप्राकारां सतोरणाम्
उत्पाट्य संक्रामयितुं सर्वे तिष्ठन्तु वानराः
verses.transliteration:
ete śaktāḥ purīṁ laṅkāṁ saprākārāṁ satoraṇām
utpāṭya saṁkrāmayituṁ sarve tiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ

translations.english: As these four persons have combined—like to the Lokapālas, heroic, accomplished in arms, and of steady prowess-viz., Dasaratha's son, Rama, the graceful Laksmana, Vibhisana, and the highly powerful Sugrīva, resembling the great Indra, these are capable of uprooting the city of Larkā—walls and gateways-and replacing her (on her former site), leave you the monkeys aside.

verses.sanskrit:
यादृशं तस्य रामस्य रूपं प्रहरणानि च
वधिष्यति पुरीं लङ्कामेकस्तिष्ठन्तु ते त्रयः
verses.transliteration:
yādṛśaṁ tasya rāmasya rūpaṁ praharaṇāni ca
vadhiṣyati purīṁ laṅkāmekastiṣṭhantu te trayaḥ

translations.english: Such is Rāma's figure and arms that he shall alone demolish Lankā, leave the other three alone.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणगुप्ता सा सुग्रीवेण च वाहिनी
बभूव दुर्धर्षतरा सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇaguptā sā sugrīveṇa ca vāhinī
babhūva durdharṣatarā sarvairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: That host protected by Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Sugrīva, shall become exceedingly hard to combat even by the Asuras and gods.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टरूपा ध्वजिनी वनौकसां; महात्मनां संप्रति योद्धुमिच्छताम्
अलं विरोधेन शमो विधीयतां; प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭarūpā dhvajinī vanaukasāṁ; mahātmanāṁ saṁprati yoddhumicchatām
alaṁ virodhena śamo vidhīyatāṁ; pradīyatāṁ dāśarathāya maithilī

translations.english: The army of the high-souled rangers of the woods, eager for encounter, contains warriors bursting with high spirits. No use of dispute. Be you intent on pacification. Do you render back Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वचः पथ्यमक्लीबं सारणेनाभिभाषितम्
निशम्य रावणो राजा प्रत्यभाषत सारणम्
verses.transliteration:
tadvacaḥ pathyamaklībaṁ sāraṇenābhibhāṣitam
niśamya rāvaṇo rājā pratyabhāṣata sāraṇam

translations.english: Hearing Sarana's words, pregnant and truthful, king Ravana addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मामभियुञ्जीरन्देवगन्धर्वदानवाः
नैव सीतां प्रदास्यामि सर्वलोकभयादपि
verses.transliteration:
yadi māmabhiyuñjīrandevagandharvadānavāḥ
naiva sītāṁ pradāsyāmi sarvalokabhayādapi

translations.english: Even if the gods, Gandharvas and Dänavas should attack me, Sītā will I not part with from fear of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं तु सौम्य परित्रस्तो हरिभिर्निर्जितो भृशम्
प्रतिप्रदानमद्यैव सीतायाः साधु मन्यसे
को हि नाम सपत्नो मां समरे जेतुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ tu saumya paritrasto haribhirnirjito bhṛśam
pratipradānamadyaiva sītāyāḥ sādhu manyase
ko hi nāma sapatno māṁ samare jetumarhati

translations.english: O amiable one, you, having been hard handled by the monkeys and distressed in consequence, deems it fit that Sītā should be rendered back this very day. What foe of mine is there who is competent to conquer me in battle?

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
आरुरोह ततः श्रीमान्प्रासादं हिमपाण्डुरम्
बहुतालसमुत्सेधं रावणोऽथ दिदृक्षया
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
āruroha tataḥ śrīmānprāsādaṁ himapāṇḍuram
bahutālasamutsedhaṁ rāvaṇo'tha didṛkṣayā

translations.english: Having uttered this rough speech, the graceful Ravana-lord of the Raksasas, desirous of surveying (the monkey-hosts), ascended an edifice white like snow, and elevated like many palms (placed one upon another).

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यां चराभ्यां सहितो रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः
पश्यमानः समुद्रं च पर्वतांश्च वनानि च
ददर्श पृथिवीदेशं सुसंपूर्णं प्लवंगमैः
verses.transliteration:
tābhyāṁ carābhyāṁ sahito rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
paśyamānaḥ samudraṁ ca parvatāṁśca vanāni ca
dadarśa pṛthivīdeśaṁ susaṁpūrṇaṁ plavaṁgamaiḥ

translations.english: And transported with passion, Răvaņa in company with those spies, saw the sea, mountains and forests. And they beheld the Earth enveloped with monkeys, and the mighty host of monkeys, boundless and irresistible. And having seen this, king Ravana asked Sarana. Who among these monkeys are the foremost, who are the heroes, and who possessed of great strength?

verses.sanskrit:
केषां शृणोति सुग्रीवः के वा यूथपयूथपाः
सारणाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं के प्रधानाः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
keṣāṁ śṛṇoti sugrīvaḥ ke vā yūthapayūthapāḥ
sāraṇācakṣva me sarvaṁ ke pradhānāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Who, bursting with spirits, stay all about the fore? Whom does Sugriva listen to? And who are the leaders of the monkey-leader? O Sarana, relate you all this to me. And what is the prowess of the monkeys?

verses.sanskrit:
सारणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचनं परिपृच्छतः
आचचक्षेऽथ मुख्यज्ञो मुख्यांस्तांस्तु वनौकसः
verses.transliteration:
sāraṇo rākṣasendrasya vacanaṁ paripṛcchataḥ
ācacakṣe'tha mukhyajño mukhyāṁstāṁstu vanaukasaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, Sarana knowing the chiefs (of the monkey-army), spoke to the sovereign of Raksasas, who had asked (him), as to who were the heads of the rangers of the woods.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वशाखामृगेन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
बलाग्रे तिष्ठते वीरो नीलो नामैष यूथपः
verses.transliteration:
sarvaśākhāmṛgendrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
balāgre tiṣṭhate vīro nīlo nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ

translations.english: This monkey, that, setting up roars, stay in front of Lankā, surrounded by hundreds and thousands of monkey-leaders, by whose tremendous shouts Laúkā tremble with her wall, gateways, hills, woods and forests, and who is posted in front of the forces of the high-souled Sugriva, master of all the monkeys-is the heroic leader of monkey-bands named Nila.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य लाङ्गूलशब्देन स्वनन्तीव दिशो दश
एष वानरराजेन सुर्ग्रीवेणाभिषेचितः
यौवराज्येऽङ्गदो नाम त्वामाह्वयति संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
yasya lāṅgūlaśabdena svanantīva diśo daśa
eṣa vānararājena surgrīveṇābhiṣecitaḥ
yauvarājye'ṅgado nāma tvāmāhvayati saṁyuge

translations.english: That one, possessed of prowess, who, folding up his arms, pace the gound on foot, who, facing Lankā, from wrath is frequently yawning, who resembles a mountain-peak and is like the filaments of a lotus, who, enraged again and again, sound his tail, and the ten cardinal points resound with the sounds of whose tail, is he who has been sprinkled by Sugrīva-king of monkeys, the heir apparent, named Angada. He challenge you to the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तु विष्टभ्य गात्राणि क्ष्वेडयन्ति नदन्ति च
उत्थाय च विजृम्भन्ते क्रोधेन हरिपुंगवाः
verses.transliteration:
ye tu viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi kṣveḍayanti nadanti ca
utthāya ca vijṛmbhante krodhena haripuṁgavāḥ

translations.english: Those that with their limbs lying inactive, and setting up roars and ululation's, are following this one,' are heroes dwelling in Candana.? *The reference is prospective. It means the monkeys, Sveta, in the next slok.

verses.sanskrit:
तूर्णं सुग्रीवमागम्य पुनर्गच्छति वानरः
विभजन्वानरीं सेनामनीकानि प्रहर्षयन्
verses.transliteration:
tūrṇaṁ sugrīvamāgamya punargacchati vānaraḥ
vibhajanvānarīṁ senāmanīkāni praharṣayan

translations.english: With his own army alone, the silver-hued Śveta of dreadful prowess hopes to subdue Lanka. Marshalling his monkey-forces and cheering up his soldiers, that intelligent monkey, famed over the three regions, having speedily met with Sugrīva, is retracting his steps.

verses.sanskrit:
यः पुरा गोमतीतीरे रम्यं पर्येति पर्वतम्
नाम्ना संकोचनो नाम नानानगयुतो गिरिः
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ purā gomatītīre ramyaṁ paryeti parvatam
nāmnā saṁkocano nāma nānānagayuto giriḥ

translations.english: From days of yore on the banks of the Gomatī there is a mountain, (named) Ramya, (otherwise) called Sanrocana. The mount abounds with various trees. There that leader of bands, named Kumuda, governs his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य वाला बहुव्यामा दीर्घलाङ्गूलमाश्रिताः
ताम्राः पीताः सिताः श्वेताः प्रकीर्णा घोरकर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
yasya vālā bahuvyāmā dīrghalāṅgūlamāśritāḥ
tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ

translations.english: He that cheerfully draws after him hundreds and thousands of monkeys, and the long grim hairs of whose tail, coppery, yellow, sable and white, are cast about, is the energetic monkey, Canda, eager for encounter. And he hopes to conquer Laňkā by help of his own forces.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु भीमां प्रवल्गन्तीं चमूं तिष्ठति शोभयन्
स्थितां तीरे समुद्रस्य द्वितीय इव सागरः
verses.transliteration:
yastu bhīmāṁ pravalgantīṁ camūṁ tiṣṭhati śobhayan
sthitāṁ tīre samudrasya dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ

translations.english: He that stay gracing the dreadful array overflowing with talk, stationed on the shore of the ocean, resembling a second sea and like to Durdara*-is the leader named Vinată. And he range, drinking of the waters of) the Veņa, best among streams-and his forces are sixty lacs of monkeys. *Name os a celebrated monkeys-leader.

verses.sanskrit:
षष्टिः शतसहस्राणि बलमस्य प्लवंगमाः
त्वामाह्वयति युद्धाय क्रथनो नाम यूथपः
verses.transliteration:
ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi balamasya plavaṁgamāḥ
tvāmāhvayati yuddhāya krathano nāma yūthapaḥ

translations.english: The monkey, named Krathana, challenges you to conflict. He has (under him) powerful and vigorous generals, and forces well divided.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु गैरिकवर्णाभं वपुः पुष्यति वानरः
गवयो नाम तेजस्वी त्वां क्रोधादभिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
yastu gairikavarṇābhaṁ vapuḥ puṣyati vānaraḥ
gavayo nāma tejasvī tvāṁ krodhādabhivartate

translations.english: The monkey owning that person of the hue of red chalk, and, who, elated with strength, disregard all the monkeys, is named Gavaya, who approach you wrathfully. Seventy lacs (of troops) girt him round; and by their means he hopes to bring down Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
एते दुष्प्रसहा घोरा बलिनः कामरूपिणः
यूथपा यूथपश्रेष्ठा येषां संख्या न विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
ete duṣprasahā ghorā balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
yūthapā yūthapaśreṣṭhā yeṣāṁ saṁkhyā na vidyate

translations.english: These are the heroes, incapable of being borne, whose numbers cannot be enumerated. These are the leaders and the heads thereof, as well as the forces set in order of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्तु तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रेक्षमाणस्य यूथपान्
राघवार्थे पराक्रान्ता ये न रक्षन्ति जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstu te'haṁ pravakṣyāmi prekṣamāṇasya yūthapān
rāghavārthe parākrāntā ye na rakṣanti jīvitam

translations.english: As you look on, I shall describe to you those leaders who shall put forth their prowess for Rāghava, and lay down their lives in his behalf.)

verses.sanskrit:
यवीयानस्य तु भ्राता पश्यैनं पर्वतोपमम्
भ्रात्रा समानो रूपेण विशिष्टस्तु पराक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
yavīyānasya tu bhrātā paśyainaṁ parvatopamam
bhrātrā samāno rūpeṇa viśiṣṭastu parākrame

translations.english: Behold this one resembling a hill-younger brother of Dhūmra, lord of all the bears. He is equal to this brother in beauty, and of superior prowess. This leader of redoubtable leaders is named Jämbavān. He is mild, obedient to his superiors and fierce in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन साह्यं सुमहत्कृतं शक्रस्य धीमता
देवासुरे जाम्बवता लब्धाश्च बहवो वराः
verses.transliteration:
etena sāhyaṁ sumahatkṛtaṁ śakrasya dhīmatā
devāsure jāmbavatā labdhāśca bahavo varāḥ

translations.english: The intelligent Jāmbavan assisted Sakra signally in the war of the gods and Asuras, and he has won many boons (in consequence).

verses.sanskrit:
आरुह्य पर्वताग्रेभ्यो महाभ्रविपुलाः शिलाः
मुञ्चन्ति विपुलाकारा न मृत्योरुद्विजन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
āruhya parvatāgrebhyo mahābhravipulāḥ śilāḥ
muñcanti vipulākārā na mṛtyorudvijanti ca

translations.english: Ascending the tops of mountains, these hurl down gigantic crags huge as colossal clouds, for does (the fear of)-death (ever) disquiet them. And their bodies covered with hair, they resemble Raksasas and ghosts (in their conduct).

verses.sanskrit:
यं त्वेनमभिसंरब्धं प्लवमानमिव स्थितम्
प्रेक्षन्ते वानराः सर्वे स्थितं यूथपयूथपम्
verses.transliteration:
yaṁ tvenamabhisaṁrabdhaṁ plavamānamiva sthitam
prekṣante vānarāḥ sarve sthitaṁ yūthapayūthapam

translations.english: This one one of immeasurable energy has innumerable troops going about, who behold this leader of leaders under unusual excitement leaping and resting (by turns). This lord of monkeys dwell near the thousand-eyed Deity; and this leader of hands, gifted with strength, is named Rambha.

verses.sanskrit:
यः स्थितं योजने शैलं गच्छन्पार्श्वेन सेवते
ऊर्ध्वं तथैव कायेन गतः प्राप्नोति योजनम्
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ sthitaṁ yojane śailaṁ gacchanpārśvena sevate
ūrdhvaṁ tathaiva kāyena gataḥ prāpnoti yojanam

translations.english: He that going touch with his side a mountain situated at the distance of a Yojana, and, rising up, measurə the same length, and whose beauty is surpassed by none among quadrupeds, is known under the name of Sannādana, the grand father of the monkeys; this intelligent one battlºd did he meet with discomfiture. This is that general of the forces. *There is a word, rane, in battle-in this line, left out on the ground of pleonasm.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेऽसितमुखा घोरा गोलाङ्गूला महाबलाः
शतं शतसहस्राणि दृष्ट्वा वै सेतुबन्धनम्
verses.transliteration:
ete'sitamukhā ghorā golāṅgūlā mahābalāḥ
śataṁ śatasahasrāṇi dṛṣṭvā vai setubandhanam

translations.english: These wondrous strong and dreadful Golāngülas* numbering hundreds and hundred thousands, seeing the building of the bridge, surrounding, O mighty monarch, the leader named Gavākṣa—a Golāngūla-set up shouts, intending to demolish Lankā with their prowess. *Vide anti.

verses.sanskrit:
षष्टिर्गिरिसहस्राणां रम्याः काञ्चनपर्वताः
तेषां मध्ये गिरिवरस्त्वमिवानघ रक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
ṣaṣṭirgirisahasrāṇāṁ ramyāḥ kāñcanaparvatāḥ
teṣāṁ madhye girivarastvamivānagha rakṣasām

translations.english: There are sixty thousand charming Golden hills. In their midst is that best of mountains,* even as you, O sinless one, are among the Raksasa. *Savarni Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
एष चैषामधिपतिर्मध्ये तिष्ठति वीर्यवान्
नाम्ना पृथिव्यां विख्यातो राजञ्शतबलीति यः
एषैवाशंसते लङ्कां स्वेनानीकेन मर्दितुम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa caiṣāmadhipatirmadhye tiṣṭhati vīryavān
nāmnā pṛthivyāṁ vikhyāto rājañśatabalīti yaḥ
eṣaivāśaṁsate laṅkāṁ svenānīkena marditum

translations.english: This powerful one staying in their midst, is their leader, eager for victory; and the puissant (monkey) always look like the Sun himself; and this one, o king, is famed on earth by the name of Satabalr.

verses.sanskrit:
गजो गवाक्षो गवयो नलो नीलश्च वानरः
एकैक एव यूथानां कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः
verses.transliteration:
gajo gavākṣo gavayo nalo nīlaśca vānaraḥ
ekaika eva yūthānāṁ koṭibhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ

translations.english: Gaya, Gavākşa, Nala, and the monkey Nīlaeach of these is encompassed by ten koțis of warriors.

verses.sanskrit:
तथान्ये वानरश्रेष्ठा विन्ध्यपर्वतवासिनः
न शक्यन्ते बहुत्वात्तु संख्यातुं लघुविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
tathānye vānaraśreṣṭhā vindhyaparvatavāsinaḥ
na śakyante bahutvāttu saṁkhyātuṁ laghuvikramāḥ

translations.english: (Besides these), there are other choice monkeys dwelling in the Vindhya mountain, but I cannot enumerate these (monkeys) possessed of fleet vigour, in consequence of their vast number.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे महाराज महाप्रभावाः; सर्वे महाशैलनिकाशकायाः
सर्वे समर्थाः पृथिवीं क्षणेन; कर्तुं प्रविध्वस्तविकीर्णशैलाम्
verses.transliteration:
sarve mahārāja mahāprabhāvāḥ; sarve mahāśailanikāśakāyāḥ
sarve samarthāḥ pṛthivīṁ kṣaṇena; kartuṁ pravidhvastavikīrṇaśailām

translations.english: All these, O mighty monarch, are of exceeding prowess, all possess persons resembling mighty mountains; and all are competent in a moment to remove and scatter the Earth with them.

verses.sanskrit:
सारणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
बलमालोकयन्सर्वं शुको वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sāraṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇaṁ rākṣasādhipam
balamālokayansarvaṁ śuko vākyamathābravīt

translations.english: Having heard the words of Säraņa, who had described the forces (of the monkeys), Suka, addressed Rāvana, lord of Rākşasas, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थितान्पश्यसि यानेतान्मत्तानिव महाद्विपान्
न्यग्रोधानिव गाङ्गेयान्सालान्हैमवतीनिव
verses.transliteration:
sthitānpaśyasi yānetānmattāniva mahādvipān
nyagrodhāniva gāṅgeyānsālānhaimavatīniva
