translations.english: Those, o king, whom you see stationed, resembling mad elephants, like to nyagrodhas* belonging to the Gangă, like to Sālas in the Himavān, are incapable of being borne, they are possessed of strength, and able to wear forms at will; resembling deities and Dänavas, and like the gods in conflict. *Banians.

verses.sanskrit:
एते सुग्रीवसचिवाः किष्किन्धानिलयाः सदा
हरयो देवगन्धर्वैरुत्पन्नाः कामरूपिणः
verses.transliteration:
ete sugrīvasacivāḥ kiṣkindhānilayāḥ sadā
harayo devagandharvairutpannāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ

translations.english: These, numbering nine, five, and seven thousand koțis and thousand sankus and an hundred urindas, are the ministers of Sugriva, residing in Kişkindhā-monkeys begot by gods and Gandharvas, capable of assuming shapes at will.

verses.sanskrit:
यौ तौ पश्यसि तिष्ठन्तौ कुमारौ देवरूपिणौ
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ ताभ्यां नास्ति समो युधि
verses.transliteration:
yau tau paśyasi tiṣṭhantau kumārau devarūpiṇau
maindaśca dvividaścobhau tābhyāṁ nāsti samo yudhi

translations.english: Those two whom you beholdest, staying there, of equal proportions and endowed with god-like shapes, are Mainda and Dvivida, who have no equals in fight. Permitted by Brahma, they had partaken of ambrosia. They hope to humble Lanka by their prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठः केसरिणः पुत्रो वातात्मज इति श्रुतः
हनूमानिति विख्यातो लङ्घितो येन सागरः
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhaḥ kesariṇaḥ putro vātātmaja iti śrutaḥ
hanūmāniti vikhyāto laṅghito yena sāgaraḥ

translations.english: He whom you seseestaying like a mad elephant, the monkey who, being enraged, can by his strength agitate the deep itself, who, searching for Vaidehi, had presented himself before you, lord, behold this monkey come again!-whom you had seen before!*—is the eldest son of Kacari, known as the offspring of the Wind-god-celebrated as Hanumān, who had bounded over the deep. *This dislocation occurs in the original. These descriptions generally are hardly amenable to a sound syntax.

verses.sanskrit:
कामरूपी हरिश्रेष्ठो बलरूपसमन्वितः
अनिवार्यगतिश्चैव यथा सततगः प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
kāmarūpī hariśreṣṭho balarūpasamanvitaḥ
anivāryagatiścaiva yathā satatagaḥ prabhuḥ

translations.english: Capable of wearing forms at pleasure, that first of monkeys is endued with grace and strength, and is of irresistible impetuosity even as that lord, the Wind.

verses.sanskrit:
आदित्यमाहरिष्यामि न मे क्षुत्प्रतियास्यति
इति संचिन्त्य मनसा पुरैष बलदर्पितः
verses.transliteration:
ādityamāhariṣyāmi na me kṣutpratiyāsyati
iti saṁcintya manasā puraiṣa baladarpitaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the Sun risen, (he) while a boy, resolving in his mind, Coursing a way measuring three thousand Yojanas, I will bring the Sun, my hunger is not appeased; and he sprang up, elated with strength.

verses.sanskrit:
अनाधृष्यतमं देवमपि देवर्षिदानवैः
अनासाद्यैव पतितो भास्करोदयने गिरौ
verses.transliteration:
anādhṛṣyatamaṁ devamapi devarṣidānavaiḥ
anāsādyaiva patito bhāskarodayane girau

translations.english: And, not getting that god, incapable of being subdued by the deities, saints and Rākṣasas, he dropped down on the Ascending-hill. And thereat a jaw of that strong jawed one was little fractured on the rock, and he is called Hanuman in consequence.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यमागमयोगेन ममैष विदितो हरिः
नास्य शक्यं बलं रूपं प्रभावो वानुभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
satyamāgamayogena mamaiṣa vidito hariḥ
nāsya śakyaṁ balaṁ rūpaṁ prabhāvo vānubhāṣitum

translations.english: I know this monkey and all his previous history. I cannot describe his strength, beauty or prowess. And this one alone hopes to lay Lankā low by his energy And why do you today forget the monkey, who had flung flaming fire into Lankā?

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु सव्यमसौ पक्षं रामस्याश्रित्य तिष्ठति
रक्षोगणपरिक्षिप्तो राजा ह्येष विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
yastu savyamasau pakṣaṁ rāmasyāśritya tiṣṭhati
rakṣogaṇaparikṣipto rājā hyeṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: He that stay occupying the left side of Rāma, and surrounded by Raksasas, is the king, Vibhīșana, sprinkled as the king of Lankā by the auspicious king of kings, he, filled with wrath, approach you (for battle).

verses.sanskrit:
एतां च मालां तारां च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्
सुग्रीवो वालिनं हत्वा रामेण प्रतिपादितः
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ ca mālāṁ tārāṁ ca kapirājyaṁ ca śāśvatam
sugrīvo vālinaṁ hatvā rāmeṇa pratipāditaḥ

translations.english: Rāma, having slain Vālī, has conferred this garland, Tārā, and the eternal monkey-kingdom on Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां महाराजसमीक्ष्य वाहिनी;मुपस्थितां प्रज्वलितग्रहोपमाम्
ततः प्रयत्नः परमो विधीयतां; यथा जयः स्यान्न परैः पराजयः
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ mahārājasamīkṣya vāhinī;mupasthitāṁ prajvalitagrahopamām
tataḥ prayatnaḥ paramo vidhīyatāṁ; yathā jayaḥ syānna paraiḥ parājayaḥ

translations.english: Observing this host, that has presented itself, resembling a flaming planet, do you, O might monarch, prepare yourself to the uttermost, so that victory may be your, and that you may not come by discomfiture at the hands of the foe.

verses.sanskrit:
अधोमुखौ तौ प्रणतावब्रवीच्छुकसारणौ
रोषगद्गदया वाचा संरब्धः परुषं वचः
verses.transliteration:
adhomukhau tau praṇatāvabravīcchukasāraṇau
roṣagadgadayā vācā saṁrabdhaḥ paruṣaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And he wrathfully spoke to them, standing in humble guise with their heads hung down, harsh words faltering with passion.

verses.sanskrit:
न तावत्सदृशं नाम सचिवैरुपजीविभिः
विप्रियं नृपतेर्वक्तुं निग्रहप्रग्रहे विभोः
verses.transliteration:
na tāvatsadṛśaṁ nāma sacivairupajīvibhiḥ
vipriyaṁ nṛpatervaktuṁ nigrahapragrahe vibhoḥ

translations.english: That counsellors subsisting (on the wealth of their master and sovereign), should say aught disagreeable to him, whether they meet with his favour or disfavour-is not meet.

verses.sanskrit:
आचार्या गुरवो वृद्धा वृथा वां पर्युपासिताः
सारं यद्राजशास्त्राणामनुजीव्यं न गृह्यते
verses.transliteration:
ācāryā guravo vṛddhā vṛthā vāṁ paryupāsitāḥ
sāraṁ yadrājaśāstrāṇāmanujīvyaṁ na gṛhyate

translations.english: Without being questioned, it is (proper) for you both to hymn the praises of a foes that is opposed and that has advanced for encounter! You have in vain worshipped your preceptors, aged people, and spiritual guides, for you have failed to appropriate the cream of Political Science, which should be availed of.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतो वा न विज्ञातो भारो ज्ञानस्य वोछ्यते
ईदृशैः सचिवैर्युक्तो मूर्खैर्दिष्ट्या धराम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhīto vā na vijñāto bhāro jñānasya vochyate
īdṛśaiḥ sacivairyukto mūrkhairdiṣṭyā dharāmyaham

translations.english: Or if you had appropriated the same, you have forgotten it afterwards;;and you bear the burden of ignorance. And it is owing to my good fortune that, having such stupid counsellors, I have as yet held my kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु मृत्योर्भयं नास्ति मां वक्तुं परुषं वचः
यस्य मे शासतो जिह्वा प्रयच्छति शुभाशुभम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu mṛtyorbhayaṁ nāsti māṁ vaktuṁ paruṣaṁ vacaḥ
yasya me śāsato jihvā prayacchati śubhāśubham

translations.english: Have you no fear of death that you use harsh speech towards me, who am the ruler and whose tongue dispense good and evil?

verses.sanskrit:
अप्येव दहनं स्पृष्ट्वा वने तिष्ठन्ति पादपाः
राजदोषपरामृष्टास्तिष्ठन्ते नापराधिनः
verses.transliteration:
apyeva dahanaṁ spṛṣṭvā vane tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ
rājadoṣaparāmṛṣṭāstiṣṭhante nāparādhinaḥ

translations.english: Even trees may exist in the forest, coming in contact with burning fire; but transgressors cannot exist, visited with the chastisement of the monarch.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्यामहमिमौ पापौ शत्रुपक्षप्रशंसकौ
यदि पूर्वोपकारैर्मे न क्रोधो मृदुतां व्रजेत्
verses.transliteration:
hanyāmahamimau pāpau śatrupakṣapraśaṁsakau
yadi pūrvopakārairme na krodho mṛdutāṁ vrajet

translations.english: I shall slay these wicked wights, who praise the side of the enemy, if my anger be not moderated, remembering their former good offices.

verses.sanskrit:
अपध्वंसत गच्छध्वं संनिकर्षादितो मम
न हि वां हन्तुमिच्छामि स्मरन्नुपकृतानि वाम्
हतावेव कृतघ्नौ तौ मयि स्नेहपराङ्मुखौ
verses.transliteration:
apadhvaṁsata gacchadhvaṁ saṁnikarṣādito mama
na hi vāṁ hantumicchāmi smarannupakṛtāni vām
hatāveva kṛtaghnau tau mayi snehaparāṅmukhau

translations.english: Avaunt! Go hence from near me! I do not wish to slay you, remembering your good acts. Slain you (already) are, who are ingrate and cherish no affection for me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तौ तु सव्रीडौ तावुभौ शुकसारणौ
रावणं जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्याभिनिःसृतौ
verses.transliteration:
evamuktau tu savrīḍau tāvubhau śukasāraṇau
rāvaṇaṁ jayaśabdena pratinandyābhiniḥsṛtau

translations.english: Thus accosted, Suka and Sarana, seeing (how things stood), covered with bashfulness, went out, saluting Ravana by uttering 'Victory!'

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीत्स दशग्रीवः समीपस्थं महोदरम्
उपस्थापय शीघ्रं मे चारान्नीतिविशारदान्
verses.transliteration:
abravītsa daśagrīvaḥ samīpasthaṁ mahodaram
upasthāpaya śīghraṁ me cārānnītiviśāradān

translations.english: Then that ranger of night, the Ten-necked one, said to Mahodara, who was present, to summon some spies. Thus accosted, Mahodara speedily ordered some spies (to present themselves).

verses.sanskrit:
ततश्चराः संत्वरिताः प्राप्ताः पार्थिवशासनात्
उपस्थिताः प्राञ्जलयो वर्धयित्वा जयाशिषा
verses.transliteration:
tataścarāḥ saṁtvaritāḥ prāptāḥ pārthivaśāsanāt
upasthitāḥ prāñjalayo vardhayitvā jayāśiṣā

translations.english: Thereat, the spies, hurriedly arriving there at the mandate of the monarch, and, presenting themselves, stood with joined hands, uttering blessing of victory.

verses.sanskrit:
इतो गच्छत रामस्य व्यवसायं परीक्षथ
मन्त्रेष्वभ्यन्तरा येऽस्य प्रीत्या तेन समागताः
verses.transliteration:
ito gacchata rāmasya vyavasāyaṁ parīkṣatha
mantreṣvabhyantarā ye'sya prītyā tena samāgatāḥ

translations.english: Then the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, addressed the spies, who were heroic, faithful, calm, and courageous, Go hence, and acquaint yourselves with the exertions of Rama; as well as with those who, being the custodians of Rāma's close counsels, have gladly joined him (here).

verses.sanskrit:
कथं स्वपिति जागर्ति किमन्यच्च करिष्यति
विज्ञाय निपुणं सर्वमागन्तव्यमशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ svapiti jāgarti kimanyacca kariṣyati
vijñāya nipuṇaṁ sarvamāgantavyamaśeṣataḥ

translations.english: How he sleep and how he wake, and what he engage himself in, having deftly acquainted yourselves with all this thoroughly, do you come (back here).

verses.sanskrit:
चारेण विदितः शत्रुः पण्डितैर्वसुधाधिपैः
युद्धे स्वल्पेन यत्नेन समासाद्य निरस्यते
verses.transliteration:
cāreṇa viditaḥ śatruḥ paṇḍitairvasudhādhipaiḥ
yuddhe svalpena yatnena samāsādya nirasyate

translations.english: The wise king that gathers (a knowledge of) his enemy through spies, can, putting forth a modicum of effort in conflict, neutralise (his exertions).

verses.sanskrit:
चारास्तु ते तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रहृष्टा राक्षसेश्वरम्
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं जग्मुर्यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
cārāstu te tathetyuktvā prahṛṣṭā rākṣaseśvaram
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṁ jagmuryatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereat the spies, saying, So it is, taking Sardula to the fore, with delighted hearts went round the sovereign of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ते सुवेलस्य शैलस्य समीपे रामलक्ष्मणौ
प्रच्छन्ना ददृशुर्गत्वा ससुग्रीवविभीषणौ
verses.transliteration:
te suvelasya śailasya samīpe rāmalakṣmaṇau
pracchannā dadṛśurgatvā sasugrīvavibhīṣaṇau

translations.english: And repairing secretly to the vicinity of the mountain bordering on the fair shore,* they saw Rāma and Lakşmaņa with Sugrīva and Vibhís ana. *Suvelasya Säilasya may also mean, of the mount Suvela.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु धर्मात्मना दृष्टा राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसाः
विभीषणेन तत्रस्था निगृहीता यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
te tu dharmātmanā dṛṣṭā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasāḥ
vibhīṣaṇena tatrasthā nigṛhītā yadṛcchayā

translations.english: That wicked Rākşasa, Sārdula, alone was taken (before Rāma).

verses.sanskrit:
वानरैरर्दितास्ते तु विक्रान्तैर्लघुविक्रमैः
पुनर्लङ्कामनुप्राप्ताः श्वसन्तो नष्टचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
vānarairarditāste tu vikrāntairlaghuvikramaiḥ
punarlaṅkāmanuprāptāḥ śvasanto naṣṭacetasaḥ

translations.english: And, on having been put to straits by the powerful monkeys of fleet vigour, they, breathing hard, and with their consciousness lost, again, arrived at Lankā. *The spies, that is.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दशग्रीवमुपस्थितास्ते; चारा बहिर्नित्यचरा निशाचराः
गिरेः सुवेलस्य समीपवासिनं; न्यवेदयन्भीमबलं महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
tato daśagrīvamupasthitāste; cārā bahirnityacarā niśācarāḥ
gireḥ suvelasya samīpavāsinaṁ; nyavedayanbhīmabalaṁ mahābalāḥ

translations.english: Then those exceedingly strong spies, always ranging outside, presenting themselves before the Ten-necked one, informed him of the forces of Rāma, stationed near mount Suvela.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तमक्षोभ्य बलं लङ्काधिपतये चराः
सुवेले राघवं शैले निविष्टं प्रत्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
tatastamakṣobhya balaṁ laṅkādhipataye carāḥ
suvele rāghavaṁ śaile niviṣṭaṁ pratyavedayan

translations.english: Then the spies communicated to Lankā's lord news concerning Rāghava and his host stationed at the mount Suvela.

verses.sanskrit:
चाराणां रावणः श्रुत्वा प्राप्तं रामं महाबलम्
जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किंचिच्छार्दूलं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
cārāṇāṁ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṁ rāmaṁ mahābalam
jātodvego'bhavatkiṁcicchārdūlaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of the spies, that Rama, accompanied by a mighty army, had arrived (there), Rāvana was a little agitated and spoke to Sardula.

verses.sanskrit:
अयथावच्च ते वर्णो दीनश्चासि निशाचर
नासि कच्चिदमित्राणां क्रुद्धानां वशमागतः
verses.transliteration:
ayathāvacca te varṇo dīnaścāsi niśācara
nāsi kaccidamitrāṇāṁ kruddhānāṁ vaśamāgataḥ

translations.english: Your colour has changed its natural aspect, and O ranger of the night, you look poorly. Did not come under the control of the wrathful foes?

verses.sanskrit:
इति तेनानुशिष्टस्तु वाचं मन्दमुदीरयत्
तदा राक्षसशार्दूलं शार्दूलो भयविह्वलः
verses.transliteration:
iti tenānuśiṣṭastu vācaṁ mandamudīrayat
tadā rākṣasaśārdūlaṁ śārdūlo bhayavihvalaḥ

translations.english: Thus ordered by him, then (Sārdula), bewildered by fear, addressed that tiger of a Raksasa, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न ते चारयितुं शक्या राजन्वानरपुंगवाः
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तश्च राघवेण च रक्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
na te cārayituṁ śakyā rājanvānarapuṁgavāḥ
vikrāntā balavantaśca rāghaveṇa ca rakṣitāḥ

translations.english: Those powerful monkeys, o king, puissant, strong, and protected by Rāghava, are incapable of being ranged (by us). or

verses.sanskrit:
नापि संभाषितुं शक्याः संप्रश्नोऽत्र न लभ्यते
सर्वतो रक्ष्यते पन्था वानरैः पर्वतोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
nāpi saṁbhāṣituṁ śakyāḥ saṁpraśno'tra na labhyate
sarvato rakṣyate panthā vānaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ

translations.english: They cannot be conversed with interrogated. All around, the courses are kept by monkeys resembling hills.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टमात्रे ज्ञातोऽहं बले तस्मिन्नचारिते
बलाद्गृहीतो बहुभिर्बहुधास्मि विदारितः
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭamātre jñāto'haṁ bale tasminnacārite
balādgṛhīto bahubhirbahudhāsmi vidāritaḥ

translations.english: As soon as I entered, and was scanning that host, I was discovered. And forcibly taken by the Rākşasa, I was pulled by them hither and thither.

verses.sanskrit:
जानुभिर्मुष्टिभिर्दन्तैस्तलैश्चाभिहतो भृशम्
परिणीतोऽस्मि हरिभिर्बलवद्भिरमर्षणैः
verses.transliteration:
jānubhirmuṣṭibhirdantaistalaiścābhihato bhṛśam
pariṇīto'smi haribhirbalavadbhiramarṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: And furiously assailed by the monkeys with thighs, clenched fists, teeth, and palms, I was dragged in the midst of the army by the enraged monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
परिणीय च सर्वत्र नीतोऽहं रामसंसदम्
रुधिरादिग्धसर्वाङ्गो विह्वलश्चलितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
pariṇīya ca sarvatra nīto'haṁ rāmasaṁsadam
rudhirādigdhasarvāṅgo vihvalaścalitendriyaḥ

translations.english: And, after having been taken all about, I was (at length) taken before Rāma, bleeding, with my limbs showing sorry work, and my senses swimming and paralysed.

verses.sanskrit:
हरिभिर्वध्यमानश्च याचमानः कृताञ्जलिः
राघवेण परित्रातो जीवामि ह यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
haribhirvadhyamānaśca yācamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
rāghaveṇa paritrāto jīvāmi ha yadṛcchayā

translations.english: And, having been belaboured by the monkeys, I, on craving his kindness with joined hands, was, at his pleasure, rescued by Rāghava, with, Don't, don't!

verses.sanskrit:
एष शैलैः शिलाभिश्च पूरयित्वा महार्णवम्
द्वारमाश्रित्य लङ्काया रामस्तिष्ठति सायुधः
verses.transliteration:
eṣa śailaiḥ śilābhiśca pūrayitvā mahārṇavam
dvāramāśritya laṅkāyā rāmastiṣṭhati sāyudhaḥ

translations.english: Having filled up the deep with rocks and crags, Rāma equipped with weapons, stay, occupying the gate of Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
गरुडव्यूहमास्थाय सर्वतो हरिभिर्वृतः
मां विसृज्य महातेजा लङ्कामेवाभिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
garuḍavyūhamāsthāya sarvato haribhirvṛtaḥ
māṁ visṛjya mahātejā laṅkāmevābhivartate

translations.english: And, letting me off, that one of suspassing vigour, surrounded by monkeys, and, arranging his forces in the Garuda fashion, advance upon Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा प्राकारमायाति क्षिप्रमेकतरं कुरु
सीतां चास्मै प्रयच्छाशु सुयुद्धं वा प्रदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
purā prākāramāyāti kṣipramekataraṁ kuru
sītāṁ cāsmai prayacchāśu suyuddhaṁ vā pradīyatām

translations.english: They advance before the wall. Speedily do one of these things-make over Sītā without delay, or give (him) battle.

verses.sanskrit:
मनसा संततापाथ तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसाधिपः
शार्दूलस्य महद्वाक्यमथोवाच स रावणः
verses.transliteration:
manasā saṁtatāpātha tacchrutvā rākṣasādhipaḥ
śārdūlasya mahadvākyamathovāca sa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing this, Ravana, lord of Raksasas, then reflecting in his mind, spoke to Sārdula these pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मां प्रतियुध्येरन्देवगन्धर्वदानवाः
नैव सीतां प्रदास्यामि सर्वलोकभयादपि
verses.transliteration:
yadi māṁ pratiyudhyerandevagandharvadānavāḥ
naiva sītāṁ pradāsyāmi sarvalokabhayādapi

translations.english: Even if gods, and Gandharvas, and Danavas should array themselves against me, I will not from fear of all creatures, render (back) Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा रावणः पुनरब्रवीत्
चारिता भवता सेना केऽत्र शूराः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ punarabravīt
cāritā bhavatā senā ke'tra śūrāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Having said this, that exceedingly energetic one again said,You have ranged this army. Who here among the monkeys are heroic?

verses.sanskrit:
कीदृशाः किंप्रभावाश्च वानरा ये दुरासदाः
कस्य पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च तत्त्वमाख्याहि राक्षस
verses.transliteration:
kīdṛśāḥ kiṁprabhāvāśca vānarā ye durāsadāḥ
kasya putrāśca pautrāśca tattvamākhyāhi rākṣasa

translations.english: O amiable one, what is their potency? And what are those monkeys that are hard to approach, like? And, O you of fair vows, whose sons and grandsons are they? Truly relate all this (to me).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रत्र प्रतिपत्स्यामि ज्ञात्वा तेषां बलाबलम्
अवश्यं बलसंख्यानं कर्तव्यं युद्धमिच्छता
verses.transliteration:
tatratra pratipatsyāmi jñātvā teṣāṁ balābalam
avaśyaṁ balasaṁkhyānaṁ kartavyaṁ yuddhamicchatā

translations.english: Having ascertained their strength and weakness, I shall in this matter adopt my course. Those who wish for fight, certainly take account of all this.

verses.sanskrit:
अथैवमुक्तः शार्दूलो रावणेनोत्तमश्चरः
इदं वचनमारेभे वक्तुं रावणसंनिधौ
verses.transliteration:
athaivamuktaḥ śārdūlo rāvaṇenottamaścaraḥ
idaṁ vacanamārebhe vaktuṁ rāvaṇasaṁnidhau

translations.english: Thus addressed by Rāvana, Sārdula—best of spies-thus began to speak in the presence of Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
अथर्क्षरजसः पुत्रो युधि राजन्सुदुर्जयः
गद्गदस्याथ पुत्रोऽत्र जाम्बवानिति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
atharkṣarajasaḥ putro yudhi rājansudurjayaḥ
gadgadasyātha putro'tra jāmbavāniti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: O king, that unconquerable one in fight, Jāmbavān, is well known as the son Gadgada, king of bears.

verses.sanskrit:
गद्गदस्यैव पुत्रोऽन्यो गुरुपुत्रः शतक्रतोः
कदनं यस्य पुत्रेण कृतमेकेन रक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
gadgadasyaiva putro'nyo guruputraḥ śatakratoḥ
kadanaṁ yasya putreṇa kṛtamekena rakṣasām

translations.english: The other son of Gadgada is the son of Śakra's preceptor. By which son, single-handed, was done immense oppression to the Rākṣasa.

verses.sanskrit:
सुषेणश्चापि धर्मात्मा पुत्रो धर्मस्य वीर्यवान्
सौम्यः सोमात्मजश्चात्र राजन्दधिमुखः कपिः
verses.transliteration:
suṣeṇaścāpi dharmātmā putro dharmasya vīryavān
saumyaḥ somātmajaścātra rājandadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ

translations.english: The righteous and puissant Sușeņa is the son of Dharma. And the mild monkey, Dadhimukha, O king, is the son of Soma. 1. Righteousness. 2. Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमुखो दुर्मुखश्चात्र वेगदर्शी च वानरः
मृत्युर्वानररूपेण नूनं सृष्टः स्वयम्भुवा
verses.transliteration:
sumukho durmukhaścātra vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ
mṛtyurvānararūpeṇa nūnaṁ sṛṣṭaḥ svayambhuvā

translations.english: And Sumukha, Durmukha and the monkey, vegadarcin (resembling) Death himself, were for certain begot by the Self-create in the shape of a monkey.* *Another meaning is, “The monkey, Vegadarsi who is death himself in the shape of a monkey." But I give the acceptable sense.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रो हुतवहस्याथ नीलः सेनापतिः स्वयम्
अनिलस्य च पुत्रोऽत्र हनूमानिति विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration:
putro hutavahasyātha nīlaḥ senāpatiḥ svayam
anilasya ca putro'tra hanūmāniti viśrutaḥ

translations.english: Nīla himself is the son of the bearer of sacrificial oblations;* and Hanumán is famed as the son of the Wind-god. * Fire.

verses.sanskrit:
नप्ता शक्रस्य दुर्धर्षो बलवानङ्गदो युवा
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ बलिनावश्विसंभवौ
verses.transliteration:
naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavānaṅgado yuvā
maindaśca dvividaścobhau balināvaśvisaṁbhavau

translations.english: The irrepressible and youthful Angada is the grandson of Śakra. And the lusty Mainda and Dvivida are sprung from Aśvi.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रा वैवस्वतस्यात्र पञ्चकालान्तकोपमाः
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः
verses.transliteration:
putrā vaivasvatasyātra pañcakālāntakopamāḥ
gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ

translations.english: And five are the sons of Vaivasvata, resembling the Reaper himself, Gaya, Gavāks a, gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamādana.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वेतो ज्योतिर्मुखश्चात्र भास्करस्यात्मसंभवौ
वरुणस्य च पुत्रोऽथ हेमकूटः प्लवंगमः
verses.transliteration:
śveto jyotirmukhaścātra bhāskarasyātmasaṁbhavau
varuṇasya ca putro'tha hemakūṭaḥ plavaṁgamaḥ

translations.english: And here are ſveta and Jyotirmukha, sprung from Vāskara's self; and the monkey Hemakūta is the son of Varuna.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वकर्मसुतो वीरो नलः प्लवगसत्तमः
विक्रान्तो वेगवानत्र वसुपुत्रः सुदुर्धरः
verses.transliteration:
viśvakarmasuto vīro nalaḥ plavagasattamaḥ
vikrānto vegavānatra vasuputraḥ sudurdharaḥ

translations.english: The heroic Nalabest of monkeys, is the son of Viśvakarmă. And powerful and impetuous, Durdhara is the son of Vasu.

verses.sanskrit:
दशवानरकोट्यश्च शूराणां युद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम्
श्रीमतां देवपुत्राणां शेषान्नाख्यातुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
daśavānarakoṭyaśca śūrāṇāṁ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇām
śrīmatāṁ devaputrāṇāṁ śeṣānnākhyātumutsahe

translations.english: But I can not enumerate the rest, ten koțis of heroic monkeys-all sons of deities—burning for battle.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रो दशरथस्यैष सिंहसंहननो युवा
दूषणो निहतो येन खरश्च त्रिशिरास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
putro daśarathasyaiṣa siṁhasaṁhanano yuvā
dūṣaṇo nihato yena kharaśca triśirāstathā

translations.english: And this is Dasaratha's son—this you resembling a lion, who slew Düşana and Khara and Triſiras.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्ति रामस्य सदृशो विक्रमे भुवि कश्चन
विराधो निहतो येन कबन्धश्चान्तकोपमः
verses.transliteration:
nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaścana
virādho nihato yena kabandhaścāntakopamaḥ

translations.english: There breathes none on Earth that is like to Rāma in prowess, by whom was slain Virādha and Kabandha, resembling the Destroyer.

verses.sanskrit:
वक्तुं न शक्तो रामस्य नरः कश्चिद्गुणान्क्षितौ
जनस्थानगता येन तावन्तो राक्षसा हताः
verses.transliteration:
vaktuṁ na śakto rāmasya naraḥ kaścidguṇānkṣitau
janasthānagatā yena tāvanto rākṣasā hatāḥ

translations.english: No person can on earth describe the virtues of Rāma; by whom have been slain all those Rākşasas that had gone to Janasthāna.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्चात्र धर्मात्मा मातंगानामिवर्षभः
यस्य बाणपथं प्राप्य न जीवेदपि वासवः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaścātra dharmātmā mātaṁgānāmivarṣabhaḥ
yasya bāṇapathaṁ prāpya na jīvedapi vāsavaḥ

translations.english: Here also is the virtuous Lakşmaņa, like to the foremost of elephants, coming in the way of whose shafts, even Vasava does not live.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां वरिष्ठश्च तव भ्राता विभीषणः
परिगृह्य पुरीं लङ्कां राघवस्य हिते रतः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ variṣṭhaśca tava bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
parigṛhya purīṁ laṅkāṁ rāghavasya hite rataḥ

translations.english: That foremost of Rāksasas, Vibhisana, your brother, engaged in the welfare of Raghava, has laid seige to Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सर्वं समाख्यातं तवेदं वानरं बलम्
सुवेलेऽधिष्ठितं शैले शेषकार्ये भवान्गतिः
verses.transliteration:
iti sarvaṁ samākhyātaṁ tavedaṁ vānaraṁ balam
suvele'dhiṣṭhitaṁ śaile śeṣakārye bhavāngatiḥ

translations.english: Thus have I described to you the entire monkey host stationed in mount Suvela. As for what remain to be done, you are the master.

verses.sanskrit:
चाराणां रावणः श्रुत्वा प्राप्तं रामं महाबलम्
जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किंचित्सचिवांश्चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
cārāṇāṁ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṁ rāmaṁ mahābalam
jātodvego'bhavatkiṁcitsacivāṁścedamabravīt

translations.english: Then the spies of the king informed him of the forces of Rāghava, incapable of being agitated, which had stationed themselves on Suvela. Hearing the arrival of Rāma's mighty army from the spies, Ravana was a little agitated, and he spoke to the ministers.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिणः शीघ्रमायान्तु सर्वे वै सुसमाहिताः
अयं नो मन्त्रकालो हि संप्राप्त इव राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
mantriṇaḥ śīghramāyāntu sarve vai susamāhitāḥ
ayaṁ no mantrakālo hi saṁprāpta iva rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: Let the ministers speedily present themselves, having their wits about them, the time forsooth has come for counsel.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तच्छासनं श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणोऽभ्यागमन्द्रुतम्
ततः संमन्त्रयामास सचिवै राक्षसैः सह
verses.transliteration:
tasya tacchāsanaṁ śrutvā mantriṇo'bhyāgamandrutam
tataḥ saṁmantrayāmāsa sacivai rākṣasaiḥ saha

translations.english: Hearing his mandate, those Raksasas, his counsellors, swiftly presented themselves. And then he consulted with his Rākşasa counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रयित्वा स दुर्धर्षः क्षमं यत्समनन्तरम्
विसर्जयित्वा सचिवान्प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्
verses.transliteration:
mantrayitvā sa durdharṣaḥ kṣamaṁ yatsamanantaram
visarjayitvā sacivānpraviveśa svamālayam

translations.english: Having deliberated duly, that resistless one, dismissing his ministers, entered his own abode.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राक्षसमाहूय विद्युज्जिह्वं महाबलम्
मायाविदं महामायः प्राविशद्यत्र मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
tato rākṣasamāhūya vidyujjihvaṁ mahābalam
māyāvidaṁ mahāmāyaḥ prāviśadyatra maithilī

translations.english: Then, taking with him the highly strong Vidyujjihva, huge bodied and gifted with the powers of illusion, he entered where Mithila's daughter was.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्युज्जिह्वं च मायाज्ञमब्रवीद्राक्षसाधिपः
मोहयिष्यामहे सीतां मायया जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
vidyujjihvaṁ ca māyājñamabravīdrākṣasādhipaḥ
mohayiṣyāmahe sītāṁ māyayā janakātmajām

translations.english: The lord of Rākşasas said to Vidyujjihva, skilled in illusion, Do you bring Janaka's daughter under the sway of illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
शिरो मायामयं गृह्य राघवस्य निशाचर
मां त्वं समुपतिष्ठस्व महच्च सशरं धनुः
verses.transliteration:
śiro māyāmayaṁ gṛhya rāghavasya niśācara
māṁ tvaṁ samupatiṣṭhasva mahacca saśaraṁ dhanuḥ

translations.english: O ranger of the night, do you, taking an illusory head of Rāghava, as well as a mighty bow with the shaft (set), present yourself before me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्याह विद्युज्जिह्वो निशाचरः
तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्राजा प्रददौ च विभूषणम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastathetyāha vidyujjihvo niśācaraḥ
tasya tuṣṭo'bhavadrājā pradadau ca vibhūṣaṇam

translations.english: Thus accosted, the night-ranger, Vidyujjibha, saying, So be it, displayed that desired illusion to Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकवनिकायां तु प्रविवेश महाबलः
ततो दीनामदैन्यार्हां ददर्श धनदानुजः
अधोमुखीं शोकपरामुपविष्टां महीतले
verses.transliteration:
aśokavanikāyāṁ tu praviveśa mahābalaḥ
tato dīnāmadainyārhāṁ dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ
adhomukhīṁ śokaparāmupaviṣṭāṁ mahītale

translations.english: Then the exceedingly powerful lord of the Naiſtas, the younger brother of the Dispenser of riches, entered (into that place) and saw (there Sitā) distressed, albeit unworthy of distress, with her head hung down, overwhelmed with woe, sitting on the ground, staying at the aśoka woods, engaged in the contemplation of her lord, conciliated by dreadful Räkşasis remaining near. then, drawing near Sita, Ravana, proclaiming his exultation, said these haughty words to the daughter of Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
सान्त्व्यमाना मया भद्रे यमुपाश्रित्य वल्गसे
खर हन्ता स ते भर्ता राघवः समरे हतः
verses.transliteration:
sāntvyamānā mayā bhadre yamupāśritya valgase
khara hantā sa te bhartā rāghavaḥ samare hataḥ

translations.english: O gentle one, he depending on whom you, being soothed by (me), slight me-that slayer of Khara, your husband, Rāghava, has fallen in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
छिन्नं ते सर्वतो मूलं दर्पस्ते निहतो मया
व्यसनेनात्मनः सीते मम भार्या भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
chinnaṁ te sarvato mūlaṁ darpaste nihato mayā
vyasanenātmanaḥ sīte mama bhāryā bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: Your roots have been completely severed, and your pride has been destroyed by me. In consequence of this calamity, O Sītā, you shall become my wife. O foolish (girl), renounce this idea. What will you do with that is dead?

verses.sanskrit:
अल्पपुण्ये निवृत्तार्थे मूढे पण्डितमानिनि
शृणु भर्तृबधं सीते घोरं वृत्रवधं यथा
verses.transliteration:
alpapuṇye nivṛttārthe mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini
śṛṇu bhartṛbadhaṁ sīte ghoraṁ vṛtravadhaṁ yathā

translations.english: O meek (wench), be you the mistress of all my wives. O you of slender religious merit! O you whose object has been defeated! O you that presumes to be wise! Hearken to the destruction of your lord, like the dreadful destruction of Vrtra!

verses.sanskrit:
समायातः समुद्रान्तं मां हन्तुं किल राघवः
वानरेन्द्रप्रणीतेन बलेन महता वृतः
verses.transliteration:
samāyātaḥ samudrāntaṁ māṁ hantuṁ kila rāghavaḥ
vānarendrapraṇītena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ

translations.english: Surrounded by a vast army gathered by the sovereign of the monkeys, Raghava had presented himself on the shore of the sea, for compassing my destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्
बलेन महता रामो व्रजत्यस्तं दिवाकरे
verses.transliteration:
saṁniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīramāsādya dakṣiṇam
balena mahatā rāmo vrajatyastaṁ divākare

translations.english: And on the sun have set, Rama stationed himself with his mighty army, oppressing the northern shore (of the sea).

verses.sanskrit:
अथाध्वनि परिश्रान्तमर्धरात्रे स्थितं बलम्
सुखसुप्तं समासाद्य चारितं प्रथमं चरैः
verses.transliteration:
athādhvani pariśrāntamardharātre sthitaṁ balam
sukhasuptaṁ samāsādya cāritaṁ prathamaṁ caraiḥ

translations.english: Then at midnight (my) spies coming to that host, thus stationed, fatigued from travel, and sleeping soundly (in consequence), first ranged it.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्प्रहस्तप्रणीतेन बलेन महता मम
बलमस्य हतं रात्रौ यत्र रामः सुलक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
tatprahastapraṇītena balena mahatā mama
balamasya hataṁ rātrau yatra rāmaḥ sulakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then my mighty forces led by Prahasta slew his host overnight, where was present Răma along with Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
यष्टीश्च तोमरान्प्रासंश्चक्राणि मुसलानि च
उद्यम्योद्यम्य रक्षोभिर्वानरेषु निपातिताः
verses.transliteration:
yaṣṭīśca tomarānprāsaṁścakrāṇi musalāni ca
udyamyodyamya rakṣobhirvānareṣu nipātitāḥ

translations.english: And repeatedly upraising pattiśas and bludgeons, swords, rods and other mighty weapons; and (discharging) showers of arrows, and darts, and daggers and maces and sticks and crows and bearded darts and discuses and clubs; the Rākşasas discharged these among the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ सुप्तस्य रामस्य प्रहस्तेन प्रमाथिना
असक्तं कृतहस्तेन शिरश्छिन्नं महासिना
verses.transliteration:
atha suptasya rāmasya prahastena pramāthinā
asaktaṁ kṛtahastena śiraśchinnaṁ mahāsinā

translations.english: While Räma was sleeping, the furious Prahasta by means of a mighty falchion, with speed cut off his head clean.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणः समुत्पत्य निगृहीतो यदृच्छया
दिशः प्रव्राजितः सर्वैर्लक्ष्मणः प्लवगैः सह
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇaḥ samutpatya nigṛhīto yadṛcchayā
diśaḥ pravrājitaḥ sarvairlakṣmaṇaḥ plavagaiḥ saha

translations.english: Vibhīşaņa, who was flying at his will, was taken captive. And Lakşmaņa along with the monkeys army has departed somewhere.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवो ग्रीवया शेते भग्नया प्लवगाधिपः
निरस्तहनुकः शेते हनूमान्राक्षसैर्हतः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvo grīvayā śete bhagnayā plavagādhipaḥ
nirastahanukaḥ śete hanūmānrākṣasairhataḥ

translations.english: O Sītā, Sugriva lord of monkeys-has his neck broken; and, O Sītā, with his jaw fractured, Hanuman has been slaughtered by the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवानथ जानुभ्यामुत्पतन्निहतो युधि
पट्टसैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नो निकृत्तः पादपो यथा
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavānatha jānubhyāmutpatannihato yudhi
paṭṭasairbahubhiśchinno nikṛttaḥ pādapo yathā

translations.english: And Jāmbavān, endeavouring to spring up bearded darts, even as a tree cut off.

verses.sanskrit:
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ निहतौ वानरर्षभौ
निःश्वसन्तौ रुदन्तौ च रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
maindaśca dvividaścobhau nihatau vānararṣabhau
niḥśvasantau rudantau ca rudhireṇa samukṣitau

translations.english: The stalwart Mainda and Dvivida-those foremost of monkeyssighing and lamenting, bathed in blood, destroyers of foes-were cut off with a sword.

verses.sanskrit:
नाराचैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नः शेते दर्यां दरीमुखः
कुमुदस्तु महातेजा निष्कूजन्सायकैर्हतः
verses.transliteration:
nārācairbahubhiśchinnaḥ śete daryāṁ darīmukhaḥ
kumudastu mahātejā niṣkūjansāyakairhataḥ

translations.english: Panasa is rolling on the earth like a (veritable) Panasa. And mangled by many iron arrows, Darīmukha lies in a cave. And the exceedingly energetic Kumuda, dumb, is slain by shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदो बहुभिश्छिन्नः शरैरासाद्य राक्षसैः
पातितो रुधिरोद्गारी क्षितौ निपतितोऽङ्गदः
verses.transliteration:
aṅgado bahubhiśchinnaḥ śarairāsādya rākṣasaiḥ
pātito rudhirodgārī kṣitau nipatito'ṅgadaḥ

translations.english: And torn by innumerable (arrows) discharged on all sides by Raksasas. Angada, vomiting blood, Leith on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
हरयो मथिता नागै रथजालैस्तथापरे
शायिता मृदितास्तत्र वायुवेगैरिवाम्बुदाः
verses.transliteration:
harayo mathitā nāgai rathajālaistathāpare
śāyitā mṛditāstatra vāyuvegairivāmbudāḥ

translations.english: The monkeys, hard pressed by elephants, and others by networks of cars, lie low in the field, having been agitated like clouds by winds.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रद्रुताश्च परे त्रस्ता हन्यमाना जघन्यतः
अभिद्रुतास्तु रक्षोभिः सिंहैरिव महाद्विपाः
verses.transliteration:
pradrutāśca pare trastā hanyamānā jaghanyataḥ
abhidrutāstu rakṣobhiḥ siṁhairiva mahādvipāḥ

translations.english: And others afflicted with affright, flee, attacked (by the enemy) in the rear, and followed by the Rākṣasas, like mighty elephants pursued by lions.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरे पतिताः केचित्केचिद्गगनमाश्रिताः
ऋक्षा वृक्षानुपारूढा वानरैस्तु विमिश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
sāgare patitāḥ kecitkecidgaganamāśritāḥ
ṛkṣā vṛkṣānupārūḍhā vānaraistu vimiśritāḥ

translations.english: Some have fallen into the sea, and some have taken refuge in the sky; and the bears have mounted up trees along with the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरस्य च तीरेषु शैलेषु च वनेषु च
पिङ्गाक्षास्ते विरूपाक्षैर्बहुभिर्बहवो हताः
verses.transliteration:
sāgarasya ca tīreṣu śaileṣu ca vaneṣu ca
piṅgākṣāste virūpākṣairbahubhirbahavo hatāḥ

translations.english: And on the shore of the sea, and in mountains and woods many are the tawny-hued monkeys that have been slain by Rākşasas of frightful forms.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं तव हतो भर्ता ससैन्यो मम सेनया
क्षतजार्द्रं रजोध्वस्तमिदं चास्याहृतं शिरः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tava hato bhartā sasainyo mama senayā
kṣatajārdraṁ rajodhvastamidaṁ cāsyāhṛtaṁ śiraḥ

translations.english: Thus has your lord been slain by my forces, along with his army; and I have his head, washed in blood and besmeared with dust.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परमदुर्धर्षो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
सीतायामुपशृण्वन्त्यां राक्षसीमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paramadurdharṣo rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
sītāyāmupaśṛṇvantyāṁ rākṣasīmidamabravīt

translations.english: Thereat, the exceedingly irrepressible lord of Raksasas, Ravana, spoke to a Raksasi, in the hearing of Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसं क्रूरकर्माणं विद्युज्जिह्वं त्वमानय
येन तद्राघवशिरः संग्रामात्स्वयमाहृतम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasaṁ krūrakarmāṇaṁ vidyujjihvaṁ tvamānaya
yena tadrāghavaśiraḥ saṁgrāmātsvayamāhṛtam

translations.english: Bring (hither) the Raksasa, Vidyujjibha of cruel deeds, who has personally brought Rāghava's head from the field.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्युज्जिह्वस्ततो गृह्य शिरस्तत्सशरासनम्
प्रणामं शिरसा कृत्वा रावणस्याग्रतः स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
vidyujjihvastato gṛhya śirastatsaśarāsanam
praṇāmaṁ śirasā kṛtvā rāvaṇasyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, Vidyujjibha, taking the head along with the bow, bowing down the head (to Ravana), stood before him. Then spoke king Rävaņa to the Rākşasa, Vidyujjibha of the long tongue, who was staying by.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्रतः कुरु सीतायाः शीघ्रं दाशरथेः शिरः
अवस्थां पश्चिमां भर्तुः कृपणा साधु पश्यतु
verses.transliteration:
agrataḥ kuru sītāyāḥ śīghraṁ dāśaratheḥ śiraḥ
avasthāṁ paścimāṁ bhartuḥ kṛpaṇā sādhu paśyatu

translations.english: Do you at once hold before Sītā the head of Dasaratha's son. Let her clearly behold the ultimate sad plight of her lord.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तं तु तद्रक्षः शिरस्तत्प्रियदर्शनम्
उपनिक्षिप्य सीतायाः क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaṁ tu tadrakṣaḥ śirastatpriyadarśanam
upanikṣipya sītāyāḥ kṣipramantaradhīyata

translations.english: Thus addressed, that Raksasa, throwing that graceful head before Sītā, swiftly vanished,

verses.sanskrit:
रावणश्चापि चिक्षेप भास्वरं कार्मुकं महत्
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं सीतामिदमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaścāpi cikṣepa bhāsvaraṁ kārmukaṁ mahat
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṁ sītāmidamuvāca ha

translations.english: Rāvana cast down the mighty blazing bow, famed through the three worlds, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं तत्तव रामस्य कार्मुकं ज्यासमन्वितम्
इह प्रहस्तेनानीतं हत्वा तं निशि मानुषम्
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ tattava rāmasya kārmukaṁ jyāsamanvitam
iha prahastenānītaṁ hatvā taṁ niśi mānuṣam

translations.english: This is Rāma's. This is the bow of your Rāma with the string fixed. Slaying that man over night, Prahasta brought it hither.

verses.sanskrit:
स विद्युज्जिह्वेन सहैव तच्छिरो; धनुश्च भूमौ विनिकीर्य रावणः
विदेहराजस्य सुतां यशस्विनीं; ततोऽब्रवीत्तां भव मे वशानुगा
verses.transliteration:
sa vidyujjihvena sahaiva tacchiro; dhanuśca bhūmau vinikīrya rāvaṇaḥ
videharājasya sutāṁ yaśasvinīṁ; tato'bravīttāṁ bhava me vaśānugā

translations.english: When Vidyujjibha placed the head of that man, Ravana poured the bow on earth. Then he spoke to illustrious Sītā, the daughter of king Videha to submit to his desire.

verses.sanskrit:
सा सीता तच्छिरो दृष्ट्वा तच्च कार्मुकमुत्तमम्
सुग्रीवप्रतिसंसर्गमाख्यातं च हनूमता
verses.transliteration:
sā sītā tacchiro dṛṣṭvā tacca kārmukamuttamam
sugrīvapratisaṁsargamākhyātaṁ ca hanūmatā

translations.english: Seeing that head and that excellent bow, and (remembering) the union of (Rama) and Sugriva related by Hanumãn, and (seeing) those eyes, and the complexion of that face, and that countenance like to that of her lord, and that hair and that forehead; and that beautiful jewel forming the crest; and recognizing (Rāma) by all these tokens combined, (Sītā), exceedingly aggrieved, rebuked Kaikeyī, lamenting like a female osprey.

verses.sanskrit:
सकामा भव कैकेयि हतोऽयं कुलनन्दनः
कुलमुत्सादितं सर्वं त्वया कलहशीलया
verses.transliteration:
sakāmā bhava kaikeyi hato'yaṁ kulanandanaḥ
kulamutsāditaṁ sarvaṁ tvayā kalahaśīlayā

translations.english: O Kaikeyſ, have your wishes attained. Slain has been the son of the race; and the entire race is exterminated by you, partial to dissension.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्येण किं नु कैकेय्याः कृतं रामेण विप्रियम्
यद्गृहाच्चीरवसनस्तया प्रस्थापितो वनम्
verses.transliteration:
āryeṇa kiṁ nu kaikeyyāḥ kṛtaṁ rāmeṇa vipriyam
yadgṛhāccīravasanastayā prasthāpito vanam

translations.english: What evil had been done to Kaikeyi by the revered Rāma, that along with me, he had been banished into the woods, with rags given him (for his covering)?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही वेपमाना तपस्विनी
जगाम जगतीं बाला छिन्ना तु कदली यथा
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu vaidehī vepamānā tapasvinī
jagāma jagatīṁ bālā chinnā tu kadalī yathā

translations.english: Having said this, Vaidehi, forlorm and trembling (all over), dropped to the earth, like a plantain cut off.

verses.sanskrit:
सा मुहूर्तात्समाश्वस्य प्रतिलभ्य च चेतनाम्
तच्छिरः समुपाघ्राय विललापायतेक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
sā muhūrtātsamāśvasya pratilabhya ca cetanām
tacchiraḥ samupāghrāya vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā

translations.english: Then, recovering after a while, and having regained her consciousness, the large-eyed one, placing the head in her front, gave way to grief.

verses.sanskrit:
हा हतास्मि महाबाहो वीरव्रतमनुव्रता
इमां ते पश्चिमावस्थां गतास्मि विधवा कृता
verses.transliteration:
hā hatāsmi mahābāho vīravratamanuvratā
imāṁ te paścimāvasthāṁ gatāsmi vidhavā kṛtā

translations.english: Ah! I am undone, O mighty-armed one! ) you that did follow stern vows! From your (death), I have come by this final plight, having been rendered a widow.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रथमं मरणं नार्या भर्तुर्वैगुण्यमुच्यते
सुवृत्तः साधुवृत्तायाः संवृत्तस्त्वं ममाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
prathamaṁ maraṇaṁ nāryā bharturvaiguṇyamucyate
suvṛttaḥ sādhuvṛttāyāḥ saṁvṛttastvaṁ mamāgrataḥ

translations.english: The greatest calamity (that can befall a woman), is said to be the death of her husband. And, possessor of an excellent character, you have departed before me, who have ever trod the path of the righteous; but who have come by a mighty grief and am plunged in a sea of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
सा श्वश्रूर्मम कौसल्या त्वया पुत्रेण राघव
वत्सेनेव यथा धेनुर्विवत्सा वत्सला कृता
verses.transliteration:
sā śvaśrūrmama kausalyā tvayā putreṇa rāghava
vatseneva yathā dhenurvivatsā vatsalā kṛtā

translations.english: And you, who was engaged in delivering me, have yourself fallen! And my mother-in-law, Kausalyā, attached (to you), through the death of you, her son, at the hands of Raksasas, has been reduced to the condition of a cow that has been deprived of her calf.

verses.sanskrit:
आदिष्टं दीर्घमायुस्ते यैरचिन्त्यपराक्रम
अनृतं वचनं तेषामल्पायुरसि राघव
verses.transliteration:
ādiṣṭaṁ dīrghamāyuste yairacintyaparākrama
anṛtaṁ vacanaṁ teṣāmalpāyurasi rāghava

translations.english: O Rāghava, even the astrologers had predicted long life for you. But their words are false, you, O Rāghava, wast short-lived. me

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा नश्यति प्रज्ञा प्राज्ञस्यापि सतस्तव
पचत्येनं तथा कालो भूतानां प्रभवो ह्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā naśyati prajñā prājñasyāpi satastava
pacatyenaṁ tathā kālo bhūtānāṁ prabhavo hyayam

translations.english: Or did your wisdom, wise and good as you were, come to naught? For God, who is the origin of all beings, make (every one) reap the fruit of his own acts.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टं मृत्युमापन्नः कस्मात्त्वं नयशास्त्रवित्
व्यसनानामुपायज्ञः कुशलो ह्यसि वर्जने
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭaṁ mṛtyumāpannaḥ kasmāttvaṁ nayaśāstravit
vyasanānāmupāyajñaḥ kuśalo hyasi varjane

translations.english: And why, versed in polity as you wast, did you come by death, unforeseen? You were acquainted with the means of warding off misfortune, and skilled in doing so.

verses.sanskrit:
उपशेषे महाबाहो मां विहाय तपस्विनीम्
प्रियामिव शुभां नारीं पृथिवीं पुरुषर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
upaśeṣe mahābāho māṁ vihāya tapasvinīm
priyāmiva śubhāṁ nārīṁ pṛthivīṁ puruṣarṣabha

translations.english: Having been brought hither by representing the Fatal Night, fierce and fell, after (being) embraced, and by force, the lotus-eyed one has met with his death. Here lie you, O longarmed one, leaving me lone, and embracing the Earth like your beloved fair.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्चितं सततं यत्नाद्गन्धमाल्यैर्मया तव
इदं ते मत्प्रियं वीर धनुः काञ्चनभूषितम्
verses.transliteration:
arcitaṁ satataṁ yatnādgandhamālyairmayā tava
idaṁ te matpriyaṁ vīra dhanuḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam

translations.english: Ever carefully worshipped with perfumed wreaths, this bow of your, O hero, embellished with gold, is dear to me.

verses.sanskrit:
पित्रा दशरथेन त्वं श्वशुरेण ममानघ
पूर्वैश्च पितृभिः सार्धं नूनं स्वर्गे समागतः
verses.transliteration:
pitrā daśarathena tvaṁ śvaśureṇa mamānagha
pūrvaiśca pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṁ nūnaṁ svarge samāgataḥ

translations.english: O sinless one, you have surely gone to heaven, and (are there) in the company of your sire and my father-in-law, Dasaratha, and all your ancestors.

verses.sanskrit:
दिवि नक्षत्रभूतस्त्वं महत्कर्म कृतं प्रियम्
पुण्यं राजर्षिवंशं त्वमात्मनः समुपेक्षसे
verses.transliteration:
divi nakṣatrabhūtastvaṁ mahatkarma kṛtaṁ priyam
puṇyaṁ rājarṣivaṁśaṁ tvamātmanaḥ samupekṣase

translations.english: You have become a star of the firmament as the fruit of your great act.* You have disregarded your righteous race of Rājarşis. *The carrying out the command of your sire.

verses.sanskrit:
किं मान्न प्रेक्षसे राजन्किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे
बालां बालेन संप्राप्तां भार्यां मां सहचारिणीम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ mānna prekṣase rājankiṁ māṁ na pratibhāṣase
bālāṁ bālena saṁprāptāṁ bhāryāṁ māṁ sahacāriṇīm

translations.english: O king, why do you not look at me? And why is it that you do not answer me, who am a girl, hardly arrived at youth, and who am your wife and companion?

verses.sanskrit:
संश्रुतं गृह्णता पाणिं चरिष्यामीति यत्त्वया
स्मर तन्मम काकुत्स्थ नय मामपि दुःखिताम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁśrutaṁ gṛhṇatā pāṇiṁ cariṣyāmīti yattvayā
smara tanmama kākutstha naya māmapi duḥkhitām

translations.english: That you at the time of your espousing my hand had vowed, I will practise (righteousness) with you, do you, O Kakutstha, recollect the same, and take me, who am overwhelmed with distrees.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्मान्मामपहाय त्वं गतो गतिमतां वर
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं त्यक्त्वा मामिह दुःखिताम्
verses.transliteration:
kasmānmāmapahāya tvaṁ gato gatimatāṁ vara
asmāllokādamuṁ lokaṁ tyaktvā māmiha duḥkhitām

translations.english: Why, O best of goers, have you gone from this world to that other, leaving behind me, overwhelmed with distress?

verses.sanskrit:
कल्याणैरुचितं यत्तत्परिष्वक्तं मयैव तु
क्रव्यादैस्तच्छरीरं ते नूनं विपरिकृष्यते
verses.transliteration:
kalyāṇairucitaṁ yattatpariṣvaktaṁ mayaiva tu
kravyādaistaccharīraṁ te nūnaṁ viparikṛṣyate

translations.english: That person of your which, decked out with auspicious things, I used to embrace, beasts of prey will for certain tear the same.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः
अग्निहोत्रेण संस्कारं केन त्वं तु न लप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairiṣṭavānāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
agnihotreṇa saṁskāraṁ kena tvaṁ tu na lapsyase

translations.english: Having performed the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices with Dakşinăs (dispensed, why had not you attained purity by means of the sacrificial fire?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रव्रज्यामुपपन्नानां त्रयाणामेकमागतम्
परिप्रक्ष्यति कौसल्या लक्ष्मणं शोकलालसा
verses.transliteration:
pravrajyāmupapannānāṁ trayāṇāmekamāgatam
pariprakṣyati kausalyā lakṣmaṇaṁ śokalālasā

translations.english: Kaucalya, over-whelmed with sorrow, shall only behold one of the three that had gone away to distant lands, come (back)-Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्याः परिपृच्छन्त्या वधं मित्रबलस्य ते
तव चाख्यास्यते नूनं निशायां राक्षसैर्वधम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasyāḥ paripṛcchantyā vadhaṁ mitrabalasya te
tava cākhyāsyate nūnaṁ niśāyāṁ rākṣasairvadham

translations.english: On being asked by her, he shall relate your as well as the deaths of your friend's troops over night at the hands of the Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वां सुप्तं हतं श्रुत्वा मां च रक्षोगृहं गताम्
हृदयेन विदीर्णेन न भविष्यति राघव
verses.transliteration:
sā tvāṁ suptaṁ hataṁ śrutvā māṁ ca rakṣogṛhaṁ gatām
hṛdayena vidīrṇena na bhaviṣyati rāghava

translations.english: O Raghava, hearing you slain while asleep, and me staying in the abode of the Rākşasa, she with her heart cleft (in twain), shall cease to exist.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु पातय मां क्षिप्रं रामस्योपरि रावणः
समानय पतिं पत्न्या कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
sādhu pātaya māṁ kṣipraṁ rāmasyopari rāvaṇaḥ
samānaya patiṁ patnyā kuru kalyāṇamuttamam

translations.english: Do you, O Ravana, speedily slay me upon Rāma; and, bringing the wife to the husband, compass my best benefit.

verses.sanskrit:
शिरसा मे शिरश्चास्य कायं कायेन योजय
रावणानुगमिष्यामि गतिं भर्तुर्महात्मनः
मुहूर्तमपि नेच्छामि जीवितुं पापजीविना
verses.transliteration:
śirasā me śiraścāsya kāyaṁ kāyena yojaya
rāvaṇānugamiṣyāmi gatiṁ bharturmahātmanaḥ
muhūrtamapi necchāmi jīvituṁ pāpajīvinā

translations.english: Do you join my head to his and my body to his body. I will, O Rāvana, follow the way of my high-souled lord.

verses.sanskrit:
इति सा दुःखसंतप्ता विललापायतेक्षणा
भर्तुः शिरो धनुस्तत्र समीक्ष्य जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
iti sā duḥkhasaṁtaptā vilalāpāyatekṣaṇā
bhartuḥ śiro dhanustatra samīkṣya janakātmajā

translations.english: Thus, burning in grief, did that large-eyed one indulge in lamentations; and Janaka's daughter kept fast gazing at the head and bow of her lord.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं लालप्यमानायां सीतायां तत्र राक्षसः
अभिचक्राम भर्तारमनीकस्थः कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ lālapyamānāyāṁ sītāyāṁ tatra rākṣasaḥ
abhicakrāma bhartāramanīkasthaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: As the Rāksasa was by while Sītā was thus bewailing, there appeared before his lord, with joined hands, the warder, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
विजयस्वार्यपुत्रेति सोऽभिवाद्य प्रसाद्य च
न्यवेदयदनुप्राप्तं प्रहस्तं वाहिनीपतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vijayasvāryaputreti so'bhivādya prasādya ca
nyavedayadanuprāptaṁ prahastaṁ vāhinīpatim

translations.english: May the worshipful one be victorious! And saluting and propitiating him, (Ravana), he told him that Prahasta, general of the forces, had arrived.

verses.sanskrit:
अमात्यैः सहितः सर्वैः प्रहस्तः समुपस्थितः
किंचिदात्ययिकं कार्यं तेषां त्वं दर्शनं कुरु
verses.transliteration:
amātyaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ prahastaḥ samupasthitaḥ
kiṁcidātyayikaṁ kāryaṁ teṣāṁ tvaṁ darśanaṁ kuru

translations.english: Prahasta has come to you, surrounded by all the courtiers. And, O lord, I was despatched by him, desirous of seeing you.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो राक्षसप्रतिवेदितम्
अशोकवनिकां त्यक्त्वा मन्त्रिणां दर्शनं ययौ
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā daśagrīvo rākṣasaprativeditam
aśokavanikāṁ tyaktvā mantriṇāṁ darśanaṁ yayau

translations.english: Hearing these words of the Rākşasa, the Tennecked one, leaving the Asoka wood, went to see the counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु सर्वं समर्थ्यैव मन्त्रिभिः कृत्यमात्मनः
सभां प्रविश्य विदधे विदित्वा रामविक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu sarvaṁ samarthyaiva mantribhiḥ kṛtyamātmanaḥ
sabhāṁ praviśya vidadhe viditvā rāmavikramam

translations.english: Having decided his entire course of action in consultation with his competent advisers, (Ravana), entering his court, well knowing Rāma's prowess, set about his work.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तैः सार्धं मन्त्रिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः
समर्थयामास तदा रामकार्यविनिश्चयम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasendrastu taiḥ sārdhaṁ mantribhirbhīmavikramaiḥ
samarthayāmāsa tadā rāmakāryaviniścayam

translations.english: As soon as Rāvaņa left that place, that head and that bow vanished. And in company with the councillors of dreadful power, (Ravana) decided his course with reference to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अविदूरस्थितान्सर्वान्बलाध्यक्षान्हितैषिणः
अब्रवीत्कालसदृशो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
avidūrasthitānsarvānbalādhyakṣānhitaiṣiṇaḥ
abravītkālasadṛśo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: Then the lord of Raksasas, Ravana, resembling the day of doom, addressed his generals, all well-wishers-staying hard by, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रं भेरीनिनादेन स्फुटकोणाहतेन मे
समानयध्वं सैन्यानि वक्तव्यं च न कारणम्
verses.transliteration:
śīghraṁ bherīninādena sphuṭakoṇāhatena me
samānayadhvaṁ sainyāni vaktavyaṁ ca na kāraṇam

translations.english: Do you speedily summon my forces with the beat of drums—not do you give out the reason (of the summons).

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तथेति प्रतिगृह्य तद्वचो; बलाधिपास्ते महदात्मनो बलम्
समानयंश्चैव समागतं च ते; न्यवेदयन्भर्तरि युद्धकाङ्क्षिणि
verses.transliteration:
tatastatheti pratigṛhya tadvaco; balādhipāste mahadātmano balam
samānayaṁścaiva samāgataṁ ca te; nyavedayanbhartari yuddhakāṅkṣiṇi

translations.english: Then assenting to his speech with So be it, the envoys immediately summoned that mighty force; and, when in had arrived, they informed their master, eager for conflict, of its arrival.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतां तु मोहितां दृष्ट्वा सरमा नाम राक्षसी
आससादाशु वैदेहीं प्रियां प्रणयिनी सखी
verses.transliteration:
sītāṁ tu mohitāṁ dṛṣṭvā saramā nāma rākṣasī
āsasādāśu vaidehīṁ priyāṁ praṇayinī sakhī

translations.english: Seeing Sītā overwhelmed with grief, a Rākşasi, named Saramā, who was the beloved companion (of Sītā), drew near to his dear (friend), Vaidehi.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हि तत्र कृता मित्रं सीतया रक्ष्यमाणया
रक्षन्ती रावणादिष्टा सानुक्रोशा दृढव्रता
verses.transliteration:
sā hi tatra kṛtā mitraṁ sītayā rakṣyamāṇayā
rakṣantī rāvaṇādiṣṭā sānukrośā dṛḍhavratā

translations.english: Sītā, who was protected there (by Saramā), had been made a friend by her. And, protecting her at the command of Rāvana, that kind-hearted companion, firm in vows, saw Sītā, deprived of her consciousness. And she' comforted with a friend's affection that one of fair vows, who was rolling in the dust and rising up from it like a mare. 1. Saramă. 2. The commentator intelligently remarks. As a mare does, to remove fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
तां समाश्वासयामास सखी स्नेहेन सुव्रता
उक्ता यद्रावणेन त्वं प्रत्युक्तं च स्वयं त्वया
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ samāśvāsayāmāsa sakhī snehena suvratā
uktā yadrāvaṇena tvaṁ pratyuktaṁ ca svayaṁ tvayā

translations.english: Having come to the solitary wood for protecting you, I, renouncing all fear of Ravana, have, remaining hid, heard everything that he addressed to you, as well as what you had replied to him. For you, O you of expansive eyes, I have no fear of Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
स संभ्रान्तश्च निष्क्रान्तो यत्कृते राक्षसाधिपः
तच्च मे विदितं सर्वमभिनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलि
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁbhrāntaśca niṣkrānto yatkṛte rākṣasādhipaḥ
tacca me viditaṁ sarvamabhiniṣkramya maithili

translations.english: And, O Maithili, I, coming out, have also learnt well as to why the lord of Rākṣasas has gone out hence hurriedly.

verses.sanskrit:
न शक्यं सौप्तिकं कर्तुं रामस्य विदितात्मनः
वधश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रे तस्मिन्नेवोपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
na śakyaṁ sauptikaṁ kartuṁ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
vadhaśca puruṣavyāghre tasminnevopapadyate

translations.english: Rāma, acquainted with self, is incapable of being surprised in sleep; nor does the slaying of that tiger-like one commend itself to me as probable.

verses.sanskrit:
न चैव वानरा हन्तुं शक्याः पादपयोधिनः
सुरा देवर्षभेणेव रामेण हि सुरक्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
na caiva vānarā hantuṁ śakyāḥ pādapayodhinaḥ
surā devarṣabheṇeva rāmeṇa hi surakṣitāḥ

translations.english: The monkeys fighting with trees, well protected by Rāghava, like the gods protected by the foremost of the celestials, are incapable of being slain.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रान्तो रक्षिता नित्यमात्मनश्च परस्य च
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा कुशली नयशास्त्रवित्
verses.transliteration:
vikrānto rakṣitā nityamātmanaśca parasya ca
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā kuśalī nayaśāstravit

translations.english: And, possessed of arms long and rounded; graceful, broad-breasted; powerful; accoutred with the bow; and mailed; righteous; and famous over the earth; endowed with energy; and along with his brother, Lakşmaņa, ever protecting himself and others; of noble descent; and versed in polity; the destroyer of the hostile ranks; and of inconceivable strength and manhood, the graceful Răghava, O Sītā, slayer of foes, is not slain.

verses.sanskrit:
अयुक्तबुद्धिकृत्येन सर्वभूतविरोधिना
इयं प्रयुक्ता रौद्रेण माया मायाविदा त्वयि
verses.transliteration:
ayuktabuddhikṛtyena sarvabhūtavirodhinā
iyaṁ prayuktā raudreṇa māyā māyāvidā tvayi

translations.english: This illusion has been spread around you by that fierce, illusion-creating one, whose mind over runs upon improper acts and who oppose himself to all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
शोकस्ते विगतः सर्वः कल्याणं त्वामुपस्थितम्
ध्रुवं त्वां भजते लक्ष्मीः प्रियं प्रीतिकरं शृणु
verses.transliteration:
śokaste vigataḥ sarvaḥ kalyāṇaṁ tvāmupasthitam
dhruvaṁ tvāṁ bhajate lakṣmīḥ priyaṁ prītikaraṁ śṛṇu

translations.english: All your sorrow has departed, and your good day has dawned. Certainly Laksmi seek you. And, O lady, hearken to what is dear to you!

verses.sanskrit:
उत्तीर्य सागरं रामः सह वानरसेनया
संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्
verses.transliteration:
uttīrya sāgaraṁ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā
saṁniviṣṭaḥ samudrasya tīramāsādya dakṣiṇam

translations.english: Having crossed over the ocean, along with the monkey-host, Rāma has encamped himself on the southern shore of the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टो मे परिपूर्णार्थः काकुत्स्थः सहलक्ष्मणः
सहितैः सागरान्तस्थैर्बलैस्तिष्ठति रक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭo me paripūrṇārthaḥ kākutsthaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
sahitaiḥ sāgarāntasthairbalaistiṣṭhati rakṣitaḥ

translations.english: By me has been seen the complete Kākutstha along with Lakşmaņa, accompanied by the forces, stationed on the marge of the main, protected (by his native might).

verses.sanskrit:
अनेन प्रेषिता ये च राक्षसा लघुविक्रमः
राघवस्तीर्ण इत्येवं प्रवृत्तिस्तैरिहाहृता
verses.transliteration:
anena preṣitā ye ca rākṣasā laghuvikramaḥ
rāghavastīrṇa ityevaṁ pravṛttistairihāhṛtā

translations.english: Those Rākşasas of fleet vigour who had been despatched by this one, have brought the news that Rāghava has crossed.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां श्रुत्वा विशालाक्षि प्रवृत्तिं राक्षसाधिपः
एष मन्त्रयते सर्वैः सचिवैः सह रावणः
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ śrutvā viśālākṣi pravṛttiṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
eṣa mantrayate sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: And, O large-eyed lady, having learnt this news, Rāvaņa-lord of Rākşasas, is consulting with all his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणा सरमा राक्षसी सीतया सह
सर्वोद्योगेन सैन्यानां शब्दं शुश्राव भैरवम्
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇā saramā rākṣasī sītayā saha
sarvodyogena sainyānāṁ śabdaṁ śuśrāva bhairavam

translations.english: As the Rākşasī, Saramā, was relating this to Sita, she heard the leonine roars of the army, emitted with the greatest energy.

verses.sanskrit:
दण्डनिर्घातवादिन्याः श्रुत्वा भेर्या महास्वनम्
उवाच सरमा सीतामिदं मधुरभाषिणी
verses.transliteration:
daṇḍanirghātavādinyāḥ śrutvā bheryā mahāsvanam
uvāca saramā sītāmidaṁ madhurabhāṣiṇī

translations.english: Hearing the mighty sounds of kettledrums produced by sticks struck (thereon), the honeytongued Saramā spoke thus to Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
संनाहजननी ह्येषा भैरवा भीरु भेरिका
भेरीनादं च गम्भीरं शृणु तोयदनिस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁnāhajananī hyeṣā bhairavā bhīru bherikā
bherīnādaṁ ca gambhīraṁ śṛṇu toyadanisvanam

translations.english: These dreadful sounds of the kettledrum, O mother, call to arms. And hark to the solemn notes of the kettledrums, resembling the rumbling of clouds!

verses.sanskrit:
कल्प्यन्ते मत्तमातंगा युज्यन्ते रथवाजिनः
तत्र तत्र च संनद्धाः संपतन्ति पदातयः
verses.transliteration:
kalpyante mattamātaṁgā yujyante rathavājinaḥ
tatra tatra ca saṁnaddhāḥ saṁpatanti padātayaḥ

translations.english: The mad elephants are caparisoned and the car-horses are yoked; and thousands of warriors) are seen, mounted on steeds, with bearded darts in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
आपूर्यन्ते राजमार्गाः सैन्यैरद्भुतदर्शनैः
वेगवद्भिर्नदद्भिश्च तोयौघैरिव सागरः
verses.transliteration:
āpūryante rājamārgāḥ sainyairadbhutadarśanaiḥ
vegavadbhirnadadbhiśca toyaughairiva sāgaraḥ

translations.english: As waters fill up the ocean, mailed warriors of wonderful forms, vehement and roaring, by thousands rush out on all aides and fill the highways.

verses.sanskrit:
शास्त्राणां च प्रसन्नानां चर्मणां वर्मणां तथा
रथवाजिगजानां च भूषितानां च रक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
śāstrāṇāṁ ca prasannānāṁ carmaṇāṁ varmaṇāṁ tathā
rathavājigajānāṁ ca bhūṣitānāṁ ca rakṣasām

translations.english: And mark the splendour spread around by the polished arins and bucklers and mail, and by the cars, horses and elephants of the followers of the Rākşasa-chief, consisting of many hues shooting up, like to the appearance of a fire in summer, burning a forest, and also mark the excitement of the high-spirited and fast-coursing Raksasa! * *This line of verse defies all attempts to make it fall into syntactical order with the rest of the sentence. It is a hideous hiatus in the passage.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रीस्त्वां भजति शोकघ्नी रक्षसां भयमागतम्
रामात्कमलपत्राक्षि दैत्यानामिव वासवात्
verses.transliteration:
śrīstvāṁ bhajati śokaghnī rakṣasāṁ bhayamāgatam
rāmātkamalapatrākṣi daityānāmiva vāsavāt

translations.english: And fierce is the excitement of these Raksasas— followers of the Raksasa-cheif, with their hands bearing upraised arms, capable of making people's hair stand on end. The sorrow removing Sree espouse you, and the fear of the Rākşasa is come.

verses.sanskrit:
अवजित्य जितक्रोधस्तमचिन्त्यपराक्रमः
रावणं समरे हत्वा भर्ता त्वाधिगमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
avajitya jitakrodhastamacintyaparākramaḥ
rāvaṇaṁ samare hatvā bhartā tvādhigamiṣyati

translations.english: As Vasava did to the Daityas, the lotus-eyed Rāma, your lord-of controlled anger, and of inconceivable prowess, slaying Rävaņa in battle and thus delivering you, shall approach you.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्रमिष्यति रक्षःसु भर्ता ते सहलक्ष्मणः
यथा शत्रुषु शत्रुघ्नो विष्णुना सह वासवः
verses.transliteration:
vikramiṣyati rakṣaḥsu bhartā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
yathā śatruṣu śatrughno viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ

translations.english: And, as Väsava put forth his prowess among his foes, in company with the foe-destroying Visnu, your lord, along with Laksmana, shall display his prowess among the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
आगतस्य हि रामस्य क्षिप्रमङ्कगतां सतीम्
अहं द्रक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थां त्वां शत्रौ विनिपातिते
verses.transliteration:
āgatasya hi rāmasya kṣipramaṅkagatāṁ satīm
ahaṁ drakṣyāmi siddhārthāṁ tvāṁ śatrau vinipātite

translations.english: On the enemy having fallen, I shall behold you, devoted to your lord, with your desire attained, soon lying on the lap of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्रूण्यानन्दजानि त्वं वर्तयिष्यसि शोभने
समागम्य परिष्वक्ता तस्योरसि महोरसः
verses.transliteration:
aśrūṇyānandajāni tvaṁ vartayiṣyasi śobhane
samāgamya pariṣvaktā tasyorasi mahorasaḥ

translations.english: And, O Janaki, embracing (your lord) you shall shed tears of joy on his mighty breast.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिरान्मोक्ष्यते सीते देवि ते जघनं गताम्
धृतामेतां बहून्मासान्वेणीं रामो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
acirānmokṣyate sīte devi te jaghanaṁ gatām
dhṛtāmetāṁ bahūnmāsānveṇīṁ rāmo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: O Sitä, soon shall the highly powerful Răma loosen this braid of your reaching to your hips, which you have been wearing for many a month.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य दृष्ट्वा मुखं देवि पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्
मोक्ष्यसे शोकजं वारि निर्मोकमिव पन्नगी
verses.transliteration:
tasya dṛṣṭvā mukhaṁ devi pūrṇacandramivoditam
mokṣyase śokajaṁ vāri nirmokamiva pannagī

translations.english: O exalted one, seeing his face like the full moon risen, you shall shed water begot of ruth, even as a she-serpent casts off her slough.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं समरे हत्वा नचिरादेव मैथिलि
त्वया समग्रं प्रियया सुखार्हो लप्स्यते सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaṁ samare hatvā nacirādeva maithili
tvayā samagraṁ priyayā sukhārho lapsyate sukham

translations.english: O Mithila's daughter, speedily slaying Ravana in battle, that one worthy of happiness shall reap felicity in the company of you, his beloved.

verses.sanskrit:
समागता त्वं रामेण मोदिष्यसि महात्मना
सुवर्षेण समायुक्ता यथा सस्येन मेदिनी
verses.transliteration:
samāgatā tvaṁ rāmeṇa modiṣyasi mahātmanā
suvarṣeṇa samāyuktā yathā sasyena medinī

translations.english: And, loved by the high-souled Rama, you, shall be happy, even as the Earth furnished with crops brought forth by plenteous showers.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिवरमभितोऽनुवर्तमानो; हय इव मण्डलमाशु यः करोति
तमिह शरणमभ्युपेहि देवि; दिवसकरं प्रभवो ह्ययं प्रजानाम्
verses.transliteration:
girivaramabhito'nuvartamāno; haya iva maṇḍalamāśu yaḥ karoti
tamiha śaraṇamabhyupehi devi; divasakaraṁ prabhavo hyayaṁ prajānām

translations.english: Do you, O exalted one, take refuge with him, who, going round the foremost of mountains, speedily assume a steed-like circular movement; for even the maker of day is the source of people's joy and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तां जातसंतापां तेन वाक्येन मोहिताम्
सरमा ह्लादयामास पृतिवीं द्यौरिवाम्भसा
verses.transliteration:
atha tāṁ jātasaṁtāpāṁ tena vākyena mohitām
saramā hlādayāmāsa pṛtivīṁ dyaurivāmbhasā

translations.english: Burning with grief on account of those words,* Sarama gladdened and cheered her, even as masses of clouds (cheer up) the burning Earth. *i.e.the words of Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तस्या हितं सख्याश्चिकीर्षन्ती सखी वचः
उवाच काले कालज्ञा स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी
verses.transliteration:
tatastasyā hitaṁ sakhyāścikīrṣantī sakhī vacaḥ
uvāca kāle kālajñā smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇī

translations.english: Then, desirous of doing her good, (Sita's) friend, conversant with season, and ever precluding her speech with a smile, spoke to her seasonably.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सहेयमहं गत्वा त्वद्वाक्यमसितेक्षणे
निवेद्य कुशलं रामे प्रतिच्छन्ना निवर्तितुम्
verses.transliteration:
utsaheyamahaṁ gatvā tvadvākyamasitekṣaṇe
nivedya kuśalaṁ rāme praticchannā nivartitum

translations.english: O you having dark eyes, I can, secretly going to Rama and communicating to him your auspicious words, come back clandestinely.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे क्रममाणाया निरालम्बे विहायसि
समर्थो गतिमन्वेतुं पवनो गरुडोऽपि वा
verses.transliteration:
na hi me kramamāṇāyā nirālambe vihāyasi
samartho gatimanvetuṁ pavano garuḍo'pi vā

translations.english: Nor, when I course the supportless sky, can even the Wind or Garuda follow me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणां तां सीता सरमां पुनरब्रवीत्
मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पूर्वशोकाभिपन्नया
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇāṁ tāṁ sītā saramāṁ punarabravīt
madhuraṁ ślakṣṇayā vācā pūrvaśokābhipannayā

translations.english: As she said this, Sita with her grief a little lightened, said to Sarama in sweet and smooth words.

verses.sanskrit:
समर्था गगनं गन्तुमपि वा त्वं रसातलम्
अवगच्छाम्यकर्तव्यं कर्तव्यं ते मदन्तरे
verses.transliteration:
samarthā gaganaṁ gantumapi vā tvaṁ rasātalam
avagacchāmyakartavyaṁ kartavyaṁ te madantare

translations.english: You are capable of even going to the nethermost regions. But do you on my behalf that which is fit to be done by you.

verses.sanskrit:
मत्प्रियं यदि कर्तव्यं यदि बुद्धिः स्थिरा तव
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तं गत्वा किं करोतीति रावणः
verses.transliteration:
matpriyaṁ yadi kartavyaṁ yadi buddhiḥ sthirā tava
jñātumicchāmi taṁ gatvā kiṁ karotīti rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: If you intend doing me a good turn, and if your sense be steady, I would know what Ravana is doing after having left this place.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि मायाबलः क्रूरो रावणः शत्रुरावणः
मां मोहयति दुष्टात्मा पीतमात्रेव वारुणी
verses.transliteration:
sa hi māyābalaḥ krūro rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
māṁ mohayati duṣṭātmā pītamātreva vāruṇī

translations.english: That guileful and wicked-minded one, Rāvana, destroyer of enemies, having powers of illusion, overwhelms me even as the Vāruni just drunk.

verses.sanskrit:
तर्जापयति मां नित्यं भर्त्सापयति चासकृत्
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्या मां रक्षन्ति नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
tarjāpayati māṁ nityaṁ bhartsāpayati cāsakṛt
rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhiryā māṁ rakṣanti nityaśaḥ

translations.english: Confining me here for ever and a day, (Rāvana) sets on dreadful Räksnasas to alike threaten and scold me constantly.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्विग्ना शङ्किता चास्मि न च स्वस्थं मनो मम
तद्भयाच्चाहमुद्विग्ना अशोकवनिकां गताः
verses.transliteration:
udvignā śaṅkitā cāsmi na ca svasthaṁ mano mama
tadbhayāccāhamudvignā aśokavanikāṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: And I am agitated and alarmed and my mind is (always) uneasy. And I, dwelling in the Asoka wood, is ever agitated.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्
निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तत्परो मे स्यादनुग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
yadi nāma kathā tasya niścitaṁ vāpi yadbhavet
nivedayethāḥ sarvaṁ tatparo me syādanugrahaḥ

translations.english: If there is any talk (of delivering me), or keeping me confined, you should communicate to me the decision arrived at.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वेवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां सरमा वल्गुभाषिणी
उवाच वचनं तस्याः स्पृशन्ती बाष्पविक्लवम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tvevaṁ bruvatīṁ sītāṁ saramā valgubhāṣiṇī
uvāca vacanaṁ tasyāḥ spṛśantī bāṣpaviklavam

translations.english: This is the highest favour that I seek (at hands). Thereat, the mild-speeched Saramā, wiping (Sītā's) face washed in tears, spoke to her, as she said this.

verses.sanskrit:
एष ते यद्यभिप्रायस्तस्माद्गच्छामि जानकि
गृह्य शत्रोरभिप्रायमुपावृत्तां च पश्य माम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa te yadyabhiprāyastasmādgacchāmi jānaki
gṛhya śatrorabhiprāyamupāvṛttāṁ ca paśya mām

translations.english: If this is your wish, I will go, O Jānaki. O Mithila's daughter, having possessed myself of the intent of the enemy, I shall come back.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो गत्वा समीपं तस्य रक्षसः
शुश्राव कथितं तस्य रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato gatvā samīpaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ
śuśrāva kathitaṁ tasya rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ

translations.english: Having said this, (Saramā), repairing to the Raksasa, heard Raksa, heard Ravana's converse with his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
सा श्रुत्वा निश्चयं तस्य निश्चयज्ञा दुरात्मनः
पुनरेवागमत्क्षिप्रमशोकवनिकां तदा
verses.transliteration:
sā śrutvā niścayaṁ tasya niścayajñā durātmanaḥ
punarevāgamatkṣipramaśokavanikāṁ tadā

translations.english: Having heard of the decision of that wickedminded one, she, understanding decisions, swiftly retraced her steps to the fair Asoka forest.

verses.sanskrit:
सा प्रविष्टा पुनस्तत्र ददर्श जनकात्मजाम्
प्रतीक्षमाणां स्वामेव भ्रष्टपद्मामिव श्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
sā praviṣṭā punastatra dadarśa janakātmajām
pratīkṣamāṇāṁ svāmeva bhraṣṭapadmāmiva śriyam

translations.english: Then, entering there, she saw Janaka's daughter, expecting (her) like a very Sri,, bereft of her lotus.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु सीता पुनः प्राप्तां सरमां वल्गुभाषिणीम्
परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धं ददौ च स्वयमासनम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu sītā punaḥ prāptāṁ saramāṁ valgubhāṣiṇīm
pariṣvajya ca susnigdhaṁ dadau ca svayamāsanam

translations.english: And, the fair-spoken Sarama, on getting back (near her), Sītā, embracing her affectionately, herself gave her a seat.

verses.sanskrit:
इहासीना सुखं सर्वमाख्याहि मम तत्त्वतः
क्रूरस्य निश्चयं तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
ihāsīnā sukhaṁ sarvamākhyāhi mama tattvataḥ
krūrasya niścayaṁ tasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ

translations.english: Sitting down here at ease, do you relate to me faithfully all about the determination of the wicked-minded and guileful Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सरमा सीतया वेपमानया
कथितं सर्वमाचष्ट रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu saramā sītayā vepamānayā
kathitaṁ sarvamācaṣṭa rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by the trembling Sītä, Saramā related everything that had been said by Råvaņa and his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
जनन्या राक्षसेन्द्रो वै त्वन्मोक्षार्थं बृहद्वचः
अविद्धेन च वैदेहि मन्त्रिवृद्धेन बोधितः
verses.transliteration:
jananyā rākṣasendro vai tvanmokṣārthaṁ bṛhadvacaḥ
aviddhena ca vaidehi mantrivṛddhena bodhitaḥ

translations.english: O Vaidehi, the Rākşasa lord was advised by his mother and the aged counsellors in pregnant words informed with affection, having your deliverance for their object.

verses.sanskrit:
दीयतामभिसत्कृत्य मनुजेन्द्राय मैथिली
निदर्शनं ते पर्याप्तं जनस्थाने यदद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration:
dīyatāmabhisatkṛtya manujendrāya maithilī
nidarśanaṁ te paryāptaṁ janasthāne yadadbhutam

translations.english: Do you make over Maithili to the king of men, paying him homage due. You have in Janasthāna profusely witnessed wonderful instances (of his prowess).

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य दर्शनं च हनूमतः
वधं च रक्षसां युद्धे कः कुर्यान्मानुषो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
laṅghanaṁ ca samudrasya darśanaṁ ca hanūmataḥ
vadhaṁ ca rakṣasāṁ yuddhe kaḥ kuryānmānuṣo bhuvi

translations.english: The crossing of the ocean, Hanuman's sight (of Sītā) and the slaughter of the Rākşasa in fight, what person is capable of doing all this in battle?

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स मन्त्रिवृद्धैश्च मात्रा च बहु भाषितः
न त्वामुत्सहते मोक्तुमर्तह्मर्थपरो यथा
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa mantrivṛddhaiśca mātrā ca bahu bhāṣitaḥ
na tvāmutsahate moktumartahmarthaparo yathā

translations.english: Thus long exhorted by his counsellors as well as his mother, Rāvaņa does not make up his mind to emancipate you, even as a covetous person is loath to pare with wealth (appropriated).

verses.sanskrit:
तदेषा सुस्थिरा बुद्धिर्मृत्युलोभादुपस्थिता
भयान्न शक्तस्त्वां मोक्तुमनिरस्तस्तु संयुगे
राक्षसानां च सर्वेषामात्मनश्च वधेन हि
verses.transliteration:
tadeṣā susthirā buddhirmṛtyulobhādupasthitā
bhayānna śaktastvāṁ moktumanirastastu saṁyuge
rākṣasānāṁ ca sarveṣāmātmanaśca vadhena hi

translations.english: O Maithili, without renouncing his life in battle, he does not intend to liberate you. Even this is the determination which that cruel one has arrived at along with his advisers. This intent is in consequence of their coveting surcease. He can not yield you up from sheer fear; not is he backward in battle, or shirk his own destruction or that of all the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य रावणं संख्ये सर्वथा निशितैः शरैः
प्रतिनेष्यति रामस्त्वामयोध्यामसितेक्षणे
verses.transliteration:
nihatya rāvaṇaṁ saṁkhye sarvathā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
pratineṣyati rāmastvāmayodhyāmasitekṣaṇe

translations.english: O dark-eyed lady slaying Rāvaņa in battle with sharp shafts, Rāma shall take the back to Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शब्दो भेरीशङ्खसमाकुलः
श्रुतो वै सर्वसैन्यानां कम्पयन्धरणीतलम्
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare śabdo bherīśaṅkhasamākulaḥ
śruto vai sarvasainyānāṁ kampayandharaṇītalam

translations.english: In the meanwhile there was heard a mighty uproar occasioned by the whole host, and drums and conchs, which shook the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु तं वानरसैन्यशब्दं; लङ्कागता राक्षसराजभृत्याः
नष्टौजसो दैन्यपरीतचेष्टाः; श्रेयो न पश्यन्ति नृपस्य दोषैः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu taṁ vānarasainyaśabdaṁ; laṅkāgatā rākṣasarājabhṛtyāḥ
naṣṭaujaso dainyaparītaceṣṭāḥ; śreyo na paśyanti nṛpasya doṣaiḥ

translations.english: Hearing that hubbub of the monkey-army, the servants of the Råkşasa monarch, ran who were in Lankā, growing dispirited, and bereft of energy, with weakness overcoming their powers, did not see any good, in consequence of the fault of the ruler.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शङ्खविमिश्रेण भेरीशब्देन राघवः
उपयतो महाबाहू रामः परपुरंजयः
verses.transliteration:
tena śaṅkhavimiśreṇa bherīśabdena rāghavaḥ
upayato mahābāhū rāmaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ

translations.english: That captor of hostile capitals, the mightarmed Rāma, was advancing (upon Larikā) with the sounds of drums mixed with the blares of conchs.

verses.sanskrit:
तं निनादं निशम्याथ रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थाय सचिवानभ्युदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
taṁ ninādaṁ niśamyātha rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
muhūrtaṁ dhyānamāsthāya sacivānabhyudaikṣata

translations.english: Hearing this noise, Ravana-lord of Raks asas-reflecting for a while, cast his eyes upon his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तान्सचिवांस्तत्र सर्वानाभाष्य रावणः
सभां संनादयन्सर्वामित्युवाच महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
atha tānsacivāṁstatra sarvānābhāṣya rāvaṇaḥ
sabhāṁ saṁnādayansarvāmityuvāca mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Addressing there all those counsellors, that afflictor of the world—the crooked and highly powerful lord of the Rākşasas, Rāvaņa, making his court resound, running down (Rāma's) crossing the main, as well as his vigour, strength and manhood, said to them.

verses.sanskrit:
तरणं सागरस्यापि विक्रमं बलसंचयम्
यदुक्तवन्तो रामस्य भवन्तस्तन्मया श्रुतम्
भवतश्चाप्यहं वेद्मि युद्धे सत्यपराक्रमान्
verses.transliteration:
taraṇaṁ sāgarasyāpi vikramaṁ balasaṁcayam
yaduktavanto rāmasya bhavantastanmayā śrutam
bhavataścāpyahaṁ vedmi yuddhe satyaparākramān

translations.english: What you have said touching Rama's (prowess), has been heard by me. And I also know you to be of sterling valour in the field. Yet why, knowing Rāma's prowess, do you silently look at each other?

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु सुमहाप्राज्ञो माल्यवान्नाम राक्षसः
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मातुः पैतामहोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu sumahāprājño mālyavānnāma rākṣasaḥ
rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ paitāmaho'bravīt

translations.english: Then the maternal grand sire (of Rāvaņa), possessed of exceeding wisdom, named Malyavān, hearing his words, said.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्यास्वभिविनीतो यो राजा राजन्नयानुगः
स शास्ति चिरमैश्वर्यमरींश्च कुरुते वशे
verses.transliteration:
vidyāsvabhivinīto yo rājā rājannayānugaḥ
sa śāsti ciramaiśvaryamarīṁśca kurute vaśe

translations.english: The king that is accomplished in the various kinds of learning,* and that follow polity, ever command affluence and bring his enemies under his subjection. *The commentator says there are four and ten kinds of learning; but unfortunately he does not enumerate them.

verses.sanskrit:
संदधानो हि कालेन विगृह्णंश्चारिभिः सह
स्वपक्षवर्धनं कुर्वन्महदैश्वर्यमश्नुते
verses.transliteration:
saṁdadhāno hi kālena vigṛhṇaṁścāribhiḥ saha
svapakṣavardhanaṁ kurvanmahadaiśvaryamaśnute

translations.english: He that seasonably concludes peace and carries on war with his enemies, and who advances his own party, attain great affluence.

verses.sanskrit:
हीयमानेन कर्तव्यो राज्ञा संधिः समेन च
न शत्रुमवमन्येत ज्यायान्कुर्वीत विग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
hīyamānena kartavyo rājñā saṁdhiḥ samena ca
na śatrumavamanyeta jyāyānkurvīta vigraham

translations.english: A king should enter into peace, if he be an equal or inferior of his adversary, and engage in war, if be more powerful, but an enemy should never be disergarded.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्मह्यं रोचते संधिः सह रामेण रावण
यदर्थमभियुक्ताः स्म सीता तस्मै प्रदीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
tanmahyaṁ rocate saṁdhiḥ saha rāmeṇa rāvaṇa
yadarthamabhiyuktāḥ sma sītā tasmai pradīyatām

translations.english: Therefore, O Rāvana, peace with Rāma is what commends itself to me; and do you render to him that for which you have been invaded (by him), viz., Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य देवर्षयः सर्वे गन्धर्वाश्च जयैषिणः
विरोधं मा गमस्तेन संधिस्ते तेन रोचताम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya devarṣayaḥ sarve gandharvāśca jayaiṣiṇaḥ
virodhaṁ mā gamastena saṁdhiste tena rocatām
