translations.english: And from the persons of the Räkşasas and the monkeys there flowed a river of gore, having hair for grass (growing on its banks) and the bodies of the warriors for pieces of planks floating (a down the current).

verses.sanskrit:
आजघानेन्द्रजित्क्रुद्धो वज्रेणेव शतक्रतुः
अङ्गदं गदया वीरं शत्रुसैन्यविदारणम्
verses.transliteration:
ājaghānendrajitkruddho vajreṇeva śatakratuḥ
aṅgadaṁ gadayā vīraṁ śatrusainyavidāraṇam

translations.english: Indrajit, growing enraged, with his mace dealt a blow at that tearer of hostile ranks, angada, like him of an hundred sacrifices striking with his · thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं रथं साश्वं ससारथिम्
जघान समरे श्रीमानङ्गदो वेगवान्कपिः
verses.transliteration:
tasya kāñcanacitrāṅgaṁ rathaṁ sāśvaṁ sasārathim
jaghāna samare śrīmānaṅgado vegavānkapiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, that graceful monkey, Angada, gifted with vehemence, with his mace crushed his car decked in gold, together with the steeds and the charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
संपातिस्तु त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रजङ्घेन समाहतः
निजघानाश्वकर्णेन प्रजङ्घं रणमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
saṁpātistu tribhirbāṇaiḥ prajaṅghena samāhataḥ
nijaghānāśvakarṇena prajaṅghaṁ raṇamūrdhani

translations.english: Sampāti was pierced with three arrows by Prajangha; and the former (in his turn) slew Prajangha on the edge of battle with an Ašvakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
जम्बूमाली रथस्थस्तु रथशक्त्या महाबलः
बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धो हनूमन्तं स्तनान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
jambūmālī rathasthastu rathaśaktyā mahābalaḥ
bibheda samare kruddho hanūmantaṁ stanāntare

translations.english: And Jambumali, mounted on a car, possessed of prodigious strength, fired with wrath, with all the access of force derived from his car wounded Hanumān between his paps.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तं रथमास्थाय हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
प्रममाथ तलेनाशु सह तेनैव रक्षसा
verses.transliteration:
tasya taṁ rathamāsthāya hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
pramamātha talenāśu saha tenaiva rakṣasā

translations.english: Thereat, getting at his car, Hanumān-son to the Wind-god with a slap speedily crushed his adversary's vehicle along with the Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
भिन्नगात्रः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः क्षिप्रहस्तेन रक्षसा
प्रजघानाद्रिशृङ्गेण तपनं मुष्टिना गजः
verses.transliteration:
bhinnagātraḥ śaraistīkṣṇaiḥ kṣiprahastena rakṣasā
prajaghānādriśṛṅgeṇa tapanaṁ muṣṭinā gajaḥ

translations.english: Then the terrific Pratapana, roaring, rushed at Nala; and thereat Nala, with his body pierced with sharp shafts by that swift handed Rākşasa, plucked out Pratapana's eyes, and cast them to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ग्रसन्तमिव सैन्यानि प्रघसं वानराधिपः
सुग्रीवः सप्तपर्णेन निर्बिभेद जघान च
verses.transliteration:
grasantamiva sainyāni praghasaṁ vānarādhipaḥ
sugrīvaḥ saptaparṇena nirbibheda jaghāna ca

translations.english: That lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, with a Saptaparma-swiftly slew Praghasa, who appeared to be devouring up the troops.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रपीड्य शरवर्षेण राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्
निजघान विरूपाक्षं शरेणैकेन लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
prapīḍya śaravarṣeṇa rākṣasaṁ bhīmadarśanam
nijaghāna virūpākṣaṁ śareṇaikena lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Tormenting the Räkşasa Virupākṣa of dreadful form, Laksmana killed him with a single arrow.

verses.sanskrit:
अग्निकेतुश्च दुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च राक्षसः
सुप्तिघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च रामं निर्बिभिदुः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
agniketuśca durdharṣo raśmiketuśca rākṣasaḥ
suptighno yajñakopaśca rāmaṁ nirbibhiduḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: The irrepressible Agniketu, the Rākṣasas Raśmiketu, Mitraghna and Yajñakopa, with their arrows rendered Rāma aflame.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां चतुर्णां रामस्तु शिरांसि समरे शरैः
क्रुद्धश्चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेद घोरैरग्निशिखोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ caturṇāṁ rāmastu śirāṁsi samare śaraiḥ
kruddhaścaturbhiściccheda ghorairagniśikhopamaiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, Rāma, growing wroth, in battle severed the heads of those four by means of four shafts, dreadful, and resembling the tongues of a fame.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रमुष्टिस्तु मैन्देन मुष्टिना निहतो रणे
पपात सरथः साश्वः पुराट्ट इव भूतले
verses.transliteration:
vajramuṣṭistu maindena muṣṭinā nihato raṇe
papāta sarathaḥ sāśvaḥ purāṭṭa iva bhūtale

translations.english: Vajramuști was slain in conflict by Mainda with a clenched fist; and down came he to the ground along with his car and horses, like a turret toppling (headlong.)

verses.sanskrit:
वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शो द्विविदोऽप्यशनिप्रभम्
जघान गिरिशृङ्गेण मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
vajrāśanisamasparśo dvivido'pyaśaniprabham
jaghāna giriśṛṅgeṇa miṣatāṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: Dvivida, possessed of the touch of the Vajra and thunder bolt, in the presence of the entire Rākşasas host hurled a mountain-peak at him that was endowed with the splendour of the thunder bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विविदं वानरेन्द्रं तु द्रुमयोधिनमाहवे
शरैरशनिसंकाशैः स विव्याधाशनिप्रभः
verses.transliteration:
dvividaṁ vānarendraṁ tu drumayodhinamāhave
śarairaśanisaṁkāśaiḥ sa vivyādhāśaniprabhaḥ

translations.english: Asaniprabha in encounter pierced that foremost of monkeys bearer of trees in conflict, Dvivida, with shafts resembling thunder-bolts.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरैरतिविद्धाङ्गो द्विविदः क्रोधमूर्छितः
सालेन सरथं साश्वं निजघानाशनिप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
sa śarairatividdhāṅgo dvividaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
sālena sarathaṁ sāśvaṁ nijaghānāśaniprabham

translations.english: Thereat, beside himself with wrath, with his entire body wounded with arrows, Dvivida with a sala destroyed Asaniprabha along with his car and horses.

verses.sanskrit:
निकुम्भस्तु रणे नीलं नीलाञ्जनचयप्रभम्
निर्बिभेद शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः करैर्मेघमिवांशुमान्
verses.transliteration:
nikumbhastu raṇe nīlaṁ nīlāñjanacayaprabham
nirbibheda śaraistīkṣṇaiḥ karairmeghamivāṁśumān

translations.english: Nikumbha in fight wounded Nila resembling a mass of blue collyrium, with sharpened shafts, as the Sun pierce clouds with his rays.

verses.sanskrit:
पुनः शरशतेनाथ क्षिप्रहस्तो निशाचरः
बिभेद समरे नीलं निकुम्भः प्रजहास च
verses.transliteration:
punaḥ śaraśatenātha kṣiprahasto niśācaraḥ
bibheda samare nīlaṁ nikumbhaḥ prajahāsa ca

translations.english: Again with an hundred arrows, that lighthanded night-ranger pierced Nīla in the field; and Nikumbha laughed thereat.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैव रथचक्रेण नीलो विष्णुरिवाहवे
शिरश्चिच्छेद समरे निकुम्भस्य च सारथेः
verses.transliteration:
tasyaiva rathacakreṇa nīlo viṣṇurivāhave
śiraściccheda samare nikumbhasya ca sāratheḥ

translations.english: At this, even as Visnu did in battle, Nila with a wheel of his car, cut off in conflict Nikumbha's head together with that of his charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्युन्माली रथस्थस्तु शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः
सुषेणं ताडयामास ननाद च मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
vidyunmālī rathasthastu śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ
suṣeṇaṁ tāḍayāmāsa nanāda ca muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: And Vidyanmālī, mounted on a car, assailed Suşeņa with shafts decked with gold, and behan to shout momentarily.

verses.sanskrit:
तं रथस्थमथो दृष्ट्वा सुषेणो वानरोत्तमः
गिरिशृङ्गेण महता रथमाशु न्यपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ rathasthamatho dṛṣṭvā suṣeṇo vānarottamaḥ
giriśṛṅgeṇa mahatā rathamāśu nyapātayat

translations.english: Seeing him mounted on his car, Suşena-best of monkeys-taking up a huge crag, swiftly brought his car down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
लाघवेन तु संयुक्तो विद्युन्माली निशाचरः
अपक्रम्य रथात्तूर्णं गदापाणिः क्षितौ स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
lāghavena tu saṁyukto vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ
apakramya rathāttūrṇaṁ gadāpāṇiḥ kṣitau sthitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, endowed with lightness, that nightranger, Vidyunmāli, at once extricating himself from his car, stood on the ground with a mace in his hand.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टः सुषेणो हरिपुंगवः
शिलां सुमहतीं गृह्य निशाचरमभिद्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ suṣeṇo haripuṁgavaḥ
śilāṁ sumahatīṁ gṛhya niśācaramabhidravat

translations.english: Thereupon that foremost of monkeys, Sușeņa, growing furious, taking up a gigantic crag, rushed at the night-ranger.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं गदया विद्युन्माली निशाचरः
वक्षस्यभिजग्नानाशु सुषेणं हरिसत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ gadayā vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ
vakṣasyabhijagnānāśu suṣeṇaṁ harisattamam

translations.english: As he was descending, the night-ranger, Vidyunmālī, with his mace swiftly hit at the breast of Susena-greatest of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
गदाप्रहारं तं घोरमचिन्त्यप्लवगोत्तमः
तां शिलां पातयामास तस्योरसि महामृधे
verses.transliteration:
gadāprahāraṁ taṁ ghoramacintyaplavagottamaḥ
tāṁ śilāṁ pātayāmāsa tasyorasi mahāmṛdhe

translations.english: Thereat, without thinking at all of the terrific hit of the mace, that best of monkeys in mighty conflict brought down that upon his head.

verses.sanskrit:
शिलाप्रहाराभिहतो विद्युन्माली निशाचरः
निष्पिष्टहृदयो भूमौ गतासुर्निपपात ह
verses.transliteration:
śilāprahārābhihato vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ
niṣpiṣṭahṛdayo bhūmau gatāsurnipapāta ha

translations.english: Assailed with the crag, the night-ranger Vidyanmali, having his chest crushed, fell down to the earth, deprived of life.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं तैर्वानरैः शूरैः शूरास्ते रजनीचराः
द्वन्द्वे विमृदितास्तत्र दैत्या इव दिवौकसैः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tairvānaraiḥ śūraiḥ śūrāste rajanīcarāḥ
dvandve vimṛditāstatra daityā iva divaukasaiḥ

translations.english: Like the celestials warring against the Daityas, the heroic monkeys warred on and confounded the valiant rangers of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
निहतैः कुञ्जरैर्मत्तैस्तथा वानरराक्षसैः
चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्च भग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः
बभूवायोधनं घोरं गोमायुगणसेवितम्
verses.transliteration:
nihataiḥ kuñjarairmattaistathā vānararākṣasaiḥ
cakrākṣayugadaṇḍaiśca bhagnairdharaṇisaṁśritaiḥ
babhūvāyodhanaṁ ghoraṁ gomāyugaṇasevitam

translations.english: And frightful was the field of battle, with darts, and other arms; and clubs, and javelins, and lances, and other weapons, and with broken cars, and war-horses, and mad horses slain, and monkeys and Rākşasas, and wheels and Akşas, and yokes and standards, broken and scattered over the ground; and swarms of jackals began to range on all sides of the monkeys and the Raksasas; and Kabandhas began to rise in that terrific encounter, resembling the encounter of the gods and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
विदार्यमाणा हरिपुंगवैस्तदा; निशाचराः शोणितदिग्धगात्राः
पुनः सुयुद्धं तरसा समाश्रिता; दिवाकरस्यास्तमयाभिकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
vidāryamāṇā haripuṁgavaistadā; niśācarāḥ śoṇitadigdhagātrāḥ
punaḥ suyuddhaṁ tarasā samāśritā; divākarasyāstamayābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: Thus destroyed by the foremost of monkeys, the rangers of night, beyond themselves with the smell of blood, eagerly wishing for the setting of the Sun, again made active preparation for a renewal of the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यतामेव तेषां तु तदा वानररक्षसाम्
रविरस्तं गतो रात्रिः प्रवृत्ता प्राणहारिणी
verses.transliteration:
yudhyatāmeva teṣāṁ tu tadā vānararakṣasām
ravirastaṁ gato rātriḥ pravṛttā prāṇahāriṇī

translations.english: As the monkeys and the Rākşasas thus faught on, the sun set, ant the fatal Night came.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यं बद्धवैराणां घोराणां जयमिच्छताम्
संप्रवृत्तं निशायुद्धं तदा वारणरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
anyonyaṁ baddhavairāṇāṁ ghorāṇāṁ jayamicchatām
saṁpravṛttaṁ niśāyuddhaṁ tadā vāraṇarakṣasām

translations.english: Then commenced a night-engagement between the dreadful Rākşasas and the monkeys of fixed hostility, each party burning for victory.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसोऽसीति हरयो हरिश्चासीति राक्षसाः
अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुस्तस्मिंस्तमसि दारुणे
verses.transliteration:
rākṣaso'sīti harayo hariścāsīti rākṣasāḥ
anyonyaṁ samare jaghnustasmiṁstamasi dāruṇe

translations.english: In that profound darkness, the monkeys and the Rākşasas began to slay each other, exclaiming, You are a Raksasa,' and 'you are a monkey.'

verses.sanskrit:
जहि दारय चैतीति कथं विद्रवसीति च
एवं सुतुमुलः शब्दस्तस्मिंस्तमसि शुश्रुवे
verses.transliteration:
jahi dāraya caitīti kathaṁ vidravasīti ca
evaṁ sutumulaḥ śabdastasmiṁstamasi śuśruve

translations.english: And in that army there was heard a mighty uproar of 'slain,' 'rive!" 'come!' 'why fliest?'

verses.sanskrit:
कालाः काञ्चनसंनाहास्तस्मिंस्तमसि राक्षसाः
संप्रादृश्यन्त शैलेन्द्रा दीप्तौषधिवना इव
verses.transliteration:
kālāḥ kāñcanasaṁnāhāstasmiṁstamasi rākṣasāḥ
saṁprādṛśyanta śailendrā dīptauṣadhivanā iva

translations.english: And, dark-hued, the Raksasas, equipped in golden mail, in that deep darkness appeared like elevated hills clad with woods of flaming incdicinal herbs.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिंस्तमसि दुष्पारे राक्षसाः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
परिपेतुर्महावेगा भक्षयन्तः प्लवंगमान्
verses.transliteration:
tasmiṁstamasi duṣpāre rākṣasāḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
paripeturmahāvegā bhakṣayantaḥ plavaṁgamān

translations.english: And in that limitless gloom, the Rākṣasas, transported with wrath, advanced with impetuous speed, devouring monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ते हयान्काञ्चनापीडन्ध्वजांश्चाग्निशिखोपमान्
आप्लुत्य दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भीमकोपा व्यदारयन्
verses.transliteration:
te hayānkāñcanāpīḍandhvajāṁścāgniśikhopamān
āplutya daśanaistīkṣṇairbhīmakopā vyadārayan

translations.english: And, fired with terrible wrath, they, bounding up, with their sharp tecih tore up steeds caparisoned in gold, and standards resembling venomous serpents. *i.e. the monkeys, as appears from the context.

verses.sanskrit:
कुञ्जरान्कुञ्जरारोहान्पताकाध्वजिनो रथान्
चकर्षुश्च ददंशुश्च दशनैः क्रोधमूर्छिताः
verses.transliteration:
kuñjarānkuñjarārohānpatākādhvajino rathān
cakarṣuśca dadaṁśuśca daśanaiḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ

translations.english: The lusty monkeys in battle agitated the Rāks asa host, and, waxing furious, with their teeth pulled and bit elephants and the riders there of, and cars furnished with flags and standards.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामश्च शरैराशीविषोमपैः
दृश्यादृश्यानि रक्षांसि प्रवराणि निजघ्नतुः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaścāpi rāmaśca śarairāśīviṣomapaiḥ
dṛśyādṛśyāni rakṣāṁsi pravarāṇi nijaghnatuḥ

translations.english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with shafts resembling venomous serpents, slaughtered the foremost among the Rakşasas-both those that were seen and those that were not.

verses.sanskrit:
तुरंगखुरविध्वस्तं रथनेमिसमुद्धतम्
रुरोध कर्णनेत्राणिण्युध्यतां धरणीरजः
verses.transliteration:
turaṁgakhuravidhvastaṁ rathanemisamuddhatam
rurodha karṇanetrāṇiṇyudhyatāṁ dharaṇīrajaḥ

translations.english: The dust of the earth arising from warring combatants, and from the hoofs of horses and the wheels of cars, choked up eye and ear.

verses.sanskrit:
वर्तमाने तथा घोरे संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे
रुधिरोदा महावेगा नद्यस्तत्र प्रसुस्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
vartamāne tathā ghore saṁgrāme lomaharṣaṇe
rudhirodā mahāvegā nadyastatra prasusruvuḥ

translations.english: And as the mighty envounter, capable of making people's hair stand on end, went on, there flowed a fearful river of gore.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भेरीमृदङ्गानां पणवानां च निस्वनः
शङ्खवेणुस्वनोन्मिश्रः संबभूवाद्भुतोपमः
verses.transliteration:
tato bherīmṛdaṅgānāṁ paṇavānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
śaṅkhaveṇusvanonmiśraḥ saṁbabhūvādbhutopamaḥ

translations.english: The sounds of kettle-drums and Mşdangas and Panavas, mingled with those of conchs and carwheels, were wonderful (to hear).

verses.sanskrit:
हतानां स्तनमानानां राक्षसानां च निस्वनः
शस्त्राणां वानराणां च संबभूवातिदारुणः
verses.transliteration:
hatānāṁ stanamānānāṁ rākṣasānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
śastrāṇāṁ vānarāṇāṁ ca saṁbabhūvātidāruṇaḥ

translations.english: The sounds of steeds neighing, and Rāks asas (roaring) and monkeys, rejoicing, were something tremendous.

verses.sanskrit:
शस्त्रपुष्पोपहारा च तत्रासीद्युद्धमेदिनी
दुर्ज्ञेया दुर्निवेशा च शोणितास्रवकर्दमा
verses.transliteration:
śastrapuṣpopahārā ca tatrāsīdyuddhamedinī
durjñeyā durniveśā ca śoṇitāsravakardamā

translations.english: And, with able monkeys slain; and darts and javelins and axes; and slaughtered Raksasa wearing forms at pleasure, lying mountain likethe field of battle, seeming to have offerings of arms representing flowers, became difficult to recognise, and inaccessible; and the earth was drenched with streams of blood.

verses.sanskrit:
सा बभूव निशा घोरा हरिराक्षसहारिणी
कालरात्रीव भूतानां सर्वेषां दुरतिक्रमा
verses.transliteration:
sā babhūva niśā ghorā harirākṣasahāriṇī
kālarātrīva bhūtānāṁ sarveṣāṁ duratikramā

translations.english: That Night, destructive to monkeys and Rākş asas, was dreadful, and difficult of being outsped by all, like to the Fatal Night of beings.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते राक्षसास्तत्र तस्मिंस्तमसि दारुणे
राममेवाभ्यधावन्त संहृष्टा शरवृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration:
tataste rākṣasāstatra tasmiṁstamasi dāruṇe
rāmamevābhyadhāvanta saṁhṛṣṭā śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ

translations.english: And in that attacked Rama with a shower of shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामापततां शब्दः क्रुद्धानामभिगर्जताम्
उद्वर्त इव सप्तानां समुद्राणामभूत्स्वनः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmāpatatāṁ śabdaḥ kruddhānāmabhigarjatām
udvarta iva saptānāṁ samudrāṇāmabhūtsvanaḥ

translations.english: The roars of those beings as they advanced, sending up shouts in anger, resembled the dashing of the Ocean at the time of the universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञशत्रुश्च दुर्धर्षो महापार्श्वमहोदरौ
वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाकायस्तौ चोभौ शुकसारणौ
verses.transliteration:
yajñaśatruśca durdharṣo mahāpārśvamahodarau
vajradaṁṣṭro mahākāyastau cobhau śukasāraṇau

translations.english: In the twinkling of an eye, Räma by means of six shafts resembling tongues of flames, struck six of the night-rangers, viz., Yajñaśatru, irrepressible (in fight), and Mahaparsva, and Mahodara, and the huge bodied Vajradanstra, and those two-Suka and Sarana.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु रामेण बाणौघः सर्वमर्मसु ताडिताः
युद्धादपसृतास्तत्र सावशेषायुषोऽभवन्
verses.transliteration:
te tu rāmeṇa bāṇaughaḥ sarvamarmasu tāḍitāḥ
yuddhādapasṛtāstatra sāvaśeṣāyuṣo'bhavan

translations.english: And, pierced in their vitals with Rama's shafts, they, having only their lives left to them, disappeared from the field.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वन्ये राक्षसा वीरा रामस्याभिमुखे स्थिताः
तेऽपि नष्टाः समासाद्य पतंगा इव पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
ye tvanye rākṣasā vīrā rāmasyābhimukhe sthitāḥ
te'pi naṣṭāḥ samāsādya pataṁgā iva pāvakam

translations.english: Then in the twinkling of an eye, that Mahāratha rendered all sides clear (of all gloom) by means of arrows resembling tongues of fire; and those other heroic Raksasas that were in front of Rāma, were destroyed on approaching the place, like insects approaching a fire.

verses.sanskrit:
सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्विशिखैः संपतद्भिः सहस्रशः
बभूव रजनी चित्रा खद्योतैरिव शारदी
verses.transliteration:
suvarṇapuṅkhairviśikhaiḥ saṁpatadbhiḥ sahasraśaḥ
babhūva rajanī citrā khadyotairiva śāradī

translations.english: And with shafts plated with gold lying in all directions the night resembled one in autumn decked with fire-flies.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां च निनदैर्हरीणां चापि गर्जितैः
सा बभूव निशा घोरा भूयो घोरतरा तदा
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ ca ninadairharīṇāṁ cāpi garjitaiḥ
sā babhūva niśā ghorā bhūyo ghoratarā tadā

translations.english: And in consequence of the uproar occasioned by the Rakşasas, and the sounds of drums, that night, already dreadful (in itself), became all the more so,

verses.sanskrit:
तेन शब्देन महता प्रवृद्धेन समन्ततः
त्रिकूटः कन्दराकीर्णः प्रव्याहरदिवाचलः
verses.transliteration:
tena śabdena mahatā pravṛddhena samantataḥ
trikūṭaḥ kandarākīrṇaḥ pravyāharadivācalaḥ

translations.english: On that sound attaining dimensions on all sides, it seemed as if the mount Trikuta, containing numerous caverns, had been speaking.

verses.sanskrit:
गोलाङ्गूला महाकायास्तमसा तुल्यवर्चसः
संपरिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां भक्षयन्रजनीचरान्
verses.transliteration:
golāṅgūlā mahākāyāstamasā tulyavarcasaḥ
saṁpariṣvajya bāhubhyāṁ bhakṣayanrajanīcarān

translations.english: And huge-bodied Golangulas of equal lustre with darkness itself binding fast the nightrangers with their arms, began to swallow them up.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्तु रथं त्यक्त्वा हताश्वो हतसारथिः
अङ्गदेन महामायस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत
verses.transliteration:
indrajittu rathaṁ tyaktvā hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ
aṅgadena mahāmāyastatraivāntaradhīyata

translations.english: And Angada was present in the encounter, for slaying foes. And Indrajit, fairing sadly at the hands of Angada, abandoning his vehicle, and having his horses as well as his charioteer slain, vanished then and there.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽन्तर्धान गतः पापो रावणी रणकर्कशः
ब्रह्मदत्तवरो वीरो रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः
अदृश्यो निशितान्बाणान्मुमोचाशनिवर्चसः
verses.transliteration:
so'ntardhāna gataḥ pāpo rāvaṇī raṇakarkaśaḥ
brahmadattavaro vīro rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
adṛśyo niśitānbāṇānmumocāśanivarcasaḥ

translations.english: And, being handled hard in battle, and having vanished from the field, the heroic and wicked son to Răvana, who had received a boon from Brahmä, transported with passion, remaining invisible, began to discharge sharpened shafts of the splendour of the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामं लक्ष्मणं चैव घोरैर्नागमयैः शरैः
बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ caiva ghorairnāgamayaiḥ śaraiḥ
bibheda samare kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: And worked up into rage, he in the conflict pierced Raghu's sons, Rāma and Lakşmaņa all over their bodies, with terrific arrows consisting of serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य गतिमन्विच्छन्राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्
दिदेशातिबलो रामो दशवानरयूथपान्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya gatimanvicchanrājaputraḥ pratāpavān
dideśātibalo rāmo daśavānarayūthapān

translations.english: Then, anxious to ascertain his* course, the king's son possessed of prowess, and endowed with exceeding strength, Rāma, ordered ten of the monkey-leaders. * Indrajit's.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ सुषेणस्य दायादौ नीलं च प्लवगर्षभम्
अङ्गदं वालिपुत्रं च शरभं च तरस्विनम्
verses.transliteration:
dvau suṣeṇasya dāyādau nīlaṁ ca plavagarṣabham
aṅgadaṁ vāliputraṁ ca śarabhaṁ ca tarasvinam

translations.english: The repressor of foes ordered Väli's sonAngada, the vigorous Śarabha, Dvivida, Hanumān, the mighty Sānuprastha, Rşabha and Rşabhaskandha.

verses.sanskrit:
ते संप्रहृष्टा हरयो भीमानुद्यम्य पादपान्
आकाशं विविशुः सर्वे मार्गामाणा दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
te saṁprahṛṣṭā harayo bhīmānudyamya pādapān
ākāśaṁ viviśuḥ sarve mārgāmāṇā diśo daśa

translations.english: Thereat with alacrity those monkeys, wielding mighty trees, shot up into the sky, and began to scour the ten cardinal points.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां वेगवतां वेगमिषुभिर्वेगवत्तरैः
अस्त्रवित्परमास्त्रेण वारयामास रावणिः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vegavatāṁ vegamiṣubhirvegavattaraiḥ
astravitparamāstreṇa vārayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ

translations.english: And Ravana's son, skilled in arms, resisted the impetuous march of those vehement ones by means of a powerful weapon as well as arms more forceful (than the force of their rush).

verses.sanskrit:
तं भीमवेगा हरयो नाराचैः क्षतविक्षताः
अन्धकारे न ददृशुर्मेघैः सूर्यमिवावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ bhīmavegā harayo nārācaiḥ kṣatavikṣatāḥ
andhakāre na dadṛśurmeghaiḥ sūryamivāvṛtam

translations.english: The exceedingly vehement monkeys, cut and mangled with Nărăcas, saw him in the dark like the sun enveloped in clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणयोरेव सर्वमर्मभिदः शरान्
भृशमावेशयामास रावणिः समितिंजयः
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇayoreva sarvamarmabhidaḥ śarān
bhṛśamāveśayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ samitiṁjayaḥ

translations.english: That conqueror in battle, Ravana's son, with shafts sorely pierced the persons of Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
निरन्तरशरीरौ तु भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
क्रुद्धेनेन्द्रजिता वीरौ पन्नगैः शरतां गतैः
verses.transliteration:
nirantaraśarīrau tu bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
kruddhenendrajitā vīrau pannagaiḥ śaratāṁ gataiḥ

translations.english: And both Rāma and Lakşmaņa had their bodies entirely covered by the angry Indrajit with shafts turned into serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः क्षतजमार्गेण सुस्राव रुधिरं बहु
तावुभौ च प्रकाशेते पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ kṣatajamārgeṇa susrāva rudhiraṁ bahu
tāvubhau ca prakāśete puṣpitāviva kiṁśukau

translations.english: And from their wounds blood began to gush out in streams; and they looked like flowercrowned Kinsukas.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पर्यन्तरक्ताक्षो भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः
रावणिर्भ्रातरौ वाक्यमन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paryantaraktākṣo bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ
rāvaṇirbhrātarau vākyamantardhānagato'bravīt

translations.english: Then that one having red corners to his eyes and resembling a mass of crushed collyrium, Rāvana's son, said to the brothers, as he vanished.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यमानमनालक्ष्यं शक्रोऽपि त्रिदशेश्वरः
द्रष्टुमासादितुं वापि न शक्तः किं पुनर्युवाम्
verses.transliteration:
yudhyamānamanālakṣyaṁ śakro'pi tridaśeśvaraḥ
draṣṭumāsādituṁ vāpi na śaktaḥ kiṁ punaryuvām

translations.english: When I fight remaining invisible, even Sakrathe lord of the celestials-cannot see or approach me, and who are you?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रावृताविषुजालेन राघवौ कङ्कपत्रिणा
एष रोषपरीतात्मा नयामि यमसादनम्
verses.transliteration:
prāvṛtāviṣujālena rāghavau kaṅkapatriṇā
eṣa roṣaparītātmā nayāmi yamasādanam

translations.english: And I, with my soul surcharged with wrath, shall, assailing them with showers of weapons furnished with Karka feathers, send Raghu's sons to the abode of Yama."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु धर्मज्ञौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
निर्बिभेद शितैर्बाणैः प्रजहर्ष ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu dharmajñau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
nirbibheda śitairbāṇaiḥ prajaharṣa nanāda ca

translations.english: Having spoken thus to the brothers-Rāma and Laksmana, cognizant of righteousness-(Indrajit)pierced them with sharpened shafts, and shouted in joy.

verses.sanskrit:
भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामो विस्फार्य विपुलं धनुः
भूयो भूयः शरान्घोरान्विससर्ज महामृधे
verses.transliteration:
bhinnāñjanacayaśyāmo visphārya vipulaṁ dhanuḥ
bhūyo bhūyaḥ śarānghorānvisasarja mahāmṛdhe

translations.english: And stretching his large bow, that one sable like to a mass of crushed collyrium again discharged terrific shafts in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मर्मसु मर्मज्ञो मज्जयन्निशिताञ्शरान्
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वीरो ननाद च मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
tato marmasu marmajño majjayanniśitāñśarān
rāmalakṣmaṇayorvīro nanāda ca muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: That one versed in the inner sense of things, with whetted arrows pierced the vitals of Rāma and Lakşmaņa and shouted momentarily.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धौ तु शरबन्धेन तावुभौ रणमूर्धनि
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण न शेकतुरुदीक्षितुम्
verses.transliteration:
baddhau tu śarabandhena tāvubhau raṇamūrdhani
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa na śekaturudīkṣitum

translations.english: And fast bound by the shackles of shafts on the edge of battle, they* could not attain respite for a moment, *i.e. Rama and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ संप्रचलितौ वीरौ मर्मभेदेन कर्शितौ
निपेततुर्महेष्वासौ जगत्यां जगतीपती
verses.transliteration:
tau saṁpracalitau vīrau marmabhedena karśitau
nipetaturmaheṣvāsau jagatyāṁ jagatīpatī

translations.english: Then with their persons pierced with shafts and darts, and resembling the flags of the Great Indra let loose from the cords and trembling (in the air), and with their bodies bristling with arrows, those heroes and mighty bowmen-lords of the earth-tormented in consequence of their vitals having been pierced, dropped down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ
शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गावार्तौ परमपीडितौ
verses.transliteration:
tau vīraśayane vīrau śayānau rudhirokṣitau
śaraveṣṭitasarvāṅgāvārtau paramapīḍitau

translations.english: Those heroes, bathed in blood and their persons covered with arrows-pained and suffering terribly, lay down as became heroes.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यविद्धं तयोर्गात्रं बभूवाङ्गुलमन्तरम्
नानिर्भिन्नं न चास्तब्धमा कराग्रादजिह्मगैः
verses.transliteration:
na hyaviddhaṁ tayorgātraṁ babhūvāṅgulamantaram
nānirbhinnaṁ na cāstabdhamā karāgrādajihmagaiḥ

translations.english: There was not so much room unpierced in their persons as could be measured by a finger; and they were wounded with arrows up to the fore-parts of their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तु क्रूरेण निहतौ रक्षसा कामरूपिणा
असृक्सुस्रुवतुस्तीव्रं जलं प्रस्रवणाविव
verses.transliteration:
tau tu krūreṇa nihatau rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā
asṛksusruvatustīvraṁ jalaṁ prasravaṇāviva

translations.english: They being wounded by that fell one capable of assuming shapes at will, blood violently gushed out of their bodies like water from a spring.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणपातान्तरे रामं पतितं पुरुषर्षभम्
स तत्र लक्ष्मणो दृष्ट्वा निराशो जीवितेऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
bāṇapātāntare rāmaṁ patitaṁ puruṣarṣabham
sa tatra lakṣmaṇo dṛṣṭvā nirāśo jīvite'bhavat

translations.english: Seeing Rāma, the foremost of men-down within arrow-range, Laksmana despaired of his life.

verses.sanskrit:
बद्धौ तु वीरौ पतितौ शयानौ; तौ वानराः संपरिवार्य तस्थुः
समागता वायुसुतप्रमुख्या; विषदमार्ताः परमं च जग्मुः
verses.transliteration:
baddhau tu vīrau patitau śayānau; tau vānarāḥ saṁparivārya tasthuḥ
samāgatā vāyusutapramukhyā; viṣadamārtāḥ paramaṁ ca jagmuḥ

translations.english: When they had been bound and had laid themselves down as become heroes, the monkeys stood around them-and, conversing with one another, they, headed by the son of the Wing, were seized with extreme sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो द्यां पृथिवीं चैव वीक्षमाणा वनौकसः
ददृशुः संततौ बाणैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tato dyāṁ pṛthivīṁ caiva vīkṣamāṇā vanaukasaḥ
dadṛśuḥ saṁtatau bāṇairbhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: The rangers of woods, gazing at the earth and the sky, at length cast their eyes on the brothersRāma and Lakşmaņa covered all over with arrows. And after that Rākşasa had gone away having performed his work, like the God* going away, after having showered, there came to that place Vibhīşaņa with sugrīva. *Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
वृष्ट्वेवोपरते देवे कृतकर्मणि राक्षसे
आजगामाथ तं देशं ससुग्रीवो विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
vṛṣṭvevoparate deve kṛtakarmaṇi rākṣase
ājagāmātha taṁ deśaṁ sasugrīvo vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: And mourning Raghu's sons, there also came in all haste Nila and Dvivida and Mainda and Sușeņa and Kumuda and Angada in company with Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
निश्चेष्टौ मन्दनिःश्वासौ शोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ
शरजालाचितौ स्तब्धौ शयानौ शरतल्पयोः
verses.transliteration:
niśceṣṭau mandaniḥśvāsau śoṇitaughapariplutau
śarajālācitau stabdhau śayānau śaratalpayoḥ

translations.english: And moveless; breathing covered with bloodpierced all over with net-works of shafts; dumb; they* were lying on the field. *Rama and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
निःश्वसन्तौ यथा सर्पौ निश्चेष्टौ मन्दविक्रमौ
रुधिरस्रावदिग्धाङ्गौ तापनीयाविव ध्वजौ
verses.transliteration:
niḥśvasantau yathā sarpau niśceṣṭau mandavikramau
rudhirasrāvadigdhāṅgau tāpanīyāviva dhvajau

translations.english: They were sighing like serpents; and were inert; and deprived of prowess; and washed in blood; and looking like to golden standards.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ मन्दचेष्टितौ
यूथपैस्तैः परिवृतौ बाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः
verses.transliteration:
tau vīraśayane vīrau śayānau mandaceṣṭitau
yūthapaistaiḥ parivṛtau bāṣpavyākulalocanaiḥ

translations.english: And as they lay moveless, as become heroes, the leaders of monkeys environed them with tear-charged eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवौ पतितौ दृष्ट्वा शरजालसमावृतौ
बभूवुर्व्यथिताः सर्वे वानराः सविभीषणाः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavau patitau dṛṣṭvā śarajālasamāvṛtau
babhūvurvyathitāḥ sarve vānarāḥ savibhīṣaṇāḥ

translations.english: Seeing the sons of Raghu lying, covered with showers of shafts, the monkeys, with Vibhisana, were pained (exceedingly).

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षं निरीक्षन्तो दिशः सर्वाश्च वानराः
न चैनं मायया छन्नं ददृशू रावणिं रणे
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣaṁ nirīkṣanto diśaḥ sarvāśca vānarāḥ
na cainaṁ māyayā channaṁ dadṛśū rāvaṇiṁ raṇe

translations.english: The monkeys, Surveying the sky as well as all directions, could not see Rāvana's son in battle enveloped with illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
तमप्रतिम कर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे
ददर्शान्तर्हितं वीरं वरदानाद्विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
tamapratima karmāṇamapratidvandvamāhave
dadarśāntarhitaṁ vīraṁ varadānādvibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then Vibhīşaņa by means of illusion saw his brother's son staying before, hidden by illusion. And Vibhīşaņa saw that hero of incomparable deeds, who had no compeer in the field and who had energy, fame and prowess-as he remained invisible in consequence of the boon received from Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनः कर्म तौ शयानौ समीक्ष्य च
उवाच परमप्रीतो हर्षयन्सर्वनैरृतान्
verses.transliteration:
indrajittvātmanaḥ karma tau śayānau samīkṣya ca
uvāca paramaprīto harṣayansarvanairṛtān

translations.english: And Indrajit, seeing his own feat and them lying at length, spoke in excess of joy, gladdening all the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
दूषणस्य च हन्तारौ खरस्य च महाबलौ
सादितौ मामकैर्बाणैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
dūṣaṇasya ca hantārau kharasya ca mahābalau
sāditau māmakairbāṇairbhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: The brothers-Rāma and Lakşmaņa, possessed of great strength, who had slain Khara and Dūşaņa, are themselves slain with my shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
नेमौ मोक्षयितुं शक्यावेतस्मादिषुबन्धनात्
सर्वैरपि समागम्य सर्षिसङ्घैः सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
nemau mokṣayituṁ śakyāvetasmādiṣubandhanāt
sarvairapi samāgamya sarṣisaṅghaiḥ surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: All the celestials and Asuras assembled together with the saints, are incompetent to emancipate these from the fetters of my shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्कृते चिन्तयानस्य शोकार्तस्य पितुर्मम
अस्पृष्ट्वा शयनं गात्रैस्त्रियामा याति शर्वती
verses.transliteration:
yatkṛte cintayānasya śokārtasya piturmama
aspṛṣṭvā śayanaṁ gātraistriyāmā yāti śarvatī

translations.english: He for whom my father was exercise with anxiety and tormented by grief, for whom my sire used to spend nights without pressing his bed, for whom this entire Lankā had resembled a river turbulent in the rainy reason, that same evil sticking by the root of all, has been dispensed his quietus by me.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्यैव सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्
विक्रमा निष्फलाः सर्वे यथा शरदि तोयदाः
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya lakṣmaṇasyaiva sarveṣāṁ ca vanaukasām
vikramā niṣphalāḥ sarve yathā śaradi toyadāḥ

translations.english: And like clouds of autumn, the prowess of Råma and Laksmana as well as that of all the rangers of the woods, has been rendered useless.

verses.sanskrit:
तानर्दयित्वा बाणौघैस्त्रासयित्वा च वानरान्
प्रजहास महाबाहुर्वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tānardayitvā bāṇaughaistrāsayitvā ca vānarān
prajahāsa mahābāhurvacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: And tormenting the monkeys with volleys of shafts and striking terror into them, that mightyarmed one. bursting out into a laugh, said.

verses.sanskrit:
शरबन्धेन घोरेण मया बद्धौ चमूमुखे
सहितौ भ्रातरावेतौ निशामयत राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
śarabandhena ghoreṇa mayā baddhau camūmukhe
sahitau bhrātarāvetau niśāmayata rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: “Let the Raksasas behold these brothers lying fast bound with dreadful arrows in front of the forces."

verses.sanskrit:
विनेदुश्च महानादान्सर्वे ते जलदोपमाः
हतो राम इति ज्ञात्वा रावणिं समपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
vineduśca mahānādānsarve te jaladopamāḥ
hato rāma iti jñātvā rāvaṇiṁ samapūjayan

translations.english: Thus addressed, those Rākşasas-wily warriors all-resembling masses of clouds, witnessing that deed (of Indrajit), struck with wonder and rejoicing (greatly), set up tremendous roars. And thinking that Rāma was slain, they honoured Ravana's son.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्पन्दौ तु तदा दृष्ट्वा तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
वसुधायां निरुच्छ्वासौ हतावित्यन्वमन्यत
verses.transliteration:
niṣpandau tu tadā dṛṣṭvā tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
vasudhāyāṁ nirucchvāsau hatāvityanvamanyata

translations.english: Seeing the brothers-Rāma and Laksmanamotionless, and lying inert on the ground, they took them for slain.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्षेण तु समाविष्ट इन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः
प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां हर्षयन्सर्वनैरृतान्
verses.transliteration:
harṣeṇa tu samāviṣṭa indrajitsamitiṁjayaḥ
praviveśa purīṁ laṅkāṁ harṣayansarvanairṛtān

translations.english: And, experiencing excess of joy, Indrajitconquerer in conflict-entered the city of Lankā, rejoicing all the Nairtas.

verses.sanskrit:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्ट्वा शरीरे सायकैश्चिते
सर्वाणि चाङ्गोपाङ्गानि सुग्रीवं भयमाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
rāmalakṣmaṇayordṛṣṭvā śarīre sāyakaiścite
sarvāṇi cāṅgopāṅgāni sugrīvaṁ bhayamāviśat

translations.english: Seeing the bodies as well as the limbs of Rāma and Lakşmana, covered entirely with arrows, fear took possession of Sugriva.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच परित्रस्तं वानरेन्द्रं विभीषणः
सबाष्पवदनं दीनं शोकव्याकुललोचनम्
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca paritrastaṁ vānarendraṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
sabāṣpavadanaṁ dīnaṁ śokavyākulalocanam

translations.english: Thereat Vibhīşaņa said to that lord of monkeys, staying in woe-begone guise, with a tearful countenance, and his eyes wild with wrath, "Do not give way to fear, O Sugriva. Restrain your rising tears!

verses.sanskrit:
पर्यवस्थापयात्मानमनाथं मां च वानर
सत्यधर्मानुरक्तानां नास्ति मृत्युकृतं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
paryavasthāpayātmānamanāthaṁ māṁ ca vānara
satyadharmānuraktānāṁ nāsti mṛtyukṛtaṁ bhayam

translations.english: This is the way of warfare: victory is not (always) sure But, O hero, If Fortune ultimately smile upon us, this stupor shall go off from these high-souled and exceedingly powerful ones. therefore, O monkey, do you cheer me, who am forlorn.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तस्य जलक्लिन्नेन पाणिना
सुग्रीवस्य शुभे नेत्रे प्रममार्ज विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tatastasya jalaklinnena pāṇinā
sugrīvasya śubhe netre pramamārja vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Saying this, with hand Vibhīşaņa washed Sugriva's graceful eyes with water.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमृज्य वदनं तस्य कपिराजस्य धीमतः
अब्रवीत्कालसंप्रातमसंभ्रान्तमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
pramṛjya vadanaṁ tasya kapirājasya dhīmataḥ
abravītkālasaṁprātamasaṁbhrāntamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And washing the face of the intelligent monkey-monarch, Vibhisana spoke these words, seasonable and sedate.

verses.sanskrit:
न कालः कपिराजेन्द्र वैक्लव्यमनुवर्तितुम्
अतिस्नेहोऽप्यकालेऽस्मिन्मरणायोपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
na kālaḥ kapirājendra vaiklavyamanuvartitum
atisneho'pyakāle'sminmaraṇāyopapadyate

translations.english: O foremost of monkey-kings, this is no time for being overcome with stupor. At this hour, even immoderate affection may lead destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादुत्सृज्य वैक्लव्यं सर्वकार्यविनाशनम्
हितं रामपुरोगाणां सैन्यानामनुचिन्त्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
tasmādutsṛjya vaiklavyaṁ sarvakāryavināśanam
hitaṁ rāmapurogāṇāṁ sainyānāmanucintyatām

translations.english: Therefore, casting off stupor, which tends to mar all work, do you bethink you how you may serve this army headed by Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा रक्ष्यतां रामो यावत्संज्ञा विपर्ययः
लब्धसंज्ञौ तु काकुत्स्थौ भयं नो व्यपनेष्यतः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā rakṣyatāṁ rāmo yāvatsaṁjñā viparyayaḥ
labdhasaṁjñau tu kākutsthau bhayaṁ no vyapaneṣyataḥ

translations.english: Or do you protect Rāma so long as he does not regain consciousness; and when the Kākutsthas shall have regained consciousness, all our apprehension shall vanish.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतत्किंचन रामस्य न च रामो मुमूर्षति
न ह्येनं हास्यते लक्ष्मीर्दुर्लभा या गतायुषाम्
verses.transliteration:
naitatkiṁcana rāmasya na ca rāmo mumūrṣati
na hyenaṁ hāsyate lakṣmīrdurlabhā yā gatāyuṣām

translations.english: This is nothing to Rāma is not dying. And Lakşmi* who is incapable of being attained by those that are doomed, shall not forsake this one. *The goddess of prosperity. to

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादाश्वासयात्मानं बलं चाश्वासय स्वकम्
यावत्सर्वाणि सैन्यानि पुनः संस्थापयाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
tasmādāśvāsayātmānaṁ balaṁ cāśvāsaya svakam
yāvatsarvāṇi sainyāni punaḥ saṁsthāpayāmyaham

translations.english: Therefore do you comfort yourself, do you also cheer up your own forces, while I am engaged in composing all the troops.

verses.sanskrit:
एते ह्युत्फुल्लनयनास्त्रासादागतसाध्वसाः
कर्णे कर्णे प्रकथिता हरयो हरिपुंगव
verses.transliteration:
ete hyutphullanayanāstrāsādāgatasādhvasāḥ
karṇe karṇe prakathitā harayo haripuṁgava

translations.english: O best of monkeys, these with distended eyes, come under the governance of terror, are, stricken with panic, whispering into each other's ears.

verses.sanskrit:
मां तु दृष्ट्वा प्रधावन्तमनीकं संप्रहर्षितुम्
त्यजन्तु हरयस्त्रासं भुक्तपूर्वामिव स्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
māṁ tu dṛṣṭvā pradhāvantamanīkaṁ saṁpraharṣitum
tyajantu harayastrāsaṁ bhuktapūrvāmiva srajam

translations.english: But seeing me, let the forces rushing about, cheered up, as well as the monkeys, cast off all fear, like a wreath that has been used before.

verses.sanskrit:
समाश्वास्य तु सुग्रीवं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः
विद्रुतं वानरानीकं तत्समाश्वासयत्पुनः
verses.transliteration:
samāśvāsya tu sugrīvaṁ rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ
vidrutaṁ vānarānīkaṁ tatsamāśvāsayatpunaḥ

translations.english: Thus comforting Sugriva, Vibhisana-lord of Rākṣasas-again instilled spirits into the flying forces of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्तु महामायः सर्वसैन्यसमावृतः
विवेश नगरीं लङ्कां पितरं चाभ्युपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
indrajittu mahāmāyaḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtaḥ
viveśa nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ pitaraṁ cābhyupāgamat

translations.english: And Indrajit, worker of mighty illusionsaccompanied by his troops, entered the city of Larkā and presented himself before his father.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र रावणमासीनमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः
आचचक्षे प्रियं पित्रे निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tatra rāvaṇamāsīnamabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ
ācacakṣe priyaṁ pitre nihatau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: And approaching Rāvana and saluting him with joined hands, he informed his sire of the welcome tidings that Răma and Lakṣmaṇa had been slain.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पपात ततो हृष्टः पुत्रं च परिषस्वजे
रावणो रक्षसां मध्ये श्रुत्वा शत्रू निपातितौ
verses.transliteration:
utpapāta tato hṛṣṭaḥ putraṁ ca pariṣasvaje
rāvaṇo rakṣasāṁ madhye śrutvā śatrū nipātitau

translations.english: And hearing that his foe had fallen, Rāvana springing up in the midst of the Rākşasas, With great joy embraced his son.

verses.sanskrit:
उपाघ्राय स मूर्ध्न्येनं पप्रच्छ प्रीतमानसः
पृच्छते च यथावृत्तं पित्रे सर्वं न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
upāghrāya sa mūrdhnyenaṁ papraccha prītamānasaḥ
pṛcchate ca yathāvṛttaṁ pitre sarvaṁ nyavedayat

translations.english: And scenting the crown of his head, (Rāvana) with a delighted heart, asked (Indrajit as to all that had taken place). And on being asked, he (Indrajit) truly related to his sire how (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) had been rendered senseless and lack-Lustre by being fastened with shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स हर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्मा; श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य महारथस्य
जहौ ज्वरं दाशरथेः समुत्थितं; प्रहृष्य वाचाभिननन्द पुत्रम्
verses.transliteration:
sa harṣavegānugatāntarātmā; śrutvā vacastasya mahārathasya
jahau jvaraṁ dāśaratheḥ samutthitaṁ; prahṛṣya vācābhinananda putram

translations.english: Thereat, with rapture surcharging his inmost soul, Rāvana, hearing the speech of the mighty car warrior, banished his fear of Dasaratha's son, and rising up, honoured his son with glad words. that had taken place). And on being asked, he (Indrajit) truly related to his sire how (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) had been rendered senseless and lack-Lustre by being fastened with shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिप्रविष्टे लङ्कां तु कृतार्थे रावणात्मजे
राघवं परिवार्यार्ता ररक्षुर्वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
pratipraviṣṭe laṅkāṁ tu kṛtārthe rāvaṇātmaje
rāghavaṁ parivāryārtā rarakṣurvānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: When Rāvana's son entered Lankā, after having accomplished his purpose, the foremost monkeys protected Raghava, surrounding him on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च वानराः
तृणेष्वपि च चेष्टत्सु राक्षसा इति मेनिरे
verses.transliteration:
vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvāstiryagūrdhvaṁ ca vānarāḥ
tṛṇeṣvapi ca ceṣṭatsu rākṣasā iti menire

translations.english: And Hanumān, and Angada, and Nīla, and Susena, and Kumuda, and Nala, and Gaya, and Gavākṣa, and Panas, and Sānuprastha-a mighty monkey-and Jämbavān, and Rishava, and Sunda, and Rambha, and Satabali, and Prthu, all forming them selves into array, and equipped with trees on all sides, and remaining vigilantthe monkeys kept gazing at all sides, awry and upwards; and even when a straw stirred, they thought it to be a Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणश्चापि संहृष्टो विसृज्येन्द्रजितं सुतम्
आजुहाव ततः सीता रक्षणी राक्षसीस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇaścāpi saṁhṛṣṭo visṛjyendrajitaṁ sutam
ājuhāva tataḥ sītā rakṣaṇī rākṣasīstadā

translations.english: Rāvana, on his part experiencing the height of exaltation, summoned the Rākṣasais engaged in guarding Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षस्यस्त्रिजटा चापि शासनात्तमुपस्थिताः
ता उवाच ततो हृष्टो राक्षसी राक्षसेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasyastrijaṭā cāpi śāsanāttamupasthitāḥ
tā uvāca tato hṛṣṭo rākṣasī rākṣaseśvaraḥ

translations.english: Thereat the Raksasi-Trijata and otherspresented themselves at his command. And then the lord of Rākşasas, delighted addressed then the Raksasis, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
हताविन्द्रजिताख्यात वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ
पुष्पकं च समारोप्य दर्शयध्वं हतौ रणे
verses.transliteration:
hatāvindrajitākhyāta vaidehyā rāmalakṣmaṇau
puṣpakaṁ ca samāropya darśayadhvaṁ hatau raṇe

translations.english: Tell Vaidehí that Rāma and Lakşmaņa have been slain in battle by Indrajit. And taking her on Pushaka, show her (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) lying slain on the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
यदाश्रयादवष्टब्धो नेयं मामुपतिष्ठति
सोऽस्या भर्ता सह भ्रात्रा निरस्तो रणमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
yadāśrayādavaṣṭabdho neyaṁ māmupatiṣṭhati
so'syā bhartā saha bhrātrā nirasto raṇamūrdhani

translations.english: That one depending on whom she had proudly set her face against me, that husband of hers, along with his brother, has been slain in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्विशङ्का निरुद्विग्ना निरपेक्षा च मैथिली
मामुपस्थास्यते सीता सर्वाभरणभूषिता
verses.transliteration:
nirviśaṅkā nirudvignā nirapekṣā ca maithilī
māmupasthāsyate sītā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā

translations.english: Then methyl's daughter, her fear gone off with her anxiety, and herself losing all support, Sītādaughter to methyl-decked out in all ornaments, shall seek me.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य कालवशं प्राप्तं रणे रामं सलक्ष्मणम्
अवेक्ष्य विनिवृत्ताशा नान्यां गतिमपश्यती
verses.transliteration:
adya kālavaśaṁ prāptaṁ raṇe rāmaṁ salakṣmaṇam
avekṣya vinivṛttāśā nānyāṁ gatimapaśyatī

translations.english: And today beholding Rāma with Lakşmaņa, come under the away of Time, she, finding no other way, shall desist from her present course. And seeing no other resource, that one of expansive eyes shall of herself seek me.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
राक्षस्यस्तास्तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रजग्मुर्यत्र पुष्पकम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
rākṣasyastāstathetyuktvā prajagmuryatra puṣpakam

translations.english: Hearing those words of the wicked-minded Rāvana, the Rākşasais, saying, “So be it,” went to where Puspaka was.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुष्पकमादय राक्षस्यो रावणाज्ञया
अशोकवनिकास्थां तां मैथिलीं समुपानयन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ puṣpakamādaya rākṣasyo rāvaṇājñayā
aśokavanikāsthāṁ tāṁ maithilīṁ samupānayan

translations.english: Then taking Pușpaka, the Rākşasis at Rāvana's command went to Maithilī staying in theasoka wood.

verses.sanskrit:
तामादाय तु राक्षस्यो भर्तृशोकपरायणाम्
सीतामारोपयामासुर्विमानं पुष्पकं तदा
verses.transliteration:
tāmādāya tu rākṣasyo bhartṛśokaparāyaṇām
sītāmāropayāmāsurvimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ tadā

translations.english: Then, taking Sītā, who was overcome with grief for her lord, the Raksasais, placed her on the car, Puspaka.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहृष्टमनसश्चापि ददर्श पिशिताशनान्
वानरांश्चापि दुःखार्तान्रामलक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः
verses.transliteration:
prahṛṣṭamanasaścāpi dadarśa piśitāśanān
vānarāṁścāpi duḥkhārtānrāmalakṣmaṇapārśvataḥ

translations.english: She found the flesh-eaters elated in spirits, and the monkeys afflicted with extreme grief at the side of Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सीता ददर्शोभौ शयानौ शततल्पयोः
लक्ष्मणं चैव रामं च विसंज्ञौ शरपीडितौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sītā dadarśobhau śayānau śatatalpayoḥ
lakṣmaṇaṁ caiva rāmaṁ ca visaṁjñau śarapīḍitau

translations.english: Then Sītā beheld both Lakşmaņa and Rāma lying in the field, senseless and bound with arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
विध्वस्तकवचौ वीरौ विप्रविद्धशरासनौ
सायकैश्छिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ शरस्तम्भमयौ क्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
vidhvastakavacau vīrau vipraviddhaśarāsanau
sāyakaiśchinnasarvāṅgau śarastambhamayau kṣitau

translations.english: Those heroes were lying on the earth, their mail torn, their bows cast off their bodies mangled all over and thickly pierce with shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ तत्र वीरौ सा पुरुषर्षभौ
दुःखार्ता सुभृशं सीता करुणं विललाप ह
verses.transliteration:
tau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau tatra vīrau sā puruṣarṣabhau
duḥkhārtā subhṛśaṁ sītā karuṇaṁ vilalāpa ha

translations.english: Seeing those brothers, foremost of heroes and best of men-having eyes resembling white lotuses, and them selves like to Kumāras, lying in the field,* the fire sprung one, Sītā stricken with grief, beg a to weep piteously. *Virān narashabhān-heroes and best of menoccurs again, left out on the score of redendancy.

verses.sanskrit:
सा बाष्पशोकाभिहता समीक्ष्य; तौ भ्रातरौ देवसमप्रभावौ
वितर्कयन्ती निधनं तयोः सा; दुःखान्विता वाक्यमिदं जगाद
verses.transliteration:
sā bāṣpaśokābhihatā samīkṣya; tau bhrātarau devasamaprabhāvau
vitarkayantī nidhanaṁ tayoḥ sā; duḥkhānvitā vākyamidaṁ jagāda

translations.english: With her eyes shedding plentiful tears, she seeing those brothers, endowed with god-like prowess, concluded them to be dead; and overwhelmed with grief, spoke as follows. as as

verses.sanskrit:
भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं शोककर्शिता
verses.transliteration:
bhartāraṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam
vilalāpa bhṛśaṁ sītā karuṇaṁ śokakarśitā

translations.english: Seeing her husband, well the exceedingly powerful Laksmana, slain, Srta, afflicted with grief, burst into bitter lamentation.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊचुर्लक्षणिका ये मां पुत्रिण्यविधवेति च
तेऽस्य सर्वे हते रामेऽज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
ūcurlakṣaṇikā ye māṁ putriṇyavidhaveti ca
te'sya sarve hate rāme'jñānino'nṛtavādinaḥ

translations.english: The soothsayers had said that I should have sons, and should never be a widow. But on Råma being slain, it sees now that those ones, possessed of knowledge, had spoken untruthfully.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्वनो महिषीं ये मामूचुः पत्नीं च सत्रिणः
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामेऽज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
yajvano mahiṣīṁ ye māmūcuḥ patnīṁ ca satriṇaḥ
te'dya sarve hate rāme'jñānino'nṛtavādinaḥ

translations.english: Those also, who having celebrated sacrifices and rites, had said that I should become the queen (of Rama), on Rāma being slain, seems today to have spoken a falsehood, although they are possessed of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
वीरपार्थिवपत्नी त्वं ये धन्येति च मां विदुः
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामेऽज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
vīrapārthivapatnī tvaṁ ye dhanyeti ca māṁ viduḥ
te'dya sarve hate rāme'jñānino'nṛtavādinaḥ

translations.english: They also asserted that I should be honoured of the wives of heroic kings as well as of my lord, but on Rāma being slain, they seem to have spoken a falsehood, although possessed of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊचुः संश्रवणे ये मां द्विजाः कार्तान्तिकाः शुभाम्
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामेऽज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः
verses.transliteration:
ūcuḥ saṁśravaṇe ye māṁ dvijāḥ kārtāntikāḥ śubhām
te'dya sarve hate rāme'jñānino'nṛtavādinaḥ

translations.english: Those twice-born ones that in any hearing had said auspicious words, on Rāma being slain, seem today to have spoken a falsehood although they were possessed of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
इमानि खलु पद्मानि पादयोर्यैः किल स्त्रियः
अधिराज्येऽभिषिच्यन्ते नरेन्द्रैः पतिभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
imāni khalu padmāni pādayoryaiḥ kila striyaḥ
adhirājye'bhiṣicyante narendraiḥ patibhiḥ saha

translations.english: These lotus-marks on the feet, betokening to gentlewomen possessing them, that they are to be installed in the kingdom in company with their husbands-who are kings-are on me.

verses.sanskrit:
वैधव्यं यान्ति यैर्नार्योऽलक्षणैर्भाग्यदुर्लभाः
नात्मनस्तानि पश्यामि पश्यन्ती हतलक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
vaidhavyaṁ yānti yairnāryo'lakṣaṇairbhāgyadurlabhāḥ
nātmanastāni paśyāmi paśyantī hatalakṣaṇā

translations.english: Those marks find I none on me by which women of rare fortune come by widowhood, but I find that in me these good tokens are nullified.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यानीमानि पद्मानि स्त्रीणामुक्त्वानि लक्षणे
तान्यद्य निहते रामे वितथानि भवन्ति मे
verses.transliteration:
satyānīmāni padmāni strīṇāmuktvāni lakṣaṇe
tānyadya nihate rāme vitathāni bhavanti me

translations.english: Those marks that are pronounced infallible by those versed in such knowledge, on Rama being slain, are nullified in me.

verses.sanskrit:
केशाः सूक्ष्माः समा नीला भ्रुवौ चासंगते मम
वृत्ते चालोमशे जङ्घे दन्ताश्चाविरला मम
verses.transliteration:
keśāḥ sūkṣmāḥ samā nīlā bhruvau cāsaṁgate mama
vṛtte cālomaśe jaṅghe dantāścāviralā mama

translations.english: My hairs are fine, equal, and blue; my eyebrows touch each other; my hips are devoid of down and round; and my teeth are close.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खे नेत्रे करौ पादौ गुल्फावूरू च मे चितौ
अनुवृत्ता नखाः स्निग्धाः समाश्चाङ्गुलयो मम
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhe netre karau pādau gulphāvūrū ca me citau
anuvṛttā nakhāḥ snigdhāḥ samāścāṅgulayo mama

translations.english: My temples, and eyes hands, feet, ankles, and thighs are equal. And my fingers are furnished with round nails, and are plump and even in the middle.

verses.sanskrit:
स्तनौ चाविरलौ पीनौ ममेमौ मग्नचूचुकौ
मग्ना चोत्सङ्गिनी नाभिः पार्श्वोरस्कं च मे चितम्
verses.transliteration:
stanau cāviralau pīnau mamemau magnacūcukau
magnā cotsaṅginī nābhiḥ pārśvoraskaṁ ca me citam

translations.english: And my breasts are close and firm and developed, and have their nipples sunk. And my navel is depressed, with high sides. And my chest is swelling.

verses.sanskrit:
मम वर्णो मणिनिभो मृदून्यङ्गरुहाणि च
प्रतिष्ठितां द्वदशभिर्मामूचुः शुभलक्षणाम्
verses.transliteration:
mama varṇo maṇinibho mṛdūnyaṅgaruhāṇi ca
pratiṣṭhitāṁ dvadaśabhirmāmūcuḥ śubhalakṣaṇām

translations.english: My complexion is like the hue of gems, and my down soft. And they said that I was furnished with twelve auspicious signs.

verses.sanskrit:
समग्रयवमच्छिद्रं पाणिपादं च वर्णवत्
मन्दस्मितेत्येव च मां कन्यालक्षणिका विदुः
verses.transliteration:
samagrayavamacchidraṁ pāṇipādaṁ ca varṇavat
mandasmitetyeva ca māṁ kanyālakṣaṇikā viduḥ

translations.english: And my hands in the middle parts of my fingers contain wheat-marks, and in the spaces between the fingers, have no uneven corners. And my feet also partake of the general complexion. And my laugh is a gentle smile. And those versed in marks of women knew that I was possessed of such marks.

verses.sanskrit:
अधिराज्येऽभिषेको मे ब्राह्मणैः पतिना सह
कृतान्तकुशलैरुक्तं तत्सर्वं वितथीकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
adhirājye'bhiṣeko me brāhmaṇaiḥ patinā saha
kṛtāntakuśalairuktaṁ tatsarvaṁ vitathīkṛtam

translations.english: Those Brähmaņas skilled in telling fortune said that I should be installed in the kingdom along with my husband; but all that has been falsified.

verses.sanskrit:
शोधयित्वा जनस्थानं प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च
तीर्त्वा सागरमक्षोभ्यं भ्रातरौ गोष्पदे हतौ
verses.transliteration:
śodhayitvā janasthānaṁ pravṛttimupalabhya ca
tīrtvā sāgaramakṣobhyaṁ bhrātarau goṣpade hatau

translations.english: Having purified Janasthana (of Raksasas), obtained tidings of me, and crossed the Ocean* incapable of being agitated, those brothers have been slain in the footprint of a cow! *The commentator assigns a metaphorical sense to ocean-but this is hardly necessary.

verses.sanskrit:
ननु वारुणमाग्नेयमैन्द्रं वायव्यमेव च
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव राघवौ प्रत्यपद्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
nanu vāruṇamāgneyamaindraṁ vāyavyameva ca
astraṁ brahmaśiraścaiva rāghavau pratyapadyatām

translations.english: The descendants of Raghu had obtained Väruņa and Āgneya and Aindra and Vāyavya and Brahmasira weapons.* * And did they not remember this now? completes the sense.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृश्यमानेन रणे मायया वासवोपमौ
मम नाथावनाथाया निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
adṛśyamānena raṇe māyayā vāsavopamau
mama nāthāvanāthāyā nihatau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Through illusion have those lords of me, who am forlorn. Rāma and Lakşmaņa, resembling Vasava himself in battle, been slain.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्य राघवस्य रणे रिपुः
जीवन्प्रतिनिवर्तेत यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः
verses.transliteration:
na hi dṛṣṭipathaṁ prāpya rāghavasya raṇe ripuḥ
jīvanpratinivarteta yadyapi syānmanojavaḥ

translations.english: Coming in battle within ken of Raghava, a foe, even if he be endowed with the fleetness of thought, does not go back living.

verses.sanskrit:
न कालस्यातिभारोऽस्ति कृतान्तश्च सुदुर्जयः
यत्र रामः सह भ्रात्रा शेते युधि निपाथितः
verses.transliteration:
na kālasyātibhāro'sti kṛtāntaśca sudurjayaḥ
yatra rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā śete yudhi nipāthitaḥ

translations.english: There is nothing which is too hard for Time; and the Destroyer is incapable of being overcome; inasmuch as Rāma along with his brother Lakşmaņa has fallen in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
सा हि चिन्तयते नित्यं समाप्तव्रतमागतम्
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां च रामं च सहलक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
sā hi cintayate nityaṁ samāptavratamāgatam
kadā drakṣyāmi sītāṁ ca rāmaṁ ca sahalakṣmaṇam

translations.english: I do not so much mourn Rāma or the mighty car-warrior-Laksmana-or, for that matter, self, as I do the wretched mother-in-law of mine. She ever think of the period of the promise. "When shall I behold Sītā and Lakşmaņa with Rāghava?

verses.sanskrit:
परिदेवयमानां तां राक्षसी त्रिजटाब्रवीत्
मा विषादं कृथा देवि भर्तायं तव जीवति
verses.transliteration:
paridevayamānāṁ tāṁ rākṣasī trijaṭābravīt
mā viṣādaṁ kṛthā devi bhartāyaṁ tava jīvati

translations.english: As she was thus lamenting, the Rākṣasai, said, O exalted lady, do not weep thus, your lord live.

verses.sanskrit:
कारणानि च वक्ष्यामि महान्ति सदृशानि च
यथेमौ जीवतो देवि भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
kāraṇāni ca vakṣyāmi mahānti sadṛśāni ca
yathemau jīvato devi bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: O dignified one, I shall unfold to you potent and probable reasons why the brothers Rāma and Laksmana live.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि कोपपरीतानि हर्षपर्युत्सुकानि च
भवन्ति युधि योधानां मुखानि निहते पतौ
verses.transliteration:
na hi kopaparītāni harṣaparyutsukāni ca
bhavanti yudhi yodhānāṁ mukhāni nihate patau

translations.english: When their leader fall, the countenances of the warriors in battle are not overspread with passion, or display cheerfulness and vivacity.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं विमानं वैदेहि पुष्पकं नाम नामतः
दिव्यं त्वां धारयेन्नेदं यद्येतौ गजजीवितौ
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ vimānaṁ vaidehi puṣpakaṁ nāma nāmataḥ
divyaṁ tvāṁ dhārayennedaṁ yadyetau gajajīvitau

translations.english: O Vaidehi, if those had lost their lives, this celestial chariot, named Puspaka, would not have held you.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं पुनरसंभ्रान्ता निरुद्विग्ना तरस्विनी
सेना रक्षति काकुत्स्थौ मायया निर्जितौ रणे
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ punarasaṁbhrāntā nirudvignā tarasvinī
senā rakṣati kākutsthau māyayā nirjitau raṇe

translations.english: An army that has its heroes and chiefs slainbecoming dispirited and drooping, range the field, like a vessel on water that has losi its helmsman. But, O lorm one, these troops, be trying neither agitation nor anxiety, are guarding the Kākutsthas, This I tell you of them out of affection.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वं भव सुविस्रब्धा अनुमानैः सुखोदयैः
अहतौ पश्य काकुत्स्थौ स्नेहादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते
verses.transliteration:
sā tvaṁ bhava suvisrabdhā anumānaiḥ sukhodayaiḥ
ahatau paśya kākutsthau snehādetadbravīmi te

translations.english: Do you, at this conclusion bringing in joy, take comfort; and behold the Kākutsthas unslain. This I tell you from affection.

verses.sanskrit:
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन
चारित्रसुखशीलत्वात्प्रविष्टासि मनो मम
verses.transliteration:
anṛtaṁ noktapūrvaṁ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
cāritrasukhaśīlatvātpraviṣṭāsi mano mama

translations.english: I never told you untruths heretofore; nor, O Mithila's daughter, will I tell them to you now. You by virtue of your character conducive to delight, have found an access into my heart.

verses.sanskrit:
नेमौ शक्यौ रणे जेतुं सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
एतयोराननं दृष्ट्वा मया चावेदितं तव
verses.transliteration:
nemau śakyau raṇe jetuṁ sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ
etayorānanaṁ dṛṣṭvā mayā cāveditaṁ tava

translations.english: These even the celestials and Asuras with Indra (at their head) are incompetent to quell. Seeing such sight, I speak to you as to their being alive.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं च सुमहच्चिह्नं शनैः पश्यस्व मैथिलि
निःसंज्ञावप्युभावेतौ नैव लक्ष्मीर्वियुज्यते
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ ca sumahaccihnaṁ śanaiḥ paśyasva maithili
niḥsaṁjñāvapyubhāvetau naiva lakṣmīrviyujyate

translations.english: And behold O Maithili, this mighty wonder! These are lying insensible with arrows; but of these Grace has not taken leave.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रायेण गतसत्त्वानां पुरुषाणां गतायुषाम्
दृश्यमानेषु वक्त्रेषु परं भवति वैकृतम्
verses.transliteration:
prāyeṇa gatasattvānāṁ puruṣāṇāṁ gatāyuṣām
dṛśyamāneṣu vaktreṣu paraṁ bhavati vaikṛtam

translations.english: It generally happens that the faces of persons dead and gone, are unsightly to a degree. Therefore, O Janka's daughter, leave off grief and sorrow and stupor. For the sake of Rāma and Lakşmaņa you can not today put a period to your existence.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्याः सीता सुरसुतोपमा
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमेवमस्त्विति मैथिली
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu vacanaṁ tasyāḥ sītā surasutopamā
kṛtāñjaliruvācedamevamastviti maithilī

translations.english: Hearing her words, Mithila's daughter-Sītāresembling the daughter of a celestial, with hands joined, said, "May this be so!

verses.sanskrit:
विमानं पुष्पकं तत्तु समिवर्त्य मनोजवम्
दीना त्रिजटया सीता लङ्कामेव प्रवेशिता
verses.transliteration:
vimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ tattu samivartya manojavam
dīnā trijaṭayā sītā laṅkāmeva praveśitā

translations.english: Then turning away the car Puşpaka fleet as the mind, the distressed Sītā entered Lankā along with Trijata.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्रिजटया सार्धं पुष्पकादवरुह्य सा
अशोकवनिकामेव रक्षसीभिः प्रवेशिता
verses.transliteration:
tatastrijaṭayā sārdhaṁ puṣpakādavaruhya sā
aśokavanikāmeva rakṣasībhiḥ praveśitā

translations.english: Then in company with Trijatā alighting from Puşpaka, she along with the Rākşasis entered the asoka wood.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविश्य सीता बहुवृक्षषण्डां; तां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विहारभूमिम्
संप्रेक्ष्य संचिन्त्य च राजपुत्रौ; परं विषादं समुपाजगाम
verses.transliteration:
praviśya sītā bahuvṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṁ; tāṁ rākṣasendrasya vihārabhūmim
saṁprekṣya saṁcintya ca rājaputrau; paraṁ viṣādaṁ samupājagāma

translations.english: Entering that sporting-ground of the Raksasa lord abounding in woody tracts, Sītā, having beheld those princes and reflected on them, became subject to a mighty grief.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरेण शरबन्धेन बद्धौ दशरथात्मजौ
निश्वसन्तौ यथा नागौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
ghoreṇa śarabandhena baddhau daśarathātmajau
niśvasantau yathā nāgau śayānau rudhirokṣitau

translations.english: Bound up terribly with shafts, Dasaratha's sons, lying down bathed in blood, sighed hard like to serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः ससुग्रीवा महाबलाः
परिवार्य महात्मानौ तस्थुः शोकपरिप्लुताः
verses.transliteration:
sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ sasugrīvā mahābalāḥ
parivārya mahātmānau tasthuḥ śokapariplutāḥ

translations.english: All those foremost monkeys, along with Sugrīva, possessed of exceeding strength, overwhelmed with sorrow, remained surrounding those high-souled ones.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तेरे रामः प्रत्यबुध्यत वीर्यवान्
स्थिरत्वात्सत्त्वयोगाच्च शरैः संदानितोऽपि सन्
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantere rāmaḥ pratyabudhyata vīryavān
sthiratvātsattvayogācca śaraiḥ saṁdānito'pi san

translations.english: In the meanwhile, the powerful Rāma, albeit fast bound by the shafts, awoke by virtue of the exceeding toughness of his person, as well as his might.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दृष्ट्वा सरुधिरं विषण्णं गाढमर्पितम्
भ्रातरं दीनवदनं पर्यदेवयदातुरः
verses.transliteration:
tato dṛṣṭvā sarudhiraṁ viṣaṇṇaṁ gāḍhamarpitam
bhrātaraṁ dīnavadanaṁ paryadevayadāturaḥ

translations.english: Then, seeing his brother having a distressful countenance, covered with blood, feeble, and fast bound by the shafts, Rāma, greatly aggrieved, began to mourn.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु मे सीतया कार्यं किं कार्यं जीवितेन वा
शयानं योऽद्य पश्यामि भ्रातरं युधि निर्जितम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu me sītayā kāryaṁ kiṁ kāryaṁ jīvitena vā
śayānaṁ yo'dya paśyāmi bhrātaraṁ yudhi nirjitam

translations.english: Of what use to me is the recovery of Sītă, or life either, when today I see my brother vanquished in fight and lying down in the field?

verses.sanskrit:
शक्या सीता समा नारी प्राप्तुं लोके विचिन्वता
न लक्ष्मणसमो भ्राता सचिवः साम्परायिकः
verses.transliteration:
śakyā sītā samā nārī prāptuṁ loke vicinvatā
na lakṣmaṇasamo bhrātā sacivaḥ sāmparāyikaḥ

translations.english: Seeking in the world (of men), I may light upon a woman like Sītā; but never on a brother, or a helper, or a warrior like to Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
परित्यक्ष्याम्यहं प्राणान्वानराणां तु पश्यताम्
यदि पञ्चत्वमापन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
parityakṣyāmyahaṁ prāṇānvānarāṇāṁ tu paśyatām
yadi pañcatvamāpannaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ

translations.english: If that enhancer of Sumitra's joy have met with his end, my life I must renounce in the sight of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यां मातरं किं नु कैकयीम्
कथमम्बां सुमित्रांच पुत्रदर्शनलालसाम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu vakṣyāmi kausalyāṁ mātaraṁ kiṁ nu kaikayīm
kathamambāṁ sumitrāṁca putradarśanalālasām

translations.english: What shall I say to Kausalyā; and what shall I say to Kaikeyi? And what shall I say to mother Sumitrā eager for a sight of her son? And if I go (back) without him, how shall I soothe her, like to a cow reft of her calf; and trembling; and resembling a mourning Kurari?

verses.sanskrit:
कथं वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्
मया सह वनं यातो विना तेनागतः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ vakṣyāmi śatrughnaṁ bharataṁ ca yaśasvinam
mayā saha vanaṁ yāto vinā tenāgataḥ punaḥ

translations.english: How shall I say to Satrughna and the illustrious Bharata, 'He went with me to the forest; but I come (back) here without him "?

verses.sanskrit:
उपालम्भं न शक्ष्यामि सोढुं बत सुमित्रया
इहैव देहं त्यक्ष्यामि न हि जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
upālambhaṁ na śakṣyāmi soḍhuṁ bata sumitrayā
ihaiva dehaṁ tyakṣyāmi na hi jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: I shall not be able to bear the rebuke of mother Sumitră. Therefore even here shall I renounce my person; for certainly I dare not live.

verses.sanskrit:
धिङ्मां दुष्कृतकर्माणमनार्यं यत्कृते ह्यसौ
लक्ष्मणः पतितः शेते शरतल्पे गतासुवत्
verses.transliteration:
dhiṅmāṁ duṣkṛtakarmāṇamanāryaṁ yatkṛte hyasau
lakṣmaṇaḥ patitaḥ śete śaratalpe gatāsuvat

translations.english: Fie on me, who am wicked and base; for me this Lakşmaņa, brought down, leith in the field of battle, like one that is without life.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं नित्यं सुविषण्णं मामाश्वासयसि लक्ष्मण
गतासुर्नाद्य शक्नोषि मामार्तमभिभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ nityaṁ suviṣaṇṇaṁ māmāśvāsayasi lakṣmaṇa
gatāsurnādya śaknoṣi māmārtamabhibhāṣitum

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, you ever comforts me when I am dispirited. But today, having lost your life, you can not speak to me, who am afflicted.

verses.sanskrit:
येनाद्य बहवो युद्धे राक्षसा निहताः क्षितौ
तस्यामेव क्षितौ वीरः स शेते निहतः परैः
verses.transliteration:
yenādya bahavo yuddhe rākṣasā nihatāḥ kṣitau
tasyāmeva kṣitau vīraḥ sa śete nihataḥ paraiḥ

translations.english: You, O hero, who had in battle slain innumerable Rākṣasa lying around, have (at length) yourself been slain in the field with shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
शयानः शरतल्पेऽस्मिन्स्वशोणितपरिप्लुतः
शरजालैश्चितो भाति भास्करोऽस्तमिव व्रजन्
verses.transliteration:
śayānaḥ śaratalpe'sminsvaśoṇitapariplutaḥ
śarajālaiścito bhāti bhāskaro'stamiva vrajan

translations.english: And lying down in the battle-field, bleeding and covered with arrows, you appear like the Sun when he has gone up the Setting-hill.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणाभिहतमर्मत्वान्न शक्नोत्यभिवीक्षितुम्
रुजा चाब्रुवतो ह्यस्य दृष्टिरागेण सूच्यते
verses.transliteration:
bāṇābhihatamarmatvānna śaknotyabhivīkṣitum
rujā cābruvato hyasya dṛṣṭirāgeṇa sūcyate

translations.english: In consequence of shafts piercing your vitals, you cannot speak; but your visible expression, albeit you are dumb, betokens pain.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव मां वनं यान्तमनुयातो महाद्युतिः
अहमप्यनुयास्यामि तथैवैनं यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
yathaiva māṁ vanaṁ yāntamanuyāto mahādyutiḥ
ahamapyanuyāsyāmi tathaivainaṁ yamakṣayam

translations.english: O you endowed with exceeding splendour, even as you did follow me into the forest, will I follow you to the mansion of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
इष्टबन्धुजनो नित्यं मां च नित्यमनुव्रतः
इमामद्य गतोऽवस्थां ममानार्यस्य दुर्नयैः
verses.transliteration:
iṣṭabandhujano nityaṁ māṁ ca nityamanuvrataḥ
imāmadya gato'vasthāṁ mamānāryasya durnayaiḥ

translations.english: You having dear friends, and ever following me, has come by this plight in consequence of my reprehensible conduct.

verses.sanskrit:
सुरुष्टेनापि वीरेण लक्ष्मणेना न संस्मरे
परुषं विप्रियं वापि श्रावितं न कदाचन
verses.transliteration:
suruṣṭenāpi vīreṇa lakṣmaṇenā na saṁsmare
paruṣaṁ vipriyaṁ vāpi śrāvitaṁ na kadācana

translations.english: I do not remember having heard any harsh speech from the heroic Lakşmaņa, even when he had happened to be exceedingly wroth.

verses.sanskrit:
विससर्जैकवेगेन पञ्चबाणशतानि यः
इष्वस्त्रेष्वधिकस्तस्मात्कार्तवीर्याच्च लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
visasarjaikavegena pañcabāṇaśatāni yaḥ
iṣvastreṣvadhikastasmātkārtavīryācca lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: He that could discharge at one shot five hundred shafts, that Lakşmaņa is superior to karttaviryya himself in that weapon-the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि यो हन्याच्छक्रस्यापि महात्मनः
सोऽयमुर्व्यांहतः शेते महार्हशयनोचितः
verses.transliteration:
astrairastrāṇi yo hanyācchakrasyāpi mahātmanaḥ
so'yamurvyāṁhataḥ śete mahārhaśayanocitaḥ

translations.english: He that with his arms could resist the arms of Sakra himself, that one worthy of a costly couchLeith down on the ground, slain.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्च मिथ्या प्रलप्तं मां प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः
यन्मया न कृतो राजा राक्षसानां विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
tacca mithyā pralaptaṁ māṁ pradhakṣyati na saṁśayaḥ
yanmayā na kṛto rājā rākṣasānāṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: That false babble shall now, without doubt, consume me; for by me has not Bibhishna been made monarch of the Rákşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रतियातुमितोऽर्हसि
मत्वा हीनं मया राजन्रावणोऽभिद्रवेद्बली
verses.transliteration:
asminmuhūrte sugrīva pratiyātumito'rhasi
matvā hīnaṁ mayā rājanrāvaṇo'bhidravedbalī

translations.english: Do you, O Sugrīva, this very moment retrace your steps. Bereft of your strength through me you will be worsted by Rāvaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदं तु पुरस्कृत्य ससैन्यः ससुहृज्जनः
सागरं तर सुग्रीव पुनस्तेनैव सेतुना
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadaṁ tu puraskṛtya sasainyaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
sāgaraṁ tara sugrīva punastenaiva setunā

translations.english: O Sugriva, placing Angada to the fore, do you, taking your host as well as the equipage, in company with Nila and Nala, cross over the Ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदेन कृतं कर्म मैन्देन द्विविदेन च
युद्धं केसरिणा संख्ये घोरं संपातिना कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadena kṛtaṁ karma maindena dvividena ca
yuddhaṁ kesariṇā saṁkhye ghoraṁ saṁpātinā kṛtam

translations.english: By you has been achieved a mighty feat incapable of being done by another in battle. And pleased am I with the king of bears, and the lord of Golãngulas; and Angada has quit himself nobly, as also Mainda and Dvivida. And Kesarin and Sampāti have both faught terribly.

verses.sanskrit:
गवयेन गवाक्षेण शरभेण गजेन च
अन्यैश्च हरिभिर्युद्धं मदार्थे त्यक्तजीवितैः
verses.transliteration:
gavayena gavākṣeṇa śarabheṇa gajena ca
anyaiśca haribhiryuddhaṁ madārthe tyaktajīvitaiḥ

translations.english: Gavaya, and Gavākşa, and Sarabha, and Gaja, and other monkeys have faught as others are incapable of fighting, determined to lay down their lives (for me).

verses.sanskrit:
न चातिक्रमितुं शक्यं दैवं सुग्रीव मानुषैः
यत्तु शक्यं वयस्येन सुहृदा वा परंतप
कृतं सुग्रीव तत्सर्वं भवताधर्मभीरुणा
verses.transliteration:
na cātikramituṁ śakyaṁ daivaṁ sugrīva mānuṣaiḥ
yattu śakyaṁ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṁtapa
kṛtaṁ sugrīva tatsarvaṁ bhavatādharmabhīruṇā

translations.english: But, O Sugriva, man cannot overrule Destiny. You, my friend, fearing righteousness, has done what lay in your power. And, You foremost of monkeys, you also have acted as become friends. Now, with my permission, go you whitersoever you are minded.

verses.sanskrit:
शुश्रुवुस्तस्य ते सर्वे वानराः परिदेवितम्
वर्तयां चक्रुरश्रूणि नेत्रैः कृष्णेतरेक्षणाः
verses.transliteration:
śuśruvustasya te sarve vānarāḥ paridevitam
vartayāṁ cakruraśrūṇi netraiḥ kṛṣṇetarekṣaṇāḥ

translations.english: Hearing Rāma's lament, the monkeys-those dark-eyed and others-began to shed tears from their eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि स्थापयित्वा विभीषणः
आजगाम गदापाणिस्त्वरितो यत्र राघवः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sarvāṇyanīkāni sthāpayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
ājagāma gadāpāṇistvarito yatra rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Then Vibhisana, quieting the army, taking a mace in his hand, swiftly went to where Rāghava was.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वरितं यान्तं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्
वानरा दुद्रुवुः सर्वे मन्यमानास्तु रावणिम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tvaritaṁ yāntaṁ nīlāñjanacayopamam
vānarā dudruvuḥ sarve manyamānāstu rāvaṇim

translations.english: Seeing him fast making his way, resembling a mass of dark collyrium, the monkeys taking him to be Ravana's son, began to run away.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोवाच महातेजा हरिराजो महाबलः
किमियं व्यथिता सेना मूढवातेव नौर्जले
verses.transliteration:
athovāca mahātejā harirājo mahābalaḥ
kimiyaṁ vyathitā senā mūḍhavāteva naurjale

translations.english: Then out spoke the highly energetic and exceedingly mighty king of monkeys, “Why is this host agitated like a bark driven hither and thither by the wind?"

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्
न त्वं पश्यसि रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā vāliputro'ṅgado'bravīt
na tvaṁ paśyasi rāmaṁ ca lakṣmaṇaṁ ca mahābalam

translations.english: Hearing Sugriva's speech, Vali's son said, Did you not see both those heroes-sons of Dasaratha, Rama and that mighty car-warriorLakşmaņa-covered with arrows?

verses.sanskrit:
शरजालाचितौ वीरावुभौ दशरथात्मजौ
शरतल्पे महात्मानौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
śarajālācitau vīrāvubhau daśarathātmajau
śaratalpe mahātmānau śayānau rudhirokṣitau

translations.english: And (did you not see) those high-should ones lying in the field of battle, covered with blood?

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्वानरेन्द्रः सुग्रीवः पुत्रमङ्गदम्
नानिमित्तमिदं मन्ये भवितव्यं भयेन तु
verses.transliteration:
athābravīdvānarendraḥ sugrīvaḥ putramaṅgadam
nānimittamidaṁ manye bhavitavyaṁ bhayena tu

translations.english: Thereat, the lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, spoke to his son, Angada "I do not deem it without cause. This may have come to pass through sheer fear.

verses.sanskrit:
विषण्णवदना ह्येते त्यक्तप्रहरणा दिशः
प्रपलायन्ति हरयस्त्रासादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः
verses.transliteration:
viṣaṇṇavadanā hyete tyaktapraharaṇā diśaḥ
prapalāyanti harayastrāsādutphullalocanāḥ

translations.english: These monkeys with sad faces, leaving their arms behind them are flying in all directions, their eyes distended in affright.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यस्य न लज्जन्ते न निरीक्षन्ति पृष्ठतः
विप्रकर्षन्ति चान्योन्यं पतितं लङ्घयन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
anyonyasya na lajjante na nirīkṣanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
viprakarṣanti cānyonyaṁ patitaṁ laṅghayanti ca

translations.english: They are not ashamed of each other, and they do not cast their looks back. And they hug each other, and go leaping over the fallen.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो गदापाणिर्विभीषणः
सुग्रीवं वर्धयामास राघवं च निरैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare vīro gadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ
sugrīvaṁ vardhayāmāsa rāghavaṁ ca niraikṣata

translations.english: In the meanwhile that hero, Vibhisana, bearing a mace in his hand, (approaching) greeted Sugrīva as well as Rāghava with blessings of victory.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणं तं सुग्रीवो दृष्ट्वा वानरभीषणम्
ऋक्षराजं समीपस्थं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇaṁ taṁ sugrīvo dṛṣṭvā vānarabhīṣaṇam
ṛkṣarājaṁ samīpasthaṁ jāmbavantamuvāca ha

translations.english: And Sugriva, seeing Vibhisana, capable of inspiring fear in the monkeys, spoke to the highsouled sovereign of bears, who stood by.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणोऽयं संप्राप्तो यं दृष्ट्वा वानरर्षभाः
विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्ता रावणात्मजशङ्कया
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇo'yaṁ saṁprāpto yaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānararṣabhāḥ
vidravanti paritrastā rāvaṇātmajaśaṅkayā

translations.english: This is Vibhișana that has come hither, seeing whom the foremost among the monkeys, from fear of Rāvana's son who, they apprehend, he is, are fleeing away, seized with a panic.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रमेतान्सुवित्रस्तान्बहुधा विप्रधावितान्
पर्यवस्थापयाख्याहि विभीषणमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
śīghrametānsuvitrastānbahudhā vipradhāvitān
paryavasthāpayākhyāhi vibhīṣaṇamupasthitam

translations.english: Do you at once stay these agitated with fear and scampering all around; and proclaim, 'This is Vibhisana, who has come here.'

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु जाम्बवानृक्षपार्थिवः
वानरान्सान्त्वयामास संनिवर्त्य प्रहावतः
verses.transliteration:
sugrīveṇaivamuktastu jāmbavānṛkṣapārthivaḥ
vānarānsāntvayāmāsa saṁnivartya prahāvataḥ

translations.english: Thus directed, Jõmbavān-king of bearsrestraining those that were flying, composed the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ते निवृत्ताः पुनः सर्वे वानरास्त्यक्तसंभ्रमाः
ऋक्षराजवचः श्रुत्वा तं च दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्
verses.transliteration:
te nivṛttāḥ punaḥ sarve vānarāstyaktasaṁbhramāḥ
ṛkṣarājavacaḥ śrutvā taṁ ca dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam

translations.english: Hearing the bear-king's words, and seeing Vibhisana, the monkeys, renouncing fear, desisted (from their flight).

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा गात्रं शरैश्चितम्
लक्ष्मणस्य च धर्मात्मा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇastu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā gātraṁ śaraiścitam
lakṣmaṇasya ca dharmātmā babhūva vyathitendriyaḥ

translations.english: Then the righteous Vibhīșaņa, viewing Rama's as well as Laksmana's body pierced with arrows, was exceedingly aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit:
जलक्लिन्नेन हस्तेन तयोर्नेत्रे प्रमृज्य च
शोकसंपीडितमना रुरोद विललाप च
verses.transliteration:
jalaklinnena hastena tayornetre pramṛjya ca
śokasaṁpīḍitamanā ruroda vilalāpa ca

translations.english: Washing their eyes with water, he, with his mind overpowered with grief, began to weep and broke out into lamentation.

verses.sanskrit:
इमौ तौ सत्त्वसंपन्नौ विक्रान्तौ प्रियसंयुगौ
इमामवस्थां गमितौ राकसैः कूटयोधिभिः
verses.transliteration:
imau tau sattvasaṁpannau vikrāntau priyasaṁyugau
imāmavasthāṁ gamitau rākasaiḥ kūṭayodhibhiḥ

translations.english: The Rāksasas, fighting in wily ways, have brought to this pass these ones endowed with prowess and possessed of every perfection and gifted with might (of arm).

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुः पुत्रेण मे तेन दुष्पुत्रेण दुरात्मना
राक्षस्या जिह्मया बुद्ध्या छलितावृजुविक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
bhrātuḥ putreṇa me tena duṣputreṇa durātmanā
