rākṣasyā jihmayā buddhyā chalitāvṛjuvikramau

translations.english: And with his guileful mind, that brother's son of mine, wicked-souled and an evil son (to me), has deceived these ones of straight prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
शरैरिमावलं विद्धौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ
वसुधायामिम सुप्तौ दृश्येते शल्यकाविव
verses.transliteration:
śarairimāvalaṁ viddhau rudhireṇa samukṣitau
vasudhāyāmima suptau dṛśyete śalyakāviva

translations.english: Pierced with innumerable shafts, and covered with blood, these are lying on the ground like Salyakas.

verses.sanskrit:
ययोर्वीर्यमुपाश्रित्य प्रतिष्ठा काङ्क्षिता मया
तावुभौ देहनाशाय प्रसुप्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ
verses.transliteration:
yayorvīryamupāśritya pratiṣṭhā kāṅkṣitā mayā
tāvubhau dehanāśāya prasuptau puruṣarṣabhau

translations.english: Those depending on whose prowess, I had sought eminence, those foremost of men, sleep here soundly for renouncing their bodies.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवन्नद्य विपन्नोऽस्मि नष्टराज्यमनोरथः
प्राप्तप्रतिज्ञश्च रिपुः सकामो रावणः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
jīvannadya vipanno'smi naṣṭarājyamanorathaḥ
prāptapratijñaśca ripuḥ sakāmo rāvaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Living, today I am in distress: and my desire of dominion is annihilated; and my foe, Rāvana, has his promise fulfilled and his aim crowned with success.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपमानं तं परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसंपन्नो हरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapamānaṁ taṁ pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam
sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṁpanno harirājo'bravīdidam

translations.english: As Vibhīşana was thus lamenting, the lord of monkeys-Sugriva-endowed with strength, embracing him spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं प्राप्स्यसि धर्मज्ञ लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः
रावणः सह पुत्रेण स राज्यं नेह लप्स्यते
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ prāpsyasi dharmajña laṅkāyāṁ nātra saṁśayaḥ
rāvaṇaḥ saha putreṇa sa rājyaṁ neha lapsyate

translations.english: O you cognisant of righteousness, you will here in Lankā obtain empire: no doubt of this; and Răvaņa along with his sons will be disappointed in their expectations.

verses.sanskrit:
शरसंपीडितावेतावुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ
त्यक्त्वा मोहं वधिष्येते सगणं रावणं रणे
verses.transliteration:
śarasaṁpīḍitāvetāvubhau rāghavalakṣmaṇau
tyaktvā mohaṁ vadhiṣyete sagaṇaṁ rāvaṇaṁ raṇe

translations.english: Both these-Rāma and Lakşmaņa-are under the aegis of Garuda; and, casting off their stupor: they will in battle slay Rävaņa along with his adherents.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवं सान्त्वयित्वा तु समाश्वास्य च राक्षसं
सुषेणं श्वशुरं पार्श्वे सुग्रीवस्तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tamevaṁ sāntvayitvā tu samāśvāsya ca rākṣasaṁ
suṣeṇaṁ śvaśuraṁ pārśve sugrīvastamuvāca ha

translations.english: Having thus soothed and comforted the Raksasa, Sugriva addressed his father-in-law, who was at his side, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सह शूरैर्हरिगणैर्लब्धसंज्ञावरिंदमौ
गच्छ त्वं भ्रातरौ गृह्य किष्किन्धां रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
saha śūrairharigaṇairlabdhasaṁjñāvariṁdamau
gaccha tvaṁ bhrātarau gṛhya kiṣkindhāṁ rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Do you along with numbers of heroic monkeys, taking those repressors of foes, the brothers-Rama and Laksmana-when they shall have regained their consciousness, repair to Kiskindha.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु रावणं हत्वा सपुत्रं सहबान्धवम्
मैथिलीमानयिष्यामि शक्रो नष्टामिव श्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu rāvaṇaṁ hatvā saputraṁ sahabāndhavam
maithilīmānayiṣyāmi śakro naṣṭāmiva śriyam

translations.english: And I, slaying Råvaņa along with his sons and friends, shall bring back Mithila's daughter, even as Sakra recovered the lost Sri.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वैतद्वानरेन्द्रस्य सुषेणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
देवासुरं महायुद्धमनुभूतं सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvaitadvānarendrasya suṣeṇo vākyamabravīt
devāsuraṁ mahāyuddhamanubhūtaṁ sudāruṇam

translations.english: Hearing the words of the monkey-king, Suşeņa said, I had witnessed the war of yore between the gods and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा स्म दानवा देवाञ्शरसंस्पर्शकोविदाः
निजघ्नुः शस्त्रविदुषश्छादयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
tadā sma dānavā devāñśarasaṁsparśakovidāḥ
nijaghnuḥ śastraviduṣaśchādayanto muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: Then the Dänavas, enveloping themselves, momentarily destroyed the deities, albeit versed in arms and accomplished in weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तानार्तान्नष्टसंज्ञांश्च परासूंश्च बृहस्पतिः
विध्याभिर्मन्त्रयुक्ताभिरोषधीभिश्चिकित्सति
verses.transliteration:
tānārtānnaṣṭasaṁjñāṁśca parāsūṁśca bṛhaspatiḥ
vidhyābhirmantrayuktābhiroṣadhībhiścikitsati

translations.english: They, their senses lost, and their lives departed, Bịhaspati treated by means of his knowledge of mantras, as well with medicines.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यौषधान्यानयितुं क्षीरोदं यान्तु सागरम्
जवेन वानराः शीघ्रं संपाति पनसादयः
verses.transliteration:
tānyauṣadhānyānayituṁ kṣīrodaṁ yāntu sāgaram
javena vānarāḥ śīghraṁ saṁpāti panasādayaḥ

translations.english: Let Sampati, Panasa, and other monkeys speedily hie to the Milky Ocean for the purpose of bringing those medicines.

verses.sanskrit:
हरयस्तु विजानन्ति पार्वती ते महौषधी
संजीवकरणीं दिव्यां विशल्यां देवनिर्मिताम्
verses.transliteration:
harayastu vijānanti pārvatī te mahauṣadhī
saṁjīvakaraṇīṁ divyāṁ viśalyāṁ devanirmitām

translations.english: The monkeys well know that mighty mountainous medicine-divine and capable of reviving the dead, and made by the deities themselves-visalya.

verses.sanskrit:
चन्द्रश्च नाम द्रोणश्च पर्वतौ सागरोत्तमे
अमृतं यत्र मथितं तत्र ते परमौषधी
verses.transliteration:
candraśca nāma droṇaśca parvatau sāgarottame
amṛtaṁ yatra mathitaṁ tatra te paramauṣadhī

translations.english: There are (the mountains) named Candra and Drona: where the ambrosia was churned, there is that supreme drug. And those mountains have been placed by the deities in the mighty deep. And, o king, let the son of the Wing-god go thither.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्मेघांश्चापि सविद्युतः
पर्यस्यन्सागरे तोयं कम्पयन्निव पर्वतान्
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare vāyurmeghāṁścāpi savidyutaḥ
paryasyansāgare toyaṁ kampayanniva parvatān

translations.english: In the meanwhile, the wing arose, and masses of clouds appeared along with lightning, and the wind blew, agitating the waters of the deep, and shaking the mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
महता पक्षवातेन सर्वे द्वीपमहाद्रुमाः
निपेतुर्भग्नविटपाः समूला लवणाम्भसि
verses.transliteration:
mahatā pakṣavātena sarve dvīpamahādrumāḥ
nipeturbhagnaviṭapāḥ samūlā lavaṇāmbhasi

translations.english: And mighty trees of the ocean-islands, broken down by-the terrible wing-raised wind, began to topple headlong into the salt waters.

verses.sanskrit:
अभवन्पन्नगास्त्रस्ता भोगिनस्तत्रवासिनः
शीघ्रं सर्वाणि यादांसि जग्मुश्च लवणार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
abhavanpannagāstrastā bhoginastatravāsinaḥ
śīghraṁ sarvāṇi yādāṁsi jagmuśca lavaṇārṇavam

translations.english: The serpents dwelling there were seized with affright; and speedily all the aquatic animals dived into the Salt sea,

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मुहूर्तद्गरुडं वैनतेयं महाबलम्
वानरा ददृशुः सर्वे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्
verses.transliteration:
tato muhūrtadgaruḍaṁ vainateyaṁ mahābalam
vānarā dadṛśuḥ sarve jvalantamiva pāvakam

translations.english: Then in a moment the monkeys saw Vinatā's son possessed of terrific strength, like to a flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य नागास्ते विप्रदुद्रुवुः
यैस्तौ सत्पुरुषौ बद्धौ शरभूतैर्महाबलौ
verses.transliteration:
tamāgatamabhiprekṣya nāgāste vipradudruvuḥ
yaistau satpuruṣau baddhau śarabhūtairmahābalau

translations.english: Seeing him come, the serpents began to dart away, those exceedingly powerful ones that, turning into shafts, had bound those persons.* *Rama and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुपर्णः काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यभिनन्द्य च
विममर्श च पाणिभ्यां मुखे चन्द्रसमप्रभे
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suparṇaḥ kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā pratyabhinandya ca
vimamarśa ca pāṇibhyāṁ mukhe candrasamaprabhe

translations.english: Then, touching the Kākutsthas and saluting them, Suparna rubbed with his hands their countenances furnished with the splendour of the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
वैनतेयेन संस्पृष्टास्तयोः संरुरुहुर्व्रणाः
सुवर्णे च तनू स्निग्धे तयोराशु बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration:
vainateyena saṁspṛṣṭāstayoḥ saṁruruhurvraṇāḥ
suvarṇe ca tanū snigdhe tayorāśu babhūvatuḥ

translations.english: Their wounds, on being touched by Vinata's son, were (immediately) healed: and the bodies of both speedily became cool and shone with an excellent complexion.

verses.sanskrit:
तेजो वीर्यं बलं चौज उत्साहश्च महागुणाः
प्रदर्शनं च बुद्धिश्च स्मृतिश्च द्विगुणं तयोः
verses.transliteration:
tejo vīryaṁ balaṁ cauja utsāhaśca mahāguṇāḥ
pradarśanaṁ ca buddhiśca smṛtiśca dviguṇaṁ tayoḥ

translations.english: They attained immense energy and prowess; and a double share of strength, and of rational and perceptive powers, and of memory.

verses.sanskrit:
तावुत्थाप्य महावीर्यौ गरुडो वासवोपमौ
उभौ तौ सस्वजे हृष्टौ रामश्चैनमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tāvutthāpya mahāvīryau garuḍo vāsavopamau
ubhau tau sasvaje hṛṣṭau rāmaścainamuvāca ha

translations.english: Then raising them up, the exceedingly energetic Garuda, resembling Vāşava himself, embraced both joyfully. And then Rāma addressed (Garuda), saying.

verses.sanskrit:
भवत्प्रसादाद्व्यसनं रावणिप्रभवं महत्
आवामिह व्यतिक्रान्तौ शीघ्रं च बलिनौ कृतौ
verses.transliteration:
bhavatprasādādvyasanaṁ rāvaṇiprabhavaṁ mahat
āvāmiha vyatikrāntau śīghraṁ ca balinau kṛtau

translations.english: By your grace we have through means survived the mighty calamity that had sprung from Răvana's son; and we have also speedily been rendered strong.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा तातं दशरथं यथाजं च पितामहम्
तथा भवन्तमासाद्य हृषयं मे प्रसीदति
verses.transliteration:
yathā tātaṁ daśarathaṁ yathājaṁ ca pitāmaham
tathā bhavantamāsādya hṛṣayaṁ me prasīdati

translations.english: My heart is delighted on having these, like to my father, Dasaratha, or my grand sire, Aja.

verses.sanskrit:
को भवान्रूपसंपन्नो दिव्यस्रगनुलेपनः
वसानो विरजे वस्त्रे दिव्याभरणभूषितः
verses.transliteration:
ko bhavānrūpasaṁpanno divyasraganulepanaḥ
vasāno viraje vastre divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ

translations.english: Who are your, furnished with beauty, and bearing wreaths and unguents (on your person); clad in stainless attire: and adorned in noble ornaments?

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच महातेजा वैनतेयो महाबलः
पतत्रिराजः प्रीतात्मा हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca mahātejā vainateyo mahābalaḥ
patatrirājaḥ prītātmā harṣaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: To him spoke the exceedingly energetic son of Vinată endowed with great strength, the lord of birds, with a pleased heart, and his eyes wild with glee.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं सखा ते काकुत्स्थ प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः
गरुत्मानिह संप्राप्तो युवयोः साह्यकारणात्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ sakhā te kākutstha priyaḥ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ
garutmāniha saṁprāpto yuvayoḥ sāhyakāraṇāt

translations.english: O Kakutstha, I am your friend-your life ranging externally-Garutmän. I am come hither for aiding you.

verses.sanskrit:
सभाग्यश्चासि धर्मज्ञ राम सत्यपराक्रम
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा समरे रिपुघातिना
verses.transliteration:
sabhāgyaścāsi dharmajña rāma satyaparākrama
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā samare ripughātinā

translations.english: O Ráma having truth for prowess, you are fortunate-along with that destroyer of foe in fight, Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
इमं श्रुत्वा तु वृत्तान्तं त्वरमाणोऽहमागतः
सहसा युवयोः स्नेहात्सखित्वमनुपालयन्
verses.transliteration:
imaṁ śrutvā tu vṛttāntaṁ tvaramāṇo'hamāgataḥ
sahasā yuvayoḥ snehātsakhitvamanupālayan

translations.english: Hearing this, I, summoning energy: have come hither swiftly, and I, doing by you as a friend, have from affection at once set you free from these dreadful arrowy bonds.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या राक्षसाः सर्वे संग्रामे कूटयोधिनः
शूराणां शुद्धभावानां भवतामार्जवं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā rākṣasāḥ sarve saṁgrāme kūṭayodhinaḥ
śūrāṇāṁ śuddhabhāvānāṁ bhavatāmārjavaṁ balam

translations.english: you should always be on your guard. By nature the Rākşasas have cunning shifts in fight and you, who are heroic and of a pure spirit, can but rely on your simplicity alone for strength.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्न विश्वसितव्यं वो राक्षसानां रणाजिरे
एतेनैवोपमानेन नित्यजिह्मा हि राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
tanna viśvasitavyaṁ vo rākṣasānāṁ raṇājire
etenaivopamānena nityajihmā hi rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: Therefore you must not trust the Raksasas in the field of battle. By this one instance you must know that Rakşasas are ever deceitful in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामं सुपर्णः सुमहाबलः
परिष्वज्य सुहृत्स्निग्धमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rāmaṁ suparṇaḥ sumahābalaḥ
pariṣvajya suhṛtsnigdhamāpraṣṭumupacakrame

translations.english: Having said this the wondrous mighty Suparna, embracing Rama tenderly again) said.

verses.sanskrit:
सखे राघव धर्मज्ञ रिपूणामपि वत्सल
अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि गमिष्यामि यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
sakhe rāghava dharmajña ripūṇāmapi vatsala
abhyanujñātumicchāmi gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam

translations.english: My friend Raghava, O you who even cherish affection for your foes, permit me, I shall go at pleasure. And O Raghva, entertain no curiosity as to our friendship. when, O hero, you shall have achieved success in battle, you shall know all about this friendship of ours.

verses.sanskrit:
बालवृद्धावशेषां तु लङ्कां कृत्वा शरोर्मिभिः
रावणं च रिपुं हत्वा सीतां समुपलप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
bālavṛddhāvaśeṣāṁ tu laṅkāṁ kṛtvā śarormibhiḥ
rāvaṇaṁ ca ripuṁ hatvā sītāṁ samupalapsyase

translations.english: And with the surges of your shafts, making Larkā contain only children and aged, and slaying your foe, Ravana, you shall recover Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणं ततः कृत्वा परिष्वज्य च वीर्यवान्
जगामाकाशमाविश्य सुपर्णः पवनो यथा
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇaṁ tataḥ kṛtvā pariṣvajya ca vīryavān
jagāmākāśamāviśya suparṇaḥ pavano yathā

translations.english: Having spoken thus, Suparna, endowed with vigour, having rendered Rāma hale in the midst of the monkeys, having gone round them and embrace them also, that one possessed of prowess, set out, covering up the sky, like to the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
विरुजौ राघवौ दृष्ट्वा ततो वानरयूथपाः
सिंहनादांस्तदा नेदुर्लाङ्गूलं दुधुवुश्च ते
verses.transliteration:
virujau rāghavau dṛṣṭvā tato vānarayūthapāḥ
siṁhanādāṁstadā nedurlāṅgūlaṁ dudhuvuśca te

translations.english: Seeing Raghu's sons rendered hale, the monkey-leaders set up leonine roars, and began to flourish their tails.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भेरीः समाजघ्नुर्मृदङ्गांश्च व्यनादयन्
दध्मुः शङ्खान्संप्रहृष्टाः क्ष्वेलन्त्यपि यथापुरम्
verses.transliteration:
tato bherīḥ samājaghnurmṛdaṅgāṁśca vyanādayan
dadhmuḥ śaṅkhānsaṁprahṛṣṭāḥ kṣvelantyapi yathāpuram

translations.english: Then beat the kettle-drums and the drums struck up. And conchs were cheerfully blown; and shouts were sent.

verses.sanskrit:
विसृजन्तो महानादांस्त्रासयन्तो निशाचरान्
लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुर्योद्धुकामाः प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
visṛjanto mahānādāṁstrāsayanto niśācarān
laṅkādvārāṇyupājagmuryoddhukāmāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: And others struck at their arms with their hands. The monkeys, accustomed to battle with trees, uprooting them, stood by hundreds and thousands. And emitting tremendous roars and thereby frightening the night-rangers, the monkeys eager for encounter, approached the gate of Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु भीमस्तुमुलो निनादो; बभूव शाखामृगयूथपानाम्
क्षये निदाघस्य यथा घनानां; नादः सुभीमो नदतां निशीथे
verses.transliteration:
tatastu bhīmastumulo ninādo; babhūva śākhāmṛgayūthapānām
kṣaye nidāghasya yathā ghanānāṁ; nādaḥ subhīmo nadatāṁ niśīthe

translations.english: That mighty and dreadful din raised by the monkeys, resembled the terrible rumbling of the clouds at midnight about the end of Summer.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां सुतुमुलं शब्दं वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
नर्दतां राक्षसैः सार्धं तदा शुश्राव रावणः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ sutumulaṁ śabdaṁ vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
nardatāṁ rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṁ tadā śuśrāva rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then Rāvana heard the tumult raised by the highly energetic monkeys roaring in company with the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा स निनदं भृशम्
सचिवानां ततस्तेषां मध्ये वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
snigdhagambhīranirghoṣaṁ śrutvā sa ninadaṁ bhṛśam
sacivānāṁ tatasteṣāṁ madhye vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing that low and solemn noise-that prodigious uproar-Rävaņa said in the midst of his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
यथासौ संप्रहृष्टानां वानराणां समुत्थितः
बहूनां सुमहान्नादो मेघानामिव गर्जताम्
verses.transliteration:
yathāsau saṁprahṛṣṭānāṁ vānarāṇāṁ samutthitaḥ
bahūnāṁ sumahānnādo meghānāmiva garjatām

translations.english: From mighty roars that are heard of in innumerous delighted monkeys, resembling the roar of couds, it is evident, beyond a doubt, that there is great rejoicing there. And the salt Ocean is vexed with these thundering noises.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तु बद्धौ शरैस्तीष्क्णैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
अयं च सुमहान्नादः शङ्कां जनयतीव मे
verses.transliteration:
tau tu baddhau śaraistīṣkṇairbhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
ayaṁ ca sumahānnādaḥ śaṅkāṁ janayatīva me

translations.english: The brother-Rama and Laksmana-have been fast bound with sharp shafts, and here this uproar is exciting my alarm.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्तु वचनं चोक्त्वा मन्त्रिणो राक्षसेश्वरः
उवाच नैरृतांस्तत्र समीपपरिवर्तिनः
verses.transliteration:
etattu vacanaṁ coktvā mantriṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
uvāca nairṛtāṁstatra samīpaparivartinaḥ

translations.english: Having spoken thus to his ministers, the lord of the Rākşasas addressed the Naiſtas present there, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञायतां तूर्णमेतषां सर्वेषां वनचारिणाम्
शोककाले समुत्पन्ने हर्षकारणमुत्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
jñāyatāṁ tūrṇametaṣāṁ sarveṣāṁ vanacāriṇām
śokakāle samutpanne harṣakāraṇamutthitam

translations.english: Do you speedily acquaint yourselves with the cause of rejoicing that has arisen of these monkeys on this mournful occasion.

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्तास्तेन संभ्रान्ताः प्राकारमधिरुह्य ते
ददृशुः पालितां सेनां सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
tathoktāstena saṁbhrāntāḥ prākāramadhiruhya te
dadṛśuḥ pālitāṁ senāṁ sugrīveṇa mahātmanā

translations.english: Thus accosted, they hurriedly mounting up on the wall, surveyed the forces maintained by the high-souled Sugrīva as well as those exalted ones-Raghu's sons-emancipated from their terrific arrowy fetters and arisen (now).

verses.sanskrit:
संत्रस्तहृदया सर्वे प्राकारादवरुह्य ते
विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे राक्षसेन्द्रमुपस्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
saṁtrastahṛdayā sarve prākārādavaruhya te
viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve rākṣasendramupasthitāḥ

translations.english: Thereat, with their hearts wrought up, grimvisaged Rākşasas descending from the wall appeared before the Rākşasa-lord with pale faces.

verses.sanskrit:
तदप्रियं दीनमुखा रावणस्य निशाचराः
कृत्स्नं निवेदयामासुर्यथावद्वाक्यकोविदाः
verses.transliteration:
tadapriyaṁ dīnamukhā rāvaṇasya niśācarāḥ
kṛtsnaṁ nivedayāmāsuryathāvadvākyakovidāḥ

translations.english: Then with woe-begone faces, those Raksasas, skilled in speech, faithfully informed Rāvana in full of that unfortunate circumstance.

verses.sanskrit:
यौ ताविन्द्रजिता युद्धे भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
निबद्धौ शरबन्धेन निष्प्रकम्पभुजौ कृतौ
verses.transliteration:
yau tāvindrajitā yuddhe bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
nibaddhau śarabandhena niṣprakampabhujau kṛtau

translations.english: Those brothers-Rāma and Lakşmaņa-who had in battle been bound up in arrowy fetters by Indrajit, and whose arms lay moveless, having been emancipated from the arrowy bonds, are seen in the field of battle; and those ones like to the foremost of elephants in strength, seem like elephants that have snapped their fetters.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः
चिन्ताशोकसमाक्रान्तो विषण्णवदनोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vacanaṁ teṣāṁ rākṣasendro mahābalaḥ
cintāśokasamākrānto viṣaṇṇavadano'bravīt

translations.english: Hearing those words of theirs, the exceedingly powerful lord of the Raksasas was wrought up with anxiety and anger, and his countenance lost its complexion.

verses.sanskrit:
घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्बद्धौ शरैराशीविषोमपैः
अमोघैः सूर्यसंकाशैः प्रमथ्येन्द्रजिता युधि
verses.transliteration:
ghorairdattavarairbaddhau śarairāśīviṣomapaiḥ
amoghaiḥ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ pramathyendrajitā yudhi

translations.english: Indrajit, having routed them in conflict, had bound them by means of irresistible and terrible arrows, resembling venomous serpents, and like to the Sun himself, which had been conferred on (Indrajit) as boons. But if my enemy having actually been bound by the weapons, can have been liberated, all this strength of mine I see placed in peril.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्फलाः खलु संवृत्ताः शरा वासुकितेजसः
आदत्तं यैस्तु संग्रामे रिपूणां मम जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
niṣphalāḥ khalu saṁvṛttāḥ śarā vāsukitejasaḥ
ādattaṁ yaistu saṁgrāme ripūṇāṁ mama jīvitam

translations.english: And those shafts resembling Fire in fierceness, which had in battle deprived my foes of their lives, have forsooth been rendered fruitless.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु संक्रुद्धो निश्वसन्नुरगो यथा
अब्रवीद्रक्षसां मध्ये धूम्राक्षं नाम राकसं
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu saṁkruddho niśvasannurago yathā
abravīdrakṣasāṁ madhye dhūmrākṣaṁ nāma rākasaṁ

translations.english: Having said this in high rage Rāvana, sighing like a serpent, addressed a Raksasa, named Dhūmrākṣa, seated in the midst of the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
बलेन महता युक्तो रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
त्वं वधायाभिनिर्याहि रामस्य सह वानरैः
verses.transliteration:
balena mahatā yukto rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām
tvaṁ vadhāyābhiniryāhi rāmasya saha vānaraiḥ

translations.english: O you of dreadful prowess, surrounded by a mighty force, do you march forth to compass the destruction of Rāma along with the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु धूम्राक्षो राक्षसेन्द्रेण धीमता
कृत्वा प्रणामं संहृष्टो निर्जगाम नृपालयात्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu dhūmrākṣo rākṣasendreṇa dhīmatā
kṛtvā praṇāmaṁ saṁhṛṣṭo nirjagāma nṛpālayāt

translations.english: Thus accosted by the intelligent lord of the Raksasas, Dhumraksa, turning about, issued out of the abode of the king.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिनिष्क्रम्य तद्द्वारं बलाध्यक्षमुवाच ह
त्वरयस्व बलं तूर्णं किं चिरेण युयुत्सतः
verses.transliteration:
abhiniṣkramya taddvāraṁ balādhyakṣamuvāca ha
tvarayasva balaṁ tūrṇaṁ kiṁ cireṇa yuyutsataḥ

translations.english: And speedily sallying forth from the gate of (Ravana's residence, he said to the general of the forces, “Do you speedily move off your forces. why should a warrior linger?”

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षस्य वचः श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो बलानुगः
बलमुद्योजयामास रावणस्याज्ञया द्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣasya vacaḥ śrutvā balādhyakṣo balānugaḥ
balamudyojayāmāsa rāvaṇasyājñayā drutam

translations.english: Hearing Dhumraksa's words, the general of the forces, following them, at the command of Rāvaņa forthwith made the army ready.

verses.sanskrit:
ते बद्धघण्टा बलिनो घोररूपा निशाचराः
विनर्दमानाः संहृष्टा धूम्राक्षं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
te baddhaghaṇṭā balino ghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
vinardamānāḥ saṁhṛṣṭā dhūmrākṣaṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: And those powerful and dreadful nightrangers, bursting with high spirits, with bells tied to their arms, set up shouts, and surrounded Dhumraksa.

verses.sanskrit:
विविधायुधहस्ताश्च शूलमुद्गरपाणयः
गदाभिः पट्टसैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैर्भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
vividhāyudhahastāśca śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ
gadābhiḥ paṭṭasairdaṇḍairāyasairmusalairbhṛśam

translations.english: And bearing various weapons in their hands, and wielding darts and clubs, and equipped with maces and bearded darts and rods and iron bludgeons and parighas and bhindipālas and lances and nooses and axes, those terrific Rāks asas sallied out roaring like to clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
रथैः कवचिनस्त्वन्ये ध्वजैश्च समलंकृतैः
सुवर्णजालविहितैः खरैश्च विविधाननैः
verses.transliteration:
rathaiḥ kavacinastvanye dhvajaiśca samalaṁkṛtaiḥ
suvarṇajālavihitaiḥ kharaiśca vividhānanaiḥ

translations.english: And others, accoutred in armour, with cars; adorned with banners; furnished with golden networks, and mules having various faces, and extremely swift steeds, and lusty elephants in rut, tiger-like Naiſtas incapable of being subdued even as tigers-sallied out (thereafter).

verses.sanskrit:
वृकसिंहमुखैर्युक्तं खरैः कनकभूषणैः
आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं धूम्राक्षः खरनिस्वनः
verses.transliteration:
vṛkasiṁhamukhairyuktaṁ kharaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
āruroha rathaṁ divyaṁ dhūmrākṣaḥ kharanisvanaḥ

translations.english: Then Dhūmrākṣa himself ascended a superb car, bearing faces of deer and lions decked with gold, and sending forth a loud clatter.

verses.sanskrit:
स निर्यातो महावीर्यो धूम्राक्षो राक्षसैर्वृतः
प्रहसन्पश्चिमद्वारं हनूमान्यत्र यूथपः
verses.transliteration:
sa niryāto mahāvīryo dhūmrākṣo rākṣasairvṛtaḥ
prahasanpaścimadvāraṁ hanūmānyatra yūthapaḥ

translations.english: The highly powerful Dhūmrākşa, surrounded by Rākşasas, cheerfully issued out of the Western Entrance, where Hanumān was posted.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयान्तं तु महाघोरं राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्
अन्तरिक्षगताः क्रूराः शकुनाः प्रत्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
prayāntaṁ tu mahāghoraṁ rākṣasaṁ bhīmadarśanam
antarikṣagatāḥ krūrāḥ śakunāḥ pratyavārayan

translations.english: Thereat, fell fowls of the air forbade that exceedingly dreadful Räksasa of a fearful form, as he went out ascending an excellent car joked with mules, and sending sharp sounds.

verses.sanskrit:
रथशीर्षे महाभीमो गृध्रश्च निपपात ह
ध्वजाग्रे ग्रथिताश्चैव निपेतुः कुणपाशनाः
verses.transliteration:
rathaśīrṣe mahābhīmo gṛdhraśca nipapāta ha
dhvajāgre grathitāścaiva nipetuḥ kuṇapāśanāḥ

translations.english: And an exceedingly terrific vulture alighted at the crest of the car and forming themselves into lines, vultures began to drop down about the top of the banner. And emitting a frightful cry, (a headless trunk) dropped down before Dhumraksa.

verses.sanskrit:
ववर्ष रुधिरं देवः संचचाल च मेदिनी
प्रतिलोमं ववौ वायुर्निर्घातसमनिस्वनः
तिमिरौघावृतास्तत्र दिशश्च न चकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
vavarṣa rudhiraṁ devaḥ saṁcacāla ca medinī
pratilomaṁ vavau vāyurnirghātasamanisvanaḥ
timiraughāvṛtāstatra diśaśca na cakāśire

translations.english: That god* showered down blood; and the earth shook. And the wind blew awry with a sound resembling thunder. And every side, covered with darkness, appeared dim. *Indra-cloud compeller.

verses.sanskrit:
स तूत्पातांस्ततो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसानां भयावहान्
प्रादुर्भूतान्सुघोरांश्च धूम्राक्षो व्यथितोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tūtpātāṁstato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvahān
prādurbhūtānsughorāṁśca dhūmrākṣo vyathito'bhavat

translations.english: And witnessing those dreadful inauspicious omens at the outset, fraught with fear to the Räkşasas, Dhūmrākṣa was greatly aggrieved; and the Räksaşas marching before him, were stupefied.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुभीमो बहुभिर्निशाचरै;र्वृतोऽभिनिष्क्रम्य रणोत्सुको बली
ददर्श तां राघवबाहुपालितां; समुद्रकल्पां बहुवानरीं चमूम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ subhīmo bahubhirniśācarai;rvṛto'bhiniṣkramya raṇotsuko balī
dadarśa tāṁ rāghavabāhupālitāṁ; samudrakalpāṁ bahuvānarīṁ camūm

translations.english: Then as that strong and fearful one, eager for encounter, surrounded by in numerable nigh rangers, issued out (of the city), he beheld that monkey-host, protected by the arm of Rāghava, resembling the deep at the time of universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षं प्रेक्ष्य निर्यान्तं राक्षसं भीमनिस्वनम्
विनेदुर्वानराः सर्वे प्रहृष्टा युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣaṁ prekṣya niryāntaṁ rākṣasaṁ bhīmanisvanam
vinedurvānarāḥ sarve prahṛṣṭā yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the Rākṣasa-Dhūmrākṣa of dreadful prowess-issue out, the monkeys, rejoicing greatly, eager for encounter, set up roars.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तु तुमुलं युद्धं संजज्ञे हरिरक्षसाम्
अन्योन्यं पादपैर्घोरैर्निघ्नतं शूलमुद्गरैः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tu tumulaṁ yuddhaṁ saṁjajñe harirakṣasām
anyonyaṁ pādapairghorairnighnataṁ śūlamudgaraiḥ

translations.english: Then there took place a terrific conflict between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, charging each other with fearful trees, and darts, and maces.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसैर्वानरा घोरा विनिकृत्ताः समन्ततः
वानरै राक्षसाश्चापि द्रुमैर्भूमौ समीकृताः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasairvānarā ghorā vinikṛttāḥ samantataḥ
vānarai rākṣasāścāpi drumairbhūmau samīkṛtāḥ

translations.english: The Rākşasas began to scatter the dreadful monkeys on all sides; and the monkeys (on their parts) felled the Raksasas with trees.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाश्चापि संक्रुद्धा वानरान्निशितैः शरैः
विव्यधुर्घोरसंकाशैः कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasāścāpi saṁkruddhā vānarānniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
vivyadhurghorasaṁkāśaiḥ kaṅkapatrairajihmagaiḥ

translations.english: The Raksasas, growing enraged, began to pierce that monkeys with straight speeding sharp shafts winged with Kanka plumes.

verses.sanskrit:
विदार्यमाणा रक्षोभिर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः
अमर्षाज्जनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्
verses.transliteration:
vidāryamāṇā rakṣobhirvānarāste mahābalāḥ
amarṣājjanitoddharṣāścakruḥ karmāṇyabhītavat

translations.english: And riven by the Rākşasa with drcadful clubs and bearded darts, daggers and maces and terrible and curious bludgeons and grasped javelins, the exceedingly powerful (monkeys), their anger aroused, began with alacrity to perform deeds of intrepid valour.

verses.sanskrit:
शरनिर्भिन्नगात्रास्ते शूलनिर्भिन्नदेहिनः
जगृहुस्ते द्रुमांस्तत्र शिलाश्च हरियूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
śaranirbhinnagātrāste śūlanirbhinnadehinaḥ
jagṛhuste drumāṁstatra śilāśca hariyūthapāḥ

translations.english: Those monkey-leaders, their bodies pierced with shafts and their persons riven with darts, took up trees and crags.

verses.sanskrit:
ते भीमवेगा हरयो नर्दमानास्ततस्ततः
ममन्थू राक्षसान्भीमान्नामानि च बभाषिरे
verses.transliteration:
te bhīmavegā harayo nardamānāstatastataḥ
mamanthū rākṣasānbhīmānnāmāni ca babhāṣire

translations.english: Those monkeys, endowed with terrific vehemence, sending up shouts, and proclaiming their respective names, set about tossing the brave Rākşasa rank,

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बभूवाद्भुतं घोरं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्
शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च बहुशाखैश्च पादपैः
verses.transliteration:
tadbabhūvādbhutaṁ ghoraṁ yuddhaṁ vānararakṣasām
śilābhirvividhābhiśca bahuśākhaiśca pādapaiḥ

translations.english: The monkeys, waged with diverse rocks and innumerable trees, waxed exceedingly furious.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसा मथिताः केचिद्वानरैर्जितकाशिभिः
ववर्षू रुधिरं केचिन्मुखै रुधिरभोजनाः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasā mathitāḥ kecidvānarairjitakāśibhiḥ
vavarṣū rudhiraṁ kecinmukhai rudhirabhojanāḥ

translations.english: Sparkling in the glory of victory, the monkeys crushed the Rākşasas and some among them feeding on gore began to vomit blood.

verses.sanskrit:
पार्श्वेषु दारिताः केचित्केचिद्राशीकृता द्रुमैः
शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताः केचित्केचिद्दन्तैर्विदारिताः
verses.transliteration:
pārśveṣu dāritāḥ kecitkecidrāśīkṛtā drumaiḥ
śilābhiścūrṇitāḥ kecitkeciddantairvidāritāḥ

translations.english: And some were severed along their flanks; and, some, slain with trees, were heaped up; and some were crushed with crags; and some were torn with teeth.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्वजैर्विमथितैर्भग्नैः खरैश्च विनिपातितैः
रथैर्विध्वंसितैश्चापि पतितै रजनीचरैः
verses.transliteration:
dhvajairvimathitairbhagnaiḥ kharaiśca vinipātitaiḥ
rathairvidhvaṁsitaiścāpi patitai rajanīcaraiḥ

translations.english: Some being broken down by means of broken standards, and some by means of fallen swords, and some crushed down by cars, the rangers of the night suffered sorely.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरैर्भीमविक्रान्तैराप्लुत्याप्लुत्य वेगितैः
राक्षसाः करजैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मुखेषु विनिकर्तिताः
verses.transliteration:
vānarairbhīmavikrāntairāplutyāplutya vegitaiḥ
rākṣasāḥ karajaistīkṣṇairmukheṣu vinikartitāḥ

translations.english: Bounding again and again, the vehement monkeys endowed with terrific prowess, with their finger-nails tore up the Rākṣasas by the mouths.

verses.sanskrit:
विवर्णवदना भूयो विप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः
मूढाः शोणितगन्धेन निपेतुर्धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
vivarṇavadanā bhūyo viprakīrṇaśiroruhāḥ
mūḍhāḥ śoṇitagandhena nipeturdharaṇītale

translations.english: With woebegone faces, and with hair dishevelled, (the Raksasas), stupified with the smell of blood, saught the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
नये तु परमक्रुद्धा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः
तलैरेवाभिधावन्ति वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्हरीन्
verses.transliteration:
naye tu paramakruddhā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ
talairevābhidhāvanti vajrasparśasamairharīn

translations.english: Other Rākşasas endowed with dreadful vigour, waxing wondrous wroth, dealt the monkeys slaps with hands having the touch of the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
वनरैरापतन्तस्ते वेगिता वेगवत्तरैः
मुष्टिभिश्चरणैर्दन्तैः पादपैश्चापपोथिताः
verses.transliteration:
vanarairāpatantaste vegitā vegavattaraiḥ
muṣṭibhiścaraṇairdantaiḥ pādapaiścāpapothitāḥ

translations.english: Gift with greater impetuosity, the monkeys felled the impetuous (Raksasas) with blows, and feet and teeth; and some were slain with trees.

verses.sanskrit:
सन्यं तु विद्रुतं दृष्ट्वा धूम्राक्षो राक्षसर्षभः
क्रोधेन कदनं चक्रे वानराणां युयुत्सताम्
verses.transliteration:
sanyaṁ tu vidrutaṁ dṛṣṭvā dhūmrākṣo rākṣasarṣabhaḥ
krodhena kadanaṁ cakre vānarāṇāṁ yuyutsatām

translations.english: Seeing the forces fleeing away, that foremost of Raksasas-Dhumraksa-flying into fury, began a terrific conflict with the monkeys desirous of encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रासैः प्रमथिताः केचिद्वानराः शोणितस्रवाः
मुद्गरैराहताः केचित्पतिता धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
prāsaiḥ pramathitāḥ kecidvānarāḥ śoṇitasravāḥ
mudgarairāhatāḥ kecitpatitā dharaṇītale

translations.english: Some of the monkeys, sore assailed with prāśas, began to bleed; and some, wounded with maces, dropped down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
परिघैर्मथितः केचिद्भिण्डिपालैर्विदारिताः
पट्टसैराहताः केचिद्विह्वलन्तो गतासवः
verses.transliteration:
parighairmathitaḥ kecidbhiṇḍipālairvidāritāḥ
paṭṭasairāhatāḥ kecidvihvalanto gatāsavaḥ

translations.english: Some were beaten hard with bludgeons; and some were cleft with bhindipālas. And some, on being assailed with bearded darts, became insensible and lost their lives.

verses.sanskrit:
केचिद्विनिहता भूमौ रुधिरार्द्रा वनौकसः
केचिद्विद्राविता नष्टाः संक्रुद्धै राक्षसैर्युधि
verses.transliteration:
kecidvinihatā bhūmau rudhirārdrā vanaukasaḥ
kecidvidrāvitā naṣṭāḥ saṁkruddhai rākṣasairyudhi

translations.english: Some among the monkeys lay slain on the ground, drenched in blood. and some, fleeing away from the field, were slaughtered by the infuriated Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
विभिन्नहृदयाः केचिदेकपार्श्वेन शायिताः
विदारितास्त्रशूलै च केचिदान्त्रैर्विनिस्रुताः
verses.transliteration:
vibhinnahṛdayāḥ kecidekapārśvena śāyitāḥ
vidāritāstraśūlai ca kecidāntrairvinisrutāḥ

translations.english: Some, having their breasts pierced, lay on their sides. and some were riven with tridents; and the entrails of some had come out.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सुभीमं महद्युद्धं हरिराकस संकुलम्
प्रबभौ शस्त्रबहुलं शिलापादपसंकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
tatsubhīmaṁ mahadyuddhaṁ harirākasa saṁkulam
prababhau śastrabahulaṁ śilāpādapasaṁkulam

translations.english: That mighty and dreadful encounter of the Räksasas and the monkeys, was waged with countless weapons and rocks and trees.

verses.sanskrit:
धनुर्ज्यातन्त्रिमधुरं हिक्कातालसमन्वितम्
मन्द्रस्तनितसंगीतं युद्धगान्धर्वमाबभौ
verses.transliteration:
dhanurjyātantrimadhuraṁ hikkātālasamanvitam
mandrastanitasaṁgītaṁ yuddhagāndharvamābabhau

translations.english: That battle he come a musical entertainment' mellifluous with bow-string for Vina, having the neighing of chargers for its measure, and with the cries of Maindas' for its strains. 1. The reader has already perceived that the carrying out of a simile to a number of details is a characteristic as much of Vālmīki as of his rival in the epic sphere-Vyāsa, but the comparisons are never on all fours, as in the case before us. 2. A classical Hindu musical instrument, having metallic strings, with a pair of gourds at one end for the sounding-board. Vide Yantra-Kosa by Sir Saurindra Mohan Tagore, Mus-Doc. 3. A species of elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षस्तु धनुष्पाणिर्वानरान्रणमूर्धनि
हसन्विद्रावयामास दिशस्ताञ्शरवृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣastu dhanuṣpāṇirvānarānraṇamūrdhani
hasanvidrāvayāmāsa diśastāñśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ

translations.english: Then in the field, Dhūmrākṣa bow in hand, laughing, pursued the monkeys in all directions with showers of shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षेणार्दितं सैन्यं व्यथितं दृश्य मारुतिः
अभ्यवर्तत संक्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य विपुलां शिलाम्
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣeṇārditaṁ sainyaṁ vyathitaṁ dṛśya mārutiḥ
abhyavartata saṁkruddhaḥ pragṛhya vipulāṁ śilām

translations.english: Seeing the forces hard beset by Dhūmrākşa and distressed thereat, the Windgod's offspring, waxing enraged, seizing a huge crag, approached (the Rākşasa).

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्द्विगुणताम्राक्षः पितृतुल्यपराक्रमः
शिलां तां पातयामास धूम्राक्षस्य रथं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
krodhāddviguṇatāmrākṣaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
śilāṁ tāṁ pātayāmāsa dhūmrākṣasya rathaṁ prati

translations.english: And with his eyes double reddened in wrath, the one, like to his sire himself in prowess, brought down the crag upon Dhūmrākṣa's car.

verses.sanskrit:
आपतन्तीं शिलां दृष्ट्वा गदामुद्यम्य संभ्रमात्
रथादाप्लुत्य वेगेन वसुधायां व्यतिष्ठत
verses.transliteration:
āpatantīṁ śilāṁ dṛṣṭvā gadāmudyamya saṁbhramāt
rathādāplutya vegena vasudhāyāṁ vyatiṣṭhata

translations.english: Seeing the crag, (Dhumraksa) upraising his mace hurriedly, leapt down in vehemence, and stood on the ground. And having shattered his car, that crag fell down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स भङ्क्त्वा तु रथं तस्य हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
रक्षसां कदनं चक्रे सस्कन्धविटपैर्द्रुमैः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhaṅktvā tu rathaṁ tasya hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
rakṣasāṁ kadanaṁ cakre saskandhaviṭapairdrumaiḥ

translations.english: Thereat letting go the car furnished with wheels, Kuvaras and a face, as well as a banner; in which Dhūmrākṣa had left his bow, Hanuman-son to the Wind-god-laid about him right lustily for destroying the Rākşasas, with trees having branches long and short.

verses.sanskrit:
विभिन्नशिरसो भूत्वा राक्षसाः शोणितोक्षिताः
द्रुमैः प्रमथिताश्चान्ये निपेतुर्धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
vibhinnaśiraso bhūtvā rākṣasāḥ śoṇitokṣitāḥ
drumaiḥ pramathitāścānye nipeturdharaṇītale

translations.english: Thereat some Rākşasas with their heads shattered, lay drenched in blood; and others, struck with trees, dropped down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्राव्य राक्षसं सैन्यं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
गिरेः शिखरमादाय धूम्राक्षमभिदुद्रुवे
verses.transliteration:
vidrāvya rākṣasaṁ sainyaṁ hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
gireḥ śikharamādāya dhūmrākṣamabhidudruve

translations.english: Then Hanumān-son to the Wind-god-charged in full career against the Räkşasa army; and, taking a mountain-peak, he rushed against Dhumraksa.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं धूम्राक्षो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
विनर्दमानः सहसा हनूमन्तमभिद्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ dhūmrākṣo gadāmudyamya vīryavān
vinardamānaḥ sahasā hanūmantamabhidravat

translations.english: As Hanumān was descending, the powerful Dhūmrākşa, upraising a mace and giving out a shout, made towards him speedily.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रुद्धस्तु वेगेन गदां तां बहुकण्टकाम्
पातयामास धूम्राक्षो मस्तके तु हनूमतः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kruddhastu vegena gadāṁ tāṁ bahukaṇṭakām
pātayāmāsa dhūmrākṣo mastake tu hanūmataḥ

translations.english: Then Dhūmrākṣa enraged, brought down that mace studded with innumerable pricks, on the head of Hanumān fired with wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
ताडितः स तया तत्र गदया भीमरूपया
स कपिर्मारुतबलस्तं प्रहारमचिन्तयन्
धूम्राक्षस्य शिरो मध्ये गिरिशृङ्गमपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
tāḍitaḥ sa tayā tatra gadayā bhīmarūpayā
sa kapirmārutabalastaṁ prahāramacintayan
dhūmrākṣasya śiro madhye giriśṛṅgamapātayat

translations.english: Thus assailed with the mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with he mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with the strength of the wind without at all heeding that blow, let fall a mountain-top right against Dhumraksa's head.

verses.sanskrit:
स विह्वलितसर्वाङ्गो गिरिशृङ्गेण ताडितः
पपात सहसा भूमौ विकीर्ण इव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo giriśṛṅgeṇa tāḍitaḥ
papāta sahasā bhūmau vikīrṇa iva parvataḥ

translations.english: On being assailed with the mountain-peak, Dhūmrākşa, having his entire body mangled, suddenly fell to the earth, like to a toppling hill.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षं निहतं दृष्ट्वा हतशेषा निशाचराः
त्रस्ताः प्रविविशुर्लङ्कां वध्यमानाः प्लवंगमैः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ
trastāḥ praviviśurlaṅkāṁ vadhyamānāḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ

translations.english: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa slain, those night-rangers that survived the carnage, in extreme agitation began to pour into Lankā, attacked by the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु पवनसुतो निहत्य शत्रुं; क्षतजवहाः सरितश्च संविकीर्य
रिपुवधजनितश्रमो महात्मा; मुदमगमत्कपिभिश्च पूज्यमानः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu pavanasuto nihatya śatruṁ; kṣatajavahāḥ saritaśca saṁvikīrya
ripuvadhajanitaśramo mahātmā; mudamagamatkapibhiśca pūjyamānaḥ

translations.english: That high-souled offspring of the Wind-god, having slain his foes, and come under the influence of fatigue incident to his slaughtering his enemies, having caused rivers of gore to flow (in the field), experienced the excess of joy on being honoured of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षं निहतं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
बलाध्यक्षमुवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣaṁ nihataṁ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
balādhyakṣamuvācedaṁ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam

translations.english: Hearing Vajradanștra slain by the son of Vāli, Rāvaņa said to the general of his forces, standing before him with joined hands,

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रं निर्यान्तु दुर्धर्षा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः
अकम्पनं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वशस्त्रप्रकोविदम्
verses.transliteration:
śīghraṁ niryāntu durdharṣā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ
akampanaṁ puraskṛtya sarvaśastraprakovidam

translations.english: Let invincible Rākşasas of dreadful prowess, march forth, placing before them Akampana, skilled in all weapons and arms.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नानाप्रहरणा भीमाक्षा भीमदर्शनाः
निष्पेतू राक्षसा मुख्या बलाध्यक्षप्रचोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
tato nānāpraharaṇā bhīmākṣā bhīmadarśanāḥ
niṣpetū rākṣasā mukhyā balādhyakṣapracoditāḥ

translations.english: Then equipped with various arms, the foremost of Rākşasas, having dreadful eyes (in their heads, and of dreadful forms, marched forth, urged on by their general.

verses.sanskrit:
रथमास्थाय विपुलं तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः
राकसैः संवृतो घोरैस्तदा निर्यात्यकम्पनः
verses.transliteration:
rathamāsthāya vipulaṁ taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ
rākasaiḥ saṁvṛto ghoraistadā niryātyakampanaḥ

translations.english: Ascending a large car, adorned with burnished gold, Akampana, possessed of the splendour of clouds,* and cloud-hued, and furnished with a voice resembling the roar of clouds, went out, environed by Rākașasas of terrific forms. *There is a pun here on the word Akampana-lit.one incapable of being shaken.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि कम्पयितुं शक्यः सुरैरपि महामृधे
अकम्पनस्ततस्तेषामादित्य इव तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
na hi kampayituṁ śakyaḥ surairapi mahāmṛdhe
akampanastatasteṣāmāditya iva tejasā

translations.english: Akampana, resembling the sun in power, was incapable of being shaken in fight by the very gods, and of being beheld by them. 1. Possessed of a person measuring, according to the commentator, a mass of clouds. I give the apparent sense, which answers. 2. Monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य निधावमानस्य संरब्धस्य युयुत्सया
अकस्माद्दैन्यमागच्छद्धयानां रथवाहिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya nidhāvamānasya saṁrabdhasya yuyutsayā
akasmāddainyamāgacchaddhayānāṁ rathavāhinām

translations.english: And as, burning for battle, he rushed out in wrath, the steeds drawing his car suddenly lost their energy.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यस्फुरन्नयनं चास्य सव्यं युद्धाभिनन्दिनः
विवर्णो मुखवर्णश्च गद्गदश्चाभवत्स्वरः
verses.transliteration:
vyasphurannayanaṁ cāsya savyaṁ yuddhābhinandinaḥ
vivarṇo mukhavarṇaśca gadgadaścābhavatsvaraḥ

translations.english: The left eye of that one delighting in encounter, began to throb. And his continence grew pale, and his voice faltered.

verses.sanskrit:
अभवत्सुदिने चापि दुर्दिने रूक्षमारुतम्
ऊचुः खगा मृगाः सर्वे वाचः क्रूरा भयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
abhavatsudine cāpi durdine rūkṣamārutam
ūcuḥ khagā mṛgāḥ sarve vācaḥ krūrā bhayāvahāḥ

translations.english: In a fair day, it looked foul with the wind breathing roughly. And fierce and frightful beasts and birds began to emit cries.

verses.sanskrit:
स सिंहोपचितस्कन्धः शार्दूलसमविक्रमः
तानुत्पातानचिन्त्यैव निर्जगाम रणाजिरम्
verses.transliteration:
sa siṁhopacitaskandhaḥ śārdūlasamavikramaḥ
tānutpātānacintyaiva nirjagāma raṇājiram

translations.english: That lion-shouldered one like a tiger in prowess, without heeding these ominous occurrences, marched forth into the field.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा निर्गच्छतस्तस्य रक्षसः सह राक्षसैः
बभूव सुमहान्नादः क्षोभयन्निव सागरम्
verses.transliteration:
tadā nirgacchatastasya rakṣasaḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
babhūva sumahānnādaḥ kṣobhayanniva sāgaram

translations.english: As that Rākşasa was setting out along with the Rākṣasas, he set up mighty roars as if agitating the deep.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां युद्धं महारौद्रं संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्
रामरावणयोरर्थे समभित्यक्तजीविनाम्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ yuddhaṁ mahāraudraṁ saṁjajñe kapirakṣasām
rāmarāvaṇayorarthe samabhityaktajīvinām

translations.english: The mighty army of monkeys was seized with trepidation at that sound. And then there took place a mighty encounter of the Rākṣasas and the monkeys equipped staying in fight with trees and rocks, who had given up all concern for their selves in behalf of Rāma and Rävaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां विनर्दातां शब्दः संयुगेऽतितरस्विनाम्
शुश्रुवे सुमहान्क्रोधादन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vinardātāṁ śabdaḥ saṁyuge'titarasvinām
śuśruve sumahānkrodhādanyonyamabhigarjatām

translations.english: And each side desirous of slaying the other, the monkeys and the Raksasas were exceedingly strong and heroic and like to mountains. And each party storming at the other, in that conflict were heard loud cries emitted by those swiftspeeding ones in anger.

verses.sanskrit:
रजश्चारुणवर्णाभं सुभीममभवद्भृशम्
उद्धूतं हरिरक्षोभिः संरुरोध दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
rajaścāruṇavarṇābhaṁ subhīmamabhavadbhṛśam
uddhūtaṁ harirakṣobhiḥ saṁrurodha diśo daśa

translations.english: And fearful was the dust red-hued that was raised incessantly by the monkeys and the Rākṣasa; and it enveloped the ten cardinal points.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यं रजसा तेन कौशेयोद्धूतपाण्डुना
संवृतानि च भूतानि ददृशुर्न रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration:
anyonyaṁ rajasā tena kauśeyoddhūtapāṇḍunā
saṁvṛtāni ca bhūtāni dadṛśurna raṇājire

translations.english: In the field of battle, each enveloped with that dust raised, pale as silk, could not be discovered by the other.

verses.sanskrit:
न ध्वजो न पताकावा वर्म वा तुरगोऽपि वा
आयुधं स्यन्दनं वापि ददृशे तेन रेणुना
verses.transliteration:
na dhvajo na patākāvā varma vā turago'pi vā
āyudhaṁ syandanaṁ vāpi dadṛśe tena reṇunā

translations.english: In consequence of that dust arising, neither standard, nor ensign, nor shield, nor steed, nor weapon, nor car could be seen.

verses.sanskrit:
शब्दश्च सुमहांस्तेषां नर्दतामभिधावताम्
श्रूयते तुमुले युद्धे न रूपाणि चकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
śabdaśca sumahāṁsteṣāṁ nardatāmabhidhāvatām
śrūyate tumule yuddhe na rūpāṇi cakāśire

translations.english: The fierce cries alone of those roaring and rushing were heard in that dreadful battle; but their forms were not visible to the sight.

verses.sanskrit:
हरीनेव सुसंक्रुद्धा हरयो जघ्नुराहवे
राक्षसाश्चापि रक्षांसि निजघ्नुस्तिमिरे तदा
verses.transliteration:
harīneva susaṁkruddhā harayo jaghnurāhave
rākṣasāścāpi rakṣāṁsi nijaghnustimire tadā

translations.english: In that conflict in the dark then monkeys extremely enraged slew monkeys, and Räkşasas also killed the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
परांश्चैव विनिघ्नन्तः स्वांश्च वानरराक्षसाः
रुधिरार्द्रं तदा चक्रुर्महीं पङ्कानुलेपनाम्
verses.transliteration:
parāṁścaiva vinighnantaḥ svāṁśca vānararākṣasāḥ
rudhirārdraṁ tadā cakrurmahīṁ paṅkānulepanām

translations.english: And monkeys and Rākşasas slaying (indiscriminately) friends and foes, made the earth wet with blood, and miry.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु रुधिरौघेण सिक्तं व्यपगतं रजः
शरीरशवसंकीर्णा बभूव च वसुंधरा
verses.transliteration:
tatastu rudhiraugheṇa siktaṁ vyapagataṁ rajaḥ
śarīraśavasaṁkīrṇā babhūva ca vasuṁdharā

translations.english: Then with showers of blood the dust was layed; and the earth was covered with corpses.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहुभिः परिघाकारैर्युध्यन्तः पर्वतोपमाः
हरयो भीमकर्माणो राक्षसाञ्जघ्नुराहवे
verses.transliteration:
bāhubhiḥ parighākārairyudhyantaḥ parvatopamāḥ
harayo bhīmakarmāṇo rākṣasāñjaghnurāhave

translations.english: Rākşasas and monkeys fast slew each other vigorously with trees and darts, maces and prasas, rocks, bludgeons and Tomaras, and by means of their arms resembling bludgeons, coped with their adversaries appearing like hills.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाश्चापि संक्रुद्धाः प्रासतोमरपाणयः
कपीन्निजघ्निरे तत्र शस्त्रैः परमदारुणैः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasāścāpi saṁkruddhāḥ prāsatomarapāṇayaḥ
kapīnnijaghnire tatra śastraiḥ paramadāruṇaiḥ

translations.english: And in the encounter monkeys slew Rākşasas of dreadful deeds. And in their turn Rākşasas, wrought up with passion, bearing in their hands prāśas and tomaras destroyed monkeys wielding dire arms.

verses.sanskrit:
हरयस्त्वपि रक्षांसि महाद्रुममहाश्मभिः
विदारयन्त्यभिक्रम्य शस्त्राण्याच्छिद्य वीर्यतः
verses.transliteration:
harayastvapi rakṣāṁsi mahādrumamahāśmabhiḥ
vidārayantyabhikramya śastrāṇyācchidya vīryataḥ

translations.english: And the monkeys forcibly snatching away the weapons (of the Rākşasas), began to rive the Rákşasas with mighty trees and giant crags.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरा हरयः कुमुदो नलः
मैन्दश्च परमक्रुद्धश्चक्रुर्वेगमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare vīrā harayaḥ kumudo nalaḥ
maindaśca paramakruddhaścakrurvegamanuttamam

translations.english: In the meanwhile those heroes among the monkeys-Kumuda, Nīla and the exceedingly exasperated Mainda, summoned the utmost impetuosity they were masters of.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु वृक्षैर्महावेगा राक्षसानां चमूमुखे
कदनं सुमह चक्रुर्लीलया हरियूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
te tu vṛkṣairmahāvegā rākṣasānāṁ camūmukhe
kadanaṁ sumaha cakrurlīlayā hariyūthapāḥ

translations.english: And those foremost of monkeys and redoubtable able warriors without much ado began to spread quite a carnage in the van of the Rākşasa army, and by means of various arms terribly beat the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्दृष्ट्वा सुमहत्कर्म कृतं वानरसत्तमैः
क्रोधमाहारयामास युधि तीव्रमकम्पनः
verses.transliteration:
taddṛṣṭvā sumahatkarma kṛtaṁ vānarasattamaiḥ
krodhamāhārayāmāsa yudhi tīvramakampanaḥ

translations.english: And witnessing that mighty exploit of the foremost of the monkeys, Akampana waxed furious with wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधमूर्छितरूपस्तु ध्नुवन्परमकार्मुकम्
दृष्ट्वा तु कर्म शत्रूणां सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
krodhamūrchitarūpastu dhnuvanparamakārmukam
dṛṣṭvā tu karma śatrūṇāṁ sārathiṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And transported with passion, he, twanging his mighty bow seeing that feat of his foe, addressed his charioteer saying.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रैव तावत्त्वरितं रथं प्रापय सारथे
एतेऽत्र बहवो घ्नन्ति सुबहून्राक्षसान्रणे
verses.transliteration:
tatraiva tāvattvaritaṁ rathaṁ prāpaya sārathe
ete'tra bahavo ghnanti subahūnrākṣasānraṇe

translations.english: O charioteer, swiftly conduct you the car to that same place. These powerful ones are slaying innumerable Rākşasas in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेऽत्र बलवन्तो हि भीमकायाश्च वानराः
द्रुमशैलप्रहरणास्तिष्ठन्ति प्रमुखे मम
verses.transliteration:
ete'tra balavanto hi bhīmakāyāśca vānarāḥ
drumaśailapraharaṇāstiṣṭhanti pramukhe mama

translations.english: And all those vigorous monkeys of dreadful deeds stay before me, armed with trees and rocks.

verses.sanskrit:
एतान्निहन्तुमिच्छामि समरश्लाघिनो ह्यहम्
एतैः प्रमथितं सर्वं दृश्यते राक्षसं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
etānnihantumicchāmi samaraślāghino hyaham
etaiḥ pramathitaṁ sarvaṁ dṛśyate rākṣasaṁ balam

translations.english: Those, pluming themselves overmuch on their martial worth, I intended to slay in battle. And all this Rākşasa force appeared to be harassed by these.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रजविताश्वेन रथेन रथिनां वरः
हरीनभ्यहनत्क्रोधाच्छरजालैरकम्पनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prajavitāśvena rathena rathināṁ varaḥ
harīnabhyahanatkrodhāccharajālairakampanaḥ

translations.english: Then on a car drawn by moving steeds, Akampana from a distance attacked the monkeys with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
न स्थातुं वानराः शेकुः किं पुनर्योद्धुमाहवे
अकम्पनशरैर्भग्नाः सर्व एव प्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
na sthātuṁ vānarāḥ śekuḥ kiṁ punaryoddhumāhave
akampanaśarairbhagnāḥ sarva eva pradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Thereat the monkeys could not so much as maintain their ground in the field, and how could they fight?

verses.sanskrit:
तान्मृत्युवशमापन्नानकम्पनवशं गतान्
समीक्ष्य हनुमाञ्ज्ञातीनुपतस्थे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tānmṛtyuvaśamāpannānakampanavaśaṁ gatān
samīkṣya hanumāñjñātīnupatasthe mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Broken by the arrows of Akampana, they began to fly. and the exceedingly strong Hanumān, seeing his kindred come under the masterdom of Death and follow the course pursued by the shafts of Akampana, advanced (to the conflict). And seeing that mighty monkey, all those heroic prime monkeys together surrounded (Hanumān) in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यवस्थितं हनूमन्तं ते दृष्ट्वा हरियूथपाः
बभूवुर्बलवन्तो हि बलवन्तमुपाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
vyavasthitaṁ hanūmantaṁ te dṛṣṭvā hariyūthapāḥ
babhūvurbalavanto hi balavantamupāśritāḥ

translations.english: Those best of monkeys, seeing Hanumán stay, grew strong by relying on that strong one.

verses.sanskrit:
अकम्पनस्तु शैलाभं हनूमन्तमवस्थितम्
महेन्द्र इव धाराभिः शरैरभिववर्ष ह
verses.transliteration:
akampanastu śailābhaṁ hanūmantamavasthitam
mahendra iva dhārābhiḥ śarairabhivavarṣa ha

translations.english: And even as the great Indra shower down rain, Akampana showered shafts on Hanuman resembling a mountain-summit in grandeur.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्तयित्वा बाणौघाञ्शरीरे पतिताञ्शितान्
अकम्पनवधार्थाय मनो दध्रे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
acintayitvā bāṇaughāñśarīre patitāñśitān
akampanavadhārthāya mano dadhre mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And without casting a thought on the showers of arrows poured on his person, that monkey gifted with exceeding strength, set his heart on compassing the death of Akampana.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रहस्य महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
अभिदुद्राव तद्रक्षः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
sa prahasya mahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
abhidudrāva tadrakṣaḥ kampayanniva medinīm

translations.english: And laughing, that exceedingly energetic offspring of the Wind-god rushed after that Rākşasa, as if making the Earth herself tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याभिनर्दमानस्य दीप्यमानस्य तेजसा
बभूव रूपं दुर्धर्षं दीप्तस्येव विभावसोः
verses.transliteration:
tasyābhinardamānasya dīpyamānasya tejasā
babhūva rūpaṁ durdharṣaṁ dīptasyeva vibhāvasoḥ

translations.english: The form of that one roaring and flaming up in energy, was irresistible, like to the appearance of a flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं त्वप्रहरणं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः
शैलमुत्पाटयामास वेगेन हरिपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
ātmānaṁ tvapraharaṇaṁ jñātvā krodhasamanvitaḥ
śailamutpāṭayāmāsa vegena haripuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: And thinking that he was unfurnished with any arms, that foremost of monkeys, waxing wroth, vehemently rooted up a hill.

verses.sanskrit:
तं गृहीत्वा महाशैलं पाणिनैकेन मारुतिः
विनद्य सुमहानादं भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ gṛhītvā mahāśailaṁ pāṇinaikena mārutiḥ
vinadya sumahānādaṁ bhrāmayāmāsa vīryavān

translations.english: And taking that huge hill, the Wind-god's son endowed with prowess, sending up a tremendous roar, began to whirl it with a single arm.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तमभिदुद्राव राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्
यथा हि नमुचिं संख्ये वज्रेणेव पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
tatastamabhidudrāva rākṣasendramakampanam
yathā hi namuciṁ saṁkhye vajreṇeva puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: As of yore Purandara had in encounter pursued Namuchi with the thunder-bolt, (Hanuman) pursued that best of RāksasasAkampana.

verses.sanskrit:
अकम्पनस्तु तद्दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गं समुद्यतम्
दूरादेव महाबाणैरर्धचन्द्रैर्व्यदारयत्
verses.transliteration:
akampanastu taddṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgaṁ samudyatam
dūrādeva mahābāṇairardhacandrairvyadārayat

translations.english: Akampana, seeing that uplifted crag, from a distance cut it off with mighty crescent-shaped shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्पर्वताग्रमाकाशे रक्षोबाणविदारितम्
विकीर्णं पतितं दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्क्रोधमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
tatparvatāgramākāśe rakṣobāṇavidāritam
vikīrṇaṁ patitaṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmānkrodhamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And finding that mountain top severed by the shafts of the Räksasa and scattered in pieces, Hanumān was seized with a mighty wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽश्वकर्णं समासाद्य रोषदर्पान्वितो हरिः
तूर्णमुत्पाटयामास महागिरिमिवोच्छ्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
so'śvakarṇaṁ samāsādya roṣadarpānvito hariḥ
tūrṇamutpāṭayāmāsa mahāgirimivocchritam

translations.english: That monkey, wrought up with rage and pride, grasping an Aśvakarņa elevated like to a hill, at once uprooted it.

verses.sanskrit:
तं गृहीत्वा महास्कन्धं सोऽश्वकर्णं महाद्युतिः
प्रहस्य परया प्रीत्या भ्रामयामास संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ gṛhītvā mahāskandhaṁ so'śvakarṇaṁ mahādyutiḥ
prahasya parayā prītyā bhrāmayāmāsa saṁyuge

translations.english: And taking that broad-shouldered Asvakarma, that one furnished with high splendour, with great glee whirled it above the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रधावन्नुरुवेगेन प्रभञ्जंस्तरसा द्रुमान्
हनूमान्परमक्रुद्धश्चरणैर्दारयत्क्षितिम्
verses.transliteration:
pradhāvannuruvegena prabhañjaṁstarasā drumān
hanūmānparamakruddhaścaraṇairdārayatkṣitim

translations.english: Thereat rushing a main vehemently (Akampana) speedily broke the trees. And (seeing this) Hanumān, transported with passion, rived the earth with his kicks.

verses.sanskrit:
गजांश्च सगजारोहान्सरथान्रथिनस्तथा
जघान हनुमान्धीमान्राक्षसांश्च पदातिकान्
verses.transliteration:
gajāṁśca sagajārohānsarathānrathinastathā
jaghāna hanumāndhīmānrākṣasāṁśca padātikān

translations.english: And Hanumān slaughtered elephants, and the riders thereof, and cars with their riders, and dreadful Rākṣasas and footmen.

verses.sanskrit:
तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धं समरे प्राणहारिणम्
हनूमन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
tamantakamiva kruddhaṁ samare prāṇahāriṇam
hanūmantamabhiprekṣya rākṣasā vipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Seeing the enraged Hanumān resembling the Finisher armed with trees and destructive, the Rākşasas began to fly fast.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं संक्रुद्धं राक्षसानां भयावहम्
ददर्शाकम्पनो वीरश्चुक्रोध च ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ saṁkruddhaṁ rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvaham
dadarśākampano vīraścukrodha ca nanāda ca

translations.english: Seeing that one enraged, terrific to the Rāks asas, the heroic Akampana was agitated greatly and sent up shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
स चतुर्दशभिर्बाणैः शितैर्देहविदारणैः
निर्बिभेद हनूमन्तं महावीर्यमकम्पनः
verses.transliteration:
sa caturdaśabhirbāṇaiḥ śitairdehavidāraṇaiḥ
nirbibheda hanūmantaṁ mahāvīryamakampanaḥ

translations.english: Akampana pierced Hanumān endowed with exceeding prowess with four and ten shafts, sharpened and capable of cleaving the bodies of people.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथा प्रतिविद्धस्तु बह्वीभिः शरवृष्टिभिः
हनूमान्ददृशे वीरः प्ररूढ इव सानुमान्
verses.transliteration:
sa tathā pratividdhastu bahvībhiḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
hanūmāndadṛśe vīraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān

translations.english: And thus covered with iron arrows and whetted darts, that hero Hanumân-looked like a hill covered with trees.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽन्यं वृक्षमुत्पाट्य कृत्वा वेगमनुत्तमम्
शिरस्यभिजघानाशु राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'nyaṁ vṛkṣamutpāṭya kṛtvā vegamanuttamam
śirasyabhijaghānāśu rākṣasendramakampanam

translations.english: Then uprooting another tree, (Hanuman) summoning up hi best impetuosity, swiftly hit Akampana foremost of Rākşasas-on the head.

verses.sanskrit:
स वृक्षेण हतस्तेन सक्रोधेन महात्मना
राक्षसो वानरेन्द्रेण पपात स ममार च
verses.transliteration:
sa vṛkṣeṇa hatastena sakrodhena mahātmanā
rākṣaso vānarendreṇa papāta sa mamāra ca

translations.english: And slain with that tree by that high souled monkeys chief wrought up with passion that Raksasas fell down and died.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं भूमौ राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्
व्यथिता राक्षसाः सर्वे क्षितिकम्प इव द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā nihataṁ bhūmau rākṣasendramakampanam
vyathitā rākṣasāḥ sarve kṣitikampa iva drumāḥ

translations.english: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas-Akampanaslain (and lying) on the ground, the Raksasa were extremely aggrieved, and (appeared)like trees in an earthquake.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्तप्रहरणाः सर्वे राक्षसास्ते पराजिताः
लङ्कामभिययुस्त्रस्ता वानरैस्तैरभिद्रुताः
verses.transliteration:
tyaktapraharaṇāḥ sarve rākṣasāste parājitāḥ
laṅkāmabhiyayustrastā vānaraistairabhidrutāḥ

translations.english: And those Rākşasas defeated, leaving their arms behind, made for Lankā in fear, pursued by the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ते मुक्तकेशाः संभ्रान्ता भग्नमानाः पराजिताः
स्रवच्छ्रमजलैरङ्गैः श्वसन्तो विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
te muktakeśāḥ saṁbhrāntā bhagnamānāḥ parājitāḥ
sravacchramajalairaṅgaiḥ śvasanto vipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: And with their hair flowing loosely, (the Rāks asas), afflicted with affright, and dispirited and beaten, fled fast, with the water of fatigue running down their persons.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यं प्रममन्तुस्ते विविशुर्नगरं भयात्
पृष्ठतस्ते सुसंमूढाः प्रेक्षमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
anyonyaṁ pramamantuste viviśurnagaraṁ bhayāt
pṛṣṭhataste susaṁmūḍhāḥ prekṣamāṇā muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: And crushing down each other, they entered the city in a panic, momentarily casting their looks behind them.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु लङ्कां प्रविष्टेषु राक्षसेषु महाबलाः
समेत्य हरयः सर्वे हनूमन्तमपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
teṣu laṅkāṁ praviṣṭeṣu rākṣaseṣu mahābalāḥ
sametya harayaḥ sarve hanūmantamapūjayan

translations.english: When the Rákşasas had entered Lankā, the exceedingly mighty monkeys, assembled together, paid homage to Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपि प्रहृष्टस्तान्सर्वान्हरीन्संप्रत्यपूजयत्
हनूमान्सत्त्वसंपन्नो यथार्हमनुकूलतः
verses.transliteration:
so'pi prahṛṣṭastānsarvānharīnsaṁpratyapūjayat
hanūmānsattvasaṁpanno yathārhamanukūlataḥ

translations.english: And Hanumăn, gifted with strength, honoured the seniors each as he deserved in consideration of his lineage.

verses.sanskrit:
विनेदुश्च यथा प्राणं हरयो जितकाशिनः
चकर्षुश्च पुनस्तत्र सप्राणानेव राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
vineduśca yathā prāṇaṁ harayo jitakāśinaḥ
cakarṣuśca punastatra saprāṇāneva rākṣasān

translations.english: The monkeys eager for victory shouted with might and main, and began to drag the Rākşasas with the view of taking their lives.

verses.sanskrit:
अपूजयन्देवगणास्तदा कपिं; स्वयं च रामोऽतिबलश्च लक्ष्मणः
तथैव सुग्रीवमुखाः प्लवंगमा; विभीषणश्चैव महाबलस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
apūjayandevagaṇāstadā kapiṁ; svayaṁ ca rāmo'tibalaśca lakṣmaṇaḥ
tathaiva sugrīvamukhāḥ plavaṁgamā; vibhīṣaṇaścaiva mahābalastadā

translations.english: That mighty monkey-son to the Wind godhaving destroyed the Rākşasas and arrived (in the midst of the host), attained heroic glory, even as did Vişnu, having slain that destroyer of enemies-the mighty and dreadful Asura possessed of exceeding strength, stationed in the ban of the forces. And then the deities and Rāma himself and the highly powerful Lakşmaņa, also the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, and Vibhīşaņa endowed with great strength, honoured that monkey.

verses.sanskrit:
अकम्पनवधं श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धो वै राक्षसेश्वरः
किंचिद्दीनमुखश्चापि सचिवांस्तानुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
akampanavadhaṁ śrutvā kruddho vai rākṣaseśvaraḥ
kiṁciddīnamukhaścāpi sacivāṁstānudaikṣata

translations.english: Hearing that Akampana had been killed, the lord of Raksasas, overwhelmed with anger, with his face somewhat fallen, cast his eyes on his counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु मन्त्रिभिः संविचार्य च
पुरीं परिययौ लङ्कां सर्वान्गुल्मानवेक्षितुम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtaṁ tu mantribhiḥ saṁvicārya ca
purīṁ pariyayau laṅkāṁ sarvāngulmānavekṣitum

translations.english: Then pondering and reflecting for a while, in the forenoon he went round the city of Lankā for inspecting the barracks.

verses.sanskrit:
तां राक्षसगणैर्गुप्तां गुल्मैर्बहुभिरावृताम्
ददर्श नगरीं लङ्कां पताकाध्वजमालिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ rākṣasagaṇairguptāṁ gulmairbahubhirāvṛtām
dadarśa nagarīṁ laṅkāṁ patākādhvajamālinīm

translations.english: The king surveyed the city guarded by the Rakşsasas, covered with innumerable barracks, and crowned with ensigns and standards,

verses.sanskrit:
रुद्धां तु नगरीं दृष्ट्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
उवाचामर्षितः काले प्रहस्तं युद्धकोविदम्
verses.transliteration:
ruddhāṁ tu nagarīṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
uvācāmarṣitaḥ kāle prahastaṁ yuddhakovidam

translations.english: Seeing the city besieged, Ravana-lord of the Rākşaşas-seasonably spoke words of welfare to Prahasta skilled in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरस्योपनिविष्टस्य सहसा पीडितस्य च
नान्यं युद्धात्प्रपश्यामि मोक्षं युद्धविशारद
verses.transliteration:
purasyopaniviṣṭasya sahasā pīḍitasya ca
nānyaṁ yuddhātprapaśyāmi mokṣaṁ yuddhaviśārada

translations.english: "Save battle, deliverance find I none for the city suddenly beleaguered and put to straits.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं वा कुम्भकर्णो वा त्वं वा सेनापतिर्मम
इन्द्रजिद्वा निकुम्भो वा वहेयुर्भारमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ vā kumbhakarṇo vā tvaṁ vā senāpatirmama
indrajidvā nikumbho vā vaheyurbhāramīdṛśam

translations.english: And this strain must be borne by these versed in warfare-me or Kumbhakarna or you-my general or Indrajit or Nikumbha.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं बलमितः शीघ्रमादाय परिगृह्य च
विजयायाभिनिर्याहि यत्र सर्वे वनौकसः
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ balamitaḥ śīghramādāya parigṛhya ca
vijayāyābhiniryāhi yatra sarve vanaukasaḥ

translations.english: Therefore do you from this place, speedily taking this force, march to where the monkeys are, for securing victory (in the encounter).

verses.sanskrit:
निर्याणादेव ते नूनं चपला हरिवाहिनी
नर्दतां राक्षसेन्द्राणां श्रुत्वा नादं द्रविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
niryāṇādeva te nūnaṁ capalā harivāhinī
nardatāṁ rākṣasendrāṇāṁ śrutvā nādaṁ draviṣyati

translations.english: And as soon as you set out, the monkeyforces, hearing the roars of the foremost Rākșasas-speedily setting themselves in motionshall flee away.

verses.sanskrit:
चपला ह्यविनीताश्च चलचित्ताश्च वानराः
न सहिष्यन्ति ते नादं सिंहनादमिव द्विपाः
verses.transliteration:
capalā hyavinītāśca calacittāśca vānarāḥ
na sahiṣyanti te nādaṁ siṁhanādamiva dvipāḥ

translations.english: And volatile and haughty and of fickle minds, the monkeys will not be able to bear your shouts; even as elephants are incapable of bearing the roaring of a lion.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्रुते च बले तस्मिन्रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
अवशस्ते निरालम्बः प्रहस्तवशमेष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vidrute ca bale tasminrāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
avaśaste nirālambaḥ prahastavaśameṣyati

translations.english: And on that monkey-army running away, Rāma in company with Sumitrās son, deprived of his power and shorn of support, shall, O Prahasta, come under your subjection.

verses.sanskrit:
आपत्संशयिता श्रेयो नात्र निःसंशयीकृता
प्रतिलोमानुलोमं वा यद्वा नो मन्यसे हितम्
verses.transliteration:
āpatsaṁśayitā śreyo nātra niḥsaṁśayīkṛtā
pratilomānulomaṁ vā yadvā no manyase hitam

translations.english: In this matter, your being slain is uncertain, but victory is certain. Now do you, as you weigh out welfare, declare yourself for or against this course.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणेनैवमुक्तस्तु प्रहस्तो वाहिनीपतिः
राक्षसेन्द्रमुवाचेदमसुरेन्द्रमिवोशना
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇenaivamuktastu prahasto vāhinīpatiḥ
rākṣasendramuvācedamasurendramivośanā

translations.english: Thus addressed by Ravana, Prahasta-general of the forces-said to the Rākşaas-chief; like Uśanas addressing the lord of Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्मन्त्रितपूर्वं नः कुशलैः सह मन्त्रिभिः
विवादश्चापि नो वृत्तः समवेक्ष्य परस्परम्
verses.transliteration:
rājanmantritapūrvaṁ naḥ kuśalaiḥ saha mantribhiḥ
vivādaścāpi no vṛttaḥ samavekṣya parasparam

translations.english: O king before this we had deliberated together with wise counsellors, and then we disputed with each other in our respective views.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदानेन तु सीतायाः श्रेयो व्यवसितं मया
अप्रदाने पुनर्युद्धं दृष्टमेतत्तथैव नः
verses.transliteration:
pradānena tu sītāyāḥ śreyo vyavasitaṁ mayā
apradāne punaryuddhaṁ dṛṣṭametattathaiva naḥ

translations.english: And I had declared myself for giving up Sītā as fraught with our welfare; and we saw war involved in withholding her.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं दानैश्च मानैश्च सततं पूजितस्त्वया
सान्त्वैश्च विविधैः काले किं न कुर्यां प्रियं तव
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ dānaiśca mānaiśca satataṁ pūjitastvayā
sāntvaiśca vividhaiḥ kāle kiṁ na kuryāṁ priyaṁ tava

translations.english: I have ever been honoured by you variously with gifts and regard and soft speech. And what is your good for which I shall not be at the pains?

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मे जीवितं रक्ष्यं पुत्रदारधनानि वा
त्वं पश्य मां जुहूषन्तं त्वदर्थे जीवितं युधि
verses.transliteration:
na hi me jīvitaṁ rakṣyaṁ putradāradhanāni vā
tvaṁ paśya māṁ juhūṣantaṁ tvadarthe jīvitaṁ yudhi

translations.english: My life I do not care to keep, nor yet my sons or my wife. Behold! for you will I offer up my life into the sacrificial fire of conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु भर्तारं रावणं वाहिनीपतिः
समानयत मे शीघ्रं राक्षसानां महद्बलम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu bhartāraṁ rāvaṇaṁ vāhinīpatiḥ
samānayata me śīghraṁ rākṣasānāṁ mahadbalam

translations.english: Having said this to his master-Rävaņa-the general, Prahasta, addressed his generals staying before him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
मद्बाणाशनिवेगेन हतानां तु रणाजिरे
अद्य तृप्यन्तु मांसेन पक्षिणः काननौकसाम्
verses.transliteration:
madbāṇāśanivegena hatānāṁ tu raṇājire
adya tṛpyantu māṁsena pakṣiṇaḥ kānanaukasām

translations.english: At once bring up the mighty host of Raksasas Today in the field of fight will I entertain the flesh-feeding fowls of the forest with the bodies of the foes slain with my resistless shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तास्ते प्रहस्तेन बलाध्यक्षाः कृतत्वराः
बलमुद्योजयामासुस्तस्मिन्राक्षसमन्दिरे
verses.transliteration:
ityuktāste prahastena balādhyakṣāḥ kṛtatvarāḥ
balamudyojayāmāsustasminrākṣasamandire

translations.english: Hearing his speech, the highly powerful leaders arrayed the army in that abode of the Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन तिग्मनानाविधायुधैः
लङ्का राक्षसवीरैस्तैर्गजैरिव समाकुला
verses.transliteration:
sā babhūva muhūrtena tigmanānāvidhāyudhaiḥ
laṅkā rākṣasavīraistairgajairiva samākulā

translations.english: In a moment Lankā swarmed with heroic and terrific Rākşasas equipped with various arms, as if with elephants, as well as with people worshipping Fire and bowing down to Brāhmaṇas. And the perfumed breeze blew, laden with the incense of sacrificial offerings.

verses.sanskrit:
स्रजश्च विविधाकारा जगृहुस्त्वभिमन्त्रिताः
संग्रामसज्जाः संहृष्टा धारयन्राक्षसास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
srajaśca vividhākārā jagṛhustvabhimantritāḥ
saṁgrāmasajjāḥ saṁhṛṣṭā dhārayanrākṣasāstadā

translations.english: The Raksasas, inspired with martial ardour, put on diverse garlands, consecrated with scriptural formulae; and donned on their armour.

verses.sanskrit:
सधनुष्काः कवचिनो वेगादाप्लुत्य राक्षसाः
रावणं प्रेक्ष्य राजानं प्रहस्तं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
sadhanuṣkāḥ kavacino vegādāplutya rākṣasāḥ
rāvaṇaṁ prekṣya rājānaṁ prahastaṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: And furnished with their boys and wearing their armour, the Rākşasas, on seeing king Ravana, leaving (their vehicles), stood, surrounding Prahasta.

verses.sanskrit:
हयैर्महाजवैर्युक्तं सम्यक्सूतसुसंयुतम्
महाजलदनिर्घोषं साक्षाच्चन्द्रार्कभास्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
hayairmahājavairyuktaṁ samyaksūtasusaṁyutam
mahājaladanirghoṣaṁ sākṣāccandrārkabhāsvaram

translations.english: The greeting the monarch, Prahasta, furnished (with all appliances of battle), winding his dreadful trumpet, ascended his car; having all sorts of weapons; yoked with wondrous fleet steeds; driven by a competent charioteer, excellently furnished; sending up sounds resembling the rumbling of mighty masses of cloud, appearing like the very sun or Moon; invincible with a serpent-standard; having a defence as well as a portion exceedingly handsome; netted with gold all round; and seeming to be laughing in grace.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दुंदुभिनिर्घोषः पर्जन्यनिनदोपमः
शुश्रुवे शङ्खशब्दश्च प्रयाते वाहिनीपतौ
verses.transliteration:
tato duṁdubhinirghoṣaḥ parjanyaninadopamaḥ
śuśruve śaṅkhaśabdaśca prayāte vāhinīpatau

translations.english: Then ascending this car, Prahasta, whom Rāvana had entrusted with authority, surrounded by a vast host, swiftly went out of Larkā. And then there were heard the sounds of kettledrums, resembling the roars of Parjanya, and the sounds of musical instruments, as if filling the Earth.

verses.sanskrit:
निनदन्तः स्वरान्घोरान्राक्षसा जग्मुरग्रतः
भीमरूपा महाकायाः प्रहस्तस्य पुरःसराः
verses.transliteration:
ninadantaḥ svarānghorānrākṣasā jagmuragrataḥ
bhīmarūpā mahākāyāḥ prahastasya puraḥsarāḥ

translations.english: And on that general of the forces marching, sounds of conchs were heard (all around); and the Rākşasas of dreadful forms and huge bodies, going before Prahasta, advanced, emitting tremendous roars.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यूढेनैव सुघोरेण पूर्वद्वारात्स निर्ययौ
गजयूथनिकाशेन बलेन महता वृतः
verses.transliteration:
vyūḍhenaiva sughoreṇa pūrvadvārātsa niryayau
gajayūthanikāśena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ

translations.english: And he went out by the Eastern entrance, environed by this exceedingly dreadful array, resembling troops of elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरप्रतिमौघेन वृतस्तेन बलेन सः
प्रहस्तो निर्ययौ तूर्णं क्रुद्धः कालान्तकोपमः
verses.transliteration:
sāgarapratimaughena vṛtastena balena saḥ
prahasto niryayau tūrṇaṁ kruddhaḥ kālāntakopamaḥ

translations.english: And resembling the Destroyer-Yama himselfPrahasta in rage went out surrounded by that mighty host resembling the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य निर्याण घोषेण राक्षसानां च नर्दताम्
लङ्कायां सर्वभूतानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः
verses.transliteration:
tasya niryāṇa ghoṣeṇa rākṣasānāṁ ca nardatām
laṅkāyāṁ sarvabhūtāni vinedurvikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ

translations.english: And at the tumult raised by their exodus, as well as the roars of the Rākşasas, all creatures in Lankā began to cry in preternatural tones.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यभ्रमाकाशमाविश्य मांसशोणितभोजनाः
मण्डलान्यपसव्यानि खगाश्चक्रू रथं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
vyabhramākāśamāviśya māṁsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
maṇḍalānyapasavyāni khagāścakrū rathaṁ prati

translations.english: And swarming under the cloudless welkin, birds feasting on flesh and gore began to gyrate at the right hand of the car.

verses.sanskrit: वमन्त्यः पावकज्वालाः शिवा घोरा ववाशिरे
verses.transliteration: vamantyaḥ pāvakajvālāḥ śivā ghorā vavāśire

translations.english: From the cloudless yet fierce sky meteors began to shoot. and throwing up flames from their mouths, dreadful jackals began to emit cries.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षात्पपातोल्का वायुश्च परुषो ववौ
अन्योन्यमभिसंरब्धा ग्रहाश्च न चकाशिरे
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣātpapātolkā vāyuśca paruṣo vavau
anyonyamabhisaṁrabdhā grahāśca na cakāśire

translations.english: And dreadful jackals, emitting live flames from their mouths, set up cries. And stars began to shoot from the firmament; and the winds to ruffle.

verses.sanskrit:
ववर्षू रुधिरं चास्य सिषिचुश्च पुरःसरान्
केतुमूर्धनि गृध्रोऽस्य विलीनो दक्षिणामुखः
verses.transliteration:
vavarṣū rudhiraṁ cāsya siṣicuśca puraḥsarān
ketumūrdhani gṛdhro'sya vilīno dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ

translations.english: And enraged at each other, the planetary bodies were shorn of their brightness. And clouds emitting sharp sounds, showered down blood upon the car, and those marching in front were washed therewith. And alighting at the top of the standard, a vulture set up cries, facing the south and began to prick both its sides, thereby depriving (Prahasta) of his grace.

verses.sanskrit:
सारथेर्बहुशश्चास्य संग्राममवगाहतः
प्रतोदो न्यपतद्धस्तात्सूतस्य हयसादिनः
verses.transliteration:
sāratherbahuśaścāsya saṁgrāmamavagāhataḥ
pratodo nyapataddhastātsūtasya hayasādinaḥ

translations.english: And from the hands of his charioteer and his driver conducting the steeds, never given to turning away from the field the goad began to drop again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्याण श्रीश्च यास्यासीद्भास्वरा च सुदुर्लभा
सा ननाश मुहूर्तेन समे च स्खलिता हयाः
verses.transliteration:
niryāṇa śrīśca yāsyāsīdbhāsvarā ca sudurlabhā
sā nanāśa muhūrtena same ca skhalitā hayāḥ

translations.english: The auspiciousness that was bright and rare when the army set out, was clean gone in a moment, and the steeds began to stumble on even ground.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहस्तं त्वभिनिर्यान्तं प्रख्यात बलपौरुषम्
युधि नानाप्रहरणा कपिसेनाभ्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
prahastaṁ tvabhiniryāntaṁ prakhyāta balapauruṣam
yudhi nānāpraharaṇā kapisenābhyavartata

translations.english: And as Prahasta of renowned worth and valour marched, the monkey-army equipped with various arms, presented themselves before him.

verses.sanskrit:
उभे प्रमुदिते सैन्ये रक्षोगणवनौकसाम्
वेगितानां समर्थानामन्योन्यवधकाङ्क्षिणाम्
परस्परं चाह्वयतां निनादः श्रूयते महान्
verses.transliteration:
ubhe pramudite sainye rakṣogaṇavanaukasām
vegitānāṁ samarthānāmanyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇām
parasparaṁ cāhvayatāṁ ninādaḥ śrūyate mahān

translations.english: And loud was the tumult that was raised by the monkeys. And mighty was the din that was heard of those, uprooting trees and taking up ponderous crags, of the Räkşasas roaring and the monkeys storming in both the exhilarated armies of Raksasa and wood-rangers, of vehement and able (warriors) eager for slaying each other, and challenging each other to fight.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहस्तः कपिराजवाहिनी;मभिप्रतस्थे विजयाय दुर्मतिः
विवृद्धवेगां च विवेश तां चमूं; यथा मुमूर्षुः शलभो विभावसुम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahastaḥ kapirājavāhinī;mabhipratasthe vijayāya durmatiḥ
vivṛddhavegāṁ ca viveśa tāṁ camūṁ; yathā mumūrṣuḥ śalabho vibhāvasum

translations.english: And like an insect falling into a flame, the wicked-minded Prahasta for obtaining victory, increasing his impetuosity entered into that host of the monkey-king.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहस्तं निर्यान्तं भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्
गर्जन्तं सुमहाकायं राक्षसैरभिसंवृतम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahastaṁ niryāntaṁ bhīmaṁ bhīmaparākramam
garjantaṁ sumahākāyaṁ rākṣasairabhisaṁvṛtam

translations.english: That mighty army of strong monkeys, wrought up with wrath, and roaring at Prahasta, saw him dreadful and of terrific prowess and huge-bodied, surrounded on all sides by the Raksasas, and setting up roars, marching.

verses.sanskrit:
खड्गशक्त्यष्टिबाणाश्च शूलानि मुसलानि च
गदाश्च परिघाः प्रासा विविधाश्च परश्वधाः
verses.transliteration:
khaḍgaśaktyaṣṭibāṇāśca śūlāni musalāni ca
gadāśca parighāḥ prāsā vividhāśca paraśvadhāḥ

translations.english: The Raksasas, eagerly desirous of victory, pursued the monkeys, wielding swords and darts and Rştis, and javelins and shafts and maces and clubs and bludgeons and práşas and various axes and curious bows.

verses.sanskrit:
जगृहुः पादपांश्चापि पुष्पितान्वानरर्षभाः
