verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sahasraṁ bherīṇāṁ yugapatsamahanyata
mṛṣṭakāñcanakoṇānāmasaktānāṁ samantataḥ

translations.english: Then they simultaneously sounded a thousand kettle-drums beaten with sticks of polished gold.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमप्यतिनिद्रस्तु यदा नैव प्रबुध्यत
शापस्य वशमापन्नस्ततः क्रुद्धा निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
evamapyatinidrastu yadā naiva prabudhyata
śāpasya vaśamāpannastataḥ kruddhā niśācarāḥ

translations.english: And coming under the sway of the curse, when that one sunk in slumber did not wake up, the night-rangers were wrought up with wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
महाक्रोधसमाविष्टाः सर्वे भीमपराक्रमाः
तद्रक्षोबोधयिष्यन्तश्चक्रुरन्ये पराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
mahākrodhasamāviṣṭāḥ sarve bhīmaparākramāḥ
tadrakṣobodhayiṣyantaścakruranye parākramam

translations.english: And overcome with choler, they endowed with dreadful prowess addressed themselves vigorously to awakening him; and others put forth their energy.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ये भेरीः समाजघ्नुरन्ये चक्रुर्महास्वनम्
केशानन्ये प्रलुलुपुः कर्णावन्ये दशन्ति च
न कुम्भकर्णः पस्पन्दे महानिद्रावशं गतः
verses.transliteration:
anye bherīḥ samājaghnuranye cakrurmahāsvanam
keśānanye pralulupuḥ karṇāvanye daśanti ca
na kumbhakarṇaḥ paspande mahānidrāvaśaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Others smote the kettle-drums, and others set up loud cries. And others cut off his hair, and others bit his ears.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ये च बलिनस्तस्य कूटमुद्गरपाणयः
मूर्ध्नि वक्षसि गात्रेषु पातयन्कूटमुद्गरान्
verses.transliteration:
anye ca balinastasya kūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ
mūrdhni vakṣasi gātreṣu pātayankūṭamudgarān

translations.english: Others-strong ones-armed with poniards (kūt as) and maces, made their poniards and maces alight on his person.

verses.sanskrit:
रज्जुबन्धनबद्धाभिः शतघ्नीभिश्च सर्वतः
वध्यमानो महाकायो न प्राबुध्यत राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
rajjubandhanabaddhābhiḥ śataghnībhiśca sarvataḥ
vadhyamāno mahākāyo na prābudhyata rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: And struck with sataghnis bound with cords, that huge-bodied one did not wake up.

verses.sanskrit:
वारणानां सहस्रं तु शरीरेऽस्य प्रधावितम्
कुम्भकर्णस्ततो बुद्धः स्पर्शं परमबुध्यत
verses.transliteration:
vāraṇānāṁ sahasraṁ tu śarīre'sya pradhāvitam
kumbhakarṇastato buddhaḥ sparśaṁ paramabudhyata

translations.english: Then when a thousand elephants rushed against his body, recovering his consciousness, he awoke.

verses.sanskrit:
स पात्यमानैर्गिरिशृङ्गवृक्षै;रचिन्तयंस्तान्विपुलान्प्रहारान्
निद्राक्षयात्क्षुद्भयपीडितश्च; विजृम्भमाणः सहसोत्पपात
verses.transliteration:
sa pātyamānairgiriśṛṅgavṛkṣai;racintayaṁstānvipulānprahārān
nidrākṣayātkṣudbhayapīḍitaśca; vijṛmbhamāṇaḥ sahasotpapāta

translations.english: Assailed with mountain-peaks and trees descending on his body, he without minding those tremendous blows, on sleep having been dispelled. Suddenly got up yawning, suffering the pangs of hunger.

verses.sanskrit:
स नागभोगाचलशृङ्गकल्पौ; विक्षिप्य बाहू गिरिशृङ्गसारौ
विवृत्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभं; निशाचरोऽसौ विकृतं जजृम्भे
verses.transliteration:
sa nāgabhogācalaśṛṅgakalpau; vikṣipya bāhū giriśṛṅgasārau
vivṛtya vaktraṁ vaḍavāmukhābhaṁ; niśācaro'sau vikṛtaṁ jajṛmbhe

translations.english: Then that night-ranger resembling an elephant or a serpent or a mountain-peak, casting about his arms superior in force to the thunder-bolt itself, and opening his deformed mouth like to that of a mule, yawned (again and again).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य जाजृम्भमाणस्य वक्त्रं पातालसंनिभम्
ददृशे मेरुशृङ्गाग्रे दिवाकर इवोदितः
verses.transliteration:
tasya jājṛmbhamāṇasya vaktraṁ pātālasaṁnibham
dadṛśe meruśṛṅgāgre divākara ivoditaḥ

translations.english: As he yawned, his mouth resembling the subterraneous regions, looked like the Sun stationed at the summit of Meru.

verses.sanskrit:
विजृम्भमाणोऽतिबलः प्रतिबुद्धो निशाचरः
निश्वासश्चास्य संजज्ञे पर्वतादिव मारुतः
verses.transliteration:
vijṛmbhamāṇo'tibalaḥ pratibuddho niśācaraḥ
niśvāsaścāsya saṁjajñe parvatādiva mārutaḥ

translations.english: That night ranger possessed of unwieldly strength woke up, yawning. And the breath that he breathed resembled a storm raging in a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
रूपमुत्तिष्ठतस्तस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य तद्बभौ
तपान्ते सबलाकस्य मेघस्येव विवर्षतः
verses.transliteration:
rūpamuttiṣṭhatastasya kumbhakarṇasya tadbabhau
tapānte sabalākasya meghasyeva vivarṣataḥ

translations.english: Then as he sat up, Kumbhakarņa's form appeared like that of the Destroyer himself at the universal wreck, intent upon consuming all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य दीप्ताग्निसदृशे विद्युत्सदृशवर्चसी
ददृशाते महानेत्रे दीप्ताविव महाग्रहौ
verses.transliteration:
tasya dīptāgnisadṛśe vidyutsadṛśavarcasī
dadṛśāte mahānetre dīptāviva mahāgrahau

translations.english: The large eyes of that one, resembling a life flame and endowed with the splendour of lighting, appeared like a pair of glowing planets.

verses.sanskrit:
आदद्बुभुक्षितो मांसं शोणितं तृषितोऽपिबत्
मेदः कुम्भं च मद्यं च पपौ शक्ररिपुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
ādadbubhukṣito māṁsaṁ śoṇitaṁ tṛṣito'pibat
medaḥ kumbhaṁ ca madyaṁ ca papau śakraripustadā

translations.english: And hungering, he fed on flesh and athirst, drank blood. And then that enemy of Sakra drank vesselfuls of fat and blood.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तृप्त इति ज्ञात्वा समुत्पेतुर्निशाचराः
शिरोभिश्च प्रणम्यैनं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
tatastṛpta iti jñātvā samutpeturniśācarāḥ
śirobhiśca praṇamyainaṁ sarvataḥ paryavārayan

translations.english: And concluding that he was replete, the nightrangers came up; and bowing down their heads stood circling him on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
स सर्वान्सान्त्वयामास नैरृतान्नैरृतर्षभः
बोधनाद्विस्मितश्चापि राक्षसानिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa sarvānsāntvayāmāsa nairṛtānnairṛtarṣabhaḥ
bodhanādvismitaścāpi rākṣasānidamabravīt

translations.english: That foremost of Naiſtas cheered all those Naiſtas: and surprised at his having been roused, spoke to the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
किमर्थमहमाहत्य भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः
कच्चित्सुकुशलं राज्ञो भयं वा नेह किंचन
verses.transliteration:
kimarthamahamāhatya bhavadbhiḥ pratibodhitaḥ
kaccitsukuśalaṁ rājño bhayaṁ vā neha kiṁcana

translations.english: Why, being honoured, have I been awakened by you? Is it well with the king? Or has any fear: sprung up here?

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा ध्रुवमन्येभ्यो भयं परमुपस्थितम्
यदर्थमेव त्वरितैर्भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā dhruvamanyebhyo bhayaṁ paramupasthitam
yadarthameva tvaritairbhavadbhiḥ pratibodhitaḥ

translations.english: Or has a mighty fear presented itself forsooth from among others; for which I have bee speedily awakened by you?

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य राक्षसराजस्य भयमुत्पाटयाम्यहम्
पातयिष्ये महेन्द्रं वा शातयिष्ये तथानलम्
verses.transliteration:
adya rākṣasarājasya bhayamutpāṭayāmyaham
pātayiṣye mahendraṁ vā śātayiṣye tathānalam

translations.english: This very day will I uproot quite the fear of the sovereign of the Rākşasas. I will split up the great Indra himself, or make Fire himself give up his heat.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यल्पकारणे सुप्तं बोधयिष्यति मां भृशम्
तदाख्यातार्थतत्त्वेन मत्प्रबोधनकारणम्
verses.transliteration:
na hyalpakāraṇe suptaṁ bodhayiṣyati māṁ bhṛśam
tadākhyātārthatattvena matprabodhanakāraṇam

translations.english: One does not awaken my like for a light cause. therefore do you give the real truth of the cause of your awakening me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं कुम्भकर्णमरिंदमम्
यूपाक्षः सचिवो राज्ञः कृताञ्जलिरुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ saṁrabdhaṁ kumbhakarṇamariṁdamam
yūpākṣaḥ sacivo rājñaḥ kṛtāñjaliruvāca ha

translations.english: Thereat a minister of the king, named Yupakş a, with joined hands said to that humbler of foesKumbhakarna-wrought up with wrath, who was thus speaking.

verses.sanskrit:
न नो देवकृतं किंचिद्भयमस्ति कदाचन
न दैत्यदानवेभ्यो वा भयमस्ति हि तादृशम्
यादृशं मानुषं राजन्भयमस्मानुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
na no devakṛtaṁ kiṁcidbhayamasti kadācana
na daityadānavebhyo vā bhayamasti hi tādṛśam
yādṛśaṁ mānuṣaṁ rājanbhayamasmānupasthitam

translations.english: And never fear so come to us anywise from Daityas or Dānavas, as it has arrived from a man, O king.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरैः पर्वताकारैर्लङ्केयं परिवारिता
सीताहरणसंतप्ताद्रामान्नस्तुमुलं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
vānaraiḥ parvatākārairlaṅkeyaṁ parivāritā
sītāharaṇasaṁtaptādrāmānnastumulaṁ bhayam

translations.english: This Lanka has been hemmed in by monkeys resembling mountains. And terrific is the terror that come even from Rāma scorched with fire springing from the ravishment of Sītă.

verses.sanskrit:
एकेन वानरेणेयं पूर्वं दग्धा महापुरी
कुमारो निहतश्चाक्षः सानुयात्रः सकुञ्जरः
verses.transliteration:
ekena vānareṇeyaṁ pūrvaṁ dagdhā mahāpurī
kumāro nihataścākṣaḥ sānuyātraḥ sakuñjaraḥ

translations.english: Ere this by a single monkey was this splendid city burnt down. And the prince Akşa has been slain along with his following and elephants.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयं रक्षोऽधिपश्चापि पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः
मृतेति संयुगे मुक्तारामेणादित्यतेजसा
verses.transliteration:
svayaṁ rakṣo'dhipaścāpi paulastyo devakaṇṭakaḥ
mṛteti saṁyuge muktārāmeṇādityatejasā

translations.english: That thorn in the sides of deities, that lord of the Raksasas-Pulastya's son himself-has been set free in conflict by Rāghava endowed with the splendour of the Sun, Saying, “Go you.

verses.sanskrit:
यन्न देवैः कृतो राजा नापि दैत्यैर्न दानवैः
कृतः स इह रामेण विमुक्तः प्राणसंशयात्
verses.transliteration:
yanna devaiḥ kṛto rājā nāpi daityairna dānavaiḥ
kṛtaḥ sa iha rāmeṇa vimuktaḥ prāṇasaṁśayāt

translations.english: What had been done to the king by neither the gods nor Daityas nor yet the Dănavas, has been done by Rāma; and he has been set free, having come to a pass imperilling his life.

verses.sanskrit:
स यूपाक्षवचः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्युधि पराजयम्
कुम्भकर्णो विवृत्ताक्षो यूपाक्षमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa yūpākṣavacaḥ śrutvā bhrāturyudhi parājayam
kumbhakarṇo vivṛttākṣo yūpākṣamidamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Yüpākşa's speech and hearing of the defeat of his brother, Kumbhakarņa, with his eyes whirling, spoke to him, saying..

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वमद्यैव यूपाक्ष हरिसैन्यं सलक्ष्मणम्
राघवं च रणे हत्वा पश्चाद्द्रक्ष्यामि रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvamadyaiva yūpākṣa harisainyaṁ salakṣmaṇam
rāghavaṁ ca raṇe hatvā paścāddrakṣyāmi rāvaṇam

translations.english: Today, O Yüpākṣa, after vanquishing in battle the monkey-army together with Laksmana and Raghava, shall I see Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसांस्तर्पयिष्यामि हरीणां मांसशोणितैः
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि स्वयं पास्यामि शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasāṁstarpayiṣyāmi harīṇāṁ māṁsaśoṇitaiḥ
rāmalakṣmaṇayoścāpi svayaṁ pāsyāmi śoṇitam

translations.english: I shall regale the Rākṣasas with the flesh and blood of the monkeys, and myself drink the blood of Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य; सगर्वितं रोषविवृद्धदोषम्
महोदरो नैरृतयोधमुख्यः; कृताञ्जलिर्वाक्यमिदं बभाषे
verses.transliteration:
tattasya vākyaṁ bruvato niśamya; sagarvitaṁ roṣavivṛddhadoṣam
mahodaro nairṛtayodhamukhyaḥ; kṛtāñjalirvākyamidaṁ babhāṣe

translations.english: Hearing his words as he haughtily spoke thus with his spirit of insolence magnified by much, that foremost of the Nairta soldiers, Mahodara, with joined hands observed.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गुणदोषु विमृश्य च
पश्चादपि महाबाहो शत्रून्युधि विजेष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā guṇadoṣu vimṛśya ca
paścādapi mahābāho śatrūnyudhi vijeṣyasi

translations.english: O long-armed one, having at first heard Rāvana's words and considered their justice or otherwise, you will afterwards defeat the foe in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरवचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसैः परिवारितः
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजाः संप्रतस्थे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
mahodaravacaḥ śrutvā rākṣasaiḥ parivāritaḥ
kumbhakarṇo mahātejāḥ saṁpratasthe mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Mahodara's words, the exceedingly energetic and mighty (Kumbhakarma) surrounded by the Rākşasas, prepared to depart.

verses.sanskrit:
तं समुत्थाप्य भीमाक्षं भीमरूपपराक्रमम्
राक्षसास्त्वरिता जग्मुर्दशग्रीवनिवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ samutthāpya bhīmākṣaṁ bhīmarūpaparākramam
rākṣasāstvaritā jagmurdaśagrīvaniveśanam

translations.english: Having roused from his slumbers that one of terrific prowess having dreadful eyes the Rāks asas speedily arrived at the residence of the Tennecked one.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गत्वा दशग्रीवमासीनं परमासने
ऊचुर्बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्व एव निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
tato gatvā daśagrīvamāsīnaṁ paramāsane
ūcurbaddhāñjalipuṭāḥ sarva eva niśācarāḥ

translations.english: And presenting themselves before the Tennecked on seated on a superb seat, all the nightrangers spoke with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रबुद्धः कुम्भकर्णोऽसौ भ्राता ते राक्षसर्षभ
कथं तत्रैव निर्यातु द्रक्ष्यसे तमिहागतम्
verses.transliteration:
prabuddhaḥ kumbhakarṇo'sau bhrātā te rākṣasarṣabha
kathaṁ tatraiva niryātu drakṣyase tamihāgatam

translations.english: O lord of the Rākṣasas, your brother, Kumbhakarņa, has been roused. Shall he march from there; or will you see him come here?

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्धृष्टो यथान्यायं च पूजितम्
द्रष्टुमेनमिहेच्छामि यथान्यायं च पूजितम्
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇastvabravīddhṛṣṭo yathānyāyaṁ ca pūjitam
draṣṭumenamihecchāmi yathānyāyaṁ ca pūjitam

translations.english: Thereat, Ravana, pleased, spoke to those Raks asas who had presented themselves, “I wish to see him here, and do you honour him fittingly."

verses.sanskrit:
तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे पुनरागम्य राक्षसाः
कुम्भकर्णमिदं वाक्यमूचू रावणचोदिताः
verses.transliteration:
tathetyuktvā tu te sarve punarāgamya rākṣasāḥ
kumbhakarṇamidaṁ vākyamūcū rāvaṇacoditāḥ

translations.english: Thereat, saying 'So be it', the Rākşasas, directed by Ravana, going back, spoke to Kumbhakarna.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रष्टुं त्वां काङ्क्षते राजा सर्वराक्षसपुंगवः
गमने क्रियतां बुद्धिर्भ्रातरं संप्रहर्षय
verses.transliteration:
draṣṭuṁ tvāṁ kāṅkṣate rājā sarvarākṣasapuṁgavaḥ
gamane kriyatāṁ buddhirbhrātaraṁ saṁpraharṣaya

translations.english: That foremost of all the Rākşasas-the kingwish to see you. So mind you going, and gladden your brother.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुर्धर्षो भ्रातुराज्ञाय शासनम्
तथेत्युक्त्वा महावीर्यः शयनादुत्पपात ह
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇastu durdharṣo bhrāturājñāya śāsanam
tathetyuktvā mahāvīryaḥ śayanādutpapāta ha

translations.english: The irrepressible Kumbhakarna possessed of prodigious prowess, learning the mandate of his brother, sa', ing, 'So be it', rose up from his bed.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रक्षाल्य वदनं हृष्टः स्नातः परमभूषितः
पिपासुस्त्वरयामास पानं बलसमीरणम्
verses.transliteration:
prakṣālya vadanaṁ hṛṣṭaḥ snātaḥ paramabhūṣitaḥ
pipāsustvarayāmāsa pānaṁ balasamīraṇam

translations.english: Washing his face, and having bathed, that one, feeling refreshed and enjoying exceeding exhilaration of spirit, wishing to drink, urged (the Rākşasas) to bring the nerve-conferring draught.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते त्वरितास्तस्य राज्षसा रावणाज्ञया
मद्यं भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान्क्षिप्रमेवोपहारयन्
verses.transliteration:
tataste tvaritāstasya rājṣasā rāvaṇājñayā
madyaṁ bhakṣyāṁśca vividhānkṣipramevopahārayan

translations.english: Then the Rākşasas at the command of Rāvana speedily procured wine and various kinds of viands.

verses.sanskrit:
ईषत्समुत्कटो मत्तस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः
कुम्भकर्णो बभौ हृष्टः कालान्तकयमोपमः
verses.transliteration:
īṣatsamutkaṭo mattastejobalasamanvitaḥ
kumbhakarṇo babhau hṛṣṭaḥ kālāntakayamopamaḥ

translations.english: Having drunk two thousand vessels (of wine) he prepared to go. And slightly swollen and flushed, Kumbhakarma, attaining access of strength and fire, waxed wroth and resembled the Doom and Destroyer-Yama himself. And striding to the residence of his brother backed by the Raksasa force, Kumbhakarņa shook the earth with his tread.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुः स भवनं गच्छन्रक्षोबलसमन्वितः
कुम्भकर्णः पदन्यासैरकम्पयत मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātuḥ sa bhavanaṁ gacchanrakṣobalasamanvitaḥ
kumbhakarṇaḥ padanyāsairakampayata medinīm

translations.english: Kumbhakarņa surrounded by numbers of Rākşasas, entered his brother's abode, making the very earth tremble with his tread.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजमार्गं वपुषा प्रकाशय;न्सहस्ररश्मिर्धरणीमिवांशुभिः
जगाम तत्राञ्जलिमालया वृतः; शतक्रतुर्गेहमिव स्वयम्भुवः
verses.transliteration:
sa rājamārgaṁ vapuṣā prakāśaya;nsahasraraśmirdharaṇīmivāṁśubhiḥ
jagāma tatrāñjalimālayā vṛtaḥ; śatakraturgehamiva svayambhuvaḥ

translations.english: Illuming the highway with the splendour of his person, like the thousand-rayed (Sun) discovering the earth with his rays, (Kumbhakarna) went on, engirt around by joined hands resembling wreaths, like Śatakratu* going to the abode of the Self-sprung. *Lit. him of an hundred sacrifices-an appellation of Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
केचिच्छरण्यं शरणं स्म रामं; व्रजन्ति केचिद्व्यथिताः पतन्ति
केचिद्दिशः स्म व्यथिताः प्रयान्ति; केचिद्भयार्ता भुवि शेरते स्म
verses.transliteration:
keciccharaṇyaṁ śaraṇaṁ sma rāmaṁ; vrajanti kecidvyathitāḥ patanti
keciddiśaḥ sma vyathitāḥ prayānti; kecidbhayārtā bhuvi śerate sma

translations.english: Then some sought the shelter of Răma, worthy of being so sought; and some, stricken (with panic), dropped to the earth; and some, suffering (from fear), fled to the carindal points; and some through stress (of apprehension) lay down on the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तमद्रिशृङ्गप्रतिमं किरीटिनं; स्पृशन्तमादित्यमिवात्मतेजसा
वनौकसः प्रेक्ष्य विवृद्धमद्भुतं; भयार्दिता दुद्रुविरे ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tamadriśṛṅgapratimaṁ kirīṭinaṁ; spṛśantamādityamivātmatejasā
vanaukasaḥ prekṣya vivṛddhamadbhutaṁ; bhayārditā dudruvire tatastataḥ

translations.english: Seeing that one resembling a very mountainpeak, decked with a diadem, seeming to touch the Sun himself with his energy, of colossal altitude, and wonderful to behold, the woodrangers, tormented with fright, began to scamper on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामो महातेजा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्
किरीटिनं महाकायं कुम्भकर्णं ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmo mahātejā dhanurādāya vīryavān
kirīṭinaṁ mahākāyaṁ kumbhakarṇaṁ dadarśa ha

translations.english: Then the exceedingly energetic Rāma possessed of prowess, taking his bow, saw Kumbhakarņa, having a huge body and decked with a diadem.

verses.sanskrit:
सतोयाम्बुदसंकाशं काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम्
दृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रदुद्राव वानराणां महाचमूः
verses.transliteration:
satoyāmbudasaṁkāśaṁ kāñcanāṅgadabhūṣaṇam
dṛṣṭvā punaḥ pradudrāva vānarāṇāṁ mahācamūḥ

translations.english: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas looking like a mountain; filling all the heavens as formerly Nārāyaṇa had done; resembling clouds charged with rain; and adorned with golden Angadas, the mighty army of monkeys began to run away at the top of its speed.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वर्धमानं च राक्षसं
सविस्मयमिदं रामो विभीषणमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
vidrutāṁ vāhinīṁ dṛṣṭvā vardhamānaṁ ca rākṣasaṁ
savismayamidaṁ rāmo vibhīṣaṇamuvāca ha

translations.english: Seeing the army scamper and the Rākşasa swelling, Rāma struck with surprise, said to Vibhisana. mass

verses.sanskrit:
कोऽसौ पर्वतसंकशः किरीटी हरिलोचनः
लङ्कायां दृश्यते वीरः सविद्युदिव तोयदः
verses.transliteration:
ko'sau parvatasaṁkaśaḥ kirīṭī harilocanaḥ
laṅkāyāṁ dṛśyate vīraḥ savidyudiva toyadaḥ

translations.english: Who is that tawny-eyed one, decked with a diadem, and looking like a hill? And in Lankā the hero appear like a of clouds embosoming lightning.

verses.sanskrit:
पृथिव्याः केतुभूतोऽसौ महानेकोऽत्र दृश्यते
यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे विद्रवन्ति ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
pṛthivyāḥ ketubhūto'sau mahāneko'tra dṛśyate
yaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti tatastataḥ

translations.english: And alone he seem like an ensign of the Earth; and seeing him the monkeys dart away hither and thither.

verses.sanskrit:
आचक्ष्व मे महान्कोऽसौ रक्षो वा यदि वासुरः
न मयैवंविधं भूतं दृष्टपूर्वं कदाचन
verses.transliteration:
ācakṣva me mahānko'sau rakṣo vā yadi vāsuraḥ
na mayaivaṁvidhaṁ bhūtaṁ dṛṣṭapūrvaṁ kadācana

translations.english: Tell me who he is, whether a Rākṣasa or an Asura. The like of him mine eyes had never before lighted on.

verses.sanskrit:
स पृष्टो राजपुत्रेण रामेणाक्लिष्टकारिणा
विभीषणो महाप्राज्ञः काकुत्स्थमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa rāmeṇākliṣṭakāriṇā
vibhīṣaṇo mahāprājñaḥ kākutsthamidamabravīt

translations.english: Accosted by the king's son-Rāma of untiring deeds-the exceedingly wise Vibhīşaņa said to Kakutstha.

verses.sanskrit:
येन वैवस्वतो युद्धे वासवश्च पराजितः
सैष विश्रवसः पुत्रः कुम्भकर्णः प्रतापवान्
verses.transliteration:
yena vaivasvato yuddhe vāsavaśca parājitaḥ
saiṣa viśravasaḥ putraḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ pratāpavān

translations.english: By whom in battle Vivasvata's offspring* and Vasava himself had been vanquished this is hethe wondrous powerful Kumbhakarņa, son to Visravā. No Rākṣasa is there that equals this one in size. *Yama-son of Vivasvata or the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन देवा युधि दानवाश्च; यक्षा भुजंगाः पिशिताशनाश्च
गन्धर्वविद्याधरकिंनराश्च; सहस्रशो राघव संप्रभग्नाः
verses.transliteration:
etena devā yudhi dānavāśca; yakṣā bhujaṁgāḥ piśitāśanāśca
gandharvavidyādharakiṁnarāśca; sahasraśo rāghava saṁprabhagnāḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, this one in battle has brought down Dānavas and Yakşas and Serpents' and flesh-feeders and Gandharvas and Vidyādharas and Pannagas by thousands. 1. Bhujanga:-semi-divine serpents. 2. Semi-divine serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
शूलपाणिं विरूपाक्षं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्
हन्तुं न शेकुस्त्रिदशाः कालोऽयमिति मोहिताः
verses.transliteration:
śūlapāṇiṁ virūpākṣaṁ kumbhakarṇaṁ mahābalam
hantuṁ na śekustridaśāḥ kālo'yamiti mohitāḥ

translations.english: The immortals themselves thinking the darthanded and fierce-eyed Kumbhakarņa possessed of great strength, as the Destroyer himself, were overwhelmed with stupor and were foiled in their exertions to slay him.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या ह्येष तेजस्वी कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
अन्येषां राक्षसेन्द्राणां वरदानकृतं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtyā hyeṣa tejasvī kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
anyeṣāṁ rākṣasendrāṇāṁ varadānakṛtaṁ balam

translations.english: The exceedingly powerful Kumbhakarņa is mighty by nature: the strength of other redoubtable Rākşasas is owing to boons obtained by them.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन जातमात्रेण क्षुधार्तेन महात्मना
भक्षितानि सहस्राणि सत्त्वानां सुबहून्यपि
verses.transliteration:
etena jātamātreṇa kṣudhārtena mahātmanā
bhakṣitāni sahasrāṇi sattvānāṁ subahūnyapi

translations.english: As soon as this high-souled one was born and was a babe, he began to devour up countless creatures by the thousand.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु संभक्ष्यमाणेषु प्रजा भयनिपीडिताः
यान्ति स्म शरणं शक्रं तमप्यर्थं न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
teṣu saṁbhakṣyamāṇeṣu prajā bhayanipīḍitāḥ
yānti sma śaraṇaṁ śakraṁ tamapyarthaṁ nyavedayan

translations.english: On these having been devoured, creatures, afflicted with affright consequent on those having been eaten up, sought the shelter of Sakra and told him what had happened.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो महेन्द्रो; जघान वज्रेण शितेन वज्री
स शक्रवज्राभिहतो महात्मा; चचाल कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇaṁ kupito mahendro; jaghāna vajreṇa śitena vajrī
sa śakravajrābhihato mahātmā; cacāla kopācca bhṛśaṁ nanāda

translations.english: Thereat the great Indra, waxing wroth, smote Kumbhakarna with the whetted levin. And hit at with Sakra's thunder bolt, that high-souled (hero) shook, and in wrath set up roars.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य नानद्यमानस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः
श्रुत्वा निनादं वित्रस्ता भूयो भूमिर्वितत्रसे
verses.transliteration:
tasya nānadyamānasya kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ
śrutvā ninādaṁ vitrastā bhūyo bhūmirvitatrase

translations.english: Hearing the roars of the Raksasa-Kumbhakarna, as he kept crying, creatures, seized with fear, were greatly agitated.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कोपान्महेन्द्रस्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
विकृष्यैरावताद्दन्तं जघानोरसि वासवम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kopānmahendrasya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
vikṛṣyairāvatāddantaṁ jaghānorasi vāsavam

translations.english: Thereat, enraged with the great Indra, the mighty Kumbhakarņa plucking a tusk of Airāvata, hurled it at Vāsava's chest.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णप्रहारार्तो विचचाल स वासवः
ततो विषेदुः सहसा देवब्रह्मर्षिदानवाः
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇaprahārārto vicacāla sa vāsavaḥ
tato viṣeduḥ sahasā devabrahmarṣidānavāḥ

translations.english: With blood overflowing his person, Vāsava looked as if aflame. Thereat, all of a sudden the gods and the Brahmarşis and the Dānavas were dispirited. Then ſakra Then Śakra alongwith alongwith others proceeded to the abode of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रजा यदि त्वेष भक्षयिष्यति नित्यशः
अचिरेणैव कालेन शून्यो लोको भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ prajā yadi tveṣa bhakṣayiṣyati nityaśaḥ
acireṇaiva kālena śūnyo loko bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Then they informed the lord of creatures touching the ravages of Kumbhakarna, and informed the gods about Kumbhakarna's devouring up, destroying asylums and outraging others, wives. If this one devour creatures constantly, in a short space the world would be empty of any.

verses.sanskrit:
वासवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः
रक्षांस्यावाहयामास कुम्भकर्णं ददर्श ह
verses.transliteration:
vāsavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
rakṣāṁsyāvāhayāmāsa kumbhakarṇaṁ dadarśa ha

translations.english: Hearing Vasava's speech, the Great-father of all creatures called up* the Rākṣasas and saw Kumbhakarņa (before him). *By reciting a certain scriptural formula.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णं समीक्ष्यैव वितत्रास प्रजापतिः
दृष्ट्वा निश्वस्य चैवेदं स्वयम्भूरिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇaṁ samīkṣyaiva vitatrāsa prajāpatiḥ
dṛṣṭvā niśvasya caivedaṁ svayambhūridamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing Kumbhkarņa, Prajāpati* was seized with exceeding great fear. And then pacifying Kumbhakarma, the Self-sprung addressed him, saying. *Lit. lord of creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रुवं लोकविनाशाय पौरस्त्येनासि निर्मितः
तस्मात्त्वमद्य प्रभृति मृतकल्पः शयिष्यसि
ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतोऽथ निपपाताग्रतः प्रभोः
verses.transliteration:
dhruvaṁ lokavināśāya paurastyenāsi nirmitaḥ
tasmāttvamadya prabhṛti mṛtakalpaḥ śayiṣyasi
brahmaśāpābhibhūto'tha nipapātāgrataḥ prabhoḥ

translations.english: Forsooth for compassing the destruction of creatures, have you been begot by Paulasta* Therefore from this day forth, you shall lie down as one dead. *ViSravana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः परमसंभ्रान्तो रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
विवृद्धः काञ्चनो वृक्षः फलकाले निकृत्यते
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ paramasaṁbhrānto rāvaṇo vākyamabravīt
vivṛddhaḥ kāñcano vṛkṣaḥ phalakāle nikṛtyate

translations.english: You hew down a golden tree when about to bear fruit. O lord of creatures, you ought not to curse thus your own grandson.

verses.sanskrit:
न नप्तारं स्वकं न्याय्यं शप्तुमेवं प्रजापते
न मिथ्यावचनश्च त्वं स्वप्स्यत्येष न संशयः
कालस्तु क्रियतामस्य शयने जागरे तथा
verses.transliteration:
na naptāraṁ svakaṁ nyāyyaṁ śaptumevaṁ prajāpate
na mithyāvacanaśca tvaṁ svapsyatyeṣa na saṁśayaḥ
kālastu kriyatāmasya śayane jāgare tathā

translations.english: Your words will never go for naught; sleep he will, without doubt. But do you appoint a time for his sleeping and one for his awaking,

verses.sanskrit:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा स्वयम्भूरिदमब्रवीत्
शयिता ह्येष षण्मासानेकाहं जागरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā svayambhūridamabravīt
śayitā hyeṣa ṣaṇmāsānekāhaṁ jāgariṣyati

translations.english: Hearing Rāvana's speech, the Self-sprung said, "having slept for six months, he shall wake for one day.

verses.sanskrit:
एकेनाह्ना त्वसौ वीरश्चरन्भूमिं बुभुक्षितः
व्यात्तास्यो भक्षयेल्लोकान्संक्रुद्ध इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
ekenāhnā tvasau vīraścaranbhūmiṁ bubhukṣitaḥ
vyāttāsyo bhakṣayellokānsaṁkruddha iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: And for a single day, that hero, coming under the influence of hunger, shall range the earth, opening his mouth wide open, and devouring people like a fire that has spread far and wide.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽसौ व्यसनमापन्नः कुम्भकर्णमबोधयत्
त्वत्पराक्रमभीतश्च राजा संप्रति रावणः
verses.transliteration:
so'sau vyasanamāpannaḥ kumbhakarṇamabodhayat
tvatparākramabhītaśca rājā saṁprati rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Now king Rāvaņa struck with terror at your prowess, encompassed with peril, has waked up Kumbhakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
स एष निर्गतो वीरः शिबिराद्भीमविक्रमः
वानरान्भृशसंक्रुद्धो भक्षयन्परिधावति
verses.transliteration:
sa eṣa nirgato vīraḥ śibirādbhīmavikramaḥ
vānarānbhṛśasaṁkruddho bhakṣayanparidhāvati

translations.english: That hero possessed of dreadful prowess, wrought up with high wrath, sallying forth from his camp, rush about, eating up monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णं समीक्ष्यैव हरयो विप्रदुद्रुवुः
कथमेनं रणे क्रुद्धं वारयिष्यन्ति वानराः
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇaṁ samīkṣyaiva harayo vipradudruvuḥ
kathamenaṁ raṇe kruddhaṁ vārayiṣyanti vānarāḥ

translations.english: Soon as the monkeys see Kumbhakarna, they fly away. And How can they resist in battle the enraged Kumbhakarna?

verses.sanskrit:
उच्यन्तां वानराः सर्वे यन्त्रमेतत्समुच्छ्रितम्
इति विज्ञाय हरयो भविष्यन्तीह निर्भयाः
verses.transliteration:
ucyantāṁ vānarāḥ sarve yantrametatsamucchritam
iti vijñāya harayo bhaviṣyantīha nirbhayāḥ

translations.english: Do you tell the monkeys this is an uplifted engine. Thus assured, the monkeys shall take heart.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत्सुमुखोद्गतम्
उवाच राघवो वाक्यं नीलं सेनापतिं तदा
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā hetumatsumukhodgatam
uvāca rāghavo vākyaṁ nīlaṁ senāpatiṁ tadā

translations.english: Hearing Vibhīşaņa's words informed with reason and tending to the good (of the monkeys), Rāghava then addressed general Nila, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छ सैन्यानि सर्वाणि व्यूह्य तिष्ठस्व पावके
द्वाराण्यादाय लङ्कायाश्चर्याश्चाप्यथ संक्रमान्
verses.transliteration:
gaccha sainyāni sarvāṇi vyūhya tiṣṭhasva pāvake
dvārāṇyādāya laṅkāyāścaryāścāpyatha saṁkramān

translations.english: Let you, monkeys, equipped with weapons and holding hill tops in your hands, and furnished with mountain-summits and trees and rocks, stay, occupying the highways and the bridges.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवेण समादिष्टो नीलो हरिचमूपतिः
शशास वानरानीकं यथावत्कपिकुञ्जरः
verses.transliteration:
rāghaveṇa samādiṣṭo nīlo haricamūpatiḥ
śaśāsa vānarānīkaṁ yathāvatkapikuñjaraḥ

translations.english: Thus instructed by Rāghava, that powerful monkey, Nila-general of the forces-accordingly issue I his orders to the monkey-hosts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गवाक्षः शरभो हनुमानङ्गदो नलः
शैलशृङ्गाणि शैलाभा गृहीत्वा द्वारमभ्ययुः
verses.transliteration:
tato gavākṣaḥ śarabho hanumānaṅgado nalaḥ
śailaśṛṅgāṇi śailābhā gṛhītvā dvāramabhyayuḥ

translations.english: Then Gavākṣa and Sarabha and Hanumān and Angada, themselves endowed with the splendour of mountain-summits, taking up mountain-tops, drew towards the gateway.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं; रराज शैलोद्यतवृक्षहस्तम्
गिरेः समीपानुगतं यथैव; महन्महाम्भोधरजालमुग्रम्
verses.transliteration:
tato harīṇāṁ tadanīkamugraṁ; rarāja śailodyatavṛkṣahastam
gireḥ samīpānugataṁ yathaiva; mahanmahāmbhodharajālamugram

translations.english: Then that dreadful army of monkeys, upraising crags and holding trees in their hands, appeared like mighty masses of scowling clouds bordering a mountain.* *This is apt, seeing that Larika was situated on a hill.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु राक्षसशार्दूलो निद्रामदसमाकुलः
राजमार्गं श्रिया जुष्टं ययौ विपुलविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu rākṣasaśārdūlo nidrāmadasamākulaḥ
rājamārgaṁ śriyā juṣṭaṁ yayau vipulavikramaḥ

translations.english: That tiger-like Rakşasa possessed of prowess, (still) under the influence of slumber, strode along the picturesque highway.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां सहस्रैश्च वृतः परमदुर्जयः
गृहेभ्यः पुष्पवर्षेण कार्यमाणस्तदा ययौ
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ sahasraiśca vṛtaḥ paramadurjayaḥ
gṛhebhyaḥ puṣpavarṣeṇa kāryamāṇastadā yayau

translations.english: That exceedingly unconquerable one, surrounded by thousands of Raksasas, went on, showered with blossoms from the houses (standing by).

verses.sanskrit:
स हेमजालविततं भानुभास्वरदर्शनम्
ददर्श विपुलं रम्यं राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa hemajālavitataṁ bhānubhāsvaradarśanam
dadarśa vipulaṁ ramyaṁ rākṣasendraniveśanam

translations.english: Then he saw the grand and graceful residence of the lord of the Räkşasas, having golden networks and sun-bright to behold.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्तदा सूर्य इवाभ्रजालं; प्रविश्य रक्षोऽधिपतेर्निवेशनम्
ददर्श दूरेऽग्रजमासनस्थं; स्वयम्भुवं शक्र इवासनस्थम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tattadā sūrya ivābhrajālaṁ; praviśya rakṣo'dhipaterniveśanam
dadarśa dūre'grajamāsanasthaṁ; svayambhuvaṁ śakra ivāsanastham

translations.english: Entering the mansion of the Raksasa sovereign, like the sun entering into a mass of clouds, he saw his elder brother seated at a distance; even as Sakra sees the Self-sprung seated.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिगम्य गृहं भ्रातुः कक्ष्यामभिविगाह्य च
ददर्शोद्विग्नमासीनं विमाने पुष्पके गुरुम्
verses.transliteration:
so'bhigamya gṛhaṁ bhrātuḥ kakṣyāmabhivigāhya ca
dadarśodvignamāsīnaṁ vimāne puṣpake gurum

translations.english: Arriving at the abode and passing the entrance, he saw his superior anxiously seated on the car, Pusphaka.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णमुपस्थितम्
तूर्णमुत्थाय संहृष्टः संनिकर्षमुपानयत्
verses.transliteration:
atha dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇamupasthitam
tūrṇamutthāya saṁhṛṣṭaḥ saṁnikarṣamupānayat

translations.english: Seeing Kumbhakarņa come, the Ten necked one, exceedingly rejoiced, raised him up and drew him near himself.

verses.sanskrit:
अथासीनस्य पर्यङ्के कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
भ्रातुर्ववन्दे चरणां किं कृत्यमिति चाब्रवीत्
उत्पत्य चैनं मुदितो रावणः परिषस्वजे
verses.transliteration:
athāsīnasya paryaṅke kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
bhrāturvavande caraṇāṁ kiṁ kṛtyamiti cābravīt
utpatya cainaṁ mudito rāvaṇaḥ pariṣasvaje

translations.english: Then the exceedingly mighty Kumbhakarņa saluted the feet of his brother and said, "What did you say?"

verses.sanskrit:
स भ्रात्रा संपरिष्वक्तो यथावच्चाभिनन्दितः
कुम्भकर्णः शुभं दिव्यं प्रतिपेदे वरासनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhrātrā saṁpariṣvakto yathāvaccābhinanditaḥ
kumbhakarṇaḥ śubhaṁ divyaṁ pratipede varāsanam

translations.english: Thereat, delighted, Ravana, springing up, again embraced (his brother). And embraced (by his brother), and duly greeted by him, that brother (of Ravana).

verses.sanskrit:
स तदासनमाश्रित्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
संरक्तनयनः कोपाद्रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tadāsanamāśritya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
saṁraktanayanaḥ kopādrāvaṇaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Kumbhakarņa seated himself on a shining and superb seat. And seating himself on that seat, the wondrous powerful Kumbhakarna, with his eyes reddened in wrath, addressed Ravana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातरं रावणः क्रुद्धं कुम्भकर्णमवस्थितम्
ईषत्तु परिवृत्ताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātaraṁ rāvaṇaḥ kruddhaṁ kumbhakarṇamavasthitam
īṣattu parivṛttābhyāṁ netrābhyāṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य ते सुमहान्कालः शयानस्य महाबल
सुखितस्त्वं न जानीषे मम रामकृतं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
adya te sumahānkālaḥ śayānasya mahābala
sukhitastvaṁ na jānīṣe mama rāmakṛtaṁ bhayam

translations.english: O highly powerful one, you have slept away a long space of time. And having been asleep, you did not know the great fear of mine springing from Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
एष दाशरथी रामः सुग्रीवसहितो बली
समुद्रं सबलस्तीर्त्वा मूलं नः परिकृन्तति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa dāśarathī rāmaḥ sugrīvasahito balī
samudraṁ sabalastīrtvā mūlaṁ naḥ parikṛntati

translations.english: This graceful son to Daśaratha possessed of strength, along with Sugriva, having crossed the ocean, is destroying our race.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्त पश्यस्व लङ्काया वनान्युपवनानि च
सेतुना सुखमागम्य वानरैकार्णवं कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
hanta paśyasva laṅkāyā vanānyupavanāni ca
setunā sukhamāgamya vānaraikārṇavaṁ kṛtam

translations.english: Alack! see in own Lanka, woods and forests have been flooded with an ocean of monkeys never even coming without any ado by the bridge (which they have constructed).

verses.sanskrit:
ये राक्षसा मुख्यतमा हतास्ते वानरैर्युधि
वानराणां क्षयं युद्धे न पश्यामि कदाचन
verses.transliteration:
ye rākṣasā mukhyatamā hatāste vānarairyudhi
vānarāṇāṁ kṣayaṁ yuddhe na paśyāmi kadācana

translations.english: Those Rākşasas that were prime have been slain in battle by the monkeys; but I find no destruction of the monkeys in fight. Nay, the monkeys have been before vanquished (by the Raksasas) in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वक्षपितकोशं च स त्वमभ्यवपद्य माम्
त्रायस्वेमां पुरीं लङ्कां बालवृद्धावशेषिताम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvakṣapitakośaṁ ca sa tvamabhyavapadya mām
trāyasvemāṁ purīṁ laṅkāṁ bālavṛddhāvaśeṣitām

translations.english: Do you, favouring me, whose exchequer is empty, save this city of Lanka, having only young folks and the aged left.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातुरर्थे महाबाहो कुरु कर्म सुदुष्करम्
मयैवं नोक्तपूर्वो हि कश्चिद्भ्रातः परंतप
त्वय्यस्ति मम च स्नेहः परा संभावना च मे
verses.transliteration:
bhrāturarthe mahābāho kuru karma suduṣkaram
mayaivaṁ noktapūrvo hi kaścidbhrātaḥ paraṁtapa
tvayyasti mama ca snehaḥ parā saṁbhāvanā ca me

translations.english: O long-armed one, do you perform your dearest acts in behalf of your brother. O subduer of enemies, I had never before said so to my brother.

verses.sanskrit:
देवासुरविमर्देषु बहुशो राक्षसर्षभ
त्वया देवाः प्रतिव्यूह्य निर्जिताश्चासुरा युधि
न हि ते सर्वभूतेषु दृश्यते सदृशो बली
verses.transliteration:
devāsuravimardeṣu bahuśo rākṣasarṣabha
tvayā devāḥ prativyūhya nirjitāścāsurā yudhi
na hi te sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyate sadṛśo balī

translations.english: In you is my affection and great is the probability of your succeeding. In the wars of the celestials and Asuras, O foremost of Rāks asas, countless were the celestials that you as an antagonist had beaten.

verses.sanskrit:
कुरुष्व मे प्रियहितमेतदुत्तमं; यथाप्रियं प्रियरणबान्धवप्रिय
स्वतेजसा विधम सपत्नवाहिनीं; शरद्घनं पवन इवोद्यतो महान्
verses.transliteration:
kuruṣva me priyahitametaduttamaṁ; yathāpriyaṁ priyaraṇabāndhavapriya
svatejasā vidhama sapatnavāhinīṁ; śaradghanaṁ pavana ivodyato mahān

translations.english: O lover of battle! O dear to friends, as you like, do this beloved good office, this prime benefit, to me. By your own energy, smite the hostile hosts, even as a mighty and strong wind (scattered away) autumnal clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य निशम्य परिदेवितम्
कुम्भकर्णो बभाषेऽथ वचनं प्रजहास च
verses.transliteration:
tasya rākṣasarājasya niśamya paridevitam
kumbhakarṇo babhāṣe'tha vacanaṁ prajahāsa ca

translations.english: Hearing the lament of the king of Rākşasas, Kumbhakarma, laughing said.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टो दोषो हि योऽस्माभिः पुरा मन्त्रविनिर्णये
हितेष्वनभियुक्तेन सोऽयमासादितस्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭo doṣo hi yo'smābhiḥ purā mantravinirṇaye
hiteṣvanabhiyuktena so'yamāsāditastvayā

translations.english: That evil which on the occasion of the conclave we had seen, has befallen you, who have passed by what was fraught with your good.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रं खल्वभ्युपेतं त्वां फलं पापस्य कर्मणः
निरयेष्वेव पतनं यथा दुष्कृतकर्मणः
verses.transliteration:
śīghraṁ khalvabhyupetaṁ tvāṁ phalaṁ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
nirayeṣveva patanaṁ yathā duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Even as a sinner reaps perdition, verily has the fruit of your unrighteous act found you.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रथमं वै महाराज कृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम्
केवलं वीर्यदर्पेण नानुबन्धो विचारितः
verses.transliteration:
prathamaṁ vai mahārāja kṛtyametadacintitam
kevalaṁ vīryadarpeṇa nānubandho vicāritaḥ

translations.english: At first, O mighty king, you did not ponder over this course of conduct; nor, from pride of prowess, did you at all take note of the evil thereof.

verses.sanskrit:
यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः
पूर्वं चोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ paścātpūrvakāryāṇi kuryādaiśvaryamāsthitaḥ
pūrvaṁ cottarakāryāṇi na sa veda nayānayau

translations.english: He that dose last what should be done first, and what should be done last, is ignorant of what is prudence and what not.

verses.sanskrit:
देशकालविहीनानि कर्माणि विपरीतवत्
क्रियमाणानि दुष्यन्ति हवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव
verses.transliteration:
deśakālavihīnāni karmāṇi viparītavat
kriyamāṇāni duṣyanti havīṁṣyaprayateṣviva

translations.english: Acts not performed in harmony with season and place, like to acts performed counter to season and place, are the occasions of misery, and resemble clarified butter poured into fire that has not been sanctified.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणां पञ्चधा योगं कर्मणां यः प्रपश्यति
सचिवैः समयं कृत्वा स सभ्ये वर्तते पथि
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇāṁ pañcadhā yogaṁ karmaṇāṁ yaḥ prapaśyati
sacivaiḥ samayaṁ kṛtvā sa sabhye vartate pathi

translations.english: He stay well in the path that, in consultation with his counsellors, ascertain the five way touching the three kinds of action* *The five ways are (1) the mans of commencing an act (2) person, thing and wealth, (3) division of season and place, (4) providing agains mischance (5) success. The three kinds of action are treaty, war, etc. All this is nebulous; And the commentator is sadly reticent over this extremely important passage.

verses.sanskrit:
यथागमं च यो राजा समयं विचिकीर्षति
बुध्यते सचिवान्बुद्ध्या सुहृदश्चानुपश्यति
verses.transliteration:
yathāgamaṁ ca yo rājā samayaṁ vicikīrṣati
budhyate sacivānbuddhyā suhṛdaścānupaśyati

translations.english: The king that aided by his own intelligence as well as his counsellors act after reflection in consonance with the science of polity, that distinguish his friends from his foes), and, O lord of the Raksasas, that seasonably' pursue righteousness, or profit, or desire, or any two, or all these combined-truly has understanding.? 1. Religion is to be sought in the morning, profit in the afternoon, and desire at nigh, so the commentator. 2. One is at sea in the midst of these formless generalities. The tantalized intellect makes a desperate attempt to grasp the body of the shadow seeming substance, but the empty air mocks his pains. A translator, however, is fast bound to the oar and must pull on, will be, nil he.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिषु चैतेषु यच्छ्रेष्ठं श्रुत्वा तन्नावबुध्यते
राजा वा राजमात्रो वा व्यर्थं तस्य बहुश्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
triṣu caiteṣu yacchreṣṭhaṁ śrutvā tannāvabudhyate
rājā vā rājamātro vā vyarthaṁ tasya bahuśrutam

translations.english: But the king or the heir apparent, that, having heard what is prime among the three, does not understand, has his time in vain on his erudition.

verses.sanskrit:
काले धर्मार्थकामान्यः संमन्त्र्य सचिवैः सह
निषेवेतात्मवाँल्लोके न स व्यसनमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
kāle dharmārthakāmānyaḥ saṁmantrya sacivaiḥ saha
niṣevetātmavā̐lloke na sa vyasanamāpnuyāt

translations.english: He that controlling his own self, consult with his counsellors seasonably touching gift, forbearance, difference and prowess, as well as virtue, profit and desire-does not in this world come by calamity.

verses.sanskrit:
हितानुबन्धमालोक्य कार्याकार्यमिहात्मनः
राजा सहार्थतत्त्वज्ञैः सचिवैः सह जीवति
verses.transliteration:
hitānubandhamālokya kāryākāryamihātmanaḥ
rājā sahārthatattvajñaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha jīvati

translations.english: Perceiving the fair fruit (of a line of action) accruing to him here, a king should act in consultation with counsellors endowed with intelligence and versed in the import of things.

verses.sanskrit:
अनभिज्ञाय शास्त्रार्थान्पुरुषाः पशुबुद्धयः
प्रागल्भ्याद्वक्तुमिच्छन्ति मन्त्रेष्वभ्यन्तरीकृताः
verses.transliteration:
anabhijñāya śāstrārthānpuruṣāḥ paśubuddhayaḥ
prāgalbhyādvaktumicchanti mantreṣvabhyantarīkṛtāḥ

translations.english: Not understanding the sense of the scriptures, persons possessed of beastly intelligence, entering into the heart of their counsellors, are inspired with a desire of speaking out of sheer volubility.

verses.sanskrit:
अशास्त्रविदुषां तेषां न कार्यमहितं वचः
अर्थशास्त्रानभिज्ञानां विपुलां श्रियमिच्छताम्
verses.transliteration:
aśāstraviduṣāṁ teṣāṁ na kāryamahitaṁ vacaḥ
arthaśāstrānabhijñānāṁ vipulāṁ śriyamicchatām

translations.english: Albeit uttered heedfully, the speech of those that are ignorant of learning and the knowledge of the sense of things, and who are intent upon attaining abounding affluence, should not be acted upon.

verses.sanskrit:
अहितं च हिताकारं धार्ष्ट्याज्जल्पन्ति ये नराः
अवेक्ष्य मन्त्रबाह्यास्ते कर्तव्याः कृत्यदूषणाः
verses.transliteration:
ahitaṁ ca hitākāraṁ dhārṣṭyājjalpanti ye narāḥ
avekṣya mantrabāhyāste kartavyāḥ kṛtyadūṣaṇāḥ

translations.english: Those-spoilers of business-who from recklessness talk of pernicious as if profitableshould certainly be rejected as counsellors.

verses.sanskrit:
विनाशयन्तो भर्तारं सहिताः शत्रुभिर्बुधैः
विपरीतानि कृत्यानि कारयन्तीह मन्त्रिणः
verses.transliteration:
vināśayanto bhartāraṁ sahitāḥ śatrubhirbudhaiḥ
viparītāni kṛtyāni kārayantīha mantriṇaḥ

translations.english: Some counsellors-destroyers of their mastersjoining intelligent enemies (of their lords), act in a way opposed to their interests in this world.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्भर्ता मित्रसंकाशानमित्रान्मन्त्रनिर्णये
व्यवहारेण जानीयात्सचिवानुपसंहितान्
verses.transliteration:
tānbhartā mitrasaṁkāśānamitrānmantranirṇaye
vyavahāreṇa jānīyātsacivānupasaṁhitān

translations.english: Their lords, at the hour of consultation, by their behaviour should know these counsellorsenemies in the guise of friends-who have been won over (by the opposite party).

verses.sanskrit:
चपलस्येह कृत्यानि सहसानुप्रधावतः
छिद्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य खमिव द्विजाः
verses.transliteration:
capalasyeha kṛtyāni sahasānupradhāvataḥ
chidramanye prapadyante krauñcasya khamiva dvijāḥ

translations.english: Even as the fowls of the air enter the hole in the Krauñca, enemies find and easy entrance into the short comings of him that is fickle and that rush into act without heed.

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि शत्रुमवज्ञाय नात्मानमभिरक्षति
अवाप्नोति हि सोऽनर्थान्स्थानाच्च व्यवरोप्यते
verses.transliteration:
yo hi śatrumavajñāya nātmānamabhirakṣati
avāpnoti hi so'narthānsthānācca vyavaropyate

translations.english: He that disregarding his foe, omits to guard himself, come by disasters and lose his place.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तु श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णस्य भाषितम्
भ्रुकुटिं चैव संचक्रे क्रुद्धश्चैनमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tattu śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇasya bhāṣitam
bhrukuṭiṁ caiva saṁcakre kruddhaścainamuvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing Kumbhakarma's words, the Tennecked one knit up his brows, and, wrought up with wrath, said to him.

verses.sanskrit:
मान्यो गुरुरिवाचार्यः किं मां त्वमनुशासति
किमेवं वाक्श्रमं कृत्वा काले युक्तं विधीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
mānyo gururivācāryaḥ kiṁ māṁ tvamanuśāsati
kimevaṁ vākśramaṁ kṛtvā kāle yuktaṁ vidhīyatām

translations.english: I am worthy of being honoured by you, like your superior. What needs this verbal travail? Do you what is fit.

verses.sanskrit:
विभ्रमाच्चित्तमोहाद्वा बलवीर्याश्रयेण वा
नाभिपन्नमिदानीं यद्व्यर्थास्तस्य पुनः कृथाः
verses.transliteration:
vibhramāccittamohādvā balavīryāśrayeṇa vā
nābhipannamidānīṁ yadvyarthāstasya punaḥ kṛthāḥ

translations.english: Vain is the mention now of what I did either through stupor or delusion or pride of prowess. Now bethink you of what is proper.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मिन्काले तु यद्युक्तं तदिदानीं विधीयताम्
ममापनयजं दोषं विक्रमेण समीकुरु
verses.transliteration:
asminkāle tu yadyuktaṁ tadidānīṁ vidhīyatām
mamāpanayajaṁ doṣaṁ vikrameṇa samīkuru

translations.english: Do you through your prowess assuage the sorrow of mine springing from my impolitic conduct, if you cherish any feeling for me, if your strength stay and if you deem this business of mine as by far more momentous to you.

verses.sanskrit:
स सुहृद्यो विपन्नार्थं दीनमभ्यवपद्यते
स बन्धुर्योऽपनीतेषु साहाय्यायोपकल्पते
verses.transliteration:
sa suhṛdyo vipannārthaṁ dīnamabhyavapadyate
sa bandhuryo'panīteṣu sāhāyyāyopakalpate

translations.english: He is a friend that succour one fallen in distress and is undergoing affliction; and he acts friendly that helped a person lapsing from the path of morality.

verses.sanskrit:
अतीव हि समालक्ष्य भ्रातरं क्षुभितेन्द्रियम्
कुम्भकर्णः शनैर्वाक्यं बभाषे परिसान्त्वयन्
verses.transliteration:
atīva hi samālakṣya bhrātaraṁ kṣubhitendriyam
kumbhakarṇaḥ śanairvākyaṁ babhāṣe parisāntvayan

translations.english: As he was speaking thus in words sedate yet severe, Kumbhakarma, concluding that Ravana was undelighted, makes his remarks mildly. And seeing his brother extremely sorry, Kumbhakarņa, pacifying him, gently said.

verses.sanskrit:
अलं राक्षसराजेन्द्र संतापमुपपद्य ते
रोषं च संपरित्यज्य स्वस्थो भवितुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
alaṁ rākṣasarājendra saṁtāpamupapadya te
roṣaṁ ca saṁparityajya svastho bhavitumarhasi

translations.english: O king, intently hear my words. O repressor of foes! O lord of Raksasas, banish this sorrow, and casting away your wrath, return you to nature.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतन्मनसि कर्तव्व्यं मयि जीवति पार्थिव
तमहं नाशयिष्यामि यत्कृते परितप्यसे
verses.transliteration:
naitanmanasi kartavvyaṁ mayi jīvati pārthiva
tamahaṁ nāśayiṣyāmi yatkṛte paritapyase

translations.english: O king, so long as I live, you must not suffer your heart to fare thus. Him will I slay for whom you grieve.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं तु हितं वाच्यं सर्वावस्थं मया तव
बन्धुभावादभिहितं भ्रातृस्नेहाच्च पार्थिव
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ tu hitaṁ vācyaṁ sarvāvasthaṁ mayā tava
bandhubhāvādabhihitaṁ bhrātṛsnehācca pārthiva

translations.english: But whatever condition you may be in, I must tell what is for your welfare; and therefore from sentiment of friendship as well as from fraternal affection I have spoken thus to you o King.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं यत्तु कालेऽस्मिन्कर्तुं स्निग्धेन बन्धुना
शत्रूणां कदनं पश्य क्रियमाणं मया रणे
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṁ yattu kāle'sminkartuṁ snigdhena bandhunā
śatrūṇāṁ kadanaṁ paśya kriyamāṇaṁ mayā raṇe

translations.english: What a friend from affection should do at a time like this, I shall do the same. See the havoc I spread among the foes in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य पश्य महाबाहो मया समरमूर्धनि
हते रामे सह भ्रात्रा द्रवन्तीं हरिवाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
adya paśya mahābāho mayā samaramūrdhani
hate rāme saha bhrātrā dravantīṁ harivāhinīm

translations.english: O long-armed one, behold, on Rāma having been slain by me on the edge of battle along with his brother, the monkey-army in headlong flight.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य रामस्य तद्दृष्ट्वा मयानीतं रणाच्छिरः
सुखीभव महाबाहो सीता भवतु दुःखिता
verses.transliteration:
adya rāmasya taddṛṣṭvā mayānītaṁ raṇācchiraḥ
sukhībhava mahābāho sītā bhavatu duḥkhitā

translations.english: And today seeing Rāma's head brought by me from the field, be you, O long-armed one, happy; and let Sitā be overwhelmed with woe.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य रामस्य पश्यन्तु निधनं सुमहत्प्रियम्
लङ्कायां राक्षसाः सर्वे ये ते निहतबान्धवाः
verses.transliteration:
adya rāmasya paśyantu nidhanaṁ sumahatpriyam
laṅkāyāṁ rākṣasāḥ sarve ye te nihatabāndhavāḥ

translations.english: And let those Raksasas in Lankā who have had their kindred slain (in battle), see that dear sight-Rāma slain (in fight).

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य शोकपरीतानां स्वबन्धुवधकारणात्
शत्रोर्युधि विनाशेन करोम्यस्रप्रमार्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
adya śokaparītānāṁ svabandhuvadhakāraṇāt
śatroryudhi vināśena karomyasrapramārjanam

translations.english: Today shall I slaying the enemies in battle, wipe the tears of those who mourn their friend slain and are overwhelmed with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य पर्वतसंकाशं ससूर्यमिव तोयदम्
विकीर्णं पश्य समरे सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration:
adya parvatasaṁkāśaṁ sasūryamiva toyadam
vikīrṇaṁ paśya samare sugrīvaṁ plavageśvaram

translations.english: To-day behold the lord of monkeys-Sugrivaresembling a mountain or a mass of clouds lighted up by (the living) sun, lying stretched on the field.

verses.sanskrit:
न परः प्रेषणीयस्ते युद्धायातुल विक्रम
अहमुत्सादयिष्यामि शत्रूंस्तव महाबल
verses.transliteration:
na paraḥ preṣaṇīyaste yuddhāyātula vikrama
ahamutsādayiṣyāmi śatrūṁstava mahābala

translations.english: O repressor of foes, do you now command me O you of unparalleled prowess, you need not yourself face the foe in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि शक्रो यदि यमो यदि पावकमारुतौ
तानहं योधयिष्यामि कुबेर वरुणावपि
verses.transliteration:
yadi śakro yadi yamo yadi pāvakamārutau
tānahaṁ yodhayiṣyāmi kubera varuṇāvapi

translations.english: I shall abolish your foes endowed with redoubted might. If even Śakra himself, and Yama, and the god of Fire, and the god of Wind, and Kubera, and Varuņa-shall range themselves against me, them shall I encounter in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
गिरिमात्रशरीरस्य शितशूलधरस्य मे
नर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य बिभीयाच्च पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
girimātraśarīrasya śitaśūladharasya me
nardatastīkṣṇadaṁṣṭrasya bibhīyācca puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: Purandara himself is seized with fright at sight of me, having a body measuring a mountain, equipped with sharpened spears, furnished with sharp teeth, and setting up shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा त्यक्तशस्त्रस्य मृद्गतस्तरसा रिपून्
न मे प्रतिमुखे कश्चिच्छक्तः स्थातुं जिजीविषुः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā tyaktaśastrasya mṛdgatastarasā ripūn
na me pratimukhe kaścicchaktaḥ sthātuṁ jijīviṣuḥ

translations.english: And who wishing to save himself shall be able to stay before me as I casting away my weapons keep pounding my enemies with celerity?

verses.sanskrit:
नैव शक्त्या न गदया नासिना न शितैः शरैः
हस्ताभ्यामेव संरब्धो हनिष्याम्यपि वज्रिणम्
verses.transliteration:
naiva śaktyā na gadayā nāsinā na śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
hastābhyāmeva saṁrabdho haniṣyāmyapi vajriṇam

translations.english: No need of the dart, or the mace, or the sword, or whetted arrows. I shall with my bare arms alone slay (Rāma) along with the thunderer himself.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि मे मुष्टिवेगं स राघवोऽद्य सहिष्यति
ततः पास्यन्ति बाणौघा रुधिरं राघवस्य ते
verses.transliteration:
yadi me muṣṭivegaṁ sa rāghavo'dya sahiṣyati
tataḥ pāsyanti bāṇaughā rudhiraṁ rāghavasya te

translations.english: If Raghava bear the impetus of my blows, the shall the vollies of my shafts drink his life blood.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तया बाध्यसे राजन्किमर्थं मयि तिष्ठति
सोऽहं शत्रुविनाशाय तव निर्यातुमुद्यतः
verses.transliteration:
cintayā bādhyase rājankimarthaṁ mayi tiṣṭhati
so'haṁ śatruvināśāya tava niryātumudyataḥ

translations.english: Why, O king, while I remain, did you burn in anxiety. And I am ready to sally out for compassing the destruction of your enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
मुञ्च रामाद्भयं राजन्हनिष्यामीह संयुगे
राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं च महाबलम्
असाधारणमिच्छामि तव दातुं महद्यशः
verses.transliteration:
muñca rāmādbhayaṁ rājanhaniṣyāmīha saṁyuge
rāghavaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ caiva sugrīvaṁ ca mahābalam
asādhāraṇamicchāmi tava dātuṁ mahadyaśaḥ

translations.english: Cast off all terror of Rāma. I shall slay in battle Rāghava and Lakşmaņa and the exceedingly powerful Sugrīva and the Räksasadestroying Hanumān, who made Lankā blaze. I shall cat up the monkeys present in the encounter. And signal is the celebrity that I shall confer on you.

verses.sanskrit:
वधेन ते दाशरथेः सुखावहं; सुखं समाहर्तुमहं व्रजामि
निहत्य रामं सहलक्ष्मणेन; खादामि सर्वान्हरियूथमुख्यान्
verses.transliteration:
vadhena te dāśaratheḥ sukhāvahaṁ; sukhaṁ samāhartumahaṁ vrajāmi
nihatya rāmaṁ sahalakṣmaṇena; khādāmi sarvānhariyūthamukhyān

translations.english: I go for securing felicity us huring in pleasures plenteous flowing from the destruction of Dasaratha's son. And slaying Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, I shall eat up all the foremost of monkey-bands.

verses.sanskrit:
रमस्व कामं पिब चाग्र्यवारुणीं; कुरुष्व कृत्यानि विनीयतां ज्वरः
मयाद्य रामे गमिते यमक्षयं; चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ramasva kāmaṁ piba cāgryavāruṇīṁ; kuruṣva kṛtyāni vinīyatāṁ jvaraḥ
mayādya rāme gamite yamakṣayaṁ; cirāya sītā vaśagā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Make merry, my king; today drink Varuni. Enjoy pleasures, banishing sorrow. And today on my having despatched Rāma to the mansion of Yama, Sītā shall come under your control for good.

verses.sanskrit:
तदुक्तमतिकायस्य बलिनो बाहुशालिनः
कुम्भकर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वोवाच महोदरः
verses.transliteration:
taduktamatikāyasya balino bāhuśālinaḥ
kumbhakarṇasya vacanaṁ śrutvovāca mahodaraḥ

translations.english: Hearing the speech of the huge-bodied, longarmed and mighty Kumbhkarma, Mahodara said.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णकुले जातो धृष्टः प्राकृतदर्शनः
अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषि कृत्यं सर्वत्र वेदितुम्
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇakule jāto dhṛṣṭaḥ prākṛtadarśanaḥ
avalipto na śaknoṣi kṛtyaṁ sarvatra veditum

translations.english: O Kumbhakarņa, although sprung in a noble line, you are wondrous haughty and of a vulgar form; and you are not everywhere competent to discern your course.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि राजा न जानीते कुम्भकर्ण नयानयौ
त्वं तु कैशोरकाद्धृष्टः केवलं वक्तुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
na hi rājā na jānīte kumbhakarṇa nayānayau
tvaṁ tu kaiśorakāddhṛṣṭaḥ kevalaṁ vaktumicchasi

translations.english: It certainly cannot well be that the king cannot distinguish between proper and improper; but you has from your youth upwards been insolent; and your joy is in talking perenially.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थानं वृद्धिं च हानिं च देशकालविभागवित्
आत्मनश्च परेषां च बुध्यते राक्षसर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
sthānaṁ vṛddhiṁ ca hāniṁ ca deśakālavibhāgavit
ātmanaśca pareṣāṁ ca budhyate rākṣasarṣabha

translations.english: But the foremost of the Raksasa is versed in place and increase and injury, and know the duties touching season and place, and how to advance his own party and lower that of the foe.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तु शक्यं बलवता कर्तुं प्राकृतबुद्धिना
अनुपासितवृद्धेन कः कुर्यात्तादृशं बुधः
verses.transliteration:
yattu śakyaṁ balavatā kartuṁ prākṛtabuddhinā
anupāsitavṛddhena kaḥ kuryāttādṛśaṁ budhaḥ

translations.english: But what person ever act according to what is proposed feebly by one having strength, yet of inferior intelligence, and who has never respected the aged.

verses.sanskrit:
यांस्तु धर्मार्थकामांस्त्वं ब्रवीषि पृथगाश्रयान्
अनुबोद्धुं स्वभावेन न हि लक्षणमस्ति ते
verses.transliteration:
yāṁstu dharmārthakāmāṁstvaṁ bravīṣi pṛthagāśrayān
anuboddhuṁ svabhāvena na hi lakṣaṇamasti te

translations.english: You are not naturally competent to understand what you yourself says touching the opposed virtue, profit and desire.

verses.sanskrit:
एकस्यैवाभियाने तु हेतुर्यः प्रकृतस्त्वया
तत्राप्यनुपपन्नं ते वक्ष्यामि यदसाधु च
verses.transliteration:
ekasyaivābhiyāne tu heturyaḥ prakṛtastvayā
tatrāpyanupapannaṁ te vakṣyāmi yadasādhu ca

translations.english: Did you show the reasons for your taking the field alone? But I shall point you out what is improper and unreasonable in this (proposed) course.

verses.sanskrit:
येन पूर्वं जनस्थाने बहवोऽतिबला हताः
राक्षसा राघवं तं त्वं कथमेको जयिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
yena pūrvaṁ janasthāne bahavo'tibalā hatāḥ
rākṣasā rāghavaṁ taṁ tvaṁ kathameko jayiṣyasi

translations.english: How shall you alone vanquish that Rāghava who formerly routed in Jansthāna innumerable Rākşasas possessed of exceeding strength?

verses.sanskrit:
ये पुरा निर्जितास्तेन जनस्थाने महौजसः
राक्षसांस्तान्पुरे सर्वान्भीतानद्यापि पश्यसि
verses.transliteration:
ye purā nirjitāstena janasthāne mahaujasaḥ
rākṣasāṁstānpure sarvānbhītānadyāpi paśyasi

translations.english: Did you not today in the palace behold those powerful Rākşasas that had been beaten in Janasthana-cowed down in fear?

verses.sanskrit:
तं सिंहमिव संक्रुद्धं रामं दशरथात्मजम्
सर्पं सुप्तमिवाबुद्ध्या प्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
taṁ siṁhamiva saṁkruddhaṁ rāmaṁ daśarathātmajam
sarpaṁ suptamivābuddhyā prabodhayitumicchasi

translations.english: Alas! you wished to awake Rima, son to Daśaratha-knowing full well that le resembles an enraged lion or a sleeping serpeni.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्वलन्तं तेजसा नित्यं क्रोधेन च दुरासदम्
कस्तं मृत्युमिवासह्यमासादयितुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
jvalantaṁ tejasā nityaṁ krodhena ca durāsadam
kastaṁ mṛtyumivāsahyamāsādayitumarhati

translations.english: But whom does it behove to confront him ever flaming in energy, difficult of being approached when enraged, and unbearable even like Death himself?

verses.sanskrit:
संशयस्थमिदं सर्वं शत्रोः प्रतिसमासने
एकस्य गमनं तत्र न हि मे रोचते तव
verses.transliteration:
saṁśayasthamidaṁ sarvaṁ śatroḥ pratisamāsane
ekasya gamanaṁ tatra na hi me rocate tava

translations.english: On approaching the foe, this whole host itself shall be imperilled: and therefore, my child, your marching alone does nowise recommend itself to me.

verses.sanskrit:
हीनार्थस्तु समृद्धार्थं को रिपुं प्राकृतो यथा
निश्चितं जीवितत्यागे वशमानेतुमिच्छति
verses.transliteration:
hīnārthastu samṛddhārthaṁ ko ripuṁ prākṛto yathā
niścitaṁ jīvitatyāge vaśamānetumicchati

translations.english: Who is there that, albeit weak bent on renouncing his life, wish to bring under subjection a foe that is powerful, as if he would act with reference to one that is inferior?

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य नास्ति मनुष्येषु सदृशो राक्षसोत्तम
कथमाशंससे योद्धुं तुल्येनेन्द्रविवस्वतोः
verses.transliteration:
yasya nāsti manuṣyeṣu sadṛśo rākṣasottama
kathamāśaṁsase yoddhuṁ tulyenendravivasvatoḥ

translations.english: O foremost of Rākasas, why did you wish to fight with him whose peer there is none among men, and who is equal to Indra and Vavasvata himself?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु संरब्धं कुम्भकर्णं महोदरः
उवाच रक्षसां मध्ये रावणो लोकरावणम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu saṁrabdhaṁ kumbhakarṇaṁ mahodaraḥ
uvāca rakṣasāṁ madhye rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇam

translations.english: Having said this to Kumbhakarņa wrought up with wrath, Mahodara addressed that destroyer of creature-Ravana-in the midst of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
लब्ध्वा पुनस्तां वैदेहीं किमर्थं त्वं प्रजल्पसि
यदेच्छसि तदा सीता वशगा ते भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
labdhvā punastāṁ vaidehīṁ kimarthaṁ tvaṁ prajalpasi
yadecchasi tadā sītā vaśagā te bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Having already obtained Vaidehi, why did you delay? If you wish it, Sītā shall come under your control.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टः कश्चिदुपायो मे सीतोपस्थानकारकः
रुचितश्चेत्स्वया बुद्ध्या राक्षसेश्वर तं शृणु
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭaḥ kaścidupāyo me sītopasthānakārakaḥ
rucitaścetsvayā buddhyā rākṣaseśvara taṁ śṛṇu

translations.english: I have perceived a way as to how Sītā may smile upon you. Do you listen: and should it please you; act you accordingly.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं द्विजिह्वः संह्रादी कुम्भकर्णो वितर्दनः
पञ्चरामवधायैते निर्यान्तीत्यवघोषय
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ dvijihvaḥ saṁhrādī kumbhakarṇo vitardanaḥ
pañcarāmavadhāyaite niryāntītyavaghoṣaya

translations.english: Do you proclaim it about that I and Dvijihva and Samhrādī, and Kumbhakarņa and Vitardanathese five-are marching for compassing the destruction of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गत्वा वयं युद्धं दास्यामस्तस्य यत्नतः
जेष्यामो यदि ते शत्रून्नोपायैः कृत्यमस्ति नः
verses.transliteration:
tato gatvā vayaṁ yuddhaṁ dāsyāmastasya yatnataḥ
jeṣyāmo yadi te śatrūnnopāyaiḥ kṛtyamasti naḥ

translations.english: We, marching out, shall battle with Rāma, putting forth our uttermost. And if we succeed in securing victory, no expedient need we resort to (or bringing Sītā round).

verses.sanskrit:
अथ जीवति नः शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसंयुगाः
ततः समभिपत्स्यामो मनसा यत्समीक्षितुम्
verses.transliteration:
atha jīvati naḥ śatrurvayaṁ ca kṛtasaṁyugāḥ
tataḥ samabhipatsyāmo manasā yatsamīkṣitum

translations.english: But if our foe live after fight and we also having faught the fight, then shall we do what I conceive in my mind.

verses.sanskrit:
वयं युद्धादिहैष्यामो रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः
विदार्य स्वतनुं बाणै रामनामाङ्कितैः शितैः
verses.transliteration:
vayaṁ yuddhādihaiṣyāmo rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ
vidārya svatanuṁ bāṇai rāmanāmāṅkitaiḥ śitaiḥ

translations.english: We shall come hither from the field, bathed in blood, and having our bodies cleft with arrows marked with the name of Rama. And we shall give out that both Ráma and Lakşmaņa have been eaten up by us And then we Shall hold your feet, saying, 'Do you gratify us'.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽवघोषय पुरे गजस्कन्धेन पार्थिव
हतो रामः सह भ्रात्रा ससैन्य इति सर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
tato'vaghoṣaya pure gajaskandhena pārthiva
hato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā sasainya iti sarvataḥ

translations.english: Then, O king, do you through Gajaskandha publish it all round that Ráma has been slain along with his brother and the army.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रीतो नाम ततो भूत्वा भृत्यानां त्वमरिंदम
भोगांश्च परिवारांश्च कामांश्च वसुदापय
verses.transliteration:
prīto nāma tato bhūtvā bhṛtyānāṁ tvamariṁdama
bhogāṁśca parivārāṁśca kāmāṁśca vasudāpaya

translations.english: O repressor of foes, (pretending to be) well pleased, do you dispense-viands, and servants, and objects of enjoyments, and wealth to your retainers; and to the many heroes and warriors distribute wreaths and attires and unguents. And do you (Simulating) delight drink.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽस्मिन्बहुलीभूते कौलीने सर्वतो गते
प्रविश्याश्वास्य चापि त्वं सीतां रहसि सान्त्वय
धनधान्यैश्च कामैश्च रत्नैश्चैनां प्रलोभय
verses.transliteration:
tato'sminbahulībhūte kaulīne sarvato gate
praviśyāśvāsya cāpi tvaṁ sītāṁ rahasi sāntvaya
dhanadhānyaiśca kāmaiśca ratnaiścaināṁ pralobhaya

translations.english: On this report-name that Rāma has been eaten up by the Rākşasas along with his friends, having spread round and round entering (the Asoka wood), and soothing and pacifying Sītā in solitude, Allure her with corn and riches and gems.

verses.sanskrit:
अनयोपधया राजन्भयशोकानुबन्धया
अकामा त्वद्वशं सीता नष्टनाथा गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
anayopadhayā rājanbhayaśokānubandhayā
akāmā tvadvaśaṁ sītā naṣṭanāthā gamiṣyati

translations.english: By this deceit, О king, working powerfully through Sītā's sorrow, she albeit unwilling, shall, having lost her lord, come under your control.

verses.sanskrit:
रञ्जनीयं हि भर्तारं विनष्टमवगम्य सा
नैराश्यात्स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्च त्वद्वशं प्रतिपत्स्यते
verses.transliteration:
rañjanīyaṁ hi bhartāraṁ vinaṣṭamavagamya sā
nairāśyātstrīlaghutvācca tvadvaśaṁ pratipatsyate

translations.english: Losing her charming husband, she from despair and female railty, shall come under your away.

verses.sanskrit:
सा पुरा सुखसंवृद्धा सुखार्हा दुःखकर्षिता
त्वय्यधीनः सुखं ज्ञात्वा सर्वथोपगमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sā purā sukhasaṁvṛddhā sukhārhā duḥkhakarṣitā
tvayyadhīnaḥ sukhaṁ jñātvā sarvathopagamiṣyati

translations.english: Having formerly been brought up in happiness, she, although worthy of felicity, (ultimately) had come by misfortune. And now finding happiness to be in your custody, she shall unreservedly come over to you.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्सुनीतं मम दर्शनेन; रामं हि दृष्ट्वैव भवेदनर्थः
इहैव ते सेत्स्यति मोत्सुको भू;र्महानयुद्धेन सुखस्य लाभः
verses.transliteration:
etatsunītaṁ mama darśanena; rāmaṁ hi dṛṣṭvaiva bhavedanarthaḥ
ihaiva te setsyati motsuko bhū;rmahānayuddhena sukhasya lābhaḥ

translations.english: In my opinion this is the proper course to follow. As soon as you see Rāma, evil shall befall you. Remain here. Do not wish (to go to the field). By refraining from fight, you shall acquire great good.

verses.sanskrit:
अनष्टसैन्यो ह्यनवाप्तसंशयो; रिपूनयुद्धेन जयञ्जनाधिप
यशश्च पुण्यं च महन्महीपते; श्रियं च कीर्तिं च चिरं समश्नुते
verses.transliteration:
anaṣṭasainyo hyanavāptasaṁśayo; ripūnayuddhena jayañjanādhipa
yaśaśca puṇyaṁ ca mahanmahīpate; śriyaṁ ca kīrtiṁ ca ciraṁ samaśnute

translations.english: O lord of people, by conquering the foe without battle, you without losing your forces and putting yourself to peril, you, O lord of earth, shall attain fame and high religious merit, and prosperity and renown for ever and for ever.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथोक्तस्तु निर्भर्त्स्य कुम्भकर्णो महोदरम्
अब्रवीद्राक्षसश्रेष्ठं भ्रातरं रावणं ततः
verses.transliteration:
sa tathoktastu nirbhartsya kumbhakarṇo mahodaram
abravīdrākṣasaśreṣṭhaṁ bhrātaraṁ rāvaṇaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed, Kumbhakarņa rebuking Mahodara, said to that foremost of Rākşasa-his brother-Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽहं तव भयं घोरं वधात्तस्य दुरात्मनः
रामस्याद्य प्रमार्जामि निर्वैरस्त्वं सुखीभव
verses.transliteration:
so'haṁ tava bhayaṁ ghoraṁ vadhāttasya durātmanaḥ
rāmasyādya pramārjāmi nirvairastvaṁ sukhībhava

translations.english: Even I shall remove your great fear by slaying the wicked minded Råma. On your foe having been slain, attain you ease.

verses.sanskrit:
गर्जन्ति न वृथा शूर निर्जला इव तोयदाः
पश्य संपाद्यमानं तु गर्जितं युधि कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
garjanti na vṛthā śūra nirjalā iva toyadāḥ
paśya saṁpādyamānaṁ tu garjitaṁ yudhi karmaṇā

translations.english: It is not for naught that the heroes roar, like to clouds containing no rain. Behold you their, like roaring resulting in action in the field!

verses.sanskrit:
न मर्षयति चात्मानं संभावयति नात्मना
अदर्शयित्वा शूरास्तु कर्म कुर्वन्ति दुष्करम्
verses.transliteration:
na marṣayati cātmānaṁ saṁbhāvayati nātmanā
adarśayitvā śūrāstu karma kurvanti duṣkaram

translations.english: Heroes do not vaunt: but without boasting of their prowess in speech, they perform feats difficult of being achieved.

verses.sanskrit:
विक्लवानामबुद्धीनां राज्ञां पण्डितमानिनाम्
शृण्वतामादित इदं त्वद्विधानां महोदर
verses.transliteration:
viklavānāmabuddhīnāṁ rājñāṁ paṇḍitamāninām
śṛṇvatāmādita idaṁ tvadvidhānāṁ mahodara

translations.english: O Mahodara, what you say is ever acceptable only to kings that are incompetent, and foolish, pluming themselves on their knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
राजशेषा कृता लङ्का क्षीणः कोशो बलं हतम्
राजानमिममासाद्य सुहृच्चिह्नममित्रकम्
verses.transliteration:
rājaśeṣā kṛtā laṅkā kṣīṇaḥ kośo balaṁ hatam
rājānamimamāsādya suhṛccihnamamitrakam

translations.english: All the affairs of the monarch have been wrecked by you-cravens in fight, sleek-tongued, following the king (fawning) you have made Lankā contain only the king, the treasury is lean; and the forces have been slain. By the king you have done like foes in the guise of friends.

verses.sanskrit:
एष निर्याम्यहं युद्धमुद्यतः शत्रुनिर्जये
दुर्नयं भवतामद्य समीकर्तुं महाहवे
verses.transliteration:
eṣa niryāmyahaṁ yuddhamudyataḥ śatrunirjaye
durnayaṁ bhavatāmadya samīkartuṁ mahāhave

translations.english: For repairing in mighty conflict the wrong that you have perpetrated, I am about to set out for battle for routing the enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तवतो वाक्यं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं प्रहसन्राक्षसाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktavato vākyaṁ kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ
pratyuvāca tato vākyaṁ prahasanrākṣasādhipaḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the intelligent Kumbhakarna, the lord of Raksasas, laughing answered.

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरोऽयं रामात्तु परित्रस्तो न संशयः
न हि रोचयते तात युद्धं युद्धविशारद
verses.transliteration:
mahodaro'yaṁ rāmāttu paritrasto na saṁśayaḥ
na hi rocayate tāta yuddhaṁ yuddhaviśārada

translations.english: Sure this Mahodara is affrighted at Rāma. Therefore, my child, O you versed in warfare, he does not relish battle.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्चिन्मे त्वत्समो नास्ति सौहृदेन बलेन च
गच्छ शत्रुवधाय त्वं कुम्भकर्णजयाय च
verses.transliteration:
kaścinme tvatsamo nāsti sauhṛdena balena ca
gaccha śatruvadhāya tvaṁ kumbhakarṇajayāya ca

translations.english: Like you have I none either in friendship or strength. Therefore, O Kumbhakama, go for destroying the foe and securing celebrity.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्तमाल्य महादाम स्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम्
आदाय निशितं शूलं शत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम्
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
raktamālya mahādāma svataścodgatapāvakam
ādāya niśitaṁ śūlaṁ śatruśoṇitarañjitam
kumbhakarṇo mahātejā rāvaṇaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: He took a whetted dart, destructive to foes on account of its impetuous vehemence; entirely made of black iron; flaming: decorated with garniture, of shining gold; looking like Indra's asani; ponderous as the thunder-bolt; capable of destroying gods and Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakşas and Pannagas, adorned with festoons of crimson flowers; and belching forth flames. And taking that huge dart decked with the blood of foes. The wondrous energetic Kumbhakarna spoke to Ravana, saying, I shall go alone; let this mighty host remain here.

verses.sanskrit:
गमिष्याम्यहमेकाकी तिष्ठत्विह बलं महत्
अद्य तान्क्षुधितः क्रुद्धो भक्षयिष्यामि वानरान्
verses.transliteration:
gamiṣyāmyahamekākī tiṣṭhatviha balaṁ mahat
adya tānkṣudhitaḥ kruddho bhakṣayiṣyāmi vānarān

translations.english: Today hungry and enraged, I shall devour up the monkeys. Hearing Kumbhakarma's words. Rāvana said.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्परमदुर्धर्षैः सैन्यैः परिवृतो व्रज
रक्षसामहितं सर्वं शत्रुपक्षं निसूदय
verses.transliteration:
tasmātparamadurdharṣaiḥ sainyaiḥ parivṛto vraja
rakṣasāmahitaṁ sarvaṁ śatrupakṣaṁ nisūdaya

translations.english: Go you surrounded by the forces bearing darts and maces in their hands. The monkeys are highsouled, heroic and well-skilled in battle; and if they find you alone or unwary, they may slay you with their teeth, Therefore do you exceedingly irresistible, go, environed by the forces; and destroy the entire party of the foes, who are bent upon doing harm to the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
अथासनात्समुत्पत्य स्रजं मणिकृतान्तराम्
आबबन्ध महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः
verses.transliteration:
athāsanātsamutpatya srajaṁ maṇikṛtāntarām
ābabandha mahātejāḥ kumbhakarṇasya rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then starting up form his seat, the exceedingly energetic Rāvana hung on Kumbhakarņa's neck a wreath stringed with gems in the centre.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदानङ्गुलीवेष्टान्वराण्याभरणानि च
हारं च शशिसंकाशमाबबन्ध महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadānaṅgulīveṣṭānvarāṇyābharaṇāni ca
hāraṁ ca śaśisaṁkāśamābabandha mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Rāvaņa also decked that high-souled one with Angadas, and finger fences and noble ornaments, and a chain resembling the Moon.

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनाङ्गदकेयूरो निष्काभरणभूषितः
कुम्भकर्णो बृहत्कर्णः सुहुतोऽग्निरिवाबभौ
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāṅgadakeyūro niṣkābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
kumbhakarṇo bṛhatkarṇaḥ suhuto'gnirivābabhau

translations.english: Rāvaņa adorned his person with garlands gorgeous and fragrant, and set ear-rings to his ears. And adorned with golden Angadas and Keyūras and other ornaments of gold, the largeeared Kumbhakarņa appeared like a fire fed full of sacrificial libations.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रोणीसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन विराजितः
अमृतोत्पादने नद्धो भुजंगेनेव मन्दरः
verses.transliteration:
śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā mecakena virājitaḥ
amṛtotpādane naddho bhujaṁgeneva mandaraḥ

translations.english: With his great dark girdle he seemed like the Mandara fastened by the serpent on the occasion of the churning of the sea.

verses.sanskrit:
स काञ्चनं भारसहं निवातं; विद्युत्प्रभं दीप्तमिवात्मभासा
आबध्यमानः कवचं रराज; संध्याभ्रसंवीत इवाद्रिराजः
verses.transliteration:
sa kāñcanaṁ bhārasahaṁ nivātaṁ; vidyutprabhaṁ dīptamivātmabhāsā
ābadhyamānaḥ kavacaṁ rarāja; saṁdhyābhrasaṁvīta ivādrirājaḥ

translations.english: Donning on his impenetrable golden mail, splendid like lightning, and shining in its own brilliance, Kumbhakarņa appeared like the monarch of mountains enveloped with evening clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वाभरणनद्धाङ्गः शूलपाणिः स राक्षसः
त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहो नारायण इवाबभौ
verses.transliteration:
sarvābharaṇanaddhāṅgaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ sa rākṣasaḥ
trivikramakṛtotsāho nārāyaṇa ivābabhau

translations.english: Having all his limbs adorned with ornaments and bearing a dart in his hand, the Rakşasas resembled Nārāyaṇa in elation of spirits, when he covered heaven and earth and the nether regions with three paces.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातरं संपरिष्वज्य कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्
प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्मै संप्रतस्थे महाबलिः
तमाशीर्भिः प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास रावणः
verses.transliteration:
bhrātaraṁ saṁpariṣvajya kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
praṇamya śirasā tasmai saṁpratasthe mahābaliḥ
tamāśīrbhiḥ praśastābhiḥ preṣayāmāsa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then embracing his brother and going round him and bowing down the head to him, that exceedingly powerful one went out.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः सैन्यैश्चापि वरायुधैः
तं गजैश्च तुरंगैश्च स्यन्दनैश्चाम्बुदस्वनैः
अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं रथिनो रथिनां वरम्
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaiḥ sainyaiścāpi varāyudhaiḥ
taṁ gajaiśca turaṁgaiśca syandanaiścāmbudasvanaiḥ
anujagmurmahātmānaṁ rathino rathināṁ varam

translations.english: And high-souled mighty warriors followed that foremost of heroes with elephant and steeds and chariots sending out rattle resembling the rumbling of thunder.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्पैरुष्ट्रैः खरैरश्वैः सिंहद्विपमृगद्विजैः
अनुजग्मुश्च तं घोरं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
sarpairuṣṭraiḥ kharairaśvaiḥ siṁhadvipamṛgadvijaiḥ
anujagmuśca taṁ ghoraṁ kumbhakarṇaṁ mahābalam

translations.english: And mounting serpents and camels and asses and lions and leopards and deer and birds, (Rāks asas) followed the grim Kumbhakarņa endowed with tremendous strength.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुष्पवर्णैरवकीर्यमाणो; धृतातपत्रः शितशूलपाणिः
मदोत्कटः शोणितगन्धमत्तो; विनिर्ययौ दानवदेवशत्रुः
verses.transliteration:
sa puṣpavarṇairavakīryamāṇo; dhṛtātapatraḥ śitaśūlapāṇiḥ
madotkaṭaḥ śoṇitagandhamatto; viniryayau dānavadevaśatruḥ

translations.english: And strewn with blossoms, and, with an umbrella held over him, that exceedingly terrible enemy of the Deities and the Dănvas, wielding a dz.: in his hand-went out maddened with the smell of blood.

verses.sanskrit:
पदातयश बहवो महानादा महाबलाः
अन्वयू राक्षसा भीमा भीमाक्षाः शस्त्रपाणयः
verses.transliteration:
padātayaśa bahavo mahānādā mahābalāḥ
anvayū rākṣasā bhīmā bhīmākṣāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ

translations.english: Countless footmen wondrous powerful and mighty and dreadful and fierce-sighted Räksasas, carrying weapons in their hands, went in his wake.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्ताक्षाः सुमहाकाया नीलाञ्जनचयोपमाः
शूरानुद्यम्य खड्गांश्च निशितांश्च परश्वधान्
verses.transliteration:
raktākṣāḥ sumahākāyā nīlāñjanacayopamāḥ
śūrānudyamya khaḍgāṁśca niśitāṁśca paraśvadhān

translations.english: The Räkşasa measuring each many a vyama and red, eyed, and resembling masses of darkblue collyrium, went out upraising darts and swords and sharpened axes and bhindipälas and parighas and maces and huge talaskandhas and irrisistible Kșepaņis.

verses.sanskrit:
अथान्यद्वपुरादाय दारुणं लोमहर्षणम्
निष्पपात महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
athānyadvapurādāya dāruṇaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
niṣpapāta mahātejāḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: The exceedingly energetic Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious strength sallied forth, assuming another form terrific and dreadful to behold.

verses.sanskrit:
नापराध्यन्ति मे कामं वानरा वनचारिणः
जातिरस्मद्विधानां सा पुरोद्यानविभूषणम्
verses.transliteration:
nāparādhyanti me kāmaṁ vānarā vanacāriṇaḥ
jātirasmadvidhānāṁ sā purodyānavibhūṣaṇam

translations.english: But the wood-ranging monkeys have not transgressed anywise to the like of us. That species is the ornament of the gardens attached to our residences.

verses.sanskrit:
पुररोधस्य मूलं तु राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः
हते तस्मिन्हतं सर्वं तं वधिष्यामि संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
purarodhasya mūlaṁ tu rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
hate tasminhataṁ sarvaṁ taṁ vadhiṣyāmi saṁyuge

translations.english: The cause of the siege of the city is Rāghava along with Laksmana. He being slain, all are slain. Therefore shall I slay him in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य राक्षसाः
नादं चक्रुर्महाघोरं कम्पयन्त इवार्णवम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ tasya bruvāṇasya kumbhakarṇasya rākṣasāḥ
nādaṁ cakrurmahāghoraṁ kampayanta ivārṇavam

translations.english: As the Rākşa—Kumbhakarņa—was speaking thus, the Rākşasas sent up terrific shouts, as if making the very sea shake.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य निष्पततस्तूर्णं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः
बभूवुर्घोररूपाणि निमित्तानि समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
