tasya niṣpatatastūrṇaṁ kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ
babhūvurghorarūpāṇi nimittāni samantataḥ

translations.english: As the intelligent Kumbhakarņa sallied out speedily, dreadful were the omens that presented themselves on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
उल्काशनियुता मेघा विनेदुश्च सुदारुणाः
ससागरवना चैव वसुधा समकम्पत
verses.transliteration:
ulkāśaniyutā meghā vineduśca sudāruṇāḥ
sasāgaravanā caiva vasudhā samakampata

translations.english: Clouds containing meteors and lightning looked dark like asses. And the earth shook with her oceans and woods.

verses.sanskrit:
घोररूपाः शिवा नेदुः सज्वालकवलैर्मुखैः
मण्डलान्यपसव्यानि बबन्धुश्च विहंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
ghorarūpāḥ śivā neduḥ sajvālakavalairmukhaiḥ
maṇḍalānyapasavyāni babandhuśca vihaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: And fierce jackals began to cry, opening their fiaming mouths. And birds began to wheel at the left.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्पपात च गृध्रेऽस्य शूले वै पथि गच्छतः
प्रास्फुरन्नयनं चास्य सव्यो बाहुरकम्पत
verses.transliteration:
niṣpapāta ca gṛdhre'sya śūle vai pathi gacchataḥ
prāsphurannayanaṁ cāsya savyo bāhurakampata

translations.english: As he marched a vulture alighted on his dart. And his left eye throbbed and his left arm shook.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्पपात तदा चोक्ला ज्वलन्ती भीमनिस्वना
आदित्यो निष्प्रभश्चासीन्न प्रवाति सुखोऽनिलः
verses.transliteration:
niṣpapāta tadā coklā jvalantī bhīmanisvanā
ādityo niṣprabhaścāsīnna pravāti sukho'nilaḥ

translations.english: A meteor dropped down with a tremendous crash. And the sun was bedimmed, and the air did not blow, enhancing pleasure.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्तयन्महोत्पातानुत्थिताँल्लोमहर्षणान्
निर्ययौ कुम्भकर्णस्तु कृतान्तबलचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
acintayanmahotpātānutthitā̐llomaharṣaṇān
niryayau kumbhakarṇastu kṛtāntabalacoditaḥ

translations.english: But without heeding these mighty omens that took place, capable of making people's down stand on end, Kumbhakarna went out, urged on by the force of the Finisher.

verses.sanskrit:
स लङ्घयित्वा प्राकारं पद्भ्यां पर्वतसंनिभः
ददर्शाभ्रघनप्रख्यं वानरानीकमद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa laṅghayitvā prākāraṁ padbhyāṁ parvatasaṁnibhaḥ
dadarśābhraghanaprakhyaṁ vānarānīkamadbhutam

translations.english: And leaping over the wall with his legs, that one resembling a mountain saw the wonderful array of the monkeys, resembling clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
ते दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं वानराः पर्वतोपमम्
वायुनुन्ना इव घना ययुः सर्वा दिशस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
te dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṁ vānarāḥ parvatopamam
vāyununnā iva ghanā yayuḥ sarvā diśastadā

translations.english: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas resembling a hill, the monkeys began to disperse in all the ten cardinal directions like clouds driven by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वानरानीकमतिप्रचण्डं; दिशो द्रवद्भिन्नमिवाभ्रजालम्
स कुम्भकर्णः समवेक्ष्य हर्षा;न्ननाद भूयो घनवद्घनाभः
verses.transliteration:
tadvānarānīkamatipracaṇḍaṁ; diśo dravadbhinnamivābhrajālam
sa kumbhakarṇaḥ samavekṣya harṣā;nnanāda bhūyo ghanavadghanābhaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that terrific host of monkeys scattering in all directions, like clouds broken through (by winds), Kumbhakarņa possessed the splendour of clouds, from joy, emitted roars like clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तस्य घोरं निनदं निशम्य; यथा निनादं दिवि वारिदस्य
पेतुर्धरण्यां बहवः प्लवंगा; निकृत्तमूला इव सालवृक्षाः
verses.transliteration:
te tasya ghoraṁ ninadaṁ niśamya; yathā ninādaṁ divi vāridasya
peturdharaṇyāṁ bahavaḥ plavaṁgā; nikṛttamūlā iva sālavṛkṣāḥ

translations.english: Hearing those terrible shouts like to the roaring of clouds in the welkin, innumerable monkeys dropped to the earth even as sāla trees that have their roots severed.

verses.sanskrit:
विपुलपरिघवान्स कुम्भकर्णो; रिपुनिधनाय विनिःसृतो महात्मा
कपि गणभयमाददत्सुभीमं; प्रभुरिव किंकरदण्डवान्युगान्ते
verses.transliteration:
vipulaparighavānsa kumbhakarṇo; ripunidhanāya viniḥsṛto mahātmā
kapi gaṇabhayamādadatsubhīmaṁ; prabhuriva kiṁkaradaṇḍavānyugānte

translations.english: And issuing forth for destroying the foe, the high-souled Kumbhakarņa, equipped with a tremendous bludgeon, struck extreme terror into the monkey-ranks, like to the Lord armed with the Fatal rod at the Universal wreck.

verses.sanskrit:
स ननाद महानादं समुद्रमभिनादयन्
जनयन्निव निर्घातान्विधमन्निव पर्वतान्
verses.transliteration:
sa nanāda mahānādaṁ samudramabhinādayan
janayanniva nirghātānvidhamanniva parvatān

translations.english: Then he sent up a mighty shout making the sea resound, and as if drowning the roar of the thunder and riving mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
तमवध्यं मघवता यमेन वरुणेन च
प्रेक्ष्य भीमाक्षमायान्तं वानरा विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
tamavadhyaṁ maghavatā yamena varuṇena ca
prekṣya bhīmākṣamāyāntaṁ vānarā vipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Seeing that fierce-eyed one, incapable of being vanquished by Maghavān or Varuņa or Yama, the monkeys began to fly away.

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्तु विद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्
नलं नीलं गवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstu vidravato dṛṣṭvā vāliputro'ṅgado'bravīt
nalaṁ nīlaṁ gavākṣaṁ ca kumudaṁ ca mahābalam

translations.english: Seeing them scamper, the king's son-Angada said to Nala and Nīla and Gavākșa and the mighty Kumuda.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानमत्र विस्मृत्य वीर्याण्यभिजनानि च
क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा
verses.transliteration:
ātmānamatra vismṛtya vīryāṇyabhijanāni ca
kva gacchata bhayatrastāḥ prākṛtā harayo yathā

translations.english: Forgetting your lineage and prowess, whither do you, exercised with fear, fly-like inferior monkeys?

verses.sanskrit:
साधु सौम्या निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ
नालं युद्धाय वै रक्षो महतीयं विभीषिकाः
verses.transliteration:
sādhu saumyā nivartadhvaṁ kiṁ prāṇānparirakṣatha
nālaṁ yuddhāya vai rakṣo mahatīyaṁ vibhīṣikāḥ

translations.english: You amiable ones, desist. Why should you save yourselves? This Rākşasa does not come to fight, this is only a great phenomenon to affright.

verses.sanskrit:
महतीमुत्थितामेनां राक्षसानां विभीषिकाम्
विक्रमाद्विधमिष्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
mahatīmutthitāmenāṁ rākṣasānāṁ vibhīṣikām
vikramādvidhamiṣyāmo nivartadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: We shall by our vigour destroy this featful phenomenon of the Rākşasas that has presented itself. Therefore, let the monkeys desist.

verses.sanskrit:
कृच्छ्रेण तु समाश्वास्य संगम्य च ततस्ततः
वृक्षाद्रिहस्ता हरयः संप्रतस्थू रणाजिरम्
verses.transliteration:
kṛcchreṇa tu samāśvāsya saṁgamya ca tatastataḥ
vṛkṣādrihastā harayaḥ saṁpratasthū raṇājiram

translations.english: Cheered with much ado, the monkeys rallying, took up trees and advanced to the field of fight.

verses.sanskrit:
ते निवृत्य तु संक्रुद्धाः कुम्भकर्णं वनौकसः
निजघ्नुः परमक्रुद्धाः समदा इव कुञ्जराः
प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च शिलाभिश्च महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
te nivṛtya tu saṁkruddhāḥ kumbhakarṇaṁ vanaukasaḥ
nijaghnuḥ paramakruddhāḥ samadā iva kuñjarāḥ
prāṁśubhirgiriśṛṅgaiśca śilābhiśca mahābalāḥ

translations.english: Ceasing from flight, the wood-rangers waxing, enraged, began to assail Kumbhakarņa, like to elephants in rut. And the exceedingly strong Kumbhakarna, attacked with towering mountain peaks and crags and trees with flowering top, did not shake.

verses.sanskrit:
पादपैः पुष्पिताग्रैश्च हन्यमानो न कम्पते
तस्य गात्रेषु पतिता भिद्यन्ते शतशः शिलाः
पादपाः पुष्पिताग्राश्च भग्नाः पेतुर्महीतले
verses.transliteration:
pādapaiḥ puṣpitāgraiśca hanyamāno na kampate
tasya gātreṣu patitā bhidyante śataśaḥ śilāḥ
pādapāḥ puṣpitāgrāśca bhagnāḥ peturmahītale

translations.english: And countless crags descending on his person, were shattered; and trees with flowering tops, being broken, fell down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपि सैन्यानि संक्रुद्धो वानराणां महौजसाम्
ममन्थ परमायत्तो वनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
so'pi sainyāni saṁkruddho vānarāṇāṁ mahaujasām
mamantha paramāyatto vanānyagnirivotthitaḥ

translations.english: Incapable of containing himself (through rage), Kumbhakarņa on his part fell to agitating the ranks of the powerful monkeys, even as a fire breaking out burn dowit a forest.

verses.sanskrit:
लोहितार्द्रास्तु बहवः शेरते वानरर्षभाः
निरस्ताः पतिता भूमौ ताम्रपुष्पा इव द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
lohitārdrāstu bahavaḥ śerate vānararṣabhāḥ
nirastāḥ patitā bhūmau tāmrapuṣpā iva drumāḥ

translations.english: Many a prime monkey, crimsoned and drenched (with blood) lay down (on the ground); and many, resisted dropped to the earth, like trees bearing coppery flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्घयन्तः प्रधावन्तो वानरा नावलोकयन्
केचित्समुद्रे पतिताः केचिद्गगनमाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
laṅghayantaḥ pradhāvanto vānarā nāvalokayan
kecitsamudre patitāḥ kecidgaganamāśritāḥ

translations.english: Without looking before or after, the monkeys bounded and rushed. And on being attacked by the Rāksasa with ease some of those heroes dropped into the deep and some entered the wilderness.

verses.sanskrit:
ते स्थलानि तथा निम्नं विषण्णवदना भयात्
ऋक्षा वृक्षान्समारूढाः केचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration:
te sthalāni tathā nimnaṁ viṣaṇṇavadanā bhayāt
ṛkṣā vṛkṣānsamārūḍhāḥ kecitparvatamāśritāḥ

translations.english: Some ran by the same way by which they had crossed the ocean; and some with pale faces darted into downs. And some of the bears ascended up trees, and some took shelter in mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
ममज्जुरर्णवे केचिद्गुहाः केचित्समाश्रिताः
निषेदुः प्लवगाः केचित्केचिन्नैवावतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
mamajjurarṇave kecidguhāḥ kecitsamāśritāḥ
niṣeduḥ plavagāḥ kecitkecinnaivāvatasthire

translations.english: Others dropped down; and some ran on. And some fell down to the earth, and some lay insensible as if dead.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्समीक्ष्याङ्गदो भङ्गान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत्
अवतिष्ठत युध्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
tānsamīkṣyāṅgado bhaṅgānvānarānidamabravīt
avatiṣṭhata yudhyāmo nivartadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Seeing the monkeys break down, Angada addressed them, saying, “Stay we shall fight.

verses.sanskrit:
भग्नानां वो न पश्यामि परिगम्य महीमिमाम्
स्थानं सर्वे निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ
verses.transliteration:
bhagnānāṁ vo na paśyāmi parigamya mahīmimām
sthānaṁ sarve nivartadhvaṁ kiṁ prāṇānparirakṣatha

translations.english: Desist, you monkeys. Going round this Earth place find I none where you may rest. Stop you all. What is the need of preserving your lives.

verses.sanskrit:
निरायुधानां द्रवतामसंगगतिपौरुषाः
दारा ह्यपहसिष्यन्ति स वै घातस्तु जीविताम्
verses.transliteration:
nirāyudhānāṁ dravatāmasaṁgagatipauruṣāḥ
dārā hyapahasiṣyanti sa vai ghātastu jīvitām

translations.english: You poltroons, if you fly away leaving your arms behind, your wives shall deride you; and that is more painful to honourable persons than death itself.

verses.sanskrit:
कुलेषु जाताः सर्वे स्म विस्तीर्णेषु महत्सु च
अनार्याः खलु यद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वा वीर्यं प्रधावत
verses.transliteration:
kuleṣu jātāḥ sarve sma vistīrṇeṣu mahatsu ca
anāryāḥ khalu yadbhītāstyaktvā vīryaṁ pradhāvata

translations.english: Born in long and noble lines, whither go you, suffering from fear, like abject monkeys? When renouncing your prowess, you fly away in fear, forsooth you are base.

verses.sanskrit:
विकत्थनानि वो यानि यदा वै जनसंसदि
तानि वः क्व च यतानि सोदग्राणि महान्ति च
verses.transliteration:
vikatthanāni vo yāni yadā vai janasaṁsadi
tāni vaḥ kva ca yatāni sodagrāṇi mahānti ca

translations.english: Where now is gone that talk of your anent your nobility and the welfare (of your king) which you had held in society.

verses.sanskrit:
भीरुप्रवादाः श्रूयन्ते यस्तु जीवति धिक्कृतः
मार्गः सत्पुरुषैर्जुष्टः सेव्यतां त्यज्यतां भयम्
verses.transliteration:
bhīrupravādāḥ śrūyante yastu jīvati dhikkṛtaḥ
mārgaḥ satpuruṣairjuṣṭaḥ sevyatāṁ tyajyatāṁ bhayam

translations.english: He that live, despised (of all), hear the reproach of being a craven. Therefore do you follow the way frequented by the worthy, and cast off fear.

verses.sanskrit:
शयामहे वा निहताः पृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः
दुष्प्रापं ब्रह्मलोकं वा प्राप्नुमो युधि सूदिताः
संप्राप्नुयामः कीर्तिं वा निहत्य शत्रुमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
śayāmahe vā nihatāḥ pṛthivyāmalpajīvitāḥ
duṣprāpaṁ brahmalokaṁ vā prāpnumo yudhi sūditāḥ
saṁprāpnuyāmaḥ kīrtiṁ vā nihatya śatrumāhave

translations.english: We will either lie down on the earth, being slain in consequence of our shortness of days, and thus attain the region of Brahmä incapable of being attained by dastards; or achieve renown by slaying the foe in fight and slain in battle, we shall enjoy the wealth of the region of heroes.

verses.sanskrit:
न कुम्भकर्णः काकुत्स्थं दृष्ट्वा जीवन्गमिष्यति
दीप्यमानमिवासाद्य पतंगो ज्वलनं यथा
verses.transliteration:
na kumbhakarṇaḥ kākutsthaṁ dṛṣṭvā jīvangamiṣyati
dīpyamānamivāsādya pataṁgo jvalanaṁ yathā

translations.english: Like an insect coming to a glowing and flaming fire, Kumbhakarna, seeing Kākutstha, shall not away.hence living.

verses.sanskrit:
पलायनेन चोद्दिष्टाः प्राणान्रक्षामहे वयम्
एकेन बहवो भग्ना यशो नाशं गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
palāyanena coddiṣṭāḥ prāṇānrakṣāmahe vayam
ekena bahavo bhagnā yaśo nāśaṁ gamiṣyati

translations.english: If we save our lives by flight, and if the many are brought down by one, we shall lose our fame utterly.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवाणं तं शूरमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम्
द्रवमाणास्ततो वाक्यमूचुः शूरविगर्हितम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ taṁ śūramaṅgadaṁ kanakāṅgadam
dravamāṇāstato vākyamūcuḥ śūravigarhitam

translations.english: As Angada decked in golden angadas was saying this, the monkeys, flying away spoke to that hero words not worthy of being spoken to an hero.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतं नः कदनं घोरं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा
न स्थानकालो गच्छामो दयितं जीवितं हि नः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtaṁ naḥ kadanaṁ ghoraṁ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasā
na sthānakālo gacchāmo dayitaṁ jīvitaṁ hi naḥ

translations.english: Great is the havoc that the Rākşasa-Kumbhakarma-has spread among us. “This not the time to stay: life is dear to us."

verses.sanskrit:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं सर्वे ते भेजिरे दिशः
भीमं भीमाक्षमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṁ sarve te bhejire diśaḥ
bhīmaṁ bhīmākṣamāyāntaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānarayūthapāḥ

translations.english: Having said this the monkey bands darted to the ten cardinal points, as they saw that dreadful and grim-eyed one approach.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रवमाणास्तु ते वीरा अङ्गदेन वलीमुखाः
सान्त्वैश्च बहुमानैश्च ततः सर्वे निवर्तिताः
verses.transliteration:
dravamāṇāstu te vīrā aṅgadena valīmukhāḥ
sāntvaiśca bahumānaiśca tataḥ sarve nivartitāḥ

translations.english: As those flower of the forces were on the flight, those heroes were made to desist by Angada with words of comfort and hope pointing to the future.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाः; कुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः
द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्या;स्त्वरिततराभिमुखं रणं प्रयाताः
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣabhaśarabhamaindadhūmranīlāḥ; kumudasuṣeṇagavākṣarambhatārāḥ
dvividapanasavāyuputramukhyā;stvaritatarābhimukhaṁ raṇaṁ prayātāḥ

translations.english: Rşabha, Sarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra, Nila, Kumuda, Susena, Gavaksa, Rambha, Dvivida, Panasa, and son of wind Hanuman and other powerf:! leaders speedily proceeded to the battle field.

verses.sanskrit:
ते निवृत्ता महाकायाः श्रुत्वाङ्गदवचस्तदा
नैष्ठिकीं बुद्धिमास्थाय सर्वे संग्रामकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
te nivṛttā mahākāyāḥ śrutvāṅgadavacastadā
naiṣṭhikīṁ buddhimāsthāya sarve saṁgrāmakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: Having desisted on hearing the words of Angada those huge-bodied ones, regaining calmness, became (again) intent on fight.

verses.sanskrit:
समुदीरितवीर्यास्ते समारोपितविक्रमाः
पर्यवस्थापिता वाक्यैरङ्गदेन वलीमुखाः
verses.transliteration:
samudīritavīryāste samāropitavikramāḥ
paryavasthāpitā vākyairaṅgadena valīmukhāḥ

translations.english: Attaining energy at the exhortation (of Angada), and summoning up their prowess, they stayed in the field agreeable to the words of the powerful Angada.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रयाताश्च गता हर्षं मरणे कृतनिश्चयाः
चक्रुः सुतुमुलं युद्धं वानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः
verses.transliteration:
prayātāśca gatā harṣaṁ maraṇe kṛtaniścayāḥ
cakruḥ sutumulaṁ yuddhaṁ vānarāstyaktajīvitāḥ

translations.english: Inspired with spirits, the monkeys, determined to face their fate, rushed into the conflict, and, casting away all care for their lives, entered into a furious fight (with the foe)

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वृक्षान्महाकायाः सानूनि सुमहान्ति च
वानरास्तूर्णमुद्यम्य कुम्भकर्णमभिद्रवन्
verses.transliteration:
atha vṛkṣānmahākāyāḥ sānūni sumahānti ca
vānarāstūrṇamudyamya kumbhakarṇamabhidravan

translations.english: And speedily upraising trees and gigantic crags, the huge-bodied monkeys charged Kumbhakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णः संक्रुद्धो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
अर्दयन्सुमहाकायः समन्ताद्व्याक्षिपद्रिपून्
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇaḥ saṁkruddho gadāmudyamya vīryavān
ardayansumahākāyaḥ samantādvyākṣipadripūn

translations.english: Thereat the mighty Kumbhakarņa possessed of a prodigious person waxing wroth taking up his mace let the same alight on the enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः
प्रकीर्णाः शेरते भूमौ कुम्भकर्णेन पोथिताः
verses.transliteration:
śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca vānarāḥ
prakīrṇāḥ śerate bhūmau kumbhakarṇena pothitāḥ

translations.english: Attacked by Kumbhakarma, seven, eight hundreds and thousands of monkeys measure their lengths on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्त्रिंशत्तथैव च
परिक्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यां खादन्विपरिधावति
भक्षयन्भृशसंक्रुद्धो गरुडः पन्नगानिव
verses.transliteration:
ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca daśa ca viṁśattriṁśattathaiva ca
parikṣipya ca bāhubhyāṁ khādanviparidhāvati
bhakṣayanbhṛśasaṁkruddho garuḍaḥ pannagāniva

translations.english: Casting about his arms, he rush on, devouring sixteen, eight, ten, twenty or thirty. And he devoured (the monkeys) like Garuda swallowing up serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमाञ्शैलशृङ्गाणि वृक्षांश्च विविधान्बहून्
ववर्ष कुम्भकर्णस्य शिरस्यम्बरमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
hanūmāñśailaśṛṅgāṇi vṛkṣāṁśca vividhānbahūn
vavarṣa kumbhakarṇasya śirasyambaramāsthitaḥ

translations.english: And remaining in the sky, Hanumān discharged at Kumbhakarņa's head mountainpeaks and rocks and various trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि पर्वतशृङ्गाणि शूलेन तु बिभेद ह
बभञ्ज वृक्षवर्षं च कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇi śūlena tu bibheda ha
babhañja vṛkṣavarṣaṁ ca kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: And all those mountain-tops he cut off with his dart; and the mighty Kumbhakarņa also baffled the shower of trees.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं; दुद्राव शूलं निशितं प्रगृह्य
तस्थौ ततोऽस्यापततः पुरस्ता;न्महीधराग्रं हनुमान्प्रगृह्य
verses.transliteration:
tato harīṇāṁ tadanīkamugraṁ; dudrāva śūlaṁ niśitaṁ pragṛhya
tasthau tato'syāpatataḥ purastā;nmahīdharāgraṁ hanumānpragṛhya

translations.english: Then grasping his sharpened spear, Kumbhakarņa darted against that terrific array of monkeys. And as he charged them, Hanuman armed with a mountain-peak, stood before him.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो जघान; वेगेन शैलोत्तमभीमकायम्
स चुक्षुभे तेन तदाभिबूतो; मेदार्द्रगात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇaṁ kupito jaghāna; vegena śailottamabhīmakāyam
sa cukṣubhe tena tadābhibūto; medārdragātro rudhirāvasiktaḥ

translations.english: Waxing enraged (Hanuman) vehemently smote Kumbhakarņa with a gigantic crag. And overpowered by that, Kumbhakarna experienced great torments, and his body was covered with fat and blood.

verses.sanskrit:
स शूलमाविध्य तडित्प्रकाशं; गिरिं यथा प्रज्वलिताग्रशृङ्गम्
बाह्वन्तरे मारुतिमाजघान; गुहोऽचलं क्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्त्या
verses.transliteration:
sa śūlamāvidhya taḍitprakāśaṁ; giriṁ yathā prajvalitāgraśṛṅgam
bāhvantare mārutimājaghāna; guho'calaṁ krauñcamivograśaktyā

translations.english: Then as Guha had pierced Krauñca with his fierce dart, Kumbhakarna the mountain-like smote the Wind-god's son in the chest with his dart resembling lightning or like a glowing mountain-summit.

verses.sanskrit:
स शूलनिर्भिन्न महाभुजान्तरः; प्रविह्वलः शोणितमुद्वमन्मुखात्
ननाद भीमं हनुमान्महाहवे; युगान्तमेघस्तनितस्वनोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
sa śūlanirbhinna mahābhujāntaraḥ; pravihvalaḥ śoṇitamudvamanmukhāt
nanāda bhīmaṁ hanumānmahāhave; yugāntameghastanitasvanopamam

translations.english: And having his mighty chest pierced in the mighty encounter, Hanumān, overwhelmed, and vomiting blood-transported with wrath, set up roars resembling the roaring of the clouds at the universal disruption.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विनेदुः सहसा प्रहृष्टा; रक्षोगणास्तं व्यथितं समीक्ष्य
प्लवंगमास्तु व्यथिता भयार्ताः; प्रदुद्रुवुः संयति कुम्भकर्णात्
verses.transliteration:
tato vineduḥ sahasā prahṛṣṭā; rakṣogaṇāstaṁ vyathitaṁ samīkṣya
plavaṁgamāstu vyathitā bhayārtāḥ; pradudruvuḥ saṁyati kumbhakarṇāt

translations.english: Then, beholding him in torments, Raksasas suddenly rejoiced, emitted shouts; and the monkeys aggrieved and overcome with fright, began to fly Kumbhakarna in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलश्चिक्षेप शैलाग्रं कुम्भकर्णाय धीमते
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य मुष्टिनाभिजघान ह
verses.transliteration:
nīlaścikṣepa śailāgraṁ kumbhakarṇāya dhīmate
tamāpatantaṁ saṁprekṣya muṣṭinābhijaghāna ha

translations.english: Then the powerful Nīla, arranging his forces, discharged a mountain-peak at the intelligent Kumbhakarma.

verses.sanskrit:
मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतं तच्छैलाग्रं व्यशीर्यत
सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात महीतले
verses.transliteration:
muṣṭiprahārābhihataṁ tacchailāgraṁ vyaśīryata
savisphuliṅgaṁ sajvālaṁ nipapāta mahītale

translations.english: Seeing it descend, he dealt it a blow; and struck by the blow, the mountain-top was shattered in pieces; and dropped to the earth glowing and shooting living flames.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषभः शरभो नीलो गवाक्षो गन्धमादनः
पञ्चवानरशार्दूलाः कुम्भकर्णमुपाद्रवन्
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣabhaḥ śarabho nīlo gavākṣo gandhamādanaḥ
pañcavānaraśārdūlāḥ kumbhakarṇamupādravan

translations.english: Then Rşabha and Sarabha and Nīla and Gavākṣa and Gandhamādana, these five terrific monkeys, rushed against Kumbhakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलैर्वृक्षैस्तलैः पादैर्मुष्टिभिश्च महाबलाः
कुम्भकर्णं महाकायं सर्वतोऽभिनिजघ्निरे
verses.transliteration:
śailairvṛkṣaistalaiḥ pādairmuṣṭibhiśca mahābalāḥ
kumbhakarṇaṁ mahākāyaṁ sarvato'bhinijaghnire

translations.english: And in the encounter those mighty monkeys began to sorely assail the huge-bodied Kumbhakarma with crags and trees and slaps and kicks and blows.

verses.sanskrit:
स्पर्शानिव प्रहारांस्तान्वेदयानो न विव्यथे
ऋषभं तु महावेगं बाहुभ्यां परिषस्वजे
verses.transliteration:
sparśāniva prahārāṁstānvedayāno na vivyathe
ṛṣabhaṁ tu mahāvegaṁ bāhubhyāṁ pariṣasvaje

translations.english: But those blows seemed to him like touches* and did not at all pain him. Then he fastened the vehement Rşabha with his arms. *Like the feel, remarks Rāmánuja, of wreaths, unguents, etc. blows

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णभुजाभ्यां तु पीडितो वानरर्षभः
निपपातर्षभो भीमः प्रमुखागतशोणितः
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇabhujābhyāṁ tu pīḍito vānararṣabhaḥ
nipapātarṣabho bhīmaḥ pramukhāgataśoṇitaḥ

translations.english: Agonised on being fastened with Kumbhakarma's arms, that foremost of monkeys, the dreadful Rşabha, fell down to the earth, vomiting blood by his mouth.

verses.sanskrit:
मुष्टिना शरभं हत्वा जानुना नीलमाहवे
आजघान गवाक्षं च तलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
muṣṭinā śarabhaṁ hatvā jānunā nīlamāhave
ājaghāna gavākṣaṁ ca talenendraripustadā

translations.english: Then the enemy of Indra smite, Sarabha with blow, and Nila, in the conflict with his thigh, struck a slap at Gavākṣa.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्तप्रहरव्यथिता मुमुहुः शोणितोक्षिताः
निपेतुस्ते तु मेदिन्यां निकृत्ता इव किंशुकाः
verses.transliteration:
dattapraharavyathitā mumuhuḥ śoṇitokṣitāḥ
nipetuste tu medinyāṁ nikṛttā iva kiṁśukāḥ

translations.english: Then he speedily hit by his feet with wrath Gandhamadana. Suffering great. pain in consequence of the (dealt by Kumbhakarņa those monkeys), deprived of their senses and bathed in blood, dropped down to the earth like Kinśukas that have been cut down.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु वानरमुख्येषु पतितेषु महात्मसु
वानराणां सहस्राणि कुम्भकर्णं प्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
teṣu vānaramukhyeṣu patiteṣu mahātmasu
vānarāṇāṁ sahasrāṇi kumbhakarṇaṁ pradudruvuḥ

translations.english: On those high-souled and mighty monkeys falling down, thousands of monkeys rushed at Kumbhakarna.

verses.sanskrit:
तं शैलमिव शैलाभाः सर्वे तु प्लवगर्षभाः
समारुह्य समुत्पत्य ददंशुश्च महाबलाः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ śailamiva śailābhāḥ sarve tu plavagarṣabhāḥ
samāruhya samutpatya dadaṁśuśca mahābalāḥ

translations.english: Ascending a mountain-summit, those foremost of monkeys, possessed of the splendour of a mountain-peak, sprang upon him and tore him with their teeth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं नखैर्दशनैश्चापि मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिस्तथा
कुम्भकर्णं महाकायं ते जघ्नुः प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ nakhairdaśanaiścāpi muṣṭibhirjānubhistathā
kumbhakarṇaṁ mahākāyaṁ te jaghnuḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: And those foremost of monkeys attacked the long-armed Kumbhakarma with their claws and teeth and blows and arms.

verses.sanskrit:
स वानरसहस्रैस्तैराचितः पर्वतोपमः
रराज राक्षसव्याघ्रो गिरिरात्मरुहैरिव
verses.transliteration:
sa vānarasahasraistairācitaḥ parvatopamaḥ
rarāja rākṣasavyāghro girirātmaruhairiva

translations.english: Then with thousands of monkeys on him that extraordinary onethat fearful Raksasa-resembling a hill, looked like a mountain with trees on it.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहुभ्यां वानरान्सर्वान्प्रगृह्य स महाबलः
भक्षयामास संक्रुद्धो गरुडः पन्नगानिव
verses.transliteration:
bāhubhyāṁ vānarānsarvānpragṛhya sa mahābalaḥ
bhakṣayāmāsa saṁkruddho garuḍaḥ pannagāniva

translations.english: Like Garuda eating up serpents, that wondours strong one, wrought up with rage, devoured those monkeys, seizing them with his arms.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रक्षिप्ताः कुम्भकर्णेन वक्त्रे पातालसंनिभे
नासा पुटाभ्यां निर्जग्मुः कर्णाभ्यां चैव वानराः
verses.transliteration:
prakṣiptāḥ kumbhakarṇena vaktre pātālasaṁnibhe
nāsā puṭābhyāṁ nirjagmuḥ karṇābhyāṁ caiva vānarāḥ

translations.english: And cast by Kumbhakarņa into his mouth resembling the nether regions the monkeys emerged from his nose and ears.

verses.sanskrit:
भक्षयन्भृशसंक्रुद्धो हरीन्पर्वतसंनिभः
बभञ्ज वानरान्सर्वान्संक्रुद्धो राक्षसोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
bhakṣayanbhṛśasaṁkruddho harīnparvatasaṁnibhaḥ
babhañja vānarānsarvānsaṁkruddho rākṣasottamaḥ

translations.english: And eating up the monkeys, that foremost of Raksasas resembling a hill, growing worth, and fired with rage, began to break the monkeys down.

verses.sanskrit:
मांसशोणितसंक्लेदां भूमिं कुर्वन्स राक्षसः
चचार हरिसैन्येषु कालाग्निरिव मूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
māṁsaśoṇitasaṁkledāṁ bhūmiṁ kurvansa rākṣasaḥ
cacāra harisainyeṣu kālāgniriva mūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And transported with passion, that Raksasa, making the earth miry with flesh and blood, spread among the monkey-ranks like to the fire at the time of the Universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रहस्तो यथा शक्रः पाशहस्त इवान्तकः
शूलहस्तो बभौ तस्मिन्कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
vajrahasto yathā śakraḥ pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ
śūlahasto babhau tasminkumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ

translations.english: In that encounter, Kumbhakarņa armed with his dart in his hand, resembled the thunderhanded ſakra, or the noose-handed Destroyer himself.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा शुष्काण्यरण्यानि ग्रीष्मे दहति पावकः
तथा वानरसैन्यानि कुम्भकर्णो विनिर्दहत्
verses.transliteration:
yathā śuṣkāṇyaraṇyāni grīṣme dahati pāvakaḥ
tathā vānarasainyāni kumbhakarṇo vinirdahat

translations.english: As a conflagration burn up a withered forest in the summer, Kumbhakarna burnt that host of the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते वध्यमानास्तु हतयूथा विनायकाः
वानरा भयसंविग्ना विनेदुर्विस्वरं भृशम्
verses.transliteration:
tataste vadhyamānāstu hatayūthā vināyakāḥ
vānarā bhayasaṁvignā vinedurvisvaraṁ bhṛśam

translations.english: Thus beaten (by Kumbhakarna), those monkeys, with their ranks destroyed, the monkeys, racked with anxiety, began to cry in unnatural tones.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेकशो वध्यमानाः कुम्भकर्णेन वानराः
राघवं शरणं जग्मुर्व्यथिताः खिन्नचेतसः
verses.transliteration:
anekaśo vadhyamānāḥ kumbhakarṇena vānarāḥ
rāghavaṁ śaraṇaṁ jagmurvyathitāḥ khinnacetasaḥ

translations.english: Having innumerable monkeys slain by Kumbhakarņa, the monkeys, aggrieved and their hearts riven with sorrow, sought the shelter of Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्
उत्पपात तदा वीरः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ saṁprekṣya kumbhakarṇaṁ mahābalam
utpapāta tadā vīraḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ

translations.english: Seeing the exceeding stout Kumbhakarņa approach, the heroic king of monkeys-Sugriva-sprang up; and taking a mountain-top that one possessed of great strength darted against the mighty Kumbhakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्णः प्लवंगमम्
तस्थौ विवृतसर्वाङ्गो वानरेन्द्रस्य संमुखः
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ saṁprekṣya kumbhakarṇaḥ plavaṁgamam
tasthau vivṛtasarvāṅgo vānarendrasya saṁmukhaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that monkey, Kumbhakarņa, stretching his limbs, stood before the lord of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गं भक्षयन्तं महाकपीन्
कुम्भकर्णं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kapiśoṇitadigdhāṅgaṁ bhakṣayantaṁ mahākapīn
kumbhakarṇaṁ sthitaṁ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing Kumbhakarņa, with his body laved in the blood of monkeys; and eating up mighty monkeys, Sugriva addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
पातिताश्च त्वया वीराः कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्
भक्षितानि च सैन्यानि प्राप्तं ते परमं यशः
verses.transliteration:
pātitāśca tvayā vīrāḥ kṛtaṁ karma suduṣkaram
bhakṣitāni ca sainyāni prāptaṁ te paramaṁ yaśaḥ

translations.english: You have felled heroes done deeds difficult of being performed, and have devoured the warriors; and you have thus attained renown. But let go now the monkey-army. What shall you do with the ignoble? Do you, O Raksasa bear the descent of this mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वाक्यं हरिराजस्य सत्त्वधैर्यसमन्वितम्
श्रुत्वा राक्षसशार्दूलः कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
tadvākyaṁ harirājasya sattvadhairyasamanvitam
śrutvā rākṣasaśārdūlaḥ kumbhakarṇo'bravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of the monkey-king instinct with strength and fortitude, that terrible Raksasa-Kumbhakarna-said.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतेस्तु पौत्रस्त्वं तथैवर्क्षरजःसुतः
श्रुतपौरुषसंपन्नस्तस्माद्गर्जसि वानर
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatestu pautrastvaṁ tathaivarkṣarajaḥsutaḥ
śrutapauruṣasaṁpannastasmādgarjasi vānara

translations.english: O monkey, you storm, because you are the grandson of Prajāpati and the son of the king of bears; and because as such you are endowed with fortitude and prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य; व्याविध्य शैलं सहसा मुमोच
तेनाजघानोरसि कुम्भकर्णं; शैलेन वज्राशनिसंनिभेन
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya; vyāvidhya śailaṁ sahasā mumoca
tenājaghānorasi kumbhakarṇaṁ; śailena vajrāśanisaṁnibhena

translations.english: Hearing Kumbhakarna's speech, Sugrīva whirling that mountain-peak, suddeniy let it go; and with that rock resembling Vajra or the thunder-bolt, smote Kumbhakarņa in the chest.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छैलशृङ्गं सहसा विकीर्णं; भुजान्तरे तस्य तदा विशाले
ततो विषेदुः सहसा प्लवंगमा; रक्षोगणाश्चापि मुदा विनेदुः
verses.transliteration:
tacchailaśṛṅgaṁ sahasā vikīrṇaṁ; bhujāntare tasya tadā viśāle
tato viṣeduḥ sahasā plavaṁgamā; rakṣogaṇāścāpi mudā vineduḥ

translations.english: On coming in contact with his wide breast, that mountain-peak was at once shattered in shivers, And thereat the monkeys grew dispirited and the Raksas's ranks shouted in joy.

verses.sanskrit:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतश्चुकोप; ननाद कोपाच्च विवृत्य वक्त्रम्
व्याविध्य शूलं च तडित्प्रकाशं; चिक्षेप हर्यृक्षपतेर्वधाय
verses.transliteration:
sa śailaśṛṅgābhihataścukopa; nanāda kopācca vivṛtya vaktram
vyāvidhya śūlaṁ ca taḍitprakāśaṁ; cikṣepa haryṛkṣapatervadhāya

translations.english: And struck with the mountain-summit, Kumbhakarna was fired with wrath; and roared, expending his face. And then, whirling his dart resembling lightning displayed, he hurled it for compassing the destruction of the master of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजप्रविद्धं; शूलं शितं काञ्चनदामजुष्टम्
क्षिप्रं समुत्पत्य निगृह्य दोर्भ्यां; बभञ्ज वेगेन सुतोऽनिलस्य
verses.transliteration:
tatkumbhakarṇasya bhujapraviddhaṁ; śūlaṁ śitaṁ kāñcanadāmajuṣṭam
kṣipraṁ samutpatya nigṛhya dorbhyāṁ; babhañja vegena suto'nilasya

translations.english: Then swiftly bounding up, the Wind-god's son, resisting that whetted dart fastened with golden chains, with his hands violently snapped it in twain.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतं भारसहस्रस्य शूलं कालायसं महत्
बभञ्ज जनौमारोप्य प्रहृष्टः प्लवगर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtaṁ bhārasahasrasya śūlaṁ kālāyasaṁ mahat
babhañja janaumāropya prahṛṣṭaḥ plavagarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: And placing the same on his thighs, (Hanuman) snapped that ponderous and terrible dart composed of black iron, and thereat the monkeys waxed delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्तदा भग्नमवेक्ष्य शूलं; चुकोप रक्षोऽधिपतिर्महात्मा
उत्पाट्य लङ्कामलयात्स शृङ्गं; जघान सुग्रीवमुपेत्य तेन
verses.transliteration:
sa tattadā bhagnamavekṣya śūlaṁ; cukopa rakṣo'dhipatirmahātmā
utpāṭya laṅkāmalayātsa śṛṅgaṁ; jaghāna sugrīvamupetya tena

translations.english: Then the mighty-minded lord of Rákşasas seeing the dart thus severed, uprooted a peak from the Malaya and with it smote Sugrīva.

verses.sanskrit:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतो विसंज्ञः; पपात भूमौ युधि वानरेन्द्रः
तं प्रेक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं विसंज्ञं; नेदुः प्रहृष्टा युधि यातुधानाः
verses.transliteration:
sa śailaśṛṅgābhihato visaṁjñaḥ; papāta bhūmau yudhi vānarendraḥ
taṁ prekṣya bhūmau patitaṁ visaṁjñaṁ; neduḥ prahṛṣṭā yudhi yātudhānāḥ

translations.english: The king of monkeys struck with the mountain-peak fell senseless upon the field, and the demons finding him in this plight shouted out in great joy.

verses.sanskrit:
तमभ्युपेत्याद्भुतघोरवीर्यं; स कुम्भकर्णो युधि वानरेन्द्रम्
जहार सुग्रीवमभिप्रगृह्य; यथानिलो मेघमतिप्रचण्डः
verses.transliteration:
tamabhyupetyādbhutaghoravīryaṁ; sa kumbhakarṇo yudhi vānarendram
jahāra sugrīvamabhipragṛhya; yathānilo meghamatipracaṇḍaḥ

translations.english: Then Kumbhakarna coming to the wonderfully mighty master of monkeys, took him up and stole away from the field, as a violent gust of wind steal away a patch of cloud.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं महामेघनिकाशरूप;मुत्पाट्य गच्छन्युधि कुम्भकर्णः
रराज मेरुप्रतिमानरूपो; मेरुर्यथात्युच्छ्रितघोरशृङ्गः
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ mahāmeghanikāśarūpa;mutpāṭya gacchanyudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ
rarāja merupratimānarūpo; meruryathātyucchritaghoraśṛṅgaḥ

translations.english: Kumbhakarņa, who resembled a mountain in loftiness of stature, while taking him away like a mass of cloud appeared like Sumeru overtopped with lofty peaks.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः समुत्पाट्य जगाम वीरः; संस्तूयमानो युधि राक्षसेन्द्रैः
शृण्वन्निनादं त्रिदशालयानां; प्लवंगराजग्रहविस्मितानाम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ samutpāṭya jagāma vīraḥ; saṁstūyamāno yudhi rākṣasendraiḥ
śṛṇvanninādaṁ tridaśālayānāṁ; plavaṁgarājagrahavismitānām

translations.english: Thus the lord of Rākşasas went on hearing thanks (from the Rākşasas) and shouts from the lords of the heavens, wondered at the capture of the foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तमादाय तदा स मेने; हरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः
अस्मिन्हृते सर्वमिदं हृतं स्या;त्सराघवं सैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः
verses.transliteration:
tatastamādāya tadā sa mene; harīndramindropamamindravīryaḥ
asminhṛte sarvamidaṁ hṛtaṁ syā;tsarāghavaṁ sainyamitīndraśatruḥ

translations.english: Thus taking him captive, that mighty one resembling Indra in puissance, thought his death would destroy the entire host of the opponents together with Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास मतिमान्मारुतात्मजः
एवं गृहीते सुग्रीवे किं कर्तव्यं मया भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
hanūmāṁścintayāmāsa matimānmārutātmajaḥ
evaṁ gṛhīte sugrīve kiṁ kartavyaṁ mayā bhavet

translations.english: Then Hanumān, the shrewd son of Maruta, finding the whole host of monkeys scattered in all directions, as well as Sugrīva captured by Kumbhakarņa bethought himself—“What ought to be done by me now that our king has been captured?

verses.sanskrit:
यद्वै न्याय्यं मया कर्तुं तत्करिष्यामि सर्वथा
भूत्वा पर्वतसंकाशो नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
yadvai nyāyyaṁ mayā kartuṁ tatkariṣyāmi sarvathā
bhūtvā parvatasaṁkāśo nāśayiṣyāmi rākṣasaṁ

translations.english: I will doubtless do as befits me now let me assume the shape of a mountain and kill the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
मया हते संयति कुम्भकर्णे; महाबले मुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे
विमोचिते वानरपार्थिवे च; भवन्तु हृष्टाः प्रवगाः समग्राः
verses.transliteration:
mayā hate saṁyati kumbhakarṇe; mahābale muṣṭiviśīrṇadehe
vimocite vānarapārthive ca; bhavantu hṛṣṭāḥ pravagāḥ samagrāḥ

translations.english: Let me kill the mighty Kumbhakarņa, splitting his body with my strong fist and thus relive the master of monkeys—thus let the whole host of monkeys become delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा स्वयमप्येष मोक्षं प्राप्स्यति पार्थिवः
गृहीतोऽयं यदि भवेत्त्रिदशैः सासुरोरगैः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā svayamapyeṣa mokṣaṁ prāpsyati pārthivaḥ
gṛhīto'yaṁ yadi bhavettridaśaiḥ sāsuroragaiḥ

translations.english: Or, even when captured by the whole host of gods or Asuras or serpents he is mighty enough to extricate himself.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये न तावदात्मानं बुध्यते वानराधिपः
शैलप्रहाराभिहतः कुम्भकर्णेन संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
manye na tāvadātmānaṁ budhyate vānarādhipaḥ
śailaprahārābhihataḥ kumbhakarṇena saṁyuge

translations.english: Meseems, the lord of monkeys struck with dart in battle by Kumbhakarna has not yet recovered his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं मुहूर्तात्सुग्रीवो लब्धसंज्ञो महाहवे
आत्मनो वानराणां च यत्पथ्यं तत्करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ muhūrtātsugrīvo labdhasaṁjño mahāhave
ātmano vānarāṇāṁ ca yatpathyaṁ tatkariṣyati

translations.english: Else in a moment he would do the needful for himself as well as the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
मया तु मोक्षितस्यास्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
अप्रीतश्च भवेत्कष्टा कीर्तिनाशश्च शाश्वतः
verses.transliteration:
mayā tu mokṣitasyāsya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
aprītaśca bhavetkaṣṭā kīrtināśaśca śāśvataḥ

translations.english: Should the relief of the mighty-minded Sugrīva come from me, I should be incurring his displeasure and it would certainly lead to the loss of his reputation for ever; then I must wait a moment and see his own mighty displayed by himself when relieved. Meanwhile let me cheer up the monkey-host.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं चिन्तयित्वा तु हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
भूयः संस्तम्भयामास वानराणां महाचमूम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ cintayitvā tu hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
bhūyaḥ saṁstambhayāmāsa vānarāṇāṁ mahācamūm

translations.english: Thinking thus within himself, Hanumăn, that son of Maruta, began to stay the mighty host of Monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽथ विवेश लङ्कां; स्फुरन्तमादाय महाहरिं तम्
विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैः; पुष्पाग्र्यवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणः
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇo'tha viveśa laṅkāṁ; sphurantamādāya mahāhariṁ tam
vimānacaryāgṛhagopurasthaiḥ; puṣpāgryavarṣairavakīryamāṇaḥ

translations.english: In the meantime Kumbhakarņa entered Lankā with Sugrīva trembling, being honoured with the showering of beautiful flowers from the sky, the buildings on the main roads and the town-gate.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स संज्ञामुपलभ्य कृच्छ्रा;द्बलीयसस्तस्य भुजान्तरस्थः
अवेक्षमाणः पुरराजमार्गं; विचिन्तयामास मुहुर्महात्मा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa saṁjñāmupalabhya kṛcchrā;dbalīyasastasya bhujāntarasthaḥ
avekṣamāṇaḥ purarājamārgaṁ; vicintayāmāsa muhurmahātmā

translations.english: Then that mighty-minded (Sugriva), caught in the arms of the powerful Räksasa, having with difficulty come to his senses and surveying around him the streets of the town bethought himself.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं गृहीतेन कथं नु नाम; शक्यं मया संप्रति कर्तुमद्य
तथा करिष्यामि यथा हरीणां; भविष्यतीष्टं च हितं च कार्यम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ gṛhītena kathaṁ nu nāma; śakyaṁ mayā saṁprati kartumadya
tathā kariṣyāmi yathā harīṇāṁ; bhaviṣyatīṣṭaṁ ca hitaṁ ca kāryam

translations.english: When thus within the grasp of the enemy how can I take revenge? Or let me do what will be acceptable and advantageous to our army.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कराग्रैः सहसा समेत्य; राजा हरीणाममरेन्द्रशत्रोः
नखैश्च कर्णौ दशनैश्च नासां; ददंश पार्श्वेषु च कुम्भकर्णम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ karāgraiḥ sahasā sametya; rājā harīṇāmamarendraśatroḥ
nakhaiśca karṇau daśanaiśca nāsāṁ; dadaṁśa pārśveṣu ca kumbhakarṇam

translations.english: Then advancing all on a sudden, he with his nails and sharp teeth cut off the ears and nose of that lord of the enemies of the gods and split both his sides with the blow of his feet.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णौ हृतकर्णनासो; विदारितस्तेन विमर्दितश्च
रोषाभिभूतः क्षतजार्द्रगात्रः; सुग्रीवमाविध्य पिपेष भूमौ
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇau hṛtakarṇanāso; vidāritastena vimarditaśca
roṣābhibhūtaḥ kṣatajārdragātraḥ; sugrīvamāvidhya pipeṣa bhūmau

translations.english: Kumbhakarņa losing his ears and nose and having his sides split with nails and teeth grew angry, and becoming all covered over with blood, threw Sugrīva to the ground and pressed him.

verses.sanskrit:
स भूतले भीमबलाभिपिष्टः; सुरारिभिस्तैरभिहन्यमानः
जगाम खं वेगवदभ्युपेत्य; पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम
verses.transliteration:
sa bhūtale bhīmabalābhipiṣṭaḥ; surāribhistairabhihanyamānaḥ
jagāma khaṁ vegavadabhyupetya; punaśca rāmeṇa samājagāma

translations.english: Thus pressed upon the ground with main force and severely struck by the enemies of gods, he flew to the skies like a ball-rolling, and once morejoined Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्णनासा विहीनस्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
रराज शोणितोत्सिक्तो गिरिः प्रस्रवणैरिव
verses.transliteration:
karṇanāsā vihīnasya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
rarāja śoṇitotsikto giriḥ prasravaṇairiva

translations.english: The mighty Kumbhakarna having lost his nose and ears and drenched in blood, appeared like a mountain covered all over with streamlets.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स पुर्याः सहसा महात्मा; निष्क्रम्य तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्
बभक्ष रक्षो युधि कुम्भकर्णः; प्रजा युगान्ताग्निरिव प्रदीप्तः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa puryāḥ sahasā mahātmā; niṣkramya tadvānarasainyamugram
babhakṣa rakṣo yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ; prajā yugāntāgniriva pradīptaḥ

translations.english: Then that mighty-minded one, the Raksasa Kumbhakarņa, issuing out of the city began to devour the terrific host of monkeys, as do the mighty fire eat up people at the end of a Yuga.

verses.sanskrit:
बुभुक्षितः शोणितमांसगृध्नुः; प्रविश्य तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्
चखाद रक्षांसि हरीन्पिशाचा;नृक्षांश्च मोहाद्युधि कुम्भकर्णः
verses.transliteration:
bubhukṣitaḥ śoṇitamāṁsagṛdhnuḥ; praviśya tadvānarasainyamugram
cakhāda rakṣāṁsi harīnpiśācā;nṛkṣāṁśca mohādyudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ

translations.english: On entering the mighty host of monkeys, the hungry Kumbhakarna, hankering after flesh and blood, ate up the monkeys and with them, devoured many a Rākşasa and Piśāca by, mistake. Thus, as Death devour creatures at the end of a Yuga, he destroyed the mighty monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
एकं द्वौ त्रीन्बहून्क्रुद्धो वानरान्सह राक्षसैः
समादायैकहस्तेन प्रचिक्षेप त्वरन्मुखे
verses.transliteration:
ekaṁ dvau trīnbahūnkruddho vānarānsaha rākṣasaiḥ
samādāyaikahastena pracikṣepa tvaranmukhe

translations.english: He in wrath, taking up with one hand the monkeys along with the Rākṣasa, hurriedly threw them into his mouth, one, two three, or many at a time.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्रस्रवंस्तदा मेदः शोणितं च महाबलः
वध्यमानो नगेन्द्राग्रैर्भक्षयामास वानरान्
ते भक्ष्यमाणा हरयो रामं जग्मुस्तदा गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁprasravaṁstadā medaḥ śoṇitaṁ ca mahābalaḥ
vadhyamāno nagendrāgrairbhakṣayāmāsa vānarān
te bhakṣyamāṇā harayo rāmaṁ jagmustadā gatim

translations.english: And blood and fat flowed copiously down his body; and though struck by the monkeys with peaks of mountains, the mighty one devoured all those monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्काले सुमित्रायाः पुत्रः परबलार्दनः
चकार लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो युद्धं परपुरंजयः
verses.transliteration:
tasminkāle sumitrāyāḥ putraḥ parabalārdanaḥ
cakāra lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho yuddhaṁ parapuraṁjayaḥ

translations.english: At this moment, that subduer of hostile hosts and captor of the capitals of foes-Sumitra's son-Laksmana, growing enraged, entered on an encounter with the enemy.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य शराञ्शरीरे सप्त वीर्यवान्
निचखानाददे चान्यान्विससर्ज च लक्ष्मणः
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇasya śarāñśarīre sapta vīryavān
nicakhānādade cānyānvisasarja ca lakṣmaṇaḥ

translations.english: Lakşamna endued with prowess shot seven shafts at Kumbhakarma's body; and next, taking up other arrows also discharged them (at his antagonist).

verses.sanskrit:
अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिं कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
राममेवाभिदुद्राव दारयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
atikramya ca saumitriṁ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
rāmamevābhidudrāva dārayanniva medinīm

translations.english: Hearing this, that night-ranger Kumbhakarna, possessed of immense might, disregarding Laks maņa and passing beyond Sumitrā's son, rushed against Rāma, making the earth tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ दाशरथी रामो रौद्रमस्त्रं प्रयोजयन्
कुम्भकर्णस्य हृदये ससर्ज निशिताञ्शरान्
verses.transliteration:
atha dāśarathī rāmo raudramastraṁ prayojayan
kumbhakarṇasya hṛdaye sasarja niśitāñśarān

translations.english: Thereat Dasaratha's son, Rāma, employing a terrific weapon, discharged sharpened shafts at Kumbhakarņa's breast.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य रामेण विद्धस्य सहसाभिप्रधावतः
अङ्गारमिश्राः क्रुद्धस्य मुखान्निश्चेरुरर्चिषः
verses.transliteration:
tasya rāmeṇa viddhasya sahasābhipradhāvataḥ
aṅgāramiśrāḥ kruddhasya mukhānniścerurarciṣaḥ

translations.english: Thereat flames mixed with live embers shot out from the mouth of that enraged one suddenly rushing (against Răma), as Rama pierced him (with his arrows).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्योरसि निमग्नाश्च शरा बर्हिणवाससः
हस्ताच्चास्य परिभ्रष्टा पपातोर्व्यां महागदा
verses.transliteration:
tasyorasi nimagnāśca śarā barhiṇavāsasaḥ
hastāccāsya paribhraṣṭā papātorvyāṁ mahāgadā

translations.english: Those shafts adorned with peacock's plumes, alighting on (Kumbhakarna's) chest, his mace, escaping his hand, dropped to the earth; and all his (other) arms also were scattered on the ground. And when that exceedingly powerful one saw himself deprived of all his arms, he began to spread a huge havoc by means of his clenched fists and hands.

verses.sanskrit:
स बाणैरतिविद्धाङ्गः क्षतजेन समुक्षितः
रुधिरं परिसुस्राव गिरिः प्रस्रवणानिव
verses.transliteration:
sa bāṇairatividdhāṅgaḥ kṣatajena samukṣitaḥ
rudhiraṁ parisusrāva giriḥ prasravaṇāniva

translations.english: With his body entirely covered with arrows and bathed in blood, he began to bleed like a hill overflowing with fountains.

verses.sanskrit:
स तीव्रेण च कोपेन रुधिरेण च मूर्छितः
वानरान्राक्षसानृक्षान्खादन्विपरिधावति
verses.transliteration:
sa tīvreṇa ca kopena rudhireṇa ca mūrchitaḥ
vānarānrākṣasānṛkṣānkhādanviparidhāvati

translations.english: And fired with wrath and maddened with blood, he rushed on, devouring monkeys and Rākşasas and bears.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्काले स धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत्
कुम्भकर्णवधे युक्तो योगान्परिमृशन्बहून्
verses.transliteration:
tasminkāle sa dharmātmā lakṣmaṇo rāmamabravīt
kumbhakarṇavadhe yukto yogānparimṛśanbahūn

translations.english: Intent on finishing Kumbhakarņa, the virtuous Laksmana, revolving many a means, (at last) spoke to Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवायं वानरान्राजन्न विजानाति राक्षसान्
मत्तः शोणितगन्धेन स्वान्परांश्चैव खादति
verses.transliteration:
naivāyaṁ vānarānrājanna vijānāti rākṣasān
mattaḥ śoṇitagandhena svānparāṁścaiva khādati

translations.english: O king, this one know not monkeys and Rākşasas, maddened with the smell of blood, he eat up his own as well as his enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
साध्वेनमधिरोहन्तु सर्वतो वानरर्षभाः
यूथपाश्च यथामुख्यास्तिष्ठन्त्वस्य समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
sādhvenamadhirohantu sarvato vānararṣabhāḥ
yūthapāśca yathāmukhyāstiṣṭhantvasya samantataḥ

translations.english: Now let the foremost monkeys, putting forth their best mount on him; and let the leaders of bands according to their rank, stand surrounding him.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्ययं दुर्मतिः काले गुरुभारप्रपीडितः
प्रपतन्राक्षसो भूमौ नान्यान्हन्यात्प्लवंगमान्
verses.transliteration:
apyayaṁ durmatiḥ kāle gurubhāraprapīḍitaḥ
prapatanrākṣaso bhūmau nānyānhanyātplavaṁgamān

translations.english: Then today this wicked-minded Rākşasa, oppressed with a mighty weight, will no longer be able to eat up any more monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः
ते समारुरुहुर्हृष्टाः कुम्भकर्णं प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ
te samāruruhurhṛṣṭāḥ kumbhakarṇaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of the intelligent prince, those exceedingly powerful monkeys with alacrity ascended Kumbhakarņa.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णस्तु संक्रुद्धः समारूढः प्लवंगमैः
व्यधूनयत्तान्वेगेन दुष्टहस्तीव हस्तिपान्
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇastu saṁkruddhaḥ samārūḍhaḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ
vyadhūnayattānvegena duṣṭahastīva hastipān

translations.english: Kumbhakarna mounted by those monkeys, waxing exceedingly enraged, shook them vehemently, even as mad elephants shake the drivers thereof,

verses.sanskrit:
तान्दृष्ट्वा निर्धूतान्रामो रुष्टोऽयमिति राक्षसः
समुत्पपात वेगेन धनुरुत्तममाददे
verses.transliteration:
tāndṛṣṭvā nirdhūtānrāmo ruṣṭo'yamiti rākṣasaḥ
samutpapāta vegena dhanuruttamamādade

translations.english: Rāghava seeing them shaken, and concluding the Rāksasa to be wroth, furiously sprang forward, taking his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
स चापमादाय भुजंगकल्पं; दृढज्यमुग्रं तपनीयचित्रम्
हरीन्समाश्वास्य समुत्पपात; रामो निबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः
verses.transliteration:
sa cāpamādāya bhujaṁgakalpaṁ; dṛḍhajyamugraṁ tapanīyacitram
harīnsamāśvāsya samutpapāta; rāmo nibaddhottamatūṇabāṇaḥ

translations.english: And equipped with an excellent quiver and arrows, Rāma checring up the monkeys sprang forward, taking a bow, resembling a serpent; terrific; having a stout string; and embellished in gold.

verses.sanskrit:
स वानरगणैस्तैस्तु वृतः परमदुर्जयः
लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामः संप्रतस्थे महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa vānaragaṇaistaistu vṛtaḥ paramadurjayaḥ
lakṣmaṇānucaro rāmaḥ saṁpratasthe mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Then surrounded by exceedingly invincible monkey-bands, that highly powerful hero, followed by Laksmana, marched forth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं प्रदीप्तानलवर्चसं
विस्फारयामास तदा कार्मुकं पुरुषर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṁ pradīptānalavarcasaṁ
visphārayāmāsa tadā kārmukaṁ puruṣarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: That best of persons, seeing that foremost of Rākṣasas having the splendour of a living fire, stretched his bow to its full bent.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य चापनिर्घोषात्कुपितो नैरृतर्षभः
अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमभिदुद्राव राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya cāpanirghoṣātkupito nairṛtarṣabhaḥ
amṛṣyamāṇastaṁ ghoṣamabhidudrāva rāghavam

translations.english: And fired with wrath at the twang of his bow, that foremost of Raksasas, inflamed with wrath, not brooking that report, rushed against Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु वातोद्धतमेघकल्पं; भुजंगराजोत्तमभोगबाहुम्
तमापतन्तं धरणीधराभ;मुवाच रामो युधि कुम्भकर्णम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu vātoddhatameghakalpaṁ; bhujaṁgarājottamabhogabāhum
tamāpatantaṁ dharaṇīdharābha;muvāca rāmo yudhi kumbhakarṇam

translations.english: Thereat, the gentle Rāma, endowed with arms resembling the body of the sovereign of serpents, in that encounter addressed Kumbhakarņa, like to an elevated cloud and possessed of the splendour of a mountain, as he darted forward, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
आगच्छ रक्षोऽधिपमा विषाद;मवस्थितोऽहं प्रगृहीतचापः
अवेहि मां शक्रसपत्न राम;मयं मुहूर्ताद्भविता विचेताः
verses.transliteration:
āgaccha rakṣo'dhipamā viṣāda;mavasthito'haṁ pragṛhītacāpaḥ
avehi māṁ śakrasapatna rāma;mayaṁ muhūrtādbhavitā vicetāḥ

translations.english: Come, O king of Rākşasa! Let no grief be your! Here I stay, taking my bow in my hand. Know me for the destroyer of the race of the Rākṣasas—you who in a moment shall be deprived of your senses.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहस्य विकृतं भीमं स मेघस्वनितोपमम्
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
prahasya vikṛtaṁ bhīmaṁ sa meghasvanitopamam
kumbhakarṇo mahātejā rāghavaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: As if riving the breasts of all the monkeys (present) the exceedingly energetic Kumbhakarņa, laughing frightfully and in a terrific manner, resembling the rumbling of clouds, addressed Rāghava, saying, “Take me not for Virādha, or for Kabandha, or yet for Khara. I am not Vāli or Mārīca. I am Kumbhakarma, that am come.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य मे मुद्गरं घोरं सर्वकालायसं महत्
अनेन निर्जिता देवा दानवाश्च मया पुरा
verses.transliteration:
paśya me mudgaraṁ ghoraṁ sarvakālāyasaṁ mahat
anena nirjitā devā dānavāśca mayā purā

translations.english: Behold my dreadful and mighty mace entirely made of iron. By help of this I had formerly brought down deities and Dänavas.

verses.sanskrit:
विकर्णनास इति मां नावज्ञातुं त्वमर्हसि
स्वल्पापि हि न मे पीडा कर्णनासाविनाशनात्
verses.transliteration:
vikarṇanāsa iti māṁ nāvajñātuṁ tvamarhasi
svalpāpi hi na me pīḍā karṇanāsāvināśanāt

translations.english: It does not behove you to scorn me in that my nose has been severed. I do not feel any the smallest torment in consequence of my ears and nose having been cut off.

verses.sanskrit:
दर्शयेक्ष्वाकुशार्दूल वीर्यं गात्रेषु मे लघु
ततस्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि दृष्टपौरुषविक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
darśayekṣvākuśārdūla vīryaṁ gātreṣu me laghu
tatastvāṁ bhakṣayiṣyāmi dṛṣṭapauruṣavikramam

translations.english: O tiger of the Ikşvāku line, O sinless one, do you witness the prowess that is in my frame. And thereafter, when you shall have displayed your prowess and power, shall I devour you up.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य; रामः सुपुङ्खान्विससर्ज बाणान्
तैराहतो वज्रसमप्रवेगै;र्न चुक्षुभे न व्यथते सुरारिः
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya; rāmaḥ supuṅkhānvisasarja bāṇān
tairāhato vajrasamapravegai;rna cukṣubhe na vyathate surāriḥ

translations.english: Hearing Kumbhakarna's words, Rama discharged (at him) shafts furnished with knobs. And smite with these having the impetus of the thunder-bolt, the foe of the celestials did not feel any pain or sinart.

verses.sanskrit:
यैः सायकैः सालवरा निकृत्ता; वाली हतो वानरपुंगवश्च
ते कुम्भकर्णस्य तदा शरीरं; वज्रोपमा न व्यथयां प्रचक्रुः
verses.transliteration:
yaiḥ sāyakaiḥ sālavarā nikṛttā; vālī hato vānarapuṁgavaśca
te kumbhakarṇasya tadā śarīraṁ; vajropamā na vyathayāṁ pracakruḥ

translations.english: Those shafts which had severed the seven stately salas, and, to boot, had slain Vāli—best of monkeys, they resembling the thunder itselfcould not impart any pain to Kumbhakarņa's body.

verses.sanskrit:
स वारिधारा इव सायकांस्ता;न्पिबञ्शरीरेण महेन्द्रशत्रुः
जघान रामस्य शरप्रवेगं; व्याविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगम्
verses.transliteration:
sa vāridhārā iva sāyakāṁstā;npibañśarīreṇa mahendraśatruḥ
jaghāna rāmasya śarapravegaṁ; vyāvidhya taṁ mudgaramugravegam

translations.english: Drinking up in his body those arrows resembling a shower, the enemy of the great Indra whirling his mace possessed of fierce ventinence, put out the arrowy discharge of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु रक्षः क्षतजानुलिप्तं; वित्रासनं देवमहाचमूनाम्
व्याविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगं; विद्रावयामास चमूं हरीणाम्
verses.transliteration:
tatastu rakṣaḥ kṣatajānuliptaṁ; vitrāsanaṁ devamahācamūnām
vyāvidhya taṁ mudgaramugravegaṁ; vidrāvayāmāsa camūṁ harīṇām

translations.english: Then that Rākşasa whirling his mace washed in blood, capable of striking terror into the mighty hosts of gods and Dānavas, and possessed of fierce impetus, made the monkeyarmy take to its heels.

verses.sanskrit:
वायव्यमादाय ततो वरास्त्रं; रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय
समुद्गरं तेन जहार बाहुं; स कृत्तबाहुस्तुमुलं ननाद
verses.transliteration:
vāyavyamādāya tato varāstraṁ; rāmaḥ pracikṣepa niśācarāya
samudgaraṁ tena jahāra bāhuṁ; sa kṛttabāhustumulaṁ nanāda

translations.english: Then Rāma, taking a trighty Vāyavya weapon, used the same against the night-ranger; and cut off his arm with the mace. And having his arm cut off, he set up tremendousrears.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य बाहुर्गिरिशृङ्गकल्पः; समुद्गरो राघवबाणकृत्तः
पपात तस्मिन्हरिराजसैन्ये; जघान तां वानरवाहिनीं च
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya bāhurgiriśṛṅgakalpaḥ; samudgaro rāghavabāṇakṛttaḥ
papāta tasminharirājasainye; jaghāna tāṁ vānaravāhinīṁ ca

translations.english: And his arm with the mace, resembling a mountain-peak, cut off by Rāghava's arrows, fell in the midst of the army of the monkey-king, and destroyed that army,* * This, or course, is not to be taken literally.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वानरा भग्नहतावशेषाः; पर्यन्तमाश्रित्य तदा विषण्णाः
प्रवेपिताङ्गा ददृशुः सुघोरं; नरेन्द्ररक्षोऽधिपसंनिपातम्
verses.transliteration:
te vānarā bhagnahatāvaśeṣāḥ; paryantamāśritya tadā viṣaṇṇāḥ
pravepitāṅgā dadṛśuḥ sughoraṁ; narendrarakṣo'dhipasaṁnipātam

translations.english: Thereat the monkeys remaining after those broken and slain, dispirited, and having their limbs wounded, moving aside, looked on the dreadfiil encounter between the Rākşasa and the lord of men.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहु;र्महान्निकृत्ताग्र इवाचलेन्द्रः
उत्पाटयामास करेण वृक्षं; ततोऽभिदुद्राव रणे नरेन्द्रम्
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇo'stranikṛttabāhu;rmahānnikṛttāgra ivācalendraḥ
utpāṭayāmāsa kareṇa vṛkṣaṁ; tato'bhidudrāva raṇe narendram

translations.english: Then Kumbhakarma, having his arm severed, resembling the foremost of mountains with its crest hewn away by a mighty sabre, tore up a tree with his (remaining) arm and in the conflict rushed against the monarch of men.

verses.sanskrit:
तं तस्य बाहुं सह सालवृक्षं; समुद्यतं पन्नगभोगकल्पम्
ऐन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेन जहार रामो; बाणेन जाम्बूनदचित्रितेन
verses.transliteration:
taṁ tasya bāhuṁ saha sālavṛkṣaṁ; samudyataṁ pannagabhogakalpam
aindrāstrayuktena jahāra rāmo; bāṇena jāmbūnadacitritena

translations.english: Thereupon with a shaft plated in gold, set upon a weapon of Indra, Rāma cut off his uplifted arm with a palm tree, looking like the body of a pannaga.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजो निकृत्तः; पपात भूमौ गिरिसंनिकाशः
विवेष्टमानो निजघान वृक्षा;ञ्शैलाञ्शिलावानरराक्षसांश्च
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇasya bhujo nikṛttaḥ; papāta bhūmau girisaṁnikāśaḥ
viveṣṭamāno nijaghāna vṛkṣā;ñśailāñśilāvānararākṣasāṁśca

translations.english: That arm of Kumbhakarma, being severed, dropped inert on the earth, like a hill, and crushed trees and rocks and crags and monkeys and Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तं छिन्नबाहुं समवेक्ष्य रामः; समापतन्तं सहसा नदन्तम्
द्वावर्धचन्द्रौ निशितौ प्रगृह्य; चिच्छेद पादौ युधि राक्षसस्य
verses.transliteration:
taṁ chinnabāhuṁ samavekṣya rāmaḥ; samāpatantaṁ sahasā nadantam
dvāvardhacandrau niśitau pragṛhya; ciccheda pādau yudhi rākṣasasya

translations.english: Rāma, seeing that one shorn of his arms suddenly spring up, roaring, took up two whetted crescents, and in the contest cut off the legs of the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
निकृत्तबाहुर्विनिकृत्तपादो; विदार्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभम्
दुद्राव रामं सहसाभिगर्ज;न्राहुर्यथा चन्द्रमिवान्तरिक्षे
verses.transliteration:
nikṛttabāhurvinikṛttapādo; vidārya vaktraṁ vaḍavāmukhābham
dudrāva rāmaṁ sahasābhigarja;nrāhuryathā candramivāntarikṣe

translations.english: Having his arms cut off and his legs also severed, (Kumbhakarma), opening wide his mouth resembling in sheen the mouth of a mare, roaring swiftly darted against Rāghava, even as Rāhu pursue the Moon in the firmament.

verses.sanskrit:
अपूरयत्तस्य मुखं शिताग्रै; रामः शरैर्हेमपिनद्धपुङ्खैः
स पूर्णवक्त्रो न शशाक वक्तुं; चुकूज कृच्छ्रेण मुमोह चापि
verses.transliteration:
apūrayattasya mukhaṁ śitāgrai; rāmaḥ śarairhemapinaddhapuṅkhaiḥ
sa pūrṇavaktro na śaśāka vaktuṁ; cukūja kṛcchreṇa mumoha cāpi

translations.english: Then Rama stuffed his mouth full of sharpened shafts having their feathered parts furnished with gold. And having his mouth filled, he could not articulate; but with extreme effort uttered indistinct accents and swooned away.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वज्रजाम्बूनदचारुपुङ्खं; प्रदीप्तसूर्यज्वलनप्रकाशम्
महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यवेगं; रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vajrajāmbūnadacārupuṅkhaṁ; pradīptasūryajvalanaprakāśam
mahendravajrāśanitulyavegaṁ; rāmaḥ pracikṣepa niśācarāya

translations.english: Then Rāma took an arrow of Indra, whetted and knobbed, impetuous as the wind, resembling the effulgence of the Sun, and like to the very banner of Brahmā, or the destroyer himself; and fatal to foes. And then Rāma hurled it at the ranger of the night.

verses.sanskrit:
स सायको राघवबाहुचोदितो; दिशः स्वभासा दश संप्रकाशयन्
विधूमवैश्वानरदीप्तदर्शनो; जगाम शक्राशनितुल्यविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
sa sāyako rāghavabāhucodito; diśaḥ svabhāsā daśa saṁprakāśayan
vidhūmavaiśvānaradīptadarśano; jagāma śakrāśanitulyavikramaḥ

translations.english: Thereat that weapon hurled by Rāma's arm, resembling a smokeless flame, lighting up the ten cardinal points with its own glory, saught him that was possessed of the dreadful energy of Sakra's thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
स तन्महापर्वतकूटसंनिभं; विवृत्तदंष्ट्रं चलचारुकुण्डलम्
चकर्त रक्षोऽधिपतेः शिरस्तदा; यथैव वृत्रस्य पुरा पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
sa tanmahāparvatakūṭasaṁnibhaṁ; vivṛttadaṁṣṭraṁ calacārukuṇḍalam
cakarta rakṣo'dhipateḥ śirastadā; yathaiva vṛtrasya purā puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: Therewith he (Rāma) cut off the head of the lord of Räkşasa resembling a mountain-summit, furnished with prominent teeth, from which the ear-rings had fallen off, even as formerly Purandara had cut off the head of Vſtra.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्रामबाणाभिहतं पपात; रक्षःशिरः पर्वतसंनिकाशम्
बभञ्ज चर्यागृहगोपुराणि; प्राकारमुच्चं तमपातयच्च
verses.transliteration:
tadrāmabāṇābhihataṁ papāta; rakṣaḥśiraḥ parvatasaṁnikāśam
babhañja caryāgṛhagopurāṇi; prākāramuccaṁ tamapātayacca

translations.english: And struck with Rāma's arrow, the head of the Rākşasa resembling a hill fell down to the earth; and (in its fall) crushed edifices on the highways and gateways; and elevated walls also it bore down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्चातिकायं हिमवत्प्रकाशं; रक्षस्तदा तोयनिधौ पपात
ग्राहान्महामीनचयान्भुजंगमा;न्ममर्द भूमिं च तथा विवेश
verses.transliteration:
taccātikāyaṁ himavatprakāśaṁ; rakṣastadā toyanidhau papāta
grāhānmahāmīnacayānbhujaṁgamā;nmamarda bhūmiṁ ca tathā viveśa

translations.english: Then that Rākşasa of gigantic proportions and vast to the view plunged into the deep; and crushing huge and mighty fishes and serpents, saught the depths.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिर्हते ब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौ; महाबले संयति कुम्भकर्णे
चचाल भूर्भूमिधराश्च सर्वे; हर्षाच्च देवास्तुमुलं प्रणेदुः
verses.transliteration:
tasmirhate brāhmaṇadevaśatrau; mahābale saṁyati kumbhakarṇe
cacāla bhūrbhūmidharāśca sarve; harṣācca devāstumulaṁ praṇeduḥ

translations.english: On that enemy of the Brāhmanas and gods, endowed with immense strength, having been slain in battle, the earth shook and the mountains also; and from excess of joy the celestials shouted aloud.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु देवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाः; सुराश्च भूतानि सुपर्णगुह्यकाः
सयक्षगन्धर्वगणा नभोगताः; प्रहर्षिता राम पराक्रमेण
verses.transliteration:
tatastu devarṣimaharṣipannagāḥ; surāśca bhūtāni suparṇaguhyakāḥ
sayakṣagandharvagaṇā nabhogatāḥ; praharṣitā rāma parākrameṇa

translations.english: Those deities and saints and Maharsis and Pannagas, and celestials and (other), beings and birds and Guhyakas, together with Yakşas and Gandharvas, all these who had stationed themselves in the welkin, were rejoiced at the prowess of Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहर्षमीयुर्बहवस्तु वानराः; प्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमैरिवाननैः
अपूजयन्राघवमिष्टभागिनं; हते रिपौ भीमबले दुरासदे
verses.transliteration:
praharṣamīyurbahavastu vānarāḥ; prabuddhapadmapratimairivānanaiḥ
apūjayanrāghavamiṣṭabhāginaṁ; hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade

translations.english: And countless monkeys experienced the very height of delight; and on (their) foe of terrific strength having been slain, they with countenances resembling awaked lotuses paid homage to the king's son-Rāghava—the sharer of good fortune.

verses.sanskrit:
स कुम्भकर्णं सुरसैन्यमर्दनं; महत्सु युद्धेष्वपराजितश्रमम्
ननन्द हत्वा भरताग्रजो रणे; महासुरं वृत्रमिवामराधिपः
verses.transliteration:
sa kumbhakarṇaṁ surasainyamardanaṁ; mahatsu yuddheṣvaparājitaśramam
nananda hatvā bharatāgrajo raṇe; mahāsuraṁ vṛtramivāmarādhipaḥ

translations.english: As the monarch of the immortals had rejoiced on slaying the mighty Asura Vrtra-Bharata's elder brother rejoiced on having in battle slain that smiter of celestial hosts, Kumbhakarna in mighty conflict, never (before) vanquished in renowned encounters.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णं हतं दृष्ट्वा राघवेण महात्मना
राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇaṁ hataṁ dṛṣṭvā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
rākṣasā rākṣasendrāya rāvaṇāya nyavedayan

translations.english: Seeing Kumbhakarņa slain by the high-souled Rāghava, the Räkşasas conveyed the tidings to the lord of the Raksasas-Ravana; (and addressed him, saying)

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा विनिहतं संख्ये कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्
रावणः शोकसंतप्तो मुमोह च पपात च
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā vinihataṁ saṁkhye kumbhakarṇaṁ mahābalam
rāvaṇaḥ śokasaṁtapto mumoha ca papāta ca

translations.english: Hearing the mighty Kumbhakarņa slain in battle, Ravana burning in grief, swooned away and dropped to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
पितृव्यं निहतं श्रुत्वा देवान्तकनरान्तकौ
त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च रुरुदुः शोकपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
pitṛvyaṁ nihataṁ śrutvā devāntakanarāntakau
triśirāścātikāyaśca ruruduḥ śokapīḍitāḥ

translations.english: Hearing their uncle slain, Trisiras* and Atikāya-destroyers of gods and men, began to weep, oppressed with sorrow. *Three-headed.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातरं निहतं श्रुत्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
महोदरमहापार्श्वौ शोकाक्रान्तौ बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration:
bhrātaraṁ nihataṁ śrutvā rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
mahodaramahāpārśvau śokākrāntau babhūvatuḥ

translations.english: Mahodara' and Mahāpārśvahearing of their uncle slain by Rāma of untiring deeds, were overcome with grief. 1. Huge-bellied. 2. Mighty flanked.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृच्छ्रात्समासाद्य संज्ञां राक्षसपुंगवः
कुम्भकर्णवधाद्दीनो विललाप स रावणः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛcchrātsamāsādya saṁjñāṁ rākṣasapuṁgavaḥ
kumbhakarṇavadhāddīno vilalāpa sa rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then regaining his senses with extreme exertion, that foremost of Rākṣasas, distressed in consequence of the destruction of Kumbhakarna, mourned with his senses overwhelmed, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
हा वीर रिपुदर्पघ्न कुम्भकर्ण महाबल
शत्रुसैन्यं प्रताप्यैकः क्व मां संत्यज्य गच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
hā vīra ripudarpaghna kumbhakarṇa mahābala
śatrusainyaṁ pratāpyaikaḥ kva māṁ saṁtyajya gacchasi

translations.english: O exceedingly powerful one, leaving me (alone) whither did you wend, without extracting my dart as well as that of your friends?

verses.sanskrit:
इदानीं खल्वहं नास्मि यस्य मे पतितो भुजः
दक्षिणो यं समाश्रित्य न बिभेमि सुरासुरान्
verses.transliteration:
idānīṁ khalvahaṁ nāsmi yasya me patito bhujaḥ
dakṣiṇo yaṁ samāśritya na bibhemi surāsurān

translations.english: Now really I am not, inasmuch as my right arm has dropped. Backed by this one, I would not fear celestials and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
कथमेवंविधो वीरो देवदानवदर्पहा
कालाग्निप्रतिमो ह्यद्य राघवेण रणे हतः
verses.transliteration:
kathamevaṁvidho vīro devadānavadarpahā
kālāgnipratimo hyadya rāghaveṇa raṇe hataḥ

translations.english: How today forsooth has such a hero-crusher of the hauteur of gods and Dänavas—resembling the fire arisen at the hour of universal wreck, been slain in fight by Raghava?

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य ते वज्रनिष्पेषो न कुर्याद्व्यसनं सदा
स कथं रामबाणार्तः प्रसुप्तोऽसि महीतले
verses.transliteration:
yasya te vajraniṣpeṣo na kuryādvyasanaṁ sadā
sa kathaṁ rāmabāṇārtaḥ prasupto'si mahītale

translations.english: He who could not be harmed by the concussion of the thunder-bolt itself-how can he, smitten with Rāma's arrows, sleep soundly on the earth?

verses.sanskrit:
एते देवगणाः सार्धमृषिभिर्गगने स्थिताः
निहतं त्वां रणे दृष्ट्वा निनदन्ति प्रहर्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
ete devagaṇāḥ sārdhamṛṣibhirgagane sthitāḥ
nihataṁ tvāṁ raṇe dṛṣṭvā ninadanti praharṣitāḥ

translations.english: These gods stationed in the sky along with the saints, beholding you slain the battle, are shouting in glee.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रुवमद्यैव संहृष्टा लब्धलक्ष्याः प्लवंगमाः
आरोक्ष्यन्तीह दुर्गाणि लङ्काद्वाराणि सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
dhruvamadyaiva saṁhṛṣṭā labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
ārokṣyantīha durgāṇi laṅkādvārāṇi sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Surely today the monkeys overjoyed, finding occasion, well scale all the gateways and fortifications of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्येन नास्ति मे कार्यं किं करिष्यामि सीतया
कुम्भकर्णविहीनस्य जीविते नास्ति मे रतिः
verses.transliteration:
rājyena nāsti me kāryaṁ kiṁ kariṣyāmi sītayā
kumbhakarṇavihīnasya jīvite nāsti me ratiḥ

translations.english: I have nothing to do with empire. And what shall I do with Sītā? And deprived of Kumbhakarma, I do not even wish to live.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यहं भ्रातृहन्तारं न हन्मि युधि राघवम्
ननु मे मरणं श्रेयो न चेदं व्यर्थजीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
yadyahaṁ bhrātṛhantāraṁ na hanmi yudhi rāghavam
nanu me maraṇaṁ śreyo na cedaṁ vyarthajīvitam

translations.english: If I do not slay in encounter that slayer of my brother-Rāghava, certainly death is even that which is good for me, otherwise, this life is useless.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यैव तं गमिष्यामि देशं यत्रानुजो मम
न हि भ्रातॄन्समुत्सृज्य क्षणं जीवितुमुत्सहे
verses.transliteration:
adyaiva taṁ gamiṣyāmi deśaṁ yatrānujo mama
na hi bhrātṝnsamutsṛjya kṣaṇaṁ jīvitumutsahe

translations.english: This very day will I repair to that place where my younger brother is. Forsaking my brother, I forsooth dare not live for a moment.

verses.sanskrit:
देवा हि मां हसिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा पूर्वापकारिणम्
कथमिन्द्रं जयिष्यामि कुम्भकर्णहते त्वयि
verses.transliteration:
devā hi māṁ hasiṣyanti dṛṣṭvā pūrvāpakāriṇam
kathamindraṁ jayiṣyāmi kumbhakarṇahate tvayi

translations.english: For the gods shall laugh on seeing me, who had formerly wronged them. But, how, O Kumbhakarņa, you having been slain, shall I conquer Indra?

verses.sanskrit:
तदिदं मामनुप्राप्तं विभीषणवचः शुभम्
यदज्ञानान्मया तस्य न गृहीतं महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
tadidaṁ māmanuprāptaṁ vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śubham
yadajñānānmayā tasya na gṛhītaṁ mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Now the beneficial words of Vibhīşaņa have been verified. And as through blindness I did not accept the advice of that high-souled one, Kumbhakarņa and of Prahasta, this disaster arisen, shame me sore.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यायं कर्मणः प्रातो विपाको मम शोकदः
यन्मया धार्मिकः श्रीमान्स निरस्तो विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāyaṁ karmaṇaḥ prāto vipāko mama śokadaḥ
yanmayā dhārmikaḥ śrīmānsa nirasto vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: As I had disgraced the virtuous and graceful Vibhīşaņa, this peril producing grief, has been the consequence of my conduct.

verses.sanskrit:
इति बहुविधमाकुलान्तरात्मा; कृपणमतीव विलप्य कुम्भकर्णम्
न्यपतदथ दशाननो भृशार्त;स्तमनुजमिन्द्ररिपुं हतं विदित्वा
verses.transliteration:
iti bahuvidhamākulāntarātmā; kṛpaṇamatīva vilapya kumbhakarṇam
nyapatadatha daśānano bhṛśārta;stamanujamindraripuṁ hataṁ viditvā

translations.english: Having thus piteously and long lamented Kumbhakarna, the Ten-necked one, with his inmost soul overwhelmed with sorrow, and sore distressed in consequence of grief, fell down, knowing his brother—the enemy of Indra-slain in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विलपमानस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
श्रुत्वा शोकाभितप्तस्य त्रिशिरा वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vilapamānasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
śrutvā śokābhitaptasya triśirā vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the lamentations of the wickedminded Ravana, overwhelmed with grief, Trisiras addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेव महावीर्यो हतो नस्तात मध्यमः
न तु सत्पुरुषा राजन्विलपन्ति यथा भवान्
verses.transliteration:
evameva mahāvīryo hato nastāta madhyamaḥ
na tu satpuruṣā rājanvilapanti yathā bhavān

translations.english: O Sire, this second uncle to us possessed of mighty prowess has* forsooth been slain in fight. But, О king, heroes never indulge in grief as youdoes. as *Evameva-forsooth, I render it. The commentator, however, says it means such as you have described him.

verses.sanskrit:
नूनं त्रिभुवणस्यापि पर्याप्तस्त्वमसि प्रभो
स कस्मात्प्राकृत इव शोकस्यात्मानमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
nūnaṁ tribhuvaṇasyāpi paryāptastvamasi prabho
sa kasmātprākṛta iva śokasyātmānamīdṛśam

translations.english: O lord, you certainly alone are competent to conquer the triple world. Wherefore then did you went such sorrow like an ignoble one?

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मदत्तास्ति ते शक्तिः कवचः सायको धनुः
सहस्रखरसंयुक्तो रथो मेघसमस्वनः
verses.transliteration:
brahmadattāsti te śaktiḥ kavacaḥ sāyako dhanuḥ
sahasrakharasaṁyukto ratho meghasamasvanaḥ

translations.english: You have your dart conferred on you by Brahmā; and your mail and your weapon—the bow-and your car yoked with a thousand asses, sending forth clatter resembling the rumbling of clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयासकृद्विशस्त्रेण विशस्ता देवदानवाः
स सर्वायुधसंपन्नो राघवं शास्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tvayāsakṛdviśastreṇa viśastā devadānavāḥ
sa sarvāyudhasaṁpanno rāghavaṁ śāstumarhasi

translations.english: The deities and the Dănavas have by means of your arms been terrified over and over again. And furnished with all arms, you ought to chastise Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
कामं तिष्ठ महाराजनिर्गमिष्याम्यहं रणम्
उद्धरिष्यामि ते शत्रून्गरुडः पन्नगानिह
verses.transliteration:
kāmaṁ tiṣṭha mahārājanirgamiṣyāmyahaṁ raṇam
uddhariṣyāmi te śatrūngaruḍaḥ pannagāniha

translations.english: But stay at your pleasure, O mighty sovereign, I will go out to battle; and even as Garuda capture serpents, will I capture your enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
शम्बरो देवराजेन नरको विष्णुना यथा
तथाद्य शयिता रामो मया युधि निपातितः
verses.transliteration:
śambaro devarājena narako viṣṇunā yathā
tathādya śayitā rāmo mayā yudhi nipātitaḥ

translations.english: As Sambara was vanquished by the lord of the immortals, or Naraka by Visnu, will I bringing down Rāma in battle make him sleep (in the field).

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā triśiraso vākyaṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
punarjātamivātmānaṁ manyate kālacoditaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Triſiras words Rāvana-lord of Rākşasas-urged on by fate, considered himself as having regained his life.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं देवान्तकनरान्तकौ
अतिकायश्च तेजस्वी बभूवुर्युद्धहर्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā triśiraso vākyaṁ devāntakanarāntakau
atikāyaśca tejasvī babhūvuryuddhaharṣitāḥ

translations.english: Hearing the speech of Triģiras, Devāntaka, and Narāntaka, and the energetic Atikāya also, were wrought up with martial enthusiam.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहमहमित्येवं गर्जन्तो नैरृतर्षभाः
रावणस्य सुता वीराः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
tato'hamahamityevaṁ garjanto nairṛtarṣabhāḥ
rāvaṇasya sutā vīrāḥ śakratulyaparākramāḥ

translations.english: Then those foremost of Naiſtas-the heroic sons of Rāvaņa-endowed with the prowess of Sakra himself-roared out, I will go,' 'I will go.' or

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षचराः सर्वे सर्वे माया विशारदाः
सर्वे त्रिदशदर्पघ्नाः सर्वे च रणदुर्मदाः
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣacarāḥ sarve sarve māyā viśāradāḥ
sarve tridaśadarpaghnāḥ sarve ca raṇadurmadāḥ

translations.english: All could range the sky, and all were skilled in illusion, and all were crushers of the pride of the immortals; and all were irresistible in encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेऽस्त्रविदुषो वीराः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः
सर्वे प्रवरजिज्ञानाः सर्वे लब्धवरास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
sarve'straviduṣo vīrāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
sarve pravarajijñānāḥ sarve labdhavarāstathā

translations.english: All of them were endowed with superior strength, and all had achieved wide celebrity. They had never been heard of as having been beaten in fight even by the gods along with the Gandharvas, the mighty serpents accompanied by the Kinnaras. And all were skilled in weapons and heroic; and all were versed in werfare. And all were possessed of the higher knowledge; and all had obtained boons.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैस्तथा भास्करतुल्यवर्चसैः; सुतैर्वृतः शत्रुबलप्रमर्दनैः
रराज राजा मघवान्यथामरै;र्वृतो महादानवदर्पनाशनैः
verses.transliteration:
sa taistathā bhāskaratulyavarcasaiḥ; sutairvṛtaḥ śatrubalapramardanaiḥ
rarāja rājā maghavānyathāmarai;rvṛto mahādānavadarpanāśanaiḥ

translations.english: Then the king surrounded by those sons of his, appearing like celestials, capable of injuring the force and fortune of the foes, looked splendid like Maghavan environed by the immortals, humblers of the hauteur of mighty Danavas.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुत्रान्संपरिष्वज्य भूषयित्वा च भूषणैः
आशीर्भिश्च प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
sa putrānsaṁpariṣvajya bhūṣayitvā ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
āśīrbhiśca praśastābhiḥ preṣayāmāsa saṁyuge

translations.english: Embracing his sons and adorning them in ornaments, he sent them to the field with his best benedictions.

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरमहापार्श्वौ भ्रातरौ चापि रावणः
रक्षणार्थं कुमाराणां प्रेषयामास संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
mahodaramahāpārśvau bhrātarau cāpi rāvaṇaḥ
rakṣaṇārthaṁ kumārāṇāṁ preṣayāmāsa saṁyuge

translations.english: Rävaņa sent the brothers, Yudhyonmatta and Matta, for protecting the princes in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं रावणं रिपुरावणम्
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं चैव महाकायाः प्रतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
te'bhivādya mahātmānaṁ rāvaṇaṁ ripurāvaṇam
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṁ caiva mahākāyāḥ pratasthire

translations.english: Then, saluting the high-souled Ravanadestroyer of creatures, and going round him, those huge-bodied ones marched forth.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वौषधीभिर्गन्धैश्च समालभ्य महाबलाः
निर्जग्मुर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठाः षडेते युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः
verses.transliteration:
sarvauṣadhībhirgandhaiśca samālabhya mahābalāḥ
nirjagmurnairṛtaśreṣṭhāḥ ṣaḍete yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

translations.english: And furnished with every description of medicinal herbs and perfumes, these six Nairtas-foremost of their kind endowed with great strength, burning for battle, marched forth, Triširas and Atikāya, and Devântaka and Narāntaka, and Mahodara and Mahāpāśva went out, urged on by Fate.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुदर्शनं नाम नीलजीमूतसंनिभम्
ऐरावतकुले जातमारुरोह महोदरः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sudarśanaṁ nāma nīlajīmūtasaṁnibham
airāvatakule jātamāruroha mahodaraḥ

translations.english: Then Mahodara mounted the elephant Sudarsana-sprung in the race of Airāvata, and resembling dark-blue clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वायुधसमायुक्तं तूणीभिश्च स्वलंकृतम्
रराज गजमास्थाय सवितेवास्तमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
sarvāyudhasamāyuktaṁ tūṇībhiśca svalaṁkṛtam
rarāja gajamāsthāya savitevāstamūrdhani

translations.english: Accoutred in every weapon, and decked with quivers, he looked splendid on his elephant like the Sun ascending the crest of the Setting-hill.

verses.sanskrit:
हयोत्तमसमायुक्तं सर्वायुधसमाकुलम्
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
hayottamasamāyuktaṁ sarvāyudhasamākulam
āruroha rathaśreṣṭhaṁ triśirā rāvaṇātmajaḥ

translations.english: Ravana's son-Trisiras, ascended a car yoked with excellent steeds, and furnished with every variety of arms.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिशिरा रथमास्थाय विरराज धनुर्धरः
सविद्युदुल्कः सज्वालः सेन्द्रचाप इवाम्बुदः
verses.transliteration:
triśirā rathamāsthāya virarāja dhanurdharaḥ
savidyudulkaḥ sajvālaḥ sendracāpa ivāmbudaḥ
