translations.english: Having ascended the car, Trisiras bow in hand appeared beautiful like a mass of burning clouds having lightning and meteors, and crowned with Indra's bow.. *The rain-bow is called sometimes Indra's bow and at others Rama's bow.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिभिः किरीटैस्त्रिशिराः शुशुभे स रथोत्तमे
हिमवानिव शैलेन्द्रस्त्रिभिः काञ्चनपर्वतैः
verses.transliteration:
tribhiḥ kirīṭaistriśirāḥ śuśubhe sa rathottame
himavāniva śailendrastribhiḥ kāñcanaparvataiḥ

translations.english: Dight with three diadems, Trisiras looked splendid in that superb car, like the monarch of mountains Himavān—with the three golden hills.

verses.sanskrit:
सुचक्राक्षं सुसंयुक्तं सानुकर्षं सकूबरम्
तूणीबाणासनैर्दीप्तं प्रासासि परिघाकुलम्
verses.transliteration:
sucakrākṣaṁ susaṁyuktaṁ sānukarṣaṁ sakūbaram
tūṇībāṇāsanairdīptaṁ prāsāsi parighākulam

translations.english: Then that foremost of all bowmen-the powerful Atikāya-son to the lord of Raksasas-ascended the best of cars, having excellent wheels and akşas, and yoked with excellent steeds, and furnished with bottoms and holes; flaming with quivers and bows; and bristling with prāścas and swords and blugdeons.

verses.sanskrit:
स काञ्चनविचित्रेण किरीटेन विराजता
भूषणैश्च बभौ मेरुः प्रभाभिरिव भास्वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa kāñcanavicitreṇa kirīṭena virājatā
bhūṣaṇaiśca babhau meruḥ prabhābhiriva bhāsvaraḥ

translations.english: Adorned with a crown plated with wrought gold' and (other) ornaments he looked like the Meru swimming in its own splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
स रराज रथे तस्मिन्राजसूनुर्महाबलः
वृतो नैरृतशार्दूलैर्वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः
verses.transliteration:
sa rarāja rathe tasminrājasūnurmahābalaḥ
vṛto nairṛtaśārdūlairvajrapāṇirivāmaraiḥ

translations.english: That powerful son of the kind surrounded by the Naiſtas looked lovely on that car like the thunder-handed (Deity) engirt by the immortals.

verses.sanskrit:
हयमुच्चैःश्रवः प्रख्यं श्वेतं कनकभूषणम्
मनोजवं महाकायमारुरोह नरान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
hayamuccaiḥśravaḥ prakhyaṁ śvetaṁ kanakabhūṣaṇam
manojavaṁ mahākāyamāruroha narāntakaḥ

translations.english: Narāntaka mounted a white steed resembling Uccaiḥśravă, caparisoned in gold, having a large frame and endowed with the velocity of the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीत्वा प्रासमुक्लाभं विरराज नरान्तकः
शक्तिमादाय तेजस्वी गुहः शत्रुष्विवाहवे
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītvā prāsamuklābhaṁ virarāja narāntakaḥ
śaktimādāya tejasvī guhaḥ śatruṣvivāhave

translations.english: Taking a prāśa, Narāntaka appeared like the energetic Guha mounted on the peacock, grasping his dart.

verses.sanskrit:
देवान्तकः समादाय परिघं वज्रभूषणम्
परिगृह्य गिरिं दोर्भ्यां वपुर्विष्णोर्विडम्बयन्
verses.transliteration:
devāntakaḥ samādāya parighaṁ vajrabhūṣaṇam
parigṛhya giriṁ dorbhyāṁ vapurviṣṇorviḍambayan

translations.english: Taking a bludgeon decked in golden Ornaments, Devántaka resembled Vişņu at the time of the churning of the ocean, holding the Dorbhya* and staying burthening (the earth). *The mountain Mandara which served as the churning-stick..

verses.sanskrit:
महापार्श्वो महातेजा गदामादाय वीर्यवान्
विरराज गदापाणिः कुबेर इव संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
mahāpārśvo mahātejā gadāmādāya vīryavān
virarāja gadāpāṇiḥ kubera iva saṁyuge

translations.english: The powerful Mahāpārsva endowed with terrific energy, taking his mace, appeared like Kuvera holding in his hand a mace in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्गजैश्च तुरंगैश्च रथैश्चाम्बुदनिस्वनैः
अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानो राक्षसाः प्रवरायुधाः
verses.transliteration:
tāngajaiśca turaṁgaiśca rathaiścāmbudanisvanaiḥ
anujagmurmahātmāno rākṣasāḥ pravarāyudhāḥ

translations.english: Like immortals issuing out of Amarāvatſ, they marched out with elephants and steeds and cars sending out clatter resembling the rumbling of clouds. And them followed high-souled Räkşasas equipped with mighty-arms.

verses.sanskrit:
ते विरेजुर्महात्मानो कुमाराः सूर्यवर्चसः
किरीटिनः श्रिया जुष्टा ग्रहा दीप्ता इवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
te virejurmahātmāno kumārāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ
kirīṭinaḥ śriyā juṣṭā grahā dīptā ivāmbare

translations.english: Those sun-bright high-souled princes decked with diadems appeared splendid like burning planets in the firmament.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रगृहीता बभौ तेषां छत्राणामावलिः सिता
शारदाभ्रप्रतीकाशां हंसावलिरिवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
pragṛhītā babhau teṣāṁ chatrāṇāmāvaliḥ sitā
śāradābhrapratīkāśāṁ haṁsāvalirivāmbare

translations.english: The various gorgeous attires which they had worn resembled rows of cranes in the sky, looking like autumnal clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
मरणं वापि निश्चित्य शत्रूणां वा पराजयम्
इति कृत्वा मतिं वीरा निर्जग्मुः संयुगार्थिनः
verses.transliteration:
maraṇaṁ vāpi niścitya śatrūṇāṁ vā parājayam
iti kṛtvā matiṁ vīrā nirjagmuḥ saṁyugārthinaḥ

translations.english: Resolved on dying or conquering the foe in fight, those heroes sallied out seeking encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
जगर्जुश्च प्रणेदुश्च चिक्षिपुश्चापि सायकान्
जहृषुश्च महात्मानो निर्यान्तो युद्धदुर्मदाः
verses.transliteration:
jagarjuśca praṇeduśca cikṣipuścāpi sāyakān
jahṛṣuśca mahātmāno niryānto yuddhadurmadāḥ

translations.english: Those high-souled ones, incapable of being repressed in fight, roared and shouted and discharged shafts and held them,

verses.sanskrit:
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटनिनदैः संचचालेव मेदिनी
रक्षसां सिंहनादैश्च पुस्फोटेव तदाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
kṣveḍitāsphoṭaninadaiḥ saṁcacāleva medinī
rakṣasāṁ siṁhanādaiśca pusphoṭeva tadāmbaram

translations.english: The earth shook as they sent up leonine roars and struck at their arms with their hands; and the sky seemed riven with the leonine roars of the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽभिनिष्क्रम्य मुदिता राक्षसेन्द्रा महाबलाः
ददृशुर्वानरानीकं समुद्यतशिलानगम्
verses.transliteration:
te'bhiniṣkramya muditā rākṣasendrā mahābalāḥ
dadṛśurvānarānīkaṁ samudyataśilānagam

translations.english: Issuing out cheerfully, those foremost of Rāks asas endowed with great strength beheld that monkey-army staying with upraised rocks and stones.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलजीमूतसंकाशं समुद्यतमहायुधम्
दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैर्नैरृतैः सर्वतो वृतम्
verses.transliteration:
nīlajīmūtasaṁkāśaṁ samudyatamahāyudham
dīptānalaraviprakhyairnairṛtaiḥ sarvato vṛtam

translations.english: The high souled monkeys also saw that mighty host of Räkşasas thronging with elephants, horses and cars, and ringing with hundreds of bell-lets; resembling dark-blue clouds; upraising mighty arms; and environed on all sides by Naiſtas resembling flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्दृष्ट्वा बलमायान्तं लब्धलक्ष्याः प्लवंगमाः
समुद्यतमहाशैलाः संप्रणेदुर्मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
taddṛṣṭvā balamāyāntaṁ labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
samudyatamahāśailāḥ saṁpraṇedurmuhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: Seeing that force advance, the monkeys, finding opportunity, upraising gaint crags momentarily set up shouts. And thereat, the Rakş asas, incapable of bearing those shouts, shouted in reply to the monkeys. And again the monkeys shouted to the Raksasa, who were unable to put up with that cry. And hearing that loud shout of the monkey-leaders, the mighty Raksasa, incapable of bearing that noise expressive of exhilaration, shouted still more dreadfully.

verses.sanskrit:
ते राक्षसबलं घोरं प्रविश्य हरियूथपाः
विचेरुरुद्यतैः शैलैर्नगाः शिखरिणो यथा
verses.transliteration:
te rākṣasabalaṁ ghoraṁ praviśya hariyūthapāḥ
vicerurudyataiḥ śailairnagāḥ śikhariṇo yathā

translations.english: Then diving into that dreadful Räkşasa army, the monkey-leaders began to range it with uplifted rocks, like to mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
केचिदाकाशमाविश्य केचिदुर्व्यां प्लवंगमाः
रक्षःसैन्येषु संक्रुद्धाश्चेरुर्द्रुमशिलायुधाः
verses.transliteration:
kecidākāśamāviśya kecidurvyāṁ plavaṁgamāḥ
rakṣaḥsainyeṣu saṁkruddhāścerurdrumaśilāyudhāḥ

translations.english: Equipped with trees and stones, the monkeys enraged, ranged the Raksasa army, now rising into the sky, and now coming down to the earth. And some among the powerful monkeys went about taking broad-shouldered trees.

verses.sanskrit:
ते पादपशिलाशैलैश्चक्रुर्वृष्टिमनुत्तमाम्
बाणौघैर्वार्यमाणाश्च हरयो भीमविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
te pādapaśilāśailaiścakrurvṛṣṭimanuttamām
bāṇaughairvāryamāṇāśca harayo bhīmavikramāḥ

translations.english: The encounter that took place between the thronging Räkşasa and monkeys was some-thing terrific. And (the monkeys) began to pour a wonderful shower of trees and rocks and cliffs. The monkeys of dread prowess were resisted with vollies of shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्च रणे राक्षसवानराः
शिलाभिश्चूर्णयामासुर्यातुधानान्प्लवंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
siṁhanādānvineduśca raṇe rākṣasavānarāḥ
śilābhiścūrṇayāmāsuryātudhānānplavaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: In the contest the monkeys and Rākşasas emitted leonine roars. And monkeys crushed Yatudhānas with rocks, and, wrought with rage, (they) in the encounter slew (Raksasas) covered with armour and ornaments; and steeds. The monkeys on a sudden slew heroic Yätudhānas.

verses.sanskrit:
निजघ्नुः सहसाप्लुत्य यातुधानान्प्लवंगमाः
शैलशृङ्गनिपातैश्च मुष्टिभिर्वान्तलोचनाः
चेलुः पेतुश्च नेदुश्च तत्र राक्षसपुंगवाः
verses.transliteration:
nijaghnuḥ sahasāplutya yātudhānānplavaṁgamāḥ
śailaśṛṅganipātaiśca muṣṭibhirvāntalocanāḥ
celuḥ petuśca neduśca tatra rākṣasapuṁgavāḥ

translations.english: Smite with mountain-peaks on their persons, and with their eyes falling off, the foremost of Rakşasas moved, dropped down, or roared in the scene of conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शैलैश्च खड्गैश्च विसृष्टैर्हरिराक्षसैः
मुहूर्तेनावृता भूमिरभवच्छोणिताप्लुता
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śailaiśca khaḍgaiśca visṛṣṭairharirākṣasaiḥ
muhūrtenāvṛtā bhūmirabhavacchoṇitāplutā

translations.english: In a moment the earth was covered with crags and swords discharged by monkeys and Raksasas, and was drenched in gore.

verses.sanskrit:
छिन्नवर्मतनुत्राणा राक्षसा वानरैर्हताः
रुधिरं प्रस्रुतास्तत्र रससारमिव द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
chinnavarmatanutrāṇā rākṣasā vānarairhatāḥ
rudhiraṁ prasrutāstatra rasasāramiva drumāḥ

translations.english: The Rākşasas, slain by the monkeys, having their mail and defence for the body rent, bled like to trees exuding sap.

verses.sanskrit:
रथेन च रथं चापि वारणेन च वारणम्
हयेन च हयं केचिन्निजघ्नुर्वानरा रणे
verses.transliteration:
rathena ca rathaṁ cāpi vāraṇena ca vāraṇam
hayena ca hayaṁ kecinnijaghnurvānarā raṇe

translations.english: And in that encounter, some among the monkeys destroyed cars with cars, elephants with elephants, and steeds with steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्द्रैश्च भल्लैश्च निशितैः शरैः
राक्षसा वानरेन्द्राणां चिच्छिदुः पादपाञ्शिलाः
verses.transliteration:
kṣuraprairardhacandraiśca bhallaiśca niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
rākṣasā vānarendrāṇāṁ cicchiduḥ pādapāñśilāḥ

translations.english: The Raksasas rived the trees and rocks of the foremost monkeys by means of Kșurapras and crescents and sharpened Bhallas and arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
विकीर्णैः पर्वताग्रैश्च द्रुमैश्छिन्नैश्च संयुगे
हतैश्च कपिरक्षोभिर्दुर्गमा वसुधाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
vikīrṇaiḥ parvatāgraiśca drumaiśchinnaiśca saṁyuge
hataiśca kapirakṣobhirdurgamā vasudhābhavat

translations.english: In that encounter the earth became impassable, having been scattered with crags baffled and severed trees and (warriors) slain by monkeys and Rākṣasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्प्रवृत्ते तुमुले विमर्दे; प्रहृष्यमाणेषु वली मुखेषु
निपात्यमानेषु च राक्षसेषु; महर्षयो देवगणाश्च नेदुः
verses.transliteration:
tasminpravṛtte tumule vimarde; prahṛṣyamāṇeṣu valī mukheṣu
nipātyamāneṣu ca rākṣaseṣu; maharṣayo devagaṇāśca neduḥ

translations.english: In that fearful conflict, which was being waged, on the monkeys having been exhilarated and the Rākşasas having been brought down, the Maharsis and the deities sent up shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हयं मारुततुल्यवेग;मारुह्य शक्तिं निशितां प्रगृह्य
नरान्तको वानरराजसैन्यं; महार्णवं मीन इवाविवेश
verses.transliteration:
tato hayaṁ mārutatulyavega;māruhya śaktiṁ niśitāṁ pragṛhya
narāntako vānararājasainyaṁ; mahārṇavaṁ mīna ivāviveśa

translations.english: Then mounted on a charger endued with the celerity of the wind, and grasping a whetted dart, Narāntaka entered into that fierce army of monkeys, like a fish diving into the deep.

verses.sanskrit:
स वानरान्सप्तशतानि वीरः; प्रासेन दीप्तेन विनिर्बिभेद
एकः क्षणेनेन्द्ररिपुर्महात्मा; जघान सैन्यं हरिपुंगवानाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa vānarānsaptaśatāni vīraḥ; prāsena dīptena vinirbibheda
ekaḥ kṣaṇenendraripurmahātmā; jaghāna sainyaṁ haripuṁgavānām

translations.english: That hero by means of an effulgent bearded dart pierced seven hundred monkeys, and at one time the high-souled enemy of Indra slew the army of the foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ददृशुश्च महात्मानं हयपृष्ठे प्रतिष्ठितम्
चरन्तं हरिसैन्येषु विद्याधरमहर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
dadṛśuśca mahātmānaṁ hayapṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhitam
carantaṁ harisainyeṣu vidyādharamaharṣayaḥ

translations.english: The Vidyadharas and Maharsis saw that highsouled one mounted on horseback, ranging the monkey-ranks.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य ददृशे मार्गो मांसशोणितकर्दमः
पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya dadṛśe mārgo māṁsaśoṇitakardamaḥ
patitaiḥ parvatākārairvānarairabhisaṁvṛtaḥ

translations.english: His course was discovered, miry with flesh and blood and blocked up with mountain-like monkeys fallen.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्विक्रमितुं बुद्धिं चक्रुः प्लवगपुंगवाः
तावदेतानतिक्रम्य निर्बिभेद नरान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
yāvadvikramituṁ buddhiṁ cakruḥ plavagapuṁgavāḥ
tāvadetānatikramya nirbibheda narāntakaḥ

translations.english: When the monkeys set their hearts on displaying their prowess, Narāntaka, baffling them, pierced them with shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
यावदुत्पाटयामासुर्वृक्षाञ्शैलान्वनौकसः
तावत्प्रासहताः पेतुर्वज्रकृत्ता इवाचलाः
verses.transliteration:
yāvadutpāṭayāmāsurvṛkṣāñśailānvanaukasaḥ
tāvatprāsahatāḥ peturvajrakṛttā ivācalāḥ

translations.english: He consumed the monkey-army, like fire burning a forest. And when the wood-rangers uprooted trees and crags, they slain by bearded darts dropped down like mountains riven by the thunder.

verses.sanskrit:
दिक्षु सर्वासु बलवान्विचचार नरान्तकः
प्रमृद्नन्सर्वतो युद्धे प्रावृट्काले यथानिलः
verses.transliteration:
dikṣu sarvāsu balavānvicacāra narāntakaḥ
pramṛdnansarvato yuddhe prāvṛṭkāle yathānilaḥ

translations.english: Raising a glowing prasa, the powerful Narāntaka began to range about in the rear of the forces; dashing everywhere (against the foe) in fight, like the wind in the rainy season. *Sangramānte, I presume, means rear of the forces; although literally it means, at the conclusion of the conflict, because this interpretation would not be proper, the battle being now at its hottest.

verses.sanskrit:
न शेकुर्धावितुं वीरा न स्थातुं स्पन्दितुं कुतः
उत्पतन्तं स्थितं यान्तं सर्वान्विव्याध वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
na śekurdhāvituṁ vīrā na sthātuṁ spandituṁ kutaḥ
utpatantaṁ sthitaṁ yāntaṁ sarvānvivyādha vīryavān

translations.english: The heroes could not appear prominently, or keep their posts. And how could they then move freely? And that one endued with prowess pierced everyone, whether springing, or staying, or moving.

verses.sanskrit:
एकेनान्तककल्पेन प्रासेनादित्यतेजसा
भिन्नानि हरिसैन्यानि निपेतुर्धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
ekenāntakakalpena prāsenādityatejasā
bhinnāni harisainyāni nipeturdharaṇītale

translations.english: Broken through by a single praśa, resembling the Reaper, and furnished with solar effulgence, the monkey-ranks began to roll on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रनिष्पेषसदृशं प्रासस्याभिनिपातनम्
न शेकुर्वानराः सोढुं ते विनेदुर्महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
vajraniṣpeṣasadṛśaṁ prāsasyābhinipātanam
na śekurvānarāḥ soḍhuṁ te vinedurmahāsvanam

translations.english: The monkeys were ill fitted to bear the impetus of that präśa having the touch of thunder itself; and they raised a loud cry.

verses.sanskrit:
पततां हरिवीराणां रूपाणि प्रचकाशिरे
वज्रभिन्नाग्रकूटानां शैलानां पततामिव
verses.transliteration:
patatāṁ harivīrāṇāṁ rūpāṇi pracakāśire
vajrabhinnāgrakūṭānāṁ śailānāṁ patatāmiva

translations.english: The appearances of those monkey-heroes falling were like mountains toppling, having their summits riven with the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तु पूर्वं महात्मानः कुम्भकर्णेन पातिताः
तेऽस्वस्था वानरश्रेष्ठाः सुग्रीवमुपतस्थिरे
verses.transliteration:
ye tu pūrvaṁ mahātmānaḥ kumbhakarṇena pātitāḥ
te'svasthā vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ sugrīvamupatasthire

translations.english: Those high-souled and powerful monkeys that formerly had been brought down by Kumbhakarma, having recovered, were present with Sugrīva in this encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
विप्रेक्षमाणः सुग्रीवो ददर्श हरिवाहिनीम्
नरान्तकभयत्रस्तां विद्रवन्तीमितस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
viprekṣamāṇaḥ sugrīvo dadarśa harivāhinīm
narāntakabhayatrastāṁ vidravantīmitastataḥ

translations.english: Sugrīva, looking around, saw that monkeyarmy flying in all directions, agitated with the fear of Narantaka.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा स ददर्श नरान्तकम्
गृहीतप्रासमायान्तं हयपृष्ठे प्रतिष्ठितम्
verses.transliteration:
vidrutāṁ vāhinīṁ dṛṣṭvā sa dadarśa narāntakam
gṛhītaprāsamāyāntaṁ hayapṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhitam

translations.english: After seeing the army in flight, he saw Narāntaka himself, advancing, wielding a prasa, and mounted on a steed.

verses.sanskrit:
अथोवाच महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः
कुमारमङ्गदं वीरं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
athovāca mahātejāḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
kumāramaṅgadaṁ vīraṁ śakratulyaparākramam

translations.english: As soon as he saw (that hero), the exceedingly energetic lord of monkeys, Sugriva addressed the heroic prince Angada endowed with strength equal to that of Indra, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छैनं राक्षसं वीर योऽसौ तुरगमास्थितः
क्षोभयन्तं हरिबलं क्षिप्रं प्राणैर्वियोजय
verses.transliteration:
gacchainaṁ rākṣasaṁ vīra yo'sau turagamāsthitaḥ
kṣobhayantaṁ haribalaṁ kṣipraṁ prāṇairviyojaya

translations.english: Go against this heroic Raksasas that is mounted on a steed; and speedily deprive of life that one who is devouring up the ranks of his foes.

verses.sanskrit:
स भर्तुर्वचनं श्रुत्वा निष्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा
अनीकान्मेघसंकाशान्मेघानीकादिवांशुमान्
verses.transliteration:
sa bharturvacanaṁ śrutvā niṣpapātāṅgadastadā
anīkānmeghasaṁkāśānmeghānīkādivāṁśumān

translations.english: Hearing his master's speech, Angada descended from that host resembling clouds, like the powerful Sun himself.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलसंघातसंकाशो हरीणामुत्तमोऽङ्गदः
रराजाङ्गदसंनद्धः सधातुरिव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
śailasaṁghātasaṁkāśo harīṇāmuttamo'ṅgadaḥ
rarājāṅgadasaṁnaddhaḥ sadhāturiva parvataḥ

translations.english: And resembling a mass of crags, Angada-foremost of monkeys, Adorned with Angadas, appeared beautiful like a mountain with metals on it.

verses.sanskrit:
निरायुधो महातेजाः केवलं नखदंष्ट्रवान्
नरान्तकमभिक्रम्य वालिपुत्रोऽब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration:
nirāyudho mahātejāḥ kevalaṁ nakhadaṁṣṭravān
narāntakamabhikramya vāliputro'bravīdvacaḥ

translations.english: And weaponless himself, and furnished only with nails and teeth, Vali's son attacking Narāntaka, said.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ किं प्राकृतैरेभिर्हरिभिस्त्वं करिष्यसि
अस्मिन्वज्रसमस्पर्शे प्रासं क्षिप ममोरसि
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha kiṁ prākṛtairebhirharibhistvaṁ kariṣyasi
asminvajrasamasparśe prāsaṁ kṣipa mamorasi

translations.english: Stay! What shall you do with these inferior monkeys? This prasa, having the feel of the thunder-bolt, do you hurl at my heart itself.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रचुक्रोध नरान्तकः
संदश्य दशनैरोष्ठं निश्वस्य च भुजंगवत्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā pracukrodha narāntakaḥ
saṁdaśya daśanairoṣṭhaṁ niśvasya ca bhujaṁgavat

translations.english: Hearing Angada's words, Narāntaka was fired with wrath. And knawing his upper lip with his teeth and sighing like a serpent, Narāntaka, wrought with wrath, approached Vali's son.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रासमाविध्य तदाङ्गदाय; समुज्ज्वलन्तं सहसोत्ससर्ज
स वालिपुत्रोरसि वज्रकल्पे; बभूव भग्नो न्यपतच्च भूमौ
verses.transliteration:
sa prāsamāvidhya tadāṅgadāya; samujjvalantaṁ sahasotsasarja
sa vāliputrorasi vajrakalpe; babhūva bhagno nyapatacca bhūmau

translations.english: Then whirling his praśa, he suddenly discharged that flaming (weapon) against Argada. And then it was snapped on the breast of Vali's son, resembling the thunder-bolt, and dropped to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रासमालोक्य तदा विभग्नं; सुपर्णकृत्तोरगभोगकल्पम्
तलं समुद्यम्य स वालिपुत्र;स्तुरंगमस्याभिजघान मूर्ध्नि
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prāsamālokya tadā vibhagnaṁ; suparṇakṛttoragabhogakalpam
talaṁ samudyamya sa vāliputra;sturaṁgamasyābhijaghāna mūrdhni

translations.english: Seeing the praśa broken in pieces, like a powerful snake severed by Suparna, Vāli's son, raising his hand, dealt a slap at the head of his (Narāntaka's) steed.

verses.sanskrit:
निमग्नपादः स्फुटिताक्षि तारो; निष्क्रान्तजिह्वोऽचलसंनिकाशः
स तस्य वाजी निपपात भूमौ; तलप्रहारेण विकीर्णमूर्धा
verses.transliteration:
nimagnapādaḥ sphuṭitākṣi tāro; niṣkrāntajihvo'calasaṁnikāśaḥ
sa tasya vājī nipapāta bhūmau; talaprahāreṇa vikīrṇamūrdhā

translations.english: Thereat, with his legs sinking down and his eye-balls coming off and his tongue hanging down, and wearing the look of a mountain, on being smite with that slap, Narāntaka's steed fell down to the ground, with its head lying at random.

verses.sanskrit:
नरान्तकः क्रोधवशं जगाम; हतं तुरगं पतितं निरीक्ष्य
स मुष्टिमुद्यम्य महाप्रभावो; जघान शीर्षे युधि वालिपुत्रम्
verses.transliteration:
narāntakaḥ krodhavaśaṁ jagāma; hataṁ turagaṁ patitaṁ nirīkṣya
sa muṣṭimudyamya mahāprabhāvo; jaghāna śīrṣe yudhi vāliputram

translations.english: Narāntaka seeing his charger slain and fallen, was seized with a furious wrath, and raising his clenched fist, that one endowed with exceeding great energy in that conflict hit Vāll's son on the head.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाङ्गदो मुष्टिविभिन्नमूर्धा; सुस्राव तीव्रं रुधिरं भृशोष्णम्
मुहुर्विजज्वाल मुमोह चापि; संज्ञां समासाद्य विसिष्मिये च
verses.transliteration:
athāṅgado muṣṭivibhinnamūrdhā; susrāva tīvraṁ rudhiraṁ bhṛśoṣṇam
muhurvijajvāla mumoha cāpi; saṁjñāṁ samāsādya visiṣmiye ca

translations.english: Thereat Angada having his head wounded by that blow, warm blood gushed out plentifully. And momentarily burning and momentarily swooning he, regaining his senses, was amazed.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाङ्गदो वज्रसमानवेगं; संवर्त्य मुष्टिं गिरिशृङ्गकल्पम्
निपातयामास तदा महात्मा; नरान्तकस्योरसि वालिपुत्रः
verses.transliteration:
athāṅgado vajrasamānavegaṁ; saṁvartya muṣṭiṁ giriśṛṅgakalpam
nipātayāmāsa tadā mahātmā; narāntakasyorasi vāliputraḥ

translations.english: Then Vāli's son, the high-souled Angada clenching his fist into a blow resembling Death itself in energy, and like to a mountain-peak, let it descend on the chest of Narāntaka.

verses.sanskrit:
स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नवक्षा; ज्वालां वमञ्शोणितदिग्धगात्रः
नरान्तको भूमितले पपात; यथाचलो वज्रनिपातभग्नः
verses.transliteration:
sa muṣṭiniṣpiṣṭavibhinnavakṣā; jvālāṁ vamañśoṇitadigdhagātraḥ
narāntako bhūmitale papāta; yathācalo vajranipātabhagnaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, with his breast riven and broken down, vomiting flames and having his body bathed in blood, Narāntaka dropped down to the earth, like a hill shattered by the impetus of the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
अथान्तरिक्षे त्रिदशोत्तमानां; वनौकसां चैव महाप्रणादः
बभूव तस्मिन्निहतेऽग्र्यवीरे; नरान्तके वालिसुतेन संख्ये
verses.transliteration:
athāntarikṣe tridaśottamānāṁ; vanaukasāṁ caiva mahāpraṇādaḥ
babhūva tasminnihate'gryavīre; narāntake vālisutena saṁkhye

translations.english: On Narāntaka of exceeding prowess having been slain by Vali's son in battle, there arose a tremendous uproar in the firmament from the wood-rangers and the foremost of celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाङ्गदो राममनः प्रहर्षणं; सुदुष्करं तं कृतवान्हि विक्रमम्
विसिष्मिये सोऽप्यतिवीर्य विक्रमः; पुनश्च युद्धे स बभूव हर्षितः
verses.transliteration:
athāṅgado rāmamanaḥ praharṣaṇaṁ; suduṣkaraṁ taṁ kṛtavānhi vikramam
visiṣmiye so'pyativīrya vikramaḥ; punaśca yuddhe sa babhūva harṣitaḥ

translations.english: Angada having performed that difficult deed of prowess, capable of delighting the mind of Rāma, was seized with amazement;* and that one of terrific feats in fight was again inspired with delight in the encounter. * Probably, at his own prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
नरान्तकं हतं दृष्ट्वा चुक्रुशुर्नैरृतर्षभाः
देवान्तकस्त्रिमूर्धा च पौलस्त्यश्च महोदरः
verses.transliteration:
narāntakaṁ hataṁ dṛṣṭvā cukruśurnairṛtarṣabhāḥ
devāntakastrimūrdhā ca paulastyaśca mahodaraḥ

translations.english: Seeing Narāntaka slain, the foremost of Naiſtas-including the three-headed Devāntaka and Pulastya's descendant, Mahodara, began to cry (in chorus).

verses.sanskrit:
आरूढो मेघसंकाशं वारणेन्द्रं महोदरः
वालिपुत्रं महावीर्यमभिदुद्राव वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
ārūḍho meghasaṁkāśaṁ vāraṇendraṁ mahodaraḥ
vāliputraṁ mahāvīryamabhidudrāva vīryavān

translations.english: Then the vehement Mahodara, mounted (on horseback), rushed against Vali's son endued with energy.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातृव्यसनसंतप्तस्तदा देवान्तको बली
आदाय परिघं दीप्तमङ्गदं समभिद्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
bhrātṛvyasanasaṁtaptastadā devāntako balī
ādāya parighaṁ dīptamaṅgadaṁ samabhidravat

translations.english: Aggrieved in consequence of the calamity that had befallen his brother, the strong Devāntaka grasping a dreadful bludgeon, darted against Angada.

verses.sanskrit:
रथमादित्यसंकाशं युक्तं परमवाजिभिः
आस्थाय त्रिशिरा वीरो वालिपुत्रमथाभ्ययात्
verses.transliteration:
rathamādityasaṁkāśaṁ yuktaṁ paramavājibhiḥ
āsthāya triśirā vīro vāliputramathābhyayāt

translations.english: Ascending a car resembling the Sun yoked with superb steeds, the heroic Triģiras rushed against Vali's son.

verses.sanskrit:
देवान्तकाय तं वीरश्चिक्षेप सहसाङ्गदः
महावृक्षं महाशाखं शक्रो दीप्तमिवाशनिम्
verses.transliteration:
devāntakāya taṁ vīraścikṣepa sahasāṅgadaḥ
mahāvṛkṣaṁ mahāśākhaṁ śakro dīptamivāśanim

translations.english: Then charged by those three powerful Räkş asas-crushers of the hauteur of immortals, Angada uprooted a tree furnished with gigantic branches. And as Sakra hurl the mighty flaming thunder-bolt, that hero-Angada, at once hurled against Devāntaka that mighty tree having giant branches.

verses.sanskrit:
देवान्तकश्च संक्रुद्धः परिघेण तदाङ्गदम्
उपगम्याभिहत्याशु व्यपचक्राम वेगवान्
verses.transliteration:
devāntakaśca saṁkruddhaḥ parigheṇa tadāṅgadam
upagamyābhihatyāśu vyapacakrāma vegavān

translations.english: Devantaka, enraged advancing, hit Angada with his bludgeon, and then, endowed with velocity, he swiftly turned away.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्रिभिर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठैर्युगपत्समभिद्रुतः
न विव्यथे महातेजा वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्
verses.transliteration:
sa tribhirnairṛtaśreṣṭhairyugapatsamabhidrutaḥ
na vivyathe mahātejā vāliputraḥ pratāpavān

translations.english: Attacked simultaneously by those three powerful Naiſtas, the exceedingly energetic son of Vali's possessed of prowess, did not feel any pain.

verses.sanskrit:
विषाणं चास्य निष्कृष्य वालिपुत्रो महाबलः
देवान्तकमभिद्रुत्य ताडयामास संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
viṣāṇaṁ cāsya niṣkṛṣya vāliputro mahābalaḥ
devāntakamabhidrutya tāḍayāmāsa saṁyuge

translations.english: Then pulling out his tusks, the highly powerful son of Vāli, darting against Devāntaka, dealt him a blow therewith in that encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
स विह्वलितसर्वाङ्गो वातोद्धत इव द्रुमः
लाक्षारससवर्णं च सुस्राव रुधिरं मुखात्
verses.transliteration:
sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo vātoddhata iva drumaḥ
lākṣārasasavarṇaṁ ca susrāva rudhiraṁ mukhāt

translations.english: Thereupon that strong one overwhelmed like a tree buffeted by the wind, began to discharge blood profusely, looking like the hue of lac.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाश्वास्य महातेजाः कृच्छ्राद्देवान्तको बली
आविध्य परिघं घोरमाजघान तदाङ्गदम्
verses.transliteration:
athāśvāsya mahātejāḥ kṛcchrāddevāntako balī
āvidhya parighaṁ ghoramājaghāna tadāṅgadam

translations.english: Then cheering him, the exceedingly energetic and powerful Narāntaka, violently whirling his bludgeon with might and main, hit Angada with it.

verses.sanskrit:
परिघाभिहतश्चापि वानरेन्द्रात्मजस्तदा
जानुभ्यां पतितो भूमौ पुनरेवोत्पपात ह
verses.transliteration:
parighābhihataścāpi vānarendrātmajastadā
jānubhyāṁ patito bhūmau punarevotpapāta ha

translations.english: And albeit struck with the bludgeon, the son of the lord of monkeys, going down on his knees, again darted up.

verses.sanskrit:
समुत्पतन्तं त्रिशिरास्त्रिभिराशीविषोपमैः
घोरैर्हरिपतेः पुत्रं ललाटेऽभिजघान ह
verses.transliteration:
samutpatantaṁ triśirāstribhirāśīviṣopamaiḥ
ghorairharipateḥ putraṁ lalāṭe'bhijaghāna ha

translations.english: As he sprang up, Triśiras hit at the temples of the son of the king of monkeys with three straight-speeding terrific shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽङ्गदं परिक्षिप्तं त्रिभिर्नैरृतपुंगवैः
हनूमानपि विज्ञाय नीलश्चापि प्रतस्थतुः
verses.transliteration:
tato'ṅgadaṁ parikṣiptaṁ tribhirnairṛtapuṁgavaiḥ
hanūmānapi vijñāya nīlaścāpi pratasthatuḥ

translations.english: Seeing Angada assailed by the three redoubtable Rakşasas, Hanumān and Nila proceeded (to his rescue).

verses.sanskrit:
ततश्चिक्षेप शैलाग्रं नीलस्त्रिशिरसे तदा
तद्रावणसुतो धीमान्बिभेद निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tataścikṣepa śailāgraṁ nīlastriśirase tadā
tadrāvaṇasuto dhīmānbibheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Then Nila hurled a mountain-top at Trisiras; and thereat that son of Rāvaņa severed it with sharpened arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बाणशतनिर्भिन्नं विदारितशिलातलम्
सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात गिरेः शिरः
verses.transliteration:
tadbāṇaśatanirbhinnaṁ vidāritaśilātalam
savisphuliṅgaṁ sajvālaṁ nipapāta gireḥ śiraḥ

translations.english: That mountain-top on being riven, dropped down, aflame and shooting out sparks of fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो जृम्भितमालोक्य हर्षाद्देवान्तकस्तदा
परिघेणाभिदुद्राव मारुतात्मजमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
tato jṛmbhitamālokya harṣāddevāntakastadā
parigheṇābhidudrāva mārutātmajamāhave

translations.english: Seeing him* yawning in joy, the stalwart Devāntaka in that encounter pursued the windgod's son with his bludgeon. *Triśiras.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तमुत्पत्य हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
आजघान तदा मूर्ध्नि वज्रवेगेन मुष्टिना
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantamutpatya hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
ājaghāna tadā mūrdhni vajravegena muṣṭinā

translations.english: As he rushed on, that foremost of monkeysHanuman-~-dealt on the crown of his head, a blow resembling the thunder-bolt itself.

verses.sanskrit:
स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविकीर्णमूर्धा; निर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिह्वः
देवान्तको राक्षसराजसूनु;र्गतासुरुर्व्यां सहसा पपात
verses.transliteration:
sa muṣṭiniṣpiṣṭavikīrṇamūrdhā; nirvāntadantākṣivilambijihvaḥ
devāntako rākṣasarājasūnu;rgatāsururvyāṁ sahasā papāta

translations.english: Thereat with his head crushed and cleft, and his ieeth and eyes falling out, and his tongue hanging down, that son to the sovereign of the Rākşasas suddenly dropped to the earth, deprived of life.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्हते राक्षसयोधमुख्ये; महाबले संयति देवशत्रौ
क्रुद्धस्त्रिमूर्धा निशिताग्रमुग्रं; ववर्ष नीलोरसि बाणवर्षम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminhate rākṣasayodhamukhye; mahābale saṁyati devaśatrau
kruddhastrimūrdhā niśitāgramugraṁ; vavarṣa nīlorasi bāṇavarṣam

translations.english: On that fierce and mighty Rākşasas warriorthat foe of the immortals— having fallen in fight, the three-headed one, waxing wondrous enraged began to shower terrific sharpened shafts on Nila's chest.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैः शरौघैरभिवर्ष्यमाणो; विभिन्नगात्रः कपिसैन्यपालः
नीलो बभूवाथ विसृष्टगात्रो; विष्टम्भितस्तेन महाबलेन
verses.transliteration:
sa taiḥ śaraughairabhivarṣyamāṇo; vibhinnagātraḥ kapisainyapālaḥ
nīlo babhūvātha visṛṣṭagātro; viṣṭambhitastena mahābalena

translations.english: Then even as a mass of roaring clouds poured down showers enwheeled with levin on a mountain, he showered arrows right on Nīla's breast. Threat showered with those shafts, that leader of monkeys Nīla with his person pierced, had his body riven and was stupefied by that exceedingly powerful one.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु नीलः प्रतिलभ्य संज्ञां; शैलं समुत्पाट्य सवृक्षषण्डम्
ततः समुत्पत्य भृशोग्रवेगो; महोदरं तेन जघान मूर्ध्नि
verses.transliteration:
tatastu nīlaḥ pratilabhya saṁjñāṁ; śailaṁ samutpāṭya savṛkṣaṣaṇḍam
tataḥ samutpatya bhṛśogravego; mahodaraṁ tena jaghāna mūrdhni

translations.english: Then that (monkey) possessed of tremendous vehemence, having regained his senses, uprooting a crag with a whole tract of trees, struck it at Mahodara's head.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स शैलाभिनिपातभग्नो; महोदरस्तेन सह द्विपेन
विपोथितो भूमितले गतासुः; पपात वर्जाभिहतो यथाद्रिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa śailābhinipātabhagno; mahodarastena saha dvipena
vipothito bhūmitale gatāsuḥ; papāta varjābhihato yathādriḥ

translations.english: Struck by that mighty enemy, Mahodara, broken down by the impetus of that rock, deprived of his senses, dropped down dead on the ground, like a cliff smite with the thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
पितृव्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा त्रिशिराश्चापमाददे
हनूमन्तं च संक्रुद्धो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
pitṛvyaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā triśirāścāpamādade
hanūmantaṁ ca saṁkruddho vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Seeing his uncle slain, Triſiras took up his bow; and inflamed with fury pierced Hanumān with whetted arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमांस्तु समुत्पत्य हयांस्त्रिशिरसस्तदा
विददार नखैः क्रुद्धो गजेन्द्रं मृगराडिव
verses.transliteration:
hanūmāṁstu samutpatya hayāṁstriśirasastadā
vidadāra nakhaiḥ kruddho gajendraṁ mṛgarāḍiva

translations.english: Then Hanumān flying into a fury, bounding to the welkin, with his nails ript the steed of Triớiras, even as a lion cleave a powerful elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ शक्तिं समादाय कालरात्रिमिवान्तकः
चिक्षेपानिलपुत्राय त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
atha śaktiṁ samādāya kālarātrimivāntakaḥ
cikṣepānilaputrāya triśirā rāvaṇātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then taking a dart even as the destroyer employ the fatal night, Ravana's son, TriSiras discharged it at the offspring of the wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
दिवि क्षिप्तामिवोल्कां तां शक्तिं क्षिप्तामसंगताम्
गृहीत्वा हरिशार्दूलो बभञ्ज च ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
divi kṣiptāmivolkāṁ tāṁ śaktiṁ kṣiptāmasaṁgatām
gṛhītvā hariśārdūlo babhañja ca nanāda ca

translations.english: Thereat catching the dart of resistless course as it descended from the sky, the powerful monkey snapped it and then shouted.

verses.sanskrit:
तां दृष्ट्वा घोरसंकाशां शक्तिं भग्नां हनूमता
प्रहृष्टा वानरगणा विनेदुर्जलदा इव
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ dṛṣṭvā ghorasaṁkāśāṁ śaktiṁ bhagnāṁ hanūmatā
prahṛṣṭā vānaragaṇā vinedurjaladā iva

translations.english: Seeing that dreadful dart broken by Hanumān, the monkeys, transported with delignt, sent up shouts, even as clouds rumble.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः खड्गं समुद्यम्य त्रिशिरा राक्षसोत्तमः
निचखान तदा रोषाद्वानरेन्द्रस्य वक्षसि
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ khaḍgaṁ samudyamya triśirā rākṣasottamaḥ
nicakhāna tadā roṣādvānarendrasya vakṣasi

translations.english: Then upraising his sword, that foremost of Raksasas-Trisiras-brought it down on the breast of the monkey-chief.

verses.sanskrit:
खड्गप्रहाराभिहतो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
आजघान त्रिमूर्धानं तलेनोरसि वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
khaḍgaprahārābhihato hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
ājaghāna trimūrdhānaṁ talenorasi vīryavān

translations.english: Overpowered with the sword-blow, Hanumān son to the wind-god, endowed with energy, dealt the three-headed one a slap on the head.

verses.sanskrit:
स तलभिहतस्तेन स्रस्तहस्ताम्बरो भुवि
निपपात महातेजास्त्रिशिरास्त्यक्तचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
sa talabhihatastena srastahastāmbaro bhuvi
nipapāta mahātejāstriśirāstyaktacetanaḥ

translations.english: And smitten with that slap, the highly powerful Triśiras, with his hands and attire dropping off, fell down to the earth, deprived of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य पततः खड्गं समाच्छिद्य महाकपिः
ननाद गिरिसंकाशस्त्रासयन्सर्वनैरृतान्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya patataḥ khaḍgaṁ samācchidya mahākapiḥ
nanāda girisaṁkāśastrāsayansarvanairṛtān

translations.english: Then that mighty monkey-resembling a hill broke his sword as he fell, and roared, terrifying all the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमुत्पपात निशाचरः
उत्पत्य च हनूमन्तं ताडयामास मुष्टिना
verses.transliteration:
amṛṣyamāṇastaṁ ghoṣamutpapāta niśācaraḥ
utpatya ca hanūmantaṁ tāḍayāmāsa muṣṭinā

translations.english: But not brooking that uproar, that night-ranger sprang up; and springing up, he dealt a blow at Hanuman.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन मुष्टिप्रहारेण संचुकोप महाकपिः
कुपितश्च निजग्राह किरीटे राक्षसर्षभम्
verses.transliteration:
tena muṣṭiprahāreṇa saṁcukopa mahākapiḥ
kupitaśca nijagrāha kirīṭe rākṣasarṣabham

translations.english: At that blow, the redoubtable monkey was wrought up with wrath; and inflamed with rage, he smote that foremost of Räkşasas about his diadem.

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य शीर्षाण्यसिना शितेन; किरीटजुष्टानि सकुण्डलानि
क्रुद्धः प्रचिच्छेद सुतोऽनिलस्य; त्वष्टुः सुतस्येव शिरांसि शक्रः
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya śīrṣāṇyasinā śitena; kirīṭajuṣṭāni sakuṇḍalāni
kruddhaḥ praciccheda suto'nilasya; tvaṣṭuḥ sutasyeva śirāṁsi śakraḥ

translations.english: Then with a sharp sword the wind-god's son cut off his heads decked with diadems and furnished with ear-rings; even as Sakra had severed the heads of Tastri' son.* *Visvarupa.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यायताक्षाण्यगसंनिभानि; प्रदीप्तवैश्वानरलोचनानि
पेतुः शिरांसीन्द्ररिपोर्धरण्यां; ज्योतींषि मुक्तानि यथार्कमार्गात्
verses.transliteration:
tānyāyatākṣāṇyagasaṁnibhāni; pradīptavaiśvānaralocanāni
petuḥ śirāṁsīndraripordharaṇyāṁ; jyotīṁṣi muktāni yathārkamārgāt

translations.english: Thereat even as burning stars, loosened, drop down from the course of Indra, the large organs of sense, and eyes flaming like glowing fire, and heads of that foe of Indra, dropped down to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्हते देवरिपौ त्रिशीर्षे; हनूमत शक्रपराक्रमेण
नेदुः प्लवंगाः प्रचचाल भूमी; रक्षांस्यथो दुद्रुविरे समन्तात्
verses.transliteration:
tasminhate devaripau triśīrṣe; hanūmata śakraparākrameṇa
neduḥ plavaṁgāḥ pracacāla bhūmī; rakṣāṁsyatho dudruvire samantāt

translations.english: On Trisiras, enemy of the immortals-having been slain by Hanuman endowed with the prowess itself of Sakra, the monkeys shouted, the earth shook, and the Rākṣas began to fly on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
अथर्षयः समुत्पत्य वानरो रवणानुजम्
महापार्श्वमुपागम्य तस्थौ तस्याग्रतो बली
verses.transliteration:
atharṣayaḥ samutpatya vānaro ravaṇānujam
mahāpārśvamupāgamya tasthau tasyāgrato balī

translations.english: Then the mighty and powerful monkey Risabha-springing up before Ravana's son, stood before the hosts of Matta.

verses.sanskrit:
तं पुरस्तात्स्थितं दृष्ट्वा वानरं पर्वतोपमम्
आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो गदया वज्रकल्पया
verses.transliteration:
taṁ purastātsthitaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānaraṁ parvatopamam
ājaghānorasi kruddho gadayā vajrakalpayā

translations.english: Seeing that mountain-like monkey staying before (him), Matta, enraged, dealt him a blow on the breast.

verses.sanskrit:
स तयाभिहतस्तेन गदया वानरर्षभः
भिन्नवक्षाः समाधूतः सुस्राव रुधिरं बहु
verses.transliteration:
sa tayābhihatastena gadayā vānararṣabhaḥ
bhinnavakṣāḥ samādhūtaḥ susrāva rudhiraṁ bahu

translations.english: And smite with the mace, that foremost of monkeys, with his breast riven and trembling, began to bleed copiously.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्राप्य चिरात्संज्ञामृषभो वानरर्षभः
क्रुद्धो विस्फुरमाणौष्ठो महापार्श्वमुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprāpya cirātsaṁjñāmṛṣabho vānararṣabhaḥ
kruddho visphuramāṇauṣṭho mahāpārśvamudaikṣata

translations.english: And regaining his senses after a long while, Risabha-lord of monkeys-inflamed with wrath pouting out his upper lip, gazed at Mahāpārsva.* *Otherwise, called Matta.

verses.sanskrit:
तां गृहीत्वा गदां भीमामाविध्य च पुनः पुनः
मत्तानीकं महापार्श्वं जघान रणमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ gṛhītvā gadāṁ bhīmāmāvidhya ca punaḥ punaḥ
mattānīkaṁ mahāpārśvaṁ jaghāna raṇamūrdhani

translations.english: And taking the terrific mace of the highsouled (Matta) and swinging it again and again, (Risabha) rushed (against the Raksasas). And that high-souled one began to slaughter Matta's forces in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्हते भ्रातरि रावणस्य; तन्नैरृतानां बलमर्णवाभम्
त्यक्तायुधं केवलजीवितार्थं; दुद्राव भिन्नार्णवसंनिकाशम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminhate bhrātari rāvaṇasya; tannairṛtānāṁ balamarṇavābham
tyaktāyudhaṁ kevalajīvitārthaṁ; dudrāva bhinnārṇavasaṁnikāśam

translations.english: On that brother of Rāvaņa having been slain, that host of Nairtas appearing like the ocean in grandeur, leaving its arms behind, solely for life rushed away, like to the deep riven (by the winds).

verses.sanskrit:
स भास्करसहस्रस्य संघातमिव भास्वरम्
रथमास्थाय शक्रारिरभिदुद्राव वानरान्
verses.transliteration:
sa bhāskarasahasrasya saṁghātamiva bhāsvaram
rathamāsthāya śakrārirabhidudrāva vānarān

translations.english: Ascending a car effulgent like a thousand suns mingling their rays into a burst of brilliance, that enemy of Sakra, charged the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स विस्फार्य महच्चापं किरीटी मृष्टकुण्डलः
नाम विश्रावयामास ननाद च महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
sa visphārya mahaccāpaṁ kirīṭī mṛṣṭakuṇḍalaḥ
nāma viśrāvayāmāsa nanāda ca mahāsvanam

translations.english: Stretching his bow, (Atikāya) decked with a diadem wearing polished ear-rings, proclaimed his name (among the monkey-ranks) and shouted in lofty tones.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन सिंहप्रणादेन नामविश्रावणेन च
ज्याशब्देन च भीमेन त्रासयामास वानरान्
verses.transliteration:
tena siṁhapraṇādena nāmaviśrāvaṇena ca
jyāśabdena ca bhīmena trāsayāmāsa vānarān

translations.english: And with his leonine roars and the proclamation of his name, and the tremendous twang of his bow-string, he struck terror into the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तस्य रूपमालोक्य यथा विष्णोस्त्रिविक्रमे
भयार्ता वानराः सर्वे विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
te tasya rūpamālokya yathā viṣṇostrivikrame
bhayārtā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti diśo daśa

translations.english: Seeing his form like to that of Vişnu when he displayed his threefold energy, the monkeywarriors seized with fear, began to scour on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽतिकायं समासाद्य वानरा मूढचेतसः
शरण्यं शरणं जग्मुर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
te'tikāyaṁ samāsādya vānarā mūḍhacetasaḥ
śaraṇyaṁ śaraṇaṁ jagmurlakṣmaṇāgrajamāhave

translations.english: On Atikāya appearing before them, the monkeys stupefied in that conflict, saught the shelter of Laksmana's elder brother.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽतिकायं काकुत्स्थो रथस्थं पर्वतोपमम्
ददर्श धन्विनं दूराद्गर्जन्तं कालमेघवत्
verses.transliteration:
tato'tikāyaṁ kākutstho rathasthaṁ parvatopamam
dadarśa dhanvinaṁ dūrādgarjantaṁ kālameghavat

translations.english: And from a distance Kakutstha saw the mountain-like Atikāya mounted on the car and equipped with his bow, like to roaring clouds (seen) on the occasion of the universal disruption.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं दृष्ट्वा महात्मानं राघवस्तु सुविस्मितः
वानरान्सान्त्वयित्वा तु विभीषणमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṁ rāghavastu suvismitaḥ
vānarānsāntvayitvā tu vibhīṣaṇamuvāca ha

translations.english: Seeing that huge-bodied one, Rāghava struck with surprise, comforting the monkeys, addressed Vibhisana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
य एष निशितैः शूलैः सुतीक्ष्णैः प्रासतोमरैः
अर्चिष्मद्भिर्वृतो भाति भूतैरिव महेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
ya eṣa niśitaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāsatomaraiḥ
arciṣmadbhirvṛto bhāti bhūtairiva maheśvaraḥ

translations.english: Who is this one resembling a mountain, furnished with a bow and having leonine eyes, that is stationed on a large car hoked with a thousand steeds, he that with effulgent sharpened darts and keen práśas and tomaras, shine like Maheśvara environed by spectres-he that displaying his fatal tongue appear splendid surrounded with darts in his car; like a mass of clouds graced with lightning.

verses.sanskrit:
धनूंसि चास्य सज्यानि हेमपृष्ठानि सर्वशः
शोभयन्ति रथश्रेष्ठं शक्रपातमिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
dhanūṁsi cāsya sajyāni hemapṛṣṭhāni sarvaśaḥ
śobhayanti rathaśreṣṭhaṁ śakrapātamivāmbaram

translations.english: And his bows adorned and backed with gold all over, beautify his car even as Indra's bow beautify the firmament.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्वजशृङ्गप्रतिष्ठेन राहुणाभिविराजते
सूर्यरश्मिप्रभैर्बाणैर्दिशो दश विराजयन्
verses.transliteration:
dhvajaśṛṅgapratiṣṭhena rāhuṇābhivirājate
sūryaraśmiprabhairbāṇairdiśo daśa virājayan

translations.english: Who is this foremost of Räkşasas and best of bowmen that embellishing the field of battle, approach on a car glorious as the sun; who,. displaying the ten cardinal points with his shafts resembling the rays of the sun, appear handsome with his peak of a banner bearing the figure of Rāhu, whose bow bent in three places, emitting roars resembling the rumbling of clouds, and plated with gold, look like the bow itself of Satakratu?

verses.sanskrit:
सध्वजः सपताकश्च सानुकर्षो महारथः
चतुःसादिसमायुक्तो मेघस्तनितनिस्वनः
verses.transliteration:
sadhvajaḥ sapatākaśca sānukarṣo mahārathaḥ
catuḥsādisamāyukto meghastanitanisvanaḥ

translations.english: His mighty car furnished with a banner and ensign and bottom, and having clatter resembling the roaring of clouds, has four horsemen (attached to it).

verses.sanskrit:
विंशतिर्दश चाष्टौ च तूणीररथमास्थिताः
कार्मुकाणि च भीमानि ज्याश्च काञ्चनपिङ्गलाः
verses.transliteration:
viṁśatirdaśa cāṣṭau ca tūṇīrarathamāsthitāḥ
kārmukāṇi ca bhīmāni jyāśca kāñcanapiṅgalāḥ

translations.english: There are on the car eight and thirty quivers and dreadful bows and yellow-golden bowstrings.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ च खड्गौ रथगतौ पार्श्वस्थौ पार्श्वशोभिनौ
चतुर्हस्तत्सरुचितौ व्यक्तहस्तदशायतौ
verses.transliteration:
dvau ca khaḍgau rathagatau pārśvasthau pārśvaśobhinau
caturhastatsarucitau vyaktahastadaśāyatau

translations.english: There are (in that car) two effulgent swords at iis side, illumining it, their hafts measuring four lands and their blades ten each.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्तकण्ठगुणो धीरो महापर्वतसंनिभः
कालः कालमहावक्त्रो मेघस्थ इव भास्करः
verses.transliteration:
raktakaṇṭhaguṇo dhīro mahāparvatasaṁnibhaḥ
kālaḥ kālamahāvaktro meghastha iva bhāskaraḥ

translations.english: That calm (warrior) wears red garlands about is neck, and resembles-a mighty mountain. And very destroyer, he has a mighty mouth, appearing like that of the destroyer himself; and he look like the sun stationed on clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाभ्यां भुजाभ्यामेष शोभते
शृङ्गाभ्यामिव तुङ्गाभ्यां हिमवान्पर्वतोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
kāñcanāṅgadanaddhābhyāṁ bhujābhyāmeṣa śobhate
śṛṅgābhyāmiva tuṅgābhyāṁ himavānparvatottamaḥ

translations.english: With his arms adorned with golden angadas, he appear splendid like that best of mountains the Himavān with its towering summits.

verses.sanskrit:
कुण्डलाभ्यां तु यस्यैतद्भाति वक्त्रं शुभेक्षणम्
पुनर्वस्वन्तरगतं पूर्णबिम्बमिवैन्दवम्
verses.transliteration:
kuṇḍalābhyāṁ tu yasyaitadbhāti vaktraṁ śubhekṣaṇam
punarvasvantaragataṁ pūrṇabimbamivaindavam

translations.english: With his pair of ear-rings, his charming yet terrific countenance shine like the full Moon entering into Punarvasu.* *The seventh lunar asterism.

verses.sanskrit:
आचक्ष्व मे महाबाहो त्वमेनं राक्षसोत्तमम्
यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे भयार्ता विद्रुता दिशः
verses.transliteration:
ācakṣva me mahābāho tvamenaṁ rākṣasottamam
yaṁ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve bhayārtā vidrutā diśaḥ

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, tell me all about this foremost of Rākşasas, seeing whom the monkeys, overwhelmed with fear, fly away in all directions.

verses.sanskrit:
स पृष्ठो राजपुत्रेण रामेणामिततेजसा
आचचक्षे महातेजा राघवाय विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
sa pṛṣṭho rājaputreṇa rāmeṇāmitatejasā
ācacakṣe mahātejā rāghavāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Asked by the king's son Rāma of immeasurable prowess, the exceedingly energetic Vibhīşaņa spoke to Rāma, informing him.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यासीद्वीर्यवान्पुत्रो रावणप्रतिमो रणे
वृद्धसेवी श्रुतधरः सर्वास्त्रविदुषां वरः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāsīdvīryavānputro rāvaṇapratimo raṇe
vṛddhasevī śrutadharaḥ sarvāstraviduṣāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: The highly powerful.king, Vaisravana's younger brother of dreadful deeds, the highsouled Rävaņa, is the sovereign of the Rāks asas. This one is his mighty son, like to Rāvaņa himself in strength. He serve the aged, is of wide celebrity and is the prime of those versed in all branches of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य बाहुं समाश्रित्य लङ्का भवति निर्भया
तनयं धान्यमालिन्या अतिकायमिमं विदुः
verses.transliteration:
yasya bāhuṁ samāśritya laṅkā bhavati nirbhayā
tanayaṁ dhānyamālinyā atikāyamimaṁ viduḥ

translations.english: He is competent to ride horses and elephants, to wield the sword or draw the bcw, or in sowing dissensions, or giving away, or in counsel, he reposing in whose arm Lanka has cast off fear. Know him to be Atikāya, son to Dhānyamāli.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेनाराधितो ब्रह्मा तपसा भावितात्मना
अस्त्राणि चाप्यवाप्तानि रिपवश्च पराजिताः
verses.transliteration:
etenārādhito brahmā tapasā bhāvitātmanā
astrāṇi cāpyavāptāni ripavaśca parājitāḥ

translations.english: Having adored the pure-souled Brahma with austerities, he has obtained weapons, and has defeated his foes (in fight).

verses.sanskrit:
सुरासुरैरवध्यत्वं दत्तमस्मै स्वयम्भुवा
एतच्च कवचं दिव्यं रथश्चैषोऽर्कभास्करः
verses.transliteration:
surāsurairavadhyatvaṁ dattamasmai svayambhuvā
etacca kavacaṁ divyaṁ rathaścaiṣo'rkabhāskaraḥ

translations.english: You shall be incapable of being slain by celestials and Asura's was the boon conferred on him by the self-sprung; and he also gave him this celestial mail and this car resembling the effulgent Sun himself.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन शतशो देवा दानवाश्च पराजिताः
रक्षितानि च रक्षामि यक्षाश्चापि निषूदिताः
verses.transliteration:
etena śataśo devā dānavāśca parājitāḥ
rakṣitāni ca rakṣāmi yakṣāścāpi niṣūditāḥ

translations.english: He has vanquished (in battle) hundreds of deities and Dänavas; and he has always) protected the Rakşasas, and destroyed Yakşas.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रं विष्टम्भितं येन बाणैरिन्द्रस्य धीमतः
पाशः सलिलराजस्य युद्धे प्रतिहतस्तथा
verses.transliteration:
vajraṁ viṣṭambhitaṁ yena bāṇairindrasya dhīmataḥ
pāśaḥ salilarājasya yuddhe pratihatastathā

translations.english: This intelligent one resisted the thunder-bolt itself of Indra; and in encounter baffled the very noonse of the king of waters.

verses.sanskrit:
एषोऽतिकायो बलवान्राक्षसानामथर्षभः
रावणस्य सुतो धीमान्देवदनव दर्पहा
verses.transliteration:
eṣo'tikāyo balavānrākṣasānāmatharṣabhaḥ
rāvaṇasya suto dhīmāndevadanava darpahā

translations.english: This one is Atikāya-foremost of Raksasas; and that son of Rāvana is the humbler of the hauteur of deities and Dänavas.

verses.sanskrit:
तदस्मिन्क्रियतां यत्नः क्षिप्रं पुरुषपुंगव
पुरा वानरसैन्यानि क्षयं नयति सायकैः
verses.transliteration:
tadasminkriyatāṁ yatnaḥ kṣipraṁ puruṣapuṁgava
purā vānarasainyāni kṣayaṁ nayati sāyakaiḥ

translations.english: Therefore, O best of persons, do you endeavour your best. This one with his shafts slaughter the monkey-hosts before (us).

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽतिकायो बलवान्प्रविश्य हरिवाहिनीम्
विस्फारयामास धनुर्ननाद च पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tato'tikāyo balavānpraviśya harivāhinīm
visphārayāmāsa dhanurnanāda ca punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Then the powerful Atikāya entering that monkey-force, stretched his bow and shouted again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
कुमुदो द्विविदो मैन्दो नीलः शरभ एव च
पादपैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च युगपत्समभिद्रवन्
verses.transliteration:
kumudo dvivido maindo nīlaḥ śarabha eva ca
pādapairgiriśṛṅgaiśca yugapatsamabhidravan

translations.english: The high-souled principal monkeys, seeing that (hero) possessed of a dreadful person, that best of car-warriors-stationed on his car, rushed forward. And Kumuda and Dvivida and Mainda and Nila and Sarabha dashed on at one time with trees and mountain-peaks.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां वृक्षांश्च शैलांश्च शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः
अतिकायो महातेजाश्चिच्छेदास्त्रविदां वरः
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ vṛkṣāṁśca śailāṁśca śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ
atikāyo mahātejāścicchedāstravidāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon that foremost of those skilled in weapons, the exceedingly energetic Atikāya, severed those trees and rocks by means of shafts dight with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
तांश्चैव सरान्स हरीञ्शरैः सर्वायसैर्बली
विव्याधाभिमुखः संख्ये भीमकायो निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁścaiva sarānsa harīñśaraiḥ sarvāyasairbalī
vivyādhābhimukhaḥ saṁkhye bhīmakāyo niśācaraḥ

translations.english: In that encounter that powerful one possessed of a gigantic person, skilled in arms, pierced all those monkeys staying before him with arrows entirely made of iron.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽर्दिता बाणबर्षेण भिन्नगात्राः प्लवंगमाः
न शेकुरतिकायस्य प्रतिकर्तुं महारणे
verses.transliteration:
te'rditā bāṇabarṣeṇa bhinnagātrāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
na śekuratikāyasya pratikartuṁ mahāraṇe

translations.english: And agonised, having their persons pierced in that mighty conflict by that arrowy shower, they were incapable of resisting the same.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सैन्यं हरिवीराणां त्रासयामास राक्षसः
मृगयूथमिव क्रुद्धो हरिर्यौवनमास्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tatsainyaṁ harivīrāṇāṁ trāsayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ
mṛgayūthamiva kruddho hariryauvanamāsthitaḥ

translations.english: The Rakşasas terrified that host of monkeyheroes, even as an enraged lion priding in his youth terrify a society of deer.

verses.sanskrit:
स राषसेन्द्रो हरिसैन्यमध्ये; नायुध्यमानं निजघान कंचित्
उपेत्य रामं सधनुः कलापी; सगर्वितं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे
verses.transliteration:
sa rāṣasendro harisainyamadhye; nāyudhyamānaṁ nijaghāna kaṁcit
upetya rāmaṁ sadhanuḥ kalāpī; sagarvitaṁ vākyamidaṁ babhāṣe

translations.english: In the midst of those bands of monkeys, that lord of Raksasas did not slay anyone without battle. And then springing up before Rāma, that one furnished with his bow and quiver, addressed him in haughty words, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
रथे स्थितोऽहं शरचापपाणि;र्न प्राकृतं कंचन योधयामि
यस्यास्ति शक्तिर्व्यवसाय युक्ता; ददातुं मे क्षिप्रमिहाद्य युद्धम्
verses.transliteration:
rathe sthito'haṁ śaracāpapāṇi;rna prākṛtaṁ kaṁcana yodhayāmi
yasyāsti śaktirvyavasāya yuktā; dadātuṁ me kṣipramihādya yuddham

translations.english: Stationed in this car holding the bow and arrows in my hands, I will not fight any that is ignoble. Him that has strength, and that also understand this business, let him today speedily give me battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य; चुकोप सौमित्रिरमित्रहन्ता
अमृष्यमाणश्च समुत्पपात; जग्राह चापं च ततः स्मयित्वा
verses.transliteration:
tattasya vākyaṁ bruvato niśamya; cukopa saumitriramitrahantā
amṛṣyamāṇaśca samutpapāta; jagrāha cāpaṁ ca tataḥ smayitvā

translations.english: Hearing his speech, that slayer of foesSumitrā's son, was fired with wrath. And not bearing him, he sprang forward disregarding his antagonist's words, and took up his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धः सौमित्रिरुत्पत्य तूणादाक्षिप्य सायकम्
पुरस्तादतिकायस्य विचकर्ष महद्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
kruddhaḥ saumitrirutpatya tūṇādākṣipya sāyakam
purastādatikāyasya vicakarṣa mahaddhanuḥ

translations.english: And flying to fury, Sumitra's son, darting up, took out arrows from his quiver, and stretched his mighty bow in front of Atikāya.

verses.sanskrit:
पूरयन्स महीं शैलानाकाशं सागरं दिशः
ज्याशब्दो लक्ष्मणस्योग्रस्त्रासयन्रजनीचरान्
verses.transliteration:
pūrayansa mahīṁ śailānākāśaṁ sāgaraṁ diśaḥ
jyāśabdo lakṣmaṇasyograstrāsayanrajanīcarān

translations.english: Filling the entire earth and the sky and the ocean and all the cardinal quarters, the terrific twang of Lakşmaņa's bow struck terror into the (hearts of the) night-rangers.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रेश्चापनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा प्रतिभयं तदा
विसिष्मिये महातेजा राक्षसेन्द्रात्मजो बली
verses.transliteration:
saumitreścāpanirghoṣaṁ śrutvā pratibhayaṁ tadā
visiṣmiye mahātejā rākṣasendrātmajo balī

translations.english: Hearing the dreadful twang of the bow of Sumitrā's son, the exceedingly energetic and powerful son of the lord of Rākşasas was struck with surprise.

verses.sanskrit:
अथातिकायः कुपितो दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमुत्थितम्
आदाय निशितं बाणमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
athātikāyaḥ kupito dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamutthitam
ādāya niśitaṁ bāṇamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Then Atikāya, enraged, seeing Lakşmaņa advance, taking sharpened shafts, spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
बालस्त्वमसि सौमित्रे विक्रमेष्वविचक्षणः
गच्छ किं कालसदृशं मां योधयितुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
bālastvamasi saumitre vikrameṣvavicakṣaṇaḥ
gaccha kiṁ kālasadṛśaṁ māṁ yodhayitumicchasi

translations.english: You are a bc/, O Sumitra's sons and as such know not how to display prowess. Go you. Why wish you to fight with me resembling death itself.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि मद्बाहुसृष्टानामस्त्राणां हिमवानपि
सोढुमुत्सहते वेगमन्तरिक्षमथो मही
verses.transliteration:
na hi madbāhusṛṣṭānāmastrāṇāṁ himavānapi
soḍhumutsahate vegamantarikṣamatho mahī

translations.english: Not Himālaya itself or the firmament or the earth is capable of bearing the impetuosity of shafts shot by my arms.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखप्रसुप्तं कालाग्निं प्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि
न्यस्य चापं निवर्तस्व मा प्राणाञ्जहि मद्गतः
verses.transliteration:
sukhaprasuptaṁ kālāgniṁ prabodhayitumicchasi
nyasya cāpaṁ nivartasva mā prāṇāñjahi madgataḥ

translations.english: You wish to rouse a fire slumbering sweetly. Leaving alone your bow, do you return. Do not lose your life by coming in contact with me.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा त्वं प्रतिष्टब्धो न निवर्तितुमिच्छसि
तिष्ठ प्राणान्परित्यज्य गमिष्यसि यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vā tvaṁ pratiṣṭabdho na nivartitumicchasi
tiṣṭha prāṇānparityajya gamiṣyasi yamakṣayam

translations.english: Or it may be that you are proud; and therefore, have no mind to return. Stay then. Renouncing your life, you shall go to Yama's mansion.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्य मे निशितान्बाणानरिदर्पनिषूदनान्
ईश्वरायुधसंकाशांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणान्
verses.transliteration:
paśya me niśitānbāṇānaridarpaniṣūdanān
īśvarāyudhasaṁkāśāṁstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇān

translations.english: Behold my whetted arrows-crushers of the insolence of foes resembling the weapon itself of the Lord,* adorned with burnished gold. *Isvara, Siva, His weapon is the trident.

verses.sanskrit:
एष ते सर्पसंकाशो बाणः पास्यति शोणितम्
मृगराज इव क्रुद्धो नागराजस्य शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
eṣa te sarpasaṁkāśo bāṇaḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
mṛgarāja iva kruddho nāgarājasya śoṇitam

translations.english: Even as a lion enraged shedded the blood of a mighty elephant, this arrow of mine resembling a serpent shall shed your blood. Having delivered himself thus, he fired with wrath set his shaft on his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वातिकायस्य वचः सरोषं; सगर्वितं संयति राजपुत्रः
स संचुकोपातिबलो बृहच्छ्री;रुवाच वाक्यं च ततो महार्थम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvātikāyasya vacaḥ saroṣaṁ; sagarvitaṁ saṁyati rājaputraḥ
sa saṁcukopātibalo bṛhacchrī;ruvāca vākyaṁ ca tato mahārtham

translations.english: Hearing in that encounter Atikāya's wrathful speech fraught with hauteur, the highly powerful and intelligent son of the king possessed of exceeding grace, was transported with passion; and he said.

verses.sanskrit:
न वाक्यमात्रेण भवान्प्रधानो; न कत्थनात्सत्पुरुषा भवन्ति
मयि स्थिते धन्विनि बाणपाणौ; विदर्शयस्वात्मबलं दुरात्मन्
verses.transliteration:
na vākyamātreṇa bhavānpradhāno; na katthanātsatpuruṣā bhavanti
mayi sthite dhanvini bāṇapāṇau; vidarśayasvātmabalaṁ durātman

translations.english: You can not attain pre-eminence solely by virtue of your speech. One cannot be a worthy person simply by say. O wicked-minded one, do you display your strength on me equipped with the bow and holding arrows in my hands.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मणा सूचयात्मानं न विकत्थितुमर्हसि
पौरुषेण तु यो युक्तः स तु शूर इति स्मृतः
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇā sūcayātmānaṁ na vikatthitumarhasi
pauruṣeṇa tu yo yuktaḥ sa tu śūra iti smṛtaḥ

translations.english: Manifest yourself by your valour, you ought not to blow your own trumpet. He, who is actually powerful identified as a real gallant.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वायुधसमायुक्तो धन्वी त्वं रथमास्थितः
शरैर्वा यदि वाप्यस्त्रैर्दर्शयस्व पराक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvāyudhasamāyukto dhanvī tvaṁ rathamāsthitaḥ
śarairvā yadi vāpyastrairdarśayasva parākramam

translations.english: Seated on a chariot and skilled in archery you are equipped with all weapons, therefore, you display your own prowess either with your arrows or with arms.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शिरस्ते निशितैः पातयिष्याम्यहं शरैः
मारुतः कालसंपक्वं वृन्तात्तालफलं यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śiraste niśitaiḥ pātayiṣyāmyahaṁ śaraiḥ
mārutaḥ kālasaṁpakvaṁ vṛntāttālaphalaṁ yathā

translations.english: Then, I shall cut off your head with my sharpened arrows like wind falls down a palm fruit from its stalk, ripened in the process of time.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य ते मामका बाणास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः
पास्यन्ति रुधिरं गात्राद्बाणशल्यान्तरोत्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
adya te māmakā bāṇāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
pāsyanti rudhiraṁ gātrādbāṇaśalyāntarotthitam

translations.english: To-day shall my shafts decked in gold, drink your blood flowing from your person and issuing of wounds inflicted by my resembling darts.

verses.sanskrit:
बालोऽयमिति विज्ञाय न मावज्ञातुमर्हसि
बालो वा यदि वा वृद्धो मृत्युं जानीहि संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
bālo'yamiti vijñāya na māvajñātumarhasi
bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho mṛtyuṁ jānīhi saṁyuge

translations.english: 'This one is a boy', thinking this, you ought not to slight me. Whether I am a boy or an old* man' death shall you know in the conflict. *The commentator says the passage means-"You know (me) for death itself.” I prefer the sense given.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विद्याधरा भूता देवा दैत्या महर्षयः
गुह्यकाश्च महात्मानस्तद्युद्धं ददृशुस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tato vidyādharā bhūtā devā daityā maharṣayaḥ
guhyakāśca mahātmānastadyuddhaṁ dadṛśustadā

translations.english: It was as a boy that Vişņu had overpowered the triune world with his prowess.” Hearing Laksmana's words, fraught with reason and high sense, Vidyadharas and ghosts, deities, Daityas out arrows and Maharşis, and the high-souled Guhyakas then beheld that marvel.* *The encounter that ensued between Lakşmaņa and Atikāya.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽतिकायः कुपितश्चापमारोप्य सायकम्
लक्ष्मणस्य प्रचिक्षेप संक्षिपन्निव चाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'tikāyaḥ kupitaścāpamāropya sāyakam
lakṣmaṇasya pracikṣepa saṁkṣipanniva cāmbaram

translations.english: Then Atikāya, enraged, setting his arrow on his bow, shot it at Lakşmaņa, as if devouring up the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं निशितं शरमाशीविषोपमम्
अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ niśitaṁ śaramāśīviṣopamam
ardhacandreṇa ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā

translations.english: Thereat, Lakşmaņa-slayer of hostile heroes-with a crescent severed that sharpened shaft resembling a venomous serpent, as it was descending.

verses.sanskrit:
तं निकृत्तं शरं दृष्ट्वा कृत्तभोगमिवोरगम्
अतिकायो भृशं क्रुद्धः पञ्चबाणान्समाददे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ nikṛttaṁ śaraṁ dṛṣṭvā kṛttabhogamivoragam
atikāyo bhṛśaṁ kruddhaḥ pañcabāṇānsamādade

translations.english: Seeing the shaft severed, like a serpent having its person cut off, Atikāya waxing exceedingly enraged, took up five arrow; and the nightranger discharged them at Lakşmaņa. Thereat Bharata's younger brother cut off the approaching arrows with whetted shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स तांश्छित्त्वा शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
आददे निशितं बाणं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁśchittvā śaraistīkṣṇairlakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
ādade niśitaṁ bāṇaṁ jvalantamiva tejasā

translations.english: Having severed them with sharpened shafts, Lakşmaņa— slayer of hostile heroes-took up a sharpened arrow, as if flaming in energy.

verses.sanskrit:
तमादाय धनुः श्रेष्ठे योजयामास लक्ष्मणः
विचकर्ष च वेगेन विससर्ज च सायकम्
verses.transliteration:
tamādāya dhanuḥ śreṣṭhe yojayāmāsa lakṣmaṇaḥ
vicakarṣa ca vegena visasarja ca sāyakam

translations.english: And taking it, Lakşmaņa set it on his excellent bow; and drawing the latter, vigorously discharged the shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन शरेणानत पर्वणा
ललाटे राक्षसश्रेष्ठमाजघान स वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena śareṇānata parvaṇā
lalāṭe rākṣasaśreṣṭhamājaghāna sa vīryavān

translations.english: That hero endowed with prowess hit that foremost of Rākşasas in the forehead with that i shaft having bent knots, discharged from his bow drawn to its full bent.

verses.sanskrit:
स ललाटे शरो मग्नस्तस्य भीमस्य रक्षसः
ददृशे शोणितेनाक्तः पन्नगेन्द्र इवाहवे
verses.transliteration:
sa lalāṭe śaro magnastasya bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ
dadṛśe śoṇitenāktaḥ pannagendra ivāhave

translations.english: That arrow piercing the forehead of that dreadful Raksasas, and smeared with blood, appeared like the lord of serpents in a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्तयामास चाश्वस्य विमृश्य च महाबलः
साधु बाणनिपातेन श्वाघनीयोऽसि मे रिपुः
verses.transliteration:
cintayāmāsa cāśvasya vimṛśya ca mahābalaḥ
sādhu bāṇanipātena śvāghanīyo'si me ripuḥ

translations.english: The Raksasas, smarting under Laksmana's shaft, showered, like the dreadful gateway of Tripura battered by Rudra. Then recovering himself and reflecting, he said.* *Cintayāmasa-thought, I apprehend, means said in this connection.

verses.sanskrit:
विचार्यैवं विनम्यास्यं विनम्य च भुजावुभौ
स रथोपस्थमास्थाय रथेन प्रचचार ह
verses.transliteration:
vicāryaivaṁ vinamyāsyaṁ vinamya ca bhujāvubhau
sa rathopasthamāsthāya rathena pracacāra ha

translations.english: Excellent well! By this discharge of your shaft, you approve yourself as a foe in whom I can well glory. Having spoken thus candidly, he, folding his hands at ease, and seated on the platform of his car, began to range in it.

verses.sanskrit:
एकं त्रीन्पञ्च सप्तेति सायकान्राक्षसर्षभः
आददे संदधे चापि विचकर्षोत्ससर्ज च
verses.transliteration:
ekaṁ trīnpañca sapteti sāyakānrākṣasarṣabhaḥ
ādade saṁdadhe cāpi vicakarṣotsasarja ca

translations.english: Then that foremost of Raksasas began to take up, set and shoot one, three, five, or seven shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ते बाणाः कालसंकाशा राक्षसेन्द्रधनुश्च्युताः
हेमपुङ्खा रविप्रख्याश्चक्रुर्दीप्तमिवाम्बरम्
verses.transliteration:
te bāṇāḥ kālasaṁkāśā rākṣasendradhanuścyutāḥ
hemapuṅkhā raviprakhyāścakrurdīptamivāmbaram

translations.english: Those shafts resembling Fate itself, plated with gold at the feathered parts, and looking like the Sun himself (in splendour), discharged from the bow of the lord of Rakşasas, lighted up the heavens.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तान्राक्षसोत्सृष्टाञ्शरौघान्रावणानुजः
असंभ्रान्तः प्रचिच्छेद निशितैर्बहुभिः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tatastānrākṣasotsṛṣṭāñśaraughānrāvaṇānujaḥ
asaṁbhrāntaḥ praciccheda niśitairbahubhiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Thereat Raghava's younger brother by means of many a sharpened shaft calmly cut off all those vollies of arrows shot by the Rakşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
ताञ्शरान्युधि संप्रेक्ष्य निकृत्तान्रावणात्मजः
चुकोप त्रिदशेन्द्रारिर्जग्राह निशितं शरम्
verses.transliteration:
tāñśarānyudhi saṁprekṣya nikṛttānrāvaṇātmajaḥ
cukopa tridaśendrārirjagrāha niśitaṁ śaram

translations.english: And finding all those arrows riven in the encounter, that enemy of the lord of the immortals, Ravana's son, was fired with wrath, and took up a whetted shaft.

verses.sanskrit:
स संधाय महातेजास्तं बाणं सहसोत्सृजत्
ततः सौमित्रिमायान्तमाजघान स्तनान्तरे
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁdhāya mahātejāstaṁ bāṇaṁ sahasotsṛjat
tataḥ saumitrimāyāntamājaghāna stanāntare

translations.english: Then aiming that arrow, that highly powerful one suddenly shot it; and with that, rushing on, hit Sumitra's son in the chest.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिकायेन सौमित्रिस्ताडितो युधि वक्षसि
सुस्राव रुधिरं तीव्रं मदं मत्त इव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
atikāyena saumitristāḍito yudhi vakṣasi
susrāva rudhiraṁ tīvraṁ madaṁ matta iva dvipaḥ

translations.english: Struck in the encounter by Atikaya, the son of Sumitra began to bleed copiously, like a mad elephant discharging the temporal jouice.

verses.sanskrit:
स चकार तदात्मानं विशल्यं सहसा विभुः
जग्राह च शरं तीष्णमस्त्रेणापि समादधे
verses.transliteration:
sa cakāra tadātmānaṁ viśalyaṁ sahasā vibhuḥ
jagrāha ca śaraṁ tīṣṇamastreṇāpi samādadhe

translations.english: Then that lord at once extricated the arrow; and then took up a keen shaft and fixed the same on his weapon.* *i.e. the bow.

verses.sanskrit:
आग्नेयेन तदास्त्रेण योजयामास सायकम्
स जज्वाल तदा बाणो धनुश्चास्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration:
āgneyena tadāstreṇa yojayāmāsa sāyakam
sa jajvāla tadā bāṇo dhanuścāsya mahātmanaḥ

translations.english: Then he set a shaft (on his bow-string) reciting a formula for the Agneya* (Belonging to the god of Fire.) weapon; and thereat his arrow as well as bow flamed up.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिकायोऽतितेजस्वी सौरमस्त्रं समाददे
तेन बाणं भुजंगाभं हेमपुङ्खमयोजयत्
verses.transliteration:
atikāyo'titejasvī sauramastraṁ samādade
tena bāṇaṁ bhujaṁgābhaṁ hemapuṅkhamayojayat

translations.english: Then the highly powerful Atikaya took up a Ruadra* weapon; and thereon fixed a shaft plated with gold at the feathered part, and resembling a serpent in sheen. *Relative to Rudra.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तं ज्वलितं घोरं लक्ष्मणः शरमाहितम्
अतिकायाय चिक्षेप कालदण्डमिवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
tatastaṁ jvalitaṁ ghoraṁ lakṣmaṇaḥ śaramāhitam
atikāyāya cikṣepa kāladaṇḍamivāntakaḥ

translations.english: And even as the reaper hurled his rod, did Lakşmaņa hurl that weapon inspired with divine energy, dreadful and aflame, at Atikaya.

verses.sanskrit:
आग्नेयेनाभिसंयुक्तं दृष्ट्वा बाणं निशाचरः
उत्ससर्ज तदा बाणं दीप्तं सूर्यास्त्रयोजितम्
verses.transliteration:
āgneyenābhisaṁyuktaṁ dṛṣṭvā bāṇaṁ niśācaraḥ
utsasarja tadā bāṇaṁ dīptaṁ sūryāstrayojitam

translations.english: Seeing that shaft set upon an Āgneya weapon, that night-ranger discharged a Raudra arrow set upon a Solar weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
तावुभावम्बरे बाणावन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः
तेजसा संप्रदीप्ताग्रौ क्रुद्धाविव भुजं गमौ
verses.transliteration:
tāvubhāvambare bāṇāvanyonyamabhijaghnatuḥ
tejasā saṁpradīptāgrau kruddhāviva bhujaṁ gamau

translations.english: There like a pair of infuriated serpents, those arrows with their heads flaming in energy, baffled each other in the sky. And burning each other, the shafts fell on the earth; and those best of arrows, shorn of brilliance and reduced to ashes, were deprived of their splendour. And having blazed in the welkin, those two fell down to the earth reft of their lustre.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽतिकायः संक्रुद्धस्त्वस्त्रमैषीकमुत्सृजत्
तत्प्रचिच्छेद सौमित्रिरस्त्रमैन्द्रेण वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
tato'tikāyaḥ saṁkruddhastvastramaiṣīkamutsṛjat
tatpraciccheda saumitrirastramaindreṇa vīryavān

translations.english: Then Atikāya wrought up with wrath discharged an arrow called Aişīka dedicated to Tvaştā. Thereat the powerful son of Sumitrā severed that shaft by an Aindra* weapon. *Belonging to Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
ऐषीकं निहतं दृष्ट्वा कुमारो रावणात्मजः
याम्येनास्त्रेण संक्रुद्धो योजयामास सायकम्
verses.transliteration:
aiṣīkaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā kumāro rāvaṇātmajaḥ
yāmyenāstreṇa saṁkruddho yojayāmāsa sāyakam

translations.english: Seeing Aisika baffled, that Prince-son to Rāvana-fired with rage, fixed an arrow on a Yămya' weapon; and then the night-ranger shot that weapon at Lakşmaņa. And Lakşmaņa resisted it by a Vāyavya' weapon. 1. What could this be like? The commentator is silent over this important point. 2. Belonging to the wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
अथैनं शरधाराभिर्धाराभिरिव तोयदः
अभ्यवर्षत संक्रुद्धो लक्ष्मणो रावणात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
athainaṁ śaradhārābhirdhārābhiriva toyadaḥ
abhyavarṣata saṁkruddho lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇātmajam

translations.english: Then as a mass of clouds poured down showers, Laksmana, enraged, poured volleys of shafts on Rāvana's son.

verses.sanskrit:
तेऽतिकायं समासाद्य कवचे वज्रभूषिते
भग्नाग्रशल्याः सहसा पेतुर्बाणा महीतले
verses.transliteration:
te'tikāyaṁ samāsādya kavace vajrabhūṣite
bhagnāgraśalyāḥ sahasā peturbāṇā mahītale

translations.english: Thereupon, hitting Atikāya, those arrows coming in contact with his mail, had their barbs broken, and fell down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्मोघानभिसंप्रेक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
अभ्यवर्षत बाणानां सहस्रेण महायशाः
verses.transliteration:
tānmoghānabhisaṁprekṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
abhyavarṣata bāṇānāṁ sahasreṇa mahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Seeing them baffled, that slayer of hostile heroes-the renowned Laksmana-began to shower shafts by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
स वर्ष्यमाणो बाणौघैरतिकायो महाबलः
अवध्यकवचः संख्ये राक्षसो नैव विव्यथे
verses.transliteration:
sa varṣyamāṇo bāṇaughairatikāyo mahābalaḥ
avadhyakavacaḥ saṁkhye rākṣaso naiva vivyathe

translations.english: And albeit showered with those arrows, that Raksasas, the mighty Atikāya-in that encounter was not pierced by them on account of his impenetrable mail; and that best of men failed to hurt him in the contest.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मदत्तवरो ह्येष अवध्य कवचावृतः
ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेण भिन्ध्येनमेष वध्यो हि नान्यथा
verses.transliteration:
brahmadattavaro hyeṣa avadhya kavacāvṛtaḥ
brāhmeṇāstreṇa bhindhyenameṣa vadhyo hi nānyathā

translations.english: Then approaching him, the wind-god spoke to him, saying, "This one has received a boon from Brahmā, and is covered with an impenetrable mail. Pierce him with a Brahma* weapon. He cannot otherwise be slain. This one clad in mail and endowed with prowess is forsooth incapable of being slain by others." *Belonging to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स वायोर्वचनं निशम्य; सौमित्रिरिन्द्रप्रतिमानवीर्यः
समाददे बाणममोघवेगं; तद्ब्राह्ममस्त्रं सहसा नियोज्य
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa vāyorvacanaṁ niśamya; saumitririndrapratimānavīryaḥ
samādade bāṇamamoghavegaṁ; tadbrāhmamastraṁ sahasā niyojya

translations.english: Hearing the words of the wind-god, Sumitrā's son like to Indra in prowess took an arrow endowed with fierce impetuosity, and at once set it on a Brahma weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्वरास्त्रे तु नियुज्यमाने; सौमित्रिणा बाणवरे शिताग्रे
दिशः सचन्द्रार्कमहाग्रहाश्च; नभश्च तत्रास ररास चोर्वी
verses.transliteration:
tasminvarāstre tu niyujyamāne; saumitriṇā bāṇavare śitāgre
diśaḥ sacandrārkamahāgrahāśca; nabhaśca tatrāsa rarāsa corvī

translations.english: On that sharp-headed best of arrows being fixed on that foremost of weapons, the cardinal quarters and the Moon and the sun and the mighty planets and the sky were saized with affright; and the earth shook.

verses.sanskrit:
तं ब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेण नियुज्य चापे; शरं सुपुङ्खं यमदूतकल्पम्
सौमित्रिरिन्द्रारिसुतस्य तस्य; ससर्ज बाणं युधि वज्रकल्पम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ brahmaṇo'streṇa niyujya cāpe; śaraṁ supuṅkhaṁ yamadūtakalpam
saumitririndrārisutasya tasya; sasarja bāṇaṁ yudhi vajrakalpam

translations.english: And inspiring that arrow furnished with a feathered part and resembling an emissary of Yama himself, and fixing the same on his bow, Sumitrā's son in that encounter discharged that shaft like to the thunder-bolt at the son of the enemy of Indra.

verses.sanskrit:
तं लक्ष्मणोत्सृष्टममोघवेगं; समापतन्तं ज्वलनप्रकाशम्
सुवर्णवज्रोत्तमचित्रपुङ्खं; तदातिकायः समरे ददर्श
verses.transliteration:
taṁ lakṣmaṇotsṛṣṭamamoghavegaṁ; samāpatantaṁ jvalanaprakāśam
suvarṇavajrottamacitrapuṅkhaṁ; tadātikāyaḥ samare dadarśa

translations.english: And in that conflict Atikāya beheld that shaft fair-feathered and having its feathered part dight with splendid diamonds, acquiring enhanced vehemence arising from its having been discharged by Lakşmaņa, and hissing and rushing on with tremendous impetuosity.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रेक्षमाणः सहसातिकायो; जघान बाणैर्निशितैरनेकैः
स सायकस्तस्य सुपर्णवेग;स्तदातिवेगेन जगाम पार्श्वम्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasātikāyo; jaghāna bāṇairniśitairanekaiḥ
sa sāyakastasya suparṇavega;stadātivegena jagāma pārśvam

translations.english: Seeing it, Atikäya swiftly resisted it with countless sharpened shafts. But endowed with the energy of Suparna himself, that shaft vehemently went to him.

verses.sanskrit:
तमागतं प्रेक्ष्य तदातिकायो; बाणं प्रदीप्तान्तककालकल्पम्
जघान शक्त्यृष्टिगदाकुठारैः; शूलैर्हलैश्चाप्यविपन्नचेष्टः
verses.transliteration:
tamāgataṁ prekṣya tadātikāyo; bāṇaṁ pradīptāntakakālakalpam
jaghāna śaktyṛṣṭigadākuṭhāraiḥ; śūlairhalaiścāpyavipannaceṣṭaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that shaft flaming and resembling the Fatal destroyer himself, coming, he, exerting himself to the utmost resisted it with darts and Rştis and maces and adzes and javelins and arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यायुधान्यद्भुतविग्रहाणि; मोघानि कृत्वा स शरोऽग्निदीप्तः
प्रसह्य तस्यैव किरीटजुष्टं; तदातिकायस्य शिरो जहार
verses.transliteration:
tānyāyudhānyadbhutavigrahāṇi; moghāni kṛtvā sa śaro'gnidīptaḥ
prasahya tasyaiva kirīṭajuṣṭaṁ; tadātikāyasya śiro jahāra

translations.english: But beating down all those weapons of wonderful forms, that arrow alive with flames, coming to the diadem-decked head of Atikāya, severed the same (in twain).

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छिरः सशिरस्त्राणं लक्ष्मणेषुप्रपीडितम्
पपात सहसा भूमौ शृङ्गं हिमवतो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tacchiraḥ saśirastrāṇaṁ lakṣmaṇeṣuprapīḍitam
papāta sahasā bhūmau śṛṅgaṁ himavato yathā

translations.english: That head furnished with a corsalet, cut off by Laksmana's arrow, suddenly dropped to the earth, like a summit of Himavān toppling (to the ground).

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहर्षयुक्ता बहवस्तु वानरा; प्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमाननास्तदा
अपूजयँल्लक्ष्मणमिष्टभागिनं; हते रिपौ भीमबले दुरासदे
verses.transliteration:
praharṣayuktā bahavastu vānarā; prabuddhapadmapratimānanāstadā
apūjaya̐llakṣmaṇamiṣṭabhāginaṁ; hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade

translations.english: On their foe endowed with terrific prowess and incapable of being conformed, having been slain, innumerable monkeys filled with excess of joy, and displaying countenances resembling blown lotuses, paid homage to Lakşmaņa working out their welfare.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हतान्राक्षसपुंगवांस्ता;न्देवान्तकादित्रिशिरोऽतिकायान्
रक्षोगणास्तत्र हतावशिष्टा;स्ते रावणाय त्वरितं शशंसुः
verses.transliteration:
tato hatānrākṣasapuṁgavāṁstā;ndevāntakāditriśiro'tikāyān
rakṣogaṇāstatra hatāvaśiṣṭā;ste rāvaṇāya tvaritaṁ śaśaṁsuḥ

translations.english: Those Raksas that remained after the others had been slain, swiftly informed Răvaņa that all those foremost of Rākşasas Devantaka and the rest, Trisiras, Atikāya and others-had been slain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हतांस्तान्सहसा निशम्य; राजा मुमोहाश्रुपरिप्लुताक्षः
पुत्रक्षयं भ्रातृवधं च घोरं; विचिन्त्य राजा विपुलं प्रदध्यौ
verses.transliteration:
tato hatāṁstānsahasā niśamya; rājā mumohāśrupariplutākṣaḥ
putrakṣayaṁ bhrātṛvadhaṁ ca ghoraṁ; vicintya rājā vipulaṁ pradadhyau

translations.english: Suddenly hearing them slain, the king with his eyes charged with brine, thinking of the disastrous destruction of his sons and brothers, was extremely agonized.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु राजानमुदीक्ष्य दीनं; शोकार्णवे संपरिपुप्लुवानम्
अथर्षभो राक्षसराजसूनु;रथेन्द्रजिद्वाक्यमिदं बभाषे
verses.transliteration:
tatastu rājānamudīkṣya dīnaṁ; śokārṇave saṁparipupluvānam
atharṣabho rākṣasarājasūnu;rathendrajidvākyamidaṁ babhāṣe

translations.english: Thereupon, seeing the king afflicted, and sunk in a sea of sorrow, that foremost of carwarriors-son to the Räkşasa king—Indrajit, addressed (his sire), saying.

verses.sanskrit:
न तात मोहं प्रतिगन्तुमर्हसि; यत्रेन्द्रजिज्जीवति राक्षसेन्द्र
नेन्द्रारिबाणाभिहतो हि कश्चि;त्प्राणान्समर्थः समरेऽभिधर्तुम्
verses.transliteration:
na tāta mohaṁ pratigantumarhasi; yatrendrajijjīvati rākṣasendra
nendrāribāṇābhihato hi kaści;tprāṇānsamarthaḥ samare'bhidhartum

translations.english: O father, it does not behove you to be overcome with this excessive grief, inasmuch as, O lord of Nairtas, Indrajit yet breaths. Smite by the enemy of Indra, (Rāghava) can by no means save his life in encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
पश्याद्य रामं सहलक्ष्मणेन; मद्बाणनिर्भिन्नविकीर्णदेहम्
गतायुषं भूमितले शयानं; शरैः शितैराचितसर्वगात्रम्
verses.transliteration:
paśyādya rāmaṁ sahalakṣmaṇena; madbāṇanirbhinnavikīrṇadeham
gatāyuṣaṁ bhūmitale śayānaṁ; śaraiḥ śitairācitasarvagātram
