translations.english: To-day behold Rāma along with Lakşmaņa with their bodies torn with my shafts, lying down lifeless on the ground, having their persons covered with my sharpened arrows!

verses.sanskrit:
इमां प्रतिज्ञां शृणु शक्रशत्रोः; सुनिश्चितां पौरुषदैवयुक्ताम्
अद्यैव रामं सहलक्ष्मणेन; संतापयिष्यामि शरैरमोघैः
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ pratijñāṁ śṛṇu śakraśatroḥ; suniścitāṁ pauruṣadaivayuktām
adyaiva rāmaṁ sahalakṣmaṇena; saṁtāpayiṣyāmi śarairamoghaiḥ

translations.english: Hear this vow of the foe of Indra, never swerving and instinct with prowess and divinity, this very day will I with unfailing shafts slay Rāma along with Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्येन्द्रवैवस्वतविष्णुमित्र; साध्याश्विवैश्वानरचन्द्रसूर्याः
द्रक्ष्यन्ति मे विक्रममप्रमेयं; विष्णोरिवोग्रं बलियज्ञवाटे
verses.transliteration:
adyendravaivasvataviṣṇumitra; sādhyāśvivaiśvānaracandrasūryāḥ
drakṣyanti me vikramamaprameyaṁ; viṣṇorivograṁ baliyajñavāṭe

translations.english: To-day let Indra and Vaivasvata and Vişnu and Rudra and Sādhyas and Vaiśvānaras (Agni) and the Sun and the Moon, behold my immeasurable prowess, terrific like that of Vişņu at the sacrificial ground of Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
स एवमुक्त्वा त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रु;रापृच्छ्य राजानमदीनसत्त्वः
समारुरोहानिलतुल्यवेगं; रथं खरश्रेष्ठसमाधियुक्तम्
verses.transliteration:
sa evamuktvā tridaśendraśatru;rāpṛcchya rājānamadīnasattvaḥ
samārurohānilatulyavegaṁ; rathaṁ kharaśreṣṭhasamādhiyuktam

translations.english: Having spoken thus, that foe of the lord of celestials endowed with exceeding energy, taking the king's permission, ascended a car having the velocity of the wind itself, yoked with asses, and furnished with every variety of weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
समास्थाय महातेजा रथं हरिरथोपमम्
जगाम सहसा तत्र यत्र युद्धमरिंदम
verses.transliteration:
samāsthāya mahātejā rathaṁ harirathopamam
jagāma sahasā tatra yatra yuddhamariṁdama

translations.english: Ascending the car, resembling the car of Hari himself, that exceedingly powerful repressor of enemies at once set out for the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रस्थितं महात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः
संहर्षमाणा बहवो धनुःप्रवरपाणयः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prasthitaṁ mahātmānamanujagmurmahābalāḥ
saṁharṣamāṇā bahavo dhanuḥpravarapāṇayaḥ

translations.english: As that high-souled (hero) marched, he was followed by countless mighty (Rākşasas) breathing spirits; bearing bows in their strong hands.

verses.sanskrit:
स शङ्खनिनदैर्भीमैर्भेरीणां च महास्वनैः
जगाम त्रिदशेन्द्रारिः स्तूयमानो निशाचरैः
verses.transliteration:
sa śaṅkhaninadairbhīmairbherīṇāṁ ca mahāsvanaiḥ
jagāma tridaśendrāriḥ stūyamāno niśācaraiḥ

translations.english: All sides were filled with the blares of conchs and the sounds of kettle-drums. And then that enemy of the lord of celestials marched forth with impetuosity.

verses.sanskrit:
स शङ्खशशिवर्णेन छत्रेण रिपुसादनः
रराज परिपूर्णेन नभश्चन्द्रमसा यथा
verses.transliteration:
sa śaṅkhaśaśivarṇena chatreṇa ripusādanaḥ
rarāja paripūrṇena nabhaścandramasā yathā

translations.english: And with an umbrella hued like the Moon, that destroyer of enemies appeared like the full Moon stationed in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
अवीज्यत ततो वीरो हैमैर्हेमविभूषितैः
चारुचामरमुख्यैश्च मुख्यः सर्वधनुष्मताम्
verses.transliteration:
avījyata tato vīro haimairhemavibhūṣitaiḥ
cārucāmaramukhyaiśca mukhyaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām

translations.english: That hero garnished in golden ornaments that foremost of all bowmen, was fanned by an excellent and graceful golden chowri.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्त्विन्द्रजिता लङ्का सूर्यप्रतिमतेजसा
रराजाप्रतिवीर्येण द्यौरिवार्केण भास्वता
verses.transliteration:
tatastvindrajitā laṅkā sūryapratimatejasā
rarājāprativīryeṇa dyaurivārkeṇa bhāsvatā

translations.english: With Indrajit furnished with the splendour of the Sun himself, and possessed of peerless prowess, Lankā looked beauteous even as the firmament graced with the glorious Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्राप्य महातेजा युद्धभूमिमरिंदमः
स्थापयामास रक्षांसि रथं प्रति समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprāpya mahātejā yuddhabhūmimariṁdamaḥ
sthāpayāmāsa rakṣāṁsi rathaṁ prati samantataḥ

translations.english: Arriving at the scene of conflict, that highly powerful repressor of foes arrayed his forces around the car.

verses.sanskrit:
स हविर्जालसंस्कारैर्माल्यगन्धपुरस्कृतैः
जुहुवे पावकं तत्र राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्
verses.transliteration:
sa havirjālasaṁskārairmālyagandhapuraskṛtaiḥ
juhuve pāvakaṁ tatra rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān

translations.english: Then that foremost of Rākşasas with choice mantras duly offered libations to fire.* And that powerful lord of Rākşasas there worshipping fire with fragrant wreaths and fired paddy, sacrificed to it. *Hutabhoktāram-eater of sacrificial offerings-a designation of fire.

verses.sanskrit:
शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ विभीतकः
लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा
verses.transliteration:
śastrāṇi śarapatrāṇi samidho'tha vibhītakaḥ
lohitāni ca vāsāṁsi sruvaṁ kārṣṇāyasaṁ tathā

translations.english: In that sacrifice the weapons were the leaves of sara,' bibhitakas? were fuels, and there were brought crimson clothes and sruvas made of black iron. 1. Saccharum-a reed or grass. 2. Beleric myrobalan. 3. A ladle with a double extremity or two oval collateral excavations made of wood to pour ghee

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्राग्निं समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः सतोमरैः
छागस्य सर्वकृष्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatrāgniṁ samāstīrya śarapatraiḥ satomaraiḥ
chāgasya sarvakṛṣṇasya galaṁ jagrāha jīvataḥ

translations.english: Spreading fire there, with tomaras representing Kāśa, he seized the neck of a living goat of black colour.

verses.sanskrit:
सकृदेव समिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः
बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं यान्यदर्शयन्
verses.transliteration:
sakṛdeva samiddhasya vidhūmasya mahārciṣaḥ
babhūvustāni liṅgāni vijayaṁ yānyadarśayan

translations.english: Then the kindled smokeless fire blazing up brilliantly, displayed signs betokening victory.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तकाञ्चनसंनिभः
हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptakāñcanasaṁnibhaḥ
havistatpratijagrāha pāvakaḥ svayamutthitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, with his right tongue whirling, the Deity of fire himself looking like one made of gold, arising, accepted the offering.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽस्त्रमाहारयामास ब्राह्ममस्त्रविदां वरः
धनुश्चात्मरथं चैव सर्वं तत्राभ्यमन्त्रयत्
verses.transliteration:
so'stramāhārayāmāsa brāhmamastravidāṁ varaḥ
dhanuścātmarathaṁ caiva sarvaṁ tatrābhyamantrayat

translations.english: Then that (Rākşasa) skilled in weapons acquired a Brāhma weapon (from that deity), and inspired his bow and car with mantras.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्नाहूयमानेऽस्त्रे हूयमाने च पावके
सार्कग्रहेन्दु नक्षत्रं वितत्रास नभस्तलम्
verses.transliteration:
tasminnāhūyamāne'stre hūyamāne ca pāvake
sārkagrahendu nakṣatraṁ vitatrāsa nabhastalam

translations.english: On that weapon having been invoked, * and on (the god of fire) also having been worshipped, the firmament furnished with the suns and stars and planets was afflicted with affright. *i.e. on the deity presiding over that weapon, being invoked.

verses.sanskrit:
स पावकं पावकदीप्ततेजा; हुत्वा महेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभावः
सचापबाणासिरथाश्वसूतः; खेऽन्तर्दध आत्मानमचिन्त्यरूपः
verses.transliteration:
sa pāvakaṁ pāvakadīptatejā; hutvā mahendrapratimaprabhāvaḥ
sacāpabāṇāsirathāśvasūtaḥ; khe'ntardadha ātmānamacintyarūpaḥ

translations.english: Having worshipped (the god of fire), that one endowed with the splendour of fire itself, that one possessed of the prowess of the great Indra and gifted with inconceivable vigour, accoutred in bows and arrows and swords and having steeds and cars and darts, disappeared in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
स सैन्यमुत्सृज्य समेत्य तूर्णं; महारणे वानरवाहिनीषु
अदृश्यमानः शरजालमुग्रं; ववर्ष नीलाम्बुधरो यथाम्बु
verses.transliteration:
sa sainyamutsṛjya sametya tūrṇaṁ; mahāraṇe vānaravāhinīṣu
adṛśyamānaḥ śarajālamugraṁ; vavarṣa nīlāmbudharo yathāmbu

translations.english: Then in that encounter, leaving his army, Indrajit became suddenly invisible to the monkey-hosts—and began to shower fierce arrows, like dark clouds pouring rain.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शक्रजिद्बाणविशीर्णदेहा; मायाहता विस्वरमुन्नदन्तः
रणे निपेतुर्हरयोऽद्रिकल्पा; यथेन्द्रवज्राभिहता नगेन्द्राः
verses.transliteration:
te śakrajidbāṇaviśīrṇadehā; māyāhatā visvaramunnadantaḥ
raṇe nipeturharayo'drikalpā; yathendravajrābhihatā nagendrāḥ

translations.english: With their persons torn by the arrows of the conqueror of Sakra, slain by his power of illusion, with their teeth uprooted, those mountain-like monkeys fell down in the field, emitting frightful cries, like a mountain smite with Indra's thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit:
ते केवलं संददृशुः शिताग्रा;न्बाणान्रणे वानरवाहिनीषु
माया निगूढं च सुरेन्द्रशत्रुं; न चात्र तं राक्षसमभ्यपश्यन्
verses.transliteration:
te kevalaṁ saṁdadṛśuḥ śitāgrā;nbāṇānraṇe vānaravāhinīṣu
māyā nigūḍhaṁ ca surendraśatruṁ; na cātra taṁ rākṣasamabhyapaśyan

translations.english: In the conflict they could only see sharp pointed shafts among the monkey-ranks, but that foe of the celestial chief-the Raksasas, hidden by virtue of illusion, they could not discover there.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स रक्षोऽधिपतिर्महात्मा; सर्वा दिशो बाणगणैः शिताग्रैः
प्रच्छादयामास रविप्रकाशै;र्विषादयामास च वानरेन्द्रान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa rakṣo'dhipatirmahātmā; sarvā diśo bāṇagaṇaiḥ śitāgraiḥ
pracchādayāmāsa raviprakāśai;rviṣādayāmāsa ca vānarendrān

translations.english: Then the high-souled lord of Rākṣasa covered all sides with sharp-pointed shafts resembling the rays of the sun; and he rived the foremost monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स शूलनिस्त्रिंश परश्वधानि; व्याविध्य दीप्तानलसंनिभानि
सविस्फुलिङ्गोज्ज्वलपावकानि; ववर्ष तीव्रं प्लवगेन्द्रसैन्ये
verses.transliteration:
sa śūlanistriṁśa paraśvadhāni; vyāvidhya dīptānalasaṁnibhāni
savisphuliṅgojjvalapāvakāni; vavarṣa tīvraṁ plavagendrasainye

translations.english: And whirling darts and nistraišas and axes, flaming and having the effulgence of fire, and furnished with flames shooting forth sparks, he discharged them furiously at the forces of the sovereign of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो ज्वलनसंकाशैः शितैर्वानरयूथपाः
ताडिताः शक्रजिद्बाणैः प्रफुल्ला इव किंशुकाः
verses.transliteration:
tato jvalanasaṁkāśaiḥ śitairvānarayūthapāḥ
tāḍitāḥ śakrajidbāṇaiḥ praphullā iva kiṁśukāḥ

translations.english: The monkey-leaders struck with Śakrajit's shafts. resembling flames, appeared like laughing Kinsukas.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यमभिसर्पन्तो निनदन्तश्च विस्वरम्
राक्षसेन्द्रास्त्रनिर्भिन्ना निपेतुर्वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
anyonyamabhisarpanto ninadantaśca visvaram
rākṣasendrāstranirbhinnā nipeturvānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: They foremost of Vānaras, pierced by the missiles of the lord of Raksasas gliding towards one another and crying bitterly fell down on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
उदीक्षमाणा गगनं केचिन्नेत्रेषु ताडिताः
शरैर्विविशुरन्योन्यं पेतुश्च जगतीतले
verses.transliteration:
udīkṣamāṇā gaganaṁ kecinnetreṣu tāḍitāḥ
śarairviviśuranyonyaṁ petuśca jagatītale

translations.english: Some looking at the sky were struck at their eyes. They gradually began to hide themselves in each other and drop to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
स वै गदाभिर्हरियूथमुख्या;न्निर्भिद्य बाणैस्तपनीयपुङ्खैः
ववर्ष रामं शरवृष्टिजालैः; सलक्ष्मणं भास्कररश्मिकल्पैः
verses.transliteration:
sa vai gadābhirhariyūthamukhyā;nnirbhidya bāṇaistapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ
vavarṣa rāmaṁ śaravṛṣṭijālaiḥ; salakṣmaṇaṁ bhāskararaśmikalpaiḥ

translations.english: Having pierced those foremost monkeys with golden-hued maces, he showered on Rāma and Lakşmaņa arrows resembling the rays of the sun.

verses.sanskrit:
स बाणवर्षैरभिवर्ष्यमाणो; धारानिपातानिव तान्विचिन्त्य
समीक्षमाणः परमाद्भुतश्री; रामस्तदा लक्ष्मणमित्युवाच
verses.transliteration:
sa bāṇavarṣairabhivarṣyamāṇo; dhārānipātāniva tānvicintya
samīkṣamāṇaḥ paramādbhutaśrī; rāmastadā lakṣmaṇamityuvāca

translations.english: And showered with those vollies of arrows, Rāma, without heeding that discharge resembling a very downpour, reflecting, spoke to Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
असौ पुनर्लक्ष्मण राक्षसेन्द्रो; ब्रह्मास्त्रमाश्रित्य सुरेन्द्रशत्रुः
निपातयित्वा हरिसैन्यमुग्र;मस्माञ्शरैरर्दयति प्रसक्तम्
verses.transliteration:
asau punarlakṣmaṇa rākṣasendro; brahmāstramāśritya surendraśatruḥ
nipātayitvā harisainyamugra;masmāñśarairardayati prasaktam

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa, this lord of Rākşasas, this foe of the lord of celestials, having obtained the Brāhma weapon, after having brought down the monkey-hosts, are assailing us with sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयम्भुवा दत्तवरो महात्मा; खमास्थितोऽन्तर्हितभीमकायः
कथं नु शक्यो युधि नष्टदेहो; निहन्तुमद्येन्द्रजिदुद्यतास्त्रः
verses.transliteration:
svayambhuvā dattavaro mahātmā; khamāsthito'ntarhitabhīmakāyaḥ
kathaṁ nu śakyo yudhi naṣṭadeho; nihantumadyendrajidudyatāstraḥ

translations.english: That high-souled heedful one, having been given a boon by the self-sprung, has rendered his dreadful body invisible. How can we slay him, who is fighting with upraised weapons, but who has hid his body.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्ये स्वयम्भूर्भगवानचिन्त्यो; यस्यैतदस्त्रं प्रभवश्च योऽस्य
बाणावपातांस्त्वमिहाद्य धीम;न्मया सहाव्यग्रमनाः सहस्व
verses.transliteration:
manye svayambhūrbhagavānacintyo; yasyaitadastraṁ prabhavaśca yo'sya
bāṇāvapātāṁstvamihādya dhīma;nmayā sahāvyagramanāḥ sahasva

translations.english: The reverend self-sprung, I deem, is incomprehensible. And this is his weapon, embodying his energy. Therefore, O intelligent one, do you today along with me calmly bear this.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रच्छादयत्येष हि राक्षसेन्द्रः; सर्वा दिशः सायकवृष्टिजालैः
एतच्च सर्वं पतिताग्र्यवीरं; न भ्राजते वानरराजसैन्यम्
verses.transliteration:
pracchādayatyeṣa hi rākṣasendraḥ; sarvā diśaḥ sāyakavṛṣṭijālaiḥ
etacca sarvaṁ patitāgryavīraṁ; na bhrājate vānararājasainyam

translations.english: Let this foremost of them all, this lord of Rāks asas-cover all sides with the showers of his shafts. And in consequence of this, the army of the monkey-king with its greatest heroes fallen, does not appear to advantage.

verses.sanskrit:
आवां तु दृष्ट्वा पतितौ विसंज्ञौ; निवृत्तयुद्धौ हतरोषहर्षौ
ध्रुवं प्रवेक्ष्यत्यमरारिवासं; असौ समादाय रणाग्रलक्ष्मीम्
verses.transliteration:
āvāṁ tu dṛṣṭvā patitau visaṁjñau; nivṛttayuddhau hataroṣaharṣau
dhruvaṁ pravekṣyatyamarārivāsaṁ; asau samādāya raṇāgralakṣmīm

translations.english: Seeing us also fallen, senseless, and desisting from fight with our joy and anger gone off from us, for certain will the enemy of the immortals, taking the Fortune of fight seek his home.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु ताविन्द्रजिदस्त्रजालै;र्बभूवतुस्तत्र तदा विशस्तौ
स चापि तौ तत्र विषादयित्वा; ननाद हर्षाद्युधि राक्षसेन्द्रः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu tāvindrajidastrajālai;rbabhūvatustatra tadā viśastau
sa cāpi tau tatra viṣādayitvā; nanāda harṣādyudhi rākṣasendraḥ

translations.english: Assailed by Indrajit with networks of arrows, they were then sore distressed in the field. And having struck them with sadness, Indrajit from joy shouted in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्तदा वानरराजसैन्यं; रामं च संख्ये सहलक्ष्मणेन
विषादयित्वा सहसा विवेश; पुरीं दशग्रीवभुजाभिगुप्ताम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tattadā vānararājasainyaṁ; rāmaṁ ca saṁkhye sahalakṣmaṇena
viṣādayitvā sahasā viveśa; purīṁ daśagrīvabhujābhiguptām

translations.english: Having thus worsted in battle that monkey army and Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, he-speedily entered the city ruled by the hand of the Ten-necked one. And extolled by the Yatudhānas, he, filled with delight, related everything to his sire.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोस्तदा सादितयो रणाग्रे; मुमोह सैन्यं हरियूथपानाम्
सुग्रीवनीलाङ्गदजाम्बवन्तो; न चापि किंचित्प्रतिपेदिरे ते
verses.transliteration:
tayostadā sāditayo raṇāgre; mumoha sainyaṁ hariyūthapānām
sugrīvanīlāṅgadajāmbavanto; na cāpi kiṁcitpratipedire te

translations.english: They were rendered inert in the field; and the army of the monkey-leaders was stupefied, with Sugrīva and Nīla and Angada and Jāmbavān, and they did not show any signs of activity.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विषण्णं समवेक्ष्य सैन्यं; विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः
उवाच शाखामृगराजवीरा;नाश्वासयन्नप्रतिमैर्वचोभिः
verses.transliteration:
tato viṣaṇṇaṁ samavekṣya sainyaṁ; vibhīṣaṇo buddhimatāṁ variṣṭhaḥ
uvāca śākhāmṛgarājavīrā;nāśvāsayannapratimairvacobhiḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, seeing them dispirited, that foremost of intelligent persons, Vibhisana, cheering them up with his peerless speech, said.

verses.sanskrit:
मा भैष्ट नास्त्यत्र विषादकालो; यदार्यपुत्राववशौ विषण्णौ
स्वयम्भुवो वाक्यमथोद्वहन्तौ; यत्सादिताविन्द्रजिदस्त्रजालैः
verses.transliteration:
mā bhaiṣṭa nāstyatra viṣādakālo; yadāryaputrāvavaśau viṣaṇṇau
svayambhuvo vākyamathodvahantau; yatsāditāvindrajidastrajālaiḥ

translations.english: You heroes of the king of monkeys, do not give way to fear. This is not the time to indulge in grief at this place; for the sons of that noble one,' inactive and depressed, and seeming to be wounded with the showers of Indrajit's shafts, are in reality in this plight, for showing reverence to the words of the self-sprung one. 1. Dasaratha. 2.Mantra.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मै तु दत्तं परमास्त्रमेत;त्स्वयम्भुवा ब्राह्मममोघवेगम्
तन्मानयन्तौ यदि राजपुत्रौ; निपातितौ कोऽत्र विषादकालः
verses.transliteration:
tasmai tu dattaṁ paramāstrameta;tsvayambhuvā brāhmamamoghavegam
tanmānayantau yadi rājaputrau; nipātitau ko'tra viṣādakālaḥ

translations.english: On him the self-sprung has conferred the mighty Brahmă weapon of unfailing power; and the king's sons are doing honour to it by lying down on the field of battle. Why then do you grieve now?

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं तदा धीमान्मानयित्वा तु मारुतिः
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हनूमांस्तमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
brāhmamastraṁ tadā dhīmānmānayitvā tu mārutiḥ
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā hanūmāṁstamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing the words of Vibhisana and honouring the Brahma weapon, Hanumăn spoke as follows.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्निहते सैन्ये वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
यो यो धारयते प्राणांस्तं तमाश्वासयावहे
verses.transliteration:
etasminnihate sainye vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
yo yo dhārayate prāṇāṁstaṁ tamāśvāsayāvahe

translations.english: The host of the quick-paced monkeys has been slain by this weapon. Let us go and console them who are still living.

verses.sanskrit:
तावुभौ युगपद्वीरौ हनूमद्राक्षसोत्तमौ
उल्काहस्तौ तदा रात्रौ रणशीर्षे विचेरतुः
verses.transliteration:
tāvubhau yugapadvīrau hanūmadrākṣasottamau
ulkāhastau tadā rātrau raṇaśīrṣe viceratuḥ

translations.english: Those two great heroes— Hanumān and that foremost of the Rakşasas, with fire-brands in their hands, began to range to and fro in the battle field.

verses.sanskrit:
पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंकुलाम्
शस्त्रैश्च पतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशाते वसुंधराम्
verses.transliteration:
patitaiḥ parvatākārairvānarairabhisaṁkulām
śastraiśca patitairdīptairdadṛśāte vasuṁdharām

translations.english: They beheld there the earth strewn on all sides with monkeys lying down like so many hills and various shining weapons. And some of these monkeys were deprived of their tails, some of their hands, some of their thighs, some of their legs, some of their fingers, and some of their heads. And blood was gushing out from the persons of some, and others were urinating out of fear.

verses.sanskrit:
मैन्दं नलं ज्योतिमुखं द्विविदं पनसं तथा
विभीषणो हनूमांश्च ददृशाते हतान्रणे
verses.transliteration:
maindaṁ nalaṁ jyotimukhaṁ dvividaṁ panasaṁ tathā
vibhīṣaṇo hanūmāṁśca dadṛśāte hatānraṇe

translations.english: Vibhīşaņa and Hanuman beheld there Sugriva, Angada Nila, Gandhamādana, Jambhavan, Susena, Vegadarshin, Mainda, Nala, Jyotimukha, and the monkey, Dvivida, almost slain.

verses.sanskrit:
सप्तषष्टिर्हताः कोट्यो वानराणां तरस्विनाम्
अह्नः पञ्चमशेषेण वल्लभेन स्वयम्भुवः
verses.transliteration:
saptaṣaṣṭirhatāḥ koṭyo vānarāṇāṁ tarasvinām
ahnaḥ pañcamaśeṣeṇa vallabhena svayambhuvaḥ

translations.english: Vibhișana and Hanuman saw in the field seven and sixty kotis of fleet-footing monkeys slain (in battle) at the fifth part of the day by the darling of the self-sprung.

verses.sanskrit:
सागरौघनिभं भीमं दृष्ट्वा बाणार्दितं बलम्
मार्गते जाम्बवन्तं स्म हनूमान्सविभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
sāgaraughanibhaṁ bhīmaṁ dṛṣṭvā bāṇārditaṁ balam
mārgate jāmbavantaṁ sma hanūmānsavibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: And surveying that host worsted, dreadful like the surges of the sea, Hanumăn and Vibhīşaņa began to search for Jāmbavān.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तमुपसंगम्य पौलस्त्यो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
कच्चिदार्यशरैस्तीर्ष्णैर्न प्राणा ध्वंसितास्तव
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā tamupasaṁgamya paulastyo vākyamabravīt
kaccidāryaśaraistīrṣṇairna prāṇā dhvaṁsitāstava

translations.english: Finding that heroic son of Prajāpati, afflicted with natural decrepitude, aged, and resembling smouldering fire, wounded with hundreds of shafts, Pulastya's son said, “O noble one, has not your life been destroyed with those sharp shafts?"

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवानृक्षपुंगवः
कृच्छ्रादभ्युद्गिरन्वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavānṛkṣapuṁgavaḥ
kṛcchrādabhyudgiranvākyamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Jambevan, best of bears, evoking utterance with extreme effort, said.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृतेन्द्रमहावीर्यस्वरेण त्वाभिलक्षये
पीड्यमानः शितैर्बाणैर्न त्वां पश्यामि चक्षुषा
verses.transliteration:
nairṛtendramahāvīryasvareṇa tvābhilakṣaye
pīḍyamānaḥ śitairbāṇairna tvāṁ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā

translations.english: O foremost of Naiſtas, endowed with exceeding prowess, I know you by your voice. Having my person pierced with sharp shafts, I cannot see you with my eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
अञ्जना सुप्रजा येन मातरिश्वा च नैरृत
हनूमान्वानरश्रेष्ठः प्राणान्धारयते क्वचित्
verses.transliteration:
añjanā suprajā yena mātariśvā ca nairṛta
hanūmānvānaraśreṣṭhaḥ prāṇāndhārayate kvacit

translations.english: Does he through whom Añjanä as well as Mātariśvan* are blessed with fair offspring, does that prince of monkeys-Hanumān, live? *The wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यमुवाचेदं विभीषणः
आर्यपुत्रावतिक्रम्य कस्मात्पृच्छसि मारुतिम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā jāmbavato vākyamuvācedaṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
āryaputrāvatikramya kasmātpṛcchasi mārutim

translations.english: Hearing Jambavan's speech, Vibhisana said, “Why, passing by the son of the high and mighty,* did you enquire after the wind-god's offsprmg? *Vide Hamlet.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव राजनि सुग्रीवे नाङ्गदे नापि राघवे
आर्य संदर्शितः स्नेहो यथा वायुसुते परः
verses.transliteration:
naiva rājani sugrīve nāṅgade nāpi rāghave
ārya saṁdarśitaḥ sneho yathā vāyusute paraḥ

translations.english: O noble one, you did not show that overflowing affection either for king Sugrīva or Angada and Raghava that you show for the son of the wind-god.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवान्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
शृणु नैरृतशार्दूल यस्मात्पृच्छामि मारुतिम्
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavānvākyamabravīt
śṛṇu nairṛtaśārdūla yasmātpṛcchāmi mārutim

translations.english: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Jambavan said, "Hear, O foremost of Raksasas, why I enquire after the wind-god's son.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिञ्जीवति वीरे तु हतमप्यहतं बलम्
हनूमत्युज्झितप्राणे जीवन्तोऽपि वयं हताः
verses.transliteration:
tasmiñjīvati vīre tu hatamapyahataṁ balam
hanūmatyujjhitaprāṇe jīvanto'pi vayaṁ hatāḥ

translations.english: While this hero is alive, this force, albeit destroyed, live; but if Hanumān is reft of life, although living, we are destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
ध्रियते मारुतिस्तात मारुतप्रतिमो यदि
वैश्वानरसमो वीर्ये जीविताशा ततो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
dhriyate mārutistāta mārutapratimo yadi
vaiśvānarasamo vīrye jīvitāśā tato bhavet

translations.english: O child, if the wind-god's offspring, resembling his sire himself or (the deity of) fire in prowess, is alive, there is hope for our lives.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वृद्धमुपागम्य नियमेनाभ्यवादयत्
गृह्य जाम्बवतः पादौ हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
tato vṛddhamupāgamya niyamenābhyavādayat
gṛhya jāmbavataḥ pādau hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then approaching that aged one, Hanumanson to the wind-god-saluted him humbly, holding Jāmbavān's feet.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं तथापि व्यथितेन्द्रियः
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं स मेने ऋक्षपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā hanumato vākyaṁ tathāpi vyathitendriyaḥ
punarjātamivātmānaṁ sa mene ṛkṣapuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Hanuman's voice, that foremost of monkeys with his senses sorely smarting, deemed himself as having regained his life.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमन्तं स जाम्बवान्
आगच्छ हरिशार्दूलवानरांस्त्रातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīnmahātejā hanūmantaṁ sa jāmbavān
āgaccha hariśārdūlavānarāṁstrātumarhasi

translations.english: Then that exceedingly energetic Jåmbavān addressed Hanumān, saying, “Come, O powerful monkey, It behove you to rescue the monkeys."

verses.sanskrit:
नान्यो विक्रमपर्याप्तस्त्वमेषां परमः सखा
त्वत्पराक्रमकालोऽयं नान्यं पश्यामि कञ्चन
verses.transliteration:
nānyo vikramaparyāptastvameṣāṁ paramaḥ sakhā
tvatparākramakālo'yaṁ nānyaṁ paśyāmi kañcana

translations.english: There is none else. Endowed with profuse prowess, you are the greatest friend of these. This is the hour when you should display you might. Any other see I not.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षवानरवीराणामनीकानि प्रहर्षय
विशल्यौ कुरु चाप्येतौ सादितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣavānaravīrāṇāmanīkāni praharṣaya
viśalyau kuru cāpyetau sāditau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Do you cheer up this host consisting of bears and monkeys; and do you also heal the wounds of these two tormented by them.

verses.sanskrit:
गत्वा परममध्वानमुपर्युपरि सागरम्
हिमवन्तं नगश्रेष्ठं हनूमन्गन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
gatvā paramamadhvānamuparyupari sāgaram
himavantaṁ nagaśreṣṭhaṁ hanūmangantumarhasi

translations.english: Bounding sheer over the main, you, O Hanumān, should repair to the Himavānforemost of mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः काञ्चनमत्युग्रमृषभं पर्वतोत्तमम्
कैलासशिखरं चापि द्रक्ष्यस्यरिनिषूदन
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kāñcanamatyugramṛṣabhaṁ parvatottamam
kailāsaśikharaṁ cāpi drakṣyasyariniṣūdana

translations.english: There you will see that best of mountiansthe golden Rşabha of terrific aspect, and, O smiter of foes, the peak also of Kailāśa.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः शिखरयोर्मध्ये प्रदीप्तमतुलप्रभम्
सर्वौषधियुतं वीर द्रक्ष्यस्यौषधिपर्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ śikharayormadhye pradīptamatulaprabham
sarvauṣadhiyutaṁ vīra drakṣyasyauṣadhiparvatam

translations.english: Lying in the lap of these two, you, O hero, O powerful monkey, will see the mountain of medicines, fraught with healing herbs of all kinds.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य वानरशार्दूलचतस्रो मूर्ध्नि संभवाः
द्रक्ष्यस्योषधयो दीप्ता दीपयन्त्यो दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
tasya vānaraśārdūlacatasro mūrdhni saṁbhavāḥ
drakṣyasyoṣadhayo dīptā dīpayantyo diśo daśa

translations.english: On its summit you will find four medicinal herbs flaming and illumining the ten cardinal quarters-viz., Mſtasanjivani,' Višalyakarani, Suvarnakarani, and the mighty medicine, Sandhănī. 1. Lit. reviving the dead. 2. Lit. healing wounds inflicted by darts. 3. Lit. transmuting any thing to gold.

verses.sanskrit:
ताः सर्वा हनुमन्गृह्य क्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि
आश्वासय हरीन्प्राणैर्योज्य गन्धवहात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
tāḥ sarvā hanumangṛhya kṣipramāgantumarhasi
āśvāsaya harīnprāṇairyojya gandhavahātmajaḥ

translations.english: O Hanumān, providing yourself with these, you should come here without delay. Do you, O offspring of the wind-god* bringing back lives to these monkeys, cheer them up. *Gandhavahātanaya-lit., son to the bearer of smell-a designation of the wind in Sanskrit.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यं हनूमान्हरिपुंगवः
आपूर्यत बलोद्धर्षैस्तोयवेगैरिवार्णवः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā jāmbavato vākyaṁ hanūmānharipuṁgavaḥ
āpūryata baloddharṣaistoyavegairivārṇavaḥ

translations.english: Thereat hearing the words of Jāmbavān Hanumān, son of wind-god filled himself with energy, even as the Ocean heave with the force of the winds (blowing on its breast).

verses.sanskrit:
स पर्वततटाग्रस्थः पीडयन्पर्वतोत्तरम्
हनूमान्दृश्यते वीरो द्वितीय इव पर्वतः
verses.transliteration:
sa parvatataṭāgrasthaḥ pīḍayanparvatottaram
hanūmāndṛśyate vīro dvitīya iva parvataḥ

translations.english: Ascending the summit of that mountain,* and hurting it with his tread, that hero-Hanumanappeared like a second mountain. *Trikuta.

verses.sanskrit:
हरिपादविनिर्भिन्नो निषसाद स पर्वतः
न शशाक तदात्मानं सोढुं भृशनिपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
haripādavinirbhinno niṣasāda sa parvataḥ
na śaśāka tadātmānaṁ soḍhuṁ bhṛśanipīḍitaḥ

translations.english: Crushed under the tread of that monkey, the mountain was dispirited; and sore distressed, it could hardly contain itself.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्संपीड्यमाने तु भग्नद्रुमशिलातले
न शेकुर्वानराः स्थातुं घूर्णमाने नगोत्तमे
verses.transliteration:
tasminsaṁpīḍyamāne tu bhagnadrumaśilātale
na śekurvānarāḥ sthātuṁ ghūrṇamāne nagottame

translations.english: The trees on it began to topple to the earth; and on account of the vehemence of the monkey, they flamed up. And smitten by Hanumān, its peaks were scattered around. And monkeys could no longer dwell on that fore. Most of mountains, which being hard pressed (by Hanumān), was trembling all over, with its slopes covered with broken trees and rocks.

verses.sanskrit:
स घूर्णितमहाद्वारा प्रभग्नगृहगोपुरा
लङ्का त्रासाकुला रात्रौ प्रनृत्तेवाभवत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
sa ghūrṇitamahādvārā prabhagnagṛhagopurā
laṅkā trāsākulā rātrau pranṛttevābhavattadā

translations.english: With her giant gateways shaking, and the doors of her edifices broken, that night Lankā, over-whelmed with fright, seemed to be dancing.

verses.sanskrit:
पृथिवीधरसंकाशो निपीड्य धरणीधरम्
पृथिवीं क्षोभयामास सार्णवां मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
pṛthivīdharasaṁkāśo nipīḍya dharaṇīdharam
pṛthivīṁ kṣobhayāmāsa sārṇavāṁ mārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: The offspring of the wind-god, resembling a mountain itself, bringing that mountain to sore straits, agitated the entire earth with her oceans.

verses.sanskrit:
पद्भ्यां तु शैलमापीड्य वडवामुखवन्मुखम्
विवृत्योग्रं ननादोच्चैस्त्रासयन्निव राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
padbhyāṁ tu śailamāpīḍya vaḍavāmukhavanmukham
vivṛtyograṁ nanādoccaistrāsayanniva rākṣasān

translations.english: And hurting the mountain with his tread, he, opening wide his mouth resembling that of a mare, sent up loud shouts, terrifying the nightrangers.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य नानद्यमानस्य श्रुत्वा निनदमद्भुतम्
लङ्कास्था राक्षसाः सर्वे न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं भयात्
verses.transliteration:
tasya nānadyamānasya śrutvā ninadamadbhutam
laṅkāsthā rākṣasāḥ sarve na śekuḥ spandituṁ bhayāt

translations.english: Hearing those tremendous roars as he kept emitting cries, the powerful Rākṣasas were quite stupified.

verses.sanskrit:
नमस्कृत्वाथ रामाय मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः
राघवार्थे परं कर्म समैहत परंतपः
verses.transliteration:
namaskṛtvātha rāmāya mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ
rāghavārthe paraṁ karma samaihata paraṁtapaḥ

translations.english: Bowing down to the Ocean, that subduer of enemies, the Wind-god's son, endowed with dreadful prowess, began to ponder over the mighty mission with which he had been entrusted in the interests of Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
स पुच्छमुद्यम्य भुजंगकल्पं; विनम्य पृष्ठं श्रवणे निकुञ्च्य
विवृत्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभ;मापुप्लुवे व्योम्नि स चण्डवेगः
verses.transliteration:
sa pucchamudyamya bhujaṁgakalpaṁ; vinamya pṛṣṭhaṁ śravaṇe nikuñcya
vivṛtya vaktraṁ vaḍavāmukhābha;māpupluve vyomni sa caṇḍavegaḥ

translations.english: Then upraising his tail resembling a serpent, bending his back, contracting his ears, and opening his mouth looking like that of a mare, that one possessed of terrific impetuosity, bounded into the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
स वृक्षषण्डांस्तरसा जहार; शैलाञ्शिलाः प्राकृतवानरांश्च
बाहूरुवेगोद्धतसंप्रणुन्ना;स्ते क्षीणवेगाः सलिले निपेतुः
verses.transliteration:
sa vṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṁstarasā jahāra; śailāñśilāḥ prākṛtavānarāṁśca
bāhūruvegoddhatasaṁpraṇunnā;ste kṣīṇavegāḥ salile nipetuḥ

translations.english: With the vehemence of his rush, he carried away in his wake whole tracts of trees, and rocks, and crags, and inferior monkeys;* and after having been carried away some distance by the vehemence of his arms and thighs, they, at length losing their velocity, fell into the waters (of the Ocean.) *Residing in the Trikuta mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
स तौ प्रसार्योरगभोगकल्पौ; भुजौ भुजंगारिनिकाशवीर्यः
जगाम मेरुं नगराजमग्र्यं; दिशः प्रकर्षन्निव वायुसूनुः
verses.transliteration:
sa tau prasāryoragabhogakalpau; bhujau bhujaṁgārinikāśavīryaḥ
jagāma meruṁ nagarājamagryaṁ; diśaḥ prakarṣanniva vāyusūnuḥ

translations.english: Stretching his arms resembling serpents, the son of the Wind-god endowed with the prowess of Garuda* coursed on towards the monarch of mountains, as if making all the quarters tremble. *The text has, the foe of serpents—an appellation of Garuda

verses.sanskrit:
स सागरं घूर्णितवीचिमालं; तदा भृशं भ्रामितसर्वसत्त्वम्
समीक्षमाणः सहसा जगाम; चक्रं यथा विष्णुकराग्रमुक्तम्
verses.transliteration:
sa sāgaraṁ ghūrṇitavīcimālaṁ; tadā bhṛśaṁ bhrāmitasarvasattvam
samīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā jagāma; cakraṁ yathā viṣṇukarāgramuktam

translations.english: Seeing the sea with its hosts of billows rolling furiously and with the confederacies of aquatic animals bewildered by the angry waters, he coursed on rapidly, like the discus discharged by the hand of Vişnu.

verses.sanskrit:
स पर्वतान्वृक्षगणान्सरांसि; नदीस्तटाकानि पुरोत्तमानि
स्फीताञ्जनांस्तानपि संप्रपश्य;ञ्जगाम वेगात्पितृतुल्यवेगः
verses.transliteration:
sa parvatānvṛkṣagaṇānsarāṁsi; nadīstaṭākāni purottamāni
sphītāñjanāṁstānapi saṁprapaśya;ñjagāma vegātpitṛtulyavegaḥ

translations.english: Surveying hills and birds and pools and rivers and tanks and splendid cities and flourishing provinces, that one equal to his sire himself in celerity, held his way.

verses.sanskrit:
नानाप्रस्रवणोपेतं बहुकंदरनिर्झरम्
श्वेताभ्रचयसंकाशैः शिखरैश्चारुदर्शनैः
verses.transliteration:
nānāprasravaṇopetaṁ bahukaṁdaranirjharam
śvetābhracayasaṁkāśaiḥ śikharaiścārudarśanaiḥ

translations.english: Remembering Jāmbavān's words, that redoubtable monkey, son to the Wind-god, possessed of terrific prowess, and resembling a mountain, suddenly saw (before him) the Himavān; furnished with countless cascades and numerous caves and rivulets; with splendid summits appearing like massess of pale clouds, and graced with various trees.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं समासाद्य महानगेन्द्र;मतिप्रवृद्धोत्तमघोरशृङ्गम्
ददर्श पुण्यानि महाश्रमाणि; सुरर्षिसंघोत्तमसेवितानि
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ samāsādya mahānagendra;matipravṛddhottamaghoraśṛṅgam
dadarśa puṇyāni mahāśramāṇi; surarṣisaṁghottamasevitāni

translations.english: Arriving at that lord of mighty mountains, furnished with excellent towering golden summits, he saw the great sacred asylums (of the ascetics), inhabited by the flower of celestial saints.

verses.sanskrit:
स ब्रह्मकोशं रजतालयं च; शक्रालयं रुद्रशरप्रमोक्षम्
हयाननं ब्रह्मशिरश्च दीप्तं; ददर्श वैवस्वत किंकरांश्च
verses.transliteration:
sa brahmakośaṁ rajatālayaṁ ca; śakrālayaṁ rudraśarapramokṣam
hayānanaṁ brahmaśiraśca dīptaṁ; dadarśa vaivasvata kiṁkarāṁśca

translations.english: He beheld Brahmakosa (a) Rajatalaya (b) Śakrālaya (c) Rudraśarapramokṣa (d) Hayānana (e) and the flaming Brahmasiras (f) and the servants of Vaivasvata (g). (a) The place of Hiranyagarbha (b) The place of Rajatanăbha— silver-neededanother from of Hiranyagarbha (c) The abode of Sakra. (d) The place where from Rudra discharged his arrow on the occasion of the destruction of Tripurā (e) Theplace of the horse-necked. (f) The place of the deity presiding ever the Brahma-weapon. (g) An appellation of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रालयं वैश्वरणालयं च; सूर्यप्रभं सूर्यनिबन्धनं च
ब्रह्मासनं शंकरकार्मुकं च; ददर्श नाभिं च वसुंधरायाः
verses.transliteration:
vajrālayaṁ vaiśvaraṇālayaṁ ca; sūryaprabhaṁ sūryanibandhanaṁ ca
brahmāsanaṁ śaṁkarakārmukaṁ ca; dadarśa nābhiṁ ca vasuṁdharāyāḥ

translations.english: He saw the abode of the Fire-god, and the abode of Vaiśravana and the effulgent suryyanivandhana, (h) and the abode of Brahmă, (i) and the bow of Sankara, and the navel of the Earth. (j) And he saw Kailasa of terrific aspect, and the stone, (k) of Himavăn, and that bull, (1) and the golden mountain, and that foremost of mountains furnished with all medicinal herbs, flaming, and illuminated with every kind of medicinal plants. (h) The spot where the suns meet. (i) The place of the four-faced Brahmă. (i) The spot of Prajāpati. (k) On which Rudra sat when engaged in asceticism. (1) Which had been mentioned by Jambavan.

verses.sanskrit:
स तं समीक्ष्यानलरश्मिदीप्तं; विसिष्मिये वासवदूतसूनुः
आप्लुत्य तं चौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रं; तत्रौषधीनां विचयं चकार
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ samīkṣyānalaraśmidīptaṁ; visiṣmiye vāsavadūtasūnuḥ
āplutya taṁ cauṣadhiparvatendraṁ; tatrauṣadhīnāṁ vicayaṁ cakāra

translations.english: Beholding that flaming mass of fire, the offspring of Vasava's* emissary wondered. And bounding up to the lord of medicinal mountains, he fell to searching for the drugs. * The emissary of Vāsavain his cloud-from is the wind driving the cloud; and the passage refers to Hanuman,

verses.sanskrit:
स योजनसहस्राणि समतीत्य महाकपिः
दिव्यौषधिधरं शैलं व्यचरन्मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
sa yojanasahasrāṇi samatītya mahākapiḥ
divyauṣadhidharaṁ śailaṁ vyacaranmārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: That mighty monkey-the Wind-god's son-leaving behind a thousand Yojanas, began to range the mountain containing the divine remedies in its entrails.

verses.sanskrit:
महौषध्यस्तु ताः सर्वास्तस्मिन्पर्वतसत्तमे
विज्ञायार्थिनमायान्तं ततो जग्मुरदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
mahauṣadhyastu tāḥ sarvāstasminparvatasattame
vijñāyārthinamāyāntaṁ tato jagmuradarśanam

translations.english: Those potent medicines, in that foremost of mountains, knowing (before-hand) that one was coming seeking for them, rendered themselves invisible.

verses.sanskrit:
स ता महात्मा हनुमानपश्यं;श्चुकोप कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद
अमृष्यमाणोऽग्निनिकाशचक्षु;र्महीधरेन्द्रं तमुवाच वाक्यम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tā mahātmā hanumānapaśyaṁ;ścukopa kopācca bhṛśaṁ nanāda
amṛṣyamāṇo'gninikāśacakṣu;rmahīdharendraṁ tamuvāca vākyam

translations.english: And not seeing them, the high-souled Hanumān was angered; and from wrath he set up roars. And not brooking that, (Hanumān) with eyes resembling glowing fire, addressed that foremost of mountains, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किमेतदेवं सुविनिश्चितं ते; यद्राघवे नासि कृतानुकम्पः
पश्याद्य मद्बाहुबलाभिभूतो; विकीर्णमात्मानमथो नगेन्द्र
verses.transliteration:
kimetadevaṁ suviniścitaṁ te; yadrāghave nāsi kṛtānukampaḥ
paśyādya madbāhubalābhibhūto; vikīrṇamātmānamatho nagendra

translations.english: What is ihis that you have decided on, that you show no compassion for Rāghava? But, O lord of mountains, today witness yourself, overpowered by my arms and torn in pieces!

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्य शृङ्गं सनगं सनागं; सकाञ्चनं धातुसहस्रजुष्टम्
विकीर्णकूटं चलिताग्रसानुं; प्रगृह्य वेगात्सहसोन्ममाथ
verses.transliteration:
sa tasya śṛṅgaṁ sanagaṁ sanāgaṁ; sakāñcanaṁ dhātusahasrajuṣṭam
vikīrṇakūṭaṁ calitāgrasānuṁ; pragṛhya vegātsahasonmamātha

translations.english: And (anon) on a sudden, he violently rooted up its summit with trees and elephants and gold, and furnished with thousand varieties of ore, having its tops torn and its slopes aflame.

verses.sanskrit:
स भास्कराध्वानमनुप्रपन्न;स्तद्भास्कराभं शिखरं प्रगृह्य
बभौ तदा भास्करसंनिकाशो; रवेः समीपे प्रतिभास्कराभः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhāskarādhvānamanuprapanna;stadbhāskarābhaṁ śikharaṁ pragṛhya
babhau tadā bhāskarasaṁnikāśo; raveḥ samīpe pratibhāskarābhaḥ

translations.english: And uprooting it, he sprang into the bosom of the air), terrifying the worlds containing celestials and the lords thereof. And hymned by countless rangers of the air, that one endowed with the terrific impetuosity of Garuda himself, taking that summit furnished with the splendour of the Sun, went along the orbit of the Sun. And near the Sun, that Sun-like one seemed to be another sun.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेन शैलेन भृशं रराज; शैलोपमो गन्धवहात्मजस्तु
सहस्रधारेण सपावकेन; चक्रेण खे विष्णुरिवोद्धृतेन
verses.transliteration:
sa tena śailena bhṛśaṁ rarāja; śailopamo gandhavahātmajastu
sahasradhāreṇa sapāvakena; cakreṇa khe viṣṇurivoddhṛtena

translations.english: With that mountain, the offspring of the bearer of perfumes appeared surpassingly grand, like very Vişņu equipped with the flaming discus having a thousand edges.

verses.sanskrit:
तं वानराः प्रेक्ष्य तदा विनेदुः; स तानपि प्रेक्ष्य मुदा ननाद
तेषां समुद्घुष्टरवं निशम्य; लङ्कालया भीमतरं विनेदुः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ vānarāḥ prekṣya tadā vineduḥ; sa tānapi prekṣya mudā nanāda
teṣāṁ samudghuṣṭaravaṁ niśamya; laṅkālayā bhīmataraṁ vineduḥ

translations.english: Seeing him, the monkeys shouted, and he also, seeing them, shouted in delight. And hearing their tremendous cheers, those residing in Lankā shouted still more dreadfully.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महात्मा निपपात तस्मि;ञ्शैलोत्तमे वानरसैन्यमध्ये
हर्युत्तमेभ्यः शिरसाभिवाद्य; विभीषणं तत्र च सस्वजे सः
verses.transliteration:
tato mahātmā nipapāta tasmi;ñśailottame vānarasainyamadhye
haryuttamebhyaḥ śirasābhivādya; vibhīṣaṇaṁ tatra ca sasvaje saḥ

translations.english: Then the high-souled one dropped on that best of mountains in the midst of the monkey-forces; and, bowing down to the principal monkeys there, he embraced Vibhisana.

verses.sanskrit:
तावप्युभौ मानुषराजपुत्रौ; तं गन्धमाघ्राय महौषधीनाम्
बभूवतुस्तत्र तदा विशल्या;वुत्तस्थुरन्ये च हरिप्रवीराः
verses.transliteration:
tāvapyubhau mānuṣarājaputrau; taṁ gandhamāghrāya mahauṣadhīnām
babhūvatustatra tadā viśalyā;vuttasthuranye ca haripravīrāḥ

translations.english: Then those sons of that king of men, smelling the perfume of that mighty medicine, were then and there healed of their wounds; and the heroic monkeys also sat up. And all the heroic monkeys were instantly healed and cured; and those also that were slain (in battle), through the smell of that best of drugs, sat up, like persons risen after sleep at break of day.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो हरिर्गन्धवहात्मजस्तु; तमोषधीशैलमुदग्रवीर्यः
निनाय वेगाद्धिमवन्तमेव; पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम
verses.transliteration:
tato harirgandhavahātmajastu; tamoṣadhīśailamudagravīryaḥ
nināya vegāddhimavantameva; punaśca rāmeṇa samājagāma

translations.english: Then that monkey, the offspring of the bearer of fragrance, endowed with terrific speed, took that medicinal mountain (back) to Himavān and again presented himself before Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः
अर्थ्यं विजापयंश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīnmahātejāḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
arthyaṁ vijāpayaṁścāpi hanūmantaṁ mahābalam

translations.english: Then the exceedingly energetic lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, said to Hanumān these words fraught with import,

verses.sanskrit:
यतो हतः कुम्भकर्णः कुमाराश्च निषूदिताः
नेदानीमुपनिर्हारं रावणो दातुमर्हति
verses.transliteration:
yato hataḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ kumārāśca niṣūditāḥ
nedānīmupanirhāraṁ rāvaṇo dātumarhati

translations.english: Inasmuch as Kumbhakarma has been slain as also the princes,' Rāvana can no longer defend the city.

verses.sanskrit:
ये ये महाबलाः सन्ति लघवश्च प्लवंगमाः
लङ्कामभ्युत्पतन्त्वाशु गृह्योल्काः प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
ye ye mahābalāḥ santi laghavaśca plavaṁgamāḥ
laṅkāmabhyutpatantvāśu gṛhyolkāḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: Now let those principal monkeys that are endowed with great strength and that are furnished with fleetness, taking fire-brands (in their hands) rapidly rush towards Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽस्तं गत आदित्ये रौद्रे तस्मिन्निशामुखे
लङ्कामभिमुखाः सोल्का जग्मुस्ते प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
tato'staṁ gata āditye raudre tasminniśāmukhe
laṅkāmabhimukhāḥ solkā jagmuste plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: Then when the Sun had set and at the terrific front of Night, those foremost of monkeys marched towards Larikā, equipped with firebrands.

verses.sanskrit:
उल्काहस्तैर्हरिगणैः सर्वतः समभिद्रुताः
आरक्षस्था विरूपाक्षाः सहसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
ulkāhastairharigaṇaiḥ sarvataḥ samabhidrutāḥ
ārakṣasthā virūpākṣāḥ sahasā vipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Charged at all points by nur bers of monkeys armed with fire-brands, those firece-eyed (Rākş asas) that guarded the gates.* suddenly fled away. *Araksasthā-according to some means gates. According to others, a gulma or division of an army.

verses.sanskrit:
गोपुराट्ट प्रतोलीषु चर्यासु विविधासु च
प्रासादेषु च संहृष्टाः ससृजुस्ते हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
gopurāṭṭa pratolīṣu caryāsu vividhāsu ca
prāsādeṣu ca saṁhṛṣṭāḥ sasṛjuste hutāśanam

translations.english: Thereat (the monkeys) delighted set fire to gates and upper apartments and spacious highways and various by-ways and edifices.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां गृहसहस्राणि ददाह हुतभुक्तदा
आवासान्राक्षसानां च सर्वेषां गृहमेधिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ gṛhasahasrāṇi dadāha hutabhuktadā
āvāsānrākṣasānāṁ ca sarveṣāṁ gṛhamedhinām

translations.english: The fire' burnt their mansions by thousands; and mountain-like superstructures toppled headiong to the earth. 1. Hutabhuk-lit. eater of sacrificial offspring's, a designation of fire. 2. According to the commentator this refers to the fire lighted by the monkeys. I differ.

verses.sanskrit:
विमानेषु प्रसुप्ताश्च दह्यमाना वराङ्गनाः
त्यक्ताभरणसंयोगा हाहेत्युच्चैर्विचुक्रुशः
verses.transliteration:
vimāneṣu prasuptāśca dahyamānā varāṅganāḥ
tyaktābharaṇasaṁyogā hāhetyuccairvicukruśaḥ

translations.english: And superb damsels asleep in lofty edifices, being burnt, cast away their ornaments and shrieked bitterly saying "Alas! Woe is me". * Vimäna, according to Rämānuja, is a sevenstoried edifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र चाग्निपरीतानि निपेतुर्भवनान्यपि
वज्रिवज्रहतानीव शिखराणि महागिरेः
verses.transliteration:
tatra cāgniparītāni nipeturbhavanānyapi
vajrivajrahatānīva śikharāṇi mahāgireḥ

translations.english: Consumed by the fire, buildings began to drop down like the summits of a mighty mountain smite with the thunder-bolt of the thunderer.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि निर्दह्यमानानि दूरतः प्रचकाशिरे
हिमवच्छिखराणीव दीप्तौषधिवनानि च
verses.transliteration:
tāni nirdahyamānāni dūrataḥ pracakāśire
himavacchikharāṇīva dīptauṣadhivanāni ca

translations.english: And those burning, appeared from a distance like the peaks of Himalaya aglow.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्म्याग्रैर्दह्यमानैश्च ज्वालाप्रज्वलितैरपि
रात्रौ सा दृश्यते लङ्का पुष्पितैरिव किंशुकैः
verses.transliteration:
harmyāgrairdahyamānaiśca jvālāprajvalitairapi
rātrau sā dṛśyate laṅkā puṣpitairiva kiṁśukaiḥ

translations.english: In consequence of those tops of the edifices burning and of the living flames, that night Lankā looked as if swarming with flowering Kinsukas.

verses.sanskrit:
हस्त्यध्यक्षैर्गजैर्मुक्तैर्मुक्तैश्च तुरगैरपि
बभूव लङ्का लोकान्ते भ्रान्तग्राह इवार्णवः
verses.transliteration:
hastyadhyakṣairgajairmuktairmuktaiśca turagairapi
babhūva laṅkā lokānte bhrāntagrāha ivārṇavaḥ

translations.english: With elephant-riders, and elephants, and steeds let loose, Lankä appeared like the Ocean at the hour of Universal tumbling, with its ferocious aquatic animals whirling in wild chaos.

verses.sanskrit:
अश्वं मुक्तं गजो दृष्ट्वा कच्चिद्भीतोऽपसर्पति
भीतो भीतं गजं दृष्ट्वा क्वचिदश्वो निवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
aśvaṁ muktaṁ gajo dṛṣṭvā kaccidbhīto'pasarpati
bhīto bhītaṁ gajaṁ dṛṣṭvā kvacidaśvo nivartate

translations.english: Sometimes, an elephant seeing a steed let loose, was flying away in fear, and sometimes a horse seeing a frightened elephant, was stopping, himself seized with fear.

verses.sanskrit:
सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन हरिभिर्दीपिता पुरी
लोकस्यास्य क्षये घोरे प्रदीप्तेव वसुंधरा
verses.transliteration:
sā babhūva muhūrtena haribhirdīpitā purī
lokasyāsya kṣaye ghore pradīpteva vasuṁdharā

translations.english: In a short time that city set on fire by the monkeys, looked like the earth glowing at the time of the Universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
नारी जनस्य धूमेन व्याप्तस्योच्चैर्विनेदुषः
स्वनो ज्वलनतप्तस्य शुश्रुवे दशयोजनम्
verses.transliteration:
nārī janasya dhūmena vyāptasyoccairvineduṣaḥ
svano jvalanataptasya śuśruve daśayojanam

translations.english: The cries of the females amidst the drift of smoke, heated by the flames, could be heard from an hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदग्धकायानपरान्राक्षसान्निर्गतान्बहिः
सहसाभ्युत्पतन्ति स्म हरयोऽथ युयुत्सवः
verses.transliteration:
pradagdhakāyānaparānrākṣasānnirgatānbahiḥ
sahasābhyutpatanti sma harayo'tha yuyutsavaḥ

translations.english: As Rākşasas having their bodies burnt came out of houses, monkeys eager for encounter on a sudden sprung upon them.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्घुष्टं वानराणां च राक्षसानां च निस्वनः
दिशो दश समुद्रं च पृथिवीं चान्वनादयत्
verses.transliteration:
udghuṣṭaṁ vānarāṇāṁ ca rākṣasānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
diśo daśa samudraṁ ca pṛthivīṁ cānvanādayat

translations.english: The shouts of the monkeys and the cries of the Rākşasas made the ten cardinal quarters and the ocean and the Earth resound.

verses.sanskrit:
विशल्यौ तु महात्मानौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
असंभ्रान्तौ जगृहतुस्तावुभौ धनुषी वरे
verses.transliteration:
viśalyau tu mahātmānau tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
asaṁbhrāntau jagṛhatustāvubhau dhanuṣī vare

translations.english: On those high-souled ones both Rāma and Lakşmaņa-having been cured of their wounds, possessing themselves in calmness, took up their excellent bows.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विस्फारयाणस्य रामस्य धनुरुत्तमम्
बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो राक्षसानां भयावहः
verses.transliteration:
tato visphārayāṇasya rāmasya dhanuruttamam
babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo rākṣasānāṁ bhayāvahaḥ

translations.english: Rāma drew that best of bows. And thereat there was heard a tremendous twang striking terror into the Rákşasas,

verses.sanskrit:
अशोभत तदा रामो धनुर्विस्फारयन्महत्
भगवानिव संक्रुद्धो भवो वेदमयं धनुः
verses.transliteration:
aśobhata tadā rāmo dhanurvisphārayanmahat
bhagavāniva saṁkruddho bhavo vedamayaṁ dhanuḥ

translations.english: And drawing his redoubtable bow, Rāma appeared like the reverend enraged Bhava, drawing his bow having sounds, and instinct with Brahma energy.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरोद्घुष्टघोषश्च राक्षसानां च निस्वनः
ज्याशब्दश्चापि रामस्य त्रयं व्याप दिशो दश
verses.transliteration:
vānarodghuṣṭaghoṣaśca rākṣasānāṁ ca nisvanaḥ
jyāśabdaścāpi rāmasya trayaṁ vyāpa diśo daśa

translations.english: The ululations of the monkeys and the cries of the Raksasas and the rattle of Rama's bowthese three filled the ten cardinal quarters.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य कार्मुकमुक्तैश्च शरैस्तत्पुरगोपुरम्
कैलासशृङ्गप्रतिमं विकीर्णमपतद्भुवि
verses.transliteration:
tasya kārmukamuktaiśca śaraistatpuragopuram
kailāsaśṛṅgapratimaṁ vikīrṇamapatadbhuvi

translations.english: With the shafts discharged from his bow, the gieway of the city resembling the summit of 1. islās. was crushed in pieces, scattered around cr the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रामशरान्दृष्ट्वा विमानेषु गृहेषु च
संनाहो राक्षसेन्द्राणां तुमुलः समपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
tato rāmaśarāndṛṣṭvā vimāneṣu gṛheṣu ca
saṁnāho rākṣasendrāṇāṁ tumulaḥ samapadyata

translations.english: See cs Rāma's shafts in cars and dwellings, the preparations for conflict were pushed on with great viour.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां संनह्यमानानां सिंहनादं च कुर्वताम्
शर्वरी राक्षसेन्द्राणां रौद्रीव समपद्यत
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ saṁnahyamānānāṁ siṁhanādaṁ ca kurvatām
śarvarī rākṣasendrāṇāṁ raudrīva samapadyata

translations.english: An' in consequence of the foremost Rakşasas preparing for fight, and emitting roars, that night appeared like the Fatal Night itself.

verses.sanskrit:
आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रास्ते सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
आसन्ना द्वारमासाद्य युध्यध्वं प्लवगर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
ādiṣṭā vānarendrāste sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
āsannā dvāramāsādya yudhyadhvaṁ plavagarṣabhāḥ

translations.english: The foremost monkeys were directed by the high-souled Sugriva, saying, “You monkeys, do you fight, approaching the gate lying at hand.

verses.sanskrit:
यश्च वो वितथं कुर्यात्तत्र तत्र व्यवस्थितः
स हन्तव्योऽभिसंप्लुत्य राजशासनदूषकः
verses.transliteration:
yaśca vo vitathaṁ kuryāttatra tatra vyavasthitaḥ
sa hantavyo'bhisaṁplutya rājaśāsanadūṣakaḥ

translations.english: But he that fly from his ranks, should be slain by main force.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषु वानरमुख्येषु दीप्तोल्कोज्ज्वलपाणिषु
स्थितेषु द्वारमासाद्य रावणं मन्युराविशत्
verses.transliteration:
teṣu vānaramukhyeṣu dīptolkojjvalapāṇiṣu
sthiteṣu dvāramāsādya rāvaṇaṁ manyurāviśat

translations.english: As the principal monkeys stationed themselves at the gate, equipped with fire-brands, wrath took possession of Rävana.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य जृम्भितविक्षेपाद्व्यामिश्रा वै दिशो दश
रूपवानिव रुद्रस्य मन्युर्गात्रेष्वदृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
tasya jṛmbhitavikṣepādvyāmiśrā vai diśo daśa
rūpavāniva rudrasya manyurgātreṣvadṛśyata

translations.english: And as he yawned, the wind (blowing) from his mouth), filled the ten cardinal regions; and his wrath resembled that appearing in the person of Rudra.

verses.sanskrit:
स निकुम्भं च कुम्भं च कुम्भकर्णात्मजावुभौ
प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
sa nikumbhaṁ ca kumbhaṁ ca kumbhakarṇātmajāvubhau
preṣayāmāsa saṁkruddho rākṣasairbahubhiḥ saha

translations.english: And wrought up with a mighty rage, he sent forth Kumbha and Nikumbha-both sons of Kumbhakarna-in company with innumerable Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
शशास चैव तान्सर्वान्राक्षसान्राक्षसेश्वरः
राक्षसा गच्छतात्रैव सिंहनादं च नादयन्
verses.transliteration:
śaśāsa caiva tānsarvānrākṣasānrākṣaseśvaraḥ
rākṣasā gacchatātraiva siṁhanādaṁ ca nādayan

translations.english: Setting up leonine roars, he commanded all those highly powerful Raksasas, saying, "Do you go this very day for battle."

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु चोदितास्तेन राक्षसा ज्वलितायुधाः
लङ्काया निर्ययुर्वीराः प्रणदन्तः पुनः पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu coditāstena rākṣasā jvalitāyudhāḥ
laṅkāyā niryayurvīrāḥ praṇadantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ

translations.english: Thus directed, those heroic heroic Rakşasas, equipped with flaming weapons, went out, roaring again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसंमोदित महानिलम्
घोरं शूरजनाकीर्णं महाम्बुधरनिस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
gandhamālyamadhūtsekasaṁmodita mahānilam
ghoraṁ śūrajanākīrṇaṁ mahāmbudharanisvanam

translations.english: Seeing the army of the Räkşasas incapable of being coped with advance, the monkey-forces began to move and send up loud cheers.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा बलमायान्तं राक्षसानां सुदारुणम्
संचचाल प्लवंगानां बलमुच्चैर्ननाद च
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā balamāyāntaṁ rākṣasānāṁ sudāruṇam
saṁcacāla plavaṁgānāṁ balamuccairnanāda ca

translations.english: Thereat that array of Räkşasas vehemently sprang forward before the force of the foe, like to insects plunging into a flame.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां भुजपरामर्शव्यामृष्टपरिघाशनि
राक्षसानां बलं श्रेष्ठं भूयस्तरमशोभत
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ bhujaparāmarśavyāmṛṣṭaparighāśani
rākṣasānāṁ balaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ bhūyastaramaśobhata

translations.english: And whirling with their arms bludgeons and asanis, that army of Rakşasas appeared exceedingly grand.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैवाप्यपरे तेषां कपीनामसिभिः शितैः
प्रवीरानभितो जघ्नुर्घोररूपा निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
tathaivāpyapare teṣāṁ kapīnāmasibhiḥ śitaiḥ
pravīrānabhito jaghnurghorarūpā niśācarāḥ

translations.english: In the same way other grim-visaged nightrangers slew with sharpened swords the foremost of monkeys on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
घ्नन्तमन्यं जघानान्यः पातयन्तमपातयत्
गर्हमाणं जगर्हान्ये दशन्तमपरेऽदशत्
verses.transliteration:
ghnantamanyaṁ jaghānānyaḥ pātayantamapātayat
garhamāṇaṁ jagarhānye daśantamapare'daśat

translations.english: And one about to slay another was himself slain by the latter; and one, about to bring another down, was himself brought down (by his adversary, and one that was railing at another, was in turn rebuked by his enemy; and one who was going to bite his foe, was himself bitten by him.

verses.sanskrit:
देहीत्यन्ये ददात्यन्यो ददामीत्यपरः पुनः
किं क्लेशयसि तिष्ठेति तत्रान्योन्यं बभाषिरे
verses.transliteration:
dehītyanye dadātyanyo dadāmītyaparaḥ punaḥ
kiṁ kleśayasi tiṣṭheti tatrānyonyaṁ babhāṣire

translations.english: One was crying 'Give.'* and his adversary anon give; and another, again said, I will give. Why put yourself to trouble? Stay. *Battle.

verses.sanskrit:
समुद्यतमहाप्रासं मुष्टिशूलासिसंकुलम्
प्रावर्तत महारौद्रं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
samudyatamahāprāsaṁ muṣṭiśūlāsisaṁkulam
prāvartata mahāraudraṁ yuddhaṁ vānararakṣasām

translations.english: Thus there did they accost each other. And there was waged a terrific encounter between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, in which arms lay scattered about; and armour and weapons strewn around; and mighty prāsas' were upraised; and which was fought with blows and darts and swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Rākşasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

verses.sanskrit:
विस्रस्तकेशरसनं विमुक्तकवचध्वजम्
बलं राक्षसमालम्ब्य वानराः पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
visrastakeśarasanaṁ vimuktakavacadhvajam
balaṁ rākṣasamālambya vānarāḥ paryavārayan

translations.english: Then the monkeys hemmed in the Rākşasaforces, with their apparels falling off and with their mail and standards strewn around. swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Rākşasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवृत्ते संकुले तस्मिन्घोरे वीरजनक्षये
अङ्गदः कम्पनं वीरमाससाद रणोत्सुकः
verses.transliteration:
pravṛtte saṁkule tasminghore vīrajanakṣaye
aṅgadaḥ kampanaṁ vīramāsasāda raṇotsukaḥ

translations.english: On that furious and destructive carnage proceeding, Angada eager for encounter, approached the heroic Kampana.

verses.sanskrit:
आहूय सोऽङ्गदं कोपात्ताडयामास वेगितः
गदया कम्पनः पूर्वं स चचाल भृशाहतः
verses.transliteration:
āhūya so'ṅgadaṁ kopāttāḍayāmāsa vegitaḥ
gadayā kampanaḥ pūrvaṁ sa cacāla bhṛśāhataḥ

translations.english: Thereat, challenging Angada in wrath, he assailed him with impetuosity. And Kampana dealt a blow to Angada with his mace; and thereat, wounded with it, he reeled.

verses.sanskrit:
स संज्ञां प्राप्य तेजस्वी चिक्षेप शिखरं गिरेः
अर्दितश्च प्रहारेण कम्पनः पतितो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁjñāṁ prāpya tejasvī cikṣepa śikharaṁ gireḥ
arditaśca prahāreṇa kampanaḥ patito bhuvi

translations.english: Then regaining his senses, that energetic one hurled a mountain-top. Borne down by the blow, Kampana dropped down to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
हतप्रवीरा व्यथिता राक्षसेन्द्रचमूस्तदा
जगामाभिमुखी सा तु कुम्भकर्णसुतो यतः
आपतन्तीं च वेगेन कुम्भस्तां सान्त्वयच्चमूम्
verses.transliteration:
hatapravīrā vyathitā rākṣasendracamūstadā
jagāmābhimukhī sā tu kumbhakarṇasuto yataḥ
āpatantīṁ ca vegena kumbhastāṁ sāntvayaccamūm

translations.english: Thereupon the force of the lord of the Rāks asas, having its foremost heroes slain, and aggrieved thereat, went to where Kumbhakarma's son was.

verses.sanskrit:
स धनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः प्रगृह्य सुसमाहितः
मुमोचाशीविषप्रख्याञ्शरान्देहविदारणान्
verses.transliteration:
sa dhanurdhanvināṁ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya susamāhitaḥ
mumocāśīviṣaprakhyāñśarāndehavidāraṇān

translations.english: And heedfully taking his bow, that first of bowmen discharged shafts resembling venomous serpents capable of piercing the body.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तच्छुशुभे भूयः सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्
विद्युदैरावतार्चिष्मद्द्वितीयेन्द्रधनुर्यथा
verses.transliteration:
tasya tacchuśubhe bhūyaḥ saśaraṁ dhanuruttamam
vidyudairāvatārciṣmaddvitīyendradhanuryathā

translations.english: And his excellent bow with shafts shone resplendent like the very bow of Indra himself affluent with the splendour of Airāvata and lightning.

verses.sanskrit:
आकर्णकृष्टमुक्तेन जघान द्विविदं तदा
तेन हाटकपुङ्खेन पत्रिणा पत्रवाससा
verses.transliteration:
ākarṇakṛṣṭamuktena jaghāna dvividaṁ tadā
tena hāṭakapuṅkhena patriṇā patravāsasā

translations.english: Then drawing his bow to its utmost bent, he hit Dvivida with a feathered shaft knobbed with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
सहसाभिहतस्तेन विप्रमुक्तपदः स्फुरन्
निपपाताद्रिकूटाभो विह्वलः प्लवगोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
sahasābhihatastena vipramuktapadaḥ sphuran
nipapātādrikūṭābho vihvalaḥ plavagottamaḥ

translations.english: Suddenly wounded with it, that best of monkeys having the splendour of Trikūța, fell down senseless to the earth, stretching his legs wide.

verses.sanskrit:
तां शिलां तु प्रचिक्षेप राक्षसाय महाबलः
बिभेद तां शिलां कुम्भः प्रसन्नैः पञ्चभिः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ śilāṁ tu pracikṣepa rākṣasāya mahābalaḥ
bibheda tāṁ śilāṁ kumbhaḥ prasannaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Mainda, seeing his brother, broken in mighty encounter, furiously rushed forward, taking a gigantic crag; and that one possessed of great strength, hurled it at the Raksasa. And thereat Kumbha "severed that crag with five shafts discharged (from his bow).

verses.sanskrit:
संधाय चान्यं सुमुखं शरमाशीविषोपमम्
आजघान महातेजा वक्षसि द्विविदाग्रजम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁdhāya cānyaṁ sumukhaṁ śaramāśīviṣopamam
ājaghāna mahātejā vakṣasi dvividāgrajam

translations.english: Then aiming other fair-headed arrows resembling venomous snakes, that exceedingly energetic one smote Dvivida's elder brother in the chest.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तेन प्रहारेण मैन्दो वानरयूथपः
मर्मण्यभिहतस्तेन पपात भुवि मूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tena prahāreṇa maindo vānarayūthapaḥ
marmaṇyabhihatastena papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And struck (with those arrows), that leader of monkey-bands, Mainda, with his marrow pierced therewith, fell down to the earth, deprived of his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदो मातुलौ दृष्ट्वा पतितौ तौ महाबलौ
अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgado mātulau dṛṣṭvā patitau tau mahābalau
abhidudrāva vegena kumbhamudyatakārmukam

translations.english: Angada seeing his uncles* endowed with exceeding prowess, overpowered, darted vehemently at Kumbha staying with bow upraised. *Maternal uncles.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽङ्गदं विविधैर्बाणैः कुम्भो विव्याध वीर्यवान्
अकुण्ठधारैर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैः कनकभूषणैः
verses.transliteration:
so'ṅgadaṁ vividhairbāṇaiḥ kumbho vivyādha vīryavān
akuṇṭhadhārairniśitaistīkṣṇaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: As he descended, Kumbha pierced him with five shafts; and as one pierce an elephant with tomaras, he also pierced (Angada) with three other arrows. And the powerful Kumbha pierced Angada with a great many arrows, sharppointed, whetted, keen and ornamented with gold.

verses.sanskrit:
स प्रचिच्छेद तान्सर्वान्बिभेद च पुनः शिलाः
कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमान्वालिपुत्रसमीरितान्
verses.transliteration:
sa praciccheda tānsarvānbibheda ca punaḥ śilāḥ
kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmānvāliputrasamīritān

translations.english: Vāli's son Angada albeit pierced all over in his person, did not shake; and he kept showering on his* head stones and trees. And the graceful son of Kumbhakarņa cut off and cleft all those (stone and trees) discharged by Valr's son. *Kumbha's.

verses.sanskrit:
आपतन्तं च संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भो वानरयूथपम्
भ्रुवोर्विव्याध बाणाभ्यामुल्काभ्यामिव कुञ्जरम्
verses.transliteration:
āpatantaṁ ca saṁprekṣya kumbho vānarayūthapam
bhruvorvivyādha bāṇābhyāmulkābhyāmiva kuñjaram

translations.english: Seeing him spring up, Kumbha pierced that monkey-leader on the ground with shafts, even as one assail an elephant with fire-brands.

verses.sanskrit:
स चिच्छेद शितैर्बाणैः सप्तभिः कायभेदनैः
अङ्गदो विव्यथेऽभीक्ष्णं ससाद च मुमोह च
verses.transliteration:
sa ciccheda śitairbāṇaiḥ saptabhiḥ kāyabhedanaiḥ
aṅgado vivyathe'bhīkṣṇaṁ sasāda ca mumoha ca

translations.english: Thereat he* severed it with seven sharp shafts capable of piercing the body. And Angada experienced a sharp pang and fell down deprived of his senses. *Kumbha.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गदं व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा सीदन्तमिव सागरे
दुरासदं हरिश्रेष्ठा राघवाय न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
aṅgadaṁ vyathitaṁ dṛṣṭvā sīdantamiva sāgare
durāsadaṁ hariśreṣṭhā rāghavāya nyavedayan

translations.english: Seeing the invincible Angada down like ebbing sea, the foremost monkeys informed Raghava of it.

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्तु व्यथितं श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रं महाहवे
व्यादिदेश हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवत्प्रमुखांस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
rāmastu vyathitaṁ śrutvā vāliputraṁ mahāhave
vyādideśa hariśreṣṭhāñjāmbavatpramukhāṁstataḥ

translations.english: Rama, hearing that Vali's son had come to grief in terrific fight, directed the principal monkeys, headed by Jambavan.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु वानरशार्दूलाः श्रुत्वा रामस्य शासनम्
अभिपेतुः सुसंक्रुद्धाः कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्
verses.transliteration:
te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śrutvā rāmasya śāsanam
abhipetuḥ susaṁkruddhāḥ kumbhamudyatakārmukam

translations.english: And hearing Rama's command, the monkeys, fired with wrath, charged Kumbha, staying with his bow upraised.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो द्रुमशिलाहस्ताः कोपसंरक्तलोचनाः
रिरक्षिषन्तोऽभ्यपतन्नङ्गदं वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
tato drumaśilāhastāḥ kopasaṁraktalocanāḥ
rirakṣiṣanto'bhyapatannaṅgadaṁ vānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: Those powerful monkeys, with their eyes crimsoned with choler and bearing rocks and trees in their hands, were engaged in defending Angada.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः
कुम्भकर्णात्मजं वीरं क्रुद्धाः समभिदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavāṁśca suṣeṇaśca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ
kumbhakarṇātmajaṁ vīraṁ kruddhāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ

translations.english: Jāmbavān and Suşeņa and the monkey, Vegadarsi, wrought with wrath, darted against that hero-son to Kumbhakarma.

verses.sanskrit:
समीक्ष्यातततस्तांस्तु वानरेन्द्रान्महाबलान्
आववार शरौघेण नगेनेव जलाशयम्
verses.transliteration:
samīkṣyātatatastāṁstu vānarendrānmahābalān
āvavāra śaraugheṇa nageneva jalāśayam

translations.english: Seeing them spring forward; he covered up those exceedingly mighty lords of monkey, with showers of shafts, even as a crag obstruct the course of a current.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बाणचयं प्राप्य न शोकेरतिवर्तितुम्
वानरेन्द्रा महात्मानो वेलामिव महोदधिः
verses.transliteration:
tasya bāṇacayaṁ prāpya na śokerativartitum
vānarendrā mahātmāno velāmiva mahodadhiḥ

translations.english: Even the great deep cannot see his own shores, those high-souled lord of monkeys, coming within the range of his arrows, could not even see.

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा हरिगणाञ्शरवृष्टिभिरर्दितान्
अङ्गदं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भ्रातृजं प्लवगेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstu dṛṣṭvā harigaṇāñśaravṛṣṭibhirarditān
aṅgadaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhrātṛjaṁ plavageśvaraḥ

translations.english: Seeing those monkeys sore distressed by the shafts, the king of the monkeys, Sugrīva, in that conflict taking his brother's son on his back, rushed against the son of Kumbhakarna, even as a powerful lion rush at an elephant ranging on the slopes of a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पाट्य च महाशैलानश्वकर्णान्धवान्बहून्
अन्यांश्च विविधान्वृक्षांश्चिक्षेप च महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
utpāṭya ca mahāśailānaśvakarṇāndhavānbahūn
anyāṁśca vividhānvṛkṣāṁścikṣepa ca mahābalaḥ

translations.english: That mighty monkey, uprooting many an asvakarna and other mighty trees of various kinds, discharged them (at the foe).

verses.sanskrit:
तां छादयन्तीमाकाशं वृक्षवृष्टिं दुरासदाम्
कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमांश्चिच्छेद निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ chādayantīmākāśaṁ vṛkṣavṛṣṭiṁ durāsadām
kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmāṁściccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: By means of his sharp arrows the graceful son of Kumbhakarņa cut off that down-pour of trees covering the welkin; and incapable of being resisted. And being beffled those trees looked like sataghnis.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रुमवर्षं तु तच्छिन्नं दृष्ट्वा कुम्भेन वीर्यवान्
वानराधिपतिः श्रीमान्महासत्त्वो न विव्यथे
verses.transliteration:
drumavarṣaṁ tu tacchinnaṁ dṛṣṭvā kumbhena vīryavān
vānarādhipatiḥ śrīmānmahāsattvo na vivyathe

translations.english: Seeing that shower of trees riven by Kumbha, the graceful lord of the monkeys endowed with exceeding strength and prowess, did not feel any mortification.

verses.sanskrit:
अवप्लुत्य ततः शीघ्रं कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
अब्रवीत्कुपितः कुम्भं भग्नशृङ्गमिव द्विपम्
verses.transliteration:
avaplutya tataḥ śīghraṁ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
abravītkupitaḥ kumbhaṁ bhagnaśṛṅgamiva dvipam

translations.english: Suddenly attacked, he bearing those arrows, seized Kumbha's bow resembling in resplendence the very bow of Indra. And swiftly bounding up and performing that feat difficult of being achieved, he, exceedingly enraged, addressed Kumbha resembling an elephant shorn of his tusks, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
वरदानात्पितृव्यस्ते सहते देवदानवान्
कुम्भकर्णस्तु वीर्येण सहते च सुरासुरान्
verses.transliteration:
varadānātpitṛvyaste sahate devadānavān
kumbhakarṇastu vīryeṇa sahate ca surāsurān

translations.english: It is only by virtue of the boon he has received, that your uncle can bear the deities and the Dānavas. But Kumbhakarņa cop with the immortals and Asuras by means of his native might. And in the bow equal to Indrajit himself and in power equal to Rāvana, you now in might and energy are the foremost of Räkşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
महाविमर्दं समरे मया सह तवाद्भुतम्
अद्य भूतानि पश्यन्तु शक्रशम्बरयोरिव
verses.transliteration:
mahāvimardaṁ samare mayā saha tavādbhutam
adya bhūtāni paśyantu śakraśambarayoriva

translations.english: Today let all creatures witness the mighty and wonderful encounter in conflict between you and me, like to the meeting of Śakra and Sambara.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतमप्रतिमं कर्म दर्शितं चास्त्रकौशलम्
पातिता हरिवीराश्च त्वयैते भीमविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtamapratimaṁ karma darśitaṁ cāstrakauśalam
pātitā harivīrāśca tvayaite bhīmavikramāḥ

translations.english: Unparalleled is the feat you have performed; and you have displayed your skill in weapons. And heroic monkeys endowed with dreadful vigour, have been brought down by you.

verses.sanskrit:
उपालम्भभयाच्चापि नासि वीर मया हतः
कृतकर्मा परिश्रान्तो विश्रान्तः पश्य मे बलम्
verses.transliteration:
upālambhabhayāccāpi nāsi vīra mayā hataḥ
kṛtakarmā pariśrānto viśrāntaḥ paśya me balam

translations.english: O hero it is only because of the apprehension* of censure of the people that I do not slay you who are fatigued in consequence of the acts that you have performed. And reposing from fight, do you see my strength! *i.e. Lest people should censure me, saying, Sugrīva slew Kumbha when he was fatigued in fight.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन सुग्रीववाक्येन सावमानेन मानितः
अग्नेराज्यहुतस्येव तेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत
verses.transliteration:
tena sugrīvavākyena sāvamānena mānitaḥ
agnerājyahutasyeva tejastasyābhyavardhata

translations.english: Being thus honoured (by Sugrīva) with fair speech, (Kumbha) flamed up like a flame into which oblations have been poured.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कुम्भः समुत्पत्य सुग्रीवमभिपद्य च
आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रवेगेन मुष्टिना
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kumbhaḥ samutpatya sugrīvamabhipadya ca
ājaghānorasi kruddho vajravegena muṣṭinā

translations.english: Then springing up, and bringing Sugriva down, Kumbha, transported with wrath dealt a blow on his chest, like to the levin.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य चर्म च पुस्फोट संजज्ञे चास्य शोणितम्
स च मुष्टिर्महावेगः प्रतिजघ्नेऽस्थिमण्डले
verses.transliteration:
tasya carma ca pusphoṭa saṁjajñe cāsya śoṇitam
sa ca muṣṭirmahāvegaḥ pratijaghne'sthimaṇḍale

translations.english: Thereat his skin was rent, and blood began to gush out, and the impetus of that blow broke Sugriva's bones.

verses.sanskrit:
तदा वेगेन तत्रासीत्तेजः प्रज्वालितं मुहुः
वज्रनिष्पेषसंजातज्वाला मेरौ यथा गिरौ
verses.transliteration:
tadā vegena tatrāsīttejaḥ prajvālitaṁ muhuḥ
vajraniṣpeṣasaṁjātajvālā merau yathā girau

translations.english: The vehemence (of the blow) caused a great fire to blaze up at that spot, even as the thunderbolt smiting the mountain Meru, make place blazed.

verses.sanskrit:
स तत्राभिहतस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरर्षभः
मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास वज्रकल्पं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tatrābhihatastena sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ
muṣṭiṁ saṁvartayāmāsa vajrakalpaṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: The mighty Sugrīva foremost of monkeys-sorely handled by him, fastened his fingers into a box resembling the thunder-bolt, and furnished with all the effulgence of the solar disc having a thousand rays.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्चिःसहस्रविकचं रविमण्डलसप्रभम्
स मुष्टिं पातयामास कुम्भस्योरसि वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
arciḥsahasravikacaṁ ravimaṇḍalasaprabham
sa muṣṭiṁ pātayāmāsa kumbhasyorasi vīryavān

translations.english: Then that powerful one made that blow descend right on on Kumbha's breast. And agonised with that stroke, Kumbha reft of his senses, dropped like to a fire that has lost its brightness.

verses.sanskrit:
मुष्टिनाभिहतस्तेन निपपाताशु राक्षसः
लोहिताङ्ग इवाकाशाद्दीप्तरश्मिर्यदृच्छया
verses.transliteration:
muṣṭinābhihatastena nipapātāśu rākṣasaḥ
lohitāṅga ivākāśāddīptaraśmiryadṛcchayā

translations.english: And overpowered by that blow, the Rākṣasa anon dropped down, like to the bright Lohitānga dropping from the firmament urged on by Destiny.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भस्य पततो रूपं भग्नस्योरसि मुष्टिना
बभौ रुद्राभिपन्नस्य यथारूपं गवां पतेः
verses.transliteration:
kumbhasya patato rūpaṁ bhagnasyorasi muṣṭinā
babhau rudrābhipannasya yathārūpaṁ gavāṁ pateḥ

translations.english: The aspect of the falling Kumbha with his breast broken by the blow, appeared like that of the Sun routed by Rudra.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्हते भीमपराक्रमेण; प्लवंगमानामृषभेण युद्धे
मही सशैला सवना चचाल; भयं च रक्षांस्यधिकं विवेश
verses.transliteration:
tasminhate bhīmaparākrameṇa; plavaṁgamānāmṛṣabheṇa yuddhe
mahī saśailā savanā cacāla; bhayaṁ ca rakṣāṁsyadhikaṁ viveśa

translations.english: On his being slain, in encounter, by the foremost of monkeys endowed with terrific strength, the earth with her hills and woods, shook; and a mighty fear took possession of the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
निकुम्भो भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवेण निपातितम्
प्रदहन्निव कोपेन वानरेन्द्रमवैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
nikumbho bhrātaraṁ dṛṣṭvā sugrīveṇa nipātitam
pradahanniva kopena vānarendramavaikṣata

translations.english: Seeing his brother slain by Sugrīva, Nikumbha, gazed at the lord of the monkeys, as if consuming him with his passion.

verses.sanskrit:
हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तं वज्रविद्रुमभूषितम्
यमदण्डोपमं भीमं रक्षसां भयनाशनम्
verses.transliteration:
hemapaṭṭaparikṣiptaṁ vajravidrumabhūṣitam
yamadaṇḍopamaṁ bhīmaṁ rakṣasāṁ bhayanāśanam

translations.english: Then that one endowed with calmness, grasped a bludgeon entwined with wreaths, and furnished with an iron ring measuring five fingers, and resembling the top of the Mahendra;* plated with gold and embellished with diamonds and lapises, and looking like the rod of Yama himself; dreadful and capable of removing the fear of the Raksas. *The mountain, so named.

verses.sanskrit:
तमाविध्य महातेजाः शक्रध्वजसमं रणे
विननाद विवृत्तास्यो निकुम्भो भीमविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tamāvidhya mahātejāḥ śakradhvajasamaṁ raṇe
vinanāda vivṛttāsyo nikumbho bhīmavikramaḥ

translations.english: And whirling this, that highly powerful one, resembling the banner itself of Sakra in energy, Nikumbha possessed of terrific strength, with his mouth wide open, set up shouts.

verses.sanskrit:
निकुम्भो भूषणैर्भाति तेन स्म परिघेण च
यथेन्द्रधनुषा मेघः सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान्
verses.transliteration:
nikumbho bhūṣaṇairbhāti tena sma parigheṇa ca
yathendradhanuṣā meghaḥ savidyutstanayitnumān

translations.english: With gold adorning his breast, and Angadas placed on his arms and a pair of curious and variegated ear-rings, Nikumbha, with his ornaments and that same bludgeon, appeared beautiful like a mass of roaring clouds laughing with lightning and furnished with the iris.

verses.sanskrit:
परिघाग्रेण पुस्फोट वातग्रन्थिर्महात्मनः
प्रजज्वाल सघोषश्च विधूम इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
parighāgreṇa pusphoṭa vātagranthirmahātmanaḥ
prajajvāla saghoṣaśca vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: The head of that huge-bodied hero's parigha undid the conjunction of the seven' Winds and appeared? like a noiseless and smokeless flame. 1. This indicates the length of the Parigha. 2. This might refer to Kumbha as well.

verses.sanskrit:
सतारागणनक्षत्रं सचन्द्रं समहाग्रहम्
निकुम्भपरिघाघूर्णं भ्रमतीव नभस्तलम्
verses.transliteration:
satārāgaṇanakṣatraṁ sacandraṁ samahāgraham
nikumbhaparighāghūrṇaṁ bhramatīva nabhastalam

translations.english: Along with the gyration of Nikumbha's parigha the whole welkin, together with the excellent city* of the gandharvas, and the planets, stars and the moon, began to whirl. *Some say Vitapabati and some say Alaka.

verses.sanskrit:
दुरासदश्च संजज्ञे परिघाभरणप्रभः
क्रोधेन्धनो निकुम्भाग्निर्युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
durāsadaśca saṁjajñe parighābharaṇaprabhaḥ
krodhendhano nikumbhāgniryugāntāgnirivotthitaḥ

translations.english: Nikumbha was hard to approach like to the fire of dissolution, being resplendent with the brilliance of parigha and other ornaments and having his anger for its fuels.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसा वानराश्चापि न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं भयात्
हनूमंस्तु विवृत्योरस्तस्थौ प्रमुखतो बली
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasā vānarāścāpi na śekuḥ spandituṁ bhayāt
hanūmaṁstu vivṛtyorastasthau pramukhato balī

translations.english: The Rākşasas and monkeys did not dare stir even out of fear. And the heroic Hanumān, spreading his breast, stood before him.

verses.sanskrit:
परिघोपमबाहुस्तु परिघं भास्करप्रभम्
बली बलवतस्तस्य पातयामास वक्षसि
verses.transliteration:
parighopamabāhustu parighaṁ bhāskaraprabham
balī balavatastasya pātayāmāsa vakṣasi

translations.english: Thereat the powerful (Nikumbha) having long-arm* threw his parigha resembling the Sun at the breast of that powerful one. *Lit. arms resembling parighas.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थिरे तस्योरसि व्यूढे परिघः शतधा कृतः
विशीर्यमाणः सहसा उल्का शतमिवाम्बरे
verses.transliteration:
sthire tasyorasi vyūḍhe parighaḥ śatadhā kṛtaḥ
viśīryamāṇaḥ sahasā ulkā śatamivāmbare

translations.english: Falling on the firm and spacious breast of Hanumān it was broken into hundred pieces. The broken portions, being scattered, appeared like hundreds of fire-brands in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तेन प्रहारेण चचाल च महाकपिः
परिघेण समाधूतो यथा भूमिचलेऽचलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tena prahāreṇa cacāla ca mahākapiḥ
parigheṇa samādhūto yathā bhūmicale'calaḥ

translations.english: Like to a mountain standing still even at the time of an earthquake that mighty monkey was not moved albeit struck with the parigha.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथाभिहतस्तेन हनूमान्प्लवगोत्तमः
मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास बलेनातिमहाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tathābhihatastena hanūmānplavagottamaḥ
muṣṭiṁ saṁvartayāmāsa balenātimahābalaḥ

translations.english: Being thus hurt that highly powerful Hanumān, the foremost of the monkeys, with great velocity clenched his fist.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुद्यम्य महातेजा निकुम्भोरसि वीर्यवान्
अभिचिक्षेप वेगेन वेगवान्वायुविक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tamudyamya mahātejā nikumbhorasi vīryavān
abhicikṣepa vegena vegavānvāyuvikramaḥ

translations.english: With this, the powerful (monkey) gifted with great impetuosity, and resembling the wind in prowess, struck Nikumbha on his breast.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुस्फोट चर्मास्य प्रसुस्राव च शोणितम्
मुष्टिना तेन संजज्ञे ज्वाला विद्युदिवोत्थिता
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pusphoṭa carmāsya prasusrāva ca śoṇitam
muṣṭinā tena saṁjajñe jvālā vidyudivotthitā

translations.english: With that fist, his (Nikumbha's) armour* was riven and blood gushed out. And a light rising out of his breast suddenly disappeared like to lightning disappearing in a mass of clouds. *Some texts read carma (skin) in the place of Varma-(armour) i.e., his skin was rent-This equally indicates Hanuman's strength.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तेन प्रहारेण निकुम्भो विचचाल ह
स्वस्थश्चापि निजग्राह हनूमन्तं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
