sa tu tena prahāreṇa nikumbho vicacāla ha
svasthaścāpi nijagrāha hanūmantaṁ mahābalam

translations.english: Being struck with his (Hanuman's) fist Nikumbha was greatly moved and restoring himself attacked the mighty Hanumān and pulled him up.

verses.sanskrit:
विचुक्रुशुस्तदा संख्ये भीमं लङ्कानिवासिनः
निकुम्भेनोद्धृतं दृष्ट्वा हनूमन्तं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration:
vicukruśustadā saṁkhye bhīmaṁ laṅkānivāsinaḥ
nikumbhenoddhṛtaṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmantaṁ mahābalam

translations.english: Beholding in conflict the terrible and powerful Hanumăn pulled up by Nikumbha, the residents of Lankā began to shout with joy.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथा ह्रियमाणोऽपि कुम्भकर्णात्मजेन हि
आजघानानिलसुतो वज्रवेगेन मुष्टिना
verses.transliteration:
sa tathā hriyamāṇo'pi kumbhakarṇātmajena hi
ājaghānānilasuto vajravegena muṣṭinā

translations.english: Being thus put to shame by that Rākşasa, Hanumăn the son of the Wind, struck him with his iron fist.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं मोचयित्वाथ क्षितावभ्यवपद्यत
हनूमानुन्ममथाशु निकुम्भं मारुतात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
ātmānaṁ mocayitvātha kṣitāvabhyavapadyata
hanūmānunmamathāśu nikumbhaṁ mārutātmajaḥ

translations.english: And releasing himself from the grasp of Nikumbha, Hanumān the Wind-god's son instantly planted his foot on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
परिगृह्य च बाहुभ्यां परिवृत्य शिरोधराम्
उत्पाटयामास शिरो भैरवं नदतो महत्
verses.transliteration:
parigṛhya ca bāhubhyāṁ parivṛtya śirodharām
utpāṭayāmāsa śiro bhairavaṁ nadato mahat

translations.english: Inflamed with ire, he, throwing down Nikumbha, began to crush him; and gifted with vehemence, he, with great impetuosity, leaped up and sat on the breast (of the Raksa). And halding his head with two hands, he, emitting loud roars, displaced his head.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ विनदति सादिते निकुम्भे; पवनसुतेन रणे बभूव युद्धम्
दशरथसुतराक्षसेन्द्रचम्वो;र्भृशतरमागतरोषयोः सुभीमम्
verses.transliteration:
atha vinadati sādite nikumbhe; pavanasutena raṇe babhūva yuddham
daśarathasutarākṣasendracamvo;rbhṛśataramāgataroṣayoḥ subhīmam

translations.english: Nikumbha being thus slain in conflict by the Wind-god's son, there ensued a terrible conflict between the highly enraged armies of the son of Dasaratha and the lord of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
निकुम्भं च हतं श्रुत्वा कुम्भं च विनिपातितम्
रावणः परमामर्षी प्रजज्वालानलो यथा
verses.transliteration:
nikumbhaṁ ca hataṁ śrutvā kumbhaṁ ca vinipātitam
rāvaṇaḥ paramāmarṣī prajajvālānalo yathā

translations.english: Beholding Kumbha and Nikumbha slain, Rāvana was excited with ire like to flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृतः क्रोधशोकाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां तु परिमूर्छितः
खरपुत्रं विशालाक्षं मकराक्षमचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
nairṛtaḥ krodhaśokābhyāṁ dvābhyāṁ tu parimūrchitaḥ
kharaputraṁ viśālākṣaṁ makarākṣamacodayat

translations.english: Being beside himself, simultaneously with wrath and grief Rāvana* spoke to Makarāksa, Kahara's son, having spacious eyes, saying, O child, do you proceed at my command with the army and destroy Rāghava and Laksmana with all the monkeys. *Nairta is another name of Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिवाद्य दशग्रीवं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्
निर्जगाम गृहाच्छुभ्राद्रावणस्याज्ञया बली
verses.transliteration:
so'bhivādya daśagrīvaṁ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
nirjagāma gṛhācchubhrādrāvaṇasyājñayā balī

translations.english: Hearing the words of Rāvana, Khara's son, Makarākşa, proud of his own own prowess, delightedly spoke to the night-ranger, saying, “Be it so." And saluting and circumambulating the ten-necked one, that hero, at Ravana's behest, issued out of the house.

verses.sanskrit:
समीपस्थं बलाध्यक्षं खरपुत्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्
रथमानीयतां शीघ्रं सैन्यं चानीयतां त्वरात्
verses.transliteration:
samīpasthaṁ balādhyakṣaṁ kharaputro'bravīdidam
rathamānīyatāṁ śīghraṁ sainyaṁ cānīyatāṁ tvarāt

translations.english: Khara's son spoke to the commander who was near him, saying, “Do you speedily bring the chariot here and all the soldiers."

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो निशाचरः
स्यन्दनं च बलं चैव समीपं प्रत्यपादयत्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā balādhyakṣo niśācaraḥ
syandanaṁ ca balaṁ caiva samīpaṁ pratyapādayat

translations.english: Hearing his words, that commanding nightranger, soon let before him the army and the chariot.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणं रथं कृत्वा आरुरोह निशाचरः
सूतं संचोदयामास शीघ्रं मे रथमावह
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇaṁ rathaṁ kṛtvā āruroha niśācaraḥ
sūtaṁ saṁcodayāmāsa śīghraṁ me rathamāvaha

translations.english: And going round the chariot and addressing the charioteer that night-ranger (Makarāksa) said, O charioteer, do you soon drive the chariot.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तान्राक्षसान्सर्वान्मकराक्षोऽब्रवीदिदम्
यूयं सर्वे प्रयुध्यध्वं पुरस्तान्मम राक्षसाः
verses.transliteration:
atha tānrākṣasānsarvānmakarākṣo'bravīdidam
yūyaṁ sarve prayudhyadhvaṁ purastānmama rākṣasāḥ

translations.english: Thereat Makarākṣa addressed those Räkşasas, saying, O Raksasas! do you all fight before me.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं राक्षसराजेन रावणेन महात्मना
आज्ञप्तः समरे हन्तुं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ rākṣasarājena rāvaṇena mahātmanā
ājñaptaḥ samare hantuṁ tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: I have been commanded by the high-souled Rāvana, the lord of Räksasas, to slay both Rāma and Lakşmaņa in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य रामं वधिष्यामि लक्ष्मणं च निशाचराः
शाखामृगं च सुग्रीवं वानरांश्च शरोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
adya rāmaṁ vadhiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṁ ca niśācarāḥ
śākhāmṛgaṁ ca sugrīvaṁ vānarāṁśca śarottamaiḥ

translations.english: I shall slay to-day, O night-ranger, with my excellent arrows, Rama, Laksmana, Sugriva and all other monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य शूलनिपातैश्च वानराणां महाचमूम्
प्रदहिष्यामि संप्राप्तां शुष्केन्धनमिवानलः
verses.transliteration:
adya śūlanipātaiśca vānarāṇāṁ mahācamūm
pradahiṣyāmi saṁprāptāṁ śuṣkendhanamivānalaḥ

translations.english: Like to fire consuming dry fuel, shall I today slay the host of monkeys with my darts.

verses.sanskrit:
मकराक्षस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं ते निशाचराः
सर्वे नानायुधोपेता बलवन्तः समाहिताः
verses.transliteration:
makarākṣasya tacchrutvā vacanaṁ te niśācarāḥ
sarve nānāyudhopetā balavantaḥ samāhitāḥ

translations.english: Hearing those words of Makarākşa, the mighty night-rangers, (addressed themselves for fight).

verses.sanskrit:
ते कामरूपिणः शूरा दंष्ट्रिणः पिङ्गलेक्षणाः
मातंगा इव नर्दन्तो ध्वस्तकेशा भयानकाः
verses.transliteration:
te kāmarūpiṇaḥ śūrā daṁṣṭriṇaḥ piṅgalekṣaṇāḥ
mātaṁgā iva nardanto dhvastakeśā bhayānakāḥ

translations.english: They were armed with various weapons, cautious; assuming shapes at will, crooked, having fearful teeth, coppery eyes; roaring like elephants, having dishevelled hair and terrible. And encircling the huge-bodied son of Khara, those gigantic (Raksasas) began to proceed, delighted and moving the earth (with the weight of their persons).

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खभेरीसहस्राणामाहतानां समन्ततः
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितानां च ततः शब्दो महानभूत्
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhabherīsahasrāṇāmāhatānāṁ samantataḥ
kṣveḍitāsphoṭitānāṁ ca tataḥ śabdo mahānabhūt

translations.english: There arose a terrible noise on all sides from the sound of conches, and thousands of bugles, and from the moving of the arms of the heroes.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभ्रष्टोऽथ करात्तस्य प्रतोदः सारथेस्तदा
पपात सहसा चैव ध्वजस्तस्य च रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
prabhraṣṭo'tha karāttasya pratodaḥ sārathestadā
papāta sahasā caiva dhvajastasya ca rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: And all on a sudden the reins slipped off (the hands of) the charioteer and the flag of the Råkşasas dropped down.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ते रथसंयुक्ता हया विक्रमवर्जिताः
चरणैराकुलैर्गत्वा दीनाः सास्रमुखा ययुः
verses.transliteration:
tasya te rathasaṁyuktā hayā vikramavarjitāḥ
caraṇairākulairgatvā dīnāḥ sāsramukhā yayuḥ

translations.english: The course of the steeds was thus slackened and they began to move slowly and poorly with their heads drooping down.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रवाति पवनस्तस्य सपांसुः खरदारुणः
निर्याणे तस्य रौद्रस्य मकराक्षस्य दुर्मतेः
verses.transliteration:
pravāti pavanastasya sapāṁsuḥ kharadāruṇaḥ
niryāṇe tasya raudrasya makarākṣasya durmateḥ

translations.english: There blew a terribly rough wind mixed with dust when the fearfully wicked-minded Makaraksa's issued out for battle.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि राक्षसा वीर्यवत्तमाः
अचिन्त्यनिर्गताः सर्वे यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.transliteration:
tāni dṛṣṭvā nimittāni rākṣasā vīryavattamāḥ
acintyanirgatāḥ sarve yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau

translations.english: Those powerful Rākşasas neglecting those bad omens proceeded towards where Rāma and Laksmana were.

verses.sanskrit:
घनगजमहिषाङ्गतुल्यवर्णाः; समरमुखेष्वसकृद्गदासिभिन्नाः
अहमहमिति युद्धकौशलास्ते; रजनिचराः परिबभ्रमुर्नदन्तः
verses.transliteration:
ghanagajamahiṣāṅgatulyavarṇāḥ; samaramukheṣvasakṛdgadāsibhinnāḥ
ahamahamiti yuddhakauśalāste; rajanicarāḥ paribabhramurnadantaḥ

translations.english: They were all black like to clouds, elephants and buffaloes, and had marks of swords and maces on their persons. And all those nightrangers were skilled in the art of warfare and began to range to and fro (in the battle field) saying, “I shall to first.”

verses.sanskrit:
निर्गतं मकराक्षं ते दृष्ट्वा वानरपुंगवाः
आप्लुत्य सहसा सर्वे योद्धुकामा व्यवस्थिताः
verses.transliteration:
nirgataṁ makarākṣaṁ te dṛṣṭvā vānarapuṁgavāḥ
āplutya sahasā sarve yoddhukāmā vyavasthitāḥ

translations.english: Beholding Makarākṣa out for battle, those foremost monkeys leaping on a sudden, addressed themselves for fight.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहत्तद्युद्धं लोमहर्षणम्
निशाचरैः प्लवंगानां देवानां दानवैरिव
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pravṛttaṁ sumahattadyuddhaṁ lomaharṣaṇam
niśācaraiḥ plavaṁgānāṁ devānāṁ dānavairiva

translations.english: Thereupon ensued a terrible conflict, capable of making one's down stand on end, between the right-rangers and the monkeys like to one between the celestials and Dänavas.

verses.sanskrit:
वृक्षशूलनिपातैश्च शिलापरिघपातनैः
अन्योन्यं मर्दयन्ति स्म तदा कपिनिशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
vṛkṣaśūlanipātaiśca śilāparighapātanaiḥ
anyonyaṁ mardayanti sma tadā kapiniśācarāḥ

translations.english: Those monkeys and night-rangers crushed each other down with trees, darts, maces and parighas.

verses.sanskrit:
पाशमुद्गरदण्डैश्च निर्घातैश्चापरैस्तथा
कदनं कपिसिंहानां चक्रुस्ते रजनीचराः
verses.transliteration:
pāśamudgaradaṇḍaiśca nirghātaiścāparaistathā
kadanaṁ kapisiṁhānāṁ cakruste rajanīcarāḥ

translations.english: Those night-rangers began to assail those foremost of monkeys with sakti.' swords, maces, kuntas, tomaras, pattisas, Bhindipālas, arrows, nooses and clubs. 1. A short arrow thrown from the hand or shot through a tube. 2. An Iron spear or dart.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणौघैरर्दिताश्चापि खरपुत्रेण वानराः
संभ्रान्तमनसः सर्वे दुद्रुवुर्भयपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
bāṇaughairarditāścāpi kharaputreṇa vānarāḥ
saṁbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve dudruvurbhayapīḍitāḥ

translations.english: Being thus assailed with fearful arrows by Khara's son, those monkeys, stricken with fear, fled away.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्दृष्ट्वा राक्षसाः सर्वे द्रवमाणान्वनौकसः
नेदुस्ते सिंहवद्धृष्टा राक्षसा जितकाशिनः
verses.transliteration:
tāndṛṣṭvā rākṣasāḥ sarve dravamāṇānvanaukasaḥ
neduste siṁhavaddhṛṣṭā rākṣasā jitakāśinaḥ

translations.english: Beholding those monkeys fly away, all the victorious Rakşasas began to roar like excited lions.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्रवत्सु तदा तेषु वानरेषु समन्ततः
रामस्तान्वारयामास शरवर्षेण राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
vidravatsu tadā teṣu vānareṣu samantataḥ
rāmastānvārayāmāsa śaravarṣeṇa rākṣasān

translations.english: The monkeys thus flying away to all quarters, Rāma with a downpour of shafts assailed the Räkşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
वारितान्राक्षसान्दृष्ट्वा मकराक्षो निशाचरः
क्रोधानलसमाविष्टो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vāritānrākṣasāndṛṣṭvā makarākṣo niśācaraḥ
krodhānalasamāviṣṭo vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Beholding the Rākşasas thus overpowered, the night-ranger Makarākşa, excited with the flame of ire, said.

verses.sanskrit:
तिष्ठ राम मया सार्धं द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ददामि ते
त्याजयिष्यामि ते प्राणान्धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
tiṣṭha rāma mayā sārdhaṁ dvandvayuddhaṁ dadāmi te
tyājayiṣyāmi te prāṇāndhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Stay, O Rama, let us both fight with each other; I shall take your life with sharp arrows discharged off my bow.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्तदा दण्डकारण्ये पितरं हतवान्मम
मदग्रतः स्वकर्मस्थं स्मृत्वा रोषोऽभिवर्धते
verses.transliteration:
yattadā daṇḍakāraṇye pitaraṁ hatavānmama
madagrataḥ svakarmasthaṁ smṛtvā roṣo'bhivardhate

translations.english: You did slay my father in the forest of Dandaka. Remembering your action and finding you before, my ire is excited.

verses.sanskrit:
दह्यन्ते भृशमङ्गानि दुरात्मन्मम राघव
यन्मयासि न दृष्टस्त्वं तस्मिन्काले महावने
verses.transliteration:
dahyante bhṛśamaṅgāni durātmanmama rāghava
yanmayāsi na dṛṣṭastvaṁ tasminkāle mahāvane

translations.english: O Raghava! O Vicious souled one! My limbs are being burnt (with wrath) for I did not see you then in that mighty forest.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्यासि दर्शनं राम मम त्वं प्राप्तवानिह
काङ्क्षितोऽसि क्षुधार्तस्य सिंहस्येवेतरो मृगः
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyāsi darśanaṁ rāma mama tvaṁ prāptavāniha
kāṅkṣito'si kṣudhārtasya siṁhasyevetaro mṛgaḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, by my good luck, I have got you today, like to a hungry lion desiring to have other animals.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य मद्बाणवेगेन प्रेतराड्विषयं गतः
ये त्वया निहताः शूराः सह तैस्त्वं समेष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
adya madbāṇavegena pretarāḍviṣayaṁ gataḥ
ye tvayā nihatāḥ śūrāḥ saha taistvaṁ sameṣyasi

translations.english: Being despatched by my arrows to the world of devils, you shall live with those heroes, who had been killed by you before.

verses.sanskrit:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन शृणु राम वचो मम
पश्यन्तु सकला लोकास्त्वां मां चैव रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration:
bahunātra kimuktena śṛṇu rāma vaco mama
paśyantu sakalā lokāstvāṁ māṁ caiva raṇājire

translations.english: What is the use of speaking more, O Rāma, do you hear my words. Let all the people behold your as well as my prowess in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्रैर्वा गदया वापि बाहुभ्यां वा महाहवे
अभ्यस्तं येन वा राम तेन वा वर्ततां युधि
verses.transliteration:
astrairvā gadayā vāpi bāhubhyāṁ vā mahāhave
abhyastaṁ yena vā rāma tena vā vartatāṁ yudhi

translations.english: Either with weapon or with clubs, in whatever you are expert, do you fight.with me in the battle-field, O Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
मकराक्षवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथात्मजः
अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्वाक्यमुत्तरोत्तरवादिनम्
verses.transliteration:
makarākṣavacaḥ śrutvā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
abravītprahasanvākyamuttarottaravādinam

translations.english: Hearing the words of Makarākşa, Rāma, Dasaratha's son, smiling, replied to the words of the babbler.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वाशितास्तव मांसेन गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः
भविष्यन्त्यद्य वै पाप तीक्ष्णतुण्डनखाङ्कुशाः
verses.transliteration:
svāśitāstava māṁsena gṛdhragomāyuvāyasāḥ
bhaviṣyantyadya vai pāpa tīkṣṇatuṇḍanakhāṅkuśāḥ

translations.english: I slew in the forest of Dandaka your father with fourteen thousand Räksasas, Trisira and Duşana. O vile one, you being slain to day, with your flesh, vultures and crows, having sharp beaks and nails, and jackals shall be satisfied.* [*Here is another śloka, which is to be found in all N.W.P. texts and in one or two texts published in Bengal-but it has been omitted by many for it conveys the same meaning as the previous ſloka; the meaning is-And the birds drinking your blood shall fly away to various quarters.]

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण खरपुत्रो निशाचरः
बाणौघानसृजत्तस्मै राघवाय रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa kharaputro niśācaraḥ
bāṇaughānasṛjattasmai rāghavāya raṇājire

translations.english: Being thus addressed by Rāghava, the mighty Makarākşa, began to dart sharp arrows towards him in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit:
ताञ्शराञ्शरवर्षेण रामश्चिच्छेद नैकधा
निपेतुर्भुवि ते छिन्ना रुक्मपुङ्खाः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tāñśarāñśaravarṣeṇa rāmaściccheda naikadhā
nipeturbhuvi te chinnā rukmapuṅkhāḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And Rāma, with his shafts, sundered into several pieces, those arrows. And being thus rendered useless those arrows, feathered in gold, fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्युद्धमभवत्तत्र समेत्यान्योन्यमोजसा
खर राक्षसपुत्रस्य सूनोर्दशरथस्य च
verses.transliteration:
tadyuddhamabhavattatra sametyānyonyamojasā
khara rākṣasaputrasya sūnordaśarathasya ca

translations.english: Then there arose a terrible conflict between the Raksasa Khara's son and Dasaratha's son.

verses.sanskrit:
जीमूतयोरिवाकाशे शब्दो ज्यातलयोस्तदा
धनुर्मुक्तः स्वनोत्कृष्टः श्रूयते च रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration:
jīmūtayorivākāśe śabdo jyātalayostadā
dhanurmuktaḥ svanotkṛṣṭaḥ śrūyate ca raṇājire

translations.english: There were audible in that battle-field, the outcry of the heroes and the twang of the bows stretched by their hands, like to the muttering of the clouds in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः किंनराश्च महोरगाः
अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration:
devadānavagandharvāḥ kiṁnarāśca mahoragāḥ
antarikṣagatāḥ sarve draṣṭukāmāstadadbhutam

translations.english: To see that wondrous conflict, the celestials, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and the mighty serpents stationed themselves in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
राममुक्तास्तु बाणौघान्राक्षसस्त्वच्छिनद्रणे
रक्षोमुक्तांस्तु रामो वै नैकधा प्राच्छिनच्छरैः
verses.transliteration:
rāmamuktāstu bāṇaughānrākṣasastvacchinadraṇe
rakṣomuktāṁstu rāmo vai naikadhā prācchinaccharaiḥ

translations.english: They were wounded with the discharged by each other and their strength was doubled. And they began to fight in that battlefield one attacking and the other withstanding the attack. And in that conflict the Rākşasa artOWS sundered the shafts discharged by Räma. And likewise Rāma severed into several pieces the arrows shot by the Räksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणौघवितताः सर्वा दिशश्च विदिशस्तथा
संछन्ना वसुधा चैव समन्तान्न प्रकाशते
verses.transliteration:
bāṇaughavitatāḥ sarvā diśaśca vidiśastathā
saṁchannā vasudhā caiva samantānna prakāśate

translations.english: All the quarters were covered with arrows and nothing on earth or in the sky was visible.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्धनुश्चिच्छेद रक्षसः
अष्टाभिरथ नाराचैः सूतं विव्याध राघवः
भित्त्वा शरै रथं रामो रथाश्वान्समपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kruddho mahābāhurdhanuściccheda rakṣasaḥ
aṣṭābhiratha nārācaiḥ sūtaṁ vivyādha rāghavaḥ
bhittvā śarai rathaṁ rāmo rathāśvānsamapātayat

translations.english: Thereupon being excited with ire, Rāghava of long arms sundered his (Raksasa's) bow in conflict and with eight Näräcas pierced the charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
विरथो वसुधां तिष्ठन्मकराक्षो निशाचरः
अतिष्ठद्वसुधां रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना
त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
viratho vasudhāṁ tiṣṭhanmakarākṣo niśācaraḥ
atiṣṭhadvasudhāṁ rakṣaḥ śūlaṁ jagrāha pāṇinā
trāsanaṁ sarvabhūtānāṁ yugāntāgnisamaprabham

translations.english: He then again rose up with a dart in his hand creating terror to all creatures and resembling the Fire of Dissolution in resplendence. It was a terribly huge dart conferred on him by Śiva, shining in the sky in its native brilliance and like to another weapon of destruction.* *This refers to the weapon used by Śiva for destruction-for Siva, according to the Hindu Mythology is the God of destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
विभ्राम्य च महच्छूलं प्रज्वलन्तं निशाचरः
स क्रोधात्प्राहिणोत्तस्मै राघवाय महाहवे
verses.transliteration:
vibhrāmya ca mahacchūlaṁ prajvalantaṁ niśācaraḥ
sa krodhātprāhiṇottasmai rāghavāya mahāhave

translations.english: Beholding which dart even the celestials fly away in fear to different quarters. And taking up that huge flaming dart, the night-ranger, being excited with ire, hurled it at the high-souled Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
तमापतन्तं ज्वलितं खरपुत्रकराच्च्युतम्
बाणैस्तु त्रिभिराकाशे शूलं चिच्छेद राघवः
verses.transliteration:
tamāpatantaṁ jvalitaṁ kharaputrakarāccyutam
bāṇaistu tribhirākāśe śūlaṁ ciccheda rāghavaḥ

translations.english: Rāghava, with four shafts, sundered that dart, in the sky, flaming and hurled at him by the son of Khara.

verses.sanskrit:
सच्छिन्नो नैकधा शूलो दिव्यहाटकमण्डितः
व्यशीर्यत महोक्लेव रामबाणार्दितो भुवि
verses.transliteration:
sacchinno naikadhā śūlo divyahāṭakamaṇḍitaḥ
vyaśīryata mahokleva rāmabāṇārdito bhuvi

translations.english: That flaming dart, feathered in gold, being splintered into several pieces by Rāma's arrows fell down on earth like a huge fire-brand.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छूलं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रामेणाद्भुतकर्मणा
साधु साध्विति भूतानि व्याहरन्ति नभोगताः
verses.transliteration:
tacchūlaṁ nihataṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇādbhutakarmaṇā
sādhu sādhviti bhūtāni vyāharanti nabhogatāḥ

translations.english: Beholding that dart beffled thus by Rāma of unwearied actions all those, stationed in the welkin began to shout, “Well done! Well done!"

verses.sanskrit:
तद्दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूलं मकराक्षो निशाचरः
मुष्टिमुद्यम्य काकुत्स्थं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taddṛṣṭvā nihataṁ śūlaṁ makarākṣo niśācaraḥ
muṣṭimudyamya kākutsthaṁ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt

translations.english: Beholding his dart thus sundered, the nightranger Makarākșa clenching his fist spoke to Kakutstha, saying, "Stay! Stay!"

verses.sanskrit:
स तं दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं वै प्रहस्य रघुनन्दनः
पावकास्त्रं ततो रामः संदधे स्वशरासने
verses.transliteration:
sa taṁ dṛṣṭvā patantaṁ vai prahasya raghunandanaḥ
pāvakāstraṁ tato rāmaḥ saṁdadhe svaśarāsane

translations.english: Seeing him advance thus, the descendant of Raghu, smiling, fixed a fiery arrow on his bow.

verses.sanskrit:
तेनास्त्रेण हतं रक्षः काकुत्स्थेन तदा रणे
संछिन्नहृदयं तत्र पपात च ममार च
verses.transliteration:
tenāstreṇa hataṁ rakṣaḥ kākutsthena tadā raṇe
saṁchinnahṛdayaṁ tatra papāta ca mamāra ca

translations.english: With that arrow the Räksa was slain by Kākutstha in battle. And having his heart pierced he fell down and died.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे मकराक्षस्य पातनम्
लङ्कामेव प्रधावन्त रामबालार्दितास्तदा
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā te rākṣasāḥ sarve makarākṣasya pātanam
laṅkāmeva pradhāvanta rāmabālārditāstadā

translations.english: Beholding Makarākṣa thus slain all the Rāks asas, being afraid of Rama's arrows, proceeded towards Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
दशरथनृपपुत्रबाणवेगै; रजनिचरं निहतं खरात्मजं तम्
ददृशुरथ च देवताः प्रहृष्टा; गिरिमिव वज्रहतं यथा विशीर्णम्
verses.transliteration:
daśarathanṛpaputrabāṇavegai; rajanicaraṁ nihataṁ kharātmajaṁ tam
dadṛśuratha ca devatāḥ prahṛṣṭā; girimiva vajrahataṁ yathā viśīrṇam

translations.english: Seeing that night-ranger, the son of Khara, slain by Rāma's arrows, like to a mountain clept by a thunder-bolt, the celestials were greatly delighted.

verses.sanskrit:
मकराक्षं हतं श्रुत्वा रावणः समितिंजयः
आदिदेशाथ संक्रुद्धो रणायेन्द्रजितं सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
makarākṣaṁ hataṁ śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ samitiṁjayaḥ
ādideśātha saṁkruddho raṇāyendrajitaṁ sutam

translations.english: Being thus angered, and thinking within himself what steps to take, he ordered his son Indrajit to proceed to the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit:
जहि वीर महावीर्यौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
अदृश्यो दृश्यमानो वा सर्वथा त्वं बलाधिकः
verses.transliteration:
jahi vīra mahāvīryau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
adṛśyo dṛśyamāno vā sarvathā tvaṁ balādhikaḥ

translations.english: O hero, gifted with great prowess as you are, do you, hidden (in clouds) or appearing before them, slay the two heroic brothers Rāma and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमप्रतिमकर्माणमिन्द्रं जयसि संयुगे
किं पुनर्मानुषौ दृष्ट्वा न वधिष्यसि संयुगे
verses.transliteration:
tvamapratimakarmāṇamindraṁ jayasi saṁyuge
kiṁ punarmānuṣau dṛṣṭvā na vadhiṣyasi saṁyuge

translations.english: You did defeat in conflict Indra of unequalled prowess. Shall you then neglect to slay men as they are?

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रतिगृह्य पितुर्वचः
यज्ञभूमौ स विधिवत्पावकं जुहुवे न्द्रजित्
verses.transliteration:
tathokto rākṣasendreṇa pratigṛhya piturvacaḥ
yajñabhūmau sa vidhivatpāvakaṁ juhuve ndrajit

translations.english: Being thus addressed by the lord of the Raks asas and obeying his father's command, Indrajit proceeded towards the sacrificial ground to satisfy Fire (with oblations).

verses.sanskrit:
जुह्वतश्चापि तत्राग्निं रक्तोष्णीषधराः स्त्रियः
आजग्मुस्तत्र संभ्रान्ता राक्षस्यो यत्र रावणिः
verses.transliteration:
juhvataścāpi tatrāgniṁ raktoṣṇīṣadharāḥ striyaḥ
ājagmustatra saṁbhrāntā rākṣasyo yatra rāvaṇiḥ

translations.english: There came some she-demons with crimson turbans and waited respectfully where Rävaņa's son was offering oblations to Fire.

verses.sanskrit:
शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ विभीतकाः
लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा
verses.transliteration:
śastrāṇi śarapatrāṇi samidho'tha vibhītakāḥ
lohitāni ca vāsāṁsi sruvaṁ kārṣṇāyasaṁ tathā

translations.english: Arms served for Kasa and Bibhitakas for fuel; and there were red cloths and a ladle made black iron.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वतोऽग्निं समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः समन्ततः
छागस्य सर्वकृष्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः
verses.transliteration:
sarvato'gniṁ samāstīrya śarapatraiḥ samantataḥ
chāgasya sarvakṛṣṇasya galaṁ jagrāha jīvataḥ

translations.english: Spreading fire on all sides with śare leaves and Tomaras, (Indrajit) caught a living goat, all black, by the neck.

verses.sanskrit:
चरुहोमसमिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः
बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं दर्शयन्ति च
verses.transliteration:
caruhomasamiddhasya vidhūmasya mahārciṣaḥ
babhūvustāni liṅgāni vijayaṁ darśayanti ca

translations.english: The fire, with oblations of sara, became greatly blazed and devoid of smoke. There were visible many good omens indicating victory.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तहाटकसंनिभः
हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptahāṭakasaṁnibhaḥ
havistatpratijagrāha pāvakaḥ svayamutthitaḥ

translations.english: The flame of the fire was like to gold, and moving Southwards began to receive offerings of clarified butter.

verses.sanskrit:
हुत्वाग्निं तर्पयित्वाथ देवदानवराक्षसान्
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठमन्तर्धानगतं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
hutvāgniṁ tarpayitvātha devadānavarākṣasān
āruroha rathaśreṣṭhamantardhānagataṁ śubham

translations.english: Thus offering oblations to fire and to celestials, Dänavas and Raksasas, he ascended in excellent car and soon disappeared.

verses.sanskrit:
स वाजिभिश्चतुर्भिस्तु बाणैश्च निशितैर्युतः
आरोपितमहाचापः शुशुभे स्यन्दनोत्तमे
verses.transliteration:
sa vājibhiścaturbhistu bāṇaiśca niśitairyutaḥ
āropitamahācāpaḥ śuśubhe syandanottame

translations.english: It was drawn by four horses and a huge bow, set with sharp arrows, appeared beautiful on that excellent car.

verses.sanskrit:
जाज्वल्यमानो वपुषा तपनीयपरिच्छदः
शरैश्चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रैश्च स रथः समलंकृतः
verses.transliteration:
jājvalyamāno vapuṣā tapanīyaparicchadaḥ
śaraiścandrārdhacandraiśca sa rathaḥ samalaṁkṛtaḥ

translations.english: The chariot was brilliant with its own native resplendence, adorned with gold and painted with the figures of deer and a cresent.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बूनदमहाकम्बुर्दीप्तपावकसंनिभः
बभूवेन्द्रजितः केतुर्वैदूर्यसमलंकृतः
verses.transliteration:
jāmbūnadamahākamburdīptapāvakasaṁnibhaḥ
babhūvendrajitaḥ keturvaidūryasamalaṁkṛtaḥ

translations.english: It was encircled on all sides with golden bracelets, adorned with flags made of viadurja and was like to the flaming fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन चादित्यकल्पेन ब्रह्मास्त्रेण च पालितः
स बभूव दुराधर्षो रावणिः सुमहाबलः
verses.transliteration:
tena cādityakalpena brahmāstreṇa ca pālitaḥ
sa babhūva durādharṣo rāvaṇiḥ sumahābalaḥ

translations.english: Being thus well protected with Brahma weapons resembling the Sun in brilliance, the mighty son of Rāvana became invincible.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिनिर्याय नगरादिन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः
हुत्वाग्निं राक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
so'bhiniryāya nagarādindrajitsamitiṁjayaḥ
hutvāgniṁ rākṣasairmantrairantardhānagato'bravīt

translations.english: Offering oblations to Fire in accordance with demoniac incantations and thus obtaining the power of hiding himself, that hero, ever victorious in battle, issued out of the city and said.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य हत्वाहवे यौ तौ मिथ्या प्रव्रजितौ वने
जयं पित्रे प्रदास्यामि रावणाय रणाधिकम्
verses.transliteration:
adya hatvāhave yau tau mithyā pravrajitau vane
jayaṁ pitre pradāsyāmi rāvaṇāya raṇādhikam

translations.english: Slaying these two brothers in battle, who have uselessly wandered away into the forest, shall I crown my father Răvana with victory.

verses.sanskrit:
कृत्वा निर्वानरामुर्वीं हत्वा रामं सलक्ष्मणम्
करिष्ये परमां प्रीतिमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत
verses.transliteration:
kṛtvā nirvānarāmurvīṁ hatvā rāmaṁ salakṣmaṇam
kariṣye paramāṁ prītimityuktvāntaradhīyata

translations.english: Destroying Rāma and Lakşmaņa, and clearing the monkeys off the earth, shall I satisfy my sire greatly. Saying this, he disappeared from their view.

verses.sanskrit:
आपपाताथ संक्रुद्धो दशग्रीवेण चोदितः
तीक्ष्णकार्मुकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णस्त्विन्द्ररिपू रणे
verses.transliteration:
āpapātātha saṁkruddho daśagrīveṇa coditaḥ
tīkṣṇakārmukanārācaistīkṣṇastvindraripū raṇe

translations.english: Thereupon that fearful foe of the lord of celestials appeared in the battle-field, excited with wrath, armed with bow and sharp Nārācas and commissioned thus by the Ten-necked one.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श महावीर्यौ नागौ त्रिशिरसाविव
सृजन्ताविषुजालानि वीरौ वानरमध्यगौ
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa mahāvīryau nāgau triśirasāviva
sṛjantāviṣujālāni vīrau vānaramadhyagau

translations.english: He beheld there those two heroes discharging flaming arrows and surrounded by the monkeys like to the fearful three-hooded serpent in the midst of other serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
इमौ ताविति संचिन्त्य सज्यं कृत्वा च कार्मुकम्
संततानेषुधाराभिः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्
verses.transliteration:
imau tāviti saṁcintya sajyaṁ kṛtvā ca kārmukam
saṁtatāneṣudhārābhiḥ parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān

translations.english: Thinking "these must be both brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa," and stretching his bow he began showering arrows like to clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वैहायसं प्राप्य सरथो रामलक्ष्मणौ
अचक्षुर्विषये तिष्ठन्विव्याध निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vaihāyasaṁ prāpya saratho rāmalakṣmaṇau
acakṣurviṣaye tiṣṭhanvivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: He was seated in a car in the welkin and hidden from the human gaze and began to assail! Ráma and Lakşmaņa with sharp shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ तस्य शरवेगेन परीतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
धनुषी सशरे कृत्वा दिव्यमस्त्रं प्रचक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
tau tasya śaravegena parītau rāmalakṣmaṇau
dhanuṣī saśare kṛtvā divyamastraṁ pracakratuḥ

translations.english: Being hurt with the arrows, Rāma and Lakş mana, fixing arrows on their bows, began to discharge celestial shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रच्छादयन्तौ गगनं शरजालैर्महाबलौ
तमस्त्रैः सुरसंकाशौ नैव पस्पर्शतुः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
pracchādayantau gaganaṁ śarajālairmahābalau
tamastraiḥ surasaṁkāśau naiva pasparśatuḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Those two highly powerful heroes could not even touch his person with their arrows resembling the Sun albeit they covered the whole welkin therewith.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि धूमान्धकारं च चक्रे प्रच्छादयन्नभः
दिशश्चान्तर्दधे श्रीमान्नीहारतमसावृतः
verses.transliteration:
sa hi dhūmāndhakāraṁ ca cakre pracchādayannabhaḥ
diśaścāntardadhe śrīmānnīhāratamasāvṛtaḥ

translations.english: And clouding the whole sky with smoke that effulgent one, enveloped in frost, his himself from their gaze.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव ज्यातलनिर्घोषो न च नेमिखुरस्वनः
शुश्रुवे चरतस्तस्य न च रूपं प्रकाशते
verses.transliteration:
naiva jyātalanirghoṣo na ca nemikhurasvanaḥ
śuśruve caratastasya na ca rūpaṁ prakāśate

translations.english: There was not audible the twang of kis bow, the sound of the wheels, or the noise of the steeds. Nor was he seen by any.

verses.sanskrit:
घनान्धकारे तिमिरे शरवर्षमिवाद्भुतम्
स ववर्ष महाबाहुर्नाराचशरवृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration:
ghanāndhakāre timire śaravarṣamivādbhutam
sa vavarṣa mahābāhurnārācaśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ

translations.english: In that terrible darkness of clouds that one of mighty arms began to make a downpour of Nāracas and arrows like hail storms.

verses.sanskrit:
स रामं सूर्यसंकाशैः शरैर्दत्तवरो भृशम्
विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु रावणिः
verses.transliteration:
sa rāmaṁ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ śarairdattavaro bhṛśam
vivyādha samare kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāvaṇiḥ

translations.english: In that encounter, Rāvana's son, inflamed with ire, wounded Rāma, with shafts, resembling the Sun and obtained by him as a boon.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ हन्यमानौ नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतौ
हेमपुङ्खान्नरव्याघ्रौ तिग्मान्मुमुचतुः शरान्
verses.transliteration:
tau hanyamānau nārācairdhārābhiriva parvatau
hemapuṅkhānnaravyāghrau tigmānmumucatuḥ śarān

translations.english: Being hurt with Nārāchas, like to mountains wet with rain, those two foremost of men, began to discharge shafts feathered in gold.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरिक्षं समासाद्य रावणिं कङ्कपत्रिणः
निकृत्य पतगा भूमौ पेतुस्ते शोणितोक्षिताः
verses.transliteration:
antarikṣaṁ samāsādya rāvaṇiṁ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ
nikṛtya patagā bhūmau petuste śoṇitokṣitāḥ

translations.english: Reaching the son of Rāvana in the sky and soaked in blood those golden arrows, fell down on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिमात्रं शरौघेण पीड्यमानौ नरोत्तमौ
तानिषून्पततो भल्लैरनेकैर्निचकर्ततुः
verses.transliteration:
atimātraṁ śaraugheṇa pīḍyamānau narottamau
tāniṣūnpatato bhallairanekairnicakartatuḥ

translations.english: Those two best of men, hurt with his arrows, became more effulgent and beffled the shafts discharged by the Räkşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
यतो हि ददृशाते तौ शरान्निपतिताञ्शितान्
ततस्ततो दाशरथी ससृजातेऽस्त्रमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
yato hi dadṛśāte tau śarānnipatitāñśitān
tatastato dāśarathī sasṛjāte'stramuttamam

translations.english: Thereupon Rama and Lakşmaņa began to aim their sharp shafts to the direction whence the arrows came down.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणिस्तु दिशः सर्वा रथेनातिरथः पतन्
विव्याध तौ दाशरथी लघ्वस्त्रो निशितैः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇistu diśaḥ sarvā rathenātirathaḥ patan
vivyādha tau dāśarathī laghvastro niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: And stationed in his chariot that mighty carwarrior disturbed all quarters with his arrows and pierced Dasaratha's sons with sharp shafts won by him.

verses.sanskrit:
तेनातिविद्धौ तौ वीरौ रुक्मपुङ्खैः सुसंहतैः
बभूवतुर्दाशरथी पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ
verses.transliteration:
tenātividdhau tau vīrau rukmapuṅkhaiḥ susaṁhataiḥ
babhūvaturdāśarathī puṣpitāviva kiṁśukau

translations.english: Being greatly hurt with those sharp-pointed and terrible arrows Rāma and Lakşmaņa appeared like blossoming kingsukas.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्य वेद गतिं कश्चिन्न च रूपं धनुः शरान्
न चान्यद्विदितं किंचित्सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसंप्लवे
verses.transliteration:
nāsya veda gatiṁ kaścinna ca rūpaṁ dhanuḥ śarān
na cānyadviditaṁ kiṁcitsūryasyevābhrasaṁplave

translations.english: Like to the sun hidden in clouds they could see neither his countenance and motion, nor his bow and arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन विद्धाश्च हरयो निहताश्च गतासवः
बभूवुः शतशस्तत्र पतिता धरणीतले
verses.transliteration:
tena viddhāśca harayo nihatāśca gatāsavaḥ
babhūvuḥ śataśastatra patitā dharaṇītale

translations.english: Being wounded with those arrows hundreds of monkeys died and fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो भ्रातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं प्रयोक्ष्यामि वधार्थं सर्वरक्षसाम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇastu susaṁkruddho bhrātaraṁ vākyamabravīt
brāhmamastraṁ prayokṣyāmi vadhārthaṁ sarvarakṣasām

translations.english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa, being excited with wrath, spoke to his brother, saying-"To slay all the Rākṣasas shall I discharge today Brahma weapon.'

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच ततो रामो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्
नैकस्य हेतो रक्षांसि पृथिव्यां हन्तुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca tato rāmo lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣaṇam
naikasya heto rakṣāṁsi pṛthivyāṁ hantumarhasi

translations.english: Thereupon Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, gifted with auspicious. marks, saying.-"It does not behove you to clear all the Rākşasas off the earth for the folly of one individual.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्यैव तु वधे यत्नं करिष्यावो महाबल
आदेक्ष्यावो महावेगानस्त्रानाशीविषोपमान्
verses.transliteration:
asyaiva tu vadhe yatnaṁ kariṣyāvo mahābala
ādekṣyāvo mahāvegānastrānāśīviṣopamān

translations.english: You should not slay him, who has retired from battle, has hidden himself, has sought your shelter, has stood before you with joined palms, has fled away or who is bewildered. O you of mighty-arms, let us try to slay him (Indrajit). And to accomplish it I shall use the weapons gifted with great impetuosity and resembling the serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
तमेनं मायिनं क्षुद्रमन्तर्हितरथं बलात्
राक्षसं निहनिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः
verses.transliteration:
tamenaṁ māyinaṁ kṣudramantarhitarathaṁ balāt
rākṣasaṁ nihaniṣyanti dṛṣṭvā vānarayūthapāḥ

translations.english: He is hidden from the public gaze so we must slay him, had he been fighting openly the leaders of the monkey hosts could have slain that Räks asas.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्येष भूमिं विशते दिवं वा; रसातलं वापि नभस्तलं वा
एवं निगूढोऽपि ममास्त्रदग्धः; पतिष्यते भूमितले गतासुः
verses.transliteration:
yadyeṣa bhūmiṁ viśate divaṁ vā; rasātalaṁ vāpi nabhastalaṁ vā
evaṁ nigūḍho'pi mamāstradagdhaḥ; patiṣyate bhūmitale gatāsuḥ

translations.english: Truly he shall be burnt to death with my shafts and fall down on the earth albeit he entered the regions under the earth of the abode of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा; रघुप्रवीरः प्लवगर्षभैर्वृतः
वधाय रौद्रस्य नृशंसकर्मण;स्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktvā vacanaṁ mahātmā; raghupravīraḥ plavagarṣabhairvṛtaḥ
vadhāya raudrasya nṛśaṁsakarmaṇa;stadā mahātmā tvaritaṁ nirīkṣate

translations.english: Having said these words pregnant with a high significance, the high-souled and heroic descendant of Raghu, being surrounded by monkeys, began to concert various plans for the destruction of that terrible Raksasa of wicked deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञाय तु मनस्तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः
संनिवृत्याहवात्तस्मात्प्रविवेश पुरं ततः
verses.transliteration:
vijñāya tu manastasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
saṁnivṛtyāhavāttasmātpraviveśa puraṁ tataḥ

translations.english: Having read the intention of that high-souled Raghava, he retired from the battle-field and entered into the city of Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽनुस्मृत्य वधं तेषां राक्षसानां तरस्विनाम्
क्रोधताम्रेक्षणः शूरो निर्जगाम महाद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
so'nusmṛtya vadhaṁ teṣāṁ rākṣasānāṁ tarasvinām
krodhatāmrekṣaṇaḥ śūro nirjagāma mahādyutiḥ

translations.english: And remembering the destruction of many a। quick-paced Raksasa, his eyes were rendered coppery with ire; and that hero, the son of Ravana, issued out of the city again.

verses.sanskrit:
स पश्चिमेन द्वारेण निर्ययौ राक्षसैर्वृतः
इन्द्रजित्तु महावीर्यः पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः
verses.transliteration:
sa paścimena dvāreṇa niryayau rākṣasairvṛtaḥ
indrajittu mahāvīryaḥ paulastyo devakaṇṭakaḥ

translations.english: That highly powerful, Indrajit, a descendant of Pulasta and an enemy of the celestials, issued out, encircled by the Rākşasas, by the western gate.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
रणायाभ्युद्यतौ वीरौ मायां प्रादुष्करोत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
indrajittu tato dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
raṇāyābhyudyatau vīrau māyāṁ prāduṣkarottadā

translations.english: Then beholding the heroic brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa prepared for fight, Indrajit spread illusions.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्तु रथे स्थाप्य सीतां मायामयीं तदा
बलेन महतावृत्य तस्या वधमरोचयत्
verses.transliteration:
indrajittu rathe sthāpya sītāṁ māyāmayīṁ tadā
balena mahatāvṛtya tasyā vadhamarocayat

translations.english: Placing an illusory figure of Sītā on the car, encircled by a huge army he began to make arrangements for her destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
मोहनार्थं तु सर्वेषां बुद्धिं कृत्वा सुदुर्मतिः
हन्तुं सीतां व्यवसितो वानराभिमुखो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
mohanārthaṁ tu sarveṣāṁ buddhiṁ kṛtvā sudurmatiḥ
hantuṁ sītāṁ vyavasito vānarābhimukho yayau

translations.english: Desiring to charm all with his illusions, that one of wicked intent, preparing himself to slay Sītā, proceeded towards the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वभिनिर्यान्तं नगर्याः काननौकसः
उत्पेतुरभिसंक्रुद्धाः शिलाहस्ता युयुत्सवः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tvabhiniryāntaṁ nagaryāḥ kānanaukasaḥ
utpeturabhisaṁkruddhāḥ śilāhastā yuyutsavaḥ

translations.english: Beholding him thus proceed, the monkeys, inflamed with ire, desirous of fighting and with crags in their hands, moved on.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमान्पुरतस्तेषां जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः
प्रगृह्य सुमहच्छृङ्गं पर्वतस्य दुरासदम्
verses.transliteration:
hanūmānpuratasteṣāṁ jagāma kapikuñjaraḥ
pragṛhya sumahacchṛṅgaṁ parvatasya durāsadam

translations.english: And preceded them all, Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, with a huge mountaintop in his hand.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श हतानन्दां सीतामिन्द्रजितो रथे
एकवेणीधरां दीनामुपवासकृशाननाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa hatānandāṁ sītāmindrajito rathe
ekaveṇīdharāṁ dīnāmupavāsakṛśānanām

translations.english: He beheld there, on Indrajit's car, Sita, deprived of all joy, poorly, greatly reduced with fasts and wearing a single braid.

verses.sanskrit:
परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजां राघवप्रियाम्
रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैः सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम्
verses.transliteration:
parikliṣṭaikavasanāmamṛjāṁ rāghavapriyām
rajomalābhyāmāliptaiḥ sarvagātrairvarastriyam

translations.english: Rāghava's beloved spouse wore a piece of soiled cloth, and though highly beautiful, the grace of her person was greatly spoiled with dirt.

verses.sanskrit:
तां निरीक्ष्य मुहूर्तं तु मैथिलीमध्यवस्य च
बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखो हनूमान्व्यथितोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ nirīkṣya muhūrtaṁ tu maithilīmadhyavasya ca
bāṣpaparyākulamukho hanūmānvyathito'bhavat

translations.english: That daughter of Janaka, was not seen by him for a long time. And beholding her and deciding instantly that she is the daughter of Mithilā, (he became greatly sorry).

verses.sanskrit:
किं समर्थितमस्येति चिन्तयन्स महाकपिः
सह तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावत रावणिम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ samarthitamasyeti cintayansa mahākapiḥ
saha tairvānaraśreṣṭhairabhyadhāvata rāvaṇim

translations.english: Seeing her on the car, innocent, poor, deprived of joy and brought under the influence of the son of the lord Rākşasas that great monkey thought within himself— 'What must be the intention of Indrajit?' and accompanied by heroic monkeys advanced towards the son of Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वानरबलं दृष्ट्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः
कृत्वा विशोकं निस्त्रिंशं मूर्ध्नि सीतां परामृशत्
verses.transliteration:
tadvānarabalaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
kṛtvā viśokaṁ nistriṁśaṁ mūrdhni sītāṁ parāmṛśat

translations.english: Beholding that monkey host, Ravana's son became beside himself with ire and unsheathing his weapon Nistrinsha, caught her by the hair.

verses.sanskrit:
तं स्त्रियं पश्यतां तेषां ताडयामास रावणिः
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति मायया योजितां रथे
verses.transliteration:
taṁ striyaṁ paśyatāṁ teṣāṁ tāḍayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ
krośantīṁ rāma rāmeti māyayā yojitāṁ rathe

translations.english: The Räkşasa addressed himself to strike her in the presence of all those monkeys and that illusory figure of Sītā began to bewail saying, “O Rāma! O Rāma!”

verses.sanskrit:
गृहीतमूर्धजां दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्दैन्यमागतः
दुःखजं वारिनेत्राभ्यामुत्सृजन्मारुतात्मजः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं क्रोधाद्रक्षोऽधिपात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
gṛhītamūrdhajāṁ dṛṣṭvā hanūmāndainyamāgataḥ
duḥkhajaṁ vārinetrābhyāmutsṛjanmārutātmajaḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ krodhādrakṣo'dhipātmajam

translations.english: Seeing her thus caught by the head, Hanumān, the son of Maruta, greatly sorry, began to shed tears.

verses.sanskrit:
दुरात्मन्नात्मनाशाय केशपक्षे परामृशः
ब्रह्मर्षीणां कुले जातो राक्षसीं योनिमाश्रितः
धिक्त्वां पापसमाचारं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी
verses.transliteration:
durātmannātmanāśāya keśapakṣe parāmṛśaḥ
brahmarṣīṇāṁ kule jāto rākṣasīṁ yonimāśritaḥ
dhiktvāṁ pāpasamācāraṁ yasya te matirīdṛśī

translations.english: It is for your destruction, O Vicious-souled one! that you have touched her hair. Being descended from that great Brahmă ascetic you are born as a Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
नृशंसानार्य दुर्वृत्त क्षुद्र पापपराक्रम
अनार्यस्येदृशं कर्म घृणा ते नास्ति निर्घृण
verses.transliteration:
nṛśaṁsānārya durvṛtta kṣudra pāpaparākrama
anāryasyedṛśaṁ karma ghṛṇā te nāsti nirghṛṇa

translations.english: O! cursed are you, since you have cherished such a desire and engaged in such a vicious deed. O vile! O wicked! O! cruel and dishonourable wight! O you having vice for your prowess!

verses.sanskrit:
च्युता गृहाच्च राज्याच्च रामहस्ताच्च मैथिली
किं तवैषापराद्धा हि यदेनां हन्तुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
cyutā gṛhācca rājyācca rāmahastācca maithilī
kiṁ tavaiṣāparāddhā hi yadenāṁ hantumicchasi

translations.english: O shameless! Are you not ashamed of perpetrating such an inhuman deed. What has Maithili done by you, O cruel one! that you are ready to slay her—She has been banished from her home, territory and has been separated from her lord.

verses.sanskrit:
सीतां च हत्वा न चिरं जीविष्यसि कथंचन
वधार्हकर्मणानेन मम हस्तगतो ह्यसि
verses.transliteration:
sītāṁ ca hatvā na ciraṁ jīviṣyasi kathaṁcana
vadhārhakarmaṇānena mama hastagato hyasi

translations.english: O you worthy of being slain, destroying Sītā, you shall not live long as you have been brought under me.

verses.sanskrit:
ये च स्त्रीघातिनां लोका लोकवध्यैश्च कुत्सिताः
इह जीवितमुत्सृज्य प्रेत्य तान्प्रतिलप्स्यसे
verses.transliteration:
ye ca strīghātināṁ lokā lokavadhyaiśca kutsitāḥ
iha jīvitamutsṛjya pretya tānpratilapsyase

translations.english: You shall after the death reach the place which is occupied by those who murder women, a place which is avoided even by those who commit every sort of crime punishable by law.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणो हनुमान्सायुधैर्हरिभिर्वृतः
अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇo hanumānsāyudhairharibhirvṛtaḥ
abhyadhāvata saṁkruddho rākṣasendrasutaṁ prati

translations.english: Saying this Hanuman, accompanied by monkeys armed with weapons, and excited with ire, proceeded towards the son of the lord or Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
आपतन्तं महावीर्यं तदनीकं वनौकसाम्
रक्षसां भीमवेगानामनीकेन न्यवारयत्
verses.transliteration:
āpatantaṁ mahāvīryaṁ tadanīkaṁ vanaukasām
rakṣasāṁ bhīmavegānāmanīkena nyavārayat

translations.english: Beholding the highly powerful monkeys advance thus the Rākṣasas, inflamed with wrath, obstructed them.

verses.sanskrit:
स तां बाणसहस्रेण विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्
हरिश्रेष्ठं हनूमन्तमिन्द्रजित्प्रत्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
sa tāṁ bāṇasahasreṇa vikṣobhya harivāhinīm
hariśreṣṭhaṁ hanūmantamindrajitpratyuvāca ha

translations.english: Assailing the monkey-hosts with thousands of arrows, Indrajit spoke to that foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां हत्वा ततो रामं लक्ष्मणं त्वां च वानर
सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामि तं चानार्यं विभीषणम्
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ hatvā tato rāmaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ tvāṁ ca vānara
sugrīvaṁ ca vadhiṣyāmi taṁ cānāryaṁ vibhīṣaṇam

translations.english: Today I shall slay before you all Vaidehī, for whom you, Sugriva and Rama have come. Slaying her, O monkey, I shall afterwards kill you, Rama, Laksmana and Sugriva and the dishonourable Vibhişaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
न हन्तव्याः स्त्रियश्चेति यद्ब्रवीषि प्लवंगम
पीडा करममित्राणां यत्स्यात्कर्तव्यमेत तत्
verses.transliteration:
na hantavyāḥ striyaśceti yadbravīṣi plavaṁgama
pīḍā karamamitrāṇāṁ yatsyātkartavyameta tat

translations.english: O monkey, about not destroying women, of which you were speaking (I might say) that we must always do what pains our enemies."* *There is one śloka intervening according to some texts, but it has been omitted by many. The reasons for this omission are best known to them. The purport is:-"Why did Rama slay Taraka before? And I shall therefore slay his spouse the daughter of king Janaka.” Hear in Indrajit attempts to justify himself and wants to prove that Räma is equally blameable for this.)

verses.sanskrit:
तमेवमुक्त्वा रुदतीं सीतां मायामयीं ततः
शितधारेण खड्गेन निजघानेन्द्रजित्स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tamevamuktvā rudatīṁ sītāṁ māyāmayīṁ tataḥ
śitadhāreṇa khaḍgena nijaghānendrajitsvayam

translations.english: Saying this, Indrajit with a sharp sword, himself killed the illusory Sitā thus bewailing.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञोपवीतमार्गेण छिन्ना तेन तपस्विनी
सा पृथिव्यां पृथुश्रोणी पपात प्रियदर्शना
verses.transliteration:
yajñopavītamārgeṇa chinnā tena tapasvinī
sā pṛthivyāṁ pṛthuśroṇī papāta priyadarśanā

translations.english: Being sundered by him obliquely in a way in which a sacred thread lies on one's own person, the innocent (Sitā) having beautiful countenance fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तामिन्द्रजित्स्त्रियं हत्वा हनूमन्तमुवाच ह
मया रामस्य पश्येमां कोपेन च निषूदिताम्
verses.transliteration:
tāmindrajitstriyaṁ hatvā hanūmantamuvāca ha
mayā rāmasya paśyemāṁ kopena ca niṣūditām

translations.english: Slaying her Indrajit spoke to Hanumān,“Behold I have slain (before you) with my sword Rāma's beloved. And Vaidehi being thus slain, all your labours have been rendered useless."

verses.sanskrit:
ततः खड्गेन महता हत्वा तामिन्द्रजित्स्वयम्
हृष्टः स रथमास्थाय विननाद महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ khaḍgena mahatā hatvā tāmindrajitsvayam
hṛṣṭaḥ sa rathamāsthāya vinanāda mahāsvanam

translations.english: a Destroying her with his own hand by means of a huge sword, Indrajit, greatly pleased ascended his car and began to emit dreadful roars.

verses.sanskrit:
वानराः शुश्रुवुः शब्दमदूरे प्रत्यवस्थिताः
व्यादितास्यस्य नदतस्तद्दुर्गं संश्रितस्य तु
verses.transliteration:
vānarāḥ śuśruvuḥ śabdamadūre pratyavasthitāḥ
vyāditāsyasya nadatastaddurgaṁ saṁśritasya tu

translations.english: The monkeys stationed near heard that terrible roar and saw him enter the castel.* *The castle built by Indrajit by means of his illusory power in the air.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तु सीतां विनिहत्य दुर्मतिः; प्रहृष्टचेताः स बभूव रावणिः
तं हृष्टरूपं समुदीक्ष्य वानरा; विषण्णरूपाः समभिप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
tathā tu sītāṁ vinihatya durmatiḥ; prahṛṣṭacetāḥ sa babhūva rāvaṇiḥ
taṁ hṛṣṭarūpaṁ samudīkṣya vānarā; viṣaṇṇarūpāḥ samabhipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: And slaying Sītā that wicked-minded son of Rāvana became greatly pleased. And beholding him thus delighted the monkeys being greatly sorry fled away.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तं भीमनिर्ह्रादं शक्राशनिसमस्वनम्
वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वा दुद्रुवुर्वानरर्षभाः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā taṁ bhīmanirhrādaṁ śakrāśanisamasvanam
vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvā dudruvurvānararṣabhāḥ

translations.english: Hearing that dreadful uproar resembling the sound of Indra's thunder-bolt, the monkeys, casting their looks on all sides fled away.

verses.sanskrit:
तानुवाच ततः सर्वान्हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
विषण्णवदनान्दीनांस्त्रस्तान्विद्रवतः पृथक्
verses.transliteration:
tānuvāca tataḥ sarvānhanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
viṣaṇṇavadanāndīnāṁstrastānvidravataḥ pṛthak

translations.english: Thereupon Hanumān, the son of Maruta, spoke to them, poorly, terrified and of a sorrowful countenance, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्माद्विषण्णवदना विद्रवध्वं प्लवंगमाः
त्यक्तयुद्धसमुत्साहाः शूरत्वं क्व नु वो गतम्
verses.transliteration:
kasmādviṣaṇṇavadanā vidravadhvaṁ plavaṁgamāḥ
tyaktayuddhasamutsāhāḥ śūratvaṁ kva nu vo gatam

translations.english: O monkeys, why do you look so melancholy and why are you flying away? Why have you renounced your earnest desire for fight? And where is your heroism gone?

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजध्वं मामग्रतो यान्तमाहवे
शूरैरभिजनोपेतैरयुक्तं हि निवर्तितुम्
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭhato'nuvrajadhvaṁ māmagrato yāntamāhave
śūrairabhijanopetairayuktaṁ hi nivartitum

translations.english: Do you remain behind me, I shall go first in the battle. It is improper for heroes of noble descent to escape from battle field.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ताः सुसंक्रुद्धा वायुपुत्रेण धीमता
शैलशृङ्गान्द्रुमांश्चैव जगृहुर्हृष्टमानसाः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktāḥ susaṁkruddhā vāyuputreṇa dhīmatā
śailaśṛṅgāndrumāṁścaiva jagṛhurhṛṣṭamānasāḥ

translations.english: Being thus addressed by that highly intelligent son of the Wind-god, they were greatly excited with wrath and being pleased took up trees and। crags in their hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिपेतुश्च गर्जन्तो राक्षसान्वानरर्षभाः
परिवार्य हनूमन्तमन्वयुश्च महाहवे
verses.transliteration:
abhipetuśca garjanto rākṣasānvānararṣabhāḥ
parivārya hanūmantamanvayuśca mahāhave

translations.english: Roaring thus the leading monkeys advanced towards the Rākşasas and stood encircling Hanumān in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit:
स तैर्वानरमुख्यैस्तु हनूमान्सर्वतो वृतः
हुताशन इवार्चिष्मानदहच्छत्रुवाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tairvānaramukhyaistu hanūmānsarvato vṛtaḥ
hutāśana ivārciṣmānadahacchatruvāhinīm

translations.english: Being surrounded on all sides by leading monkeys, Hanuman began to burn down enemy's host like to fire spreading its flames.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसानां कदनं चकार सुमहाकपिः
वृतो वानरसैन्येन कालान्तकयमोपमः
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasānāṁ kadanaṁ cakāra sumahākapiḥ
vṛto vānarasainyena kālāntakayamopamaḥ

translations.english: Being encircled by monkey-hosts that mighty monkey resembling death himself began to grind the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु शोकेन चाविष्टः क्रोधेन च महाकपिः
हनूमान्रावणि रथे महतीं पातयच्छिलाम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu śokena cāviṣṭaḥ krodhena ca mahākapiḥ
hanūmānrāvaṇi rathe mahatīṁ pātayacchilām

translations.english: Being overwhelmed with grief and wrought up with ire, that monkey Hanumān, threw a huge crag on the car of that son of Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
तामापतन्तीं दृष्ट्वैव रथः सारथिना तदा
विधेयाश्व समायुक्तः सुदूरमपवाहितः
verses.transliteration:
tāmāpatantīṁ dṛṣṭvaiva rathaḥ sārathinā tadā
vidheyāśva samāyuktaḥ sudūramapavāhitaḥ

translations.english: Beholding that crag about to fall down on the car, the charioteer moved his horses and it was speedily brought at some distance.

verses.sanskrit:
तमिन्द्रजितमप्राप्य रथथं सहसारथिम्
विवेश धरणीं भित्त्वा सा शिलाव्यर्थमुद्यता
verses.transliteration:
tamindrajitamaprāpya rathathaṁ sahasārathim
viveśa dharaṇīṁ bhittvā sā śilāvyarthamudyatā

translations.english: And not reaching Indrajit stationed on the car and the charioteer, that crag, uselessly hurled, fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
पतितायां शिलायां तु रक्षसां व्यथिता चमूः
तमभ्यधावञ्शतशो नदन्तः काननौकसः
verses.transliteration:
patitāyāṁ śilāyāṁ tu rakṣasāṁ vyathitā camūḥ
tamabhyadhāvañśataśo nadantaḥ kānanaukasaḥ

translations.english: As the crag falling down the army of the Rakşasas were violently crushed.

verses.sanskrit:
ते द्रुमांश्च महाकाया गिरिशृङ्गाणि चोद्यताः
चिक्षिपुर्द्विषतां मध्ये वानरा भीमविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
te drumāṁśca mahākāyā giriśṛṅgāṇi codyatāḥ
cikṣipurdviṣatāṁ madhye vānarā bhīmavikramāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon hundreds of huge-bodied monkeys, emitting cries and taking up crags and trees proceeded towards him (Indrajit) and hurled them at him.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरैर्तैर्महावीर्यैर्घोररूपा निशाचराः
वीर्यादभिहता वृक्षैर्व्यवेष्टन्त रणक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
vānarairtairmahāvīryairghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
vīryādabhihatā vṛkṣairvyaveṣṭanta raṇakṣitau

translations.english: The grim-visaged night-rangers were assailed with trees in that field by the terrible monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वसैन्यमभिवीक्ष्याथ वानरार्दितमिन्द्रजित्
प्रगृहीतायुधः क्रुद्धः परानभिमुखो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
svasainyamabhivīkṣyātha vānarārditamindrajit
pragṛhītāyudhaḥ kruddhaḥ parānabhimukho yayau

translations.english: Beholding his army thus distressed by the monkeys, Indrajit, excited with wrath, and taking up his dart, proceeded towards the enemies, and encircled by his soldiers showered terrible shafts upon them. And that one of dreadful prowess slew many a leading monkey by means of darts, Asanis, swords, pattisas and clubs.

verses.sanskrit:
सस्कन्धविटपैः सालैः शिलाभिश्च महाबलैः
हनूमान्कदनं चक्रे रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्
verses.transliteration:
saskandhaviṭapaiḥ sālaiḥ śilābhiśca mahābalaiḥ
hanūmānkadanaṁ cakre rakṣasāṁ bhīmakarmaṇām

translations.english: The highly powerful monkeys destroyed his retinue, with crags, stones and trees having strong trunks. And Hanumān thus crushed many a Rākşasa of terrible deeds.

verses.sanskrit:
स निवार्य परानीकमब्रवीत्तान्वनौकसः
हनूमान्संनिवर्तध्वं न नः साध्यमिदं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
sa nivārya parānīkamabravīttānvanaukasaḥ
hanūmānsaṁnivartadhvaṁ na naḥ sādhyamidaṁ balam

translations.english: Obstructing the Rākṣasas (for some time) Hanumān spoke to monkeys, saying, “Stay, we should not fight now.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्विचेष्टन्तो राम प्रियचिकीर्षवः
यन्निमित्तं हि युध्यामो हता सा जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
tyaktvā prāṇānviceṣṭanto rāma priyacikīrṣavaḥ
yannimittaṁ hi yudhyāmo hatā sā janakātmajā

translations.english: That daughter of Janaka has been slain, for whom we have engaged in fight, renouncing all hope of life and desiring to accomplish Rāma's satisfaction.

verses.sanskrit:
इममर्थं हि विज्ञाप्य रामं सुग्रीवमेव च
तौ यत्प्रतिविधास्येते तत्करिष्यामहे वयम्
verses.transliteration:
imamarthaṁ hi vijñāpya rāmaṁ sugrīvameva ca
tau yatpratividhāsyete tatkariṣyāmahe vayam

translations.english: Let us now go and inform Rāma and Sugrīva of it. And we shall do as we shall be commanded by them.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा वानरश्रेष्ठो वारयन्सर्ववानरान्
शनैः शनैरसंत्रस्तः सबलः स न्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā vānaraśreṣṭho vārayansarvavānarān
śanaiḥ śanairasaṁtrastaḥ sabalaḥ sa nyavartata

translations.english: Saying this and desisting all the monkeys from encounter that foremost of monkeys proceeded undaunted and heroically.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु प्रेक्ष्य हनूमन्तं व्रजन्तं यत्र राघवः
निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठाय पावकं जुहुवे न्द्रजित्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu prekṣya hanūmantaṁ vrajantaṁ yatra rāghavaḥ
nikumbhilāmadhiṣṭhāya pāvakaṁ juhuve ndrajit

translations.english: Beholding Hanumăn proceed thus where Rāghava was that wicked-minded one (Indrajit) with a view to offer oblations to fire entered the sacrificial altar Nikumbhila.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽर्चिः पिनद्धो ददृशे होमशोणिततर्पितः
संध्यागत इवादित्यः स तीव्राग्निः समुत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
so'rciḥ pinaddho dadṛśe homaśoṇitatarpitaḥ
saṁdhyāgata ivādityaḥ sa tīvrāgniḥ samutthitaḥ

translations.english: Reaching there Indrajit lighted up fire and began to pour oblations therein. And the fire blazed up receiving oblations of blood, and being satisfied assumed the appearance of the setting sun.

verses.sanskrit:
अथेन्द्रजिद्राक्षसभूतये तु; जुहाव हव्यं विधिना विधानवत्
दृष्ट्वा व्यतिष्ठन्त च राक्षसास्ते; महासमूहेषु नयानयज्ञाः
verses.transliteration:
athendrajidrākṣasabhūtaye tu; juhāva havyaṁ vidhinā vidhānavat
dṛṣṭvā vyatiṣṭhanta ca rākṣasāste; mahāsamūheṣu nayānayajñāḥ

translations.english: Indrajit conversant with all ceremonials, offered oblations in due form for the welfare of the Rākşasas. And they all stood there watching the result and desirous of ascertaining the success of the battle.* *This Sloka has been left off in some editions.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवश्चापि विपुलं तं राक्षसवनौकसाम्
श्रुत्वा संग्रामनिर्घोषं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaścāpi vipulaṁ taṁ rākṣasavanaukasām
śrutvā saṁgrāmanirghoṣaṁ jāmbavantamuvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing the terrible war-cry of the Rākşasas and monkeys Rāghava spoke to Jämbavän, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सौम्य नूनं हनुमता कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्
श्रूयते हि यथा भीमः सुमहानायुधस्वनः
verses.transliteration:
saumya nūnaṁ hanumatā kṛtaṁ karma suduṣkaram
śrūyate hi yathā bhīmaḥ sumahānāyudhasvanaḥ

translations.english: O gentle one, forsooth has Hanumān performed some mighty act for I hear the dreadful sound of the weapons.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्गच्छ कुरु साहाय्यं स्वबलेनाभिसंवृतः
क्षिप्रमृष्कपते तस्य कपिश्रेष्ठस्य युध्यतः
verses.transliteration:
tadgaccha kuru sāhāyyaṁ svabalenābhisaṁvṛtaḥ
kṣipramṛṣkapate tasya kapiśreṣṭhasya yudhyataḥ

translations.english: Do you therefore proceed speedily, O lord of bears, with all your soldiers to assist that foremost of monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षराजस्तथेत्युक्त्वा स्वेनानीकेन संवृतः
आगच्छत्पश्चिमद्वारं हनूमान्यत्र वानरः
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣarājastathetyuktvā svenānīkena saṁvṛtaḥ
āgacchatpaścimadvāraṁ hanūmānyatra vānaraḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, saying, 'So be it,' that king of bears, surrounded by his forces, approached the Western gate, where the monkey, Hanumān, was stationed.

verses.sanskrit:
अथायान्तं हनूमन्तं ददर्शर्क्षपतिः पथि
वानरैः कृतसंग्रामैः श्वसद्भिरभिसंवृतम्
verses.transliteration:
athāyāntaṁ hanūmantaṁ dadarśarkṣapatiḥ pathi
vānaraiḥ kṛtasaṁgrāmaiḥ śvasadbhirabhisaṁvṛtam

translations.english: Then the lord of bears saw Hanumān approach, surrounded by monkeys sighing hard, who had faught the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा पथि हनूमांश्च तदृष्कबलमुद्यतम्
नीलमेघनिभं भीमं संनिवार्य न्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā pathi hanūmāṁśca tadṛṣkabalamudyatam
nīlameghanibhaṁ bhīmaṁ saṁnivārya nyavartata

translations.english: Seeing on the way that host of bears dreadful and resembling dark clouds, on the march, Hanumān made them desist.

verses.sanskrit:
स तेन हरिसैन्येन संनिकर्षं महायशाः
शीघ्रमागम्य रामाय दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tena harisainyena saṁnikarṣaṁ mahāyaśāḥ
śīghramāgamya rāmāya duḥkhito vākyamabravīt

translations.english: That illustrious one along with that force, speedily presented himself (before Rāma), and with a heavy heart addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
समरे युध्यमानानामस्माकं प्रेक्षतां च सः
जघान रुदतीं सीतामिन्द्रजिद्रावणात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
samare yudhyamānānāmasmākaṁ prekṣatāṁ ca saḥ
jaghāna rudatīṁ sītāmindrajidrāvaṇātmajaḥ

translations.english: As we were fighting the field, Ravana's son, Indrajit in our very sight slew Sītā, crying (in distress).

verses.sanskrit:
उद्भ्रान्तचित्तस्तां दृष्ट्वा विषण्णोऽहमरिंदम
तदहं भवतो वृत्तं विज्ञापयितुमागतः
verses.transliteration:
udbhrāntacittastāṁ dṛṣṭvā viṣaṇṇo'hamariṁdama
tadahaṁ bhavato vṛttaṁ vijñāpayitumāgataḥ

translations.english: O subduer of enemies, seeing her (in this plight) I, with my senses bewildered, have been overwhelmed with grief. Therefore I have come to you to inform you of what has befallen.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोकमूर्छितः
निपपात तदा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāghavaḥ śokamūrchitaḥ
nipapāta tadā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words of his, Raghava, overwhelmed with grief, dropped down to the earth, like a tree whose roots have been severed.

verses.sanskrit:
तं भूमौ देवसंकाशं पतितं दृश्य राघवम्
अभिपेतुः समुत्पत्य सर्वतः कपिसत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ bhūmau devasaṁkāśaṁ patitaṁ dṛśya rāghavam
abhipetuḥ samutpatya sarvataḥ kapisattamāḥ

translations.english: Seeing the god-like Råghava down on the earth, the foremost monkeys from all sides rushed forward and came to where (he was).

verses.sanskrit:
असिञ्चन्सलिलैश्चैनं पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिभिः
प्रदहन्तमसह्यं च सहसाग्निमिवोत्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
asiñcansalilaiścainaṁ padmotpalasugandhibhiḥ
pradahantamasahyaṁ ca sahasāgnimivotthitam

translations.english: With water scented with lotuses, they fell to sprinkling that one resembling a furious fire that has suddenly arisen. 1. Padmotpalasugadhibhiḥ-water scented with padmas-lotuses proper, and utpalas-blue lotuses (Nymphea cerulea). 2. 'Rama,' remarks the commentator, 'was a fire lighted by his grief for Sītā.'

verses.sanskrit:
शुभे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठन्तं त्वामार्यविजितेन्द्रियम्
अनर्थेभ्यो न शक्नोति त्रातुं धर्मो निरर्थकः
verses.transliteration:
śubhe vartmani tiṣṭhantaṁ tvāmāryavijitendriyam
anarthebhyo na śaknoti trātuṁ dharmo nirarthakaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Laksmana, over-come with sorrow, embracing Rāma, spoke to his words fraught with reason and import, “Profitless* virtue is incapable, O noble one, of delivering from calamities you, who have subdued your senses, and who ever abidst in the good path. * 'Profitless, although apparently an epither of virtue, is really the predicate of the sentence. 'Virtue, incapable of delivering you is profitless.

verses.sanskrit:
भूतानां स्थावराणां च जङ्गमानां च दर्शनम्
यथास्ति न तथा धर्मस्तेन नास्तीति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
bhūtānāṁ sthāvarāṇāṁ ca jaṅgamānāṁ ca darśanam
yathāsti na tathā dharmastena nāstīti me matiḥ

translations.english: Beings and the mobile as well as the immobile cannot have that direct perception of virtue which they have of happiness. Therefore, I ween, virtue is a non-entity.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव स्थावरं व्यक्तं जङ्गमं च तथाविधम्
नायमर्थस्तथा युक्तस्त्वद्विधो न विपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
yathaiva sthāvaraṁ vyaktaṁ jaṅgamaṁ ca tathāvidham
nāyamarthastathā yuktastvadvidho na vipadyate

translations.english: Inasmuch as the immobile (albeit devoid of any regard for virtue) are nevertheless happy and as the mobile also are so, this virtue cannot lead to happiness. (If it were so), one like you would have not been placed in peril.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यधर्मो भवेद्भूतो रावणो नरकं व्रजेत्
भवांश्च धर्मसंयुक्तो नैवं व्यसनमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
yadyadharmo bhavedbhūto rāvaṇo narakaṁ vrajet
bhavāṁśca dharmasaṁyukto naivaṁ vyasanamāpnuyāt

translations.english: If unrighteousness would bring unhappiness on creatures, Ravana should hence to hell, and you possessed of virtue, should not come by misfortune.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य च व्यसनाभावाद्व्यसनं च गते त्वयि
धर्मेणोपलभेद्धर्ममधर्मं चाप्यधर्मतः
verses.transliteration:
tasya ca vyasanābhāvādvyasanaṁ ca gate tvayi
dharmeṇopalabheddharmamadharmaṁ cāpyadharmataḥ

translations.english: Seeing that he is free from danger, and you are in itrighteousness and its opposite are found to have tendencles the very reverse of those assigned to them respectively (by the Vedas).

verses.sanskrit:
यदि धर्मेण युज्येरन्नाधर्मरुचयो जनाः
धर्मेण चरतां धर्मस्तथा चैषां फलं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
yadi dharmeṇa yujyerannādharmarucayo janāḥ
dharmeṇa caratāṁ dharmastathā caiṣāṁ phalaṁ bhavet

translations.english: If by means of virtue, one attain the felicity attached to it, and by means of unrighteouness, one reap its proper fruit, then let those that are unrighteous reap the fruit of their impiety nor let those that set their face against sin, be deprived of the fruit of their righteousness, and let those that walk in the way of virtue reap the fruit of their piety.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मादर्था विवर्धन्ते येष्वधर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः
क्लिश्यन्ते धर्मशीलाश्च तस्मादेतौ निरर्थकौ
verses.transliteration:
yasmādarthā vivardhante yeṣvadharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
kliśyante dharmaśīlāśca tasmādetau nirarthakau

translations.english: But as prosperity attend those that are established in unrighteousness, and as those regardful of righteousness fare lamentably, these*have not the senses assigned to them (by the scriptures). *Virtue and vice.

verses.sanskrit:
वध्यन्ते पापकर्माणो यद्यधर्मेण राघव
वधकर्महतो धर्मः स हतः कं वधिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vadhyante pāpakarmāṇo yadyadharmeṇa rāghava
vadhakarmahato dharmaḥ sa hataḥ kaṁ vadhiṣyati

translations.english: If, O Rāghava, Rāghava, (it is contended that) unrighteousness cut off the wicked, then whom shall Unrighteousness, himself slain by the act of slaughter of the destroyer, slay in his turn?

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा विहितेनायं हन्यते हन्ति वा परम्
विधिरालिप्यते तेन न स पापेन कर्मणा
verses.transliteration:
atha vā vihitenāyaṁ hanyate hanti vā param
vidhirālipyate tena na sa pāpena karmaṇā

translations.english: Or if it is said that one is slain or slay another by ordinance, then it is destiny, which is touched by the sinful act and not he.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टप्रतिकारेण अव्यक्तेनासता सता
कथं शक्यं परं प्राप्तुं धर्मेणारिविकर्शन
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭapratikāreṇa avyaktenāsatā satā
kathaṁ śakyaṁ paraṁ prāptuṁ dharmeṇārivikarśana

translations.english: O chastiser of foes, incapable of meting out retribution,* unmanifest itself, and non-existent, how can virtue, even if we grant its existence, find out the person that should be slain? *"In consequence,' remarks Ramanuja, 'of their being devoid of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि सत्स्यात्सतां मुख्य नासत्स्यात्तव किंचन
त्वया यदीदृशं प्राप्तं तस्मात्सन्नोपपद्यते
verses.transliteration:
yadi satsyātsatāṁ mukhya nāsatsyāttava kiṁcana
tvayā yadīdṛśaṁ prāptaṁ tasmātsannopapadyate

translations.english: If, O foremost of the good, it had existed, you wouldst not have come by any misfortune. But inasmuch as you have fallen into this plight, there is no such thing as virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वा दुर्बलः क्लीबो बलं धर्मोऽनुवर्तते
दुर्बलो हृतमर्यादो न सेव्य इति मे मतिः
verses.transliteration:
atha vā durbalaḥ klībo balaṁ dharmo'nuvartate
durbalo hṛtamaryādo na sevya iti me matiḥ

translations.english: Or itself feeble and impotent, it take refuge in manliness. And being powerless and bereft of dignity, it should, I deem, by no means be followed.

verses.sanskrit:
बलस्य यदि चेद्धर्मो गुणभूतः पराक्रमे
धर्ममुत्सृज्य वर्तस्व यथा धर्मे तथा बले
verses.transliteration:
balasya yadi ceddharmo guṇabhūtaḥ parākrame
dharmamutsṛjya vartasva yathā dharme tathā bale

translations.english: If virtue is a property of manliness, then carefully forsaking virtue, do you follow strength as you have hitherto followed virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ चेत्सत्यवचनं धर्मः किल परंतप
अनृतस्त्वय्यकरुणः किं न बद्धस्त्वया पिता
verses.transliteration:
atha cetsatyavacanaṁ dharmaḥ kila paraṁtapa
anṛtastvayyakaruṇaḥ kiṁ na baddhastvayā pitā

translations.english: But, O subduer of enemies, if truthfulness be virtue, are you not bound by that departing from which the king lost his life?* *Explains the commentator, 'King Dasaratha lost his life, because he did not observe his word of installing you in the kingdom. Are you not bound by his word as well?'

verses.sanskrit:
यदि धर्मो भवेद्भूत अधर्मो वा परंतप
न स्म हत्वा मुनिं वज्री कुर्यादिज्यां शतक्रतुः
verses.transliteration:
yadi dharmo bhavedbhūta adharmo vā paraṁtapa
na sma hatvā muniṁ vajrī kuryādijyāṁ śatakratuḥ

translations.english: O chastiser of foes, if virtue must be practised above all, or if prowess must have precedence, then the thunder-handed Satakratu would not have celebrated his sacrifice, slaying the ascetic.* *The Logic is all in a jumble; but such is the text. The ascetic was Visvarūpa. The meaning, according to the commentator, is that, prowess is first and virtue next. Indra first used force, and then acquired merit.)

verses.sanskrit:
अधर्मसंश्रितो धर्मो विनाशयति राघव
सर्वमेतद्यथाकामं काकुत्स्थ कुरुते नरः
verses.transliteration:
adharmasaṁśrito dharmo vināśayati rāghava
sarvametadyathākāmaṁ kākutstha kurute naraḥ

translations.english: O Rāghava, virtue aided by prowess, destroy enemies. Therefore, O Kakutstha, people, for compassing their ends, resort to both virtue and prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
मम चेदं मतं तात धर्मोऽयमिति राघव
धर्ममूलं त्वया छिन्नं राज्यमुत्सृजता तदा
verses.transliteration:
mama cedaṁ mataṁ tāta dharmo'yamiti rāghava
dharmamūlaṁ tvayā chinnaṁ rājyamutsṛjatā tadā

translations.english: This, sire, is my opinion, this, O Raghava, is virtue. But you, having then renounced the kingdom, have laid the axe at the root* of righteousness. **Root, remarks, Rāmānuja, 'which is interest!'

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थेभ्यो हि विवृद्धेभ्यः संवृद्धेभ्यस्ततस्ततः
क्रियाः सर्वाः प्रवर्तन्ते पर्वतेभ्य इवापगाः
verses.transliteration:
arthebhyo hi vivṛddhebhyaḥ saṁvṛddhebhyastatastataḥ
kriyāḥ sarvāḥ pravartante parvatebhya ivāpagāḥ

translations.english: Like streams issuing out mountains, all acts spring from wealth flowing from various regions and attaining magnitude.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थेन हि वियुक्तस्य पुरुषस्याल्पतेजसः
व्युच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा
verses.transliteration:
arthena hi viyuktasya puruṣasyālpatejasaḥ
vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā

translations.english: Like a shrunken stream in summer, all the acts of that foolish person who has been devorced by wealth, are annihilated.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽयमर्थं परित्यज्य सुखकामः सुखैधितः
पापमारभते कर्तुं तथा दोषः प्रवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
so'yamarthaṁ parityajya sukhakāmaḥ sukhaidhitaḥ
pāpamārabhate kartuṁ tathā doṣaḥ pravartate

translations.english: He that renouncing riches, within his reach,* hankers after enjoyment, being carried away by his overmastering desire, take to getting at wealth by sinful acts; and then he incur guilt. *The commentator would have gotten riches.'

verses.sanskrit:
यस्यार्थास्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यार्थास्तस्य बान्धवः
यस्यार्थाः स पुमाँल्लोके यस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः
verses.transliteration:
yasyārthāstasya mitrāṇi yasyārthāstasya bāndhavaḥ
yasyārthāḥ sa pumā̐lloke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ

translations.english: To him that has wealth are friends, to him that has wealth are acquaintances, he that has wealth is an individuality in this world, and he that has wealth is a learned person.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्यार्थाः स च विक्रान्तो यस्यार्थाः स च बुद्धिमान्
यस्यार्थाः स महाभागो यस्यार्थाः स महागुणः
verses.transliteration:
yasyārthāḥ sa ca vikrānto yasyārthāḥ sa ca buddhimān
yasyārthāḥ sa mahābhāgo yasyārthāḥ sa mahāguṇaḥ

translations.english: He that has wealth is powerful; he that has wealth is intelligent; he that has wealth is mighty-armed; and he that has wealth is full of all graces.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थस्यैते परित्यागे दोषाः प्रव्याहृता मया
राज्यमुत्सृजता वीर येन बुद्धिस्त्वया कृता
verses.transliteration:
arthasyaite parityāge doṣāḥ pravyāhṛtā mayā
rājyamutsṛjatā vīra yena buddhistvayā kṛtā

translations.english: All these that I have en-numerated are the evils of forsaking fortune. (I cannot divine) what made you, renouncing the monarchy, to adopt such a course.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्यार्था धर्मकामार्थास्तस्य सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम्
अधनेनार्थकामेन नार्थः शक्यो विचिन्वता
verses.transliteration:
yasyārthā dharmakāmārthāstasya sarvaṁ pradakṣiṇam
adhanenārthakāmena nārthaḥ śakyo vicinvatā

translations.english: He that has riches, has virtue and desire attending on him, and has everything auspicious. That one without wealth, that seek it, cannot secure the wealth of prowess, without riches and desire.

verses.sanskrit:
हर्षः कामश्च दर्पश्च धर्मः क्रोधः शमो दमः
अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते नराधिप
verses.transliteration:
harṣaḥ kāmaśca darpaśca dharmaḥ krodhaḥ śamo damaḥ
arthādetāni sarvāṇi pravartante narādhipa

translations.english: O lord of men, cheerfulness, and desire, and pride, and piety, and anger, and self-restraint, and self-control, all these come from wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
येषां नश्यत्ययं लोकश्चरतां धर्मचारिणाम्
तेऽर्थास्त्वयि न दृश्यन्ते दुर्दिनेषु यथा ग्रहाः
verses.transliteration:
yeṣāṁ naśyatyayaṁ lokaścaratāṁ dharmacāriṇām
te'rthāstvayi na dṛśyante durdineṣu yathā grahāḥ

translations.english: As the planets are not discovered on a stormy day, that wealth, the want of which renders this world naught even to the ascetics practising righteousness, is not visible in you.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयि प्रव्रजिते वीर गुरोश्च वचने स्थिते
रक्षसापहृता भार्या प्राणैः प्रियतरा तव
verses.transliteration:
tvayi pravrajite vīra gurośca vacane sthite
rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā prāṇaiḥ priyatarā tava

translations.english: O hero, you having abode by the words of your superior and having come (to the forest), your wife dearer then life itself has been ravished by Rākṣasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तदद्य विपुलं वीर दुःखमिन्द्रजिता कृतम्
कर्मणा व्यपनेष्यामि तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ राघव
verses.transliteration:
tadadya vipulaṁ vīra duḥkhamindrajitā kṛtam
karmaṇā vyapaneṣyāmi tasmāduttiṣṭha rāghava

translations.english: But, O hero, today, O Raghava, by my acts will I remove this huge sorrow that has been heaped upon us by Indrajit. Therefore, rise you up.

verses.sanskrit:
अयमनघ तवोदितः प्रियार्थं; जनकसुता निधनं निरीक्ष्य रुष्टः
सहयगजरथां सराक्षसेन्द्रां; भृशमिषुभिर्विनिपातयामि लङ्काम्
verses.transliteration:
ayamanagha tavoditaḥ priyārthaṁ; janakasutā nidhanaṁ nirīkṣya ruṣṭaḥ
sahayagajarathāṁ sarākṣasendrāṁ; bhṛśamiṣubhirvinipātayāmi laṅkām

translations.english: Osinless one, urged on behalf of your welfare, I, waxing wroth on hearing of the slaughter of Janaka's daughter, shall with my shafts entirely raze to the ground Larkā with cars and elephants and steeds and the foremost Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
राममाश्वासयाने तु लक्ष्मणे भ्रातृवत्सले
निक्षिप्य गुल्मान्स्वस्थाने तत्रागच्छद्विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
rāmamāśvāsayāne tu lakṣmaṇe bhrātṛvatsale
nikṣipya gulmānsvasthāne tatrāgacchadvibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: As Lakşmaņa devoted to his brother was comforting Rāma, Vibhīşaņa, posting his forces at their proper quarters, came there, surrounded by four heroes accoutred in various arms, resembling masses of collyrium or leaders of elephant-herds.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं राघवं शोकलालसं
वानरांश्चैव ददृशे बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणान्
verses.transliteration:
so'bhigamya mahātmānaṁ rāghavaṁ śokalālasaṁ
vānarāṁścaiva dadṛśe bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇān

translations.english: And approaching the high-souled Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, he saw the monkeys with tears in their eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवं च महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्
ददर्श मोहमापन्नं लक्ष्मणस्याङ्कमाश्रितम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaṁ ca mahātmānamikṣvākukulanandanam
dadarśa mohamāpannaṁ lakṣmaṇasyāṅkamāśritam

translations.english: He saw that joy of the Ikşvāku race the high-souled Raghava-stupefied with grief, lying on the lap of Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
व्रीडितं शोकसंतप्तं दृष्ट्वा रामं विभीषणः
अन्तर्दुःखेन दीनात्मा किमेतदिति सोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vrīḍitaṁ śokasaṁtaptaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
antarduḥkhena dīnātmā kimetaditi so'bravīt

translations.english: son Seeing Rāma cast down and inflamed with grief, Vibhisana, inlay pained, said, "What is this?

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषण मुखं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवं तांश्च वानरान्
उवाच लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमिदं बाष्पपरिप्लुतः
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇa mukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvaṁ tāṁśca vānarān
uvāca lakṣmaṇo vākyamidaṁ bāṣpapariplutaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, gazing at Vibhisana's countenance as well as all those monkeys, Laksmana, with his eyes flooded with tears, said these words pregnant with dire import.

verses.sanskrit:
हतामिन्द्रजिता सीतामिह श्रुत्वैव राघवः
हनूमद्वचनात्सौम्य ततो मोहमुपागतः
verses.transliteration:
hatāmindrajitā sītāmiha śrutvaiva rāghavaḥ
hanūmadvacanātsaumya tato mohamupāgataḥ

translations.english: O placid one, hearing from Hanumān's lips that Sītā has been slain by Indrajit. Rāghava has been overcome with stupor.

verses.sanskrit:
कथयन्तं तु सौमित्रिं संनिवार्य विभीषणः
पुष्कलार्थमिदं वाक्यं विसंज्ञं राममब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
kathayantaṁ tu saumitriṁ saṁnivārya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
puṣkalārthamidaṁ vākyaṁ visaṁjñaṁ rāmamabravīt

translations.english: As Sumitra's was speaking thus, Vibhisana,. preventing him, addressed the stupefied Rāma in these pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit:
मनुजेन्द्रार्तरूपेण यदुक्तस्त्वं हनूमता
तदयुक्तमहं मन्ये सागरस्येव शोषणम्
verses.transliteration:
manujendrārtarūpeṇa yaduktastvaṁ hanūmatā
tadayuktamahaṁ manye sāgarasyeva śoṣaṇam

translations.english: O king, all that Hanumān in distressful guise had communicated to you I deem as improbable, like to the drying of the deep.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिप्रायं तु जानामि रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
सीतां प्रति महाबाहो न च घातं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
abhiprāyaṁ tu jānāmi rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
sītāṁ prati mahābāho na ca ghātaṁ kariṣyati

translations.english: I know the intent of the impious Rāvana with reference to Sita, O mighty-armed one. Her he will not slay.

verses.sanskrit:
याच्यमानः सुबहुशो मया हितचिकीर्षुणा
वैदेहीमुत्सृजस्वेति न च तत्कृतवान्वचः
verses.transliteration:
yācyamānaḥ subahuśo mayā hitacikīrṣuṇā
vaidehīmutsṛjasveti na ca tatkṛtavānvacaḥ
