translations.english: I, seeking his welfare, had besought him much, saying, 'Let go Vaidehi', but he did not act up to my speech.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव साम्ना न भेदेन न दानेन कुतो युधा
सा द्रष्टुमपि शक्येत नैव चान्येन केनचित्
verses.transliteration:
naiva sāmnā na bhedena na dānena kuto yudhā
sā draṣṭumapi śakyeta naiva cānyena kenacit

translations.english: Neither by conciliation, nor by gift, nor by dissension, and where is war? nor by any other means is one capable of obtaining the very sight of Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
वानरान्मोहयित्वा तु प्रतियातः स राक्षसः
चैत्यं निकुम्भिलां नाम यत्र होमं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
vānarānmohayitvā tu pratiyātaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ
caityaṁ nikumbhilāṁ nāma yatra homaṁ kariṣyati

translations.english: Today, going to the sacrificial ground (called) Nikumbhilā, he will offer oblations into fire; and there the deity of fire will present himself along with Vasava and the (other) divinities.

verses.sanskrit:
हुतवानुपयातो हि देवैरपि सवासवैः
दुराधर्षो भवत्येष संग्रामे रावणात्मजः
verses.transliteration:
hutavānupayāto hi devairapi savāsavaiḥ
durādharṣo bhavatyeṣa saṁgrāme rāvaṇātmajaḥ

translations.english: Then Rāvana's son shall be invincible in batile. Indubitably that illusion has been wrought by him, to deceive (the monkeys), so that they might not through their prowess disturb him there.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन मोहयता नूनमेषा माया प्रयोजिता
विघ्नमन्विच्छता तात वानराणां पराक्रमे
ससैन्यास्तत्र गच्छामो यावत्तन्न समाप्यते
verses.transliteration:
tena mohayatā nūnameṣā māyā prayojitā
vighnamanvicchatā tāta vānarāṇāṁ parākrame
sasainyāstatra gacchāmo yāvattanna samāpyate

translations.english: Thither will we go before he has furnished his (sacrifice). O foremost of men, shake off this vain sorrow that has overcome you!

verses.sanskrit:
इह त्वं स्वस्थ हृदयस्तिष्ठ सत्त्वसमुच्छ्रितः
लक्ष्मणं प्रेषयास्माभिः सह सैन्यानुकर्षिभिः
verses.transliteration:
iha tvaṁ svastha hṛdayastiṣṭha sattvasamucchritaḥ
lakṣmaṇaṁ preṣayāsmābhiḥ saha sainyānukarṣibhiḥ

translations.english: Seeing you smitten with grief, this entire host is dispirited. Here, with your heart composed, do your stay, summoning your strength. Send Lakşmañana along with us and the flower of the forces.

verses.sanskrit:
एष तं नरशार्दूलो रावणिं निशितैः शरैः
त्याजयिष्यति तत्कर्म ततो वध्यो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
eṣa taṁ naraśārdūlo rāvaṇiṁ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
tyājayiṣyati tatkarma tato vadhyo bhaviṣyati

translations.english: This foremost of men by means of sharpened shafts will make Rāvana's son give up his rites; and then shall he be capable of being slain by us.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैते निशितास्तीक्ष्णाः पत्रिपत्राङ्गवाजिनः
पतत्रिण इवासौम्याः शराः पास्यन्ति शोणितम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyaite niśitāstīkṣṇāḥ patripatrāṅgavājinaḥ
patatriṇa ivāsaumyāḥ śarāḥ pāsyanti śoṇitam

translations.english: These keen and sharpened shafts of his, attaining access of velocity through the feathers of birds, and themselves resembling fierce fowls, will drink his* blood. *Indrajit's.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्संदिश महाबाहो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्
राक्षसस्य विनाशाय वज्रं वज्रधरो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tatsaṁdiśa mahābāho lakṣmaṇaṁ śubhalakṣaṇam
rākṣasasya vināśāya vajraṁ vajradharo yathā

translations.english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you in order to the destruction of the Rākşasa, commission Lakşmana, even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt command the same.

verses.sanskrit:
मनुजवर न कालविप्रकर्षो; रिपुनिधनं प्रति यत्क्षमोऽद्य कर्तुम्
त्वमतिसृज रिपोर्वधाय बाणी;मसुरपुरोन्मथने यथा महेन्द्रः
verses.transliteration:
manujavara na kālaviprakarṣo; ripunidhanaṁ prati yatkṣamo'dya kartum
tvamatisṛja riporvadhāya bāṇī;masurapuronmathane yathā mahendraḥ

translations.english: As today no time should be lost, therefore do you send Lakşmaņa for campassing the destruction of the foe, even as Mahendra send the thunder-bolt for bringing about the destruction of the enemies of the immortals.

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्तकर्मा हि स राक्षसेन्द्रो; भवत्यदृश्यः समरे सुरासुरैः
युयुत्सता तेन समाप्तकर्मणा; भवेत्सुराणामपि संशयो महान्
verses.transliteration:
samāptakarmā hi sa rākṣasendro; bhavatyadṛśyaḥ samare surāsuraiḥ
yuyutsatā tena samāptakarmaṇā; bhavetsurāṇāmapi saṁśayo mahān

translations.english: If that foremost of Räkşasas can finish his rites, he shall be invisible to both celestials and Asuras; and, he fighting after finishing his sacrifice, the celestials themselves shall be placed in great jeopardy.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोककर्शितः
नोपधारयते व्यक्तं यदुक्तं तेन रक्षसा
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ
nopadhārayate vyaktaṁ yaduktaṁ tena rakṣasā

translations.english: Hearing his speech, Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, could not perfectly comprehend what was said by the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो धैर्यमवष्टभ्य रामः परपुरंजयः
विभीषणमुपासीनमुवाच कपिसंनिधौ
verses.transliteration:
tato dhairyamavaṣṭabhya rāmaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ
vibhīṣaṇamupāsīnamuvāca kapisaṁnidhau

translations.english: Then, summoning up patience, Rāma-captor of hostile capitals, spoke to Vibhisana, seated near the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृताधिपते वाक्यं यदुक्तं ते विभीषण
भूयस्तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि ब्रूहि यत्ते विवक्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
nairṛtādhipate vākyaṁ yaduktaṁ te vibhīṣaṇa
bhūyastacchrotumicchāmi brūhi yatte vivakṣitam

translations.english: O lord of Naiſtas, I once more wish to hear what, O Vibhisana, you have said.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
यत्तत्पुनरिदं वाक्यं बभाषे स विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
yattatpunaridaṁ vākyaṁ babhāṣe sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Raghava's words, Vibhisana, skilled in speech, again spoke these words, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाज्ञप्तं महाबाहो त्वया गुल्मनिवेशनम्
तत्तथानुष्ठितं वीर त्वद्वाक्यसमनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
yathājñaptaṁ mahābāho tvayā gulmaniveśanam
tattathānuṣṭhitaṁ vīra tvadvākyasamanantaram

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, I have stationed the forces, O hero, agreeably to your directions.

verses.sanskrit:
तान्यनीकानि सर्वाणि विभक्तानि समन्ततः
विन्यस्ता यूथपाश्चैव यथान्यायं विभागशः
verses.transliteration:
tānyanīkāni sarvāṇi vibhaktāni samantataḥ
vinyastā yūthapāścaiva yathānyāyaṁ vibhāgaśaḥ

translations.english: The entire force has been divided around; and the leaders have also been placed properly.

verses.sanskrit:
भूयस्तु मम विजाप्यं तच्छृणुष्व महायशः
त्वय्यकारणसंतप्ते संतप्तहृदया वयम्
verses.transliteration:
bhūyastu mama vijāpyaṁ tacchṛṇuṣva mahāyaśaḥ
tvayyakāraṇasaṁtapte saṁtaptahṛdayā vayam

translations.english: Further, O mighty master, listen to what I have to say. On your having been causelessly aggrieve, we all of us were seized with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यज राजन्निमं शोकं मिथ्या संतापमागतम्
तदियं त्यज्यतां चिन्ता शत्रुहर्षविवर्धनी
verses.transliteration:
tyaja rājannimaṁ śokaṁ mithyā saṁtāpamāgatam
tadiyaṁ tyajyatāṁ cintā śatruharṣavivardhanī

translations.english: It this anxiety of your conduce to the joy of the enemy, do you cast it off. and, O hero, bestir yourself, and summon up spirits.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यमः क्रियतां वीर हर्षः समुपसेव्यताम्
प्राप्तव्या यदि ते सीता हन्तव्यश्च निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
udyamaḥ kriyatāṁ vīra harṣaḥ samupasevyatām
prāptavyā yadi te sītā hantavyaśca niśācarāḥ

translations.english: If you are to have Sītā, and if the nightrangers are to be slain by you, do you, Raghu's son, listen to my profitable speech.

verses.sanskrit:
रघुनन्दन वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां मे हितं वचः
साध्वयं यातु सौमित्रिर्बलेन महता वृतः
निकुम्भिलायां संप्राप्य हन्तुं रावणिमाहवे
verses.transliteration:
raghunandana vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṁ me hitaṁ vacaḥ
sādhvayaṁ yātu saumitrirbalena mahatā vṛtaḥ
nikumbhilāyāṁ saṁprāpya hantuṁ rāvaṇimāhave

translations.english: Let Sumitra's son go forth, environed by a mighty force, for slaying in battle the son of Ravana, who has gone to Nikumbhila; with shafts resembling Venomous serpents, discharged from the round* of his bow. *The bow drawn to its full stretch, becomes circular.

verses.sanskrit:
तेन वीरेण तपसा वरदानात्स्वयम्भुतः
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरः प्राप्तं कामगाश्च तुरंगमाः
verses.transliteration:
tena vīreṇa tapasā varadānātsvayambhutaḥ
astraṁ brahmaśiraḥ prāptaṁ kāmagāśca turaṁgamāḥ

translations.english: By virtue of his austerities, that hero, from a boon conferred by the self-sprung, has obtained the Brahmasira weapon, together with steeds coursing at their will.

verses.sanskrit:
निकुम्भिलामसंप्राप्तमहुताग्निं च यो रिपुः
त्वामाततायिनं हन्यादिन्द्रशत्रो स ते वधः
इत्येवं विहितो राजन्वधस्तस्यैव धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
nikumbhilāmasaṁprāptamahutāgniṁ ca yo ripuḥ
tvāmātatāyinaṁ hanyādindraśatro sa te vadhaḥ
ityevaṁ vihito rājanvadhastasyaiva dhīmataḥ

translations.english: When not reaching Nikumbhilā, and not having finished your offerings to fire, you, equipped with arms, are slain by a foe, O enemy of Indra, that is your death. Thus, O mightyarmed one, did the lord of all creatures confer a boon (on Indrajit), and, o king, thus was the death of this intelligent one ordained.

verses.sanskrit:
वधायेन्द्रजितो राम तं दिशस्व महाबलम्
हते तस्मिन्हतं विद्धि रावणं ससुहृज्जनम्
verses.transliteration:
vadhāyendrajito rāma taṁ diśasva mahābalam
hate tasminhataṁ viddhi rāvaṇaṁ sasuhṛjjanam

translations.english: O Rāma, for compassing the destruction of Indrajit, do you commission a mighty force. On his being slain, know that Rāvana along with his retainers are slain.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्व रामो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्
जानामि तस्य रौद्रस्य मायां सत्यपराक्रम
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutva rāmo vākyamathābravīt
jānāmi tasya raudrasya māyāṁ satyaparākrama

translations.english: Hearing Vibhīşana's words, Rāma said, “O you having truth for prowess, I know the illusion of that fierce one.

verses.sanskrit:
स हि ब्रह्मास्त्रवित्प्राज्ञो महामायो महाबलः
करोत्यसंज्ञान्संग्रामे देवान्सवरुणानपि
verses.transliteration:
sa hi brahmāstravitprājño mahāmāyo mahābalaḥ
karotyasaṁjñānsaṁgrāme devānsavaruṇānapi

translations.english: Without doubt, the is skilled in the Brahma weapon, is potent in illusion and, is possessed of exceeding strength. In conflict, he deprive of consciousness even the celestials with Varuņa (at their head).

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्तु रिपोर्ज्ञात्वा मायावीर्यं दुरात्मनः
लक्ष्मणं कीर्तिसंपन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavastu riporjñātvā māyāvīryaṁ durātmanaḥ
lakṣmaṇaṁ kīrtisaṁpannamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: As that illustrious (one) go about in the welkin on his chariot, none, can perceive his course, like the course of the sun when the sky is covered with clouds.” And Raghava, being well acquainted with the illusive energy of his wicked-minded foe, addressed the renowned Laksmana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्वानरेन्द्रस्य बलं तेन सर्वेण संवृतः
हनूमत्प्रमुखैश्चैव यूथपैः सहलक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
yadvānarendrasya balaṁ tena sarveṇa saṁvṛtaḥ
hanūmatpramukhaiścaiva yūthapaiḥ sahalakṣmaṇa

translations.english: Environed by the entire host of the lord of monkeys, accompanied by the leaders, O Laksmana, headed by Hanuman, with Jambavan, king of bears-and girt round by the forces, do you slay this son of the Raksasa, possessed of the strength of illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं त्वां सचिवैः सार्धं महात्मा रजनीचरः
अभिज्ञस्तस्य देशस्य पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ tvāṁ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṁ mahātmā rajanīcaraḥ
abhijñastasya deśasya pṛṣṭhato'nugamiṣyati

translations.english: And accompanied by his counsellors, this high-souled night-ranger shall follow at you back, in this engagement with that one skilled in illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः सविभीषणः
जग्राह कार्मुकं श्रेष्ठमन्यद्भीमपराक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ
jagrāha kārmukaṁ śreṣṭhamanyadbhīmaparākramaḥ

translations.english: Then hearing Rāghava's words, Lakşmaņa endowed with dreadful prowess, with Vibhīşaņa, took up another excellent bow.

verses.sanskrit:
संनद्धः कवची खड्गी स शरी हेमचापधृक्
रामपादावुपस्पृश्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁnaddhaḥ kavacī khaḍgī sa śarī hemacāpadhṛk
rāmapādāvupaspṛśya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrirabravīt

translations.english: And donning on his mail, and putting on his armour and his sword, and furnished with arrows, and a bow in his left hand, Sumitrā's son, touching Rāma's feet, feeling elated, addressed Rāma, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य मत्कार्मुकोन्मुखाः शरा निर्भिद्य रावणिम्
लङ्कामभिपतिष्यन्ति हंसाः पुष्करिणीमिव
verses.transliteration:
adya matkārmukonmukhāḥ śarā nirbhidya rāvaṇim
laṅkāmabhipatiṣyanti haṁsāḥ puṣkariṇīmiva

translations.english: Today the shafts discharged from my bow, piercing Ravana's son, shall fall into Lanka, even as swans drop into a tank.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्यैव तस्य रौद्रस्य शरीरं मामकाः शराः
विधमिष्यन्ति हत्वा तं महाचापगुणच्युताः
verses.transliteration:
adyaiva tasya raudrasya śarīraṁ māmakāḥ śarāḥ
vidhamiṣyanti hatvā taṁ mahācāpaguṇacyutāḥ

translations.english: This very day shall my arrows, shot from my redoubtable bow-string, rive the body of that terrific one.

verses.sanskrit:
स एवमुक्त्वा द्युतिमान्वचनं भ्रातुरग्रतः
स रावणिवधाकाङ्क्षी लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
sa evamuktvā dyutimānvacanaṁ bhrāturagrataḥ
sa rāvaṇivadhākāṅkṣī lakṣmaṇastvarito yayau

translations.english: Having spoken thus, the effulgent Lakşmana, eager to slay Rāvana's son, went before his brother.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिवाद्य गुरोः पादौ कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्
निकुम्भिलामभिययौ चैत्यं रावणिपालितम्
verses.transliteration:
so'bhivādya guroḥ pādau kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
nikumbhilāmabhiyayau caityaṁ rāvaṇipālitam

translations.english: Having saluted at the feet of his superior and went round him, Lakşmaņa set out for the sacrificial ground (named) Nikumbhila, protected by the son of Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणेन सहितो राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्
कृतस्वस्त्ययनो भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇena sahito rājaputraḥ pratāpavān
kṛtasvastyayano bhrātrā lakṣmaṇastvarito yayau

translations.english: Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, that powerful son of the king-Lakşmaņa-after his brother had offered up prayers in his behalf, set off with all speed.

verses.sanskrit:
वानराणां सहस्रैस्तु हनूमान्बहुभिर्वृतः
विभीषणः सहामात्यस्तदा लक्ष्मणमन्वगात्
verses.transliteration:
vānarāṇāṁ sahasraistu hanūmānbahubhirvṛtaḥ
vibhīṣaṇaḥ sahāmātyastadā lakṣmaṇamanvagāt

translations.english: Surrounded by thousands of monkeys, Hanumān as well as Vibhīşaņa together with his counsellors speedily went in the wake of Lakş mana.

verses.sanskrit:
महता हरिसैन्येन सवेगमभिसंवृतः
ऋक्षराजबलं चैव ददर्श पथि विष्ठितम्
verses.transliteration:
mahatā harisainyena savegamabhisaṁvṛtaḥ
ṛkṣarājabalaṁ caiva dadarśa pathi viṣṭhitam

translations.english: And strongly encompassed by that mighty monkey-host, (Laksmana) saw the forces of the bear-king stationed on the way.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः
राक्षसेन्द्रबलं दूरादपश्यद्व्यूहमास्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā dūramadhvānaṁ saumitrirmitranandanaḥ
rākṣasendrabalaṁ dūrādapaśyadvyūhamāsthitam

translations.english: Having proceeded far, Sumitra's Sumitra's son-enhancer of the delight of friends, from a distance discovered the forces of the Rākşasmonarch, drawn up in battle-array.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्राप्य धनुष्पाणिर्मायायोगमरिंदम
तस्थौ ब्रह्मविधानेन विजेतुं रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprāpya dhanuṣpāṇirmāyāyogamariṁdama
tasthau brahmavidhānena vijetuṁ raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: That subduer of enemies-Raghu's sonbearing his bow in his hand, coming upon him whose martial might lay in illusion, stopped (there) for conquering his foe agreeably to the ordinance * of Brahma. *The ordinance was that Indrajit should be slain while remaining outside Nikumbhilā, his rites not yet finished.

verses.sanskrit:
विविधममलशस्त्रभास्वरं त;द्ध्वजगहनं विपुलं महारथैश्च
प्रतिभयतममप्रमेयवेगं; तिमिरमिव द्विषतां बलं विवेश
verses.transliteration:
vividhamamalaśastrabhāsvaraṁ ta;ddhvajagahanaṁ vipulaṁ mahārathaiśca
pratibhayatamamaprameyavegaṁ; timiramiva dviṣatāṁ balaṁ viveśa

translations.english: Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, the heroic Angada, and the Wind-god's offspring, the powerful son of the king dived into the forces of the foe, various, blazing with burnished arms, dense with standards, and thronging with mighty cars,* capable of striking terror (into the hearts of the spectators), instinct with immeasurable energy, and resembling darkness. *Maharathai (ab.) may also mean with mighty carwarriors.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ तस्यामवस्थायां लक्ष्मणं रावणानुजः
परेषामहितं वाक्यमर्थसाधकमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha tasyāmavasthāyāṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ rāvaṇānujaḥ
pareṣāmahitaṁ vākyamarthasādhakamabravīt

translations.english: When things were in this condition, Rāvana's younger brother addressed Lakşmaņa in words fraught with evil to foes and conducing to the welfare (of his own party), saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्यानीकस्य महतो भेदने यतलक्ष्मण
राक्षसेन्द्रसुतोऽप्यत्र भिन्ने दृश्यो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
asyānīkasya mahato bhedane yatalakṣmaṇa
rākṣasendrasuto'pyatra bhinne dṛśyo bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Do you without delay bring on an engagement between this cloud-black Räksasa army, which you behold, and the monkeys having rocks for their arms. O Lakşmaņa, do you exert yourself to break through his* mighty-army; and when the ranks are broken, the son of the Rákşasa-lord shall be visible. * Indrajit's, that is.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वमिन्द्राशनिप्रख्यैः शरैरवकिरन्परान्
अभिद्रवाशु यावद्वै नैतत्कर्म समाप्यते
verses.transliteration:
sa tvamindrāśaniprakhyaiḥ śarairavakiranparān
abhidravāśu yāvadvai naitatkarma samāpyate

translations.english: Scattering among the foes shafts resembling Indra's thunder-bolt, charge him while he has not yet finished this ceremony.

verses.sanskrit:
जहि वीरदुरात्मानं मायापरमधार्मिकम्
रावणिं क्रूरकर्माणं सर्वलोकभयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
jahi vīradurātmānaṁ māyāparamadhārmikam
rāvaṇiṁ krūrakarmāṇaṁ sarvalokabhayāvaham

translations.english: Slay, O hero, this wicked one, this son of Ravana, given to illusion, and of terrific feats, the fear of all the worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः
ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi rākṣasendrasutaṁ prati

translations.english: Hearing Vibhisana's.words, Laksmana graced with auspicious marks began to shower arrows on the son of the Raksasa-chief.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षाः शाखामृगाश्चैव द्रुमाद्रिवरयोधिनः
अभ्यधावन्त सहितास्तदनीकमवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣāḥ śākhāmṛgāścaiva drumādrivarayodhinaḥ
abhyadhāvanta sahitāstadanīkamavasthitam

translations.english: And bears and monkeys, given to fighting excellently with trees, in a body rushed towards that army (of Rākşasa) drawn up there.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसाश्च शितैर्बाणैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः
उद्यतैः समवर्तन्त कपिसैन्यजिघांसवः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasāśca śitairbāṇairasibhiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ
udyataiḥ samavartanta kapisainyajighāṁsavaḥ

translations.english: The Rākşasas (on their part) burning to slaughter the monkey-forces, rushed in the encounter with sharpened shafts and darts and tomaras.

verses.sanskrit:
शस्त्रैर्बहुविधाकारैः शितैर्बाणैश्च पादपैः
उद्यतैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च घोरैराकाशमावृतम्
verses.transliteration:
śastrairbahuvidhākāraiḥ śitairbāṇaiśca pādapaiḥ
udyatairgiriśṛṅgaiśca ghorairākāśamāvṛtam

translations.english: There took place a tremendous onslaught of the monkeys and the Raksasas. And Lankā resounded all around with that mighty tumult; and the sky was covered with weapons of various shapes, and whetted arrows and trees and dreadful upraised mountain-tops.

verses.sanskrit:
ते राक्षसा वानरेषु विकृताननबाहवः
निवेशयन्तः शस्त्राणि चक्रुस्ते सुमहद्भयम्
verses.transliteration:
te rākṣasā vānareṣu vikṛtānanabāhavaḥ
niveśayantaḥ śastrāṇi cakruste sumahadbhayam

translations.english: Rākşasas having frightful faces and arms, playing their arms among the foremost monkeys, began to spread terror (there).

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव सकलैर्वृक्षैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च वानराः
अभिजघ्नुर्निजघ्नुश्च समरे राक्षसर्षभान्
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva sakalairvṛkṣairgiriśṛṅgaiśca vānarāḥ
abhijaghnurnijaghnuśca samare rākṣasarṣabhān

translations.english: In the same way the monkeys in the conflict fell to slaying and wounding the Rākşasas with trees and hill-tops.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋक्षवानरमुख्यैश्च महाकायैर्महाबलैः
रक्षसां वध्यमानानां महद्भयमजायत
verses.transliteration:
ṛkṣavānaramukhyaiśca mahākāyairmahābalaiḥ
rakṣasāṁ vadhyamānānāṁ mahadbhayamajāyata

translations.english: And great was the terror that was spread among the warring Räkşasas by the flower of the bears and monkeys, possessed of gigantic persons and endowed with prodigious strength.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वमनीकं विषण्णं तु श्रुत्वा शत्रुभिरर्दितम्
उदतिष्ठत दुर्धर्षस्तत्कर्मण्यननुष्ठिते
verses.transliteration:
svamanīkaṁ viṣaṇṇaṁ tu śrutvā śatrubhirarditam
udatiṣṭhata durdharṣastatkarmaṇyananuṣṭhite

translations.english: Hearing his own army hard beset by the enemies, and dropping, the unconquerable one, ere yet he had finished his rites, rose up.

verses.sanskrit:
वृक्षान्धकारान्निष्क्रम्य जातक्रोधः स रावणिः
आरुरोह रथं सज्जं पूर्वयुक्तं स राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
vṛkṣāndhakārānniṣkramya jātakrodhaḥ sa rāvaṇiḥ
āruroha rathaṁ sajjaṁ pūrvayuktaṁ sa rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Issuing from the gloom of the trees, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, ascended his car, which had already been well yoked (with steeds).

verses.sanskrit:
स भीमकार्मुकशरः कृष्णाञ्जनचयोपमः
रक्तास्यनयनः क्रूरो बभौ मृत्युरिवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
sa bhīmakārmukaśaraḥ kṛṣṇāñjanacayopamaḥ
raktāsyanayanaḥ krūro babhau mṛtyurivāntakaḥ

translations.english: Accoutred in a dreadful bow and arrows, that one, resembling a mass of collyrium, having a red face and eyes, looked dreadful like the reaper-death.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वैव तु रथस्थं तं पर्यवर्तत तद्बलम्
रक्षसां भीमवेगानां लक्ष्मणेन युयुत्सताम्
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvaiva tu rathasthaṁ taṁ paryavartata tadbalam
rakṣasāṁ bhīmavegānāṁ lakṣmaṇena yuyutsatām

translations.english: As soon as they saw him mounted on his car, that host of Rākşas possessed of dreadful impetuosity, eager to engage with Lakşmaņa, stood on their ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्काले तु हनुमानुद्यम्य सुदुरासदम्
धरणीधरसंकाशी महावृक्षमरिंदमः
verses.transliteration:
tasminkāle tu hanumānudyamya sudurāsadam
dharaṇīdharasaṁkāśī mahāvṛkṣamariṁdamaḥ

translations.english: At this time that subduer of enemies, Hanumăn-resembling a mountain, uprooted a giant tree incapable of being handled.

verses.sanskrit:
स राक्षसानां तत्सैन्यं कालाग्निरिव निर्दहन्
चकार बहुभिर्वृक्षैर्निःसंज्ञं युधि वानरः
verses.transliteration:
sa rākṣasānāṁ tatsainyaṁ kālāgniriva nirdahan
cakāra bahubhirvṛkṣairniḥsaṁjñaṁ yudhi vānaraḥ

translations.english: In that encounter, the monkey, consuming (the forces) like the fire risen at Doomsday, made that army of Rākşasas insensible with innumerable trees.

verses.sanskrit:
विध्वंसयन्तं तरसा दृष्ट्वैव पवनात्मजम्
राक्षसानां सहस्राणि हनूमन्तमवाकिरन्
verses.transliteration:
vidhvaṁsayantaṁ tarasā dṛṣṭvaiva pavanātmajam
rākṣasānāṁ sahasrāṇi hanūmantamavākiran

translations.english: Finding the Wind-god's son, Hanumān, suddenly spreading devastation among the Rāks asas by thousands, (they) showered (shafts) on him.

verses.sanskrit:
स ददर्श कपिश्रेष्ठमचलोपममिन्द्रजित्
सूदयानममित्रघ्नममित्रान्पवनात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dadarśa kapiśreṣṭhamacalopamamindrajit
sūdayānamamitraghnamamitrānpavanātmajam

translations.english: Indrajit saw that foremost of monkeys resembling a hill, the offspring of the Windgod possessing himself if calmness, while destroying his foes.

verses.sanskrit:
स सारथिमुवाचेदं याहि यत्रैष वानरः
क्षयमेव हि नः कुर्याद्राक्षसानामुपेक्षितः
verses.transliteration:
sa sārathimuvācedaṁ yāhi yatraiṣa vānaraḥ
kṣayameva hi naḥ kuryādrākṣasānāmupekṣitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat, be* addressed his charioteer, saying, "Go where the monkeys is. Being disregarded by the Raksasas, he makes havoc among us." *Indrajit.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तः सारथिस्तेन ययौ यत्र स मारुतिः
वहन्परमदुर्धर्षं स्थितमिन्द्रजितं रथे
verses.transliteration:
ityuktaḥ sārathistena yayau yatra sa mārutiḥ
vahanparamadurdharṣaṁ sthitamindrajitaṁ rathe

translations.english: Thus accosted by him, the charioteer went where the Wind-god's offspring was, carrying the exceedingly invincible Indrajit seated on the car.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभ्युपेत्य शरान्खड्गान्पट्टसासिपरश्वधान्
अभ्यवर्षत दुर्धर्षः कपिमूर्ध्नि स राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
so'bhyupetya śarānkhaḍgānpaṭṭasāsiparaśvadhān
abhyavarṣata durdharṣaḥ kapimūrdhni sa rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: And rushing forward, that irrepressible one the Rākşasas-began to shower on the monkey's head arrows and swords and pațțišas and scimitars and axes.

verses.sanskrit:
तानि शस्त्राणि घोराणि प्रतिगृह्य स मारुतिः
रोषेण महताविषो वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tāni śastrāṇi ghorāṇi pratigṛhya sa mārutiḥ
roṣeṇa mahatāviṣo vākyaṁ cedamuvāca ha

translations.english: And bearing all those dreadful arms, the Wind-god's offspring, overcome with a mighty rage said.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि रावणात्मज दुर्मते
वायुपुत्रं समासाद्य न जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि
verses.transliteration:
yudhyasva yadi śūro'si rāvaṇātmaja durmate
vāyuputraṁ samāsādya na jīvanpratiyāsyasi

translations.english: O wicked-minded son of Rävaņa, if you are a hero, fight on. Combat with me with your arms.

verses.sanskrit:
बाहुभ्यां संप्रयुध्यस्व यदि मे द्वन्द्वमाहवे
वेगं सहस्व दुर्बुद्धे ततस्त्वं रक्षसां वरः
verses.transliteration:
bāhubhyāṁ saṁprayudhyasva yadi me dvandvamāhave
vegaṁ sahasva durbuddhe tatastvaṁ rakṣasāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: If in the encounter, you bear my impetus, then, O you of perverse sense, you indeed are the foremost of Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमन्तं जिघांसन्तं समुद्यतशरासनम्
रावणात्मजमाचष्टे लक्ष्मणाय विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
hanūmantaṁ jighāṁsantaṁ samudyataśarāsanam
rāvaṇātmajamācaṣṭe lakṣmaṇāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then Vibhīşana pointed out to Lakşmaņa the son of Ravana, who with his bow upraised, was eager to slay Hanumān.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तु वासवनिर्जेता रावणस्यात्मसंभवः
स एष रथमास्थाय हनूमन्तं जिघांसति
verses.transliteration:
yastu vāsavanirjetā rāvaṇasyātmasaṁbhavaḥ
sa eṣa rathamāsthāya hanūmantaṁ jighāṁsati

translations.english: This one that, mounted on his car, is eager to slay Hanumăn, is the son of Rāvaņa that has vanquished Vasava himself (in battle). Do you, O son of Sumitrā, with peerless shafts capable of resisting enemies, dreadful, and competent to finish the lives (of foes), slay the son of Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवमुक्तस्तु तदा महात्मा; विभीषणेनारिविभीषणेन
ददर्श तं पर्वतसंनिकाशं; रथस्थितं भीमबलं दुरासदम्
verses.transliteration:
ityevamuktastu tadā mahātmā; vibhīṣaṇenārivibhīṣaṇena
dadarśa taṁ parvatasaṁnikāśaṁ; rathasthitaṁ bhīmabalaṁ durāsadam

translations.english: Thus accosted by Vibhīşaņa terrific to foes, that high-souled one saw (Indrajit) of dreadful prowess, difficult to gut at, and resembling a hill, stationed on his car.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सौमित्रिं जातहर्षो विभीषणः
धनुष्पाणिनमादाय त्वरमाणो जगाम सः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu saumitriṁ jātaharṣo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
dhanuṣpāṇinamādāya tvaramāṇo jagāma saḥ

translations.english: Having spoken thus to Sumitra's son, Vibhișaņa experienced delight, and taking (Laksmana) bearing a bow in his hand, hurriedly went off.

verses.sanskrit:
अविदूरं ततो गत्वा प्रविश्य च महद्वनम्
दर्शयामास तत्कर्म लक्ष्मणाय विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
avidūraṁ tato gatvā praviśya ca mahadvanam
darśayāmāsa tatkarma lakṣmaṇāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Proceeding some way and entering the mighty wood, Vibhīşaņa pointed out to Lakşmaņa the place (of sacrifice).

verses.sanskrit:
नीलजीमूतसंकाशं न्यग्रोधं भीमदर्शनम्
तेजस्वी रावणभ्राता लक्ष्मणाय न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
nīlajīmūtasaṁkāśaṁ nyagrodhaṁ bhīmadarśanam
tejasvī rāvaṇabhrātā lakṣmaṇāya nyavedayat

translations.english: The energetic brother of Rāvana showed to Lakşmaņa the Nyagrodha, dreadful to behold and resembling a mass of sable clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
इहोपहारं भूतानां बलवान्रावणातजः
उपहृत्य ततः पश्चात्संग्राममभिवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
ihopahāraṁ bhūtānāṁ balavānrāvaṇātajaḥ
upahṛtya tataḥ paścātsaṁgrāmamabhivartate

translations.english: Here offering presents to the ghosts, the powerful son of Răvaņa afterwards engages in conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति राक्षसः
निहन्ति समरे शत्रून्बध्नाति च शरोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ tato bhavati rākṣasaḥ
nihanti samare śatrūnbadhnāti ca śarottamaiḥ

translations.english: Then the Rākşasas becomes invisible to all beings; and he slay his enemies in battle and fastens them with excellent shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तमप्रविष्टं न्यग्रोधं बलिनं रावणात्मजम्
विध्वंसय शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः सरथं साश्वसारथिम्
verses.transliteration:
tamapraviṣṭaṁ nyagrodhaṁ balinaṁ rāvaṇātmajam
vidhvaṁsaya śaraistīkṣṇaiḥ sarathaṁ sāśvasārathim

translations.english: Do you, ere he has passed beyond the Nyagrodha, with flaming arrows destroy the powerful son of Rävaņa along with his car and steeds and charioteer.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेत्युक्त्वा महातेजाः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः
बभूवावस्थितस्तत्र चित्रं विस्फारयन्धनुः
verses.transliteration:
tathetyuktvā mahātejāḥ saumitrirmitranandanaḥ
babhūvāvasthitastatra citraṁ visphārayandhanuḥ

translations.english: Thereupon saying, 'So be it,' the exceedingly energetic son of Sumitrā-that delight of his friends, took up his post there stretching his variegated bow.

verses.sanskrit:
स रथेनाग्निवर्णेन बलवान्रावणात्मजः
इन्द्रजित्कवची खड्गी सध्वजः प्रत्यदृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
sa rathenāgnivarṇena balavānrāvaṇātmajaḥ
indrajitkavacī khaḍgī sadhvajaḥ pratyadṛśyata

translations.english: Ravana's son Indrajit, endowed with strength, mailed, and armed with a sword, and furnished with a banner, was seen mounted on a fire-hued chariot.

verses.sanskrit:
तमुवाच महातेजाः पौलस्त्यमपराजितम्
समाह्वये त्वां समरे सम्यग्युद्धं प्रयच्छ मे
verses.transliteration:
tamuvāca mahātejāḥ paulastyamaparājitam
samāhvaye tvāṁ samare samyagyuddhaṁ prayaccha me

translations.english: The highly powerful Lakşmaņa addressed Pulastya's son never knowing defeat, saying, I challenge you to the encounter. Do you give me battle, exerting your utmost.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो महातेजा मनस्वी रावणात्मजः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं तत्र दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्
verses.transliteration:
evamukto mahātejā manasvī rāvaṇātmajaḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ tatra dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam

translations.english: Thus addressed, the exceedingly energetic and intelligent son of Rāvana, seeing Vibhīşaņa there, spoke to him harshly, thus.

verses.sanskrit:
इह त्वं जातसंवृद्धः साक्षाद्भ्राता पितुर्मम
कथं द्रुह्यसि पुत्रस्य पितृव्यो मम राक्षस
verses.transliteration:
iha tvaṁ jātasaṁvṛddhaḥ sākṣādbhrātā piturmama
kathaṁ druhyasi putrasya pitṛvyo mama rākṣasa

translations.english: Born and bred in this Rākşasa race, you are the very brother of my father Why, O Rākşasa being my uncle, did you range yourself against your son?

verses.sanskrit:
न ज्ञातित्वं न सौहार्दं न जातिस्तव दुर्मते
प्रमाणं न च सोदर्यं न धर्मो धर्मदूषण
verses.transliteration:
na jñātitvaṁ na sauhārdaṁ na jātistava durmate
pramāṇaṁ na ca sodaryaṁ na dharmo dharmadūṣaṇa

translations.english: But neither kinship, nor emity, nor race, O wicked-minded one, nor co-birth, can, destroyer of righteousness, avail to make you discern your duty.

verses.sanskrit:
शोच्यस्त्वमसि दुर्बुद्धे निन्दनीयश्च साधुभिः
यस्त्वं स्वजनमुत्सृज्य परभृत्यत्वमागतः
verses.transliteration:
śocyastvamasi durbuddhe nindanīyaśca sādhubhiḥ
yastvaṁ svajanamutsṛjya parabhṛtyatvamāgataḥ

translations.english: O you of perverse understanding you are indeed to be pitied; as you are worthy of being reproached by the virtuous; since, renouncing your own, you have espoused servitude under another.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतच्छिथिलया बुद्ध्या त्वं वेत्सि महदन्तरम्
क्व च स्वजनसंवासः क्व च नीचपराश्रयः
verses.transliteration:
naitacchithilayā buddhyā tvaṁ vetsi mahadantaram
kva ca svajanasaṁvāsaḥ kva ca nīcaparāśrayaḥ

translations.english: Neither by your character nor yet your understanding did you perceive the mighty difference that Leith between living with one's own kindred, and taking refuge with the base.

verses.sanskrit:
गुणवान्वा परजनः स्वजनो निर्गुणोऽपि वा
निर्गुणः स्वजनः श्रेयान्यः परः पर एव सः
verses.transliteration:
guṇavānvā parajanaḥ svajano nirguṇo'pi vā
nirguṇaḥ svajanaḥ śreyānyaḥ paraḥ para eva saḥ

translations.english: If one that is not our own, be furnished with every grace, and if one's own be void of all merit, one's kindred, albeit unworthy, is preferable; and he that is not ours, is even always such.

verses.sanskrit:
निरनुक्रोशता चेयं यादृशी ते निशाचर
स्वजनेन त्वया शक्यं परुषं रावणानुज
verses.transliteration:
niranukrośatā ceyaṁ yādṛśī te niśācara
svajanena tvayā śakyaṁ paruṣaṁ rāvaṇānuja

translations.english: O night-ranger, such is this your relentlessness, that, O Ravana's younger brother, you being a kindred, are capable of displaying your manliness (as no other person can do so).

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तो भ्रातृपुत्रेण प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः
अजानन्निव मच्छीलं किं राक्षस विकत्थसे
verses.transliteration:
ityukto bhrātṛputreṇa pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
ajānanniva macchīlaṁ kiṁ rākṣasa vikatthase

translations.english: Thus addressed by his brother's son, Vibhis ana answered, “O Raksasa, why did you speak as if in ignorance of my character? O impious son of the Rākşasa chief, do you for ego the roughness which you assume on behalf of my dignity.* *Or, on account of your heroism.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसेन्द्रसुतासाधो पारुष्यं त्यज गौरवात्
कुले यद्यप्यहं जातो रक्षसां क्रूरकर्मणाम्
गुणोऽयं प्रथमो नॄणां तन्मे शीलमराक्षसं
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasendrasutāsādho pāruṣyaṁ tyaja gauravāt
kule yadyapyahaṁ jāto rakṣasāṁ krūrakarmaṇām
guṇo'yaṁ prathamo nṝṇāṁ tanme śīlamarākṣasaṁ

translations.english: Albeit born in the race of Rākşas of cruel deeds, yet having regard to the first of principles pertaining to men, my character is not that of a Rākşasa. I do not take pleasure in the terrible; not do I revel in unrighteousness.” But how can a brother, although differing from his brother in character, be renounced by the latter?* *Some read Vişamasilena. Then the sense would be: 'How else could a brother bearing a difference in character, renounce his brother' meaning Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
परस्वानां च हरणं परदाराभिमर्शनम्
सुहृदामतिशङ्कां च त्रयो दोषाः क्षयावहाः
verses.transliteration:
parasvānāṁ ca haraṇaṁ paradārābhimarśanam
suhṛdāmatiśaṅkāṁ ca trayo doṣāḥ kṣayāvahāḥ

translations.english: Robbing others property, outraging the wives of others, and inspiring fear among friends, these three vices lead to destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
एते दोषा मम भ्रातुर्जीवितैश्वर्यनाशनाः
गुणान्प्रच्छादयामासुः पर्वतानिव तोयदाः
verses.transliteration:
ete doṣā mama bhrāturjīvitaiśvaryanāśanāḥ
guṇānpracchādayāmāsuḥ parvatāniva toyadāḥ

translations.english: The dreadful slaughter of sages, rebellion against all the gods, overweening conceit, anger long-continued enmity, and running amuck of counsel, these sins are sapping the life and fortune of my brother; and they have hidden his virtues even as clouds cover a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः परित्यक्तो मया भ्राता पिता तव
नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न च त्वं न च ते पिता
verses.transliteration:
doṣairetaiḥ parityakto mayā bhrātā pitā tava
neyamasti purī laṅkā na ca tvaṁ na ca te pitā

translations.english: It is on account of these vices that my brother, your sire, has been deserted by me. And this city of Lankā will not be, nor you, nor your father.

verses.sanskrit:
अतिमानी च बालश्च दुर्विनीतश्च राक्षस
बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन ब्रूहि मां यद्यदिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
atimānī ca bālaśca durvinītaśca rākṣasa
baddhastvaṁ kālapāśena brūhi māṁ yadyadicchasi

translations.english: You are proud, and haughty, and a boy, O Raksasa. You are fettered by the noose of Fate. Do you say to me whatever you like.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य ते व्यसनं प्राप्तं किमिह त्वं तु वक्ष्यसि
प्रवेष्टुं न त्वया शक्यो न्यग्रोधो राक्षसाधम
verses.transliteration:
adya te vyasanaṁ prāptaṁ kimiha tvaṁ tu vakṣyasi
praveṣṭuṁ na tvayā śakyo nyagrodho rākṣasādhama

translations.english: To-day you have addressed harshly me, who have fallen on evil days; but, O worst of Raks asas, you cannot pass this Nyagrodha.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्षयित्वा तु काकुत्स्थौ न शक्यं जीवितुं त्वया
युध्यस्व नरदेवेन लक्ष्मणेन रणे सह
हतस्त्वं देवता कार्यं करिष्यसि यमक्षये
verses.transliteration:
dharṣayitvā tu kākutsthau na śakyaṁ jīvituṁ tvayā
yudhyasva naradevena lakṣmaṇena raṇe saha
hatastvaṁ devatā kāryaṁ kariṣyasi yamakṣaye

translations.english: Having smitten the Kākutstha, you cannot live. Fight with that man-god, Laksmana, in encounter. Being slain, you shall serve the deities in the abode of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
निदर्शयस्वात्मबलं समुद्यतं; कुरुष्व सर्वायुधसायकव्ययम्
न लक्ष्मणस्यैत्य हि बाणगोचरं; त्वमद्य जीवन्सबलो गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
nidarśayasvātmabalaṁ samudyataṁ; kuruṣva sarvāyudhasāyakavyayam
na lakṣmaṇasyaitya hi bāṇagocaraṁ; tvamadya jīvansabalo gamiṣyasi

translations.english: Displaying you own prowess, do you spend all your weapons and all your shafts. But coming within the ken of Laksmana's arrows, your will not today go hence, living with your forces.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषण वचः श्रुत्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं वेगेनाभ्युत्पपात ह
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇa vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
abravītparuṣaṁ vākyaṁ vegenābhyutpapāta ha

translations.english: Hearing Vibhisana's words, the son of Ravana, deprived of his senses by passion, spoke harshly, and rushed forward in wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यतायुधनिस्त्रिंशो रथे तु समलंकृते
कालाश्वयुक्ते महति स्थितः कालान्तकोपमः
verses.transliteration:
udyatāyudhanistriṁśo rathe tu samalaṁkṛte
kālāśvayukte mahati sthitaḥ kālāntakopamaḥ

translations.english: With upraised weapons and scimitars, he, resembling the Destroyer himself, was mounted on a mighty car yoked with black steeds, and ornamented (on all sides).

verses.sanskrit:
महाप्रमाणमुद्यम्य विपुलं वेगवद्दृढम्
धनुर्भीमं परामृश्य शरांश्चामित्रनाशनान्
verses.transliteration:
mahāpramāṇamudyamya vipulaṁ vegavaddṛḍham
dhanurbhīmaṁ parāmṛśya śarāṁścāmitranāśanān

translations.english: That one endowed with terrific strength upraised a huge, gigantic, strong and powerful bow, and shafts capable of destroying foes.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य वो मामका बाणा महाकार्मुकनिःसृताः
विधमिष्यन्ति गात्राणि तूलराशिमिवानलः
verses.transliteration:
adya vo māmakā bāṇā mahākārmukaniḥsṛtāḥ
vidhamiṣyanti gātrāṇi tūlarāśimivānalaḥ

translations.english: fo-day my shafts discharged from my mighty bow shall mangle your limbs, even as fire burn up a heap of cotton.

verses.sanskrit:
तीक्ष्णसायकनिर्भिन्नाञ्शूलशक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः
अद्य वो गमयिष्यामि सर्वानेव यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
tīkṣṇasāyakanirbhinnāñśūlaśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ
adya vo gamayiṣyāmi sarvāneva yamakṣayam

translations.english: To-day with your persons pierced with sharp shafts, with darts, and javelins, and Rstis and arrows, Shall I despatch you all to the abode of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षिपतः शरवर्षाणि क्षिप्रहस्तस्य मे युधि
जीमूतस्येव नदतः कः स्थास्यति ममाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
kṣipataḥ śaravarṣāṇi kṣiprahastasya me yudhi
jīmūtasyeva nadataḥ kaḥ sthāsyati mamāgrataḥ

translations.english: Who shall stay before me, fleet-handed, creating an arrows shower in the field, and roaring like to clouds?

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गर्जितं लक्ष्मणस्तदा
अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावणिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā rākṣasendrasya garjitaṁ lakṣmaṇastadā
abhītavadanaḥ kruddho rāvaṇiṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the vaunt of the Rākşasa-chief, Rahgu's son, inflamed with rage, with an undaunted countenance, spoke to Ravana's son.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वमर्थस्य हीनार्थो दुरवापस्य केनचित्
वचो व्याहृत्य जानीषे कृतार्थोऽस्मीति दुर्मते
verses.transliteration:
sa tvamarthasya hīnārtho duravāpasya kenacit
vaco vyāhṛtya jānīṣe kṛtārtho'smīti durmate

translations.english: O Rākşasa, hard is the achievement of the task that you have mentioned. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. But you, O wicked-minded one, incompetent as you are to bring about your end, attaining your arduous aim by words only, deem yourself as crowned with success.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तर्धानगतेनाजौ यस्त्वयाचरितस्तदा
तस्कराचरितो मार्गो नैष वीरनिषेवितः
verses.transliteration:
antardhānagatenājau yastvayācaritastadā
taskarācarito mārgo naiṣa vīraniṣevitaḥ

translations.english: That your had rendered yourself invisible in the field of conflict, was the work of a thief, and not the way of a hero.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा बाणपथं प्राप्य स्थितोऽहं तव राक्षस
दर्शयस्वाद्य तत्तेजो वाचा त्वं किं विकत्थसे
verses.transliteration:
yathā bāṇapathaṁ prāpya sthito'haṁ tava rākṣasa
darśayasvādya tattejo vācā tvaṁ kiṁ vikatthase

translations.english: Coming within the range of your shafts, I stay here, do you display your prowess. What did you say in words.?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो धनुर्भीमं परामृश्य महाबलः
ससर्जे निशितान्बाणानिन्द्रजित्समिजिंजय
verses.transliteration:
evamukto dhanurbhīmaṁ parāmṛśya mahābalaḥ
sasarje niśitānbāṇānindrajitsamijiṁjaya

translations.english: Thus addressed, the mighty IndrajitConqueror of enemies-stretching his dreadful bow, showered sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ते निसृष्टा महावेगाः शराः सर्पविषोपमाः
संप्राप्य लक्ष्मणं पेतुः श्वसन्त इव पन्नगाः
verses.transliteration:
te nisṛṣṭā mahāvegāḥ śarāḥ sarpaviṣopamāḥ
saṁprāpya lakṣmaṇaṁ petuḥ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ

translations.english: And discharged by him, those exceedingly impetuous arrows, resembling the venom of serpents, hitting Laksmana, fell down like to hissing snakes.

verses.sanskrit:
शरैरतिमहावेगैर्वेगवान्रावणात्मजः
सौमित्रिमिन्द्रजिद्युद्धे विव्याध शुभलक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
śarairatimahāvegairvegavānrāvaṇātmajaḥ
saumitrimindrajidyuddhe vivyādha śubhalakṣaṇam

translations.english: In that encounter, Rāvana's son-Indrajit, possessed of eminent impetuosity, pierced Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks, with vehement shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरैरतिविद्धाङ्गो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः
शुशुभे लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान्विधूम इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
sa śarairatividdhāṅgo rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ
śuśubhe lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmānvidhūma iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: And pierced with those arrows and bathed in blood, the graceful Lakşmaņa appeared like a smokeless fire.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनः कर्म प्रसमीक्ष्याधिगम्य च
विनद्य सुमहानादमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
indrajittvātmanaḥ karma prasamīkṣyādhigamya ca
vinadya sumahānādamidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Seeing his own feat, Indrajit, coming forward, and setting up a tremendous cry, said.

verses.sanskrit:
पत्रिणः शितधारास्ते शरा मत्कार्मुकच्युताः
आदास्यन्तेऽद्य सौमित्रे जीवितं जीवितान्तगाः
verses.transliteration:
patriṇaḥ śitadhārāste śarā matkārmukacyutāḥ
ādāsyante'dya saumitre jīvitaṁ jīvitāntagāḥ

translations.english: O son of Sumitrā, my feathered and sharpedged shafts shot from my bow, capable of destroying life, will today finish you up.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य गोमायुसंघाश्च श्येनसंघाश्च लक्ष्मण
गृध्राश्च निपतन्तु त्वां गतासुं निहतं मया
verses.transliteration:
adya gomāyusaṁghāśca śyenasaṁghāśca lakṣmaṇa
gṛdhrāśca nipatantu tvāṁ gatāsuṁ nihataṁ mayā

translations.english: To-day, O Laksmana, swarms of jackals and hosts of hawks and vultures shall alight on you lying lifeless, having been slain by me.

verses.sanskrit:
विशस्तकवचं भूमौ व्यपविद्धशरासनम्
हृतोत्तमाङ्गं सौमित्रे त्वामद्य निहतं मया
verses.transliteration:
viśastakavacaṁ bhūmau vyapaviddhaśarāsanam
hṛtottamāṅgaṁ saumitre tvāmadya nihataṁ mayā

translations.english: This very day shall the exceedingly wicked Råma behold you, who are the friend of Kș atriyas and devoted to your brother, and who ėver bear yourself ignobly, slain by me; today see you, O Sumitra's son, slain by me, with your armour fallen off your person, your bow broken, and your head severed.

verses.sanskrit:
इति ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं परुषं रावणात्मजम्
हेतुमद्वाक्यमत्यर्थं लक्ष्मणः प्रत्युवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
iti bruvāṇaṁ saṁrabdhaṁ paruṣaṁ rāvaṇātmajam
hetumadvākyamatyarthaṁ lakṣmaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha

translations.english: As Ravana's son was speaking thus harshly, Lakşmaņa conversant with the import of words, replied in a reasonable speech, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
अकृत्वा कत्थसे कर्म किमर्थमिह राक्षस
कुरु तत्कर्म येनाहं श्रद्दध्यां तव कत्थनम्
verses.transliteration:
akṛtvā katthase karma kimarthamiha rākṣasa
kuru tatkarma yenāhaṁ śraddadhyāṁ tava katthanam

translations.english: Why, O Raksasa, without doing (what you say), did you simply say it? Do the deed, so that I may have regard for your utterances.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं किंचिदप्यनवक्षिपन्
अविकत्थन्वधिष्यामि त्वां पश्य पुरुषादन
verses.transliteration:
anuktvā paruṣaṁ vākyaṁ kiṁcidapyanavakṣipan
avikatthanvadhiṣyāmi tvāṁ paśya puruṣādana

translations.english: Mark! without speaking anything harsh, without censuring you in the least, without venting any brag, shall, I, O cannibal, slay you.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा पञ्चनाराचानाकर्णापूरिताञ्शरान्
निचखान महावेगाँल्लक्ष्मणो राक्षसोरसि
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā pañcanārācānākarṇāpūritāñśarān
nicakhāna mahāvegā̐llakṣmaṇo rākṣasorasi

translations.english: Saying this, Lakşmaņa drawing his bow to its full bent, hit at the Raksasas chest five nārācas, wondrous impetuous arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
स शरैराहतस्तेन सरोषो रावणात्मजः
सुप्रयुक्तैस्त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रतिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम्
verses.transliteration:
sa śarairāhatastena saroṣo rāvaṇātmajaḥ
suprayuktaistribhirbāṇaiḥ prativivyādha lakṣmaṇam

translations.english: And wounded with those shafts, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, pierced Lakşmaņa with arrows discharged (from his bow).

verses.sanskrit:
स बभूव महाभीमो नरराक्षससिंहयोः
विमर्दस्तुमुलो युद्धे परस्परवधैषिणोः
verses.transliteration:
sa babhūva mahābhīmo nararākṣasasiṁhayoḥ
vimardastumulo yuddhe parasparavadhaiṣiṇoḥ

translations.english: And exceedingly dreadful was the encounter that took place between those leonine man and Rākşasa, each eager to conquer the other.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरं दाशरथिः संधायामित्रकर्शनः
ससर्ज राक्षसेन्द्राय क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śaraṁ dāśarathiḥ saṁdhāyāmitrakarśanaḥ
sasarja rākṣasendrāya kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan

translations.english: Then sighing like an enraged serpent, that chastiser of foes, Dasaratha's son, setting shafts (on his bow-string) showered them on the Raksasa-chief.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं स श्रुत्वा रावणात्मजः
विवर्णवदनो भूत्वा लक्ष्मणं समुदैक्षत
verses.transliteration:
tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṁ sa śrutvā rāvaṇātmajaḥ
vivarṇavadano bhūtvā lakṣmaṇaṁ samudaikṣata

translations.english: And hearing the twang of his bow-string the lord of Rākṣasas, with his countenance fallen, gazed at Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
तं विषण्णमुखं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं रावणात्मजम्
सौमित्रिं युद्धसंसक्तं प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ viṣaṇṇamukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṁ rāvaṇātmajam
saumitriṁ yuddhasaṁsaktaṁ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then Vibhīşaņa spoke to Sumitrā's son as he was fighting, “I find (inauspicious) signs in Rāvana's son.

verses.sanskrit:
निमित्तान्यनुपश्यामि यान्यस्मिन्रावणात्मजे
त्वर तेन महाबाहो भग्न एष न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
nimittānyanupaśyāmi yānyasminrāvaṇātmaje
tvara tena mahābāho bhagna eṣa na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Do therefore hasten on, broken he is, without doubt.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संधाय सौमित्रिः शरानग्निशिखोपमान्
मुमोच निशितांस्तस्मै सर्वानिव विषोल्बणान्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁdhāya saumitriḥ śarānagniśikhopamān
mumoca niśitāṁstasmai sarvāniva viṣolbaṇān

translations.english: Then fixing arrows (on his bow) resembling venomous snakes, he let go those keen shafts, like to serpents furnished with poison.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्राशनिसमस्पर्शैर्लक्ष्मणेनाहतः शरैः
मुहूर्तमभवन्मूढः सर्वसंक्षुभितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
śakrāśanisamasparśairlakṣmaṇenāhataḥ śaraiḥ
muhūrtamabhavanmūḍhaḥ sarvasaṁkṣubhitendriyaḥ

translations.english: And smite by Lakşmaņa with arrows having the touch of the levin, (Indrajit) for a while was stupefied and had his senses overwhelmed.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिचक्राम सौमित्रिं रोषात्संरक्तलोचनः
अब्रवीच्चैनमासाद्य पुनः स परुषं वचः
verses.transliteration:
so'bhicakrāma saumitriṁ roṣātsaṁraktalocanaḥ
abravīccainamāsādya punaḥ sa paruṣaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: And eyeing that heroson to Dasaratha-present in the encounter, (Indrajit) with his eyes crimsoned on choler, drew near Sumitrā's son. And coming up to him (Laksmana), he again addressed (that hero) in a harsh speech, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
किं न स्मरसि तद्युद्धे प्रथमे मत्पराक्रमम्
निबद्धस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा यदा युधि विचेष्टसे
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ na smarasi tadyuddhe prathame matparākramam
nibaddhastvaṁ saha bhrātrā yadā yudhi viceṣṭase

translations.english: Did you not remember my prowess at that first encounter, when you along with your brother was bound up, that now you are discharging arms (at me)? Forsooth you two in mighty encounter, with shafts resembling the thunder-bolt and vajra, by me were first laid down on the ground, deprived of your lives, along with your principal adherents.

verses.sanskrit:
स्मृतिर्वा नास्ति ते मन्ये व्यक्तं वा यमसादनम्
गन्तुमिच्छसि यस्मात्त्वं मां धर्षयितुमिच्छसि
verses.transliteration:
smṛtirvā nāsti te manye vyaktaṁ vā yamasādanam
gantumicchasi yasmāttvaṁ māṁ dharṣayitumicchasi

translations.english: Either this has escaped your memory or I fancy, you plainly act to go to the abode of Yama, inasmuch as you have set your heart on beating me.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ते प्रथमे युद्धे न दृष्टो मत्पराक्रमः
अद्य त्वां दर्शयिष्यामि तिष्ठेदानीं व्यवस्थितः
verses.transliteration:
yadi te prathame yuddhe na dṛṣṭo matparākramaḥ
adya tvāṁ darśayiṣyāmi tiṣṭhedānīṁ vyavasthitaḥ

translations.english: If at the first encounter you have not witnessed my prowess, today shall I show it to you. Do you now stay, summoning your attention.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्त्वा सप्तभिर्बाणैरभिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम्
दशभिश्च हनूमन्तं तीक्ष्णधारैः शरोत्तमैः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktvā saptabhirbāṇairabhivivyādha lakṣmaṇam
daśabhiśca hanūmantaṁ tīkṣṇadhāraiḥ śarottamaiḥ

translations.english: Seeing this, he pierced Lakşmaņa with seven shafts, and Hanumān with ten keen-edged excellent shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरशतेनैव सुप्रयुक्तेन वीर्यवान्
क्रोधाद्द्विगुणसंरब्धो निर्बिभेद विभीषणम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śaraśatenaiva suprayuktena vīryavān
krodhāddviguṇasaṁrabdho nirbibheda vibhīṣaṇam

translations.english: Then, fired with double fury, that powerful one pierced Vibhīşana with an hundred arrows, powerfully discharged (from his weapons.)

verses.sanskrit:
तद्दृष्ट्वेन्द्रजितः कर्म कृतं रामानुजस्तदा
अचिन्तयित्वा प्रहसन्नैतत्किंचिदिति ब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
taddṛṣṭvendrajitaḥ karma kṛtaṁ rāmānujastadā
acintayitvā prahasannaitatkiṁciditi bruvan

translations.english: Seeing this act of Indrajit, that foremost of men, Rama's younger brother, Laksmana, with an undaunted countenance, fired with wrath without minding the same, and saying with a laugh, this is nothing.'

verses.sanskrit:
मुमोच स शरान्घोरान्संगृह्य नरपुंगवः
अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावणिं लक्ष्मणो युधि
verses.transliteration:
mumoca sa śarānghorānsaṁgṛhya narapuṁgavaḥ
abhītavadanaḥ kruddho rāvaṇiṁ lakṣmaṇo yudhi

translations.english: Taking dreadful arrows, in the conflict, discharged them at the son of Ravana. "O nightrangers, heroes, coming to the field never discharge (such shafts as these). These arrows of your are light and of slight strength, and they conduce to my comfort. Heroic warriors eager for encounter, do not fight thus.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवं शूरास्तु युध्यन्ते समरे जयकाङ्क्षिणः
इत्येवं तं ब्रुवाणस्तु शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्
verses.transliteration:
naivaṁ śūrāstu yudhyante samare jayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
ityevaṁ taṁ bruvāṇastu śaravarṣairavākirat

translations.english: Speaking thus, (Laksmana) accoutred with his bow showered vollies of shafts (on his adversary).

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बाणैस्तु विध्वस्तं कवचं हेमभूषितम्
व्यशीर्यत रथोपस्थे ताराजालमिवाम्बरात्
verses.transliteration:
tasya bāṇaistu vidhvastaṁ kavacaṁ hemabhūṣitam
vyaśīryata rathopasthe tārājālamivāmbarāt

translations.english: And at his arrows (hitting), (Indrajit's) mighty golden mail fell off his person, and dropped to the platform of his car like a cluster of stars dropping from the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
विधूतवर्मा नाराचैर्बभूव स कृतव्रणः
इन्द्रजित्समरे शूरः प्ररूढ इव सानुमान्
verses.transliteration:
vidhūtavarmā nārācairbabhūva sa kṛtavraṇaḥ
indrajitsamare śūraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān

translations.english: With his armour dropping off, that hero— Indrajit was wounded with nárachas, like the Sun at dawn.

verses.sanskrit:
अभीक्ष्णं निश्वसन्तौ हि युध्येतां तुमुलं युधि
शरसंकृत्तसर्वाङ्गो सर्वतो रुधिरोक्षितौ
verses.transliteration:
abhīkṣṇaṁ niśvasantau hi yudhyetāṁ tumulaṁ yudhi
śarasaṁkṛttasarvāṅgo sarvato rudhirokṣitau

translations.english: And sighing again and again, they faught furiously. And with their persons cut all over, and laved in blood, for a long while the heroes kept cleaving each other with sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्राण्यस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठौ दर्शयन्तौ पुनः पुनः
शरानुच्चावचाकारानन्तरिक्षे बबन्धतुः
verses.transliteration:
astrāṇyastravidāṁ śreṣṭhau darśayantau punaḥ punaḥ
śarānuccāvacākārānantarikṣe babandhatuḥ

translations.english: Those foremost of those acquainted with weapons repeatedly displayed their weapons; and their long and short shafts enveloped the welkin.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यपेतदोषमस्यन्तौ लघुचित्रं च सुष्ठु च
उभौ तु तुमुलं घोरं चक्रतुर्नरराक्षसौ
verses.transliteration:
vyapetadoṣamasyantau laghucitraṁ ca suṣṭhu ca
ubhau tu tumulaṁ ghoraṁ cakraturnararākṣasau

translations.english: The skill that they displayed was perfect, and showed lightness, variety and grace; and both man and the Rākşasa carried on fearful and terrible conflict.

verses.sanskrit:
ते गात्रयोर्निपतिता रुक्मपुङ्खाः शरा युधि
असृग्दिग्धा विनिष्पेतुर्विविशुर्धरणीतलम्
verses.transliteration:
te gātrayornipatitā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śarā yudhi
asṛgdigdhā viniṣpeturviviśurdharaṇītalam

translations.english: in that engagement gold-knobbed shafts hitting each other's person, pierced the same and covered with gore, entered the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्यैः सुनिशितैः शस्त्रैराकाशे संजघट्टिरे
बभञ्जुश्चिच्छिदुश्चापि तयोर्बाणाः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
anyaiḥ suniśitaiḥ śastrairākāśe saṁjaghaṭṭire
babhañjuścicchiduścāpi tayorbāṇāḥ sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: And other shafts were resisted in the sky by sharpened weapons, and some were snapped, and thousands of their arrows were cleft (in the sky).

verses.sanskrit:
स बभूव रणे घोरस्तयोर्बाणमयश्चयः
अग्निभ्यामिव दीप्ताभ्यां सत्रे कुशमयश्चयः
verses.transliteration:
sa babhūva raṇe ghorastayorbāṇamayaścayaḥ
agnibhyāmiva dīptābhyāṁ satre kuśamayaścayaḥ

translations.english: In that field, the vollies of their shafts were dreadful to behold like to a heap of Kusa aflame in a sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः कृतव्रणौ देहौ शुशुभाते महात्मनोः
सपुष्पाविव निष्पत्रौ वने शाल्मलिकुंशुकौ
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ kṛtavraṇau dehau śuśubhāte mahātmanoḥ
sapuṣpāviva niṣpatrau vane śālmalikuṁśukau

translations.english: The wounded frames of those high-souled ones appeared beautiful like a leafless flowering Kinsuka and Sālmali in wood.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं घोरं संनिपातं मुहुर्मुहुः
इन्द्रजिल्लक्ष्मणश्चैव परस्परजयैषिणौ
verses.transliteration:
cakratustumulaṁ ghoraṁ saṁnipātaṁ muhurmuhuḥ
indrajillakṣmaṇaścaiva parasparajayaiṣiṇau

translations.english: Each eager to vanquish the other, Indrajit and Lakşmaņa momentarily discharged tremendous and terrific showers (of arms).

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणो रावणिं युद्धे रावणिश्चापि लक्ष्मणम्
अन्योन्यं तावभिघ्नन्तौ न श्रमं प्रत्यपद्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇiṁ yuddhe rāvaṇiścāpi lakṣmaṇam
anyonyaṁ tāvabhighnantau na śramaṁ pratyapadyatām

translations.english: Laksmana smiting Ravana's son, and Ravana's son smiting Lakşmaņa, they did not experience any fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
बाणजालैः शरीरस्थैरवगाढैस्तरस्विनौ
शुशुभाते महावीरौ विरूढाविव पर्वतौ
verses.transliteration:
bāṇajālaiḥ śarīrasthairavagāḍhaistarasvinau
śuśubhāte mahāvīrau virūḍhāviva parvatau

translations.english: With net-works of arrows deeply entering their persons, those vehement and exceedingly powerful ones resembled mountains topped (with trees).

verses.sanskrit:
तयो रुधिरसिक्तानि संवृतानि शरैर्भृशम्
बभ्राजुः सर्वगात्राणि ज्वलन्त इव पावकाः
verses.transliteration:
tayo rudhirasiktāni saṁvṛtāni śarairbhṛśam
babhrājuḥ sarvagātrāṇi jvalanta iva pāvakāḥ

translations.english: All their limbs, drenched in blood and covered with arrows, looked like a blazing fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोरथ महान्कालो व्यतीयाद्युध्यमानयोः
न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं वाप्युपजग्मतुः
verses.transliteration:
tayoratha mahānkālo vyatīyādyudhyamānayoḥ
na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṁ śramaṁ vāpyupajagmatuḥ

translations.english: A long time went by as they faught. Not did they turn away from the encounter, or know fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ समरपरिश्रमं निहन्तुं; समरमुखेष्वजितस्य लक्ष्मणस्य
प्रियहितमुपपादयन्महौजाः; समरमुपेत्य विभीषणोऽवतस्थे
verses.transliteration:
atha samarapariśramaṁ nihantuṁ; samaramukheṣvajitasya lakṣmaṇasya
priyahitamupapādayanmahaujāḥ; samaramupetya vibhīṣaṇo'vatasthe

translations.english: Then to remove (Laksmana's) fatigue from fight, the high-souled Vibhisana, working the weal of Laksmaņa staying in front of the field, came forward in the encounter and took up his post.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यमानौ तु तौ दृष्ट्वा प्रसक्तौ नरराक्षसौ
शूरः स रावणभ्राता तस्थौ संग्राममूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
yudhyamānau tu tau dṛṣṭvā prasaktau nararākṣasau
śūraḥ sa rāvaṇabhrātā tasthau saṁgrāmamūrdhani

translations.english: Seeing the man and the Rākṣasa engaged in battle, with their whole soul, each eager to beat the other, like to elephants with the temporal juice trickling from their temples, desirous of beholding their encounter, Răvaņa's mighty and heroic brother, bearing an excellent bow, stood in front of the arena.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विस्फारयामास महद्धनुरवस्थितः
उत्ससर्ज च तीक्ष्णाग्रान्राक्षसेषु महाशरान्
verses.transliteration:
tato visphārayāmāsa mahaddhanuravasthitaḥ
utsasarja ca tīkṣṇāgrānrākṣaseṣu mahāśarān

translations.english: Taking up his post, he stretched his great bow and shot terrific sharp-pointed shafts at the Rāks asas.

verses.sanskrit:
ते शराः शिखिसंकाशा निपतन्तः समाहिताः
राक्षसान्दारयामासुर्वज्रा इव महागिरीन्
verses.transliteration:
te śarāḥ śikhisaṁkāśā nipatantaḥ samāhitāḥ
rākṣasāndārayāmāsurvajrā iva mahāgirīn

translations.english: Even like thunder-bolt cleaving mighty mountains, those shafts furnished with peacock's plumes falling powerfully (upon the foe), rent the Raksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्यानुचरास्तेऽपि शूलासिपट्टसैः
चिच्छेदुः समरे वीरान्राक्षसान्राक्षसोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇasyānucarāste'pi śūlāsipaṭṭasaiḥ
ciccheduḥ samare vīrānrākṣasānrākṣasottamāḥ

translations.english: Those foremost of Raksasas, Vibhisana's followers, also in the encounter discharged darts and scimitars and pațțiśas at heroic Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसैस्तैः परिवृतः स तदा तु विभीषणः
बभौ मध्ये प्रहृष्टानां कलभानामिव द्विपः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasaistaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa tadā tu vibhīṣaṇaḥ
babhau madhye prahṛṣṭānāṁ kalabhānāmiva dvipaḥ

translations.english: Surrounded by those Raksasas, Vibhisana, then in the midst of his followers, appeared like an elephant in the midst of young ones.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः संचोदयानो वै हरीन्रक्षोरणप्रियान्
उवाच वचनं काले कालज्ञो रक्षसां वरः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ saṁcodayāno vai harīnrakṣoraṇapriyān
uvāca vacanaṁ kāle kālajño rakṣasāṁ varaḥ

translations.english: Then inciting the monkeys, whose dear object was to slay Ravana, that one versed in time, the foremost of Rākşasas,spoke seasonably thus.

verses.sanskrit:
एकोऽयं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य परायणमिव स्थितः
एतच्छेषं बलं तस्य किं तिष्ठत हरीश्वराः
verses.transliteration:
eko'yaṁ rākṣasendrasya parāyaṇamiva sthitaḥ
etaccheṣaṁ balaṁ tasya kiṁ tiṣṭhata harīśvarāḥ

translations.english: This one that stay (in the field) is the sole and mighty support of the Raksasa-chief; and this is his remaining force. Why then do the monkeychiefs remain inactive? On this wicked Rāksasa being slain on the edge of battle, the remnant of his army, with the single exception of Rāvawa, is destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
एतान्निहत्यातिबलान्बहून्राक्षससत्तमान्
बाहुभ्यां सागरं तीर्त्वा लङ्घ्यतां गोष्पदं लघु
verses.transliteration:
etānnihatyātibalānbahūnrākṣasasattamān
bāhubhyāṁ sāgaraṁ tīrtvā laṅghyatāṁ goṣpadaṁ laghu

translations.english: Having slain these many powerful Rākşasas endowed with excess of might, having crossed the sea with your arms, do you cross this foot print of a cow.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावदिह शेषं वो जेतव्यमिह वानराः
हताः सर्वे समागम्य राक्षसा बलदर्पिताः
verses.transliteration:
etāvadiha śeṣaṁ vo jetavyamiha vānarāḥ
hatāḥ sarve samāgamya rākṣasā baladarpitāḥ

translations.english: This is the remaining force which you monkeys must conquer; all those Rākşasas, that had come forward, elated with the pride of strength, have all been slain.

verses.sanskrit:
अयुक्तं निधनं कर्तुं पुत्रस्य जनितुर्मम
घृणामपास्य रामार्थे निहन्यां भ्रातुरात्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
ayuktaṁ nidhanaṁ kartuṁ putrasya janiturmama
ghṛṇāmapāsya rāmārthe nihanyāṁ bhrāturātmajam

translations.english: It is not meet for me to slay the son of my brother, yet, casting off compassion will I for Rama slay him.* *The text has 'brother's son.'

verses.sanskrit:
हन्तुकामस्य मे बाष्पं चक्शुश्चैव निरुध्यते
तदेवैष महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणः शमयिष्यति
वानरा घ्नन्तुं संभूय भृत्यानस्य समीपगान्
verses.transliteration:
hantukāmasya me bāṣpaṁ cakśuścaiva nirudhyate
tadevaiṣa mahābāhurlakṣmaṇaḥ śamayiṣyati
vānarā ghnantuṁ saṁbhūya bhṛtyānasya samīpagān

translations.english: Tears surcharge the eyes of me who seek to slay him. Let therefore Lakşmaņa administer him his quietus.

verses.sanskrit:
इति तेनातियशसा राक्षसेनाभिचोदिताः
वानरेन्द्रा जहृषिरे लाङ्गलानि च विव्यधुः
verses.transliteration:
iti tenātiyaśasā rākṣasenābhicoditāḥ
vānarendrā jahṛṣire lāṅgalāni ca vivyadhuḥ

translations.english: You monkeys, do you in a body (first) slaughter those that are beside him (Indrajit.)" Thus exhorted by that illustrious Rākşasa, the monkey-chiefs, were exhilarated and began to flourish their tails.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते कपिशार्दूलाः क्ष्वेडन्तश्च मुहुर्मुहुः
मुमुचुर्विविधान्नादान्मेघान्दृष्ट्वेव बर्हिणः
verses.transliteration:
tataste kapiśārdūlāḥ kṣveḍantaśca muhurmuhuḥ
mumucurvividhānnādānmeghāndṛṣṭveva barhiṇaḥ

translations.english: Then those mighty monkeys roared again and again, and sent up various shouts, even as peacocks cry on seeing clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
जाम्बवानपि तैः सर्वैः स्वयूथैरभिसंवृतः
अश्मभिस्ताडयामास नखैर्दन्तैश्च राक्षसान्
verses.transliteration:
jāmbavānapi taiḥ sarvaiḥ svayūthairabhisaṁvṛtaḥ
aśmabhistāḍayāmāsa nakhairdantaiśca rākṣasān

translations.english: Then Jämbavān surrounded by his own forces, assailed the Raksasas with rocks-and with their nails and teeth.

verses.sanskrit:
शरैः परशुभिस्तीक्ष्णैः पट्टसैर्यष्टितोमरैः
जाम्बवन्तं मृधे जघ्नुर्निघ्नन्तं राक्षसीं चमूम्
verses.transliteration:
śaraiḥ paraśubhistīkṣṇaiḥ paṭṭasairyaṣṭitomaraiḥ
jāmbavantaṁ mṛdhe jaghnurnighnantaṁ rākṣasīṁ camūm

translations.english: Thereat Räkşasas, endowed with exceeding strength, equipped with various weapons reproaching the lord of bears, as he was engaged in smiting (the foe), and renouncing fear, with shafts and sharp axes and pațțiśas and yaşțis, and tomaras, in the encounter assailed Jambavān, who was engaged in beating the Räkşasa forces.

verses.sanskrit:
स संप्रहारस्तुमुलः संजज्ञे कपिराक्षसाम्
देवासुराणां क्रुद्धानां यथा भीमो महास्वनः
verses.transliteration:
sa saṁprahārastumulaḥ saṁjajñe kapirākṣasām
devāsurāṇāṁ kruddhānāṁ yathā bhīmo mahāsvanaḥ

translations.english: That conflict between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, waxed furious, like to the tumultuous encounter of the immortals and the Asuras fired with wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
हनूमानपि संक्रुद्धः सालमुत्पाट्य पर्वतात्
रक्षसां कदनं चक्रे समासाद्य सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
hanūmānapi saṁkruddhaḥ sālamutpāṭya parvatāt
rakṣasāṁ kadanaṁ cakre samāsādya sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: The magnanimous Hanumān incapable of being approached growing wroth, uprooting a mountain, and putting down Lakşmaņa from his back, began a great carnage among the Rākşasas by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
स दत्त्वा तुमुलं युद्धं पितृव्यस्येन्द्रजिद्युधि
लक्ष्मणं परवीरघ्नं पुनरेवाभ्यधावत
verses.transliteration:
sa dattvā tumulaṁ yuddhaṁ pitṛvyasyendrajidyudhi
lakṣmaṇaṁ paravīraghnaṁ punarevābhyadhāvata

translations.english: And fighting a furious fight with his uncle, the powerful Indrajit, slayer of hostile heroesagain rushed against Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
अभीक्ष्णमन्तर्दधतुः शरजालैर्महाबलौ
चन्द्रादित्याविवोष्णान्ते यथा मेघैस्तरस्विनौ
verses.transliteration:
abhīkṣṇamantardadhatuḥ śarajālairmahābalau
candrādityāvivoṣṇānte yathā meghaistarasvinau

translations.english: Then there took place an encounter between those heroes in the field, Laksmana and the Räksasa-discharging vollies of shafts and smiting each other; and those mighty and impetuous ones repeatedly covered each other with networks of arrows; like to the sun and the moon covered by clouds at the expiration of Summer.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यादानं न संधानं धनुषो वा परिग्रहः
न विप्रमोक्षो बाणानां न विकर्षो न विग्रहः
verses.transliteration:
na hyādānaṁ na saṁdhānaṁ dhanuṣo vā parigrahaḥ
na vipramokṣo bāṇānāṁ na vikarṣo na vigrahaḥ

translations.english: And on account of their light-handedness, neither discharge of arrows, nor the drawing of the bow; nor the setting of the shaft on the bowstring; not the taking of the bow; nor the selection of shafts; nor the clenching fast of their fists; nor the hitting of aims, could be perceived as they faught on.

verses.sanskrit:
चापवेगप्रमुक्तैश्च बाणजालैः समन्ततः
अन्तरिक्षेऽभिसंछन्ने न रूपाणि चकाशिरे
तमसा पिहितं सर्वमासीद्भीमतरं महत्
verses.transliteration:
cāpavegapramuktaiśca bāṇajālaiḥ samantataḥ
antarikṣe'bhisaṁchanne na rūpāṇi cakāśire
tamasā pihitaṁ sarvamāsīdbhīmataraṁ mahat

translations.english: In consequence of the sky being covered with networks of arrows all around, discharged powerfully from their bows, the forms (of objects) could not be discovered.

verses.sanskrit:
न तदानीं ववौ वायुर्न जज्वाल च पावकः
स्वस्त्यस्तु लोकेभ्य इति जजल्पश्च महर्षयः
संपेतुश्चात्र संप्राप्ता गन्धर्वाः सह चारणैः
verses.transliteration:
na tadānīṁ vavau vāyurna jajvāla ca pāvakaḥ
svastyastu lokebhya iti jajalpaśca maharṣayaḥ
saṁpetuścātra saṁprāptā gandharvāḥ saha cāraṇaiḥ

translations.english: The Maharsis said, 'Fair befell creatures.' And the Gandharvas along with the Cāranas grew exceedingly agitated.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ राक्षससिंहस्य कृष्णान्कनकभूषणान्
शरैश्चतुर्भिः सौमित्रिर्विव्याध चतुरो हयान्
verses.transliteration:
atha rākṣasasiṁhasya kṛṣṇānkanakabhūṣaṇān
śaraiścaturbhiḥ saumitrirvivyādha caturo hayān

translations.english: Then Sumitrā's son pierced the four black steeds of the leonine Räksasa, caparisoned in gold.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन सूतस्य विचरिष्यतः
लाघवाद्राघवः श्रीमाञ्शिरः कायादपाहरत्
verses.transliteration:
tato'pareṇa bhallena sūtasya vicariṣyataḥ
lāghavādrāghavaḥ śrīmāñśiraḥ kāyādapāharat

translations.english: Then he hit at (Indrajit's) charioteer with another yellow and sharpened javelin splendid, furnished with feathers; and resembling the thunder-bolt of the great Indra. And through his fleet handedness the graceful son of Raghu with the thunder-bolt of his shaft, resonant with the sound of his palm, separated the (charioteer's head) from his trunk.

verses.sanskrit:
निहतं सारथिं दृष्ट्वा समरे रावणात्मजः
प्रजहौ समरोद्धर्षं विषण्णः स बभूव ह
verses.transliteration:
nihataṁ sārathiṁ dṛṣṭvā samare rāvaṇātmajaḥ
prajahau samaroddharṣaṁ viṣaṇṇaḥ sa babhūva ha

translations.english: Seeing his charioteer slain in the contest, Rāvana's son forewent his martial ardour, and was cast down.

verses.sanskrit:
विषण्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं हरियूथपाः
ततः परमसंहृष्टो लक्ष्मणं चाभ्यपूजयन्
verses.transliteration:
viṣaṇṇavadanaṁ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṁ hariyūthapāḥ
tataḥ paramasaṁhṛṣṭo lakṣmaṇaṁ cābhyapūjayan

translations.english: Seeing the Rākşasa with his face fallen, the leaders of monkey-hands, were exceedingly delighted and rendered homage to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रमाथी शरभो रभसो गन्धमादनः
अमृष्यमाणाश्चत्वारश्चक्रुर्वेगं हरीश्वराः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pramāthī śarabho rabhaso gandhamādanaḥ
amṛṣyamāṇāścatvāraścakrurvegaṁ harīśvarāḥ

translations.english: Then those monkey-chiefs— Pramāthi, Rabhasa, Sarabha and Gandamādana, not brooking (their foe) summoned their impetuosity.

verses.sanskrit:
ते चास्य हयमुख्येषु तूर्णमुत्पत्य वानराः
चतुर्षु सुमहावीर्या निपेतुर्भीमविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration:
te cāsya hayamukhyeṣu tūrṇamutpatya vānarāḥ
caturṣu sumahāvīryā nipeturbhīmavikramāḥ

translations.english: And suddenly springing up, those highly powerful monkeys endowed with terrific prowess descended upon those four best of steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषामधिष्ठितानां तैर्वानरैः पर्वतोपमैः
मुखेभ्यो रुधिरं व्यक्तं हयानां समवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmadhiṣṭhitānāṁ tairvānaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ
mukhebhyo rudhiraṁ vyaktaṁ hayānāṁ samavartata

translations.english: On those chargers being assailed by those monkeys resembling mountains, blood gushed out of their mouths.

verses.sanskrit:
ते निहत्य हयांस्तस्य प्रमथ्य च महारथम्
पुनरुत्पत्य वेगेन तस्थुर्लक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः
verses.transliteration:
te nihatya hayāṁstasya pramathya ca mahāratham
punarutpatya vegena tasthurlakṣmaṇapārśvataḥ

translations.english: Then the steeds were smashed and sent to the ground. And having slain the steeds, and smitten the mighty car-warrior,* again by a vehement bound, came to the side of Laksmana. *Maharatham (ac.) may also mean mighty car. By the way the samasa or junction called Tatpurusha is a frequent source of obscurity in Sanskrit specially where the gender of the word without samása is the same with that of the thing signified by the samāsa, as in this case.

verses.sanskrit:
स हताश्वादवप्लुत्य रथान्मथितसारथेः
शरवर्षेण सौमित्रिमभ्यधावत रावणिः
verses.transliteration:
sa hatāśvādavaplutya rathānmathitasāratheḥ
śaravarṣeṇa saumitrimabhyadhāvata rāvaṇiḥ

translations.english: Springing down from his car whose steeds had been slain, Ravana's son, his charioteer having been pounded, charged the son of Sumitra with arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महेन्द्रप्रतिमः स लक्ष्मणः; पदातिनं तं निशितैः शरोत्तमैः
सृजन्तमादौ निशिताञ्शरोत्तमा;न्भृशं तदा बाणगणैर्न्यवारयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato mahendrapratimaḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ; padātinaṁ taṁ niśitaiḥ śarottamaiḥ
sṛjantamādau niśitāñśarottamā;nbhṛśaṁ tadā bāṇagaṇairnyavārayat

translations.english: Then Lakşmaņa resembling the great Indra, on (Indrajit's) best of chargers having been despatched, in the encounter began to terribly rive with arrows discharged (his foe) footing on the earth and showering excellent sharpened shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
स हताश्वो महातेजा भूमौ तिष्ठन्निशाचरः
इन्द्रजित्परमक्रुद्धः संप्रजज्वाल तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
sa hatāśvo mahātejā bhūmau tiṣṭhanniśācaraḥ
indrajitparamakruddhaḥ saṁprajajvāla tejasā

translations.english: Having his steeds slain, the night-rangerIndrajit, standing on the ground, waxing fiercely angered, flamed up in energy.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ धन्विनौ जिघांसन्तावन्योन्यमिषुभिर्भृशम्
विजयेनाभिनिष्क्रान्तौ वने गजवृषाविव
verses.transliteration:
tau dhanvinau jighāṁsantāvanyonyamiṣubhirbhṛśam
vijayenābhiniṣkrāntau vane gajavṛṣāviva

translations.english: And armed with bows, they, desirous of slaying each other with shafts resembled an elephant and a bull in a forest, came out for securing victory in encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
निबर्हयन्तश्चान्योन्यं ते राक्षसवनौकसः
भर्तारं न जहुर्युद्धे संपतन्तस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
nibarhayantaścānyonyaṁ te rākṣasavanaukasaḥ
bhartāraṁ na jahuryuddhe saṁpatantastatastataḥ

translations.english: And slaughtering one another the Rākşasas and the wood-rangers, rushing this way and that, did not (for a moment) leave their lords.

verses.sanskrit:
स लक्ष्मणं समुद्दिश्य परं लाघवमास्थितः
ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि वर्षाणीव पुरंदरः
verses.transliteration:
sa lakṣmaṇaṁ samuddiśya paraṁ lāghavamāsthitaḥ
vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi varṣāṇīva puraṁdaraḥ

translations.english: Then aiming at Lakşmaņa, he, summoning his utmost celerity, showered arrows, as shower Purandara in the season of rains.

verses.sanskrit:
मुक्तमिन्द्रजिता तत्तु शरवर्षमरिंदमः
अवारयदसंभ्रान्तो लक्ष्मणः सुदुरासदम्
verses.transliteration:
muktamindrajitā tattu śaravarṣamariṁdamaḥ
avārayadasaṁbhrānto lakṣmaṇaḥ sudurāsadam

translations.english: Thereat Laksmana, subduer of enemies, retaining his calmness, resisted that powerful arrows shower shot by Indrajit.

verses.sanskrit:
अभेद्यकचनं मत्वा लक्ष्मणं रावणात्मजः
ललाटे लक्ष्मणं बाणैः सुपुङ्खैस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित्
अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धः शीघ्रमस्त्रं प्रदर्शयन्
verses.transliteration:
abhedyakacanaṁ matvā lakṣmaṇaṁ rāvaṇātmajaḥ
lalāṭe lakṣmaṇaṁ bāṇaiḥ supuṅkhaistribhirindrajit
avidhyatparamakruddhaḥ śīghramastraṁ pradarśayan

translations.english: Thereat considering Lakşmaņa as clad in an impenetrable armour, Ravana's son-Indrajitgrowing furiously enraged, displaying his lighthanedness in arms, pierced Lakşmaņa in the temples with three well-knobbed shafts. And with those arrows lodged in his temples, Raghu's son, delighting in battle, appeared beautiful in the field like a mountain furnished with three summits.

verses.sanskrit:
स तथाप्यर्दितो बाणै राक्षसेन महामृधे
तमाशु प्रतिविव्याध लक्ष्मणः पनभिः शरैः
verses.transliteration:
sa tathāpyardito bāṇai rākṣasena mahāmṛdhe
tamāśu prativivyādha lakṣmaṇaḥ panabhiḥ śaraiḥ

translations.english: Albeit thus smitten in the contest by the Rākşa with shafts, Lakşmaņa swiftly smote him in turn with five arrows; and in the encounter Lakşmaņa drawing his bow, pierced with shafts Indrajit's face graced with elegant ear-rings.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौ वीरौ महाबलशरासनौ
अन्योन्यं जघ्नतुर्बाणैर्विशिखैर्भीमविक्रमौ
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇendrajitau vīrau mahābalaśarāsanau
anyonyaṁ jaghnaturbāṇairviśikhairbhīmavikramau

translations.english: And those heroes-Lakşmaņa and Indrajitequipped with exceedingly powerful bows, and endowed with heroism and dreadful prowess, wounded each other with sharp arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ परस्परमभ्येत्य सर्वगात्रेषु धन्विनौ
घोरैर्विव्यधतुर्बाणैः कृतभावावुभौ जये
verses.transliteration:
tau parasparamabhyetya sarvagātreṣu dhanvinau
ghorairvivyadhaturbāṇaiḥ kṛtabhāvāvubhau jaye

translations.english: And approaching each other, those bowmen, each setting his heart on victory, wounded each other all over the body with terrific shafts.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मै दृढतरं क्रुद्धो हताश्वाय विभीषणः
वज्रस्पर्शसमान्पञ्च ससर्जोरसि मार्गणान्
verses.transliteration:
tasmai dṛḍhataraṁ kruddho hatāśvāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
vajrasparśasamānpañca sasarjorasi mārgaṇān

translations.english: And Vibhîşana of a tough bow, growing enraged, discharged at (Indrajit), who had his steeds slain, five speeding shafts having the touch of the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तस्य कायं निर्भिद्य रुक्मपुङ्खा निमित्तगाः
बभूवुर्लोहितादिग्धा रक्ता इव महोरगाः
verses.transliteration:
te tasya kāyaṁ nirbhidya rukmapuṅkhā nimittagāḥ
babhūvurlohitādigdhā raktā iva mahoragāḥ

translations.english: And those arrows furnished with gold at the feathered parts, riving his person, were bathed in blood, and resembled mighty red serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
स पितृव्यस्य संक्रुद्ध इन्द्रजिच्छरमाददे
उत्तमं रक्षसां मध्ये यमदत्तं महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
sa pitṛvyasya saṁkruddha indrajiccharamādade
uttamaṁ rakṣasāṁ madhye yamadattaṁ mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thereat wroth with his uncle, Indrajit took up an excellent shaft-bestowed on him by Yama himself-endowed with terrific force, the flower of shafts among all the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
कुबेरेण स्वयं स्वप्ने यद्दत्तममितात्मना
दुर्जयं दुर्विषह्यं च सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration:
kubereṇa svayaṁ svapne yaddattamamitātmanā
durjayaṁ durviṣahyaṁ ca sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ

translations.english: Seeing that mighty shaft set by him (on the bow-string), the highly powerful Laksmana, possessed of dreadful prowess, (in his turn) took up another arrow, bestowed by Kuvera himself of imme jurable soul in a dream, unconquerable, and incapable of being borne even by the celestials and Asuras with Indra at their head.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यां तौ धनुषि श्रेष्ठे संहितौ सायकोत्तमौ
विकृष्यमाणौ वीराभ्यां भृशं जज्वलतुः श्रिया
verses.transliteration:
tābhyāṁ tau dhanuṣi śreṣṭhe saṁhitau sāyakottamau
vikṛṣyamāṇau vīrābhyāṁ bhṛśaṁ jajvalatuḥ śriyā

translations.english: On those foremost of shafts set on those excellent bows of those heroes, being drawn, flamed up in exceeding splendour.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ भासयन्तावाकाशं धनुर्भ्यां विशिखौ च्युतौ
मुखेन मुखमाहत्य संनिपेततुरोजसा
verses.transliteration:
tau bhāsayantāvākāśaṁ dhanurbhyāṁ viśikhau cyutau
mukhena mukhamāhatya saṁnipetaturojasā

translations.english: Those flaming arrows, discharged from the bows, illumining the welkin, with vehemence struck at each others head.

verses.sanskrit:
तौ महाग्रहसंकाशावन्योन्यं संनिपत्य च
संग्रामे शतधा यातौ मेदिन्यां विनिपेततुः
verses.transliteration:
tau mahāgrahasaṁkāśāvanyonyaṁ saṁnipatya ca
saṁgrāme śatadhā yātau medinyāṁ vinipetatuḥ

translations.english: And dashing against each other like to mighty planets, they, reduced to an hundred shivers in the encounter, saught the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
शरौ प्रतिहतौ दृष्ट्वा तावुभौ रणमूर्धनि
व्रीडितो जातरोषौ च लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितावुभौ
verses.transliteration:
śarau pratihatau dṛṣṭvā tāvubhau raṇamūrdhani
vrīḍito jātaroṣau ca lakṣmaṇendrajitāvubhau

translations.english: Seeing their shafts baffled, Indrajit and Laks mana, staying on the edge of the battie, were seized with shame and wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
सुसंरब्धस्तु सौमित्रिरस्त्रं वारुणमाददे
रौद्रं महेद्रजिद्युद्धे व्यसृजद्युधि विष्ठितः
verses.transliteration:
susaṁrabdhastu saumitrirastraṁ vāruṇamādade
raudraṁ mahedrajidyuddhe vyasṛjadyudhi viṣṭhitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat Sumitra's son, flying into a fury, took up a Vāruņa weapon. And the conqueror of the great Indra intent on battle, in the encounter discharged a terrific Raudra weapon; and the exceedingly wonderful Văruņa weapon was baffled by him.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः सुतुमुलं युद्धं संबभूवाद्भुतोपमम्
गगनस्थानि भूतानि लक्ष्मणं पर्यवारयन्
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ sutumulaṁ yuddhaṁ saṁbabhūvādbhutopamam
gaganasthāni bhūtāni lakṣmaṇaṁ paryavārayan

translations.english: The encounter that took place between them was wonderful and capable of making people's down stand on end. And beings stationed in the sky surrounded Lakşmaņa on all sides.

verses.sanskrit:
भैरवाभिरुते भीमे युद्धे वानरराक्षसाम्
भूतैर्बहुभिराकाशं विस्मितैरावृतं बभौ
verses.transliteration:
bhairavābhirute bhīme yuddhe vānararākṣasām
bhūtairbahubhirākāśaṁ vismitairāvṛtaṁ babhau

translations.english: In that terrific encounter of the monkeys and the Rākşasas resounding with dreadful roars, the welkin was covered with innumerable beings seized with wonderment.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषयः पितरो देवा गन्धर्वा गरुणोरगाः
शतक्रतुं पुरस्कृत्य ररक्षुर्लक्ष्मणं रणे
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā gandharvā garuṇoragāḥ
śatakratuṁ puraskṛtya rarakṣurlakṣmaṇaṁ raṇe
