verses.transliteration:
abhyaṣiñcannaravyāghraṁ prasannena sugandhinā
salilena sahasrākṣaṁ vasavo vāsavaṁ yathā

translations.english: Vasistha, Vijaya, Jabali, Katyayana, Gautama and Vāmadeva, sprinkled that foremost of men, with clear and fragrant water as Vasus did the thousand eyed Vasava.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋत्विग्भिर्ब्राह्मणैः पूर्वं कन्याभिर्मन्त्रिभिस्तथा
योधैश्चैवाभ्यषिञ्चंस्ते संप्रहृष्टाः सनैगमैः
verses.transliteration:
ṛtvigbhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ pūrvaṁ kanyābhirmantribhistathā
yodhaiścaivābhyaṣiñcaṁste saṁprahṛṣṭāḥ sanaigamaiḥ

translations.english: Ministers, soldiers and the merchants all delighted. (Thereupon with the juice of Oshadhis (he was sprinkled by) the celestials stationed in the sky, the deities presiding over four quarters and all other celestials collected.

verses.sanskrit:
छत्रं तस्य च जग्राह शत्रुघ्नः पाण्डुरं शुभम्
श्वेतं च वालव्यजनं सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः
अपरं चन्द्रसंकाशं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
chatraṁ tasya ca jagrāha śatrughnaḥ pāṇḍuraṁ śubham
śvetaṁ ca vālavyajanaṁ sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
aparaṁ candrasaṁkāśaṁ rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Śatrughna held the white and excellent umbrella and Sugrīva the lord of monkeys took the white Chowrie. And Vibhīşaņa the lord of Rákşasas took up another Chowrie resembling the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
मालां ज्वलन्तीं वपुषा काञ्चनीं शतपुष्कराम्
राघवाय ददौ वायुर्वासवेन प्रचोदितः
verses.transliteration:
mālāṁ jvalantīṁ vapuṣā kāñcanīṁ śatapuṣkarām
rāghavāya dadau vāyurvāsavena pracoditaḥ

translations.english: The wind commanded by Väsava conferred upon Rāghava, a garland or hundred golden lotuses, shining in their native lustre. And the wind commanded by Sakra conferred upon that lord of men a jewelled garland crested with diverse gems.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजगुर्देवगन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरो गणाः
अभिषेके तदर्हस्य तदा रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
prajagurdevagandharvā nanṛtuścāpsaro gaṇāḥ
abhiṣeke tadarhasya tadā rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: The intelligent and worthy Rāma being installed the celestials and the Gandharvas sang and the Apsaras danced.

verses.sanskrit:
भूमिः सस्यवती चैव फलवन्तश्च पादपाः
गन्धवन्ति च पुष्पाणि बभूवू राघवोत्सवे
verses.transliteration:
bhūmiḥ sasyavatī caiva phalavantaśca pādapāḥ
gandhavanti ca puṣpāṇi babhūvū rāghavotsave

translations.english: The earth was filled with crops, the trees with fruits and the flowers were fragrant on the occassion of Rāghava's installation.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिंशत्कोटीर्हिरण्यस्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुनः
नानाभरणवस्त्राणि महार्हाणि च राघवः
verses.transliteration:
triṁśatkoṭīrhiraṇyasya brāhmaṇebhyo dadau punaḥ
nānābharaṇavastrāṇi mahārhāṇi ca rāghavaḥ

translations.english: That foremost of men conferred upon the twice-born ones one million of horses, hundred thousand cows and hundred thousand bulls. And Rāghava again conferred upon the Brāhmaṇas thirty crores of golden coins and diverse costly ornaments and clothes.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशां काञ्चनीं मणिविग्रहाम्
सुग्रीवाय स्रजं दिव्यां प्रायच्छन्मनुजर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
arkaraśmipratīkāśāṁ kāñcanīṁ maṇivigrahām
sugrīvāya srajaṁ divyāṁ prāyacchanmanujarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon that lord of men conferred upon Sugriva a celestial garland brilliant like the rays of the Sun and crested with gold and jewels.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदूर्यमणिचित्रे च वज्ररत्नविभूषिते
वालिपुत्राय धृतिमानङ्गदायाङ्गदे ददौ
verses.transliteration:
vaidūryamaṇicitre ca vajraratnavibhūṣite
vāliputrāya dhṛtimānaṅgadāyāṅgade dadau

translations.english: And he, gifted with intelligence, conferred upon Angada, Vali's son, two Angadas (A kind of ornament worn on upper arms.) brilliant as the rays of the moon and made of Vaidurya.

verses.sanskrit:
मणिप्रवरजुष्टं च मुक्ताहारमनुत्तमम्
सीतायै प्रददौ रामश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
maṇipravarajuṣṭaṁ ca muktāhāramanuttamam
sītāyai pradadau rāmaścandraraśmisamaprabham

translations.english: Rāma conferred upon Sitā an excellent pearl necklace crested with precious jems, celestial clothes and various excellent ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
अवमुच्यात्मनः कण्ठाद्धारं जनकनन्दिनी
अवैक्षत हरीन्सर्वान्भर्तारं च मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.transliteration:
avamucyātmanaḥ kaṇṭhāddhāraṁ janakanandinī
avaikṣata harīnsarvānbhartāraṁ ca muhurmuhuḥ

translations.english: And taking off the necklace from her person Vaidehi, the daughter of king Janaka, conferred it upon the Wind-god's son remembering the services (rendered by him) and cast her looks again and again upon her lord and the monkeys.

verses.sanskrit:
तामिङ्गितज्ञः संप्रेक्ष्य बभाषे जनकात्मजाम्
प्रदेहि सुभगे हारं यस्य तुष्टासि भामिनि
verses.transliteration:
tāmiṅgitajñaḥ saṁprekṣya babhāṣe janakātmajām
pradehi subhage hāraṁ yasya tuṣṭāsi bhāmini

translations.english: Beholding that (Rāma) capable of reading the gestures, spoke to the daughter of king Janaka, saying, "O fortunate and beautiful lady, do you confer this necklace upon him with whom you are pleased."

verses.sanskrit:
पौरुषं विक्रमो बुद्धिर्यस्मिन्नेतानि नित्यदा
ददौ सा वायुपुत्राय तं हारमसितेक्षणा
verses.transliteration:
pauruṣaṁ vikramo buddhiryasminnetāni nityadā
dadau sā vāyuputrāya taṁ hāramasitekṣaṇā

translations.english: Thereupon the lotus-eyed (Sitā) conferred that upon the Wind god's son. And Hanuman, the foremost of monkeys, in whom perpetually exist, energy, forgiveness, fame, skilfulness, prowess, humility, tactics, manliness, valiance and intellect, appeared with that necklace like a mountain beautified with the rays of the moon and white clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो द्विविद मैन्दाभ्यां नीलाय च परंतपः
सर्वान्कामगुणान्वीक्ष्य प्रददौ वसुधाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
tato dvivida maindābhyāṁ nīlāya ca paraṁtapaḥ
sarvānkāmaguṇānvīkṣya pradadau vasudhādhipaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon, the lord of earth and the slayer of foes conferred, all wished for things, upon Dvivida, Mainda and Nila.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्ववानरवृद्धाश्च ये चान्ये वानरेश्वराः
वासोभिर्भूषणैश्चैव यथार्हं प्रतिपूजिताः
verses.transliteration:
sarvavānaravṛddhāśca ye cānye vānareśvarāḥ
vāsobhirbhūṣaṇaiścaiva yathārhaṁ pratipūjitāḥ

translations.english: All other elderly and leading monkeys were respectively honoured with clothes and ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
यथार्हं पूजिताः सर्वे कामै रत्नैश्च पुष्कलैर्
प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे जग्मुरेव यथागतम्
verses.transliteration:
yathārhaṁ pūjitāḥ sarve kāmai ratnaiśca puṣkalair
prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve jagmureva yathāgatam

translations.english: Being honoured by Rāma of unwearied actions with enough of jewels and other wishedfor objects, Vibhisana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan and other leading monkeys, delighted, returned to their respective habitations.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवः परमोदारः शशास परया मुदा
उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामो धर्मज्ञं धर्मवत्सलः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaḥ paramodāraḥ śaśāsa parayā mudā
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṁ rāmo dharmajñaṁ dharmavatsalaḥ

translations.english: Having slain his foes, the highly generous and glorious Rama, ruled in great delight, the kingdom extending all over the earth. And Rama, fond of the pious, spoke to Laksmana, conversant with piety, saying-

verses.sanskrit:
आतिष्ठ धर्मज्ञ मया सहेमां; गां पूर्वराजाध्युषितां बलेन
तुल्यं मया त्वं पितृभिर्धृता या; तां यौवराज्ये धुरमुद्वहस्व
verses.transliteration:
ātiṣṭha dharmajña mayā sahemāṁ; gāṁ pūrvarājādhyuṣitāṁ balena
tulyaṁ mayā tvaṁ pitṛbhirdhṛtā yā; tāṁ yauvarājye dhuramudvahasva

translations.english: O you conversant with piety, do you with me and four fold forces, govern this kingdom, ruled by our predecessors. Like to our ancestors do you now carry the burden of an associate in the throne.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वात्मना पर्यनुनीयमानो; यदा न सौमित्रिरुपैति योगम्
नियुज्यमानो भुवि यौवराज्ये; ततोऽभ्यषिञ्चद्भरतं महात्मा
verses.transliteration:
sarvātmanā paryanunīyamāno; yadā na saumitrirupaiti yogam
niyujyamāno bhuvi yauvarājye; tato'bhyaṣiñcadbharataṁ mahātmā

translations.english: When the son of Sumitrā did not accept the heir apparentship albeit solicited earnestly again and again, the high-souled (Rāma) conferred upon Bharata that dignity.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवश्चापि धर्मात्मा प्राप्य राज्यमनुत्तमम्
ईजे बहुविधैर्यज्ञैः ससुहृद्भ्रातृबान्धवः
verses.transliteration:
rāghavaścāpi dharmātmā prāpya rājyamanuttamam
īje bahuvidhairyajñaiḥ sasuhṛdbhrātṛbāndhavaḥ

translations.english: Obtaining that excellent kingdom, the virtuous souled Raghava performed many sacrifices with his sons, brothers and friends.

verses.sanskrit:
पौण्डरीकाश्वमेधाभ्यां वाजपेयेन चासकृत्
अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैरयजत्पार्थिवर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
pauṇḍarīkāśvamedhābhyāṁ vājapeyena cāsakṛt
anyaiśca vividhairyajñairayajatpārthivarṣabhaḥ

translations.english: That son of king performed various sacrifices such as Paundarika, Asvamedha', Vajimedha and other of various kinds. 1. A kind of sacrifice. 2. A kind of Sacrifice in which a horse is slain.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्यं दशसहस्राणि प्राप्य वर्षाणि राघवः
शताश्वमेधानाजह्रे सदश्वान्भूरिदक्षिणान्
verses.transliteration:
rājyaṁ daśasahasrāṇi prāpya varṣāṇi rāghavaḥ
śatāśvamedhānājahre sadaśvānbhūridakṣiṇān

translations.english: And governing the kingdom for ten thousand years Rāghava performed ten horse-sacrifices with excellent horses and profuse presents.

verses.sanskrit:
आजानुलम्बिबाहुश्च महास्कन्धः प्रतापवान्
लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामः पृथिवीमन्वपालयत्
verses.transliteration:
ājānulambibāhuśca mahāskandhaḥ pratāpavān
lakṣmaṇānucaro rāmaḥ pṛthivīmanvapālayat

translations.english: That highly powerful Rāma, having his arms extended up to the knee-joint, having a spacious breast and Lakşmaņa as his attendant, ruled the earth (in this.wise).

verses.sanskrit:
न पर्यदेवन्विधवा न च व्यालकृतं भयम्
न व्याधिजं भयं वापि रामे राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.transliteration:
na paryadevanvidhavā na ca vyālakṛtaṁ bhayam
na vyādhijaṁ bhayaṁ vāpi rāme rājyaṁ praśāsati

translations.english: Rāma governing the kingdom, the widows were not distressed and there was no fear from voracious animals or from diseases.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्दस्युरभवल्लोको नानर्थः कंचिदस्पृशत्
न च स्म वृद्धा बालानां प्रेतकार्याणि कुर्वते
verses.transliteration:
nirdasyurabhavalloko nānarthaḥ kaṁcidaspṛśat
na ca sma vṛddhā bālānāṁ pretakāryāṇi kurvate

translations.english: The people were saved from the thieves and there was no other trouble. And the old were not constrained to perform the funeral ceremonies of the children.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वं मुदितमेवासीत्सर्वो धर्मपरोऽभवत्
राममेवानुपश्यन्तो नाभ्यहिंसन्परस्परम्
verses.transliteration:
sarvaṁ muditamevāsītsarvo dharmaparo'bhavat
rāmamevānupaśyanto nābhyahiṁsanparasparam

translations.english: All were delighted and devoted to pious observances. And beholding Rāma they did not envy one another.

verses.sanskrit:
आसन्वर्षसहस्राणि तथा पुत्रसहस्रिणः
निरामया विशोकाश्च रामे राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.transliteration:
āsanvarṣasahasrāṇi tathā putrasahasriṇaḥ
nirāmayā viśokāśca rāme rājyaṁ praśāsati

translations.english: Rāma governing the kingdom, (people) lived for thousand years and had thousand children, they were freed from diseases and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यपुष्पा नित्यफलास्तरवः स्कन्धविस्तृताः
कालवर्षी च पर्जन्यः सुखस्पर्शश्च मारुतः
verses.transliteration:
nityapuṣpā nityaphalāstaravaḥ skandhavistṛtāḥ
kālavarṣī ca parjanyaḥ sukhasparśaśca mārutaḥ

translations.english: The trees bore fruits and flowers perpetuallythere were showers at will and the wind blew pleasant.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वकर्मसु प्रवर्तन्ते तुष्ठाः स्वैरेव कर्मभिः
आसन्प्रजा धर्मपरा रामे शासति नानृताः
verses.transliteration:
svakarmasu pravartante tuṣṭhāḥ svaireva karmabhiḥ
āsanprajā dharmaparā rāme śāsati nānṛtāḥ

translations.english: The people delighted engaged in their respective works and the subjects grew pious and truthful, under Rāma's regime, and were devoted to the observances of all pious works and gifted with all auspicious marks. And Rāma ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य राक्षसानां वधे कृते
आजग्मुरृषयः सर्वे राघवं प्रतिनन्दितुम्
verses.transliteration:
prāptarājyasya rāmasya rākṣasānāṁ vadhe kṛte
ājagmurṛṣayaḥ sarve rāghavaṁ pratinanditum

translations.english: On the Rākṣasas having been slain, all the ascetics, for the purpose of congratulating Rāghava, came to Rāma as he gained (back) his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्त्यात्रेयश्च भगवान्नमुचिः प्रमुचुस्तथा
आजग्मुस्ते सहागस्त्या ये श्रिता दक्षिणां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
svastyātreyaśca bhagavānnamuciḥ pramucustathā
ājagmuste sahāgastyā ye śritā dakṣiṇāṁ diśam

translations.english: Kausika, and Yavakrīta, and Gārgya, and Gālava and Kaņva, son of Medhātithi,who dwelt in the east, (came thither); and the reverend Svastyāstreya, and Namuci, and Pramuci, and Agastya, and the worshipful Atri, and Sumukha, and Vimukha, who dwelt in the south, came in company with Agastya.* *The name of Agastya had before been just specified among the incomes; but so it is in the text.

verses.sanskrit:
पृषद्गुः कवषो धौम्यो रौद्रेयश्च महानृषिः
तेऽप्याजग्मुः सशिष्या वै ये श्रिताः पश्चिमां दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣadguḥ kavaṣo dhaumyo raudreyaśca mahānṛṣiḥ
te'pyājagmuḥ saśiṣyā vai ye śritāḥ paścimāṁ diśam

translations.english: Nrisadgu, and Kavasi, and Dhaumya, and that mighty sage-Kauseya-who abode in th quarter, came there accompanied by their disciples.

verses.sanskrit:
वसिष्ठः कश्यपोऽथात्रिर्विश्वामित्रोऽथ गौतमः
जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजस्तेऽपि सप्तमहर्षयः
verses.transliteration:
vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapo'thātrirviśvāmitro'tha gautamaḥ
jamadagnirbharadvājaste'pi saptamaharṣayaḥ

translations.english: Vasiştha and Kasyapa and Atri and Viśvāmitra with Gautama and Jamadagni and Bharadvāja and also the seven sages*, who for aye resided in the northern quarter, (came there). *Ursa Major, or the great bear, the seven stars of which are the souls of as many saints, Marici, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha.

verses.sanskrit:
संप्राप्यैते महात्मानो राघवस्य निवेशनम्
विष्ठिताः प्रतिहारार्थं हुताशनसमप्रभाः
verses.transliteration:
saṁprāpyaite mahātmāno rāghavasya niveśanam
viṣṭhitāḥ pratihārārthaṁ hutāśanasamaprabhāḥ

translations.english: On arriving at the residence of Rāghava, those high-souled ones, resembling the fire in radiance, stopped at the gate, with the intention of communicating their arrival (to Rama) through the warder.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु बालसूर्यसमप्रभान्
तदोवाच नृपो द्वाःस्थं प्रवेशय यथासुखम्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā prāptānmunīṁstāṁstu bālasūryasamaprabhān
tadovāca nṛpo dvāḥsthaṁ praveśaya yathāsukham

translations.english: Hearing of the arrival of the anchorets, possessed of the effulgence of the sun new-risen, he answered the warder, saying, "Do you usher them in, having regard to their comfort."

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः
रामोऽभिवाद्य प्रयत आसनान्यादिदेश ह
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā prāptānmunīṁstāṁstu pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
rāmo'bhivādya prayata āsanānyādideśa ha

translations.english: Seeing the ascetics him, Rāma with joined hands worshipped their feet with arghyas, and with regard consecrated a cow to each, and saluting them with the collecting mind, he ordered seats (for the saints).

verses.sanskrit:
रामेण कुशलं पृष्टाः सशिष्याः सपुरोगमाः
महर्षयो वेदविदो रामं वचनमब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
rāmeṇa kuśalaṁ pṛṣṭāḥ saśiṣyāḥ sapurogamāḥ
maharṣayo vedavido rāmaṁ vacanamabruvan

translations.english: And having, according to their rank, seated themselves on gorgeous and superb seats of kuća or deerskins embroidered with gold, those foremost of sages-those mighty saints, versed in the Vedas, along with their disciples and leaders, having (previously) been asked as to their welfare, addressed Rāma, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशलं नो महाबाहो सर्वत्र रघुनन्दन
त्वां तु दिष्ट्या कुशलिनं पश्यामो हतशात्रवम्
verses.transliteration:
kuśalaṁ no mahābāho sarvatra raghunandana
tvāṁ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṁ paśyāmo hataśātravam

translations.english: O son of Raghu. O mighty-armed one, complete welfare is ours. By good luck it is that we see you fortunate, with all your foes finished. Bygood luck it is that, Oking, Ravana-destroyer of creatures, has been slain byyou.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि भारः स ते राम रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
सधनुस्त्वं हि लोकांस्त्रीन्विजयेथा न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
na hi bhāraḥ sa te rāma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
sadhanustvaṁ hi lokāṁstrīnvijayethā na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: Sure, O Rama, it was no great matter for you (to slay) Rāvaņa along with his sons and grandsons. Furnished with your bow, you can, without doubt, destroy the three worlds themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान्
दिष्ट्या विजयिनं त्वाद्य पश्यामः सह भार्यया
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā tvayā hato rāma rāvaṇaḥ putrapautravān
diṣṭyā vijayinaṁ tvādya paśyāmaḥ saha bhāryayā

translations.english: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that Ravana along with his sons and grandsons has been slain by you. By good fortune it is that today we see you victorious along with $ītā, and, O righteoussouled one, with your brother, Lakşmaņa, (ever) compassing your profit. (By good fortune it is) that, Oking, today we behold (you) in company with your mothers and your brothers.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या प्रहस्तो विकटो विरूपाक्षो महोदरः
अकम्पनश्च दुर्धर्षो निहतास्ते निशाचराः
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā prahasto vikaṭo virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ
akampanaśca durdharṣo nihatāste niśācarāḥ

translations.english: By good fortune it is that those night-rangers, Prahasta, and Vikata; and Virupāksa, and Mahodara, and the unconquerable Akampana, have all been slain (by you).

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य प्रमाणाद्विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते
दिष्ट्या ते समरे राम कुम्भकर्णो निपातितः
verses.transliteration:
yasya pramāṇādvipulaṁ pramāṇaṁ neha vidyate
diṣṭyā te samare rāma kumbhakarṇo nipātitaḥ

translations.english: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that he than whose proportions there are no other's greater on earth, even Kumbhakarņa, was brought downy (by you).

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रेण द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः
देवतानामवध्येन विजयं प्राप्तवानसि
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā tvaṁ rākṣasendreṇa dvandvayuddhamupāgataḥ
devatānāmavadhyena vijayaṁ prāptavānasi

translations.english: By good luck it is that you had been encountered in a hand-to-hand combat with that foremost of Rākşasas, incapable of being slain by the celestials themselves; and achieved victory (ultimately).

verses.sanskrit:
संख्ये तस्य न किंचित्तु रावणस्य पराभवः
द्वन्द्वयुद्धमनुप्राप्तो दिष्ट्या ते रावणिर्हतः
verses.transliteration:
saṁkhye tasya na kiṁcittu rāvaṇasya parābhavaḥ
dvandvayuddhamanuprāpto diṣṭyā te rāvaṇirhataḥ

translations.english: To defeat Ravana in battle was (for you) in small matter; but it is a piece of good fortune that Ravana's son, who had confronted you for combat, has been slain (by you) in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या तस्य महाबाहो कालस्येवाभिधावतः
मुक्तः सुररिपोर्वीर प्राप्तश्च विजयस्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā tasya mahābāho kālasyevābhidhāvataḥ
muktaḥ surariporvīra prāptaśca vijayastvayā

translations.english: By good fortune it is that you, O mightyarmed one, had been liberated from the bonds of) that foe of the celestials whose course resembled that of Time;*-and that you also had secured victory. *i.e. surpassing perception.

verses.sanskrit:
विस्मयस्त्वेष नः सौम्य संश्रुत्येन्द्रजितं हतम्
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां महामायाधरो युधि
verses.transliteration:
vismayastveṣa naḥ saumya saṁśrutyendrajitaṁ hatam
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ mahāmāyādharo yudhi

translations.english: Hearing of the destruction of Indrajit, we congratulate you (on your success). He was in capable of being slain by all creatures, and in battle possessed mighty powers of illusion.

verses.sanskrit:
दत्त्वा पुण्यामिमां वीर सौम्यामभयदक्षिणाम्
दिष्ट्या वर्धसि काकुत्स्थ जयेनामित्रकर्शन
verses.transliteration:
dattvā puṇyāmimāṁ vīra saumyāmabhayadakṣiṇām
diṣṭyā vardhasi kākutstha jayenāmitrakarśana

translations.english: Hearing that Indrajit slain, amazement have seized us all. Having conferred on us this holy freedom from fear, O Kākutstha, O repressor of enemies. you through good fortune, will grow in victory.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषामृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्
विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रामः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu vacanaṁ teṣāmṛṣīṇāṁ bhāvitātmanām
vismayaṁ paramaṁ gatvā rāmaḥ prāñjalirabravīt

translations.english: Hearing the speech of the ascetics of sacred souls, Rāma, coming under the influence of a mighty wonder, said with joined hands.

verses.sanskrit:
भवन्तः कुम्भकर्णं च रावणं च निशाचरम्
अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यौ किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम्
verses.transliteration:
bhavantaḥ kumbhakarṇaṁ ca rāvaṇaṁ ca niśācaram
atikramya mahāvīryau kiṁ praśaṁsatha rāvaṇim

translations.english: You worshipful ones, wherefore, passing by those exceedingly powerful ones-Kumbhakarna and the night-ranger, Ravana, do you praise Ravana's son?

verses.sanskrit:
महोदरं प्रहस्तं च विरूपाक्षं च राक्षसं
अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान्किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम्
verses.transliteration:
mahodaraṁ prahastaṁ ca virūpākṣaṁ ca rākṣasaṁ
atikramya mahāvīryānkiṁ praśaṁsatha rāvaṇim

translations.english: Wherefore, passing by Mahodara, and Prahasta, and the Rākşasa-Virüpākşa-and Matta, and Unmatta, and the irrepressible Devāntaka and Narāntaka-redoubtable heroes all-do you extol Ravana's son?

verses.sanskrit:
कीदृशो वै प्रभावोऽस्य किं बलं कः पराक्रमः
केन वा कारणेनैष रावणादतिरिच्यते
verses.transliteration:
kīdṛśo vai prabhāvo'sya kiṁ balaṁ kaḥ parākramaḥ
kena vā kāraṇenaiṣa rāvaṇādatiricyate

translations.english: What was his prowess? And what his strength? And what his might? And by virtue of what cause did he surpass Rāvana?

verses.sanskrit:
शक्यं यदि मया श्रोतुं न खल्वाज्ञापयामि वः
यदि गुह्यं न चेद्वक्तुं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्
कथं शक्रो जितस्तेन कथं लब्धवरश्च सः
verses.transliteration:
śakyaṁ yadi mayā śrotuṁ na khalvājñāpayāmi vaḥ
yadi guhyaṁ na cedvaktuṁ śrotumicchāmi kathyatām
kathaṁ śakro jitastena kathaṁ labdhavaraśca saḥ

translations.english: If I can well hear the same (do you tell it me). I by no means command you. If the thing can bear disclosure, I would hear it. Pray, speak out.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः
कुम्भयोनिर्महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
kumbhayonirmahātejā vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing those words of Rāghva, the exceedingly energetic Kumbhayoni spoke as follows.

verses.sanskrit:
शृणु राजन्यथावृत्तं यस्य तेजोबलं महत्
जघान च रिपून्युद्धे यथावध्यश्च शत्रुभिः
verses.transliteration:
śṛṇu rājanyathāvṛttaṁ yasya tejobalaṁ mahat
jaghāna ca ripūnyuddhe yathāvadhyaśca śatrubhiḥ

translations.english: Having regard to his (Indrajit's) energy and might, I shall relate to you the history of his race, in the light of which you will perceive why Rāvana's son had been capable of slaying his enemies, but could not himself be slain by them.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव
वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ te rāvaṇasyedaṁ kulaṁ janma ca rāghava
varapradānaṁ ca tathā tasmai dattaṁ bravīmi te

translations.english: I shall, O Rāghava, describe to you Răvaņa's race and birth, as well as the boon that had been conferred on him.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा कृतयुगे राम प्रजापतिसुतः प्रभुः
पुलस्त्यो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षादिव पितामहः
verses.transliteration:
purā kṛtayuge rāma prajāpatisutaḥ prabhuḥ
pulastyo nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣādiva pitāmahaḥ

translations.english: Formerly in the Krita age, O Rama, there was a Brahmarsi-lord (of creatures), son to Prajapati, and like to the very self of the great-father.

verses.sanskrit:
नानुकीर्त्या गुणास्तस्य धर्मतः शीलतस्तथा
प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः
verses.transliteration:
nānukīrtyā guṇāstasya dharmataḥ śīlatastathā
prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṁ śakyaṁ hi nāmataḥ

translations.english: His virtues, springing from righteousness and excellency of character, are past all delineation; I can only say that, forsooth, he went by the name of Prajāpati's son.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः
तृणबिन्द्वाश्रमं गत्वा न्यवसन्मुनिपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ
tṛṇabindvāśramaṁ gatvā nyavasanmunipuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: And on a religious mission that foremost of ascetics, repairing to the asylum of Triņabindu at the side of the mighty mountain, Meru, took up his abode there.

verses.sanskrit:
तपस्तेपे स धर्मात्मा स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः
गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति कन्यकाः
verses.transliteration:
tapastepe sa dharmātmā svādhyāyaniyatendriyaḥ
gatvāśramapadaṁ tasya vighnaṁ kurvanti kanyakāḥ

translations.english: And with his senses centred on the study of the Vedas, that righteous-souled one, going to the hermitage, carried on austerities; but his religious rites were disturbed by certain girls. And daughters of sages and Pannagas and those of Rājarşis, as well as those of Apsarās, sporting, arrived at that quarter.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वर्तुषूपभोग्यत्वाद्रम्यत्वात्काननस्य च
नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः
verses.transliteration:
sarvartuṣūpabhogyatvādramyatvātkānanasya ca
nityaśastāstu taṁ deśaṁ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ

translations.english: And an account of every season being genial at that spot and also of the loveliness of the wood, the damsels, repairing to this place. ever disport there.

verses.sanskrit:
तृणबिन्दोस्तु राजर्षेस्तनया न शृणोति तत्
गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विचचार सुनिर्भया
verses.transliteration:
tṛṇabindostu rājarṣestanayā na śṛṇoti tat
gatvāśramapadaṁ tasya vicacāra sunirbhayā

translations.english: ‘She that comes within my kin, shall conceive.' Hearing the words of the high-souled one, (the damsels), afraid of a Brāhamana's curse, ceased to to haunt that place. But Triņabindu's daughter had not heard anything of all this, and going to the asylum, she ranged it fearlessly.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिन्नेव तु काले स प्राजापत्यो महानृषिः
स्वाध्यायमकरोत्तत्र तपसा द्योतितप्रभः
verses.transliteration:
tasminneva tu kāle sa prājāpatyo mahānṛṣiḥ
svādhyāyamakarottatra tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ

translations.english: She did not see there any of her associates come to that spot. And at that time that exceedingly energetic and mighty sage, Prajāpati's son, with his soul sanctified through eticism, was engaged in the study of the Veda.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु वेदध्वनिं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा चैव तपोधनम्
अभवत्पाण्डुदेहा सा सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा
verses.transliteration:
sā tu vedadhvaniṁ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā caiva tapodhanam
abhavatpāṇḍudehā sā suvyañjitaśarīrajā

translations.english: Hearing the sounds of Vedic recitation, and seeing that storehouse of asceticism, she had her body turned pale, and signs of pregnancy displayed themselves.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा परमसंविग्ना सा तु तद्रूपमात्मनः
इदं मे किं न्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वाग्रतः स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā paramasaṁvignā sā tu tadrūpamātmanaḥ
idaṁ me kiṁ nviti jñātvā piturgatvāgrataḥ sthitā

translations.english: Seeing that evil befall her, she was wrought up with anxiety; and, understanding matters, she said, "What is this?' And, going to her father's hermitage, stayed there.

verses.sanskrit:
तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथा भूतां तृणबिन्दुरथाब्रवीत्
किं त्वमेतत्त्वसदृशं धारयस्यात्मनो वपुः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ tu dṛṣṭvā tathā bhūtāṁ tṛṇabindurathābravīt
kiṁ tvametattvasadṛśaṁ dhārayasyātmano vapuḥ

translations.english: Seeing her in this condition, Triņabindu said, "Wherefore is the person that you bear unlike what it used to be?'

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योवाच तपोधनम्
न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṁ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam
na jāne kāraṇaṁ tāta yena me rūpamīdṛśam

translations.english: Thereat, in.woe-begone guise, with joined hands, his daughter replied to that one having asceticism for the riches, 'O father, cause know I none whereby I have come by this appearance.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तु पूर्वं गतास्म्येका महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः
पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं दिव्यमन्वेष्टुं स्वसखीजनम्
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tu pūrvaṁ gatāsmyekā maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ
pulastyasyāśramaṁ divyamanveṣṭuṁ svasakhījanam

translations.english: But searching for my associates, I had ere this alone repaired to the noble asylum of the Maharși Pulastya of a purified spirit.

verses.sanskrit:
न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र कांचिदप्यागतां सखीम्
रूपस्य तु विपर्यासं दृष्ट्वा चाहमिहागता
verses.transliteration:
na ca paśyāmyahaṁ tatra kāṁcidapyāgatāṁ sakhīm
rūpasya tu viparyāsaṁ dṛṣṭvā cāhamihāgatā

translations.english: But associate found there I none, that had come thither. And seeing this change for the worse of my form, I from fear have come hither.

verses.sanskrit:
तृणबिन्दुस्तु राजर्षिस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः
ध्यानं विवेश तच्चापि अपश्यदृषिकर्मजम्
verses.transliteration:
tṛṇabindustu rājarṣistapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ
dhyānaṁ viveśa taccāpi apaśyadṛṣikarmajam

translations.english: Thereat the Rajarsi, Trinabindu, having a live effulgence through asceticism, entered into contemplation, and saw the consequence of the sage's act.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः
गृहीत्वा तनयां गत्वा पुलस्त्यमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vijñāya taṁ śāpaṁ maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ
gṛhītvā tanayāṁ gatvā pulastyamidamabravīt

translations.english: And coming to know that curse of the Maharși of a purified spirit, he, taking his daughter, went to Pulastya and said.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम्
भिक्षां प्रतिगृहाणेमां महर्षे स्वयमुद्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavaṁstanayāṁ me tvaṁ guṇaiḥ svaireva bhūṣitām
bhikṣāṁ pratigṛhāṇemāṁ maharṣe svayamudyatām

translations.english: O worshipful one, O mighty sage, do you accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her native perfections, who of herself has come to you as alms.

verses.sanskrit:
तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य श्राम्यमाणेन्द्रियस्य ते
शुश्रूषातत्परा नित्यं भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
tapaścaraṇayuktasya śrāmyamāṇendriyasya te
śuśrūṣātatparā nityaṁ bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: She will, without doubt, constantly tend you, practising asceticism, and having your senses fatigued.

verses.sanskrit:
तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षिं धार्मिकं तदा
जिघृक्षुरब्रवीत्कन्यां बाढमित्येव स द्विजः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ bruvāṇaṁ tu tadvākyaṁ rājarṣiṁ dhārmikaṁ tadā
jighṛkṣurabravītkanyāṁ bāḍhamityeva sa dvijaḥ

translations.english: When that virtuous (sage) had said this, the twice-born Räjarși, desirous of accepting the girl (after due nuptial rights), said to the former, 'Well!'

verses.sanskrit:
दत्त्वा तु स गतो राजा स्वमाश्रमपदं तदा
सापि तत्रावसत्कन्या तोषयन्ती पतिं गुणैः
प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
dattvā tu sa gato rājā svamāśramapadaṁ tadā
sāpi tatrāvasatkanyā toṣayantī patiṁ guṇaiḥ
prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Having given away his daughter, the king went (back) to his asylum; and the girl stayed there, gratifying her husband with her virtues.

verses.sanskrit:
परितुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते गुणानां संपदा भृशम्
तस्मात्ते विरमाम्यद्य पुत्रमात्मसमं गुणैः
उभयोर्वंशकर्तारं पौलस्त्य इति विश्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
parituṣṭo'smi bhadraṁ te guṇānāṁ saṁpadā bhṛśam
tasmātte viramāmyadya putramātmasamaṁ guṇaiḥ
ubhayorvaṁśakartāraṁ paulastya iti viśrutam

translations.english: 'O you of shapely hips, well-pleased am I with you with your wealth of worth, and therefore, O exalted one, I will today confer on you a son like to yourself, who will perpetuate both the lines*-being celebrated as Paulastya. *(i.e. maternal and paternal lines.)

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्तु विश्रुतो वेदस्त्वयेहाभ्यस्यतो मम
तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
yasmāttu viśruto vedastvayehābhyasyato mama
tasmātsa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: And as you had heard the Veda recited by me, so, without doubt, he shall be named Visravā.* *(From the root, Śru-to hear.)

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
अचिरेणैव कालेन सूता विश्रवसं सुतम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā kanyā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
acireṇaiva kālena sūtā viśravasaṁ sutam

translations.english: Thus addressed, that noble damsel with her soul wrought with delight, in a short time brought forth her son Visravā, famed over the three worlds and furnished with virtue and fame: versed in the Vedas, of an impartial spirit, and ever engaged in observing vows. And the ascetic, Viśravă, was furnished with asceticism even like his sire. ever

verses.sanskrit:
अथ पुत्रः पुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवा मुनिपुंगवः
अचिरेणैव कालेन पितेव तपसि स्थितः
verses.transliteration:
atha putraḥ pulastyasya viśravā munipuṁgavaḥ
acireṇaiva kālena piteva tapasi sthitaḥ

translations.english: Pulastya's son-that prime of ascetics-Visravāin a short time was engaged in asceticism like his father.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यवाञ्शीलवान्दक्षः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचिः
सर्वभोगेष्वसंसक्तो नित्यं धर्मपरायणः
verses.transliteration:
satyavāñśīlavāndakṣaḥ svādhyāyanirataḥ śuciḥ
sarvabhogeṣvasaṁsakto nityaṁ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ

translations.english: And he was truthful, and of excellent character and controlled senses; was engaged in the study of the Vedas; and was of the sanctified spirit; and he was not addicted to any of the pleasures of life, and was always studious of religion.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वैश्रवणस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा
अवर्धत महातेजा हुताहुतिरिवानलः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu vaiśravaṇastatra tapovanagatastadā
avardhata mahātejā hutāhutirivānalaḥ

translations.english: Then the exceedingly energetic Vaiśravana, repairing to the wood of asceticism, increased in power) like to a fire fed by sacrificial oblations.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याश्रमपदस्थस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः
चरिष्ये नियतो धर्मं धर्मो हि परमा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāśramapadasthasya buddhirjajñe mahātmanaḥ
cariṣye niyato dharmaṁ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ

translations.english: And as he was staying in the hermitage, that high-souled one thought, 'I shall practice prime righteousness: verily virtue is the supreme way.'

verses.sanskrit:
स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु तं तं विधिमवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptvā mahāvane
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu taṁ taṁ vidhimavartata

translations.english: For a thousand years, he, having his senses controlled, practised rigid austerities in that mighty forest, observing (all the while) the most rigorous restrictions.

verses.sanskrit:
जलाशी मारुताहारो निराहारस्तथैव च
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि जग्मुस्तान्येव वर्षवत्
verses.transliteration:
jalāśī mārutāhāro nirāhārastathaiva ca
evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi jagmustānyeva varṣavat

translations.english: And on a thousand years having been numbered, he by turns observed the rules relative to each term; (at first) living on water, (then) on air, and (last) going absolutely without any food. Thus passed away a thousand years like one.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ प्रीतो महातेजाः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह
गत्वा तस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मेदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
atha prīto mahātejāḥ sendraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha
gatvā tasyāśramapadaṁ brahmedaṁ vākyamabravīt

translations.english: Then the highly energetic Brahmā along with the Indra and the celestials, coming to that asylum, addressed (Vaisravana), saying, '0 child, I am well-pleased with you for this act of your, O you of excellent vows. Do you, good betide you, ask for the 'boon (that you would have), for, O magnanimous one, you are worthy of a boon.'

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः पितामहमुपस्थितम्
भगवँल्लोकपालत्वमिच्छेयं वित्तरक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
athābravīdvaiśravaṇaḥ pitāmahamupasthitam
bhagava̐llokapālatvamiccheyaṁ vittarakṣaṇam

translations.english: Then Vaisravaņa said to the Pitāmaha, who was present, 'O reverend one, I crave for the power of maintaining and protecting people.'

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीद्वैश्रवणं परितुष्टेन चेतसा
ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धं बाढमित्येव हृष्टवत्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīdvaiśravaṇaṁ parituṣṭena cetasā
brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṁ bāḍhamityeva hṛṣṭavat

translations.english: Thereat, Brahmä along with the deities gladly said to Vaiśravana in a gratified spirit, Very well!

verses.sanskrit:
अहं हि लोकपालानां चतुर्थं स्रष्टुमुद्यतः
यमेन्द्रवरुणानां हि पदं यत्तव चेप्सितम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi lokapālānāṁ caturthaṁ sraṣṭumudyataḥ
yamendravaruṇānāṁ hi padaṁ yattava cepsitam

translations.english: I am about to create the fourth of the Protectors of the creatures-Yama, Indra and Varuna, the position which is sought for by you.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्कृतं गच्छ धर्मज्ञ धनेशत्वमवाप्नुहि
यमेन्द्रवरुणानां हि चतुर्थोऽद्य भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
tatkṛtaṁ gaccha dharmajña dhaneśatvamavāpnuhi
yamendravaruṇānāṁ hi caturtho'dya bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: Do you, O you cognisant of righteousness, attain the same; do you receive the position of the lord of riches. You shall be the fourth among the Sakra, the lord of waters, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्च पुष्पकं नाम विमानं सूर्यसंनिभम्
प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यानार्थं त्रिदशैः समतां व्रज
verses.transliteration:
etacca puṣpakaṁ nāma vimānaṁ sūryasaṁnibham
pratigṛhṇīṣva yānārthaṁ tridaśaiḥ samatāṁ vraja

translations.english: Do you take for your vehicle this car, named Puşpaka, resembling the Sun himself, and thus raise yourself to an equality with the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामः सर्व एव यथागतम्
कृतकृत्या वयं तात दत्त्वा तव महावरम्
verses.transliteration:
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmaḥ sarva eva yathāgatam
kṛtakṛtyā vayaṁ tāta dattvā tava mahāvaram

translations.english: Good betide you! We shall (now) go whither we had come, having, my child, done my duty and bestowed on you the couple of boons.

verses.sanskrit:
रमणीया पुरी सा हि रुक्मवैदूर्यतोरणा
राक्षसैः सा परित्यक्ता पुरा विष्णुभयार्दितैः
शून्या रक्षोगणैः सर्वै रसातलतलं गतैः
verses.transliteration:
ramaṇīyā purī sā hi rukmavaidūryatoraṇā
rākṣasaiḥ sā parityaktā purā viṣṇubhayārditaiḥ
śūnyā rakṣogaṇaiḥ sarvai rasātalatalaṁ gataiḥ

translations.english: Formerly she was renounced by the Raksasas afflicted with the fear of Vişnu; and was empty of swarms of Rākşasa, who had gone to the nethermost regions. Now Lanka is vacant, and there is no one that lords it over her. Do you, my child, for abode, at your ease repair thither. Your stay there shall meet with no rub, and no manner of disturbance shall occur there.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु धर्मात्मा धर्मिष्ठं वचनं पितुः
निवेशयामास तदा लङ्कां पर्वतमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
etacchrutvā tu dharmātmā dharmiṣṭhaṁ vacanaṁ pituḥ
niveśayāmāsa tadā laṅkāṁ parvatamūrdhani

translations.english: Hearing the righteous speech of his sire, that virtuous-souled one along with thousands of delighted and joyous Rākşasas, began to reside in Lanka stationed on the ion of the mount.

verses.sanskrit:
नैरृतानां सहस्रैस्तु हृष्टैः प्रमुदितैः सदा
अचिरेणैककालेन संपूर्णा तस्य शासनात्
verses.transliteration:
nairṛtānāṁ sahasraistu hṛṣṭaiḥ pramuditaiḥ sadā
acireṇaikakālena saṁpūrṇā tasya śāsanāt

translations.english: In a short time (Lankā), through his sway, abounded (in wealth). And that foremost of Nairtas, the righteous-son of Visrava, wellpleased, abode in Lankā having the Ocean for her entrenchment.

verses.sanskrit:
काले काले विनीतात्मा पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः
अभ्यगच्छत्सुसंहृष्टः पितरं मातरं च सः
verses.transliteration:
kāle kāle vinītātmā puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaraḥ
abhyagacchatsusaṁhṛṣṭaḥ pitaraṁ mātaraṁ ca saḥ

translations.english: At times the righteous-souled lord of riches, mounted on Pușpaka, in humble guise visited his father and mother.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वागस्त्येरितं वाक्यं रामो विस्मयमागतः
पूर्वमासीत्तु लङ्कायां रक्षसामिति संभवः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvāgastyeritaṁ vākyaṁ rāmo vismayamāgataḥ
pūrvamāsīttu laṅkāyāṁ rakṣasāmiti saṁbhavaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words uttered by Agastya, Răma wondered as to how formerly Rākşasas were generated in Lanka.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शिरः कम्पयित्वा त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम्
अगस्त्यं तं मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śiraḥ kampayitvā tretāgnisamavigraham
agastyaṁ taṁ muhurdṛṣṭvā smayamāno'bhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Then shaking his head, he, struck with wonder, momentarily eyeing Agastya, addressed Agastya resembling fire, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्पूर्वमप्येषा लङ्कासीत्पिशिताशिनाम्
इतीदं भवतः श्रुत्वा विस्मयो जनितो मम
verses.transliteration:
bhagavanpūrvamapyeṣā laṅkāsītpiśitāśinām
itīdaṁ bhavataḥ śrutvā vismayo janito mama

translations.english: O worshipful one, hearing your words that formerly Lankā had been in the possession of the flesh-eaters, I have been seized with great amazement.

verses.sanskrit:
पुलस्त्यवंशादुद्भूता राक्षसा इति नः श्रुतम्
इदानीमन्यतश्चापि संभवः कीर्तितस्त्वया
verses.transliteration:
pulastyavaṁśādudbhūtā rākṣasā iti naḥ śrutam
idānīmanyataścāpi saṁbhavaḥ kīrtitastvayā

translations.english: We had heard that the Rākṣasas had sprung in the race of Pulastya. But now you have said that they owe their origin to a different source.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणात्कुम्भकर्णाच्च प्रहस्ताद्विकटादपि
रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇātkumbhakarṇācca prahastādvikaṭādapi
rāvaṇasya ca putrebhyaḥ kiṁ nu te balavattarāḥ

translations.english: But were they more powerful than Rāvana, Kumbhakarma and Prahasta and Vikața and the sons of Rāvana?

verses.sanskrit:
क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किंनामा किंतपोबलः
अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः पुरा
verses.transliteration:
ka eṣāṁ pūrvako brahmankiṁnāmā kiṁtapobalaḥ
aparādhaṁ ca kaṁ prāpya viṣṇunā drāvitāḥ purā

translations.english: Who was their progenitor? And what was the name of that terrific strength? And through what transgression were they driven out by Vişnu?

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ
कौतूहलं कृतं मह्यं नुद भानुर्यथा तमः
verses.transliteration:
etadvistarataḥ sarvaṁ kathayasva mamānagha
kautūhalaṁ kṛtaṁ mahyaṁ nuda bhānuryathā tamaḥ

translations.english: All this, O sinless one, do you tell me in detail, and do you dispel my curiosity even as the sun dispels darkness.

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य तु तच्छ्रुत्वा संस्कारालंकृतं वचः
ईषद्विस्मयमानस्तमगस्त्यः प्राह राघवम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya tu tacchrutvā saṁskārālaṁkṛtaṁ vacaḥ
īṣadvismayamānastamagastyaḥ prāha rāghavam

translations.english: Hearing Rāghava's words, fair and fraught with polished phrase and period, Agastya, struck with surprise, said to Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतिः पुरा सृष्ट्वा अपः सलिलसंभवः
तासां गोपायने सत्त्वानसृजत्पद्मसंभवः
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatiḥ purā sṛṣṭvā apaḥ salilasaṁbhavaḥ
tāsāṁ gopāyane sattvānasṛjatpadmasaṁbhavaḥ

translations.english: The lord of creatures sprang from water, first created water. And the lotus-born one generated creatures for protecting that element.

verses.sanskrit:
ते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वकर्तारं विनीतवदुपस्थिताः
किं कुर्म इति भाषन्तः क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः
verses.transliteration:
te sattvāḥ sattvakartāraṁ vinītavadupasthitāḥ
kiṁ kurma iti bhāṣantaḥ kṣutpipāsābhayārditāḥ

translations.english: Thereupon those creatures humbly presented themselves before the creator, saying, What shall we do? We are sore tried by hunger and thirst.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतिस्तु तान्याह सत्त्वानि प्रहसन्निव
आभाष्य वाचा यत्नेन रक्षध्वमिति मानदः
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatistu tānyāha sattvāni prahasanniva
ābhāṣya vācā yatnena rakṣadhvamiti mānadaḥ

translations.english: The lord of creatures, laughing, addressed them, saying, “You men, do you carefully guard this (water).”

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षाम इति तत्रान्यैर्यक्षामेति तथापरैः
भुङ्क्षिताभुङ्क्षितैरुक्तस्ततस्तानाह भूतकृत्
verses.transliteration:
rakṣāma iti tatrānyairyakṣāmeti tathāparaiḥ
bhuṅkṣitābhuṅkṣitairuktastatastānāha bhūtakṛt

translations.english: Thereat some said 'Raksama,' (i.e. we shall protect.) and others 'Yaksāma.' (We shall worship.) Thus accosted by those afflicted with hunger and thirst, the creator said.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः
यक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं ते वै यक्षा भवन्तु वः
verses.transliteration:
rakṣāma iti yairuktaṁ rākṣasāste bhavantu vaḥ
yakṣāma iti yairuktaṁ te vai yakṣā bhavantu vaḥ

translations.english: Those among you who have said 'Raksama,' shall be Raksasas; and those among you, who have said 'Yaksama' shall be Yaksas.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र हेतिः प्रहेतिश्च भ्रातरौ राक्षसर्षभौ
मधुकैटभसंकाशौ बभूवतुररिंदमौ
verses.transliteration:
tatra hetiḥ prahetiśca bhrātarau rākṣasarṣabhau
madhukaiṭabhasaṁkāśau babhūvaturariṁdamau

translations.english: And there sprang the brothers-repressors of foes-Heti and Praheti lords of Raksasas, resembling Madhu Kaitabha himself.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहेतिर्धार्मिकस्तत्र न दारान्सोऽभिकाङ्क्षति
हेतिर्दारक्रियार्थं तु यत्नं परमथाकरोत्
verses.transliteration:
prahetirdhārmikastatra na dārānso'bhikāṅkṣati
hetirdārakriyārthaṁ tu yatnaṁ paramathākarot

translations.english: Praheti, who was righteous, went to the wood of asceticism. And Heti exerted himself to the utmost to get himself wived.

verses.sanskrit:
स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम भयावहाम्
उदावहदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव महामतिः
verses.transliteration:
sa kālabhaginīṁ kanyāṁ bhayāṁ nāma bhayāvahām
udāvahadameyātmā svayameva mahāmatiḥ

translations.english: And that magnanimous one of immeasurable soul married the exceedingly terrific sister of Kala, named Bhayā (Fear.)

verses.sanskrit:
स तस्यां जनयामास हेती राक्षसपुंगवः
पुत्रं पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केश इति श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tasyāṁ janayāmāsa hetī rākṣasapuṁgavaḥ
putraṁ putravatāṁ śreṣṭho vidyutkeśa iti śrutam

translations.english: And on her Heti-foremost of Rākşasas and best of those having sons-beget a son, known as Vidyutkeśa.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्युत्केशो हेतिपुत्रः प्रदीप्ताग्निसमप्रभः
व्यवर्धत महातेजास्तोयमध्य इवाम्बुजम्
verses.transliteration:
vidyutkeśo hetiputraḥ pradīptāgnisamaprabhaḥ
vyavardhata mahātejāstoyamadhya ivāmbujam

translations.english: Heti's son, the exceedingly energetic Vidyutkeśa, possessed of the splendour of the sun, grew up even like a lotus in water.

verses.sanskrit:
स यदा यौवनं भद्रमनुप्राप्तो निशाचरः
ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता
verses.transliteration:
sa yadā yauvanaṁ bhadramanuprāpto niśācaraḥ
tato dārakriyāṁ tasya kartuṁ vyavasitaḥ pitā

translations.english: And when that night-ranger arrived at proper youth, his sire turned his attention towards his marriage.

verses.sanskrit:
संध्यादुहितरं सोऽथ संध्यातुल्यां प्रभावतः
वरयामास पुत्रार्थं हेती राक्षसपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
saṁdhyāduhitaraṁ so'tha saṁdhyātulyāṁ prabhāvataḥ
varayāmāsa putrārthaṁ hetī rākṣasapuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: And that best of Rākṣasas-heti-in the interests of his son asked for the hand of Sandhya's daughter; like to Sandhyā* herself in the potency. * The evening Twilight-spouse of the Sun.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यमेव दातव्या परस्मै सेति संध्यया
चिन्तयित्वा सुता दत्ता विद्युत्केशाय राघव
verses.transliteration:
avaśyameva dātavyā parasmai seti saṁdhyayā
cintayitvā sutā dattā vidyutkeśāya rāghava

translations.english: Sandhya, reflecting that she needs must have to be given away by her, bestowed her on Vidyutkesa, O Raghava. Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-ranger Vidyutkeśa, sports with her even as Maghavan does with the daughter of Puloma.

verses.sanskrit:
केनचित्त्वथ कालेन राम सालकटंकटा
विद्युत्केशाद्गर्भमाप घनराजिरिवार्णवात्
verses.transliteration:
kenacittvatha kālena rāma sālakaṭaṁkaṭā
vidyutkeśādgarbhamāpa ghanarājirivārṇavāt

translations.english: It came to pass that after a length of time, O Răma, Sälakatankata was filled with child by Vidyutkeśa, as the clouds are furnished with water by the Ocean,

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सा राक्षसी गर्भं घनगर्भसमप्रभम्
प्रसूता मन्दरं गत्वा गङ्गा गर्भमिवाग्निजम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sā rākṣasī garbhaṁ ghanagarbhasamaprabham
prasūtā mandaraṁ gatvā gaṅgā garbhamivāgnijam

translations.english: Then repairing to Mandara, the Rākşasi brought forth her child, having the splendour of rain-charged clouds; even as Gangā had delivered herself of the child begotten by fire.* And having delivered herself of her offspring, she again became bent on disporting with Vidyutkeśa. *Mahesvara.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोत्सृष्टः स तु शिशुः शरदर्कसमद्युतिः
पाणिमास्ये समाधाय रुरोद घनराडिव
verses.transliteration:
tayotsṛṣṭaḥ sa tu śiśuḥ śaradarkasamadyutiḥ
pāṇimāsye samādhāya ruroda ghanarāḍiva

translations.english: And forsaken by them both, the infant furnished with the brightness of the autumnal sun, entering his clenched fist into his mouth, began to cry slowly.

verses.sanskrit:
अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवोऽक्षयोऽव्ययः
पुरमाकाशगं प्रादात्पार्वत्याः प्रियकाम्यया
verses.transliteration:
amaraṁ caiva taṁ kṛtvā mahādevo'kṣayo'vyayaḥ
puramākāśagaṁ prādātpārvatyāḥ priyakāmyayā

translations.english: Along with Uma, he saw the Raksasas's son, as he was crying. And sent by Pārvatī, whose heart was moved by by compassion, Bhava destroyer of Tripura-made that Raksasa's offspring attain the age of his mother, and conferred him immortality. And for compassing Parvati's pleasure, Mahadeva, indestructible and undeteriorating granted (the Raksasa) the power of ranging the air.

verses.sanskrit:
उमयापि वरो दत्तो राक्षसीनां नृपात्मज
सद्योपलब्धिर्गर्भस्य प्रसूतिः सद्य एव च
सद्य एव वयःप्राप्तिर्मातुरेव वयः समम्
verses.transliteration:
umayāpi varo datto rākṣasīnāṁ nṛpātmaja
sadyopalabdhirgarbhasya prasūtiḥ sadya eva ca
sadya eva vayaḥprāptirmātureva vayaḥ samam

translations.english: O son of the king, Umă also bestowed a boon: “Henceforth the Rāksasis shall conceive in a day, bring forth (child) in a day, and the child shall in a day be furnished with the age of its mother.'

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः; श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः
चचार सर्वत्र महामतिः खगः; खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरंदरो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sukeśo varadānagarvitaḥ; śriyaṁ prabhoḥ prāpya harasya pārśvataḥ
cacāra sarvatra mahāmatiḥ khagaḥ; khagaṁ puraṁ prāpya puraṁdaro yathā

translations.english: Then the great and magnanimous Sukeśa, puffed up with the receipt of boons, having obtained auspiciousness at the hands of the lord, Hara, began to range everywhere, even as Purandara did on having obtained heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम्
ग्रामणीर्नाम गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुसमप्रभः
verses.transliteration:
sukeśaṁ dhārmikaṁ dṛṣṭvā varalabdhaṁ ca rākṣasam
grāmaṇīrnāma gandharvo viśvāvasusamaprabhaḥ

translations.english: Cveing Sukeśa righteous and furnished with the boon, a virtuous Gandharva, named Grāmani, of the effulgence of fire, who had a daughter, called Devavati, like to a second Sri herself, famed over the three worlds, and endowed with beauty and youth, bestowed her on Sukeśa as if he had bestowed the goddess of fortune of the Rākşasa.

verses.sanskrit:
वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम्
आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः
verses.transliteration:
varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṁ sā taṁ prāpya patiṁ priyam
āsīddevavatī tuṣṭā dhanaṁ prāpyeva nirdhanaḥ

translations.english: And like an indigent person on obtaining wealth, Devavati, on obtaining her beloved husband, affluent in consequence of having received the boon, was (greatly) delighted. And in her company, that night-ranger appeared graceful, even as a mighty elephant sprung from Añjanā* does in the company of a she-elephant. *The designation of an elephant.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयो लोका इवाव्यग्राः स्थितास्त्रय इवाग्नयः
त्रयो मन्त्रा इवात्युग्रास्त्रयो घोरा इवामयाः
verses.transliteration:
trayo lokā ivāvyagrāḥ sthitāstraya ivāgnayaḥ
trayo mantrā ivātyugrāstrayo ghorā ivāmayāḥ

translations.english: That lord of Rākşasas begot (on her) three sons, resembling his three eyes the Raksasas, Mālyavän, Sumāli and that foremost of the strong-Māli; all resembling the three worlds possessing themselves in calmness; like to the three Fires established; fierce like to the three mantras, dreadful like three diseases springing respectively from morbid Air, Bile and Phlegm.* *The entire edifice of Hindu Pathology is based on the three-fold division of the morbid humours into Air, Bile and Phlegm. This division, albeit it may appear crude and unscientific to Europeans, taken all, in all, wonderfully answers its purpose. The tact displayed by Hindu physicians in diagnosing diseases on this method is wonderful. From feeling the Pulse alone, a Hindu physician, getting at the predominance of one or more morbid humours of the system, can accurately ascertain a patient's health. The infallibility with which predictions of death are generally made, attests the scientific soundness of the division in question, and renders superfluous any elaborate argument in its defence.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयः सुकेशस्य सुतास्त्रेताग्निसमवर्चसः
विवृद्धिमगमंस्तत्र व्याधयोपेक्षिता इव
verses.transliteration:
trayaḥ sukeśasya sutāstretāgnisamavarcasaḥ
vivṛddhimagamaṁstatra vyādhayopekṣitā iva

translations.english: The three sons of Sukeśa, having the energy of the three fires, grew up like a disease which has been disregarded.

verses.sanskrit:
वरप्राप्तिं पितुस्ते तु ज्ञात्वैश्वर्यं ततो महत्
तपस्तप्तुं गता मेरुं भ्रातरः कृतनिश्चयाः
verses.transliteration:
varaprāptiṁ pituste tu jñātvaiśvaryaṁ tato mahat
tapastaptuṁ gatā meruṁ bhrātaraḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ

translations.english: And learning that their father had received a boon by virtue of his power proceeding from asceticism, the brothers, firmly resolved, went to Meru for practising penances.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रगृह्य नियमान्घोरान्राक्षसा नृपसत्तम
विचेरुस्ते तपो घोरं सर्वभूतभयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
pragṛhya niyamānghorānrākṣasā nṛpasattama
viceruste tapo ghoraṁ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham

translations.english: And adopting rigid restrictions, the Rākṣasas, O best of kings, entered upon austerities, terrible, and capable of arousing the fear of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यार्जवदमोपेतैस्तपोभिर्भुवि दुष्करैः
संतापयन्तस्त्रीँल्लोकान्सदेवासुरमानुषान्
verses.transliteration:
satyārjavadamopetaistapobhirbhuvi duṣkaraiḥ
saṁtāpayantastrī̐llokānsadevāsuramānuṣān

translations.english: Practising penances rare on the earth with truth and candour and self-control, they afflicted the three worlds with gods, Asuras and human beings.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विभुश्चतुर्वक्त्रो विमानवरमास्थितः
सुकेशपुत्रानामन्त्र्य वरदोऽस्मीत्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
tato vibhuścaturvaktro vimānavaramāsthitaḥ
sukeśaputrānāmantrya varado'smītyabhāṣata

translations.english: Then that lord-the four-faced one-stationed on a superb car, addressed Sukeśa's sons, saying, “I am for conferring boons (on you).'

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्माणं वरदं ज्ञात्वा सेन्द्रैर्देवगणैर्वृतम्
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव द्रुमाः
verses.transliteration:
brahmāṇaṁ varadaṁ jñātvā sendrairdevagaṇairvṛtam
ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve vepamānā iva drumāḥ

translations.english: Knowing that Brahmā surrounded by Indra and the other celestials was ready to bestow boons, they, with joined hands, said, trembling like trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम्
अजेयाः शत्रुहन्तारस्तथैव चिरजीविनः
प्रभविष्णवो भवामेति परस्परमनुव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
tapasārādhito deva yadi no diśase varam
ajeyāḥ śatruhantārastathaiva cirajīvinaḥ
prabhaviṣṇavo bhavāmeti parasparamanuvratāḥ

translations.english: O god! that have been adored through asceticism, if you do intend to confer on us a boon, let us be invincible, capable of slaying foes, immortal, lordly, and ever devoted to each other.'

verses.sanskrit:
वरं लब्ध्वा ततः सर्वे राम रात्रिंचरास्तदा
सुरासुरान्प्रबाधन्ते वरदानात्सुनिर्भयाः
verses.transliteration:
varaṁ labdhvā tataḥ sarve rāma rātriṁcarāstadā
surāsurānprabādhante varadānātsunirbhayāḥ

translations.english: Thereat saying 'So be it,' to the sons of Sukeśa, the lord Brahmā, (ever) cherishing Brāhmaṇas with affection, went to the Brahmā regions. O Rāma, having obtained the boons, those night-rangers, rendered intrepid in consequences of having the boon conferred on them, began to disturb celestials and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit:
तैर्वध्यमानास्त्रिदशाः सर्षिसंघाः सचारणाः
त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति निरयस्था यथा नराः
verses.transliteration:
tairvadhyamānāstridaśāḥ sarṣisaṁghāḥ sacāraṇāḥ
trātāraṁ nādhigacchanti nirayasthā yathā narāḥ

translations.english: And like to men abiding in hell, the celestials, chāraṇas and hosts of sages, being harassed (by Raksasas), did not find any deliverer. And then, O foremost of the Raghus, the Raksasas, assembled together, joyfully said to the undeteriorating Viśvakarmá—prince of artist.

verses.sanskrit:
दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः
शिखरे तस्य शैलस्य मध्यमेऽम्बुदसंनिभे
शकुनैरपि दुष्प्रापे टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि
verses.transliteration:
dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre trikūṭo nāma parvataḥ
śikhare tasya śailasya madhyame'mbudasaṁnibhe
śakunairapi duṣprāpe ṭaṅkacchinnacaturdiśi

translations.english: On the midmost peak of that mountain resembling clouds, inaccessible even to the fowls of the air, all the four quarters have been hewn with bones.* If I am desired by you, I can construct the city of Lanka (there), having an area of thirty Yojanas, and measuring an hundred in length; surrounded with a golden wall and furnished with golden gateways. *Tanka-may also mean a hatchet or a sword.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यां वसत दुर्धर्षाः पुर्यां राक्षससत्तमाः
अमरावतीं समासाद्य सेन्द्रा इव दिवौकसः
verses.transliteration:
tasyāṁ vasata durdharṣāḥ puryāṁ rākṣasasattamāḥ
amarāvatīṁ samāsādya sendrā iva divaukasaḥ

translations.english: In her do-you dwell, you irrepressible ones, you foremost of Rākşasas; even as do the elestials with Indra, approaching Amaravati.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्कादुर्गं समासाद्य राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृताः
भविष्यथ दुराधर्षाः शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनाः
verses.transliteration:
laṅkādurgaṁ samāsādya rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtāḥ
bhaviṣyatha durādharṣāḥ śatrūṇāṁ śatrusūdanāḥ

translations.english: And occupying the citadel of Lankā, backed by innumerable Rākṣasas, you will be invincible to foes and capable of destroying them.'

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वकर्मवचः श्रुत्वा ततस्ते राम राक्षसाः
सहस्रानुचरा गत्वा लङ्कां तामवसन्पुरीम्
verses.transliteration:
viśvakarmavacaḥ śrutvā tataste rāma rākṣasāḥ
sahasrānucarā gatvā laṅkāṁ tāmavasanpurīm

translations.english: Hearing Viśvakarmā's speech, those foremost of Rākṣasas, accompanied by thousands of followers, went to the palace and set-up in the same, having a strong wall and a moat, abounding in hundreds of golden edifices. And obtaining Lanka, the night-rangers, exceedingly delighted, began to dwell therein.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्येष्ठक्रमेण सा तेषां राक्षसानामराक्षसी
कन्यास्ताः प्रददौ हृष्टा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः
verses.transliteration:
jyeṣṭhakrameṇa sā teṣāṁ rākṣasānāmarākṣasī
kanyāstāḥ pradadau hṛṣṭā pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ

translations.english: At this time, O Rāghava, there lived at her pleasure a Gandharvi, named Narmadā. O son of Raghu, She hai three daughters, resembling Sri, Hri, and kirti in splendour. And albeit no Rāks asi herself, she, beginning with the eldest, gladly married to the Räkşasas her daughter having faces resembling the full moon.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयाणां राक्षसेन्द्राणां तिस्रो गन्धर्वकन्यकाः
मात्रा दत्ता महाभागा नक्षत्रे भगदैवते
verses.transliteration:
trayāṇāṁ rākṣasendrāṇāṁ tisro gandharvakanyakāḥ
mātrā dattā mahābhāgā nakṣatre bhagadaivate

translations.english: And under the influence of the star, Bhagadaivata, those three exalted daughters of a Gandharvi were respectively conferred by their mother on the three several Raksasas of eminence.

verses.sanskrit:
कृतदारास्तु ते राम सुकेशतनयाः प्रभो
भार्याभिः सह चिक्रीडुरप्सरोभिरिवामराः
verses.transliteration:
kṛtadārāstu te rāma sukeśatanayāḥ prabho
bhāryābhiḥ saha cikrīḍurapsarobhirivāmarāḥ

translations.english: And having wedded, O Rama, Sukesa's sons began to sport with their wives, like celestials sporting with Apsarās.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी
स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत्
verses.transliteration:
tatra mālyavato bhāryā sundarī nāma sundarī
sa tasyāṁ janayāmāsa yadapatyaṁ nibodha tat

translations.english: Malyavän's beautiful spouse was named Sundari. On her he begot, do you understand, whom.

verses.sanskrit:
वज्रमुष्टिर्विरूपाक्षो दुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः
सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च मत्तोन्मत्तौ तथैव च
अनला चाभवत्कन्या सुन्दर्यां राम सुन्दरी
verses.transliteration:
vajramuṣṭirvirūpākṣo durmukhaścaiva rākṣasaḥ
suptaghno yajñakopaśca mattonmattau tathaiva ca
analā cābhavatkanyā sundaryāṁ rāma sundarī

translations.english: Vajramuşti, and Virūpākşa, and the Räksasa Durmukha, and Suptaghna, and Yajñakopa, and Matta and Unmatta; and, O Rāma, there was also born a lovely daughter of Sundari, Anala. And Sumāli's wife of face like the full Moon, named Ketumati, was dearer to him than his life itself.

verses.sanskrit:
संह्रादिः प्रघसश्चैव भासकर्णश्च राक्षसः
राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिता
कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः
verses.transliteration:
saṁhrādiḥ praghasaścaiva bhāsakarṇaśca rākṣasaḥ
rākā puṣpotkaṭā caiva kaikasī ca śucismitā
kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ

translations.english: O mighty king, do you, gradually, know the offspring that were begot by Sumāli on Ketumatī-Prahasta and Akampana, and Vikata, and Kālikāmukha, and DhumrāKșa, and Danda, and the redoubtable Supārsva, and Sañhrãi, and Praghasa, and the Rākşasa, Bhāsakarņa, and Rākā, and Pushpotkată, and Kaikasi of luminous smiles, and Kumbhinasi these are known as the offspring of Sumali. Māli had for wife a graceful Gandharvi, named Vasudă having having eyes resembling lotus-petals, of a lovely look and like to the most magnificent Yakși of them all.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमालेरनुजस्तस्यां जनयामास यत्प्रभो
अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तन्मया त्वं शृणु राघव
verses.transliteration:
sumāleranujastasyāṁ janayāmāsa yatprabho
apatyaṁ kathyamānaṁ tanmayā tvaṁ śṛṇu rāghava

translations.english: Do you, O master, listen to me as I mention to you, O Raghava the offspring that Sumali's younger brother beget on her, Anala, and Nila, and Sampāti. These night-rangers sons to Mali were the courtiers of Vibhișana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुंगवास्त्रयो; निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृताः
सुरान्सहेन्द्रानृषिनागदानवा;न्बबाधिरे ते बलवीर्यदर्पिताः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu te rākṣasapuṁgavāstrayo; niśācaraiḥ putraśataiśca saṁvṛtāḥ
surānsahendrānṛṣināgadānavā;nbabādhire te balavīryadarpitāḥ

translations.english: And those three foremost of Rākṣasa, accompanied by hundreds of sons night rangers all-elated on account of their measureless prowess, began to worry the sages and serpents and Yakşas, and celestials with Indra (at their head).

verses.sanskrit:
जगद्भ्रमन्तोऽनिलवद्दुरासदा; रणे च मृत्युप्रतिमाः समाहिताः
वरप्रदानादभिगर्विता भृशं; क्रतुक्रियाणां प्रशमंकराः सदा
verses.transliteration:
jagadbhramanto'nilavaddurāsadā; raṇe ca mṛtyupratimāḥ samāhitāḥ
varapradānādabhigarvitā bhṛśaṁ; kratukriyāṇāṁ praśamaṁkarāḥ sadā

translations.english: Incapable of being confronted (in battle), these resembling Death himself in energy, wondrous elated in consequences of the boon having been conferred on them, ranging the world like to the Wind, were ever engaged in disturbing the sacrifices (of the sages).

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः
प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधन
verses.transliteration:
sukeśaputrairbhagavanpitāmahavaroddhataiḥ
prajādhyakṣa prajāḥ sarvā bādhyante ripubādhana

translations.english: O reverend one, the creatures of the lord of creatures are being (sorely) troubled by the sons of Sukesa, given to harassing their foes,-swolen with insolence on account of the benn conferred on them by the great-father, asylums, constituting our refuges,-have been divested of their power of granting shelter, and driving off the deities from the etherial regions, they are sporting there like the immortals.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम्
अहं यमोऽहं वरुणश्चन्द्रोऽहं रविरप्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ viṣṇurahaṁ rudro brahmāhaṁ devarāḍaham
ahaṁ yamo'haṁ varuṇaścandro'haṁ ravirapyaham

translations.english: 'I am Vişnu,' 'I am Rudra,' 'I am the king of the celestials,' 'I am Yama,' 'I an Varuna,' 'I am the moon,' 'I am the Sun,' flattering themselves in this fashion, Māli and Sumāli and the Rākşasa Malyavān as well as those going before them, are annoying (the gods), breathing exhilaration of martial spirits.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्नो देवभयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि
अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि दैवतकण्टकान्
verses.transliteration:
tanno devabhayārtānāmabhayaṁ dātumarhasi
aśivaṁ vapurāsthāya jahi daivatakaṇṭakān

translations.english: Therefore, O god, it behove you to liberate us from fear, who have been greatly tormented by it. Do you, assuming your terrific form, slay the thorns of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः
सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्ष आह देवगणान्प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
ityuktastu suraiḥ sarvaiḥ kapardī nīlalohitaḥ
sukeśaṁ prati sāpekṣa āha devagaṇānprabhuḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed by the immortals in a body, that lord, Kaparddi of red-blue hue, reflecting that it would be wrong for him to destroy Sukesa (with his own hands), spoke to the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं तान्निहनिष्यामि अवध्या मम तेऽसुराः
किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
nāhaṁ tānnihaniṣyāmi avadhyā mama te'surāḥ
kiṁ tu mantraṁ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati

translations.english: I shall not slay them, you gods; they are incapable of being slain by me. But I shall unfold to you the way in which they will be destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य सुरर्षभाः
गच्छन्तु शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
evameva samudyogaṁ puraskṛtya surarṣabhāḥ
gacchantu śaraṇaṁ viṣṇuṁ haniṣyati sa tānprabhuḥ

translations.english: Do you, you Maharsis, in the heat of this affairs, seck the shelter of Visnu. That lord will slay them.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम्
विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः
verses.transliteration:
tataste jayaśabdena pratinandya maheśvaram
viṣṇoḥ samīpamājagmurniśācarabhayārditāḥ

translations.english: Thereat, saluting Maheśvara with the sounds of Jaya, (the celestial) afflicted with the fear of the night-rangers, presented themselves before Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च
ऊचुः संभ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयार्दिताः
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhacakradharaṁ devaṁ praṇamya bahumānya ca
ūcuḥ saṁbhrāntavadvākyaṁ sukeśatanayārditāḥ

translations.english: And bowing down to the god holding the conch, discus and mace, and paying him high homage, they, greatly flurried, addressed him about the sons of Sukeśa, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसंनिभैः
आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहृतानि नः
verses.transliteration:
sukeśatanayairdeva tribhistretāgnisaṁnibhaiḥ
ākramya varadānena sthānānyapahṛtāni naḥ

translations.english: O god, by virtue of the boon (that has been bestowed on them), resembling the three fires, Sukesa's three sons, assailing us, have deprived us of our abode.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता
तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः
verses.transliteration:
laṅkā nāma purī durgā trikūṭaśikhare sthitā
tatra sthitāḥ prabādhante sarvānnaḥ kṣaṇadācarāḥ

translations.english: There is a city named Lankā, stationed on the top of Trikuta, (extremely) difficult of entrance. Taking up their station at that place, the nightrangers in a body pursue us.

verses.sanskrit:
भयेष्वभयदोऽस्माकं नान्योऽस्ति भवता समः
नुद त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः
verses.transliteration:
bhayeṣvabhayado'smākaṁ nānyo'sti bhavatā samaḥ
nuda tvaṁ no bhayaṁ deva nīhāramiva bhāskaraḥ

translations.english: Slay in encounter the elated Rākşasas along with their adherents; and even as the sun dried up dew, do you dispel this fear of ours.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः
अभयं भयदोऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ daivatairukto devadevo janārdanaḥ
abhayaṁ bhayado'rīṇāṁ dattvā devānuvāca ha

translations.english: Thus accosted by the deities, that god of gods Janārdana who brings fear to foes cheering up the celestial up the celestials, said to them.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम्
तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान्
verses.transliteration:
sukeśaṁ rākṣasaṁ jāne īśānavaradarpitam
tāṁścāsya tanayāñjāne yeṣāṁ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa mālyavān

translations.english: 'I know the Raksasa, Sukesa, as flushed with the boon bestowed by Iśāna. And I also know his sons, of whom Mālyavān is the eldest. Those worst if Rākṣasas that have over-riden your dignity will I, wrought up with wrath, slay (in battle); therefore, you gods, be of good cheer.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
यथा वासं ययुर्हृष्टाः प्रशमन्तो जनार्दनम्
verses.transliteration:
ityuktāste surāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
yathā vāsaṁ yayurhṛṣṭāḥ praśamanto janārdanam

translations.english: Thus addressed by the mighty Vişņu, the gods, highly rejoiced, went to their respective quarters, extolling Janārdana.

verses.sanskrit:
विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवान्स निशाचरः
श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
vibudhānāṁ samudyogaṁ mālyavānsa niśācaraḥ
śrutvā tau bhrātarau vīrāvidaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: And hearing of the activity of the celestials; the night-rangers Mālyavân addressed his heroic brothers, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सुकेशतनया देव वरदानबलोद्धताः
बाधन्तेऽस्मान्समुद्युक्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे
verses.transliteration:
sukeśatanayā deva varadānabaloddhatāḥ
bādhante'smānsamudyuktā ghorarūpāḥ pade pade

translations.english: The immortals and sages, going to Sankara, spoke these words, desirous of our destruction, The terrific sons of Sukeśa, puffed up, and swollen on account of their strength flowing from the boon, are crossing us at every step.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म उमापते
स्वेषु वेश्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasairabhibhūtāḥ sma na śaktāḥ sma umāpate
sveṣu veśmasu saṁsthātuṁ bhayātteṣāṁ durātmanām

translations.english: We have been overpowered by the Rākṣasas. And, o lord of creatures, from fear of those wicked-minded ones, we cannot remain in our own homes.

verses.sanskrit:
तदस्माकं हितार्थे त्वं जहि तांस्तांस्त्रिलोचन
राक्षसान्हुंकृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर
verses.transliteration:
tadasmākaṁ hitārthe tvaṁ jahi tāṁstāṁstrilocana
rākṣasānhuṁkṛtenaiva daha pradahatāṁ vara

translations.english: Therefore, to do us good, do you, O threeeyed one, destroy them; and, O best of consuming ones, do you with your roars, burn them up.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः
शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
ityevaṁ tridaśairukto niśamyāndhakasūdanaḥ
śiraḥ karaṁ ca dhunvāna idaṁ vacanamabravīt

translations.english: Thus addressed by the deities, the slayer of Andhaka, hearing their speech, said, shaking his head and hands.

verses.sanskrit:
अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे
मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
avadhyā mama te devāḥ sukeśatanayā raṇe
mantraṁ tu vaḥ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati

translations.english: You gods, Sukesa's sons are incapable of being slain by me in battle. But I shall tell you the means whereby they may be slain.

verses.sanskrit:
यः स चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः
हनिष्यति स तान्युद्धे शरणं तं प्रपद्यथ
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ sa cakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ
haniṣyati sa tānyuddhe śaraṇaṁ taṁ prapadyatha

translations.english: Do you seek the shelter of him who hold the discus and mace in his hands, and who is clad in a yellow attire, of Janardana, Hari, even of the auspicious Nārāyaṇa.

verses.sanskrit:
हरान्नावाप्य ते कामं कामारिमभिवाद्य च
नारायणालयं प्राप्तास्तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन्
verses.transliteration:
harānnāvāpya te kāmaṁ kāmārimabhivādya ca
nārāyaṇālayaṁ prāptāstasmai sarvaṁ nyavedayan

translations.english: Having received this counsel of Hara, they, rendering reverence to that enemy of Kāma, came the abode of Nārāyana and communicated everything to him.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः
सुरारीन्सूदयिष्यामि सुरा भवत विज्वराः
verses.transliteration:
tato nārāyaṇenoktā devā indrapurogamāḥ
surārīnsūdayiṣyāmi surā bhavata vijvarāḥ

translations.english: Then Nārāyana spoke to the celestials with Indra at their head, I will slay those foes of the celestials. You gods, cast off all fear!

verses.sanskrit:
देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ
प्रतिज्ञातो वधोऽस्माकं तच्चिन्तयथ यत्क्षमम्
verses.transliteration:
devānāṁ bhayabhītānāṁ hariṇā rākṣasarṣabhau
pratijñāto vadho'smākaṁ taccintayatha yatkṣamam

translations.english: to O foremost of Rākşasas, Hari promised to the frightened celestials that he would slay us. Therefore do you think as to what is fit.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः
ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं भगांशाविव वासवम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sumālī mālī ca śrutvā mālyavato vacaḥ
ūcaturbhrātaraṁ jyeṣṭhaṁ bhagāṁśāviva vāsavam

translations.english: Thereat Sumāli and Māli, hearing the words of Malyavān, said to their eldest brother, like the Asvins addressing Vāsava.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं च ऐश्वर्यं परिपालितम्
आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं स्वधर्मः स्थापितश्च नः
verses.transliteration:
svadhītaṁ dattamiṣṭaṁ ca aiśvaryaṁ paripālitam
āyurnirāmayaṁ prāptaṁ svadharmaḥ sthāpitaśca naḥ

translations.english: We have studied, performed sacrifices, practised charity, and obtained riches; and attaining long health and long life, we have established sterling righteousness in our path.

verses.sanskrit:
देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रौघैः प्रविगाह्य च
जिता देवा रणे नित्यं न नो मृत्युकृतं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
devasāgaramakṣobhyaṁ śastraughaiḥ pravigāhya ca
jitā devā raṇe nityaṁ na no mṛtyukṛtaṁ bhayam

translations.english: With arms plunging into the sea of celestials, we have conquered our unrivalled enemies. Therefore, we have no fear touching death.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणश्च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा
अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्व एव हि बिभ्यति
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇaśca rudraśca śakraścāpi yamastathā
asmākaṁ pramukhe sthātuṁ sarva eva hi bibhyati

translations.english: Even Narayana and Rudra, Sakra and Yama, ever fear to stay before us (in the field).

verses.sanskrit:
विष्णोर्दोषश्च नास्त्यत्र कारणं राक्षसेश्वर
देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः
verses.transliteration:
viṣṇordoṣaśca nāstyatra kāraṇaṁ rākṣaseśvara
devānāmeva doṣeṇa viṣṇoḥ pracalitaṁ manaḥ

translations.english: O lord of Raksasas. There is no occasion for Visnu's displeasure of us. The mind of Visnu has wavered in consequence of the evil caused by the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादद्य समुद्युक्ताः सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः
देवानेव जिघांसामो येभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः
verses.transliteration:
tasmādadya samudyuktāḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtāḥ
devāneva jighāṁsāmo yebhyo doṣaḥ samutthitaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, will we even avenge ourselves on the gods, from whom has sprung this wrong.

verses.sanskrit:
इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवानग्रजः प्रभुः
उद्योगं घोषयित्वाथ राक्षसाः सर्व एव ते
युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धा जम्भवृत्रबला इव
verses.transliteration:
iti mālī sumālī ca mālyavānagrajaḥ prabhuḥ
udyogaṁ ghoṣayitvātha rākṣasāḥ sarva eva te
yuddhāya niryayuḥ kruddhā jambhavṛtrabalā iva

translations.english: Having taken counsel together, those powerful ones conciliated their forces. And proclaiming (their order) that preparations were to be made, all the foremost Nairtas sallied forth for battle, like to those led by Jambha and Vſtra.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ
भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः
verses.transliteration:
laṅkāviparyayaṁ dṛṣṭvā yāni laṅkālayānyatha
bhūtāni bhayadarśīni vimanaskāni sarvaśaḥ

translations.english: Perceiving the destruction of Lanka hand, those deities that had taken up their quarters there, everywhere were struck with fear and felt their spirits depressed.

verses.sanskrit:
भौमास्तथान्तरिक्षाश्च कालाज्ञप्ता भयावहाः
उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावायोत्थिता द्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
bhaumāstathāntarikṣāśca kālājñaptā bhayāvahāḥ
utpātā rākṣasendrāṇāmabhāvāyotthitā drutam

translations.english: At the command of Kala, terrible evil omens foreshadowing the destruction of the Raksasachief began to arise on the earth well as in the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्थीनि मेघा वर्षन्ति उष्णं शोणितमेव च
वेलां समुद्रोऽप्युत्क्रान्तश्चलन्ते चाचलोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration:
asthīni meghā varṣanti uṣṇaṁ śoṇitameva ca
velāṁ samudro'pyutkrāntaścalante cācalottamāḥ

translations.english: The clouds showered down bones and hot blood. The oceans overleapt their continents and the mountains shook.

verses.sanskrit:
गृध्रचक्रं महच्चापि ज्वलनोद्गारिभिर्मुखैः
राक्षसानामुपरि वै भ्रमते कालचक्रवत्
verses.transliteration:
gṛdhracakraṁ mahaccāpi jvalanodgāribhirmukhaiḥ
rākṣasānāmupari vai bhramate kālacakravat

translations.english: Creatures were one after another seen to drop down; and mighty swarms of vultures, with mouths belching forth flames, began to wheel over the Raksasa, like to Kala himself.

verses.sanskrit:
तानचिन्त्य महोत्पातान्राक्षसा बलगर्विताः
यन्त्येव न निवर्तन्ते मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः
verses.transliteration:
tānacintya mahotpātānrākṣasā balagarvitāḥ
yantyeva na nivartante mṛtyupāśāvapāśitāḥ

translations.english: But fast bound with the noose of Death, the Raksasas, proud of their strength, disregarding these omens, march on, and do not stay their course, Mälyavān and Sumāli possessed of prodigious strength, going before the Raksasas, like flaming fires.

verses.sanskrit:
माल्यवन्तं तु ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम्
निशाचरा आश्रयन्ते धातारमिव देहिनः
verses.transliteration:
mālyavantaṁ tu te sarve mālyavantamivācalam
niśācarā āśrayante dhātāramiva dehinaḥ

translations.english: Even as the gods take refuge under Dhātā, the night-rangers take refuge under Mālyavân resembling the mountain, Mälyavān.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम्
जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ माली वशे स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
tadbalaṁ rākṣasendrāṇāṁ mahābhraghananāditam
jayepsayā devalokaṁ yayau mālī vaśe sthitam

translations.english: Under the command of Māli that host of Raksasas, roaring like mighty clouds, inspired with the desire of victory, went to the celestial regions.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः
देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य दध्रे युद्धे ततो मनः
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ samudyogaṁ taṁ tu nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
devadūtādupaśrutya dadhre yuddhe tato manaḥ

translations.english: The lord Nārāyana, hearing of the preparations of the Rākşasas from a celestial messenger, set his heart on fight. And equipped with weapons and quivers, he mounted on Vinata's offspring.* *Garuda, Narayana's vehicle.

verses.sanskrit:
स देवसिद्धर्षिमहोरगैश्च; गन्धर्वमुख्याप्सरसोपगीतः
समाससादामरशत्रुसैन्यं; चक्रासिसीरप्रवरादिधारी
verses.transliteration:
sa devasiddharṣimahoragaiśca; gandharvamukhyāpsarasopagītaḥ
samāsasādāmaraśatrusainyaṁ; cakrāsisīrapravarādidhārī

translations.english: And hymned by Siddhas and celestials and sages and mighty (semi-divine) serpents and Gandharvas and Yakşas, the enemy of the Asura hosts presented himself, bearing in his hands the discus, sword, that weapon Śärnga and the conch.

verses.sanskrit:
सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं; भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम्
चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं; चलोपलो नील इवाचलेन्द्रः
verses.transliteration:
suparṇapakṣānilanunnapakṣaṁ; bhramatpatākaṁ pravikīrṇaśastram
cacāla tadrākṣasarājasainyaṁ; calopalo nīla ivācalendraḥ

translations.english: The Raksasa-hosts, struck by the wind produced by the wings of Suparņa, with their pennons swinging to and fro and their weapons scattered about, quaked like the blue summit of a mountain with its crags tossed about.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शितैः शोणितमांसरूषितै;र्युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः
निशाचराः संपरिवार्य माधवं; वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śitaiḥ śoṇitamāṁsarūṣitai;ryugāntavaiśvānaratulyavigrahaiḥ
niśācarāḥ saṁparivārya mādhavaṁ; varāyudhairnirbibhiduḥ sahasraśaḥ
