translations.english: Then the night-rangers, hemming in Madhava,* began to pierce him with thousands of excellent sharpened weapons dyed in flesh and blood, and resembling the fire of Doomsday. *One of the many designations of Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणगिरिं ते तु गर्जन्तो राक्षसाम्बुदाः
अवर्षन्निषुवर्षेण वर्षेणाद्रिमिवाम्बुदाः
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇagiriṁ te tu garjanto rākṣasāmbudāḥ
avarṣanniṣuvarṣeṇa varṣeṇādrimivāmbudāḥ

translations.english: As clouds assail a mountain with showers, then the Raksasas, representing clouds, setting up shouts, began to assail Nārāyaṇa representing a mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
श्यामावदातस्तैर्विष्णुर्नीलैर्नक्तंचरोत्तमैः
वृतोऽञ्जनगिरीवासीद्वर्षमाणैः पयोधरैः
verses.transliteration:
śyāmāvadātastairviṣṇurnīlairnaktaṁcarottamaiḥ
vṛto'ñjanagirīvāsīdvarṣamāṇaiḥ payodharaiḥ

translations.english: Visnu of a bright brown-blue hue, being surrounded by the flower of the night-rangers with dark visages, resembled the Añjana mountain, on which the clouds pour down.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ता वज्रानिलमनोजवाः
हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोकास्तमिव पर्यये
verses.transliteration:
tathā rakṣodhanurmuktā vajrānilamanojavāḥ
hariṁ viśanti sma śarā lokāstamiva paryaye

translations.english: As locusts (flood) a field, knots (throng) about a flame, gad-flies (cluster) around a pot of honey, or makaras (range) in the sea, so the shafts shot by the bows of the Rākṣasa, having (the energy of) the thunder-bolt and endowed with (the velocity of) the wind or thought, pierce Hari as if at the universal dissolution.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसेन्द्रा गिरिनिभाः शरशक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः
निरुच्छ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायाम इव द्विजम्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasendrā girinibhāḥ śaraśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ
nirucchvāsaṁ hariṁ cakruḥ prāṇāyāma iva dvijam

translations.english: Those mounted on cars (assailed him) with their cars, and those mounted on the backs of elephants (assailed him) with their elephants, and those riding horses (assailed him) with their horses, and the foot-soldiers attacked him, stationed in the sky; and the foremost of Rākşasas resembling mountains, by means of darts, rstis and tomaras, suspended the respiration of Hari even as the prāņāyāma* does that of a twice-born one. *The practice of regulation respiration and finally suspending the same. This is practised by the Yogis of India, who attribute wonderful virtues to it.

verses.sanskrit:
शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्वज्रवक्त्रैर्मनोजवैः
चिच्छेद तिलशो विष्णुः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭairvajravaktrairmanojavaiḥ
ciccheda tilaśo viṣṇuḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: With sharpened arrows resembling the thunder, and endowed with the velocity of the wind, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch, Visnu cut off (Raksasas) by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्राव्य शरवर्षं तं वर्षं वायुरिवोत्थितम्
पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्खं प्रदध्मौ पुरुषोत्तमः
verses.transliteration:
vidrāvya śaravarṣaṁ taṁ varṣaṁ vāyurivotthitam
pāñcajanyaṁ mahāśaṅkhaṁ pradadhmau puruṣottamaḥ

translations.english: And dashing away (the Rākṣasa ranks) with his arrowy shower, even as the wind aroused dashes away a downpour, that best of male beings blew his mighty conch Pāñcajanya.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽम्बुजो हरिणा ध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट्
ररास भीमनिह्रादो युगान्ते जलदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
so'mbujo hariṇā dhmātaḥ sarvaprāṇena śaṅkharāṭ
rarāsa bhīmanihrādo yugānte jalado yathā

translations.english: Winded by Hari with his utmost might, that water-sprung king of conchs, endowed with terrific blares, roared, as if afflicting the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खराजरवः सोऽथ त्रासयामास राक्षसान्
मृगराज इवारण्ये समदानिव कुञ्जरान्
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkharājaravaḥ so'tha trāsayāmāsa rākṣasān
mṛgarāja ivāraṇye samadāniva kuñjarān

translations.english: The sounds of that king of conchs struck terror into the Rākşasas, even as in a mighty forest a lion (strikes terror into the hearts of) elephants in rut.

verses.sanskrit:
न शेकुरश्वाः संस्थातुं विमदाः कुञ्जराभवन्
स्यन्दनेभ्यश्च्युता योधाः शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः
verses.transliteration:
na śekuraśvāḥ saṁsthātuṁ vimadāḥ kuñjarābhavan
syandanebhyaścyutā yodhāḥ śaṅkharāvitadurbalāḥ

translations.english: Thereat the horses could not keep their ground, and the elephants were reſt of their temporal flow, and shorn of their virtue at the roars of the conch, heroes began to topple down from their cars.

verses.sanskrit:
शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ता वज्रतुल्याननाः शराः
विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम्
verses.transliteration:
śārṅgacāpavinirmuktā vajratulyānanāḥ śarāḥ
vidārya tāni rakṣāṁsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim

translations.english: And dight with dainty feathered parts having heads, the shafts discharged from the śārnga, resembling thunder-bolts, riving those Rākşása, entered the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
भिद्यमानाः शरैश्चान्ये नारायणधनुश्च्युतैः
निपेतू राक्षसा भीमाः शैला वज्रहता इव
verses.transliteration:
bhidyamānāḥ śaraiścānye nārāyaṇadhanuścyutaiḥ
nipetū rākṣasā bhīmāḥ śailā vajrahatā iva

translations.english: In that conflict, pierced by the arrows discharged from Nārāyana's arm, the Rākşasa began to drop to the ground like mountains struck with the thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit:
व्रणैर्व्रणकरारीणामधोक्षजशरोद्भवैः
असृक्क्षरन्ति धाराभिः स्वर्णधारामिवाचलाः
verses.transliteration:
vraṇairvraṇakarārīṇāmadhokṣajaśarodbhavaiḥ
asṛkkṣaranti dhārābhiḥ svarṇadhārāmivācalāḥ

translations.english: The wounds on the persons of the foes inflicted by the discus of Vişnu discharge blood in streams, like mountains discharging streams of red chalk.

verses.sanskrit:
शङ्खराजरवश्चापि शार्ङ्गचापरवस्तथा
राक्षसानां रवांश्चापि ग्रसते वैष्णवो रवः
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkharājaravaścāpi śārṅgacāparavastathā
rākṣasānāṁ ravāṁścāpi grasate vaiṣṇavo ravaḥ

translations.english: The sound of that king of conchs, as well as those of the Sārnga, combined with the roars emitted by Vişņu himself, swallowed up the roars of the Rākşasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा बाणा विनिर्मुक्ताः शार्ङ्गान्नरायणेरिताः
निर्धावन्तीषवस्तूर्णं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration:
tathā bāṇā vinirmuktāḥ śārṅgānnarāyaṇeritāḥ
nirdhāvantīṣavastūrṇaṁ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ

translations.english: Like fierce rays streaming about from sun, like torrents dashing from the ocean, like elephants coming adown a mountain, or like showers descending from clouds, the shafts shot by Nārāyaṇa pursue (the foes) by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसानां सहस्राणि निहत्य मधुसूदनः
वारिजं नादयामास तोयदं सुरराडिव
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasānāṁ sahasrāṇi nihatya madhusūdanaḥ
vārijaṁ nādayāmāsa toyadaṁ surarāḍiva

translations.english: Then, having despatched thousands of Rākşasas, the destroyer of Madhu blew his water-sprung (conch), even as the sovereign of the celestials filleth clouds (with rain).

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणशरग्रस्तं शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम्
ययौ लङ्कामभिमुखं प्रभग्नं राक्षसं बलम्
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇaśaragrastaṁ śaṅkhanādasuvihvalam
yayau laṅkāmabhimukhaṁ prabhagnaṁ rākṣasaṁ balam

translations.english: Agitated by the arrows of Nārāyaṇa, with their senses bewildered by the blares of the conch, the broken Raksasa forces made for Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रभग्ने राक्षसबले नारायणशराहते
सुमाली शरवर्षेण आववार रणे हरिम्
verses.transliteration:
prabhagne rākṣasabale nārāyaṇaśarāhate
sumālī śaravarṣeṇa āvavāra raṇe harim

translations.english: On the Rākşasa army having been broken in consequence of the beating it got at the hands of Nārāyaṇa, Sumāli with showers of shafts resisted Hari in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्क्षिप्य हेमाभरणं करं करमिव द्विपः
ररास राक्षसो हर्षात्सतडित्तोयदो यथा
verses.transliteration:
utkṣipya hemābharaṇaṁ karaṁ karamiva dvipaḥ
rarāsa rākṣaso harṣātsataḍittoyado yathā

translations.english: As an elephant flourishes its trunk, that Rāks asa, lifting up his arm adorned with ornaments, began to roar from rapture, like a mass of clouds, lighted up with lightening.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमालेर्नर्दतस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्
चिच्छेद यन्तुरश्वाश्च भ्रान्तास्तस्य तु रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
sumālernardatastasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam
ciccheda yanturaśvāśca bhrāntāstasya tu rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: And (Visņu) cut off the head flaming with ear rings of the charioteer of the shouting Sumáli; and thereat the horses of that Raksasa aimlessly strayed hither and thither.

verses.sanskrit:
तैरश्वैर्भ्राम्यते भ्रान्तैः सुमाली राक्षसेश्वरः
इन्द्रियाश्वैर्यथा भ्रान्तैर्धृतिहीनो यथा नरः
verses.transliteration:
tairaśvairbhrāmyate bhrāntaiḥ sumālī rākṣaseśvaraḥ
indriyāśvairyathā bhrāntairdhṛtihīno yathā naraḥ

translations.english: And with his bewildered steeds Sumali wanders like a person deprived of patience, whose senses are under hallucination.

verses.sanskrit:
माली चाभ्यद्रवद्युद्धे प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः
मालेर्धनुश्च्युता बाणाः कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः
विविशुर्हरिमासाद्य क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव
verses.transliteration:
mālī cābhyadravadyuddhe pragṛhya saśaraṁ dhanuḥ
mālerdhanuścyutā bāṇāḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitāḥ
viviśurharimāsādya krauñcaṁ patrarathā iva

translations.english: Like birds entering the Krauñca mountain, the arrows discharged from Mali's bow, graced with gold, hit Hari and entered (into his body).

verses.sanskrit:
अर्द्यमानः शरैः सोऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः
चुक्षुभे न रणे विष्णुर्जितेन्द्रिय इवाधिभिः
verses.transliteration:
ardyamānaḥ śaraiḥ so'tha mālimuktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
cukṣubhe na raṇe viṣṇurjitendriya ivādhibhiḥ

translations.english: Thereat, as a person holding his senses under subjection is not thrown out of his mental balance, Vişnu, assailed in that encounter with thousands of arrows shot by Māli, was not disturbed ever so little.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ मौर्वी स्वनं कृत्वा भगवान्भूतभावनः
मालिनं प्रति बाणौघान्ससर्जासिगदाधरः
verses.transliteration:
atha maurvī svanaṁ kṛtvā bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ
mālinaṁ prati bāṇaughānsasarjāsigadādharaḥ

translations.english: Then that creator of all beings, the reverend Gadādhara,* twanging his bow-string, showered volleys of shafts on Máli. *Lit. the holder of the mace, a name of Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
ते मालिदेहमासाद्य वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः शराः
पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव पुरामृतम्
verses.transliteration:
te mālidehamāsādya vajravidyutprabhāḥ śarāḥ
pibanti rudhiraṁ tasya nāgā iva purāmṛtam

translations.english: And getting at Mali's body, the arrows furnished with the luminousness of lightening drink his blood, like to serpents drinking nectar.

verses.sanskrit:
मालिनं विमुखं कृत्वा मालिमौलिं हरिर्बलात्
रथं च सध्वजं चापं वाजिनश्च न्यपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
mālinaṁ vimukhaṁ kṛtvā mālimauliṁ harirbalāt
rathaṁ ca sadhvajaṁ cāpaṁ vājinaśca nyapātayat

translations.english: And baffling Māli, the holder of the conch, discus, and mace, brought down Māli's crown, standard, bow and steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
विरथस्तु गदां गृह्य माली नक्तंचरोत्तमः
आपुप्लुवे गदापाणिर्गिर्यग्रादिव केषरी
verses.transliteration:
virathastu gadāṁ gṛhya mālī naktaṁcarottamaḥ
āpupluve gadāpāṇirgiryagrādiva keṣarī

translations.english: Then that foremost of night-rangers, on being deprived of his car, sprang forward, mace in hand, even as lion bounds up from the brow of a hillock.

verses.sanskrit:
स तया गरुडं संख्ये ईशानमिव चान्तकः
ललाटदेशेऽभ्यहनद्वज्रेणेन्द्रो यथाचलम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tayā garuḍaṁ saṁkhye īśānamiva cāntakaḥ
lalāṭadeśe'bhyahanadvajreṇendro yathācalam

translations.english: He with his mace smote at the forehead of that lord of birds, even as the Destroyer had smitten Isana,* or as Indra smites a mountain with his thunder-bolt. *There took place an encounter betwcen Radra and Yama in the Sveta forest, for the protection of Märkandeya and a certain king. In this battle, Yama had smitten Rudra. This is narrated in the Puranas.

verses.sanskrit:
गदयाभिहतस्तेन मालिना गरुडो भृशम्
रणात्पराङ्मुखं देवं कृतवान्वेदनातुरः
verses.transliteration:
gadayābhihatastena mālinā garuḍo bhṛśam
raṇātparāṅmukhaṁ devaṁ kṛtavānvedanāturaḥ

translations.english: On being severely struck by Mali with his mace, Garuda, writhing in torments, moved the god away from the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै
उदतिष्ठन्महानादो रक्षसामभिनर्दताम्
verses.transliteration:
parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai
udatiṣṭhanmahānādo rakṣasāmabhinardatām

translations.english: On the god having been removed from the field by Mäli as well as Garuda, there arose a mighty din of Raksasa roaring (in chorus).

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षसां नदतां नादं श्रुत्वा हरिहयानुजः
पराङ्मुखोऽप्युत्ससर्ज चक्रं मालिजिघांसया
verses.transliteration:
rakṣasāṁ nadatāṁ nādaṁ śrutvā harihayānujaḥ
parāṅmukho'pyutsasarja cakraṁ mālijighāṁsayā

translations.english: Hearing the cheers of the Raksasa, Indra's younger brother, the reverend Hari, sitting on that lord of birds, albeit moved off from the scene of conflict, waxing enraged, from a desire of slaying (Mali) hurled his disc at him.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सूर्यमण्डलाभासं स्वभासा भासयन्नभः
कालचक्रनिभं चक्रं मालेः शीर्षमपातयत्
verses.transliteration:
tatsūryamaṇḍalābhāsaṁ svabhāsā bhāsayannabhaḥ
kālacakranibhaṁ cakraṁ māleḥ śīrṣamapātayat

translations.english: Thereat the disc, possessed of the splendour of the solar disc, and resembling the wheel itself of Kāla, flooding all the heavens with radiance, brought down Māli's head to the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छिरो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रोत्कृत्तं विभीषणम्
पपात रुधिरोद्गारि पुरा राहुशिरो यथा
verses.transliteration:
tacchiro rākṣasendrasya cakrotkṛttaṁ vibhīṣaṇam
papāta rudhirodgāri purā rāhuśiro yathā

translations.english: That head of lord of Rākşasas, terrific to behold, on being cut off (by Visnu), vomiting blood, fell down before (the Rākşasas), as formerly Rahu's head had fallen.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः सुरैः सुसंहृष्टैः सर्वप्राणसमीरितः
सिंहनादरवो मुक्तः साधु देवेति वादिभिः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ suraiḥ susaṁhṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaprāṇasamīritaḥ
siṁhanādaravo muktaḥ sādhu deveti vādibhiḥ

translations.english: Then the deities experiencing excess of joy set up leonine cheers with might and main, crying,' Excellent, O god.' Seeing Mali slain, Sumali and Mālyavån, burning in grief, fled precipitately towards Lankä along with their forces.

verses.sanskrit:
गरुडस्तु समाश्वस्तः संनिवृत्य महामनाः
राक्षसान्द्रावयामास पक्षवातेन कोपितः
verses.transliteration:
garuḍastu samāśvastaḥ saṁnivṛtya mahāmanāḥ
rākṣasāndrāvayāmāsa pakṣavātena kopitaḥ

translations.english: Garuda, being cheered, turned round, and growing enraged, as before drove the Rākşasas with the wind of his wings.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणोऽपीषुवराशनीभि;र्विदारयामास धनुःप्रमुक्तैः
नक्तंचरान्मुक्तविधूतकेशा;न्यथाशनीभिः सतडिन्महेन्द्रः
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇo'pīṣuvarāśanībhi;rvidārayāmāsa dhanuḥpramuktaiḥ
naktaṁcarānmuktavidhūtakeśā;nyathāśanībhiḥ sataḍinmahendraḥ

translations.english: And as the thunder-bolt with lightening (riveth) a mighty mass of clouds, Narayana by means of the thunder-bolts of his arrows discharged from his bow, rived the night-rangers with their hair dishevelled and streaming (in the wind).

verses.sanskrit:
भिन्नातपत्रं पतमानशस्त्रं; शरैरपध्वस्तविशीर्णदेहम्
विनिःसृतान्त्रं भयलोलनेत्रं; बलं तदुन्मत्तनिभं बभूव
verses.transliteration:
bhinnātapatraṁ patamānaśastraṁ; śarairapadhvastaviśīrṇadeham
viniḥsṛtāntraṁ bhayalolanetraṁ; balaṁ tadunmattanibhaṁ babhūva

translations.english: The forces having their umbrellas rent, their arms falling off, their goodly garments scattered, their entrails coming out and their eyes rolling, became incapable of distinguishing their own party from that of the foe.

verses.sanskrit:
सिंहार्दितानामिव कुञ्जराणां; निशाचराणां सह कुञ्जराणाम्
रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः; पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम्
verses.transliteration:
siṁhārditānāmiva kuñjarāṇāṁ; niśācarāṇāṁ saha kuñjarāṇām
ravāśca vegāśca samaṁ babhūvuḥ; purāṇasiṁhena vimarditānām

translations.english: Even like (the roars and the vehemence) displayed by elephants on being attacked by lions, the roars, and the vehemence of the nightrangers and their elephants, sore assailed by the Primaeval Lion,* were equal. *Vişnu as a man-lion had formerly taken the conceit out of Hiranyakasipu the Asura king-and slain him, to rid his devotee Prahlada of his mortal foc in the from of a father.

verses.sanskrit:
संछाद्यमाना हरिबाणजालैः; स्वबाणजालानि समुत्सृजन्तः
धावन्ति नक्तंचरकालमेघा; वायुप्रणुन्ना इव कालमेघाः
verses.transliteration:
saṁchādyamānā haribāṇajālaiḥ; svabāṇajālāni samutsṛjantaḥ
dhāvanti naktaṁcarakālameghā; vāyupraṇunnā iva kālameghāḥ

translations.english: And driven by Hari's networks of arrows, and discharging (all the while) their own showers of shafts, those night-rangers resembling the clouds of doom, are driven like the veritable clouds of the universal dissolution drifted by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्रप्रहारैर्विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः; संचूर्णिताङ्गाश्च गदाप्रहारैः
असिप्रहारैर्बहुधा विभक्ताः; पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः
verses.transliteration:
cakraprahārairvinikṛttaśīrṣāḥ; saṁcūrṇitāṅgāśca gadāprahāraiḥ
asiprahārairbahudhā vibhaktāḥ; patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ

translations.english: Their heads cut by discus, their parts of bodies crushed with the mace, and hewn in twain with swords, thus they foremost of Rākşasas fell like to hills (toppling headlong).

verses.sanskrit:
केचिच्चैवासिना छिन्नास्तथान्ये शरताडिताः
निपेतुरम्बरात्तूर्णं राक्षसाः सागराम्भसि
verses.transliteration:
keciccaivāsinā chinnāstathānye śaratāḍitāḥ
nipeturambarāttūrṇaṁ rākṣasāḥ sāgarāmbhasi

translations.english: And (some) with their lotus-faces cut by the discus, (some) with their chests crushed with the mace, (some) with their necks torn off by the plough, (some) with their heads riven by the club, and some hewn by the sword, and others pierced by arrows, the Rākṣasas began to drop fast from the sky into the waters of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
तदाम्बरं विगलितहारकुण्डलै;र्निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः
निपात्यमानैर्ददृशे निरन्तरं; निपात्यमानैरिव नीलपर्वतैः
verses.transliteration:
tadāmbaraṁ vigalitahārakuṇḍalai;rniśācarairnīlabalāhakopamaiḥ
nipātyamānairdadṛśe nirantaraṁ; nipātyamānairiva nīlaparvataiḥ

translations.english: The Earth was seen to be (covered) with night-rangers resembling dark clouds, adorned with jewelled necklaces and ear rings, falling down, as if covered with dark mountains dropping down.

verses.sanskrit:
हन्यमाने बले तस्मिन्पद्मनाभेन पृष्ठतः
माल्यवान्संनिवृत्तोऽथ वेलातिग इवार्णवः
verses.transliteration:
hanyamāne bale tasminpadmanābhena pṛṣṭhataḥ
mālyavānsaṁnivṛtto'tha velātiga ivārṇavaḥ

translations.english: On that host being sore pressed at its back by Padmanabha,* Mālyavăn turned back even as the ocean does on meeting with its shore. *Lit. the lotus-naveled-a name of Visnu.

verses.sanskrit:
संरक्तनयनः कोपाच्चलन्मौलिर्निशाचरः
पद्मनाभमिदं प्राह वचनं परुषं तदा
verses.transliteration:
saṁraktanayanaḥ kopāccalanmaulirniśācaraḥ
padmanābhamidaṁ prāha vacanaṁ paruṣaṁ tadā

translations.english: And with his eyes reddened, that night-ranger waxing wroth, shaking his head, addressed that prime of male persons Padmanabha, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायण न जानीषे क्षत्रधर्मं सनातनम्
अयुद्धमनसो भग्नान्योऽस्मान्हंसि यथेतरः
verses.transliteration:
nārāyaṇa na jānīṣe kṣatradharmaṁ sanātanam
ayuddhamanaso bhagnānyo'smānhaṁsi yathetaraḥ

translations.english: O Nārāyaṇa, you are ignorant of the timehonoured morality of Kşatriyas; and therefore like a base wight you slay us, desisting from fight and exercised with fear.

verses.sanskrit:
पराङ्मुखवधं पापं यः करोति सुरेश्वर
स हन्ता न गतः स्वर्गं लभते पुण्यकर्मणाम्
verses.transliteration:
parāṅmukhavadhaṁ pāpaṁ yaḥ karoti sureśvara
sa hantā na gataḥ svargaṁ labhate puṇyakarmaṇām

translations.english: O lord of the celestials, he that commits the crime of slaying one that desists from fight cannot go to the celestial regions as the fruit of meritorious acts.

verses.sanskrit:
युद्धश्रद्धाथ वा तेऽस्ति शङ्खचक्रगदाधर
अहं स्थितोऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत्तव
verses.transliteration:
yuddhaśraddhātha vā te'sti śaṅkhacakragadādhara
ahaṁ sthito'smi paśyāmi balaṁ darśaya yattava

translations.english: If you are bent upon battle, a holder of the conch, the discus and the mace, taking up my post (here), I shall see (your strength). Do you show (me) the same.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं तं देवराजानुजो बली
युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मयाभयम्
राक्षसोत्सादनं दत्तं तदेतदनुपाल्यते
verses.transliteration:
uvāca rākṣasendraṁ taṁ devarājānujo balī
yuṣmatto bhayabhītānāṁ devānāṁ vai mayābhayam
rākṣasotsādanaṁ dattaṁ tadetadanupālyate

translations.english: I have removed the fear of the deities, affrighted at you, by promising that I will make root and branch work with the Räkşasas; and that same promise I am now fulfilling.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया
सोऽहं वो निहनिष्यामि रसातलगतानपि
verses.transliteration:
prāṇairapi priyaṁ kāryaṁ devānāṁ hi sadā mayā
so'haṁ vo nihaniṣyāmi rasātalagatānapi

translations.english: I should always lay down my life for serving the celestials and you I will slay even if you should go to the nethermost regions.

verses.sanskrit:
देवमेवं ब्रुवाणं तु रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम्
शक्त्या बिभेद संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रो ररास च
verses.transliteration:
devamevaṁ bruvāṇaṁ tu raktāmburuhalocanam
śaktyā bibheda saṁkruddho rākṣasendro rarāsa ca

translations.english: As that god of gods having eyes resembling the red lotuses was speaking thus, the lord of Rākşasas in high wrath pierced his breast with a dart.

verses.sanskrit:
माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना
हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतह्रदा
verses.transliteration:
mālyavadbhujanirmuktā śaktirghaṇṭākṛtasvanā
harerurasi babhrāja meghastheva śatahradā

translations.english: And hurled by the hand of Mālyavān, the dart resonant with bells, appeared graceful on Hari's breast like lightening embosomed in clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तामेव चोत्कृष्य शक्तिं शक्तिधरप्रियः
माल्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य चिक्षेपाम्बुरुहेक्षणः
verses.transliteration:
tatastāmeva cotkṛṣya śaktiṁ śaktidharapriyaḥ
mālyavantaṁ samuddiśya cikṣepāmburuhekṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Thereat drawing out the same dart, that one dear to the Wielder of the Dart,* having eyes resembling red lotuses, aiming at Mālyāvan, hurled it at him. *A name of Kārtikeya, the celestial generallissimo.

verses.sanskrit:
स्कन्दोत्सृष्टेव सा शक्तिर्गोविन्दकरनिःसृता
काङ्क्षन्ती राक्षसं प्रायान्महोल्केवाञ्जनाचलम्
verses.transliteration:
skandotsṛṣṭeva sā śaktirgovindakaraniḥsṛtā
kāṅkṣantī rākṣasaṁ prāyānmaholkevāñjanācalam

translations.english: Thereat the dart discharged by the hand of Govinda like to the Dart discharged by the hand of Skanda, rushing towards the Rākṣasa like a meteor coursing towards the Anjana mountain, descended on the spacious chest of the lord of the Rākşasas decked with the weight of a chain, even as the thunder clap bursts at the summit of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
तया भिन्नतनुत्राणाः प्राविशद्विपुलं तमः
माल्यवान्पुनराश्वस्तस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः
verses.transliteration:
tayā bhinnatanutrāṇāḥ prāviśadvipulaṁ tamaḥ
mālyavānpunarāśvastastasthau giririvācalaḥ

translations.english: On having his mail rent, Mālyāvan was utterly deprived of his senses; but (anon) reposing for a while, he again stood like a moveless hill.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कार्ष्णायसं शूलं कण्टकैर्बहुभिश्चितम्
प्रगृह्याभ्यहनद्देवं स्तनयोरन्तरे दृढम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kārṣṇāyasaṁ śūlaṁ kaṇṭakairbahubhiścitam
pragṛhyābhyahanaddevaṁ stanayorantare dṛḍham

translations.english: Then taking up a javelin made of black iror girt with many a thorn, he furiously smote that deity on the chest.

verses.sanskrit:
तथैव रणरक्तस्तु मुष्टिना वासवानुजम्
ताडयित्वा धनुर्मात्रमपक्रान्तो निशाचरः
verses.transliteration:
tathaiva raṇaraktastu muṣṭinā vāsavānujam
tāḍayitvā dhanurmātramapakrānto niśācaraḥ

translations.english: And that night-ranger delighting in battle, dealing a box at Vāsavā's younger brother, moved away a distance measuring a bow's length.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽम्बरे महाञ्शब्दः साधु साध्विति चोत्थितः
आहत्य राक्षसो विष्णुं गरुडं चाप्यताडयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato'mbare mahāñśabdaḥ sādhu sādhviti cotthitaḥ
āhatya rākṣaso viṣṇuṁ garuḍaṁ cāpyatāḍayat

translations.english: And now there arose a mighty tumult in the sky of 'Excellent!' 'Excellent!' and having struck Visnu, the Raksasa also hit Garuda.

verses.sanskrit:
वैनतेयस्ततः क्रुद्धः पक्षवातेन राक्षसं
व्यपोहद्बलवान्वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयं यथा
verses.transliteration:
vainateyastataḥ kruddhaḥ pakṣavātena rākṣasaṁ
vyapohadbalavānvāyuḥ śuṣkaparṇacayaṁ yathā

translations.english: Thereat Vinata's son, growing engaged, drove the Rākşasas away with the wind of his wings, even as the lusty wind bloweth about sere leaves.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विजेन्द्रपक्षवातेन द्रावितं दृश्य पूर्वजम्
सुमाली स्वबलैः सार्धं लङ्कामभिमुखो ययौ
verses.transliteration:
dvijendrapakṣavātena drāvitaṁ dṛśya pūrvajam
sumālī svabalaiḥ sārdhaṁ laṅkāmabhimukho yayau

translations.english: Seeing his elder brother driven by the wind produced by the wings of that bird, Sumali along with his forces, made for Lankā.

verses.sanskrit:
पक्षवातबलोद्धूतो माल्यवानपि राक्षसः
स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः
verses.transliteration:
pakṣavātabaloddhūto mālyavānapi rākṣasaḥ
svabalena samāgamya yayau laṅkāṁ hriyā vṛtaḥ

translations.english: And pushed off by the violence of the wind of (Garuda's) wings, the Rākṣasa Mālyavān also, joined by his own forces, departed for Lankā, covered with shame.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ते राक्षसा राम हरिणा कमलेक्षण
बहुशः संयुगे भग्ना हतप्रवरनायकाः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ te rākṣasā rāma hariṇā kamalekṣaṇa
bahuśaḥ saṁyuge bhagnā hatapravaranāyakāḥ

translations.english: Thus, O Rama, O lotus-eyed one, (the Rākşasas) had innumerable warriors beaten down and their foremost leaders slain.

verses.sanskrit:
अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धुं भयार्दिताः
त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः
verses.transliteration:
aśaknuvantaste viṣṇuṁ pratiyoddhuṁ bhayārditāḥ
tyaktvā laṅkāṁ gatā vastuṁ pātālaṁ sahapatnayaḥ

translations.english: And albeit inflated with pride, they, incapable of coping with Vişnu, leaving Lankā, went to the nether regions with their wives dwelling there.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुनन्दन
स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे
verses.transliteration:
sumālinaṁ samāsādya rākṣasaṁ raghunandana
sthitāḥ prakhyātavīryāste vaṁśe sālakaṭaṅkaṭe

translations.english: O best of the Raghus, these Rākşasa of celebrated prowess, related to the race of Sälakatankața, remained under the leadership of the Rākṣasa Sumāli.

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वया निहतास्ते वै पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः
सुमाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः
सर्व एते महाभाग रावणाद्बलवत्तराः
verses.transliteration:
ye tvayā nihatāste vai paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ
sumālī mālyavānmālī ye ca teṣāṁ puraḥsarāḥ
sarva ete mahābhāga rāvaṇādbalavattarāḥ

translations.english: All those exalted Rākşasas going under the name of Pulastya that had been headed by Sumāli, Mālyavān and Māli, were stronger than Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
न चान्यो रक्षसां हन्ता सुरेष्वपि पुरंजय
ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्
verses.transliteration:
na cānyo rakṣasāṁ hantā sureṣvapi puraṁjaya
ṛte nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ śaṅkhacakragadādharam

translations.english: No other than the god Nārāyaṇa, holding the conch, the discus and the mace, could slay those Råkşasa-foes to the celestials and thorns in the side of the deties.

verses.sanskrit:
भवान्नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः
राक्षसान्हन्तुमुत्पन्नो अजेयः प्रभुरव्ययः
verses.transliteration:
bhavānnārāyaṇo devaścaturbāhuḥ sanātanaḥ
rākṣasānhantumutpanno ajeyaḥ prabhuravyayaḥ

translations.english: And you are that eternal god the four armed Narayana, the lord, undeteriorating and unconquerable, sprung to exterminate Rāksasas.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वामरसंकाशं गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम्
अथाब्रवीत्सुतां रक्षः कैकसीं नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvāmarasaṁkāśaṁ gacchantaṁ pāvakopamam
athābravītsutāṁ rakṣaḥ kaikasīṁ nāma nāmataḥ

translations.english: And that great-minded lord of Rākşasas, resembling dark clouds, decked in burnished earrings of gold, then began to reflect. And then the Raksasa addressed his daughter, named Kaikasi.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्रि प्रदानकालोऽयं यौवनं तेऽतिवर्तते
त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः
verses.transliteration:
putri pradānakālo'yaṁ yauvanaṁ te'tivartate
tvatkṛte ca vayaṁ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ

translations.english: But desirous of acquiring religious merit, we are striving our best in your interests. My daughter, you are finished with every perfection like to Śrī herself.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः सपद्मेव पुत्रिके
प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः प्रतिगृह्यसे
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sapadmeva putrike
pratyākhyānācca bhītaistvaṁ na varaiḥ pratigṛhyase

translations.english: O daughter, the time has come when I should give you away. Your youth is about to be passed. (Kept back) by the fear of refusal, no suiter has sought you (up to his time).

verses.sanskrit:
कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्
न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति पुत्रिके
verses.transliteration:
kanyāpitṛtvaṁ duḥkhaṁ hi sarveṣāṁ mānakāṅkṣiṇām
na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṁ varayediti putrike

translations.english: The being father to a daughter is misery to every one that seekes honour. O daughter, one does not know who shall ask for one's daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते
कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
mātuḥ kulaṁ pitṛkulaṁ yatra caiva pradīyate
kulatrayaṁ sadā kanyā saṁśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati

translations.english: Whenever may a daughter be conferred, a daughter stayes, placing in uncertainly the three races* to which she is related. *The races respectively of her father, mother and husband.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वं मुनिवरश्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम्
गच्छ विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
sā tvaṁ munivaraśreṣṭhaṁ prajāpatikulodbhavam
gaccha viśravasaṁ putri paulastyaṁ varaya svayam

translations.english: Do you, my daughter, seek for your husband that best and foremost of ascetics sprung in the line of Prajăpati Pulastya's son, Viśravā, and of yourself accept him (for your lord).

verses.sanskrit:
ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः
तेजसा भास्करसमा यादृशोऽयं धनेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
īdṛśāste bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṁśayaḥ
tejasā bhāskarasamā yādṛśo'yaṁ dhaneśvaraḥ

translations.english: Then, O daughter, even as this lord of riches, so you will, without doubt, have sons resembling the Sun himself in energy.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः
अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare rāma pulastyatanayo dvijaḥ
agnihotramupātiṣṭhaccaturtha iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: In the meanwhile, O Rama, that twice-born one-Pulastya's was performing the Agnihotra, like the fourth Fire itself.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु तां दारुणां वेलामचिन्त्य पितृगौरवात्
उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता
verses.transliteration:
sā tu tāṁ dāruṇāṁ velāmacintya pitṛgauravāt
upasṛtyāgratastasya caraṇādhomukhī sthitā

translations.english: And without minding that terrific time, (Kaikasi), having regard to the dignity of her sire, coming up before him, stood (there) son hanging her head down towards his feet and throwing up the earth with her great foe.

verses.sanskrit:
भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता
किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने
verses.transliteration:
bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvamihāgatā
kiṁ kāryaṁ kasya vā hetostattvato brūhi śobhane

translations.english: Seeing that one of the shapely hips, having a face fair as the full Moon, (that exceedingly high-minded ascetic) flaming in energy accosted her thus. O gentle one, whose daughter are you? And when do you come hither? And what is your errand? And for whom (do you come)? O beauteous (damsel), truly tell me this.

verses.sanskrit:
किं तु विद्धि हि मां ब्रह्मञ्शासनात्पितुरागताम्
कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tu viddhi hi māṁ brahmañśāsanātpiturāgatām
kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṁ śeṣaṁ tvaṁ jñātumarhasi

translations.english: Thus addressed, the girl, with joined hands, said, 'O ascetic, you are competent to get at my intent by virtue of your own power. Yet, O Brahmarși, know me as having come here at the mandate of my sire. My name is Kaikasī. The rest do you read yourself.

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद्वचः
भगवन्नेदृशाः पुत्रास्त्वत्तोऽर्हा ब्रह्मयोनितः
verses.transliteration:
sā tu tadvacanaṁ śrutvā praṇipatyābravīdvacaḥ
bhagavannedṛśāḥ putrāstvatto'rhā brahmayonitaḥ

translations.english: Hearing his speech, she, bowing down, said, 'O reverend (ascetic), such sons of terrific ways seek I not from you that follow the Veda. Therefore it behoves you to favour me.'

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीन्मुनिस्तत्र पश्चिमो यस्तवात्मजः
मम वंशानुरूपश्च धर्मात्मा च भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
athābravīnmunistatra paścimo yastavātmajaḥ
mama vaṁśānurūpaśca dharmātmā ca bhaviṣyati

translations.english: O fair-faced one, the son that you bring forth last, shall be like to my line, he shall, without doubt-be righteous-souled.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित्
जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā kanyā rāma kālena kenacit
janayāmāsa bībhatsaṁ rakṣorūpaṁ sudāruṇam

translations.english: Having been thus accosted, the girl, O Rama, after a length of time brought forth a very terrible and hideous offspring having the form of a Raksasa, having ten necks, furnished with large teeth, and resembling a heap of collyrium, with coppery lips, twenty arms, huge faces, and flaming hair.

verses.sanskrit:
जातमात्रे ततस्तस्मिन्सज्वालकवलाः शिवाः
क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रिरे
verses.transliteration:
jātamātre tatastasminsajvālakavalāḥ śivāḥ
kravyādāścāpasavyāni maṇḍalāni pracakrire

translations.english: On his having been born, jacka.s with flaming mouths and other ferocious beasts began to gyrate on the left.

verses.sanskrit:
ववर्ष रुधिरं देवो मेघाश्च खरनिस्वनाः
प्रबभौ न च खे सूर्यो महोल्काश्चापतन्भुवि
verses.transliteration:
vavarṣa rudhiraṁ devo meghāśca kharanisvanāḥ
prababhau na ca khe sūryo maholkāścāpatanbhuvi

translations.english: That god showered down blood; and the clouds uttered forth harsh sounds. And the sun was deprived of his splendour; and meteors began to dart to the earth. And the earth shook; and the wind swept away violently. And that lord of streams-the ocean, which was calm before, became agitated.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ नामाकरोत्तस्य पितामहसमः पिता
दशशीर्षः प्रसूतोऽयं दशग्रीवो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
atha nāmākarottasya pitāmahasamaḥ pitā
daśaśīrṣaḥ prasūto'yaṁ daśagrīvo bhaviṣyati

translations.english: And his sire resembling his grand-father named him, (saying), 'As this one has been born with ten necks, he shall be called Ten-necked.'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य त्वनन्तरं जातः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
प्रमाणाद्यस्य विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते
verses.transliteration:
tasya tvanantaraṁ jātaḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
pramāṇādyasya vipulaṁ pramāṇaṁ neha vidyate

translations.english: After him was born Kumbhakarņa endowed with prodigious strength, than whose proportions there are none other's on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शूर्पणखा नाम संजज्ञे विकृतानना
विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा कैकस्याः पश्चिमः सुतः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā nāma saṁjajñe vikṛtānanā
vibhīṣaṇaśca dharmātmā kaikasyāḥ paścimaḥ sutaḥ

translations.english: Then was born she that, having a frightful visage, goes under the name of Surpanakha; the righteous Vibhīşaņa is the youngest son of Kaikasi.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु तत्र महारण्ये ववृधुः सुमहौजसः
तेषां क्रूरो दशग्रीवो लोकोद्वेगकरोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
te tu tatra mahāraṇye vavṛdhuḥ sumahaujasaḥ
teṣāṁ krūro daśagrīvo lokodvegakaro'bhavat

translations.english: 'Excellent!' And in that extensive forest those exceedingly energetic ones, Kumbhakarņa and the Ten-necked one grew up, and became the sources of anxiety to the people.

verses.sanskrit:
कुम्भकर्णः प्रमत्तस्तु महर्षीन्धर्मसंश्रितान्
त्रैलोक्यं त्रासयन्दुष्टो भक्षयन्विचचार ह
verses.transliteration:
kumbhakarṇaḥ pramattastu maharṣīndharmasaṁśritān
trailokyaṁ trāsayanduṣṭo bhakṣayanvicacāra ha

translations.english: Kumbhakarma, maddened to the height, devouring mighty-saints devoted to religion, constantly ranged the triune world in a dissatisfied spirit.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपथे स्थितः
स्वाध्यायनियताहार उवास नियतेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā nityaṁ dharmapathe sthitaḥ
svādhyāyaniyatāhāra uvāsa niyatendriyaḥ

translations.english: But the righteous Vibhișana, ever intent on piety, dwelt there studying the Veda, restraining his fare, and controlling his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वित्तेश्वरो देवस्तत्र कालेन केनचित्
आगच्छत्पितरं द्रष्टुं पुष्पकेण महौजसं
verses.transliteration:
atha vitteśvaro devastatra kālena kenacit
āgacchatpitaraṁ draṣṭuṁ puṣpakeṇa mahaujasaṁ

translations.english: It came to pass that after a length of time the god, Vaisravana-lord of riches-came to see his sire, mounted on Puspaka.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसी तत्र ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा
आस्थाय राक्षसीं बुद्धिं दशग्रीवमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā kaikasī tatra jvalantamiva tejasā
āsthāya rākṣasīṁ buddhiṁ daśagrīvamuvāca ha

translations.english: Seeing him, the Raksasi-Kaikasi-flaming up in energy, coming to the Ten-necked one, represented to him.

verses.sanskrit:
पुत्र वैश्रवणं पश्य भ्रातरं तेजसा वृतम्
भ्रातृभावे समे चापि पश्यात्मानं त्वमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
putra vaiśravaṇaṁ paśya bhrātaraṁ tejasā vṛtam
bhrātṛbhāve same cāpi paśyātmānaṁ tvamīdṛśam

translations.english: O son, behold your brother, Vaisravana, enfolded in effulgence; and, albeit of equal fraternity, behold you in this plight!

verses.sanskrit:
दशग्रीव तथा यत्नं कुरुष्वामितविक्रम
यथा भवसि मे पुत्र शीघ्रं वैश्वरणोपमः
verses.transliteration:
daśagrīva tathā yatnaṁ kuruṣvāmitavikrama
yathā bhavasi me putra śīghraṁ vaiśvaraṇopamaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, O Ten-necked one, O you of measureless prowess, do you so strive that you also, my son, may be like Vaisravana himself.

verses.sanskrit:
मातुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्
अमर्षमतुलं लेभे प्रतिज्ञां चाकरोत्तदा
verses.transliteration:
mātustadvacanaṁ śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān
amarṣamatulaṁ lebhe pratijñāṁ cākarottadā

translations.english: Hearing that speech of his mother, the powerful Ten-necked one was wrought up with exceeding great ill-will, and he vowed then.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि तुल्यो भ्रात्राधिकोऽपि वा
भविष्याम्यचिरान्मातः संतापं त्यज हृद्गतम्
verses.transliteration:
satyaṁ te pratijānāmi tulyo bhrātrādhiko'pi vā
bhaviṣyāmyacirānmātaḥ saṁtāpaṁ tyaja hṛdgatam

translations.english: I truly promise to you that I will be equal to my brother (in energy), or excel him in it. Therefore do you cast off this sorrow in your heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः क्रोधेन तेनैव दशग्रीवः सहानुजः
प्राप्स्यामि तपसा काममिति कृत्वाध्यवस्य च
आगच्छदात्मसिद्ध्यर्थं गोकर्णस्याश्रमं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ krodhena tenaiva daśagrīvaḥ sahānujaḥ
prāpsyāmi tapasā kāmamiti kṛtvādhyavasya ca
āgacchadātmasiddhyarthaṁ gokarṇasyāśramaṁ śubham

translations.english: And influenced by that passion, the tennecked one with his younger brother began to perform rigid acts, with his mind fixed on asceticism. 'I must through austerities have my wish,' thus fixed and resolved, he compassing his end, came to the sacred asylum of Gokarna.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्द्विजं रामः कथं ते भ्रातरो वने
कीदृशं तु तदा ब्रह्मंस्तपश्चेरुर्महाव्रताः
verses.transliteration:
athābravīddvijaṁ rāmaḥ kathaṁ te bhrātaro vane
kīdṛśaṁ tu tadā brahmaṁstapaścerurmahāvratāḥ

translations.english: Then Rāma spoke to the ascetic, O Brahmana, how did those exceedingly mighty brothers carry on austerities in that forest; and what kind of penances was theirs?

verses.sanskrit:
अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र रामं प्रयत मानसं
तांस्तान्धर्मविधींस्तत्र भ्रातरस्ते समाविशन्
verses.transliteration:
agastyastvabravīttatra rāmaṁ prayata mānasaṁ
tāṁstāndharmavidhīṁstatra bhrātaraste samāviśan

translations.english: Thereat there Agastya said to Rāma of a complacent mind, “The brothers severally observed the morality proper to each.”

verses.sanskrit:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तस्यातिचक्रमुः
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्पथे निष्ठितस्य च
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa tasyāticakramuḥ
dharme prayatamānasya satpathe niṣṭhitasya ca

translations.english: Thus passed away ten thousand of that one putting forth exertions in behalf of religion, and established in the path of honesty.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपरः शुचिः
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि पादेनैकेन तस्थिवान्
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā nityaṁ dharmaparaḥ śuciḥ
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi pādenaikena tasthivān

translations.english: The virtuous Vibhīşaņa, ever intent on virtue and pure of spirit, remained standing on one leg for five thousand years.

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्ते नियमे तस्य ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः
पपात पुष्पवर्षं च क्षुभिताश्चापि देवताः
verses.transliteration:
samāpte niyame tasya nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ
papāta puṣpavarṣaṁ ca kṣubhitāścāpi devatāḥ

translations.english: When he had completed (his term of restriction), swarms of apsaras danced, and blossoms showered, and the deities hymned (him).

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यं चैवान्ववर्तत
तस्थौ चोर्ध्वशिरोबाहुः स्वाध्यायधृतमानसः
verses.transliteration:
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi sūryaṁ caivānvavartata
tasthau cordhvaśirobāhuḥ svādhyāyadhṛtamānasaḥ

translations.english: And for five thousand years, he adored the Sun, and with his mind concentrated in the study of the Veda, remained with his head and hands raised up.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विभीषणस्यापि गतानि नियतात्मनः
दशवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गस्थस्येव नन्दने
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ vibhīṣaṇasyāpi gatāni niyatātmanaḥ
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi svargasthasyeva nandane

translations.english: In this wise Vibhīşaņa like a deity in Nandana passed away ten thousand years, observing restrictions.

verses.sanskrit:
दशवर्षसहस्रं तु निराहारो दशाननः
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्चाग्नौ जुहाव सः
verses.transliteration:
daśavarṣasahasraṁ tu nirāhāro daśānanaḥ
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraścāgnau juhāva saḥ

translations.english: The ten-necked passed ten thousand years without fare. On a thousand years being complete, he offered his own head as a sacrifice to Fire.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि नव तस्यातिचक्रमुः
शिरांसि नव चाप्यस्य प्रविष्टानि हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ varṣasahasrāṇi nava tasyāticakramuḥ
śirāṁsi nava cāpyasya praviṣṭāni hutāśanam

translations.english: In this way, he passed away nine thousand years, and nine of his heads entered into Fire.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ वर्षसहस्रे तु दशमे दशमं शिरः
छेत्तुकामः स धर्मात्मा प्राप्तश्चात्र पितामहः
verses.transliteration:
atha varṣasahasre tu daśame daśamaṁ śiraḥ
chettukāmaḥ sa dharmātmā prāptaścātra pitāmahaḥ

translations.english: And as in the tenth year he intended to strike off his tenth head, the Great-father (Brahmā) presented himself at that place.

verses.sanskrit:
पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतः सार्धं देवैरुपस्थितः
वत्स वत्स दशग्रीव प्रीतोऽस्मीत्यभ्यभाषत
verses.transliteration:
pitāmahastu suprītaḥ sārdhaṁ devairupasthitaḥ
vatsa vatsa daśagrīva prīto'smītyabhyabhāṣata

translations.english: Well-pleased, the Pitamaha Brahmā came there along with the celestials. 'O Ten-necked one,' said (the Great-father), 'I am well-pleased with you.

verses.sanskrit:
शीघ्रं वरय धर्मज्ञ वरो यस्तेऽभिकाङ्क्षितः
किं ते कामं करोम्यद्य न वृथा ते परिश्रमः
verses.transliteration:
śīghraṁ varaya dharmajña varo yaste'bhikāṅkṣitaḥ
kiṁ te kāmaṁ karomyadya na vṛthā te pariśramaḥ

translations.english: Do you, O cognisant of righteousness, at once ask for the boon that you wish to have. What wish of your shall I realise? Your toil must not go for nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीद्दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा
verses.transliteration:
tato'bravīddaśagrīvaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
praṇamya śirasā devaṁ harṣagadgadayā girā

translations.english: Thereat, the Ten-necked one, bowing down his head to the deity, said with a delighted heart, his words faltering with ecstasy.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्प्राणिनां नित्यं नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्
नास्ति मृत्युसमः शत्रुरमरत्वमतो वृणे
verses.transliteration:
bhagavanprāṇināṁ nityaṁ nānyatra maraṇādbhayam
nāsti mṛtyusamaḥ śatruramaratvamato vṛṇe

translations.english: O reverend one, creatures have no other fear than (that of) death; and enemy there is none that is like to death. Therefore immortality is even what I crave for.

verses.sanskrit:
सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्
अवध्यः स्यां प्रजाध्यक्ष देवतानां च शाश्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṁ daityadānavarakṣasām
avadhyaḥ syāṁ prajādhyakṣa devatānāṁ ca śāśvatam

translations.english: O lord of creatures, I would, O external one, he incapable of being slain by birds and serpents, Yaksas, Daityas, Danavas and Raksasas, and the deities; for, O you that are worshipped by the immortals, anxiety I have none from any other beings. Indeed, I deem as straw creatures such as men etc.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा
उवाच वचनं राम सह देवैः पितामहः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu dharmātmā daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā
uvāca vacanaṁ rāma saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ

translations.english: Thus accosted by the Rākşasa the Ten-necked one-that righteous-souled one, the great-father, along with the celestials, said.

verses.sanskrit:
हुतानि यानि शीर्षाणि पूर्वमग्नौ त्वयानघ
पुनस्तानि भविष्यन्ति तथैव तव राक्षस
verses.transliteration:
hutāni yāni śīrṣāṇi pūrvamagnau tvayānagha
punastāni bhaviṣyanti tathaiva tava rākṣasa

translations.english: I, having been gratified, will confer on you a fresh boon. O Raksasa, O sinless one, those heads of your which have been offered as sacrifices and which have sunk, into the fire, shall again be your. And, a placid one, I shall also confer on you another boon difficult of being obtained, The form that you shall wish to wear, shall instantly be yours.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं पितामहोक्तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः
अग्नौ हुतानि शीर्षाणि यानि तान्युत्थितानि वै
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ pitāmahoktasya daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ
agnau hutāni śīrṣāṇi yāni tānyutthitāni vai

translations.english: As soon as the Ten-necked Rākṣasa had spoken, thus, the heads that had been offered as sacrifices into the fire, rose up again.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं प्रजापतिः
विभीषणमथोवाच वाक्यं लोकपितामहः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu taṁ rāma daśagrīvaṁ prajāpatiḥ
vibhīṣaṇamathovāca vākyaṁ lokapitāmahaḥ

translations.english: Having said this to the Ten-necked one, the. great sire of all creatures addressed Vibhīşana, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषण त्वया वत्स धर्मसंहितबुद्धिना
परितुष्टोऽस्मि धर्मज्ञ वरं वरय सुव्रत
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇa tvayā vatsa dharmasaṁhitabuddhinā
parituṣṭo'smi dharmajña varaṁ varaya suvrata

translations.english: O Vibhisana, gratified have I been by you, whose intelligence is established in righteousness. Therefore, my child, O righteoussouled one, O you of excellent vows, ask for the boon that you would have.

verses.sanskrit:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा वचनं प्राह साञ्जलिः
वृतः सर्वगुणैर्नित्यं चन्द्रमा इव रश्मिभिः
verses.transliteration:
vibhīṣaṇastu dharmātmā vacanaṁ prāha sāñjaliḥ
vṛtaḥ sarvaguṇairnityaṁ candramā iva raśmibhiḥ

translations.english: Thereat the virtuous Vibhīşaņa spoke with joined hands, 'O reverend one, since the spiritual preceptor of all creatures himself (is pleased) with me, I (deem myself) as furnished with every perfection, even as the Moon is envisioned with rays. If you will bestow on me a boon with pleasure, then, O you of excellent vows, hear of the boon that I would have.

verses.sanskrit:
या या मे जायते बुद्धिर्येषु येष्वाश्रमेष्विह
सा सा भवतु धर्मिष्ठा तं तं धर्मं च पालये
verses.transliteration:
yā yā me jāyate buddhiryeṣu yeṣvāśrameṣviha
sā sā bhavatu dharmiṣṭhā taṁ taṁ dharmaṁ ca pālaye

translations.english: And inay every sense of mine sprung during the observance of particular modes of life, be in unison with righteousness, so that I may practice the form of religion (in harmony with any particular mode of life!) O exceedingly noble one, this best of boons, is even what is sought for by me, for nothing in this world is incapable of being attained by those attached to righteousness.' Then the lord of creatures, being again delighted, spoke to Vibhīşaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्माद्राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रकर्षण
नाधर्मे जायते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददामि ते
verses.transliteration:
yasmādrākṣasayonau te jātasyāmitrakarṣaṇa
nādharme jāyate buddhiramaratvaṁ dadāmi te

translations.english: As you are virtuous, so all this shall come to pass on your behalf. And inasmuch as in spite of your having been born in the Rākṣasa race, your thoughts, ( destroyer of enemies, do not originate in sin, I confer on the immortality. Having said this, he intended to grant boons to Kumbhakarna.

verses.sanskrit:
न तावत्कुम्भकर्णाय प्रदातव्यो वरस्त्वया
जानीषे हि यथा लोकांस्त्रासयत्येष दुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
na tāvatkumbhakarṇāya pradātavyo varastvayā
jānīṣe hi yathā lokāṁstrāsayatyeṣa durmatiḥ

translations.english: Thereat the celestials in a body represented to the lord of creatures with joined hands. 'On Kumbhakarņa you should confer no boons, since you know in what manner does this wickedminded one frighten people.

verses.sanskrit:
नन्दनेऽप्सरसः सप्त महेन्द्रानुचरा दश
अनेन भक्षिता ब्रह्मन्नृषयो मानुषास्तथा
verses.transliteration:
nandane'psarasaḥ sapta mahendrānucarā daśa
anena bhakṣitā brahmannṛṣayo mānuṣāstathā

translations.english: And, O Brāhmaṇa, even Apsarās in Nandana, ten attendants of Mahendra, as well as sages and human beings, have been devoured by this one.

verses.sanskrit:
वरव्याजेन मोहोऽस्मै दीयताममितप्रभ
लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्याद्भवेदस्य च संनतिः
verses.transliteration:
varavyājena moho'smai dīyatāmamitaprabha
lokānāṁ svasti caiva syādbhavedasya ca saṁnatiḥ

translations.english: Do you then, o lord having immeasurable prowess, pretending to give him a boon, give stupefaction (instead). Thereby the welfare of the people would be secured, and the honour of this one too shall be maintained.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्माचिन्तयत्पद्मसंभवः
चिन्तिता चोपतस्थेऽस्य पार्श्वं देवी सरस्वती
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ surairbrahmācintayatpadmasaṁbhavaḥ
cintitā copatasthe'sya pārśvaṁ devī sarasvatī

translations.english: Thus addressed by the celestials, Brahmā, the Lotus-sprung one, pondered. The goddess, Sarasvatī, who was by his side was also agitated by anxiety.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राञ्जलिः सा तु पर्श्वस्था प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वती
इयमस्म्यागता देव किं कार्यं करवाण्यहम्
verses.transliteration:
prāñjaliḥ sā tu parśvasthā prāha vākyaṁ sarasvatī
iyamasmyāgatā deva kiṁ kāryaṁ karavāṇyaham

translations.english: And remaining by him, Sarasvatī with joined hands observed, 'O god, I have come here. What work shall I accomplish?'

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजापतिस्तु तां प्राप्तां प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वतीम्
वाणि त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भव या देवतेप्सिता
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatistu tāṁ prāptāṁ prāha vākyaṁ sarasvatīm
vāṇi tvaṁ rākṣasendrasya bhava yā devatepsitā

translations.english: And the lord of creatures, on having her, spoke to Sarasvatī,' O Vāņi!' be you the goddess of speech of this foremost of Rākşasas, favourable to the deities. 1. Lit. word, a designation of Saraswati. 2. i.e. preside over Kumbhakarna's speech while asking for the boon, and let him, through your power, ask for such a gift as may turn our profitable to the gods.

verses.sanskrit:
तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत्
कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहो वरं वरय यो मतः
verses.transliteration:
tathetyuktvā praviṣṭā sā prajāpatirathābravīt
kumbhakarṇa mahābāho varaṁ varaya yo mataḥ

translations.english: Having said, 'So be it,' she entered (within Kumbhakarna's throat); and Prajapati said,' O Kumbhakarma, O mighty-armed one, do you ask for the boon that you would have.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं लब्धवराः सर्वे भ्रातरो दीप्ततेजसः
श्लेष्मातकवनं गत्वा तत्र ते न्यवसन्सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ labdhavarāḥ sarve bhrātaro dīptatejasaḥ
śleṣmātakavanaṁ gatvā tatra te nyavasansukham

translations.english: Having thus obtained the boons, the brothers endowed with flaming energy, going to the Śleşmātaka wood, began to dwell there peacefully.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमाली वरलब्धांस्तु ज्ञात्वा तान्वै निशाचरान्
उदतिष्ठद्भयं त्यक्त्वा सानुगः स रसातलात्
verses.transliteration:
sumālī varalabdhāṁstu jñātvā tānvai niśācarān
udatiṣṭhadbhayaṁ tyaktvā sānugaḥ sa rasātalāt

translations.english: Learning that these night-rangers had obtained boons, Sumāli with his followers, casting off fear, rose up from the nether regions.

verses.sanskrit:
मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च विरूपाक्षो महोदरः
उदतिष्ठन्सुसंरब्धाः सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
mārīcaśca prahastaśca virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ
udatiṣṭhansusaṁrabdhāḥ sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: And wrought up with exceeding great wrath, the counsellors of that Rākşasas-Mārīca and Prahasta and Virūpākṣa and Mahodara-also rose up.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमाली चैव तैः सर्वैर्वृतो राक्षसपुंगवैः
अभिगम्य दशग्रीवं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sumālī caiva taiḥ sarvairvṛto rākṣasapuṁgavaiḥ
abhigamya daśagrīvaṁ pariṣvajyedamabravīt

translations.english: Accompanied by his counsellors-foremost of Rākşasas-Sumāli presenting himself before the Ten-necked one and embracing him, addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
दिष्ट्या ते पुत्र संप्राप्तश्चिन्तितोऽयं मनोरथः
यस्त्वं त्रिभुवणश्रेष्ठाल्लब्धवान्वरमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
diṣṭyā te putra saṁprāptaścintito'yaṁ manorathaḥ
yastvaṁ tribhuvaṇaśreṣṭhāllabdhavānvaramīdṛśam

translations.english: By good fortune it is, O child, that through you we have had the wish that was in our heart, inasmuch as you have received the best of boons from him that is the foremost of all these three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्कृते च वयं लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा याता रसातलम्
तद्गतं नो महाबाहो महद्विष्णुकृतं भयम्
verses.transliteration:
yatkṛte ca vayaṁ laṅkāṁ tyaktvā yātā rasātalam
tadgataṁ no mahābāho mahadviṣṇukṛtaṁ bhayam

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, that great fear arising from Vişnu, from which leaving Larkā, we had gone to the nethermost abysses, has been removed.

verses.sanskrit:
असकृत्तेन भग्ना हि परित्यज्य स्वमालयम्
विद्रुताः सहिताः सर्वे प्रविष्टाः स्म रसातलम्
verses.transliteration:
asakṛttena bhagnā hi parityajya svamālayam
vidrutāḥ sahitāḥ sarve praviṣṭāḥ sma rasātalam

translations.english: Full many a time, brought down by that fear, we, on being pursued (by our enemies), forsaking our homes, had gone to the nether regions along with all those (related to us).

verses.sanskrit:
अस्मदीया च लङ्केयं नगरी राक्षसोषिता
निवेशिता तव भ्रात्रा धनाध्यक्षेण धीमता
verses.transliteration:
asmadīyā ca laṅkeyaṁ nagarī rākṣasoṣitā
niveśitā tava bhrātrā dhanādhyakṣeṇa dhīmatā

translations.english: This Lankā was our city, inhabited by Rākşasas. (Now) it is inhabited by the brotherthe intelligent lord of riches.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि नामात्र शक्यं स्यात्साम्ना दानेन वानघ
तरसा वा महाबाहो प्रत्यानेतुं कृतं भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
yadi nāmātra śakyaṁ syātsāmnā dānena vānagha
tarasā vā mahābāho pratyānetuṁ kṛtaṁ bhavet

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, if you can through selfcontrol or charity or by a sudden display of prowess, repossesses yourself of the same, a (great) thing shall have been achieved; and then, O child, you should, without doubt, be the lord of Lankā; and this Raksasa race, which has sunk, shall have been raised up by you.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवो मातामहमुपस्थितम्
वित्तेशो गुरुरस्माकं नार्हस्येवं प्रभाषितुम्
verses.transliteration:
athābravīddaśagrīvo mātāmahamupasthitam
vitteśo gururasmākaṁ nārhasyevaṁ prabhāṣitum

translations.english: O you endowed with prodigious strength, you shall be the lord of all. Then the Ten-necked one addressed his maternal grand-father, who was present.

verses.sanskrit:
दशग्रीव महाबाहो नार्हस्त्वं वक्तुमीदृशम्
सौभ्रात्रं नास्ति शूराणां शृणु चेदं वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
daśagrīva mahābāho nārhastvaṁ vaktumīdṛśam
saubhrātraṁ nāsti śūrāṇāṁ śṛṇu cedaṁ vaco mama

translations.english: O Ten-necked one, O long-armed (hero), it does not behove you to speak thus. Faternal feeling there is none among heroes. Listen to these words of mine!

verses.sanskrit:
अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव भगिन्यौ सहिते किल
भार्ये परमरूपिण्यौ कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः
verses.transliteration:
aditiśca ditiścaiva bhaginyau sahite kila
bhārye paramarūpiṇyau kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ

translations.english: There two sisters-Aditi and Diti, mutually attached to each other, those (damsels) endowed with surpassing beauty, became the wives of that lord of creatures-Kaśyapa.

verses.sanskrit:
अदितिर्जनयामास देवांस्त्रिभुवणेश्वरान्
दितिस्त्वजनयद्दैत्यान्कश्यपस्यात्मसंभवान्
verses.transliteration:
aditirjanayāmāsa devāṁstribhuvaṇeśvarān
ditistvajanayaddaityānkaśyapasyātmasaṁbhavān

translations.english: Aditi brought forth the gods, who are the lords of three worlds. And Diti gave birth to the Daityas, offspring of Kasyapa.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य तांस्तु समरे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
देवानां वशमानीतं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्
verses.transliteration:
nihatya tāṁstu samare viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
devānāṁ vaśamānītaṁ trailokyamidamavyayam

translations.english: O you cognisant of righteousness, formerly this earth, O hero, having the ocean for her garment, and furnished with mountains, belonged to the Daityas; and (gradually) they grew very powerful. And then this undeteriorating triune world was brought under the dominion of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
नैतदेको भवानेव करिष्यति विपर्ययम्
सुरैराचरितं पूर्वं कुरुष्वैतद्वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
naitadeko bhavāneva kariṣyati viparyayam
surairācaritaṁ pūrvaṁ kuruṣvaitadvaco mama

translations.english: So that you are not the only one that would act inimically (to your brother); but this course had formerly been pursued by both the celestials and the Asuras. Therefore do you act in conformity with my word.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहस्तेन दुरात्मना
चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं वै बाढमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
evamukto daśagrīvaḥ prahastena durātmanā
cintayitvā muhūrtaṁ vai bāḍhamityeva so'bravīt

translations.english: Thus exhorted, the Ten-necked one, with a delighted heart, reflecting for a moment, said, 'Very well.' And wrought up with delight, the Ten-necked one endowed with prowess the very same day went to the forest, accompanied by the night-rangers.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिकूटस्थः स तु तदा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
प्रेषयामास दौत्येन प्रहस्तं वाक्यकोविदम्
verses.transliteration:
trikūṭasthaḥ sa tu tadā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
preṣayāmāsa dautyena prahastaṁ vākyakovidam

translations.english: Arriving at Trikuta, that one skilled in speechthe night-ranger, Ravana-sent Prahasta in the ca vacity of an ambassador:

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहस्त शीघ्रं गत्वा त्वं ब्रूहि नैरृतपुंगवम्
वचनान्मम वित्तेशं सामपूर्वमिदं वचः
verses.transliteration:
prahasta śīghraṁ gatvā tvaṁ brūhi nairṛtapuṁgavam
vacanānmama vitteśaṁ sāmapūrvamidaṁ vacaḥ

translations.english: O Prahasta, hie you; and tell the foremost of Naiſtas-the lord of riches-in my words informed with mildness.

verses.sanskrit:
इयं लङ्का पुरी राजन्राक्षसानां महात्मनाम्
त्वया निवेशिता सौम्य नैतद्युक्तं तवानघ
verses.transliteration:
iyaṁ laṅkā purī rājanrākṣasānāṁ mahātmanām
tvayā niveśitā saumya naitadyuktaṁ tavānagha

translations.english: This city of Lankā, O king, belongs to the high-souled Rākṣasas; but you have established yourself in her. This, O sinless one, is not proper for you.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्भवान्यदि साम्नैतां दद्यादतुलविक्रम
कृता भवेन्मम प्रीतिर्धर्मश्चैवानुपालितः
verses.transliteration:
tadbhavānyadi sāmnaitāṁ dadyādatulavikrama
kṛtā bhavenmama prītirdharmaścaivānupālitaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, O you of unrivalled prowess, if you should render the same (back), I shall be highly gratified; and righteousness also you will maintain.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहस्तादपि संश्रुत्य देवो वैश्रवणो वचः
प्रत्युवाच प्रहस्तं तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
verses.transliteration:
prahastādapi saṁśrutya devo vaiśravaṇo vacaḥ
pratyuvāca prahastaṁ taṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ

translations.english: Hearing these words from Prahasta, the god Vaiśravaņa, best of those skilled in speech, answered the former.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रूहि गच्छ दशग्रीवं पुरी राज्यं च यन्मम
तवाप्येतन्महाबाहो भुङ्क्ष्वैतद्धतकण्टकम्
verses.transliteration:
brūhi gaccha daśagrīvaṁ purī rājyaṁ ca yanmama
tavāpyetanmahābāho bhuṅkṣvaitaddhatakaṇṭakam

translations.english: Go and tell the Ten-necked one, as this city and this kingdom are mine, so they are your, O mighty-armed one. Do you enjoy this kingdom without a foe.

verses.sanskrit:
एष तात दशग्रीवो दूतं प्रेषितवान्मम
दीयतां नगरी लङ्का पूर्वं रक्षोगणोषिता
मयात्र यदनुष्ठेयं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत
verses.transliteration:
eṣa tāta daśagrīvo dūtaṁ preṣitavānmama
dīyatāṁ nagarī laṅkā pūrvaṁ rakṣogaṇoṣitā
mayātra yadanuṣṭheyaṁ tanmamācakṣva suvrata

translations.english: May my kingdom and wealth never undergo division when you are present! 'Having said this, the lord of riches sought the side of his sire, and, paying him reverence, he communicated Ravana's wish to him:' My father, this Tennecked one had sent a messenger to me, saying, Give (back) the city Lankā, which had before been inhabited by hosts of Rakşasa. Now, O you of excellent vows, do you tell me what I should do.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वेवमुक्तोऽसौ विश्रवा मुनिपुंगवः
उवाच धनदं वाक्यं शृणु पुत्र वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
brahmarṣistvevamukto'sau viśravā munipuṁgavaḥ
uvāca dhanadaṁ vākyaṁ śṛṇu putra vaco mama

translations.english: Thus accosted, that foremost of ascetics, the Brahmarși Viśravă spoke to the lord of riches (standing) with joined hands, 'O son, listen to my words.

verses.sanskrit:
दशग्रीवो महाबाहुरुक्तवान्मम संनिधौ
मया निर्भर्त्सितश्चासीद्बहुधोक्तः सुदुर्मतिः
verses.transliteration:
daśagrīvo mahābāhuruktavānmama saṁnidhau
mayā nirbhartsitaścāsīdbahudhoktaḥ sudurmatiḥ

translations.english: The mighty-armed Ten-necked one had (once); spoken in my presence (to that effect). Thereat I greatly rebuked that wicked-minded one; and I said again and again in anger, You disregard (your religion and honour).

verses.sanskrit:
वरप्रदानसंमूढो मान्यामान्यं सुदुर्मतिः
न वेत्ति मम शापाच्च प्रकृतिं दारुणां गतः
verses.transliteration:
varapradānasaṁmūḍho mānyāmānyaṁ sudurmatiḥ
na vetti mama śāpācca prakṛtiṁ dāruṇāṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Do you listen to my words fraught with religion and profit. Of a wicked heart, you, with your understanding spoilt in consequence of the granting of the boon, can not distinguish between those deserving honour and those not; and, further, through my curse, you have come by fierce nature.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्माद्गच्छ महाबाहो कैलासं धरणीधरम्
निवेशय निवासार्थं त्यज लङ्कां सहानुगः
verses.transliteration:
tasmādgaccha mahābāho kailāsaṁ dharaṇīdharam
niveśaya nivāsārthaṁ tyaja laṅkāṁ sahānugaḥ

translations.english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, go to the mountain, Kailasa. Do you, along with your retainers, for the purpose of dwelling there, take up your quarters (there).

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र मन्दाकिनी रम्या नदीनां प्रवरा नदी
काञ्चनैः सूर्यसंकाशैः पङ्कजैः संवृतोदका
verses.transliteration:
tatra mandākinī ramyā nadīnāṁ pravarā nadī
kāñcanaiḥ sūryasaṁkāśaiḥ paṅkajaiḥ saṁvṛtodakā

translations.english: There flowes the Mandākini best of streams, with her water covered with golden lotuses resembling suns, as also with lilies and blue lotuses and various other fragment flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि क्षमं त्वया तेन वैरं धनद रक्षसा
जानीषे हि यथानेन लब्धः परमको वरः
verses.transliteration:
na hi kṣamaṁ tvayā tena vairaṁ dhanada rakṣasā
jānīṣe hi yathānena labdhaḥ paramako varaḥ

translations.english: And coming there frequently, celestials with Gandharvas and Apsarās and serpents and Kinnaras, ever sport there. O lord of riches, you ought not to enter into hostilities with that Raksasa. You know how he has obtained a great boon.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो गृहीत्वा तु तद्वचः पितृगौरवात्
सदारपौरः सामात्यः सवाहनधनो गतः
verses.transliteration:
evamukto gṛhītvā tu tadvacaḥ pitṛgauravāt
sadārapauraḥ sāmātyaḥ savāhanadhano gataḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed, Vaisravana, for the sake of his father's dignity, with his wives and sons, with his counsellors and his vehicles and wealth went (to Kailasa).

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहस्तस्तु दशग्रीवं गत्वा सर्वं न्यवेदयत्
शून्या सा नगरी लङ्का त्रिंशद्योजनमायता
प्रविश्य तां सहास्माभिः स्वधर्मं तत्र पालय
verses.transliteration:
prahastastu daśagrīvaṁ gatvā sarvaṁ nyavedayat
śūnyā sā nagarī laṅkā triṁśadyojanamāyatā
praviśya tāṁ sahāsmābhiḥ svadharmaṁ tatra pālaya

translations.english: The city of Lanka is (now) empty. Renouncing her, the bestower of riches has gone out of her. (Now) entering into her, along with us, do you there maintain your own religion.

verses.sanskrit:
स चाभिषिक्तः क्षणदाचरैस्तदा; निवेशयामास पुरीं दशाननः
निकामपूर्णा च बभूव सा पुरी; निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः
verses.transliteration:
sa cābhiṣiktaḥ kṣaṇadācaraistadā; niveśayāmāsa purīṁ daśānanaḥ
nikāmapūrṇā ca babhūva sā purī; niśācarairnīlabalāhakopamaiḥ

translations.english: Having been installed, that night-ranger the Ten-faced one dwelt in that city; and that city teemed with night-rangers resembling dark clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
धनेश्वरस्त्वथ पितृवाक्यगौरवा;न्न्यवेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम्
स्वलंकृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां; पुरंदरस्येव तदामरावतीम्
verses.transliteration:
dhaneśvarastvatha pitṛvākyagauravā;nnyaveśayacchaśivimale girau purīm
svalaṁkṛtairbhavanavarairvibhūṣitāṁ; puraṁdarasyeva tadāmarāvatīm

translations.english: The lord of riches, for the sake of his father's dignity, dwelt in a palace situated on the hill bright as moon-light, graced with ornamented superb piles; even as Purandara dwells in Amaravati.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिषिक्तस्तु भ्रातृभ्यां सहितस्तदा
ततः प्रदानं राक्षस्या भगिन्याः समचिन्तयत्
verses.transliteration:
rākṣasendro'bhiṣiktastu bhrātṛbhyāṁ sahitastadā
tataḥ pradānaṁ rākṣasyā bhaginyāḥ samacintayat

translations.english: The lord of Räkşasas was installed along with his brothers. And then he thought of the giving away in marriage of his Rakşasi sister.

verses.sanskrit:
ददौ तां कालकेयाय दानवेन्द्राय राक्षसीम्
स्वसां शूर्पणखां नाम विद्युज्जिह्वाय नामतः
verses.transliteration:
dadau tāṁ kālakeyāya dānavendrāya rākṣasīm
svasāṁ śūrpaṇakhāṁ nāma vidyujjihvāya nāmataḥ

translations.english: Then that Raksasa bestowed his sister, the Rākşasī Śūrpanakhā, on that lord of the Dänavas and king of the Kālakeśa Vidyujjihvä.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्यासहायं तं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
अपृच्छत्को भवानेको निर्मनुष्य मृगे वने
verses.transliteration:
kanyāsahāyaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
apṛcchatko bhavāneko nirmanuṣya mṛge vane

translations.english: Having given her away, the Rākşasa was wandering about for the purpose of hunting, when, o Rāma, he happened to see Diti's son, named Maya. And seeing him accompanied by his daughter, that night-ranger the Ten-necked one asked him, saying, 'Who are you that (wanderest) alone in this first devoid of men as well as deer? And are you accompanied by this one having the eyes of a young deer?' Thereat Maya, O Rama, answered that nightranger, when he had asked this.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्राहमरतिं विन्दंस्तया हीनः सुदुःखितः
तस्मात्पुराद्दुहितरं गृहीत्वा वनमागतः
verses.transliteration:
tatrāhamaratiṁ vindaṁstayā hīnaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ
tasmātpurādduhitaraṁ gṛhītvā vanamāgataḥ

translations.english: From then, taking my daughter, I have come to this wood. This, O king, is my daughter, grown in her womb.

verses.sanskrit:
कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि नराणां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्
कन्या हि द्वे कुले नित्यं संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति
verses.transliteration:
kanyāpitṛtvaṁ duḥkhaṁ hi narāṇāṁ mānakāṅkṣiṇām
kanyā hi dve kule nityaṁ saṁśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati

translations.english: I have come hither with her, seeing of her husband. Verily being father to a daughter is misery to everyone that seekes one's honour. A daughter, forsooth, stayes, ever placing the two lines* in uncertainity. *The lines, namely, of her father and mother. The line of a mother as distinct from that of a father would be impossible under the present economy of Hindu society inasmuch as, as soon as a girl is married, she by that ceremony leaves her father's line and becomes incorporated with that of her husband. But this seems to have been otherwise in ancient times, This opens up an interesting social problem for the research of orientalists.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वौ सुतौ तु मम त्वस्यां भार्यायां संबभूवतुः
मायावी प्रथमस्तात दुन्दुभिस्तदनन्तरम्
verses.transliteration:
dvau sutau tu mama tvasyāṁ bhāryāyāṁ saṁbabhūvatuḥ
māyāvī prathamastāta dundubhistadanantaram

translations.english: On this wife of mine I have also beget two sons. The first is Māyāvī and the next Dundubhi.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः
त्वामिदानीं कथं तात जानीयां को भवानिति
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ
tvāmidānīṁ kathaṁ tāta jānīyāṁ ko bhavāniti

translations.english: Thus have I truly related to everything to you that had asked for it. But, my child, how can I know you now? Who are you?

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रो विनीतमिदमब्रवीत्
अहं पौलस्त्यतनयो दशग्रीवश्च नामतः
verses.transliteration:
evamukto rākṣasendro vinītamidamabravīt
ahaṁ paulastyatanayo daśagrīvaśca nāmataḥ

translations.english: Thus addressed, the Rākşasas humbly said, 'Ten-necked by name, I am the son of ascetic, Paulastya, who was born as the third son of Brahmā.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मर्षेस्तं सुतं ज्ञात्वा मयो हर्षमुपागतः
दातुं दुहितरं तस्य रोचयामास तत्र वै
verses.transliteration:
brahmarṣestaṁ sutaṁ jñātvā mayo harṣamupāgataḥ
dātuṁ duhitaraṁ tasya rocayāmāsa tatra vai

translations.english: Thus accosted, O Rama, by that lord of Raks asas, that Dänava and foremost of Dānavas, Maya; learning that he was the son of Maharsi, Paulastya, there desired in his heart to give away his daughter to him.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रहसन्प्राह दैत्येन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रमिदं वचः
इयं ममात्मजा राजन्हेमयाप्सरसा धृता
कन्या मन्दोदरी नाम पत्न्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
prahasanprāha daityendro rākṣasendramidaṁ vacaḥ
iyaṁ mamātmajā rājanhemayāpsarasā dhṛtā
kanyā mandodarī nāma patnyarthaṁ pratigṛhyatām

translations.english: This daughter of mine, O king, O king, borne by the Apsarā, Hemā, this my daughter named Mandodari do you accept as my wife.

verses.sanskrit:
बाढमित्येव तं राम दशग्रीवोऽभ्यभाषत
प्रज्वाल्य तत्र चैवाग्निमकरोत्पाणिसंग्रहम्
verses.transliteration:
bāḍhamityeva taṁ rāma daśagrīvo'bhyabhāṣata
prajvālya tatra caivāgnimakarotpāṇisaṁgraham

translations.english: 'Well' thereupon the Ten-necked answered him, O Rāma. And lighting a fire, he took her hand.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि तस्य मयो राम शापाभिज्ञस्तपोधनात्
विदित्वा तेन सा दत्ता तस्य पैतामहं कुलम्
verses.transliteration:
na hi tasya mayo rāma śāpābhijñastapodhanāt
viditvā tena sā dattā tasya paitāmahaṁ kulam

translations.english: O Rāma, Maya knew the curse of the sage touching him.* Knowing this, he gave away his daughter, having regard to the race of Ravana's paternal grand-father; and he also conferred on him an exceedingly wonderful dart acquired through the most rigid austerities, by which he wounded Laksmana. *Respecting his birth.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स कृतदारो वै लङ्कायामीश्वरः प्रभुः
गत्वा तु नगरं भार्ये भ्रातृभ्यां समुदावहत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa kṛtadāro vai laṅkāyāmīśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
gatvā tu nagaraṁ bhārye bhrātṛbhyāṁ samudāvahat

translations.english: Having thus wedded, that master-Lankā's lord-going (back) to that city, married his brothers.

verses.sanskrit:
गन्धर्वराजस्य सुतां शैलूषस्य महात्मनः
सरमां नाम धर्मज्ञो लेभे भार्यां विभीषणः
verses.transliteration:
gandharvarājasya sutāṁ śailūṣasya mahātmanaḥ
saramāṁ nāma dharmajño lebhe bhāryāṁ vibhīṣaṇaḥ

translations.english: Rāvana married the grand-daughter of Virocana (on the maternal side) named Vajrajvālā, to Kumbhakarņa. And Vibhīşaņa obtained for his wife the righteous (damsel) named Saramā-daughter to the high-souled Sailusa-sovereign of the Gandharvas.

verses.sanskrit:
मात्रा तु तस्याः कन्यायाः स्नेहेनाक्रन्दितं वचः
सरो मा वर्धतेत्युक्तं ततः सा सरमाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
mātrā tu tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ snehenākranditaṁ vacaḥ
saro mā vardhatetyuktaṁ tataḥ sā saramābhavat

translations.english: Saramā was born on the shores of the lake, Mānasa, was swollen with water on the arrival of the rains, her mother, hearing her cries, affectionately said, Saro mā varddhata 'O lake, do not swell,' and from this circumstance, her name became Saramā.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ते कृतदारा वै रेमिरे तत्र राक्षसाः
स्वां स्वां भार्यामुपादाय गन्धर्वा इव नन्दने
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ te kṛtadārā vai remire tatra rākṣasāḥ
svāṁ svāṁ bhāryāmupādāya gandharvā iva nandane

translations.english: Having thus wedded, those Rākşasas, taking each his wife, set about sporting there, like to Gandharvas sporting in Nandana. And then was born Mandodari's son-Meghanāda. Him you call Indarjit.

verses.sanskrit:
जातमात्रेण हि पुरा तेन राक्षससूनुना
रुदता सुमहान्मुक्तो नादो जलधरोपमः
verses.transliteration:
jātamātreṇa hi purā tena rākṣasasūnunā
rudatā sumahānmukto nādo jaladharopamaḥ

translations.english: As soon as he was born, Ravana's son, formerly crying, emitted a tremendous roar resembling the rumbling of clouds.

verses.sanskrit:
जडीकृतायां लङ्कायां तेन नादेन तस्य वै
पिता तस्याकरोन्नाम मेघनाद इति स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
jaḍīkṛtāyāṁ laṅkāyāṁ tena nādena tasya vai
pitā tasyākaronnāma meghanāda iti svayam

translations.english: O Rāghava, Lankā was petrified at his voice: and (accordingly) his sire himself kept his name, Meghanāda.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽवर्धत तदा राम रावणान्तःपुरे शुभे
रक्ष्यमाणो वरस्त्रीभिश्छन्नः काष्ठैरिवानलः
verses.transliteration:
so'vardhata tadā rāma rāvaṇāntaḥpure śubhe
rakṣyamāṇo varastrībhiśchannaḥ kāṣṭhairivānalaḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, remaining hidden like a fire by fuel, Ravana's son, rejoicing (the bosoms of) his father and mother, grew up in Rāvana's elegant inner apartments.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तत्र कालेन केनचित्
निद्रा समभवत्तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी
verses.transliteration:
atha lokeśvarotsṛṣṭā tatra kālena kenacit
nidrā samabhavattīvrā kumbhakarṇasya rūpiṇī

translations.english: Once upon a time in came to pass that, despatched by the lord of creatures, Steep in her (native) form powerfully overpowered Kumbhakarna.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः
निद्रा मां बाधते राजन्कारयस्व ममालयम्
verses.transliteration:
tato bhrātaramāsīnaṁ kumbhakarṇo'bravīdvacaḥ
nidrā māṁ bādhate rājankārayasva mamālayam

translations.english: Then Kumbhakarņa spoke to his brother, who was seated, 'O king, Sleep obstructs me. Do you, therefore, have my mansion made.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो निशाचरः
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो नावबुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
tatra nidrāṁ samāviṣṭaḥ kumbhakarṇo niśācaraḥ
bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi śayāno nāvabudhyate

translations.english: There, overcome with slumber, the wondrous strong Kumbhakarņa, lying down for many thousand years, did not wake up.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्यानानि विचित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च
तानि गत्वा सुसंक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः
verses.transliteration:
udyānāni vicitrāṇi nandanādīni yāni ca
tāni gatvā susaṁkruddho bhinatti sma daśānanaḥ

translations.english: While Kumbhakarna was overpowered by sleep, Daśānana* without let began to destroy Devarşis, Yakşas and Gandharvas, and going to graceful gardens, Nandana, etc., he devastated them (ruthlessly). *Henceforth we shall use this significant surname of Rāvana, meaning Ten-faced.

verses.sanskrit:
नदीं गज इव क्रीडन्वृक्षान्वायुरिव क्षिपन्
नगान्वज्र इव सृष्टो विध्वंसयति नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
nadīṁ gaja iva krīḍanvṛkṣānvāyuriva kṣipan
nagānvajra iva sṛṣṭo vidhvaṁsayati nityaśaḥ

translations.english: That Rākşasa spread destruction, even as an elephant sporting agitates a river, as the wind bring down trees, or as the thunder-bolt rive mountain-peaks.

verses.sanskrit:
सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्वरणस्तदा
लङ्कां संप्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम्
verses.transliteration:
saubhrātradarśanārthaṁ tu dūtaṁ vaiśvaraṇastadā
laṅkāṁ saṁpreṣayāmāsa daśagrīvasya vai hitam

translations.english: Hearing of the doings of Dasagrīva,* and remembering his conduct chiming in with his race, the righteous lord of riches Vaisravanashowing his fraternal affection, despatched a messenger to Lankā, seeking the welfare of Dasagriva. *Ten-necked.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा नगरीं लङ्कामाससाद विभीषणम्
मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā nagarīṁ laṅkāmāsasāda vibhīṣaṇam
mānitastena dharmeṇa pṛṣṭaścāgamanaṁ prati

translations.english: Going to the city of Lankā, he presented himself before Vibhīşaņa. And having received him with honour, he asked him as to the cause of his visit.

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनपि च बान्धवान्
सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम्
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṁ rājño jñātīnapi ca bāndhavān
sabhāyāṁ darśayāmāsa tamāsīnaṁ daśānanam

translations.english: Having enquired after the welfare of the king as well as his kindred, Vibhīşaņa, showed him to Daśānana seated in his court.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा
जयेन चाभिसंपूज्य तूष्णीमासीन्मुहूर्तकम्
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā tatra rājānaṁ dīpyamānaṁ svatejasā
jayena cābhisaṁpūjya tūṣṇīmāsīnmuhūrtakam

translations.english: Seeing the king there flaming in his own energy, he (the messenger), saluting him (Rāvana) with the word Jaya* stood silent. *Jaya may mean (1) victory and (2) all the deities of the Hindu pantheon.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्योपनीते पर्यङ्के वरास्तरणसंवृते
उपविश्य दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tasyopanīte paryaṅke varāstaraṇasaṁvṛte
upaviśya daśagrīvaṁ dūto vākyamathābravīt

translations.english: The envoy addressed Dasagrīva, seated on a superb couch, graced with a costly coverlet.

verses.sanskrit:
साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत्कृतश्चारित्रसंग्रहः
साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते
verses.transliteration:
sādhu paryāptametāvatkṛtaścāritrasaṁgrahaḥ
sādhu dharme vyavasthānaṁ kriyatāṁ yadi śakyate

translations.english: O king, I shall tell you all that your brother has said, worthy of both the character and race of your father and mother, Enough of wrong doing. Now you should mend your ways. If you can, stay in righteousness. I have seen Nandana ravaged; and I have heard of the sages slain, and Oking, of the preparations the deities are making against you.

verses.sanskrit:
निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वयाहं राक्षसाधिप
अपराद्धा हि बाल्याच्च रक्षणीयाः स्वबान्धवाः
verses.transliteration:
nirākṛtaśca bahuśastvayāhaṁ rākṣasādhipa
aparāddhā hi bālyācca rakṣaṇīyāḥ svabāndhavāḥ

translations.english: I have been utterly disregarded by you; but even if a boy should transgress, he should, for all that be protected by his family members.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम्
रौद्रं व्रतं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration:
ahaṁ tu himavatpṛṣṭhaṁ gato dharmamupāsitum
raudraṁ vrataṁ samāsthāya niyato niyatendriyaḥ

translations.english: Self-restrained and controlling my senses, I, adopting a terrific vow, had gone to the breast to the Himavān for practising righteousness.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र देवो मया दृष्टः सह देव्योमया प्रभुः
सव्यं चक्षुर्मया चैव तत्र देव्यां निपातितम्
verses.transliteration:
tatra devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha devyomayā prabhuḥ
savyaṁ cakṣurmayā caiva tatra devyāṁ nipātitam

translations.english: There I saw that lord of the gods in company with Umā. There I happened to cast my left eye on the goddess, for ‘knowing, O mighty king, who she was, and not for any other reason. Rudrāņi was staying then, wearing a surpassing form.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो देव्याः प्रभावेन दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम्
