रेणुध्वस्तमिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गलत्वमुपागतम्
verses.transliteration:
tato devyāḥ prabhāvena dagdhaṁ savyaṁ mamekṣaṇam
reṇudhvastamiva jyotiḥ piṅgalatvamupāgatam

translations.english: Thereupon through the divine energy of the goddess my left eye was burnt and seemed to be covered with dust, and its lustre became tawny.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहमन्यद्विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम्
पूर्णं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ समवाप महाव्रतम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'hamanyadvistīrṇaṁ gatvā tasya girestaṭam
pūrṇaṁ varṣaśatānyaṣṭau samavāpa mahāvratam

translations.english: Then I, going to another spacious peak of the inountain, became engaged in silently observing a mighty vow.

verses.sanskrit:
समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः
प्रीतः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः
verses.transliteration:
samāpte niyame tasmiṁstatra devo maheśvaraḥ
prītaḥ prītena manasā prāha vākyamidaṁ prabhuḥ

translations.english: On my term of restraint having been complete, that lord of the gods Maheśvara with a gratified heart addressed me, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसानेन सुव्रत
मया चैतद्व्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप
verses.transliteration:
prīto'smi tava dharmajña tapasānena suvrata
mayā caitadvrataṁ cīrṇaṁ tvayā caiva dhanādhipa

translations.english: O righteous one, you of fair vows, I am wellpleased with this asceticism of your. I also had observed this vow; and you also, O lord of riches, have done the same.

verses.sanskrit:
तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चरेद्व्रतमीदृशम्
व्रतं सुदुश्चरं ह्येतन्मयैवोत्पादितं पुरा
verses.transliteration:
tṛtīyaḥ puruṣo nāsti yaścaredvratamīdṛśam
vrataṁ suduścaraṁ hyetanmayaivotpāditaṁ purā

translations.english: A third person there is none that practise such a vow. This vow is hard to perform, and formerly it was I that introduced it.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्सखित्वं मया सार्धं रोचयस्व धनेश्वर
तपसा निर्जितत्वाद्धि सखा भव ममानघ
verses.transliteration:
tatsakhitvaṁ mayā sārdhaṁ rocayasva dhaneśvara
tapasā nirjitatvāddhi sakhā bhava mamānagha

translations.english: Therefore, O mild one, O lord of riches, do you contract friendship with me. And you have conquered me by your penances. Therefore, O be you my friend.

verses.sanskrit:
देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेन यच्च साव्यं तवेक्षणम्
एकाक्षि पिङ्गलेत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम्
verses.transliteration:
devyā dagdhaṁ prabhāvena yacca sāvyaṁ tavekṣaṇam
ekākṣi piṅgaletyeva nāma sthāsyati śāśvatam

translations.english: This your left eye has been burnt through the energy of the goddess, and has turned tawny in consequence of having seen the grace of the goddess; your shall be Ekāksipingala. Then at Saikara's command I sinless one, SO name ever have obtained the privilege of companionship (with him). Having come here I have heard of your evil designs.

verses.sanskrit:
तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगान्निवर्त कुलदूषण
चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसंघैः सुरैस्तव
verses.transliteration:
tadadharmiṣṭhasaṁyogānnivarta kuladūṣaṇa
cintyate hi vadhopāyaḥ sarṣisaṁghaiḥ suraistava

translations.english: Do you then desist from this impious course, tending to sully your line. The celestials along with the sages are pondering over the means of compassing your death.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः क्रुद्धः संरक्तलोचनः
हस्तान्दन्तांश संपीड्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamukto daśagrīvaḥ kruddhaḥ saṁraktalocanaḥ
hastāndantāṁśa saṁpīḍya vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Thus addressed, the Ten necked one, with his eyes reddened in wrath, rubbing his hands and knashing his teeth, said.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यत्त्वं प्रभाषसे
नैव त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि प्रेषितः
verses.transliteration:
vijñātaṁ te mayā dūta vākyaṁ yattvaṁ prabhāṣase
naiva tvamasi naivāsau bhrātrā yenāsi preṣitaḥ

translations.english: O messenger, I have learnt what you have uttered. Neither you nor this brother of mine by whom you have been despatched, (shall live); nor does the keeper of riches say what is for my good. And the fool makes me hear the circumstance of his having made friends with Mahesvara.

verses.sanskrit:
न हन्तव्यो गुरुर्ज्येष्ठो ममायमिति मन्यते
तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः
verses.transliteration:
na hantavyo gururjyeṣṭho mamāyamiti manyate
tasya tvidānīṁ śrutvā me vākyameṣā kṛtā matiḥ

translations.english: But now hearing his (utterances), even this is my resolve. Depending upon the might of my arms, I shall conquer the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रीँल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः
एतन्मुहूर्तमेषोऽहं तस्यैकस्य कृते च वै
चतुरो लोकपालांस्तान्नयिष्यामि यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
trī̐llokānapi jeṣyāmi bāhuvīryamupāśritaḥ
etanmuhūrtameṣo'haṁ tasyaikasya kṛte ca vai
caturo lokapālāṁstānnayiṣyāmi yamakṣayam

translations.english: On his account solely I shall on the instant despatch the four Lokapālas to the abode of Death.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खड्गेन जघ्निवान्
ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu laṅkeśo dūtaṁ khaḍgena jaghnivān
dadau bhakṣayituṁ hyenaṁ rākṣasānāṁ durātmanām

translations.english: Having said this, Lanka's lord killed the emissary with his sword and made him over to the wicked Räksasas for being eaten.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः
त्रैलोक्यविजयाकाङ्क्षी ययौ तत्र धनेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛtasvastyayano rathamāruhya rāvaṇaḥ
trailokyavijayākāṅkṣī yayau tatra dhaneśvaraḥ

translations.english: Then, having performed Svastyayana, Rāvana, ascending his car, went to where the lord of riches was, bent on conquering the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगृध्नुना
वृतः संप्रययौ श्रीमान्क्रोधाल्लोकान्दहन्निव
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣeṇa ca vīreṇa nityaṁ samaragṛdhnunā
vṛtaḥ saṁprayayau śrīmānkrodhāllokāndahanniva

translations.english: Accompanied by his six counsellor Mohodara and Prahasta, Marica, Suka and Sarana, and the heroic Dhümrākṣa eager for encounter the graceful Rāvana, elated with his strength sallied out, as if consuming all creatures with his wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
पुराणि स नदीः शैलान्वनान्युपवनानि च
अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
purāṇi sa nadīḥ śailānvanānyupavanāni ca
atikramya muhūrtena kailāsaṁ girimāviśat

translations.english: Leaving behind cities and steams and hills and woods and groves, he in a moment came to the mountain Kailāśa.

verses.sanskrit:
तं निविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन्राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु
राज्ञो भ्रातायमित्युक्त्वा गता यत्र धनेश्वरः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ niviṣṭaṁ girau tasminrākṣasendraṁ niśamya tu
rājño bhrātāyamityuktvā gatā yatra dhaneśvaraḥ

translations.english: And hearing that wicked-minded lord of Räks asas, breathing high spirits, had arrived at the mount in company with his counsellors, the Yakşas could not stay before that Rākşasa, and knowing this one is the king's brother,' went to where the lord of riches was.

verses.sanskrit:
गत्वा तु सर्वमाचख्युर्भ्रातुस्तस्य विनिश्चयम्
अनुज्ञाता ययुश्चैव युद्धाय धनदेन ते
verses.transliteration:
gatvā tu sarvamācakhyurbhrātustasya viniścayam
anujñātā yayuścaiva yuddhāya dhanadena te

translations.english: Going to him they in full related all about the doings of his brother. And on being permitted by the bestower of treasures, they went out for battle.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो बलस्य संक्षोभः सागरस्येव वर्धतः
अभून्नैरृतराजस्य गिरिं संचालयन्निव
verses.transliteration:
tato balasya saṁkṣobhaḥ sāgarasyeva vardhataḥ
abhūnnairṛtarājasya giriṁ saṁcālayanniva

translations.english: And then, like to the agitation of the ocean, there took place a mighty ferment of the forces of the Naiſta king, as if making the mountain tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो युद्धं समभवद्यक्षराक्षससंकुलम्
व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tato yuddhaṁ samabhavadyakṣarākṣasasaṁkulam
vyathitāścābhavaṁstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: And then there took place an encounter between the Yakşas and the Räksasa were smitten fiercely.

verses.sanskrit:
तं दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः
हर्षान्नादं ततः कृत्वा रोषात्समभिवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṁ sainyaṁ daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
harṣānnādaṁ tataḥ kṛtvā roṣātsamabhivartata

translations.english: And finding his forces in that plight, Daśagrīva set up full many a cheerful shout and in wrath began to speak.

verses.sanskrit:
ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमः
ते सहस्रं सहस्राणामेकैकं समयोधयन्
verses.transliteration:
ye tu te rākṣasendrasya sacivā ghoravikramaḥ
te sahasraṁ sahasrāṇāmekaikaṁ samayodhayan

translations.english: Each of the terrific and mightiest councillors of the Rākşasa-chief, coped with a thousand Yaksas.

verses.sanskrit:
स दुरात्मा समुद्यम्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम्
प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन्यक्षान्यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa durātmā samudyamya kāladaṇḍopamāṁ gadām
praviveśa tataḥ sainyaṁ nayanyakṣānyamakṣayam

translations.english: And that high-souled one, raising up his mace resembling the rod itself of Time, entered into that army, despatching Yakşas to the abode of Yama.

verses.sanskrit:
स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्केन्धनसमाकुलम्
वातेनाग्निरिवायत्तोऽदहत्सैन्यं सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration:
sa kakṣamiva vistīrṇaṁ śuṣkendhanasamākulam
vātenāgnirivāyatto'dahatsainyaṁ sudāruṇam

translations.english: And as a flaming fire burn up an extensive sward of grass stocked with dry fire-wood, he began to consume that Yakşa army.

verses.sanskrit:
तैस्तु तस्य मृधेऽमात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः
अल्पावशिष्टास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः
verses.transliteration:
taistu tasya mṛdhe'mātyairmahodaraśukādibhiḥ
alpāvaśiṣṭāste yakṣāḥ kṛtā vātairivāmbudāḥ

translations.english: And as the wind scatter clouds, the small remnant of Yaksa army was scattered by the redoubtable councillors (of Ravana) Mahodara, Suka, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
हतानां स्वर्गसंस्थानां युध्यतां पृथिवीतले
प्रेक्षतामृषिसंघानां न बभूवान्तरं दिवि
verses.transliteration:
hatānāṁ svargasaṁsthānāṁ yudhyatāṁ pṛthivītale
prekṣatāmṛṣisaṁghānāṁ na babhūvāntaraṁ divi

translations.english: And no room was left (in the sky) in consequence of its being thronged by hosts of sages; and warriors, wounded and rushing for conflict, and (finally) ascending heaven.* *The idea of the author is: "The welkin was thronged with sages as well as warriors, who swelled the ranks of the sages stationed in the sky, by ascending heaven after having fallen in fight.”

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः
अगमत्सुमहान्यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare rāma vistīrṇabalavāhanaḥ
agamatsumahānyakṣo nāmnā saṁyodhakaṇṭakaḥ

translations.english: In the meantime, o Rāma, a Yakşa named Sañyodhakanțaka, accompanied by an extensive force and a large number of vehicles, on being despatched, rushed (on the foe).

verses.sanskrit:
तेन यक्षेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव समाहतः
पतितः पृथिवीं भेजे क्षीणपुण्य इवाम्बरात्
verses.transliteration:
tena yakṣeṇa mārīco viṣṇuneva samāhataḥ
patitaḥ pṛthivīṁ bheje kṣīṇapuṇya ivāmbarāt

translations.english: And wounded in the conflict (by Sañyodhakanţaka) with his discus, as if by Vişnu himself, Márica toppled down to the ground from the mountain, like to a planet whose merit has waned.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन विश्रम्य च निशाचरः
तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे
verses.transliteration:
prāptasaṁjño muhūrtena viśramya ca niśācaraḥ
taṁ yakṣaṁ yodhayāmāsa sa ca bhagnaḥ pradudruve

translations.english: And in a moment regaining his consciousness and resting (for a while), that night-ranger fought with the Yaksa; and thereat, on being defeated, he* fled. *The Yaksa, that is.)

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राम दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम्
सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत्
verses.transliteration:
tato rāma daśagrīvaṁ praviśantaṁ niśācaram
sūryabhānuriti khyāto dvārapālo nyavārayat

translations.english: Then (Rāvana) entered within the gate-way (of the place), garnished with gold, and decked with lapises and silver, And thereat, o king, the warder named Sūryabhānu prevented the nightranger Daśagrīva as he was entering.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तेनैव तं यक्षं तोरणेन समाहनत्
नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्म तेन कृतस्तु सः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tenaiva taṁ yakṣaṁ toraṇena samāhanat
nādṛśyata tadā yakṣo bhasma tena kṛtastu saḥ

translations.english: And on being struck by the same gate-way, the Yakșa ceased to be seen, his body having then been consumed to ashes.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे यक्षा दृष्ट्वा पराक्रमम्
ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve yakṣā dṛṣṭvā parākramam
tato nadīrguhāścaiva viviśurbhayapīḍitāḥ

translations.english: And witnessing the prowess of the Rākșasa, all began to flee; and then they afflicted with affright, fatigued, and with pale faces entered into rivers and caves, leaving their arms behind.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र माणिचारो नाम यक्षः परमदुर्जयः
वृतो यक्षसहस्रैः स चतुर्भिः समयोधयत्
verses.transliteration:
tatra māṇicāro nāma yakṣaḥ paramadurjayaḥ
vṛto yakṣasahasraiḥ sa caturbhiḥ samayodhayat

translations.english: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed and invincible Mānibhadra, surrounded by four thousand Yakşas began the fight.

verses.sanskrit:
ते गदामुसलप्रासशक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः
अभिघ्नन्तो रणे यक्षा राक्षसानभिदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
te gadāmusalaprāsaśaktitomaramudgaraiḥ
abhighnanto raṇe yakṣā rākṣasānabhidudruvuḥ

translations.english: And attacking the Rākşasas with maces and clubs and bearded darts, and with darts tomoras and bludgeons, the Yaksas rushed at (their adversaries).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रहस्तेन तदा सहस्रं निहतं रणे
महोदरेण गदया सहस्रमपरं हतम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prahastena tadā sahasraṁ nihataṁ raṇe
mahodareṇa gadayā sahasramaparaṁ hatam

translations.english: And a thousand of the Yakşas were slain by Praśasta in the conflict; and another thousand of capable warriors were slain by Mahodara.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धेन च तदा राम मारीचेन दुरात्मना
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्रे निपातिते
verses.transliteration:
kruddhena ca tadā rāma mārīcena durātmanā
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa dve sahasre nipātite

translations.english: O king, in the twinkling of an eye Märīca, waxing wroth and eager for encounter brought down two thousand (of enemy's soldiers).

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे
मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात्ताडितो न च कम्पितः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣeṇa samāgamya māṇibhadro mahāraṇe
musalenorasi krodhāttāḍito na ca kampitaḥ

translations.english: And Dhūmrākşa, confronting Māņibhadra in the mighty conflict hit him as the chest with a bludgeon; but he did not move thereat.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः
धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलो निपपात ह
verses.transliteration:
tato gadāṁ samāvidhya māṇibhadreṇa rākṣasaḥ
dhūmrākṣastāḍito mūrdhni vihvalo nipapāta ha

translations.english: Then Mänibhadra dealt the Raksasa a blow with his mace; and thereat Dhūmrākṣa smite at the head fell down senseless (on the ground).

verses.sanskrit:
धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम्
अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धो माणिभद्रं दशाननः
verses.transliteration:
dhūmrākṣaṁ tāḍitaṁ dṛṣṭvā patitaṁ śoṇitokṣitam
abhyadhāvatsusaṁkruddho māṇibhadraṁ daśānanaḥ

translations.english: And seeing Dhūmrākṣa wounded and down, bathed in blood, the Ten-necked Răvaņa rushed at Māņibhadra in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
तं क्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम्
शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुंगवः
verses.transliteration:
taṁ kruddhamabhidhāvantaṁ yugāntāgnimivotthitam
śaktibhistāḍayāmāsa tisṛbhiryakṣapuṁgavaḥ

translations.english: Then that foremost of Yakşas hit Daśānana with three darts as he was rushing in wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राक्षसराजेन ताडितो गदया रणे
तस्य तेन प्रहारेण मुकुटः पार्श्वमागतः
तदा प्रभृति यक्षोऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरिति स्मृतः
verses.transliteration:
tato rākṣasarājena tāḍito gadayā raṇe
tasya tena prahāreṇa mukuṭaḥ pārśvamāgataḥ
tadā prabhṛti yakṣo'sau pārśvamauliriti smṛtaḥ

translations.english: And on being thus hit, (Rāvana) struck at Manibhadra's head: and at that stroke his crown was depressed at one side.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मिंस्तु विमुखे यक्षे माणिभद्रे महात्मनि
संनादः सुमहान्राम तस्मिञ्शैले व्यवर्धत
verses.transliteration:
tasmiṁstu vimukhe yakṣe māṇibhadre mahātmani
saṁnādaḥ sumahānrāma tasmiñśaile vyavardhata

translations.english: From that day forth that Yaksa remained with his head hollow on one side. And on the highsouled Māņibhadra having been baffled, a great uproar, O king rose in that mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दूरात्प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः
शुक्रप्रोष्टःपदाभ्यां च शङ्खपद्मसमावृतः
verses.transliteration:
tato dūrātpradadṛśe dhanādhyakṣo gadādharaḥ
śukraproṣṭaḥpadābhyāṁ ca śaṅkhapadmasamāvṛtaḥ

translations.english: Then at a distance, the lord of riches, mace in hand, accompanied by Sukra and Praushthapada and Padma and Sanka saw (Ravana) in the field.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं संख्ये शापाद्विभ्रष्टगौरवम्
उवाच वचनं धीमान्युक्तं पैतामहे कुले
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṁ saṁkhye śāpādvibhraṣṭagauravam
uvāca vacanaṁ dhīmānyuktaṁ paitāmahe kule

translations.english: Seeing his brother in the encounter with his glory obscured through the curse (he had ere this come by), the intelligent (Lord of Yaksas) spoke in words worthy of the line of his grand-father.

verses.sanskrit:
मया त्वं वार्यमाणोऽपि नावगच्छसि दुर्मते
पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः
verses.transliteration:
mayā tvaṁ vāryamāṇo'pi nāvagacchasi durmate
paścādasya phalaṁ prāpya jñāsyase nirayaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: As, O wicked-minded one, you desistest not, albeit forbidden by me, you shall, afterwards attaining the fruit of this, and repairing to hell, know (the fate that follow there).

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि मोहाद्विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति मानवः
परिणामे स वि मूढो जानीते कर्मणः फलम्
verses.transliteration:
yo hi mohādviṣaṁ pītvā nāvagacchati mānavaḥ
pariṇāme sa vi mūḍho jānīte karmaṇaḥ phalam

translations.english: That perverse one, that through ignorance having drunk poison, neglects to adopt proper measures, know the consequence of his act ultimately.

verses.sanskrit:
दैवतानि हि नन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तेन केनचित्
येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्तच्च न बुध्यसे
verses.transliteration:
daivatāni hi nandanti dharmayuktena kenacit
yena tvamīdṛśaṁ bhāvaṁ nītastacca na budhyase

translations.english: The gods have set their face against you on account of a certain misdeed of your; and having for this, been reduced to this condition, you do not understand things.

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि मातॄः पितॄन्भ्रातॄनाचर्यांश्चावमन्यते
स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः
verses.transliteration:
yo hi mātṝḥ pitṝnbhrātṝnācaryāṁścāvamanyate
sa paśyati phalaṁ tasya pretarājavaśaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: He that dishonour his father and mother* and spiritual preceptor, reap the fruit of his act on coming under the sway of the sovereign of the dead. *Unless he serve his parents, his heart does not incline to piety.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोऽर्जनम्
स पश्चात्तप्यते मूढो मृतो दृष्ट्वात्मनो गतिम्
verses.transliteration:
adhruve hi śarīre yo na karoti tapo'rjanam
sa paścāttapyate mūḍho mṛto dṛṣṭvātmano gatim

translations.english: Having regard that this body is uncertain, that foolish person, that does not acquire asceticism, dying go the way that he deserve.

verses.sanskrit:
कस्यचिन्न हि दुर्बुधेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः
यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते
verses.transliteration:
kasyacinna hi durbudheśchandato jāyate matiḥ
yādṛśaṁ kurute karma tādṛśaṁ phalamaśnute

translations.english: The mind of a perverse man does not willingly incline towards good; and as he acts, he gets the fruits (he reaps as he sows).

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिं रूपं बलं वित्तं पुत्रान्माहात्म्यमेव च
प्रप्नुवन्ति नराः सर्वं स्वकृतैः पूर्वकर्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
buddhiṁ rūpaṁ balaṁ vittaṁ putrānmāhātmyameva ca
prapnuvanti narāḥ sarvaṁ svakṛtaiḥ pūrvakarmabhiḥ

translations.english: In this world people, making their own good fortune and beauty, strength, sons, wealth and valour, gain these by virtue of their pious acts.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी
न त्वां समभिभाषिष्ये दुर्वृत्तस्यैष निर्णयः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ nirayagāmī tvaṁ yasya te matirīdṛśī
na tvāṁ samabhibhāṣiṣye durvṛttasyaiṣa nirṇayaḥ

translations.english: Being given to such iniquitous acts, you will go to hell; and your designs being such, I will not hold parley with you.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः
मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tatastena tasyāmātyāḥ samāhatāḥ
mārīcapramukhāḥ sarve vimukhā vipradudruvuḥ

translations.english: Honest people should act carefully in connection with the wicked.' Thus reprimanded by him, his (Rāvana's) councillors, headed by Marica, on being struck, took to their heels.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना
गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानाद्व्यकम्पत
verses.transliteration:
tatastena daśagrīvo yakṣendreṇa mahātmanā
gadayābhihato mūrdhni na ca sthānādvyakampata

translations.english: Then Daśagrīva on being Struck in the head with the mace by the lord of Yakşas, did not move from his place.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तौ राम निघ्नन्तावन्योन्यं परमाहवे
न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ बभूवतुरमर्षणैः
verses.transliteration:
tatastau rāma nighnantāvanyonyaṁ paramāhave
na vihvalau na ca śrāntau babhūvaturamarṣaṇaiḥ

translations.english: And then, O Rama, the Yaksa and Raksasa, smiting each other in mighty encounter, did not get bewildered of experience fatigue.

verses.sanskrit:
आग्नेयमस्त्रं स ततो मुमोच धनदो रणे
वारुणेन दशग्रीवस्तदस्त्रं प्रत्यवारयत्
verses.transliteration:
āgneyamastraṁ sa tato mumoca dhanado raṇe
vāruṇena daśagrīvastadastraṁ pratyavārayat

translations.english: And then the bestower of riches discharged a fiery weapon at him; and thereat the lord of Rāks asa resisted it with a Varuņa weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः
कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa tenābhihato vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ
kṛttamūla ivāśoko nipapāta dhanādhipaḥ

translations.english: Thus smitten by him, the lord of wealth, baffled, toppled down to the earth covered with blood like an aśoka whose roots have been hewn away.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स धनाधिपः
नन्दनं वनमानीय धनदो श्वासितस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ padmādibhistatra nidhibhiḥ sa dhanādhipaḥ
nandanaṁ vanamānīya dhanado śvāsitastadā

translations.english: Thereat Padma and other Nidhi deities, surrounding the granter the granter of wealth, raised him up and brought him to the Nandana wood.

verses.sanskrit:
स जित्वा भ्रातरं राम धनदं राक्षसाधिपः
महासेनप्रसूतिं तु ययौ शरवणं ततः
verses.transliteration:
sa jitvā bhrātaraṁ rāma dhanadaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
mahāsenaprasūtiṁ tu yayau śaravaṇaṁ tataḥ

translations.english: O Rāma, having, vanquished his brother, the lord of riches, the king of Räkşasas went to the great wood of reeds, where Mahasena was born.

verses.sanskrit:
अथापश्यद्दशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं तदा
गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम्
verses.transliteration:
athāpaśyaddaśagrīvo raukmaṁ śaravaṇaṁ tadā
gabhastijālasaṁvītaṁ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram

translations.english: The Ten-necked Rāvana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पार्श्वमुपागम्य भवस्यानुचरो बली
नन्दीश्वर उवाचेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pārśvamupāgamya bhavasyānucaro balī
nandīśvara uvācedaṁ rākṣasendramaśaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: As they were speaking thus, that attendant of Bhava, Nandi, terrific, of yellow black hue, dwarfish, frightful, with his head shaven, having short arms, and stout, coming up to them, said (this). And the lordly Nandi, undaunted, addressed the sovereign of the Raksasas, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्
प्राणिनामेव सर्वेषामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः
verses.transliteration:
suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṁ daityadānavarakṣasām
prāṇināmeva sarveṣāmagamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ

translations.english: Desist you O Ten-necked one; Śankara sport in the mountain; and (now) He is incapable of being approached by every one, birds, serpents and Yaksas; gods, Gandharvas and Raksasas?

verses.sanskrit:
स रोषात्ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य च
कोऽयं शंकर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागमत्
verses.transliteration:
sa roṣāttāmranayanaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya ca
ko'yaṁ śaṁkara ityuktvā śailamūlamupāgamat

translations.english: Hearing Nandi's speech, (Ravana), wrought up with wrath, his eyes coppery, and his earrings shaking, leapt down from Puspaka. And saying, 'who is this Sankara? and he came down to the base of the mount. He beheld there Nandi stationed at the side of the deity, supporting himself on his flaming dart, resembling a second Sankara.

verses.sanskrit:
स वानरमुखं दृष्ट्वा तमवज्ञाय राक्षसः
प्रहासं मुमुचे मौर्ख्यात्सतोय इव तोयदः
verses.transliteration:
sa vānaramukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā tamavajñāya rākṣasaḥ
prahāsaṁ mumuce maurkhyātsatoya iva toyadaḥ

translations.english: And seeing that one having the face of a monkey, the Raksasas, deriding him, burst out into laughter, and seemed as if a mass of clouds were sending roars.

verses.sanskrit:
संक्रुद्धो भगवान्नन्दी शंकरस्यापरा तनुः
अब्रवीद्राक्षसं तत्र दशग्रीवमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁkruddho bhagavānnandī śaṁkarasyāparā tanuḥ
abravīdrākṣasaṁ tatra daśagrīvamupasthitam

translations.english: Thereat, growing enraged, the reverend Nandi Sankara's other body spoke into that Rākṣasa The Ten-necked one present there.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्मद्रूपसंयुक्ता मद्वीर्यसमतेजसः
उत्पत्स्यन्ते वधार्थं हि कुलस्य तव वानराः
verses.transliteration:
tasmānmadrūpasaṁyuktā madvīryasamatejasaḥ
utpatsyante vadhārthaṁ hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ

translations.english: “As O Daśānana, deriding me for my monkery-form, you have indulged in a laughter resembling the bursting of thunder, do monkeys endowed with prowess, and possessed of my form and energy shall be born for compassing the destruction of your race.

verses.sanskrit:
किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं यत्त्वां निशाचर
न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ tvidānīṁ mayā śakyaṁ kartuṁ yattvāṁ niśācara
na hantavyo hatastvaṁ hi pūrvameva svakarmabhiḥ

translations.english: But, O night-ranger, I can even now end you quite; yet I must not slay you for you have ere this been slain by your acts.

verses.sanskrit:
अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं निशाचरः
पर्वतं तं समासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṁ niśācaraḥ
parvataṁ taṁ samāsādya vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: But without heeding Nandi's speech, that highly powerful one Daśānana coming to the mountain, said.

verses.sanskrit:
पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः
तदेतच्छैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते
verses.transliteration:
puṣpakasya gatiśchinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ
tadetacchailamunmūlaṁ karomi tava gopate

translations.english: 'O Gopati, I will even uproot this mountain, for whom Pușpaka was deprived of its motion as I was journeying.

verses.sanskrit:
केन प्रभावेन भवस्तत्र क्रीडति राजवत्
विज्ञातव्यं न जानीषे भयस्थानमुपस्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
kena prabhāvena bhavastatra krīḍati rājavat
vijñātavyaṁ na jānīṣe bhayasthānamupasthitam

translations.english: It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्भुजान्प्रक्षिप्य पर्वते
तोलयामास तं शैलं समृगव्यालपादपम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rājanbhujānprakṣipya parvate
tolayāmāsa taṁ śailaṁ samṛgavyālapādapam

translations.english: Having said this, O Rama, Ravana seizing the mountain with his arms, lifted it up at once; and then the mountain trembled greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राम महादेवः प्रहसन्वीक्ष्य तत्कृतम्
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया
verses.transliteration:
tato rāma mahādevaḥ prahasanvīkṣya tatkṛtam
pādāṅguṣṭhena taṁ śailaṁ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā

translations.english: Then, O Rāma, Mahadeva foremost of the deities even Hara, as in sport pressed the mount with his great toe.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते पीडितास्तस्य शैलस्याधो गता भुजाः
विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tataste pīḍitāstasya śailasyādho gatā bhujāḥ
vismitāścābhavaṁstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: Thereat his arms, resembling blocks of stone felt the shock and then there the councillors of that Rākşasa were struck with amaze.

verses.sanskrit:
रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात्तथा
मुक्तो विरावः सुमहांस्त्रैलोक्यं येन पूरितम्
verses.transliteration:
rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṁ pīḍanāttathā
mukto virāvaḥ sumahāṁstrailokyaṁ yena pūritam

translations.english: The Rākṣasa, from wrath and the pain felt in his arms, set up a shout that shook the entire triune world.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाग्रे विष्ठितस्तदा
मुक्त्वा तस्य भुजान्राजन्प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāgre viṣṭhitastadā
muktvā tasya bhujānrājanprāha vākyaṁ daśānanam

translations.english: Thereat that Lord Mahādeva, pleased, set free the hands of Daśānana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rāma, addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्माल्लोकत्रयं त्वेतद्रावितं भयमागतम्
तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना तेन भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
yasmāllokatrayaṁ tvetadrāvitaṁ bhayamāgatam
tasmāttvaṁ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā tena bhaviṣyasi

translations.english: O Daśānana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले
एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम्
verses.transliteration:
devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale
evaṁ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṁ lokarāvaṇam

translations.english: And deities and men, Yakşas and others living on earth shall call you Rāvana terror to creatures,

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धः पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि
मया त्वमभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
gaccha paulastya visrabdhaḥ pathā yena tvamicchasi
mayā tvamabhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām

translations.english: Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.

verses.sanskrit:
साक्षान्महेश्वरेणैवं कृतनामा स रावणः
अभिवाद्य महादेवं विमानं तत्समारुहत्
verses.transliteration:
sākṣānmaheśvareṇaivaṁ kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ
abhivādya mahādevaṁ vimānaṁ tatsamāruhat

translations.english: Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Rāvana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो महीतले राम परिचक्राम रावणः
क्षत्रियान्सुमहावीर्यान्बाधमानस्ततस्ततः
verses.transliteration:
tato mahītale rāma paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ
kṣatriyānsumahāvīryānbādhamānastatastataḥ

translations.english: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaņa, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Kșatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ राजन्महाबाहुर्विचरन्स महीतलम्
हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः
verses.transliteration:
atha rājanmahābāhurvicaransa mahītalam
himavadvanamāsādya paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ

translations.english: Then, O King, the mighty-armed Ravana ranging the earth, came to Himavān and began to go round it.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रापश्यत वै कन्यां कृष्टाजिनजटाधराम्
आर्षेण विधिना युक्तां तपन्तीं देवतामिव
verses.transliteration:
tatrāpaśyata vai kanyāṁ kṛṣṭājinajaṭādharām
ārṣeṇa vidhinā yuktāṁ tapantīṁ devatāmiva

translations.english: It came to pass that there he saw a damsel wearing a dark deer-skin and matted locks, leading the life of a saint, and flaming like a celestial.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम्
काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā rūpasaṁpannāṁ kanyāṁ tāṁ sumahāvratām
kāmamohaparītātmā papraccha prahasanniva

translations.english: Seeing the girl observing high vows, endowed with beauty, he, with his soul overwhelmed with lust asked her, laughing.

verses.sanskrit:
किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते
न हि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्येयं प्रतिक्रिया
verses.transliteration:
kimidaṁ vartase bhadre viruddhaṁ yauvanasya te
na hi yuktā tavaitasya rūpasyeyaṁ pratikriyā

translations.english: How is it, o amiable one, that you act thus contrary to your youth? This course of life surely does not befit your beauty.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या तेनानार्येण रक्षसा
अब्रवीद्विधिवत्कृत्वा तस्यातिथ्यं तपोधना
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu sā kanyā tenānāryeṇa rakṣasā
abravīdvidhivatkṛtvā tasyātithyaṁ tapodhanā

translations.english: Thus accosted by Rāvana, that illustrious girl, having asceticism for wealth, having received him hospitably in due form, said.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशध्वजो नाम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिर्मम धार्मिकः
बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान्बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः
verses.transliteration:
kuśadhvajo nāma pitā brahmarṣirmama dhārmikaḥ
bṛhaspatisutaḥ śrīmānbuddhyā tulyo bṛhaspateḥ

translations.english: My sire is named Kušadhvaja a Brahmarși of immeasurable energy, son to Bệhaspati, endowed with grace, and like to Bphaspati himself in intelligence.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः
संभूता वान्मयी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता
verses.transliteration:
tasyāhaṁ kurvato nityaṁ vedābhyāsaṁ mahātmanaḥ
saṁbhūtā vānmayī kanyā nāmnā vedavatī smṛtā

translations.english: And while that high sound one was engaged in the daily study of the Vedas, I was born as his word-impregnated daughter, named Vedavati.

verses.sanskrit:
न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान्राक्षसेश्वर
कारणं तद्वदिष्यामि निशामय महाभुज
verses.transliteration:
na ca māṁ sa pitā tebhyo dattavānrākṣaseśvara
kāraṇaṁ tadvadiṣyāmi niśāmaya mahābhuja

translations.english: When the gods and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas, Raksasas, and Pannagas, coming to my sire asked for me, O foremost of Rākşasas, my father did not bestow me on any one of them. And I shall you the reason thereof; listen, O long-armed one.

verses.sanskrit:
दातुमिच्छति धर्मात्मा तच्छ्रुत्वा बलदर्पितः
शम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितोऽभवत्
तेन रात्रौ प्रसुप्तो मे पिता पापेन हिंसितः
verses.transliteration:
dātumicchati dharmātmā tacchrutvā baladarpitaḥ
śambhurnāma tato rājā daityānāṁ kupito'bhavat
tena rātrau prasupto me pitā pāpena hiṁsitaḥ

translations.english: My father's intended son-in-law was even Vişņu sovereign of the celestials, and the lord of the triune world; and my father would not bestow me on any other. And hearing this, a certain king of the Daityas, named Sambhu proud, of his prowess was wrought up with wrath, and one night as my sire was on bed, that wicked one slew him. Thereat my forlorn mother, of exalted righteousness embracing my father's body entered into fire.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति
करोमीति ममेच्छा च हृदये साधु विष्ठिता
verses.transliteration:
tato manorathaṁ satyaṁ piturnārāyaṇaṁ prati
karomīti mamecchā ca hṛdaye sādhu viṣṭhitā

translations.english: Then wishing to realise my father's wish touching Närāyana, I have fixed my heart even upon him.

verses.sanskrit:
विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन्गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन
जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
vijñātastvaṁ hi me rājangaccha paulastyanandana
jānāmi tapasā sarvaṁ trailokye yaddhi vartate

translations.english: I know you, O king. Go you, O son of Paulastya. By virtue of my asceticism I know all that takes place in these three regions.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽब्रवीद्रावणस्तत्र तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम्
अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात्कन्दर्पशरपीडितः
verses.transliteration:
so'bravīdrāvaṇastatra tāṁ kanyāṁ sumahāvratām
avaruhya vimānāgrātkandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ

translations.english: Thereat descending from the front of his car, Ravana, affected with the shafts of Kandarpa, again addressed that girl, observant of a mighty VOW. a

verses.sanskrit:
अवलिप्तासि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी
वृद्धानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते धर्मसंचयः
verses.transliteration:
avaliptāsi suśroṇi yasyāste matirīdṛśī
vṛddhānāṁ mṛgaśāvākṣi bhrājate dharmasaṁcayaḥ

translations.english: O you of sharply hips, in as much as such is your intent, you must be very proud. O you having the eyes of young antelope, accumulation of religious merit suits old people.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वं सर्वगुणसंपन्ना नार्हसे कर्तुमीदृशम्
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवने वार्धकं विधिम्
verses.transliteration:
tvaṁ sarvaguṇasaṁpannā nārhase kartumīdṛśam
trailokyasundarī bhīru yauvane vārdhakaṁ vidhim

translations.english: You, furnished with every perfection, should not talk thus. You are the paragon in these three worlds,. Your youth wax away.

verses.sanskrit:
कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे
वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च
न मयासौ समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसेऽङ्गने
verses.transliteration:
kaśca tāvadasau yaṁ tvaṁ viṣṇurityabhibhāṣase
vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca
na mayāsau samo bhadre yaṁ tvaṁ kāmayase'ṅgane

translations.english: Who is he whom you call Vişņu O mild one, neither in prowess, nor in asceticism, nor in enjoyment, nor in strength, is he my equal, whom, O damsel, you seek.

verses.sanskrit:
मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम्
मूर्धजेषु च तां रक्षः कराग्रेण परामृशत्
verses.transliteration:
mā maivamiti sā kanyā tamuvāca niśācaram
mūrdhajeṣu ca tāṁ rakṣaḥ karāgreṇa parāmṛśat

translations.english: Thus addressed there by Vedavatī, the nightranger seized the girl by the hair.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन साच्छिनत्
उवाचाग्निं समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा
verses.transliteration:
tato vedavatī kruddhā keśānhastena sācchinat
uvācāgniṁ samādhāya maraṇāya kṛtatvarā

translations.english: Thereat Vedavati, wroth, cut off her hair with her hand transformed into a sword.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य नेदानीं मम जीवितम्
रक्षस्तस्मात्प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम्
verses.transliteration:
dharṣitāyāstvayānārya nedānīṁ mama jīvitam
rakṣastasmātpravekṣyāmi paśyataste hutāśanam

translations.english: You object, having been outraged by you I wish not to live. Therefore, O Raksasa, I will enter into fire in your very presence.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहमपापा चाप्यनाथवत्
तस्मात्तव वधार्थं वै समुत्पत्स्याम्यहं पुनः
verses.transliteration:
yasmāttu dharṣitā cāhamapāpā cāpyanāthavat
tasmāttava vadhārthaṁ vai samutpatsyāmyahaṁ punaḥ

translations.english: As I have in this world been dishonoured by you you are nefarious. I shall again be born to compass your destruction.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि शक्यः स्त्रिया पाप हन्तुं त्वं तु विशेषतः
शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत्
verses.transliteration:
na hi śakyaḥ striyā pāpa hantuṁ tvaṁ tu viśeṣataḥ
śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaśca vyayo bhavet

translations.english: It lie not in a female to slay a male intent on sin; and if I utter a curse, it shall cost my asceticism.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि त्वस्ति मया किंचित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा
तेन ह्ययोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता
verses.transliteration:
yadi tvasti mayā kiṁcitkṛtaṁ dattaṁ hutaṁ tathā
tena hyayonijā sādhvī bhaveyaṁ dharmiṇaḥ sutā

translations.english: But if I have done anything, given away any thing, offered oblations to the fire, then I shall be the chaste daughter of some virtuous person, albeit unborn of any female vessel.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलन्तं वै हुताशनम्
पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā praviṣṭā sā jvalantaṁ vai hutāśanam
papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ

translations.english: Having delivered herself thus, she entered into the flaming fire; and thereat a celestial shower of blossoms rained all around from heaven.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं क्रोधहतः शत्रुर्ययासौ निहतस्त्वया
समुपाश्रित्य शैलाभं तव वीर्यममानुषम्
verses.transliteration:
pūrvaṁ krodhahataḥ śatruryayāsau nihatastvayā
samupāśritya śailābhaṁ tava vīryamamānuṣam

translations.english: The enemy, endowed with the splendour of a hill, formerly that been slain by her, by help of your superhuman prowess.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेषा महाभागा मर्त्येषूत्पद्यते पुनः
क्षेत्रे हलमुखग्रस्ते वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा
verses.transliteration:
evameṣā mahābhāgā martyeṣūtpadyate punaḥ
kṣetre halamukhagraste vedyāmagniśikhopamā

translations.english: This one of eminent righteousness would again spring up on earth like a flame from a field furrowed by the plough.

verses.sanskrit:
एषा वेदवती नाम पूर्वमासीत्कृते युगे
त्रेतायुगमनुप्राप्य वधार्थं तस्य रक्षसः
सीतोत्पन्नेति सीतैषा मानुषैः पुनरुच्यते
verses.transliteration:
eṣā vedavatī nāma pūrvamāsītkṛte yuge
tretāyugamanuprāpya vadhārthaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ
sītotpanneti sītaiṣā mānuṣaiḥ punarucyate

translations.english: This one named Vedavatſ was born in the Kệta age; and in the Tretā age, for compassing the destruction of that Rākşasa, she was born in the Maithila line of the high-souled Janaka.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः
पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
praviṣṭāyāṁ hutāśaṁ tu vedavatyāṁ sa rāvaṇaḥ
puṣpakaṁ tatsamāruhya paricakrāma medinīm

translations.english: When Vedavati had entered into the fire, Rāvana, ascending Puşpaka, began to range the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः
उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
tato maruttaṁ nṛpatiṁ yajantaṁ saha daivataiḥ
uśīrabījamāsādya dadarśa sa tu rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: And coming to Uśirabīja, Rāvaņa saw a king (named) Marutta, sacrificing along with the deities.

verses.sanskrit:
संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्भ्राता साक्षाद्बृहस्पतेः
याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगणैर्वृतः
verses.transliteration:
saṁvarto nāma brahmarṣirbhrātā sākṣādbṛhaspateḥ
yājayāmāsa dharmajñaḥ sarvairbrahmagaṇairvṛtaḥ

translations.english: And a righteous Brahmarşi named Samvarta, the very brother of Bphaspati, officiated at the sacrifice accompanied by the deities.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद्रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम्
तां तां योनिं समापन्नास्तस्य धर्षणभीरवः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā devāstu tadrakṣo varadānena durjayam
tāṁ tāṁ yoniṁ samāpannāstasya dharṣaṇabhīravaḥ

translations.english: Seeing that Rākşasa invincible by reason of the boon he had received, the deities, apprehensive of being worsted by him, assumed the forms of beasts.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः
कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसो वै वरुणोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
indro mayūraḥ saṁvṛtto dharmarājastu vāyasaḥ
kṛkalāso dhanādhyakṣo haṁso vai varuṇo'bhavat

translations.english: Indra became a peacock and the king of righteousness, a crow and the bestower of riches a lizard, and Varuna a swan; and, O slayer of foes, others also became other beasts. And then Rāvana entered into that sacrifice like an unclean dog.

verses.sanskrit:
तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्चेति निर्जितोऽस्मीति वा वद
verses.transliteration:
taṁ ca rājānamāsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
prāha yuddhaṁ prayacceti nirjito'smīti vā vada

translations.english: Then coming up to the king, Răvaņa lord of Raksāsas said: 'Give me battle, or say, I am defeated.

verses.sanskrit:
अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतोऽस्मि तव पार्थिव
धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम्
verses.transliteration:
akutūhalabhāvena prīto'smi tava pārthiva
dhanadasyānujaṁ yo māṁ nāvagacchasi rāvaṇam

translations.english: Whereat king Marutta asked, him 'Who are you'? And Ravana laughing in contempt said. "O king, I am delighted, that lacking curiosity, you do not dishonour Rävaņa, younger brother to the bestower of riches.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिषु लोकेषु कः सोऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम्
भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम्
verses.transliteration:
triṣu lokeṣu kaḥ so'sti yo na jānāti me balam
bhrātaraṁ yena nirjitya vimānamidamāhṛtam

translations.english: What other man is there in these three regions that know not the might of me, who, conquering my brother, has got possession of this car.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च स पार्थिवः
रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śarāsanaṁ gṛhya sāyakāṁśca sa pārthivaḥ
raṇāya niryayau kruddhaḥ saṁvarto mārgamāvṛṇot

translations.english: Then taking up his bow and arrows, that king of men went out for encounter; but Samavartta stood in the way.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽब्रवीत्स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः
श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं संप्रहारो न ते क्षमः
verses.transliteration:
so'bravītsnehasaṁyuktaṁ maruttaṁ taṁ mahānṛṣiḥ
śrotavyaṁ yadi madvākyaṁ saṁprahāro na te kṣamaḥ

translations.english: And that great sage said to Marutta words informed with affection 'If you hear my speech, you should not fight.

verses.sanskrit:
संशयश्च रणे नित्यं राक्षसश्चैष दुर्जयः
स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः
विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
saṁśayaśca raṇe nityaṁ rākṣasaścaiṣa durjayaḥ
sa nivṛtto gurorvākyānmaruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
visṛjya saśaraṁ cāpaṁ svastho makhamukho'bhavat

translations.english: If this Maheśvara-sacrifice should remain incomplete, it will burn up your dynasty. Where is the fight of one initiated in a sacrifice? And where is the passion of one initiated in a sacrifice? And victory is ever uncertain; and the Rākşasa is difficult to vanquish. And thereupon, the lord of Earth Marutta desisted in consonance with the instructions of his spiritual preceptor; and composed addressed himself to completing the sacrifice, giving up his bow with the arrow set. And thereat considering him as defeated, Suka proclaimed this all round, and from delight cried aloud, 'Victory to Rāvana!

verses.sanskrit:
तान्भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान्महर्षीन्यज्ञमागतान्
वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः संप्रययौ महीम्
verses.transliteration:
tānbhakṣayitvā tatrasthānmaharṣīnyajñamāgatān
vitṛpto rudhiraisteṣāṁ punaḥ saṁprayayau mahīm

translations.english: Then devouring the Maharsis that were present at the place of sacrifice, Rāvana, satiated with their blood, again went to the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः
ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वान्यथाब्रुवन्
verses.transliteration:
rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāścaiva divaukasaḥ
tataḥ svāṁ yonimāsādya tāni sattvānyathābruvan

translations.english: On Ravana having departed, the deities, inhabiting the etherial regions Indra etc. assuming their proper forms, addressed those creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
मम नेत्रसहस्रं यत्तत्ते बर्हे भविष्यति
वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
mama netrasahasraṁ yattatte barhe bhaviṣyati
varṣamāṇe mayi mudaṁ prāpsyase prītilakṣaṇam

translations.english: And from joy Indra spoke to the purpleplumed peacock, 'Pleased am I with you righteous one. No fear shall spring to you from serpents; and your plumage shall be furnished with an hundred eyes. And when I shall shower, you shall be filled with glee as a token of my satisfaction with you.' Thus did Indra chief of celestials, confer a boon on the peacock.

verses.sanskrit:
नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप
सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वे विचित्रताम्
verses.transliteration:
nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṁ narādhipa
surādhipādvaraṁ prāpya gatāḥ sarve vicitratām

translations.english: Formerly, O King, the peacock's wings had one unvaried blue. Having received the boon, the peacock departed.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मराजोऽब्रवीद्राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं स्थितम्
पक्षिंस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य च वचः शृणु
verses.transliteration:
dharmarājo'bravīdrāma prāgvaṁśe vāyasaṁ sthitam
pakṣiṁstavāsmi suprītaḥ prītasya ca vacaḥ śṛṇu

translations.english: O Rāma, then the king of righteousness said to the crow, seated in front of the sacrificial apartment 'O bird, I am well pleased with you. Listen to my words as I utter them.

verses.sanskrit:
यथान्ये विविधै रोगैः पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया
ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
yathānye vividhai rogaiḥ pīḍyante prāṇino mayā
te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: As I have been pleased with you, you shall without doubt, enjoy immunity from the various ailments to which the birds are subject.

verses.sanskrit:
मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान्मम विहंगम
यावत्त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद्भविष्यसि
verses.transliteration:
mṛtyutaste bhayaṁ nāsti varānmama vihaṁgama
yāvattvāṁ na vadhiṣyanti narāstāvadbhaviṣyasi

translations.english: O bird, from my curse fear of death shall not approach you; and you shall exist so long as people do not slay you.

verses.sanskrit:
ये च मद्विषयस्थास्तु मानवाः क्षुधयार्दिताः
त्वयि भुक्ते तु तृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः
verses.transliteration:
ye ca madviṣayasthāstu mānavāḥ kṣudhayārditāḥ
tvayi bhukte tu tṛptāste bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ

translations.english: Those men residing in my dominion, being smitten with hunger, shall be refreshed along with your relations, when you have eaten and been refreshed.

verses.sanskrit:
वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविचारिणम्
श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं वचः पत्ररथेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
varuṇastvabravīddhaṁsaṁ gaṅgātoyavicāriṇam
śrūyatāṁ prītisaṁyuktaṁ vacaḥ patraratheśvara

translations.english: Then Varuņa addressed that lord of birds the swan ranging the waters of the Gangā, 'Listen to my words fraught with joy, your hue shall be charming, mild, and like to the lunar disc; and it shall be beautiful, resembling the sheen of spotless foam.

verses.sanskrit:
मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि
प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम्
verses.transliteration:
maccharīraṁ samāsādya kānto nityaṁ bhaviṣyasi
prāpsyase cātulāṁ prītimetanme prītilakṣaṇam

translations.english: And approaching my person you shall ever be beautiful to behold; and you shall, as a sign of my gratification, attain unparalleled complacence.

verses.sanskrit:
हंसानां हि पुरा राम न वर्णः सर्वपाण्डुरः
पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः
verses.transliteration:
haṁsānāṁ hi purā rāma na varṇaḥ sarvapāṇḍuraḥ
pakṣā nīlāgrasaṁvītāḥ kroḍāḥ śaṣpāgranirmalāḥ

translations.english: Formerly, O Rama, swans had not a hue of one unvaried whiteness. Their wings ended in, blue, and their breasts wore the spotless hue of tender grass. Then Vaiśravana addressed the chameleon as it was stationed at the mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम्
एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
sadravyaṁ ca śiro nityaṁ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam
eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Your hue shall be gold-gleaming. Pleased am I with you. Your undeteriorating head shall be ever gold-hued. And this golden hue of your shall proceed from my gratification?

verses.sanskrit:
एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन्यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः
निवृत्ते सह राज्ञा वै पुनः स्वभवनं गताः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ dattvā varāṁstebhyastasminyajñotsave surāḥ
nivṛtte saha rājñā vai punaḥ svabhavanaṁ gatāḥ

translations.english: Having thus conferred boons on them at that festal place, the celestials, along with the king, (on the sacrifice) having ended, went to their abode.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः
नगराणि नरेन्द्राणां युद्धकाङ्क्षी दशाननः
verses.transliteration:
atha jitvā maruttaṁ sa prayayau rākṣasādhipaḥ
nagarāṇi narendrāṇāṁ yuddhakāṅkṣī daśānanaḥ

translations.english: Having vanquished Marutta, that lord of Rākşasas the Ten-faced Răvaņa, eager for encounter, began to range the capitals of the foremost monarchs (of the earth).

verses.sanskrit:
स समासाद्य राजेन्द्रान्महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान्
अब्रवीद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु युद्धं मे दीयतामिति
verses.transliteration:
sa samāsādya rājendrānmahendravaruṇopamān
abravīdrākṣasendrastu yuddhaṁ me dīyatāmiti

translations.english: And coming to the most powerful crowned heads (in the world) resembling Mahendra and Varuna, the Raksasa king said: 'Give me battle; or declare we have been defeated. This I am resolved upon. Otherwise there is no escape for you?'

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु बहवः प्राज्ञाः पार्थिवा धर्मणिश्चयाः
निर्जिताः स्मेत्यभाषन्त ज्ञात्वा वरबलं रिपोः
verses.transliteration:
tatastu bahavaḥ prājñāḥ pārthivā dharmaṇiścayāḥ
nirjitāḥ smetyabhāṣanta jñātvā varabalaṁ ripoḥ

translations.english: Thereat those wise kings, possessed of great strength, and ever abiding by righteousness, being frightened (at Ravana's intimidation), took counsel of each other. And knowing the superior strength of the foe, they said, “We have been defeated.

verses.sanskrit:
अनरण्यः सुसंक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रमथाब्रवीत्
दीयते द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ते राक्षसाधिपते मया
verses.transliteration:
anaraṇyaḥ susaṁkruddho rākṣasendramathābravīt
dīyate dvandvayuddhaṁ te rākṣasādhipate mayā

translations.english: The lord of Ayodhyā, on hearing the words of that wicked-minded one, Anaranya, enraged, addressed the Raksasa-chief, saying, 'O king of Raksasas, I will give you combat, stay you. At once prepare for fight, and I also shall go and prepare myself.'

verses.sanskrit:
अथ पूर्वं श्रुतार्थेन सज्जितं सुमहद्धि यत्
निष्क्रामत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्य बलं रक्षोवधोद्यतम्
verses.transliteration:
atha pūrvaṁ śrutārthena sajjitaṁ sumahaddhi yat
niṣkrāmattannarendrasya balaṁ rakṣovadhodyatam

translations.english: When he had heard everything (regarding Răvaņa), the forces of that foremost of kings that had been intended for conquering (Ravana), sallied forth ready for bringing about the destruction of the of the Raksasa, ten-thousand elephants, a niyuta horse, and many thousands of cars and infantry, O best of men; and, that host consisting of infantry and cars, marched for encounter, covering up the earth.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्रावणबलं प्राप्य बलं तस्य महीपतेः
प्राणश्यत तदा राजन्हव्यं हुतमिवानले
verses.transliteration:
tadrāvaṇabalaṁ prāpya balaṁ tasya mahīpateḥ
prāṇaśyata tadā rājanhavyaṁ hutamivānale

translations.english: That host, of the king encountering the forces of Rāvana, were extinguished like to clarified butter thrown into the (sacrificial) fire. And having fought valorously for a long time, the remnant of the royal forces, suddenly coming in contact with the flaming Räkşasas ranks, were destroyed like to swarms of locusts entering into fire.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽपश्यत नरेन्द्रस्तु नश्यमानं महद्बलम्
महार्णवं समासाद्य यथा पञ्चापगा जलम्
verses.transliteration:
so'paśyata narendrastu naśyamānaṁ mahadbalam
mahārṇavaṁ samāsādya yathā pañcāpagā jalam

translations.english: He saw the mighty army of that powerful monarch destroyed by the (adversary), like to a hundred streams absorbed by an approaching ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं धनुर्विस्फारयन्स्वयम्
आसदाद नरेन्द्रास्तं रावणं क्रोधमूर्छितः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śakradhanuḥprakhyaṁ dhanurvisphārayansvayam
āsadāda narendrāstaṁ rāvaṇaṁ krodhamūrchitaḥ

translations.english: And then himself drawing his bow resembling the bow itself of Sakra, that foremost of sovereigns, beside himself with wrath, approached Rāvana.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो बाणशतान्यष्टौ पातयामास मूर्धनि
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
tato bāṇaśatānyaṣṭau pātayāmāsa mūrdhani
tasya rākṣasarājasya ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ

translations.english: Then that son of the Ikşvāku race discharged eight hundred arrows at Rāvana's head.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित्
वारिधारा इवाभ्रेभ्यः पतन्त्यो नगमूर्धनि
verses.transliteration:
tasya bāṇāḥ patantaste cakrire na kṣataṁ kvacit
vāridhārā ivābhrebhyaḥ patantyo nagamūrdhani

translations.english: And like to showers pouring down on the top of a mountain, his shafts did not inflict any wound (on Ravana).

verses.sanskrit:
ततो राक्षसराजेन क्रुद्धेन नृपतिस्तदा
तलेन भिहतो मूर्ध्नि स रथान्निपपात ह
verses.transliteration:
tato rākṣasarājena kruddhena nṛpatistadā
talena bhihato mūrdhni sa rathānnipapāta ha

translations.english: Then the king, smitten on the head with a slap by the enraged king of Rākşasas, dropped down from his car.

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलाङ्गः प्रवेपितः
वज्रदग्ध इवारण्ये सालो निपतितो महान्
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā patito bhūmau vihvalāṅgaḥ pravepitaḥ
vajradagdha ivāraṇye sālo nipatito mahān

translations.english: The king, deprived of his senses, fell down on the earth, with his body trembling all over; as falls in a forest a sāla scathed with heaven's fire.

verses.sanskrit:
तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद्रक्ष इक्ष्वाकुं पृथिवीपतिम्
किमिदानीं त्वया प्राप्तं फलं मां प्रति युध्यता
verses.transliteration:
taṁ prahasyābravīdrakṣa ikṣvākuṁ pṛthivīpatim
kimidānīṁ tvayā prāptaṁ phalaṁ māṁ prati yudhyatā

translations.english: Thereat the Raksasa, laughing, spoke to that Iksvāku, lord of the earth, 'What is this that you have gathered as the fruit of your encounter with me.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यान्नराधिप
शङ्के प्रमत्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम
verses.transliteration:
trailokye nāsti yo dvandvaṁ mama dadyānnarādhipa
śaṅke pramatto bhogeṣu na śṛṇoṣi balaṁ mama

translations.english: O king, there is none in this triune sphere that can combat with me. Having hitherto been sunk in lunacy, you have not heard of my strength.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो राजा मन्दासुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै यत्कालो दुरतिक्रमः
verses.transliteration:
tasyaivaṁ bruvato rājā mandāsurvākyamabravīt
kiṁ śakyamiha kartuṁ vai yatkālo duratikramaḥ

translations.english: As he was speaking thus, the king, whose sounds were fast running out said: 'What can I do in this matter. Verily time is incapable of being controlled.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यहं निर्जितो रक्षस्त्वया चात्मप्रशंसिना
कालेनेह विपन्नोऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान्
verses.transliteration:
na hyahaṁ nirjito rakṣastvayā cātmapraśaṁsinā
kāleneha vipanno'haṁ hetubhūtastu me bhavān

translations.english: I have been overcome by Time; you are merely an instrument. What can I do now, when I am going to-lose my life? I never turned away from fight; I have been slain fighting.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः
यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक्तथा सत्यं वचोऽस्तु मे
verses.transliteration:
yadi dattaṁ yadi hutaṁ yadi me sukṛtaṁ tapaḥ
yadi guptāḥ prajāḥ samyaktathā satyaṁ vaco'stu me

translations.english: But, O Raksasas, I shall tell you something in consequence of the disgrace that the Ikşvāku race has met with (today). If I have practised charity, if I have offered oblations into fire, if I have carried on pious penances, if i have governed my people well, then be my words verified!

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पत्स्यते कुले ह्यस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्
राजा परमतेजस्वी यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
utpatsyate kule hyasminnikṣvākūṇāṁ mahātmanām
rājā paramatejasvī yaste prāṇānhariṣyati

translations.english: There shall spring in the line of the highsouled Ikşvāku, one named Rāma son to Dasaratha who shall deprive your life.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो जलधरोदग्रस्ताडितो देवदुन्दुभिः
तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता
verses.transliteration:
tato jaladharodagrastāḍito devadundubhiḥ
tasminnudāhṛte śāpe puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā

translations.english: As he uttered this imprecation, the celestial kettle-drums sounded like the roaring of clouds; and blossoms showered down from the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम्
स्वर्गते च नृपे राम राक्षसः स न्यवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa rājā rājendra gataḥ sthānaṁ triviṣṭapam
svargate ca nṛpe rāma rākṣasaḥ sa nyavartata

translations.english: Then, that best of kings, went to heaven; and when that king had gone to the celestial regions, the Raksasa (also) went away.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वित्रासयन्मर्त्यान्पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः
आससाद घने तस्मिन्नारदं मुनिसत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tato vitrāsayanmartyānpṛthivyāṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
āsasāda ghane tasminnāradaṁ munisattamam

translations.english: As the lord of Rākşasas was ranging the earth frightening everyone, Nārada foremost of ascetics, came to that wood mounted on a cloud,

verses.sanskrit:
नारदस्तु महातेजा देवर्षिरमितप्रभः
अब्रवीन्मेघपृष्ठस्थो रावणं पुष्पके स्थितम्
verses.transliteration:
nāradastu mahātejā devarṣiramitaprabhaḥ
abravīnmeghapṛṣṭhastho rāvaṇaṁ puṣpake sthitam

translations.english: That Devarsi the exceedingly energetic Nārada of immeasurable splendour, seated on the back of the cloud, addressed Ravana, who was stationed in Puspaka, saying, O lord of Raks asas, o placid one, O son of Viśravā, stay. I am well pleased with your prowess and fame.

verses.sanskrit:
विष्णुना दैत्यघातैश्च तार्क्ष्यस्योरगधर्षणैः
त्वया समरमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः
verses.transliteration:
viṣṇunā daityaghātaiśca tārkṣyasyoragadharṣaṇaiḥ
tvayā samaramardaiśca bhṛśaṁ hi paritoṣitaḥ

translations.english: And even as Vişnu had pleased me by destroying the Daityas, you pleased me by harassing the Gandharvas and serpents.

verses.sanskrit:
किमयं वध्यते लोकस्त्वयावध्येन दैवतैः
हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः
verses.transliteration:
kimayaṁ vadhyate lokastvayāvadhyena daivataiḥ
hata eva hyayaṁ loko yadā mṛtyuvaśaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Why, my child, do you slay these*; you are incapable of being slain by even the celestials. All these (men) are subject to death, they are verily slain. *i.e. human being.

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचिद्वादित्रनृत्तानि सेव्यन्ते मुदितैर्जनैः
रुद्यते चापरैरार्तैर्धाराश्रुनयनाननैः
verses.transliteration:
kvacidvāditranṛttāni sevyante muditairjanaiḥ
rudyate cāparairārtairdhārāśrunayanānanaiḥ

translations.english: O mighty-armed one, o lord of Rākşasas, behold man, albeit having their sense stupified, engaged in the pursuit of various interests, and themselves not understanding their own ways;* some pass their time merrily with dancing and playing on musical instruments while others weep distressfully with tears streaming from their eyes down their cheeks. *Gati, according to the commentator, means the time of employment and suffering. I think the ordinary meaning answers, and give it accordingly.

verses.sanskrit:
माता पितृसुतस्नेहैर्भार्या बन्धुमनोरमैः
मोहेनायं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते
verses.transliteration:
mātā pitṛsutasnehairbhāryā bandhumanoramaiḥ
mohenāyaṁ jano dhvastaḥ kleśaṁ svaṁ nāvabudhyate

translations.english: Down fallen on account of their attachment for their mothers and fathers and sons, and of their desires touching their wives and friends they set small store by labours having the hereafter as their object.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्किमेवं परिक्लिश्य लोकं मोहनिराकृतम्
जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
tatkimevaṁ parikliśya lokaṁ mohanirākṛtam
jita eva tvayā saumya martyaloko na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: What then is the use of affecting a race that is brought down ever by its own infatuation. O placid one, this world is verily conquered by you, there is no doubt.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशो दीप्यमान इवौजसा
अब्रवीन्नारदं तत्र संप्रहस्याभिवाद्य च
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu laṅkeśo dīpyamāna ivaujasā
abravīnnāradaṁ tatra saṁprahasyābhivādya ca

translations.english: Thus addressed Lankā's lord, flaming in native energy, addressed Narada, laughing and saluting him. 'O you that delightest in the sport of gods and Gandharvas, and that take pleasure in warfare, I am ready to go to the nethermost regions for the purpose of conquest.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो लोकत्रयं जित्वा स्थाप्य नागान्सुरान्वशे
समुद्रममृतार्थं वै मथिष्यामि रसालयम्
verses.transliteration:
tato lokatrayaṁ jitvā sthāpya nāgānsurānvaśe
samudramamṛtārthaṁ vai mathiṣyāmi rasālayam

translations.english: And conquering the three worlds, and bringing under subjection serpents and celestials I shall for ambrosia churn the nether regions.

verses.sanskrit:
अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवं नारदो भगवानृषिः
क्व खल्विदानीं मार्गेण त्वयानेन गमिष्यते
verses.transliteration:
athābravīddaśagrīvaṁ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ
kva khalvidānīṁ mārgeṇa tvayānena gamiṣyate

translations.english: Then the reverend sage Närada spoke to the Ten-necked Ravana, Who save you can on forsooth go that journey? Verily, o irrepressible one, O destroyer of foes, the way leading to the city of the lord of the dead is difficult of access.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु शारदमेघाभं मुक्त्वा हासं दशाननः
उवाच कृतमित्येव वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu śāradameghābhaṁ muktvā hāsaṁ daśānanaḥ
uvāca kṛtamityeva vacanaṁ cedamabravīt

translations.english: Thereat laughing, the Ten-faced one said to the saint resembling a mass of white clouds, "This is done.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादेष महाब्रह्मन्वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः
गच्छामि दक्षिणामाशां यत्र सूर्यात्मजो नृपः
verses.transliteration:
tasmādeṣa mahābrahmanvaivasvatavadhodyataḥ
gacchāmi dakṣiṇāmāśāṁ yatra sūryātmajo nṛpaḥ

translations.english: Therefore,* O great Brahmana, intent upon slaying the Vaivasvata's son, I will go by this way which lead to the king-the offspring of the sun. *As you has commanded me.

verses.sanskrit:
मया हि भगवन्क्रोधात्प्रतिज्ञातं रणार्थिना
अवजेष्यामि चतुरो लोकपालानिति प्रभो
verses.transliteration:
mayā hi bhagavankrodhātpratijñātaṁ raṇārthinā
avajeṣyāmi caturo lokapālāniti prabho

translations.english: O master, from wrath I have vowed that I will, eager for encounter, O reverend one, conquer the four Lokapālas.

verses.sanskrit:
तेनैष प्रस्थितोऽहं वै पितृराजपुरं प्रति
प्राणिसंक्लेशकर्तारं योजयिष्यामि मृत्युना
verses.transliteration:
tenaiṣa prasthito'haṁ vai pitṛrājapuraṁ prati
prāṇisaṁkleśakartāraṁ yojayiṣyāmi mṛtyunā

translations.english: Then here go I to the city of the lord of the Pitſs; and I am determined to compass the death of him that visit creatures with smart.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मुनिं तमभिवाद्य च
प्रययौ दक्षिणामाशां प्रहृष्टैः सह मन्त्रिभिः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā daśagrīvo muniṁ tamabhivādya ca
prayayau dakṣiṇāmāśāṁ prahṛṣṭaiḥ saha mantribhiḥ

translations.english: Having delivered himself thus and saluted the sage, he, entering the southern way with his councillors, proceeded along.

verses.sanskrit:
नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः
चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः
verses.transliteration:
nāradastu mahātejā muhūrtaṁ dhyānamāsthitaḥ
cintayāmāsa viprendro vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ

translations.english: The exceedingly energetic Nārada best of Brāhmaṇas resembling a smokeless fire, remaining rapt for a while, began to reflect.

verses.sanskrit:
येन लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः क्लिश्यन्ते सचराचराः
क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मे च स कालो हिंस्यते कथम्
verses.transliteration:
yena lokāstrayaḥ sendrāḥ kliśyante sacarācarāḥ
kṣīṇe cāyuṣi dharme ca sa kālo hiṁsyate katham

translations.english: How can (Ravana) conquer Time who, when its life wane, righteously visit with affection the time, sphere with Indra, fraught with mobile and immobile.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः
तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रोऽसौ स्वयमेवाभिगच्छति
verses.transliteration:
yasya nityaṁ trayo lokā vidravanti bhayārditāḥ
taṁ kathaṁ rākṣasendro'sau svayamevābhigacchati

translations.english: How can this lord of Raksasas, of himself, go to him who, resembling another fire, bear to the gifts and acts (of persons), that high-souled one of whom attaining consciousness, people put forth their activity; and; afflicted with the fear of whom these three worlds fall away?

verses.sanskrit:
यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृते दुष्कृते यथा
त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं नु विजेष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yo vidhātā ca dhātā ca sukṛte duṣkṛte yathā
trailokyaṁ vijitaṁ yena taṁ kathaṁ nu vijeṣyati

translations.english: How can (Rāvana) subdue him who ordain things both great and small, who met rewards and punishments for good and bad acts, and who himself has conquered the three worlds? Resorting* to what other means shall Rāvana secure (victory)? *Explains the commentator: "Time has every thing under its control. Like the all-enclosing space, time pervades all that is. This being so, resorting what transcending Time, shall Rāvana obtain victory over it."

verses.sanskrit:
अपरं किं नु कृत्वैवं विधानं संविधास्यति
कौतूहलसमुत्पन्नो यास्यामि यमसादनम्
verses.transliteration:
aparaṁ kiṁ nu kṛtvaivaṁ vidhānaṁ saṁvidhāsyati
kautūhalasamutpanno yāsyāmi yamasādanam

translations.english: I am curious about it. To Yama's abode shall I go for witnessing the encounter between Yama and the Raksasa.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं संचिन्त्य विप्रेन्द्रो जगाम लघुविक्रमः
आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ saṁcintya viprendro jagāma laghuvikramaḥ
ākhyātuṁ tadyathāvṛttaṁ yamasya sadanaṁ prati

translations.english: Having reflected thus, that foremost of Vipras endowed with fleet vigour, bent his steps towards the abode of Yama, for the purpose of relating to him all that had taken place.

verses.sanskrit:
अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम्
विधानमुपतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम्
verses.transliteration:
apaśyatsa yamaṁ tatra devamagnipuraskṛtam
vidhānamupatiṣṭhantaṁ prāṇino yasya yādṛśam

translations.english: There he saw that god Yama sitting in front of fire and offering into it the good and evil fruits of their actions. * *Ordaining happiness and misery to the lives of people according to their acts.'

verses.sanskrit:
स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम्
अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṁ maharṣiṁ tatra nāradam
abravītsukhamāsīnamarghyamāvedya dharmataḥ

translations.english: Seeing the Maharși Nārada arrive there, Yama offering him arghya according to the ordinance, addressed him saying, when he was seated at his case:

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चित्क्षेमं नु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति
किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित
verses.transliteration:
kaccitkṣemaṁ nu devarṣe kacciddharmo na naśyati
kimāgamanakṛtyaṁ te devagandharvasevita

translations.english: 'O Devarsi, is it well with you? And does virtue deteriorate.'* And, why, O you honoured of deities, and Gandharvas, do you come?' *The Original has: "Do not virtue wane." This in English would imply the very reverse what Nārada intends to say. He says: 'Do religion deteriorate?' i.e. 'I hope, religion does not deteriorate.' This is an idiom and natural usage accounts for it, although that usage must in the nature of things be based on a subtle ground of season.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
abravīttu tadā vākyaṁ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi vidhānaṁ ca vidhīyatām

translations.english: Thereat the reverend sage, Narada, said; Hearken. I shall tell (you); and (after hearing me out) do you what is fit. o king of the Pitrs, here come the night-ranger named ten-necked, for bringing you under his sway you who are incapable of being conquered.

verses.sanskrit:
एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितोऽस्म्यागतः प्रभो
दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु करिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
etena kāraṇenāhaṁ tvarito'smyāgataḥ prabho
daṇḍapraharaṇasyādya tava kiṁ nu kariṣyati

translations.english: O master, for this reason it is that I have come hither hastily, doubtful what shall befall you who have the rod for your weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दूरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम्
ददृशे दिव्यमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
etasminnantare dūrādaṁśumantamivoditam
dadṛśe divyamāyāntaṁ vimānaṁ tasya rakṣasaḥ

translations.english: In the meanwhile they saw the Rākṣasa's car approach from afar, flaming and like to the rayfurnished (one) risen.

verses.sanskrit:
तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं समवर्तत
verses.transliteration:
taṁ deśaṁ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ
kṛtvā vitimiraṁ sarvaṁ samīpaṁ samavartata

translations.english: And dispelling the gloom of that region with the effulgence of Pușpaka; that exceedingly powerful (Raksasa) came forward.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वपश्यन्महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः
प्राणिनः सुकृतं कर्म भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tvapaśyanmahābāhurdaśagrīvastatastataḥ
prāṇinaḥ sukṛtaṁ karma bhuñjānāṁścaiva duṣkṛtam

translations.english: The mighty-armed ten-necked one all around saw creatures reaping the consequences of their fair and foul acts.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन बलीयसा
प्रेतगोपाः सुसंरब्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन्
verses.transliteration:
preteṣu mucyamāneṣu rākṣasena balīyasā
pretagopāḥ susaṁrabdhā rākṣasendramabhidravan

translations.english: On being liberated by that Rākṣasa the tennecked one, those creatures in a moment began to enjoy their release, that had come to them without thought or suspense. And on the dead being delivered by the magnanimous Rākşasa, the guards of the dead, getting enraged, rushed at the Rākşasa sovereign.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यासनानि प्रासादान्वेदिकास्तरणानि च
पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव
verses.transliteration:
tasyāsanāni prāsādānvedikāstaraṇāni ca
puṣpakasya babhañjuste śīghraṁ madhukarā iva

translations.english: And those heroes by hundreds and by thousands assailed (Puspaka) with prāsas, and bludgeons, and darts and maces, and spears and tomaras. And swiftly swarming like bees, they began to break the seats, blocks, daises and gateways (of the car.)

verses.sanskrit:
देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे
भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा
verses.transliteration:
devaniṣṭhānabhūtaṁ tadvimānaṁ puṣpakaṁ mṛdhe
bhajyamānaṁ tathaivāsīdakṣayaṁ brahmatejasā

translations.english: In that conflict Pușpaka presided over by divine energy, incapable of being destroyed by virtue of Brahma power, being broken, resumed its former shape.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्ते रावणामात्या यथाकामं यथाबलम्
अयुध्यन्त महावीर्याः स च राजा दशाननः
verses.transliteration:
tataste rāvaṇāmātyā yathākāmaṁ yathābalam
ayudhyanta mahāvīryāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ

translations.english: According to the measure of their might his (Rāvana's) councillors great heroes all, as well as the ten-faced one himself with might and main, fought with trees and crags and hundreds of blocks of buildings.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः
अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत्
verses.transliteration:
te tu śoṇitadigdhāṅgāḥ sarvaśastrasamāhatāḥ
amātyā rākṣasendrasya cakrurāyodhanaṁ mahat

translations.english: And those councillors of the lord of Räkşasas, assailed with every kind of weapons, with their persons bathed in blood, fought fiercely.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः
विमाने राक्षसश्रेष्ठः फुल्लाशोक इवाबभौ
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtaḥ
vimāne rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ phullāśoka ivābabhau

translations.english: And then pierced through and through by those weapons, with his person covered with blood, the Rākṣasa king appeared like a flowering Kinśuka in Pușpaka. * *This simile is peculiarly appropriate and beautiful. Puspaka, the name of Ravana's car, means composed of flowers; and this signification shining one arms. a askance, as it were, over the direct sense of the sentence, heightens the delight the reader feels on imagining the principal figure. "Rāvana seated in Puspaka, covered with blood, looked likeblossoming Kinsuka.'

verses.sanskrit:
स शूलानि गदाः प्रासाञ्शक्तितोमरसायकान्
मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली
verses.transliteration:
sa śūlāni gadāḥ prāsāñśaktitomarasāyakān
musalāni śilāvṛkṣānmumocāstrabalādbalī

translations.english: Thereat that powerful one, by virtue of his mastery over weapons, began to hurl darts and maces, prāsas and spears and tomaras and crags and trees.

verses.sanskrit:
तांस्तु सर्वान्समाक्षिप्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च
जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रकः
verses.transliteration:
tāṁstu sarvānsamākṣipya tadastramapahatya ca
jaghnuste rākṣasaṁ ghoramekaṁ śatasahasrakaḥ

translations.english: And snapping those weapons and resisting (those volleys of) arms, they smote at the Räkșasa fighting alone by hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit:
परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मेघोत्करा इव
भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमकारयन्
verses.transliteration:
parivārya ca taṁ sarve śailaṁ meghotkarā iva
bhindipālaiśca śūlaiśca nirucchvāsamakārayan

translations.english: And encompassing him even as clouds encompass mountain, they rendered (Ravana) inert by means of Bhindipālas and darts. And with his mail torn open, his anger raging fiercely, and covered with blood streaming over his person, he, forsaking, his car, stood upon the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स कार्मुकी बाणी पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः
लब्धसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa kārmukī bāṇī pṛthivyāṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
labdhasaṁjño muhūrtena kruddhastasthau yathāntakaḥ

translations.english: Then furnished with his bow and holding his shafts, (Ravana) regaining his senses in a short time, increased in energy and stood in the field like the finisher.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं संधाय कार्मुके
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं व्यपकर्षत
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ pāśupataṁ divyamastraṁ saṁdhāya kārmuke
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tānuktvā taccāpaṁ vyapakarṣata

translations.english: Now fixing the divine Pāśupata on his bow, and saying to them, 'stay! stay!' he drew that bow.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे
मुक्तो गुल्मान्द्रुमांश्चैव भस्मकृत्वा प्रधावति
verses.transliteration:
jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe
mukto gulmāndrumāṁścaiva bhasmakṛtvā pradhāvati

translations.english: And garlanded with glory that shaft followed byghosts,* in that encounter; rushed on, burning to ashes the loose bushes and trees lying in its way. *The instrument being Siva's, it naturally was followed by ghosts as his attendants.

verses.sanskrit:
ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु
रणे तस्मिन्निपतिता दावदग्धा नगा इव
verses.transliteration:
te tasya tejasā dagdhāḥ sainyā vaivasvatasya tu
raṇe tasminnipatitā dāvadagdhā nagā iva

translations.english: And burnt up by its energy, the most of Vaivasvata fell down in the field like to banners of Mahendra.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः
ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ sa sacivaiḥ sārdhaṁ rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ
nanāda sumahānādaṁ kampayanniva medinīm

translations.english: Thereat the Räksasa of terrific prowess along with his councillors began to set up tremendous shouts; as if making the earth tremble.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तस्य महानादं श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतो यमः
शत्रुं विजयिनं मेने स्वबलस्य च संक्षयम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tasya mahānādaṁ śrutvā vaivasvato yamaḥ
śatruṁ vijayinaṁ mene svabalasya ca saṁkṣayam

translations.english: Hearing his mighty-shouts, that lord Vaivasvata knew that his adversary had gained the day and that his own host had been destroyed.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु योधान्हतान्मत्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणः
अब्रवीत्त्वरितं सूतं रथः समुपनीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
sa tu yodhānhatānmatvā krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
abravīttvaritaṁ sūtaṁ rathaḥ samupanīyatām

translations.english: Knowing that his forces had been slain, he, with his eyes crimsoned with passion hastily spoke to his charioteer, ‘Bring you my car.'

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य सूतो रथं दिव्यमुपस्थाप्य महास्वनम्
स्थितः स च महातेजा आरुरोह महारथम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya sūto rathaṁ divyamupasthāpya mahāsvanam
sthitaḥ sa ca mahātejā āruroha mahāratham

translations.english: Thereat the charioteer brought the noble and mighty car and stood (there) and then that exceeding energetic one mounted the car.

verses.sanskrit:
पाशमुद्गरहस्तश्च मृत्युस्तस्याग्रतो स्थितः
येन संक्षिप्यते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्
verses.transliteration:
pāśamudgarahastaśca mṛtyustasyāgrato sthitaḥ
yena saṁkṣipyate sarvaṁ trailokyaṁ sacarācaram

translations.english: In front (of his car) stood death, equipped with prāsas and maces in his hands, who makes nothing of this entire triune world; incapable of deterioration.

verses.sanskrit:
कालदण्डश्च पार्श्वस्थो मूर्तिमान्स्यन्दने स्थितः
यमप्रहरणं दिव्यं प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
kāladaṇḍaśca pārśvastho mūrtimānsyandane sthitaḥ
yamapraharaṇaṁ divyaṁ prajvalanniva tejasā

translations.english: And beside (him) was the rod of Kāla in its native from the divine instrument of Yama like to a flaming fire on account of its own energy.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो लोकास्त्रयस्त्रस्ताः कम्पन्ते च दिवौकसः
कालं क्रुद्धं तदा दृष्ट्वा लोकत्रयभयावहम्
verses.transliteration:
tato lokāstrayastrastāḥ kampante ca divaukasaḥ
kālaṁ kruddhaṁ tadā dṛṣṭvā lokatrayabhayāvaham
