स्वास्तीर्णं राजभवनात्सीतायाश्चासनं शुभम्
verses.transliteration:
sārathe turagāñśīghraṁ yojayasva rathottame
svāstīrṇaṁ rājabhavanātsītāyāścāsanaṁ śubham

translations.english: O charioteer, do you soon yoke quick coursing steeds to an excellent chariot, and for Sītā place an excellent seat on the car. At the command of the King, I shall take Sītā to the hermitage of the ascetics ever engaged in pious actions. Do you soon bring the chariot here.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः
रथं सुरुचिरप्रख्यं स्वास्तीर्णं सुखशय्यया
verses.transliteration:
sumantrastu tathetyuktvā yuktaṁ paramavājibhiḥ
rathaṁ suruciraprakhyaṁ svāstīrṇaṁ sukhaśayyayā

translations.english: Obeying the mandate, and bringing a beautiful and holy car drawn by first-rate steeds and having excellent seats, he said to Saumitri, the enhancer of friends' honour “O lord, here is the chariot ready-do you now satisfy your desire.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तः सुमन्त्रेण राजवेश्म स लक्ष्मणः
प्रविश्य सीतामासाद्य व्याजहार नरर्षभः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktaḥ sumantreṇa rājaveśma sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
praviśya sītāmāsādya vyājahāra nararṣabhaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of Sumantra, Laksmana, the foremost of men, approached Sītā in the inner apartment and said.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे गमनं चाभ्यरोचयत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktā tu vaidehī lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe gamanaṁ cābhyarocayat

translations.english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Lakşmaņa, Janaki attained to excessive delight and became anxious to go.

verses.sanskrit:
वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च
गृहीत्वा तानि वैदेही गमनायोपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
vāsāṁsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
gṛhītvā tāni vaidehī gamanāyopacakrame

translations.english: Taking various jewels and costly clothes she said to Lakşmaņa, on the eve of her departure “I shall confer these ornaments, these costly clothes and riches on the female ascetics."

verses.sanskrit:
इमानि मुनिपत्नीनां दास्याम्याभरणान्यहम्
सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा रथमारोप्य मैथिलीम्
प्रययौ शीघ्रतुरगो रामस्याज्ञामनुस्मरन्
verses.transliteration:
imāni munipatnīnāṁ dāsyāmyābharaṇānyaham
saumitristu tathetyuktvā rathamāropya maithilīm
prayayau śīghraturago rāmasyājñāmanusmaran

translations.english: Saying 'we shall do the same' he made Sītā ascend the car and remembering Rāma's command proceeded, being carried by quickcoursing steeds.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च तदा सीता लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्
अशुभानि बहून्यद्य पश्यामि रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca tadā sītā lakṣmaṇaṁ lakṣmivardhanam
aśubhāni bahūnyadya paśyāmi raghunandana

translations.english: Thereupon Sītā said to Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of prosperity:-:0 descendant of Raghu, I behold many inauspicious omens. My right eye and body are trembling.

verses.sanskrit:
नयनं मे स्फुरत्यद्य गात्रोत्कम्पश्च जायते
हृदयं चैव सौमित्रे अस्वस्थमिव लक्षये
verses.transliteration:
nayanaṁ me sphuratyadya gātrotkampaśca jāyate
hṛdayaṁ caiva saumitre asvasthamiva lakṣaye

translations.english: My mind is growing depressed. It is stricken with anxiety and I have accordingly grown restless.

verses.sanskrit:
औत्सुक्यं परमं चापि अधृतिश्च परा मम
शून्यामिव च पश्यामि पृथिवीं पृथुलोचन
verses.transliteration:
autsukyaṁ paramaṁ cāpi adhṛtiśca parā mama
śūnyāmiva ca paśyāmi pṛthivīṁ pṛthulocana

translations.english: I behold the earth as void of all happiness. O you fond of brothers— has your brother met with any calamity?

verses.sanskrit:
पुरे जनपदे चैव कुशलं प्राणिनामपि
इत्यञ्जलिकृता सीता देवता अभ्ययाचत
verses.transliteration:
pure janapade caiva kuśalaṁ prāṇināmapi
ityañjalikṛtā sītā devatā abhyayācata

translations.english: Are all my mothers-in-law and subjects well?

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वासमुपागम्य गोमतीतीर आश्रमे
प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय सौमित्रिः सूतमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tato vāsamupāgamya gomatītīra āśrame
prabhāte punarutthāya saumitriḥ sūtamabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon having arrived at the hermitage situate on the banks of Gomati Lakşmaņa spent the night there. Thereupon at dawn he rose up and asked the charioteer to get the chariot ready, saying, “Like to the powerful Mahādeva we shall hold the waters of the Bhāgirathi on our head.”

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽश्वान्विचारयित्वाशु रथे युक्त्वा मनोजवान्
आरोहस्वेति वैदेहीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
so'śvānvicārayitvāśu rathe yuktvā manojavān
ārohasveti vaidehīṁ sūtaḥ prāñjalirabravīt

translations.english: Thereupon Sumantra yoked the horses, gifted with the fleet course of the mind, to the chariot and with folded hands said to Sītā “Do you ascend the car."

verses.sanskrit:
सा तु सूतस्य वचनादारुरोह रथोत्तमम्
सीता सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सुमन्त्रेण च धीमता
verses.transliteration:
sā tu sūtasya vacanādāruroha rathottamam
sītā saumitriṇā sārdhaṁ sumantreṇa ca dhīmatā

translations.english: According to the request of the intelligent charioteer, Sītā, with Lakşmaņa, ascended that excellent conveyance. In no time the daughter of Janaka, having expansive eyes, arrived at the banks of the Gangā removing all sins.

verses.sanskrit:
अथार्धदिवसं गत्वा भागीरथ्या जलाशयम्
निरीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणो दीनः प्ररुरोद महास्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
athārdhadivasaṁ gatvā bhāgīrathyā jalāśayam
nirīkṣya lakṣmaṇo dīnaḥ praruroda mahāsvanam

translations.english: Reaching the currents of Bhāgirathi before noon Laksmana, on beholding her, cried aloud.

verses.sanskrit:
सीता तु परमायत्ता दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमातुरम्
उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञ किमिदं रुद्यते त्वया
verses.transliteration:
sītā tu paramāyattā dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamāturam
uvāca vākyaṁ dharmajña kimidaṁ rudyate tvayā

translations.english: Thereupon beholding Lakşmaņa thus distressed, Sītā, conversant with piety, waxing are anxious said. “Why you weeping, Lakşmaņa? I have reached the banks of Jāhnavī, for which I have so long desired. So this is the time for rejoicing and do not give me pain at this time.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यं त्वं रामपादेषु वर्तसे पुरुषर्षभ
कच्चिद्विनाकृतस्तेन द्विरात्रे शोकमागतः
verses.transliteration:
nityaṁ tvaṁ rāmapādeṣu vartase puruṣarṣabha
kaccidvinākṛtastena dvirātre śokamāgataḥ

translations.english: O foremost of men, you do spend your days and nights in the company of Rama. You have left him for two days only, are you sorry for this?

verses.sanskrit:
ममापि दयितो रामो जीवितेनापि लक्ष्मण
न चाहमेवं शोचामि मैवं त्वं बालिशो भव
verses.transliteration:
mamāpi dayito rāmo jīvitenāpi lakṣmaṇa
na cāhamevaṁ śocāmi maivaṁ tvaṁ bāliśo bhava

translations.english: O Lakşmaņa! Rāma is also dearer than my life, but I am not so sorry— do you not be therefore overwhelmed with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
तारयस्व च मां गङ्गां दर्शयस्व च तापसान्
ततो धनानि वासांसि दास्याम्याभरणानि च
verses.transliteration:
tārayasva ca māṁ gaṅgāṁ darśayasva ca tāpasān
tato dhanāni vāsāṁsi dāsyāmyābharaṇāni ca

translations.english: Do you take me to the other side of the Gangā so that I may behold the ascetics and other confer upon them clothes and ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कृत्वा महर्षीणां यथार्हमभिवादनम्
तत्र चैकां निशामुष्य यास्यामस्तां पुरीं पुनः
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kṛtvā maharṣīṇāṁ yathārhamabhivādanam
tatra caikāṁ niśāmuṣya yāsyāmastāṁ purīṁ punaḥ

translations.english: Having paid them due salutation to the ascetics, and spending a night we shall return to the capital.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रमृज्य नयने शुभे
तितीर्षुर्लक्ष्मणो गङ्गां शुभां नावमुपाहरत्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāstadvacanaṁ śrutvā pramṛjya nayane śubhe
titīrṣurlakṣmaṇo gaṅgāṁ śubhāṁ nāvamupāharat

translations.english: Hearing the words of Sītā and wiping his beautiful eyes, Laksmana, the slayer of enemies, sent for boatmen. As soon as they were called, with folded hands they said. “The boat is ready."

verses.sanskrit:
अथ नावं सुविस्तीर्णां नैषादीं राघवानुजः
आरुरोह समायुक्तां पूर्वमारोप्य मैथिलीम्
verses.transliteration:
atha nāvaṁ suvistīrṇāṁ naiṣādīṁ rāghavānujaḥ
āruroha samāyuktāṁ pūrvamāropya maithilīm

translations.english: Having at first conducted Sītā to the spacious and well decorated boat plied by fishermen Laksmana himself got up.

verses.sanskrit:
सुमन्त्रं चैव सरथं स्थीयतामिति लक्ष्मणः
उवाच शोकसंतप्तः प्रयाहीति च नाविकम्
verses.transliteration:
sumantraṁ caiva sarathaṁ sthīyatāmiti lakṣmaṇaḥ
uvāca śokasaṁtaptaḥ prayāhīti ca nāvikam

translations.english: Thereupon he ordered Sumantra to wait there with the chariot, and being beside himself with sorrow ordered the sailors to move on.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तीरमुपागम्य भागीरथ्याः स लक्ष्मणः
उवाच मैथिलीं वाक्यं प्राञ्जलिर्बाष्पगद्गदः
verses.transliteration:
tatastīramupāgamya bhāgīrathyāḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
uvāca maithilīṁ vākyaṁ prāñjalirbāṣpagadgadaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon having reached the other side of Bhāgirathi, Lakşmaņa, with subdued voice and folded palms, said to Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
हृद्गतं मे महच्छल्यं यदस्म्यार्येण धीमता
अस्मिन्निमित्ते वैदेहि लोकस्य वचनीकृतः
verses.transliteration:
hṛdgataṁ me mahacchalyaṁ yadasmyāryeṇa dhīmatā
asminnimitte vaidehi lokasya vacanīkṛtaḥ

translations.english: O daughter of the king of Videha, this has pierced my heart like a dart, that my brother, by making me the instrumental of this action has made me the object of censure in the world.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयो हि मरणं मेऽद्य मृत्योर्वा यत्परं भवेत्
न चास्मिन्नीदृशे कार्ये नियोज्यो लोकनिन्दिते
verses.transliteration:
śreyo hi maraṇaṁ me'dya mṛtyorvā yatparaṁ bhavet
na cāsminnīdṛśe kārye niyojyo lokanindite

translations.english: The death and the pain consequent upon it are better than the action I am engaged in.

verses.sanskrit:
वैदेह्या चोद्यमानस्तु लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः
अवाङ्मुखो बाष्पगलो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
vaidehyā codyamānastu lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ
avāṅmukho bāṣpagalo vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Sītā having addressed him thus, Lakşmaņa with a poorly heart and suppressed tone, said thus.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा परिषदो मध्ये अपवादं सुदारुणम्
पुरे जनपदे चैव त्वत्कृते जनकात्मजे
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā pariṣado madhye apavādaṁ sudāruṇam
pure janapade caiva tvatkṛte janakātmaje

translations.english: O worshipful queen! I have kept within my heart all those words, which the king said, before he entered his palace, rendered sorry and impatient on hearing in the assembly the report of censure regarding you, O daughter of king Janaka. All those words are indeed above description and so I desist.

verses.sanskrit:
सा त्वं त्यक्ता नृपतिना निर्दोषा मम संनिधौ
पौरापवादभीतेन ग्राह्यं देवि न तेऽन्यथा
verses.transliteration:
sā tvaṁ tyaktā nṛpatinā nirdoṣā mama saṁnidhau
paurāpavādabhītena grāhyaṁ devi na te'nyathā

translations.english: I only say so much, that afraid of the calumny of the citizens he has renounced you although your purity was sufficiently proved before me. But for that, do not consider yourself in any way guilty. Rāma has commanded me to leave you near the hermitage on the pretext of satisfying your desire as you are big with a child.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञो दशरथस्यैष पितुर्मे मुनिपुंगवः
सखा परमको विप्रो वाल्मीकिः सुमहायशाः
verses.transliteration:
rājño daśarathasyaiṣa piturme munipuṁgavaḥ
sakhā paramako vipro vālmīkiḥ sumahāyaśāḥ

translations.english: Do not uselessly give vent to sorrow any more. There is the holy and beautiful hermitage of the saints on the banks of Jähnavī. There lives Vālmīki, the foremost of saints, a great friend of our sire Dasaratha. O daughter of Janaka, approaching that high-souled saint, do you spend your days happily keeping Rāma always in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
पतिव्रतात्वमास्थाय रामं कृत्वा सदा हृदि
श्रेयस्ते परमं देवि तथा कृत्वा भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
pativratātvamāsthāya rāmaṁ kṛtvā sadā hṛdi
śreyaste paramaṁ devi tathā kṛtvā bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Do you satisfy the deities, O chaste damsel. This shall crown you with auspiciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दारुणं जनकात्मजा
परं विषादमागम्य वैदेही निपपात ह
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dāruṇaṁ janakātmajā
paraṁ viṣādamāgamya vaidehī nipapāta ha

translations.english: Hearing the ruthless words of Laksmana, the daughter of Janaka, greatly sorry, fell down on earth.

verses.sanskrit:
सा मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञा बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणा
लक्ष्मणं दीनया वाचा उवाच जनकात्मजा
verses.transliteration:
sā muhūrtamivāsaṁjñā bāṣpavyākulitekṣaṇā
lakṣmaṇaṁ dīnayā vācā uvāca janakātmajā

translations.english: And remaining senseless for some time, Sītā, with her eyes full of tears said to Lakşmaņa.

verses.sanskrit:
मामिकेयं तनुर्नूनं सृष्टा दुःखाय लक्ष्मण
धात्रा यस्यास्तथा मेऽद्य दुःखमूर्तिः प्रदृश्यते
verses.transliteration:
māmikeyaṁ tanurnūnaṁ sṛṣṭā duḥkhāya lakṣmaṇa
dhātrā yasyāstathā me'dya duḥkhamūrtiḥ pradṛśyate

translations.english: Forsooth, O Laksmana, the great Dispenser has created this body to suffer miseries, and all my affections are manifest in form today.

verses.sanskrit:
किं नु पापं कृतं पूर्वं को वा दारैर्वियोजितः
याहं शुद्धसमाचारा त्यक्ता नृपतिना सती
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ nu pāpaṁ kṛtaṁ pūrvaṁ ko vā dārairviyojitaḥ
yāhaṁ śuddhasamācārā tyaktā nṛpatinā satī

translations.english: Methinks, I committed a mighty iniquity in my pristine existence or brought about me albeit I am pure and chaste.

verses.sanskrit:
पुराहमाश्रमे वासं रामपादानुवर्तिनी
अनुरुध्यापि सौमित्रे दुःखे विपरिवर्तिनी
verses.transliteration:
purāhamāśrame vāsaṁ rāmapādānuvartinī
anurudhyāpi saumitre duḥkhe viparivartinī

translations.english: O son of Sumitrā, the affliction of residing in the forest appeared to me as pleasure ere this for I knew that I would be able to serve Rāma's feet.

verses.sanskrit:
सा कथं ह्याश्रमे सौम्य वत्स्यामि विजनीकृता
आख्यास्यामि च कस्याहं दुःखं दुःखपरायणा
verses.transliteration:
sā kathaṁ hyāśrame saumya vatsyāmi vijanīkṛtā
ākhyāsyāmi ca kasyāhaṁ duḥkhaṁ duḥkhaparāyaṇā

translations.english: But how shall I, O gentle one, live in the hermitage being divorced from all my kith and kin? and being afflicted to whom shall I express my sorrow?

verses.sanskrit:
किं च वक्ष्यामि मुनिषु किं मयापकृतं नृपे
कस्मिन्वा कारणे त्यक्ता राघवेण महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ ca vakṣyāmi muniṣu kiṁ mayāpakṛtaṁ nṛpe
kasminvā kāraṇe tyaktā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā

translations.english: What reply shall I offer to the ascetics when they shall ask me "Child, why has the highsouled Rāghava renounced you? What sin have you committed?"

verses.sanskrit:
न खल्वद्यैव सौमित्रे जीवितं जाह्नवीजले
त्यजेयं राजवंशस्तु भर्तुर्मे परिहास्यते
verses.transliteration:
na khalvadyaiva saumitre jīvitaṁ jāhnavījale
tyajeyaṁ rājavaṁśastu bharturme parihāsyate

translations.english: O Saumitri, I shall just renounce my life in the waters of Jāhnavi? But I desist from this for it shall bring about the termination O my husband's race.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाज्ञां कुरु सौमित्रे त्यज मां दुःखभागिनीम्
निदेशे स्थीयतां राज्ञः शृणु चेदं वचो मम
verses.transliteration:
yathājñāṁ kuru saumitre tyaja māṁ duḥkhabhāginīm
nideśe sthīyatāṁ rājñaḥ śṛṇu cedaṁ vaco mama

translations.english: O Saumitri, do you carry out the orders you have received. By renouncing this wretched wight do you satisfy the King's orders. But hear, what I say.

verses.sanskrit:
श्वश्रूणामविशेषेण प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहेण च
शिरसा वन्द्य चरणौ कुशलं ब्रूहि पार्थिवम्
verses.transliteration:
śvaśrūṇāmaviśeṣeṇa prāñjaliḥ pragraheṇa ca
śirasā vandya caraṇau kuśalaṁ brūhi pārthivam

translations.english: Without making any distinction, do you, in my name, with folded hands, bow to my mothers-in-law and then ask the well-being of the kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा भ्रातृषु वर्तेथास्तथा पौरेषु नित्यदा
परमो ह्येष धर्मः स्यादेषा कीर्तिरनुत्तमा
verses.transliteration:
yathā bhrātṛṣu vartethāstathā paureṣu nityadā
paramo hyeṣa dharmaḥ syādeṣā kīrtiranuttamā

translations.english: Do you tell further-more that king established in righteousness to treat the citizens as his brothers, to acquire piety by protecting his subjects duly for this is the greatest mortality and by this may be acquired excellent fame,

verses.sanskrit:
यत्त्वं पौरजनं राजन्धर्मेण समवाप्नुयाः
अहं तु नानुशोचामि स्वशरीरं नरर्षभ
यथापवादं पौराणां तथैव रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
yattvaṁ paurajanaṁ rājandharmeṇa samavāpnuyāḥ
ahaṁ tu nānuśocāmi svaśarīraṁ nararṣabha
yathāpavādaṁ paurāṇāṁ tathaiva raghunandana

translations.english: Tell him that I am not sorry for my person-my greatest sorrow is that the citizens have vilified me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ब्रुवन्त्यां सीतायां लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः
शिरसा धरणीं गत्वा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ bruvantyāṁ sītāyāṁ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ
śirasā dharaṇīṁ gatvā vyāhartuṁ na śaśāka ha

translations.english: Sita having said this, Laksmana, with a bewildered heart, saluted her touching the ground which his head. He could not speak more.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रदक्षिणं च कृत्वा स रुदन्नेव महास्वनम्
आरुरोह पुनर्नावं नाविकं चाभ्यचोदयत्
verses.transliteration:
pradakṣiṇaṁ ca kṛtvā sa rudanneva mahāsvanam
āruroha punarnāvaṁ nāvikaṁ cābhyacodayat

translations.english: Having addressed Sītā in this wise Lakşmaņa again sent for a boat and ascending it ordered the boatman to go.

verses.sanskrit:
स गत्वा चोत्तरं कूलं शोकभारसमन्वितः
संमूढ इव दुःखेन रथमध्यारुहद्द्रुतम्
verses.transliteration:
sa gatvā cottaraṁ kūlaṁ śokabhārasamanvitaḥ
saṁmūḍha iva duḥkhena rathamadhyāruhaddrutam

translations.english: Thereupon having reached the other side and being beside himself with sorrow and grief he speedily ascended the car.

verses.sanskrit:
दूरस्थं रथमालोक्य लक्ष्मणं च मुहुर्मुहुः
निरीक्षमाणामुद्विग्नां सीतां शोकः समाविशत्
verses.transliteration:
dūrasthaṁ rathamālokya lakṣmaṇaṁ ca muhurmuhuḥ
nirīkṣamāṇāmudvignāṁ sītāṁ śokaḥ samāviśat

translations.english: And casting his looks behind behind while proceeding he espied that Sītā, on the other side of the Gangă, was rowing wildly like one having none to look after her. Looking again and again when Sītā saw that Lakşmaņa and the chariot have gone beyond the range of her vision, she became overwhelmed with anxiety and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
सा दुःखभारावनता तपस्विनी; यशोधरा नाथमपश्यती सती
रुरोद सा बर्हिणनादिते वने; महास्वनं दुःखपरायणा सती
verses.transliteration:
sā duḥkhabhārāvanatā tapasvinī; yaśodharā nāthamapaśyatī satī
ruroda sā barhiṇanādite vane; mahāsvanaṁ duḥkhaparāyaṇā satī

translations.english: Being sunk in grief and pressed down with the weight of sorrow on not beholding Rāma, the foremost of the illustrious, the chaste Şītā began to cry aloud in the forest resounded with the notes of peacocks.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिवाद्य मुनेः पादौ मुनिपुत्रा महर्षये
सर्वे निवेदयामासुस्तस्यास्तु रुदितस्वनम्
verses.transliteration:
abhivādya muneḥ pādau muniputrā maharṣaye
sarve nivedayāmāsustasyāstu ruditasvanam

translations.english: Beholding Sītā thus wailing, the sons of the Rşis there speedily approached the great Vālmīki, well-established in asceticism. And saluting him they all communicated to him Sītā's bewailing and said.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वा भगवन्कस्याप्येषा महात्मनः
पत्नी श्रीरिव संमोहाद्विरौति विकृतस्वरा
verses.transliteration:
adṛṣṭapūrvā bhagavankasyāpyeṣā mahātmanaḥ
patnī śrīriva saṁmohādvirauti vikṛtasvarā

translations.english: O great Rşi, we do not know the wife of what great man, beautiful like the very Lakşmī, and not seen before, is crying aloud very poorly?

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्साधु पश्येमां देवतामिव खाच्च्युताम्
न ह्येनां मानुषीं विद्मः सत्क्रियास्याः प्रयुज्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavansādhu paśyemāṁ devatāmiva khāccyutām
na hyenāṁ mānuṣīṁ vidmaḥ satkriyāsyāḥ prayujyatām

translations.english: It is better that you should see her once. That beautiful damsel, like a goddess failing from heaven being bewildered, is waiting on the banks of the river.

verses.sanskrit:
तां सीतां शोकभारार्तां वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुंगवः
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं ह्लादयन्निव तेजसा
verses.transliteration:
tāṁ sītāṁ śokabhārārtāṁ vālmīkirmunipuṁgavaḥ
uvāca madhurāṁ vāṇīṁ hlādayanniva tejasā

translations.english: Having gladdened a little the aggrieved Sītā by virtue of his own effulgence of the great ascetic Vālmīki addressed her in following sweet ascents. She did not appear to us to be a woman. Do you receive her duly. She is near the hermitage and so has come to seek your shelter.

verses.sanskrit:
स्नुषा दशरथस्य त्वं रामस्य महिषी सती
जनकस्य सुता राज्ञः स्वागतं ते पतिव्रते
verses.transliteration:
snuṣā daśarathasya tvaṁ rāmasya mahiṣī satī
janakasya sutā rājñaḥ svāgataṁ te pativrate

translations.english: O chaste damsel, you at the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, the beloved wife of Rāma and the daughter of Janaka; your coming here is auspicious. O illustrious Sir, she is on the look out for a protector-do you protect her.” The pious Vālmīki could perceive everything by virtue of his asceticism: and ascertaining the truth of the words of the Rși boys by the power of his understanding, he, with quick steps, approached Sita.

verses.sanskrit:
आयान्त्येवासि विज्ञाता मया धर्मसमाधिना
कारणं चैव सर्वं मे हृदयेनोपलक्षितम्
verses.transliteration:
āyāntyevāsi vijñātā mayā dharmasamādhinā
kāraṇaṁ caiva sarvaṁ me hṛdayenopalakṣitam

translations.english: I am apprised, by virtue of asceticism and meditation, of the object of your coming here. O great lady, I am also fully aware that you are by all means chaste. In fact I am conscious of all the incidents in the three worlds. And the disciple followed that high-minded ascetic. Thereupon proceeding a little on foot with Arghya in his hands, the wise Vālmiki reached the banks of the river and saw that Rāghava's spouse was bewailing like a helpless woman.

verses.sanskrit:
अपापां वेद्मि सीते त्वां तपोलब्धेन चक्षुषा
विशुद्धभावा वैदेहि साम्प्रतं मयि वर्तसे
verses.transliteration:
apāpāṁ vedmi sīte tvāṁ tapolabdhena cakṣuṣā
viśuddhabhāvā vaidehi sāmprataṁ mayi vartase

translations.english: By the eyes of asceticism, I perceive, O daughter of Janaka, that you are innocent. You have come under my shelter, O Vaidehi-to be you consoled.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्रमस्याविदूरे मे तापस्यस्तपसि स्थिताः
तास्त्वां वत्से यथा वत्सं पालयिष्यन्ति नित्यशः
verses.transliteration:
āśramasyāvidūre me tāpasyastapasi sthitāḥ
tāstvāṁ vatse yathā vatsaṁ pālayiṣyanti nityaśaḥ

translations.english: O child, the pious ascetics live around my hermitage. They shall daily take care of you as their daughter.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं सीता मुनेः परममद्भुतम्
शिरसा वन्द्य चरणौ तथेत्याह कृताञ्जलिः
verses.transliteration:
śrutvā tu bhāṣitaṁ sītā muneḥ paramamadbhutam
śirasā vandya caraṇau tathetyāha kṛtāñjaliḥ

translations.english: Do you accept this Arghya now, and confiding in me do you remove your grief. Be not sorry for anything; consider that you have come to your own home. Hearing the wonderful words of the great ascetic, Sītā humbly touched his feet and said Your desire shall be fulfilled.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वागतं ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ चिरस्यागमनं प्रभो
अभिवादयामः सर्वास्त्वामुच्यतां किं च कुर्महे
verses.transliteration:
svāgataṁ te muniśreṣṭha cirasyāgamanaṁ prabho
abhivādayāmaḥ sarvāstvāmucyatāṁ kiṁ ca kurmahe

translations.english: Saying this, She with folded hands, followed the ascetic. Beholding the great ascetic and Sītā approach, the wives, of the Rsis, delighted neared them and said. “Do you come, O foremost of Rșis, you have arrived here after a long time. We all bow to you-do you order what we shall do."

verses.sanskrit:
तासां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिरिदमब्रवीत्
सीतेयं समनुप्राप्ता पत्नी रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
tāsāṁ tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vālmīkiridamabravīt
sīteyaṁ samanuprāptā patnī rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Hearing their words the great Vālmīki replied in worthy accents-"This Sītā is the wife of the intelligent Rāma, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha and the daughter of Janaka. She has now come to our hermitage. She is chaste and innocent, still her husband has renounced her. So we should all protect her.

verses.sanskrit:
इमां भवत्यः पश्यन्तु स्नेहेन परमेण ह
गौरवान्मम वाक्यस्य पूज्या वोऽस्तु विशेषतः
verses.transliteration:
imāṁ bhavatyaḥ paśyantu snehena parameṇa ha
gauravānmama vākyasya pūjyā vo'stu viśeṣataḥ

translations.english: She is worthy of your reverence specially while such is order of mine-your preceptor. So. do you all, take care of her with great affection.

verses.sanskrit:
मुहुर्मुहुश्च वैदेहीं परिसान्त्व्य महायशाः
स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः पुनरायान्महातपाः
verses.transliteration:
muhurmuhuśca vaidehīṁ parisāntvya mahāyaśāḥ
svamāśramaṁ śiṣyavṛtaḥ punarāyānmahātapāḥ

translations.english: Having consigned the charge of Sītā to the hands of the female ascetics, the great and illustrious ascetic Vālmīki, followed by his disciples, speedily proceeded towards his holy hermitage.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तु मैथिलीं सीतामाश्रमं संप्रवेशिताम्
संतापमकरोद्घोरं लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः
verses.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā tu maithilīṁ sītāmāśramaṁ saṁpraveśitām
saṁtāpamakarodghoraṁ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ

translations.english: Beholding the great ascetic Vālmīki thus conducting Sītā into his own hermitage Lakş mana's heart was bewildered with grief.

verses.sanskrit:
अब्रवीच्च महातेजाः सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रसारथिम्
सीतासंतापजं दुःखं पश्य रामस्य धीमतः
verses.transliteration:
abravīcca mahātejāḥ sumantraṁ mantrasārathim
sītāsaṁtāpajaṁ duḥkhaṁ paśya rāmasya dhīmataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon he said to the expert charioteer Sumantra. Do you perceive Rāma's grief consequent upon the separation from Sītā.

verses.sanskrit:
अतो दुःखतरं किं नु राघवस्य भविष्यति
पत्नीं शुद्धसमाचारां विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम्
verses.transliteration:
ato duḥkhataraṁ kiṁ nu rāghavasya bhaviṣyati
patnīṁ śuddhasamācārāṁ visṛjya janakātmajām

translations.english: His spouse-the daughter of Janaka, is perfectly pure; what can be more painful than that Rāma is living alone having renounced her?

verses.sanskrit:
व्यक्तं दैवादहं मन्ये राघवस्य विनाभवम्
वैदेह्या सारथे सार्धं दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
vyaktaṁ daivādahaṁ manye rāghavasya vinābhavam
vaidehyā sārathe sārdhaṁ daivaṁ hi duratikramam

translations.english: It is clear to me, O Sumantra, that this separation of Rāma, has been brought about by the influence of destiny-for it is hard to get over accident.

verses.sanskrit:
यो हि देवान्सगन्धर्वानसुरान्सह राक्षसैः
निहन्याद्राघवः क्रुद्धः स दैवमनुवर्तते
verses.transliteration:
yo hi devānsagandharvānasurānsaha rākṣasaiḥ
nihanyādrāghavaḥ kruddhaḥ sa daivamanuvartate

translations.english: Even that Rāma, who, when enraged, is capable of slaying the celestials, Gandharvas, Asuras and Rākşasas, has been engaged in the worship of destiny.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा मम पितुर्वाक्यैर्दण्डके विजने वने
उषितो नव वर्षाणि पञ्च चैव सुदारुणे
verses.transliteration:
purā mama piturvākyairdaṇḍake vijane vane
uṣito nava varṣāṇi pañca caiva sudāruṇe

translations.english: Formerly did Rāma go through miserics, residing in the forest of Dandaka, at the command of his sire for fourteen years.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो दुःखतरं भूयः सीताया विप्रवासनम्
पौराणां वचनं श्रुत्वा नृशंसं प्रतिभाति मे
verses.transliteration:
tato duḥkhataraṁ bhūyaḥ sītāyā vipravāsanam
paurāṇāṁ vacanaṁ śrutvā nṛśaṁsaṁ pratibhāti me

translations.english: But this banishment of Sītā appears to me as exceedingly painful and most ruthless. O charioteer, the opinion of the citizens is by no means just; consequently what shall we gain by performing such a bad action for fame as the exile of Sita?

verses.sanskrit:
एता बहुविधा वाचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणभाषिताः
सुमन्त्रः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
etā bahuvidhā vācaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇabhāṣitāḥ
sumantraḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing those words of Lakşmaņa of various types, the wise Sumantra reverentially replied.

verses.sanskrit:
न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः सौमित्रे मैथिलीं प्रति
दृष्टमेतत्पुरा विप्रैः पितुस्ते लक्ष्मणाग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
na saṁtāpastvayā kāryaḥ saumitre maithilīṁ prati
dṛṣṭametatpurā vipraiḥ pituste lakṣmaṇāgrataḥ

translations.english: Be not aggrieved for Sītā, O Saumitri Formerly in the presence of your sire the Brāhmaṇas related this account of Sītā's exile.

verses.sanskrit:
भविष्यति दृढं रामो दुःखप्रायोऽल्पसौख्यवान्
त्वां चैव मैथिलीं चैव शत्रुघ्नभरतौ तथा
संत्यजिष्यति धर्मात्मा कालेन महता महान्
verses.transliteration:
bhaviṣyati dṛḍhaṁ rāmo duḥkhaprāyo'lpasaukhyavān
tvāṁ caiva maithilīṁ caiva śatrughnabharatau tathā
saṁtyajiṣyati dharmātmā kālena mahatā mahān

translations.english: Rāma shall be deprived of all happiness and be separated from his dear wife; what more, the virtuous-souled Rāma, having long arms, shall, under the influence of time, renounce you, Sītā, Śatrughna and Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्विदं त्वयि वक्तव्यं सौमित्रे भरतेऽपि वा
राज्ञा वोऽव्याहृतं वाक्यं दुर्वासा यदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
na tvidaṁ tvayi vaktavyaṁ saumitre bharate'pi vā
rājñā vo'vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ durvāsā yaduvāca ha

translations.english: O Lakṣmaṇa, when Durvāsa was addressed by the king Dasaratha as to your future he replied in the above way. I have told you the same. Do you not communicate this to Śatrughna Bharata or any body. O foremost of men, Durbasa said this to Daſaratha before me, Vaşistha and other great men.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋषेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा मामाह पुरुषर्षभः
सूत न क्वचिदेवं ते वक्तव्यं जनसंनिधौ
verses.transliteration:
ṛṣestu vacanaṁ śrutvā māmāha puruṣarṣabhaḥ
sūta na kvacidevaṁ te vaktavyaṁ janasaṁnidhau

translations.english: Hearing the words of Rsi, Dasaratha, the foremost of men, said to me, "O charioteer, do not reveal this secret to any body.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याहं लोकपालस्य वाक्यं तत्सुसमाहितः
नैव जात्वनृतं कुर्यामिति मे सौम्य दर्शनम्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāhaṁ lokapālasya vākyaṁ tatsusamāhitaḥ
naiva jātvanṛtaṁ kuryāmiti me saumya darśanam

translations.english: O gentle one, it is not proper by any means to falsify the words of the king Dasaratha. I shall always, very carefully, carry out his orders. It is not proper to reveal this mystery before you. Still I do so for your curiosity has been greatly excited.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यप्यहं नरेन्द्रेण रहस्यं श्रावितः पुरा
तच्चाप्युदाहरिष्यामि दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
yadyapyahaṁ narendreṇa rahasyaṁ śrāvitaḥ purā
taccāpyudāhariṣyāmi daivaṁ hi duratikramam

translations.english: Tough this mystery was communicated formerly by the king Dasaratha and though it is not proper to reveal it to any body, still I express it before you that you may not, on hearing it, be worked up with sorrow; for destiny is hard to be got over. And it is by the influence of that destiny that you have met with such a sorrow and grief. However, do you not reveal this secret to Satrughna and Bharata.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य गम्भीरार्थपदं महत्
तथ्यं ब्रूहीति सौमित्रिः सूतं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā bhāṣitaṁ tasya gambhīrārthapadaṁ mahat
tathyaṁ brūhīti saumitriḥ sūtaṁ vākyamathābravīt

translations.english: Hearing these grave and important words of Sumantra, Laksmana ordered him to relate.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा संचोदितः सूतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना
तद्वाक्यमृषिणा प्रोक्तं व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tathā saṁcoditaḥ sūto lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
tadvākyamṛṣiṇā proktaṁ vyāhartumupacakrame

translations.english: Being thus requested by the high-souled Laks maņa, Sumantra began to reveal the mystery of Durbasa's account.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरा नाम्ना हि दुर्वासा अत्रेः पुत्रो महामुनिः
वसिष्ठस्याश्रमे पुण्ये स वार्षिक्यमुवास ह
verses.transliteration:
purā nāmnā hi durvāsā atreḥ putro mahāmuniḥ
vasiṣṭhasyāśrame puṇye sa vārṣikyamuvāsa ha

translations.english: In the days of yore the great ascetic Durbāsā, the son of Atri, resided for a year in the holy hermitage of Vasiştha.

verses.sanskrit:
तमाश्रमं महातेजाः पिता ते सुमहायशाः
पुरोधसं महात्मानं दिदृक्षुरगमत्स्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
tamāśramaṁ mahātejāḥ pitā te sumahāyaśāḥ
purodhasaṁ mahātmānaṁ didṛkṣuragamatsvayam

translations.english: At that time your sire, the highly effulgent and illustrious Dasaratha, with a view to see his high-souled priest Vasistha, repaired there.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा सूर्यसंकाशं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा
उपविष्टं वसिष्ठस्य सव्ये पार्श्वे महामुनिम्
तौ मुनी तापसश्रेष्ठौ विनीतस्त्वभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā sūryasaṁkāśaṁ jvalantamiva tejasā
upaviṣṭaṁ vasiṣṭhasya savye pārśve mahāmunim
tau munī tāpasaśreṣṭhau vinītastvabhyavādayat

translations.english: He saw the great ascetic Durbásā, burning like the sun in his effulgence, seated on the right hand side of Vasiștha. Thereupon he humbly saluted those two leading ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
स ताभ्यां पूजितो राजा स्वागतेनासनेन च
पाद्येन फलमूलैश्च सोऽप्यास्ते मुनिभिः सह
verses.transliteration:
sa tābhyāṁ pūjito rājā svāgatenāsanena ca
pādyena phalamūlaiśca so'pyāste munibhiḥ saha

translations.english: And they too, welcoming him, received him duly with seat, water to wash feet, Arghya, fruits and roots, Then he lived there in the company of the ascetics.

verses.sanskrit:
तेषां तत्रोपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः
बभूवुः परमर्षीणां मध्यादित्यगतेऽहनि
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṁ tatropaviṣṭānāṁ tāstāḥ sumadhurāḥ kathāḥ
babhūvuḥ paramarṣīṇāṁ madhyādityagate'hani

translations.english: Thereupon during the noon, all those ascetics, seated there, began to dwell upon various pleasant topics.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः कथायां कस्यांचित्प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः
उवाच तं महात्मानमत्रेः पुत्रं तपोधनम्
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ kathāyāṁ kasyāṁcitprāñjaliḥ pragraho nṛpaḥ
uvāca taṁ mahātmānamatreḥ putraṁ tapodhanam

translations.english: During an interval Dasaratha, with folded hands and uplifted arms, said to the high-souled son of Atri-Durbāsā, having asceticism for his wealth.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्किंप्रमाणेन मम वंशो भविष्यति
किमायुश्च हि मे रामः पुत्राश्चान्ये किमायुषः
verses.transliteration:
bhagavankiṁpramāṇena mama vaṁśo bhaviṣyati
kimāyuśca hi me rāmaḥ putrāścānye kimāyuṣaḥ

translations.english: O illustrious Sir, how long shall my family remain in existence? What is the extent of the lease of life granted to Rāma and my other sons?

verses.sanskrit:
रामस्य च सुता ये स्युस्तेषामायुः कियद्भवेत्
काम्यया भगवन्ब्रूहि वंशस्यास्य गतिं मम
verses.transliteration:
rāmasya ca sutā ye syusteṣāmāyuḥ kiyadbhavet
kāmyayā bhagavanbrūhi vaṁśasyāsya gatiṁ mama

translations.english: How long shall the descendants of Rāma live? And what shall be the end of my race? Do you relate all this to me.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं राज्ञो दशरथस्य तु
दुर्वासाः सुमहातेजा व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ rājño daśarathasya tu
durvāsāḥ sumahātejā vyāhartumupacakrame

translations.english: Hearing the words of the king Dasaratha the highly effulgent Durbāsā replied.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्यायाः पती रामो दीर्घकालं भविष्यति
सुखिनश्च समृद्धाश्च भविष्यन्त्यस्य चानुजाः
verses.transliteration:
ayodhyāyāḥ patī rāmo dīrghakālaṁ bhaviṣyati
sukhinaśca samṛddhāśca bhaviṣyantyasya cānujāḥ

translations.english: O conferer of honours, for sooth shall Rāma partake of the fruits of Bhrgu's curse. He shall reign in Ayodhyā for a long time.

verses.sanskrit:
दशवर्षसहस्रणि दशवर्षशतानि च
रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
daśavarṣasahasraṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca
rāmo rājyamupāsitvā brahmalokaṁ gamiṣyati

translations.english: All his followers shall be happy and prosperous. Having reigned for eleven thousand years Rāma shall repair to the region of Brahmă.

verses.sanskrit:
समृद्धैर्हयमेधैश्च इष्ट्वा परपुरंजयः
राजवंशांश्च काकुत्स्थो बहून्संस्थापयिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
samṛddhairhayamedhaiśca iṣṭvā parapuraṁjayaḥ
rājavaṁśāṁśca kākutstho bahūnsaṁsthāpayiṣyati

translations.english: None shall be able to vanquish him. He shall celebrate many a horse-sacrifice with profuse gifts and shall establish many royal families.

verses.sanskrit:
स सर्वमखिलं राज्ञो वंशस्यास्य गतागतम्
आख्याय सुमहातेजास्तूष्णीमासीन्महाद्युतिः
verses.transliteration:
sa sarvamakhilaṁ rājño vaṁśasyāsya gatāgatam
ākhyāya sumahātejāstūṣṇīmāsīnmahādyutiḥ

translations.english: He shall beget on Sită two sorts. Having thus related to Dasaratha the past and future of his family the highly effulgent great ascetic Durbāsā became silent.

verses.sanskrit:
तूष्णींभूते मुनौ तस्मिन्राजा दशरथस्तदा
अभिवाद्य महात्मानौ पुनरायात्पुरोत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tūṣṇīṁbhūte munau tasminrājā daśarathastadā
abhivādya mahātmānau punarāyātpurottamam

translations.english: He being silent-the great king Dasaratha, having bowed to the two high-souled ascetics, again returned to his city Ayodhyā.

verses.sanskrit:
एतद्वचो मया तत्र मुनिना व्याहृतं पुरा
श्रुतं हृदि च निक्षिप्तं नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
etadvaco mayā tatra muninā vyāhṛtaṁ purā
śrutaṁ hṛdi ca nikṣiptaṁ nānyathā tadbhaviṣyati

translations.english: I had heard there all there words of the great ascetic Durbāså. Up to this time they are lying in my heart. Rsis' words shall never prove fruitless.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं गते न संतापं गन्तुमर्हसि राघव
सीतार्थे राघवार्थे वा दृढो भव नरोत्तम
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ gate na saṁtāpaṁ gantumarhasi rāghava
sītārthe rāghavārthe vā dṛḍho bhava narottama

translations.english: Under these circumstances, O Laksmana, you should not grieve for Sītā or Rāma; in their interest do you become patient.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं सूतस्य परमाद्भुतम्
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ sūtasya paramādbhutam
praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt

translations.english: Hearing those wondrous words of the charioteer Sumantra, Lakşmaņa became greatly happy and eulogised him again and again?

verses.sanskrit:
तयोः संवदतोरेवं सूतलक्ष्मणयोः पथि
अस्तमर्को गतो वासं गोमत्यां तावथोषतुः
verses.transliteration:
tayoḥ saṁvadatorevaṁ sūtalakṣmaṇayoḥ pathi
astamarko gato vāsaṁ gomatyāṁ tāvathoṣatuḥ

translations.english: They thus conversing with one another on their way back, the sun set. They accordingly spent that night on the banks of Kesini.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते प्रविवेश महारथः
अयोध्यां रत्नसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम्
verses.transliteration:
tato'rdhadivase prāpte praviveśa mahārathaḥ
ayodhyāṁ ratnasaṁpūrṇāṁ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām

translations.english: Having spent the night on the banks of Kesini, the mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa, got up early in the morning and again proceeded on his journey (home) and reached in the noon the city of Ayodhyā filled with various jewels and delighted and plump citizens.

verses.sanskrit:
सौमित्रिस्तु परं दैन्यं जगाम सुमहामतिः
रामपादौ समासाद्य वक्ष्यामि किमहं गतः
verses.transliteration:
saumitristu paraṁ dainyaṁ jagāma sumahāmatiḥ
rāmapādau samāsādya vakṣyāmi kimahaṁ gataḥ

translations.english: But the high-souled Lakşmaņa became greatly sorry stricken with the thought as to what he should relate on approaching the feet of Rāma.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं चिन्तयानस्य भवनं शशिसंनिभम्
रामस्य परमोदारं पुरस्तात्समदृश्यत
verses.transliteration:
tasyaivaṁ cintayānasya bhavanaṁ śaśisaṁnibham
rāmasya paramodāraṁ purastātsamadṛśyata

translations.english: While proceeding with this thought he saw the highly picturesque palace of Rāma resembling the rays of the moon.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञस्तु भवनद्वारि सोऽवतीर्य नरोत्तमः
अवाङ्मुखो दीनमनाः प्रविवेशानिवारितः
verses.transliteration:
rājñastu bhavanadvāri so'vatīrya narottamaḥ
avāṅmukho dīnamanāḥ praviveśānivāritaḥ

translations.english: Having descended from his car at the palacegate, Laksmana, the foremost of men, with his face down wards and a distressed heart, unobstructed, entered the palace.

verses.sanskrit:
स दृष्ट्वा राघवं दीनमासीनं परमासने
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां ददर्शाग्रजमग्रतः
verses.transliteration:
sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṁ dīnamāsīnaṁ paramāsane
netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāṁ dadarśāgrajamagrataḥ

translations.english: Having entered there he saw his elder brother Rāma seated poorly on an excellent seat with his eyes full of tears. Being greatly pained at the sight, Saumitri touched his feet and with folded palms said.

verses.sanskrit:
आर्यस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम्
गङ्गातीरे यथोद्दिष्टे वाल्मीकेराश्रमे शुभे
पुनरस्म्यागतो वीर पादमूलमुपासितुम्
verses.transliteration:
āryasyājñāṁ puraskṛtya visṛjya janakātmajām
gaṅgātīre yathoddiṣṭe vālmīkerāśrame śubhe
punarasmyāgato vīra pādamūlamupāsitum

translations.english: O worshipful sir, having obeyed your behest's I have left the daughter of Janaka at the holy hermitage of Vālmiki near the banks of the Gangā. Having left that illustrious pure lady at the skirt of the hermitage. I have again come to serve your feet

verses.sanskrit:
मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र कालस्य गतिरीदृशी
त्वद्विधा न हि शोचन्ति सत्त्ववन्तो मनस्विनः
verses.transliteration:
mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra kālasya gatirīdṛśī
tvadvidhā na hi śocanti sattvavanto manasvinaḥ

translations.english: Do you not grieve, O foremost of men, for such is the cause of time. The intelligent people like you do not grieve.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्
verses.transliteration:
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ
saṁyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṁ ca jīvitam

translations.english: When there is grow there is decay, where there is prosperity there is ruin, and where there is birth there is death.

verses.sanskrit:
शक्तस्त्वमात्मनात्मानं विजेतुं मनसैव हि
लोकान्सर्वांश्च काकुत्स्थ किं पुनर्दुःखमीदृशम्
verses.transliteration:
śaktastvamātmanātmānaṁ vijetuṁ manasaiva hi
lokānsarvāṁśca kākutstha kiṁ punarduḥkhamīdṛśam

translations.english: O Kakutstha, While you can control yourself and your mind, should you not be able to bear this trifling pain of separation? Leading men like yourself are never overwhelmed by all these things.

verses.sanskrit:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धैर्येण सुसमाहितः
त्यजेमां दुर्बलां बुद्धिं संतापं मा कुरुष्व ह
verses.transliteration:
sa tvaṁ puruṣaśārdūla dhairyeṇa susamāhitaḥ
tyajemāṁ durbalāṁ buddhiṁ saṁtāpaṁ mā kuruṣva ha

translations.english: Therefore do you restore yourself patiently, O foremost of men. Do you give up this weakness and or not sorry.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना
उवाच परया प्रीत्या सौमित्रिं मित्रवत्सलम्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu kākutstho lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
uvāca parayā prītyā saumitriṁ mitravatsalam

translations.english: The intelligent Lakşmaņa, the son of Sumitrā, having said this, Rāma, the descendant of Käkutstha and fond of friends, with great delight said.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमेतन्नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण
परितोषश्च मे वीर मम कार्यानुशासने
verses.transliteration:
evametannaraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa
paritoṣaśca me vīra mama kāryānuśāsane

translations.english: You have spoken the truth, O Laksmana, O foremost of men. I have been greatly delighted, O hero for your carrying out my orders.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्वृतिश्च कृता सौम्य संतापश्च निराकृतः
भवद्वाक्यैः सुमधुरैरनुनीतोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण
verses.transliteration:
nirvṛtiśca kṛtā saumya saṁtāpaśca nirākṛtaḥ
bhavadvākyaiḥ sumadhurairanunīto'smi lakṣmaṇa

translations.english: O gentle Saumitrī, my grief and sorrow have been removed for those pleasant words of yours.

verses.sanskrit:
भार्गवं च्यवनं नाम पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः
दर्शनं ते महाराज चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः
प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः
verses.transliteration:
bhārgavaṁ cyavanaṁ nāma puraskṛtya maharṣayaḥ
darśanaṁ te mahārāja codayanti kṛtatvarāḥ
prīyamāṇā naravyāghra yamunātīravāsinaḥ

translations.english: At this time Sumantra, entering, addressed him, saying, “O king, stopped at the gate, some ascetic stay there, Maharsis, led by Bhargava and Cyavana. And, O mighty monarch, eager for a sight of you, those dwellers on the banks of the Yamunā, well pleased, have despatched me (hither), O tiger among men.” Hearing his words, the righteous Rāma answered: “Let the exalted Brāhmaṇas leaded by Bhārgava, enter."

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
प्रवेशयामास ततस्तापसान्संमतान्बहून्
verses.transliteration:
rājñastvājñāṁ puraskṛtya dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
praveśayāmāsa tatastāpasānsaṁmatānbahūn

translations.english: Thereat, honouring the royal mandate, the warder with joined hands brought those ascetics difficult of being approached.

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन्
इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम्
verses.transliteration:
uvāca ca mahābāhuḥ sarvāneva mahāmunīn
imānyāsanamukhyāni yathārhamupaviśyatām

translations.english: "Do you agreeably to desert take these seats." Hearing Rāma's speech, all the Maharşis sat down on those graceful and elegant golden seats.

verses.sanskrit:
उपविष्टानृषींस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरंजयः
प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
upaviṣṭānṛṣīṁstatra dṛṣṭvā parapuraṁjayaḥ
prayataḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā rāghavo vākyamabravīt

translations.english: And seeing the saints seated there, that captor of hostile capitals Rāghava, restraining himself, with joined hands, observed.

verses.sanskrit:
किमागमनकार्यं वः किं करोमि तपोधनाः
आज्ञाप्योऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम्
verses.transliteration:
kimāgamanakāryaṁ vaḥ kiṁ karomi tapodhanāḥ
ājñāpyo'haṁ maharṣīṇāṁ sarvakāmakaraḥ sukham

translations.english: What is the reason of your visit? What shall I heedfully perform for you? I am worthy of being commanded by the Maharşis; and I must without demur compass every pleasure of theirs.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम्
सर्वमेतद्द्विजार्थं मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि वः
verses.transliteration:
idaṁ rājyaṁ ca sakalaṁ jīvitaṁ ca hṛdi sthitam
sarvametaddvijārthaṁ me satyametadbravīmi vaḥ

translations.english: And this entire monarchy, and the life that is resident in my heart, all these are for the regenerate ones. This I tell you in the name of truth.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुवादो महानभूत्
ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम्
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā sādhuvādo mahānabhūt
ṛṣīṇāmugratapasāṁ yamunātīravāsinām

translations.english: Hearing his words, the sages of fierce austerities inhabiting the banks of the Yamunā, broke out into a peal of plandits.

verses.sanskrit:
ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महतान्विताः
उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः
verses.transliteration:
ūcuśca te mahātmāno harṣeṇa mahatānvitāḥ
upapannaṁ naraśreṣṭha tavaiva bhuvi nānyataḥ

translations.english: And those high-souled ones, exceedingly rejoiced, said: On earth, O crown of men, this can only be expected from you and nobody else.

verses.sanskrit:
बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नतिक्रान्ता महाबलाः
कार्यगौरवमश्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन्
verses.transliteration:
bahavaḥ pārthivā rājannatikrāntā mahābalāḥ
kāryagauravamaśrutvā pratijñāṁ nābhyarocayan

translations.english: Many kings wielding great power have passed away who, having regard to the (possible) gravity of the undertaking, could not bring themselves to promise anything before hand.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं; कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम्
कुरुष्व कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो; महाभयात्त्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि
verses.transliteration:
tvayā punarbrāhmaṇagauravādiyaṁ; kṛtā pratijñā hyanavekṣya kāraṇam
kuruṣva kartā hyasi nātra saṁśayo; mahābhayāttrātumṛṣīṁstvamarhasi

translations.english: But, without knowing the task, you have bound yourself by a promise for the glory of the Brahmanas. And you, without doubt, will succeed in effecting the work; and it behove you to deliver the sages from a mighty fright.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रुवद्भिरेवमृषिभिः काकुत्स्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
किं कार्यं ब्रूत भवतां भयं नाशयितास्मि वः
verses.transliteration:
bruvadbhirevamṛṣibhiḥ kākutstho vākyamabravīt
kiṁ kāryaṁ brūta bhavatāṁ bhayaṁ nāśayitāsmi vaḥ

translations.english: When the sages had spoken thus, Käkutstha said: "O ascetics, tell me what is the work which I shall have to accomplish in your behalf. Your fear shall be removed."

verses.sanskrit:
तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे भार्गवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
भयं नः शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर
verses.transliteration:
tathā vadati kākutsthe bhārgavo vākyamabravīt
bhayaṁ naḥ śṛṇu yanmūlaṁ deśasya ca nareśvara

translations.english: As Käkutstha was speaking thus, Bhārgava remarked! O lord of men, do you hear of the origin of the fear that threatens our country.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे राम दैतेयः सुमहाबलः
लोलापुत्रोऽभवज्ज्येष्ठो मधुर्नाम महासुरः
verses.transliteration:
pūrvaṁ kṛtayuge rāma daiteyaḥ sumahābalaḥ
lolāputro'bhavajjyeṣṭho madhurnāma mahāsuraḥ

translations.english: O king, formerly in the Kita age, there was a magnanimous offspring of Diti, the mighty Asura, Madhu, eldest son of Lotā.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः
सुरैश्च परमोदारैः प्रीतिस्तस्यातुलाभवत्
verses.transliteration:
brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca buddhyā ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ
suraiśca paramodāraiḥ prītistasyātulābhavat

translations.english: He was well disposed towards Brāhmaṇas, kind to those seeking his refuge, and gifted with high intelligence. The exceedingly generous deities delighted in him greatly.

verses.sanskrit:
स मधुर्वीर्यसंपन्नो धर्मे च सुसमाहितः
बहुमानाच्च रुद्रेण दत्तस्तस्याद्भुतो वरः
verses.transliteration:
sa madhurvīryasaṁpanno dharme ca susamāhitaḥ
bahumānācca rudreṇa dattastasyādbhuto varaḥ

translations.english: And by way of honouring him, Rudra conferred a wonderful boon upon Madhu endowed with prowess and ever intent on religion.

verses.sanskrit:
शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य महावीर्यं महाप्रभम्
ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
śūlaṁ śūlādviniṣkṛṣya mahāvīryaṁ mahāprabham
dadau mahātmā suprīto vākyaṁ caitaduvāca ha

translations.english: And extracting a dart from his own, possessed of terrific energy, endowed with great force; and furnished with exceeding splendour that highsouled one, well pleased, made it over (to Madhu) and spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वयायमतुलो धर्मो मत्प्रसादात्कृतः शुभः
प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यायुधमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
tvayāyamatulo dharmo matprasādātkṛtaḥ śubhaḥ
prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmyāyudhamuttamam

translations.english: You have practised excellent and unrivalled righteousness, which has won my good graces, and (therefore), I highly gratified, bestow on you this choice weapon.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्सुरैश्च विप्रैश्च न विरुध्येर्महासुर
तावच्छूलं तवेदं स्यादन्यथा नाशमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
yāvatsuraiśca vipraiśca na virudhyermahāsura
tāvacchūlaṁ tavedaṁ syādanyathā nāśamāpnuyāt

translations.english: So long as you, O mighty Asura, do not assail celestials and Vipras, so long shall this be your, otherwise it shall come to naught.

verses.sanskrit:
यश्च त्वामभियुञ्जीत युद्धाय विगतज्वरः
तं शूलं भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम्
verses.transliteration:
yaśca tvāmabhiyuñjīta yuddhāya vigatajvaraḥ
taṁ śūlaṁ bhasmasātkṛtvā punareṣyati te karam

translations.english: Reducing to cinders the person that shall rashly enter upon conflict with you, this dart shall return to your hand.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं रुद्राद्वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः
प्रणिपत्य महादेवं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ rudrādvaraṁ labdhvā bhūya eva mahāsuraḥ
praṇipatya mahādevaṁ vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: Having thus obtained the boon from Rudra, the mighty Asura, again bowing to Mahādeva, addressed him, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्मम वंशस्य शूलमेतदनुत्तमम्
भवेत्तु सततं देव सुराणामीश्वरो ह्यसि
verses.transliteration:
bhagavanmama vaṁśasya śūlametadanuttamam
bhavettu satataṁ deva surāṇāmīśvaro hyasi

translations.english: O reverend one, may this excellent dart be the possession of my family O god, you are the lord of the immortals.

verses.sanskrit:
तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः
प्रत्युवाच महादेवो नैतदेवं भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
taṁ bruvāṇaṁ madhuṁ devaḥ sarvabhūtapatiḥ śivaḥ
pratyuvāca mahādevo naitadevaṁ bhaviṣyati

translations.english: Thereat the lord of all beings, the mighty deity Śiva, answered Madhu, when he had spoken thus: This will not be.

verses.sanskrit:
मा भूत्ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा
भवतः पुत्रमेकं तु शूलमेतद्गमिष्यति
verses.transliteration:
mā bhūtte viphalā vāṇī matprasādakṛtā śubhā
bhavataḥ putramekaṁ tu śūlametadgamiṣyati

translations.english: But in order that your prayer may not go for nothing. I graciously say in your behalf that one of your sons shall sway this dart.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्करस्थः शूलोऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां शूलहस्तो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration:
yāvatkarasthaḥ śūlo'yaṁ bhaviṣyati sutasya te
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ śūlahasto bhaviṣyati

translations.english: So long that dart-handed one shall be incapable of being destroyed be any creature.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं मधुर्वरं लब्ध्वा देवात्सुमहदद्भुतम्
भवनं चासुरश्रेष्ठः कारयामास सुप्रभम्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ madhurvaraṁ labdhvā devātsumahadadbhutam
bhavanaṁ cāsuraśreṣṭhaḥ kārayāmāsa suprabham

translations.english: Having obtained this wonderful boon from the god, Madhu, foremost of Asuras, caused a splendid city to be constructed.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसी हि या
विश्वावसोरपत्यं सा ह्यनलायां महाप्रभा
verses.transliteration:
tasya patnī mahābhāgā priyā kumbhīnasī hi yā
viśvāvasorapatyaṁ sā hyanalāyāṁ mahāprabhā

translations.english: His beloved wife the exalted and majestic Kumbhīnasſ is the offspring of Viśvāvasu by Anala.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः
बाल्यात्प्रभृति दुष्टात्मा पापान्येव समाचरत्
verses.transliteration:
tasyāḥ putro mahāvīryo lavaṇo nāma dāruṇaḥ
bālyātprabhṛti duṣṭātmā pāpānyeva samācarat

translations.english: Her son, the highly powerful wicked, and fierce Lavana, ever since his boyhood, gave himself up to a sinful course of life.

verses.sanskrit:
तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा दुःखसमन्वितः
मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किंचिदब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration:
taṁ putraṁ durvinītaṁ tu dṛṣṭvā duḥkhasamanvitaḥ
madhuḥ sa śokamāpede na cainaṁ kiṁcidabravīt

translations.english: Seeing his son, committed to an impious course Madhu was overcome with grief, but he did not say anything to him.

verses.sanskrit:
स विहाय इमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम्
शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्
verses.transliteration:
sa vihāya imaṁ lokaṁ praviṣṭo varuṇālayam
śūlaṁ niveśya lavaṇe varaṁ tasmai nyavedayat

translations.english: And forsaking this world, he entered the region of Varuņa; and making over the dart to Lavana, communicated to him all about the boon he had obtained.

verses.sanskrit:
एवंप्रभावो लवणः शूलं चैव तथाविधम्
श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः
verses.transliteration:
evaṁprabhāvo lavaṇaḥ śūlaṁ caiva tathāvidham
śrutvā pramāṇaṁ kākutstha tvaṁ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ

translations.english: And by virtue of the power of the dart, he oppress the three worlds in especial the ascetics; such is the power of Lavaņa, and such is his dart. Hearing all this O Kākutstha, you are capable (of righting our wrong.) You are our chief resource.

verses.sanskrit:
बहवः पार्थिवा राम भयार्तैरृषिभिः पुरा
अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे
verses.transliteration:
bahavaḥ pārthivā rāma bhayārtairṛṣibhiḥ purā
abhayaṁ yācitā vīra trātāraṁ na ca vidmahe

translations.english: O Rāma, many a monarch has been already sued by the sages, O hero, to deliver them from this fear, but we have not yet found a deliverer.

verses.sanskrit:
ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम्
त्रातारं विद्महे राम नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम्
तत्परित्रातुमिच्छामो लवणाद्भयपीडिताः
verses.transliteration:
te vayaṁ rāvaṇaṁ śrutvā hataṁ sabalavāhanam
trātāraṁ vidmahe rāma nānyaṁ bhuvi narādhipam
tatparitrātumicchāmo lavaṇādbhayapīḍitāḥ

translations.english: Hearing, O child, that Ravana together with all his forces and vehicles has been destroyed (by you), we know that there breathes not another king on earth capable of delivering us. Therefore our prayer is that you may deliver us afflicted with the fear of Lavana.

verses.sanskrit:
तथोक्ते तानृषीन्रामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः
किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते
verses.transliteration:
tathokte tānṛṣīnrāmaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
kimāhāraḥ kimācāro lavaṇaḥ kva ca vartate

translations.english: Thus accosted (by the sages), Rāma answered them with joined hands: "What does he live on? What are his ways? And where does Lavana live?"

verses.sanskrit:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते
ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा
verses.transliteration:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te
tato nivedayāmāsurlavaṇo vavṛdhe yathā

translations.english: Hearing Räghava's words, the sages informed him of the way in which Lavana increased in power.

verses.sanskrit:
आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः
आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने सदा
verses.transliteration:
āhāraḥ sarvasattvāni viśeṣeṇa ca tāpasāḥ
ācāro raudratā nityaṁ vāso madhuvane sadā

translations.english: His food is every creature specially ascetics; his manner of life is regulated by ferocity and his constant home is Madhuvana.

verses.sanskrit:
हत्वा दशसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विपान्
मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम्
verses.transliteration:
hatvā daśasahasrāṇi siṁhavyāghramṛgadvipān
mānuṣāṁścaiva kurute nityamāhāramāhnikam

translations.english: Slaying constantly thousands on thousands of lions and tigers and deer, and birds and human beings, he provides his daily food (with their flesh.)

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽपराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः
संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः
verses.transliteration:
tato'parāṇi sattvāni khādate sa mahābalaḥ
saṁhāre samanuprāpte vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ

translations.english: And like the Destroyer on the occasion of the universal dissolution, that one possessed of gigantic strength feeds on other creatures as well.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन्
घातयिष्यामि तद्रक्षो व्यपगच्छतु वो भयम्
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā rāghavo vākyamuvāca sa mahāmunīn
ghātayiṣyāmi tadrakṣo vyapagacchatu vo bhayam

translations.english: Hearing this, Rāghava spoke to the mighty ascetics: "I will slay that Raksasa. Let your depart."

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तेषां प्रतिज्ञाय मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम्
स भ्रातॄन्सहितान्सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
tathā teṣāṁ pratijñāya munīnāmugratejasām
sa bhrātṝnsahitānsarvānuvāca raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: Having thus bound himself with that promise to the ascetics of fierce energy, Raghu's son along with his brothers spoke.

verses.sanskrit:
को हन्ता लवणं वीराः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम्
भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्याथ वा पुनः
verses.transliteration:
ko hantā lavaṇaṁ vīrāḥ kasyāṁśaḥ sa vidhīyatām
bharatasya mahābāhoḥ śatrughnasyātha vā punaḥ

translations.english: What hero shall slay Lavana? Do you decide this. On whom shall devolve this duty? Whether the mighty armed Bharata or the intelligent Śatrughna shall (do this work?).

verses.sanskrit:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम्
verses.transliteration:
rāghaveṇaivamuktastu bharato vākyamabravīt
ahamenaṁ vadhiṣyāmi mamāṁśaḥ sa vidhīyatām

translations.english: Thus addressed by Raghava Bharata remarked: "I will slay this. Let this task be entrusted to me."

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम्
कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnastvabravīdvākyaṁ praṇipatya narādhipam
kṛtakarmā mahābāhurmadhyamo raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: Hearing Bharata's speech instinct with fortitude and valour, the younger brother of Lakş maņa stood up, leaving his golden seat. And Śatrughna, saluting the king represented: “The mighty-armed second son of Raghu has already achieved a grand work: he formerly governed Ayodhyā empty of the noble one,* bearing in his heart the grief connected with his return. *Rama.

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखानि च बहूनीह अनुभूतानि पार्थिव
शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे महात्मना
verses.transliteration:
duḥkhāni ca bahūnīha anubhūtāni pārthiva
śayāno duḥkhaśayyāsu nandigrāme mahātmanā

translations.english: Undergoing many a hardship, o king, that illustrious one passed his days, lying down on a bed of sorrow, and living on fruits and roots, and wearing rags.

verses.sanskrit:
फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटाचीरधरस्तथा
अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः
प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration:
phalamūlāśano bhūtvā jaṭācīradharastathā
anubhūyedṛśaṁ duḥkhameṣa rāghavanandanaḥ
preṣye mayi sthite rājanna bhūyaḥ kleśamāpnuyāt

translations.english: Having suffered such misery, Raghu's son should not be suffered to undergo trouble, while, O king I his servant is by.

verses.sanskrit:
अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व मयोद्यतम्
वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्विप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्
verses.transliteration:
abhiṣekaṁ ca kākutstha pratīcchasva mayodyatam
vasiṣṭhapramukhairviprairvidhimantrapuraskṛtam

translations.english: So if you accept my words, then slaying Madhu's son, the sinful Lavana, rule the kingdom righteously. O hero, you must say anything after what I have spoken. Without doubt, a youthful younger brother must obey the injunctions of his elder brother. Do you, o Kākutstha, accept the installation which I confer on the, precluded by the prescribed religious formulae uttered by Vipras headed by Vasiştha."

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण परां व्रीडामुपागतः
शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसंपन्नो मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa parāṁ vrīḍāmupāgataḥ
śatrughno vīryasaṁpanno mandaṁ mandamuvāca ha

translations.english: Thus accosted by Rāma, the exceedingly energetic Satrughna was powerfully wrought up with bashfulness, and replied slowly.

verses.sanskrit:
अवश्यं करणीयं च शासनं पुरुषर्षभ
तव चैव महाभाग शासनं दुरतिक्रमम्
अयं कामकरो राजंस्तवास्मि पुरुषर्षभ
verses.transliteration:
avaśyaṁ karaṇīyaṁ ca śāsanaṁ puruṣarṣabha
tava caiva mahābhāga śāsanaṁ duratikramam
ayaṁ kāmakaro rājaṁstavāsmi puruṣarṣabha

translations.english: I must, O best of men, do your behest: for, O exalted one, your mandate can never be passed by me.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्ते तु शूरेण शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना
उवाच रामः संहृष्टो लक्ष्मणं भरतं तथा
verses.transliteration:
evamukte tu śūreṇa śatrughnena mahātmanā
uvāca rāmaḥ saṁhṛṣṭo lakṣmaṇaṁ bharataṁ tathā

translations.english: Thus addressed by the heroic and high-souled Śatrughna, Rāma, delighted, spoke to Bharata and Laksmana.

verses.sanskrit:
संभारानभिषेकस्य आनयध्वं समाहिताः
अद्यैव पुरुषव्याघ्रमभिषेक्ष्यामि दुर्जयम्
verses.transliteration:
saṁbhārānabhiṣekasya ānayadhvaṁ samāhitāḥ
adyaiva puruṣavyāghramabhiṣekṣyāmi durjayam

translations.english: Do you carefully provide the things necessary for the coronation: this very day shall I install that foremost of men, the descendant of Raghu.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोधसं च काकुत्स्थौ नैगमानृत्विजस्तथा
मन्त्रिणश्चैव मे सर्वानानयध्वं ममाज्ञया
verses.transliteration:
purodhasaṁ ca kākutsthau naigamānṛtvijastathā
mantriṇaścaiva me sarvānānayadhvaṁ mamājñayā

translations.english: And by my order do you summon the Purodhasas, O Kākutstha, and the citizens and the Rtvijas, and the councillors.

verses.sanskrit:
राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तथाकुर्वन्महारथाः
अभिषेकसमारम्भं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोधसं
प्रविष्टा राजभवनं पुरंदरगृहोपमम्
verses.transliteration:
rājñaḥ śāsanamājñāya tathākurvanmahārathāḥ
abhiṣekasamārambhaṁ puraskṛtya purodhasaṁ
praviṣṭā rājabhavanaṁ puraṁdaragṛhopamam

translations.english: Having received the royal behest, the mighty car-warriors did accordingly. And the Kșatriyas and the Brāhmaṇas entered the royal mansion with the priest as well as the requisite things for the installation.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽभिषेको ववृधे शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः
संप्रहर्षकरः श्रीमान्राघवस्य पुरस्य च
verses.transliteration:
tato'bhiṣeko vavṛdhe śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ
saṁpraharṣakaraḥ śrīmānrāghavasya purasya ca

translations.english: And then commenced the auspicious sprinkling of the high-souled Satrughna, gladdening (the hearts of all in) the palace of Rāghava.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽभिषिक्तं शत्रुघ्नमङ्कमारोप्य राघवः
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं तेजस्तस्याभिपूरयन्
verses.transliteration:
tato'bhiṣiktaṁ śatrughnamaṅkamāropya rāghavaḥ
uvāca madhurāṁ vāṇīṁ tejastasyābhipūrayan

translations.english: Then placing the installed Satrughna on his lap Rāghava, extolling his prowess, addressed him sweet words.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं शरस्त्वमोघस्ते दिव्यः परपुरंजयः
अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्तासि रघुनन्दन
verses.transliteration:
ayaṁ śarastvamoghaste divyaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ
anena lavaṇaṁ saumya hantāsi raghunandana

translations.english: O captor of hostile capitals, this divine arrow never missing is your. With this, O son of Raghu, you, O spliced one, with slay Lavana.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां तेनायं हि शरोत्तमः
सृष्टः क्रोधाभिभूतेन विनाशार्थं दुरात्मनोः
मधुकैटभयोर्वीर विघाते वर्तमानयोः
verses.transliteration:
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ tenāyaṁ hi śarottamaḥ
sṛṣṭaḥ krodhābhibhūtena vināśārthaṁ durātmanoḥ
madhukaiṭabhayorvīra vighāte vartamānayoḥ

translations.english: O Kākutstha, this shaft was forged when invisible by celestials and Asuras the divine selfsprung and invincible (deity) reposed on the mighty main, and when creation was oppressed by Madhu and Kaitabha as well as other Räks asas. He, overwhelmed with rage desirous of creating the three worlds, created the best of arrows invincible to all beings, for the extraction of the wicked ones; and destroyed them in battle by means of this very arrow. And having with this foremost of shafts finished Madhu and Kait abha, they set about creating the worlds.

verses.sanskrit:
नायं मया शरः पूर्वं रावणस्य वधार्थिना
मुक्तः शत्रुघ्न भूतानां महांस्त्रासो भवेदिति
verses.transliteration:
nāyaṁ mayā śaraḥ pūrvaṁ rāvaṇasya vadhārthinā
muktaḥ śatrughna bhūtānāṁ mahāṁstrāso bhavediti

translations.english: When, O Satrughna, formerly I sought to slay Råvaņa, I did not discharge this arrow, thinking that if discharged, it would inflict great havoc on creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
अप्रविष्टं च भवनं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभ
आह्वयेथा महाबाहो ततो हन्तासि राक्षसम्
verses.transliteration:
apraviṣṭaṁ ca bhavanaṁ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabha
āhvayethā mahābāho tato hantāsi rākṣasam

translations.english: Therefore, O foremost of men, you should, before entering the city, stand at the gate obstructing his course. O you having long arms, you should invite him for battle when he shall be weaponless and in that way would be able to destroy him.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु अवध्यः स भविष्यति
यदि त्वेवं कृते वीर विनाशमुपयास्यति
verses.transliteration:
anyathā kriyamāṇe tu avadhyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
yadi tvevaṁ kṛte vīra vināśamupayāsyati

translations.english: And by no other means he is to be slain. If you can encompass this, he shall forsooth be slain.

verses.sanskrit:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शूलस्य च विपर्ययम्
श्रीमतः शितिकण्ठस्य कृत्यं हि दुरतिक्रमम्
verses.transliteration:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṁ śūlasya ca viparyayam
śrīmataḥ śitikaṇṭhasya kṛtyaṁ hi duratikramam

translations.english: O my son, I have thus told you the way in which the dare should be thwarted. It is impossible to surpass the prowess of the graceful Nilkantha.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः
पुनरेवापरं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu kākutsthaṁ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
punarevāparaṁ vākyamuvāca raghunandanaḥ

translations.english: Having thus addressed Satrughna, Rāma again and again praised him and said.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तरापणवीथ्यश्च नानापण्योपशोभिताः
अनुगच्छन्तु शत्रुघ्न तथैव नटनर्तकाः
verses.transliteration:
antarāpaṇavīthyaśca nānāpaṇyopaśobhitāḥ
anugacchantu śatrughna tathaiva naṭanartakāḥ

translations.english: O foremost of men, let four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, one hundred excellent elephants, shops with various articles and songsters follow you.

verses.sanskrit:
हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य अयुतं पुरुषर्षभ
गृहीत्वा गच्छ शत्रुघ्न पर्याप्तधनवाहनः
verses.transliteration:
hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya ayutaṁ puruṣarṣabha
gṛhītvā gaccha śatrughna paryāptadhanavāhanaḥ

translations.english: O foremost of men, O Śatrughna, do you proceed with Niyuta gold and silver coins and necessary riches and conveyances.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यर्थास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः
सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गस्तु यत्र तिष्ठति राघव
verses.transliteration:
na hyarthāstatra tiṣṭhanti na dārā na ca bāndhavāḥ
suprīto bhṛtyavargastu yatra tiṣṭhati rāghava

translations.english: Do you so act, O hero, that soldiers might be well-fed and delighted and be not annoyed with you. Do you please them with sweet words, for the servants, when they face enemies, have not with them friends or wives—and so they are pleased, O Rāghava when they receive sufficient food and presents.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम्
लवणस्तु मधोः पुत्रस्तथा गच्छेरशङ्कितः
verses.transliteration:
yathā tvāṁ na prajānāti gacchantaṁ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam
lavaṇastu madhoḥ putrastathā gaccheraśaṅkitaḥ

translations.english: O Śatrughna, having sent before a huge and well contended army do you proceed afterwards to Madhuvana. You should proceed so fearlessly that Madhu's son Lavaņa might not know that you were going for encounter.

verses.sanskrit:
न तस्य मृत्युरन्योऽस्ति कश्चिद्धि पुरुषर्षभ
दर्शनं योऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि
verses.transliteration:
na tasya mṛtyuranyo'sti kaściddhi puruṣarṣabha
darśanaṁ yo'bhigaccheta sa vadhyo lavaṇena hi

translations.english: O foremost of men, he shall not be slain by any other expedient than that I have acquainted yourself with. If he can perceive before, whoever that enemy might be, Lavana shall forsooth destroy him.

verses.sanskrit:
स ग्रीष्मे व्यपयाते तु वर्षरात्र उपस्थिते
हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य स हि कालोऽस्य दुर्मतेः
verses.transliteration:
sa grīṣme vyapayāte tu varṣarātra upasthite
hanyāstvaṁ lavaṇaṁ saumya sa hi kālo'sya durmateḥ

translations.english: When rains shall set in after the expiration of the present summer you should slay him for that is the proper time for destroying that viciousminded one.

verses.sanskrit:
महर्षींस्तु पुरस्कृत्य प्रयान्तु तव सैनिकाः
यथा ग्रीष्मावशेषेण तरेयुर्जाह्नवीजलम्
verses.transliteration:
maharṣīṁstu puraskṛtya prayāntu tava sainikāḥ
yathā grīṣmāvaśeṣeṇa tareyurjāhnavījalam

translations.english: Let the soldiers only now proceed with ascetics before them; the summer has not as yet fully expired and this is the time, when they shall, without any trouble, be able to cross the Gangā. Afterwards having encamped your army on the other side of the Gangā you should alone proceed speedily with your bow.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण शत्रुघ्नस्तान्महाबलान्
सेनामुख्यान्समानीय ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
evamuktastu rāmeṇa śatrughnastānmahābalān
senāmukhyānsamānīya tato vākyamuvāca ha

translations.english: Hearing those words of Rāma and summoning all his highly powerful and leading warriors Satrughna said "Do you all proceed and halt at those places which are well known to you. Do not oppress any body."

verses.sanskrit:
तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य निर्याप्य च महद्बलम्
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत्
verses.transliteration:
tathā tāṁstu samājñāpya niryāpya ca mahadbalam
kausalyāṁ ca sumitrāṁ ca kaikeyīṁ cābhyavādayat

translations.english: Having thus ordered the powerful warriors the highly powerful Śatrughna bowed to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyi.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः
पुरोधसं वसिष्ठं च शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान्
प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा निर्जगाम महाबलः
verses.transliteration:
lakṣmaṇaṁ bharataṁ caiva praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
purodhasaṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ ca śatrughnaḥ prayatātmavān
pradakṣiṇamatho kṛtvā nirjagāma mahābalaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon having circumambulated with folded hands Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Bharata he reverentially saluted the feet of the priests. And then with Rāma's permission and having gone round him the highly powerful Śatrughna issued out.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रस्थाप्य तद्बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि
एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितस्तदा
verses.transliteration:
prasthāpya tadbalaṁ sarvaṁ māsamātroṣitaḥ pathi
eka evāśu śatrughno jagāma tvaritastadā

translations.english: Having thus despatched his army and waited at Ayodhya for a month Śatrughna, the slayer of enemies, proceeded alone.

verses.sanskrit:
द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः
वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद्वासमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration:
dvirātramantare śūra uṣya rāghavanandanaḥ
vālmīkerāśramaṁ puṇyamagacchadvāsamuttamam

translations.english: Having spent two nights on his way he arrived at the holy and picturesque hermitage of the great ascetic Vālmīki.

verses.sanskrit:
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाल्मीकिं मुनिसत्तमम्
कृताञ्जलिरथो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
verses.transliteration:
so'bhivādya mahātmānaṁ vālmīkiṁ munisattamam
kṛtāñjaliratho bhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha

translations.english: And having bowed to that high-souled Muni Vālmīki, he with folded palms, said thus.

verses.sanskrit:
भगवन्वस्तुमिच्छामि गुरोः कृत्यादिहागतः
श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीचीं वारुणीं दिशम्
verses.transliteration:
bhagavanvastumicchāmi guroḥ kṛtyādihāgataḥ
śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmi pratīcīṁ vāruṇīṁ diśam

translations.english: "O illustrious Sir, I wish to wait here this day; I have come here for some business of our master Rāma. To-morrow morning I shall proceed to the dreadful West.”

verses.sanskrit:
शत्रुघ्नस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुंगवः
प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं स्वागतं ते महायशः
verses.transliteration:
śatrughnasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasya munipuṁgavaḥ
pratyuvāca mahātmānaṁ svāgataṁ te mahāyaśaḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics, replied saying: “O you of great renown, do you wait here without any hesitation. O gentle one, this hermitage belongs to the descendants of the Raghu face. Do you fearlessly take your seat and water to wash your feet.”

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतिगृह्य ततः पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम्
भक्षयामास काकुत्स्थस्तृप्तिं च परमां गतः
verses.transliteration:
pratigṛhya tataḥ pūjāṁ phalamūlaṁ ca bhojanam
bhakṣayāmāsa kākutsthastṛptiṁ ca paramāṁ gataḥ

translations.english: Thereupon taking water to wash his feet and feeding upon fruits and roots Satrughna attained to great delight.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु भुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्महर्षिं तमुवाच ह
पूर्वं यज्ञविभूतीयं कस्याश्रमसमीपतः
verses.transliteration:
sa tu bhuktvā mahābāhurmaharṣiṁ tamuvāca ha
pūrvaṁ yajñavibhūtīyaṁ kasyāśramasamīpataḥ

translations.english: After eating the fruits and roots he asked the great ascetic Vālmīki saying: “O great ascetic, to whom belong the articles of sacrifice in the east near this hermitage?”

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्
शत्रुघ्न शृणु यस्येदं बभूवायतनं पुरा
verses.transliteration:
tasya tadbhāṣitaṁ śrutvā vālmīkirvākyamabravīt
śatrughna śṛṇu yasyedaṁ babhūvāyatanaṁ purā

translations.english: Whereto Vālmīki replied “Satrughna, hear I shall tell you, whose sacrificial ground was this in the days of yore.

verses.sanskrit:
युष्माकं पूर्वको राजा सुदासस्य महात्मनः
पुत्रो मित्रसहो नाम वीर्यवानतिधार्मिकः
verses.transliteration:
yuṣmākaṁ pūrvako rājā sudāsasya mahātmanaḥ
putro mitrasaho nāma vīryavānatidhārmikaḥ

translations.english: There was a king by the name of Saudāsa, one of your ancestors. His son Vīryasaha was a highly powerful and pious king.

verses.sanskrit:
शार्दूलरूपिणौ घोरौ मृगान्बहुसहस्रशः
भक्षयाणावसंतुष्टौ पर्याप्तिं च न जग्मतुः
verses.transliteration:
śārdūlarūpiṇau ghorau mṛgānbahusahasraśaḥ
bhakṣayāṇāvasaṁtuṣṭau paryāptiṁ ca na jagmatuḥ

translations.english: The heroic Saudāsa was fond of hunting from his boyhood. Once on a time while a hunting, he espied two Rākṣasas in the forest. He had heard about them many times before: they were in the shape of tigers and of a dreadful figure and were not satisfied with devouring many thousand deer.

verses.sanskrit:
स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मृगं च वनं कृतम्
क्रोधेन महताविष्टो जघानैकं महेषुणा
verses.transliteration:
sa tu tau rākṣasau dṛṣṭvā nirmṛgaṁ ca vanaṁ kṛtam
krodhena mahatāviṣṭo jaghānaikaṁ maheṣuṇā

translations.english: King Saudāsa saw those two Rākşasas and found the forest divested of all creatures. And enraged in consequence thereof he slew one of them.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं रक्षस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत
कालपर्याययोगेन राजा मित्रसहोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tu taṁ rakṣastatraivāntaradhīyata
kālaparyāyayogena rājā mitrasaho'bhavat

translations.english: Having said this the Rākşasa vanished therefrom. Thereupon in time the prince Mitrasaha became king.

verses.sanskrit:
राजापि यजते यज्ञं तस्याश्रमसमीपतः
अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं तं वसिष्ठोऽभ्यपालयत्
verses.transliteration:
rājāpi yajate yajñaṁ tasyāśramasamīpataḥ
aśvamedhaṁ mahāyajñaṁ taṁ vasiṣṭho'bhyapālayat

translations.english: Saudása engaged in celebrating a mighty horse-sacrifice in the vicinity of this hermitage. Vasiștha officiated as a priest at that sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र यज्ञो महानासीद्बहुवर्षगणायुतान्
समृद्धः परया लक्ष्म्या देवयज्ञसमोऽभवत्
verses.transliteration:
tatra yajño mahānāsīdbahuvarṣagaṇāyutān
samṛddhaḥ parayā lakṣmyā devayajñasamo'bhavat

translations.english: It continued for many Ayuta years. For immense riches the sacrifice appeared like one performed by the celestials.

verses.sanskrit:
अथावसाने यज्ञस्य पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्
वसिष्ठरूपी राजानमिति होवाच राक्षसः
verses.transliteration:
athāvasāne yajñasya pūrvavairamanusmaran
vasiṣṭharūpī rājānamiti hovāca rākṣasaḥ

translations.english: Thereupon when the sacrifice was about to be finished the aforesaid Rākşasa, remembering his former enmity, assumed the shape of Vasiştha and said to the king Saudāsa.

verses.sanskrit:
अद्य यज्ञावसानान्ते सामिषं भोजनं मम
दीयतामिति शीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration:
adya yajñāvasānānte sāmiṣaṁ bhojanaṁ mama
dīyatāmiti śīghraṁ vai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā

translations.english: O king, today the sacrifice shall end; do therefore, without any delay, feed me with meat.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं रक्षसा कामरूपिणा
भक्षसंस्कारकुशलमुवाच पृथिवीपतिः
verses.transliteration:
tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṁ vākyaṁ rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā
bhakṣasaṁskārakuśalamuvāca pṛthivīpatiḥ

translations.english: Hearing the words of the Rākşasa in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, the king ordered his expert cooks, saying.

verses.sanskrit:
हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम्
तथा कुरुष्व शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद्यथा गुरुः
verses.transliteration:
haviṣyaṁ sāmiṣaṁ svādu yathā bhavati bhojanam
tathā kuruṣva śīghraṁ vai parituṣyedyathā guruḥ

translations.english: "Do you soon prepare such dishes of meat as may satisfy my preceptor Vasiştha."

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्त्वं भोजनं राजन्ममैतद्दातुमिच्छसि
तस्माद्भोजनमेतत्ते भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.transliteration:
yasmāttvaṁ bhojanaṁ rājanmamaitaddātumicchasi
tasmādbhojanametatte bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ

translations.english: "O king, let this be your food which you have offered me; this shall not prove otherwise."

verses.sanskrit:
स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः
पुनर्वसिष्ठं प्रोवाच यदुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणा
verses.transliteration:
sa rājā saha patnyā vai praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ
punarvasiṣṭhaṁ provāca yaduktaṁ brahmarūpiṇā

translations.english: Thereupon the king with his spouse again and again bowed to Vasistha's feet and informed him of what the Rākşasa had done under the guise of a Brāhmana.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुज्यारिमर्दनः
प्रतिलेभे पुना राज्यं प्रजाश्चैवान्वपालयत्
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ sa rājā taṁ śāpamupabhujyārimardanaḥ
pratilebhe punā rājyaṁ prajāścaivānvapālayat

translations.english: Having thus suffered the consequences of the curse, Saudasa, the slayer of enemies, again obtained his kingdom an governed his subjects.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य कल्माषपादस्य यज्ञस्यायतनं शुभम्
आश्रमस्य समीपेऽस्मिन्यस्मिन्पृच्छसि राघव
verses.transliteration:
tasya kalmāṣapādasya yajñasyāyatanaṁ śubham
āśramasya samīpe'sminyasminpṛcchasi rāghava

translations.english: O descendant of Raghu, the sacrificial ground of which you have asked me, belongs to the king Saudasa.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम्
विवेश पर्णशालायां महर्षिमभिवाद्य च
verses.transliteration:
tasya tāṁ pārthivendrasya kathāṁ śrutvā sudāruṇām
viveśa parṇaśālāyāṁ maharṣimabhivādya ca

translations.english: Having thus heard the dreadful; story of the king Saudāsa and saluted the ascetic Vālmīki, Śatrughna entered a thatched cottage.

verses.sanskrit:
यामेव रात्रिं शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालां समाविशत्
तामेव रात्रिं सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम्
verses.transliteration:
